hotel.desc: A heritage-listed 1905 Victorian Arts and Crafts bed and breakfast in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood, steps from the Inner Harbour. The property is chef-owned and operated by culinary instructor Vanessa von Schellwitz, whose elaborate gourmet breakfasts are the centrepiece of the stay. Two themed guest rooms — including a family suite sleeping up to five — feature antique clawfoot baths and private semi-entrances that keep guests out of the family living areas.

hotel.name: Denman Island Guesthouse
hotel.desc: The Earth Club Factory — operating as the Denman Island Guesthouse — is a 20-bed hostel, bistro, art gallery, and performance venue housed in a 110-year-old farmhouse on Denman Island, one of BC's northern Gulf Islands. Operating for over 25 years, it blends budget accommodation (dorms, private rooms, seasonal cabins, and on-site camping) with a thriving community hub for music, organic food, and local culture. The website specifically highlights Denman and Hornby as cycling destinations and notes that many summer visitors arrive by bike.

detail.address: 3806 Denman Road, Denman Island, BC V0R 1T0

notes.Laundry: Listed alongside camping in the accommodations summary: '4 rooms inside guesthouse, 3 seasonal trailers/cabins. Camping, Laundry.'

hotel.name: MTN Fun Basecamp
hotel.desc: MTN Fun Basecamp is a small, quiet campground in Squamish, BC, situated directly on the town's extensive trail network and offering true ride-in, ride-out access to some of British Columbia's best mountain biking and hiking terrain. Accommodation options range from unserviced tent sites and group sites to serviced RV hookups and cabin-style rooms, all managed by a small on-site team focused on a calm, respectful atmosphere. Dialed-In Cycling, a separate bike rental, coaching, and guiding business, operates on the property, making it a natural hub for visiting cyclists.

notes.Device charging: Website states: "A communal charging station for phones and small personal electronics is available in a shared area"
notes.Bike wash / hose: Website states: "On-site bike wash station for post-ride clean-ups"

hotel.name: The Rockwell Harrison Guest Lodge
hotel.desc: A premium adult-only bed and breakfast in Harrison Hot Springs, housed in a custom-built post-and-beam lodge designed and constructed by owners Kristy and Roy Molnar over seven years. The lodge is known for its complimentary home-cooked brunches made from locally sourced and garden-grown ingredients. Situated near Harrison Lake, it serves as a base for hiking, kayaking, fishing, and exploring the eastern Fraser Valley.

hotel.name: Harrison Hammond House Farmstay
hotel.desc: Harrison Hammond House is a 25-acre rural farmstay at the confluence of the Harrison and Fraser rivers near Harrison Mills, about 1.5 hours east of Vancouver. The property offers mountain views, a hot tub, wood-burning fireplace, and organic gardens, alongside an unusual secondary use as a musician's rehearsal studio. Touring cyclists are well-placed to access the Harrison Hot Springs corridor, Kilby Museum, and river kayaking routes from this secluded base.

detail.address: 1926 School Road, Harrison Mills, Kent District, BC V0M 1L0

notes.Nearby evening food: Location page lists 'Sasquatch pub (3 minutes)' as a nearby destination

hotel.name: Blue Bear Bed and Breakfast
hotel.desc: Blue Bear Bed and Breakfast is a guest house situated in Tofino, on Vancouver Island's wild west coast — one of BC's premier cycling destinations. Located on Tonquin Park Road, it sits near Tonquin Beach and the old-growth forest trails that attract visitors to this remote surf town. Touring cyclists finishing or starting the Pacific Coast route would find Tofino a logical base, and a B&B of this type typically offers a more personal stay than a motel.

hotel.name: Nowhere Special
hotel.desc: Nowhere Special is a modern, social hostel-style lodge sitting at the base of RED Mountain Resort in Rossland, BC, a community celebrated for both its world-class skiing and its extensive mountain-bike trail network. The lodge is purpose-built for groups, offering crew-style rooms sleeping 2–10 guests, a fully equipped community kitchen, shared laundry, and a lively outdoor gathering area with fire pit and gas grills. Rossland's renowned singletrack starts virtually at the door, and a free shuttle connects guests to the town's restaurants, brewery, and shops in about five minutes.

notes.Laundry: Front-page amenity checklist explicitly lists 'SHARED LAUNDRY ROOM'
notes.Nearby evening food: Website states Rossland (5-minute shuttle ride) offers 'restaurants, bars, a local award-winning brewery'
notes.Luggage storage: Front-page amenity checklist lists 'LUGGAGE CHECK-IN'

hotel.name: Invermere Hostel
hotel.desc: Invermere Hostel is a year-round, 24-hour hostel a short walk from Windermere Lake, James Chabot Beach, and the Columbia River in Invermere, BC. It offers a range of room types from four-person dorms to private queen rooms, making it a flexible option for budget-minded touring cyclists passing through the Columbia Valley. The hostel sits near the town centre and is a stop on the Invermere/Panorama free winter shuttle route.

notes.Nearby evening food: Rocky River Grill Station Pub listed in the hostel's own Local Info navigation menu
notes.Wi-Fi: Wireless Internet available throughout the entire property at no extra cost; most rooms also have wired Ethernet connections

hotel.name: Cycle-Inn Bed & Breakfast
hotel.desc: Cycle-Inn Bed & Breakfast is a cycling-themed B&B located in the Langford/Victoria area of BC, near the Vancouver Crossing Loop route. The cycling-specific name suggests a property historically oriented toward bike tourists. No current website content is available to confirm offerings or current operations.

detail.address: 3158 Anders Rd, Victoria, BC V9B 4C4, Canada

hotel.name: Rodee Homestay
hotel.desc: Rodee Homestay is a four-room bed and breakfast on Stevenson Road in West Kelowna, operated by Rodica Grecu, offering mountain and lake views from rooms and a deck overlooking the Okanagan vineyards. The property serves daily American breakfast alongside Romanian and French cuisine with BBQ facilities, and welcomes pets at no extra charge. Most rooms are on the ground floor and wheelchair accessible, and the homestay is within 8 km of Kelowna.

notes.Laundry: Guest review states: 'We were warmly welcomed to use the kitchen and laundry facilities which we took advantage of.'
notes.Wi-Fi: Website states: 'Free & Unlimited Wifi — WiFi is available in the hotel rooms and is free of charge 24/7.'

hotel.name: Windsor House
hotel.desc: Windsor House is a bed and breakfast located at 325 West 11th Avenue in Vancouver, a two-storey residential-style property in a walkable South Cambie neighbourhood. As a small guest house, it would offer touring cyclists a more personal, home-style stay compared to larger hotels. The surrounding Mount Pleasant and Cambie corridor area provides easy access to urban cycling infrastructure.

hotel.name: Purcell House (College of the Rockies)
hotel.desc: Purcell House Hostel, also known as HI Cranbrook, is a Hostelling International-affiliated property located on the College of the Rockies campus in Cranbrook, BC. Operating seasonally (summer only per OSM), it occupies what appears to be a student residence building and serves as the primary budget accommodation option in this East Kootenay gateway city. Its campus setting on College Way places it away from the town centre but within reach of the Cranbrook trail network.

hotel.name: Hampton Inn by Hilton Vancouver-Airport/Richmond
hotel.desc: The Hampton Inn by Hilton Vancouver-Airport/Richmond is a full-service airport hotel located in Richmond, BC, convenient to Vancouver International Airport and positioned along the Vancouver Crossing Loop cycling route. As part of the Hampton Inn brand, it offers consistent mid-scale hotel amenities in a suburban setting near the airport's southern approach. Touring cyclists finishing or starting near YVR will find it a practical overnight option with easy access to the flat cycling infrastructure of Richmond.

detail.address: 8811 Bridgeport Rd, Richmond, BC V6X 1R9, Canada

hotel.name: Amethyst
hotel.desc: Amethyst is a Scandinavian-inspired deluxe cottage at Nectar Yoga Retreat, a wellness retreat set on 20 acres of forested land on Bowen Island, reachable by a 20-minute ferry from Horseshoe Bay. It is one of three gemstone-named deluxe cottages, sleeping 1-2 guests with a covered cedar porch overlooking a maple and alder grove. Every stay includes daily breakfast, yoga, and meditation sessions, giving the property a structured retreat character rather than a drop-in lodging feel.

detail.address: 720 Gardner Lane, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G2

notes.Early or packed breakfast: Website states stays include daily breakfast as part of the Experience Package

hotel.name: Spinnakers Guesthouses
hotel.desc: Spinnakers Guesthouses sit on the grounds of Spinnakers Gastro Brewpub, Canada's first licensed in-house brewpub, which has been operating since 1984 in Victoria's Vic West neighbourhood. The accommodation offers Heritage Houses, Garden Suites, and a Bungalow steps from the waterfront sea walk along Lime Bay, with check-in handled through the on-site Provisions Store. Guests have immediate access to a full-service brewpub restaurant and a provisions shop stocked with baked goods, bottled beer, and local treats.

notes.Nearby evening food: Spinnakers Gastro Brewpub and Restaurant is on the same grounds as the guesthouses, serving dinner on-site

hotel.name: Raging Elk Adventure Lodging
hotel.desc: Raging Elk is a long-running adventure hostel in downtown Fernie, BC, operated by outdoor enthusiasts Joe and Sadie Howse, offering dorm beds, private rooms, family rooms, and unique deluxe pod-style accommodation. Situated within walking distance of downtown with mountain biking and hiking trails right outside the door, it serves as a well-equipped base camp for cyclists exploring the Fernie area. The property includes an onsite bar (Kodiak Lounge), sauna, games room, and dedicated cycling infrastructure that goes well beyond typical hostel offerings.

notes.Laundry: Amenities page lists 'Daily housekeeping & Laundry Facilities.'
notes.Drying area: Amenities page photo caption reads 'Gear storage and drying area.'
notes.Luggage storage: Amenities page photo caption mentions 'Lockers for personal items.'
notes.Bike wash / hose: Amenities page explicitly lists 'Bike Wash Station.'

hotel.name: HI Vancouver Jericho Beach
hotel.desc: HI Vancouver Jericho Beach is a Hostelling International hostel situated steps from Jericho Beach on Vancouver's west side, placing guests directly on the seaside cycling corridor that connects to the Spirit Trail and the Arbutus Greenway. As part of Canada's largest hostel network, it offers budget accommodation in a low-rise setting surrounded by parkland rather than the dense downtown core. Touring cyclists arriving from the Sea to Sky corridor or the BC Ferries terminals at Tsawwassen or Horseshoe Bay will find it a convenient and affordable base on the western edge of the city.

hotel.name: Stoneshire Guesthouse
hotel.desc: Stoneshire Guesthouse is a self-contained vacation rental property in Clearwater, BC, offering two suites — the Obsidian Suite (sleeps 2) and the Basalt Suite (sleeps 5) — each with a private kitchen and bathroom. It sits in the gateway community to Wells Gray Provincial Park, making it a natural stopping point for cyclists exploring the Trophy Mountain and Helmcken Falls corridors. The property is operated under the broader 'Stay Clearwater' hospitality group, which also manages Fieldstone Guesthouse and River's Edge Retreat.

hotel.name: Blue Grouse Country Inn
hotel.desc: Blue Grouse Country Inn is a four-room, first-class guest house established in 2001 on 26 treed acres within Wells Gray Park near Clearwater, BC. Each room features en-suite bath, satellite TV, bar fridge, and in-room coffee bar, while a shared kitchen and outdoor BBQ support self-catering guests. The inn is affiliated with BC Backcountry Adventures Ltd. and sits close to Helmcken Falls, Moul Falls, and extensive hiking and mountain biking trails throughout the park.

notes.Laundry: Laundry service offered with sufficient notice for an additional charge

hotel.name: Tofino Swell Lodge
hotel.desc: Tofino Swell Lodge is a three-generation family-run guest house on Olsen Road, operating since 1984, with seven private rooms featuring views of Clayoquot Sound. Guests share a communal living and kitchen area designed for socializing with fellow travellers. The lodge emphasizes immersive coastal experiences including fishing, natural hot springs, and scenic boat tours.

hotel.name: Ponderosa Coach House
hotel.desc: Ponderosa Coach House is a self-catering vacation rental unit perched atop a bluff on a private waterfront estate between Peachland and Summerland, overlooking Okanagan Lake. Bookable through Airbnb and managed by FreedomStay Properties, it sleeps up to three guests in a Queen bedroom plus a double pull-out sofa, with two outdoor decks offering panoramic lake and mountain views. It is part of a larger estate that includes several other rental units and a 300-foot private lakefront.

hotel.name: Ashby House Bed & Breakfast
hotel.desc: Ashby House is a heritage bed and breakfast housed in a 3-story wood-frame Victorian home built in 1899 in Vancouver's West End, and is listed as a heritage site. Marketed as "Vancouver's Funkiest Accommodation," it sits on Bute Street close to the seawall cycling network, English Bay, and the dense dining and grocery options of the West End. The building's late-19th-century character sets it apart from standard urban hotels, making it a distinctive overnight option for visitors exploring the city by bike.

hotel.name: Quartz
hotel.desc: Quartz is one of three Scandinavian-inspired deluxe cottages at Nectar Yoga Retreat, a wellness sanctuary nestled on 20 forested acres on Bowen Island, a 20-minute ferry ride from Horseshoe Bay. The cottage sleeps 1-2 guests and features a covered cedar porch, reading nook, ensuite bathroom with indoor and outdoor shower, and a stay package that includes daily breakfast, yoga, and meditation. Bowen Island itself offers mountain biking, hiking, kayaking, and a tight-knit island community for cyclists exploring the region.

detail.address: 720 Gardner Lane, Bowen Island, BC, V0N 1G2

hotel.name: Squamish Adventure Inn
hotel.desc: Squamish Adventure Inn is a waterfront hostel and hotel-style property in Squamish, BC — Canada's Outdoor Recreation Capital — sitting at the midpoint of the Sea-to-Sky corridor between Vancouver and Whistler. Guests choose from hotel-style rooms with private entrances and ensuite bathrooms, private rooms, dorms, or suites with private kitchens, all sharing a waterfront BBQ patio and a large communal kitchen. The inn offers complimentary cruiser bikes for guests plus on-site rentals of kayaks, bikes, and SUPs, and connects guests with local tour operators at discount rates.

notes.Laundry: Website explicitly lists 'Guest laundry facilities' as a standard amenity

hotel.name: Gage Apartments
hotel.desc: University-operated suite-style accommodation on the UBC campus, surrounded by forests and ocean views on Vancouver's west side. Suites come with full kitchens and the property is pursuing LEED Gold certification with carbon-neutral building operations powered by biomass and hydro electricity. A major bus exchange on campus connects to downtown Vancouver in about 25 minutes.

detail.address: 5959 Student Union Blvd, Vancouver, BC V6T 1K2

notes.Laundry: Laundry facilities available on site

hotel.name: The Wild Turkey Inn
hotel.desc: The Wild Turkey Inn is a restored 1890 Victorian heritage home in Rossland, BC, originally commissioned for the first Bank of Montreal manager in town during the height of the Red Mountain gold rush, and still showcasing eleven-foot ceilings, original fir floors, and period craftsmanship. Offered exclusively as a whole-house private stay for groups and families, it sits three blocks from downtown Rossland and ten minutes from RED Mountain Ski Resort, in a town that has reinvented itself as a Western Canadian hub for skiing and mountain biking. Owner-hosts Shauna and Mike live on site and are available to share local knowledge, making it a characterful and personal base for exploring the Kootenays.

notes.Laundry: Website front page lists 'on-site laundry' as a feature of the inn

hotel.name: Eagle Rock Bed and Breakfast
hotel.desc: Eagle Rock Bed and Breakfast is a small, adult-only luxury retreat in Chemainus, BC, positioned steps from a pebble beach with ocean views along Vancouver Island's coast. It offers two private rooms (a king and a queen) and serves hearty gourmet breakfasts. The property markets itself as a serene, exclusive escape, appealing to cyclists looking for a quieter, upscale overnight stop on the Island.

hotel.name: Gage Suites at UBC
hotel.desc: Gage Suites is a UBC campus accommodation offering studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom self-contained suites available year-round, situated on the sprawling UBC campus roughly 25 minutes from downtown Vancouver by transit. The suites feature full kitchens and laundry facilities, making them well-suited for multi-night touring stays. UBC building operations are carbon neutral with heating and power supplied by biomass generation and hydroelectricity, and select Gage Suites are pursuing LEED Gold certification.

detail.address: 5959 Student Union Blvd, Vancouver, British Columbia V6T 1K2

notes.Laundry: Website lists 'Laundry facilities available' under Gage Suites features

hotel.name: The Lakeside Resort
hotel.desc: A lakefront resort on spring-fed Tuc-el-Nuit Lake in Oliver, BC that has operated since the 1930s. The 5-acre property offers suites, cabanas, and RV/campsites with a 500-foot private beach. They actively promote cycling getaways with wine-touring planning services through the South Okanagan wine country.

notes.Laundry: Laundry facilities listed as a guest amenity in the Guest Information section
notes.Nearby evening food: Dedicated 'Dining Guide' section provided to guests under Guest Information

hotel.name: Oceanfront Suites at Cowichan Bay
hotel.desc: Oceanfront Suites at Cowichan Bay is an all-suite waterfront hotel perched in the seaside village of Cowichan Bay with panoramic views of the bay and Mount Tzouhalem. The property offers spacious one- and two-bedroom suites with full kitchens, an indoor heated pool, hot tub, sauna, and fitness centre. An on-site restaurant, The Cook and Butcher by Cow Cafe, and 24-hour guest services make it a comfortable base for exploring the Cowichan Valley's wine and cycling routes.

detail.address: 1681 Cowichan Bay Rd Cowichan Bay BC V0R 1N0

notes.Nearby evening food: On-site restaurant The Cook and Butcher by Cow Cafe open for lunch and dinner Tuesday–Sunday; in-room dining also available

hotel.name: Snugglers Cottage
hotel.desc: Snugglers Cottage is a self-contained vacation rental house situated in Snug Cove on Bowen Island, a short ferry ride from Horseshoe Bay on BC's Lower Mainland. The island is a popular cycling day-trip and overnight destination, and the cottage offers a private residential-style stay. As an Airbnb listing it operates without on-site staff, with all arrangements handled through the platform and the host remotely.

hotel.name: The Fish & Chicks
hotel.desc: The Fish & Chicks is a glamping cabin retreat in Chilliwack, BC, listed on Airbnb as 'Eco Retreat Cabin 2, The Fish N Chicks,' suggesting at least two cabin units on the property. It is situated in the Fraser Valley and offers a nature-focused cabin experience. The property is booked exclusively through Airbnb with no direct contact channel available.

hotel.name: Knouff Lake Wilderness Resort
hotel.desc: Knouff Lake Wilderness Resort was established in 1904 and is one of the oldest four-season resorts in BC, situated near Kamloops and Sun Peaks. The resort offers rustic log cabins with wood-burning cook stoves, RV and tent camping, and lake-based activities including fishing and paddling. Access is via 14.6 km of dirt road with a gated entry, and there is no cell service on site.

detail.address: 9608 Knouff Lake Road, Heffley Creek, British Columbia V0E 1Z1, Canada

notes.Wi-Fi: Available at the Lodge only with limited data; no cell service on site so guests are advised to enable Wi-Fi calling before arrival

hotel.name: Queen Mary Lake Cabin
hotel.desc: Queen Mary Lake Cabin is a BC Parks wilderness hut situated in Height of the Rockies Provincial Park in the Kootenays region of British Columbia. It offers basic backcountry shelter for those venturing deep into a remote mountain wilderness area. For touring cyclists exploring multi-day routes through the park, this cabin represents one of the few overnight options in the backcountry.

hotel.name: Farm Cabin
hotel.desc: Farm Cabin is a remote wilderness hut in the McGregor Mountains of British Columbia, operated by the Prince George Backcountry Recreation Society and reachable only by a 5 km non-motorized trail that takes 2–6 hours to hike in summer or 4–8 hours to ski/snowshoe in winter. The self-maintained cabin sleeps four and is stocked with a wood stove, firewood, sleeping mattresses, and a propane two-burner stove. Advance bookings are managed online through PGBRS.org up to four months ahead.

hotel.name: Hummingbird Guesthouse & Charters
hotel.desc: Hummingbird Guesthouse is a luxury bed and breakfast situated on the old Howitt Homestead along the banks of the Somass River in Port Alberni, offering four unique suites including one with a full kitchen and living room. Guests enjoy mountain panoramas and river views alongside a gazebo-covered hot tub, games room, and fishing charter excursions. The property is well-positioned for exploring Vancouver Island attractions such as Cathedral Grove, Stamp Falls, and the Pacific Rim National Park.

hotel.name: Green coast
hotel.desc: Green Coast Lodge is a 6-room, 13-acre oceanside property in Lawn Hill on Graham Island, Haida Gwaii, operated by Green Coast Kayaking, which has been running guided Gwaii Haanas kayak expeditions since 1981. Situated directly on Hwy 16 about 20 km north of Skidegate, it offers accommodation styles ranging from private ensuite queen rooms to hostel-style bunks, all sharing kitchen facilities. The property sits steps from the Hecate Strait and includes established forest trails, a creekside setting, and on-site rental bikes for exploring nearby logging roads and scenic highway.

detail.address: 24786 Hwy 16, PO Box 282, Tlell, BC V0T 1S0

notes.Laundry: Website states: 'All units include the use of shared kitchen, common spaces, and laundry.'

hotel.name: All Seasons Roost B&B
hotel.desc: All Seasons Roost B&B is a guest house located on Timberlane Road in the Courtenay-Comox area of Vancouver Island, BC. It is listed in OpenStreetMap as a guest_house under the tourism category, suggesting accommodation for travellers passing through this cycling-friendly region of eastern Vancouver Island.

hotel.name: Beaverfoot Lodge
hotel.desc: Beaverfoot Lodge is a 97-year-old heritage log building nestled between Yoho National Park and Lake Louise, approximately 40 km from the town of Golden in a remote mountain setting. The property offers lodge guest rooms, rustic cabins, and camping and RV sites, and is a cultural heritage landmark of the Golden region. It operates as a boutique resort and events venue, with a focus on wellness retreats, yoga, and sustainable living as part of the broader Eightfold Mountain Village development.

detail.address: 4220 Beaverfoot Rd, Golden, BC V0A 1H0, Canada

hotel.name: Woodcrest
hotel.desc: A family-run bed and breakfast on a one-acre property just 2 km from Clearwater, gateway to Wells Gray Provincial Park. Two accommodation options: a spacious suite sleeping four and a rustic forest cabin sleeping two, both with their own patio, gazebo, and BBQ. The owners partner with Wells Gray Outfitters to offer bike rental packages for exploring the area.

detail.address: 217 Sunshine Valley Road, Clearwater, BC V0E 1N2

notes.Laundry: Both the Woodcrest Suite and Owl's Wing Guesthouse include a washer and dryer
notes.Nearby evening food: Gateway Grill Restaurant and 52 Ridge pub mentioned as nearby dining options

hotel.name: Mountain Thyme Getaway
hotel.desc: Mountain Thyme Getaway is a 1940s Miner's Cottage set in the historic Wells/Barkerville area of the Cariboo, sleeping up to 8 guests in a heritage setting from the gold-rush era. Located along the Barkerville Highway, it sits near Barkerville Historic Town, one of BC's most storied destinations. The property caters to couples, families, and groups seeking an authentic small-town experience in a remote region of the Interior.

notes.Wi-Fi: Stayinwells.ca not fetched to corroborate

hotel.name: Connor Lake Cabin
hotel.desc: Connor Lake Cabin is a BC Parks wilderness hut located in Height of the Rockies Provincial Park in the Kootenays, one of BC's largest and most remote wilderness parks. As a backcountry shelter, it offers touring cyclists a basic overnight refuge deep in the Rockies, well away from road services. The OSM position is noted as approximate, so route-planning should account for some uncertainty in its exact location.

hotel.name: Lakeshore
hotel.desc: Lake Shore is a rustic log chalet within Knouff Lake Wilderness Resort, one of British Columbia's oldest resorts, established in 1904 and situated on a remote lake roughly 45 minutes from Kamloops via a 14.6 km dirt road. The four-season resort offers historic log cabins equipped with cast iron wood cook stoves, plus RV and tent camping, boat rentals, and guided fishing on a lake that holds a North American fly-fishing record. Biking is listed among the summer activity offerings, making it a potential backcountry destination for adventurous touring cyclists.

detail.address: 9608 Knouff Lake Road, Heffley Creek, British Columbia V0E 1Z1, Canada

notes.Wi-Fi: Available at the Lodge only; network name 'Knouff Lake guest'. Limited data — website advises downloading content before arrival

hotel.name: Terra Nostra Guest Ranch
hotel.desc: Terra Nostra Guest Ranch sits on the shores of Clearwater Lake in the remote Chilcotin, accessible off Highway 20 between Williams Lake and Bella Coola near Tweedsmuir Provincial Park. The property offers a range of rustic accommodation from a renovated log saddle cabin to campsites and a wilderness cabin, with a strong focus on horseback riding, backcountry hiking, canoeing, and winter activities including ski touring and heli-skiing. The ranch markets primarily to German-speaking European travellers seeking a wilderness ranch experience far from tourist crowds.

hotel.name: Cedar Song B&B and Cottage
hotel.desc: Cedar Song B&B and Cottage is a custom-built cedar home on 5 forested acres in Errington, between Qualicum Beach and Parksville on central Vancouver Island, offering two en-suite guest rooms and a fully self-contained 1,100 sq ft cottage. Host Anneke Van Vugt is an experienced tour operator and longtime tour guide, well placed to advise guests on the surrounding region. The property sits near hiking trails and the Englishman River, making it a peaceful rural base for cyclists touring the central Island corridor.

notes.Laundry: Guest rooms page states 'Laundry services available'; the cottage has its own washer and dryer

hotel.name: Cahilty Lodge
hotel.desc: Cahilty Lodge is a 168-room condominium-style hotel and the first accommodation built at Sun Peaks Resort, situated centrally in the ski and bike village just steps from shops and restaurants. Rooms range from traditional lodge rooms with two queen beds to spacious three-bedroom suites, all with heated tile bathroom floors. The lodge is well-suited to self-supported touring cyclists with dedicated secure parkade bike storage and coin-operated guest laundry on-site.

detail.address: 3220 Village Way, Sun Peaks, BC V0E 5N0, Canada

notes.Laundry: Fourth-floor guest laundry room with coin-operated washing and drying machines; detergent purchasable from front desk
notes.Nearby evening food: Website states lodge is 'steps away from everything you need in the village' including 'amazing shops and restaurants'; site includes a dedicated Dining section for Sun Peaks Village

hotel.name: Bearberry Meadows
hotel.desc: A handcrafted log-home guest house in the Robson Valley near Tete Jaune Cache, offering two private suites each with en-suite bathroom and kitchenette. Situated between three mountain ranges and just a 10-minute drive from Mt. Robson, the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies. The area offers mountain biking and hiking, and the property can serve as a base for cyclists travelling the Yellowhead Highway corridor.

detail.address: 12190 Crown Road, Tete Jaune Cache, BC

hotel.name: Cougar Mountain Lodge
hotel.desc: Cougar Mountain Lodge & Resort sits outside Valemount in the Robson Valley, surrounded by 360-degree views of the Rocky, Cariboo, and Monashee Mountains. The property offers main lodge rooms and individual mini chalets accommodating groups of one to twelve, with self-catering facilities available. Valemount is an established mountain biking destination, and the lodge explicitly markets mountain bike storage as a service.

hotel.name: Port O'Pierre
hotel.desc: Port O'Pierre is a pet-friendly, rustic cottage in Port Renfrew managed by Handsome Dan Enterprises, sleeping up to 4 guests in a queen bedroom and pull-out sofa, with a gas fireplace, fully equipped kitchen, outdoor BBQ, and wood-burning fire pit. It sits at the edge of the wild southern tip of Vancouver Island, a 10-minute walk from the Pacific Gateway Marina and surrounded by world-class hiking, kayaking, and storm-watching at Botanical Beach and Avatar Grove. An optional adjacent Bunkhouse can extend capacity to 7 guests, making it a practical base for groups or families on multi-day tours.

detail.address: 6574 Baird Rd #1, Port Renfrew, BC V0S 1K0

notes.Nearby evening food: Tomi's Home Cooking is across the street; The Coastal Kitchen Café and The Renfrew Pub are a 10-minute walk away
notes.Nearby grocery: General store offering beer, wine, and other essentials approximately 1 km away on Parkinson Road

hotel.name: Kokanee Glacier Cabin
hotel.desc: Kokanee Glacier Cabin is a remote backcountry alpine hut operated by the Alpine Club of Canada in the Kokanee Glacier area of British Columbia's Kootenay region. With a capacity of 13 guests and a mandatory reservation system, it serves mountaineers and wilderness travelers seeking a basecamp in the Selkirk Mountains. As a classic ACC hut, it offers basic wilderness shelter well beyond road access, making it an adventurous destination for self-sufficient cycle-tourers willing to venture into the alpine.

hotel.name: Victory Cove Seaside Cottages
hotel.desc: Victory Cove Seaside Cottages is a remote wilderness fishing and nature retreat founded in 2017, situated on a float in the sheltered waters of Victory Bay on the Work Channel Inlet in Northwest British Columbia. The property offers a range of accommodations from bunkhouse rooms to nine-person chalets, alongside guest moorage, guided fishing charters, and daily complimentary coffee. The inlet is a rich marine ecosystem frequented by humpback whales, orcas, black bears, and bald eagles, making it a true off-grid basecamp for adventure.

hotel.name: Lake Front
hotel.desc: Knouff Lake Wilderness Resort is one of BC's oldest resorts, established in 1904 on a remote fly-fishing lake about 45 minutes from Kamloops. The resort offers rustic log cabins with cast iron wood cook stoves, RV and tent camping, and lists biking among its summer activities. Access requires 14.6 km on a dirt road with no cell service available on site.

detail.address: 9608 Knouff Lake Road, Heffley Creek, BC V0E 1Z1

notes.Wi-Fi: Available at the Lodge only

hotel.name: Little Bear Garden View B&B
hotel.desc: Little Bear Garden View B&B is a small guest house located on Vancouver Island's Sunshine Coast area at 14 Little Bear Way. It operates under the B&B model, suggesting a hosted, residential-style stay. No further detail about the property, its setting, or its offerings is available from current web evidence.

hotel.name: Whiskey Jack Hostel
hotel.desc: Whiskey Jack Hostel is an HI Canada wilderness hostel set within Yoho National Park in the Canadian Rockies, accessible via Yoho Valley Road near Field, BC. As part of HI Canada's wilderness hostel network, it offers a stripped-back, off-grid overnight experience surrounded by glacial rivers, waterfalls, and dramatic mountain terrain. For touring cyclists on the Trans-Canada Highway corridor, it is a rare opportunity to stay inside a national park in an otherwise very remote and sparsely serviced stretch of road.

hotel.name: Vidette Lake Nature Retreat
hotel.desc: Vidette Lake Nature Retreat is an off-grid wilderness escape on the southern edge of the Cariboo Plateau, occupying the site of a historic gold mine. It offers six distinct rustic cabin accommodations — from the Hudson Bay Cottage to the Box Car Cabin — plus a communal space, with access to 16 lakes, a 200-foot waterfall, and extensive hiking. Reached via 56km of Deadman Vidette Road from Highway 1, this is a genuine backcountry destination that also hosts retreats, spiritual events, and guided tours of the 'Centre of the Universe' vortex.

detail.address: Deadman Vidette Rd, Thompson-Nicola J, BC V0K 2K1, Canada

hotel.name: Misty River Lodge
hotel.desc: Misty River Lodge is a mountain lodge and guest house at the gateway to the Columbia Valley in Radium Hot Springs, BC, framed by the Purcell and Rocky Mountain ranges. It offers several distinct suite types — including a glamping family suite sleeping up to six, a cross suite, and a whitetail suite — each with private bathrooms and varying kitchenette configurations. A shared full kitchen stocked with pots, pans, and utensils is available to all guests, making it a practical base for self-sufficient travelers exploring the Kootenays.

detail.address: 5036 Banff-Windermere Parkway, Radium Hot Springs, BC V0A 1M0

hotel.name: 5th Avenue Bed and Breakfast
hotel.desc: A bed and breakfast located in Port Alberni in the heart of Vancouver Island, BC. The property operates as a small guesthouse with a Facebook presence showing recent activity and a small but engaged following. Port Alberni sits at the head of the Alberni Inlet and is a common stopping point for cyclists crossing Vancouver Island on routes such as Highway 4.

hotel.name: Outdoor Lovers Bed & Breakfast
hotel.desc: Outdoor Lovers Bed & Breakfast is a family-run B&B in Port Alberni overlooking the historic Alberni Inlet, operated by Bill and Milly since 2018 and positioned midway on the Highway 4 corridor between Nanaimo and Tofino. The property offers three distinct rooms with full breakfast (including vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, and lactose-free options), a front balcony with inlet views, and a poolside pergola with koi pond. It sits at the gateway to Stamp River Provincial Park, Cathedral Grove, and day-trip access to Pacific Rim National Park, making it a natural base for cyclists touring Vancouver Island's west coast.

hotel.name: Stone Haven Inn B&B
hotel.desc: Stone Haven Inn B&B is a small, family-owned bed and breakfast located in Valemount, a mountain town on the Yellowhead Highway corridor near Mount Robson Provincial Park — a natural overnight stop for cyclists touring the Yellowhead or headed to or from the Rockies. The property operates primarily through Airbnb and maintains an active, welcoming social media presence. Its rural Sawyer Road location places it slightly outside the village centre.

hotel.name: Tetsa River Lodge
hotel.desc: A three-generation family-run lodge and campground at Historic Mile 375 of the Alaska Highway, Tetsa River Lodge has been welcoming travellers since 1942 and is widely celebrated as the 'Cinnamon Bun Centre of the Galactic Cluster.' Five self-catering rustic cabins, 30 RV sites with power and water, and open tent camping occupy a quiet wilderness setting alongside the Tetsa River. An on-site gift shop and café offers freshly baked cinnamon buns, artisan meats, homemade bread, and daily soup — all made on premises.

notes.Wi-Fi: RV & Campsites page lists 'wifi' among included site amenities; tenting fee also stated to include 'showers & Wifi'

hotel.name: Midgeley Cabin
hotel.desc: Midgeley Cabin is a primitive, unlocked wilderness hut in BC's Kootenays (Creston Valley area), maintained in connection with the Trails for Creston Valley Society trail network. It requires no reservation and is freely accessible to the public, making it a potential emergency or overnight refuge for backcountry cyclists on remote routes. The shelter is truly bare-bones — no mattresses, toilets, running water, or any utility services.

hotel.name: Lake Trail Guesthouse
hotel.desc: Lake Trail Guesthouse is a small guest house located on Lake Trail Road on Vancouver Island, BC. Situated in the Courtenay/Comox area, it sits in a region popular with cyclists exploring the Island's scenic routes and trails. Without website access, specific amenities and character details cannot be confirmed.

hotel.name: Fish Lake Cabin
hotel.desc: Fish Lake Cabin is a fee-based backcountry wilderness hut situated within Top of the World Provincial Park in BC's Kootenay region. It offers remote overnight shelter for adventurers accessing the park's high-elevation terrain. Cyclists considering a stop here should plan for full self-sufficiency, as it is a primitive backcountry structure managed by BC Parks.

hotel.name: Osprey Snowheelers Shelter
hotel.desc: A free, reservation-free wilderness hut in the Okanagan & Thompson backcountry, operated by the Osprey Snowheelers snowmobile club. The shelter features a fireplace but has no drinking water, no mattresses, and no internet. Publicly accessible with no fee, it offers a basic roofed rest point in a remote setting.

hotel.name: Ripple Ridge Cabin
hotel.desc: Ripple Ridge Cabin is a backcountry wilderness hut in the Kootenays, situated within the Ripple Ridge Recreation Site and managed by the volunteer Ripple Ridge Recreation Association in partnership with Recreation Sites and Trails BC. It sits about 3.2 km from the Kootenay Pass parking area and is one of two cabins (the other being Lightning Strike Cabin) located just 50 metres apart at high elevation. Reservation is required and summer access via the Maryland FSR is subject to snow until early July, making this a destination suited to self-sufficient adventure cyclists rather than casual touring.

hotel.name: Great Bear Chalet
hotel.desc: Great Bear Chalet is an intimate, all-inclusive wilderness retreat on the banks of the Atnarko River inside Tweedsmuir Provincial Park, accommodating a maximum of four guests in two private queen-bedroom suites with ensuites. The property operates entirely off-grid and is best known for guided grizzly bear viewing, eco-river drifts, and interpretive hikes through one of BC's most significant salmon and grizzly habitats. Hosts and accredited guides Jefferson and Bindi Bray have been immersing guests in this ecosystem for over 20 years.

detail.address: 8080 Mackenzie Highway, Tweedsmuir Provincial Park, BC V0T 1H0

notes.Laundry: Listed explicitly under 'Included Services' on the Chalet page: 'Laundry service'

hotel.name: Jags Beanstalk
hotel.desc: Jags Beanstalk is a family-run oceanfront guest house in Skidegate on Haida Gwaii, offering 12 thoughtfully appointed rooms with private ensuites, mini kitchens, and — in some rooms — sweeping ocean views. Rooted in community since its origins as a garden shop in 1996, the property pairs comfortable lodging with an attached coffee shop serving 49th Parallel espresso and housemade baked goods, including cinnamon buns guests call worth the trip alone. It sits along BC-16 in Skidegate, making it a natural hub for exploring Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve, old-growth forests, and Haida cultural heritage sites on this remote northern archipelago.

notes.Laundry: FAQ confirms guest-access laundry machines on-site; guests must text staff to have the door unlocked and to receive a laundry soap pod. Access is restricted to a daily window
notes.Nearby grocery: FAQ states: 'the local co-op grocery is just down the road.'
notes.Luggage storage: FAQ explicitly confirms: 'Storage is available for your luggage if you'd like to drop it off prior to check in or if you want to leave it for a week while you explore the Gwaii Haanas!'

hotel.name: Whatshan Lake Retreat
hotel.desc: Whatshan Lake Retreat is listed in OpenStreetMap as a chalet-style accommodation in the Arrow Lakes area of BC's Okanagan & Thompson region. The remote lakeside setting would appeal to touring cyclists seeking off-the-beaten-path lodging. No current business information could be verified due to the domain being compromised.

detail.address: 645 Whatshan Lake Road, Edgewood, BC V0G 1J0

hotel.name: Bill Putnam (Fairy Meadow) Hut
hotel.desc: The Bill Putnam (Fairy Meadow) Hut is an Alpine Club of Canada backcountry hut situated at 2050m elevation in the Selkirk Mountains of British Columbia. It is a fee-based wilderness hut historically used by mountaineers and ski tourers accessing the Fairy Meadow area. Access is remote and non-motorized, making it a niche but potentially adventurous option for backcountry cyclists.

hotel.name: Estuary House B&B
hotel.desc: Estuary House Reflexology B&B sits between Courtenay and Comox on Vancouver Island, with a southern exposure overlooking the Comox Estuary and the Comox Glacier. The property offers queen-sized beds and en suite private bathrooms, with valley farmland to the rear. The inclusion of reflexology services suggests a wellness-oriented hospitality experience for guests.

hotel.name: Mountain Views Cabins
hotel.desc: Mountain View Cabins is a remote, rustic cabin retreat nestled in the Blaeberry Valley about 20 minutes northwest of Golden, BC, surrounded by Rocky Mountain and Selkirk Mountain scenery. The property offers individual cabins (each with two queen beds, heater, and private washroom) as well as budget 'bunkies' with glamping-style amenities including shared kitchen access, BBQs, and a communal fire pit. Guests are encouraged to unplug and enjoy the natural setting, with a viewpoint trail and campfire area on site.

detail.address: 2383 Forde Station Rd, Golden, BC V0A 1H1

hotel.name: Kokanee Chalets RV Park and Campground
hotel.desc: Kokanee Chalets Resort is a 20-acre forested retreat in the Selkirk Mountains on the shores of Kootenay Lake near Crawford Bay, operating for over 50 years. The property offers 16 chalet cabins, 9 hotel-style guest rooms, 53 RV sites, and 17 tenting sites nestled in a signature cedar grove, alongside an onsite bakery and outdoor hot tub. The resort explicitly promotes itself as 'Bike FRIENDLY,' making it an appealing base for cyclists exploring the scenic Kootenay Lake corridor.

detail.address: 15981 Highway 3A, Crawford Bay BC V0B 1E0, Canada

notes.Early or packed breakfast: Onsite Bakery Breakfast listed as a resort amenity on the About page

hotel.name: Mount Washington Chalet
hotel.desc: Mount Washington Chalet is listed as a guest house on Cruikshank Ridge in the Mount Washington Alpine Resort area on Vancouver Island, BC. The resort area is a known ski and outdoor recreation destination, making a chalet-style accommodation plausible. However, the business's website is currently an unconnected Wix domain stub, leaving its current operational status unverifiable.

hotel.name: Radium Chalet
hotel.desc: Radium Chalet is a chalet-style accommodation in the Radium Hot Springs area of the Kootenays, British Columbia. Located on Madsen Road, it sits near the hot springs and the entrance to Kootenay National Park, a region popular with touring cyclists riding the Columbia Valley or Banff-to-Radium routes. No current web presence could be verified to provide further detail.

hotel.name: Elk Lakes Cabin
hotel.desc: Elk Lakes Cabin is a backcountry wilderness hut operated by the Alpine Club of Canada, situated in the Kootenays region of British Columbia near Elk Lakes Provincial Park. It offers mattresses and requires advance reservation, serving as a remote overnight refuge for mountain travellers. Touring cyclists venturing into this high-alpine area would find a staffed-organization-managed hut with basic sleeping infrastructure in a spectacular wilderness setting.

hotel.name: Alouette Cabin
hotel.desc: Alouette Cabin is a fee-based wilderness hut operated by BC Parks within Golden Ears Provincial Park, one of BC's largest and most popular parks located roughly an hour east of Vancouver. The cabin offers basic backcountry shelter with a fireplace and toilets in the park's rugged, mountainous interior. Cyclists considering a stay should note that Golden Ears' backcountry terrain is described by BC Parks as extremely rugged, and no cell service is available in most areas of the park.

hotel.name: Helmcken Falls Lodge
hotel.desc: Helmcken Falls Holiday Resort is a wilderness resort established in 1952 and situated inside Wells Gray Provincial Park, offering log cabins, chalets, heritage rooms, RV sites, and tent camping across 20 acres of forest. Its central location places guests 15–20 minutes from major park attractions including Helmcken, Dawson, and Spahats Falls. An on-site restaurant and lounge, camping store, and friendly front-desk staff make it a self-contained base for multi-day backcountry touring in one of BC's most spectacular parks.

detail.address: 6664 Clearwater Valley Road, Clearwater, BC V0E 1N1

notes.Nearby evening food: On-site Restaurant & Lounge in the 1948 Main Lodge serves breakfast, à la carte dinner, and drinks; seats up to 84 guests indoors and on a covered outdoor deck
notes.Nearby grocery: On-site Camping Store stocks daily essentials, camping gear, firewood, and snacks; limited range, not a full grocery

hotel.name: Chims Motel & Guest House
hotel.desc: Chims Motel & Guest House is an accommodation property on Vancouver Island near Port Alberni, a gateway to the Island's west coast and a potential stop on routes such as the Pacific Marine Circle Route. The property operates a dedicated email address (sleep@chims.ca) and accepts cash, Visa, and Mastercard, consistent with a small owner-operated establishment. No further detail about the property's layout, facilities, or cyclist services could be retrieved from the available website content.

hotel.name: Cornerstones B&B
hotel.desc: Cornerstones is a provincially registered, adult-oriented bed and breakfast in the heart of Qualicum Beach, recognized by TripAdvisor as one of the top 1% of inns and B&Bs worldwide and one of the top 25 in Canada. The property offers three spacious suites with private en-suites, daily full breakfasts using locally sourced ingredients, and a guest lounge with a fireplace and kitchenette. Its central location gives cyclists immediate access to Qualicum Beach's downtown, beach, trail systems, and parks, with 24/7 keyless entry and concierge services including shuttle arrangements to ferry terminals.

detail.address: 166 Harlech Road, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 1G9

hotel.name: Cedar Wood Lodge Bed & Breakfast
hotel.desc: Cedar Wood Lodge is Alberni Valley's self-described only four-star accommodation, offering 8 guestroom suites with private en-suite spa tubs, gas fireplaces, and air conditioning, run by hosts Tom and Marla Housholder who relocated from Utah in 2004 to build the property. Situated on BC Highway 4 in Port Alberni, it serves as a comfortable base for exploring the Alberni Inlet, Harbour Quay, and area trails, with a full continental breakfast buffet and packed lunches available on request. Conference and catering facilities round out a property that blends leisure hospitality with practical amenities.

detail.address: 5895 River Road (BC Hwy 4), Port Alberni, BC V9Y 6Z5

notes.Early or packed breakfast: Website states: 'On request, for a nominal fee, we will prepare a hearty Fisherman's packed lunch to take with you on your daily adventures.'
notes.Nearby evening food: Website states the lodge is 'conveniently located near local restaurants, shopping and golf.'

hotel.name: Swift Creek Cabins
hotel.desc: Swift Creek Cabins are remote backcountry wilderness cabins operated by Headwaters Outfitting near Valemount, BC, sitting in subalpine terrain close to Mount Robson Provincial Park. The self-catered cabins are wood-heated, propane-lit, and designed for small groups pursuing backcountry skiing in winter or alpine hiking in summer. Guests must sign a wilderness release waiver on arrival, reflecting the genuinely remote and rugged nature of the location.

hotel.name: Lake View
hotel.desc: Knouff Lake Wilderness Resort, established in 1904, is one of the oldest resorts in BC, situated on Knouff Lake roughly 45 minutes from Kamloops. The family-run resort offers rustic log cabins with cast iron wood cook stoves, RV/tent camping, and fishing in a lake that holds a North American fly fishing record. Access requires a 14.6 km dirt road off Tod Heffley Louis Creek Road, making it a remote wilderness destination rather than a roadside stop.

detail.address: 9608 Knouff Lake Road, Heffley Creek, British Columbia V0E 1Z1, Canada

notes.Laundry: Laundry room available in the Redwood Cottage only; not a general resort amenity
notes.Wi-Fi: Available at the Lodge only; limited data, no cell service on site

hotel.name: Telegraph Cove Resort
hotel.desc: Telegraph Cove Resort is a historic seasonal destination on the northeast coast of Vancouver Island, built around a restored 1912 sawmill village centred on an 800-foot boardwalk with heritage cabins used as guest accommodation. Founded in 1979, the resort offers houses, cabins, RV and tent camping, a full marina, and was home to British Columbia's first commercial whale-watching operation. A major fire on December 31, 2024 destroyed the restaurant, pub, and several landmark buildings; the resort is rebuilding and welcoming guests again for the 2026 season.

detail.address: 1610 Telegraph Cove Road, Telegraph Cove, BC V0N 3J0

notes.Nearby grocery: The General Store at Telegraph Cove is listed in the resort's own navigation menu as an on-site retail facility

hotel.name: Belle Vue Bed & Breakfast
hotel.desc: Belle Vue Bed & Breakfast is a guest house on Coral Road on Vancouver Island, BC, within the region served by the Island's cycling touring routes. It operates as a small accommodation property in the classic B&B format. Touring cyclists passing through this part of Vancouver Island would find it a potential overnight stop, though specific cyclist-oriented facilities remain unconfirmed.

hotel.name: Mount Robson Lodge
hotel.desc: Mount Robson Lodge is a family-owned cabin resort established in 1978, set 5 km west of the Mount Robson Provincial Park entrance on Yellowhead Highway 16, with direct views of BC's highest peak and a short walk to the Fraser River. Self-contained rustic cabins each sleep up to four guests and include a kitchenette, making the property a practical base for multi-day touring along the Yellowhead corridor. The lodge also operates Mount Robson Whitewater Rafting, so cyclists seeking an adventure rest day have options directly on site.

notes.Nearby evening food: FAQ and cabins pages state Valemount (20-minute drive) and Jasper (1-hour drive) offer several dining options
notes.Nearby grocery: FAQ and cabins pages confirm closest grocery stores are in Valemount (20-minute drive) or Jasper (1-hour drive)

hotel.name: The Log Cabin & Bunkhouse
hotel.desc: The Log Cabin & Bunkhouse is a seasonal retreat on the DeeKayTee Ranch, a family-run working farm in the Comox Valley north of Courtenay on Vancouver Island, operating since 1926. The bunkhouse sits in a forested setting with panoramic mountain views and offers a quiet, private escape on an active beef, poultry, and produce farm. Guests can browse the on-farm market for locally raised meats, eggs, jams, and baked goods.

hotel.name: Royal
hotel.desc: Knouff Lake Wilderness Resort is a historic 4-season resort established in 1904, situated on Knouff Lake about 45 minutes from Kamloops. 'Royal' is one of several rustic log cabins on the property, each equipped with a wood burning cook stove, propane heater, full-size fridge, and electric cook-top. The resort is reached via 14.6 km of dirt road, in a remote wilderness setting focused primarily on fishing and outdoor recreation.

detail.address: 9608 Knouff Lake Road, Heffley Creek, British Columbia V0E 1Z1, Canada

notes.Wi-Fi: Available at the Lodge only; limited data, guests advised to download content before arrival

hotel.name: Lake Side
hotel.desc: Knouff Lake Wilderness Resort is a historic 4-season resort established in 1904, situated on Knouff Lake roughly 45 minutes from Kamloops. 'Lake Side' is one of the resort's small rustic log cabins featuring a cast iron wood cook stove, propane heater, and basic kitchen amenities. The resort is accessed via 14.6 km of dirt road, making it extremely remote and better suited to motorized visitors than touring cyclists.

detail.address: 9608 Knouff Lake Road, Heffley Creek, British Columbia V0E 1Z1, Canada

notes.Wi-Fi: Available at the Lodge only; limited data; no cell service on site so Wi-Fi calling is recommended

hotel.name: Knouff Lake Wilderness Resort
hotel.desc: Lake Wood (Lakewood) is one of several rustic cabins at Knouff Lake Wilderness Resort, a historic 4-season resort established in 1904 on Knouff Lake, about 45 minutes from Kamloops. The small cabin sleeps up to 4 and features a cast iron wood cook stove, propane heater, full-size fridge, and electric cook-top, with a shared bathhouse a short walk away. The resort is remote, accessed via 14.6 km of dirt road, and caters primarily to fishing, boating, and outdoor recreation enthusiasts.

detail.address: 9608 Knouff Lake Road, Heffley Creek, British Columbia V0E 1Z1, Canada

notes.Wi-Fi: Available at the Lodge only, not in cabins

hotel.name: Bella's Beachfront Bed & Breakfast
hotel.desc: Bella's Beachfront B&B is a small, intimate oceanfront guest suite in Comox on the Georgia Strait, offering front-row views of eagles, herons, seals, and cruise ships passing to and from Alaska. The private suite includes direct deck access without entering the main house, a soaker tub, and a kitchenette with microwave and fridge. The Comox Valley puts kayaking, whale watching, and skiing on Mount Washington within easy reach of touring cyclists.

notes.Laundry: Website states: 'Guests may use the laundry facilities upon request.'

hotel.name: High Hopes Bed & Breakfast
hotel.desc: A bed and breakfast perched on Thacker Mountain with panoramic views of the Cascade Mountains and the town of Hope below. The property overlooks Hope Golf and Country Club and is about a 30-minute walk or 5-minute drive from downtown Hope. Each room includes a full hot or continental breakfast and a private deck.

detail.address: 21623 Thacker Mountain Road, Hope, BC, V0X 1L1

notes.Nearby evening food: Hope Golf Club restaurant described as open to the public; B&B overlooks the golf course

hotel.name: Powell Lake Outdoor Learning Center
hotel.desc: An off-grid outdoor learning centre and retreat facility on Powell Lake, at the junction of the Sunshine Coast Trail and the Powell Forest Canoe Route. The centre offers cabin accommodations for up to 60 overnight guests, with catered meals and a wide range of guided outdoor activities including hiking, canoeing, and kayaking. It primarily hosts school groups, weddings, and corporate retreats, though individual adventurers are also welcomed.

detail.address: C/O School District 47, 4351 Ontario Avenue, Powell River, BC V8A 1V3

notes.Early or packed breakfast: Catering team provides three meals a day and can provide trip food and other meals to go, as well as drop meals at adventuring destinations

hotel.name: Rose's Cottage
hotel.desc: Rose Cottage is a small bed-and-breakfast guest house in Valemount, BC, set in the Robson Valley surrounded by the Rocky, Monashee, and Cariboo mountain ranges. It offers three rooms each with a private washroom and an included breakfast, and sits within easy reach of Mount Robson Provincial Park, Jasper National Park, and Valemount's well-regarded mountain biking network. The location makes it a plausible overnight stop on a touring or bikepacking route through the central BC interior.

hotel.name: Hišimy̓awiƛ (5040 Alpine Hut)
hotel.desc: Hišimy̓awiƛ (5040 Alpine Hut) is a backcountry alpine hut on Vancouver Island operated by the Alpine Club of Canada's Vancouver Island Chapter, bearing both its Indigenous name and a reference to the 5040 peak. It sits in remote mountain terrain, making it an unusual and adventurous overnight option for cyclists exploring the island's backcountry. A fee applies for stays, consistent with ACC hut booking practices.

hotel.name: Four Winds B&B
hotel.desc: Four Winds B&B is a small guest house on Saturna Island, one of BC's Southern Gulf Islands, accessible only by ferry or floatplane. Suites include in-room kitchenettes, smart TVs, and ocean views, making it a self-sufficient base for island exploration. A sister property, Sandy Bay B&B, is within walking distance, and the island has a pub, café, and general store nearby.

detail.address: 443 East Point Road, Saturna, B.C. V0N 2Y0, Canada

notes.Nearby evening food: Discover Saturna page lists Saturna Lighthouse Pub, Saturna Cafe at the General Store, and Wild Thyme 'The Bus' Coffee House as local dining options
notes.Nearby grocery: Discover Saturna page lists Saturna General Store & Freight and Saturna Point Store & Marine Services

hotel.name: Hemlock Hut
hotel.desc: Hemlock Hut is a 225 sq. ft. off-grid backcountry ski hut perched at 2,000 m in the Selkirk Mountains outside Revelstoke, operated by Revelstoke Backcountry Guides on a private tenure and reached exclusively by helicopter from Glacier Helicopters. The hut sleeps up to four guests on an exclusive buyout basis and features a wood stove, propane cookstove, solar power, and a custom wood-burning sauna used as a daily ritual after skiing. All trips are fully guided (ACMG) and catered, with guests and guide sharing custodial duties such as hauling water and stoking fires.

notes.Device charging: Website states hut has 'solar power for lights and charging'

hotel.name: Red Goat Lodge
hotel.desc: Red Goat Lodge is a wilderness resort perched alongside Eddontenajon Lake in the remote Iskut Valley of Northern BC, 3 km south of Iskut on the Cassiar Highway. The property offers fully furnished cabins with kitchenettes and private baths, motel-style rooms with in-floor boiler heating, and a lakeside campground with power and water hookups — an unusually complete set of options for this stretch of remote highway. Canoe rentals, shuttle services, and floatplane connections to wilderness canoe routes make it a genuine basecamp in the heart of the northwest BC lakes district.

notes.Laundry: Website (/about.html and /services.html): 'We have showers, laundry and washrooms' in the campground; 'Showers and laundry are accessible.'
notes.Nearby evening food: On-site dining room services available; website states 'Please inquire about bagged lunches and dinner services. Reservations required.' Intended for larger groups but available on-site
notes.Nearby grocery: Website (/services.html): 'Iskut has a small grocery store/post office/gas station' — Iskut is 3 km north of the lodge

hotel.name: Sandy Bay B&B
hotel.desc: Sandy Bay B&B is a small waterfront bed and breakfast on Saturna Island with two rooms featuring ensuite bathrooms, separate entrances, and a private dining and sitting area overlooking a quiet sandy beach. Room #2 includes an adjoining room for families or larger groups. Saturna Island is promoted by its own tourism association as a cycling destination with peaceful, low-traffic roads — making this property a natural base for cycle touring in the Southern Gulf Islands.

detail.address: 449 East Point Road, Saturna Island, BC V0N 2Y0

notes.Nearby evening food: Saturna Café at the General Store (101 Narvaez Bay) serves chef-created dinners, per the tourism directory
notes.Nearby grocery: Saturna General Store & Freight at 101 Narvaez Bay is open every day and stocks groceries, fresh produce, deli, liquor store, and more

hotel.name: Bayview Garden
hotel.desc: Bayview Garden is a small oceanfront guesthouse in K'il Kun - Sandspit on Moresby Island, the only community on Moresby Island and the gateway to Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve. Built around a WWII-era military police building from the Alliford Bay Seaplane base, it offers private rooms in a shared facility with a fully equipped guest kitchen and common lounge areas overlooking Shingle Bay. The owner, Flavien, is himself a cycling enthusiast and manages the local Visitor Centre, making this a well-connected base for exploring Haida Gwaii.

notes.Nearby evening food: Food page lists multiple in-town options: Clubhouse Restaurant and Café (golf course), Beaches Restaurant at Northern Shores Lodging, Raincoast Breads (by reservation), and Shingle Bay Bistro at the airport terminal
notes.Nearby grocery: Website mentions Fresh Mart (formerly Super Valu) local grocery store and K'il Kun Convenience store on School Rd, close to Bayview Garden
notes.Luggage storage: Website states: 'For all our guests going on a tour, we can store your luggage for you, for a fee.' Guest review (2024) confirms: 'For a small fee, we stored our surplus luggage here when we went on our kayak trip.'
notes.Wi-Fi: Website states: 'Wi-Fi is available at the Bayview Garden, at no extra cost.' island data capacity and slow connection speeds are flagged

hotel.name: Glacier View Cabins
hotel.desc: Three self-catering log cabins set in a remote, scenic location 12km south of Atlin with views over glaciers, mountains, and lakes. The property also rents canoes and kayaks for exploring the surrounding waterways. Atlin itself is a tiny historic gold rush town at the end of a spur road off the Alaska Highway, making this a true wilderness destination.

detail.address: Warm Bay Road, Box 368, Atlin, BC V0W 1A0

hotel.name: Creekside Cabin
hotel.desc: Creekside Cabin is a free-use wilderness hut located in the Chilliwack Lake area of BC's Fraser Valley, managed under the BC Parks system. Tagged with a fireplace and no fee, it offers basic backcountry shelter for overnight travellers exploring the S⨱ótsaqel/Chilliwack Lake Park area. As a wilderness hut, it is a primitive but functional overnight option for cycle tourists venturing into this remote provincial park corridor.

hotel.name: Cona Vacation Getaways
hotel.desc: Cona Vacation Getaways is a small family-run vacation rental management company based in the Comox Valley, named after nearby Strathcona Provincial Park. Founded in 2008 as a backpacker's hostel in downtown Courtenay, it has grown to manage a portfolio of ski chalets and lodges concentrated around Mt. Washington. The owners hold backgrounds in eco-tourism and outdoor leadership and describe themselves as passionate outdoor enthusiasts.

notes.Wi-Fi: Policies page lists WiFi among advertised amenities across rental units: 'such as but not limited to WiFi, satellite/cable, hot tubs and saunas'

hotel.name: Chateau Norm
hotel.desc: Chateau Norm Vacation Rentals is a collection of four oceanfront vacation rental units on the remote Haida Gwaii archipelago, situated halfway between the BC Ferries terminal and the Village of Daajing Giids. The property markets itself as an 'adult summer camp' with an oceanfront hot tub, beach access, fossil hunting, and a large fenced yard stocked with outdoor games. Guests can borrow e-bicycles, a canoe, a kayak, or a paddleboard — all gear included — making it a practical and adventurous base for exploring this culturally significant and geographically isolated coastline.

detail.address: 4112 Oceanview Drive, Daajing Giids, BC, Canada V0T1S0

notes.Laundry: Website amenities list explicitly states 'fluff and fold laundry service.'

hotel.name: Knouff Lake Wilderness Resort
hotel.desc: Knouff Lake Wilderness Resort is one of British Columbia's oldest resorts, established in 1904 and running year-round on a remote lake roughly 45 minutes from Kamloops. The resort offers historic log cabins with cast-iron wood cook stoves alongside RV and tent campsites, set within a wilderness landscape that supports fishing, hiking, and biking. Access requires 14.6 km of unpaved dirt road from Knouff Lake Road, making this a genuinely off-the-beaten-path destination for self-sufficient adventurers.

detail.address: 9608 Knouff Lake Road, Heffley Creek, British Columbia V0E 1Z1, Canada

notes.Laundry: Laundry room available in The Redwood Cottage only
notes.Wi-Fi: Available at the Lodge only, under network 'Knouff Lake guest'; resort explicitly notes limited data and advises downloading content before arrival

hotel.name: Klippers Guest Suites
hotel.desc: Klippers Guest Suites are spacious, self-contained three-bedroom units on a working certified organic farm in Cawston, BC's Similkameen Valley, with each suite offering a private entrance, full kitchen, and scenic farmland views. The property is part of a larger agri-tourism destination that includes the Row Fourteen farm-to-table restaurant, Untangled Craft Cider, and a CSA operation, and guests can request fresh organic produce brought directly to their suite. It sits within easy reach of Okanagan and Similkameen wine-route cycling, with popular destinations like Osoyoos, Penticton, and Naramata nearby.

notes.Nearby evening food: Row Fourteen restaurant is on-site at Klippers Organics; reservations mentioned on website

hotel.name: Mount Washington Hostel
hotel.desc: Mount Washington Hostel is a hostel located on Vancouver Island, BC, in a mixed-use building at 275 8th Street. As a hostel it would typically offer budget accommodation well-suited to cycle tourists passing through the region. No further detail could be confirmed due to website unavailability.

hotel.name: The Artists Point B&B
hotel.desc: A two-suite B&B set on 2.3 acres in the rural Hyde Creek community near Port McNeill, offering sweeping ocean views of Broughton Strait and a three-minute walk to a wildlife-rich beach frequented by orcas, eagles, and dolphins. The property is run exclusively by Rolf Hicker, an award-winning professional wildlife and nature photographer with over 35 years of experience, who offers private custom photo tours — grizzly watching, whale watching, Cape Scott — available only to his guests. It sits at the gateway to the Broughton Archipelago and is within easy reach of Telegraph Cove and Port Hardy.

hotel.name: Copper Beech House Inn
hotel.desc: Copper Beech House is a heritage inn in Masset on the north coast of Haida Gwaii, set in a historic 1914 house overlooking Delkatla Inlet and managed by Canadian poet and writer Susan Musgrave. The property is celebrated for its eccentric literary character—walls hung with Haida art and bookshelves stocked by celebrated guests including Margaret Atwood, David Suzuki, and Douglas Coupland. It has been featured in Vogue and National Geographic, making it one of the most distinctive and storied places to stay in remote British Columbia.

hotel.name: Stafford House B&B
hotel.desc: Stafford House B&B is a guest house on Vancouver Island or the Gulf Islands region of British Columbia, listed in OSM with a Stafford Avenue address. No website content was retrievable, so specific details about the property's character or offerings are unavailable. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it worth contacting directly to confirm availability and any bike-friendly arrangements.

hotel.name: Eagle Bluff B&B
hotel.desc: Eagle Bluff Bed & Breakfast is a waterfront B&B established in 1990 in Prince Rupert's historic Cow Bay district, offering six uniquely appointed guest rooms and harbour and mountain views from a signature western cedar oceanside deck. An on-site chef-manager prepares a full home-cooked breakfast served in a second-floor dining room overlooking the ocean. Situated at the northern BC ferry terminal connecting to Haida Gwaii and the Alaska Marine Highway, it is a natural staging point for cyclists making long-haul coastal connections.

detail.address: 201 Cow Bay Road, Prince Rupert, BC V8J 1K4

notes.Nearby evening food: About page states the Cow Bay district has 'coffee shops, restaurants, and a neighbourhood pub' within the immediate area

hotel.name: Nemiah Valley Lodge
hotel.desc: Nemiah Valley Lodge is an Indigenous-owned, off-grid wilderness retreat operated by the Xeni Gwet'in community of the Tŝilhqot'in Nation, set among the mountains and lakes of BC's remote Chilcotin region. The lodge offers modern log cabin lodging alongside all-inclusive adventure and wellness packages featuring guided hiking, fishing, and equine programs rooted in Xeni culture. Its extreme remoteness—accessible by a single road into Nemiah Valley—makes it a rare destination-class stop in an otherwise very sparse stretch of Central Interior BC.

hotel.name: Guesthouse at Crowsnest Vineyards
hotel.desc: The Guesthouse at Crowsnest Vineyards is a family-run 3-star, 7-room bed and breakfast set among the vineyards and orchards of the Similkameen Valley, right on the Crowsnest Highway #3 just south of Cawston. A continental breakfast of fruits, breads, charcuterie, and coffee is included with each stay, and guests have access to an on-site restaurant, winery, tasting bar, and bakery. The rural vineyard setting and views from above the orchard make it a distinctive and self-contained stop for anyone cycling the Similkameen.

notes.Nearby evening food: On-site restaurant serving lunch and dinner; open seasonally with full dinner service

hotel.name: Copper Fern Guest House
hotel.desc: Copper Fern Guest House is a self-contained 780 sq. ft. suite on a private lane just five minutes from downtown Courtenay in the Comox Valley on Vancouver Island. Hosts Chris and Molly are long-time local residents who greet guests with homemade muffins, granola, and fresh eggs and can point cyclists toward favourite trails, beaches, and restaurants. The suite is designed to be wheelchair accessible and sleeps up to four, offering a quiet garden retreat away from traffic.

notes.Laundry: Dedicated laundry room listed as part of the 780 sq. ft. suite

hotel.name: Mount Washington Guest House
hotel.desc: Mt. Washington Guesthouse is a self-catering vacation rental property managed by Cona Vacation Getaways, a family-run boutique company operating multiple chalets and lodges near Mount Washington Alpine Resort on Vancouver Island. The company was founded by two avid outdoor enthusiasts with a background in eco-tourism and began as a backpacker's hostel in Courtenay before expanding into vacation rental management. The Mount Washington area offers both alpine and Nordic terrain and is a destination for mountain biking, making this rental a possible base for cycle-touring or trail riders.

hotel.name: Berkie's Bed and Breakfast
hotel.desc: Berkie's is a licensed bed and breakfast in Port Alberni hosted by Bob and Yvonne Rogers, who emphasize home cooking and personalized hospitality in a residential setting. Port Alberni sits at the mid-island crossroads for cyclists heading to Tofino and Ucluelet (1.5 hours away) and serves as a base for exploring the salmon-rich Alberni Valley, Stamp Falls, Della Falls, and the Frances Barkley cruise through Barkley Sound. The property is within walking distance of Save-On Foods, a liquor store, a pharmacy, and other everyday conveniences.

detail.address: 3835 7th Avenue, Port Alberni, British Columbia, Canada V9Y 4P1

notes.Nearby grocery: Front page lists Save-On Foods within driving or walking distance; 'What We Offer' page also cites 'Grocery Stores' among nearby amenities

hotel.name: Char's Landing
hotel.desc: A hostel and guesthouse housed in a beautifully converted 1912 Methodist church in Port Alberni's Uptown Art District. The venue doubles as a live music hall that hosts over 100 touring musicians per year, giving overnight guests a unique cultural experience. Accommodation ranges from shared dorm-style bunk rooms to a private 1000-square-foot guesthouse suite, all with keypad self-check-in.

notes.Laundry: Shared kitchen & laundry for hostel guests; private kitchen & laundry in the guesthouse suite
notes.Luggage storage: Accommodations page states they accommodate luggage drop-offs for early/late check-in; 3 lockers available first come first served

hotel.name: Kye Bay Bed & Breakfast
hotel.desc: Kye Bay BnB is a quiet seaside bed and breakfast near Comox on Vancouver Island, offering three individually themed private suites—Starfish Cove, Driftwood Cove, and Beachcombers Cove—each with its own private locked entrance and full ensuite bathroom. The property sits a 2–3 minute walk from a wildlife-rich beach and is a 10-minute drive from the town of Comox, making it a tranquil base for exploring the Comox Valley. Guests receive a full hot home-cooked breakfast served on the garden patio or in-room, with food allergy accommodations available.

detail.address: 1549 Kye Bay Road, Comox, BC V9M 3T7

hotel.name: Stone Tree Cottage
hotel.desc: Stone Tree Cottage is a private, self-catered 750 sq ft vacation cottage in Courtenay's Comox Valley, set within one acre of owner-cultivated botanical gardens that back onto a 20-acre nature park with walking trails. The fenced and gated property offers genuine seclusion, with two bedrooms and a fully equipped kitchen for self-sufficient stays. It sits minutes from downtown Courtenay, making it a quiet base from which to explore the wider Comox Valley by bike.

detail.address: 2271 Lake Trail Road, Courtenay, BC V9N 9C3

hotel.name: Royston House B&B
hotel.desc: Royston House B&B is a carriage-house loft suite set on 2+ park-like acres in the seaside community of Royston, just outside Courtenay on Vancouver Island. The property fronts directly onto the Royston Waterfront Trail along Comox Bay, and is recognised as a Canadian Wildlife Certified Backyard Habitat with woodlands, ponds, and deer trails. Guests stay in a self-contained suite with a private entrance and covered ocean-view deck, and breakfast is served in a glass-enclosed plant solarium.

hotel.name: Coquihalla Lakes Lodge
hotel.location: Remote & backcountry, Vancouver, Coast and Mountains
hotel.community: Remote & backcountry, Vancouver, Coast and Mountains
hotel.desc: Coquihalla Lakes Lodge is a self-catered wilderness cabin resort set at 1200m in the Cascade Mountains, halfway between Hope and Merritt on the Coquihalla Highway. The property borders Coquihalla Summit Park and Crown land, with lakeside cabins sleeping up to 8 people. Offered activities include mountain biking, hiking, boating, fishing, and ATV riding, making it a base for multi-sport backcountry trips.

detail.address: 35600 Coquihalla Lakes Rd, Hwy 5 Exit 228, Merritt, BC V1K 1B8

hotel.name: Frog Hollow Emergency Shelter
hotel.desc: Frog Hollow Emergency Shelter is a free, publicly accessible wilderness cabin in the Manning Provincial Park area of British Columbia, operated by the Summit Seekers Snowmobile Club. As an unstaffed emergency shelter, it provides basic refuge for backcountry travelers caught in difficult conditions. Touring cyclists traversing remote routes in the Okanagan highlands may find it a useful last-resort overnight option.

hotel.name: Salsbury House Bed & Breakfast
hotel.desc: Salsbury House Bed & Breakfast is a guest house located on Vancouver Island, BC, tagged in OpenStreetMap as a tourism guest_house. It sits in the Comox Valley region, an area popular with touring cyclists travelling the Island. No further details about the property, its rooms, or its amenities are available from the current evidence.

hotel.name: Mount 7 Lodges
hotel.desc: Mount 7 Lodges is a collection of three private luxury wilderness chalets perched above Golden, BC, offering 360-degree views of the Canadian Rockies and Purcell Mountains. The property sits near Kicking Horse Mountain Resort in one of BC's premier outdoor adventure towns, making it a natural base for exploring the region. Each self-contained lodge sleeps between two and eight guests, with one lodge (Red Fox) designed to universal accessibility standards.

hotel.name: Copes' Islander Bed & Breakfast
hotel.desc: Copes' Islander is a family-run oceanfront B&B on the Comox Peninsula of Vancouver Island, operated by hosts Mike and Patti since 1996, with direct beach access and sweeping views of the ocean and Coast Mountains. The property sits minutes from the Comox (Little River) BC Ferries terminal, making it a convenient stop for cyclists travelling between Vancouver Island and the Sunshine Coast. Patti's elaborately prepared breakfasts are a noted highlight of the stay.

hotel.name: Johnson Yew and Arbutus Cabins
hotel.desc: The Johnson Yew and Arbutus Cabins are two adjoining modern log cabins opened in 2009 at Loon Lake Lodge & Retreat Centre, a UBC-operated wilderness retreat facility nestled in the Malcolm Knapp Research Forest roughly 50 km east of Vancouver. Together the cabins sleep up to 48 guests in shared bunkroom-style rooms, each with a writing desk and WiFi, and both buildings are connected on the ground floor with lounge areas and fireplaces. The broader Loon Lake property offers hiking, waterfront activities, sauna, and on-site dining, making it a full-service but group-oriented destination.

detail.address: 14500 Silver Valley Road, Maple Ridge, BC V4R 2R3

hotel.name: Bella Coola Eagle Lodge
hotel.desc: A luxury wilderness lodge in Bella Coola on BC's Central Coast, nestled between the Coastal Mountains within the Great Bear Rainforest. The property offers 10 spacious guest rooms with mountain views and private bathrooms, plus a common area with complimentary coffee and tea. A rare full-service accommodation option for cyclists reaching the end of Highway 20.

hotel.name: McMurdo Cabin
hotel.desc: McMurdo Cabin is a rustic backcountry wilderness hut in the Northern Purcell Mountains, one of five remote huts maintained by the Columbia Valley Hut Society, a non-profit founded in 1983. The area around the cabin offers wildlife viewing, high country travel in summer, and ski touring in winter. Access requires backcountry travel with variable hiking distances depending on route-finding and seasonal road conditions.

hotel.name: Scott Duncan Hut
hotel.desc: Scott Duncan Hut is an Alpine Club of Canada backcountry wilderness hut situated at 2682 metres elevation in British Columbia, making it one of the higher-elevation ACC huts in the region. Operated by the ACC and requiring a fee, it serves as a base for mountaineering and alpine objectives in a remote setting. Touring cyclists who venture into this terrain would find basic backcountry shelter in an exceptional mountain environment.

hotel.name: Days Inn by Wyndham Victoria Uptown
hotel.desc: A Days Inn by Wyndham franchise hotel located in Victoria's Uptown area along Gorge Road East, part of one of North America's largest economy hotel chains.
