notes.Early or packed breakfast: Website states 'Start your day right with our complimentary breakfast' and 'Start your day with our complimentary breakfast, fueling up for whatever adventures lie ahead.'
notes.Nearby evening food: Onsite restaurant open Tue–Sun until 9pm and onsite George's Pub open Tue–Sat, both on the property
notes.Nearby grocery: Website notes 'proximity to gas stations, grocery stores, and convenient shopping options' in the surrounding area

hotel.name: Holiday Inn Express Fort St John
hotel.desc: A Holiday Inn Express hotel in Fort St John, BC, providing standard midrange accommodation in a 3-level property. Suitable as a rest stop for touring cyclists passing through Northern BC.

hotel.name: Friendship Motel
hotel.desc: Friendship Inn Motel & RV Park is a combination motel and RV park located along the Island Highway in Campbell River, BC. The property offers both motel rooms and RV accommodation, and sits near beaches and hiking trails in the Campbell River area. It serves both short-stay road-trippers and longer-term guests, with an RV component that suggests basic outdoor infrastructure on site.

hotel.name: Vagabond Lodge
hotel.desc: Vagabond Lodge is an exclusive boutique inn perched steps from the gondola at Kicking Horse Mountain Resort, about 10 minutes from Golden, BC, in the heart of the Canadian Rockies. The property is known for its cozy character — river rock fireplace, split-log bar, Douglas fir floors, and floor-to-ceiling mountain views — along with warm, host-led hospitality and a communal living-room atmosphere. Summer guests are well-placed for mountain biking and hiking, with easy access to Yoho, Banff, Kootenay, and Glacier National Parks.

hotel.name: Sandman Inn McBride
hotel.desc: A hotel located in McBride, a small village on the Yellowhead Highway (Hwy 16) between Prince George and Jasper in the Robson Valley. McBride is a common overnight stop for touring cyclists riding across northern BC, and this property is part of the Sandman Hotels chain. The hotel sits along the frontage road just off the highway.

hotel.name: Pinewood Inn
hotel.desc: The Pinewood Inn is a small, owner-operated 8-unit motel at the north end of Golden, BC, offering 1- and 2-bedroom kitchen suites equipped with modern appliances and designed for stays of any length. Golden sits at the confluence of the Kicking Horse and Columbia Rivers, making it a natural hub for cyclists tackling the Rocky Mountains or the Columbia Valley route. The hands-on ownership style and fully equipped kitchens give the property a self-sufficient, home-like character well suited to touring travellers.

hotel.name: Shannon Motel
hotel.desc: Shannon Motel is a 3-star, approximately 60-room property situated along the Alaska Highway in Fort Nelson, a key waypoint for cyclists traversing northern British Columbia. Rooms include kitchenette or full kitchen options, making it well-suited for touring cyclists who need to cook or resupply. The motel is pet-friendly, offers ample parking including space for RVs and large vehicles, and is steps from the Fort Nelson Heritage Museum and recreation centre.

detail.address: 5423 50th Avenue S, Fort Nelson, BC, Canada

hotel.name: Green Gables Beach Resort
hotel.desc: Green Gables Beach Resort is a family-run lakeside motel on Osoyoos Lake operating since 1975, known for its private sandy beach considered one of the finest on the lake and a loyal multigenerational guest following. Located in Osoyoos—Canada's only desert region—the resort is steps from shops, restaurants, and the town centre, making it a convenient base for cyclists exploring the Okanagan wine country and surrounding trails. The property has an old-school character appreciated by guests who return for the personalized service from on-site managers.

notes.Laundry: Listed as 'Laundry' in the resort amenities section on both the rooms overview and individual room subpages
notes.Nearby evening food: Website lists nearby dining partners: Bear Fish, Root Berry, Campo Marina, Sage Pub, Junction 3, Barn Owl Eatery

hotel.name: Leland Hotel
hotel.desc: A hotel serving the Nakusp community in British Columbia's Kootenays region. Offers Wi-Fi connectivity for guests.

hotel.name: Royston Retreat
hotel.desc: Royston Retreat is a self-catering apartment accommodation located on Marine Drive in Royston, a small community on the east coast of Vancouver Island between Courtenay and Campbell River. The area sits along a popular cycling corridor on Vancouver Island and is close to the waterfront. As an apartment-style rental, guests typically have access to private, home-like amenities rather than shared hotel facilities.

hotel.name: Takysie Lake Resort
hotel.desc: Takysie Lake Resort is a secluded, family-run lakeside retreat in BC's Central Interior, sitting on a 514-hectare rainbow trout lake whose name means 'lake of many fishes.' The resort offers rustic lakeside cabins, RV and tent sites, a boat launch, guest docks, and floatplane docking, making it a self-contained base camp for fishing, paddling, and exploring the remote Southside backroads. On-site amenities include a café, general market, hardware store, 24-hour pay-at-pump gas station, and a mechanic shop — an unusually full-service stop for such a remote location.

detail.address: 37530 Eakin Settlement Road, Burns Lake BC

notes.Nearby evening food: On-site Takysie Café serves comfort food; open most days including weekends starting at 9am
notes.Nearby grocery: On-site Takysie Market Store open daily 9am–9pm; website says 'stock up on supplies.'

hotel.name: Hospitality Inn
hotel.desc: A hotel located in Port Alberni, British Columbia, providing overnight accommodation for travelers and tourists. Cyclists can contact the hotel directly to arrange lodging and discuss bike storage options.

hotel.name: Bobbie Burns Lodge
hotel.desc: Bobbie Burns Lodge is a legendary backcountry heli-skiing lodge in the Kootenays operated by Canadian Mountain Holidays, famous for massive peak-to-valley vertical runs and a fast-paced, expert-focused atmosphere. One of the original heli-skiing lodges in British Columbia, it is accessible only by helicopter as part of a booked CMH program. In summer it serves as a base for guided heli-accessed hiking in remote alpine terrain.

hotel.name: Highliner Hotel & Conference Centre
hotel.desc: The Highliner Hotel & Conference Centre is a newly renovated 17-storey high-rise occupying a prominent position in downtown Prince Rupert, with 97 guest rooms and sweeping ocean views. It sits minutes from both the BC Ferry and Alaska Ferry terminals, making it a natural staging point for cyclists arriving on or departing to Vancouver Island, Haida Gwaii, or Alaska. An on-site restaurant, First Avenue Bistro, serves the local community as well as hotel guests.

detail.address: 815 1st Avenue West, Prince Rupert, BC V8J 1B3

notes.Laundry: Self-serve guest laundry facilities (coin operated); dry cleaning send-out service also available
notes.Early or packed breakfast: Free Continental Breakfast included for all stays

hotel.name: Green View Motel and RV Park
hotel.desc: Green View Motel & RV Park sits on Highway 3, one kilometre east of Greenwood — reputedly Canada's smallest city — making it a practical overnight stop for cyclists on the Southern Trans-Canada route. The property offers renovated motel rooms with kitchenettes and family units alongside a full-service RV park with pull-through sites (60+ ft), tent camping, water/sewer hookups, and 30-amp electrical service. It is open year-round and accepts multiple payment methods including Interac.

detail.address: 256 n Copper Ave, Greenwood, BC, VOH 1JO, Canada

hotel.name: Spirit Ridge Vineyard Resort & Spa
hotel.desc: Spirit Ridge Vineyard Resort & Spa is a Hyatt Unbound Collection property situated among the vineyards and desert landscape of the Okanagan near Osoyoos, BC. The resort offers a full-service spa and overlooks Osoyoos Lake in one of Canada's warmest and driest regions, making it a notable destination stop for cyclists touring the South Okanagan wine country. Rancher Creek Road places it at the edge of a working vineyard estate.

hotel.name: Motel Tyrol
hotel.desc: Motel Tyrol is a family-owned motel in the Village of Radium Hot Springs, situated in the Columbia Valley between the Rocky and Purcell Mountains along Highway 93/the Banff-Windermere Parkway. The property is 2 km from the famous natural mineral hot springs pool and offers mountain views from every room, plus its own year-round swim spa and seasonal heated outdoor pool and hot tub. Guests receive a complimentary breakfast voucher to Screamers Cafe, 800 m away, and the Juniper Trail trailhead is a five-minute walk from the motel.

detail.address: 5016 Highway 93, Radium Hot Springs, BC V0A 1M0

notes.Nearby evening food: About page states 'Short walk to local restaurants.'

hotel.name: Prestige Harbourfront Resort, BW Premier Collection
hotel.desc: The Prestige Harbourfront Resort is Salmon Arm's only resort situated directly on Shuswap Lake, with views of the Columbia Mountains and waterfront access. It operates as a WorldHotels Luxury property under the BWH Hotels umbrella, drawing visitors for events like the Roots & Blues Festival and lakeside weddings. Touring cyclists finishing a day on the Shuswap routes will find a full-service resort experience in a notable scenic setting.

detail.address: 251 Harbourfront Drive NE, Salmon Arm, BC V1E 2W7

hotel.name: Super 8 by Wyndham Golden
hotel.desc: Super 8 by Wyndham Golden is a roadside motel situated directly on the Trans-Canada Highway in Golden, BC, a hub town for cyclists travelling through the Rocky Mountain Trench between Yoho and Glacier national parks. As part of the Super 8 by Wyndham brand it offers standardised budget accommodation in a location that sees heavy touring-cyclist traffic on the TransCanada corridor. The motel is well-positioned for resupply and rest between the challenging mountain passes on either side of Golden.

hotel.name: Colonial 900 Motel
hotel.desc: Colonial 900 Motel is a motel located on Old Hope Princeton Way in British Columbia's Lower Mainland & Fraser Valley region. Specific amenities and policies for cyclists are not available online; contact the motel directly for information about bike storage and facilities.

hotel.name: Copper Point Resort
hotel.desc: Copper Point Resort is Invermere's premier upscale destination in the Columbia Valley, offering accommodations ranging from standard queen rooms to two-bedroom loft suites. The resort serves as a four-season base with access to golf, skiing at nearby Kootenay Rockies resorts, and outdoor adventures — making it a comfortable stopping point for touring cyclists on routes through the Columbia Valley. On-site dining, a spa, and full event facilities give it a full-service resort character.

notes.Laundry: In-suite washer and dryer listed for One Bedroom Suite and One Bedroom Loft Suite on the rooms page; likely available in larger suites as well
notes.Nearby evening food: Resort has an on-site restaurant and dining facility listed prominently in navigation and homepage ('Restaurant & Dining')

hotel.name: Houston Motor Inn
hotel.desc: Houston Motor Inn is a family-run motel on the Yellowhead Highway (Hwy 16) in Houston, BC, operating since 1993. The two-storey property offers basic rooms alongside an on-site restaurant, making it a practical overnight stop on one of northern BC's main touring corridors. Pet-friendly policies and an RV area reflect its orientation toward travellers passing through the region.

detail.address: 2940 Yellowhead 16 W, Houston, British Columbia V0J 1Z1

notes.Laundry: Listed as 'Public laundry' in the motel amenities on the /services page
notes.Nearby evening food: On-site restaurant confirmed on front page: 'We also feature a restaurant that serves delicious food.'

hotel.name: Inn On Canyon
hotel.desc: Inn On Canyon is a family-owned boutique hotel in the heart of Radium Hot Springs, operating from a 10,000-square-foot Victorian-style building just 200 metres from the famous Radium Hot Springs pools. The age-restricted property (12+) serves a warm homestyle breakfast each morning in a shared dining room and is ideally placed at the gateway to Kootenay National Park, with the Columbia Valley's extensive biking trail network — including Panorama Mountain Resort, Kloosifier-Johnson, and Sinclair Creek trails — easily accessible. Pubs, restaurants, and trails are all within walking distance, and Banff is a scenic one-hour drive north on Highway 93.

detail.address: 7557 Canyon Ave., Radium Hot Springs, B.C, V0A 1M0

notes.Early or packed breakfast: Warm homestyle breakfast (hot or cold, with coffee, juice, tea, spreads and jams) served each morning in the common room; customer review states 'early morning breakfast makes it easy to get a jumpstart to the day.'
notes.Nearby evening food: About page states 'pubs, restaurants and trails all within walking distance.'

hotel.name: Westridge Motor Inn
hotel.desc: The Westridge Motor Inn is a fully renovated 32-room motel sitting at the junction of Highway 3 (Crowsnest Highway) and Highway 97 in Osoyoos, at the heart of Canada's warmest desert. It offers a range of room types from courtyard queens to king suites with new Serta mattresses, kitchenettes in all suites, and a seasonal outdoor pool and BBQ patio. Located directly across from the Osoyoos Visitor Information Centre, it is a natural stop for cyclists riding the Crowsnest route through the South Okanagan wine country.

notes.Laundry: Complimentary guest laundry available for all guests, per /motel-information page

hotel.name: Crest Hotel
hotel.desc: A hotel in the North Coast region of British Columbia. The business can be reached by phone and email. Website content could not be verified to confirm specific amenities and services for touring cyclists.

hotel.name: Ocean Trails Resort
hotel.desc: Ocean Trails Resort is a 78-unit self-contained condo resort spread across seven wooded acres immediately adjacent to Rathtrevor Beach in Parksville, rated #1 specialty lodging in Parksville on TripAdvisor. Suites range from one to three bedrooms and come with fully equipped kitchens, private entrances, and free parking, making extended stays practical. The surrounding Parksville–Qualicum Beach region offers cycling-friendly terrain including beach trails, provincial parks, and routes toward Englishman River Falls and Mount Arrowsmith.

hotel.name: Northway Motor Inn
hotel.desc: The Northway Motor Inn is a 43-room motor inn in Dease Lake sitting along the Stewart-Cassiar Highway (Hwy 37), one of only two BC routes leading to the Yukon and Alaska — making it a key resupply and rest stop for cyclists tackling this remote corridor. The hotel serves as a practical base for the surrounding wilderness, including the Stikine River country and Cassiar Mountains. The Info & Tips page offers unusually candid travel advice for the highway, including the complete absence of cell service between Kitwanga and the Alaska Highway Junction.

detail.address: 81 Boulder Avenue, Dease Lake, BC V0C 1L0

notes.Laundry: Listed under Services as 'Guest laundry *fees apply'
notes.Nearby evening food: Info & Tips page lists 'Take-out restaurants *seasonal hours' in Dease Lake; on-site pizzeria is listed but noted as '*currently closed'
notes.Nearby grocery: Info & Tips page lists 'Grocery store' under 'WHAT'S IN DEASE LAKE?'

hotel.name: Travelodge
hotel.desc: A Travelodge by Wyndham situated directly on the Trans-Canada Highway in Salmon Arm, a key stop in the Shuswap region for cyclists travelling between Vancouver and the Rockies. As a highway motor hotel, it offers straightforward roadside accommodation in a town with reasonable access to services. Salmon Arm sits roughly midway along the Trans-Canada corridor, making it a natural overnight break for loaded touring cyclists.

hotel.name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott Salmon Arm
hotel.desc: A Fairfield Inn & Suites hotel in Salmon Arm offering standard chain hotel accommodations along the Trans-Canada Highway route. Specific cyclist amenities could not be verified due to website access issues.

hotel.name: Bell 2 Lodge
hotel.desc: Bell 2 Lodge is a full-service wilderness resort perched on the Stewart-Cassiar Highway (Hwy 37) at kilometer mark 248, making it one of the very few services stops on the long haul between Meziadin Junction and Dease Lake for cyclists riding the Alaska Highway corridor. The property offers log chalet rooms, camping, an on-site cafe serving homemade soups and sandwiches, and fuel (gasoline, diesel, propane) — essentially a self-contained oasis in a stretch with no cell service. In winter the lodge doubles as the base for Last Frontier Heliskiing, considered the largest single heliski area on the planet.

detail.address: Highway 37, Kilometer 248, Northern BC (96km North of Meziadin Junction)

hotel.name: Comox Valley Inn & Suites
hotel.desc: The Comox Valley Inn & Suites is a centrally located motel in downtown Courtenay on Vancouver Island, offering a wide range of room types from single-bed units to multi-bed kitchen suites sleeping up to six, with a pet-friendly policy for dogs. The property sits within a 10-minute walk of more than eight restaurants, bistros, pubs, the Puntledge River trail, and a beer and wine store, making it a practical overnight base for cyclists touring the Comox Valley. The website notes a forthcoming redesign but the business is clearly operational.

detail.address: 1190 Cliffe Avenue, Courtenay, British Columbia V9N 2K1

notes.Laundry: Website lists 'Laundry – coin-operated washers and dryers' as an on-site facility
notes.Nearby evening food: Website states 'More than 8 restaurants,' 'Bistros and pubs,' and 'Dairy Queen' are all within a 10-minute walk
notes.Wi-Fi: Website lists 'FREE Internet access' and 'Wi-Fi' as included with every room at no extra charge

hotel.name: Trend Mountain Hotel & Conference Centre
hotel.desc: Trend Mountain Hotel & Conference Centre is a full-service hotel and conference facility located in the Northern BC community near the Rocky Mountain foothills. It would serve as a logical overnight stop for touring cyclists on routes through the Peace River region. The property appears to offer standard hotel amenities, though details could not be confirmed from the website.

hotel.name: Sun Peaks Lodge
hotel.desc: Sun Peaks Lodge is a full-service mountain hotel situated in the heart of Sun Peaks Resort village, offering traditional rooms and studios with kitchenettes steps from the chairlift with ski-in/ski-out access. The lodge features an on-site steakhouse, a Swiss-style Fondue Stube, and a wellness area with hot tub, sauna, and steam room. It also offers a bike rental service on-site and sits within easy reach of the resort's biking and hiking trails, making it a practical base for cycling tourism in the Thompson-Okanagan region.

detail.address: 3180 Creekside Way, Sun Peaks, BC V0E 5N0

notes.Nearby evening food: On-site Steakhouse and Fondue Stube; website also describes the village as having 'charming shops and delectable restaurants lining the streets'

hotel.name: Canyon Alpine Motel
hotel.desc: Canyon Alpine Motel is a roadside motel located on the Trans-Canada Highway in the Okanagan & Thompson region of British Columbia. Its highway-side position makes it a potential overnight stop for cyclists travelling the corridor. Current operational status cannot be confirmed as the motel's website domain appears to have been taken over by an unrelated third party.

hotel.name: The Bayside Inn
hotel.desc: A hotel located on Fir Street in the Vancouver Island & Gulf Islands region. Without access to the website, specific amenities and cyclist-specific facilities cannot be confirmed.

hotel.name: Hacas Inn
hotel.desc: Hacas Inn (Ḥačas, meaning 'place of high ground') is Bamfield's only motel, situated on the east shore of Bamfield Inlet and owned and operated by the Huu-ay-aht First Nations. The renovated property — formerly the Bamfield Motel — offers a range of rooms from standard twins to full kitchenette suites, making it a practical base for cyclists tackling the nearby West Coast Trail or exploring the Pacific Rim coast. The village setting puts guests steps from a historic boardwalk with a pub, café, general stores, and boat moorage.

notes.Nearby evening food: Malsit Public House and The Café are listed as nearby Huu-ay-aht-operated businesses; the community description also references a restaurant accessible via the village boardwalk
notes.Nearby grocery: 'The Market' is listed as a nearby Huu-ay-aht Group of Businesses location; the community description also references 'general stores' on the boardwalk
notes.Luggage storage: Policies page states: 'Bag Check – We will watch your bag for you should you check out and wish to explore.'

hotel.name: Caravan Inn
hotel.desc: A motel accommodation in the Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior region. Limited details about specific cyclist amenities and services are publicly available.

hotel.name: Travelodge
hotel.desc: The Travelodge by Wyndham Hope is a branded chain hotel situated on Old Hope-Princeton Way in Hope, BC, a gateway town at the confluence of the Fraser and Coquihalla rivers and a natural rest stop on several major touring routes. As part of the Wyndham portfolio it offers standard hotel amenities in a convenient highway location. Touring cyclists passing through on the Kettle Valley Railway route or the Trans Canada corridor would find it a straightforward overnight option in an otherwise limited accommodation landscape.

hotel.name: The View Hotel
hotel.desc: The View Hotel is a 62-room property opened in 2013 on the shores of Stuart Lake in Fort St. James, described on its own website as the first and only hotel in the area. Rooms range from classic queens to spacious kitchenette suites with lake views, and the hotel sits within minutes of Fort St. James National Historic Site and the Murray Ridge Ski Area. An on-site restaurant and pet-friendly policy make it a practical full-service stop for touring cyclists moving through Central BC's Cariboo-Chilcotin corridor.

detail.address: 309 Stuart Drive West, Fort St. James, BC V0J 1P0

notes.Nearby evening food: On-site restaurant listed in the hotel's own summary: '62 Rooms – Kitchenettes – Pet Friendly – On Site Restaurant'

hotel.name: CMH Galena
hotel.desc: CMH Galena is a 34-room hotel in the Kootenays, part of Canadian Mountain Holidays' lodge network. Located in a mountainous region, it provides accommodation for visitors to the area.

hotel.name: Super 8 by Wyndham Quesnel BC
hotel.desc: Super 8 by Wyndham is a budget hotel chain property situated on Valhalla Road in Quesnel, a service hub in BC's Cariboo region. It offers a predictable roadside overnight stop for touring cyclists moving through central BC, with direct booking available through the Wyndham Rewards loyalty program. As a franchise property, amenities may vary from brand standards and are not detailed on the corporate website for this location.

hotel.name: Black Bear Resort
hotel.desc: Black Bear Resort is a cedar-clad hotel and cabin resort on the northern tip of Vancouver Island, offering 40 ocean-view guest rooms and 11 cabins overlooking Port McNeill harbour, Malcolm Island, and the BC coastal mountains. The property sits on the fringe of a natural rainforest and is within easy reach of the town centre, BC Ferries connections to Alert Bay and Sointula, and access to the Broughton Archipelago. It is well positioned as a base for cyclists exploring northern Vancouver Island's coastal communities.

detail.address: 1812 Campbell Way, Port McNeill, BC V0N 2R0

notes.Laundry: Coin-operated washing machine and dryer available to resort guests (facilities page)
notes.Early or packed breakfast: Complimentary continental breakfast included with all accommodation (policies page)
notes.Nearby evening food: Front page states the hotel is 'handy to various restaurants' in Port McNeill
notes.Luggage storage: Facilities page states: 'We have a storage room for the exclusive use of our guests.'

hotel.name: Rodway Heritage Hotel
hotel.desc: The Rodmay Heritage Hotel (listed in OSM as 'Rodway') is a heritage-style hotel located in Powell River, BC, a community on the Sunshine Coast accessible by ferry and popular with cyclists riding the Sunshine Coast Trail region. As a heritage property it likely occupies a historic building, offering a sense of place that larger chain hotels lack. Touring cyclists passing through Powell River on multi-day routes would find it a convenient overnight base.

hotel.name: Park Motel
hotel.desc: Park Motel is a freshly renovated motel in Hope, BC, offering rooms and suites ranging from standard singles to family suites sleeping up to six guests. Situated minutes from downtown Hope and close to Coquihalla Canyon Provincial Park, it serves as a convenient base for exploring the Fraser Canyon area. The property is pet-friendly and non-smoking, with complimentary on-site parking including accessible spaces.

hotel.name: Fernie Slopeside Lodge
hotel.desc: Fernie Slopeside Lodge sits at the base of Fernie Alpine Resort, offering true ski-in access just a two-minute walk from the lifts and one minute from the resort plaza. Accommodation ranges from cozy Standard Rooms with kitchenettes to a full Alpine Suite sleeping up to 10, catering to groups and families. Located 5 km from the town of Fernie, it serves as a practical base for exploring the Elk Valley in both winter and summer.

detail.address: 5368 Ski Hill Road, Fernie, BC V0B 1M6

notes.Laundry: Free guest laundry listed under Comfort & Convenience on the amenities page
notes.Nearby evening food: Griz Bar, Cirque Restaurant, Legends Restaurant, and the Slopeside Deli are all within the resort plaza, described as a one-minute walk from the lodge
notes.Nearby grocery: Mountain Pantry & Liquor Store is located next door to the lodge, carrying groceries, snacks, beer, wine, spirits, and a Starbucks coffee bar
notes.Vending machines: Vending machines available on site, listed under Common Spaces on the amenities page

hotel.name: Bon Voyage Inn
hotel.desc: The Bon Voyage Inn is a family-friendly motel on the Yellowhead Highway (Highway 16 West) at the western edge of Prince George, offering room types ranging from twin and queen rooms to family suites and a Jacuzzi suite, as well as adjoining rooms for groups of up to six. The property sits within the Bon Voyage Plaza, putting an on-site restaurant, laundry, and retail stores steps from the guest rooms. Pet-friendly rooms, winter vehicle plug-ins, and on-site RV power and water hookups make it a practical overnight stop on the Yellowhead corridor.

notes.Laundry: Laundry available in the adjacent Bon Voyage Plaza: 'Just outside your door there are restaurants, laundry, and stores.'
notes.Nearby evening food: Adjoining Bon Voyage Restaurant on site; additional restaurants in the Bon Voyage Plaza immediately adjacent

hotel.name: Sea Raven Motel
hotel.desc: Sea Raven Motel is the largest accommodation in Daajing Giids (Queen Charlotte) on Haida Gwaii, offering 30 rooms including ocean-view suites overlooking Skidegate Inlet. It sits within walking distance of local facilities and serves as a practical base for exploring the remote archipelago, including Gwaii Haanas National Park, wildlife watching, and kayaking. Pet-friendly ground-floor rooms are available for cyclists traveling with animals.

detail.address: 3301 Oceanview Drive, Queen Charlotte, BC V0T 1S0

hotel.name: Sportsman's Inn On The Harbour Front
hotel.desc: Sportsman's Inn On The Harbour Front is Port McNeill's only harbour-front hotel, with every room overlooking the Port McNeill Harbour. The property lists three affiliated restaurants as a guest amenity, and all rooms include a fridge, microwave, coffee maker, and work desk. It sits at the waterfront end of Beach Drive, making it a straightforward destination for cyclists arriving via the Island Highway corridor.

detail.address: 1597 Beach Drive, Port McNeill, BC V0N 2R0

notes.Nearby evening food: Amenities page lists '3 affiliated restaurants' as a hotel service

hotel.name: Overlook Inn & Cabins
hotel.desc: Overlook Cabin is a motel-style accommodation located on Clearwater Village Road, near the gateway to Wells Gray Provincial Park in the Cariboo-Chilcotin region. The property appears to offer cabin-style lodging in a small village setting convenient for cyclists traveling through central British Columbia.

hotel.name: Sandman Hotel Abbotsford Airport
hotel.desc: The Sandman Hotel Abbotsford Airport is a full-service chain hotel situated adjacent to Abbotsford International Airport (YXX), offering rooms and suites with fridges, microwaves, and in some cases full kitchens. The property features an indoor pool, fitness centre, on-site Denny's Restaurant and Bar One Lounge, and a 24-hour front desk. It has earned Silver Certification from GreenStep Solutions under Global Sustainable Tourism Council standards, reflecting a documented commitment to environmental practices.

notes.Nearby evening food: Denny's Restaurant and Bar One Lounge both listed as on-site dining options
notes.Device charging: USB Charging Ports listed as a room feature in the Grand Room description

hotel.name: Evergreen Motel
hotel.desc: A family-owned and operated motel in Princeton, BC, nestled in the Similkameen Valley along Hwy 3 (the Crowsnest Highway). The 20-room property sits near the junction of the Tulameen and Similkameen Rivers, with convenient access to the Trans Canada Trail and local mountain biking trails. Amenities like a heated pool, continental breakfast, and pet-friendly rooms make it a practical overnight stop for touring cyclists passing through the region.

notes.Laundry: Complimentary Commercial Laundry Service for Teams, Groups etc. listed under amenities
notes.Early or packed breakfast: Free Continental Breakfast listed under amenities

hotel.name: Sandman Hotel Terrace
hotel.desc: Sandman Hotel Terrace is a full-service chain hotel on the Yellowhead Highway in Terrace, BC, offering an indoor pool, fitness centre, and an on-site Denny's restaurant with room service. The property has earned Silver Certification from GreenStep Solutions under Global Sustainable Tourism Council standards, reflecting an active sustainability program. All room types include a fridge, microwave, and free parking, making it a practical base for touring cyclists passing through the Skeena region.

notes.Nearby evening food: On-site Denny's restaurant with room service, confirmed on amenities page and individual room pages

hotel.name: Comfort Inn & Suites
hotel.desc: Comfort Inn & Suites is a mid-range hotel chain operating a location in Langley. As a Choice Hotels International property, it provides the standardized accommodations and service expected from the brand. This is a familiar, established lodging option for touring cyclists.

hotel.name: Super 8
hotel.desc: Super 8 by Wyndham is a national motel chain property located in Fort Nelson, BC, a remote community on the Alaska Highway in the Northern Rockies. Fort Nelson sits at a key waypoint for cyclists riding the Alaska Highway corridor — one of the most dramatic and isolated touring routes in North America. As one of the few accommodation options in town, this motel serves as a practical base for long-distance riders covering significant mileage between services.

hotel.name: Royal Lodge Motel
hotel.desc: Royal Lodge Motel is a clean, affordable motel in Hope, BC, positioned at the convergence of Highways 1, 3, 5, and 7 — making it a natural overnight stop for cyclists on any of the major interior routes. The property offers king, queen, double, and triple rooms with in-room fridges and microwaves. Hope's trailhead access and highway crossroads position make this a practical base for touring cyclists passing between the coast and the BC interior.

hotel.name: Sandman Signature
hotel.desc: Sandman Signature Prince George is a full-service hotel offering a wide range of room types from standard kings to two-level loft suites and jacuzzi suites, many with kitchenettes. The property features an indoor pool, fitness centre, 24-hour front desk, and the on-site Rockford Grill restaurant. It holds GreenStep sustainability certification and is pet-friendly, making it a practical base for touring cyclists passing through central BC.

notes.Laundry: Coin-Operated Laundry listed in the amenities subpage
notes.Nearby evening food: On-site Rockford Grill restaurant listed in amenities; Denny's and Moxie's also referenced as redemption venues in hotel deals

hotel.name: Bear Claw Lodge
hotel.desc: A hotel in Kispiox Valley, a remote area of Northern BC. Website access is currently unavailable, preventing verification of amenities and services for touring cyclists.

hotel.name: The Lodge Motor Inn
hotel.desc: The Lodge Motor Inn is a 40-room motel centrally located in Dawson Creek on the Alaska Highway, a primary northern BC cycling corridor, offering 24-hour check-in and wheelchair-accessible rooms. The property is part of a small family-run chain with locations in Dawson Creek and Grande Prairie, known for clean, quiet rooms and friendly service. An on-site café operates in the same building, though its current status is unclear from the website.

detail.address: 1317 Alaska Avenue, Dawson Creek, BC V1G 1Z4

hotel.name: Fairmont Hot Springs Resort
hotel.desc: Fairmont Hot Springs Resort is a large, full-service mountain resort in BC's Columbia Valley, anchored by Canada's largest natural hot springs with a daily flow of over 1.2 million gallons. It offers a wide range of accommodations — from main lodge rooms and a motel-style Juniper Lodge to cabins, villas, an RV resort, and a riverside campground — along with two golf courses and a full spa. Touring cyclists arriving after a long day in the Rockies will find hot mineral pools, multiple on-site restaurants, and a fitness centre, making it a notably comfortable overnight stop.

notes.Laundry: Mountainside Villas include in-suite laundry; not mentioned for other accommodation types
notes.Nearby evening food: On-site dining includes Antlers Restaurant, Desperados, and Sundance Cafe, all referenced on the resort website
notes.Wi-Fi: RV Resort page advertises 'unlimited free basic Wi-Fi in your sites and throughout the public areas of the resort'; Mountainside Villas listing also explicitly includes WiFi

hotel.name: Port Renfrew Hotel
hotel.desc: Wild Renfrew is a resort complex on the southwest tip of Vancouver Island offering waterfront cottages, forest domes, and a renovated 20-suite lodge — all positioned as a basecamp for the West Coast Trail and Juan de Fuca Marine Trail. The property includes an on-site pub and saunas, making it one of the more complete hospitality options in this remote stretch of coast. Accommodation ranges from dog-friendly beachfront cottages with fire pits to geodesic domes with private hot tubs.

notes.Nearby evening food: Renfrew Pub is listed as an on-site venue in the Wild Renfrew navigation menu ('Renfrew pub')

hotel.name: Camelot Court Motel
hotel.desc: A motel with WiFi access. Operational status and cyclist-specific amenities cannot be verified due to a non-functional website.

hotel.name: Best Western Sicamous Inn
hotel.desc: The Best Western Sicamous Inn sits on the Trans-Canada Highway in Sicamous, a gateway town known as the Houseboat Capital of Canada, with Shuswap Lake and Mara Lake just minutes away. The property has earned the TripAdvisor Award of Excellence and offers pet-friendly rooms with kitchenette options and jetted tubs. The Shuswap region surrounding Sicamous provides year-round outdoor recreation, making this a natural overnight stop for cyclists on the Trans-Canada corridor.

notes.Early or packed breakfast: Page-level amenity tags include 'free-breakfast', indicating complimentary breakfast is offered

hotel.name: Travelodge by Wyndham Parksville
hotel.desc: The Travelodge by Wyndham Parksville sits on the West Island Highway in Parksville, a seaside town on Vancouver Island's east coast popular with cyclists riding the Island route. As a national chain property, it offers predictable overnight accommodation in a well-serviced community with restaurants and shops nearby. Touring cyclists passing through the Parksville-Qualicum Beach corridor would find it a convenient overnight stop on a multi-day island tour.

hotel.name: Cross River Wilderness Centre
hotel.desc: Cross River Wilderness Centre is a remote cabin-based retreat in the Kootenays offering accommodation alongside outdoor recreation and education programs. The centre appears to provide meals on-site, making it a potentially self-contained stopover for touring cyclists venturing into this mountainous wilderness. Its blend of cabin lodging, guided activities, and education programs suggests a destination-style experience rather than a simple pass-through stop.

hotel.name: Travellers Inn
hotel.desc: Travellers Inn is a motel in Dawson Creek, the 'Mile 0' city of the Alaska Highway in northeastern BC, making it a natural stopping point for cyclists heading north or completing long-distance tours. The property offers air-conditioned rooms with private bathrooms, a shared lounge, and a mini market on site. Rotary Lake and Kiskatinaw Provincial Park are nearby for those wanting to extend their outdoor experience.

notes.Laundry: Listed as 'Loundry Srvice' (sic) in main facilities section of aggregator site
notes.Early or packed breakfast: Website states 'Offering a daily breakfast'
notes.Nearby grocery: On-site mini market described: 'Mini market is also on site for those looking to stock up on snacks or drinks'

hotel.name: Travelodge by Wyndham Quesnel
hotel.desc: The Travelodge by Wyndham Quesnel is a national chain hotel situated on Front Street in Quesnel, a regional service hub in BC's Cariboo region along the Gold Rush Trail corridor. As a Travelodge property it offers standard roadside hotel amenities and participates in the Wyndham Rewards loyalty program. Touring cyclists passing through the Cariboo will find it a convenient overnight stop in a town with good access to supplies and services.

notes.Wi-Fi: Not explicitly confirmed by website content (corporate portal only)

hotel.name: Edgewater Motel
hotel.desc: Edge Water Motel is a roadside motel situated on South Island Highway on Vancouver Island, BC. Its waterfront-suggestive name places it along a coastal or lakeside stretch of the Island's main touring route, a corridor frequently travelled by cycle tourists. No further details about the property are available from accessible sources.

hotel.name: Tree To Me Inn
hotel.desc: Tree to Me Inn is a rustic-refined organic farm inn on a 40-acre property in the Similkameen Valley near Keremeos, offering five appointed guest suites with mountain and farm views. An on-site bistro and farm market serve organic produce, fresh-baked goods, and cooked meals through the week, making it a genuine stop rather than just a bed. The property sits a short drive from Apex Mountain Resort and is close to BC wine country, hiking, and the nearby lakes and rivers of the region.

notes.Nearby evening food: On-site bistro serves dinner Tuesday through Saturday until 8pm
notes.Nearby grocery: On-site market sells organic farm produce, condiments, breads, take-away meals, soups, and locally sourced products

hotel.name: Brookside Motel
hotel.desc: Brookside Motel is a cabin-style property in Golden, BC, offering individual self-contained units with full kitchens, mountain views, and air conditioning. Golden sits at the gateway to six national parks—including Yoho, Banff, and Kootenay—and is home to Kicking Horse Mountain Resort, a notable summer mountain-biking destination. Fast-food, gas stations, and restaurants are within walking distance, making it a practical stopover for touring cyclists passing through the Columbia Valley.

notes.Nearby evening food: Website states '5 minutes from... restaurants and bars' and 'fast-food restaurants... within walking distance.'
notes.Nearby grocery: Website states '5 minutes from grocery stores.'

hotel.name: Green Coast Lodge
hotel.desc: Green Coast Lodge is a 5-room hotel on Highway 16 in Haida Gwaii. The business appears connected to kayaking services based on its email domain (gckayaking.com). Located in a remote, ferry-accessible coastal area, it provides lodging for travelers to the North Coast region.

hotel.name: Lost Horse Motel
hotel.desc: Lost Horse Motel is a motel in the Okanagan & Thompson region of British Columbia serving travelers passing through the area.

hotel.name: Y5 Motel & Campground
hotel.desc: Y-5 Motel & Campground Ltd has been serving travellers in Barriere, BC since 1998, offering 22 motel units (1- or 2-bedroom, some with kitchenettes) alongside pull-through campground facilities. Situated on the Southern Yellowhead Highway in south-central BC, it sits amid forest-covered mountains with access to hiking, fishing, kayaking, and rafting, and is a short drive from Sun Peaks Resort and Wells Gray Park. The property welcomes work crews, tourists, and extended-stay guests, with a restaurant immediately next door.

detail.address: 4325 Southern Yellowhead Hwy, Barriere, BC V0E 1E0

notes.Nearby evening food: Website states 'There is a restaurant located right next door to our motel' and notes the property is 'within walking distance of different restaurants.'

hotel.name: Adventure Domes
hotel.desc: Adventure Domes is listed in OSM as a hotel accommodation in the Kootenays region of British Columbia, situated at 620 6th Avenue. The 'domes' name suggests distinctive geodesic or dome-style lodging structures, which would make it a memorable overnight stop for touring cyclists passing through the region. No further detail about the property or its facilities could be confirmed as the business website is currently a parked domain.

hotel.name: Wells Hotel
hotel.desc: The Wells Hotel is a heritage country inn that has anchored the small gold-rush town of Wells, BC since 1934, operating as the primary accommodation provider in the area. It sits at the gateway to Barkerville Historic Town, Bowron Lakes Canoe Chain, and Troll Ski Resort, making it a natural overnight stop for touring cyclists exploring the Cariboo region. The hotel features 13 guest rooms, a rooftop hot tub, and an on-site pub and restaurant notable for BC craft beer and one of the largest single-malt Scotch collections in Western Canada.

notes.Nearby evening food: On-site pub, lounge, and restaurant on the main floor with seasonal patios

hotel.name: Prestige Hudson Bay Lodge Premier Collection
hotel.desc: Prestige Hudson Bay Lodge & Conference Centre is a full-service hotel situated on the Yellowhead Highway (Hwy 16) in Smithers, BC, surrounded by mountain views. The property offers a variety of rooms and suites including new kitchenette units, a recently renovated lobby, fitness room, and convention facilities. It sits minutes from downtown Smithers shops and restaurants, making it a convenient base for touring cyclists passing through the Bulkley Valley.

detail.address: 3251 E Highway 16, Smithers, British Columbia V0J 2N0

hotel.name: Invermere Inn & Suites
hotel.desc: A hotel in the heart of downtown Invermere, part of the INNhotels chain, with an onsite restaurant (Begginnings) serving breakfast, brunch, and lunch with locally sourced ingredients. The location puts guests steps from Kinsmen Beach, the Invermere Farmer's Market, and downtown shops, making it a convenient base for exploring the Columbia Valley. Pet-friendly ground-floor rooms are available by request.

detail.address: 1310-7th Ave, Box 1080, Invermere, BC V0A 1K0, Canada

notes.Early or packed breakfast: Breakfast To-Go bag explicitly offered for early departures; includes fresh fruit, granola bar, yogurt, muffin, and fruit juice; can be ordered in advance or requested at the front desk
notes.Nearby evening food: Website lists Restaurants & Cafes within 30 steps of the hotel

campground.name: Pierre's Point Campground
campground.desc: Large 208-site commercial campground on Shuswap Lake, 6 km west of Salmon Arm off the Trans-Canada, with lake swimming and a pine-forest setting managed by Adams Lake Indian Band; open seasonally to mid-September.

detail.address: 2569 Campground Rd, Salmon Arm, BC V1E 3A2

campground.name: Pass Creek Regional Park
campground.desc: A regional district campground along Pass Creek near the small community of Crescent Valley in the West Kootenay, offering a creek-side setting as a handy overnight on the Slocan Valley corridor. Amenity details are sparse from available sources, so verify facilities before arriving.

campground.name: Gold Mountain RV Park and Cabins
campground.desc: A family-run riverside resort on Highway 3 west of Hedley, with direct Similkameen River access for tubing, fishing, and kayaking, plus a short hike to a historic gold mine; flush washrooms and a store add comfort, but at $47/night for a campsite this skews toward resort pricing for cycle tourists.

campground.name: Sunnyside Campground
campground.desc: A large, full-service family campground on the shores of clear Cultus Lake, 100 km from Vancouver, with waterfront and view tent sites, flush washrooms, and free hot showers, all within walking distance of beaches, restaurants, and a waterpark; expect crowds throughout summer.

detail.address: 3395 Columbia Valley Highway, Cultus Lake, V2R 5A3

campground.name: Pirates Cove Campsite (BCMT)
campground.desc: A boat-in marine campsite on De Courcy Island in the Gulf Islands, set in a sheltered cove steeped in the lore of the infamous Brother Twelve; cyclists must arrange water transport as there is no road access whatsoever.

campground.name: Mountainaire Campground & RV Park
campground.desc: Mountainaire is a family-oriented 40-acre campground and RV park set in Vancouver Island wilderness between Ladysmith and Nanaimo, offering tenting, full/partial-service RV sites, glamping units, and cabins. It sits about 5 km from the Trans-Canada Highway and roughly 20 minutes from both Nanaimo ferry terminals (Duke Point and Departure Bay), making it a natural start or end point for island touring routes. A short rainforest trail leads to the Nanaimo River's Crystal Bowl swimming hole, and the park hosts a convenience store, arcade, and regular family events.

campground.name: Peach Orchard Campground
campground.desc: A municipal campground on Okanagan Lake's shore in Summerland with showers, potable water, and flush washrooms — a solid amenity-rich stop on the Okanagan cycling corridor, busiest in peak summer.

campground.name: Kamloops RV Park
campground.desc: RV-only park on the Trans-Canada highway east of Kamloops, directly beside BC Wildlife Park with guest discount admission; full-hookup sites cater to self-contained rigs, and no tent rate is listed, making it a marginal option for cycle tourers.

campground.name: Jones Lake Main Recreation Area
campground.desc: A free BC Hydro recreation site on a mountain reservoir above Chilliwack, offering basic camping with washrooms in a quiet backcountry setting; access is via a gravel forest service road that is rideable but rough for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Oxbow RV Resort
campground.desc: A tidy, well-maintained RV resort directly across from Skaha Lake in central Penticton, with flush washrooms, coin showers, and walking distance to beaches, a splash park, and marina; primarily serviced RV sites with no tent-specific option confirmed.

campground.name: Group Campground
campground.desc: Kokanee Creek Park's dedicated group campsite anchors a flagship Kootenay provincial park with over a kilometre of sandy lake beach, old-growth cedar, and a Kokanee Creek canyon trail; group bookings carry a minimum charge equivalent to 15 adults.

campground.name: Sandstone Campground
campground.desc: A campground in the Chemainus area of Vancouver Island; no page content was retrievable from the linked URL (Dionisio Point Provincial Park, Galiano Island), so details on setting, amenities, and access remain unconfirmed.

campground.name: Blackfoot Regional Park Campground
campground.desc: A regional park campground along the Peace River near Clayhurst, offering river views, forest trails, and wildlife; bring all your own water as none is available on site, and expect no cell service.

campground.name: Wya Point Resort Campground
campground.desc: A Ucluelet First Nation resort on 600 acres of old-growth coastal rainforest, offering oceanside and sheltered woodland tent sites a short walk from secluded private beaches; flush toilets and showers on site, but advance online reservation is required and no walk-up camping.

campground.name: Holiday Park Four Season RV & Condo Resort
campground.desc: A large four-season RV-and-condo resort community between Kelowna and Vernon with resort-level amenities including a restaurant, pool, and 24/7 security; the Okanagan Rail Trail runs directly alongside the property, making it a convenient corridor stop for touring cyclists, though accommodation is primarily RV sites and condos rather than tent pitches.

campground.name: Norbury Lake Campground
campground.desc: A BC Parks campground fronting Norbury and Peckham's lakes with sandy beach areas, non-motorized boating, rainbow trout fishing, and a dramatic backdrop of The Steeples in the Hughes Range; gate closes outside the operating season.

campground.name: Marble Canyon Campground
campground.desc: Frontcountry campground in Kootenay National Park on Highway 93, sitting near the narrow turquoise Marble Canyon limestone gorge and its short suspension-bridge trail. A national park entry pass and camping permit are required; reservations open in January and summer sites fill quickly.

campground.name: Bench Campground
campground.desc: Bench Campground in Sasquatch Provincial Park offers easy paved access 6 km off Highway 7 near Harrison Hot Springs, set among pocket lakes and birch forest with sandy beaches and warm summer swimming on Hicks and Deer lakes; swimmer's itch is occasionally reported.

campground.name: Kitwanga River RV Campground
campground.desc: A privately-run riverside campground sitting directly on the Kitwanga River, right off the Cassiar Highway (Hwy 37), with the class 2 steelhead and salmon river flowing through the property and full amenities including showers, laundry, and device charging — a rare resupply on a remote northern corridor.

campground.name: Wolf Lake Group Campsite
campground.desc: Small reservation-only group site tucked beside Wolf Lake, with a dock for swimming and fishing; dry camping with no potable water and a single outhouse, so come self-sufficient.

campground.name: Sidney Spit Group Campsite
campground.desc: Boat- or kayak-in group campsite at the north end of Sidney Island in Gulf Islands National Park Reserve, with sandy beaches, wooded trails, and abundant birdlife and marine life; inaccessible to loaded touring cyclists without a boat.

campground.name: Valhalla Pines Campground
campground.desc: Valhalla Pines is a six-acre forested campground near Vallican in the Slocan Valley, offering private huts, RV sites, and tent sites set among fir and pine forest with mountain and river surroundings. Host Tom is a local guide who provides hands-on recommendations for cycling, hiking, swimming holes, and paddling the Slocan River, making it a natural base for Kootenay adventure. The campground sits on the Frog Peak Loop route with no cell coverage on the approach road but excellent on-site Wi-Fi, giving it a genuinely off-grid character.

campground.name: Toquart Bay Campground
campground.desc: Toquaht Nation-operated campground on Barkley Sound, the primary land base for kayaking and boating the world-famous Broken Group Islands; open May–September with $55/night tent sites, a playground, and a paved pump track, but no RV hookups and no cell service on site.

detail.address: Toquaht Bay, Ucluelet, BC V0R 3A0, Canada

campground.name: Fairmont Hot Springs RV Resort
campground.desc: Full-service RV resort in the Columbia Valley with included discounted access to Fairmont's natural mineral hot springs pools; blacktop pull-through sites with full hook-ups, resort amenities, and a $10/day resort experience fee on top of site rates.

detail.address: 5225 Fairmont Resort Road, Fairmont Hot Springs, V0B 1L1

campground.name: Squawkum Park Campground
campground.desc: A campground on the outskirts of Chilliwack in the Fraser Valley; details are sparse as the operator website was unreachable, so confirm conditions before arriving.

campground.name: Alice Lake Campground
campground.desc: A popular family park near Squamish with four freshwater lakes, sandy beaches, and dramatic mountain backdrop; demand is intense July–September so reserve well ahead — the park fills even on weekdays.

campground.name: Pine Point Campground
campground.desc: A 60-site campground at Lake Cowichan on Vancouver Island, likely suited to a lakeside rest day or straightforward overnight; basic facilities and caravan-site character keep it functional rather than polished.

campground.name: Camperland Bridal Falls RV Resort & Cabins
campground.desc: A large, full-service RV resort at the base of Mt. Cheam in the Fraser Valley, directly off the Trans-Canada Highway and steps from Bridal Veil Falls Provincial Park; amenities run to heated pools, hot tubs, playgrounds, and an on-site store, though the focus is firmly on RVs and cabins rather than tent camping.

detail.address: 53730 Bridal Falls Rd, Rosedale, BC V0X 1X1

campground.name: Bear Spring Eco Retreat
campground.desc: A BC Green-certified eco glamping retreat near Beasley (Nelson area) offering furnished tents with hot outdoor shower and flush toilets; no BYO tents or pets allowed, sites are walk-in only up a short steep trail from the parking lot, and the season opens mid-May.

campground.name: Wasa Lake Campground
campground.desc: A full-service provincial campground on warm, shallow Wasa Lake in a sunny Kootenay valley, with 2,000 m of sandy beach, an 8 km paved loop cyclists can ride around the lake, and a striking Purcell and Rocky Mountain backdrop; just 1 km off Highway 93/95 with showers on site. Powerboats share the lake all summer.

campground.name: McLeod Meadows Campground
campground.desc: McLeod Meadows is a frontcountry Parks Canada campground in a wide river meadow along the Kootenay River — a classic overnight anchor on the Banff-to-Radium corridor with wildlife-rich scenery; a national park entry pass plus camping permit are required and summer reservations fill fast.

campground.name: Beaumont Provincial Park Campground
campground.desc: A developed 54-site BC Parks campground on the shore of Fraser Lake, right off Highway 16 west of Prince George, with a sandy beach, roped swimming area, and canoe access; walk-in beach sites add a quieter option. Gate is locked outside operating season.

campground.name: Page's Resort & Marina Campground
campground.desc: A forested, oceanfront campground at a full-service resort on Gabriola Island, with waterfront tent sites nestled among an orchard and gardens; flush washrooms, showers, laundry, and a well-stocked on-site store make it unusually comfortable. Reaching it requires the short BC Ferries crossing from Nanaimo, which accommodates cyclists routinely.

detail.address: 3350 Coast Road, Gabriola Island, BC V0R 1X7

campground.name: Conovoer Cove Campsite (BCMT)
campground.desc: A sheltered cove campsite on Wallace Island Marine Provincial Park in the Gulf Islands, accessible only by boat or kayak from Chemainus; a stunning island destination that is completely off-limits to touring cyclists without water transport.

campground.name: Bear Creek Campground
campground.desc: A popular BC Parks campground on the west shore of Okanagan Lake with 400 metres of sandy beach and a scenic creek canyon; extremely busy in summer and reservations are required.

detail.address: Westside Road, west of Kelowna, BC

campground.name: Long Beach Campground
campground.desc: A well-serviced rainforest campground at a golf course between Tofino and Ucluelet, with flush toilets, free showers, and a 30-minute walking trail to Pacific Rim's famous surf beach; tent sites run $55–70/night, making it one of the pricier private options on the coast.

detail.address: 1850 Pacific Rim Hwy, Tofino, BC V0R 2Z0

campground.name: Raven's Nest RV
campground.desc: Full-hookup RV park on paved roads in Westbank, near Kelowna; no tent camping is permitted, making it a non-option for cycle tourers on any setup.

detail.address: 3000-1920 Old Okanagan Highway, Westbank, BC V4T 3K6

campground.name: Burnaby Cariboo RV Park and Campground Vancouver
campground.desc: A well-maintained urban RV park in Burnaby with an indoor pool, hot tub, and fitness centre, a 10–12 minute walk from SkyTrain and about 30 minutes from downtown Vancouver; tent sites are available but the setting is a paved RV lot and open fires are prohibited by city bylaw.

campground.name: Hicks Lake Group Campsite
campground.desc: A group-only campsite within Sasquatch Park on Hicks Lake, a warm pocket lake with a sandy beach north of Harrison Hot Springs; easy highway access makes it convenient for cycling groups, though swimmer's itch can affect the lake in summer.

campground.name: Anvils Foot
campground.desc: A free BC Marine Trails campsite near Squamish, accessible only by water; no confirmed facilities or amenities, making it effectively off-limits for loaded touring cyclists arriving by road.

campground.name: Sheridan Lake Resort
campground.desc: A full-service fishing resort on Sheridan Lake along BC's famous paved 'Fishing Highway 24,' offering pull-through and back-in RV sites plus cabins, boat rentals, a tackle shop, beach, and swimming; heavily oriented around trophy rainbow trout but open year-round for ice fishing and snowmobiling.

campground.name: Spring Salmon Place Campground
campground.desc: A 67-site riverside campground inside Sooke Potholes Regional Park, set among forests and the Sooke River's signature carved rock pools and clear green swimming holes; directly adjacent to the Galloping Goose Regional Trail, making it a natural overnight for cyclists. Open mid-May to mid-September, cash only, no showers, and little to no cell service.

campground.name: Kekuli Bay
campground.desc: A manicured BC Parks campground on a scenic bay of Kalamalka Lake with the Okanagan Rail Trail running right through the park — outstanding for spring and fall shoulder visits; swimming area is rocky, summer parking is tight, and the gate closes off-season.

campground.name: Chehalis River Group Site
campground.desc: A reservation-only group campsite beside the Chehalis River near Agassiz, with a riverside open area for tents and separate RV pads; it sits in a busy, non-secluded spot next to the main campground and a popular day-use area across the river.

detail.address: 16440 Morris Valley Road, Agassiz, BC V0M1A1

campground.name: Sol Sante Club
campground.desc: A family-oriented social nudist club on 175 wooded acres in the Cowichan Valley, with a stream-fed lake, heated pool, hot tub, and sauna; 24-hour advance notice and approval required before arriving, and campsites close in the off-season.

detail.address: 3120 Cameron Taggart Road, Cobble Hill, BC V8H 0B6

campground.name: Spruce Grove RV Park and Campground
campground.desc: A full-service RV-style campground on the banks of the Columbia River, five minutes from Fairmont Hot Springs Resort's natural mineral pools — an ideal rest stop for tired legs, though hot-spring entry carries an extra fee.

detail.address: Spruce Grove Frontage Road, Fairmont Hot Springs, V0B 1L1

campground.name: Moyie Lake Campground
campground.desc: A 111-site BC Parks campground on the shores of Moyie Lake, 20 km south of Cranbrook on paved Highway 3/95, with 1,300 m of developed sandy beach, hot showers, and an adventure playground; heavily popular in summer and reservable.

campground.name: Thurston Meadows Campground
campground.desc: A managed recreation campground along Chilliwack Lake Road with sites either beside the river or tucked in forest, each with a picnic table and firepit; pack-in/pack-out required, gates lock at 10 pm, and the FSR approach adds some load to a loaded bike.

campground.name: Peachland RV Park
campground.desc: Year-round RV park in pine forest on the bench lands above Peachland, a short ride from Okanagan Lake beaches and area wineries; cyclists can tent at full RV-site rates with an optional private washroom (shower, toilet, sink) delivered to your site for $39/night extra.

detail.address: 4795 Paradise Valley Drive, Peachland, BC V0H 1X3

campground.name: Rum Island
campground.desc: Rum Island (Isle-de-Lis Marine Provincial Park) is a small Gulf Islands park near Sidney, reachable only by boat or kayak; there is no road or trail access, making it effectively off-limits for loaded touring cyclists.

campground.name: Lakeview Park Campground
campground.desc: Town-run campground on Cowichan Lake — one of Vancouver Island's largest freshwater lakes — with easy paved access right in Lake Cowichan; tent sites run $44/night and the campground fills quickly, so advance reservations are essential.

detail.address: 8815 Lakeview Park Road, Lake Cowichan, BC

campground.name: Beaverview RV Park and Campground
campground.desc: A well-kept all-grass private campground directly on Hwy 16, 2 km east of McBride, set in the Robson Valley between the Rocky Mountains and the Cariboo Range with some river-view sites; open May 1–October 15 with full amenities including hot showers and laundry.

campground.name: Cheakamus Lake Campground
campground.desc: Backcountry campground on the shore of a glacially-fed lake deep in Garibaldi Provincial Park, reached by a hiking trail from the road-end trailhead; spectacular Coast Mountain scenery but fully hike-in with no services and complete self-sufficiency required.

campground.name: Riverside Municipal Campground
campground.desc: A municipal campground on the banks of the Bulkley River in Smithers, offering an in-town base with straightforward bike access and proximity to local services; specific amenities are unconfirmed from available sources.

campground.name: Fort Steele Campground
campground.desc: Quiet forested private campground set half a mile off Highway 93/95 on paved access near the base of the Rockies; best known for a heated swimming pool and fire pits on every site, though cash only and no reservations are accepted.

detail.address: 335 Kelly Road, Regional District of East Kootenay

campground.name: Harrison River RV & Campground
campground.desc: Private campground set right on the Harrison River at Harrison Mills, with 30 tent sites, hot showers, flush washrooms, a swimming dock, and a playground; summer-seasonal, at the end of Kennedy Road near Harrison Mills.

campground.name: Gordon Bay Campground
campground.desc: A large 127-site BC Parks campground on the sandy shores of warm Cowichan Lake, set in one of Vancouver Island's sunniest valleys with a full suite of amenities including showers. Access via paved Hwy 18 and 14 km on South Shore Road makes it straightforward for loaded bikes.

campground.name: Friends Campground And Day Use
campground.desc: Friends Campground is one of four campgrounds within Kokanee Creek Provincial Park on Kootenay Lake, 19 km east of Nelson off paved Hwy 3A, with access to over a kilometre of sandy beach, old-growth cedar canyon trails, and a kokanee spawning channel; full amenities including showers, e-bike charging, and electrical hook-ups make it comfortable, but it is a heavily visited summer destination that books out fast.

campground.name: Magnesia Meadows Camp
campground.desc: A hike-in backcountry camp in a subalpine meadow within Cypress Provincial Park above North Vancouver, with views toward Howe Sound and the Salish Sea; the approach is foot-only through rugged mountain terrain, campfires are permanently banned, and backcountry experience is required.

campground.name: Toad River Lodge RV Park
campground.desc: A full-service commercial stop on the Alaska Highway (mile 422) sitting right on Reflection Lake in northern BC, with tent sites alongside RV hookups, a restaurant, laundromat, and fuel; open year-round though winter brings limited services and extreme cold.

detail.address: Mile 422 Alaska Highway, Toad River, BC V0C 2X0

campground.name: Vedder River Campground
campground.desc: A Fraser Valley Regional District campground on the banks of the Vedder River near Chilliwack, with full amenities (flush toilets, hot showers, fire pits) and easy access to fishing, kayaking, rafting, and mountain biking; family-friendly and well-serviced but closer to suburban than wild.

campground.name: Kinnikinnick Campground & RV Park
campground.desc: An RV park and campground in Port Edward, a small community near Prince Rupert on BC's north coast; website is under construction and details are sparse, so confirm amenities and availability before arriving.

campground.name: Dutch Lake Motel and RV Campground
campground.desc: Commercial motel and RV campground in Clearwater, BC, situated on or near Dutch Lake and convenient to the Wells Gray Provincial Park corridor. Oriented toward RV travellers; tent options and touring-cyclist amenities are unconfirmed.

campground.name: Windy Point Campsite
campground.desc: A fee-based Mosaic Forest Management recreation campsite on central Vancouver Island near Nanaimo, likely reached via managed forest roads; the sparse page content confirms little beyond the booking requirement.

detail.address: 4 F Br Rd, Nanaimo Lakes, BC V9R 1L5, Canada

campground.name: Alder Bay Resort
campground.desc: A 30-acre waterfront RV park and marina on Johnstone Strait, 6 km off Highway 19 between Port McNeill and Telegraph Cove, with rustic oceanfront tent sites alongside full-service RV hookups, a food truck, and a boat launch. Primarily an RV resort, but cyclists wanting a genuine wildlife-rich base on Northern Vancouver Island — orcas, humpbacks, and eagles regularly visible from camp — will find it welcoming.

detail.address: 1 Alder Bay Road, Port McNeill, V0N 2R0

campground.name: Green Point Campground
campground.desc: Green Point is the flagship frontcountry campground of Pacific Rim National Park Reserve's Long Beach unit, tucked in old-growth temperate rainforest above a sweeping Pacific beach; fully serviced with showers and flush toilets, but summer reservations are near-essential and it draws large crowds.

detail.address: Green Point Campground, BC-4, Ucluelet, BC V0R 3A0, Canada

campground.name: Camp Foley
campground.desc: A private campground in the Chilliwack area offering reservations and washroom facilities; website unavailable so details on setting, amenities, and road access could not be confirmed.

campground.name: Cool Waters RV Park
campground.desc: A creek-side RV park in a valley 5 minutes south of Nelson, with showers and flush toilets on-site and easy access to mountain biking, hiking, and the west arm of Kootenay Lake. No sani-dump on-site; road surface not specified but location implies paved access.

campground.name: Dogwood Campgrounds & RV Park
campground.desc: An urban RV park in Surrey within Metro Vancouver, handy as a city-access overnight for cyclists passing through the Lower Mainland; device charging is a practical bonus but no scenic draw is evident.

campground.name: Stoltz Pool Campground
campground.desc: Stoltz Pool sits on the Cowichan River — a BC and Canadian Heritage River celebrated for wild salmon and steelhead — with a converted rail corridor running alongside that is tailor-made for loaded cyclists; the park is a busy summer recreation corridor, so expect company at peak season.

campground.name: Malahat Mountain Meadows RV Resort & Campground - Campsite
campground.desc: Private RV resort near the Malahat summit, set among giant cedars on the Trans-Canada with flush washrooms, hot showers, and laundry; unserviced tent 'nature sites' are available, but cyclists must approach southbound — northbound riders need to overshoot and U-turn at South Shawnigan Lake.

detail.address: 304 Trans Canada Hwy, Malahat, BC V0R 2L0

campground.name: Grand Forks Municipal Campground
campground.desc: Municipal campground along the Kettle River in the heart of downtown Grand Forks, within easy walking distance of grocery stores, restaurants, and services; open May 1–October 15 with a resident host and online reservations.

campground.name: Camp-Along Resort
campground.desc: A private resort campground tucked inside a working organic apricot and pear orchard with views over Skaha Lake, minutes from Penticton, with paved internal roads, a heated pool, hot showers, and flush toilets. No open campfires are permitted, and the beach requires a short drive rather than a walk.

campground.name: Washtok Family Campground
campground.desc: A rustic, off-grid working-farm campground in the Nahatlatch Valley where the Fraser and Nahatlatch rivers meet, reached by roughly 6 km of government-maintained gravel road from Boston Bar; flush toilets and hot showers on site, with Nahatlatch Provincial Park lakes a short distance beyond.

detail.address: 52702 Chaumox Road, Boston Bar, BC V0K 1C0

campground.name: Montague Harbour Campground - First-come, first-served
campground.desc: A southern Gulf Islands marine park on Galiano Island's southwest shore with white shell beaches, tidal lagoons, glacially-carved rock ledges, ancient Indigenous middens, and 130+ bird species; reaching it requires a BC Ferries crossing, then a 10 km paved ride from Sturdies Bay terminal.

campground.name: Fairway RV Park
campground.desc: An RV park in Taylor, a small Peace River town near Fort St. John; the 'Fairway' name suggests proximity to a golf course, but no further details are available from the fetched page.

campground.name: Alderbrook R.V. Park
campground.desc: An RV park in suburban Aldergrove in BC's Fraser Valley; no details are available as the listing page was unreachable, so treat all fields below as low-confidence placeholders.

campground.name: Gridlock RV Campground
campground.desc: A private RV-oriented campground on Hwy 1 at Emory Creek, roughly 13 km north of Hope, offering powered sites in a wooded riverside setting. Primarily geared toward RVs; tent campers are secondary, and the Trans-Canada location means highway noise is a factor.

campground.name: Pathfinder Camp Resorts - Parksville
campground.desc: A private camp resort in Parksville on Vancouver Island; no site details could be retrieved as the linked website returned unrelated content — treat all fields here as low-confidence estimates.

campground.name: Loon Bay Resort
campground.desc: A family-run lakeside resort with 2,000 ft of waterfront on Sheridan Lake, offering RV sites and cabins (no listed tent camping) with showers, laundry, boat rentals, and fishing; cyclists can use a cabin or hookup site but this is primarily an RV destination.

campground.name: Stawamus Chief Campground
campground.desc: Pitched beneath the Stawamus Chief — one of the world's largest granite monoliths — this 57-site provincial park on the Sea to Sky Highway is an international rock-climbing destination with hiking trails to three summits overlooking Howe Sound; the gate closes off-season, leaving a walk-in with no fees or services.

campground.name: Pink Mountain Campsite & RV Park
campground.desc: A full-service highway stop right on the Alaska Highway at Pink Mountain, open year-round with fuel, a general store, coin showers, and laundry — pure utility on a remote northern stretch with no scenic draw.

detail.address: Mile 143 Alaska Highway, Pink Mountain, V0C 2B0

campground.name: Rainey Creek Campground
campground.desc: A 73-site campground in the remote frontier town of Stewart, BC — the long paved spur off the Cassiar Highway is the commitment, rewarded by proximity to Bear Glacier and Salmon Glacier day trips; showers and device charging make it a proper resupply stop.

campground.name: The Ledge Campground
campground.desc: Small private campground in Jordan River offering sea views and rainforest surroundings with fewer than 20 unserviced tent sites; tidy facilities including a heated shower and full bathroom, right on the Sooke–Port Renfrew cycling corridor.

campground.name: Fort Steele Resort and RV Park
campground.desc: Commercial resort campground 14 km northeast of Cranbrook off Hwy 93/95, with 60+ shaded tent sites, an outdoor pool, free hot showers, and Rocky Mountain views of Fisher Peak; open year-round and directly across from Fort Steele Heritage Town.

campground.name: Deadwood Campsite
campground.desc: A Mosaic Forest Management campsite in the Nanaimo area, set on private managed forest land; expect a rustic bush camp with logging-road access and minimal facilities, booking required through Mosaic's reservation system.

campground.name: Riverside Campground
campground.desc: A simple recreation site strung along the Chilliwack River several kilometres past Thurston Meadows on Chilliwack Lake Road, with riverside and forested pitches each offering a picnic table and firepit; pack-in/pack-out with no garbage service, open April through October.

campground.name: Porteau Cove Provincial Park Campground
campground.desc: Waterfront campsites on Howe Sound with mountain views across BC's southernmost fjord, plus dedicated scuba-diving facilities; an active rail line borders the park bringing periodic train noise, sites are tightly spaced, and a 7-night-per-year cap limits lingering.

campground.name: White Swan RV Park
campground.desc: A free 22-site municipal RV park in the small village of Fraser Lake, sitting along the Yellowhead Highway (Hwy 16) corridor in central BC — a straightforward overnight stop with no confirmed services or amenities.

campground.name: Vaseux Lake Campground
campground.desc: Small 12-site BC Parks campground on the shore of Vaseux Lake in the warm, dry Okanagan — an area known for birding and bighorn sheep. The gate closes off-season but walk-in camping from the gate is permitted with no services provided.

campground.name: Kilby Provincial Campground
campground.desc: Pastoral 41-site campground on the Harrison River reached by easy paved roads off Highway 7, with swimming, fishing, boating, and the historic Kilby General Store Museum next door; spring high water makes the river hazardous.

detail.address: Harrison Mills, BC (off Kilby Road, 15 km west of Agassiz via Highway 7)

campground.name: Rainbow Ranch R.V. Park
campground.desc: A ranch-style RV park on the edge of Chilliwack in the Fraser Valley; primarily catered to RVs, but its flat valley location makes it an easy stop for loaded touring cyclists moving through the corridor.

detail.address: 53560 Bridal Falls Road, Rosedale, BC V0X 1X0

campground.name: Bella Pacifica Campground
campground.desc: Walk-out beachfront campground on sandy MacKenzie Beach (tinwis) with both ocean-facing and forested tent sites, minutes from Tofino village; extremely popular in summer and advance reservations are required.

detail.address: 400 MacKenzie Beach Rd, Tofino, BC V0R 2Z0

campground.name: Springer Creek RV Park & Campground
campground.desc: Village-operated campground in Slocan with creekside forested tent sites and coin-op showers, steps from the Slocan Valley Rail Trail and Slocan Lake beach; open May 1 to October 15.

detail.address: 1020 Giffin Avenue, PO Box 50, Slocan, BC V0G 2C0

campground.name: French Beach Provincial Park Group Site
campground.desc: Oceanside campground on the Strait of Juan de Fuca with a 1,600m sand-and-pebble beach, lush forest trails, and prime whale-watching; reached via paved Highway 14 and open year-round with pit toilets and fresh water.

campground.name: Bamberton Provincial Park Campground
campground.desc: Vehicle-accessible forest campground perched above a 225-metre sandy beach on Mill Bay inlet, with sweeping views to the Gulf Islands and Mt. Baker; popular and crowded in summer, with a steep trail linking the campground to the beach.

campground.name: Arbutus Point Campsite / BCMT
campground.desc: A primitive coastal campsite on the BC Marine Trails network near Sidney, reachable by kayak or small boat along the Saanich Peninsula shoreline; arbutus-lined and scenic but not accessible by bicycle without a water crossing.

campground.name: Family Tree Riverside RV & Campground
campground.desc: Family-owned riverside resort on the Eagle River in Sicamous, with tent sites set in open green spaces, a swimming pool, rental kayaks and paddleboards, and easy access to Shuswap and Mara Lakes. More full-service family resort than rustic camp — strong amenities but a heavy RV-park atmosphere.

campground.name: Descanso Bay Regional Park
campground.desc: Descanso Bay Regional Park is a Regional District of Nanaimo campground on Gabriola Island, reachable by ferry from Nanaimo. It sits along the sheltered shores of Descanso Bay and serves as a key overnight stop on the Vancouver Crossing Loop touring route. The park is managed by the RDN and represents one of the few formal camping options on Gabriola Island for cycle tourists.

detail.address: 595 Taylor Bay Rd, Gabriola, BC V0R 1X1, Canada

campground.name: Campers Corner
campground.desc: A campground in Ladysmith on Vancouver Island's east coast; details are sparse as the source page failed to load, so verify amenities and access before arriving.

detail.address: 10935 Trans Canada Hwy 41 # 41, Ladysmith, BC, V9G 1X7

campground.name: Toad Rock Motorcycle Campground
campground.desc: A private, motorcycle-focused campground on 34 forested acres beside Kootenay Lake on Highway 31, with flush toilets, showers, coin-op laundry, and a social pavilion; seasonal summer operation with cash or e-transfer payment only, and Ainsworth Hot Springs five minutes away.

campground.name: Silverton Campground - Lakeside
campground.desc: A small municipal campground on the shore of Slocan Lake in the quiet village of Silverton; the 'Lakeside' name and lake-town setting suggest a scenic overnight, though amenity details are unconfirmed as the town website is offline.

campground.name: Entrance Bay Campground
campground.desc: One of four campgrounds within busy Cultus Lake Park, sitting beside a large warm freshwater lake ringed by forested mountains about 90 minutes from Vancouver; fully serviced with showers and flush toilets, though swimmer's itch and a sudden nearshore drop-off are noted lake hazards.

campground.name: Tamihi Rapids Campground
campground.desc: Seven tent sites sit directly along the Tamihi River at a rapids stretch in the Chilliwack Valley, accessed via Forest Service road; pack-in/pack-out with no garbage service, cash only on site, and gates locked 10 pm–8 am. Season runs April 1 through October 31.

campground.name: Mount Baker RV Park
campground.desc: A private RV-focused campground in Cranbrook offering a convenient overnight base in a well-serviced town; specific amenities are unconfirmed but road access is easy and resupply is close.

campground.name: Living Forest Oceanside Campground & RV Park
campground.desc: A large, year-round private campground on 53 acres where the Nanaimo River meets the harbour, with flush toilets, hot showers, a seasonal café, and miles of on-site trails; heavily RV-oriented with 300+ sites but tent spots are available right in the city's southern edge.
