campground.name: Kaslo Municipal Campground
campground.desc: A municipal campground on the shores of Kootenay Lake in the charming village of Kaslo, with hot showers, free Wi-Fi, and a short walk to the S.S. Moyie National Historic Site and downtown; open spring through fall only with no published tent rate.

campground.name: Group Campground
campground.desc: A developed BC Parks destination off Highway 99 north of Squamish featuring four freshwater swimming lakes, extensive hiking trails, and mountain backdrops; the group site has electrical hook-ups but summer demand is intense — even weekdays fill in July–September, so reserve well ahead.

campground.name: Jordan River Regional Park campground
campground.desc: Coastal campground on paved Hwy 14 at the Jordan River village, a well-known surf break and classic overnight on the Sooke–Port Renfrew cycling corridor; 23 sites with washrooms, but the vibe is surf-crowd busy rather than a quiet retreat.

campground.name: Jones Lake West Recreation Area
campground.desc: Free BC Hydro recreation area at a scenic mountain reservoir in the Cascades east of Chilliwack; access is via a forest service road so expect gravel, but the lake setting is a worthwhile payoff on a clear day.

campground.name: Nairn Falls Campground
campground.desc: A 92-site frontcountry campground on Highway 99 between Whistler and Pemberton, with a signed trail to a dramatic 60-metre waterfall on the Green River; amenities are solid but riverbanks are steep and the water is fast and cold.

campground.name: MTN Fun Basecamp
campground.desc: A quiet, well-run private basecamp in Squamish backing directly onto the extensive trail network, with ride-in/ride-out mountain bike and hike access, hot showers, and a bike wash station; explicitly not a party campground — serious riders and early risers only.

campground.name: Paradise Valley Campground
campground.desc: A family-oriented, music-free campground on 28 acres of coastal rainforest near Squamish, with maintained riverside trails, a general store, and clean flush washrooms with pay showers; tent sites run $55/night, making it one of the pricier private options in the Sea to Sky corridor.

detail.address: 3520 Paradise Valley Road, Squamish, BC V0N 1T0

campground.name: Shingle Bay Campground (BCMT)
campground.desc: A BC Marine Trails paddle-in campsite near Sidney in the Gulf Islands, reachable only by kayak or small boat; there is no road access, making this site a non-starter for loaded touring cyclists.

campground.name: Liard Hot Springs Lodge RV Park
campground.desc: A year-round highway lodge and campground at Mile 497 of the Alaska Highway, directly across from Liard River Hot Springs — Canada's second-largest natural hot springs, a 15-minute walk via boardwalk through boreal forest. Basic tent sites at a commercial stop, but the hot springs make it a genuine rest-and-soak destination for northbound Alaska Highway cyclists.

detail.address: Mile 497 Alaska Highway, Liard River, V0C 1R0

campground.name: Hicks Lake Provincial Campground
campground.desc: Hicks Lake sits within Sasquatch Park's pocket-lake landscape north of Harrison Hot Springs, offering a sandy beach, warm-water swimming, and easy canoeing amid birch and second-growth forest; swimmer's itch is occasionally present in summer.

campground.name: N V Mountainview Chalets and RV Resort
campground.desc: Private RV resort and chalet operation on the edge of McBride in the scenic Robson Valley; offers a full suite of cyclist-friendly amenities including showers, laundry, and device charging, making it a practical service stop on a long valley traverse.

campground.name: Gold Panner
campground.desc: Family-run campground in the Monashee Mountain foothills on Highway 6 near Cherryville, with gold panning on active placer mining claims as its signature draw; flush toilets and showers run May long weekend through Thanksgiving, with dry camping available year-round.

campground.name: Prior Centennial Campground
campground.desc: Drive-in frontcountry campground on Pender Island within Gulf Islands National Park Reserve, reached by BC Ferries ferry; a short trail on the western side links to local hiking routes outside the park. Open May 15–September 30 only.

detail.address: 5714 Canal Rd, Pender Island, BC V0N 2M1, Canada

campground.name: Wright's Beach Camp RV Park
campground.desc: A family-oriented private campground directly on Skaha Lake at Penticton's south entrance off Highway 97, offering waterfront tent sites, a private sandy beach, and a heated outdoor pool; expect crowds in peak summer and note that advance reservations require week-long minimum stays.

detail.address: 4200 Skaha Lake Road, Penticton, BC V2A 0K4

campground.name: Jimsmith Lake Provincial Park Campground
campground.desc: A 35-site lakeside campground in Douglas fir and larch forest just 4 km on paved road from Cranbrook, with a sandy beach, swimming, and fishing for rainbow trout and largemouth bass. The gate closes outside the operating season, so confirm dates before planning.

campground.name: Goldstream Group Campsite - Goldminer (Lower) Site
campground.desc: A vehicle-accessible group campsite set in Goldstream Provincial Park's cathedral old-growth of 600-year-old Douglas firs, just 16 km from Victoria; the annual chum salmon spawning run draws bald eagles and thousands of visitors each autumn. Group sites carry a minimum charge for 15 adults, making them cost-effective only for larger parties.

campground.name: Pinegrove Campground and RV Park
campground.desc: A family-run commercial campground just off Highway 5 in McLure, 25 minutes north of Kamloops, offering touring cyclists a convenient stop with hot showers, laundry, a convenience store, and flush toilets; the setting is pleasant but unremarkable highway-side.

campground.name: Mowhinna Creek Campground
campground.desc: Wooded campground 1km south of Ganges on Salt Spring Island's main paved road, well-suited as a central island base with flush toilets, coin showers, and WiFi; tent sites from $45, closed to tents November through mid-March.

detail.address: 515 Fulford-Ganges Rd, Saltspring Island, BC V8K 2K1

campground.name: Meziadin Lake Campground
campground.desc: A well-equipped 66-site BC Parks campground on the shores of Meziadin Lake at the Cassiar Highway junction, with potable water, washrooms, and e-bike charging — a natural anchor for cyclists on the Cassiar corridor. Summer season only; expect a scenic mountain-lake setting and a genuine rest rather than a rushed stop.

campground.name: Clearwater Valley Resort
campground.desc: A commercial resort campground at the gateway to Wells Gray Park, offering tent sites with access to an on-site pool and summer restaurant; a convenient base for exploring 250+ waterfalls and park activities, though the fenced, gated resort setting trades wilderness feel for amenity comfort.

campground.name: Witset RV Park and Campground
campground.desc: A First Nation-operated RV park and campground at Witset on the Yellowhead Highway beside the Bulkley River, with solid cycle-tourer amenities including showers, laundry, and device charging; the famous Witset Canyon salmon weir is a short walk from camp.

campground.name: South Beach Gardens Campground
campground.desc: A campground in Penticton's south end, likely near Skaha Lake beach given the name; website was unreachable so amenities and exact setting are unconfirmed. Penticton is a well-serviced Okanagan town, making this a plausible urban base camp.

campground.name: Hot Spring RV
campground.desc: A private, year-round RV park in the heart of Harrison Hot Springs village, one block from Harrison Lake and the famous hot springs pool, with 21 fully serviced sites; the park caters to RVs only — no tent camping is mentioned and the booking form accepts motorhomes and trailers exclusively.

detail.address: 272 Lillooet Ave, Harrison Hot Springs, BC, Canada V0M 1K0

campground.name: Fintry Campground
campground.desc: A large 160-site full-service campground on the historic Fintry Estate along Okanagan Lake's west shore, offering a natural sand beach, mountain canyon views, and a dramatic triple waterfall through Shorts Creek; expect crowds in peak summer.

campground.name: Glencoe Campground
campground.desc: A private campground on Hot Springs Road in Harrison Hot Springs village, directly across from the public hot mineral pool — a classic soak stop for tired legs; open year-round but washrooms close before frost and tent rates are on the high side.

detail.address: 259 Hot Springs Road, Harrison Hot Springs, BC V0M 1K0

campground.name: Ucluelet Campground
campground.desc: A well-equipped private campground right in Ucluelet on the west coast of Vancouver Island, with 125 sites ranging from waterfront harbour-view spots to semi-private forested sites, open year-round. Flush washrooms, showers, laundry, and a playground are on site; expect a busy commercial atmosphere with heavy RV presence alongside tent campers.

detail.address: 260 Seaplane Base Road, Ucluelet, BC V0R 3A0

campground.name: Snaʕsnulax̌tn Campground (Pow-wow Grounds)
campground.desc: First Nations-operated campground in the Ashnola Valley, 8.5 km up a gravel road from Highway 3 near Keremeos, with 55 sites on 33 acres, indoor showers, and easy access to the Similkameen River for floating, paddling, and fishing; open May to September.

campground.name: Anmore Camp & RV Park
campground.desc: A well-maintained private RV park at the entrance to Buntzen Lake, offering showers, laundry, and flush toilets with easy access to lake swimming and surrounding hiking trails; sites are full-hookup RV-oriented at $85+/night with no tent-only rate listed.

campground.name: Princess Bay Campsite / BCMT
campground.desc: A marine-trail campsite on the Gulf Islands near Sidney, reached by kayak or boat via the BC Marine Trails network; touring cyclists would need to combine riding with a water crossing, and facilities are basic.

campground.name: Mountainaire Campground
campground.desc: A 40-acre private campground near Nanaimo with tenting options, renovated flush washrooms, showers, and a short rainforest trail to a Nanaimo River swimming hole; conveniently located minutes from both ferry terminals, making it a practical island transition stop.

campground.name: Horseshoe Bend Group Campsite
campground.desc: A group campsite on the Heritage-designated Cowichan River, celebrated for salmon and steelhead, with a cycling rail trail and restored trestle viewpoints right at hand; note this is a group site billed at a minimum of 15 adults — suited to organized riding clubs, not solo tourers — and it closes in winter with no water off-season.

campground.name: Hoodoo Mountain Resort
campground.desc: A resort-style caravan and camping site near Fairmont Hot Springs in the Columbia Valley; details on tent camping, amenities, and road surface are unconfirmed as the listing page was unavailable.

campground.name: Tranquille River Canyon Campsite
campground.desc: A primitive camp site in Tranquille River Canyon within Lac du Bois Grasslands near Kamloops, set amid ecologically rare grassland communities with canyon scenery and bighorn sheep; no potable water on site and road access may be seasonal or gravel.

campground.name: Riverside Campsite
campground.desc: A small three-site managed campsite near Nanaimo, positioned beside a river; no amenities are confirmed so arrive self-sufficient.

detail.address: 4 F Br Rd, Nanaimo Lakes, BC V9R 1L5, Canada

campground.name: Claybanks RV Park
campground.desc: Municipal RV park on the banks of the Coldwater River in Merritt, open April through October with full hookups and heated showers; cyclists can use the single non-serviced site at $33/night, with a five-minute walk to downtown restaurants and shops.

campground.name: Boulder Mountain Resort
campground.desc: Walk-in tent sites in old-growth cedar forest 3.5 km west of Revelstoke on the Trans-Canada, with resort flush showers, hot tub, and coin laundry a short walk from the pad; fees apply and no power or wifi at the tent.

campground.name: Cedar Falls Campground
campground.desc: A tidy private campground nestled in cedar trees 12 minutes from downtown Vernon on the Silver Star Road corridor, offering flush showers, device charging, and free Wi-Fi; BX Creek Falls hiking trail is a short walk from the exit gate.

campground.name: Ruckle Provincial Park
campground.desc: Ruckle Provincial Park occupies the southeastern tip of Salt Spring Island, offering tent camping in open grassy meadows overlooking Swanson Channel where ferries and pleasure craft pass in a steady parade. With seven kilometres of rocky shoreline, the park is one of the most biodiverse in the southern Gulf Islands, drawing wildlife watchers, scuba divers, and beachcombers to its tidal pools and coastal trails. For touring cyclists arriving by BC Ferries, it is a short ride from the Fulford Harbour terminal to one of the most scenic campgrounds in the region.

campground.name: OutPost Camping
campground.desc: A campsite near Princeton, BC with fee camping; website unavailable so amenities, setting, and access details are unconfirmed. Treat as a basic overnight option until more information can be verified.

campground.name: Country Maples RV Resort
campground.desc: A large commercial RV resort on the Chemainus River amid old-growth forest, with 54 dedicated tent sites alongside 130+ RV sites; the heated pool, mini-golf, and four playgrounds suit families well, though the resort atmosphere is decidedly RV-park in character.

detail.address: 9010 Trans Canada Hwy, Chemainus, BC V0R 1K4

campground.name: Rosco's RV Park
campground.desc: A full-service, year-round RV park on the edge of Fort St. John offering hot showers, laundry, and 82 serviced sites; geared to RVs with no tent rate listed, but a practical amenity stop for cyclists passing through the Peace region.

detail.address: 10688 Alder Cres, Fort St John, BC V0C 1H0

campground.name: Russet Lake Campgrounds
campground.desc: Hike-in backcountry campsite at a remote alpine lake in Garibaldi Park, reached via the demanding Singing Pass trail from Whistler; expect self-sufficient wilderness conditions, no vehicle access, and a multi-hour approach on foot.

campground.name: Schroeder Creek Resort
campground.desc: A quiet, treed resort on the shore of Kootenay Lake near Kaslo, offering hot showers, a sheltered marina, and a small store; tenting is $45/night for two and the season runs April 15 to October 15.

campground.name: Chute Lake Lodge
campground.desc: A historic mountain lodge-resort above Naramata Bench where the Kettle Valley Railway trail passes the front door, offering private wooded campsites with access to lodge washrooms, showers, and a full restaurant; the 11 km gravel approach road is maintained but unpaved and the KVR itself is dirt with bumps and potholes.

campground.name: Paul Lake Campground
campground.desc: A large, popular lakeshore campground in mixed Douglas fir and aspen forest, 30 minutes from Kamloops, with 400 m of sandy beach, stocked rainbow trout fishing, and a trail to Gibraltar Rock; arrives full quickly in peak summer.

campground.name: Lac Le Jeune Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A popular high-elevation lake campground at 1,280 m, just off the Coquihalla near Kamloops, with a sandy swimming beach, a fishing wharf, and access to 45+ km of hiking and biking trails; paved access is easy but the park sees heavy summer use.

campground.name: Hazelmere RV Park & Campground
campground.desc: A well-amenitied suburban RV park in South Surrey with a swimming pool, hot tub, mini golf, and sports courts, conveniently placed 45 minutes from downtown Vancouver and five minutes from the US border; primarily an RV resort, but tent sites are available year-round.

campground.name: Waters Edge Campground
campground.desc: A lakeside off-grid campground directly on Dease Lake along the Cassiar Highway, with a complimentary boat launch for registered guests; no potable water on site and pit toilets only.

campground.name: Okanagan Lake Provincial Park, South Campground
campground.desc: A large provincial campground on Okanagan Lake with pebbly beaches, ponderosa pine and sagebrush setting, and panoramic lake views; rattlesnakes inhabit the dry hillsides above camp.

campground.name: Pinantan Lake Resort
campground.desc: A private resort on the peaceful shores of Pinantan Lake, 20 minutes from Kamloops, with cabin rentals and full-service RV sites; no tent camping is listed, cell service drops before arrival, and the gate locks at 8 pm.

detail.address: 2488 Harper Ranch Road, Pinantan Lake, BC V0E 3E1

campground.name: Nelson RV Park & Marina
campground.desc: Small private campground on the west arm of Kootenay Lake in Balfour, with only 4 waterfront tent sites, a private beach, flush washrooms with showers, and mountain views in every direction; the RV-heavy layout means tent spots are scarce and should be confirmed by phone before making it a target.

campground.name: Goldstream Campground
campground.desc: A large, well-serviced provincial campground 16 km from downtown Victoria, tucked among 600-year-old Douglas fir and cedar with riverside trails, a 47.5 m waterfall, and an acclaimed fall chum salmon spawning run complete with bald eagles; 173 sites means it fills fast.

campground.name: Princeton Municipal RV Park & Campground
campground.desc: Town-operated RV park and campground in Princeton, BC, conveniently located for cyclists on the Crowsnest Highway (Hwy 3) corridor through the Similkameen Valley. A functional overnight with no frills; amenities and road surface unconfirmed as the source page was unreachable.

campground.name: Montague Harbour Campground - Walk-in
campground.desc: Walk-in campsites in a BC marine provincial park on Galiano Island, reached by BC Ferries then a 10 km ride on island roads; the park features white shell beaches, tidal lagoons, old-growth forest, and protected Indigenous shell middens over 3,000 years old. Loaded touring bikes must be walked from the parking area into the walk-in loop.

detail.address: Montague Park Road, Galiano Island, BC

campground.name: Smonećten (McDonald) Campground
campground.desc: A forested Parks Canada drive-in campground minutes from the Swartz Bay ferry terminal, with bike-friendly walk-in sites and direct access to the Lochside Cycling Trail linking Swartz Bay to downtown Victoria; expect some road noise from the adjacent highway.

detail.address: 10740 McDonald Park Road, North Saanich, BC V8L 5S5

campground.name: Whistler RV Park and Campgrounds
campground.desc: Whistler RV Park sits just outside the village with ridge views of the Whistler Valley and Black Tusk; a well-amenitied commercial campground with an on-site café, watercraft rentals, and games facilities that skew heavily toward RVs and glamping guests rather than touring cyclists.

campground.name: Moyie Lake Provincial Park Campground
campground.desc: A large, well-serviced provincial park campground on Moyie Lake, 20 km south of Cranbrook directly off Highway 3/95, with 1,300 m of developed sandy beach, hot showers, boat launch, and playground — popular and busy through the summer season.

campground.name: Canyon Alpine RV Park & Campground
campground.desc: A well-amenitized RV resort on the Trans-Canada Highway through the Fraser Canyon, with flush showers, on-site games, and a playground; no tent rate is published and a boil water advisory is in effect.

detail.address: 50490 TRANS CANADA HWY, BOSTON BAR, V0K 1C0

campground.name: Old Mill Campsite
campground.desc: A Mosaic Forest Management campsite on central Vancouver Island near Nanaimo, likely set in second-growth timber company lands; amenities and road surface are unconfirmed from available sources, so verify access before routing.

campground.name: Hope Valley RV & Campground
campground.desc: A large adult-oriented RV park just off the Trans-Canada Highway at Hope, offering full-hookup sites with showers, cable TV, and wi-fi included; no tent rate is listed and the park caters primarily to RV travellers.

campground.name: Honeymoon Bay Group Campground
campground.desc: Group-only campground inside Cultus Lake Park, forested and close to the Teapot Hill trailhead, with flush washrooms, showers, and potable water; solo or small-party cyclists cannot use this site — minimum billing for 15 adults applies, and the gate is closed off-season.

campground.name: High Falls (5.5km) Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, rustic clearing 5.5 km up the Squamish River FSR, shaded by big-leaf maples, cottonwoods, and cedars — no amenities, no bear caches, and flood-prone during heavy rain.

campground.name: Sidney Spit Campsite / BC Marine Trail
campground.desc: A celebrated sandy spit on Sidney Island in the Gulf Islands, reached only by seasonal passenger ferry or private boat from Sidney; the beach and warm shallow water are the draw, but the water-only access makes it a non-starter for a loaded bike without advance planning.

campground.name: Yahk Provincial Park Campground
campground.desc: A quiet, well-spaced forest campground beside the Moyie River, straddling Highway 3/95 as a convenient rest stop near the small community of Yahk; the river runs fast and high in spring, and the gate closes in the off-season.

campground.name: Copper Quarter Campground
campground.desc: Urban campground on Tk'emlúps te Secwe̓pemc land in central Kamloops, within easy reach of all town services; the setting is an events-centre facility rather than a natural site, but showers are included with tent sites.

detail.address: 485 Mount Paul Centre Way, Kamloops, BC V2H 0A8

campground.name: Dutch Lake Resort & RV Park
campground.desc: A full-service lakeside RV resort on spring-fed Dutch Lake in Clearwater, with flush toilets, showers, an on-site restaurant, and dock access for swimming, fishing, and paddling; note there are no dedicated tent sites — cyclists must book a full-hookup RV pad. Open April to October, four minutes from Wells Gray Provincial Park.

campground.name: Monte Lake Resort
campground.desc: A 30-site resort campground on Monte Lake in BC's dry interior, priced at the premium tier; amenities are unconfirmed as the website returned no content.

campground.name: Montague Harbour Campground - Vehicle
campground.desc: Vehicle-accessible BC Parks campground on Galiano Island in the southern Gulf Islands, set among shell-midden beaches, tidal lagoons, old forest, and 130+ bird species; reaching it requires a BC Ferries crossing to Sturdies Bay followed by a 10 km signed ride on Montague Park Road.

campground.name: Barefoot Beach Resort
campground.desc: A resort campground in Penticton bearing a beach-focused name, likely on Okanagan or Skaha Lake — details on facilities and exact location are unconfirmed as the website was unreachable.

detail.address: 4145 Skaha Lake Road, Penticton, BC V2A 6J7

campground.name: Golden Municipal Campground and RV Park
campground.desc: Municipal campground beside the Kicking Horse River in the heart of downtown Golden, walkable to restaurants, shops, and trails, and a short ride from six national parks including Yoho and Banff; night train noise is a noted drawback.

campground.name: Ruckle Park, Walk-in Camping
campground.desc: Walk-in tent camping in grassy meadows along 7 km of rocky Salt Spring Island shoreline, with sweeping views over Swanson Channel and strong wildlife watching; potable water is shut down November 1–March 15 and all sites require carrying gear from the parking lot.

campground.name: Helm Creek Campground
campground.desc: A hike-in backcountry campsite deep in Garibaldi Provincial Park's Cheakamus Lake zone, surrounded by glaciated Coast Mountain terrain; accessible only on foot, fully self-sufficient, and demanding conditions year-round.

campground.name: Mayne Island Camping
campground.desc: A tenter-only walk-in campground on Mayne Island with 15 sites strung along 1,800 ft of sand-and-pebble beach and undeveloped forest overlooking Miners Bay; outhouses only (plus a celebrated outdoor tree shower), a 1–4 minute carry from the car park, and ferry access required to reach the island. Open April to October, with groceries and a pub 1 km away.

campground.name: Kinaskan Lake Campground
campground.desc: Kinaskan Lake Provincial Park offers lakeshore camping on a remote northern lake along the Stewart-Cassiar Highway (Hwy 37), with potable water and washrooms on-site; the site is popular with anglers and operates on a short summer season in a genuinely wild Stikine setting.

campground.name: Callaghan Lake
campground.desc: A small, free, rustic drive-in campground on a subalpine lake in the Callaghan Valley, reached via 8 km of rough gravel FSR where high-clearance vehicles are recommended; active grizzly habitat, no garbage facilities, and the access road is gated from November to early June.

campground.name: Rondalyn Resort
campground.desc: Commercial Parkbridge-managed RV resort in Ladysmith on Vancouver Island; primarily oriented toward RVs and seasonal cottage rentals, with no tent-specific or cyclist amenity details available from the scraped pages.

campground.name: Blue Cedars RV Park and Campground
campground.desc: A full-service private campground in a Douglas-fir forest on the western edge of Prince George, with direct trailhead access to the 25 km Cranbrook Hill Greenway; open year-round with showers, laundry, and WiFi, though tent rates are steep for an RV-focused park.

detail.address: 4433 Kimball Rd, Prince George, BC V2N 5N7

campground.name: Jordan River Regional Park Campground
campground.desc: Coastal campground on the Strait of Juan de Fuca along Highway 14, popular with surfers and wind-sport enthusiasts; exposed oceanfront setting with basic facilities and no confirmed amenities from available sources.

campground.name: Capilano RV Park
campground.desc: Urban RV park in West Vancouver beside Lions Gate Bridge, with flush showers, outdoor pool, and hot tub; tent sites are first-come-first-served and closed October through April, and premium pricing reflects the city-gateway location.

detail.address: 295 Tomahawk Avenue, West Vancouver, BC V7P 1C5

campground.name: Lion's Campground
campground.desc: A community campground in the mountain town of Rossland, serving as a practical base for cyclists passing through the Kootenays; the website was unavailable so expect a functional overnight rather than a resort-style experience.

campground.name: Canyon Farms RV Park
campground.desc: RV-only park (no tent or car camping) on an agri-tourism farm in East Kelowna, a 5-minute walk from Mission Creek Greenway and minutes from Myra Canyon's historic KVR trestles; cycle tourers cannot stay here as tenting is explicitly prohibited.

campground.name: Village Campground
campground.desc: Campsite within the SilverStar Mountain Resort village, perched at high elevation above Vernon with access to resort amenities, restaurants, and a bike park; the access road is a long paved climb of roughly 900 m from the valley, and the campground operates only during the summer season.

campground.name: Nelson Camp Ground
campground.desc: City-run campground in a forested setting on High Street just east of downtown Nelson, within walking distance of shops, parks, and the beach. Amenities include showers, laundry, and cooking facilities; open May 1–October 16 with tent sites from $26/night.

campground.name: Silver Sage RV Park & Campgrounds
campground.desc: Private RV park on the South Thompson River just off the Yellowhead Highway, with shaded tent sites, flush washrooms, showers, and coin laundry; open April to mid-October at $39/night for unserviced tent sites.

campground.name: Pedder Bay RV Park
campground.desc: RV-focused resort on sheltered Pedder Bay near Sooke, primarily catering to RVs and boaters with marina access; tent-camping suitability and facilities are unclear as the site was unreachable.

detail.address: 925 Pedder Bay Drive, Victoria, BC V9C 4H1

campground.name: Brannen Lake RV Park & Campsite
campground.desc: A third-generation family-run campground on Brannen Lake with 130+ forested sites and a private beach, just minutes from Nanaimo's services — a practical lakeside base with a suburban-park feel rather than a wilderness retreat.

campground.name: Kamloops Riverview RV Park
campground.desc: A year-round, RV-oriented park on the eastern edge of Kamloops with full washrooms, showers, and laundry; a tenting area exists but the park caters primarily to self-contained rigs, and tent rates are not published.

campground.name: Purden Lake Provincial Park Campground
campground.desc: A 78-site provincial park on the north shore of Purden Lake, 64 km east of Prince George right off Yellowhead Highway 16, offering lakeshore swimming, canoeing, and fishing for rainbow trout and kokanee in boreal forest surroundings. Be aware that the lake is prone to sudden heavy winds — a hazard for paddlers.

detail.address: Purden Lake Provincial Park, Sinclair Mills, BC V0J 3M0

campground.name: Dodd Island
campground.desc: Dodd Island is a backcountry island campsite in the Broken Group Islands unit of Pacific Rim National Park Reserve, reachable only by boat — a paddler's and sea-kayaker's destination set in a sheltered, wildlife-rich archipelago off Vancouver Island's west coast; no road access means cyclists must arrive by water, making it a logistical undertaking rather than a touring stop.

campground.name: Shell Beach Campsite (BCMT)
campground.desc: A BC Marine Trails paddle-in beach campsite near Sidney on the Saanich Peninsula; access is by kayak or small boat, placing it effectively off-route for loaded cycle tourers.

campground.name: Zuiderzee Campsites
campground.desc: A family-owned lakeside campground on Quennell Lake, 20 minutes south of Nanaimo, with swimming, bass and trout fishing, rowboat rentals, and hot showers on 28.5 acres; expect a busy, multigenerational summer crowd.

campground.name: D'Arcy Island Campground / BC Marine Trail
campground.desc: Wilderness island campground in the Haro Strait accessible only by kayak or small boat as part of the BC Marine Trail; notable for its haunting history as BC's leper colony (1891–1924) and Gulf Islands National Park Reserve setting, with no road or bike access, no drinking water on island, and primitive facilities.

campground.name: Williamson Lake Campground
campground.desc: A privately operated 50-site campground on Williamson Lake at the edge of Revelstoke, with showers, device charging, and potable water; handy for resupply and Revelstoke's trail network.

campground.name: Chehalis River Main Campground
campground.desc: A large, supervised riverside campground on the banks of the Chehalis River in BC's Fraser Valley, reached by paved road; the main draw is steelhead and salmon fishing, with a forest trail down to the river.

campground.name: Caycuse Campsite
campground.desc: A fee campsite on Mosaic Forest Management private timberland in the Caycuse watershed, accessed via active logging roads south of Lake Cowichan — a utilitarian forest stop with no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Northern Experience RV Park
campground.desc: A tidy highway RV park 8 minutes south of Prince George off Highway 97, offering modern flush washrooms, coin showers, laundry, and free wifi; tent sites are water-only at $41/night and the setting is functional rather than scenic.

campground.name: Horseshoe Lake Campground
campground.desc: A small four-site lakeside campground near Kamloops in the Roche Lake area, suited to a quiet overnight; services are withdrawn off-season and access is via unpaved gravel road.

campground.name: Van Isle Cowichan RV Park & Campground
campground.desc: Van Isle Cowichan RV Park & Campground is an 11-acre riverside campground nestled along the Cowichan River just off the Trans-Canada Highway near Duncan, under new ownership and rebranding. It offers a mix of full-service RV sites, partial-service sites, and tent sites on Vancouver Island in one of Canada's warmest climates. Touring cyclists can access the campground as a base for river tubing, trail hiking, and exploring the Cowichan Valley wine region.

campground.name: Squamish Valley Campground
campground.desc: Family-owned private campground on the Squamish River with an expansive sandy beach and glacier views; no drinking water or showers on site, and the 14 km approach up Squamish Valley Road is a long haul for a loaded bike.

detail.address: 12975 Squamish Valley Rd, Squamish, BC, V0N 1T0

campground.name: Lemon Creek Pioneer Campground
campground.desc: A well-kept private campground in the Slocan Valley with 17 grass-and-treed tent sites, flush washrooms, hot showers, and a covered gazebo; walking distance to the Lemon Creek confluence and a Japanese Internment Garden. Reservations require a 50% deposit to confirm.

campground.name: Camp Bridal
campground.desc: A caravan-oriented campground near Chilliwack with almost no detail available online; suitability for loaded touring bikes and tent campers is unclear from available sources.

campground.name: Roche Lake North Campground
campground.desc: A small 8-site campground on the north shore of Roche Lake, a popular trout-fishing destination in the rolling hills south of Kamloops; reached by gravel road, services are seasonal with nothing provided off-season.

campground.name: Royalwood RV Resort
campground.desc: A full-hookup RV resort in the Fraser Valley, directly off Trans-Canada Highway exit 109, with showers, laundry, and a championship golf course adjacent; all sites are serviced RV pads with no tent-only option mentioned.

campground.name: Tsawaak RV Resort
campground.desc: Indigenous-owned Tla-o-qui-aht resort on Pacific Rim Hwy about 3 km from Tofino with exclusive access to tinwis Beach; only 5 tent sites amid mostly RV and cabin accommodation, so book early for this high-demand destination.

detail.address: 1119 Pacific Rim Highway, Tofino, British Columbia, V0R 2Z0

campground.name: Peace Arch RV Park
campground.desc: A well-maintained 27-acre RV park in suburban South Surrey with ornamental gardens, a pool, showers, and laundry; listed as a caravan site with no tent camping confirmed, but a practical base near the US border crossing and Tsawwassen ferry.

campground.name: Bonanza Resort
campground.desc: Family-run lakeside resort on Horse Lake, 16 km east of 100 Mile House, with well-maintained tent sites set among pine, spruce, fir, and aspen; boat and kayak rentals on-site make it a natural hub for a water-activity layover day. Tent sites are $30/night; the commercial resort atmosphere suits families more than solitude-seekers.

campground.name: Port Hardy RV Resort & Cabins
campground.desc: A private campground tucked between the Quatse River and a 138-acre estuary wildlife sanctuary, just off Highway 19 and under a kilometre from BC Ferries — a tidy staging stop with showers, coin laundry, and Wi-Fi.

campground.name: Brookside Resort
campground.desc: A private resort on Cluculz Lake in central BC, likely offering lakeside camping for tents and RVs; details on facilities and pricing are unavailable as the Facebook page could not be fetched.

campground.name: Dutch's Campground
campground.desc: A year-round commercial campground on 4 acres in the heart of Coldstream, BC, with a creek on site and a 5-minute walk to Kalamalka Beach; free hot showers and laundry on site, though open fires are not permitted and rates apply.

campground.name: Jones Lake Main Recreation Area
campground.desc: A free BC Hydro reservoir campground beside Jones Lake in the mountains above Chilliwack, with washrooms on site; access is via a gravel forest service road that will be rough for loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Heritage Campsite & RV Park
campground.desc: A family-oriented private campground on Highway 97 at Monte Lake offering showers, laundry, and WiFi for tent and RV campers; recreational amenities such as pickleball and volleyball are still coming online and wood fires are not permitted.

campground.name: Stoltz Pool Group Campground
campground.desc: A group campground on the Cowichan River — a BC and Canadian Heritage River internationally renowned for salmon and steelhead — directly adjacent to the Trans Canada Trail rail corridor, making it a natural anchor for cycling groups; group-site pricing applies a minimum charge for 15 adults.

campground.name: Sooke River Campground
campground.desc: A family-oriented private campground nestled along the Sooke River and De Mamiel Creek, 45 minutes from Victoria on paved Highway 14, with flush washrooms and coin showers, river access for paddling, wildlife watching, and a playground — open seasonally late March to mid-October with tent sites priced at the higher end of private campground rates.

campground.name: Clear Creek Campground
campground.desc: Clear Creek is one of four campgrounds within Cultus Lake Provincial Park, set among forested mountains beside a large warm freshwater lake prized for swimming and watersports; expect crowds in peak summer as this is one of the busiest park destinations in the Lower Mainland.

campground.name: Cabin Bay Campsite (BCMT)
campground.desc: A two-site primitive campsite on Wallace Island Marine Provincial Park in the Gulf Islands, reachable only by boat from Chemainus — beautiful sheltered island scenery, but completely inaccessible to loaded touring cyclists without arranging water transport.

campground.name: Maple Bay Campground
campground.desc: Maple Bay is one of four campgrounds at Cultus Lake Park, a busy Lower Mainland favourite set beside a large warm freshwater lake about 10 km from Sardis via paved highway; showers and full services, but expect crowds in summer.

campground.name: Burns Lake Municipal Campground
campground.desc: Free municipal campground right on Burns Lake in the town centre, with swimming, a 24/7 kayak rental shack, and two lakeside restaurants steps away; no hookups on-site and paid showers at the nearby Lakeside Multiplex are the main catches.

campground.name: Texas Creek Campground
campground.desc: A small, quiet private campground three minutes from downtown Lillooet offering mountain views, flush washrooms, and a cozy cabin explicitly pitched at cyclists; no tent sites are listed, no dogs allowed, and the season opens May 1st.

detail.address: 2211 Texas Creek Road, Lillooet, BC V0K 1N0

campground.name: Whiskey Creek RV Campground
campground.desc: A small wooded RV park off Highway 4 near Parksville, with 15 grassy treed sites on 3 acres at the foot of Mount Arrowsmith. Primarily RV-oriented with full hook-ups; tent sites run $45/night, but the position is handy for riders transiting toward Tofino with Cathedral Grove and Little Qualicum Falls just minutes away.

campground.name: Group Campsite
campground.desc: Ruckle Park's group campsite on Salt Spring Island sits in a grassy meadow overlooking Swanson Channel with rich wildlife and shoreline; access requires a BC Ferries crossing from Swartz Bay, group fees apply to a minimum of 15 adults, and potable water is off November through mid-March.

campground.name: Gardenside Acres
campground.desc: Gardenside Acres is a small, family-run tent-only campground on the Harper family farm in Brentwood Bay, a short walk from the world-famous Butchart Gardens and the village waterfront. Guests camp on a working farm with laying hens, an orchard, and a vegetable garden, with optional home-style breakfasts featuring fresh eggs and seasonal produce grown on-site. The site backs onto five acres of natural parkland and the ocean, placing cyclists within easy reach of kayaking, marine life, restaurants, and hiking.

detail.address: 1117 Greig Avenue, Brentwood Bay, BC V8M 1J6

campground.name: Riverside Resort Campground
campground.desc: A commercial RV resort in Whistler operated by Parkbridge, likely positioned along a river corridor; the scraped pages are Parkbridge corporate content only and contain no details specific to this property, so facilities, tent availability, and amenities are unconfirmed.

campground.name: Blue Lake Resort
campground.desc: Family-run lakeside resort 15 km north of Boston Bar in the Fraser Canyon, with wooded and lakeside campsites beside a crystal-clear lake, a sandy beach, flush washrooms, and pay showers; access is 1.5 km of gravel climbing a mountainside — manageable for cars but a stiff push for a loaded bike.

campground.name: Secret Beach Campground & Kayak Launch
campground.desc: A Toquaht Nation-operated bayfront campground on Barkley Sound with 67 sites, a marina, and a dedicated kayak launch — the main land base for paddlers heading into the Broken Group Islands; well-developed with a pump track and playground but seasonal (May 15–Sept 15), $55/night, no cell service, and a busy booking calendar.

campground.name: Sandspit Campground
campground.desc: Sandspit campground anchors Kokanee Creek Park's kilometre of sandy Kootenay Lake beach, 19 km east of Nelson on paved Hwy 3A, with full amenities including showers and e-bike charging. It's the park's most popular campground — expect crowds in summer, offset by beach swimming, canyon trails through old-growth cedar, and a kokanee spawning channel.

campground.name: Rapids Campground
campground.desc: Seven tent sites sit directly along the Tamihi River in the Chilliwack Valley, offering a genuine riverside wilderness feel; access is via Forest Service Roads, it's cash-only on arrival, and there is no garbage service — pack in, pack out.

campground.name: Burton Historical Park Campground
campground.desc: Treed, family-oriented campground sitting directly on the Arrow Lakes shore near Burton, BC, with sandy beaches, a boat launch, and full modern washrooms with showers; reached by paved Highway 6 then a short run down Lakeview Park Road, open May 1–October 15.

campground.name: Taylor Meadows Campground
campground.desc: Hike-in backcountry campground set in subalpine meadows beneath the iconic Black Tusk in Garibaldi Park; spectacular alpine terrain but trail access only means a loaded touring bike stays at the Rubble Creek trailhead.

campground.name: Surf Junction Campground
campground.desc: A forested campground on Vancouver Island's wild west coast midway between Ucluelet and Tofino, with private wooded sites, a hot tub, sauna, and on-site surf school — not on the beach but a short drive to Pacific Rim's surf breaks. Open April to mid-October only.

campground.name: Wild Rose Camping and RV Park
campground.desc: A family-run campground sitting between the Cascade Mountains and the Fraser River, 7.7 km west of Hope on Hwy 1, with grassy tent sites, free hot showers, flush washrooms open 24/7, and an explicit cross-Canada cyclist welcome; highway-adjacent and open year-round.

detail.address: 62030 Flood Hope Road, Hope BC V0X 1L2

campground.name: Surf Grove Campground
campground.desc: Surf Grove sits at Cox Bay — Canada's top-rated surf beach — 7 km south of Tofino, with forested semi-serviced tent sites featuring 15-amp power, showers, and wi-fi just a short walk from the sand. A polished, year-round commercial campground with top-tier amenities; expect crowds and premium pricing.

detail.address: 1451 Pacific Rim Hwy, PO Box 1109, Tofino BC V0R2Z0 Canada

campground.name: Redfish Campground
campground.desc: Redfish Campground sits within Kokanee Creek Provincial Park on Kootenay Lake, reached by a walking bridge and connected to over a kilometre of sandy beach, old-growth cedar, and a kokanee salmon spawning channel; full amenities but busy in summer and closed by gate off-season.

campground.name: Darke Lake Provincial Park
campground.desc: A quiet, remote fishing lake ringed by pine and fir hills northwest of Summerland, reached via 16 km of gravel road; no potable water on site, so arrive self-sufficient.

campground.name: Laughing Raven Resort
campground.desc: Family resort on the shore of Burn Lake, a quiet non-motorized wilderness lake in the South Cariboo Interlakes area, with 145 acres of forest and meadow trails; well-serviced with flush showers but priced at resort rates.

detail.address: 7669 Double T Road, Bridge Lake / Lone Butte, BC, V0K 1E0

campground.name: Cheam Fishing Village and Campground
campground.desc: A First Nations-run campground on historic Cheam fishing grounds along the Fraser River, with 52 sites, a boat launch, and prime salmon and sturgeon access; for 2026 the site operates as private group bookings only — individual touring cyclists cannot reserve a site.

campground.name: Tyhee Lake Provincial Park Campground
campground.desc: A well-equipped 71-site provincial park campground on Tyhee Lake near Telkwa, with showers, potable water, and e-bike charging; closed by gated access outside the summer operating season.

campground.name: Lighthouse Marine Park
campground.desc: Lighthouse Marine Park is a 24-acre oceanfront park operated by Whatcom County, perched at the 49th parallel on the southern tip of the Tsawwassen Peninsula in the US exclave of Point Roberts. It is widely regarded as one of the best land-based spots to watch orca whales from shore, with views across the Strait of Georgia toward Mount Baker. The park offers a main campground plus five group camp areas, a 2-mile connector trail network, beach access, picnic areas, and a playground — making it a natural overnight stop for cyclists riding the Vancouver Crossing Loop through Point Roberts.

campground.name: Long Beach Golf Campground
campground.desc: A 76-site rainforest campground on a golf-course property midway between Tofino and Ucluelet, a 2-minute drive or 30-minute walk to Long Beach in Pacific Rim National Park; flush toilets and free showers on-site, but tent rates are steep at $55–$70/night.

detail.address: 1850 Pacific Rim Hwy, Tofino, BC V0R 2Z0

campground.name: Shadow Falls Campground
campground.desc: LGBTQ+, adult-only (19+), clothing-optional campground near Harrison Mills with flush washrooms, coin-op showers, electrical hookups on tent sites, and a packed calendar of community long-weekend events from Victoria Day through Labour Day.

detail.address: 17575 Morris Valley Road, Harrison Mills, V0M1L0

campground.name: Island View Beach Regional Park Campground
campground.desc: Sandy beach campground on the Saanich Peninsula east of Sidney, set along a broad tidal shore with views across Haro Strait toward the Gulf Islands; paved access makes it easy to reach by bike, and the fee-required sites draw families and beach campers through the summer season.

campground.name: Salish Seaside RV Haven
campground.desc: Indigenous-owned full-service RV resort and marina on Esquimalt Harbour with waterfront views of Victoria's inner harbour, less than 4 km from downtown; designed exclusively for large motorhomes with no tent sites and RV rates starting at $82/night, making it a poor fit for most cycle tourists.

campground.name: Riverhaven RV Park
campground.desc: Friendly private RV park right off Highway 3 on the Similkameen River, with shaded grassed sites, a sandy beach for swimming and tubing, flush showers, and coin laundry; primarily hook-up-oriented and open April 15 to Thanksgiving.

campground.name: White Moose Resort
campground.desc: A seasonal fishing and hunting resort on the shore of Loon Lake, open May long weekend through October, with tent and RV campsites, boat rentals, and deliberately no WiFi or reliable cell service. Access is via Loon Lake Rd off Hwy 97; phone reservations recommended as sites fill fast.

detail.address: 2890 Loon Lake Rd, Cache Creek, BC V0K 1H1

campground.name: Cranbrook / St. Eugene KOA Journey
campground.desc: A highway-convenience KOA Journey campground on Mission Road, 4.8 km off Hwy 95A north of Cranbrook, with premium tent sites and well-lit late check-in; primarily an RV park but a reliable paid overnight for cyclists passing through the Cranbrook–Kimberley corridor.

campground.name: Riverside RV Park & Camping
campground.desc: A private, full-service campground on the Cowichan River near Duncan with 25 grassed and shaded tent sites, flush washrooms with showers, and river swimming; well-positioned as a base for Cowichan Valley cycling, fishing, and trail riding.

campground.name: Whispering Spruce Campground
campground.desc: Full-service private campground on the edge of Golden, BC, a convenient base for day trips into Yoho and Banff National Parks; tenting sites include fire pits and picnic tables, with flush showers and coin laundry open seasonally (Apr 15–Oct 15) — washrooms and office close through winter even though the site stays open.

campground.name: Beehive RV Park & Campground
campground.desc: Family-run campground on open grassy fields amid South Cowichan Valley farmland, with coin showers, laundry, and a direct trail to Mill Bay Nature Park beach; primarily a basecamp for exploring southern Vancouver Island's wineries, trails, and towns rather than a scenic destination in itself.

detail.address: 780 Kilmalu Road, Mill Bay BC V8H 1E2

campground.name: Lemon Creek Pioneer Campground
campground.desc: Lemon Creek Pioneer Campground is a small, tranquil campground in the Slocan Valley near Winlaw, BC, offering 26 well-groomed sites arranged in a horseshoe layout with a mix of serviced RV spots and treed tent sites with firepits. Its non-commercial, secluded atmosphere lends itself to extended stays, and the grounds sit within walking distance of the historic Japanese Internment Garden and the Lemon Creek Confluence. It is a natural rest stop for cyclists riding the Frog Peak Loop.

detail.address: 7680 Kennedy Rd Lemon Creek near, Slocan, BC V0G 2C0, Canada

campground.name: Bear River RV Park
campground.desc: A well-run riverside RV park on the edge of Stewart with glacier-capped peaks rising on all sides, offering cyclists clean showers, laundry, and a proper tent area — a natural stopping point for anyone riding the Cassiar toward Alaska, open May through September.

campground.name: Grace Lake Campground
campground.desc: Small 10-site year-round recreation site directly beside Grace Lake, with a floating dock for fishing and outhouse facilities; cash-only and first-come first-served, sharing a staging area with motorized-trail users from the West Harrison Riding Area.

campground.name: Little Flower Islet
campground.desc: A small islet on the BC Marine Trails network near North Vancouver, reachable only by kayak or boat; free and primitive with no confirmed amenities, making it a non-starter for loaded cycle tourists.

campground.name: Riverside Resort Campground
campground.desc: An RV and caravan resort in Whistler operated by Parkbridge, likely riverside given the name, in one of BC's premier mountain towns with easy highway access. Specific site amenities and facilities are not detailed on the corporate website, so confirm services before arrival.

campground.name: Pacific Border RV Park
campground.desc: A suburban RV park situated near the Tsawwassen ferry terminal and US border crossing, making it a convenient overnight for cyclists catching an early sailing or staging a border crossing; no amenity details were retrievable from the website.

campground.name: Ellison Provincial Campground
campground.desc: Ellison sits on the northeastern shore of Okanagan Lake with rocky headlands, sheltered coves, and three warm-water beaches — plus western Canada's only freshwater dive park. Full-amenity provincial park reached by paved road from Vernon; open spring through fall and busy in peak summer.

campground.name: Watch Lake Lodge
campground.desc: Family-owned guest ranch on Watch Lake's lakeshore in the South Cariboo, with 8 tent and trailer sites in a park-like setting, firewood included and rainbow trout fishing steps away; the resort feel means more amenities than a typical campground but also more cost, and the 20-mile drive east of 70 Mile House is on rural BC road.

detail.address: 6355 Little Green Lake Road, 70 Mile House, BC V0K 2K1

campground.name: Sweltzer Creek Campground
campground.desc: A Soowahlie First Nation campground nestled between Sweltzer Creek and the Vedder River under old-growth cedar, with a family atmosphere and flush facilities; access is via a short downhill gravel road, and the site runs May through Labour Day only.

detail.address: 4745 Sleepy Hollow Road, Cultus Lake, V2R4Y2

campground.name: Tamihi West Campground
campground.desc: A large 102-site campground in the Tamihi Creek corridor east of Chilliwack, popular with anglers and families; accessed via gravel forest service road typical of the Chilliwack River valley.

campground.name: Saysutshun (Newcastle Island Marine Park) Campground
campground.desc: A walk-in island campground reached by a 10-minute passenger ferry from Maffeo Sutton Park in downtown Nanaimo; no road or vehicle access, so loaded bikes ride the ferry over. 18 walk-in tent sites a 5-minute walk from the dock, plus 5 group sites. Sandstone cliffs, beaches, old-growth forest, and historic trails. Hot showers, flush and pit toilets, potable water, and bear- and raccoon-proof food lockers. $18 per night for an individual site; open May through October. First-come first-served, but reservations through camping.bcparks.ca are recommended.

notes.Hiker/biker sites: Walk-in tent sites, no vehicle needed; bikes come over on the passenger ferry.
notes.Animal-safe food storage: Bear- and raccoon-proof food lockers at the campground.

campground.name: Elfin Lakes Camp Site
campground.desc: Alpine backcountry shelter camp in Garibaldi Park reached by an ~11 km hike with significant elevation gain from the Diamond Head trailhead; expect spectacular volcanic-peak panoramas and fully self-sufficient conditions — no road or bike access, no resupply.

campground.name: Klahanie Campground
campground.desc: A 94-site private campground in Squamish sitting along the Sea to Sky corridor, offering a functional base for cyclists between Vancouver and Whistler with easy highway access and device charging on-site. No standout natural feature at the campground itself, but world-class climbing, mountain biking, and hiking are minutes away.

campground.name: Skands Campground
campground.desc: Family-run lakefront campground on Christina Lake with 300 feet of sandy beach, swim dock, hot showers, and boat moorage — sites sit close together and facilities are self-described as old-school but clean, drawing loyal summer regulars for decades. Highway 3 access via a short paved lane makes it effortless to reach by bike.

campground.name: Piper's Glen Resort
campground.desc: A family-oriented lakeside resort on Fraser Lake, directly off Highway 16 between Prince George and Prince Rupert, with forested and open lake-view tent sites, a shower house, boat launch, and direct waterfront access. Open May 1–October 15; tent sites from $32/night.

detail.address: 14108 Highway 16 East, Fort Fraser, BC V0J 1N0

campground.name: Snaw Naw As Campground
campground.desc: A Snaw-naw-as First Nation-operated campground on the Nanoose Bay shoreline north of Nanaimo, with sweeping views across the Salish Sea toward the Winchelsea islands; the park skews heavily RV with hookups, but non-serviced tent sites are available and full amenities (showers, flush washrooms, store) are on-site.

campground.name: Delta Grove Campground
campground.desc: Delta Grove is one of four campgrounds at popular Cultus Lake Provincial Park, set beside a large warm freshwater lake ringed by forested mountains about 90 minutes from Vancouver. Full amenities include showers and flush toilets, but gates close in the off-season making this a summer-only destination that draws big crowds.

detail.address: Cultus Lake Provincial Park, Chilliwack, BC

campground.name: Harrison Country Club RV Resort
campground.desc: An RV resort in the popular Harrison Hot Springs resort village, putting cyclists within easy reach of the famous public hot springs pool and Harrison Lake beach. Likely geared toward RV clients, but the town setting and attractions make it a solid rest stop.

detail.address: 400 Hot Springs Road, Harrison Hot Springs, V0M 1K0

campground.name: Okanagan Lake Provincial Park, North Campground
campground.desc: A summer-season provincial park campground set among ponderosa pine and sagebrush directly on Okanagan Lake, with pebbly beach access, swim areas, and panoramic lake and mountain views; the gate is locked off-season and rattlesnakes inhabit the dry hillsides above camp.

campground.name: Irvin's RV Park
campground.desc: A quiet private RV park in Valemount's Robson Valley with 360-degree mountain views and the odd wandering deer; tent/no-services pitches are available at around $35/night, but the park is RV-centric and open only April through October.

campground.name: Swan Lake RV Park & Campground
campground.desc: Private RV park on the west shore of Swan Lake with tent sites looking out over calm water; free pedal boats, canoes, and a rowboat make this a laid-back lakeside stop, though the marshy shores mean paddling out for a proper swim. Coin showers, laundry, and Wi-Fi on site.

detail.address: 7235 Old Kamloops Road, Vernon BC, V1H 1W6

campground.name: Riverside Resort Campground
campground.desc: A commercially managed Parkbridge RV resort in Whistler, positioned beside a river in the Sea-to-Sky corridor; the scraped website returned only generic corporate pages with no site-specific details on layout, facilities, or tent camping.

campground.name: Goldstream Group Campsite - Prospector (Upper) Site
campground.desc: A group campsite in old-growth Goldstream Park, 16 km from Victoria, set among 600-year-old Douglas firs beside a chum salmon–spawning river with waterfall and ridge trails nearby; flush washrooms and showers on site, but group-minimum pricing applies.

campground.name: sx̌ʷəx̌ʷnitkʷ (Okanagan Falls) Campground
campground.desc: A frontcountry BC Parks campground managed by the Osoyoos Indian Band, sitting just off Hwy 97 on Green Lake Road at the edge of Okanagan Falls town and near the historic 'little falls' on the Okanagan River; easy highway access but gate-locked off-season and closed one weekend in late September for the Salmon Feast.

detail.address: Green Lake Road, Okanagan Falls, BC

campground.name: Ruckle Provincial Park RV Sites 1-8
campground.desc: Ruckle Park occupies Salt Spring Island's southeastern shore with seven kilometres of rocky headlands, tidal pools, and grassy meadows overlooking Swanson Channel; ferry access is required and potable water is shut off November 1–March 15.

campground.name: Cedar Springs Ranch
campground.desc: A family-oriented commercial campground in cedar groves on the Malahat, 20 minutes from Victoria on the Trans-Canada Highway, with a pool, playground, flush washrooms, showers, and a camp store. Tenting sites run $44–45 CAD/night plus tax — a comfortable highway stopover rather than a wilderness experience.

campground.name: Garden Faire
campground.desc: Walk-in tent sites tucked into old-growth forest on Salt Spring Island, each with its own character and a fire ring, connected directly to Mouat Park trails and a 10-minute walk from downtown Ganges; open year-round with lower winter rates.

campground.name: French Beach Campground
campground.desc: A 1,600-metre sand-and-pebble beach on the Strait of Juan de Fuca with sweeping Olympic Mountain views and gray whale sightings during migration; year-round camping via Highway 14, but facilities are pit toilets only.

campground.name: Tsawaak RV Resort
campground.desc: Tla-o-qui-aht Nation-owned resort on Pacific Rim Highway 3 km from Tofino, with exclusive access to tinwis Beach and full amenities including showers and laundry; only 5 tent sites among many RV hookups and cabins, so tent spots are scarce and advance reservations are critical.

detail.address: 1119 Pacific Rim Highway, Tofino, BC V0R 2Z0

campground.name: Everglades Resort on Hatzic Lake
campground.desc: A private strata resort on Hatzic Lake in Mission, BC, with 395 fully serviced sites, lake swimming, and water sports; sites are primarily privately owned seasonal lots and transient availability for passing cyclists is uncertain.

campground.name: Camp Cove Group Campsite
campground.desc: A group-only campsite set in a sheltered cove right on the west shore of Harrison Lake, with a sandy beach well-suited for swimming; accessed via 7.9 km of forest service road and available by advance reservation only, with no walk-in option.

detail.address: 16440 Morris Valley Road, Agassiz, BC V0M1A1

campground.name: Parry Lagoon Campground
campground.desc: A fee campground near Chemainus with no confirmed facilities in available sources; the linked webpage describes Dionisio Point Provincial Park on Galiano Island, which does not match this listing's name or community.

campground.name: Lakeside Campground
campground.desc: Lakeside Campground is a developed BC Parks site within Sasquatch Provincial Park, set among pocket lakes, birch forest, and mountain ridges six kilometres north of Harrison Hot Springs. Sandy-beach swimming, canoeing, and short hiking trails make it a well-rounded stop; swimmer's itch is possible in the lakes during summer.

campground.name: Tynehead R.V. Camp
campground.desc: An RV-oriented camp in suburban Surrey near Tynehead Regional Park, convenient for riders navigating Metro Vancouver but offering little in the way of natural setting or cyclist-specific amenities.

campground.name: Chivers Point Campsite (BCMT)
campground.desc: Chivers Point is a small boat-in campsite on Wallace Island Marine Provincial Park in the Gulf Islands, reachable only by kayak or motorboat from Chemainus; a wild island escape with no road access and minimal facilities.

campground.name: Mamquam River Campground
campground.desc: A rustic non-profit campground on Squamish's edge near the Mamquam River, serving climbers, cyclists, and paddlers at very affordable rates; no water on site (bring your own — potable water is 600 m away), outhouses only, and strong afternoon winds make it a genuine hazard for tents.

detail.address: 2023 Centennial Way, Squamish, British Columbia V8B 0A9, Canada

campground.name: Scotty's RV Park & Campground
campground.desc: A tidy, flower-lined adult-only RV park on the edge of Creston with large level tent sites and clean heated washrooms; walking distance to grocery stores, pharmacy, and pool, making it a practical town stop with no scenic draw.

campground.name: Lakeside Heffley Hideaway
campground.desc: A resort-style campground sitting directly on Heffley Lake between Kamloops and Sun Peaks, with showers, fire pits, water-activity rentals, and an on-site bistro; the amenities and lake access make it a genuine layover destination, though the seasonal window (mid-May to end of September) and resort pricing apply.

detail.address: 2544 Golden Horn Road, Heffley Creek, BC V0E 1Z0

campground.name: Coquihalla Campground
campground.desc: A well-serviced, family-oriented campground along the Coquihalla River in Hope, with riverfront and forested sites plus showers, laundry, and a playground on site; a bike park and disc golf course sit directly across the street, and the season runs late April through mid-October.

detail.address: 800 Kawkawa Lake Rd, Hope, BC V0X 1L4

campground.name: Boya Lake Provincial Campground
campground.desc: Boya Lake is celebrated across BC for its vivid turquoise water, making this 44-site developed park on the Cassiar Highway a genuine Stikine Region destination; potable water and washrooms are on-site, but the gate closes on first snowfall so timing is everything.

campground.name: Nanoose Creek Campground
campground.desc: A private forested campground beside a small creek on mid-Vancouver Island, with serviced tent sites, hot showers, Wi-Fi, and natural spring water; handy to Nanaimo and BC Ferries but primarily an RV park that also takes tents.

detail.address: 2212 Island Hwy E, Nanoose Bay, BC V9P 9A8, Canada

campground.name: Kettle Creek Campground
campground.desc: A riverside campground in Ponderosa pine and bunchgrass country where the Kettle River meets the historic Kettle Valley Railway corridor; summer tubing, canoeing, and KVR trail cycling are the main draws, with flush toilets and showers on straightforward Highway 33 access.

campground.name: Bear Beach
campground.desc: Bear Beach is a hike-in backcountry campsite on the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail, a rugged 47 km wilderness route along Vancouver Island's wild southwest coast; trail closures from storm damage are frequent, and there is no vehicle or bike access.

campground.name: Creekside Campground
campground.desc: A private campground alongside Wilson Creek on the Sunshine Coast Highway between Gibsons and Sechelt, with 14 tent sites, flush washrooms, and showers. Right off Hwy 101 with easy access to Davis Bay Beach, groceries, and coffee shops — functional and convenient rather than scenic.

detail.address: 4314 Sunshine Coast Hwy, Sechelt, Sunshine Coast BC, Canada V7Z 0B2

campground.name: Lindeman City
campground.desc: A backcountry campsite at the historic Lindeman City gold-rush townsite along the Chilkoot Trail, reachable only by multi-day hike; entirely inaccessible to loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Cariboo Trailer Park
campground.desc: A mixed-use RV and tent park on the Trans-Canada in Hope, within a 10-minute walk of Lake of the Woods and easy reach of Fraser Canyon trails; expect a trailer-park atmosphere with showers, laundry, and wifi alongside long-term residents.

detail.address: 22885 Trans-Canada Hwy, Hope, BC V0X 1L3, Canada

campground.name: Mahood Lake Campground
campground.desc: Mahood Lake sits at the quiet southwestern corner of Wells Gray Park, a family-friendly lakeshore campground noted for fishing and access to more remote marine campsites; reached via a long gravel road separate from the main park corridor.

campground.name: Beaver Creek Campground
campground.desc: Vehicle-accessible campground on the Columbia River flats 7 km south of Trail, with a short riverside grassland walk and fishing for rainbow trout and walleye; note that bicycles are restricted to park roads — trails are off-limits — and the site is flanked by residential land and the Trail Airport.

detail.address: Old Waneta Road (Highway 22A), 7 km south of Trail, BC

campground.name: Seeley Lake Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A tidy 20-site BC Parks campground beside a small sandy beach on Seeley Lake, backed by the Hazelton Mountains, 10 km west of Hazelton on Highway 16; good for a quiet overnight with swimming, trout fishing, canoeing (electric motors only), and a short marsh wildlife-viewing trail. Pit toilets only; highway access is paved and straightforward.

campground.name: Cogburn Beach Recreation Site
campground.desc: Tent-only camping stretched along a 2km pebble beach directly on Harrison Lake, with a handful of shaded forested sites; no potable water, no garbage service (pack everything out), and cash only — bring everything you need.

campground.name: Nugget Hills RV
campground.desc: An RV park in BC's Cariboo/Chilcotin region; website was unreachable so facilities, fees, and road surface are unknown — confirm details before routing here.

campground.name: Snowforest Campground
campground.desc: A well-appointed national park campground set in cedar-hemlock rainforest at the foot of the Meadows in the Sky Parkway, just 5 km from downtown Revelstoke — and 2 km by bike — with hot showers, flush toilets, and potable water on site. Both a campsite fee and a National Park pass are required for overnight stays.

campground.name: Lucerne Campground
campground.desc: Lucerne Campground sits beside Yellowhead Lake inside Mount Robson Provincial Park along Highway 16, framed by the highest peaks in the Canadian Rockies; an iconic overnight anchor for Yellowhead corridor cyclists with straightforward paved access.

campground.name: Raven's Nest Outdoor Group Campsite
campground.desc: Group-only campsite within Metro Vancouver's regional park system, designed for clubs or organized touring parties rather than solo or pair cyclists; fee applies and a group reservation is required.

campground.name: Widgeon Creek Campsite
campground.desc: A paddle-in wilderness campsite on Widgeon Creek in Pinecone Burke Park, reached by canoe or kayak across Pitt Lake; designated tent pads only, no campfires allowed, no garbage service, and creek water must be treated before use.

campground.name: Crystal Lake
campground.desc: A remote backcountry lake camp in Tweedsmuir Provincial Park (South), reached only by a 20 km trail with 1,000 m of elevation gain through alpine terrain — strictly hike-in and inaccessible to loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Sunset RV Park and Campground
campground.desc: A mossy, tree-sheltered village campground at the south end of Sunset Park beside the Yakoun River Estuary on Haida Gwaii; four tent sites with potable water and outhouses, no showers, first come first served.

detail.address: 36 Cedar Avenue West, Port Clements, BC V0T 1R0

campground.name: Spruce Lake Wilderness Campground
campground.desc: A remote backcountry wilderness camp in the South Chilcotin Mountains, set among alpine meadows, lakes, and mountain peaks; no potable water, no staffed facilities, grizzly bears are common, and the adjacent Spruce Lake Vehicle Closure Area means access is trail-only.

campground.name: Fort Camping
campground.desc: A large commercial resort campground on the Fraser River within Brae Island Regional Park, offering 156 full-service sites with flush bathrooms, laundry, WiFi, and a camp store just minutes from Fort Langley village. Gated and family-resort in feel with organised theme weekends; expect company rather than solitude.

campground.name: Cave Creek Campground
campground.desc: One of five campgrounds inside Whiteswan Lake Park, Cave Creek is reached by roughly 25 km of gravel forest service road shared with mine ore and oversized logging trucks; the payoff is two mountain lakes, Lussier Hot Springs, and trophy rainbow trout fishing deep in the Kootenay Rockies with zero cell service.

campground.name: West Pond Campground
campground.desc: A small 6-site camp in the rolling grasslands and dry open forest of the Kentucky-Alleyne area, near turquoise fishing lakes and cattle-country scenery; drinking water is on site but muddy lake edges limit swimming, and the site is open roughly April through October.

campground.name: Kleanza Creek Provincial Campground
campground.desc: Forested provincial campground beside Kleanza Creek near Terrace, offering a shaded creekside setting with easy highway access along the Yellowhead corridor; a solid overnight with potable water and washrooms.

campground.name: Poland Lake Campground
campground.desc: Hike-in backcountry campsite at an alpine lake deep in E.C. Manning Park's Cascade Mountains; a permit is required ($5/person/night) but no advance reservation, and the site is unreachable by any road or loaded bike.

campground.name: Gingolx Community Campground
campground.desc: A community campground in the remote Nisga'a village of Gingolx, at the end of Highway 113 where the Nass River meets Portland Inlet — simple, locally-run facilities in a place of deep quiet, panoramic mountain views, and rich Indigenous culture, with day trips possible to Hlgu Isgwit Hot Springs and the Nisga'a Lava Bed Park. Tourism infrastructure is basic and the pace is slow, but the setting is genuinely special.

detail.address: 607 Front Street, Gingolx, British Columbia, Canada V0V 1B0

campground.name: Wokas Lake Campsite
campground.desc: A Mosaic Forest Management lakeside campsite on northern Vancouver Island, reached via active forestry roads; rustic and quiet with a lake as the main draw.

campground.name: Wood Lake Campground
campground.desc: A dry-camping lake site within the fee-based West Harrison recreation system on the west shore of Harrison Lake; family-oriented and pet-friendly, but specific amenities for Wood Lake itself are not detailed in the available page text.

campground.name: Walk-In Campsite
campground.desc: A 4-site walk-in cluster at Green Lake Park's Sunset View area in the Cariboo, beside a warm, shallow 14 km lake with sandy beaches and roped swimming areas; powerboats dominate the main lake, but the carry-in keeps the immediate sites quieter.

campground.name: Golden Riverside Campground
campground.desc: A riverside campground in Golden, BC — a cycling hub at the confluence of the Kicking Horse and Columbia Rivers. Amenities and road conditions are unconfirmed as the campground website was unreachable.

campground.name: Upper Campground
campground.desc: Big Bar Lake Park sits in the southern Cariboo against a mountain backdrop, offering lakeside camping with a beach, rainbow trout fishing, and a wetland interpretive trail; the 34 km gravel access road is the main hurdle for loaded cyclists.

campground.name: Macktush Creek Campsite
campground.desc: A Mosaic Forest Management campsite beside Macktush Creek in central Vancouver Island's working forest; expect gravel logging-road access and basic or no facilities, with no confirmed drinking water.

campground.name: Bare Loon Lake
campground.desc: A remote wilderness campsite at Bare Loon Lake in northern BC or Yukon; no facilities are confirmed and the source page was unavailable, so treat this as a self-sufficient backcountry stop with uncertain access.

campground.name: Saw Blades Camp
campground.desc: Remote backcountry camp in central Vancouver Island's rugged Strathcona Park region, reachable only by hike-in or equivalent non-road access — effectively off the table for loaded touring cyclists. Washrooms confirmed on site; no fee, water, or season details available.

campground.name: Gwedat'sih Campground
campground.desc: A small 8-site wilderness campground in the remote Chilcotin, associated with Ts'il?os Provincial Park near Chilko Lake; reached via long gravel roads and suited to self-sufficient riders comfortable with limited services.

campground.name: Group Camp
campground.desc: Shuswap Lake Park's group camp sits beside a one-kilometre sandy beach on Shuswap Lake, with an adventure playground, boat launch, and hiking trail on site; it runs at capacity July through Labour Day, so expect a busy, social atmosphere rather than quiet.

campground.name: Inkaneep Campground
campground.desc: A compact 7-site park in riverside cottonwoods just north of Oliver, positioned as a tenter-friendly base for cycling the International Hike and Bike Trail or riding to South Okanagan wineries. The park itself offers little beyond bird watching and a short dike walk; abundant poison ivy keeps you on the paths.

campground.name: Texas Creek Campground
campground.desc: Lakeside BC Parks campground at the north end of Christina Lake — reputed one of Canada's warmest and clearest — with pocket beaches, short trails to the water, and a Monashee Mountains backdrop. Fully reservable with 63 sites, showers, and flush toilets; accessed via paved Hwy 3 and closed by a seasonal gate in fall.

campground.name: Raven Creek Marine Campsite
campground.desc: A boat-in lakeside camp on Alouette Lake within Golden Ears Park's rugged backcountry, offering 16 sites in coastal hemlock forest with pit toilets; reachable only by paddle craft, so inaccessible to touring cyclists but a genuine wilderness retreat.

campground.name: Trailhead Campground
campground.desc: A trailhead staging campground deep within Strathcona Park — BC's oldest provincial park and a 250,000-hectare mountain wilderness — suited to hikers and backpackers pushing into the alpine; hard vehicle access and a short snow-free window make it a committed stop, not a casual one.

campground.name: Vetter Creek Campground
campground.desc: Vetter Creek Campground sits inside Nisg̱a'a Memorial Lava Bed Park, where one of BC's youngest lava flows meets old-growth forest and First Nations cultural sites, with guided tours to the volcanic crater; the primary approach via paved Nisg̱a'a Highway is manageable on a loaded bike, though it is 100 km north of Terrace with services only in the adjacent Nisg̱a'a villages. An alternate route uses 86 km of unpaved Nass Forest Service Road — rideable but rough.

campground.name: Whitworth Meadow Campground
campground.desc: A small 11-site campground within Skagit Valley Provincial Park, reached via roughly 60 km of loose-surface gravel road through active logging country; potable water on site, but access is seasonal and the gate closes off-season.

campground.name: Rathtrevor Beach Campsite
campground.desc: A premier Vancouver Island park where old-growth forest meets 2 km of warm sandy beach, with all campsites a five-minute walk from the water and tide-warmed swimming at high tide; extremely popular in summer and reservations are required.

campground.name: Lakeside Campground
campground.desc: A busy lakeside park 12 km north of Quesnel on paved Highway 97, offering three sandy beaches, flush toilets, showers, and rainbow trout fishing; campground gates close off-season so access is summer only.

campground.name: Liard River Hot Springs Campground
campground.desc: A legendary stop on the Alaska Highway, Liard River Hot Springs gives touring cyclists access to Canada's second-largest hot spring — a geothermal pool in lush boreal forest — though the 53-site campground fills before noon most summer days.

campground.name: Kakwa Lake
campground.desc: A remote backcountry wilderness set on Kakwa Lake beneath 3000m peaks and sweeping alpine meadows on the Continental Divide; mountain bikes can ride the final Tote Road section but the first 75km from the staging site requires a 4x4 high-clearance vehicle, and no potable water is available at the park.

campground.name: Birkenhead Lake Provincial Campsite
campground.desc: Lakeside provincial campground in Birkenhead Lake Park reached via 17 km of gravel road, set among old-growth forest with mountain views across the lake; bears are very active and the gravel approach is rough for loaded bikes.

campground.name: Buckhorn Campground
campground.desc: Buckhorn is a hike-in backcountry campground in E.C. Manning Park, located more than 1 km from any highway within the Cascade Mountains; a $5-per-person nightly permit fee applies, and advance reservations are required during peak summer season. Loaded bikes cannot access it — this is a foot-only wilderness overnight in one of BC's most popular backcountry parks.

campground.name: Home Basin Campground
campground.desc: One of five campgrounds within Whiteswan Lake Park in the Kootenay Rockies, Home Basin offers mountain-lake scenery and access to Lussier Hot Springs; the approach is a gravel forest service road shared with mine ore trucks and logging trucks, with a technically demanding canyon section requiring extreme caution.

campground.name: Hirsch Creek Park Campground
campground.desc: A municipal campground beside Hirsch Creek in Kitimat, offering a basic overnight base in an industrial port town at the end of a paved highway spur off Hwy 16; facilities and amenities are unconfirmed.

campground.name: Mountain Park Resort
campground.desc: Family-run resort campground beside Highway 3 in Erickson, set above the Goat River with flush showers, a playground, general store, and regular live-music events; highway noise carries into the sites.

campground.name: Kin Beach Provincial Campground
