campground.desc: A small community-managed park on a rocky Strait of Georgia shoreline tucked into a quiet Comox neighbourhood, offering mainland views and shade under mature Douglas firs; no designated swim area and no sani-station on site.

campground.name: Wigeon Lake
campground.desc: Wigeon Lake sits deep inside Pinecone Burke Provincial Park, reachable only by paddling across Pitt Lake and hiking up Widgeon Creek — firmly out of reach for a loaded touring bike. The wilderness lake is a salmon-country gem with no services: treat all water, pack out all waste, and no campfires are permitted anywhere in the park.

campground.name: Bivy Camp
campground.desc: A backcountry bivy site within Elk Lakes Park, set amid sub-alpine glaciers, rugged peaks, and productive lakes in the southern Rocky Mountains; no potable water or supplies available, and the approach involves active logging roads with industrial traffic.

campground.name: San Josef Recreation Area
campground.desc: San Josef Recreation Area serves as the trailhead base for San Josef Bay within Cape Scott Park, surrounded by old-growth Sitka Spruce and Western Red Cedar at Vancouver Island's remote northwestern tip; access is via logging road with active truck traffic.

campground.name: Jewel Lake Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A 26-site lakeside campground on a quiet 3 km lake east of Greenwood, best known for stocked rainbow trout fly fishing and flat-water paddling; the 12 km approach off Hwy 3 is mostly paved with the final 1.5 km on gravel.

campground.name: Rip Rap Campsite
campground.desc: A well-run private campground on Hwy 20 in Hagensborg, set along the Bella Coola River with a river viewing deck and snow-capped mountain backdrops; flush toilets, showers, and Wi-Fi make it one of the best-equipped stops in the valley. Seasonal only — open late May to mid-October.

campground.name: Lone Duck Two
campground.desc: A group campsite attributed to E.C. Manning Park in the Cascade Mountains, accessible from Highway 3; confirmed amenities include showers, potable water, and device charging, but the specific Lone Duck site is absent from available park prose — season is snow-dependent and the park has no cellphone service.

campground.name: Island View RV Resort
campground.desc: Full-service RV resort on Osoyoos Lake with a private sandy beach, lake views, flush washrooms, and year-round operation; tent camping is explicitly not permitted, making this a skip for most touring cyclists unless arriving by RV or renting an on-site unit.

campground.name: Tyax Adventures Spruce Camp
campground.desc: A remote spruce-forest camp run by Tyax Adventures in BC's Cariboo/Chilcotin, likely near Tyaughton Lake in the Gold Bridge area; access involves long gravel roads and amenity details are unconfirmed as the operator website was unavailable.

campground.name: Golden Golf Club RV Park
campground.desc: An RV park attached to Golden's golf club, likely on the valley floor near the Columbia River with mountain surrounds; facilities and services are unconfirmed as the campground's website returned a 404 error.

detail.address: 576 Golf Course Dr, Golden, BC V0A 1H0

campground.name: Allison Lake Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A 22-site provincial campground on Allison Lake in the Okanagan-Thompson region, offering a calm lakeside stay with potable water and washrooms; gate closes at season's end so plan arrival accordingly.

campground.name: Ralph River Campground
campground.desc: Ralph River Campground occupies a forested valley inside Strathcona Provincial Park — BC's oldest park and a 250,000-hectare mountain wilderness — offering a large developed basecamp near Buttle Lake for hiking, fishing, and alpine exploration on a summer operating season.

campground.name: Girl Scout
campground.desc: A backcountry wilderness campsite deep in the Purcell Wilderness Conservancy, reached through rugged terrain with unbridged stream crossings, grizzly bear country, no potable water, and no supplies of any kind — strictly for experienced, self-sufficient wilderness travellers.

campground.name: Parkside Campground
campground.desc: A private RV park in Campbell River on northern Vancouver Island; the scraped pages returned only generic coalition content, so setting, amenities, and access details are unknown.

campground.name: Logan Lake Municipal Campground
campground.desc: A municipal campground on Logan Lake with 50 lakeview sites, flush washrooms, hot showers, and potable water — but only two designated tent sites at $28/night plus a $7 resort fee, so availability for cyclists is tight. Walking distance to trails, disc golf, a bike park, and a waterpark makes it an activity-rich overnight in a small Thompson-area town.

detail.address: #1 Opal Drive, Logan Lake, BC V0K 1W0

campground.name: Buckinghorse River Wayside Campground
campground.desc: A tidy highway wayside on the Buckinghorse River at km 278 of the Alaska Highway, offering river swimming, arctic grayling fishing, and reliable moose and bear sightings in the northern Rocky Mountain foothills; cooperatively managed with basic facilities and a gate-controlled season from late May through September.

detail.address: Mile 175 Rd, Peace River, BC V0C 2V0, Canada

campground.name: Cinnemousun Narrows Walk-In Campground
campground.desc: Walk-in campground on the scenic narrows of Shuswap Lake, offering 28 sites with potable water and washrooms in a sheltered lakeside setting; loaded touring bikes cannot be ridden directly to the sites from the parking area.

campground.name: Puntledge RV Park and Campground
campground.desc: A full-service private campground managed by the K'ómoks First Nation, set along the Puntledge River and within a 10-15 minute walk of downtown Courtenay; showers, laundry, and a camp store on site, but note that the lower campground and river access are currently closed for ongoing construction.

campground.name: Colonel Creek
campground.desc: Colonel Creek is a remote BC interior forest service-style site reachable only by high-clearance or 4x4 vehicle; expect no confirmed amenities, no drinking water, and a raw backcountry overnight with no frills.

campground.name: Tunkwa Campground
campground.desc: A large mid-elevation grassland park southwest of Kamloops anchored by two stocked rainbow trout lakes, with 275 campsites across three campgrounds and paved access; curious marmots are abundant and known to chew gear and damage vehicles.

campground.name: Cluxewe Resort
campground.desc: Kwakiutl First Nation–owned riverfront resort where the Cluxewe River meets Broughton Strait, near Port McNeill on northern Vancouver Island, with 123 sites and cabins in a historically significant setting well-suited for fishing, birding, and wildlife watching. Seasonal operation (roughly May–October); washroom type and exact road surface unconfirmed.

detail.address: #1 Cluxewe Campground Rd, Port McNeill, BC V0N 2R0

campground.name: Monkman RV Park
campground.desc: An RV park in Tumbler Ridge serving as a functional base for the UNESCO Global Geopark region, with dinosaur trackways, waterfalls, and extensive trail networks nearby; no campground-specific details were available from the retrieved pages.

campground.name: West - West Sombrio Beach Campsite
campground.desc: A backcountry beach campsite on the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail, set on a wild Pacific shore with surf and marine wildlife views; access is hike-in only on a rugged trail prone to storm closures, making it a skip for loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Cottonwood
campground.desc: A campground in BC's Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior region; no website text was retrieved, so setting, facilities, and access remain unconfirmed from available sources.

campground.name: North Beach Campground
campground.desc: North Beach Campground is one of three large campgrounds in Golden Ears Park, a major provincial destination about an hour east of Vancouver with Alouette Lake swimming, paddling rentals, and an extensive hiking trail network. It draws big summer crowds and has no cell service on site.

campground.name: Swan Lake Campground
campground.desc: A developed 44-site BC Parks campground on Swan Lake in Northern BC, with potable water, a covered shelter, and washroom facilities; the gate closes when snow falls, so access is limited to the snow-free season.

campground.name: East Beach Marine Campround
campground.desc: Boat-access-only campground on Alouette Lake's east shore within Golden Ears Provincial Park; a secluded forested lakeshore setting that is unreachable by loaded bike—watercraft required.

campground.name: Cahill Lake Campground
campground.desc: Cahill Lake is a backcountry, trail-access campground within Valhalla Provincial Park, set amid the majestic peaks and alpine terrain of the Selkirk Mountains; stocked fishing is a draw, but the hike-in approach rules it out for loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Shelter Bay Campground
campground.desc: Small BC Parks campground on Upper Arrow Lake in the Kootenays, sitting close to the free Shelter Bay–Galena Bay ferry crossing; washrooms and potable water on site, but no services outside the operating season.

campground.name: Boy Scout
campground.desc: A backcountry wilderness campsite deep in the Purcell Wilderness Conservancy, reachable only by multi-day hike through rugged glaciated terrain with unbridged stream crossings and active grizzly habitat — wholly impractical for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Hekate's Retreat RV Site & Camping
campground.desc: Small resort campsite on Moresby Island, Haida Gwaii, with four dry camping spots a short walk from the beach and full access to the on-site restaurant, nordic sauna, golf course, and pickleball courts. Reaching the island requires a BC Ferries connection from Prince Rupert or a flight into Sandspit Airport, making this a true edge-of-the-world stop.

detail.address: 342 School Road, K'il Kun-Sandspit, Haida Gwaii, BC V0T 1T0

campground.name: Haida Gwaii Glamping
campground.desc: A boutique luxury glamping resort in Tlell on Haida Gwaii, with 10 cedar prospector tents (4 ocean-facing, 6 in the rainforest), each with a private ensuite and deck; complimentary breakfast, cedar spa tub, and geodesic dome kitchen are included, but rates are premium and the site is mid-spring to fall only — reachable by BC Ferries from Prince Rupert.

detail.address: 40175 Yellowhead Hwy, Tlell, BC, V0T 1Y0, Canada

campground.name: Charlie Lake RV & Leisure
campground.desc: An RV-oriented leisure park near Charlie Lake in Northern BC; with the website unavailable, details on tent sites, facilities, and access are unconfirmed — verify before routing here.

detail.address: Mile 52, Alaska Hwy, Fort St. John, BC V0C 1H0

campground.name: Kalispell Trail Campground
campground.desc: A sunny Kootenay park set in ponderosa pine and Douglas fir forest, built around Surveyors Lake's warm, sandy swimming beach with on-site kayak and paddleboard rentals; paved internal park roads make it an easy roll for loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Loop Brook Campground
campground.desc: Loop Brook Campground offers frontcountry trailer and tent sites in Glacier National Park, right at Rogers Pass and accessible from the Trans-Canada Highway; a national park pass plus camping permit are required, and strict bear-safe food storage is mandatory.

campground.name: Golden Municipal Campground
campground.desc: A municipal campground on the banks of the Kicking Horse River in the heart of downtown Golden, BC, with walkable access to restaurants, shops, and a pool across the street; primarily an RV park with some riverside tent spots, open from April, and train noise is a noted drawback at night.

campground.name: Radley Park
campground.desc: A municipal campground in Kitimat on BC's North Coast; details are unconfirmed as the city parks page returned a 404 error, so expect basic amenities typical of a small-city facility.

campground.name: Robson River Campground
campground.desc: Full-amenity frontcountry campground in Mount Robson Park along Highway 16, with the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies overhead; showers, e-bike charging, and potable water on site, but seasonal park gates mean summer-only access.

campground.name: Valemount Pines Golf Course & RV Park
campground.desc: A private campground and golf course 3 km outside Valemount, with grassy tent sites beside Swift Creek and the McLennan River under mountain views; flush bathrooms and filtered drinking water are included, tent sites from $34/night plus taxes.

campground.name: Spahats Creek Resort
campground.desc: Commercial resort on Spahats Creek Forest Service Road at the gateway to Wells Gray Provincial Park, directly across from Spahats Falls Day Use Area, with serviced and unserviced sites, showers, laundry, and Wi-Fi; a natural basecamp for the park's waterfalls and Trophy Mountain flower meadows, but the FSR approach means a rough ride in with loaded bags.

detail.address: 988 Spahats Creek Forest Service Rd, Clearwater, BC V0E 1N1

campground.name: Summit Lake Campground
campground.desc: Frontcountry campground on the Alaska Highway in Stone Mountain Park's remote northern Rockies, with dramatic mountain scenery and strong wildlife viewing; cash-only fees, seasonal gate closure (walk-in off-season only), and rapidly changing weather require preparation.

campground.name: Seal Bay RV Park
campground.desc: A large year-round private RV park on 20 wooded acres just north of Courtenay, with 10 quiet tent-only sites and a direct trail into Seal Bay Nature Park; primarily an RV facility with coin showers and WiFi, so expect a suburban campground feel.

detail.address: 1901 Larch Road, Courtenay, BC, Canada V9J 1X7

campground.name: Kalum Lake Campsite
campground.desc: Small user-maintained lakeshore campsite on Kitsumkalum Lake, reached via a short gravel road off the Nisga'a Highway 25 km north of Terrace; sandy beach for swimming and good paddling, but pit toilet only with no potable water — bring your own.

campground.name: Phillip Lake Wilderness Campsite
campground.desc: A remote wilderness campsite at Phillip Lake in the Cariboo region, reachable only by non-vehicle means; the hard approach rules it out for loaded tourers, and facilities are minimal despite a fee.

campground.name: Willington Point Campsite
campground.desc: A Mosaic Forest Management campsite on northern Vancouver Island, accessed via logging or forest service road; reservations are accepted but site-specific details on setting and amenities are not available from current sources.

campground.name: Saratoga Beach Resort
campground.desc: A private resort on 200 feet of sandy beach between Courtenay and Campbell River, offering calm east-coast swimming, full-hookup RV sites, flush showers, and laundry; open year-round but July–August requires minimum weekly bookings.

detail.address: 8958 Clarkson Avenue, Black Creek, BC V9J 1B2

campground.name: Williams Lake Stampede Campground
campground.desc: A flat, full-service campground at the Williams Lake Stampede rodeo grounds in town, with hookups, WiFi, and laundry; tenting is available but the site has no natural appeal — it earns its keep during the annual Stampede rodeo weekend.

campground.name: Birch Beach
campground.desc: A BC Parks campsite whose name suggests a birch-fringed beach in the Cariboo–Chilcotin interior; no scraped page text is available, so details on access, facilities, and fees remain unconfirmed.

campground.name: Bowron Lake Lodge
campground.desc: A private lakeside resort sitting at the gateway to Bowron Lake Provincial Park's renowned 116 km canoe circuit, offering spacious lakefront and riverside campsites with showers and flush toilets; the final approach from Quesnel (~125 km) ends on gravel.

detail.address: Bowron Lake, approximately 125 km east of Quesnel, BC

campground.name: Cayoosh Creek Campground
campground.desc: A full-service private campground on Highway 99 just south of Lillooet, set near the Fraser River with dramatic mountain views; tent sites run $35–40/night depending on season, with hot showers, flush toilets, and playground on site.

campground.name: Campers Haven RV & Tent Park
campground.desc: A well-equipped private campground off the Trans-Canada between Donald and Golden, offering flush washrooms, laundry, playground, and mountain views — a solid highway stop within day-trip range of six national parks.

campground.name: Martens Resort
campground.desc: A managed lakefront resort on Timothy Lake offering shaded forest and open group tent sites, a free shower house, and watercraft rentals; the 20 km rural road off Highway 97 is the main catch for loaded cyclists.

detail.address: 5636 Timothy Lake Road, Lac la Hache, BC V0K 1T0

campground.name: Seaside RV Park
campground.desc: A seaside-named RV park on Vancouver Island or the Gulf Islands; details are sparse as the listing page is unavailable, so confirm amenities and services before arrival.

detail.address: 1235 South Maquinna Drive, Tahsis, BC V0P 1X0

campground.name: Downing Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A small vehicle-accessible campground nearly encircling Kelly Lake near Clinton, with a long sandy beach for swimming and rainbow trout fishing; a popular stopover on the scenic Pavilion Mountain Road corridor.

campground.name: Quilakwa RV & Campground
campground.desc: An Indigenous-owned campground on the Shuswap River in central Enderby, offering 15 tent sites with full amenities — showers, laundry, camp store, kayak rentals — backed by the Enderby Cliffs; a social, activity-oriented stop with karaoke and movie nights rather than a quiet retreat.

campground.name: Beatton Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A 320-hectare BC Parks campground on the shores of Charlie Lake, 13 km northwest of Fort St. John, with a sandy swimming beach, walleye and pike fishing, hiking trails, and groomed cross-country ski trails in winter; the gate closes during the off-season so confirm dates before arrival.

campground.name: Kettle Bay Campground
campground.desc: A large campground on Carp Lake in northern BC, accessed by gravel road and suited to fishing and flatwater paddling; remote from services with no confirmed facilities beyond basic camping.

campground.name: Bridge Lake Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A tiny 3-site campground on the south shore of Bridge Lake, offering open shoreline for paddling, swimming, and fishing amid bald eagle nests and beaver colonies; no drinking water (well decommissioned due to arsenic).

campground.name: Molly Lake Camp
campground.desc: A small campsite in BC's Cariboo-Chilcotin interior with no confirmed details on facilities, road surface, or amenities; riders should verify access and water availability before routing here.

campground.name: Conkle Lake Campground
campground.desc: A 34-site BC Parks campground on the shores of Conkle Lake in the Okanagan-Similkameen, with potable water and washrooms available during the operating season; the gate stays open year-round (weather permitting) so shoulder-season stops are possible, though services and fees only apply in season.

campground.name: Tulameen Campsite
campground.desc: A campsite near the small historic community of Tulameen in the Similkameen Valley, likely situated along the Tulameen River; facility details are unknown as the source page failed to load.

campground.name: Toad River Flats Campground
campground.desc: A private lodge complex at Mile 422 of the Alaska Highway, set on Reflection Lake, offering a restaurant, laundry, and WiFi; the website describes an RV-hookup operation and the OSM name 'Toad River Flats' does not match, so tent-site conditions and the exact campground are uncertain.

campground.name: Lamplighter Campground
campground.desc: A campground in the Revelstoke area of BC; the website was unreachable so details on setting, amenities, and access are unknown. Verify current conditions before routing here.

campground.name: Walk-In Camping
campground.desc: Beaumont Park fronts sandy Fraser Lake 134 km west of Prince George via Highway 16, with walk-in tent sites steps from the beach offering fire rings and picnic tables for swimming and paddling. The park closes each winter, the lake is prone to sudden dangerous winds, and a large Western Thatch Ant colony is resident.

campground.name: Open Bight Beach Camp
campground.desc: A remote beach camp at an exposed coastal bight, reachable only by non-road means; amenities and water are unconfirmed, and conditions will be exposed and self-sufficient.

campground.name: Cable Car Camp
campground.desc: A hike-in backcountry camp deep within Strathcona Park, BC's oldest provincial park and a vast alpine wilderness on central Vancouver Island; no vehicle or bike access, no confirmed amenities, and snow can linger into July at elevation.

campground.name: Rock Bay
campground.desc: A BC recreation site apparently situated on a bay in Northern BC; no facility or access details are available as the official page could not be retrieved.

campground.name: Bastion Mountain Campground
campground.desc: A developed BC Parks frontcountry campground in the Okanagan & Thompson region with showers, potable water, and reservations; setting and terrain unknown as the matched web page describes a different park.

campground.name: Kasiks Camping
campground.desc: Kitsumkalum-owned resort campground set in spruce forest along the Skeena River, directly on Highway 16 between Terrace and Prince Rupert, with hot showers, flush toilets, and a full-service restaurant on site. A genuine standout on this corridor for cycle tourers, with treed sites, river access, and dramatic mountain scenery — seasonally operated.

campground.name: Brown's Bay Resort
campground.desc: A full-service oceanfront resort on Vancouver Island with cliffside glamping tents, oceanfront cabins, a marina, and a restaurant — the tent option is luxury glamping rather than basic camping, so expect premium pricing but full amenities in a striking coastal setting.

campground.name: Takakkaw Falls Campground
campground.desc: Walk-in tent campground at the foot of Takakkaw Falls, one of Canada's highest waterfalls, in a dramatic glacial valley deep in Yoho National Park — the falls roar constantly. Access is via the Yoho Valley Road, which has steep, tight switchbacks that restrict large vehicles and are punishing on a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Nahatlatch Lake Campsite
campground.desc: A rustic BC Parks site set among old-growth forest, glaciers, and three interconnected mountain lakes whose waters flow into the rapid-filled Nahatlatch River; the access road is an active logging route — narrow, hilly, rough, and heavily trafficked on weekdays. Water must be treated from lakes or creeks, and the setting suits paddlers, anglers, and hikers prepared for a demanding approach.

campground.name: Robson Meadows Campground
campground.desc: A large, well-serviced frontcountry campground in Mount Robson Provincial Park — home to the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies — with showers, potable water, and e-bike charging along the paved Yellowhead Highway corridor; reserve well ahead as this is one of BC's most visited parks.

campground.name: Alouette Campground
campground.desc: One of three large campgrounds in Golden Ears Provincial Park, set in coastal western hemlock forest a short walk from Alouette Lake about an hour east of Vancouver; extremely popular in summer with no cell service in camp.

campground.name: Chilcotin Lodge
campground.desc: A historic 1940 frontier lodge on the Chilcotin Plateau at Riske Creek, offering tent camping with included hot showers just off paved Highway 20; the surrounding area features Farwell Canyon hoodoos, bighorn sheep, and classic Big Sky ranch country.

detail.address: 1080 Stack Valley Road, Riske Creek, BC V0L 1T0

campground.name: Morice Lake Campground
campground.desc: Remote BC Parks campground on the shores of large, wild Morice Lake, reached by a long gravel forest service road out of Houston; no confirmed amenities on record, so self-sufficiency is essential.

campground.name: Stemwinder Provincial Park Campground
campground.desc: A small, pine-dotted provincial campground beside the Similkameen River just off Highway 3, popular with anglers casting from the rocky shoreline; note the river runs fast (strong swimming skills required) and poison ivy lines the bank.

campground.name: Redstreak Campground
campground.desc: A large Parks Canada campground on the hillside above Radium Hot Springs with sweeping views of the Columbia Valley and Purcell Mountains; bighorn sheep wander through camp, and trails connect directly to the famous hot springs pools and the village below.

campground.name: Frypan Camp Site
campground.desc: A primitive backcountry campsite within Pinecone Burke Park's 38,000-hectare Lower Mainland wilderness; hard hike-in or equivalent access and zero confirmed facilities make it inaccessible for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Cabana Beach Campground & RV Park
campground.desc: A private beach-oriented campground and RV park in Osoyoos, likely on or near the warm waters of Osoyoos Lake in Canada's only desert region; amenities and exact beach access unconfirmed as the listing page was unavailable.

detail.address: 2231 Lakeshore Drive, Osoyoos, BC, Canada, V0H 1V6

campground.name: Tumbling Creek
campground.desc: A hike-in backcountry campsite along Tumbling Creek in Kootenay National Park; a mandatory backcountry permit and National Park Pass are required, campfires are prohibited, and advance reservations are strongly advised for July through September.

campground.name: Tyax Adventures Trigger Camp
campground.desc: A remote wilderness camp operated by Tyax Adventures in the Cariboo-Chilcotin interior; no facility details are available as the listing page returned a 404, so cyclists should contact the operator directly before relying on this stop.

detail.address: 1 Tyaughton Lake Rd, Gold Bridge, British Columbia V0K 1P0

campground.name: Garden Bay RV Resort | Park & Campground
campground.desc: A privately operated RV resort and campground on a 12-acre multi-level property near Pender Harbour on the Sunshine Coast, with tent sites alongside serviced RV pitches; access requires a BC Ferries crossing from West Vancouver and a paved drive north on Highway 101.

campground.name: Lindeman Lake Camp
campground.location: Remote & backcountry, Vancouver, Coast and Mountains
campground.community: Remote & backcountry, Vancouver, Coast and Mountains
campground.desc: Hike-in wilderness camp on a subalpine lake within Sx̱ótsaqel/Chilliwack Lake Park, set below old-growth forested slopes and spectacular alpine ridges roughly 150 km east of Vancouver. No fires permitted in the backcountry, cell service ends well before the trailhead, and the trailhead parking lot is a noted break-in target.

campground.name: Riders Ranch Motorcycle Campground
campground.desc: A motorcycle-dedicated campground in the Kootenays, likely a social stop for riders on the region's famous touring roads. The website offers no detail on facilities, so expect basic amenities and confirm ahead.

campground.name: Elkford Municipal Campground
campground.desc: A well-equipped municipal campground on the Elk River with showers, a cookhouse, and wildlife-resistant lockers for tenters; spectacular mountain views and walking distance to full town services make it an ideal resupply stop deep in the Kootenay Rockies.

campground.name: Ponderosa Campground
campground.desc: Ponderosa Campground sits within Kikomun Creek Park's dry, sunny Kootenay valley amid ponderosa pine and Douglas fir, beside Surveyors Lake with a sandy beach, warm-water swimming, and rental kayaks; paved park roads suit loaded bikes, but the gate closes outside the operating season.

campground.name: Leighton North Campground
campground.desc: Leighton North Campground sits on Leighton Lake in Tunkwa Park's mid-elevation grasslands, reached by paved road from Savona or Logan Lake; rainbow trout fishing, swimming, and canoeing are the main draws, though resident marmots are known to investigate unattended gear.

campground.name: Atnarko Campground
campground.desc: A 15-site riverside campground on the Atnarko River within Tweedsmuir South Provincial Park, set in a steep mountain valley along Highway 20; the site is best known for fall salmon runs that concentrate grizzly bears, making it a wildlife-watching anchor rather than a simple overnight stop.

campground.name: Halcyon Hot Springs Resort
campground.desc: A resort campground directly on Hwy 23 North near Nakusp, offering caravan/camping sites with access to mineral-rich lithia hot springs, spa, and poolside café; fees apply and weekend stays have a two-night minimum.

campground.name: Snass View Camp
campground.desc: A camp site in the Okanagan & Thompson region bearing a 'View' name that hints at elevated, scenic terrain, likely in the Manning Park vicinity; no amenity or access details are available as the source page returned a 404.

campground.name: Monck Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A large, popular family campground on the shore of Nicola Lake in a hot, dry Ponderosa pine and bunchgrass landscape, offering swimming, fishing, boating, and windsurfing; gets very busy in summer and sudden windstorms can make the lake hazardous.

campground.name: Flora Lake Camp
campground.desc: Hike-in backcountry camp at Flora Lake within Sx̱ótsaqel/Chilliwack Lake Park, set amid old-growth forested slopes and spectacular subalpine terrain 150 km east of Vancouver. Advance backcountry registration required, no fires permitted, and no cell service once on park road.

campground.name: Noahs Ark Resort
campground.desc: A commercial resort campground near Revelstoke (inferred from domain); no page content could be retrieved, so amenities, setting, and access details are unknown.

detail.address: 4599 Camp Creek Road, Revelstoke, British Columbia V0E 2S0

campground.name: Johnstone Creek Campground
campground.desc: A small BC Parks campground in mature Douglas fir, larch, and spruce forest beside Johnstone Creek, five kilometres west of Rock Creek on paved Highway 3; pleasant for a quiet overnight with a short gorge-viewpoint loop, but seasonal gate closure limits the window.

detail.address: Highway 3, 5km west of Rock Creek, BC

campground.name: Prudhomme Lake Campground
campground.desc: Small forested lakefront campground on Highway 16 just 16 km east of Prince Rupert, with lake paddling, fishing for five Pacific salmon species, and swimming; nearby Diana Lake Park adds a coastal rainforest trail. Easy highway access makes it a convenient overnight or layover on the North Coast.

detail.address: 16 km East of Prince Rupert on Hwy 16, BC

campground.name: Tarahne Park Campground
campground.desc: A BC Parks campground in the remote Skeena East region of northern BC; the park's web page provides no details on facilities, access road, or setting beyond its regional designation.

campground.name: Quinn Creek Campground
campground.desc: A private highway-side campground on Highway 95 near Parson, set within the Columbia Wetlands and surrounded by mountains, offering tent sites with access to a shower house, flush toilets, coin laundry, and WiFi; open May through September with a nightly gate closure at 10 pm.

campground.name: Saltery Bay Campground
campground.desc: A BC Parks campground set in lush second-growth forest at Mermaid Cove, 1 km north of the Saltery Bay ferry terminal on Hwy 101; rocky shoreline tidal pools, ocean swimming, scuba diving, and occasional orca and sea lion sightings from shore make it a genuine overnight anchor on the Sunshine Coast.

campground.name: Devil's Creek Campsite
campground.desc: A backcountry campsite within Monkman Park's rugged Hart Ranges; access is hard (no road-accessible approach), the park carries a boil-water advisory, and facilities are unconfirmed — best suited to experienced wilderness travellers.

campground.name: Comox and District Fish and Game Campground
campground.desc: A fish-and-game club campground on Colake Road near Courtenay, open year-round but restricted to club members; staffed May–September with a boat launch, archery range, and shooting facilities on the grounds.

campground.name: Central Walbran Valley
campground.desc: A remote wilderness campground in Vancouver Island's unprotected Central Walbran Valley, tucked amid ancient old-growth forest on Pacheedaht Nation territory; volunteer-maintained with outhouses, trails, and a visitor centre since 2012, but no cell service and rough forest-service road access.

campground.name: Shuswap Lake Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A busy provincial beach campground on Shuswap Lake with one kilometre of sandy shore, adventure playground, and boat launch; extremely popular and at capacity from early July to Labour Day.

campground.name: Lower Elk Lake Campground
campground.desc: Remote backcountry campground near Elk Lakes in the southern Rockies, with reservations managed by the Alpine Club of Canada; hard trail-in access makes it impractical for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Ksan Campground
campground.desc: Campground associated with the Ksan Historical Village at the confluence of the Skeena and Bulkley rivers in Old Hazelton; a culturally significant stop on the northern Highway 16 corridor, though facilities are unconfirmed as the website was unavailable.

campground.name: Dry Gulch Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A shady benchland camp tucked into a cool creek gully under the Stanford Range, 4.5 km south of Radium Hot Springs via paved Highway 93/95 — easy to reach and positioned as a quiet layover amid Columbia Valley recreation. The site itself is modest; the draw is the restful setting and proximity to hot springs, wetland birding, and Invermere.

campground.name: Haydn Turner Campground
campground.desc: Municipal campground tucked on a forested peninsula in Daajing Giids (Haida Gwaii) with ocean views of surrounding islands and Sleeping Beauty mountain; only 2 walk-in tent sites, outhouse only, and potable water available in summer season only.

detail.address: 903A Oceanview Drive, Daajing Giids, BC V0T 1S0

campground.name: Lost Ledges Campground
campground.desc: A small 14-site BC Parks campground within Kootenay Lake Provincial Park; facilities are unconfirmed and access details are unclear, making it a moderate gamble for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Sheila Lake Wilderness Campsite
campground.desc: A remote wilderness campsite at Sheila Lake in the Cariboo region, offering a backcountry lake experience with no confirmed services; expect rough or trail-only access and a carry-in/carry-out setup.

campground.name: Ten Mile Bay Campground
campground.desc: A new 54-site dry-camping ground on the west shore of Harrison Lake, reached by 15 km of forest service road; the lakeside setting and ample beach access are the draw, but there is no potable water and outhouses only.

campground.name: Twenty Mile Bay Campground
campground.desc: A large, supervised campground on a forested peninsula along Harrison Lake's west shore, with over 1.5 km of beach and more than half the sites directly on the water; reached via a forest service road and open seasonally.

campground.name: Salmon Arm Camping Resort
campground.desc: A commercial camping resort in the Salmon Arm area; with the website unavailable, specific amenities, setting, and facilities cannot be confirmed beyond its caravan-site classification.

detail.address: 381 Hwy 97B NE, Salmon Arm, BC V1E 1X5

campground.name: Inlet Creek Campground
campground.desc: A remote mountain campground on the gravel Whiteswan Forest Service Road within a park anchored by two alpine lakes and Lussier Hot Springs; active mine ore and logging trucks share the narrow canyon section of the access road, making the approach demanding for loaded tourers.

campground.name: Laura Creek Campsite
campground.desc: Laura Creek is a backcountry campsite within Cape Scott Park, a rugged coastal wilderness at the northwestern tip of Vancouver Island reached by a long gravel forest-service road and then a multi-kilometre hike through old-growth rainforest. This is a serious commitment — hike-in only, no services, reliably wet, and very remote.

campground.name: Lac La Hache Campground
campground.desc: A well-serviced BC Parks campground on Highway 97 in the Cariboo, with flush toilets, tap water, and a sani-station; the lake beach, playground, and boat launch are across the highway in a separate day-use area. Good fishing for kokanee, rainbow, and lake trout, with a short self-guided history trail on site.

campground.name: Lorna Lake Wilderness Campground
campground.desc: Lorna Lake sits inside South Chilcotin Mountains Park, a staffed-facility-free wilderness zone with no potable water, frequent grizzly activity, and rapidly changing alpine weather — every visitor must be fully self-sufficient and filter water from the lake or streams. The payoff is a spectacular high-country setting with 200+ km of trails connecting broad valleys, alpine meadows, and mountain ridges.

campground.name: Maple Pool Campsite
campground.desc: A private campground and RV park on the Tsolum River, half a kilometre from the highway and minutes from Courtenay's shops and services, with hot showers, laundry, and a dedicated cyclist/backpacker rate; primarily an RV operation but a practical city-edge stop for touring riders.

campground.name: Stamp River Campground
campground.desc: Forested riverside park northwest of Port Alberni where thousands of Pacific salmon stage below Stamp Falls before climbing the fish ladders each fall — one of Vancouver Island's most accessible wildlife spectacles for a touring cyclist. Hiking trails follow the river, black bears frequent the area during the run, and no swimming is permitted due to strong currents.

detail.address: Beaver Creek Road, Port Alberni, BC

campground.name: Phillips Creek Marine Campground
campground.desc: A tiny 4-site marine campground in the Strathcona Park wilderness, reachable by boat only — a kayaker's or paddler's stop with no road or trail access for loaded cyclists.

campground.name: Nicomen Lake Campground
campground.desc: Nicomen Lake is a hike-in backcountry campsite in E.C. Manning Park's Cascade Mountains, accessible only on foot more than 1 km from any road; a $5-per-person nightly permit is required, no reservations needed, and the high-elevation season is short.

campground.name: Paarens Beach Campground
campground.desc: A 42-site BC Parks beach campground in the Cariboo interior with potable water and washrooms; the gate closes off-season, making this a summer-only stop.

campground.name: Roberts Creek Campground
campground.desc: A BC Parks campground tucked in old-growth cedar, fir, and hemlock forest on the Sunshine Coast, with a separate cobblestone tidal beach for tidepooling and watching whales, seals, and ducks; cash is the only payment accepted.

campground.name: Gwillim Lake Campground
campground.desc: A 50-site BC Parks campground on Gwillim Lake in Northern BC, running from late May through early September with potable water and washrooms. Road surface to camp is unconfirmed, so cyclists should check access conditions before routing here.

campground.name: Leighton Campground
campground.desc: Leighton Campground sits on the shore of man-made Leighton Lake in Tunkwa Park's mid-elevation Thompson Plateau grasslands, southwest of Kamloops; stocked rainbow trout fishing, swimming, and canoeing are the main draws, and the approach is fully paved.

campground.name: Premier Lake Provincial Campground
campground.desc: Premier Lake Provincial Campground sits on the shore of Premier Lake in the East Kootenays, a full-service provincial site with showers and drinking water well-suited to a rest day; open year-round but services are seasonal and self-sufficiency is required outside the operating window.

campground.name: Little Dipper Hideaway B&B & Campground
campground.desc: Secluded lake in the Okanagan Highland east of Osoyoos, ringed by western larch and lodgepole pine, popular for rainbow trout fishing, swimming, and viewpoint hikes; both access routes are narrow, winding forest service roads (16–26 km from the highway) unsuitable for low-clearance vehicles.

campground.name: Fight Lake Wilderness Campsite
campground.desc: A remote wilderness campsite on Fight Lake in the Wells Gray area, reachable only by hard off-road travel; no confirmed amenities or water on record, making it a true backcountry overnight with nothing guaranteed.

campground.name: The Canyon RV Resort
campground.desc: An RV resort somewhere in the Kootenays whose name suggests a canyon setting; no further detail was retrievable as the website timed out during fetch.

campground.name: Apocynum Campground
campground.desc: A small private camp beside the Nahatlatch River near Boston Bar — one RV/tent spot attached to a cabin rental property, with shared washroom facilities and direct access to Nahatlatch Provincial Park for fishing, paddling, and rafting; open April 1 to Thanksgiving only.

campground.name: Tuckkwiowhum Campground
campground.desc: A Boston Bar First Nation campground in the Fraser Canyon, set between the Fraser River and Anderson Creek with mountain and water views, full facilities including flush toilets and showers, and a Nlaka'pamux Heritage Village on-site; riverside and creekside sites are closed through late May due to spring runoff, and the season runs April to October.

campground.name: McArthur Creek
campground.desc: McArthur Creek is a hike-in backcountry campground in Yoho National Park, accessible by trail only with no road access for cyclists; a mandatory backcountry permit and advance reservations are required for peak season. High-elevation terrain means snow can persist into late June and wintry conditions are possible any time of year.

campground.name: Kissinger Campsite
campground.desc: A fee-based lakeside campsite on Mosaic Forest Management timberlands in south Vancouver Island, almost certainly reached via active logging or gravel forest service road; amenities are unconfirmed and the booking page yields minimal detail.

campground.name: Surveyors Lake Campground
campground.desc: A sunny Kootenay park centred on Surveyors Lake's warm water and sandy beaches, with paved internal roads, water-craft rentals, and summer interpretive programs; the gate closes outside the operating season.

campground.name: Alouette River Marine Campsite
campground.desc: A boat-access campsite on the Alouette River inside Golden Ears Park, set in coastal western hemlock old-growth; the marine-only access makes it a non-starter for loaded touring cyclists.

campground.name: Mountain Shadows Campground
campground.desc: Well-treed municipal campground minutes from downtown Sparwood with flush showers, free firewood, and 14 unserviced tent sites; mountain bike trails run directly from the back of the property, though sites near Highway 3 can catch road noise.

campground.name: Salmon Valley Campground
campground.desc: A family-run campground 25 minutes north of Prince George on the Salmon River, with riverfront and forested tent sites, a renovated washhouse with flush toilets and free hot showers, and an on-site coffee-and-treats shack; advance reservations required and a two-night minimum applies on weekends and July–August.

detail.address: 3865 Salmon Valley Road, Prince George, BC V2K 5X3

campground.name: Eagle campground & RV Park
campground.desc: An RV park and campground in the Okanagan-Thompson region of BC; no further detail is available as the website could not be retrieved. Amenities, access road, and pricing are unconfirmed.

campground.name: Pair-A-Dice RV Campground
campground.desc: Private RV park on Highway 3 in downtown Creston with flush showers, laundry, and WiFi; tenting is available at a flat rate, and the location puts restaurants, shops, and community trails within walking distance with Kootenay Lake 20 minutes away.

campground.name: Nu Chugh Beniz Campground
campground.desc: Nu Chugh Beniz Campground sits within Ts'il?os Provincial Park on the shore of Chilko Lake, one of BC's largest and most striking high-elevation glacial lakes deep in the Chilcotin; the payoff is immense but the roughly 100 km of rough gravel road from Hanceville makes this one of the more demanding approaches in the region.

campground.name: Fisherman's Creek
campground.desc: A backcountry campsite within Cape Scott Provincial Park, reached only by multi-kilometre hiking trail through old-growth rainforest at Vancouver Island's remote northwestern tip; loaded bikes cannot approach — this is strictly hike-in wilderness camping. No vehicle access, basic facilities, and full coastal exposure make this a committed undertaking.

campground.name: Porpoise Bay Campground
campground.desc: A well-loved Sunshine Coast family park with sandy beaches, grassy areas, and second-growth forest at the southern end of Sechelt Inlet, four kilometres north of Sechelt; campfires are restricted to communal sites only, and cash is the sole accepted payment.

campground.name: Twin Falls Campground
campground.desc: A hike-in backcountry campsite in Yoho National Park's Yoho Valley, positioned near the celebrated Twin Falls waterfall; a Parks Canada backcountry permit and advance reservation are mandatory for peak season, and the Yoho Valley road is snowbound for much of the year, restricting access to roughly June through October.

campground.name: Kokanee Chalets RV Park and Campground
campground.desc: A forested cedar-grove resort on highway 3A in Crawford Bay with 17 tent sites, hot showers, an outdoor hot tub, and an onsite bakery; the beach is a 10-minute walk from camp, not at the site, and summer weekends fill fast.

detail.address: 15981 Highway 3A Crawford Bay BC V0B 1E0 Canada

campground.name: Pachena Bay Campground
campground.desc: Old-growth rainforest backs onto a 1.2 km sandy Pacific beach at this well-serviced Huu-ay-aht campground near Bamfield and the West Coast Trail trailhead; the access road is chip-sealed but an active logging road shared with trucks.

campground.name: Shadybrook Resort
campground.desc: Seasonal RV resort on Lake Windermere with a marina, beach, and full hookups — only 3 overnight hookup sites exist for the general public (minimum 2–7 nights, no tents permitted), making drop-in access for cycle tourists unlikely.

campground.name: White Lake Campground
campground.desc: Small 10-site campground on the shore of a saline Okanagan grassland lake; stays open into the off-season until the lake freezes, with no services or fees outside the regular operating period.

campground.name: McLaughlin
campground.desc: A backcountry wilderness campsite deep in the Purcell Wilderness Conservancy, reached only by serious multi-day hiking with unbridged stream crossings through grizzly country; no services, no potable water, and full self-sufficiency required.

campground.name: Cedar Point Campground
campground.desc: A BC Parks campground on Lac la Hache in the Cariboo, offering lakeside access and a calm interior-plateau setting; reservations are accepted and potable water is on-site, making it a reliable planned stop.

campground.name: Kelsey Bay RV Campground
campground.desc: Small oceanside RV park in Sayward with Pacific Ocean and mountain views, a free boat launch, firewood, and coin-op hot showers. All six sites are full-hookup oceanfront; it caters primarily to RVs, but the wildlife-rich setting and village amenities make it a worthwhile overnight for cyclists passing through.

campground.name: Grey Bay Campsite
campground.desc: Grey Bay is a frontcountry campsite on Haida Gwaii's northeast Moresby coast within the Kun⨱alas Heritage Site/Conservancy, offering road access to coastal hiking trails, beaches, and Haida cultural heritage sites. The site is not serviced December to May, and reaching Haida Gwaii requires ferry travel from the mainland.

campground.name: Syringa Main Campground
campground.desc: Syringa Park sits on the Arrow Lake Reservoir in the Kootenays, offering swimming, fishing, and boating from a large frontcountry campground, with Rocky Mountain bighorn sheep grazing nearby bluffs and Douglas fir and grassland ecosystems worth exploring.

detail.address: Hwy 3A, 19 km northwest of Castlegar, BC

campground.name: Bull Canyon Campground
campground.desc: A small provincial campground tucked into a canyon along Highway 20, where the glacier-blue Chilcotin River runs past the sites and a short riverside interpretive trail provides an easy evening stretch. The only provincial park on the long Hwy 20 corridor between Williams Lake and Tweedsmuir, making it a natural anchor — though the river is too cold and fast for swimming.

detail.address: 6 km west of Alexis Creek, Highway 20, BC

campground.name: Three Sisters Camp
campground.desc: A remote wilderness camp within Carmanah Walbran Park, set beneath old-growth Sitka spruce reaching 95 metres and ancient cedars over 1,000 years old; access is via active private logging roads shared with industrial trucks, making this one of the most demanding reaches on Vancouver Island.

campground.name: Nitinaht Campground
campground.desc: Operated by the Ditidaht First Nation on the shores of Nitinaht Lake on Vancouver Island's remote west coast, this campground serves as the gateway to Parks Canada's third entrance to the West Coast Trail. The Ditidaht Nation also operates the famous Windsurf Park Campsite at the lake, blending outdoor adventure with a living Indigenous cultural landscape that has been cared for for over 5,000 years. For cyclists on the Vancouver Crossing Loop, it offers a rare overnight option deep in the wilderness with both drive-in and walk-in camping, plus cabin and room accommodations.

campground.name: Nahwitti River Campsite
campground.desc: Remote campsite beside the Nahwitti River in northern Vancouver Island's old-growth backcountry, reached by rough logging roads with no confirmed services or drinking water.

campground.name: Quilchena RV Park
campground.desc: A small RV park in BC's semi-arid Nicola Valley ranch country, linked to the historic Douglas Lake Ranch; specific amenities, water, and site layout are unconfirmed as the operator website was unreachable.

campground.name: Hartway RV Park
campground.desc: A year-round RV park on the Hart Highway in Prince George offering a shaded tenting area with flush washrooms and showers; the hosts bring a genuine northern cultural angle (Inuit carvings, trapline stories, northern photography) that distinguishes it from a plain highway stopover.

campground.name: Canoe River Campground
campground.desc: A private campground on the Canoe River in BC's central interior offering dedicated tent sites and a range of larger numbered sites; the website is essentially a booking page with almost no detail about the setting, facilities, or road access.

campground.name: Ranger Station Campsite
campground.desc: A single rustic campsite inside Nahatlatch Park, surrounded by old-growth forest below glaciated peaks; the ~27 km approach on an active logging road is narrow, hilly, rough, and dusty, and all water must be treated before use.

campground.name: Sandy Point
campground.desc: A private campground with a wide sandy beach directly on Shuswap Lake near Salmon Arm, offering mountain views, a swim dock, playground, hot showers, and a convenience store; open seasonally to September 15th with a firm deposit-and-cancellation policy.

detail.address: 2100 Sandy Point Rd, Salmon Arm, BC V1E 2Z8

campground.name: Starchuk Beach Campsite
campground.desc: Beach campsite on Christina Lake, renowned as one of the warmest and clearest lakes in Canada, set against a Monashee Mountain backdrop within Gladstone Park; accessed via Highway 3 northeast of Grand Forks.

campground.name: Triple G Hideaway RV
campground.desc: A full-service private campground at Mile 300 on the Alaska Highway in Fort Nelson, with an on-site restaurant, coin showers, laundry, and propane — a practical resupply stop for Alaska Highway cyclists, though the setting is purely highway-town utilitarian.

campground.name: Bush Creek Campground
campground.desc: Sandy and pebble beach on Adams Lake with lightly forested upland; no potable water on-site and the access road carries heavy logging traffic, so riders must be self-sufficient.

campground.name: Gold Creek Campground
campground.desc: Gold Creek is one of three large campgrounds inside Golden Ears Park, BC's most popular camping destination about an hour east of Vancouver, with access to Alouette Lake swimming and an extensive trail network into rugged coastal hemlock forest. Cell service is poor or absent in the campgrounds, and repeated extreme-weather closures have affected access in recent years.

campground.name: Pacific Palms RV Resort
campground.desc: Full-service RV resort directly on Parksville Beach with panoramic Georgia Strait views and steps from the community park; all 84 sites are 50-amp full-hookup RV pads with no tent sites mentioned, making this a poor fit for most touring cyclists.

detail.address: 161 Island Highway West, Parksville, BC V9P 2G6

campground.name: Mackenzie Junction Rv Park & Rooms
campground.desc: Commercial RV park and rooms at a highway junction in northern BC, functioning as a straightforward overnight stop for travellers on the road to Mackenzie. No detailed amenity or access information could be retrieved.

detail.address: PO BOX 2437, Mackenzie, BC, Canada, V0J 2C0

campground.name: Buckhorn Campground
campground.desc: Buckhorn is the vehicle-accessible trailhead campground for Cathedral Park, reached via a long rough gravel road through the Ashnola River valley; from here hikers ascend to jagged peaks, turquoise alpine lakes, and wildflower meadows. A permanent boil-water advisory is in effect, there is no cell service, and the 2023 Crater Creek wildfire has opened the forest canopy across much of the park.

campground.name: Bull Canyon Campground
campground.desc: A small provincial campground set in a scenic canyon right on Highway 20, with the glacier-blue Chilcotin River flowing past — the only BC Parks site along this stretch between Williams Lake and Tweedsmuir. A short riverside interpretive trail is a nice stretch, but the cold, fast river is unsafe for swimming.

detail.address: 6 km west of Alexis Creek, Highway 20, BC

campground.name: Carmanah Walbran Campground
campground.desc: Remote old-growth sanctuary protecting some of the world's largest Sitka spruce (to 95 m) and 1,000-year-old cedars, accessed exclusively via active industrial logging roads that are narrow, bumpy, and shared with heavy trucks having right-of-way — a stunning destination but effectively off-limits for loaded touring cyclists.

campground.name: Silver Beach Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A 35-site BC Parks campground in the Okanagan & Thompson region; the Silver Beach name implies a lakeside beach setting that would suit a rest day, though page detail is thin — off-season access is available but no services or fee collection.

campground.name: Moon Shadows RV Park
campground.desc: Full-service campground tucked in the trees along the Coldwater River just south of Merritt, with flush washrooms, showers, laundry, and a convenience store; the final ½-mile approach is unpaved, and festival weekends bring large crowds with mandatory prepayment.

campground.name: Arrowvale Campground & Farm
campground.desc: A 67-acre working farm and campground along the Somass River near Port Alberni, with 40 riverside sites, flush washrooms and showers, swimming, fishing, riverside trails, and a petting farm. Family-oriented private operation at premium rates.

detail.address: 5955 Hector Rd, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 9E8

campground.name: Evergreen Fishing Resort
campground.desc: A privately run lakeside fishing resort on Loon Lake in the South Cariboo, open May through Thanksgiving, with tent sites, flush washrooms, boat rentals, and a playground; the 18 km of gravel on Loon Lake Road is RV-accessible but will rattle a loaded bike. The lake is one of BC's few naturally stocked rainbow trout fisheries and the main draw.

detail.address: 1820 Loon Lake Road, Cache Creek, BC V0K 1H1

campground.name: Boundary Creek Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A first-come, first-served highway stopover on the banks of Boundary Creek, 4 km west of Greenwood on paved Highway 3, with small rainbow and brook trout in the creek; a convenient pass-through overnight in the Boundary Region rather than a destination.

campground.name: Lowhee Campground
campground.desc: Lowhee Campground puts 80 well-treed sites in a quiet forest-to-wetland setting at Barkerville Historic Town & Park, Canada's largest living history museum and a National Historic Site; flush toilets, coin showers, and a playground are on-site, but access is seasonal (mid-June to late September only).

campground.name: Grace Harbor Campsite
campground.desc: Grace Harbour is a sheltered bay campsite within Desolation Sound Marine Park, reachable only by boat or kayak; pit toilets and designated sites are provided, but no potable water is available and campfires are not permitted.

campground.name: Monashee Campground
campground.desc: A long sandy beach on 35 km Mabel Lake, backed by cool hemlock and cedar forest — quiet, well off the beaten track, and a noted fishing destination reached by 36 km of paved road plus 1 km of gravel from Lumby.

campground.name: Willingdon Beach Park and Campsite
campground.desc: Municipal oceanfront campsite in the heart of Powell River, with tenting sites beside a sandy beach, spray park, and playgrounds; showers on site, ferry to Comox a 5-minute walk, and open year-round.

detail.address: 4845 Marine Ave, Powell River, BC V8A 1V4

campground.name: Lillooet Lake Lodge
campground.desc: Seven creekside and lakefront tent sites at a small private lodge on Lillooet Lake, 10.5 km down a gravel FSR off Hwy 99 near Pemberton; panoramic mountain views, rocky beach, outhouses with shared shower, and solid basecamp access to Joffre Lakes, Stein Valley, and hot springs.

campground.name: Moon Gate Farms
campground.desc: A small working flower-and-vegetable farm tucked in the forest off Wilson Forest Service Road above Roberts Creek, offering raised tent platforms, hot showers, flush toilets, a cold plunge tub, and communal fire pit; the FSR approach is rideable but expect washboard.

detail.address: 2089 East Wilson Forest Service Road, Roberts Creek, BC V0N 2W1

campground.name: Gallagher Lake
campground.desc: A private Parkbridge RV resort on a spring-fed lake in Canada's only recognized desert region near Oliver, with a sandy beach, full amenities, and year-round access; primarily targets RVs and cabin guests, with no tent camping explicitly listed — confirm availability before routing here.

campground.name: Rock Lakc Campground
campground.desc: A remote campground in the Kootenays region with no road access, reachable only by trail or non-motorized means; the scraped webpage covers Mount Assiniboine Park and makes no mention of Rock Lake, leaving site-specific details unconfirmed.

campground.name: Historic Hat Creek Ranch
campground.desc: Historic Hat Creek Ranch near Cache Creek sits on the original Cariboo Wagon Road, offering camping at a heritage working ranch with period buildings and stagecoach history; a summer-season stop with easy Highway 97 access.

detail.address: 3484 Jackson Road, Cache Creek, BC V0K 1H0

campground.name: RV Park
campground.desc: Skyview RV Campground sits at Manning Park Resort on Highway 3 in the Cascade Mountains, open year-round with full-hookup RV sites (15/30/50-amp) alongside a ski hill, hiking trails, and Lightning Lake; the site is RV-oriented and tent camping availability is unclear, but it is an easy highway pull for cyclists passing through.

campground.name: Pacheedaht Campground
campground.desc: Pacheedaht First Nation's campground sits between two rivers along a wild, driftwood-strewn mile of west coast shore near Port Renfrew, offering beachfront, riverside, and forested sites with easy road access. Open year-round, but unserviced tent sites run $45–57/night—budget accordingly.

detail.address: 305 Pachidah Rd, Port Renfrew, BC V0S 1K0

campground.name: Otter Lake Campground
campground.desc: A scenic lakeside campground tucked in the Cascade Mountains near Tulameen, best known for lake trout fishing and old-fashioned camping with abundant wildlife; access roads are narrow and winding with logging truck traffic, and the gate closes for winter.

detail.address: 33 km northwest of Princeton off Hwy 5A, near Tulameen, BC

campground.name: Group Campground
campground.desc: Group campground at Tyhee Lake in the Bulkley Valley, set back from a 200-metre sandy beach with mountain ranges visible in every direction; the minimum 15-adult fee structure makes this impractical for solo or small-party cycle tourists.

campground.name: Cedar Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A primitive 22-site rec site on a forested bench above the Columbia River near Golden, with two sandy beaches, a swimming and fishing dock, and direct trailhead access to 50+ km of Moonraker mountain bike and hiking trails. No drinking water on site (pack in/pack out); reached via a Forest Service Road, open May to mid-October.

detail.address: 1400 Cedar Lake Forest Service Road, Golden, BC V0A 1H2

campground.name: Kinuseo Falls Campground
campground.desc: A remote northern BC campground set amid old growth at the foot of the spectacular ~60 m Kinuseo Falls in Monkman Provincial Park, reached by roughly 65 km of gravel road from Tumbler Ridge — demanding on a loaded bike but one of the most dramatic waterfall camps in the province.

campground.name: Clearwater Lake Campground
campground.desc: Vehicle-accessible campground at the end of the Wells Gray Corridor road, set on Clearwater Lake amid old-growth forest with hiking trails and spectacular valley views nearby; the gate closes in the off-season so this is a summer-only destination.

campground.name: Steelhead Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A 44-site BC Parks front-country campground in the Okanagan & Thompson region with a well-appointed amenity set including showers, potable water, and e-bike charging; the site operates seasonally, with gates potentially open off-season but no services or fees outside the main window.

campground.name: Misty Meadows Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A 30-site provincial campground in Naikoon Park on Haida Gwaii, set among a hundred kilometres of wild beach of deep Haida cultural significance; the park is a true wilderness with no supplies, cash-only payment, and cool foggy winds possible any day of the year.

campground.name: Ptarmigan Lake Camp
campground.desc: A remote backcountry camp at a high-elevation lake inside Tweedsmuir Provincial Park, reached by trail through active grizzly bear country; wilderness experience, self-sufficiency, and bear awareness are essential.

campground.name: Municipal Campground and RV park
campground.desc: Treed municipal campground in the centre of Nakusp, three blocks from the Arrow Lake public beach, with flush washrooms and heated showers; open from May 1 with nightly fees for non-serviced tent sites.

campground.name: Strike Lake Campground
campground.desc: Hike-in backcountry lakeside camp deep in E.C. Manning Park's Cascade Mountain wilderness, accessible only on foot (more than 1 km from any road); a permit ($5/person/night) is required and no cellphone service exists in the park.

campground.name: Cumberland Campground
campground.desc: Non-profit-run lakeside campground on Comox Lake with a boat launch, kayak/SUP rentals, and rock climbing crags directly behind the sites; open March through November with easy road access from the village of Cumberland, putting 80 km of legendary mountain-bike singletrack within minutes of camp.

detail.address: 1100 Comox Lake Road, Cumberland, BC V0R 1S0

campground.name: Nancy Greene Campground
campground.desc: A small 11-site provincial campground on Nancy Greene Lake near Rossland in the Kootenays, with washrooms and potable water; the gate closes in the off-season, limiting this to a summer stop.

campground.name: Rustic Camping
campground.desc: A campground near Keremeos in the Okanagan-Thompson region; with no website data available, details on facilities, access, and setting are unknown.

campground.name: Tyax Lodge - Campground
campground.desc: Lodge-adjacent tent campground on the shores of Tyaughton Lake in the Southern Chilcotin Range, with hot showers, outhouses, spa day-pass access, a restaurant, and complimentary kayaks and canoes; the final 8 km on Tyaughton Lake Road is unpaved gravel.

campground.name: Rockingham Creek
campground.desc: A small 6-site creek-side camp in BC's Cariboo/Chilcotin interior with no confirmed amenities on record; the hard-rated access makes it effectively off-limits for loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Emerald Bay Campground
campground.desc: Emerald Bay is a developed BC Parks campground on the shore of Green Lake, a warm shallow Cariboo lake with a distinctive greenish hue and sand-and-pebble beaches with designated swimming areas. Access is via 16–18 km of secondary gravel road off Hwy 97 or Hwy 24, and the gate closes outside the summer operating season.

campground.name: MacDonald Campground
campground.desc: A 15-site BC Parks campground on the shore of Muncho Lake in the Northern Rockies, sitting directly off the Alaska Highway; gate is locked and services cease outside the operating season.

campground.name: Fraser Bridge Inn & RV Park
campground.desc: A 10-site RV park attached to a motel in central Quesnel, open March–October, with full hookups, flush toilets, and showers; a cedar hedge gives privacy and the site is walking distance from the Fraser River's historic wooden bridge and a riverfront trail.

detail.address: 100 Ewing Ave, Quesnel, BC V2J 1R4, Canada

campground.name: Bell II
campground.desc: Bell 2 Lodge sits directly on the Stewart-Cassiar Highway (Hwy 37) at km 248, offering fuel, cafe meals, and camping against a backdrop of the Skeena Mountains and Bell Irving River — a rare full-service stop on a long, remote stretch with no cell service for hundreds of kilometres.

campground.name: Cambie Creek (Winter Only)
campground.desc: A winter-only campground in the Okanagan & Thompson region with a notably developed amenity set for the season — showers, potable water, e-bike and device charging — though road surface and exact setting are not confirmed by the available page content.

campground.name: Rock Creek Riverside Campground
campground.desc: A riverside campground in the small community of Rock Creek along Highway 3 in BC's Boundary region, offering a natural riparian setting for touring cyclists on the Crowsnest corridor. Fee-based with washrooms; further details unavailable as the Facebook listing could not be fetched.

campground.name: Woodhaven Campground
campground.desc: A shaded, family-oriented forest campground near Sorrento with a short walk to White Lake; flush washrooms and free showers on site make it a comfortable stop. Tent sites run $50/night, it skews RV-heavy, and the season is May through September only.

campground.name: Haywire Bay Regional Park Campsite
campground.desc: A regional park campground on the shores of Powell Lake near Powell River, offering a forested lakeside setting managed by qathet Regional District; website content did not load fully so amenity details are limited. Fees apply and advance reservation is likely required in peak season.

campground.name: Michigan Creek Camp
campground.desc: Michigan Creek Camp is a designated overnight stop on the West Coast Trail within Pacific Rim National Park Reserve, accessible only by multi-day hike through coastal rainforest; entirely unsuitable for cycling access, suited to fit backpackers on the full trail traverse.

campground.name: Edgewater Bar Campground
campground.desc: A Metro Vancouver Regional Parks campground situated on a river bar in the Fraser Valley, offering a waterside setting with 38 sites; specific amenities and road surface details were not available from the site text.

campground.name: Hiellen Village Campsite
campground.desc: A Haida-owned campground on the northern tip of Haida Gwaii, with North Beach's vast tidal sands and Naikoon Park trails steps away; tent sites share a central flush bathroom, but water is non-potable and the experience is intentionally rustic and off-grid.

campground.name: Mule Deer Campground
campground.desc: One of four drive-in campgrounds in E.C. Manning Park, set in the Cascade Mountains along Highway 3 between Hope and Princeton; a popular, accessible base with a wide range of trails, though note there is no cellphone service in the park.

campground.name: Campbell River Fishing Village & R.V. Park
campground.desc: An RV-oriented fishing park in Campbell River, BC's self-styled salmon capital; the name signals a fishing-community atmosphere though facility details are unavailable from the failed website fetch.

detail.address: 260 South Island Highway, Campbell River, BC

campground.name: Mount Sir Donald Campground
campground.desc: A first-come, first-served backcountry campground in Glacier National Park beneath the iconic pyramid of Mount Sir Donald; hike-in only with no vehicle access and minimal facilities.

campground.name: Smelt Bay Campground
campground.desc: The sole provincial campground on remote Cortes Island, Smelt Bay offers wooded campsites overlooking a sweeping bay and beach extending to Sutil Point; two ferry crossings from Campbell River make this a deliberate, rewarding destination rather than a casual stop.

campground.name: Moberly Lake Campground
campground.desc: A large, well-serviced BC Parks campground sitting on the shores of Moberly Lake near Chetwynd, offering easy highway access and a calm lakeside setting good for swimming and fishing.

campground.name: Touring Campground
campground.desc: A popular BC Parks campground on Ten Mile Lake, 12 km north of Quesnel via Highway 97, with three sandy beaches, showers, flush toilets, rainbow trout fishing, and a 2 km nature trail to a beaver pond; gates close for the off-season.

campground.name: Sunset View Campground
campground.desc: Sunset View Campground occupies a developed section of Green Lake Park in the Cariboo, fronting a warm, shallow lake known for its striking greenish hue and sandy pebble beaches with roped swimming areas; the site is 16–18 km off the highway on secondary roads and the gate closes outside the operating season.

campground.name: Lockhart Beach Campground
campground.desc: A small 18-site provincial campground on the sunny shores of Kootenay Lake, offering the only easy public beach camping on the lake's south arm, with a sand-and-gravel beach for swimming and paddling right off Highway 3A. The gate closes for the off-season, making this a summer-only stop.

campground.name: Radley Park Campground
campground.desc: A campground in BC's North Coast & Haida Gwaii region with a fee; no amenity details are publicly available, so come self-sufficient and verify conditions before routing here.

campground.name: Viewpoint Beach Campground
campground.desc: Viewpoint Beach is a boat-in or walk-in campground on Alouette Lake within Golden Ears Park, offering a quiet lakeshore setting in one of BC's premier parks; hard non-road access makes it effectively unreachable for loaded touring cyclists.

campground.name: Schoen Lake Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A small 9-site wilderness campground beside Schoen Lake on Vancouver Island, reached via a gravel forest service road; closed November through March due to slide risk, and subject to closure during extreme rainfall events — plan accordingly.

campground.name: Arrowhead Campground, Green Lake Provincial Park
campground.desc: A developed lakeshore campground on 14 km Green Lake in BC's Cariboo, with warm shallow sand-and-pebble beaches and rainbow trout fishing; reached via gravel roads from Hwy 97 or Hwy 24, with the gate closed in winter.

campground.name: Timberlodge Motor Inn & RV Campground
campground.desc: A motor-inn-attached RV campground on Vancouver Island; expect a roadside commercial stop with basic overnight amenities, though details are unavailable as the website could not be reached.

campground.name: Heart Lake Campground
campground.desc: Thirteen-site provincial park campground on Heart Lake within Pine Le Moray Provincial Park in northern BC; a quiet lakeside retreat reached by a northern forest-service corridor with minimal developed amenities.

campground.name: Hoodoo Creek Campground
campground.desc: Frontcountry campground in Yoho National Park set in mountain forest near distinctive hoodoo rock formations; a national park entry pass and camping permit are both required, and mountain weather can deliver rain or snow even in midsummer.

campground.name: Fawn Lake Resort
campground.desc: A private lakeside resort near Lone Butte in the BC Cariboo, open May–October for tent camping, with resort-grade flush toilets, coin showers, laundry, kayak rentals, and a dock on a quiet fly-fishing lake. The Fawn Lake Access Road is likely gravel, and a 50% deposit is required to reserve a site.

detail.address: 6850 Fawn Lake Access Rd #1, Lone Butte, BC V0K 1X1

campground.name: Furlong Bay Campground
campground.desc: Furlong Bay is the main section of Lakelse Lake Provincial Park, set on a sandy lakeshore framed by the Kitimat Mountain Range and surrounded by old-growth cedar, hemlock, and Sitka spruce; showers, device charging, and on-site kayak and SUP rentals make it a well-equipped summer base. Access is straightforward via paved Highway 37 about 20 km south of Terrace.

campground.name: Kicking Horse Campground
campground.desc: Kicking Horse is a hike-in backcountry campground in E.C. Manning Park's Cascade Mountains, reachable only on foot more than 1 km from any road; a permit is required year-round and advance reservation is mandatory in peak summer season — inaccessible to a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Frances Lake Campsite
campground.desc: A rustic campsite at Frances Lake within Nahatlatch Provincial Park, surrounded by old-growth forest and mountain scenery with canoeing on placid lakes and a nearby whitewater river. Access is via a narrow, hilly, rough logging road with heavy truck traffic Monday–Friday; all water from lakes and creeks must be boiled or treated.

campground.name: Surprise Creek Campground
campground.desc: A free backcountry campsite accessible only on foot in or near Mount Assiniboine Provincial Park, a UNESCO World Heritage area of glaciers and alpine meadows; no road access of any kind, no services, and rapidly changing mountain weather.

campground.name: Monument 78 Campground
campground.desc: Backcountry campground in E.C. Manning Park near the northern terminus of the Pacific Crest Trail at the Canada-US border; hike-in only (more than 1 km from any road), so inaccessible to loaded touring bikes. A permit ($5/person/night) is required but no advance reservation needed.

campground.name: Woodbury Resort & Marina
campground.desc: A full-service lakeshore resort on Kootenay Lake offering treed and waterfront tent sites alongside a pub, marina, boat rentals, heated pool, and private beach; Ainsworth Hot Springs is a short ride up BC-31, though tent rates of $38–42/night reflect the resort price point.

detail.address: 4112 BC-31, Ainsworth Hot Springs, BC V0G 1A0

campground.name: Lone Duck Group Campground
campground.desc: A group campground within Manning Provincial Park on Highway 3, set among Cascade Mountain forests with access to the park's lakes, trails, and summer naturalist programs. Designed for groups rather than individual parties, so solo tourers should confirm site availability before planning a stop.

campground.name: Kentucky Lake Campground
campground.desc: A scenic BC Parks campground set on turquoise Kentucky and Alleyne Lakes amid rolling grasslands and dry open forest near Merritt, offering fishing, wildlife watching, and a quiet cattle-country vibe. Note that lake edges are deeply muddy with no practical swimming, and full services run April through late October only.

campground.name: Little Qualicum Falls - Lower Campground
campground.desc: A popular BC Parks campground hugging the Little Qualicum River gorge, where impressive waterfalls cascade through old-growth forest and shaded riverside trails leave directly from the sites; Cameron Lake swimming and sailboarding are a 10-minute drive west on Highway 4.

campground.name: Cedar Grove RV Park & Campground
campground.desc: Cedar Grove sits along the Little Qualicum River in Qualicum Beach with a clear summer swimming hole and forested sites, within walking distance of sandy ocean beaches, seafood restaurants, and a Saturday farmers market. Open year-round, it's a well-maintained private campground with 108 sites—ideal for families and cyclists exploring central Vancouver Island.

detail.address: 246 Riverbend Road, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 2N2

campground.name: Happy Camp
campground.desc: Backcountry campsite above treeline along the historic Chilkoot Trail (Chilkoot Trail National Historic Site, Yukon/BC), reachable only by multi-day foot travel; dramatic alpine setting but zero road or bike access makes it a non-starter for cycle tourists.

campground.name: Whispering Pines
campground.desc: A large family RV resort near the south end of Mara Lake with a heated pool, flush washrooms, and a full slate of recreational activities; tent sites are available but at $65/night this is a premium private resort primarily built for RVs, and the lake is a 2–3 minute drive rather than steps away. Open May to September with limited off-season windows in spring and fall.

campground.name: Blue River Campground
campground.desc: A private campground on Highway 5 in Blue River, BC, midway between Jasper and Kamloops, offering tent sites with public showers and an outdoor kitchen; the surrounding mountains, rivers, and lakes make it a solid active base, with tent sites from $30/night.

detail.address: 991 Blue River West Frontage Road, V0E 1J0

campground.name: Upper Campground
campground.desc: The upper of two campgrounds at Sproat Lake Provincial Park, reached via Highway 4 fifteen minutes west of Port Alberni, sits above the lake and connects to the waterfront beach by a trail through a highway underpass. Warm swimming, windsurfing, and nearby access to K'ak'awin — one of BC's finest petroglyph panels — make this park worth stopping for despite the campground being a step removed from the lake.

campground.name: Tetsa River Campground
campground.desc: A legendary Alaska Highway lodge-stop at Mile 375 with tenting at $25/night (showers and WiFi included), famous for fresh-baked cinnamon buns and house-made artisan meats; gates close at 5pm daily and the season runs to October 1st.

campground.name: Dinosaur Lake ATV Park
campground.desc: A municipal ATV-oriented campground near Hudson's Hope in Northern BC, designed primarily as a trailhead base for quad and ATV riders; thin detail on amenities, road surface, and facilities for cycle tourers.

campground.name: Lighthouse RV Park
campground.desc: An RV park on Vancouver Island whose name hints at a coastal or lighthouse setting, but no details could be confirmed as the website was unreachable. Verify amenities, access, and availability directly before routing here.
