campground.name: Falls Lake Campsite
campground.location: Remote & backcountry, Vancouver, Coast and Mountains
campground.community: Remote & backcountry, Vancouver, Coast and Mountains
campground.desc: A free campsite within the high-elevation Coquihalla Summit Recreation Area, beside a 25-hectare lake offering rainbow trout fishing and granite peak scenery; no potable water is available and access is via a 1 km spur road west off Hwy 5.

campground.name: Woodlands Groupsite
campground.desc: A group-only campsite within Golden Ears Provincial Park — one of BC's largest and most visited parks about an hour east of Vancouver — with access to Alouette Lake swimming and coastal hemlock forest trails; the 15-adult minimum fee floor makes it impractical for solo riders or small touring groups.

campground.name: White River Resort
campground.desc: A private campground beside the White River near Sayward on northern Vancouver Island, with tent sites in an open meadow along the riverbank; flush toilets, showers, and power hookups add comfort, and kayakers can launch directly to the Salmon River and Kelsey Bay.

campground.name: Whiskers Point Provincial Park
campground.desc: A forested peninsula campground on McLeod Lake, 130 km north of Prince George via paved Highway 97, offering a sheltered sandy beach, celebrated lake sunsets, and full family amenities including playground and volleyball.

detail.address: Highway 97, 130 km north of Prince George, BC

campground.name: Lightning Lake Campground
campground.desc: Drive-in campground on Lightning Lake within E.C. Manning Park in the Cascade Mountains, offering full amenities including showers, e-bike charging, and potable water; paved Highway 3 access makes it easy to reach but expect a busy, popular park atmosphere in summer.

campground.name: Emory Creek Campground
campground.desc: A treed campground on Emory Creek's gold-rush-era townsite, 18 km north of Hope via Highway 1, with paved internal roads and easy access; the adjacent CP Rail mainline brings frequent train noise day and night.

campground.name: Nakusp Hot Springs Campground
campground.desc: Riverside campground on Kuskanax Creek in the Selkirk Mountain foothills, with tent sites steps from community-owned natural mineral soaking pools; open May 1 to mid-October, tent sites have no direct vehicle access.

detail.address: 8500 Hot Springs Road, PO Box 280, Nakusp BC V0G 1R0

campground.name: Apple Beach RV Park
campground.desc: A private RV resort on the sandy shores of Tucelnuit Lake near Oliver, with a willow-shaded beach, dock, kayak and paddleboard rentals, and year-round operation; rates and site types listed are RV hook-ups only, with no tent or walk-in option apparent.

campground.name: Pacific Crest Campground
campground.desc: Pacific Crest is a hike-in backcountry campground in E.C. Manning Park's Cascade Mountains, more than 1 km from any road and sitting near the northern terminus of the Pacific Crest Trail. A nightly permit ($5/person) is required but no advance reservation is needed; no cellphone service anywhere in the park.

campground.name: Desert Lake RV Resort
campground.desc: Full-hookup RV resort sitting directly on Tuc-El-Nuit Lake in Oliver wine country, with hot showers and Wi-Fi included across all 40 serviced sites; no tent-only option is evident, and daily rates require contacting the resort directly.

campground.name: Frog Ponds Camp
campground.desc: A small wilderness campsite in Strathcona Park — BC's oldest provincial park and a rugged mountain wilderness — likely near the ponds implied by its name; no confirmed amenities and access details are unverified, so treat it as a backcountry stop and prepare accordingly.

campground.name: Kwai Lake Campsite
campground.desc: A remote wilderness campsite on Kwai Lake within Strathcona Park, BC's oldest provincial park and a vast rugged mountain wilderness; access is almost certainly a hike-in with no developed amenities and limited information available.

campground.name: Alleyne Lake Campground
campground.desc: A BC Parks frontcountry campground on the shores of Alleyne and Kentucky Lakes in cattle-country grasslands near Merritt, offering good fishing and wildlife watching; note that Alleyne Lake's deep mud makes swimming impractical and children risk getting stuck near the water's edge.

campground.name: Twenty Mile Bay Overflow Area
campground.desc: The 7-site overflow area at Twenty Mile Bay Campground shares the main site's dramatic setting: an old-growth forest peninsula on Harrison Lake's west shore with 1.5 km of beach; overflow spots are less likely to be waterfront but the lake access and forest are the same.

detail.address: 16440 Morris Valley Road, Agassiz, BC V0M 1A1

campground.name: Summit Lake Campground
campground.desc: A 35-site BC Parks campground sitting on Summit Lake in the Kootenays, with potable water, a covered shelter, and washrooms — a solid lakeside base. Gate closes seasonally; outside the operating window campers can walk in from the gate but must be fully self-sufficient.

campground.name: Group Camping
campground.desc: Group campsites at Porpoise Bay Provincial Park sit among second-growth forest steps from sandy beaches on Sechelt Inlet, making it a natural basecamp for coastal paddling and wildlife watching; group bookings carry a minimum 15-adult charge and campfires are restricted to three shared communal pits.

campground.name: Summit RV Park
campground.desc: Full-service RV resort on the Anarchist Mountain summit along Hwy 3, sitting above Okanagan valley heat with clear night skies and sage-scented air; tent sites are available at $35–45/night, and the Kettle Valley Rail Trail is accessible nearby.

campground.name: Sunshine Valley RV Resort & Cabins
campground.desc: A full-service, year-round RV resort tucked in Sunshine Valley among the Cascade Mountains, 15 minutes east of Hope, with heated indoor and outdoor pools and hot tubs; geared heavily toward RVers and members, with tent camping options and pricing unclear from the site.

detail.address: 14850 Alpine Blvd, Sunshine Valley, BC V0X 1L5

campground.name: Champion Lakes Campground
campground.desc: Three small Rainbow Trout–stocked lakes linked by 6.5 km of easy trails in mature Kootenay forest, with warm-water swimming at the 3rd lake and paddling on two of the three lakes; accessed via Highway 3B off Highway 3, with a seasonal opening around mid-May.

campground.name: Shelter Point Regional Campground
campground.desc: A qathet Regional District campground on the north shore of Texada Island, reached by BC Ferries from Powell River to Blubber Bay with a short coastal ride to the site; a pleasant island overnight, though the website returned no usable campground prose so details on water, facilities, and fees are unconfirmed.

campground.name: Bighorn Campground
campground.desc: Bighorn Campground sits inside Syringa Provincial Park on the shore of Arrow Lake Reservoir, offering swimming, fishing, and boating with full amenities including showers and potable water. Access is straightforward via paved Hwy 3A, 19 km from Castlegar, though the gate closes at season's end and reservations are accepted.

detail.address: Syringa Provincial Park, 19 km northwest of Castlegar on Hwy 3A, BC

campground.name: Illecillewaet Campground
campground.desc: A Parks Canada frontcountry campground sitting in the heart of Rogers Pass within Glacier National Park, with easy Trans-Canada Highway access and dramatic glaciated peaks all around; bear-country food protocols are strictly enforced and the site is summer-only at this elevation.

campground.name: Christina Lake Motel and RV Park
campground.desc: A private, year-round motel-and-RV park in the Christina Lake village with 7 tent sites, on-site showers, and a short walk to the lake; facilities skew toward RV guests and no tent pricing is published.

detail.address: 19 West Lake Drive, Christina Lake, BC V0H 1E2

campground.name: Quatse River Campground
campground.desc: A regional campground on the Quatse River in Port Hardy, the northern highway terminus of Vancouver Island and a natural staging point for cyclists taking the BC Ferries Inside Passage to Prince Rupert. Specific amenities are unconfirmed from available sources.

campground.name: Packrat Point Campground
campground.desc: One of five campgrounds in Whiteswan Lake Park, reached by 25 km of gravel forest service road shared with mine ore and oversized logging trucks; rewards riders with mountain lakes, wildlife, trophy rainbow trout, and Lussier Hot Springs near the park entrance.

campground.name: Crooks Meadow Group Campground
campground.desc: Group campground in Kootenay National Park. Unserviced sites, reservable, open June 15 to September 30.

campground.name: Qualicum Bay Resort
campground.desc: A private oceanfront resort on the old Island Highway near Qualicum Beach, open roughly July 1 to September 1, offering coastal views over the Strait of Georgia; amenity details are thin on the website so arrive with expectations calibrated.

campground.name: Ferry Island Campground
campground.desc: Municipal campground on a forested island in the Skeena River at Terrace, reached by a short bridge; a calm riverside base with walking trails around the island perimeter and the big-river atmosphere of one of BC's great salmon systems.

campground.name: Rathtrevor Beach Campsite
campground.desc: A premier Vancouver Island beach park near Parksville with old-growth forest campsites all within a 5-minute walk of a 2 km sandy beach; warm tidal swimming and easy trails make it a classic family anchor, but summer demand is high and reservations are required.

campground.name: South Pool Group Campground
campground.desc: A group campground in sunny Kikomun Creek Park among ponderosa pine and Douglas fir, with paved roads throughout and direct access to Surveyors Lake's warm sandy beach; group-site minimums make this a non-starter for solo tourers.

campground.name: ViewPoint RV Park and Cottages
campground.desc: Well-maintained private RV park just outside Salmon Arm on the Trans-Canada, set among pines and cedars with mountains and Shuswap Lake nearby; good amenities including free showers and WiFi, though it is primarily RV-focused with only a single grassy tent area at $40/night.

campground.name: Fair Harbour Marina & Campground
campground.desc: Fair Harbour sits at the end of a long logging road on Vancouver Island's remote northwest coast, serving as the boat-launch staging point for Kyuquot Sound; facilities are basic and the gravel access road is a serious commitment for a loaded touring bike.

detail.address: #1 Fair Harbour Forest Service Road, Fair Harbour, BC V0P 2A0

campground.name: Gold Trail RV Park
campground.desc: An RV park in Clinton, BC along the historic Gold Rush corridor on Highway 97; no detailed information is available as the operator website returned a 404 error, so amenities and facilities are unconfirmed.

campground.name: Bradsdadsland Campground
campground.desc: Bradsdadsland is a campground in the Vancouver Island and Gulf Islands region; the website offers virtually no information about setting, facilities, or access, making it a low-confidence listing.

detail.address: 2105 Shingle Spit Rd, Hornby Island, BC V0R 1Z0

campground.name: Driftwood by the Sea
campground.desc: A commercial inn and full-service RV resort on the South Island Highway in Campbell River with ocean-view cottages and hookup sites; no tent camping is mentioned, and the resort is oriented toward longer stays rather than one-night cycle touring stops.

detail.address: 170 South Island Highway, Campbell River B.C. V9W1A3

campground.name: Englishman River Falls Campground
campground.desc: A developed BC Parks campground in a lush canyon on central Vancouver Island, set among old-growth Douglas fir and cedar beside the Englishman River and two dramatic waterfalls; easy paved access from Highway 4 near Parksville, with a swimming hole below the lower falls and fall salmon viewing as seasonal draws.

campground.name: Deep Lake
campground.desc: A backcountry lakeside camp on the historic Chilkoot Trail in northern BC; hike-in only with basic facilities, a short summer season, and no road access for cyclists.

campground.name: Buckley Campground (BC Hydro)
campground.desc: A basic BC Hydro recreation site in the Pend d'Oreille River valley of southeastern BC, offering a quiet riverside overnight with minimal facilities and no frills.

campground.name: Bull Canyon Campground
campground.desc: Compact BC Parks campground in a scenic canyon on Highway 20, set beside the glacier-blue Chilcotin River with a short interpretive trail and nearby fishing and wildlife watching; the river is cold and fast-moving (no swimming), and gates are locked from mid-September to mid-May.

campground.name: Nk'Mip Campground and RV Park
campground.desc: Lakeside resort campground on the shore of Osoyoos Lake—Canada's warmest—at the edge of the Sonora Desert, with beach access, indoor pool, marina, and Indigenous cultural attractions next door; easy paved access from town, though the resort scale and pricing lean heavily toward RV visitors.

campground.name: Tweedsmuir Wilderness Camp
campground.desc: A backcountry wilderness camp within Tweedsmuir Provincial Park (South), set amid some of BC's most dramatic mountain and river scenery; access involves rough or 4x4 roads, trails are poorly maintained, and self-sufficiency in active grizzly bear habitat is required.

campground.name: Butterwort Flats Campsite
campground.desc: A backcountry wilderness campsite within Strathcona Provincial Park—BC's oldest park—set in a rugged mountain landscape of peaks, rivers, and old-growth forest; access is hike-in only, facilities are minimal or absent, and the remote character is the entire point.

campground.name: Vagabond RV Park
campground.desc: A family-run private park sitting directly on Nimpo Lake—BC's self-styled floatplane capital—with free showers, laundry, and Wi-Fi making it a comfortable base for fishing, paddling, and Rainbow Mountains hikes 30 minutes away. Tent sites are $40/night at a seasonal operation that closes October 1.

detail.address: 1891 Otter Road, Nimpo Lake, BC V0L 1R0

campground.name: Ahdatay Creek Provincial Site
campground.desc: A small provincial creek-side site in Northern BC with no available detail; expect minimal facilities typical of a remote backcountry stopping point. Verify current access and conditions before routing here.

campground.name: Coldspring Campground
campground.desc: Coldspring is one of four frontcountry campgrounds in E.C. Manning Park, strung along Highway 3 in the Cascades about 68 km east of Hope; it offers showers, potable water, and e-bike charging, but there is no cellphone service anywhere in the park.

campground.name: Lone Duck One
campground.desc: A small campground in the Okanagan & Thompson region with minimal confirmed details; the scraped website describes E.C. Manning Park's frontcountry sites, none of which match this name.

campground.name: Quinsam Campground
campground.desc: Large riverside campground on the Quinsam River within Elk Falls Park, 3 km north of Campbell River off Hwy 28, offering paved easy access and a full-service base for year-round salmon fishing, old-growth forest trails, and a short side trip to the 25-metre Elk Falls waterfall.

campground.name: Canyon Hot Springs Resort
campground.desc: Private resort campground 35 km east of Revelstoke off the Trans-Canada, set in old-growth Selkirk rainforest between Glacier and Mount Revelstoke National Parks; two natural mineral hot-spring pools are on-site but charged separately from camping, and the season closes in September.

campground.name: Little Qualicum Falls - Upper Campground
campground.desc: A scenic BC Parks campground on the Little Qualicum River with direct trail access to impressive upper and lower waterfalls through old-growth forest; very popular with families in summer and operates on a seasonal schedule only.

campground.name: Roche Lake West Campground
campground.desc: A 21-site provincial campground on Roche Lake in the Thompson/Okanagan interior; services and fee collection operate in-season only, with no facilities in the off-season.

campground.name: Donnelly Lake Site
campground.desc: A wilderness lake campsite reached by a 2.5 km hike from the parking area, surrounded by old spruce, Douglas fir and pine forest in the Cariboo; bikes cannot reach the lakeshore, and facilities are minimal.

campground.name: Falls Creek Campground
campground.desc: Vehicle-accessible campground in the Corridor area of Wells Gray Park, set among the Cariboo Mountains with hiking trails and sweeping valley views; summer services run seasonally and the gate stays open off-season until winter closes it, with no services or fees then.

campground.name: Ten Mile Bay North Group Site
campground.desc: A group site within the new Ten Mile Bay Campground on the west shore of Harrison Lake, reached via roughly 15 km of forest service road; the lakeside setting offers beach access and a relaxed atmosphere, but it is dry camping (no potable water), outhouses only, and the FSR approach will be washboard for a loaded bike.

campground.name: Tete Jaune Lodge
campground.desc: A lodge campground at Tete Jaune Cache on Highway 16, conveniently positioned between Jasper and Prince George with showers, potable water, and device charging — a practical resupply and rest stop at a key route junction.

campground.name: Helmet / Ochre Junction
campground.desc: A hike-in backcountry junction camp deep in Kootenay National Park's wilderness, requiring a mandatory permit and advance reservation in peak season; campfires are prohibited and food must be secured against wildlife.

campground.name: Group Camp
campground.desc: A reservable group site at Davis Creek on the north-western shore of Kootenay Lake, reached via paved Hwy. 31 and sized for 15–50 people; lake beach access and Purcell mountain panoramas make it a strong group anchor, though fees are charged against a minimum of 15 adults.

campground.name: Shelter Bay Resort
campground.desc: A 55-plus RV resort on a private beachfront lot alongside Highway 19A just south of Campbell River, with full hookups, heated washrooms, and coastal mountain views; no tent camping is offered and the park trends toward longer-stay residents.

detail.address: 3860 S Island Hwy, Campbell River, BC V9H 1M5

campground.name: Loveland Bay Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A small, rustic lakeside campground on Lower Campbell Lake near Campbell River, reached via a 12 km active logging road shared with heavy trucks; calm waters suit swimming, trout fishing, and paddling.

campground.name: Rolley Lake Campground
campground.desc: Flat second-growth forest park on a small warm-water lake less than an hour from Vancouver, with a sandy beach, stocked trout fishing, and short trails; proximity to the city means busy weekends.

campground.name: Heather Campsite
campground.desc: A fee campsite managed by Mosaic on southern Vancouver Island's working forest lands; specific amenities, road surface, and water availability are unconfirmed from available sources.

campground.name: Miracle Beach Campground
campground.desc: A broad, safe sandy beach on the Strait of Georgia with rich tide pools at low tide, spacious campsites in second-growth forest, hot showers, and a playground — a classic family beach camp that fills fast in summer.

campground.name: Village of Alert Bay Campground
campground.desc: Municipal campground on Cormorant Island (ferry from Port McNeill), a short walk from Alert Bay's renowned First Nations cultural sites and the adjacent Ecological Park boardwalk trails; open spring through fall only.

detail.address: 101 Alder Rd, Alert Bay, BC V0N 1A0

campground.name: Ross Lake Campground
campground.desc: Ross Lake Campground sits on a glacier-carved reservoir deep in the Skagit Valley wilderness, adjacent to North Cascades National Park, with 50 km of trails and river fishing; the lake only reaches full pool in July–August, and the 60 km loose-surface logging road from Hope is the price of admission.

campground.name: Buttle Lake Campground
campground.desc: An 85-site campground on the shores of Buttle Lake inside Strathcona Park, BC's oldest provincial park and a vast mountain wilderness on Vancouver Island, with good trout fishing and access to alpine hiking; expect a summer season, cool evenings, and rain at any time.

campground.name: Eagle Island Resort
campground.desc: A fishing-focused lake resort on BC's Highway 24 — the 'Fishing Highway' — in the Cariboo; lake access and angling culture are the main draw, but facility details are thin from available sources.

detail.address: 4950 Eagle Island Rd, Lac Des Roches, BC

campground.name: Mystic Beach Campsite
campground.desc: A wilderness beach campsite on the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail, reached by a roughly 2.5 km hike through old-growth coastal forest to a dramatic ocean beach with a sea cave and waterfall; no vehicle or bike access, fee required, and a short summer season.

campground.name: Timberline RV Park
campground.desc: A small 10-site treed RV park in Earls Cove on the Sunshine Coast, set among conifers and positioned minutes from the ferry terminal linking to Powell River and Vancouver Island; the site is hookup-oriented (water, sewer, 30A power) with no tent-specific facilities mentioned, making it a practical layover rather than a destination camp.

detail.address: 16451B Timberline Rd, Earls Cove, BC V0N 1N0

campground.name: Willow Springs Resort
campground.desc: A family-run roadside resort on Highway 97 at Clinton with tent sites, swimming, hot showers, and laundry — a solid cyclist layover on the busy Interior corridor, open seasonally from mid-April; call ahead for rates.

campground.name: The Lakeside Resort
campground.desc: A classic Okanagan resort on safe, shallow Tuc-el-Nuit Lake with a 500-foot private beach and shaded full hook-up RV campsites; situated in Oliver's wine country with dozens of rideable winery destinations nearby, though all listed sites are full hook-up RV pads with no tent-specific pitches mentioned.

campground.name: Fernie RV Resort
campground.desc: Full-service RV resort in Fernie with 11 tent sites (some backing onto the Elk River), two flush washroom buildings with showers, and twelve loaner bikes for riding paved paths into town; open year-round with winter camping packages and a ski-hill shuttle.

campground.name: Morton Lake Campground
campground.desc: A 24-site BC Parks campground on the forested shore of Morton Lake near Campbell River, suited for a rest day with swimming and fishing; open year-round but services are suspended October through April.

campground.name: Cogburn Family Wilderness Resort
campground.desc: Tent-only camping stretched along 2 km of pebble beach on Harrison Lake, with 6 forested walk-in sites and the rest directly on the shore — no potable water, no garbage service, pit toilets only, and a forest-service road shared with logging trucks.

campground.name: Nakusp Municipal Campground
campground.desc: A treed, in-village municipal campground in Nakusp with heated showers, fire pits, and Wi-Fi, sitting three blocks from the public beach and adjacent to community sports fields; open seasonally from May 1 with a non-refundable booking fee.

campground.name: Pacheedaht Campground
campground.desc: A Pacheedaht First Nation campground where two rivers meet the Pacific at Port Renfrew, with a full mile of rugged beachfront alongside forested and riverside pitches, open all year. Unserviced tent rates run $45–$54/night depending on season—premium pricing that reflects the exceptional west coast setting near Avatar Grove and Botanical Beach.

detail.address: 305 Pachidah Rd, Port Renfrew, BC V0S 1K0

campground.name: Mount Fernie Campground
campground.desc: A well-serviced provincial campground 3 km south of Fernie on Highway 3, set in Rocky Mountain forest beside a Lizard Creek waterfall, with showers and potable water on-site and the town's restaurants, trails, and mountain-bike network minutes away. Gates close outside the summer operating season.

detail.address: 3 km South of Fernie on Highway 3, Fernie, BC

campground.name: Paradise Bay Campground
campground.desc: A campground named for its bay setting on Vancouver Island or the Gulf Islands; no facility, access, or amenity details could be confirmed from the linked website, which returned only RDN navigation menus unrelated to this site.

campground.name: Compressor
campground.desc: A remote backcountry campsite deep in Purcell Wilderness Conservancy Park, reachable only by multi-day foot travel through rugged glaciated terrain with unbridged creek crossings, grizzly country, and no potable water; demands full wilderness self-sufficiency before entry.

campground.name: Cameron Lake Campground
campground.desc: Municipal campground on Cameron Lake near Hudson's Hope in Northern BC, appearing to offer lakeside camping with a playground; limited details available as the page content did not fully load.

campground.name: Cascade Peninsula Campground
campground.desc: Forested Recreation Site on the sheltered east shore of Harrison Lake, a draw for swimmers and kayakers; no potable water, pack-out garbage, pit toilets only, cash fees, and a forest-service-road approach.

campground.name: China Beach Campground
campground.desc: A 79-site vehicle-accessible forested campground at the east end of Juan de Fuca Provincial Park, with trail connections to China Beach and Second Beach on the Strait of Juan de Fuca; the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail trailhead is roughly 1 km west, making this a serious coastal hiking base.

campground.name: Kiskatinaw Campground
campground.desc: A 28-site BC Parks campground on the Kiskatinaw River along the original Alaska Highway, anchored by a rare surviving WWII-era curved wooden trestle bridge just a short walk from camp; the warm, slow river is good for tubing though fishing is limited by murky water.

campground.name: Bailey Bridge Cabins & Campsites
campground.desc: A commercial riverside campground on the Bella Coola River with a sandy beach, tent sites, powered RV pads, and rustic cabins near Hagensborg, in a remote valley renowned for salmon fishing, hiking, and dark-sky stargazing. Reaching it requires either a long drive down Highway 20 or a ferry crossing.

campground.name: Blanket Creek Campground
campground.desc: A family-oriented provincial park on the Columbia River 25 km south of Revelstoke via paved Hwy 23, with a warm man-made swimming lagoon, adventure playground, and easy trail to Sutherland Falls; bears are active in fall due to old orchard trees, so a spotless camp is essential.

campground.name: Hannah Lake Campsite
campground.desc: A rustic campsite on Hannah Lake inside Nahatlatch Provincial Park, set among old-growth forest, mountain peaks, and a three-lake wilderness draining into the Nahatlatch River. Access requires a long drive on an active logging road that is narrow, hilly, rough, and dusty; all water must be treated.

campground.name: Bromley Rock Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A small, forested BC Parks campground on the Similkameen River directly off Highway 3, 21 km east of Princeton, with a striking rock bluff backdrop, river swimming, a popular kayak put-in, and tubing downstream to Stemwinder Park; variable currents and no lifeguards warrant caution.

detail.address: Highway 3, 21 km east of Princeton, BC

campground.name: Salmon Beach Campsite
campground.desc: A named beach campsite in the Okanagan & Thompson region; no matched web content is available, so setting, facilities, and access are unverified beyond OSM data.

campground.name: Murray River Campsite
campground.desc: Frontcountry campsite in Monkman Provincial Park, positioned near Kinuseo Falls where the Murray River plunges 60 metres — taller than Niagara Falls — deep in the Hart Ranges; expect a long gravel forest service road to reach it and a boil-water advisory once you arrive.

campground.name: Hampton Campground
campground.desc: Hampton Campground is a full-service frontcountry site within E.C. Manning Park, set in the Cascade Mountains along Highway 3 with showers, potable water, and e-bike charging; no cellphone service anywhere in the park.

campground.name: Horsefly Lake
campground.desc: A developed BC Parks campground on a large, deep Cariboo lake with a roped swimming beach, rainbow trout fishing, and rentable canoes amid old-growth cedars; the 65 km access from Hwy 97 is mostly paved with a final 10 km of well-maintained gravel.

campground.name: Crazy Creek Hot Pools Resort
campground.desc: A four-season resort on the Trans-Canada between Shuswap Lake and Revelstoke, set along the Eagle River with outdoor hot pools (40°C soak to 8°C cold plunge) open every day of the year; tenting and unserviced sites share the grounds with full RV hookups and cabins, so expect a resort atmosphere and fees.

campground.name: Valemount Pines Golf Course & RV Park
campground.desc: A wooded, family-oriented RV park and golf course 3 km from Valemount town, with grassy shaded tent sites beside Swift Creek and the McLennan River, filtered drinking water, and flush bathrooms; expect a commercial atmosphere but solid amenities.

campground.name: Pyramid Campground
campground.desc: A 50-site vehicle-accessible campground in the main Corridor of Wells Gray Provincial Park, set among old-growth forest with easy access to hiking trails, waterfalls, and the scenic park road; a summer concession operates nearby.

campground.name: Sayres Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A rustic forest service recreation site on Sayres Lake reached via an active gravel logging road with a steep, potentially 4WD-required final 2 km; no water on site so riders must carry all they need.

campground.name: Marmot Campground
campground.desc: A remote campsite reachable only by non-cycling means, with no confirmed amenities on record; the linked park website covers Mount Robson Park generally but does not describe Marmot Campground specifically, leaving details unverified.

campground.name: Bere Point Regional Park Campground
campground.desc: A 30-site regional campground on the northern tip of Malcolm Island, reached by BC Ferries from Port McNeill then a short paved ride to a dramatic coastal headland celebrated as one of BC's best spots to watch orcas from shore during summer salmon runs; pit toilets and reservations available.

campground.name: Irony Creek Campsite
campground.desc: A hike-in backcountry campsite set within Cape Scott Provincial Park's old-growth coastal rainforest on the remote northwestern tip of Vancouver Island; accessible only on foot via multi-day wilderness trails, making it effectively off-limits for loaded touring cyclists.

campground.name: Azouzetta Lake Lodge & Cabins
campground.desc: A lakeside lodge and campground in the Pine Pass on paved Highway 97, with an on-site café serving homemade meals, kayaking, fishing, and adjacent Powder King ski resort; a commercial, year-round destination that draws both summer and winter visitors.

detail.address: Mile 122 John Hart Hwy, Mackenzie, BC V0J 2C0

campground.name: Alces Lake Campground
campground.desc: A remote mountain lake campground deep in Whiteswan Lake Park, offering moose sightings on fog-shrouded Alces Lake, trophy rainbow trout fishing, and a short drive to Lussier Hot Springs; the 25 km gravel forest service road carries active ore and logging trucks and requires real caution.

detail.address: Whiteswan Lake Park, Canal Flats, BC

campground.name: Babine Lake Campground
campground.desc: A free 16-site provincial campground on the shores of Babine Lake — the longest natural lake in BC — in the remote forests of Northern BC; no amenities are confirmed so arrive self-sufficient.

campground.name: Broadview Lake
campground.desc: A remote lake campsite in the Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior region; access is hard and amenities are unconfirmed, making it a serious undertaking for a loaded touring cyclist.

campground.name: Gibsons Pass Ski Area RV Area
campground.desc: A utilitarian RV area situated at the Gibson Pass ski hill within Manning Provincial Park, best suited as an overnight base for skiers and snowshoers with convenient slope access; it lacks the amenities and setting of the nearby Skyview RV Campground.

campground.name: Juniper Beach Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A semi-arid canyon campground beside the Thompson River just off Highway 1, ringed by sagebrush, prickly pear cactus, and juniper with freight trains rumbling past; the river looks inviting but runs dangerously swift in early summer and the exposed desert heat demands sun protection.

campground.name: Telegraph Cove Campground
campground.desc: A large old-growth forest campground 1 km from the famous historic boardwalk village, serving as the base for world-class orca watching in Johnstone Strait and coastal kayaking; open May–September only, with tent sites starting at $45/night.

campground.name: White River Campground
campground.desc: A high-elevation Kootenay Rocky Mountain park reached by 25 km of gravel forest service road shared with active mine ore and logging trucks; natural hot springs, two mountain lakes, and moose sightings reward the rough approach.

campground.name: The Orchard at Oliver
campground.desc: Set in a working fruit orchard on Hwy 97 in Oliver, this full-service RV park offers shaded grass sites, secure bike storage at no charge, and flush washrooms a short walk from town. Flat roads, surrounding wineries, and nearby lakes suit a relaxed cycling tour of the Okanagan.

campground.name: Chilliwack Lake Provincial Campground
campground.location: Remote & backcountry, Vancouver, Coast and Mountains
campground.community: Remote & backcountry, Vancouver, Coast and Mountains
campground.desc: Large frontcountry campground at the end of a 40 km valley road on sparkling Chilliwack Lake, ringed by old-growth forest and subalpine ridges, with 40 km of trails and backcountry lake access; no cell service past the last store on the approach.

campground.name: EZ RV Park
campground.desc: An RV-oriented park on the river in Oliver, off Highway 97, with full hookups, showers, and internet in the heart of South Okanagan wine country; no tent sites are listed, so cycle tourers seeking a pitch may find limited options here.

campground.name: King Gething Park
campground.desc: Municipal campground in Hudson's Hope serving the Peace River dam country, open May Long Weekend through Labour Day — a functional base for exploring WAC Bennett Dam, dinosaur fossil sites, and local trails with minimal site-specific detail published.

campground.name: Emperor Falls Campground
campground.desc: Backcountry campsite on the Berg Lake Trail in Mount Robson Provincial Park, set near the thundering Emperor Falls on the Robson River; access is hike-in only (~11 km from the trailhead), making it a summer-season, non-cycling overnight.

campground.name: Laughing Falls Campground
campground.desc: A backcountry campsite in Yoho National Park's Yoho Valley, reachable only by trail after driving a road that is snowbound much of the year; a backcountry permit, advance reservation (July–September), and National Park Pass are all required.

campground.name: Summit River Lodge & Campsites
campground.desc: Family-run lodge and campground 20 km from Valemount, set on 40 acres with Albreda Glacier views and Camp Creek flowing through the property; primarily lodge and RV-focused with year-round operation, tent-specific amenities and pricing not detailed on the site.

campground.name: Lower Horse Camp
campground.desc: A remote wilderness camp associated with Kakwa Park, set amid ice-clad peaks and alpine meadows near the Continental Divide; reaching it demands roughly 100 km on a rutted, 4x4-only forest service road, and no potable water is available.

campground.name: MK Bay Marina
campground.desc: A working marina campground on Douglas Channel near Kitimat offering the only beachfront sites in the area, with coin-operated showers and laundry; camping is first-come, first-served and there is no WiFi at the sites.

detail.address: 4935 Kitamaat Village Road, Kitimat, BC V8C 2G7

campground.name: Kicking Horse Campground
campground.desc: A large Parks Canada campground set in the Kicking Horse River valley at the heart of Yoho National Park, with paved Trans-Canada–adjacent access and peaks filling every sightline; the natural anchor point for Takakkaw Falls, Emerald Lake, and Burgess Shale guided hikes.

campground.name: Walk-In Campground
campground.desc: Walk-in campsites at Rathtrevor Beach nestle among old-growth trees within a five-minute stroll of a 2-km sandy beach where low tide exposes nearly a kilometre of warm tidal flats; summer reservations are required at one of Vancouver Island's busiest parks.

campground.name: Country Hideaway Campground
campground.desc: A family-run private campground on the Kettle River east of Grand Forks, with flush showers, a sandy beach, and paved/easy access just 5 km off Highway 3; the Trans-Canada Trail runs directly from camp.

detail.address: 1285 Manly Meadows Rd, Grand Forks, BC V0H 1H9

campground.name: Telegraph Resort Campground
campground.desc: The Forest RV Campground is part of Telegraph Cove Resort, nestled among old-growth trees on the northeast corner of Vancouver Island, about 1 km uphill from the historic boardwalk village. With over 100 serviced sites accommodating both tenters and RVs, the campground sits trailside to the Bauza Cove coastal trail and the Dave Farrant Blinkhorn Trail. The resort is the gateway to whale watching, the Whale Interpretive Centre, and marine activities in Johnstone Strait.

campground.name: Link River Regional Park Campground
campground.desc: A revitalized 41-site municipal campground where Link River meets Alice Lake in remote Port Alice, offering a swimming beach, boat launch, horseshoe pits, and play equipment; no potable water on site, and the village sits 30 minutes off Highway 19.

campground.name: Telte-Yet
campground.desc: A fee campground in BC's Lower Mainland & Fraser Valley; the source website was unreachable and no amenity or access details are confirmed beyond OSM tags, so specifics of setting and facilities remain unknown.

campground.name: Bayside Campgroud RV & Park
campground.desc: A tidy private campground on Sechelt Inlet Road in Sechelt, two minutes from Porpoise Bay Provincial Park, with treed tent sites, coin showers, flush toilets, and easy access to Sechelt Inlet paddling and Coast Gravity Park's downhill trails; requires a ferry crossing from the mainland and charges nightly fees.

detail.address: 6040 Sechelt Inlet Road, Sechelt, BC V0N 3A3

campground.name: Bates Beach Oceanfront Resort
campground.desc: A private oceanfront resort on Georgia Strait just north of Courtenay, offering tidal pools, sandbars, and coastal mountain views alongside kayak rentals and a boat launch; tenting sites share the grounds with full-service RV hookups.

campground.name: Chase Lion's Club RV Park
campground.desc: A community-operated Lions Club RV park in the town of Chase, BC — a functional in-town stop in the Thompson region near Little Shuswap Lake; specific amenities and pricing could not be verified as the park website was unreachable.

campground.name: Roberts Roost Resort
campground.desc: Family-owned lakefront resort on Dragon Lake, 10 minutes from Quesnel, with unserviced tent sites offering coin showers, playground, boat rentals, and access to trophy rainbow trout fishing; resort-style atmosphere with fees.

campground.name: Homestead campground
campground.desc: Herald Park fronts the west shore of Shuswap Lake with a large roped swimming beach, forested uplands, and a self-guided trail to Margaret Falls; a busy, popular frontcountry park that works well as a base for Shuswap-area touring.

campground.name: Upper Campbell Reservoir Campground
campground.desc: A free BC Hydro recreation campground on the shore of Upper Campbell Reservoir near Strathcona Provincial Park, accessible from Highway 28; amenities are unconfirmed so expect a basic experience with no guaranteed water or services.

campground.name: Cevallos Campground
campground.desc: A basic campsite near the remote village of Zeballos at the head of Zeballos Inlet on the wild west coast of Vancouver Island, reached via a 40 km well-maintained gravel road off Highway 19; the area draws kayakers, sport fishers, and nature travellers but specific campground amenities are unconfirmed.

campground.name: Inland Lake Campground
campground.desc: A provincial lakeshore park north of Powell River reached via a short steep hill and roughly 7 km of gravel road; the flat 13 km loop trail around the lake doubles as a cycling circuit, and the lake offers warm-summer swimming, fishing, and paddling, though the beach area is minimal and off-season the site runs with no services or fees.

campground.name: Martha Creek Provincial Campground
campground.desc: Reservoir-side campground 20 km north of Revelstoke on paved Highway 23, with one of the few sandy beaches in the region, a fishing wharf, playground, and an indoor picnic shelter; gate closes outside the operating season.

campground.name: Forest Loop Campground
campground.desc: Rolling grasslands and dry open forest frame two turquoise fishing lakes—Kentucky and Alleyne—about 90 minutes from the central Okanagan; a staffed BC Parks frontcountry site open roughly April to late October with water standpipes and good highway access.

campground.name: Heather Lake Campsite
campground.desc: Remote wilderness campsite at Heather Lake within a Northern BC provincial park; expect a backcountry setting with minimal or no facilities and a likely rough or hike-in approach to reach the lake.

campground.name: Forest Rose Campground
campground.desc: A forested creek-side campground on Williams Creek at the edge of Barkerville Historic Town, western North America's largest living history museum; flush toilets, coin showers, and potable water on site, though cyclists must push bikes through the heritage townsite itself. Open mid-May to late September only.

campground.name: Tyax Wilderness Resort and Spa
campground.desc: A lakeside wilderness lodge campground on Tyaughton Lake in the Southern Chilcotin Range, sharing grounds with a spa, gourmet restaurant, and heliskiing operation — a social, resort atmosphere far from any town. The long approach via Lillooet and Gold Bridge includes an 8 km gravel stretch on Tyaughton Lake Road.

campground.name: Frank Carpenter Memorial Campground
campground.desc: A village-run campground right on the Kettle River in downtown Midway, with flush toilets, showers, and a dedicated cyclist shelter; just blocks south of Highway 3 with full town amenities within walking distance.

campground.name: Niskonlith Lake Campground
campground.desc: A 29-site BC Parks campground set on Niskonlith Lake in the Thompson region, operating seasonally with no services outside the window; camping is allowed while the gate remains open, making it a quiet off-season option.

campground.name: Little Yoho Valley Campground
campground.desc: A backcountry campground deep in the Little Yoho Valley of Yoho National Park, reachable by trail only with a mandatory overnight permit and advance reservation; the Yoho Valley road is snowbound much of the year and no amenities are confirmed, making this a remote summer-only stop.

campground.name: Kitty Coleman Campground
campground.desc: A seasonal BC Parks beach campground near Courtenay on Vancouver Island, offering 65 sites with potable water and washrooms; access is summer-only as the gate is locked off-season.

campground.name: We Wai Kai
campground.desc: Large waterfront campground on Quadra Island bordering Rebecca Spit Provincial Park, with beaches on both sides of the spit for swimming, kayaking, and whale watching from the eastern shore; cyclists reach it via BC Ferries then a mostly paved 8 km ride, and tent-only unserviced sites sit amid a sea of powered RV pads.

detail.address: 428 Rebecca Spit Road, Heriot Bay, BC V0P 1H0, Canada

campground.name: South Sayres Group Site
campground.desc: A remote, reservation-only waterfront group site on Florence Lake Forest Service Road with a dock for paddling and fishing; no tap water, no garbage service, and key pickup is required at Rock Creek 9 km away. The active industrial gravel FSR has bumps, potholes, and seasonal mud — a rough loaded-bike ride in.

campground.name: Elk Pass Camp
campground.desc: A backcountry wilderness camp inside Strathcona Provincial Park — BC's oldest, a 250,000-hectare alpine wilderness on central Vancouver Island — accessible only by trail; no vehicle access, no confirmed facilities or water.

campground.name: Strawberry Flats Campground
campground.desc: Strawberry Flats Campground is a 15-site BC Parks site within Muncho Lake Provincial Park along the Alaska Highway in far Northern BC, offering access to the park's celebrated turquoise lake and mountain scenery; it operates seasonally with the gate locked and no services off-season.

campground.name: Riverside Park Campground
campground.desc: Municipal campground on the Nechako River inside Vanderhoof's Riverside Park, with flush toilets, showers, and water and electric hookups at every site; a pleasant town-edge stop with a 10-minute walk to services, operating May through early October.

campground.name: sẃiẃs (Haynes Point) Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A narrow sandbar jutting into Osoyoos Lake, managed by the Osoyoos Indian Band, with lakeside campsites in BC's hottest, driest climate; beware poison ivy throughout the park and dangerous undercurrents near the exposed sandy point.

campground.name: Golden Ears Groupsite
campground.desc: Group campsite within one of BC's largest and busiest provincial parks, set in coastal hemlock forest about an hour east of Vancouver with Alouette Lake swimming, paddling, and fishing on the doorstep; no cell service in the campground and summer day-use passes are required for non-camping visitors.

campground.name: Tanya Lakes Camp
campground.desc: A remote backcountry lake camp deep in Tweedsmuir Provincial Park's wilderness, reachable only by floatplane or extended trail through serious grizzly country; total self-sufficiency is required and no amenities are confirmed.

campground.name: Silver Lake Provinical Campground
campground.desc: A small, rustic lakefront campground in the Skagit Valley with a mountain backdrop, offering trout fishing, swimming, and quiet lake-edge camping; access involves several kilometres of gravel on Silver Skagit Road, and bears are very active.

campground.name: China Creek Campground and Marina
campground.desc: Full-service private campground on the Alberni Inlet with beachfront and forested tent sites, a working marina, playground, and the Alberni Inlet Trail nearby; propane fires only (no wood), open April–September.

detail.address: 2011 Franklin River Rd, Port Alberni, BC, V0R 2B0

campground.name: Ptarmigan Lake Camp
campground.desc: A remote backcountry camp at an alpine lake in the Cariboo/Chilcotin wilderness; the name and setting suggest a hike-in or very rough approach through isolated terrain with no services — self-sufficiency is essential.

campground.name: Sayward Valley Resort
campground.desc: A small full-service resort in the village of Sayward offering camping alongside cottages and motel rooms, with an on-site store stocking groceries, liquor, and local produce. A practical resupply point for cyclists on the northern Vancouver Island route, with showers, laundry, and propane available.

campground.name: Bowron Lake Campground
campground.desc: A pleasant 25-unit drive-in campground at the registration centre for the world-renowned Bowron Lake Canoe Circuit, a short distance from the lake with hiking trails nearby; both black and grizzly bears are active April through November.

campground.name: lower campground
campground.desc: Sproat Lake Park's lower campground sits directly on the warm lakeshore with its own swimming area, 13 km northwest of Port Alberni via paved Highway 4; a short trail also leads to K'ak'awin, considered one of BC's finest prehistoric petroglyph panels.

campground.name: Kwaksistah Regional Park Campsite
campground.desc: Free regional park campsite near the remote community of Winter Harbour on northwest Vancouver Island, reached by a long gravel logging road; the website loaded only navigation — amenity details are unpublished, so expect a basic self-sufficient stop.

campground.name: Bella Coola Valley Campground
campground.desc: Family-run campground on Highway 20 in the Bella Coola Valley, deep in the Great Bear Rainforest amid glacier-fed rivers, old-growth forest, and abundant wildlife; flush toilets, coin showers, and laundry on-site with town minutes away.

campground.name: Primitive Camping
campground.desc: Primitive backcountry camping in Babine Mountains Provincial Park near Smithers, set among glacier-fed lakes, rugged peaks, and vast sub-alpine meadows; the west-end road is closed to vehicles beyond the parking lot so access is trail-only, and all water must be treated on site.

campground.name: Monarch Campground
campground.desc: Parks Canada campground in Yoho National Park's Kicking Horse Valley, reached via paved Trans-Canada access; a summer-only base for Takakkaw Falls, Burgess Shale guided hikes, and Emerald Lake, with fees applicable and waterways currently closed to watercraft until March 2027.

campground.name: Fisheries Pool Campground
campground.desc: A small 9-site riverside campground in BC's Cariboo/Chilcotin interior, named for a nearby fishing pool; amenities are unconfirmed and access details are unavailable from the source page.

campground.name: Tetsa River Regional Park
campground.desc: A riverside campground in the boreal forest along the Alaska Highway in Northern BC, offering a quiet break from highway miles beside the Tetsa River; facilities are basic with 25 sites.

campground.name: Park Sands Beach Resort RV Park & Campground
campground.desc: Oceanfront resort in the heart of Parksville with direct access to Georgia Strait's famous wide tidal flats; tent sites are spring–summer only and share full-hookup RV infrastructure with coin showers and no open wood fires.

campground.name: Salmon Point Resort RV Park
campground.desc: Full-service oceanfront RV resort and marina on Georgia Strait between Campbell River and Courtenay, with flush showers, heated pool, hot tub, and boat launch; tenting is in designated areas only and rates reflect the resort setting.

detail.address: 2176 Salmon Point Road, Campbell River B.C. Canada V9H 1E5

campground.name: North Park Campground
campground.desc: A campground within Horne Lake Regional Park on Vancouver Island, where a freshwater lake and the nearby Horne Lake Caves make for an active stop; the access road off Highway 19A is a rural mix of pavement and gravel passable by regular vehicles. No amenity details were recoverable from the scraped pages.

campground.name: SunLund RV Park & Cabins
campground.desc: An RV park and cabins operation on Vancouver Island or the Gulf Islands; the website did not load so setting, facilities, and access details are unknown — verify before routing here.

detail.address: 1496 Murray Road, Lund, British Columbia V0N 2G0

campground.name: Fairy Lake Campground
campground.desc: A small forest lake near Port Renfrew offering a quiet, basic overnight on a logging-road approach typical of Vancouver Island's west-side rec sites; no confirmed water or flush facilities.

campground.name: Little Shaw Campsite
campground.desc: A fee-based Mosaic Forest Management campsite on southern Vancouver Island, likely set in second-growth forest and reached via logging road; website content was unavailable, so details on water, facilities, and road surface are unconfirmed.

campground.name: Kinney Lake Campground
campground.desc: A hike-in campground on the shore of glacial Kinney Lake along the Berg Lake Trail in Mount Robson Provincial Park, framed by the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies; the roughly 4 km walk from the trailhead puts it entirely out of reach for loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Trigger Lake Wilderness Campground
campground.desc: A remote wilderness campsite on Trigger Lake inside South Chilcotin Mountains Park, with no staffed facilities, no potable water, and grizzly encounters not uncommon; visitors must be fully self-sufficient and prepared for sudden snow even in summer. The payoff is deep access to over 200 km of trails through spectacular alpine meadows, ridges, and peaks.

campground.name: Chin Beach Campsite
campground.desc: A vehicle-accessible forested campground at the east end of Juan de Fuca Provincial Park, serving as a trailhead for the rugged 47 km Juan de Fuca Marine Trail and a short drive from the tide-pool-rich Botanical Beach; the exposed Pacific surf coast is wild rather than gentle, and a seasonal gate limits access to summer.

campground.name: Narvaez Bay Campsite (BCMT)
campground.desc: A 7-site wilderness walk-in on Saturna Island — 1.7 km on foot from the trailhead (or by boat) into one of the most undisturbed bays in the southern Gulf Islands, set among Douglas fir and Garry oak-arbutus ecosystems; no potable water, pit toilets only, and a permanent fire ban make self-sufficiency essential.

detail.address: Narvaez Bay Rd, Saturna Island, BC, V0N2Y0

campground.name: Rearguard Campground
campground.desc: A riverside campground in Mount Robson Provincial Park near Rearguard Falls, the farthest inland point Pacific chinook salmon reach on their Fraser River migration; basic amenities along the Yellowhead corridor with a compelling natural spectacle in late summer.

campground.name: One Island Lake Campground
campground.desc: A 28-site BC Parks campground on the shore of One Island Lake in Northern BC, with potable water and washrooms in a calm lakeside setting. The gate closes outside the operating season, making this a summer-only stop.

campground.name: Coastal Sands Resort
campground.desc: Small boutique beachfront RV resort and cabin property on sandy Saratoga Beach, east Vancouver Island, with ocean views, coastal mountain backdrop, shallow warm water, and a playground; no tent camping is offered and sites are priced at resort rates.

detail.address: 8914 Clarkson Ave, Black Creek, BC V9J 1B1

campground.name: Hummingbird Lake Wilderness Campground
campground.desc: Backcountry wilderness campground at Hummingbird Lake within South Chilcotin Mountains Park, a visually spectacular alpine setting of meadows, peaks and lakes roughly 150 km north of Whistler; no potable water (filter all sources), no staffed facilities, and grizzly bear encounters are not uncommon — full self-sufficiency required.

campground.name: Numa Creek
campground.desc: Numa Creek is a hike-in backcountry campground deep in Kootenay National Park, requiring a paid permit and advance reservation for July–September; snow-dependent access limits the usable window to roughly late June through October, with no campfires and bear cables the norm.

campground.name: Lions Flatbed Creek Campground
campground.desc: A community campground alongside Flatbed Creek in the foothills near Tumbler Ridge, a UNESCO Global Geopark town in northeastern BC; amenities are unconfirmed and the access road surface is unknown, so treat this as a basic overnight and verify conditions before arriving.

campground.name: Yellowhead Campground
campground.desc: A 30-acre forested private campground beside Swift Creek on Yellowhead Highway 5 at the edge of Valemount, where Chinook salmon spawn in summer; town centre, restaurants, and shops are a short walk away.

detail.address: 325 North Highway #5, P.O. Box 387, Valemount, B.C., V0E 2Z0

campground.name: Qualicum First Nation Campground
campground.desc: First Nations-operated waterfront campground on the Strait of Georgia where the Big Qualicum River meets the sea, with basic tent sites, serviced RV pads, flush washrooms, hot showers, and a playground; open May long weekend through September, with tent sites at $40/night.

detail.address: 5861 West Island Hwy. (Hwy. 19), Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 1Z5

campground.name: Silverthorne RV Park
campground.desc: An RV and mobile home park in BC's Cariboo-Chilcotin interior; details are sparse as the listing page failed to load, so conditions, amenities, and tent-camping suitability are unconfirmed.

campground.name: The Golden Eco-Adventure Ranch
campground.desc: A large private campground near Golden in the Kootenays with potable water, device charging, and washrooms; the eco-adventure branding implies activity-focused programming, but the website was offline so details are unavailable.

campground.name: Revelstoke RV & Cabin Resort
campground.desc: Full-service commercial resort just outside Revelstoke on the doorstep of Mount Revelstoke National Park, with tent sites, cabins, glamping domes, RV hookups, seasonal pool, and two playgrounds. A comfortable, amenity-rich base for mountain activities; expect resort pricing and a lively atmosphere.

campground.name: Pacific Playgrounds
campground.desc: A well-appointed year-round RV resort and cottage complex on the Strait of Georgia at the Oyster River mouth, with a 140-slip marina, heated pool, and sandy beach; no tent-only sites are mentioned, so touring cyclists should confirm availability before arriving.

detail.address: 9082 Clarkson Avenue, Black Creek, BC, V9J 1B3

campground.name: Squakum Creek Campsite
campground.desc: A small creek-side campsite in BC's Okanagan & Thompson region with washrooms; road surface and detailed amenities are unconfirmed from available sources.

campground.name: North Thompson River Campground
campground.desc: A developed BC Parks campground at the scenic confluence of the Clearwater and North Thompson Rivers, 5 km south of Clearwater just off Highway 5 — easy access and proximity to Wells Gray Park make it a natural touring stopover. Gate closes off-season; flood-season currents June–July warrant water caution.

detail.address: 5 km south of Clearwater, just off Highway 5, BC

campground.name: Sowchea Bay Campground
campground.desc: A 30-site BC Parks campground on Sowchea Bay in the Cariboo/Central Interior, with potable water and washrooms; the gate closes in the off-season so this is a strictly summer destination.

campground.name: Emory Bar RV Park
campground.desc: A privately-run RV park on the Trans-Canada in the Fraser Canyon, 18 km from Hope, set among tall evergreens with mountain views, showers, laundromat, and an adjacent general store with café and smoked salmon. Dry tent sites are available, though the park is oriented toward RVs and the highway setting is busy.

detail.address: 28775 Trans Canada HWY, Hope, British Columbia V0X 1L3

campground.name: Thunderbird RV Park
campground.desc: Year-round oceanfront RV resort on the Campbell River estuary with flush toilets, hot showers, fire pits, and full hookups; primarily set up for RVs and cottages — confirm tent camping availability before arriving, as no tent sites are explicitly listed.

detail.address: 2660 Spit Road, Campbell River, BC V9W 6E3

campground.name: Margaret Creek Camp
campground.desc: A backcountry wilderness campsite within Strathcona Provincial Park — BC's oldest park — set among rugged peaks, alpine lakes, and creek valleys in the heart of Vancouver Island; hard hike-in access and minimal services make this a serious commitment for prepared campers.

campground.name: Log Creek Campground
campground.desc: A single RV/camping pitch at a small private riverside retreat on the Nahatlatch River near Boston Bar, reached via the gravel Nahatlatch FSR off Highway 1; open April through Thanksgiving with shared washroom facilities on site.

campground.name: Cluxewe Resort Campsite
campground.desc: First Nations-owned oceanfront and woodland resort near Port McNeill on northern Vancouver Island, with ocean-view and woodland tent sites, flush washrooms, and a playground; tap water is non-potable so bring your own drinking water.

detail.address: #1 Cluxewe Campground Road, PO Box 245, Port McNeil, BC V0N 2R0

campground.name: Port Renfrew RV Park
campground.desc: Marina-side campground at the southern West Coast Trail trailhead, serving as a base for trophy salmon and halibut fishing, kayaking, and whale watching; open May to mid-October only, cash payment required, no reservations.

detail.address: 7505 Gordon River Rd, Port Renfrew, BC

campground.name: The Narrows Marine Campsite
campground.desc: A boat-in marine campsite on Alouette Lake inside Golden Ears Park, offering a remote lakeshore setting reachable only by water; completely inaccessible to loaded touring cyclists without a boat.

campground.name: Tudyah Lake Campground
campground.desc: A developed BC Parks campground on Tudyah Lake in Northern BC, offering 36 sites with potable water and washrooms; opening and closing dates shift with weather, so confirm before planning.

campground.name: Cyclist Camping
campground.desc: A well-developed BC Parks campground on the Sunshine Coast with sandy beaches, second-growth forest, and a dedicated cyclists' campsite that always has room regardless of reservation status. Paved access via Sechelt Inlet Road; showers, potable water, and flush washrooms on-site.

campground.name: Garnet Beach
campground.desc: A backcountry wilderness beach campsite in the Kootenays, reachable only by boat or multi-day hike through rugged grizzly country with stream crossings often impassable until late July; no facilities, no potable water, and full self-sufficiency required.

campground.name: Agate Beach Campground
campground.desc: Agate Beach Campground sits within Naikoon Provincial Park on Haida Gwaii, at the edge of vast wild Pacific beaches on Haida traditional territory; the park is a genuine wilderness with no supplies nearby, cash-only fees, and cool, rainy, windy weather possible any time.

campground.name: Misty Meadows Tentsite
campground.desc: A frontcountry tentsite within Naikoon Provincial Park on Haida Gwaii, bordering over 100 km of wild Pacific beach on traditional Haida territory; cash only, no internet, and cool rainy weather with high winds is possible any day.

campground.name: Rosebery Provicial Campground
campground.desc: A small, intimate campground tucked along Wilson Creek just off Highway 6, 5 km north of New Denver, with Valhalla Park rising across Slocan Lake to the west; well-positioned as a base for backcountry exploration of Valhalla, Kokanee Glacier, Goat Range, nearby ghost-mining towns, and natural hot springs.

campground.name: San Josef Bay Campsite
campground.desc: Walk-in wilderness campsite at a sweeping white-sand bay on the southern edge of Cape Scott Provincial Park, reached by an easy trail through old-growth Sitka spruce and cedar; the trailhead is at the end of an active logging road with truck traffic.

campground.name: Mowich Campground
campground.desc: Mowich is a hike-in backcountry campground in E.C. Manning Park, set in the Cascade Mountains more than 1 km from any road; a permit ($5/person/night) is required but no advance reservation, making it a solid wilderness night with real commitment to reach.

campground.name: Hermit Campground
campground.desc: Hike-in backcountry campground in Glacier National Park set in the alpine terrain above Rogers Pass, reaching into the glaciated Selkirk Mountains; requires both a national park pass and a camping permit, and is accessible only on foot.

campground.name: Davis Creek Campground
campground.desc: A 32-site BC Parks campground on the north-western shore of Kootenay Lake, reached via paved Hwy. 31 about 25 km north of Kaslo, with sheltered lakeview sites and easy beach access for paddling and swimming (water runs cold). Purcell mountain panoramas, WiFi, and an upgraded drinking water system make it a comfortable base for fishing, hiking, and on-water activities.

campground.name: Arrowvale Campground & Cottages
campground.desc: A 67-acre working farm and campground on the Somass River near Port Alberni, with riverside campsites, a petting farm, farm tours, and gentle river trails — a family-friendly rural stop with genuine pastoral character.

detail.address: 5955 Hector Rd, Port Alberni, BC, V9Y 9E8

campground.name: Lizard Lake Campground
campground.desc: A quiet 20-site camp on the shores of Lizard Lake in the forests of Vancouver Island, offering a peaceful lakeside stop with basic facilities; accessed via gravel forest service road.

campground.name: Prince Rupert RV
campground.desc: A full-service, landscaped RV park on Hwy 16 in Prince Rupert, roughly a mile from the BC Ferries terminal for Haida Gwaii and Alaska sailings; tent sites run $30/night with showers included, making it a solid transit stop with city amenities but no natural setting to speak of.

detail.address: 1750 Park Avenue, Prince Rupert, British Columbia, Canada V8J 3R5

campground.name: Croteau Lake Group Campsite
campground.desc: A group campsite on Croteau Lake in Strathcona Park, BC's oldest provincial park and a rugged mountain wilderness at the centre of Vancouver Island; amenities are unconfirmed and access road surface is unknown but likely rough given the park's largely undeveloped character.

campground.name: Tyax Bear Paw Camp
campground.desc: A remote wilderness camp operated by Tyax Adventures in the Cariboo Chilcotin, likely near Tyaughton Lake in the Gold Bridge area; access involves long gravel road approaches typical of this backcountry region.

detail.address: General Delivery, Gold Bridge, BC V0K 1P0

campground.name: Trinity Campground
campground.desc: Sandy-beach campground on 35 km Mabel Lake in a cool forested mountain setting, reached by 36 km of paved road plus 1 km gravel; popular for fishing, swimming, and wildlife watching, though the lake bottom drops off steeply near shore.

campground.name: Murtle River Camp
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site free camp on the Murtle River in the backcountry of Wells Gray Park; no confirmed amenities and hard access make this a spot only reached by determined wilderness travelers on foot or by canoe.

campground.name: Swift Creek Resort
campground.desc: A private resort on Highway 5 just north of Valemount with tent sites along Swift Creek, where you fall asleep to rushing water beneath Rocky and Cariboo Mountain peaks; most sites are full-hookup RV slots and this is a paid commercial operation.

campground.name: Dinosaur Lake Campground
campground.desc: Municipal campground on Dinosaur Lake near Hudson's Hope, open May Long Weekend to Labour Day only; a quiet lakeside stop in a region known for dinosaur fossil tracks and Peace Region dams, though specific on-site amenity details are sparse.

campground.name: Emar Lakes Campground
campground.desc: A self-sufficient wilderness park on a chain of lakes and wetlands in the upper Emar Creek watershed, with user-maintained campsites at Janice and Willowgrouse Lakes; no potable water and an unmarked entrance off Hwy 24.

campground.name: Riverside RV Park and Campground
campground.desc: A well-maintained city-owned campground on the banks of the Shuswap River in Enderby, with flush washrooms, hot showers, a boat launch, and downtown shops a short walk along the riverwalk. Unserviced tent sites sit at $35/night and the site skews toward RV guests, but it works well as a comfortable riverside stop on the Kelowna–Kamloops corridor.

campground.name: Skyview Campground
campground.desc: A full-service, RV-oriented campground at the heart of E.C. Manning Park in the Cascades, open year-round with flush washrooms, a playground, and optional resort pool and hot-tub access for a fee; the hookup-heavy layout skews toward RVs, but tent campers share the same modern facilities and can walk to Lightning Lake in 10 minutes.

campground.name: Mitchell Meadows Campground
campground.desc: A remote backcountry campsite in the alpine meadows of Mount Assiniboine Park, reachable only by multi-day trail or helicopter; no services, fires prohibited in the core area, and mountain weather turns fast.

campground.name: Seton Dam Campground
campground.desc: A BC Hydro recreation-area campground on the shores of Seton Reservoir near Lillooet, set in a hot, semi-arid canyon landscape; the website provided no campground-specific details on amenities, facilities, or access road surface.

campground.name: Crooked River Campground
campground.desc: A 65-site BC Parks campground in the Cariboo/Central Interior with full amenities including showers, potable water, and reservations — a comfortable overnight along the Crooked River corridor; opening date depends on snowmelt, so confirm before an early-season visit.

campground.name: Dina Lake Campsite
campground.desc: A small, free primitive campsite on Dina Lake within Heather-Dina Lakes Provincial Park in Northern BC; five sites with no confirmed amenities mean you pack everything in and out.

campground.name: Bear Creek Campground
campground.desc: Rustic forested Recreation Site where Bear Creek meets Harrison Lake, with drive-in, walk-in forest, and walk-in beach sites; no potable water or flush toilets, cash only, and some low-lying sites flood during spring freshet — bring all your own water and pack out everything. Opens mid-May.

campground.name: Salmo Municipal Campground
campground.desc: A quiet, shaded municipal campground inside KP Park, two blocks off Highway 6, with hot showers, a playground, and BMX track — within easy walking distance of Salmo's downtown; open mid-May to early September at $20/night, first-come basis.

campground.name: Homesite Creek Campground
campground.desc: A wilderness campground 1.75 km up a groomed forest service road near Secret Cove on the Sunshine Coast, with 30 sites, outhouses, and no running water — bring all drinking water and firewood.

campground.name: Greendrop Lake Camp
campground.desc: Greendrop Lake is a hike-in wilderness camp tucked among old-growth forest and subalpine terrain in Sx̱ótsaqel/Chilliwack Lake Park; a backcountry permit and fee are required in advance, and no fires are allowed.

campground.name: Overflow
campground.desc: Overflow camping at Horsefly Lake Provincial Park, set among old-growth cedar and Douglas fir on a large Cariboo lake popular for rainbow trout fishing and paddling; the overflow designation means fewer amenities than the primary 23-site campground, and the final 10km of access road is gravel.

campground.name: Reinecker campground
campground.desc: Reinecker campground sits within Herald Park on the forested west shore of Shuswap Lake, offering a roped swimming beach, boat launch, and the self-guided Margaret Falls trail; it is a busy, full-amenity park that fills quickly in summer.

campground.name: Centennial Campground
campground.desc: Municipal campground in Centennial Park on the eastern shore of Slocan Lake in the small Kootenay village of New Denver, offering swimming, Selkirk Mountain scenery, and the historic Nikkei Internment Memorial Centre within walking distance. Online reservations are required; a natural anchor stop for cyclists riding the Slocan Valley.

detail.address: 115 Slocan Avenue, PO Box 40, New Denver, BC V0G 1S0

campground.name: Fillongley Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A small 10-site provincial campground on Denman Island, reached by BC Ferries from Buckley Bay on Vancouver Island and set in old-growth Douglas fir; potable water and washrooms are on-site, but services are suspended in winter and campers must be fully self-sufficient.

campground.name: Will-O-Bend RV Park
campground.desc: A fully serviced, 80-site RV park with a 9-hole golf course and swimming pond at the foot of the Rockies near Jaffray on Hwy 3/93; primarily oriented toward RV owners and long-term renters, with overnight stays at $65/night for 30-amp power — no tent-only rate is listed.

campground.name: Okeover Arm Campground
campground.desc: A small vehicle-accessible campground at the northern tip of Hwy 101 near Lund, sitting on the doorstep of Desolation Sound Marine Park with 14 seasonal tent sites plus 4 year-round walk-in sites (off-season: free, no services, user-maintained). The shore is rocky with no sand — paddlers thrive here, casual swimmers less so.

detail.address: Northern terminus of Hwy 101, 19 km north of Powell River, BC

campground.name: Twin Pines Campground
campground.desc: A camp site on Vancouver Island in the Horne Lake area managed by the Regional District of Nanaimo; the scraped website returned navigation-only pages with no campground-specific detail, so conditions, access, and amenities are unknown.

campground.name: McDonald Creek Provincial Campground
campground.desc: A large provincial campground on the eastern shore of Upper Arrow Lake, 10 km south of Nakusp via Highway 6, with waterfront sites and kilometres of fine sandy beach; swimming is prime July–August as low spring water leaves the shoreline muddy.

campground.name: Purden Lake Resort
campground.desc: A mountain lake resort right off Hwy 16 about 60 km east of Prince George, offering lakefront and dry sites with sandy beach, lake swimming, boat launch, and legendary sunsets; reservation-only (no drop-ins), no public wifi, and limited cell service.

detail.address: P.O. Box 1239, Prince George, BC V2L 4V3

campground.name: Baby Bedwell Lake Campground
campground.desc: Hike-in backcountry campsite on an alpine lake deep in Strathcona Park's rugged mountain wilderness — BC's oldest provincial park; no services, snow possible into early summer at elevation, and the trailhead approach rules out loaded bikes.

campground.name: Gooseneck Lake Campsite
campground.desc: A Mosaic Forest Management lakeside campsite on northern Vancouver Island, likely accessed via logging roads through working forest; expect basic pit facilities and a quiet, undeveloped setting.

campground.name: Eva Lake
campground.desc: A hike-in backcountry campground beside an alpine lake in Mount Revelstoke National Park; reservable but requires a multi-hour trail approach with no vehicle or loaded-bike access to the lakeshore.

campground.name: Porcupine Campground
campground.desc: Backcountry campground in UNESCO-listed Mount Assiniboine Park, reachable only by multi-day trail or helicopter with no vehicle access and no on-site services; expect sudden alpine weather and fire restrictions in the core area, offset by world-class glacier and peak scenery.

campground.name: Grant Bay Recreation Site
campground.desc: A remote, free white-sand beach on Quatsino Sound reached by a 10-minute walk from the trailhead; rustic overnight camping with zero services and strict pack-in/pack-out — loaded bikes must be left at the trailhead.

campground.name: Cluxewe Resort
campground.desc: Indigenous-owned oceanfront resort where the Cluxewe River meets the Broughton Strait on northern Vancouver Island, offering ocean and woodland tent sites with flush washrooms, whale and estuary bird watching right from camp; tap water is non-potable so cyclists must carry drinking water.

detail.address: #1 Cluxewe Campground Road, Port McNeill, BC V0N 2R0

campground.name: Skihist Campground
campground.desc: A 58-site BC Parks campground in the Thompson River canyon near Lytton, sitting just off Highway 1 with potable water and washrooms; gate closes in the off-season so plan for a summer visit only.

campground.name: Charlie Lake Campground
campground.desc: A 57-site BC Parks campground on the southwestern shore of 13 km Charlie Lake, 11 km north of Fort St. John, offering swimming, canoeing, fishing for northern pike and walleye, a playground, and disc golf; gate closes for the off-season.

detail.address: 11 km north of Fort St. John, Alaska Highway at Highway 29, BC

campground.name: Air Force Beach Campground
campground.desc: A Canadian Forces-operated beach campground at CFB Comox on Vancouver Island, almost certainly restricted to CAF members, veterans, and their families — touring cyclists must confirm eligibility before planning a stop here.

campground.name: Red Bluff Campground
campground.desc: A BC Parks campground on the Fraser River near Quesnel, framed by the namesake red volcanic bluffs; 34 sites with potable water and reservations accepted, but the gate is locked in the off-season so plan a summer visit.

campground.name: Riverbend Cottage & RV Resort
campground.desc: A private resort on 16 wooded acres along the Englishman River just off Highway 19A near Parksville, with large partially-shaded tent sites including 9 directly on the riverbank, flush washrooms, and showers; fees apply and the site is a full commercial resort adjacent to Rathtrevor Provincial Park.

detail.address: 1-924 East Island Highway, Parksville, BC, V9P 1R6

campground.name: Hampton Overflow Campground
campground.desc: A basic overflow area adjacent to E.C. Manning Park's Hampton campground, on Hwy 3 in the Cascade Mountains; amenities are unconfirmed for the overflow itself, but highway-side access is straightforward and Manning Park's trail network is nearby.

campground.name: Nitinaht Lake Campground
campground.desc: Ditidaht-operated campground on the shores of Nitinaht Lake — a 20 km ocean fjord renowned for consistent thermal winds and a world-class windsurfing and kitesurfing scene — also serving as the West Coast Trail's third entry point; outhouse facilities only, advance online reservation required, and access is via remote logging roads.

detail.address: Area F (Cowichan Lake South / Skutz Falls), BC

campground.name: Riverside Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, partially treed free rec site directly on the Elk River, reached by 155 km of forest service road north of Elkford — remote and peaceful, with 3 sites and no confirmed services.

campground.name: Owen Flats 'A'
campground.desc: Owen Flats 'A' is an open roadside site on the Morice River FSR with a gravel boat launch, picnic table, and fire ring—a simple river-access stop near prime steelhead and salmon water. The approach is roughly 30 km of active logging road with narrow, rough sections; a VHF radio for resource-road channels is strongly advised.

campground.name: Dease River Crossing Campground and Cabins
campground.desc: A Dease River Crossing Campground and Cabins in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: O'Connell Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, remote rec site on scenic O'Connell Lake in northern Vancouver Island, featuring a historic trestle on a lake isthmus and dual boat launches; access demands a 4x4 vehicle on unmaintained industrial logging roads with active traffic.

campground.name: Rocky Point Recreation Site
campground.desc: A constructed 30-site recreation site on the Stave Lake reservoir foreshore with sweeping water views, though lake levels can drop to expose up to 300 m of foreshore; reached via roughly 10 km of gravel Forest Service Road from Mission.

campground.name: Lava Camp
campground.desc: A Lava Camp in Malibu.

campground.name: Chuchi Lake North
campground.desc: A small, free 4-site rec site on the north shore of remote Chuchi Lake, reached after 100 km of highway from Fort St James followed by 20 km of Forest Service Road; expect primitive conditions with no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Hahas Lake Recreation Site
