campground.desc: A 14-site fee-for-service lake recreation site outside Kimberley, reached via the Lost Dog Forest Service Road off Highway 95A; expect gravel washboard on the roughly 4 km approach, and basic amenities once you arrive.

campground.name: Six Mile Lakes Recreation Site
campground.desc: Four-site rustic rec site among three connected sub-alpine lakes, with a 3 km forest trail looping between them; the 13 km access road turns very rough in the final stretch and requires high clearance.

campground.name: French Lake South Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, single-site rec site on a power-restricted quiet lake, reached by a very rough 4WD-only forest service road; popular with anglers but has no confirmed amenities and trailers cannot access.

campground.name: Overflow Campsite
campground.desc: A Overflow Campsite in Liard River.

campground.name: Larry's Point
campground.desc: A Larry's Point in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: Eagle Bay Recreation Site
campground.desc: Free lakeshore rec site on Upper Arrow Lake reached via 10.5 km of Forest Service Road off Hwy 23 — rewarding lake and mountain scenery with morning sunrises, but the gravel approach is a real push for a loaded bike.

campground.name: Little Rock R.V. Park
campground.desc: A Little Rock R.V. Park in Campbell River.

campground.name: Camp Woodside
campground.desc: A Camp Woodside in Chilliwack.

campground.name: Wilbur Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free 2-site rec site on a quiet fishing lake with a dock and cartop boat launch, reached via 13 km of active logging road from Parson; CB radio is recommended and the final 500 m down to the lake is rough.

campground.name: Little Bouleau Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-site camp on a small, remote fishing lake reached by a lengthy forest service road; the final 12.7 km on Whiteman-Granite FSR passes through 2021 fire-affected sections with windfall and rock obstacles, and no amenities are confirmed on-site.

campground.name: Troy Creek
campground.desc: A Troy Creek in Lafferty.

campground.name: Findlay Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free recreation site near Canal Flat with a short trail to canyon viewpoints and impressive twin waterfalls; reached via 5 km of active logging road where CB radio is recommended, and a trail washout near the falls requires care.

detail.address: Findlay Creek Road, Canal Flat, V0B 1B0

campground.name: Long Island Bay Campground
campground.desc: A free, boat-access-only recreation site on the west side of Long Island in Harrison Lake, with outhouses, a fire pit, a picnic shelter, and hiking trails to a lookout — completely unreachable by bicycle.

campground.name: Forlorn Campsite
campground.desc: A Forlorn Campsite in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: Mount Begbie Campground Recreation Site
campground.desc: A hike-in-only alpine site reached by a steep 6 km trail and perched at 2045 m below the Mount Begbie glacier; no road access, fly-out toilet, and mountaineering terrain beyond camp.

campground.name: Nahmint Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A lakeshore rec site nestled beneath towering old-growth hemlock with a beach and good fishing; reaching it demands 26+ km of chained forest service roads from Port Alberni, a real grind on a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Blackwater River Crossing Recreation Site
campground.desc: A scenic camp in open Douglas Fir forest on both sides of the road just before the Blackwater River bridge, offering pit toilets, tables, and fire rings; the 42 km gravel approach from the pavement cutoff is long but rideable.

campground.name: Lodgepole Lake Campground
campground.desc: A small rec-site fishery on a popular rainbow trout lake, reached via roughly 3 km of forest service road off Lac Le Jeune Road near Kamloops; the winter-maintained road makes it a rare year-round option, with ice fishing drawing visitors in colder months.

campground.name: Site 1 (BCMT)
campground.desc: A Site 1 (BCMT) in Dolphin Beach.

campground.name: Lak La More Recreation Site
campground.desc: A paddle-in-only sandy beach campsite on the Sayward Forest Canoe Route, reached by canoe from Amor Lake Recreation Site; summer low water exposes the most sand. With just two sites and zero road access, this is a remote quiet stop — cyclists cannot reach it.

campground.name: Rainbow Cove Campground
campground.desc: A Rainbow Cove Campground in 12 Mile.

campground.name: Pendleton Creek - BC Recreation Site
campground.desc: ORV-focused rec site west of Kamloops accessed via the Dairy Lake Forest Service Road, primarily serving the Greenstone/Duffy motorized trail network — expect noise and heavy ATV traffic. A functional free overnight with no particular draw for a loaded touring cyclist.

campground.name: Emma Lake Cabin
campground.desc: High-elevation wilderness cabin outside Powell River, reached by roughly 52 km of active one-way logging road followed by a hike-in trail from B-Branch; built primarily for winter recreation with no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Belmont Point Recreation Site
campground.desc: A Belmont Point Recreation Site in Nuchatlitz.

campground.name: Islet View Marine Site
campground.desc: A free, boat-access marine rec site on the Sea to Sky Marine Trail near Porteau Cove, offering a cleared camping area behind a rough beach with sacred offshore islands (Squamish First Nation) visible; reachable only by water, making it a non-option for cyclists without a kayak.

campground.name: Flora Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, little-known lake reached by roughly 53 km of gravel logging road from Port Alberni, offering five basic lakeside pitches in a remote, quiet setting; no amenities are confirmed.

campground.name: Boot Lake Rec Site
campground.desc: A tiny, free, high-elevation rec site on Boot Lake's southeastern shore at 1485 m, favoured by anglers and hunters; reaching it demands 15+ km of very rough forest service road that the listing explicitly deems unsuitable for anything without high clearance and good suspension.

campground.name: Fish Trap (Dean River) Recreation Site
campground.desc: A quiet 2-site rec site on the slow, lily-pad-lined Dean River right off Highway 20, appealing for birdwatching and canoe exploration; no confirmed facilities or water.

campground.name: Big Cedar Tree
campground.desc: A single-site rec area reachable only by boat through South Bentinck Arm, protecting one of BC's largest Western Red Cedars — roughly 5 m in diameter — with a 1 km walk from the Larso Bay trailhead to the tree; no docking facilities and no listed amenities.

campground.name: Chimney Lake Centre Recreation Site
campground.desc: Open grassy recreation site with recently upgraded lakefront pitches on Chimney Lake, reached by 30 km of gravel roads (Dog Creek and Chimney Valley Roads) off Highway 20.

campground.name: Marion Lake Campground
campground.desc: A Marion Lake Campground in Harrogate.

campground.name: Monroe Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, secluded mountain lake recreation site off Hwy 3/95 south of Cranbrook, with a quiet 'all to yourself' feel; note this is a day-use only site — no overnight camping.

campground.name: Naka Creek (BCMT)
campground.desc: Tiny free camp on the Johnstone Strait shore near the Robson Bight Ecological Reserve, reached by roughly 32 km of forest service road from Highway 19; the setting is remarkable for orca and marine mammal watching, but the long FSR haul makes it a serious undertaking for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Gorman Lake & Trail Recreation Site
campground.desc: A scenic alpine lake in a deep bowl above Golden with short looping trails — touring cyclists should know that bikes and motor vehicles are explicitly restricted from the area during snow-free months, making this effectively a winter snowmobile destination.

campground.name: Gun Creek Campground
campground.desc: A free, roadside rec site at the confluence of Gun Creek and Carpenter Lake reservoir, roughly 9 km northeast of Gold Bridge; swimming and boating are not recommended due to fluctuating reservoir levels and swift creek currents, but it works well as a base for exploring the surrounding area.

campground.name: Chuchi Lake Point A
campground.desc: A free, remote rec site on the east end of Chuchi Lake in northern BC, used mainly as a boat-launch staging area with no confirmed amenities; the 94 km forest service road approach makes this a serious commitment for a loaded cyclist.

campground.name: Carnes Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A large 44-site rec site split into two clusters directly on the shores of Lake Revelstoke, reached via paved Highway 23N about 36–39 km north of Revelstoke; each section has a boat launch and the fee season runs May to mid-October, but washroom type is unconfirmed.

campground.name: Point Site
campground.desc: A Point Site in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: Promontory Lookout Recreation Site
campground.desc: A former fire lookout atop a mountain northwest of Merritt with sweeping views over Merritt, Lower Nicola, and Stoyoma Mountain; the 9.7 km approach is steep, narrow, and rutted with 4x4 strongly recommended, snow possible into mid-June, and no confirmed facilities.

campground.name: The Monolith
campground.desc: A The Monolith in Oyama.

campground.name: Strawberry Point Recreation Site Campground
campground.desc: A 27-site drive-in rec site on a lakeside forest service road about 6 km off the Duffy Lake Road, with a large sandy beach a short walk away; expect washboard and active industrial traffic on the approach, and self-register cash payment on arrival.

campground.name: un-serviced camp sites (5)
campground.desc: A un-serviced camp sites (5) in Sproat Lake.

campground.name: Upper Fowl Lake
campground.desc: A Upper Fowl Lake in Gramsons.

campground.name: Vicker's Creek South
campground.desc: A Vicker's Creek South in Williams Landing.

campground.name: Tantalus Landing Marine Site
campground.desc: A free 7-site paddle-in marine campsite at the north end of Howe Sound, part of the Sea to Sky Marine Trail — formerly Friday Night Harbour. Reachable only by kayak or boat (roughly an hour from Squamish); no road or trail access for cyclists.

campground.name: Jurrasic Park Campsite
campground.desc: A Jurrasic Park Campsite in Malibu.

campground.name: Ghost Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A remote 4-unit rec site at the end of 70 km of active logging road, serving as the sole trailhead for Cariboo Mountains Provincial Park and the regionally significant Ghost Lake Falls. The long rough approach keeps crowds away but demands commitment from loaded-bike tourers.

campground.name: Bouleau Lake Rec Site
campground.desc: A quiet 4-site rec site on a medium-sized fishing lake, reached via roughly 58 km of gravel and forest service roads including a fire-affected stretch on Whiteman-Granite FSR where windfall and rock obstacles are common. No amenities are confirmed; come fully self-sufficient and prepared to move debris.

campground.name: Side Bay
campground.desc: A remote, rustic rec site on the west coast of Vancouver Island near Port Alice, reached via unmaintained industrial logging roads that demand self-rescue readiness; the reward is a beautiful sand beach with freshwater on site.

campground.name: Snow Creek Campground
campground.desc: A supervised recreation site on the southeast shores of Sproat Lake with a sandy beach and boat launch, popular with families and anglers for swimming, waterskiing, and windsurfing; access requires ~10 km on a forest service road from Highway 4.

campground.name: Cabbage Island Campsite (BCMT) [CLOSED]
campground.desc: A small island campsite on the BC Marine Trails network in the Gulf Islands, reachable only by kayak or boat; currently listed as closed and the trail association page returned a 404, so status and facilities are unconfirmed.

campground.name: Tamihi East Campground
campground.desc: A riverside recreation site at the confluence of Tamihi Creek and the Chilliwack River, with direct Trans Canada Trail access and an extensive ATV and motorcycle trail network nearby; a scenic stop for cycle tourers, though motorized recreation defines the vibe. Cash-only overnight permits required.

campground.name: Top Lake South Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 2-unit free site on a small lake at a low pass in the Fawnie Range, reached at km 140 on the Klukus-Ootsa Forest Road; active logging traffic on the road makes pulling out hazardous.

campground.name: Gosling Lake North Recreation Site
campground.desc: A quiet 2-site lakeside rec site on Gosling Lake along the Sayward Forest Canoe Route, upgraded in 2021 with a day-use picnic area and car-top boat launch; reaching it requires roughly 16 km of mixed forest service roads from Highway 19.

campground.name: Dragon Lake campsite
campground.desc: A Dragon Lake campsite in Nass Camp.

campground.name: Hammer Lake North Recreation Site
campground.desc: Remote interior lake rec site with 11 campsites and a boat launch; power vessels are banned so the water stays quiet for paddlers and anglers, but reaching it demands 40–70 km of forest service road from either Highway 97 or Highway 24.

campground.name: Insect Island
campground.desc: A Insect Island in Health Bay.

campground.name: Tete Jaune Spawning Grounds Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 2-site open campsite on the McLennan River with a walking trail to the Fraser River; access requires roughly 10 km of gravel road and no amenities are confirmed.

campground.name: Sunny Daze Campground
campground.desc: A Sunny Daze Campground in Duncan.

campground.name: Help Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A three-pitch forest site sitting between Help and Comfort Lake, about 30 km along the Bush Forest Service Road with no confirmed amenities; primarily an overflow stop for the nearby Blackwater Lake Site.

campground.name: Agur Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site recreation site on a small, marshy lake west of Summerland, requiring 16 km of forest service road including a 4WD-recommended final 300 m; no confirmed amenities and marshy shores limit the appeal.

campground.name: Dot Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A semi-treed lakeside rec site southeast of Chataway Lake, reached by roughly 8 km of forest service road off Aberdeen Road near Merritt; popular with anglers and hunters, with a boat launch and nearby hiking trails.

campground.name: Garrison Lakes Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single hike-in tent site reached by a roughly 2 km unmaintained, poorly-marked trail from a forest service road west of Princeton — suited for anglers packing in belly boats or small kayaks, with no confirmed facilities and GPS strongly recommended.

campground.name: Cottonwood Recreation Site
campground.desc: A forested rec site on Cayoosh Creek with direct Highway 99 access between Lillooet and Pemberton; a straightforward pull-off with no stated amenities beyond the creek setting and 17 sites.

campground.name: Bluewater Bridge Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, remote rec site on Bluewater Creek accessed via the Bush River FSR, best known as a put-in for whitewater paddlers running the grade 2–3 stretch to Bluewater Creek Rec Site; no confirmed amenities and forest service road approach make it a functional stop rather than a touring destination.

campground.name: Pathfinder Campground/RV Park
campground.desc: A Pathfinder Campground/RV Park in Chilliwack.

campground.name: Nepopekum
campground.desc: A Nepopekum in Manning Park.

campground.name: Hadow Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: Free remote site at the mouth of Hadow Creek on the Beaton Arm, offering fishing and boating in a quiet lakeside setting; reached by roughly 11 km of forest service road after an already lengthy drive from Nakusp, making it a serious commitment for loaded bikes.

campground.name: Lake of the Woods Campground
campground.desc: A Lake of the Woods Campground in Keremeos.

campground.name: Cabin Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Remote sub-alpine lake camp west of Merritt, reached by a long, extremely rough 4WD-only forest service road with creek crossings and loose rock; 3 flat sites suit summer hiking and landscape viewing or winter snowmobiling, but the approach is firmly off-limits to a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Horseshoe Lake
campground.desc: A quiet 2-site rec site on a small lake with a view across to a tiny island, reached by 8 km of good 2WD gravel from Highway 6 near Nakusp; suits flat-water paddling and fishing, and doubles as a base for exploring the surrounding forestry roads by bike.

campground.name: Hahas Lake Campground
campground.desc: A 14-site fee recreation site on Hahas Lake, accessed by the Lost Dog Forest Service Road off Highway 95A; a calm lakeside stop with Solar Lake also reachable nearby, but the FSR approach means a loaded-bike gravel grind to get there.

campground.name: Skookumchuck Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: Tiny free two-site rec site tucked at the end of a 43 km forest service road slog in the Kootenays; a short trail rewards with a viewpoint over Skookumchuck Creek rapids, and fishing is possible (check regs).

campground.name: Arden Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A treed, cobble-shore site on Alberni Inlet reached via 22 km of Canal Main forest road — quiet, largely undiscovered, with marine wildlife at the water's edge; the entrance is unmarked and no amenities are confirmed.

campground.name: Nanton Ireland North Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small 4-site wilderness camp at Ireland Lake marking the end of the portage from Nanton Lake, intended for canoe-trippers on a backcountry paddle route; walk-in only with no confirmed facilities.

campground.name: Lang Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site rec site at pretty waterfalls on Lang Creek, reached via gravel logging roads from Powell River and a short trail — primarily a day-use picnic stop with no confirmed facilities.

campground.name: Cummins Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single hike-in, user-maintained site on Cummins Lake, reached via a long rough forest service road and a trail; offers fishing and winter-sports access but has no confirmed amenities and no water.

campground.name: State Lake Road Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-site treed campsite serving as the trailhead for State Lake, reached via 9 km of forest service road off Christian Valley Road; free with no confirmed facilities.

campground.name: Bute Lake
campground.desc: A Bute Lake in Kamloops.

campground.name: Side Bay
campground.desc: Remote and rustic rec site on Vancouver Island's west coast, offering a beautiful sand beach and on-site freshwater reached via unmaintained industrial logging roads from Port Alice — self-rescue gear essential.

campground.name: Hoodoo Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Three small spots sit directly on high-elevation Hoodoo Lake, reached via roughly 14 km of FSR roads from Hwy 33; the lake thaws late so fishing and paddling hit their stride after ice-off, and a car-top boat launch is on site.

campground.name: Begbie Falls Rec Site
campground.desc: A 26-site rec-site campground on a Forest Service Road just short of Begbie Falls, with trail access to the waterfall and Begbie Bluffs near Revelstoke. Water is not easily accessible on site, so arrive prepared.

campground.name: Windy Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free 3-unit backcountry rec site in the Cariboo, reached by 37+ km of forest and active log-hauling roads; the lake itself is a short 5-minute trail walk from the parking area.

campground.name: Craab Spot
campground.desc: A Craab Spot in Olson.

campground.name: Brewster Point Recreation Site
campground.desc: A sunny, sandy-beach campsite on Brewster Lake along the Sayward Forest Canoe Route, with three tent pads and a large picnic table — boat access only means it is completely unreachable by loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Cal Cheak South Camp
campground.desc: A shaded, heavily treed camp straddling Callaghan Creek and the Cheakamus River, reached via a short gravel run on the Daisy Lake Forest Service Road off Highway 99 north of Whistler; self-register and pay $18/night (May–Oct), first-come-first-served, with regular bear activity.

campground.name: Brewster Camp Recreation Site
campground.desc: A split rec site straddling the Gray Lake FSR along the Sayward Forest Canoe Route, with a grassy lakeside area on one side and horse corrals on the other; access is entirely via forest service roads and the seasonal fee (May long weekend to Labour Day) is cash-only on site.

campground.name: Squamish Riverside Campground
campground.desc: A free, forested rec site on the Squamish River reached by several kilometres of Squamish Valley Road followed by roughly 1 km of dirt track; popular for fishing with tables, fire rings, and pit toilets, but note active bear country, no garbage pickup, and a real flooding risk in heavy rain.

campground.name: Roscoe Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small 6-site free recreation site on Roscoe Lake, popular with anglers and hunters, with non-motorized trails to a lake lookout and onward to Knight (Echo) Lake. Access is via the Skuhun-Roscoe Forest Service Road, expect a rough gravel ride in.

campground.name: Ocean Camping
campground.desc: A Ocean Camping in Tofino.

campground.name: Community Lake Southwest Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 40-hectare rainbow trout lake at 1,370 m elevation, popular with fly fishers all summer; 9 sites off Knouff Lake Road on a first-come, cash-only basis.

campground.name: Davis Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A large semi-open recreation site on Davis Lake in the Voght Valley south of Merritt, popular for fishing, boating, and camping with two boat launches and horseshoe pits; the approach requires several kilometres of gravel road and the site is cash-only at the gate.

campground.name: Popeye's Campground
campground.desc: A Popeye's Campground in Sidney.

campground.name: Mt Thompson Campsite
campground.desc: A Mt Thompson Campsite in Canyon.

campground.name: Red Sand Operations Trail Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free forest-service rec site on Redsand Lake within a demonstration forest, reached by 26 km of West Kalum forestry road from Terrace; three short loop trails explore logged and replanted stands and follow the Kalum River with lake and mountain views, but expect a long gravel approach and minimal amenities.

campground.name: Colvile Camp
campground.desc: A Colvile Camp in Sunshine Valley.

campground.name: Camping gratuit
campground.desc: A Camping gratuit in Liard River.

campground.name: Mile High Campsite
campground.desc: A Mile High Campsite in Chilliwack.

campground.name: McCreight Lake Campground
campground.desc: A free 3-site rec site perched on an old railroad grade above McCreight Lake, ending at a historic trestle ruin — atmospheric for anglers and history buffs, but access is 4 km of gravel FSR with very limited turnaround and no stated water or facilities.

campground.name: Rogers Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: Forested creek-side rec site on Cayoosh Creek with direct Highway 99 access, sitting roughly midway between Lillooet and Pemberton — a convenient overnight pull-off with 14 small-to-medium sites and a two-entrance layout. No amenities are listed, and fees apply seasonally.

campground.name: Elaho 53k
campground.desc: A Elaho 53k in Malibu.

campground.name: Spanish Lake Rec Site
campground.desc: A small, treed forest rec site on Spanish Lake, reached by 6 km of gravel on Silvernail Road with a rough, potentially muddy final section; free with no confirmed facilities.

campground.name: Home Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A user-maintained A-frame cabin at the west end of Home Lake, reached by a 6 km one-way hike from the Kluskus Forest Service Road; riders must leave bikes at the trailhead and pack in on foot, with a 2-night maximum stay and no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Bonus Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A compact 3-site recreation site on a small lake just off the highway north of Cranberry Junction, with views of the Kitwanga Range and good wildlife watching; a rough boat launch serves canoeists but no amenities are confirmed.

campground.name: Bain Creek Recreational Campsite
campground.desc: A small 6-site free campsite on the north shore of Gambier Island, accessed by water via Thornbrough Channel as part of the BC Marine Trail; for cycle tourers, the hard reality is this is a boat-in only stop with no road or trail connection.

campground.name: North Foley Lake
campground.desc: A North Foley Lake in Chilliwack.

campground.name: RCMP Campground
campground.desc: A RCMP Campground in Barrett.

campground.name: Mosquito Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: An 11-site shoreline camp on Mosquito Lake, deep on Moresby Island (Haida Gwaii), with a day-use shelter and boat launch; access via the Moresby Mainline logging road makes for a rough ride on a loaded bike.

campground.name: Bisson Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 4-site free rec site on a fishing lake deep in the Okanagan highlands; the final 2.3 km of road is severely eroded and 4WD-only, making it inaccessible to loaded touring cyclists.

campground.name: Starlight
campground.desc: A Starlight in Jersey.

campground.name: Kaikash Creek (BCMT)
campground.desc: A boat-in forest recreation site on Broughton Strait south of Telegraph Cove, popular with sea kayakers; completely inaccessible without a vessel and a non-option for loaded touring cyclists.

campground.name: Blacksmith Landing Eco Camp
campground.desc: A Blacksmith Landing Eco Camp in Copper Creek.

campground.name: Sea-Esta
campground.desc: A Sea-Esta in Saratoga Beach.

campground.name: Starvation Lake
campground.desc: A Starvation Lake in Squamish.

campground.name: Eagle Vista RV Resort & Campground
campground.desc: An RV resort and campground on the edge of Squamish, a hub for climbing, mountain biking, and kiteboarding; amenities and exact setting are unknown as the website is currently unreachable.

campground.name: Bell Mountain Meadow Recreation Site
campground.desc: High alpine meadow rec site near McBride, primarily a winter snowmobile destination with a safety cabin; summer vehicle access is currently closed due to deteriorating road conditions, making it a non-option for most touring cyclists.

campground.name: Executive RV Campground
campground.desc: A Executive RV Campground in Sperling.

campground.name: Clearwater Lake Recreation Area
campground.desc: A quiet 2-site lakeshore rec site in the Chilcotin, just 300 metres off Highway 20, offering views of Mount Nogwon and Peak 2448 with easy access to kayaking, swimming, and fishing; minimal facilities at this small free site.

campground.name: Pyper Lake (Tatla Lake)
campground.desc: A small 3-site clearing at the northeast end of Pyper Lake, with broad Coast Mountain views and a popular swimming hole with a cartop boat launch; a brief 2.5 km detour off Highway 20 on what appears to be a basic gravel road.

campground.name: Muncho Lake RV Park
campground.desc: A Muncho Lake RV Park in Muncho Lake.

campground.name: Miner's Camp
campground.desc: A Miner's Camp in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: Silverthorne Lake
campground.desc: A forested lakeshore campground 8 km south of Houston with a sandy beach, picnic shelter with wood stove, and trails connecting to the Morice Mountain Nordic Ski Area; not a fishing lake but suited for swimming and paddling.

campground.name: Canuck Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A grassy flat beside Canuck Creek with a small scenic waterfall just downstream, offering swimming and fishing 6.5 km off Highway 3 near Yahk. The 2WD-suitable approach is an active logging road, so expect truck traffic and drive with lights on.

campground.name: Homestead Creek Campsite
campground.desc: A two-site roadside rest stop where the Sunshine Coast Trail crosses Southview Road, about 3 km off Highway 101 near Powell River; no confirmed amenities and a bare-bones setup suited to trail pass-throughs rather than a comfortable stay.

campground.name: Sunshine
campground.desc: A Sunshine in Jersey.

campground.name: Fenwick Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A two-site forested rec site on Fenwick Lake, reached via 45 km of Kootenay River FSR plus 6.5 km of navigated side road with four junctions; high-clearance access and active logging make this a significant commitment for a loaded touring bike. A short 150 m trail leads to Fenwick Falls viewpoint.

campground.name: Boulder Bay Site
campground.desc: A Boulder Bay Site in Williams Landing.

campground.name: Cinnamon Recreation Site
campground.desc: A forested recreation site on Cayoosh Creek with direct off-highway access on Hwy 99 between Lillooet and Pemberton; cash only with basic facilities and no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Shea Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 10-site rec site in semi-open forest on the north shore of Shea Lake, well suited to anglers with a small boat launch on site; both approach routes include several kilometres of gravel road and the site is cash only.

campground.name: Jackpine Pass
campground.desc: A Jackpine Pass in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: Twin Lakes
campground.desc: A Twin Lakes in Cherryville.

campground.name: Snowshoe Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small fishing lake hidden in the hills with grassy and treed campsites, good for canoeing and osprey-watching; both access routes involve 4WD or steep, rutted dirt roads that make this a tough reach on a loaded bike.

campground.name: Hihium Lake South Campground
campground.desc: A free, remote interior lake rec site celebrated for its rainbow trout fishery, with a low-power motor restriction keeping things quiet; reaching it requires 37+ km of forest service road before a short access spur.

campground.name: Cypress Harbour (BCMT)
campground.desc: A boat-in-only recreation site on the quiet north shore of Broughton Island, offering a scenic anchorage, grassy landing, and small trails — completely inaccessible by bike and relevant only to multi-modal touring with a kayak or water taxi leg.

campground.name: Greenway Sound (BCMT)
campground.desc: A remote, boat-access-only rec site on Broughton Island's northern shore, offering a grassy knoll with two picnic tables overlooking the bay and a trail connection to Broughton Lake. Unreachable by any road — cyclists must arrive by water.

campground.name: Maynard Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 2-site rec site on the Alice Lake Loop, tucked beside a dammed lake with fluctuating water levels and a rough cartop boat launch; access is entirely via active industrial logging roads.

campground.name: Cat Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Walk-in sites encircle a popular swimming lake just off Hwy 99 near Squamish; active bear problems require strict food storage, and the site fills fast on summer long weekends.

campground.name: Farm Bay
campground.desc: A Farm Bay in Buccaneer Bay.

campground.name: Blue Lake West Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny walk-in tenting site (1–2 tents) set in a mature Douglas-fir stand at the edge of Blue Lake in the Cariboo; a 335m carry from the roadside parking keeps it quiet, but no amenities are listed and space is extremely limited.

campground.name: Fletcher Creek Falls Recreation Site
campground.desc: Semi-open beach site on the west shore of Kootenay Lake with a short trail to a waterfall and moss-lined grotto on Fletcher Creek; the viewing platform above the falls is currently closed due to unstable rock and trees overhead.

campground.name: Manson's Camp
campground.desc: A Manson's Camp in Othello.

campground.name: Flyfish Lake # 1 Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small 3-site free rec site on the Aberdeen Plateau, centred on a backcountry lake with rainbow trout fishing; no confirmed facilities and plateau location suggest a rough forest service road approach.

campground.name: Weaver Lake Campground
campground.desc: A mid-sized rec site on a stocked fishing lake south of Harrison Mills, with a boat launch, dock, and a 6 km boardwalk trail around the lake; the steep, rough Forest Service Road explicitly requires 4WD, making it effectively off-limits for loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: McNair Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free walk-in site on a quiet multi-armed lake in second-growth forest, reached via 2.3 km of McNair FSR then a 500 m carry from the parking lot; suited to fishing and canoeing but impractical for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Antler Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small 3-site Thompson interior rec site where 4x4 is recommended for access; two drive-to spots sit away from the lake, and the third requires a 400 m carry to reach the water.

campground.name: Tsilcoh Falls Recreation Site
campground.desc: A primitive 3-site free rec site on a forest road in northern BC, perched above Tsilcoh Falls with a steep trail down to the river and an exceptional front-row seat to the August kokanee salmon run; no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Stave Island Dispersed Site
campground.desc: A Stave Island Dispersed Site in Miracle Valley.

campground.name: Twan Lake (Williams Lake)
campground.desc: A tiny, remote BC recreation site on Twan Lake reached by forest service road from Quesnel, popular as a hunting and fishing base; no confirmed amenities or water, and a rough 6 km spur off the 100c road.

campground.name: Meta
campground.desc: A Meta in Jersey.

campground.name: Little Bear Bay Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, open recreation site right on Johnstone Strait with broad views of the ocean and Thurlow Islands, renowned as a shore-based orca and cruise-ship watching spot; reached via gravel road with no confirmed water or facilities.

campground.name: Mineral Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site rec site on a warm lake south of Cranbrook, accessed via Lamb Creek FSR; described primarily as a day-use swimming spot with no confirmed overnight amenities.

campground.name: Sussex Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 3-site lake-side rec site sitting in a pine-beetle clearcut, used mainly for day-use fishing and hunting; the narrow, rough approach road is explicitly rated for 4x4 vehicles only, making it a poor choice for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Bob's Lake Recreation Site South Campground
campground.desc: A small alpine lake on Texada Island with 7 sites split between shaded north-shore and sunny south-facing positions; gravel road access from Gillies Bay requires following posted rec-site signs through several intersections.

campground.name: Billy Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, 4-site rec site on the south shore of Billy Lake in the Thompson-Okanagan, offering a semi-open lakeside setting for fishing and boating; access is via the Pamanius Lake Forest Service Road.

campground.name: Mid Valley Camp
campground.desc: A Mid Valley Camp in Alvin.

campground.name: SU8
campground.desc: A SU8 in Vermilion Crossing.

campground.name: Nanton Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, user-maintained lakeside rec site on Nanton Lake, part of the Powell Forest Canoe Route, reached via roughly 17 km of gravel and FSR road from Highway 101; the portage to Ireland Lake is currently closed (May 2025).

campground.name: Francis Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A flat, open landing on the shore of Francis Lake with pit toilets, fire rings, and a basic boat launch for canoes; popular and busy on summer weekends owing to its easy 2WD drive from Prince George.

campground.name: Gavin Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small 5-site lakeside rec site beside the Gavin Lake Education Center, with a boat launch, 800 m of accessible boardwalk around the lake, and mountain bike single-track across the road; reached by 8 km of gravel off the Likely Highway.

campground.name: Sloquet Hot Springs
campground.desc: A rustic rec site on the In-Shuck-ch FSR centred on a small natural hot spring in Xa'xtsa traditional territory; $20/night includes spring access, but the long logging-road approach brings active truck traffic and no cell service, with outhouses only. Gets busy on weekends.

campground.name: Chain Lakes
campground.desc: A Chain Lakes in Creekside.

campground.name: Tenquille Lake
campground.desc: A sub-alpine lake above Pemberton reached only by a multi-kilometre hike from an FSR trailhead; mountain bikes and dogs are banned on all approach trails and at the site, campfires are prohibited, and advance reservation is mandatory.

campground.name: Fowl Lake
campground.desc: A Fowl Lake in Creekside.

campground.name: Cal Cheak Central Camp
campground.desc: A Cal Cheak Central Camp in Whistler.

campground.name: Christmas Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A quiet, free 2-site rec site on Christmas Lake north of Canim Lake, popular with anglers; reached by a long gravel forest service road well beyond Forest Grove.

campground.name: Glen Alder RV Park
campground.desc: A Glen Alder RV Park in Stories Beach.

campground.name: Stella Lake North Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-site rec site on a long gravel forest road deep in Vancouver Island, with a small-boat and canoe launch 100 m down the road; no listed amenities and roughly 18 km of gravel from Highway 19.

campground.name: Wye Lake Campsite
campground.desc: Tent platforms along the semi-alpine Kludahk Trail on Vancouver Island's San Juan Ridge, reached only via logging roads subject to gate closures; snow typically buries the route from November through May.

campground.name: free camping near a river
campground.desc: A free camping near a river in Arrowsmith.

campground.name: Seagull Bay Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small lakeside clearing on Mohun Lake's northeast shore, sitting along the Sayward Forest Canoe Route — overflow tent space for paddlers only, as access is strictly by boat.

campground.name: Jubilee Mountain Campground
campground.desc: A small 2-site free rec site perched on Jubilee Mountain with wide Columbia Valley views; the site is described as day-use but recorded as a campsite, and roughly 6 km of forest service road from Spillimacheen is required to reach it.

campground.name: Lakeside Cabins & Campground
campground.desc: A Lakeside Cabins & Campground in Ainsworth Hot Springs.

campground.name: Caven/Gold Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: Two-site rec site at the confluence of Caven and Gold Creeks, heavily shaded by mature spruce and fir with lush understory; reached via 14 km of Caven Creek FSR, free and secluded.

campground.name: Pollock Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, free, 4-site rec site in partial trees on the Flathead River, reached via an extensive chain of Forest Service Roads totalling well over 60 km from the highway — remote and bare-bones with no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Arlington Lake Campground
campground.desc: Picturesque recreation site on the southernmost of the Arlington Lakes chain with 29 sites across three areas, sitting right beside the Kettle Valley Railway grade; reached via 3.5 km of forest service road, and the adjacent KVR trail carries loose ballast unsuitable for street bikes.

campground.name: Upper Kitimat River Recreation Site
campground.desc: A rustic, user-maintained wilderness site with 6 spots near the confluence of the Wedeene River and Raley Creek, reached via roughly 14.5 km of forestry mainline road north of Kitimat; no confirmed services or facilities.

campground.name: Camper's Roost Park
campground.desc: A Camper's Roost Park in Choate.

campground.name: Khartoum Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A user-maintained treed campsite on Khartoum Lake, one of the larger lakes in the Powell Forest Canoe Route, reached after 27+ km of gravel and active industrial forest-service roads — primarily a paddler's anchor with no confirmed facilities.

campground.name: Rosemond Lake Campground
campground.desc: A Rosemond Lake Campground in Mara.

campground.name: Tobermory Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small, partially treed rec site on Tobermory Creek with a public-use Forest Service cabin — a rare amenity at a free site; access requires roughly 162 km up the Elk River FSR, a long gravel commitment on a loaded bike.

campground.name: Lombardy Park
campground.desc: A Lombardy Park in Langley.

campground.name: Monica Meadows Recreation Site
campground.desc: A hike-in backcountry camp with 4 tent pads set just below the Monica Meadows alpine plateau, offering dramatic mountain views; reaching the trailhead requires a 43 km forest service road with deep water bars and a 2WD high-clearance vehicle, followed by an 8 km round-trip trail.

campground.name: Quesnel Forks Recreation Site
campground.desc: Free 11-site rec site at the confluence of the Quesnel and Cariboo Rivers, beside a gold rush townsite that predates Barkerville; the 13 km access road is well maintained but ends with a steep hill, and two sites plus the day-use area are currently closed due to erosion.

campground.name: Rottacker Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single hike-in site at Rottacker Lake, reached by a rough brushy trail from a trailhead 20 km along Kate-Sitkum Forest Service Road; free and wild but in active grizzly bear habitat with no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Gwen Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site lakeshore rec site on the western shore of Gwen Lake, south of Merritt, with a pleasing grassland view across the water; the final 1 km is an explicitly rough 4x4 track with a steep drop to camp, ruling it out for loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Bose Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small free lakeside rec site with 5 first-come sites, accessed by forest service roads near Highland Valley Copper Mine; the lake is a known fishing draw but no drinking water is mentioned.

campground.name: Bonnington Steed Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny two-site free rec site in the Bonnington Range near Crescent Valley, linked to a Kootenay Mountaineering Club hut; expect primitive conditions, no confirmed water, and a backcountry approach not suited to loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Old Hedley Road East Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 14-site forest recreation site on the banks of the Similkameen River, off Highway 3 between Princeton and Hedley, with river kayaking and swimming as the main draws; fees are cash only and amenities are unconfirmed.

campground.name: Morchuea Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free 8-site forested rec site off the Stewart-Cassiar Highway with Mount Edziza's extraordinary volcanic landscape as a backdrop; no water or washrooms are confirmed, and facilities are minimal for this remote Northern BC setting.

campground.name: Johnson Lake Recreation Site (South)
campground.desc: The south site at Johnson Lake sits in an open Ponderosa Pine and bunchgrass landscape with a small sandy beach and day-use picnic area; a short steep pitch on the gravel approach and cattle-range stiles are the only catches.

campground.name: Camping pullouts along road
campground.desc: A Camping pullouts along road in Pacific Rim National Park.

campground.name: Lowry Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small treed lake site on Vancouver Island, reached after 24 km of forest service and privately managed logging road from Port Alberni; quiet and good for a swim or a fish, but check gate status before you leave.

campground.name: Blinkhorn Peninsula (BCMT)
campground.desc: Boat-in only marine rec site on a wind-sheltered gravel beach south of Telegraph Cove, reached by kayak or small boat across Broughton Strait; no road access and no stated water or facilities.

campground.name: Long Point Recreation Site
campground.desc: A quiet 6-site boat-in rec site on the south shore of Lower Campbell Lake, with a beautiful beach and campsites perched above the water on a short trail — effectively inaccessible to cyclists without arranging a boat.

campground.name: Moira Lake South Recreation Site
campground.desc: A quiet 5-unit semi-open rec site on Moira Lake with a gravel boat launch, reached via 42 km of forest service roads including an active log-hauling road; free and remote, but industrial truck traffic and long rough-road approach make it a serious commitment for a loaded tourer.

campground.name: Harris Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny, free rec site sitting right on the edge of Harris Lake with just two tent spots, a picnic table, and an outhouse; a quiet stop for cyclists coming off the Galena Bay Ferry, though the single-post turnoff on Highway 23 is easy to miss.

campground.name: St. Marie Lake West
campground.desc: A semi-open recreation site sitting directly on St. Marie Lake about 35 km along the Willow-Cale Forest Service Road south of Prince George, with pit toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables; expect company — it sees heavy use all summer.

campground.name: Skmana Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, rustic 3-site camp on the shore of Skmana Lake, reached via roughly 16 km of forest service road north of Chase; suited to fishing, mountain biking, hiking, and XC skiing, but no amenities are confirmed.

campground.name: Mayson Lake North Recreation Site
campground.desc: A remote, first-come-first-served forest service rec site at the 50 km mark on Jamieson Creek FSR, primarily used as a horse camp; the long rough FSR approach makes this a demanding ride for a loaded tourer.

campground.name: Wapiti River Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free 7-site forest rec site on the Wapiti River in remote northern BC, reached by 25 km of forest service road; no confirmed facilities or water on site.

campground.name: Jolly Beach Campground
campground.desc: A Jolly Beach Campground in Camp McKinney.

campground.name: Barnes Lake Recreation Site - North End
campground.desc: A free rec site on a popular rainbow-trout lake near Ashcroft, with 15 vehicle-camping units spread across three areas and a boat launch that can flood at high water; no water or washroom details are stated.

campground.name: Doctor Creek Cabin Recreation Site
campground.desc: A remote log cabin deep in the Kootenay backcountry, renovated and maintained by the Windermere Valley Snowmobile Society as a base for alpine snowmobiling and hiking; overnight use may not be available, and the site sits at the end of roughly 38 km of forest service road.

campground.name: Gordon Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Tiny 4-site rec site on a remote lake southwest of Merritt, drawing anglers and hunters willing to tackle a rough forest service road; the last 2 km over a washed-out cut-block road requires high clearance and makes it a non-starter for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Kappan Lake West Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site lakeside rec site south of Anahim Lake, popular for fishing, boating, and bird watching; the final 1.5 km of access road is steep, narrow, and rough, with 4WD explicitly recommended.

campground.name: Cleswuncut Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-site Cariboo rec site on a quiet lake, offering a table, fire ring, pit toilet, and car-top boat or canoe launch; rainbow trout fishing is possible but uncertain, and the final 34 km of access road is gravel.

campground.name: Hydraulic Lake Campground
campground.desc: A reservoir-side rec site 35 km southeast of Kelowna with rainbow trout fishing, a cartop boat launch, and canoe route, plus direct access to the Kettle Valley Rail Trail — though the KVR surface here runs from hard-packed gravel to loose ballast, unsuitable for road bikes.

campground.name: Tanglechain Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, quiet forested lake site near Smithers with four pitches and a gravel boat launch, drawing anglers after cutthroat trout; the access involves roughly 48 km of active logging road where VHF radio is recommended and the narrow, rough final stretch will rattle a loaded bike.

campground.name: The Grand View
campground.desc: A The Grand View in Lake Country.

campground.name: Balsam
campground.desc: A Balsam in McLeod Lake.

campground.name: Horsefly River Recreation Site
campground.desc: A long, open rec site strung along the Horsefly River, ideal for multi-day stays built around drifting or fishing the river downstream to Horsefly village. Access requires ~127 km of forest service road; the first entrance is steep.

campground.name: Site 2 (BCMT)
campground.desc: A Site 2 (BCMT) in Dolphin Beach.

campground.name: Lake Lovely Water Campsite
campground.desc: A Lake Lovely Water Campsite in Squamish.

campground.name: Palmer Bar Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A compact 3-site recreation site on a partially treed historic mill pond south of Cranbrook, best suited to anglers wanting a quiet overnight. Getting there requires the Lumberton Forest Service Road and a rocky quarry section — rough but rideable on a loaded bike.

campground.name: McLean Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny two-site treed rec site in the Kootenays above a quiet lake, reached by a confusing maze of forest service roads requiring 4WD, then a 100m carry to the water — genuinely hard to find and inaccessible on a loaded bike.

campground.name: Butts Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny, very remote Forest Service rec site on the Flathead Border Road, with a public Forest Service cabin and a short hike to Beryl and Marl lakes; reaching it requires 57+ km on rough FSR roads.

campground.name: South Kendrick Islet Informal Camp (BCMT)
campground.desc: A South Kendrick Islet Informal Camp (BCMT) in Ladysmith.

campground.name: Boolean lake dispersed camping
campground.desc: A Boolean lake dispersed camping in Sweetsbridge.

campground.name: Placer Lake Campsite
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site sub-alpine lake camp suited to tenters only; the final approach demands a high-clearance 4WD vehicle or a 600-metre hike on rough track, making it effectively walk-in for cycle tourers.

campground.name: Patrick Bay
campground.desc: A Patrick Bay in Malibu.

campground.name: Ensign Creek
campground.desc: A Ensign Creek in Cathedral.

campground.name: Trout Creek Crossing
campground.desc: A small, free rec site on Trout Creek alongside the Princeton Summerland Road — a natural overnight for KVR cyclists with a creek dip on offer, though the 8 km of unpaved gravel access and road traffic are real trade-offs.

campground.name: Fish Lake North Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, 3-unit BC Forest Recreation Site on a small lake with a cartop boat launch — ideal for a quiet paddle or fishing stop, accessed via 3.5 km of Forest Service road off Hwy 27.

campground.name: Turner Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny, user-maintained rec site on Turner Lake offering a natural boat launch for car-top boats but zero facilities; reached via a long Forest Service Road northwest of Prince George.

campground.name: Rocky Camp
campground.desc: A Rocky Camp in Malibu.

campground.name: Lost Shoe Campground
campground.desc: A Lost Shoe Campground in Ucluelet.

campground.name: Stewart Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A quiet fishing lake set in old-growth forest 37 km from Sayward, with four sites right at the water's edge and a shoreline trail through ancient trees; access requires several kilometres of gravel logging roads.

campground.name: Germansen Narrows Campground
campground.desc: A Germansen Narrows Campground in 12 Mile.

campground.name: Three Sisters Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small one-party grassy site near Ashcroft used mainly as a base for hang-gliding at nearby Cornwall Hills Provincial Park; the access road is rough and 4x4-recommended in wet weather, and the on-site creek is off-limits as a community water source.

campground.name: Jim Creek (Windy Mountain Road) Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single creekside campsite tucked between Bowers and Needa Lakes in the Cariboo interior, reached via 13.7 km of the Windy Mountain Forest Service Road; no listed amenities and just one site, so solitude is the main draw.

campground.name: Maple Grove Recreation Site
campground.desc: A large, popular rec site on Cowichan Lake with a south-facing beach that holds sun well into the evening and a small boat launch; the final stretch after Youbou turns to gravel, and the site is cash-only at $20/night.

campground.name: Ida Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free highway-side day-use and picnic stop on Highway 30 near Port Alice, primarily a pull-off rest area with a trailhead for the Beaver Lake Interpretive Forest directly across the road; no garbage service and no confirmed overnight facilities.

campground.name: Twin Bay Recreation Site
campground.desc: A quiet two-site lakeshore rec site on Duncan Lake with an outhouse; reached by turning off Highway 31 near Kaslo and then riding 14.5 km of the Duncan Lake FSR — gravel and unconfirmed condition, no drinking water mentioned.

campground.name: Pebbly Beach
campground.desc: A Pebbly Beach in Buccaneer Bay.

campground.name: Goat River Canyon Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free 6-site rec site nestled below Goat River Canyon, reached by roughly 11 km of forest service road plus a narrow 1 km spur, with a short trail to canyon viewpoints and good cutthroat and brook trout fishing. No confirmed water or facilities; the gravel approach is rideable but expect a slow, bumpy haul.

campground.name: Crapapple Creek Campsite
campground.desc: A Crapapple Creek Campsite in Malibu.

campground.name: Free camping spot
campground.desc: A Free camping spot in Leanchoil.

campground.name: Sun Valley RV Park
campground.desc: A cyclist-specific stop in Mission on Highway 7, roughly 1.25 hours east of Vancouver, accredited by multiple bike associations and explicitly geared to touring cyclists — note family camping is not available and the former u-catch fish farm closed in 2024.

campground.name: South Weaver Lake Group Site
campground.desc: A seasonal group campsite on a stocked fishing lake off a steep, rough FSR near Harrison Mills, with a boat launch and a 6 km lakeside trail popular with anglers and families; 4WD is required for access and all overnight options are group-site bookings at $270+/night, making it a skip for solo touring cyclists.

campground.name: Pine Creek Campground
campground.desc: A Pine Creek Campground in Atlin.

campground.name: Copper Hut Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site backcountry recreation site tied to the Kootenay Mountaineering Club's Copper Mountain Cabin above Nelson; expect a hike-in approach, no services, and high-alpine terrain.

campground.name: Progress Point
campground.desc: A Progress Point in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: Saltlick Camp
campground.desc: A Saltlick Camp in Sunshine Valley.

campground.name: Camp Midnight
campground.desc: A Camp Midnight in Gates.

campground.name: Squamish Riverside Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free riverside recreation site with 9 tent pitches, tables, and fire rings on the Squamish River near Ashlu Creek, popular for fishing; the last ~1 km of approach is unpaved dirt road, there is no treated water or garbage service, and bear activity plus flood risk during heavy rain are noted.

campground.name: Meadow Cabin
campground.desc: A remote mountain cabin managed by the Nelson Sno-Goers snowmobile club, reached by 29 km of rough forest service road requiring high clearance and 4WD — a winter snowmobiling destination with no practical utility for a loaded touring cyclist.

campground.name: Zacharias Bay
campground.desc: A Zacharias Bay in Queens Cove.

campground.name: Coyote Lake Campground
campground.desc: A Coyote Lake Campground in Lang Bay.

campground.name: Deer Camp
campground.desc: A Deer Camp in Sunshine Valley.

campground.name: Goldilocks
campground.desc: A Goldilocks in Alvin.

campground.name: Old Hedley Road West
campground.desc: A BC rec site on the north bank of the Similkameen River, well-suited for a swimmer or paddler's layover; cash only with seasonally adjusted fees. Old Hedley Road is likely unpaved gravel running parallel to Highway 3.

campground.name: Leroy Lakes Campsite
campground.desc: A small 2-site rec site on Leroy Lake south of Logan Lake, offering fishing, boating, and a side trip to nearby Dorothy Lake; access is via a rough hydro-line track off Highway 97C.

campground.name: Gump Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, first-come-first-served rec site on a small stocked 20-hectare lake accessed via a 2.5 km powerline road after a sequence of back-road turns off Highway 97C; fly fishing for rainbow trout is the only real draw, and the single site means it can easily be taken.

campground.name: Larchwood Campsite
campground.desc: Open, sunny lakeside sites at a small Kootenays lake with good views and strong spring fishing; access is 6 km of gravel FSR that can get rough, and the site fills fast in summer.

campground.name: Abbot Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small 3-site rec site on the northeast shore of Abbott Lake in a semi-open setting northwest of Merritt, popular for fishing and boating; 4x4-only access via Tyner Lake FSR rules it out for most loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Fletcher Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A remote alpine lake reached only by steep hike after a 4x4-required forest service road; two primitive sites in sub-alpine forest with good backcountry fishing, but active grizzly bears demand noise and strict food storage.

campground.name: Grassy Hut Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site backcountry recreation site in the Kootenay mountains near Crescent Valley, linked to the Kootenay Mountaineering Club's Grassy Hut; details are sparse but expect a primitive, likely hike-in stop suited to mountaineers rather than road tourers.

campground.name: Tyner Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free 6-site rec site on Tyner Lake suited to anglers and hunters, with a small gravel boat launch; reached via 14 km of rough Pamanuis FSR that is explicitly flagged as requiring caution.

campground.name: Cairnes Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: Remote rec site at the Blaeberry River trailhead for the historic Howse Pass wilderness trail, reached via roughly 41km of active forest service road from Golden; no confirmed amenities and demanding FSR access make this a committed backcountry objective.

campground.name: Moose Lake Campground
campground.desc: A free lakeside rec site set back 5.5 km on a gravel Forest Service Road near Tumbler Ridge, with a small dock and a Rainbow Trout–stocked lake; ATV trails surround the area and 15 pads handle overflow use.

campground.name: Francis Lake Campground
campground.desc: A free, four-site rec site on a small, no-motorboat lake off the West Harrison Forest Service Road, reached by a 4WD-only spur; the quiet water draws anglers and hikers but the access road makes it a non-starter for loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Lighthouse RV Park
campground.desc: A Lighthouse RV Park in Kelowna.

campground.name: Sandspit Camping Area
campground.desc: A Sandspit Camping Area in Squamish.

campground.name: 7 Mile Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, shaded valley-bottom rec site with mature Larch and Lodgepole Pine beside a shallow lake stocked with Cutthroat trout every other year; the 29 km forest service road approach is a real commitment on a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Mission Dam Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small 3-site rec site beside the Terzaghi (Mission) Dam at the eastern end of Carpenter Lake, northwest of Lillooet; spots are open and sunny but can be dusty, and swimming is prohibited at the dam outlet due to frequent water releases.

campground.name: Drewry Lake East Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, free 3-site rec site on the northeast shore of Drewry Lake in the Cariboo interior, offering lakeside camping with fishing and boating access; the final 10.8 km of the approach is gravel on the Mahood Lake Public Road.

campground.name: Ideal Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, 7-site forest recreation site on the shore of 146-hectare Ideal Lake, reached via forest service roads and valued locally for Rainbow trout fishing. No confirmed amenities; expect a long gravel approach and a remote, unfacilitated stay.

campground.name: Camp Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single shaded site tucked behind spruce and pine on Camp Lake, accessed by a charming footbridge off Stone Creek FSR; the lake suits kayaks and canoes, but the 10 km FSR approach is gravel and the lone site fills fast.

campground.name: Jacobson Lake Camp
campground.desc: A five-site treed rec site at the 45.8 km mark of the Tulameen River FSR, serving as the trailhead for the 'Treasures of the Tulameen' historic trail network with a large interpretive kiosk. Access involves 45+ km of active industrial logging road — expect heavy trucks, dust, and low visibility in dry weather.

campground.name: ParkCanada RV Park
campground.desc: A ParkCanada RV Park in Tsawwassen.

campground.name: Pebble Beach Campground
campground.desc: A Pebble Beach Campground in Germansen Landing.

campground.name: Little Slocan River Recreation Area
campground.desc: A small, free lakeside rec site on Little Slocan Lakes in a semi-open setting; the 21 km forest service road approach from Highway 6 is the main hurdle, and no amenities are confirmed.

campground.name: Trapper Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A Trapper Lake Recreation Site in Manning Park.

campground.name: Mohun Beach Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small boat-access-only lakeside site on the Sayward Forest Canoe Route, fitting just 2–3 tents on the east shore of Mohun Lake; a loaded touring bike cannot reach it without first launching a canoe.

campground.name: Delacy Camp
campground.desc: A Delacy Camp in Sunshine Valley.

campground.name: Cal Cheak Callaghan Camp
campground.desc: A large, heavily shaded forest service campground set between Callaghan Creek and Cheakamus River, just off Highway 99 three kilometres north of Brandywine Falls; access is via a short forest service road, fees are self-registered seasonally, and bears are frequently active in camp.

campground.name: Wapiti Crossing Recreation Site
campground.desc: A remote free rec site on the Wapiti River, reached by 25 km of forest service road deep in Northern BC; no confirmed amenities and a long FSR approach keep crowds thin.

campground.name: Douglas Bay
campground.desc: A Douglas Bay in Squamish.

campground.name: Deadman Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small 4-site lakeshore rec site tucked in a narrow, breezy valley amid the arid Thompson Country — good for swimming, kayaking, and cartop-boat fishing, with no cell service and private residences on both sides requiring respectful behaviour.

campground.name: Boer Mountain Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free rec site 10-15 minutes from Burns Lake anchored by a sizeable mountain bike network managed by Ride Burns, a 3 km trail circling Kager Lake with a dock, and a mix of vehicle-accessible and walk-in tent sites; note some trails remain closed for post-fire danger-tree assessment.

campground.name: Macdonald Island
campground.desc: A Macdonald Island in Malibu.

campground.name: McMurray Bay Campsite
campground.desc: A McMurray Bay Campsite in McCalls Landing.

campground.name: Becher Bay Campground
campground.desc: A Becher Bay Campground in Sooke.

campground.name: Hart Farm Recreation Site
campground.desc: A large lakeshore site on Kalum Lake with a sandy beach, boating, fishing, and 7 km of adjacent cycling trails; the 26 km West Kalum forestry road floods repeatedly in spring and heavy rain, potentially trapping campers for weeks.

campground.name: Tyaughton Creek Recreation Site Campground
campground.desc: A primitive 4-site recreation site deep in Cariboo-Chilcotin country, reached by Tyaughton Lake Road and Mud Creek Forest Service Road; no confirmed facilities, so self-sufficiency is essential, but the creek-side setting and big-sky scenery draw riders, hunters, and horse packers.

campground.name: Cat Lake Overflow camping
campground.desc: Walk-in campsites ringing a popular Squamish-area swimming lake, reached via ~2.5 km of Cheekeye Forest Service Road off Hwy 99; recurring bear activity requires strict food storage discipline.

campground.name: 2 Bear Campsite
campground.desc: A 2 Bear Campsite in Egmont.

campground.name: Tamarack Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Three-site lakeshore rec site tucked on the south end of Tamarack Lake near Skookumchuck, with a dock and boat launch for small watercraft; reached via a signed gravel forest road off the Torrent FS Road, manageable by 2WD.

detail.address: Tamarack Lake Recreation Road, Skookumchuck, V0B 2E0

campground.name: Log House Campground
campground.desc: A Log House Campground in Bonnet Hill.

campground.name: Knapp Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-unit forest service site on a forested bench above Knapp Lake, drawing anglers and hunters to its gravel boat launch and multi-species fishery; the narrow, rough FSR approach (~34 km) requires high clearance and is prohibitive for trailers.

campground.name: Eagle Lake West Recreation Site
campground.desc: Free 4-site recreation site on the open meadow edge of Eagle Lake, a shallow alkaline lake deep in Tsilhqot'in country; a couple of hilltop sites sit above the north end, but no water or facilities are confirmed.

campground.name: Fraser Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, free two-site rec site at the 9 km mark of Beaverfoot FSR, doubling as the trailhead for a 1.8 km hike to a viewpoint over Wapta Falls; only a pit toilet and picnic tables, no water mentioned.

campground.name: East Maury Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small 2-site treed rec site on Maury Lake with a gravel boat launch, accessed via roughly 56 km of forest service and active log-hauling roads from Clearwater; no confirmed amenities beyond the boat ramp.

campground.name: Paska Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A large, locally popular lakeside rec site 50 km southwest of Kamloops, offering plentiful (if small) trout and kokanee fishing in a family-friendly setting. Access is via a gravel road off the Coquihalla; first-come, first-served with a 14-day limit.

campground.name: Third Beach
campground.desc: A Third Beach in Nuchatlitz.

campground.name: Chist Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, free 3-site recreation site off the North Kitimat Mainline near Kitimat, positioned as a base for rock climbing and bouldering; no water on site, and reaching it requires several turns along a gravel mainline road.

campground.name: Tupper Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 3-site lakeside rec site southwest of Logan Lake, used mainly by anglers and hunters with a small boat launch; 4x4-only access makes it impractical for most loaded touring cyclists.

campground.name: Meadow Mountain Cabin
campground.desc: A remote winter cabin deep in the Selkirks, managed by the Nelson Sno-Goers snowmobile club; the 29 km forest service road requires high clearance and 4WD with steep rough sections, making this effectively inaccessible to loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Felker Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A medium-sized free recreation site with 11 defined campsites along the Felker Lake shoreline in the Cariboo; accessed via roughly 22 km of rural roads off Hwy 20, with no confirmed water or facilities beyond the site.

campground.name: Cat Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Walk-in sites encircle a popular swimming lake just 2.5 km off Hwy 99 north of Squamish, with firewood usually available on site. Recurring bear activity demands strict food storage, and the site fills quickly on long-weekend Fridays.

campground.name: Boulder Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-site natural camp tucked beside a remote Northern BC lake, reached by 17 km of forest road to a gas plant gate and then a kilometre down an NEB pipeline right-of-way; no amenities whatsoever and access is described as ATV/snowmobile terrain.

campground.name: Klein Lake Camground
campground.desc: Klein Lake is a community-run lakeshore campground on BC's Sunshine Coast with 23 drive-in sites spread around a quiet turtle-habitat lake; access is via a forest service road off Highway 101 near Egmont, cell service is unreliable, and payment is cash only. Fishing and canoeing from the docked shoreline are the main draws, though dogs must stay leashed to protect nesting Western Painted Turtles.

campground.name: Nighthawk
campground.desc: A Nighthawk in Squamish.

campground.name: Olivine Camp
campground.desc: A Olivine Camp in Tulameen.

campground.name: Brittany Bay
campground.desc: A Brittany Bay in Bloedel.

campground.name: Upper Gnat Rest Area
campground.desc: A Upper Gnat Rest Area in Dease Lake.

campground.name: Vuich Falls Recreation Site
campground.desc: A compact 3-site forest rec site at kilometre 34 of the Tulameen River Forest Service Road, with a short trail to a cliff-top lookout above the cascading falls of Vuich Creek; no confirmed amenities and a steep drop at the viewpoint.

campground.name: Pinch Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small open-grass site sitting beside a large creek with a small scenic waterfall just downstream; good for a swim or a cast, reached via an active logging road that demands headlights and patience.

campground.name: Twin Bridges
campground.desc: A Twin Bridges in Chilliwack.

campground.name: Harmon Lake West Recreation Site
campground.desc: A well-developed lakeside rec site in Kane Valley reached by 9 km of maintained gravel off Highway 5A; the cattle-fenced site offers a floating dock, boat launch, horseshoe pits, and access to 50+ km of trails, with a 24/7 site host.

campground.name: Kernaghan Lake North Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-spot primitive rec site in forested terrain near Kernaghan Lake, reached by rough road; no confirmed amenities, so treat it as a bare backcountry stop.

campground.name: War Lake
campground.desc: A War Lake in McLeod Lake.

campground.name: Trout Creek Ranch (basic campsite)
campground.desc: A small 2-site stopover nestled between the Kettle Valley Railway trail and Trout Creek, well-positioned for KVR cycle tourists passing through the Summerland area; no confirmed amenities and the only non-trail access is a narrow 4WD road.

campground.name: Chase Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, free provincial recreation site on Chase Creek roughly 14 km north of Falkland, reached by a named paved/gravel road; the draw is creek fishing, with no confirmed water or facilities on site.

campground.name: Bannock Point Recreation Site
campground.desc: Walk-in campground on Slocan Lake reached by a 700 m moderately steep trail from the parking lot; lower sites sit steps from a pebble beach with clear swimming and evening views of the Valhalla Mountains, but loaded bikes mean a stiff carry-in.

campground.name: Madeley Lake Campsite
campground.desc: A Madeley Lake Campsite in Whistler.

campground.name: Beaver South Recreation Site
campground.desc: A paddle-in overnight on Beaver Lake along the Powell Forest Canoe Route, reached only by water from the Little Horseshoe Lake portage — entirely unreachable by loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Mud Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single free site beside Big Sheep Creek, reached by a short gravel spur off Highway 3 near Nancy Greene Lake; bare-bones with no confirmed amenities, but a useful trailhead base for the Paulson trail system.

campground.name: Raffuse Creek Recreation Area
campground.desc: A Raffuse Creek Recreation Area in Squamish.

campground.name: Etcho Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-vehicle site on a small, secluded lake in the Cariboo, reached by two forest service roads and a rough narrow 900m spur — genuinely quiet but bare-bones with no confirmed facilities. The demanding access makes it best suited to cyclists comfortable on rugged gravel.

campground.name: Alder Grove Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-site shaded recreation site on a historic rail grade, with a short trail to the lakeshore; reached by the gravel Rock Bay FSR off Highway 19 north of Campbell River.

campground.name: Stump Lake Rec Site Campground
campground.desc: A sheltered rec site on a bay of Stump Lake, set on a steep grassy hillside and popular with anglers; reached by roughly 4.5 km of secondary road off Highway 5A via Peter Hope Road.

campground.name: Windfall Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 2-site camp on the Sukunka River accessed via 45 km of active industrial FSR from Hwy 29; expect logging truck traffic in spring and summer and no confirmed facilities.

campground.name: Dairy Lake West Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small 4-site forest recreation site on a stocked 25-hectare lake east of Kamloops, suited to a quiet fishing stop focused on trolling and fly-fishing; access is via the Dairy FSR, a forest service road.

campground.name: Private Campground
campground.desc: A Private Campground in Oyama.

campground.name: Greenacres Mobile Home Park
campground.desc: A Greenacres Mobile Home Park in Chilliwack.

campground.name: Aileen Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site outhouse-only spot on a small fishing lake deep in the Coldstream backcountry; the last 800 m of ingrown track with water bars and standing puddles demands a 4WD truck and makes the site effectively unreachable by loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Defrauder Falls Marine Day Use Area
campground.desc: A Defrauder Falls Marine Day Use Area in Williams Landing.

campground.name: Tansky
campground.desc: A Tansky in Sooke.

campground.name: Ogre Lake
campground.desc: A Ogre Lake in Pemberton Meadows.

campground.name: Archer Point Dispersed Campsite
campground.desc: A Archer Point Dispersed Campsite in Squamish.

campground.name: Sapperton Dyke
campground.desc: A Sapperton Dyke in North Vancouver.

campground.name: Battleship Bay Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single user-maintained gravel-beach site on the eastern shore of Stuart Lake, roughly 13 km from Fort St James — genuinely scenic but reachable by boat only, making it a non-starter for any cyclist without water transport.

campground.name: Campo Mucho Relaxo
campground.desc: A Campo Mucho Relaxo in Skookumchuck.

campground.name: Little Slocan Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, semi-open, free rec site on the shore of Little Slocan Lakes, offering a quiet lakeside overnight for 6 parties. Getting there requires roughly 21 km of Little Slocan Forest Service Road — gravel, potentially washboard — and no amenities are confirmed on site.

campground.name: Free camping
campground.desc: A Free camping in Tumbler Ridge.

campground.name: Paddy Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-unit recreation site at the southeast end of Paddy Lake, reached via the gravel 6000 Road and then a rough, narrow 3.5 km access road; a short 100 m trail drops down to the water.

campground.name: Twin One Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 15-site rec site sitting somewhat open on jade-coloured Lillooet Lake with two small grassy areas and an unimproved boat launch; reached via 8.5 km of active In-shuck-ch Forest Service Road shared with logging trucks.

campground.name: Ramillies Channel
campground.desc: A Ramillies Channel in Camp Artaban.

campground.name: Sulphur Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free 3-site rec site on Sulphur Creek reached via the Bull River FSR and a final 2 km of good gravel road; cold mineral springs a short drive east add a point of interest to an otherwise simple, open creek-side stay.

campground.name: Tacheeda Lakes Northeast Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free lakeshore rec site on Tacheeda Lakes with good multi-species fishing, but positioned right on the road with noise, dust, and a notoriously busy industrial FSR approach shared with heavy truck traffic.

campground.name: Redwillow River
campground.desc: A small free rec site with 4 pads tucked along the Red Willow River in the Peace Country, reached via a short FSR spur off Hwy 52; no confirmed amenities and a remote feel.

campground.name: Oldham Beach Recreation Site
campground.desc: A Oldham Beach Recreation Site in Nuchatlitz.

campground.name: Calling Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small free rec site on Calling Lake, reached via the Pimainus and Calling FSRs with access that can be rough; primarily a fishing base camp for nearby Big Ok (Island Lake), with 4 sites and basic washrooms.

campground.name: Colin Arthur Dionne Memorial Climbers Camp
campground.desc: A volunteer-built climbers' base camp at the end of 34 miles of the Goat Lake Mainline in the Eldred Valley, serving as the launch point for Psyche Slab, Caragdur, and other major rock walls. Free and remote with no listed amenities — carry all water and supplies.

campground.name: Baynes Lake RV Park
campground.desc: A Baynes Lake RV Park in Baynes Lake.

campground.name: Duffy Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 54-site forest recreation site on Duffy Lake on Greenstone Mountain, south of Cherry Creek; access is via the Dairy Lake FSR, making it a rough but manageable ride to a calm lakeside stopover.

campground.name: Lizard Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A treed lakeside rec site sitting directly on the Pacific Circle Route, with lake swimming, a stocked trout fishing dock, and a separated beach day-use area; cash only with on-site supervision.

campground.name: Borrow pit 8 recreation site
campground.desc: A single-site pull-off on the paved Alaska Highway at the 416km mark, used by through-travellers as a quick rest and by anglers; no confirmed amenities or water on site.

campground.name: Divide Lake Campground
campground.desc: A Divide Lake Campground in Naramata.

campground.name: Butts Cabin
campground.desc: A remote Forest Service recreation site and public-use cabin on the Flathead Border Road deep in the Kootenays, reached after 57+ km of forest service road; a short hike west leads to Beryl and Marl alpine lakes.

campground.name: Top Lake & Peta Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Two small rec sites at km 23-24 on the narrow, winding Sutherland-Trout Forest Service Road: Peta Lake has 4 units on a quiet lake with good canoeing, while Top Lake's single picnic unit sits at the continental Skeena-Fraser watershed divide. No facilities are confirmed and the FSR approach is rough.

campground.name: Tent Lake Campsite
campground.desc: Tent platforms perched on the semi-alpine Kludahk Trail along San Juan Ridge, surrounded by wildflower meadows, bogs, and small lakes; access requires forest service roads with potential gate closures, and the ridge is snow-covered roughly November through May.

campground.name: Blueberry Lake
campground.desc: A Blueberry Lake in Dunster.

campground.name: Bremner Delta Recreation Reserve
campground.desc: A Bremner Delta Recreation Reserve in Tipella.

campground.name: Lambe Creek
campground.desc: A Lambe Creek in Donald.

campground.name: Swan's Point Resort & Trailer Park
campground.desc: A Swan's Point Resort & Trailer Park in Chilliwack.

campground.name: Free dispersed camping
campground.desc: A Free dispersed camping in Big Eddy.

campground.name: Woodcock Lake Recreation Site
