campground.desc: A rustic, isolated rec site on a small Cariboo lake, reached by roughly 67 km of Forest Service road; free and quiet but remote and basic with no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Erie Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small free forest service site tucked in semi-open forest beside clear Erie Creek, about 10 km up a gravel FSR from Highway 3 near Salmo. Shade, creek access, and room for a few groups, but no confirmed amenities and the gravel approach adds effort.

campground.name: Ladybird Recreation Site
campground.desc: Quiet, five-site lakeside rec site on 30-hectare Crescent Lake, prized for spring and fall rainbow trout fishing and a cartop boat launch; nearly 29 km of Peachland Forest Service Road separates it from the highway.

campground.name: Miller Creek Campground
campground.desc: A forest and lakefront campground set among fir and hemlock off Hwy 28 west of Campbell River, with a sandy beach, boat launch, dock, and fishing access — reached via a short gravel FSR spur. No garbage disposal on site and cash only for walk-in payment.

campground.name: Kwanila Beach
campground.desc: A Kwanila Beach in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: Barton Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Seven sites split between two areas on the terraced, forested shores of Barton Lake, surrounded by Douglas fir; reached via a long Forest Service Road haul (40+ km on the Pelican FSR) complicated by a current bridge closure requiring a lengthy alternative route. Kayaking and canoeing are available but fishing is limited to coarse fish.

campground.name: Little Horseshoe Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 2-site paddle-in overnight stop at the eastern portage between Horseshoe Lake and Little Horseshoe Lake on a BC canoe route; accessible only by water with no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Marquart Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Open, sunny 13-site lake rec site southeast of Merritt, popular with anglers and mountain bikers; access is via gravel Lundbom Lake Road off Highway 5A/97C.

campground.name: Reflector Lake East Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, free 3-site rec site in treed forest beside Reflector Lake near Clearwater; reached via roughly 12 km of explicitly rough forest road that will slow and shake a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Random
campground.desc: A Random in Tumbler Ridge.

campground.name: Canuck Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small open grassy site beside a creek with a scenic waterfall just downstream, good for swimming and fishing; reached via 6.5 km of active logging road from Yahk.

detail.address: Yahk Meadow Creek Road, Yahk, V0B 2P0

campground.name: Gold Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small, partially treed site on the bank of Gold Creek near Lake Koocanusa, set well below the Newgate highway so road noise is minimal; access is a rough, steep 4WD-only gravel road that effectively rules it out for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Bernard Beaches
campground.desc: A popular Kootenay Lake rec site offering tent pitches directly on the water; reached via 12 km of 2WD forest service road from Riondel, which is manageable but expect gravel and washboard on a loaded bike.

campground.name: Dease Lake RV Park
campground.desc: A Dease Lake RV Park in Dease Lake.

campground.name: Ram/Cabin Pass Recreation Site
campground.desc: A two-site snowmobile cabin in the Kootenay backcountry south of Fernie, explicitly open for winter use only and reached by roughly 47 km of branching forest service roads — of no practical value to a summer cycle tourer.

campground.name: Cypress Point
campground.desc: A Cypress Point in Miracle Valley.

campground.name: Tunnel - Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, open 4-site rec site on the banks of the Ashnola River, reached via ~14 km of gravel Ashnola Road from Hwy 3 near Keremeos; minimal shade and no stated water supply, but free and first-come first-served.

campground.name: Wadey Recreation Site
campground.desc: Thirty treed sites on Lake Revelstoke with a beach day-use area, accessed directly off Highway 23 North making it an easy pull-off for cyclists; open and fee-charging May through September only.

campground.name: Dinner Rock Recreation Site
campground.desc: A Dinner Rock Recreation Site in Lund.

campground.name: Hubbard Creek Camp
campground.desc: A Hubbard Creek Camp in Sunshine Valley.

campground.name: Mossland Dispersed Camping
campground.desc: A Mossland Dispersed Camping in Big Eddy.

campground.name: Group Campground
campground.desc: A Group Campground in Kingfisher.

campground.name: Chimney Lake North Recreation Site
campground.desc: Open grassland recreation site on Chimney Lake featuring a large sandy beach and designated swimming area, with spacious campsites; access requires roughly 27 km of gravel on Dog Creek and Chimney Valley Roads from Hwy 20.

campground.name: Mcculloch Reservoir Campground
campground.desc: A 39-site reservoir campground with a cartop boat launch and quiet canoe route southeast of Kelowna, accessed via Forest Service Road; seasonal operation runs May 1 to October 15 with no on-site reservations.

campground.name: Missezula Lake Campground
campground.desc: A small, shady 10-site recreation site at the north end of long, narrow Missezula Lake, suited to fishing and power boating; access is via Dillard Creek Forest Service Road off Highway 5A, and tight sites may challenge larger rigs.

campground.name: Riley Dam (Clinton)
campground.desc: A small semi-open rec site on dam-formed Riley Lake, popular for fishing and picnicking; reaching it demands roughly 42 km of forest service road from Hwy 97, with no confirmed water or facilities.

campground.name: Conglomerate Flats Camp
campground.desc: A Conglomerate Flats Camp in Sunshine Valley.

campground.name: Derrick Lake (Steward) Recreation Site
campground.desc: A rustic 4-site free rec site on Derrick Lake in Northern BC, with two sites tucked into mature hemlock forest above the lake and two more near a boat launch and dock; reached by roughly 7 km of rough forest service road off Hwy 37.

campground.name: Lodestone Lake Camp
campground.desc: A tiny alpine lake camp on the historic HBC Brigade Trail, prized by anglers and wildflower enthusiasts and marked by a historical kiosk; the final kilometre is a rough, steep 4x4 track that makes it inaccessible to loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Bush Arm
campground.desc: A small, open recreation site on the south shore of Kinbasket Lake, accessed via 46 km of Forest Service road; the unimproved boat launch works only at higher water levels and no amenities are confirmed.

campground.name: tent area
campground.desc: A tent area in Naramata.

campground.name: Johnson Lake Recreation Site (North)
campground.desc: A 5-site north-shore camp in open Ponderosa Pine and bunchgrass country less than 1 km off Hwy 93/95, accessed via a gravel pit road; cattle fencing requires using stiles, and the lake edge here is marshy — the south site is the preferred stop for swimming.

campground.name: Motel 66
campground.desc: A Motel 66 in Gates.

campground.name: Heffley Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Popular lakeside rec site on Heffley Lake with 30 first-come sites split between a lakeshore area and a quieter forested east section; fills fast in summer and cannot be reserved.

campground.name: Last Call Lake Campground
campground.desc: A Last Call Lake Campground in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: Engstrom's Pond Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, secluded pothole lake rec site with a dock, reached via roughly 22 km of active logging road requiring 4WD and high clearance — the final stretch is impassable when wet, making this a non-starter for loaded bikes.

campground.name: Fourteen Mile Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single secluded site overlooking a small lake deep in the Kootenays, reached via 32 km of active logging road where CB radio is recommended; free and quiet, but the long rough approach limits spontaneity.

campground.name: Poplar Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A semi-open, forested 7-unit rec site on the southeastern shore of Tagetochlain (Poplar) Lake with a gravel boat launch; reached via 60+ km of active logging roads where a VHF radio is recommended, and prized for lake trout and burbot fishing in spring and fall.

campground.name: Horseguard Camp
campground.desc: A Horseguard Camp in Tulameen.

campground.name: Bobtail Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, three-area rec site strung along the shores of Bobtail Lake in open Douglas Fir country, with pit toilets, a boat launch, and good fishing for rainbow trout, kokanee, and burbot; the catch is 35+ km of Forest Service road to reach it, so plan for a self-sufficient overnight.

campground.name: Sedan Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A Sedan Creek Recreation Site in Woodcock.

campground.name: North Deka Camp
campground.desc: Prose provided describes Sulphurous Lake Recreation Site, a day-use-only facility with a boat launch, swimming bay, and picnic tables — no overnight camping is permitted there.

campground.name: Halkett Bay
campground.desc: A tiny 3-site backcountry marine campground reachable only by boat, with limited services outside summer; registration is required either online or on arrival.

campground.name: Pebble Beach Recreation Site
campground.desc: A hike-in wilderness beach camp (2 km trail from the forest service road trailhead) on a sheltered pebble-and-rock bay on Kootenay Lake's east shore — free and beautiful, but loaded touring bikes must be left at the trailhead.

campground.name: Tye
campground.desc: A Tye in Tye.

campground.name: Dodd Lake Campground
campground.desc: A free, user-maintained lakeshore site on the Powell Forest Canoe Route, reached via roughly 24 km of gravel/FSR from Powell River with no confirmed amenities; a remote and quiet spot best suited to self-sufficient tourers willing to earn the approach.

campground.name: Richmond Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A compact 4-site rec site on a crystal-clear stocked rainbow trout lake, reached by a well-maintained gravel FSR a few kilometres off Hwy 16; no confirmed facilities, so come self-sufficient.

campground.name: Airplane Creek
campground.desc: A Airplane Creek in Chilliwack.

campground.name: Trophy Mountain Buffalo Ranch
campground.desc: A Trophy Mountain Buffalo Ranch in Clearwater.

campground.name: Garland Bay Recreation Site
campground.desc: A large open beach on Kootenay Lake's east shore, well-suited for swimming, fishing, and boating; accessed via ~13 km of 2WD-suitable forest service road from Riondel.

campground.name: Kitwanga Centennial Park
campground.desc: A Kitwanga Centennial Park in Kitwanga.

campground.name: Cougar Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A large 65-site rec site perched on Tlupana Inlet among towering Red Cedar, with a recently upgraded dock and fish-cleaning station serving anglers and kayakers headed into Nootka Sound; reached by roughly 40 km of forest service and logging road from Gold River, cash only, no garbage pickup.

campground.name: Decent spots
campground.desc: A Decent spots in Summit Lake.

campground.name: Boot Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A popular stocked-trout lake in Northern BC with 22 sites and a small dock, accessed via 16 km of the Noel Resource Road off Hwy 52. Free with no confirmed water or washroom amenities; the resource-road approach adds effort.

campground.name: Vicker's Creek North
campground.desc: A Vicker's Creek North in Alvin.

campground.name: Homesite Creek Falls Recreation Site
campground.desc: Quiet forested rec site on a 2 km forest service road beside Homesite Creek, with scenic waterfalls and trailhead access to the Suncoaster Trail's Secret Cove section; cash only at $20/night.

campground.name: Marble River Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, well-maintained rec site just off Highway 30 near Port Alice, with riverside lower-loop sites along the Marble River and tree-sheltered upper-loop sites connecting to a 4.2 km trail in adjacent provincial park; no garbage services and gated closed each September.

campground.name: Cal Woods Recreation Reserve
campground.desc: A small, free winter-recreation staging area reached by a 17 km uphill grind on a narrow mixed-surface road from Lytton, offering 3 picnic tables and an enclosed day-use shelter for snowmobilers and tobogganing; summer camping is bare-bones with no confirmed water or washrooms.

campground.name: Bowman Point Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site boat-in recreation site on Lower Arrow Lake where Bowman Creek meets the lake, offering shaded treed spots among rocky outcrops or open beach camping with morning sun and good fishing; completely inaccessible without a boat.

campground.name: Ashnola River Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, no-frills grassy riverside site about 18 km from Keremeos on what is likely a gravel road, set directly beside cattle and horse corrals; two picnic tables and a toilet are the only facilities.

campground.name: Willies Cove Campsite
campground.desc: A Willies Cove Campsite in McCalls Landing.

campground.name: Sunset Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free lakeside recreation site near Topley offering open grassy camping, a designated swimming area, and a concrete boat launch on a lake known for rainbow trout and burbot; a short gravel-road detour off Hwy 16.

campground.name: Sweetwater Spring
campground.desc: A Sweetwater Spring in Billings Bay.

campground.name: Scary Crossing Pass
campground.desc: A Scary Crossing Pass in Alvin.

campground.name: Quiniscoe Lake Campground
campground.desc: A Quiniscoe Lake Campground in Keremeos.

campground.name: Marshall Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small 3-site treed campground at the south end of Marshall Lake near the creek outflow, offering fishing and boating in a quiet mountain setting. Reaching it requires roughly 11 km of gravel forest road off Highway 40 with several turns; tents or small units only.

campground.name: Haystack Lakes
campground.desc: A Haystack Lakes in Keremeos.

campground.name: Barsby Lake Camp Site
campground.desc: A Barsby Lake Camp Site in Nanaimo.

campground.name: Little Douglas Lake Campground
campground.desc: A free, first-come tent camp on Little Douglas Lake, reached by a 2 km hike-in trail from Zum Peak Recreation Site — bog bridges, 70 m of elevation, and an unbridged creek that is impassable in high water. Facilities are minimal: small tent pads, food caches, a toilet, and a communal fire pit; no drinking water is mentioned.

campground.name: Big OK Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A rocky, exposed, and often windy high-elevation (1504 m) rec site beside a remote lake prized for fly-fishing; the lengthy forest-road approach with a 4x4 recommendation makes this a near-impossible reach on a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Whiskey Flats Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small free 3-unit rec site on a forest service road 14 km from historic Barkerville, offering a quiet base for exploring the townsite and the back roads toward Yanks Peak; no confirmed amenities or water.

campground.name: Claimpost
campground.desc: A Claimpost in Alvin.

campground.name: Grizzly Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: Two free campsites perched on scenic rock ledges beside Koch Creek, with natural swimming pools below; reached by roughly 22 km of forest service road from Highway 6, making it a rewarding but remote hideaway for self-sufficient tourers.

campground.name: Nine Bay Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A quiet 3-site forested rec site on a scenic, remote lake in the Kootenays, reached via 20 km of active logging road requiring a CB radio; boats must be portaged 200 m to the water and anglers are the main draw.

campground.name: Meadow Mountain Cabin Recreation Site
campground.desc: A remote Kootenays cabin run by the Nelson Sno-Goers explicitly for winter snowmobiling, sharing terrain with Selkirk Snowcat Skiing Dec–Apr; reached via ~29 km of steep, rough forest service road requiring high-clearance 4WD — not a realistic stop for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Blackwater Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Two tent pads on a forested point jutting into Blackwater Lake, reached by a 100m walk-in trail off a gravel forest service road; the setting offers great lake views and a small canoe launch, but the approach involves active logging traffic.

campground.name: Blue Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 2-site rec site on Blue Lake deep in the Elk Valley, reached via a long stretch of the Elk River FSR; the lake is calm and boat-motor-free, but the site was heavily burned in 2023 and the forested setting is significantly diminished. Free and remote, with no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Hart Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A rustic, open, grassy site alongside the West Yahk River, sitting at the end of 25.5 km of active gravel logging road (Hawkins Main) off Highway 3. Road is relatively level but rough in spots with logging truck traffic — ride with lights on.

campground.name: Okanagan Falls Trails Recreation Site Campground
campground.desc: A basic rec site east of Okanagan Falls that serves primarily as a staging area for the adjacent OHV trail network, with campsites, picnic tables, and outhouses; Allendale Lake Road into the site is described as rough condition, making for an unpleasant loaded-bike approach.

campground.name: French Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A compact 4–5 site free rec site perched at the confluence of French Creek and Dease River, right alongside Cassiar Highway 37 — a convenient roadside fishing stop in remote northern BC; no drinking water mentioned.

campground.name: Crump Siding (BC Recreation Site)
campground.desc: A flat bench-top BC rec site just off Princeton-Summerland Road, overlooking the historic Kettle Valley Railway corridor with 11 open sites and a short 2.7 km gravel approach — bring all your own water as there is none on-site.

campground.name: O.B. Campground
campground.desc: A O.B. Campground in Blaeberry.

campground.name: White Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A bare-bones 2-unit lakeside rec site reached via a long active logging road; the lake itself requires a steep foot trail and the site has minimal facilities.

campground.name: Owl Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: An open dry-forest site on a former homestead where Owl Creek meets the Birkenhead River, with a remnant apple orchard and good fishing; outhouses only, self-register fees, and active bear presence.

campground.name: Lakit Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Two-site free rec site on a shallow man-made lake east of Cranbrook, notable for the old corduroy road visible on the lake bottom; access requires 4 km of rough but 2WD-passable gravel and no amenities are confirmed on site.

campground.name: Carter Lake Campsite
campground.desc: A Carter Lake Campsite in Gold River.

campground.name: Secrest Hill Agricultural Worker’s Campsite
campground.desc: A Secrest Hill Agricultural Worker’s Campsite in Eagle Bluff.

campground.name: Skwellepil Creek Wilderness Site
campground.desc: A no-service wilderness site on the west side of Chehalis Lake, 30 km up the Chehalis FSR from Harrison Mills; pack-in/pack-out only, first-come/first-served, and access is effectively barred to loaded bikes by three large waterbars cut into the entry road since 2022.

campground.name: Appleton Creek Campsite
campground.desc: A hike-in creekside camp in a stand of large old-growth Douglas Fir on the Sunshine Coast Trail, reached by a 10-minute walk from a trailhead that itself requires a deactivated road and a high-clearance 4x4 to access; no confirmed facilities.

campground.name: Williamson Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A two-site backcountry lake in the Okanagan highlands where powerboats are banned, reached by 10 km of rough logging road plus a final 300 m stretch the directions advise walking; no confirmed amenities and free.

campground.name: Ireland Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-site overnight stop on the Powell Forest Canoe Route, positioned for a morning portage to Dodd Lake; canoe access only — completely unreachable by bike.

campground.name: Wolverine Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny free two-site rec site on the eastern shore of Wolverine Lake, reached via 8 km of the Kangaroo FSR from Likely; you'll either have it entirely to yourself or find it full, with a rough boat launch and good fishing but minimal facilities.

campground.name: Rossmoore Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, quiet fishing lake south of Kamloops drawing fly fishers and trollers to its 4 first-come sites; the access road turns rough and narrows after the second pipeline crossing, with 4x4 possibly required.

campground.name: Lois Point Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, quiet rec site on the south shore of Lois Lake, serving the Sunshine Coast Trail and Powell Forest Canoe Route — reached only by a 2 km paddle or hike from the Lois Lake launch, with no road access for touring cyclists.

campground.name: Herman Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small forested rec site on a quiet lake south of Blind Bay, with a 50-metre boardwalk over marsh to the water's edge and looping trails for waterfowl viewing; reached via 8.3 km of forest service road off Hwy 1.

campground.name: Suscha Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free 5-site rec site on an open lakeside point in the remote Cariboo interior, reached by roughly 135 km of forest service roads from Vanderhoof; no confirmed water or facilities on site.

campground.name: Harmon Lake East Recreation Site
campground.desc: A popular, well-appointed family campground on Harmon Lake in the Kane Valley, with gravelled pads, a floating dock, boat launch, and access to 50+ km of cross-country ski and hiking trails; the 9 km gravel approach off Hwy 5A is highway-maintained but loaded-bike rough, and it's cash only.

campground.name: Spirea
campground.desc: A Spirea in McLeod Lake.

campground.name: Miner Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, free 3-site roadside camp on the southwest shore of Miner Lake in the Chilcotin, reached via roughly 16 km of forest service road; draws anglers and serves as a jumping-off point for alpine terrain at Perkins Peak about 14 km away.

campground.name: Grassy Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A remote single-site rec site on a small, marshy lake at the end of roughly 21 km of forest service road; shore fishing is the main draw, and the marsh edge keeps the swimming nil.

campground.name: Tahla Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small, sunny 5-site lakeside rec site popular for fishing, kayaking, and ATV/trail riding, with a short boardwalk leading to lake views; both approach routes require several kilometres of gravel road.

campground.name: Wedgemount Lake Campground
campground.desc: A Wedgemount Lake Campground in Whistler.

campground.name: Trail RV Park
campground.desc: A Trail RV Park in Waneta Junction.

campground.name: Mt. Patrick Recreation Site
campground.desc: A winter-only backcountry hut-and-yurt in the Kootenay mountains, open November to April via reservation and access code; the approach runs 7.5 km on Dewar Creek FSR then 1–2 km of rough spur — no tent camping, effectively inaccessible to a loaded touring bike in winter.

campground.name: Lundbom Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A large, popular 102-site recreation site on Lundbom Lake southeast of Merritt, suited to fishing, horse camping (corrals on-site), and mountain biking. Cash only; no amenities confirmed, so come self-sufficient.

campground.name: Moose Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-site forest rec site on Moose Lake in BC's Cariboo interior, with a small boat launch and pit toilet; the long approach via FSR includes a Francois Lake ferry crossing and a narrow, winding, brushy final road that the site itself flags as requiring high clearance or 4x4.

campground.name: Graffunder Lakes North Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-unit BC rec site on Graffunder Lakes, drawing anglers and boaters willing to follow roughly 20 km of forest service road from the Vavenby area; no amenities are confirmed on site.

campground.name: Norton Lake
campground.desc: A Norton Lake in North Vancouver.

campground.name: Bear Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A large motorized recreation site built around 350 km of ATV and motorcycle trails in the Okanagan highlands, partially closed following the 2023 McDougal Creek wildfire; camping at designated trailhead areas with a separate trail fee on top of the nightly rate.

campground.name: Blueberry Horse Camp
campground.desc: A Blueberry Horse Camp in Dunster.

campground.name: Dease Lake Informal Camping
campground.desc: A Dease Lake Informal Camping in Dease Lake.

campground.name: Indata
campground.desc: A Indata in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: Beaver North Recreation Site
campground.desc: A paddle-in overnight stop at the start of the portage between Beaver Lake and Dodd Lake, accessed by paddling north across the lake; with only one site and no confirmed amenities, it is essentially inaccessible to loaded touring cyclists.

campground.name: Hozomeen
campground.desc: A Hozomeen in Manning Park.

campground.name: Copper Kettle Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A remote 20-hectare hike-in lake in the Okanagan backcountry, reached via a 3 km trail from the Kettle River FSR trailhead; the rustic shoreside tent site suits fly-fishing anglers, but loaded bikes must be left at the parking area.

campground.name: Esplanade Bay
campground.desc: A free BC forest rec site on a forested bench overlooking Kinbasket Lake, reached by driving 40 km on the Bush River Forest Road and then 2.5 km further west; no confirmed facilities or water, so arrive fully self-sufficient.

campground.name: Ispah Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A compact, single-group site nestled at the edge of Ispah Lake, reached by a long forest service road south of Prince George; a fire ring, picnic table, and pit toilet are on site, and the lake yields wild rainbow trout with no motorized boats allowed.

campground.name: Clements Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A quiet 5-site rec site on a motor-restricted lake north of Stewart, with a sandy beach for swimming and canoeing; access requires a short gravel spur off Highway 37A and the site operates May to October only.

campground.name: Aloha R.V. Manufacture Homes and Camp Grounds
campground.desc: A Aloha R.V. Manufacture Homes and Camp Grounds in Bradner.

campground.name: Anutz Lake Recreation Campsite
campground.desc: A south-facing lake beach with warm swimming, fishing, and a boat launch (14 ft max) keeps visitors returning; the supervised, cash-only site charges $20. Reaching it requires roughly 18 km of gravel road past Youbou, a meaningful push on a loaded bike.

campground.name: Queest Mountain South Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny, free single-site rec site at a forestry lookout on Queest Mountain near Malakwa; the access road is explicitly described as very rough, making it a demanding approach for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: White Spruce
campground.desc: A White Spruce in McLeod Lake.

campground.name: Red Sand Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free two-area lake campground in Red Sand Lake Demonstration Forest near Terrace, with tables, pit toilets, a picnic shelter, and three short easy trails; the 26 km West Kalum forestry road access floods repeatedly in spring and heavy rain, sometimes stranding campers for weeks.

campground.name: Lizzie Bay Campsite
campground.desc: A rustic, heavily treed rec site with every campsite directly on the jade-colored shore of Lillooet Lake, reached by 13 km of active industrial forest service road from Pemberton; self-register and pay on arrival.

campground.name: Little Fort Campground
campground.desc: A Little Fort Campground in Bridge Lake.

campground.name: Squamish-Elaho Recreation Site
campground.location: Remote & backcountry, Vancouver, Coast and Mountains
campground.community: Remote & backcountry, Vancouver, Coast and Mountains
campground.desc: A Squamish-Elaho Recreation Site in Remote & backcountry, Vancouver, Coast and Mountains.

campground.name: Chek Canyon Recreation Site
campground.desc: A well-known sport-climbing rec site off a steep, signed forest service road 15 minutes north of Squamish, offering roughly 100 routes for all skill levels; most campsites are walk-in and AWD is recommended for the approach.

campground.name: Murray Creek Rec Site
campground.desc: Small, semi-open forest rec site northwest of Spences Bridge, reached via roughly 20 km of narrow, switchbacking Murray Creek FSR — free and managed by a local dirt-riding club, but the long FSR haul makes it a poor fit for loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Free camping area along Coldwater River
campground.desc: A Free camping area along Coldwater River in Kingsvale.

campground.name: Border RV Park
campground.desc: A Border RV Park in Tsawwassen.

campground.name: Kane Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A spacious, family-friendly rec site in the Kane Valley roughly 30 km south of Merritt, offering big valley views and a trail network that includes 50+ km of cross-country ski trails and a forest interpretive loop; the 9 km Kane Valley Road approach is unpaved and the site is cash only.

campground.name: Sock Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny, free, forested rec site on a quiet interior lake suited to canoes and small boats, reached via roughly 18 km of forest-service road from Clearwater; only one campsite and no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Buck Lake Rec Site
campground.desc: Free rec site on Buck Lake's northern shore, reached via 7.5 km of active logging road off Hwy 97C; a popular, sometimes crowded stop for anglers and hunters.

campground.name: Hart Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A rustic, open grassy camp on the West Yahk River, reached after 25.5 km of active logging road (Hawkins Main) from Highway 3 near Yahk — free and scenic, but heavy-truck traffic and rough stretches make the approach a real commitment on a loaded bike.

campground.name: Spruce Bay Recreation Site
campground.desc: A sunny, open rec site on Victoria Lake near Port Alice with all five pitches directly on the water; reached via logging roads off Highway 30, and note the Old Growth Trail is currently closed.

campground.name: Bernard Beaches Recreation Site
campground.desc: A popular lakeside rec site on Kootenay Lake's east shore offering vehicle campsites and tent sites directly on the water, accessed by 12 km of 2WD forest service road from Riondel; first-come, first-served with no reservation system.

campground.name: Dundas Islet SE
campground.desc: A Dundas Islet SE in Metlakatla.

campground.name: Old Hedley Road East Recreation Site
campground.desc: Riverside rec site on the Similkameen River accessed via a short spur off Highway 3, with swimming and kayaking as the main draws; cash only and no amenities confirmed.

campground.name: Meuoon Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Tiny free rec site on a small interior lake deep in the Holy Cross-Binta Forest Road corridor, reachable only after roughly 62 km of forest service road from Hwy 16; no confirmed amenities and very remote.

campground.name: Minnes Dock
campground.desc: A Minnes Dock in Malibu.

campground.name: Noyse Lake Campsite
campground.desc: Noyse Lake Campsite is one of five tent platforms along the semi-alpine Kludahk Trail on San Juan Ridge, reached via active forest service roads subject to temporary gate closures; a remote, trail-side stop with no confirmed amenities and snow on the ridge from roughly November through May.

campground.name: Big Sheep Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-vehicle creek-side rec site tucked in the Rossland Range's Big Sheep Creek valley, accessed by 9 km of gravel FSR after a scenic climb over Record Ridge; the site is minimal but a good fishing hole is right beside the picnic table.

campground.name: Blue Lake North Campground
campground.desc: A small walk-in tent-only site tucked in a mature Douglas-fir stand right beside Blue Lake in the Cariboo; a short trail leads to the lakeshore, but cyclists must park at the road and carry gear 335m to reach the site.

campground.name: Dease Lake Lions Tanzilla River Campground
campground.desc: A Dease Lake Lions Tanzilla River Campground in Dease Lake.

campground.name: Murray Lake North Recreation Site
campground.desc: Free, open and sunny rec site on a small picturesque interior lake with a good boat launch, reached via the Juliet Creek FSR off the Coquihalla Highway; no confirmed water or amenities on site.

campground.name: Borrow Pit 1
campground.desc: A Borrow Pit 1 in Prophet River.

campground.name: Cerulean Lake
campground.desc: A Cerulean Lake in Pemberton Meadows.

campground.name: Upper Elk River Recreation Site
campground.desc: A remote 4-site recreation site deep in the upper Elk River valley, offering open views of alpine meadows and avalanche chutes in a partially treed riverside setting. The 163.5 km forest service road approach from Elkford is a major commitment for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Eaton Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, user-maintained 3-site rec site in the Skagit River Valley serving as a trailhead staging point for Eaton Lake; no confirmed water or facilities, accessed via gravel FSR.

campground.name: Jeb Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Four-site rec site on the north end of Jeb Lake with an improved boat launch; Spokin Lake Road is gravel and 4x4 is recommended for launching, making this a functional fishing and paddling base rather than a scenic layover.

campground.name: Gilnockie Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: Bare-bones 3-site rec site in an open meadow deep in the Kootenays, reached after roughly 43 km on the Waldo-Gold Forest Service Road; the historic cabin burned in 2017 and no facilities are confirmed.

campground.name: Km 64 Alexander Mackenzie Heritage Trail Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny two-site roadside pullout serving as trailhead for the historic Alexander Mackenzie/Nuhaulk Carrier Grease Trail, set in forest burnt over in 2010; no confirmed water or facilities, and reached via roughly 99 km of rural gravel road from Quesnel.

campground.name: Susan Lake
campground.desc: Small free rec site perched above Susan Lake with a dock and car-top boat launch; access is roughly 23 km of steep, rough forest service road with 4x4 recommended, making it a tough haul on a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Murray Lake South Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, free three-site rec site tucked in trees beside a picturesque mid-to-high elevation lake, with a boat launch and a fishing-and-hunting crowd; access is via a gravel FSR that can be wet and rough.

campground.name: Lost Horse Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small 4-site fishing-focused rec site on Lost Horse Lake, reached via Forest Service roads off Highway 24; free and first-come-first-served with no mention of drinking water or flush facilities.

campground.name: Cedar Spirit Grove
campground.desc: A Cedar Spirit Grove in Alvin.

campground.name: Mary Lake Campsite
campground.desc: A Mary Lake Campsite in Bloedel.

campground.name: Mosquito Lake Campsite
campground.desc: A free 11-site rec site on the shoreline of Mosquito Lake on Moresby Island, with a day-use shelter and boat launch; access is via the Moresby Mainline, an active forest service road typical of Haida Gwaii backcountry.

campground.name: Wilson Lake East
campground.desc: A spacious open flat at the east end of a deep, narrow 4.5 km Kootenay lake, with campsites around a clearing suited for groups and good trout fishing in the lake and Fitzstubbs Creek; reached via 33–34 km of gravel FSR from Rosebery or a steep rough climb from Nakusp.

campground.name: Emma Lake Forest Service Recreation Site
campground.desc: A fee-for-service fishing lake doubling as a water supply reservoir, with abundant small rainbow trout and a resident site operator; access requires roughly 24 km of mixed pavement (often poor condition) and maintained gravel forest service road.

campground.name: Summit Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single remote campsite on a small Kootenays lake, set just past a beaver pond deep in the forest service road network; the rough access road crosses a waterway with no turnarounds, and the recommended approach is to park at the creek and walk the last stretch to the lake.

campground.name: Kate Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny, treed walk-in site at Kate Lake reached by a 2.5 km trail that begins 4.5 km along a very rough 4WD track off a long forest service road — genuinely remote, no confirmed facilities, and signed grizzly bear habitat. Essentially inaccessible to a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Sugar Lake 1 Mile Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small 2-site gated recreation site on Sugar Lake with beach and fishing access; entry requires stopping at the Sugar Lake 2 Mile operator first, and the site fills fast given its popularity.

campground.name: Holmes Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-site, free BC rec site sitting on the forest access road to Holmes Lake southeast of Keefer Lake near Cherryville; no confirmed amenities and likely rustic.

campground.name: Cariboo Island South Recreation Site
campground.desc: Two level beach campsites on the south tip of Cariboo Island in Quesnel Lake, reachable only by canoe or kayak; the lake can develop severe storms quickly, making this a paddler's destination rather than a cycling stop.

campground.name: Sutter Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, open 3-site rec site on rushing Sutter Creek in the Tulameen backcountry, 34.6 km up a forest service road that carries active industrial traffic — expect dust, road noise, and a creek-side slope hazard at one site.

campground.name: South Foley Lake
campground.desc: A South Foley Lake in Chilliwack.

campground.name: Buccaner Bay Provincial Park
campground.desc: A Buccaner Bay Provincial Park in Buccaneer Bay.

campground.name: Cal Cheak North Camp
campground.desc: A large, heavily shaded campground tucked between Callaghan Creek and Cheakamus River just off Hwy 99 south of Whistler, with 63 sites across four areas and a short forest-service road approach; bears are frequently sighted so strict food storage is essential.

campground.name: Bittern Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny two-site rec site on a tranquil lake in the Kootenays, offering a peaceful free overnight; the 15 km approach runs on an active logging road where CB radio is recommended, making the ride in genuinely hazardous.

campground.name: Chek Canyon Camping Area
campground.desc: A dedicated climbing basecamp known locally as 'Chek,' with roughly 100 routes ranging from beginner to expert set into the canyon walls above Squamish. Access requires a steep forest service road where AWD is recommended; sites are walk-in with outhouses and bear caches but no potable water — pack everything in and out.

campground.name: Ruth Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single walk-in site on a small fishing lake, reached by short trail from Flyfish Lakes #2 — no facilities confirmed, and loaded-bike riders will need to leave gear at the trailhead.

campground.name: Middle Point Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 2-site creekside rec site positioned mid-portage on the Nanton-to-Dodd Lake canoe route; reached on foot along the portage trail, making it effectively inaccessible to loaded touring cyclists.

campground.name: Government Point
campground.desc: A free, roadside rec site on the north shore of Francois Lake offering a boat launch and fishing access; the approach road is paved for most of the way with only a short gravel finish, making it straightforward for loaded bikes.

campground.name: Snohoosh Lake North Recreation Site
campground.desc: A very rustic 2-site recreation site on the north shore of Snohoosh Lake with a cartop boat launch; reached via 43 km of Deadman Vidette Lake Road off Highway 1, making this a real gravel commitment for a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Proud Outlook
campground.desc: A Proud Outlook in Squamish.

campground.name: Pickard Creek Campground
campground.desc: A rec site wedged between Highway 3 and the Similkameen River, popular for swimming, canoeing, and kayaking in the river; cash only with seasonal fee dates that can shift.

campground.name: Stewart Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A quiet lakeside rec site on Rainbow Trout–stocked Stewart Lake in Northern BC, with 12 camp pads, a gravel boat launch, and a fishing dock; reaching it requires roughly 32 km of gravel road beyond the highway.

campground.name: Tatlayoko Lake Northeast Recreation Site
campground.desc: A scenic free rec site in mature Douglas-fir forest on the northeast shore of turquoise Tatlayoko Lake, with striking views of Niut Mountain and a small boat launch; the 35.5 km gravel road from Hwy 20 is a real commitment, and the lake is prone to strong winds.

campground.name: Sawmill Point Campground
campground.desc: Upgraded forested rec site on the eastern shore of Dease Lake, with a stream along the north edge and recent improvements; the steep spur off Hwy 37 will have most loaded riders walking.

campground.name: Pine Point
campground.desc: A Pine Point in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: Lake Of The Trees Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small 3-site free rec site on the eastern shore of Lake of The Trees, oriented westward for evening sunsets; accessed via forest service road off 100 Mile House and suitable for cartop boats and kayaks.

campground.name: Mr. Canoehead Recreation Site
campground.desc: A boat-access-only portage site between Amor Lake and Surprise Lake on the Sayward Forest Canoe Route, with sweeping lake views and genuine solitude; completely unreachable by loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Gibson’s RV Resort
campground.desc: An RV resort on Vancouver Island or the Gulf Islands; no usable web content could be retrieved, so site character, amenities, and setting are unknown.

campground.name: Surprise Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, free recreation site overlooking the southwest end of Surprise Lake, reached by a gravel road roughly 20 km east of Atlin; basic and remote with no confirmed services, but a genuine northern wilderness lake setting.

campground.name: Kootenay-White Junction Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 2-site peninsula camp at the confluence of the Kootenay and White Rivers, reached by forest service roads off the Kootenay River FSR; scenic and secluded but no developed amenities and expect rough gravel access.

campground.name: Evely Campground
campground.desc: Free, no-reservation rec site sitting directly on Okanagan Lake with a swimming beach, small boat launch, and short trails; there is no potable water on-site, so riders must carry their own.

campground.name: Keyhole Hot Springs Camp Site
campground.desc: A Keyhole Hot Springs Camp Site in Pemberton Meadows.

campground.name: Crater Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site walk-in lakeshore camp on Crater Lake, reached via rough forest roads from Nazko and a short steep trail; the remote setting is rewarding but the hike-in rules out most loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Sowaqua Road Camp
campground.desc: A Sowaqua Road Camp in Sunshine Valley.

campground.name: Elbow Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-site forested rec site beside a shallow lake in the Okanagan highlands, reached by a long forest service road that is slow and rough; no boat launch and no listed amenities.

campground.name: Mineral Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny two-site lakeside rec site with warm water for swimming, reached by a short forest service road spur off the highway south of Cranbrook; no confirmed facilities on site.

campground.name: Robinson Pass Low Tide
campground.desc: A Robinson Pass Low Tide in Remote & backcountry, Vancouver Island.

campground.name: Frozen Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, secluded free rec site deep in the Flathead Valley near the Canada-USA border, reached via 95+ km of forest service roads; offers a quiet canoe and car-top boat launch with no confirmed facilities.

campground.name: Sun Valley Trout Park
campground.desc: A private campground on Highway 7 in Mission catering exclusively to touring cyclists, with accreditation from multiple bike associations; family camping is not available, and the former u-catch fish farm closed in 2024.

campground.name: Mcclure Pit
campground.desc: A free, recently upgraded 7-site rec site on the north shore of Francois Lake, with spacious sites, a gravel boat launch, and easy paved access off Colleymount Road — well suited to a loaded touring bike. The main draws are the lake views and fishing; no drinking water is mentioned.

campground.name: Zorro Bay Marine Site
campground.desc: A kayak-in marine campsite on a pebble-rock beach near Porteau Cove, with 9 tent platforms, picnic tables, a fire ring, compost toilet, and bear cache along the Sea to Sky Marine Trail; reachable only by kayak or small watercraft, and bordering private land with strict boundary rules.

campground.name: Salisbury Lake
campground.desc: A Salisbury Lake in Miracle Valley.

campground.name: Pimainus Lake East Recreation Site
campground.desc: A sparse lakeside rec site on a chain of four lakes, heavily logged for pine beetle control and now largely shadeless; reached via 36+ km of active industrial forest service road with narrow corners and a steep rough final descent to the water.

campground.name: Wolverine Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small terraced lakeshore rec site with a natural boat launch, good paddling, and fishing on Wolverine Lake — accessed via roughly 160 km of forest service roads from Mackenzie, so arrive fully self-sufficient.

campground.name: Leon Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A bare-bones, single-vehicle rec site tucked directly beside Leon Creek, reached by driving 52.5 km along the West Pavilion Forest Service Road then 8 km down Leon Creek Road — primarily a hunters' camp with no listed amenities.

campground.name: Horse Camp
campground.desc: A Horse Camp in Summit Lake.

campground.name: Shambhalodging
campground.desc: A Shambhalodging in Jersey.

campground.name: Porcher East
campground.desc: A Porcher East in Oona River.

campground.name: Island Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Free 8-site rec site beside Island Lake with an easy boat launch, popular with anglers and hunters; access is mostly paved with only a short 400 m unpaved spur to camp.

campground.name: Bald Mountain Recreation Site
campground.desc: A secluded tenting site on the south arm of Cowichan Lake, reachable only by boat launched from the North Shore Road weir — about 8 km by water along the north shore. No confirmed amenities; carry everything in.

campground.name: Little Wilson Lake
campground.desc: A small, open grassy campsite tucked at the base of 2350m Mount Ferrie on a quiet mountain lake suited to fishing and small boats; reached via 31km of gravel FSR plus a rough 800m dirt spur.

campground.name: Tanli Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A former silvicultural camp on a small lake in the Cariboo, open to the public only when not in use by reforestation crews — a free but uncertain stop with no confirmed amenities on a forest service road.

campground.name: Loon Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A single-site rec site on a small, quiet fishing lake deep in the forest, reached only by an unmaintained 4WD-only track; fly-fishing for trout and char under strict catch regulations is the sole draw.

campground.name: Bob's Lake Recreation Site North Campground
campground.desc: A free 7-site alpine lake camp on Texada Island — reached by ferry then a gravel road climb — with shaded north-shore sites and sunnier south-shore sites sharing one outhouse.

campground.name: Lawrence Lake West Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny, free, treed rec site at the west end of Lawrence Lake, reached via roughly 43 km of forest roads capped by an active log-hauling road that warrants real caution for loaded touring bikes.

campground.name: Gosling Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free 6-site lakeside rec site on the Sayward Forest Canoe Route, reached via 10.8 km of gravel road followed by two forest service roads; no confirmed amenities or potable water.

campground.name: Germansen East Campground
campground.desc: A Germansen East Campground in Germansen Landing.

campground.name: Snow Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 30-site recreation site on the southeast shore of Sproat Lake with a sandy beach, small-boat launch, and water sports; reached by roughly 10 km of Forest Service Road off Highway 4. Cash only with on-site supervision; reservations available.

campground.name: Lizzie Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A Lizzie Lake Recreation Site in Skookumchuck.

campground.name: Bruer Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, single-site roadside stop deep on the Kettle River FSR, popular with hunters and anglers; the 14.5 km of active logging road means noise from trucks and a washboard approach.

campground.name: Big Island
campground.desc: A Big Island in Takla Landing.

campground.name: Gambier Lake Overflow Site
campground.desc: A Gambier Lake Overflow Site in Ekins Point.

campground.name: Kappan Lake East Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free lakeshore rec site on Kappan Lake's eastern shore with views of Kappan Mountain, popular for fishing and boating; the final 1.7 km access road is rough and narrow with 4WD recommended.

campground.name: Chipmunk Peninsula on Dodd Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small 3-site recreation site on the southeast shore of Dodd Lake, reachable only by portaging from Beaver Lake or paddling across from the main Dodd Lake campsite — no road access, no confirmed facilities or water.

campground.name: North Dodd Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 2-site portage camp between Dodd and Windsor Lake, reached only by paddling to the north end of Dodd Lake; free and remote with no confirmed facilities, making it a non-starter for loaded touring cyclists.

campground.name: Cockburn Roberts Homesite
campground.desc: A Cockburn Roberts Homesite in Billings Bay.

campground.name: Botanie Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, remote mountain lake camp reached by 17 km of uphill, narrow paved-and-gravel road from Lytton; the site has 3 tables and an enclosed winter shelter (day use for snowmobilers only, no overnight stays inside), with no water or washroom facilities confirmed.

campground.name: Trout Camp Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, isolated rec site for 1–2 groups on the southwest shore of Trout Lake, cradled by a steep valley and towering mountains; reached by a short spur off West Trout Road FSR with an outhouse but no confirmed drinking water.

campground.name: Gambier Lake
campground.desc: A Gambier Lake in Ekins Point.

campground.name: Barnes Lake Recreation Site - South End
campground.desc: A popular rainbow trout lake 11 km from Ashcroft with free camping split across three areas; the south/west cluster has 5 quieter sites, though the steep switchback climb on Hwy 97C out of Ashcroft and an unsigned gravel turnoff add effort for loaded riders.

campground.name: Big Country Campground & RV Park
campground.desc: A Big Country Campground & RV Park in 114 Mile House.

campground.name: Boss Lake - BC Recreation Site
campground.desc: A four-area lakeside recreation site in the Voght Valley south of Merritt, popular for fishing and boating, with a boat launch and two docks; both access routes finish on gravel roads, and the site is cash only.

campground.name: East Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A scenic lakeshore rec site on the south shore of East Lake, reached by parking off the Duck Lake Forest Service Road and hiking in along the Lang Creek Trail; primarily a day-use area with just one overnight spot and no confirmed facilities.

campground.name: Old tent site
campground.desc: Five tent platforms scattered along the 40 km semi-alpine Kludahk Trail on southern Vancouver Island, accessed via active logging roads prone to gate closures; the ridge sits under snow from roughly November to May, and the hike-in approach makes this a backcountry commitment, not a roadside stop.

campground.name: Camp Ground
campground.desc: A Camp Ground in Kingsvale.

campground.name: Wright Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site free camp on a reportedly scenic Northern BC fishing lake, reachable only after 5 km of ATV trail or hiking beyond an already rough, unmaintained forest service road — winching may be required in wet conditions, and the final FSR has an active closure at km 41.

campground.name: Chuchi Lake Point
campground.desc: Remote free campsite on the east shore of Chuchi Lake in northern BC, serving mainly as a boat-launch staging area with no confirmed amenities; reached after roughly 100 km of gravel road from Fort St. James.

campground.name: Lily Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, free 3-site recreation site on Lily Lake southwest of Merritt, suited for lakeside fishing, canoeing, and nature watching; the final few kilometres of access road are very rough and demand high-clearance vehicles, making the approach an unpleasant slog for a loaded tourer.

campground.name: Moore Bay (BCMT)
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site sheltered cove on Kingcome Inlet with a small dock and boat ramp — reachable by boat only, making it a non-starter for any touring cyclist without water transport.

campground.name: Gillis Lake West Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, shady free rec site sitting directly on Gillis Lake's north shore with a boat launch, popular with anglers and hunters; the 6.3 km Murray Lake Forest Service Road approach and a very sharp campsite entrance will slow a loaded tourer.

campground.name: Cultus Lake Thousand Trails RV Resort
campground.desc: A Cultus Lake Thousand Trails RV Resort in Lindell Beach.

campground.name: Fido Camp
campground.desc: A Fido Camp in Manning Park.

campground.name: Paul Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, user-maintained forest camp on a secluded lake near Babine Lake, offering a dock and rainbow and cutthroat trout fishing with no crowds; reached via several kilometres of forest service road.

campground.name: Ladies Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: The sole campsite on Cariboo Lake, this 6-site rec site perches above the eastern shore and makes a base for exploring the Cariboo Goldrush country and Ghost Lake; access is 12 km of forest service road with no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Gypsum Lake West Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, sunny lake-side rec site southeast of Chataway Lake, serving as the trailhead for the 2 km Gypsum Mountain Hiking Trail with views north to Logan Lake; expect roughly 11 km of forest service road after the pavement ends.

campground.name: Moresby Camp Recreation Site
campground.desc: A remote 6-site rec site at the head of Cumshewa Inlet on Moresby Island, equipped with a boat launch, dock, and shelter — the practical departure point for kayakers and boaters heading into Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve; reached by ~25 km of logging road with no confirmed water or washrooms.

campground.name: Cascade Beach Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site walk-in rec site on the Mabel Lake Forest Service Road, with excellent lakeside beaches and trail access; cyclists ride a forest service road to the 14 km marker then walk gear down to camp.

campground.name: Noreen Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A one-site timbered rec site on small Noreen Lake, reached by a lengthy rough forest road that the site description explicitly requires 4WD to drive — a practical skip for any loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Pascal's Camping
campground.desc: A Pascal's Camping in Lund.

campground.name: Blackeye's Plateau Camp
campground.desc: A Blackeye's Plateau Camp in Tulameen.

campground.name: Chakima Horse Camp
campground.desc: A Chakima Horse Camp in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: Buchanan Lookout Recreation Site
campground.desc: Refurbished fire lookout at high elevation above the Kootenays with sweeping panoramic views and seasonal wildflowers; reached by 11.9 km of 2WD forest service road, and listed as day-use only with no confirmed overnight amenities.

campground.name: Sundorn Estates
campground.desc: A Sundorn Estates in Chilliwack.

campground.name: Susan Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small open recreation site perched above Susan Lake with a dock and cartop boat launch; 23 km of steep, rough forest service road with 4x4 recommended makes this a likely skip for loaded bike tourers.

campground.name: Leiner River Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small riverside rec site just outside Tahsis on Vancouver Island, with easy river access, swimming holes, and a sandy beach; reached via the long Head Bay Road from Gold River.

campground.name: Encampment
campground.desc: A Encampment in North Vancouver.

campground.name: Zum Peak Campground
campground.desc: A tiny 2-site rec site on the Coquihalla plateau, popular for berry picking and as the trailhead for the Little Douglas Lake trail; expect 7 km of gravel on Upper Coldwater Road and a snowbound closure well into June.

campground.name: Random
campground.desc: A Random in Cedarside.

campground.name: Lavoie Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small 5-site recreation site on the eastern shore of Lavoie Lake, a popular fishing lake deep in the Cariboo; reaching it demands roughly 75 km of forest service road (Kluskus FSR then Gold Road), making it a deliberate destination rather than a casual overnight.

campground.name: Horseshoe Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny walk-in wilderness camp at the end of the portage between Lois Lake and Dodd Lake, crossing the Stillwater Main logging road at 10 km; suited to canoe-tourers on a multi-lake route, not accessible to loaded bikes.

campground.name: Dugan Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Free two-section rec site on Dugan Lake, just 8 km off Hwy 97: the first half has large level gravel pads for bigger rigs, while the quieter second half tucks tent-sized spots into a treed strip along the lakeshore. No confirmed water or washrooms.

campground.name: Seal Cove Dispersed Site
campground.desc: A Seal Cove Dispersed Site in Squamish.

campground.name: Ruckell Point Scout Camp
campground.desc: A Ruckell Point Scout Camp in St. Ives.

campground.name: Levette Lake
campground.desc: A forested lake with mountain views north of Squamish, popular for swimming on hot summer days, but the access road is 4x4-only and very rough — a practical skip for loaded touring cyclists. High bear activity demands strict food storage discipline at all times.

campground.name: Tamihi Meadows
campground.desc: A private farm RV park on the Chilliwack River at the base of Mount Church, with a sandy beach, world-class fishing, and a quiet wilderness feel; tent campers must supply their own portable toilet as campground facilities have been closed, making this a very poor fit for most cycle tourists.

campground.name: Mccall Flats Recreation Site
campground.desc: Sandy riverside beach camp in the Bella Coola valley with good salmon angling, but bear activity is serious enough that the site explicitly advises against tents and soft-sided units — a significant problem for cycle tourers.

campground.name: St. Marie Lake East Recreation Site
campground.desc: Open natural camping with tables, fire rings, and a pit toilet set 300 m off the Willow-Cale FSR, giving direct access to the eastern shore of St. Marie Lake; proximity to Prince George means heavy weekend use throughout the snow-free season.

campground.name: Lawrence Lake East Recreation Site
campground.desc: A compact 2-unit rec site on the east shore of Lawrence Lake with a gravel boat launch; reaching it means ~43 km on Forest Service roads, the last stretch on an active log-hauling road.

campground.name: Brookvale Holiday Resort
campground.desc: A Brookvale Holiday Resort in East Osoyoos.

campground.name: Walton's Lakefront Resort
campground.desc: A Walton's Lakefront Resort in East Osoyoos.

campground.name: Coldscaur Lake South Recreation Site
campground.desc: Free lakeside rec site at the south end of Coldscaur Lake, reached by 27 km of active log-hauling road northwest of Clearwater; quiet once you arrive, but logging truck traffic demands real caution on the approach.

campground.name: Third Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, 4-site lakeside rec site on the northwest shore of Third Lake, popular with anglers and hunters; reached via 41-plus kilometres of forest service road from Merritt with numerous unsigned junctions.

campground.name: Echo Lake
campground.desc: A Echo Lake in Squamish.

campground.name: Pasayten River Trail Campsite
campground.desc: A Pasayten River Trail Campsite in Manning Park.

campground.name: Applebee Dome Campground
campground.desc: A Applebee Dome Campground in Spillimacheen.

campground.name: Crystal Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 13-site rec site on the northern shore of Crystal Lake, popular with anglers; a boat launch and fishing dock are on-site, reached via a short RV-accessible gravel spur off Highway 24 with a modest nightly fee.

campground.name: Nickel Plate Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Secluded 4-site rec site on a glaciated alpine lake near Apex Mountain Resort, with fishing, hiking, and nearby Nordic skiing; the final 0.7 km of access road is 4x4-only and very rough.

campground.name: Cariboo Island North Recreation Site
campground.desc: Two beach campsites on the northern tip of Cariboo Island, sitting mid-lake on Quesnel Lake with expansive Cariboo Mountain views — spectacular setting, but reachable by boat only from launches at Abbott Creek, Horsefly Bay, or Likely, with shallow waters near the island and sudden violent windstorms adding real hazard.

campground.name: Big Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A remote Chilcotin plateau lake set among rolling forested hills with sweeping views of Mt. Tatlow and the Coast Mountains; reached by roughly 76 km of forest service road and popular for rainbow trout fishing, with no confirmed facilities or water.

campground.name: Warburton Camp
campground.desc: A Warburton Camp in Sunshine Valley.

campground.name: Yellow Bluff Recreation Site
campground.desc: A Yellow Bluff Recreation Site in Queens Cove.

campground.name: Goose Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Two small free rec sites on a clear-water rainbow-trout lake in Northern BC, reached by roughly 17 km of active industrial FSR with heavy logging truck traffic — 2-way radio recommended; outhouses and boat launches provided but no potable water mentioned.

campground.name: Limestone
campground.desc: A Limestone in Remote & backcountry, Northern British Columbia.

campground.name: Giant Cedars
campground.desc: A forest service day-use site 37 km up the Bush River FSR, anchored by a gentle 0.8 km loop trail through old-growth cedars beside a small creek; listed as day-use only, so overnight camping is unconfirmed despite the camp_site tag.

campground.name: Bob Lake West Recreation Site
campground.desc: Tiny free lakeshore rec site on the west end of Bob Lake, suited to fishing and boating; the last 2 km is an explicitly rough 4x4 track that rules out loaded touring bikes and any trailer.

campground.name: Tony Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 2-site lake rec site prized for its seclusion, reached via a multi-leg logging road network with active logging traffic and one-way sections; no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Wap Lake West Recreation Site
campground.desc: A 2-site timbered rec site on a scenic small lake with good fishing and wildlife viewing, reached via 12 km of active industrial forest service road off the Trans-Canada west of Three Valley Gap; industrial traffic is a real concern for cyclists.

campground.name: Kagan Bay Campsite
campground.desc: A free 6-unit BC rec site on Kagan Bay, Graham Island (Haida Gwaii), accessed via 3 km of the Honna Forest Service Road from Queen Charlotte, with a small day-use area 1 km before the camping units. No amenities are listed.

campground.name: Marmot City Camp
campground.desc: A Marmot City Camp in Eastgate.

campground.name: Bluff Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Day-use area only — no overnight camping — beside a clear Chilcotin lake reached via roughly 17 km of forest-service gravel; the draws are exceptional Rainbow and Bull Trout fishing and a short trail with sweeping views over the lake and West Branch Valley.

campground.name: Boar Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny free rec site on the western shore of Boar Lake in the Cariboo backcountry, offering camping, car-top boating, and fishing — but reached only by a famously rough 6 km 4x4 trail that makes it effectively inaccessible to a loaded touring bike.

campground.name: Bedrock City Recreation Site
campground.desc: Boat-access-only forest campsite with 4 tent spots on the Sayward Forest Canoe Route at Mohun Lake; completely unreachable by bicycle — paddlers only.

campground.name: Krivensky Farm Recreation Site
campground.desc: A Krivensky Farm Recreation Site in Round Prairie.

campground.name: Monashee-Kettle Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, free, two-site recreation site on the Kettle River with riverside fishing, picnicking, and hiking; note seasonal fishing closures (no fishing July 25–Aug 25) and a bait ban April through October.

campground.name: Tall Timbers
campground.desc: A Tall Timbers in Kleecoot.

campground.name: Hen Ingram Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free lakeshore rec site in the Cariboo with nine defined campsites and a good boat launch; the access road has been improved but remains roughly 18 km of gravel off the Hen Ingram Road, and the site draws heavy summer traffic.

campground.name: Buckhorn Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small free lakeside rec site on the Willow Cale FSR south of Prince George with tables, fire rings, pit toilet, and a basic boat launch; popular with locals means expect heavy weekend crowds throughout summer.

campground.name: Isobel Lake Rec Site
campground.desc: A year-round recreation lake 20 km north of Kamloops set in an interpretive forest, with a 2 km accessible loop trail, stocked Rainbow Trout fishing, and winter cross-country skiing; the last 4 km to camp is on a Forest Service Road.

campground.name: White Boar Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A striking subalpine cirque lake framed by the sheer 2665 m wall of Mount McKay and a remnant glacier — scenically exceptional, but the final 4 km to the parking area is a rough 4WD/high-clearance track, leaving a 100 m walk to the two campsites. No drinking water mentioned; free, tables, and fire rings provided.

campground.name: Meadow Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: Small free Forest Service rec site on Meadow Lake reached via Pelican FSR and the '56' Road; draws anglers after wild rainbow trout and hunters in fall, but the tight FSR approach, swampy shoreline, and minimal amenities make it a niche stop rather than a touring highlight.

campground.name: Horseshoe Canyon - Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, no-reservation rec site alongside the Ashnola River, reached by roughly 15 km of gravel road south of Keremeos; expect basic facilities and a quiet riverside canyon atmosphere.

campground.name: Benson Point Recreation Site
campground.desc: A Benson Point Recreation Site in Nuchatlitz.

campground.name: McMurdo Cabin Recreation Site
campground.desc: A six-person log cabin managed by the Columbia Valley Hut Society, accessed via a long forest-service drive with industrial traffic, a creek ford requiring a truck or SUV, and a 1.5 km walk-in; radio communication is recommended. Used on foot in summer and by snowmobile in winter, making it a true backcountry destination rather than a cycle-in stop.

campground.name: Site 3 (BCMT)
campground.desc: A Site 3 (BCMT) in Dolphin Beach.

campground.name: Potlatch Creek Recreation Site
campground.desc: Open user-maintained recreation site on the Red Rock Forest Service Road overlooking Kinbasket Lake, 2.5 km past Mica Dam; popular with anglers and has a boat launch, but no confirmed amenities and facilities are user-maintained.

campground.name: Granite Creek Campground
campground.desc: Riverside recreation site on the Tulameen River near Coalmont, positioned as a natural trailhead for the Kettle Valley Railway — a marquee cycling route — with river paddling and hiking also on offer; cash only with no confirmed on-site amenities.

campground.name: Riverside Dispersed Camping
campground.desc: A Riverside Dispersed Camping in Whistler.

campground.name: Pye Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, 4-site lakeside rec site reached by 5.5 km of gravel road off Highway 19 north of Campbell River, set between the road and the lake with a steep boat launch; a functional stop for anglers and hunters with three other sites on the same lake nearby.

campground.name: Horsefly Bay Recreation Site
campground.desc: Tiny 2-site rec site at the mouth of the Horsefly River where it drains into Quesnel Lake, serving mainly as a small-boat and kayak launch; the end-of-road location has tight turnaround space and no confirmed amenities.

campground.name: Boot Lake Recreation Site
campground.desc: A tiny free lakeside rec site 85 km out on the Blackwater Road from Quesnel, with just 2–3 pitches and no confirmed facilities; expect a long gravel drive and a remote, quiet setting.

campground.name: Red Bridge Lake
campground.desc: A Red Bridge Lake in Keremeos.

campground.name: Upper Elk River Recreation Site
campground.desc: A small, partially treed site on the Elk River with open views of meadows and avalanche chutes; reached via 163.5 km of forest service road from Elkford — a very long, remote gravel approach on a loaded bike.

campground.name: Scout Beach Recreation Site
campground.desc: A free, treed campsite on Great Central Lake with pedestrian beach access, reached via 23+ km of privately managed logging roads that may close without notice — check gate status before riding in.

campground.name: Duhu Lake Campground
campground.desc: A small 7-pad rec site on Duhu Lake, sitting on a plateau just south of the Sikanni Chief River in deep Northern BC, with a large covered shelter and natural trout in an unstocked lake. Access is 6 km of PDR gravel west off the Alaska Highway.

campground.name: North Weaver Lake Group Site
campground.desc: A group-only site on a stocked fishing lake with a boat launch, dock, and 6 km loop trail; the steep, rough Forest Service Road explicitly requires 4x4 and is not suitable for loaded touring bikes. Open March 15–October 31, cash only, gates locked at 11 PM.

campground.name: Thornbrough Channel Campsite
campground.desc: A small free marine-trail campsite perched on the west shore of Howe Sound at the north end of Thornbrough Channel — scenic fjord surroundings, but reachable only by boat or kayak with no road or trail approach for cyclists.
