restaurant.name: True Grain Bread
restaurant.desc: True Grain is an organic craft bakery that has been handcrafting sourdough loaves, pastries, and cookies in the seaside village of Cowichan Bay since 2004, using 100% BC-farmed organic grain that the team stone-mills on-site in the Cowichan Valley. The bakery follows a farm-to-mill-to-baker model rooted in European tradition, working with ancient and heritage grains like Einkorn, Emmer, Spelt, and Red Fife with no additives or preservatives. It has grown into a destination for bread lovers exploring Vancouver Island, with in-store pickup, local home delivery, and Canada-wide mail order available.

detail.address: 1735 Cowichan Bay Rd., Cowichan Bay, BC V0R 1N0

notes.Takeout: In-store pickup available; cart page states 'STORE PICKUP Cowichan Bay Store is open every day 8am–5pm' and homepage shows 'ORDER PICKUP' call-to-action

restaurant.name: 40 Knots Vineyard and Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: 40 Knots is one of Vancouver Island's largest wineries, farming 24 acres of ocean-cooled vineyards in the Comox Valley. Visitors can explore interpretive trails, stroll gardens, or relax on a terrace with vineyard and ocean views while tasting sustainably produced wines. The winery emphasizes organic and biodynamic farming practices shaped by its proximity to the Salish Sea.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states wines are produced using 'clean, vegan, gluten-free winemaking' practices

restaurant.name: O'Rourke's Peak Cellars
restaurant.desc: Peak Cellars is an award-winning, cool-climate winery in Lake Country's Okanagan Valley, producing estate-grown wines recognized internationally — including a Gold Medal Chardonnay at the 2025 Chardonnay du Monde. The property includes a Garden Bistro serving farm-to-table seasonal dishes sourced from an on-site garden, a tasting room with guided premium seated tastings overlooking the vineyard and lake, and on-site accommodations. It is a full-destination stop on the Okanagan wine trail, offering a relaxed, scenic environment well suited to cycling visitors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple bistro menu items explicitly labeled Vegetarian, Vegan & Gluten-Friendly, Vegetarian & Gluten-Friendly, or Gluten-Friendly (e.g., Garden Bistro Salad 'Vegan & Gluten-Friendly', Roasted Delicata Squash Salad 'Vegetarian & Gluten-Friendly')

restaurant.name: Île Sauvage Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Île Sauvage — French for 'Wild Island' — is a Victoria craft brewery specialising exclusively in Belgian-style wild ales and sour beers, using Kveik, Lactobacillus, and Brettanomyces fermentations alongside oak-ageing vessels and local fruit refermentations. The name pays dual homage to the wilderness of Vancouver Island and the wild-fermentation philosophy at the heart of every batch. Cyclists passing through Victoria's inner harbour area can stop at the Bridge Street tasting room for on-site pours or pick up canned releases to take on the road.

restaurant.name: 4 Mile Restaurant & Brewpub
restaurant.desc: A full-service restaurant and brewpub situated in View Royal along the Island Highway, housed in what the domain name 'fourmilehouse' suggests is a historic roadhouse building. The on-site brewery produces a rotating lineup of year-round and seasonal beers — from a light lager and West Coast IPA to a non-alcoholic option — all available on draft in the pub. The venue also includes the '4 Below' sports bar, a High Tea program, and weekend brunch, making it an unusually varied stop for cyclists passing through the western edge of Greater Victoria.

restaurant.name: Red Truck Brewery Company
restaurant.desc: Red Truck Brewery Company is a craft brewery located in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, producing beer on-site. Situated on East 1st Avenue, it occupies a standalone building and is likely a destination-style taproom typical of the neighbourhood's brewery scene. Touring cyclists riding through the area may find it a natural stop for a post-ride pint in one of Vancouver's most bike-friendly districts.

restaurant.name: Divino Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Divino Estate Winery is a 100% estate winery on a 40-acre Cobble Hill vineyard, tracing its roots to owner-winemaker Joe Busnardo's original Oliver, BC operation in the early 1980s before relocating to the Cowichan Valley in 1996. The winery produces Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Pinot Grigio, Trebbiano, and a rotating cast of limited-release and late-harvest wines entirely from estate-grown fruit, with some rare old vintages only available on-site. Situated just off the Island Highway at the Cowichan Bay Road exit, it sits conveniently between Victoria and Nanaimo for cyclists riding the Vancouver Crossing Loop.

detail.address: 1500 Freeman Rd, Cobble Hill, BC V8H 0J2

notes.Takeout: Wine available for direct retail purchase from the winery shop; full selection including special old vintages, seasonal specials, and case-lot options sold on-site. Cash or cheque only — no cards accepted

restaurant.name: Electric Bicycle Brewing
restaurant.desc: Electric Bicycle Brewing is a craft brewery and tasting room in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, named with an unmistakable nod to cycling culture. The taproom offers a rotating lineup of house beers spanning pilsners, pale ales, hazy IPAs, sours, and nitro stouts, served in a social space with high tops, booths, and long communal tables. It pitches itself as a lively destination with music and a welcoming atmosphere — a natural stop for cyclists exploring the area.

restaurant.name: Kalala Organic Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Kalala Organic Estate Winery is an award-winning, certified-organic estate winery situated on the upper bench of West Kelowna in the Okanagan Valley, producing VQA wines from grapes hand-picked from its own organic vineyards since 2006. It holds one of the largest portfolios of organic Icewines in British Columbia and has garnered gold medals at competitions including Chardonnay du Monde in France. Visitors can book guided vineyard tours and wine tastings at the on-site tasting room.

detail.address: 3361 Glencoe Road, West Kelowna, BC V4T 1M1

restaurant.name: Hester Creek Winery
restaurant.desc: Hester Creek Estate Winery is one of the oldest wine properties in the South Okanagan, with 58 years of history on the Golden Mile Bench wine route just outside Oliver. Cyclists can stop in for a complimentary tasting at the wine shop, enjoy a sit-down meal at the on-site Terrafina Restaurant, or extend their stay at the luxury Villa. Award-winning estate wines and vineyard views make it a standout destination on the Okanagan's wine-country cycling circuit.

restaurant.name: Sage Hayward Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Sage Hayward Vineyards is a family-owned estate winery and bistro on Saturna Island in BC's Southern Gulf Islands, with vines first planted in 1995 in clay soils layered with ancient marine sediment. The property includes a seasonal tasting room and the Feral Goat Bistro, led by Chef Lee Yarrow and focused on locally sourced, seasonal ingredients paired with estate wines. Situated on a dramatic south-facing sea bench between sheer cliffs and ocean currents, it is accessible by BC Ferries, seaplane, or private boat — including via the property's own dock and mooring buoys.

restaurant.name: The View Winery & Vineyard
restaurant.desc: The View Winery & Vineyard is a family-owned estate winery housed in a restored 1920s apple packing house in East Kelowna, perched above Okanagan Lake with views of Black Knight and Dilworth Mountains. The winery has been on Ward family land for five generations and produces award-winning cool-climate whites, fruit-forward reds, and Wards Cider from its heritage orchards. Walk-in tastings are available seven days a week, and seasonal guided vineyard hikes, Sunday live music sessions, and occasional food trucks make it one of the more animated stops on the Okanagan wine route.

restaurant.name: Howe Sound Brewing
restaurant.desc: Howe Sound Inn & Brewing is Squamish's original craft brewery, founded in 1996 with the help of John Mitchell, the 'grandfather of micro-brewing,' and named Canadian Brewery of the Year in 2022. The flagship Squamish location operates as a full-service brewpub with a kitchen serving stone-fired pizzas, burgers, and shareables, alongside an on-site inn with pet-friendly rooms. Situated in the heart of Sea to Sky Country at the midpoint between Vancouver and Whistler, it is a natural gathering spot for cyclists travelling the corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Veggie burger option listed on taphouse menus at multiple locations: 'BEEF OR VEGGIE BURGER W/ FRIES'

restaurant.name: Dirty Laundry Vineyard
restaurant.desc: Dirty Laundry Winery is a Summerland destination celebrating 20 years of award-winning BC wines, with Gold medals at national and international competitions across multiple varietals. The property features an on-site Red Iron Grille with self-serve patio kiosks offering pizza and smoked meats alongside the tasting bar and wine shop. It sits on the Bottleneck Drive wine route, making it a natural midday stop for cyclists touring the Okanagan's wine country.

restaurant.name: House of Rose Winery
restaurant.desc: House of Rose Winery is a craft winery and wine shop located on Garner Road in Kelowna, situated in British Columbia's Okanagan Valley — one of Canada's premier wine regions. The winery is noted as a standout stop on guided wine tours of the Kelowna area. Touring cyclists exploring the region's vineyard routes and the nearby Kettle Valley Rail Trail would find it a natural waypoint.

restaurant.name: Whistler Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Whistler's craft brewery features a taphouse with a full menu of snacks and pizzas alongside their award-winning beers, including BC's first craft gluten-free lager. They also offer brewery tours and growler fills on-site at their Millar Creek Road location south of Whistler Village.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated gluten-free beer line including Forager Lager and Forager Pale Ale, both award-winning; gluten-free section on taphouse menu

restaurant.name: Backcountry Brewing
restaurant.desc: Backcountry Brewing is a craft brewery, tasting room, and kitchen that opened in Squamish in 2017, winning 'Rookie of the Year' at the BC Beer Awards with medals for all three core beers. The 70s ski cabin-inspired tasting room pairs an inventive menu of pizzas, salads, and snacks with more than 50 limited-edition beers released annually, plus a retail store stocked with cans and branded merchandise. A shipping container patio and a 38-seat Barrel Lounge round out a space well-suited to post-ride celebrations.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms vegan and dairy-free food options; gluten-free food options described as limited but accommodated where possible
notes.Covered bike parking: FAQ explicitly states 'covered bike parking in front of the taproom.'

restaurant.name: Pacific Breeze Winery
restaurant.desc: Pacific Breeze Winery claims the distinction of being the first Garagiste (garage winery) in Canada, a family-owned operation that has earned over 50 international medals including multiple Best of Class awards since its first release in 2007. Housed in a light-industrial unit in New Westminster, the winery operates a walk-in tasting room with a patio and lounge where visitors can sample handcrafted small-lot reds, whites, and seasonal frozen rosé drinks. All wines are certified vegan, and the winery also sells fresh grapes to home winemakers during harvest season.

detail.address: 6 – 320 Stewardson Way, New Westminster, BC V3M 6C3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About Us page states: 'All of our wines 100% vegan.'

restaurant.name: Crown and Thieves
restaurant.desc: Crown & Thieves is a small-batch winery built inside a striking four-story faux-ruin tucked into the vines of West Kelowna, operated by winemaker Jason Parkes. Part of the Westside Wine Trail, it offers tastings, a rooftop patio with vineyard views, and a speakeasy-style venue called The Broken Hearts Club hosting live music, comedy, and cabaret. It's an eccentric, memorable stop for cyclists touring the Okanagan wine country.

restaurant.name: Take THE Cake
restaurant.desc: Take THE Cake is a bakery business located in Richmond, BC, suggested by its URL domain. Beyond its name and approximate location, no verified details about its offerings, setting, or cyclist-relevant features are available from current evidence.

restaurant.name: Wolf Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Wolf Brewing Company is a craft brewery and taproom in Nanaimo, Vancouver Island, serving small-batch beers on 10+ taps including a nitro pour from their on-site brewery. Their kitchen turns spent brewing grain into pizza crust, and local Vancouver Island artists design each beer label. The dog-friendly patio, live music nights, and proximity to the Nanaimo Ferry Terminals and Airport make it a natural gathering point for cyclists arriving on or departing the island.

detail.address: #2-940 Old Victoria Road, Nanaimo, BC V9R6Z8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists explicit 'VEGETARIAN OPTIONS' and 'GLUTEN FREE OPTIONS' sections; FAQ also confirms 'a selection of GF food AND canned beer options.'

restaurant.name: Abandoned Rail Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Abandoned Rail Brewing Co. is a family-run estate brewery on the Naramata Bench where the owners farm their own barley to produce European-inspired, award-winning craft beers. The taproom sits alongside the Kettle Valley Rail Trail with sweeping bench views, explicitly positioned as a 20-minute bike ride from downtown Penticton and a natural trail stop. A kitchen serves pizza alongside an extensive tap list that includes a certified gluten-free sorghum-based pale ale, and a Guest House is available for overnight stays.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Gluten Schmuten Citrus Pale Ale is a sorghum-based gluten-free beer tested to below 20ppm per Canadian standards; a GF IPA variant is also available

restaurant.name: Bomber Brewing
restaurant.desc: Bomber Brewing is an East Vancouver craft brewery and taproom situated on Adanac Street, one of the city's most-used cycling routes. The taproom pours a rotating lineup of Czech-style lagers, IPAs, sours, and stouts alongside a food truck (B'SHAKE BURGER), making it a natural rest stop for cyclists passing through East Van. Package sales and delivery via Uber Eats and DoorDash are also available.

restaurant.name: Volcanic Hills Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Volcanic Hills Estate Winery is a three-generation family estate winery perched on the southeast slope of Mt. Boucherie, a 60-million-year-old dormant volcano whose rich volcanic soils inspired the name. The Gidda family has been growing grapes here since 1978, producing a wide range of wines including whites, reds, icewine, and fruit wines, with tastings available by reservation or walk-in. Seasonal events such as yoga-and-bubbles mornings and wedding hosting make it a lively destination on the Okanagan wine route.

detail.address: 2845 Boucherie Road, West Kelowna, BC V1Z 2G6

restaurant.name: Okanagan Crush Pad Winery
restaurant.desc: Okanagan Crush Pad is a Summerland-based winery producing organic wines under several labels including Haywire, Garnet Valley Ranch, and Free Form. Haywire's modern tasting lounge overlooks Okanagan Lake and Switchback Organic Vineyard, while Garnet Valley Ranch is a 320-acre working farm with lavender fields, vineyards, and a separate visitor centre open by appointment. Both venues host weddings and music events, making them notable destinations on the Okanagan wine-country cycling circuit.

restaurant.name: Wesbert Winery
restaurant.desc: Founded in 2019 by the South African Joubert family, Wesbert Winery cultivates over a dozen grape varieties on two Naramata Bench vineyards to produce award-winning wines, including a Double Gold Merlot. The winery sits near the road crossing of the Kettle Valley Rail Trail and describes itself as a favourite among cyclists and hikers. Visitors can book a tasting, enjoy wood-fired pizza on the terrace, or stay overnight in one of three guest suites overlooking the Okanagan hills.

restaurant.name: Salt Spring Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Salt Spring Vineyards is a craft winery and wine retail shop situated at 151 Lee Road on Salt Spring Island, BC. As one of the Gulf Islands' estate wineries, it draws visitors seeking locally produced wines in a rural island setting. Touring cyclists completing Salt Spring Island's wine route may find it a natural stop along a scenic ride.

restaurant.name: Parallel 49 Brewing
restaurant.desc: Parallel 49 Brewing is a Vancouver craft brewery founded in 2012, recognised as one of BC's early leaders in the craft beer movement. Their on-site Street Kitchen is billed as one of BC's largest craft brewery restaurants, with 40+ beers on tap and a fully stocked indoor food truck concept. An on-site retail beer store carries the full range of releases, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking to resupply with local craft beer.

restaurant.name: Torchlight Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Torchlight Brewing Co. is a locally-owned craft brewery and full-service lounge in Nelson, BC, founded in 2014 by two friends inspired by their love of craft beer. What began as a nano-brewery grew into a proper micro-brewery with a lounge that opened in 2017, offering house-made craft beers alongside a food menu. Situated in the heart of Nelson, it draws cyclists and visitors looking to relax over a pint or a meal after exploring the Kootenay region.

restaurant.name: Serendipity Winery
restaurant.desc: A boutique family-run winery in the heart of the Naramata Bench, founded in 2005 by Judy Kingston and now operated with her daughter Katie as head winemaker. The property features a wine shop with tastings, plus an on-site bistro called Terroir Kitchen offering seasonal, locally-sourced food paired with their estate wines. Named BC Winery of the Year and known for small-lot reds including Syrah, Merlot, and Pinot Noir.

restaurant.name: Neighbourhood Brewing
restaurant.desc: Neighbourhood Brewing is an independently owned craft brewery in downtown Penticton with a tasting room and a kitchen serving Mexican-inspired food. They offer a wide range of beers from hazy IPAs to sours, and the brewery features a seasonal outdoor patio that's dog-friendly and great for people-watching. Family-friendly and centrally located on Westminster Avenue, it's a natural stop for cyclists exploring Penticton's brewery scene.

detail.address: 187 Westminster Avenue W, Penticton, BC V2A 1J7

restaurant.name: Brassneck Brewery
restaurant.desc: Brassneck Brewery is an independent craft brewery with a walk-in tasting room and growler shop on Vancouver's Main Street, offering a rotating tap list of eclectic styles ranging from tart barrel-aged fruit beers to an 11% Chocolate Banana Imperial Milkshake Stout. The brewery fills growlers from other breweries as well, making it a handy stop for cyclists wanting to stock up. Food is available from their sister restaurant The Magnet, including options to take home.

restaurant.name: Streetcar Brewing
restaurant.desc: Streetcar Brewing is a craft brewery in North Vancouver producing beer. As a local brewery, it would offer touring cyclists a place to sample locally made beers and take a break from the road. Its North Vancouver location puts it within reach of popular cycling routes on the North Shore.

restaurant.name: Shawnigan House Coffee + Chocolate
restaurant.desc: Shawnigan House Coffee + Chocolate has been serving the Shawnigan Lake community since 2000, offering globally sourced coffee alongside house-made artisan chocolates crafted with Belgian and organic ingredients. Located on the Shawnigan Lake-Mill Bay Road, it is a natural stop for cyclists riding the Vancouver Crossing Loop through the Cowichan Valley. The shop sells individual truffles and chocolate bars as well as a full espresso menu, making it an easy place to refuel with something sweet.

detail.address: 1761 Shawnigan Lake-Mill Bay Rd, Shawnigan Lake, BC V0R 2W2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page explicitly labels multiple items: Vegan Truffle, Vegan Box of 12 Truffles, Gluten free Organic Chocolate bar, Gluten free Dipped Mango, Vegetarian labels on cappuccino, americano, drip coffee, and various chocolates

restaurant.name: Batch 44 Brewery & Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Batch 44 is a family-owned craft brewery and full-service kitchen on Sechelt's waterfront, pouring award-winning house beers alongside cocktails, BC wines, and cider. A dog-friendly patio, long communal tables, and a broad menu from poutine to fresh tuna poke make it an inviting gathering spot on the Sunshine Coast. Regular community events — trivia nights, karaoke, and Rock and Roll Bingo — give it a lively local character.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple GF-tagged items (chicken wings, Greek salad, spring garden salad, tuna poke with GF option) and vegetarian options including veggie spring rolls, mushroom flatbread, and crispy tofu as an add-on

restaurant.name: Logjam Coffee
restaurant.desc: Logjam Coffee is Kamloops' original specialty coffee roaster, founded in 2020 in a humble cabin and now running a cafe out of the city's iconic pink building on the North Shore at 437 Tranquille Rd. They roast small-batch, single-origin coffees at their roastery in the hills of Knutsford above the city, with roastery tours available by request. Cyclists on the Lac du Bois Tranquility route will find this an appealing stop for quality espresso and locally roasted beans.

restaurant.name: SummerGate Winery
restaurant.desc: SummerGate Winery is a family-run organic estate winery established in 2009 by the Stohler family, producing 100% BC wine from certified-organic grapes grown on their own Prairie Valley property in Summerland. Located along Summerland's Bottleneck Drive wine route, the property features a family- and pet-friendly licensed patio with picnic area, a weekend kitchen with food service including Sunday waffle breakfasts, and wine tastings of their specialty white, rosé, and frizzante-style wines. It is a natural and convivial rest stop on one of the Okanagan's most popular cycling corridors.

restaurant.name: Serious Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: A craft brewery mapped in Chemainus on Vancouver Island. No verified website content is available for this location — the discovered URL belongs to an unrelated brewery of the same name in New York State.

restaurant.name: Dockside Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Dockside Restaurant is a full-service waterfront dining destination inside the Granville Island Hotel, with floor-to-ceiling windows and views across False Creek to the downtown Vancouver skyline and North Shore Mountains. Its award-winning patio stretches over 200 seats and is sheltered on three sides, drawing diners from morning through late afternoon. The seasonal menu draws on fresh, local farm-to-table ingredients served across breakfast, lunch, dinner, and weekend brunch.

restaurant.name: Cliffside Cider
restaurant.desc: Cliffside Cider is a small-batch cidery located in Squamish, BC, producing cider on-site at a unit on Second Avenue. Squamish sits at the gateway to the Sea-to-Sky corridor, making it a natural stop for cyclists riding between Vancouver and Whistler. No current web presence could be confirmed, so the operating status of this taproom is uncertain.

restaurant.name: Granville Island Brewery
restaurant.desc: Granville Island Brewing has been crafting BC beers since 1984 and is one of the province's pioneering craft breweries, with a vibrant public taproom on Granville Island at the heart of Vancouver's seawall cycling network. The taproom pours a rotating small-batch Taproom Series alongside its mainline beers, and serves food on-site with off-sales for those continuing their ride. The patio is dog-friendly and the brewery is wheelchair accessible via a ramp through the side door.

restaurant.name: Six Mile Pub & Eatery
restaurant.desc: The Six Mile Pub & Eatery, established in 1855, is British Columbia's oldest pub, occupying a historic building along Old Island Highway just west of Victoria. The kitchen produces everything in-house — artisan breads raised from named sourdough starters, fresh pasta, and charcuterie — while an on-site apiary supplies honey used throughout the menu and in signature cocktails. A multiple-time Times Colonist Readers' Choice winner, it welcomes patrons of all ages and offers a seasonal riverside patio.

detail.address: 494 Old Island Hwy at Six Mile Rd, Victoria, BC V9B 1H5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menus page lists 'our gluten-free program' as a feature under Authentic Cuisine

restaurant.name: The Woods Spirit Co.
restaurant.desc: The Woods Spirit Co. is a family-owned, female-led craft distillery on North Vancouver's North Shore, producing Italian-inspired liqueurs and spirits using a proprietary vacuum distillation process with 100% BC grain and locally sourced botanicals. Their Barrel-aged Amaro earned Best in Class at the 2026 CASC Awards, and the operation includes a cocktail lounge (Bar in The Woods), regular Friday distillery tours, and cocktail workshops. As a BC Green Business Certified enterprise, they prioritize sustainable production and community engagement.

detail.address: 1450 Rupert Street, North Vancouver, BC V7J1E9

restaurant.name: Mariner Brewing
restaurant.desc: Mariner Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom in Coquitlam specializing in a rotating lineup of house beers. The taproom includes a full kitchen focused on smash burgers, plus an outdoor patio that welcomes dogs. It hosts community events and actively donates to local causes, giving it a neighbourhood-hub character that touring cyclists passing through the Tri-Cities area may find welcoming.

notes.Takeout: Growler fills explicitly offered ('Do you do growler fills? Yes! Our growler fill lineup changes frequently'); beer to go confirmed. Food takeout not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: The Parkside Brewery
restaurant.desc: The Parkside Brewery is a craft brewery and tasting room on Port Moody's celebrated Brewer's Row, situated directly across from Rocky Point Park at the foot of Eagle Mountain. Beers are brewed on site with a regularly rotating lineup of award-winning ales, lagers, and IPAs, with cans and growler fills available to go. The front patio welcomes dogs, and food trucks are hosted outside on most days, making it a sociable stop at the head of Burrard Inlet.

detail.address: 2731 Murray St, Port Moody, BC V3H 1X1

restaurant.name: Church and State Wines - Victoria
restaurant.desc: Vancouver Island's largest winery, Church and State Wines sits in Brentwood Bay just 15 minutes from downtown Victoria, pouring award-winning BC VQA wines grown exclusively on their own estate vineyards on Vancouver Island and in the Okanagan. The property features a tasting bar and a full bistro menu, plus a covered veranda and event programming that includes yoga in the vineyard and seasonal brunches. Named #1 Small Winery in British Columbia, it is a worthy scenic detour for cyclists riding the Saanich Peninsula near BC Ferries.

restaurant.name: Sheringham Distillery
restaurant.desc: Sheringham Distillery is a small Vancouver Island craft distillery that won the world's largest gin competition and produces a range of award-winning gins, whisky, vodka, akvavit, and liqueurs. Visitors can explore the tasting room and sample spirits made with a chef-inspired, botanical-forward approach. The distillery production is rooted in Sooke using BC grain, with the tasting room located in Langford.

detail.address: 103-4382 West Shore Parkway, Langford, BC V9B 5Z1

restaurant.name: Wild Ambition Brewing
restaurant.desc: Wild Ambition Brewing is a craft brewery based in Kelowna, BC, producing beer on site. Kelowna is a hub of the Okanagan cycling corridor, and a local brewery makes a natural rest stop for touring cyclists passing through. No further details about the taproom, food offerings, or facilities could be verified at time of enrichment.

restaurant.name: Beere Brewing
restaurant.desc: Beere Brewing is a family-run craft brewery on North Vancouver's waterfront, founded by a father-and-son duo who put their own name on every can. The tasting room pours a rotating lineup spanning hazy IPAs, West Coast IPAs, fruit sours, Italian-style pilsners, and a non-alcoholic pale ale. Beer is available to take home by the can or by the keg for private events, with a monthly subscription option for home delivery.

restaurant.name: Field House Brewing
restaurant.desc: Field House Brewing Co. opened its original tasting room in East Abbotsford in 2016 and is known for a constantly rotating tap list spanning crushable ales, experimental IPAs, and funky barrel-aged sours, with at least one new beer released every week. The Abbotsford location features a laid-back patio and beer lawn alongside a farm-to-table canteen, weekly live music, and a community run club. Non-alcoholic beer options are also on tap, making it a genuinely welcoming stop for cyclists who may not be drinking.

detail.address: 2281 W Railway St, Abbotsford, BC V2S 2E3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: CHWK menu page labels items with 'ⓥ VEGETARIAN' and 'Ⓖ GLUTEN AWARE' symbols; same canteen program operates at both locations

restaurant.name: Townsite Brewing
restaurant.desc: A coastal micro-brewery in the historic Townsite district of Powell River, on the shores of the Salish Sea along BC's Sunshine Coast. Known for Belgian-inspired craft beers, the tasting room pours a wide rotating selection including hazy pale ales, IPAs, stouts, and non-alcoholic options like craft soda and Nonny NA beer. The brewery is community-focused and also offers wine, cider, kombucha, and cocktails alongside its house brews.

detail.address: 5824 Ash Avenue, Powell River, BC V8A 4R4

restaurant.name: Red Arrow Brewery
restaurant.desc: Red Arrow Brewing Company is a craft brewery established in 2015 in the Cowichan Valley, operating a 35-seat taproom and a 65-seat outdoor patio at its Duncan location on Chaster Road. The brewery pours 12 of its own beers on tap alongside craft cocktails, local wines, and non-alcoholic options, all backed by a full-service food menu. The property also features a Sports Court used for concerts, fundraisers, and community events, giving it a strong community-hub character beyond a typical taproom.

restaurant.name: Millstone estate winery
restaurant.desc: Millstone is a small family farm winery and vineyard situated in Nanaimo, crafting wines that reflect the unique character of Vancouver Island's coastal terroir. The estate offers tastings by appointment and regular walk-in hours, making it a relaxed rural stop for cyclists exploring the East Wellington area. As a working farm vineyard, it provides a distinctly local taste of BC wine country outside of the Okanagan.

restaurant.name: Longwood Brewery
restaurant.desc: Longwood Brewery on Boxwood Road is an 'obsessively local' craft brewery sourcing most of its barley, hops, and other ingredients from Vancouver Island and the BC Mainland — named one of 'the most local of local breweries and beers in BC' by The Tyee Magazine. Its tasting room features a growler bar with 6 core beers and 4 rotating seasonals, plus a seasonal outdoor picnic patio that is pet and family friendly. Visitors are welcome to bring outside food, and the brewery also produces an alcohol-free, gluten-free Hop Soda for non-drinkers.

restaurant.name: 33 Acres Brewing
restaurant.desc: A family-owned craft brewery in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood with two side-by-side tasting rooms on West 8th Avenue. Their core lineup spans amber lagers to Belgian tripels, including a World Beer Cup Silver Award-winning Belgian Tripel. Walk-in only with a casual, spacious atmosphere and seasonal food offerings.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: 33 Acres of Cid3r is explicitly described as gluten-free on the menu page

restaurant.name: Frind Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Frind Estate Winery is a large beachfront estate winery on the shores of Okanagan Lake in West Kelowna, self-described as the most-visited winery in Canada with over 10,000 guests weekly. The estate spans 400+ acres of vineyards across the Okanagan Valley, including the largest contiguous vineyard in BC. Touring cyclists can stop for lakeside wine tastings, casual meals at the Takeout Hut with picnic tables, or a full sit-down meal at the patio restaurant with lake views.

detail.address: 3725 Boucherie Rd, West Kelowna, BC V4T 0A8

restaurant.name: Mission Hill Family Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Mission Hill Family Estate is a landmark Okanagan winery perched high above the valley with sweeping views of mountains, vineyards, and Okanagan Lake. Named Canada's Winery of the Year a record six times and listed among the World's 50 Best Vineyards in 2025, it offers curated tasting experiences, a fine-dining Terrace Restaurant, and a summer concert series in an outdoor amphitheatre. Access to the estate requires a reservation or membership, though same-day bookings are accommodated when space is available.

restaurant.name: Small Block Brewery
restaurant.desc: Small Block Brewery is a craft brewery in the Cowichan Valley near Duncan, BC, producing small-batch hand-crafted British Ales with locally sourced BC ingredients. The taproom has a cozy 'garage' atmosphere where visitors can enjoy tasters or pints, or take home a growler. Wood-fired pizza from Vancouver Island Pizza is available on weekends alongside snacks, making it a worthwhile stop on the Cowichan Valley cycling corridor.

detail.address: 203 - 5301 Chaster Road, Cowichan Valley D, British Columbia V9L 6T7, Canada

restaurant.name: La Frenz Winery
restaurant.desc: La Frenz Winery is a family-owned estate established in 1999 on the celebrated Naramata Bench, farming 62 acres across six vineyards with varieties and clones deliberately matched to each site's soils and climate. It earned recognition as #1 Best Performing Small Winery of the Year and #2 Winery of the Year at the 2021 WineAlign National Wine Awards, making it one of the Okanagan's most decorated boutique producers. Cyclists riding the Naramata Bench wine route can stop at the wine shop for tasting flights and bottle purchases.

restaurant.name: Seaside Pearl Farmgate Winery
restaurant.desc: Seaside Pearl Farmgate Winery is a family-owned boutique farmgate winery set among rolling fields and quiet country roads in the Mount Lehman area of Abbotsford, BC. The winery produces small-lot, cool-climate artisanal wines from both estate-grown and Okanagan grapes, with labels named after local pioneer history. Tastings are held in a copper-spired chapel tasting room with panoramic Fraser Valley views, and a separate Barrel Room is available for events.

restaurant.name: Category 12
restaurant.desc: Category 12 is a small-batch craft brewery and taproom on Keating Cross Road, brewing just 30 kegs at a time using Canadian-made equipment produced less than 1 km from the brewhouse. The taproom includes a bistro serving scratch-made food with local ingredients, plus a viewing window into the brewing operation so visitors can watch while waiting for growler fills. Regular events — live music, wing nights, and trivia — give it a strong community-gathering character.

detail.address: Unit C, 2200 Keating Cross Road, Victoria, BC

restaurant.name: Stoneboat Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Stoneboat Vineyards is a family-owned estate winery on Oliver's Black Sage benchlands, with vineyards maturing since the late 1970s planted to Pinot Noir, Pinotage, Pinot Gris, and Pinot Blanc. The name references the flat sledge once used to clear the abundant river rocks from the vineyard — those calcium-encrusted rocks are credited with lending the wines a distinct mineral character. Cyclists riding the South Okanagan wine routes can stop at the wine shop for tastings of handcrafted estate, small-lot, and reserve wines.

restaurant.name: Wild North Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Wild North Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and taproom in Creston, BC, situated just off Canyon St in the heart of the Creston Valley. The brewery emphasises locally sourced ingredients and an authentic approach to craft beer, pouring its own lineup in a taproom with a patio and a lively events calendar that includes trivia nights and community gatherings. It is a natural social hub for cyclists passing through the Kootenays on a longer touring route.

restaurant.name: Threefold Brewery
restaurant.desc: Threefold is a brewery collective on Powell Street in East Vancouver, bringing three independent craft breweries together under one roof alongside Neapolitan pizza. The taproom pours a rotating tap list of craft beers and other drinks, with a food menu that gives cyclists the chance to sample multiple local producers in a single stop. The menu includes a wide range of vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options alongside more conventional fare.

restaurant.name: Grey Fox Brewery
restaurant.desc: Grey Fox Brewing is a dedicated gluten-free brewery located in Lake Country (Winfield), BC, making it a notable stop for cyclists with celiac disease or gluten sensitivities. The brewery has an online shop and a beer-finder page, suggesting both taproom presence and wider distribution. Touring cyclists in the Okanagan wine and orchard corridor will find it a distinctive craft beverage destination.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website page titles on every subpage read 'Dedicated Gluten-Free Brewery in BC', indicating all beers are gluten-free

restaurant.name: Ancient Hill Winery
restaurant.desc: Ancient Hill Estate Winery is a family-owned boutique estate winery in the Ellison area of North Kelowna, situated on a hillside across from the Kelowna Airport where wine grapes were first grown in the 1940s. The European-style winery building was designed by a noted Penticton architect and produces small-lot wines entirely from grapes grown on-site, including Lemberger, Pinot Noir, Baco Noir, and Pinot Gris. Cyclists can taste wines in the old-world-style shop or enjoy a glass on the patio with panoramic valley views, accompanied by cheeses, crackers, and non-alcoholic beverages.

restaurant.name: White Sails Brewery
restaurant.desc: White Sails Brewing is an award-winning craft brewery that has been a fixture of downtown Nanaimo since 2015, located across from Maffeo Sutton Park on the waterfront. The open-concept taproom seats over 100 and pours up to 14 beers alongside guest taps, a selection of wines and ciders, a full coffee bar, and a locally-sourced food menu. Their flagship beers have earned gold medals at the BC Beer Awards, Canadian Brewing Awards, and World Beer Awards.

notes.Takeout: Beers-to-go available from the Taproom beer fridge; growler fills (32oz, 64oz) and tall cans (473mL) offered for flagship and seasonal beers

restaurant.name: Cambium Cider Co
restaurant.desc: The BX Press Cidery is a craft cider producer rooted in a third-generation transitional organic apple orchard outside Vernon, BC. The operation is currently rebranding to 'Cambium Cider Co' and opening a new farm-to-table restaurant celebrating local purveyors alongside its artisan cider. The 70-year-old Spartan apple trees and generational farming heritage give this destination a distinctive sense of place.

detail.address: 4667 East Vernon Road, Vernon, BC V1B 3H9

restaurant.name: Little Engine Wines
restaurant.desc: Little Engine Wines is a boutique winery and tasting room situated on Naramata Road along the Naramata Bench, one of the Okanagan's most celebrated cycling corridors. The tasting room pours across multiple wine series — Elevation, Silver, Gold, and Platinum — and offers a small bites food menu alongside wine club membership. The winery also hosts events and weddings, making it a destination stop rather than just a bottle shop.

restaurant.name: Twin Sails Brewery
restaurant.desc: Twin Sails Brewing opened in 2015 on Port Moody's 'Brewers Row', founded by identical twin brothers whose name also nods to the sailboats visible on Burrard Inlet right out front. The brewery specialises in progressive American IPAs, stouts, sours, and wild barrel ales, with a taproom, patio, arcade, and a weekend food truck (Mama Said's Pizza) on site. Dogs are welcome on the patio and guests may bring outside food, making it a convivial stop for cyclists riding the Burrard Inlet corridor.

detail.address: 2821 Murray Street, Port Moody, BC V3H 1X3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQs state: 'We do! Although we don't make any gluten free beers in house, we have several gluten free options available in our taproom.' No explicit vegetarian/vegan claim found

restaurant.name: BNA Brewing
restaurant.desc: BNA Brewing Co. & Eatery is Kelowna's flagship craft brewery, set inside a century-old building that once housed the British North American Tobacco Company — the source of the BNA name. All beer is brewed on-site and spans a wide range of styles from easy-drinking lagers to adventurous sours, served alongside a full kitchen menu in a space that also includes bowling lanes. It is a lively, locally-owned destination in the heart of downtown Kelowna, operating since 2015.

restaurant.name: Terravista Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Terravista Vineyards is a small estate winery on the Naramata Bench — one of BC's most popular cycling corridors — specializing in rare Spanish white varieties such as Albariño and Verdejo alongside a premium small-lot series called En Terre. All three of the winery's Naramata Bench vineyards achieved 100% certified organic status in Fall 2025, reflecting a commitment to sustainable viticulture including solar arrays, electric utility vehicles, and livestock integration. Touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan can book seated tasting experiences and purchase wines directly on site.

restaurant.name: Slackwater Brewing
restaurant.desc: Slackwater Brewing is a craft brewery in Penticton producing BC-brewed craft beer. Located on Martin Street in Penticton's downtown core, it sits within the Okanagan's cycling heartland and offers a taproom destination for touring cyclists. The brewery's active 2025 website references beers, events, and a 'Find Us' section suggesting a welcoming public venue.

restaurant.name: Deep Blue Distilleries
restaurant.desc: Deep Blue Distilleries is a craft distillery in Richmond, BC, producing small-batch gins and vodkas inspired by the purity of the BC coast using custom-built distillation equipment sourced from Hungary and Spain. The distillery offers guided tours by appointment (typically Wednesday through Friday) covering the full distillation process and concluding with spirit tastings and handcrafted cocktails. Multiple spirit brands are produced on-site — including Nookum Gin and Charm Vodka — and are available for retail purchase directly from the distillery.

restaurant.name: Venturi Schulze Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Venturi-Schulze Vineyards is a family farmstead winery established in 1987 on Vancouver Island, practising natural viticulture — no pesticides, herbicides, or irrigation — on a south-facing estate that also produces artisan balsamic vinegar, verjus, and jams. The property includes an outdoor patio tasting area that welcomes leashed dogs, and products can be purchased directly from the wine shop or ordered online with gate pickup available. The winery has earned recognition for its eco-friendly approach and estate-grown, minimally-intervened wines.

detail.address: 4235 Vineyard Road, Cobble Hill, BC V8H 0A6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states: 'We do not use any animal products in our processing, including, but not limited to, egg white, gelatin, isinglass (derived from fish) or blood. Our wines meet the requirements for vegan or vegetarian diets.'

restaurant.name: Tinhouse Brewing
restaurant.desc: Tinhouse Brewing is a Port Coquitlam craft brewery and taproom that opened in 2019, with roots going back nearly a decade under the name Sapperton Brewing. The taproom features a 30-seat licensed outdoor patio and welcomes outside food, with local food trucks on weekends and nearby restaurant delivery options. A FAQ note points cyclists toward Dominion Park, just 600m along the trail, where open liquor is permitted and there is a playground.

detail.address: #2140 - 550 Sherling Place, Port Coquitlam, BC V3B 0J6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ lists 'veggie or butter chicken samosas' as hot snack options, confirming at least one vegetarian item

restaurant.name: Vinoscenti Vineyards
restaurant.desc: A family winery set on 13 acres of pastoral farmland alongside the Serpentine River on the edge of White Rock. They produce a range of wines including Merlot, Cabernet blends, Gewürztraminer, Rosé, and a late harvest red, all available for tasting and purchase on-site. The rural setting and vineyard grounds make it an appealing rest stop for cyclists riding the flat agricultural roads of south Surrey.

restaurant.name: Little Straw Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Little Straw Vineyards is one of the Okanagan's oldest family estate wineries, with vineyard roots dating to 1969 when the Slamka family first planted in West Kelowna. Now under the stewardship of the Sidhu family, the 12-acre estate is transitioning toward organic certification and hosts TULA Restaurant, offering refined Indian cuisine alongside its VQA wines. Touring cyclists on the Okanagan wine route can combine vineyard tastings and guided tours with a full sit-down meal at this historic property.

detail.address: 2815 Ourtoland Road, West Kelowna, BC V1Z 2H7

restaurant.name: Ravens Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Ravens Brewing Company is a family-owned Indigenous brewery and distillery founded in 2014 by Paul and Jocelyn Sweeting, producing a wide range of craft beers from IPAs and Belgian tripels to sours and stouts in the Fraser Valley. The brewery has won a BC Beer Award every year for five consecutive years and took best Gose at the 2018 World Beer Cup. They also offer contract brewing and distribution services, making them a regional hub for craft beverage production.

restaurant.name: Steel & Oak Brewing
restaurant.desc: Steel & Oak Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and tasting room in New Westminster producing unfiltered, unpasteurized beer using a blend of North American and German brewing traditions, from dry Irish stouts to hazy IPAs. An on-site food truck offers a full menu of burgers, sandwiches, salads, and snacks — a proper sit-down fuel stop rather than just a drink destination. The brewery also hosts events and offers private keg sales, giving it a lively community feel.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: S&O Veggie Burger explicitly labelled '(vegan)' on the menu: beyond meat patty, brioche or pretzel bun

restaurant.name: Heaven's Gate Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: A family-run boutique winery on Summerland's Bottle Neck Drive, producing small-batch wines from 100% BC VQA grapes grown in the volcanic soils of Giant Head Mountain. The property features a cozy log-cabin tasting room and an outdoor picnic area with a fountain where visitors are encouraged to bring a lunch and relax. A good rest stop for touring cyclists riding the Summerland wine route.

detail.address: 8001 Happy Valley Road, Summerland, BC V0H 1Z4

restaurant.name: Meyer Family Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Meyer Family Vineyards is an award-winning Okanagan Falls winery recognized as a Top 3 Winery in Canada at the 2025 National Wine Awards, producing about 8,000 cases of Burgundian-style Chardonnay and Pinot Noir from hand-harvested grapes. Operating since 2006, the winery has a tasting room and wine shop where visitors can sample and purchase critically acclaimed small-lot wines. It sits along McLean Creek Road in the heart of BC wine country, making it a natural destination stop on a cycling tour of the Okanagan Valley.

restaurant.name: Blackwood Lane Winery
restaurant.desc: Blackwood Lane Winery is a family-run estate operated by father-and-son team Carlos and Daniel Lee, who use traditional French winemaking methods without chemicals or mechanical pumps to produce award-winning Okanagan wines. Recently relocated from Aldergrove to Penticton, it sits at the very first stop on the Naramata Bench, making it a natural pull-off for cyclists riding that iconic route. The tasting room is open seven days a week and the online shop offers store pickup for those who want to load a bottle into their panniers.

detail.address: 134 Lower Bench Road, Penticton, BC V2A 1A8

restaurant.name: Tin Whistle Brewing Co
restaurant.desc: Tin Whistle is a craft brewery and taproom set inside the historic Cannery Trade Centre, a former fruit cannery turned industrial-chic gathering space in Penticton. It holds the distinction of being the first carbon neutral brewery in British Columbia, a milestone the company announced on Earth Day 2021. The taproom pours a rotating lineup of South Okanagan-inspired beers — including their iconic Peach Cream Ale and experimental seasonal taps — in a setting the brewery describes as always playing records and always pouring something new.

detail.address: Unit 118 - 1475 Fairview Road, Penticton, BC V2A 7W5

restaurant.name: Upper Bench Winery and Creamery
restaurant.desc: Upper Bench Winery and Creamery is a 9.5-acre estate winery on the Naramata Bench sub-GI in the South Okanagan, known for award-winning bold reds, crisp dry whites, and handcrafted artisanal cheeses made on-site from pasteurized cow's milk. The property features a private patio for guided wine-and-cheese tasting experiences and a wood-fired oven wine bar called The Oven. The Naramata Bench is one of BC's premier cycling routes, making this a natural destination stop for touring cyclists exploring the region.

detail.address: 170 Upper Bench Road South, Penticton, BC V2A 8T1

restaurant.name: 33 Brewing Experiment
restaurant.desc: 33 Brewing Experiment (33B) is the experimental taproom arm of 33 Acres Brewing Company, occupying a single-storey retail space on West 8th Avenue in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood. It operates on a walk-in basis with bar service alongside a seasonally rotating food menu, and can host private events for up to 60 guests. The location sits steps from the main 33 Acres taproom (33A) at 15 West 8th Avenue.

restaurant.name: Île Sauvage Brewing
restaurant.desc: Île Sauvage Brewing is a craft brewery in Victoria specializing in Belgian-style wild ales and sour beers, with a tasting room on Bridge Street. The name translates to 'Wild Island,' referencing both Vancouver Island's wilderness and the brewery's focus on Kveik, Lactobacillus, and Brettanomyces fermentations, oak-ageing, and local fruit refermentations. Cyclists stopping in will find a rotating selection of wild and sour beers available on tap and for takeout.

restaurant.name: Sandhill Wines
restaurant.desc: Sandhill Wines is an urban winery operating on the historic Calona Wines estate — established in 1932, it holds the distinction of being BC's original and oldest continuing winery. Crafting VQA wines since 1997 from grapes sourced across six vineyards in the Okanagan and Similkameen valleys, it offers guided tastings, curated food pairings, live music, and private events in the heart of downtown Kelowna. A touring cyclist finishing a day's ride into Kelowna will find it a short walk from the waterfront and city centre.

restaurant.name: Silkscarf Winery
restaurant.desc: Silkscarf is a family boutique estate winery that has operated under the same founding proprietors and winemakers since 2004, making it one of the longer-running family wineries in the Okanagan. The estate cultivates over 10 varieties across 10-plus acres of class-1 terroir on the Summerland Bench Sub-GI, with a declared commitment to sustainable farming. Touring cyclists on the Naramata–Summerland bench roads can stop for a tasting and browse an extensive library collection of older vintages.

restaurant.name: Privato Vineyard & Winery
restaurant.desc: Privato is a boutique, family-owned winery nestled along the scenic slopes of the North Thompson River in the Thompson Valley wine region, specializing in small-lot Burgundian-style Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. Their flagship Pinot Noir has earned double gold medals at the All Canadian Wine Awards. Visiting cyclists can enjoy a personalized tasting in the wine garden or linger on the picnic grounds with a glass overlooking the vineyard.

restaurant.name: High Mountain Brewing
restaurant.desc: High Mountain Brewing Co. — widely known as The Brewhouse — has been a Whistler Village anchor since 1997, brewing award-winning ales and lagers on-site and serving a full scratch kitchen of barbecue, pastas, and flatbreads. Part of the Mark James Group, it occupies a large multi-room space with a two-sided fireplace and a generous patio beside the Olympic Rings, making it a natural gathering spot after a day on the bike or the slopes. It is open year-round and capable of handling large groups across its restaurant, bar, and mezzanine levels.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegetarian dishes appear across menus: Crispy Tofu, Gochujang Cauliflower, Brussels Sprouts, Mac and Cheese, Farmers Market Avocado Toast, and a Breakfast Skillet offered with 'impossible meat' as a plant-based option

restaurant.name: Poplar Grove Winery
restaurant.desc: Poplar Grove Winery is a family-owned, estate-grown winery near Penticton celebrating its 30th vintage, producing a full range of Okanagan reds, whites, and rosés from its own vineyards. The property features a walk-in tasting room and The Restaurant at Poplar Grove, a full-service dining room with a patio offering vineyard views, open seven days a week for lunch and dinner. Cyclists riding through the Penticton bench country will find it a relaxed stop for wine tasting, a sit-down meal, and retail wine purchases including convenient 3-litre bag-in-box formats.

detail.address: 425 Middle Bench Road North, Penticton, BC V2A 8S5

restaurant.name: Foamers' Folly Brewing
restaurant.desc: Foamers' Folly Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and full-service tasting room in Pitt Meadows, BC, pouring 20 taps of house-made beer alongside rotating wine and cider. The tasting room is known for adventurous, boundary-pushing recipes — wild sours, fruit lagers, and hard seltzers sit alongside approachable core styles. A beautiful patio, food menu, and regular events make it a natural gathering point for cyclists passing through the Pitt Meadows flats.

restaurant.name: Grizzli Winery
restaurant.desc: A family-owned estate winery in the heart of West Kelowna's wine country, housed in an architecturally award-winning building with a year-round art gallery. The on-site restaurant 31 Charkay serves contemporary Canadian cuisine with vineyard views, making it a rewarding stop along Boucherie Road for touring cyclists exploring the Okanagan wine routes.

restaurant.name: Millionaires' Row Cider Co.
restaurant.desc: Millionaires' Row Cider Co. is a family-run cidery on a 100+ year-old apple orchard in Summerland's historic Prairie Valley, named for the wealthy investors who shaped the region's early fruit industry. Visitors taste hand-crafted estate ciders at a stand-up bar in the cellar, then can relax in a picnic area surrounded by the working orchard, with views of Conkle Mountain and Giants Head Mountain. The cidery sells its full range of vegan, gluten-free ciders to take away, making it a natural stop on a cycling tour through the South Okanagan.

notes.Takeout: Ciders sold by the bottle at the tasting room; tasting fee waived with any purchase
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: All five cider varieties described as 'Vegan and naturally gluten-free' on the product pages

restaurant.name: Hoyne Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Family-owned craft brewery on Bridge Street in Victoria, voted Best Brewery seven years running by the Times Colonist Reader's Choice Awards. They produce a wide range of lagers, ales, and seasonal brews, and operate a growler bar and brewery tours on select Saturdays.

restaurant.name: Ex Nihilo Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Ex Nihilo Vineyards is a boutique estate winery in Lake Country whose name—Latin for 'out of nothing'—reflects its artisan philosophy of crafting wines from the ground up in the Okanagan. The property houses a tasting room open seven days a week alongside Chaos Bistro, an evening restaurant that regularly features live music and al fresco dining under the Okanagan sky. Cycling visitors exploring the Okanagan wine country will find it a polished destination stop with walk-in tastings available as well as reservable guided experiences.

restaurant.name: White Rock Beach Beer Brewery
restaurant.desc: White Rock Beach Beer Company is a locally-owned craft microbrewery founded in 2013 by two White Rock secondary school teachers who built the operation from scratch. The brewery operates a tasting room and lounge adjacent to its production space on Russell Avenue, where visitors can sample a range of house-brewed beers from light lagers and pilsners to a Baltic-style porter and a highly-hopped IPA. Its tagline 'Because beaches and beer go better together' reflects its identity as a neighbourhood hangout close to the White Rock waterfront.

detail.address: 15181 Russell Ave, White Rock, BC V4B 3Z6

restaurant.name: Off the Grid Organic Winery
restaurant.desc: A family-owned organic winery on a 105-year-old Paynter family farm in West Kelowna, featuring a solar-powered straw bale tasting room and a seasonal food truck. The permaculture property includes farm animals (goats on the roof, sheep, chickens), a local artisan gift shop, and PACS-certified organic wines. A distinctive Okanagan stop where sustainability is baked into everything from the building to the bottle.

detail.address: 3623 Glencoe Rd, West Kelowna, BC V4T 1L8

notes.Takeout: Seasonal outdoor food truck with hand-crafted menu items using local ingredients

restaurant.name: Freddy's Brewing
restaurant.desc: Freddy's Brewing is an in-house craft brewery and full-service brewpub operating inside the McCurdy Bowling Centre, a large entertainment complex in Kelowna. The brewpub pours over 12 in-house craft beers alongside cocktails, wine, and spirits, paired with an elevated pub food menu spanning breakfast through dinner. A touring cyclist stopping here gets a rare combination of serious craft beer and a lively, spacious venue.

restaurant.name: Intrigue Wines
restaurant.desc: Intrigue Wines is a boutique, family-owned winery in Lake Country, BC, founded in 2008 by two local families who combined winemaking, business, and community expertise to build an award-winning Okanagan estate. All wines are crafted from 100% BC-grown grapes with sustainability at the core, earning consistent recognition for quality across white, red, rosé, and sparkling styles. Cyclists riding the Okanagan Wine Route can drop in for a bookable tasting experience or pick up bottles at the on-site wine shop in a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere.

restaurant.name: Ace Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Ace Brewing Company is a family-owned microbrewery and taproom in Courtenay's Comox Valley, themed around the ace fighter pilots of WWI and WWII who flew from nearby CFB Comox. The Landolt family built the brewery around a commitment to quality, producing everything from crisp German-style Pilsners to bold West Coast IPAs. The taproom pours a rotating lineup of craft beers that includes the 2022 Canada Beer Cup Silver Medal-winning Wingman Pale Ale.

restaurant.name: Tantalus Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Tantalus Vineyards is a boutique estate winery on the eastern slopes of the Okanagan Valley, operating on one of BC's oldest continuously producing vineyards — first planted to grapes in 1927. It holds the distinction of being British Columbia's first LEED-certified winery, and has earned a national and international reputation for its terroir-driven Riesling, Chardonnay, and Pinot Noir. Touring cyclists can book a tasting experience overlooking Lake Okanagan and the City of Kelowna.

restaurant.name: Black Kettle Brewing
restaurant.desc: Black Kettle Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom that opened in January 2014 just past the rail tracks in North Vancouver, a short ride from the Spirit Trail. The brewpub pours its own lagers, IPAs, and seasonal ales alongside a full kitchen menu of smash burgers, tacos, pizza, and wings. It is pet-friendly on the patio and regularly hosts live music, making it a welcoming destination for cyclists coming off the North Shore mountains or arriving via the Seabus.

detail.address: 720 Copping Street – Unit 106, North Vancouver, BC V7M 3N2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Veggie Smash Burger (Impossible patty), Chicken Fingers explicitly labeled gluten free, and G.O.A.T Salad with a veggie patty add-on option

restaurant.name: Laughing Stock Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Laughing Stock Vineyards is a boutique estate winery on the Naramata Bench renowned for its flagship Portfolio Bordeaux-style blend, which has earned 90+ points from WineAlign in 8 of 10 submissions since 2012 and is regarded as one of BC's cult wines. The estate grows all five Bordeaux varieties on-site and offers premium seated tastings with access to limited-production wines sold only at the winery. Cyclists passing by without a reservation can call from the gate to check walk-in availability.

restaurant.name: BNA Brewing Co
restaurant.desc: BNA Brewing Co is a craft brewery and eatery located steps from the beach in Penticton, the third location in a growing Okanagan chain. The venue pairs its own craft beer lineup with a full food menu that spans Filipino-inspired dishes, a raw bar seafood tower, and smash burgers, all inside a lively space with four-lane bowling, shuffleboard, darts, and bocce. It sits in the heart of one of BC's most popular cycling destinations, making it a natural post-ride social stop.

restaurant.name: The Parkside Brewery
restaurant.desc: The Parkside Brewery is a craft brewery and tasting room on Port Moody's celebrated 'Brewer's Row,' situated directly across from Rocky Point Park at the eastern end of Burrard Inlet. The brewery produces award-winning beers across a wide range of styles, from easy-drinking lagers to bold hoppy ales, all brewed on-site by head brewer Vern Lambourne. Its location near waterfront trails, forested parklands, and the broader Burrard Inlet cycling network makes it a natural and rewarding stop for touring cyclists.

detail.address: 2731 Murray St, Port Moody, BC V3H 1X1

restaurant.name: Okanagan Spirits Craft Distillery
restaurant.desc: Western Canada's original craft distillery, Okanagan Spirits has been producing award-winning spirits from 100% BC grain and fruit since 2004. The Vernon flagship is a full-service destination featuring a tasting room, cocktail lounge, experience classroom, and drop-in tastings requiring no reservation. In 2025 the distillery earned the World-Class Distillery designation at the World Spirits Awards in Germany, taking home 11 Gold and 5 Silver medals across its whisky, gin, brandy, and liqueur portfolio.

restaurant.name: Nichol Vineyard & Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Nichol Vineyard is one of the first three pioneering wineries on the Naramata Bench, with vines planted in 1989 at the northernmost tip of Naramata, directly abutting the Kettle Valley Railway trail. The winery is historically notable for planting the first Syrah vines in Canada and takes a rigorous minimal-intervention approach — hand-harvested, unfined, unfiltered, and vegan. A touring cyclist arriving via the KVR will find a relaxed tasting room with Okanagan Lake views, a record player, a covered picnic area for lingering with a brought lunch, and wine available by the glass or bottle.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page states: 'Our wines are technically vegan.'

restaurant.name: Dageraad Brewing
restaurant.desc: Dageraad Brewing is a small-batch artisan brewery crafting Belgian-inspired beers from a warehouse tasting room steps from Production Way SkyTrain station in Burnaby, named after the Dageraadplaats neighbourhood square in Antwerp. The 50-seat indoor tasting room is complemented by a 50-seat covered, heated patio — a welcoming stop in any weather. Dageraad was awarded 2018 Brewery of the Year by the Canadian Brewing Awards and offers a rotating lineup of Belgian-style ales including saisons, strong goldens, and mixed-culture fermentations.

restaurant.name: Beach Fire Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Beach Fire Brewing Company is Campbell River's own craft brewery, producing award-winning beers including the High Tide Pale Ale (People's Choice at the Mount Washington Tapped Beer Festival) and the Ember Red Ale (Canada Beer Cup Gold in 2023 and 2025). The taproom backs its lineup with a full kitchen menu built entirely around locally sourced, in-house-prepared food — from snacks and shareables to hearty mains and decadent desserts. The brewery markets itself explicitly around community and the active West Coast lifestyle, with a trail-nodding house stout called WheelBender Stout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu labels items with GF (gluten-free) and V (vegetarian) icons throughout; Black Bean Tostadas explicitly noted as having a vegan option

restaurant.name: Mission Springs Brewing
restaurant.desc: Mission Springs Brewing Company is one of BC's oldest craft brewhouses, opened in 1996 and operating a 10-barrel facility overlooking the Fraser River in Mission. The brewpub pairs its house-crafted beers — available on tap, in growlers, cans, and bottles — with a full pub menu served across three patios and a dining room. It is part of the Springs Group, which also runs an attached liquor store where cyclists can pick up beer to go.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page includes a dedicated link: 'VIEW OUR VEGETARIAN/VEGAN/GF MENU'

restaurant.name: Play Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Play Estate Winery is an estate winery and restaurant perched on Skaha Hills Drive with sweeping, unobstructed views of Skaha Lake and the surrounding mountains, just minutes from downtown Penticton. The property houses both a wine shop carrying estate-grown wines crafted by winemaker Rebecca Ruggeri and The Vista Restaurant, which serves flatbreads, charcuterie, seafood, and other light fare. The winery's arts-inspired identity — its name evoking theatre and the spirit of Shakespeare — lends it a distinctive character among the Okanagan's many wine destinations.

detail.address: 507 Skaha Hills Drive, Penticton, BC V2A 0A9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated Veggie flatbread; multiple items (flatbreads, charcuterie, mussels, sautéed prawns, seafood rangoon) are individually noted as having a gluten-free option available

restaurant.name: Persephone Brewing
restaurant.desc: Persephone Brewing is a certified B Corp farm brewery on BC's Sunshine Coast, running a working five-acre farm — barley fields, apple orchards, market gardens, and laying hens — alongside its craft brewing operation. The on-site tasting room and kitchen serve multiple award-winning beers, including Canadian Brewing Award winners, made with farm-grown and locally sourced ingredients. Cyclists passing through Gibsons will find a genuinely distinctive farm-to-barrel stop with outdoor picnic areas and a community-rooted ethos.

restaurant.name: Brave Brewing Co
restaurant.desc: Brave Brewing Co is a craft brewery in North Vancouver serving its own beers on-site with outdoor seating. The taproom accepts Bitcoin Lightning and on-chain payments in addition to cash, making it notable for crypto-friendly cyclists. It operates most days of the week with evening hours, offering a relaxed stop after a ride in the North Shore mountains.

restaurant.name: Westholme Tea Farm
restaurant.desc: Westholme Tea Company is an 18-year-old organic tea operation on Vancouver Island's Cowichan Peninsula, operating a teashop inside a converted barn alongside a working tea garden with several hundred tea plants — one of Canada's very few commercial tea-growing operations. The shop carries over 150 organic loose-leaf teas, hand-blended tisanes, handbuilt ceramic teaware, and limited-harvest teas grown on the property itself. At least one visiting cyclist reported being greeted with a complimentary tea sample, making this an unusually characterful rest stop on the Vancouver Crossing Loop.

detail.address: 8350 Richards Trail, Duncan, BC V9L 6B2, Canada

restaurant.name: Deep Cove Winery
restaurant.desc: Deep Cove Winery is a family-owned estate winery nestled between Horth Hill Regional Park and the shores of Deep Cove in North Saanich on the Saanich Peninsula. With three acres of vines planted over 22 years ago, they produce hand-crafted wines including Ortega, Pinot Gris, Marechal Foch, and their signature Alchemy blend. The winery has a lounge with a full food menu and hosts regular events, making it a rewarding stop on a Saanich Peninsula ride.

detail.address: 11195 Chalet Road, North Saanich, BC V8L 5M1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes vegetarian options: Mediterranean Hummus Bowl, Baked Spinach & Artichoke Dip, Margherita Pizza

restaurant.name: Da Silva Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Da Silva Vineyards is a boutique family-owned winery on the Naramata Bench just north of Penticton, rooted in a Portuguese farming heritage brought to the South Okanagan in 1955. The property features an intimate seated tasting room where a winemaker guides small groups through terroir-driven wines drawn from six estate vineyards. An on-site restaurant, The Kitchen, offers unconventional fine dining with Mexican and Portuguese-inspired tapas, making it a potential rest-and-refuel destination for cyclists touring the Naramata Bench.

detail.address: 375 Upper Bench Road North, Penticton, BC V2A 8T2

restaurant.name: The Cumberland Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: A community-focused craft brewery on Dunsmuir Avenue in the village of Cumberland, a renowned mountain biking destination in the Comox Valley. Founded in 2014, it follows a hyper-local model with no distribution outside Cumberland, so the only way to taste their house-brewed beers is to visit in person. The globally inspired food menu and outdoor dog-friendly patio make it a natural gathering spot after a day on the trails.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu items labelled V (vegan), VO (vegan option), GF (gluten-free), GFO (gluten-free option), DF (dairy-free), DFO (dairy-free option); e.g. Coconut Red Thai Vegetable Curry is V, DF, GF

restaurant.name: Daydreamer Wines
restaurant.desc: Daydreamer Wines is a sustainable, family-run winery on the Naramata Bench founded by Rachel and Marcus Ansems, where Marcus holds the Master of Wine designation. The winery produces limited-batch wines without systemic pesticides, herbicides, or fungicides, earning multiple platinum and gold medals at the National Wine Awards of Canada including Best Red Wine in Canada in 2019. Cyclists on the Naramata Bench can book a tasting at the on-site Wine Shack and purchase bottles to take away.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Winemaking philosophy page states: 'Vegan Friendly — All of our wines are made without animal products or byproducts.'

restaurant.name: Pentage Winery
restaurant.desc: Pentâge Winery is a family-owned estate on 23 acres overlooking Skaha Lake, producing small-batch, handcrafted wines from their Skaha Bench vineyards since their inaugural 1999 vintage. The property features a striking 5,000-square-foot natural rock wine cellar hand-built by founder Paul Gardner, and a tasting room with panoramic views of the lake and surrounding vineyards. It sits just outside Penticton on Valleyview Road, making it a natural waypoint on the South Okanagan wine route.

restaurant.name: Britannia Brewing
restaurant.desc: Britannia Brewing Co is a craft brewery with taprooms across the Lower Mainland and Okanagan, producing a nautically themed lineup of ales, lagers, and sours. The Richmond presence is described on the website as a bar and restaurant in Steveston Village, a historic fishing village popular with cyclists riding the Steveston Dyke trail. The brewery's range spans sessionable lagers and blond ales through hoppy IPAs and dark porters.

restaurant.name: Hillside Winery
restaurant.desc: Hillside Winery has been producing award-winning wines on the Naramata Bench since 1984, making it one of the area's longest-running wineries. The on-site Bistro serves terroir-to-table small plates with locally foraged ingredients in a 65-seat dining room and on two outdoor patios overlooking Okanagan Lake. Located on Naramata Road—a cornerstone of Okanagan cycling—it is a natural refreshment stop for touring cyclists riding the Bench.

restaurant.name: Victoria Distillers
restaurant.desc: A small-batch craft distillery on the Sidney waterfront, producing award-winning gins including the well-known Empress 1908 Indigo Gin. The retail space offers complimentary tastings and bottle purchases, making it a worthwhile stop for cyclists riding through the Saanich Peninsula. The copper pot stills and waterfront setting give the visit a sense of place beyond a typical liquor store.

restaurant.name: Festina Lente Estate Winery and Meadery
restaurant.desc: Festina Lente is a 5-acre family-run hobby farm in Langley's wine country, specializing in award-winning mead and honey wines crafted by beekeepers-turned-winemakers Bill and Teresa. The farm hosts a covered, heated patio with walk-in tastings, free live music events, and a weekend food truck serving flatbreads, gourmet hot dogs, charcuterie boards, and high tea boxes. Touring cyclists with dogs are explicitly welcomed, and the winery's Renaissance Faire and seasonal events make it a distinctive rural stop on any Langley route.

restaurant.name: Luppolo Brewing
restaurant.desc: Luppolo Brewing is a Vancouver craft brewery and tasting room inspired by the convivial atmosphere of the Italian birrificio, operating for nearly a decade at 1123 Venables St. in the Grandview-Woodland neighbourhood. The brewery produces a wide and rotating range of craft beers — from pilsners and lagers to sours, stouts, and IPAs — and partners with Local Pizzaiolo for hand-stretched authentic Italian pizzas made fresh daily. A seasonal dog-friendly patio and fully wheelchair-accessible space make it a welcoming stop for cyclists exploring Vancouver's east side.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu marks items with (v) for vegetarian and (vegan) for vegan (e.g. Marinara VEGAN, The Spicy Vegan pizza, Veggie Platter vegan/gf option). FAQ confirms GF drink options (wine, cocktails, gluten-free beer, cider) and GF-friendly food substitutions

restaurant.name: Lightning Rock Winery
restaurant.desc: Lightning Rock Winery is an estate winery perched above Okanagan Lake with sweeping views down to Penticton, producing award-winning wines from several distinct Summerland-area vineyards. The tasting room is known for its warm, unpretentious hospitality from hands-on owners, and outdoor tasting options make it a natural rest stop on the Naramata Bench cycling circuit. A wine shop on-site lets cyclists pick up bottles to go.

restaurant.name: Wildeye Brewing
restaurant.desc: Wildeye Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom on the North Shore, a short ride from the Iron Workers Memorial Bridge cycling corridor. The house lineup spans award-winning Czech Pilsner, hazy IPAs, sours, and stouts, alongside an entirely non-alcoholic Easy Series for riders staying dry. The taproom hosts regular live music and trivia nights, offers a full bistro menu, and can accommodate private events for up to 75 guests.

detail.address: 1385 Main Street, North Vancouver, BC V7J 1C4

restaurant.name: Unsworth Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Unsworth Vineyards is a family-owned estate winery founded by the Turyk family in 2009 on a historic early-1900s farmhouse property in the Cowichan Valley, celebrated as 'Canada's Provence.' The estate produces coastal Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, sparkling wines, and expressive whites shaped by a rare rain-shadow microclimate on southern Vancouver Island. Cyclists riding the Cowichan Valley corridor will find a welcoming tasting room only 45 minutes from Victoria, set among rolling vineyards overlooking the Salish Sea.

restaurant.name: Noble Ridge Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Noble Ridge Vineyards is a family-founded estate winery perched on a ridge above Okanagan Falls in the South Okanagan wine country, offering stunning vineyard views and curated tastings of its award-winning sparkling, white, rosé, and red wines. The tasting room features a five-wine flight experience and a retail wine shop, with tasting fees donated to community causes. The property also hosts seasonal food-and-wine pairing events and offers on-site accommodations, making it a scenic destination for cyclists exploring the South Okanagan wine route.

detail.address: 2320 Oliver Ranch Road, Okanagan Falls, BC V0H 1R2

restaurant.name: Glenora Store and Cafe
restaurant.desc: Glenora Farm is a biodynamic, life-sharing community near Duncan on Vancouver Island where adults with developmental disabilities live and work alongside caregivers as part of the international Camphill movement. The farm produces organic vegetables, candles, and other workshop goods, some of which are sold at local markets. The website describes the property as people's private homes where visitor access requires advance approval.

restaurant.name: Lulu Island Winery
restaurant.desc: A family-owned winery on Westminster Highway in Richmond with a retail shop and tasting room. They produce award-winning wines using grapes grown on their own farmland on Lulu Island. A welcoming stop along the flat Richmond cycling corridors, with events like paint nights and bingo alongside regular tastings.

detail.address: 16880 Westminster Hwy, Richmond BC Canada V6V 1A8

restaurant.name: Zanatta Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Zanatta Estate Winery holds the distinction of being Vancouver Island's first estate winery, farming 25 acres in the Glenora area of the Cowichan Valley for over half a century. The family-run operation specializes in Champagne-style sparkling wines made entirely from estate-grown fruit across sparkling, white, rosé, and red styles. Cyclists can linger on the verandah with a glass, join wine club events, or pick up bottles to bring home from this heritage stop in a region celebrated for cycle touring.

restaurant.name: Sons of Vancouver
restaurant.desc: Sons of Vancouver is an independently owned craft distillery on Vancouver's North Shore, founded in 2015 and now centered on a flavour-driven rye whisky program fermented, distilled, and matured entirely on-site. The tasting room offers hand-crafted cocktails made with in-house spirits alongside retail bottle sales, making it a distinctive destination stop rather than a mid-ride refuel. Originally known for its No. 82 Amaretto, the distillery has pivoted to becoming a serious rye whisky producer with limited special releases that often sell out within a day.

restaurant.name: Riley's Cidery
restaurant.desc: Riley's Cidery sits in a remarkable one-of-a-kind heirloom apple orchard on Bowen Island containing nearly a thousand varieties, planted over 30 years by collectors John and Josephine Riley. Visitors can taste craft ciders made from these heritage apples and enjoy a picnic area overlooking the orchard.
