The cidery is run by Christine and Rob, who took over stewardship of this living museum in 2019 and trained in traditional English cidermaking.

detail.address: 620 Laura Road, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G2

restaurant.name: Gillespie's Fine Spirits
restaurant.desc: Gillespie's Fine Spirits is a craft distillery based in Squamish, BC, producing small-batch spirits in one of the Sea-to-Sky corridor's most bike-friendly towns. Touring cyclists passing through Squamish may find it a worthwhile stop to pick up locally made liquor. As a craft producer it likely offers a tasting room or retail counter, though this could not be confirmed from available data.

restaurant.name: Blue Mountain Winery
restaurant.desc: Blue Mountain Vineyard and Cellars is a family-owned estate winery in Okanagan Falls that has been producing cool-climate wines since 1991, with all grapes grown on a single contiguous site farmed by the Mavety family for nearly 50 years. The winery focuses on minimal-intervention, terroir-driven wines — sparkling, Pinot Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris, and reds — with hand-picked, gravity-racked fruit. Tastings are reservation-only and the winery hosts occasional events at the estate and around the broader Okanagan region.

detail.address: 2385 Allendale Road, Okanagan Falls, BC V0H 1R2

restaurant.name: Brittannia Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Britannia Brewing Co. is a nautically-themed craft brewery operating a Brewery & Tap House in Lake Country near Kelowna, one of several BC locations. Their lineup spans West Coast IPAs, farmhouse saisons, Gose-style watermelon sours, oatmeal stouts, and classic lagers — all with ocean-inspired names. The Lake Country tap house sits in the heart of the Okanagan's popular cycling corridor connecting Kelowna-area wineries and trails.

restaurant.name: Merridale Cidery & Distillery
restaurant.desc: Merridale is a family-owned, woman-led farm cidery and distillery on a 20-acre orchard in the Cowichan Valley, crafting award-winning ciders and spirits for over 30 years. The property functions as a full farm destination with a farmhouse eatery, farm store, guided tastings, distillery tours, yurt accommodations, and seasonal events. Touring cyclists can settle in for a meal or tasting in an orchard setting, with dogs welcome on leash throughout the grounds and patio.

detail.address: 1230 Merridale Road, Cobble Hill, B.C. V8H 1A1

restaurant.name: Off The Rail
restaurant.desc: Off The Rail Brewing is an East Vancouver craft brewery with a tasting room sitting directly on the Adanac bike path, one of Vancouver's primary cycling corridors. The tasting room pours 10–12 of the brewery's own beers across 15 taps — including 3 nitro taps — and serves light food such as Jamaican patties, potato pea samosas, and grilled cheese sandwiches. The brewery also produces Bine Sparkling Hop Water, a non-alcoholic, hop-infused sparkling water for alcohol-free riders.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Tasting room page lists 'Potato pea Samosas' as a food item, which is an inherently vegetarian option. No explicit vegan or GF claims are made

restaurant.name: Copper Spirit Distillery
restaurant.desc: Copper Spirit Distillery is a family-run boutique craft distillery on Bowen Island, founded by Miguel and Candice Kabantsov, who spent over five years building it from the ground up. Using German copper stills, organic BC grain, and pure West Coast water, they handcraft vodka, gin, rye and wheat whisky, and other spirits. The tasting room serves a seasonal cocktail menu made entirely from fresh organic ingredients, including sugar-free and alcohol-free options.

detail.address: 441 Bowen Island Trunk Rd, Bowen Island, British Columbia V0N 1G0

restaurant.name: Deol Family Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Deol Family Estate Winery is a family-owned estate operation on an 18-acre vineyard in North Cowichan, growing vines since 1984 and producing wines entirely from estate-grown grapes—Pinot Gris, Pinot Noir, Marechal Foch, and Gamay Noir—with all steps from harvest to bottling done on-site. Touring cyclists can stop at the tasting room and wine shop, and a patio picnic area with tables invites visitors to bring their own lunch and linger over a glass amid vineyard scenery. The winery also sells wines online and at the Cowichan Farmer's Market.

restaurant.name: Central City Brewers & Distillers
restaurant.desc: Central City Brewers & Distillers has been producing award-winning craft beers and spirits in Surrey since 2003, with well-known brands including Red Racer, Beer League, and the non-alcoholic Street Legal. Their Bridgeview Drive location houses the production brewery alongside a massive 10,000 sq ft retail liquor store carrying one of BC's largest selections of beer, wine, and spirits. The facility also accommodates event and group bookings.

restaurant.name: Strange Fellows Brewing
restaurant.desc: Strange Fellows is an East Vancouver craft brewery known for blending old-world tradition with West Coast innovation, with a particular focus on sour, barrel-aged, and vintage limited releases alongside a broad roster of hoppy ales, stouts, pilsners, and Belgians. The tasting room on Clark Drive pours a rotating tap list that also includes cider, wine, and a non-alcoholic IPA, backed by a full snack-and-panini food menu sourced from a local bakery. Cyclists looking to stock up can fill growlers from most taps or shop packaged cans and bottles to carry on the road.

notes.Takeout: Growler fills available for all beers except those marked 'by the glass only'; cans and bottles sold via the 'SHOP STRANGE FELLOWS' online store linked in site navigation
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu explicitly includes a Veggie Panini (pesto mayo, roasted cherry tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, arugula on ciabatta) plus vegetarian-friendly snacks (Mediterranean Olives, Cheezy Chipotle Popcorn, Tater Tots, Loaded Nachos). No explicit vegan or gluten-free claims on the website

restaurant.name: Blue Grouse Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Blue Grouse Estate Winery is one of the oldest vineyards on Vancouver Island, a sustainably farmed and award-winning estate situated in the southern Cowichan Valley about 8 kilometres south of Duncan and roughly 1 kilometre west of the Trans-Canada Highway. The winery produces a full range — sparkling, white, rosé, red, and dessert wines — and welcomes visitors for tastings and tours by reservation, with dogs permitted on site. It sits in the heart of a celebrated cycling and wine region, making it a natural destination stop on a Cowichan Valley tour.

restaurant.name: Cobble Hill Winery
restaurant.desc: Cobble Hill Winery is a regenerative-farming estate winery in the heart of the Cowichan Valley, producing cool-climate varietals under the guidance of winemaker Dylan Sheldon alongside proprietors Steve and Tricia. Visitors are welcome to taste wines led by tasting-room staff with views over the vineyard and lavender fields, and are encouraged to bring a picnic to enjoy with a bottle on the garden patio. The winery also participates in the Cowichan Valley Wine Festival and hosts weddings and private events, making it a genuine destination stop rather than a simple tasting counter.

detail.address: 3500 Telegraph Rd, Cobble Hill, BC V8H 0E1

restaurant.name: Calona Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Calona Vineyards is listed as a winery and on-site alcohol retail shop on Richter Street in Kelowna, operating under Andrew Peller Limited, one of Canada's largest premium wine producers with estate properties across the Okanagan. The Richter Street location places it within Kelowna's city core, potentially accessible to cyclists touring the region. Andrew Peller's BC estate properties are recognized within the tourism and hospitality industry for wine and dining experiences.

restaurant.name: Blind Tiger Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Blind Tiger Vineyards is a family-owned, seasonal winery in Lake Country's Okanagan wine country offering wine tastings by appointment, a lively outdoor patio with lake views, and wood-fired pizza from Marno's. The vineyard leans into a spirit of inclusivity and good vibes, hosting regular live-music events, a drag show series, and welcoming pets and families alike. A Tiger Trunk Gift Shop sells branded merch and canned goods alongside a lineup of naturally grown, chemical-free estate wines.

detail.address: 11014 Bond Road, Lake Country, BC V4V 1J6

restaurant.name: Mount Boucherie Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Mount Boucherie Estate Winery is a long-established Okanagan estate winery farming vines since 1968, now anchored by a striking 15,000 sq ft Wine Experience Centre designed by Ciccozzi Architects and opened in 2020. The property combines a daily tasting room, award-winning estate wines across five tiers, and The Modest Butcher Kitchen + Market — a farm-to-table restaurant with full bar service and a rooftop patio overlooking the lake. For a touring cyclist cutting through Okanagan wine country, it offers a full stop with food, wine, and sweeping valley views at the foot of a former volcano.

detail.address: 829 Douglas Road, West Kelowna, BC V1Z 1N9

restaurant.name: Russell Brewing
restaurant.desc: Russell Brewing Company is a Richmond-based craft brewery that has been producing beer since 1995, making it one of BC's longer-running independent craft operations. Their lineup spans styles from a citrusy Pale Ale and hop-forward Punch Bowl IPA to a traditionally malt-forward Angry Scotch Ale. Whether or not the facility has a public taproom, their beers are widely distributed to retailers across the region.

restaurant.name: Tofino Distillery
restaurant.desc: A small-batch craft distillery in Tofino's industrial area, handcrafting certified organic spirits from BC grain and Meares Island watershed water. The tasting room offers mini-cocktail samplers from a rotating lineup that includes gin, vodka, absinthe, whiskey, and limoncello, plus grab-and-go kombucha and craft tonics.

detail.address: 681 Industrial Way, Unit G & H, Tofino, BC V0R 2Z0

restaurant.name: CedarCreek Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Award-winning estate winery on Lakeshore Road overlooking Lake Okanagan, known for cool-climate Pinot Noir and sustainable farming practices including cover crops and Scottish Highland cattle. Features the Home Block Restaurant with a wine-first menu showcasing Okanagan produce, plus guided wine tastings and vineyard tours.

restaurant.name: Damali Wine & Lavender Farm
restaurant.desc: A working vineyard and lavender farm in the Cowichan Valley, producing cool-climate varietals with winemaker Dylan Sheldon and operating under the Cobble Hill Winery brand. Visitors are welcomed for guided tastings in the tasting room and are encouraged to bring a picnic to enjoy on the garden patio overlooking the vineyard and lavender fields. The scenic rural setting and patio make it a memorable stop for cyclists touring the Cowichan Valley.

detail.address: 3500 Telegraph Rd, Cobble Hill, BC V8H 0E1

restaurant.name: Red Truck Beer Company
restaurant.desc: Red Truck Beer Company is a Vancouver craft brewery and taproom whose name and identity are built around a nostalgic working-truck aesthetic. Located near the Vancouver Crossing Loop route, it is a destination-worthy stop for cyclists seeking local beer and a sit-down break. No further details about the space or experience could be confirmed due to website inaccessibility.

detail.address: 295 E 1st Ave, Vancouver, BC V5T 1A7, Canada

restaurant.name: Rewind Beer Co
restaurant.desc: Rewind Beer Co is a space-time-travel-themed craft brewery and tasting room housed in an industrial building, pouring its own rotating lineup of lagers, IPAs, sours, and saisons alongside guest taps and cider. The taproom doubles as 'Home of Pizza,' serving wood-fired-style pies made in-house with creative toppings and online ordering available. A touring cyclist would find a full sit-down destination with food, craft beer, and a lively atmosphere in Port Moody's industrial corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Pizza menu includes at least two vegetarian options: CHEEEEESE (Basil, Olive Oil, Housemade Marinara, Mozzarella) and THE SHROOMINATOR (Roasted Mushrooms, Caramelized Onions, Truffle Aioli, Scallion Oil, Mozzarella). No vegan or GF options explicitly noted

restaurant.name: Vivezza Vineyard
restaurant.desc: Vivezza Vineyard is a family-owned boutique winery on Salt Spring Island, built on over two decades of research into disease-resistant grape varieties suited to BC's coastal climate. The estate produces two distinct lines: a Traditional Series from old-vine vinifera on Salt Spring and Vancouver Islands, and an innovative Modern Series featuring newly developed disease-resistant varieties grown on the estate itself. The cellar door offers direct wine sales and tastings, making it a genuine destination stop on one of BC's most scenic cycling islands.

detail.address: 1625 North End Road, Salt Spring Island, V8K 1C6

restaurant.name: Four Winds
restaurant.desc: Four Winds Brewing is a BC craft brewery focused on bold West Coast and European-style beers, operating a full taproom in the Tilbury industrial area of Delta. The taproom doubles as a taco shop and casual restaurant, making it a solid mid-ride destination for cyclists looking for a meal alongside a pint. A second Beach House location in Tsawwassen offers another option for cyclists riding the south Delta and Tsawwassen routes.

restaurant.name: 8th Generation Vineyard
restaurant.desc: 8th Generation Vineyard is a family-owned estate winery in Summerland operated by Bernd and Stefanie Schales, who brought eight generations of German winemaking heritage to the Okanagan Valley when they arrived in 2003. The winery produces small-batch, estate-grown wines using sustainable, additive-free methods from vineyards they manage entirely themselves. Cyclists passing along Highway 97 can visit the farmhouse wine shop for tastings and to pick up a bottle.

restaurant.name: Wheelhouse Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Wheelhouse Brewing Company is a craft brewery and full-service restaurant established in 2013, now housed inside Prince Rupert's original train station—a heritage landmark with 270° harbour views and an authentic Italian wood-fired pizza oven burning local red alder. Self-described as 'the wettest brewery in Canada,' it sits at the northern terminus of BC's Yellowhead Highway cycling corridor and serves award-winning craft beers alongside a rotating menu of wood-fired pizzas and coastal-inspired food.

detail.address: 380 Bill Murray Drive, Prince Rupert, V8J 4P5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists [GF] and [DF] tags throughout; dedicated Vegetariana pizza (artichokes, roasted peppers, goat cheese, spinach); website notes 'items marked [GF][DF] can be made that way upon request.'

restaurant.name: Caffe Divano
restaurant.desc: Caffe Divano Port Moody is a community-oriented café nestled in the Klahanie neighbourhood, a short walk from Rocky Point Park and connected to St. John's Street via a pedestrian overpass. It was the founding location of the Divano family of cafés, opened in 2008 by Patrick and Lisa Beecroft with a vision of a true neighbourhood gathering spot decorated with local art. All baked goods are sourced from the Beecrofts' sister business, Gabi & Jules Handmade Pies & Baked Goodness, which also employs individuals with autism.

detail.address: 101-101 Klahanie Drive, Port Moody, BC V3H 0C3

restaurant.name: North Point Brewing
restaurant.desc: North Point Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and tasting room in Lower Lonsdale's Shipyards District in North Vancouver, founded by three North Shore locals inspired by West Coast cabin culture. The taproom pours a rotating roster of house-brewed beers spanning session lagers to high-ABV IPAs, alongside in-house pizza and snacks. An elevated loft with views of the North Shore and Downtown Vancouver is available for private events.

detail.address: 266 East 1st Street, North Vancouver, BC V7L 1B3

restaurant.name: Averill Creek Vineyard
restaurant.desc: Averill Creek Vineyard is an estate winery on the slopes of Mount Prevost in the Cowichan Valley, founded in 2001 and farming 30 acres of vines using organic and biodynamic principles. The winery is known for low-intervention, cool-climate wines made with techniques like wild fermentation, foot-stomping, and whole-bunch fermentation. Touring cyclists can stop at the tasting room for wine flights served on a garden terrace, seasonal snacks including vegan options, and bottles to take away from the wine shop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Snack menu lists 'VEGAN HUMMUS - Pickles' Pantry carrot & cashew hummus, olives, tapenade, crackers' as an explicitly vegan option

restaurant.name: Farm Gate Winery
restaurant.desc: Farm Gate Winery is a lovingly restored heritage orcharding homestead perched above Skaha Lake on Highway 97 in Kaleden, roughly ten minutes south of Penticton. The property produces an award-winning portfolio of both traditional Okanagan grape wines and distinctive fruit wines made from estate-grown cherries, peaches, apricots, and plums, all produced and bottled on-site. A rustic tasting room, a back patio with sweeping views of Skaha Lake and surrounding orchards, and an attached fruit stand selling heirloom Okanagan produce make it a genuinely memorable roadside stop for cyclists riding the Skaha Lake corridor.

restaurant.name: Backroads Brewery
restaurant.desc: Backroads Brewing is an award-winning craft brewery founded in 2017 on historic Baker Street in downtown Nelson, BC, producing small-batch ales and lagers with a constantly rotating tap list. The taproom showcases local art and a patio, giving it a character the website describes as 'unique to Nelson.' Food is available on-site through a partnership with The Block Railtown sandwich menu plus bar snacks, and beer can be taken away via growler fill or online order.

restaurant.name: Arrowleaf Cellars
restaurant.desc: Arrowleaf Cellars is an estate winery in Lake Country (Winfield) in the heart of the Okanagan, named after the arrowleaf wildflower native to its vineyards. The property features a tasting room, a picnic and patio area, and rotating food truck days, making it a multi-sensory stop on BC's wine route. Touring cyclists exploring the Okanagan's Camp Road corridor would find it a scenic and well-established destination for local wine and seasonal bites.

restaurant.name: Red Collar Brewing
restaurant.desc: Red Collar Brewing is a craft brewery and distilling operation in downtown Kamloops, running its taproom alongside the in-house Gin Lane Distillery. The space is divided into a main taproom, a dog-friendly fireplace room, and a summer patio with a combined capacity of up to 140 guests. An open BYOF (Bring Your Own Food) policy means cyclists can bring outside food to pair with house-brewed beers and gin cocktails, and growler fills are available for all beers on the menu.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Order beer for pick up or local delivery'; online ordering available for in-store pickup with no minimum order required, per /info-1

restaurant.name: Corcelettes Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Corcelettes Estate Winery is a 160-acre small-lot estate winery in the Similkameen Valley, consistently ranked in the Top 10 Small Wineries at the National Wine Awards of Canada. Visitors can experience curated wine flights seated on a scenic patio, shop estate wines in the on-site wine shop, or stay overnight at the Sunshot Vineyard Guest House. The winery's portfolio — Bordeaux varietals, Syrah, Pinot Noir, and Chardonnay — is grown entirely in the valley's distinctive stony, mineral-rich soils.

detail.address: 2582 Upper Bench Rd, Keremeos, BC V0X 1N4

restaurant.name: Emandare Vineyard
restaurant.desc: Emandare Vineyard is a boutique, family-run winery perched on a south-sloping hillside in the Cowichan Valley, overlooking Somenos Lake in the rain shadow of Mount Prevost on Vancouver Island. Founded by Mike and Robin Nierychlo, it produces low-intervention, organically dry-farmed, terroir-driven wines from estate and single-vineyard sources using old-world techniques. Visitors can drop into the wine shop for tastings, book a private tour with the winemaker, or take part in a unique wine-and-golf-simulator experience held in the barrel cellar.

restaurant.name: The Shed Cypress
restaurant.desc: The Shed is an open-air wood-fired pizza and coffee bar perched at Cypress Village, offering panoramic views stretching from Mount Baker to Vancouver Island. It operates year-round as a relaxed pop-up patio with no reservations — cyclists can simply roll up, grab a slice, and take in the mountain air. Come winter, it doubles as an après-ski venue with fire pits and seasonal cocktails.

detail.address: 3757 Cypress Bowl Rd, West Vancouver, BC

restaurant.name: Frequency Winery
restaurant.desc: Frequency Winery is a craft winery and alcohol retailer located on Gulley Road in Kelowna, in the heart of BC's Okanagan wine country. Touring cyclists riding the region's wine routes would find it a natural stop for local wine. Its combination of craft production and retail shop suggests visitors can purchase wine directly from the producer.

restaurant.name: Island Brew Byou
restaurant.desc: Island Brew Byou is a long-running (since 1999) brew-on-premise and homebrew supply shop on Station Avenue in Langford, where customers participate in making their own craft beer, wine, fruit wine, and sparkling cider using stainless steel, gas-fired kettles and 200+ product choices. The shop stocks an extensive range of homebrewing equipment and ingredients and is the only Victoria-area location brewing beer this way. It also sells packaged products — including gluten-free beer — to take home.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We now also have gluten-free beer options.'

restaurant.name: Storm Brewing
restaurant.desc: Storm Brewing is Vancouver's longest-running craft brewery, operating since 1994 on the lively Commercial Drive under founder and brewer James Walton. The brewery is celebrated for its ever-changing roster of inventive 'Brainstorm' small-batch beers — over 400 unique brews produced to date — all unfiltered, unpasteurized, and additive-free. Visitors enter through a loading door directly into an active working brewery, an experience that earned a 'Legendary local brewery' nod from Lonely Planet.

restaurant.name: A-Frame Brewing
restaurant.desc: A-Frame Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom in Squamish, BC, open since December 2016 and built around the nostalgia of BC lake cabin life — each beer is named after a beloved provincial lake. The spacious patio features a fire pit and resident food truck Flipside Burgers, and the BYO-food policy makes it a relaxed, accessible stop for hungry visitors. The brewery has earned multiple Canadian Brewing Awards, including Gold for its Arctic Lake Dark Lager at the 2023 nationals.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Resident food truck Flipside Burgers offers vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free burger options per website ('including ethical meats, vegetarian and vegan options as well as Gluten Free')

restaurant.name: Macaloney's Island Distillery and TWA Dogs Brewery
restaurant.desc: Macaloney's is Canada's most awarded craft distillery, producing award-winning single malt whiskies using traditional Scottish methods in hand-hammered Forsyth's copper pot stills. The same facility houses TWA Dogs Brewery, with craft beers brewed onsite including rotating seasonals. Touring cyclists can visit the tasting room to enjoy whisky flights, a pint of craft beer, or a behind-the-scenes distillery tour with the option to pour their own personalized whisky.

restaurant.name: Rocky Creek Winery
restaurant.desc: Rocky Creek Winery is a small family-run winery in Cowichan Bay, currently under new ownership by Jeremy and Susanna East, who took over from founders Mark and Linda (operating since 2005). Jeremy holds a WSET Level 3 award and is completing professional winemaking certification through UC Davis, bringing a craft-focused approach to the operation. The winery sells wines online, with a physical tasting room described as coming soon — making it an emerging destination on the Vancouver Island cycling circuit.

restaurant.name: Liquidity Wines
restaurant.desc: Liquidity Wines is an estate winery perched on a hillside in Okanagan Falls, overlooking Vaseux Lake and the iconic McIntyre Bluff, with curated art installations woven throughout the property. Cyclists can stop for wine tastings in the tasting room, share plates in the Tapas Room, or book a night at The Loft on-site accommodation. The winery sits in the heart of the South Okanagan wine country, a region well-travelled by touring cyclists on the Naramata and Okanagan Falls circuits.

detail.address: 4720 Allendale Road, Okanagan Falls, BC V0H 1R2

restaurant.name: Meadow Vista Honey Wines
restaurant.desc: Meadow Vista Honey Wines is a working meadery and artisan farm on a 5.5-acre property nestled among the orchards of East Kelowna, producing award-winning honey wines (meads) from the honey of 150 on-site beehives. The farm offers walk-in tastings, guided bee tours, and a seasonal farm-to-table bistro with outdoor patio and gazebo seating. It is a distinctive stop in Okanagan wine country, offering something genuinely different from the region's many grape wineries.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms all wines are gluten-free except Pictish Beast Braggot; bistro menu includes a vegetarian panini option

restaurant.name: The Masthead Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Masthead Restaurant is a waterfront dining destination in Cowichan Bay on Vancouver Island, historically known for seafood and regional cuisine in a harbour-side setting. It sits along the Vancouver Crossing Loop route, making it a potential stop for touring cyclists exploring the Cowichan Valley. Its current operating status is unclear based on prominent closure notices on its website.

restaurant.name: Seastar Estate Farm and Vineyard
restaurant.desc: Sea Star Vineyard and Winery is a boutique estate winery on Pender Island in BC's Gulf Islands, recognized by Sip Northwest as one of the '9 Wineries to Visit Before You Die.' The 26-acre terraced vineyard climbs to the summit of Mount Menzies, and the cedar-and-stone tasting room opens onto outdoor seating with views of the surrounding forest and vines. In summer months a local food truck is on site, and the winery produces limited-run coastal whites, rosés, and light reds using minimal-intervention methods.

detail.address: 6621 Harbour Hill, Pender Island, BC V0N 2M1

restaurant.name: Fitzpatrick Family Vineyards at Greata Ranch
restaurant.desc: Fitzpatrick Family Vineyards at Greata Ranch is a historic lakeside winery on Highway 97 between Peachland and Summerland, specializing in Traditional Method sparkling wines made from estate-grown grapes on a site that has grown fruit since 1901. The property features a wine shop patio with panoramic Okanagan Lake views and the 19 Bistro serving lunch. It sits on a quiet bench above the lake, making it a scenic mid-ride stop for cyclists touring the Okanagan Valley.

restaurant.name: Fort Berenes Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Fort Berens Estate Winery is Lillooet's first winery, established in 2009 on sagebrush-covered benchland along the Fraser River at the foot of the Coast Mountains — a striking high-desert setting unlike any other BC wine region. The tasting room sits above the vineyard with panoramic views and no reservations required for drop-in visits. The winery sits at the halfway point of the scenic Coast Mountain circle tour via Highways 99, 12, and 1, making it a natural destination stop for cyclists traveling between Whistler and the BC interior.

restaurant.name: Lake Breeze Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Lake Breeze Vineyards is a family-owned estate winery on the Naramata Bench above Lake Okanagan, with vines first planted in 1985 that rank among the oldest on the bench. The property features The Patio Restaurant serving seasonally inspired, locally sourced plates designed to pair with their estate wines, as well as a daily-open wine shop and tasting room. Located just minutes from both Naramata village and Penticton, it sits directly on one of BC's most celebrated cycling corridors.

restaurant.name: Barn Owl Brewing
restaurant.desc: Barn Owl Brewing is a community-focused craft brewery housed in a beautifully restored 1920s Surtees family dairy barn on Kelowna's Lakeshore Road, listed on the BC Ale Trail. The brewery is BC Green Business Certified, uses a water-efficient BREWHA system, and feeds spent grain to a local cattle farm. Touring cyclists will find 20+ small-batch beers alongside rotating food trucks (wood-fired pizza and handmade ramen), plus a lively weekly events calendar featuring live music and a run club.

restaurant.name: The 101 Brewhouse + Distillery
restaurant.desc: The 101 Brewhouse + Distillery has been the community gathering spot in Upper Gibsons since 2017, brewing award-winning craft beers — including a 2022 BC Beer Awards first-place lager — and distilling small-batch gin and vodka made from BC-grown ingredients. The kitchen turns out a broad menu of locally-inspired dishes alongside the taps, and the venue runs a steady calendar of live music, trivia nights, and themed events. For a touring cyclist arriving on the Sunshine Coast, it offers a full sit-down meal with vegetarian and gluten-free options plus online ordering for takeaway.

detail.address: 1009 Gibsons Way, Gibsons, British Columbia, V0N 1V8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu marks Santa Fe Salad and Nachos as (GF); Gyoza offered in a Vegetarian option; site states 'Our menu covers most dietary requirements.'

restaurant.name: The Kitchen Dada
restaurant.desc: The Kitchen Dada is a sushi bar and grill on Alma Street in Vancouver's Point Grey neighbourhood, close to the Vancouver Crossing Loop route. The restaurant posts daily takeout specials and offers online ordering and delivery alongside dine-in service. It is an accessible neighbourhood spot for a quick sushi meal mid-ride.

restaurant.name: Therapy Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Therapy Vineyards is a boutique winery situated on the Naramata Bench, one of British Columbia's most celebrated wine touring routes. Walk-in tastings are welcome for individuals and small groups, making it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the area. The winery operates its own ecommerce platform and tasting room booking system, suggesting a well-established visitor experience.

detail.address: 940 Lower Debeck Road, Naramata, BC V0H 1N1

restaurant.name: Ripples Winery & New Wave Distilling
restaurant.desc: Ripples Winery & New Wave Distilling is a family-run estate on 12 acres of organic blueberry fields in the Fraser Valley, combining a winery and craft distillery in a lush garden setting with ponds, tropical plants, and shaded patios. The operation produces organic blueberry wines, BC grape wines, and handcrafted small-batch spirits—gins, vodkas, rums, and liqueurs—all from locally grown or sourced ingredients. Touring cyclists can settle into covered or open-air patio seating for a flight, a craft cocktail, or small bites in what the owners describe as a serene garden oasis.

restaurant.name: Okanagan Spirits Craft Distillery
restaurant.desc: Okanagan Spirits is Western Canada's original craft distillery, founded in 2004 and crafting internationally awarded spirits from 100% BC grain and fruit. The Kelowna location on Bernard Avenue features a tasting room, cocktail lounge, and patio open to drop-in visitors without a reservation. In 2025 the distillery swept the podium at the World Spirits Awards in Germany, earning the World-Class Distillery designation alongside 11 Gold and 5 Silver medals.

restaurant.name: Train Wreck Brewing
restaurant.desc: Train Wreck Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom that opened in Port Moody in 2024, producing unfiltered, full-flavoured beers — from hazy IPAs and hefeweizens to Belgian dubbels and dry Irish stouts — using time-honoured techniques and quality local ingredients. The sprawling yet intimate taproom doubles as an event venue with daily food vendors, bar games, and live music, making it a genuine community gathering place. The brewery also offers behind-the-scenes tours, adding an educational dimension for curious visitors.

detail.address: 3044 St Johns St, Port Moody, BC V3H 2C5

restaurant.name: Tofino Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Tofino Brewing Co. is a locally rooted craft brewery and taproom that has been part of the Tofino community since April 2011, brewing West Coast-inspired beers including a Kelp Stout made with locally harvested kelp and a seasonal Spruce Tree Ale conditioned with fresh spruce tips. The taproom offers an evolving roster of small-batch beers alongside ciders, non-alcoholic options, and wine, with an on-site food truck partner (Picnic at the Brewery) serving grilled sandwiches and local charcuterie on the front patio. Dogs are welcome on the patios and kids are allowed with an adult, making it a relaxed and inclusive destination for visiting cyclists.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website FAQ explicitly states 'IS YOUR BEER VEGAN? Yes!' No gluten-free or food-specific vegetarian/vegan claims found

restaurant.name: Dead Frog Brewery
restaurant.desc: Dead Frog Brewery is a Fraser Valley craft brewery that has been producing small-batch, unpasteurized beer for over 10 years, brewed just 50 feet from the tasting room taps. Their Langley tasting room pairs a rotating lineup of creative craft beers — from habanero hazy IPAs to peanut butter stouts — with a full food menu and a dog-friendly patio. Regular events including live music, themed brew competitions, and family-friendly afternoons make it a lively community stop in Langley's industrial corridor.

restaurant.name: Rewind Beer Co
restaurant.desc: Rewind Beer Co is a Port Moody brewery tasting room with a time-travel theme, pouring a rotating lineup of house-brewed craft beers alongside guest taps and ciders. The tasting room doubles as a pizza kitchen, serving creative wood-fired pies available for dine-in. It's a lively neighbourhood spot with a full non-alcoholic beverage selection and regular food features.

restaurant.name: Bad Dog Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Bad Dog Brewing Company is a craft micro-brewery tucked into the rural back roads of Sooke, BC, pouring 12 taps of house-brewed ales, IPAs, stouts, and seasonal specialties in an indoor tasting room, on a heated patio, or at outdoor picnic tables. An on-site Hot Diggity Dog food trailer rounds out the experience with hot food. Now celebrating its 8th year, the brewery hosts live music events and community fundraisers, making it a lively destination on the quieter roads west of Victoria.

restaurant.name: Arbutus Distillery
restaurant.desc: Arbutus Distillery is a BC-classified craft distillery in Nanaimo that brews, ferments, distils, and bottles all its spirits on-site using 100% BC-grown fermentables and many botanicals grown on the property. Its award-winning lineup includes Canadian Single Malt Whisky, Canadian Rye Whisky, brandy, absinthe, and gin. Visiting cyclists can sample and purchase bottles directly at the on-site Tasting Lounge, which also offers weekend cocktail service.

restaurant.name: Salt Spring Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Salt Spring Brewing Co. is a craft brewery tucked into the woods of Salt Spring Island, offering a tasting room and outdoor patio where visitors can sample core and seasonal beers. The brewery bills itself as 'a gem hidden in the woods' and hosts events including an annual Oktoberfest celebration. For cyclists touring the island, it serves as a scenic off-the-beaten-path destination to rest and enjoy locally made beer.

detail.address: 270 Furness Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 1Z7

restaurant.name: Waddling Dog
restaurant.desc: The Waddling Dog is an award-winning neighbourhood pub attached to the Quality Inn Waddling Dog hotel in Saanichton, serving classic pub dishes with a west coast twist alongside a full bar. An onsite beer, wine, and spirits shop rounds out the offering, making it a convenient stop near the BC Ferries Swartz Bay terminal and Butchart Gardens. It sits just off Highway 17 (Patricia Bay Hwy), a key artery for cyclists on the Saanich Peninsula.

detail.address: 2476 Mt. Newton X Road, Saanichton, British Columbia V8M 2B8

restaurant.name: Enrico Winery
restaurant.desc: Enrico Winery is a 100% local, family-owned BC winery set on a working vineyard in Mill Bay, offering drop-in tastings in their tasting room and across two outdoor patios. Dogs are welcome on the outdoor patio and the facilities are confirmed accessible. Wine is available to purchase and take away, and light snack items are available for on-site purchase.

restaurant.name: Kutatás Wines
restaurant.desc: Kutatás Wines is a small artisan winery with an open cellar door in Chemainus on Vancouver Island, where visitors can taste and purchase wines produced on-site. The food program is seasonal, but the winery actively encourages guests to bring a picnic to enjoy with their wines. Bottles can be purchased to take away or shipped within BC for those stocking up for the road.

restaurant.name: Summerhill Pyramid Winery
restaurant.desc: Summerhill Pyramid Winery is Canada's only Demeter-certified biodynamic vineyard, founded by the Cipes family in 1986 on 17 hectares above Okanagan Lake in Kelowna. The property is anchored by a replica Egyptian pyramid cellar built to sacred geometry proportions, used to age the winery's 100% organic wines. Cyclists can browse the retail wine shop, dine in the bistro with panoramic lake views, or arrange a tour of the pyramid — a genuinely singular stop in the Okanagan wine country.

detail.address: 4870 Chute Lake Road, Kelowna, BC V1W 4M3

restaurant.name: Truck 59 Cider House
restaurant.desc: Truck 59 Cider House is a craft cider tasting room perched along the West Kelowna wine trail with panoramic Okanagan Lake views, wide-open lawn space, and a laid-back family-friendly atmosphere. Part of the Jason Parkes Customs family of producers, it pours its own handcrafted ciders alongside beer from The Hatching Post, JPC wines, and cocktails in the newer adults-only Truck Yard section. A regular calendar of live music, food-truck pop-ups, and seasonal events makes it a lively stop on a West Kelowna ride.

detail.address: 2345 Boucherie Road, West Kelowna, BC V1Z 2E6

restaurant.name: Twin Island Cider
restaurant.desc: Twin Island Cider is an artisan cidery on North and South Pender Islands that harvests fruit from dozens of century-old settler orchards, fermenting exclusively with native yeasts to produce terroir-driven natural ciders and perries. Visitors are welcomed to an outdoor picnic area for drop-in tastings and cider by the glass, with current bottled releases available for purchase on-site. The cidery has been featured in Wine Enthusiast, Montecristo Magazine, and Cider Craft Magazine for its distinctive place-based approach to craft fermentation.

restaurant.name: R & B Brewing
restaurant.desc: R&B Brewing is one of Vancouver's original craft microbreweries, operating in the historic Brewery Creek district of East Vancouver since 1997. Their Ale & Pizza House taproom pairs house-brewed artisan ales and lagers — including award-winning staples like Raven Cream Ale and Stolen Bike Lager — with a full menu of pizzas, sandwiches, and salads crafted by an in-house chef. The space is dog-friendly on the patio, kids-welcome indoors, and driven by a strong community ethos with a live code of conduct and growler fills available for take-home beer.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states 'We have LOTS of vegan snacks, salads, sandwiches & PIZZAS!' and confirms GF snacks, salads, and sandwiches (though pizzas are not GF). Menu page explicitly labels most beer, cider, and mead items as 'Vegan' and marks some items (e.g. Banditry cider, Humblebee Meadery) as 'Gluten free Vegan'

restaurant.name: Bridge Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Bridge Brewing Company is a North Vancouver craft brewery operating a taproom and tasting room at its original Charlotte Road location, one of three Bridge Brewing venues across the North Shore. The taproom pours a rotating lineup of core and seasonal house beers, and the site also hosts a playful 'Bridge Arcade' experience. A keg rental program and private event space at a sister location round out the brewery's community presence.

restaurant.name: Garry Oaks Winery
restaurant.desc: Garry Oaks is a boutique, award-winning estate winery on Salt Spring Island where every grape is grown on-site across seven acres of vineyard. Current owner Nalini Samuel has expanded the program to include sparkling and dessert wines, and the winery operates with certified organic practices under the BC Environmental Farm Plan Program. Visitors can drop in for tastings, join a guided vineyard tour, and browse the on-site shop stocked with estate-bottled wines and locally sourced food and beverages.

detail.address: 1880 Fulford-Ganges Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2A5

restaurant.name: Kettle River Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Kettle River Brewing Company is a small-batch craft brewpub in downtown Kelowna's North End, running a 5-barrel in-house brewhouse with ten rotating draught taps since 2016. The kitchen is helmed by Food Network Canada Top Chef veteran Brock Bowes, producing a monthly-changing premium pub food menu crafted with the brewery's own beers in mind. The taproom is a self-described BIPOC and LGBTQ2S+ inclusive safe space with regular live music, trivia nights, and Sunday brunch.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'veggie burger option available' for the May burger item

restaurant.name: Luppolo Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Luppolo Brewing Company is a neighbourhood craft brewery and tasting room in Vancouver's East Side, inspired by the relaxed social culture of the Italian birrificio, pairing an extensive rotating tap list with hand-stretched authentic Italian pizzas made fresh daily in partnership with Local Pizzaiolo. The brewery has been a community gathering spot for nearly a decade, owned and shaped by two couples whose warmth sets the tone for the space. Touring cyclists will find dedicated bike parking, a full food menu, and a wide range of non-alcoholic and gluten-free drink options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu explicitly marks items (v), (vegan), (gf), and (gf option) throughout starters, pizzas, and salads. FAQ confirms gluten-free beer, wine, cider, and cocktails, plus non-alcoholic options including house sodas and coffee

restaurant.name: Quails' Gate Winery
restaurant.desc: Quails' Gate Estate Winery has been growing and crafting award-winning wines on Boucherie Road since 1989, when the Stewart family planted their first vines on this Okanagan Lake-side estate. The property combines a daily-open wine shop and guided tasting experiences with the acclaimed Old Vines Restaurant, offering farm-to-table cuisine alongside sweeping lake and vineyard views. On-site accommodations at The Lake House and The Nest make this a natural overnight destination for touring cyclists exploring the West Kelowna wine-route corridor.

detail.address: 3303 Boucherie Rd, West Kelowna, BC V1Z 2H3

restaurant.name: Hainle Vineyards Estate Winery Ltd.
restaurant.desc: Hainle Vineyards Estate Winery is BC's 8th estate winery, founded in 1972, and holds the distinction of being both the birthplace of North American Icewine and Canada's first certified organic winery (1988). The estate produces naturally handcrafted, chemical-free wines from its own Peachland vineyard using winemaking traditions dating to the mid-1800s. Touring cyclists can visit the wine shop for tastings and in-store purchases, and the property also offers a Bed & Breakfast for those looking to extend their stay in the Okanagan.

detail.address: 5355 Trepanier Bench Road, Peachland, BC V0H 1X2

restaurant.name: Gray Monk Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Gray Monk Estate Winery is one of British Columbia's pioneering wineries, established in 1972 when founders George and Trudy Heiss planted Canada's first Pinot Gris vines. The estate overlooks Okanagan Lake in Lake Country and features The Lookout Restaurant with lake views, wine tastings, and a shop. Touring cyclists on the Okanagan rail trail or lake loop will find it a scenic and rewarding stop for award-winning cool-climate wines and a sit-down meal.

detail.address: 1055 Camp Road, Lake Country, BC V4V 2H4

restaurant.name: Superflux Brewery
restaurant.desc: Superflux Beer Company is a craft brewery and taproom nestled between Strathcona and East Vancouver, specializing in IPA alongside a broader range of styles including lagers and pale ales. The brewery offers a full food menu with seating both indoors and on a covered patio, and operates an on-site beer store selling cans to go. The /home page title also identifies it as a dog-friendly brewery, which may appeal to cyclists travelling with pets.

restaurant.name: Angel Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Angel Estate Winery sits on Westham Island Road in the agricultural flatlands of the Fraser River delta, a scenic rural cycling area accessible from the Ladner area of Delta, BC. Tagged in OSM as both a craft winery and an alcohol shop, it appears to operate as an estate winery with on-site sales. The pastoral delta setting — dyke roads, farmland, and river views — makes it a natural waypoint for cyclists exploring the South Delta cycling network.

restaurant.name: Spinnakers
restaurant.desc: Spinnakers Gastro Brewpub is Canada's first purpose-built gastro brewpub, crafting beer on the Victoria waterfront since 1984 with views of the Inner Harbour. The site combines a pub-style restaurant, taproom, a covered and heated outdoor patio, and heritage guesthouses, all supported by house-brewed ales, ciders, and sours made with local ingredients. Touring cyclists can fuel up on locally-sourced seasonal fare and pick up growler fills from the on-site provisions store.

restaurant.name: Slow Hand Brewery
restaurant.desc: Slow Hand Beer Company is a small BC-licensed craft brewery that brews a constantly rotating selection of small-batch beers skewing toward lighter, crisper, and sessionable styles with creative twists on world beer traditions. Their retail store and tasting lounge are hosted within Threefold Brewery at 1507 Powell St in Vancouver's Strathcona neighbourhood. The two-person operation — one owner focused on sales, one on brewing — keeps things intimate and craft-forward.

restaurant.name: Gibsons Tapworks
restaurant.desc: A community-focused craft brewpub on the Sunshine Coast, brewing award-winning beers inspired by the coastal lifestyle since 2017. The patio overlooks Howe Sound and has been voted best patio by the Sunshine Coast People's Choice Awards. The on-site Burger Shack serves food seven days a week, making it a reliable refuelling stop for touring cyclists on the Sunshine Coast.

restaurant.name: Sternwheeler Craft Distillery
restaurant.desc: Sternwheeler Craft Distillery is an award-winning small-batch operation in downtown Creston producing spirits exclusively from locally grown fruit — saskatoons, apples, and other Creston Valley produce — with no grains, nuts, or artificial additives. Founded in 2017 as Wynndel Craft Distilleries, it relocated to a converted heritage building on Canyon Street in 2024 and opened a Lounge Bar in early 2025 stocked entirely with local beers, wines, ciders, and its own spirits. The distillery has accumulated multiple Canadian Artisan Spirit Competition honours including several Best in Class and Gold medals, making it a notable destination in the Kootenays.

restaurant.name: Cherry Point Estate Wines
restaurant.desc: Cherry Point Estate Wines is one of Vancouver Island's pioneering wineries, established in 1990 on 34 acres of a former mink ranch in the Cowichan Valley, and among the first licensed wineries on the island. Positioned along the Vancouver Island Wine Route about 50 km north of Victoria, it offers daily guided tastings of award-winning whites and reds — including notable dessert wines — with suggested pairings from knowledgeable staff. A seasonal bistro on a brick patio amid the vines serves West Coast-inspired lunches, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists on a multi-day tour.

detail.address: 840 Cherry Point Road, Cobble Hill, BC V0R 1L3

restaurant.name: Lang Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Lang Vineyards holds the distinction of being British Columbia's first farm-gate winery, founded by Guenther Lang in 1990 and home to the oldest vines on the Naramata Bench. Now in its 35th year, this boutique family estate produces a wide range from crisp whites and rosés to dessert wines, with tastings available by reservation. The Naramata Bench is one of the Okanagan's premier cycling corridors, and this historic winery sits directly along that route.

restaurant.name: Painted Rock Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Painted Rock Estate Winery is a family-owned operation perched on the eastern bench of Skaha Lake, producing ultra-premium terroir-driven wines from a 56-acre single-estate vineyard in the Okanagan Valley. The Skinner family has spent over 20 years crafting award-winning Bordeaux blends and single-varietal wines with the stated goal of raising the profile of Canadian wine internationally. A touring cyclist stopping here can visit the daily-open tasting room and take in sweeping views of Skaha Lake alongside tastings of some of Canada's most acclaimed estate wines.

restaurant.name: Black Swift Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Black Swift Vineyards is a single-vineyard winery perched in the hills of West Kelowna, part of the Jason Parkes Customs family of wineries and tasting rooms on the Westside. The tasting room is open daily with a casual, no-reservations-needed atmosphere, offering guided tastings and vineyard tours by golf cart. Named after the elusive Black Swift bird that lays just one egg per season, the winery emphasizes restraint and terroir-driven winemaking.

restaurant.name: Vancouver Urban Winery
restaurant.desc: Vancouver Urban Winery is a working urban winery and atmospheric event venue in Railtown, housed in a 1923 building featuring exposed Douglas fir beams and floor-to-ceiling barrels. Established in 2011, it produces its own label wines and pours a rotating selection of over 30 BC wines on tap. Casual visitors are welcome for wine flights and tastings alongside the private-event bookings that anchor the business.

restaurant.name: Beaumont Family Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Beaumont Family Estate Winery is a family-run boutique winery at the foot of Boucherie Mountain in West Kelowna, producing 100% certified-organic estate wines since 1995 across 36 acres of vineyards. The Lubchynski family crafts small-batch wines including Pinot Noir, Gamay Noir, skin-contact Pinot Gris, and icewine, with daughter Alana serving as winemaker after working vintages in Australia, New Zealand, and Europe. Cyclists on the Okanagan wine route can stop in for a tasting, pick up bottles to go, and take in 360-degree views of the surrounding mountain valley and lake.

detail.address: 2775 Boucherie Road, West Kelowna, BC V1Z 1N3

restaurant.name: Yellow Dog Brewing
restaurant.desc: Yellow Dog Brewing is a craft brewery that opened in Port Moody in 2014 and sits on Murray Street, the heart of the city's well-known Brewers Row. The tasting room serves daily snacks sourced from local bakeries and butchers alongside rotating food trucks throughout the week. In 2024 the brewery expanded with a second tasting room in Penticton.

detail.address: 2817 Murray Street, Port Moody, BC V3H 1X3

restaurant.name: Ramification Cellars
restaurant.desc: Ramification Cellars is an estate winery on the shores of Vaseux Lake near Penticton, producing wines exclusively from grapes grown on their own property with a focus on ecological stewardship of the Okanagan Valley. The winery offers tastings, a wine club, and event hosting in a scenic lakeside setting, making it a natural stop on the Okanagan wine route. Cyclists riding the area will find a tasting room with on-site washrooms and parking.

restaurant.name: Left Field Cider Co.
restaurant.desc: Left Field Cider Co. is a family-owned artisanal cidery making handcrafted English-style cider from blends of English, French, and BC dessert apples. Founded in 2011 by sisters Theresa and Kate on their family ranch at Mamette Lake, they converted a hayfield into an orchard and a barn into a ciderhouse. The tasting room is located on Hwy 97C between Merritt and Logan Lake, offering a seasonal stop for passing cyclists in BC's Interior.

restaurant.name: Twin City Brewery
restaurant.desc: Twin City Brewing Company is an award-winning craft brewery and full-service taproom in Port Alberni, crafting a rotating roster of beers—from West Coast IPAs and German pilsners to fruit sours—entirely on-site. The kitchen turns out scratch-made food including hand-stretched pizza, smoked meat sandwiches, tacos, and rice bowls, making it a genuine meal stop rather than just a tasting room. Positioned in the Alberni Valley as part of Port Alberni's emerging tourism and recreation identity, it serves as a lively community hub for both locals and visitors exploring Vancouver Island.

detail.address: 4503 Margaret Street, Port Alberni, British Columbia V9Y 6G8

restaurant.name: Rust Wine Co
restaurant.desc: Rust Wine Co. is a small-lot winery on the Golden Mile Bench — BC's first designated sub-appellation — sourcing from old-vine vineyards planted as far back as 1968. The tasting room offers sweeping views over the Black Sage Bench toward Osoyoos, and a restored 19th-century bunkhouse relocated from a silver mine serves as a unique vacation rental on the property. Weekly live music events through the season make it an animated stop along the South Okanagan winery route.

detail.address: 4444 Golden Mile Drive, Oliver, BC V0H 1T1

restaurant.name: White Tooth Brewery
restaurant.desc: Whitetooth Brewing Company is a craft brewery and tasting room established in 2016 in Golden, BC, nestled between the Purcell and Rocky Mountain ranges near the confluence of the Kicking Horse and Columbia Rivers. They specialize in award-winning Belgian-inspired and West Coast-influenced small-batch beers, with names like 'Speed Metal Foreign Extra Stout' and 'Blower Pow IPA' directly celebrating mountain biking and powder skiing culture. The tasting room has no in-house kitchen but has delivery partnerships with three local restaurants, positioning it as a welcoming post-ride stop in one of BC's premier adventure-sport hubs.

restaurant.name: Red Barn Winery
restaurant.desc: Red Barn Winery is a boutique winery situated on Black Sage Road in Oliver, squarely in the heart of South Okanagan wine country and along one of BC's most popular cycling corridors. Wines are sourced from Jagged Rock Vineyard and lean into bold fruit expression under an intentionally rebellious brand identity. The property hosts seasonal events including Tramonto Music Nights with live music on the patio, making it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the region.

detail.address: 4305 Black Sage Rd, Oliver, BC V0H 1T1

restaurant.name: Alberni Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Alberni Brewing Company is a craft brewery and full-service brewpub in the heart of Port Alberni, producing its own house beers alongside rotating guest taps, wine, and cider. The kitchen menu is extensive — drawing on local suppliers for specialty bakery and meat products — and intentionally complements the brewery side of the operation. Dog-friendly patios, varied indoor seating, and a welcoming atmosphere make it a practical rest stop for cyclists riding the Alberni Valley corridor toward the Pacific Rim.

detail.address: 4630 Adelaide Street, Port Alberni, British Columbia V9Y 6N4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian dishes: hummus & pita, cauliflower bites, truffle fries, poutine, nachos (meat is an add-on), avocado dip, frickles. No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Mt. Begbie Brewery
restaurant.desc: Mt. Begbie Brewery is an award-winning craft brewery that has been operating in Revelstoke, BC since 1996, making it one of the longest-running independent craft breweries in the province. The brewery features a tasting room and a retail store where cyclists can pick up packaged beer to go, alongside a food menu. Revelstoke's position as a gateway to mountain recreation makes this a natural stop for touring cyclists passing through town.

restaurant.name: Celista Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Celista Estate Winery is an 80-acre farm and vineyard on the north shore of Shuswap Lake in BC's interior, producing award-winning wines that have accumulated 115 medals over 14 years at national and international competitions. Visitors can take guided vineyard and winery tours, sample wines in the tasting room, dine at the on-site restaurant, rent one of four lakeside cabins, or attend a summer concert. The property is kid- and pet-friendly and wheelchair accessible, and the vineyard-and-lake panorama makes it a memorable destination stop.

restaurant.name: Celista Estate Winery Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: Celista Estate Winery is an 80-acre vineyard estate on the north shore of Shuswap Lake in BC's interior, with vines first planted in 2002 and over 115 medals accumulated in national and international competitions across its first 14 years. Beyond wine tasting, the property offers guided vineyard tours, fine dining, four lakeside cabin rentals, weddings, and a busy summer concert series — making it an unusually multi-faceted destination. Cyclists exploring the Shuswap's quieter north shore will find it a welcoming, pet- and family-friendly stop with sweeping vineyard and lake views.

restaurant.name: Mythology
restaurant.desc: Mythology is a boutique winery and distillery near Osoyoos in BC's South Okanagan, producing a range of reds, whites, rosés, and craft spirits including brandy, vodka, and gin. Visitors can book a guided tasting in the vineyard-side tasting room or linger in the pet-friendly picnic grounds over wine and charcuterie. The property also includes the Sonora Desert Inn, offering overnight accommodation surrounded by vineyard-lined hills and Okanagan valley views.

restaurant.name: Gladstone Brewery
restaurant.desc: Gladstone Brewing Co. is a BC Brewery of the Year award-winner set inside a converted mechanic's garage in the heart of downtown Courtenay, in the Comox Valley. It serves a full scratch-made menu from brunch through dinner alongside its European lagers, Pacific Northwest pale ales, and experimental small-batch beers. Two distinct indoor spaces — the lively Brewers Bar and the intimate Engine Room — plus a large outdoor patio make it a natural gathering spot for locals and travellers alike.

detail.address: Unit A - 244 4th Street, Courtenay, BC V9N 1G6

restaurant.name: Chaberton Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Chaberton Estate Winery is the Fraser Valley's oldest winery, founded in 1981 and set on a 55-acre vineyard in South Langley roughly 45 minutes from Vancouver. Visitors can take guided tours through the crush pad, tank room, and barrel cellar before tasting award-winning 100% BC VQA wines in the boutique tasting room or at outdoor picnic tables overlooking the vines. The on-site Bacchus Bistro serves authentic French-inspired cuisine made with local ingredients, making this a genuine wine-and-dine destination for touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

restaurant.name: Hidden Chapel Winery
restaurant.desc: A small boutique winery on the northern edge of the Great Basin Desert near Oliver, producing about 18,000 bottles per year. Wines are aged in a unique underground cellar overlooked by the namesake hidden chapel, and the tasting room is set among pines and gardens. Located only 5 km outside Oliver and 3 km from the District Wine Village, making it a feasible side trip for cyclists touring the South Okanagan wine country.

restaurant.name: Bordertown Cider & Winery
restaurant.desc: Bordertown Cider & Winery is a family-owned estate winery and cidery in the heart of Osoyoos, operated by the Gill family whose fifth-generation farming roots go deep in the South Okanagan. The winery produces 14 VQA-certified varietals from 100 acres of estate vineyards, including award-winning Cabernet Franc and Viognier, plus a craft hard apple cider pressed from their own orchard fruit. Visitors are welcomed into a Mission-style tasting room with no reservation required, making it an accessible stop on a wine-country cycling route.

restaurant.name: Angry Hen Brewing
restaurant.desc: Angry Hen Brewing is a craft brewery and lounge in the heart of historic Kaslo, BC, operating a 7-barrel brewhouse — one of the last built by Newlands — that produces a rotating lineup of lagers, ales, and a signature dry Irish stout on nitro. Originally founded in 2017 by brewer Shirley Warne, it is now owned by Cassie and Rogan, who continue the tradition of pairing quality craft beer with live music on a covered patio year-round. A welcoming stop for cyclists passing through the Kootenays, it positions itself as Kaslo's community living room with snacks, non-alcoholic drinks, and frequent local music events.

restaurant.name: Roots and Wings Distillery
restaurant.desc: Roots and Wings Distillery is Langley's first craft distillery, a family-owned farm operation near Fort Langley producing seed-to-sip spirits — including vodka, whiskey, gin, absinthe, and liqueurs — from ingredients grown on their own land. Visitors can sample craft cocktails, enjoy an in-house menu, and browse a bar gift shop stocked with artisan bottles to take away. The rural Fraser Valley setting and farm-to-glass story make it a distinctive destination on cycling routes through the Langley countryside.

restaurant.name: Land and Sea Brewery
restaurant.desc: Land & Sea Brewing Co. is a community-focused craft brewery and taproom in Comox, opened in December 2018 as the third craft brewery in the Comox Valley. The bright tasting room seats 70 guests with an open kitchen, and a sunny patio adds room for 40 more. The brewery actively encourages guests to arrive by bike or transit, noting its location steps from two BC Transit Route #1 bus stops.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Beer menu lists 'GLUTEN FREE BEER Whistler Forager Lager'; vegetarian/vegan options not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: Wilson Creek UBrew
restaurant.desc: Wilson Creek UBrew is the Sunshine Coast's longest-running Brew on Premise facility, established in 1993 and located in Wilson Creek halfway between Gibsons and Sechelt. Customers select and brew wine kits, craft beers, ciders, and hard seltzers in a purpose-built on-site facility, then return to bottle and take their finished beverages home. The business also offers an in-house cider line made from Okanagan apple juice and nine all-natural hard seltzer flavours.

restaurant.name: Robin Ridge Winery
restaurant.desc: Robin Ridge Winery is a small, family-operated organic estate winery on the Similkameen Bench near the junction of Hwy 3 and Hwy 3A in Keremeos, with 18 acres of vines farmed without synthetic chemicals or pesticides. Founded by Tim and Caroline Cottrill, the winery is best known for its award-winning Gamay and produces a broad range of varietals including Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meritage, and a traditional Sparkling Finch. Cyclists exploring the Similkameen wine country will find a tasting room offering wines that aim to express the distinctive terroir of the valley.

detail.address: 2686 Middle Bench Rd, Keremeos, BC V0X 1N2

restaurant.name: Beaufort Vineyard and Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Beaufort Vineyard and Estate Winery is Vancouver Island's first certified organic winery, established in 2007 and situated on a 20-acre estate in the Comox Valley near Courtenay. The winery produces cool-climate varietals including Ortega, Gewürztraminer, and Pinot Noir under Ecocert organic certification using regenerative farming practices. Visiting cyclists can book guided tastings in a gazebo overlooking the vines, linger at the picnic area with a wine flight, and pick up locally sourced charcuterie boards on site.

restaurant.name: Black Hills Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Black Hills Estate Winery is a premier South Okanagan estate on the Black Sage Bench near Oliver, founded in 1999 and renowned for its flagship Nota Bene red blend, which quickly developed a cult following. The winery has practiced organic and regenerative viticulture since 2020 and features a Wine Experience Centre with panoramic views of Mount Kobau, weekend dining at The Vineyard Kitchen in partnership with acclaimed Chef Jeff Van Geest, and the Vineyard Lodge for overnight stays. Black Sage Road is one of the most popular cycling routes through the South Okanagan wine region, placing this winery directly on many touring cyclists' routes.

detail.address: 4190 Black Sage Road, Oliver, BC V0H 1T1

restaurant.name: Lariana Cellars
restaurant.desc: Lariana Cellars is a winery and wine retail shop located in the Okanagan region of British Columbia, one of Canada's premier wine-producing areas. Touring cyclists riding through the South Okanagan can stop in to browse or purchase local wines directly from the producer. The winery sits along a route that connects several other estate wineries and farm stands.

restaurant.name: Quinta Ferreira Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Quinta Ferreira is a family-owned Portuguese-heritage estate winery on the Black Sage Bench near Oliver, BC, established as an orchard in 1979 and converted to a vineyard beginning in 1999. The winery produces an extensive range of reds, whites, rosé, and dessert wines from varietals including Merlot, Syrah, Viognier, and Zinfandel, and is internationally recognized for award-winning wines. It hosts seasonal food-and-wine events on a licensed patio — including a Pig Roast and Paella Party with live music — making it a destination stop on one of the Okanagan's premier cycling roads.

restaurant.name: Fox Mountain Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Fox Mountain Brewing Co. is Williams Lake's hometown craft brewery, pouring a rotating lineup of house-brewed beers — from a Hillbilly Blonde to a hazy IPA named Pumptrack — alongside a full kitchen menu in a taproom with patio views of Williams Lake. The brewery operates with a no-reservations walk-in policy and welcomes dogs on the patio, making it an approachable stop for travellers passing through the Cariboo. Growler fills and 4-pack takeout are available for cyclists who want to carry their haul down the road.

detail.address: 215 Donald Road, Williams Lake, BC V2G 4K4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items flagged 'gf' (gluten-free), including wings, nachos, salads, and rice bowls; Angry Burger explicitly lists a 'Veggie option'

restaurant.name: Smithers Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Smithers Brewing Co. is a timber-framed craft brewery in northern BC, crowned Brewery of the Year at the 2025 Canadian Brewing Awards. Their taproom runs 12 taps with four mainstay beers and five rotating seasonals alongside house-brewed kombucha, nitro cold brew, and BC wines for non-beer drinkers. It is a walk-in-friendly, first-come-first-served space with an outdoor patio that welcomes pets.

restaurant.name: Baillie-Grohman Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: A family-owned estate winery nestled in the Creston Valley of the Kootenays, Baillie-Grohman grows cool-climate varieties including Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris, and Gewürztraminer on its own vineyard. The tasting room pairs wine flights with a food menu of local charcuterie boards, warm brie, and seasonal accompaniments sourced from valley producers. Summer evenings bring live music and Sunday DJ sessions in the outdoor pavilion, making this a lively destination stop for cyclists exploring the Kootenay wine route.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu states 'Gluten free crackers are available upon request' and notes staff accommodate allergies and dietary requirements. The Forager board (hummus, tapenade, vegetables, fruit, focaccia) is a vegetarian option

restaurant.name: La Stella Winery
restaurant.desc: LaStella Winery is an Italian-inspired boutique estate winery perched beside Osoyoos Lake in the sun-drenched South Okanagan, crafting Tuscan-style blends named after musical terms — Allegretto, Maestoso, Vivace — from one of Canada's hottest and driest wine regions. The winery features outdoor sit-down tastings and a picnic area where visitors can enjoy their own snacks alongside a flight of wine. A portion of tasting fees is donated to the Canucks Autism Network, and 5% goes toward tree-planting to offset the winery's full carbon footprint.

notes.Takeout: Website states: 'Appointments are NOT needed to purchase to-go wines by the bottle.'

restaurant.name: SouthEnd Farm Winery
restaurant.desc: SouthEnd Farm Winery & ClearCut Distilling Co. is a small-batch winery and distillery on Quadra Island, crafting wines from organically grown grape hybrids suited to the island climate and spirits from botanicals grown or foraged on the farm. The multi-purpose tasting room doubles as the winery itself, so visitors are essentially on a farm tour the moment they walk in, with sheep, chickens, and goats nearby. A vacation 'Shack' on the property is also available for overnight stays via Airbnb, making it a potential overnight stop for cycle tourists.

detail.address: 319 Sutil Road, Quadra Island, BC V0P 1N0

notes.Takeout: Bottled wines and spirits listed for sale on the tasting room page with prices including taxes and bottle deposit, indicating bottles can be purchased to take away

restaurant.name: Cassini Cellars
restaurant.desc: Cassini Cellars is a boutique estate winery situated on the Golden Mile Bench—described on its own site as the finest grape-growing region in Canada—halfway between Oliver and Osoyoos on Highway 97. The winery has accumulated an impressive awards haul including Lieutenant Governor's Awards of Excellence, Double Golds at the Canadian Wine Championship, and a Platinum at Wine Press Northwest, making it one of the most decorated small producers in the South Okanagan. Cyclists riding the popular Okanagan wine-route corridor will pass directly in front of the property on HWY97 and can stop at the tasting room to sample celebrated Cabernet Franc, Malbec, and other estate reds.

restaurant.name: Seven Stones Winery
restaurant.desc: Seven Stones Estate Winery sits on a sun-drenched bench overlooking the Similkameen Valley and is known for bold red wines aged in underground cave cellars carved into the hillside. Founded by winemaker George Hanson, the estate practices sustainable viticulture and small-lot winemaking, earning recognition for blends like the award-winning Legend. Cyclists on the Crowsnest Highway can stop for a tasting, explore the cave tours, and take in panoramic vineyard views from the patio.

restaurant.name: Empty Keg Brew House
restaurant.desc: Empty Keg Brew House is a family-friendly craft brewery established in May 2019 in Merritt, BC's Nicola Valley, featured on the Southern Interior Ale Trail, with over 67 handcrafted beer varieties created since opening. The brewhouse pairs a rotating tap list of unfiltered ales, lagers, stouts, and hard seltzers with a food menu of burgers, chicken, charcuterie, and pub fare ordered at a self-serve front bar. A recent solar installation and an expanded patio reflect the owners' community-minded ethos in this small-town gathering spot.

restaurant.name: Kismet Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Kismet Estate Winery is a family-owned estate winery in Oliver, BC — the self-proclaimed 'Wine Capital of Canada' — rooted in the Punjabi-Canadian heritage of the Dhaliwal family, who farm 600 acres of South Okanagan vineyards. The winery pairs its estate wines with Manzil, an on-site restaurant reimagining vibrant Indian cuisine using locally sourced Okanagan ingredients and fresh spices from India. It sits squarely in the heart of the South Okanagan wine-route cycling corridor and offers wine club memberships, vineyard tours, and bookable tasting experiences.

restaurant.name: Clos du Soleil Winery
restaurant.desc: Clos du Soleil is a small artisan winery and estate vineyard on the Upper Bench of the South Similkameen Valley, producing ultra-premium Bordeaux-inspired wines from organically farmed, biodynamic vineyards since 2006. The tasting room invites visitors to tour the vineyard and taste wines that express the rocky, sun-drenched character of this distinctive Similkameen microclimate. A natural destination stop for cyclists touring this scenic valley corridor, the winery's organic credentials and welcoming hospitality ethos set it apart from larger commercial operations.

detail.address: 2568 Upper Bench Road, Keremeos, BC V0X 1N4

restaurant.name: Beach Fire Brewery
restaurant.desc: Beach Fire Brewing is Campbell River's own craft brewery and taproom, producing award-winning beers such as the gold-medal Ember Red Ale and the locally beloved High Tide Pale Ale alongside a kitchen stocked with ingredients from regional farmers. The brewery is a community partner of the River City Cycle Club and even names one of its year-round beers 'WheelBender Stout,' giving it a natural affinity with the cycling crowd. Growlers, howlers, and cans are available to go, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking to restock before the next stretch of Vancouver Island road.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu explicitly labels items with GF (gluten-free), V (vegetarian), and Vegan designations, e.g. Mixed Olives 'GF V', Black Bean Tostadas 'GF, V, Vegan option', Buddha Bowl 'GF V'

restaurant.name: True North Distilleries
restaurant.desc: True North Distilleries is a craft distillery in Qualicum Beach on Vancouver Island, producing Canadian whiskeys (including the 54-40 and 54-40 10 reserve series), gin (Djinneh), and absinthe. They offer bookable tasting experiences for both whiskey and absinthe, and run a Barrel Buyers Club allowing enthusiasts to purchase shares in aging barrels with custom-labeled bottles at maturity. A retail store on site sells their spirits range.

detail.address: 103-680 Berwick Rd. S, Qualicum Beach, BC

restaurant.name: Church & State Wines
restaurant.desc: Church & State Wines is an estate winery in the Oliver-Osoyoos wine corridor of the South Okanagan, producing 100% BC VQA wines grown exclusively on its 80+ acres of owned vineyards under the direction of Bordeaux-trained winemaker Arnaud Thierry. Named #1 Small Winery in British Columbia, it offers guided taste experiences at the tasting bar and ships wine nationally through its club. The property is a natural stop on the Okanagan's celebrated wine-touring routes, which attract many cyclists annually.

restaurant.name: Northern Lights Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Northern Lights Estate Winery is BC's most northern and largest fruit winery, built on the banks of the Nechako River at the base of Prince George's famous cutbanks. The estate grows gooseberries, raspberries, apples, rhubarb, black currants, cherries, and blueberries on-site, crafting award-winning wines from 100% BC-grown fruit. Visitors can enjoy tours and tastings, a full riverside restaurant (RiverHouse), and the distinction of sipping carbon-neutral, fully vegan wines at a destination unlike any other in northern BC.

detail.address: 745 Prince George Pulpmill Rd, Prince George, BC V2K 5P4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states explicitly: 'all of our wines are vegan' — no animal products (gelatin, egg whites, casein, isinglass) used; bentonite clay used instead. Vegan confirmed for all wine products; restaurant menu options not specified

restaurant.name: Moon Curser Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Moon Curser Vineyards is a boutique Osoyoos winery named after gold-rush-era smugglers who dodged moonlight on the Dewdney Trail, just shy of the US border. It specializes in rare old-world varieties like Touriga Nacional, Carménère, and Tannat — grapes seldom grown elsewhere in Canada — and has earned recognition seven times on Top Winery lists at the WineAlign National Wine Awards of Canada. Cyclists on the Crowsnest Highway (Hwy 3) will find a welcoming tasting room with vineyard and Osoyoos Lake views, plus a seated 'Smuggler's Sitting' experience on select days.

restaurant.name: Rust Wine Co
restaurant.desc: Rust Wine Co is a boutique estate winery on the Golden Mile Bench in Oliver, BC, drawing grapes from five vineyards — some planted as far back as 1963 — to produce small-lot, single-vineyard wines that reflect distinct Okanagan and Similkameen terroirs. The property includes a tasting room with sweeping views over Black Sage Bench toward Osoyoos, and a restored 19th-century heritage bunkhouse available as vacation accommodation. Regular live music events make it a social stop on a corridor that is one of BC's most popular cycling routes.

detail.address: 4444 Golden Mile Drive, Oliver, BC V0H 1T1

restaurant.name: Phantom Creek Estates
restaurant.desc: Phantom Creek Estates is a premium winery and estate restaurant on the Black Sage Bench in Oliver, BC, one of Canada's most celebrated wine sub-regions. The gravity-flow facility sources fruit from four estate vineyards and produces up to 50,000 cases annually using biodynamic farming and optical-sorting technology. Touring cyclists riding the South Okanagan's wine-country roads can stop for seated tastings, guided estate tours, and full restaurant dining with seasonal chef's pairings.

restaurant.name: Dubh Glas Distillery
restaurant.desc: Dubh Glas Distillery is a craft spirits producer in BC's Okanagan region, making single-malt whisky, gin, and VSOP brandy. The distillery operates an online shop and, based on its Square payment integration, likely has a physical tasting room or retail counter where cyclists can sample and purchase local spirits. It sits in one of Canada's premier wine and spirits corridors, making it a noteworthy detour for touring cyclists passing through the South Okanagan.

restaurant.name: Gehringer Brothers Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Gehringer Brothers Estate Winery is a family-owned estate winery established in 1985 on the Golden Mile Bench near Oliver in the South Okanagan, where Walter and Gordon Gehringer — BC-born winemakers trained in Europe — produce an extensive range from sparkling and whites to icewines. Their Minus 9 Icewine has earned Double Platinum 'Best of the Best' recognition from Wine Press Northwest, and the winery has been described as 'one of the finest wine producers anywhere on the west coast.' Wine can be purchased at the on-site wine shop or ordered online for Canadian delivery.

restaurant.name: Backyard Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Backyard Vineyards is an award-winning BC VQA winery in the Township of Langley, marketing itself as the bountiful backyard to Vancouver. Visitors can enjoy wine flights, charcuterie, and wine by the glass in the tasting room, or take bottles out to the casual first-come-first-served picnic area, which welcomes outside food and leashed dogs. The winery offers bubble tours, private event bookings, and a wine club, making it a destination rather than a simple tasting stop.

restaurant.name: Antidote Distilling Company
