restaurant.desc: Antidote Distilling Company is a craft distillery in Port Alberni, Vancouver Island, producing award-winning artisanal spirits — including a Black Gin that earned Double Gold at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition — made with locally sourced grains and wild-foraged ingredients. They operate an on-site restaurant serving cocktails and food, and offer a 'Gin Academy' experience where visitors distill and bottle their own personalized gin. With a sustainability focus on recycled glass bottles and a low carbon footprint, they describe themselves as a postcard for the Alberni Valley.

detail.address: 103-4721 Johnston Road, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 5M4

restaurant.name: Hidden Chael Winery
restaurant.desc: Hidden Chapel Winery is a small boutique winery nestled in the pines near Oliver in the South Okanagan, producing estate wines from sandy loam soils at the northern tip of the Great Basin Desert. The winery ages its wines in a unique underground cellar overlooked by the namesake hidden chapel, surrounded by beautiful gardens. Visitors can explore a range of whites, rosés, and reds — including estate-grown Cabernet Sauvignon — at the cheerful tasting room and wine shop, located only 5 km from Oliver and 3 km from the District Wine Village.

restaurant.name: Trench Brewing & Distilling
restaurant.desc: Trench Brewing & Distilling is a craft brewery and distillery in Prince George whose entire identity is rooted in the Rocky Mountain Trench — every beer named after a local natural landmark. The taproom pairs a rotating lineup of flagship and small-batch pilot brews with a food menu built around house-smoked meats and gourmet tacos, making it a substantial sit-down stop. Beers can also be purchased to take home, and the brewery distributes widely across BC.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian items: Falafel tacos, Roasted Brussels Sprouts, and Spinach & Artichoke Dip. No vegan or GF labelling explicitly mentioned

restaurant.name: Raven's Moon Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Raven's Moon is a farm-based estate winery and cidery near Courtenay on Vancouver Island, producing handcrafted ciders and fruit wines from organically grown local blueberries and apples. The operation blends old-world fermentation traditions with farm experimentation, offering still, sparkling, and fortified styles alongside farm foods like jams and honey. A past customer review specifically calls it out as a highlight of a multi-farm cycle tour, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists on the Island.

restaurant.name: Nk'Mip Cellars
restaurant.desc: Nk'Mip Cellars is the first Indigenous-owned winery in North America, operated by the Osoyoos Indian Band on their 32,000-acre Sonoran Desert reserve at the southern end of the Okanagan Valley. The winery produces international award-winning wines across multiple tiers and is home to the Sweetgrass @Nk'Mip Cellars restaurant, offering lunch in a setting rich with Syilx cultural history. For touring cyclists on the Okanagan wine route, it is a distinctive cultural and culinary destination unlike any other stop in the region.

detail.address: 1400 Rancher Creek Road, Osoyoos, BC V0H 1V6

restaurant.name: Vasanti Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Vasanti Estate Winery is a family-owned estate winery on the northern edge of Oliver opened in June 2024 by the Sidhu family, who have farmed the South Okanagan for over 40 years. The winery offers guided tastings of small-lot, award-winning wines paired with locally inspired small plates and cocktails served on a patio overlooking the estate vineyards. Sitting directly on Highway 97 in the heart of Okanagan wine country, it is a natural stop on the classic Oliver–Osoyoos cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Burrowing Owl Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Burrowing Owl Estate Winery is a family-owned premium VQA wine estate in Oliver, at the heart of the South Okanagan cycling corridor, operating since 1993. The property encompasses a wine shop, the Sonora Room fine-dining restaurant, and an 11-room guest house, all situated within the northernmost reach of the antelope brush ecosystem. It is a natural destination stop for cyclists exploring Black Sage Road and the broader Okanagan wine country.

detail.address: 500 Burrowing Owl Place (off Black Sage Road), Oliver, BC, V0H 1T1

restaurant.name: Mount Arrowsmith Brewery
restaurant.desc: Mount Arrowsmith Brewing Company is a family-run craft brewery in Parksville producing a wide range of award-winning hand-crafted beers, from crisp lagers and hazy IPAs to a spruce-tip brut IPA made with locally foraged Sitka tips. Their west-coast themed tasting room pours pints, flights, and cans to go, while the newly opened Arrowsmith Smokehouse adds Southern-style BBQ with house-smoked meats, pizzas, and handhelds. The brewery is a genuine community hub on mid-Vancouver Island, regularly hosting live music nights and an annual craft beer and mini-putt festival in Parksville.

detail.address: 109-425 Stanford Avenue E., Parksville, BC V9P 2N4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes meatless items: falafel shawarma wrap, garden salad wrap (avocado, tomato, cucumber), wild mushroom pizza, and Mediterranean pizza

restaurant.name: Maverick Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Maverick Estate Winery occupies the Golden Mile Slopes appellation on Highway 97, sitting roughly halfway between Oliver and Osoyoos in the heart of South Okanagan wine country. Founded in 2009 and releasing its first vintage in 2011, the winery follows slow-wine principles—biodynamic and organic farming, natural fermentation, and minimal cellar intervention—producing small-lot wines that aim to express the character of the site. Guests can taste in a tasting room, on a patio, or in the Villa Tasting Garden, and the winery also runs intimate dinners and wine-education Flight School sessions.

restaurant.name: Silver Sage Winery
restaurant.desc: Silver Sage Winery is a family-owned, award-winning estate winery established in 1996 by Romanian immigrants Anna and Victor Manola, drawing on four generations of winemaking tradition in Oliver, BC's Golden Mile region. Set on the banks of Oxbow Creek with mountain views, the winery produces premium Okanagan grape wines alongside distinctive fresh-fruit dessert wines — claimed to be a Canadian first. Beyond tastings, the property offers three on-site guest suites and event hosting, making it a potential overnight stop for cycling tours through the Okanagan wine country.

restaurant.name: Locality Brewing
restaurant.desc: Locality Brewing is a family-owned farm brewery on MacInnes Farms in North Langley that grows its own barley and hops, malts its own grain, and brews entirely on-site — a true field-to-glass operation. The taproom opens onto outdoor picnic areas and hiking trails, giving visiting cyclists a rural farm setting to relax in. An on-site food truck (Stampede Burger) serves burgers, poutine, and salads alongside the house-brewed beers.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Stampede Burger menu lists a Black Bean Burger and a Salad option, confirming vegetarian choices; a Keto Option is also offered

restaurant.name: Oak & Sparrow
restaurant.desc: Oak & Sparrow Estate Winery is a family-owned small-batch winery perched on the Golden Mile slopes of the Okanagan Valley near Oliver, BC — one of the most celebrated cycling wine routes in Canada. The estate produces wines including Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, and Rosé from its own vineyard, and recently completed a tasting room and large patio with vineyard views where tastings can be booked in advance or taken as walk-ins.

restaurant.name: Township 7 Vineyards & Winery
restaurant.desc: Township 7 Vineyards & Winery is a distinguished BC winery founded in 2000 with two locations; this South Langley Fraser Valley outpost sits in a serene rural countryside setting where visitors can witness a working winery in action and meet the winemakers. The winery is known for small-lot, hand-harvested wines crafted from sustainably grown estate and local grapes, blended from over 15 single vineyards. The tasting room encourages guests to linger over a glass and enjoy a picnic on the property.

restaurant.name: Singletree Winery
restaurant.desc: Singletree Winery is a small, family-operated vineyard in the Mt. Lehman area of Abbotsford, producing VQA wines crafted by second-generation winemaker Andrew Etsell from Fraser Valley grapes. Visitors can choose between guided indoor tastings, outdoor wine flights at fire tables, private Wine Cabanas, or themed Di Vine Domes set in an Enchanted Forest or Canadian Cabin setting. The winery also hosts regular live-music events and is available for weddings, making it a notable destination stop along Fraser Valley cycling routes.

detail.address: 5782 Mount Lehman Road, Abbotsford, BC V4X 1V4

restaurant.name: The Fort Wine Co.
restaurant.desc: The Fort Wine Co. is a winery and wine shop located on 84 Avenue in the Langley area of the Fraser Valley, a region known for its agricultural heritage and cycling routes. Tagged in OpenStreetMap as both a craft winery and a wine retail shop, it would represent a farm-gate style destination for cyclists exploring the valley. No current website content is available to confirm operating details.

restaurant.name: Mountainview Brewing
restaurant.desc: Mountainview Brewing Co. is a family-friendly craft brewery and taproom in Hope, BC, brewing with fresh Fraser Valley mountain water and a mandate to be a welcoming, inclusive community gathering space. The rotating tap list spans everything from hoppy IPAs showcasing BC-grown hops to barrel-aged mixed-culture saisons aged on golden plums picked locally in Hope. Sitting at the junction of the Crowsnest Highway corridor and the Fraser Valley, it is a natural refuelling stop for cyclists on multi-day tours through the region.

detail.address: 390 Old Hope-Princeton Way, Hope, BC V0X 1L4

restaurant.name: Tinhorn Creek Winery
restaurant.desc: Tinhorn Creek Vineyards is a landmark South Okanagan estate winery with over 30 years of history on the Golden Mile Bench near Oliver, BC, recognized as Canada's first carbon-neutral winery. The property includes the full-service Miradoro Restaurant with sweeping valley views, a guest house, guided wine tastings, and an outdoor amphitheatre that hosts a summer Sunset Concert Series. It is a natural destination-stop for cyclists exploring the Okanagan wine country route.

detail.address: 537 Tinhorn Creek Road, Oliver, BC V0H 1T1

restaurant.name: The Patch Brewery Laity Farms
restaurant.desc: The Patch Brewery is a farm-to-table craft brewery and taproom situated on Laity Farms in Maple Ridge, brewing with BC-sourced hops and barley grown on the property — a true farm-to-glass operation rooted in a family farming heritage dating to 1879. Alongside a rotating tap list, the brewery serves artisan pizzas, coffee drinks, and has a picnic area that welcomes dogs. It is a notable stop for cyclists exploring the Fraser Valley, blending a working farm setting with a full kitchen and a well-stocked taproom.

detail.address: 12745 Laity Street, Maple Ridge, BC V4R 2P3

notes.Takeout: Website states beers are available in four-packs to go, sold exclusively at the brewery. Does not sell or fill growlers
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states all salads and pizzas can be made vegan with vegan cheese and meat substitutes; gluten-free beer and cider available; gluten-friendly pizza crust option available (not recommended for celiac due to shared oven)

restaurant.name: River Stone Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: River Stone Estate Winery is a small, family-owned estate winery perched on a rocky knoll in the South Okanagan, just south of the landmark McIntyre Bluff and north of Oliver — BC's self-styled Wine Capital. The winery is celebrated for big, bold Bordeaux-style reds and aromatic whites grown on deep glacial rock and gravel soils at River Rock Vineyards. Cyclists riding the Oliver wine route can stop at the open-air tasting garden, with walk-ins welcome or bookable tasting sessions available.

restaurant.name: Monashee Spirits
restaurant.desc: Monashee Spirits is a small family-run craft distillery and cocktail lounge on Revelstoke's main Mackenzie Avenue strip, hand-distilling award-winning spirits with local ingredients and pure mountain spring water. Their Ethos Gin was named Best in Class Gin in Canada and Canadian Artisan Spirit of the Year 2019, and the bar was ranked #42 in Canada's 100 Best Bars. They also boast one of the largest whisky collections in Canada with over 700 bottles.

notes.Takeout: Website states: 'we are offering online purchase with curb-side delivery' for local customers; out-of-town delivery also available on request via contact form

restaurant.name: Vanessa Vineyard
restaurant.desc: Vanessa Vineyard is a boutique estate winery perched on the rocky hillside of the Similkameen Valley in Cawston, growing premium red wine grapes on 75 acres of sloping, mineral-rich terrain along the Crowsnest Highway. Named for the Greek word for butterfly, the estate has earned national recognition for bold reds crafted under Master Winemaker Howard Soon, an Order of Canada recipient. The on-site tasting room offers curated guided experiences, making it a compelling destination for cyclists touring one of Canada's most scenic wine corridors.

restaurant.name: Homura Yakiniku
restaurant.desc: Homura Yakiniku is a Japanese yakiniku restaurant on the second floor of a building on West Broadway in Vancouver, where guests grill their own meats tableside. The menu spans lunch courses, à la carte cuts, a drinks list, and a happy hour, with both pick-up and delivery available. The name 'Homura' means flame in Japanese, and the restaurant leans into that identity through its emphasis on the shared warmth of grilling together.

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Freshslice Pizza is a BC-founded pizza chain known for its any-toppings flat-price model, serving pizza by the slice and whole pies for dine-in or takeout. This Burnaby location on Royal Oak Avenue is a strip-mall fast-food stop with indoor seating and no drive-through. For a touring cyclist it offers a quick, filling, and affordable calorie stop in a suburban Burnaby corridor.

restaurant.name: Halston Pub & Liquor Store
restaurant.desc: Halston Pub & Liquor Store is a combined neighbourhood pub and off-sale liquor retailer in Kamloops, BC. The dual format means touring cyclists can grab a meal or drink on-site and stock up on take-home beverages in one stop. Its commercial building footprint suggests a full-service venue rather than a kiosk or pop-up.

detail.address: 1271 Salish Rd, Kamloops, BC V2H 1P6, Canada

restaurant.name: Firehouse Subs
restaurant.desc: Firehouse Subs is a Canadian sandwich chain built around hot, steamed subs and a charitable mission: its Public Safety Foundation of Canada has donated over $6.3 million in equipment grants to first responders nationwide. The Pitt Meadows franchise sits in the Meadowtown retail area along the Lougheed Highway, a key east–west corridor for cyclists connecting the Lower Mainland to the Fraser Valley. It is a no-drive-through, takeout-friendly counter-service stop with a gluten-free roll option available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'Gluten Free Roll' as a menu option under Orders & Rewards navigation

restaurant.name: Marigold Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Marigold Cafe is a chef-driven cafe and bakery operated by a husband-and-wife team — Ryan, a Red Seal Executive Chef, and Jenny — situated directly on the Lochside Trail in Saanichton. The cafe explicitly serves trail users and invites cyclists to stop in for specialty coffee, freshly made gourmet paninis, soup, and baked goods. Guests can eat in the industrial-inspired interior or relax on a covered outdoor patio overlooking a garden and water feature.

detail.address: Suite 2 - 7900 Lochside Drive, Saanichton, BC V8M 0B9

restaurant.name: Sooke Oceanside Brewery
restaurant.desc: Sooke Oceanside Brewery is a craft microbrewery and taproom on the southern tip of Vancouver Island, pouring a rotating lineup of west coast-style beers brewed on-site — from blonde ales and IPAs to seasonal schwarzbiers and hard seltzers. The taproom features an ocean-view patio and a lively events calendar including Open Mic Nights and stand-up comedy. Cyclists passing through Sooke on the Westshore or heading toward the Juan de Fuca Trail will find the Grilled To The Mac food truck stationed in the courtyard, serving locally sourced food alongside the house brews.

restaurant.name: Big Way Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Big Way Hot Pot is a growing Chinese hot pot chain offering an individual self-serve dining experience with over 100 premium ingredients and more than 18 broths, from rich Signature Mala to light Tomato with vegan options. The Kingsway location in Burnaby is one of several BC outposts in a chain that now spans across Canada and into the US. Diners select their own broth and cook ingredients tableside in individual pots.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Tomato Broth is explicitly marked 'Vegan Option Available' on both the front page and menu page

restaurant.name: Wood N Frog Coffee Company
restaurant.desc: Wood N Frog Coffee Company is a cozy café in Tsawwassen (Delta, BC) positioned close to the BC Ferries terminal—a natural refuelling point for cyclists arriving or departing by ferry. The café is known for artisan espresso drinks, freshly made sandwiches and wraps, and homemade baked goods including scones, croissants, and coconut cake. Gluten-free and vegetarian options are woven throughout the menu, and the welcoming atmosphere has earned it a loyal following among both locals and ferry travellers.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'wide range of gluten-free options shows its commitment to catering to all dietary preferences'; menu lists vegetarian items including warm havarti veggie baguette and quinoa veggie wrap

restaurant.name: Anita's Organic Bread & Coffee
restaurant.desc: Anita's Bread & Coffee is an organic cafe and bakery housed inside the Anita's Organic Milling facility on South Sumas Road in Chilliwack, operated by Nature's Path Organic Foods. The bakery follows a rotating daily sourdough schedule — producing loaves such as country white, medium rye, miche, vollkornbrot, einkorn, and seasonal fougasse — all baked fresh each morning. It also serves as a baking education centre showcasing Anita's Organic Milling grains and flours, alongside organic coffee and a range of vegan-friendly pastries.

restaurant.name: Marilena Cafe & Raw Bar
restaurant.desc: Marilena Cafe & Raw Bar is Toptable Group's first Victoria location, bringing the same team behind Blue Water Cafe, CinCin, and Araxi to the heart of BC's capital. Executive Chef Kristian Eligh, trained at Jean-Georges and The French Laundry, leads a menu centred on local and globally sourced seafood alongside a Japanese raw bar offering nigiri, sashimi, and sushi rolls. The restaurant has earned national acclaim including No. 1 Fine Dining in Canada on Tripadvisor's Best of the Best 2025 and Best Restaurant in Victoria from Vancouver Magazine 2025–2026.

restaurant.name: Divine Sandwich
restaurant.desc: Divine Sandwich is a fast-food restaurant in Richmond, BC specializing in sandwiches. It offers quick-service meals suitable for cyclists seeking convenient nutrition stops while touring the region.

restaurant.name: Earls
restaurant.desc: Earls Robson is a location of the well-known Canadian casual-dining chain, situated on Vancouver's busy Robson Street shopping corridor. The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating with American-influenced cuisine and caters to vegan and vegetarian diners. Its central position in the West End makes it a convenient urban stop on a popular cycling and pedestrian thoroughfare.

restaurant.desc: Banditry Cider is an award-winning craft cidery on BC's Sunshine Coast, set on a farm property in Gibsons where 100% BC-grown apples are pressed without concentrates or artificial flavourings. The cidery has earned back-to-back Cidery of the Year recognition and multiple gold awards, and hosts regular community events including live music, jazz festivals, and open mic nights. Visiting cyclists will find outdoor seating in a relaxed orchard setting, a food truck (Banditry Cantina), and a dog- and family-friendly atmosphere complete with a playground and duck pond.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website FAQ explicitly states 'Is your cider Gluten Free? Yes! Even our hopped ciders are gluten free.'

restaurant.name: Real Thai Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Real Thai Restaurant is an authentic Thai eatery in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood, operated by a chef with over 15 years of traditional Thai culinary expertise. The menu spans soups, stir-fries, deep-fries, and desserts including Pad Thai and Thai curry, with reviewers praising fresh ingredients, a wide range of spice levels, and a welcoming atmosphere. Both dine-in and takeout are offered, with table reservations available.

restaurant.name: Mr Sushi
restaurant.desc: Mr Sushi Canada is a family-owned sushi restaurant established in North Vancouver in the early 1990s, with this third location opening in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant/Olympic Village neighbourhood in 2023. The restaurant emphasises carefully sourced, fresh ingredients and has earned a North Shore News Readers' Choice Award. Cyclists can eat in or order for pickup or third-party delivery.

restaurant.name: The Pavilion Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Pavilion Restaurant is a full-service sit-down restaurant in Prince Rupert offering a broad menu spanning local BC seafood (halibut, ling cod, BC mussels, ahi tuna), South Asian curries, burgers, steaks, and pasta. The kitchen emphasizes fresh, locally sourced ingredients and works with local farmers and producers as part of an explicit sustainability commitment. The restaurant also accommodates group dining, birthday celebrations, and conference meetups, making it a practical option for larger touring parties.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels 'Quinoa Bowl With Blackened Tofu Vegan $19.5'; additional vegetarian options include Hummus + Pita, Fresh Green Salad, Sweet Yam Fries, Spinach Dip, and Cauliflower Manchurian. No GF labelling observed

restaurant.name: Motoretta Gelato
restaurant.desc: Motoretta is a gelato and granita shop in Vancouver's Coal Harbour neighbourhood, part of the Kitchen Table restaurant group. It highlights BC seasonal ingredients prepared with traditional Italian techniques, offering a rotating roster of classic and inventive flavours alongside a dedicated dairy-free line. Situated steps from the Coal Harbour seawall, it is a natural mid-ride treat stop for cyclists exploring the waterfront.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists a dedicated DAIRY-FREE section including Taro, Lemon, Mango, Pistachio, Strawberry, Blood Orange, and Dark Chocolate flavours

restaurant.name: M.E Concept Cakes
restaurant.desc: M.E Concept Cakes is a specialty bakery on Granville Street in Vancouver focused on cakes and desserts. The OSM record was field-verified as recently as October 2025, suggesting the business is actively operating. A touring cyclist stopping along Granville could pick up baked goods here, though this is a niche confectionery rather than a general provisioning stop.

restaurant.name: Booster Juice
restaurant.desc: Booster Juice is a Canadian smoothie and fresh juice chain offering blended-to-order drinks, açai bowls, and light food items. As a juice bar focused on nutritious, high-energy beverages, it could serve as a convenient refuelling stop for touring cyclists. This location is in Nanaimo, BC, in a unit-addressed commercial space.

restaurant.name: Yuan's Garden Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Yuan's Garden is an award-winning sit-down restaurant in Richmond's Alexandra Road food corridor, serving authentic Jiangsu and Zhejiang cuisine rooted in a culinary tradition tracing back to 18th-century scholar Yuan Mei. Chef Ge Feng, a Nanjing native, has been recognized by the 2024 Chinese Restaurant Awards Critics' Choice for his Nanjing-Style Salted Duck and was nominated for Vancouver's Best Casual Chinese Restaurants the same year. The restaurant offers a full menu of dumplings, seafood, poultry, and vegetable dishes in a sit-down dining room that accepts table reservations.

restaurant.name: Christina Lake Welcome Centre
restaurant.desc: The Christina Lake Welcome Centre is a community hub opened in 2010 and located in the community park in the heart of Christina Lake, serving as both an interpretive centre and regional tourism information point. It houses a gallery of arts and crafts from Boundary region artists, a retail shop with locally produced items, and an innovative on-site Eco Machine wastewater treatment system that doubles as an environmental education exhibit. Per OSM tags, a coffee and dessert counter ('Lisa's coffee and desert') operates within the building, though this is not confirmed by the current website.

restaurant.name: Columbia Bakery
restaurant.desc: Columbia Bakery is a family-owned European specialty bakery operating in Nanaimo since 1972, known for high-quality breads, pastries, and baked German classics like Bee-sting cake. Cyclists stopping in can grab a fresh daily soup or sandwich for a satisfying mid-ride meal. Located at the corner of Bowen and Northfield Road, it is a well-established local institution with decades of community presence.

restaurant.name: Uno Beef Noodle
restaurant.desc: Uno Beef Noodle is a Taiwanese restaurant in Richmond specializing in authentic beef noodle soup prepared with traditional techniques. The focused menu spans noodle soups, dry noodles, bento rice combos, and appetizers, and the restaurant operates across two Richmond locations. It offers a warming, filling meal option for cyclists passing through the city.

restaurant.name: Nizzy's Cafe & Catering
restaurant.desc: A cafe and catering business located on Byrne Road in Vancouver, serving the local community with both dining and catering services.

restaurant.name: The Railside Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Railside Restaurant is a family restaurant in Chase, BC, serving the small community along Shuswap Avenue. For cycling tourists, it represents a reliable dining option in the interior of British Columbia.

restaurant.name: Golden Sweets & Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Golden Sweets & Restaurant is an authentic Indian cuisine spot in Surrey specializing in butter chicken, Tandoori items, traditional thali, and Indian sweets made fresh daily. The menu spans a wide range of vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes including Indian street food classics like Gol Gappe, Chaat Papri, and assorted pakoras. A touring cyclist looking for a filling, flavourful sit-down meal or a quick takeout stop will find a broad menu with something for most dietary preferences.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes a dedicated 'VEG APPETIZERS' section with multiple vegetarian dishes (samosas, pakoras, chaat, paneer items, etc.)

restaurant.name: La Forêt
restaurant.desc: La Forêt is a cozy café and bakery with roots going back to 2013, grown into a beloved Burnaby and Vancouver destination known for specialty espresso drinks, brunch platters, housemade croissants, and custom cakes. The Royal Oak branch opened in 2023 and offers both indoor and outdoor seating in a welcoming atmosphere. Touring cyclists will find a full food menu with hearty brunch options and a range of hot and iced beverages.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: No GF mention found

restaurant.name: Grab and Go Persian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Grab and Go is a North Vancouver Persian restaurant serving freshly made, never-frozen dishes daily from its Lonsdale Avenue location. Founded in 2019, the fast-casual concept has grown to two Lower Mainland locations. Cyclists on Lonsdale will find a convenient stop for a filling, made-fresh meal with online ordering available.

detail.address: 1805 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2J8

restaurant.name: Jägerhof
restaurant.desc: Jägerhof is a long-established Alpine-cuisine restaurant in North Vancouver serving authentic German, Austrian, Swiss, and South Tyrol dishes such as Wiener Schnitzel, Beef Rouladen, and Swiss Raclette. Reopened in 2014 by local owners who grew up visiting the original, it retains a cozy European atmosphere complete with a 125-year-old piano and regular live music on weekend evenings. Now celebrating 40 years, it pairs its regional menu with a carefully curated selection of European imported beers and wines.

detail.address: 71 Lonsdale Avenue, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2E5

restaurant.name: Cora's
restaurant.desc: Cora's is a franchise location of the well-known Canadian breakfast and lunch chain celebrated for its elaborate fresh fruit platters, crêpes, and egg-based dishes. Situated on the Princeton-Kamloops Highway, this full-service restaurant offers a dining room, outdoor patio, takeout, and delivery. It provides a reliable and filling meal stop for touring cyclists passing through Kamloops.

detail.address: 1801 Princeton-Kamloops Highway, Unit 601-602, Kamloops, BC V2E2J7

restaurant.name: Continental Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Continental Seafood Restaurant is a long-established Cantonese restaurant in Richmond with over 20 years of operation, housed in a spacious 12,000 sq ft dining room capable of hosting events for up to 600 guests. The menu spans traditional dim sum served from trolley carts, seafood, and rice and noodle dishes from multiple Chinese provinces, with set dinners popular for groups. Touring cyclists stopping here will find a full-service restaurant with takeout service and a lively atmosphere including nightly live entertainment and a dance floor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states under Chinese Dishes: 'we won't forget vegeterian [sic] dishes'

restaurant.name: Oakberry Açaí bowls
restaurant.desc: Oakberry is a global açaí bowl chain with a Vancouver West End location on Davie Street, offering build-your-own bowls topped with granola, fresh fruit, nut butter, honey, and coconut. The brand is vegetarian-friendly and operates a mobile OAKVAN catering unit currently available in Vancouver for events. It sits in a dense, walkable neighbourhood frequented by recreational and commuter cyclists.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website catering page states 'Allergen and special diet-friendly options are available'

restaurant.name: nuba
restaurant.desc: Nuba is a beloved Vancouver Lebanese restaurant group; the Kitsilano outpost is styled as a Lebanese taverna, with a cavernous multi-level interior of low-ceilinged nooks and a glass-covered courtyard filled with plants. Founded nearly 20 years ago, Nuba sources fresh, local, and organic ingredients daily and has long been regarded as one of Vancouver's go-to spots for feel-good, health-conscious Lebanese cooking. The menu is substantially vegan-friendly, with all meats halal and hormone-free, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists with diverse dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page states 'A large portion of our menu items are vegan.'. Menu items throughout are individually labelled Vegan and/or GF (e.g. Classic Hummus, Garden Falafel, Najib's Special, Mjadra)

restaurant.name: Rocky Point Spirits
restaurant.desc: Rocky Point Spirits is Port Moody's first commercial distillery, opened in late 2020 and situated in front of Rocky Point Park with views of the sea and mountains. The indoor lounge accommodates up to 100 guests and serves handcrafted cocktails alongside house-made spirits including low-calorie gin and vodka. Food trucks are typically stationed outside, and bottles and ready-to-drink cocktails can be purchased to go.

detail.address: 2805 Murray St, Port Moody, BC V3H1X3

restaurant.name: Ox King Noodles
restaurant.desc: Ox King Noodles is a Vietnamese noodle restaurant located in downtown Victoria, tucked into a unit on View Street. It offers a menu with both vegan and vegetarian options, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists with dietary preferences. Its central Victoria location puts it within easy reach of major cycling routes through the city.

detail.address: 1029 View Street, Unit 105, Victoria, BC V8V 0C9

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's franchise location on 88 Avenue in Langley serving burgers, chicken sandwiches, fries, and McCafé beverages, with a drive-through for quick service. The location is wheelchair accessible and air-conditioned, making it a reasonable comfort stop on a hot day's ride. Touring cyclists will find it a familiar and predictable resupply point in Langley's suburban corridor.

restaurant.name: Peace and Culture Coffee
restaurant.desc: Peace and Culture Coffee is a neighbourhood café on East Georgia Street in Vancouver's east side, operating as a coffee shop with weekday and weekend hours. Its name suggests a community-oriented ethos that may appeal to cyclists looking for a relaxed stop. Beyond OSM's basic tags, no further detail about its offerings or atmosphere could be verified.

restaurant.name: Farmer's Apprentice
restaurant.desc: Farmer's Apprentice is a chef-driven Vancouver restaurant on West 6th Avenue built around consciously sourced, seasonal ingredients, with menus that shift frequently according to what the season and chefs' inspiration dictate. The relaxed dining room aims to make thoughtfully curated meals feel accessible rather than precious. The restaurant has a Wikipedia entry and regularly hosts special events designed to connect farmers, chefs, and diners in what it calls authentic community.

restaurant.name: Westcoast Poke
restaurant.desc: Westcoast Poké is a BC-based poke bowl chain emphasizing chef-inspired flavours, fresh ingredients, and sustainable practices, with fully customizable bowls built from proteins like ahi tuna, sockeye salmon, and tofu. Located in a unit on Steveston Highway in Richmond, it offers online ordering and catering alongside in-store dining. The Steveston area is a popular cycling destination, making this a convenient stop for riders exploring the Fraser River delta routes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Tofu as a protein option; website notes 'FOR CURRENT PRICING AND DIETARY RESTRICTIONS - PLEASE VIEW THE FULL MENU BELOW', indicating dietary accommodation awareness. Vegan/GF status not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: Toyo Sushi
restaurant.desc: Toyo Sushi is a small, traditional Japanese sushi restaurant in Burnaby run by Chef Masaaki Toyokawa, who trained at a renowned sushi establishment in Japan and brings over 30 years of experience to the counter. The restaurant focuses on an authentic, intimate experience using freshly imported fish including specialties like bluefin tuna and shimaaji. It offers a genuine taste of Japan in a neighbourhood setting on Hastings Street.

restaurant.name: Cosmos Pizza
restaurant.desc: Cosmos Pizza is a pizza fast food restaurant located on Pandora Avenue in Victoria. It serves as a casual dining option for the local area.

restaurant.name: Little Yunnan Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Little Yunnan Restaurant is a family-owned eatery on Victoria's historic Fisgard Street, run by Yunnanese immigrants who specialize in authentic regional Chinese cuisine. Their flagship dish, Crossing the Bridge Rice Noodle Soup, features a broth simmered for eight hours from pork bone, chicken, and Yunnan ham, served with fresh vegetables and house-made ingredients. It is a welcoming, affordable spot for a restorative sit-down meal after a ride through Victoria.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists a 'Vegetarian option' for the signature Crossing the Bridge Rice Noodle Soup

restaurant.name: Tap & Barrel Bridges
restaurant.desc: Tap & Barrel Bridges is a large, full-service waterfront restaurant located on the western tip of Granville Island, steps from the Public Market — a location previously occupied by the long-running Bridges Restaurant. Part of the multi-location Tap & Barrel chain, which operates its own brewery (BREWHALL Beer Co.) and is recognized as one of Canada's Best Managed Companies. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a comfortable stop in any weather on one of Vancouver's most popular cycling corridors.

restaurant.name: Sheer Bliss Bakery Cafe Ltd
restaurant.desc: A bakery cafe in Gibsons serving baked goods and cafe beverages. Provides a convenient refreshment stop for touring cyclists in the community.

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: Starbucks is the world's largest coffeehouse chain, tracing its origins to Seattle's Pike Place Market in 1971 and now operating tens of thousands of locations globally. This North Vancouver location (unit 21) is part of that network, offering the brand's full range of espresso drinks, teas, refreshers, and food items. Touring cyclists across BC will recognize Starbucks as a consistent waypoint along busy urban and suburban corridors.

detail.address: 800 McBride Blvd, Unit 21, Royal Square Mall, New Westminster, BC V3L 2B8

restaurant.name: The Sprouted Fig
restaurant.desc: The Sprouted Fig is a restaurant in Vernon serving the local community. It provides a dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Just Poké
restaurant.desc: Just Poké is a Pacific Northwest poke bowl chain with a Richmond, BC franchise location offering dine-in, pickup, and delivery. The menu features signature bowls, build-your-own options, and sustainably-sourced sushi-grade fish. The chain emphasizes clean eating with compostable packaging and sustainably-caught ingredients.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Franchising page states 'Just Poke offers a variety of options to fit many dietary restrictions, including but not limited to those adhering to a Gluten Free, Vegetarian, Vegan or Keto diet.'

restaurant.name: Brew Mountain Café
restaurant.desc: Brew Mountain Eatery is a café and casual eatery situated just inside the gates of Whistler RV Park on Highway 99, open to both campground guests and the general public passing through. The menu spans breakfast sandwiches, hand-crafted burgers, made-to-order pizzas, and locally roasted coffee from Forecast Coffee, a B.C. roaster, with seasonal menus shifting between hearty winter comfort food and lighter summer fare. The park setting includes outdoor seating with mountain views, and the business also offers year-round catering for events and tours.

restaurant.name: Kourosh Bakery
restaurant.desc: Kourosh Bakery is a bakery on Lynn Valley Road in North Vancouver offering fresh baked goods. Touring cyclists can stop here for pastries and provisions.

restaurant.name: Eggstatic
restaurant.desc: Eggstatic Vancouver is a halal, Middle Eastern-inspired brunch restaurant in the Riley Park neighbourhood, described on its own site as the first in Vancouver to bring an artisan Middle Eastern brunch format to the city at this level of ambition. The menu centres on shakshuka, Lotus Biscoff pancakes, benedicts, and specialty lattes such as the Baklava latte. It is part of a growing Canadian chain with over a dozen locations across Ontario, Quebec, and now BC, and appears to have just completed its Vancouver grand opening.

restaurant.name: R Ki Dessert Studio
restaurant.desc: R Ki Dessert Studio is a specialty dessert cafe operated by the R Ki Coffee Lab team, a Richmond-based specialty coffee roaster known for hosting cupping events featuring single-origin lots from Panama, Bolivia, and Peru. Located in a shopping complex on Hazelbridge Way in Richmond, the studio specializes in custom cakes and desserts available for pre-order through an online ordering system. Cyclists passing through Richmond's busy Hazelbridge corridor will find it a sweet stop for a break.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Order Link: https://microsite.talech.com/shop/R-KI-DESSERT-STUDIO-RICHMOND-BC/...' and notes the main site is for display only — orders placed through that external link, implying pickup/takeout fulfillment

restaurant.name: Bistro Taiyo
restaurant.desc: Bistro Taiyo is a 100% authentic Japanese-owned sushi bar and izakaya that has been operating in Nanaimo's historic Old City Quarter since 2001. The restaurant is celebrated for handcrafted specialty rolls, in-house ramen, fresh seafood, and traditional izakaya fare paired with an extensive sake and Japanese beer selection. The name 'Taiyo' means 'Sun' in Japanese, reflecting the founders' philosophy of being a welcoming presence for all who visit.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegan ramen options explicitly listed (Vegan Original, Vegan Black, Vegan Tantan) with vegan toppings section; website states 'We have VEGAN RAMEN on our menu now' and references being among the first to serve vegan options. Tofu-based dishes appear throughout the menu

restaurant.name: Horseshoe Bay Chinese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A Chinese and Western restaurant located in the Horseshoe Bay area of North Vancouver. A casual dining spot serving mixed cuisine to locals and passing cyclists.

restaurant.name: Karabji Grill Lebanese Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Karabji Grill is a Lebanese restaurant with halal certification located on Marine Drive in White Rock. The restaurant features outdoor seating for casual dining.

restaurant.name: Romeo's Place
restaurant.desc: Romeo's is a family-owned Italian restaurant chain established in 1974, with one of its four Vancouver Island locations sitting on the Trans-Canada Highway in Duncan. The Duncan outpost serves gourmet pizza, pasta, burgers, and casual favourites in a laid-back, cozy atmosphere. It is a convenient dine-in or takeout option for cyclists travelling through the Cowichan Valley along the Trans-Canada corridor.

restaurant.name: Analog Coffee
restaurant.desc: Analog Coffee is a specialty coffee chain founded in Calgary in 2011, now operating multiple locations including this Vancouver café on Helmcken Street. The brand is built around an obsessive pursuit of sourcing and carefully crafting single-origin coffees, using innovative equipment and celebrating the skill of individual baristas. Touring cyclists stopping here will find a community-focused café with both indoor and outdoor seating in a wheelchair-accessible space.

restaurant.name: Dahlak Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Dahlak African Restaurant is an East African and Mediterranean eatery established in 2019, named after the Dahlak Archipelago off the coast of Eritrea. The menu features traditional dishes alongside hookah service. Touring cyclists riding through the Burnaby area would find it a distinctive cultural dining stop.

restaurant.name: Tojos
restaurant.desc: Tojo's is a celebrated Japanese fine dining restaurant on West Broadway, internationally recognized as the birthplace of the California Roll, created by resident chef Hidekazu Tojo. For nearly four decades it has offered omakase menus built around local, seasonal, and organic Pacific Northwest ingredients. Touring cyclists seeking a special dinner destination or curbside takeout sushi will find a nationally acclaimed kitchen operating on Vancouver's main cycling corridor.

notes.Takeout: Website prominently features a TAKEAWAY section; contact page states 'Curbside Pickup is available. Order Online by 4PM.'

restaurant.name: Panago
restaurant.desc: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain franchise offering delivery and takeout in Langley, BC, with an emphasis on quality ingredients including fresh-made dough from 100% Canadian wheat and no artificial colours or flavours. The chain offers an extensive plant-based, dairy-free, and meat-free menu alongside traditional pizzas, salads, and sides. A touring cyclist can expect a reliable quick-stop for hot pizza or a salad with no drive-through and takeout as the primary service model.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Plant-based options. Fill up and feel good. We've got abundant veggie, dairy-free and meat-free choices to help you live your best plant life.'

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast food restaurant located in North Vancouver, BC, offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, wraps, McCafé beverages, and quick takeout service. As a well-known chain stop, it can serve touring cyclists as a resupply point along the North Shore. The corporate website provides no location-specific details about this outlet.

detail.address: 2001 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2K4, Canada

restaurant.name: Phở Hòa
restaurant.desc: Phở Hòa is a long-running Vietnamese pho franchise founded in 1983, now with over 60 locations across six countries. This Surrey location seats up to 50 guests and specialises in traditional pho prepared with lean, quality meat cuts for a lighter broth. The menu spans beef, chicken, seafood, and vegetarian pho alongside rice plates and vermicelli bowls, with a rewards app available for frequent visitors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Vegetarian Phở Chay' — tofu, broccoli, cauliflower, mushrooms, and carrots in mushroom broth topped with crispy fried shallots

restaurant.name: Match Eatery & Public House
restaurant.desc: Match Eatery & Public House is a casual dining pub chain affiliated with Gateway Casinos, with the Delta location situated along Highway 17A. It offers a full dine-in menu spanning burgers, pasta, pizza, and wings alongside an extensive drinks program, plus takeout and delivery. Touring cyclists passing through the Delta/Tsawwassen corridor will find a reliable full-service stop with hot meals and a broad menu.

restaurant.name: Stega Eatery
restaurant.desc: Stega Eatery is a daytime café on West Cordova Street in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, focused on breakfast, brunch, sandwiches, and salads. It offers gluten-free baked goods including loaves and bagels available for pre-order, signalling a thoughtful approach to dietary needs. Its location near the downtown waterfront makes it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists on the seawall or passing through Gastown.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website subpage title explicitly references 'GF Loaves & Bagels', confirming gluten-free options. OSM cuisine tag includes 'salad', consistent with vegetarian offerings, but

restaurant.name: Ex Animo
restaurant.desc: Ex Animo is a Vancouver-based wholesale coffee roaster and artisan bakery whose name is Latin for 'From the Heart.' Founded by co-owners with over 20 years of combined food-and-beverage experience — including a red seal pastry chef — the operation produces premium espresso blends, single-origin filter coffees, and a full lineup of handcrafted baked goods including croissants, cruffins, and cinnamon buns. The facility is located in an industrial building and appears to focus on supplying cafés, hotels, and restaurants rather than serving walk-in customers.

notes.Takeout: FAQ confirms order pickup is available at the roastery; requires advance ordering (before 9 AM PST) with phone or email

restaurant.name: Porto Peach
restaurant.desc: Porto Peach is a full-service restaurant sitting on Beach Avenue steps from the Okanagan Lake waterfront in Peachland, serving a broad menu that spans breakfast through dinner — from Eggs Benedict and French toast to Mediterranean tapas, Cuban sandwiches, and prime rib beef dip. The restaurant has a lively events calendar including open mic nights, live music, and themed Caribbean dinners. The formerly named Beach Avenue Café & Tapas Bar has rebranded and expanded its offering while keeping the beachside location that makes it a natural stop on the Okanagan touring corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Gluten-free English muffin listed as a menu add-on; vegetarian options confirmed including Jamaican Vegetarian Patties, Greek Pita and Dips, Mediterranean Flatbread, and granola/yogurt/fruit bowl

restaurant.name: ZUBU Ramen
restaurant.desc: ZUBU Ramen is a Japanese-inspired restaurant chain with a Burnaby Metrotown outpost, known for ramen crafted by Executive Chef William Cao who trained at the Kitchen Hyodo Ramen School in Japan. The menu extends well beyond ramen to include fresh temaki, handmade gyoza, rice bowls, and signature Japanese-inspired cocktails. Ingredients are sourced locally or imported from Japan, and the restaurant offers both dine-in and online pickup or delivery options.

detail.address: 4575 Central Boulevard, Unit M101, Burnaby, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists multiple broth and topping options consistent with vegetarian adaptation

restaurant.name: Jay Nok
restaurant.desc: Jay Nok is a modern Thai restaurant in Vancouver's Olympic Village neighbourhood, helmed by Thai-born Executive Chef Bumpen 'Nok' Khangrang and co-owner Bobby Kongsilp, whose family roots stretch back to the legendary Sala Thai. The menu reimagines Thai street food classics — from Khao Soi to Pad Thai — alongside a full cocktail program, in a lively, music-forward dining room a short ride from the Seawall and False Creek cycling paths.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page marks multiple items [GF] (e.g. Green Curry, Central Papaya Salad, Pad Thai) and at least one [V] item (Nok's Fen Fry); tofu substitutions offered on several mains

restaurant.name: Banana Leaf
restaurant.desc: Banana Leaf is Vancouver's original Malaysian restaurant, established in 1995 and now operating five locations across Metro Vancouver, including this Davie Street outpost in the West End. The menu draws on Malaysian, Indonesian, Singaporean, Thai, Chinese, and Indian influences, offering over 40 dishes from Roti Canai to Beef Rendang. The Davie location is wheelchair accessible and offers both dine-in and takeout.

restaurant.name: Bomber Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: Bomber Brewing is an East Vancouver craft brewery whose taproom sits directly on the Adanac cycling corridor, one of Vancouver's most-used bike routes. The taproom pours an extensive rotating lineup of house-brewed Czech-style lagers, ales, IPAs, and stouts, always including two Czech-style side-pull draft taps. Package sales and third-party beer delivery complement the sit-down taproom experience.

restaurant.name: Einstein Wrap House
restaurant.desc: Einstein Wrap House is a fast-food wrap restaurant located on Abbott Street in downtown Vancouver. It offers a quick meal option for cycling tourists passing through the city.

restaurant.name: New West Pizza
restaurant.desc: New West Pizza is a neighbourhood pizza counter in Coquitlam, BC, formerly operating as Pizza One, that has built a local following for its fresh daily dough and traditional recipes. The menu spans classic and specialty pizzas, pasta, Italian dishes, chicken wings, and salads, with several vegetarian-friendly options. It operates as a pickup-only spot, making it a straightforward and filling pitstop for cyclists moving through the Como Lake corridor.

notes.Takeout: 'PICK UP ONLY' listed as a menu category on the website
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes 'VEGETARIAN PIZZA' (bell peppers, onions, mushrooms, tomatoes, olives) and 'VEGE ALFREDO PIZZA' (roasted veggies, Alfredo sauce)

restaurant.name: Ocean Park Pizza & Steakhouse
restaurant.desc: Ocean Park Pizza & Steak House is a family-run Greek-Canadian restaurant in Langley's Brookswood neighbourhood, owned and operated by Maria and Leo, immigrants from Greece with over 50 years of combined restaurant experience. In 30 years of continuous operation it has been voted best pizza in Langley and nominated best steakhouse, offering an extensive menu spanning pizza, steaks, Greek dishes, seafood, and a full bar. Touring cyclists will find a relaxed, full-service sit-down dining option with takeout also available.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Pick Up Available After 12 Noon' on every page
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a vegetarian pizza option ('29. Veg' category listed), salads, and Greek vegetable dishes

restaurant.name: Chicken Box
restaurant.desc: Chicken Box is a Korean-style fried chicken and burger restaurant on Main Street in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, part of a small BC chain with locations also in North Vancouver and Abbotsford. The Main Street location specialises in fried chicken with Korean influence and offers online ordering for convenient pickup. It sits on a well-travelled urban cycling corridor, making it a practical food stop on routes along Main Street.

restaurant.name: Serious Coffee
restaurant.desc: Serious Coffee is a locally-owned BC franchise chain founded in Duncan in 1994, now operating 16 locations across Vancouver Island, Powell River, and New Westminster. The brand distinguishes itself through an air roasting process applied to premium Arabica beans, producing a smoother, less bitter cup than conventional drum roasting. The Nanaimo Jingle Pot Road location offers a full menu of espresso drinks, cold beverages, teas, and fresh baked goods sourced from the company's own bakery adjacent to its Cowichan Valley roasting plant.

restaurant.name: Blacksmith Bakery
restaurant.desc: Blacksmith Bakery is a licensed café bistro founded in 2014 by Chef Stephan Schigas, a pastry veteran of Michelin-starred London kitchens, on the historic site of Fort Langley's original blacksmith shop (Reid's Blacksmith Shop, circa 1910). The Fort Langley flagship offers handcrafted European-style pastries, brunch, bistro fare, and pizza, with both indoor and outdoor seating. It is the anchor location of a small regional chain with four outposts across the Langley and Maple Ridge area.

restaurant.name: Frying Pan
restaurant.desc: Frying Pan is a Korean-style fried chicken brand in Vancouver's West End, serving crispy fried chicken sandwiches, rice bowls, and loaded fries made with halal chicken sourced from local BC farms. The Denman Street dine-in location sits along a well-traveled cycling corridor connecting downtown Vancouver to Stanley Park. The brand also operates a downtown food truck and a catering service, making it a flexible stop for groups of riders.

restaurant.name: Kent's Ice Cream Co.

restaurant.name: Blue Hat Bakery & Cafe

It shares the building with the Blue Hat Bistro event space at the school's West 2nd Avenue campus.

restaurant.name: Blnd Tger Dumplings

restaurant.name: Collective Goods Bistro
restaurant.desc: Collective Goods Bistro is a dinner-focused neighbourhood bistro on Commercial Street in East Vancouver, serving an upscale casual menu of seafood, small plates, and cocktails. The restaurant features a dedicated Happy Hour and a weekly Seafood Sunday, reflecting a focus on quality local ingredients. It operates as a reservations-forward dining room, a pleasant stop for a cyclist's evening meal in the heart of a lively commercial corridor.

restaurant.name: Tea on the Quay
restaurant.desc: Tea on the Quay is a waterfront café on Nanaimo's Front Street, steps from the harbour, with a name evoking a specialty tea focus in a quayside setting. It occupies Unit 3 at 90 Front Street, placing it within easy reach of the seawall and the downtown core frequented by cyclists touring Vancouver Island. OSM records outdoor seating, suggesting an al-fresco option with views toward the water.

restaurant.name: Sabà Cafe and Bistro
restaurant.desc: Sabà is a woman- and family-owned cafe and bistro nestled in historic Fort Langley, drawing inspiration from Mediterranean and Middle Eastern flavours with ingredient-forward, largely seasonal menus. The cafe side at 23343 Mavis Ave offers espresso, baked goods, and all-day light meals including vegan and gluten-free options, with a charming courtyard described as evoking a small Italian piazza. A pre-order system and Grab & Go menu make it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the Fort Langley area.

restaurant.name: The Deck Kitchen + Bar

restaurant.name: purebread
restaurant.desc: Purebread is a well-regarded BC artisan bakery chain with origins in Whistler, now operating seven locations across the province including this spot on the Village Stroll near Olympic Plaza. The bakery has earned recognition from the New York Times, Lonely Planet, and Vogue for its freshly baked breads, pastries, and cakes. The Whistler Village location sits in the heart of the resort corridor, making it a natural refuelling point for cyclists moving through the valley.

restaurant.name: Snackshot

A cyclist looking for a sweet stop in south Richmond will find a photo-friendly, sit-down dessert experience.

restaurant.name: Shaughnessy Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Shaughnessy Restaurant is a garden-inspired sit-down restaurant located within VanDusen Botanical Garden, offering a seasonally driven menu by Chef Pavlo Onopriienko that draws on local seafood, botanicals, and garden produce. Touring cyclists cutting through Vancouver's south side will find a full-service lunch destination amid lush botanical surroundings, with a menu ranging from casual burgers and sandwiches to elegant halibut and scallop dishes. The restaurant is also a venue for weddings and seasonal garden events tied to VanDusen's programming.

restaurant.name: Stan's Pizza Joint

It also offers private event hosting and catering, positioning it as more than a quick stop.

restaurant.name: Mackenzie Cafe

For a cyclist who has made the climb up Burnaby Mountain, it offers a broad range of made-to-order and grab-and-go options in a single stop.

restaurant.name: Mucho Burrito

restaurant.name: Li's China Grill

The restaurant offers table reservations through its website and online ordering. It has been described on its own site as a beloved fixture of the Kingsway dining scene, delivering Sichuan-influenced flavours in the heart of the city.

restaurant.name: The Cod Squad
restaurant.desc: The Cod Squad is a fish and chips restaurant located in Nanaimo, BC, serving classic British-style fried seafood. restaurant.name: Ancora
restaurant.desc: Ancora False Creek is an upscale waterfront restaurant at False Creek in downtown Vancouver serving Peruvian-Japanese fusion cuisine with a focus on sustainable Pacific Northwest seafood. Open since July 2015, it has earned repeated Wine Spectator Awards of Excellence and multiple appearances on Canada's 100 Best Restaurants list. The restaurant's coastal-inspired interior and outdoor patio overlook the False Creek waterfront, placing it directly on one of Vancouver's most popular cycling corridors.

restaurant.name: Moose's Down Under
restaurant.desc: Moose's Down Under is an Australian-themed bar and grill that has anchored Vancouver's downtown pub scene since 1995, tucked into a basement on West Pender Street near the Burrard and Waterfront SkyTrain stations. The kitchen turns out Aussie comfort food — kangaroo burgers, chicken parmies, lamingtons, and pavlova — alongside Australian beers like Cooper's Pale Ale that the owners say are unique to their bar in Vancouver. It doubles as the city's hub for live AFL, NRL, and cricket streaming.

restaurant.name: 54th Ave Cafe

The restaurant offers both eat-in dining and a fully integrated online ordering system for takeout and delivery. Its extensive menu and community-oriented atmosphere make it a practical meal stop for cyclists riding the nearby routes along 49th Avenue or the Central Valley Greenway.

restaurant.name: Bar Burrito
restaurant.desc: BarBurrito is Canada's largest burrito chain, proudly Canadian since 2005, with over 385 locations. This Nanaimo outpost sits inside Port Place mall on Terminal Avenue, offering build-your-own Mexican-inspired meals including burritos, bowls, tacos, and quesadillas with a wide range of proteins and toppings. It's a quick, no-fuss refuelling stop for cyclists passing through central Nanaimo.

restaurant.name: Pourquoi Pas
restaurant.desc: Pourquoi Pas is a modern French-inspired artisan patisserie in Coquitlam, BC, founded by self-taught pastry chef Annie Chang, who trained formally in Vancouver before opening her own shop in 2022. The bakery is known for labour-intensive butter croissants (a 4-day process using only real ingredients) and a creative menu spanning viennoiseries, cakes, choux, canelés, savoury pull-aparts, and coffee drinks. It is a genuine neighbourhood café-patisserie offering quality handmade pastries and coffee — a rewarding stop for touring cyclists looking for a proper treat.

restaurant.name: Doner Dude

A touring cyclist can expect a quick, filling meal with both meat and vegan options in a fast-casual setting.

restaurant.name: Dante Italian Sandwich

restaurant.name: Alpine Cafe

Its location outside the main village gives it a quieter, neighbourhood character that makes it a worthwhile detour for cyclists on the corridor.

restaurant.name: Yoka's

The shop stocks more than twenty single-sourced and blended coffees—including fair-trade and certified organic options—alongside loose tea, chocolate, and local honey. It is a cash-only shop with an old-world, non-corporate character, about a 15-minute walk from Old Town Victoria.

restaurant.name: Rendezvous
restaurant.desc: Rendezvous is Whistler Blackcomb's on-mountain day lodge, perched on Whistler Mountain and accessible in summer via the resort's gondola and lift infrastructure used by the Whistler Mountain Bike Park. It serves as a major rest and refuelling stop for riders tackling the bike park's trails. Being a full-service resort dining facility operated by Vail Resorts, it offers a sit-down food experience in a dramatic mountain setting.

restaurant.name: Zhao Mah Bakery Ltd
restaurant.desc: Zhao Mah Bakery Ltd (金峰餅店) is a Chinese bakery located in Vancouver's Chinatown neighbourhood on East Pender Street. A touring cyclist passing through Chinatown would find this a convenient stop for a quick snack in a historically rich area.

restaurant.name: Myth Szechuan Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Myth Szechuan Cuisine is a nature-inspired sit-down restaurant in Richmond specialising in bold Sichuan and Hunan dishes. The interior features natural wood tables, living plants, and fresh flowers, creating a calm forest-like atmosphere amid spicy, aromatic food. Takeout is available through multiple platforms, making it a feasible quick-stop option for cyclists passing through the Ackroyd Road area.

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: Tim Hortons is a Canadian quick-service chain with a dine-in, drive-thru, and take-out location in Nanaimo's Uplands area. The menu spans freshly brewed coffee, espresso-based drinks, baked goods including Timbits and donuts, breakfast wraps, soups, and sandwiches. It is a reliably consistent stop for touring cyclists looking for a hot drink, a quick meal, or free WiFi on a long ride.

restaurant.name: Steve's Poke Bar

Touring cyclists can order customizable bowls or signature creations in-store or for pickup via the restaurant's app.

restaurant.name: The Garden Café at VanDusen
restaurant.desc: The Garden Café sits inside VanDusen Botanical Garden's LEED-certified Visitor Centre, offering Fair Trade coffees, handcrafted beverages, handmade sandwiches, soups, curries, and daily-changing locally-inspired entrees with views of the surrounding flora. The indoor space seats 58 and the heated patio accommodates 40. In summer the café offers popular picnic baskets, making it a potential destination stop for cyclists exploring the garden's 55 acres.

restaurant.name: Amberdo Cafe and Bakery

The interior uses wood, stone, and greenery to create a calm retreat from urban activity, and the cafe hosts community events including open mic nights and art exhibitions. With seven years of history and five active locations across the city, it has become a well-established neighbourhood hub.

restaurant.name: Gallagher's Cafe

Both dine-in and take-out are available, with outdoor seating and a broad menu that accommodates vegan, gluten-free, and nut-free diets.

restaurant.name: Louie's Steakhouse

Cyclists stopping in Nelson will find a full sit-down dinner experience backed by a serious bar program including the city's largest scotch, rum, and digestif collections.

restaurant.name: Green Olive Market & Café

restaurant.name: Blackbird Bakery

Located in the village train centre with both indoor and outdoor seating, it offers fresh bread, croissants, sandwiches, and savoury pies—solid provisions for a touring cyclist passing through the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

restaurant.name: Do Chay

restaurant.name: Mnimes Restaurant

The restaurant has received recognition through the Greek Taste Beyond Borders program and the Canadian Choice Awards.

restaurant.name: BNA Brewery

restaurant.name: John B Pub

restaurant.name: Guu Toramasa

restaurant.name: Le Belisse Cafe

restaurant.name: Genoa Bay Café

restaurant.name: Paragon Tea Room

restaurant.name: Oishinoya Japanese Gyudon

restaurant.name: Off The Rail Tasting Room

restaurant.name: Wild Oak Café

Touring cyclists will find a clean, non-smoking space with both indoor and outdoor seating and free Wi-Fi.

restaurant.name: The Brunch Club & Coffee Bar

restaurant.name: The Taphouse

It is a 19+ venue with live music nights and operates as a community gathering spot.
