Their lineup spans dozens of distinct ciders, including ice cider and keeved expressions that reflect serious traditional craft.

restaurant.name: Communal Kitchen
restaurant.desc: The Communal Kitchen is a fully equipped self-catering kitchen house at the Canadian Princess Lodge & Marina on Ucluelet Harbour. It includes two stovetops, two ovens, two refrigerators, a cooking island, and a covered private terrace with high-top seating and a firepit — a rare find for cyclists who prefer to cook their own meals rather than eat out. Access is available exclusively to resort guests via a front-desk rental arrangement.

restaurant.name: Krave Kulture
restaurant.desc: Krave Kulture is a craft yogurt shop in Edgemont Village that bills itself as Vancouver's first, founded during the pandemic by Kamran and Moji and now expanded to a second location at Lonsdale Quay. The shop makes fresh yogurt in-house daily from organic Canadian milk, serving froyo bowls, smoothies, and probiotic-rich kefir. It has grown into a community hub and offers school and corporate programs alongside its walk-up retail trade.

restaurant.name: Billy G's Doughnuts
restaurant.desc: Billy G's Doughnuts is a fresh-made doughnut shop within The Old Country Market, a 50-year-old Coombs landmark on the Alberni Highway — the main cycling and driving corridor to the west coast of Vancouver Island. The shop is famous for a large rotating menu of crullers, fritters, and inventively named doughnuts with local flavour references (Nanaimo Bar, Coombs Cut Off, Ukee Magic). The broader market campus includes groceries, a deli, a garden centre, and multiple restaurants, making it a substantial stop for cyclists passing through.

restaurant.name: Firehouse Subs
restaurant.desc: Firehouse Subs is a sandwich chain serving hot toasted subs, operating out of a single-storey building in Fort St. John's commercial corridor on 96A Street. The brand is notable for its Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation, which has donated over $100 million in lifesaving equipment to first responders. Takeout is available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Peace River region.

restaurant.name: Got Lot Tea
restaurant.desc: Got Lot Tea is a bubble tea café situated in a unit along Kingsway, one of Burnaby's main commercial corridors. It offers indoor seating, making it a potential rest stop for cyclists on that route. The café specializes in bubble tea drinks.

restaurant.name: Ganh Vietnamese Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Ganh Vietnamese Kitchen is an Indochine-inspired sit-down restaurant on Vancouver's Kingsway corridor serving authentic dishes including signature Pho, Bun Bo Hue, Bun Ca, Bun Rieu Cua, and Com Tam prepared by Vietnamese descendants with traditional techniques. The elegantly appointed interior is designed for private dining, business meetings, and group events with large communal tables. Founded to introduce Vietnamese culinary heritage to Canadian diners, Ganh emphasizes hand-selected spices and dedicated dipping sauces for each dish.

restaurant.name: Bull River Inn
restaurant.desc: Bull River Inn is a pub situated in the Bull River valley southeast of Cranbrook, in the rugged East Kootenay region of British Columbia. The area sits along quiet back roads that connect cycling routes between Cranbrook and the Alberta border, making a local pub a welcome landmark for self-supported tourers. Specific details about the establishment's layout, food, and services remain unverifiable due to inaccessible online content.

detail.address: 4569 Wardner Fort Steele Rd, Bull River, BC V0B 1N0, Canada

restaurant.name: Secret Garden
restaurant.desc: Secret Garden is a Korean buffet and grill restaurant situated beside Lougheed Town Centre Mall in Burnaby, offering an all-you-can-eat experience of Korean cuisine in a sit-down indoor setting. The restaurant also offers takeout boxes for customers who want to bring the buffet experience home. It is a full-service dine-in establishment suited for a longer meal stop on a ride.

restaurant.name: Cenote Restaurant and Lounge
restaurant.desc: Cenote Lounge has been a downtown Victoria institution since 2012, situated downstairs beneath street level on Yates Street for a subterranean, cave-like atmosphere. The bar is celebrated for award-winning craft cocktails and a rotating menu of shareable plates ranging from garlic prawns and duck wings to lamb sliders and baked brie. A touring cyclist finishing a day on the road would find an inventive drinks program and satisfying small-plate dining in the heart of the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu explicitly states flatbreads are available gluten-free (+3) and/or dairy-free (+2); drinks menu features 'House-made Vegan Whisky Cream Liqueur' and 'Vegan Foamer'; multiple vegetarian share plates are available (tabbouleh salad, warm focaccia, chips & salsa, marinated olives, nachos, etc.)

restaurant.name: Sushi Kamizato
restaurant.desc: Sushi K Kamizato is an intimate, reservation-only omakase restaurant in Port Coquitlam where Executive Chef Keith Kamizato — originally from Okinawa, Japan — crafts personalized multi-course sushi meals set to a rock music soundtrack. The restaurant is run entirely by Keith and his wife Chika, who aim to create a distinctive, chef-driven experience far removed from standard sushi dining. A touring cyclist looking for a memorable sit-down dinner in the Tri-Cities area would find this a highly unique option.

restaurant.name: KI-ISU Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: KI-ISU is a Japanese restaurant on Marine Drive in West Vancouver offering a wide-ranging menu spanning sushi, sashimi, pressed sushi, Japanese curry, tempura, udon, and donburi alongside specialty rolls and combination sets. It sits on a well-travelled cycling corridor along the North Shore and accepts online orders for in-house pickup. Indoor seating is available, making it a practical refueling stop for cyclists exploring the area.

detail.address: 1534 Marine Drive, West Vancouver, BC V7V 1H8

restaurant.name: Cardero Cafe
restaurant.desc: Cardero Cafe is a neighbourhood cafe situated at 1016 Cardero Street in Vancouver's West End, steps from the Stanley Park seawall cycling route. OSM records it as a standalone building with both vegan and vegetarian menu options. Its location on a quiet residential street makes it a natural stop for cyclists riding the seawall or exploring the West End.

restaurant.name: Uva
restaurant.desc: Uva Wine & Cocktail Bar is an award-winning downtown Vancouver institution occupying a dual identity: a European-inspired caffè bar by day serving handcrafted coffees, fresh juices, and small plates, and a celebrated wine and cocktail destination by night. Located at the heart of Vancouver's cultural and entertainment district, it has garnered numerous industry awards for its seasonal cocktail and wine program. Part of the Viaggio Hospitality group, it also offers a private dining room (the Madonna Room) for up to 12 guests.

restaurant.name: Pita Land Mideast Urban Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Pita Land Mideast Urban Kitchen is a Canadian halal fast-food chain with over 50 locations, specializing in fresh Middle Eastern fare including shawarma wraps, falafel, garlic potato bowls, and plates with choice of protein. All meat is 100% Halal hand-certified and the menu is built around real, unprocessed ingredients. The brand explicitly caters to vegetarian, gluten-free, and keto dietary needs, making it a flexible stop for cyclists with varied nutrition requirements.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Whether your diet is gluten or dairy-free, vegetarian, or keto, Pita Land has OPTIONS.' Menu includes falafel, salad bowls, and hummus/baba ganoush appetizers

restaurant.name: Craig Street Brew Pub
restaurant.desc: Craig Street Brew Pub is a locally rooted craft brewery and full-service restaurant that has anchored downtown Duncan since 2006, housed in a cedar-beamed space with high ceilings and vintage West Coast character. Cyclists can watch new batches being brewed from the dining room, and the kitchen focuses on Cowichan Valley ingredients — house nachos, pear salads, and taco salads among the popular eats. It is the flagship of a small family of Cowichan Valley venues, making it a natural hub for riders exploring the valley.

restaurant.name: Fatburger
restaurant.desc: Fatburger is a casual burger chain with roots dating to Los Angeles in 1947, operating in Canada since 2005 and proudly Canadian-owned. The Lougheed Coquitlam location serves cooked-to-order burgers made with fresh-never-frozen Alberta Angus beef, alongside chicken wings, veggie burgers, hand-scooped milkshakes, and homemade onion rings. Takeout and delivery are available, making it a convenient refuelling stop along the Lougheed Highway corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'veggie burgers & sandwiches' as a menu item

restaurant.name: Togo Sushi
restaurant.desc: Togo Sushi is a BC-based quick-service sushi chain offering fresh rolls and Japanese staples strictly for takeout, with no dine-in seating. This location sits inside Metropolis at Metrotown mall on Level 1, making it a convenient grab-and-go stop for cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor. The chain operates multiple Lower Mainland locations and accepts online orders through its website and app.

restaurant.name: Yama Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Yama Kitchen is a casual Japanese restaurant on Richter Street in Kelowna, offering sushi and appetizers alongside a western-inspired menu in a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere. Owner and head chef Mancheol Kim holds a professional Japanese cuisine certification earned through study in Japan and brings over a decade of experience to the kitchen. It sits a block from Clement Ave near Dr. Knox Mountain and is described as having ample parking.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'After 2:00pm and After 8:00pm, Takeout Order Only', confirming takeout service is available

restaurant.name: Bubble Waffle Cafe
restaurant.desc: Bubble Waffle Cafe brings Hong Kong street-snack culture to the Vancouver area, serving its namesake egg waffles (雞蛋仔), curry fish balls, rice noodle rolls, and fish soup noodle combos with an expansive array of Taiwanese-style milk teas and fruit drinks. The cafe operates across multiple Metro Vancouver locations including Aberdeen Centre, the Public Market, and Park Royal. It is a quick-service counter-style spot ideal for a fuelling stop mid-ride.

detail.address: Park Royal FC03 - 2002 Park Royal South, West Vancouver, BC V7T 2W4

restaurant.name: Cactus Club Cafe
restaurant.desc: Cactus Club Cafe is a well-known upscale-casual Canadian chain with a Nanaimo location in the Northridge Village retail area on Turner Road. The chef-driven menu spans sushi, handhelds, pasta, steaks, and desserts, backed by a full lounge, patio, happy hour, and private dining spaces. Touring cyclists will find a reliable option for a substantial sit-down meal or a pickup order after a long ride.

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Freshslice Pizza is a Canadian fast-food pizza chain with a franchise location in Chilliwack, BC. The brand is known for by-the-slice pizza with customizable toppings available for in-store pickup or delivery. It operates as a takeout-focused establishment and could serve as a quick calorie stop for cyclists passing through town.

restaurant.name: Thai Son Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Thai Son is a Vietnamese restaurant with five locations offering authentic Vietnamese cuisine. The business provides both dine-in and takeout service, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking a quick meal or sit-down dining.

restaurant.name: Fred's
restaurant.desc: Fred's is a modern Italian kitchen owned by Catalog Hospitality, serving handmade pasta, wood-fired-style pizzas, and Italian small plates across three BC locations — Ambleside in West Vancouver, Sechelt, and Kitsilano. The Ambleside location offers private dining for groups up to 48 seated and features an exclusive wine list alongside a thoughtful cocktail program. Cyclists riding the North Shore waterfront corridor will find it a well-positioned sit-down meal stop in the Ambleside village.

detail.address: 1467 Bellevue Ave, West Vancouver, BC V7T 1B8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items across all three location menus are labelled VE (vegetarian/vegan), GF (gluten-free), DF (dairy-free), and PB (plant-based), e.g. Market Greens (VE, GF, DF), Harvest pizza (PB), Smoked Marinated Olives (PB, GF)

restaurant.name: 49th Parallel Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: 49th Parallel Coffee Roasters is a celebrated BC-based specialty coffee chain; the Lonsdale location is their fifth cafe, opened March 2022. It occupies a heritage building whose interior design draws from the site's early-1900s mercantile history as a hardware store, using repurposed materials to create an authentic, permanent feel. For a touring cyclist rolling through North Vancouver, it offers a well-regarded espresso program and takeout in a distinctive stop on Lonsdale Avenue.

detail.address: 93 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2E5

restaurant.name: Yi Fang Tea
restaurant.desc: Yi Fang Tea is a bubble tea café specializing in fruit-based tea beverages available for takeaway. Operating as part of a Taiwan-based franchise, it provides a quick refreshment stop in North Vancouver. Cyclists passing through can grab a beverage without needing to linger indoors.

restaurant.name: Be Fresh Market
restaurant.desc: Be Fresh Market is a community-oriented organic cafe and local market in Kitsilano, cultivated by SPUD.ca, serving wholesome meals and fresh juices made from locally sourced and organic ingredients. It has earned a devoted neighbourhood following, with customers praising the house-made nut milks, specialty coffee, and relaxed work-friendly atmosphere. The 1900 West 1st Ave location is the flagship Cypress Market, with a sister store operating as Organic Acres on Main Street.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website consistently emphasizes healthy, organic, locally sourced ingredients throughout, consistent with vegan and vegetarian options

restaurant.name: Mag's 99
restaurant.desc: Mag's 99 is a vibrant fusion restaurant in Squamish that marries Mexican cantina staples — burritos, chimichangas, tacos, and enchiladas — with signature crispy fried chicken and loaded poutines, earning a loyal local following for its generous portions and fast service. The restaurant is an established presence in the Sea-to-Sky corridor and is actively expanding via a franchise model. Touring cyclists will find a broad comfort-food menu with clearly marked vegetarian and gluten-free options well-suited for refuelling after rides.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels vegetarian (V) and gluten-free (GF) options including Burrito Bowl (V/GF), Enchiladas (V/GF), Taco Salada (V), and Burrito (V); plant-based proteins listed are crispy cauliflower, golden falafel, and Spanish beans

restaurant.name: Big Orange
restaurant.desc: Big Orange is a BC-born bubble tea franchise that launched at Metrotown Mall in Burnaby in 1996 and has grown to more than 20 locations across Canada, the US, and Malaysia. This Metrotown unit — the original flagship store — offers fresh fruit bubble teas, smoothies, slushes, ice cream drinks, Belgium waffles, and freshly squeezed juices. Located inside the mall at level 1, it makes a convenient refreshment stop for cyclists passing through Burnaby's commercial core.

restaurant.name: Aloha Hawaiian Grill
restaurant.desc: Aloha Hawaiian Grill is a family-owned fast-casual restaurant in Richmond bringing Hawaiian plate lunch culture to the BC coast, with signature dishes like Huli Huli Chicken, Maui Beef Ribs, and shave ice served in a laid-back, island-themed setting. The restaurant celebrates the multicultural food heritage of Hawaii and treats guests like 'ohana' (family). It also offers corporate and event catering, making it a convenient stop for larger cycling groups.

detail.address: Unit 110 - 3900 Bayview Street, Richmond, BC V7E 4R7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Maui Tofu and Vegetarian Spring Rolls; catering page notes 'Vegan options available also if you ask!'; catering page lists garlic shrimp and spam as gluten-free options

restaurant.name: Bar Corso
restaurant.desc: Bar Corso is a modern Italian bar in Vancouver's Little Italy neighbourhood on Commercial Drive, specializing in cicchetti (small Italian tapas), craft cocktails, grappa, and a curated wine selection. Executive Chef Luke Boswell leads a seasonal, ever-changing menu rooted in classic Italian technique and local ingredients, with intimate winemaker dinners rounding out the experience. Walk-ins are welcome, and the convivial late-night atmosphere makes it a natural evening destination for cyclists exploring the Drive.

restaurant.name: Latin Square
restaurant.desc: Latin Square is a Latin American cafe and snack shop on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, serving espresso drinks, frappes, and an eclectic roster of traditional foods from across the region — empanadas from Argentina, Colombia, Peru, and Chile, alongside tamales, arepas, churros, and tres leches cake. The shop also carries Latin grocery products and celebrates Latin American Independence events with themed specials. It bills itself as Vancouver's favourite Latin coffee shop and draws a lively neighbourhood crowd.

restaurant.name: Privé
restaurant.desc: Privé is an upscale Kitchen + Bar + Karaoke venue on West Broadway in Vancouver, offering full dining, patio seating, and private karaoke rooms bookable online. It operates as an evening and nightlife destination, making it a distinctive option for cyclists seeking a sit-down dinner or a group night out. The combination of a full kitchen and private entertainment rooms sets it apart from a typical neighbourhood restaurant.

restaurant.name: Sasquatch Inn
restaurant.desc: The Sasquatch Inn is a family-owned pub and inn along the Lougheed Highway in the Fraser Valley, continuously operated since 1954 by the Maclean family. It offers a full sit-down restaurant menu alongside accommodations bookable online, making it a potential rest stop or overnight destination for touring cyclists on the Highway 7 corridor. The inn has a local community character, hosting an annual motorcycle Show & Shine and charity golf tournament.

restaurant.name: SUD Café
restaurant.desc: SUD Café is a French-inspired café in Vancouver's West End, founded by the owners of Gastown's PETRICHOR restaurant and devoted to the relaxed culinary spirit of the South of France. The kitchen turns out house-made pastries and viennoiserie—croissants, fougasse, moelleux au chocolat—alongside brunch sandwiches built on fresh brioche and a full espresso bar with specialty drinks like apricot-lavender iced matcha. Its intimate space doubles as a private-events venue, making it a versatile neighbourhood anchor for cyclists exploring the West End.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian options: Roasted Vegetable Sando, Avocado Toast, Spinach & Mushroom Feuilleté, Ratatouille & Goat Cheese Feuilleté, Blueberry Granola Parfait, and Small Spring Mix. No explicit vegan or gluten-free labelling found

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: A Starbucks Coffee location on Southwest Marine Drive in south Vancouver, part of the international chain that notably expanded from Seattle to Vancouver in the late 1980s. The store sits on a busy arterial corridor with outdoor seating, making it a recognizable waypoint for cyclists traveling through this part of the city. A full menu of espresso drinks, seasonal Refreshers, and light food items is available.

restaurant.name: Boston Pizza
restaurant.desc: Boston Pizza is Canada's largest casual dining chain, founded in Edmonton in 1964 and operating hundreds of locally owned franchise locations coast-to-coast. This Chilliwack location runs as a full-service restaurant and sports bar serving pizza, pasta, wings, sandwiches, and more. For a touring cyclist, it offers a reliable sit-down meal with broad menu coverage including gluten-wise and vegan options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states: 'Vegan and Glutenwise® options also available.'

restaurant.name: Joe Burger
restaurant.desc: Joe Burger is a fast-casual smash burger counter tucked inside the Country Club Centre food court in Nanaimo, known for hand-crafted burgers made from fresh-ground beef and daily-prepared ingredients. The menu spans classic burgers, poutine, onion rings, breakfast sandwiches, and churros, and the spot has earned a reputation as one of the top-rated burger destinations in the city. The sheltered mall food court setting with ample seating makes it a practical and filling refuelling stop for touring cyclists passing through Nanaimo.

detail.address: 3200 North Island Highway, Nanaimo, BC V9T 1W1

restaurant.name: Moon Wok
restaurant.desc: Moon Wok is a family-owned Chinese restaurant operating three locations across Kamloops, with the Valleyview location on Oriole Road. The menu spans over 100 items including appetizers, entrees, and combo dinners, with vegetarian and gluten-free options available. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, delivery, and full catering services, making it a versatile meal stop for cyclists of varying group sizes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Whether you're vegetarian or have food allergies, we have plenty of delicious menu choices' and 'Be sure to ask about our gluten-free menu'

restaurant.name: Chad Thai Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Chad Thai Restaurant is a Thai restaurant in Burnaby, BC offering traditional Thai cuisine. It serves as a potential meal and beverage stop for touring cyclists in the Hastings Street corridor.

restaurant.name: Tartine Bread & Pies
restaurant.desc: Tartine Bread & Pies is a neighbourhood bakery established in 2002, situated just off English Bay on Beach Avenue in Vancouver. Founded by Jo-Ann and grown from a home kitchen, it serves freshly baked pies, quiches, muffins, breads, and pastries alongside soups, salads, and breakfast and lunch sandwiches. The bakery uses premium natural ingredients with no artificial preservatives and offers both indoor and outdoor seating.

restaurant.name: Los Cuervos Taqueria & Cantina
restaurant.desc: Los Cuervos Taqueria & Cantina is an authentic Mexican restaurant in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, inspired by the street stalls and cantinas of Mexico and using fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The menu spans signature tacos and burritos to weekend brunch dishes like Huevos Rancheros, alongside handcrafted cocktails and margaritas. Cyclists seeking a sit-down meal or a quick online order can also pick up take-home taco and margarita kits.

restaurant.name: Ratio Coffee and Pastry
restaurant.desc: Ratio Coffee & Pastry is a community-rooted Vernon café with an origin story tailor-made for cyclists: it began as a coffee cart on bike wheels before growing into a full-service espresso and pastry destination. The café is known for its quality-first ethos, daily brunch service, and a cult-favourite Friday donut program that sells out on a pre-order system. A private meeting room and a warm, inviting atmosphere round out a spot that has clearly become a social hub for the neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Molly Tea
restaurant.desc: Molly Tea is a Chinese jasmine tea beverage franchise originating from Shenzhen, built around high-quality floral teas scented with fresh flowers and inspired by the Four White Flowers of the East. The Richmond Union Square location offers a menu of fresh milk teas, snowy whipped cream drinks, oat milk teas, and floral fruit slushes, all centred on jasmine and other Eastern floral aromas. It is part of an expanding international chain with over 1,000 locations in China and growing presence across Canada, the US, UK, Australia, and Thailand.

restaurant.name: Bluefin Sushi
restaurant.desc: Bluefin Sushi is a Japanese fusion restaurant in New Westminster's Columbia Street corridor, specializing in fresh sushi made from seafood, meat, and produce the kitchen describes as the finest available. The restaurant offers indoor seating and online ordering, making it a straightforward lunch or dinner stop for cyclists moving through the Lower Mainland.

detail.address: 319 E Columbia St, New Westminster, BC V3L 3W8

restaurant.name: Dosa Corner
restaurant.desc: Dosa Corner is an authentic South Indian restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver that has been operating since 2012. The menu spans a wide range of dosas, idlis, vadas, chutneys, and South Indian soups alongside chicken, mutton, and seafood dishes, earning a Best Indian Award in 2019. The restaurant bills itself as a family-style spot, making it a solid stop for cyclists wanting a filling, flavour-forward meal on the Fraser Street corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu extensively labels dishes as '(Veg)'; About Us page states dosas 'are usually considered appropriate for vegetarians and individuals with wheat allergies.'

restaurant.name: Subcity Donair
restaurant.desc: Subcity Donair is a BC-based donair and sub chain with a Westside Kelowna location on Industrial Road. The restaurant is known for beef and chicken donairs made with top sirloin and a proprietary blend of 23 herbs and spices, served with a choice of seven sauces. A dedicated veggie menu including freshly prepared falafel and vegetarian pita makes it a flexible refuelling stop for cyclists with varied dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website About page highlights a dedicated 'VEGGIE LOVERS' section; menu lists falafel and Vegetarian Pita under Veggie Delights

restaurant.name: Townhall Public House
restaurant.desc: Townhall Public House is a contemporary pub restaurant operated by JRG Restaurant Group on Lougheed Highway in Maple Ridge, offering classic pub fare with a modern twist — from chicken wings and perogies to pizza and brunch. The space is designed to feel like a neighbourhood gathering place, with a full bar program, group booking options, and an online ordering system. Touring cyclists would find a solid mid-ride meal stop with a broad menu including dietary-friendly options.

detail.address: 206-20690 Lougheed Highway, Maple Ridge, BC V2X 2P8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page explicitly labels items as VEGETARIAN, VEGAN, GLUTEN AWARE, and DAIRY-FREE

restaurant.name: Pizza64
restaurant.desc: Pizza64 is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 2010, with over 20 locations across British Columbia, known for making fresh dough and sauce at each individual location. The Surrey location sits in a commercial unit on 64 Avenue and offers a broad menu of specialty, signature, and gourmet pizzas alongside wings, pasta, and sides. Online ordering and a loyalty rewards program are available, making it a convenient refuelling stop on a longer ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian pizza options: Garden Fresh (onions, mushrooms, black olives, tomatoes, green peppers, pizza sauce, mozzarella) and Pesto Veggie (garlic, spinach, onions, green peppers, tomatoes, mozzarella, pesto sauce). No vegan or gluten-free options explicitly mentioned

restaurant.name: Bae Side
restaurant.desc: Bae Side is a waterfront restaurant and event venue on the False Creek seawall in Vancouver, operated by Mishree Restaurant Concepts (the team behind Tandoori Flame and Happy Singh Eats) at the former Mahony & Sons location. It serves pan-Asian tapas, fresh salads, and handcrafted cocktails from an indoor-outdoor space with skyline views and a 300+ seat patio. With capacity for up to 600 guests and a dog-friendly patio, it is a substantial stop on one of Vancouver's most popular cycling corridors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Navigation menu includes a dedicated 'Vegan & Kids' menu section

restaurant.name: Audielicious
restaurant.desc: Audielicious is an eclectic sit-down restaurant in Fort St. John offering an unusually broad menu that spans steakhouse cuts, fresh seafood platters, Filipino cuisine favourites, burgers, and sandwiches all under one roof. The Filipino influence sets it apart from typical northern BC eateries, with dishes like pork shumai, wonton soup, and spring rolls alongside Western classics. It operates as a full-service restaurant with delivery and takeout also available through SkipTheDishes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Vegetable Burger (vegetable patty) and Fried Vegetable Spring Roll (6 pcs), confirming vegetarian options

restaurant.name: Just Jake's
restaurant.desc: Just Jakes is recorded in OpenStreetMap as a restaurant in Duncan, BC, but no verifiable contact information or website specific to this location exists in the available data. restaurant.name: The Courtney Room
restaurant.desc: The Courtney Room is an award-winning fine dining restaurant located in the Magnolia Hotel, two blocks from Victoria's Inner Harbour. It offers seasonally driven menus built on classic European techniques and locally sourced ingredients including in-house dry-aged beef, sustainable seafood, and produce from local farm partners. The restaurant earned Restaurant of the Year at the 2024 YAM Magazine Best Restaurant Awards and Platinum Distinction in the 2025 VIWF Wine Program Excellence Awards.

restaurant.name: Lucky Fortune Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Lucky Fortune Seafood Restaurant (天喜海鲜酒家) is a long-standing Cantonese-style seafood restaurant on Granville Street in South Vancouver, serving a broad range of regional Chinese cuisines including Cantonese, Sichuan, and Shanghainese dishes. It accommodates tourist groups and banquet-style dining, which could suit larger cycling parties. Dine-in, pickup, delivery, and catering are all available.

restaurant.name: Trees Organic Coffee
restaurant.desc: Trees Organic Coffee is a Vancouver institution founded in 1996, operating 13+ locations across the city and known for in-house small-batch roasted organic coffee and award-winning New York-style cheesecakes made fresh daily. This Granville Street branch is one of two the chain operates on that corridor in the heart of downtown Vancouver. Cyclists passing through the city core will find a full cafe menu of sandwiches, baked goods, and teas alongside the signature coffee and cheesecake.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists sandwiches, salads, baked goods, and cheesecakes consistent with vegetarian options

restaurant.name: Sushi Yama
restaurant.desc: Sushi Yama is a Japanese sushi restaurant on East Broadway in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, offering dine-in service with air-conditioned indoor seating and a full menu of sushi and Japanese cuisine. The restaurant is wheelchair accessible and supports online ordering as well as in-person dining, making it a convenient midride meal stop along the busy Broadway corridor. Vegetarian options are available, broadening its appeal to diverse touring groups.

restaurant.name: Lee's Donuts
restaurant.desc: Lee's Donuts is a beloved BC institution founded in 1979 at Granville Island Public Market, now expanded to over ten locations including this outpost inside Willowbrook Mall in Langley. The shop is known for handmade, classic donuts crafted fresh daily from original recipes, with rotating seasonal flavours alongside perennial favourites like the Honey Dip. A handy stop for a quick sugar boost mid-ride on the Fraser Highway corridor.

restaurant.name: Diya Restaurant & Sweets
restaurant.desc: Diya Restaurant & Sweets is a fully vegetarian Indian restaurant serving an extensive menu of North Indian mains, South Indian dosas, street-food chaats, Indo-Chinese dishes, and house-made sweets. The kitchen uses freshly ground herbs and no MSG, with every dish customizable from mild to extra spicy. It offers a warm sit-down dining room alongside pickup and direct-contact delivery.

restaurant.name: East Café in Marpole
restaurant.desc: East Café is a community-focused café built around the concept of the 'third place' — a welcoming space outside home and work where neighbours connect over coffee. It operates the City Smiles initiative, which has served over 3,200 free meals and drinks to homeless community members, and hosts weekly events including open mic nights, a book club, creative writing sessions, and Sunday jazz. The OSM node identifies this as the Marpole branch of the East Café brand, formerly operating as Gigi Blin.

restaurant.name: Coffee + Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Coffee + Kitchen is the on-site restaurant at WOODS on Pender, a glamping resort set on 7.3 forested acres adjacent to Prior Centennial National Park on Pender Island. By day it operates as an artisan coffee house serving fresh-baked pastries and Fernwood Coffee Company coffee; by evening it becomes a farm-to-table dinner restaurant with hand-crafted cocktails and a B.C. wine and local craft beer list. The restaurant is open to the public — not just resort guests — and features both indoor seating for up to 22 and a patio for an additional 16.

The booth-style seating and friendly staff make it a welcoming stop for cyclists passing through Coquitlam.

restaurant.name: Hello Toast

Cyclists will find a welcoming, casual atmosphere with a sidewalk-side patio and a menu ranging from creative egg dishes to hearty grain bowls.

restaurant.name: Frog Peak Café & Guesthouse

restaurant.name: Illuminate Restorante

restaurant.name: Empire Coffee

restaurant.name: Jenna's

restaurant.name: Sweet Puffin

restaurant.name: Q Pizza

restaurant.name: Parsley Doner

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Veggie Full Nelson Sandwich'; other vegetarian-friendly items include Avocado on Toast, PB & J on Toast, and Muesli & Yogurt Bowl. Vegan and GF not explicitly labeled

restaurant.name: Fresh Cup Roastery Café
restaurant.desc: Fresh Cup Roastery Café is an independent, award-winning craft coffee roastery and café that sources farmer-direct, single-origin, organic Arabica beans and roasts them in-house using patented Roastaire® technology designed to produce near-zero emissions. The business has earned multiple accolades including the 2020 Peninsula Readers Choice for 'Best Coffee' and consecutive Golden Bean awards. The website references a lower mainland café alongside its Vancouver Island locations, though the Surrey address is not explicitly listed or detailed.

restaurant.name: A Wee Cupcakery
restaurant.desc: A Wee Cupcakery is a small-batch specialty cupcake shop tucked into Nanaimo's historic Old City Quarter, a short roll from the downtown core and waterfront. The shop produces an ever-rotating lineup of original-recipe cupcakes and specialty baked goods using fresh dairy, eggs, and Belgian Callebaut Chocolate. Vegan and gluten-free options are available daily, making it a welcoming treat stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

restaurant.name: La Tortilleria
restaurant.desc: La Tortilleria is a Mexican food counter located inside the Granville Island Public Market, serving fresh, made-daily dishes including burritos, tacos, enchiladas, and slow-rotisserie chicken with a house marinade. The stall also offers a full deli takeout menu — house-made salsas, guacamole, tortillas, and sauces — suitable for provisioning on the go. Its location at the heart of Granville Island makes it a natural pit stop for cyclists riding the False Creek seawall.

detail.address: 145-1689 Johnston St, Vancouver, British Columbia V6H 3R9, Canada

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu marks (V) Vegetarian and (GF) Gluten Free options throughout; confirmed items include Bean and Cheese Burrito (V), Pinche Tacos (GF)(V), Enchilladas (GF)(V), Mexi-Wrap (V), and multiple taco salad variants (V)

restaurant.name: Thai Away Home
restaurant.desc: Thai Away Home is a multi-location Thai restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver serving dine-in, take-out, and delivery meals rooted in authentic Thai recipes with fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The menu caters broadly to diverse dietary needs, including vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options across curries, noodle dishes, salads, and fried chicken. Cambie Street is a recognized cycling corridor in Vancouver, making this a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly states the menu includes 'vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options'; menu page lists tofu/veggie substitutions and curry combos

restaurant.name: Boba Run
restaurant.desc: Boba Run is a health-focused bubble tea café in Vancouver's downtown core that rejects powdered creamers and artificial flavorings in favour of fresh-brewed loose-leaf teas, house-made organic syrups, and real or vegan milks. Their menu spans matcha series, hojicha, fresh-brewed teas, and signature lattes, with customizable toppings like boba, lychee jelly, and organic chia. The shop also offers event catering, having served clients including Arc'teryx, Lululemon, and Meta.

detail.address: 102 West Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 1G8

notes.Takeout: Website features an online ordering cart; business is a boba drink shop with no dine-in food service evident
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website confirms vegan milk alternatives ('fresh milk or your choice of vegan mylks') and notes non-dairy options throughout the Our Story page

restaurant.name: My Toan Vietnamese Gourmet
restaurant.desc: My Toan is a Vietnamese restaurant chain founded by an immigrant entrepreneur who brought traditional Vietnamese cooking from his hometown to Vancouver over 30 years ago. The Harbour Centre location sits in the mall food court at basement level (unit FC-14), offering a broad menu spanning pho, rice and noodle combinations, fresh salad rolls, baguettes, and Vietnamese crepes. The chain operates multiple Metro Vancouver locations and partners with food delivery platforms for online ordering.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Vegetarian Tofu Spring Roll, Tofu Salad Roll, Veggie Salad Roll, Tofu Baguette, and Veggie Baguette

restaurant.name: CAVU Kitchen Bar
restaurant.desc: CAVU Kitchen Bar is a regional-cuisine restaurant and bar situated within (or alongside) the Hilton in Richmond, serving breakfast, an all-day menu, and happy hour. The kitchen produces house-smoked brisket, OceanWise seafood, and a broad range of globally inflected small plates and mains. The venue also hosts regular public events including themed brunches and Paint Nites, giving it a lively community atmosphere.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu uses 🌱 Vegetarian and 🌾 Gluten Friendly labels on multiple items (e.g., Tempura Cauliflower Bites marked VG, Cavucado Toast, CAVU Chicken Fingers marked GF)

restaurant.name: Smoking Gun Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Smoking Gun Coffee Roasters is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe located in the District 1881 development in the heart of downtown Chilliwack. The cafe serves a full range of hot and cold espresso drinks, filter coffee, matcha, teas, alternative milks, baked goods, and savoury sandwiches, with seasonal rotating options. The roastery side ships freshly roasted single-origin and blended beans Canada-wide, making it both a neighbourhood gathering spot and a draw for coffee-focused riders.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Cafe menu page states: 'we always have gluten free and vegan options, while supplies last.'

restaurant.name: Damso Modern Korean Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Damso is a modern Korean restaurant operated by Damso Group, offering an all-you-can-eat Korean menu with dishes like Korean BBQ, pork belly, tteokbokki, and Korean fried chicken. The restaurant is card-only and uses a waitlist seating system. Online ordering is available for takeout.

restaurant.name: Banana Leaf on Broadway
restaurant.desc: Banana Leaf is Vancouver's original Malaysian restaurant, established in 1995 and now operating five Metro Vancouver locations. The Broadway flagship on the corner of West Broadway and Oak offers over 40 dishes drawing from Malaysian, Indonesian, Singaporean, Thai, Chinese, and Indian influences. A touring cyclist seeking a substantial sit-down meal on the Broadway corridor will find a full-service restaurant with dine-in and takeout options.

restaurant.name: Twins Chinese Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Twins Chinese Kitchen is a sit-down Cantonese restaurant on Vancouver's Davie Street with an extensive menu spanning congee, wonton soups, fried noodles, hot pot, combo dinners, and over 80 dishes in total. The restaurant accepts online orders for takeout and is marked wheelchair accessible in OSM. It draws a steady local following with over 40 customer reviews and caters to groups with multi-person dinner combos.

restaurant.name: The Beagle Pub
restaurant.desc: Beagle Pub is a classic neighbourhood pub anchoring Victoria's lively Cook Street Village, offering a wide range of beer on tap alongside food service in a welcoming, unpretentious setting. The Cook Street corridor is a popular cycling route connecting residential Victoria to the waterfront, making the pub a natural candidate stop for touring cyclists. OSM records the venue as wheelchair accessible.

restaurant.name: Sammy J's Grill & Bar
restaurant.desc: Sammy J's Grill & Bar is a BC-grown casual restaurant chain founded in Langley City in 1996, now with four locations including this South Surrey outpost. The menu leans American grill — steaks, pastas, thin-crust pizzas, and a well-stocked bar centered on a signature wraparound 'Rock' bar — alongside dedicated vegetarian, vegan-friendly, and gluten-free sections. A touring cyclist can fuel up with a full sit-down meal or order pickup for the road.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists dedicated Vegetarian, Vegan Friendly, and Gluten Free menu sections with snacks, soups, plates, bowls, handhelds, and thin-crust pizza options

restaurant.name: Marble Slab Creamery
restaurant.desc: Marble Slab Creamery is a Canadian chain ice cream shop known for hand-mixed ice cream on a frozen marble slab. This location sits along Lougheed Highway in Coquitlam, making it an easy roadside stop for cyclists passing through the Tri-Cities area.

restaurant.name: Merridale Eatery
restaurant.desc: Merridale Eatery is the farmhouse dining room of Merridale Cidery & Distillery, a family-owned, woman-led farm operation that has been crafting ciders and spirits in the Cowichan Valley for over 30 years. The eatery serves farm-fresh comfort food designed to pair with their house-made ciders, spirits, and artisanal sodas on a 20-acre working orchard. Cyclists will find a relaxed pub-style setting with heated patio and courtyard seating, plus a farm store stocked with award-winning ciders, spirits, and local gifts.

detail.address: 1230 Merridale Road, Cobble Hill, BC V8H 1A1

restaurant.name: Edo Japan
restaurant.desc: Edo Japan is a Japanese fast-food restaurant chain with takeaway service. The North Vancouver location features air conditioning. As a casual fast-food venue, it provides quick meal options for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Minnoz Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Minnoz Restaurant + Lounge is an elegant yet casual full-service dining room and lounge inside the Coast Bastion Hotel in downtown Nanaimo, serving breakfast through dinner plus weekend brunch. The menu spans homemade breakfasts, appetizers, and a rotating set of daily lunch specials. Its downtown hotel location puts it within reach of the Nanaimo waterfront cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Helen's Grill
restaurant.desc: Helen's Grill is a classic old-school diner on Main Street in Vancouver, a well-travelled urban cycling corridor. The single-storey spot serves diner staples and has been a neighbourhood fixture long enough to cultivate a loyal local following. For a touring cyclist rolling through South Vancouver, it offers a sit-down meal in an unpretentious, no-fuss setting.

restaurant.name: JINYA Ramen Bar
restaurant.desc: JINYA Ramen Bar is a Japanese ramen chain known for broths simmered in-house for over 20 hours using whole pork bones, chicken, vegetables, and classic Japanese seasonings. The Langley location offers a contemporary sit-down dining room alongside a full bar with Japanese-inspired craft cocktails and a menu of small plates. It sits in a commercial unit along Fraser Highway and is part of a rapidly expanding North American franchise founded by Tomo Takahashi.

detail.address: 19705 Fraser Highway, Unit 525, Langley, BC V3A7E9

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Freshslice Pizza is a BC-based pizza chain offering by-the-slice and whole-pie options for takeout and delivery. The East Hastings Street location sits in a dense urban corridor in East Vancouver. It is a no-frills fast-food stop with a broad menu of customizable pizzas.

restaurant.name: Mr Mikes
restaurant.desc: Mr Mikes is a Canadian casual steakhouse chain with roots going back to 1960, now branded as 'SteakhouseCasual' — a relaxed, unpretentious sit-down experience built around affordable premium steaks, burgers, pastas, and shareable appetizers. The Duncan location welcomes walk-ins and offers both dine-in and takeout, making it a solid option for a substantial post-ride meal. The chain prides itself on a come-as-you-are attitude with no dress code.

restaurant.name: Triumph Coffee
restaurant.desc: Triumph Coffee is an independent café in Vernon, BC, branding itself around 'outstanding coffee.' It offers online ordering through its website, suggesting a takeout-friendly model well suited to cyclists passing through the Okanagan. Its location on 30 Avenue puts it within reach of the Vernon town centre and surrounding cycling routes.

restaurant.name: The Mantra
restaurant.desc: The Mantra is an Indian restaurant located on Fort Street in downtown Victoria. It serves Indian cuisine and provides a place for travelers and residents to dine.

restaurant.name: Canadian Pizza Plus
restaurant.desc: Canadian Pizza Plus is a Burnaby restaurant blending two distinct cuisines — classic Canadian-style pizza (customizable with up to five toppings, or as gourmet fusion pies like Butter Chicken Pizza) alongside a full authentic Indian menu of curries, biryanis, and tandoori wraps. The hybrid concept makes it a practical stop for a hungry cycling group with varied tastes. Online ordering supports both pickup and delivery.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu has a dedicated 'Authentic Indian Food - Vegetarian' section (Shahi Paneer, Channa Masala, Palak Paneer, etc.) and menu legend labels vegetarian items. Multiple vegetarian wraps, samosas, and pakoras also listed

restaurant.name: Grill Haven
restaurant.desc: Grill Haven is a Middle Eastern restaurant in Fort St. John offering a menu that includes kebab wings, hummus with falafel, hummus with beef, dipping shrimp, and loaded chicken fries. It operates via a Lightspeed online ordering system and serves appetizers, mains, salads, sides, desserts, and a kids menu. For cyclists riding through the Peace River region, it offers a distinctive alternative to typical road-food options in a town that serves as a northern hub on BC Highway 97.

restaurant.name: Van. Tea Cafe
restaurant.desc: Van Tea Cafe is a Hong Kong-style Chinese restaurant in Richmond offering dishes including fried chicken, laksa, and seafood prepared from fresh ingredients. The Richmond location features a large dining hall with a broad menu of Chinese comfort food. A second location operates in Vancouver on Main Street.

restaurant.name: Cobblestone Public House
restaurant.desc: The Cobblestone has been a community fixture in Cobble Hill since 1983, occupying the historic site of the Cowichan Creamery (1895–early 1940s). It operates as a locally owned, family-run public house serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner alongside an attached liquor store. Regular live music and weekly events make it a lively gathering spot for anyone passing through the Cowichan Valley.

restaurant.name: Yolks
restaurant.desc: Yolks is a breakfast and brunch restaurant founded by Chef Steve Ewing, known for scratch-made dishes built around Perfectly Poached™ eggs, house-made hollandaise, and locally sourced free-range eggs from Coligny Creek Eggs in Abbotsford. The Broadway location is one of several across BC and Canada, situated on a major Vancouver arterial. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a full sit-down meal with outdoor seating available.

restaurant.name: Bun & Beans Cafe
restaurant.desc: Bun & Beans Cafe is a cafe located on West Hastings Street in downtown Vancouver. Its West Hastings address places it in a busy urban corridor convenient to cyclists moving through the core of the city. No further details about its menu, seating, or offerings could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: bb.q chicken
restaurant.desc: A casual fast-food chicken restaurant in Chilliwack offering takeaway service. No drive-through or outdoor seating. Free WiFi (SSID: BBQ Guest) and on-site washrooms make it a practical quick stop for touring cyclists needing food and connectivity.

restaurant.name: Pizza Factory
restaurant.desc: Pizza Factory is a long-established Coquitlam pizzeria founded in 1984 by Sam Sanghera, now operating as a franchise with locations across British Columbia. The Clarke Road location hand-makes fresh dough daily and offers a wide menu spanning specialty pizzas, pasta, chicken wings, and Indian-inspired dishes. With 528 customer reviews and both pickup and delivery available, it is a well-used neighbourhood food stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated 'Veggie Speciality Pizza' section with items including Vegetarian Pizza, Spinach Lovers, Tandoori Paneer, and Paneer Pizza; menu legend indicates vegetarian items. No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Sharkey's Seafood Bar & Grille
restaurant.desc: Established in 1992, Sharkey's is a long-standing Ladner waterfront institution known for fish and chips, gourmet burgers, and craft beer in an east coast-style setting. Its award-winning waterfront patio makes it a natural stopping point for cyclists touring the South Delta flatlands along the Fraser delta. The family-friendly atmosphere and broad menu — from clam chowder and seafood fettuccine to kids' meals — cater to groups of all sizes.

restaurant.name: Sushi Heaven
restaurant.desc: Sushi Heaven is a Japanese takeout restaurant on Penticton's Main Street offering an extensive menu of sushi rolls, sashimi, nigiri, teriyaki, tempura, donburi, and specialty combo trays. It operates as a phone-ahead or walk-in pickup spot, making it a practical meal stop for cyclists passing through downtown Penticton. The broad menu — including lunch boxes and BBQ combos — gives touring cyclists plenty of fuelling options.

restaurant.name: Cheung Hing Food Co.
restaurant.desc: Cheung Hing Food Co. is a Chinese restaurant on Kingsway in Vancouver, serving as a convenient meal stop for cyclists traveling through the area.

restaurant.name: Anza Club
restaurant.desc: The Anza Club is a long-running non-profit social club and live music venue in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, tracing its roots to the Australian New Zealand Association and its presence in the community since the 1960s. The downstairs members' lounge features a pool table, dart boards, and a fireplace, while the main hall hosts an eclectic mix of live music, dance nights, trivia, and community events. Annual membership is open to everyone, making it an inclusive neighbourhood hub rather than a private retreat.

restaurant.name: Wow Full Noodle House
restaurant.desc: A Chinese noodle restaurant located on Dunsmuir Street in downtown Vancouver. Indoor seating is available with no outdoor seating. No smoking is permitted.

restaurant.name: Caribbean Village Cafe
restaurant.desc: Caribbean Village Cafe is a small family-run kitchen on a quiet corner of Victoria's Quadra Street, cooking slow-simmered island dishes rooted in the owner's grandfather's recipes. The rotating menu leans on pimento-smoked jerk chicken, four-hour curry goat, oxtail, cou cou and fried fish, and Jamaica's ackee and saltfish — with key ingredients sourced from named growers. The atmosphere is deliberately relaxed and welcoming, with a record player, bright walls, and an open invitation to walk in and pull up a chair.

detail.address: 2646 Quadra Street, Victoria, British Columbia V8T 5G7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian items: Curried Veggie meal, Veggie samosas, Veggie roti, Curried Veggie patties, Spinach & Feta samosas, and vegetable soups (callaloo, sweet potato & carrot, pea)

restaurant.name: Huong Lan
restaurant.desc: Huong Lan is a family-owned Vietnamese restaurant that has been a Nanaimo institution since 1998, voted the #1 Asian restaurant in Nanaimo by the Nanaimo News Bulletin every year from 2013 to 2022. The menu centres on pho, wonton soup, grilled lemongrass chicken, and bubble tea, with dedicated gluten-free and vegan options. Located in a plaza on Bowen Road, it offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery — a reliable hot-meal stop for cyclists passing through central Nanaimo.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists dedicated 'VEGETARIAN & TOFU' and 'GLUTEN FREE' sections; home page highlights 'gluten-free and vegan selections'

restaurant.name: Golden Spring
restaurant.desc: Golden Spring is a Chinese restaurant in Vancouver offering dine-in service and online food ordering. Located on Nanaimo Street, it provides a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking a meal.

restaurant.name: Bohemian Spirits
restaurant.desc: Bohemian Spirits is a small-batch craft distillery and tasting room perched in Kimberley, BC — self-described as Canada's highest city — producing hand-crafted, hand-corked spirits from Rocky Mountain botanicals. The owner-operated venue doubles as an axe-throwing venue, making it an unexpectedly lively stop in an otherwise quiet mountain community. It sells spirits online and in person, with cheese available for local pickup.

restaurant.name: Aqui es Mexico
restaurant.desc: Aqui es Mexico serves authentic Mexican food on BC's Sunshine Coast in the small community of Madeira Park on the Sechelt Peninsula. The menu features classics like enchiladas, burritos, chile rellenos, and huevos rancheros with a choice of chicken, beef, pork, or veggie fillings. Both dine-in and takeout are available, with online ordering supported during restaurant hours.

detail.address: 12808 Madeira Park Road, Madeira Park, V0N 2H0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu items including enchiladas, burritos, quesadillas, and chilaquiles all offer 'veggies' as an explicit protein/filling choice. No GF or vegan claims confirmed

restaurant.name: Caffe Fantastico
restaurant.desc: Caffe Fantastico is a locally-owned, family-run coffee roastery operating multiple café locations in Victoria, BC, roasting a diverse menu of sustainably sourced coffees from value staples to boutique microlots. Beyond espresso drinks, the bar-deli offers deli items and charcuterie boxes available for pickup seven days a week. The business has a strong community focus, regularly hosting poetry slams, live music, and book launches at its venues.

detail.address: 965 Kings Road, Victoria, British Columbia V8T 1W7

restaurant.name: Saxe Point Public House
restaurant.desc: Saxe Point Public House is Esquimalt's community-focused neighbourhood pub, serving craft beers from Victoria's local breweries alongside a seasonal menu of fresh, modern takes on pub classics. The pub features a patio, regular live events including trivia and live music, and a warm atmosphere curated by owner Demian Merino, a Victoria hospitality veteran. Cyclists will find a full food and drink menu with vegetarian and gluten-free options in a welcoming spot close to Saxe Point Park.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Beer menu lists 'Breakthru Gluten Free Pilsner, IPA, Stout'; food menu described as having options for everyone including vegetarian dishes

restaurant.name: Cantina Norte
restaurant.desc: Cantina Norte is a modern Mexican restaurant in Edgemont Village, North Vancouver, carrying forward the spirit of the neighbourhood's beloved Café Norte with house-made tortillas, bold Pacific Northwest-inflected flavours, and a full agave-forward bar program. The lively room offers both indoor and patio seating and handles everything from casual lunches to full venue buyouts for up to 120 guests. It has been voted Favourite Mexican Restaurant on the North Shore five years running (2021–2025).

detail.address: 108 - 3246 Connaught Crescent, North Vancouver, BC V7R 0A7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Browse vegetarian, gluten-friendly, and shareable Mexican dishes across every menu.' FAQ also lists 'Do you offer vegetarian dishes?' and 'Do you offer gluten-friendly options?' as FAQ topics

restaurant.name: Sushi California
restaurant.desc: Sushi California is a Japanese sushi restaurant operating multiple locations in the Vancouver area. The chain provides takeout options for touring cyclists seeking Japanese cuisine.

restaurant.name: Neate Donuts
restaurant.desc: Neate Donuts is a donut shop in downtown Vancouver operated by JJ Bean, a well-known local coffee roaster. Located on West Hastings Street, it offers a takeout-friendly format that suits cyclists passing through the downtown core.

restaurant.name: Bombay Kitchen and Bar
restaurant.desc: Bombay Kitchen and Bar is an Indian restaurant on Vancouver's beloved Commercial Drive, self-described as the highest-rated Indian restaurant in Vancouver. The menu ranges from traditional regional curries and mughal-inspired rice dishes to tandoori specialties baked in a Jaipuri clay oven, with a dedicated street food section featuring pani puri and chaat. Dine-in service is complemented by direct online ordering with delivery from the restaurant.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'We deliver orders directly from our restaurant. Order Online Now!' indicating online ordering with delivery; takeout pickup is not explicitly distinguished but online ordering system implies it

restaurant.name: Bukchon Korean Cuisine
restaurant.desc: A Korean restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver offering dine-in and takeout service. The business operates daily with online ordering, providing quick meal service for visitors and commuters. It's a convenient dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: HAAN Korean BBQ
restaurant.desc: HAAN Korean BBQ is an authentic Korean barbecue restaurant located in Sunwood Square near Coquitlam Centre, where diners cook their own selection of beef or pork on smokeless tabletop grills. Every meal comes with traditional Banchan side dishes, and the kitchen also prepares fully cooked dishes for those who prefer. It is a full sit-down dining experience with a drink menu and staff on hand to guide first-timers.

detail.address: Sunwood Square, 780-3025 Lougheed Highway, Coquitlam, BC V3B 6S2

restaurant.name: Momo Sushi Downtown
restaurant.desc: Momo Sushi Downtown is a sushi restaurant in downtown Kelowna. The business website currently resolves to a GoDaddy parked domain, indicating potential closure or outdated contact information.

restaurant.name: Cactus Club Cafe
restaurant.desc: Cactus Club Cafe is a well-established upscale casual dining chain with this Coquitlam location situated near shopping and VIP cinemas on Schoolhouse Street. The restaurant features a chef-driven international menu spanning sushi, steaks, pasta, and shareables, served in a stylish, energetic space. A patio, private dining rooms, and both pickup and delivery options are available.

restaurant.name: Mundo Nova
restaurant.desc: Mundo Novo Coffee Roasters bills itself as the first facility on Canada's West Coast to offer wholesale, private label, and co-op coffee roasting under a single roof. Founded by Cristina Dias, whose family has farmed coffee in Brazil since 1890, the operation also runs a coffee Education Centre offering training, cupping sessions, and lectures to culinary institutions and hospitality businesses across the Lower Mainland. The business is primarily trade-facing rather than a walk-in café.

restaurant.name: Smitty's Oyster House
restaurant.desc: Smitty's Oyster House is an independent waterfront seafood restaurant in Gibsons on British Columbia's Sunshine Coast, self-described as 'the institution on the water.' The menu centres on a rotating selection of fresh raw and broiled oysters alongside Dungeness crab, sablefish, scallops, and other Pacific and East Coast seafood. It is a distinctly local spot — the OSM record explicitly flags it as unrelated to the Smitty's breakfast chain — making it a notable destination meal for cyclists touring the Sunshine Coast.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Several vegetarian-suitable items appear on the menu: Smitty's Salad, Wild Mushroom Risotto, Edamame, Grilled Broccolini, Pappardelle (pasta), and Kennebec Fries. Not explicitly labelled as vegetarian; no vegan or GF claims noted

restaurant.name: River's Edge Clubhouse
restaurant.desc: River's Edge Clubhouse is the signature restaurant at Sandpiper Resort, situated alongside the Harrison River in Harrison Mills and widely regarded as one of the Fraser Valley's most scenic destination restaurants. Part of a historic 160-acre golf and lodging resort, it serves a full breakfast and lunch/dinner menu featuring BC farm-fresh ingredients. The riverside clubhouse setting draws golfers, resort guests, and locals alike, making it a notable food stop for cyclists touring the Harrison River valley.

detail.address: 14282 Morris Valley Rd. Harrison Mills, BC, Canada V0M 1L0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists gluten-free bread substitution ('Substitute gluten-free bread'); Smashed Avocado Benedict and Granola and Mixed Berry Parfait are meatless; Golfcart Sandwich offers 'sub smashed avocado for a meatless option'; Frittata is vegetarian

restaurant.name: Yan's Garden
restaurant.desc: Yan's Garden (潮樓) is a well-established Cantonese restaurant in Burnaby celebrated for its daily push-cart dim sum service, live seafood, and Peking duck. Seating over 180 guests across a large column-free main hall and three private VIP rooms, it has hosted weddings and large banquets and is recommended by locals and visitors as one of the top Chinese restaurants in the area. The restaurant is situated at the busy corner of Lougheed Highway and North Road with ample on-site parking.

notes.Takeout: Website features a dedicated 'Pickup/Delivery Order' section; all-day delivery extended to 20 km radius; take-out dine-in menu listed on menus page

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: Tim Hortons at 463 Robson Street is a downtown Vancouver location of Canada's ubiquitous coffee chain, sitting on one of the city's busiest pedestrian-and-cyclist corridors. Cyclists can refuel with coffee, breakfast wraps, soups, sandwiches, and baked goods with full dine-in seating and takeout service. The location has no drive-through, keeping the street-level experience walkable and accessible.

restaurant.name: Vera's Burger Shack
restaurant.desc: Vera's Burger Shack is a BC-based burger chain known for hand-pressed patties made from 100% fresh Canadian beef, with every item prepared to order from fresh ingredients. The Pitt Meadows franchise sits on Lougheed Highway, placing it along a major cycling corridor in the Fraser Valley. As a franchise with a Hall of Fame menu and rotating daily specials, it offers a consistent and recognizable stop for hungry riders.

detail.address: 390-19800 Lougheed Hwy, Pitt Meadows, BC V3Y 2W1

restaurant.name: Black & Blue
restaurant.desc: Black & Blue is a Kobe-beef certified upscale steakhouse operated by the Glowbal Restaurant Group in downtown Vancouver. The venue includes a ground-floor dining room and The Roof, described as Vancouver's largest rooftop dining destination, featuring a Josper wood-coal grill. Private dining rooms and group event booking are available, making it a destination for special occasions rather than a casual cyclist stop.

restaurant.name: Thomas Haas Chocolates
restaurant.desc: Thomas Haas Chocolates is a celebrated artisanal chocolatier and café in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, operated by award-winning pastry chef Thomas Haas. The café offers handcrafted pastries, gourmet croissants and sandwiches, house-made confections, chocolate bars, coffee, and hot chocolate, with both indoor and outdoor seating. Cyclists riding the West Broadway corridor will find this a tempting stop for high-quality baked goods and sweets.

restaurant.name: Pressato
restaurant.desc: Pressato is a European-inspired sandwich shop on Vancouver's busy Robson Street, built around house-baked focaccia made daily from five simple, preservative-free ingredients. Owner Stefan's menu spans Italian, French, Spanish, and Portuguese flavours across focaccia sandwiches, paninis, hand-crafted coffee, and fresh pastries. The shop offers both indoor and outdoor seating and accepts catering orders, making it a solid mid-ride refuelling stop in the heart of downtown Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu marks vegetarian items with '(V)' — Caprese and Amalfi focaccia sandwiches confirmed vegetarian; no vegan designation found on site

restaurant.name: Pizza Garden
restaurant.desc: Pizza Garden is a BC-based Neapolitan pizza chain with over 25 years in the industry, serving wood-fired pizzas with charred crusts, sun-ripened tomatoes, and fresh mozzarella. The West Vancouver Park Royal South location is one of more than a dozen locations across the province, from Victoria to Fort St. John. The chain offers both pickup and delivery with online ordering via app.

detail.address: 704 Main St, West Vancouver, BC V7T 0A5

restaurant.name: Beijing Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Beijing Hot Pot (京門涮肉) is a hot pot restaurant located in a unit at 8251 Westminster Highway in Richmond, BC. Hot pot dining is a communal, interactive style of Chinese cuisine where diners cook ingredients in a simmering broth at the table, making it a warming and social stop. The restaurant maintains an Instagram presence under @beijing_hotpotvan.

restaurant.name: Sushi Bar Shu
restaurant.desc: Sushi Bar Shu is an intimate omakase sushi bar on Granville Street, founded in 2018 by Chef Hyunki Shin, who draws on 18 years of culinary experience including training in Japan. The restaurant offers curated multi-course tasting menus built around seasonal Japanese ingredients, served at a sushi bar in a refined, guided dining setting. Reservations are required well in advance and the experience is designed as a deliberate, unhurried culinary journey.

restaurant.name: Ipoh Malay Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Ipoh Malay Cuisine is a Malaysian restaurant in Vancouver's Marpole neighbourhood, taking its name from Ipoh — a city in Peninsular Malaysia's Perak state renowned for a distinct local food culture. The restaurant offers delivery and sits on a quiet residential stretch of West 73rd Avenue in South Vancouver. Touring cyclists exploring the southern reaches of the city will find it a rare stop for authentic Malaysian flavours.

restaurant.name: Gordon Ramsay Steak
restaurant.desc: Gordon Ramsay Steak is an upscale steakhouse in Richmond, BC, part of the global restaurant empire of Michelin-starred celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay. Situated at 8811 River Rd, it offers a fine-dining experience with table reservations and takeout. Touring cyclists looking for a high-end dinner option in the Richmond area will find this a notable stop.

detail.address: 8811 River Rd, Richmond, British Columbia, V6X 3P8, Canada

restaurant.name: Night Owl Kichen + Bar
restaurant.desc: Night Owl Kitchen + Bar is a multi-location BC chain that brings globally inspired cuisine—think Baja Shrimp Tacos, Chimichurri Salmon, and Weekend Brunch—to a lively seaside setting on Marine Drive in White Rock. The venue blends a casual daytime vibe with an evening bar atmosphere, and regularly hosts live music, trivia nights, and sports watch parties. Its location near the White Rock pier makes it a natural stop for cyclists riding the coastal Marine Drive corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page explicitly labels items as 'Gluten Smart,' 'Vegetarian,' and 'Can Be Made Vegan.'

restaurant.name: Paper Crane Coffee
restaurant.desc: Paper Crane Coffee is a café on East Broadway in Vancouver. Located on a busy arterial street that connects several neighbourhoods, it is positioned along a common cycling corridor on Vancouver's east side. The business is a small independent café identifiable by its presence on Instagram.

restaurant.name: Shen Sushi
restaurant.desc: Shen Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Burnaby with online takeout ordering. It provides a quick food stop for cyclists touring through the area.

restaurant.name: Ban Bu Xian Szechuan
restaurant.desc: Ban Bu Xian Szechuan is a Chinese restaurant specializing in Szechuan cuisine, located on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. The OSM record confirms both indoor and outdoor seating, giving cyclists the option to sit outside after a ride. Robson Street is a busy, pedestrian-friendly corridor popular with both locals and visitors exploring the West End.

restaurant.name: Local Pizza
restaurant.desc: Local Pizza is a Vancouver Island–born pizza chain with five Victoria-area outlets, including food court locations at Hillside and Mayfair malls and standalone shops on Douglas, Shelbourne, and Goldstream. The chain emphasises fresh ingredients and locally hired staff, positioning itself as a neighbourhood alternative to national pizza brands. Cyclists passing through Victoria will find multiple convenient locations for a quick pizza or side order via walk-in pickup or online ordering.

detail.address: 1483 Douglas St #105, Victoria, BC V8W 2G2, Canada

restaurant.name: Punk Rock Pastries
restaurant.desc: Punk Rock Pastries is a Burnaby bakery founded in 2019 by Chef Hollie Fraser, a three-time Food Network champion (The Big Bake Halloween, Bake Master Battle, Halloween Baking Championship), specializing in jaw-dropping 3D sculpted cakes, moving cakes, and unconventional pastries. The shop operates as a 100% nut-free facility and carries vegan and gluten-free options alongside its full menu of custom and walk-in treats, including its alter-ego line Peep Show Pastries for adult-themed events. After a temporary closure, the bakery has reopened at the same Hastings Street location.

restaurant.name: SunTea
restaurant.desc: SunTea Canada is a fresh-brewed bubble tea chain founded in 2019, offering fruit teas and milk teas with online ordering and a rewards app. The Kingsway Burnaby location is one of several Metro Vancouver outlets, situated in a unit-style retail space with indoor seating. Cyclists passing through the area can order ahead for quick pickup via the chain's Toast-integrated online platform.

restaurant.name: Soft Peaks Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Soft Peaks Ice Cream is an ice cream shop located on Alexander Street in Vancouver, offering frozen treats to the local community. It provides a casual stop for touring cyclists seeking refreshment during their travels.

restaurant.name: Momo Tea
restaurant.desc: Momo Tea is a bubble tea café on Yates Street in downtown Victoria. It sits in a walkable, cycling-friendly part of the city close to the Inner Harbour area. A touring cyclist passing through would find it a convenient stop for a cold or hot tea drink.

restaurant.name: Big Wheel Burger
restaurant.desc: Big Wheel Burger is a Victoria-born fast food chain and Canada's first carbon neutral fast food restaurant, open since 2011 and now operating five locations. The Cook Street Village outpost is surrounded by a community garden the company created from an unused boulevard. It sources 100% fresh BC beef, local buns from Irene's Bakery, and dairy from Island Farms, making it a locally-rooted stop for a calorie-dense meal on a touring ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Two house-made plant-based burgers (Nashville Hawt Chickpea, Yam & Black Bean available vegan); GF buns; dedicated GF fryer; vegetarian and GF poutine gravy

restaurant.name: Yaas Grill House
restaurant.desc: Yaas Grill House is a family-owned Persian restaurant that has been serving the North Shore community for over three decades, specializing in halal kababs, traditional stews, and an extensive range of vegetarian dishes. Situated on Lonsdale Avenue — a primary cycling corridor through North Vancouver — it offers dine-in, takeout, delivery, and catering, with a high-turnover kitchen that emphasizes freshness across its Iranian-inspired menu.

detail.address: 2057 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2K6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'a huge selection of vegetarian dishes, all available for eating in, taking out, delivering, and catering.' No mention of vegan or gluten-free specifically

restaurant.name: Kokoro Tokyo Mazesoba
restaurant.desc: Kokoro Tokyo Mazesoba is a Japanese restaurant specializing in mazesoba, a cold noodle soup with thick noodles and rich broth. Located on Steveston Highway in Richmond, it offers sit-down dining service.

restaurant.name: Pelican Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Pelican Seafood Restaurant (又一村海鲜酒家) is a family-owned Chinese seafood restaurant that has been operating in East Vancouver for over 10 years. The menu spans dim sum, lunch, and full dinners, with custom-order meals accommodating a range of dietary preferences. A street-facing patio adds an outdoor dining option for cyclists passing through the area.

detail.address: 1895 E Hastings St, Vancouver, BC V5L 1T3

restaurant.name: Cheng Du Street Food
restaurant.desc: Cheng Du Street Food is a multi-city Sichuan restaurant chain with locations in Richmond, Toronto, and Montreal, serving authentic Chengdu-style cuisine including bold Sichuan peppercorn dishes and seasonal specials like spicy crayfish. The Richmond location sits on Alderbridge Way in central Richmond. The restaurant's name in Chinese (苍蝇馆子) translates roughly to 'fly restaurant,' a colloquial term in China for beloved no-frills neighbourhood eateries known more for flavour than decor.

restaurant.name: Alexandra's Bistro
restaurant.desc: Alexandra's Bistro is a cozy, family-run Greek and Italian restaurant located on the upper level of Beban Plaza at the corner of Bowen and Northfield Road in Nanaimo. Known for generous portions of Mediterranean fare — including lamb souvlaki platters, moussaka, and house-made pasta — it has earned a loyal local following and a TripAdvisor Traveller's Choice award. Touring cyclists can order takeout for dinner or dine in, with private party capacity for up to 87 guests.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Our menus are Vegetarian friendly with Vegan and Gluten-Free options.'

restaurant.name: Wendy's
restaurant.desc: Wendy's is a major North American fast food chain offering square fresh-never-frozen beef burgers, chicken sandwiches, salads, and its signature Frosty dessert. This Chilliwack location has drive-through and takeout service, providing a reliable high-calorie stop for cyclists moving through the Fraser Valley corridor. As a large chain franchise, cyclist-specific amenities are not documented on the corporate website.

restaurant.name: Best Of Stone Baked Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Best Of Stone Baked Pizzeria is a full-service pizza restaurant in Fort St. John offering an unusually broad menu — stone-baked pizzas in multiple sizes, donairs, burgers, wings, pasta, and ice cream. The online ordering system and wide variety make it a practical stop for cyclists riding the Alaska Highway corridor who want a hearty, customizable meal. The eclectic mix of cuisines reflects the diverse tastes of a northern BC highway town.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Vegetarian Pizza' (mushrooms, green peppers, red onions, fresh tomatoes) and 'Falafel Donair' as distinct menu items

restaurant.name: That Place 4 Pasta & Pizza
restaurant.desc: That Place Italian Restaurant is a long-standing neighbourhood staple in Coquitlam's historic Maillardville district, serving an extensive menu of hand-crafted pastas, stone-baked pizzas, and traditional Italian mains like marsala chicken and linguini pescatore. The restaurant is known for its relaxed, friendly atmosphere and the personal touch of owner Rob, who has built a devoted local following. Cyclists can order pasta or pizza for take-out or sit down for a full Italian meal to refuel after a ride on the nearby trails and greenways.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states pasta is 'available in whole wheat or gluten-free options.' Multiple vegetarian pizzas listed (e.g., No Meater: red/green peppers, mushrooms, pineapple, spinach, onions, olives, feta; Mammolazy: grilled zucchini, roasted red pepper, mushrooms, figs, ricotta) and vegetarian pasta dishes (e.g., Linguini Primavera, Gnocchi in pesto rosé, Spaghetti ala Olio)

restaurant.name: Miso Taco
restaurant.desc: Miso Taco is a Mexican-Japanese fusion restaurant on Vancouver's Cambie Street, serving street-food-inspired dishes like teriyaki chicken tacos and pork chashu fillings that blend both culinary traditions. The restaurant is fully licensed, offers online ordering and takeout, and is part of a small growing chain with a second location on West Pender and a North Vancouver outpost announced. Cyclists on the Cambie corridor will find it a distinctive and filling stop with a varied menu including plant-based options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists vegetarian add-on options: Mushrooms, Fried Tofu, Fried Egg

restaurant.name: Rhino Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Rhino Coffee House is a surf-culture café anchored in Tofino's downtown core, serving espresso drinks, handcrafted matcha lattes, and a rotating lineup of fresh-baked goods including their signature savory 'Bro Nut' stuffed donut. The menu spans hearty all-day breakfasts and lunch sandwiches — pastrami on rye, triple grilled cheese, BBQ chicken — alongside a dedicated vegan menu and gluten-friendly options. Built around Tofino's outdoor lifestyle, the café actively markets itself as a pre-surf and post-hike refuel destination, with a takeout program specifically designed for beach days and trail runs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website has dedicated vegan menu page with vegan breakfasts, lunches, and bakery items; vegetarian options noted throughout menu. Takeout page explicitly lists 'Gluten-Free Baked goods and meals' (contradicts; website preferred)

restaurant.name: motherlove ferments
restaurant.desc: Motherlove Ferments is a Kelowna craft brewery specializing in live, unpasteurized kombucha and water kefir made with organic ingredients and whole-food flavours. Founded about nine years ago by Rochelle, a former national champion hammer thrower turned fermentation entrepreneur, the brewery sells its beverages in cans, cornelius kegs, and 2L growler refills from its Vaughan Avenue taproom. The location doubles as a community event space (the 'Flamingo Room') hosting wellness workshops and brewery tours, making it a distinctive stop for cyclists seeking a probiotic boost.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'absolutely no artificial additives' and describes all beverages as made from organic, plant-based whole-food ingredients — kombucha and water kefir are inherently vegan

restaurant.name: Folietta
