restaurant.desc: Folietta is an Italian restaurant from the Wentworth Hospitality Group situated in Vancouver's Grandview-Woodlands neighbourhood on the east side. The menu centres on pasta, meat, and fish dishes built from fresh West Coast ingredients with inspiration drawn from regional Italian culinary traditions. The restaurant offers both dinner service throughout the week and weekend brunch, with walk-ins welcomed alongside reservations.

restaurant.name: Signature Sports Bistro
restaurant.desc: Signature Sports Bistro is a bar and bistro located in Chilliwack. It serves as a casual dining and refreshment establishment in the community.

restaurant.name: Uptown Pizza
restaurant.desc: Uptown Pizza is a Salt Spring Group restaurant anchored in the busy Uptown district of Ganges, serving house-made pizzas built on fresh-made dough and marinara with real mozzarella, plus burgers, wings, and Kelly's homemade desserts. A garden-view seating area makes it a pleasant stop to watch the activity of one of Salt Spring Island's most active commercial strips. The restaurant is locally owned and operated as part of a multi-venue group with deep roots on the island.

detail.address: 324 Lower Ganges Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K2V7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple pizza options explicitly marked '* Vegetarian *' on the published menu (e.g., Cheese, Pesto Vegematic, Margherita, Popeye, Green Planet, Super Veggie, Secret Garden, Vegetarian); a veggie patty burger is also listed

restaurant.name: Modern Café
restaurant.desc: Modern Cafe is a brunch-focused restaurant on Commercial Street in downtown Nanaimo, serving dishes like Ahi Tuna Poke Bowl, Smoked Chowder, and Brisket Dip alongside classic brunch fare. The restaurant has outdoor seating and offers online ordering, catering, and reservations, making it a flexible stop for cyclists passing through the city. Its tagline 'Where Past Meets Present, and Every Bite Tells a Story' reflects a casual but deliberate dining experience.

restaurant.name: La Foret
restaurant.desc: La Forêt is a cozy café and bakery chain with roots going back to 2013, known for its spacious, forest-themed spaces and a menu spanning espresso drinks, brunch platters, croissants, and waffles. The Austin location in Coquitlam is the newest of three Lower Mainland outposts, offering the full La Forêt experience including signature velvet matcha drinks and Benedict platters. Touring cyclists will find a welcoming sit-down spot with substantial food options and a relaxed community atmosphere.

restaurant.name: The Station Taphouse
restaurant.desc: The Station Taphouse is a restaurant and pub set inside Port Alberni's historic train station, blending heritage character with a modern hospitality concept. Connected to Twin City Brewing Company, it operates 24 rotating taps focused on local and regional BC craft beer, alongside a curated comfort-food menu, BC wines, and cocktails. It positions itself as a destination for both locals and travelers passing through the Alberni Valley.

detail.address: 3100 Kingsway Avenue, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 3B1

restaurant.name: Silver Creek Cookhouse
restaurant.desc: Silver Creek Cookhouse is a casual diner on Alaska Road North in Fort St. John, serving breakfast, coffee, burgers, and sandwiches — the kind of hearty, no-frills fuel a touring cyclist needs after grinding through northeastern BC. It sits along the Alaska Highway corridor, making it a natural waypoint for riders heading north toward Dawson Creek or beyond. Air conditioning provides a welcome break on hot summer days in the Peace River region.

detail.address: 10104 Alaska Road North, Fort St. John, V1J 1A8

restaurant.name: Penguin Bros.
restaurant.desc: Penguin Bros. is a bubble tea specialty cafe in Richmond. It offers a convenient stop for refreshments during cycling tours of the area.

restaurant.name: The Pizza Co.
restaurant.desc: The Pizza Co. is a pizza restaurant located in Cranbrook, BC, in the East Kootenay region. Cranbrook sits along several popular cycling routes in the Columbia Valley corridor, making it a potential refuelling stop for touring cyclists passing through. No further details about the restaurant's offerings or facilities could be verified.

restaurant.name: The Copper Coil Still & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Copper Coil Still & Grill is a locally owned, family-operated restaurant in Squamish that fuses Cajun and Louisiana cooking traditions with Pacific Northwest seasonal and regional ingredients. Hand-crafted BBQ dishes anchor a menu designed around fresh, local produce in the spirit of New Orleans cuisine. Squamish is a major hub on the Sea to Sky cycling corridor, and the restaurant sits on Cleveland Avenue near the town centre.

restaurant.name: Church's Chicken
restaurant.desc: Church's Chicken is a fast-food restaurant serving fried chicken with takeaway and indoor seating available. A convenient quick-meal option for cyclists passing through Burnaby.

restaurant.name: Pizza Now
restaurant.desc: Pizza Now is a pizza-focused fast food outlet in a Hillside Drive strip mall beside Canadian Tire in Kamloops. It offers delivery, curbside pickup, and a drive-thru window, making it a quick stop for a hot meal without needing to lock up for long. The menu centres on classic 12-inch pizzas ordered online or by phone.

restaurant.name: Gray's Cafe
restaurant.desc: Grays Cafe is a sister-owned neighbourhood café in Sidney by the Sea, opened in 2021 by sisters Lisa and Amy who built it around locally sourced ingredients — coffee from Drumroaster, local produce, baked goods, and meat. The breakfast-and-lunch menu spans wraps, bagels, salads, and smoothies with a strong vegetarian and vegan lean. It bills itself as a place for community gathering, making it a welcoming mid-ride stop in the heart of Sidney.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegan items (Breakfast Bagel with Vegan Just Egg and vegan smoked gouda; Kidney Bean Wrap; House Salad and Veggie Wrap with vegan feta) and GF granola in the Yogurt Cup; numerous vegetarian options throughout breakfast and lunch sections

restaurant.name: Place2be Cafe
restaurant.desc: Yet's Cafe claims to be Vancouver's first fresh fruit boba tea and juice shop, specializing in bubble teas, fresh fruit boba teas, and a range of international juice flavors. Located on Burrard Street, the shop emphasizes fresh, real-fruit ingredients and has drawn comparisons to Persian-style juice bars. However, the business's current status is uncertain, as the Wix site appears frozen at 2021 and a rebrand to 'Place2be Cafe' has been flagged.

restaurant.name: New Owly Cade
restaurant.desc: New Owly Cade is a café located on Douglas Street in downtown Victoria, BC. It sits in a central, walkable area of the city convenient to the Inner Harbour cycling routes. OSM records outdoor seating, suggesting a patio presence that may appeal to cyclists stopping mid-ride.

restaurant.name: Brackendale Bean
restaurant.desc: Brackendale Bean is a café in the Brackendale neighbourhood of Squamish, a popular hub for cyclists tackling the Sea-to-Sky corridor. The café offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a potential rest stop for riders in all weather. OSM discovery notes suggest the business may now operate under the name Bean & Co at the same location.

restaurant.name: Donair Shack
restaurant.desc: Donair Shack is a fast-casual restaurant specializing in authentic donairs — grilled meat carved from a rotating spit, wrapped in warm flatbread with fresh vegetables and house sauces. It is part of a small regional chain with five locations across Abbotsford, Mission, and Surrey, making it a familiar refuelling stop along the Fraser Valley corridor. The menu spans several donair styles, rice and salad platters, and falafel options, offering a filling and customizable meal for cyclists on the move.

detail.address: 130 - 32151 South Fraser Way, Abbotsford, BC V2T 1W3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Veg. Falafel Donair', a Falafel Rice Platter, a Falafel Salad Platter, and Paneer Wraps (Shahi Paneer / Tandoori Paneer), confirming vegetarian options. No explicit GF or vegan claims found

restaurant.name: Desserts Artisanaux
restaurant.desc: Desserts Artisanaux is an authentic Cantonese dessert cafe on the Kingsway corridor in East Vancouver, specializing in handcrafted sweets made from traditional recipes — including double skin steamed milk pudding, mochi, sago soups, and seasonal specialties like pumpkin paste. The shop emphasizes 'not too sweet' flavours and slow, intentional preparation, and offers takeout with outdoor seating available.

notes.Takeout: OSM note states outdoor seating is for takeout only, corroborated by Instagram posts referencing stopping by and picking up items

restaurant.name: Thai Pudpong
restaurant.desc: Thai Pudpong is a family-owned authentic Thai restaurant operating since 2002, founded by head chef Sutthi Srilanpong whose mother cooked in the palace for King Rama the 9th's family in Bangkok. It was the first Thai restaurant in West Vancouver and earned early acclaim from the North Shore newspaper for its elegant, cozy atmosphere. The menu spans classics like Pad Thai, Red Curry, and Tom Yum, with spice levels adjustable to taste.

detail.address: 1474 Marine Dr, West Vancouver, BC V7T 1B7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Lunch menu lists 'Basil Vegetarian' (mixed vegetables with fresh Thai basil in red chili paste, served with rice) and multiple dishes offered with vegetable protein substitutions

restaurant.name: 1181 Lounge
restaurant.desc: 1181 Lounge is an LGBTQ-primary bar on Vancouver's Davie Street, known for craft cocktails, resident DJs, and a casual modern atmosphere. It is a well-established fixture of the city's gay village, drawing a lively crowd for music and nightlife. Touring cyclists visiting Vancouver's West End will find it near the Seawall and Davie Village.

restaurant.name: Sushi Misoya
restaurant.desc: Sushi Misoya is a Japanese restaurant on Dewdney Trunk Road in Maple Ridge, serving sushi and other Japanese dishes with both dine-in and takeout options. The restaurant supports online ordering, making it easy for cyclists to place an order in advance. It sits on a major arterial road through Maple Ridge, convenient for cyclists traveling the Lougheed corridor.

restaurant.name: Koi Sushi
restaurant.desc: Koi Sushi is a freshly made sushi counter located on the first floor of the University Centre Building at UBC Okanagan, operated by the Students' Union Okanagan. It sits within the campus food services hub alongside other student-union-run outlets including a pub and an Indian cuisine counter. As a campus food outlet, it is primarily oriented toward the university community, though the campus itself is accessible from Kelowna's road network.

detail.address: 1st floor, University Centre Building (UNC), 3272 University Way, Kelowna, BC V1V 1V7

restaurant.name: Flour Dance Bakery
restaurant.desc: Flour Dance Bakery is an artisan bakery in Richmond specializing in Asian-inspired breads and desserts, including matcha, taro, sesame, and lychee loaves made with premium hard spring flour and pure milk over 16-hour fermentation. The bakery operates both a retail storefront and an online ordering system with local delivery and self-pickup routes serving Richmond, Burnaby, and Vancouver. It is a bilingual (English and Chinese) business with a loyal community following, marketing itself as the 'Flour Dance Union.'

restaurant.name: Donair Express
restaurant.desc: Donair Express is a fast-casual wrap and bowl restaurant on Goldstream Avenue serving Lebanese, Halifax, and Caribbean-style donairs alongside rice bowls and sides. Chicken, beef, and vegetarian falafel are available across the entire menu, making it a flexible stop for mixed groups. The Goldstream Avenue location sits on a well-travelled cycling corridor connecting Victoria's western neighbourhoods.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu states 'All donairs come with choice of chicken, beef or vegetarian falafel'; falafel protein option is listed across all donairs, bowls, and sides

restaurant.name: PokeLani
restaurant.desc: PokeLani is a Hawaiian poke restaurant on Main Street in North Vancouver where customers build customizable bowls from a selection of proteins (tuna, salmon, shrimp, chicken, tofu), bases (white rice, brown rice, noodles, spring mix, kale), and an array of fresh vegetables, sauces, and toppings. The fast-casual format is well-suited to hungry cyclists looking for a fresh, filling meal assembled quickly to order. Online ordering and delivery are also available for those who want to plan ahead.

detail.address: 1331 Main St, North Vancouver, BC V7J 3J7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists tofu as a protein option and includes a dedicated 'Veggie Heaven' signature bowl (tofu, rice, mixed vegetables, citrus soy sauce); spring mix and kale bases also available. GF not explicitly mentioned

restaurant.name: Catelowna
restaurant.desc: Catelowna is a cat café on the second floor of a building in downtown Kelowna where visitors can enjoy organic, fair-trade coffee and tea while spending time with adoptable rescue cats. The café partners with local rescue organizations and has facilitated 548 cat adoptions to date. Beyond daily café visits, it hosts regular events including yoga sessions, paint-a-pet classes, and afternoon tea services.

detail.address: Suite 201 - 1441 Ellis Street, Kelowna, BC V1Y 2A3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu confirms organic ingredients, oat milk, natural sweeteners, peanut-free environment, and 100% vegan teas from Tea Sparrow

restaurant.name: Bin 4 Burger Lounge
restaurant.desc: Bin 4 Burger Lounge is a BC-born gourmet burger chain founded in 2011, now with seven locations including this Westshore outpost at 716 Goldstream Avenue. The menu leans on locally sourced ingredients—natural BC beef, Fraser Valley free-run chicken, and seasonal produce—paired with a wide roster of house-made aiolis and craft-inspired cocktails. The casual lounge format offers dine-in, online ordering, and a daily happy hour, making it a solid refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the Langford corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu offers tofu substitutions ('sub blackened tofu'), a BIN 4 BOWL with tofu, vegan red pepper dressing, vegan red pepper garlic aioli dip, and the Bin 4 Spiced Aloo Tikki vegetarian patty (potato, peas, cilantro)

restaurant.name: John 3:16 Malaysian Delights
restaurant.desc: John 3:16 Malaysian Delights is a Malaysian restaurant chain founded in Richmond in 2014, with the Burnaby outpost on the busy Kingsway corridor offering authentic Malaysian rice dishes, noodles, and hot beverages. The restaurant prides itself on chefs skilled in traditional Malaysian cooking and serves a broad menu from appetizers to desserts. With online ordering and a takeout-friendly format, it makes a practical meal stop on a Kingsway cycling route.

restaurant.name: Cockney Kings
restaurant.desc: Cockney Kings is a family-owned fish and chips institution that has been serving classic English-style fish and chips across Metro Vancouver since 1965. The Kitsilano location on Cornwall Avenue — steps from the Seaside Greenway cycling route — opened in 2023 and offers dine-in and takeout of battered fish, chips, and a full seafood menu. Now with four locations across Vancouver, Burnaby, and New Westminster, it remains a multi-generational local landmark.

restaurant.name: Ashiana Tandoori
restaurant.desc: Ashiana Tandoori is a family-run Indian restaurant on Vancouver's Kingsway corridor that has been serving authentic cuisine since 1980, and is recognized by Vancouver Magazine judges for housing the city's first tandoor oven. The restaurant offers a broad menu spanning tandoori specialties, curries, seafood, and rice dishes, with dedicated vegan and gluten-free sections. Dine-in, takeout, and local delivery are all available, making it a viable meal stop for cyclists passing through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a 'Tandoori Specialties (Vegetarian)' section and a dedicated 'Vegan & Gluten Free Dishes' section

restaurant.name: Smitty's
restaurant.desc: Smitty's is a Canadian casual dining chain founded in Calgary in 1960, with over 80 locations across Canada, serving all-day breakfast, pancakes, and comfort food classics. The Fort St. John location is one of the newer additions to the chain, confirmed open via the corporate news feed. For cyclists passing through the Peace River region, it offers a full sit-down dining experience with a broad menu served all day.

detail.address: 8808 96A Street Unit P2, Fort St. John, BC

restaurant.name: Rocky Point Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Rocky Point Ice Cream is a family-owned artisan ice cream chain that has operated in the Lower Mainland since 1997, making its own ice cream from scratch at BC's first licensed dairy plant dedicated solely to craft production. The New Westminster location is one of four storefront locations across the region and offers both indoor and outdoor seating. Visitors can choose from a rotating lineup of house-made flavours including plant-based and sorbet options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website front page explicitly names 'Plant-Based Blackberry Crumble: Plant-based coconut vanilla ice cream' and notes trucks carry '3 plant-based/sorbet options'; multiple flavours appear to be vegetarian by default

restaurant.name: House of Dosas
restaurant.desc: House of Dosas is a South Indian restaurant at the corner of Kingsway and Knight in Vancouver, a community staple for over 16 years known for its signature dosas — crispy, cylindrical crepes made from fermented rice and lentil batter served with chutneys and curries. The Kingsway flagship operates around the clock every day of the year, making it one of the few full-service restaurant options in Vancouver available to cyclists arriving at any hour. The menu spans dosas, biryanis, curries, and South Indian café drinks, with extensive options for vegan, gluten-free, and omnivore diners.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About Us page explicitly states 'Whether you are gluten-free, vegan or just a plain omnivore, our team will ensure their ancient recipes, local products and friendly service will cater to your needs.' Menu items are tagged (VG) and (GF) throughout both the Kingsway and Davie St. menus

restaurant.name: Little Fox Bakehouse
restaurant.desc: Little Fox Bakehouse is an artisan scratch bakery founded by Red Seal pastry chef Eric Ho, who pivoted from a 13-year engineering career to pursue his passion for baking. Everything is handcrafted on-site using traditional French techniques with real butter — no shortening or margarine — and the menu spans croissants in a wide variety of flavours, mousse cakes, canelés, and more. An espresso bar rounds out the offering for take-out drinks.

restaurant.name: Timmy Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Timmy Kitchen (添味馆) is a Chinese restaurant in the Steveston village area of Richmond, a popular cycling destination at the southern tip of Lulu Island. The restaurant offers dine-in service with outdoor seating and is wheelchair accessible. Its Steveston location puts it within easy reach of the waterfront dyke cycling routes that attract touring and recreational cyclists.

restaurant.name: Ugly Duckling Dining & Provisions
restaurant.desc: Ugly Duckling is an award-winning innovative tasting-menu restaurant that opened in February 2023 in the heart of Victoria's historic Chinatown. It was named Victoria's Best New Restaurant by YAM Magazine and long-listed among Canada's Best New Restaurants by Air Canada's En Route Magazine. The kitchen produces entirely handcrafted, seasonally rotating dishes sourced from Vancouver Island's small farms and wild ingredients.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We are happy to accommodate most dietary restrictions and preferences with advance notice.' FAQ confirms: 'We're able to accommodate most allergies and dietary preferences with advance notice,' though modifications must be confirmed prior to arrival

restaurant.name: Keating Coffee
restaurant.desc: Keating Coffee is a small weekday café on the Saanich Peninsula focused on quality fair-trade organic coffee and fresh homemade food, situated next to the Co-op Grocery on Keating Cross Road. The kitchen makes soups from scratch and builds sandwiches and paninis with local produce and bread from nearby bakeries — a practical fuelling stop for a cyclist passing through Saanichton. Customers consistently rate it among the best coffee spots on the Peninsula, and the café also offers catering.

detail.address: 2126B Keating Cross Road, Saanichton, BC V8M 2A6

restaurant.name: Legendary Noodle House
restaurant.desc: Legendary Noodle House is a Vietnamese restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, handcrafting noodles in an open kitchen since 1997. The compact interior is decorated with an antique wooden waterwheel at the entrance, Chinese lanterns, dark wood tables and benches imported from China, and wooden screens backlit by turquoise lights. A second location operates on West Broadway, and the English Bay location offers both dine-in and takeout.

restaurant.name: Sushi Mura
restaurant.desc: Sushi Mura is a Japanese sushi restaurant chain founded in Vancouver in 2012, with the Richmond branch situated in the Hollybridge Way commercial area. The restaurant emphasizes daily-delivered fresh fish and authentic Japanese recipes, offering a broad menu spanning rolls, sashimi, nigiri, tempura, and cooked entrees. It is part of a growing multi-location franchise across Metro Vancouver, making it a recognizable and consistent stop for a sit-down or takeout meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian items tagged 'Veggie' including Veggie Wakame (seaweed salad), Vegetable Tempura, Vegetable Sunomono, Edamame, and Gomae (spinach with peanut dressing)

restaurant.name: Ajisai Sushi Bar
restaurant.desc: Ajisai Sushi Bar is a long-running traditional Japanese sushi restaurant on West 42nd Avenue in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, offering dine-in lunch and dinner as well as telephone takeout. The restaurant is known for a focused menu of nigiri, sashimi, chirashi, and donburi made with high-quality seafood. A sister grab-and-go outlet, Ajisai 2 Go, operates next door at 2087 W.42nd Ave with ready-made rolls and bento for cyclists who want a quick stop.

detail.address: 2081 W.42nd Ave. Vancouver, BC, Canada V6M 2B4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple items marked (V) for vegetarian across menus: Vegetable Chirashi, Edamame, Moro Kyu, Spinach Gomaae, Spinach Ohitashi, Wakame Sunomono, Hiya Yakko (cold tofu), Tamago, Inari

restaurant.name: Sparky Chicken
restaurant.desc: Sparky Chicken is a Korean fried chicken shop on Fraser Street in Vancouver, specializing in a wide variety of sauced and grilled chicken dishes served with pickled radish and tteok (rice cake). The menu spans bone-in and boneless options in flavours from honey garlic to extreme hot, plus Korean rice bowls and samgak kimbap. Takeout and delivery are both available, making it a convenient stop for a hearty meal on a Fraser Street cycling route.

restaurant.name: Church's Chicken
restaurant.desc: Church's Chicken (operating as Church's Texas Chicken in the Lower Mainland) is a fried chicken fast food chain at a strip-mall location in Richmond's Blundell area. This location offers drive-through, in-store pickup, and delivery via DoorDash, Skip, UberEats, and Fantuan. A touring cyclist would find it a functional, round-the-clock food stop with Wi-Fi.

restaurant.name: Cafe Medina
restaurant.desc: Café Medina is a Mediterranean-inspired brunch destination in the heart of downtown Vancouver, open since 2008 and recognized by the Michelin Guide every year since 2022. The restaurant is celebrated for its signature Belgian waffles, eclectic bistro fare, and connoisseur-level coffee in a bright, open space with soaring ceilings and an open kitchen. It also hosts private evening events for up to 70 guests in its curated private dining room.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms GF options ('some of our dishes can be prepared without wheat, and we also offer gluten-free option') and vegetarian dishes ('we serve some vegetarian dishes made with fresh, seasonal ingredients'); several menu items are explicitly marked 'can be vegetarian'

restaurant.name: Steve's Poke Bar
restaurant.desc: Steve's Poké Bar is an authentic Hawaiian poke chain founded by Steve Huynh, who grew up between Vancouver and Honolulu and draws on family recipes and local Hawaiian poké traditions. The Canada Place location places it steps from Vancouver's waterfront and convention centre, making it a convenient stop on a harbour cycling route. With over 10,000 five-star Google reviews and a menu spanning signature bowls, build-your-own options, and catering, it has become a well-established local institution.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Shoyu Tofu bowl (7 pcs tofu with avocado, rice, and toppings), confirming at least one vegetarian option

restaurant.name: Ocean Beach - Crafts | Drafts | Eats
restaurant.desc: The Ocean Beach is a historic waterfront pub housed in a building dating back to 1930 — originally part of the Blue Moon Empire and later the Ocean Beach Hotel — now rebranded in 2020 under the long-standing Veltri family. Perched on Marine Drive in White Rock with direct ocean views, the industrial-chic interior features oak décor and old-world brick, making it a natural and atmospheric stop for cyclists on the waterfront route. The menu spans craft cocktails, seafood platters, and hearty bar food with plant-based options.

detail.address: 14995 Marine Drive, White Rock, BC V4B 1C3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Sweet Chili Tofu described as '100% plant-based', plus multiple vegetarian dishes including Parmesan Crusted Cauliflower, Beet Harvest Salad, and Whipped Ricotta Bruschetta

restaurant.name: Popeyes
restaurant.desc: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen is a national fast food chain specializing in Southern-style fried chicken, located on Bridgeport Road in Richmond. This location is halal-certified according to OSM tags, which may be relevant to some touring cyclists. It offers takeout service and is situated in a commercial area of Richmond.

restaurant.name: Fanny Bay Oyster Bar
restaurant.desc: Fanny Bay Oyster Bar is a Michelin-recommended seafood restaurant and retail shellfish market in Vancouver's stadium district, serving freshly shucked oysters and BC shellfish farmed directly by the Taylor Shellfish family for over 40 years. Cyclists will find a full dine-in oyster bar alongside a retail shellfish market with online ordering for pickup, located near BC Place at 762 Cambie Street.

notes.Takeout: Onsite Shellfish Market offers retail pickup of live shellfish; online ordering available with same-day pickup. Note: prepared dine-in shellfish explicitly cannot be taken to go per the website

restaurant.name: Hokkaido Ramen Santouka
restaurant.desc: Hokkaido Ramen Santouka is a Japanese ramen chain founded in 1988 in Asahikawa, Hokkaido, celebrated for its mild white tonkotsu broth and signature shio ramen served with a pickled plum in a specially designed round bowl. The Robson Street location places it in Vancouver's West End, a short ride from Stanley Park and the seawall — a natural refueling stop on one of the city's most popular cycling corridors. The menu spans shio, shoyu, miso, spicy miso, and char siu ramen varieties, all made from scratch at each restaurant.

restaurant.name: Hiro Sushi Xpress
restaurant.desc: Hiro Japan Sushi Xpress is a quick-serve Japanese food chain with a Victoria outlet inside Hillside Shopping Centre, offering fresh-made sushi, teriyaki meals, bento boxes, and Japanese noodle dishes. The concept was established in Vancouver in 2003 and prioritizes fresh, daily-made product with a focus on health and sustainability. A touring cyclist stopping at Hillside can grab a ready-made sushi or bento box to go.

restaurant.name: PureBread
restaurant.desc: PureBread is an artisan bakery originating in Whistler that has grown to multiple BC locations, including this Gastown outpost on West Hastings Street. It is known for freshly baked breads, pastries, and savoury treats, and has been featured in outlets such as the New York Times and Lonely Planet. For a touring cyclist passing through downtown Vancouver, it is a quality food stop within the Gastown neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Gelato Express
restaurant.desc: Gelato Express is a gelato shop on Robson Street in Vancouver's West End, specializing in authentic Italian-style gelato with flavors ranging from passion fruit and blood orange to tiramisu and Ferrero Rocher. The shop features both indoor and outdoor seating in a cozy, modern space decorated with artwork and Minions paraphernalia. It's a convenient sweet-stop for cyclists riding through downtown Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Honolulu Coffee
restaurant.desc: Honolulu Coffee is a Hawaii-origin specialty coffee chain bringing farm-to-cup Kona coffee to its café locations, including this spot in downtown Vancouver. The brand sources its beans from its own Kona farm on the Big Island and emphasizes single-origin quality. Touring cyclists passing through the Nelson Street corridor will find indoor and outdoor seating and vegetarian-friendly options.

restaurant.name: Shaughnessy's Cove
restaurant.desc: Shaughnessy's Cove is a premium casual lakeside restaurant on South Lakeshore Drive in Summerland, operated by Mackenzie Hospitality Group since a full gut-and-rebuild renovation in 2021. The space carries nearly 35 years of history under the 'Cove' name and features a heated patio with lake views. It serves lunch, dinner, and weekend brunch, and accommodates walk-ins as well as reservations.

restaurant.name: Olympus Ice Cream & Bubble Tea
restaurant.desc: Olympus Ice Cream & Bubble Tea is a dessert shop on Victoria's busy Government Street, serving both ice cream and bubble tea. It sits on one of downtown Victoria's main tourist corridors, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the city centre.

restaurant.name: Liberty Wine Merchants
restaurant.desc: Liberty Wine Merchants is a Vancouver institution founded in 1986, built around artisan and small-batch wines from independent producers rather than mass-market labels. With five Lower Mainland locations — including Point Grey, Commercial Drive, and Granville Island — it also stocks a wide range of spirits, beer, cider, and sake. A touring cyclist looking to pick up a distinctive bottle for the evening would find the selection well above average for a neighbourhood bottle shop.

detail.address: 510 W 8th Ave, Vancouver, BC V5Z 1C5, Canada

restaurant.name: Cliffhouse Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Cliff House Restaurant is a casual West Coast dining room inside Capilano Suspension Bridge Park, perched above the canyon on the site of the original 1889 Cliff House. It serves fresh local ingredients, Ocean Wise seafood, BC wines, and regional craft beer on tap, with a large summer patio and cozy historic interior. Access requires purchasing paid park admission, making it a destination experience rather than a quick cyclist stop.

detail.address: 3735 Capilano Road, North Vancouver, BC V7R 4J1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Black Bean & Corn Burger, Hummus & Pita, Capilano Canyon Salad, and Rice Bowl — multiple vegetarian options confirmed

restaurant.name: Beach Grove Golf Club Lounge
restaurant.desc: Beach Grove Golf Club is a private, member-owned coastal club near Boundary Bay in Tsawwassen, operating for nearly a century. The clubhouse hosts two dining venues—the Grille and the Bistro—serving chef-inspired menus using fresh, local, and sustainable ingredients. Guests are welcome for dining and private events, making the clubhouse accessible to non-members passing through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dining page explicitly mentions 'thoughtfully prepared vegetarian creations' as part of Chef Kay Noh's menu offering

restaurant.name: The Pie Hole
restaurant.desc: The Pie Hole is a Lower Mainland pie bakery founded in 2011 by Jenell Parsons — dubbed 'Canada's Pie Queen' and featured on Guy Fieri's Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives — now operating three locations including this Burnaby shop on 6th Street. The menu spans an eclectic mix of freshly made sweet and savory pies (from Fat Elvis banana-cream to Thai Chicken and Mac & Cheese) available by the slice, whole pie, or hand pie for eat-in or takeout. All pies are made from scratch using locally sourced produce and free-range eggs.

restaurant.name: Rice and Noodle
restaurant.desc: Rice and Noodle is a BC-based fast-casual Southeast Asian chain that has operated since 2010, specializing in cooked-to-order dishes like pad thai, curries, and noodle bowls with customizable protein and spice levels. The Lonsdale Avenue location sits in a busy North Vancouver corridor and offers dine-in, takeout, and third-party delivery. It is part of a growing franchise with multiple Lower Mainland locations.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu offers tofu as a selectable protein across all dishes, and mixed veggies as a protein option; many dishes are vegetable-forward. Vegan and GF status not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: Rise & Grind Coffee
restaurant.desc: Rise & Grind Coffee is a cafe located in Courtenay. It provides a stopping point for touring cyclists seeking refreshment and a break during their travels.

restaurant.name: Flavor Balance Espresso Bar
restaurant.desc: Flavour Balance Espresso Bar is a neighbourhood café on Belmont Street in North Vancouver offering espresso drinks and vegetarian-friendly food, with both indoor and outdoor seating. The no-smoking policy and patio make it a potentially pleasant rest stop for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Bread Co.
restaurant.desc: Bread Co. is a fifth-generation Dutch-heritage bakery café whose founders began baking in the Netherlands in 1851; the current Bronswyk family owners bring those traditions to three Kelowna locations. The Pandosy Ave café serves freshly baked artisan breads made with organic flours and sea salt, house-made soups, breakfast and lunch dishes, and a rotating menu of specialty coffee and seasonal drinks. Touring cyclists will find a full-service sit-down café with a vegan bread range and online pickup ordering.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'Vegan Artisan Breads' as a dedicated menu category. Menu includes vegetarian items (avocado/spinach egg sandwiches, vegetable platters). Site notes products are 'not suitable for those with Celiac Disease' but 'recommended for gluten intolerance or dietary choice only', indicating gluten-friendly but not certified GF

restaurant.name: Steamworks Brewery and Tap Room
restaurant.desc: The Steamworks Burnaby Brewery and Taproom is a large-scale craft production facility opened in 2013, housing 32 fermentors, 3 grain silos, and a 500-foot canning line that produces thousands of barrels of beer annually. The taproom pours directly from tank to tap, rotating through core and seasonal steam-brewed beers alongside occasional test taps. A Steamworks food truck stationed outside serves burgers, wings, and poutine, and the facility also offers growler fills, cold beer sales, and keg rentals.

restaurant.name: Chubby Duck's
restaurant.desc: Chubby Duck's is a casual kebab and poutine spot in Whistler Village, notable for serving exclusively certified halal meats alongside falafel and vegetarian options. Located in Village Green, it caters to a late-night crowd and offers online ordering. A touring cyclist looking for a quick, filling meal with halal or vegetarian options will find a solid selection here.

detail.address: Unit 9, 4122 Village Green, Whistler, BC V8E1G9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Falafel as a protein choice in kebabs and packs, a dedicated Veggie Pack (falafel salad with fries, hummus & tzatziki), and Pita & Hummus. Allergen note mentions sesame, dairy, and gluten but no GF confirmation

restaurant.name: Trocadero Pizza & Steak House
restaurant.desc: Trocadero has been feeding East Vancouver since 1970, offering home-style Italian and Greek cooking — think all-natural-ingredient pizzas, charbroiled lamb chops, and hand-made spanakopita — in a spacious dining room built for families and large parties. The restaurant sits on Nanaimo Street between 8th Avenue and Broadway, a busy urban cycling corridor, with a secure 16-space on-site parking lot and a 10-minute walk to Broadway-Commercial SkyTrain.

notes.Takeout: 'Order Online' link in website navigation header; website also references delivery ('Debit is not available for deliveries'), confirming off-premise orders are accepted
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian items: Spanakopita (handmade spinach-feta filo pastry), Hummus, Tzatziki, Saganaki, Fasolada (white bean and vegetable soup), Zucchini Sticks, and several salads

restaurant.name: Glo Restaurant & Lounge
restaurant.desc: Glo Restaurant + Lounge sits on the Selkirk Waterway in Victoria, just minutes from the Galloping Goose Regional Trail, making it a natural stop for cyclists on one of BC's most popular multi-use paths. The 180-degree wrap-around patio features heaters, blankets, and umbrellas for year-round outdoor dining with unobstructed waterway views. Executive Chef Andrew Fawcett's seasonally changing menu draws on local and global inspiration, with strong vegetarian and gluten-friendly representation throughout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu consistently marks items 'veg' (vegetarian) and 'gf' (gluten friendly) throughout starters, flatbreads, and other sections; e.g. Crispy Cauliflower + Potatoes (veg), Queso Jalapeño + Spinach Dip (gf + veg), Chicken Wings (gf)

restaurant.name: Eleni's Greek Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Eleni's Greek Restaurant is a family-owned establishment in Downtown Mission serving a broad menu of Greek specialties alongside pasta, seafood, chicken, veal, steaks, and burgers. It has built a local reputation for generous platters, attentive service, and a welcoming atmosphere. A touring cyclist passing through the Fraser Valley would find it a solid sit-down meal option in the heart of Mission's main street.

restaurant.name: Portguese Club of Vancouver
restaurant.desc: The Portuguese Club of Vancouver (PCOV), founded in 1962, claims to be Canada's oldest Portuguese club and has been a cornerstone of the Portuguese community on Vancouver's Commercial Drive for over six decades. It operates a full restaurant serving authentic Portuguese cuisine — including bacalhau, grilled calamari, and chouriço — available for dine-in, takeout, and event catering. The club also features dual big-screen TVs for live sports and hosts cultural events like Sardine Day, making it a lively neighbourhood destination.

restaurant.name: Syren's Bistro
restaurant.desc: Syren's Bistro is a restaurant located in Sidney, BC, a small seaside town on the Saanich Peninsula at the southern tip of Vancouver Island. Sidney is a popular stop on Gulf Islands cycling routes and the BC Ferries corridor. The bistro name and coastal setting suggest a nautical character typical of the Sidney waterfront area.

detail.address: 9801 Spalding Rd, Pender Island, BC V0N 2M3, Canada

restaurant.name: Floyd's Diner
restaurant.desc: Floyd's Diner is a Victoria, BC institution established in 2004, best known for 'The Mahoney' — a large breakfast challenge that has become a local legend. The Royal Oak location on West Saanich Road is one of four family-friendly diners across greater Victoria. It offers a casual, welcoming atmosphere with a breakfast and lunch menu, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring the Saanich Peninsula.

detail.address: 4496 West Saanich Rd, Victoria, BC V8Z 3E9

restaurant.name: Alice & Brohms
restaurant.desc: Alice & Brohm Ice Cream Co. is a New Zealand-inspired real-fruit ice cream shop with two Squamish locations, blending locally sourced BC berries and dairy right in front of customers with no added colours or flavours. Both shops offer outdoor seating — the Mamquam Road location has a large patio at the Squamish Town Hub, while the Second Ave location has a patio just off the downtown main strip. It's a natural post-ride treat stop given Squamish's reputation as an outdoor adventure hub.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Our berry ice cream flavours are gluten free' and offers a 'coconut plant-based ice cream' base option for vegan customers

restaurant.name: Ora Sushi
restaurant.desc: Ora Sushi is a sit-down sushi restaurant on Moncton Street in Richmond's Steveston neighbourhood, a short ride from the waterfront and popular cycling paths along the Fraser River. It brands itself around fresh sushi and a casual, welcoming atmosphere. Touring cyclists passing through Steveston would find it a convenient option for a Japanese meal near the water.

restaurant.name: Niagara Falls Resaurant
restaurant.desc: Niagara Pizza has been a Ladner community institution since 1975, run by the same family across two generations. Located in the Harbourside Strip Mall, it offers a broad scratch-made menu spanning homemade pizzas, classic Greek dishes (spanakopita, souvlaki, saganaki), steaks, seafood, and pasta. The 85-seat dining room can accommodate large groups, and takeout and local delivery are also available.

notes.Takeout: Website states: 'give us a call for convenient takeout or delivery (in Ladner only).'

restaurant.name: Afghan Turkish Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Afghan Turkish Cuisine is a restaurant in Burnaby serving Afghan and Turkish cuisine with indoor seating. A touring cyclist can stop here for a sit-down meal on Willingdon Avenue.

restaurant.name: The Fernie Taphouse
restaurant.desc: The Fernie Taphouse is a historic gastropub at the heart of downtown Fernie, housed in a building rebuilt after the Great Fire of 1908 with bootlegger tunnels still intact beneath it. It offers a wide menu of classic pub fare — from beer-battered fish and chips to rotating daily specials — alongside 20+ rotating BC craft beers on tap and a heated seasonal patio. The venue is actively community-connected, sponsoring local cycling events such as the Gravel Grind Post Race Afterparty and the Fernie Trails & Touring Club.

notes.Wi-Fi: Website mentions 'private meeting room with WiFi and TV access — perfect for work meetings and lunches'; Wi-Fi confirmed for that space, but general dining-room availability is not explicitly stated

restaurant.name: Hundo-P Smoothies and Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Hundo-P is a health-focused smoothie and non-dairy ice cream shop that originated in Whistler Village before expanding to Burnaby. Everything is made fresh in front of you using real fruit and whole-food ingredients, with protein-packed 24oz smoothies and a full line of coconut-and-cashew-based ice cream proudly made in Canada. For a touring cyclist, it's a solid stop for a nutritious, on-the-go refuel with options to suit dairy-free and plant-based diets.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items labelled '(V)' (vegan) and '(DF)' (dairy-free) on the website; entire ice cream line is non-dairy (coconut and cashew base). No explicit gluten-free labelling found

restaurant.name: Tokyo In April
restaurant.desc: Tokyo in April is a Japanese restaurant in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood specializing in premium sushi and contemporary Japanese dishes, with particular emphasis on bluefin tuna, uni, and signature omurice creations. The restaurant offers both dine-in and online pick-up ordering through its own platform. The building provides free two-hour underground parking for customers.

notes.Takeout: Website shows 'Order for Pick-up' option with online ordering system; party tray menu is listed as 'Take-Out Only'

restaurant.name: Coffeehouse at Shoal Point
restaurant.desc: Coffeehouse at Shoal Point is a coffee shop tucked inside the Shoal Point condominium complex on Dallas Road along Victoria's southern waterfront. Its location puts it directly on a popular cycling corridor connecting the Inner Harbour to Beacon Hill Park and the Dallas Road seawall. OSM notes outdoor seating, making it a plausible rest stop for cyclists passing through.

detail.address: Unit 110, 19 Dallas Road, Victoria, BC V8V 5A6

restaurant.name: Sun Bo Kong Vegetarian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Sun Bo Kong is a fully vegetarian and vegan Cantonese restaurant that has anchored Vancouver's plant-based dining scene since 1992, built around 100% handmade dim sum and a menu of over 160 authentic dishes. Founded by Ken Chau, the restaurant has long pioneered innovative vegetarian interpretations of classic Chinese cuisine, with some of its original creations now considered mainstream vegetarian staples. Cyclists seeking substantial plant-based fuel will find a calm dine-in room alongside takeout and third-party delivery options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Cantonese vegetarian and vegan fare since 1992'; all menu items are vegetarian/vegan

restaurant.name: Terra Breads
restaurant.desc: Terra Breads is a Vancouver artisan bakery founded in 1993, celebrated for its small-batch sourdough loaves, granola, and café selections made with locally sourced, whole ingredients and no added preservatives. The Olympic Village location sits in a waterfront neighborhood that is a natural waypoint for cyclists exploring the Seawall and surrounding routes. Visitors experience a warm, community-focused café with both indoor and outdoor seating and a menu built around hearty, quality baked goods.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website recipes and café menu include explicitly vegetarian items (Smashed Chickpea Sandwich, Avocado Toast with Halloumi, Breakfast Toast with Ricotta); no GF claim found on website

restaurant.name: Sushi King House
restaurant.desc: A sushi restaurant on Granville Street in south Vancouver. Offers sushi and Japanese cuisine to cyclists and other travelers passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Mama's Japanese Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Mama's Japanese Kitchen is a small, no-reservations Japanese restaurant situated at the Harbour Spirit Centre on the corner of Madeira Park Road and Highway 101 in Madeira Park. The kitchen uses no MSG or peanuts and offers both dine-in and takeout, including a signature Big Tray sushi platter available with advance ordering. It is a locally-run spot serving authentic Japanese cuisine in a small Sunshine Coast community, making it a notable meal stop for cyclists travelling the Highway 101 corridor.

detail.address: 12808 Madeira Park Road, Madeira Park, V0N 2H0

restaurant.name: Kozak Ukrainian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kozak is a Ukrainian restaurant and cafe in Langley serving homemade Ukrainian food. It presents itself as an authentic destination for traditional Ukrainian cuisine in the Fraser Valley. Online ordering is available, suggesting the kitchen can accommodate both dine-in and takeout customers.

restaurant.name: Woking Dragon Chop Suey House
restaurant.desc: Woking Dragon Chop Suey House is a family-owned Chinese restaurant chain operating since 2003, offering modern western-style Chinese cuisine with a nod to traditional recipes. The Maple Ridge location sits on Dewdney Trunk Road and is one of three Lower Mainland locations. It has earned recognition as a favourite Chinese restaurant in the Tri-Cities area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Some menu items are able to be made Vegan & Gluten-Free'

restaurant.name: Non-Stop Pizza
restaurant.desc: Non-Stop Pizza is a fast-food pizza takeout shop mapped in Tsawwassen/Ladner. Its current operational status is uncertain, as an OSM contributor has flagged a concern that it may no longer exist or may have merged with an adjacent pizza business.

notes.Takeout: No independent confirmation available)

restaurant.name: Golden Smell Mee Malaysian Singaporeon Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Golden Smell Mee is a Malaysian-Singaporean restaurant in Vancouver's Chinatown reuniting two family culinary legacies that trace back to 1986. The menu centres on handmade noodles, laksa, roti canai, Hainanese chicken rice, and slow-cooked curries drawing on Malay, Chinese, and Indian influences. A touring cyclist stopping in the Chinatown area will find a cozy, full-service dine-in restaurant with online ordering.

detail.address: 142 East Pender Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 1T3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels 'Vegetarian option' for Curried Potatoes and Vegetables curry puff; no vegan or GF labels observed

restaurant.name: Working Culture Bread
restaurant.desc: Working Culture Bread is a family-run neighbourhood bakery and coffee shop in Victoria's Rock Bay area, open since 2020. They specialize in organic sourdough loaves made with just flour, water, and salt — using stone-milled BC whole grain flours — alongside rustic pastries and focaccia sandwiches. Their daily rotating bread menu and community-focused ethos make it a genuine local stop for cyclists looking for quality baked goods and a fresh coffee.

restaurant.name: Cherry Pit Restaurant & Catering
restaurant.desc: Cherry Pit is a restaurant in Kelowna, BC, recorded in OpenStreetMap with minimal metadata. No further details about its cuisine, setting, or offerings could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Little Minh's
restaurant.desc: Little Minh's is a Vietnamese restaurant on Marine Way in Vancouver offering vegetarian-friendly dining. The restaurant accepts both credit and debit card payments, making it convenient for touring cyclists.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian options confirmed

restaurant.name: Montana's
restaurant.desc: Montana's BBQ & Bar is a barbecue restaurant chain location in Fort St. John. It offers a convenient dining stop for touring cyclists moving through the region.

restaurant.name: The Bunker
restaurant.desc: The Bunker is a cafe located in Whistler, BC, operating under a name that suggests a distinctive, perhaps underground-themed atmosphere suited to a mountain resort town. As a cafe in one of Canada's premier cycling and outdoor destinations, it is potentially a useful stop for touring cyclists passing through the Whistler corridor.

detail.address: 7015 Nesters Rd #104, Whistler, BC V8E 0X1, Canada

restaurant.name: 8th generation vineyard
restaurant.desc: 8th Generation Vineyard is a family-owned estate winery in Summerland, BC, carrying 243 years of unbroken winemaking heritage that traces back to 1783 in the Rheinhessen village of Dalsheim, Germany. Founders Bernd and Stefanie Schales arrived in the Okanagan in 2003, bringing their grandfather's winepress and generations of grape-growing expertise to produce 100% BC-fruit wines using minimal-intervention techniques. Visitors are welcomed at the farmhouse wine shop to taste and purchase the boutique lineup of whites, rosés, reds, frizzante, and cider.

restaurant.name: Saku
restaurant.desc: SAKU is a Canadian katsu restaurant chain that introduced traditional Japanese tonkatsu to Vancouver in 2018, distinguishing itself with Duroc-breed pork sourced from Canadian farms and fresh panko baked daily by COBS Bread. The Burquitlam location serves a full dine-in and takeout menu of pork, chicken, seafood, and vegetable katsu sets with unlimited rice and miso soup. The brand gained wider recognition after appearing on Dragon's Den and has since expanded to multiple Metro Vancouver locations and Toronto.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels 'Vegetable Katsu' (deep fried breaded tofu and seasonal vegetables) and 'Vegetable Curry' as Vegetarian

restaurant.name: Kyabia Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kyabia is a Japanese restaurant in Richmond with indoor seating. The restaurant serves customers throughout the week. Touring cyclists can stop for meals during their travels through the area.

restaurant.name: Doughgirls
restaurant.desc: Doughgirls is a neighbourhood bakeshop and comfort kitchen in Wesbrook Village, founded by two culinary professionals with decades of combined experience. The shop turns out artisan breads baked fresh daily, handcrafted comfort foods made with local and sustainable ingredients, and take-n-bake meals including savoury pies and seasonal soups. A large reclaimed fir communal table anchors the welcoming dining room, making it a practical and convivial stop for fresh food.

restaurant.name: Tackle Box Coffee Bar
restaurant.desc: The Tackle Box Coffee Bar is a specialty coffee bar nestled inside Rustic Reel Brewing Company in Kelowna, offering espresso drinks, teas, hot chocolate, and seasonal specialties alongside locally-sourced pastries and grab-and-go sandwiches. The space features a modern-rustic design with a cozy fireplace, nook seating, and a Community Room suited for meetings or work sessions. It draws both locals and visitors as a morning stop before an afternoon at the brewery taproom.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu includes vegetarian/vegan options (falafel Mediterranean wrap, black bean quesadilla, vegan nacho build options) and gluten-free bun substitutions noted throughout

restaurant.name: Greta YVR
restaurant.desc: Greta YVR is an adults-only arcade bar in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, combining craft cocktails, scratch-made locally sourced street food, and 50+ arcade games under one roof. It is part of a Canadian multi-city chain and offers a lively venue for small groups, large parties, and corporate events. Cyclists of legal drinking age stopping in Gastown for an evening out would find food, drinks, and entertainment all in one place.

restaurant.name: Pizza Factory
restaurant.desc: Pizza Factory is a pizza fast-food restaurant in Burnaby offering delivery and takeaway service. It provides convenient quick-service dining for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: R & B Ale & Pizza House
restaurant.desc: A pub in Vancouver serving ale and pizza. Specific details about the establishment and amenities could not be verified.

restaurant.name: East Van Roasters
restaurant.desc: East Van Roasters is a social enterprise cafe and bean-to-bar chocolate maker in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside, providing career training and meaningful employment for women experiencing barriers to employment. The cafe serves specialty espresso drinks, single-origin drinking chocolates, and freshly baked cookies, with an open-door community ethos that includes a suspended coffee program for local community members. The business has taken home multiple International Chocolate Awards and makes all its single-origin chocolates on-site.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states: 'Vegan alternatives are available for all drinks.'

restaurant.name: Perro Negro
restaurant.desc: Perro Negro is a Spanish tapas restaurant located on Yates Street in downtown Victoria. The restaurant specializes in small plates characteristic of Spanish cuisine, offering a sit-down dining option for touring cyclists. The business is listed as currently operational, though website verification is pending.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: McDonald's is a globally recognized fast-food chain serving burgers, chicken sandwiches, fries, and McCafé beverages. This Richmond location on Sweden Way includes drive-through and takeaway service, making it a quick and convenient calorie stop. It sits in Richmond's industrial Sweden Way corridor, a useful refuelling point for cyclists navigating that part of the city.

restaurant.name: Pointage Bakery
restaurant.desc: Pointage Bakery is a small-batch artisan bread shop in Richmond, BC, founded by Vivian after training in French boulangerie at Le Cordon Bleu Japan. The name 'Pointage' refers to the fermentation stage of bread-making, reflecting the bakery's philosophy of patience, natural ingredients, and no preservatives. Items such as Mentaiko Baguette, Double Matcha Bagel, and a curated Weekly Bread Surprise Box are available for pre-order.

restaurant.name: Kin Sushi
restaurant.desc: Kin Sushi is a sushi restaurant located in North Vancouver, BC. It offers indoor seating in a no-smoking environment. As a sit-down Japanese cuisine spot, it could serve as a meal stop for cyclists exploring the North Shore.

detail.address: 1760 Marine Dr #113, West Vancouver, BC V7V 1A9, Canada

restaurant.name: Jun Yuan Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Jun Yuan Restaurant is an all-you-can-eat Chinese hotpot restaurant specializing in broths simmered for over five hours from scratch, alongside a vast selection of fresh meats, handmade fish puffs, seafood, and vegetables. The founder has over 20 years in the food industry and developed the restaurant's signature handmade fish tofu (魚腐), a Cantonese Shunde tradition, which became popular enough to supply local supermarkets and restaurants. Chicken wing takeout combos are also available for cyclists looking for a quick, portable meal.

restaurant.name: Chuan Yue
restaurant.desc: Chuan Yue is a Chinese restaurant on Oak Street offering both dine-in and takeout service, with online ordering available. It serves a wide range of Chinese dishes and has earned enthusiastic reviews from local customers. A touring cyclist coming through the area would find it a convenient stop for a sit-down meal or a quick pickup order.

restaurant.name: Dudes Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Dudes Coffee House is a local, family-run café in South Surrey opened in 2015 by Kelly and Larry Kristof. The shop roasts and brews specialty coffee and serves an all-day breakfast and lunch menu, house-made baked goods, and weekend brunch with Dim Sum on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays. It sits in a small strip-unit setting on Crescent Road, making it a convenient stop for cyclists exploring the South Surrey area.

restaurant.name: Nemesis
restaurant.desc: Nemesis is a specialty coffee roaster and multi-location cafe headquartered in Vancouver, with the Gastown flagship at 302 West Hastings Street offering espresso, filter coffee, and pastries from their in-house Dope Bakehouse. The company sources single-origin coffees directly from named producers and proudly supports World Coffee Research. Touring cyclists will find both indoor and outdoor seating at this well-established stop in the heart of Gastown.

restaurant.name: The Grind
restaurant.desc: The Grind is a cafe located at 1006 Beach Avenue in Vancouver's West End, positioned directly along the city's iconic seawall cycling route. It offers vegan and vegetarian menu options alongside both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists completing the seawall loop. Its outdoor patio faces one of Vancouver's busiest recreational corridors.

restaurant.name: HK B.B.Q. Master
restaurant.desc: HK B.B.Q. Master (明家燒臘專家, 'Ming Family Roasted Meats Specialist') is a Cantonese-style roast meat restaurant in Richmond, BC, specializing in Hong Kong-style BBQ staples like char siu, roast duck, and soy chicken. Richmond is one of Canada's premier destinations for authentic Cantonese cuisine, and this spot — operated by Eric Leung — sits within that culinary hub. For a touring cyclist, it offers a calorie-dense, flavour-forward meal typical of the region's exceptional Chinese food culture.

restaurant.name: Tapas on Oak
restaurant.desc: A tapas restaurant on Oak Bay Avenue offering Spanish-style small plates and drinks in a casual dining setting.

restaurant.name: Osaka Sushi
restaurant.desc: Osaka Sushi is a Japanese restaurant on West King Edward Avenue in Vancouver offering an extensive menu spanning traditional nigiri, sashimi, maki rolls, teriyaki, curry rice, and donburi. Online ordering with 15-minute pickup makes it a practical quick stop for cyclists moving through the area. The menu covers a wide range of Japanese dishes and includes clearly marked vegetarian options across most categories.

detail.address: 960 W King Edward Ave, Vancouver, BC V5Z 2E2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu legend explicitly marks vegetarian items; multiple vegetarian dishes confirmed including Vegetable Gyoza, Vegetable Tempura, Vegetable Curry, Tofu Teriyaki, Avocado Roll, and Kappa Roll

restaurant.name: Pho Bo Ga Ottawa
restaurant.desc: A Vietnamese pho restaurant serving traditional Vietnamese cuisine in North Vancouver. Offers sit-down dining for cyclists passing through the community.

restaurant.name: Grand Chinese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Grand Chinese Restaurant – Yaletown is a sit-down Chinese restaurant in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood offering an extensive menu of Northern Chinese, dim sum, and Korean-influenced dishes. The kitchen stands out for specialties like hand-folded Xinjiang cumin lamb dumplings, Shanghai xiao long bao, and Szechuan broth-braised beef that go well beyond a standard takeout menu. Its location one block from the False Creek Seawall puts it within easy reach of cyclists on one of Vancouver's most popular riding corridors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian items: Vegetable & Tofu Chow Mein, Steamed Veggie Dumplings, Deep-Fried Veggie Dumplings, Vegetable Buns, Pan-Fried Chive Pockets, and Red Bean Pan Cake

restaurant.name: Avalanche Pizza
restaurant.desc: Avalanche Pizza is a fast-food pizza restaurant located in Whistler, BC, serving the Gateway Drive area of the resort community. As a fast-food outlet in one of BC's premier cycling destinations, it would likely be a convenient refuelling stop for riders passing through Whistler. Its current operational status and on-site amenities could not be verified due to a compromised website.

restaurant.name: Yah-Yah-Ya
restaurant.desc: Yah-Yah-Ya is Richmond's outpost of a Tokyo-origin ramen chain, opened in 2014 as the brand's first overseas location. The kitchen specialises in Yokohama Iekei-style ramen, built on a tonkotsu-chicken broth simmered daily for at least 12 hours from pork backbones, pork knuckles, and chicken bones — no concentrated stock. A touring cyclist stopping here gets a substantial, deeply flavoured bowl in an indoor-only setting inside what appears to be a shopping-centre food court.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Gallery includes a labelled 'Veg. Mountain Vegan Ramen' dish, confirming at least one vegan menu item

restaurant.name: Sweet 7
restaurant.desc: Sweet 7 is a global mango drink and fruit tea chain that started in 2006 and has grown to over 1500 stores worldwide, with its Robson Street location serving Vancouver's busy West End. The brand specialises in fresh-fruit beverages brewed with raw ingredients and no artificial flavourings, drawing on Asian drink-shop tradition while catering to Canadian tastes. Robson Street is a high-traffic pedestrian and cycling corridor, making this a convenient stop for riders exploring the seawall or Stanley Park area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website describes all beverages made from fresh fruits and pure raw ingredients with no artificial flavourings — inherently vegetarian menu

restaurant.name: Caffè Fantastico
restaurant.desc: Caffè Fantastico is a locally-owned, family-run coffee roastery based in Victoria that has been roasting sustainably sourced, high-quality beans since at least 2009. The Kings Road location is one of several in the city, operating as either the Roastery or bar-deli, and hosts regular community events including poetry slams, live music, and book launches. Touring cyclists will find a full café menu, takeout options including charcuterie boxes, and a community-focused atmosphere.

restaurant.name: Mani
restaurant.desc: Mani is a Persian-fusion quick-service restaurant operated by Mani Food Services Ltd., offering a menu that blends traditional Iranian kabobs (koobideh, joojeh, lamb) with burgers, sandwiches, and sides. The combination of saffron chicken, rosemary lamb, and smoky eggplant preparations gives it a distinctly Middle Eastern flair unusual for a Marine Drive strip location. Cyclists passing through the West Vancouver corridor can order online for pickup or delivery, making a hot kabob plate an easy mid-ride fuel stop.

detail.address: 205-1425 Marine Dr, West Vancouver, BC V7T 1B8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Eggplant Parmesan Sandwich (fried eggplant, mozzarella, parmesan, basil, marinara on sourdough) and Caesar Salad as vegetarian options; no explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Paul Bakery, Café & Restaurant
restaurant.desc: PAUL Bakery, Café & Restaurant is the Vancouver outpost of the French artisan bakery chain founded in 1889, positioned here as a full-service dining destination on busy Robson Street. The space offers indoor and outdoor seating and hosts regular evening events including live music and a Martini Society. A touring cyclist looking for a sit-down meal, pastries, or bread in the West End will find a polished, accessible café experience.

restaurant.name: Verandah Cafe by the Beach
restaurant.desc: Verandah Cafe is a boutique beachside cafe on Marine Drive in White Rock, set in a historic rustic beach-house property overlooking East Beach near Semiahmoo Park. The menu draws on the culinary heritage of the Indian subcontinent, offering Indian-inspired street food, fusion dishes, samosas, masala chai, and locally roasted fair-trade espresso. It opened in April 2018 as a community-minded gathering space and has hosted cooking classes, fitness events, and mental health talks.

detail.address: 15782 Marine Dr #3B, White Rock, BC V4B1E6

restaurant.name: Treats Concession
restaurant.desc: Treats Concession is a seasonal, takeout-only food kiosk operated within a City of New Westminster park. It serves as a convenient pit stop for cyclists passing through the park during summer months. No indoor or outdoor seating is provided, making it a grab-and-go stop.

restaurant.name: Deep Cove Caf/Eh
restaurant.desc: Deep Cove Caf/Eh is a café nestled in the scenic Deep Cove neighbourhood of North Vancouver, a beloved endpoint for cyclists riding out from the city along the inlet. The name is a knowing Canadian pun on 'café' and 'eh.' It offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a natural rest stop after exploring the local trails and waterfront.

restaurant.name: Clubhouse Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Clubhouse Restaurant sits at the edge of The Willows Golf Course on Moresby Island in Haida Gwaii—one of the most remote destinations in British Columbia—with a patio overlooking the ocean. The menu leans into casual coastal comfort: Haida Gwaii fish and chips, seared tuna, flatbread pizzas, and stacked burgers, alongside a newly added specialty coffee café. For a touring cyclist who has made it this far out to 'the edge of the world,' it serves as a genuine community hub and a rare full-service meal stop.

restaurant.name: HellCrust Pizza
restaurant.desc: HellCrust Pizza is a fast-food pizza franchise located inside Metrotown shopping mall in Burnaby, operating from unit E9 on the mall's upper level. It offers both delivery and carry-out ordering, making it a quick stop for a slice on the go. The surrounding Metrotown complex is a major transit and commercial hub along Kingsway.

detail.address: E9 4700 Kingsway Street, Burnaby, BC V5H 4N2

restaurant.name: Shishlik Grill House
restaurant.desc: Shishlik Grill House is a Persian kebab restaurant on North Vancouver's busy Lonsdale Avenue, serving an extensive menu of authentic Iranian grilled meats — from house-made Loghmeh to premium Shishlik lamb racks — alongside traditional stews like Ghormeh Sabzi and Fesenjan. It is one of two Lower Mainland locations (the second in Coquitlam) and uses a Square-powered platform for online pickup and delivery ordering. Cyclists riding the Lonsdale corridor will find filling rice-and-kebab platters and a broad menu well suited to a mid-tour meal.

detail.address: 1629 Lonsdale Avenue, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2J5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'VEGGIE KEBAB | کباب سبزیجات' as a standalone item

restaurant.name: Oriental Village
restaurant.desc: Chinese restaurant in Chilliwack. Website is currently inaccessible, but the business has a complete contact record with address and phone number for customer inquiries.

restaurant.name: Pizza64
restaurant.desc: Pizza64 is a BC pizza chain franchise located on Shaughnessy Street in Port Coquitlam, offering both counter pickup and delivery. The Port Coquitlam location is a quick-service spot suited for a casual meal stop on a ride through the Tri-Cities area. The menu and seating details are not described on the website, but the takeout option with a 15-minute estimated pickup time makes it a potentially efficient stop.

restaurant.name: Resurrection Distillery and Lounge
restaurant.desc: Resurrection Spirits is a small-batch craft distillery located in East Vancouver's industrial district at the north end of Commercial Drive, producing gin, rye whisky, and vodka using 100% BC rye grain. The operation draws on Vancouver's Prohibition-era drinking culture and pairs an on-site lounge with distillery production. Cyclists exploring East Van have a locally owned destination for craft spirits in a distinctive industrial setting.

restaurant.name: Tickleberry's
restaurant.desc: Tickleberry's Downtown is the year-round outpost of the beloved Okanagan Falls ice cream institution, serving made-in-house ice cream cones, Bright Jenny Coffee from Kelowna, and house-made treats at a full-service coffee shop. The location also houses an in-house Fudge Factory where visitors can watch confections being made, plus a gift shop stocked with local B.C. gourmet food and artisan goods. It's a natural stop for cyclists travelling the Okanagan corridor looking for a sweet treat and a rest.

restaurant.name: MKR Kitchen & Bar
restaurant.desc: MKR Kitchen & Bar brings authentic Nepali cuisine to Marine Drive in White Rock, serving house-made momos, chatamari, thali sets, and biriyani alongside Western pub fare in a warm, community-oriented setting. The restaurant features outdoor seating and positions itself as a destination for both casual meals and celebrations. It is a distinctive culinary stop on the White Rock waterfront, offering a flavour profile rarely found along BC cycling routes.

detail.address: 15019 Marine Drive, White Rock, BC V4B 1C3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists multiple vegetarian options: Veg Momo (steam or fried), Mix Veg Chowmein, Veg Biriyani, Veg Chatamari, Crispy Veg Pakora, and a Nepali Thali Set including seasonal vegetables and yogurt. No explicit GF or vegan labels found on site

restaurant.name: Sushi Mura
restaurant.desc: Sushi Mura is a Japanese sushi restaurant chain that has been growing in Vancouver since 2012, with the Oak Street location seating up to 50 guests. The kitchen emphasises daily-delivered fresh fish, generous roll portions, and a broad menu spanning nigiri, sashimi, specialty rolls, noodles, and donburi. Cyclists can dine in or order takeout for pickup, with delivery also available through UberEats, Skip The Dishes, and DoorDash.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple 'Veggie'-labelled items including Veggie Wakame (seaweed salad), Veggie Ebi Sunomono, Vegetable Sunomono, Veggie Ika Karage, and Agedashi Tofu; no GF or vegan labelling found

restaurant.name: Triple O's
restaurant.desc: Triple O's is a BC-born quick-service burger chain celebrated for its signature Triple "O" sauce, hand-scooped milkshakes, and fresh-cut Kennebec fries. This Sardis/Chilliwack location is co-located inside a Chevron gas station on Vedder Road and offers drive-thru, dine-in, and takeout options including breakfast. It sits on a main arterial route through the Fraser Valley, making it a convenient calorie stop for touring cyclists moving through the Chilliwack area.

restaurant.name: Boston Pizza
restaurant.desc: Boston Pizza Tsawwassen is a franchise location of Canada's largest casual dining chain, situated in the Tsawwassen area of Delta near the Tsawwassen Mills shopping development. The restaurant combines a full sit-down dining room with a sports bar atmosphere, offering a broad menu of pizzas, pastas, wings, and more. Cyclists on the Canoe Pass Way corridor will find it a convenient full-service meal stop with dietary accommodations including gluten-free and vegetarian options.

detail.address: 3 - 5000 Canoe Pass Way, Tsawwassen, BC, V4M 0B3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Vegan and Glutenwise® options also available'; menu includes a dedicated GlutenWise® section

restaurant.name: Mr Mikes
restaurant.desc: Mr. Mikes is a Canadian casual steakhouse chain founded in 1960, serving premium steaks, burgers, pastas, and shareable appetizers in a relaxed, unpretentious setting the brand calls 'SteakhouseCasual.' The Cranbrook location on Cranbrook Street North welcomes walk-ins and reservations, and positions itself as a gathering spot for both locals and travellers. A daily happy hour and a full takeout and delivery service make it a flexible stop for cyclists needing a proper sit-down meal or a meal to go.

detail.address: 1028 Cranbrook Street North, Cranbrook, BC V1C 3S3

restaurant.name: 4 Brothers Pizza
restaurant.desc: 4 Brothers Pizza is a pizza-focused fast-food restaurant on Howe Street in downtown Vancouver, positioning itself on quality ingredients and consistent results. The shop has indoor seating and accepts credit and debit cards, making it a convenient urban stop. It also operates a second location on Commercial Drive.

restaurant.name: Ra Sushi
restaurant.desc: Ra Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant offering dine-in and online ordering. Located on McCallum Road in a commercial area, it provides a convenient takeout option for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Joyeaux Café and Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Joyeaux Café & Restaurant is a long-running casual eatery in downtown Vancouver serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner from a menu blending Western dishes with Asian and Vietnamese cooking, including Vietnamese noodle soups, all rooted in owner Annie's home-cook recipes. Located on Howe Street in the city core, it offers dine-in and take-out as well as delivery, making it a convenient food stop for cyclists moving through the downtown grid.

restaurant.name: Felice Cafe
restaurant.desc: A cafe in Nanaimo offering Korean beef, coffee, and bubble tea. With outdoor seating and to-go options available, it's a convenient stop for cycling tourists seeking refreshment.

restaurant.name: Bella Gellataria
restaurant.desc: Bella Gelateria is a multiple award-winning artisan gelato shop that has claimed Best Gelato/Ice Cream in Vancouver from the Georgia Straight nearly every year since 2010, and placed in international competitions in Italy, Chicago, and Austin. The English Bay location on Davie Street sits just steps from the Stanley Park Seawall, making it a natural sweet-stop for cyclists completing the seawall loop. All gelato is made in small batches from 100% natural ingredients using Italian-imported Effi machines, with vegan sorbetto and gluten-free options available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu page: 'nut-free, gluten-free and dairy-free options'; sorbettos described as 'water-based and vegan friendly'

restaurant.name: Bubble Waffle Cafe
restaurant.desc: Bubble Waffle Cafe is a Hong Kong-style street food chain specialising in egg waffles (雞蛋仔), curry fish balls, rice noodle rolls, fish soup noodle combos, and a broad selection of Asian bubble teas and fruit drinks. The Burnaby outpost sits on the second floor of a Lougheed Highway mall, part of a wider BC chain with locations also in Aberdeen Centre, Public Market, and Park Royal. Cyclists passing through Burnaby can grab a quick hot snack or a customisable noodle bowl before continuing their ride.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: A Subway franchise located in Tsawwassen Commons, a retail centre near the Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal and BC Ferries routes. The restaurant offers made-to-order sandwiches, wraps, and salads with breakfast service and catering available. For cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen area, it is a reliable resupply stop with vegetarian and limited vegan options.

detail.address: 1612-4949 Canoe Pass Way, Tsawwassen, BC V4M 0B2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: No gluten-free evidence found

restaurant.name: Avenue Pizza
restaurant.desc: Avenue Pizza is a pizza-focused restaurant in the heart of Lumby, serving a wide range from classic pies to gourmet specialty pizzas alongside wings, poutine, wraps, and salads. It is a full sit-down and call-ahead spot that has been a local staple in this small North Okanagan community. Touring cyclists passing through Lumby on Highway 6 would find it a solid hot-meal option with a broad menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu states 'Gluten free available for any medium size only' and 'Dairy free cheese available upon request.' Vegetarian pizza option 'Garden Picks' (mushrooms, green peppers, onion, olives, fresh tomato) is listed. No explicit vegan claim

restaurant.name: Ucluelet Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Ucluelet Brewing Company is a craft brewery and tasting room housed inside the beautifully restored historic St. Aidan's on the Hill church on Peninsula Road in Ucluelet. The brewery produces a full lineup of house-crafted beers — from easy-drinking lagers and kölsch to hazy IPAs and an oatmeal coffee stout — served alongside a food menu in a cozy, community-oriented atmosphere. It is a genuine gathering place for locals and a natural stop for cyclists exploring Vancouver Island's wild west coast.

restaurant.name: Pemberton Hotel Pub Liquor  Store
restaurant.desc: The Pemberton Hotel is a historic local institution dating to around 1914, operating as an affordable hotel and community hub in the heart of Pemberton on the Sea-to-Sky corridor. The property includes an on-site pub, liquor store, and cannabis store, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists stocking up between Whistler and the rest of the region. It sits steps from restaurants, a supermarket, and a gas station, with free parking on site.

restaurant.name: Original Joe's
restaurant.desc: Original Joe's is a franchise bar and grill along the Princeton-Kamloops Highway in Kamloops. The casual restaurant provides a convenient refueling stop with a varied menu accommodating different dietary preferences. A reliable option when cycling through the area.

restaurant.name: Zab Bite
restaurant.desc: Zab Bite is an authentic Thai restaurant on Vancouver's Fraser Street specializing in bold E-Sarn cuisine from Thailand's Northeastern Khon Kaen region, with dishes prepared using culinary traditions passed down through generations. In 2024 it earned a Michelin Recommended designation, a notable distinction on a neighbourhood strip popular with cyclists. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, and catering, with a wide menu spanning papaya salads, aromatic soups, grilled meats, and vegetarian small plates.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes explicitly vegetarian items including Deep-Fried Tofu and Veggie Spring Rolls. No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Siam Thai Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Siam Thai Victoria is a Thai restaurant on Victoria's Fort Street offering a broad menu of classic and regional Thai dishes, from Pad Thai and curries to Isaan specialties like Som Tum and Crying Tiger Beef.
