Online ordering with a 15-minute pickup window makes it a practical and fast meal stop for cyclists moving through downtown. The menu includes a dedicated vegetarian section alongside seafood, chicken, beef, and pork options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated 'Vegetarian' menu section with 9+ items (Pad Thai Vegetarian, Vegetarian Curry, Garlic Broccoli, etc.); menu legend includes a vegetarian marker applied across multiple categories

restaurant.name: Sushi on the Strip
restaurant.desc: Sushi Rang is a food and drink establishment located in Cranbrook, BC, tagged in OpenStreetMap as a cafe. Its name suggests Japanese cuisine, though no further details about its offerings or character could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Switch Cafe
restaurant.desc: Switch Cafe is a specialty coffee and breakfast spot on Ellis Street in downtown Kelowna, serving creative espresso drinks, premium matcha lattes, London Fog teas, and breakfast wraps. The café has earned a 5.0 rating on Uber Eats and offers a compact but inventive menu that includes tiramisu lattes and iced strawberry matcha. Its central Kelowna location on Ellis Street puts it within easy reach of cyclists passing through the city core.

restaurant.name: Honest to Pete Roasters
restaurant.desc: Honest to Pete Coffee Roasters is a Vancouver café and micro-roastery founded by Peter, who developed an air-roasting technique he credits with producing a smoother, richer cup with a smaller environmental footprint. The shop sells its own house roasts — including the flagship Retrospresso blend — alongside barista equipment and accessories, and offers local delivery as well as in-store pickup. A blog post titled 'Espresso on wheels' suggests some community connection to cycling culture.

restaurant.name: VQA Wine Store
restaurant.desc: The BC Wine Information Centre has served as the official gateway to BC wine country since 1996, operated by a not-for-profit society that reinvests all proceeds into wine education, scholarships, and bursaries for viticulture students. It carries wines from over 170 BC wineries and regularly hosts in-store tastings featuring guest wineries. For cyclists touring the Okanagan's wine routes, it offers curated gourmet products, gift baskets, and a WSET-certified staff to guide selections.

detail.address: 553 Vees Dr Unit 101, Penticton, BC V2A 8S3

restaurant.name: Sushiway
restaurant.desc: Sushiway is a Japanese restaurant in Port Coquitlam featuring an open-kitchen concept where diners can watch chefs steam, chop, and stir fry. The menu spans sushi, sashimi, katsu, and Japanese comfort food alongside vegetarian staples like agedashi tofu and edamame. Online ordering is available for convenient takeout.

detail.address: 1150-1502 Broadway St, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 0G1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Agedashi Tofu, Edamame, and Gomae — all vegetarian options

restaurant.name: Moja Coffee
restaurant.desc: Moja Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster founded in 2003, with its Commercial Drive cafe serving as one of two Vancouver-area locations for a company that roasts small-batch, primarily single-origin beans in a handmade Joper roaster imported from Portugal. The name 'Moja' is Swahili for 'one,' a nod to co-founder Andrew Wentzel's Tanzanian roots and the company's philosophy of showcasing individual growing regions. Situated on one of Vancouver's most celebrated cycling corridors, the cafe offers both indoor and outdoor seating.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: Subway is a fast-food sandwich chain offering quick meals and takeout service. Located in downtown Grand Forks, it provides a convenient option for touring cyclists passing through the community.

restaurant.name: Taste of Thai
restaurant.desc: Taste of Thai is an established Vancouver Thai restaurant that has been serving authentic dishes since 1986, with chefs using special herbs and spices flown in fresh from Thailand. The menu spans curries, stir-fries, and rice dishes prepared without MSG, promising bold flavours and aromatic complexity. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down dining experience with online ordering for takeout on West Broadway, a major cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Heritage Asian Eatery
restaurant.desc: Heritage Asian Eatery is a casual downtown Vancouver spot in the Financial District serving classic Chinese comfort food with local ingredients in a communal, laid-back setting. The Pender Street location seats up to 60 guests and also accommodates private event bookings. It offers dine-in, takeout, and a relaxed vibe suited to a quick refuel stop.

restaurant.name: Café Today
restaurant.desc: Café Today is a neighbourhood coffee shop and all-day breakfast café in Nanaimo that has been serving fresh food and drinks since 2015. The café sources organic coffee beans from a local roaster and prepares all food on the day it is sold, offering an extensive menu of omelettes, sandwiches, wraps, bagels, and specialty coffee drinks. It has earned multiple third-party awards from platforms including Restaurant Guru and DoorDash, reflecting a strong local following.

detail.address: Unit 4, 5771 Turner Rd, Nanaimo, BC V9T 6L8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian items: Veggie Ranch Wrap, Avocado Toast, Spinach Feta Omelette, Avocado B.L.T. Sandwich, Green Salad, Granola Yogurt, and others. No vegan or GF labelling confirmed

restaurant.name: Tanlu Grill
restaurant.desc: Tanlu Grill is a Northeastern Chinese charcoal BBQ restaurant located in Richmond's Garden City area, carrying on generations-old grilling traditions centred on quality meats cooked tableside over live charcoal. The concept draws on a heritage spanning both China and the diaspora, positioning itself as a social fine-dining experience with sizzling grilled meats and cold beer. A touring cyclist heading to or from Richmond can expect a sit-down dinner destination with a distinctly immersive atmosphere.

detail.address: Unit 1430, 4771 McClelland Road, Richmond, BC V6X 0M5

restaurant.name: Sushi Mori
restaurant.desc: Langley Sushi Mori is a Japanese fusion restaurant located in a Langley shopping centre, part of a small chain that opened its first location in Coquitlam in 2010. The kitchen emphasizes fresh ingredients and an exclusive house-made sauce crafted from fruits and vegetables, served in a vintage interior featuring natural stone and wood elements meant to evoke a forest setting. Touring cyclists can stop in for dine-in or takeout, with third-party delivery also available.

restaurant.name: Functional Pi Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Functional Pi Pizzeria is a Whistler pizza shop blending East Coast inspiration — classic New York-style slices and Detroit-style pan crust — made with house-prepared dough and premium imported ingredients. The menu offers a range of creative specialty pies alongside a fully customizable build-your-own option. Touring cyclists can stop in for a filling dine-in meal or grab a takeout order to fuel up on the road.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'PICKUP ONLY' in the header and 'dine-in or take-out' in the body copy

restaurant.name: Hugo's Mexican Kitchen

Everything is made from scratch, including house-made corn tortillas, using local and fresh ingredients. The Vedder Road location is one of several across the Fraser Valley and beyond, with a menu designed to accommodate a wide range of dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Our menus offer plenty of vegan, vegetarian, dairy and gluten free dishes to satisfy a range of dietary needs and restrictions.'

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: A 24-hour Subway franchise located in Burnaby on Hastings Street, offering customizable Footlong and 6-inch sandwiches, wraps, and salads with fresh-cut vegetables and freshly baked bread. The location features both indoor and outdoor seating and accepts multiple payment methods including major credit cards. Its round-the-clock hours make it a potential stop for cyclists at any time of day.

restaurant.name: Dae-ji
restaurant.desc: Dae-ji is a Korean restaurant located in North Vancouver at The High Street. It offers sit-down dining for touring cyclists and other visitors. The restaurant is situated in a commercial shopping district.

detail.address: 1153 The High Street, Unit 128, North Vancouver, BC V3B 0B7

restaurant.name: Triple O's
restaurant.desc: Triple O's is a BC-born quick-service burger chain with 70+ locations, known for its secret Triple 'O' sauce, hand-scooped milkshakes, and Kennebec fries. This Kelowna outpost is co-located inside a Chevron gas station on Adams Road, making it a natural stop for cyclists already pulling in for fuel. The menu spans breakfast through dinner, with burgers, sides, and kids' options.

restaurant.name: The Teahouse at Abkhazi Garden
restaurant.desc: The Teahouse at Abkhazi Garden occupies a heritage house set within the historic Abkhazi Garden in Victoria's Fairfield neighbourhood, a landscape created by Princess Peggy Abkhazi and celebrated for its rare plants and naturalistic design. The teahouse offers multi-course high teas and seasonal lunches built around regional and garden-grown produce, with Silk Road loose leaf teas as the centrepiece. It is a well-known Victoria destination for a leisurely midday sit-down, and guided garden tours can be arranged on site.

restaurant.name: Macchiato Caffe
restaurant.desc: Macchiato Caffe is a locally owned Italian-inspired cafe with two locations in downtown Victoria, serving premium Caffe Umbria espresso alongside freshly made panini, salads, and baked goods — all prepared onsite daily. After nearly two decades in Victoria, it has become a neighbourhood institution drawing on ingredients sourced through its Italian deli supplier, Italian Food Imports. Both locations offer comfortable indoor seating and outdoor patio space, making it a welcoming mid-ride stop in the heart of downtown.

restaurant.name: The Haney Public House
restaurant.desc: Originally The Haney Public House, this Maple Ridge venue has rebranded as SPURS Country Bar, a community-focused country bar featuring live music, line-dancing nights, and comfort food. It operates as a lively nightlife destination on Lougheed Highway in the heart of Maple Ridge. A touring cyclist rolling through town on a weekend evening would find cold drinks, hearty food, and a welcoming local crowd.

detail.address: 22222 Lougheed Hwy., Maple Ridge, BC V2K 2T2

restaurant.name: Rockit Coffee Co.
restaurant.desc: Rockit Coffee Co. is a retro-themed independent café nestled in Whistler's Creekside Village, just steps from the Creekside Gondola. It leans into a groovy mid-century aesthetic with a food and drink menu, branded merchandise, and an online ordering option. Its location at the base of Whistler Creekside makes it a natural stop for cyclists heading into or out of the mountains.

detail.address: 227-2063 Lake Placid Road, Whistler BC, Canada V8E 0B6

restaurant.name: Basil Garden Pho
restaurant.desc: Basil Garden Pho is a family-run Vietnamese restaurant on East Broadway in Vancouver, known for its pho broth simmered for over 18 hours using fresh, carefully chosen ingredients. The menu ranges from classic beef and pork bone noodle soups to appetizers, rice dishes, and salad bowls, with vegetarian options available. It offers a relaxed, home-cooked atmosphere that would suit a cyclist looking for a filling, authentic meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Vegetarian Spring Rolls (item 3, rice paper with vegetarian stuffing) and Veggie Pho with vegetarian broth (item 24)

restaurant.name: Persimmon Tree
restaurant.desc: Persimmon Tree is a Korean restaurant located in Victoria, BC, tagged in OpenStreetMap as serving Korean cuisine. Beyond its cuisine style, no further details about the establishment — its setting, specialties, or cyclist-friendly features — could be confirmed due to inaccessible web content.

restaurant.name: L'OTUS Cake Boutique
restaurant.desc: L'OTUS Cake Boutique is a Richmond cake shop operating primarily as an online-order and pickup business through Square. Customers place orders in advance and collect custom cakes from the unit at 8580 Cambie Road. It offers a sweet stop for cyclists passing through the Cambie Road corridor in Richmond.

restaurant.name: Kamo Bakery
restaurant.desc: Kamo Bakery is a family-run Middle Eastern bakery on Victoria Drive in East Vancouver with over thirty years of baking experience. It specialises in daily-baked Tandoori bread (NAN), Samoon sandwich bread, and traditional pastries such as baklava, kleicha, and labzina — items it claims to be the only bakery in Vancouver producing. All products are described as handmade, and the shop donates unsold goods to local non-profit organisations supporting low-income families.

restaurant.name: KnChicken
restaurant.desc: KnChicken is a Korean restaurant in Burnaby specializing in deep-fried chicken offered in multiple sauces — including sweet spicy, spicy garlic, volcano, and butter garlic — alongside tteokbokki, the popular Korean rice cake dish. The dining room is intentionally small and intimate, making it a cozy stop for a sit-down meal or a quick pick-up order after a ride along Canada Way. The menu also includes rice bowls combining fried chicken with teri-mayo sauce, offering a filling option for hungry cyclists.

restaurant.name: Brock House Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Brock House Restaurant is a sit-down dining establishment located on Point Grey Road in Vancouver, a route well-travelled by cyclists following the waterfront corridor between downtown and UBC. The address places it directly along one of the city's most popular recreational cycling routes, making it a natural rest stop for touring and recreational riders alike.

restaurant.name: Romeo's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Romeo's is a family-owned Italian restaurant that has been serving Victoria since 1974, now operating four locations across Vancouver Island. The Broadmead Village location sits in a shopping plaza off Royal Oak Drive and offers a broad menu of handcrafted pizzas, pastas, burgers, and salads with dine-in, takeout, and delivery options. With over 50 years as a community staple and a reputation as one of the island's most-voted best pizza spots, it's a well-established stop for a sit-down meal.

detail.address: 777 Royal Oak Drive, Victoria, BC V8X 4V1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ on website states: 'Do You Have Vegetarian Options? Yes, we offer a variety of options' (text truncated but affirmative)

restaurant.name: Deepwater Micro Eatery
restaurant.desc: Deepwater Micro Eatery is a casual North Vancouver restaurant focused on Pacific seafood, offering fish & chips with wild BC cod, halibut, and salmon alongside a broad taco and burger menu. It has both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a comfortable stop in any weather. A solid selection of canned craft beer, cider, and wine rounds out the offering for cyclists looking to refuel after a ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple gluten-free items explicitly labelled (all taco varieties marked 'gluten-free, dairy free'). Vegetarian options include Veggie Tacos and Black Bean Brown Rice Burger

restaurant.name: Dami Sushi
restaurant.desc: Dami Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Nanaimo specializing in sushi and Japanese cuisine. It provides both dine-in and takeout service, making it convenient for touring cyclists passing through. The air-conditioned interior and available washrooms make it a comfortable stop.

restaurant.name: The Patio at SpearHead Winery
restaurant.desc: SpearHead Winery is an award-winning Okanagan estate winery recognized as the 2024 Best Performing Winery and Winery of the Year, known for its single-vineyard Pinot Noir program led by winemaker Grant Stanley. The OSM record specifically captures the winery's outdoor patio, which forms part of the tasting room experience at their Spiers Road property. Touring cyclists passing through the South Kelowna wine corridor can stop here for a wine tasting in a vineyard setting.

restaurant.name: Cactus Club Cafe
restaurant.desc: Cactus Club Cafe's Bentall 5 location is a polished downtown Vancouver outpost of a well-established BC chain, offering chef-driven international cuisine in an upbeat, stylish room. The restaurant features both indoor and patio seating and operates a full pickup and delivery service. As a high-traffic anchor in the Burrard Street office and retail corridor, it draws a broad mix of business and leisure diners.

restaurant.name: Killer Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Killer Ice Cream is a Kitsilano shop serving real fruit ice cream, frozen yogurt, and vegan ice cream alongside espresso drinks and premium snacks. It accepts Bitcoin on-chain and Lightning Network payments, an unusual feature for a neighbourhood ice cream counter. The shop has an events program and delivery option in addition to walk-in service.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'vegan ice cream' as a core offering

restaurant.name: Float30
restaurant.desc: Float30 is a seafood and fish-and-chips restaurant situated at Reed Point Marina in Port Moody, offering panoramic waterfront views. The kitchen serves fresh daily seafood alongside a full scratch breakfast menu, making it a substantial meal stop on the Inlet waterfront route. A covered, heated patio lets cyclists eat outside in variable west-coast weather.

detail.address: Reed Point Way, Port Moody, BC V3H 3R5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items offer vegetarian substitutions explicitly, e.g. 'Make it Veggie by Substituting Avocado instead of Bacon' on the Sunrise Breakfast Sandwich, Chorizo Grilled Cheese, and Classic Ham Eggs Benedict

restaurant.name: Rogue Kitchen & Wetbar
restaurant.desc: Rogue Kitchen & Wetbar is a full-service restaurant and bar anchored in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, offering a broad West Coast-inspired menu alongside an extensive cocktail list and live tap selection. The venue has both indoor and outdoor seating and runs a daily happy hour, making it a potential mid-ride or post-ride stop for cyclists exploring the waterfront area. Online ordering with curbside pickup is available, which suits cyclists who prefer a quick grab-and-go.

detail.address: 601 West Cordova Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 1G1

restaurant.name: Chieftain Pool & Pinball

The bar's game-focused atmosphere sets it apart from typical pubs in the area.

restaurant.name: HUB Co. Brewing
restaurant.desc: HUB Co. Brewing is a craft brewery with an expansive tasting room situated on the historic North Railway Avenue in downtown Mission, BC. The venue pours its own house-brewed beers alongside a food menu, and regularly hosts community events including trivia nights, gaming evenings, and creative workshops. Cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley corridor will find it a lively local gathering spot with a distinctly neighbourhood feel.

restaurant.name: Tamaly Shop
restaurant.desc: Tamaly Shop is a Vancouver Mexican tamale specialty shop on Main Street, crafting authentic corn husk-wrapped tamales from 100% natural ingredients with both traditional and signature fillings. The menu spans savoury options (chicken mole, pork with salsa verde), dessert tamales (chocolate, pineapple, blackberry with cream cheese), and dedicated vegan varieties, alongside tortas, sides, and aguas frescas. Tamales were historically designed as portable, energy-dense trail food, making this a naturally fitting stop for a hungry cyclist.

restaurant.name: Antico Pizza Napoletana
restaurant.desc: Antico Pizza Napoletana is a family-owned Neapolitan pizzeria officially certified by the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana in Naples and ranked #1 in Kelowna and British Columbia, with a top-50 North America ranking from Top 50 Italy. Every pizza is handmade from naturally leavened dough and baked in a wood-fired oven custom-built in Naples using imported Italian ingredients including San Marzano tomatoes and Mozzarella di Bufala. The restaurant sits in downtown Kelowna with a patio one block from Okanagan Lake, placing it directly on a natural cycling route through the Okanagan.

restaurant.name: Wahaha Tea

restaurant.name: Fresh Bite Food
restaurant.desc: Fresh Bite Food is a kebab and sandwich counter that opened its first location in 2024, backed by over a decade of culinary experience. The menu centres on grilled koobideh and chicken kebab sandwiches as well as Philly-style cheese steaks, all served in fresh pitta bread with a generous spread of toppings. A vegetarian chickpea-and-kidney-bean sandwich rounds out the menu, making it a handy refuelling stop for cyclists riding through Port Coquitlam.

restaurant.name: The London Fish
restaurant.desc: The London Fish is a fish-and-chips restaurant on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most bike-friendly and pedestrian-oriented streets. Touring cyclists on the Commercial Drive corridor will find indoor seating available.

restaurant.name: IKEA Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The IKEA Restaurant is a Swedish cafeteria-style eatery on the second floor of IKEA Richmond, one of the busiest IKEA locations in Western Canada. It serves Swedish staples including breakfast, and is a rare opportunity for touring cyclists to refuel with a full sit-down meal in a large, climate-controlled setting. The store is currently undergoing an expansion, signalling continued investment in the Richmond location.

restaurant.name: Phonomenal
restaurant.desc: Phonomenal Vietnamese Café is an authentic pho restaurant that has been serving Greater Victoria since November 2011, located in Shelbourne Village Square at the intersection of Cedar Hill Cross Rd. and Shelbourne St. The menu spans appetizers, large-format pho, grilled sandwiches, rice dishes, and vermicelli, with a signature 'jumble size' pho that the kitchen describes as a standout. Its location within walking distance of the University of Victoria and near Camosun College makes it a natural refuelling stop along the Shelbourne corridor.

restaurant.name: Monaco Cafe

The about-us page highlights it as a neighborhood gathering place with vegan, dairy-free, and gluten-free options woven throughout the menu.

restaurant.name: Fluffle Cafe

restaurant.name: Sandy's Bake Shoppe
restaurant.desc: Sandy's Bake Shoppe is a scratch bakery and café founded in 2018 by co-owners Sandy Bryhn and Adam Townsend, who bring over 16 years of combined culinary experience on BC's Sunshine Coast. The shop produces a full range of traditional baked goods — breads, pastries, tarts, cakes — alongside savory lunch items including soups, wraps, and sandwiches made on their own house-baked breads. Special orders and catering, including wedding cakes, are available by arrangement.

restaurant.name: Pho 37
restaurant.desc: Pho 37 is an award-winning Vietnamese restaurant chain with its Commercial Drive location sitting on one of Vancouver's most bike-friendly corridors. The restaurant serves authentic, scratch-made pho, vermicelli bowls, and a broad menu of Vietnamese appetizers and mains — all prepared fresh daily with MSG-free ingredients. Past accolades include the Canadian Choice Award for Vietnamese Restaurant and recognition on Yelp Elites' Top Places to Eat.

restaurant.name: Main Street Cafe
restaurant.desc: Main Street Cafe is a downtown Revelstoke institution operating since 2003 in a beautifully converted heritage house, celebrated for creative eggs benedict variations, quality espresso, and an extensive all-day breakfast and lunch menu. It has earned coverage from Forbes, Transworld Snowboarding, and international travel guides, and draws a loyal local crowd as much as passing visitors. A sunny street-side patio makes it a natural and welcoming stop for anyone arriving in Revelstoke by bike.

restaurant.name: Shamrock Storehouse
restaurant.desc: Shamrock Storehouse is an Irish pub chain founded in 2024 by William and Laura Donnellan, immigrants from Co. Galway, Ireland, who built the brand around authentic Irish hospitality. The Granville location at 678 Nelson St. is one of three active Vancouver spots, offering live music, hearty Irish food, and properly poured Guinness in a cozy neighbourhood atmosphere. A fourth Stadium District location is listed as coming soon, signalling the brand's rapid local expansion.

restaurant.name: Burrata Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Burrata Pizzeria is a Kerrisdale neighbourhood pizzeria focused on delivering what it calls the most authentic Italian pizza to Vancouver's West Side. The restaurant offers both takeout and delivery, as well as event catering for corporate and private functions. It sits on West 41st Avenue, a key east-west cycling corridor on the south side of Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Carbone Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Carbone Pizzeria is a Nanaimo Italian restaurant specializing in traditional and American-style pizzas and pasta, helmed by a chef with over 30 years of fine dining experience. The kitchen sources fresh ingredients from local farmers' markets and uses imported DOP Italian cheeses alongside housemade pastas, clay-oven dishes, and a full antipasto selection. Originally a takeout-only East Coast pizzeria concept, the restaurant expanded to dine-in service in fall 2025.

restaurant.name: Golden Chopsticks

restaurant.name: The Pawn Shop
restaurant.desc: The Pawn Shop YVR is an East L.A.-inspired taco and tequila bar on Vancouver's Granville Street, featuring hand-painted graffiti walls, cozy bench seating, and an open-concept kitchen. The menu spans tacos, burritos, rice bowls, and handcrafted tequila cocktails, with multiple vegetarian and gluten-free items clearly marked throughout. A touring cyclist arriving in Vancouver's entertainment district will find a lively full-service sit-down meal with delivery options also available.

restaurant.name: LIFT Bar Grill View
restaurant.desc: LIFT Bar Grill View is an upscale waterfront restaurant in Vancouver's Coal Harbour, known for panoramic views of the harbour, Stanley Park, and the North Shore mountains from what the restaurant describes as the city's only waterfront rooftop deck. The kitchen centres on regionally sourced West Coast cuisine — sustainable Pacific seafood, locally grown produce — paired with an award-winning BC and Pacific Northwest wine list. The multi-level space features floor-to-ceiling windows that open in summer and outdoor fire features, making it a well-established landmark dining destination.

restaurant.name: Chef Hung Taiwanese Beef Noodle
restaurant.desc: Chef Hung Taiwanese Beef Noodle is the North American flagship of an international chain founded by a three-time champion of the Taipei International Beef Noodle Festival Competition (2007–2010). The restaurant serves traditional Taiwanese beef noodle soup made with premium beef cuts and noodles imported from Taiwan, developed through the founder's 20 years of culinary research. It sits in Richmond's dense Asian food district, offering touring cyclists a distinctive regional dining experience.

restaurant.name: The Duke Saloon
restaurant.desc: The Duke Saloon is Victoria's premiere country music venue, established in 2014 inside a heritage brick building originally constructed in 1902 to house BC Electric Company streetcars. Every night it opens, a live band performs on The Jim Beam Stage, making it a lively stop for cyclists looking to catch some authentic country music after a day on the road. The venue is 19+ and is a proud member of the BarWatch Program.

restaurant.name: Pizza 64
restaurant.desc: Pizza 64 is a BC pizza chain with a Pitt Meadows location along McMyn Road, offering both takeout and delivery. The restaurant is a franchise operation with a loyalty rewards program, making it a reliable stop in the Pitt Meadows area for a quick, filling meal. Touring cyclists passing through this suburban community will find it a convenient refuel option.

restaurant.name: Ramen Danbo
restaurant.desc: Ramen Danbo is a Japanese chain rooted in Fukuoka-style Tonkotsu ramen, with its Kitsilano location on West 4th Avenue being one of the brand's very first restaurants outside Japan. Diners can deeply customize their bowl — choosing noodle thickness, broth richness, and spice level — from both a regular and a dedicated vegan menu. Sitting in one of Vancouver's most cycling-friendly neighbourhoods, it's a popular refuelling stop along the busy West 4th corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated 'Vegan Menu' listed on the Vancouver menu page

restaurant.name: Cowpuccino's Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Cowpuccino's Coffee House is a cafe in Prince Rupert, BC, on Cow Bay Road. It serves as a rest and refreshment stop for cyclists and travelers in this northern coastal community.

restaurant.name: Orange Julius
restaurant.desc: Orange Julius is a juice and fast food establishment offering takeaway service. The location provides a convenient stop for cyclists seeking quick refreshments while traveling through Fort St. John.

restaurant.name: Arc

The restaurant's curved space frames sweeping views of Vancouver Harbour and the North Shore mountains, making it a standout waterfront dining experience. Its location at Canada Place puts cyclists directly on the seawall, and offerings span breakfast through late-night lounge service.

restaurant.name: Jam Cafe
restaurant.desc: Jam Cafe is a beloved breakfast and brunch institution that opened in Victoria's historic Old Town in 2012 and has since expanded to multiple BC locations. A popular neighbourhood gathering spot, it is a well-regarded fuel stop for cyclists exploring Victoria's downtown core.

restaurant.name: Ajiya Sushi
restaurant.desc: Ajiya Sushi is a Japanese restaurant situated on West 4th Avenue in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, a street that serves as a major cycling corridor with dedicated infrastructure. The restaurant offers both dine-in and takeout, making it a practical stop for cyclists passing through the area. Its location on one of the city's busiest cycling routes gives it natural appeal as a mid-ride or end-of-ride meal option.

restaurant.name: The Old Spaghetti Factory
restaurant.desc: The Old Spaghetti Factory is a Canadian chain restaurant anchoring a corner of Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, operating out of one of its earliest Canadian locations. It offers a distinctive 'It's all included' dining model where every entrée arrives with sourdough bread, soup or salad, spumoni ice cream, and coffee — a filling proposition after a long ride. The Gastown location carries a well-known local reputation for being haunted, lending extra atmosphere to the Victorian-era surroundings.

restaurant.name: Umami Sushi
restaurant.desc: Umami Sushi is a casual Japanese sushi restaurant in Langley offering online ordering and takeout service. It operates seven days a week with consistent lunch and dinner hours, providing a convenient food stop for cycling tourists passing through the area. The restaurant serves the local community as a traditional sit-down establishment.

restaurant.name: Sushi Bar Nagomi
restaurant.desc: Sushi Bar Nagomi is an authentic Japanese sushi restaurant on BC's Sunshine Coast, opened in 2008 by Tokyo-trained chef Hiro Funaki who settled in Gibsons for its natural beauty and community spirit. The restaurant occupies the ground floor of a beloved 1945 heritage building known locally as 'The Pink House' in Gibsons Landing, with an interior influenced by Japanese architectural sensibility. The menu emphasizes freshness and technique — from hand-prepared sushi rice to in-house fish preparation — alongside a curated selection of premium sake.

restaurant.name: Menya Raizo
restaurant.desc: Menya Raizo is a Japanese ramen izakaya on West Broadway in Vancouver, part of the Zakkushi Group which has operated in the city for over 20 years. The restaurant handcrafts its soup, noodles, and cha-shu daily in a central kitchen, and the interior evokes a nostalgic Japanese ramen-ya atmosphere with tin roof, orange bulbs, and lanterns. Touring cyclists can stop in for a hearty bowl of authentic ramen or grab a takeout order on the go.

restaurant.name: Grit Studio
restaurant.desc: Grit Studio is an independent café in Port Moody offering specialty coffee and tea alongside a rotating selection of pastries, savoury snacks, and sandwiches. It operates Wednesday through Monday and maintains an active presence on Instagram and Facebook where it posts news, events, and specials. The café's small, community-focused character makes it a welcoming stop for cyclists passing through the Port Moody area.

restaurant.name: Triple O's
restaurant.desc: Triple O's is the quick-service burger concept under the White Spot family, BC's longest-running restaurant chain operating since 1928. Located on Kingsway in Vancouver, this location features a drive-through and outdoor seating. Cyclists passing through the Burnaby-Vancouver corridor on Kingsway will find it a convenient stop for burgers and BC-sourced ingredients.

restaurant.name: Nest at the Lake
restaurant.desc: Nest at the Lake is a coffee shop cafe located at 121 Presley Place in the western communities of Greater Victoria. The name suggests proximity to a lake, which could make it a pleasant stop for cyclists exploring trails in the Langford or Colwood area. Beyond its cafe designation, no further details about the business are available from verifiable sources.

restaurant.name: Mei Le Bakery & Restaurant Inc.
restaurant.desc: Mei Le Bakery & Restaurant is a Chinese dim sum restaurant and bakery in Coquitlam, serving daily from morning through evening. The menu reflects traditional dim sum offerings alongside bakery items, making it a solid stop for cyclists looking for a hearty sit-down meal. Its location in a commercial unit on Schoolhouse Street puts it within reach of Coquitlam's cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Goldie's Donuts & Bakery
restaurant.desc: Goldie's is a gourmet donut and bakery chain with a Kitsilano outpost on West 4th Avenue, celebrated for its 24-hour slow-fermented brioche donuts using a Korean-inspired technique that produces unusually light and fluffy results. The menu spans creative flavours like Mango Passion Fruit Glaze and Matcha Cream alongside signature specialty drinks such as a Peanut Butter Cream Latte. It is a multi-location BC chain that has been featured in DailyHive, Vancouver Is Awesome, and the North Shore News.

restaurant.name: Village Sushi
restaurant.desc: Village Sushi is a small sushi bar in Richmond with a capacity of around 14 seats, situated on Number 2 Road near Richmond's well-developed cycling network. It offers takeout service, making it a potential quick stop for cyclists riding the nearby dyke and greenway trails. The compact, neighbourhood-scale setting is typical of Richmond's local dining spots.

restaurant.name: Paramjit's Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Paramjit's Kitchen is an Indian restaurant serving Revelstoke from 1st Street West, offering both dine-in and takeout options. It provides a meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the community.

restaurant.name: Holy Guacamole
restaurant.desc: Holy Guacamole is an authentic Mexican restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, co-founded by Miguel Villalobos Luna and Indalecio Xicohtencatl-Lara, both of whom bring decades of culinary experience from Mexico. The menu spans tacos, pozole, birria, chimichangas, quesadillas, and enchiladas, with vegetarian and vegan options woven throughout. Its location near Stanley Park and the Seawall makes it a natural stop on one of Vancouver's most popular cycling corridors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists 'Veggie' as a filling option across tacos, quesadillas, burritos, chimichangas, and enchiladas. Special 3 Tacos includes beyond meat, jackfruit, and tofu, with the note '*The vegan option comes with guacamole on the side.' Chile Relleno is explicitly labelled (VEGGIE). No GF mention found

restaurant.name: Sing Yee Chinese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Founded in 2010 in Richmond, BC, Sing Yee Chinese Restaurant is a well-regarded Cantonese dining destination led by Master Chef Tony, who brings over 30 years of culinary experience from acclaimed Chinese restaurants and culinary groups. The kitchen specialises in traditional hand-crafted dishes such as Crispy Squab, Eight Treasure Duck, and Double Boiled Winter Melon Soup, alongside a Chiuzhou-style supper menu and advance-order specialties like Fotiaoqiang and snake soup. Cyclists seeking authentic Cantonese cuisine in Richmond can dine in or order takeout online or by phone.

restaurant.name: Ophelia
restaurant.desc: Ophelia is a Michelin Guide–recommended Mexican restaurant in Vancouver's Olympic Village, helmed by Chef Francisco Higareda and named in honour of his mother. The kitchen takes an elevated approach to authentic regional Mexican cooking, from house-made moles and quesabirria tacos to corn-crusted octopus, supported by a fully licensed bar stocked with premium tequilas and mezcals. Its location in the heart of Olympic Village places it directly on one of Vancouver's most-cycled urban corridors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'TACOS VEGAN' (guajillo marinated portobello mushroom, spicy almond sauce) on both dine-in and pickup menus; enchiladas note a mushroom substitute option

restaurant.name: Greens & Beans Deli
restaurant.desc: A family-owned deli operating in the historic Sapperton neighbourhood of New Westminster since 1994, serving soups, sandwiches, and salads made from fresh local produce. The business donates all tips to local charities for eleven months of each year and has hosted actor Larry Thomas ('The Soup Nazi' from Seinfeld) for in-store appearances. In addition to the restaurant, Greens & Beans runs a mobile lunch truck serving business parks across the region.

detail.address: 143 East Columbia Street, New Westminster, BC V3L 3V9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Restaurant menu lists 'Veggie' and 'Veggie Avocado' sandwiches and 'Veggie Cream Cheese' wedge sandwich; truck menu includes vegetarian wrap options

restaurant.name: The Rose Neighbourhood Public House
restaurant.desc: The Rose Neighbourhood Public House occupies a converted 1925 heritage home in Colwood that has anchored the Westshore community as a pub under various names since 1985. The current owners relaunched it in 2018 with house-crafted cocktails, cold draught, and hearty pub fare including house-smoked fish chowder and hand-cut fries. A backyard garden provides extra outdoor seating, giving the place an inviting stop-and-stay feel for anyone passing through the Westshore.

notes.Takeout: Menu page states food is 'Available during our operational hours, for in-room dining & take out (pick up only)'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly offers 'substitute gluten free bun on any burger or sandwich'; several salad and vegetable-forward dishes are listed, but no explicit vegan labeling appears

restaurant.name: Cosmos Greek Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Cosmos Greek Restaurant has been a White Rock waterfront institution since 1980, serving traditional family-recipe Greek dishes — souvlaki, moussaka, handmade dips, and fresh-baked pita — just steps from the ocean. The restaurant offers one of the area's most-praised patios with direct water views, making it a natural stop on the White Rock seafront cycling route. With over five decades of community presence and 1,200+ reviews, it functions as a local gathering place as much as a restaurant.

restaurant.name: Mount Currie Coffee Co
restaurant.desc: Mount Currie Coffee Co is a specialty coffee shop in the heart of Whistler Village, serving premium Gradient Coffee roasted fresh in nearby Pemberton. The café is a known supporter of both WORCA and PORCA — Whistler and Pemberton's off-road cycling associations — co-sponsoring annual events and acting as a community hub for the mountain bike scene. Grab-and-go service and a call-ahead ordering option make it a practical fuel stop for cyclists moving through the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

restaurant.name: Domino's
restaurant.desc: Domino's Pizza is a national chain franchise located in a Langley strip-mall unit offering pizza delivery and carryout. The menu covers classic and specialty pizzas, cheesy breads, chicken, pastas, and soft drinks. Cyclists passing through can order carryout but will find limited on-site amenities.

restaurant.name: COCO Cafe
restaurant.desc: COCO Cafe is a mission-driven community cafe in the rural Cedar area, operated by Cedar Opportunities BC Society, a registered charity that provides supported employment and training for adults with developmental disabilities. The cafe serves a made-from-scratch breakfast and lunch menu featuring eggs benedict, breakfast bowls, waffles, and handhelds alongside coffee and beverages. Touring cyclists will find a warm, inclusive community hub with outdoor seating and online takeout ordering available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Vegetarian Eggs Benedict' (poached eggs, roasted red peppers, tomato, avocado, hollandaise) as a named menu item

restaurant.name: Park Drive
restaurant.desc: Park Drive is a bar and restaurant on Commercial Drive in Vancouver that also operates The Gemm, a cocktail lounge on the same premises. The menu ranges from craft cocktails and local draft beer to eclectic pub fare including Detroit-style pizza and bao buns. It sits on one of Vancouver's busiest and most cycle-traveled urban streets.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes VEGI pizza (tomato sauce, spinach, gem tomatoes, mozzarella, parmigiano, feta), Wild Mushroom Toast, Blistered Shishito Peppers, Corn Ribs, Grilled Halloumi Skewers, House Salad, and Kale Caesar Salad

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: A Subway franchise on Summit Drive in Kamloops serving made-to-order sandwiches, wraps, and salads with fresh-baked bread and fresh-cut vegetables. The location supports in-restaurant dining, pickup, delivery, and curbside pickup, and also offers breakfast. Like all Subway locations, it is independently owned and operated.

detail.address: 1203 A Summit Dr, Kamloops, BC V2C 6C5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Subway's standard menu includes vegetarian sub options

restaurant.name: Loon Fong Hotpot
restaurant.desc: Loon Fong Hotpot is an authentic Hong Kong-style hotpot restaurant in Richmond, BC, part of a small multi-location chain with outposts in Ontario. Diners cook fresh ingredients in flavourful broths tableside, following traditional Hong Kong recipes. It is located in a commercial plaza on busy Number 3 Road, a major cycling corridor in Richmond.

restaurant.name: Christina Lake Marina & Grill
restaurant.desc: Christina Lake Marina is the premier marina on Christina Lake, a 20-kilometre lake known for the warmest tree-lined lake water in Western Canada. The waterfront Marina Bistro offers a family-friendly patio atmosphere with games and fishing off the wharves, making it a welcoming stop after a ride. The marina store also stocks sundries, clothing, and watersports equipment.

restaurant.name: Ingrain
restaurant.desc: InGrain Pastificio is a craft pasta manufacturer in Deep Cove that makes slow-dried, bronze-extruded pasta from BC-grown grains — durum, einkorn, emmer, spelt — and Seymour Lake alpine water filtered through a five-stage reverse-osmosis system, following traditional Gragnano IGP methods. The Deep Cove retail shop is the production outlet for what the company bills as a distinctly Canadian pasta story, with products also stocked at dozens of grocery stores across the province. For a cyclist rolling into Deep Cove, it is an artisan specialty shop rather than a place to sit down and refuel.

detail.address: 126 - 1133 Mt. Seymour Rd, Deep Cove, BC

restaurant.name: Denny's
restaurant.desc: Denny's is a well-established Canadian chain diner serving all-day breakfast, burgers, and comfort-food dinners from an extensive menu. The Coquitlam location on Austin Avenue is a dependable, high-capacity refuelling stop for touring cyclists passing through the Tri-Cities corridor. Takeout and delivery are available for those who prefer to eat on the move.

restaurant.name: Bubble Waffle Cafe
restaurant.desc: Bubble Waffle Cafe is a Hong Kong-style street snack spot specializing in the classic egg waffle alongside curry fish balls, rice noodle rolls, stinky tofu, and a broad fish soup noodle combo with dozens of customizable toppings and noodle types. Located on level -1 of a downtown Vancouver food court (unit FC-04), it offers a dense, flavourful quick stop drawing on Cantonese and broader East Asian street food traditions. A touring cyclist looking for a filling, fast, and affordable Asian-style meal in the heart of Vancouver's downtown will find a wide menu here.

restaurant.name: The Captain's Boil
restaurant.desc: The Captain's Boil is a Cajun-inspired seafood boil chain where diners choose their catch — lobster, king crab, snow crab, Dungeness crab, shrimp, and more — then select a flavour sauce and spice level before digging in hands-first at the table. The menu blends Louisiana-style boil technique with Asian aromatics and proprietary seasonings in a casual, communal dining format. This Richmond location sits in the Capstan Way commercial area and is one of several BC outposts of the Canadian franchise.

restaurant.name: The Columbia Diner
restaurant.desc: The Columbia Diner is a modern roadside-style diner in downtown Kamloops serving all-day breakfast alongside lunch and dinner menus built around smash burgers, fried chicken and waffles, and classic comfort food with a contemporary twist. With wall-to-wall windows overlooking the Kamloops mountain backdrop and a welcoming ethos toward locals and travellers alike, it makes a natural refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the BC Interior. The kitchen also offers takeout and delivery, and the restaurant hosts private events with flexible seating.

restaurant.name: TaoTaoJu
restaurant.desc: Tao's Kitchen is a Chinese restaurant located in the Marpole neighbourhood of Vancouver, in a unit along the busy Granville Street corridor. It offers indoor dining and is positioned on a major arterial cycling route connecting South Vancouver to the city centre, making it a potential stop for cyclists moving through the area.

restaurant.name: Chili House Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Chili House Restaurant is a family-run fusion eatery in Cloverdale (Surrey) with culinary roots tracing four generations across China, India, and Sweden before the family settled in British Columbia in 2000. The kitchen serves a distinctive blend of Indian-style Chinese dishes — from pakoras and chicken kabab to Manchurian and Szechuan preparations — with boldly adjustable spice levels. Gluten-free modifications are available on most dishes, and the menu spans an extensive range of appetizers, soups, and mains.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes vegetable spring rolls, House Style Spicy Crispy Tofu, vegetable dumplings, vegetable soups, and other vegetarian dishes; about page states 'it is also possible to alter most of our dishes to be gluten free'

restaurant.name: Akari Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Akari is a Japanese restaurant in Delta's Scott 72 Centre that has been serving fine Japanese cuisine since 1996 and is consistently voted best Japanese restaurant in the neighbourhood. The menu spans sushi and rolls, tempura prepared by a 20-year tempura master, rice and noodle dishes, and a dedicated vegetarian section. Online ordering for pickup and delivery is available, and the restaurant also handles catering and private events.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists a dedicated 'vegetarian' menu category alongside standard menu sections

restaurant.name: Off the Hook
restaurant.desc: Off the Hook is a neighbourhood coastal-inspired restaurant on Salt Spring Island's Fernwood Road, situated near Walker's Hook, brought to life by a couple with two decades of shared food adventures around the world. The menu centres on seafood boils, crudos, ceviche, sushi (when a sushi chef is available), smashburgers, and craft cocktails, with a rotating series of globally themed pop-up dinners running in the off-season. The restaurant revived a beloved community space that had closed during the pandemic and has since become a gathering point for both island residents and visitors.

detail.address: 321 Fernwood Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 1C3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly codes multiple items: Steamed Edamame (Vn, GF), Crispy Eggplant (Vn, GFO), Lemon Cream Pasta (Vegetarian, Vegan Option +$3), Penang Coconut Curry (Vegan & GF), Miso Spinach Salad (GF), and several GFO mains

restaurant.name: Tomo Sushi To Go
restaurant.desc: Tomo Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Nanaimo, BC, operating under a name that means 'Friend' in Japanese. The OSM record places it in unit 106, suggesting a strip-mall or commercial-plaza setting typical for casual sushi dining. A touring cyclist passing through Nanaimo may find it a convenient stop for a hot meal, though details about the specific location remain unverified.

restaurant.name: L.A. Chicken
restaurant.desc: A casual fried-chicken restaurant in Richmond offering indoor seating. Useful as a quick refueling stop for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: BackCountry Pizza
restaurant.desc: BackCountry Pizza is a fast-food pizza restaurant located in Whistler, BC. It serves quick meal options for travelers and locals passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Todai Sushi
restaurant.desc: Todai Sushi is a small, 7-table Japanese restaurant in the Delta neighbourhood of the Lower Mainland, offering a broad menu of sushi, rolls, tempura, teriyaki, and noodle dishes rooted in Japanese culinary tradition. The restaurant emphasizes fresh ingredients and a friendly neighbourhood atmosphere, with online ordering available for those who prefer to grab food on the go. A dedicated Vegetarian menu section makes it accessible to a range of dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists a dedicated 'Vegetarian' category among its menu sections

restaurant.name: Sandbar Cafe & Art Gallery
restaurant.desc: Sandbar Cafe & Art Gallery combines food service with a local art gallery in Qualicum Beach. Located on West Island Highway, it serves as a cafe where cyclists can rest and enjoy local art. Wi-Fi is available to customers.

detail.address: 6087 West Island Highway, Qualicum Beach, V9K 2E2

restaurant.name: Bartholomew's Pub
restaurant.desc: Bartholomew's Public House, known locally as Bart's, has been a Victoria institution since 1975 and is located one block from the Inner Harbour with its entrance on Humboldt Street. Reopened under new management in 2020 with a Gastro English Pub direction, it runs 26 rotating craft draught taps and claims the largest gin selection on Vancouver Island. A touring cyclist finishing a day's ride near the Inner Harbour would find a lively, full-service pub serving fresh pub classics alongside a premium drinks program.

restaurant.name: The Lido
restaurant.desc: The Lido is a casual bar in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighborhood that welcomes drop-in patrons with no reservations required or cover charge. It positions itself as a relaxed social gathering space.

restaurant.name: Mangia's Sandwiches
restaurant.desc: Mangia's Sandwiches is a casual Italian-style deli on Granville Street, sister restaurant to Jo's Italian Deli, where meats are sliced to order and bread is delivered fresh daily from a local bakery. The menu spans Italian specialty sandwiches, hot sandwiches, and classic deli options, with several vegetarian choices. The shop also offers catering with sandwich platters, charcuterie boards, and individually packed bagged lunches.

notes.Packed lunches: Catering menu explicitly lists 'BAGGED LUNCHES: individually packed sandwiches and a small side salad' with choice of side salads
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly marks CAPRESE and BREADED EGGPLANT with '(V)' for vegetarian. No vegan or gluten-free labelling found

restaurant.name: Rooftop Surfclub
restaurant.desc: The Rooftop Patio is an open-air seasonal venue perched atop The Sticky Wicket, billed as Vancouver Island's largest pub, at 919 Douglas St in downtown Victoria. It offers an open-air barbeque grill, cocktails, and local beer, along with bookable outdoor volleyball courts. The venue hosts a busy schedule of live music and special events, making it a lively urban stop for cyclists passing through the city centre.

restaurant.name: The Old Bavaria Haus
restaurant.desc: Open since 1967, The Old Bavaria Haus is a nationally acclaimed German restaurant set inside a beautifully restored century-old home in the heart of New Westminster. The restaurant serves authentic Bavarian specialties — schnitzels, beef rouladen, bratwurst, spatzle — paired with German draft beers and wines. It accommodates everything from intimate family dinners to large corporate events and private parties, and also offers delivery through major platforms.

restaurant.name: Crust N Crunch
restaurant.desc: Crust N Crunch is a pizza and donair counter located inside SFU's Academic Quadrangle building (Level 3000) on Burnaby Mountain campus, part of a small Metro Vancouver chain. The menu features pizza by the slice, whole pies, and donair — all prepared with halal ingredients and a wide range of vegetarian options. It is a convenient calorie stop for cyclists climbing Burnaby Mountain or passing through the SFU campus.

detail.address: 8888 University Dr W, Burnaby, BC V5A 1S6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian pizzas marked with 🌿 (e.g., Greek Delight, Pesto Garden, Spinach Feta Delight, Shahi Paneer Delight, Veggie Trio). No vegan or GF options confirmed

restaurant.name: Chau Veggie Express
restaurant.desc: Chau VeggiExpress is a vegan-only fast food restaurant in Vancouver's V6H postal area, offering plant-based quick-service meals. It is tagged in OpenStreetMap as exclusively vegan, making it a notable stop for cyclists seeking fully plant-based fuel. The business also has a catering menu listed on its OSM record.

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: Tim Hortons on Cadboro Bay Road is a Canadian coffee chain institution serving brewed coffee, Timbits, baked goods, breakfast wraps, and soups. This location offers dine-in and takeout but no drive-through, making it a sit-down-friendly stop near the University of Victoria and Cadboro Bay Village. It's a convenient and familiar refuelling point for cyclists navigating Victoria's eastern neighbourhoods.

detail.address: 2000 Cadboro Bay Rd, Victoria, BC V8R 5G5

restaurant.name: Ngon Banh Mi & Tea
restaurant.desc: Ngon is a Vietnamese café on Kingsway specializing in banh mi sandwiches, rice and vermicelli bowls, and an extensive lineup of Vietnamese coffees — from classic drip with condensed milk to signature salted cream and coconut blended variations. The café also carries a full bubble tea and fresh smoothie menu, and a dedicated Halal menu section broadens its appeal. It makes a well-rounded stop for a hearty sandwich and a sweet drink on a longer ride through East Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Vegan Banh Mi (New)' with marinated tofu and shiitake mushroom, 'Vegan Bowl' with tofu and vegan spring roll, and a 'Spring Roll (2pcs) Pork or Vegan' option

restaurant.name: The Chopped Leaf
restaurant.desc: The Chopped Leaf is a proudly Canadian fast-casual chain founded in 2009, now spanning 124+ locations, built around customizable salads, wraps, bowls, and sandwiches meant to feel like comfort food rather than a health chore. This Kamloops location sits at 700 Tranquille Road and offers online ordering and catering in addition to dine-in service. The build-your-own format and vegetarian-forward menu make it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists wanting a fresh, filling, customizable meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu centres on salads, wraps, and bowls with customizable plant-based ingredients

restaurant.name: Four Points Books
restaurant.desc: Four Points Books is a family-owned independent bookstore in downtown Golden, BC, operating out of what was formerly Bacchus Books and Cafe — the in-house Bacchus Café component remains part of the location. It bills itself as a place to browse, discover, and linger, championing Canadian voices and nurturing local culture as part of the Canadian independent bookselling community.

restaurant.name: Bun Cha Ca Hoang Yen
restaurant.desc: Bun Cha Ca Hoang Yen is a Vietnamese noodle-soup restaurant specializing in bún chả cá (fish cake vermicelli), phở, hủ tiếu, and a wide range of traditional appetizers, operating since at least 2012. The restaurant was a finalist for 'Best Vietnamese' in Vancouver in 2018 and announced a move to a larger 3,000 sq ft space with a patio and 150 seats. Touring cyclists would find a full Vietnamese menu with hearty, restorative noodle soups.

restaurant.name: Lucy's Cafe & Bakery
restaurant.desc: Lucy's Cafe & Bakery is an Ethiopian cafe and bakery operating in a small unit on Sixth Avenue, formerly known as 6th Ave Bread & Deli. The shift to Ethiopian cuisine makes it a distinctive cultural dining stop in what appears to be a New Westminster neighbourhood. Indoor seating is available in a no-smoking setting, offering touring cyclists a sit-down rest option.

restaurant.name: Mr Mikes
restaurant.desc: MR MIKES is a Canadian steakhouse casual chain with a Langford, BC location serving premium steaks, burgers, pastas, and shareable appetizers in a relaxed, come-as-you-are atmosphere. Founded in 1960 and revitalized under the 'SteakhouseCasual' concept, it positions itself as a community gathering spot welcoming locals and tourists alike. Touring cyclists will find full dine-in service alongside takeout and delivery options.

detail.address: 985 Whirlaway Crescent, Victoria, British Columbia, V9B 6W6, Canada

restaurant.name: Prairie Donair
restaurant.desc: Prairie Donair is a Canadian fast-food franchise specialising in donairs, shawarma, rice bowls, salads, and poutines, with a strong emphasis on fresh toppings and customisable build-your-own options. The White Rock branch sits on Marine Drive, the waterfront road that is a natural cycling corridor along the south shore of BC. The chain markets itself as a healthier alternative to conventional fast food, offering a wide protein range including beef, chicken, lamb, and falafel.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Falafel Pita (falafel balls, onions, lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, tahini, mozzarella, tzatziki) as a fully plant-based protein option; salads also available

restaurant.name: Cafe Tica
restaurant.desc: Cafe Tica is a restaurant in Vancouver with vegetarian dining options. A non-smoking, air-conditioned space with indoor seating offering a comfortable stop for touring cyclists seeking a sit-down meal.

detail.address: 843 Seymour St, Vancouver, BC V6B 3L4, Canada

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian options available

restaurant.name: Akemi Sushi
restaurant.desc: Akemi Sushi is a long-running Japanese restaurant in Langford's Station Square on Goldstream Avenue, operated by owner Frank since 2006. It offers a broad menu of sushi, sashimi, and cooked Japanese dishes — spanning everything from boat combos to tempura — in a dining room that seats over 100 guests, with a private fireside party room for groups of up to 25. Its position near several bus routes and a large free parking lot makes it an accessible sit-down meal option for cyclists exploring the Western Communities west of Victoria.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian items: Edamame, Vegetable Gyoza, Vegetable Spring Roll, Vegetable Tempura, Yam Tempura, and Gomaae. Vegan and gluten-free not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: The Landing Pub & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Ladner Landing Pub has been a community fixture in Ladner since 1978, rooted in the local farming community and known for its laid-back atmosphere and genuine hospitality. It operates as a sports-focused pub with multiple big-screen TVs, classic pub fare, and cold drinks. A drive-through liquor store operates next door, making it a convenient stop for those wanting to stock up.

detail.address: 5449 Ladner Trunk Rd, Delta, B.C. V4K 1W6, Canada

restaurant.name: Pappa Leo's
restaurant.desc: Pappa Leo's is a locally owned and operated pizza chain founded in 2003 by two brothers in Pitt Meadows, now grown to seven lower mainland locations. The Coquitlam Schoolhouse Street outlet is one of those independently managed franchises, known for scratch-made dough prepared daily and award-winning recipes. Cyclists can order pizza for pickup or delivery, with contactless payment and an environmentally focused packaging policy.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Locations page states: 'We also offer gluten free pizza crust options.'

restaurant.name: Good Sushi
restaurant.desc: Good Sushi is a fully plant-based sushi restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver, offering a 100% vegan menu that sets it apart from conventional sushi spots. Cyclists will find a sit-down dining room with online ordering and in-store pickup as options. The loyalty rewards program is a small perk for repeat visitors passing through the neighbourhood.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states '100% VEGAN PLANT-BASED SUSHI MENU'

restaurant.name: La Pache Pizza
restaurant.desc: La Pache Pizza is a Neapolitan-influenced pizza counter on West Broadway offering a broad menu of Italian-style pies made with fior di latte and fresh toppings. The shop operates primarily as a takeout and online-order business, with a dedicated vegan pizza lineup alongside classic meat and vegetable options. West Broadway is a major cycling corridor in Vancouver, making this a convenient hot-food stop for riders passing through the Fairview and Kitsilano neighbourhoods.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu has dedicated 'Vegan Pizzas' and 'Vegetable Pizzas' sections. No gluten-free option mentioned

restaurant.name: Paramount Chinese Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Paramount Chinese Seafood Restaurant is a Chinese seafood restaurant located on Rupert Street in East Vancouver. Beyond its OSM listing as a full-service restaurant with daily hours, no further details about the dining experience, specialties, or cyclist-specific facilities could be confirmed due to a mismatched website URL.

restaurant.name: Jagga Sweets
restaurant.desc: Jagga Sweets is an Indian vegetarian restaurant and sweet shop located on Scott Road in the Surrey/Delta corridor. It specialises in South Asian cuisine and sweets, making it a potential stop for cyclists seeking vegetarian-friendly food along this busy commuter and touring route.

restaurant.name: everything WINE
restaurant.desc: everything WINE is a BC-based specialty wine and spirits retail chain offering a broad selection of wines organized by varietal, region, and occasion, alongside beer, cider, and spirits. The Chilliwack location at McCallum Road is part of the company's multi-store footprint serving the Fraser Valley. The store stocks a curated range of local BC wines alongside international selections, and offers a wine club and event consultation services.

restaurant.name: Kelly O'Bryan's Neighborhood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kelly O'Bryan's is an Irish-themed family restaurant and pub chain with locations across British Columbia, established in 1988. The Kamloops outpost on Victoria Street offers casual sit-down dining with a full menu, a kids menu, and an extensive wine and liquor selection. The chain is well known for its 'Birthday Tradition,' a free birthday meal program that has cumulatively donated nearly $900,000 to local food banks across BC.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Kids menu page marks items with a 'Gluten Friendly' symbol and instructs customers to 'inform your server of any food sensitivities and allergies'; gluten-friendly options confirmed

restaurant.name: Unwind
restaurant.desc: Unwind is a fast-food establishment serving breakfast and european cuisine in downtown Vancouver. Located on Howe Street with indoor seating, it's a convenient spot for touring cyclists to grab a meal while exploring the city.

restaurant.name: Green Leaf Vietnamese Bistro
restaurant.desc: Green Leaf Vietnamese Bistro is an authentic Vietnamese restaurant operating three locations in British Columbia, with its original Victoria outpost on Douglas Street. The menu spans classic pho noodle soups, fresh salad rolls, vermicelli bowls, and rice plates crafted from fresh, premium ingredients in the tradition of Vietnamese culinary heritage. Cyclists stopping in can choose between a full sit-down dining experience with reservations or convenient online ordering for takeout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'Gluten-Friendly and Veggie Option Available' for spring rolls; dedicated tofu dishes (Deep Fried Tofu) and a vegetable plate (Stir-fried Mixed Vegetables with tofu) appear throughout the menu

restaurant.name: O-Lake Cafe & Bistro
restaurant.desc: O-Lake Cafe & Bistro is a dessert-focused cafe in downtown Kelowna specializing in handcrafted mille crepe cakes and elegant high tea, founded in 2022 by a designer-turned-baker who blends Western pastry technique with lighter Asian-inspired flavors. The cafe uses real seasonal ingredients and prepares each birthday cake fresh on the day of pickup. Private dining for intimate groups of 2–15 is also available, with custom multi-course menus.

restaurant.name: Rasoi Fine Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Rasoi Fine Indian Cuisine is a South Surrey restaurant specializing in authentic Indian cooking since 2008, with chefs who bring over 20 years of experience to dishes prepared entirely from scratch. The menu spans tandoori specialties, curries, biryanis, and a strong selection of vegetarian options, with a liquor menu also available. Dine-in reservations, online ordering, and full catering services make it a viable stop for a sit-down meal on a longer touring route.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes: Cauliflower Tandoori, Paneer Tikka, Aloo Tikki, Gol Gappa, Vegetable Samosa, and Mix Veggie Platter

restaurant.name: Pampanga's Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Pampanga's Cuisine is a Filipino family-owned restaurant that opened in 2018, specializing in authentic Kapampangan dishes including crispy sisig, breakfast silogs, and traditional Filipino desserts. It operates in turo-turo style — pre-cooked dishes displayed buffet-style in food warmers, reflecting the beloved carinderia street-food tradition of the Philippines — alongside an all-day breakfast menu. restaurant.name: Uptown Bistro
