The restaurant has over 10 years of experience and emphasizes fresh, consistently prepared food. Its central location near Stanley Park and the seawall makes it a natural refuelling stop for cyclists in the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'great variety for all diets including vegetarians'; menu explicitly lists Vegetarian Plate, Falafel Plate, Grilled Veggie Wrap, Falafel Wrap, and Falafel w/fries Wrap

restaurant.name: Scott Hill Pizza
restaurant.desc: Fast food pizzeria offering pizza slices and pies with in-person ordering at the counter. No drive-through service. A quick meal stop for cyclists seeking casual dining in the area.

restaurant.name: Sabrosito
restaurant.desc: Sabrosito is a Latin American and Mexican restaurant at 4421 Hastings Street, serving cuisine from that culinary tradition in a neighbourhood setting. The Facebook tag associated with the OSM record references a page named 'donososrestaurant', hinting at a possible prior identity or related business. For a touring cyclist, it represents a stop for hearty, flavourful food along the Hastings corridor.

restaurant.name: L'Authentique Poutine & Burgers
restaurant.desc: A fast-food restaurant specializing in poutine and burgers, located on Wharf Street in Victoria's waterfront district. Offers quick counter-service meals suitable for touring cyclists seeking a fast food stop.

restaurant.name: Chipotle
restaurant.desc: Chipotle is a fast-casual Mexican chain in South Surrey offering fully customizable burritos, bowls, tacos, quesadillas, and salads built from responsibly sourced ingredients with no artificial colors, flavors, or preservatives. The company's 'Food with Integrity' philosophy emphasizes sustainable and humane farming practices across its compact, whole-ingredient menu. Both indoor seating and a patio are available, making it a practical stop for a filling, customizable meal on a longer ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website describes a fully customizable menu with beans, rice, and vegetable toppings

restaurant.name: Pirate Pizza Company
restaurant.desc: Pirate Pizza Company is a seaside pizza restaurant perched on the floating boardwalk at Fisherman's Wharf, one of Victoria's most distinctive waterfront destinations and a short ride from the Inner Harbour pathway. They serve New York-style slices and whole pies using local, organic ingredients alongside locally brewed craft beer and cider, all with a front-row view of seaplanes, sailboats, and harbour wildlife. The surrounding wharf neighbourhood also offers water taxis, kayak rentals, and whale-watching, making it a natural rest stop on a coastal cycling tour.

detail.address: C1-1 Dallas Road, Fisherman's Wharf, Victoria, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About-us page states: 'Gluten Free, Vegan and Dairy Free options available.' Menu also lists gluten-free crust (small only) and dairy-free cheese substitute (Vitalite)

restaurant.name: Open Outcry
restaurant.desc: Open Outcry is an indoor-seating restaurant in Vancouver with a no-smoking policy. Without access to working website content, further details about the restaurant's cuisine and character were unavailable to verify.

restaurant.name: Fife Bakery
restaurant.desc: Fife Bakery is a cozy artisan sourdough and coffee shop located just outside Olympic Village in the Mount Pleasant neighbourhood of Vancouver, open since December 2016. The bakery hand-crafts levain loaves using organic, sustainably grown Canadian grains and slow fermentation, alongside a full specialty coffee menu. A warm, rustic interior designed by award-winning designer Perry Chua makes it a welcoming stop for cyclists passing through East Van.

restaurant.name: Melt Confectionary
restaurant.desc: Melt Confectionary is a queer-owned artisan chocolate and ice cream shop on Vancouver's Main Street, producing small-batch handmade confections that blend nostalgic classics with inventive modern twists. The shop partners with local Vancouver makers and growers to source sustainable ingredients, and all packaging is recyclable or compostable. Cyclists can choose from an extensive menu of dairy and vegan ice cream scoops, dipped bars, and artisan chocolate bars, with online ordering available for chocolates.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated vegan ice cream scoops (Pistachio, Matcha Ginger, Vanilla, Turtles) and vegan chocolate bars explicitly listed; FAQs confirm dairy-free chocolate options including Cookies and Cream, Salted Pretzel, London Fog, Raspberry Dark, Honeycomb. Nut/fruit milk used as dairy substitute

restaurant.name: Gator's Pub
restaurant.desc: Gator's Pub is a bar located in Chilliwack. Touring cyclists can stop for food and drinks in a casual pub setting.

restaurant.name: Saint Franks
restaurant.desc: Saint Franks is a casual hot dog and snackbar restaurant located on Yates Street in downtown Victoria. It offers quick-service meals in a convenient location accessible to local patrons and passing cyclists.

restaurant.name: Ricardo's Ice Cream, Coffee, Bubble Tea
restaurant.desc: Ricardo's is a cafe on White Rock's Marine Drive serving ice cream, coffee, and bubble tea. Marine Drive runs along the waterfront promenade, making this a natural stop for cyclists riding the popular White Rock beachfront route. The multi-item menu covers both refreshment and pick-me-up options in a single stop.

restaurant.name: Ha Cafe
restaurant.desc: Ha Cafe is a Vietnamese restaurant that has been serving Burnaby since 2006, located directly across from Metrotown on Kingsway. It specializes in pho and freshly cooked Vietnamese cuisine, built on a family kitchen tradition of rich broths and herbs. The restaurant offers both a full dine-in experience and a takeout menu including banh mi, rice, vermicelli, and vegetarian dishes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian' section. No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Amsterdam Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Amsterdam Restaurant is a locally owned breakfast and lunch eatery that introduced Dutch pannenkoeken (crêpes) to Kamloops over 20 years ago, carving out a distinctive niche with its European-Canadian fusion menu. The cozy spot is known for its extensive dietary accommodations, including dedicated gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian options, with particular attention to minimising cross-contamination for celiac diners. Takeout is available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through Kamloops.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website has a dedicated section 'Gluten Free Friendly, Vegetarian & Vegan Options' and notes celiac accommodations: 'We will go to the greatest lengths to ensure that the risk of cross contamination is minimized.' Vegan batter, smoked tempeh, vegan cheese, and coconut whipped cream listed as available ingredients

restaurant.name: Song Huong
restaurant.desc: Song Huong is a Vietnamese restaurant in Vancouver offering casual dine-in and takeaway service. Located on Nanaimo Street, it provides a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking for a meal while exploring the area.

restaurant.name: Sushi Go
restaurant.desc: Sushi Go is a casual, family-friendly Japanese restaurant in East Vancouver's Kerr Street neighbourhood, distinguishing itself with an unusually broad menu that spans traditional nigiri and rolls, house-made aburi (torched) oshi sushi, donburi, udon, and full sashimi sets. Reviewers highlight the freshness of the fish and call out the assorted aburi as a standout item. For a touring cyclist stopping in the area, it offers a filling sit-down or takeaway meal with a quiet, cosy atmosphere and free on-site parking.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian' bento box option and multiple vegetarian sushi/roll items (e.g. Vegetarian combo, Avocado, Yam Tempura, Kitsune Udon). Website also lists 'Healthy options' under offerings

restaurant.name: Salt Spring Wild Cider
restaurant.desc: Salt Spring Wild Cider is a craft cidery and farm restaurant producing artisanal ciders from heritage apple and pear trees — some over 100 years old — harvested from properties across Salt Spring Island, drawing on the island's history as once the largest apple producer in BC. Visitors can taste, share a bottle, or sit down for a full lunch or dinner in a rustic farm setting with both indoor seating and outdoor picnic tables. The cidery is open year-round, seven days a week, and welcomes families and dogs in the outdoor area.

detail.address: 151 Sharp Rd, Salt Spring Island BC

restaurant.name: Sushi Nara
restaurant.desc: Sushi Nara is a sushi fast-food restaurant in Chilliwack, BC, operating since 2012 according to OSM records. It is located in a unit within a commercial building in the Fraser Valley. No current web presence is available to provide further detail about the business.

detail.address: Suite 150, 2362 Whatcom Rd, Abbotsford, BC V3G 0C1

restaurant.name: HYDE on Main
restaurant.desc: HYDE on Main is a restaurant located on Main Street in Vancouver. Without access to website content, specific details about the business's offerings or facilities cannot be confirmed.

restaurant.name: Five Guys
restaurant.desc: Five Guys is a well-known burger chain founded in 1986 in Arlington, Virginia, now with nearly 1,700 locations worldwide, including this Richmond outpost in a shopping centre on Steveston Highway. The brand is known for hand-formed fresh burgers cooked well done, fresh-cut fries in peanut oil, and a no-freezer policy. A touring cyclist looking for a substantial, customizable meal in Richmond's south end would find this a reliable if chain-style option.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website /contact-us FAQ states: 'Our veggie sandwich and grilled cheese sandwiches are suitable for lacto-ovo vegetarians.' No vegan or GF claims confirmed

restaurant.name: Butterica
restaurant.desc: Butterica is a fresh-and-fast Indian grill kitchen whose signature Butterica™ butter chicken sauce is made daily from quality ingredients and locally grown tomatoes, with no processed additives or artificial food colouring. The broad menu runs from samosas, pakoras, and naan through curries, noodles, burgers, and rice bowls, covering both meat and vegetarian diners. Orders can be placed for in-person pickup or via Ubereats delivery.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian confirmed:. Vegan explicitly not available. Gluten-free explicitly not available

restaurant.name: OYA Sushi
restaurant.desc: Oya Japanese Restaurant is a Japanese cuisine establishment located in Kamloops, BC. The URL slug suggests a sushi focus, though this cannot be confirmed from available evidence. No further detail about the dining experience or cyclist-relevant facilities could be retrieved.

restaurant.name: Queensboro Pizza
restaurant.desc: Queensboro Pizza is a family-owned neighbourhood pizzeria established in 2000, specializing in Punjabi-style pizza — a distinctive fusion that sets it apart from typical pizza chains. Located in the Queensborough area of New Westminster, it has built a loyal local following over more than two decades. Cyclists passing through can phone ahead for a takeout order.

restaurant.name: The Polly Fox
restaurant.desc: The Polly Fox is a completely gluten-free bakery and café established in 2016 in downtown Abbotsford's Essendene Avenue corridor, free from gluten, peanuts, and sesame with extensive vegan and dairy-free options. The menu spans house-baked goods, cooked breakfast and lunch items, and locally roasted small-batch coffees, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions or anyone wanting a quality sit-down break. It also sells packaged gluten-free products (baking mixes, cookie dough, granola) for take-home.

restaurant.name: BiblioCafe
restaurant.desc: BiblioCafe is a University of Victoria Food Services café tucked into the ground floor of the William C. Mearns Centre for Learning (McPherson Library) on the UVic campus. It offers specialty coffees and teas alongside a selection of grab-and-go items including sushi, sandwiches, wraps, salads, and freshly baked pastries and sweets. The UVic campus is well connected to Victoria's cycling network, making this a convenient mid-ride refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the Gordon Head area.

detail.address: McPherson Library, Ground Floor, 3800 Finnerty Road, Victoria, BC

restaurant.name: Cora
restaurant.desc: Cora is a well-known Canadian breakfast and lunch franchise chain with a Kelowna outpost inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre. The menu leans heavily on fresh fruit, crêpes, waffles, eggs, and omelettes — the kind of high-carbohydrate morning meal that touring cyclists appreciate before a big day on the road. A patio is available for outdoor dining, and takeout and delivery are also offered.

restaurant.name: Ba Le Deli & Banh Mi
restaurant.desc: Ba Le Deli & Bakery is a family-owned Vietnamese delicatessen that has been baking its own baguettes and crafting bánh mì sandwiches in Vancouver since 1987. The Rupert Street shop is one of several Lower Mainland locations, offering a menu that spans classic Vietnamese cold cut subs, vegan and vegetarian options, vermicelli bowls, and desserts. For cyclists moving through East Vancouver, it is a quick, affordable stop for a filling handmade sandwich.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Vegan Steak Banh Mi, Vegan Bologna Banh Mi, Vegetarian Lemongrass Chicken Banh Mi, Classic Vietnamese Veggie Sandwich, and Vermicelli Bowl with Tofu and Spring Rolls

restaurant.name: The Canadian Grind Coffee & Tea
restaurant.desc: The Canadian Grind is a coffee and tea café on 100 Avenue in Fort St. John, distinguished by an extensive loose-leaf tea catalog spanning over 135 varieties across categories including black, green, herbal, chai, matcha, oolong, and wellness blends. The shop also offers in-house café service and catering, making it a warm stop for cyclists passing through this northeastern BC hub city. Its tea-forward identity sets it apart from the typical roadside coffee stop.

restaurant.name: Beere Brewing Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: Beere Brewing is a father-and-son craft brewery and tasting room on Esplanade East in North Vancouver, pouring a rotating lineup of house-brewed ales, IPAs, lagers, and sours with playful names. The taproom features outdoor seating and a retail shop selling individual cans to go. The brewery leans into local sourcing, using BC-grown ingredients including Pemberton hops and Armstrong barley in some of its beers.

detail.address: 312 Esplanade East, North Vancouver, BC V7L 1A4

restaurant.name: Bliss Bakery
restaurant.desc: Bliss Bakery is a long-established artisan bakery and bistro founded in 2005, known for slow-fermented sourdough breads made with a starter originally cultivated from Okanagan grapes. The West Kelowna location operates as a grab-and-go kitchen serving house-made croissants, hearty sandwiches, soups, and crafted organic coffee. A second lakeside location in Peachland offers views of Okanagan Lake.

detail.address: 320-1405 Stevens Rd, West Kelowna, BC V1Z 3Y2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website shop page lists 'Vegetarian 10 Products' as a dedicated category

restaurant.name: Little Mexico Cantina
restaurant.desc: Little Mexico Cantina is a full-service Mexican restaurant and bar in the Steveston village area of Richmond, offering house-made tortillas, a wide taco selection, and a full bar with daily happy hour. The Chatham Street location puts it within easy reach of cyclists riding the popular Fraser River dyke trail network. A broad appetizer menu and online ordering make it a flexible stop for groups of varying sizes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels multiple vegetarian items: Vegetarian Taco Fillings, Deep Fried Cauliflower, Chips & Salsa, Chips & Guacamole, Chips & Pico de Gallo, Queso Fundido with vegetarian sub option, and LMC Salad

restaurant.name: Banh Mi Saigon
restaurant.desc: Banh Mi Saigon is a family-run Vietnamese sandwich shop on Victoria Drive in South East Vancouver, recognized for baking its baguettes in-house daily from a house recipe. The shop has earned praise from Scout Magazine, Gastrofork, and American Express Essentials for its fresh, locally sourced ingredients and standout bread. Its compact menu spans a dozen banh mi variations, Vietnamese desserts, and traditional drinks — a quick, high-quality fuel stop for cyclists passing through East Vancouver.

notes.Takeout: Counter-service sandwich shop; website describes it as a 'Vietnamese sandwich shop' with no mention of dine-in seating; menu page lists individual items and notes a bulk-order deal (buy 10 get 1 free), consistent with takeout-only operation
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu item #8 Veggie Chay: tofu, cooked veggies, and vermicelli served on a freshly baked baguette

restaurant.name: Angus T Bakery & Cafe
restaurant.desc: Angus T is a Belgian-inspired artisan bakery and cafe founded in 2016 around a family croissant recipe from a small village in Belgium. Located in Vancouver's River District, it produces an extensive range of sweet and savory croissants, cinnamon buns, and babka buns daily in an open kitchen using locally and European-sourced ingredients. The cafe also serves a full espresso bar menu, making it a satisfying stop for cyclists exploring the Fraser River area.

restaurant.name: Trattoria Italian Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Italian restaurant on Kingsway in Burnaby serving pizza and pasta, with both indoor and outdoor seating. Part of the Glowbal Group; wheelchair accessible and non-smoking.

restaurant.name: Dosa Paragon
restaurant.desc: Dosa Paragon is an Indian restaurant in Victoria specializing in South Indian dosas and traditional Indian cuisine. The menu includes vegetarian and vegan options, making it suitable for cyclists with various dietary preferences.

restaurant.name: WhataFood!
restaurant.desc: WhataFood! is a Brazilian street food restaurant inside the New Westminster SkyTrain Station, best known for its freshly-made pastéis—Brazil's crispy, golden fried pastries—offered in both savory and dessert varieties alongside Whatabites and an all-you-can-eat experience. The business grew from a festival market stall in 2017 to a permanent storefront that opened in 2020, building a loyal following for its authenticity and warmth. Its transit-hub location makes it a quick and convenient food stop for cyclists moving through New Westminster.

detail.address: 800 Carnarvon St #255, New Westminster, BC V3M 0G3

restaurant.name: Kokomo
restaurant.desc: Kokomo is a plant-based eatery with four Metro Vancouver locations, serving fresh bowls, salads, acai bowls, smoothies, and handhelds made entirely from plant-based ingredients. The East Van location sits near Trout Lake on Commercial Street and is notable for also offering vegan burgers alongside the core bowl menu. The brand describes itself as bringing 'the energy and warmth of summer' through nourishing food in a sun-filled space.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website describes 'plant-based bowls' and 'vegan burgers'; Jobs page calls it 'a plant-based eatery'. Entire menu is vegan

restaurant.name: Donair acafe
restaurant.desc: Donair Cafe is a fast-food spot in Sardis, Chilliwack, specializing in donairs — a Maritime-style spiced beef dish served in flatbread that is popular across Western Canada. Located in the Fraser Valley, it sits along cycling routes connecting Chilliwack's communities. As a quick-service eatery, it would offer a calorie-dense, inexpensive stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

detail.address: 7670 Vedder Rd #105, Chilliwack, BC V2R 4G9, Canada

restaurant.name: Damaskino Shawarma
restaurant.desc: Damaskino Shawarma is a halal restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, a neighbourhood that sits at the gateway to the Stanley Park seawall — one of the city's busiest cycling corridors. The OSM record notes locally-sourced ingredients and a fully smoke-free, indoor-only dining environment. It is a plausible refuelling stop for cyclists completing the seawall loop or heading north toward the Lions Gate Bridge.

restaurant.name: Café Crêpe
restaurant.desc: Café Crêpe is a French-style crêperie making crepes from homemade batter since 1999, located steps from the Granville SkyTrain Station entrance in the heart of downtown Vancouver. The menu spans a wide range of savoury and sweet crêpes alongside specialty illy espresso drinks, milkshakes, and French sodas, with a gluten-free buckwheat crêpe substitution available on any item. Both indoor and outdoor seating are on offer, making it a convenient refuelling stop on a downtown cycling route.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian confirmed:; website menu includes 'Le Vegetarien' (spinach, feta, mushroom, tomato). Gluten-free buckwheat crêpe substitution available on all crêpes. Vegan explicitly no

restaurant.name: Mashti
restaurant.desc: Mashti Cafe describes itself as the first Iranian juice and ice cream bar in British Columbia, serving fresh juices, smoothies, shakes, ice creams, and traditional Persian sweets at its flagship North Vancouver location on Lonsdale Avenue. Founded by Armin NejadYousefi and Hooman Khabbaz, the business brings Persian hospitality to the community with both indoor and outdoor seating available. It operates multiple locations including a Coquitlam branch and a wholesale operation, suggesting an established and growing presence.

restaurant.name: Sedap Plus
restaurant.desc: Sedap Plus is a Malaysian restaurant located on Cambie Street in Vancouver offering casual dining in an established neighborhood setting. The restaurant provides traditional Malaysian cuisine, making it a destination for touring cyclists seeking something beyond standard fare. It serves as a reliable food stop with indoor seating.

restaurant.name: Timberlands Pub
restaurant.desc: Timberland Pub is a neighbourhood pub and liquor store in the Cassidy/Ladysmith area of Vancouver Island, offering dine-in and takeout with a full menu of pub classics including fresh local oysters and daily specials. The pub features pool tables, dart boards, keno, and an outdoor patio. A separately operated liquor store sits next door, making it a handy one-stop for a meal and supplies.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists clearly vegetarian items by ingredients: Pakora (chickpea flour, spinach, cauliflower), Garden Salad, Yam Fries, Nachos. No explicit GF or vegan labelling found

restaurant.name: Bin 4 Burger Lounge
restaurant.desc: Bin 4 Burger Lounge is a BC-grown burger chain with a South Granville location serving creative smashed-patty burgers, bowls, and salads using locally sourced ingredients including premium BC beef and Rossdown Farms chicken. The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating and a full bar program, making it a substantial stop for hungry cyclists on the Granville Street corridor. Plant-based and vegetarian diners are well catered for, with tofu substitutions available across the menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly offers tofu substitutions ('sub blackened tofu'), a vegan red pepper dressing on the Bin 4 Bowl, and the Bin 38 Aloo Tikki patty (potato, peas, cilantro — plant-based)

restaurant.name: Embers Wine & Charcuterie Cellar
restaurant.desc: Embers Wine & Charcuterie Cellar bills itself as Nanaimo's only wine and charcuterie cellar, offering curated cured meats, artisan cheeses, cured seafood, and an extensive wine list in a cellar-style setting on Front Street. It is part of a family of local restaurants also including The View Oceanside Grill and Top Notch Burgers. The intimate venue is reservations-recommended and is a 19+ establishment.

notes.Takeout: FAQ states: 'We can arrange for a board to be prepared for take-out with one week advance notice.' A take-out fee and automatic gratuity apply; request via email
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms: 'We do have many vegetarian options, as well as some vegan options, including a vegan cheddar.' Also: 'many gluten-free crackers and accompaniments available, and our cheeses, meats, and seafood options are all gluten-free' (cross-contamination caveat noted)

restaurant.name: The Old Firehouse Wine & Cocktail Bar
restaurant.desc: The Old Firehouse Wine & Cocktail Bar is an artisanal wine and cocktail bar opened in March 2012 by the Downie Family, located in Downtown Duncan's City Square in the Cowichan Valley. It serves scratch-made food using fresh, often locally sourced and organic ingredients, alongside an extensive collection of wines, cocktails, whiskies, and creative non-alcoholic drinks. The bar regularly hosts live music, comedy nights, winemaker's dinners, and hands-on cocktail classes, making it a lively cultural anchor in the heart of Duncan.

restaurant.name: Oidé Coffee
restaurant.desc: Oidé Coffee began as a small coffee window in Vancouver's Waterfall Building and has grown into a destination for specialty coffee, stocking single-origin beans from Ethiopia, Colombia, Kenya, and Brazil. Knowledgeable baristas serve carefully brewed cups while the shop also carries equipment, tableware, art, books, and branded merchandise. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a focused, independent coffee experience on West 2nd Avenue near the Seawall.

restaurant.name: The Regalia Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A Chinese restaurant located in Richmond. Current operational status is uncertain due to website inaccessibility.

restaurant.name: Hot House Pizza
restaurant.desc: Hot House Pizza is a locally-operated pizza chain with five or more locations across Victoria, BC, including Oak Bay, Gordon Head, Cook Street Village, Victoria West, and UVic campus. They hand-make their crusts and offer a wide range of specialty and custom pizzas, including gluten-free, dairy-free, and soy-cheese options. Fresh slices are available to-go at all locations, making this a quick and flexible refuelling stop for cyclists on many routes across the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website confirms gluten-free and dairy-free crust, Daiya cheese, soy cheese, and a wide selection of vegetable toppings including fresh spinach, artichoke hearts, and others

restaurant.name: Mangos Kitchen Bar
restaurant.desc: Mangos Kitchen Bar is a Latin American restaurant and bar in downtown Vancouver's Howe Street corridor, serving dishes drawn from across the continent — Peruvian ceviche and lomo saltado, Mexican birria tacos, Colombian empanadas, Venezuelan arepas, and Argentine choripán. The venue pairs an extensive cocktail list (premium tequilas, Colombian aguardiente, Peruvian pisco) with a lively events calendar including salsa and bachata dance nights. Outdoor patio seating and a high-energy atmosphere make it a spirited stop in the heart of downtown.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Enchiladas Suizas with explicit 'chicken or veggy' choice; Nachos Perrones can be ordered without meat

restaurant.name: Sushi Aboard
restaurant.desc: A sushi restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, steps from the Stanley Park seawall cycling routes. The menu spans bento boxes, nigiri, sashimi, specialty rolls, donburi, and party trays, making it a flexible stop for solo riders or groups. Online ordering with pick-up is available, convenient for cyclists who want to grab food without waiting.

restaurant.name: The Sour Pickle Cafe
restaurant.desc: A restaurant on Store Street in central Victoria. Website is not currently accessible, limiting available information about the business and its services.

restaurant.name: Bombay Kitchen On Denman
restaurant.desc: Bombay Kitchen on Denman is an Indian restaurant on the West End's Denman Street, a well-travelled cycling corridor connecting Stanley Park to the rest of Vancouver. The kitchen draws on North Indian traditions with a menu spanning tandoori grills, street-food kathi rolls, and a broad range of curries made with fresh ingredients and house-blend masalas. Online ordering with free delivery is available, and the restaurant also offers full catering for private and corporate events.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Catering menu lists a dedicated 'Vegetarian / Vegan' combo featuring veg and paneer curries; gluten-free naans explicitly noted as available; multiple vegetarian dishes on the regular menu (Channa Masala, Paneer Tikka Masala, Chef Special Mix Veg, etc.)

restaurant.name: Thetis Island Marina Pub
restaurant.desc: Thetis Island Marina Pub is a waterfront pub and restaurant at Thetis Island Resort on Thetis Island in the Gulf Islands, reachable by BC Ferries from Chemainus or by seaplane. The kitchen emphasizes locally sourced ingredients from Thetis Island and Vancouver Island, with signature offerings including beer-battered fish and chips and char-broiled burgers, plus an outdoor licensed barbecue area capable of hosting groups of up to 150. The resort complex includes a general store, fuel dock, hotel suites, and marina moorage, making it a self-contained destination for visitors arriving by ferry or boat.

restaurant.name: White Spot
restaurant.desc: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, founded in 1928 and celebrated for crowd-pleasing classics made with fresh Canadian beef, BC chicken, and locally sourced ingredients. The Abbotsford (Whatcom) location on North Parallel Road is a full-service family restaurant open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner with outdoor seating. Touring cyclists will find a reliable, well-known stop for a sit-down or takeout meal in the Fraser Valley.

restaurant.name: Kazumi
restaurant.desc: Kazumi is a Japanese and Korean fusion restaurant in Langford, offering an extensive menu that spans hand-crafted sushi rolls, sashimi, aburi nigiri, donburi, noodles, hot pot, and Korean dishes like BBQ kalbi. The kitchen emphasizes fresh, quality ingredients sourced internationally, with eye-catching specialty rolls like the Lobster Roll and Volcano Roll. It makes a well-rounded meal stop for cyclists exploring the western Greater Victoria region.

restaurant.name: Yew Street Food Hall
restaurant.desc: Yew Street Food Hall is a vibrant indoor food hall in Kamloops' North Shore neighbourhood, bringing together ten independent food and drink vendors under one roof. The eclectic vendor lineup spans Korean fried chicken, Vietnamese, Mexican, pasta, crepes, and craft beverages from local and regional producers. It's a community-focused culinary hub where a touring cyclist can choose from a wide variety of cuisines without committing to a single restaurant.

restaurant.name: Connection Café (Lost Lake Passivhaus)
restaurant.desc: Lost Lake Passivhaus — formerly known as Austria House — is a public building located near Lost Lake in Whistler, BC. It is associated with the Canadian Passive House Institute as a demonstration project showcasing passive-house energy construction standards. Whether it currently operates as a cafe with public food and drink service cannot be confirmed from available evidence.

restaurant.name: Upstream Bar + Grill
restaurant.desc: Fast-food bar and grill located within the Vancouver Aquarium. Offers both indoor and outdoor seating, serving as a dining option for visitors to this major North Vancouver attraction.

restaurant.name: The Taco Club
restaurant.desc: The Taco Club is a downtown Revelstoke restaurant that evolved from a retrofitted Canada Post van food truck — affectionately nicknamed Jade — into a local institution serving Latin-inspired tacos, burritos, nachos, and an extensive cocktail list. The business explicitly frames itself as a refueling stop for adventure athletes including trail riders, with an outdoor deck and deep community roots including a regular presence at local bike races and events. A broad menu with clearly marked vegetarian and vegan options makes it a versatile stop for mixed-diet groups.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items marked 'VG' (Chips/Guacamole/Salsa, The Club Salad); Street Corn and Tortilla Soup note 'Ask for VG'; Crispy Avocado listed as a standalone taco filling option

restaurant.name: 3rd Street Cafe
restaurant.desc: 3rd Street Cafe is a cafe located in Sidney, BC, a popular stop on the Saanich Peninsula cycling circuit near the BC Ferries Swartz Bay terminal. Sidney is a compact, bikeable waterfront town and cafes in this area commonly serve touring cyclists arriving from or departing to the Gulf Islands.

detail.address: 2466 Beacon Ave, Sidney, BC V8L 1X8, Canada

restaurant.name: The Kootenay Bakery Cafe Cooperative
restaurant.desc: The Kootenay Bakery Cafe Cooperative is a worker-owned organic bakery and café on Nelson's main commercial street, producing over 300 from-scratch products using certified organic and locally sourced ingredients. As a cooperative, it embeds principles of mutual aid and sustainability into its operations, supplying restaurants and retailers across the Kootenays alongside its café trade. Touring cyclists will find fresh breads, pastries, coffee, and warm beverages, with options for vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, and egg-free diets.

restaurant.name: Gate-Way Pizza
restaurant.desc: Gateway Pizza is a long-running Surrey restaurant that merges Canadian-style pizza with an extensive Indian curry menu, including biryanis, butter chicken, and paneer dishes. The Surrey Centre location is one of two family-owned outlets serving the broader Surrey area and offers takeout alongside delivery. Cyclists passing through the Guildford corridor would find a wide range of filling options, including a substantial vegetarian selection.

It sits within a self-contained complex that also houses BC's Best Buy Liquor Store — a handy one-stop for touring cyclists resupplying on the Cowichan Valley trail corridor.

detail.address: 56 North Shore Road, Lake Cowichan, BC V0R 2G0

restaurant.name: Northern Cafe
restaurant.desc: Northern Cafe & Grill is a family-run diner perched above a working lumberyard in South Vancouver, serving Asian-Western fusion comfort food since 1949. The menu blends Canadian breakfast classics with handmade wontons, gyozas, smoked salmon eggs benny, and bottomless fresh-brewed coffee, earning Vancouver Magazine's 'Best Brunch' award in 2025 and 2026 and Yelp's #1 spot in Canada in 2023. Its off-the-beaten-path location, retro atmosphere, and walls covered in handwritten notes from guests around the world make it a genuine neighbourhood destination well off the tourist trail.

detail.address: 1640 E. Kent Avenue South, Vancouver, BC V5P 2S7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms: 'Yes, Northern Cafe has vegan and vegetarian options. From our Vegetarian Spring Rolls to our Veggie Clubhouse Sandwich.' Menu also lists Veggie Eggs Benny and Garden Omelet. GF not explicitly mentioned

restaurant.name: Papa John's
restaurant.desc: Papa John's is a national pizza chain franchise on Fort Street in Victoria's Fernwood neighbourhood, offering delivery and carryout of pizza, breadsticks, and wings. It operates as a takeout-focused location with no dine-in seating, making it a quick stop for a cyclist needing a hot meal or something to go.

restaurant.name: Kilimanjaro Snack House
restaurant.desc: Kilimanjaro Snack House is an East African and South Asian snack house and catering business on Kingsway in Vancouver, serving handmade samosas, kebabs, Mogo (cassava fries), biryanis, and dishes rooted in the Kenyan-Indian coastal culinary tradition. The menu spans quick snacks to full feature dishes like Kuku Paka, Akni, and Mishkaki, reflecting a distinctive culinary heritage rarely found in BC. Cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor will find a neighbourhood counter-service spot with a broad, flavourful menu and catering available for larger groups.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian items: Vegetable Samosas, Daal Bhajia, Nylon Bhajia, Chana Bateta, Vegetable Pakora, Vegetable Curry, Karela/Bhinda Curry, Daal & Rice, Spinach Curry, Coconut Daal. No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: K-Bunsik

restaurant.name: Just Fold
restaurant.desc: Just Fold is a dessert café situated at Lonsdale Quay in North Vancouver, steps from the SeaBus terminal that connects to downtown Vancouver. Its waterfront commercial setting makes it a natural stop for cyclists arriving or departing via the SeaBus or riding the North Shore. The café's dessert focus offers a sweet refuelling option along one of the region's busiest cycling corridors.

detail.address: 123 Carrie Cates Court, North Vancouver, BC

restaurant.name: Gon Sushi
restaurant.desc: Gon Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Chilliwack serving sushi rolls, sashimi, tempura, teriyaki, and Korean-influenced dishes such as bulgogi bibimbob. It offers both pickup and delivery, making it a practical meal stop for cyclists travelling the Vedder Road corridor. The menu spans appetizers through specialty rolls and full rice plates.

restaurant.name: Jalapenos Mexican Food
restaurant.desc: Mexican restaurant on Island Highway East in Parksville serving local and touring diners. A sit-down dining establishment with Mexican cuisine.

restaurant.name: Riverway Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Riverway Restaurant is a City of Burnaby-operated dining room situated at the Riverway Clubhouse golf facility, part of the Burnaby Hospitality group that manages several restaurants, venues, and accommodations across the city. The restaurant is marketed as offering West Coast-inspired cuisine in a scenic setting among rolling hills and trees. It sits alongside a cluster of other city-run food and event facilities, making it a notable stop in Burnaby's park and recreation corridor.

detail.address: 9001 Bill Fox Way, Burnaby, BC V5J 5J3

restaurant.name: Bee Thai
restaurant.desc: Bee Thai Cuisine is a family-owned Thai restaurant specializing in North Eastern Isan Thai cuisine, operating in Mission, BC since 2015. The menu spans traditional curries, stir-fries, and a bubble tea selection, made with recipes passed down through generations. Its reputation draws diners from across the Canada-US border, with at least one reviewer making a cross-border trip specifically for the food.

restaurant.name: Browns Social House
restaurant.desc: Browns Socialhouse Fort St. John is a casual full-service chain restaurant situated in Fort St. John's commercial core, part of the Browns Restaurant Group with dozens of locations across BC and Alberta. The restaurant offers a social-house menu with weekend brunch service, making it one of the more substantial sit-down dining options in this northern BC community. Fort St. John sits along the Alaska Highway corridor, a key waypoint for cyclists undertaking long-distance northern routes.

restaurant.name: Sushi Bar Kilala
restaurant.desc: Sushi Bar Kilala is a small, intimate Japanese restaurant in the Burnaby Heights neighbourhood, run by a Japanese couple who prepare traditionally styled sushi with fresh seafood. It is consistently described by reviewers as a neighbourhood hidden gem, especially praised for its uni nigiri. The space is quiet and casual with limited seating and a classy atmosphere.

restaurant.name: Yianni's Greek Taverna
restaurant.desc: Yianni's Greek Taverna is a family-owned restaurant that has anchored Uptown New Westminster since 2000, earning multiple Best Greek Restaurant awards in the city. The blue-and-white interior seats diners alongside a patio, and the menu spans classic Greek dips, grilled meats, lamb dishes, and imported Greek wines and beer. It caters to families and corporate groups alike and also offers community catering.

detail.address: 543 Sixth Street, New Westminster, BC V3L 3B9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated Veggie Platter (Veggie Mousaka, Spanakopita, Tiropita, Veg Dolmathes) and multiple vegetarian appetizers and dips; no vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Sushi Zion
restaurant.desc: Sushi Zion is a neighbourhood Japanese restaurant in Surrey serving sushi alongside Korean-Japanese fusion dishes. The compact spot offers both dine-in and take-out, and supports online ordering with a loyalty points program. It sits along the 168 Street corridor in the Cloverdale area of Surrey.

restaurant.name: June
restaurant.desc: June is a brasserie-inspired restaurant and cocktail bar in Vancouver's Cambie Village occupying a two-level space, with a main dining room serving French-influenced West Coast cuisine and an intimate downstairs vinyl listening bar called Lala. The venture comes from the team behind Vancouver's award-winning Keefer Bar and has earned widespread press recognition, including being an Air Canada Best New Restaurant 2025 finalist. An expansive centre bar with an open-kitchen view and a deeply curated global spirits list — spanning dozens of gins, tequilas, and whiskies — make it a notable destination in the neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Edo Japan
restaurant.desc: Edo Japan at Totem Mall is a Canadian-founded Japanese-inspired fast food chain serving teppanyaki meals grilled fresh to order, hand-rolled sushi, ramen, and bubble tea. The Fort St. John location sits streetfront in Totem Mall off 96A Street, easily reached from the Alaska Highway. With over 200 locations nationwide, it offers dine-in seating, takeout, delivery, and catering.

restaurant.name: The Dirty Apron
restaurant.desc: The Dirty Apron is a cooking school, award-winning delicatessen, and full-service catering company in downtown Vancouver's Crosstown neighbourhood, founded in 2009 by Chef David Robertson and Sara Robertson. It teaches over 10,000 students a year and produces gourmet deli fare alongside curated picnics and catering. A touring cyclist stopping downtown will find freshly made lunches and baked goods at the deli counter.

detail.address: 540 Beatty Street, Crosstown Vancouver, BC V6B 2L3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Daily specials list multiple items labelled GF/Vegetarian, including Roasted Squash & Apple Soup (GF/Vegetarian) and BBQ Broccolini & Radicchio Salad (GF/Vegetarian)

restaurant.name: Popeyes
restaurant.desc: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen is a national fried-chicken chain with a location in Fort St. John on Alaska Road South, a major artery for cyclists and travellers heading toward or returning from Alaska Highway country. The restaurant features a drive-through as well as dine-in and takeout options, making it a convenient calorie stop on a long northern BC touring route.

detail.address: 11203 Alaska Road South, Fort St. John, V1J 6N2

restaurant.name: Stillfood Bistro & Cappuccino Bar
restaurant.desc: StillFood Bistro is an artisan coffee and fresh-fare restaurant on Front Street in downtown Penticton, a well-positioned stop for cyclists exploring the Okanagan. The bistro emphasizes vegan-friendly options alongside its cappuccino bar, making it a solid refuelling choice for riders with dietary restrictions. Penticton's Front Street sits near the waterfront and multi-use paths connecting Okanagan and Skaha lakes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website subtitle 'Artisan Coffee & Fresh Fare' consistent with health-conscious menu

restaurant.name: Sasha Sushi
restaurant.desc: Sasha Sushi is an established Japanese restaurant in Abbotsford serving dine-in and takeout, known in the community for its modern takes on classic sushi and fresh, high-quality ingredients. Formerly operating as Sumas Sushi Café, it offers a wide menu of creative rolls alongside traditional nigiri and Japanese mains. A touring cyclist on Sumas Way would find a solid sit-down or grab-and-go meal option conveniently located in a retail strip.

restaurant.name: Marulilu Cafe
restaurant.desc: Marulilu Cafe is a Japanese classic-style cafe on West Broadway in Vancouver, one minute's walk from Broadway-City Hall Station. It serves traditional Japanese comfort food popular in Japan — including Omu-Rice, Curry-Rice, Onigiri, and Donburi — alongside coffee and tea. Online ordering for counter pickup is available, making it a convenient stop on a busy cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Egg Bomb
restaurant.desc: Egg Bomb is a breakfast and brunch café in Langley serving creative fare including crodises (croissant-donut hybrids), croffles, French toast, sandwiches, and salads alongside an extensive coffee and drink menu. The restaurant offers dine-in seating with advance reservations and phone-based takeout orders. It would serve as a refuelling stop for cyclists riding along the Fraser Highway corridor.

restaurant.name: Dovetail
restaurant.desc: Dovetail is a sophisticated Yaletown restaurant built around California-inspired, family-style shared plates and an elevated cocktail menu. The space channels a modern boho aesthetic informed by west coast seasonal produce, groovy house music, and an effortlessly chic energy. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a viable stop for cyclists riding through Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Toki's Chinese Food
restaurant.desc: Toki's Chinese Food is a Langley neighbourhood Chinese restaurant serving an extensive Cantonese-style menu spanning soups, chow mein (soft and crispy), fried rice, chop suey, seafood, beef, and chicken dishes. The restaurant offers structured family dinner packages sized for two to ten diners, as well as individual combination dinners — useful for a solo cyclist or a group refuelling together. Pickup orders are actively promoted, making it a practical stop for takeaway on a touring route through the Fraser Valley.

notes.Takeout: Website homepage advertises '10% DISCOUNT (CASH OR DEBIT ONLY) ON PICK UP ORDERS OVER $50.00 BEFORE TAXES', confirming takeout/pickup service
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels 'Crispy Egg Roll (Vegetarian)' and lists several meatless dishes: Mixed Veggies (No Meat), Vegetable or Mushroom Chow Mein, Vegetable or Mushroom Fried Rice, Tofu Chop Suey, Salt & Pepper Tofu, and Tofu Veggies in Black Bean Sauce

restaurant.name: Booster Juice
restaurant.desc: Booster Juice is a Canadian smoothie and juice bar chain founded in 1999 in Alberta, specializing in blended-to-order smoothies, fresh-pressed juices, açaí bowls, and healthy grab-and-go snacks. This River District branch sits in a newer mixed-use neighbourhood on Vancouver's south shore and offers indoor seating. It's a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists looking for a quick, nutritious liquid meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Entire menu is plant-based: smoothies, fresh juices, açaí bowls, and grab-and-go snacks; website describes high-quality fruits and vegetables as core ingredients

restaurant.name: Blue Ox Pub
restaurant.desc: The Blue Ox Pub is a classic neighbourhood pub in Lumby, BC, serving pub food and drinks in a cozy, welcoming atmosphere. Open seven days a week, it is a solid stop for touring cyclists passing through the North Okanagan on routes connecting Vernon and the Monashee corridor. The pub hosts regular events and draws a local crowd, giving visiting riders an authentic taste of small-town BC.

restaurant.name: Liberty Wine Merchants
restaurant.desc: Liberty Wine Merchants is one of the largest independent private fine wine retail chains in Western Canada, operating since 1986 with six Metro Vancouver locations. The Commercial Drive shop sits on one of Vancouver's most vibrant and cycling-friendly corridors, stocking an extensive selection of wines, spirits, craft beer, cider, and sake. Cyclists exploring East Van could stop in for a BC bottle to take back to camp or a local accommodation.

restaurant.name: Bonjour Banh Mi
restaurant.desc: Bonjour Banh Mi is a Vietnamese sandwich shop on Cambie Street specializing in banh mi made with house-baked bread and in-house sauces prepared fresh daily. The concise menu spans signature cold cut subs, grilled pork and lemongrass chicken banh mi, salad rolls, rice and vermicelli bowls, and soup — offering quick, filling meals well-suited to cyclists passing through South Vancouver. Vegetarian choices appear across multiple menu categories.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu item #4 Veggie / Chay (veggie pate, veggie ham, jicama) and item #10 Veggie Salad Rolls (carrots, jicama, lettuce, vermicelli, rice paper) confirm vegetarian options

restaurant.name: Far Out Coffee Post
restaurant.desc: Far Out Coffee Post is a café in North Vancouver with outdoor seating, suggesting a casual setting that could suit cyclists stopping for a break. restaurant.desc: Old Street Express is a Chinese fast-food outlet in Richmond, BC, tagged in OpenStreetMap as operating at ground level within an indoor space — consistent with a food-court or mall unit. The cuisine tag suggests Chinese fare typical of quick-service counters common in Richmond's dense dining scene. A touring cyclist passing through Richmond's urban core may find it a convenient stop for a fast hot meal.

restaurant.name: Bynns
restaurant.desc: Bynns Subs is a neighbourhood sandwich and coffee counter on Dunbar Street in Vancouver, serving ciabatta subs alongside espresso drinks and drip coffee. The shop has a customer-satisfaction guarantee and runs a weekly raffle for regulars, giving it a community-café feel. It sits along a residential cycling corridor in the Dunbar neighbourhood.

notes.Takeout: Website presents a takeout-oriented sub and coffee menu with no dine-in seating mentioned

restaurant.name: Pallas Athena Greek Kouzina
restaurant.desc: Pallas Athena Greek Kouzina is a family-operated Greek restaurant in Port Coquitlam, BC, founded in 2006 and run by a mother-daughter team who prepare authentic homemade Greek cuisine fresh daily. The menu spans traditional mezes, seafood, and classic entrees including dolmathes, spanakopita, kalamari, and a range of salatas. Cyclists passing through the tri-city area will find a casual sit-down dining experience with a full menu and a catering service.

restaurant.name: Eurobean Coffee
restaurant.desc: Eurobean Coffee is a cafe in Kelowna serving coffee and beverages. It provides a stopping point for refreshments during cycling travels through the Okanagan region.

restaurant.name: Kappo Marta
restaurant.desc: Kappo Marta is a Japanese restaurant on Bay Street in Victoria's Fernwood neighbourhood offering traditional kappo-style counter dining, where chefs prepare food directly in front of seated guests. The kappo format — meaning 'to slice and cook' — is an elite culinary style similar to kaiseki but less formal, creating an intimate choreography between chef and diner. The menu spans teishoku, donburi, and broader Japanese cuisine categories.

restaurant.name: Jollibee
restaurant.desc: Jollibee is a Philippine-origin fast food chain known for its Chickenjoy fried chicken, Jolly Spaghetti, and burgers, now with a location on Vancouver's busy Granville Street corridor. It offers indoor seating and takeaway, making it a quick calorie stop for cyclists passing through the downtown core. The chain is notable for its Filipino comfort-food menu, which sets it apart from typical North American fast food options.

restaurant.name: Sushi Nanaimo
restaurant.desc: Sushi Nanaimo is a Japanese restaurant situated on Nanaimo Street in East Vancouver, offering a broad menu spanning sushi, ramen, noodles, teriyaki, and more. The name refers to its street location rather than the city of Nanaimo on Vancouver Island. Online pickup ordering is available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists moving through the area.

restaurant.name: 10 Acres At The Pier
restaurant.desc: 10 Acres At The Pier is a west coast seafood and farm-to-table restaurant located inside the Pier Hotel on Sidney's waterfront, operated by the 10 Acres Farm & Restaurants group. The kitchen draws on ingredients grown at the group's own 10-acre farm, including heritage-breed livestock, orchard fruit, and heirloom vegetables, making for a menu that changes with the seasons. A cyclist finishing the Saanich Peninsula loop would find a full sit-down lunch and dinner service steps from the waterfront, with a sushi bar, fresh oysters, and a weekend brunch option as well.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items explicitly marked GF (gluten-free) and V (vegetarian), including 'GREEN SALAD GF', 'ROASTED BEETS GF + V', 'ROASTED CAULIFLOWER G.F D.F', and a Falafel add-on option

restaurant.name: Disco Cheetah
restaurant.desc: Disco Cheetah is a fast-casual Korean restaurant in Vancouver's Davie Village, specializing in Korean bowls and bao with a Western twist. The business evolved from a food truck launched in 2014 into a brick-and-mortar location that opened in 2019 in the lively, diverse Davie Village neighbourhood. Online ordering and catering services are available alongside a companion food truck that operates downtown on weekdays.

restaurant.name: The Village Taverna
restaurant.desc: The Village Taverna is a family-run Greek restaurant situated in Victoria's Cook Street Village, built around the concept of 'filoxenia' — legendary Greek hospitality — with recipes inherited from the owner's father. The menu features fresh Greek classics including souvlaki, moussaka, calamari, and mezethes, sourced from carefully selected local vendors and made from scratch where possible. It operates as a first-come, first-served casual eatery with both dine-in and counter takeout service, making it a practical stop for cyclists exploring the neighbourhood.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Falafel pita wrap, Vegetarian pita wrap, Falafel kebab meal, and Vegetarian Platter — multiple clearly labelled vegetarian options. No explicit vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Pinky's On Main
restaurant.desc: Pinky's On Main is a bar on Vancouver's Main Street, one of the city's most active and cyclist-friendly commercial corridors. The 2400 block sits in a dense mixed-use neighbourhood well-served by bike routes and close to transit. No business-specific web presence was accessible beyond an Instagram handle.

restaurant.name: CM Chicken
restaurant.desc: CM Chicken is a restaurant located in a unit at 2918 Glen Drive in Coquitlam, BC. The Instagram handle (@cmchickencoqcntr) suggests a connection to the Coquitlam Centre area. Beyond its name and location, no further details about cuisine style or offerings could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Torchlight Brewing
restaurant.desc: Torchlight Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and full-service taproom lounge in downtown Nelson, BC, co-founded in 2014 by two friends who scaled from a nano-brewery to a proper micro-brewery with a full lounge by 2017. Nelson is one of BC's premier cycling destinations and the brewery is a partner with Nelson and Kootenay Lake Tourism. Touring cyclists stopping in town will find house-crafted beers alongside a full food menu in a welcoming brewpub setting.

restaurant.name: Tuba Cafe
restaurant.desc: Tuba Café is a fully plant-based coffee shop and café in the heart of Squamish, serving an entirely vegan menu of house-made sandwiches, lentil soup, protein-packed smoothies, and desserts alongside a full espresso and tea program. Every item on the menu uses plant-based ingredients, making it a reliable stop for vegan and plant-curious cyclists on the Sea-to-Sky corridor. The indoor seating creates a relaxed space to recharge after a ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Entirely vegan menu; all listed food, drinks, and desserts are vegan

restaurant.name: Green Lettuce
restaurant.desc: Green Lettuce is Vancouver's first Indian-style Chinese food restaurant, a homestyle Kingsway institution established in 1999 that melds traditional Chinese technique with Indian spices. The late food critic James Barber was a devoted fan, and the restaurant has attracted Bollywood celebrities including Hrithik Roshan and Aishwarya Rai. The Vancouver location seats 60 people and offers a broad menu spanning chilli dumplings, Manchurian chicken, paneer, and gluten-free rice-noodle dishes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms vegetarian dishes (paneer, tofu, vegetable dishes) and explicitly lists gluten-free options including vermicelli (rice noodles), paneer, and many vegetarian dishes

restaurant.name: Forecast Coffee
restaurant.desc: Forecast Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe brand born in Whistler in 2020, built around mountain culture and outdoor community. Their cafes serve ethically sourced beans and the brand has a notable sustainability focus, including recyclable packaging and an impact initiative. OSM lists an East Hastings Street location with outdoor seating, though this address is absent from the company's current cafe listings.

restaurant.name: Shaketown Brewing
restaurant.desc: Shaketown Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and taproom in North Vancouver that celebrates the community's history through character-driven, locally made beers. Their spacious tasting room features floor-to-ceiling windows, sweeping skyline views, and large communal tables, with a window bar that's become a local landmark for people-watching. The on-site 20HL brewhouse produces a rotating lineup of core and seasonal beers, from a 3% session lager to a 6.75% grapefruit IPA.

restaurant.name: Beach Grove Cafe & Boutique
restaurant.desc: Beach Grove Cafe & Boutique is a combined cafe and lifestyle boutique in Delta's Beach Grove neighbourhood that has been operating since 2009. The boutique carries home decor, beauty and wellness products, women's clothing, jewellery, and artisan packaged foods, and also offers home styling services. The cafe component is not reflected on the business's current website, making it difficult to assess the food and beverage experience a visiting cyclist would encounter.

restaurant.name: Bún Riêu Phương Nam
restaurant.desc: Bún Riêu Phương Nam is a Vietnamese restaurant on Edmonds Street in the Edmonds neighbourhood of Burnaby. The name references bún riêu, the Vietnamese crab and tomato noodle soup, suggesting a menu centered on that dish. The restaurant sits along a commercial strip and is listed as non-smoking.

restaurant.name: Fusion Food Lounge
restaurant.desc: Fusion Food Lounge is a restaurant in Kelowna, BC, suggesting a menu that blends culinary traditions. Its OSM record was checked as recently as October 2024, but its website domain is currently parked, leaving much of its current offering unverifiable. Touring cyclists passing through Kelowna's dining scene may wish to confirm current operations before visiting.

restaurant.name: Truong Thanh 2
restaurant.desc: Truong Thanh 2 is a Vietnamese restaurant in a downtown commercial unit in Nanaimo. It serves traditional Vietnamese cuisine in a casual setting, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking for a meal.

restaurant.name: The View Oceanside Grill
restaurant.desc: The View Oceanside Grill is a casual fine-dining seafood and steakhouse located inside the Best Western Dorchester in downtown Nanaimo, offering water views of the harbour. It relocated from its original Stewart Avenue location and has since been voted TripAdvisor's #1 restaurant in Nanaimo as well as Best of the City in 2022 and 2023. The restaurant focuses exclusively on in-house dining with a menu of fresh seafood, steaks, and seasonal dishes, making it a destination experience rather than a quick stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms 'several vegetarian options available'; 'most of our entrees are gluten free' with appetizers and pastas adjustable; limited vegan options noted

restaurant.name: Top of Vancouver
restaurant.desc: Top of Vancouver is a fine dining revolving restaurant perched 553 feet (167m) above street level at the top of Harbour Centre Tower, offering a slow 360-degree panoramic sweep of the city skyline, coastal mountains, and ocean as you dine. The kitchen focuses on award-winning continental cuisine with an emphasis on premium seafood and meats. A touring cyclist seeking a special-occasion splurge will find this one of the most dramatically situated dining experiences in British Columbia.

restaurant.name: Kathmandu Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: Kathmandu Bar & Grill is a full-service restaurant and bar blending Nepalese, Indo-Chinese, and Western cuisine, with halal options also available. Located on Scott Road in Surrey, it offers dine-in with table reservations, takeout, and delivery across a 15 km radius. The menu is developed in-house by expert chefs aiming to merge culinary traditions into a cohesive dining experience.

restaurant.name: Cantonese BBQ
restaurant.desc: Cantonese BBQ is an authentic Cantonese restaurant in Richmond's Capstan Way area specialising in traditional roast meats — think soy-sauce chicken, char siu, and roast duck — served as platter combinations or over rice. It is one of two Lower Mainland locations and offers online ordering with quick pickup, making it a practical stop for cyclists fuelling up in the No. 3 Road / Capstan corridor.

restaurant.name: Glowbal
restaurant.desc: Glowbal is an upscale contemporary restaurant in the heart of downtown Vancouver, part of the well-established Glowbal Restaurant Group. The menu celebrates West Coast ingredients with dishes like fresh spot prawns, tableside prime rib, and Vancouver Island oysters. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the restaurant offers a full bar alongside a seasonal, ingredient-driven menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu confirms compatible dishes including Kale Salad, Fried Brussels Sprouts, and Burrata

restaurant.name: Lighthouse Bistro & Pub
restaurant.desc: Lighthouse Bistro & Pub is a waterfront restaurant on Nanaimo's harbourfront serving West Coast cuisine — fresh halibut, salmon, tuna poke, chowder, gourmet burgers, and craft drinks from Vancouver Island producers. The scenic outdoor patio overlooks Nanaimo Harbour and the restaurant sits close to the ferry terminal and seaplane dock, making it a natural stop for cyclists arriving or departing the island. Walk-ins are welcomed for groups under six.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states: 'We offer vegetarian and gluten-friendly options. Please let your server know about any dietary needs.'

restaurant.name: Sushi House
restaurant.desc: Sushi House is a Japanese restaurant in Richmond with indoor seating. As a dine-in establishment, it could serve as a rest and refuel stop for touring cyclists passing through the suburban area.

restaurant.name: Bamboo Garden
restaurant.desc: Bamboo Garden is a Chinese restaurant on Victoria Crescent in downtown Nanaimo specializing in authentic dishes including dim sum combos, fried noodles, spring rolls, and classics like sweet and sour pork and lemon chicken. The restaurant offers indoor seating and online ordering, making it a convenient sit-down or takeout stop for cyclists moving through the city centre.

restaurant.name: Chai Samosa
restaurant.desc: Chai Samosa by Roy's is an Indian street-food counter inside Tsawwassen Mills mall, specializing in freshly made samosas, traditional Indian sweets, and chai brewed with bold spices. The compact menu covers savoury snacks, desserts, and drinks rooted in classic Indian street-food tradition. Cyclists stopping in Tsawwassen can grab a quick takeout order or sit down for a snack before continuing their ride.

restaurant.name: Red Burrito
restaurant.desc: Red Burrito is a locally rooted Vancouver Mexican restaurant that has been making fresh burritos, tacos, and handmade tamales since opening in 2006 on Commercial Drive. The Alberni Street location sits in Vancouver's West End and is one of three active locations in the city. Food is made fresh daily in-house using a short, focused menu of classic Mexican staples.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'VEGAN MEAT' (soy-based protein in Red Burrito spices) and 'VEGETARIAN' (Spanish rice, beans, toppings, salsas, and fresh guacamole) as dedicated filling options

restaurant.name: CCTV珍味轩 Chinese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: CCTV Chinese Restaurant sits on Marine Drive in White Rock's popular waterfront tourist corridor, its name an acronym for China, Canada, Tsingtao, and Vancouver. Owner-chef Shi Lilong trained at Chinese culinary schools specializing in Shandong cuisine and earned recognition including a Healthy Dining certificate and a top-five ranking in the 2015 'Best Asian Food in Canada' competition. The broad menu spans seafood, lamb, pork, beef, cold dishes, and hand-crafted tofu, with online ordering available.

restaurant.name: Cafe & Life Co.
restaurant.desc: Cafe & Life Co. is a community-focused café founded during the COVID-19 pandemic with the explicit goal of reconnecting the local neighbourhood through great coffee and a warm, welcoming space. The Vancouver location on West 7th Avenue offers specialty lattes, freshly baked pastries, and elevated brunch dishes ranging from smoked salmon benny to romesco roast chicken. The café recently completed a soft reopening at this address, making it a cozy neighbourhood stop in a residential, cyclist-friendly part of the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian-suitable items: Smashed Avocado (sourdough, poached egg, cherry tomatoes), Fresh Papaya Salad, a full range of pastries, and numerous plant-based specialty drinks. No explicit vegan or GF labeling found on the website

restaurant.name: Nikkyu Japanese Restaurant

restaurant.name: Swagat Indian Sweet & Restaurant

restaurant.name: Kyros Kitchen

restaurant.name: Chongqing

restaurant.name: Brynn's Bakery
