restaurant.name: Big Wheel Burger
restaurant.desc: Big Wheel Burger is a Victoria-based fast food chain that has operated as Canada's first carbon neutral fast food restaurant since 2011, sourcing 100% fresh BC beef and buns baked daily by Irene's Bakery. The Vic West location is one of five across greater Victoria, offering a menu built around local and sustainable suppliers including Berryman Brothers and Island Farms. Touring cyclists will find a range of dietary options including plant-based burgers, a dedicated gluten-free fryer, and vegan-available items.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists Nashville Hawt Chickpea Burger and Yam & Black Bean Burger (available vegan), GF buns, a dedicated GF fryer, and vegetarian GF poutine gravy. Social post: 'two plant-based burgers made in-house, gf buns, a dedicated gf fryer, and poutine gravy that's vegetarian and gf.'

restaurant.name: Fusion Feast Pizza & Curry
restaurant.desc: Fusion Feast is a family-owned fast-food restaurant in Lansdowne Mall in Richmond, serving a creative mashup of pizza and Indian cuisine — think Butter Chicken pizza, Palak Paneer, and samosas alongside more familiar pies. The kitchen also runs catering and hot lunch programs for local schools and businesses. A touring cyclist stopping in Richmond will find a broad, filling menu with both vegetarian and meat options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian options including Fusion Veggie pizza, Palak Paneer, Chana Masala, and Samosa. Catering page states they 'can accommodate many dietary restrictions and allergies.'

restaurant.name: Capilano Sushi
restaurant.desc: Capilano Sushi is a Japanese restaurant on Marine Drive in North Vancouver serving an extensive menu of hand-crafted rolls, nigiri, sashimi, and teriyaki mains alongside sake and Japanese beer. The restaurant operates an online ordering platform offering both pickup and local delivery. With over 200 customer reviews and a menu spanning everything from simple avocado rolls to specialty craft rolls, it is a well-established neighbourhood dining option for cyclists on the North Shore.

detail.address: 1240 Marine Drive, North Vancouver, BC V7P1T2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian items: Veggie Roll, Veggie Gyoza, Veggie Spring Roll, Veggie Sunomono Salad, Tofu & Avocado Salad, Avocado Roll, Edamame, Yam Fries, and Yam & Avocado Roll, among others. No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Blenz Coffee
restaurant.desc: Blenz Coffee is a BC-based specialty coffee chain founded in 1992, offering hand-crafted espresso drinks, organic whole-leaf teas, protein shakes, and a range of baked goods. The Penticton location is situated inside Cherry Lane Mall, making it a convenient indoor stop for cyclists moving through the South Okanagan. The brand emphasizes premium ingredients including 100% Arabica beans, single-origin chocolate, and organic matcha.

restaurant.name: Scott 96 Pizza
restaurant.desc: Scott's Pizza 96 is a fast-food pizza outlet located in the Fraser Valley corridor of Metro Vancouver. The business operates under a Facebook-only web presence, limiting publicly available information. Touring cyclists in the area may find it a convenient roadside stop, but details about its layout and offerings could not be verified.

restaurant.name: Vassillis Souvlaki Greek Taverna
restaurant.desc: Vassillis Souvlaki Greek Taverna is a Greek restaurant specializing in souvlaki. Located on Kingsway in Vancouver, it serves traditional Greek cuisine.

restaurant.name: Town Square
restaurant.desc: Town Square is a community-focused full-service restaurant, food truck, and off-site catering operation at the centre of Pemberton, BC. The kitchen leans on locally sourced and organic ingredients from the Pemberton Valley, and the brunch menu stands out with eggs Benedict served on house-made bannock topped with house-cured salmon or locally sourced bison. Friday nights bring live music, cementing its role as a genuine gathering place for locals and travellers passing through the valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'we offer Gluten free options, vegetarian and vegan!'

restaurant.name: Hot Pan Pizza
restaurant.desc: Hot Pan Pizza is a multi-location pizza chain with outlets in Richmond, Vancouver, and Surrey, offering hand-crafted pizzas baked in stone ovens using traditional recipes and premium ingredients. The Richmond location on Alexandra Road is one of three BC locations, each offering online ordering and a full menu of classic and specialty pizzas. The business also provides catering services for corporate events, weddings, and private parties.

detail.address: 8531 Alexandra Rd unit 108, Richmond, BC V6X 1C3

restaurant.name: Guu ​with Garlic
restaurant.desc: Guu with Garlic, also known as Guu Robson, is a Japanese izakaya on Vancouver's busy Robson Street and was the second location opened by Guu Izakaya, the chain credited with pioneering izakaya dining in Vancouver. The restaurant's concept centres on garlic-infused takes on classic izakaya dishes — skewers, karaage, sashimi, and shared plates — in a lively evening atmosphere. It is part of Kitanoya Marketing Corp., which operates five locations across Vancouver and Toronto.

restaurant.name: Olympia Pizza
restaurant.desc: Olympia Pizza is a Greek-influenced pizza restaurant on West Broadway offering an extensive menu of specialty and custom pizzas alongside pasta, Greek dishes, and appetizers. The restaurant supports both dine-in and online-order pickup, with in-house delivery also available. Weekly wine specials hint at a neighbourhood dining experience that goes beyond a quick slice.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian pizzas including Aegean (artichoke, tomato, banana pepper, feta), Ambrosia (spinach, feta, onion), and Margherita (cheese and fresh basil). Vegan and GF options not mentioned

restaurant.name: Kinara Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Kinara Indian Cuisine is an authentic Indian restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, specializing in tandoor-cooked dishes such as Butter Chicken, Fish Tikka, and Tandoori Prawn prepared by master chefs using traditional spices and clay tandoor techniques. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the heart of Vancouver. Vegetarian options including Palak Paneer and Crispy Pakora round out a diverse menu celebrating regional Indian culinary heritage.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists multiple vegetarian dishes including Palak Paneer (spinach and paneer cheese), Crispy Pakora (fresh vegetables in gram flour batter), and Mango Lassi; no explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Rudi
restaurant.desc: Rudi is a Victoria restaurant that channels the owner's west coast upbringing and international travels into an evolving, craft-driven menu — described as discovering a personal culinary identity rather than replicating tradition. The restaurant operates both a daytime express concept and evening dinner service, and can host group events for up to 70 guests.

restaurant.name: Thai Corner
restaurant.desc: Thai Corner is a well-established Thai restaurant on Sidney's main commercial strip, blending central and northeastern (I-San) Thai culinary traditions under a chef with over two decades of experience cooking in Thailand and abroad. The restaurant offers a broad menu of curries, spicy salads, stir-fries, and noodles with customizable spice levels, and serves both buffet-style lunch and à la carte dinner. Cyclists passing through Sidney-by-the-sea will find a sit-down meal, takeout, and even free delivery within downtown Sidney.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'We can modify any dish to be vegetarian and/or gluten free' and the dinner page highlights vegetarian dishes specifically

restaurant.name: Holts Café
restaurant.desc: Holts Café is a café affiliated with Holt Renfrew, located on Dunsmuir Street in downtown Vancouver. It offers indoor seating with reservations available, providing a sit-down dining option for cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: Spicy Pro Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Spicy Pro Hot Pot is a hot pot restaurant located in Richmond, BC, a city known for its diverse and high-quality Asian dining scene. Hot pot dining is a communal, table-cooked experience where diners simmer fresh ingredients in a shared broth — a filling option for cyclists refuelling after a ride. The restaurant is located in a multi-unit commercial address on Capstan Way.

restaurant.name: Papa John's
restaurant.desc: Papa John's is a well-known international pizza chain with a location in North Vancouver offering takeout and delivery. The brand emphasizes fresh dough and quality ingredients under its 'Better Ingredients, Better Pizza' promise. Cyclists looking for a quick, hot meal can order for carryout without a drive-through queue.

restaurant.name: Perry's
restaurant.desc: Perry's Pizza and Grill is a long-established Cranbrook restaurant that started in Kimberley's Platzl in 1988 and relocated to Cranbrook in 2004. The menu centres on fresh daily-made dough pizzas, house-made burgers on Kaiser buns, pasta, and salads, with catering and online ordering available. A convenient stop for touring cyclists needing a filling sit-down or takeout meal in central Cranbrook.

detail.address: 408 Cranbrook Street North, Cranbrook, BC, Canada

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists dedicated 'Veggie Pizzas' and 'Veggie Burgers' sections; no GF or vegan claims found

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: This Subway franchise sits on Columbia Avenue in Castlegar and offers the full lineup of Footlong and 6" sandwiches, wraps, and salads alongside breakfast options. It features a drive-through lane and supports multiple ordering modes including in-restaurant dining, curbside pickup, and delivery. A convenient calorie stop for cyclists passing through the Castlegar corridor on a long touring day.

restaurant.name: Tripke Bakery
restaurant.desc: Tripke Bakery is a neighborhood bakery in Kelowna serving baked goods and related food items. As a bakery stop, it offers a place for cyclists to rest and purchase food.

restaurant.name: Café salade de fruits
restaurant.desc: Café salade de fruits is a French bistro tucked into Vancouver's Fairview neighbourhood at the corner of Fir Street and West 7th Avenue. It offers dine-in lunch and dinner service in a neighbourhood-bistro setting. Cyclists riding the nearby Seaside Greenway or the Arbutus Corridor will find it a convenient midday or evening stop for French-inspired cuisine.

restaurant.name: Manchu Wok
restaurant.desc: Manchu Wok is a Canadian Chinese fast food chain that has operated for over 45 years, founded in 1980 and now present in over 80 locations across three countries. This location sits in the food court at Metropolis at Metrotown, one of Metro Vancouver's largest shopping malls. Cyclists can expect quick counter-service combos with choices of rice or noodle base and a variety of wok-fired entrées including vegetable options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu page lists a dedicated 'VEGETABLE ENTREES' section

restaurant.name: Sake Sushi
restaurant.desc: Sake Sushi is a restaurant in Ucluelet, a small gateway community on the west coast of Vancouver Island adjacent to Pacific Rim National Park Reserve — a popular destination for touring cyclists. The OSM record tags the cuisine as Chinese while the name suggests Japanese (sushi), and the business website domain appears to have been abandoned or compromised. Ucluelet has limited dining options, so this establishment could be a valuable stop for cyclists coming off the Broken Group Islands or the Wild Pacific Trail area.

restaurant.name: Pidgin
restaurant.desc: Pidgin is an Asian-French fusion restaurant situated in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, blending the culinary traditions of two distinct food cultures into a single dining experience. It occupies a prominent spot on Carrall Street, a key corridor connecting downtown Vancouver to the seawall cycling network. The restaurant has garnered enough acclaim to announce a future location at Time Out Market Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Best Bite Pizza
restaurant.desc: Best Bite Pizza is a Chilliwack pizzeria that has been serving the community since 1995. The menu spans an extensive range of specialty pizzas — from a Tandoori Masala to a HOT-HONEY — alongside pasta, cheesy fingers, and desserts, making it a substantial food stop for hungry cyclists. Gluten-free crust is available across the menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Gluten free crust available' and lists at least ten distinct vegetarian pizzas under a dedicated Vegetarian menu category

restaurant.name: Britbar
restaurant.desc: Brexit Pub is a pub located in Penticton, BC. Its original standalone website appears to be defunct, and discovery notes suggest a possible rebrand may have occurred. No further details about the venue's character or offerings could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Crêpe & Café
restaurant.desc: Crêpe & Café is a French cuisine spot on West 41st Avenue in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, offering both dine-in and takeaway. Its accessible entrance (wheelchair=yes per OSM) and takeout option make it a plausible quick stop for a cyclist passing through the area. No outdoor seating is noted, so riders would be eating indoors or taking food to go.

restaurant.name: Mr. Dumpling
restaurant.desc: Mr. Dumpling (包好吃) is a Chinese fast food counter in Richmond, BC serving dumplings from a unit inside a larger commercial complex on Westminster Highway. Richmond is one of Canada's premier destinations for authentic Chinese cuisine, and this spot sits within that rich culinary corridor. A touring cyclist looking for a quick, filling bite after riding the flat dyke trails of the Fraser delta would find it a practical and flavourful stop.

restaurant.name: The Fish Man
restaurant.desc: The Fish Man is a restaurant in Richmond offering both indoor and outdoor seating in a smoke-free environment. It provides a casual dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Copa Cafe
restaurant.desc: Copa Cafe is a Hong Kong-style cafe restaurant that has been serving classic Cantonese-Western fusion dishes since 2006. Signature items include baked pork chop on rice, sizzling hot plates, and a coconut-milk curry beef brisket rooted in traditional Hong Kong cafe (cha chaan teng) cooking. The restaurant operates a VIP membership program and rotating seasonal specials, suggesting a loyal local following.

restaurant.name: Marina Bay Cafe
restaurant.desc: Marina Bay Cafe is a Deaf-owned and operated specialty cafe perched on the scenic Esquimalt waterfront in Victoria, offering a creative menu of espresso drinks, tea lattes, smoothies, and toasties sourced from local suppliers including Fernwood Coffee. The cafe was featured on CHEK News for its community story, and staff are encouraged to learn American Sign Language, making it a notably inclusive stop on Victoria's waterfront cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Brunch
restaurant.desc: Brunch is a Mexican-inspired brunch restaurant in Downtown Vancouver's Granville Street corridor, specializing in dishes like chilaquiles, enchiladas suizas, and eggs Benedict made with Mexican-sourced flavors and techniques. The restaurant offers a warm dine-in experience alongside takeout and delivery, making it a flexible stop for those exploring the downtown core. Vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free accommodations are available on request from staff.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'Ask our servers for our vegan/vegetarian/gluten free options'; several menu items are individually marked gluten free

restaurant.name: Belgard Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Belgard Kitchen is a full-service restaurant in Vancouver's Railtown Design District, just east of Gastown, highlighting Canadian ingredients from coast to coast with globally influenced techniques and a drink menu centred on BC wines and craft beer. It operates lunch on weekdays, brunch on weekends, happy hour, and dinner seven nights a week, with private dining spaces available in the Mezzanine and Cellar venues. The same hospitality group runs sister restaurants Havana Vancouver, The Flamingo Room, and Violeté.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu items carry explicit dietary tags: (vg) vegan, (v) vegetarian, (gf) gluten-free, (df) dairy-free. Examples include Margherita pizzette (vg), Dragon Bowl (v, gf, df), and Belgard Greens (vg, gf)

restaurant.name: Jita's Cafe
restaurant.desc: Jita's Cafe is a coffee shop in downtown Golden on 11th Avenue North. It offers internet access and serves as a stopping point for cyclists and visitors to the area.

restaurant.name: TAKO
restaurant.desc: TAKO is a Korean-fusion fast food shop specializing in tacos, burritos, quesadillas, bibimbap bowls, and poutine built around Korean BBQ fillings like bulgogi, spicy pork belly, and BBQ short rib. It sits directly across from Rogers Arena at the Stadium/Chinatown SkyTrain stop, putting it squarely on Vancouver's inner-harbour cycling corridor. The outdoor patio makes it a natural drop-in stop for cyclists exploring the nearby seawall.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegetarian options across all menu categories: Veggie Taco (Kimchi & Tofu), Vegetable burrito, Vegetable bibimbap, Veggie Quesadilla, Vegetable poutine; no gluten-free options mentioned

restaurant.name: Smile Chicken
restaurant.desc: Smile Chicken is a Korean fast-casual restaurant in downtown Victoria specializing in Korean-style fried chicken and corndogs alongside sides like kimchi and pickled radish. Located in a unit at 1001 Douglas St, it offers online ordering with a 15-minute pickup window, making it a quick stop for cyclists passing through the city centre. With 53 customer reviews, it has established a following for its corndog and seasoned chicken offerings.

detail.address: 1001 Douglas St G12, Victoria, BC V8W2C5

restaurant.name: Pizza Rubato Napoletana
restaurant.desc: Pizza Rubato Napoletana is a Neo-Neapolitan pizzeria on West Broadway that takes its name from the musical concept of 'tempo rubato' — staying rooted in 300-year-old Neapolitan tradition while freely riffing on ingredients and flavour combinations. The kitchen uses imported Italian '00' flour, a 48-hour fermentation process, and an AVPN-approved Valoriani oven that replicates a wood-fired experience, producing a crispy, charred crust. Cyclists heading along the Broadway corridor will find an extensive creative menu alongside catering and events services.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated Verdure (vegetable) section with multiple meatless pizzas: Margherita, Verde Noce, Rucola, Patate al Forno, Funghi Tartufo, Rossa Verdure, Quattro Formaggi, Pesto Spinaci, Ricotta con Aglio. No explicit vegan or gluten-free labelling found

restaurant.name: Charqui Grill
restaurant.desc: Charqui is a gastropub and resto-bar that has anchored the Kitsilano neighbourhood since 2007, known for its wings, craft beer selection, and lively entertainment programming including live music and karaoke. It sits on Cornwall Avenue, close to the popular Kitsilano Beach cycling corridor along the Vancouver waterfront. Indoor and outdoor seating are both available.

restaurant.name: Fol Épi Bakery
restaurant.desc: Fol Épi is an organic bakery and cafe established in 2009 in Victoria, BC, whose name means 'crazy wheat head' — an homage to French baking tradition and wild yeast cultures. Operating out of Dockside Green, they stone-grind their own flour on-site and produce artisan breads, all-butter viennoiserie, seasonal pastries, and daily sandwiches using local, small-scale producers. It is a well-established community fixture that also supplies other local businesses.

detail.address: 398 Harbour Rd #101, Victoria, BC V9A 0B7, Canada

restaurant.name: Fuego
restaurant.desc: Fuego Old Town Eatery is a lively, rustic Mexican-style brunch spot established in 2015 in Victoria's historic Old Town neighbourhood. It serves a creative all-day breakfast and lunch menu featuring chorizo, pulled pork, eggs benedict, chilaquiles, and house-made cornbread on a first-come, first-served basis. Its location on Store Street puts it squarely in the heart of Victoria's waterfront cycling corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items note 'Vegetarian option available', including the Original Eggs Benedict and Spanish Omelette

restaurant.name: Wise Club & Hall
restaurant.desc: The WISE Hall is a storied East Vancouver institution founded in 1957 as a social club for Welsh, Irish, Scottish, and English immigrants, now a 250-capacity concert venue with a rich history of Canadian performers gracing its stage. The downstairs Lounge is a classic cash-only neighborhood pub with pool table and darts, operating as a members-and-guests club open to anyone 19+ with valid ID. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a genuinely local hangout steeped in community history, steps from the Adanac cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Shelter
restaurant.desc: Shelter Waterfront is a long-running Tofino dining institution first opened in 2003, relocated in 2022 to a scenic waterfront home at the Tofino Resort and Marina after a fire destroyed the original location. The restaurant celebrates locally sourced West Coast ingredients — including fresh-shucked Vancouver Island oysters and locally caught salmon — served in an open-concept space with natural wood finishes and a patio overlooking the Tofino Inlet and Clayoquot Sound. It operates as a full-service café through dinner service and is a well-known gathering place for both locals and visitors passing through Tofino.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page features a dedicated 'gluten guide' section, indicating gluten-free options are available

restaurant.name: Zubu
restaurant.desc: ZUBU is a Japanese ramen restaurant with four Lower Mainland locations, with this downtown Vancouver outpost opening in January 2023. The menu, helmed by Executive Chef William Cao (a graduate of Kitchen Hyodo Ramen School in Oyama, Japan), centres on ramen made with locally sourced and Japanese-imported ingredients, alongside temaki, hand-made gyoza, and rice bowls. A full cocktail program rounds out the experience.

restaurant.name: Blooming Spice Fish House
restaurant.desc: Blooming Spice Fish House is a Sichuan-style restaurant specialising in its signature 'boiling fish' — black fish slices doused tableside in two pounds of scorching hot oil loaded with chili and Sichuan peppercorns sourced directly from China. The dish follows a 30-year-old recipe, and the menu extends to cold jelly noodles, spicy frog, and dry-pot dishes. This is the chain's sole BC location, situated in a commercial complex in central Richmond.

detail.address: 8368 Capstan Way, Unit 1318, Richmond, BC V6X4B6

restaurant.name: Cafe Bel
restaurant.desc: Bel Café is a patisserie café located within the Rosewood Hotel Georgia, a beautifully restored 1927 heritage landmark in downtown Vancouver. Operated by the Hawksworth Restaurant group, it serves handcrafted drinks, fresh pastries, and light fare including soups, sandwiches, and salads. The refined lobby-café setting provides a distinctive midday stop for cyclists passing through Vancouver's downtown core.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes soups, sandwiches, and salads consistent with vegetarian options

restaurant.name: Small Block Lounge
restaurant.desc: Small Block Brewery is a small-batch craft brewery in the Cowichan Valley specializing in hand-crafted British Ales brewed with locally sourced BC ingredients. The taproom cultivates a cozy 'garage' atmosphere where visitors can enjoy tasters, pints, or fill a growler for the road. Wood-fired pizza is available on weekends alongside snacks, making it a worthwhile stop on a Cowichan Valley ride.

detail.address: 203 - 5301 Chaster Road, Cowichan Valley, BC V9L 6T7

restaurant.name: Social
restaurant.desc: Social is a full-service restaurant and bar on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most bicycle-friendly streets and a hub of the local cycling community. The venue features a street-level dining room and a rooftop patio, making it a lively spot for a sit-down meal after a ride. Reservations are accepted downstairs while the rooftop operates on a first-come, first-served basis.

restaurant.name: Boston Pizza
restaurant.desc: Boston Pizza Big Bend is a full-service Canadian casual dining chain restaurant and sports bar located in the Big Bend area of Burnaby. Founded by a Greek immigrant in Edmonton in 1964, it is now Canada's largest casual dining brand with hundreds of locally owned franchise locations. The Big Bend location offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery with a broad menu spanning pizzas, pastas, wings, burgers, and more.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'Vegan and Glutenwise® options also available'; GlutenWise® items are listed throughout the nutritional information page

restaurant.name: Cilantro & Jalapeño
restaurant.desc: Cilantro & Jalapeño is a multi-award-winning authentic Mexican takeout restaurant inside Lonsdale Quay Market on North Vancouver's waterfront, voted Best Mexican Restaurant on the North Shore six consecutive years (2010–2015). The kitchen produces scratch-made tacos, tamales, enchiladas, burritos, and house sauces using traditional recipes, alongside a retail selection of hard-to-find Latin American specialty ingredients. The market location sits steps from the SeaBus terminal, making it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists travelling between downtown Vancouver and the North Shore.

detail.address: 123 Carrie Cates Court, North Vancouver, BC V7M 3K7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Chipotle Veggies' as a protein choice for tacos, burritos, monster burritos, and other dishes, confirming vegetarian options are available

restaurant.name: Simply Pho
restaurant.desc: Simply Pho is a family-owned Vietnamese restaurant in Tsawwassen offering an extensive menu of authentic pho varieties alongside classic appetizers like spring rolls, salad rolls, and calamari. The restaurant is located in the Canoe Pass Way retail complex near the Tsawwassen Mills area, making it a convenient sit-down meal stop for cyclists riding the South Delta region. It is one of the few Vietnamese dining options in this part of the Lower Mainland.

detail.address: 1608-4949 Canoe Pass Way, Tsawwassen, BC V4M 0B2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Phở rau cải' (seasonal vegetables with rice noodles in beef broth) as a non-meat option, though the beef broth means full vegetarian/vegan status cannot be. No gluten-free options mentioned

restaurant.name: Uptown Pizza
restaurant.desc: Uptown Pizza is a sit-down pizza and Italian restaurant offering an unusually broad menu spanning classic and specialty pizzas, stuffed pastas, seafood dishes, wings, burgers, and more. The restaurant has both indoor and outdoor seating and accepts online orders for pickup and delivery. Its extensive menu makes it a substantial refuelling stop for cyclists seeking a full meal rather than a quick snack.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian Pizza' section and vegetarian appetizer options such as Veg Root Medley and Zucchini Sticks

restaurant.name: Kami Pizza
restaurant.desc: Kami Pizza is a pizza fast food establishment in Kamloops on Tranquille Road. It provides a casual food option for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Nemesis Coffee
restaurant.desc: Nemesis Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster and multi-location café group based in Metro Vancouver, with this Surrey 'Pavilion' branch serving espresso and filter coffee sourced from named farms and individual producers. Pastries from their in-house Dope Bakehouse label — including croissants and pain au chocolat — round out the menu. The company roasts its own beans and is a proud supporter of World Coffee Research, signalling a genuine craft-roaster ethos rather than a commodity café.

restaurant.name: La Cantina
restaurant.desc: La Cantina (branded online as Tacos La Cantina) is an authentic Mexican taqueria founded by Pepe Barajas, inspired by the street-food culture of Mexico. The Nesters Plaza location operates as a takeout and delivery outlet, offering tacos, burritos, quesadillas, and margaritas with a strong emphasis on dietary inclusivity. It has built a local reputation as Whistler's best taqueria, with delivery available through Skip the Dishes, DoorDash, and Uber Eats.

notes.Takeout: Website explicitly designates the Nesters Plaza location as 'Pickup only' with online ordering via the website, Skip the Dishes, DoorDash, and Uber Eats
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'extensive variety of GLUTEN-FREE, DAIRY FREE, VEGAN, VEGETARIAN OPTIONS'; specific items include Vegan Chili Beans taco and Cauliflower taco

restaurant.name: Yu Xiang Yuan Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Yu Xiang Yuan Restaurant is a Chinese cuisine spot on Fraser Street in Vancouver, specializing in regional dishes spanning Szechuan, Northern Chinese, and Xinjiang traditions. The menu features hand-pulled and dragging noodles, steamed dumplings, cumin lamb kabobs, and classic stir-fries like Ginger Beef and Kung Pao Chicken. Online ordering is available through their website, offering a convenient stop option for cyclists fueling up on a long urban route.

restaurant.name: Foodies On Board
restaurant.desc: Foodies on Board is a chef-driven dine-in and takeout restaurant in Burnaby's Production Way corridor, built around an ever-changing weekly menu sourced directly from local BC farmers and cooperatives. Chef Ken's all-day brunch program features house-baked pastries, organic eggs from Rabbit River Farm, and nitrate-free smoked bacon, paired with Lavazza espresso drinks. Beyond the restaurant, the business also runs a catering service and a weekend meal prep program offering a wide range of dietary options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQs page explicitly lists 'vegetarian, vegan, keto, gluten-free, paleo, and more' as dietary options in the meal prep service

restaurant.name: The Black Forest Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A family-owned German restaurant established in 1975, The Black Forest sits on the Esplanade in Harrison Hot Springs overlooking Harrison Lake, about 10 km off Highway 1. It specialises in authentic schnitzel, pork hock, bratwurst, and housemade spaetzle, and is widely regarded as one of the area's standout dining destinations. A heated patio with lake views makes it a rewarding stop after a day on the bike.

detail.address: 180 Esplanade Ave, Harrison Hot Springs, BC V0M 1K0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Lunch menu lists 'Vegetarian Pasta (Alfredo Sauce)' and 'Home Made Veggie Burger'; wines/beer menu lists gluten-free beer options including 'Whistler Forager Glutten Free Lager'

restaurant.name: Peqish
restaurant.desc: Peqish is a walk-in fast food restaurant on Seymour Street in downtown Vancouver. The business does not operate a drive-through service. It provides quick-service dining for area visitors and locals.

restaurant.name: Drip Coffee Social
restaurant.desc: Drip Coffee Social is a community-focused café established in 2018 on the Departure Bay waterfront in Nanaimo, offering indoor seating, a patio, and a sandy beach directly across the street. The menu spans specialty espresso drinks, grain bowls, sandwiches, and baked goods alongside beer, wine, and seasonal cocktails. A second location operates on Dufferin Crescent, but the Departure Bay outpost is the standout cycling stop given its beachside setting.

detail.address: 100 - 2835 Departure Bay Rd, Nanaimo, BC V9S 3X1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Roasted Veggie sandwich, Avocado Toast, Roast Chickpea Kale Salad, and Harvest Salad (vegetarian options), plus Gluten Free Brownie and Gluten Free Shortbread

restaurant.name: Browns Socialhouse
restaurant.desc: Browns Socialhouse is a restaurant in the North Vancouver town centre. It offers a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Woo Korean BBQ
restaurant.desc: Woo Korean BBQ is a table-grill Korean BBQ restaurant in South Surrey emphasizing fresh premium Canadian meats alongside seafood and traditional Korean dishes. It bills itself as Greater Vancouver's best Korean BBQ spot and offers a broad menu ranging from beef BBQ courses to dolsot bibimbap and stews. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a sit-down, full-service meal suited to refuelling after a long ride.

restaurant.name: Cream Pony
restaurant.desc: Cream Pony is a casual counter-service spot on Main Street in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood specializing in fried chicken and donuts, with a second location in North Vancouver's Shipyard District. The shop has built a loyal following for its glazed donuts and juicy chicken sandwiches. It also offers catering and is available through major delivery platforms.

restaurant.name: Pacific Poke
restaurant.desc: Pacific Poke is a chef-driven, quick-serve poke restaurant chain founded in Vancouver by two food-passionate entrepreneurs who discovered Hawaiian poke in California and brought a fresh West Coast spin to it. The menu features build-your-own poke bowls with locally-sourced ingredients alongside chef-inspired signature bowls, emphasizing responsible sourcing and sustainability. The brand has expanded to multiple BC and Alberta locations, making it a recognizable stop for cyclists passing through Vancouver's West Broadway corridor.

restaurant.name: The Keg
restaurant.desc: The Keg Steakhouse + Bar is a well-known Canadian steakhouse chain with a recently renovated Abbotsford location situated just off Highway 1 at Sumas Way. The restaurant features a full lounge and bar with televisions, a semi-private dining room, and patio seating, making it a comfortable stop for a sit-down meal after a long day in the saddle. Free parking and wheelchair accessibility round out the practical amenities at this location.

detail.address: 2142 West Railway Street, Abbotsford, BC V2S 2E2

restaurant.name: Landmark Hot Pot House
restaurant.desc: Landmark Hot Pot House is a restaurant specializing in hot pot cuisine on Cambie Street in Vancouver. It features indoor seating and operates daily for dinner service, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking a meal. The restaurant offers a communal dining experience where diners cook ingredients in a shared broth at their table.

restaurant.name: The Old Spaghetti Factory
restaurant.desc: The Old Spaghetti Factory is a 100% Canadian-owned chain Italian restaurant with a New Westminster location on Eighth Street, offering multi-course pasta meals made with locally-sourced ingredients where possible. The restaurant is a full-service sit-down establishment with indoor seating and no outdoor patio. It is one of 15 locations across Canada and can accommodate a range of dietary needs including gluten-free, vegan, and allergen requests.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: "Gluten Free? Vegan? Allergy? We got you. Our menu is adaptable to accommodate many different dietary needs."

restaurant.name: La Ruota
restaurant.desc: La Ruota Pizzeria is a Neapolitan-inspired pizza franchise with four Metro Vancouver locations, cooking its pies in a 900°F oven using authentic Caputo '00' flour and fresh ingredients sourced from Italy and BC. The West Broadway location sits on one of Vancouver's primary east-west cycling corridors and offers a broad menu spanning meat and veggie pizzas, sandwiches, pastas, and antipasti. The restaurant operates a franchise model with online ordering, delivery, and a loyalty rewards program.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'Veggie Pizzas' as a distinct menu category alongside meat pizzas

restaurant.name: Crafted Street Food
restaurant.desc: A street food vendor specializing in waffles operating in Kelowna. Offers quick takeaway meals ideal for cyclists seeking a casual roadside stop.

restaurant.name: C Market Coffee
restaurant.desc: C Market Coffee takes its name from the global commodity exchange where Arabica coffee is traded, and the Port Coquitlam location is part of a growing BC chain that roasts micro-lot beans in-house and pairs them with fresh, thoughtfully crafted food in a design-forward space. Beyond espresso drinks, the café offers matcha, loose-leaf tea, coffee classes, pop-up markets, and room rental, functioning as a genuine community hub rather than just a quick-stop café. Cyclists will find a full food menu with published nutrition and allergen guides, and a mobile app for ordering ahead.

detail.address: 820 Village Drive Unit 110, Port Coquitlam, BC V3B 0G9

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A two-storey McDonald's location in Delta, BC offering drive-through, takeaway, and outdoor seating. As a full-service fast food restaurant on 56 Street, it serves as a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. The national rewards app offers app-exclusive deals that can be useful on longer rides.

restaurant.name: The Salty Caramel Kitchen
restaurant.desc: The Salty Caramel Kitchen is a fully plant-based bakery and cafe just off Okanagan Lake in Lake Country, serving breakfast, lunch, baked goods, and specialty coffees. Started in 2016 as a home-based vegan cake business, it opened its brick-and-mortar shop in 2018 and has built a loyal following for plant-based food that appeals well beyond the vegan crowd. The cafe's relaxed beach vibe and proximity to Pebble Beach make it a natural stop for cyclists on the Okanagan Centre road.

detail.address: 11407 Okanagan Centre Road West, Lake Country, BC V4V 2J6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website describes a 'fully plant-based menu' (vegan and vegetarian by definition); gluten-aware products offered but kitchen carries high cross-contamination risk for gluten, nuts, soy, and other allergens

restaurant.name: Waterfront Wines Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Waterfront Wines Restaurant is a multiple-award-winning fine dining destination on Kelowna's Okanagan Lake waterfront, recognized as the 'Best Okanagan Restaurant' by Vancouver Magazine twelve consecutive years running. Chef-Sommelier Mark Filatow builds seasonal menus around a curated network of Okanagan producers — Ocean Wise seafood, heritage proteins, foraged mushrooms, and organic produce — paired with a cellar of over 300 local and international wines. A touring cyclist looking for a celebratory dinner will find inventive, ingredient-driven plates in an approachable waterfront setting.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Vegan Beluga Lentil Cakes' as a main course; multiple starters (hummus, asparagus salad, burrata) are vegetarian-compatible

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: A Starbucks Coffee location in Langley, BC, offering the full range of espresso drinks, cold refreshers, and grab-and-go food items. With outdoor seating and free Wi-Fi, it serves as a comfortable mid-ride rest stop in the city. As a corporate chain location, cyclists can expect consistent service and indoor facilities.

restaurant.name: Viva Mexicana
restaurant.desc: Viva Mexicana is an authentic Mexican restaurant founded by Carmen Ruiz, who set out to bring traditional flavours from scratch-made dishes to the Okanagan, opening in Lake Country during the pandemic and later adding a second Vernon location. The restaurant serves a broad menu of tacos, burritos, enchiladas, tamales, and seasonal specials like Sunday pozole, alongside a Mexican grocery section where cyclists can pick up authentic ingredients to go. It sits on Highway 97, a primary cycling corridor through the central Okanagan.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'soy meat' as a protein substitute across tacos, burritos, enchiladas, and other dishes; multiple items are marked '(GF)' or '(GF Option)' throughout the menu

restaurant.name: Gozen Sushi Bar Izakaya
restaurant.desc: Gozen Sushi Bar Izakaya is a Japanese-style sushi bar and izakaya in downtown Victoria, located on Langley Street. An izakaya offers a casual dining experience centred on shared plates and drinks, typical of Japanese gastropub culture. Touring cyclists finishing a ride in the city centre would find it a natural stop for a sit-down meal in the heart of Victoria.

restaurant.name: Pâtisserie Lebeau
restaurant.desc: Founded in 1995 by Belgian-trained pastry chef Olivier Lebeau, this patisserie specializes in authentic Liège and Bruxelles waffles, rice pies, craquelins, and speculoos made fresh daily from natural ingredients. Located on West 2nd Avenue near the Arbutus Greenway, it sits along a popular Vancouver cycling corridor. The shop has been a proud multi-year waffle sponsor of Ride to Conquer Cancer and a supplier for Tour de Cure, giving it a genuine footprint in the local cycling community.

restaurant.name: Big Way Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Big Way Hot Pot Olympic Village is part of a rapidly expanding BC-based self-serve hot pot chain offering over 100 fresh ingredients and more than 18 broths and dry mixes, including signature Mala and slow-simmered Collagen Bone Broth options. Located in the Olympic Village neighbourhood near Vancouver's seawall cycling routes, it offers a customizable, hearty sit-down meal format where each diner cooks ingredients in their own individual pot. The chain has grown to include locations across Metro Vancouver, Ontario, and the United States.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Tomato Broth listing explicitly states '*Vegan Option Available*'; no gluten-free claims found

restaurant.name: Score
restaurant.desc: Score on Davie is a long-running sports bar and pub that has operated in Vancouver's West End since 2007, earning multiple 'Best of Vancouver' awards. Known for its Caesar cocktails and a comfort-food menu of wings, burgers, and deep-fried snacks, it draws a lively crowd from the surrounding neighbourhood. The bar has both indoor and outdoor seating and a no-smoking policy.

restaurant.name: Taco Nori
restaurant.desc: Taco Nori is a fast-casual fusion concept inside downtown Vancouver's Bentall Centre, serving nori tacos made with deep-fried seaweed shells filled with fresh sushi-style ingredients like Atlantic salmon, ahi tuna, and avocado. The concept originated at the Richmond Night Market in 2018 under the name Nori Express and expanded to a fleet of three food trucks and a trailer before opening its first permanent storefront. It sits along the busy Burrard Street corridor, making it a quick and inventive lunch stop for cyclists moving through the financial district.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Wakame Nori Taco explicitly labeled '*VEGETARIAN' on the online menu

restaurant.name: Halibut House Chinese Food
restaurant.desc: Halibut House is a family-owned and operated Cantonese restaurant in Victoria, BC, well regarded locally for its warm, kid-friendly atmosphere in a small but comfortable dining room. The kitchen cooks with no MSG added and is happy to accommodate allergies, dietary restrictions, and gluten-free or wheat-free needs. Both dine-in (reservation recommended) and takeout/pickup are available, making it a practical stop for a touring cyclist looking for a hot meal.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'order meals to take out' and lists a pickup service; about page confirms 'Come dine in with us or order meals to take out. We do not offer delivery services.'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'We are more than happy to accommodate any allergies, dietary restrictions, gluten-free or wheat-free needs and so on.'

restaurant.name: Sailor Hägar's
restaurant.desc: Sailor Hägar's is a neighbourhood brew pub in North Vancouver offering views of Vancouver Harbour and the city skyline, with a rotating selection of craft beers on tap alongside a full pub menu of burgers, wings, fish and chips, and more. The pub is known as one of the only spots on the North Shore staying open until 2am on weekends, and hosts regular karaoke nights, themed parties, live music, and sports viewing. An attached liquor store adds convenience for cyclists stocking up before a ride.

restaurant.name: Indian Essence Bistro
restaurant.desc: Indian Essence Bistro is an authentic Indian restaurant in Fort St. John, BC, where a chef with experience in India's 5-star hotels serves an extensive menu of meat and vegetarian dishes in an elegant dining room suited to intimate dinners or group events. The menu spans tandoori grills, biryanis, curries, and a full vegetarian selection. Online ordering and local food delivery are also available.

detail.address: 10123 100 Street, Fort St. John, BC V1J 3Y6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated 'Vegetarian Menu' section on website with numerous dishes including Aloo Gobi, Dal Makhani, Channa Masala, Saag Paneer, Malai Kofta, and more

restaurant.name: Cantonese BBQ Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Cantonese BBQ Seafood Restaurant is an authentic Cantonese eatery on Kingsway in east Vancouver, specializing in BBQ meats alongside an extensive menu of noodle dishes, fried rice, and seafood. It is part of a small two-location chain (Vancouver and Richmond) and offers online ordering with in-store pickup. Touring cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor will find a wide-ranging lunch and dinner menu covering everything from quick single-item BBQ-over-rice plates to large combination banquet sets.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Buddha's Feast Chow Mein 羅漢齋炒麵', a traditional Buddhist vegetarian dish, confirming at least one vegetarian option

restaurant.name: Monzo Burger
restaurant.desc: Monzo Burger is a smashburger restaurant located in Vancouver House on Granville Street, inspired by the 1980s Milanese youth movement known as the 'Paninari.' The menu centres on house-ground Canadian beef smash patties, hand-made chicken cutlets, beef-tallow fries, and soft serve gelato, alongside a custom Italian-style pilsner brewed in collaboration with Ravens Brewing. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a full sit-down meal with online ordering and a vegetarian burger option.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'BIG LEGUME (V) House-made veggie patty' explicitly labelled vegetarian

restaurant.name: Japanese Village Teppan Steak & Seafood House
restaurant.desc: Japanese Village is a long-established teppanyaki restaurant in downtown Victoria where personal chefs cook steak and seafood on a searing iron grill right at the table — part culinary performance, part dinner. Voted Best Japanese Restaurant in Victoria since 1994 by Black Press Media readers, the restaurant features an extensive sake and cocktail bar alongside its signature teppan dinners. Takeout is available by phone, and a dedicated children's menu makes it a flexible option for touring groups stopping in the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Teppan menu lists 'Tofu Steak' described as 'lavished with our spicy, vegan-friendly sauce'

restaurant.name: Lennox Pub
restaurant.desc: Lennox Pub is a neighbourhood pub at 800 Granville Street in the heart of Vancouver's entertainment district. It offers both indoor and outdoor seating in a smoke-free space and is wheelchair accessible, making it a welcoming mid-ride stop for cyclists moving through downtown. Card payments are accepted.

restaurant.name: Aling Ening Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Aling Ening is a Filipino restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver. The venue serves as a meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Rosemary Rocksalt
restaurant.desc: Rosemary Rocksalt is a Montreal-style bagel shop on Vancouver's cycling-friendly Commercial Drive, hand-rolling and stone-baking honey-boiled bagels fresh each day in an open-flame hearth oven. The menu spans breakfast sandwiches, deli-style bagel sandwiches using wild BC sockeye salmon and Montreal smoked meat, and take-home dozens — making it a practical fuelling or stocking-up stop mid-ride. The shop operates three Metro Vancouver locations, with the Commercial Drive outpost sitting at the heart of one of the city's busiest cycling corridors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes vegetarian sandwiches (North Shore: garden veggie cream cheese, lettuce, tomato, cucumber, green pepper), vegan cashew cream cheese (Classic, Death by Garlic, Jalapeño Cheddar), Butternut Squash Soup labelled 'Vegetarian & Gluten Free', Broccoli Cheddar Soup labelled 'Vegetarian', and an 'Almost Gluten Free' bagel variety

restaurant.name: 5th Street Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: 5th Street is a neighbourhood pub and full-service restaurant in Victoria's Quadra Village, built around a wood-fired rotisserie and stone-oven pizza program alongside a broad scratch kitchen menu. The pub side hosts regular community events including Monday trivia nights and Thursday music bingo, giving it a genuinely local feel beyond the tourist circuit. Cyclists will find dine-in, takeout, and weekend brunch all available under one roof.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Gluten-free flatbread option listed for spinach & artichoke dip; vegetarian dishes include Veggie Breakfast Hash, House Salad, Brussel Sprouts, Fruit and Waffles, and Burrito Breakfast Bowl

restaurant.name: Freshii
restaurant.desc: Freshii is a Canadian-founded fast-casual chain specializing in salads, wraps, bowls, and burritos aimed at health-conscious diners. This unit is located at 2325 Ottawa Street in Port Coquitlam. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a quick, customizable meal option in a suburban retail setting.

restaurant.name: Le Coq Frit
restaurant.desc: Le Coq Frit is a Vancouver fried chicken eatery that opened on West Broadway in 2021, offering hand-battered chicken in Korean-inspired preparations (Nashville Hot, Black Soy, Sweet & Spicy) alongside signature brioche bun burgers and croissant waffles. The restaurant has a sustainability focus, using recyclable non-woven bags in place of plastic. It has a second location in North Vancouver's Lonsdale Quay.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes vegetarian-compatible sides (fries, onion rings, cole slaw, yam fries, corn salad) though no explicit vegetarian mains are flagged

restaurant.name: Akihana Sushi
restaurant.desc: Akihana Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Vancouver's Davie Street offering both dine-in and online takeout service. It provides a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists in an urban neighborhood, with the option to order ahead. The restaurant features indoor seating.

restaurant.name: Kuroki Kaiseki Omakase Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Kuroki Kaiseki Omakase Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant in Richmond's Chatham Street area specializing in kaiseki-style omakase dining, a multi-course format curated entirely by the chef. Omakase restaurants typically offer an intimate, counter-style experience that can be a memorable stop for a touring cyclist seeking a distinctive meal in Metro Vancouver's food-rich Richmond district.

restaurant.name: In Er G Plant Alchemy
restaurant.desc: In Er G Plant Alchemy is a Victoria-based raw, plant-based wellness shop specializing in cold-pressed juices, smoothies, health shots, cleanses, nut milks, and raw food. All products are 100% vegan, gluten-free, and made without artificial colours, flavours, or preservatives. The business operates as a pick-up and delivery service, making it a convenient stop for cyclists seeking nutrient-dense, whole-food refreshments in the downtown Victoria area.

notes.Takeout: Website banner states 'Order for Pick-Up or Delivery — Minimum 50$ Order Required for Free Delivery in the Victoria Area', confirming pick-up (takeout) is available
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website repeatedly states '100% RAW GLUTEN-FREE VEGAN MADE WITH NON-GMO INGREDIENTS'

restaurant.name: CRAFT Beer Market
restaurant.desc: CRAFT Beer Market English Bay is a multi-level restaurant and bar perched directly on the seawall, with a heated rooftop patio overlooking English Bay beach and floor-to-ceiling windows throughout. Part of a Canadian chain rooted in the craft beer movement, it pours a broad selection of craft beers alongside a menu of fresh, locally sourced food. Its beachside location on Beach Avenue puts it squarely on one of Vancouver's busiest recreational cycling corridors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page includes a dedicated 'Plant Based & Vegetarian' section and individual items explicitly labeled Vegan, Vegetarian, and Gluten Aware throughout all menu categories

restaurant.name: Famoso Pizzaria
restaurant.desc: Famoso Italian Pizzeria + Bar is a Canadian chain specializing in authentic Neapolitan-style pizzas fired in an imported Italian bell-shaped oven at 900°F for 90 seconds. The Ladner location is a full sit-down pizzeria and bar in Delta, offering a broad menu of pizzas, pastas, salads, and sandwiches with vegetarian and vegan options. Delivery is available through Skip the Dishes, DoorDash, and Uber Eats, and take-out can be ordered online.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu confirms with a dedicated 'Vegetarian Appetizers' section and a vegetarian menu filter on the Ladner menu page

restaurant.name: Troller Ale House
restaurant.desc: The Troller Ale House is a storied Horseshoe Bay institution with roots going back to 1977, holding the distinction of being the first pub in Canada to serve micro-brewed beer since Prohibition — pouring Bay Ale from Horseshoe Bay Brewing in 1982. Situated steps from the BC Ferries terminal, it serves as a natural waypoint for touring cyclists heading to Vancouver Island, the Sunshine Coast, or Bowen Island, offering a wide selection of BC craft draught beers and full pub-kitchen fare. Large windows face the ferry terminal, giving the space a relaxed, unhurried atmosphere suited to a longer break between legs of a journey.

detail.address: 6342 Bay Street West Vancouver, BC V7W 2G9

notes.Takeout: Website states: 'Kitchen open for dine in and take-out. Daily 11am-10pm'

restaurant.name: Deacon's Corner
restaurant.desc: Deacon's Corner is a southern-style comfort food restaurant that has anchored the Gastown neighbourhood since 2009, inspired by a truck stop diner on the Trans-Canada Highway outside Winnipeg. The menu leans heavily on hearty all-day breakfast dishes — fried chicken, eggs every style, biscuits, hash bowls, and bennys — made in-house from scratch with generous portions. The restaurant describes itself as a 'perfect pit stop for explorers,' and its brunch-focused format suits a mid-ride refuel well.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists vegetarian options including Veggie scramble (mushrooms, peppers, onions, cheddar, spinach), Veggie hash bowl, and Avocado Toast. No explicit vegan or gluten-free labelling found

restaurant.name: Sushi Village
restaurant.desc: Sushi Village is a landmark Japanese restaurant in Whistler Village that has been serving sushi, sashimi, and Japanese cuisine since December 1985, making it one of the earliest restaurants in the resort town. Founded by three friends who moved to Whistler to ski and never left, it has grown into a beloved local institution known for its warm service and often boisterous atmosphere. The restaurant offers an extensive menu including gluten-free and vegetarian options, with both dine-in and phone-in takeout available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists a dedicated 'GLUTEN FREE / VEGETARIAN MENU Available nightly from 5pm'; menu items include vegetable gyoza and Pete's Beet Roll (vegan-friendly)

restaurant.name: Gokudo Shabu Shabu Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Gokudo Shabu Shabu is a Japanese-Taiwanese fusion hot pot restaurant where diners cook thinly sliced meats and fresh vegetables in simmering broth at their own table. The restaurant offers 17 unique soup bases — including Sukiyaki, Satay, and Spicy Mix — alongside house-crafted sauces developed by the founder's family. A value combo meal with soup, main, sides, vegetables, sauce, beverage, and dessert makes it a substantial stop for hungry cyclists passing through Burnaby.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'We also offer a vegetarian broth to satisfy all tastes.'

restaurant.name: Best Bite Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Best Bite Indian Cuisine is a Richmond restaurant specializing in authentic Indian cooking, with dishes prepared using traditional tandoor ovens and classic regional recipes. The menu spans a wide range from street food appetizers like Papdi Chaat and Pani-Puri to hearty mains including Chicken Biryani, Lamb Shank with Pulao, and an extensive vegetarian selection. Takeout and delivery are available alongside dine-in, making it a practical stop for cyclists seeking a substantial meal near the south Richmond waterfront.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Extensive vegetarian options confirmed on menu: Palak Paneer, Paneer Pakora, Veggie Platter, Spinach Naan, Vegetable Samosa, Pani-Puri. No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Soul Sweet Cafe & 250 Pizza
restaurant.desc: Soul Sweet Cafe & 250 Pizza is a combined café and pizza shop on 100 Avenue in Fort St. John, BC, serving both coffee drinks and pizza under one roof. It offers takeout service, making it a potential refueling stop for cyclists passing through the Peace River region of northeastern BC. The '250' in the name is a nod to the local BC telephone area code, signalling a local identity.

restaurant.name: Nikko Sushi
restaurant.desc: Nikko Sushi is a sushi restaurant located in a strip-mall unit on South Fraser Way in Chilliwack, BC. It offers a cuisine style consistent with Japanese sushi and sashimi. For touring cyclists passing through Chilliwack, it would serve as a sit-down meal stop on a major through-route.

detail.address: Unit 12, 33324 South Fraser Way, Chilliwack, BC V2S 2B4

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: McDonald's in Richmond, BC is a drive-through and takeout fast food outlet serving burgers, chicken sandwiches, and McCafé beverages as part of the national chain. The menu spans breakfast, mains, snacks, and desserts including seasonal items, and the location participates in the MyMcDonald's Rewards app loyalty program. No address is recorded in OSM for this specific node, limiting its usefulness as a directory entry without further verification.

detail.address: 7120 Number 3 Rd, Richmond, BC V6Y 2C6, Canada

restaurant.name: Chang'an
restaurant.desc: Chang'an is a fine-dining Chinese restaurant on Vancouver's Granville Street corridor, specializing in Shaanxi cuisine inspired by the ancient capital city from which it takes its name. The restaurant describes itself as a 'Miniature Cultural Museum,' with décor and dishes rooted in the philosophy and heritage of thirteen Chinese dynasties. Skilled chefs present traditional Shaanxi flavours with contemporary plating techniques, making it a destination for diners seeking an immersive cultural meal experience.

restaurant.name: The Chairman's Room Lounge & Buffet
restaurant.desc: The Chairman's Room Lounge & Buffet is a sit-down lounge and buffet restaurant located inside the River Rock Casino Resort in Richmond, BC. The resort sits on the Fraser River and is operated by Great Canadian Entertainment, one of Canada's largest casino and hospitality companies. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a full-service dining experience in an upscale casino-resort environment close to the riverfront.

restaurant.name: Kien Giang Pho
restaurant.desc: A Vietnamese pho restaurant in Sechelt. A casual dining option for cyclists seeking a warm meal while passing through the community.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: This Subway franchise operates inside the Seafair Shopping Centre in Richmond, offering made-to-order Footlong and 6" sandwiches, wraps, and salads. It serves breakfast and provides catering, delivery, and curbside pickup in addition to in-restaurant dining. For a touring cyclist, it is a convenient stop along No. 1 Road for a customizable, filling meal.

detail.address: 8671 Number 1 Road, Unit 6, Richmond, BC V7C 1V2

restaurant.name: Hot Chili House
restaurant.desc: Hot Chili House is a Chinese restaurant in Abbotsford offering an extensive menu of Cantonese and Szechuan-style dishes, from ginger beef and kung pao chicken to a solid selection of tofu and vegetable plates. With over 200 customer reviews and a full online ordering system supporting both delivery and pickup, it is a well-established local spot. Touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley corridor will find filling, varied options including lunch specials.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Mixed Vegetables, Spicy String Bean Szechuan Style, Tofu & Eggplant with Chili & Garlic Sauce, Spicy Tofu Szechuan Style, Deep-Fried Tofu with Spicy Pepper, and Mapo Tofu

restaurant.name: Pizza Garden
restaurant.desc: Pizza Garden is a BC-based Neapolitan pizza chain operated by Neapolitan Pizza Ltd., with over 25 years in the industry and locations across British Columbia. The Victoria outpost sits on Government Street in the heart of downtown, serving wood-fired pizzas with charred crusts, sun-ripened tomatoes, and creamy mozzarella. Cyclists rolling through Victoria's core will find a central, accessible spot for a sit-down meal or a quick pickup order.

restaurant.name: The Chopped Leaf
restaurant.desc: The Chopped Leaf is a Canadian fast-casual franchise focused on salads, wraps, bowls, and other fresh-forward meals. This Maple Ridge location sits along Lougheed Highway, a main arterial corridor, making it a potential mid-ride food stop for cyclists passing through the area. The chain is known for customizable, lighter fare including a kids menu and signature dressings.

detail.address: 20395 Lougheed Highway Unit 520, Maple Ridge, BC V2X 2P9

restaurant.name: Vesuvius Cafe&Store
restaurant.desc: Vesuvius Cafe&Store is a cafe in Chemainus offering food and drink to visitors. It serves as a rest and refreshment stop for cyclists and travelers in the area.

restaurant.name: 900 Bistro
restaurant.desc: 900 Degrees Bistro Sidney is the peninsula outpost of a Vancouver Island wood-fired Italian restaurant committed to fresh, organic ingredients with no frozen food, deep fryers, or microwaves. The menu extends well beyond pizza to include house-made pastas, wood-fired filet mignon, and escargots, giving Saanich Peninsula cyclists a sit-down meal that goes beyond typical roadside fare. It is the second location of a locally-owned operation run by chef-owner Adrian Ortiz-Mena.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Online menu explicitly lists Vegetarian, Vegan, and Gluten-Free as pizza subcategories

restaurant.name: Steveston Bakery
restaurant.desc: Steveston Bakery and Café has been a family-run fixture in historic Steveston Village since 1989, founded by Hemant and Bimla Rao and known for traditional breads, homemade soups, and a wide range of desserts and baked goods. The café offers an all-day breakfast and lunch menu with items ranging from veggie wraps to paninis and grilled chicken burgers, making it a substantial refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the Steveston waterfront. A beloved local tradition — a 99¢ sourdough loaf every Saturday — has been unbroken since opening day.

restaurant.name: Barside Lounge & Grill
restaurant.desc: Barside Lounge & Grill is a full-service casual dining restaurant and bar located inside Chances Casino Kamloops, offering an extensive menu of pub-style mains, handheld sandwiches, burgers, and seafood dishes. The venue supports local BC vintners by serving exclusively regional wines, and features rotating BC craft taps including Mount Begbie and The Cannery. As an amenity within a large casino complex, it provides a substantial sit-down dining option in Kamloops' north end.

restaurant.name: The Derby Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Derby Restaurant is a licensed dining room located on the second floor of the Cedar Hill Golf Course Clubhouse, operated by Lakeland Golf Management on behalf of the District of Saanich. The menu leans toward casual favourites including house-ground burgers, seafood chowder, and fresh fish tacos, alongside starters and desserts. A separate Derby Express counter offers a faster service option, and the clubhouse is fully accessible via elevator with accessible washrooms on site.

restaurant.name: Ginkgo Chinese Food
restaurant.desc: Ginkgo Chinese Food is a locally rooted Chinese restaurant that has served the Sardis and Chilliwack area since 1999, earning a spot on the Chilliwack Progress A-List for five consecutive years. Located beside Staples on Vedder Road, it is one of two locations operated by the same family under the same brand. Touring cyclists passing through Sardis will find it a convenient casual stop for fresh Chinese food with online ordering available.

notes.Takeout: Website prominently features an 'ORDER ONLINE' option and notes that orders are accepted until 30 minutes before closing

restaurant.name: 852 Kitchen
restaurant.desc: 852 Kitchen is a multi-location Hong Kong-style food shop specializing in handcrafted dim sum, home-style dishes, nourishing soups, frozen dumplings, and signature pineapple buns, all prepared in a commercial kitchen in Richmond. The Joyce Street Vancouver branch is one of four locations across Metro Vancouver. Products are designed for pickup or delivery, making it a convenient stop for cyclists seeking authentic Cantonese and Hong Kong flavors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website product list includes a 'Vegan' category; no GF or vegetarian-specific label found

restaurant.name: Handi Cuisine of India
restaurant.desc: Handi Indian Restaurant is an Indian cuisine establishment located on Bellevue Avenue in West Vancouver. Based on OSM data it offers indoor seating only. No further details about the restaurant's offerings or cycling amenities could be verified due to domain hijacking.

restaurant.name: Lakeside Sushi
restaurant.desc: Lakeside Sushi is a sushi restaurant located on Cowichan Lake Road in Lake Cowichan. Situated in the Cowichan Valley, it serves the local community. Specific menu details and amenities could not be verified from available sources.

restaurant.name: Deep Cove Osaka
restaurant.desc: Osaka Japanese Restaurant has been serving fresh, high-quality sushi and Japanese cuisine in the heart of Deep Cove village since April 2012. Deep Cove is a popular cycling destination on the North Shore, making this restaurant a natural stop for riders exploring the area. Both dine-in and takeout are available, offering flexibility for cyclists on the move.

restaurant.name: DunnEnzies

The Mission location is set around a back-yard style patio shaded by a 200-year-old London Plane tree, and doubles as a live-music and events stage hosting comedy, drag, trivia, and theatre. The menu spans creative specialty pizzas, tacos, and a full drinks list with daily specials.

restaurant.name: Serious Coffee

The café is known for a unique air-roasting process applied to premium Arabica beans sourced from Mexico, Kenya, Colombia, and beyond, producing a smooth, low-bitterness cup. Alongside espresso drinks and specialty teas, the chain runs its own bakery offering fresh muffins, scones, and breakfast wraps.

restaurant.name: Wings on Kingsway
restaurant.desc: Wings on Kingsway is the Burnaby franchise of the WINGS restaurant chain, located on the busy Kingsway corridor connecting Vancouver and Burnaby. The restaurant is known for award-winning chicken wings in 28 globally-inspired flavours, alongside a full menu of burgers, salads, pastas, and plant-based options. It offers indoor seating and online ordering, making it a convenient sit-down meal stop for cyclists travelling the Kingsway route.

restaurant.name: Carlos O' Bryans Neighborhood Pub
restaurant.desc: Kelly & Carlos O'Bryan's is a multi-concept venue in the heart of downtown Kelowna, combining a full-service neighborhood restaurant, a pub, and a rooftop patio ('Rooftop Paddy O') just a short walk from Okanagan Lake. Part of a BC-wide chain with Irish-pub-inspired character, the Kelowna location hosts regular live events, karaoke, and DJ nights, and features a broad menu including local Okanagan wines. It sits in a walkable downtown core that is convenient as a resupply or meal stop mid-ride.

restaurant.name: Datang Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Datang Hot Pot is a modern Chinese restaurant in Richmond specializing in build-your-own mala tang and dry pot, with broths made fresh daily. The spacious dine-in setting features a wide sauce bar, buffet ice cream, and snacks like roujiamo and skewers. Customer reviews highlight generous portions and friendly service, making it a notable stop for a substantial hot meal.

restaurant.name: Kagura Hand Roll Bar
restaurant.desc: Kagura Hand Roll Bar is a Japanese restaurant in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood on West 4th Avenue, specializing in hand rolls (temaki sushi). It sits along a busy cycling corridor popular with riders heading toward the Arbutus Greenway and foreshore routes. A touring cyclist passing through Kitsilano would find it a compact, likely counter-style spot for a quick Japanese meal.

restaurant.name: BarBurrito
restaurant.desc: BarBurrito is Canada's largest burrito chain, proudly Canadian since 2005, with 385+ locations nationwide. This Westbank location serves fully customizable Mexican-inspired burritos, bowls, tacos, and quesadillas built from fresh, in-house ingredients with a wide variety of proteins. It is a convenient quick-service stop for cyclists passing through the Westbank commercial corridor near Kelowna.

detail.address: 2127 Louie Drive Unit #108, Westbank, British Columbia V4T 1R5

restaurant.name: Foamers' Folly Tap Room
restaurant.desc: Foamers' Folly is a craft microbrewery and taproom in Pitt Meadows pouring 20 rotating house-brewed taps — from lagers and wheat ales to wild sours and hard seltzers — alongside a full food menu and a patio. The brewery leans into an adventurous, community-oriented ethos with regular live music, trivia nights, food trucks, and comedy events. Cyclists will find a genuinely welcoming stop: the venue explicitly lists a bike rack, allows pets, and welcomes children.

restaurant.name: Sunshine
restaurant.desc: Sunshine Eatery is a UBC Okanagan campus eatery located on the main floor of the Admin Building, operated by UBCO Food Services as one of 11 on-campus dining locations. It offers breakfast and lunch fare including grab-and-go sandwiches, salads, pastries, hot take-out dishes, and coffee. As a university food services outlet, it primarily serves the campus community of over 12,000 students, staff, and faculty.

detail.address: Admin Building (main floor), 1138 Alumni Ave, Kelowna, BC

restaurant.name: The Last Drop
restaurant.desc: The Last Drop is a bar in Revelstoke with outdoor seating and brewery connections. Touring cyclists will find a social venue for food and drinks when passing through town.

restaurant.name: JJ's Restaurant
restaurant.desc: JJ's Restaurant is a student-run teaching restaurant at Vancouver Community College where second-level culinary students prepare and serve a three-course a la carte lunch under the guidance of Chef Instructors. The experience offers gourmet cuisine at accessible prices in a formal dining room setting inside VCC's downtown Vancouver campus. Dietary restrictions can be accommodated with advance notice, making it a distinctive lunch option in the heart of the city.

restaurant.name: Eat Bar & Patio Haraheri
restaurant.desc: Eat Bar & Patio Haraheri is a Japanese izakaya restaurant located in downtown Vancouver near the corner of Nelson and Howe streets. The izakaya format centres on sharing small plates alongside drinks, making it a sociable stop for groups. The unit M101 address places it in a mixed-use building footprint common to Vancouver's West End dining corridor.

restaurant.name: Kutlet
restaurant.desc: Kutlet is a Korean restaurant in Tsawwassen's Canoe Pass Way development, specialising in Korean-style cutlets. It offers dine-in with reservations as well as pickup and third-party delivery through DoorDash and Uber Eats. The restaurant also produces and sells house-made kimchi jars as a retail item.

detail.address: 2208-4949 Canoe Pass Way, Tsawwassen, BC V4M 0B2

restaurant.name: Mui Kee Chicken Pot
restaurant.desc: Mui Kee Chicken Pot is a Chinese restaurant located in Richmond's Alexandra Road dining corridor, a stretch well known to locals for its concentration of Asian cuisine. The restaurant specializes in chicken pot dishes, a style of Hong Kong-influenced comfort food popular in the area. Cyclists riding the Richmond area's flat, bike-friendly streets would find this a convenient stop for a hearty meal.

restaurant.name: Gino's Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Gino's Coffee House is a community-focused cafe on Osoyoos's Main Street, centred around a custom Italian-built 'STEAMHAMMER' espresso machine imported by the owners themselves. The cafe sources Fairtrade, organic beans through Spirit Bear Coffee Company, a locally owned First Nations business, and rounds out its menu with sandwiches, soups, and baked goods. Osoyoos is one of the Okanagan's most popular cycling destinations, and the cafe explicitly positions itself as a welcoming stop for visitors and travellers.

restaurant.name: Wendy's
restaurant.desc: Wendy's is a North American fast-food chain founded in 1969, known for its square beef patties made from fresh, never-frozen beef and a menu spanning burgers, chicken, chili, salads, and the iconic Frosty dessert. This location on 152 Street serves as a drive-through and takeout stop in the South Surrey corridor. The all-day menu and drive-through configuration make it a practical refuelling point for cyclists on longer routes through the area.

restaurant.name: The Saigonville Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Saigonville is a family-owned Vietnamese restaurant on East Hastings Street led by Chef Kevin Nguyen, who blends classic Saigon flavours with Western culinary techniques in dishes like truffle crab spring rolls, grilled La Lot beef, and house-made bánh khọt. Open since 2024, it has collected several local food awards including recognition from Vancouver Foodster and the Canadian Choice Award. Catering and online ordering for pickup or delivery are available in addition to dine-in service.

detail.address: 2129 East Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V5L 1V2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated Vegan Menu and Gluten Free Menu sections on the website; multiple individual items labelled Vegan throughout the lunch menu

restaurant.name: Fresh Box Sushi
restaurant.desc: Fresh Box Sushi is a sushi restaurant located in unit 221 in Vancouver, BC. Based on OSM data it offers Japanese sushi cuisine, but no further detail about the business, its setting, or its offerings could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Botanist
restaurant.desc: Botanist is the flagship fine-dining restaurant of the Fairmont Pacific Rim hotel, set in Vancouver's waterfront Coal Harbour district with both an indoor dining room and an outdoor garden terrace. Executive Chef Hector Laguna leads a menu rooted in Pacific Northwest ingredients — sustainably sourced seafood, organic produce from local farmers, and regionally inspired seasonal dishes. The venue also houses an inventive cocktail bar and lab with a terroir-driven wine program focused on small-batch, biodynamic producers.

restaurant.name: Stoked Wood Fired Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Stoked Wood Fired Pizzeria is a seasonal, take-out-focused wood-fired pizza restaurant on Vancouver Island's wild west coast near Shirley, BC, explicitly positioned as a refuelling stop before or after outdoor adventures along the Juan de Fuca corridor. The menu leans on locally sourced ingredients and features a rotating selection of Vancouver Island beers, ciders, wines, and craft cocktails, alongside a small market stocking locally made goods and trail guides. Generous outdoor seating, a dog-friendly lower patio, and a laid-back west coast atmosphere make it a natural gathering point for cyclists passing through.

notes.Takeout: FAQ states: 'We are currently operating as take-out only. However, there is plenty of outdoor seating available. At this time, ordering ahead of time is recommended.'
