restaurant.name: SukkoThai Restaurant
restaurant.desc: SukkhoThai Restaurant is an award-winning Thai restaurant on Commercial Street in downtown Nanaimo, serving authentic dishes such as Pad Thai, Green Curry, and Panaeng Curry with Prawns. The restaurant prides itself on consistent quality and offers both dine-in with table reservations and a takeout/pickup service, making it a practical meal stop for cyclists passing through the city centre.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states lunch combos come 'With your choice of Tofu, Vegetables, Chicken, or Beef', confirming vegetarian protein options are available

restaurant.name: Andreas Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Andreas Restaurant is a long-established Greek and Italian family restaurant in Langley, operated since 1984 by father-and-son duo Andreas and Dimitrios. The scratch kitchen turns out over 130 menu items daily—from souvlaki and lamb dishes to house-made pizzas and 28-day-aged AAA steaks—with a firm commitment to never using pre-packaged or vacuum-sealed prepared food. Touring cyclists will find a warm, family-focused atmosphere with dine-in, takeout, and delivery all available, and a banquet room for larger groups.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Pizza menu includes a dedicated Vegetarian pizza (mushrooms, green peppers, onions, tomatoes, pineapple, olives, cheese & tomato sauce); Greek salads and Mediterranean-style dishes also available

restaurant.name: Luroufan Tasty
restaurant.desc: Lu Rou Fan Tasty is a restaurant specializing in lu rou fan, the beloved Taiwanese braised pork belly rice dish. Based in Richmond, BC, it appears to serve the area's large Taiwanese and broader Asian community. The name suggests a focused, specialty menu built around this classic comfort food.

restaurant.name: J's Cafe and Bistro
restaurant.desc: J's Cafe & Bistro is a downtown Kelowna fusion café at 1282 Ellis Street, serving a globe-spanning menu of Asian-Western comfort food — Kimchi Burgers, Tonkatsu Sandos, Bulgogi Beef Poutine, Pad Thai, and Szechuan Noodles sit alongside a full espresso bar and milk-tea drinks. The broad menu makes it a versatile stop for cyclists who need anything from a quick coffee to a filling hot meal. Online takeout ordering is available through Clover.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Crispy Tofu (deep-fried tofu in sweet chilli sauce), Cucumber Salad, and Side Salad, confirming vegetarian options are available

restaurant.name: Field House Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Field House Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and taproom located in Downtown Chilliwack's District 1881, the second location of a two-site operation that opened in 2020. The taproom pours a constantly rotating lineup of ales, experimental IPAs, barrel-aged sours, and non-alcoholic beers — guaranteed at least one new release every week. A farm-to-table canteen program and regular live music nights round out the experience for cyclists looking to linger.

detail.address: 251 Woolly Dog Alley #102, Chilliwack, BC V2P 0J6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: CHWK menu page explicitly marks items with ⓥ VEGETARIAN and Ⓖ GLUTEN AWARE symbols

restaurant.name: The Brownsville Pub

restaurant.name: Fatburger
restaurant.desc: Fatburger on Davie Street is a casual burger restaurant in Vancouver's West End, serving fresh-never-frozen Alberta Angus beef burgers cooked to order, alongside chicken wings, hand-scooped milkshakes, and veggie options. The Canadian franchise has been operating since 2005 and is part of a chain founded in Los Angeles in 1952. It offers dine-in and takeout in a lively neighbourhood corridor popular with pedestrians and cyclists.

restaurant.name: Laneway Coffee and Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Laneway Coffee and Kitchen is an owner-operated multi-roaster cafe in Cumberland run by a coffee professional and a trained chef. It serves hand-crafted espresso and rotating pour-over selections from Canadian roasters alongside made-to-order sandwiches and elevated comfort food using local and seasonal ingredients. The cafe aims to bring the same culture of craft and quality found in a taproom to the coffee experience in a small-town setting.

restaurant.name: Javawocky Coffee House

restaurant.name: Chosun Korean BBQ
restaurant.desc: Chosun Korean BBQ is a sit-down Korean restaurant in Vancouver's West End offering traditional Korean dishes alongside online ordering for takeout. The menu highlights items like Padak Chicken, Sweet Pig Trotters, Mussel Soup, and Cheese Kimchi Rice, aiming for an authentic Korean experience in a relaxed, cozy setting. A touring cyclist arriving on Davie Street would find a full-service restaurant with indoor and outdoor seating.

restaurant.name: Off the Tracks
restaurant.desc: Off the Tracks is a Granville Island original cafe and bistro tucked into the artisan corridor of Railspur Alley, serving specialty espresso, house-made baked goods, and locally sourced sandwiches and breakfast. The kitchen makes everything from scratch using organic and sustainable ingredients, and the spot is fully licensed with local craft beers, wines, and spirits. Cyclists exploring Granville Island will find a charming garden patio and naturally lit loft seating ideal for a relaxed mid-ride stop.

restaurant.name: Jasmine Garden Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Jasmine Garden Seafood Restaurant is a family-owned Chinese restaurant in West Abbotsford, in business since June 2000, serving authentic Cantonese and Szechuan cuisine. The full-service dine-in restaurant also offers takeout and local delivery, with a broad menu spanning dim-sum-style appetizers, seafood, noodles, and family dinner combos. A dedicated gluten-free menu section makes it a practical stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

restaurant.name: Gina's Mexican Cafe

Situated just off Highway 1 and a short walk from the boat basin and waterfront walkway, it makes a convenient and distinctive stop for cyclists passing through the city centre.

restaurant.name: High Street Pizza

restaurant.name: KrunChicken

restaurant.name: Mumbaiyaa Street Foods

The restaurant's name blends 'Mumbai' with 'yaa,' the Marathi word for 'come,' reflecting its mission to bring the communal, flavour-forward spirit of Mumbai's streets to Canada. Cyclists stopping here will find an entirely plant-based menu of bold Indian street food with a vibrant, eclectic atmosphere described as mirroring the streets of Mumbai.

restaurant.name: Tasty Donair
restaurant.desc: Tasty Donair is a Lebanese-inspired fast-food counter specializing in donairs, shawarma-style wraps, and Mediterranean plates built around hummus, tabouli, and falafel. restaurant.name: Tandoori Grill

The kitchen specialises in clay-oven tandoor cooking at 600 °F — a technique rooted in Mughal culinary tradition — using free-range chicken, premium lamb, and Oceanwise seafood. Touring cyclists will find a broad menu that accommodates vegans, vegetarians, and gluten-free diets, with pickup and local delivery also available.

restaurant.name: J's Pizza

Online ordering and delivery are available, and the broad menu offers substantial refuelling options for cyclists passing through Chilliwack.

restaurant.name: JINYA Ramen Bar

As a sit-down ramen restaurant, it would provide a warm, restorative meal for cyclists passing through central Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Old Farmhouse Kitchen
restaurant.desc: A farmhouse-themed cafe operated by Avolon Dairy, located on North Fraser Way in Richmond. It offers casual dining as part of Avolon Dairy's retail presence in an agricultural region of the Lower Mainland.

restaurant.name: Mandarin Garden Buffet Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Mandarin Garden is a long-running all-you-can-eat Chinese buffet restaurant in Abbotsford offering over 60 items spanning dim sum, seafood, soups, and desserts. restaurant.name: Creekside Grill
restaurant.desc: Creekside Grill is a full-service restaurant and bar situated inside the Westfield Country Club, overlooking a tranquil creek and championship golf course in Surrey. Open to both club members and the general public, it serves a fusion menu drawing on local and international flavours. In addition to dine-in service, the restaurant offers delivery through Skip the Dishes, Uber Eats, and DoorDash, making it a flexible stop for riders in the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu description states 'vibrant vegetarian options' are available

restaurant.name: OK Falls Hotel
restaurant.desc: The OK Falls Hotel is a combined pub, bar & grill, and boutique hotel in Okanagan Falls, sitting three blocks from the shores of Skaha Lake. The kitchen serves elevated pub fare built around local Okanagan ingredients — burgers, fresh-caught seafood, and comfort plates — in a relaxed setting with a patio. Freshly renovated suites make it a viable overnight stop for cyclists touring the South Okanagan wine corridor.

restaurant.name: Starbucks

Its campus setting makes it a convenient stop for cyclists touring the University Way corridor in Kelowna.

restaurant.name: Freshii
restaurant.desc: Freshii is a Canadian quick-service restaurant chain founded in Toronto in 2005, now with over 300 locations worldwide. The Wesbrook Mall location offers a health-focused menu of salads, energy bowls, burritos, wraps, poke bowls, and smoothies, all fully customizable. Touring cyclists will find it a convenient stop for a nutritious, build-your-own meal in the UBC/Wesbrook Village area.

restaurant.name: The Squeezed Grape

It is a locally rooted West Kootenay business with a hands-on, welcoming atmosphere aimed at the home-brewing community.

restaurant.name: South Silk Road Restaurant
restaurant.desc: South Silk Road is a Canadian restaurant group bringing authentic Southwest Chinese cuisine — rooted in the culinary traditions of Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, and Hunan — to Richmond, BC. The menu emphasizes bold, complex flavors featuring chili, Sichuan peppercorn, fermented and pickled ingredients sourced from diverse regional traditions. The Richmond location is part of a three-city Canadian chain recommended by Alberta Tourism, with online ordering and table reservations available.

restaurant.name: Pho An Nam
restaurant.desc: Pho An Nam is a Vietnamese restaurant in Richmond serving traditional dishes including phở and spring rolls made with fresh ingredients and homemade sauces. It is one of two locations (the other in Surrey) and offers online ordering for takeout. A touring cyclist passing through Richmond's commercial Number 3 Road corridor could stop here for a hot, filling meal.

restaurant.name: Elysium Korean Bistro & Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Elysium Korean Bistro & Restaurant is a Korean cuisine establishment located in Richmond's Alexandra Road commercial corridor. It operates out of a unit in what appears to be a multi-tenant commercial building. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's busy food district may find it a convenient stop for a Korean meal.

restaurant.name: True Confections
restaurant.desc: True Confections is a long-established Vancouver dessert destination that has been making all of its cakes, pies, cheesecakes, and baked goods from scratch using pure ingredients for over 35 years. The shop operates two locations and offers an extensive menu including gluten-free and vegan options, catering, and high tea. For a touring cyclist, it represents a notable sweet-stop on the West Broadway corridor.

restaurant.name: Peek A Boo Japanese Bistro
restaurant.desc: Peek A Boo Japanese Bistro is a sit-down Japanese restaurant located in a unit at 1297 56 Street in Tsawwassen, Delta. It offers a full lunch and dinner service for cyclists touring the South Delta area, which is popular for its flat terrain and connections to the Tsawwassen ferry terminal. The bistro format suggests a more relaxed dining experience than fast casual, making it a reasonable rest stop on a longer ride.

restaurant.name: Firehouse Subs
restaurant.desc: Firehouse Subs is a North American sandwich chain known for its hot, steamed subs and a charitable foundation that has donated over $6.3 million to Canadian first responders. This Delta location offers dine-in, takeout, delivery, and catering. For a touring cyclist on Scott Road / 120th Street, it provides a reliable, high-calorie refuelling stop in a busy suburban corridor.

restaurant.name: Castella Cheesecake
restaurant.desc: Castella Cheesecake is a Japanese-style pastry bakery established in 2018, known for hand-crafted Basque burnt cheesecake, soufflé cheesecake, and molten cheese tarts made without heavy machinery. The YVR McArthurGlen Designer Outlet location is one of several storefronts the brand operates across Metro Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, and Alberta. Every product is made by a team of pastry specialists following home-baking methods championed by founder Billy.

restaurant.name: Trollers Fresh Fish and Chips
restaurant.desc: Trollers is a floating seafood restaurant moored in Nanaimo's working harbour, offering fresh halibut, wild salmon, and cod alongside smoked meats and bowls, all on a 100% gluten-free menu. Part of the Off the Hook Surf Turf and Smokery Family, the spot has both an open waterfront deck with ocean views and a covered indoor seating area for rainy west coast days. Its waterfront location on the Harbourfront Walkway puts it squarely on the route for cyclists exploring Nanaimo's coastline.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'our food menu is 100% gluten free'; menu includes a Sunshine Vegan Bowl (gochujang BBQ crispy cauliflower) explicitly listed as vegan

restaurant.name: The Flying Whale
restaurant.desc: The Flying Whale Café is the in-house café of Flyover, Vancouver's immersive aerial flight simulation attraction anchored at the iconic Canada Place on the downtown waterfront. The café serves a full range of specialty coffee drinks, teas, pastries, hot food items, and alcoholic beverages, with both indoor and outdoor seating. Its location on the Coal Harbour waterfront puts it steps from Stanley Park and Gastown, making it a convenient stop on a downtown Vancouver cycling loop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Vegetarian Spring Rolls served with Plum Sauce'; salads and parfait also present. No GF labelling observed

restaurant.name: The Hideout Diner
restaurant.desc: A neighbourhood diner in Vancouver's East Side serving an eclectic mix of brunch alongside Greek and Italian dishes. The casual, community-focused spot has cultivated enough local identity to operate under the 'Hideout' brand, suggesting a welcoming atmosphere for drop-in diners. Online ordering is available, and the kitchen runs through the afternoon, making it a practical mid-ride food stop.

restaurant.name: Pinpin
restaurant.desc: Pinpin is a beloved Filipino-Chinese restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver, founded by owners Jojo and Virginia Lee whose families have deep roots in Manila's restaurant scene going back to 1945. The dining room is decorated with photos of Philippine scenes including the iconic jeepney, making it both a culinary and cultural experience. A touring cyclist would find it a welcoming spot for a hearty meal of classics like crispy pata, sisig, and a variety of noodle dishes.

restaurant.name: Fassil Ethiopian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Fassil Ethiopian Restaurant is named after Emperor Fasiladas, the 17th-century founder of Gondar, Ethiopia, and brings that cultural heritage to Vancouver's East Broadway neighbourhood. The kitchen specializes in traditional injera-based dishes with slow-cooked meats and aromatic spices, and the restaurant actively encourages the Ethiopian custom of Gursha — hand-feeding a dining companion as a gesture of warmth and hospitality. It is a sit-down destination dining experience rather than a quick-service stop.

restaurant.name: PBF Pita Bread Factory Factory Outlet
restaurant.desc: The factory outlet of Bakestone Brothers, the Pita Bread Factory's consumer-facing brand, founded in 1984 by Fady Hayek from a single family pita recipe. Now a certified organic bakery producing a wide range of ethnic breads and baked goods including pita, bagels, naan, tortillas, and pretzels sold across Canada and parts of the US. A touring cyclist can pick up fresh bread products directly from the manufacturer at this outlet location.

restaurant.name: Veneto's Cakes & Pastries
restaurant.desc: Veneto's Cakes & Pastries is a Surrey bakery specializing in handcrafted cakes, pastries, cookies, and sandwiches made fresh daily. The shop is known locally for custom birthday and wedding cakes, and also offers eggless and gluten-free options alongside classics like Black Forest, Tiramisu, and Hazelnut Torte. Cyclists passing through can pick up individual pastries or sandwiches in-store, or order ahead for pickup.

restaurant.name: Osaka Sushi
restaurant.desc: Osaka Sushi is a Japanese restaurant on Hastings Street in Burnaby offering an extensive menu spanning nigiri, sashimi, specialty rolls, ramen, udon, tempura, and donburi. The restaurant serves beer and house wine alongside its food menu. Both dine-in and takeout are available, with online ordering through the restaurant's own website.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian Roll Sushi' category with 14 items

restaurant.name: Ask for Luigi
restaurant.desc: An Italian restaurant on Alexander Street in Vancouver offering sit-down dining. It serves as a convenient food and beverage stop for touring cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: NoodleBox
restaurant.desc: NoodleBox is a Canadian fast-food franchise chain serving customizable Asian-inspired noodle and rice bowls wok-fired to order, with a menu spanning teriyaki, pad thai, kung pao, curry, and more. The Langley Bypass location is part of a nationally operating franchise with dozens of locations across BC and beyond. Dishes can be modified to accommodate vegan and gluten-friendly dietary needs, making it broadly accessible for cyclists with varied requirements.

restaurant.name: Cassidy Country Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Cassidy Country Kitchen is a restaurant located directly on the Trans-Canada Highway through Nanaimo, serving southwest-style cuisine. The establishment operates from a single-level building at this busy highway location. It functions as a food and rest stop for cyclists and travelers passing through the region.

restaurant.name: Vietnam Garden Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Vietnam Garden Restaurant is a well-regarded Vietnamese restaurant on Admirals Road in Esquimalt, serving a broad menu of pho, vermicelli bowls, stir-fries, and curry dishes. Reviewers praise the fresh ingredients, friendly staff, and willingness to accommodate dietary restrictions. It is a small, cozy spot with dine-in and fast pickup service, making it a convenient stop along the Esquimalt cycling corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated Vegetarian Dishes menu section with multiple tofu and vegetable options; reviewer confirmed dairy-free and gluten-free accommodations

restaurant.name: The Pint
restaurant.desc: The Pint is a pub located on Abbott Street in Vancouver. It provides a public venue where touring cyclists can stop to rest and enjoy food and beverages.

restaurant.name: KeeLung Taiwanese Breakfast & Lunch
restaurant.desc: KeeLung Taiwanese Breakfast & Lunch is a quick-service Taiwanese restaurant in Richmond, specializing in traditional morning and midday dishes from Taiwan. Operating out of a unit in a larger commercial building at McKim Way, it serves the diverse Richmond community with Taiwanese breakfast staples — a cuisine not commonly found in fast-casual format in the region. A touring cyclist passing through Richmond's commercial district would find it a distinctive and filling stop during morning or early-afternoon riding hours.

restaurant.name: Saku
restaurant.desc: Saku is an authentic Japanese tonkatsu (pork cutlet) restaurant specializing in premium Canadian-raised hormone-free pork prepared in a variety of classic katsu styles. The Broadway location features an all-year-round heated patio seating 26 guests, making it a viable stop in any season. The menu spans pork, chicken, seafood, and vegetable katsu sets, all served with unlimited rice, tonjiru, and shredded cabbage.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Vegetable Katsu (deep fried breaded tofu with seasonal vegetables) and Vegetable Curry

restaurant.name: Express Pho
restaurant.desc: Pho Express & Chill is a Vietnamese restaurant in Vancouver's West End serving pho noodle soups, vermicelli bowls, bánh mì sandwiches, and spring rolls with both dine-in and online pickup ordering. The menu spans a wide range of proteins as well as no-meat options, with vegetarian items flagged in the menu legend. Its Bute Street address sits just a few blocks from the Stanley Park Seawall cycling route, making it a convenient urban refuelling stop.

restaurant.name: Cactus Club Cafe
restaurant.desc: Cactus Club Cafe North Burnaby is an upscale-casual chain restaurant positioned near the Brentwood neighbourhood, offering a chef-driven international menu with a lounge, patio, and private dining spaces. The stylish, full-service venue draws a lively crowd and covers the full day with lunch, dinner, happy hour, and late-night service. Touring cyclists will find a sit-down meal with pickup and delivery options as well as a patio for outdoor seating.

restaurant.name: Sip Song Thai Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Sip Song Thai Cuisine is a Thai restaurant on West 16th Avenue in Vancouver's Dunbar-Southlands neighbourhood, offering both dine-in with reservations and online ordering for pickup or delivery. The restaurant operates with Square-powered checkout and emphasizes personalized service from front-of-house to kitchen. Touring cyclists navigating the quieter residential streets of the west side will find a sit-down Thai meal option with the convenience of online pre-ordering.

restaurant.name: Tandoori Palace
restaurant.desc: Tandoori Palace is an Indian restaurant located on Commercial Drive in Vancouver, specializing in tandoori cuisine. The restaurant serves the local cycling community and visitors with takeout and dine-in service.

restaurant.name: Level V Bakery
restaurant.desc: Level V Bakery is a 100% plant-based bakery tucked into Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, founded in 2017 by a self-taught baker who grew the business from a home kitchen into a brick-and-mortar shop. Everything is made from scratch — no dairy, no eggs — with a rotating lineup of cakes, pastries, buns, cookies, macarons, and cream puffs, plus gluten-free and nut-free options. Cyclists passing through the area can stop in for daily walk-in stock or pre-order items for pickup.

notes.Takeout: Same-day pickup ordering via Square Site; pre-orders also available for pickup. Website states 'sorry we do not hold any orders over the phone' and all orders are pick-up only

restaurant.name: Shaw Donair Bites Ltd
restaurant.desc: Shaw Donair Bites Ltd is a donair restaurant located in Richmond's commercial district. Donair, a popular sandwich cuisine in Canada, offers a filling option for cyclists looking for a quick meal while touring.

restaurant.name: Krishna's Dosa Grill
restaurant.desc: Krishna's Dosa Grill is a South Indian restaurant on Scott Road specializing in dosas, the crispy fermented rice-and-lentil crepes that are a staple of South Indian cuisine. The restaurant serves the Scott Road corridor, a densely commercial stretch straddling Surrey and North Delta. A touring cyclist stopping here would find Indian cuisine in a full-service restaurant setting.

restaurant.name: Ice Queen
restaurant.desc: Ice Queen is a local ice cream shop serving the Richmond community. It's a casual refreshment stop where cyclists can grab frozen treats during summer rides through the area.

restaurant.name: Happy Day Cafe
restaurant.desc: Happy Day Cafe is a Hong Kong-style restaurant with locations in Richmond and Vancouver, serving classic Cantonese dishes alongside other Asian-inspired creations for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The Richmond outpost is a unit-based location within a larger complex on McClelland Road, offering both comfortable dine-in seating and a full online ordering system with self pick-up. Touring cyclists in south Richmond will find it a convenient stop for a sit-down meal or a quick takeout order.

restaurant.name: Dragon Bowl
restaurant.desc: Dragon Bowl is a fast-casual Chinese restaurant chain with a Richmond outpost on No. 3 Road near Richmond Centre, serving customizable rice bowls, noodle bowls, protein-packed salads, and bubble tea made with natural ingredients. The location sits steps from Richmond-Brighouse SkyTrain and nearby shopping, making it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists passing through central Richmond. The chain also offers corporate catering and a personalized meal-prep service for those planning ahead.

detail.address: 4140 Number 3 Road Unit 120, Richmond, BC V6X 2C2

restaurant.name: Bufala
restaurant.desc: Bufala Kerrisdale is an award-winning independent Neapolitan pizzeria described by Vancouver Magazine as 'the beating heart of the Kerrisdale food scene,' earning multiple Best Pizzeria and Best West Side Restaurant honours. Fresh, scratch-made pizzas are fired in an 800-degree stone oven alongside Italian-inspired small plates, cocktails, and craft beers. It is the original location of a three-location Vancouver restaurant group, with walk-ins always welcome.

restaurant.name: Dubh Linn Gate
restaurant.desc: Dubh Linn Gate is a lively Irish pub set inside the Pan Pacific Whistler Mountainside hotel at the base of the Whistler and Blackcomb gondolas, making it one of the most centrally located watering holes in Whistler Village. It pours Whistler's true 20 oz imperial pint from 25 draught taps spanning BC craft breweries, Irish classics like Guinness and Kilkenny, and rotating specialty taps. A full food menu runs from brunch through late-night dinner, and live music most evenings draws a crowd of locals and visiting riders alike.

restaurant.name: Masiero Pizzeria Napoletana
restaurant.desc: Masiero Pizzeria Napoletana is Vernon's dedicated Neapolitan pizza restaurant, baking pies in a handcrafted wood-fired oven imported directly from Naples, Italy. Situated in downtown Vernon, the 50-seat dining room (including an 8-seat bar) serves house-made antipasti and desserts alongside a curated selection of local craft beers and wines. Ingredients are sourced both locally and from premium Italian suppliers, giving the menu a farm-meets-Italy character.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items marked '(v)' for vegetarian: Warm Smoked Olives, Focaccia, Insalata di Farro, Ricotta Piadina, Tanto Latte Burrata, Tomato Bruschetta, Gnocchi. No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Timothy's Frozen Yogurt
restaurant.desc: Timothy's Frozen Yogurt is a long-running gelato parlour that first opened in 1989 on the Steveston Pier, growing from a small café into a Richmond institution. The shop produces small-batch Italian gelato entirely in-house using fresh, locally sourced ingredients, with an extensive roster spanning classics like pistachio and vanilla bean alongside originals like durian and blood orange sorbetto. Situated at Steveston Landing on the Fraser River waterfront, it sits directly on one of Richmond's most popular recreational cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Song
restaurant.desc: Song (Kin Kao Song) is a Thai dine-in and takeout restaurant in Vancouver's Mt. Pleasant neighbourhood, operated by the same team behind Kin Kao on Commercial Drive. The kitchen is led by a Bangkok-native executive chef who imports spices directly from Thailand and pairs them with locally sourced daily ingredients, delivering refined street-style and home-cooked Thai dishes. Cyclists riding East Broadway will find a compact, focused menu with reservations via OpenTable and a full takeout option.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Takeout menu marks select items as gluten-free, e.g. 'tom yum prawns soup (gf)'; no explicit vegetarian or vegan labelling found in fetched content

restaurant.name: Stepho's Greek Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A casual Greek restaurant on Vancouver's Davie Street offering traditional Mediterranean cuisine with vegetarian options. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available. Provides washroom facilities including wheelchair-accessible restrooms.

restaurant.name: Vera's Burger Shack
restaurant.desc: Vera's Burger Shack is a BC-born burger chain with a cult following for its 100% fresh Canadian beef patties, hand-pressed to order. The Main Street location sits in one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors, making it a natural pit stop on a city ride. The menu spans classic burgers, daily rotating specials, fries, and sides.

restaurant.name: Pallino's Italian Bistro
restaurant.desc: Pallino's Italian Bistro is a casual sit-down restaurant located inside Predator Ridge Resort, a master-planned resort community in the Okanagan Valley about 15 minutes south of Vernon. The kitchen turns out signature thin-crust pizzas, baked pastas, and freshly made sandwiches using locally sourced ingredients, paired with Italian wines, craft beers, and specialty coffee. The resort is a notable cycling destination with 13 km of on-site biking trails connecting to 40+ km at Ellison Provincial Park, and offers a dedicated 'Ride & Stay' package, making Pallino's a natural meal stop for touring and trail cyclists in the area.

detail.address: 301 Village Centre Place, Vernon, BC V1H 1T2

restaurant.name: Cakes n Sweets
restaurant.desc: Cakes n Sweets is a specialty bakery in Coquitlam crafting custom and wedding cakes, cupcakes, macarons, and cake pops for all occasions. The cozy shop offers dine-in service and a reservation-only high tea experience with sweets, savouries, and fine teas. Dietary-friendly options including eggless, gluten-friendly, and vegan choices are available for most products.

restaurant.name: Sake Dining HASHIGO by Zakkushi
restaurant.desc: Sake Dining Hashigo is a boutique Japanese sake bar steps from Davie and Granville Street in downtown Vancouver, operated by the Zakkushi Group. The restaurant stocks more than 15 varieties of sake, offers tasting flights, and serves Japanese small plates such as sashimi and oden designed for sake pairing. It is part of a family of Japanese restaurants spanning Vancouver and Toronto, giving it an established reputation in the city's Japanese dining scene.

restaurant.name: Sidewinders Coffee Co
restaurant.desc: SideWinders is a cafe in Nelson, BC, a well-known Kootenay cycling hub at the confluence of mountain biking and touring routes. Beyond its OSM classification as a cafe, no substantive detail about its offerings, setting, or atmosphere could be retrieved from public sources. A visiting cyclist would need to verify on the ground whether it serves the needs of a touring stop.

restaurant.name: The Garden Strathcona
restaurant.desc: The Garden Strathcona is an independent cafe, retail shop, and events venue situated on East Hastings Street in Vancouver's historic Strathcona neighbourhood. It operates its own online shop and hosts a studio space for community events, making it more than a typical coffee stop. Touring cyclists passing through east Vancouver will find it a neighbourhood anchor with a local, independent character.

restaurant.name: COBS Bread
restaurant.desc: COBS Bread is a Canadian franchise of the Australian Bakers Delight chain, baking all products from scratch on-site each day — no freezing or transporting. The 8th at Cambie location offers a broad range of breads, scones, cruffins, croissants, and savoury pastries in a neighbourhood commercial strip. Any unsold baked goods at closing are donated to local charities, a practice consistent across the chain.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: A Subway sandwich franchise in Tsawwassen serving footlongs, 6" sandwiches, wraps, and salads with fresh-cut vegetables and freshly baked bread. The location offers both in-restaurant dining and curbside pickup, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen area. Vegetarian options and limited vegan choices are available.

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: A Starbucks Coffee location on King George Boulevard in Surrey, part of the global chain known for espresso drinks, teas, Refreshers, and light food items. Situated on a major arterial road in Surrey, it serves as a recognizable and reliable rest stop for touring cyclists moving through the South Fraser region.

restaurant.name: Crescent Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Crescent Coffee House is a neighbourhood café in Surrey's Crescent Beach area, a coastal community that attracts recreational and touring cyclists along the Boundary Bay corridor. It appears as a small, community-oriented café based on its OSM listing, though no current details about its offerings or atmosphere are verifiable. Its location near cycling routes through South Surrey makes it a plausible rest stop, but current operating status cannot be confirmed.

restaurant.name: Twisted Indian
restaurant.desc: Twisted Indian is a fast-casual Indian fusion chain serving halal-certified customizable bowls, naan wraps, burritos, and poutines across BC, Alberta, and Ontario. The Surrey Panorama location is one of several BC outposts of this growing franchise, which bills itself as healthy food served fast. The menu accommodates a wide range of dietary needs, making it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists with varied restrictions.

restaurant.name: Illo Kimbap Cafe
restaurant.desc: Illo Kimbap Cafe is a health-focused Korean eatery in Coquitlam specializing in handcrafted kimbap made with whole grains and non-processed ingredients rather than conventional white rice. The menu extends beyond classic rolls to include keto kimbap, bibimbap-style salad bowls, sandwiches, paninis, and Korean sides, all framed around fresh, home-style cooking. Cyclists can order ahead for quick pickup via the website's online ordering system.

restaurant.name: Fireside Grill
restaurant.desc: Fireside Grill occupies a lovingly restored heritage Tudor estate—originally Maltwood Manor, built in the 1930s—set among wild Garry oak trees and manicured gardens about 10 minutes from Victoria's downtown core. The restaurant has earned multiple Readers' Choice awards from the Victoria Times Colonist for Best Fine Dining, Best Brunch, Best Patio, and Best Happy Hour, making it a well-regarded local institution. A touring cyclist arriving here will find a full farm-to-table menu, weekend brunch, patio seating, and event spaces in a distinctly Victorian setting.

restaurant.name: Garibaldi Lift Company
restaurant.desc: Garibaldi Lift Co. is Whistler's iconic après venue, perched slopeside in the Upper Village with a sunset deck and panoramic mountain views. It operates year-round and draws a strong mountain-bike and ski crowd with craft bites, cocktails, and a rotating roster of live DJs. The globally-inspired menu spans shareables, burgers, tacos, and poke bowls, with multiple vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options throughout.

restaurant.name: Mum's the Word
restaurant.desc: Opened in 2022 in Vancouver's Little Italy neighbourhood on Commercial Drive, Mum's the Word is an equal-parts café, cocktail bar, and community hub serving Habitat coffee, classic and signature cocktails, BC craft beer and wine, and comfort-food sandwiches on sourdough from Fife Bakery. The eclectic, laidback spot prides itself on sourcing local purveyors and ingredients and has quickly become a neighbourhood gathering place. A touring cyclist stopping on Commercial Drive will find hot coffee, cold beer, a solid sandwich, and a welcoming vibe.

restaurant.name: Dark Table
restaurant.desc: Dark Table is Vancouver's pitch-black dining restaurant in Kitsilano, where guests are guided through a completely dark dining room by blind or visually impaired servers trained to ensure comfort throughout the meal. The concept originated in Switzerland and has appeared in London, Paris, New York, and Montreal before coming to Vancouver, designed to heighten taste, smell, and touch by eliminating sight entirely. The restaurant is also a social-enterprise of sorts, deliberately employing blind and visually impaired staff in a role where their skills are unmatched.

restaurant.name: Persian Grill House
restaurant.desc: Persian Grill House is a Persian restaurant in Victoria serving traditional Middle Eastern cuisine. Located on Burnside Road East with casual table service. Website was inaccessible during review, limiting verification of cycling-specific amenities.

restaurant.name: Sushimoto
restaurant.desc: Sushimoto is a Japanese sushi restaurant operating since at least 2010 in a retail complex on Holdom Avenue in Burnaby. The restaurant occupies a unit within a shared commercial building alongside Starbucks, Subway, and a chiropractic clinic, with access to a gated parking lot behind the building. It offers both dine-in and online ordering for cyclists looking for a sit-down Japanese meal stop.

restaurant.name: Kokoro Japanese Ramen House
restaurant.desc: Kokoro Tokyo Mazesoba is a Tokyo-founded chain specializing in mazesoba, a rich, broth-free saucy noodle dish that sparked a mazesoba boom in Japan before expanding to North America. The Surrey location is one of several BC outposts of this internationally growing brand, offering mazesoba, ramen, rice bowls, gyoza, and Japanese soft serve. Cyclists stopping here get a filling, fast Japanese noodle meal with online ordering available for convenience.

restaurant.name: La Trattoria
restaurant.desc: La Trattoria is a long-established Italian restaurant in downtown Maple Ridge, open since 1998 and led by a chef with over two decades of Italian culinary experience. The kitchen follows a "la cucina leggera" philosophy — hearty, full-flavoured dishes made with simply prepared, health-conscious ingredients — and offers gluten-free pasta, appetizers, and entrées. An extensive international wine list, including BC VQA selections, rounds out a sit-down dinner experience.

restaurant.name: Saunter
restaurant.desc: Saunter is a specialty coffee shop opened in 2022 and housed in the historic Victory Building in Gastown, a 1908 structure retaining its original sandstone facade, exposed beams, and red brick. The shop serves espresso classics, specialty teas, hojicha, matcha, and pastries baked fresh each morning in a space deliberately designed around slowing down. A touring cyclist passing through downtown Vancouver can stop here for a quality drink and a bite before continuing on.

restaurant.name: Blasted Church Vineyards
restaurant.desc: Blasted Church Vineyards is an award-winning South Okanagan winery celebrated for its irreverent church-inspired branding and critically acclaimed wines, including a Cabernet Franc recently ranked among BC's top 50 and awarded silver in London. The property features a tasting room with a seasonal food menu, regular live-music events, and two wine club programs. Cyclists riding the Okanagan Falls wine corridor will find it a well-known and lively destination along Parsons Road.

restaurant.name: Pinhalla

The 100-seat venue pairs New York/Sicilian-style pizza and locally brewed craft beer with a hall of 35+ vintage and modern pinball machines. It runs a weekly pinball league, trivia nights, and DJ events, making it a lively stop for cyclists looking for a full meal and entertainment in the heart of downtown.

restaurant.name: Chilli Lee Szechuan Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Chilli Lee is a family-run Szechuan and Cantonese restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver, open since 2010 with the same chef and same address. The menu spans Cantonese classics — soft and crispy chow mein, congee, egg foo yong — alongside real-heat Szechuan dishes, hot pot, and chef's specials. Pickup, delivery, and catering are all available, and the dining room seats 20.

The menu also features a full specialty coffee program, house-blend smoothies named after local landmarks, and a curated selection of Silk Road loose-leaf teas. restaurant.name: Aegir Room

Weekly themed nights — Prime Rib Sundays with live music, Burger & Beer Wednesdays, and Pasta Thursdays — give touring cyclists a reason to time a visit.

restaurant.name: Forecast

restaurant.name: Bean Around The World
restaurant.desc: Bean Around The World is a BC-based specialty coffee roaster with over 30 years in the industry, known for small-batch roasting and blends such as the long-running Rainforest Organic Dark. The brand operates multiple cafe locations alongside an active e-commerce business shipping beans across Canada and the US. Visiting cyclists can expect a no-smoking environment with both indoor and outdoor seating and vegetarian-friendly beverage options.

restaurant.name: Sushi Lovers

restaurant.name: Cafe Du Soleil

It is a cozy, fully licensed bistro with just seven tables and bar seating, emphasizing organic, locally sourced, plant-based vegan and vegetarian West Coast cuisine. Its no-reservations, first-come policy and small group cap of four make it an intimate drop-in stop for cyclists riding through the Grandview Woodlands neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Denny's

Dine-in, takeout, and delivery are all available at this location.

restaurant.name: Cafe Monet Bread & Coffee
restaurant.desc: Cafe Monet is a Korean-influenced bakery and cafe on Vancouver's busy Robson Street, serving espresso drinks, matcha latte, smoothies, and shaved ice alongside baked goods. The air-conditioned indoor space is wheelchair accessible, making it a downtown pit stop in a high-traffic shopping and tourism corridor. The cafe operates under the name 'CAFE MONET Bakery & Cafe' in its own branding.

restaurant.name: Chickasta

restaurant.name: Summerhill Winery

restaurant.name: Beyond Bread Artisan Bakery

restaurant.name: Kove Kitchen

For a cycling tourist, the scenic Steveston waterfront location and relaxed atmosphere make it a natural rest stop on the South Dyke Trail corridor.

restaurant.name: Whole Wheat 'n' Honey Cafe

Fort St. John is one of the few larger centres cyclists encounter across this remote stretch of northern BC.

restaurant.name: The Dime

restaurant.name: Dragon Fort Restaurant

restaurant.name: True Grain

For a touring cyclist, it offers a rare chance to pick up freshly milled flour alongside genuinely artisan sourdough bread and baked goods in a scenic destination village.

restaurant.name: bb.q Chicken

restaurant.name: J's Pizza

Online ordering is available, making it a practical stop for a quick refuel on a longer ride through the valley.

restaurant.name: McDonald's

Free Wi-Fi is available per OSM tagging, consistent with McDonald's Canada standard practice.

restaurant.name: Sura Korean

The restaurant blends timeless Korean tradition with modern elegance, offering classic dishes ranging from hearty soups and stews to Korean BBQ and lunch specials. Situated on busy Robson Street in the heart of downtown, it is a well-established destination for both locals and visitors.

restaurant.name: Sandy's Ukrainian Kitchen

restaurant.name: Edo Japan

restaurant.name: Fortuna Bakery & Deli

restaurant.name: Havana

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza

restaurant.name: BNA Eatery

The venue also houses six 10-pin bowling lanes, making it a lively destination stop rather than just a quick refuel.

restaurant.name: Waffleland Café

restaurant.name: JM7 Bakery
restaurant.desc: JM7 Bakery is a family-owned Filipino bakery in Surrey's Whalley neighbourhood, specializing in traditional baked goods such as pandesal, ube loaf, hopia, and pan de coco. The business traces its roots to Concepcion, Iloilo, Philippines in 1973 and has been baking in BC since 2007, now nearly 20 years under Master Baker Nanay Mila. Touring cyclists will find a range of affordable, carb-dense baked goods well-suited for refuelling on the road.

restaurant.name: Lucha Libre Taqueria
restaurant.desc: Lucha Libre Taqueria — now reimagined as Lucha Libre Barra — is a Mexican street-food and cocktail bar in Vancouver's downtown core, built around the bold vintage aesthetic of classic Lucha Libre wrestling culture, with retro posters, masked-hero iconography, and mid-century Mexican décor. The kitchen serves street-style tacos alongside creative cocktails in a lively bar atmosphere, with online ordering and a catering service available. The venue is part of the Original's Mexicano restaurant group, which operates several related Mexican concepts across Metro Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Diamond sweets & restaurant
restaurant.desc: Diamond Sweets & Restaurant is an authentic Indian cuisine restaurant serving over 100 items including tandoori specialties, Indian sweets, seafood, and vegetarian dishes. It is one of three Metro Vancouver locations operated by the same family, with dine-in, takeout, and mobile catering services. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a full sit-down restaurant experience with a broad vegetarian-friendly menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists 'vegetarian dishes' among 100+ menu items; menu page includes a dedicated 'VEGETABLE specialities' category and vegetarian thali specials

restaurant.name: Izba Bistro
restaurant.desc: Izba Bistro is a Polish and European restaurant in Port Coquitlam led by Chef Iwona, who draws on generations-old recipes to produce handmade perogies, schnitzel, and cabbage rolls. The bistro seats up to 40 guests and cultivates a warm, home-like atmosphere rooted in Polish hospitality. It uses fresh local ingredients alongside certified Angus beef and Oceanwise seafood.

restaurant.name: Jack's Chinese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Jack's Chinese Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant located on Wilkinson Road in Victoria.

restaurant.name: Union Latino's
restaurant.desc: Union Latino's is a Colombian restaurant and Latin event venue on Granville Street in Vancouver, serving authentic dishes like Bandeja Paisa, fresh empanadas, and whole fried tilapia alongside a full bar menu. The space doubles as a party venue with weekly Salsa and Bachata classes, Karaoke nights, and themed Latin events. Owner Miguel Potes opened it to bring traditional Colombian atmosphere — food, music, and warmth — to British Columbia.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page explicitly labels multiple items as Vegetarian, including avocado, coconut rice, french fries, beans, salad, and ripe plantain. Empanadas also available with veggie filling

restaurant.name: Vadapav Mirchi
restaurant.desc: Vadapav Mirchi is a strictly vegetarian Indian restaurant specializing in Maharashtrian street food, with the signature dish being vada pav — a deep-fried spiced potato dumpling served in a bread bun with garlic chutney and fried green chillies. The menu spans traditional Maharashtra staples including Misal Pav, Pav Bhaji, Puran Poli, and Thalipeeth, representing a regional Indian cuisine rarely found in the Lower Mainland. A touring cyclist seeking a filling, meat-free meal near New Westminster's 12th Street corridor would find this a distinctive stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu confirms all items are vegetarian. Pithla Bhakri (Bajra/Jowar) described as 'naturally gluten free.'

restaurant.name: Sandrine French Pastry and Chocolate
restaurant.desc: Sandrine French Pastry and Chocolate is a well-regarded French patisserie in Kelowna offering handcrafted pastries, macarons, artisan chocolates, celebration cakes, and a coffee menu. The shop has expanded to two Kelowna locations — the original on Dilworth Drive and a newer outpost in Lower Mission on Lakeshore Road. Vegan, gluten-free, and dairy-free options are available, and the online shop ships products internationally.

restaurant.name: Kafka's
restaurant.desc: Kafka's Coffee is a Vancouver specialty roaster and multi-location cafe that has been sourcing beans directly from farmers and roasting them in-house weekly since opening on Main Street in 2010. The Gastown outpost is described as featuring bright colours and huge windows, with an emphasis on high-quality espresso and pour-over coffee. Kafka's doubles as a community arts hub, regularly rotating gallery shows by local painters, photographers, and illustrators.

detail.address: 151 W Hastings St, Vancouver, BC V6B 1H4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels 'NOT-MEATBALLS SUB' (Beyond Plant-Based Meatballs, tahini, Moroccan sauce) as Vegan; multiple other vegetarian-compatible items visible on the Park and Great Northern Way menus

restaurant.name: Super Thai Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Super Thai Hot Pot is a Southeast Asian-inspired restaurant on Vancouver's Kingsway corridor specialising in interactive Malatang-style hot pot, where diners handpick fresh ingredients cooked tableside in a choice of house-made broths ranging from classic Thai Tom Yum to spicy Signature Malatang. The extensive broth menu draws on Thai, Chinese, and Cantonese traditions, making it a distinctive stop for cyclists looking for a hearty, communal meal. Online ordering and delivery are available for those who prefer a quick pick-up.

restaurant.name: Captain's Oven Pizza
restaurant.desc: Captain's Oven Pizza is a Neapolitan-style pizza restaurant that bakes its hand-tossed pies in a custom 3-ton stone brick oven shipped directly from Regello, Tuscany, cooking each pizza in about two minutes at up to 1,000 degrees. The Langley location on Fraser Highway is one of five BC locations, offering a broad menu of artisan pizzas made with imported Italian ingredients like fior di latte and grana padano. Cyclists passing through Langley will find a full sit-down restaurant experience with online ordering and local delivery also available.

detail.address: 19705 Fraser Highway Unit 520, Langley, BC V3A 7E9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQs confirm gluten-free pizza crust available (not a GF environment), vegan cheese offered, and pizzas can be customized for vegan/vegetarian diets; salads also customizable

restaurant.name: Kurotaki
restaurant.desc: Kurotaki House is a casual Taiwanese restaurant located in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood near the University Canada West campus, serving beef noodle soup, braised pork rice, popcorn chicken, and a full range of boba milk teas. The space is designed as a social hub with varied seating — from standard restaurant chairs to coffee-table-style nooks — and is equally welcoming to solo diners and large groups. Alcoholic beverages including beer, soju, and wine are also on offer.

restaurant.name: Red Chilli Szechuan
restaurant.desc: Red Chilli Szechuan is a long-running authentic Szechuan Chinese restaurant in North Vancouver's Lower Lonsdale neighbourhood with over 25 years of operation. The kitchen specialises in boldly spiced Szechuan classics — hot-and-sour soup, wontons in spicy garlic pepper, ma po tofu — alongside a broader menu of seafood, pork, beef, and vegetarian dishes. The restaurant has been a repeat winner of the Readers' Choice Award and offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery, making it a solid stop for a hungry cyclist rolling through Lonsdale.

detail.address: 741 Lonsdale Avenue, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2G9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Contact page states: 'We offer vegetarian and pescatarian options in addition to our pork, lamb, chicken, beef, noodles, rice dishes.' Menu labels multiple dishes as Vegetarian

restaurant.name: Great Wall Mongolian BBQ
restaurant.desc: Great Wall Mongolian BBQ is a mongolian grill restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver. Touring cyclists can stop for dine-in meals. No further details are available due to website access restrictions.

restaurant.name: Black Sheep Pub
restaurant.desc: The Black Sheep Public House is a long-running neighbourhood pub established in 1987, voted the best pub in the Maple Ridge and Ridge Meadows area. It seats over 200 people and pours more than 18 beers on tap alongside an extensive food menu, with a full liquor store occupying an adjacent corner of the building. Situated just minutes from Golden Ears Park, it makes a solid stop for cyclists coming off the trails or riding the Fraser Valley routes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu marks multiple items with (V) for vegetarian: Spinach & Artichoke Dip, Yam Fries, and Tzatziki Dip

restaurant.name: Mui Garden
restaurant.desc: Mui Garden is a Hong Kong-style cafe established in Vancouver since 1992, celebrated for its authentic Malaysian curry blended from over twenty spices and its world-famous Hai-Nam chicken made with both free-range and farm chickens. Originally operating in Hong Kong for over a decade before opening its first Canadian location on Victoria Drive, the restaurant has grown to four Greater Vancouver locations. The Victoria Drive spot offers full dine-in service and online ordering, making it a convenient meal stop in East Vancouver.

notes.Takeout: Website lists 'Online Order: Daily 11:00am – 8:15pm' for the Vancouver location, with a dedicated online ordering system

restaurant.name: JJang Korean BBQ and Social House
restaurant.desc: JJang Korean BBQ & Social House is a Korean barbecue restaurant in Richmond's Hollybridge development, offering a 'social house' dining format. The restaurant manages both reservations and a live waitlist, reflecting consistent demand from the local community. It is a sit-down establishment that could serve as a substantial meal stop for cyclists in the area.

detail.address: 5668 Hollybridge Way, Unit 115, Richmond, BC V7C 4N3

restaurant.name: City Pizza
restaurant.desc: City Pizza is a pizza-focused fast-food counter in Abbotsford offering an unusually broad menu that blends classic North American pies with South Asian-inspired options like Butter Chicken, Tandoori Chicken, and Shahi Paneer pizzas. The shop offers both delivery and quick pickup, with a full menu of pizzas, pasta, wings, burgers, wraps, and lassi drinks. Customer reviews highlight friendly staff and consistent quality, making it a viable calorie stop for cyclists passing through the Clearbrook corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu legend explicitly marks vegetarian items; dedicated 'Veggie Pizzas' section lists 12 options including Garden Veggie, Greek Veggie, and Veggie Korma. No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: W Breakfast & Lunch
restaurant.desc: W Breakfast & Lunch (marketed on its own website as W Restaurant) is a sit-down restaurant in downtown Fort St. John serving western-style breakfast and lunch fare — from fluffy pancakes and eggs benedicts to hearty hash, burgers, and sandwiches — crafted with an emphasis on fresh ingredients. The restaurant operates seven days a week and offers online ordering through Square for takeout convenience. Fort St. John sits along the Alaska Highway corridor, making it a natural resupply point for long-distance touring cyclists heading north.

detail.address: 9608 100 St, Fort St. John, BC V1J 3X8

restaurant.name: Damiko Sushi
restaurant.desc: Damiko Sushi is a Japanese restaurant occupying a retail unit on King George Boulevard in Surrey, BC. It is the sole remaining open location following the permanent closure of the Langley branch, and offers both dine-in service and online ordering. Touring cyclists riding the King George corridor will find it a convenient stop for a sushi meal.

restaurant.name: White Rock Beach Beer
restaurant.desc: White Rock Beach Beer Company is a craft microbrewery founded in 2013 by two local secondary school teachers, operating a tasting room and lounge where visitors can try a range of house beers on tap. The lineup spans lagers, pilsners, pale ales, wheat ales, an IPA, and a porter, all brewed on-site and available by the glass or as growler fills and canned 6-packs to take away. Located near the White Rock waterfront — a popular Lower Mainland cycling corridor — it makes a relaxed stop for riders exploring the area.

restaurant.name: The Beanery Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Beanery Cafe is a specialty espresso and all-day cafe nestled in the Okanagan desert wine country of Summerland, BC, serving elevated espresso drinks, lattes, smoothies, sandwiches, and breakfast and lunch. The cafe leans hard into a bold, irreverent identity while explicitly welcoming vegan, paleo, and gluten-free guests. It also offers online ordering and catering, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists passing through the South Okanagan.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Vegans, Paleo and Gluten-Free friends are welcome'

restaurant.name: El Cafecito
restaurant.desc: El Cafecito is the daytime café concept within Alimentaria Mexicana, an authentic Mexican restaurant and cultural gathering place on Granville Island, directly across from the main public market entrance. The broader establishment celebrates Mexican culinary traditions through housemade heirloom corn chips, chilaquiles, birria, and an extensive mezcal and tequila program. Regular spirits workshops and taco omakase events make this a destination rather than just a pit stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items explicitly labeled '(VEGAN)': Golden Beet Ceviche, Greens con Pipián Verde, Soy Chorizo & Papas tacos. Additional vegetarian items (halloumi tostada, chilaquiles) are present

restaurant.name: Bridgemans Bistro
restaurant.desc: Bridgemans Bistro sits at the water's edge at Mill Bay Marina on the Saanich Inlet, serving West Coast-inspired lunch and dinner menus built around locally sourced seafood and regional ingredients. Every table takes in views of the inlet and Mount Baker, with local beers on tap and Cowichan Valley wines rounding out the experience. The no-reservations, first-come-first-served policy means touring cyclists can walk in without advance planning.

restaurant.name: King Taps
restaurant.desc: King Taps Lakeside is a multi-story waterfront restaurant and craft beer bar located along the Kelowna boardwalk, with panoramic Okanagan Lake views from its large patio and direct boardwalk access. The menu leans into Italian-inspired cooking, handmade pizzas, and shareable plates, paired with a weekly-rotating selection of regional BC craft beers and local wines. A lively spot with event space and regular programming, it sits squarely on the lakefront route that most Kelowna-area cyclists travel.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website describes menu as approachable for everyone with broad options

restaurant.name: Damien's Belgian Waffles
restaurant.desc: Damien's Belgian Waffles is a small independent restaurant in Richmond, BC, specializing in Belgian-style waffles. It occupies a unit on Chatham Street and maintains its public presence primarily through Instagram. The business appears to be a compact, locally run café-style operation.

restaurant.name: The Chopped Leaf
restaurant.desc: The Chopped Leaf is a proudly Canadian fast-casual chain founded in 2009, now with 124+ locations, specializing in customizable salads, wraps, bowls, soups, and sandwiches built around fresh greens. The Surrey location on 56 Ave sits within a commercial area and offers a menu designed to feel like comfort food while staying health-forward. Touring cyclists looking for a quick, lighter meal stop would find a broad range of customizable options including a kids menu and signature dressings.

restaurant.name: Time Out Cafe & Market
restaurant.desc: Time Out Cafe is a café listed on OSM at 1150 Melville Street in downtown Vancouver. The associated website describes a Korean food concept — fried chicken and traditional dishes such as cheese kimchi rice and mussel soup — but that content is tied to a Davie Street address, raising uncertainty about what is actually offered at the Melville Street location.

restaurant.name: Chicko Chicken
restaurant.desc: Chicko Chicken is a Korean fried chicken fast food chain with dozens of locations across BC and Canada. The Burnaby Metrotown location sits on Kingsway and offers indoor seating with card payment accepted. Cyclists passing through the Metrotown corridor will find it a quick stop for a hot meal.

restaurant.name: Nuba
restaurant.desc: Nuba is a well-established Vancouver Lebanese restaurant group with four city locations; the Yaletown 'Canteen' on Davie Street occupies a striking space fitted with overlapping ogival arches and wooden screens that blend traditional Middle Eastern geometry with a modern urban aesthetic. Founded nearly 20 years ago, Nuba sources fresh, local, and organic ingredients daily and emphasizes scratch cooking, with a large share of the menu being vegan and halal-certified meats. The Davie Street location includes both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a solid meal stop in a busy, cyclist-friendly neighbourhood.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu confirms numerous items labelled 'Vegan, GF' (e.g. hummus varieties, Garden Falafel, Najib's Special, Mjadra) and 'Vegetarian' dishes throughout brunch and lunch menus

restaurant.name: Thai Basil
restaurant.desc: Thai Basil is a Thai restaurant chain established in 2008, with this Cornwall Ave location serving the Kitsilano neighbourhood near the popular seaside cycling routes along the Vancouver waterfront. The menu spans a full range of Thai classics — curries, noodle soups, salads, and appetizers — with both dine-in and takeout available. It is one of four Vancouver locations operated under the same brand.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu offers tofu as a protein choice across curries, noodle soups, and appetizers (e.g. Deep Fried Tofu, curries with tofu option). No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Judge Begbie's Tavern
restaurant.desc: Judge Begbies Tavern is a lively neighborhood sports bar and live-entertainment venue anchored on historic Columbia Street in New Westminster's downtown core. It screens major league sports including Canucks, Whitecaps, and NFL games, and hosts weekly open mic nights and karaoke, drawing a regular local crowd. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available in a non-smoking setting.

restaurant.name: Icy Bar
restaurant.desc: Icy Bar is a Taiwanese-style shaved-ice dessert bar specializing in DIY bowls, signature fruity shaved icy, and soft snowflake milk ice customized with toppings like mochi, grass jelly, fresh fruit, and red bean. The Richmond shop is one of several Lower Mainland locations and also offers catering and self-serve dessert stations for private events. It could serve as a cooling refreshment stop for touring cyclists passing through the Number 3 Road corridor.

restaurant.name: Spice of Life
restaurant.desc: Spice of Life is an Indian restaurant in Prince George, BC. The restaurant caters to dietary preferences with dedicated vegetarian and pescetarian options, making it accessible for cyclists with diverse dietary needs.

restaurant.name: Sapporo Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Sapporo Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant in Surrey's 152 Street area offering dine-in service alongside online ordering through its website and a dedicated mobile app with a loyalty rewards program. It is a convenient sit-down meal option for touring cyclists passing through South Surrey.

restaurant.name: Socrates in the Heights
restaurant.desc: Socrates in the Heights is a family-run Greek restaurant on Hastings Street in Burnaby, where the current chef continues recipes developed alongside his father over 23 years. The menu leans heavily Greek — souvlaki, moussaka, lamb chops, spanakopita — with outdoor seating and a full catering operation for events. Touring cyclists on the Hastings corridor can stop in for a sit-down meal or grab a souvlaki wrap and Greek fries to go.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes veggie wrap (chickpea carrot & feta fritters), spanakopita, Greek and kale Caesar salads, bulgur salad, and multiple dips — clearly vegetarian options available

restaurant.name: Artisan Bistro
restaurant.desc: Artisan Bistro is a West Coast-inspired casual dining restaurant set inside Broadmead Village Shopping Centre in the Saanich area of Victoria, with a menu built around local ingredients spanning pasta, fish and chips, handcrafted cocktails, and a curated BC wine list. The espresso bar runs on locally roasted Fernwood Coffee beans, and a spacious outdoor patio accommodates 25–30 guests. The kitchen explicitly caters to vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free diets, and the restaurant is reachable via Uber Eats, SkipTheDishes, and DoorDash in addition to in-house takeout.

detail.address: 350 – 777 Royal Oak Drive, Victoria, BC V8X 4V1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ explicitly states: 'Yes, we offer a variety of vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options on our menu.' Lunch page also flags individual items as gluten-free or vegetarian

restaurant.name: Lumiere Cafe
restaurant.desc: Lumiere Cafe is a multi-location Vancouver artisanal coffee cafe specializing in micro-batch roasting of single-origin beans sourced from Ethiopia, Colombia, Rwanda, Kenya, and other origins. Their mission centres on an elevated cafe experience using high-quality ingredients and advanced preparation techniques. The West Broadway location sits near the Cambie Street intersection in a busy urban corridor.

restaurant.name: Deer Lake Wonton House
restaurant.desc: Deer Lake Wonton House is a Chinese restaurant in North Vancouver offering indoor dining. It provides a casual meal stop for touring cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: Kung Fu Noodle
restaurant.desc: Kung Fu Noodle is a Chinese noodle restaurant in Vancouver's Kingsway neighbourhood, specializing in northern Chinese cuisine including hand-pulled Lanzhou beef noodle soup, dim sum, and a range of chow mein and rice dishes. The menu spans a wide variety from spicy Sichuan-style fish and beef dishes to milder stir-fries and dumplings, giving hungry cyclists plenty of hearty refuelling options. Online ordering for pickup is available.

restaurant.name: Superbolt Lab
restaurant.desc: Superbolt Lab is a specialty tea retail store and tea bar in the Kitsilano neighbourhood of Vancouver, operated by Superbolt™ Tea, a local brand focused on performance and wellness. The shop offers high-grade matcha sourced from a family-run farm in Shizuoka, Japan alongside proprietary functional tea blends formulated with adaptogens and superfoods to support energy, focus, and recovery. It is a distinctive stop for cyclists interested in organic, sugar-free alternatives to coffee and conventional energy drinks.

restaurant.name: Bread x Butter
restaurant.desc: Bread x Butter is a gourmet sandwich and breakfast cafe situated at the corner of Hornby and Georgia in downtown Vancouver, built around freshly baked artisan bread and locally sourced ingredients. The menu leans into Asian fusion touches — wagyu beef with kewpie mayo, unagi egg toast, Hawaiian Luau SPAM brioche — alongside classic breakfast and sandwich fare. The cafe also features a beautiful outdoor courtyard accommodating up to 200 people and a fully licensed bar, doubling as a private event venue.

detail.address: 925 West Georgia Street, Unit 140, Vancouver, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Catering menu uses 'VG - Vegetarian | GF - Gluten Free' labels throughout; explicit vegan items listed (vegan avocado toast, vegan cookies, vegan apple muffin, fully vegan boxed breakfast options); gluten-free loaf and GF bread substitution available

restaurant.name: Faubourg Paris
restaurant.desc: Faubourg is a family-owned French bakery-café founded in Vancouver in 2010, offering freshly baked baguettes, viennoiseries, pastries, and macarons made on-site daily using traditional French techniques. The Yaletown location on Davie Street also serves a curated specialty coffee program with single-origin blends sourced from Peru, Brazil, and Ethiopia. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a comfortable stop for a coffee and croissant mid-ride.

restaurant.name: End Dive
restaurant.desc: End Dive is a downtown Victoria restaurant offering both seated reservations and walk-in bar service on Government Street. The venue is adults-only (19+) and focuses on intimate dining. Touring cyclists will find it a useful food stop, though advance reservations are recommended for seating.

restaurant.name: Firehouse Subs
restaurant.desc: Firehouse Subs is a North American sandwich chain with a public-safety theme, known for hot subs piled with premium meats and toppings. This Victoria location sits in a retail unit and serves the standard Firehouse menu. For touring cyclists passing through the area, it offers a reliably familiar stop for a substantial hot meal.

restaurant.name: Liberty Wines
restaurant.desc: Liberty Wine Merchants is a Vancouver institution founded in 1986, built on a mission to source rare and artisan wines from small-batch producers worldwide rather than mass-market labels. The Granville Island location places it within one of Vancouver's most-visited waterfront destinations and a natural stop on the seawall cycling route. The shop carries an extensive range of wine, spirits, beer, cider, and sake.

restaurant.name: NoodleBox
restaurant.desc: NoodleBox is a Canadian fast-casual franchise specializing in customizable wok-fired Asian noodle and rice dishes, with sauces spanning Pad Thai, Cambodian Jungle Curry, Kung Pao, and beyond. Every box is made to order at the counter, and a range of dishes can be modified for vegan or gluten-friendly diets on request. Touring cyclists in the Tri-Cities area can stop in for a hot, filling meal with their choice of protein, noodle type, and sauce.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Can be made VEGAN — Please ask when ordering' and 'Can be made GLUTEN-FRIENDLY — Please ask when ordering' for identified dishes

restaurant.name: Ba Le Deli & Bakery
restaurant.desc: Ba Le Deli & Bakery is a family-owned Vietnamese delicatessen that has been baking its own French baguettes and crafting bánh mì sandwiches in Vancouver since 1987. The Broadway location is one of several across Metro Vancouver, offering a broad menu of sandwiches, vermicelli bowls, and drinks at street-food prices. Its long-standing community reputation and quick-service takeout format make it a practical and flavourful mid-ride food stop on East Broadway.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly includes Vegan Steak Banh Mi, Vegan Bologna Banh Mi, Vegetarian Lemongrass Chicken Banh Mi, Classic Vietnamese Veggie Sandwich, and Vermicelli Bowl with Tofu and Spring Rolls. No GF claim found

restaurant.name: Nammos Estiatorio
restaurant.desc: Nammos Estiatorio is a modern Greek restaurant on Vancouver's Fraser Street serving traditional Mediterranean dishes family-style, with house-made cocktails and an exclusively Greek wine list. The restaurant has been featured in the Michelin Guide, Montecristo Magazine, and Destination Vancouver, placing it among the city's more acclaimed neighbourhood dining destinations. Dishes span Greek classics from hand-rolled dolmathes and saganaki to grilled octopus and slow-roasted lamb shoulder.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'MOUSSAKA BEEF OR VEGETARIAN' and includes multiple vegetarian-suitable dishes: Spanakopita, Horiatiki, Marouli, Dolmathes, Hummus, and vegetable sides

restaurant.name: Finch x Barley
restaurant.desc: Finch x Barley is a music-centric bar and restaurant in North Vancouver offering a globally influenced menu with a strong focus on Middle Eastern culinary traditions alongside craft beer, cocktails, wine, and spirits. The venue hosts regular Friday and Saturday night DJ sets and occasional live music, making it a lively social destination. A patio is available, and the food program spans brunch plates, dinner mains, and a full cocktail list.

detail.address: 250 East 1st Street, North Vancouver, BC V7L 1B3

restaurant.name: Buffalo Bill's
restaurant.desc: Buffalo Bill's is a pub in Whistler, BC, serving as a casual food and beverage destination in the mountain resort community.

detail.address: 4122 Village Green, Whistler, BC V8E 1G9, Canada

restaurant.name: Lions Bay General Store & Café
restaurant.desc: Lions Bay General Store & Café combines a convenience store and café serving this small British Columbia coastal community. As a combined venue offering both supplies and food service, it provides a useful stop for local and touring cyclists passing through the area.

detail.address: 350 Centre Road, Lions Bay, BC V0N 2E0

restaurant.name: The Central
restaurant.desc: The Central is a nightclub and bar in Fernie, BC, housed in one of the only buildings to survive the town's catastrophic fire of 1908. Owned and operated by the Himalayan Spice Bistro, it functions as Fernie's primary live music and dance venue, hosting touring and local acts throughout the year. Touring cyclists looking for a lively evening stop in a venue with genuine local history will find it here.

restaurant.name: Ships A-Hoy
restaurant.desc: A fish and chips restaurant on Beach Avenue in Naramata, a scenic touring destination in BC's wine country. The establishment occupies a commercial building and serves as a casual dining option for passing cyclists.

restaurant.name: Space Chicken
restaurant.desc: Space Chicken is a halal-certified chicken fast-food restaurant on the Kingsway corridor in Vancouver, serving an extensive space-themed menu of crispy and grilled chicken pieces, galaxy-branded burgers, wraps, salads, and combo meals. The restaurant offers indoor seating and partners with major delivery platforms for online ordering. Its location on a major east-west arterial makes it a convenient fuel stop for cyclists passing through East Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: This Subway franchise sits in Lake Cowichan, a small Vancouver Island community at the western end of Cowichan Lake and a natural stop on cycling routes through the Cowichan Valley. It offers the standard Subway lineup of footlongs, 6-inch sandwiches, wraps, and salads built with fresh-baked bread and fresh-cut vegetables. Orders can be placed for in-store pickup, delivery, or curbside pickup, and the location accepts all major credit cards.

restaurant.name: Dosa Club Indian Kitchen & Bar
restaurant.desc: Dosa Club is a modern South Indian restaurant in Chilliwack offering elevated takes on dosas, tandoori, biryani, and street-food-inspired dishes. The restaurant blends authentic South Indian culinary heritage with a contemporary dining space and attentive service. It accepts online orders and table reservations, serving both the Chilliwack and Abbotsford communities.

restaurant.name: Spice Republic Indian Restaurant & Lounge
restaurant.desc: Spice Republic Indian Restaurant & Lounge is a full-service Indian restaurant in Surrey offering traditional and contemporary Indian cuisine in a stylish dining space with both indoor and outdoor seating. The restaurant emphasizes authentic spices and bold flavors, catering to relaxed lunches, intimate dinners, and group outings. Online ordering, pickup, and delivery within 15 km are available, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: La Reina DT
restaurant.desc: La Reina DT is a restaurant in Chilliwack with outdoor seating and public entrance. Website information is currently unavailable for detailed verification.

restaurant.name: Bicycle Pizza
restaurant.desc: Bicycle Pizza is a small-but-mighty pop-up pizza operation serving hand-tossed, thin-crust pizzas at events, markets, and community celebrations around greater Victoria. They hold regular weekly spots at Junction Orchard + Cidery and offer full catering with pizza, brunch, charcuterie, and sweet carts. Recognized by enRoute magazine as 2022 Best New Takeout, they are a beloved local operation with deep Island roots.

restaurant.name: Tacofino Ocho
restaurant.desc: Tacofino Ocho is the Vancouver outpost of the beloved BC-born Tacofino chain, which grew from a humble Tofino food truck into a regional institution known for Mexican-inspired west coast cooking. Situated in the Mount Pleasant neighbourhood at the corner of East 5th and Main, it makes a natural stop on one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors. Cyclists can order at the counter or pick up online orders, and delivery-app pickup options are also available.

restaurant.name: 4 Seasons Chaat House
restaurant.desc: 4 Seasons Chaat House is a casual Indian street-food restaurant in New Westminster specializing in authentic chaats, samosas, pav bhaji, and clay-oven tandoori dishes. The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating in a lively atmosphere with Hindi music and a menu spanning North and South Indian cuisine. Reviewers consistently praise the generous portions, fresh ingredients, and welcoming owner.

restaurant.name: Hana Sushi

The restaurant operates an online ordering platform with 15-minute pickup, making it a practical stop for cyclists moving through the city core. OSM records wheelchair accessibility and a non-smoking indoor dining room.
