restaurant.name: Sen Pho + Cafe
restaurant.desc: Vietnamese pho restaurant and cafe in Vancouver's Champlain Heights area, specializing in traditional Vietnamese cuisine. Offers dine-in service with reservations available.

restaurant.name: Springwater Lodge
restaurant.desc: Springwater Lodge is a pub located on what appears to be Mayne Island in British Columbia's Gulf Islands, based on its coordinates and Facebook URL. As a pub on a Gulf Islands ferry route, it would likely serve as a natural stop for cycle tourists travelling between islands. No additional detail about the venue could be confirmed due to the Facebook page being inaccessible during prefetch.

detail.address: 400 Fernhill Road, Miners Bay, Mayne Island, BC

restaurant.name: SunTea
restaurant.desc: SunTea is a BC-born bubble tea chain founded in 2019, specialising in fresh-brewed fruit tea and milk tea with locations across BC and Alberta. The Hastings Street Burnaby outpost is a pickup-focused shop with online ordering through the SunTea app or website. A recently launched 1-litre Mega Size option makes it a notable hydration stop for cyclists passing through East Burnaby.

restaurant.name: Panorama Pizza and Curry
restaurant.desc: Panorama Pizza and Curry is a Surrey restaurant serving both pizza and Indian curry dishes, catering to a broad range of tastes under one roof. Cyclists can order ahead online and pick up a hot meal without waiting, or take advantage of the delivery service. The dual-cuisine menu makes it an unusual and practical stop for groups with mixed preferences.

detail.address: 6225 136 Street Unit A, Surrey, BC V3X 1H3

restaurant.name: Barb's Fish & Chips
restaurant.desc: Barb's Fish & Chips is a floating restaurant moored in Victoria's Inner Harbour, serving classic fish and chips from a converted two-storey vessel with a distinctive blue roof. It is a long-standing Victoria landmark and a natural stop for cyclists arriving via the Inner Harbour pathways. The waterfront setting and casual takeout-style format make it a memorable rest point on any touring loop through the city.

restaurant.name: Hoa Phuong Do
restaurant.desc: Hoa Phuong Do is a Vietnamese restaurant on Victoria Drive in Vancouver's East Side, serving the Fraserview and Killarney neighbourhoods. The restaurant operates bilingually in English and French, and offers online ordering with both pickup and delivery options via their own website. Cyclists passing through this stretch of Victoria Drive will find it a convenient sit-down or takeout stop for Vietnamese food.

detail.address: 5088 Victoria Dr, Vancouver, BC V5P 3T8, Canada

restaurant.name: Lee's Donuts
restaurant.desc: Lee's Donuts is a beloved BC institution founded in 1979 at Granville Island Public Market, now expanded to multiple locations including Lower Lonsdale in North Vancouver. All donuts are handmade fresh daily in small batches from scratch using the original recipes developed by founders Alan and Betty Lee. The shop has earned a cult following over 45+ years and has been featured on Netflix.

detail.address: 124 West 1st Street, Unit 100, North Vancouver, BC

restaurant.name: La Playita Seafood
restaurant.desc: La Playita Seafood is a Mexican seafood restaurant located on Cambie Street in downtown Vancouver. It offers takeout service and is situated in a dense urban corridor convenient to cyclists navigating the city centre. The Instagram-only web presence suggests a casual, community-oriented spot.

restaurant.name: Yaga Cafe Garden Co.
restaurant.desc: Yaga Cafe Garden Co. is an award-winning, Indigenous community-owned business operated by the Gitmaxmak'ay Nisga'a Society in Seal Cove — 'Yaga' meaning 'down a hill' in Nisga'a, an apt description of its hillside location. The cafe serves coffee, tea, sandwiches, snacks, and salads harvested fresh from onsite hydroponics greenhouses, with an outdoor patio overlooking the cove. The business has operated continuously at this site since 1991 and is a recipient of the 2021 BC Indigenous Community-Owned Business of the Year award.

detail.address: 2250 Bellis Road, Prince Rupert, BC V8J 2P2

restaurant.name: Shanghai Lao Wei Dao
restaurant.desc: Shanghai Lao Wei Dao is a Shanghai-style Chinese fast-food spot in Richmond serving an extensive menu of hand-crafted dumplings, xiao long bao, pan-fried buns, noodle soups, and rice dishes rooted in classic Shanghai home cooking. The restaurant offers convenient online pickup ordering through its own website. A touring cyclist passing through Richmond's McKim Way commercial area can grab a filling meal of wontons, beef noodles, or a combo plate to go.

restaurant.name: Purple Grain
restaurant.desc: Purple Grain is a health-focused café inside Vancouver General Hospital's Diamond Plaza Building, serving fresh salads, warm bowls, pho, smoothies, and hot rolls made from wholesome ingredients prepared daily. The globally inspired menu includes Salmon Poke Bowls, Masala Chickpea Buddha Bowls, Jamaican Patties, and an extensive catering program. It is open to the public and draws a mix of hospital staff, visitors, and neighbourhood regulars.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu labels many items (v) vegetarian and (gf) gluten free throughout; catering menu explicitly notes 'Chia Pudding or Overnight Oats (vegan)'

restaurant.name: Don at Kitsilano
restaurant.desc: Don at Kitsilano is a restaurant in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood. As a food establishment, it provides a meal stop for touring cyclists. Website information is currently unavailable for detailed verification.

restaurant.name: Osmow's
restaurant.desc: Osmow's is a Canadian shawarma chain founded in 2001 by Egyptian immigrant Sam Osmow, now spanning more than 225 locations across Canada and the U.S. The Richmond Bridgeport location serves chicken and beef shawarma, falafel, and signature dishes like Chicken On the Rocks® and Chicken On the Stix®, all made to order with proprietary spice blends and a signature garlic sauce. Dine-in, takeout, delivery, and catering are all available, making it a practical fuel stop for cyclists passing through Richmond's Bridgeport commercial area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Falafel listed as a menu protein option alongside chicken and beef, confirming at least one vegetarian choice

restaurant.name: Menbow Ramen Bar
restaurant.desc: Menbow Ramen Bar is an authentic Japanese ramen restaurant in downtown Victoria, part of a growing BC chain with locations on Vancouver Island and the Lower Mainland. The kitchen imports key ingredients directly from Japan and is one of the few ramen spots offering both creamy Tonkotsu (pork bone) and clear Tori (chicken) broths across multiple flavor profiles including Shio, Shoyu, Miso, and a vegetarian Tomato Ramen. Cyclists looking for a hot, filling bowl after a long ride can dine in or order pickup through the restaurant's online ordering system.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists Tomato Ramen as '(Vegetarian)' in the menu description

restaurant.name: The Blue Nile
restaurant.desc: The Blue Nile is a sit-down East African restaurant in the heart of Victoria specializing in authentic Ethiopian and Eritrean cuisine, where dishes of richly spiced stews, lentils, and vegetables are served communally atop injera flatbread. The menu is extensive, covering poultry, beef, and a full range of vegan and vegetarian dishes, with gluten-free substitutions available. Ethiopian coffee (Bunna) is prepared tableside in the traditional roast-and-brew ceremony, making this a distinctive cultural dining stop for touring cyclists passing through downtown Victoria.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu has a dedicated 'Vegan combos' section and multiple vegetarian dishes (Shiro, Bursen Tumtumo, Hamli Kawlo, etc.). Website states: 'All dishes are gluten free except injera. For Gluten Free option substitute rice instead of Injera.'

restaurant.name: Sam's Sushi Bar
restaurant.desc: Sam's Sushi Bar has been serving artisan sushi in Parksville, BC since 2007, making it a long-standing local institution on Vancouver Island's cycling corridor. The menu spans classic rolls, bento boxes, yakisoba, and large party trays, with both dine-in and takeout available most days. Touring cyclists looking for a sit-down Japanese meal near the Parksville waterfront will find a compact, focused menu sourced for freshness — the restaurant notes it may close early if fresh supplies run out.

restaurant.name: Craft 42 Roasters
restaurant.desc: Craft 42 Roasters is a specialty coffee roaster and café in Kelowna that sources competition-level, single-origin beans from Colombia, Ethiopia, Guatemala, and Honduras through Canadian importers with an emphasis on fair wages and sustainable packaging. The name references the childhood home address of the founder, and the business carries those family values — compassion, respect, and education — into every aspect of sourcing and roasting. Cyclists stopping in can also book a guided coffee tasting experience or browse brewing gear alongside their café visit.

restaurant.name: Mill Bay Sushi
restaurant.desc: A sushi restaurant located in Sidney. As a food service establishment, it may serve touring cyclists seeking a meal.

restaurant.name: Pita Pit
restaurant.desc: Pita Pit is a Canadian fast-casual chain serving customizable pita sandwiches, salads, and rice bowls made to order. This Christina Lake location on McGregor Frontage Road sits along a key corridor for cyclists riding through the Boundary region. Smoothies are confirmed available at this location, and both takeout and delivery ordering are offered.

detail.address: 1590 McGregor Frontage Road, Christina Lake, V0H 1E0

restaurant.name: Guu with Otokomae
restaurant.desc: Guu with Otokomae is a Japanese izakaya restaurant in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, part of the Guu Izakaya chain credited as the pioneer of izakaya dining in Canada. The name 'Otokomae' evokes 'true masculinity' and the kitchen applies near-artisanal precision to its dishes, making them as visually striking as they are satisfying. The space works equally well for a boisterous group or a quieter counter-seat dinner for two.

restaurant.name: Horstman Hut
restaurant.desc: Horstman Hut is an on-mountain dining venue operated by Whistler Blackcomb, located high on Blackcomb Mountain near the Horstman Glacier area. It functions as a warming hut and restaurant serving guests accessing the alpine zone, primarily in winter by chairlift and in summer via the PEAK 2 PEAK gondola or on-mountain hiking. For a touring cyclist, reaching it on two wheels would require either lift access or a substantial mountain climb.

restaurant.name: Harbour Spoon
restaurant.desc: Harbour Spoon is an Eastern European restaurant tucked into the Harbour Centre food court in downtown Vancouver, serving hand-made comfort food including borscht, pierogies, cabbage rolls, Siberian pelmeni, and traditional pastries alongside house-made fermented beverages like kvass and cranberry mors. The kitchen prides itself on using locally sourced ingredients with no preservatives, MSG, GMO, or nuts. It's a rare find for cyclists wanting an affordable, filling, made-from-scratch meal in the heart of the city.

detail.address: 555 West Hastings Street, FC-12, Vancouver, BC V6B 4N6

restaurant.name: 4 Brothers' Pizza
restaurant.desc: 4 Brothers Pizza is a Vancouver pizza chain emphasizing consistent quality made from high-quality ingredients, with online ordering available. restaurant.name: Coffee On The Moon
restaurant.desc: Coffee on the Moon is a community gathering place in downtown Duncan that has been serving the Cowichan Valley since 1997, with two locations in the area. Beyond specialty coffee, smoothies, and fresh-baked food, the cafe doubles as a rotating gallery for local and regional artists. Cyclists stopping in will find a welcoming, linger-worthy atmosphere with vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free menu options.

restaurant.name: Greenhorn Cafe
restaurant.desc: Greenhorn Cafe is a neighbourhood brunch and coffee spot in Vancouver's West End, offering indoor dining, a patio, and online takeout ordering through Ritual. The menu is notable for extensive vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free labelling across its brunch lineup. The cafe also hosts private evening events, making it a flexible space that operates well beyond a typical quick-stop.

restaurant.name: Beef Broccoli

The restaurant offers dine-in and takeout service, with a broad menu that includes gluten-free and vegetarian options. It sits within a commercial complex near Louie Drive, a corridor accessible to cyclists riding through the West Kelowna area.

restaurant.name: Myth Dessert & Patisserie
restaurant.desc: Myth Dessert & Patisserie is a cozy Richmond dessert shop specializing in handcrafted sweet soups and pastries made with natural ingredients. The shop features a minimalist, sunlit interior with greenery and wooden furnishings, designed for quiet moments or social gatherings. It is part of the Myth Group restaurant family, with a loyalty points program redeemable across all Myth Group locations.

restaurant.name: Hungrey Zus
restaurant.desc: Hungry Zus is a fast-casual Mediterranean restaurant in downtown Vancouver's Financial District, serving bowls, pita wraps, falafel, grilled meats, and house-made sides with a strong emphasis on fresh, locally sourced ingredients. Located on Granville Street steps from Waterfront SkyTrain Station, it offers indoor dining and a summer outdoor patio. The restaurant runs a loyalty rewards program and offers customizable catering for groups.

restaurant.name: The Village Taphouse
restaurant.desc: The Village Taphouse is a casual pub and restaurant in North Vancouver's Park Royal area, operated by Park Royal Village Tap House Ltd. (affiliated with Cactus Restaurants Ltd.). The menu spans shareable plates, artisan pizzas, burgers, salads, and handhelds, with both indoor seating and an outdoor patio. Online ordering for pickup and delivery is available, making it a flexible food stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes clearly vegetarian dishes: Santorini Salad (quinoa, hummus, greens, avocado, chickpeas), Brussels Sprouts, Margherita pizza, and a veggie patty substitution option on handhelds. No explicit vegan or GF labelling observed

restaurant.name: Roadrunner Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Roadrunner Restaurant is a classic greasy-spoon diner in Langley Township with a country-town aesthetic, serving a full brunch menu of Eggs Bennys, omelettes, sandwiches, and burgers. Both dine-in and takeout are offered, and customer reviews consistently highlight friendly staff and well-cooked food. It sits on 62 Avenue and makes a practical and welcoming refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Hirame Sushi
restaurant.desc: Hirame Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Langley serving sushi and traditional Japanese cuisine in a sit-down setting. The restaurant takes online orders and operates seven days a week, making it a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists moving through the Langley area on 200 Street.

restaurant.name: Grill & Vine
restaurant.desc: Grill & Vine is a Pacific Northwest-inspired restaurant inside the Westin Resort and Spa in Whistler, where Executive Chef Elliot Brass builds menus around regional, fresh, and sustainable BC ingredients — including locally sourced salmon on a mountain-view summer patio. The restaurant also runs a Grab & Go counter stocked with fresh-baked goods, sandwiches, coffee, and snacks, making it a practical stop for cyclists who need a quick resupply rather than a sit-down meal. The attached FireRock Lounge rounds out the offering for an end-of-day wind-down.

restaurant.name: Tea at the Empress
restaurant.desc: Tea at the Empress is a world-renowned afternoon tea served in the grand Lobby Lounge of the Fairmont Empress, a Victoria landmark continuously operating since 1908. The experience centres on a proprietary Empress Blend tea and an elaborate spread of finger sandwiches, freshly baked scones with house-made clotted cream, and handcrafted pastries. It has hosted royalty, celebrities, and dignitaries, and remains one of the most storied culinary traditions in British Columbia.

detail.address: 721 Government Street, Victoria, British Columbia V8W 1W5

restaurant.name: Yoshi Sushi
restaurant.desc: Yoshi Sushi is a Japanese restaurant established in 1989, located inside Gateway Village in Victoria. It offers an extensive menu spanning traditional nigiri, sashimi, specialty rolls, teriyaki, tempura, and ramen, alongside party trays for takeout. Both dine-in and pickup are available, and a vegetable-focused menu section makes it accessible to non-meat-eating cyclists.

restaurant.name: L'aromas Coffee & Bakehouse
restaurant.desc: L'aromas is a locally founded coffee roasting company and bakery that grew from a single Tsawwassen café opened in 2015 into a four-location chain across Delta and Richmond. The Bakehouse location offers espresso drinks and baked goods in a neighborhood café setting, part of a brand built on community connection and in-house roasting. Touring cyclists on routes through the Tsawwassen–Delta corridor have a full-service café stop here.

restaurant.name: Nori
restaurant.desc: Nori is a Japanese restaurant established in Nanaimo in 2010, recognized with the BC Restaurant Hall of Fame Best Restaurant Independent Award in 2016. The restaurant is known for its fresh sushi and a signature omakase program featuring named sashimi sets such as 'Nami' (layered like waves), 'Sora', and 'Hana', as well as house-only creations like the Toro Truffle Oshi. Cyclists stopping on the Island Highway corridor will find a full sit-down dining experience with takeout and online ordering also available.

restaurant.name: Munchie Bar
restaurant.desc: The Munchie Bar is the café and concession stand inside Cinecenta, the University of Victoria's non-profit student cinema operating since 1971. By day it functions as a standalone coffee shop serving Kicking Horse espresso, fresh ciabatta sandwiches, and locally sourced baked goods; by evening it supplies the theatre crowd with popcorn, candy, and beverages. It sits in the heart of UVic's Student Union Building, making it a convenient stop for cyclists cutting through the campus.

detail.address: Student Union Building, 3800 Finnerty Road, University of Victoria, Victoria, BC V8P 5C2

restaurant.name: The Lion's Head
restaurant.desc: The Lion's Head Smoke & Brew Pub is a historic Tudor-style pub on the banks of the Columbia River in Robson, BC, re-opened in 2009 after a period of closure. It is known throughout the Kootenays for its on-site BBQ smoker that slow-cooks meats up to 12 hours using local Robson applewood, and for its 12 rotating taps exclusively pouring BC craft beers. Two outdoor riverside patios and an associated AIRBNB make it a natural rest or overnight stop for touring cyclists on the Columbia Valley route.

restaurant.name: Logan Lake Urban Cafe

restaurant.name: South Castle Korean Restaurant

The Korean name '남한산성 순대' (Namhansanseong Sundae) suggests a focus on traditional Korean cuisine, particularly sundae (Korean blood sausage). Dine-in service is available, with catering and reservations handled by phone.

restaurant.name: Maude Hunter's Pub
restaurant.desc: Maude Hunter's Pub is a neighbourhood pub on Shelbourne Street in Victoria with an attached liquor store. It carries an extensive tap list spotlighting local BC breweries including Phillips, Hoyne, Driftwood, and Ile Sauvage. Weekly events such as music bingo, trivia night, and wing night give it a lively community feel, and a dedicated plant-based menu sets it apart from a typical pub kitchen.

The menu covers a broad range of Japanese cuisine styles, and online ordering for takeout is available.

restaurant.name: Japan Sushi

restaurant.name: Taco Rio

The spot offers online ordering with pickup, gift cards, and catering, making it a flexible stop for groups or solo riders. Its bold street-food menu and proximity to the Harrison Hot Springs resort area make it a natural refuelling point for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

restaurant.name: Su Casa Mexican Cafe

restaurant.name: Donair Affair

The Port Coquitlam location on Mary Hill Road serves wraps, Mayan platters, and combo specials in a casual, wheelchair-accessible setting. Touring cyclists will find quick, filling meals including vegetarian and vegan-friendly falafel options with a variety of sauces and toppings.

restaurant.name: Lumberman's Arch Cafe

The outdoor seating area faces the park, offering a relaxed spot to refuel surrounded by old-growth trees.

restaurant.name: Sushiteria & Catering

restaurant.name: Railtown Café
restaurant.desc: Railtown Café has been a fixture in Vancouver's historic Railtown District of the Downtown Eastside since 2012, founded by classically trained chefs Dan Olson and Tyler Day who also run the award-winning Railtown Catering out of the same facility. The café serves heaping portions of scratch-made comfort food — gourmet sandwiches, soups, pastries, and a build-your-own salad bar — using local and organic ingredients. With multiple Vancouver locations and a community-focused ethos, it's a well-regarded stop for a filling, quality meal.

restaurant.name: Homer St Cafe and Bar
restaurant.desc: Homer St Cafe & Bar is a Michelin-recommended contemporary neighbourhood restaurant occupying the historic Homer Building and the newer Beasley Building in Vancouver's Yaletown District. The kitchen centres on a fire engine red rotisserie that slow-roasts a rotating cast of proteins, anchoring a menu of classic comfort cooking. Brunch, lunch, dinner, and daily happy hour are all on offer, and walk-ins are always welcome.

restaurant.name: White Spot

The brand also operates Triple O's as a fast-casual sub-brand, and this OSM node appears to reference one of its many Vancouver-area locations. A touring cyclist would find reliable indoor seating, a broad menu including vegetarian options, and takeout availability.

restaurant.name: Good Fortune Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Good Fortune Restaurant is a family-run Chinese food restaurant in Sidney, BC, celebrated locally as 'Sidney's Finest Chinese Food' and known especially for its Ginger Fried Beef. Meals are prepared fresh to order in a licensed dining room, with catering and delivery also available. Cyclists passing through Sidney will find a full dine-in experience alongside takeout options and a menu that accommodates gluten-free and MSG-free dietary needs.

restaurant.name: Intermezzo Restaurant

The menu draws on global inspiration — Moroccan lamb, West Coast seafood, house-made gnocchi — paired with a cellar of over 100 wines including many Okanagan labels. A sister venue, The Castle Bistro, operates about 8 minutes north of the downtown location.

restaurant.name: The Dam

Touring cyclists can refuel on award-winning burgers, fresh salads, and comfort food in an all-ages, family-friendly pub setting. A weekly Sunday open-stage jam session adds a lively cultural draw for those spending time in the valley.

restaurant.name: Aladdin Cafe
restaurant.desc: Aladdin Cafe is a restaurant located on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. The establishment offers both indoor and outdoor seating and explicitly supports vegan and vegetarian diets. It provides a casual dining option in a central Vancouver location convenient to cyclists.

restaurant.name: Long Table Distillery
restaurant.desc: Long Table Distillery is a craft distillery and pub on Hornby Street in downtown Vancouver, producing a range of gins, vodkas, and liqueurs under their own label. Beyond spirits retail, they offer hands-on cocktail-making classes and a distinctive Sushi + Cocktail Making Class in partnership with a local sushi restaurant. It sits in the heart of downtown Vancouver, making it a potential stop for cyclists exploring the nearby seawall corridor.

restaurant.name: Cinnzeo
restaurant.desc: Cinnzeo is a Canadian cinnamon roll bakery franchise located inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre, Kelowna's largest mall with over 170 stores. The brand describes itself as offering a warm and inviting setting with high-quality cinnamon products. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a quick sweet treat inside a large indoor mall on Harvey Avenue.

restaurant.name: Westview Bakery
restaurant.desc: Westview Bakery is North Vancouver's original French artisan bakery, operating since 1971 and producing slow-fermented sourdough breads, artisan loaves, pastries, sandwiches, and custom cakes from a retail storefront on Westview Drive. The bakery uses preservative-free, unbleached-flour recipes with traditional 48-hour sourdough fermentation across a wide range of flavour profiles. Touring cyclists can resupply with fresh bread, buns, and ready-made sandwiches, and the shop also offers online ordering and kids baking classes.

restaurant.name: Aurora Café + Roastery

The combined café and roastery lets visitors taste carefully sourced single-origin and blended coffees roasted on-site, alongside baked goods and kitchen specials. The team regularly hosts workshops, private tastings, and pop-up events, making it a lively stop for coffee-curious cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

detail.address: 2615 Montrose Ave, Unit A, Abbotsford, BC V2S 3T5

restaurant.name: Blenz Coffee
restaurant.desc: Blenz Coffee is a Canadian specialty coffee chain founded in 1992, offering hand-crafted espresso drinks, organic whole-leaf teas, protein shakes, and a range of baked goods, sandwiches, and wraps. This Granville Street location sits in a well-trafficked Vancouver commercial corridor and is listed in the chain's own store locator as the Granville & Davie downtown outlet. The brand emphasizes premium natural ingredients and a loyalty rewards app.

restaurant.name: Waves Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Waves Coffee House is a Vancouver-born specialty coffee chain founded in 2005, built around 100% Specialty Grade Arabica beans and real Belgian chocolate in its signature mochas. The downtown Howe Street location offers indoor and outdoor seating, a bookable private meeting room with a smart TV and power outlets, and a food menu spanning sandwiches, wraps, soups, and pastries. Takeout, online ordering, and DoorDash delivery make it a flexible stop in the heart of the city.

restaurant.name: Popeyes

This Cook Street location sits in one of Victoria's most walkable and cyclist-friendly neighbourhoods, close to Beacon Hill Park and the Dallas Road waterfront route. No drive-through means the entrance is pedestrian- and cyclist-oriented, with takeout orders available.

restaurant.name: Saboten

The restaurant is operated by Fairchild Group and situated inside Aberdeen Centre, a large indoor mall in central Richmond. Cyclists stopping here can fuel up on hearty Japanese comfort food in a climate-controlled mall environment.

restaurant.name: Toro
restaurant.desc: Toro Bar&Bar is a sushi restaurant in the heart of downtown Victoria, marketing itself as the city's best sushi destination. The restaurant offers both dine-in with reservations and online pick-up ordering with a discount. Beer, wine, and cocktails round out the Japanese-focused menu, making it a full sit-down dining option for cyclists passing through the city centre.

restaurant.name: The Pleasant
restaurant.desc: The Pleasant is a spacious counter-service eatery and social house in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, serving creative Asian and Western comfort food alongside 24 taps of local craft beers and ciders. The building has a history as a billiard hall, and a pool table remains in the main dining room, giving the space a distinctive character. A community gallery showcasing local artists and a large private party room round out what the owners describe as an extension of the neighbourhood's living room.

restaurant.name: Dynasty Seafood Restaurant

restaurant.name: COBS Bread

The Davie Street location is a takeaway-only counter-service bakery offering a wide range of breads, buns, pastries, bagels, scones, cruffins, and savoury items including pizza. Leftover baked goods are donated to local charities at the end of each day.

restaurant.name: Red's Bakery
restaurant.desc: Red's Bakery is a local bakery established in 2017 on Commercial Street in downtown Nanaimo. Located in a walkable urban core, it would serve as a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the city. As a bakery, it likely offers baked goods suitable for restocking on a ride, though specific offerings could not be confirmed.

restaurant.name: Dinesty Dumpling House
restaurant.desc: Dinesty Dumpling House is Greater Vancouver's leading Chinese restaurant chain, founded in Richmond in 2006 and celebrated for its handcrafted Xiaolongbao (soup dumplings) made with natural chicken broth, double-ground pork, and ultra-thin hand-kneaded wrappers. The chain has won multiple prestigious Chinese Restaurant Awards and Diner's Choice honours for best soup dumpling and best Shanghainese restaurant. Touring cyclists can stop in for a full sit-down meal or take-out dumplings across several Richmond and Vancouver locations.

restaurant.name: Sushi 7 Japanese Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: Sushi 7 is a neighbourhood Japanese restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver offering a broad menu of sushi, sashimi, teriyaki, donburi, and noodle dishes. It has built a loyal local following with 151 reviews and is known for consistent quality and fast service. An online ordering system with a quick pickup turnaround makes it a practical stop for cyclists passing through the Cambie corridor.

restaurant.name: Everything Wine
restaurant.desc: Everything Wine is a large-format specialty beverage retailer with multiple BC locations, offering an extensive range of wines from around the world alongside beer, cider, and spirits. This Vancouver outlet is located in the River District, a relatively new mixed-use development along the Fraser River. The store also runs a wine club, educational content, and event consultation services, catering to casual shoppers and serious enthusiasts alike.

restaurant.name: Dante Italian Sandwich
restaurant.desc: Dante Italian Sandwich is a Vancouver sandwich shop serving Italian-style sandwiches piled high on house-made schiacciata bread, with premium ingredients including prosciutto, mortadella, stracciatella cheese, and house-prepared spreads. The Commercial Drive location is one of three outposts across the city, sitting on one of Vancouver's most vibrant and cyclist-frequented streets. Touring cyclists will find a focused, quality-driven menu with vegetarian options and a no-frills fast-food format suited to a quick, satisfying stop.

restaurant.name: Pizza Nation

restaurant.name: Coffee on the Moon

The café doubles as a rotating gallery space for Cowichan Valley artists, giving it a distinctive neighbourhood character. The website references two Duncan locations, though this OSM node represents a single point.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states: "Healthy vegetarian, vegan and gluten free options"

restaurant.name: Finest Cup

It operates primarily as an online Shopify store with a physical storefront for local pickup.

restaurant.name: Cor's 2 For 1 Pizza
restaurant.desc: Cor's 2 For 1 Pizza has been serving gourmet pizza in Aldergrove since 1988, making it the longest-established pizza takeout in the area. The kitchen makes all doughs fresh daily from scratch and produces house-made pizza sauce and gourmet meat sauce in-house. Cyclists passing through on Fraser Highway can order pizzas, pastas, wings, and sides for pickup, or arrange catering for larger groups.

detail.address: 27256 Fraser Highway, Unit 103, Aldergrove, BC V4W 3P8

restaurant.name: Chongqing on Robson
restaurant.desc: ChongQing on Robson is the downtown Vancouver outpost of a multi-location Szechuan Chinese restaurant chain that has operated in Vancouver for over twenty years. Located on busy Robson Street in the city centre, it specialises in traditional Szechuanese dishes and offers both dine-in and takeout. The central location puts it within easy reach of cyclists navigating the downtown core.

restaurant.name: Sawasdee Thai Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Sawasdee Thai has been a Vancouver institution since 1986, recognized as one of the city's first Thai restaurants and a long-standing fixture on Main Street. The family-owned restaurant serves authentic Thai cuisine—from pad thai and tom yum to Thai barbecue and regional specialties—prepared with fresh ingredients rooted in time-honored recipes. It is deeply embedded in the local community, participating in events like Main Street Car Free Day and the Vancouver Thai Festival.

restaurant.name: Lavash Seaside Grill

The menu features a broad range of Persian dishes including multiple vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options.

restaurant.name: Menchie's Frozen Yogurt

As a franchise of a well-established Canadian chain, it offers a consistent and quick treat experience.

restaurant.name: Backcountry Tasting Room

The 70s ski cabin-inspired taproom pours from a 20-tap tower alongside cider, wine, and non-alcoholic options, with a scratch kitchen turning out rotating pizzas, seasonal salads, and snacks using local organic ingredients. Set in a mountain town renowned for cycling and outdoor adventure, it bills itself as an après-adventure destination, complete with covered bike parking and map-top tables for planning your next route.

restaurant.name: The Grand Buddha Bistro
restaurant.desc: Grand Buddha Bistro is an Asian restaurant located in Crescent Valley, a small community in the Slocan Valley of British Columbia. Crescent Valley sits along quiet back roads that attract touring cyclists exploring the West Kootenay region. As the settlement has limited food options, this bistro could serve as a welcome meal stop for riders passing through.

restaurant.name: Earl Grey Lodge
restaurant.desc: Earl Grey Lodge is a chalet-style bed and breakfast in the heart of Panorama Mountain Village, voted #1 small hotel in Canada by TripAdvisor in 2021. The 8,000 sq ft lodge sleeps up to 12 adults across six guest rooms and a separate two-bedroom cabin with a full kitchen, all decorated with rustic log walls and an art-deco interior. Situated steps from the ski slopes and surrounded by Purcell Mountain trails used for hiking and mountain biking, it makes a comfortable base for cyclists exploring the Columbia Valley.

restaurant.name: Oui Patisserie
restaurant.desc: Oui Patisserie is a French-style patisserie and bakery located in a commercial unit on River Road in Richmond. As a bakery, it likely offers pastries, cakes, and baked goods — a useful stop for a touring cyclist seeking a sweet treat or a quick snack along the Fraser River corridor. No further detail about the shop's offerings or layout is available from accessible sources.

restaurant.name: Mission Donair Shack
restaurant.desc: Donair Shack is a quick-service Middle Eastern restaurant specializing in authentic donairs — grilled meat sliced from a rotating spit and wrapped in warm flatbread with house sauces and salad. The Mission location on 7th Avenue is one of five Fraser Valley outlets, making it a convenient protein-and-carb refuel stop on cycling routes through the lower Fraser Valley. The menu spans wraps, platters, and falafel options, with a focus on fresh ingredients and flavour.

restaurant.name: Historic Dewdney Pub
restaurant.desc: The Historic Dewdney Pub — also known as the Church of the Blues — is a genuine roadhouse operating inside a 1912 Anglican church building along the Dewdney slough, just off scenic Highway 7 east of Mission in the Fraser Valley. The pub is recognized as one of Canada's top 35 blues clubs, drawing locals and road-trippers alike for its legendary Sunday blues jams, live music events, and large patio with mountain views. An on-site full-service liquor store stocks beer, wine, spirits, and ciders, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking to resupply.

restaurant.name: Stackhouse Steak Sandwiches
restaurant.desc: Stackhouse Steak Sandwiches is a fast-food spot on Abbott Street in Vancouver's Gastown-adjacent downtown core, specializing in steak sandwiches. It sits in a high-traffic area popular with cyclists navigating the seawall and Gastown routes. A touring cyclist looking for a quick, filling sandwich stop in central Vancouver would find it conveniently located.

restaurant.name: Nat's Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Nat's Coffee House is a community café situated in the Tsawwassen Springs development, serving Rainforest Alliance and Beyond Fair Trade certified coffee that is roasted locally in small-batch blends. The shop offers both a drive-through and takeout service, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through Tsawwassen. Its focus on socially and environmentally responsible sourcing gives it a distinct character beyond a typical chain café.

restaurant.name: Cactus Club Cafe
restaurant.desc: Cactus Club Cafe Byrne Road is a high-energy, upscale-casual restaurant in Burnaby's Market Crossing retail district, part of a large Canadian chain with locations across BC and beyond. A stylish patio and full lounge make it a comfortable option for a sit-down meal after a ride.

Whether a real café operates at the Vancouver address cannot be determined from the available evidence.

restaurant.name: White Spot
restaurant.desc: White Spot is BC's oldest restaurant chain, founded in 1928 and built around crowd-pleasing comfort food — burgers, fish and chips, and seasonal menu items made with fresh, local ingredients. The Kingsway location sits on a major arterial road through the Burnaby/Vancouver urban corridor, offering a familiar full-service sit-down dining experience with air conditioning and indoor seating. It's a reliable midride stop for a proper meal on one of the busiest cycling routes connecting the two cities.

restaurant.name: Enishi Japanese Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Enishi Japanese Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant in Richmond with an active social media presence. As a sit-down restaurant, it serves as a meal stop for touring cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: Royal Oak Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Royal Oak is a Greek restaurant on Fraser Highway in Surrey, offering dine-in, takeout, and catering services. It operates under the tagline 'Let us do the Cooking!' and presents itself as a neighbourhood Greek dining destination. Touring cyclists on the Fraser Highway corridor will find a sit-down meal or takeout option here.

restaurant.name: SUYO Modern Peruvian
restaurant.desc: SUYO Modern Peruvian is a chef-driven dinner restaurant on Main Street in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, drawing its menu from Peru's three great landscapes — the Amazonian rainforest, the Andean mountains, and the Pacific coast. The kitchen showcases dishes like ceviches, tiraditos, and anticucheros alongside larger plates such as lomo saltado and arroz con pato, with an optional multi-course Chef's Tasting Menu. The intimate 49-seat room includes a private Nazca Room for groups, making it a destination for a post-ride celebratory dinner.

restaurant.name: Leo's Tapas & Grill Greek Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Leo's Tapas & Grill has been a community fixture in lower Gibsons since 1999, serving authentic Greek and Mediterranean cuisine including charbroiled dishes, seafood, house-made tapas, and whole-wheat pizzas. The restaurant features summer patio seating in the heart of lower Gibsons, live music and belly dancing on weekend nights, and a full catering service for events. Cyclists finishing a Sunshine Coast ride will find a welcoming, family-oriented atmosphere with dine-in, takeout, and local delivery options.

restaurant.name: Alpine Pub & Grill

restaurant.name: Bahar Bakery & Cafe
restaurant.desc: Bahar Bakery & Cafe is an artisanal bakery and espresso bar on downtown Vancouver's Robson Street, founded as a heartfelt tribute to Bahareh Karami Moghadam, a victim of PS752. The cafe serves an extensive lineup of handcrafted Persian and Western pastries, whole custom cakes, sandwiches, and specialty coffee drinks in a warm, community-focused setting. Catering and event services are also available for larger occasions.

restaurant.name: CRAFT Beer Market (Olympic Village / False Creek)

The venue is LEED Gold and LEAF certified, making it one of Canada's most sustainably designed restaurants. Cyclists riding the False Creek seawall will find a full-service food and drink stop with brunch, late-night options, and both indoor and covered patio seating.

restaurant.name: The Heidout Restaurant & Brewhouse
restaurant.desc: The Heid Out is a downtown Cranbrook institution combining a full-service restaurant with an on-site craft brewery producing Fisher Peak beers, brewed in 1000-litre tanks and poured fresh from tap. Five Red Seal chefs drive a kitchen that ranges from South Indian Masala to Kootenay-inspired burgers, drawing on hyper-local suppliers and the restaurant's own dedicated celiac-friendly kitchen area — a rarity in the region. The outdoor patio welcomes dogs, and private event spaces make it a natural gathering point for groups passing through the Kootenays.

restaurant.name: Golden Dragon Village

restaurant.name: Oz Korean Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Korean restaurant in a Coquitlam strip mall that accepts online orders for takeout service. Provides a specialized cuisine option for touring cyclists seeking meals beyond typical chains.

restaurant.name: Subway

The location serves breakfast and offers catering, making it a flexible stop for groups or individuals on a longer route. As an independently owned franchise, it operates under the Subway brand while being a local business.

restaurant.name: Michele Cake Shop

A touring cyclist can pick up fresh baked buns and bread for the road.

restaurant.name: Po Kong
restaurant.desc: Po Kong Vegetarian Restaurant is a fully vegetarian Chinese restaurant on Vancouver's Kingsway corridor, established in 2011 as the successor to the long-running Bo Kong chain that first popularized Chinese vegetarian cuisine in the Lower Mainland in 1992. The menu features Buddhist vegetarian cooking with vegan options, dim sum service, and set menus. It is a rare opportunity for plant-based cyclists to sit down to a full Chinese meal rather than a quick snack.

restaurant.name: Royal Canadian Legion Branch #229
restaurant.desc: The Whalley Legion Branch 229 is a Royal Canadian Legion chapter that has served the North Surrey community since 1948, operating the Vimy Lounge — a full pub and restaurant open to the public. The lounge features 14 big-screen TVs, a large dance floor, pool tables, darts, and live entertainment on weekends, alongside a banquet room available for private functions. It is a short walk from the Gateway SkyTrain station, making it a convenient stop for cyclists travelling along the King George Boulevard corridor.

restaurant.name: Me-n-Ed's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Me-n-Ed's Pizza is a proudly Canadian-owned family pizza chain operating in the Lower Mainland since 1969, known for specialty and premium pizzas made with fresh ingredients. The restaurant offers dine-in alongside delivery and takeout, and pours local BC craft beers on tap. With a catering menu and a loyalty program, it's a solid stop for a hungry touring cyclist looking for a full sit-down meal.

restaurant.name: First Perk Coffee House
restaurant.desc: First Perk Coffee House & Eatery is a community-oriented café and eatery in Jaffray, BC, sitting at the midpoint between Fernie and Cranbrook on a popular touring corridor. The shop has partnered with Cupper's Coffee for 15 years and serves espresso drinks, paninis, and baked goods alongside locally made artisan goods from vendors like Asteria Tea and Soco Soaps. It's a small-town gathering place with a reputation for consistency and a welcoming atmosphere where strangers become friends.

restaurant.name: Oretachi Curry
restaurant.desc: Oretachi Curry is a casual Japanese curry restaurant in the historic Steveston village of Richmond, serving authentic Osaka-style curry rice and a distinctive curry ramen in a house-made prawn miso broth, built from a blend of over 20 spices with locally sourced BC ingredients. The original Oretachi Curry shop was founded in 2012 in Namba, Osaka, Japan by Mr. Sugimura, and the Steveston outpost brings that tradition to one of BC's most popular cycling destinations. restaurant.name: Black Kettle Tasting Lounge
restaurant.desc: Black Kettle Brewing Company is a North Shore craft brewery and taproom that has been pouring house-crafted ales and lagers since opening in January 2014, founded by Bryan Lockhart and Phil Vanderborre in a no-frills industrial unit just past the rail tracks. The about page describes it as 'minutes down the Spirit Trail' and 'a casual & pet-friendly oasis,' making it a natural pit-stop for cyclists finishing a ride on the North Shore trail network. The kitchen turns out burgers, tacos, salads, and wings, and the pet-friendly patio hosts live music on Saturdays.

detail.address: 720 Copping Street – Unit 106, North Vancouver, BC V7M 3N2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Chicken Fingers (gluten free)', a 'Veggie Smash Burger' with Impossible™ patty, and a 'G.O.A.T Salad' with vegetarian toppings; Hibiscus Ginger Kombucha (ABV 0%) also available

restaurant.name: The Humboldt
restaurant.desc: Humboldt Bar is an intimate cocktail bar in downtown Victoria inspired by the life and work of Alexander von Humboldt, the 19th-century German naturalist. Located on the Arcade Level of the DoubleTree Victoria hotel, it offers an immersive nature-themed environment with a creative cocktail program drawing on Humboldt's travels and discoveries. Small plates from the kitchen are also available on most evenings.

restaurant.name: Motonobu Udon
restaurant.desc: Motonobu Udon is Vancouver's first authentic Japanese udon restaurant, opened in August 2020 during the pandemic and earning Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand recognition consecutively in 2023, 2024, and 2025. Chef Shin Iwamoto follows his grandmother's Sanuki-style family recipe, using locally sourced Canadian flour to produce handmade noodles freshly cut and boiled to order. Located on East Hastings Street near PNE Playland, it operates as a walk-in-only spot with takeout and Uber Eats delivery available.

restaurant.name: Ramie's Greek Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Ramie's Greek Restaurant is a family-owned Greek restaurant on Burnaby's Kingsway corridor, celebrating 25 years in business. It has been voted Best Greek Restaurant in Burnaby, winning the Quality Business Award for both 2023 and 2024 based on satisfaction, quality, service, and reputation. The restaurant is operated by owner Ramie and his two sons, with a stated commitment to authenticity and quality in their cooking.

restaurant.name: Little June
restaurant.desc: Little June is a neighbourhood café nestled in the heritage building at the heart of Fernwood Square, one of Victoria's most distinctive communities. Founded by a former bush pilot who learned to roast coffee in a Yellowknife bathroom at -40°, it serves an entirely house-made menu of breakfast and lunch dishes built around seasonal ingredients from local farms. The cosy spot draws on its 110-year-old building's history while offering everything from grab-and-go baked goods to lingering egg dishes and locally sourced beer and wine.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'gluten free oat' cookie, 'Roasted veggie and Havarti sandwich', grain bowl, and daily farm-inspired salad, confirming vegetarian and gluten-free options

restaurant.name: Iron Road Brewing
restaurant.desc: Iron Road Brewing is an award-winning craft brewery in Kamloops, BC, founded by two geologists who teamed up with an award-winning brewer to produce a rotating lineup of balanced, flavourful beers. The 60-person, family-friendly taproom is steps from Thompson Rivers University and serves food alongside the house-brewed lineup. Cyclists may catch a live band or watch the brewing process up close.

restaurant.name: Tavola
restaurant.desc: Tavola is a neighbourhood Italian restaurant on Robson Street in Vancouver's West End, celebrated for house-made pastas, fresh burrata, and family-style sharing plates sourced from local farmers. The street-level patio spills laughter onto Robson Street and has earned praise from the Globe and Mail and Scout Magazine for unpretentious, quality-driven cooking. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down meal or a quick takeout order available nightly, with weekend brunch service as well.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu states '*Gluten free pasta available for most selections'; multiple vegetarian pasta and salad dishes listed (e.g. Spaghetti cacio e pepe, Ricotta Gnocchi, Arugula Salad)

restaurant.name: Tutto Belle Il Gelato
restaurant.desc: Tutto Belle Il Gelato is a gelateria on the popular West 4th Avenue cycling corridor in Kitsilano, blending Canadian seasonal ingredients with authentic Italian gelato-making traditions. The menu spans classic Italian flavors such as pistachio and tiramisu alongside Asian-influenced options including ube, black sesame mochi gelato, and pineapple bun gelato. The shop also produces 'Babylato,' a dog- and toddler-safe frozen treat made with organic Greek yogurt and coconut oil, inspired by the owners' German Shepherd.

restaurant.name: Lao Shan Dong Homemade Noodle House
restaurant.desc: Lao Shan Dong Homemade Noodle House is a long-established Chinese noodle restaurant (est. 1949) located in Richmond's busy Number 3 Road corridor, serving handmade Taiwanese and northern Chinese noodle soups, dry noodles, dumplings, and rice dishes. The kitchen distinguishes itself by using no MSG or preservatives, and the menu spans beef tendon broth soups, braised cold meats, and Taiwanese night-market staples like scallion pancakes and pork chops. A touring cyclist can expect a hearty, carb-rich meal well-suited to refueling mid-ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels meat-free items: D2 Dry Noodle w/ Sesame Sauce '(no meat)', N13 Noodle in Beef Soup '(No Meat)'; additional vegetarian-compatible dishes include Deep Fried Tofu (A4), Vegetable Spring Rolls (A6), Boiled Seasonal Vegetable (A14), and multiple tofu, cucumber, and seaweed cold dishes

restaurant.name: Driftwood Great Chinese Buffet
restaurant.desc: Driftwood Great Chinese Buffet is the Nanaimo outpost of a Vancouver Island–owned chain celebrated for its all-you-can-eat lunch and dinner buffets alongside a full à la carte Chinese menu. The chain prides itself on fresh, hand-crafted dishes made with 100% vegetable oil and no added MSG, and each location features a full bar with local beers. Cycling through Nanaimo's south end, riders will find both dine-in and take-out options readily available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menus consistently list 'Spring Roll(veg)' and vegetable-based dishes; all menus note '100% Vegetable Oil & No Added MSG.'

restaurant.name: Cofu
restaurant.desc: COFU is a fully plant-based Japanese restaurant in Vancouver's Chinatown, founded by Akiko Gulkison, a Japanese immigrant and single mother who built Canada's first fully plant-based omakase experience. The intimate 18-course tasting menu is served at an 8-seat counter handcrafted by Japanese carpenters, blending traditional technique with seasonal vegetables sourced locally and from Japan. On weekends, the same address also houses Hush, a quiet coffee space serving Japanese-roasted beans and ceremonial-grade matcha from Kyoto.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states 'COFU Chinatown is proudly 100% vegan' and 'We're happy to accommodate gluten-free and oriental vegetarian/vegan diets.'

restaurant.name: Alta Bistro
restaurant.desc: Alta Bistro is a modern seasonal alpine cuisine restaurant in Whistler, established in 2010, built around locally sourced ingredients from suppliers such as North Arm Farm and Pemberton Valley producers. The menu showcases creative dishes including venison tartare with bone marrow dressing and hokkaido scallop carpaccio, making it a strong option for a celebratory post-ride dinner. The restaurant operates a transparent Employee Health Benefit program, collecting 2% of net sales before tax to support year-round staff wellness.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items marked (V) for vegetarian, including Roasted Cauliflower (creamed pearl barley, kyoto miso) and Chocolate Torte

restaurant.name: Cafe Lu
restaurant.desc: Cafe Lu Quan is a cafe located on Kingsway in Vancouver. Its Instagram account carries the display name 'The World Famous Cafe Lu,' hinting at a degree of local notoriety. Beyond its presence on a well-travelled arterial corridor, little detail is publicly verifiable without access to its social media content.

restaurant.name: The Italian Bakery
restaurant.desc: Victoria's first and only Italian bakery, established in 1978 and now operated across three generations of the Pozzolo family. The shop produces organic sourdough breads, Northern Italian pastries, cakes, gelato, and frozen meals, and offers both eat-in table service and take-away. A characterful Quadra Street stop where a touring cyclist can pick up fresh artisan bread, a croissant, or a sit-down coffee.

restaurant.name: Ole Chicken
restaurant.desc: Ole Chicken is a Korean pub situated on the second floor at 1256 Robson Street in downtown Vancouver, specializing in Korean fried chicken served in a variety of sauces alongside traditional anju share plates and soups. The space has a lively pub atmosphere with music, drinks, and a commissary kitchen available for rent. It sits on one of Vancouver's busiest pedestrian corridors, making it a convenient urban stop for cyclists coming in off the Robson Street corridor.

detail.address: 2nd Floor 1256 Robson St, Vancouver, BC V6E 1C1

restaurant.name: The Lookout Café
restaurant.desc: A cafe associated with Sewells Marina in North Vancouver. Specific amenities and services could not be verified due to website unavailability.

restaurant.name: Pizza Pizza
restaurant.desc: Pizza Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 1967 with over 750 locations coast to coast, including this Delta outpost. Cyclists can grab a quick hot meal with a wide range of pizza styles, sides, and specialty items. The location is open late into the night, making it a convenient stop on longer evening rides.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website confirms gluten-free crust ('prepared, cooked and cut with dedicated utensils') and plant-based items (Plant-Based Chick'n Bites listed in nutrition section)

restaurant.name: Jak's Beer Wine Spirits
restaurant.desc: JAK's Beer Wine Spirits is a Vancouver-area chain of neighbourhood liquor stores with 10 locations across Greater Vancouver, known for knowledgeable staff who focus on personalized service and product expertise. This Lougheed Highway location (likely the Westwood or Coquitlam store) stocks wine, craft beer, and premium spirits. Online ordering with delivery through third-party platforms is available.

restaurant.name: Joey
restaurant.desc: JOEY is a well-established Canadian casual-dining chain with locations across North America, known for its globally inspired menu developed by a team of Executive Chefs. The Coquitlam location sits on Lougheed Highway and offers a full-service dining room, lounge, bar, and patio. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find a reliable stop for a sit-down meal with a broad menu.

restaurant.name: Provence Marinaside
restaurant.desc: Provence Marinaside is an award-winning French seafood restaurant and bar on Marinaside Crescent in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, situated steps from the False Creek seawall — one of the city's most popular cycling routes. The menu centres on Provençal-inspired dishes featuring local seafood, with both indoor and outdoor patio seating overlooking the marina. It offers group and private dining bookings and participates in seasonal dining events such as Dine Out Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Lucky Hong Kong Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Lucky Hong Kong Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant in Richmond offering dine-in service. Located on Westminster Highway, it provides a full-service sit-down dining option for touring cyclists seeking a more substantial meal. Wi-Fi access is available for customers.

restaurant.name: Ogopogo Burgers & Shakes
restaurant.desc: Ogopogo Burgers & Shakes is a casual diner on Osoyoos's main commercial strip, named after the legendary Okanagan lake monster. The menu leans into comfort food — hand-crafted burgers on brioche buns, Guinness beer-battered fish and chips, gyro donair platters, and loaded fries — making it a hearty refueling stop in a town that sits at the hub of some of the South Okanagan's most popular cycling routes. Takeout and delivery are both available via Clover online ordering.

restaurant.name: Arriva Ristorante
restaurant.desc: Arriva Ristorante is a 42-year landmark on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, the city's historic 'Little Italy' district, where owner Paolo Frau serves entirely house-made Italian cuisine including scratch-made gnocchi, sausages, pancetta, breads, and desserts. It has become a destination restaurant drawing diners from across the region with an extensive Italian and international wine list. Commercial Drive itself is a major cycling corridor through east Vancouver, putting this long-established sit-down restaurant directly on common touring routes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'a wide selection of vegetarian pasta dishes and gluten free choices'; menu includes a dedicated 'Pasta - Vegetarian Sauces' section and offers 'Substitute rice pasta (gluten free)' as a menu option

restaurant.name: Mello
restaurant.desc: Mello is an artisan donut shop in Vancouver's Chinatown specializing in fresh brioche donuts made entirely from scratch each day, with fillings ranging from Madagascar vanilla custard and tiramisu to an Everything Bagel cream cheese option. The shop rotates seasonal and specialty flavours regularly and also serves coffee using a custom blend from Agro Roasters. Donuts can be pre-ordered online or purchased in-store while supplies last — the handmade process means sell-outs are common.

detail.address: 223 E Pender St, Vancouver, BC V6A 2T9

restaurant.name: The Shameful Tiki Room
restaurant.desc: The Shameful Tiki Room is a dimly lit, immersive vintage tiki bar on Vancouver's Main Street corridor, serving expertly crafted classic exotic cocktails like the Zombie, Jet Pilot, and Mai Tai alongside share plates. The decor is sourced from around the world — tapa cloth from Tonga and Fiji, custom California-carved tikis, and puffer fish lamps — evoking a genuine mid-century escape. Live surf bands and ukulele players appear regularly, and the venue welcomes all ages.

restaurant.name: CoCo Fresh Tea & Juice
restaurant.desc: CoCo Fresh Tea & Juice is a bubble tea cafe serving specialty tea drinks and refreshments. The location provides indoor seating in Burnaby, convenient for touring cyclists looking for a quick rest stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegan and vegetarian options available

restaurant.name: Tealips
restaurant.desc: Tealips Cafe is a bubble tea and dessert café serving Burnaby's Highgate neighbourhood with a broad menu of milk teas, fruit slushes, coffee drinks, Korean-style bingsoo, Belgian waffles, and fresh focaccia sandwiches. The café operates under a shared brand with a second Burnaby location (Metrotown/Arcola Way) and supports online ordering with in-store pickup. Cyclists will find a wide range of cold and hot drinks, light meals, and vegetarian-friendly options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Our avocado sandwich is a vegetarian favorite'; milk teas described as 'lactose free'; oat milk substitution available on tea lattes and smoothies

restaurant.name: Hainan Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Hainan Kitchen is a Chinese restaurant in Richmond's Garden City area specializing in authentic Hainanese chicken rice and Southeast Asian comfort food. It is particularly known for its signature Hainanese Chicken Rice served with fragrant seasoned rice and artisanal dipping sauces, alongside dishes like Curry Beef Brisket and hand-pulled cold noodles. Both dine-in and takeout options are available, making it a practical meal stop for cyclists passing through the Blundell Road corridor.

restaurant.name: HellCrust Pizza
restaurant.desc: HellCrust Pizza is a pizza chain operating on Vancouver's busy Main Street corridor, offering online and app-based ordering. The franchise model and 'Locations' page on their website suggest multiple outlets across the region. For a touring cyclist, it is a convenient hot-meal stop on a well-travelled urban route.

restaurant.name: Spice of Punjab
restaurant.desc: Spice of Punjab is an Indian restaurant located in Tsawwassen, BC. It would offer a warm sit-down meal option for touring cyclists passing through the South Delta area. No further detail about the menu, facilities, or current operation could be confirmed.

restaurant.name: Blenz Coffee
restaurant.desc: Blenz Coffee is a BC-based specialty coffee chain with a location inside Library Square, a busy commercial and office complex in the heart of downtown Vancouver. The cafe serves a full espresso menu alongside specialty drinks such as nitro coffee, whole-leaf teas, and the signature Blue Matcha Latte, plus a range of baked goods, breakfast sandwiches, and wraps. It sits on Robson Street, a key cycling corridor connecting the West End to downtown, making it a convenient stop for urban touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Mittz Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Mittz Kitchen is a downtown Kamloops upscale casual restaurant founded by brothers Jeff and Steve Mitton, who bring a combined 54 years of hospitality experience to the table. The menu is described as Canadian cuisine built on local ingredients with global influences — what the owners call 'tasty goodness' — served in a relaxed, neighborhood gathering atmosphere. Its central Victoria Street location puts it squarely in the heart of the city, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through or based in Kamloops.

restaurant.name: The Lion's Den Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Lion's Den Cafe is a restaurant located on East 15th Avenue in Vancouver. The casual name suggests a welcoming neighborhood atmosphere. It serves as a dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Camp Lifestyle and Coffee Co
restaurant.desc: Camp Lifestyle & Coffee Co. is a mountain espresso bar and lifestyle store in Whistler, BC, serving third-wave coffee using 49th Parallel beans in a space that celebrates West Coast outdoor culture. The store occupies two levels — a ground-floor espresso bar and a curated loft with designer clothing and homewares — and features an outdoor seating area called The Camp Site with Adirondack chairs, a fountain, and a fire pit. For touring cyclists rolling through Whistler, it offers quality coffee and a relaxed outdoor spot to sit and decompress.

detail.address: 1066 Millar Creek Road, Whistler BC V8E 0S8

restaurant.name: The Wizard Grill
restaurant.desc: The Wizard Grill is a dining venue within the Whistler Blackcomb resort complex, operated as part of the Vail Resorts mountain dining portfolio. It serves skiers, mountain bikers, and resort visitors at one of North America's largest ski and bike destinations. Current web content at the restaurant's URL displays the name 'Merlin's Cafe', suggesting the venue may have been renamed.

restaurant.name: Commodore
restaurant.desc: The Commodore Grand Cafe & Lounge is a tapas bar and lounge on Victoria Street in downtown Kamloops, offering drinks, small plates, and occasional events. It operates exclusively as a late-night venue and maintains a VIP guest list program. The atmosphere and programming are oriented toward nightlife rather than daytime food service.

detail.address: Victoria Street, City of Kamloops, V2C 3N3

restaurant.name: StonesEdge
restaurant.desc: Stonesedge Kitchen is a modern sports bar in Whistler Village operated by the Gibbons Hospitality Group, blending elevated comfort food — centred on high-quality burgers — with craft cocktails, frozen drinks, and boozy milkshakes, plus an unexpected caviar offering. It runs weekly themed nights and is a lively gathering spot in the heart of the village. For a touring cyclist rolling into Whistler, it offers a full sit-down meal and cocktail experience steps from the village centre.

restaurant.name: Lucky Bar
restaurant.desc: Lucky Bar is a storied live-music and DJ venue in downtown Victoria, programming an eclectic range of genres — punk, metal, hip-hop, house, reggae, folk, jazz, and more — alongside variety shows and film screenings under the motto 'Everything happens at Lucky Bar.' Situated on Yates Street, it runs multiple events most nights of the week and draws a devoted local crowd. For touring cyclists, it offers an accessible evening entertainment option right in the heart of the city.

restaurant.name: Pho Stanley
restaurant.desc: Pho Stanley is a family-owned Vietnamese restaurant in North Delta serving steaming bowls of pho, vermicelli, and rice plates made with fresh ingredients and time-honoured recipes. Under new ownership as of roughly 2024, the restaurant has maintained its loyal following while refreshing its service. The casual dining room is described as comfy and welcoming, suited to a relaxed post-ride meal.

restaurant.name: Yummy Donair & Kebab
restaurant.desc: Yummy Donair & Kebab is a fast-casual restaurant in North Vancouver specializing in Middle Eastern and Persian-inspired cuisine, including donairs, kebabs, and falafel. Opened in 2011, the restaurant developed its own spice blends and cooking processes around a healthier take on traditional kebabs. Online ordering and catering services are available, making it a practical stop for a quick hot meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Falafel Donair, Falafel Fries, Falafel Platter, and Falafel Salad Box — multiple vegetarian/vegan options

restaurant.name: Pokeritto
restaurant.desc: Pokeritto Renfrew is a Pan-Asian poke bowl and sushi burrito chain location in East Vancouver's Renfrew Village neighbourhood. The menu features sushi-grade salmon, tuna, and plant-based proteins with over 50 customizable combinations across Classic Poke Bowls, Sushi Burritos, Warm Pokerritos, and a Kids Bowl. It is one of roughly a dozen Pokeritto locations across Metro Vancouver and Toronto.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu pages label options with vegan (🌱) and gluten-free (GF) icons; plant-based proteins include fried tofu and avocado; multiple vegan-labeled sauces (Citrus Ponzu, Classic Shoyu, SSS, Sweet Chili, Wasabi Basil listed as GF/vegan)

restaurant.name: Wok Box
restaurant.desc: Wok Box is a Canadian fast-casual franchise founded in Edmonton in 2004 and now operating over 60 locations coast to coast, drawing its menu from more than 10 Asian culinary traditions — rice boxes, noodle boxes, wings, poutines, and more. The Fort St. John outpost sits in a commercial strip on 96 Street, making it a convenient resupply stop for cyclists travelling through northeastern BC's Peace Region. The chain emphasizes freshness and offers diet-accommodating options including vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-friendly dishes.

detail.address: 9317 96 Street, Fort St. John, BC V1J 6V5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states: 'Yes, we do! See our Special Diet Guide to find your next customized dish' in response to a question about vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-friendly options

restaurant.name: RE-UP BBQ
restaurant.desc: RE-UP BBQ is a barbecue restaurant situated on Quayside Drive in New Westminster, with a capacity of 50 and both indoor and outdoor seating. Its waterfront location makes it a potential stop for cyclists riding the Fraser River trail corridor. OSM tags indicate vegetarian options are available and the premises are wheelchair accessible.

detail.address: 114-810 Quayside Drive, New Westminster, BC V3M 6B9

restaurant.name: The Colander
restaurant.desc: The Colander is a Trail institution opened in 1972 by the LeRose family, rooted in the all-you-can-eat boarding house dining tradition of early Italian immigrant workers at Cominco. Renowned for its secret-recipe pasta sauce, it has been named by Beautiful BC magazine as one of the province's top 24 restaurants and voted the #1 Italian restaurant in the East and West Kootenays. Cyclists passing through the Kootenays will find generous, hearty portions — reviewers routinely leave with leftovers.

restaurant.name: Fuji Market
restaurant.desc: Fuji Market is a Japanese grocery store and casual deli eatery at the heart of Whistler Resort, serving locals and visitors for several decades with an authentic taste of Japan. The deli counter offers freshly made sushi rolls, donburi rice bowls, karaage chicken, gyoza, and other Japanese sides available to go or eat in. The grocery side stocks Japanese pantry staples — soy sauces, miso, short-grain rice, noodles, tofu, and frozen foods — making it equally useful for cyclists looking to cook their own Japanese meals.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a dedicated 'Vegan Bowl' (avocado and yam tempura) and 'Vegetable Gyoza'; no GF labelling mentioned

restaurant.name: Sushi Time Express
restaurant.desc: Sushi Time Express is a fast-casual sushi counter in Victoria's St. Andrew's Square, serving an extensive menu of rolls, rice bowls, bento boxes, nigiri and sashimi, noodles, and breakfast items alongside healthy smoothies. The Express concept centers on fresh ingredients prepared quickly at counter service, making it a practical downtown stop for cyclists passing through the Yates Street corridor. Bento boxes and a broad roll menu — including several vegetarian and potentially vegan options — give touring cyclists flexible, portable meal choices.

notes.Packed lunches: Bento boxes listed as a dedicated menu category, providing portable packaged meals suitable for the road
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes avocado roll, yam roll, vegetable roll, and salad wrap (romaine, avocado, carrot, cucumber, rice paper, sweet chili sauce); avocado and chicken salads also available

restaurant.name: Modus
restaurant.desc: Modus is a Vancouver-based specialty coffee micro-roaster operating an intimate cafe at 112 West Broadway, known for a hyper-seasonal menu of single-origin light roasts built around close producer relationships. The Broadway shop doubles as a retail space for beans, brewing gear, and apparel, and is available for private events seating up to 30 people. Coffee education is offered through The Coffee Division, the workshop arm of the business, running public tastings and private corporate sessions.

restaurant.name: IKEA Bistro
restaurant.desc: IKEA Bistro is a Swedish-style fast food counter on level 1 of the IKEA Richmond store, serving classic IKEA fare in a large retail environment. The Richmond location is undergoing a planned expansion and is conveniently accessible from the Canada Line via several bus routes. For cyclists navigating Richmond's flat terrain, it sits just off Sweden Way near Jacombs Road.

notes.Covered bike parking: Covered bike racks available near the store entrance

restaurant.name: Kwan Kee Noodle House
restaurant.desc: Kwan Kee Noodle House is a Chinese fast-food noodle restaurant in North Vancouver. It offers quick dining service typical of casual Asian cuisine establishments, providing a convenient meal option for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: KJ Enjoy Garden Restaurant
restaurant.desc: KJ Enjoy Garden Restaurant is a Chinese cuisine restaurant in Pitt Meadows serving a broad Cantonese and Szechuan menu spanning beef, chicken, pork, seafood, tofu, noodle, and rice dishes. It offers both dine-in and online ordering with pickup and delivery. Located on Harris Road, it sits near cycling corridors connecting Pitt Meadows to the Golden Ears and Pitt River recreational areas.

detail.address: 12520 Harris Rd, Pitt Meadows, BC V3Y2J4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Vegetable Chow Mein (#16), Mushroom Chow Mein (#17), Vegetable Crispy Noodles (#32), Mushroom Crispy Noodles (#33), and Bean Cake with Mushrooms (#93) — all appear meatless

restaurant.name: Tobiko Sushi
restaurant.desc: Tobiko Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant inside Fleetwood Plaza on Fraser Highway in Surrey, operating as 'Tobiko Sushi 1' — the first of what appears to be a multi-location operation. The menu spans classic rolls, nigiri, sashimi, and an extensive lineup of party trays in sizes from 33 to 104 pieces. Both dine-in and online takeout ordering are available, making it a functional meal stop for cyclists moving along the Fraser Highway corridor.

restaurant.name: Sakuya Sushi
restaurant.desc: Sakuya Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in South Surrey offering a broad menu of rolls, sashimi, nigiri, tempura, donburi, and teriyaki. The kitchen features dozens of specialty and signature rolls alongside bento lunches and party trays. It sits near the Tsawwassen boundary, making it a convenient meal stop for cyclists on the South Surrey–Delta corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes: Edamame, Goma-ae, Agedashi Tofu, Spicy Agedashi Tofu, Yam Tempura, Vegetable Tempura, Kappa Roll (cucumber), Asparagus Roll, Avocado Roll, Mango Avocado Roll, and Vegetable Roll

restaurant.name: Clover Sushi
restaurant.desc: Clover Sushi is a Japanese-focused restaurant in a commercial unit on Admirals Road in the Esquimalt/View Royal area of Greater Victoria, blending traditional sushi techniques with creative rolls, premium sashimi, and a few Korean-inspired dishes like bibimbap. The restaurant offers both a dine-in experience in what it describes as an elegant yet comfortable setting, and a pickup option through their mobile ordering service.

restaurant.name: Gathering Tree Eatery and Gift Shop
restaurant.desc: A cafe and gift shop on 5th Avenue in Valemount serving food and beverages to locals and travelers. Located in a small mountain community on the Yellowhead corridor, it provides a convenient stopping point for cycling tours.

restaurant.name: Copper Beach Bar + Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Copper Beach Bar + Kitchen is a full-service restaurant and bar perched on the Sea to Sky Highway in the historic copper-mining village of Britannia Beach, roughly halfway between Vancouver and Squamish. The heated patio overlooks Howe Sound and Britannia Bay, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists riding the Sea to Sky corridor. The venue seats up to 120 guests, serves burgers, American classics, and brunch, and is dog-friendly on the patio.

restaurant.name: Fernwood Pizza Company
restaurant.desc: Fernwood Pizza Company is a neighbourhood pizzeria in Victoria's Fernwood district, billing itself as 'The People's Pie' for its community-minded, inclusive ethos. The menu spans creative vegetarian combinations to classic meat pies, with gluten-free crust and vegan cheese substitutions available. Rotating craft beer, wine, and cider complement the pizza selection, making it a solid refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated Fernwood Vegetarian pizza listed; gluten-free crust substitution available; vegan cheese substitution available

restaurant.name: Gringo
restaurant.desc: Gringo is a casual Mexi-Cali cantina in North Vancouver's Lonsdale neighbourhood, one of three Vancouver-area locations that trace their roots to a Gastown opening in 2013. The restaurant pitches itself as an unpretentious 'white-trash cantina' serving tacos, burritos, bowls, and a full bar of margaritas and cocktails in a lively, community-minded atmosphere. It is a full-service, sit-down establishment with a takeout option, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists passing through the area.

detail.address: 100 East 2nd Street, North Vancouver, BC V7L 1C3

restaurant.name: ignite Pizzaria
restaurant.desc: Ignite Pizzeria's South Surrey location sits in the Morgan Crossing open-air mall, offering 60 indoor seats and a 24-seat south-facing patio in a contemporary minimal space. The menu centres on stone-fired, hand-tossed artisanal pizzas alongside pastas and appetizers, and the location is fully licensed for beer, wine, and housemade cocktails. Crescent Beach is roughly 15 minutes away, making this a practical refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the South Surrey waterfront.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes a dedicated 'HERBIVORE + VEGAN' pizza section and a housemade gluten-friendly crust available for medium-size pizzas

restaurant.name: Once Upon @ Thai
restaurant.desc: A Thai restaurant in Chilliwack operating since 2021 that also offers catering services. A dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Waves Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Waves Coffee House is a Canadian coffee chain with a location on Columbia Street in North Vancouver. It provides both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a practical stop for cyclists on tours in the area.

restaurant.name: Trees Organic Coffee
restaurant.desc: Trees Organic Coffee is a Vancouver-area cafe chain established in 1996, known for its in-house roasted organic coffee and award-winning homemade New York-style cheesecakes. This Capstan (Richmond) location offers coffee, tea, sandwiches, salads, soups, and baked goods. With 14 locations across greater Vancouver, Trees also hosts live music events and offers online ordering with in-store pickup and delivery.

restaurant.name: Caffè Cittadella
restaurant.desc: Caffè Cittadella is an espresso bar and bistro housed in a heritage building dating to 1894, complete with a scenic outdoor patio that makes it a welcoming rest stop. The menu spans specialty coffee, teas, fresh-baked pastries, breakfast and lunch sandwiches, soups, and a full bar including wine, beer, and cocktails. A curated thrift boutique operates on the second floor, giving the stop an unusually eclectic character.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists 'Gluten-Free and Vegan Pastries', 'Vegetarian and Vegan Selections', Keto Muffins, and menu items marked (V/GF) and (GF/V)

restaurant.name: Sutton Place Wine Merchant
restaurant.desc: Sutton Place Wine Merchant is a boutique wine, beer, and spirits shop in the heart of downtown Vancouver, with over 17 years in business and a curated selection of 1,000+ bottles sourced from local and international vineyards. The store employs certified sommeliers who offer personalized consultations and hosts regular guided tasting events, including a free weekly Friday tasting and monthly Backroom Barrel Sessions. Cyclists can purchase a bottle to go or have products delivered via Uber Eats, making it a convenient downtown stop for those wanting to bring home a local BC wine.

restaurant.name: Orrange Kitchen + Bar
restaurant.desc: Orrange Kitchen + Bar is an independently owned neighbourhood restaurant and bar in Port Coquitlam, founded in 2013 by local resident Brian Orrange as a community gathering place inspired by family recipes and travel. The menu spans shareable starters, burgers, mains, and hand-crafted cocktails in a room designed after the founder's family rec-room. A Mezzanine with a private patio is available for group events, making it a capable stop for a larger riding party.
