detail.address: 111-1125 Nicola Ave, Port Coquitlam, BC V3B 8B2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items carry a 'gf' label (e.g., CAJUN CHICKEN HOUSE gf, TORTILLA SOUP gf, SOY + WASABI SALMON gf); crispy tofu substitution noted as available on request for the Coquitlam Crunch Salad

restaurant.name: Caveman Cafe
restaurant.desc: Caveman Cafe bills itself as the 'King of Keto' — a health-focused restaurant and bakery serving globally-inspired whole-food meals that are fully customizable for keto, paleo, vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free diets. The menu runs from butter chicken and burritos to grassfed steaks and raw-vegan desserts, all made without refined sugar or processed ingredients. The operation also does large-scale off-site catering and has a community record of supplying healthy meals to social-service organizations across Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, paleo, and keto options including plant-based entrees and raw-vegan desserts

restaurant.name: Amore Bistro Café
restaurant.desc: A casual bistro café in Nanaimo offering both dine-in and takeout service. Located on McCullough Road, it provides a convenient food stop for touring cyclists needing a meal break.

restaurant.name: The Buvette
restaurant.desc: The Buvette is a cozy lunch spot in Squamish serving gourmet homemade sandwiches alongside coffee, natural wine, and beer. It sits with a view of the Stawamus Chief and doubles as a natural pit stop for cyclists travelling the Sea-to-Sky corridor between Squamish and Whistler. Outdoor seating and a take-away option make it easy for cyclists to refuel without lingering.

restaurant.name: Bayview Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Bayview Brewing Company is a microbrewery and pub in Ladysmith that brews its own beer on-site. It offers outdoor seating and accepts multiple payment methods. Touring cyclists will find a casual spot to enjoy locally-crafted beverages.

restaurant.name: Steve's Poké Bar
restaurant.desc: Steve's Poke Bar is an authentic Hawaiian poke chain founded by Steve Huynh, whose recipes draw on family traditions from Oahu and years spent between Vancouver and Honolulu. The chain has earned over 10,000 five-star Google reviews across its Lower Mainland locations and is widely recognized as Vancouver's top-rated poke spot. Cyclists can order customizable poke bowls for pickup with vegetarian options including a tofu bowl.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists a Shoyu Tofu bowl (tofu, avocado, rice, vegetables) as a vegetarian signature option

restaurant.name: Dusty's
restaurant.desc: Dusty's Bar & BBQ is one of the oldest bars in the Whistler valley, established in 1965 and anchored in Whistler Creekside with a lively mythology involving a stuffed horse that allegedly galloped into the night. The venue serves slow-smoked BBQ alongside a creative cocktail menu, with live music three times a week and a daily après scene that draws locals and visitors alike. A 'Bike 'n' Grab' section on the menu signals a deliberate nod to the cycling crowd passing through Creekside.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels multiple items: Vegetarian (Signature Potato Wedges, Yam Fries, Corn Ribs, Southwest Salad), Vegan (Smoked Vegan Burger, Southwest Salad vegan option), Gluten free (Classic Dusty's Burger, Smoked Vegan Burger, Crispy Chicken Burger, Southwest Salad), and Dairy free (Signature Potato Wedges, Yam Fries)

restaurant.name: Lakeside Beach Club
restaurant.desc: Lakeside Beach Club is a full-service restaurant and patio in Cultus Lake, roughly 10 km south of Chilliwack and a five-minute walk from the main beach. Owned by chef Chris Ovens and his wife Christy since 2015, the kitchen draws on locally sourced ingredients from Columbia Valley farms and pairs them with creative cocktails and an innovative menu. Cyclists can settle hearthside in winter or cool off on the patio in summer, making it a year-round destination on the Cultus Lake circuit.

detail.address: 4131 Columbia Valley Road, Cultus Lake, BC V2R 4Y1

restaurant.name: Cockney Kings
restaurant.desc: Cockney Kings is a family-owned fish and chips institution that has been serving classic English-style fish and chips in Metro Vancouver since 1965, growing from a single East Hastings shop to four locations across the Lower Mainland. The New Westminster location is a full-service dine-in restaurant offering traditional battered fish — cod, haddock, snapper, salmon, and halibut — fried in beef tallow alongside hand-cut chips, seafood starters, and comfort sides. It remains a multi-generational family operation with a loyal local following built over six decades.

detail.address: Unit 130 – 66 10th Street, New Westminster, BC V3M 1A6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms gluten-friendly options (grilled or steamed fish, garden salad, coleslaw, Caesar salad without croutons, fish tacos on locally made corn tortillas); chips noted as technically gluten-free but sharing fryers with wheat products. Vegetarian-suitable salads and certain sides available, though deep-fried items including chips are cooked in beef tallow

restaurant.name: Fable Diner
restaurant.desc: Fable Diner is an East Vancouver original established in 2016 inside the historic Lee Building at the busy Main & Broadway intersection in Mount Pleasant. Featured on Food Network's Diners Drive-Ins and Dives (Season 29, Episode 17), the diner is celebrated for creative comfort food built on locally sourced ingredients, with signature dishes like the Duck Pancake with kimchi. It is a well-rooted neighbourhood institution offering full table service, weekend brunch, and online ordering.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Brunch menu states 'Gluten free buns, bread and english muffins available for substitution [charges apply]'; menu also lists a veggie patty sub and Avocado Benny

restaurant.name: The Greek Kouzina Express
restaurant.desc: The Greek Kouzina Express is a family-run Greek restaurant and food truck in Kamloops's Westsyde neighbourhood, operated by third-generation restauranteur Andreas Mougholias whose family has run Greek and Italian eateries in the area since 1975. The menu centres on souvlaki wraps, traditional Greek plates, and shareable sides made from house recipes and fresh ingredients. In addition to the brick-and-mortar dine-in location, they operate a mobile food truck that appears at various community events around the region.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Catering section lists 'Vegetarian and gluten aware options' as part of customizable packages

restaurant.name: Big Feast Bistro
restaurant.desc: Big Feast Bistro is a locally-celebrated small-town bistro with an urban atmosphere that opened in Maple Ridge in 2010 and was featured on the Food Network's 'You Gotta Eat Here.' The kitchen sources from over 50 local suppliers and hand-crafts its menu daily with a strong emphasis on gluten-free, vegetarian, vegan, and Ocean Wise seafood options. The bistro also operates a retail line of artisan small-batch products available in-house, making it a useful resupply stop for cyclists wanting to take local goods on the road.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states menu focuses on gluten-free options, vegetarian and vegan choices, and Ocean Wise certified seafood; entire menu can be made gluten-free except stir-fry sauce; GF buns toasted on clean grill; keto options also available

restaurant.name: Manvirros Indian Grill
restaurant.desc: Manvirros Indian Grill is a family-owned restaurant in Nanaimo serving authentic East Indian cuisine using recipes passed down through generations, with a menu spanning tandoori, biryani, curries, and regional specialties. The dining room is described by customers as cozy and warmly decorated, and the kitchen is helmed by a chef trained in Chandigarh with experience cooking North Indian and Mughalai cuisine. Catering for events and parties is also available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated vegetarian section with multiple dishes: Aloo Gobi, Chana Masala, Eggplant, Navrattan Korma, Paneer Butter Masala, Paneer Korma, Paneer Tikka Masala, Paneer Vindaloo, Shahee Paneer, Vegetable Vindaloo, Bhindi Masala, Veggie Biryani, and Paneer Biryani. Vegan and GF options not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: Rosemary Rocksalt Bagelry
restaurant.desc: Rosemary Rocksalt is a Vancouver-area bagel chain specializing in authentic Montreal-style bagels that are hand-rolled, honey-boiled, and baked fresh daily in a traditional open-flame stone-hearth oven. The Richmond location on Steveston Highway offers bagel sandwiches, house-made cream cheeses, soups, and take-home grocery items sourced from local suppliers. It sits along the Steveston cycling corridor and markets itself as a community gathering place, making it a welcoming and substantive food stop on a coastal or delta touring route.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Cashew Cream Cheese (Vegan) in three flavours, Butternut Squash Soup (Vegetarian & Gluten Free), Broccoli Cheddar Soup (Vegetarian), and a North Shore veggie bagel sandwich. Catering page notes 'Vegetarian options available upon request.'

restaurant.name: Pine House Bread & Cake Shop
restaurant.desc: Pine House Bread & Cake Shop is a local bakery situated on Kingsway in Vancouver's east side. It specializes in bread and cakes, making it a convenient stop for cyclists looking to pick up freshly baked goods along a busy arterial route. The OSM record notes wheelchair accessibility at the premises.

restaurant.name: Wings West Kelowna
restaurant.desc: Wings West Kelowna is part of the WINGS restaurant chain, a BC franchise known for award-winning chicken wings in 28 globally-inspired flavours. This 'food primary, all ages welcome' location offers a full sit-down menu including wings, burgers, salads, and pastas alongside weekly dine-in specials. Cyclists in the West Kelowna area will find a casual, family-friendly stop with online ordering available.

detail.address: 1-2484 Main Street, West Kelowna, BC V4T 2G2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'CAULI' WINGERZ' (cauliflower-based, vegetarian) and 'GLUTEN-SMART' wings as distinct menu options

restaurant.name: Black Clover Pub
restaurant.desc: The Black Clover is a downtown Prince George Irish pub offering authentic Irish-inspired cuisine alongside an extensive selection of spirits, a 10-tap 'Brass Cascade' draught system featuring Irish and domestic craft brews, and a revolving wine list. It bills itself as Prince George's newest downtown gathering spot with a traditional Public House atmosphere — quiet corners, live entertainment, and an unpretentious service ethos.

restaurant.name: Cavo Bar+Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Cavo Bar+Kitchen is a modern Mediterranean restaurant and bar on Granville Street in Vancouver's entertainment district, serving mezze plates, handmade pastas, flame-grilled skewers, and craft cocktails with a coastal-inspired flair. The venue features both indoor seating and a back patio with a laid-back island atmosphere, and sits just steps from a SkyTrain station. Private event bookings are also available for groups and corporate gatherings.

notes.Takeout: Menu page lists 'Souvlaki Bar (Online Order Only)' as a distinct menu section, confirming online ordering and takeout is offered

restaurant.name: The Borscht Bowl
restaurant.desc: The Borscht Bowl is a regional restaurant in Grand Forks specializing in Eastern European cuisine and traditional borscht soup. Located on downtown Market Avenue, it offers a distinctive dining experience for touring cyclists and travelers passing through the area. The restaurant contributes a unique cultural flavor to Grand Forks' food scene.

restaurant.name: Jolly Mac's
restaurant.desc: Jolly Mac's is a family-owned neighborhood pub and liquor store in Surrey serving American-style comfort food including burgers, wings, ribs, and fish and chips. The venue features a 200-person seating capacity, a 1,000 sq ft outdoor patio, and a large HD screen for sports viewing. It also hosts events such as birthday parties, fundraisers, and has run an annual car and bike show.

restaurant.name: Pho 68
restaurant.desc: Pho 68 is an authentic Vietnamese restaurant in Surrey, BC, with over two decades of community presence. It specializes in traditional noodle soups — including the signature Pho Dac Biet and spicy Bun Bo Hue — alongside desserts like the Everything Coconut. Cyclists can dine in or order online for pickup.

notes.Wi-Fi: Website does not explicitly mention Wi-Fi

restaurant.name: Ryuu Japanese Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Ryuu Japanese Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant serving authentic home-style Japanese cuisine with a UBC campus location on University Boulevard. It is one of three Ryuu locations in Vancouver and offers online ordering with a loyalty rewards program. Cyclists navigating the UBC area will find it a convenient dine-in or takeout option.

restaurant.name: Hynes' Irish Pub
restaurant.desc: Hynes' is an Irish-owned and Irish-run pub in the Kitsilano neighbourhood, dedicated to the Hynes family of Galway and built around good Guinness, draught beers, and comfort-food cooking. It hosts traditional Irish music sessions and live musicians multiple nights a week, and offers a hireable private lounge for groups of up to 60. Weekend brunch is served Saturday and Sunday, making it a viable stop at multiple points in a cycling day.

restaurant.name: Kent's Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Kent's Kitchen is a long-established Cantonese takeout restaurant on Victoria Drive that relocated from Vancouver's Chinatown and has retained a devoted local following. The menu spans classic dishes — fried rice, chow mein, spareribs, and fresh seafood — with online ordering available for fast pickup. Cyclists will find it a convenient, affordable stop for a filling hot meal on a busy arterial corridor in south Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes: Eggplant and Tofu (茄子豆腐), Egg Tofu (玉子豆付), and Buddha's Feast (羅漢斋)

restaurant.name: Loriz - Our Daily Bread
restaurant.desc: Loriz - Our Daily Bread is a Filipino specialty bakery offering traditional breads including pandesal, ensaymada, Spanish bread, monay, and pan de coco. The bakery emphasizes authentic island baking traditions rooted in Philippine culinary heritage, with a product line spanning sweet buns, savoury buns, empanadas, and hopia pastries. Cyclists stopping in would find a distinctive selection of Filipino baked goods not commonly found at mainstream grocery stops.

restaurant.name: House of James
restaurant.desc: House of James is a well-established Christian bookstore and coffeeshop in Abbotsford, BC, carrying an extensive selection of books, music, church supplies, and gifts across a two-storey retail building. The store features rotating art installations by local artists, including fluid art canvases displayed on the grand staircase. The in-house coffeeshop makes it a practical rest point for cyclists moving through the Abbotsford commercial corridor.

restaurant.name: Carmelis Goat Cheese and Gelato
restaurant.desc: Carmelis Goat Cheese and Gelato is an ice cream and cheese shop in Naramata, BC. Based on its name, it specializes in both gelato and artisanal goat cheese products. The shop offers these items to the public.

restaurant.name: New Parmar Sweets & Catering
restaurant.desc: An Indian restaurant and sweets shop in Surrey's Newton neighbourhood, now operating under the name New Parmar Sweets & Catering, with a second South Surrey location recently added. The kitchen prepares a broad range of authentic subcontinental dishes daily — from street-food chaats and tandoori items to curries and Indo-Chinese fusion — alongside house-made fresh sweets. The dining hall seats up to 50 guests and the business offers online ordering and full event catering.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Extensive vegetarian sections throughout the menu: vegetarian samosas, paneer dishes, veg curries, vegetarian Indo-Chinese options (Chilli Paneer, Veggie Manchurian, Honey Chilli Potato, etc.), and vegetarian tandoori items. No explicit vegan or gluten-free claims found

restaurant.name: Everything Wine
restaurant.desc: Everything Wine is a BC-based specialty wine and spirits retailer carrying a broad selection of wine by region, variety, and occasion, alongside beer, cider, and spirits. The Surrey location sits in a strip-mall unit and is part of a multi-store chain. Cyclists passing through could pick up wine, craft beer, or cider for the evening, though the store offers no on-site consumption.

detail.address: 15735 Croydon Drive, Unit 112, Surrey, BC V3Z 2L5

restaurant.name: Ramen Bella Poco
restaurant.desc: A ramen restaurant located in Port Coquitlam. No details about amenities, services, or current operational status are available due to website unavailability.

restaurant.name: Cozen Japanese Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Cozen Japanese Cuisine is a full-service Japanese restaurant on Vancouver's busy Commercial Drive, formerly known as Tatsu Japanese Bistro. The menu centres on sushi, sashimi, and Japanese mains prepared from fresh, globally sourced ingredients, including creative specialty rolls the restaurant considers exclusive to its kitchen. The business also provides online ordering, catering packages, and private event hosting.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu marks Agedashi Tofu as '(VG)', lists Vege Gyoza and Cauliflower Karage as vegetarian options; Real Crab Roll and Blue Ocean Roll note 'GF available'

restaurant.name: Sushi King George
restaurant.desc: A Japanese sushi restaurant situated in a strip mall on King George Boulevard in Surrey, BC. The restaurant offers dine-in service and online ordering, making it a convenient stop for a hot meal on a long King George corridor ride. The OSM record lists it as wheelchair accessible.

restaurant.name: Moodys Pub
restaurant.desc: A pub located in Lake Country (Winfield). Serves as a gathering place for locals and visitors seeking food and beverage.

restaurant.name: Zalas Steak House
restaurant.desc: Zalas Restaurant is a Revelstoke institution since 1976, serving charbroiled steaks, classic Italian pastas and pizzas, and seafood in a warm dining room with a fireplace and full bar. The restaurant explicitly welcomes guests arriving after outdoor adventures in the Monashees and Selkirk Mountains, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists finishing a big day. Private event hosting and a curated wine list round out the experience.

restaurant.name: umé
restaurant.desc: Umé is a family-owned Japanese restaurant tucked into Burtch Plaza on Highway 97 (Harvey Avenue) in Kelowna, serving sushi, sashimi, bento boxes, donburi, and more—all prepared MSG-free with fresh ingredients. It has earned a strong local reputation, landing in TripAdvisor's Top 10 best sushi in Kelowna and holding a 4.7-star Google rating from 360+ reviews. Cyclists riding the Highway 97 corridor have the option to dine in or grab takeout via Skip the Dishes or DoorDash.

restaurant.name: Mott 32
restaurant.desc: Mott 32 is a globally acclaimed Chinese restaurant brand with locations across Asia, the Middle East, and North America, known for its 42-day applewood-roasted Peking Duck, handcrafted dim sum, and award-winning interior design blending New York industrial style with traditional Chinese culture. The Vancouver location sits at the base of the Arthur Erickson-designed tower in Coal Harbour, featuring an expansive main dining room, four private dining rooms, and an outdoor terrace with views over downtown Vancouver. It is one of the more celebrated upscale Chinese dining destinations in the city.

detail.address: 1161 W Georgia Street, Vancouver, BC V6E 0C6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes 'Plant Based Crispy Chicken, Szechuan Red Peppercorns, Chilli & Cashew', 'Wild Mushroom & Water Chestnut Dumpling', 'Stir-Fried Wild Mushroom, Lettuce Cup, Black Truffle', and 'Braised Egg Tofu with Morel Mushrooms'

restaurant.name: Cantina Di Luigi
restaurant.desc: Cantina di Luigi is a dimly lit Italian wine bar nestled in the back of Mercato di Luigi in Vancouver's Chinatown, offering a curated all-Italian wine list by the glass, half litre, or bottle alongside pasta, cheeses, and cured meats. It is part of the Kitchen Table Restaurants group and shares its style of service with the well-regarded Ask for Luigi next door. The space is designed for slow, convivial dining with an emphasis on small-producer and indigenous Italian grape varieties.

detail.address: 213 E Georgia Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 1Z6

restaurant.name: Hot Pie Pizza
restaurant.desc: Hot Pie Pizza is a casual pizza restaurant located on Water Street in Vancouver. It provides quick-service pizza dining as a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Kekuli Cafe
restaurant.desc: Kekuli Cafe is an Indigenous-owned fast-casual cafe founded by Sharon Bond-Hogg of the Nooaitch First Nation, celebrating Indigenous culinary traditions through bannock-based sandwiches, tipi tacos, Mother Earth Bowls, and organic fair-trade espresso drinks. The menu draws on locally sourced ingredients and highlights traditional ingredients like venison, wild salmon, and saskatoon berries. It is part of a small BC franchise with locations in West Kelowna, Kelowna, Merritt, and Kamloops.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists 'Vegetarian Breakfast Bannock' explicitly; vegan and GF options not confirmed

restaurant.name: Fomi's Bakery
restaurant.desc: Fomi's Bakery is a bakery on Highway 6 in Winlaw, BC. Bakeries provide fresh baked goods and are a convenient food stop for touring cyclists. Website content is unavailable, so specific services and amenities cannot be confirmed.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: This Subway franchise, branded 'Subway Metropolis At Metrotown', is located inside the large Metropolis at Metrotown shopping mall on the busy Kingsway corridor in Burnaby. It offers the full Subway lineup of customizable sandwiches, wraps, and salads with multiple ordering options including pickup, delivery, and in-restaurant dining. As a mall-level food court unit, it gives cyclists access to a quick, customizable meal near a major transit hub.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website highlights fresh-cut veggies and customizable options

restaurant.name: The Templeton
restaurant.desc: The Templeton is a nostalgic American-style diner in the heart of Vancouver's Granville entertainment district, dishing up all-day breakfast made with free-run eggs and naturally smoked bacon alongside gourmet burgers and authentic milkshakes. The retro atmosphere features a jukebox and a no-reservations, first-come first-served policy that keeps things lively. Fully licensed and indoors-only, it is a locally loved comfort-food destination in a central, high-traffic part of downtown Vancouver.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast-food restaurant in the Lynn Valley area of North Vancouver, offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, McCafé beverages, and desserts. The location has a drive-through and takeaway service, making it a quick stop for cyclists passing through this suburban corridor. As part of a large national chain, the range of hot and cold food and drink options is broadly consistent across locations.

restaurant.name: Eatology
restaurant.desc: EATology is a bright, quick-service diner in downtown Vernon, established in 2015, serving breakfast and lunch with 90% of dishes made in-house using fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The menu changes regularly and always includes vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options, with coffee from Vernon-roasted Multiply Coffee. Touring cyclists will find it a convenient downtown stop for a real meal, with takeout available for those hitting the road.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: 'Vegetarian, gluten-free and vegan-friendly options are always available.'

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: This McDonald's, branded internally as the 'TV Towers' branch, sits on Robson Street in central Vancouver near the entertainment and shopping district. It is a dine-in location with both indoor and outdoor seating and no drive-through. As a 24/7 urban fast-food stop it offers a reliable resupply point for cyclists passing through the city core.

restaurant.name: Old Durbar Nepalese & Indian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A sit-down Nepalese and Indian restaurant on East Broadway in Vancouver offering traditional South Asian cuisine with vegan and vegetarian options. The restaurant supports online ordering and serves as a dining option for touring cyclists in the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegan and vegetarian options confirmed

restaurant.name: Yellow Deli
restaurant.desc: Yellow Deli is a chain of rustic, handcrafted delis founded in Chattanooga, Tennessee in 1973 and operated by an intentional religious community. Locations are known for their distinctive décor of barn beams, macramé, leatherwork, and custom booth seating, often spread across multiple floors of converted spaces. The menu centres on sandwiches on fresh-baked bread, made-from-scratch soups, garden salads, and homemade desserts.

restaurant.name: The Italians
restaurant.desc: The Italians is a small, intimate Italian restaurant in Vancouver's West End where all pasta is made in-house daily and the menu stays unapologetically rooted in regional Italian tradition—dishes like Spaghetti alla Carbonara and Bucatini all'Amatriciana are prepared the authentic Roman and central-Italian way. The room has a cozy date-night atmosphere with table service, but the kitchen also handles takeout orders and full-scale catering for private events. Reviewers consistently single out the freshness of ingredients and the attentiveness of staff.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Customer review confirms gluten-free Alfredo available. Menu lists multiple meatless pasta dishes (Linguine al Pesto, Spaghetti all'Arrabbiata, Tagliatelle al Tartufo) and vegetarian starters (Bruschetta, Caprese, Insalata Mista). No explicit vegan claim

restaurant.name: Everything Wine
restaurant.desc: Everything Wine is a BC-based specialty alcohol retailer offering an extensive selection of wine, beer, cider, and spirits from around the world, with a particular emphasis on wine education and food pairing. The Langley Bypass location is part of a provincial chain known for knowledgeable staff, wine consultations, and curated buyers-picks programs. Touring cyclists exploring the Fraser Valley wine corridor could stop here to pick up local BC wines or other provisions for the road.

restaurant.name: Grouse Grind Coffee Bar
restaurant.desc: Grouse Grind Coffee Bar is a café within the Grouse Mountain resort in North Vancouver, named after the famous Grouse Grind hiking trail that draws thousands of visitors to the area. The resort also hosts the Grouse Bike Park — a lift-accessed mountain bike park — making this a natural stop for cyclists in the area. It sits within a busy outdoor recreation hub that includes gondola access, wildlife habitats, and multiple dining venues.

restaurant.name: Legends Pub & Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Legends Pub & Restaurant is a well-established Richmond sports bar with roots going back to 1994, now settled in a two-storey building near Vancouver International Airport. The venue boasts over 30 TVs including three large screens, making it Richmond's self-described prime sports destination. It offers a full kitchen with daily house-made soups, a wide selection of vegetarian dishes, and off-sales beer to go.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website front page states 'Vegetarian options galore. Salads, Veggie burgers, and delicious Pastas.'

restaurant.name: 14th Ave Pub
restaurant.desc: A neighbourhood sports pub and casual eatery in Mission that has been serving the community since 1977. The pub features a broad selection of Pacific Northwest craft beers, daily food and drink specials, multiple big-screen TVs for sports, and an attached liquor store open 365 days a year. Live bands perform every second Saturday and karaoke runs every Friday, making it a lively stop for an evening meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Tuesday taco special listed as 'spicy beef or veggie', confirming at least one vegetarian menu item

restaurant.name: Peninsula U Brew Winery
restaurant.desc: A wine shop located in Sidney on the Saanich Peninsula. The business operates as a wine retailer serving the local community and passing cyclists.

restaurant.name: Beacon Pub & Eatery
restaurant.desc: Beacon Pub & Eatery is a craft beer and comfort food pub located in the heart of Whistler Village Square, with what the venue describes as the best patio and après vibe in town. The menu leans into hearty fare — Canadian beef and bison burgers, poutine, wings, and loaded tacos — designed to refuel after a full day on the trails or slopes. The venue operates on a first-come, first-served basis with a 90-minute dining limit, so arriving early is advisable during peak periods.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Gluten-free buns available for all handhelds; vegetarian options include a garden black bean veggie burger, Mediterranean mezze with warm falafel, and butternut squash bruschetta

restaurant.name: El Torito Mexican Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Mexican restaurant on Keefer Street in Vancouver's Chinatown neighborhood. Offers casual dining in the heart of the historic district. Active on social media but maintains a minimal online presence.

restaurant.name: KFC
restaurant.desc: A fast-food location on Harvey Avenue, one of Kelowna's main commercial strips, positioned conveniently for cyclists passing through the city core. The OSM record identifies it as KFC, but the linked website is a Taco Bell location page with the same address and phone — it is likely a co-branded KFC/Taco Bell restaurant. Either brand offers quick, affordable hot food and takeout options well-suited to a mid-ride stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Veggie Cravings Menu has indulgent vegetarian items like the Cheesy Bean and Rice Burrito' — confirmed for the Taco Bell side of this location

restaurant.name: Rice Bowl Rose Garden
restaurant.desc: Rice Bowl Rose Garden is a fast food establishment located on Columbia Street West in Kamloops, BC. Beyond its OSM address record, no further details about the restaurant's cuisine, format, or cyclist amenities could be verified due to its website domain resolving to an unrelated third-party delivery platform.

restaurant.name: Cobs
restaurant.desc: COBS Bread is a Canadian franchise arm of the Australian Bakers Delight chain, with 190 locations across Canada. Everything is baked from scratch on-site daily, and any unsold goods are donated to local charities at closing time. A touring cyclist stopping here can pick up fresh bread, rolls, bagels, scones, and savory baked items including mini pizzas and croissant-based pastries.

restaurant.name: Plaisir Sucré
restaurant.desc: Plaisir Sucré is a traditional French bakery and cafe in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, established in December 2009 by Fabrice, a Paris-born baker who brings daily fresh-baked croissants, artisan breads, and classic pastries to the counter. The family-run shop has been voted Best in Vancouver for its almond tartes and is known for its authentic atmosphere and kid-friendly environment with a dedicated play corner. Touring cyclists will find a full lunch menu of soups, quiches, and sandwiches alongside a complete espresso bar.

restaurant.name: Rusted Rake Brewing
restaurant.desc: Rusted Rake Brewing is a farm-to-tap craft brewery and gourmet eatery on a working farm in Nanoose Bay, where the barley for its beers is grown on-site alongside honey, berries, garlic, and herbs used in the kitchen. The brewery has been voted Best Brewery Food Program in BC two years running by Growler Readers' Choice Awards, and its seasonal tap list reflects whatever is growing on the farm at any given time. Set between the sea and fields of barley, the grass patio and farmhouse setting make it a standout experiential stop on Vancouver Island's craft beer trail.

detail.address: 3106 Northwest Bay Road, Nanoose Bay, BC V9P 9E6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ page explicitly lists GF options: Chips and Dip, Burnt Ends, Mushroom Calamari, Moroccan Chickpea, Pulled Pork Tacos, and Sweet Potato Salad; celiac accommodations available on request via server

restaurant.name: Naked Sprout
restaurant.desc: Naked Sprout is a cafe in Whistler, BC offering online food ordering. Cyclists can conveniently order and pick up meals while visiting the area.

restaurant.name: La Casa Gelato
restaurant.desc: La Casa Gelato is a Vancouver institution housed in an iconic pink building on Venables Street, holding the Guinness World Record for 'Most Commercially Available Flavours' with 238 gelato flavours available at any one time. Family-owned and operated for three generations, the shop also offers gelato cakes, Italian pastries, and handmade chocolates. A well-known destination in East Vancouver and a natural stop for cyclists exploring the area — though note they accept only Canadian cash, Canadian debit, or U.S. cash; no credit cards.

restaurant.name: Popeyes
restaurant.desc: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen is a national fast-food chain specializing in Louisiana-style fried chicken, operating out of a ground-floor unit at 700 Hamilton Street in downtown Vancouver. This location has no drive-through and offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a sit-down quick-service option in a dense urban area. For touring cyclists passing through the downtown core, it provides a convenient calorie stop with takeout available.

restaurant.name: 24 Train Express Noodle House
restaurant.desc: 24 Train Express Noodle House is a Vietnamese noodle restaurant located on Nelson Street in downtown Vancouver, offering both indoor dining and a street-facing patio. Its express-style concept and train-themed branding set it apart from the neighbourhood's broader dining scene. Cyclists passing through the downtown core will find it a convenient stop for a hot bowl mid-ride.

restaurant.name: Fountain Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Fountain Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant situated in Blanshard Square in central Victoria, BC. The establishment offers dine-in, takeout, and online ordering, with delivery also available for those staying nearby. Its location in a commercial plaza in a busy part of the city makes it a convenient stop for cyclists moving through the area.

detail.address: 2680 Blanshard Street, Unit 4, Victoria, BC V8T 5E1

restaurant.name: Silvano's Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Silvano's Restaurant is a dining establishment located in the Fraser Valley region of British Columbia. Beyond its classification as a restaurant, no further details about cuisine style, setting, or cyclist-specific offerings could be verified from available sources.

restaurant.name: Jack's Spot
restaurant.desc: Jack's Spot is a small, independently operated cafe on Kingsway in East Vancouver, offering coffee, matcha, sandwiches, bread, and pastries. Its Instagram-only web presence gives it a distinctly local, community-facing character on this busy commercial corridor. Cyclists passing through the Kingsway strip will find it a compact neighbourhood spot for a quick coffee and bite.

restaurant.name: Milano Cafe
restaurant.desc: Milano Coffee is a Vancouver-rooted specialty coffee roaster with over 30 years of history and an Italian-heritage blending tradition, earning 15 gold medals from the International Institute of Coffee Tasters. The West 8th Avenue location is both the head office and working roastery, where Master Roaster Brian Turko crafts blends of up to 20 Arabica bean varietals on-site. It is also one of the only places in Vancouver offering an espresso tasting bar where visitors can sample up to eight different espressos.

restaurant.name: Rice 'N Spice
restaurant.desc: Rice 'N Spice is a family-run food court restaurant that has been a downtown Vancouver institution since 1992, blending Sri-Lankan curries with Mediterranean and Southeast Asian flavours. Located on the lower level of Harbour Centre near the edge of historic Gastown, it is known for freshly ground spices, overnight-marinated shawarma, and a commitment to no MSG and no preservatives. Touring cyclists stopping in the core will find a wide range of hearty rice-bowl dishes, including a fully vegan and gluten-free vegetarian line-up.

detail.address: 555 West Hastings Street, FC-28, Vancouver, BC V6B 4N6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'All vegetarian orders are served with rice and are 100% vegan and gluten free.'

restaurant.name: LR Pizza & Curry
restaurant.desc: LR Pizza & Curry is a Burnaby fast-food restaurant that fuses classic Canadian-style pizza with a full South Asian kitchen covering tandoori, curry, and Indo-Chinese dishes — an unusually broad menu under one roof. Unique offerings like Desi Style pizzas (Tandoori Chicken, Palak Paneer, Shahi Paneer) sit alongside extensive beef, lamb, and seafood curries, giving cyclists a substantial and varied refuelling option. Indoor seating is confirmed via OSM.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists numerous vegetarian items including Veg Samosa, Veg Pakora, Gobi Pakora, Paneer Pakora, Aloo Tikki, Palak Paneer Pizza, Spinach Pizza, Shahi Paneer Pizza, and multiple paneer and vegetable curry dishes

restaurant.name: Panago
restaurant.desc: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain franchise with a location in Coquitlam's Clarke Road corridor, known for using 100% Canadian wheat dough made fresh in-house and organic tomato sauce. The menu leans into plant-based and meat-free options alongside conventional pizzas, salads, and sides. A touring cyclist passing through Coquitlam could stop here for a quick hot meal or a takeout order.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Plant-based options. Fill up and feel good. We've got abundant veggie, dairy-free and meat-free choices to help you live your best plant life.' No GF mention found

restaurant.name: Vegan Fried Chick'un
restaurant.desc: Vegan Fried Chick'un is a fully plant-based fast-food restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver specializing in vegan fried chicken alternatives, Asian-inspired comfort food, burgers, wraps, poutines, and desserts. Every item on the menu is vegan, making it a reliable stop for plant-based cyclists who might otherwise struggle to find cruelty-free options in the fast-food landscape. The restaurant offers takeout, online ordering, and dine-in seating in a casual setting, and can also host group events.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website describes the entire menu as plant-based vegan, with no non-vegan items mentioned

restaurant.name: Mr. Pretzels
restaurant.desc: Mr. Pretzels is a global soft-pretzel franchise founded in Puerto Rico in 1994, operating kiosk-style in shopping centres worldwide. The Victoria location on Douglas Street offers freshly hand-rolled pretzels baked on the spot in sweet and savoury flavours including cinnamon sugar, chocolate, salted, sesame seed, and pretzel dogs. It is a quick, portable snack stop well placed in downtown Victoria for cyclists passing through.

restaurant.name: Waffle House Diner
restaurant.desc: Waffle House Diner is a retro-style breakfast and brunch spot in Surrey, BC, that recently relocated from New Westminster and brought with it an updated menu and a modern twist on the classic diner atmosphere. The kitchen leans into elevated comfort food — think Chicken and Waffles with chili-infused maple syrup, Turkish Eggs on garlic yogurt, and a rotating lineup of creative waffle and French toast builds. Pickup and delivery are both available, making it a practical stop for cyclists wanting a substantial meal without a long sit-down commitment.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Veggie Omelette (roasted red peppers, mushrooms, green onion, tomatoes, cheese) listed on menu; no explicit vegan or GF callouts found

restaurant.name: Faculty Brewing
restaurant.desc: Faculty Brewing Co. is a 7-barrel craft microbrewery and 30-seat tasting room in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, occupying the former space of the Pedal Bike Depot bicycle shop on the Ontario Street cycling corridor. The brewery operates as an 'open-source' brewery, publishing all recipes publicly and numbering beers by flavour complexity using a university course system. Cyclists can enjoy rotating taps of house-brewed beer and Oddity Kombucha alongside snacks, or fill a growler to take on the road.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple items tagged vegan and/or gluten-free: Pickle (vegan, GF), Chips + Salsa (vegan, GF), Tater Tots (vegan, GF). Non-alcoholic Oddity Kombucha also available on tap

restaurant.name: MeiWei Chinese Cuisine
restaurant.desc: MeiWei Chinese Cuisine is a fully licensed Chinese restaurant on Highway 97 in Kelowna serving a broad menu of traditional Cantonese and Szechuan dishes, group share dinners, and combination plates. The kitchen prides itself on fresh, quality ingredients — their ginger beef uses real red pepper flakes, honey, and freshly ground ginger with no MSG. Online ordering, takeout, delivery, and catering options make it a flexible meal stop for solo cyclists and touring groups alike.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page confirms 'a variety of Gluten-friendly dishes'; menu includes Combo V (vegetable-only combo), Veggie Chow Mein, Veggie Fried Rice, Mushroom Fried Rice, Deep Fried Vegetarian Spring Rolls, and Deep Fried Vegetable

restaurant.name: Back and Forth Bar
restaurant.desc: Back and Forth Bar is a games-and-drinks venue in Vancouver offering six rentable ping-pong tables, two basketball pop-a-shot machines, air hockey, and buck hunter alongside a rotating selection of BC craft beers and cocktails. The space bills itself as a one-of-a-kind atmosphere in Vancouver and welcomes outside food, making it a flexible social stop. Entry is restricted to ages 19 and up with valid ID.

restaurant.name: Phở Pasteur Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Pho Pasteur Restaurant is a Vietnamese noodle house on Hastings Street in Burnaby serving a broad menu of pho, wonton noodle soups, and vermicelli dishes made with traditional flavors and fresh ingredients. The restaurant describes itself as a cozy, modern space offering dine-in alongside online ordering for pickup. Touring cyclists heading along the Hastings corridor will find it a solid stop for a filling hot meal.

restaurant.name: Ukee Scoops
restaurant.desc: Ukee Scoops is an ice cream shop in Ucluelet, BC — 'Ukee' being the affectionate local shorthand for the town. The shop offers outdoor seating, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists passing through this gateway community to Pacific Rim National Park Reserve. It sits at the tip of the Ucluelet Peninsula, where touring routes converge after the scenic Highway 4 approach.

detail.address: 1705 Peninsula Rd, Ucluelet, BC V0R 3A0, Canada

restaurant.name: Formosa Tea Cafe
restaurant.desc: Established in 2013, Formosa Tea Café is a locally owned Taiwanese bubble tea shop in Kelowna serving authentic milk teas, iced teas, cream drinks, fresh fruit smoothies, and specialty coffee — most teas sourced from USDA-certified organic beans and leaves tracing back to Tai-Chung, Taiwan. The café partners with local Kelowna businesses to feature regional products and artworks. Cyclists on Harvey Avenue will find a wide drinks menu including hot, iced, and blended options, plus delivery service for the surrounding area.

restaurant.name: Gojo Little Africa Cafe
restaurant.desc: Gojo Little Africa Cafe specializes in Ethiopian and international cuisine on Vancouver's Commercial Drive. It's a sit-down restaurant with no outdoor seating, so cyclists must secure bikes inside before dining. The restaurant serves traditional Ethiopian fare in a casual neighborhood setting.

restaurant.name: Sky Space Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Sky Space Indian Cuisine is a full-service Indian restaurant in Abbotsford offering a broad menu of traditional and Indo-Chinese dishes made with fresh, seasonally sourced ingredients. The kitchen emphasizes authenticity alongside international standards, with a lunch buffet, daily house-made bread, and a specialized catering program for events. A tiffin service is also available, allowing customers to order prepared meals packed to go.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian' section with numerous dishes (Shahi Paneer, Malai Kofta, Karahi Paneer, Aloo Gobi, Mix Veg. Sabzi, etc.); no GF or vegan claims found

restaurant.name: Mike's Place Pub
restaurant.desc: Mike's Place Pub is a classic multi-level pub inside the historic Hume Hotel in downtown Nelson, drawing a colourful mix of locals, artists, and ski-bums. The pub is well known for its broad lineup of local and BC craft beers and a menu anchored by the 100 Mile Burger, made with hormone-free grass-fed beef from a neighbouring Creston farm. Pool tables, darts, and foosball make it a natural stop for a post-ride pint in one of BC's most celebrated cycling towns.

notes.Takeout: Website menus page lists 'Hume 2 Go — our delivery menu available 9am until 11pm, 7 days a week', indicating takeout/delivery is available from the Hume Hotel kitchen shared with Mike's Place Pub

restaurant.name: The Bombay Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Bombay Restaurant is an established Indian fine-dining restaurant on Lougheed Highway in Port Coquitlam, offering a broad menu spanning tandoori, curries, biryani, and both meat and vegetarian dishes. The kitchen draws on chefs with experience across India, Malaysia, the UK, and North America. A daily lunch buffet and online ordering for takeout make it a practical stop for riders looking for a substantial Indian meal.

detail.address: 2748 Lougheed Hwy, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 3L8

notes.Takeout: Website prominently advertises online takeout orders and delivery: 'Dine-In and Delivery' in the page title; '20% Off Online Takeout Orders over $35'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu has a dedicated 'Vegetarian Specials' section. No mention of vegan or gluten-free

restaurant.name: Olove Greek Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Olove Greek Kitchen is a family-run Greek restaurant on East Hastings Street in Burnaby, serving traditional dishes like moussaka, grilled octopus, housemade spanakopita, and souvlaki wraps stuffed with house-cut chips in the Greek street-food style. The kitchen carries a warm, playful brand voice rooted in home-cooking, and the menu caters to a range of dietary needs including a dedicated vegan option. Takeout is available alongside full dine-in service.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dinner menu includes a VEGAN Goddess Bowl, FALAFEL souva, SPANAKOPITA (organic spinach), BOUREKAKIA (organic wild greens and feta), KOUNOUPITHI (cauliflower), and multiple vegetarian dips and salads. No GF labelling found

restaurant.name: MOD Pizza
restaurant.desc: MOD Pizza is a fast-casual pizza chain where customers build their own individual pizza or salad from over 40 fresh ingredients and eight finishing sauces, cooked in a high-temperature gas-fired oven in minutes. This Country Club Centre location is MOD's second-ever Canadian outpost, opened in 2022 inside a large shopping centre conveniently near a Save-On-Foods grocery store. Touring cyclists will find a quick, filling, fully customizable meal available for carryout.

detail.address: 3200 Island Highway North, Unit 92, Nanaimo, BC V9T 1W1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms vegan cheese, dairy-free dough, and multiple vegetarian toppings; gluten-friendly and cauliflower crust options available (not recommended for those with celiac/gluten sensitivity due to shared prep line)

restaurant.name: Triple O's
restaurant.desc: Triple O's is a BC-based premium quick-service burger chain known for its secret 'Triple O' sauce, hand-scooped milkshakes, and fresh Canadian beef patties. This outlet is tucked inside SFU's AQ Building at the Mackenzie Café on Burnaby Mountain, making it a potential refuelling stop for cyclists who make the climb to the university. It is a counter-service, takeout-only operation with no dine-in seating.

restaurant.name: The Arms Pub
restaurant.desc: A neighbourhood pub and full-service restaurant in Port Coquitlam, The Arms Pub offers a broad daily menu of steak dinners, seafood, flatbreads, and weekend breakfast, alongside an attached liquor store stocked with cold beer, wine, and spirits. Regular entertainment nights — Tuesday trivia, Wednesday music bingo, and Saturday live bands — make it a lively community hub. Touring cyclists passing through on Coast Meridian Road would find a hearty sit-down meal and a convenient stop for cold drinks.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Mushroom-Swiss Bistro Flatbread explicitly labelled 'Vegetarian friendly option' on the menu

restaurant.name: Wild Ambition Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: Wild Ambition is a craft microbrewery and tasting room in Kelowna, operating since December 2018. The tasting room doubles as a retail alcohol outlet, meaning visitors can sample on-site and purchase packaged beer to go. It is an air-conditioned indoor venue — a welcome stop for cyclists navigating the Okanagan in summer heat.

restaurant.name: Pepino's
restaurant.desc: Pepino's Spaghetti House is a neighbourhood Italian restaurant on Commercial Drive in East Vancouver, formerly operating as Nick's Spaghetti House and now reborn as a lively spot for pasta, pizza, and Italian mains. Situated on one of Vancouver's most walkable and cyclist-friendly thoroughfares, it offers both dine-in service and a full takeout menu. A sister wine bar, La Tana, operates next door at 635 Commercial Drive.

notes.Takeout: Dedicated TAKE OUT MENU page on website. Phone-in orders with limited pickup windows

restaurant.name: COBS Bread
restaurant.desc: COBS Bread is a Canadian franchise bakery that bakes all products fresh on-site every day with no frozen or refrigerated products used. The Fort St. John location offers a broad range of breads, loaves, buns, rolls, bagels, scones, croissants, and savoury items including pizzas and buffins. As part of a community-focused brand, any leftover baked goods are donated to local charities at the end of each day.

restaurant.name: Ladner Pho Saigon
restaurant.desc: Ladner Pho Saigon is a Vietnamese restaurant in the Ladner neighbourhood of Delta, BC, specializing in house-simmered bone broth pho and a broad menu of noodle soups, rice dishes, vermicelli bowls, and fresh salad rolls. The kitchen takes care with its broths and sources fresh seasonal toppings, making it a solid hot-meal stop for cyclists passing through Tsawwassen or the South Delta area. Online ordering and delivery are available for those who want to eat on the move.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Vegetarian Spring Rolls, Vegetarian Salad Roll, Vegetarian Noodle Soup, vegetarian broth on request, and Curry (Chicken / Vegetarian) on rice and vermicelli

restaurant.name: De Dutch
restaurant.desc: De Dutch is a long-established Canadian breakfast and brunch chain founded in 1975, specializing in Dutch-style pannekoeken, hearty omelettes, and signature DeBakon. The Tsawwassen location sits near the BC Ferries terminal, making it a natural fueling stop for cyclists arriving from or heading to the Gulf Islands and Vancouver Island. The restaurant is licensed for alcohol and offers both dine-in and delivery service through DoorDash.

detail.address: Unit 504 - 4949 Canoe Pass Way, Tsawwassen, BC V4M 4G9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes vegetarian items such as the Mediterranean omelette (spinach, onion, mushrooms, tomato, feta cheese) and other non-meat options

restaurant.name: Stir Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Stir Coffee House is a community-minded cafe at the entrance to historic Ladner Village in Delta, BC. It occupies the site of a beloved 1963 corner grocery and is now run by the original proprietor's son, carrying on a family tradition of neighbourhood gathering. They roast their own coffee off-site and source all baked goods, sandwiches, and tea from local BC producers.

restaurant.name: Soul Bite Food
restaurant.desc: Soul Bite Food is a Coquitlam-based social enterprise producing award-winning plant-based comfort food inspired by Eastern European and Middle Eastern traditions — think crispy phyllo pastries filled with Balkan mushroom-leek or smoked eggplant and walnut cheese. The company donates 51% of its profits to fighting hunger and food waste globally through the Food Link Society. Products are available for takeout at the Coquitlam facility and distributed through grocery retailers across four provinces.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: All products are vegan

restaurant.name: Bamboo Chopsticks
restaurant.desc: Bamboo Chopsticks is a family-founded Vietnamese restaurant group that has grown from a single Kelowna location in 2011 into three locations across the Kelowna-Westbank area. Every dish is made from the founder's mother's recipes, emphasizing fresh, bold flavors in a welcoming atmosphere. The Westbank location is a full-service sit-down restaurant with online table booking and takeout options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Express menu states 'Items marked gluten friendly are made with no gluten-containing ingredients' and lists Crispy Tofu as a protein option in multiple dishes, indicating vegetarian and GF choices

restaurant.name: Tasty Planet Indian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: An Indian restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver. Unable to verify current amenities or services due to website unavailability.

restaurant.name: Pizza 2001
restaurant.desc: Pizza 2001 is a downtown Vancouver institution that has been hand-crafting stone-baked pizzas for over 25 years, using dough made fresh daily and premium ingredients sliced in-store. It's a small corner spot well-known for its slice counter, making it a quick and filling stop for cyclists passing through the heart of the city. The business uses traditional deck ovens and has built a loyal following for consistent, generously topped pizzas.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Customer review explicitly ordered 'a large veggie' pizza; website highlights fresh vegetables as standard toppings. No mention of vegan or gluten-free options

restaurant.name: Sushi Hama
restaurant.desc: Sushi Hama is a Japanese fusion restaurant in downtown Qualicum Beach, where Chef Peter offers a menu blending traditional sushi with creatively inspired items. The casual, family-friendly atmosphere makes it a welcoming stop for cyclists exploring the Qualicum Beach area. Takeout is available via a regularly updated menu.

restaurant.name: Arigato Sushi
restaurant.desc: Arigato Sushi is a fusion Japanese restaurant in Kamloops' Aberdeen neighbourhood, known for creative sushi rolls and consistently praised service. The casual, booth-filled dining room has earned a loyal local following for both lunch and dinner visits. Takeout and catering are available, making it a flexible stop for cyclists passing through Kamloops.

restaurant.name: Unicorn Sparkles
restaurant.desc: Unicorn Sparkles is a fine dining restaurant in downtown Victoria from the team behind acclaimed local spots hanks, nowhere, ate, and somewhere. It represents the group's attempt to bring together everything they've learned across those award-winning projects into a single new venture. Touring cyclists passing through the heart of Victoria will find it at unit G4 on Douglas Street, with reservations recommended.

detail.address: Unit G4, 1001 Douglas Street, Victoria, BC V8W2C5

restaurant.name: Shoom Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Shoom Restaurant is a Hong Kong-style Chinese eatery on Fraser Street in south Vancouver, seating up to 90 guests and serving a full menu of dishes including salted egg yolk prawns, Peking duck, house special chicken, and a broad range of Hong Kong-style beverages. The restaurant accepts table reservations and offers online ordering via Instagram, making it a substantial sit-down meal option for cyclists passing through the Fraser Street corridor.

restaurant.name: Prophecy Cocktail Bar
restaurant.desc: Prophecy Cocktail Bar is an upscale cocktail lounge located within the Rosewood Hotel Georgia in downtown Vancouver, presenting an elaborate story-driven menu where each cocktail is inspired by writers, poets, musicians, and artists from around the world. The bar offers a curated selection of inventive house cocktails, classic serves, small plates, and a Cocktail Hour program. It positions itself as a sophisticated, design-forward destination with private event capabilities.

detail.address: 801 W Georgia St, Vancouver, BC V6C 1P7

restaurant.name: Cove Creek Gallery and Cappuccino Bar
restaurant.desc: Cove Creek Gallery is a family-run boutique art gallery in the scenic Deep Cove neighbourhood of North Vancouver, open since 2010, offering contemporary paintings, sculptures, jewellery, and fabric pieces. Visitors can browse artwork while enjoying a cappuccino in a relaxed, friendly atmosphere. The gallery also makes its space available for self-managed pop-up shows, giving it a lively, community-oriented character.

detail.address: 4344 Gallant Avenue, North Vancouver, BC V7G 1K8

restaurant.name: Ironworks Cafe & Crepperie
restaurant.desc: Ironworks Café & Crêperie is a locally-owned café established in 2018 by Dina Stuehler, specializing in Belgian-style crepes made from scratch alongside freshly roasted Italian coffee. The Duncan location on Station Street is part of a small Vancouver Island chain with a warm, community-focused atmosphere and a menu that ranges from savoury lunch crepes to indulgent sweet options. It is a well-regarded stop in downtown Duncan, drawing regulars and visitors alike with its inclusive menu and welcoming ethos.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Gluten-Free & Vegan options'; menu lists Gluten-Free Buckwheat Batter and Whole Wheat Vegan Batter; most sweet crepes are marked as vegan-substitutable and gluten-free adaptable. Note: kitchen cannot safely accommodate celiac disease due to cross-contamination risk

restaurant.name: Bru-Go's Coffee
restaurant.desc: Bru-Go's Coffee is a cafe in Mill Bay serving coffee and refreshments. Located on Mill Bay Road, it provides a convenient stop for locals and travelers passing through the area.

detail.address: 2720 Mill Bay Road, Mill Bay, V0R 2P1

restaurant.name: Rimrock Cafe
restaurant.desc: Rimrock Café is a well-established Whistler Creekside restaurant that has been serving guests since 1986, celebrating its 40th anniversary in 2026. The kitchen emphasizes sustainability and seasonality, with a menu crafted around local ingredients. It offers full sit-down dining, group bookings, and private event options, positioning it as a destination-worthy meal stop on a Whistler cycling tour.

restaurant.name: Pho Thai Ha
restaurant.desc: Pho Thai Ha is a Vietnamese restaurant located on East 49th Avenue in East Vancouver. As a dining establishment, it provides a rest and refueling opportunity for touring cyclists in the area, though specific cyclist amenities have not been verified.

restaurant.name: Brooklyn Dumpling Shop
restaurant.desc: Brooklyn Dumpling Shop is a New York-founded fast casual Asian fusion chain that brings creative, globally-inspired dumplings to Vancouver's busy Robson Street corridor. The menu leans into bold, unexpected combinations — Korean BBQ Ribeye, Bacon Cheeseburger, Pork Soup dumplings — built around the idea that everything is better stuffed in a dumpling. It's a quick, filling stop for cyclists passing through the downtown core.

restaurant.name: Perfecto Cafe
restaurant.desc: Perfecto Cafe is an artisan bakery-cafe chain with a North Vancouver outpost in the Shipyards district, where bakers work from 5am crafting croissants, cakes, gelato, and sandwiches entirely from scratch using a custom coffee blend developed exclusively with Agro Roasters. One of four Metro Vancouver locations, the Shipyards cafe sits at the waterfront Esplanade and draws on the same made-in-house philosophy as its sister cafes. Touring cyclists will find a full food stop with pastries, sandwiches, and specialty coffee in a welcoming community-oriented space.

restaurant.name: Red Swan Pizza
restaurant.desc: Red Swan Pizza is a pizza franchise with a location on Edmonds Street in Burnaby, situated beside New Vista Care Home. Previously operating as Villages Pizza, this spot offers delivery and takeout with online ordering. It's a straightforward pizza stop for cyclists passing through the Edmonds corridor.

restaurant.name: Viet Sub
restaurant.desc: Viet Sub is a Vietnamese fast-food spot on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver, known for its freshly made banh mi sandwiches on crusty baguettes, fragrant pho, and crispy spring rolls. The restaurant has both indoor and outdoor seating and a reputation for friendly service and consistent quality in a bright, high-energy setting. It is a practical and affordable pit stop for cyclists moving through the downtown core.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists 'B6.Veggie Sub (Deep-fried tofu)' and salad rolls, confirming vegetarian options

restaurant.name: Kobo  Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Kobo Ice Cream is a small-batch artisan scoop shop on Vancouver's Main Street, crafting flavours from locally sourced natural ingredients with roots in family tradition. The rotating menu spans creative offerings like London Fog, Tahini & Roasted Walnut, and Caramelized Banana, alongside dairy-free and vegan choices. The shop is sustainability-focused, using compostable or recyclable packaging wherever possible.

notes.Takeout: Scoop shop format — ice cream is served to-go as the primary service mode; website presents the product as individual scoops with no mention of dine-in seating
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQs state 'Yes! We offer rotating dairy-free and vegan flavours made with high-quality plant-based ingredients.' Flavours page marks vegan items with '(V)' (e.g. Dark Chocolate Sorbet, Mandarin Sorbet)

restaurant.name: Ho Fung
restaurant.desc: Ho Fung is a Chinese restaurant at 724 Sixth Street offering dine-in and takeout. Based on OSM data last verified in early 2023, it serves Chinese cuisine with no outdoor seating. Touring cyclists would find it a straightforward meal stop, though no cycling-specific amenities have been confirmed.

restaurant.name: Tapley's Neighbourhood Pub
restaurant.desc: Tapley's Pub, open since 1981, is Whistler's first pub and a cornerstone of the village's social fabric, operating as part of the Gibbons Hospitality Group. Known as the locals' living room, it is a lively sports bar serving pub food, local craft beers, and hosting weekly community events like trivia and bingo nights. The dog-friendly patio adds to its welcoming character, making it a natural gathering spot in the heart of Whistler Village.

detail.address: 4119 Golfers Approach, Whistler, BC V0N 1B4, Canada

restaurant.name: Murchie's Cafe
restaurant.desc: Murchie's is Canada's oldest tea company, founded in Victoria in 1894, and its Downtown Government Street flagship pairs a full retail store with a sit-down café serving the company's own in-house blended teas and freshly roasted 100% Arabica coffees. The heritage brand has operated continuously for over 130 years and is a well-known landmark on one of Victoria's busiest pedestrian and cycling corridors. The combined retail-and-café format means cyclists can grab a drink, browse loose-leaf teas, and pick up supplies in a single stop.

restaurant.name: Tractor
restaurant.desc: Tractor Foods is a scratch-made fast-casual chain with eight locations across Vancouver and Victoria, known for its plant-forward bowls, soups, sandwiches, and fresh breakfast options. The Pender Street location (Unit 102B) serves the downtown core and offers both walk-in and pre-order pickup. A touring cyclist heading through downtown Vancouver will find a filling, health-oriented meal with quick turnaround.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website catering page describes menu as 'Plant-Forward'; main menu features power greens, market side veggies, and salads alongside grilled proteins. No explicit GF claim found

restaurant.name: Pioneer's Pub
restaurant.desc: Pioneer's Pub has been a Richmond community institution since 1977, offering pub food, cold beer, and a warm neighbourhood atmosphere. The venue features 10 large screens with DAZN and FUBO for sports viewing, and also operates an adjacent Pioneer Liquor Store. restaurant.name: Bendick's Ice Cream Factory

restaurant.name: Sushi Asakusa

restaurant.name: Big Way Hot Pot

Diners choose their broth — including a vegan tomato option — and cook premium meats, seafood, and vegetables tableside.

restaurant.name: Yugo

restaurant.name: Mega Sushi

Part of the Mega Group's 14-location BC chain, this independently run outpost is known for using fresh local ingredients and a distinctive roasted-salt technique that enhances the flavour of its fish. Cyclists exploring the Steveston waterfront will find it a short ride from the pier, with a full dine-in menu as well as Korean dishes and desserts.

restaurant.name: Chaibaba

It is a calm, intentional stop with sidewalk seating — a nice contrast to the typical cyclist pit stop.

restaurant.name: Blaze Cafe

The business also offers a mobile coffee catering service for events around the city.

restaurant.name: McDonald's

restaurant.name: Dragon Garden

restaurant.name: The Bent Mast

Located less than a 10-minute walk from the Inner Harbour, it serves a wide selection of local craft beers alongside its kitchen menu, with a spacious patio and upstairs event rooms. Touring cyclists finishing a ride along the waterfront will find a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere right in the heart of the neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Jake's at the Lake
restaurant.desc: Jake's at the Lake is a year-round waterfront restaurant on the shores of Lake Cowichan, housed in a classic woody cabin with high ceilings and large windows framing open lake views. Part of the Craig Street Hospitality Group, it serves bold West Coast cuisine with daily seasonal features crafted by an in-house culinary team. The waterfront patio explicitly welcomes boaters, hikers, and families, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring the Cowichan Valley.

restaurant.name: One20 Public House

restaurant.name: Wood Fire Bakery

restaurant.name: Longwood Tasting Room

A seasonal uncovered picnic patio is pet- and family-friendly, with no onsite kitchen.

restaurant.name: Small Gods Brewpub

The brewery draws deep inspiration from literature, hosting monthly author readings, book swaps, and a book club, making it a notably community-rooted gathering space. Cyclists stopping in will find a rotating lineup of house-brewed ales and lagers alongside a counter-service deli of house-baked sandwiches and snacks, with a dog-friendly patio.

restaurant.name: Rancher's Restaurant

restaurant.name: Gasthaus on the Lake

Founded by two Germans who came to retire and instead built a community landmark, the restaurant expanded to include a pub and lakeside patio in 2000 and has been under its current ownership since 2018. The lakeside setting and hearty menu make it a natural stop for cyclists riding the Okanagan Valley routes.

restaurant.name: Rodney's Oyster House

It draws both locals and visitors seeking a lively West Coast dining experience in a vibrant neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Seymour's Pub

restaurant.name: Agra Sweets & Restaurant

restaurant.name: White Heather Tea Room

Cyclists can settle in for an elaborate multi-course experience featuring handmade scones, seasonal finger sandwiches, and rotating desserts, or pick up takeout teaboxes and patisserie items to go. Seasonal themed menus — Valentine's, Easter, Mother's Day — make it a notable destination stop on longer tours of the Saanich Peninsula.

restaurant.name: Balkan Bakery

The shop prides itself on freshly made products using high-quality ingredients and traditional techniques rooted in Balkan home-baking culture. It sits in a residential-commercial neighbourhood with street-level access and car parking front and rear, making it a practical savory-snack stop for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Winter Bear Dessert & Teahouse
restaurant.desc: Winter Bear Dessert & Teahouse is a dessert-focused cafe and teahouse on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, steps from the Stanley Park Seawall cycling route. restaurant.name: Blenz Coffee

It is a locally owned and operated franchise in a busy mall setting on Kelowna's main commercial strip.

restaurant.name: The Vic

A sunny street-corner patio makes it a natural gathering spot in the middle of downtown Kamloops.

restaurant.name: Cactus Club Cafe

restaurant.name: Murmur

The space sits quietly on East Broadway, positioned as a neighbourhood destination with a personal, community-minded feel.

restaurant.name: Uma Sushi

restaurant.name: Big Daddy's Fish Fry
restaurant.desc: Big Daddy's Fish Fry has been a Tofino institution since 2001, built on a commitment to locally sourced, fresh Pacific seafood. The casual counter-style spot offers scratch-made chowder, seafood burgers featuring locally caught halibut and lingcod, fish fry classics, and poutine. For a touring cyclist arriving hungry on the Pacific coast, it represents a hearty, community-rooted meal a short distance from the waterfront.

restaurant.name: Blenz Coffee

restaurant.name: Main Street Brewing
