The taproom doubles as a retail store where cyclists can pick up canned beer to take on the road, and an in-house kitchen serves food most days. The brewery's Main Street Premium Pilsner earned a gold medal at the 2024 Canadian Brewing Awards, and an ongoing 'Tunnerman's True Cask Ale' program offers traditional cask-conditioned pours.

restaurant.name: Puerto Vallarta Amigos
restaurant.desc: Puerto Vallarta Amigos is a Mexican food operation whose flagship location occupies a colourful floating houseboat in the vibrant community of Fisherman's Wharf in Victoria. The business also runs kiosks at Uptown Mall and the Royal BC Museum courtyard, and operates mobile food trucks for catering. Cyclists exploring the Victoria waterfront can stop here for wraps, burgers, and Mexican street food right at the harbour's edge.

restaurant.name: Chuihong
restaurant.desc: Chuihong is a Korean-Chinese fusion restaurant in Surrey's Fraser Heights neighbourhood, specializing in classics like Jjajangmyeon (black bean noodles), TangSooYuk (sweet-and-sour fried pork), and Jjambong (spicy seafood noodle soup). It has built a loyal local following and manages demand through a virtual waitlist system. The restaurant also offers meal kits for customers who want to recreate the dishes at home.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Customer testimonial on website states: 'From vegetarians to meat lovers, this place covers it all.'

restaurant.name: Scott's On The Go Eats
restaurant.desc: Scott's Inn & Suites is a long-established downtown Kamloops hotel that has operated for over 60 years, offering studio to three-bedroom suites with kitchenettes and amenities including a rooftop sundeck with BBQ and free parking. On-site food is now provided by 'Scott's On The Go Eats,' a grab-and-go counter offering fresh snacks, coffee, cold beverages, and ice cream after the original restaurant closed due to fire. Its central location and ample parking make it a practical overnight stop for touring cyclists passing through Kamloops.

restaurant.name: Bean Around The World
restaurant.desc: Bean Around The World is a Vancouver-area specialty coffee roaster with over 30 years in the business, roasting small batches daily and sourcing beans from around the world. The brand operates multiple retail café locations across the region alongside a robust online subscription service. A touring cyclist stopping in can expect freshly roasted espresso and drip coffee in a well-established local coffee culture setting.

restaurant.name: Bean scene
restaurant.desc: Bean Scene is a pioneer of third wave coffee in the Okanagan, roasting small-batch, hand-crafted espresso since 2002 using a vintage 12 kg Probat roaster retrofitted with an emission control system. The company operates multiple locations across Kelowna and runs its own wholesale bakery, producing fresh scratch-baked goods daily with local ingredients. Touring cyclists will find a serious, independent coffee culture with baristas trained to international competition standards.

restaurant.name: The Burrow
restaurant.desc: The Burrow is a Mexican-inspired vegetarian and vegan restaurant that has anchored Commercial Drive in East Vancouver since 2009. It is known for creative weekend brunch served on morning-baked cornbread, handmade tacos on locally sourced corn tortillas, and cult-favourite baked burritos and nachos — all made entirely without meat. The casual, community-driven atmosphere and entirely plant-based menu make it a compelling stop for cyclists riding one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website describes 'Mexican-inspired Vegetarian & Vegan Fare'. Menu confirms vegan wings, vegan cheese, vegan sour cream options throughout. No gluten-free claim found

restaurant.name: Lynx Cafe
restaurant.desc: Lynx Cafe is a food truck located on the Sea to Sky Highway in Pemberton, offering a convenient stop for cyclists passing through this mountain community. Operating in the fast food tradition with fish and chips and coffee, it provides quick service for travelers. The truck represents a casual, mobile dining option along the highway corridor.

detail.address: 7374 Sea to Sky Highway, Pemberton, V0N 2L1

restaurant.name: Archrcoffee
restaurant.desc: Archr Coffee + Bakery is a community-focused specialty cafe in Langley, BC, offering espresso drinks and a rotating menu of baked goods, sandwiches, and burritos sourced from local BC producers including Elysian Coffee Roasters and To Live For Bakery. Located in unit A150 behind the building at 20161 86 Ave, the shop is tucked away from the street but serves as a neighbourhood gathering spot with catering available for larger events.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists 'Vegan Breakfast Sandwich' explicitly

restaurant.name: White Spot
restaurant.desc: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, founded in 1928 and still serving its legendary burgers made from 100% fresh Canadian beef alongside a broad family menu at this Kerrisdale location. The West Boulevard spot sits in a walkable, bikeable neighbourhood and offers a patio as well as full dine-in service. Touring cyclists will find familiar comfort food, takeout and delivery options, and a well-known brand with dozens of locations across BC for route planning.

restaurant.name: Rumi Rose Tea
restaurant.desc: Rumi Rose Tea is a Sufi-inspired tea and coffee café at 3660 East Hastings, offering over 49 custom-blended healing teas alongside signature espresso and Turkish coffee, and voted Vancouver's Best Sufi Coffee & Espresso. The 6,000-square-foot space doubles as a Middle Eastern market stocking halal meats, Turkish and Iranian sweets, spices, and over 400 grocery items — making it an unusually well-stocked stop for a touring cyclist needing more than just a drink. Local pickup and delivery are available, and the shop operates six days a week.

restaurant.name: Got Pho?
restaurant.desc: Got Pho? is a Vietnamese restaurant located on Nanaimo Street in Vancouver. The name and OSM cuisine tag indicate a focus on pho and other Vietnamese dishes. It provides a casual dining option for tourists and local cyclists.

restaurant.name: Kakai Sushi
restaurant.desc: Kakai Sushi is a Japanese restaurant with two Greater Vancouver locations, offering dine-in and online ordering at its East Broadway location near Commercial Drive. The restaurant focuses on authentic Japanese cuisine with contemporary atmosphere and table reservations available. Cyclists on the Broadway corridor will find it a convenient stop for a sit-down meal or takeout.

restaurant.name: Kootenay Tamil Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Kootenay Tamil Kitchen is a South Indian restaurant on Nelson's main commercial street, run by Tamil immigrants who cook authentic, family-heirloom recipes — heart-healthy dishes free of butter and cream. The operation has expanded to include an Indian grocery store across the street at 639 Baker St and a neighbourhood cafe (KTK Rosemont) at 1516 Crease Avenue. Chef Ciraj's background includes eight years on US cruise lines feeding thousands of guests, making this a genuinely accomplished kitchen in a small-town setting.

restaurant.name: Donair Dude
restaurant.desc: Donair Dude is a Mediterranean-style fast food chain that opened its first location on Davie Street during the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics and has since grown into a multi-location franchise. The restaurant serves freshly prepared donairs, pita wraps, and platters made with premium BC-sourced meats slowly roasted in-house, alongside a dedicated vegan menu featuring falafel. The Davie Street location sits in Vancouver's walkable West End and offers both indoor and outdoor seating.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes a dedicated 'VEGAN' category; falafel wrap, falafel platter, and falafel plate are listed

restaurant.name: Drip Coffee Social
restaurant.desc: Drip Coffee Social is a community-minded independent café established in 2018, operating two Nanaimo locations with a stated focus on inclusivity and local gathering. The Dufferin Crescent location offers a full espresso and tea menu alongside food bowls, sandwiches, baked goods, and even beer, wine, and seasonal cocktails. Mobile ordering is available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists moving through the south Nanaimo corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Roasted Veggie sandwich, Roast Chickpea Kale Salad, Avocado Toast, and explicitly labelled Gluten Free Brownie and Gluten Free Shortbread

restaurant.name: The Green
restaurant.desc: The Green is a modern Korean-fusion breakfast and brunch restaurant on East Hastings Street in Vancouver, specializing in vibrant, plant-forward dishes like bibim tofu bowls, smoked duck with brown rice, and signature multigrain cloud-foam beverages. The cafe operates under a 'Eat Green, Stay Green' philosophy and also offers catering with individual lunch boxes and buffet-style options. Touring cyclists heading through Vancouver's east side will find a health-conscious, vegan-friendly stop with a distinctive Korean-Canadian menu.

detail.address: 2261 E Hastings St, Vancouver, BC V5L 1V3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Instagram content shows oat milk drinks, plant-based protein blends, kale/spinach/mango smoothies, and a BibimTofuTable dish, consistent with strong vegan offerings

restaurant.name: The Chopped Leaf
restaurant.desc: The Chopped Leaf is a Canadian chain founded in 2009, specializing in fresh salads, wraps, bowls, and sandwiches with a focus on making greens feel like comfort food. This location is on Willowbrook Drive in Langley, convenient for cyclists passing through the Township. The menu emphasizes customizable, produce-forward meals that could appeal to riders looking for a lighter, nutritious stop.

restaurant.name: Grand Noodle Emporium
restaurant.desc: Grand Noodle Emporium is an AMS-owned and operated pan-Asian restaurant located in the Lower Level of the Nest at UBC Vancouver, seating up to 60 guests. It serves made-to-order comfort dishes spanning Chinese, Thai, and Southeast Asian cuisines — think Pad Thai and Thai curry alongside classic Chinese take-out from a concourse window. It also offers catering and online ordering for pickup, making it a practical stop for cyclists passing through the UBC campus.

detail.address: Lower Level of the Nest, 6133 University Blvd, UBC Campus, Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1

restaurant.name: Royal Garden Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Royal Garden Seafood Restaurant occupies a prominent spot inside the Empire Centre shopping mall on Number 3 Road in Richmond, serving authentic Chinese cuisine including traditional Dim Sum, lunch, and dinner. The kitchen team is selected for skill in sourcing fresh, seasonal ingredients, and the restaurant is well regarded in the Lower Mainland for its quality. Beyond everyday dining, the venue hosts banquet events, wine tastings, and caviar evenings, making it a notable stop for a post-ride feast.

restaurant.name: Pizza Craft
restaurant.desc: Pizza Craft is a fast-food pizza restaurant in Abbotsford offering takeout and delivery. The brand's website, which describes a Prince George location, suggests a menu blending Italian-style pizzas with South Asian street food, burgers, and specialty drinks — though whether this Abbotsford location shares the same concept and menu cannot be confirmed from available sources.

detail.address: 30485 Cardinal Ave, Unit 120, Abbotsford, BC V2T 0E5

restaurant.name: Zaaki Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Zaaki Cuisine is a fast-food doner and donair restaurant in New Westminster offering quick, casual meals. The menu includes vegetarian options, providing choices for cyclists with diverse dietary needs.

restaurant.name: Pizza Garden
restaurant.desc: Pizza Garden is a BC-based Neapolitan pizza chain operated by Neapolitan Pizza Ltd. with over 25 years in the industry, offering authentic wood-fired pizzas with charred crusts, sun-ripened tomatoes, and fresh mozzarella at more than a dozen locations across British Columbia. The chain supports both pickup and delivery and operates a rewards app, making it a straightforward resupply stop on longer cycling routes through urban and university-adjacent corridors.

detail.address: 3033 Main St, Vancouver, BC V5T 3G6, Canada

restaurant.name: Truffle Pigs Bistro
restaurant.desc: Truffle Pigs Bistro & Lodge is a long-running mountain restaurant and lodge in Field, BC, situated in the heart of Yoho National Park and established in 2000. It evolved from a general store and café into a full bistro with twelve lodge rooms, known for passionate, locally inspired cooking and warm Rocky Mountain hospitality. The bistro offers an all-day menu with appetizers, burgers, and mains, and will prepare packed lunch kits for hikers and adventurers on request.

notes.Packed lunches: FAQ states: 'Do you prepare lunch kits for hikers? Absolutely, and you don't even have to be a hiker. We would be happy to get a lunch ready for you so you don't run out of steam on your daily adventure.'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states: 'We have select vegetarian and gluten free options on our menus.' Bistro menu also lists a vegan beet burger with 'vegan dill aioli'

restaurant.name: Caffe Motivo
restaurant.desc: Caffe Motivo is an independent café in the heart of downtown Kamloops, serving specialty coffee sourced from JJ Bean alongside fresh-baked goods and light breakfasts and lunches made in-house daily. It occupies a street-level location on Victoria Street, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the city centre. The café also offers a catering service, suggesting a kitchen capable of producing larger food orders.

detail.address: 229 Victoria Street, Kamloops, BC, V2C 2A1, Canada

restaurant.name: Swiss Bakery Catering & Wholesale
restaurant.desc: Swiss Bakery is a Vancouver institution established in 1993, now operating as Luminous Foods Inc. while retaining the Swiss Bakery name at its two locations. The UBC outlet on University Boulevard offers artisan breads, gourmet pretzels, frissants, hand-made pastries, and a seasonal lunch menu — a worthwhile stop for cyclists riding through the UBC campus area. Wholesale and catering services are also available from this location.

restaurant.name: Tashkent
restaurant.desc: Tashkent is a family-owned Uzbek halal restaurant occupying a stall in the International Village Mall Food Court in downtown Vancouver, bringing generations-old Central Asian recipes to the city. The business grew from a delivery-only service launched in 2023 into a full dine-in establishment, serving dishes such as Uzbek Plov cooked in a traditional cauldron, hand-pulled Lagman noodles, and steamed Manti dumplings. It fills a distinctive culinary niche as one of very few authentic Uzbek restaurants in Vancouver, with a warm atmosphere designed to reflect Central Asian dining traditions.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels items: 'V' (Vegetarian Lagman), 'VG' (Vegan Ganfan with tofu/eggplant), and 'GF' (Pilaf/Plov, Ganfan, Borscht)

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: A Subway franchise located in the Clover Square Village shopping centre in Surrey, offering the chain's full lineup of Footlong and 6-inch sandwiches, wraps, and salads. The location supports in-restaurant dining, curbside pickup, and delivery, and serves breakfast. Like all Subway franchises, it is independently owned and operated.

restaurant.name: Flower & Horse In Spring
restaurant.desc: Flower & Horse in Spring is a Yunnan-style rice noodle restaurant on Vancouver's Robson Street, specializing in authentic Chinese dishes including Crossing the Bridge rice noodles, beef rice noodles, and sweet rice balls. The restaurant is part of a small chain with a second location in Markham, Ontario. It offers indoor seating in a no-smoking environment on one of Vancouver's busiest pedestrian corridors.

restaurant.name: The MAQ Pub
restaurant.desc: The MAQ Pub occupies the lower level of the historic Maquinna Hotel in Tofino and has been a local gathering spot since the 1950s, originally frequented by fishermen and loggers and nicknamed 'The Dirty MAQ'. Today it draws surfers, tourists, and hospitality workers with a rotating lineup of live music, karaoke nights, DJs, and dancing. It is part of the MAQ Hotel complex, which also includes The MAQ Cafe and The Bear Bierhaus.

detail.address: 120 First St, Tofino, British Columbia, V0R 2Z0

restaurant.name: 93 Coffee
restaurant.desc: 93 Coffee is a cozy Japanese-style cafe tucked inside the Denman Place Mall in Vancouver's West End neighbourhood. It offers breakfast, lunch, dinner, and a dedicated drink menu, positioning itself as an all-day stop. Its central West End location makes it a convenient refuelling point for cyclists exploring the nearby Seawall.

restaurant.name: JAK's Beer Wine Spirits
restaurant.desc: Formerly known as Kitsilano Wine Cellar, this location is now part of the JAK's Beer Wine Spirits chain — a neighbourhood liquor retailer with 10 stores across Greater Vancouver, offering wine, craft beer, and premium spirits. It sits on West 4th Avenue in Kitsilano, a well-travelled cycling corridor, and the brand places emphasis on knowledgeable, personalized staff service rather than a self-serve retail experience. Online ordering with home delivery is available through the chain's website.

restaurant.name: Jo's Italian Deli
restaurant.desc: Jo's Italian Deli is a family-owned Italian deli and restaurant on Main Street serving sliced-to-order sandwiches on homemade bread, fresh pasta with scratch-made sauces, espresso drinks, and imported Italian grocery items. The brand originated in Chilliwack in 2018 and has since grown to several Lower Mainland locations, each aiming to be a casual neighbourhood staple. The Main St location is a newer addition, opened in 2026, with online ordering and delivery available.

restaurant.name: Packing House Pub
restaurant.desc: The Packing House Pub has been a Kelowna institution since 1977, tucked off Highway 97 in an industrial area on Finns Road and self-described as 'one of Kelowna's oldest and most notorious establishments.' It leans into its working-class roots with large portions of homemade comfort food, ice-cold beer, and staff who remember regulars by name. A unique draw is the attached bowling alley, making it an unexpectedly fun stop for cyclists wanting more than just a meal.

restaurant.name: Spice Hut Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Spice Hut Indian Cuisine is an East Indian restaurant located in Tofino, BC, one of Vancouver Island's premier surf and cycling destinations on the remote west coast. Situated on Main Street, it offers a warm meal option for cyclists completing the challenging ride into Tofino along Highway 4. The restaurant operates an online ordering platform under the brand Spice Hut Canada.

restaurant.name: Tacos Del Norte
restaurant.desc: Tacos Del Norte is an authentic Mexican taqueria located just off Main Street in downtown Penticton, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Okanagan. The shop is known for homemade corn tortillas, slow-roasted meats like carnitas and pollo, and salsas made fresh daily from scratch. Outdoor seating and a casual, festive atmosphere make it a local favourite for both visitors and residents.

restaurant.name: Claudio's Ristorante
restaurant.desc: Claudio's Ristorante is an Italian restaurant in Burnaby's Solo District development, serving housemade fresh pasta, wood-fired-style pizzas, and a full bar with happy hour offerings. The restaurant has both indoor and outdoor seating and caters to private events from intimate dinners to full restaurant buyouts. Cyclists passing through the Brentwood area will find a range of vegetarian-friendly dishes and online ordering for takeout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu marks multiple items (V) for vegetarian across categories: Focaccia, Broccolini, Giardino salad, Chitarra Pomodoro pasta, Margherita pizza, Pera e Gorgonzola pizza

restaurant.name: D-Plus Pizza
restaurant.desc: A pizza fast_food restaurant located in Richmond. The business does not offer drive-through service.

restaurant.name: Guildford Station Pub
restaurant.desc: Guildford Station Pub is a neighbourhood pub and sports bar in Surrey's Guildford area, also operating an attached liquor store. Described on its own website as a 'hidden gem' and cozy social hub, it offers a broad menu of pub classics, wings, tacos, and cocktails alongside a well-stocked tap list of BC craft and mainstream beers. Minors are not permitted inside the pub.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu labels at least one item as 'Vegetarian' (appears as a dietary label within the appetizers section, associated with Deep Fried Pickles)

restaurant.name: Good Co. Granville
restaurant.desc: Good Co. Granville is a lively bar and entertainment venue on Granville Street in downtown Vancouver, part of a four-location chain offering food, drinks, games, and sports viewing. The venue runs a packed calendar of regular events including salsa and bachata dance nights, music video bingo, trivia competitions, and live TV watch parties on a large LED screen. It is non-smoking throughout, wheelchair accessible, and accepts both credit and debit cards.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Sofritas Tacos (vegan), Veggie Dumplings, Veggie Burger (mushroom-rice patty with avocado mayo), Glory Bowl (fried tofu, quinoa, mixed greens), and a gluten-free vegan bun substitute option

restaurant.name: Kintaro Ramen
restaurant.desc: Kintaro Ramen is a Japanese ramen restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, a short ride from the Stanley Park Seawall cycling network. The restaurant is known for its house-crafted broths, including a signature miso blend drawn from four regional Japanese soybean pastes and twelve spices. Online ordering is available for both pickup and delivery.

restaurant.name: Mamalee
restaurant.desc: Mamalee is a beloved Malaysian restaurant on West Broadway founded by Betty Lee, a Kuala Lumpur-born cook who overcame serious hardship — including a partially paralyzing car accident — to bring authentic Malaysian flavours to Vancouver in the early 1990s. The menu centres on Hainanese chicken rice, laksa noodle soup, roti canai, and curry beef brisket, all prepared with meticulous technique. The Broadway location is the original main store; a second outpost in Chinatown has since extended the family's reach across the city.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Take-out is available after 6:00 pm' and offers online ordering/delivery

restaurant.name: Thai Ni Yom
restaurant.desc: Thai Ni Yom is an authentic Thai restaurant tucked into a unit on West 4th Avenue in Kitsilano, one of Vancouver's most cycle-friendly neighbourhoods. It operates as a full sit-down restaurant with table service and online ordering, making it a convenient meal stop for cyclists on the nearby Arbutus Greenway or the 4th Avenue corridor. The restaurant has been established long enough to earn a consistent OSM presence and maintains an active website with reservations and gift cards.

detail.address: 2953 West 4th Avenue Unit 2, Vancouver, BC V6K 1R3

restaurant.name: Kurumba
restaurant.desc: Kurumba is a casual Asian fusion restaurant drawing on the cuisines of China, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Singapore, and Malaysia, with signature dishes like Beef Kotthu Roti, Sambal Prawns, and the Kurumba Platter. The dining room is described as intimate and low-key, and the restaurant offers efficient takeout service alongside dine-in. It presents a flavorful and affordable option for cyclists passing through Port Moody.

detail.address: 107-3003 St John's Street, Port Moody, British Columbia V3H 2R6

notes.Takeout: Website front page invites customers to 'place your order for take-out' and the About Us page describes 'efficient take-out service that is second to none.'

restaurant.name: QUIK BITE
restaurant.desc: QUIK BITE is a restaurant located on Rumble Street in the Burnaby area of Metro Vancouver. The business is listed in OpenStreetMap with a recent verification date, suggesting it is an active local eatery. Cyclists passing through south Burnaby may find it a convenient stop, though specific cuisine details are not available from public records.

restaurant.name: The Drive Canteen
restaurant.desc: The Drive Canteen is a community-oriented snack bar and non-alcoholic bottle shop on Vancouver's bustling Commercial Drive, established in 2021. It offers locally made snacks, a curated selection of sophisticated non-alcoholic beverages, eclectic goods, and even a dedicated pet section. Situated on one of Vancouver's most bike-friendly corridors, it makes a distinctive pit stop for cyclists seeking a refreshment without alcohol.

restaurant.name: Cactus Club Cafe
restaurant.desc: Cactus Club Cafe Coal Harbour is an upscale-casual chain restaurant perched at 1085 Canada Place with panoramic views of the Burrard Inlet and the North Shore mountains. The chef-driven international menu spans sushi, steaks, pastas, and handhelds alongside a full lounge and patio — making it a prominent stop along the Coal Harbour waterfront seawall. Private dining and large-group event spaces are available, and the venue hosts a daily happy hour.

restaurant.name: Village Pub
restaurant.desc: Village Pub is a pub and restaurant in Vancouver offering food service in a public dining environment. Limited information about specific amenities is available due to website fetch failure.

restaurant.name: 7Days Coffee
restaurant.desc: 7Days Coffee is a café on Beatty Street in downtown Vancouver, steps from BC Place and Rogers Arena in a high-traffic area for commuters and event-goers. The café offers both indoor and outdoor seating, accepts card payments, and is wheelchair accessible. Its name suggests a seven-days-a-week operation, making it a consistent stop for cyclists passing through the downtown core.

restaurant.name: barBURRITO
restaurant.desc: barBURRITO is part of Canada's largest burrito chain, operating since 2005, with over 385 locations nationwide. The Sidney location serves fully customizable Mexican-inspired meals — burritos, bowls, tacos, and quesadillas — assembled to order from fresh, in-house ingredients. Cyclists will find a quick, filling stop with a broad menu that includes vegetarian proteins and gluten-free tortilla options.

detail.address: 10330 McDonald Park Road, Sidney, BC V8L2L5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Nutrition calculator lists 'Veggie Ground' and 'Falafel' as protein options, and 'Gluten Free' as a tortilla choice for burritos and quesadillas

restaurant.name: The Bee's Knees
restaurant.desc: The Bee's Knees is a homemade-focused cafe on West Pender Street in downtown Vancouver, taking its name from the old English expression for 'the best.' It specializes in focaccia sandwiches with quality ingredients like prosciutto and stracciatella, alongside a creative drinks menu featuring signature bee-themed beverages such as The Bee's Latte with honey and bee pollen. Cyclists stopping in will find a full cafe and bakery menu available for quick pickup via online ordering.

detail.address: 1139 W Pender St, Vancouver, British Columbia V6E 2V2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels 'Honey gorgonzola & Fig (🧀 Vegetarian)'; no vegan or GF labelling observed

restaurant.name: Bowen Island Pub
restaurant.desc: A family-owned community institution for over 35 years, the Bowen Island Pub sits at the Four Corners intersection just 300 metres up the hill from the Snug Cove ferry terminal — making it a natural first or last stop for cyclists riding on Bowen Island. The pub offers a broad menu spanning pub classics, sushi, pizza, and a kids menu, along with a full cocktail and BC craft beer list. Live music events and a sun-drenched patio add to the appeal for anyone settling in after a day on the island's roads.

detail.address: 479 Bowen Island Trunk Road, Bowen Island

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Takeout menu explicitly notes 'Vegetarian and/or vegan option (foods may come into contact with non-vegan ingredients) | gluten free or can be made gluten free' across multiple menu items

restaurant.name: The Marmalade Cat Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Marmalade Cat Café is a community-oriented café on Pandosy Street in Kelowna serving specialty coffees, handmade baked goods, brunch, and sandwiches with homemade soups. The café supports local culture by displaying and selling work by local artists, giving it a distinctly neighbourhood feel. Dietary accommodations include gluten-free baked goods, vegan sandwiches on request, and milk alternatives such as almond, oat, and soy.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website confirms gluten-free breads, dessert bars, and carrot cake; vegan sandwiches available on request; milk alternatives include almond, oat, and soy

restaurant.name: Zio's
restaurant.desc: Zio's is a pizza counter in the food court of River Rock Casino Resort, a large casino resort complex in Richmond, BC. As a fast-food outlet inside a major entertainment venue, it offers a dining option for cyclists in the area. Be aware that entry to River Rock Casino now requires government-issued photo ID under BC casino regulations.

restaurant.name: The Shed
restaurant.desc: SHED is a casual, family-friendly restaurant in the heart of downtown Tofino, celebrated for its burgers, bowls, and brews made with locally sourced ingredients from Vancouver Island farms and waters. The space features both a patio and indoor dining, with a separate late-night menu running until midnight. It draws on a warm west coast vibe and operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations required.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu offers gluten-free bun substitution ('SUB GLUTEN FREE BUN'); vegetarian/plant-based options include the Attenburger (black bean & quinoa fritter), Aphrodite burger (black bean & quinoa patty on late-night menu), Mayan Picnic bowl, and Pachamama bowl

restaurant.name: 1931 Gallery Bistro
restaurant.desc: 1931 Gallery Bistro is a contemporary dining destination situated inside the iconic Vancouver Art Gallery, named to honour the gallery's founding year of 1931. The bistro features a recently renovated 120-seat licensed outdoor patio overlooking Robson Square, alongside a vibrant interior dining room serving West Coast fusion cuisine and cocktails. Located at 750 Hornby Street in the heart of downtown Vancouver, it offers both walk-in and reservation seating as well as takeout and delivery.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Not explicitly

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast food restaurant in North Vancouver serving burgers, chicken, breakfast, and McCafé beverages, with both drive-through and dine-in options available. The drive-through is noted in OSM as operating around the clock, making it a reliable stop for cyclists needing food at any hour. As part of the McDonald's Canada chain, it offers takeout and a broad menu including value meals and seasonal items.

restaurant.name: Anna's Cake House
restaurant.desc: Anna's Cake House is a family-owned Hong Kong-style bakery founded in 1974 by Anna, Ronald, and Kathleen Cheung, now celebrating 50 years of baking. The Burnaby location at Lougheed Mall is one of four Greater Vancouver outposts offering freshly baked cakes and buns made daily with no artificial additives. Known for its Hong Kong-style buns and made-to-order fresh cream cakes in over 15 flavours, it has become a community institution with a multigenerational following.

detail.address: Unit D15-9855 Austin Rd, Burnaby, BC

restaurant.name: Blenz Coffee
restaurant.desc: Blenz Coffee at Granville & Davie is a 24-hour location of the BC-based coffee chain, situated in Vancouver's busy Davie Village neighbourhood. The café serves espresso drinks, nitro coffee, whole-leaf teas, protein shakes, and a broad food menu spanning breakfast items, pastries, sandwiches, wraps, and desserts. Its round-the-clock hours make it a dependable food and drink stop for cyclists arriving or departing at any hour.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu is dominated by coffee, tea, and baked goods that are inherently vegetarian

restaurant.name: Mumbai Masala
restaurant.desc: Mumbai Masala is a family-owned Indian restaurant located in the Park and Tilford complex in North Vancouver, serving authentic Indian cuisine since 2005. It offers a full dine-in experience with courteous table service alongside online ordering for delivery or pickup, plus catering. The menu spans appetizers, mains, and desserts with both vegetarian and non-vegetarian options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu section lists 'Meals Hot & ready to serve. Veg / Non-Veg', confirming vegetarian options are available

restaurant.name: The Portside Pub
restaurant.desc: The Portside Pub is a maritime-themed bar in Historic Gastown that evokes East Coast pub culture with hand-shucked fresh oysters, a chef-designed menu of garlic fingers, pirogies, and sandwiches, and a lively events calendar featuring karaoke, resident DJs, and live music. Voted one of the friendliest bars in Vancouver, the venue occupies a below-deck-style space with a dedicated stage area and capacity for private corporate events. The venue is 19+ only.

restaurant.name: Italia Bella
restaurant.desc: Italia Bella Bar & Grill is a full-service Italian restaurant on Vancouver's Broadway corridor, helmed by owner and executive chef Kam Khinda whose Italian culinary training shapes a menu of homemade pastas, grilled meats, seafood, and pizzas. The restaurant positions itself as a neighbourhood gathering place with a warm atmosphere and locally sourced ingredients where possible. Online ordering and group dining options are available, making it a practical stop for a sit-down meal on a city cycling route.

restaurant.name: Inside Out Tea Loft
restaurant.desc: Inside Out Tea Loft is a bubble tea café located in a unit at 1180 Pinetree Way in Coquitlam. Specializing in bubble tea drinks, it serves as a refreshment stop in a commercial area of the city. Details about the interior, seating, and full menu are not available from accessible sources.

restaurant.name: Sushi Modo
restaurant.desc: Sushi Modo is a Japanese sushi restaurant listed at 3017 Saint Johns Street in Port Moody. The associated website currently advertises only a Burnaby location, suggesting the Port Moody branch may have closed or relocated. A touring cyclist on the Saint Johns Street corridor should verify the location is still operating before relying on it as a stop.

restaurant.name: Sylvia's Bar
restaurant.desc: Sylvia's Bar is the cocktail lounge of the historic Sylvia Hotel on English Bay, operating as Vancouver's first cocktail bar since 1954. Situated steps from the English Bay Seawall with ocean views from every seat, it serves food from breakfast through late evening alongside live music several nights a week. The hotel also offers bike rentals, making it a natural anchor stop for cyclists on the seawall route between Stanley Park and Granville Island.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Bar menu labels 'GF' on Cajun Dusted Calamari and Harissa Prawns; 'V' label on Hummaganoush indicates vegetarian option

restaurant.name: PAUL Le Café
restaurant.desc: PAUL Le Café is a Vancouver location of the venerable French bakery and café chain founded in 1889, bringing a refined European café atmosphere to downtown Vancouver. The restaurant side of the operation leans upscale, offering high tea, a Martini Society with weekly off-menu cocktails, and regular live music evenings with candlelight. It is a sit-down destination café rather than a quick-stop, with indoor seating and no outdoor patio.

restaurant.name: Petite Café
restaurant.desc: A Lebanese-inspired café at 945 Columbia Street West in Kamloops, offering vegetarian-friendly options. Its Lebanese culinary roots suggest a menu distinct from conventional coffee shops, potentially appealing to cyclists seeking varied fare. The physical café experience at this location could not be fully confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: G-Men at Steveston Ramen Shop
restaurant.desc: G-Men Ramen (branded online as Gmen @ Steveston) is an authentic Japanese ramen restaurant nestled in Steveston Village, a heritage fishing village and popular cycling destination on Richmond's southern waterfront. The compact, focused menu centres on noodle dishes, and the restaurant has cultivated a strong local following. Cyclists exploring the Steveston Seawalk or the South Dyke Trail will find it a convenient stop in the heart of the village.

restaurant.name: Tendon Kohaku
restaurant.desc: Tendon Kohaku is an international Japanese chain specializing in tendon — hearty bowls of crispy tempura over rice — born from a collaboration between Japan's largest soba company Nadai Fujisoba and the Kings Know Group, with locations across Asia and Canada. The Burnaby Metrotown location uses a proprietary water-fryer technology and a custom sesame-vegetable oil blend intended to produce tempura that is less oily and extra crunchy. The menu also covers udon noodles and a range of Japanese sides including takoyaki, karaage, and chawanmushi.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a Vegetable Tendon bowl (kabocha pumpkin, seaweed, french bean, shiitake mushroom, enoki mushroom, yam, baby corn, rice) with no meat or seafood

restaurant.name: Liberty Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Liberty Kitchen is a Canadian neighbourhood restaurant chain (part of Browns Restaurant Group) serving made-from-scratch meals in a community-focused setting. The Langford (Belmont Market) outpost sits in a busy retail and dining complex on the western edge of Greater Victoria. Touring cyclists passing through the Capital Region would find it a convenient full-service meal stop with a full dining room.

restaurant.name: Moncton Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Moncton Pizzeria is a pizza fast-food restaurant in the Richmond neighbourhood offering casual dining. It provides a convenient meal stop for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Dine Kanadiyan
restaurant.desc: Dine Kanadiyan is an authentic Filipino restaurant that opened in 2024 in New Westminster, occupying the former Union Jack Public House space on Seventh Street. The menu spans ala carte classics, a weekend brunch silog lineup, party tray catering, and a communal 'Boodle Fight' buffet format rooted in traditional Filipino dining culture. Live entertainment rounds out the experience, making it a destination for both casual meals and celebrations.

detail.address: 525 Seventh Street, New Westminster, BC V3M 3L6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple ala carte items explicitly marked '(V)': Enokoi (crispy enoki and sweet potato fritters), Sizzling Tofu Sisig, Lato Salad (Seagrapes), Ensaladang Gulay (steamed veggies); brunch menu also includes Sizzling Tofu sizzler

restaurant.name: Taco Del Mar
restaurant.desc: Taco Del Mar is a coastal Mexican fast-food chain serving mission-style burritos, baja fish tacos, burrito bowls, and loaded nachos. This Surrey location (White Rock area) is part of the Canadian franchise network known for its Rippin' Fish Tacos made with crispy baked cod. The menu is built around customizable options, making it a flexible quick-stop for cyclists with varied dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu page explicitly states 'options available: vegetarian vegan gluten-free' on the coastal Mexican menu

restaurant.name: Power House Living Foods Co.
restaurant.desc: Power House Living Foods Co. is a Victoria restaurant specializing in smoothies and salads with a focus on raw vegan and gluten-free options. Touring cyclists seeking plant-based meals will find this establishment offers relevant dietary accommodations.

restaurant.name: Indian Courtyard Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Indian Courtyard Restaurant has been serving authentic North Indian cuisine in New Westminster for over 23 years, specializing in tandoori dishes, aromatic biryanis, and curries made from traditional recipes. The restaurant is particularly noted for its rare Galouti Kababs—finely spiced melt-in-your-mouth kebabs that it claims are unavailable elsewhere in the area. Dine-in, takeout, catering, and third-party delivery are all offered.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes: Vegetable Pakoras, Vegetable Manchurian, Dal Makhni, Shahi Paneer, Chaat Papri, Chole Bhature. No explicit vegan or GF labeling found on the site

restaurant.name: Main Street Diner
restaurant.desc: A Nelson institution since 1983, this family-owned diner on Baker Street is celebrated for fresh halibut fish and chips, authentic Greek specialties, aged AAA steaks, and gourmet burgers. Cyclists can eat inside or on what the restaurant bills as Nelson's first outdoor patio, with locally brewed draft beer, wine, and cocktails on offer. Its central downtown location makes it a natural refueling stop for riders passing through the Kootenays.

restaurant.name: CRAFT Beer Market
restaurant.desc: A craft brewery and pub in Kelowna featuring microbrewed beers and pub cuisine with outdoor seating. As a microbrewery, it supports local craft beer production.

restaurant.name: MORE Cafe & Bakeshop
restaurant.desc: MORE Café & Bakeshop is an owner-operated European bakery and café in Upper Gibsons, founded in 2012 by Andrew, Leslie, and their Master Baker Alain, and is one of only four BC bakeries making scratch croissants daily. Situated on Gibsons Way along the Sunshine Coast Highway, it sits directly on the cycling route between the community and the Langdale Ferry terminal, making it a natural stop for cyclists arriving or departing the coast. The café serves European-style pastries, muffins, sandwiches, salads, and hot beverages with dine-in seating and online ordering available.

detail.address: 1057 Gibsons Way, Gibsons, BC V0N 1V4, Canada

restaurant.name: Sahota's Live Grill
restaurant.desc: Sahota's Live Grill is a well-established Indian and Western fusion restaurant that has been operating for over a decade across Surrey, Langley, and Abbotsford. It is best known for its live grill concept, where chefs cook meats and seafood over an open flame in view of diners, turning the meal into a culinary experience. With a capacity of 140, outdoor seating, a full bar, and takeout and delivery options, it serves a broad range of needs for cyclists passing through the 56 Avenue corridor.

restaurant.name: Kanadell Japanese Bakery
restaurant.desc: Kanadell Japanese Bakery is a small East Vancouver storefront founded by Japanese-born baker Keiko Nakanishi, specializing in authentic Japanese breads and pastries such as melon pan, curry pan, and elaborately crafted whole cakes. The bakery grew from an online operation and farmers-market vendor into a neighbourhood shop with indoor café seating, and was featured on Food Network Canada's 'Project Bakeover.' It also participates in local farmers markets and offers pre-ordering, catering, and UberEats delivery.

detail.address: 3596 East Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V5K 2A7

restaurant.name: The Blue Poppy
restaurant.desc: The Blue Poppy is a casual lunch restaurant housed in a large atrium-style former greenhouse within the world-famous Butchart Gardens near Brentwood Bay. It serves fresh, seasonal fare including soups, salads, burgers, and regional entrées. Access requires paid garden admission, making it a destination in itself rather than a casual en-route stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page explicitly labels items as Gluten Free, Vegan, and Dairy Free; curry entrée offers a vegetarian portobello option

restaurant.name: L & G Bubble Tea
restaurant.desc: L & G Bubble Tea is a specialty bubble tea cafe located on Fraser Street in Vancouver. It offers indoor seating for cyclists seeking a beverage and snack stop.

restaurant.name: Hee Rae Deung Korean Chinese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Hee Rae Deung is a Korean-Chinese restaurant offering traditional Korean dishes including fried chicken, kimchi rice, mussel soup, and pig trotters in what the website describes as a relaxed and cozy environment. The restaurant accepts online orders, making it convenient for cyclists planning meals in advance. The menu leans heavily into Korean comfort food with a few Chinese-influenced items.

restaurant.name: Olympia Pizza & Pasta Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A long-running Greek and Italian restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, steps from the Stanley Park seawall cycling loop. Olympia is locally famous for successfully fighting off IOC legal threats during the 2010 Winter Olympics, becoming the only small business known to have beaten the Olympic trademark machine. The restaurant offers a broad menu of souvlaki, pasta, pizza, and salads, with a heated licensed patio.

notes.Takeout: Website front page advertises free delivery from 4 pm with a minimum order, confirming off-premises food service
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists vegetarian lasagna and pasta dishes available with vegetable sauces, plus vegan fasolatha soup on lunch menu

restaurant.name: Nellie's European Deli Foods & Imports
restaurant.desc: Nellie's European Deli has been a community institution in Nanaimo since 1998, operating out of Rock City Centre and specialising in imported European groceries from Holland, Germany, Sweden, Poland, and beyond. The deli counter turns out house-made sandwiches, daily soups, and freshly baked meat pies in varieties ranging from steak-and-kidney to turkey cranberry, with gluten-free options available. For a touring cyclist, it offers a convenient stop for a hot or packaged meal along the Island Highway corridor.

detail.address: 2980 Island Highway North #500, Nanaimo, BC V9T 5V4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'We offer both a meat soup and a vegetarian soup daily' and lists a 'Gluten-Free selection' among meat pie options

restaurant.name: Noodlebox
restaurant.desc: Noodlebox is a Canadian quick-service chain specializing in wok-fired noodle and rice boxes inspired by Asian cuisines, from Pad Thai to Butter Chicken. Dishes are made to order with your choice of noodle or rice and can be customized for vegan or gluten-friendly diets. The Tsawwassen location sits in the Canoe Pass Way retail area, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the ferry corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Can be made VEGAN – Please ask when ordering' and 'Can be made GLUTEN-FRIENDLY – Please ask when ordering'

restaurant.name: The Gray Olive Cafeteria
restaurant.desc: The Gray Olive Cafeteria is a sit-down breakfast and brunch spot on Hastings Street in Burnaby, known for creative egg dishes, specialty benedicts, and brioche-bun sandwiches. The menu spans approachable comfort food — from a Pork Belly Benny with kabocha squash to an Impossible patty Veggie Burger — with an extensive drinks list including Thai iced tea and specialty lattes. The restaurant uses a waitlist system and takes reservations, pointing to a popular neighbourhood destination.

notes.Takeout: Website add-ons list includes 'TO GO CONTAINER $0.25', indicating takeout orders are accommodated
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Veggie Benny (avocado, tomatoes, hollandaise), Veggie Burger (Impossible patty), and a gluten-free option available for sandwiches

restaurant.name: Howl Brewing
restaurant.desc: Howl Brewing is an independently owned nano brewery that has been crafting small-batch beer from BC-grown ingredients since 2018, operating a newly opened tasting room in Esquimalt as of April 2026. Their ever-changing lineup leans toward the unusual — medieval gruits, Viking-era ales, fresh-hopped seasonals, and historic styles from Poland, Germany, and Belgium — making it a destination for curious drinkers. Beer is also available for free local delivery and at area farmers markets, private liquor stores, and restaurants.

restaurant.name: Foglifter Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Foglifter Coffee Roasters is a family-run specialty roaster with roots in over 20 years of Vancouver retail coffee, now roasting on Vancouver Island's Cowichan Valley and serving the public through its East Vancouver flagship cafe at the corner of Main & 20th. The business sources beans through carefully chosen importers and roasts on a Diedrich IR-12, with an emphasis on craft and producer relationships. Cyclists passing through East Van can stop in for espresso or filter coffee prepared with the same beans the roastery ships across Canada.

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: Starbucks is a globally recognized coffeehouse chain with a location in Vancouver's coordinates at 49.264°N, 123.167°W. It offers a broad menu of espresso drinks, refreshers, teas, and packaged food items available for takeaway. For touring cyclists, it represents a well-known and consistent stop in an urban setting, though store-specific amenities are not documented in available sources.

detail.address: 3492 Cambie St., Vancouver, BC V5Z 2W8, Canada

restaurant.name: The Hide Out Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Hide Out Cafe is a Fair Trade, organic coffee shop and fresh-food lunch spot in downtown New Westminster, serving locally-roasted coffee from Continental Coffee in Vancouver alongside house-made paninis, wraps, salads, and soups. Situated on Carnarvon Street across from the New Westminster Law Courts, it offers both indoor seating and a patio in a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere. Touring cyclists will find a solid mid-day stop with a broad menu including vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free choices, plus free Wi-Fi and takeout service.

detail.address: 716 Carnarvon Street, New Westminster, BC V3M 6V4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page states 'fresh and delicious offerings made in-house daily - including vegan, vegetarian, organic, and gluten free choices'

restaurant.name: Zarak
restaurant.desc: Zarak is an Afghan-Persian restaurant on Main Street in Vancouver serving refined dishes rooted in traditional family recipes, including a celebrated secret cake that has been a Sarwari family tradition for over 20 years. The restaurant describes itself as an unpretentious space where gold flakes meet mum's cooking, offering dinner, weekend brunch, and happy hour menus. Beyond dining, Zarak extends its Afghan heritage through a shop selling hand-harvested spices, traditional vests, and inspired dinnerware.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states: 'Menu items marked ‘v’ can be vegan, and ‘gfo’ can be gluten-free.'

restaurant.name: The Keg
restaurant.desc: The Keg is a well-established Canadian steakhouse and bar chain situated in Pinetree Village, at the corner of Anson Avenue and Pinetree Way, across from Coquitlam Centre. The full-service restaurant features a bar and lounge, a patio, and a menu centred on premium steaks and classic North American fare. Takeout and DoorDash delivery are available for cyclists who prefer a meal on the go.

detail.address: 2991 Lougheed Hwy, Unit 130, Coquitlam, BC V3B 6J6

restaurant.name: Hellcrust Pizza
restaurant.desc: Hellcrust Pizza is a fast-food pizza chain with a White Rock location on Vidal Street. The brand operates multiple BC locations and offers online ordering through its app and website, along with coupons and deals. It is a straightforward quick-service pizza stop for cyclists passing through the White Rock area.

restaurant.name: Chaiiwala of London
restaurant.desc: Chaiiwala of London is a British-South Asian franchise cafe known for specialty chai drinks like Karak Chaii and Limbu Pani alongside desi-inspired street food including roti rolls and savoury snacks. The New Westminster location occupies a unit at 607 Belmont Street and offers indoor seating, making it a warming rest stop with a distinctly different flavour profile from standard coffee shops. Cyclists looking for a chai fix or a quick desi bite will find this a novel option on a BC touring route.

restaurant.name: Dave & Mel's Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Dave & Mel's is a North Vancouver pizzeria that makes its dough fresh from scratch every night, turning out classics alongside locally-named creations like the 'North Shore Shredder' and the 'Wowee Maui' Pineapple Pizza. The menu covers vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options, and the shop offers online ordering for takeout. They also run event catering services for larger groups.

detail.address: 113 West 1st Street, North Vancouver, BC V7M 1B1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We also offer delicious vegetarian, vegan and Gluten-free options, making sure there's something for everyone to enjoy.'

restaurant.name: Red Burrito
restaurant.desc: Red Burrito is a beloved local Mexican restaurant that opened on Commercial Drive in January 2006 and has grown to multiple Vancouver locations. The kitchen makes everything fresh daily — handmade tamales wrapped in banana leaf, house-ground salsas, and slow-cooked meats — keeping to a simple, quality-focused menu for nearly two decades. Cyclists heading along Commercial Drive will find a filling, made-from-scratch burrito or taco in a lively neighbourhood setting.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists a dedicated Vegetarian filling (Spanish rice, beans, toppings, fresh guacamole) and a Vegan Meat filling (soy-based protein in Red Burrito spices). No gluten-free option mentioned

restaurant.name: Oldhand Cafe and Bakery
restaurant.desc: Oldhand Coffee is a family-owned specialty cafe and bakery in downtown Abbotsford, rooted in European traditions of hospitality and community. Everything is baked in-house daily using local and seasonal ingredients, with a full espresso bar and a rotating menu of pastries, sandwiches, and sweets. A second location opened in Langley in March 2025, and the Abbotsford cafe has become a well-established downtown social hub.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels jam thumbprint cookie '(gf + vegan)', date and nut bliss ball '(gf + vegan)', chocolate nut brownie '(gf)', and amaretti cookie '(gf)'

restaurant.name: Pizzeria Spacca Napoli
restaurant.desc: Pizzeria Spacca Napoli is an authentic Neapolitan pizzeria in Port Moody founded in 2016 by Davide Di Giovanni and Danny Pero, built around a commitment to Italian tradition using imported 00 flour, DOP San Marzano tomatoes, and even European scissors for slicing pizza the Neapolitan way. In 2024 it was named the Best Neapolitan Pizzeria in Canada and became the first Canadian pizzeria to earn three 'spicchi' from Italy's prestigious Gambero Rosso guide. Cyclists will find a welcoming sit-down restaurant with pickup and delivery options, vegan-adaptable pizzas, and gluten-free pasta on the menu.

detail.address: 2801 St. Johns Street, Port Moody, BC V3H 2C1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states pizzas can be made vegan (without cheese; dough is vegan). Gluten-free pasta options are also available per FAQ

restaurant.name: Lotus
restaurant.desc: Lotus Restaurant is a Vietnamese and Asian food eatery in Richmond serving dishes such as pho, fried rolls, and salad rolls. The restaurant operates on a walk-in basis with no reservations, making it an accessible drop-in option. Online ordering and a dedicated takeout service are available for cyclists wanting a quick meal to go.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'A3 Vegetarian Salad Roll (Goi Cuon Chay)' as a dedicated vegetarian item; no vegan or GF claims confirmed

restaurant.name: Gina's Sandwich & Coffee
restaurant.desc: Gina's Sandwich & Coffee is a cafe located in Maple Ridge, BC, operating out of unit 110 of a local commercial building. The business appears to be a recent rebranding of the former Sushi Eben-Ezer, now offering sandwiches and coffee. It sits along a cycling-accessible corridor in Maple Ridge, making it a potential stop for riders passing through the community.

restaurant.name: Casa Del Pane Italian Bakery
restaurant.desc: Casa Del Pane is a family-owned Italian bakery and deli in Port Moody with over 30 years of tradition, producing bread, pastries, donuts, and custom cakes from heritage recipes. The shop also serves freshly made pizza and panini daily, making it a genuine stop for a hot meal on the road. Its warm, community-oriented atmosphere and broad savoury-and-sweet menu offer touring cyclists a meaningful resupply and rest point.

detail.address: 242 Newport Drive, Port Moody, BC V3H 5B9

restaurant.name: Lion Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Lion Hot Pot is a Chinese restaurant on Marine Drive in North Vancouver offering an extensive Szechuan and Cantonese-influenced menu with signature dishes including roasted fish, hot spicy pot, and roasted duck. Despite its name, the restaurant serves a broad range of stir-fries, noodle dishes, cold appetizers, and soups alongside its hot pot offerings. Online ordering with in-store pickup is available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area.

detail.address: 1356 Marine Drive, North Vancouver, BC V7P 1T4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu legend explicitly includes a 'vegetarian' label; multiple vegetarian dishes identified including Braised Tofu, Tomato and Egg, Potato with Vinegar Sauce, Sauteed Mixed Vegetables, and Stir-Fried Cabbage. No GF or vegan labeling mentioned

restaurant.name: Hiraku Sushi
restaurant.desc: Hiraku Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Coquitlam offering an extensive menu of sushi rolls, sashimi, aburi nigiri, donburi, noodles, and hot pot. The kitchen emphasizes fresh, high-quality ingredients and carefully crafted presentation across a broad range of traditional and fusion Japanese dishes. Touring cyclists passing through the Coquitlam area would find a full sit-down or takeout Japanese meal option here.

restaurant.name: Cafe Overflow
restaurant.desc: Cafe Overflow is a North Vancouver café blending Korean cuisine with brunch and coffee-shop offerings — an unusual combination that could make it a compelling stop for touring cyclists looking for something beyond standard cafe fare. Its location in North Vancouver places it near popular cycling routes on the North Shore.

detail.address: 467 Mountain Hwy #105, North Vancouver, BC V7J 2L3, Canada

restaurant.name: Brassneck Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: Brassneck Brewery is a well-established craft brewery and tasting room on Main Street in Vancouver, known for a rotating roster of adventurous beers ranging from tart barrel-aged fruit ales to imperial milkshake stouts. The on-site tasting room pours a wide selection on tap and sells cans to go, with food available from sister restaurant The Magnet. Growler fills are offered for 0.5L, 1L, and 2L vessels, including those from other breweries.

restaurant.name: Yaletown Gelato
restaurant.desc: Yaletown Gelato is a neighbourhood ice cream and gelato shop on Homer Street in Vancouver's Yaletown district. It sits within easy reach of the False Creek Seawall, one of the most popular cycling corridors in the city, making it a natural mid-ride treat stop. The area is dense with street-level retail and is highly accessible by bike.

restaurant.name: Osaka Sushi
restaurant.desc: Osaka Sushi is a Japanese restaurant on Burrard Street in Vancouver offering sushi, sashimi, donburi, noodles, hot pot, and more. The menu emphasizes fresh, globally sourced ingredients across a wide range of traditional and contemporary Japanese dishes. OSM notes both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a convenient stop on one of Vancouver's major cycling corridors.

restaurant.name: Pallet Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Pallet Coffee Roasters is a locally owned Vancouver specialty coffee roastery established in East Vancouver in 2014, now operating eight café locations across Metro Vancouver. The Melville Street outpost (branded 'Pallet Melville') is one of several cafés serving expertly roasted single-origin coffees alongside food and freshly baked goods. Beyond its cafés, Pallet runs a full-service roastery, barista training program, and wholesale supply operation across Canada.

restaurant.name: Horin Ramen + Sake
restaurant.desc: Horin Ramen + Sake is a Japanese ramen restaurant on Robson Street in Vancouver whose heritage traces back 59 years to a pioneering tonkotsu ramen shop in Ogori, Fukuoka Prefecture — the first in Japan to use chili peppers in pork-bone broth. The Vancouver location carries on that legacy by making its broth and tare sauce by hand daily, adjusting for season and weather. Online ordering is available for the Robson location.

restaurant.name: Jolly Miller Pub
restaurant.desc: The Jolly Miller Pub is a traditional pub in Chilliwack offering food and beverages. It serves as a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking for a meal or refreshment while traveling through the area.

detail.address: 5865 Vedder Rd Chilliwack, BC, Canada V2R 1C3

restaurant.name: The Churchill
restaurant.desc: Churchill Draughthouse is a cozy Victoria pub occupying a historic Government Street building whose roots trace back to the Garrick's Head Saloon of 1867, with its most colourful chapter being the rough-and-tumble Churchill Hotel of the 1940s–70s. The pub pours 20 rotating taps focused on BC and Pacific Northwest craft breweries, backed by a broad whiskey selection and West Coast pub-fare menu. It sits steps from Bastion Square in the heart of downtown Victoria, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists riding the inner harbour area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu explicitly labels items: GF (can be made gluten-free), VG (can be made Vegan), V (Vegetarian). Examples include Waffle Yam Fries (V), Mac & Cheese (V), Beet Salad (GF, VG, V), Churchill Cheeseburger (GF, VG option)

restaurant.name: Alley 16
restaurant.desc: Alley 16 is an upscale Japanese BBQ restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver where guests grill premium cuts tableside, with the menu centred on A5 wagyu beef — the highest possible rating — alongside uni sashimi, seafood, and handcrafted sides. The concept draws on the vibrant alley-food culture of Shanghai, Beijing, and Taipei, translated into an elegant Vancouver dining room. Reservations are strongly recommended, and the kitchen takes pride in locally sourced, fresh ingredients.

restaurant.name: The Farmer's Daughter
restaurant.desc: The Farmer's Daughter is a fromagerie, bistro, and wine bar on Sidney's main Beacon Avenue, specializing in over 150 artisan and farmhouse cheeses cut to order alongside a curated wine selection. The shop offers cheese and wine flights with tasting notes, a small plates menu, and grazing platters and picnic boxes to go. It's an excellent resupply stop for touring cyclists looking for high-quality charcuterie, cheese, or a ready-made picnic on the Saanich Peninsula.

notes.Packed lunches: Website lists a 'Picnic Box' product available for purchase

restaurant.name: JAPADOG
restaurant.desc: JAPADOG is an award-winning, iconic Vancouver hot dog concept founded in 2005 that blends Japanese flavours and ingredients with the classic North American hot dog. The McArthurGlen Outlet Mall location serves the full menu of specialty dogs featuring Kurobuta pork, Wagyu beef, and authentic Japanese sauces alongside veggie and vegan options. It has become a sought-after culinary stop for locals and tourists alike, drawing celebrity attention and international recognition for its unique fusion approach.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists a dedicated 'VEGGIE HOT DOGS' section including explicitly vegan items: Vegan Avocado & Cheez, Vegan Tomato & Cheez, plus multiple other veggie options

restaurant.name: Mek's Delight
restaurant.desc: Mek's Delight is a Malaysian restaurant located on 104 Avenue in Surrey, BC. It offers indoor dining in a no-smoking environment, making it a sit-down stop for cyclists passing through the area. Malaysian cuisine — with its rice dishes, noodles, and hearty curries — can be a satisfying refuel for long-distance riders.

detail.address: 14910 104 Ave, Surrey, British Columbia V3R 1M7, Canada

restaurant.name: Haidilao Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Haidilao Hot Pot is a globally recognized Chinese hot pot chain whose first Canadian location opened in Richmond in December 2018. Diners choose up to four broth bases in a divided pot, then cook thinly sliced meats, seafood, and vegetables at the table — a communal, interactive meal well-suited to groups. The brand is widely known for elaborate tableside service and a broad menu spanning dozens of proteins, vegetables, and custom dipping sauces.

restaurant.name: Sushi Farm
restaurant.desc: Sushi Farm is a fast food sushi restaurant on Princess Street in North Vancouver with indoor seating. It provides a quick dining option for touring cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: Ichiro Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Ichiro Japanese Restaurant is a Japanese-owned and operated full-service restaurant in Steveston Fisherman Village, serving authentic washoku cuisine since 2006. The restaurant is notable for its exceptional sashimi quality — it is reportedly the only sushi restaurant in the Vancouver area using a specialty -60°C freezer — and imports fresh fish and Wagyu beef directly from Japan. Steveston is a well-known cycling destination in Richmond, making this a potential rest stop for cyclists exploring the Steveston waterfront.

restaurant.name: The 49th Cafe
restaurant.desc: 49th Parallel Cafe is a cafe located in Ladysmith on the east coast of Vancouver Island, British Columbia. Ladysmith lies along the busy cycling corridor connecting Nanaimo and Duncan, making cafes in the town natural rest stops for touring cyclists. Beyond its OSM record, no detailed business information was retrievable from the Facebook page.

restaurant.name: Sushi Sei
restaurant.desc: Sushi Sei is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Kingsway in Vancouver, offering both dine-in and online ordering options. Touring cyclists can stop in for a fresh sushi meal and Japanese cuisine in a casual dining environment. The restaurant's central location makes it accessible to cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor.

restaurant.name: Tekkaba
restaurant.desc: Tekkaba is a Japanese restaurant on East Cordova Street in Vancouver, specializing in Kaiseki-style Omakase and traditional Izakaya cuisine, established by Pacific Dream Group. The space is decorated with Korean paintings and egg crafts donated by artist Gyungja Jung in support of a social welfare initiative, giving the dining room a distinctive cultural character. Multi-course Omakase dinners are offered in two evening seatings, with reservations strongly recommended.

restaurant.name: Golden Inn Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Golden Inn Seafood Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant in Nanaimo serving authentic dishes including Peking duck, Peking ginger beef, lobster, and crab, with lunch and dinner buffets. It is part of a two-location operation alongside its sister restaurant Dragon City in Ladysmith. Delivery, pick-up, and catering are all available, making it a flexible dining option for cyclists passing through Nanaimo.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Mushroom Chop Suey, Tofu Chop Suey, and Pan Fried Tofu with Chinese Mushrooms as vegetarian options

restaurant.name: Bella Nonna's Bakery

Named after the owner's mother and daughter, the shop celebrates Italian culinary traditions with a community-focused ethos. A touring cyclist stopping here can pick up artisan breads, pastries, and specialty deli items to fuel the road ahead.

restaurant.name: Garrick's Head Pub

The two-level pub boasts an outdoor patio overlooking the historic square — a welcoming stop for cyclists coming through downtown Victoria — along with a wood-burning fireplace for cooler days. The menu runs to classic pub fare alongside what the owners claim is Victoria's largest selection of craft and import beers on tap.

restaurant.name: Plum Garden

restaurant.name: Good Choice Restaurant

Delivery via Uber, DoorDash, and SkipTheDishes is also available for those coordinating a rest stop.

restaurant.name: Yayu

restaurant.name: Pogue Mahone Irish Pub and Liquor Store

Regular entertainment such as Music Bingo, Karaoke, and Live Music rounds out the experience for anyone settling in after a ride.

restaurant.name: Grist and Mash Brewery

For cyclists passing through the Kimberley area, it offers a relaxed stop for a locally brewed pint in a no-smoking environment.

restaurant.name: Crystal Hut

It appears in Whistler Blackcomb's official dining listings alongside other resort restaurants, indicating it is a fully staffed, sit-down-style facility rather than a kiosk. For a cyclist descending from the bike park, it represents a mid-mountain refuelling stop with full resort infrastructure behind it.

restaurant.name: Essence of India

The menu features classics like butter chicken, biryani, tandoori dishes, and fresh naan, with dine-in, takeout, and catering all available. It sits in a suburban commercial area and would serve as a warm sit-down meal stop for cyclists tackling the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

restaurant.name: Nobi Nobi Obanzai
restaurant.desc: Nobi Nobi Obanzai is a Japanese comfort food restaurant in Richmond inspired by the Obanzai cooking tradition of Kyoto, which centres on small seasonal dishes. Online ordering is available, making it a practical stop for a quick meal.

restaurant.name: The Anchor Eatery

restaurant.name: Bon Sushi

A touring cyclist could stop here for fresh-baked bread and savoury meat pies as a food resupply.

restaurant.name: Original Pho

Nearly every item is made from scratch — herbs and garnishes prepped fresh daily, bowls finished tableside — earning it a loyal local following. Cyclists can dine in or order pickup and delivery from a broad menu spanning pho, vermicelli, rice plates, and iced coffee.

restaurant.name: The Hestia Veggie

The kitchen emphasises bold flavours, fresh ingredients, and thoughtful visual presentation in an entirely vegan setting with no non-vegan options. The restaurant also offers catering and group orders with free delivery within downtown Vancouver, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking to fuel up or arrange a group meal.

restaurant.name: Lakesider Brewing Co

restaurant.name: Ragazzi Pizza Co.

restaurant.name: Jac's On The Beach

The restaurant draws both locals and visitors with its lively atmosphere, Saturday Prime Rib nights, and daily happy hour.

restaurant.name: Beaucoup Bakery

restaurant.name: Café Gloucester

The Cambie Street location sits along a major cycling corridor in South Vancouver, making it a potential mid-ride dining stop.

restaurant.name: Curry Lounge

restaurant.name: Chào Mámì

The menu spans small plates, specialty noodle soups including pho, and a full bar with Vietnamese-inspired cocktails and imported Asian beers. It operates as a full-service dine-in restaurant with delivery available through major platforms.

restaurant.name: Fresh Tracks Cafe

restaurant.name: Billy Button Dessert

The shop specializes in desserts and offers online ordering for convenient pickup. It sits on a well-travelled urban cycling corridor connecting south Vancouver to the city core.

restaurant.name: Sahand Bread & Kebab

Touring cyclists can fuel up on hearty Persian staples including lamb and ground beef koobideh kebabs, flank steak barg, and saffron chicken.

restaurant.name: Adrienne's Restaurant & Tea Garden

It serves breakfast, lunch, and afternoon High Tea alongside an in-house bakery, deli counter, and ice cream parlour. The farm setting, locally-sourced and ocean-wise ingredients, and explicitly wheelchair-accessible premises make it a distinctive destination on a Saanich Peninsula cycling route.

restaurant.name: Curry Hut Indian Bistro

restaurant.name: Cindy's

With a 4.3 Google rating across 425 reviews, it draws a steady crowd of regulars and visitors alike.

It offers indoor seating and online ordering for pickup or delivery, making it a convenient full-meal stop for hungry cyclists passing through New Westminster.

restaurant.name: The Peri Peri Shack: Flame Grilled Chicken

Diners can choose from seven heat levels ranging from Mild to the blazing Peri Nero, with whole chickens, wings, skewers, sharing packs, and a handful of seafood and vegetarian options rounding out the menu. The restaurant describes itself as a community gathering spot and is actively expanding, with franchising information on its site.

restaurant.name: Lupo

restaurant.name: Straight Outta Brooklyn NYC Pizzeria

restaurant.name: The Capitol Restaurant

Touring riders on the Pacific Rim route will find it a well-positioned fuel stop near the edge of town.

restaurant.name: Kinton Ramen

restaurant.name: Ethical Bean Café
restaurant.desc: Ethical Bean Coffee is a Vancouver-based coffee roaster founded in 2003, certified 100% fair trade and organic from day one, sourcing Arabica beans seasonally from Central and South America with full crop-to-cup traceability. The Kootenay Street address is tagged in OSM as a café associated with the brand's Canadian roasting operations. Cyclists stopping here would be drinking coffee roasted by one of Canada's most recognized ethical sourcing brands.

restaurant.name: Pearl Hot Pot

The menu is built around bold, shared plates — curries, claypots, satays, and noodles — drawing on both Singaporean and Malaysian traditions. The Burnaby location was recognized on DoorDash's Canada's 50 Most Loved All Stars list for 2022.

restaurant.name: Ono Poké
restaurant.desc: Ono Poké is a Victoria-based Hawaiian poke bowl chain with four shopping-centre locations across the city and Saanich. Founded after the owner's transformative first taste of poke in Hawaii, the restaurant prepares traditional Hawaiian poke and BBQ layered with fresh West Coast ingredients. Cyclists will find a range of customizable bowls — including vegan, gluten-free, and high-protein options — plus Hawaiian hot plates and snacks like spam musubi.

restaurant.name: Uno Gelato

The shop rotates a wide selection of seasonal flavours alongside year-round favourites, and also offers gelato-making classes and event cart services across the Lower Mainland. Located at Stamp's Landing on False Creek, it's a notable stop along Vancouver's waterfront cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Torafuku
restaurant.desc: Torafuku is a contemporary pan-Asian restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street, helmed by Taiwanese-born chef Steve Kuan, who first made his mark with the acclaimed Le Tigre food truck before opening this brick-and-mortar location. Dishes range from an award-winning beef noodle soup and signature Kickass Rice bowls to east-meets-west shared plates in an open-concept dining room on the edge of historic Chinatown. The restaurant is now celebrating its 10th anniversary and has built a loyal following for its Asian-inspired cocktails and seasonal chef's tasting menu.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Takeout options available till 7PM online or phone calls, also via delivery by doordash & Uber' with an online lunch ordering page and direct phone ordering

restaurant.name: Fishboat
restaurant.desc: Fishboat — also known as Fishboat Fish & Chippery — is a fish and chips eatery on White Rock's Marine Drive waterfront that has been operating since 2009. It sits on a popular recreational and touring cycling corridor along the Semiahmoo shoreline, with outdoor seating available. The seafront setting makes it a fitting food stop for cyclists exploring the White Rock waterfront and promenade.

restaurant.name: Panago
restaurant.desc: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain franchise offering delivery and takeout only, with no dine-in seating at this downtown Vancouver location. The menu emphasizes quality ingredients including antibiotic-free chicken and pork, organic tomato sauce, and daily-fresh dough, with vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-smart options available. For a touring cyclist, this is a convenient fuel stop for hot pizza and sides in the West End neighbourhood.

detail.address: 1199 West Pender Street, Vancouver, BC V6E 2R1
