restaurant.name: Melriches Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Melriches Coffee House is an independent cafe that has served Vancouver's West End neighbourhood since 1997, deliberately positioning itself as a community alternative to chain coffee shops with mismatched furniture and a weekly neighbour meet-up table by the window. It offers coffee, teas, pastries, soups, and sandwiches in a wheelchair-accessible indoor setting on Davie Street near Bute. The cafe's community-first ethos — prompt cards on the counter to help strangers start conversations — sets it apart from more transactional coffee stops.

restaurant.name: Sweet Leaf Bakery & Cafe
restaurant.desc: Sweet Leaf Bakery & Cafe is a locally-owned bakery and espresso bar tucked inside Piccadilly Mall in the heart of Salmon Arm, serving creative seasonal desserts including cupcakes, macarons, and custom cakes alongside freshly roasted local coffee. The kitchen also turns out savoury light lunches — soups, focaccia, croissant sandwiches, and a variety of rolls — making it a solid mid-ride refuel stop. The cafe prides itself on sourcing as many locally made and harvested ingredients as possible.

detail.address: 128 - 1151 10th Avenue South West, Salmon Arm, BC V1E 1T3

restaurant.name: Amsterdam
restaurant.desc: Amsterdam Restaurant is a cozy, locally owned breakfast and lunch eatery that has been introducing Kamloops to Dutch pannenkoeken (crepes) for over 20 years. Its menu fuses North American favourites with European specialties including Belgian waffles, German Reuben, and Moroccan Chicken Shawarma, all made with fresh, locally sourced ingredients. Cyclists with dietary restrictions will find extensive gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian options, and takeout is readily available for those on the move.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Gluten Free, vegetarian, vegan? We have it all!' and dedicates a section to gluten-free friendly, vegetarian, and vegan waffles, pannenkoeken, skillets, sandwiches, salads, and soups; also notes precautions for celiac disease

restaurant.name: Fox & Hounds Pub & Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Fox & Hounds is a long-established neighbourhood pub in Aldergrove, BC, whose fanciful origin story claims its heavy timber frame was shipped from England by a fox-hunting publican and reassembled in the alder grove that gave the town its name. Over generations the building grew through eclectic additions, each filled with artifacts and memorabilia, creating a distinctive collection of rooms. Touring cyclists will find a full-service kitchen with online ordering, a VIP rewards program, and a genuine community pub atmosphere on the edge of the Fraser Valley.

restaurant.name: Goldie's Donuts and Bakery
restaurant.desc: Goldie's Donuts & Bakery is a gourmet brioche donut shop that uses a 24-hour slow fermentation process imported from Korean baking tradition to produce exceptionally light and flavourful donuts. The Horseshoe Bay location in West Vancouver sits along a popular Sea-to-Sky cycling corridor, making it a natural pit stop for cyclists heading to or from Squamish. The shop also offers signature espresso drinks like Peanut Butter Cream Latte and Oreo Cream Mocha to pair with its donuts.

detail.address: 101-6693 Nelson Ave, West Vancouver, BC V7W 2B2

restaurant.name: Kwao Thai Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kwao Thai Restaurant is a family-run authentic Thai restaurant in Esquimalt, just outside Victoria. The name 'Kwao' means rice in Thai, and the menu centres on traditional dishes — curries, stir-fries, soups, and noodles — with customizable spice levels from mild to Thai hot. Cyclists will find a welcoming neighbourhood spot offering both dine-in and takeout, with explicit support for vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-friendly diets.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website front page states 'Vegetarian & Vegan are available'; About page notes rice dishes are 'naturally good for gluten-free diets' and advises vegans to request fish sauce be omitted

restaurant.name: Blind Rabbit
restaurant.desc: Blind Rabbit is a neighbourhood bar and charcuterie restaurant on East Hastings Street in Vancouver's Hastings-Sunrise area, specializing in an extensive lineup of BC craft gins and spirits alongside boards, paninis, and fondue. The venue is fully wheelchair accessible, including accessible washrooms. Its food-forward bar menu makes it a potential refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the east side of the city.

restaurant.name: Flamingo Cafe
restaurant.desc: Flamingo Cafe is a café and casual restaurant on Granville Street in downtown Vancouver, serving espresso drinks, specialty lattes, breakfast plates, and Mediterranean-influenced sandwiches and flatbreads. The café offers both indoor and outdoor seating and accepts online orders for delivery or pickup. Its central location in Vancouver's entertainment district makes it a convenient stop for cyclists moving through the city core.

restaurant.name: Blue Ox Pub

It hosts regular events — including an annual Big Buck Contest — making it a lively local gathering spot. For touring cyclists passing through the North Okanagan on routes connecting Vernon and the Monashee corridor, it offers a full sit-down meal and bar in a relaxed atmosphere.

restaurant.name: Subway

restaurant.name: White Lotus Cafe
restaurant.desc: White Lotus Cafe is an authentic Vietnamese restaurant in North Burnaby serving pho, Bún Bò Huế, bánh mì made with daily-baked bread, and fresh salad rolls. The cafe offers dine-in with reservations, online takeout ordering, full catering services, and private event packages. Customer reviews consistently single out the Spicy Beef & Pork Noodle Soup as among the best in the greater Vancouver area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels a Vegetarian (VG) Banh Mi with fried tofu and vegetarian 'ham' (excludes pate)

restaurant.name: Caffè Artigiano
restaurant.desc: Caffè Artigiano is a pioneering Vancouver specialty coffee brand with over 25 years of history and international barista competition recognition, known for award-winning latte art and its own Burnaby roastery producing 100% Arabica blends. This West Pender Street location is one of 25-plus cafes across BC and Alberta, serving specialty coffees, house-made baked goods, and artisanal food made from organic and seasonal ingredients with no artificial additives. The brand has recently expanded into cocktail-serving Cafe-Bars, making it a stop suited to cyclists looking for a quality sit-down coffee or a light meal.

restaurant.name: Kaide Sushi Bar

Its central Vancouver location could make it a convenient meal stop for urban cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Patrón Tacos & Cantina

restaurant.name: Gotham Steakhouse & Bar
restaurant.desc: Gotham Steakhouse is a long-established downtown Vancouver institution, celebrating 25 years as of 2024, housed in an opulent art deco dining room of mahogany and soaring windows. The kitchen serves exclusively Canada Prime grade beef alongside fresh seafood, hand-crafted cocktails, and a deep award-winning wine cellar. Private dining rooms — the Club Room (up to 32 guests) and the intimate Boardroom (up to 20) — make it a destination for group dining as well as solo indulgence.

restaurant.name: BridgeDeck Kitchen & Taps
restaurant.desc: BridgeDeck Kitchen & Taps is the Lonsdale Avenue restaurant and taproom of North Vancouver's Bridge Brewing Co., pairing the brewery's full craft beer lineup with a food menu in a full-service sit-down setting. Located on a main North Shore cycling artery, it offers both indoor and outdoor seating. It is one of three Bridge Brewing locations on the North Shore.

restaurant.name: Kimu Japanese Cuisine

restaurant.name: Flavours of India

restaurant.name: Nook
restaurant.desc: Nook is a Vancouver-born Italian restaurant group that opened its first location in the West End in 2009, now with five Nook locations across Metro Vancouver plus sister restaurants Oddfish and Radish. The Coal Harbour location on Melville Street serves housemade pasta, wood-fired-style pizzas, and antipasto using locally sourced ingredients alongside imported Italian products. It's a casual neighbourhood spot with daily pizza and pasta specials, making it a solid sit-down refuelling stop for cyclists in the Coal Harbour area.

restaurant.name: Chef Tony Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Chef Tony Seafood Restaurant is an award-winning upscale Cantonese dining destination in Richmond's Imperial Centre, recognized with multiple Gold wins for Best Chinese and Best Dim Sum by local dining guides. The menu showcases premium ingredients including black truffle, fresh abalone, BC sea cucumber, and wagyu beef alongside an extensive specialty dim sum selection. The restaurant features a large banquet hall and four private VIP dining rooms, making it a destination for celebratory meals rather than a quick cyclist pit stop.

restaurant.name: The Cordova Room
restaurant.desc: The Cordova Room is an intimate whiskey and cocktail bar tucked into the heart of Gastown, featuring dark green walls, warm wood, and golden accents. It specializes in scratch-made cocktails and a curated selection of rare single malts, paired with refined small bites. Located on Carrall Street in one of Vancouver's most historically rich and cycle-friendly neighbourhoods, it makes a distinctive evening stop for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Browns Socialhouse
restaurant.desc: Browns Socialhouse Tofino is a casual full-service chain restaurant located within the Best Western Tin Wis Resort on the Pacific Rim Highway, serving regional and American cuisine. Part of the Browns Restaurant Group with dozens of locations across BC and Alberta, the Tofino outpost sits on the main highway corridor into town, making it a natural stop for cyclists arriving or departing the area. The restaurant acknowledges it rests on the ancestral and traditional lands of the Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation.

restaurant.name: Lin Chinese Cuisine And Tea House
restaurant.desc: Lin Chinese Cuisine is an award-winning Shanghainese restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver, known for dishes like Xiao Long Bao (Shanghai juicy pork dumplings), Tea Smoked Duck, and Honey Prawns. The restaurant offers both dine-in and online ordering, and a gluten-free menu is available on request. A touring cyclist heading along the Broadway corridor would find a full sit-down meal experience with a wide range of classic and regional Chinese dishes.

restaurant.name: Gong Cha

The Langley Willoughby location sits in a retail unit at 8045 204 Street, making it a handy refreshment stop for cyclists passing through the Willoughby area. With a takeout-focused model, orders are quick and portable.

restaurant.name: Cafe Bella Bean

restaurant.name: Panago
restaurant.desc: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain franchise in Tsawwassen offering delivery and takeout. The chain emphasizes Canadian-sourced ingredients including 100% Canadian wheat dough made fresh in-house, organic tomato sauce, and meats raised without antibiotics. Touring cyclists will find a range of pizzas, salads, and plant-based options available for quick pickup.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We've got abundant veggie, dairy-free and meat-free choices to help you live your best plant life.'

restaurant.name: Afghani Kabul Kebab Donair
restaurant.desc: Afghani Kabul Kebab Donair is an Afghan restaurant on Robson Street in Vancouver's West End, serving kabobs, kebabs, and donairs. It sits on one of Vancouver's busiest pedestrian and cycling corridors, with both indoor and outdoor seating. Vegetarian options are available, making it a flexible stop for mixed cycling groups.

restaurant.name: Kappa Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A tiny, family-run Japanese restaurant that has been serving authentic food in White Rock for over 40 years, founded by Yoshi and Michiko in 1982. The menu spans nigiri, aburi sushi, sashimi, rolls, and full dinner entrees, served in a fully licensed dine-in setting with takeout also available. The restaurant is notably sustainability-minded, partnering with ChopValue to recycle used chopsticks into furniture and home goods.

restaurant.name: Mix the Bakery
restaurant.desc: Mix the Bakery is an award-winning artisan bakery and neighbourhood café located in Vancouver's West Point Grey, operating since 2003. It produces handmade, preservative-free breads using a 100-year-old natural yeast starter alongside freshly made coffee, handcrafted sandwiches, and soups. The bakery supplies bread to several of Vancouver's top-rated restaurants and offers catering and wholesale services alongside its walk-in café.

restaurant.name: Pearl Fever Tea House
restaurant.desc: Pearl Fever Tea House is a bubble tea chain rooted in the lower mainland since 2002, now operating six locations dedicated to handcrafted Asian tea drinks. The Coquitlam-origin brand emphasizes consistency and customization across its menu of taro, matcha, mango, and other specialty drinks. A touring cyclist stopping in would find a quick, refreshing drink stop — particularly appealing on warm-weather routes through the Fraser Valley corridor.

restaurant.name: Thai Son
restaurant.desc: Thai Son offers authentic Vietnamese cuisine with dine-in and takeout service across multiple Vancouver locations. The East Broadway branch provides casual dining suitable for touring cyclists passing through the neighborhood.

restaurant.name: Eagles Nest Pub
restaurant.desc: The Eagle's Nest Pub is a full-service waterfront pub on the second floor of the marina building at Island West Resort, with sweeping views over Ucluelet Harbour and the working fishing dock below. With over 100 seats plus a patio, it serves scratch soups, salads, and hand-cut-fry burgers alongside pool tables and big-screen TVs. It sits at the centre of the resort complex, walkable to the campground, motel, and Ucluelet town centre—making it a natural end-of-ride stop for cyclists touring the Pacific Rim.

restaurant.name: Anna's Cake House
restaurant.desc: Anna's Cake House is a family-owned Hong Kong-style bakery founded in 1974 by Anna, Ronald, and Kathleen Cheung, now celebrating 50 years as a community institution in Greater Vancouver. The Oakridge location on Cambie Street is one of four outlets across the region, offering made-to-order fresh cakes and classic Hong Kong-style buns baked daily with Canadian butter and cream and no artificial additives. Cyclists passing through the Cambie corridor will find a well-loved neighbourhood stop for a sweet, freshly baked treat.

restaurant.name: Vegan Shoku Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Vegan Shoku is a fully plant-based Japanese restaurant on West 41st Avenue in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, offering an extensive menu of sushi rolls, ramen, udon, donburi, and creative vegan interpretations of Japanese seafood dishes. Every item on the menu is vegan, making it a reliable stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions. The restaurant offers dine-in and takeout, with online ordering available through their POS portal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Entire menu on website is plant-based (vegan Japanese cuisine including vegan salmon, vegan shrimp, vegan crab, etc.)

restaurant.name: Chez Christophe
restaurant.desc: Chez Christophe is a Swiss-inspired chocolaterie and patisserie founded in 2013 by Swiss-trained pastry chef Christophe Bonzon, operating its original flagship in Burnaby Heights on Hastings Street. The café serves espresso beverages made with locally roasted beans from Pallet Coffee Roasters alongside freshly baked croissants, cakes, tarts, macarons, and handcrafted artisan chocolates. A touring cyclist passing through Burnaby Heights will find it a high-quality stop for a specialty coffee and house-made pastry.

restaurant.name: Kissa Tanto
restaurant.desc: Kissa Tanto is an intimate Japanese-Italian fusion restaurant occupying the upper floor of a heritage building in Vancouver's Chinatown, blending the delicate flavours of Japan with the warmth of Italian cooking. The menu features dishes like charcoal udon with dungeness crab, yuzu tagliatelle with hand-cut Wagyu, and elegant crudos, alongside sake, Barolo, and classic cocktails. The room is deliberately small — a single large table seating a maximum of six — making it a memorable destination for cyclists seeking a special post-ride dinner in a historic neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Stinky's on the Stroll
restaurant.desc: Stinky's on the Stroll is a legendary neighborhood pub on Whistler's Village Stroll, conceived by long-time local Jeremy 'Stinky' Peterson as a community gathering place and love letter to the town. Repeatedly voted Locals' Favourite Hangout in Best of Whistler polls, it doubles as a living museum of Whistler sports and music memorabilia. The kitchen focuses on inventive sandwiches and comfort food alongside craft beers, local brews, and cocktails.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About-us page explicitly names vegetarian choices including a veggie sub with roasted sweet potato, arugula, and house-made pineapple chutney; menu lists The Veggie flatbread/pizza and vegetable taco option

restaurant.name: Notti Biscotti
restaurant.desc: Notti Biscotti is a South Surrey artisan bakery and café founded by Shelley Quesnel, specializing in over twenty flavours of thick, chocolate-based Italian biscotti made with all-natural, preservative-free ingredients. Located at Morgan Creek Corporate Centre, the café also serves muffins, scones, Notti Squares, brownies, and a fresh lunch menu including soups. The business won the Surrey Board of Trade Business Excellence Award in 2007 and has expanded to over 50 retail outlets across the region.

restaurant.name: Pho 37 Vietnamese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Pho 37 is a multi-location Vietnamese restaurant chain that started in Steveston and expanded to Robson Street in Vancouver, serving freshly made pho, vermicelli bowls, and traditional Vietnamese appetizers. The brand has earned recognition including a Canadian Choice Award for Vietnamese Restaurant and Yelp Elites Top Places to Eat, and promotes MSG-free cooking with ingredients prepared daily in each location. Touring cyclists on Robson Street will find a full sit-down dining room with takeout and delivery options available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists vegetarian options including 'Spring Rolls (3) Regular / Vegetarian', 'Salad Roll (1) Shrimp / Tofu', 'Vegetables and Tofu Noodle', and vermicelli bowls with vegetarian choice

restaurant.name: Blend Bites
restaurant.desc: Blend Bites is a quick-service cafe in West Kelowna offering bubble tea, smoothies, and sandwiches. The shop operates an online ordering portal through Clover, making it easy for cyclists to pre-order before arriving. It sits in a commercial unit on Dobbin Road, a corridor with several shops and services.

restaurant.name: Desi Indian Lounge
restaurant.desc: Desi Indian Lounge is a modern fine-dining Indian restaurant on Hornby Street in downtown Vancouver, blending traditional regional recipes with elegant lounge-style presentation and a full cocktail bar featuring Indian-inspired drinks. The menu spans tandoori platters, slow-cooked curries, and a wide range of vegetarian options, with several gluten-free and dairy-free items. The restaurant participates in Dine Out Vancouver and offers catering for private and corporate events.

restaurant.name: Benanna Bakery Inc
restaurant.desc: Benanna Bakery is a quaint, artisanal European-inspired bakery in Chilliwack that has been baking from scratch since 2012. They are known for sourdoughs made with 16+ hour fermentation, traditional European pastries and cakes, and custom celebration cakes using locally sourced ingredients. A touring cyclist stopping here would find freshly baked breads and pastries made daily in-shop — a solid resupply for energy on the road.

restaurant.name: Chicha San Chen
restaurant.desc: Chicha San Chen is a bubble tea cafe chain location. It offers indoor seating and takeaway service, providing cyclists with a spot to grab a beverage during a ride.

restaurant.name: The Sunflower Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Sunflower Café is a beloved Crescent Beach institution serving wholesome breakfast and lunch for over 20 years, with everything made in-house from whole ingredients including freshly baked multigrain sourdough. Its garden patio welcomes guests and their pets on sunny days, while the interior features rotating local artwork and comfortable seating. A stocked freezer of take-home soups and prepared meals offers a practical resupply option for cyclists passing through the White Rock and Crescent Beach area.

restaurant.name: Deadbeetz Burgers
restaurant.desc: Deadbeetz Burgers is a locally focused fast-food burger spot on Oak Bay Avenue in Victoria, built around house-made ingredients like pickled beets, dill pickles, and a signature Vancouver Island sauce. The menu spans beef, breaded chicken, grilled Alaskan salmon, and fully plant-based patties, making it one of the more diverse quick-service stops in the neighbourhood. Online ordering with pickup is available, and a small dessert and drinks menu rounds out the offering for a full refuelling stop.

restaurant.name: Sushi California

restaurant.name: Nook

The group also operates sister restaurants Oddfish and Radish, giving the neighbourhood a cluster of casual dining options.

restaurant.name: Dae Bak Bon Ga
restaurant.desc: Dae Bak Bon Ga is a long-running Korean BBQ restaurant on Vancouver's busy Robson Street, serving both à la carte and all-you-can-eat BBQ menus with over 140 seats for small and large groups. The restaurant has operated for more than 20 years and also features eight private karaoke rooms available for booking. It is located on the second floor (unit 201) of its building, presented by Mirak Foods Ltd.

restaurant.name: Paris Baguette
restaurant.desc: Paris Baguette is a Korean-origin international bakery café chain known for freshly baked pastries, custom celebration cakes, and café beverages. The Alberni Street location sits in Vancouver's dense West End neighbourhood, a short ride from Stanley Park and the seawall cycling routes. Cyclists will find a broad grab-and-go selection of sandwiches, wraps, donuts, and sweet pastries alongside hot and iced drinks.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes numerous vegetarian-suitable items (cakes, pastries, donuts, salads, wraps). No vegan or GF claims confirmed

restaurant.name: The Golden Horn Turkish Bakery & Cafe

The Cambie location is described as a comfortable space to relax, socialize, or study, and also offers heartier dishes like iskender platters and wraps (durums) that can make for a substantial mid-ride meal. The business operates a second location at Canada Place on the seawall, which offers harbour and mountain views.

restaurant.name: Blackfish Pub
restaurant.desc: Blackfish Pub is a neighbourhood pub in Gibsons on British Columbia's Sunshine Coast, positioned as a casual local gathering spot with a seasonal menu of food and drink. The tagline 'Winter's fading, good times are growing' and a call for groups to reserve ahead suggest a lively, community-oriented atmosphere. For touring cyclists completing the ferry crossing to the Sunshine Coast, it offers a sit-down meal and drinks right in Gibsons.

restaurant.name: Burger Crush
restaurant.desc: Burger Crush is a BC-born fast-casual chain reviving the classic burger shop with smashed Canadian Angus beef burgers, vegan and veggie alternatives, hand-dipped shakes, and loaded fries. This Colwood location sits on Sooke Road, positioning it as a convenient refueling stop for cyclists heading out toward the West Shore and beyond. The menu skews inclusive, with house-made vegan patties, tofu nuggets, and dairy-free shakes alongside the beef options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Vegan Cheeseburger (vegan bun, crush-made vegan patty, vegan cheese), 'Veggie Style' Cheeseburger (crush-made vegan patty with dairy cheese), Vegan Nuggets (house-made tofu), vegan dips, and Vegan Shakes made with Nora's cashew & coconut milk ice cream

restaurant.name: BBQ King Delight
restaurant.desc: BBQ King Delight is a Cantonese-style roasted meat shop in Surrey specializing in Hong Kong BBQ classics: roasted duck, honey BBQ pork, soy sauce chicken, and crispy roasted pork, sold by weight or as rice bento boxes. Online ordering with a 15-minute pickup window makes it a fast, no-fuss stop. The menu skews heavily toward roasted and marinated meats, with canned soft drinks rounding out the offerings.

detail.address: 8973 152 St, Unit A, Surrey, BC V3R4E5

notes.Takeout: Website shows 'Order Online' and 'Pickup 15 min' with a full cart/checkout flow; pickup is the only fulfillment method listed

restaurant.name: Domino's
restaurant.desc: Domino's is a national pizza chain franchise located on Highway 97 N in Lake Country, sitting directly on the main Okanagan cycling corridor between Kelowna and Vernon. The store offers both delivery and carryout, with a full menu of pizzas, sides, and desserts. For touring cyclists rolling through the Okanagan, it is a reliable and accessible option for a quick hot meal.

detail.address: 10051 Highway 97 N Unit 2, Lake Country, BC V4V 1P6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website coupon page lists 'Veggie' pizza as a named specialty ('Including our Deluxe, Pepperoni Feast, Veggie, Hawaiian Feast & Brooklyn Style Pizza')

restaurant.name: Mazaj Best Donair
restaurant.desc: Mazaj Best Donair is a Middle Eastern restaurant in Langley specializing in donairs, a beloved street-food staple in BC. Located in a strip-mall unit on 210 Street, it offers the kind of hearty, affordable fare that hungry touring cyclists gravitate toward after a long day in the saddle.

restaurant.name: Bellaggio Café
restaurant.desc: Bellaggio Café is an owner-operated Italian restaurant in the heart of downtown Vancouver, steps from the Vancouver Art Gallery and Pacific Centre. Owners Barbara and Emil offer an authentic Italian menu featuring wood stone oven pizza, with full bar service and the ability to host groups up to 120 guests on the patio or indoors. Its central Hornby Street location makes it a natural stop on any urban cycling route through the downtown core.

restaurant.name: Theo's Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Theo's Restaurant is a Penticton landmark that has been serving authentic Greek cuisine since 1976, earning a reputation as the Okanagan's award-winning Greek dining destination. The menu is made entirely from scratch in-house — including soups, dips, phyllo pies, and desserts — with ingredients sourced from Okanagan farms and paired with regional wines. A touring cyclist rolling into Penticton will find generous portions, a warm and storied atmosphere, and a kitchen that accommodates a broad range of dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About-us page states: 'We are also proud to offer a wide selection of GF and Vegan dishes—including a dedicated GF and Vegan dessert.' Menu page labels items with Gluten and Vegan indicators and notes all salads are gluten-free

restaurant.name: VanLove Sushi
restaurant.desc: VanLove Sushi is a sushi and coffee restaurant on Robson Street near Stanley Park, founded by Ukrainian immigrants who bring a Ukrainian twist to sushi, mojitos, and desserts. The welcoming, owner-operated story sets it apart from typical sushi chains, and its patio and proximity to the Stanley Park cycling loop make it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the area.

restaurant.name: Spicy 6
restaurant.desc: Spicy 6 Fine Indian Cuisine is a long-standing North Indian restaurant on Vancouver's busy Robson Street, established in 2012 and now operated by the Bassi family alongside Chef Ram, who brings a fine-dining background from India. The restaurant offers dine-in, pickup, and delivery, with a fully licensed bar and a weekday lunch buffet. Its central downtown location makes it a convenient stop for cyclists touring the West End or Stanley Park area.

restaurant.name: Royal Taj Cusine
restaurant.desc: Indian restaurant with bar service in Tsawwassen offering dine-in and takeaway. Provides a convenient dining option for touring cyclists seeking south Asian cuisine in the area.

restaurant.name: Himalayan Momo Restaurant and Bar
restaurant.desc: Himalayan Momo Restaurant and Bar is a Nepali restaurant in downtown Vancouver specializing in handcrafted momos — Nepalese-style dumplings — alongside a broad menu of Himalayan, Indian, and Chinese dishes including tandoori chicken, biryanis, and traditional items like Sukuti (dried buffalo meat) and Jhol MoMo soup. The restaurant brings age-old Himalayan recipes made with locally sourced ingredients to the heart of the city, with full bar service and a warm, vibrant dining room. Touring cyclists passing through downtown Vancouver will find an extensive menu with dedicated vegetarian sections and the option to order online for takeout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu has dedicated 'Veg Appetizers,' 'Veg Curries,' and 'Veg Foods' categories with multiple dishes (Chana Masala, Dal Makhani, Himalayan Aloo Gobi, Kadhai Paneer, etc.). No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: MAiiZ Tortilleria & Eatery
restaurant.desc: MAiiZ Tortilleria & Eatery is a Victoria restaurant and tortilleria founded by Chef Israel Alvarez Molina, formerly of the celebrated Pujol in Mexico City, who revived the traditional Mesoamerican Nixtamal process using certified organic corn grown in Armstrong, BC. The result is a menu of tacos, quesadillas, tamales, pozole, and chilaquiles built on fresh masa tortillas with a flavour and texture rarely found outside Mexico. The restaurant has earned multiple awards including YAM Producer of the Year 2022 and Tasting Victoria People's Choice for Favourite Artisanal Food or Beverage Product.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian options: Mushroom Tacos, Grilled Cactus Tacos, Huitlacoche Tacos, Cheese Quesadilla, Mushrooms Quesadilla, Grilled Cactus Pozole, and several vegetarian tamales. Corn-based nixtamal tortillas are naturally gluten-free though no explicit GF claim is made

restaurant.name: Ding Tea
restaurant.desc: A bubble tea cafe in Victoria offering takeout and delivery service. Part of the Ding Tea chain, this location provides a convenient stop for cyclists seeking a beverage.

restaurant.name: Oshi Nori
restaurant.desc: Oshi Nori is a fast-casual sushi bar in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood offering an omakase-style hand roll experience at an open counter, where guests watch chefs craft each roll to order. The restaurant draws on the Osaka tradition of oshi-pressed sushi while emphasizing sustainably-sourced ingredients and a contemporary atmosphere. It serves both dine-in and takeout, making it a compact urban stop for cyclists passing through the downtown core.

restaurant.name: Pallet Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Pallet Coffee Roasters is a community-minded Vancouver specialty coffee roastery established in East Vancouver in 2014, now operating eight cafes across Metro Vancouver including this Broadway location. The company roasts its own beans and serves coffee alongside food and freshly baked goods, with both indoor and outdoor seating available. As a full-service roastery and cafe operator, it offers a welcoming stop with a strong local identity for cyclists passing through the Broadway corridor.

restaurant.name: Jaipur Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Jaipur Indian Restaurant is an Indian restaurant situated on Scott Road in Surrey, BC. It takes its name from the city of Jaipur in Rajasthan, India. No further details about its menu, atmosphere, or facilities are available from accessible sources.

restaurant.name: Chén
restaurant.desc: Chén is a Vietnamese restaurant located on Hastings Street in Burnaby, BC. The name 'Chén' (meaning 'bowl' in Vietnamese) suggests a focus on bowl-based Vietnamese dishes. It sits along a commercial stretch of Hastings that touring cyclists riding through Burnaby would pass.

restaurant.name: Highwayman Pub
restaurant.desc: The Highwayman Pub is a community-oriented neighbourhood pub in Abbotsford operated by the Otter Co-op, whose motto is 'Where Friends Meet.' It boasts 19 TVs including an HD projector streaming UFC, NHL, NFL, and CFL, two pool tables, a jukebox, and a dog-friendly patio that is the only location in BC with an outdoor Keno TV. The pub regularly hosts trivia nights, game nights, fundraisers, and other community events, making it a lively stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu subpage uses explicit 'Vegetarian', 'Vegan', and 'Gluten Friendly' labels on menu items

restaurant.name: The Landlubber Pub
restaurant.desc: The Landlubber Pub is a family-owned neighbourhood pub in Nanaimo's Beban Plaza with nearly 30 years of history serving a wide-ranging local clientele. It is known for wing night four nights a week with over 30 flavours, homemade comfort food, and a lively entertainment calendar including karaoke, music trivia, poker nights, and open mic sessions. Located at the corner of Bowen and Northfield roads, it sits on two bus routes and draws everyone from post-work regulars to weekend brunch crowds.

restaurant.name: Spice Cart Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Spice Cart Indian Cuisine is an authentic Indian restaurant in Port Coquitlam specializing in fresh curries, tandoori dishes, and biryani made with traditional spices and high-quality ingredients. The menu features both meat and vegetarian options prepared with time-tested cooking methods. Cyclists can dine in or order for pickup, with delivery also available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Paneer Butter Masala described as 'Homemade cheese cooked with ginger, garlic in a tomato based butter sauce' — a vegetarian dish. No vegan or GF claims confirmed

restaurant.name: The Pony Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Pony is an OSM-tagged cafe located in Pemberton, BC, a small mountain community north of Whistler along the Duffy Lake Road corridor. No verified website content is available to describe the business further, as the listed domain has been squatted by an unrelated content site.

restaurant.name: Farmhouse Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Davison Farmhouse Café occupies the original 1946 farmhouse on a working fifth-generation orchard property in Vernon's Okanagan Valley, offering farm-to-table breakfasts and lunches where many ingredients are grown steps away. The café is known for house-made pies, freshly crafted lattes, and seasonal baked goods, with indoor seating and patios overlooking the orchards. It is part of Davison Orchards, a family farm operating since 1933 that also runs U-pick experiences and guided orchard tours — a genuinely distinctive stop in the Okanagan.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ explicitly confirms gluten-free options: 'We usually offer Tomato Herb Soup daily as a gluten-free choice, along with other menu items. Most beverages, including our Apple Juice and Applelanches, are gluten-free.' Menu also includes vegetarian items (Double Grilled Cheese, Egg Salad Croissant, soups)

restaurant.name: Austin Fish & Chips
restaurant.desc: A fast-food fish and chips shop on Lougheed Highway in Pitt Meadows. Offers quick takeout meals suitable as a convenient food break for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Oyster Express
restaurant.desc: Oyster Express (OX) is a small, intimate oyster bar in Vancouver's historic Chinatown neighbourhood, specialising in freshly shucked, locally sourced British Columbia oysters served in a characterful atmosphere. It opened in 2012 and earned a wave of media coverage from the Vancouver Sun, Scout Magazine, cityfood, and several other local outlets. Touring cyclists riding through Chinatown would find a casual neighbourhood spot focused on Pacific oysters.

restaurant.name: Golden Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Golden Seafood Restaurant (金福源) is a Chinese dim sum and seafood restaurant on Nanaimo Street in East Vancouver, serving traditional dim sum alongside dinner specialties including Peking duck. The restaurant offers both dine-in and takeout options, including party trays suited for groups, making it a practical food stop for cyclists passing through the neighbourhood. OSM notes limited wheelchair accessibility on site.

restaurant.name: Osteria Otto
restaurant.desc: Osteria Otto is a dinner-focused Italian restaurant on East 8th Avenue in Vancouver that merges seasonal Italian cooking and Pacific Northwest produce with the intimate atmosphere of a Japanese kissa listening bar, complete with curated vinyl and hi-fi sound. The menu leans into ingredient-forward, sharing-style dishes that reflect both Italian culinary clarity and the West Coast landscape. A touring cyclist looking for a full sit-down evening meal in a warm, unhurried setting will find it a distinctive stop.

restaurant.name: ChiuChow Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: ChiuChow Seafood Restaurant is a Chiu Chow (Teochew)-style Chinese restaurant specializing in dim sum and seafood, situated on the second floor of a building near Vancouver General Hospital in the Cambie corridor. The menu spans handmade dumplings, fresh seafood congee, and traditional slow-marinated meats including goose and duck — hallmarks of the Chiu Chow culinary tradition rarely found outside of specialist restaurants. Online table booking and ordering are available through the restaurant's dedicated ordering platform.

restaurant.name: Wendy's
restaurant.desc: Wendy's is a national fast food chain located on Alaska Road in Fort St. John, a key service community along the Alaska Highway corridor in northeastern BC. The location offers burgers, chicken sandwiches, chili, and Frosty desserts, with drive-through and takeout options that accommodate cyclists who may not want to leave loaded bikes unattended. For touring cyclists on the Alaska Highway route, this is one of the more reliably open food stops in the area.

detail.address: 9827 Alaska Road, Fort St. John, V1J 1A6

restaurant.name: Steve's Poke Bar
restaurant.desc: Steve's Poké Bar is an authentic Hawaiian poke chain founded in 2017 by Steve Huynh, who grew up splitting time between Vancouver and Honolulu and learned traditional poke preparation from family recipes. Unlike fusion-style competitors, the restaurant marinates fish the way it's done in Hawaii and has accumulated over 10,000 five-star Google reviews across its Lower Mainland locations. Touring cyclists can build their own bowls or choose from signature options including tuna, salmon, scallop, spam, and tofu varieties.

detail.address: 156 3rd St W #1, North Vancouver, BC V7M 1E8, Canada

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: This McDonald's is located in the Woodgrove area of Nanaimo at 6675 Mary Ellen Drive, serving burgers and a full fast-food menu. The restaurant offers Drive-Thru, Curbside, and McDelivery ordering channels, making it a convenient stop for cyclists who don't want to lock up and head inside. It is part of the McDonald's Canada chain, which first opened in Richmond, BC in 1967.

restaurant.name: GlassHouse
restaurant.desc: GlassHouse is a neighbourhood restaurant in Kitsilano anchored in Pacific Northwest cuisine, drawing on local farms, coastal producers, and changing seasons to build a menu that layers global techniques over thoughtfully sourced ingredients. The kitchen runs an active fermentation program — pickling onions, fennel, preserved lemons, and cucumbers — and operates under a genuine zero-waste philosophy where scraps become stocks and peels become ferments. A dog-friendly patio and a relaxed, unpretentious atmosphere make it a natural mid-ride stop on the West 4th Ave cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Triple O's
restaurant.desc: Triple O's is a BC-born quick-service burger chain with roots going back to White Spot's 1928 origin story, now operating over 70 locations across Canada and Asia. The Richmond location sits on Number 3 Road and offers the chain's signature fresh Canadian beef burgers, hand-scooped milkshakes, and Kennebec fries. Takeout and delivery are available, making it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists passing through Richmond's commercial corridor.

restaurant.name: Mountain Burger House
restaurant.desc: Mountain Burger House is a classic downtown Squamish diner on Cleveland Ave, positioned directly off Highway 99 and well-placed for cyclists traveling the Sea-to-Sky corridor. It serves a broad all-day breakfast menu spanning bacon-and-eggs, skillets, omelets, and fresh-baked pastries, alongside burgers and lunch specials. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and a Friday evening buffet gives it a distinct local character.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Veggie Omelet, Vegetarian Skillet, Vegetable Quiche, and Granola & Yogurt

restaurant.name: Coast Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Coast Restaurant is an upscale seafood destination in downtown Vancouver operated by the Glowbal Restaurant Group, celebrated for its raw bar, elaborate seafood towers, and award-winning sushi program. Seasonal highlights such as a spot prawn menu and omakase evenings with Chef Henry Kim reflect a strong commitment to locally sourced, ocean-to-table ingredients. A touring cyclist finishing a day on the seawall or arriving from the North Shore would find this a premium splurge stop a short roll from the waterfront.

notes.Takeout: Website lists a 'DELIVERY' nav item and explicitly offers 'PREMIUM SUSHI BOX | PICKUP ONLY | SERVES 4-6', confirming pickup/takeout is available

restaurant.name: Miku Richmond
restaurant.desc: Miku Richmond is an upscale Japanese restaurant specializing in Aburi cuisine — traditional sushi elevated with contemporary sauces and live-flame searing — located on the third level of River Rock Casino Resort along the Fraser River waterfront. Part of the award-winning Miku group that has pioneered Aburi cuisine in North America since 2008, the Richmond location emphasizes locally sourced B.C. produce alongside fine Japanese ingredients and a private dining program. It opened in early 2026 as Miku's newest outpost.

restaurant.name: The Doghouse
restaurant.desc: A Cowichan Valley institution since 1954, the Doghouse Family Restaurant is a sprawling highway diner on the Trans-Canada serving homestyle breakfasts, hearty dinners, and award-winning pies and desserts. The menu spans everything from Logger's Breakfasts and Prime Rib nights to a full kids menu, making it a welcoming stop for groups of all sizes. Touring cyclists riding through Duncan will find generous portions and a classic Canadian roadside-diner atmosphere.

detail.address: 271 Trans Canada Hwy, Duncan BC V9L 3R1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dinner menu lists a dedicated 'Veggie' omelette (tomato, mushrooms, green onions, green peppers) and notes egg-white substitution available in omelettes

restaurant.name: Canadian Brewhouse & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Canadian Brewhouse & Grill is a large, nationally-franchised sports bar and grill located in the Uptown shopping centre area of Victoria. It offers a broad pub menu including daily specials, happy hour, and a kids menu, with online ordering available. Touring cyclists stopping in the Uptown corridor will find a spacious, family-friendly venue open through late evening.

restaurant.name: Elevated Pizza Co
restaurant.desc: Elevated Pizza Co is an artisan pizza shop situated inside the District 1881 development in Chilliwack, offering 12" and 16" pies, panuozzo sandwiches, focaccia bites, and drinks. The menu leans toward elevated ingredients — nduja sausage, goat cheese, smoked scamorza, balsamic reduction — making it a step above typical fast-food pizza. Online ordering supports both pickup and delivery, and the shop operates seven days a week.

detail.address: 103-9235 Sasquatch Alley, Chilliwack, British Columbia V2P 0J6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian pizzas: Margherita (tomato, fresh mozzarella, basil), Cheese, Arugula (goat cheese, antipasto spread), and White Pie (ricotta, mozzarella, hot honey). No explicit vegan or GF labeling found

restaurant.name: Ça Marche
restaurant.desc: Ça Marche is a fast-food creperie specializing in savory and sweet crepes. Located on Continental Street in Vancouver, it offers quick, casual dining suitable for cyclists seeking a quick meal stop. No drive-through service.

restaurant.name: Elysian Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Elysian Coffee Roasters is a Vancouver-based specialty coffee company that sources, roasts, and serves its own beans across four neighbourhood cafés. The Mount Pleasant location at 7th & Ontario sits in a cycling-friendly district and offers both indoor and outdoor seating in a wheelchair-accessible space. The roastery's founding philosophy — consistently good coffee made by happy, well-led staff — has expanded into a subscription service and online shop alongside the in-person café experience.

restaurant.name: Super India Sweets & Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Super India Sweets & Restaurant is an Abbotsford establishment specializing in traditional Punjabi recipes prepared with carefully sourced spices. The menu spans a wide range of vegetarian and non-vegetarian North Indian fare, from tandoori grills and biryanis to street-food classics like gol gappe and chaat papri. In addition to dine-in and online ordering, the restaurant offers large-scale catering for events including weddings and corporate gatherings.

detail.address: 32883 South Fraser Way #105, Abbotsford, BC V2S 2A6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes numerous vegetarian items: Veggie Wrap, Paneer Tikka, Veg Pakoras, Vegetable Samosa, Veg Manchurian, Vegetable Biryani, Aloo Tikki, Chana Puri, and more

restaurant.name: Frick & Frack Tap House
restaurant.desc: Frick & Frack Tap House is a long-established casual dining spot in central Kamloops that has been welcoming guests since 1996. It offers an eclectic menu drawing on international influences — from Swiss schnitzel to Greek-style lamb — alongside an extensive selection of craft beers on tap and wines from around the world. The laid-back, family-friendly atmosphere and full catering service make it a natural gathering point for cycling groups finishing a ride through the heart of BC's interior.

restaurant.name: Green Leaf Bubble Tea
restaurant.desc: Green Leaf Bubble Tea is a bubble tea shop on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most cycling-friendly and culturally vibrant corridors. The Drive is a popular route for cyclists moving between east Vancouver neighbourhoods, making this a natural stop for a cold drink mid-ride. The Instagram handle @greenleafbubbletea.yvr suggests an active social presence, though no further detail was accessible without login.

restaurant.name: BarBurrito
restaurant.desc: BarBurrito is Canada's largest burrito chain, proudly Canadian since 2005, with over 385 locations nationwide. This Kelowna outlet sits inside Capri Centre mall and serves fully customizable Mexican-inspired burritos, bowls, tacos, and quesadillas built from fresh, in-house ingredients. A touring cyclist can quickly assemble a filling, high-calorie meal with a wide range of proteins and dietary options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Nutrition calculator lists 'Veggie' and 'Falafel' protein options and a 'Gluten Free' tortilla option across multiple menu categories

restaurant.name: Fast Fired
restaurant.desc: Fast Fired by Carbone is a BC-based quick-service pizza chain offering fully customizable pizzas with over a million topping combinations, fired fresh to order. The menu spans classic and signature pies, pastas, paninis, salads, calzones, and wings, with a strong selection of vegan and gluten-free options. A rewards program and VIP pizza passes make it a practical stop for cyclists looking for a filling, affordable meal.

notes.Takeout: Rewards page states 'Dine-in & pickup only – No delivery,' confirming pickup/takeout is available
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms gluten-free dough (vegan), Daiya vegan cheese, and all dough types are vegan. Menu includes a dedicated Vegan Pizzas section

restaurant.name: Melo Patisserie
restaurant.desc: Melo Patisserie is a French-style patisserie in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood specialising in handcrafted pastries, mini cakes, cookies, and savoury items such as quiches and croissant sandwiches. The business operates on a pre-order pickup model, making it a reliable stop for cyclists who plan ahead and want quality baked goods or a hearty sandwich on the road. The menu includes gluten-free and vegetarian options, adding flexibility for riders with dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian quiche listed explicitly ('Savoury Bacon and Cheese Quiche or Vegetarian'); Lavender Earl Grey Cookie labelled '[Gluten Free]'

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's franchise on King George Boulevard, a major arterial road through Surrey, with a drive-through in addition to standard counter service. The location offers the full McDonald's Canada menu including McCafé beverages, McValue meals, and seasonal limited-time items. Touring cyclists riding through Surrey along King George Boulevard will find this a reliable and familiar stop for food and drinks.

restaurant.name: U Town Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: U Town Hot Pot is a Chinese hot pot restaurant in Richmond, BC, located at 8328 Capstan Way in what appears to be a multi-unit commercial development. Hot pot dining is an interactive communal experience where diners cook meat, vegetables, and other ingredients in a shared simmering broth at the table. Richmond's Capstan Way corridor sits near the Canada Line and is part of a growing mixed-use neighbourhood, making it accessible to cyclists exploring the city's dining scene.

restaurant.name: Harajuku
restaurant.desc: Harajuku Izakaya is an informal Japanese gastropub located in the Royal Bank Building in Whistler Village, serving tapas-style food alongside a sake bar since 2011. The interior is styled after a Japanese village of the early 1900s, with cozy nooks and large booths suited for groups or solo diners. It offers a relaxed sit-down dinner option for cyclists finishing a day in the Whistler corridor.

restaurant.name: Mitchie Matcha
restaurant.desc: Mitchie Matcha is a Vancouver cafe specializing in ceremonial-grade matcha sourced directly from three distinct regions in Japan — Shizuoka, Kagoshima, and Yame — each yielding a different flavour profile from mild and grassy to bold and umami-rich. Located on the Main Street corridor, the cafe also sells retail matcha powder online and can be hired as a drink vendor for private events ranging from small family celebrations to weddings and corporate functions. Cyclists passing through the Main Street neighbourhood will find a focused, specialty-tea experience with a strong direct-trade ethos.

restaurant.name: Neptune Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A Chinese seafood restaurant in North Vancouver providing casual dining. The establishment caters to diners seeking traditional Asian cuisine in a neighborhood setting.

restaurant.name: Petite Bao
restaurant.desc: Petite Bao is a Kitsilano restaurant specializing in Asian-influenced bao burgers made with handmade, daily-fresh bao buns and locally sourced, organic, non-GMO ingredients from BC farmers. The menu spans pork belly, wagyu, B.C. salmon, and several vegetarian/vegan options, alongside sides like poutine and wings. Situated on the West Broadway cycling corridor, it offers dine-in and online ordering with catering available for events.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'IMPOSSIBLE BAO (V)', 'Portobello Bao (V)', and 'THAI BASIL MOZZARELLA SALAD (V) (GF)' — vegetarian and gluten-free options confirmed

restaurant.name: Tableau
restaurant.desc: Tableau Bar Bistro is an award-winning French bistro in Vancouver's Coal Harbour neighbourhood, blending classic French fare with West Coast flavours in a relaxed, inviting atmosphere. The restaurant features main dining, bar, patio seating, and two private dining rooms for larger gatherings. Walk-ins are always welcome, making it an accessible option for cyclists passing through Coal Harbour.

restaurant.name: Green Lake Station
restaurant.desc: Green Lake Station is a combined cafe and Chevron fuel stop near the north end of Whistler, making it a rare spot where both rider and vehicle can refuel in one stop. The kitchen turns out all-day breakfast, pizza, burgers, and paninis, with a menu broad enough to satisfy most dietary needs. Inside, a live-edge wooden communal table and a patio offer comfortable places to linger, and free Wi-Fi with ample outlets make it a practical mid-ride or end-of-day stop.

detail.address: 8110 Crazy Canuck Dr, Whistler, BC V8E 0G8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Vegan Burger, Veggie Burger, Veggie Panini, Smashed Avocado Toast, Margherita and Gardener's pizzas (vegetarian), and a GF pizza crust option
notes.Device charging: Website front page states 'Free wifi and plenty of outlets.'

restaurant.name: Baik Mi Korean Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Baik Mi Korean Restaurant is a Korean eatery on Fraser Highway in Surrey that has been operating since at least 2012, serving dishes including Jjambong (spicy seafood soup), Jjang sauce, and Kkan Pung Gi (fried chicken). Run by operator Moon Young Jang, the restaurant has maintained a current 'Low' hazard rating through regular Fraser Health Authority inspections. A touring cyclist passing through Surrey's commercial strip along Fraser Highway will find a sit-down Korean meal at this long-established local restaurant.

restaurant.name: Tomato's
restaurant.desc: Tomato's is an Indian restaurant in Surrey's Newton neighbourhood serving a broad menu spanning tandoori appetizers, Indo-Chinese dishes, biryanis, and a dedicated vegetarian section. The restaurant offers dine-in with table reservations as well as takeaway and delivery within a 15 km radius. Menu filters for vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, and nut-free options make it accessible to riders with a range of dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian Dishes' category; order filters explicitly list Vegetarian, Vegan, Gluten Free, Dairy Free, and Nut Free options

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A 24/7 McDonald's drive-through and dine-in location in the Kerrisdale neighbourhood of Vancouver, offering the full Canadian McDonald's menu including McCafé beverages. As a round-the-clock fast food stop with drive-through access, it is a reliable resupply point for touring cyclists on long days or early-morning departures. The Kerrisdale location sits near several residential cycling corridors on Vancouver's west side.

restaurant.name: Bearfoot Bistro
restaurant.desc: Bearfoot Bistro is one of British Columbia's most acclaimed fine dining restaurants, operating in Whistler's village core for over 30 years and serving innovative modern Canadian cuisine with ingredients sourced from producers coast to coast. The restaurant is known for its signature champagne sabering tableside, a Grey Goose Vodka Ice Room, and an underground wine cellar that hosts private dinners for groups up to 400 guests. Located inside the Listel Whistler hotel building, it is a destination evening restaurant that a touring cyclist might seek out for a celebratory meal after a long ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Spring 2026 prix fixe menu lists 'Glazed Maitake Mushroom vegan' as a main course option

restaurant.name: Eighties Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Eighties Restaurant is a North Shore landmark that has been serving all-day breakfast and classic diner fare from its North Vancouver location since the 1980s. Helmed by Red Seal chef and James Beard participant Noel Scott — whose training spans Italy, Portugal, and Morocco — the diner is consistently voted the North Shore's top breakfast venue. The cozy space also includes The Green Room, a private section seating up to 50 with a full bar, and the kitchen caters events for up to 100 guests.

restaurant.name: TJ's Country Kitchen
restaurant.desc: TJ's Country Kitchen is a family-owned homestyle diner in Fort St. John run by owner Theresa, who has spent her entire career in the restaurant industry. The menu spans Belgian waffles, Eggs Benny, burgers, sandwiches, soups, and salads — with a reputation for generous portions. The warm, family-first atmosphere has made it a local favourite and a worthwhile stop for cyclists passing through the Peace Region.

detail.address: 10688 Alder Road, Fort St. John, V1J 4J2

restaurant.name: Bubble Queen
restaurant.desc: Bubble Queen is a bubble tea café located in a unit at 8888 Odlin Crescent in Richmond, BC. It offers a range of bubble tea drinks typical of the genre, making it a useful refreshment stop for cyclists riding Richmond's flat, bikeable streets. The café sits in a commercial complex, likely alongside other shops and services.
