restaurant.desc: Tony's Fish & Oyster Café has been a fixture at the entrance of Granville Island since 2002, earning recognition as one of Vancouver's Top 20 Seafood Restaurants and multiple TripAdvisor Certificates of Excellence. The restaurant specializes in battered fish and chips made with wild sockeye salmon, Pacific cod, and Atlantic haddock, alongside house-made clam chowder and a signature banana flambé. It's a walk-in, first-come-first-served spot well-positioned on the cycling routes that converge at Granville Island.

restaurant.name: Ridge Garden
restaurant.desc: Ridge Garden is a Chinese restaurant in Vancouver's Arbutus Ridge neighbourhood, situated near the ICBC office on Macdonald Street. The restaurant offers dine-in service and has recently reopened its dining room, making it a sit-down meal option for cyclists moving through this quieter residential corridor of the city.

restaurant.name: Washington Avenue Grill
restaurant.desc: Washington Avenue Grill is a long-standing White Rock landmark with over 28 years of operation, serving upscale casual Pacific-Northwest cuisine from a dining room overlooking Semiahmoo Bay at the east end of White Rock Beach. The restaurant features an award-winning wine list, weekly live music, and has been recognized as one of Canada's top 100 scenic restaurants. Its location on Marine Drive places it directly on a popular waterfront cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Otreat
restaurant.desc: Otreat is a Korean-influenced brunch cafe tucked into a commercial complex in Langley, serving a creative menu of coffee drinks, mimosa flights, mocktails, and hearty brunch plates alongside dishes like Gochujang Bulgogi wings and chicken benny. The menu is updated regularly and the waitlist feature on the site signals a popular local destination. A touring cyclist stopping here can expect a full sit-down brunch experience with both alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverage options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes vegetarian dishes (deep fried cauliflowers, roasted brussel sprouts) and plant-based milk alternatives (oat, soy, almond milk) for coffee drinks

restaurant.name: Butchers Block BBQ
restaurant.desc: Butchers Block BBQ is a family-owned backyard-style barbecue restaurant in Burnaby Heights, slow-smoking beef brisket, pulled pork, ribs, pork belly, and sausages daily with house-made rubs and sauces. Operating since 2005, it has earned recognition including Vancouver Magazine's 'Best Barbecue' award and multiple 'Best of Burnaby' honours. Cyclists on the Hastings Street corridor can fuel up with generous platters or grab takeout via phone or online order.

restaurant.name: Mogiana Coffee
restaurant.desc: Mogiana Coffee is a family-heritage specialty coffee roaster founded in 2008 by Cristina Dias, sourcing beans directly from her family's farm in the Mogiana region of Brazil — a tradition spanning five generations since the 1890s. The Burnaby roastery sells small-batch, roasted-to-order beans direct to the public and operates a regular circuit of Vancouver-area farmers markets. Cyclists can purchase whole-bean coffee on-site at the roastery, though calling ahead is recommended to ensure staff are available.

restaurant.name: Sunday Cider
restaurant.desc: Sunday Cider is a craft cidery and cider bar on a 20-acre property along the Sunshine Coast Highway near Gibsons, producing small-batch ciders from 100% fresh-pressed BC apples with no added yeast, filtration, or additives. Cyclists can settle into the outdoor picnic area with cider flights, resident food trucks (Sea Monkey Coffee and Casa Beto Tacos), and regular live music on the grass. Dogs and kids on leashes are explicitly welcome, making it a relaxed stop on the Sunshine Coast route.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Yes, it's all gluten free and vegan friendly' for all ciders (/visit page)

restaurant.name: Bow & Stern
restaurant.desc: Bow & Stern is a family-owned, ocean-inspired seafood restaurant founded in 2014 by the Smith family, rooted in a fish-and-chips recipe the founders have been perfecting since 1988. The Abbotsford location on Montrose Ave is the original of three Fraser Valley and Lower Mainland outposts, offering a full sit-down menu of fish, chips, oysters, and ale alongside brunch, happy hour, and dessert menus. Cyclists passing through the Abbotsford area will find online pickup ordering available as well as table reservations.

restaurant.name: Aiyaohno Cafe
restaurant.desc: Aiyaohno Cafe is a Japanese-inspired cafe in Vancouver's Chinatown, run by a husband and wife team who draw from countryside café experiences gathered during travels through Japan. The kitchen focuses on vegetable-forward cuisine with many vegan options and some local wild seafood, paired with matcha imported directly from Kyoto. The space doubles as a small retail hub for pottery, merch, and curated fashion, making it a distinctive neighbourhood stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'healthy vegetable focused cuisine with many vegan options'

restaurant.name: Spinnakers Brewpub
restaurant.desc: Canada's first purpose-built gastro brewpub, Spinnakers has been crafting its own ales and pairing them with farm-to-table cuisine since 1984, drawing on partnerships with over 35 local Vancouver Island producers. Perched on Victoria's Vic West waterfront with views of the Inner Harbour, the site combines a full-service restaurant, taproom, provisions store with growler fills, and heritage guesthouses in a single destination. Cyclists can linger over a range of house-brewed craft beers and seasonal pub fare on a covered heated patio.

restaurant.name: Granville Kebab & Poutine
restaurant.desc: Granville Kebab & Poutine is a Middle Eastern and Mediterranean restaurant on Vancouver's busy Granville Street, blending classic Canadian poutine with grilled beef and chicken kebabs in platters, wraps, and loaded poutine bowls. The fusion concept is a notable curiosity — baklava and kebab skewers share a menu with fries and gravy. Online ordering with a quick pickup window makes it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists moving through the downtown entertainment district.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Veggie Samosa' ($2.99) and 'Large Classic Poutine' ($12.99) as meat-free options; vegan or GF status not stated

restaurant.name: Kojima Sushi
restaurant.desc: Kojima Sushi is a sushi restaurant on Commercial Drive in Vancouver, serving a broad menu of rolls, sashimi, nigiri, oshi sushi, bento combos, and Japanese appetizers. The restaurant is noted for its Salmon Oshi Sushi and creative specialty rolls, and handles a high volume of online orders. Both dine-in and pickup are available through the Zomi platform.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Chef's Veggie Roll (8pcs)' section, 'Vegetarian items' label, Veg Combo A, Vegetable Box, Tofu Teriyaki Box, Agedashi Tofu, Spicy Tofu, Vegetable Gyoza, and Veggie Spring Roll

restaurant.name: Taco Bell
restaurant.desc: A standard Taco Bell franchise location in Delta, BC serving Tex-Mex fast food including tacos, burritos, and the Crunchwrap Supreme. The restaurant offers both dine-in and drive-thru service, as well as online ordering and delivery. It is one of several Taco Bell locations in the Metro Vancouver area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website mentions 'Veggie Cravings Menu has indulgent vegetarian items like the Cheesy Bean and Rice Burrito.'

restaurant.name: Nyonya House Malaysian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Nyonya House is a Malaysian restaurant in Richmond's Steveston area serving a broad menu of Southeast Asian classics including Hainanese Chicken Rice, Curry Laksa, Rendang Beef, Roti Canai, and Satay. The restaurant operates an online ordering system with over 56 menu items spanning appetizers, noodles, rice dishes, and desserts. It is a sit-down restaurant that also supports takeout orders, making it a convenient stop for cyclists exploring the Steveston waterfront area.

restaurant.name: LURE Restaurant & Bar
restaurant.desc: LURE Restaurant & Bar occupies a prime position on Victoria's Inner Harbour, serving a West Coast seasonal menu built around local seafood, Vancouver Island produce, and craft cocktails made with local spirits. The venue offers both indoor dining and an outdoor waterfront patio with panoramic harbour views, and hosts live music on Friday evenings. It draws a broad mix of locals and visitors, making it a natural destination for touring cyclists arriving at or departing from Victoria's waterfront.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu labels vegetarian dishes with (V) (e.g. Lavender Yogurt Parfait, Avocado Toastie, Simple Start) and gluten-free dishes with (GF) (e.g. Open Faced Omelette)

restaurant.name: Cuckoo Trattoria & Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Cuckoo Trattoria & Pizzeria is a full-service Italian restaurant in the small Vancouver Island town of Coombs, led by Italian-born Head Chef Fausto Bellicini who blends traditional Italian technique with local west coast ingredients such as wild-caught salmon, locally sourced mussels, and foraged mushrooms. Wood-fired oven pizza is a centrepiece of the menu, and a forest-facing patio is open through the summer season. Situated on the Alberni Highway, it also functions as an events venue for weddings and larger gatherings.

restaurant.name: Pizza Garden
restaurant.desc: Pizza Garden is a BC-based Neapolitan pizza chain with over 25 years in the industry, serving wood-fired pizzas with authentic charred crusts, san marzano-style tomatoes, and creamy mozzarella. The Abbotsford location at Trethewey Street is one of more than a dozen locations across British Columbia. Cyclists can order ahead via the Pizza Garden app and choose pickup or delivery.

detail.address: 2653 Trethewey Street, Unit 108, Abbotsford, BC V2T 0B5

restaurant.name: S+L Kitchen & Bar
restaurant.desc: S+L Kitchen & Bar is a restaurant in Langley, BC. It provides a dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Shipyards Coffee
restaurant.desc: Shipyards Coffee is an independent coffee bar tucked into the Shipyards District at Lonsdale Quay in North Vancouver, proudly serving the waterfront community for over 15 years. The café offers a full espresso bar, freshly baked croissants and pastries, smoothies, and a rotating selection of specialty single-origin and blended coffee beans. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a welcoming stop along the North Shore waterfront cycling corridor.

detail.address: 123 Carrie Cates Ct #156, North Vancouver, BC V7M 3K7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists oat, soy, almond, and coconut milk alternatives; explicitly includes 'Gluten Free selections of Cookies, Muffins and Bars'

restaurant.name: King Kabob
restaurant.desc: King Kabob is a halal Persian grill restaurant on South Fraser Way in Abbotsford, billing itself as the first dedicated kabob house in the Fraser Valley. The menu centres on flame-broiled kebabs marinated with saffron, dried limes, and traditional Middle Eastern spices, served with basmati rice. The restaurant holds BCMA halal certification and offers both dine-in and online pickup/delivery ordering.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a dedicated 'Veggie Kebab (Vegetarian and Gluten-Friendly)' and multiple entrees labelled 'Gluten-free'; website states 'Our dishes are mostly gluten free.' No vegan claim confirmed

restaurant.name: Domino's
restaurant.desc: Domino's is a national pizza chain franchise offering delivery and carryout from its Nanaimo location on Norwell Drive. The menu covers pizza, wings, pasta, cheesy bread, and desserts, with a gluten-free crust option available. As a takeout-and-delivery-focused operation, it provides no dine-in seating or dedicated cyclist facilities.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Coupons page lists 'Small 2-Topping Gluten Free Pizza'; vegetarian toppings available as standard pizza options (Veggie Feast listed)

restaurant.name: Lac Des Roches Resort & Italian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A full-service lakefront resort and Italian restaurant on Highway 24 (The Fishing Highway) near Lone Butte, BC, open year-round and set on 47 acres beside one of British Columbia's most photographed lakes. The Italian restaurant features northern Italian chefs preparing fresh entrees daily, offering a distinctive sit-down dining option along this rural cycling corridor. The resort is widely known among anglers for trophy Gerrard Rainbow trout fishing, and the surrounding area provides access to over 100 lakes within an hour's drive.

restaurant.name: Bella Gelateria
restaurant.desc: Bella Gelateria is an internationally award-winning artisan gelato maker founded in Vancouver in 2010, recognized at competitions in Italy, Chicago, and Austin, and ranked No. 1 in the Gelato World rankings. The Metrotown Mall location is one of five Greater Vancouver outposts serving handcrafted small-batch gelato made from 100% natural ingredients using Italian Effi machines. Cyclists looking for a sweet mid-ride treat will find a broad menu including dairy-free, gluten-free, and vegan sorbetto options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu page states: 'we have nut-free, gluten-free and dairy-free options' and 'our sorbettos are water-based and vegan friendly.'

restaurant.name: Davie Dosa Company
restaurant.desc: An Indian restaurant specializing in dosas in Richmond. Offers vegetarian and vegan menu options. A casual dining stop for touring cyclists seeking quality Indian cuisine.

restaurant.name: New Mandarin Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: New Mandarin Seafood Restaurant (時代文華海鮮酒家) is a Cantonese seafood and dim sum restaurant located in East Vancouver's Gladstone neighbourhood. The kitchen leans heavily on traditional Hong Kong-style preparations — roasted and hotpot squab, fresh BC crab, whole lobster combos, and a daily dim sum service — earning a local reputation cited on the restaurant's own site. Online ordering and pickup are available, making it a practical meal stop as well as a sit-down destination.

notes.Takeout: Dedicated takeout-specials page (外賣特價) and explicit '15% OFF FOR PICKUP ONLY' promotion; online ordering available at site

restaurant.name: Master Rice Roll
restaurant.desc: Master Rice Roll (腸粉大王) is a Chinese specialty restaurant in Richmond focused on cheung fun (rice rolls) and congee, offering more than 20 varieties of rice roll alone. Located in a retail unit on Number 3 Road, it also serves a range of snacks and drinks. Cyclists passing through Richmond's busy commercial corridor will find it a practical stop for a quick, filling Cantonese meal.

restaurant.name: Orange Julius
restaurant.desc: Orange Julius is a juice beverage chain with a Vancouver location offering fresh juices and casual refreshment. Located in a mall basement, it provides indoor seating and takeout service. A convenient stop for cyclists seeking a quick drink while touring the area.

restaurant.name: The Links Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Links Cafe is a cafe in Richmond offering both indoor and outdoor seating options. The establishment features air-conditioning, providing weather protection for diners. As a casual venue with flexible seating, it may serve as a refreshment stop for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Cioffi's Cucina
restaurant.desc: Cioffi's Cucina is the scratch-made kitchen arm of Cioffi's Italian Meat Market & Deli, a family-run Burnaby institution operating for over 25 years. Award-winning chef Jason Symington turns out daily hot specials, housemade panini, fresh pasta, and baked goods drawing directly from the adjacent deli and meat counter. A touring cyclist can grab anything from a quick Lavazza espresso to a full cold-pack of lasagna, arancini, or roasted chicken to go.

notes.Packed lunches: Cold prepared meals, panini, and 'Meals To Go' items including lasagna, roasted chicken, and arancini are explicitly designed for takeaway
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists vegetarian lasagna, eggplant parmigiana, gluten-free deli meat options, and organic products; multiple meat-free dishes appear in regular rotation

restaurant.name: Ajuker Fried Chicken
restaurant.desc: Ajuker Fried Chicken is a Korean and fried chicken restaurant in North Vancouver with indoor seating. It offers casual dining as a meal option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Mayuri Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Mayuri Indian Cuisine is a family-run, fully vegetarian restaurant in Surrey specializing in South Indian cooking, with dosas as its centrepiece alongside pakoras, rice dishes, and vegetable entrees made from scratch using traditional spice blends. The restaurant has a family-focused dining room atmosphere and also offers off-site catering for parties and functions. It has received recognition on Restaurant Guru and draws a loyal local following for its authentic regional Indian flavours.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Fully vegetarian restaurant; website states 'The Best and authentic South Indian Vegetarian Cuisine' and 'Mayuri is a family run Vegetarian Restaurant.'. Entire menu is plant-based (no meat items listed)

restaurant.name: The Break Café
restaurant.desc: The Break is a scratch-kitchen café and bakery in the heart of Ucluelet, known for house-smoked meats, fermented vegetables, fresh-baked sourdough and bagels, and made-to-order brunch sandwiches. Everything from pastry fillings to sandwich sauces is prepared in-house using fresh, seasonal, and locally sourced ingredients. Touring cyclists stopping in Ucluelet will find a quality sit-down food stop with a strong local reputation.

detail.address: 250 Main St #8, Ucluelet, BC V0R 3A0, Canada

restaurant.name: Cook & Pan Polish Delicatessen & Cafe
restaurant.desc: Cook & Pan is a Polish delicatessen and cafe established in 1996, now operating out of a restored heritage house in downtown Victoria. It combines an imported-goods deli, a fresh-sausage and cold-cuts counter, an espresso bar, and a kitchen turning out traditional dishes like pierogi, cabbage rolls, and bigos. A dedicated frozen take-home menu and an upstairs event space make it a distinctive stop for cyclists wanting a substantial, home-style Polish meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Frozen foods page states 'All pierogi are vegan (unless they contain cheese or meat)' and lists multiple plant-based dishes including Vegetable Stew (Leczo), Mushroom Goulash, Red Barszcz in vegetable broth, and Vegetable Barley soup

restaurant.name: Food Folk Eatery
restaurant.desc: Food Folk Eatery is a food court venue inside McArthurGlen Designer Outlet Vancouver, a large open-air outlet mall directly across from the SkyTrain Canada Line's Templeton Station in Richmond. The centre sits only two stops from Vancouver International Airport and about 20 minutes from downtown Vancouver, placing it on a heavily trafficked cycling corridor near the Sea Island routes. Outdoor seating is available at the eatery, and the surrounding centre offers a variety of quick-service food vendors including Cha House, JAPADOG, and A&W.

detail.address: 1000-7899 Templeton Station Road, Richmond, BC V7B 0B7

restaurant.name: Bulalohan Sa Ilocos
restaurant.desc: Bulalohan Sa Ilocos is a Filipino restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver serving authentic cuisine from the Ilocos region. It offers a casual dining stop for cyclists seeking local flavors while touring the area.

restaurant.name: Obanhmi
restaurant.desc: Obanhmi is a BC-grown Vietnamese sandwich chain specializing in bánh mì, fresh spring rolls, and iced coffee, now serving nine locations across the Lower Mainland. The menu spans classic French-influenced cold-cut sandwiches to halal chicken and fully vegan options, all built on freshly toasted baguettes with house-made ingredients. Cyclists passing through Coquitlam's North Road corridor will find quick, customizable, and filling meals available for in-store pickup or delivery.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'options for vegetarians, vegans, and halal diets'; dedicated VEGETARIAN/VEGAN bánh mì listed on menu (remove house mayo for vegan). No gluten-free option mentioned

restaurant.name: Peaceful Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Peaceful Restaurant is an award-winning Northern Chinese restaurant that has been serving Metro Vancouver since 1998, recognized by Food Network and USA Today for its hand-pulled noodles, beef rolls, and dumplings. Executive chef and owner Charlie Huang draws on the spice-laden culinary traditions of Xi'an and the Silk Road, offering a menu spanning artisanal dim sum to noodle creations. A touring cyclist would find a full sit-down meal with vegetarian options available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: No vegan or gluten-free confirmation found in website content

restaurant.name: The Yoga Chef Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Yoga Chef is a chef-led artisan catering company based in Port Coquitlam, serving corporate, wedding, private, and film productions across Metro Vancouver and the Sea to Sky corridor. The business emphasizes seasonal, locally sourced ingredients and visually considered menus. With over 300 Google reviews, it is an established presence in the Lower Mainland catering scene.

detail.address: 1760 McLean Avenue, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 4L3

restaurant.name: Mucho Burrito
restaurant.desc: Mucho Burrito is a Canadian fast-casual chain serving Mexican-inspired food with what the brand calls a 'Modern Mexicana' twist, located in the Tuscany Village shopping centre on McKenzie Avenue in Saanich. The menu centres on burritos, bowls, quesadillas, and tacos, with online ordering and a punch-card loyalty program available. It is a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the McKenzie corridor in Victoria's eastern suburbs.

restaurant.name: The Spud Shack Fry Co.
restaurant.desc: The Spud Shack Fry Co. is a Belgian-inspired frite and poutine counter tucked into the New Westminster SkyTrain station above Safeway, making it one of the more transit-accessible food stops in the Lower Mainland. The menu leans into creative poutines — from smoked meat to butter chicken to a full vegetarian chili version — alongside handmade burgers and a rotating selection of craft beers and sodas. It's a no-fuss, satisfying refuel spot with a distinctly local character.

detail.address: 352-800 Carnarvon Street, New Westminster, BC V3M 0G3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'Vegan | Vegetarian Options available, please ask for details.' Named vegetarian items include The Big V poutine (vegetarian chili, shredded cheese, sour cream) and the Yam, Quinoa & Oat Burger. No gluten-free items explicitly identified

restaurant.name: Milk Jam Donuts
restaurant.desc: Milk Jam Donuts is a small-batch artisan donut shop in downtown Nanaimo specializing in 24-hour-raised brioche donuts, filled cronuts, and house-made flavoured milks. Their glazes and fillings are crafted from real ingredients — fresh fruit, vanilla bean, organic cocoa — and coffee is brewed from locally roasted Drumroaster beans. Stock is limited and sells out regularly, so cyclists stopping by should check their @milkjamdonuts social feed before making a detour.

restaurant.name: Frankie's Modern Diner
restaurant.desc: Frankie's Modern Diner is a family-friendly sit-down restaurant on Victoria's Government Street serving breakfast through dinner daily, with a broad menu of house-made dishes built around fresh local ingredients including locally caught wild cod and salmon, craft beers from Hoyne, Phillips, and Driftwood, and breads from Irene's Bakery. The kitchen leans on from-scratch preparation — stuffed meatballs, house desserts, fresh-squeezed mimosas — and the diverse menu is designed so everyone at the table can find something. It has been voted Victoria's best for brunch, burgers, and value by Open Choice Diners.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website describes a diverse menu 'designed with the idea that everyone can sit down and enjoy a meal together'; no contradiction found in website content

restaurant.name: Flamez Chicken
restaurant.desc: Flamez Chicken is a fried and flame-grilled chicken restaurant in the heart of Downtown Nanaimo, located at the corner of Wallace and Fitzwilliam streets. The menu spans signature fried chicken, grilled options, poutines, seafood, wraps, rice bowls, and house-made sauces, with catering available for groups. Positioned near the Harbourfront Walkway and ferry terminal, it sits in a convenient spot for cyclists exploring downtown Nanaimo.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Seafood & Vegetarian' category; customer review states 'Great veggie options.'

restaurant.name: Kelly's Kitchen Café
restaurant.desc: Kelly's Kitchen Café is a breakfast-and-lunch spot in Nanaimo serving homemade all-day breakfast with a locally-flavoured menu — dishes are named after Nanaimo landmarks like Newcastle, Duke Point, Millstone, and Mount Benson. The menu leans heavily on classic egg preparations: bennys with fresh Hollandaise, omelettes, hashes, and griddle favourites, all served with homestyle hash browns. It's a filling sit-down stop for cyclists looking for a substantial meal before or after a ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a 'Veggie Lover's' omelette (tomatoes, green onions, green peppers, mushroom, cheddar) and a 'no meat Newcastle' egg plate variant

restaurant.name: Masala India Bistro
restaurant.desc: Masala India Bistro is an Indian restaurant in Langley, BC. Status and specific details could not be verified due to website unavailability.

restaurant.name: Lee's Donuts
restaurant.desc: Lee's Donuts is an iconic Vancouver-born donut chain founded in 1979 at the Granville Island Public Market, now with multiple Metro Vancouver locations including this Brentwood outpost. The shop is known for handmade, small-batch classic donuts using original recipes, with rotating seasonal flavours made fresh daily. A quick and reliable sugar stop for touring cyclists passing through Burnaby, with indoor seating and no drive-through.

restaurant.name: The Coffee Pitt
restaurant.desc: The Coffee Pitt is an independent community cafe in Pitt Meadows specializing in specialty espresso drinks, freshly baked goods, and made-to-order sandwiches using locally roasted beans. Beyond the daytime cafe menu, the shop offers a cocktail program featuring espresso martinis and aperol spritzes, and rents its venue for private events after closing. Cyclists riding the Pitt Meadows area trails and dyke routes will find vegan and gluten-free options alongside the signature cinnamon buns.

detail.address: 12528 Harris Road, Pitt Meadows, BC V3Y 2H1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Vegan Breakfast Sandwich, Vegan Raspberry Oreo, Gluten Free Brownie, and Gluten Free Cookie; scones include vegan-friendly flavours

restaurant.name: Jordan Sushi
restaurant.desc: Jordan Sushi is listed in OSM as a sushi restaurant, but its website now presents an entirely Korean menu — including Padak Chicken, Cheese Kimchi Rice, and Sweet Pig Trotters — under the tagline 'Enjoy the Authentic Taste of Korea in a Relaxed and Cozy Environment.' Online ordering is available through the site. The significant mismatch between the OSM address and the website address raises questions about whether the original business still operates at the listed location.

restaurant.name: Chili Pepper House
restaurant.desc: Chili Pepper House is a Chinese restaurant on Kingsway in East Vancouver, a corridor well-travelled by cyclists connecting Burnaby to downtown. It offers indoor dining in a no-smoking environment. The Kingsway stretch has a variety of services making it a practical stop on a longer ride through the area.

restaurant.name: Just Matcha Tea Shop
restaurant.desc: Just Matcha is a specialty matcha tea shop founded in 2013 by Tiffanie and Kip Home, now operating from its second Victoria home on Pandora Avenue after its original Oak Bay Avenue location closed during the pandemic. The shop sources a curated range of premium Japanese matcha powders, traditional bowls, and accessories, built on years of hands-on sourcing expertise. Cyclists passing through downtown Victoria will find a focused specialist with deep matcha knowledge and an authentic product selection.

restaurant.name: Hanwoori Korean Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Hanwoori has been serving authentic Korean cuisine since 1997, earning 8 Gold Awards from Vancouver Magazine and three 'Best Korean Restaurant' titles from Burnaby Now — a remarkable record of sustained excellence. The menu spans Korean staples like shabu shabu, seafood pancake, and beef combos alongside cocktails such as their signature Pink Blossom. Its longevity and award history make it a well-known dining destination in the Burnaby area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu page lists a dedicated 'Vegetarian' menu category alongside Main and Drinks

restaurant.name: Koffi
restaurant.desc: Koffi is a neighbourhood coffee house that opened in 2007 in a converted laundromat at Haultain Corners, founded on a philosophy of serving only the highest-quality espresso in just two sizes. The café partners with local Victoria bakeries and makes paninis in-house, and features a rotating 22-by-12-foot art wall showcasing local artists. It also hosts events and provides catering, making it a genuine community hub in a quiet residential corner of Victoria.

restaurant.name: Sushi Street
restaurant.desc: Sushi Street is a Japanese takeout restaurant inside King George Hub at the King George SkyTrain Station in Surrey, offering a broad menu of sashimi, nigiri, rolls, bento boxes, tempura, teriyaki, and ready-to-eat foods. The transit-adjacent location and emphasis on quick, convenient service make it a practical stop for cyclists passing through the area. Online ordering and delivery through Skip the Dishes and Uber Eats are available, and catering services are offered for larger groups.

restaurant.name: Cafe Log
restaurant.desc: Cafe Log is a coffee and desserts café occupying a second-floor unit in North Vancouver, previously operating under the name Snowy Village. It offers indoor seating in a no-smoking environment and is noted as wheelchair accessible. Cyclists looking for a sweet stop in North Vancouver may find it a quiet, sheltered retreat for coffee and desserts.

restaurant.name: Local Public Eatery
restaurant.desc: A Local Public Eatery in Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Villages Pizza
restaurant.desc: Villages Pizza is a regional pizza chain with deep roots in Victoria's neighbourhoods, operating under Sanderson & Louis Holdings. The Oak Bay Avenue location sits in a walkable, bikeable commercial strip and offers both delivery and in-store pickup. The chain supports school lunch programs and community catering, making it a practical stop for groups or solo touring cyclists passing through Oak Bay.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Catering page lists 'vegetarian options,' 'lactose free cheese,' and 'gluten conscious crusts.'

restaurant.name: Osmanthus Chinese Fusion Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Osmanthus is a fine-dining Chinese restaurant on Level 2 of Aberdeen Centre in Richmond, specializing in Jiangnan cuisine with roots in the Song Dynasty. The restaurant has hosted a Michelin Chef's Night event and offers an extensive menu of crafted beverages alongside its food menu. Touring cyclists looking for an upscale sit-down meal in Richmond's busy Aberdeen Centre area will find this a distinctive cultural dining experience.

restaurant.name: House of Dosas
restaurant.desc: House of Dosas on Davie Street is a South Indian restaurant specializing in dosas, biryanis, and spiced chicken dishes rooted in Chef Ganesh's authentic southern Indian recipes. It operates around the clock every day of the week, making it a rare all-hours dining option in Vancouver's West End. Cyclists passing through the Davie Village corridor will find a warm sit-down meal available at any hour.

restaurant.name: Proud Up Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Proud Up is a sit-down Canadian comfort food restaurant serving breakfast and dinner, formerly operating as The Taco Factory. The menu leans hearty — eggs Benedict variations, skillets, chicken and waffles — with a selection of vegetarian-friendly dishes. Located on East Columbia Street in New Westminster, it offers a relaxed neighbourhood dining experience for cyclists passing through.

detail.address: 418 East Columbia St, New Westminster, BC V3L 3W9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian options: Veggo Benny (spinach, bell peppers, tomato, cilantro pumpkin pesto), Cali Veggie omelette (tomatoes, mushrooms, avocado, mozzarella, cilantro pesto), green fields skillet (crispy tofu, spinach, caramelized onion, corn, tomato), and Toasty Avocado

restaurant.name: Blanshard Street Winery
restaurant.desc: Blanshard St. Winery is a locally owned, family-operated craft winery that has been producing wines in Victoria since 1996, making it the longest-running winery in the city under its original owners. Spread across a 4,000 sq ft facility with state-of-the-art bottling equipment, it offers an extensive lineup spanning premium reds and whites, dessert wines, wine coolers, and ciders sourced from vineyards around the world. A touring cyclist interested in BC's craft beverage scene could visit to browse or purchase bottles, with wedding and custom-label wine services also available.

detail.address: 661 Burnside Road East, Victoria, BC V8T 2X9

restaurant.name: Matteo's Gelato
restaurant.desc: Matteo's Gelato is a neighborhood Italian gelato shop on Mary Hill Road in Port Coquitlam, run by a passionate gelato maker who prepares small daily batches from traditional recipes using imported Italian ingredients. Beyond its signature gelato, the shop serves authentic espresso, specialty coffee drinks, fresh sandwiches, and artisanal chocolates, making it a full Italian cafe stop. The shop has earned strong local acclaim for flavor authenticity from reviewers with firsthand travel experience in Italy.

detail.address: 2615 Mary Hill Road, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 3B5

restaurant.name: Newton Pizza
restaurant.desc: Newton Pizza is a local pizza chain with several locations across the Surrey and North Delta area of British Columbia, built on a reputation for fresh ingredients and house-perfected recipes. The Surrey/North Delta outlet on 128 Street serves the surrounding community with dine-in and online ordering. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find it a straightforward stop for a quick hot meal.

restaurant.name: Cocobay
restaurant.desc: Cocobay is a bubble tea café on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver specializing in bubble tea and vegetarian-friendly drinks. Located at street level in a busy urban corridor, it offers air-conditioned indoor seating — a welcome refuge on a hot ride. The downtown location puts it within easy reach of the Vancouver Seawall and other popular cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Saigon Ivy
restaurant.desc: Saigon Ivy is a Vietnamese restaurant in downtown New Westminster, an area well-suited to cycling stop-offs on the Central Valley Greenway and nearby routes. OSM records place its founding before 1948, making it one of the older eateries in the community. Indoor seating is noted in OSM tags, offering a sit-down meal option for cyclists passing through New Westminster.

restaurant.name: Original Udder Guys
restaurant.desc: Original Udder Guys is a scratch-made artisan ice cream parlour and retro candy shop on the Cowichan Bay waterfront, scooping from recipes perfected since 1999 and operating year-round under new ownership since 2023. The 24-flavour cabinet spans classics to inventive combinations alongside in-store fudge, imported British crisps and sweets, espresso drinks, milkshakes, and Slush Puppies. Cyclists can sit outside at picnic tables with a view of the bay or settle into indoor booths after a ride through the Cowichan Valley.

detail.address: 1765 Cowichan Bay Road, Cowichan Bay, BC V0R 1N0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dairy-free sorbets listed among the 24 scooping cabinet flavours; sugar-free candy options also stocked

restaurant.name: Portly Penguin Pizza
restaurant.desc: A pizza restaurant in Christina Lake serving the local community and passing travelers.

restaurant.name: Sushi 2 Go
restaurant.desc: Sushi 2 Go is a fast-food sushi spot located on or near Salt Spring Island, BC, suggested by the Instagram handle 'sushi2go_ssi'. It offers a quick sushi option for cyclists exploring the Gulf Islands. The recent OSM check date of March 2026 indicates the business was active as of that visit.

restaurant.name: Caffe Motivo
restaurant.desc: Caffe Motivo is a downtown Kamloops café situated on Victoria Street in the city core, specializing in fresh-baked goods and coffee sourced from JJ Bean roasters. It also offers light lunches and breakfasts prepared in-house daily, making it a solid resupply stop for cyclists rolling through the Thompson Valley. Catering is available for groups with advance notice.

restaurant.name: Pho Goodness
restaurant.desc: Pho Goodness is a Vietnamese comfort food restaurant established in 2011 in Vancouver's West End, serving pho, banh mi, rice dishes, and vermicelli bowls with a focus on home-style cooking. The Davie Street location has been a neighbourhood staple for over a decade, earning Westender Magazine's Best Vietnamese and Best Pho awards in 2012, 2016, and 2017. Online ordering with pickup is available, making it a quick and convenient stop for cyclists passing through the West End.

restaurant.name: Neptune Wonton Noodle
restaurant.desc: Neptune Wonton Noodle is a fast-casual Chinese noodle restaurant in Richmond operated by the Neptune Restaurant Group, a Greater Vancouver hospitality company established in 1997. The group's sister brand, Neptune Seafood Restaurant, holds membership in the Commanderie des Cordons Bleu de France and has won Vancouver's Top Ten Chinese Restaurant Award, reflecting the culinary pedigree behind the brand. For touring cyclists, it offers a quick, filling Chinese noodle meal with convenient takeout and delivery options in the heart of Richmond.

restaurant.name: Miku
restaurant.desc: Miku pioneered Aburi (flame-seared) sushi in Canada when it opened in Vancouver in 2008 and has earned Michelin Guide recognition and the Wine Spectator Award of Excellence. The waterfront location at Granville Square features a full bar and lounge, a patio overlooking the harbour, a private dining room, and a full-service sushi bar showcasing Ocean Wise seafood and regional west coast ingredients. A touring cyclist arriving along the seawall would find a distinctive upscale dining experience blending traditional Japanese technique with local flavours.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Garden Shokai — Our vegetarian lunch selection of appetizers and assortment of sushi' and a Tofu Salad with organic greens and miso tofu

restaurant.name: Smitty's
restaurant.desc: Smitty's is a Canadian-owned casual dining chain operating since 1960, with this Parksville location sitting on the East Island Highway — a key corridor for cyclists touring Vancouver Island. The menu centres on all-day breakfast, pancakes, and burgers, positioning it as a substantial meal stop for riders needing to refuel. As part of a well-established national chain, the restaurant offers a predictable, family-friendly dining experience.

restaurant.name: Yook Korean Grilled BBQ and Bistro
restaurant.desc: Yook Korean Grilled BBQ and Bistro is a sit-down Korean BBQ restaurant on Nanaimo Street in East Vancouver, where guests grill premium meats at the table alongside traditional Korean dishes. The head chef brings over 30 years of experience from home-style Korean restaurants in both South Korea and Canada, and the kitchen produces all banchan in-house. It offers a substantial, warm meal stop well-suited to hungry cyclists finishing a longer urban or cross-town ride.

restaurant.name: El Dorado Pies & Treats
restaurant.desc: El Dorado Pie & Treats is a family-run bakery operating since 2002, run by a mother, daughter, and son team, offering an extensive menu of sweet and savory baked goods with a Latin American influence. The shop is best known for its handcrafted empanadas in over a dozen varieties — from traditional beef to vegan — alongside fruit pies, tarts, quiches, and hand-decorated cookies. Located at Lonsdale Quay in North Vancouver, it is a convenient stop for cyclists riding the North Shore waterfront.

detail.address: 116 - 123 Carrie Cates Court, North Vancouver, BC V7M 3L4

restaurant.name: Quayside Tiki Bar
restaurant.desc: Quayside Tiki Bar is a tropical-themed bar and restaurant located steps from the Fraser River in New Westminster, serving handcrafted cocktails — including Mai Tais, Blue Lagoon, and Quay Breeze Punch — alongside a wide-ranging menu of sushi, seafood, pizzas, and grilled meats. The venue features a spacious waterfront patio with river views and a lively atmosphere, making it a colourful option for cyclists riding the riverfront. The business appears to have opened recently, with a grand opening event listed on its website.

detail.address: 810 Quayside Dr #126, New Westminster, BC V3M 6B9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly includes Veggie Pizza, Mixed Greens salad, Burrata with heirloom tomatoes, and Caesar Salad; no explicit GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Purebread
restaurant.desc: Purebread is a well-regarded artisan bakery chain with roots in Whistler that has expanded to multiple BC locations including this Mount Pleasant shop. It specialises in freshly baked breads, pastries, pies, and cakes, and has been featured by the New York Times, Lonely Planet, and Vogue. The Mount Pleasant location offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a pleasant urban rest stop for cyclists.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: McDonald's is a globally recognised fast food chain offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, fries, and McCafé beverages. This North Vancouver location includes a drive-through and takeaway service. It is a reliable, familiar stop for touring cyclists in need of a quick and filling meal along a busy corridor.

detail.address: 2001 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2K4, Canada

restaurant.name: Crazy Cows Ice-Cream
restaurant.desc: Crazy Cows Ice-Cream is a small ice cream shop on Marine Drive in White Rock serving visitors and locals with cold treats and refreshments.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: Subway is a fast-food sandwich chain with takeaway service located in Chilliwack. It provides quick meal options for touring cyclists passing through the community. Specific cyclist amenities such as bike parking and water refill are not documented.

restaurant.name: AM Cafe
restaurant.desc: AM Cafe is a 100% plant-based, order-at-the-counter café in the heart of Mount Pleasant, founded by chef Lindsay Loudon whose background spans yacht kitchens and high-end corporate events. The menu leans into plant-based comfort food built to surprise — dishes like the Rogue Waffle and the Faux-Let O' Fish Burger regularly prompt the reaction 'This isn't chicken?' It is a community-focused neighbourhood spot with a relaxed, settle-in atmosphere built around the philosophy of a few ingredients done extremely well.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states '100% Plant Based Café' and all menu items are plant-based. GF options not mentioned

restaurant.name: Gawon Express
restaurant.desc: Gawon Express is a quick-service Korean restaurant near SFU's University High Street, specializing in rice bowls, noodle dishes, soups, and Korean dumplings. The restaurant encourages online pre-ordering for pickup to reduce wait times, making it a practical stop for cyclists passing through the Burnaby Mountain area. A substantial dedicated vegetarian menu — including bibimbap, kimchi fried rice, and soft tofu soup — gives plant-based riders plenty of fueling options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website has a dedicated 'Vegetarian Menu' section including Veggie Bimbim-bap, Veggie Bibim-Noodle, Veggie Kimchi Fried Rice, Vegetarian Mandu, Tofu Bap Burger, Vegetarian Soft Tofu Soup, Egg Udon, and Vegetable Udon/Ramen

restaurant.name: Rain or Shine Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Rain or Shine Ice Cream is a Kitsilano institution making small-batch, scratch ice cream from BC dairy sourced exclusively from Birchwood Dairy Farm in Abbotsford, with flavours built around locally and organically sourced ingredients like Okanagan honey, Surrey blueberries, and Vancouver-roasted espresso. Founded by a couple inspired by artisan ice cream encountered while travelling, the shop now operates three Vancouver locations, with this one sitting directly on West 4th Avenue—one of the city's busiest cycling corridors. The entirely egg-free base, rotating seasonal menu, and dedicated vegan options make it a distinctive treat stop rather than a generic chain.

notes.Takeout: Walk-up ice cream shop serving scoops, cones, milkshakes, and toppings; the entire service model is counter/takeout with no table-service component mentioned

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: A Starbucks Coffee location in Sardis, part of the well-known international coffee chain. This outlet includes a drive-through lane, making it convenient for quick stops along Luckakuck Way. Touring cyclists passing through Chilliwack's commercial corridor will find it a familiar and reliable refuelling spot.

restaurant.name: Prado Cafe
restaurant.desc: Prado Coffee is a Vancouver specialty coffee brand founded by Sammy Piccolo, a four-time Canadian Barista Champion who has represented Canada at the World Barista Championships. What began as a single shop on Commercial Drive has grown into a network of neighbourhood cafes across Vancouver, Burnaby, and Surrey, each focused on craft espresso and fresh baked goods. The Dunbar Street location brings that same community-first ethos to a residential cycling corridor on the west side of Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Murrayville Town Pub
restaurant.desc: Established in 1992, Murrayville Town Pub is a long-standing Langley neighbourhood pub known for its warm, community-oriented atmosphere. It boasts over 200 seats, pool tables, and 20 screens for sports, plus an adjoining private banquet room called Manhattans. The pub has raised over $100,000 for Big Brothers & Sisters and is deeply embedded in the local Murrayville community.

restaurant.name: Cold Shoulder Cafe
restaurant.desc: Cold Shoulder Cafe is a small family-run cafe and bakery in Jordan River on the south end of Vancouver Island, founded in 2014 and now operated by one of the original founders and his family. Situated on West Coast Road near surf breaks and provincial parks, it serves soups, sandwiches, and pastries and also sells branded merchandise online and in-store. It sits on the challenging but scenic cycling route between Sooke and Port Renfrew, making it a natural rest stop for touring cyclists on this stretch of coast.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states 'We have a few GF and Vegan options. Soups and pastries change daily, so be sure to ask at the till.' Cross-contamination caveat noted for severe allergies

restaurant.name: Jim's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Jim's Pizza Walnut Grove is a locally run pizza restaurant in Langley's Walnut Grove neighbourhood, serving a broad menu of specialty and build-your-own pizzas alongside pasta, ribs, and chicken wings. The shop operates its own delivery fleet and also accepts online orders, making it a practical stop for a takeout meal. Gluten-free crust and vegetarian options are available on request.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Gluten-free crust available in medium size (add-on noted on menu page); vegetarian pasta available on request ('Make it Vegetarian, ask for your pasta to be made with marinara')

restaurant.name: Britannia Brewing
restaurant.desc: Britannia Brewing Lake Country is a craft brewery restaurant and bar set on a 10,000 sq ft facility in the Okanagan, near the popular Okanagan Rail Trail cycling corridor. Established in 2014 and expanded from its Steveston and Ladner origins, it offers a full menu of house ales alongside locally inspired dishes featuring Okanagan ingredients like peaches and BC mushrooms. The 200-seat restaurant with outdoor picnic area makes it a substantial stop for cyclists exploring the Okanagan Valley.

restaurant.name: Pappa Leo's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Pappa Leo's Pizza is a locally owned and operated chain founded in 2003 by two brothers in Pitt Meadows, now expanded to 7 Metro Vancouver locations. The Port Coquitlam shop makes pizza dough fresh daily and sources quality ingredients, earning multiple best-pizza awards. Gluten-free crust is available, and the location offers both pickup and delivery.

restaurant.name: Kinkura Sushi + Sake
restaurant.desc: Kinkura Sushi + Sake is a Japanese restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, blending traditional sushi culture with a modern dining experience. The menu is extensive, covering salads, tempura, udon, teriyaki, sashimi, and a wide range of classic and specialty rolls including aburi (flame-seared) preparations. Online ordering is available, offering touring cyclists a convenient option for a quick Japanese meal in a dense, walkable neighbourhood.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes a dedicated 'VEGETARIAN ROLL' category

restaurant.name: Craft Bierhaus
restaurant.desc: Craft Bierhaus is a bar and restaurant billing itself as being 'in the heart of Revelstoke,' with a kitchen centred on slow-smoked meats — brisket, beef ribs, whole chicken, and pork — alongside rotating craft beers and local BC wines. The OSM record notes outdoor seating, making it a sociable place to unwind after a long day in the saddle. Its central downtown location in Revelstoke positions it as a natural end-of-day stop on popular cycling routes through the Columbia Mountains.

restaurant.name: Red Arrow Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: Red Arrow Brewing Company is a craft brewery established in 2015 in the Cowichan Valley, operating out of a distinctive red-brick building that was originally an Arrow Custom Motorcycles showroom built in 1990. The taproom pours 12 beers on tap alongside craft cocktails and a full food menu, with a spacious family- and pet-friendly patio that features a Coast Salish totem carved by artist Tom Lafortune. It functions as a community hub in Duncan and welcomes reservations and brewery tours by arrangement.

restaurant.name: Wok Box
restaurant.desc: Wok Box is a fast-casual Chinese restaurant chain offering takeaway service to customers. Located in a commercial shopping area, it provides quick meals for those seeking Asian cuisine. Touring cyclists can grab food without waiting for full table service.

restaurant.name: Golden Boot
restaurant.desc: The Golden Boot is a family-owned Northern Italian trattoria that has been serving handmade pasta, pizza, and sauces in Coquitlam since 1997. Chef-owner David Azzi trained in Modena, Italy and has maintained a strict 'quality over quantity' philosophy, with everything from the bread to the desserts made in-house. The restaurant has earned Restaurant Guru's 2019 Best Italian Restaurant Award and OpenTable's Diners' Choice 2022, and also offers U-Bake take-home items and full event catering.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes: Margherita pizza (Fior Di Latte and fresh basil), Pizza Victoria (roasted pepper, tomato, onion, spinach), Garden Salad, Insalata Caprese, Minestrone, and Bruschetta

restaurant.name: Rossland Beer Company
restaurant.desc: Rossland Beer Company is an award-winning craft brewery and tasting room in Rossland, BC, producing small-batch beers including the Canadian Brewing Award gold-medal-winning Seven Summits Milk Stout and the BC Beer Award-winning Paydirt Pale Ale. The tasting room overlooks the brewing operation and opens onto a sunny patio, drawing outdoor enthusiasts directly from Rossland's world-class mountain bike trails and ski slopes. The brewery actively sponsors local mountain biking athletes and is deeply embedded in the town's adventure-sports culture, making it a natural gathering point for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Davie Village Bakery & Gelato
restaurant.desc: Operating for over 30 years, this artisan bakery on Vancouver's Davie Street produces traditional-style breads, pastries, muffins, and gluten-free baked goods using no preservatives or artificial ingredients. It is notably the premier film-industry catering provider in Vancouver, supplying on-location production sets across Metro Vancouver. The Davie Street shop offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a comfortable stop in the heart of the West End.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: McDonald's at 1055 West Georgia Street is a fast food restaurant in downtown Vancouver, situated inside a mixed-use building near the West End and steps from the central business district. The restaurant offers a broad menu spanning burgers, chicken, breakfast items, and McCafé beverages, with indoor seating and vegetarian options available. Its downtown core location makes it a practical food and beverage stop for cyclists transiting through Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Hunnybee Bruncheonette
restaurant.desc: Hunnybee Bruncheonette is a counter-service cafe and brunch spot in Vancouver's Strathcona neighbourhood, sitting on the corner of Gore Avenue and Union Street. It serves brunch classics — shakshuka, ricotta pancakes, eggs benny variations, and fresh-pressed juice — alongside espresso drinks and cocktails. The same address hosts a sibling evening restaurant, Thank You Pizza, making it a versatile stop on a city ride.

notes.Takeout: Described as a counter-service bruncheonette; walk-in, no-reservation model implies takeout is available

restaurant.name: Ali & Baba

restaurant.name: Two Stones Grill
restaurant.desc: Two Stones Grill is a casual grill-house restaurant inside the Tsawwassen Commons shopping centre in Delta, BC, serving a broad menu of handcrafted burgers, charcoal-broiled steaks, grilled salmon, pasta, and Mediterranean-influenced dishes alongside a full cocktail and BC wine list. The restaurant covers all three dayparts—breakfast, lunch, and dinner—making it a versatile refuelling stop for cyclists riding the Tsawwassen waterfront corridor. Catering with delivery or pickup is also available for events in the Tsawwassen/Delta region.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu confirms Veggie Burger (Life Stream brown rice patty) and other plant-compatible dishes. GF not mentioned

restaurant.name: Mandarin Garden Buffet
restaurant.desc: Mandarin Garden Buffet has been a Chilliwack-area institution since 1998, serving a wide-ranging Chinese smorgasbord buffet alongside a full take-out menu six days a week. It has earned the Chilliwack Times Reader's Choice award for Favourite Buffet, drawing diners from Chilliwack, Abbotsford, and Agassiz. A large private banquet room rounds out the offering for groups and special occasions.

restaurant.name: MeeT on Blanshard
restaurant.desc: MeeT on Blanshard is a restaurant in Victoria offering vegetarian and vegan menu options. Website access issues prevent confirmation of other details relevant to touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: The Acorn
restaurant.desc: The Acorn is a Michelin-recommended, award-winning vegetable-forward locavore restaurant and bar on Vancouver's Main Street, operating a zero-waste kitchen that sources 99% of its ingredients from BC and Western Canada. Cyclists can choose between a multi-course blind tasting menu served family-style or an à la carte menu featuring inventive dishes built around seasonal foraged and farmed produce. The restaurant is also noted by Michelin for its weekend brunch program.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'cater to vegans and gluten free diners'; menu items throughout labelled GF+V

restaurant.name: Andreas Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Andreas Restaurant is a family-owned North Vancouver institution open since 1984, run by father-and-son duo Andreas and Dimitrios, with a scratch kitchen that hand-makes an extensive menu of over 130 items — from Greek specialties to pizza, pasta, steaks, and seafood — every morning. The restaurant explicitly welcomes tour groups with specially crafted group menus and offers free delivery across North Vancouver, West Vancouver, and Deep Cove. A long-standing local favourite, it sends guests home with complimentary fresh-baked bread as a nod to the founder's original tradition.

restaurant.name: Sushi Tengoku

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: This McDonald's sits on the second floor (level 1) of a building on the busy Broadway-Cambie corridor in Vancouver, without a drive-through. It offers both indoor and outdoor seating alongside takeaway and delivery options, making it a quick resupply stop for cyclists travelling along the Broadway corridor. The location is a standard urban franchise outlet with no cycling-specific features confirmed.

restaurant.name: Mai's Vietnamese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Mai's Vietnamese Restaurant is a family-owned establishment that has been serving authentic Vietnamese cuisine to the Langley community since 2008. The menu spans phở, vermicelli bowls, bánh mì, salad rolls, and family-style hot pot, with Western and Asian-inspired options available for catering. Cyclists can order for pickup or dine in at a full-service restaurant that prides itself on fresh ingredients and consistent quality.

restaurant.name: Delicious Pho
restaurant.desc: Delicious Pho is a Vietnamese restaurant on downtown Vancouver's Robson Street, one of two Lower Mainland locations (the other in Coquitlam). The menu centres on signature satay pho with aromatic broth, alongside fresh salad rolls, banh mi, and a deluxe combo pho loaded with mixed proteins. The restaurant emphasises traditional recipes and is wheelchair accessible, making it a practical sit-down stop in a busy urban cycling corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes salad rolls with shrimp, vegetables, and herbs, and vegetable-forward dishes

restaurant.name: Tom Khao Thai Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Ton Khao Thai Cuisine is a family-run restaurant in Historic Downtown Abbotsford, owned by Suthin and Ya, offering an extensive menu of Thai street-food classics spanning curries, noodles, stir-fries, and grills. Dishes are built around the five traditional Thai flavour pillars — sweet, sour, salty, spicy, and creamy — with adjustable spice levels from none to Thai hot. Cyclists passing through downtown Abbotsford will find both dine-in and call-ahead takeout service.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Most menu items list 'vegetables or tofu' as a protein choice; several dishes note 'Can be made dairy free upon request'

restaurant.name: Bagheera
restaurant.desc: Bagheera is a hidden speakeasy cocktail bar in Vancouver's Chinatown, concealed behind the fictional storefront of the Happy Valley Turf Club — a betting parlour facade that masks the entrance. Inside, the theme shifts to Victorian India and Jungle Book imagery, with expertly crafted cocktails and small Indian-inspired dishes. The elaborate concept extends to the bar's own website, which is disguised as a horse-racing racecard.

restaurant.name: Thai Basil
restaurant.desc: Thai Basil is a Thai restaurant established in 2008 with four Vancouver locations, including this one on Commercial Drive — a popular cycling corridor in the city's east side. The menu spans curries, noodle soups, salads, and rice dishes with a range of protein choices including tofu. Cyclists can dine in or order takeout for a convenient mid-ride meal.

restaurant.name: Bonnie Bread Bakery

restaurant.name: Sago To Go
restaurant.desc: Sago To Go is a café in Vancouver. As a food service business, it can serve as a convenient stop for cycling tourists moving through the neighborhood.

restaurant.name: The Ramen Butcher

The Burnaby location on Hastings Street offers a broad menu spanning classic tonkotsu, tsukemen, miso, and coconut curry ramens alongside donburi rice bowls and gyoza. It is one of two BC locations, with a second shop in Vancouver's Chinatown.

restaurant.name: Grand Crystal Seafood
restaurant.desc: Grand Crystal is a Chinese seafood restaurant and wedding banquet venue located in Burnaby's Kingsway corridor. It serves dim sum and dinner, and also functions as an event space for large gatherings. Touring cyclists riding through the Burnaby stretch of Kingsway would find it a substantial stop for a full sit-down meal.

restaurant.name: Dana Pani Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Dana Pani Indian Cuisine is a North Indian restaurant in the Queensborough neighbourhood of New Westminster, offering a broad menu of tandoori specialities, biryanis, curries, and freshly baked breads. The kitchen is notable for its range of both meat and vegetarian dishes, from classic Butter Chicken to Paneer Stuffed Chana Bhatura, with wraps and rice bowls also available for quick meals. Touring cyclists can order pickup directly through the restaurant's own website.

detail.address: 805 Boyd Street, J120, New Westminster, BC V3M 5X2

restaurant.name: Kamei on Broadway
restaurant.desc: Kamei on Broadway is a long-established Japanese restaurant tucked behind Broadway Plaza in Vancouver, celebrated as a local hidden gem since 1988. It offers distinctive Japanese Tatami rooms and private booths with sweeping panoramic views of downtown Vancouver. The menu focuses on innovative Japanese cuisine with an emphasis on fresh, high-quality seafood prepared by specially trained Japanese chefs.

restaurant.name: 21 Steps Kitchen & Bar
restaurant.desc: Established in 2004, 21 Steps Kitchen & Bar is a locally owned and operated second-storey restaurant in the heart of Whistler Village, offering views of the village and surrounding mountains. It serves modern comfort food with generous portions in a warm, casual atmosphere with a full bar. The restaurant has earned recognition for Best Casual Dining and Best Customer Service in Pique News Magazine's 'Best Of Whistler' awards.

restaurant.name: Caffe Artigiano
restaurant.desc: Caffe Artigiano (now branded as Artigiano) is a Vancouver-founded specialty coffee chain with over 25 locations across BC and Alberta, built on a reputation for latte art and internationally award-winning barista craft. The Main Street location offers indoor and outdoor seating, accepts credit and debit cards, and is wheelchair accessible. The chain roasts its own 100% Arabica beans at a Burnaby roastery and emphasizes organic, locally sourced ingredients in its house-made baked goods.

restaurant.name: Hoi An Cafe
restaurant.desc: Hoi An Cafe is a Vietnamese cafe on Victoria Drive in Vancouver with indoor seating. It provides a casual stop for cyclists to rest and refresh during tours in the area.

restaurant.name: Pudgie's Pizza & Pasta
restaurant.desc: Pudgie's Pizza & Pasta is a long-established neighbourhood restaurant at Horseshoe Bay, serving pizza and pasta with fresh, locally sourced ingredients since the late 1980s. Its location steps from the BC Ferries terminal makes it a natural stop for cyclists riding to or from the Sunshine Coast. The restaurant is also known for stocking what it bills as Vancouver's largest selection of rare and specialty sodas.

restaurant.name: Mr India Meats & Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Mr. India Restaurant & Bar is an Indian restaurant in Abbotsford serving cuisine inspired by regions across the subcontinent, from street snacks like golgappa and vada paav to full curry entrées and cocktails. The restaurant offers both a dine-in bar experience and a robust takeout and catering operation, including tiffin service and large-group party packs. With over 600 Google reviews and more than 30 vegetarian and non-vegetarian entrées, it is a well-established local dining destination.

restaurant.name: St. Lawrence Restaurant
restaurant.desc: St. Lawrence is a Michelin-starred restaurant on Powell Street in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, blending classic French technique with the culinary traditions of Québec under Chef/Owner Jean-Christophe Poirier. Opened in 2017, it has earned placement on Canada's 100 Best Restaurants list multiple years running and was named to the World's 50 Best Discovery List. The experience centres on a four-course table d'hôte menu with a rotating seasonal focus, currently drawing inspiration from Provence.

restaurant.name: Board with Friends Cafe
restaurant.desc: Board with Friends Cafe is a board game cafe on Victoria's Johnson Street where visitors can drop in and play from an extensive in-house library for as long as they like, with no time limit. The cafe also retails what it describes as Victoria's largest selection of board games, available in-store and online, along with a loyalty rewards program and a private room that seats up to 12 for group occasions. As of the most recent website check, the business is actively relocating to an undisclosed address, so cyclists should verify the current location before visiting.

restaurant.name: Bubble Waffle Cafe
restaurant.desc: Bubble Waffle Cafe is a Hong Kong-style street food cafe specializing in egg waffles (雞蛋仔), fish soup noodle combos, curry fish balls, and rice noodle rolls — popular street snacks brought from Hong Kong to Metro Vancouver. Located inside a mall food court, it offers an extensive menu with dozens of soup base, noodle, and topping combinations alongside a full range of bubble teas and fruit drinks. The cafe operates multiple locations including Aberdeen Centre, Public Market, and Park Royal.

restaurant.name: D² Tea Lab
restaurant.desc: D² Tea Lab is a specialty craft tea café in Burnaby built around the '3/7' ratio — three parts milk to seven parts tea — developed through what the owners describe as years of scientific research and sensory analysis. The menu centers on craft milk teas, pure teas, and snowy lattes, sourced from premium leaves chosen for quality and sustainability. The lab-themed branding and data-driven flavour philosophy give it a distinctive character among BC's bubble tea scene.

restaurant.name: Hydra Estiatorio Mediterranean
restaurant.desc: Hydra Estiatorio is a high-end Greek seafood restaurant occupying the soaring 60-foot atrium of Vancouver's EXchange Tower, named after the Aegean island renowned for its culinary traditions. The restaurant operates a Raw Bar with daily fresh seafood flown in from Greece, New Zealand, and Hawaii alongside locally sourced BC salmon and oysters, with fish deboned and plated tableside. The venue is located within Vancouver's first LEED Platinum heritage conversion hotel and uses geo-exchange thermal regulators, solar thermal panels, and storm water retention systems as part of its sustainability program.

restaurant.name: Outer Clove Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Outer Clove is a locally owned European comfort-food restaurant in downtown Nelson specializing in Balkan and Hungarian cuisine — think schnitzel, chicken paprikash, halusky, and Hungarian cabbage rolls. The restaurant stands out for its curated selection of Czech draft beers poured from Lukr faucets and rare Central European craft wines. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery are all available, making it a flexible stop for cyclists passing through Nelson.

restaurant.name: Machi Sushi
restaurant.desc: Machi Sushi is a compact neighbourhood Japanese restaurant on Cadboro Bay Road in Oak Bay, serving an extensive menu of creative specialty rolls, sashimi, nigiri, and donburi bowls with a focus on fresh and locally sourced ingredients. The chef's signature rolls — including the Vancouver Roll and Caterpillar Roll — have earned consistent praise from local diners. Dine-in, takeout, and online ordering are all available.

restaurant.name: Garrison Wine & Liquor Merchants
restaurant.desc: Garrison Wine & Liquor Merchants is a neighbourhood liquor store in the Garrison Crossing shopping area of Chilliwack, BC, with a curated selection of wines, spirits, and local BC producers from the Okanagan Valley and Fraser Valley. The store regularly hosts in-store tastings featuring regional and international labels. Touring cyclists passing through Chilliwack could stop here to pick up locally made BC wines and spirits.

restaurant.name: West B Pizza
restaurant.desc: West B Pizza is a Vancouver pizzeria on West Broadway serving a creative lineup of pies including fusion options like Paneer Masala and Vietnamese Chilli Chicken alongside classics and pasta dishes. The shop offers indoor seating and online ordering, making it a convenient stop for cyclists along the busy Broadway corridor. A range of vegetarian options and sides like peri peri wings and fries round out the menu.

restaurant.name: The Bund Shanghai Cuisine & Bar
restaurant.desc: The Bund Shanghai Cuisine & Bar is a Chinese restaurant and bar on White Rock's scenic Marine Drive, specializing in Shanghai-style dishes alongside Sichuan and Cantonese favourites. The menu spans dim sum staples like soup dumplings and a full Peking duck service alongside a broad selection of wok dishes. Situated on one of the Lower Mainland's most popular waterfront cycling corridors, it offers a full sit-down meal or online pickup for cyclists on the move.

restaurant.name: Buckhorn & Main
restaurant.desc: Buckhorn & Main Mountain Eatery is the full-service restaurant and lounge inside Trickle Creek Lodge, a ski-in/ski-out resort at Kimberley Alpine Resort. The menu spans burgers, seafood, steaks, salads, and desserts, with a kids' menu and a lounge offering cocktails and draft beer on tap. Its location at the base of the alpine resort and near the Peak to Plaza trail network makes it a natural refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the Kimberley area.

restaurant.name: E Yong Oriental Restaurant
restaurant.desc: E. Yong Oriental Restaurant is a Vietnamese restaurant located in Chilliwack, BC. It appears to serve the local community as a sit-down dining establishment, offering cuisine that could appeal to touring cyclists seeking a warm meal after a long day on the road. Beyond the cuisine tag and name, no further details about the dining experience are available from current sources.

restaurant.name: Wild Ginger
restaurant.desc: Wild Ginger is an Asian fusion restaurant on Main Street in downtown Penticton, serving a broad menu spanning Vietnamese, Thai, and Chinese cuisines including Beef Pho, Pad Thai, Chow Mein, and signature stir-fries. The kitchen caters to dietary needs with gluten-free and vegan adaptations available across most dishes and free tofu substitutions on request. Online ordering and local delivery make it a convenient refuelling option for cyclists passing through the Okanagan.

restaurant.name: Molly's Reach by Black Bean
restaurant.desc: Molly's Reach by Black Bean occupies one of British Columbia's most storied cafe buildings — a Gibsons landmark that served as the primary filming location for the CBC series 'The Beachcombers' from 1972 to 1990. Since December 2024, the Black Bean Cafe has brought its locally roasted Sunshine Coast coffee and daily house-baked goods to this iconic waterfront address. It's a walk-in, no-reservations spot with outdoor seating and a relaxed coastal atmosphere — an easy diversion for cyclists arriving via the Langdale ferry.

restaurant.name: The Royal
restaurant.desc: The Royal Grill is a restaurant located on Baker Street in Nelson, BC, a cycling-friendly downtown corridor. Beyond its OSM listing as a restaurant, no current details about cuisine, atmosphere, or cyclist-specific features can be confirmed, as the business's registered domain has been taken over by unrelated gambling content. A visit or direct call would be needed to assess its suitability for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Roy's Towne Pub
restaurant.desc: Roy's Towne Pub is a well-established neighbourhood pub sitting right on the South Island Highway in Royston, in the heart of the Comox Valley between Courtenay and Union Bay. Under current ownership since 2021, it serves classic pub meals, cold drinks, and hosts regular live music featuring local artists across rock, folk, Celtic, jazz, country, and blues. It's a genuine community hub with ample on-site parking and a welcoming, family-friendly atmosphere.

restaurant.name: The Kitchen
restaurant.desc: The Kitchen is a restaurant on Sasamat Street in Vancouver. As a food establishment, it can serve as a rest stop for touring cyclists. Specific details about amenities and services could not be verified due to website access failure.

restaurant.name: Pho Canada
restaurant.desc: Pho Canada is a Vietnamese restaurant in Surrey serving an extensive menu of pho noodle soups, stews, fried plates, and appetizers including salad rolls and spring rolls. The menu spans dozens of pho variations — beef, chicken, seafood, and vegetarian — making it a substantial stop for a hungry touring cyclist. The restaurant is located in a unit at a Surrey strip-style address on 100 Avenue.

restaurant.name: L'OTUS Cake Boutique
restaurant.desc: L'OTUS Cake Boutique is an artisan cake shop specializing in handcrafted crepe cakes, chiffon layer cakes, cheesecakes, and gelato with Asian-inspired flavour profiles such as matcha yuzu and mango sticky rice. It operates on a pre-order pickup model, so cyclists planning a stop should order in advance. The boutique offers a distinctive selection of visually elaborate celebration cakes that would make an unusual but memorable mid-tour treat.

restaurant.name: White Sails Taproom
restaurant.desc: White Sails is an award-winning craft brewery and taproom that has been a fixture of downtown Nanaimo since 2015, located across from Maffeo Sutton Park. The large, open-concept west-coast-inspired space seats over 100 guests and offers up to 14 beers on tap alongside wines, ciders, a full coffee bar, and a hyper-local food menu sourced from neighbourhood butchers, bakers, and cheese-makers. Its medal-winning flagship beers and rotating small-batch releases make it a genuine destination stop on any Vancouver Island cycling route.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast food restaurant situated on the busy Kingsway corridor in Vancouver, serving burgers, chicken, breakfast items, and McCafé beverages. The location includes both indoor and outdoor seating areas and a drive-through lane. It sits on a well-travelled urban cycling route connecting Burnaby and Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Tonics Pub & Grill
restaurant.desc: Tonics Pub is a downtown Kelowna institution on Ellis Street, offering an extensive tap selection of 11 domestic and imported beers alongside premium spirits and wines in a casual setting. The venue features two of the largest screens in Kelowna, drawing crowds for games and events. Its menu reaches well beyond standard pub fare, with an emphasis on home-style quality — a solid option for a meal stop in the heart of the city.

restaurant.name: The Farmhouse
restaurant.desc: The Farmhouse is an intimate Italian restaurant housed in a restored heritage home in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, featuring a backyard patio and a short service bar overlooking the open kitchen. Its kitchen is stocked by local BC growers and foragers — notably Campagna Farm in Abbotsford — weaving West Coast seasonality into classic Italian antipasti, mains, and desserts. The restaurant is part of the Viaggio Hospitality group and offers brunch through late dinner service alongside a curated list of biodynamic and organic wines from BC and Italy.

restaurant.name: The Locavore Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Locavore Bar & Grill grew from a humble food truck into a vibrant hybrid indoor/outdoor venue set inside former greenhouses on the edge of Squamish, sharing a property with the Cloudburst Cafe. The kitchen focuses on local BC flavours for lunch and dinner, with a bar program built around regional cocktails, beer, and wine. The venue explicitly positions itself as a destination for unwinding after mountain biking or hiking, making it a natural stop on the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

restaurant.name: New Amsterdam Cafe
restaurant.desc: Founded in 1998, New Amsterdam Cafe bills itself as North America's first 420-friendly cafe and one of the oldest cannabis companies in the world, operating as an inclusive cannabis-inspired lounge in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood. The venue combines a relaxed lounge atmosphere with food, drinks, catering, and event bookings, and hosts the annual Cannabis Hospitality Summit. Patrons must be 19 or older to enter.

restaurant.name: Mucho Burrito
restaurant.desc: Mucho Burrito is a Canadian fast-casual Mexican chain serving burritos, bowls, quesadillas, and tacos with a 'Modern Mexicana' approach emphasising fresh ingredients. This Tsawwassen location sits at 4949 Canoe Pass Way — close to the Tsawwassen ferry terminal, making it a plausible quick-fuel stop for cyclists arriving or departing on BC Ferries routes. Vegan and vegetarian options are available across the menu.

restaurant.name: Black Frog Eatery
restaurant.desc: Black Frog Eatery is a sports bar, restaurant, and live entertainment venue perched on the edge of Gastown with waterfront views of Vancouver harbour. A long-standing local institution, it draws locals, tourists, and sports fans with multiple big screens, rotating BC craft beers, and a packed event calendar of live music, stand-up comedy, and trivia nights. Its all-season patio and hearty pub menu make it a lively food-and-drink anchor in one of Vancouver's most visited neighbourhoods.

restaurant.name: Sagewood winery
restaurant.desc: Sagewood Winery is a small estate winery on the outskirts of Kamloops producing a broad range of whites, reds, rosé, and sparkling wines from their own vineyard. The operation emphasizes sustainable practices including biodiversity, drip irrigation, and organic methods in the vineyard. The property is dog-friendly and welcomes visitors for tastings, making it an appealing rural stop for touring cyclists exploring Thompson Valley wine country.

restaurant.name: Thai Cook
restaurant.desc: Thai Cook is an authentic Thai restaurant on Victoria Crescent in downtown Nanaimo, serving dine-in, takeout, and delivery. The menu spans curries, noodles, stir-fries, and appetizers with spice levels ranging from mild to Thai hot. Many dishes are gluten-free, and multiple tofu and vegetable protein options appear throughout both the lunch and dinner menus.

restaurant.name: Mi Casa Mexicana

The menu focuses on handmade pozole, birria, tacos, and tamales built from family recipes and daily-fresh ingredients. Touring cyclists will find a warm sit-down spot with takeout available and gluten-free options on the menu.

restaurant.name: Champagnes Exotic Show Lounge

restaurant.name: OPA! of Greece
restaurant.desc: OPA! of Greece is a Canadian Greek quick-service chain that has been grilling souvlaki skewers, pita wraps, and gyros since 1998. The Chilliwack outlet is located inside Cottonwood Mall, offering a sheltered indoor stop for touring cyclists needing a substantial calorie refuel. The menu spans chicken, lamb, beef, shrimp, and falafel proteins alongside salads and sides.

restaurant.name: The Grad House Restaurant
