It offers sit-down dining, table reservations by email, and in-house catering for both public and private events. Cyclists exploring the UVic campus grounds will find it a convenient meal stop, with the venue welcoming all guests.

restaurant.name: Captain Thai Noodle House
restaurant.desc: Captain Thai Noodle House is a Thai restaurant on Kingsway, one of Vancouver's main arterial roads connecting the city to Burnaby. OSM tags it as a cafe serving Thai cuisine with indoor seating. Its location on a busy commuter corridor makes it a convenient stop for cyclists riding the Kingsway route.

restaurant.name: Les Faux Bourgeois
restaurant.desc: Les Faux Bourgeois is an award-winning French bistro and café on East 15th Avenue in Vancouver's east side, consistently voted the city's best French restaurant by Georgia Straight readers across multiple years. The menu centres on classic Parisian bistro fare — duck confit, beef tartare, French onion soup — in a relaxed neighbourhood setting that one reviewer likened to the bistros of Paris itself. A take-out option is available for cyclists wanting to eat on the move.

restaurant.name: CHAU Cafe

restaurant.name: Kinton Ramen
restaurant.desc: Kinton Ramen is a Canadian ramen chain with over 50 locations, serving authentic Japanese-style ramen with pork, beef, chicken, and vegetarian broths at their newly opened McArthurGlen Designer Outlet YVR location in Richmond. The brand is known for its customizable bowls — diners choose soup base, flavour (original, shoyu, miso, or spicy), and noodle type — and for greeting every guest with the Japanese welcome 'irasshaimase.' The outlet location is situated within a large designer shopping complex near the YVR airport corridor.

restaurant.name: Janevca
restaurant.desc: Janevca is a fine dining restaurant housed in a heritage building in Victoria's Esquimalt neighbourhood, built around a team of seasoned culinary professionals including an award-winning Red Seal pastry chef and a sommelier with over 30 years of experience at establishments such as The Ritz Carlton Montreal and Hôtel Westminster Paris. The menu takes a dynamic, seasonal approach and the beverage program is curated to pair precisely with each dish. A lounge and veranda provide a walk-in-friendly alternative to the reservation-only main dining room.

restaurant.name: The Wolf and Hound
restaurant.desc: The Wolf and Hound is a full-service Irish pub on Vancouver's West Broadway corridor, founded in 2002 as a tribute to the late Danny Burns — a Belfast musician and beloved figure of Vancouver's Irish diaspora. The pub carries on his legacy with live entertainment nights, a full drinks menu, brunch and dinner service, and private event bookings. A touring cyclist arriving on the Broadway corridor would find a sit-down pub atmosphere with food and drink options across several menu categories.

restaurant.name: The Greek by Anatoli
restaurant.desc: The Greek by Anatoli is a Greek restaurant in Yaletown, Vancouver, part of a three-location group (Yaletown, Gastown, North Vancouver) with over 40 years of hospitality behind it. The Yaletown location sits on Mainland Street and offers a lively Mediterranean dining room with indoor and outdoor seating, handcrafted cocktails, and a broad menu of grilled meats, fresh seafood, and house-made dips. Private dining spaces and a full catering service make it a capable stop for groups as well as solo riders.

restaurant.name: Marmalade Bakery

They also stock grab-and-go lunch items and specialty coffees and teas, making it a convenient mid-ride food stop near Skaha Lake. Vegan and gluten-free options are woven throughout the menu.

restaurant.name: Noodlebox
restaurant.desc: Noodlebox is a BC-founded franchise chain serving customizable Asian-inspired noodle and rice boxes made fresh to order at a counter-service format. It is a practical hot-meal stop for touring cyclists passing through South Surrey.

The Korean cuisine focus suggests hearty, carb-rich meals well-suited to refuelling after a long ride.

restaurant.name: Angelina's Dutch Corner
restaurant.desc: Angelina's Dutch Corner is a family-owned restaurant at the New Westminster Quay waterfront, serving authentic Dutch-inspired breakfast and lunch in a warm, kid-friendly setting with scenic river views. It has been a community institution for over two decades — a decade under current owner Eric Missouri — and prides itself on locally and responsibly sourced ingredients. The quayside pedestrian-zone patio and welcoming atmosphere make it a natural rest stop on any Lower Mainland cycling route.

restaurant.name: Lee Garden
restaurant.desc: Lee Garden Seafood is a Chinese dim sum and seafood restaurant located in Coquitlam's Pinetree Way area, serving both traditional dim sum and a full all-day menu with items like crystal prawn dumplings and sticky rice lotus leaf wraps. It is one of two Lower Mainland locations and offers online ordering with pickup. A touring cyclist passing through Coquitlam would find it a substantial sit-down meal option.

restaurant.name: My Thai Café

restaurant.name: Le Gateau Bakeshop

The shop has earned recognition from Rocky Mountain Bride (Best of 2023) and a Food Network win, and has been featured in PEOPLE magazine and numerous wedding publications. Cyclists passing through East Hastings can pick up freshly baked pastries, cupcakes, and cookies from the daily in-store selection, or pre-order for pickup.

restaurant.name: Mission Springs Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Mission Springs Brewing Company is one of BC's oldest craft brewhouses, operating since 1996 in a 10-barrel facility overlooking the Fraser River in Mission. The pub and restaurant offers its own lineup of craft beers on tap alongside a full food menu, with beer also available in growlers, cans, and kegs to take home. Three patios and a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere make it a natural gathering spot for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

Part of a growing Vancouver Island chain with additional locations in Sidney, Oak Bay, and Duncan, the restaurant offers both elegant dine-in service and private event hosting. restaurant.name: Pita Pit

The menu includes calorie-labelled signature recipes and a fully customizable build-your-own option, making it a practical stop for cyclists wanting a filling, relatively healthy meal.

restaurant.name: Hunter Gatherer

Walk-ins of all group sizes are welcome, making it a natural pit stop for cyclists passing through the valley.

restaurant.name: The Mad Hen

restaurant.name: Pizza Pietra

Both delivery and in-person takeout are available with online ordering through the website.

restaurant.name: Origin Bakery & Cafe
restaurant.desc: Origin Bakery & Cafe is a 100% dedicated gluten-free bakery and cafe with two Victoria-area locations, founded in 2009 and now expanding through franchising. The Langford (Belmont) branch offers a full range of fresh baked goods including breads, breakfast items, lunch, cakes, pastries, and cookies, made using over 20 alternative gluten-free flour substitutes. Touring cyclists with celiac disease or gluten sensitivities will find a rare dedicated safe-space bakery that also accommodates dairy-free, egg-free, nut-free, and soy-free diets.

restaurant.name: Best Garden Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Best Garden Restaurant is a long-established casual Chinese dining room that has been serving South Delta since 1991, offering an extensive Cantonese and Szechuan menu prepared without MSG. It operates as a licensed premises with both dine-in and takeout available, as well as home delivery to Tsawwassen and Ladner. A touring cyclist will find a welcoming, unpretentious neighbourhood restaurant with free Wi-Fi.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists multiple vegetarian items including Vegetarian Egg Roll, Mixed Veg. Chow Mein, Mushroom Chow Mein, Vegetable Fried Rice, and Lettuce Wrap (Vegetables)

restaurant.name: NiNNiN Ramen House
restaurant.desc: NiNNiN Ramen House is a ramen-focused restaurant on Abbott Street in Vancouver's downtown area, offering indoor dining in a non-smoking environment. It operates without a drive-through, making it a sit-down destination for cyclists looking to refuel with a hot bowl of ramen after a ride.

restaurant.name: Cherry's Food House
restaurant.desc: Cherry's Food House is a Chinese restaurant in Richmond providing sit-down dining service. It serves as a reliable meal option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: 75 West Coast Grill
restaurant.desc: 75 West Coast Grill is a full-service restaurant inside the Vancouver Airport Marriott Hotel in Richmond, specializing in flavour-forward West Coast dishes alongside a curated selection of BC wines and local craft beers. The modern, cozy space features bar and lounge seating, and the restaurant regularly hosts live music nights, wine pairing dinners, and weekend brunch specials. It sits along Westminster Highway in the YVR corridor, a part of Richmond that is accessible by bicycle.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels a 'Vegetarian' omelette (roasted mushrooms, spinach, goat cheese, basil); plant-friendly items such as Greek Yogurt & Granola and oatmeal also appear on the menu

restaurant.name: Lieto Cafe
restaurant.desc: Lieto Cafe is a cafe situated in a commercial unit on 72 Avenue in Langley, BC. Its Facebook page handle suggests it launched in 2023, making it a relatively new addition to the local food scene. Touring cyclists passing through the Langley area may find it a convenient stop along the 72 Avenue corridor.

restaurant.name: Six Mile Pub
restaurant.desc: The Six Mile Pub & Eatery holds the distinction of being British Columbia's oldest pub, operating continuously since 1855 in a historic two-storey building beside Millstream. The kitchen produces everything from artisan breads and fresh pastas to house-made sausages and honey sourced from their on-site apiary, with a strong emphasis on locally and ethically sourced ingredients. A riverside patio opens seasonally, making it a scenic and substantial stop for touring cyclists passing through the Colwood/Langford corridor.

detail.address: 494 Old Island Hwy at Six Mile Rd, Victoria, BC V9B 1H5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menus page states 'From our tradition pub favourites to our gluten-free program, we have something for you.' Gluten-free confirmed; vegetarian/vegan not explicitly stated

restaurant.name: Dex Burger Bar & Vinam Vietnamese Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Dex Burger Bar is a burger-focused fast food spot on Chadwick Court in North Vancouver. It sits in a commercial area of the lower North Shore, a common staging ground for cyclists heading to or from the Sea-to-Sky corridor. Beyond being a potential quick-refuel stop, no further details about the venue or its cyclist amenities could be confirmed.

restaurant.name: Cockney Kings Fish and Chips
restaurant.desc: A family-owned Vancouver institution serving classic English-style fish and chips since 1965, Cockney Kings fries in beef tallow for a distinctly traditional British flavour and offers cod, haddock, snapper, salmon, and halibut. The Main Street Mount Pleasant location is the newest in the chain, opened in early 2026 by the same family that has run the brand for decades. Dine-in and takeout are both available, with online ordering supported directly through the website.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms gluten-friendly options (grilled/steamed fish, salads, corn tortilla fish tacos) with shared-fryer caveat, and vegetarian-suitable salads and sides; deep-fried items including chips use beef tallow so are not vegan

restaurant.name: Rocanini Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Rocanini Coffee Roasters is an artisan coffee company established in 2010, its name derived from the Latin word for 'rock' in homage to Italian tradition — evoking a foundation of strength and presence. Beyond handcrafted beverages, the cafe sells freshly roasted coffee beans, tea, and brewing equipment on-site. The company also runs a wholesale operation and offers private cupping and barista training for those pursuing a deeper coffee education.

restaurant.name: Eivan
restaurant.desc: Eivan is a restaurant located on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Embers BBQ House
restaurant.desc: Embers BBQ House is a family-owned-and-operated comfort food restaurant that has been serving authentic slow-smoked BBQ for over 15 years. Now located in Mission on the north bank of the Fraser River, the restaurant features an open kitchen and dining concept where guests can watch the cooking in action. Their signature slow-roasted pulled pork drives a menu of sandwiches, poutines, and wraps popular with returning customers.

restaurant.name: Cafe Artigiano
restaurant.desc: Artigiano is a pioneering Vancouver specialty coffee chain with over 25 years in BC's coffee culture, now operating 25 locations across BC and Alberta. The Davie Street location is one of the brand's Cafe Bar outposts, offering locally roasted 100% Arabica espresso drinks alongside cocktails, fresh sourdough pizzas, and light Italian bites in the evenings. The brand is known for internationally award-winning barista craft and house-made baked goods sourced from organic and seasonal ingredients.

restaurant.name: Mom's Cafe
restaurant.desc: Mom's Cafe is a casual dining restaurant located in Sooke on Shields Road. It provides food service to local customers and travelers passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Di Beppe
restaurant.desc: Di Beppe is an Italian caffè and ristorante in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, self-described as 'a young Italian restaurant with an old Italian soul.' The front caffè room serves morning espresso and transitions into a wine bar by evening, also housing a deli, pastry shop, and retail market — all in one warm space. Part of the KT Restaurants group, the menu spans antipasti, house-made pasta, Neapolitan-style pizza, and a daily aperitivo hour.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Lunch/dinner menu labels vegetarian items with (v) and vegan items with (vg); gluten-free pasta is offered as a +$3 substitution on all pasta dishes

restaurant.name: Gold Train Express Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Gold Train Express is a Vietnamese restaurant on Kingsway in East Vancouver offering an extensive menu of pho, rice dishes, banh mi, spring rolls, and Vietnamese drinks. It has built a loyal local following over the years, with 28 reviews consistently praising the pho broth and lemongrass chicken. Online ordering with fast pickup makes it a practical meal stop for cyclists passing through this busy corridor.

restaurant.name: Showcase Restaurant & Bar
restaurant.desc: Showcase Restaurant & Bar is a casual-dining restaurant inside the Vancouver Marriott Pinnacle Downtown in Coal Harbour. It features West Coast cuisine with seasonally inspired menus emphasizing locally and regionally sourced ingredients, plus a bar with local craft beers, BC wines, and hand-crafted cocktails. The restaurant also offers breakfast, brunch, and private event dining, making it a convenient stop in the downtown core.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website happy hour page states 'Vegan Option Available' and 'Gluten Sensitive With Additional Options Available'; OSM confirms; menu emphasizes diverse West Coast cuisine

restaurant.name: Doc Morgan's
restaurant.desc: Doc Morgan's is an oceanfront restaurant and pub on Bowen Island serving elevated West Coast comfort food with an emphasis on fresh local seafood, including oysters and fish and chips. Located at the Union Steamship Marina, it is the island's main sit-down dining destination and caters to both casual visitors and private group events. For a touring cyclist arriving by ferry, it offers a welcoming spot to refuel with a full menu in a waterfront setting.

detail.address: 439 Bowen Island Trunk Road, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G0

restaurant.name: Cuhillo
restaurant.desc: Cuchillo (spelled 'Cuhillo' in OSM) is a Mexican restaurant on Powell Street in Vancouver's East Side offering food, drinks, and a late-night menu. The venue has a private downstairs room called 'The Boogie Van' that can host up to 60 guests, and a 'Harvest Table' used for group dining. It is a sit-down dinner destination rather than a quick-service stop.

restaurant.name: Banchan Su
restaurant.desc: Banchan Su is a Korean food shop in New Westminster specializing in authentic banchan (Korean side dishes), soups, stews, braised meats, and kimchi available for individual takeout via online order. The business also offers event catering and meal box delivery with rotating weekly set menus featuring traditional Korean home-style cooking. A touring cyclist passing through New Westminster can order ready-to-eat items ranging from kimchi and braised tofu to LA-style short ribs and japchae for a hearty, flavourful stop.

notes.Packed lunches: Dedicated MealBox (도시락) section on website offers packaged bento-style meal boxes with rice, soup, kimchi, salad, and side dishes; minimum order 20 units, also available for events

restaurant.name: Crimson Café
restaurant.desc: Crimson Café is a cafe in Chilliwack operating from a central location. The venue was previously known as the Spotted Owl Bar and Air Fare Lounge. It maintains an online presence through Facebook.

restaurant.name: Sizzling Wok
restaurant.desc: Sizzling Wok is a Chinese fast-food counter located inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre, Kelowna's large enclosed mall on the Harvey Avenue corridor. It specialises in a 'pick your own combo' format, letting customers choose a base of rice or noodles and then select from dishes such as sesame chicken, BBQ pork, sweet and sour pork, and a variety of vegetables. For cyclists riding through the Harvey Avenue commercial strip, it offers a quick and filling hot meal in a sheltered indoor setting.

restaurant.name: Refuge Tap Room
restaurant.desc: Refuge Tap Room is a 38-seat craft beverage bar on Fort Street in downtown Victoria, dedicated exclusively to BC-made products: 21 craft beers, five craft ciders, small-batch spirits, and wines on tap. A secluded back patio and a covered, heated courtyard make it a welcoming place to decompress at the end of a riding day. Sharable small plates—charcuterie, marinated olives, cured sausage—sourced from local providers round out the offering.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast food restaurant on McCallum Road in Chilliwack, part of the McCallum Junction commercial area. It offers drive-through and takeaway service, making it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists passing through. Free Wi-Fi is available according to OSM tags.

restaurant.name: Corona's Mexican Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Corona's Mexican Restaurant Inc is a sit-down and takeout Mexican eatery serving a wide range of traditional dishes including tacos, burritos, quesadillas, dinner platters, and soups such as pozole and birria ramen. Located in a unit at 32555 London Ave in Mission, it offers online ordering with a 15-minute pickup window, making it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley. The menu includes vegetarian options across multiple categories.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Vegetariana' variants under Tacos, Burritos, and Quesadillas, with a vegetarian legend indicator

restaurant.name: Torquay Village Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Torquay Village Restaurant is an all-day brunch spot operating as part of The Village franchise in Victoria's Shelbourne Valley neighbourhood, just a short distance from Lambrick Park. The menu leans into creative eggs benedict variations, bagels, and directly traded, locally roasted coffee, and the business was voted Best Breakfast in the City in 2020. Both a dining room with patio and a takeout option are available, with takeout orders packed specifically for travel.

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: Tim Hortons is a major Canadian coffee and quick-service restaurant chain. It serves as a convenient rest stop for touring cyclists to purchase beverages, light food, and takeaway items.

restaurant.name: The Hungry Duck Grill Kitchen
restaurant.desc: The Hungry Duck Grill Kitchen is a Japanese grill restaurant at 1835 West 4th Avenue in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighborhood. It sits along a well-traveled cycling corridor on Vancouver's west side, within easy reach of the Arbutus Greenway and the Seaside route. No additional detail about the restaurant's interior, seating, or menu style could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Pho 99
restaurant.desc: Pho 99 is a Vietnamese noodle restaurant in Delta offering traditional pho and noodle-based Vietnamese cuisine. It provides a casual dining option for touring cyclists seeking authentic Asian food along Scott Road.

restaurant.name: Woudas Bakery
restaurant.desc: Woudas Bakery is a locally owned Dutch bakery and cafe situated in Penticton's Apple Plaza Mall, offering a wide selection of freshly baked breads — including sourdough, rye, and multigrain varieties — alongside pastries, desserts, and specialty cakes. For cyclists looking to refuel mid-ride, the cafe serves fresh soup, salads, and sandwiches at lunch as well as hot coffee. The extensive gluten-free dessert options (brownie, chocolate ganache slice, hazelnut mousse) make it a notable stop for riders with dietary restrictions.

restaurant.name: TOUK
restaurant.desc: TOUK is a contemporary Cambodian restaurant in Vancouver's West End helmed by Chef Chanthy Yen, winner of Top Chef Canada Season 11 and alumnus of world-renowned kitchens including Ferran Adrià's. The restaurant takes its name from Bon Om Touk, the Cambodian water festival, and weaves together BC's local seafood, produce, and seasonal harvests with Cambodian flavours and French bistro technique. A touring cyclist looking for a distinctive, chef-driven meal on the waterfront edge of downtown Vancouver will find a seasonally evolving menu with strong local-sourcing credentials.

restaurant.name: The Monkey Tree Pub
restaurant.desc: The Monkey Tree Pub is a spacious Victoria neighbourhood pub that has been a community gathering place since 1986, founded by BC hospitality icon Gordon Card on a commitment to craft food and drink. The kitchen uses fresh, hand-cut ingredients and runs rotating seasonal specials alongside pub classics, while the bar offers a daily happy hour and rotating beer and cocktail selections. The venue also operates an on-site liquor store and accepts takeout orders by phone.

restaurant.name: Scoopz Ice Cream Parlour
restaurant.desc: Scoopz Ice Cream Parlor is an ice cream shop on Lorne Street in downtown Kamloops, a city that sits at the junction of two major river valleys and sees intense summer heat — making a cold treat a genuine draw for touring cyclists. Its downtown location places it within easy reach of the Trans Canada Trail corridor and the Thompson River cycling routes that pass through the city.

restaurant.name: Earls
restaurant.desc: Earls Station Square is a full-service Kitchen + Bar situated in Burnaby's Station Square development, part of a well-established Canadian casual-dining chain with locations across BC and North America. The restaurant offers both indoor seating and an outdoor patio, a broad American-style menu with vegan and vegetarian options, and accepts cash as well as cards. It sits within a large mixed-use complex and is a comfortable sit-down stop for cyclists passing through the Metrotown corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: No contradiction found in website content

restaurant.name: Dragonboat Pub
restaurant.desc: Dragonboat Pub is a waterfront pub and restaurant situated on the shores of Skaha Lake in Penticton, offering craft beer, a full bar, and an extensive pub menu ranging from fish and chips to sushi rolls and grain bowls. It is a family-friendly and dog-friendly destination with a patio and a live webcam of the lake. The pub has deep ties to the local community, supporting organizations such as Ronald McDonald House BC and Penticton Paddle Sports.

restaurant.name: Parker Place Food Court
restaurant.desc: Parker Place Food Court is a multi-vendor food service venue in Richmond. It provides a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists seeking diverse quick-service options. The shared dining environment makes it suitable for casual breaks during cycling tours.

restaurant.name: Clive's Classic Lounge
restaurant.desc: Established in 2008, Clive's Classic Lounge is Victoria's longest-standing cocktail bar, located on the lobby level of the Chateau Victoria Hotel and named in honour of the hotel's founder, Clive Piercy. The bar has earned seven nominations for Canada's Best International Hotel Bar at the Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Awards and is known for its rotating seasonal cocktail menu, one of Victoria's largest whisky collections, and a food program built around locally-sourced small plates and sharing platters. The intimate, speakeasy-style space features commissioned artwork and trophy fish that reflect the legacy of the outdoorsman it honours.

restaurant.name: Eh! Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A restaurant located at 1050 Alberni Street in downtown Vancouver. Specific amenities and cuisine details cannot be verified as the website is currently unreachable.

restaurant.name: Trees Organic Coffee
restaurant.desc: Trees Organic Coffee is a Vancouver institution operating since 1996, celebrated for its award-winning homemade cheesecakes and small-batch roasted organic coffee across 14 locations in the city. The 450 Granville Street downtown location doubles as a live music venue with free Thursday and Friday evening performances. Cyclists passing through downtown Vancouver will find indoor and outdoor seating, a full menu of sandwiches and baked goods, and online ordering with in-store pickup.

restaurant.name: Ton Ton Sushi
restaurant.desc: Ton Ton Sushi is a Japanese-Korean sushi restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver, offering a menu that includes vegan and vegetarian options alongside traditional sushi. The restaurant operates an online ordering platform and mobile app. It sits on a busy cycling corridor (Broadway), making it a plausible mid-ride or post-ride stop.

restaurant.name: The Rendezvous Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Rendezvous Restaurant is a family-owned Greek and Italian restaurant established in 1994 and located in Abbotsford's Old Clayburn Mall. It serves pizza, pasta, and traditional Greek dishes, with house-made dressings and sauces as signature items — including the famous Rendezvous Dressing, available by the bottle to take home. A warm, casual dining room and the ability to host private groups of 20–45 make it a practical stop for cycling groups passing through the Fraser Valley.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'For takeout please call 604-853-9911'; in-house delivery also available after 4pm

restaurant.name: Orto Artisan Pasta
restaurant.desc: Orto Artisan Pasta is a small Italian restaurant in North Vancouver founded by veteran restaurateur Brigitte Raye, specializing in handmade pasta crafted from fresh, in-house ingredients. The restaurant shares its space with local bakery Bad Dog Bread and features a lush urban garden patio with a grape vine, quince tree, and herbs that transforms into an outdoor dining area in the warmer months. Cyclists passing through can refuel with dine-in lunches or dinners, or pick up daily takeout.

detail.address: 1600 MacKay Road, North Vancouver, BC V7P 2M4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Prix fixe menu lists 'Vegetarian lasagna' as a main course option

restaurant.name: Pho Japolo
restaurant.desc: Pho Japolo is a proudly family-run Vietnamese and Japanese fusion restaurant that has been serving the Lower Mainland since 1995, growing from a single storefront to four locations. The Richmond outpost offers hearty bowls of beef noodle soup alongside inventive sushi creations like the signature sushi pizza. It is a sit-down restaurant with takeout available, making it a practical and satisfying stop for cyclists needing a substantial meal.

notes.Takeout: Menu page notes 'for take-out, only large available' and the Richmond locations page includes an 'Order Online' link

restaurant.name: Sangam Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: An Indian restaurant in Chilliwack located on Vedder Road. Serves Indian cuisine to the local community.

restaurant.name: Pür & Simple
restaurant.desc: Pür & Simple is a breakfast-and-brunch franchise restaurant in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, serving creative comfort-food classics like Eggs Benedict, French toast, pancakes, and smoothies. It is one of 65+ Canadian locations in this growing chain, positioning itself as an 'upscale' daytime dining destination with dine-in, takeout, and delivery options. The wide menu includes dedicated vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-sensitive categories, making it accessible to cyclists with varied dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu pages label items V (vegetarian), Vg (vegan), and include a 'gluten sensitive' category

restaurant.name: Sushi Story
restaurant.desc: Sushi Story is an authentic Japanese restaurant situated in Victoria's Vic West neighbourhood on Head Street, a short ride from the Gorge waterway and the downtown core. The restaurant offers dine-in service alongside an online ordering platform with local delivery, making it a convenient stop for cyclists looking for a Japanese meal near the waterfront.

notes.Takeout: Website prominently features 'Order Online' and a delivery/takeout service for orders over $50 within 3 km, confirming takeout is available

restaurant.name: Mean Poutine
restaurant.desc: Mean Poutine is a family-run takeout-only poutine and hot dog shop founded in 2011 by a former BC Lions football player in Vancouver's Granville entertainment district. The restaurant serves gourmet poutines with handcrafted recipes and a variety of toppings, including vegetarian options, and has since expanded to New Westminster and Ontario. With no indoor or outdoor seating, it is strictly a walk-up counter service spot suited to cyclists needing a quick, filling meal on the go.

notes.Takeout: No indoor or outdoor seating (capacity=0); website menus and locations page confirm counter-service takeout-only model at all locations
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian options confirmed: 'Mean And Green' poutine (vegetarian gravy) and 'Veggie Dog' on Downtown Vancouver menu. Website states 'we do not offer Gluten Free options on our poutine, hot dogs or fries menu.' No vegan options

restaurant.name: Kopitiam Malaysia
restaurant.desc: Kopitiam Malaysia is a sit-down Malaysian restaurant in East Vancouver serving authentic dishes such as Laksa, Roti Canai, Hainanese Chicken, Bak Kut Teh, and Sambal Kang Kong. The word 'kopitiam' refers to a traditional Malaysian coffee shop, and the restaurant leans into that heritage with recipes emphasizing fresh ingredients and culinary authenticity. Online ordering and table reservations are available, giving touring cyclists flexibility in how they plan a meal stop.

restaurant.name: C Market Coffee
restaurant.desc: C Market Coffee takes its name from the global Arabica commodity exchange and has grown into a multi-location café chain across the Tri-Cities and Pitt Meadows area. The Pitt Meadows outpost sits at 19265 Airport Way and offers in-house-roasted coffee alongside fresh food, matcha, Korean Kkokdam tea, and baked goods. Beyond the cup, the business runs coffee classes, pop-up markets, and room rentals, positioning itself as a community hub as well as a quick-service café.

detail.address: 19265 Airport Way, Unit 301a, Pitt Meadows, BC V3Y 2M5

restaurant.name: The Lakehouse at Shawnigan
restaurant.desc: The Lakehouse at Shawnigan is a farm-to-table lakeside restaurant and accommodation venue situated at the end of the west arm of Shawnigan Lake in the Cowichan Valley, featuring three patios, a large dock, and water views from every table. The seasonally changing menu rigorously sources from local Cowichan Valley farms, breweries, cideries, and wineries. The About page explicitly invites guests to arrive by foot, bicycle, or car, making it a natural destination for cyclists exploring the Shawnigan Lake area.

detail.address: 2460 Renfrew Rd, Shawnigan Lake, BC V8H 2E5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page tags multiple items as VEG (e.g. Falafel Burger, Mac and Cheese, Corn & Queso Dip) and GF (e.g. Roasted Asparagus Salad, Albacore Tuna, Dirty Fries)

restaurant.name: Blue Water Cafe + raw bar
restaurant.desc: Blue Water Cafe + raw bar is a landmark seafood restaurant in the heart of Yaletown, celebrating 25 years of operation with a raw bar showcasing daily-rotating oysters, Dungeness crab, and chilled seafood prepared by Executive Chef Frank Pabst and Sushi Chef Masaaki Kudo. The restaurant offers both indoor dining and a garden patio with a retractable awning, situated in one of Vancouver's most cycling-accessible waterfront neighbourhoods.

restaurant.name: Tractor
restaurant.desc: Tractor Foods is a BC-born healthy fast-casual chain founded in 2013, serving scratch-made salads, soups, breakfast bowls, and sandwiches with a focus on local and plant-forward ingredients. The Victoria Harbour outpost on Government Street sits in the heart of downtown Victoria's main tourist and commercial corridor — a practical refuelling stop for cyclists riding through the city centre. Online ordering with quick pickup turnaround makes it easy to grab a meal without a long wait.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website catering page describes food as 'plant-forward' and 'locally sourced'

restaurant.name: Yume Dining
restaurant.desc: Yume Dining is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Vancouver offering online ordering and takeout options. Located on West 2nd Avenue, it provides a convenient food stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: El Camino's
restaurant.desc: El Camino's is a Latin American street food restaurant and cocktail bar on Main Street in Vancouver, serving Mexican and South American-inspired dishes—tacos, ceviche, empanadas, and poutine—alongside craft cocktails and a well-curated local beer list. The kitchen also runs a weekend brunch program with dishes like Huevos Rancheros and Chilaquiles. It is part of a small local hospitality group that also operates The Cascade Room nearby.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu header reads 'GF: GLUTEN-FREE | CC: CROSS-CONTACT | V: VEGAN | DF: DAIRY-FREE'; multiple dishes across snacks, small plates, tacos, and brunch are individually labelled GF, V, and/or DF

restaurant.name: Bonnie Martin Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Bonnie Martin Restaurant is a family-run diner in Chemainus, BC, serving home-style Canadian and Chinese cuisine since 1998. Open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner with all menu items available all day, it's a well-established local favourite offering everything from omelettes and eggs benny to burgers and steak. Eat-in and takeout options make it a practical stop for cyclists passing through Chemainus.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a Veggie Omelette ('Three-egg omelette with chopped veggies topped with cheddar cheese'). No vegan or gluten-free options explicitly identified

restaurant.name: Chun Fun How
restaurant.desc: Chun Fun How is a Taiwanese bubble tea brand with three Greater Vancouver locations, founded on the heritage and entrepreneurial spirit of its founder's father in Taiwan. The Kingsway location offers an extensive menu spanning osmanthus milk teas, purple yam fresh milk green teas, aloe vera fruit teas, and seasonal specials rooted in authentic Taiwanese ingredients. The brand also offers catering via a 3-litre party box format and free everyday delivery, making it a versatile refreshment stop.

restaurant.name: Dolpan Seoul BBQ
restaurant.desc: Dolpan Seoul BBQ is a Korean BBQ restaurant situated in Richmond's Sexsmith Road area, offering the communal tabletop-grill dining experience characteristic of Seoul-style BBQ. The restaurant also takes online orders for pickup and delivery directly through its own website. It would serve as a hearty refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the Richmond area.

restaurant.name: Cypress Creek Lodge
restaurant.desc: Cypress Creek Lodge is the main base lodge at Cypress Mountain resort, perched high above West Vancouver at the end of the steep Cypress Bowl Road climb. The lodge houses the Gold Medal Cafe (light breakfast, coffee and tea) and the Cypress Creek Grill food court, plus the Big Bear Sports retail store and resort guest services. For touring cyclists who have made the demanding ascent to Cypress Mountain, it serves as a natural rest stop with food, shelter, and sweeping views of the North Shore.

detail.address: 6000 Cypress Bowl Road, West Vancouver, BC V7V 3N9

restaurant.name: Giancarlo Cafe
restaurant.desc: Giancarlo Cafe is an Italian cafe on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most beloved cycling corridors and a hub for independent coffee culture in the East Side. It operates daily with early-morning hours, positioning it well for cyclists heading out on a day ride or commuting through the neighbourhood. The OSM record notes no outdoor seating, suggesting a compact interior-focused space typical of boutique espresso bars on The Drive.

restaurant.name: Pure Delight Cafe
restaurant.desc: Pure Delight Café is a Vietnamese restaurant in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood serving authentic Vietnamese cuisine including pho noodles, located on the south side of West Broadway between Trutch St. and Blenheim St. The restaurant emphasizes regional diversity in Vietnamese cooking and community connection within the Kitsilano area. It offers dine-in, pickup, and delivery options.

restaurant.name: New District Wine Beer Spirits
restaurant.desc: New District is a well-regarded private liquor store on Vancouver's west side, carrying over a thousand wines alongside a deep selection of craft beer, spirits, and cider. The shop prides itself on knowledgeable staff who can source hard-to-find limited releases and natural wines. It also runs a bimonthly wine club and regular in-store tasting events for locals and visitors alike.

restaurant.name: Don José
restaurant.desc: Carnitas Don José is a food court stall in downtown Vancouver helmed by Don José Velázquez, an 8-time Mexican Charrería national champion turned chef who brings carnitas estilo Michoacán to the city. The menu centres on slow-cooked pork served in tacos, tortas, and combo plates made with locally sourced ingredients. It holds a 4.7-star Uber Eats rating from over 1,500 reviews and is accessible for delivery through both Uber Eats and DoorDash.

detail.address: 88 West Pender Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 6N9

restaurant.name: Curry Express
restaurant.desc: Curry Express is a family-run quick serve Indian restaurant chain that has been serving the Vancouver area since 1996, with locations inside Metropolis at Metrotown, Lougheed Town Centre, and CF Richmond Centre. The menu draws on North Indian traditions, featuring biryanis, karhai curries, tandoori wraps, and street food specialties like samosa chaat and chole kulche, all prepared fresh using quality meats and produce cooked in tandoor ovens and traditional vessels. The mall food court setting makes it a convenient hot meal stop for cyclists passing through Burnaby or Richmond.

detail.address: 4820 Kingsway (Metropolis at Metrotown), Burnaby, BC V5H 4P1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly includes vegetarian items: Vegetable Pulao, Chana Bhatura, Samosa Combo, Vegetarian Stuffed Naan, and Paneer Tandoori Wrap option

restaurant.name: Abbey Road Taphouse
restaurant.desc: Abbey Road Taphouse is a large sports bar and full-service restaurant in Abbotsford with over 55 HD displays, live band weekends, karaoke nights, and UFC pay-per-view events. The kitchen turns out an eclectic menu spanning burgers, pastas, Mexican tacos, breakfast on weekends, and 30-plus wing flavours, alongside 25 beers on tap and what the bar bills as the largest tequila collection in BC. An all-season covered patio operates year-round with heaters, making it a usable stop in variable Fraser Valley weather.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly marks several items GF (e.g. Loaded Nachos, Warm Spinach Dip w/corn chips, Shrimp Scampi w/corn chips) and offers a Veggie slider option

restaurant.name: Ba Le Sandwich Shop
restaurant.desc: Ba Le Sandwich Shop is a long-standing, family-run Vietnamese banh mi shop on Vancouver's Main Street, celebrated by regulars for its in-house baked baguette bread and remarkably affordable sandwiches. The space is intentionally minimal — just two small tables — making it almost entirely a takeout operation, well suited to a cyclist grabbing a quick, cheap meal on the go. Multiple reviewers note it has been a neighbourhood fixture for years and offers a genuinely casual, no-frills experience.

restaurant.name: Good Co. Bars
restaurant.desc: Good Co. Bars is a multi-location Vancouver bar and restaurant chain with its Main Street outpost anchoring the Mount Pleasant neighbourhood. The venue blends pub-style dining with sports viewing, games, and a busy events calendar including trivia nights, dance parties, and TV watch parties. Touring cyclists will find a full food menu with substantial meal options in a lively, social setting.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Veggie Burger (mushroom-rice patty), Sofritas Tacos, Veggie Dumplings, Crispy Cauliflower, Glory Bowl with fried tofu, and a gluten-free vegan bun substitution option

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: Subway at Kensington Square Plaza is a franchise location of the global sandwich chain, serving footlong sandwiches, wraps, and salads in Burnaby's Hastings corridor. The location supports in-restaurant dining, curbside pickup, and delivery, and accepts major credit cards. As a national chain with no documented cycling-specific amenities, its utility to touring cyclists is limited to basic food resupply.

detail.address: 6626B Hastings Street Unit 146B, Burnaby, BC V5B 1S2

restaurant.name: Horin Ramen
restaurant.desc: Horin Ramen is a Japanese ramen restaurant tracing its roots to a 1966 Fukuoka Prefecture original that pioneered chili-pepper tonkotsu broth. The Vancouver-area chain revives that legacy with hand-made broth and tare sauce adjusted daily by season and weather. The Burnaby location is situated inside Metropolis at Metrotown, one of BC's largest urban shopping malls.

restaurant.name: Pho d'lite
restaurant.desc: Pho d'lite is a Vietnamese restaurant specializing in pho. With indoor seating and a no-smoking policy, it offers a comfortable stop for touring cyclists seeking a reliable meal.

restaurant.name: La Taqueria
restaurant.desc: La Taquería is a full-service Mexican restaurant in Burnaby's Brentwood area, one of three distinct concepts operated by the same restaurant group. It offers a culinary-focused dining experience with cocktails, full table service, and an expansive menu of traditional dishes — from street-style tacos and quesabirria to enchiladas and birriamen. Touring cyclists stopping in the Brentwood corridor will find a sit-down meal with both indoor and outdoor seating and vegetarian and vegan options.

detail.address: 4580 Lougheed Highway, Unit 1210, Burnaby, BC V5C 3Z6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu confirms multiple plant-based options including Frijoles Refritos, Hongos Huitlacoche, Rajas con Crema, and Hongos Salteados tacos and burritos

restaurant.name: Bean Around The World
restaurant.desc: Bean Around The World is a long-established BC coffee roaster — over 30 years in business — known for small-batch, hand-roasted single-origin and blended coffees. The brand operates multiple retail café locations alongside an online store and roastery headquarters in North Vancouver. A visiting cyclist would find a specialty-coffee-focused stop with a well-regarded regional brand behind it.

restaurant.name: Happy Valley Food City
restaurant.desc: Happy Valley Food City is a large multi-concept Chinese dining venue on Lougheed Highway in Burnaby, housing both 'Wonder House' (dim sum lunches and Cantonese seafood dinners) and 'HV Cafe' (Hong Kong-style cafe serving breakfast and cafe fare all day). The restaurant also offers frozen prepared foods for sale and online ordering with pickup or delivery. Wheelchair access is confirmed via OSM.

restaurant.name: The Grateful Table
restaurant.desc: The Grateful Table is a sit-down Greek restaurant in Castlegar serving traditional cuisine made with fresh, local ingredients. The restaurant includes a banquet room available for groups and events and is located next door to the Recharge gym. Customer reviews highlight generous portions, attentive service, and a welcoming family atmosphere.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Customer review on front page explicitly mentions 'vegetarian gyro' as a menu item

restaurant.name: Kerala Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Kerala Kitchen is an award-winning South Indian restaurant in Surrey, earning 1st Place at the Vancouver Foodster Curry Challenge 2024 and an official appreciation from the City of Surrey. The menu centres on traditional Kerala cuisine — fresh-made dosas, coastal curries, and Indo-Chinese dishes drawn from family recipes — and the restaurant has amassed over 2,200 Google reviews. A spacious, welcoming dining room makes it a comfortable stop for groups or solo travellers passing through the Scott Road corridor.

restaurant.name: Happy Day Cafe
restaurant.desc: Happy Day Cafe is a Hong Kong-style cha chaan teng on Vancouver's Kingsway corridor, serving classic Hong Kong dishes and Asian-inspired cuisine for dine-in or takeout. One of two Lower Mainland locations, the cafe offers mobile app ordering and is wheelchair-accessible with air conditioning. Cyclists on the Kingsway route will find a full sit-down meal or a quick takeout option in a comfortable, accessible setting.

restaurant.name: Moki's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Moki's Pizza is a takeout and delivery pizza restaurant on Macdonald Street. A casual spot offering quick pizza grabs for touring cyclists passing through the neighborhood.

restaurant.name: Tall Shadow Bakery
restaurant.desc: Tall Shadow Bakery is an artisan sourdough bakery in East Vancouver specializing in breads made from quality local and organic grains, with an emphasis on community and seasonal sourcing. The bakery offers a full sit-down brunch menu on weekends alongside daily toast options, making it a genuine café-style stop as well as a place to stock up on fresh bread, jam, and granola. They also participate in local farmer's markets and offer pre-order and catering services.

detail.address: 2474 East Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V5K 1Z1

restaurant.name: Pho Ace
restaurant.desc: Pho Ace is a Vietnamese restaurant on Sixth Avenue in New Westminster, recently opened and warmly received by the local community during its grand opening. It offers indoor dining in a smoke-free, wheelchair-accessible space, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists passing through the area. The kitchen focuses on Vietnamese fare, with pho as the signature draw.

restaurant.name: White Spot
restaurant.desc: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, founded in 1928 and known for classic burgers made with fresh Canadian beef, fish and chips, milkshakes, and other comfort-food staples sourced from local BC producers. This Scott Road location sits near the 72nd Avenue intersection and operates as a full-service family restaurant with dine-in and takeout available. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a predictable, filling meal in a welcoming sit-down setting with a broad menu spanning breakfast through dinner.

restaurant.name: Twisted Fork
restaurant.desc: Fork & Friends (branding its brunch program as 'Twisted Fork') is a sit-down brunch spot in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, a short roll from the waterfront Seawall cycling route. The restaurant serves a regional brunch menu and also runs an evening cocktail bar called the Breeze Bar later in the week. Its Gastown location puts it squarely in one of Vancouver's most cycle-accessible corridors.

restaurant.name: Steveston Built Local Taphouse
restaurant.desc: Steveston Built Local Taphouse is a neighbourhood pub situated near the historic Steveston waterfront in Richmond, an area well-travelled by cyclists on the dike trails and coastal routes. The taphouse bills itself as locally focused, with its menu available as a PDF download from the website. It occupies a unit in a mixed-use development at the edge of the Steveston community.

detail.address: 12480 Number 1 Road, Unit 130, Richmond, BC V7E 0A2

restaurant.name: Milk & Sugar BBQ Bar
restaurant.desc: A restaurant on Vancouver's Joyce Street serving bubble tea and barbecue with indoor seating. Touring cyclists can grab a meal and use the available customer WiFi while dining. A convenient urban refueling stop in a walkable neighborhood.

restaurant.name: Thai by Thai
restaurant.desc: Thai by Thai is a sit-down and pickup Thai restaurant on Scott Road (120 St) in Surrey, offering an extensive menu of curries, noodle dishes, and stir-fries alongside lunch specials. The restaurant has earned 209 customer reviews and operates a fully functional online ordering system for pickup. Cyclists riding the Surrey/Delta corridor will find it a convenient stop for a hot meal or a quick takeout order.

notes.Takeout: Website banner states 'Please order for PICKUP only on this website'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page legend explicitly lists 'gluten free' and 'vegetarian' markers; multiple vegetarian dishes present (e.g. Vegetable Thai Spring Roll, Stir-Fried Mixed Vegetables, Pad Tofu, Yellow Curry Tofu)

restaurant.name: India Delight Bistro & Bar
restaurant.desc: India Delight Bistro & Bar is a North Indian and Mughlai restaurant on Sooke Road serving authentic curries, tandoori dishes, and Indo-Chinese appetizers for dine-in or takeout. Chef Data Ram Bhaat brings experience from kitchens in India, Singapore, and Germany, with a focus on freshly prepared sauces and handpicked herbs and spices. The restaurant also offers catering for events of 50 or more people, making it a notable stop in an otherwise limited dining corridor west of Victoria.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian items: Vegetable Samosa, Onion Bhaji, Veg Pakora, Veg Manchurian, Chilli Paneer, Chilli Soya Chaap, and Veggi Noodles

restaurant.name: Slo Coffee
restaurant.desc: Slo Coffee is a specialty coffee shop that originated in Vancouver's Fraserhood neighbourhood and expanded to a second downtown location at Pacific Centre in December 2025. The shop is built around a philosophy of mindful, unhurried coffee culture—emphasizing community, connection, and quality pour-overs and espresso drinks. Food offerings include vegan-friendly spreads, toasts, and overnight oats alongside sandwiches and seasonal signature beverages.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly mentions vegan spreads, toasts, and overnight oats available on the menu

restaurant.name: The Naam
restaurant.desc: Founded in Kitsilano in 1968, The Naam is Vancouver's oldest natural foods restaurant and a long-standing neighbourhood institution on West 4th Avenue. It is a fully vegetarian, family-run restaurant that uses organic, locally-sourced ingredients including house-made tofu and tempeh, and locally-sourced vegan beer and wine. The relaxed, homey atmosphere and central Kitsilano location make it a welcoming stop for cyclists passing through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: 100% vegetarian restaurant; FAQ states 'A majority of our menu can be made vegan upon request.'. No explicit GF mention

restaurant.name: Nana Sushi
restaurant.desc: Nana Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant situated on Victoria Crescent in downtown Nanaimo, marketing itself as the 'Best Sushi in Nanaimo.' The menu spans traditional appetizers, miso soups, salads, and a range of sushi in a relaxed dine-in setting. Online ordering for pickup is available, which can be convenient for cyclists wanting a quick meal on the go.

restaurant.name: Sleeping Giant Fruit Winery
restaurant.desc: Sleeping Giant Fruit Winery is a BC fruit winery near Summerland offering 19 table wines, 12 late-harvest dessert wines, and four sparkling wines, all made from BC-grown fruit using classic winemaking techniques. The tasting room is operated alongside its parent company Summerland Sweets, and sits just 210 steps from the historic Summerland Steam Train trestle bridge — a natural stop on that scenic rail-trail corridor. Tastings are offered by reservation or walk-in, and wines can be purchased in-store or through the online Shopify shop.

detail.address: 6206 Canyon View Road, Summerland, BC V0H 1Z7

restaurant.name: Obanhmi
restaurant.desc: Obanhmi is a Vietnamese bánh mì restaurant located in Burnaby's Newton Street area. The name suggests a specialty in the classic Vietnamese baguette sandwich, a popular quick and filling meal for cyclists on the move. The OSM record lists daily hours, indicating consistent availability throughout the week.

restaurant.name: Panago
restaurant.desc: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain with a location in Fort St. John offering delivery and takeout. The brand distinguishes itself with a commitment to Canadian-grown wheat, organic tomato sauce, and a broad selection of plant-based, dairy-free, and gluten-free options. For a touring cyclist passing through Fort St. John, it is a convenient stop for a hot meal with customizable dietary accommodations.

detail.address: 8808 96A Street, Fort St. John, BC V1J 6E2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'abundant veggie, dairy-free and meat-free choices'

restaurant.name: Breaking Bean
restaurant.desc: Breaking Bean is a coffee shop at 551 Cardero Street in Vancouver. The establishment serves coffee and beverages to the local community.

restaurant.name: CinCin Ristorante + Bar
restaurant.desc: CinCin Ristorante + Bar is a long-established Italian restaurant on Robson Street, accessed by a winding stone stairway above street level. The kitchen is anchored by a Grillworks Infierno, a two-metre wood-fired grill and rotisserie where fish and prime meats are cooked over fruitwood charcoal alongside housemade pastas. With over 25 years of operation and a nationally recognized wine program, it is considered one of Vancouver's premier fine-dining Italian destinations.

restaurant.name: Patisserie Le Pont
restaurant.desc: Patisserie Le Pont is a premium French-Japanese artisan pastry shop in West Vancouver, founded by Makoto Yamaguchi, a classically trained pâtissière who graduated from Le Cordon Bleu in Paris and previously ran her own shop in Tokyo for 15 years. The patisserie specializes in handcrafted eclairs — both sweet and savoury — alongside cakes, tarts, and baked goods made fresh daily without preservatives or pre-mixes. OSM records both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a pleasant stop for a cyclist looking for a quality sweet treat.

restaurant.name: MGM
restaurant.desc: MGM is a family-run community institution in Nanaimo that has been serving home-cooked all-day breakfast, lunch, and dinner since 1984. The restaurant doubles as a neighbourhood gathering place, hosting chess nights, live music with dancing, game nights, and other community events in a space that includes a dance floor, stage area, and large banquet section. A seniors menu and kids menu round out its broad, welcoming appeal.

restaurant.name: Milano Coffee
restaurant.desc: Milano Coffee is a Vancouver institution founded in 1984 by Italian Master Roaster Francesco Curatolo, bringing three generations of artisan espresso tradition to the West Coast. The Denman Street espresso bar sits at the gateway to Stanley Park and the seawall — one of the most heavily cycled corridors in Metro Vancouver. The roaster has earned 15 gold medals from the International Institute of Coffee Tasters and is known for blending up to 20 origin coffees into its signature espressos, with outdoor seating available.

restaurant.name: fable café
restaurant.desc: Fable Café is the brick-and-mortar café of Fable, a Certified B Corp best known for its premium tableware and homewares brand. Situated in Vancouver's South Granville neighbourhood, it serves espresso drinks, rotating pour overs, matcha, hojicha, and seasonal beverages alongside sweet bites. The café runs a no-tipping model with living wages for staff and charges nothing extra for alternative milks.

restaurant.name: Family Thai Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Family Thai Restaurant is a family-owned eatery that has brought authentic Thai cuisine to Cranbrook's East Kootenay community since 2017. The menu spans a wide range of Thai classics — curries, stir-fries, noodle dishes, and soups — with a house spice scale from 1 (mild) to 5 (Thai-nationals-only). The kitchen cooks each dish fresh to order without MSG, and can accommodate vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free diners on selected items.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Vegetarian, Glute-Free or Vegan Guests we can accommodate your food preferences on selected item in the menu' and notes 'we have some gluten free and vegan option.'

restaurant.name: Thai Green Elephant
restaurant.desc: Thai Green Elephant is a family-run Thai restaurant established in September 2014, drawing on over 30 years of culinary experience to serve authentic Thai cuisine in Esquimalt near Victoria. The extensive all-day menu caters to a wide range of dietary needs, with clearly labelled vegan, vegetarian, and allergen-tagged dishes. Online ordering and takeout are available, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists looking for a full sit-down or take-away meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items explicitly labelled 'Vegan' (e.g., Spring Rolls, Param Long Song tofu option, Vegetable Samosa, Deep Fried Tofu). Allergen tags throughout menu indicate allergy-awareness

restaurant.name: The Ruby
restaurant.desc: The Ruby on Johnson is a locally owned breakfast and brunch restaurant open since 2015, located inside the Best Western Carlton Plaza Hotel on Johnson Street in Victoria. It offers a refined take on brunch blending eclectic southern-inspired fare with scratch cooking and locally sourced ingredients. The restaurant is part of a small Victoria-based group with two additional locations and is known for its vinyl record collection and emphasis on staff wellbeing.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'VEGAN FARE' section (Vegan Mexi Hash, The Greenhouse Sandwich, Vegan Breakfast Tacos) and a gluten-free biscuit substitution option listed across multiple menu items

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Freshslice Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain offering by-the-slice and whole-pizza options with a wide variety of customizable toppings, including vegetarian choices and a gluten-free cauliflower crust. This Tsawwassen location on Ladner Trunk Road sits in a commercial strip in Delta and offers both dine-in and takeout service. It is a practical calorie stop for cyclists passing through the area en route to or from the Tsawwassen ferry terminal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists Veggie pizza as a standard classic option; nutritional info page lists a Gluten Free Cauliflower crust as a dough option

restaurant.name: Tofino Licks
restaurant.desc: Tofino Licks is an artisanal soft-serve ice cream shop in Tofino that collaborates with local restaurants and bakeries — Tacofino, Sobo, Common Loaf, and the Tofino Ucluelet Culinary Guild — to create uniquely topped sundaes using ingredients from the town's culinary scene. Their Italian-imported soft serve and sorbets are prepared in-house, with both creamy vanilla gelato and a vegan chocolate sorbet as bases. It's a well-known local stop for a sweet treat after a ride on Vancouver Island's west coast.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly describes vegan chocolate sorbet ('dairy free and vegan'), vegan berry sauces, and a vegan peanut butter chocolate oat bar topping

restaurant.name: The Bubble Tea Shop
restaurant.desc: The Bubble Tea Shop is a local small business with locations in Richmond and Vancouver's Olympic Village, specializing in bubble tea and DIY milk tea kits. The Richmond storefront offers in-store pickup of ready-made drinks and retail supplies including loose leaf teas, flavoured powders, and toppings. It is a community-oriented café-style shop that also ships its DIY kits across Canada.

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: Tim Hortons is a Canadian quick-service chain institution on Northfield Road in Nanaimo, offering coffee, baked goods, soups, and breakfast wraps with both dine-in and drive-thru options. For a touring cyclist, it provides a reliable, familiar stop for a hot drink and a quick meal at the northern edge of the city. The location supports mobile ordering and a loyalty rewards program.

restaurant.name: Floyd's Diner
restaurant.desc: Floyd's Diner is a Victoria, BC institution established in 2004, celebrated for its signature challenge dish 'The Mahoney' and generous breakfast and brunch portions. The family-oriented diner has grown to four locations across the greater Victoria area, including James Bay, Langford, Royal Oak, and the Gorge. Touring cyclists will find it a reliable all-day breakfast stop open seven days a week.

restaurant.name: Cooks Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Cooks Restaurant is a gourmet smash burger joint on Cumberland's historic former mining town main street, operated by chefs Jake Galbraith and Christopher Matthews. It was called a 'worth-the-detour' destination by the Vancouver Sun, serving freshly ground local chuck burgers, fried chicken sandwiches, hand-spun milkshakes made with Island Farms dairy, and local draft beer. Cumberland itself is a well-known cycling hub, making this a natural post-ride stop.

restaurant.name: BeaverTails
restaurant.desc: BeaverTails is an iconic Canadian pastry chain, famous for hand-stretched whole-wheat pastries fried to order and topped with a wide range of sweet or savory options. The Victoria location on Broughton Street sits close to the Inner Harbour, one of the city's busiest cycling and tourist corridors. Beyond pastries, the menu includes poutines, BeaverDogs, lemonades, and hot chocolate — a solid quick-fuel stop on a ride through downtown Victoria.

restaurant.name: Il Covo Trattoria
restaurant.desc: Il Covo Trattoria is a family-run authentic Italian restaurant located in Victoria's historic James Bay neighbourhood, housed in a 112-year-old heritage building steps from the Inner Harbour. The restaurant holds the Ospitalità Italiana seal from the Italian Chamber of Commerce, certifying its authenticity, with an owner originally from Genova who has been bringing Italian flavours to Victoria since 1999. Cyclists can dine on northern Italian classics and family recipes, with the option of eating al fresco in the garden patio.

notes.Takeout: Website states: 'Takeout orders for pickup are available by phone.' Phone-only, no third-party delivery services used

restaurant.name: Pappa Roti
restaurant.desc: PappaRoti is a Malaysian-origin café chain famous for its signature roti buns: a soft, pillowy interior wrapped in a crisp coffee-caramel crust with a salted butter centre, baked fresh throughout the day. The Coquitlam location is one of several BC outposts of a brand with over 400 locations worldwide, serving buns alongside hot and cold drinks, pastries, sandwiches, salads, and soups. It makes a convenient stop on Pinetree Way for a quick, filling snack.

detail.address: Unit 100, 1196 Pinetree Way, Coquitlam, BC V3B 2P7

restaurant.name: The Longhorn Saloon
restaurant.desc: The Longhorn Saloon is one of Whistler's most iconic après-ski and après-bike bars, situated at the base of Whistler Mountain just steps from the gondolas and operated by the Gibbons Hospitality Group. It features an expansive slopeside patio known for high-energy atmosphere, live music, and weekly themed events. The venue explicitly caters to mountain bikers finishing their day on the mountain alongside skiers and snowboarders.

restaurant.name: The Firehouse Grill
restaurant.desc: The Firehouse Grill is a casual full-service restaurant in downtown Nanaimo on Front Street, offering an eclectic fusion of house sushi rolls, grill items, and craft beer. The menu blends West Coast ingredients — sockeye salmon, local prawns, and albacore tuna — with Japanese technique, making it a distinctive dining stop near the Nanaimo waterfront. Cyclists finishing a coastal or inland route into Nanaimo will find a broad menu suited to refuelling.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Veggie Tempura, Edamame, Tossed Salad, and Black N' Blue Tuna salad — multiple vegetarian-suitable items present

restaurant.name: Pamir Diner Afghan Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Pamir Diner is an Afghan restaurant in Delta, BC, serving traditional dishes including handcrafted mantu dumplings, slow-cooked lamb, and mixed kebab platters using family recipes. The menu draws on generations of Afghan culinary tradition with an emphasis on fresh, daily-prepared ingredients. Online ordering is available for pickup and delivery, making it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists riding through the area.

restaurant.name: cuisine Of India
restaurant.desc: An Indian restaurant situated on 43 Avenue in Vernon, BC, with a dining capacity of 78. It offers both takeout and delivery in addition to dine-in service, making it a potential stop for cyclists looking for a hearty meal in the Okanagan. The outdoor area permits smoking.

restaurant.name: Sachi Sushi
restaurant.desc: Sachi Sushi has been a Whistler institution since 2003, earning the Best Sushi award in the Pique Newspaper's Best of Whistler competition and a glowing mention in Lonely Planet. Owner and head chef Toshiyuki Kobayashi brings over 30 years of sushi experience, with a focus on the freshest ingredients in creative rolls and sashimi. Located in the Summit Lodge on Main Street, it's a popular walk-in-only spot that draws visitors from around the world.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes explicitly vegetarian rolls: Veggie Roll (asparagus tempura, carrot, avocado, cucumber), Cucumber Roll, Avocado Roll, and Cupcakes (avocado roll with sweet potato tempura). No vegan or GF claims confirmed

restaurant.name: Village Books & Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Village Books & Coffee House is an independent bookstore and coffee shop tucked into a Richmond retail unit, offering a curated selection of fiction, young adult, and new-release titles alongside café service. It is a community-oriented stop where browsing a book shelf and a coffee order go hand in hand. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's southwest corner would find it a welcoming place to rest and recharge mentally, if not mechanically.

restaurant.name: Standard Pizza
restaurant.desc: Standard Pizza is a small, independently owned neighbourhood pizzeria on Cook Street in Victoria, serving wood-fired pizzas in two sizes (12" and 16") for dine-in or takeout. The menu centres on classic and creative combinations using quality ingredients, with a flexible build-your-own approach and a strong selection of vegetarian options. Cook Street Village is a lively, walkable strip and a natural waypoint for cyclists moving through the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a pizza explicitly labeled 'VEGETARIAN' (tomato, cheese, kale, mushroom, olive, onion) plus additional vegetarian-friendly options (TOMATO, KALE, MUSHROOM, WHITE, MARGHERITA, etc.); no vegan or gluten-free options are mentioned

restaurant.name: CHARLIE don't SURF
restaurant.desc: Charlie Don't Surf has been a fixture on the White Rock waterfront strip since 1985, serving fresh wild seafood alongside local organic vegetables and a broad selection of craft beers. Situated on Marine Drive directly adjacent to White Rock Beach, it draws both locals and visitors looking for a casual seaside meal. The restaurant also operates a bar and offers outdoor seating, making it a natural rest point for cyclists riding the waterfront.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We proudly offer many gluten free options.'

restaurant.name: Banter Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Banter Ice Cream is a Fraser Valley-founded handmade ice cream shop located in Abbotsford's Jubilee Park, housed in the old library building with adjacent outdoor green space. Founded by Laura and Zach after a trip to the Gulf Islands, the shop rotates four new seasonal flavours each month using locally sourced ingredients from Fraser Valley farmers and artisans. The park setting with outdoor space makes it a natural rest stop, and the shop encourages visitors to bring picnics and lawn games.

detail.address: 33660 South Fraser Way, Abbotsford, BC V2S 2B9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu items marked '(V)' indicate vegan options; examples include Mango and Chocolate flavours

restaurant.name: So Hyang Korean Cuisine
restaurant.desc: So Hyang Korean Cuisine is a Korean restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver's Sunset neighbourhood, open seven days a week. The restaurant operates on a walk-in basis with no reservations accepted, and offers online order-ahead for pickup. It sits on a busy arterial cycling corridor connecting south Vancouver to the city centre.

restaurant.name: Crab Hot Lau
restaurant.desc: Crab Hot Lau is Vancouver's original Hải Phòng rice field crab hotpot restaurant, specializing in authentic Northern Vietnamese cuisine with signature hand-filtered crab broths and traditional regional dishes. The restaurant has earned the Vancouver Magazine Gold Award for Best Vietnamese Restaurant three consecutive years (2024–2026), drawing a loyal local following and consistent media coverage. The Kingsway location sits on a major east–west arterial in East Vancouver, making it a convenient sit-down dining option for cyclists in that corridor.

restaurant.name: The Vault Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Vault Cafe is a cafe and bar on Wallace Street in Nanaimo offering indoor and sidewalk seating. The cafe serves vegan and vegetarian options and features free Wi-Fi for customers.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegan and vegetarian options available

restaurant.name: Smokin Tuna Cafe
restaurant.desc: A casual cafe located on Becher Bay Road in Sooke. Positioned on a scenic coastal cycling route, it offers a convenient refueling stop for cyclists exploring the region.

restaurant.name: D-Plus Pizza
restaurant.desc: D-Plus Pizza is a locally-owned and operated pizza and Indian food chain with five locations across Surrey and Delta, BC. Originally founded as D Hut Pizza in the Fraser Valley, it grew by blending classic pizza with Indian-influenced dishes like butter chicken pizza, paneer pizza, samosas, and channa bathura. Cyclists stopping here can expect a varied menu available for walk-in pickup or online pre-order.

restaurant.name: ZUBU Ramen
restaurant.desc: ZUBU Ramen is a Japanese ramen chain with four Lower Mainland locations, including a Park Royal outpost in West Vancouver. Executive Chef William Cao trained at the Kitchen Hyodo Ramen School in Oyama, Japan, and sources ingredients both locally from Pacific West Coast farms and directly from Japan. Beyond ramen, the menu spans fresh temaki, handmade gyoza, rice bowls, and Japanese-inspired cocktails.

restaurant.name: The Watson
restaurant.desc: The Watson is a neighbourhood cocktail bar in the heart of Mount Pleasant on Main Street, created by the team behind Bartholomew bar in Yaletown. It features inventive, expertly crafted cocktails alongside elevated bar food and hearty comfort dishes. There is a sun-drenched patio and a mezzanine lounge, making it a welcoming stop along one of Vancouver's main north-south cycling corridors.

restaurant.name: The Meat Up
restaurant.desc: The Meat Up BBQ is a modern all-you-can-eat restaurant specialising in Asian charcoal-grill BBQ and customisable hotpot, with multiple tiered menu options and a lively, communal atmosphere. It is part of a small chain with locations in both Richmond and Burnaby. The Richmond location sits on busy Number 3 Road, making it a convenient stop for cyclists exploring Richmond's main commercial corridor.

restaurant.name: Thong La's Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A Chinese restaurant in Chilliwack operating since 2011. Provides a meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Elysian Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Elysian Coffee Roasters is a Vancouver specialty coffee roaster that sources and roasts its own single-origin beans from Ethiopia, Rwanda, Guatemala, and Colombia, with four neighbourhood cafes across the city. The Kitsilano location at 5th & Burrard sits on West 5th Avenue, a well-known cycling corridor connecting the waterfront to the broader metro network. The brand built its identity around consistent, high-quality espresso and filter coffee, with a stated emphasis on a positive in-cafe work environment.

restaurant.name: Red Burrito
restaurant.desc: Red Burrito is a Vancouver-born Mexican restaurant chain that has been making fresh, house-made burritos, tacos, and tamales since 2006. The Cambie Street location sits along one of Vancouver's primary cycling corridors and offers both indoor and outdoor seating. Handmade tamales, tortilla soup, and a catering programme round out a menu built around daily-fresh ingredients.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a dedicated Vegetarian filling (Spanish rice, beans, toppings, fresh guacamole) and a Vegan Meat filling (soy-based protein seasoned in house spices). No gluten-free option mentioned

restaurant.name: Restaurant 62
restaurant.desc: Restaurant 62 is a farm-to-table restaurant in Abbotsford billing itself as the Fraser Valley's top farm-to-table destination, with a menu built around locally sourced ingredients including Fraser Valley meats, Mt. Lehman cheese, and seasonal produce. The kitchen offers lunch, dinner, and happy hour alongside private dining and catering. Touring cyclists would find a full sit-down dining experience with a regionally rooted menu and a catering operation that speaks to the restaurant's scale.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Lunch menu explicitly lists 'Gluten free cornbread'; multiple vegetarian-suitable dishes appear across menus (roasted heirloom beet salad, mushroom bisque, tomato soup, gnocchi with halloumi add-on option)

restaurant.name: Pho Garden
restaurant.desc: Vietnamese pho restaurant located at 1469 Marine Drive in North Vancouver. The business website was not accessible for verification of amenities or current operational details.

restaurant.name: McCulloch Station Pub
restaurant.desc: McCulloch Station Pub is Kelowna's original neighbourhood pub, opened in 1985 in East Kelowna and named in honour of Andrew McCulloch, the engineer who built the Kettle Valley Railway — the very rail corridor that touring cyclists now ride as the KVR trail. Situated near historic East Kelowna landmarks, the family-owned pub features a celebrated patio, a full food menu, an on-tap draught selection, and an attached liquor store. It is an adult-only (19+) establishment.

detail.address: 2789 K.L.O. Road, Kelowna, British Columbia, V1W 4A5

restaurant.name: Yalla
restaurant.desc: Yalla is a family-owned Middle Eastern street-eats restaurant in Victoria serving halal shawarma, falafel, and Persian-inspired dishes across pita and bowl formats. The kitchen draws on culinary traditions from multiple Middle Eastern countries, with standout items like the Persian shawarma and lamb shank with baghali polo. The team is openly accommodating of food allergies including gluten and nuts, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegetarian options confirmed: falafel pita, falafel bowl, falafel fries pita/bowl, and vegetarian Maquli (no meat version). Website explicitly mentions accommodating gluten/celiac customers: 'We have had a lot of customers with allergies to nuts or gluten (or celiac) who tried our food.' Vegan not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: Gelateria Benvenuto
restaurant.desc: The Gelateria is a walk-up gelato and sorbetto counter situated inside The Butchart Gardens' Italian Garden, one of BC's most celebrated horticultural destinations near Sidney. The culinary team travelled to Italy specifically to learn authentic gelato-making, and seasonal flavours feature locally-sourced ingredients. Cyclists visiting Butchart Gardens will find this a fitting sweet stop mid-garden-tour, though paid garden admission is required to reach it.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists sorbetto alongside gelato, which is inherently dairy-free/vegan

restaurant.name: Corner Cafe
restaurant.desc: Corner Cafe is a casual breakfast and lunch spot serving the Cloverdale area of Surrey, blending Korean-inspired dishes (Cupbop, wonton soup) with classic cafe fare like club sandwiches and wraps. The owners emphasize simple, quality ingredients cooked well over elaborate presentation, creating a warm and unpretentious atmosphere. The cafe also offers online ordering and catering for group inquiries.

restaurant.name: Beeryani Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Beeryani Indian Cuisine is a full-service Indian restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street, known for its signature 'Beeryani' — a fusion dish blending traditional slow-cooked biryani with locally brewed Canadian craft beer. The menu spans tandoor-grilled proteins, rich curries, and vegetarian staples like Dal Makhani, rounded out by curated craft beer pairings suggested by staff. The restaurant also offers catering for events of all sizes.

detail.address: 4129 Main Street, Vancouver, British Columbia V5V 3P6

notes.Takeout: Offers page terms state 'Valid for dine-in, takeout, and delivery orders'; website also prominently features an 'Order Online' button and a 10% off pickup-only discount
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website front page lists 'Vegetarian' as a named menu category; dishes such as Dal Makhani, Aloo Gobhi, Okra Masala, and Samosa are featured

restaurant.name: Anatolia's Gate
restaurant.desc: Anatolia's Gate is a Turkish restaurant located on Kingsway in Vancouver, offering halal-certified cuisine. It provides sit-down dining suitable for a touring cyclist's meal break. A specialized ethnic cuisine option in the local area.

restaurant.name: The Alley
restaurant.desc: The Alley is a bubble tea and specialty coffee franchise cafe on Hornby Street in downtown Vancouver, operating under a 'Hub' concept that blends a drinks counter with individual working pods, a collaborative multi-purpose room for up to ten people, and a lounge area. The menu centres on hand-crafted drinks alongside grab-and-go food including pastries, salads, and fried snacks, with house-made sugar cane syrup and freshly hand-rolled tapioca prepared on-site each day. The multilingual branding (English, French, Traditional Chinese) reflects the cafe's origins as a Taiwanese-rooted international franchise.

restaurant.name: Penang Szechuan Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Penang Szechuan Cuisine Restaurant is a Szechuan Chinese restaurant in White Rock praised by reviewers for bold, authentic flavors including kung pao chicken, mapo tofu, dan dan noodles, and spicy fish fillet.
