It offers dine-in with a cozy atmosphere as well as online ordering and takeout, making it a practical meal stop for cyclists exploring the South Surrey and White Rock waterfront area.

detail.address: 15228 Russell Avenue, White Rock, BC V4B 2P6

restaurant.name: Bar Asra
restaurant.desc: Bar Asra is a South Granville cocktail lounge and share plates restaurant led by Executive Chefs Kanwardeep Ahluwalia and Baldeep Singh, whose backgrounds span 16 Taj properties, the 2010 Commonwealth Games, and Fairmont hotels in Vancouver and Lake Louise. The menu draws on global travel and memory — paneer tarts, crab satay, chargrilled steak — paired with a craft cocktail program featuring fat-washed gins, milk-clarified cachaca drinks, and zero-proof options. Free live acoustic music on select evenings makes it a distinctive neighbourhood spot steps from Downtown Vancouver and Kitsilano.

detail.address: 1480 W 11th Ave, South Granville, Vancouver, BC, V6H 1L1

restaurant.name: Grapes and Soda
restaurant.desc: A cozy 25-seat natural wine and cocktail bar tucked beside its sister restaurant Farmer's Apprentice in Vancouver's South Granville neighbourhood. The kitchen and bar emphasize low-intervention wines, seasonal ingredients, and a zero-waste ethos, turning leftover herbs and citrus peels into syrups and infusions. Walk-ins are welcome, making it an easy stop for cyclists exploring the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu clearly marks items as vegetarian (V), vegan (V+), gluten-free (GF), and dairy-free (DF); multiple options in each category including spring greens salad (V, GF), smoked olives (V+), and tocino de cielo dessert (GF, DF)

restaurant.name: Village Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Village Pizzeria is a family-owned takeout restaurant that has been baking artisan pizza in Harrison Hot Springs since 1994, using 48-hour aged handmade dough pressed thin and cooked in a traditional deck oven. Situated right behind Harrison Lake and a short walk from Harrison Spa Resort, it sits in the heart of a popular resort town. The menu rounds out with Greek salad, pasta, and chicken wings — a solid refuelling option after a ride into the Hot Springs.

detail.address: Unit 101 - 160 Lillooet Ave, Harrison Hot Springs, BC V0M 1K0

notes.Takeout: Website header reads 'Take out Pizza Restaurant'; Tripadvisor review quoted on site states 'Supposed to be take out only, but very accommodating.'

restaurant.name: Cazba
restaurant.desc: Cazba is a Persian grill on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, part of a multi-location Lower Mainland chain rooted in the traditions of Persian hospitality. The menu centres on slow-cooked, heritage recipes — kebabs, Ghormeh Sabzi, and lamb shank dishes prepared from fresh ingredients. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the restaurant is wheelchair accessible.

restaurant.name: Zambri's
restaurant.desc: Zambri's has been serving honest, authentic Italian food in downtown Victoria since 1999, earning a loyal following and critical recognition over more than two decades. Founded by Peter Zambri and now co-led by Executive Chef Julia McInnis, the restaurant occupies the Atrium building and draws on seasonal, local ingredients for its ever-changing feature menus. Private dining rooms accommodating up to 55 guests make it a popular destination for celebrations, and delivery via Uber Eats extends its reach beyond dine-in.

restaurant.name: Cafe Malabar
restaurant.desc: Cafe Malabar is a Kerala cuisine restaurant in downtown Victoria, founded by chefs Kiran Kolathodan and Karma Tenpa, both raised in Southern India with over 30 years of combined experience in luxury kitchens across Canada and India. The menu centres on Malabar seafood—prawns, curries—alongside vegetarian and meat dishes layered with spices reflecting Portuguese, Dutch, and French culinary influences. A seasonal patio is available, and the restaurant takes reservations as well as take-out orders.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states the menu includes 'vegetarian and meat dishes, each infused with aromatic spices'; no mention of vegan or GF specifically

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: This Tim Hortons occupies the Library building at UBC Okanagan campus, offering the familiar Canadian staples of coffee, tea, baked goods, and sandwiches to the campus community and any visitors passing through. The website notes that line-ups are very common, reflecting its high traffic volume. As one of several food outlets managed by UBCO Food Services, it sits within a larger campus dining ecosystem.

restaurant.name: Polish Bistro
restaurant.desc: Polish Bistro is a Polish cuisine restaurant in Penticton, British Columbia, operating from a compact single-storey retail building. Penticton is a hub on the Okanagan cycling circuit and near the Kettle Valley Rail Trail, making it a natural resupply point for touring riders. A Polish menu typically offers hearty, filling dishes — a welcome prospect after a long day in the saddle.

detail.address: 65 Nanaimo Ave E, Penticton, BC V2A 1M1, Canada

restaurant.name: Sabà Bistro
restaurant.desc: Sabà Bistro is a woman and family-owned Mediterranean-inspired restaurant nestled in historic Fort Langley. The ingredient-forward menu features a crafted balance of local and seasonal flavours, with dishes designed to be shared family style. It operates alongside a sister café and an upcoming pizzeria, both within walking distance on Mavis Avenue.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Vegan Burrito and multiple items marked 'Gf option' (e.g. Sabà Breakfast, Breakfast Sandwich, Avocado Toast)

restaurant.name: The Butcher & Bullock
restaurant.desc: The Butcher & Bullock is a burger restaurant and bar in downtown Vancouver, part of the Donnelly Group hospitality portfolio. It features indoor seating and bar service. The location on West Pender Street positions it as a convenient dining stop for cyclists traveling through Vancouver's downtown core.

restaurant.name: Stuffies Pastries Cafe
restaurant.desc: Stuffies Pastries is a North Vancouver café bringing a South Korean animal-shaped waffle pastry concept to Vancouver, with custard- and jam-filled treats as their signature item. The cafe also serves coffee and beverages, soft-serve ice cream, and sandwiches, salads, and soups, making it a reasonable stop for a sweet or savoury refuel. It is part of a small multi-location chain with stores in Burnaby and Surrey as well.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Stuffies menu page lists '24 Pieces Reg. Vegan/GF (Min. Order 48 pcs.)' as an explicit option

restaurant.name: Locus Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Established in 1998, Locus is a long-standing fixture on Vancouver's Main Street — a funky, gothic-decored neighbourhood restaurant and lounge offering an eclectic fusion of globally inspired dishes built around seasonal, locally sourced ingredients. The kitchen rotates through daily brunch, lunch, happy hour, and dinner specials, with local wines and craft beers on offer throughout. Walk-ins are welcome, making it an easy drop-in along one of Vancouver's most active cycling corridors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'we feature a variety of meat, seafood and vegetarian choices that are constantly refreshed to reflect the best local and seasonal ingredients.' Vegan and GF not mentioned

restaurant.name: Rose and Crown Pub
restaurant.desc: The Rose and Crown bills itself as Tsawwassen's only neighbourhood pub, a lively sports bar with 12 large-screen TVs, a games room with pool table and dartboard, and a separate quieter lounge called Metro's Lounge for a more relaxed visit. The kitchen runs seven days a week with a full pub menu and a weekend brunch, while the pub calendar includes live music nights, themed DJ nights, monthly karaoke, and a last-Wednesday trivia night. It is a well-established local institution — the head chef has been on staff for over 23 years — and a natural stop for cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen ferry and border corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes salads, Avocado Benny, and a range of non-alcoholic beer, wine, and coolers

restaurant.name: The Sportsbar LIVE! At Rogers Arena
restaurant.desc: The Sportsbar is a 14,000-square-foot, 420-seat sports bar and full-service restaurant on the 3rd level of Rogers Arena, home of the Vancouver Canucks. It is accessible directly from outside the arena without a game ticket via the Georgia Viaduct entrance, making it a standalone dining destination in downtown Vancouver. The venue features over 100 4K HDTVs, a 90-foot illuminated bar, 60+ draft taps, and a menu from Executive Chef Robert Bartley built on fresh and local ingredients.

detail.address: 99 West Georgia Street, Vancouver, BC, V6B 0N9

restaurant.name: Ninja Bubble Tea
restaurant.desc: Ninja Bubble Tea is a handcrafted bubble tea and Asian fusion café founded in 2013, now operating three locations across BC's Lower Mainland. The menu spans classic tapioca milk teas, artisanal designer teas, fresh poke bowls, Filipino halo-halo shaved ice, and comfort food items like mac and cheese. The New Westminster location sits inside the Rivermarket complex on Quayside Drive.

detail.address: Unit 131 - 810 Quayside Dr Rivermarket, New Westminster, BC V3M 6B9

restaurant.name: Maguro Sushi
restaurant.desc: A Japanese sushi restaurant in Tsawwassen offering online ordering and dine-in service. The recently redesigned website indicates an active, well-maintained business. Useful to touring cyclists needing a meal stop in the area.

restaurant.name: The Shed
restaurant.desc: The Shed is a low-and-slow BBQ smokehouse and bar in downtown Kimberley, leaning into the Kootenay ethos of 'dirt-baggery' — a celebration of adventure and free time over busy-ness. The menu is a deep roster of smoked meats, tacos, loaded nachos, and sandwiches built for sharing, alongside local draught beer and cocktails. It operates entirely first-come-first-served with no reservations, making it a laid-back stop after a day on the trails.

detail.address: 180 Deer Park Avenue, Kimberley, BC V1A 2J4

restaurant.name: Wela
restaurant.desc: Wela is a fast-casual health restaurant in downtown Vancouver specializing in globally-inspired bowls, wraps, and superfood smoothies built around a Thai-rooted 'find your balance' philosophy. Founded in 2019, it offers a wide spectrum of customizable options spanning vegan, gluten-free, and omnivore diets, making it a practical and satisfying stop for touring cyclists seeking a quick nutritious meal. The restaurant also partners with Too Good To Go to reduce food waste, reflecting its sustainability-minded ethos.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu pages confirm with Ⓥ and GF labels on multiple items including bowls and wraps

restaurant.name: The Parsonage Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Parsonage Cafe in Victoria's Fernwood neighbourhood is the founding location of Fernwood Coffee Company, where a 1936 Barth roaster once sat in the back and sparked a craft roasting business that went on to win the Canadian Barista Championship. The cafe has outdoor seating and serves as a neighbourhood anchor for Fernwood Coffee's specialty coffee culture. Cyclists riding through Victoria's residential streets will find it a welcoming spot for quality coffee with a genuine local history.

restaurant.name: Cookie's Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Cookie's Ice Cream is a family-owned shop in the Tsawwassen Southlands development offering premium small-batch, barrel-churned ice cream and sorbet in over 90 rotating flavours served in a cookie, cup, or cone. Beyond scoops, the shop carries custom ice cream cakes, mini donuts, artisan soda floats, specialty candy, and hot chocolate bombs, making it a well-stocked sweet-stop on a ride through the Delta farmlands. Cookie's also runs a mobile fleet — trailer, truck, and cargo bike — for events across the Lower Mainland.

detail.address: 6388 Market Avenue, Unit 106, Delta, BC V4L 1M9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists sorbet (dairy-free/vegan) as a core product alongside ice cream; also offers a No Sugar Added flavour (Caramel Coffee Macchiato NSA)

restaurant.name: Brewers Corner - The Nanaimo Wine Shoppe
restaurant.desc: Brewers Corner is a homebrew supply shop and U-Brew facility where customers bring in kits or fresh fruit and use the owner-operated, climate-controlled equipment to ferment and bottle their own wine, beer, or cider on premise. Founded in 2019 by Wendy and Guillermo, who together bring decades of brewing expertise, the shop also stocks specialty ingredients including nitrogen-flushed pellet hops, Gambrinus barley, and specialty coffee beans. A touring cyclist with a taste for DIY craft beverages or in search of quality coffee supplies will find knowledgeable, owner-run service at this community-focused Nanaimo shop.

restaurant.name: Regard Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Regard Coffee Roasters is a Nanaimo-based coffee roaster with an e-commerce presence offering coffee subscriptions, merchandise, and wholesale supply. OSM identifies a physical location on Bowen Road tagged as a cafe, which may serve as a retail counter or tasting space alongside the roasting operation. The nature and scale of walk-in service are unclear from available evidence.

restaurant.name: Skinny Duke's Glorious Emporium
restaurant.desc: Skinny Duke's Glorious Emporium is a retro-inspired dinner restaurant and cocktail bar on Kelowna's waterfront Water Street, blending nostalgic aesthetics with a forward-thinking, eclectic menu of creative dishes. The venue leans into a lively atmosphere with curated music, private event space, and a late-night dim sum program on weekends. Takeout is available directly through DoorDash for cyclists who prefer to eat on the go.

restaurant.name: Hope Mountain Cafe
restaurant.desc: Hope Mountain Cafe is a breakfast and lunch destination in Hope, BC, founded in 2018 with a menu inspired by global flavors and fresh, sustainable ingredients. The cafe serves specialty coffee, all-day breakfast, sandwiches, and desserts, positioning itself as a solid full-meal stop for cyclists moving through the Fraser Canyon corridor. Online ordering and takeout are available for those who need to eat on the move.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian items (Double V Burger Veggie, Veggie Breakfast Poutine, Vegetarian Breakfast Sandwich); GF not explicitly

restaurant.name: Woomi Sushi
restaurant.desc: A Japanese sushi restaurant in New Westminster offering online ordering with delivery service. Customers can place orders online for takeout or delivery.

restaurant.name: Sector 7 Kitchen + Bar
restaurant.desc: Sector 7 Kitchen + Bar is a full-service restaurant and bar in Richmond's arts and culture district, offering an extensive menu of creative craft cocktails alongside a burger-focused food menu. The restaurant emphasizes community connection, local and sustainable sourcing, and an atmosphere where food and art intersect. It also accommodates corporate events, private events, and catering, making it a versatile dining destination.

detail.address: 9371 No 5 Rd Unit 10, Richmond, BC V7A 4E1, Canada

restaurant.name: Uno Beef Noodle
restaurant.desc: Uno Beef Noodle is a Taiwanese restaurant in Richmond's main commercial strip on Number 3 Road, specializing in authentic beef noodle soup prepared with traditional techniques. The restaurant is popular enough to use a waitlist system and operates a second Richmond location on No. 2 Road. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a sit-down meal of Taiwanese noodle soups, dry noodles, bento rice combos, and appetizers.

restaurant.name: JJ's Kitchen
restaurant.desc: JJ's Kitchen is a restaurant in North Vancouver offering both indoor and outdoor seating in a non-smoking environment.

restaurant.name: Suzette's
restaurant.desc: Suzette's Deli is a weekday breakfast and lunch spot tucked into a Burnaby business park, known for fresh, natural ingredients across a broad menu of bagels, wraps, sandwiches, soups, and pastries. Under newer ownership with a revamped menu, it caters heavily to the local office crowd and offers full catering services for group orders. A touring cyclist passing through the Henning Drive corridor would find solid takeout options and a wide selection of handheld, portable fare.

notes.Packed lunches: Website lists 'Special Lunch Box for Group Orders (minimum 10 boxes)' and 'Special Sandwich Box for Group Orders' / 'Special Wrap Box for Group Orders' on the catering menu, indicating packaged lunch options are available

restaurant.name: Sushi Main
restaurant.desc: Sushi Main is a Japanese restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street corridor offering a broad menu of sushi rolls, sashimi, nigiri, donburi, teriyaki, and noodle dishes. The restaurant serves both dine-in and online delivery orders, with a free delivery radius of 3 km. It sits in the lively Main Street neighbourhood, a natural waypoint for cyclists touring south Vancouver.

notes.Takeout: Website features 'Order Online' and states free delivery within 3 km; takeout and online ordering are core offerings

restaurant.name: Fry's Red Wheat Bread Bakery
restaurant.desc: Fry's Bakery is a small family-run wood-fired sourdough bakery in the Vic West neighbourhood of Victoria, using organic stone-milled flours and locally sourced ingredients to produce long-fermentation sourdough breads, pastries, and pizza. The business has remarkable historical continuity — the original Fry's Bakery was founded nearby in 1897 by the current owner's ancestor, and the modern operation revived that legacy in 2012 at a storefront directly across the street from the original location. It functions as a community-supported artisan bakery, also supplying a select few local shops and restaurants.

restaurant.name: Politano Cafe
restaurant.desc: Politano Cafe is listed as a cafe in Sidney, BC on OpenStreetMap. No business website content is available to describe the offering, atmosphere, or what a touring cyclist would find here. Physical existence and current operation cannot be verified from available sources.

restaurant.name: Hi5 Pizza and Donair
restaurant.desc: Hi5 Pizza and Donair is a neighbourhood fast-food shop on East Hastings Street in Vancouver specializing in pizza and donairs, making their dough in-house daily and using house-made sauce from local tomatoes. Cyclists passing through the area can order online for quick counter pickup via SkipTheDishes, UberEats, or DoorDash, or call ahead to skip the line.

restaurant.name: Scott Hill Pizza
restaurant.desc: Scott Hill Pizza is a local, independently owned pizza restaurant that has been serving the Newton neighbourhood of Surrey since 2006. The shop specializes in homemade pizza sauce, fresh dough, and a wide roster of specialty pies — from a classic Meat Lovers to a Butter Chicken pizza — available for pickup or local delivery. A strip-mall takeout operation with no drive-through, it is a practical hot-meal stop for cyclists passing through Surrey's Newton area.

notes.Takeout: Website prominently features a 'Pick Up' section and 'Pick Up DEALS', including pickup-only specials

restaurant.name: House of India
restaurant.desc: House of India is an Indian restaurant on Main Street in Vancouver's Strathcona neighborhood. It serves as a dining option for cyclists passing through this area.

restaurant.name: Just Another
restaurant.desc: Just Another is a cafe located on West Broadway in Vancouver's Kitsilano area. Situated along a well-traveled urban cycling corridor, it could be a convenient stop for cyclists heading through the west side of the city.

restaurant.name: Dutch Wooden Shoe Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Dutch Wooden Shoe Cafe is a breakfast and brunch restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver specializing in Dutch-inspired dishes including traditional pannekoeks, Eggs Bene-Dutch on Dutch rusks with Edam cheese and Hollandaise, and Dutch recipe waffles. The menu also reflects the Dutch-Indonesian colonial culinary tradition with dishes like Nasi Goreng and Bahmi Goreng served with shrimp chips. Gluten-free pannekoek options are available on request, and the menu offers broad variety from hearty meat platters to vegetable-forward options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'All Pannekoeks are available gluten free – please ask your server.' Menu also includes multiple vegetarian-suitable options including Veggie Hash pannekoek, Sautéed Mushroom & Eggs Hollandaise, and Spinach & Tomatoes Benny

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: This McDonald's sits on the busy Main Street corridor in Vancouver, operating without a drive-through in a format suited to foot and cycle traffic. The full menu spans breakfast through late night, with McCafé beverages available alongside the standard burger lineup. It is a practical high-calorie resupply point for cyclists passing through the Main Street and 29th Avenue neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: District Noodle House
restaurant.desc: District Noodle House is a South Vancouver Vietnamese restaurant founded by two friends, Jennifer and Donna, after years of pandemic-related delays pushed their opening back to 2021. The kitchen focuses on hand-crafted, time-intensive dishes — including pho broths simmered for over eight hours and hand-rolled spring rolls — served in a sit-down setting that also supports delivery via multiple platforms. The restaurant has earned recognition among Vancouver's top restaurants and maintains a dedicated vegan menu section.

restaurant.name: Kabuki Sushi
restaurant.desc: Kabuki Sushi is a Japanese and Asian restaurant in Pitt Meadows serving sushi and other dishes made with fresh ingredients. The restaurant offers both dine-in with table reservations and online ordering, making it a convenient stop for cyclists riding the Pitt Meadows area. Its name pays homage to the highly stylised classical Japanese dance-drama known for elaborate costumes and detailed movement.

detail.address: 12522 Harris Rd, Pitt Meadows, BC V3Y 2J4

restaurant.name: Pita Land
restaurant.desc: Pita Land Victoria is part of a Canadian halal Middle Eastern chain serving shawarma, falafel, kebabs, wraps, and rice plates rooted in family recipes originating in Toronto in 2003. Located in Victoria's Wilson Street area, it offers both dine-in and takeout with a broad menu that accommodates a range of dietary needs. The emphasis on fresh, unprocessed ingredients and generous portions makes it a practical stop for hungry cyclists.

detail.address: 182 Wilson St, Unit #110, Victoria, BC V9A 7N6

restaurant.name: Thai-Isaan
restaurant.desc: Thai-Isaan is a small, family-run restaurant in Tsawwassen serving authentic homestyle Thai and Isaan cuisine made with fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The cozy, welcoming space is filled with traditional decorations and is well-suited to a solo dinner or a group meal after a day on the bike. Takeout is available for cyclists who need to eat on the go.

restaurant.name: Drumroaster Coffee
restaurant.desc: Drumroaster Coffee is a family-owned specialty coffee roastery and café that has been roasting and serving ethically sourced beans since 2007, located in Cobble Hill just off the Trans-Canada Highway. The Oglend family brings decades of coffee industry experience, sourcing directly from farms in Colombia, Ethiopia, Peru, Kenya, and Guatemala with a philosophy of long-term producer relationships. It is a local anchor on Vancouver Island's cycling corridor, with its beans served at cafés from Tofino to Victoria.

restaurant.name: Linh Café
restaurant.desc: Linh Café is a casual French-Vietnamese restaurant in Vancouver's Beach District, tucked under the Granville Bridge at the corner of Pacific and Granville Streets. Chef-owner Tai Nguyen trained at several acclaimed French restaurants in Vancouver before merging his Vietnamese heritage with classical French technique — resulting in a menu that spans salad rolls and pho-adjacent comfort alongside foie gras, steak tartare, and Beef Wellington using locally sourced BC and Alberta ingredients. The restaurant opened in 2014 and relocated to its current Granville Street home in 2021.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes: Red Beet Salad, Mimosa Salad, Wild & Cultivated Mushrooms, Cheese Omelette; no explicit vegan or gluten-free labeling found

restaurant.name: Pappa Leo's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Pappa Leo's Pizza is a Lower Mainland pizza chain that has been locally owned and operated since 2003, with each outlet run by community members rather than a corporate franchisee. The brand is known for scratch-made dough and award-winning pizzas loaded with fresh ingredients, available for pickup or delivery. Touring cyclists passing through New Westminster can grab a quick meal with contactless payment options.

detail.address: 450 East Columbia Street, Unit 102, New Westminster, BC

restaurant.name: Latin Fiesta
restaurant.desc: Latin Fiesta is an authentic Mexican restaurant located in Kelowna's Rutland neighbourhood, celebrated for scratch-made dishes like hand-pressed pupusas, Tacos Dorados, and slow-cooked pozole rojo. Cyclists will find a relaxed, festive atmosphere with an outdoor patio for al fresco dining when weather permits, plus a broad menu with vegetarian and gluten-free options. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery, making it a flexible stop for riders at different energy levels.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly calls out 'Vegetarian Friendly' and 'Gluten Free Options' as named features; menu lists vegetarian taco, burrito, quesadilla, tamale, and kids options

restaurant.name: Skye Avenue Kitchen & Lounge
restaurant.desc: Skye Avenue Kitchen & Lounge is an upscale restaurant and whisky lounge in Surrey's Central City, established in 2023 and claiming Canada's largest whisky collection with over 1,300 expressions sourced from whisky-producing regions worldwide. The menu is built around modern Canadian cuisine drawing on global influences, and the venue has earned TripAdvisor's Traveller's Choice Award. A touring cyclist stopping here would find an elevated sit-down dining experience with dedicated gluten-free, brunch, happy hour, and high tea menus.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website confirms a dedicated Gluten-Free menu ('crafted with care for dietary needs... prepared separate using certified gluten-free ingredients') and vegetarian options appear on the main menu

restaurant.name: Embe Bakery
restaurant.desc: Embe Bakery is a local bakery located in Duncan, BC on Vancouver Island. For touring cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley, it represents a stop for fresh baked goods in a community known for its agricultural and artisan food scene. Contact details and amenity information are not confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: Tim Hortons is a widespread Canadian coffee and quick-service chain. This North Vancouver location offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a convenient rest point for touring cyclists. The franchise provides reliable, accessible service along cycling routes.

restaurant.name: 2 For 1 Great Cannon Pizza
restaurant.desc: A 2-for-1 pizza fast food spot serving the Westshore communities of greater Victoria, including Langford, Colwood, and surrounding areas. The online ordering focus and takeout-oriented format makes it a practical stop for cyclists looking for a quick, filling meal. The unit-114 location suggests it sits within a larger commercial or strip-mall complex.

restaurant.name: Naughty Nellie's Fish & Chips
restaurant.desc: Naughty Nellie's is a neighbourhood fish and chips shop on Shelbourne Street in Victoria offering a wide range of fresh seafood — halibut, cod, ling cod, salmon, prawns, oysters, and scallops — alongside classic British-style sides. The restaurant operates both a takeout counter and a dining room, making it a flexible stop for cyclists who want to eat in or grab food on the go. Homemade chips, coleslaw, and tartar sauce round out a menu built around generous combo portions.

restaurant.name: Harrison Hamburgers
restaurant.desc: Harrison Hamburgers is a casual American-style burger restaurant situated in the heart of Harrison Hot Springs, a popular lakeside resort town. The kitchen is known for standout items like the Fish Burger and Mushroom Swiss Burger, alongside classic sides such as onion rings, sweet potato fries, and milkshakes. Outdoor seating is available, and the welcoming atmosphere and convenient location on Esplanade Avenue make it a natural rest stop for cyclists passing through the Harrison Hot Springs corridor.

detail.address: 111-196 Esplanade Ave, Harrison Hot Springs, BC V0M 1K0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly mentions veggie omelet and fresh green salad as menu items

restaurant.name: The Basic
restaurant.desc: The Basic is a family-owned breakfast and lunch restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, previously known as Joe's Grill, with over 30 years serving the local community. Classic homemade dishes — eggs Florentine, French toast, pulled pork hash — are made with locally sourced ingredients in a friendly neighbourhood-diner setting. Outdoor seating makes it a practical mid-ride refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the West End.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple egg-based and vegetarian breakfast options

restaurant.name: Ramen Gojiro
restaurant.desc: Ramen Gojiro is Canada's first Jiro-style ramen shop, part of the Menya Kouji Group, specializing in voluminous gatsuri-style bowls with house-made noodles, rich pork-and-chicken broths, and extensive topping customization. The menu spans classic, spicy, tsukemen, vegetarian, and donburi options alongside house-made gyoza, making it a versatile and filling stop in downtown Vancouver. Pickup ordering and fresh noodle delivery are both available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'VEGETARIAN RAMEN: Creamy miso & soy milk broth topped with assorted vegetables & a shitake mushroom' and 'MATCHA VEGE' gyoza stuffed with soy meat, cabbage, garlic, and chives

restaurant.name: Fish & Rice Sushi & Beyond
restaurant.desc: Fish & Rice is a Japanese sushi restaurant in downtown Pemberton opened in 2017 by chef Koji Miyagawa, a Sea to Sky local with nearly three decades of culinary experience. The menu spans traditional sashimi, specialty rolls, Japanese appetizers, and cooked entrees in a cozy sushi bar setting. The restaurant has earned a TripAdvisor five-star rating and 'Best of Pemberton' recognition, making it a notable stop for cyclists passing through the Sea to Sky corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'Gluten free options available'; menu includes multiple vegetarian items (Edamame, Gomae, Vegetable Gyoza, Avocado rolls, Cucumber rolls, Vegetable rolls, Agedashi Tofu)

restaurant.name: Pizza 64
restaurant.desc: Pizza 64 is a fast-casual pizza chain with a Richmond location in a strip-mall unit on Thorpe Road. The restaurant offers both walk-in pickup and delivery, with indoor seating available. It is part of a multi-location BC franchise with an online ordering system.

restaurant.name: Sopra Sotto
restaurant.desc: Sopra Sotto is a sit-down Italian pizzeria and pasta restaurant on Burnaby's Hastings Street corridor, one of two Lower Mainland locations. The kitchen makes fresh pasta in-house and fires pizzas in a wood-burning oven, with a full menu spanning antipasti, pastas, and Neapolitan-style pies. The restaurant accommodates large group bookings and private buyouts, making it a viable stop for club rides or touring groups.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Burnaby and Vancouver menus mark vegetarian items with (v), gluten-friendly options available for pastas (+$3) and pizzas (+$4.5), dairy-free items marked (df) on Vancouver menu, and vegan mozzarella offered as a pizza add-on (+$3)

restaurant.name: Q Brew Coffee Bar
restaurant.desc: Q Brew is a specialty coffee bar in rural Lac La Hache, bringing quality espresso to the remote Southern Cariboo region. The business features outdoor seating and serves as a notable stop for touring cyclists passing through.

detail.address: 3979 Cariboo Highway, Lac La Hache, V0K 1T0

notes.Wi-Fi: No fee in

restaurant.name: Happy Sushi
restaurant.desc: Happy Sushi is a neighbourhood Japanese restaurant on Victoria Drive in Vancouver offering a broad menu of sushi, nigiri, donburi, tempura, ramen, and udon. The restaurant emphasises fresh, high-quality ingredients and serves both dine-in and takeout customers. It is a practical meal stop for cyclists exploring the Victoria Drive corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian items: Vegetable Tempura, Yam Tempura, Pumpkin Tempura, Vegetable Udon, Agedashi Tofu, Edamame, Seaweed Salad, Gomaae Spinach Salad, and Inari Nigiri. No explicit vegan or GF labelling observed

restaurant.name: Bourbon St. Grill
restaurant.desc: Bourbon St. Grill is a Cajun/Creole-inspired fast-food counter located in the Metrotown food court in Burnaby, serving dishes like blackened chicken, jambalaya rice, and mashed potatoes in a quick-service, choose-your-own-combo format. It is one of several BC locations of the chain and sits inside one of Metro Vancouver's largest transit-accessible shopping centres. For a cyclist passing through Burnaby on Kingsway, it offers a fast, affordable, hot meal with confirmed bike parking and free Wi-Fi.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: A Subway franchise on Main Street in Penticton serving made-to-order footlongs, 6" sandwiches, wraps, and salads with fresh-cut vegetables and fresh-baked bread. This independently owned and operated location offers in-restaurant dining, curbside pickup, and delivery, making it a quick and flexible stop for cyclists passing through town. Breakfast items are also available.

restaurant.name: King Do Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A Chinese seafood restaurant located in Surrey offering delivery and takeout services. Provides dining options for touring cyclists seeking a meal between rides.

restaurant.name: Spice Kitchen The Indian Palette
restaurant.desc: Spice Kitchen The Indian Palette is an Indian restaurant in Chilliwack offering buffet service. This provides a casual, self-service dining option for touring cyclists passing through the region.

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Freshslice Pizza is a Canadian quick-service pizza chain offering pizza by the slice and whole pies for takeout and delivery. The menu includes classic and specialty Feast pizzas alongside a gluten-free cauliflower crust option, making it a flexible stop for cyclists with dietary needs. As a high-turnover slice shop, it offers a fast, affordable hot meal option on the road.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists Veggie pizza as a Classic option; Gluten Free Cauliflower crust is listed in the allergen/nutritional info page

restaurant.name: The Butler's Pantry Bake Shop
restaurant.desc: The Butler's Pantry Bake Shop is a bakery in Lake Cowichan. It offers a convenient food stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Darcy's Pub
restaurant.desc: Darcy's Pub is a downtown Victoria pub on Wharf Street serving house-made west coast pub fare alongside a curated selection of local BC beers and original cocktails. The venue hosts regular live music events and features both indoor and outdoor seating. It is an adults-only (19+) licensed establishment.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'House made west coast pub fare with gluten friendly and vegan options.'

restaurant.name: My Name Is Sushi
restaurant.desc: My Name Is Sushi is a Japanese restaurant on Jacklin Road in Langford offering a broad menu of sushi, sashimi, nigiri, maki, teriyaki, udon, donburi, and bento boxes. The restaurant supports online ordering with pickup, delivery, and dine-in options, and has been noted for gluten-free sushi options. It is a neighbourhood spot in the Westshore area of Greater Victoria.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Blog post titled 'Gluten Free Sushi' confirms gluten-free options are available; vegetarian/vegan status not explicitly stated

restaurant.name: Jambo Grill
restaurant.desc: Jambo Grill Tandoor & Paan House is a family-owned African and Indian fusion restaurant operating since 2005 on Vancouver's busy Kingsway strip, a short walk from Joyce SkyTrain station. The kitchen draws on cooking traditions from Iran, India, East Africa, and Canada, turning out tandoori meats, curries, biryanis, and house-made naan alongside a fully licensed bar in a space that seats up to 100 people. All meats are halal, dishes are made to order, and the restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, delivery, and large-scale catering.

restaurant.name: Long Beach Golf Course Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Long Beach Golf Course is a 9-hole championship course minutes from the world-famous Long Beach in Pacific Rim National Park, operating a Tacofino food outlet on site alongside a campground, driving range, and pro shop. The Tacofino serves tacos, burritos, and snacks in a casual West Coast counter-service style that fits the area's surf-and-outdoors culture. Situated on the Pacific Rim Highway between Ucluelet and Tofino, it sits squarely on one of BC's most-travelled cycle-touring corridors.

detail.address: 1850 Pacific Rim Hwy, Tofino, BC V0R 2Z0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian options confirmed on Tacofino menu: Yam Taco (tempura yam, sriracha crema, kale cabbage slaw, pickled ginger), Bean & Cheese burrito, Chips & Guac, and Tater Tots

restaurant.name: The Mexican Antojitos y Cantina
restaurant.desc: The Mexican Antojitos y Cantina is a full-service Mexican restaurant and cantina on Vancouver's Granville Street, serving traditional antojitos, regional moles, fresh aguachile, and an extensive tequila and mezcal cocktail program. The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating and hosts regular events including weekly La Lotería Night. Online ordering is available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the heart of downtown Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes vegetarian-adaptable items: Enfrijoladas (cheese-filled corn tortillas with option to add veggies), guacamole, nachos (meat-free base), and multiple non-alcoholic drinks. No explicit vegan or GF claims

restaurant.name: Hops
restaurant.desc: Hops is a neighborhood pub in downtown New Westminster specializing in micro-brews from the Pacific Northwest, with a rotating selection of craft drafts, cocktails, and a full food menu prepared by in-house staff. The pub offers both a cozy indoor space and a summer patio, and is notably dog-friendly, providing water and treats for well-behaved canine companions. Regular events including Sunday cult-classic movie nights, Tuesday trivia, and open game nights make it a lively social hub in the heart of New Westminster.

restaurant.name: Wooden Fish
restaurant.desc: Wooden Fish is a Vietnamese restaurant on North Vancouver's Marine Drive with both indoor and outdoor seating areas. It's a casual dining option where touring cyclists can stop for Southeast Asian cuisine while exploring the North Shore cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Deville Coffee Bernard
restaurant.desc: Deville Coffee Bernard is a specialty coffee chain cafe situated on Bernard Avenue, Kelowna's main downtown thoroughfare and a natural waypoint for cyclists exploring the city core. The chain operates across Western Canada with a focus on quality coffee and a streamlined cafe experience. An order-ahead option makes it a quick stop for riders who want to minimize time off the bike.

restaurant.name: The Shed
restaurant.desc: The Shed is a pizza and coffee shop on Cypress Bowl Road in West Vancouver, near Cypress Mountain, offering both indoor and outdoor seating. It serves as a food and beverage stop for cyclists and visitors in the area.

restaurant.name: Happy Slice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Happy Slice Pizza is a quick-service pizza-by-the-slice outlet located inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre, Kelowna's largest indoor mall on Harvey Avenue. The mall setting gives cyclists a sheltered place to grab a quick hot meal along one of the city's main commercial corridors. The business was previously branded as Freshslice Pizza, a Canadian chain, and appears to have rebranded at this location.

restaurant.name: Sushi ON
restaurant.desc: Sushi ON is a Japanese restaurant in Burnaby's Edmonds neighbourhood offering dine-in, takeout, and third-party delivery through Skip the Dishes, Uber Eats, and DoorDash. The menu centres on sushi rolls, with house favourites like California Roll and Tempura alongside a broader selection of Japanese dishes. It is one of two Lower Mainland locations, with a sister restaurant in Port Coquitlam.

restaurant.name: Hanayuki Sushi
restaurant.desc: Hanayuki Sushi is a Japanese restaurant on Ioco Road in Port Moody, serving sushi and offering online ordering through their website and a dedicated app. It sits in a strip-mall-style address with a unit number, making it a convenient sit-down or takeout stop for cyclists riding through the Port Moody area.

detail.address: 100-221 Ioco Rd, Port Moody, BC V3H 2V7

restaurant.name: Kam Do Bakery
restaurant.desc: Kam Do Bakery is a beloved Chinese bakery in Richmond serving freshly made pastries, savory buns, egg tarts, and traditional baked goods to a steady stream of neighbours and visitors. Located in a mall unit steps from a busy bus stop, it has earned a 4.1/5 rating across over 1,200 reviews and is regarded as one of the best Chinese bakeries in the area. A touring cyclist could stop here for a quick, filling snack—generous fillings and individual wrapping make the buns easy to take on the road.

detail.address: 6211 No. 3 Rd Unit 130, Richmond, BC V6Y 0C2

restaurant.name: Italian Tomato Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Italian Tomato is a sit-down Italian restaurant in Richmond with over a decade of experience serving traditional dishes like lasagna and cannelloni. It offers a highly customizable pasta menu with 12 pasta types and 39 freshly-made sauces, plus thin-crust pizza made with house-made dough and San Marzano tomatoes. Takeout and delivery are available alongside dine-in service, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists in the Bridgeport Road corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Catering menu marks multiple items as vegetarian with an asterisk, including Pomodoro, Primavera, Portofino, Alfredo, and Pesto sauces. No explicit vegan or gluten-free claims found

restaurant.name: Sunrise Pita Bread
restaurant.desc: Sunrise Pita Bread is a family-run Burnaby bakery founded in 2005 that produces stone-ground whole-wheat pita bread and pita chips using all-natural ingredients. Products are stocked at major supermarkets across the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley, but cyclists can also pick up fresh bags directly at the bakery outlet. It is a compact specialty stop for high-quality fresh bread to fuel a ride.

restaurant.name: Megabite
restaurant.desc: Megabite Pizza is a BC-based pizza franchise chain with outlets across the Greater Vancouver area. The menu spans pizzas, wings, poutine, chicken rolls, cheese sticks, and beverages, providing a substantial calorie stop for cyclists. Catering orders can be placed online for group rides or events.

restaurant.name: The Vic Downtown
restaurant.desc: The Vic Downtown is a specialty cafe in the heart of Kamloops that roasts its own coffee beans in small batches on-site and stocks over 65 varieties of loose-leaf tea. Situated on the corner of 4th and Victoria, the shop draws a loyal downtown crowd to its sunny patio and comfortable interior. Touring cyclists will find a broad food menu spanning breakfast sandwiches, wraps, pastries, and savoury baked goods alongside quality locally-roasted coffee.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists vegetarian rolls, GF carrot cake, GF chocolate brownies, GF chocolate chip cookies, GF breakfast sandwiches, and dairy-free + GF Emily's fudgy chocolate chunk cookies
notes.Device charging: Website front page states 'plenty of outlets' available for customers inside the cafe

restaurant.name: Liuyishou Hotpot Robson
restaurant.desc: Liuyishou Hotpot Robson is the Vancouver West End outpost of an international Chinese hotpot chain with locations across North America, including two other BC locations in Richmond and Burnaby. The restaurant sits on Robson Street, a main artery running from downtown Vancouver toward Stanley Park — a natural corridor for city-touring cyclists. It offers an all-you-can-eat hotpot format alongside a regular menu.

restaurant.name: PB X1 PIZZA AND GRILL
restaurant.desc: PBX1 Pizza and Grill is an Abbotsford pizzeria and grill that blends Italian-style pizza with South Asian-influenced dishes such as Punjabi Tadka and Paneer Pizza, made with farm-fresh ingredients. The restaurant offers both dine-in table reservations and takeout, positioning itself as a casual sit-down spot as well as a quick pickup option. With multiple Abbotsford locations and a menu spanning pizzas, wings, lasagna, and salads, it is a substantial refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Paneer Pizza (paneer is a vegetarian ingredient) and Salads as featured items

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: Tim Hortons is a national Canadian coffee chain offering brewed coffee, specialty beverages, baked goods, wraps, soups, and hot breakfast items at its Valemount outpost on Swift Creek Road. In a small, remote mountain community sitting between Prince George and Jasper on Highway 5, this is one of very few quick-service food options available to touring cyclists resupplying in Valemount. Both dine-in and take-out service are available.

detail.address: 1506 Swift Creek Road, Valemount, BC V0E 2Z0

restaurant.name: Teppan Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Teppan Kitchen is a teppanyaki fast food restaurant located in downtown Vancouver at 555 West Hastings Street. The basement-level location makes it a convenient meal stop for cyclists navigating the downtown area.

restaurant.name: The Cranberry Arms Hotel & Pub
restaurant.desc: The Cranberry Arms is a historic pub and hotel south of Nanaimo with roots dating to 1878, when it was established by Irish settlers on property reportedly won in a card game. It operates as a full-service restaurant and bar with draught beer, daily specials, and live events including karaoke nights. Hotel accommodation is available on-site, making it a potential stop for touring cyclists seeking food, drink, and a bed in the Cedar area.

restaurant.name: Dosa Paragon
restaurant.desc: Dosa Paragon is an Indian restaurant on Victoria's Wharf Street offering takeout service. The restaurant provides a food and beverage option for touring cyclists in the downtown waterfront area.

restaurant.name: Boston Pizza
restaurant.desc: Boston Pizza Broadway is a Canadian chain family restaurant and sports bar located on West Broadway in Vancouver, celebrating 60 years as Canada's largest casual dining brand. The menu spans gourmet pizzas, pasta, wings, sandwiches, and shareables, with vegan and GlutenWise® options available. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down dining experience alongside takeout and delivery service on a busy urban corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Vegan and GlutenWise® options also available' on the menu page; GlutenWise® items are itemized on the nutritional information page

restaurant.name: Wendel's Books
restaurant.desc: Wendel's Bookstore & Cafe is a well-established local institution in the historic village of Fort Langley, pairing a working bookstore with a full-service cafe that serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner using locally sourced BC ingredients. The heated covered patio overlooks the picturesque village, and the in-house bakery produces fresh desserts daily alongside a full espresso bar featuring Moja coffee, BC wines, and craft beers. Fort Langley is a popular cycling destination on the scenic Fraser River, making this a natural rest stop for touring riders.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website cafe page explicitly states 'plant based and gluten-free options'; menu lists multiple plant-based items (Avocado Tofu Breakfast Wrap, Coconut Curry Bowl, Avocado Cucumber Wrap) and gluten-free bread/wrap substitution

restaurant.name: Rocky Mountain Flatbread
restaurant.desc: Rocky Mountain Flatbread is an award-winning family pizza restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street, built around a forno-fired pizza oven and open kitchen where diners can watch pizzas being handcrafted from scratch. The 50-seat dining room includes a full bar pouring local craft beers, BC VQA wines, and house cocktails, plus a kid's play kitchen area. The restaurant emphasizes local and organic ingredients, Ocean Wise seafood, free-range meats, and is always nut-free.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'lots of gluten-friendly & vegan options. Always nut free.' Thursday Date Night menu also explicitly lists 'vegetarian, gluten free & vegan options.'

restaurant.name: HiFive Chicken
restaurant.desc: HiFive Chicken is a BC-born fast-food chain established in 2016 that has grown from a single Vancouver location to over 11 outlets across the Lower Mainland. The menu centres on freshly marinated fried and roasted chicken served in pieces, family platters, and sandwiches, alongside sides like poutine and maple chive biscuits. The chain also runs a dedicated boxed lunch program, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking to fuel up or stock up for the road.

detail.address: 8669 East Tenth Avenue, North Vancouver, BC

notes.Takeout: Website references in-store ordering ('Only When You Visit Us In-Store') alongside online ordering and delivery-app options, confirming counter/takeout service
notes.Packed lunches: Menu page lists 'Boxed Lunch' and 'School Lunch Program' as distinct menu categories
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a 'Veggie Sandwich' (toasted bun, mayo, lettuce, veggie patty, tomato, onion rings)

restaurant.name: Stuffies Pastries
restaurant.desc: Stuffies Pastries brings a South Korean-inspired pastry concept to Metro Vancouver, specialising in animal-shaped, waffle-like treats stuffed with custard crème, jam, and buttercream fillings. The brand holds exclusive Canadian rights to the DeliManjoo automatic baking machines that produce the signature pastry, and has grown to three locations across North Vancouver, Metrotown (Burnaby), and Guildford (Surrey). Beyond pastries, the menu includes coffee, soft-serve, and sandwiches, salads, and soups — making it a viable quick-stop for a touring cyclist moving through Metro Vancouver.

notes.Takeout: Website menu pages show individual add-to-cart options for all products with no dine-in option referenced
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website /stuffies page lists a '24 Pieces Reg. Vegan/GF' product variant, confirming both vegan and gluten-free pastry options are offered

restaurant.name: Panda Island Chinese Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Panda Island is a cozy family-run restaurant in Central Oak Bay, specializing in Guangdong-style cuisine with Western influences, led by head chef Wen. The kitchen emphasizes fresh ingredients and minimized oils, offering everything from quick on-the-go lunches to relaxed dine-in experiences. Delivery is available through DoorDash and SkipTheDishes, making it a flexible stop for cyclists passing through the Oak Bay Avenue corridor.

detail.address: 1950A Oak Bay Avenue, Victoria, BC V8R 1C9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple dishes can be made gluten-friendly (wheat-free and soy sauce-free) on request. Tofu Chop Suey (No. 8) can be made 'gluten-friendly and/or vegan upon request.' Hot & Sour Soup has a vegetarian version. Site notes they do not have a dedicated gluten-free kitchen and advises celiac customers to inquire

restaurant.name: Chongqing Restaurant
restaurant.desc: ChongQing Restaurant is a multi-location Szechuanese Chinese restaurant that has operated in the Vancouver area for over twenty years. The Kingsway location in Burnaby offers both dine-in with indoor seating and online ordering for takeout and delivery. It is one of four Lower Mainland locations, making it a recognizable chain stop for cyclists traveling along the Kingsway corridor.

restaurant.name: Elysian Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Elysian Coffee Roasters is a Vancouver-based specialty roaster with four neighbourhood cafes across the city; this downtown location sits at the corner of Burrard and Helmcken. The company sources and roasts its own single-origin and blended coffees, and the cafes also carry brewing gear, teas, and books. The downtown café offers both indoor and outdoor seating and is wheelchair accessible.

restaurant.name: Trini to D Bone
restaurant.desc: Trini to D Bone is a family-run Trinidadian restaurant on Burnside Road West in Saanich, founded by husband-and-wife team Nirmala and Jeff. The kitchen specialises in authentic Caribbean roti — warm flatbreads stuffed with curried chicken, goat, shrimp, pulled pork, or vegetables — alongside doubles, a beloved Trinidadian street food. It is widely regarded as one of the few spots on Vancouver Island serving genuine Trinidadian cuisine, with a loyal following among locals and visitors passing through the area.

detail.address: 650 Burnside Road West, Saanich, BC V8Z 1M8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Roti with Curried Vegetable' as a standard all-day menu item

restaurant.name: World Wrap Place
restaurant.desc: World Wrap Place is a family-run Middle Eastern fast food counter in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, founded in 2005 by Chef Majid Shekarchi. The menu revolves around donairs, wraps, and platters built from local farm-fresh ingredients, with full halal certification. It is a compact, takeout-friendly stop offering both meat and vegetarian or vegan options a short ride from the central waterfront cycling routes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website product collections include a labelled 'Vegetarian / Vegan 5 products' section; individual items include the Vegetarian Falafel Wrap and a Falafel Platter

restaurant.name: Trails Coffee
restaurant.desc: Trails Coffee is a specialty coffee cafe in Anmore situated steps from the trailheads of Buntzen Lake, Sasamat Lake, White Pine Beach, and Belcarra Park, making it a natural stop for cyclists and hikers exploring the area. The cafe operates as a community hub with a mobile ordering app, a local vendor marketplace, and a fundraiser program supporting area schools and sports teams. It is one of the few cafes in the region to prominently accept Bitcoin Lightning payments, with a discount offered for doing so.

restaurant.name: Monarca
restaurant.desc: Monarca is a Mexican supper club and restaurant in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, led by Executive Chef Francisco Higareda whose family roots near the Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve in Michoacán shape his refined, tradition-inspired menu. The name honours the monarch butterfly, a symbol of returning ancestral spirits in Mexican culture, and the venue's concept mirrors that transformation — an elegant dinner that evolves into a full DJ-driven nightlife experience as the evening deepens. For a touring cyclist looking for a substantial sit-down meal with cocktails in the heart of Gastown, Monarca offers an elevated, occasion-worthy stop.

restaurant.name: The Hatching Post
restaurant.desc: The Hatching Post is a Texas-style BBQ saloon and microbrewery in West Kelowna, specialising in slow-smoked meats alongside a roster of house-crafted beers available on tap. The patio welcomes dogs, the dining room is kid-friendly with high chairs on request, and the venue offers private event bookings and a Beer Club. It is a full sit-down destination with online reservations through OpenTable and takeout or delivery via DoorDash.

restaurant.name: Cue's N Cushion
restaurant.desc: Cue's N Cushion is a family-owned social entertainment lounge open since 2022 in Tsawwassen (Delta), BC, combining pool tables, darts, board games, air hockey, arcade games, and ping pong with a Mediterranean-inspired kitchen serving snacks, meals, specialty coffees, and milkshakes. The venue runs a packed weekly events calendar—movie nights, pool training sessions, UFC screenings, and fundraiser events—and can host private or corporate groups with full-lounge buyouts. A touring cyclist would find a lively, welcoming stop with real food and a range of beverages in a purpose-built community hub.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: 'Veggie Dog' explicitly listed on the published menu as a standalone item

restaurant.name: Pho Lan Beef Noodle Soup
restaurant.desc: Pho Lan Beef Noodle Soup is a Vietnamese restaurant on Number 3 Road in Richmond specializing in beef noodle soup. It operates on a cash-and-e-transfer model with no credit or debit cards accepted, which is worth noting for cyclists on the road. The restaurant is located along a busy commercial corridor in Richmond's city centre.

restaurant.name: Originals Mexicano
restaurant.desc: Originals Mexicano is an authentic Mexican restaurant that has operated since 2013 inside a quaint heritage home on Clarke Street in Port Moody. The intimate setting offers traditional Mexican dishes alongside cocktails, Micheladas, and Mexican coffee, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists seeking a real sit-down meal. It is part of a small local restaurant group with several other Greater Vancouver locations.

detail.address: 2231 Clarke St, Port Moody, BC V3H 1Y6

restaurant.name: Big Star Sandwich Co.
restaurant.desc: Big Star Sandwich Co. is a Lower Mainland sandwich chain founded in 2013 by tradesman-turned-restaurateur Clint Bondzuk, now operating six locations across the region. Their signature filone bread — a rustic cross between ciabatta and baguette — is loaded with in-house slow-roasted beef (13 hours overnight), hand-pulled turkey, and imported bacon, all sliced fresh daily. The Richmond location on Coppersmith Way also offers catering and online ordering, making it a practical stop for a hearty mid-ride meal.

restaurant.name: SABOOS BREAD
restaurant.desc: SABOOS Bread Factory Ltd. is a North Vancouver artisan bakery and specialty food shop producing Persian flatbreads, sourdough loaves, Lebanese-style baklavas, and fresh cream puffs daily with no additives or preservatives. Beyond baked goods, the shop carries a broad selection of Middle Eastern and Mediterranean provisions including housemade hummus, halva, dairy products, imported olives, premium olive oils, and spices — making it a practical stop for cyclists looking to restock quality pantry staples. The combination of fresh bread and ready-to-eat items like hummus makes it a notable provisioning option in North Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Pink Peppercorn Seafood House
restaurant.desc: Pink Peppercorn Seafood House is a fine-dining seafood restaurant on Kingsway in East Vancouver, well regarded for fresh, ethically sourced ingredients including wild-caught salmon, Nova Scotia lobster, and free-range chicken. The menu blends classic West Coast preparations with creative chef-driven dishes, and the intimate décor is pitched toward special-occasion dining. Takeout is also available for those eating on the go.

restaurant.name: Bow & Stern
restaurant.desc: Bow & Stern is a family-owned, ocean-inspired seafood restaurant group founded in 2014 by the Smith family, with their signature fish and chips recipe at the heart of the menu. The Brentwood location, the newest of three BC restaurants, is situated inside The Amazing Brentwood shopping centre on the second floor. It offers dine-in table bookings, online pickup ordering, and group booking options.

restaurant.name: Eden Bento Café
restaurant.desc: Eden Bento Café is a Japanese restaurant in Kamloops serving sushi, bento boxes, sashimi, donburi, poke bowls, and more from a retail unit on Lansdowne Street.
