It sits in a suburban commercial area of Maple Ridge, a community popular with cyclists exploring the Fraser Valley and Golden Ears region. Touring cyclists passing through would find it a straightforward stop for a hot meal.

restaurant.name: Lucky Yeung
restaurant.desc: Lucky Yeung is a Chinese restaurant in Kamloops, BC. The OSM record also carries a motel tag, suggesting the building may have historically served or currently serves a dual hospitality function. Touring cyclists passing through Kamloops would find it a potential stop for a sit-down Chinese meal.

restaurant.name: Spice Magic
restaurant.desc: Spice Magic is an Indian restaurant located in Penticton, BC, offering flavours from the Indian subcontinent to locals and visitors alike. Penticton sits at the heart of the Okanagan cycling circuit between Skaha and Okanagan lakes, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists moving through the region. The website is live but minimal, so cyclists should contact the restaurant directly to confirm details before visiting.

restaurant.name: Grimm's Gourmet & Deli Ltd & Brooklyn's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Grimm's Deli is a family-owned landmark in downtown Pemberton that has served the community for over 27 years, offering all-day breakfast featuring locally sourced Pemberton potatoes, gourmet sandwiches, homemade soups, and Brooklyn's Pizza. The restaurant prides itself on ingredients sourced from the Sea to Sky Corridor and is known for its signature homemade cream puffs and Grandma's Hot Sauce. It is a beloved local gathering spot and a natural refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the Pemberton Valley.

restaurant.name: The General Public
restaurant.desc: The General Public is a Japanese fusion sushi restaurant situated at Main and 17th in Vancouver, self-described as 'Sushi To Die For.' The tagline 'From Kits to Main' signals a relocation from Kitsilano to its current spot on a well-travelled urban cycling corridor. It offers both dine-in reservations and a dedicated takeout hotline.

restaurant.name: Yummy BBQ Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Yummy BBQ Restaurant is a barbecue and Chinese restaurant located in a commercial complex in Richmond, BC. Serving a blend of BBQ and Chinese cuisine, it likely caters to the dense mixed-use neighbourhood around the McClelland Road corridor. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's urban grid would find it a potential stop for a sit-down meal.

detail.address: 4720 McClelland Road, Unit 1830, Richmond, BC V6X 0M6

restaurant.name: Baan-Do's Stir Fry
restaurant.desc: Baan Do's Stir Fry is a Chinese fast-food restaurant on James Street in Duncan, BC, serving stir-fry dishes and appetizers with online ordering for both pickup and delivery. It sits in a commercial building in Duncan's main commercial corridor, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley. The straightforward menu and quick-service format suit a cyclist needing a warm, filling meal without a long wait.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: 'Veg Spring Roll (5pcs)' listed as a popular menu item on the website, confirming at least one vegetarian option

restaurant.name: Aureliana
restaurant.desc: Aureliana is a casual American diner on West Hastings in downtown Vancouver, turning out hearty breakfasts, hand-formed burgers, and fresh-cut fries in a compact, approachable setting. The menu spans classic morning fare like pastrami hash and eggs benedict through to poutine, milkshakes, and draft beer, making it a capable refuelling stop. Online ordering is available, and catering can be arranged by phone or email.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a VEGGIE burger (mushroom patty, american cheese, lettuce, tomato, pickle, onion, signature mayo) plus vegetarian-friendly sides and desserts. No explicit vegan or gluten-free options mentioned

restaurant.name: Bucky's Taphouse
restaurant.desc: Bucky's Taphouse is a long-established neighbourhood pub in Langford that explicitly courts cyclists rolling off the nearby Galloping Goose Regional Trail. It offers an extensive menu of wings, burgers, poutine, and appies alongside a sunny west-facing patio the website bills as 'the sunniest patio on the West Shore.' The spot has served the community for over 40 years and has been under its current kitchen direction since 2013.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items marked '(V)', including Cauliflower Bites and Classic Poutine; note that (V) appears inconsistently on some meat-containing dishes as well

restaurant.name: Pho 99
restaurant.desc: Pho 99 is a Vietnamese noodle house in Surrey's Fleetwood area serving a broad menu of pho, grilled meats, rice plates, and Vietnamese submarine rolls. The restaurant emphasizes traditional balance of flavours using fish sauce, fresh herbs, and rice-based dishes. Table reservations and online ordering are available, making it a convenient full-service stop for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Ricky's
restaurant.desc: Ricky's is a Canadian family restaurant chain with over 60 years of history, serving all-day breakfast, lunch, and dinner in a full-service dining room. The Ladner location is a dual-branded Ricky's Famoso facility offering dine-in, takeout, and delivery via Skip the Dishes and UberEats. It sits on Ladner Trunk Road and provides a reliable, family-casual meal stop with a broad menu that includes vegetarian options.

detail.address: 5239 Ladner Trunk Rd, Ladner, BC V4K 1W4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes diverse options consistent with vegetarian availability

restaurant.name: Super Great Pizza
restaurant.desc: Super Great Pizza is a small, no-frills pizza-by-the-slice shop located directly across from Joyce-Collingwood SkyTrain Station in East Vancouver, making it an exceptionally easy pit stop for cyclists on or near the Central Valley Greenway. The shop is known for generous cheese and toppings across a rotating variety of slices, with indoor seating available though limited. Takeout is the dominant mode here, well-suited to a quick refuel on the go.

restaurant.name: Panino Mio
restaurant.desc: Panino Mio is a North Burnaby Italian sandwich shop bringing award-winning panini from La Grotta Del Formaggio to Hastings Street, located next to Glenburn Ice Cream. The menu features a wide selection of pressed Italian sandwiches with specialty cured meats, imported cheeses, and house-made pesto, alongside cannoli, biscotti, and Italian sodas. Vancouver Magazine named it a top sandwich destination in Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes dedicated vegetarian panini: NAPOLETANO (fresh mozzarella, tomatoes, spinach, pesto) and VEGETARIANO (provolone, artichokes, roasted red peppers, olives)

restaurant.name: La Ruota
restaurant.desc: La Ruota Pizzeria is a Neapolitan-style pizza chain that hand-crafts its pies in a 900° oven using Caputo '00' flour and ingredients sourced from both Italy and BC. The West 4th Avenue location sits on one of Vancouver's key cycling corridors near the Arbutus Greenway. The chain operates a franchise model with multiple Metro Vancouver locations and an online ordering app.

restaurant.name: Pinoy Cravings
restaurant.desc: Pinoy Cravings is a Filipino fusion restaurant in Burnaby offering a broad menu of classic comfort dishes — silogs, barbecue, sizzling platters, noodles, and desserts — alongside catering and group reservation services. The restaurant presents traditional Filipino flavours with a creative twist in a family-friendly dine-in setting, and also offers takeout for customers on the go.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Crispy Tofu and Sizzling Tofu as dedicated vegetarian dishes; no vegan or GF claims confirmed

restaurant.name: Chef Claire's
restaurant.desc: Chef Claire's is a well-regarded Vancouver catering company operating out of a luncheonette on Main Street, serving sandwiches, soups, salads, and sweets to walk-in customers as well as offering platters, plated dinners, and frozen take-home meals. The business has been featured in Canada.com and regional food media, and its creative menu spans gluten-free cheese selections to Moroccan spiced lamb and fennel-cured wild salmon. Cyclists passing through Main Street's corridor can stop in for a quick lunch or pick up frozen meals for the road.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Platters menu labels numerous items 'GF – Gluten Free' (e.g. cheese selection, turkey breast, smoked salmon, fresh fruit, crudités, porchetta); vegetarian platters include Mediterranean Meze and farmers market crudités

restaurant.name: Steamworks Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Steamworks Mount Pleasant Kitchen & Taphouse is a craft brewery taproom at the gateway to Vancouver's historic Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, pouring 20 Steamworks taps alongside 10 rotating local guest taps. The full kitchen serves reimagined pub classics, bold fusion dishes, and plant-based options including vegan jambalaya. A dog-friendly patio overlooking an urban park adds to its appeal as a neighbourhood gathering spot.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'plant-based delights', 'mouthwatering plant-based options', vegan jambalaya, and 'Vegan Goddess Bowl' (Gastown menu reference)

restaurant.name: Mr Mikes
restaurant.desc: MR MIKES SteakhouseCasual is a long-running Canadian chain (est. 1960) serving premium steaks, burgers, pastas, and shareable appetizers in a relaxed, no-dress-code atmosphere. The Vernon location welcomes both walk-ins and reservations, and positions itself as a neighbourhood gathering spot for locals and tourists alike. A solid option for touring cyclists seeking a full sit-down meal with a broad menu after a day on the road.

detail.address: 3908 32 Street, Vernon, British Columbia, V1T 5P2, Canada

restaurant.name: Straight Outta Brooklyn NYC Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: A New York-style pizzeria on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver, serving pizza by the slice and whole pies. The restaurant has both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the city centre.

restaurant.name: Hei Hei Rice Roll
restaurant.desc: Hei Hei Rice Roll is a Chinese fast-food counter specialising in cheung fun — steamed rice noodle rolls — a popular Cantonese street-food staple. The Chinese name 囍記腸粉 signals a traditional Hong Kong-style offering, making it a quick and filling stop for cyclists passing through Richmond's busy Westminster Highway corridor. It is situated inside a larger commercial building (unit 2430), likely a food court or plaza.

restaurant.name: Roxy Burger
restaurant.desc: Roxy Burger is a locally owned and operated full-service restaurant on Granville Street in Vancouver's entertainment district, serving generous portions of comfort food anchored by a broad menu of made-to-order burgers using Certified Angus Beef. The venue doubles as a late-night sports bar with daily live sports and events, and offers both indoor and outdoor seating. It's a practical refuelling stop for cyclists moving through downtown, with online ordering available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a Veggie Burger: 'Soy veggie patties made special, just for us.'

restaurant.name: Fritz's European Fry House/Poutine
restaurant.desc: Fritz's European Fry House is a Davie Street institution that has been serving Belgian-style fries and poutine since 1996, making it one of Vancouver's longest-running late-night spots. It is a pickup-only counter known for its signature gravy with real cheese curds and an extensive sauce wall with over 20 dipping options. Located in the heart of the West End, it offers a quick and filling refuel for cyclists passing through.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Veg & Gluten-Free Gravy Available.'

restaurant.name: Bibi's Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Bibi's Kitchen is listed in OSM as a restaurant on Terminal Avenue in Vancouver. However, the business website is currently parked and inaccessible, and no phone number is available for verification.

restaurant.name: Papa John's
restaurant.desc: Papa John's on McKenzie Avenue is a pizza chain franchise serving Victoria's Saanich area, offering delivery and carryout of pizza, breadsticks, and wings. It is a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the McKenzie Ave corridor who want a hot meal or quick carryout. The location is part of the national Papa Rewards loyalty program.

restaurant.name: James Bay Coffee House
restaurant.desc: James Bay Coffee House is a neighbourhood café in Victoria's historic James Bay district, steps from the Inner Harbour and Beacon Hill Park — a well-travelled area for cycling tourists exploring the city. It opened in September 2025, making it a fresh addition to the local café scene. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find it a convenient stop in a walkable, bike-friendly part of downtown Victoria.

restaurant.name: Number e Food
restaurant.desc: Number E Food is a chef-inspired gourmet sandwich shop that has been serving downtown Vancouver's Burrard Street corridor for over 13 years, specializing in artisanal sandwiches on house-made focaccia and Tuscan bread sourced from local purveyors including Two Rivers Meats. Beyond sandwiches, the shop offers fresh salads, soups, take-home meals, a cookie bar, and Moja coffee roasted on the North Shore. Eat-in and takeout are both available, with vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free choices catering to a broad range of dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Catering page explicitly lists 'vegetarian, vegan, gluten free' dietary options

restaurant.name: Kirstens Hideout Café
restaurant.desc: Kirstens Hideout Cafe is a cozy homestyle cafe located inside the Acadian Motel on Columbia Street in Kamloops, specializing in breakfast, brunch, lunch, sandwiches, and coffee. The cafe emphasizes a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere with comfort food and a variety of menu options. For touring cyclists moving through Kamloops, it offers a convenient morning or midday meal stop in the heart of the city.

restaurant.name: Baking Factory
restaurant.desc: Baking Factory is a bakery in a Richmond commercial complex on Cambie Road, presenting itself with an artisanal ethos centred on quality ingredients and hand-crafted flavors. OSM notes indoor seating is available, making it a potential sit-down rest stop for cyclists passing through the area. The business maintains an active social media presence via Facebook and Instagram.

restaurant.name: Esquimalt Bake Shop
restaurant.desc: Esquimalt Bake Shop is a family-owned institution in Victoria's Esquimalt neighbourhood, operated by owners Hong and Cam since 1992 and a fixture of the Esquimalt Plaza. The shop is celebrated for its freshly made donuts—particularly Apple Fritters and Raspberry Jam Filled—earning both Best Donuts and Best Bakery honours in the 2024 CommunityVotes Victoria awards. Beyond donuts, the full menu spans bread, sausage rolls, meat pies, scones, and cookies, making it a solid energy-restock stop for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Popeyes
restaurant.desc: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen is a well-known fast food chain specializing in Louisiana-style fried chicken and Southern-inspired sides. This downtown Vancouver location sits on Granville Street, a major commercial corridor convenient to cyclists moving through the city centre. Indoor seating is available, making it a viable stop for a sit-down meal after a ride.

restaurant.name: Burdock & Co
restaurant.desc: Burdock & Co is a Michelin-starred fine dining restaurant in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, opened by Chef Andrea Carlson in 2013 and the first Canadian restaurant owned and operated by a female chef to earn that distinction. The kitchen builds hyper-seasonal, botanically-driven tasting menus — called Moon Menus — around wild-foraged and locally grown Pacific Northwest ingredients that shift every two months. A bar area accepts walk-ins for individual courses and snacks, offering a more casual entry point into the experience.

restaurant.name: Fogg N' Suds
restaurant.desc: Fogg N' Suds is a full-service restaurant and beer bar situated beside the Holiday Inn Vancouver Airport Hotel in Richmond, BC. Known for an impressive beer selection and a broad menu spanning breakfast through dinner, it draws a mix of locals, airport travellers, and beer enthusiasts. The relaxed, welcoming atmosphere makes it a natural refuelling stop for anyone passing through the Richmond area.

restaurant.name: Local Pizza
restaurant.desc: Local Pizza is a Vancouver Island-born pizza chain emphasizing local ownership and fresh ingredients, with five locations across the Victoria area. The Shelbourne location serves the eastern Victoria neighbourhood with customizable and pre-set pizzas available for pickup or delivery. Founded on Vancouver Island and operated by local employees, it positions itself as a neighbourhood pizzeria rather than a national franchise.

restaurant.name: La Terrazza
restaurant.desc: La Terrazza is a fine-dining Italian restaurant in Yaletown, Vancouver, operating since 1998 under Chef-owner Gennaro Iorio and partners. The kitchen pairs heirloom Italian recipes with seasonal BC-sourced seafood and produce, backed by an award-winning cellar of over 2,000 Italian wines curated by an in-house sommelier team. Private dining rooms accommodate weddings, corporate events, and anniversary dinners, and the restaurant also hosts curated wine-pairing evenings.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes: Garden Arugula Apple Salad, Melanzane alla Parmigiana (baked Italian eggplant), Burrata & Beet Insalata, Burrata Caprese, and Insalata Caprese on the happy-hour menu

restaurant.name: Akira Sushi
restaurant.desc: Akira Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, a neighborhood well-traveled by cyclists heading to and from the Stanley Park seawall. The restaurant offers indoor seating and online ordering with a pickup option. Its location along Denman Street places it directly on one of Vancouver's primary cycling corridors.

restaurant.name: Surfside Grill
restaurant.desc: Surfside Grill is a takeout-focused seafood and burger restaurant located within Tsawaak RV Resort and Campground on Tofino's Pacific Rim Highway, founded by commercial fisherman Jeff Mikus. The menu leans heavily on fresh local seafood — fish tacos, chowder, oysters, and salmon burgers — sourced with the owner's direct knowledge of the BC fishing industry. A licensed patio serves local beers, ciders, and wines, and the site is accessible via a beach path from Mackenzie Beach.

detail.address: 1119 Pacific Rim Hwy - Tin Wis Road, Tofino, BC V0R 3A0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Veggie / Vegan $22' burger under Burgers & Sandwiches, and a 'GF bun' upgrade option is available

restaurant.name: Ocean Park Pizza & Steak house
restaurant.desc: A pizzeria and steakhouse restaurant located in Chilliwack's retail district. Combines two popular cuisines in one establishment, offering a range of dining options.

restaurant.name: Pound Steak
restaurant.desc: Pound Steak is a casual Japanese steakhouse in Richmond specializing in AAA Flat Iron Steak and handmade Hamburg Steak with Japanese-inspired sauces. The restaurant features a self-serve bar with unlimited Japanese-imported rice and miso soup with customizable toppings. Online ordering is available, and the dining experience blends authentic Japanese flavors with an approachable, casual atmosphere.

restaurant.name: Mayne Brewing
restaurant.desc: Mayne Brewing is a craft brewery in Sidney specializing in locally produced beer. It serves as a potential stop for touring cyclists passing through the area seeking refreshment at a local business.

restaurant.name: Cookies by George
restaurant.desc: Cookies by George is a proudly Canadian cookie chain founded in Vancouver in 1983, now franchised across Canada with its head office in Edmonton. Each location bakes fresh cookies daily in-store from scratch using natural ingredients and Valrhona chocolate, following the same original recipes from 1983. The chain offers a loyalty stamp card ('Club George'), catering trays, and a gluten-free/vegan macaroon option for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

restaurant.name: Sarhad Dhaba Indian and Pizza
restaurant.desc: Sarhad Dhaba is an Indian and pizza restaurant in Penticton serving a wide range of South Asian dishes — from Chana Bhatura and Goat Biryani to tandoori meats and vegetarian curries — alongside a pizza menu, all available for dine-in or takeout. The kitchen blends traditional techniques with a broad menu spanning snacks, mains, rice dishes, and sweets, making it a solid stop for a substantial hot meal mid-tour. Catering for large events is also available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu has a dedicated vegetarian section with numerous options including Dal Tadka, Chana Masala, Palak Paneer, Malai Kofta, and many others. No GF or vegan confirmation

restaurant.name: Between 2 Buns Burgers
restaurant.desc: Between 2 Buns is a smash burger spot on East Pender Street in Vancouver, specializing in smashed patties with online ordering and a catering menu. The restaurant has no drive-through, making it a walk-in or order-ahead destination. It also sells branded merchandise, suggesting a loyal local following.

restaurant.name: Morgan's
restaurant.desc: Morgan's is a restaurant in Chilliwack, BC. Website content is unavailable, limiting detail about specific offerings or amenities.

restaurant.name: The Stable House Bistro
restaurant.desc: The Stable House Bistro is a community-founded wine bar and bistro in Vancouver's South Granville neighbourhood, named to honour the historic stable structures that dotted the area over a century ago. The kitchen centres on seasonal, locally sourced sharing plates built around signature in-house charcuterie boards, while the eclectic wine list is curated by one of BC's top sommeliers with a focus on unpretentious everyday European wines. It is part of a small local restaurant group that also operates Brasserie Coquette and Fiore Famiglia, all within a short distance of each other in the same neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: The Bayside Restaurant & Lounge
restaurant.desc: The Bayside Restaurant & Lounge is the signature dining room of the Bayside Oceanfront Resort, a full-service oceanfront hotel in Parksville. The kitchen spotlights local ingredients through a rotating seasonal menu supported by an extensive cocktail and wine program. Weekend evenings feature free live music, and a dedicated Sunday brunch service makes it a sociable stop for cyclists passing through town.

restaurant.name: Bar Bravo
restaurant.desc: Bar Bravo is a MICHELIN Guide Recommended seafood restaurant in Vancouver's Fraserhood neighbourhood, opened in August 2023 and awarded Vancouver Magazine's Best New Restaurant 2024. The small, intimate space features an open kitchen and an evolving seasonal menu of raw and cooked dishes with bold, globally inspired flavours. A touring cyclist stopping in would find a thoughtful bar program and creative cocktails alongside standout plates like Tofino King Salmon and house-shucked oysters.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes: marinated olives, roasted shishitos, V2 greens salad, burrata, Japanese eggplant, and mushroom pappardelle. A vegan-friendly 'cheesecake' made with cashew cream cheese is also offered

restaurant.name: Apple Tree Family Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Appletree Family Restaurant is a long-established regional-cuisine breakfast and lunch spot situated in the Admirals Walk shopping centre in View Royal, just outside Victoria. After more than two decades at Hillside Centre, it relocated to its current larger space in May 2013. It operates as a table-service family restaurant, making it a solid sit-down meal option for cyclists passing through the western Greater Victoria corridor.

restaurant.name: Pho Angkor
restaurant.desc: Pho Angkor Noodle House is a Vietnamese restaurant in New Westminster's Tenth Street area, known for its generous portions of pho and vermicelli bowls with multilingual menus in English, Vietnamese, and Chinese. Reviews praise the flavourful broth, crispy spring rolls, and quick service, making it a solid refuelling stop for hungry cyclists passing through the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu legend includes a vegetarian icon; menu offers Vegetable Noodle Soup, Wonton Vegetable Noodle Soup, and Thai Veggies Spring Rolls

restaurant.name: Chicko Chicken
restaurant.desc: Chicko Chicken is a Canadian fast-food chain specializing in fried chicken with multiple Lower Mainland locations, including this Lonsdale Avenue outpost in North Vancouver. The Lonsdale corridor is a busy cycling route connecting the waterfront to upper North Van, making this a convenient quick-stop option for riders. Orders are fulfilled as pickup, making it a fast refueling option mid-ride.

restaurant.name: 27th Street Grille1
restaurant.desc: The 27th Street Grille is the full-service restaurant within Divya Sutra Plaza & Conference Centre, a 138-room hotel in the heart of Vernon's North Okanagan. The hotel complex includes a swimming pool, sauna, and large on-site parking lot described as accommodating trucks with boats or small trailers. Touring cyclists staying or dining here would have access to a full suite of hotel amenities in a centrally located Vernon property.

restaurant.name: Tickleberry's
restaurant.desc: Tickleberry's is an Okanagan institution that has been scooping ice cream since 1990, offering 150 flavors alongside an in-house fudge factory where visitors can watch confections being made in real time. Beyond ice cream, the shop stocks chocolate-covered dried fruits, local crafts, and a broad gift selection, making it a natural and memorable rest stop on the Okanagan cycling corridor. A second location operates in Downtown Penticton.

detail.address: Hwy 97, Main St., OK Falls, BC V0H 1R0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Vegan Peanut Butter Brownie' as a flavor; 'NSA Caramel Macchiato' (No Sugar Added) also listed. No GF claim found

restaurant.name: Temaki Sushi
restaurant.desc: Temaki Sushi is a sushi restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, operating since 2003. The restaurant offers three seating styles — standard tables, a sushi bar, and a communal shared table — along with a full takeout and catering menu. They describe their approach as 'sushi reimagined,' with a focus on consistent quality and evolving flavours.

restaurant.name: Mükasi Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Mükasi Coffee Roasters is a North Vancouver–based specialty coffee roaster offering a range of single-origin and blended whole-bean coffees sourced from Ethiopia, Vietnam, Guatemala, Honduras, and Indonesia. Their lineup spans bold espresso blends to delicate floral washed naturals, with an emphasis on traceable origins and cupping notes. The business operates an active online store with local delivery and Canada-wide shipping.

detail.address: 417 Front Street Mews, New Westminster, BC V3L 1A4

restaurant.name: Señor Froggy
restaurant.desc: Señor Froggy is a Mexican fast-food restaurant situated in a shopping mall on Lansdowne Street in Kamloops. It features a salsa bar alongside its Mexican menu and includes sections for allergies and gluten-friendly choices. Catering services are also available for larger orders.

detail.address: Unit 235 - 450 Lansdowne Street, Kamloops, BC V2C 1Y3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu page explicitly lists 'Gluten Friendly' and an 'Allergies' section

restaurant.name: Switch
restaurant.desc: Switch is a bar and karaoke venue on Vancouver's Robson Street offering private karaoke suites, a food menu, and a drink menu. Located in the heart of the West End, it draws a lively evening crowd. The venue is wheelchair accessible per OSM tags and sits on one of Vancouver's most walkable and cyclable commercial corridors.

restaurant.name: Tippy's Cookhouse
restaurant.desc: A breakfast-focused restaurant on Bowen Island that opened in April 2024. It offers outdoor seating and serves as a convenient dining stop for touring cyclists exploring the island.

detail.address: 433 Bowen Island Trunk Road, Bowen Island, V0N 1G0

restaurant.name: Hush
restaurant.desc: Hush is the weekend coffee alter-ego of COFU Chinatown, a celebrated plant-based Japanese restaurant in Vancouver's Chinatown neighbourhood. The space offers specialty beans from Japanese roaster Hiyori, ceremonial-grade Uji matcha and hojicha from Kyoto, house-made sweets, and a short cocktail list. It shares the refined, quietly intentional atmosphere of the COFU brand, which earned national television recognition for its innovative fully plant-based omakase.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states 'COFU Chinatown is proudly 100% vegan'; Hush operates from the same location under the same brand. FAQ also notes gluten-free accommodation is available

restaurant.name: Tea Origin
restaurant.desc: Tea Origin (茗外) is a specialty Chinese tea bar and retail shop in Richmond that presents high-end Chinese teas through a modern lens while honoring traditional brewing methods. Operating under the legal entity Nutrinature Tea & Herbs Ltd., the business sources teas directly from producers in China and has each batch independently tested by Intertek for pesticide residues and heavy metals. Cyclists can stop in for a dine-in tea experience or pick up loose-leaf teas, curated gift sets, and tea accessories to go.

restaurant.name: Pizza Pizza
restaurant.desc: Pizza Pizza is a Canadian fast-food pizza chain founded in 1967, with over 750 locations coast to coast. This New Westminster outlet offers both indoor and outdoor seating along with takeout service. The chain carries a broad menu including vegetarian options and gluten-free crust, making it a quick calorie-refuel stop for riders passing through downtown New Westminster.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website FAQ confirms gluten-free crust option and vegetarian-compatible ingredients are available

restaurant.name: Skewers Souvlaki Pita Bar
restaurant.desc: Skewers Souvlaki Pita Bar brings authentic Greek street food to Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most popular cycling corridors. The kitchen uses BC-farmed chicken and pork alongside New Zealand lamb sirloin, marinated in-house for twelve hours in Greek olive oil and Mediterranean herbs, with every dish cut and prepared fresh daily. From classic pork gyro pitas to mixed grill platters and Cretan salads, it's a satisfying and affordable refuelling stop on a long urban ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Halloumi Cheese pita wrap, Mixed Salad with Feta, Greek Salad, and Cretan Salad — all vegetarian options

restaurant.name: The Sullivan
restaurant.desc: Established in 1925 and named after the Sullivan Mine that anchored Kimberley's economy for over a century, The Sullivan Pub (locally 'The Sully') is one of the town's most storied gathering spots. It serves a full pub menu of hearty classics and creative dishes alongside a wide selection of local and craft beers. Regular live music nights, karaoke, and music bingo make it a lively community hub, and an adjacent drive-through liquor store adds convenience for stocking up.

restaurant.name: Jigger's
restaurant.desc: Jigger's is a casual fast food fish and chips shop on Peninsula Road in Ucluelet. It serves quick takeout meals convenient for touring cyclists passing through the community. No amenities beyond basic takeout service have been confirmed.

restaurant.name: Sandcastle Sea Shoppe & Ice Cream Parlour
restaurant.desc: Sandcastle Sea Shoppe is an ice cream and gift shop on White Rock's waterfront Marine Drive, advertising over 50 flavours. It sits at street level on one of the most popular seaside cycling corridors in Metro Vancouver's south end. The dual ice cream and gift shop format is a classic seaside stop that typically draws walkers and cyclists exploring the White Rock promenade.

restaurant.name: John's Pan Pizza
restaurant.desc: John's Pan Pizza is a local Richmond pizzeria specializing in pan-style pizza made fresh daily, with dine-in, pickup, and delivery options. The menu spans classic and loaded pizzas, appetizers, flatbreads, sides, and milkshakes. Cyclists will appreciate the inclusive menu that includes gluten-free and vegan pizza options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'We do offer Gluten-free and Vegan pizza as well.'

restaurant.name: Chit Chat Burger Bar
restaurant.desc: Chit Chat Burger Bar is a casual lounge-style gourmet burger bar on downtown Vancouver's Granville Street, founded by Aldo Velaj with a commitment to fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The menu features hand-crafted burgers on brioche buns alongside creative loaded fries, tacos, salads, and house-made milkshakes and ice cream. An extensive cocktail list and rotating BC craft draft beers make it a lively spot for cyclists passing through the heart of the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Where Have You Bean! Vegetarian · 4oz Home-made Bean Patty' burger. Website also notes 'Allergen Friendly — You can specify if you have any allergies, and we can offer alternative options.'

restaurant.name: Harmony Bakery
restaurant.desc: Harmony Bakery is a bakery located in a commercial unit on Hazelbridge Way in Richmond, BC, an area known for its dense retail and dining options. The extensive menu spans Xinjiang-style lamb skewers and desert mutton to hand-caught seafood platters, cold dishes, and fried bistro bites, making it a substantive meal stop for hungry cyclists. The restaurant also supports online ordering for takeout.

detail.address: 7771 Westminster Hwy, Unit 180, Richmond, BC V6X3Y5

restaurant.name: Danpung Momiji 310
restaurant.desc: Danpung Momiji 310 is a restaurant located on Terminal Avenue North in Nanaimo, BC. The name blends Korean and Japanese words both referencing autumn foliage, suggesting an Asian culinary focus, though the specific cuisine and format could not be confirmed from available sources. It sits along a major arterial route through Nanaimo that touring cyclists commonly travel.

restaurant.name: Cafe Club
restaurant.desc: Cafe Club is a downtown Vancouver cafe on West Georgia Street built around an order-ahead model, letting customers skip the queue by ordering via the cafe's own mobile app or website before they arrive. The menu covers all-day breakfast and lunch — coffee, matcha lattes, juices, pastries, breakfast wraps, and salads — and the cafe also handles corporate and private event catering. Its location in Vancouver's business district makes it a convenient mid-ride fuel stop for cyclists moving through the city core.

detail.address: 1018 West Georgia St, Vancouver, BC V6E 2Y2

restaurant.name: Edo Japan
restaurant.desc: Edo Japan Country Club Centre is a Canadian-founded, Japanese-inspired fast-food franchise serving teppanyaki, hand-rolled sushi, bubble tea, and ramen from a mall food-court unit in Nanaimo. Founded in Calgary in 1979, the chain now has more than 200 locations nationwide and offers dine-in seating, take-out, delivery, and catering. It's a practical stop for a hot, filling meal on a ride through the Island Highway corridor.

detail.address: #103, 3250 Island Hwy N, Nanaimo, British Columbia

restaurant.name: Cafe Brio
restaurant.desc: Cafe Brio is a farm-to-table Italian-inspired restaurant in Victoria that has been showcasing the seasonal bounty of Southern Vancouver Island since 1997. The kitchen cures its own meats, butchers whole animals, makes fresh pasta, and sources produce from named local organic farms including Saanich Organics and North Star Organics. With a wine cellar of nearly 300 selections and capacity for private parties up to 70, it is a destination-worthy spot for a touring cyclist's evening meal.

restaurant.name: Boom + Batten Restaurant & Cafe
restaurant.desc: Boom + Batten is an elevated casual dining restaurant and café perched at Victoria's Inner Harbour, offering Pacific Northwest-inspired cuisine with inventive seasonal menus built around local and regional ingredients. The venue runs a full bar program alongside a daytime café and evening dining room, with a weather-dependent patio overlooking the harbour. It has earned awards and recognition and is a destination-worthy waterfront stop in the heart of Victoria.

detail.address: 2 Paul Kane Place, Victoria, BC V9A 7J8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Happy hour menus explicitly mark multiple items with (v) for vegan (e.g. falafel, market greens, szechuan broccolini), (veg) for vegetarian (e.g. margherita pizzette), and (gf) for gluten-friendly options

restaurant.name: Tacofino - Burrito Bar
restaurant.desc: Tacofino is a popular BC-born Mexican-inspired chain that grew from a food truck in Tofino into a network of fast-casual restaurants across the province. The Metrotown location is a sit-down spot near the Metrotown shopping hub in Burnaby, offering burritos and west coast beach food. Cyclists passing through the Burnaby area will find it a convenient stop for a filling meal, with takeout and delivery options available.

restaurant.name: Tacoholic
restaurant.desc: Tacoholic is a Mexican fast-food taco shop on Fraser Highway in Langley, BC, operating without a drive-through window. It sits on a busy commercial arterial that touring cyclists on the Trans Canada Trail corridor pass through when moving between Langley and Abbotsford. The Facebook branding as a 'Taco Shop' suggests a casual, quick-service format well suited to a quick refuel stop.

restaurant.name: La Bocca
restaurant.desc: La Bocca is an Italian restaurant located on Village Stroll in the heart of Whistler village, one of the primary pedestrian thoroughfares in the resort. Its central location on a busy tourist promenade makes it a natural stop for cyclists passing through Whistler. No current web presence could be verified to describe the dining experience in more detail.

restaurant.name: Salt Chinatown
restaurant.desc: The OSM record lists 'Gina's' as a Mexican restaurant at 227 E Pender Street in Vancouver's Chinatown neighbourhood, but the address is currently occupied by Salt Tasting Room, a long-running Vancouver institution that pivoted from a charcuterie and wine bar to a sandwich and deli shop in late 2023. Salt is owned by Seán and Erin Heather (also owners of The Irish Heather) and focuses on artisan salami, cheese, and condiment-laden sandwiches and salads.

restaurant.name: 184 Pizza Corner
restaurant.desc: 184 Pizza Corner is a locally owned pizza and Indian cuisine restaurant in Surrey's Cloverdale neighbourhood, open since 2007 and recognized as a neighbourhood favourite. The menu spans classic and specialty pizzas alongside a full Indian cuisine menu, with both pickup and delivery available through online ordering. A touring cyclist looking for a hot meal with variety in South Surrey will find this a convenient stop near 64 Avenue.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website specialty pizza list includes 'Alfredo Veggie Pizza' confirming at least one vegetarian option

restaurant.name: Chipotle
restaurant.desc: Chipotle West End - Davie Street is a fast-casual Mexican restaurant located near Davie & Burrard in Vancouver's West End, offering customizable burritos, bowls, tacos, quesadillas, and salads. The chain operates under a 'Food with Integrity' philosophy, using 53 real ingredients sourced from farms following humane and sustainable practices with no artificial colors, flavors, or preservatives. In-store pickup and delivery are both available, making it a quick and filling carbohydrate stop for cyclists traveling the Davie Street corridor.

restaurant.name: The Lamplighter Public House
restaurant.desc: Vancouver's oldest pub, The Lamplighter has operated since 1925 in the heart of historic Gastown, in a building that dates to 1899 when it opened as The Dominion Hotel. The 4,000 sq ft brick-lined venue features stained glass windows, a street-level patio, 50 beers on tap, arcade games, and a DJ booth—and holds the distinction of being the first beer parlour licence issued in BC after Prohibition. Operated by the Donnelly Group's Freehouse Collective, it sits on Water Street within easy reach of the Gastown cycling network.

restaurant.name: La Brasserie
restaurant.desc: La Brasserie is a casual all-day restaurant on Whistler's pedestrian Village Stroll, serving a European-bistro inspired menu that includes Eggs Benedict, cheese fondue, and rotating cocktail specials. Operating on a strict first-come, first-served basis with no reservations, it offers a relaxed drop-in dining option in the heart of Whistler Village. Its central location on the Stroll makes it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Underbelly - By the Pig
restaurant.desc: Underbelly - By the Pig is a restaurant in Kamloops located at 120 5th Avenue. It provides a dining stop for touring cyclists exploring the interior of British Columbia.

restaurant.name: Wah Laiyuen
restaurant.desc: Wah Laiyuen is a restaurant at 560 Fisgard Street in Victoria's historic Chinatown, one of the oldest in Canada. It sits on one of the most recognizable streets in the city, making it a natural stop for cyclists exploring downtown Victoria.

restaurant.name: Akbar's Own
restaurant.desc: Akbar's Own is a family-owned Indian restaurant on West Broadway serving generations-old recipes made with fresh local ingredients and traditional cooking methods. Located a short ride from downtown Vancouver near Commercial Drive, it offers a warm sit-down dining room and a full menu spanning curries, tandoori grills, and vegetarian dishes. Catering and online ordering are also available, making it a practical stop for a group or a solo cyclist wanting a substantial meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes (Aloo Gobi, Paneer Pakora); no vegan claim found on website

restaurant.name: Red Robin
restaurant.desc: Red Robin is a casual burger restaurant chain. The Chilliwack location features outdoor seating and is situated on South Fraser Way in a commercial area, offering a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking a meal break.

restaurant.name: Happy Village Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Happy Village Restaurant serves daily meals in Sooke, on Vancouver Island's west coast. A convenient dining stop for cycling tourists passing through the rural area.

restaurant.name: Double DD Pizza
restaurant.desc: A pizza restaurant on West 4th Avenue in Vancouver. Serves as a dining option for cyclists traveling through the area.

restaurant.name: Nero Belgian Waffle Bar
restaurant.desc: Nero Belgian Waffle Bar is an independent, family-owned business founded by Belgian immigrants who arrived from Belgium in 2011 and began crafting authentic Brussels and Liège waffles on Robson Street in 2012. The Yaletown location is their flagship downtown spot, seating 70-plus guests and offering a full menu of sweet and savoury waffles from breakfast through late evening. Freshly baked mini Liège waffles are available daily for takeout, and a pre-order pickup option makes it easy for cyclists on the move to grab something on their schedule.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website notes vegan mini waffles are available but specifies them only for the South Granville location

restaurant.name: The Poké Lounge
restaurant.desc: The Poké Lounge is a poke bowl restaurant located on Yates Street in downtown Victoria. It sits in a retail building in a walkable, cycling-friendly part of the city core. Touring cyclists passing through Victoria would find it a convenient stop for a fresh, customizable meal.

restaurant.name: Sushi Yan Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Sushi Yan was a sushi restaurant located on Thurlow Street in downtown Vancouver, BC. Based on OSM data it offered indoor seating in a non-smoking environment. Its current operational status is uncertain, as the domain now resolves to a domain-sale parking page.

restaurant.name: Firehouse Subs
restaurant.desc: Firehouse Subs is a North American sandwich chain with a public-safety theme, known for hot subs piled with premium meats and toppings. This Burnaby location on Dawson Street offers takeout service and is part of a franchise network that donates a portion of sales to first-responder causes. For a touring cyclist needing a quick, filling meal stop, it provides a familiar menu with hearty sandwich options.

restaurant.name: SYU Japanese Cuisine & Sushi Bar
restaurant.desc: SYU Japanese Cuisine & Sushi Bar is an upscale Japanese restaurant in Richmond offering a sushi bar, à la carte dining, omakase experiences, and lunch sets. The restaurant blends traditional Japanese culinary artistry with contemporary elegance and is noted by customers for exceptionally fresh seafood and an authentically Japanese atmosphere. It sits near the River Road corridor, making it a potential destination stop for cyclists exploring the Richmond waterfront area.

restaurant.name: Fresh Sushi
restaurant.desc: Fresh Sushi is a Japanese restaurant located on Expo Boulevard in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, steps from the seawall and the city's busy cycling network. The restaurant offers dine-in and takeout options, with online ordering available through the website. Its location near the waterfront makes it a convenient stop for cyclists riding the False Creek routes.

restaurant.name: Mystic Market
restaurant.desc: Mystic Market is UVic's main food court, housed in the Jamie Cassels Centre on the University of Victoria campus, with seven distinct kiosks covering everything from Asian noodles and Indian cuisine to pizza, tacos, ramen, and breakfast sandwiches, plus a General Store for grab-and-go items. The breadth of vendors and the campus setting make it a practical stop for touring cyclists passing through the Saanich area who need a full meal or quick provisions. The General Store also stocks packaged items and drinks for riders stocking up before heading out.

detail.address: Jamie Cassels Centre, University of Victoria, Victoria, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website dietary legend lists Vegan, Vegetarian, Made without gluten, and Made without dairy options across multiple kiosks

restaurant.name: Cha Don
restaurant.desc: Cha Don (茶檔) is a Chinese fast food spot in Richmond, BC — the name is Cantonese for 'tea stall,' suggesting a Hong Kong-style cha chaan teng offering quick, affordable Chinese and Chinese-Western dishes. Richmond's dense cycling network and large Cantonese-speaking community make it a natural stop for riders exploring the city. Details about the menu and setup are limited due to sparse online information.

detail.address: 4540 Number 3 Rd Unit 1175, Richmond, BC V6X 4E4, Canada

restaurant.name: Bohemian Cafe & Catering Co.
restaurant.desc: Known locally as 'The Boh,' Bohemian Cafe & Catering Co. has been an Okanagan brunch institution on Kelowna's main Bernard Avenue since 1991, drawing a loyal following for its hearty breakfast and brunch fare in a family-friendly atmosphere with outdoor patio seating. The business also operates a catering arm serving private and corporate events across the region. Its central downtown Kelowna location makes it a natural morning fuel stop for cyclists passing through the city.

restaurant.name: The Dolar Shop Burnaby
restaurant.desc: The Dolar Shop Burnaby, branded on the website as The Dolar Shop Station Square, is a Macau-style hot pot restaurant where guests cook fresh, house-made ingredients in individual tabletop pots at their own pace. The concept draws on East-West culinary influences rooted in Macau, emphasizing premium ingredients, communal dining, and a philosophy of continuous innovation. The restaurant features both indoor and outdoor seating and is wheelchair accessible.

restaurant.name: Captain's Oven Pizza
restaurant.desc: Captain's Oven Pizza is a BC-grown Neapolitan-style pizza chain founded by two siblings who trained in Naples and Istanbul before bringing their craft to North Vancouver. Pizzas are hand-stretched daily and baked in under two minutes in a custom 3-ton stone-brick oven imported from Tuscany, producing a light, charred crust true to the Neapolitan tradition. The North Vancouver location is one of five across the Lower Mainland, with a broad menu of meat, vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options alongside salads, desserts, and catering.

detail.address: 935 Marine Dr, North Vancouver, BC V7P 1S3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated Vegetarian Pizza category on menu; vegan cheese available; gluten-free crust offered. FAQ notes: 'Captain's Oven is not a gluten-free environment.'

restaurant.name: York St. Diner
restaurant.desc: York St. Diner is a locally owned family restaurant that has been a Cowichan Valley staple since 2012, known for scratch-made eggs Benedict, chicken and waffles, and a rotating menu of daily features. It is fully licensed and sources ingredients from local Cowichan Valley suppliers. Touring cyclists will find a welcoming diner atmosphere with full breakfast, brunch, lunch, and dinner service.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu states 'Gluten Free Options & Egg Whites Available – Just ask your Server'; Veggie Skillet listed on menu; blog post titled 'Gluten-Free and Classic Breakfast Options at York Diner'

restaurant.name: District Eleven
restaurant.desc: District Eleven is a Vietnamese-Asian fusion restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street, founded by Chef Phi Le — formerly of New Westminster's Pho Pho You — and built around bold flavours honouring his Vietnamese heritage alongside Japanese and broader East Asian influences. The menu ranges from elevated Vietnamese classics and street-food-inspired appetizers to experimental fusion dishes like Pho Poutine and Aburi Crispy Rice. It describes itself as a restaurant run by cooks for those passionate about food.

restaurant.name: Sequoia Coastal Coffee
restaurant.desc: Sequoia Coastal Coffee is a Vancouver Island-rooted cafe that sources locally produced ingredients to craft coffee drinks, handmade sandwiches, salads, and baked goods celebrating West Coast culture. The Royal Bay location in Colwood operates as a drive-thru, offering a quick, no-fuss stop for cyclists moving through the western Greater Victoria corridor. The brand partners with local suppliers including 2% Jazz coffee and Truffles Catering.

restaurant.name: Denny's
restaurant.desc: Denny's is a casual American dining chain with a location in Chilliwack. It serves traditional diner fare and provides a sit-down dining experience for travelers. As an established chain restaurant, it offers a familiar meal option for touring cyclists seeking a place to rest and refuel.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast food restaurant on Scott Road offering burgers, chicken, wraps, and McCafé beverages, with a drive-through lane for quick stops. The location sits along a busy arterial corridor and is a recognizable, consistent option for touring cyclists needing a fast meal or snack refuel. Standard Canadian McDonald's menu items including breakfast are available.

restaurant.name: Popina
restaurant.desc: Popina is a fast-casual canteen perched at the Ferry Dock on Granville Island, conceived by a team of celebrated Vancouver chefs who wanted to elevate street food with a lobster roll, fried chicken, falafel, and a flagship burger. The menu expands into local seafoods, specialty toasts, soft-serve, and salads, making it a compelling stop for cyclists passing through the Granville Island end of the Seawall. Being open-air and right on the waterfront, it fits naturally into a cycling day on Vancouver's waterfront routes.

detail.address: Ferry Dock, Granville Island, Vancouver, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'amazing falafel' as one of the four signature menu items, confirming at least one vegetarian option

restaurant.name: Pane E Formaggio
restaurant.desc: Pane E Formaggio is a family-owned artisanal bakery in downtown Vancouver that has been crafting sourdough breads, pastries, and sweet treats using traditional recipes since 2005. The bakery maintains a decade-old sourdough starter and sources ingredients from local farmers committed to sustainability. Beyond walk-in retail, it offers catering and wholesale services, and provides both indoor and outdoor seating for customers.

restaurant.name: Shabusen
restaurant.desc: Shabusen is a Japanese and Korean restaurant in downtown Vancouver that has been operating since 1992. The restaurant caters to vegetarian diners seeking a full dining experience.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian options confirmed ( in OSM)

restaurant.name: Booster Juice
restaurant.desc: Booster Juice is a Canadian juice-bar chain offering freshly blended smoothies, cold-pressed juices, açai bowls, and light food items with a focus on health and active lifestyles. This location sits in a retail unit at 4949 Canoe Pass Way in Tsawwassen, near the BC Ferries terminal area. The menu is entirely vegetarian and vegan-friendly, making it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists seeking a lighter, nutrient-dense option.

detail.address: 4949 Canoe Pass Way, Unit 1610, Tsawwassen, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Corporate website confirms menu is built around fruits, vegetables, and plant-based ingredients

restaurant.name: Raisu
restaurant.desc: Raisu is a Japanese restaurant on Vancouver's busy West 4th Avenue cycling corridor, specializing in Teishoku (Japanese set meals) and sake. It is part of a wider hospitality group with locations across Vancouver and Toronto. Both dine-in reservations and takeout/pickup are available, making it a practical stop for cyclists passing through Kitsilano.

restaurant.name: Uncle Fatih's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Uncle Fatih's Pizza is a Metro Vancouver pizza chain with 12 locations, serving freshly made pies on daily-prepared dough with non-hydrogenated ingredients and an emphasis on vegetables over cheese. The Brentwood, Burnaby outpost offers a relaxed indoor dining room along with robust takeout and online ordering. The menu spans meat and vegetarian specialties, with vegan cheese (Daiya), gluten-free crust (OGGI brand), and halal chicken available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website catering FAQ confirms: vegan cheese (Daiya), gluten-free crust (OGGI brand), and a dedicated Veggie Pizzas menu section

restaurant.name: Juke
restaurant.desc: Juke is a popular fried chicken restaurant in Vancouver's Chinatown, self-billed as Vancouver's number one fried chicken spot with a menu blending Southern and Asian influences — from Nuoc Cham ribs to jalapeño cheddar waffles. The adjoining Chickadee Room cocktail bar was recognized by Vancouver Magazine as the best Happy Hour in the city. A high-volume, independently operated spot open every day, it makes a solid refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the downtown core.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels gluten-free items: 'CHICKEN & WAFFLES (GF)' and 'GF BUN AVAILABLE' on sandwiches. No explicit vegetarian or vegan options confirmed

restaurant.name: The Juice Truck
restaurant.desc: The Juice Truck is a Vancouver-based cold-pressed juice bar and wellness shop with a storefront on West 5th Avenue, not far from popular cycling corridors. It specializes in made-to-order hydraulic cold-pressed juices, high-protein smoothies, and wellness shots using organic produce. Cyclists looking for a nutrient-dense, plant-based refuel stop will find a broad menu ranging from simple celery juice to dense superfood smoothies.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Entire in-store menu (juices, smoothies, shots) is plant-based: almond milk bases, vegetable/fruit ingredients, plant proteins (pea protein, hemp, chia). No animal products listed on the menu page other than optional collagen add-in

restaurant.name: Juillet Cafe
restaurant.desc: Juillet Cafe is a specialty cafe established in July 2016 in the Lougheed neighbourhood of Burnaby, with a particular focus on premium matcha, hojicha, and espresso drinks alongside house-made pastries, cakes, and sandwiches. The cafe positions itself as a community hub, hosting events and workshops centred on coffee culture. For a touring cyclist, it offers a welcoming stop for quality drinks and baked goods with online pre-ordering available for pickup.

restaurant.name: Milos Greek Taverna
restaurant.desc: Milos Greek Taverna is a full-service Greek restaurant on the Esplanade in Harrison Hot Springs, overlooking the lake with seating on a second-floor deck. It is known for generous portions of roasted lamb, calamari, and ribs, and has earned a 4.2-star rating from over 630 Google reviews. Touring cyclists passing through Harrison Hot Springs will find a sit-down meal with a scenic lakeside setting and online reservation options.

detail.address: 234 Esplanade, Harrison Hot Springs, BC V0M 1K0

restaurant.name: My Toan
restaurant.desc: My Toan is a chain of modern Vietnamese restaurants founded by a Vietnamese-Canadian entrepreneur who brought traditional recipes from his hometown to BC over 30 years ago. The menu centres on pho-style noodle soups, rice and vermicelli combinations, Vietnamese crepes, and baguettes. The OSM node is tagged at basement level (-1), consistent with its food-court locations inside Harbour Centre and Waterfront Centre in downtown Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists Vegetarian Tofu Spring Roll, Tofu Salad Roll, Veggie Salad Roll, Tofu Baguette, and Veggie Baguette

restaurant.name: One Under Vancouver
restaurant.desc: One Under is a 5,000-square-foot urban golf club, eatery, and bar centrally set in Vancouver's Financial District, featuring six HD Golf simulation bays alongside a full kitchen and craft cocktail bar. Guests can play virtual rounds on world-famous courses or compete in long-drive contests, then settle in for chef-crafted pizzas, sandwiches, and rotating local craft beers. The venue welcomes non-golfers as well, making it a lively spot for a meal or drinks in the heart of downtown.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels Ortaggio pizza as '(vegetarian)' and includes a Falafel Sandwich with house-made chickpea patties

restaurant.name: Sally's Homemade Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Sally's Homemade Ice Cream is a confectionery and ice cream shop tucked into a unit on 2nd Avenue in Richmond, BC. The 'homemade' branding suggests house-made ice cream products rather than a national franchise. It would make a sweet mid-ride treat stop for cyclists exploring the cycling-friendly streets and dyke trails of the Richmond area.

restaurant.name: Sushi Wara
restaurant.desc: Sushi Wara is an authentic Japanese restaurant situated just off the Trans-Canada Highway in Ladysmith, operated since 2016 by master chef Paul Pak who brings 30 years of Japanese culinary experience. The restaurant uses fresh, local fish and offers both indoor dine-in and outdoor patio seating, giving cyclists a comfortable place to rest. Its highway-adjacent location makes it a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley corridor.

restaurant.name: President Plaza Food Court
restaurant.desc: President Plaza Food Court is a multi-vendor food court located in the President Plaza shopping centre on Cambie Road in Richmond, BC. As a food court, it likely offers a variety of cuisines under one roof, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists looking for a quick, varied meal in Richmond's commercial corridor.

restaurant.name: Amici Wine Bar Osteria & Enoteca
restaurant.desc: Amici is a modern Italian wine bar in downtown Abbotsford celebrating the Italian tradition of gathering around food, wine, and conversation. The restaurant operates two concepts under one roof — an osteria-style main room and a Piccolo Pizzeria — with a curated Italian-inspired wine list and a members-only Supper Club launching in 2026. It's a sit-down destination well suited for a post-ride meal or a longer evening stop in the Fraser Valley.

restaurant.name: Osaka Sushi & Oshi
restaurant.desc: Osaka Sushi & Oshi is a fast-food Japanese counter located in the food court (concourse level, unit FC-18) of Harbour Centre in downtown Vancouver. The OSM record links it to the Hiro Japan Sushi Xpress brand, which has operated quick-serve sushi counters in BC food courts since 2003, though the Harbour Centre location no longer appears on that brand's website. The differing name and absent listing suggest the unit may have changed operators or closed.

restaurant.name: Bandra Cafe
restaurant.desc: Bandra Cafe is an Indian cafe on White Rock's Marine Drive that pays homage to the street food culture and Irani cafes of Mumbai's Bandra neighbourhood. The menu spans Mumbai classics like Pav Bhaji, Pan Rolls, and Iranian-style Biryani alongside an extensive chai and coffee program. The cafe is fully licensed and has a second location on Scott Road in Surrey.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Order Now (takeout only)' and lists Skip the Dishes, Uber Eats, and Doordash as ordering platforms

restaurant.name: Casa Beto
restaurant.desc: Casa Beto is a Mexican food truck rooted in traditional home-cook recipes, emphasising fresh locally sourced ingredients. For the 2026 season it operates out of Sunday Cider on the Sunshine Coast Highway in Gibsons. It is a takeout-only operation, making it a convenient roadside stop for cyclists travelling the Sunshine Coast route.

notes.Takeout: Food-truck format confirmed by website — takeout is the only service mode

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: A Starbucks Coffee location on Terminal Avenue in Nanaimo, a major arterial road near the BC Ferries terminal that sees significant through-traffic from cyclists traveling between Vancouver Island destinations. Outdoor seating is available, making it a viable rest stop. As part of the global Starbucks chain, it serves the full range of espresso drinks, teas, and packaged food items.

restaurant.name: Hummingbird Pub
restaurant.desc: The Hummingbird Pub is a beloved year-round destination in South Galiano, offering lunch, dinner, drinks, and frequent live music events in a quintessential island pub atmosphere. It runs a seasonal 'Pub Bus' that shuttles riders hourly from Montague Provincial Park and the marina, making it accessible to campers and ferry travellers alike. Situated just minutes from the Sturdies Bay ferry terminal, it is a natural gathering spot for cyclists exploring the island.

detail.address: 47 Sturdies Bay Rd, Galiano Island, BC, V0N 1P0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian pizza explicitly listed on menu: crisped dough with mushroom, spinach, tomato, onion, and mozzarella

restaurant.name: Johnny's On Oak
restaurant.desc: A casual fast food restaurant on Oak Street serving burgers, Greek, and pizza. Provides quick meal options for touring cyclists passing through the Kitsilano area.

restaurant.name: Xin Pai Zibo BBQ
restaurant.desc: A Xin Pai Zibo BBQ in Richmond.

restaurant.name: Bistro Sakana
restaurant.desc: A Japanese sushi restaurant in downtown Vancouver offering both indoor and outdoor seating. It provides a sit-down dining option for touring cyclists passing through the city.

restaurant.name: Bhav's Indian Cuisine & Sweet Shop
restaurant.desc: An Indian restaurant with an attached sweet shop offering both dine-in and takeaway service. The dual function as a full-service restaurant and confectionery shop distinguishes it as a distinctive food option in the area.

restaurant.name: Cafe de L'Orangerie
restaurant.desc: Cafe de l'Orangerie is a long-running French-Japanese fusion restaurant that has been operating in the Marpole neighbourhood of Vancouver since 2009. The menu blends European cafe staples — pastas, clam chowder, Salade Niçoise — with Japanese-inflected dishes like karaage, curry rice, hayashi rice, and matcha parfaits, reflecting an unusual and genuinely distinctive culinary identity. A touring cyclist finishing a loop through south Vancouver would find a full sit-down meal and a range of coffees and desserts here.

restaurant.name: El Comal Mexican Food
restaurant.desc: El Comal Burnaby is the factory and restaurant location of a two-location Mexican food group, combining a working tortilla production facility with a sit-down restaurant and an on-site retail store selling handmade tortillas and Mexican provisions. The menu spans tacos on hand-pressed tortillas, birria specialties, burritos, and fresh seafood dishes drawing on traditional Mexican regional recipes. The attached store gives cyclists the option to pick up housemade tortillas and packaged goods to take on the road.

restaurant.name: Sweet Home Cafe
restaurant.desc: A cafe on Hillside Drive in Kamloops. Limited information is available due to website unavailability.

restaurant.name: Dukes Pub
restaurant.desc: Duke's Country Pub is a neighbourhood pub in Chilliwack, BC, part of the Liquor Giant Group. The venue bills itself as a local spot for food, drinks, and good times, and its gallery highlights a history of hosting community car shows. Touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley would find it a potential food-and-drink stop, though the available information is limited.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: Subway Port Place Shopping Centre is a franchise sandwich shop inside Nanaimo's Port Place Shopping Centre, offering the full Subway lineup of footlongs, wraps, and salads. Orders can be placed in-store, online, via the app, through delivery, or curbside pickup. The location is independently owned and operated and serves breakfast in addition to the standard menu.

restaurant.name: Garden City Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Garden City Hot Pot is a Hong Kong-style restaurant in Richmond's Cosmo Plaza, serving traditional dim sum and hot pot dishes rooted in classic Cantonese cuisine. The restaurant bills itself as a 20-year establishment ("20年老字號") and offers a fully bilingual English and Chinese dining experience. Cyclists stopping in Richmond's busy Aberdeen area will find both dine-in and takeout available through an online ordering system and dedicated mobile app.

detail.address: Cosmo Plaza, 8788 McKim Way #1205, Richmond, BC V6X 4E2

restaurant.name: Black Rabbit Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Black Rabbit Coffee House is an independent specialty coffee shop in Kelowna, run by a 17-year industry veteran who named the cafe after her two pet rabbits rescued from a Calgary brewery patio. The shop features direct-trade Rosso Coffee Roasters beans, a full espresso bar, house-baked goods, and a retail shelf stocked with coffee products. Its personal backstory and commitment to small Canadian suppliers give it a distinct character among Kelowna cafes.

detail.address: 652 Cook Road, Kelowna, British Columbia V1W 4T4, Canada

restaurant.name: KFC
restaurant.desc: A KFC fast-food restaurant specializing in fried chicken and related items. Offers takeout service, making it a quick meal option for cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor in Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Bright Jenny Coffee
restaurant.desc: Bright Jenny Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster and café in Kelowna, BC, roasting their own beans and serving a full drink and food menu in a café environment they describe as warm, welcoming, and personality-driven. They offer mobile ordering so cyclists can skip the line and have drinks ready on arrival. In addition to the café, they ship coffee Canada-wide and offer wholesale, subscriptions, and gift cards.

restaurant.name: Yogen Früz
restaurant.desc: Yogen Früz is a long-running international frozen yogurt franchise founded in 1986, with over 1,300 locations in more than 40 countries. This Burnaby outlet on Kingsway offers frozen yogurt, smoothies, matcha drinks, and milk teas with health-focused bases including dairy-free and no-sugar-added options. It is a takeout-focused counter-service stop suited to cyclists needing a quick cold treat along this busy commercial corridor.

restaurant.name: Red Accordion
restaurant.desc: The Red Accordion is a farm-to-table restaurant and pub housed in a converted red house on the corner of Alberni and Cardero Streets, tucked between Vancouver's West End and Coal Harbour. The menu spans brunch through dinner with dishes like lobster eggs benedict and shakshuka alongside an extensive lineup of BC craft beers, local wines, and classic cocktails. The venue also hosts live music and featured artists, giving it a neighbourhood living-room character amid downtown high-rises.

restaurant.name: Little Japan Sushi
restaurant.desc: Little Japan Sushi is a sushi restaurant in Chilliwack located in a small unit. Specific details about amenities and facilities for cyclists cannot be confirmed due to website unavailability.

restaurant.name: The Pizza King
restaurant.desc: The Pizza King is a takeout-and-delivery-only pizza and pasta spot on East Broadway, offering made-to-order pizzas in three sizes, baked pastas, and salads. The operation is streamlined for quick pickup and online ordering with no dine-in option. Cyclists passing through the East Broadway corridor can grab a hot meal but will need to find seating elsewhere.

detail.address: 1464 E Broadway, Vancouver, BC V5N 1V6, Canada

restaurant.name: Gaya Sushi

The restaurant offers online ordering exclusively for to-go pickup, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking to grab a sushi meal on the go. A 10% discount is advertised for online orders.

detail.address: 6908 Island Highway North, Unit 11, Nanaimo, BC V9V 1P6

restaurant.name: The Tipper
restaurant.desc: The Tipper is a cozy, casual neighbourhood restaurant in East Vancouver at Kingsway and Victoria Drive, describing itself as 'Cozy, Casual, Comforting' and doubling as a community gathering space that displays and sells work by local artists and craftspeople. The menu spans an all-day breakfast through to a lunch and dinner selection of sandwiches, burgers, and comfort food, with house-made sides and a rotating selection of specials. Touring cyclists will find a genuinely welcoming full-service meal stop on a major east–west corridor, with takeout available by phone.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page references 'Tipper's cheesy, vegetarian poutine' as a side option and lists multiple egg- and avocado-based breakfast items. GF not mentioned

restaurant.name: Islands Cafe
restaurant.desc: Islands Cafe is a Hawaii-inspired café chain and craft coffee roaster with roots in surf culture — the business began as a surfboard company before pivoting to cafés and eventually setting up its own in-house roastery. The Grandview Corners location (branded 'Mauka') is one of three South Surrey/White Rock outposts, each carrying Hawaiian location names. Cyclists riding the 24 Avenue corridor through Surrey will find a specialty coffee stop with a distinct personality and house-roasted beans.

restaurant.name: Pho Galaxy
restaurant.desc: Pho Galaxy is a family-run Vietnamese restaurant inside Chilliwack's Southgate Shopping Centre, founded by Al Trieu and family on a commitment to scratch-made pho broth — beef bones, charred ginger, and star anise simmered all day with no concentrates or shortcuts. The restaurant grew from a small spot near Chilliwack General Hospital into a larger, community-loved destination that describes itself as 'worth the drive.' Touring cyclists will find a warm sit-down meal or quick takeout order made fresh to order.

restaurant.name: Fuggles Beer Co.
restaurant.desc: Fuggles Beer Co. is Richmond's only brewery, producing award-winning craft beers served fresh in their tasting room. The venue features both indoor and outdoor reservable space, a hot food menu, and a dog-friendly patio — a natural gathering point for cyclists exploring the Richmond dyke trail network. Takeout is also available via DoorDash.

restaurant.name: Boston Pizza
restaurant.desc: Boston Pizza Stadium District is the Vancouver flagship of Canada's largest casual dining chain, a two-level family restaurant and sports bar situated steps from BC Place Stadium at Beatty and Robson. The location was renovated and reopened in 2018 and offers both indoor and outdoor seating. The brand traces its roots to 1964 Edmonton and now operates hundreds of franchise locations across Canada.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Vegan and Glutenwise® options also available'; menu page lists dedicated GlutenWise® and Kids sections

restaurant.name: Frankie G's Pub
restaurant.desc: Frankie G's is a Queensborough neighbourhood gastropub that has been a community gathering place since 1999, housed in an open-concept building with vaulted ceilings, large cedar pillars, hardwood floors, and fireplaces that earned the City of New Westminster's Commercial Building of the Year Award in 1999. The pub serves global-fusion gastro-pub cuisine from resident Chef Dante alongside a selection of local craft beers, wine, and cocktails. Situated on Queensborough island in New Westminster, it draws a diverse crowd and promotes an inclusive 'One World in Our Neighbourhood' ethos.

detail.address: 305 Ewen Avenue, Queensborough, New Westminster, BC V3M 5B4

restaurant.name: Kitami Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kitami Japanese Restaurant is a Japanese cuisine establishment located in Harrison Hot Springs, a small resort town known for its hot springs and proximity to popular cycling routes in the Fraser Valley. Touring cyclists passing through Harrison Hot Springs would find it a sit-down dining option in what is otherwise a small community with limited restaurant choices. The restaurant's Facebook presence uses 'Sushi Kitami,' suggesting a sushi focus.

restaurant.name: Baselines Pub
restaurant.desc: Baselines Pub is a neighbourhood sports pub in Fleetwood, Surrey, open since December 2005 and self-described as the Lower Mainland's best sports bar. It offers screens throughout the space for game-day viewing alongside pub fare, cocktails, and BC Lottery gaming. Touring cyclists would find a full sit-down pub with dine-in and takeout options.

restaurant.name: Copper Otter
restaurant.desc: Copper Otter is a full-service restaurant on Pender Island serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner with chef-inspired menus that range from Eggs Benny and smashburgers to upscale plates like Peachfire Black Cod and Seafood Linguini. The menu has clear vegetarian-friendly options alongside seafood and meat dishes, and the setting offers both indoor and outdoor seating. For cyclists touring the Gulf Islands, it is a rare spot offering all-day dining with online ordering and takeout.

detail.address: 4605 Bedwell Harbour Road, Pender Island, V0M2M1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes falafel, falafel naan wrap, Butternut Squash Ravioli, Braised King Oyster Mushroom, and multiple salad options

restaurant.name: Platform 7
restaurant.desc: Platform 7 Coffee is an atmospheric specialty café with two Vancouver locations — one in Kitsilano and one in East Vancouver — each designed to evoke Victorian London and Belle-Époque Parisian train stations. The café runs a full espresso bar, a brew bar featuring single-origin coffees via V60, Chemex, AeroPress, and siphon, plus cold brew, nitro, and an artisan ice cream bar. A substantial food menu of sandwiches, wraps, baked goods, and protein snacks makes it a practical mid-ride stop with both indoor and outdoor seating.
