restaurant.name: TurF
restaurant.desc: TurF is a three-in-one community space in the Kitsilano neighbourhood combining a fitness studio, a plant-forward bistro and cafe, and a boutique shop, operating since 2017. The bistro serves food and specialty coffee with dine-in, takeout, and delivery options, making it a natural stop on the popular West 4th Avenue cycling corridor. It has been featured by Elle Canada as one of Vancouver's best pilates studios, reflecting its wellness-oriented identity.

restaurant.name: Creston Food Junction
restaurant.desc: Creston Food Junction is a weekday daytime cafe in downtown Creston serving breakfast, brunch, sandwiches, and burgers. It offers takeout, making it a convenient fuel stop for cyclists passing through the Creston Valley on routes connecting the Kootenays. The compact menu and midday closing time suit the rhythm of a touring day.

restaurant.name: Hiroshi Ramen
restaurant.desc: Hiroshi Ramen is a Japanese ramen restaurant on Fraser Highway in Surrey, offering a focused menu of traditional broth styles — Shio, Shoyu, Miso, Mayu, and Sesame — alongside udon and Japanese appetizers like karaage, gyoza, and takoyaki. It operates as the Surrey branch of the Hiroshi Japanese Kitchen brand. Online ordering with both pickup and delivery options is available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes 'Vege Ramen — Vegetarian-friendly broth with multiple veggie toppings.'

restaurant.name: Westward Ho
restaurant.desc: Westward Ho! is a public house and bar & grill situated within the University Golf Club on Vancouver's west side, open to the general public and not restricted to golfers. It features a first-come, first-served outdoor patio and a varied menu spanning pub classics and brunch options. Cyclists exploring the UBC and University Endowment Lands area will find it a full-service dining stop with a relaxed clubhouse atmosphere.

restaurant.name: Enjoy Cafe 1+1
restaurant.desc: Enjoy Cafe 1+1 is a Chinese restaurant situated on Westminster Highway in Richmond, BC. The bilingual name — rendered as 'Enjoy Cafe 1+1餐廳' on Instagram — suggests a cafe-restaurant hybrid catering to the area's large Chinese-speaking community. It sits on a busy arterial road in Richmond, a city well served by cycling infrastructure.

restaurant.name: Craffles
restaurant.desc: Craffles is a locally owned brunch restaurant nestled in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, serving gourmet crepes, waffles, French toast, eggs benedict, omelettes, and milkshakes all day long. It operates as a full-service, first-come-first-served spot with both indoor and outdoor seating in a warm, welcoming space. The brand has franchise ambitions and positions itself as a daily neighbourhood staple for breakfast through afternoon.

restaurant.name: Toku Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Toku Japanese Restaurant is a Japanese dining destination inside Lansdowne Centre in Richmond, specializing in sushi rolls, sashimi, chirashi, and desserts made with high-quality seafood and house secret sauces. The restaurant offers ample seating suited for large gatherings and includes a kids' area, making it a welcoming sit-down stop for groups. It is currently celebrating its 10th anniversary and offers online pick-up ordering.

detail.address: Lansdowne Centre, 5300 Number 3 Rd #221, Richmond, BC V6X 2X9

restaurant.name: Noodlebox
restaurant.desc: Noodlebox is a Canadian fast-casual franchise serving Asian-inspired wok-fired noodle and rice bowls, with a wide range of sauces from Pad Thai to Cambodian Jungle Curry. The New Westminster location is one of many BC outlets, offering dine-in and online ordering. Touring cyclists will appreciate the broad dietary accommodation, with dishes readily adaptable to vegan and gluten-friendly requirements.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Can be made VEGAN — Please ask when ordering' and 'Can be made GLUTEN-FRIENDLY — Please ask when ordering'; OSM confirms

restaurant.name: Slo Coffee
restaurant.desc: Slo Coffee is a neighbourhood café anchored in Vancouver's Fraserhood community, built around the philosophy of slowing down and savouring the moment over specialty coffee. The menu includes food items such as bacon sandos, vegan spreads, toasts, and overnight oats alongside pour-over and espresso drinks. A second downtown location at Pacific Centre opened in December 2025, expanding the brand's footprint in the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website staff Q&A references 'delicious vegan spreads, toasts and overnight oats' available on the menu, made by team member Evelina's company Pippsi

restaurant.name: Saffron Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: A family-run Indian restaurant opened in 2004 by Kewal and Surinder Sandhu, who brought their love of authentic Indian cooking from their homeland to Burnaby's Kingsway corridor. Voted Burnaby's best Indian restaurant for over 20 years, it serves a broad menu of tandoor dishes, curries, seafood, and vegetarian fare alongside a full bar. The restaurant is wheelchair accessible and features a patio along a busy commercial strip.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page labels items 'GF - Gluten Friendly' and 'VO - Vegan Option available upon request'

restaurant.name: Flourish BeauTea
restaurant.desc: Flourish BeauTea is a Victoria-based bakery specializing in handcrafted custom cakes and cupcakes made to order with fresh, local ingredients, offered in flavours ranging from matcha to purple yam to passionfruit. The business operates from both a Victoria Downtown location on Fort Street and a Langford location, and also runs hands-on cake workshops. For a touring cyclist, it is a distinctive local stop for a sweet treat or a unique edible souvenir.

restaurant.name: The Seoulful
restaurant.desc: The Seoulful is a Korean cafe and bakery in Richmond's Number 3 Road corridor, known for Korean-style salted butter breads, kimbap rolls, tteokbokki, and non-coffee lattes. The menu leans heavily on Seoul street-food staples — from bulgogi kimbap to creamy rose tteokbokki — alongside a creative lineup of matcha and fruit lattes. Online ordering for pickup is available, and recent customer reviews highlight the quality of the baked goods as a standout draw.

detail.address: 4940 Number 3 Rd Unit 125, Richmond, BC V6X3A5

restaurant.name: Sushi Ryu
restaurant.desc: Sushi Ryu is a fusion Japanese restaurant in north Nanaimo that has been serving the neighbourhood since 2014. The menu spans sushi rolls, sashimi, donburi, and bento sets, with dedicated vegetarian and gluten-free options built into the menu rather than treated as afterthoughts. Both dine-in and takeout are available, supported by an online ordering system.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Veggie Bento (Veggie Roll & Tofu Teriyaki) and a dedicated Gluten Free Bento with gluten-free teriyaki sauce. OSM confirms

restaurant.name: Geng Shi Ji

restaurant.name: Pokey Okey Shokudo
restaurant.desc: Pokey Okey is a local Vancouver poke bowl chain founded in 2018, now with three locations across the metro area. The Kingsway outpost serves Hawaiian-style poke bowls built from fresh fish and locally sourced vegetables, with signature sauces and a range of customizable toppings. It sits on a major arterial cycling corridor in East Vancouver, making it a convenient stop for riders passing through the area.

restaurant.name: The Deluxe Chinese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Deluxe Chinese Restaurant is the first North American location of the Deluxe Restaurant Group, which operates a number of restaurants in China. The restaurant occupies approximately 600 square metres and offers Cantonese dim sum, Sichuan dishes, and a Japanese sashimi bar — an unusual fusion for a Richmond dim sum house. Five private VIP rooms seating 16–40 guests make it a destination for group dining.

restaurant.name: Hao's Lamb Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Hao's Lamb Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant on Richmond's busy Number 3 Road corridor specializing in roasted whole lamb, lamb series dishes, and sheep offal, alongside seafood and classic hot dishes. It is part of the Hao's restaurant group, which also operates Royal Beef and Hao's Tapas Kitchen in Richmond. Online ordering is available through the group's shared platform.

restaurant.name: Ginger Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Ginger Indian Cuisine is an authentic Indian restaurant in Richmond serving a wide-ranging menu that draws from multiple regional traditions, including tandoori specialties, slow-cooked biryanis, and rich curries. The restaurant is Halal certified by HIC Canada and has been recognized by Restaurantji as one of Richmond's best. Cyclists will find a full dine-in experience alongside takeout and delivery, with vegetarian and celiac-friendly items clearly identified on the menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes (Paneer Pakora, Paneer Handi, Channa Bhatura, vegetable Biryani). Website also has a dedicated celiac/gluten-free section describing clear menu labeling and cross-contamination prevention protocols

restaurant.name: Hanlin Tea House
restaurant.desc: Hanlin Tea House specializes in tea and patisseries, located in Richmond with indoor seating available. It serves as a casual refreshment stop for touring cyclists seeking tea and pastry items.

restaurant.name: The Cockpit
restaurant.desc: The Cockpit is a cafe located within the Harbour Air seaplane terminal in downtown Vancouver, one of the world's largest all-seaplane airline hubs serving destinations across BC and the Pacific Northwest. Situated at basement level (level -1) inside the terminal building, it serves travellers and visitors passing through the waterfront facility. Touring cyclists in the Coal Harbour area may find it a convenient stop, though access requires locking bikes outside and entering the terminal.

restaurant.name: Howe Sound Brew Pub
restaurant.desc: Howe Sound Inn & Brewing is Squamish's original craft brewery, operating since 1996 in the heart of Sea to Sky Country at the gateway to world-class mountain biking, climbing, and road cycling terrain. The flagship Squamish location combines a full-service brewpub and kitchen with an attached inn and outdoor patio, serving award-winning craft beers — the brewery was named Canadian Brewery of the Year in 2022 — alongside stone-fired pizzas and hearty pub fare. It is a natural refueling and overnight stop for cyclists on the Sea to Sky corridor between Vancouver and Whistler.

restaurant.name: Las Margaritas

restaurant.name: Biercraft
restaurant.desc: BierCraft UniverCity is a craft beer restaurant and pub located in the SFU UniverCity neighbourhood on Burnaby Mountain, offering 26 Belgian and craft beers on draught alongside a full food menu covering lunch, dinner, brunch, and kids options. It occupies a community-hub role at the top of one of the Lower Mainland's more demanding cycling climbs, making it a natural endpoint or mid-tour refuelling stop. The venue also screens major sporting events and runs a beer loyalty programme.

detail.address: 8902 University High St, Burnaby, BC V5A 4X6

restaurant.name: A Bread Affair
restaurant.desc: A Bread Affair is BC's first certified organic artisan bakery, founded in 2005 and located beside the Granville Island Public Market in Vancouver. The bakery uses slow fermentation and small-batch techniques with locally sourced organic BC ingredients to produce sourdough loaves, croissants, artisan sandwiches, and seasonal pastries. A second production bakery in Langley supplies organic bread to retailers across the Lower Mainland.

restaurant.name: Dublin Crossing
restaurant.desc: Dublin Crossing is an authentic Irish pub in Surrey serving a full menu of food alongside Irish and local craft draught beers. The venue features live music several nights a week and hosts seasonal events including St. Patrick's Day and Oktoberfest celebrations. Dine-in, patio seating, and take-out are all available.

restaurant.name: Wah Wing Szechuan Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A Szechuan restaurant in North Vancouver offering Chinese cuisine as a dining stop for cyclists. Listed as wheelchair accessible.

restaurant.name: Baja Racing Sports Bar
restaurant.desc: A Mexican-cuisine restaurant and sports bar located on Cambie Street in Vancouver. Limited information available due to website access failure.

restaurant.name: Caspian Castle Food
restaurant.desc: Caspian Castle Food is a restaurant located on Hornby Street in Vancouver's downtown core, offering vegetarian dining options. As a sit-down restaurant with indoor seating, it provides a sheltered place for cycling tourists to rest and refuel in the city.

restaurant.name: The Modern Bakeshop & Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Modern Bakeshop & Cafe is a heritage artisan bakery and coffee shop in the heart of Revelstoke, in operation since 1903. It is known for freshly baked goods made with organic ingredients — standout items highlighted by reviewers include Aussie meat pies, sticky cinnamon buns, and housemade chai lattes — alongside expertly brewed espresso drinks. The space offers a cozy indoor atmosphere and outdoor seating, drawing both local regulars and travelers passing through.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About-us page states: 'Guests can enjoy gluten-free dining, vegetarian specials, and vegan fine dining options.' Reviewer Lisa Goodwin also notes 'Gluten free treats that are moist and flavour full!'

restaurant.name: The Greek Corner
restaurant.desc: The Greek Corner is a locally owned, award-winning Greek restaurant in Surrey serving traditional dishes such as souvlaki, moussaka, spanakopita, and slow-roasted lamb. The restaurant offers licensed liquor service with Greek wines and cocktails alongside a full dine-in experience in a Mediterranean-inspired atmosphere. Their catering arm handles events from small gatherings up to 700 guests, reflecting an established presence in the community.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Gluten-free and vegetarian-friendly options available' and catering menu lists halal, vegetarian, gluten-free, and vegan options

restaurant.name: Mr. Bro
restaurant.desc: Mr. Bro is a Korean bistro and izakaya situated in a commercial plaza on Alexandra Road in Richmond's busy dining corridor. The late-night izakaya format means it stays open well past midnight most evenings, making it a useful stop for cyclists finishing a long day on the road. Online ordering and takeout are available.

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Freshslice Pizza is a BC-based pizza chain offering pizza by the slice and whole pies with vegetarian options. This New Westminster location sits on the second floor of a building on Carnarvon Street, providing a quick and affordable meal stop for cyclists moving through the downtown core.

restaurant.name: Greek Fellas Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Greek Fellas Restaurant is a family-owned Greek dining destination in Delta, BC, originally founded in 2002 and revived under the same family in 2022. Situated on River Road near the Fraser River—a corridor frequented by touring cyclists—it serves traditional dishes such as Chicken Souvlaki and Roast Lamb made from family recipes and fresh local produce. The restaurant also offers catering services, making it a potential stop for larger cycling groups.

restaurant.name: Boardwalk Fries Burgers Shakes
restaurant.desc: Boardwalk Fries Burgers Shakes is a Canadian fast-casual chain founded in 1981, built around made-to-order burgers, signature boardwalk-style fries, and creamy milkshakes made with premium Canadian dairy. The Abbotsford location is one of 27+ across Canada, offering cyclists a quick and filling stop with a casual beachside diner atmosphere. The menu extends beyond the classic burger lineup to include veggie burgers, poutine, sweet potato fries, and chicken dishes.

detail.address: 32650 South Fraser Way Unit P700, Abbotsford, BC V2T 4W2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website (franchise and our-story pages) explicitly lists veggie burgers as a menu item

restaurant.name: Prado Cafe
restaurant.desc: Prado Cafe is a Vancouver specialty coffee institution founded by Sammy Piccolo, a four-time Canadian Barista Champion who has represented Canada at the World Barista Championships. The Fraser Street location is one of eight cafes across Vancouver, Burnaby, and Surrey, each built around craft espresso and a genuine neighbourhood-first ethos. Cyclists passing through the Fraser Street corridor will find a well-regarded independent-style coffee destination with in-store pickup available.

restaurant.name: Murasaki
restaurant.desc: Murasaki is a neighbourhood Japanese kitchen that has anchored Port Moody's Newport Village since 2012, earning the Tri-Cities Best Sushi award three times over its 14-year run. Owned by Chuck and Gracia, it serves sushi, sashimi, ramen, donburi, and traditional grilled specialties in a cozy, family-oriented space with booth and table seating and outdoor seating. It is a well-loved community fixture with catering services and a loyalty stamp program.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states: 'Yes, we have dishes that are catered to vegetarian and vegan diets. To customers who seek gluten-free option, we provide gluten-free soy sauce, and recommend menu dishes that lack deep-fried... Many of our dishes cater to GF dietary needs. Our servers can assist you in choosing the right dishes.'

restaurant.name: Savorhill
restaurant.desc: Savorhill is a bakery in Richmond offering baked goods and prepared foods. It maintains a mobile-friendly ordering system for customer convenience. The business serves as a potential food stop for touring cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: Skaha Pizza
restaurant.desc: Skaha Pizza is a stone-baked, artisan thin-crust pizza spot located a few blocks from Skaha Lake in Penticton's Yorkton Plaza. Owner Kyra King, a baker by trade who relocated from Winnipeg, took over this well-loved local restaurant and brings careful attention to dough and fresh ingredients. Cyclists passing through the Skaha Lake corridor will find a broad menu of classic and specialty pizzas, including dedicated vegetarian and vegan options.

detail.address: 3450 Skaha Lake Rd, Yorkton Plaza, Penticton, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Four dedicated vegetarian pizzas listed (Spinach & Feta, More Than Margherita, All Greek To Me, All Veggies Balsamic); Skaha Sweet Heat explicitly offers a vegan version with plant-based cheese at no extra charge. No gluten-free option mentioned

restaurant.name: Jam Cafe
restaurant.desc: Jam Cafe is a beloved West Coast breakfast and brunch chain that opened its Vancouver Beatty Street location in the Crosstown neighbourhood in 2016. The cozy, vintage-inspired space serves Southern-inspired comfort food made with locally sourced ingredients, with standout dishes including Fried Chicken French Toast, fluffy three-stack pancakes, and the Charlie Bowl. Sugar-cured bacon Caesars, original mimosas, and locally brewed artisanal coffees round out a menu well-suited to fuelling a day on the bike.

restaurant.name: Honeybee Centre
restaurant.desc: Honeybee Centre is Western Canada's top commercial honey farm, operating a publicly accessible Country Store in Surrey where visitors can browse and purchase locally produced specialty honeys, bee pollen, propolis, royal jelly, and beeswax candles. Cyclists can stop in to shop and watch honeybees at work in the back of the store. The centre also runs educational tours, workshops, and field trips, making it a genuinely distinctive stop on any Lower Mainland cycling route.

restaurant.name: FusionCore
restaurant.desc: FusionCore is a Japanese fast-food eatery located on 6th Street in Burnaby. It sits in an urban neighbourhood and could serve as a quick refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the area. No further detail about the menu, seating, or facilities is available from the website.

restaurant.name: Liberty Bakery
restaurant.desc: Liberty Bakery is a community-driven bakery and cafe on Vancouver's Main Street, celebrated for its artisan pastries — croissants, pain au suisse, sourdough sandwiches — and a full specialty coffee program. The team is dedicated to sourcing local, high-quality ingredients and serves a wide range of baked goods alongside savoury mains including seasonal soups, flatbreads, and charcuterie-style sandwiches. It sits on one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors, making it a natural food stop for riders exploring the city.

restaurant.name: Sip of Life
restaurant.desc: Sip of Life is a family-owned coffee house on West Broadway in Vancouver, offering a full range of espresso drinks, brewed coffee, frappes, smoothies, and a tea bar alongside non-coffee options. The café emphasizes sustainability through locally-sourced organic ingredients and eco-friendly practices, with a plant-adorned interior intended as a community gathering spot. It sits on a busy commercial corridor well-travelled by cyclists crossing the city.

restaurant.name: Baik Mi Korean Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Baik Mi is a Korean restaurant in Gibsons on British Columbia's Sunshine Coast, serving traditional Korean cuisine with both dine-in and online ordering options. Located at 900 Sunnycrest Road, it is a local independent spot catering to the Gibsons community and visitors alike. Touring cyclists rolling off the ferry or exploring the Sunshine Coast Highway will find it a convenient stop for a hot Korean meal.

restaurant.name: Sushi Man
restaurant.desc: Sushi Man is a well-established Japanese restaurant on Marine Drive in North Vancouver, celebrated by long-time regulars for the freshness and simplicity of its sushi — no heavy sauces masking the fish. The menu spans classic nigiri and sashimi to inventive specialty rolls, with vegetarian, vegan, and teriyaki options rounding out the selection. A novelty sushi delivery robot adds a modern, playful touch to the otherwise casual, family-friendly dining room.

detail.address: 1307 Marine Drive, District of North Vancouver

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website amenities section lists 'Vegan options' and 'Vegetarian options'; menu description also notes a range of veggie rolls

restaurant.name: Wild Poppy Market
restaurant.desc: Wild Poppy Market is a dedicated 100% gluten-free bakery and café in the heart of historical downtown Ladysmith on Vancouver Island, founded by Chef Kate Cram. It offers house-made grab-and-go savoury meals, fresh daily baked goods, and a retail section stocking gluten-free staples sourced from local producers including Cowichan Milk Company and Farmer Ben's Eggs. Touring cyclists with gluten intolerance will find an unusually broad range of safe, ready-to-eat options alongside packaged goods they can carry onward.

restaurant.name: Bike Shop Cafe and Catering
restaurant.desc: Founded in 1998 and housed in a century-old historic warehouse in Kelowna's cultural district, Bike Shop Cafe and Catering takes its name from the building's former life as a bicycle shop — regulars have donated their old bikes to hang on the walls, with some returning specifically to dine beneath their old ride. The fully licensed, independently owned cafe has won multiple Peoples Choice awards including Best Soup, Best Sandwich, Best Specialty Coffee, and Best Use of Local Ingredients, offering an ever-changing menu of locally sourced soul food, specialty organic beverages, craft beer, and a catering service guided by the same philosophy.

restaurant.name: NeNe Chicken
restaurant.desc: NeNe Chicken is a Korean fried chicken restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, part of a small Canadian chain with locations across BC and Ontario. The restaurant offers indoor seating and online ordering through its own app and website. Touring cyclists passing through the West End will find it a convenient stop for a hearty Korean fried chicken meal in a busy urban neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Pine House Bread & Cake Shop
restaurant.desc: Pine House Bread & Cake Shop is a bakery in Richmond's busy Number 3 Road commercial corridor, trading under the Chinese name 松屋麵飽西餅, which suggests a focus on Asian-style breads and Western pastries. It sits in a strip-mall or mixed-use retail complex and would be a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through Richmond's urban core for fresh baked goods.

restaurant.name: Papa's Gourmet Pizza
restaurant.desc: Papa's Gourmet Pizza is a fast-food pizza spot on Main Street in Vancouver, billing itself on 'Taste the Gourmet Difference' — a nod to quality ingredients above the typical fast-food tier. Sitting on a well-traveled urban cycling corridor, it could make a convenient fuel stop for cyclists riding the Main Street route. Very little operational detail is publicly available, so on-the-ground verification is warranted.

restaurant.name: Outbound Station
restaurant.desc: Outbound Station is a quick-dine craft burger shop and café on the Sea-to-Sky Highway in Britannia Beach, positioned squarely on one of BC's most popular cycling corridors between Vancouver and Squamish. The kitchen serves handcrafted burgers alongside specialty espresso drinks, hot chocolate, and matcha lattes, with a stated mission to 'fuel your adventure' for travellers heading in or returning from the mountains. A rewards program and online ordering round out a setup clearly aimed at road and outdoor users looking for a quality, efficient stop.

restaurant.name: Sula Indian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Sula Indian Restaurant on Main Street is a well-established Vancouver restaurant serving heritage Indian cuisine drawing from North India, coastal Mangalore, and Delhi street food, with an award-winning Indian cocktail program curated by mixologist Jeff Savage. The Main Street location has been operating since 2010 and earned Gold for Best Indian Restaurant at the 2025 Georgia Straight Golden Plates Awards. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down dining experience in the Riley Park neighbourhood, with takeout and delivery also available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'dedicated vegetarian and vegan Indian section' with dairy-free curries, vegan naan (coconut cream), halal-friendly dishes, and accommodation for celiac guests on request

restaurant.name: Ostera Coastal Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Osetra Coastal Cuisine is a contemporary seafood restaurant in downtown Vancouver, known for precision sourcing and an elevated atmosphere. The menu spans caviar service, Dungeness crab cake, house-cured King Salmon, and a weekend brunch, all presented under the banner of 'The Key Collection.' Indoor and outdoor seating are available and the venue is wheelchair accessible.

restaurant.name: Guangzhou Garden
restaurant.desc: Guangzhou Garden is an authentic Chinese restaurant in Duncan, BC, serving traditional dishes including dim sum, dumplings, and wonton soup prepared without MSG. The dining room seats up to 125 people, making it a practical stop for cycling clubs or larger tour groups passing through the Cowichan Valley. A weekly lunch and dinner buffet runs Tuesday through Sunday alongside regular dine-in, takeout, and delivery options.

restaurant.name: Brewing August
restaurant.desc: Brewing August bills itself as the only brewery in Kitsilano, operating a relaxed taproom with 10 house taps alongside mead, cocktails, and non-alcoholic options. Burgers are served from an on-site vendor (Between2Buns), and the upstairs section can be booked for private events up to 50 guests. A weekly run club that sets off from the back of the brewery makes this a natural stop for active visitors exploring the Kitsilano neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Beyond Coffee
restaurant.desc: Beyond Coffee is a cafe in central Vancouver with non-smoking indoor seating and vegetarian options available. The location is wheelchair accessible and provides Wi-Fi connectivity, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists in this central neighborhood.

restaurant.name: The Kop Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: The Kop Coffee Roasters is an independent specialty roastery and café founded in 2020 on Annacis Island in Delta, BC, run by a certified Q grader with over a decade of green-bean sourcing experience across Africa. Beyond its single-origin and blended roasts, the shop sells a dedicated line of camping coffee — single-serve bags designed for outdoor use — making it a natural fit for cycle-tourers who want quality coffee on and off the bike. The café sits in an industrial pocket of Annacis Island, a point of interest in itself given the island's unique geography.

detail.address: Unit 1B, 1080 Cliveden Avenue, Delta, BC V3M 6G6

restaurant.name: La Mezcaleria
restaurant.desc: Proudly Canada's first Mezcaleria since 2013, La Mezcaleria is a lively Mexican cantina on Commercial Drive serving authentic regional cuisine made with local, organic ingredients and free-range meats. The restaurant is particularly known for its extensive agave spirits program — flights of tequila and mezcal are a specialty alongside expertly crafted cocktails. Weekend brunch, catering, and full buy-outs round out an offering that goes well beyond a typical neighbourhood restaurant.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items across brunch and dinner menus are labelled GF (gluten-free), VG (vegetarian), V (vegan), and DF (dairy-free), e.g. Guacamole is marked GF, NF, VG, V, DF

restaurant.name: Open Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Open Kitchen is a large, multi-station residence dining hall inside UBC's Orchard Commons, open to the public and not just students. It offers five concurrent food stations spanning flatbreads and baked pasta, stir-fry, Asian noodle dishes, grill favourites, and fresh sandwiches, drawing on Vancouver's diverse culinary scene. More than 60% of ingredients are sourced locally from UBC Farm and other BC producers, with certified halal beef, Ocean Wise seafood, and a dedicated range of vegan and vegetarian options.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast food restaurant located inside or adjacent to a Walmart on Hillside Drive in Kamloops, offering burgers, chicken, wraps, McCafé beverages, and snacks. Situated in a large retail parking area, it serves as a convenient urban food stop for cyclists passing through the Kamloops corridor. Ordering is available via the McDonald's app with contactless payment, as well as curbside pickup and delivery.

restaurant.name: COBS Bread
restaurant.desc: COBS Bread at Lonsdale Quay Market is a franchise bakery located inside the covered Lonsdale Quay Market, part of the Bakers Delight family with over 190 Canadian locations. All products — including loaves, buns and rolls, bagels, scones, cruffins, croissants, and savoury baked items — are made from scratch on-site daily. Leftover baked goods are donated to local charities at end of day.

detail.address: 123 Carrie Cates Court, North Vancouver, V7M 3K7

restaurant.name: Yu Ki BBQ Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Yu Ki BBQ Kitchen is a restaurant located in a multi-unit commercial building on East 49th Avenue in Vancouver. The name suggests a BBQ-focused menu. Touring cyclists riding through Vancouver's eastern neighbourhoods would find it a potential meal stop.

restaurant.name: 19 Okanagan Grill + Bar
restaurant.desc: 19 Okanagan Grill + Bar is an owner-operated steakhouse and full-service bar in West Kelowna, built around a philosophy of sourcing from local Okanagan farmers, winemakers, and producers. The menu spans steaks, burgers, salads, and appetizers, with private event space and an active local dining community. The same operator runs a second location, 19 Bistro @ Fitz, indicating an established presence in the region.

restaurant.name: Mentora Ramen
restaurant.desc: Mentora Ramen is an authentic Japanese tonkotsu ramen restaurant on Store Street in downtown Victoria, serving a menu of slow-simmered pork bone broths from classic Tonkotsu to specialty dishes like Tsukemen and Lobster Ramen. The restaurant's 'Slurp Like a Tiger' philosophy reflects a commitment to bold, immersive flavours built on broths simmered for hours with pork bones, chicken, and aromatics. Its downtown location on Store Street makes it a convenient stop for cyclists riding through the Inner Harbour area.

restaurant.name: Sushi Island
restaurant.desc: Sushi Island is an authentic Japanese restaurant in Victoria's Hillside neighbourhood, open since 2013 and built on a reputation for freshness through high turnover. The menu spans traditional sushi, sashimi, nigiri, hot pots, donburi, and Korean-influenced dishes. The casual modern interior suits a quick post-ride lunch as easily as a longer sit-down dinner.

restaurant.name: Ossie's Deli & Meats
restaurant.desc: A family-run deli in Tsawwassen operating since 1982, Ossie's is known for fresh-made sandwiches, European deli meats, and German-inspired specialties like schnitzel and frikadella prepared in front of customers. The menu spans named burgers, soups, and a rotating specials board, earning strong ratings on Google (4.7), TripAdvisor (4.5), and Zomato (4.2). It has a loyal local following and a nostalgic 1950s-style atmosphere with a 'customer picture wall.'

The space regularly hosts cultural events such as live Arabic music nights, making it a memorable stop for touring cyclists seeking an immersive meal experience.

restaurant.name: Giovane Caffè

The café has both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a pleasant stop for cyclists passing through the downtown core.

restaurant.name: Chocho Hot Pot

restaurant.name: New Town Bakery & Restaurant
restaurant.desc: New Town Bakery & Restaurant is a family-run institution in Vancouver's historic Chinatown, serving Chinese and Filipino baked goods and pastries since 1980. The bakery earned a CNN Travel 'must-visit restaurant' designation and multiple Chinese Restaurant Critics' Choice awards for its pastries. Signature items include award-winning Apple Tarts and World Famous Steamed Buns (Siopao — BBQ Pork Asado and Chicken Deluxe Bola Bola), made fresh daily.

Ranked No. 59 on Canada's 100 Best Restaurants 2026 and awarded Gold for Best Fine Dining at the Vancouver Magazine Restaurant Awards, it stands among the city's most decorated culinary destinations. Guests can dine in a vintage-style lounge, at a marble-top bar, in a private dining room, or on an expansive wrap-around patio.

Weekend buffets rotate daily based on seasonal ingredients and chef's specials, offering cyclists a substantial and varied meal stop.

For a touring cyclist passing through Chilliwack, it represents a quick, filling hot-food stop with multiple protein and vegetarian options.

restaurant.name: Tall Tree Bakery

The bakery produces high-quality breads and pastries baked fresh each morning from clean-label ingredients, and was recognized with the Best Small Business Service Excellence Award by the Squamish Chamber of Commerce in 2018. Touring cyclists will find a wide selection of freshly baked artisan breads, pastries, baguette sandwiches, grilled paninis, and locally-roasted coffee.

restaurant.name: Jungle Room

restaurant.name: Little Saigon

It is the Mission location of a two-restaurant Fraser Valley operation, housed in a strip-mall unit with free parking. Cyclists passing through Mission will find it a convenient stop for a filling, from-scratch Vietnamese meal.

restaurant.name: Lost in the 50's Burgers
restaurant.desc: A 1950s-themed classic American diner in Burnaby serving fresh-never-frozen Alberta beef burgers, all-beef hotdogs, hand-cut fries, and creamy milkshakes. The kitchen emphasizes no preservatives, additives, or fillers, working from time-honored diner recipes. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a viable stop for a sit-down meal mid-ride.

The intimate dining room features an open kitchen, full-service bar, heated covered atrium, and a walk-in wine cellar repurposed from an original bank vault. Since opening in 2021, Okini has been nominated for Best West Coast by Vancouver Magazine and twice recognised as Best Kerrisdale Restaurant by Georgia Straight's Golden Plates Awards.

restaurant.name: The Chopped Leaf

Touring cyclists heading through the Peace River region would find it a convenient stop for a fresh, customizable meal.

restaurant.name: Kami Sushi

restaurant.name: Finest At Sea

Touring cyclists can grab freshly cooked fish and chips from the food truck or pick up smoked salmon, candied sablefish, and live spot prawns from the market.

restaurant.name: Dairy Queen

restaurant.name: SWEET7

restaurant.name: Golestan Bakery

Cyclists passing through can stop in for baked goods, custom cakes, or ice cream and faloodeh — a refreshing Persian frozen treat.

restaurant.name: In and Out Donair

restaurant.name: Nikkei Ramen-Ya
restaurant.desc: Nikkei Ramen-ya is a family-owned scratch ramen restaurant in Courtenay, founded by third-generation Japanese Canadian Greg Masuda, who hand-makes all noodles and broths from whole, locally sourced ingredients with no shortcuts. The restaurant holds the distinction of being BC's only Certified Living Wage Restaurant and rotates over forty ramen flavours weekly. It also produces a line of frozen ramen kits sold in 100+ BC grocery stores, and features Vancouver Island's largest selection of Japanese beers alongside a seasonal patio.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website confirms Miso Yasai as 'hearty, plant-based miso ramen' and notes 'Vegan available' on multiple menu items, as well as a Vegan Shoyu frozen kit

restaurant.name: Kuan Zhai Road Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kuan Zhai Road Restaurant is a Chinese takeout spot on Kingsway in Vancouver operating as a pickup-only establishment with online ordering. It offers a wide range of flavours and is open daily. Cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor can grab a meal without a long dine-in wait.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Pickup Only' and prominently features 'Order Online Now'

restaurant.name: Nektar's Pizza and Greek food
restaurant.desc: Nektar's is a neighbourhood pizza and Greek food restaurant in the Dollarton Shopping Centre on North Vancouver's eastern waterfront edge. The menu spans hand-made pizzas with 20 fresh-cut toppings alongside a full slate of Greek specialties—souvlaki, spanakopita, slow-roasted lamb shoulder, and housemade pasta sauces. Both dine-in and pickup are available, with delivery offered within a 3 km radius.

detail.address: 397 N. Dollarton Hwy, North Vancouver, BC V7G-1M9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated 'Nektar's Vegetarian Pizza' (mushrooms, onions, green peppers, tomatoes, olives, pineapple) listed on menu; Spanakopita Dinner also available. No vegan or GF options mentioned

restaurant.name: Woody's Pub
restaurant.desc: Woody's Pub is a cozy, long-established neighborhood pub on Highway 97 in Lake Country (Winfield), part of the Woodsman Group's family of Okanagan pubs. Known for hearty pub classics like beef dip, steak dinners, and Sunday roast, it draws a loyal local following and welcomes visitors with a warm, laid-back atmosphere. The pub regularly hosts live music nights and comedy events, making it a lively stop along the Okanagan corridor.

restaurant.name: Hiro Japan Sushi Xpress
restaurant.desc: Hiro Sushi is mapped in OSM as a fast-food sushi outlet in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, but the linked website belongs to 'Hiro Japan Xpress,' a small BC sushi chain operating express-style Japanese food counters. The chain's only listed Vancouver location is inside Bentall Centre at 1055 Dunsmuir Street — a different address, phone number, and brand name than the OSM node — raising serious doubts about whether this record corresponds to an active, correctly attributed business.

restaurant.name: Petrichor French Farmhouse Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Petrichor is a French farmhouse-style restaurant in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, founded by Luc-André Duval, who hails from Montpellier in southern France and brings his background in high-end French and international hospitality to the menu. The kitchen focuses on elevated French classics — escargots, duck breast, boeuf bourguignon — made in-house with locally sourced ingredients wherever possible. The space is designed to evoke a southern French farmhouse and emphasises social dining, with cocktails, local beers, and wines alongside the food.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ Q3: 'Yes, we offer a variety of vegetarian and vegan dishes on our menu.' FAQ Q8: 'Yes, we have gluten-free options.'

restaurant.name: Buffalo Trails Coffee Shop
restaurant.desc: Buffalo Trails Coffee House is a family-owned, community-rooted coffee house in Creston that has been part of the Kootenay community since 2008. The business operates its own small-batch artisan roastery and sources ingredients hyper-locally — organic dairy from Kootenay Meadows, meats from Famous Fritz, and seasonal produce from valley fruit stands. The patio hosts a seasonal ice cream parlour called Happy Trails, offering Foothills ice cream, milkshakes, and fresh-squeezed lemonade.

restaurant.name: Lavash Seaside Grill
restaurant.desc: Lavash Seaside Grill is a family-owned restaurant nestled in historic Steveston Village on the Richmond waterfront, blending West Coast staples like fish and chips with house Persian dishes drawn from generational family recipes. The menu leans on fresh, locally sourced ingredients, and the seaside setting offers a relaxed atmosphere well-suited to a mid-ride meal. Live music runs every Saturday, and the kitchen accommodates group bookings, making it a social stop as well as a practical one.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states menu offers 'vegetarian options' alongside fish, lamb, and other dishes; no vegan or GF claim found

restaurant.name: Sushi Mori
restaurant.desc: Sushi Mori is a sushi restaurant located on Capilano Road in North Vancouver, listed in OSM as offering takeout service. The restaurant sits in a neighbourhood convenient to cyclists exploring the North Shore.

restaurant.name: Hủ Tiếu Hồng Phát
restaurant.desc: Hủ Tiếu Hồng Phát is a family-run Vietnamese restaurant on Victoria Drive in Vancouver, continuing a tradition founded in 1975 by Chef Đặng Thị Nguyệt, who began with a humble Phnom Penh-style rice noodle stall in Saigon. The menu spans signature noodle soups, hearty stews, and Vietnamese comfort food rooted in a blend of Khmer, Chinese, and Vietnamese culinary traditions. The Vancouver location offers full sit-down dining and online ordering, making it a substantial meal stop for cyclists riding the Victoria Drive corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Plant-Based Dishes' section; multiple individual items (e.g., Pork & Shrimp Spring Rolls, Fried Squid Cakes) are labeled 'gluten free' in the menu listing

restaurant.name: Basil Pasta Bar
restaurant.desc: Basil Pasta Bar, established in 2010, is Vancouver's first build-your-own pasta restaurant and a long-running fixture on Davie Street in the West End. Diners choose their own combination of pasta, sauce, and toppings in a casual indoor setting. Takeout and daily delivery are available, making it a practical carb-loading stop for cyclists passing through downtown Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Blenz Coffee
restaurant.desc: Blenz Coffee is a BC-based coffee chain with a downtown Victoria location at 1001 Douglas Street, a block from the Inner Harbour. The cafe offers espresso drinks, specialty lattes, whole-leaf teas, and a food menu spanning pastries, sandwiches, wraps, and more. Cyclists moving through the city core will find it a convenient stop for hot or cold drinks and a quick meal.

detail.address: G1 – 1001 Douglas Street, Victoria, BC V8W 2C5

restaurant.name: R Ki Coffee Lab
restaurant.desc: R Ki Coffee Lab is a specialty coffee roastery and café in Richmond, BC that sources beans directly from origin farmers and international auctions, performing rigorous batch-level quality control including Agtron colour, moisture, and blind cupping on its 3.2kg semi-air drum roaster. The lab has earned international recognition, placing in worldwide mystery-coffee leaderboards and participating in events such as the 2026 Shanghai Hotelex and Panama Highlands Treasures. They also operate an adjacent dessert studio and host ticketed coffee-cupping and sensory sessions.

restaurant.name: Whisk Matcha Cafe
restaurant.desc: Whisk Matcha Cafe is a female-owned premium matcha cafe and retail space in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, sourcing artisanal Japanese matcha directly from small independent farms in Uji, Kyoto. Opened in 2020, the brick-and-mortar location pairs an in-person matcha drink bar with an extensive curated selection of premium matcha powders and traditional tea wares. The business has grown to supply over 100 cafe wholesale partners across North America, making it a notable destination for matcha enthusiasts.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: All menu items are matcha or plant-based tea beverages with no animal-product offerings evident on the website

restaurant.name: Earls
restaurant.desc: Earls is a well-known Canadian casual dining chain operating as Earls Kitchen + Bar, offering a full sit-down menu alongside bar service in a modern setting. The Chilliwack location sits in the Sardis retail corridor and serves the Fraser Valley, making it a recognizable stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. Online ordering with pickup is available for those wanting a quicker stop.

restaurant.name: Tarboosh
restaurant.desc: Tarboosh is a Middle Eastern fast-food restaurant in Victoria, BC. The OSM record tags it with Middle Eastern cuisine, suggesting fare such as shawarma and falafel typical of the style. No further details about this specific location could be verified due to a URL mismatch with a same-named restaurant in Ontario.

restaurant.name: El Furniture Warehouse
restaurant.desc: El Furniture Warehouse is a bustling pub and restaurant in the heart of downtown Victoria, located steps from the Inner Harbour on Yates Street. The space features exposed brick, roll-up windows, and dog-friendly street-side seating, giving it a relaxed, welcoming character. Part of a Canadian multi-location chain, the Victoria outpost is a well-reviewed neighbourhood staple serving pub food with late-night hours and easy takeout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes plant-based options such as the Southwest Tortilla Ensalada (avocado, mixed greens, black beans, corn salsa, cucumber — no meat in base version) and General Tao Bowl (mixed vegetables, jasmine rice). No explicit GF or vegan labelling found

restaurant.name: Handworks Coffee Studio
restaurant.desc: Handworks Coffee Studio is a small, takeout-only coffee operation located on 6th Street in Burnaby. With no indoor or outdoor seating, it functions as a grab-and-go stop for cyclists passing through the neighbourhood. Its compact, studio-style format suggests a specialty coffee focus.

restaurant.name: 101 Boba
restaurant.desc: 101 Canada Boba is a Vancouver-founded bubble tea chain launched in 2020, serving grab-and-go fruit teas, milk teas, and seasonal specialty drinks made with premium ingredients—70% sourced directly from Taiwan. The Main Street location is one of six BC stores built around a streamlined quick-service model, making it a fast hydration stop for cyclists passing through the neighbourhood. The brand operates a loyalty rewards program with over 80% customer return rate.

restaurant.name: HiFive Chicken 24
restaurant.desc: HiFive Chicken 24 is a quick-service restaurant specializing in chicken, located in Vancouver. As a casual eatery with takeaway options, it provides convenient meal service for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Wildfire Bakery
restaurant.desc: Wildfire Bakery is a small, family-owned artisan bakery on Victoria's Quadra Street, operating since 1998 and specializing in naturally leavened sourdough breads baked in a wood-fired oven. They grind all their whole grain flours using a custom stone mill, sourcing certified organic and mostly BC-grown wheat, spelt, and rye. Cyclists will find a broad selection of fresh loaves, croissants, muffins, pastries, custom cakes, and packaged grocery items like pasta and granola.

restaurant.name: Donair Dude
restaurant.desc: Donair Dude is a BC-based Mediterranean fast-food chain launched during the 2010 Winter Olympics, serving donair wraps, platters, poutine, and falafel dishes made with locally sourced BC meats. The Nanaimo location on Fifth Street offers a broad menu spanning chicken, beef, lamb, and vegan options, with online ordering available. For a touring cyclist, it is a convenient calorie stop with familiar quick-service format in a central Nanaimo location.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website front page lists 'VEGAN' as a distinct menu category; menu includes Falafel Wrap, Falafel Platter, and Falafel Plate confirming vegetarian/vegan options

restaurant.name: Tandoori Corner
restaurant.desc: Gian's Tandoori Corner is a modern Indian restaurant in Westbank (West Kelowna) carrying on a culinary tradition dating to 1999. Specializing in high-heat clay oven cooking, it serves charred skewers, freshly baked naan, and aromatic curries crafted from time-honored recipes. The restaurant also offers catering for events, food truck bookings, and freshly made Indian sweets daily.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Extensive vegetarian menu including Daal Makhni, Daal Tarka, Palak Paneer, Paneer Butter Masala, Kadai Paneer, Shahi Paneer, Malai Kofta, Mixed Vegetables, Aloo Ghobi, and multiple paneer appetizers

restaurant.name: Salmon n' Bannock
restaurant.desc: Salmon n' Bannock is Vancouver's only Indigenous restaurant, founded in 2010 and now owned by Inez Cook of the Nuxalk Nation. The kitchen sources wild BC seafood and organic free-range game meats alongside traditional ingredients like bannock and Anishnaabe wild rice to craft modern dishes rooted in First Nations culinary heritage. It sits on the unceded territories of the Musqueam, Squamish, and Tsleil-Waututh Nations on the West Broadway corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu labels vegetarian dishes '(v)' (e.g., 3 Sisters and a Cuzzin Stuffed Pepper, Rotating Vegetarian Indigenized Risotto) and gluten-free items '(gf)' including Gluten Free Bannock and multiple mains

restaurant.name: Il Nido Italian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Il Nido is a well-regarded Italian restaurant in downtown Vancouver's West End, earning OpenTable Best Restaurant recognition for both 2024 and 2025 and a TripAdvisor Recommended designation. The menu leans into Roman and Sicilian classics—carbonara, cacio e pepe, arancini, lasagna—alongside a charcuterie board and rotating salumi. Both indoor and patio seating are available in a smoke-free setting steps from Robson Street.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels multiple dishes 'Vegetarian' (e.g. Balsamic Bruschetta, Rigatoni Cacio e Pepe, Spinach Ravioli, Il Nido Beetroot Salad) and 'Gluten free' (e.g. Burrata Caprese, Calamari & Prawns, Funghi & Crostini); gluten-free pasta substitutions also noted on several pasta dishes

restaurant.name: Fiorino
restaurant.desc: Fiorino is an authentic Florentine-inspired Italian street food restaurant founded by Florence native Giovanni Mascagni, built around house-baked Tuscan schiacciata bread sandwiches crafted using centuries-old techniques learned at Florence's Mercato di Sant'Ambrogio. The Lonsdale Quay Market location seats up to 150 guests and offers a full Italian cocktail and wine bar alongside its sandwich and dinner menus. A second location operates in Vancouver's Chinatown.

detail.address: #218 - 123 Carrie Cates Court, North Vancouver, BC V7M 3K7

restaurant.name: Farros Pizza and Greek
restaurant.desc: Farros Pizza and Greek is a Kamloops restaurant offering an eclectic menu that combines Greek classics, wood-fired pizzas, and Indian dishes from two city locations. The Tranquille Road outpost (Unit 10) is one of the pair, with the menu spanning souvlaki, Greek ribs, calamari, and paneer tikka. The kitchen emphasizes fresh, handcrafted and fully customizable dishes, with the Family Pack — loaded with skewers, ribs, prawns, calamari, and sides — as the house favourite.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Paneer Tikka ('marinated cheese cooked with green peppers, tomatoes in hot clay oven') — a vegetarian dish — and Greek salad

restaurant.name: Uncle Sal's Shawarma
restaurant.desc: Uncle Sal's Shawarma is a family-run Mediterranean restaurant in Richmond, operated by the same family behind the Al Basha Richmond location since 2015. The menu centres on shawarma wraps and plates featuring lamb, beef, and falafel, all prepared to halal standards. It occupies a strip-mall unit on Blundell Road and pitches itself on consistent food quality and a warm, family-style atmosphere.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu subpage title lists 'Falafel' as a distinct menu category alongside Shawarma, Lamb, and Beef, confirming at least one vegetarian option

restaurant.name: Ricardo's
restaurant.desc: Ricardo's is an ice cream shop on Granville Street in the heart of downtown Vancouver's entertainment district. The shop offers vegan-friendly options and air-conditioned indoor seating, making it a comfortable rest stop for cyclists in the area. Payments by credit and debit card are accepted.

restaurant.name: JoongWon
restaurant.desc: JoongWon is a restaurant on Robson Street in Vancouver's West End, a busy commercial corridor popular with pedestrians and cyclists. OSM records indoor seating and a no-smoking policy. No accessible website content was available to provide further detail about cuisine or dining experience.

restaurant.name: It's a Bakery
restaurant.desc: It's a Bakery is an artisan bread and pastry shop operating as a sister brand to Okanagan Grocery, with this Anders Road site serving as one of three locations across Kelowna and West Kelowna. New ownership took over in May 2025, transforming the space into a cozy coffee house where guests can enjoy freshly brewed coffee alongside pastries, cake, and artisan loaves. Pre-ordering is available through the website, making it a convenient planned stop on a ride.

detail.address: 101-845 Anders Road, West Kelowna, BC V1Z 1J9

restaurant.name: Sora Sushi House
restaurant.desc: Sora Sushi House is a Japanese sushi restaurant in New Westminster with a broad menu spanning nigiri, sashimi, specialty rolls, donburi, and appetizers, all available for pickup via an online ordering system. The restaurant has accumulated over 80 customer reviews and offers a convenient, fast turnaround for a fresh meal. A touring cyclist passing through New Westminster will find a wide variety of filling options including several vegetarian rolls and combos.

detail.address: 74 Eighth St, New Westminster, BC V3M 5Z5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian rolls (Yam & Avocado, Avocado, Vegetables, Kappa) and vegetarian appetizers (Edamame, Seaweed Salad, Veggie Sunomono, Veggie Combo). No explicit vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Fortune Terrace Chinese Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Fortune Terrace Chinese Cuisine is a full-service Cantonese restaurant on River Road in Richmond offering an expansive menu that spans dim sum, congee, BBQ duck and pork, fresh seafood, and seasonal chef's specials. The restaurant also accepts online orders for in-store pickup, making it a practical stop for cyclists wanting a sit-down or grab-and-go Chinese meal. Its location on River Road places it near the popular cycling routes that follow the south arm of the Fraser River.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetable and tofu dishes including Deep-Fried Tofu in Hong Kong Style, Dry-Fried Spicy Green Beans, Pan-Fried Choy Sum Vegetables, Stir-Fried Chinese Yam with Fresh Lily & Celery, and Pea Tips with Tofu Skin in Soup

restaurant.name: Waku North
restaurant.desc: Waku North is a ramen and izakaya restaurant located in a commercial strip on Metral Drive in north Nanaimo. Specializing in Japanese ramen, it offers a sit-down dining experience with both lunch and dinner service across most of the week. Touring cyclists looking for a hot, filling bowl after a long day on the road will find this a solid stop in the Nanaimo area.

restaurant.name: Samosa Time
restaurant.desc: Samosa Time is a fast-food restaurant in Chilliwack specializing in Indian samosas and cakes. It offers quick takeout service, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking packable meals in the area.

restaurant.name: The Blarney Stone
restaurant.desc: Established in 1972, The Blarney Stone is Vancouver's longest-running Irish pub and one of the most iconic landmarks in British Columbia, housed in an 1888 building in the heart of historic Gastown that originally served as the Klondike Hotel. It draws locals and tourists alike with Irish-inspired comfort food, live music on weekends, and a boisterous atmosphere on a massive 240-inch screen for sporting events. Its location in Gastown places it directly along popular Vancouver cycling routes near the waterfront.

restaurant.name: Driftwood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A Chinese restaurant on Campbell River's South Island Highway. Serves dine-in meals to locals and touring cyclists passing through the community.

detail.address: 4329 South Island Highway, Campbell River, V9H 1B7

restaurant.name: Solly's
restaurant.desc: Solly's Bagelry is a Vancouver institution billing itself as 'Jewish Baking and Deli at its Finest,' offering freshly baked traditional bagels, deli items, soups, sandwiches, and grocery staples. The Up Main location on Main Street is one of three Vancouver retail outlets for the brand. It's a practical urban food stop for touring cyclists riding the Main Street corridor looking for a hearty, freshly made meal.

restaurant.name: Mighty Peace Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Mighty Peace Brewing Co. opened in 2018 as Fort St. John's community craft brewery and tap room, founded by four local friends inspired by BC's diverse brewing scene and the spirit of the North. The tap room pours a rotating lineup of house-crafted beers — from an authentic German pilsner to a fruited sour — alongside a pub food menu that spotlights locally sourced ingredients including meats from Mackay Farms. Housed in a two-storey building in the heart of Fort St. John, it functions as a lively gathering hub for a northern BC city perched on the Peace River plateau.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu explicitly lists a Veggie Burrito Bowl (corn, black beans, cheese, romaine lettuce, mexi rice, tortilla chips, sour cream, salsa, and guacamole)

restaurant.name: New York Fries
restaurant.desc: New York Fries is a Canadian fast-food chain specializing in hand-cut, skin-on fries cooked to order in non-hydrogenated sunflower oil, served alongside poutines, premium hot dogs, and a range of dips. This Kelowna location sits on Harvey Avenue at what appears to be the Orchard Park Shopping Centre, a major commercial hub on the city's main arterial corridor. Touring cyclists will find a quick, filling carb stop with vegetarian and vegan-friendly options on the menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website fries page labels items 'Vegetarian Vegan-Friendly Gluten-Friendly'; dips page states 'All dips are vegetarian'; Classic Poutine noted as vegetarian

restaurant.name: Sushi Nova
restaurant.desc: Sushi Nova is a Japanese restaurant nestled in Kitsilano, steps from West 4th Avenue and within easy walking distance of Kits Beach. The restaurant offers a broad menu spanning classic rolls, specialty hand rolls, robata, donburi, and sashimi, with a dedicated takeout menu and online ordering. Reviewers consistently highlight fresh ingredients, friendly service, and an inviting atmosphere with good decor.

notes.Takeout: Website lists a dedicated 'TAKE OUT ONLY MENU' section and prominent 'ORDER ONLINE' button; customer review confirms: 'Got it to go and took about 30 mins.'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'VEGETABLE ROLL' category, confirming vegetarian roll options are available

restaurant.name: Church's Chicken
restaurant.desc: Church's Chicken is a fried chicken fast-food chain offering takeaway service. Located on Kingsway in Burnaby, it provides a quick meal option for cycling tourists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Kanpeki Teppanyaki & Seafood Bar
restaurant.desc: Kanpeki Teppanyaki & Seafood Bar is a Japanese restaurant in Richmond's Alexandra Road dining corridor, specialising in teppanyaki and seafood. The teppanyaki format typically centres on tableside iron-griddle cooking, making it a more substantial sit-down experience than a quick café stop. It sits within a unit-based commercial building, suggesting a larger multi-tenant retail or dining complex.

restaurant.name: Stem Japanese Eatery
restaurant.desc: Stem Japanese Eatery is a kappo-style Japanese restaurant in Burnaby where chef-owner Tatsuya Katagiri brings Tokyo training and Vancouver fine-dining experience to a seasonally driven menu emphasising the 'cut and cook' proximity between diner and chef. Dishes are crafted from locally sourced and imported Japanese ingredients, and the restaurant offers an omakase kaiseki experience alongside à la carte small plates. Takeout is also available via email order, making it a convenient stop for cyclists seeking a quality Japanese meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dinner menu explicitly labels 'Gluten Free' items (BC Potato Salad, Chawan Mushi with miso option) and 'Vegan' (Daikon Beer Pickles); multiple vegetable-based obanzai small plates also listed

restaurant.name: Stonehouse Pub
restaurant.desc: The Stonehouse Pub occupies a historic 1930s stone manor at Canoe Cove Marina, just minutes from the BC Ferries Swartz Bay terminal, making it a natural stop for cyclists arriving or departing by ferry. Established as a pub in 1985 and under new ownership since November 2023, it serves upmarket pub fare crafted from locally sourced ingredients in a cozy marina-side setting. Live music on the patio, craft beers, and a shaded outdoor area give it a distinct character beyond the typical roadside stop.

detail.address: 2215 Canoe Cove Rd, North Saanich, BC V8L 3X9

restaurant.name: Dinesty Dumpling House
restaurant.desc: Dinesty Dumpling House is a Greater Vancouver Chinese restaurant chain celebrated for its award-winning Xiaolongbao (soup dumplings), having taken top honours at the HSBC Chinese Restaurant Diners' Choice Awards multiple times since 2010. The Richmond Gilbert Road location is a full sit-down restaurant serving a broad menu of Chinese delicacies, with dine-in, takeout, and delivery available. Founded in 2006, the company emphasizes all-natural, fresh ingredients and traditional handcraft techniques across its five Lower Mainland locations.

restaurant.name: La Gondola
restaurant.desc: La Gondola is a family-owned Italian and Canadian restaurant that has anchored Prince Rupert's dining scene since 1952. It occupies a Venetian-style building overlooking Prince Rupert Harbour, offering dine-in with harbour-view window seats alongside a nostalgic old-fashioned drive-in with curbside car service. The menu ranges from homemade burgers and milkshakes to Northern Italian classics like veal scallopini a la Marsala and baked lasagna Bolognese, with a licensed dining room rounding out the experience.

detail.address: 710 1st Ave W, Prince Rupert, BC V8J 3V6

restaurant.name: M Cafe
restaurant.desc: M Cafe is a casual Pan-Asian restaurant in Creekside Plaza along Barnet Highway in Coquitlam, serving everything from Hong Kong-style milk teas and fried rice noodles to Singaporean vermicelli, Japanese-inspired mini hot pots, and Western staples like rack of lamb and lobster fettuccine. The broad menu and dine-in atmosphere make it a solid fuelling stop for cyclists riding the Barnet Highway corridor. Online ordering via a dedicated mobile app is available for both takeout and dine-in.

detail.address: Creekside Plaza Unit C - 2773 Barnet Highway, Coquitlam, BC

restaurant.name: bb.q Chicken
restaurant.desc: A Korean fried chicken restaurant from the bb.q Chicken franchise located on Main Street in Vancouver. Offers casual dining with Korean-style chicken as the specialty. A convenient refueling stop for cycling tourists, though specific amenities for cyclists could not be verified.

restaurant.name: Odd Burger
restaurant.desc: Odd Burger is Canada's first fully vegan fast-food chain, founded in London, Ontario in 2014 and now operating locations across Canada. The company manufactures its own plant-based ingredients and built its brand on accessible, minimally processed vegan fast food — including what it calls the 'Famous Burger,' which sold out at a meat-centric Ontario ribfest in 2016. The Vancouver Main Street location opened in late 2024, bringing a mission-driven vegan fast food option to a well-trafficked urban cycling corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: 100% vegan menu confirmed by website ('As a 100% vegan company') and. All menu items are plant-based

restaurant.name: Hiel Cafe
restaurant.desc: Hiel Cafe is a ground-floor cafe in a commercial building on 6th Street in Burnaby, offering indoor seating in a no-smoking environment. It operates as a neighbourhood cafe with a social-media presence on Instagram, suggesting a community-oriented character. Touring cyclists passing through the area would find it a potential rest stop, though details about the menu and facilities are not publicly verifiable.

restaurant.name: Damiano's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Damiano's Pizza & Pasta has operated under the S&S Restaurants banner since 1998, serving a broad menu of specialty pizzas, pastas, Greek dishes, BBQ ribs, and fusion sides like samosas from its location on Johnston Road in White Rock. The restaurant offers 21 specialty pizzas with crust options including whole wheat, thin-crust, and gluten-free, making it a solid stop for cyclists with dietary needs. Its central location in White Rock puts it within easy reach of the seaside cycling routes along the waterfront.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website /order page lists a 'Vegetarian Options' menu category; /about page explicitly mentions gluten-free crust as an available option

restaurant.name: The Wee Chippie Fish & Chips
restaurant.desc: The Wee Chippie is a casual British-style fish and chips restaurant located in a strip mall on the Lougheed Highway in Mission, BC. It offers both dine-in and takeout service, with delivery also available through Skip The Dishes and DoorDash. For cyclists riding the Lougheed corridor, it would serve as a hearty, sit-down refuelling stop in the Fraser Valley.

restaurant.name: End Of The Line General Store
restaurant.desc: A locally owned general store and cafe nestled at the end of Lynn Valley Road in Upper Lynn Valley, occupying a corner with roots going back to 1910 as the final stop on the historic Lynn Valley Trolley Line. The store serves JJBean coffee and espresso drinks alongside soups, sandwiches, scones, ice cream, and its signature gluten-free and vegan Trail Pucks, plus locally made art and gifts. It sits minutes from the Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge, Lynn Headwaters, the Seymour Valley Trailway, and the world-renowned Mount Fromme mountain biking network, making it a natural basecamp for North Shore adventurers.

detail.address: 4193 Lynn Valley Road, North Vancouver, BC V7K 2T1

notes.Takeout: General store and cafe format with coffee, sandwiches, soups, scones, and ice cream sold over the counter; website invites customers to 'stop by for a delicious cup of coffee and snack before and after you explore the trails.'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly names 'famous gluten-free & vegan Trail Pucks' as a signature product

restaurant.name: Handi Grill
restaurant.desc: Handi Grill is a long-established Indian restaurant on Vancouver's West Broadway, offering award-winning traditional East Indian cuisine including Tandoori specialties, aromatic curries, and regional favourites crafted from locally-sourced ingredients. The restaurant has operated for over a decade and positions itself as a community-oriented destination rather than just a dining stop. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery are all available, along with a full catering service for events.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists dedicated Vegetarian Lunch Thali, Vegetarian Dinner Thali, and vegetarian curry options throughout; website references 'vegetarian specialties' as a menu section

restaurant.name: Kim's Korean BBQ House
restaurant.desc: Kim's Korean BBQ House is a Korean barbecue restaurant located on Bowen Road in Nanaimo. Korean BBQ restaurants typically centre the dining experience on table-top grills where guests cook marinated meats, making them a satisfying stop for a hungry touring cyclist looking for a hearty, social meal.

restaurant.name: Jamaican Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Jamaican Kitchen is a family-owned Caribbean restaurant on Kamloops' Tranquille Road, founded by Red Seal chef Kamau Metsimela and his wife Denese, who brought authentic Jamaican home-style cooking to BC's interior in 2012. The casual spot serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner featuring jerk dishes, johnnycakes, island-spiced French toast, and creative twists on Canadian favourites, with a soundtrack of Bob Marley to match. Cyclists can fuel up with hearty plates or order for pickup via the online shop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Vegetarian Benedict, Garden Omelet, Vegan Skillet (explicitly labelled vegan, with tofu scramble and vegan cheese), and Vegan Grab and Go Sandwich

restaurant.name: Lambda Cabaret

restaurant.desc: The Keg is a well-established Canadian steakhouse chain with this location housed in a historical building in Vancouver's downtown Financial and Entertainment District, at the corner of Dunsmuir and Granville, steps from the Skytrain station. The Dunsmuir location offers a dining room, lounge, bar, and private and semi-private dining rooms accommodating groups of various sizes. Free Wi-Fi and takeout ordering are available for those wanting a quick stop or a full sit-down meal after a ride.

restaurant.name: Blue Chip Cafe
restaurant.desc: Blue Chip Cafe is a student-union-owned cafe on the main floor of the AMS Nest at UBC Vancouver, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the campus. It serves Spirit Bear coffee, specialty barista drinks, baked goods, sandwiches, and a range of vegan and gluten-free options. Catering and online pickup ordering are also available.

restaurant.name: Merci Boulangerie
restaurant.desc: Merci Boulangerie is a French-inspired artisan bakery on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, founded by Red Seal Baker Natalie Cumberbirch, who trained at the two-Michelin-star L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon in Paris and the celebrated boulangerie Mamiche. The shop serves freshly baked croissants, pastries, and bread alongside coffee and locally curated retail items. For touring cyclists riding Commercial Drive, it is a well-located stop for high-quality baked goods in one of Vancouver's most vibrant neighbourhood corridors.

restaurant.name: Europe Old Fashion Bakery and Deli
restaurant.desc: Europe Bakery & Deli is a Port Coquitlam bakery producing fresh bread, donuts, and an extensive range of European-style pastries entirely in-house daily. The deli component rounds out the offering beyond pure baked goods. It serves both walk-in customers and online delivery orders via Uber Eats and SkipTheDishes.

detail.address: 2552 Shaughnessy St, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 3G4, Canada

restaurant.name: Donair Affair
restaurant.desc: Donair Affair is a BC-based fast food chain with over 20 locations, specializing in Mediterranean-style donair kebabs that blend Middle Eastern and Canadian flavors — one of the originals in the province for close to a quarter century. The Surrey Guildford branch offers beef, lamb, chicken, and vegetarian falafel wraps with a variety of toppings and sauces, plus Mayan-style platters and combination options. It is a quick, filling stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley corridor.

restaurant.name: Biscuit: A Place To Sup
restaurant.desc: Biscuit is a casual supper restaurant and wine bar in Kimberley founded in 2021, committed to locally sourced and premium ingredients with everything made in-house. Run by Ryan, a Southern BC hospitality veteran, it aims for the simplicity of a pub environment paired with fine-dining quality, offering an ever-changing menu for adventurous eaters. The spot also carries a retail selection of specialty ingredients, house-made condiments, and cocktail kits, plus a recurring wine club.

restaurant.name: Grand Seasons Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Grand Seasons Restaurant is a Cantonese Chinese eatery in Coquitlam specializing in congee, Hong Kong-style noodles, BBQ meats, and seafood dishes. With 97 online reviews and a reputation for fast service and generous portions, it draws a loyal neighbourhood following. Cyclists passing through the Coquitlam area can order online for quick pickup or dine in for a hearty, affordable meal.

restaurant.name: Smuggler's Cove
restaurant.desc: Smuggler's Cove is a cozy British-style neighbourhood pub in the Cadboro Bay area of Saanich, featuring a second-floor deck and 12 beers on draught. It serves global comfort fare including burgers, fish and chips, and entrees, with an adjacent liquor store on site. Touring cyclists will find a welcoming local atmosphere with online ordering and takeout options available.

restaurant.name: Osmow's
restaurant.desc: Osmow's is a Canadian fast-food chain founded by Egyptian immigrant Sam Osmow, now operating over 215 locations across Canada and the United States. The Surrey location serves Mediterranean-inspired shawarma wraps, plates, and salads with a range of proteins. It is a quick and filling stop for touring cyclists passing through the 88 Avenue corridor in Surrey.

restaurant.name: Deep Cove Pizza
restaurant.desc: Deep Cove Pizza is a pizza restaurant in North Vancouver's Deep Cove neighborhood, offering both indoor and outdoor seating. Located on Gallant Avenue, it provides casual pizza dining for local visitors and passing cyclists.

restaurant.name: Togo Sushi
restaurant.desc: Togo Sushi is a takeout-focused sushi chain with a location at UBC Vancouver on Shrum Lane, well-positioned for cyclists riding the popular paths through the UBC campus and Pacific Spirit Park. The brand is built around grab-and-go ordering, with online and app-based ordering available. As one of several Lower Mainland locations, it offers a familiar, quick-service option for cyclists needing a fast, filling meal.

restaurant.name: Pokerrito
restaurant.desc: Pokerrito Mount Pleasant is a Pan-Asian poke bowl and sushi burrito chain location in Vancouver's Brewery District, offering over 50 customizable combinations built from sushi-grade proteins, plant-based options, and globally inspired sauces. Situated at the crossroads of Mount Pleasant, Fairview, and Kitsilano, the spot is a short ride from the Broadway–City Hall Canada Line station and easily accessible along the Broadway cycling corridor. It is one of more than a dozen Pokerrito franchise locations across BC and Ontario.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels vegan options (🌱) including Citrus Ponzu, Classic Shoyu, SSS sauce, and tofu/plant-based proteins; gluten-free (GF) sauces also marked on menu

restaurant.name: Half Blind Bean Coffee
restaurant.desc: Half Blind Bean Coffee is a specialty espresso bar in Kelowna's Richter Street neighbourhood, built around locally roasted beans and a consistent approach to craft coffee. The café welcomes both quick stops and longer visits, pairing espresso drinks with fresh baking made without shortcuts. It holds a 4.8-star customer rating and also sells retail beans for home or on-the-road brewing.

restaurant.name: Sun Garden Chinese
restaurant.desc: Sun Garden Chinese is a sit-down Chinese restaurant on Oak Street in Vancouver serving an extensive Cantonese-style menu spanning chicken, beef, pork, seafood, tofu, and vegetarian dishes. The restaurant operates its own online ordering system for takeout. With 63 customer reviews and a broad menu, it is a reliable full-meal stop for cyclists passing through the Oak Street corridor.
