restaurant.name: Sushi Giwa
restaurant.desc: Sushi Giwa is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Hastings Street in Burnaby serving a full menu from late morning through the evening seven days a week. The restaurant offers online ordering and occasional promotional deals. It sits along a busy commercial corridor that touring cyclists travelling the Hastings Street corridor may find convenient for a sit-down meal.

restaurant.name: Best Falafel
restaurant.desc: Best Falafel is a Syrian-Lebanese restaurant on Commercial Drive, a popular Vancouver cycling corridor, founded by Damascus-born owner Hisham Wattar who has run the location since 2000. The menu spans falafel, shawarma, donair wraps, plates, and salads with vegetarian and gluten-free choices, and the restaurant has grown to three Metro Vancouver locations. It has served over a million customers and is considered a local fixture on the Drive.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a dedicated Vegetarian Plate, Falafel Wrap and Plate, and Gluten Free Tabbouleh Salad as named menu items

restaurant.name: Song Huong
restaurant.desc: Song Huong is a Vietnamese restaurant located on Hastings Street in Burnaby, a well-travelled commercial corridor. The Hastings Street corridor connects East Vancouver to Burnaby and sees regular bicycle commuter and touring traffic. Beyond its Vietnamese cuisine, no distinguishing details are verifiable from available sources.

restaurant.name: Alexander's Pub and Liquor Store
restaurant.desc: Alexander's Pub and Liquor Store sits on the shores of Kalamalka Lake in Coldstream, offering lakeside dining with an outdoor patio overlooking the water — a scenic stop for cyclists riding the Okanagan's lake routes. The pub serves a broad menu of comfort food including wings, nachos, burgers, and mains like halibut and ribs, alongside an attached liquor store. The combination of a full kitchen, patio seating, and a relaxed neighbourhood atmosphere makes it a practical and pleasant rest point on a touring ride.

detail.address: 12408 Kalamalka Rd, Coldstream, BC V1B 1M3, Canada

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'The Veggie Panini' and 'Garden Burger' as dedicated vegetarian options; no explicit GF or vegan labelling found

restaurant.name: Le Brunch Café
restaurant.desc: Le Brunch Café is a gourmet brunch, breakfast, and lunch restaurant located in Nanaimo, BC. The café offers a dedicated reservations system and a full menu, positioning itself as a sit-down dining destination rather than a quick-service stop. For touring cyclists passing through Nanaimo, it would serve as a relaxed mid-ride or end-of-day meal option.

restaurant.name: Marais Tea Company & Café
restaurant.desc: Marais Tea Company & Café is a specialty tea purveyor and café in Chilliwack sourcing fine teas from premier growing regions worldwide, including single-origin orthodox teas, blended black teas, matcha, and herbal infusions. The business operates both a physical café with outdoor seating and an active online retail store, offering a calm, intentional pause for those wanting a carefully steeped cup. Notably, the café accepts Bitcoin and Lightning Network payments — an unusual feature for a small-town tea house.

restaurant.name: The Green Olive By Old City
restaurant.desc: The Green Olive Bar & Grill is a restaurant and bar located at 150 Skinner Street in downtown Nanaimo, operating adjacent to the Old City Station Pub. It serves food and drinks in a casual atmosphere and regularly hosts live comedy and music events. The venue is available for private event bookings and shares operations with the Old City Station Pub, which has been Nanaimo's top sports bar since 2008.

restaurant.name: Taps & Tacos
restaurant.desc: Taps & Tacos is a 40-seat globally inspired Mexican restaurant nestled steps from Rocky Point Park and Port Moody's Brewers Row craft brewery district. The bright, glass-exterior building features an open-concept kitchen, a loft level with additional seating, and a menu built around house-made sauces, salsas, and free-run meats sourced locally. It also operates a catering taco truck, making it a lively stop in an area popular with recreational cyclists.

detail.address: 91 Moody St, Port Moody, BC V3H 0H1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Customer review on the restaurant's own website states: 'My companion is Celiac and can eat almost the entire menu.'

restaurant.name: Dear Gus
restaurant.desc: Dear Gus Snack Bar is a small European wine and snack bar in Vancouver's Mt. Pleasant neighbourhood, offering a rotating selection of curated wines alongside aperitivo-style small plates, seasonal charcuterie, and European-influenced mains. The intimate indoor space encourages walk-ins and runs a monthly wine club featuring hand-selected bottles that are hard to find in local liquor stores. Private dining for larger groups is available by booking the entire space.

restaurant.name: Sushi Kaido
restaurant.desc: Sushi Kaido is a Japanese restaurant at the busy Main and Broadway intersection in Vancouver, serving handcrafted sushi and Japanese cuisine with indoor seating. The restaurant offers online ordering with a rewards program, and has expanded into catering for schools and companies. It sits on a major cycling corridor connecting east Vancouver to the city centre.

restaurant.name: The Tannenbaum Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Tannenbaum is a family-run German and Bavarian-inspired restaurant emphasizing fresh, high-quality ingredients and a warm, nostalgic atmosphere. Located in New Westminster, it offers both indoor and outdoor seating and accepts cash, credit, and debit. The restaurant occupies a former Chronic Tacos location and has established itself as a local destination for authentic German cuisine in the Greater Vancouver area.

restaurant.name: Chipotle
restaurant.desc: Chipotle Mexican Grill is a fast-casual chain serving customizable burritos, bowls, tacos, quesadillas, and salads made with responsibly sourced ingredients and no artificial colors, flavors, or preservatives. Located on Robson Street near Homer, this location offers both in-store pickup and delivery. The outdoor seating and central downtown Vancouver location make it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Buzzy's Luncheonette
restaurant.desc: Buzzy's Luncheonette is a beloved Jewish deli on Salt Spring Island, celebrated for house-made Montreal Smoked Meat — briskets cured for 8–10 days, smoked for 10 hours, and steamed to order. Founded in 2017 by a former LA standup comic and his wife, the tiny shop punches well above its weight and won the 2019 Salty Award for Best New Business and Best Menu Item. Cyclists crossing to Salt Spring will find hearty, distinctive sandwiches and house-made potato latkes ready for takeout.

restaurant.name: Asian Pear Buffet
restaurant.desc: Asian Pear Buffet is an all-you-can-eat Chinese and Western cuisine restaurant on Harvey Avenue in Kelowna, with over 100 menu items spanning both culinary traditions. The buffet format makes it an appealing option for hungry touring cyclists looking to seriously refuel after a day on the Okanagan's cycling routes. The restaurant also offers takeout and delivery for those who prefer a grab-and-go approach.

restaurant.name: Trails End
restaurant.desc: Trails End is a cafe, taproom, and bistro operated by Smugglers Trail Caskworks, situated beside the Fraser River in the historic village of Fort Langley. The spot pours the brewery's cask-conditioned craft ales alongside a full food menu running from breakfast through dinner, making it a natural refuelling stop on the Transcanada Trail corridor. Live music on Saturday evenings and outdoor seating add to the appeal for cyclists finishing a ride through the Fort Langley area.

detail.address: 23285 Billy Brown Rd #100, Langley Twp, BC

restaurant.name: Lazzez's Grill Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Lazzez's Grill is a fully licensed fine-dining Indian restaurant on Barnet Highway in Coquitlam, with a focus on tandoor cooking — clay-oven tikkas, seekh kebabs, and freshly baked naan are menu centrepieces. Chef Gurdeep Singh brings experience from India, the UK, and Canada, and the kitchen produces a broad menu spanning meat, seafood, vegetable, and gluten-free options. The restaurant has outdoor seating, accepts walk-ins, and offers takeout and catering, making it a viable sit-down or grab-and-go stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu labels several items as vegan (e.g. Vegetable Samosa, Vegetable Pakora, Onion Bhaji) and many items as gluten free (e.g. Vegetable Pakora, most Tandoori Sizzler dishes, numerous chicken and lamb items)

restaurant.name: Blaze Gourmet Burgers
restaurant.desc: Blaze Gourmet Burgers began as a COVID-era ghost kitchen in 2019 and grew into a multi-location brand anchored in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood. The restaurant is built around dietary inclusivity, offering certified Angus beef burgers alongside a full range of vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, and halal options — including vegan poutine and vegan chicken strips. The Mount Pleasant flagship also houses Blaze Cafe, a sister company serving premium Indonesian-sourced coffee, making it a capable one-stop for a cyclist wanting both a substantial meal and a quality coffee.

restaurant.name: BiBo Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: BiBo Pizzeria is an authentic Italian restaurant located inside the McArthurGlen Designer Outlet in Richmond, operated by a team of Italian expatriates who have been serving Neapolitan pizza and housemade pasta since 2011. The restaurant sources high-quality ingredients directly from Italian farms and BC producers, including buffalo mozzarella DOP and Cortese Gavi di Gavi wine. It has earned recognition from Gambero Rosso, Italy's prestigious food and wine guide, and holds an Ospitalità Italiana certification.

detail.address: 1067C – 7899 Templeton Station Road, Richmond, BC V7B 0B7

restaurant.name: Station House Pub & Grill
restaurant.desc: A pub in Abbotsford serving Canadian cuisine with outdoor seating available. A convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Vera's Burger Shack
restaurant.desc: Vera's Burger Shack is a BC-based burger chain that hand-presses every patty using 100% fresh Canadian beef and prepares all food to order. The Commercial Drive location puts cyclists in one of Vancouver's most vibrant and walkable neighbourhoods. The chain runs rotating daily specials alongside a full burger and sides lineup, making it a reliable calorie stop mid-ride.

restaurant.name: Khaghan Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Khaghan is a modern Persian restaurant specialising in fire-grilled meats, fragrant saffron stews, and traditional dishes made with halal-certified meats and imported Iranian rice. The multi-level venue includes a street-level dining room, a second-floor event space with 40-foot ceilings and floor-to-ceiling glass, and a patio. Weekend evenings feature live music and dance, making it a lively destination for groups as well as solo diners.

detail.address: 935 Marine Dr Unit 66, North Vancouver, BC V7P 1S3

restaurant.name: Select Pizza
restaurant.desc: Select Pizza is a carry-out pizza restaurant specializing in Punjabi-style pizzas loaded with fresh toppings, blending South Asian flavours — tandoori chicken, paneer, butter chicken sauce — with familiar pizza formats. The North Delta location on 120 Street (Scott Road) is the OSM-mapped site, with a second location in Newton. The menu spans more than 20 specialty pizzas plus a build-your-own option.

restaurant.name: Coquette
restaurant.desc: Brasserie Coquette is a Parisian-style brasserie in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, celebrating local suppliers alongside traditional French cuisine with seasonal dishes anchored by French classics. The restaurant offers both indoor dining and a patio, hosts regular live jazz and blues music nights, and accommodates private events for groups of 8 to 100. It is part of a small local restaurant group with two sister establishments in the neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: The Art We Are
restaurant.desc: The Art We Are began in August 2008 as a local art gallery and evolved into a cafe while keeping rotating works by local artists on its walls and shelves. It serves a freshly made menu of brunch wraps, house soups (rotating daily with at least one always vegan and GF), wraps, sandwiches, and desserts—with ingredients sourced as locally as possible. Touring cyclists will find strong gluten-free and vegan options throughout the menu, and the cafe also offers catering with delivery for group orders.

restaurant.name: Maxim's Bakery
restaurant.desc: Maxim's Bakery is a neighborhood bakery on Fraser Street in Vancouver. As a bakery, it offers baked goods suitable for touring cyclists seeking food provisions.

restaurant.name: Wind Cries Mary
restaurant.desc: Wind Cries Mary is a west coast bar and restaurant tucked into 45 Bastion Square in Victoria's downtown core, built around a nose-to-tail menu that draws on local Vancouver Island farmers, foragers, fishmongers, and winemakers. The ever-changing sharing menu is complemented by a full bar program of local wines and craft cocktails. Outdoor seating is available on a front patio and in a hidden courtyard.

restaurant.name: Herald Street Brew Works
restaurant.desc: Herald Street Brew Works is a craft brewery and taproom in Victoria's Old Town, pouring tank-fresh beer directly from 10 bright tanks visible from nearly every seat in the tasting room. The brewery favours constant experimentation over core recipes, releasing an ever-changing lineup of ales, lagers, IPAs, and collaboration brews with neighbouring Victoria breweries. The multi-level space accommodates up to 150 guests and offers event bookings with catering through The Drake Eatery.

restaurant.name: Hyderabad Biryani House
restaurant.desc: Hyderabad Biryani House is a restaurant located on Fraser Street in Vancouver. Based on its name, it specializes in biryani, a traditional South Indian rice dish. Specific information about the restaurant's amenities and cyclist-friendly features is not available.

restaurant.name: Legato Cafe
restaurant.desc: Now operating as Khao Thai by Legato Cafe, this Thai restaurant and breakfast spot in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood serves an extensive menu of curries, noodles, stir-fries, and appetizers. The business has rebranded from its former identity as a general cafe while retaining the same West 41st Avenue location. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and online pickup ordering is offered for those wanting to grab food on the go.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu legend indicates vegetarian items; includes 'Vegetable Delight' and 'Thai Style Vegetarian Rice Cakes'

restaurant.name: Moon Wok
restaurant.desc: Moon Wok is a family-owned Chinese restaurant group with three Kamloops locations (North Shore, South Shore, and Valleyview), all fully licensed. The restaurant is well-known locally for fresh ingredients, no added MSG, and a broad menu including vegetarian and gluten-free options. Cyclists can order take-out, dine in, or arrange catering for group events.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: "Whether you're vegetarian or have food allergies, we have plenty of delicious menu choices to choose from. Be sure to ask about our gluten-free menu."

restaurant.name: Hero's Welcome
restaurant.desc: Hero's Welcome is a community pub on Main Street in Vancouver, occupying a space that housed the Army, Navy & Air Force Veterans Taurus Club Unit 298 from 1948 until 2019. Extensive renovations preserved and displayed irreplaceable veterans memorabilia alongside pieces sourced from the Canadian Military Archives, giving the room a distinctive historic character. Touring cyclists stopping in will find a full bar and food menu, bar games including pinball, pool, skeeball, and darts, and a regular live music program.

restaurant.name: Wally's Burgers
restaurant.desc: Wally's Burgers is a family-operated, seasonal burger stand with over 65 years of history, currently serving at Cates Park in North Vancouver. Known for classic burgers, loaded hot dogs, crispy sides, shakes, and the legendary Wally's Sauce — a recipe perfected over 50 years — it has been a gathering place for generations of Lower Mainland locals. The park setting and nostalgic menu make it a natural pit stop for cyclists exploring the North Shore.

restaurant.name: Obanhmi
restaurant.desc: Obanhmi is a sandwich shop on Kingsway, Vancouver's vibrant East Side arterial corridor, with a name that strongly suggests a Vietnamese bánh mì focus. Situated on a well-traveled cycling route connecting Burnaby to downtown Vancouver, it offers a convenient midpoint rest stop. The OSM record lists it as a sit-down restaurant with extended daily hours.

restaurant.name: Winfield Chinese
restaurant.desc: Winfield Chinese Restaurant is a long-established sit-down restaurant that has been serving the Winfield community for over a decade, offering a broad menu of authentic Chinese dishes alongside western options. Located on Highway 97 beside Tim Hortons, it sits on a major cycling corridor through the Okanagan. The menu spans appetizers, soups, chow mein, fried rice, and a dedicated vegetarian section, making it a versatile meal stop for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Kosoo
restaurant.desc: Kosoo Robson is a Korean fried chicken bar and casual dining restaurant situated along the bustling Robson Street corridor in downtown Vancouver, specializing in bone-in and boneless fried or oven-baked chicken in multiple sauces alongside traditional Korean BBQ and soul food. It is one of three Kosoo locations in the Vancouver area, each with a distinct menu focus. The restaurant offers dine-in with indoor seating and online ordering for takeout.

restaurant.name: Bliss Bakery
restaurant.desc: Bliss Bakery is a family-owned artisan bakehouse that has been operating on Okanagan Lake's shoreline in Peachland for over 20 years, producing slow-fermented sourdoughs, buttery croissants, and a full bistro lunch menu using only natural, preservative-free ingredients. The Peachland location sits on Beach Avenue with a lakeside patio and views of Okanagan Lake, making it a natural rest stop on any lakeshore cycling route. The sourdough starter — originally cultivated from Okanagan Valley grapes — has been in continuous use since the bakery opened in 2005.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website shop page lists a 'Vegetarian' category with 10 products

restaurant.name: Hungry Otters
restaurant.desc: Hungry Otters is a street food vendor on King George Boulevard in Surrey, serving an eclectic lineup of hot dogs, samosas, pierogies, and grilled cheese sandwiches. The stall accommodates a wide range of dietary needs, with vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, and sugar-free options all confirmed. Notably, the vendor accepts Bitcoin payments, making it one of the few street food stops in the region with crypto-friendly checkout.

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: Starbucks Coffee location on the University of British Columbia campus in the University Marketplace. Offers espresso drinks, coffee, and light food with outdoor seating available for customers.

restaurant.name: Davie's The Best
restaurant.desc: Davie's the Best is a Turkish and Mediterranean restaurant in Vancouver's West End, serving flame-grilled kebabs, fragrant rice pilaf, handcrafted mezzes, and Persian-influenced dishes. Opened just over a year ago as a family project, the restaurant also functions as an entertainment venue with live music and DJ nights. Cyclists in the area will find an extensive dine-in menu, online ordering with pickup and delivery, and both indoor and outdoor seating on Davie Street.

restaurant.name: Amoka
restaurant.desc: AMOKA Coffee & Bites is a neighborhood café and bakery in Vancouver's West End, serving handcrafted espresso drinks alongside freshly baked croissants, pastries, and savory breakfast sandwiches on Davie Street. The shop bakes fresh daily and never resells day-old items, making it a reliable morning fuel stop. Dine-in, pickup, and delivery are all available.

restaurant.name: PIVA Modern Italian
restaurant.desc: PIVA Modern Italian is a fine-dining restaurant on New Westminster's Columbia Street serving seasonal Italian cuisine — traditional dishes, meat, and seafood — alongside an extensive BC and Italian wine list and craft cocktails. The restaurant offers both indoor seating and a patio, and accommodates intimate dinners, weddings, and corporate events. Wheelchair accessible, it sits in the heart of a walkable downtown corridor convenient for cyclists passing through New Westminster.

restaurant.name: ZUBU Ramen
restaurant.desc: ZUBU Ramen is a multi-location Japanese restaurant group with four Lower Mainland outposts; the Kerrisdale location serves ramen, fresh temaki, hand-made gyoza, and rice bowls in a lively neighbourhood setting. Executive Chef William Cao trained at Kitchen Hyodo Ramen School in Oyama, Japan, and sources ingredients either locally or imported directly from Japan. The chain has received press coverage from the Vancouver Sun, WestCoast Families, and Montecristo Magazine since opening in 2020.

restaurant.name: J Kitchen Korean & Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: J Kitchen is a Korean and Japanese restaurant located in Sidney, BC, offering Asian cuisine in a community known as a popular stop on the Saanich Peninsula cycling circuit. Sidney's compact downtown makes it a natural refuelling point for cyclists riding the Gulf Islands ferry route or the Lochside Regional Trail. No further detail about the restaurant's interior, capacity, or cyclist amenities could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Wing Kee Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Wing Kee Restaurant is a restaurant located in Richmond, BC on Granville Avenue. No further details about cuisine style, dining format, or cyclist-relevant features could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Fishworks
restaurant.desc: Fishworks is a full-service West Coast seafood restaurant set in a heritage building in Lower Lonsdale, one block from the Lonsdale Quay SeaBus terminal — making it a natural stop for cyclists arriving from or departing to Vancouver by water. The menu is built around wild Pacific salmon, lingcod, locally farmed oysters, and shellfish, prepared with global influences ranging from Peruvian ceviche to Spanish paella to New England chowder. As a neighbourhood bakery, it would offer freshly baked goods to passing customers, making it a potential stop for cyclists seeking a snack or treat. No further details about the business's offerings or layout could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Tom Sushi
restaurant.desc: Tom Sushi is a premium Japanese restaurant on Davie Street in the heart of downtown Vancouver, founded in 2019 by Chef Tom Jeon, who brings over a decade of sushi expertise to a menu that blends traditional Japanese flavours with Pacific Northwest ingredients. The restaurant has been recognized by Yelp as the second-best rated restaurant in Canada. Its understated, elegant interior is designed for a relaxed dining experience, and an online ordering system is also available.

notes.Takeout: Website notes a bag charge for takeout orders ('we will need to charge $0.5 for each Kraft bag') and links to an online ordering menu at order.codefusion.tech/menu
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Not explicitly

restaurant.name: Java Cat
restaurant.desc: Java Cat is a café in Vancouver with indoor seating available to customers.

restaurant.name: Duffin's Donuts
restaurant.desc: Duffin's Donuts is a long-standing community donut shop in Vancouver's East Side, serving the neighbourhood for over four decades. The shop offers donuts, chicken, and sandwiches, making it a versatile quick-stop for cyclists needing a snack or light meal. Indoor seating and air conditioning provide a comfortable place to rest mid-ride.

restaurant.name: Anna's Cake House
restaurant.desc: Anna's Cake House is a beloved family-owned Hong Kong-style bakery founded in 1974 by Anna, Ronald, and Kathleen Cheung, now celebrating 50 years of operation across four Greater Vancouver locations. The Richmond outpost sits inside Lansdowne Mall and offers freshly baked, made-to-order cakes in over 15 flavours — made daily with no artificial additives, using Canadian butter and cream. Cyclists looking for a sweet stop will find a well-established community institution known for Hong Kong-style buns and layered cream cakes.

restaurant.name: Kwong Tung Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kwong Tung Seafood Restaurant is a traditional Chinese seafood and dim sum restaurant located on the second floor of a building on Fisgard Street in Victoria's Chinatown district. The menu features live seafood, Shanghai dumplings, sticky rice, BBQ pork buns, and specialty hot pots, with a notable range of vegetarian and vegan options. It is a well-established local favourite praised for generous portions and fast, friendly service.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'extensive range of vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options available on the menu'; services page lists vegetarian fried rice, chow mein, and steamed Bao as examples

restaurant.name: duft & co. bakehouse
restaurant.desc: Duft & Co. Bakehouse is an artisan café and bakehouse in Abbotsford run by a husband-and-wife team, offering handcrafted pastries, seasonal sandwiches on house-made bread, and custom-roasted coffee without additives or preservatives. The kitchen produces small batches daily — including almond croissants, cinnamon buns, and Saturday doughnuts — and closes once sold out, so early-arriving cyclists are rewarded. All ingredients are locally sourced from the Fraser Valley, giving the menu a strong regional character.

detail.address: Unit #103 - 2636 Montrose Ave, Abbotsford, BC V2S 3T6

restaurant.name: Nanoose Bay Cafe Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A family-run, marina-side restaurant and coffee shop on Vancouver Island offering locally-sourced brunch, lunch, and dinner alongside a Best of BC Marketplace stocked with local artisan goods. The cafe sits roughly 20 minutes from Parksville and doubles as Nanoose Bay's main dining destination, with an outdoor waterfront setting that hosts a live music series. On-site accommodation through the adjacent Fairwinds Residences makes it a potential overnight stop for touring cyclists.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu pages carry an explicit legend 'VG - Vegan GF - Gluten-free' with those labels applied to a wide range of dishes across brunch, lunch, all-day, and happy hour menus

restaurant.name: Gyu King Teppanyaki
restaurant.desc: Gyu King Teppanyaki is a Japanese teppanyaki restaurant located on Burrard Street in downtown Vancouver. The restaurant specializes in teppanyaki-style cooking — meats, seafood, and vegetables prepared on large tabletop iron grills. Its central downtown location makes it a convenient dining stop for cyclists moving through the core of the city.

restaurant.name: Paradise Donair
restaurant.desc: Paradise Donair has been a New Westminster neighbourhood staple since 1998, specializing in beef, chicken, lamb, and falafel donair wraps, platters, and salads made to order. Located on 12th Street, it has established itself as a community fixture known for fresh ingredients and a broad menu that spans quick bites to full platters. Appetizers such as dolmades, samosas, and spring rolls round out the offering for cyclists looking for a complete meal stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian options confirmed: Falafel Donair Platter, Falafel Donair Wrap, Falafel Donair Salad, and Veggie Samosas. Vegan and gluten-free status not mentioned

restaurant.name: PureBread
restaurant.desc: PureBread is a celebrated artisan bakery with roots in Whistler and locations now spanning Squamish, Vancouver, and YVR Airport. The Function Junction outpost is a take-away-only spot where cyclists can stock up on fresh-baked breads, pastries, and sweets before or after hitting the trails. The bakery has earned coverage in the New York Times, Lonely Planet, and Vogue, cementing its status as a culinary landmark in the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

notes.Takeout: Website /find-us page explicitly describes Function Junction location as 'take-away only'

restaurant.name: Joey
restaurant.desc: JOEY Burnaby is an upscale-casual chain restaurant in Burnaby's Brentwood neighbourhood, built around modern interiors with handmade lighting and a rooftop patio. Part of the family-owned JOEY Restaurants group operating since 1992, this location serves a globally inspired menu alongside handcrafted cocktails and maintains a dedicated private event space. The restaurant is wheelchair accessible and offers both indoor and outdoor patio seating.

restaurant.name: Caffe Barney
restaurant.desc: Since 1988, Caffe Barney has been a neighbourhood institution on South Granville, serving brunch, lunch, dinner, and late-night comfort food in a warm, artsy interior with a street-facing patio. The kitchen prepares everything in-house and the bar pours a rotating selection of twelve local craft beers on tap alongside cocktails and wine. Situated minutes from Kits Beach and downtown Vancouver, it is a well-positioned refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the South Granville corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu labels 'Veggie Breakfast Burrito' and ''Shrooms on Toast' as Vegetarian; brunch section header states 'Substitute bread for gluten free option'

restaurant.name: NHAU
restaurant.desc: NHAU is a Vietnamese restaurant located in central Campbell River, offering traditional cuisine in a sit-down dining setting. It serves as a convenient dining option for touring cyclists traveling through the community.

restaurant.name: Levantine
restaurant.desc: Levantine is a Syrian Middle Eastern restaurant in Victoria dedicated to authentic cuisine, from shawarma and kebabs to traditional breakfast plates and freshly made pastries. The menu spans a wide range of dishes rooted in Syrian culinary heritage, making it a satisfying and distinctive stop for cyclists seeking a substantial meal. Warm hospitality and a focus on genuine flavours set it apart from generic Mediterranean spots.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels Fresh Falafel wrap as 'vegan'; falafel platter, Fattoush salad, Tabbouleh salad, and Zaatar/Muhammara pastries are additional plant-based options

restaurant.name: Vogue Cakes
restaurant.desc: Vogue Cakes is a fully vegan bakery on West Broadway in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood. The shop specialises in vegan cakes and baked goods, which could offer a convenient sweet stop for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Go-Go Sushi & Cafe
restaurant.desc: Go-Go Sushi & Cafe is a sushi restaurant in Delta offering online ordering and takeout options, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through Tsawwassen.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast-food restaurant located in a unit at 1581 Hillside Avenue in Victoria, offering burger-focused fare. The location features a drive-through as well as curbside and delivery options, making it a convenient stop for a quick meal. As a high-volume chain location in an urban Victoria neighbourhood, it serves as a reliable resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Burgoo
restaurant.desc: Burgoo is a cosy comfort-food bistro group with three Vancouver neighbourhoods represented; the Downtown location sits at 1100 Burrard Street and has been part of the city's dining scene since the original Point Grey bistro opened in 2001. The menu leans into hearty, warming dishes — French onion soup, poutine, mac and cheese, and stews — in an old-world countryside atmosphere using earth tones and natural materials. Cyclists will find a full sit-down experience as well as takeout and delivery options, with vegetarian dishes woven throughout the menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Hummus & Flatbread, Guacamole, F.A.B. Salad, Mac & Cheese, and Kale Caesar; no gluten-free labelling found on menu

restaurant.name: Orange Julius
restaurant.desc: Orange Julius / Dairy Queen is a combination fast-food outlet inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre, Kelowna's largest indoor mall with over 170 stores. The location serves the brand's signature Orange Julius beverages, Julius Juicers fresh-squeezed juice, and smoothies alongside Dairy Queen classics including Blizzards, DQ Cakes, and hot dogs. It sits along the busy Harvey Avenue commercial corridor, making it a convenient mid-ride refreshment stop for cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: Congee Noodle House
restaurant.desc: Congee Noodle House has been serving refined Cantonese cuisine on East Broadway since 1998, specializing in congee, hand-pulled rice noodle rolls, and roasted meats including signature crispy roast pork and roast duck. The single-storey restaurant features jade-themed décor and an immersive dining atmosphere inspired by Chinese tea culture. Online ordering is available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists looking for a hearty Cantonese meal in the heart of Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Crêpe Montagne
restaurant.desc: Crêpe Montagne has been serving locally crafted French-style food in Whistler's village since 1997, specializing in both sweet crepes (wheat flour) and savoury crepes (white and buckwheat flour). The menu extends to fondue, raclette, salads, and full breakfast plates, with both indoor seating and a patio. It is a walk-in-only spot with online ordering available for delivery and pickup.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'We offer delivery and takeaway' with prominent 'ORDER DELIVERY' and 'ORDER PICK UP' buttons throughout; not all items available online

restaurant.name: Chongqing
restaurant.desc: ChongQing is a long-established Szechuan-style Chinese restaurant in Surrey, BC, with over twenty years of operation focused on authentic spicy and flavourful dishes. The restaurant offers both dine-in and takeout, with featured items including Honey Garlic Sliced Pork and Noodle Soup with Mixed Meat & Seafood. It sits in a strip-mall plaza on 120th Street (Scott Road), a major arterial route through South Surrey and Delta.

restaurant.name: The Vine
restaurant.desc: The Vine is a restaurant in the Duncan/Cowichan Valley area of Vancouver Island, BC. It maintains an Instagram presence under the handle @thevinecowichan, suggesting a local identity tied to the Cowichan region. Beyond that, no further detail about the establishment's style, cuisine, or offerings could be confirmed from available sources.

detail.address: 1765 Cowichan Bay Rd, Cowichan Bay, BC V9L 6N2, Canada

restaurant.name: Café 106
restaurant.desc: Café 106 is a specialty coffee shop tucked into a commercial unit on Royal Oak Avenue in Burnaby, emphasizing quality beans and made-to-order preparation. The café offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a relaxed stop for cyclists passing through the Royal Oak corridor. Online ordering is available for those wanting a quick grab-and-go.

detail.address: 106-6588 Royal Oak Ave, Burnaby, BC V5H 2E6

restaurant.name: roast
restaurant.desc: Roast is a Victoria sandwich shop that has been crafting fast-casual meals from locally sourced, naturally raised BC meats since 2013, with a menu centred on beef, porchetta, chicken, and veggie sandwiches alongside superfood salads. The Uptown location is one of two active Victoria outlets, situated in a shopping centre setting convenient for a midday stop on a city or suburban ride. The shop is notably BC's first sandwich shop to offer living wages and runs a reusable container program in partnership with the Bread and Butter Collective.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Fresh meat and greens are ready to go, all day. Pop by for your next lunch break, we'll get something delicious in your hand in no time.'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'Veggie' as a sandwich option alongside meat options; superfood salads also featured. No explicit vegan or GF claims

restaurant.name: Jin Jiang Shanghai Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Jin Jiang Shanghai Restaurant is a sit-down restaurant on Kingsway in Burnaby specializing in traditional Shanghai cuisine, including Shengjianbao (pan-fried pork buns), Malan head, and Drunken Chicken. The restaurant emphasizes fresh, high-quality ingredients and a professional chef team blending heritage recipes with innovation. It offers both dine-in and online ordering for cyclists looking for a substantial meal along a busy urban corridor.

restaurant.name: Uni Modern Japanese
restaurant.desc: Uni Modern Japanese is a Japanese restaurant on Victoria's Wharf Street, near the Inner Harbour waterfront. The restaurant offers dine-in and online ordering with pickup, making it a convenient stop along the harbour cycling corridor. A welcoming spot for cyclists looking for a Japanese meal in the heart of downtown Victoria.

restaurant.name: Berry Good
restaurant.desc: Berry Good Cafe is a Richmond dessert café proudly operating since 2006, founded by Ivy, a former pastry chef at a Michelin-starred restaurant. The café specializes in freshly baked cakes and pastries made daily from scratch using real butter, fresh cream, and minimal sugar and artificial additives. It also hosts private high tea parties for special occasions, making it a distinctive sweet stop on any Richmond cycling route.

restaurant.name: Witchcraft Beer Market and Bistro
restaurant.desc: Witchcraft Beer Market and Bistro is a neighbourhood pub operated by the Springs Group in Maple Ridge, pouring 40 craft beers on tap sourced from BC breweries and beyond. The kitchen centres on a wood-burning forno oven hand-crafted in Naples, turning out Neapolitan-inspired pizzas made with local organic flour alongside hearty comfort food. The rustic, welcoming space includes a patio and regular live music nights, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring the Fraser Valley corridor.

detail.address: 22648 Dewdney Trunk Road, Maple Ridge, BC V2X 3K1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'We are vegetarian-friendly, and offer gluten free options' (front page and About page)

restaurant.name: Firepit Pizza
restaurant.desc: Firepit Pizza is a Surrey pizzeria operating since 2009, distinguished by its 'Desi Flavours' lineup of Indian-inspired toppings such as Chicken Tandoori and Butter Chicken alongside classic options. Located along the Fraser Highway corridor, it offers both phone and online ordering with local delivery and in-store pickup. Vegetarian pizza options are a regular part of the menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists dedicated vegetarian options: 'Veggie' and 'Ultimate Veg' pizzas

restaurant.name: Inasal House
restaurant.desc: Inasal House is a Filipino restaurant on Saanich Road in Victoria serving cuisine centred on inasal, the beloved Philippine tradition of marinated, char-grilled meat. It is one of the relatively few Filipino eateries in Greater Victoria, making it a distinctive stop for cyclists riding through the Saanich peninsula. The casual, community-oriented nature typical of inasal restaurants makes it a welcoming spot for hungry riders.

restaurant.name: Shilla Korean
restaurant.desc: Shilla Korean is a Korean restaurant located on Kingsway in Vancouver, a commercial corridor well-travelled by cyclists crossing the city. The restaurant offers Korean cuisine and sits in a dense urban neighbourhood with a variety of services nearby. Touring cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor may find it a convenient stop for a full sit-down meal.

restaurant.name: Burger Crush
restaurant.desc: Burger Crush is a fast-casual burger chain with three BC locations, serving smashed Canadian Angus beef burgers, house-made vegan patties, tofu nuggets, and dairy or cashew-milk shakes. Founded by self-described kids of the 80s, it aims to revive the stress-free classic burger shop experience. The Vancouver location on Nelson Street offers both pickup and delivery, with indoor seating in an air-conditioned, wheelchair-accessible space.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Vegan Cheeseburger (vegan bun, vegan patty, vegan cheese, vegan sauce), Veggie Style Cheeseburger, Vegan Nuggets (house-made tofu), vegan shakes, and vegan dip options. No gluten-free claim found on website

restaurant.name: Anh And Chi
restaurant.desc: Anh and Chi is a Michelin Bib Gourmand-recognized Vietnamese restaurant (2022–2025) on Vancouver's Main Street, run by a Vietnamese-Canadian family whose parents founded the city's first pho house. The brother-and-sister team, with their mother as Executive Chef, reimagines authentic Vietnamese cuisine using fresh local ingredients in an award-winning room and patio in the Mount Pleasant neighbourhood. It has raised over $500,000 for local nonprofits through its reservation-by-donation program.

restaurant.name: One Restaurant
restaurant.desc: One Restaurant is the casual, family-friendly dining room within Woodlands Inn & Suites, one of Fort Nelson's primary accommodation hubs along the Alaska Highway. Dinner offerings span house classics like pork schnitzel, butter chicken, fish and chips, and prime rib, plus daily specials — a welcome spread after long riding days on the highway corridor. The adjacent 1 Lounge provides an evening wind-down option with cocktails, mocktails, and light bites like steak sandwiches and rib burgers.

restaurant.name: Kelly O'Bryan's & Carlos O'Bryan's Pub
restaurant.desc: Kelly & Carlos O'Bryan's is a lively Irish-themed neighborhood pub and restaurant occupying an iconic building in downtown New Westminster, one stop on a chain of BC locations. The venue features both indoor and outdoor patio seating, regular live music on the patio, trivia nights, karaoke, and a broad pub menu including a kids' menu — making it a sociable stop for groups of cyclists. Its central Columbia Street location puts it within easy reach of the New Westminster waterfront cycling routes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Kids menu page states 'Gluten Friendly Items marked with this symbol are gluten friendly. Please inform your server of any food sensitivities and allergies.' GF options confirmed; vegetarian/vegan not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: Misty Pines Cafe & Bakery
restaurant.desc: Misty Pines Cafe & Bakery is a local café and bakery located in Nanaimo at 335 Wesley Street. As a combined café and bakery, it would offer touring cyclists a spot to stop for baked goods and café beverages in a community setting. The business operates seven days a week according to OSM.

restaurant.name: Bonpot
restaurant.desc: Bonpot (本锅) is a Chinese restaurant in Richmond's Alexandra Road food corridor, specialising in hot pot dining. It sits in a unit within a commercial plaza, placing it among the dense concentration of Asian restaurants that make this stretch a notable food destination for cyclists riding through Richmond.

restaurant.name: Nanoose Bay Cafe Coffeeshop
restaurant.desc: The Nanoose Bay Cafe Coffee Shop is a marina-side morning destination at Schooner Cove, serving locally-roasted French Press Coffee Roasters beans alongside house-made light fare and artisan goods from the on-site Marketplace. It is the coffee-focused daytime arm of a larger full-service restaurant and bar operation that also offers brunch, lunch, happy hour, and dinner. The work-friendly setup — with power outlets at nearly every seat and a Kids' Corner — makes it a practical stop for touring cyclists passing through the Parksville–Nanaimo corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu items throughout all pages are labeled 'VG GF' (vegan and gluten-free options); includes items such as Korean Fried Cauliflower, Chickpea Hummus, Buffalo Cauliflower Wrap, and Fried Eggplant
notes.Device charging: Website states: 'We've got power outlets at nearly every seat.'

restaurant.name: Sushi Valley
restaurant.desc: A Japanese sushi restaurant located in Kamloops on the Trans-Canada Highway. Offers online takeout ordering for customer convenience. A suitable dining option for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Indian Roti Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Indian Roti Kitchen bills itself as Vancouver's first East Indian roti shop, serving a focused menu of roti wraps filled with classic Indian curries — from dal and channa to butter chicken and lamb vindaloo. The Cambie Street location operates as a takeout-only spot, making it a quick and hearty refuelling option for cyclists passing through the neighbourhood. The menu features an extensive vegetarian section alongside meat and shrimp options.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Take-out Only'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian Rotis' section with over a dozen options including Dal Pakora Roti, Channa Curry Roti, Saag Paneer Roti, and others

restaurant.name: Spoons Diner
restaurant.desc: A casual breakfast and comfort food diner located on Victoria's Douglas Street. Offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it accessible for cyclists who want to sit down for a meal. Serves homemade comfort food in a traditional neighborhood diner setting.

detail.address: 2915 Douglas St. Victoria, BC CA V8T 4M8

restaurant.name: Comma Cafe
restaurant.desc: Comma Cafe is a non-smoking cafe in Vancouver. It has a changing table on-site, suggesting a family-friendly environment. Beyond these OSM-recorded details, specific information about its menu, seating, or character is unavailable as the business's Instagram profile requires a login to view.

detail.address: 3208 Oak St, Vancouver, BC V6H 2L3, Canada

restaurant.name: My Sushi
restaurant.desc: My Sushi is a Japanese-inspired restaurant in Fort St. John serving sushi rolls, miso soup, and pho. Located on 100 Street in the city centre, it offers both dine-in and online ordering with pickup and delivery. The menu blends Japanese staples with Vietnamese dishes, giving touring cyclists a solid hot-meal option in the Peace River region.

restaurant.name: Mariner Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: Mariner Brewing is a community-focused craft brewery in Coquitlam that brews under the motto 'Made to Explore' — a fitting ethos for cycling visitors. The taproom pairs a rotating house beer lineup with a food program specializing in smash burgers, and an outdoor patio that welcomes dogs. Growler fills are available with a frequently changing lineup, making it easy to carry local craft beer onward.

restaurant.name: Pad Thai Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Pad Thai Restaurant is a family-owned Thai eatery in Pitt Meadows operated by sisters Jenny and Jessie Trakulthongroj since December 1999, built on treasured family recipes adapted for a modern palate. The restaurant has earned multiple Times Readers Choice awards for Best Thai Restaurant in the Pitt Meadows/Maple Ridge area and has developed a loyal following across the Tri-cities region. Touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley corridor will find a warm, established dining room serving signature dishes like house Pad Thai and Tom Yum Koong, with online ordering also available.

restaurant.name: KINTON RAMEN
restaurant.desc: KINTON RAMEN Victoria Downtown is a Japanese ramen chain restaurant situated on Wharf Street in Victoria's Inner Harbour, surrounded by waterfront views and local attractions. Part of one of the largest ramen chains in North America with over 50 locations across Canada and the US, it serves customizable ramen bowls with a choice of pork, beef, chicken, or vegetarian broth. A touring cyclist finishing a ride along the waterfront will find a warm, casual sit-down meal with online ordering also available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page states 'vegetarian options' available; menu lists Veggie as a soup base choice and veggie as a protein option

restaurant.name: Coquitlam Grill
restaurant.desc: Coquitlam Grill is a diner and burger restaurant serving American cuisine, breakfast, and classic diner fare. The restaurant offers free parking and accepts takeout orders. Located in Coquitlam, it provides a casual dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

detail.address: 2635 Barnet Hwy Unit 108 Coquitlam BC V3E 1K9

restaurant.name: Saint Cecilia
restaurant.desc: Saint Cecilia is a specialty coffee and made-to-order soft-serve ice cream shop in downtown Victoria built around a stay-awhile philosophy — guests are encouraged to bring a book or laptop and settle in. The coffee program rotates weekly through diverse roasters and origins, served as espresso or hand brew, while the ice cream uses locally produced bases from Parachute Ice Cream with fruit sourced from named BC farms. The shop also stocks slow-fashion garments and home-brew coffee equipment, giving it a curated neighbourhood feel well beyond a standard café.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists Vegan Coconut ice cream base, Cowgirl Cookie (Vegan/GF), and oat milk available for espresso and hot chocolate drinks

restaurant.name: Church's Chicken
restaurant.desc: Church's Chicken is a fast-food chain location on Kingsway in Vancouver serving fried chicken meals, sandwiches, and sides. The local franchise operates under the brand 'Church's Texas Chicken™' and emphasizes hand-crafted, Texas-style fried chicken for the Lower Mainland market. It offers drive-through and indoor seating in a single-storey retail building.

restaurant.name: The Sticky Wicket
restaurant.desc: The Sticky Wicket bills itself as Vancouver Island's biggest pub, occupying multiple distinct rooms — including a cricket-themed main floor, a rooftop patio, a games room with pool and darts, and a large live music venue — all within the historic Strathcona Hotel complex in the heart of downtown Victoria. Operating since 1913, it offers a full food menu including a kids menu and late-night options alongside an active calendar of live music and special events. A touring cyclist rolling into downtown Victoria would find this a substantial refuelling stop with plenty of seating options.

restaurant.name: The Pie Hole
restaurant.desc: The Pie Hole is a BC-born specialty pie bakery founded by Jenell Parsons in 2011, expanding from farmers markets and food trucks to three brick-and-mortar locations across Greater Vancouver. The West Broadway location offers a rotating menu of both sweet and savory pies — from Vietnamese Coffee Pie to Thai Chicken and Mac & Cheese — made from scratch with locally sourced produce, dairy, and free-range eggs. Parsons has been featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives and has earned the nickname Canada's Pie Queen.

restaurant.name: Drama Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Drama Hot Pot is a Chinese hot pot restaurant located in a commercial complex in Richmond, BC. Hot pot dining is a communal, interactive format where diners cook meats, vegetables, and other ingredients in a simmering broth at the table — a popular and social dining tradition. Richmond is well known for its concentration of authentic Asian restaurants, and this spot sits in a mixed-use development near the city's southern neighbourhoods.

restaurant.name: The Lion Rampant Scottish Pub
restaurant.desc: The Lion Rampant is a Scottish-themed pub in Maple Bay in the Cowichan Valley, founded by two Scottish-born partners and built inside the former Brigantine Pub. The space was redesigned by TV celebrity designer Nancy Hadley and the menu crafted by chef Brian Duffy of Bar Rescue fame, giving it an unusually polished pedigree for a rural Vancouver Island pub. It is known for a patio with an 'unparalleled view' of the bay, a locally sourced menu ranging from Cullen Skink to seafood mains, and live music every weekend.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'celiac-friendly items' are offered; menu includes a Black Bean Veggie Burger as a vegetarian option

restaurant.name: 1914 Coffee Company
restaurant.desc: 1914 Coffee Company is a café located in downtown Squamish, a well-known hub for outdoor recreation and a common stop on cycling routes through the Sea-to-Sky corridor. The name likely references a historical theme tied to Squamish's early settlement era. Touring cyclists passing through Squamish on Highway 99 or the Sea-to-Sky Greenway would find it a convenient spot to rest.

restaurant.name: The Office Pub & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Office Pub & Grill is a neighbourhood pub and full-service restaurant in the Valleyview area of Kamloops, serving all-day breakfast alongside classic pub fare like wings, poutine, and burgers. The space features two separate dining rooms accommodating up to 30 people and a patio, making it a viable stop for cycling groups. Customer reviews highlight generous portions and attentive service, including at least one reviewer who specifically noted stopping in after a long drive.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'From classic burgers to vegan options, there's something to satisfy every craving and taste preference.'

restaurant.name: Sushi Garden
restaurant.desc: Sushi Garden is a popular Japanese restaurant chain with three Burnaby locations, of which the Metro Town branch sits on the busy Kingsway corridor near Metrotown mall. The restaurant offers indoor seating and online ordering for takeout. Its accessible location along a major urban cycling route makes it a convenient stop for riders passing through the Metrotown area.

restaurant.name: Gene Coffee Bar
restaurant.desc: Gene Coffee Bar is a neighbourhood café on Main Street in Vancouver focused on specialty espresso drinks, organic pastries, and an unhurried atmosphere designed for staying a while. The space features window seating with natural light, communal benches, and a notably generous supply of power outlets popular with laptop users. Cyclists can fuel up on all-day breakfast wraps, croissant sandwiches, and a range of vegan and gluten-free baked goods.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Explicit vegan options (milk alternatives, vegan loaves, cakes, cookies, vegan tofu wrap); gluten-free cookies from Epicurean listed on menu
notes.Device charging: Website states 'abundance of charging outlet while working on your laptop.'

restaurant.name: Pho Boi A Taste of Vietnam
restaurant.desc: Phở Bội is a Vietnamese restaurant in Nanaimo serving a broad menu of traditional pho, vermicelli bowls, and appetizers rooted in the five-taste profile of Vietnamese cuisine. The restaurant emphasizes fresh ingredients, herbs, and vegetables, offering both hearty beef-broth noodle soups and lighter options. It is a sit-down neighbourhood restaurant with an extensive menu that could satisfy a hungry touring cyclist looking for a filling, flavourful meal.

detail.address: Unit 108 - 6596 Applecross Road, Nanaimo, BC V9V 0A4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists '00. Phở Chay Vegetable' and a tofu curry option ('S8. Cari...Tofu'), confirming vegetarian and vegan-friendly dishes are available

restaurant.name: Browns Socialhouse
restaurant.desc: Browns Socialhouse is a proudly Canadian franchise chain with over 80 locations, describing itself as the balance between a neighbourhood pub and upscale casual dining. The Cambie Street location sits in downtown Vancouver near the Queen Elizabeth Theatre precinct and offers both indoor and outdoor seating. Touring cyclists would find a full-service sit-down meal with a broad menu in a central urban location.

restaurant.name: Public Liquor
restaurant.desc: Public Liquor is a locally owned Kelowna retail shop specializing in curated BC craft beers, Okanagan wines, and artisan spirits, with a stated mission to showcase local winemakers, distillers, and brewers. Proudly rooted in the Kelowna community, it positions itself as a destination for discovering regional craft beverages rather than a generic off-licence. Online ordering with in-store pickup and delivery to Kelowna and Lake Country are also available.

restaurant.name: Bad Tattoo
restaurant.desc: Bad Tattoo is a craft brewery, restaurant, and bar in Penticton, BC — a hub of Okanagan cycling routes including the KVR trail and Kettle Valley Rail Trail. The brewery produces its own beer on-site, making it a natural post-ride destination in one of BC's most popular cycling regions. Touring cyclists passing through Penticton will find it a full-service stop combining food, drink, and locally made craft beer.

restaurant.name: Veranda
