restaurant.desc: Pick Thai is an authentic Thai restaurant situated in the heart of downtown Kelowna on Bernard Avenue, a short walk from City Park and the lakefront. The menu spans Thai street-food staples — like Moo Ping BBQ pork skewers and Papaya Salad — through northern Thai specialties such as Kao Soy Yellow Curry Noodle, plus hot pot available daily. Summer brings patio seating along one of Kelowna's main pedestrian corridors, and the kitchen offers catering for groups.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Front page: 'Yes, we do offer vegetarian and vegan options!'; About Us page: 'equipped to accommodate all major dietary restrictions (including vegetarian, vegan, and gluten free) for most of our dishes'

restaurant.name: Top Hat Pizza
restaurant.desc: Top Hat Pizza is a pizza restaurant located in Squamish, BC, a well-known gateway community for cyclists exploring the Sea-to-Sky corridor. As a sit-down or takeout pizza spot in a busy outdoor recreation town, it could serve as a refuelling stop for touring cyclists passing through.

detail.address: 40386 Tantalus Rd, Squamish, BC V8B 0P3, Canada

restaurant.name: Opa! of Greece
restaurant.desc: Opa! of Greece is a Greek fast-food concept located inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre, Kelowna's large regional mall on Harvey Avenue. The chain is known for fresh, Mediterranean-style wraps, salads, and souvlaki made to order. A cyclist stopping here would find a quick, filling meal in an air-conditioned mall environment with seating in the common areas.

restaurant.name: Sushi Sen
restaurant.desc: Sushi Sen is a Japanese sushi restaurant situated in Garibaldi Highlands, a neighbourhood east of downtown Squamish along the Sea-to-Sky corridor. The restaurant offers both dine-in and online ordering, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area. OSM records it as wheelchair accessible.

restaurant.name: Bon Cafe
restaurant.desc: Bon Cafe is a neighbourhood Vietnamese restaurant in Vancouver's Little Mountain area, a short ride from Queen Elizabeth Park at the corner of Main Street and E. 33rd Ave. The menu centres on pho, banh mi, and Vietnamese coffee, with reviewers consistently praising generous portions and solid value. Both dine-in and takeout are available, making it a practical pit-stop on the Main Street cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Tequila Cocina
restaurant.desc: Tequila Cocina is an authentic Mexican restaurant on the south end of Granville Street in downtown Vancouver, adjacent to the Davie Street entertainment district and close to the SkyTrain. The restaurant offers a lively atmosphere with indoor and outdoor seating, a full bar, and a menu of locally-made Mexican food. Takeout and delivery are also available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists moving through the downtown core.

restaurant.name: Creekside Coffee Factory
restaurant.desc: Creekside Coffee Factory is a neighbourhood café and in-house roastery in Coquitlam's Westwood area, roasting its own beans on-site and emphasising community warmth over chain-style efficiency. Customer reviews highlight a cozy, welcoming atmosphere well-suited to lingering — a handy stop on the Lougheed corridor for touring cyclists passing through the Tri-Cities.

restaurant.name: Matadora Taperia
restaurant.desc: Matadora Taperia is an award-winning Spanish tapas restaurant in Victoria's Historic Chinatown, founded in 2020 by mother-and-daughter team Veerle Peeters and Vanessa Davies. The kitchen imports ingredients directly from Spain and makes everything in-house, from croquetas to Basque cheesecake, alongside what the restaurant describes as BC's largest Spanish vermouth selection and Victoria's first vermouth flight. A Yam Magazine Best Restaurant Award winner, it offers a distinctly Spanish atmosphere in one of the most culturally vibrant blocks in Victoria.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu uses V (vegetarian), VG (vegan), and GF (Gluten-Friendly) markers on multiple items, including Aceitunas, Marcona Almonds, Patatas Bravas, and others

restaurant.name: Grand Honour
restaurant.desc: Grand Honour is a Chinese restaurant located on Granville Street in South Vancouver, offering both lunch and dinner service. It operates out of a ground-floor unit in a mixed-use building and seats guests indoors. Cyclists riding the Granville corridor would find it a convenient stop for a sit-down Chinese meal.

detail.address: B1-5701 Granville Street, Vancouver, British Columbia, V6M 4J7

restaurant.name: Panago
restaurant.desc: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain franchise located in the Lake Hill neighbourhood near McKenzie Avenue and Borden Street, serving the broader Saanich area. They emphasize quality ingredients including antibiotic-free chicken and pork, 100% organic tomato sauce, and dough made fresh daily. In addition to pizzas, the menu includes wings, salads, sides, and desserts, with delivery available across a wide swath of Saanich.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Panago offers vegan, vegetarian and gluten-smart options.'

restaurant.name: Alderlea Farm and Cafe
restaurant.desc: Alderlea Farm and Cafe is a multi-generational biodynamic family farm in the Cowichan Valley that has been running a wood-fired, farm-to-table restaurant for seventeen years, growing much of the food served on-site. The café is now helmed by the second generation of the founding family and features an expanded outdoor dining area, making it a genuine destination meal stop in the Cowichan Valley. Beyond the café, the farm also offers CSA harvest boxes and year-round farm stays.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists veggie burgers alongside grass-fed beef burgers; gluten-free and dairy-free pizza is available on request ('Make any pizza gluten or dairy free for an additional cost'). Vegetarian pizza options also present (Spinach Delight, The Forager, Margarita)

restaurant.name: Firehouse Subs
restaurant.desc: Firehouse Subs is a Canadian franchise of the American fast-casual sandwich chain, specializing in hot subs with a first-responder-themed brand identity. This Tsawwassen location sits at 4949 Canoe Pass Way in the Tsawwassen Mills retail area and offers dine-in, delivery, and mobile ordering. Touring cyclists in the area will find a familiar, quick-service meal stop with indoor seating and a broad sub menu.

detail.address: 4949 Canoe Pass Way, Delta, BC V4M 0B2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website homepage references a 'Gluten Free Roll' option in the navigation/footer area

restaurant.name: Indian Grill's
restaurant.desc: Indian Grill is a North Indian and Punjabi restaurant at the corner of Milton and Albert Streets in downtown Nanaimo, serving dishes freshly made with traditional spices including tandoori items pulled from a clay oven, biryanis, and creamy curries. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, online ordering, and catering, and has earned a 95%+ quality score and a ranking among the top 1% of Canadian restaurants in its category. Its central downtown location makes it a practical meal stop for cyclists passing through Nanaimo.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegetarian dishes listed: Aloo Gobhi, Dal Makhani, Vegetable Mixed Pakora, Chole Bhature, Amritsari Kulcha. No vegan or GF claims confirmed

restaurant.name: Murray's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Murray's Pizza is a beloved Okanagan pizza chain that has been serving the region since 1994, with locations across Summerland, West Kelowna, Oliver, Peachland, and Kelowna. Beyond pizzas, the menu spans calzones, baby back ribs, baked lasagna, donairs, and salads, offering a wide range of options for hungry cyclists. The Kelowna location on Summit Drive is one of several community anchors this local chain has built across the valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Customer testimonial on website states 'Great gluten free crust!', confirming gluten-free pizza crust is offered

restaurant.name: Kekuli Cafe Indigenous Cuisine
restaurant.desc: An indigenous-inspired cafe in Merritt serving bannock and coffee alongside other Indigenous cuisine. Operated by Elijah Mack, it offers takeout service for touring cyclists seeking a cultural dining break.

restaurant.name: Milk & Honey Café
restaurant.desc: Milk & Honey Café is a Vancouver café offering food and beverage service with online ordering capability.

restaurant.name: Pho Super Bowl
restaurant.desc: Pho Super Bowl is a Vietnamese restaurant serving fresh, aromatic pho and a broad menu of noodle soups, vermicelli bowls, rice plates, and appetizers at its Coquitlam strip-mall location. The restaurant emphasises house-made broth developed over years of recipe refinement and offers delivery in addition to dine-in service. A second location operates in Burnaby, making this a small local chain with a loyal following in the Metro Vancouver area.

restaurant.name: Torimaru
restaurant.desc: Torimaru is a fast food restaurant in Vancouver specializing in chicken, formerly operating under the name Canra Plus. The Instagram handle 'torimaruramen' hints at a Japanese-influenced concept, likely centred on chicken ramen or related dishes. It is a no-drive-through location, suggesting a walk-in counter-service format typical of quick-service ramen spots.

restaurant.name: The Blue Parrot Coffee
restaurant.desc: Founded in 1979 and named after the rival bar in Casablanca, The Blue Parrot Coffee is a family-owned café tucked inside the Granville Island Public Market, offering what many consider the best espresso in Metro Vancouver using Italian La Cimbali machines. The Granville Island location boasts a spectacular vantage point with views of the mountains, ocean, and downtown Vancouver — a natural rest stop on one of Vancouver's most popular cycling corridors. The business operates as a certified 'Beyond Green™' enterprise, prioritizing eco-friendly practices and organic coffees.

restaurant.name: Pho Zen Vietnamese Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Phở Zen is a Vietnamese restaurant opened in 2023 on Southeast Marine Drive in Vancouver, specializing in traditional beef noodle soup made with house-crafted broth, rice noodles, and fresh herbs including Thai basil and culantro. The menu emphasizes seasonal Vietnamese dishes and drinks alongside the core phở program, and the restaurant operates as both a sit-down dining room and bar. Online ordering is available for those wanting a quick stop.

detail.address: 654 SE Marine Dr, Vancouver BC V5X2T4, Canada

restaurant.name: Field & Social
restaurant.desc: Field & Social is a salad-focused fast-casual restaurant founded in Vancouver in 2016, built around the idea that salads can be the main event — filling, flavourful, and worth craving. The Mount Pleasant location serves creative salads and bowls made with fresh-cut greens, scratch-made dressings, and locally sourced proteins and produce. It's a practical lunch stop for cyclists moving through the South Main corridor, with online ordering and pickup available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu labels Thai Peanut Satay as vegan; Soy Mushroom Miso Bowl as 'plant based option'; multiple items (Chicken Tostada, Beets Bowl, Soy Mushroom Miso Bowl) labelled gluten free

restaurant.name: Gillnetter Pub
restaurant.desc: The Gillnetter Pub is a two-storey neighbourhood pub in Port Coquitlam, situated at the junction of the Mary Hill Bypass and Pitt River Road. It combines a full dine-in and takeout food menu with an attached liquor store carrying domestic and imported wines, specialty beers, and spirits — including VQA wines at below-government-store prices. The pub is adults-only (no minors permitted), making it a local fixture for the surrounding community.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'GLUTEN FREE OPTIONS AVAILABLE-PLEASE ASK YOUR SERVER'; vegetarian/vegan options not mentioned

restaurant.name: Jumping Jiminy's
restaurant.desc: A cafe with associated playground facilities in Nanaimo. This family-oriented venue offers refreshment and recreation opportunities for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Ding Hao Noodle House
restaurant.desc: Ding Hao Noodle House is a Taiwanese restaurant established in 2007 in Coquitlam, specializing in traditional beef noodle soup made with slow-cooked bone broth — no MSG or artificial concentrates. The owner/chef trained at Lao Shan Dong Homemade Noodle House in Taiwan, a restaurant recognized on the Michelin Bibendum Recommendation List. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down menu of Taiwanese classics — dumplings, braised beef rice, noodle soups, and an extensive bubble tea selection — in a spot conveniently located on Barnet Highway.

restaurant.name: Nong Geng Ji Hunan Cuisine
restaurant.desc: NongGengji is a global chain restaurant specializing in authentic Hunan cuisine, founded in 2017 by Chinese culinary master Feng Guohua and now operating over 100 direct stores across China, Hong Kong, Singapore, and beyond. The Richmond location is one of the brand's North American outposts, bringing fiery, ingredient-forward Hunan cooking to a sit-down dining room in the Aberdeen area. Touring cyclists will find it a substantial meal stop on the busy Number 3 Road corridor.

restaurant.name: Katsu Heaven
restaurant.desc: Katsu Heaven is a Japanese cutlet restaurant in downtown Penticton specializing in tonkatsu-style dishes. It offers a focused menu of breaded cutlets in the Japanese tradition, making it a distinctive dining option in BC's Okanagan wine country. A touring cyclist passing through Penticton will find it a compact, sit-down spot a short roll from the main corridor through town.

restaurant.name: Tamm Mexican Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Tamm Mexican Restaurant is a family-run eatery founded in 2009 by the Tarin family, who relocated from Chihuahua, Mexico to share authentic regional cooking with Kelowna. The menu spans classic dishes like enchiladas, Chiles Rellenos, fish tacos, tortilla soup, and a wide taco selection, alongside a Latin Market stocking Mexican beverages and pantry items. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down dining experience with online ordering and family-sized packages available.

restaurant.name: Ambit Cafe
restaurant.desc: Ambit Cafe is an artisan café located in Kensington Square Plaza in Burnaby, offering house-made sandwiches, wraps, soups, salads, and custom espresso drinks made with local, seasonal ingredients. The café pitches itself as a welcoming stop for 'morning commuters, quick-lunch crowd, afternoon loungers, and weekend warriors.' Cycling tourists will find a solid selection of hearty, portable food options plus third-party delivery partnerships.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page labels items with '_pb = plant based' and '_gf = gluten-friendly'; examples include macro salad (PB, GF), refresh salad bowl (GF), and power salad (GF)

restaurant.name: Mr. Falafel
restaurant.desc: Mr. Falafel is a family-owned Mediterranean grill that has anchored Vancouver's west side since 2002, serving falafel wraps, shawarma, souvlaki skewers, kibbeh, and house-made dolmades made with locally-sourced ingredients. The casual counter-service format makes it a quick and filling stop for cyclists passing through the Kitsilano area. Both dine-in and takeout are available, with online ordering for pickup.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegetarian items explicitly listed: Vegetarian Dish (dolmades, falafel, tabouleh, hummus, pita), Falafel Platter, Hummus Platter, Grilled Veggie wrap, and falafel-based appetizers. Vegan and GF status not explicitly stated

restaurant.name: Kanpai Asian Eatery & Bar
restaurant.desc: Kanpai Asian Eatery & Bar is an Asian restaurant and bar located on Blanshard Street in downtown Victoria. OSM records it as open Friday and Saturday evenings only, suggesting a focused dinner-and-drinks format rather than an all-day café. Very little public information was retrievable during review, as the business's Facebook page was inaccessible.

restaurant.name: Domo Sushi
restaurant.desc: A Japanese sushi restaurant located on Melville Street in downtown Vancouver. Standard full-service restaurant seating typical of the Vancouver sushi scene.

restaurant.name: Pho Dundas
restaurant.desc: Pho Dundas is a Vietnamese noodle restaurant in East Vancouver specializing in traditional pho broth soups alongside specialty sate varieties and fresh appetizers like salad rolls and bao sliders. The kitchen accommodates a range of diets with dedicated vegan and gluten-free menu sections. Online ordering with pickup and Uber Delivery options makes it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu has explicit Vegan Noodle Soups, Vegan Appys, Vegan Main, and Gluten free Items categories

restaurant.name: L'Apres Midi Patisserie
restaurant.desc: L'Apres Midi Patisserie is a French-style patisserie and cafe located in Vancouver's West End neighbourhood on West Pender Street. The name evokes a classic afternoon pastry culture, suggesting a spot suited to a mid-ride coffee-and-pastry break. No dedicated website is available beyond an Instagram presence, so further details on offerings are limited.

restaurant.name: Sushi Nara
restaurant.desc: Sushi Nara is an authentic Japanese restaurant with multiple locations in Abbotsford. A casual dining option where touring cyclists can stop for sushi and traditional Japanese cuisine.

restaurant.name: RedCan Gourmet
restaurant.desc: RedCan Gourmet is a restaurant located on Industrial Way in Tofino, a town known as a hub for Pacific Rim outdoor adventure including surfing and cycling. Its Industrial Way address puts it in a working district of Tofino accessible to cyclists moving through the area. The business has defined operating hours suggesting a stable, established operation.

restaurant.name: Tsukiya
restaurant.desc: Tsukiya is a small, walk-in-only ramen shop on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, a short ride from Stanley Park. The menu centres on a single specialty: house-made tonkotsu ramen with rich pork-bone broth and chewy noodles crafted from scratch. Its location on one of the West End's main cycling corridors makes it a natural refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the seawall.

notes.Takeout: Website contact page states takeout orders are accepted in-store only upon payment; phone orders not accepted

restaurant.name: Deep Cove Chalet
restaurant.desc: Deep Cove Chalet is a restaurant situated along Chalet Road on the Saanich Peninsula near Sidney, BC, in a scenic rural area popular with cyclists exploring the peninsula. The website navigation references lunch menus, dinner menus, and a wine list, suggesting a sit-down dining establishment. Its location near the Deep Cove area makes it a potential stop on the many cycling routes that thread through the peninsula toward the Gulf Islands ferry terminals.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's Canada franchise location in Chilliwack on Clearbrook Road, offering burgers, chicken, McCafé beverages, and breakfast. The site includes a drive-through lane for cyclists wanting quick service without dismounting. As a national chain with an in-app rewards program, it offers a reliable calorie stop on routes through the Fraser Valley.

restaurant.name: The Keg
restaurant.desc: The Yaletown Keg is a multi-floor steakhouse and bar occupying a corner building in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, steps from BC Place and Rogers Arena. The location spans four floors including a street-front patio and a year-round rooftop patio, which the venue describes as one of the best in Vancouver. It offers private and semi-private dining for large groups, full accessibility via elevator, and delivery exclusively through DoorDash.

restaurant.name: Tre Fantastico
restaurant.desc: Tre Fantastico is a bistro-style restaurant and bar opened in 2011 inside the Parkside Hotel, steps from Beacon Hill Park in the heart of downtown Victoria, and one of three Caffe Fantastico locations. It centres on three pillars — espresso, local craft ales, and an extensive BC-only wine list hand-selected by the owner — alongside a seasonally driven menu of locally sourced bistro food. The West Coast-designed space features floor-to-ceiling windows, a walnut and concrete bar, live-edge wood slab tables, and a patio, making it a comfortable stop for locals and travelling visitors alike.

restaurant.name: Thai Chef Eatery
restaurant.desc: Thai Chef Eatery is an authentic street food eatery serving home-cooked Thai classics in a casual dining setting. The unpretentious atmosphere and traditional preparation methods make it a reliable stop for touring cyclists seeking hearty, genuine Thai cuisine.

restaurant.name: Blackberry Cove Market Place
restaurant.desc: Blackberry Cove Market Place is a cafe located on Main Street in Ucluelet, a small coastal community on the west coast of Vancouver Island and a popular stop on the Pacific Rim cycling corridor. The business trades under a marketplace-style name suggesting a combination of café and retail offerings, though details could not be verified. Ucluelet's Main Street location would make it a convenient stop for cyclists riding the West Coast trails or touring the peninsula.

restaurant.name: Virtue Natural Bakery
restaurant.desc: Virtue Natural Bakery is an artisanal gluten-free bakery-café on West Broadway in Kitsilano, founded in 2017 by Certified Natural Chef Lisa Virtue. Every item — from sourdough-style loaves and French baguettes to brownies, butter tarts, and specialty cookies — is made with organic and seasonal ingredients and is 100% gluten-free, with many options also dairy-free, egg-free, or grain-free. Specialty organic coffee roasted by Moja Coffee and loose-leaf teas from Denman Island Tea Company make it a worthwhile stop for cyclists looking for quality café fare and fresh-baked provisions.

restaurant.name: Thaigo
restaurant.desc: Thaigo is a Thai fast-food chain operated by Broadway Foods Group, focused on delivering traditional Thai flavours quickly using fresh ingredients. The Park Royal location sits inside the Park Royal shopping centre food court in West Vancouver, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area. The brand has grown to four Metro Vancouver and Victoria locations since 2016.

detail.address: FC01-2002 Park Royal, West Vancouver, BC

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: This Tim Hortons in Tsawwassen is a dine-in cafe with no drive-through, making it a sit-down stop for cyclists. It sits close to the BC Ferries Tsawwassen terminal, a natural gathering point for touring cyclists heading to or from Vancouver Island. The menu covers coffee, breakfast wraps, baked goods, soups, and snacks throughout the day.

restaurant.name: Puerto Mexico, Tacos and Mexican Products
restaurant.desc: A Mexican taco restaurant and shop serving authentic Mexican cuisine in Vancouver. Offers a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists traveling through the West 4th Avenue area.

restaurant.name: Saint Germain Bakery
restaurant.desc: Saint Germain Bakery is an award-winning Canadian bakery chain founded in the mid-1980s, having earned multiple Gold Medals at the Culinary Olympics in Germany and supplied desserts to nine airlines and major hotel chains. The bakery draws on techniques from pastry chefs in France, Japan, Hong Kong, and Australia, using natural ingredients like whole vanilla beans, fresh cream from Calgary, and seasonal local fruit. This Richmond location is a mall-based shop — a handy refuelling stop for cyclists seeking fresh baked goods.

detail.address: 6060 Minoru Blvd Unit 2000, Richmond, BC V6Y 2B6, Canada

restaurant.name: The Pub, Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Pub Bar & Grill at Park Place Lodge is Fernie's neighbourhood gathering spot explicitly marketed to mountain bikers, skiers, and fly-fishers looking to refuel after a day in the outdoors. The pub pours 16 beers on tap—including local Fernie Brewing Co. selections—and serves an extensive menu of Canadian pub classics alongside a British-inspired seasonal menu. A sunny outdoor patio with mountain views rounds out the experience at this lodge-based pub in the heart of the Elk Valley.

restaurant.name: Robba da Matti
restaurant.desc: Robba Da Matti is a Vancouver-based Italian restaurant group with three locations — Gastown, Yaletown, and West End — serving regional Italian dishes and family recipes in a warm, home-style setting. The Gastown location at 12 Powell Street places it steps from the historic neighbourhood's cobblestone streets and near the Seawall cycling route. The restaurant's focus is on fresh pasta, wine, and a convivial atmosphere reminiscent of Italian home dining.

restaurant.name: Glacier Creek
restaurant.desc: Glacier Creek is an on-mountain restaurant at Whistler Blackcomb, one of North America's largest ski and bike resorts. Its coordinates place it mid-mountain on Whistler, making it a natural stop for riders using the Whistler Mountain Bike Park during summer operations. The building is a dedicated structure serving the mountain's dining needs across seasons.

restaurant.name: Himalaya Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Himalaya Restaurant is an Indian and Asian restaurant in Richmond serving a broad menu that spans tandoori dishes, biryanis, samosas, and Indian sweets. It is a two-location operation with a Richmond branch and a Vancouver branch, both offering online ordering and pickup. Touring cyclists in the Richmond area would find a wide selection of hearty, made-to-order South Asian food including dedicated vegetarian options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists a dedicated 'Vegetarian Dishes' category. No evidence of vegan or GF options specifically

restaurant.name: The Vault
restaurant.desc: The Vault is a 100% Canadian-owned, locally cherished restaurant that has served Downtown Historic Cloverdale for over 18 years, offering globally inspired comfort dishes under Chef Thomas Gilbert. Part of the Pacific Northcoast Restaurant Group, the restaurant features live music on weekend evenings and can host special events and large parties for up to 90 guests.

restaurant.name: Ricky's Grill
restaurant.desc: Café Solo is a Ricky's-branded family restaurant in Burnaby serving all-day breakfast, lunch, and dinner as part of a Canadian chain that has operated since 1962. This location is a dual-branded facility (Ricky's and Famoso) with both a dining room and a patio. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down meal option with takeout and delivery also available.

restaurant.name: Blenz Coffee
restaurant.desc: Blenz Coffee is a BC-based specialty coffee chain with a location steps from Vancouver's waterfront on Howe Street. The café serves espresso drinks, nitro coffee, whole-leaf teas, protein shakes, and a food menu spanning breakfast sandwiches, wraps, baked goods, and desserts. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a workable rest stop for cyclists passing through the downtown financial district.

restaurant.name: Taco Justice
restaurant.desc: Taco Justice is a fast-food Mexican eatery in downtown Victoria. Its central location makes it a convenient refueling stop for cyclists riding through the city core.

restaurant.name: Shore Line Brewing
restaurant.desc: Shore Line Brewing is a craft brewery and kitchen on the shores of Okanagan Lake on Lakeshore Road, directly across from Gyro Beach in Kelowna's Lower Mission neighbourhood. The brewery produces a rotating lineup of house-crafted beers—from crisp lagers to hazy IPAs and oatmeal stouts—using locally sourced Okanagan ingredients. The lakeside patio with mountain and lake views makes it a scenic and sociable stop for cyclists riding the Mission corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists dedicated 'GLUTEN FREE' and 'PLANT BASED/VEGAN' sections

restaurant.name: Lupins Café
restaurant.desc: Lupins Café is one of several dining venues at the summit of Grouse Mountain, a major year-round outdoor recreation destination above North Vancouver. The mountain is home to the Grouse Bike Park, making the café a natural post-ride stop for mountain bikers who have taken the Skyride up. The site is also reachable on foot via the iconic Grouse Grind trail, a popular challenge for active visitors.

restaurant.name: Emdee's Fish and Chips
restaurant.desc: A fast-food restaurant specializing in fish and chips located in Delta. Offers a quick meal option for cycling tourists. Wheelchair accessible according to OSM.

restaurant.name: X-Site Grill & Bistro
restaurant.desc: X-Site Grill & Bistro is a family-owned sit-down restaurant on Hastings Street in Burnaby, serving a broad menu spanning starters, pastas, grilled mains, and hand-held sandwiches. The kitchen makes several house-made sauces and the menu spans casual comfort food with Greek and North American influences. It sits on a main east-west arterial that connects Burnaby to Vancouver and Coquitlam, making it a potential mid-ride meal stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items explicitly labeled 'Vegetarian' on website: Tzatziki, Hummus, X-site Spuds, Cheese Garlic Bread, and Nachos

restaurant.name: Jitterz Coffee
restaurant.desc: A drive-thru espresso and coffee shop in Grand Forks offering quick beverage service for cyclists passing through the area. The drive-thru model provides convenient refueling without dismounting or parking concerns.

restaurant.name: Murder Burger
restaurant.desc: A burger restaurant in downtown Victoria known for the signature Mahoney burger. Offers both takeout and dine-in service with flexible seating options. A casual spot located centrally on Menzies Street.

restaurant.name: Miss Margaret's Espresso Bar
restaurant.desc: Margaret's is a coffee kiosk inside Harrison Hot Springs Resort, serving Starbucks Coffee, specialty drinks, and a selection of quick breakfast sandwiches, baked goods, soups, salads, and snacks. Harrison Hot Springs is a popular destination on the Lougheed Highway corridor, making this kiosk a convenient quick-fuel stop for touring cyclists without requiring a full restaurant sit-down. As a resort kiosk, service is designed to be fast and the menu broad enough to cover both sweet and savoury cravings.

restaurant.name: Uno Gelato
restaurant.desc: Uno Gelato is a Vancouver artisan gelato maker producing small-batch, farm-to-cone gelato and sorbetto from scratch using local ingredients such as Vancouver Island sea salt, Avalon Dairy milk, and freshly harvested fruits and herbs. This location sits within the Vancouver Convention Centre at Canada Place, one of multiple city locations. The shop rotates seasonal flavours alongside year-round favourites, with a strong vegan sorbetto lineup and gluten-friendly options throughout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Vegan Options available' and 'Gluten Friendly'; all sorbettos are explicitly vegan

restaurant.name: Mountain Top Beef House
restaurant.desc: Mountain Top Beef House is a Chinese private-kitchen restaurant (峨眉派私房菜) located in a Richmond commercial unit, specializing in beef dishes in the Emei style. The concept suggests a curated, intimate dining experience rather than a large chain restaurant. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's south end may find it a distinctive stop if confirmed open.

restaurant.name: Wall Flowers
restaurant.desc: Wall Flowers is a cafe-florist combination in Vancouver, offering a unique dual-purpose stop for travelers. The establishment provides food and beverage service in a welcoming indoor environment.

restaurant.name: Kadoya
restaurant.desc: Kadoya is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, serving sushi and Japanese cuisine in a compact indoor dining room. The restaurant offers online ordering as well as phone-in options, and is wheelchair accessible. It sits in a busy, bikeable urban corridor convenient to cyclists exploring the West End.

restaurant.name: Tropical Island
restaurant.desc: Tropical Island is a Southeast Asian fusion restaurant in Victoria's Shelbourne Village neighbourhood, where the chef-owner draws on training in Thai, Malaysian, Singaporean, and Chinese culinary traditions to offer a single, diverse menu. Dishes span appetizers, seafood, noodles, rice, and samplers, with a kitchen that cooks extensively with coconut milk — guests with allergies are asked to notify their server. The neighbourhood strip-mall location and eclectic fusion menu make it a distinctive stop for cyclists exploring the area.

restaurant.name: Stanley's Sports Bar and Grill
restaurant.desc: Stanley's Grill is a fully licensed sports bar and restaurant situated upstairs inside the Richmond Ice Centre, overlooking the main ice rinks with views of hockey action. The menu spans comfort-food staples — burgers, wraps, pizza, poutine, fish and chips, and pasta — alongside a rooftop patio and nine large flat-screen TVs. A second concession, the Rinkside Grill, operates at ice level for quicker grab-and-go options.

restaurant.name: Central Station Pub
restaurant.desc: Central Station Pub is a pub located in downtown Kamloops at 122 4th Avenue, in the city's core near the South Thompson River. As a downtown pub it may serve as a rest stop for cyclists passing through Kamloops, a hub city on several long-distance cycling routes including the Trans Canada Trail. No further detail about the venue's character or offerings could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: The Village Estevan Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Village Estevan is an all-day brunch restaurant steps from Willows Beach in Victoria's Estevan neighbourhood, voted Best Breakfast in the City 2022. Part of The Village franchise, it serves locally inspired brunch dishes alongside directly traded and locally roasted coffee. Tucked into a residential neighbourhood about five minutes from downtown Victoria, it draws both tourists and locals to a classic neighbourhood chippy with a full eat-in dining room. Street parking is available directly in front of the building.

restaurant.name: T.J. Beans
restaurant.desc: TJ Beans is a local coffee shop situated in the heart of Ganges, the main village on Salt Spring Island. It serves coffee and hot lunches in a relaxed, device-friendly environment well suited to travellers. The shop touts five charging ports and free Wi-Fi, making it a practical stop for cyclists crossing to or around the island.

restaurant.name: Just Waffles
restaurant.desc: Just Waffles is a neighbourhood specialty restaurant in East Vancouver run by owners Kathy and Calvin Klein, focusing entirely on Belgian liège waffles made from scratch. The menu swings from sweet fan-favourites like 'Nutella Lovers' and 'S'more Strawberry' to savoury items like 'Ham and Bacon Benny' and a 'Pulled Pork Pizza Waffle', with adventurous extras like alligator sausages. Bottomless coffee and a casual, locally loved atmosphere give it strong hidden-gem appeal as a refuelling stop on the East Hastings corridor.

restaurant.name: Indian Rasoi Curry House & Pizzeria

It could serve as a meal stop for cyclists passing through the Abbotsford corridor.

restaurant.name: Barcelo's Flame Grilled Chicken

restaurant.name: Mui Ngo Gai
restaurant.desc: Mui Ngo Gai is a Vietnamese and Singaporean fusion restaurant on Vancouver's Kingsway corridor, blending the bold flavors of two Southeast Asian culinary traditions under one roof. Chefs from Vietnam and Singapore bring regional authenticity to dishes spanning pho, Singaporean specialties, and a broad range of vegetarian options. The restaurant accepts reservations and offers online ordering, making it a versatile stop for touring cyclists along this busy urban route.

restaurant.name: Sushi Town
restaurant.desc: Sushi Town is a Japanese restaurant on the Barnet Highway corridor in Coquitlam offering traditional sushi, sashimi, specialty rolls, teriyaki, udon, and tempura dishes. The restaurant provides both dine-in service with table reservations and online delivery across multiple distance zones. Touring cyclists passing through Coquitlam on Barnet Highway will find a full sit-down Japanese meal available here.

restaurant.name: Storeys Cafe
restaurant.desc: Storeys Café is a nonprofit social enterprise in Richmond where every purchase supports people in recovery from addiction as they build job skills and confidence. Located half a block from Richmond City Hall, the café offers fresh coffee, wholesome sandwiches, soups, salads, and baked goods in a relaxed, welcoming space. The menu includes vegetarian and gluten-free options alongside classic breakfast and lunch fare.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a Vegetarian Sandwich (avocado, pesto, cucumber, spinach & Swiss); customer testimonial states 'the gluten-free sandwiches have been excellent.'

restaurant.name: New Sun Restaurant
restaurant.desc: New Sun Restaurant is a Chinese-Canadian neighbourhood restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver, offering a broad menu of classic dishes spanning chop suey, egg foo yong, seafood, pork, and family dinner specials. Online ordering with curbside pickup is available through their own ordering platform, including WeChat login integration. It is a practical stop for cyclists seeking a filling sit-down or takeout meal along the Cambie corridor.

restaurant.name: Earls Guildford
restaurant.desc: Earls Kitchen + Bar is a well-established Canadian casual dining chain offering a broad American-style menu in a full-service bar-and-restaurant setting. The Guildford location sits within a suburban retail corridor in Surrey and offers dine-in and pickup ordering. It provides a predictable, reliable full-meal option for touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley corridor.

restaurant.name: D Dutchmen Dairy
restaurant.desc: D Dutchmen Dairy is a family-run dairy farm established in 1978, producing 62 flavours of artisan ice cream, handmade cheeses, and fresh milk products entirely on-site in Sicamous. The Vancouver Sun named it 'BC's Best Ice Cream' in 2004, and multi-generational visitors continue to return, making it a beloved Shuswap landmark. The farm also features a Tractor Town attraction and resident animals, offering touring cyclists a memorable and rewarding detour off the Shuswap routes.

restaurant.name: Isami Sushi
restaurant.desc: Isami Sushi is a family-run Japanese restaurant that has served the Burnaby community near Metrotown since 1991, growing from a small family kitchen into a multi-generational neighborhood fixture. Located at basement level along Kingsway, it offers a curated menu built on over 30 years of culinary experience. Free underground parking is available on site.

restaurant.name: Maple Leaf Delicatessen Coffe Shop
restaurant.desc: A cafe and delicatessen on Burrard Street in downtown Vancouver offering both indoor and outdoor seating. Serves vegetarian food options. Part of the downtown commercial district.

restaurant.name: Silver House Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Silver House Restaurant is a family-owned Chinese restaurant on Dewdney Trunk Road in Maple Ridge, in continuous operation since 1999. It has been voted Best Chinese Food in Ridge Meadows six times between 2009 and 2017. The restaurant offers dine-in, pickup with a discount, and local delivery, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Maple Ridge town corridor.

detail.address: 22378 Dewdney Trunk Road, Maple Ridge, BC V2X 3J2

restaurant.name: La Stella Trattoria
restaurant.desc: La Stella Trattoria is a cozy Italian restaurant in Nanaimo focused on fresh, seasonal Vancouver Island ingredients prepared using old-world methods. It holds the distinction of importing Nanaimo's first wood-fired pizza oven, producing Neapolitan-style pies with a crisp, charred crust alongside hand-made pastas crafted from scratch daily. The kitchen also makes gluten-free pasta in-house using its own recipe, making it one of the more accommodating stops for cyclists with dietary needs.

restaurant.name: Bruno
restaurant.desc: Bruno is an upscale restaurant and bar located inside the Versante Hotel in Richmond's Airport District, occupying a 6,000-square-foot space anchored by a 30-seat bar and an 18-seat community table. The kitchen is built around locally-sourced British Columbia ingredients — Fraser Valley duck, Vancouver Island lavender, Pacific shellfish — served in family-style plates designed to encourage conversation. Its signature Saffron Shellfish Tagliatelle and a rotating menu spanning breakfast, brunch, dinner, and cocktails make it a notable destination in an area close to the YVR cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: A Tim Hortons franchise located on Tranquille Road in the north end of Kamloops, offering brewed coffee, specialty beverages, breakfast wraps, soups, and baked goods. The location features dine-in seating, a drive-through, and free Wi-Fi, making it a practical rest stop for cyclists coming in from the north or heading toward Sun Peaks. It is part of Canada's largest quick-service restaurant chain, known for reliable, affordable food and coffee across the country.

restaurant.name: Pearl Castle Cafe
restaurant.desc: Established in 1996, Pearl Castle Cafe is a Richmond institution credited with introducing freshly-made Taiwanese pearl tea to the city, later expanding to a full café concept in 1997. It has earned four consecutive Chinese Restaurant Awards for Best Taiwanese Café and offers a broad menu spanning bubble teas, hotpot, noodles, fried rice, and Taiwanese street food. The cafe is situated inside the Continental Centre shopping mall, making it a sheltered stop for cyclists navigating Richmond's commercial corridors.

detail.address: Continental Centre (#1128-3779 Sexsmith Rd.), Richmond, BC

restaurant.name: Mahek Restaurant & Lounge
restaurant.desc: Mahek is an Indian restaurant in Surrey serving a broad menu of North Indian cuisine including tandoor-grilled dishes, curries, seafood, and lamb preparations. The restaurant offers both a full dinner menu and a lunch menu, with dedicated vegetarian selections spanning paneer, dal, and vegetable curries. Online ordering with 15-minute pickup is available, making it a practical stop for a quick meal on a ride.

restaurant.name: Zakkushi Dining on Main
restaurant.desc: Zakkushi on Main is a Japanese yakitori izakaya that opened in 2008 as the second location of the Vancouver-based Zakkushi Group, skewering each item fresh over imported Bincho charcoal for authentic flavour. It occupies a booth-seating dining room on Vancouver's vibrant Main Street corridor and carries a rotating seasonal menu available exclusively at this location. Touring cyclists passing through Vancouver's east side will find it a well-established full-service restaurant with both dine-in and takeout options.

restaurant.name: The Rice Box
restaurant.desc: The Rice Box is a long-established Asian restaurant in Vernon, celebrating 25 years of operation in the community. It offers takeout and online ordering, making it a convenient meal option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Gong Cha
restaurant.desc: Gong Cha is a globally recognized bubble tea franchise originating in Taiwan, offering highly customizable tea-based drinks with a choice of toppings, sugar levels, and ice levels. The Coquitlam location operates as a takeout-focused shop inside a commercial unit with no outdoor seating. For a touring cyclist, it offers a quick cold drink stop but has no confirmed cycling-specific infrastructure.

restaurant.name: Lantzville Pub
restaurant.desc: Established July 25, 1925, the Lantzville Pub is a century-old coastal institution perched on Vancouver Island with views over the Strait of Georgia and the coastal mountains. It serves hearty pub food alongside local and imported beers, wines, and spirits in a historic building. Situated just north of Woodgrove Mall in the heart of Lantzville, it makes a natural stop for cyclists riding the Island's coastal corridor.

restaurant.name: Azure Play Cafe
restaurant.desc: Azure Play Cafe is a dessert-focused cafe located in a unit at 9100 Garden City Road in Richmond, BC. The space is wheelchair accessible and sits within a larger commercial complex. Cyclists in the Garden City area could use it as a sweet-treat stop, though the indoor-only seating (no outdoor seating confirmed via OSM) may limit bike visibility.

restaurant.name: Third Wave Coffee
restaurant.desc: Third Wave Coffee is a cafe in Chemainus providing refreshments and a resting stop for travelers and cyclists. It serves beverages and food to locals and visitors passing through the community.

restaurant.name: Mister
restaurant.desc: Mister is an artisan ice cream shop in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, one of three Vancouver locations, specializing in made-to-order ice cream flash-frozen with liquid nitrogen for a uniquely rich, dense texture. The shop uses pure, natural ingredients sourced from local B.C. farmers and rotates seasonal flavour combinations. It offers a welcoming indoor seating area and accepts cash, credit, and debit.

restaurant.name: Pane e Formaggio
restaurant.desc: Pane e Formaggio is a family-run artisan bakery that has been producing sourdough breads, pastries, and baked goods from scratch since 2005, with this Beatty Street location sitting near Vancouver's city centre close to the Art Gallery and Law Courts. The café offers indoor and outdoor seating and serves espresso, coffee drinks, and sandwiches alongside a daily-baked bread selection. Cyclists passing through downtown Vancouver will find it a practical stop for fresh bread loaves and a hot drink.

restaurant.name: Vina Vietnamese
restaurant.desc: A Vietnamese fast-food restaurant in Vancouver offering indoor seating for casual dining. Serves Vietnamese cuisine in a convenient fast-food format, providing a quick meal option for touring cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: Subway

It offers the full Subway menu of Footlongs, 6" sandwiches, wraps, and salads with in-restaurant dining, takeout, curbside pickup, and delivery. Breakfast service is also available.

restaurant.name: Cortado Cafe and Coffee House

The cafe emphasizes sustainability, vegan and gluten-free options, and outdoor seating, making it a welcoming stop for visitors passing through.

restaurant.name: Green Bamboo

restaurant.name: Super Chef Grill

restaurant.name: Bufala

restaurant.name: Umami Ramen + Grill

restaurant.name: Deville Coffee
restaurant.desc: Deville Coffee is a locally owned coffee chain operating since 2008 across Alberta and BC, known for small-batch direct trade beans that are sourced, roasted, and brewed in-house. Their espresso drinks are crafted with touches like organic vanilla and house-made chocolate ganache, and the menu extends to breakfast wraps and fresh sandwiches made daily by local bakeries. The Vancouver location is part of a growing network of community-focused cafes that take pride in knowing their regulars.

restaurant.name: Snowy Village

restaurant.name: Caravanserai Uyghur Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Caravanserai Uyghur Cuisine brings the bold flavors of the Central Asian Silk Road to Vancouver's SE Marine Drive, specializing in hand-stretched Laghman noodles, slow-simmered lamb Polo rice pilaf, and hearth-baked Nang bread using 100% Halal-certified ingredients. The menu spans signature dishes like the showstopping Dapanji big-plate chicken to lighter cold noodle dishes, making it one of Metro Vancouver's rare dedicated Uyghur restaurants. It is a distinctive cultural dining destination for cyclists exploring the southern reaches of the city.

restaurant.name: JOS

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons

restaurant.name: Buro Coffee Bar

restaurant.name: Subway

restaurant.name: Seaside Restaurant

Takeout and delivery service make it a practical morning or midday stop for cyclists passing through the Brentwood corridor.

restaurant.name: Triple O's

restaurant.name: Han Lin Noodle House

restaurant.name: Roberts Street Pizza

restaurant.name: La Forchetta

It is a sit-down dining destination with table reservations and online ordering, making it a solid stop for a cycling-day meal.

restaurant.name: Cactus Club Cafe

restaurant.name: Song Cafe
restaurant.desc: Song Cafe is a Hong Kong-style restaurant on Heather Street in Vancouver offering a broad menu spanning Cantonese, Sichuan, and other regional Chinese cuisines alongside Western dishes. The restaurant accommodates tourist group meals and provides multiple service modes including dine-in, pickup, delivery, and catering. restaurant.name: Freshii

restaurant.name: Boston Pizza

restaurant.name: Fat Boy Kitchen

restaurant.name: Watashi Sushi

Their signature 'peaked' preparation tops a pie with mashed potatoes, mushy peas, and gravy — a hearty, filling option for cyclists fuelling up. Rated #3 of 134 restaurants in Whistler on Google, it is tucked into the village on Main Street and draws a loyal local and visitor following.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'traditional meat and veggie options available'; blog post titled 'Calling All Vegans…' (July 2019) indicates vegan options exist. No GF evidence found

restaurant.name: Lemonade Gluten Free Bakery
restaurant.desc: Lemonade Gluten Free Bakery is a dedicated celiac-friendly bakery on Cambie Street in Vancouver, producing gluten-free cakes, tarts, pastries, cookies, and bread. They also accommodate a wide range of other dietary needs including dairy-free, egg-free, nut-free, and vegan options, making it a rare all-inclusive stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions. Orders are placed online or by phone with advance notice and collected as in-store pickup.

restaurant.name: % Arabica
restaurant.desc: % Arabica is an internationally recognized specialty coffee brand with a striking Whistler Village location designed around the theme of ice caves, featuring white metal mesh domes suspended across the ceiling. The counter is positioned centrally for clear sightlines from the entrance, creating an open, welcoming atmosphere suited to all weather conditions. It is part of a global network of architecturally distinctive cafés known for high-quality coffee sourced from around the world.

restaurant.name: Laila Laila Hotpot
restaurant.desc: Laila Laila Hotpot bills itself as Victoria's only all-you-can-eat Chinese hotpot restaurant, co-founded by two Shanghai natives who spent six months in Sichuan developing their signature soup base recipes. The menu spans 35–60+ items across Classic and Premium tiers, covering premium meats, seafood, vegetables, fried snacks, and ice cream. The name 'LailaLaila' is a Shanghainese expression of warm welcome — fitting for a touring cyclist looking for a hearty, communal meal.

detail.address: 1540 Cedar Hill Cross Rd, Victoria, BC, V8P 2P4

restaurant.name: Pizza 64
restaurant.desc: Pizza 64 is a Canadian pizza chain that has been operating since 2010, with over 20 locations across British Columbia including this Kamloops outpost. The chain emphasizes fresh-made dough and sauce at each location, and offers a broad menu spanning specialty, signature, and gourmet pizzas alongside wings, pasta, and sides. For a touring cyclist rolling into Kamloops, it's a reliable spot for a filling hot meal with online ordering available for quick pickup.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegetarian pizzas on menu: Garden Fresh (no meat), Pesto Veggie (no meat), Passion of India and Shahi Paneer (Tandoori Paneer, no meat). No confirmed vegan or GF options

restaurant.name: Ed's Coffee House
restaurant.desc: A cafe in Lake Cowichan offering Wi-Fi access. Located on South Shore Road.

detail.address: 67 South Shore Road, Lake Cowichan, V0R 2G0

restaurant.name: Oakberry Açaí bowls
restaurant.desc: Oakberry is a Brazilian-origin açaí bowl chain with a Vancouver outpost on Water Street in Gastown. The format is entirely takeout-focused — no indoor or outdoor seating — making it a quick stop for a customizable, fruit-forward bowl. The brand is operated in Canada by Snowbank Brands and also offers a mobile OAKVAN catering unit for events in Vancouver.

notes.Takeout: Business model is takeout-only (no seating)

restaurant.name: Vennie's Sub Shop
restaurant.desc: Vennie's Sub Shop is a community-focused sandwich spot started in 2021 by a group of friends devoted to hand-crafted subs, now operating out of a physical location near the top of Commercial Drive in Vancouver. The menu spans creative cold subs like The Muffaletta (mortadella, salami, giardiniera) and hot options such as a French Beef Dip and Chopped Cheese, alongside sides and cookies. The shop also offers event catering.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'The Veggie' sub (Roast Zucchini, Tomato, Arugula, Fior di latte, Pesto Mayo, Balsamic Glaze). No explicit vegan or gluten-free options confirmed

restaurant.name: Double Double
restaurant.desc: Double Double is a Hong Kong-style Chinese restaurant in Richmond specializing in the 'back alley faves' of Hong Kong and Chiu Chow cuisine. The menu draws on traditional street-food staples — hand-pulled oil donuts (油條), hand-made steamed rice rolls, ChiuChow congee, and wok-fried noodles — prepared with what the owners describe as time-honored techniques. It occupies a unit in the 4600 No.3 Road retail complex, a busy commercial corridor in central Richmond.

detail.address: Unit 128 4600 No.3 Road, Richmond, BC V6X 2C2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Crispy Veg Spring Roll 香脆炸素春捲' and multiple soy-sauce-only noodle and noodle-in-soup dishes that contain no stated meat ingredients; no GF or vegan labelling found

restaurant.name: Sopra Sotto Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Sopra Sotto Pizzeria is a neighbourhood Italian restaurant on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, serving fresh in-house pastas and pizzas from a wood-fired oven. The restaurant has a full Italian menu spanning antipasti, pasta, and pizza, and is one of two locations (the other in Burnaby). Commercial Drive is one of Vancouver's most cycling-friendly corridors, making this a natural stop on a city ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu labels items vegetarian (v), gluten-free (gf), and dairy-free (df); vegan mozzarella available as an add-on on both Vancouver and Burnaby menus

restaurant.name: Atlas Steak + Fish
restaurant.desc: Atlas Steak + Fish is a modern, upscale steakhouse and seafood restaurant operated by Gateway Casinos, situated inside Cascades Casino Langley on Fraser Hwy. The restaurant describes itself as a 'flirtatious and modern twist on the iconic North American steakhouse,' emphasizing premium ingredients, global flavour influences, and engaging table-side service. It is part of a multi-location Canadian chain with BC outposts in Langley, Burnaby, and Kamloops.

restaurant.name: The Funky Monkey Food Corp.
restaurant.desc: The Funky Monkey Food Corp. is a sandwich-focused cafe on Murray Street in Port Moody, BC. It operates as a compact neighbourhood lunch spot with no outdoor seating. Touring cyclists passing through Port Moody's waterfront corridor may find it a convenient midday stop.

restaurant.name: The One Sixty Wine Bar & Cafe
restaurant.desc: The One Sixty is a well-regarded wine bar and café in Port Moody's Murray Street area, voted Best Restaurant in Port Moody. It runs an ambitious wine program with over 20 pours by the glass and wines on tap, alongside a full food menu spanning brunch, lunch, and dinner. A touring cyclist arriving from the Shoreline Trail or Inlet trails would find a full sit-down meal, takeout options, and happy hour service available most days.

detail.address: 3141 Murray Street, Port Moody, BC V3H 2R8

restaurant.name: Asteras
restaurant.desc: Asteras is an authentic Greek taverna set inside a heritage home more than 100 years old in downtown Nanaimo's Old City Quarter, specializing in traditional Cretan recipes made entirely in-house from whole foods daily. The menu spans house-made mezethes, fresh seafood, slow-roasted lamb, and a dedicated vegetarian section, all served with generous portions and a full wine selection. The restaurant has earned six Best of City Awards in 2024, including Best Overall Restaurant.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated vegetarian section on menu: Vegetarian Moussaka (eggplant, zucchini, tofu & béchamel), Spanakopita Meal, and Vegetable Brochette. Website also specifically calls out 'vegetarian dishes such as Moussaka and Spanakopita.'

restaurant.name: Espresso Café
restaurant.desc: Espresso Café appears to be a coffee shop offering espresso drinks, cold beverages, and a breakfast and bakery menu, based on page-title remnants visible in its sitemap. The domain has been taken over by an unrelated online gambling affiliate site, making current operational details unverifiable. The café's community is listed as Tsawwassen in OSM, though archived page titles reference 'Surrey Coffee.'

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: Starbucks is a chain coffee shop offering espresso drinks and light food items. Located on Sea Island Way in Richmond, it serves as a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. This location provides the familiar, reliable service expected from the Starbucks brand.

restaurant.name: Cloudburst Coffee
restaurant.desc: Cloudburst Coffee is a neighbourhood cafe on Mamquam Road in Squamish, a hub town for mountain biking, road cycling, and multi-day touring routes through the Sea-to-Sky corridor. The café operates seven days a week and appears family-friendly based on its OSM tags. Its location in Squamish makes it a practical stop for cyclists moving between Vancouver and Whistler.

restaurant.name: Sashimi & Sushi Express
restaurant.desc: Sashimi & Sushi Express is a fast-food sushi counter operating from unit 101c of a commercial building. The Instagram handle references Surrey, suggesting a quick-service Japanese food stop in the Fraser Valley corridor. It represents a convenient option for touring cyclists looking for a light, protein-rich meal on the go.

restaurant.name: Pho Han Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Pho Han Restaurant is a Vietnamese family restaurant established in 2011 in the West Cambie neighbourhood of Richmond, serving traditional dishes including pho, grilled lemongrass chicken and pork, banh mi, and fresh salad rolls. The restaurant is located in a strip-mall unit and offers dine-in, phone takeout, and delivery via UberEats. A touring cyclist stopping in Richmond will find a hearty, affordable hot meal well-suited for refuelling.

restaurant.name: Café Kitsuné
restaurant.desc: Café Kitsuné is the café arm of the Paris-born Maison Kitsuné lifestyle brand, blending specialty coffee culture with the brand's distinctive aesthetic. The Vancouver branch sits in Gastown at 157 Water Street, placing it in one of the city's most walkable and tourist-frequented heritage neighbourhoods. It is part of an international network of cafés known for quality espresso drinks, matcha, and French-inspired patisseries.

restaurant.name: Xin Qiao Feng Noodles Ltd.
restaurant.desc: A noodle restaurant in Richmond, BC serving casual dining options. An accessible food stop for touring cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: Hula Poke
restaurant.desc: Hula Poké is a Hawaiian-inspired fast-casual poke bowl chain with a location inside the McArthurGlen Designer Outlet near YVR Airport in Richmond. Cyclists can build customizable bowls from proteins like ahi tuna, salmon, chicken, or tofu, paired with bases including coconut rice or kelp noodle. The menu leans fresh and nutrient-dense, with multiple vegan-friendly and gluten-friendly options and online order-ahead available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple bowls labeled VEGAN FRIENDLY (e.g., Yuzu Traditional, Koko Spicy Korean, Ponzu Citrus Soy, Cali Veg) and GLUTEN FRIENDLY across the menu; tofu and sweet potato protein options available

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: Starbucks is a widely-recognized coffee chain offering espresso beverages and food. Touring cyclists can expect consistent, reliable service and a comfortable environment for a break. The location provides both indoor and outdoor seating for a quick or extended rest stop.

restaurant.name: Georgie's Local Kitchen and Bar
restaurant.desc: Georgie's Local is a neighbourhood kitchen and bar at the east end of Columbia Street in New Westminster, one block from the Columbia SkyTrain station. The venue is known for its panoramic Fraser River views, a private event room with expansive garage doors, and a lively lineup of events including Open Mic, Trivia, and Karaoke. Indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists finishing a ride along the river.

detail.address: 250 Columbia St, New Westminster, BC V3L 1A6

restaurant.name: Himalaya Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Himalaya Restaurant is an Indian cuisine chain with locations in Vancouver and Richmond, BC. The Vancouver outpost sits on Main Street and offers online ordering. Touring cyclists in the Main Street corridor will find it a convenient stop for a sit-down Indian meal.

restaurant.name: Nice Meating You
restaurant.desc: Nice Meating You BBQ is a Chinese-style barbecue restaurant in Coquitlam specializing in grilled skewers ranging from lamb kebabs and chicken wings to more adventurous offal cuts and seafood options like grilled squid and braised abalone. The menu also features tinfoil-cooked dishes, spicy hot pots, and cold appetizers, reflecting a Mainland Chinese street-BBQ tradition. Online ordering with quick pickup makes it a practical refueling stop for cyclists passing through the Clarke Road corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu legend explicitly marks vegetarian items; plant-based options include Towering Tofu Treats, Roasted Cauliflower Florets, Tin Foil Enoki Mushrooms, Tin Foil Roasted Baby Chinese Cabbage, and others

restaurant.name: Menbow
restaurant.desc: Menbow Ramen Bar is an authentic Japanese ramen restaurant in downtown Victoria that imports key ingredients directly from Japan and features Japanese-trained chefs. It is one of the few ramen spots on Vancouver Island to offer both a creamy tonkotsu (pork bone) broth and a clear tori (chicken) broth across a wide range of flavour profiles. Touring cyclists can dine in or order for pick-up via the website or third-party delivery apps.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists 'Tomato Ramen (Vegetarian)' as a menu option under available flavours

restaurant.name: Hara Sushi
restaurant.desc: Hara Sushi is a licensed Japanese and Korean restaurant located in the Village Food Market in central Sooke, BC. The kitchen emphasizes fresh, locally sourced ingredients — reviewers note fish caught the same day — and the small but efficient operation has earned a strong local reputation. A touring cyclist stopping in Sooke will find both dine-in and take-out options served by attentive staff.

detail.address: 6661 Sooke Rd #105, Sooke, BC (Village Food Market)

restaurant.name: Schnitzelz
restaurant.desc: German cuisine restaurant in Chilliwack. Information about amenities and services could not be verified due to website access limitations.

restaurant.name: Smugglers Trail Caskworks and Brewery
restaurant.desc: Smugglers Trail Caskworks is a craft brewery and kitchen in Langley, BC, founded in 2017 by two former rugby teammates who set out to bring quality cask-conditioned ales to the Fraser Valley. The spacious taproom features a covered heated patio that is dog-friendly year-round, and a full kitchen with dishes designed to pair with their rotating lineup of core, seasonal, and exclusive on-tap brews. Their award-winning beers—ranging from light lagers to stouts—are also available at local beer and wine stores across the region.

restaurant.name: Main Street Poke
restaurant.desc: Main Street Poke is a fast-casual bowl restaurant in Whistler serving fresh poke bowls, ramen, and rice bowls with a wide range of proteins, bases, and toppings including vegan options. The menu draws on the Hawaiian tradition of marinated fish bowls updated with West Coast and fusion flavours, and the business also offers catering for events. It's a popular quick-service stop in the village for hungry cyclists looking for a customizable, nourishing meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Our selection will indulge everyone, from fish lovers, to vegans' confirming vegan options; GF status not mentioned

restaurant.name: Massawa Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Massawa Restaurant is an Ethiopian and Eritrean restaurant established in 2021 in New Westminster, serving traditional dishes such as doro wat, injera firfir, awaze tibs, and kitfo, all presented on injera made fresh daily from teff. The kitchen is halal-certified, fully licensed, and offers an extensive vegetarian and vegan menu alongside gluten-free options. Free Wi-Fi, takeout, and delivery make it a practical and flavorful stop for cyclists touring the Lower Mainland.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page lists 'Vegetarian & vegan-friendly' and 'Halal options'; menu page states 'All dishes served with injera (100% gluten-free teff)'; front page notes 'gluten-free injera and halal options always ready.'

restaurant.name: Bing & Noodle World
restaurant.desc: Bing & Noodle World is a casual noodle and bing (Chinese pancake) restaurant on Granville Street in Vancouver. The business operates primarily through social media and specializes in quick, affordable noodle and bing dishes. A convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking casual dining.

restaurant.name: Pedal & Tap
restaurant.desc: Pedal & Tap is a bar and restaurant set in Kimberley's Platzl, a pedestrian plaza in the heart of downtown, with a name that gives a knowing wink to cycling culture. The kitchen turns out creative, scratch-made dishes — from Vietnamese pork meatball bowls to panko-crusted seafood cakes — alongside a full bar with draught beer, cocktails, and seasonal happy hour specials. The outdoor-recreation-friendly vibe, reinforced by the hashtag #getmuckedup, makes it a natural gathering spot for cyclists finishing a day on the trails.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels: Vegetable Tart (Vegetarian), Sweet Potato Fritters (Vegan), Harvest Grain Bowl (Vegetarian), Asian Crispy Noodle Salad (Vegetarian; gluten-free when crispy noodles are omitted), Pedal House Salad (Vegan)

restaurant.name: Domino's
restaurant.desc: Domino's is a franchise pizza chain location in Victoria's Fairfield/Gonzales neighbourhood on Foul Bay Road. It offers both delivery and carryout, making it a quick calorie stop for cyclists passing through the area. The menu includes pizza, chicken wings, cheesy bread, pasta, and desserts.

detail.address: 1070 Foul Bay Rd, Victoria, BC V8S4J2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Coupons page lists 'Veggie' pizza among named specialty pizzas

restaurant.name: Side Project Coffee
restaurant.desc: Side Project Coffee is a campus coffee shop operated by the University of Victoria Graduate Students' Society (GSS), located on the UVic Ring Road campus in Victoria. It shares an organizational home with the Grad House Restaurant, both run as student-facing food and beverage services by the GSS. Touring cyclists on the Galloping Goose or Lochside trails — which connect directly to the UVic area — would find it a convenient on-campus stop for coffee and a rest.

restaurant.name: Pho 37
restaurant.desc: Phở 37 is an award-winning Vietnamese restaurant chain that began in the Steveston neighbourhood of Richmond and has since grown to five BC locations. The Steveston Highway location has earned the Canadian Choice Award for Vietnamese Restaurant in Richmond and recognition from Richmond Business Excellence Awards. Cyclists will find a full sit-down menu of pho, vermicelli bowls, rice plates, and appetizers, with vegetarian and tofu substitutions throughout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Regular / Vegetarian' for spring rolls, 'Tofu' salad rolls, a dedicated 'Vegetables and Tofu Noodle' soup with choice of beef or veggie broth, and 'Choice of regular/vegetarian' for vermicelli bowls

restaurant.name: Deer Garden Signatures
restaurant.desc: Deer Garden Signatures is a well-known Richmond noodle restaurant group celebrated for their signature fish soup rice noodles (魚湯米線) made without MSG. The Alexandra Road flagship sits in Richmond's busy 'food street' corridor, a popular dining destination in the city's heart. Cyclists will find a substantial sit-down meal with online pre-ordering available.

restaurant.name: Cannon Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Cannon Estate Winery is a family-owned estate winery opened in 2022 on 20 acres in the Mt. Lehman area of Abbotsford, producing French-style terroir-focused wines under the Cannon and The Wick labels. The property includes Calibre by Cannon, a lounge offering sit-down dining, weekend brunch, and regular live music, making it a destination rather than a simple bottle shop. Located 10 minutes north of Highway 1, it sits in the heart of the Fraser Valley wine country and is a natural stop on rural cycling routes through the region.

restaurant.name: Pulp Fiction Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Pulp Fiction Coffee House is a one-of-a-kind café in downtown Kelowna where freshly roasted espresso drinks share space with rare pulp fiction books, Art Deco antiques, and vivid jacket-cover art, all curated by owner Max Sloan over a 45-year career of global collecting. Situated on the corner of Pandosy and Lawrence, the groovy retro interior spills into back rooms filled with glowing Art Deco globes, old clocks, and collectible book cover prints. Touring cyclists will find a genuinely distinctive and unhurried rest stop that doubles as a small museum of mid-century popular culture.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels 'Rocky Road Gluten Free/Vegan', 'Power Ball Gluten Free/Vegan', 'Cookie - Florentine Gluten Free', 'Date Square Also available as Gluten Free', and 'Nanaimo Bar Also available gluten free'

restaurant.name: PETPLS Café & Supply
restaurant.desc: PETPLS is a pet food and supply store in Richmond's Number 3 Road commercial corridor, offering a curated selection of high-quality pet foods and supplies for cats and dogs sourced from Canada, Korea, Germany, Italy, and New Zealand. The store features a bookable cat room where visitors can interact with adoptable rescue cats, and also offers cat boarding services. Located beside a SkyTrain station, it is an accessible stop for cyclists traveling with animal companions.

restaurant.name: Frank's Honeybun Café
restaurant.desc: Frank's Honeybun Café is a Yates Street diner that bridges all-day North American breakfast with a full Chinese cuisine menu — wonton soups, udon noodles, stir-fry lunch combos, and more. The broad, eclectic menu makes it a practical refueling stop for cyclists at any time of day. Real fruit smoothies and bubble teas are also on offer alongside the full food menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu legend lists 'vegetarian' as a tagged label; menu includes Vegetarian Combo and multiple Vegetable Egg Foo Young options. No vegan or GF claims confirmed

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A 24-hour McDonald's drive-through and dine-in location on Main Street in Vancouver, offering the full Canadian McDonald's menu including breakfast, McCafé beverages, and vegetarian options. Situated in a standalone retail building, this location is convenient for cyclists passing through the Main Street corridor. Indoor seating is available.

restaurant.name: Blenz Coffee
restaurant.desc: Blenz Coffee is a BC-born specialty coffee chain founded in Vancouver in 1992, now operating locally owned and operated franchise locations across Canada. The Davie Street location serves handcrafted espresso drinks, organic teas, protein shakes, and a full food menu ranging from croissants and breakfast sandwiches to samosas. Outdoor seating and a central West End location make it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists riding the Seawall or nearby routes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes vegetarian food items (croissants, muffins, samosas, bowls, protein shakes with natural ingredients)

restaurant.name: Maggie's Seafood Market Fish & Chips
restaurant.desc: A Nanaimo seafood restaurant with fish and chips as its signature item, complemented by burgers, salads, and soups. Offers a meal option for the community and visitors to the area.

restaurant.name: Seoul Grill House
restaurant.desc: Seoul Grill House is a Korean restaurant situated in a commercial unit along 101 Avenue in Surrey, BC. Specializing in Korean cuisine, it offers a sit-down dining experience that could serve as a satisfying meal stop for cyclists exploring the Surrey area. The restaurant's location along a commercial strip makes it reasonably accessible to riders passing through.

restaurant.name: Mr. Red Cafe
restaurant.desc: Mr. Red Cafe is a Vietnamese restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver. It offers casual dine-in service.

restaurant.name: Sushi Yoi
restaurant.desc: Sushi Yoi is a casual Japanese restaurant in Burnaby specializing in fresh sushi, sashimi, and aburi-style nigiri alongside classics like tempura and donburi. The restaurant emphasizes high-quality, locally sourced ingredients and offers both dine-in and takeout, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Rosser Avenue corridor. Outdoor seating is noted in OSM, which may allow cyclists to keep an eye on their bikes.

restaurant.name: White Spot
restaurant.desc: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, founded in 1928, known for burgers made with 100% fresh Canadian beef and locally sourced ingredients including BC chicken and BC-grown potatoes. The New Westminster location on Sixth Street offers full table-service dining as well as a patio, curbside pickup, and third-party delivery. Touring cyclists will find a familiar, family-friendly stop with a broad menu and vegetarian options.

restaurant.name: Happy Family Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Happy Family Restaurant has been serving Cantonese-style Chinese cuisine on Vancouver's Kingsway corridor since 2010, with a menu that leans into traditional Hong Kong-style cooking — think whole braised chicken, lobster in lotus leaves, and house-made BBQ pork cheek, all available in limited daily quantities. The air-conditioned dining room offers a full sit-down table-service experience in a neighbourhood-focused setting. Cyclists looking for a substantial hot meal mid-tour will find a wide-ranging menu with both familiar and adventurous options.

restaurant.name: Bonta Italian Ristorante
restaurant.desc: Bonta is an authentically Italian restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, run by an owner with over 20 years of multiregional Italian cuisine experience. The kitchen leans on generational recipes and locally sourced artisanal ingredients, spanning antipasti, house-made pasta, pizza, and mains such as saffron lamb shank with house gnocchi. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and online ordering is supported.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels 'Minestrone Alla Toscana' as 'our vegetarian based broth with seasonal vegetable'; multiple salads and pasta dishes appear meat-free. No explicit vegan or GF labeling found

restaurant.name: Soi ram
restaurant.desc: Soi Ram is a Thai restaurant located in Tsawwassen, BC, serving the Delta Street corridor. As a sit-down Thai restaurant, it would offer a warm meal stop for cyclists exploring the South Delta area near the Tsawwassen ferry terminal and the surrounding flat farmland cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Kobe
restaurant.desc: Kobe Japanese Steakhouse is a long-running teppanyaki-style restaurant in Vancouver's West End, billing itself as 'a party at every table' — a nod to the theatrical tableside cooking style. Located on Alberni Street near the Coal Harbour waterfront, it occupies a standalone building and draws both locals and visitors for Japanese cuisine in a lively setting. A touring cyclist finishing a ride in downtown Vancouver would find a sit-down dinner destination within easy reach of the seawall.

restaurant.name: El Santo
restaurant.desc: El Santo is a contemporary Mexican restaurant in the heart of New Westminster, named after El Santo — the legendary masked luchador and childhood hero of founder Alejandro Diaz. Since opening in 2015, Executive Chef Sam Fabbro has built a menu around Pacific Northwest ingredients with a Mexican twist, including house-made corn tortillas and regional specialties not found elsewhere on the Canadian coast. The restaurant also runs el Santo CAN, a community fundraising initiative that has raised over $120,000 for the Canucks Autism Network.

detail.address: 680 Columbia St, New Westminster, BC V3M 1A9

restaurant.name: Mereon
restaurant.desc: Mèreon is a French-inspired bistro in West Vancouver offering brunch, happy hour, and dinner menus that blend classic French technique with fresh West Coast ingredients. The restaurant was founded by Ophelia Arida and features menu development by Chef Emmanuel Joinville, who trained at a Michelin 3-starred restaurant in Dijon before becoming known in Vancouver for the long-running Jules Bistro in Gastown. The bistro seats up to 50 guests and is committed to locally sourced produce and house-made preparations throughout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists several dishes without meat: Zucchini Galette with Crispy Egg (lemon ricotta, zucchini, heirloom tomatoes), Braid & Bisque (spinach, mushroom, gruyère, parmesan in braided bread), Croque Forestier (mushrooms, gruyère, mornay), Classic French Omelette (gruyère, herbs), Bistro Chèvre Shakshouka (tomato & fennel sauce, soft baked eggs, chèvre), and Tomato Bisque.
