restaurant.name: The Vienna Cafe
restaurant.desc: A family-friendly breakfast and lunch cafe in Nelson specializing in homemade fare and sandwiches. Offering indoor seating on Kootenay Street, it provides a casual dining stop for cyclists passing through downtown Nelson.

restaurant.name: Kitchen on the Ridge
restaurant.desc: Kitchen on the Ridge is a family-owned restaurant that has been serving Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows since 2005, offering a full dine-in menu alongside weekend Dim Sum service. Situated on the Lougheed Highway, it is a convenient meal stop for cyclists traveling through the Fraser Valley corridor.

restaurant.name: Thai Town Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Thai Town Restaurant is an authentic Thai eatery on Vancouver's busy Granville Street, serving dishes like Traditional Pad Thai with tamarind, Red and Green Curries, Spicy Drunken Noodle, and Som-Tum. The kitchen emphasizes the classic Thai balance of sweet, umami, sour, and spicy. Online ordering with pickup is available, making it convenient for cyclists passing through central Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Cofee Loft
restaurant.desc: Cofee Loft is a neighbourhood cafe in Burnaby's Metrotown area serving coffee alongside a varied menu of salads, soups, sandwiches, cakes, and ice cream. It offers indoor seating in a smoke-free environment, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking for a sit-down meal or snack near the Metrotown corridor.

restaurant.name: JJ Bean
restaurant.desc: JJ Bean is a local coffee shop in Vancouver. For touring cyclists, it offers a practical stop to grab a quick beverage and rest from the road.

restaurant.name: Rusticana Coffee
restaurant.desc: Rusticana Coffee is a café located in Sidney, BC, a compact waterfront town on the Saanich Peninsula that serves as a gateway to the Gulf Islands ferry network and is popular with touring cyclists. The 'Ltd' in its Facebook name suggests an established local business rather than a pop-up or chain outlet. Sidney's walkable downtown core and proximity to the Lochside Regional Trail make cafés here natural rest stops for cyclists arriving or departing via the nearby ferry terminal.

restaurant.name: Trees Organic Coffee
restaurant.desc: Trees Organic Coffee is a Vancouver-area cafe chain that has been operating since 1996, known for its in-house roasted organic coffee and award-winning homemade cheesecakes voted best in Vancouver. The Gilmore location in Burnaby is one of 13–14 locations across the region. The menu extends beyond coffee to include sandwiches, baked goods, and a lunch selection, making it a practical stop for a mid-ride meal.

restaurant.name: Tacofino
restaurant.desc: Tacofino is a BC-born West Coast beach food chain with roots in Tofino, now operating multiple Lower Mainland locations including this White Rock outpost on Johnston Road. The restaurant serves Mexican-inspired fare with a casual, coastal vibe well suited to a post-ride meal. Pickup and third-party delivery options make it easy to grab food quickly and get back on the road.

restaurant.name: Uptown Sportsbar
restaurant.desc: Uptown Pizza & Sports Bar is Nelson's self-described only dedicated sports bar, housed within the Adventure Hotel on Vernon Street in the heart of downtown. The venue features wall-to-wall flat screens, a rotating lineup of BC craft beers on tap from breweries like Mt. Begbie, Four Winds, and Fernie Brewing, and a full pub menu of hand-made pizzas, burgers, and wings prepared by an in-house chef. Touring cyclists can also take advantage of takeout and delivery service if they prefer to eat elsewhere.

restaurant.name: The Eatery
restaurant.desc: The Eatery has been Kitsilano's home for creative sushi and Japanese fusion since 1983, earning a devoted local following over four decades on West Broadway. Billed as 'The Funkiest Place for Japanese Food,' it combines inventive rolls and Japanese dishes with a lively, music-filled atmosphere. A touring cyclist finishing a ride on the Arbutus Greenway or along the Vancouver waterfront would find it a well-placed stop for a sit-down meal or a takeout order.

restaurant.name: Subcity Donair
restaurant.desc: Subcity Donair is a multi-location Okanagan chain specializing in beef and chicken donairs made with a proprietary blend of 23 herbs and spices, served with a choice of seven sauces. The downtown Kelowna location sits on Bernard Avenue, the city's main commercial street, making it a convenient mid-ride stop. A dedicated vegetarian menu featuring falafel and veggie subs broadens its appeal to cyclists with varied dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website's About page highlights a dedicated 'Veggie Lovers' section including falafel, vegetarian pita, soups, and salads

restaurant.name: CRAFT Beer Market
restaurant.desc: CRAFT Beer Market sits right on Victoria Harbour, offering waterfront views from its surf lounge and an all-year patio. A full-service restaurant and bar with over 100 beers on tap, craft cocktails, and a sharing-style food menu, it is a lively chain destination known for its extensive draft selection and group-friendly spaces. Cyclists arriving at the Inner Harbour area will find it a substantial stop for a meal or post-ride drinks.

restaurant.name: Siam Le Bien Thai Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Siam Le Bien is an authentic Thai restaurant and bar established in 2023 on Burnaby's Hastings Street, named for Siam (the former name of Thailand) and the French word for 'good.' The kitchen emphasizes fresh, high-quality ingredients and a defining balance of sweetness, sourness, saltiness, spiciness, and umami across a wide menu of classic Thai dishes. Touring cyclists can dine in or order takeout via Uber Eats and DoorDash.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Delivery services available through Uber Eats and Doordash' and lists a separate 'Last call Take-Out 8.30 pm' time, confirming takeout service
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Lettuce Wrap: chicken / pork / Tofu' indicating at least one vegetarian protein option is available

restaurant.name: hoang gai
restaurant.desc: Hoang Gia is a Vietnamese restaurant in Kelowna near Costco on Highway 97 N, specializing in pho, sushi, and noodles. The restaurant distinguishes itself by using Brant Lake Wagyu Beef — naturally raised, hormone-free Alberta beef — in all beef dishes. Online reservations are available and the dining room is described as having a distinct atmosphere.

restaurant.name: Wendy's
restaurant.desc: Wendy's on Grandview Highway is a full-service fast food restaurant offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, salads, breakfast, and Frosty desserts. The location features a drive-through and supports mobile ordering and mobile payment. It is one of five Vancouver Wendy's locations and sits along a major east-west arterial road.

restaurant.name: Artisan Eats Café & Fine Foods
restaurant.desc: A French-inspired café perched on a small hill above the Snug Cove ferry landing on Bowen Island, with sweeping views of ocean, mountains, and forest. In operation since 2009, it draws both locals and visitors with fresh-baked breads, viennoiserie, rich lattes, and grilled paninis. For touring cyclists arriving by ferry, it offers a welcoming first stop with outdoor seating, Wi-Fi, and vegetarian and vegan options.

detail.address: 539 Artisan Lane, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: No gluten-free mention in OSM or website

restaurant.name: Boston Pizza
restaurant.desc: Boston Pizza is a well-established Canadian casual dining chain and sports bar serving gourmet pizzas, pasta, wings, and more, with roots going back to Edmonton in 1964. The Fort St. John location on Alaska Road North serves as a full sit-down restaurant with dine-in and delivery options. For touring cyclists passing through this northern BC hub on the Alaska Highway corridor, it offers a reliable, high-capacity meal stop with a broad menu.

detail.address: 9508 Alaska Road North, Fort St. John, V1J 6L5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'Vegan and Glutenwise® options also available'; nutritional page lists GlutenWise® as a dedicated menu section

restaurant.name: Poké Aye
restaurant.desc: Poké Aye is a Hawaiian-cuisine restaurant in Langford (Greater Victoria), specializing in poke bowls. Located in a unit-numbered commercial space (Unit 103), it sits in the western suburban corridor popular with cyclists commuting or touring between Langford and Victoria. The restaurant's name and Facebook branding are consistent with a contemporary, counter-service poke concept.

restaurant.name: Ministère of Seafood
restaurant.desc: Ministère of Seafood is a French-inspired seafood bistro in East Abbotsford, founded by Executive Red Seal Chef Gaya and General Manager Ishara, whose combined decades of experience span renowned hotels and restaurants worldwide. The menu centres on fresh BC seafood — spot prawns, halibut, Dungeness crab, and lobster — prepared with French and Italian technique, alongside a broad cocktail and wine program. It won a Community Votes Abbotsford 2025 award and offers family-sized take-home meals as well as a three-course dinner experience.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page marks multiple items (GF): Truffle Fries, Chicken Wings, Sautéed Calamari and Chorizo, Shrimp Scampi, Tuna Tataki, Oysters, soups, Nicoise Salad, Arugula Salad, and more. Vegetarian Flatbread and Vegetarian Linguine appear on the menu and happy hour pages

restaurant.name: Bozzini's
restaurant.desc: Bozzini's is a restaurant in North Vancouver with established operating hours and local service. A dining option for the community with both weekday and weekend availability.

restaurant.name: Snackshot
restaurant.desc: Snackshot is a Chinese and dessert-focused cafe on Kingsway in Vancouver. It offers a casual environment for customers seeking light meals and Asian sweets.

restaurant.name: Simonholt Food & Drink
restaurant.desc: Simonholt is a locally operated full-service restaurant in Nanaimo's north end, featuring a mainly from-scratch kitchen with a focus on fresh local seafood, an extensive wine selection, and a fully stocked bar. The restaurant offers three patios including a rooftop deck with ocean and mountain views, and can accommodate groups of up to 150 for corporate and club events. It regularly hosts live music from local and touring artists, giving it a lively community atmosphere well beyond a typical dinner stop.

restaurant.name: Wendy's Drive-Thru
restaurant.desc: A Wendy's fast food location on Hawthorne Avenue in Abbotsford offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, salads, and breakfast. The restaurant operates a drive-thru as well as dine-in seating and supports mobile ordering and payment. For a touring cyclist passing through the Abbotsford area, it offers a reliable late-night food option with free Wi-Fi.

restaurant.name: Aroy Thai
restaurant.desc: Aroy Thai Kitchen is a family-owned Thai restaurant situated in Rocky Point Centre in Port Moody, where 'aroy' means 'delicious' in Thai. The kitchen prides itself on fresh, locally sourced vegetables picked daily and house-made sauces, dressings, and hand-rolled spring rolls prepared from scratch each day. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down restaurant offering both dine-in and takeout, with delivery available through Skip The Dishes and DoorDash.

detail.address: 1-2816 St Johns Street, Port Moody, BC V3H 2C1

restaurant.name: Bean to Cup
restaurant.desc: Bean to Cup is a specialty coffee house in Vernon that has been roasting its own beans since 1998 — notably, it claims to be the only specialty coffee bar in the North Okanagan doing so in-house. The cafe offers gourmet espresso drinks alongside a full breakfast and lunch menu of wraps, paninis, soups, and fresh-baked pastries, set in a space that includes a garden patio. It has earned three consecutive TripAdvisor Certificates of Excellence (2017–2019) and accepts Bitcoin Lightning payments.

restaurant.name: Sushi Q
restaurant.desc: Sushi-Q is a Canadian chain founded in 1997 and one of the country's early pioneers of grab-and-go sushi, serving sushi rolls, sashimi, nigiri, and Japanese ramen. The Burnaby outlet is located inside Lougheed Town Centre mall. The chain emphasises fresh daily preparation and chef-inspired presentation as its main differentiators.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Veggie Combo, Avocado Roll Plus, Avocado Maki Plus, Kappa Maki Plus, Avocado Cucumber Plus, and Seaweed Salad — multiple vegetarian options confirmed

restaurant.name: Van 168 Coffee
restaurant.desc: Van 168 Coffee is a family-run Vietnamese cafe and restaurant on Kingsway founded by Lynda, who brought her mother's Northern Vietnamese recipes to Vancouver nearly 40 years after immigrating. The menu centres on authentic pho, bun noodle soups (including regional specialties like Bun Bo Hue and freshwater snail vermicelli), rice plates, and Vietnamese iced coffee. It opened in 2023 and occupies a storefront unit in a mixed-use building on one of Vancouver's main east-side corridors.

restaurant.name: Quality Coffee Systems
restaurant.desc: Established in 1998, Quality Coffee Systems is the official JURA Hospitality and Service Centre for Western Canada, operating a public showroom in Burnaby where visitors can see live espresso machine demonstrations and receive expert guidance on commercial and residential equipment. The company carries premium European brands including JURA, Profitec, Olympia Express, and Rocket, alongside coffee beans, grinders, and accessories. A touring cyclist could stop in to purchase coffee beans or small accessories, though this is fundamentally a specialty equipment retailer and repair shop rather than a place to get a drink.

restaurant.name: Dining Commons
restaurant.desc: The Dining Commons is Capilano University's main on-campus cafeteria in North Vancouver, housed in a two-storey building serving the university community. It is listed under CapU's student services as the primary food and dining destination on campus. Cyclists in the North Shore area may find it a convenient stop given its location on an established university campus.

restaurant.name: Moore's Bakery
restaurant.desc: Moore's Bakery of Kerrisdale is one of Vancouver's oldest storefronts, operating since the 1930s with Dutch and British baking traditions passed down through a family-owned business. The bakery produces handmade breads, buns, pastries, cakes, cookies, and savoury items fresh daily on site. A touring cyclist passing through Kerrisdale will find a genuine neighbourhood institution offering hearty baked goods well suited for fuelling a ride.

restaurant.name: Oretachi Curry
restaurant.desc: Oretachi Curry is the Canadian outpost of an Osaka, Japan original, serving authentic Japanese curry rice and a signature curry ramen built on a house-made shrimp oil and ebi miso broth. Every order gets a freshly panko-fried katsu made in-house, and the curry blend draws on over 20 spices with locally sourced BC ingredients. The restaurant sits in the Riley Park stretch of Main Street, one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors, and offers online ordering and takeout for riders on the move.

restaurant.name: N.S.C.S. Discovery Café
restaurant.desc: N.S.C.S. Discovery Café is a burger and American food restaurant in Vancouver staffed by culinary school students. It offers a casual dining experience with outdoor seating and is licensed with beer on tap, making it a welcoming stop for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Pacifico Pizzeria & Ristorante
restaurant.desc: Pacifico Pizzeria & Ristorante is a downtown Vancouver Italian restaurant that combines Pacific Northwest ingredients with traditional Italian recipes and has earned recognition as Vancouver's Best Pizzeria. The Smithe Street location offers dine-in and online takeout or delivery, with a second outpost near English Bay on Davie Street. It sits in the heart of the city core, making it a practical meal stop for cyclists on urban routes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: No GF information available from website or OSM

restaurant.name: Shio Japanese Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Shio Japanese Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant that opened on The High Street in Coquitlam in May 2018, serving a mix of traditional sushi and original dishes like the Katsu Burger. It sits in a busy commercial hub near Douglas College, Lafarge Lake, and Coquitlam Centre, with free underground parking accessible off Atlantic Ave. Dine-in and takeout are both available, with Uber Eats delivery as well.

detail.address: 102 – 1168 The High Street, Coquitlam, BC V3B 0C6

restaurant.name: Abbondanza
restaurant.desc: A pizza restaurant in Ucluelet on the west coast of Vancouver Island. Situated along the route to the Pacific Rim region, it could be a convenient dinner stop for cyclists touring the area.

detail.address: 1972 Peninsula Road A, Ucluelet, BC V0R 3A0

restaurant.name: Bánh Mì 64
restaurant.desc: A Vietnamese sandwich shop specializing in bánh mì (traditional Vietnamese sandwiches) in Chilliwack. Operates as a fast-food takeout establishment serving fresh sandwich fare to locals and travelers.

restaurant.name: Shanghai Dumpling King
restaurant.desc: Shanghai Dumpling King is an authentic Shanghai pot sticker restaurant in Richmond specializing in Huaiyang-style dumplings with thin wrappers, crisp bottoms, and abundant juices. The owner hand-grinds the meat and hand-rolls the wrappers, blending traditional Shanghai pot sticker technique with northeastern Chinese dumpling influences. Cyclists passing through Richmond's Westminster Highway corridor can order online for quick pick-up.

restaurant.name: Diplomat Bakery
restaurant.desc: Diplomat Bakery is a family-owned European-style dessert bakery operating since 1996, specializing in luxury cakes, cheesecakes, and espresso-based drinks. Located on London Road in Richmond near the Dyke Road entrance, it sits close to popular cycling routes along the Richmond dyke trail system. Cyclists can stop in for a range of coffee drinks, cakes by the slice, or pre-order whole cakes for pickup.

restaurant.name: Freddy's Brewpub
restaurant.desc: Freddy's Brewpub is a pub located in Kelowna on McCurdy Road. The name and amenity tags suggest it operates as both a craft brewery and public house. Limited verifiable information is available due to website access issues.

restaurant.name: Cibo & Vine Ristorante
restaurant.desc: Cibo & Vine Ristorante is an Italian restaurant on Beach Avenue in Peachland, serving housemade pasta, artisan pizza, and an extensive drinks list anchored by Okanagan wines. The restaurant operates two outdoor patios overlooking Lake Okanagan and the boutiques along Beach Ave, making it a scenic lakeshore stop on the Okanagan cycling corridor. It was formerly known as The Waterfront Grill & Pizzeria.

detail.address: #5842 B, Beach Ave, Peachland, BC V0H 1X7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'We are able to offer many gluten friendly options but are not Celiac friendly.'

restaurant.name: Cookie's Ice Cream Co.
restaurant.desc: Cookie's Ice Cream Co. is a family-owned, small-batch ice cream shop in the historic Ladner Village neighbourhood of Delta, offering premium barrel-churned ice cream, sorbet, and sherbet across 90+ rotating flavours served in cups, cones, or house-made cookies. Beyond the scoop shop, they operate a mobile fleet — trailer, truck, and tricycle — serving events across the Lower Mainland. Specialty items include made-in-house ice cream sandwiches and cakes, hot chocolate bombs, and custom decorated sugar cookies.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists sorbets and sherbets among offerings, and mobile fleet page explicitly names 'sorbet' as a product category

restaurant.name: Le Marché St. George
restaurant.desc: Le Marché St. George is a home-based café and general store in Vancouver that also serves as an occasional event space. The business blends residential and commercial functions in a community-oriented model. Touring cyclists can visit for refreshments, food, and locally-sourced supplies.

restaurant.name: Kulinarya Filipino Eatery
restaurant.desc: Kulinarya is an authentic Filipino restaurant established in 2009 on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, cooking family recipes anchored in fresh local ingredients. It is known for dishes like kare-kare and sinigang, as well as a communal Kamayan feast served directly on banana leaves. The restaurant offers both dine-in and takeout, making it a viable stop for cyclists riding one of Vancouver's most active commercial corridors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu annotations confirm with '(V)' (vegetarian) and '(VO)' (vegan option) labels on multiple dishes. No gluten-free mention found

restaurant.name: Sushi Garden
restaurant.desc: Sushi Garden is a Japanese restaurant chain with three Burnaby locations, offering a broad sushi menu in a casual sit-down setting. The Brentwood branch is located on Lougheed Highway near Brentwood Town Centre, on a major arterial route through Burnaby. Online ordering and takeout are available at all branches.

restaurant.name: Oliver's Tearoom
restaurant.desc: Oliver's Tearoom is the High Tea section of Dickens Sweets and British Museum, an immersive British-themed complex in downtown Chilliwack that also houses a Victorian-era museum, a replica Tally Ho pub, Pickwick's Pie Shop, and a British sweet and grocery shop. The multi-storey museum takes visitors through Royal history, a vintage office, Fred's Toyshop, and a Titanic exhibit. Cycling visitors can pick up takeout savories — sausage rolls, steak pies, and baked goods — from Pickwick's, making it an unusual and memorable detour.

restaurant.name: Fern Cafe and Bakery
restaurant.desc: Fern Cafe and Bakery is a 100% vegan bakery cafe tucked into the Fernwood neighbourhood of Victoria, established in 2018 and owner-operated by a couple with over a decade of plant-based cooking experience. The menu leans into vegan comfort food — burgers, poutine, mac and cheese, fried chickun, all-day breakfast — alongside specialty pastries and espresso drinks made entirely in-house from scratch. Their famously oversized cinnamon buns and fresh-daily doughnuts have earned a strong local following, making it a worthwhile stop for plant-based touring cyclists passing through central Victoria.

detail.address: 1-1115 North Park Street, Victoria, BC V8W 1C7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Allergies page states 'Everything on our menu is vegan and made in house.' Menu lists several gluten-free items (e.g. Jackfruit Scrambler labelled 'Gluten free'; Crafty Mac offered with gluten-free noodles)

restaurant.name: Southside Diner
restaurant.desc: A Whistler institution since 2003, the Southside Diner serves hearty homestyle breakfasts and burgers in an old-school diner atmosphere at Whistler's Creekside neighbourhood. The building also houses Southside Suds, described as Creekside's only coin-operated laundromat, making it an unusually practical stop for multi-day touring cyclists who need to refresh their kit. The diner has cultivated a loyal following among both locals and visitors over more than two decades.

detail.address: 2102 Lake Placid Rd, Creekside, Whistler, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a labeled 'VEGAN VEGGIE WRAP', a vegetarian 'BUDDHA BOWL' (mushroom, avocado, carrot, cucumber, rice & quinoa), and a 'VEGGI-LICOUS' Eggs Benedict option with grilled mushrooms and greens

restaurant.name: Big Star Sandwich Co.
restaurant.desc: Big Star Sandwich Co. is a Lower Mainland sandwich chain founded in 2013, now operating six locations including this Langley outpost. Sandwiches are built on fresh-baked filone bread with meats cooked in-house — beef slow-roasted overnight for 13 hours, hand-pulled turkey breast, and authentically prepared corned beef. Catering is available for groups, and a loyalty rewards program makes it a worthwhile repeat stop on a multi-day tour through the Fraser Valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website. No gluten-free claim found

restaurant.name: Brass Monkey Taproom
restaurant.desc: Brass Monkey Taproom is a craft microbrewery and taproom on Bay Street in Victoria, brewing its own beer on-site and serving a food menu that includes burgers and wings. The venue runs a packed weekly events calendar — trivia leagues, specialty cask tappings, bingo nights, and live DJ sets — giving it a lively neighbourhood pub atmosphere. It sits a short ride from Victoria's inner harbour in a mixed residential-commercial area, making it a natural end-of-ride destination for cyclists exploring the city.

restaurant.name: Basalt Wine
restaurant.desc: Basalt Wine & Salumeria is a dine-in restaurant and wine bar located in the heart of Whistler Village, describing itself as 'Authentic. Lively. Local.' The salumeria focus suggests a menu centred on cured meats, charcuterie, and wine. Outdoor seating makes it a pleasant stop after a ride through the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

restaurant.name: McClennan Car/Truck Stop
restaurant.desc: McClennan Car/Truck Stop is a casual family dining restaurant and truck stop located on McLennan Road on the outskirts of Valemount, BC. Positioned along a route through the Robson Valley, it serves travellers — including those passing through on Highway 5 — looking for a sit-down meal. The 'Where You're Part Of the Family' tagline suggests a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere typical of rural BC roadside stops.

restaurant.name: Secret Zone
restaurant.desc: Secret Zone Bar & Grill is a neighbourhood sports bar near the Burquitlam SkyTrain station serving wings, burgers, pasta, and cocktails. It screens major sporting events including UFC, Champions League, NHL, NBA, and the World Cup. Online ordering and pickup make it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Burquitlam corridor.

restaurant.name: Bodega
restaurant.desc: Bodega on Main is an updated take on a long-standing Vancouver Spanish tapas institution, serving authentic tapas made with locally sourced and specialty imported ingredients, including OceanWise certified seafood. The 75-seat lounge and dining area features custom leather seating, hand-carved bar stools, and a blend of vintage artwork and antique accents. Touring cyclists will find a full-service sit-down restaurant with a well-stocked bar, takeout options, and delivery partnerships.

restaurant.name: The Corner Stone Bistro
restaurant.desc: The Corner Stone Bistro is a casual coffee shop and cafe in North Vancouver that welcomes the cycling community. It offers a comfortable outdoor seating area and complimentary Wi-Fi—practical amenities for touring cyclists looking for a break.

detail.address: 1096 W 22 St, District of North Vancouver, V7P 2E5

restaurant.name: Tamam
restaurant.desc: Tamam is a fine-dining Palestinian restaurant on East Hastings Street in Vancouver, serving scratch-made dishes such as freekeh with lamb shanks, fried Mediterranean sea bass, kibbeh, and kunafah alongside Lebanese arak and BC VQA wines. The restaurant operates as a cultural gathering space and regularly runs community fundraisers with proceeds directed to Gaza. A touring cyclist will find a thoughtful menu with clearly labelled vegan and gluten-free options, catering available, and online ordering.

detail.address: 2616 East Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V5K 1Z6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items explicitly labelled '(vegan, gf)': falafel, stuffed cabbage rolls, tabbouleh, mujaddarah, humus. Vegetarian chicken kebab listed as a category

restaurant.name: Cafe de Gourmet
restaurant.desc: Café de Gourmet is an award-winning neighbourhood sandwich café in Ladner, BC, operated by the same owners since they purchased it years ago. Everything is made fresh daily in-house, from handcrafted sandwiches and home-style soups to baked goods from their own bakery. Located in the heart of Ladner near South Delta cycling routes, it offers a full espresso bar and call-ahead takeout for cyclists in a hurry.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Plant-based and gluten-free options confirmed; menu lists vegetarian sandwiches and GF bread options (white buns or focaccia)

restaurant.name: Donair Affair
restaurant.desc: Donair Affair is a BC-based fast-food chain approaching 25 years in operation, specializing in donair kebabs that blend Middle Eastern and Canadian flavors using beef, lamb, chicken, or falafel. The Maple Ridge location on Dewdney Trunk Road is one of more than 20 outlets across the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley. It offers a casual sit-down atmosphere alongside takeout and online ordering, making it a convenient stop for a filling wrap or platter mid-ride.

detail.address: 22645 Dewdney Trunk Rd #108, Maple Ridge, BC V2X 3K3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website front page states 'vegetarian choices as well' and describes falafel as 'a vegan and protein-rich option'; dedicated Veggie Falafel category on menu

restaurant.name: Sisters Family Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A family restaurant in Coldstream offering regional cuisine with outdoor seating and takeaway service. The venue is wheelchair-accessible with customer washrooms and welcomes both dine-in and take-away customers.

detail.address: 2G0, 1920 Vernon St, Lumby, BC V0E 2G0, Canada

restaurant.name: Rocky Point Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Rocky Point Ice Cream started as a small scoop shack at Rocky Point Park in Port Moody in 1997 and has grown into a beloved multi-location artisan ice cream brand — operating BC's first licensed dairy plant dedicated exclusively to craft ice cream production. The original Port Moody location sits right in Rocky Point Park, making it a natural and satisfying stop for cyclists on the area's waterfront trails. All ice cream is handcrafted from scratch, with rotating seasonal flavours and a permanent selection that includes plant-based options.

detail.address: 2800 Murray St, Port Moody, BC V3H 1X2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Plant-based options confirmed: 'Plant-Based Blackberry Crumble: Plant-based coconut vanilla ice cream' listed as a current seasonal flavour; trucks offer '3 plant-based/sorbet options'

restaurant.name: Dining Wok Shanghai Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Dining Wok Shanghai Restaurant is a casual dine-in Chinese restaurant in White Rock specializing in Sichuan, Peking, and Shanghai cuisine. The relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere makes it a comfortable stop for a sit-down meal. Online ordering is available for those who prefer takeout.

detail.address: 15246 Russell Ave, White Rock, BC V4B 2P6

restaurant.name: Papa John's
restaurant.desc: Papa John's is an international pizza chain with over 5,000 locations in 44 countries, emphasizing fresh dough and quality ingredients under the 'Better Ingredients. Better Pizza.' brand promise. This Chilliwack location at McCallum Road offers carryout and delivery pizza. It is a familiar, predictable refuelling option for touring cyclists moving through the Fraser Valley corridor.

restaurant.name: Scratch Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Scratch Kitchen is a North Shore artisan pizza restaurant that started in Deep Cove in 2018 and expanded to Central Lonsdale in 2024, built around made-from-scratch food using fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The menu spans creative 12-inch pizzas, sharing plates, salads, and rice bowls, with a carefully curated list of local craft beer and BC wine. Both locations offer strong plant-based and gluten-free options throughout the menu, making it a flexible stop for cyclists with dietary needs.

detail.address: 437 Dollarton Highway North, North Vancouver, BC V7G 1M9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'we also cater to plant lovers'; menu items marked * 'can be made 100% plant based'; 'ALL OF OUR PIZZAS CAN BE MADE GLUTEN FREE'; vegan cashew mozza substitution available; multiple GF and DF salads and bowls listed

restaurant.name: The Copper Room
restaurant.desc: The Copper Room is the signature evening dining venue at Harrison Hot Springs Resort & Spa, situated on the shores of Harrison Lake beneath the Coastal Mountains. It offers a multi-format dinner menu (à la carte, table d'hôte, children's menu, and a drink menu) alongside nightly live music and an open dance floor, making it one of the more theatrical dining experiences in the Fraser Valley. A touring cyclist arriving here would find a polished, reservation-required dinner room inside a full-service resort rather than a casual stop.

restaurant.name: Hime Sushi
restaurant.desc: Hime Sushi is a Japanese restaurant on East Broadway in Vancouver, serving an extensive menu of sushi rolls, nigiri, sashimi, and cooked Japanese dishes such as tonkatsu and chicken karaage. The restaurant is open daily and offers both dine-in and takeout, with delivery also available through third-party services. It sits on a busy commercial corridor convenient to cyclists riding the Broadway route.

restaurant.name: D'oro Gelato e Caffè
restaurant.desc: D'oro Gelato e Caffè is a multiple-award-winning Italian gelateria and full-service café on Denman Street, producing small-batch handmade gelato and sorbetto daily from original Sicilian recipes. Beyond gelato, it serves full meals including freshly baked pastries, paninos, soups, and salads alongside artisan espresso drinks from Seattle-based Caffè Umbria. Situated close to Stanley Park and the Seawall, it sits along one of Vancouver's most popular recreational cycling corridors.

restaurant.name: OEB Breakfast Co.
restaurant.desc: OEB Breakfast Co. is a chef-driven Canadian breakfast and brunch chain founded in Calgary in 2009 by classically trained Chef Mauro Martina, built on a farm-to-table philosophy emphasizing locally sourced Canadian ingredients. The Langley location is part of a growing national network, serving inventive dishes such as breakfast poutines, chef-crafted eggs bennies, and bold blue plate specials alongside familiar classics. OSM records outdoor seating at this location, offering a comfortable al fresco option for cyclists looking to fuel up on a ride through the Fraser Valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Calgary menu lists gluten-friendly pesto potatoes and gluten-free English muffin substitutions, plus vegetarian-friendly dishes including avocado toast and chia seed pudding

restaurant.name: Beach Ave Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: Beach Ave Bar & Grill is a full-service bar and restaurant situated on Beach Avenue in Vancouver, steps from the English Bay waterfront and the popular Seawall cycling corridor. The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists riding the waterfront route. The menu spans food and drinks with a dedicated weekend brunch program.

restaurant.name: Ice Cream Mountain
restaurant.desc: Ice Cream Mountain is a Kawartha Dairy retail outlet on the Trans-Canada Highway on the western edge of Victoria, BC, selling scoops and packaged products from this Ontario-based family dairy that has been crafting ice cream since the 1950s. As a dedicated branded retail store, it carries the full Kawartha lineup including flavoured ice creams and ice cream cakes. Its position on the Trans-Canada places it directly along the corridor cyclists use when travelling between Victoria and the western communities of the Capital Regional District.

restaurant.name: Niji
restaurant.desc: Niji is an Asian restaurant situated on Dunsmuir Avenue in Cumberland, a village well known as a mountain biking hub on Vancouver Island. The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a welcoming spot to wind down after a ride. It operates out of a two-storey retail building in the village core.

restaurant.name: Simply Delicious
restaurant.desc: Simply Delicious is a Chinese restaurant on Main Street in Vancouver serving a loyal neighbourhood crowd. It offers a daily happy hour and positions itself as a late-night dining destination. The 'SD FAM' sign-off on the website suggests a tight-knit, community-oriented vibe.

restaurant.name: Steamworks
restaurant.desc: Steamworks is a landmark Gastown brew pub operating since 1995, credited as the first urban brew pub in Canada, spread across 8,191 square feet on two floors overlooking Vancouver Harbour. The steam-powered brewery pours 20 rotating taps — including year-round core beers, seasonals, and Brew Pub exclusives — best sampled through their signature 10 Tap Taster Paddle. Heated and covered patios, a full food menu ranging from pub classics to plant-based dishes, and a heritage Gastown location just off the Seaside Greenway make it a natural destination stop for touring cyclists.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly mentions 'modern plant-based creations like the Vegan Goddess Bowl' alongside classic pub fare, confirming plant-based/vegan menu options

restaurant.name: Indian Masala Express
restaurant.desc: Indian Masala Express is an Indian fine dining restaurant in Squamish offering Northern and Southern Indian cuisine alongside modern Mumbai fusion dishes, all prepared with house-blended herbs and spices. The restaurant operates its own Kismet wine label and offers curated Indian food and wine pairings, which sets it apart from typical Indian restaurants. The restaurant is walk-in only with no reservations accepted, and has a garden out back.

Regular weekly events—trivia nights, music bingo, and Beyblade battles—make it a lively community gathering spot that a cyclist looking for a long, restorative stop would enjoy.

Touring cyclists passing through Kimberley will find a welcoming spot with friendly service and hearty, satisfying meals well-suited to refueling after a long day in the saddle.

restaurant.name: Saigon Char-broil

All three locations offer takeout, including through third-party delivery apps.

The business is a certified BC Green Business and sources high-quality local ingredients.

restaurant.name: Greek House Restaurant

Owner and executive chef Christos Vassilopoulos prepares authentic dishes — souvlaki, spanakopita, keftethes, and roast lamb — entirely from scratch using fresh ingredients. The restaurant is popular enough that its branded products now appear in regional supermarkets and specialty stores, making it a genuine culinary landmark for touring cyclists passing through Lake Country.

An attached cold beer and liquor store next door rounds out the offering for visitors looking to extend the evening.

restaurant.name: Kafka's Coffee

The company actively supports local artists with rotating gallery exhibitions across its locations and runs a wholesale and franchising program. Cyclists passing through downtown Vancouver will find a community-focused café with both indoor and outdoor seating and a full all-day food menu.

restaurant.name: Shanghai Fortune Cuisine

Cyclists riding the Kingsway route have a range of hot, filling options available for quick pickup.

Cyclists passing through Gastown will find a full sit-down meal with vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options, steps from the waterfront.

restaurant.name: Chance Cafe

The menu spans daily breakfast sandwiches, wraps, soups, stir fries, grab-and-go bowls, and a signature line of cashew-based cheesecakes available for drop-in or pre-order. The name (French for 'mix') reflects its blending of culinary backgrounds and scratch-made approach, from house-infused cocktails to rotating oyster selections. restaurant.name: Dragon Bowl

The kitchen turns out brunch, lunch, and dinner all made from scratch, with a dog-friendly patio for those traveling with four-legged companions. The venue also operates an on-site cocktail speakeasy called Nigel's Cocktails, adding a distinctive evening dimension to what is otherwise a full-day food-and-drink destination.

restaurant.name: Transylvanian Traditions Bakery
restaurant.desc: Transylvanian Traditions Bakery is a Romanian-inspired specialty dessert shop on Vancouver's Davie Street, open since February 2008. It is one of the first establishments in Canada to make Kürtőskalács (chimney cake), a traditional sweet spiral pastry glazed with caramel and crushed walnuts, alongside more than a dozen preservative-free European cakes. The bakery has been featured in the Vancouver Sun and is considered one of Vancouver's premier dessert destinations.

restaurant.name: Paratha 2 Pasta

A catering program with food truck and live-catering options, plus online ordering, rounds out a well-established multi-branch operation.

restaurant.name: FUNK coffee bar

Its location near UBC makes it a convenient refuelling stop on routes through the west side.
