restaurant.desc: Golden City is a Chinese restaurant situated on Fisgard Street in Victoria's historic Chinatown neighbourhood, one of the oldest in Canada. The restaurant offers a broad Cantonese and Szechuan menu spanning soups, chow mein, seafood, and combo plates, with online ordering and fast pickup available. Its location at the edge of downtown makes it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the inner harbour or the surrounding neighbourhoods.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu legend includes a vegetarian marker; confirmed vegetarian dishes include Vegetable Chow Mein, Vegetable Fried Rice, Stir Fried Tofu with Vegetable, Sweet & Sour Tofu, and multiple mushroom dishes

restaurant.name: A Bite Of SHUNDE
restaurant.desc: A Bite of Shunde is a Chinese restaurant in Richmond, BC, specializing in cuisine from Shunde — a district in Guangdong province renowned as a cradle of Cantonese cooking. Richmond's dense concentration of authentic regional Chinese restaurants makes this part of a notable food destination for cyclists exploring the area. Touring cyclists passing through on the River Road or Garden City corridors have a range of nearby dining options, with this spot representing a more specialized regional offering.

restaurant.name: Tak Fook Noodle & Congee Shop
restaurant.desc: Tak Fook Noodle & Congee Shop (徳福麵家) is a Cantonese fast-food counter in Richmond's busy Number 3 Road commercial corridor, specializing in noodles and congee. It sits within a multi-unit retail complex and caters primarily to the local Chinese community with traditional comfort food. For touring cyclists passing through Richmond, it offers a quick, inexpensive, and filling meal option in one of the region's densest food districts.

restaurant.name: Panago
restaurant.desc: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain with a Duncan location offering takeout and delivery of fresh-dough pizzas made with Canadian wheat and organic tomato sauce. The chain emphasizes Canadian-sourced ingredients and carries a broad range of plant-based, dairy-free, and meat-free menu options. For a touring cyclist passing through Duncan, it is a convenient fast-food stop with familiar options and reliable hours.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Plant-based options... abundant veggie, dairy-free and meat-free choices.' Gluten-free not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: AMJ Pizza & Curry House
restaurant.desc: A fast-food restaurant in Chilliwack serving pizza and curry. It offers quick-service ordering and casual dining, making it accessible for brief stops during cycling tours. The combination of pizza and curry is relatively uncommon for a fast-food establishment.

restaurant.name: Garrick's Head
restaurant.desc: Garrick's Head is one of the oldest English pubs in Canada, operating continuously in Victoria's historic Bastion Square since 1867 and claiming Vancouver Island's largest selection of craft and import beer on tap. The two-storey pub features a wood-burning fireplace, a 2012-expanded front dining room, and a sunny outdoor patio overlooking the square — a natural rest stop after riding through the Inner Harbour area. Traditional English pub fare and an extensive rotating draught list make it a well-rounded stop for hungry and thirsty touring cyclists.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian options: House Greens salad, Beet Salad, Waffle Yam Fries, Bowl O' Fries, Mac & Cheese, Fried Pickles. No explicit vegan or GF labeling found

restaurant.name: Screamers Soft Serve & Treats
restaurant.desc: Screamers Soft Serve & Treats is an ice cream shop located in Steveston, the historic fishing village at the south end of Richmond, a popular destination for cyclists riding the dyke trails and waterfront paths of the Lower Mainland. The shop's location in a well-travelled tourist and recreational area makes it a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring the region.

restaurant.name: Daikichi Sushi
restaurant.desc: Daikichi Sushi is a compact Japanese restaurant on Burrard Street in Vancouver offering a broad menu of sushi rolls, sashimi, ramen, teriyaki bowls, and tempura. The shop supports online ordering with a pickup window, making it a practical quick-stop option. Vegetarian diners are well accommodated with dedicated tofu, vegetable, and plant-based menu items throughout the menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes vegetarian-labelled items such as Veggie Gyoza, Tofu Salad, Tofu Teriyaki Don, Vegetable Udon, and Vegetable Yakisoba

restaurant.name: Cap'n Hook Cappuccino & Fishing Gear
restaurant.desc: Cap'n Hook is a distinctly west-coast hybrid: a fishing supply shop and coffee bar rolled into one, located in Ucluelet on Vancouver Island's rugged outer coast. The café pours Creekmore's certified organic coffee, locally roasted on the Island, with the option to linger over a harbour view or grab a cup to go. The quirky pairing of fishing tackle, frozen bait, and specialty espresso makes it a memorable and characterful stop for cyclists passing through 'Ukee.'

detail.address: Shop 4 - 1920 Lyche Road, Box 341, Ucluelet, BC V0R 3A0

restaurant.name: New Brandiz Fast Food
restaurant.desc: New Brandiz Fast Food is a fast food spot on East Hastings Street in Vancouver's busy urban corridor. The restaurant offers indoor seating and has an ATM on site, making it a handy stop for cyclists who need cash or a sit-down break. Its location on Hastings places it along a common east-west cycling route through the city.

restaurant.name: Bray's
restaurant.desc: Bray's is a West Coast tapas restaurant and wine bar rooted in the Bray family's multi-generational history in Victoria, dating back to Richard Bray's arrival in 1882. The menu celebrates local BC produce and seafood through family-style sharing plates, with an extensive wine list spanning local vineyards and international wineries. It occupies a cozy yet contemporary space in downtown Victoria, making it a solid post-ride dining option in the heart of the city.

restaurant.name: RedBeef Noodle Kitchen
restaurant.desc: RedBeef Noodle Kitchen is a Taiwanese beef noodle restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street, specializing in handcrafted soups built from slow-boiled beef bone broth simmered for over 12 hours with exotic Chinese spices. The menu spans more than two dozen noodle preparations alongside rice bowls, dumplings, and desserts, reflecting serious culinary craft rooted in a Taiwanese tradition. Multiple branch locations and an online ordering option make it a substantive dining stop for cyclists moving through the Main Street corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Signature Vegetarian Noodle Soup (紅燒素食湯麵), Vegetarian Dry Noodles (素食乾拌麵), and Teriyaki Tofu Rice (照燒豆腐飯)

restaurant.name: Galini's
restaurant.desc: Galini Greek Kouzina is a family-run sit-down Greek restaurant on Fraser Highway in Surrey, rooted in the culinary traditions of Epirus, Greece and open since 2005. The menu spans a full mezedes program — calamari, saganaki flambé, spanakopita, and a signature pulled lamb poutine — through to souvlaki and grilled steaks. The two-storey building also houses event ballrooms used for wedding receptions and catering, giving the restaurant a notably larger footprint than a typical neighbourhood Greek spot.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegetarian menu items confirmed: spanakopita, Greek salad, balsamic hummus, tzatziki, spinach & artichoke dip, zucchini wedge, saganaki. House salad dressing explicitly described as 'Gluten-free, dairy-free, trans-fat free.'

restaurant.name: Pita Pit
restaurant.desc: Pita Pit is a Canadian fast-casual chain serving customizable pita sandwiches, salads, and rice bowls built from fresh ingredients. Located in Fort St. John in northeastern BC, it sits along a key supply corridor for cyclists riding the Alaska Highway region. The menu spans meat, falafel, and build-your-own options with smoothies and desserts also available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Signature menu includes Spicy Falafel (vegetarian); build-your-own options allow further customization. No explicit vegan or GF labelling

restaurant.name: L'Apéro
restaurant.desc: L'Apéro Wine & Cheese Bistro is a French-inspired wine and cheese restaurant in downtown Victoria built around the French apéro tradition of drinks, small plates, and convivial evenings. Founded by Guillaume, a Lyon-raised cheesemonger, the bistro serves lunch, dinner, and weekend brunch centered on artisan cheeses, charcuterie, raclette, and French bistro classics. The in-store and online shop sells ready-made cheese and charcuterie boards billed as perfect for a picnic, making it a tempting resupply stop for touring cyclists.

notes.Packed lunches: Website offers ready-made cheese and charcuterie boards under 'Boards & Picnic' navigation, described as 'perfect for a picnic, appies with friends, corporate events or family celebrations.'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page explicitly lists 'Vegan Vegetarian' as menu filter categories and states 'Most dishes can be made Gluten Free.'

restaurant.name: Milestones
restaurant.desc: Milestones is a Canadian bar-and-grill chain offering familiar North American cuisine with a refined twist, operating out of a two-storey retail building on Barnet Highway in Coquitlam. The restaurant features a full sit-down dining room and bar, making it a reasonable stop for a meal after a ride through the Tri-Cities area. Online ordering and delivery are supported, indicating takeout is also an option.

restaurant.name: Bucky's West Coast Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Bucky's is an artisan hearth-style pizzeria serving hand-tossed and thin-crust pizzas from a large menu of specialty pies and build-your-own options. Located near the South Surrey/White Rock border, it offers counter pickup as well as delivery through Uber Eats, Skip the Dishes, and DoorDash. A touring cyclist fueling up for the road would find a broad menu including gluten-free crust and a dedicated veggie option.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu states 'GLUTEN FREE AVAILABLE IN A 10.5 INCH SIZE'; Veggie Supreme pizza listed; no explicit vegan claim

restaurant.name: Kin Thai Kitchen & Bar
restaurant.desc: Kin Thai Kitchen is an authentic Thai restaurant situated in the Morgan Crossing area of Grandview Corners in South Surrey, offering an extensive menu of classic Thai dishes with a customizable spice-level system ranging from mild to Thai Hot. The restaurant accommodates individuals and groups alike, and can host private and business functions. Both dine-in and takeout are available, and the menu includes vegetarian and gluten-free options alongside traditional Thai cocktails and a wine list.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About Us page states 'Our menu, including vegetarian and gluten-free options, is also available for take-out.' Menu includes a dedicated Vegetarian Delight dish and spring rolls marked as veg

restaurant.name: Browns Crafthouse Kitchen & Bar;Browns Crafthouse
restaurant.desc: Browns Crafthouse on Main Street is a full-service kitchen and bar operated by Browns Restaurant Group, a BC-based multi-location chain with outlets from Fort St. John to Victoria. Situated at the intersection of Main Street and East 16th Avenue in Vancouver, it offers a sit-down dining experience spanning a full food menu, weekend brunch, and a dedicated beer menu. For a touring cyclist passing through Vancouver's Main Street corridor, it offers a substantial mid-ride or end-of-day meal option in a neighbourhood setting.

restaurant.name: John 3:16 Malaysian Delights
restaurant.desc: John 3:16 Malaysian Delights is a multi-location Malaysian restaurant group that originated in Richmond in 2014 and expanded to West Broadway in Vancouver. The menu spans classic Malaysian dishes including Beef Rendang, Hainanese Chicken, Nasi Lemak, and a range of noodle and rice plates. Online ordering is available directly through the restaurant's website for the Vancouver location.

restaurant.name: The Coriander Indian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Coriander Indian is a sit-down Indian restaurant located in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood, steps from the Inner Harbour and Beacon Hill Park — a natural stop on popular cycling routes through the area. The restaurant seats up to 50 guests, offering a full dine-in experience in a compact neighbourhood setting.

restaurant.name: Wolf Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: Wolf Brewing Company is a small-batch craft brewery and taproom (The Wolf Den) located just off the edge of downtown Nanaimo, close to the ferry terminals and Nanaimo Airport. The taproom pours 10+ taps of flagships and limited releases alongside signature 'Mash' pizzas made from spent brewing grain. A dog-friendly patio, regular live music nights, and growler fill service make it a welcoming destination for cyclists exploring Vancouver Island.

detail.address: #2-940 Old Victoria Road, Nanaimo, BC V9R6Z8

notes.Takeout: Growler fills explicitly confirmed in FAQ: 'Absolutely! Growlers are a great way for you to take brewery-fresh beer away to share (or not). We can fill your pre-cleaned growler or provide you with one.' Beer to-go also noted on /our-beers page
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists dedicated 'GLUTEN FREE OPTIONS' and 'VEGETARIAN OPTIONS' sections with multiple items each. FAQ also confirms: 'We've got you covered! We have a selection of GF food AND canned beer options.'

restaurant.name: Mr. Shawarma
restaurant.desc: Mr. Shawarma claims to be the first Middle Eastern and shawarma food truck in Canada, serving Vancouver since 2009. Their 800 Robson Street spot is their main location among several downtown Vancouver outposts, all offering halal-certified chicken shawarma, beef steak shawarma, and freshly made falafel wraps prepared daily from scratch. The takeout-focused, meals-on-the-go format is well suited to cyclists fuelling up in the heart of the city.

detail.address: 800 Robson Street, Vancouver, British Columbia V6Z 2C5, Canada

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Falafel is listed as a standalone menu item and wrap filling — described as made in-house from ground chickpeas, fresh herbs, and vegetables, with no meat

restaurant.name: Dosa Crepe Café
restaurant.desc: Dosa Crepe Café is a South Indian restaurant on Bernard Avenue in Downtown Kelowna specializing in dosa — gluten-free, vegan crepes made from fermented rice and black gram batter — blended with French crepe influences. Beyond dosa, the menu spans biriyani, curries, kothu roti, bubble tea, and licensed beverages, giving hungry cyclists a broad range of options. It is the flagship of a growing BC chain with branches in Rutland, Vernon, and Osoyoos.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly states 'Our Dosa is gluten free, vegan.' Menu includes numerous plant-based dosa, vegetable, and lentil-based dishes

restaurant.name: Tracy Cakes
restaurant.desc: Tracycakes Bakery Cafe is a charming from-scratch bakery and cafe that has been baking daily since 2006, known for over 60 varieties of cupcakes, elegant Signature High Teas, and savoury lunch items including paninis, soups, and wraps. The Abbotsford location features both indoor and outdoor seating and is part of the Downtown Abby Hospitality Collective, making it a welcoming stop in a locally-focused dining neighbourhood. A touring cyclist can eat in or take out, and online pre-orders for pick-up are also available.

restaurant.name: Kernels Popcorn
restaurant.desc: Kernels Popcorn is a 100% Canadian-owned popcorn franchise founded in 1983, with this location operating as a mall kiosk on the upper level at 4820 Kingsway. The shop offers a wide range of flavoured popcorn varieties — all gluten-free and whole-grain, with no nuts used in any product or ingredient sourcing. With no on-site seating of any kind, it functions strictly as a quick grab-and-go snack stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu page states 'GLUTEN FREE — Corn is the basis for any No Gluten diet, and so we ensure nothing is added to change that' and 'WHOLE GRAIN — Every Kernels product starts with an all-natural Whole Grain.'

restaurant.name: Scoops by the Sea
restaurant.desc: Scoops by the Sea is an outdoor ice cream stand in Chemainus, BC, tucked behind a building across from the local visitor center. The shop handcrafts all its ice cream in-store daily, with an extensive roster of signature flavours, rotating seasonal specials, and a full vegan and dairy-free lineup using water-based sorbets, coconut milk, and cashew milk. Beyond ice cream, they serve gourmet beef hotdogs, milkshakes, frappes, iced coffee, and freshly squeezed lemonade — making it a rewarding treat stop for touring cyclists passing through this historic waterfront town.

notes.Takeout: Outdoor stand with takeout-only service: ice cream scoops, gourmet hotdogs, milkshakes, frappes, iced coffee, freshly squeezed lemonade, and frozen lemonade blended with sorbet
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dairy-free and vegan options explicitly offered: water-based fruit sorbets (lime, lemon, raspberry, peach, mango) and coconut milk and cashew milk ice creams (e.g. Pomegranate, Berry Good, Cashew Caramel Chip)

restaurant.name: The Bunny Cafe
restaurant.desc: Launched in 2021 as North America's first bunny cafe, The Bunny Cafe is a therapeutic lounge where guests interact with adoptable rabbits in partnership with Rabbitats Rescue Society. The fully vegan menu features plant-based sweet and savory snacks alongside coffee, and the space doubles as a retail shop with rabbit-themed merchandise. A touring cyclist visiting Vancouver's Commercial Drive neighbourhood will find a genuinely one-of-a-kind rest stop that also supports rabbit rescue and adoption.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Our cafe is fully vegan with plant-based sweet and savory snacks'; OSM confirms

restaurant.name: Trees Organic Coffee & Cheesecake
restaurant.desc: Trees Organic Coffee & Cheesecake is a Vancouver-area cafe chain operating since 1996, famous for its award-winning homemade cheesecakes made from a signature New York-style recipe and freshly roasted small-batch organic coffee. This Surrey location is one of 13-14 retail outlets across the Lower Mainland, each offering a full cafe menu including sandwiches, baked goods, and a variety of teas. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a full sit-down cafe experience with online ordering and in-store pickup available.

restaurant.name: Naas Foods
restaurant.desc: Naas Foods is an Indigenous-owned specialty shop in Tofino selling premium wild kelp seasonings, seafood packages, and custom sport fish processing services from their Campbell Street storefront. They source kelp from Ahousaht waters and support the T'aaq-wiihak indigenous fishery, making this one of the most distinctly local food stops on the west coast of Vancouver Island. Touring cyclists can pick up ready-to-prepare seafood packages or browse kelp-based seasonings to take on the road.

restaurant.name: Dominion Bar & Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Dominion Bar + Kitchen is a full-service restaurant and bar in the lobby of Surrey's Civic Hotel, overlooking the city's Civic Plaza — one of the municipality's main gathering squares. The menu is built around locally sourced ingredients including Ocean Wise-certified seafood, Richmond eggs, and Langley chicken, paired with handcrafted cocktails, BC wines, and local craft beers. It operates across multiple dayparts from early breakfast through late-night service and offers a private dining room for groups.

detail.address: 13475 Central Avenue, Unit D1, Surrey, BC V3T 0L8

restaurant.name: Dakoda's Sports Bar & Grill / Dakoda's Pub
restaurant.desc: A sports bar and grill in Kelowna offering food and drinks. The establishment accepts cash and card payments. Online presence is minimal, but OSM records show regular operating hours.

restaurant.name: Plethore by Fauburg
restaurant.desc: Faubourg is a family-owned French boulangerie-pâtisserie founded in Vancouver in 2010, with three city locations including this Kerrisdale outpost. The bakery produces artisan baguettes baked five times daily in an authentic French deck oven, alongside croissants, macarons, cakes, and a full savoury menu of sandwiches, quiches, soups, and hot dishes. For a touring cyclist passing through Kerrisdale, it offers a genuine French café stop with both sweet and substantial savoury options made fresh on site every day.

restaurant.name: Off The Hook
restaurant.desc: Off The Hook is a lively, casual contemporary seafood restaurant in Nanaimo specializing in fish and chips, smokery dishes, and global-inspired seafood. The entire food menu is 100% gluten-free, making it a notable stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions. The restaurant offers both dine-in with outdoor seating and online ordering for takeout, and accommodates large groups.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly states '100% Gluten-Free Food Menu'

restaurant.name: Sfinaki Greek Taverna
restaurant.desc: Sfinaki Greek Taverna is a family-owned Greek restaurant operated by the Karamessinis family in The Heights neighbourhood of Burnaby for over 25 years. It has earned multiple 'Burnaby's Best' awards for Greek food, catering, and family dining. Touring cyclists can fuel up on gyros, souvlaki, moussaka, and fresh salads either dining in or ordering takeout for pickup.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian items: spanakopita, fasolada (white bean soup), village salad, greek salad, zucchini kefte, sfinaki dips (hummus, tzatziki, tarama), saganaki. No explicit GF or vegan labelling found

restaurant.name: Manjal South Indian Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Manjal — Tamil for 'turmeric' — is a South Indian kitchen in Burnaby's Edmonds neighbourhood dedicated to preserving authentic regional recipes like dosas, biriyani, kothu parotta, and chaats. The restaurant offers a full dine-in experience as well as online ordering for takeout, and has earned a loyal following for the freshness and authenticity of its food. Both vegetarian and non-vegetarian menus are offered across a wide range of dishes, making it a solid refuelling option for cyclists with varied dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple dedicated vegetarian menu sections listed: 'Appetizers (Vegetarian)', 'Curries Vegetarian', 'Seasonal Dosa (Vegetarian)', 'Dosa (Vegetarian)'

restaurant.name: Muffin Delight
restaurant.desc: Muffin Delight is a bakery in North Vancouver, also listed under the alternate name Bubble Tea Delight, suggesting it may offer both baked goods and bubble tea. It sits at street level and would be a casual food stop for cyclists moving through the area. No further detail about the shop's offerings or layout could be confirmed from available sources.

detail.address: 123 Carrie Cates Ct, North Vancouver, BC V7M 3K7, Canada

restaurant.name: Earls
restaurant.desc: Earls Kitchen + Bar is a well-established Canadian casual dining chain with a full-service bar and a broad American-style menu. The Port Coquitlam location is situated in a retail complex on Shaughnessy Street and is part of a large network of BC locations. OSM records outdoor seating, making it a reasonable rest stop for cyclists seeking a sit-down meal or takeout.

restaurant.name: Lá Chuối Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Lá Chuối Cuisine is a Vietnamese restaurant in East Vancouver along the Kingsway corridor, serving traditional dishes including crispy fried spring rolls, deep-fried chicken rice, and beef offal. The restaurant offers both in-person dining and online ordering with pickup and delivery. It sits on a busy arterial route that cyclists frequently travel between Burnaby and downtown Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Agra Tandoori Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Agra Tandoori Restaurant is a full-service Indian restaurant in Burnaby specializing in traditional tandoori preparations, curries, and fresh-baked naan. The restaurant operates two Burnaby locations and offers both dine-in buffet service and a takeout menu with a wide range of vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes. Touring cyclists passing through Burnaby would find it a solid option for a hot sit-down meal or a packaged takeout order.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegetarian items confirmed: Vegetarian Special Thali, Channa Masala, Palak Paneer, Dal Turka, Aloo Gobhi, Paneer Makhani, Vegetable Pakora, and others across menu pages

restaurant.name: Habitat
restaurant.desc: Habitat Pub is located on the BCIT Burnaby campus in Building SE02, serving the college community at 3700 Willingdon Avenue. It appears to have previously operated under the name Professor Mugs Pub based on its Facebook presence. As a campus pub, its primary clientele is BCIT students and staff, though Canadian campus pubs are generally open to the public.

restaurant.name: Delany's Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Delany's Coffee House is a family-owned neighbourhood café that has anchored Edgemont Village in North Vancouver since the late 1990s, one of several locations spread across the North Shore. Unlike chain coffee shops, each Delany's has its own distinct decor featuring local photography and art, with both indoor and outdoor seating. The brand maintains an Athlete Ambassadors program, signalling a connection to the active outdoor community that defines the North Shore.

restaurant.name: Hariyali Express
restaurant.desc: Hariyali Express is an authentic Indian restaurant on Vancouver's cycling-friendly Commercial Drive, helmed by Chef Anil Rawat whose 20-plus years of experience span kitchens in India, Germany, and Canada. The menu covers tandoori classics, aromatic curries, street-food favorites, and Indian sweets, with dietary labels clearly indicating gluten-free, dairy-free, vegetarian, and vegan choices. Dine-in, takeout, delivery, and catering are all available, making it a versatile stop for riders exploring the Drive.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'VEGAN THALI'; About page lists 'Vegetarian & Non-Vegetarian Options'; multiple appetizers carry GF (gluten-free) and DF (dairy-free) labels

restaurant.name: Tap and Barrel
restaurant.desc: Tap and Barrel Brentwood is part of a seven-location BC restaurant group with a strong focus on local craft beer, BC wine, and comfort food made with seasonal ingredients. Located in the Brentwood neighbourhood of Burnaby, the restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating. The group is known for its extensive BC-only tap selections and rotating menus developed in partnership with local breweries and wineries.

restaurant.name: Ross Crepe & Cafe
restaurant.desc: Ross Crêpe and Cafe is a French-style creperie specializing in sweet and savory crepes, located inside Lonsdale Quay Market on the North Vancouver waterfront. The market setting places it steps from the Lonsdale Quay SeaBus terminal, making it a natural stop for cyclists crossing Burrard Inlet or riding the North Shore. Being within the market means access to a sheltered, indoor eating environment alongside other food vendors and shops.

detail.address: 148 Chadwick Court, North Vancouver, BC V7M 3K2

restaurant.name: Chef Big D's Restaurant & Grill
restaurant.desc: Chef Big D's is a restaurant on Cleveland Avenue in Squamish, BC's main commercial corridor. OSM records it as a sit-down establishment with indoor seating. Very little additional detail is publicly available about its menu or character.

restaurant.name: Pappa Leo's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Pappa Leo's Pizza is a locally-founded Lower Mainland chain started in 2003 by two brothers, now spanning 7 locations including this Barnet Highway outpost — one of two in Coquitlam. The kitchen makes dough fresh daily and sources quality toppings, earning multiple best-pizza awards across the region. Touring cyclists will find a full pizza menu plus sides like wings, lasagna, and Caesar salad, with gluten-free crust on offer.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly states 'We also offer gluten free pizza crust options.'

restaurant.name: Wildlight Kitchen + Bar
restaurant.desc: Wildlight Kitchen + Bar is a MICHELIN Guide Recommended modern West Coast restaurant at UBC's Lelǝm Village, nestled between the University Endowment Lands and Pacific Spirit Park on Musqueam Nation territory. Chef Warren Chow — recipient of Michelin's inaugural Vancouver Young Chef Award in 2023 — leads an all-day menu built around ethically sourced Pacific seafood, produce from UBC Farm, and locally raised meats, paired with BC wines and handcrafted cocktails. A warmly styled dining room and enclosed glass year-round atrium make it a notable stop for cyclists riding the UBC loop or Point Grey routes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels items V (Vegetarian), VE (Vegan), and GF (Gluten Free) throughout small plates and large plates sections

restaurant.name: Dinesty Dumpling House
restaurant.desc: Dinesty Dumpling House on Robson Street is a Vancouver chain restaurant specializing in handcrafted Xiaolongbao (soup dumplings), opened in winter 2013 on one of the city's busiest dining strips. The restaurant is known for its open-kitchen window and a street-facing live dumpling-making display visible from Robson Street. It is part of a multi-location Lower Mainland chain that has won the HSBC Chinese Restaurant Diners' Choice Award for best Xiao Long Bao.

restaurant.name: Daimanya
restaurant.desc: Daimanya is a Japanese restaurant located in Unit 150 at 4160 Number 3 Road in Richmond, BC. The Instagram account identifies it as 'Daimanya Japanese Restaurant by Meet Oyster,' suggesting an affiliation or co-branding with the Meet Oyster group. Beyond Japanese cuisine, details about the dining style, seating, or cyclist-specific features are not available from the fetched content.

restaurant.name: Gather Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Gather is a neighbourhood restaurant occupying a glass-encased corner of Kelowna's Innovation Centre, serving a distinctive fusion of modern Korean and Italian cuisine crafted by Chef Sung Ji Park, whose background spans traditional Korean home cooking and a decade in fine Italian kitchens. The intimate interior was designed and built in Italy by co-owner Luigi Coccaro, with an open kitchen that lets diners watch the cooking unfold. The menu is built around shareable small, medium, and large plates — a format rooted in both Korean and Italian dining culture — paired with a wine list of over 180 curated selections.

restaurant.name: Sushi Van
restaurant.desc: Sushi Van is a Japanese sushi restaurant located on Granville Street in Vancouver with both indoor and outdoor seating. As a casual dining spot with takeaway service, it offers convenient dining options for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Duoduo Fruit Shop
restaurant.desc: A fruit shop in Burnaby offering fruit-based refreshments and likely juice or smoothie service. The minimal web presence suggests a small, focused operation catering to quick refreshment stops.

restaurant.name: Misty Mountain Pizza
restaurant.desc: Misty Mountain Pizza has been a Whistler institution since 1991, located at the base of Whistler Mountain near the village entrance to the Hilton. The restaurant explicitly serves mountain bikers and skiers and offers pizza by the slice in-store, whole pies in multiple sizes, pasta, and desserts. A second location exists in Rossland, making this a familiar name for cyclists traveling BC's mountain corridors.

detail.address: 4293 Mountain Square – Unit 203, Whistler, BC V0N 1B0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Gluten free and dairy options available' and lists Gluten Free 9" and 12" pizzas, Cauliflower Crusts 12", and Daiya Dairy Free Cheese. Vegetarian toppings appear on the menu (The Greek, Presto Pesto) but vegetarian/vegan are not explicitly called out

restaurant.name: Hungry Guys Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Hungry Guys Kitchen is a casual downtown Vancouver eatery on Granville Street serving handcrafted burgers, salads, bowls, and burritos made from locally sourced, fresh ingredients. Founded by Aldo Velaj, who learned to cook from his mother and committed to sustainable sourcing, the 545 Granville location is the daytime counterpart to a second evening-focused location at 988 Granville. The menu is highly customizable and explicitly allergen-friendly, with staff able to accommodate dietary restrictions.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Tofu is listed as a protein option across salads, bowls, and burritos throughout the menu. Website also states 'Allergen Friendly — You can specify if you have any allergies, and we can offer alternative options.'

restaurant.name: Phở Don
restaurant.desc: Phở Don is a Vietnamese restaurant on East Hastings Street in Vancouver, serving pho and likely other traditional Vietnamese dishes in an indoor-only setting. It sits in a busy commercial strip along a popular east-west cycling corridor, making it a convenient mid-ride stop for cyclists coming through the Hastings area.

restaurant.name: Cafe Mexico
restaurant.desc: Cafe Mexico is a Mexican Grill & Cantina on Store Street in Victoria, serving an extensive menu of tacos, enchiladas, alambres, and antojitos with clearly labeled vegetarian options throughout. The restaurant also boasts one of the more comprehensive tequila and mezcal selections in the city, with dozens of expressions listed. Touring cyclists arriving in downtown Victoria will find a full sit-down dining experience rooted in authentic Mexican flavours.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple dishes explicitly labeled vegetarian on the menu: TACOS VEGETARIANOS, TACOS RAJAS (vegetarian), ALAMBRE VEGETARIANO, CHILE RELLENO (VEGETARIANO)

restaurant.name: Caffe La Tana
restaurant.desc: Caffè La Tana is an Italian alimentari-style cafe, restaurant, and wine bar on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, designed after the old-world neighbourhood food shops found throughout Italy. The kitchen rolls fresh pasta daily in full view of guests, pairs it with an all-Italian wine list of well-loved and lesser-known varietals, and fills a gourmet grocery corner with artisan Italian ingredients and handmade pasta tools to take home. Commercial Drive is a well-established cycling corridor through East Vancouver, making La Tana a natural stop for cyclists seeking a proper Italian meal.

notes.Takeout: Online shop offers grocery and prepared food items 'Available to Pre-Order for Pick up'; walk-in takeout not explicitly mentioned but shop pickup is confirmed
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian dishes including Kale Salad, Caesar Salad, Spaghetti Cacio e Pepe, Uova Verdi, and several pasta options; no explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Mile One Eating House
restaurant.desc: Mile One Eating House is a Pemberton institution founded in 2011, serving regionally inspired British Columbian comfort food with an emphasis on natural beef, local producers, and slow-food techniques. Signatures include natural beef burgers, slow-roasted brisket, pork belly sandwiches, and mac 'n' cheese, all sourced from regional farmers, ranchers, and artisans. Positioned as the beginning, middle, or end of a journey into BC's wild spaces, it's a natural refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the Pemberton Valley.

detail.address: 7330 Arbutus Street, Unit 107, Pemberton, BC V0N 2L1

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: A Starbucks coffee shop with indoor and outdoor seating, offering takeaway service and free Wi-Fi. The location includes wheelchair-accessible toilets and air conditioning, making it a comfortable stop for touring cyclists needing refreshments and rest.

restaurant.name: Cho Sun Korean BBQ
restaurant.desc: Cho Sun Korean BBQ is a Korean restaurant serving traditional dishes including Korean BBQ, fried chicken, kimchi rice, and mussel soup in what the restaurant describes as a relaxed and cozy environment. The business offers online ordering for takeout. The OSM-listed Kingsway address conflicts with the address shown on the business website, raising questions about which location is currently active.

restaurant.name: Agra Tandoori
restaurant.desc: Agra Tandoori is an Indian tandoori restaurant in the Vancouver area, offering cuisine from the Indian subcontinent. The business operates with a TouchBistro point-of-sale system, indicating an established restaurant operation. Touring cyclists passing through the area would find it a potential stop for a substantial Indian meal.

restaurant.name: Wild Mountain
restaurant.desc: Wild Mountain is a farm-to-table dinner restaurant in Sooke serving West Coast Canadian cuisine grounded in organic, locally sourced ingredients from regional farmers, fishers, foragers, and fermenters. A certified Slow Food Chef's Alliance and Safe Space restaurant, it features a wood-fired brick oven producing sourdough thin-crust pizzas alongside a harvest-driven seasonal menu. The walk-in patio offers a relaxed outdoor option for cyclists arriving after a ride through the Sooke hills.

restaurant.name: The Junction Coffee House
restaurant.desc: The Junction Coffee House is a cafe with outdoor seating located on Cariboo Highway in Clinton. The business accepts credit card payments and offers a convenient stop for cyclists traveling the area.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: A locally operated Subway franchise on Kingsway in Burnaby, offering customizable Footlong sandwiches, wraps, and salads built with fresh-baked bread, fresh-cut vegetables, and a range of proteins. The location features indoor seating and supports pickup, delivery, and curbside service. Situated on a busy commercial arterial in the Burnaby–Vancouver corridor, it offers a quick and accessible meal stop for cyclists passing through.

restaurant.name: Mad Rona's Coffee Bar
restaurant.desc: Mad Rona's Coffee Bar is a contemporary west coast-inspired café located at Madrona Marketplace East on Gabriola Island, just walking distance from the BC Ferries terminal. The café serves house-made sandwiches, paninis, and scratch-baked goods alongside quality espresso sourced from Cobble Hill's Drumroaster Coffee, roasted in small batches and delivered fresh weekly. A licensed patio and free Wi-Fi make it a welcoming and practical stop for cyclists exploring the island.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes vegetarian items (Falafel Wrap, Veggie Patty with house-made patty and mozzarella, multiple veggie paninis); website states 'All sandwiches can be made on a gluten free wrap or bun.'

restaurant.name: Sushi & Roll
restaurant.desc: Sushi & Roll is a sushi restaurant located on King George Boulevard in Surrey, BC. It sits along a busy urban arterial corridor that cycling tourists passing through the Fraser Valley region may use as a rest stop. Beyond its OSM listing as a restaurant, details about the dining experience or offerings are not available from current sources.

restaurant.name: Kuku's
restaurant.desc: Kuku's is a family-owned East Indian restaurant on Victoria's Burnside corridor, founded by Anita and Randy Mahadar and now in its 17th year of operation. The menu spans tandoori specialties, rice dishes, naan, and traditional Indian desserts, with a full vegetarian section and gluten-free alternatives. Takeout, delivery, online ordering, and catering are all available, making it a practical refueling stop for cyclists moving through the area.

detail.address: 24 Burnside Rd W, Victoria, BC V9A 1B3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists 'Vegetarian Menu Items' and 'Gluten-Free Options' as distinct features. No vegan claim found

restaurant.name: Pearsons Deli
restaurant.desc: Pearsons European Deli is a family-run breakfast-and-lunch cafe on Harvey Ave in Kelowna, operated by Red Seal Chef Stephanie Schoales and her husband Landon, who took over from the founding Pearson family after 30 years. The deli is known for hearty, house-made European-style food including build-your-own sandwiches, daily soups, and deli salads. Cyclists rolling through Kelowna will find a broad midday menu with vegan and vegetarian options and online ordering available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a dedicated 'Vegan Feature' (Mediterranean Wrap) and marks soups as '(veg)'; multiple salad and vegetarian sandwich options are present throughout the menu

restaurant.name: Brown's Socialhouse
restaurant.desc: Brown's Socialhouse is a BC-based casual dining chain with dozens of locations across western Canada; the Schoolhouse outpost occupies a two-storey standalone building on Lougheed Highway in Coquitlam. The brand pitches itself on a 'signature mix of great food, drink, atmosphere, music and people,' with a full bar, weekend brunch service, and a daily social hour. For a cyclist on the Lougheed corridor, it offers a sit-down meal with delivery and pickup options as an alternative.

restaurant.name: Cordo Resto & Bar
restaurant.desc: Cordo Resto & Bar is a regionally-inspired full-service restaurant and bar in downtown Kamloops, named after the Cordillera mountain geography of interior BC, offering indoor and outdoor patio dining. The menu celebrates Thompson-Okanagan regional cuisine with locally sourced produce, craft beers on tap, wines from the Kamloops Wine Trail and Okanagan, and house-crafted cocktails. A dedicated Grab + Go counter — a 'we proudly serve' Starbucks location — offers nutritious packaged meals and premium coffee for cyclists needing a quick, fuelling stop.

notes.Packed lunches: Grab + Go section describes 'wholesome food on the go featuring balanced, nutritious meals… Perfect for an early departure, working lunch or a picnic in the park' in environmentally-responsible packaging
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Recipes page explicitly notes Crispy Seed Crackers are 'gluten free'; no explicit vegetarian or vegan confirmation found in website text

restaurant.name: TV Dinner Market & Café
restaurant.desc: TV Dinner is a neighborhood market and café offering frozen and refrigerated foods, pantry staples, and quality coffee. It provides convenient meal options and casual food stops for cyclists and pedestrians passing through the West 3rd Avenue corridor. The business emphasizes delivering convenience without sacrificing quality.

restaurant.name: Sushi Garden
restaurant.desc: Sushi Garden is an established Japanese sushi chain with three Burnaby locations offering dine-in service in a non-smoking, air-conditioned setting with vegetarian-friendly options. Online ordering is available at all branches. The probable South Burnaby (Highgate) location sits on Kingsway, a major arterial corridor regularly used by cyclists.

restaurant.name: Truck Stop Diner
restaurant.desc: The Truck Stop Diner is a pub and diner operated by Red Truck Beer Company, one of BC's well-known craft breweries, in Vancouver. The brewery's website navigation references a dedicated food menu, live music, and weekly specials at this venue alongside draft beer service. It is a full-service food-and-drink establishment in an urban Vancouver setting.

restaurant.name: New Town Bakery
restaurant.desc: New Town Bakery is a family-run Chinese and Filipino bakery and restaurant operating since 1980, with roots in Vancouver's historic Chinatown. The Surrey branch is one of two currently operating locations, known for award-winning apple tarts and world-famous steamed buns (Siopao) in both BBQ pork and chicken varieties. The business has been recognized by CNN Travel as a must-visit Chinatown restaurant and has received multiple Chinese Restaurant Critic's Choice awards.

restaurant.name: Via Tevere
restaurant.desc: Via Tevere Pizzeria Napoletana is a certified Neapolitan pizzeria — member #399 of the Associazione Vera Pizza Napoletana (AVPN) — serving wood-fired pizza made with authentic Neapolitan ingredients and tradition. Rooted in a family heritage tracing back to a street in Naples called Via Tevere, the restaurant operates two Vancouver locations (Main Street and Victoria Drive) plus a mobile catering unit. For a touring cyclist, it offers a sit-down meal at a well-regarded neighbourhood restaurant in East Vancouver.

restaurant.name: The Brewery Creek Liquor Store
restaurant.desc: Established in 2005, The Brewery Creek Liquor Store is Vancouver's first specialty craft beer retail store, housed in a 3,000-square-foot space in the Mt. Pleasant neighbourhood. It stocks over 500 craft beers and 500 wines alongside spirits, ciders, hard seltzers, and alcohol-free options, and has earned multiple awards including Best Beer Store from The Georgia Straight and Best Local Private Liquor Store from CAMRA. Dogs are explicitly welcomed inside, making it a friendly stop for cyclists touring the area.

restaurant.name: ebisu sushi
restaurant.desc: Ebisu Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Abbotsford serving sushi and related cuisine. It offers online ordering, making it a convenient stop for cyclists wanting to pre-order a meal. The restaurant occupies a retail unit at 2596 McMillan Rd.

restaurant.name: Pho54
restaurant.desc: Pho54 is a locally-owned Vietnamese restaurant on Shoppers Row in central Campbell River, serving traditional pho and other Vietnamese dishes with a modern twist. The restaurant also offers Boba 54 bubble tea drinks alongside its main menu. It sits in a commercial shopping strip convenient to downtown Campbell River, making it a handy meal stop for cyclists passing through town.

detail.address: 1090A Shoppers Row, Campbell River, BC V9W 2C6

restaurant.name: Salsa and Agave Mexican Grill
restaurant.desc: Salsa & Agave is a well-established Mexican restaurant on Pacific Boulevard in Vancouver, serving authentic dishes including tacos, enchiladas, birria, pozole, and margaritas for over a decade. The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating in a relaxed atmosphere and is praised by regulars for consistent food quality and friendly service. Online ordering and takeout are available, making it a convenient mid-ride fuel stop in central Vancouver.

notes.Takeout: Website explicitly promotes online ordering with 'no calls, no lines, no complications' and 'enjoy our delicious Mexican food from the comfort of your home'

restaurant.name: Club Salmon
restaurant.desc: Club Salmon is a Japanese restaurant in Vancouver located on Imperial Street. It offers indoor seating in a smoke-free environment.

restaurant.name: Mason's Kitchen + Bar
restaurant.desc: Mason's Kitchen + Bar is a full-service restaurant and bar set on the edge of the Big Horn Golf Course in Kamloops, offering patio dining with views of the surrounding landscape. The menu focuses on locally inspired, handmade dishes suited to everything from casual lunches to group gatherings. Online table reservations and a catering menu are available.

restaurant.name: The Katsu Japanese Cutlet House
restaurant.desc: The Katsu Japanese Cutlet House is a Japanese restaurant in downtown Langley specializing in panko-breaded katsu made with house-made breadcrumbs and the restaurant's own signature sauces. The menu features chicken, hira pork, kimchi, and cheese katsu variations, all using fresh ingredients. A customer review on the site mentions it as a natural stop before exploring downtown Langley on foot—making it a potential mid-ride meal destination for cyclists passing through.

restaurant.name: The Den
restaurant.desc: The Den is a retro arcade bar and lounge tucked into the ground floor of the Barclay Hotel on Vancouver's Robson Street, featuring classic games like Pac-Man, pinball, Golden Tee, and Buck Hunter alongside a jukebox and nostalgic murals of the Beastie Boys, Run DMC, and Bill Murray. The bar has no kitchen but openly welcomes guests to bring their own food or order in from nearby restaurants. It bills itself as a deliberately casual, basement-den atmosphere — cheap drinks, killer tunes, and a chill vibe.

restaurant.name: Republica Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Republica Coffee Roasters is a locally owned artisan coffee roasteria founded in 2007 and located in Fort Langley, BC's historic birthplace. The roastery specializes in single-estate fair trade organic coffees from around the world, roasted fresh to order and date-stamped for freshness. Cyclists can stop in at the Fort Langley storefront to pick up freshly roasted beans or browse their range of specialty blends and green beans.

restaurant.name: Milestones
restaurant.desc: Milestones Grill & Bar is a well-established Canadian casual dining chain located at Tsawwassen Mills, near the Tsawwassen ferry terminal and the South Delta cycling network. The restaurant offers a full sit-down menu with bar service, accommodating dietary needs including vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options. Its proximity to the BC Ferries terminal makes it a logical stop for cyclists arriving from or departing to Vancouver Island or the Southern Gulf Islands.

restaurant.name: Sushi Mago
restaurant.desc: Sushi Mago is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Shelbourne Street in Victoria's Gordon Head neighbourhood. It operates as a compact sit-down and takeout spot, with online ordering available through its website. Cyclists exploring Victoria's east side residential corridors will find it a convenient stop for a Japanese meal.

restaurant.name: Wolf in the Fog
restaurant.desc: Wolf in the Fog is a celebrated ingredient-driven dinner restaurant anchored in the culinary culture of Tofino, BC, named Air Canada enRoute's Canada's Best New Restaurant in 2014. Chef Nicholas Nutting's kitchen draws directly from the surrounding ocean and rainforest — fishing and foraging are central to the menu's identity. The restaurant has sea views from its patio and an extensive, globally curated wine list overseen by a dedicated wine director.

restaurant.name: Thai Basil
restaurant.desc: Thai Basil is a Vancouver Thai restaurant chain established in 2008 with four city locations, including one situated just off Davie Street in the downtown West End. The menu covers a broad range of Thai dishes — curries, noodle soups, salads, and noodles — with vegetarian and gluten-free options woven throughout. Dine-in and takeout with delivery are both available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes tofu substitutions across curries, soups, and noodle dishes, and a dedicated Mixed Veggie Salad

restaurant.name: The Mint
restaurant.desc: The Mint is a long-established Himalayan dining lounge in downtown Victoria, founded in April 2002, blending traditional Himalayan dishes like Tibetan Momos and butter chicken curry with contemporary West Coast fare and craft cocktails. Located below street level on Douglas Street, it pairs an eclectic food menu with rotating local craft beer taps and a live entertainment program featuring DJs and performances. The venue has a private dining area available for functions and draws a devoted local crowd.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'Many items can be made dairy or gluten free'; multiple dishes are individually labelled 'Vegan' (e.g. Olives, French Fries, Onion Pakora, Hummus and Naan) and 'Vegetarian' (e.g. Goat Cheese Salad, Nachos)

restaurant.name: J's Cafe & Bistro
restaurant.desc: A cafe in Kelowna offering casual food and beverages to the community.

restaurant.name: Green Leaf Sushi
restaurant.desc: A sushi restaurant located on West Broadway in Vancouver. Offers a casual dining option for touring cyclists to refuel. Limited information available due to website access failure.

restaurant.name: eF & Be Bakehouse
restaurant.desc: eF & Be Bakehouse is a Burnaby-based Japanese bakery founded by friends Fumie and Bowie, specializing in authentic Japanese baked goods such as melon pan, mochi-filled buns, and savory stuffed breads like beef curry pan and meatball pan. The business runs on a pre-order model with scheduled pickup from their commercial kitchen at YVR Prep on Still Creek Avenue, plus delivery through a local partner and regular appearances at farmers markets around the region. Cyclists who plan ahead can pick up a satisfying haul of handheld baked goods — ideal trail or road fuel.

detail.address: A5 - 5279 Still Creek Ave, Burnaby, BC

restaurant.name: Afghan Chopan Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Afghan Chopan Restaurant serves traditional Afghan cuisine with dine-in, pickup, and third-party delivery options in the Surrey area. The restaurant also offers a catering menu alongside its regular menu, making it a versatile stop for larger groups. A touring cyclist would find it a distinctive ethnic dining option with convenient takeout for those continuing on the road.

restaurant.name: Guffo Cafe
restaurant.desc: Guffo Cafe is a cafe situated on Robson Street in the heart of downtown Vancouver, one of the city's most walkable and heavily trafficked retail corridors. Its Instagram-only web presence suggests a small, independently run establishment. OSM records confirm it is wheelchair accessible and accepts both credit and debit cards.

restaurant.name: 49th Parallel Café & Lucky's Doughnuts
restaurant.desc: 49th Parallel Café & Lucky's Doughnuts is a well-established Vancouver institution pairing specialty 49th Parallel coffee with handcrafted Lucky's Doughnuts made fresh on-site from scratch throughout the day. The downtown Thurlow location, at the corner of West Georgia and Thurlow, is the chain's third outpost and uniquely features a kitchen serving breakfast sandwiches and brunch plates alongside the famous seasonal doughnuts. Indoor and outdoor seating and wheelchair accessibility round out what is a capable urban rest stop in the heart of downtown Vancouver.

notes.Takeout: Website FAQ states 'We offer pick-up only' for online pre-orders; Uber Eats delivery also available as a limited option
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website FAQ confirms two varieties of vegan and gluten-friendly doughnuts (cocoa base and plain base), though prepared in shared kitchens with cross-contamination risk noted

restaurant.name: Harold's Family Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A family restaurant located in Kamloops, BC. Without access to the restaurant's website, specific details about the establishment and its amenities cannot be verified.

restaurant.name: Roseland Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Roseland Restaurant has been a fixture of the Abbotsford community since 1990, serving a broad menu of Western-style breakfast, lunch, and dinner in a cozy, flower-decorated dining room with a mini lounge and leather booth seating. The restaurant operates as a full-service restaurant and bar and accommodates groups and large parties. Pickup and delivery options are available alongside the sit-down experience.

detail.address: 33550 South Fraser Way, Abbotsford, BC V2S 5G7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a dedicated 'VEGAN BREAKFAST' item (Beyond sausages with hashbrowns and fresh fruit cup); website states 'no matter what dietary regiment you follow, we have something for everyone.'

restaurant.name: Syriana
restaurant.desc: Syriana is an Arab restaurant located on Esquimalt Road in Esquimalt, just west of downtown Victoria. It sits along a well-travelled cycling corridor connecting the Galloping Goose Trail to the city centre, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Freshslice Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain with locations across BC, including this Nanaimo outlet. Known for by-the-slice and whole-pie options with any toppings, it offers both in-store pickup and delivery. A convenient stop for touring cyclists looking for a quick, filling meal in Nanaimo.

restaurant.name: Altitudes Bistro
restaurant.desc: Altitudes Bistro sits at the summit of Grouse Mountain, roughly 3,700 feet above the Lower Mainland, serving distinctly British Columbian cuisine with sweeping views. It is one of several dining options at the Grouse Mountain resort, which also hosts a lift-accessed mountain bike park with rentals and guided camps. The restaurant is reachable only by gondola (Skyride) or by hiking the Grouse Grind trail — not by bicycle from the base.

restaurant.name: The Golden Horn Turkish Bakery & Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Golden Horn is a 100% Halal Turkish bakery and café located at Canada Place on Vancouver's seawall, serving handcrafted baklavas made from in-house yufka dough, boreks, pide-wrapped durums, and traditional Turkish coffee. The Canada Place location is steps from the harbour and offers stunning views of the mountains, making it a natural stop on any seawall cycling route. The menu spans sweet pastries through to hearty sandwiches and platters.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Veggie Curry, Veggie Iskender, Chickpea Durum, and Spinach & Feta; Coconut & Almond Baklava is explicitly marked Dairy Free

restaurant.name: Magma Cafè
restaurant.desc: A UBC Food Services café on Main Mall with indoor seating and Wi-Fi connectivity. Useful as a food stop for touring cyclists visiting the campus, though specific bike-touring amenities are unconfirmed.

restaurant.name: Cedar Park Chaat House
restaurant.desc: Cedar Park Chaat House is an Indian restaurant in Abbotsford specializing in traditional chaat alongside a broad menu spanning tandoor breads, biryani, Indo-Chinese dishes, and classic South Asian comfort food. The kitchen emphasizes fresh, seasonal ingredients and recipes described as rooted in a decade of experience with traditional Indian flavours. The restaurant also runs a lunch buffet and full catering service for events of all sizes.

detail.address: 2598 Cedar Park Place, Abbotsford, BC V2T 3S5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes extensive vegetarian options: Veg Samosa, Veg Burger, Veg Pakora, Gobi Pakora, Paneer Pakora, Paneer Specialties, Vegetarian Sabzis, Daal, Veg Fried Rice, Veg Noodles, and more

restaurant.name: It's Okay
restaurant.desc: It's Okay is a neighborhood bar and restaurant in East Vancouver serving food, breakfast, and wine with late-night hours. The casual hangout spot offers table reservations and attracts late-night diners and groups. Touring cyclists passing through Vancouver can find a relaxed venue for evening meals and drinks.

restaurant.name: Koko Monk
restaurant.desc: Koko Monk is an internationally recognized artisan chocolate boutique open since 2013 on Vancouver's West Broadway, celebrated for its signature Harem A La Turca hot chocolate and listed among the world's top 20 chocolate companies. The shop specializes in raw, organic, vegan bean-to-bar chocolate crafted from single-origin cacao with no refined additives, alongside hand-made bonbons, small-batch gelatos, and theatrical drinking chocolates. It's a distinctive sweet stop for cyclists passing through Kitsilano, with award-winning creations regularly featured in international media.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Extensive vegan product lines.g. 'Vegan Mystery dark hot chocolate with almond milk')

restaurant.name: Mirchi Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Mirchi is a restaurant on Granville Street in Vancouver's Marpole neighbourhood, open six days a week for lunch and dinner. The name 'Mirchi' (Hindi/Urdu for chili pepper) suggests South Asian cuisine, making it a potential stop for cyclists cruising the Granville corridor looking for a hot meal. Beyond its location on a major arterial route, specific details about the dining experience are not available from current online sources.

restaurant.name: Tokyo Joe's
restaurant.desc: Tokyo Joe's is a sushi restaurant in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, serving dishes like Deluxe Tempura, Spicy Tuna Sashimi, and Nigiri boxes. The kitchen emphasizes wild, ethically sourced seafood and fresh, high-quality ingredients, with vegetarian options on the menu. Indoor and outdoor seating are available, and online takeout orders can be placed through the restaurant's website.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'We provide vegetarian options'

restaurant.name: Big Bang Sushi
restaurant.desc: Big Bang Sushi is a Japanese restaurant established in 2016 on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, steps from the Stanley Park Seawall — one of the city's most popular cycling corridors. The menu spans sushi, sashimi, teriyaki, udon, and tempura, with both dine-in and online carryout ordering available. A second location operates in Richmond, but the Denman Street shop is the one most relevant to cyclists touring the seawall or West End.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated VEGETARIAN category listed on the order-online page

restaurant.name: Klasik Inasal
restaurant.desc: Klasik Inasal and Noodle Express is an authentic Filipino restaurant on East Broadway in Vancouver, specializing in grilled chicken inasal, Filipino noodle dishes, and traditional rice plates. The restaurant offers dine-in service alongside pickup and large-format boodle fight platters for groups. Its broad menu of classic Filipino comfort food makes it a distinctive stop for cyclists looking for a hearty, culturally rich meal.

detail.address: 650 East Broadway, Vancouver, British Columbia V5T 1X6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Vegetarian Pancit (2-3 person)', 'Veggie Lumpia (8pcs)', and 'Veggie Salad'; no GF or vegan labelling found

restaurant.name: Chao Shou Wang
restaurant.desc: Chao Shou Wang is a Chinese fast-food spot in Vancouver, likely situated inside a multi-level commercial building (OSM tags indicate unit 2113, level 1). The restaurant specialises in wonton-style dishes and offers both counter pickup and dine-in service. Online ordering is available for those who want to grab a quick meal on the go.

restaurant.name: Asian Noodle House
restaurant.desc: Asian Noodle House is a casual sit-down Asian restaurant on Goldstream Avenue in the commercial corridor west of Victoria, specializing in wonton soup and noodle dishes. The restaurant bills itself as serving the best wonton soup in the greater Victoria area and operates under a focused, straightforward menu. Goldstream Avenue is a well-traveled route for cyclists heading toward Goldstream Provincial Park and the Malahat.

restaurant.name: Daddy's Grill Richmond
restaurant.desc: Daddy's Grill Richmond is a Persian grill and kebab restaurant in Richmond, BC, serving kabab platters, wraps, and traditional accompaniments like naan and dough. The menu centres on skewered beef and chicken dishes alongside hearty wraps, making it a calorie-dense stop for cyclists. Online ordering with a 20-minute pickup window is available.

restaurant.name: Olivier's La Boulangerie
restaurant.desc: Olivier's La Boulangerie is an artisan French bakery and café founded by a family who relocated from Southern France to Vancouver, introducing authentic slow-fermented breads to Western Canada in 2009. The Fraser Street location is the brand's largest Vancouver outpost, set in the Fraserhood neighbourhood with exclusive menu items not available at other locations. All products are made without chemical preservatives, GMO grain, or high-gluten elements by master bakers from France.

restaurant.name: Naked Lunch
restaurant.desc: Naked Lunch is a sandwich restaurant in downtown Squamish offering casual, quick-service dining for passing cyclists. Focused on sandwiches, it provides a convenient refueling stop for those on the road.

restaurant.name: Relish
restaurant.desc: Relish is a full-service pub in the heart of downtown Vancouver, situated between Hornby and Howe Streets on Nelson. The venue features an outdoor patio equipped with heaters, a sound system, and multiple TVs for sports viewing, making it a lively stop in a dense urban cycling corridor. Regular programming includes NFL game nights and weekly wing specials.

restaurant.name: Chef Hung Taiwanese Beef Noodle
restaurant.desc: Chef Hung Taiwanese Beef Noodle is an award-winning Taiwanese restaurant whose chef is a three-time champion of the Taipei International Beef Noodle Festival Competition. The restaurant is part of an international chain that opened its North American flagship in Richmond, BC, and specializes in hand-crafted noodles made from Taiwan-imported flour and a slow-cooked, additive-free premium beef bone broth. Online ordering and pickup are available, making it a potential stop for cyclists in the UBC-area Shrum Lane neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Casey's Community House
restaurant.desc: Casey's Community House is a community-oriented restaurant and bar in downtown Creston, BC, positioning itself around community connection and good food. The venue features billiards and a selection of various beers. Access from the rear parking lot is level, making it approachable for cyclists arriving loaded.

restaurant.name: Riley's Fish & Steak
restaurant.desc: Riley's Fish & Steak is a destination dining room in the heart of downtown Vancouver, operated by the Glowbal Restaurant Group and led by CEO Emad Yacoub. The menu is entirely chef-driven, centering on premium seafood — including an oyster bar and seafood towers — alongside top-tier steaks and chops, complemented by a curated wine room and signature cocktail program. The venue also features live music, private dining rooms, and a virtual tour, positioning it as an upscale evening-out rather than a casual mid-ride stop.

restaurant.name: Hon Sushi
restaurant.desc: Hon Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant located on Kingsway in Vancouver, a major east-west arterial with active cycling infrastructure. The restaurant offers indoor table service with air conditioning, making it a potential sit-down meal stop for cyclists travelling the Kingsway corridor. Card payments are accepted according to OSM data.

restaurant.name: 10 Acres Bistro
restaurant.desc: 10 Acres Bistro is a farm-to-table restaurant in downtown Victoria, part of the 10 Acres Farm & Restaurants group that operates four distinct dining locations across Greater Victoria and Sidney. The restaurant draws directly from its own farm, giving cyclists stopping in the city a chance to enjoy locally sourced, seasonally driven meals. Its central Courtney Street location makes it a convenient stop on a ride through downtown Victoria.

restaurant.name: Eggette
restaurant.desc: Eggette is a Hong Kong-style bubble waffle shop on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver, part of the Eggette House brand founded by young Vancouver entrepreneurs. The menu features creative eggette flavors such as salted egg yolk, Portuguese egg tart, black sesame, and double chocolate, alongside hand-made bean cubes and Hong Kong-style milk tea. A compact dessert-focused stop that could serve as a quick snack break for cyclists passing through the West End.

restaurant.name: La Pache Pizza
restaurant.desc: La Pache Pizza is a proudly Canadian, multi-location pizzeria specializing in authentic Neapolitan-style handmade pizza with dough made fresh from scratch daily. The New Westminster location on East Columbia Street is one of several Lower Mainland outposts, offering meat, vegetable, and vegan pizza options available for online ordering and takeout. A straightforward stop for a hot meal mid-ride.

detail.address: 323 East Columbia Street, New Westminster, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists 'Vegan Pizza' as a distinct category alongside meat and vegetable options

restaurant.name: Michi Craft Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Michi Craft Kitchen is a Chinese-Filipino fusion restaurant on Kingsway in East Vancouver, known for its 'Michi' grilled rice skewers and a menu that blends Cantonese comfort food with Filipino merienda snacks. The restaurant offers indoor seating in a unit within a Kingsway strip, with an active online ordering system for pickup. Its diverse menu — spanning grilled rice, omelette rice bowls, dry noodles, spaghetti, toast, and fresh beverages — makes it a versatile stop for a hungry cyclist.

restaurant.name: Power House Living Foods Co.
restaurant.desc: Power House Living Foods Co. is a restaurant in Duncan specializing in whole and living foods. The OSM record indicates offerings for gluten-free, raw, vegan, and vegetarian diets. Website details could not be verified at time of assessment.

restaurant.name: Sushi Moon

The kitchen emphasizes fresh, globally sourced ingredients with a broad menu that extends well beyond traditional Japanese fare. Online ordering is available for those wanting a quick meal on the go.

restaurant.name: Saigon Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Saigon Kitchen is a family-run Vietnamese restaurant on Nanaimo's Metral Drive serving traditional pho, fresh spring rolls, vermicelli noodle bowls, and Vietnamese curries made from recipes passed down through generations. The restaurant has earned a loyal following for its richly simmered pho broths and friendly atmosphere. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down dining experience with an extensive menu and online ordering for takeout.

The kitchen is known for its signature pho, slow-simmered for over 17 hours, alongside a full menu of rice dishes, vermicelli bowls, and fresh salads using local ingredients. Beer and wine are available, rounding out the experience for those looking to unwind after a ride.

restaurant.name: Fat Tony's Pizza

Positioned in the heart of the village surrounded by bars and nightclubs, it caters to a wide range of diets with dedicated vegan (Daiya cheese), vegetarian, and gluten-free pizza options. Pizza by the slice is available for a quick grab-and-go stop, and delivery covers all of Whistler.

restaurant.name: Salam Bombay

It is situated in a multi-unit building at 755 Burrard Street, making it convenient for cyclists passing through the heart of the city. The restaurant accommodates group reservations and private functions with an Indian cultural theme.

restaurant.name: Fish With You
restaurant.desc: Fish With You (鱼你在一起) is a Chinese restaurant on Kingsway specialising in fish dishes such as Szechuan Pepper Suancai Fish and Royal Tomato Fish. The restaurant offers dine-in with indoor seating and takeout, making it a potential mid-ride meal stop in the Burnaby/Vancouver border stretch of Kingsway. Its OSM record was last checked in late 2025, suggesting the Vancouver location is active.

restaurant.name: The Fish Counter
restaurant.desc: The Fish Counter is a fish-and-chips restaurant located on Main Street in Vancouver. Based on OSM data it specializes in fish and chips cuisine in the Mount Pleasant/Main Street neighbourhood, a well-travelled corridor for cyclists. No first-hand website content from the business could be confirmed.

restaurant.name: Mom's Dosa Palace
restaurant.desc: An Indian restaurant in Surrey specializing in dosas, the traditional South Indian rice flour flatbread. Appears to be a family operation based on the restaurant's name.

restaurant.name: Canffle
restaurant.desc: Canffle is a waffle-focused restaurant on Kingsway in East Vancouver, established in 2020, specializing in waffles made from traditional recipes with fresh ingredients. The spot offers indoor seating and a pickup/online order option, making it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor.

restaurant.name: Tea One Bubble Tea
restaurant.desc: Tea One is an authentic Taiwanese bubble tea shop in Maple Ridge's Haney neighbourhood, self-described as the only dedicated bubble tea spot in the area. The shop specialises in handcrafted drinks — fruit slushes, classic milk teas, and house-made tapioca pearls — using ingredients sourced directly from Taiwan. Online ordering for pickup is available through the website and a dedicated mobile app, making it a convenient refreshment stop on Lougheed Highway.

detail.address: 22529 Lougheed Hwy #150, Maple Ridge, BC V2X 0L5

restaurant.name: Bubble Tasty Tea
restaurant.desc: Bubble Tasty Tea is a bubble tea café located in a commercial unit on King Road in Chilliwack. It offers a spot for cyclists passing through the area to take a break and hydrate with cold or hot tea-based drinks. The café occupies approximately 1,051 square feet, suggesting a comfortable sit-down space.

detail.address: 33689 King Road, Unit 120, Chilliwack, BC V2S 7M9

restaurant.name: Anarchy Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Anarchy Coffee Roasters is a punk rock-inspired specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Kelowna, roasting small-batch, ethically sourced beans on-site and serving them alongside food in a community-minded shop. Founded in 2019 out of a passion for quality coffee and music, the business offers single-origin coffees, espresso blends, decaf options, and even in-house espresso machine repair services. Touring cyclists will find a characterful, welcoming stop with fresh-roasted coffee and food in the heart of Kelowna.

detail.address: 1880 Baron Rd C-Unit, Kelowna, BC, Canada

restaurant.name: One Saigon
restaurant.desc: One Saigon is a Vietnamese fast food spot at 979 Hornby Street in downtown Vancouver, serving pho, salad rolls, banh mi baguettes, and rice vermicelli dishes. The restaurant offers online ordering with 15-minute pickup, making it a practical fuel stop for cyclists navigating the city core. The focused menu includes several vegetarian choices across multiple categories.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu legend marks vegetarian items; Veggie Pho, Tofu Roll, Tofu baguette, and Tofu Roll are explicitly vegetarian. Vegan and GF not confirmed

restaurant.name: The Keg
restaurant.desc: The Keg Steakhouse + Bar Alberni Street is a full-service upscale steakhouse connected to the Shangri-La Hotel in the heart of downtown Vancouver, a short ride from Stanley Park and the Robson Street shopping corridor. The location features four patios and a private dining room, The Georgia Room, which can seat up to 120 guests. Takeout and DoorDash delivery are available, and the restaurant is wheelchair accessible.

restaurant.name: Bento Cafe
restaurant.desc: A sushi restaurant on West 1st Avenue in Vancouver. The business maintains an Instagram presence but no detailed online information is available.

restaurant.name: Imran Beef Noodle
restaurant.desc: Imran Beef Noodle is a halal Chinese restaurant on Vancouver's busy Robson Street specializing in Lanzhou-style hand-pulled beef noodles, as indicated by the Chinese name 伊穆兰·兰州牛肉面. It is a sit-down restaurant with indoor seating and wheelchair-accessible entry, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking for a filling halal meal in the West End.

restaurant.name: Tugboat Annie's Pub
restaurant.desc: Tugboat Annie's Pub & Grille is a family-operated waterfront pub at Shelter Island Marina in East Richmond, open since 1986 and run by the McPhail family ever since. Perched steps from the Fraser River, it offers a renovated patio with river views and a classic maritime atmosphere. The venue is adult-only (19+) and includes an attached liquor store alongside its full pub and grille menu.

restaurant.name: Coho Coffee
restaurant.desc: Coho Coffee is a cafe located on East Georgia Street in Vancouver. Touring cyclists passing through may stop for coffee and refreshment.

restaurant.name: Over Time Beer Works
restaurant.desc: Over Time Beer Works is a craft microbrewery and taproom in Kimberley, BC — a mountain town it proudly calls Canada's highest city — brewing a year-round lineup of ales and an IPA alongside rotating seasonal releases available only in the taproom. The casual, locals-friendly atmosphere is described as a good spot to get trail tips and area information from people who actually know the place. Cyclists can also take beer to go in growlers or 'bulldogs' for off-sales, and the brewery closes its sustainability loop by sending spent grains to a local butcher and composting hop and yeast waste for a nearby farmers market.

restaurant.name: Kranky Café
restaurant.desc: Kranky Café is a cozy, community-focused neighbourhood coffee shop in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant, built around locally roasted coffee and entirely homemade food — from fresh-baked pastries to hearty sandwiches and wraps. The space is designed as a gathering spot for the neighbourhood, offering a relaxed atmosphere for conversation, study, or a break from the road. A customer review highlights the 'great variety of sandwiches, wraps and drinks,' making it a practical mid-ride stop for fuelling up.

restaurant.name: Italia Bakery Vancouver
restaurant.desc: Italia Bakery Vancouver is a family-run Italian bakery with roots going back to 1966, tracing its lineage from Cesenatico, Italy through Montreal before settling in East Vancouver in 1973. In addition to handcrafted cannoli, artisan breads, and traditional pastries like sfogliatelle, the shop stocks a curated selection of Italian pantry staples — olive oil, dry pasta, lasagnas, pizza dough, olives, and cheese — making it a genuine mini Italian grocery stop. The bakery has operated continuously under its current name since 1985, making it one of Vancouver's longest-standing Italian food destinations.

restaurant.name: Harrison Corner Cafe
restaurant.desc: A cafe in Harrison, British Columbia, serving as a food and beverage stop for touring cyclists and other travelers in the area. Located on Hot Springs Road with retail building status. Specific services and amenities are unconfirmed.

restaurant.name: Burgoo
restaurant.desc: Burgoo is a Vancouver-born comfort food bistro founded in 2001, with an old-world countryside aesthetic built around earth tones and natural finishes. The Mount Pleasant outpost on Main Street serves hearty classics like French onion soup, mac and cheese, poutine, and a range of sandwiches and bowls in a cosy neighbourhood setting. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery are all available, making it a practical stop for cyclists needing a proper sit-down meal or a quick pickup.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian items: Veggie Sando, Hummus & Flatbread, Guacamole, F.A.B. Salad, Kale Caesar, Mac & Cheese. No explicit vegan or GF labelling visible in fetched content

restaurant.name: Mary Brown's
restaurant.desc: Mary Brown's is a 100% Canadian-owned fast food chain specializing in fresh, hand-cut and hand-breaded chicken and scratch-made Taters from whole Canadian-grown potatoes. This Kamloops location sits on Tranquille Road in a commercial building with drive-through service, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the North Shore area.

restaurant.name: Time Out Cafe
restaurant.desc: Time Out Cafe at City Hall is a café located inside Richmond City Hall, operated by BullMRKT & Truffles Fine Foods. It offers a wide-ranging menu of espresso drinks, breakfast items, sandwiches, salads, soups, pastries, and smoothies — a solid resupply stop for cyclists in central Richmond. Orders can be placed online for counter pickup.

restaurant.name: Vina Vietnamese
restaurant.desc: Vina Vietnamese is a Vietnamese fast food outlet located on the upper floor of a building in North Vancouver. It is part of a small chain serving Vietnamese cuisine in a quick-service format. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a convenient spot for a hot Vietnamese meal in the North Shore area.

restaurant.name: Pink Pearl Chinese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Pink Pearl is a long-established Cantonese and Szechuan Chinese seafood restaurant on East Hastings Street in East Vancouver, serving the community for nearly 30 years. The restaurant is known for dim sum service delivered by cart and for bringing live fish and crab tableside for customer inspection before cooking. With capacity for up to 70 tables, a free on-site parking lot, and full banquet and wedding hosting, it is one of the larger Chinese dining venues in the area.

detail.address: 1132 East Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 1S2
