restaurant.name: Triple O's
restaurant.desc: Triple O's is a BC-born premium quick-service burger chain with 70+ locations across British Columbia and beyond, famous for its secret 'Triple O' sauce, 100% fresh Canadian beef, and hand-scooped milkshakes. This Delta location, opened in 2021, is a walk-in and takeout stop with no drive-through, making it a direct-access option for cyclists riding through the Ladner area. It shares heritage with White Spot, and the Kennebec potatoes in its thick-cut fries have been grown in Delta, BC since 1935.

detail.address: 5206 Ladner Trunk Rd, Delta, BC V4K 1W3

restaurant.name: Nook
restaurant.desc: Nook is a well-established Italian restaurant group with multiple Vancouver locations, serving housemade pastas and wood-fired pizzas in the cycling-friendly Olympic Village neighbourhood. The Olympic Village location sits near the seawall and the Cambie Bridge cycling corridor, making it a convenient mid-ride or post-ride meal stop. Indoor and outdoor seating are available, and pickup orders can be placed online.

restaurant.name: Point No Point Resort
restaurant.desc: Point No Point Resort is a historic waterfront retreat established in 1952, perched on 40 acres of rugged Pacific coastline overlooking the Strait of Juan de Fuca near Shirley, BC, about 40 km west of Sooke on the West Coast Road. Its acclaimed fine-dining restaurant emphasizes fresh west coast Pacific seafood and has been recognized by Zagat, Sunset Magazine, and CBC. The resort's 25 private oceanfront cabins also make it a notable destination for cyclists seeking a multi-day stay along this scenic coastal route.

detail.address: 10829 West Coast Road, Shirley, BC V9Z 1G9

restaurant.name: The Canteen
restaurant.desc: The Canteen is an ice cream cafe located on Murray Street in North Vancouver. It provides a casual refreshment stop for cyclists exploring the North Shore area.

restaurant.name: Sunset Lounge & Grill
restaurant.desc: Sunset Lounge & Grill is a restaurant in downtown Prince Rupert. Website content is unavailable, limiting detailed information about the establishment. It serves as a dining option for tourists and touring cyclists visiting the community.

restaurant.name: Kokomo
restaurant.desc: Kokomo is a plant-based eatery and part of a small Vancouver-area chain, serving fresh bowls, acai bowls, smoothies, and handhelds in what the brand describes as a sun-filled, summer-inspired space. The Edgemont Village outpost sits in a neighbourhood commercial strip in North Vancouver, making it a natural refuelling stop for cyclists on the North Shore. The entirely plant-based menu—from lemongrass noodle salads to vegan burgers—caters well to health-conscious touring riders.

detail.address: 3270 Edgemont Boulevard, North Vancouver, BC V7R 2P2

restaurant.name: Coco Grill

It offers patio seating overlooking the water — a scenic and distinctive stop for cyclists riding the Dallas Road waterfront. The wharf setting makes it one of the more atmospheric dining options in downtown Victoria.

detail.address: 1 Dallas Road, Fisherman's Wharf, Victoria BC, Canada

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: A 24-hour Subway franchise on Knight Street in Vancouver, independently owned and operated, serving Footlongs, 6" sandwiches, wraps, and salads. Cyclists passing through the area at any hour can order in-restaurant, via curbside pickup, or for delivery. Wheelchair-accessible with indoor seating and no drive-through.

restaurant.name: A Taste of Vietnam
restaurant.desc: A Vietnamese restaurant situated on West Broadway in Vancouver, offering both dine-in and takeout service. West Broadway is a major east-west arterial commonly used by cyclists crossing the city, making this a convenient stop for riders moving through the Fairview or South Granville neighbourhoods.

restaurant.name: MeeT on Main
restaurant.desc: MeeT on Main is a fully plant-based comfort food restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street, founded in 2014 by three longtime Vancouver hospitality veterans with a mission to bring mainstream diners to plant-based eating. The menu leans into familiar comfort staples — poutine, burgers, 'chikkin' skewers, mac and cheese — all made from scratch with house-made sauces and no animal products. A patio, full craft cocktail program, and brunch service round out what is a lively neighbourhood anchor on a busy cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Swiss Bakery
restaurant.desc: Swiss Bakery operates on Main Street in Valemount, a small community in BC's Robson Valley. As a local bakery, it provides a natural stop for touring cyclists seeking fresh-baked goods and refreshment while passing through the region.

restaurant.name: lovelarte
restaurant.desc: Lovelarte is a charming artisan coffee café on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver, known for skillful latte art and a curated selection of specialty drinks including Spanish lattes and oat lattes. The café pairs its coffee with house-baked goods like pistachio raspberry tarts and muffins, and cultivates a cozy, welcoming atmosphere that regulars praise as a community hub.

restaurant.name: Pizza Art
restaurant.desc: Pizza Art is a halal pizza restaurant on Kingsway in Burnaby, part of a two-location operation serving Burnaby and Surrey. The menu spans meat, chicken, veggie, seafood, and classic pizza categories, alongside lahmacun, köfte, and salads. Dough is hand-stretched daily by in-house chefs, and the kitchen accommodates vegan and gluten-free diets.

restaurant.name: Chun Fun How
restaurant.desc: Chun Fun How is a Taiwanese bubble tea and specialty beverage shop grounded in values of heritage, authenticity, and devotion to quality Taiwanese ingredients. The West Broadway location offers an extensive menu spanning milk teas, fresh milk teas, fruit teas, and seasonal creations featuring osmanthus, purple yam, wintermelon, aloe vera, and lychee. The shop also offers office catering with large-format 3L drink boxes, reflecting a community-oriented, neighbourhood presence.

restaurant.name: Meat & Bread
restaurant.desc: Meat & Bread is a beloved Vancouver sandwich chain built around a small, focused menu of chef-crafted sandwiches anchored by their signature porchetta, carved fresh to order from whole-roasted pork. The West Broadway location also serves breakfast sandwiches and sides, making it a versatile stop for cyclists on the busy Broadway corridor. The interior is wheelchair accessible and offers indoor seating.

restaurant.name: Bean Scene North

It is part of the multi-location Bean Scene Coffee Works brand, which is a pioneer of the Third Wave Coffee movement in the Okanagan and operates its own small-batch roastery. The shop serves house-made baked goods prepared fresh daily from scratch using real, locally sourced ingredients.

restaurant.name: Artigiano Phibbs Exchange
restaurant.desc: Artigiano Phibbs Exchange is part of a Vancouver-born specialty coffee chain with over 25 years of history, known for house-roasted 100% Arabica espresso, in-house baked goods, and a European-inspired café aesthetic. The Phibbs Exchange location sits in North Vancouver, a popular gateway for cyclists riding the Seymour and Lynn Valley routes. The chain emphasizes organic and seasonal ingredients, avoiding artificial additives, and sources responsibly from local growers.

restaurant.name: Big Bang Sushi
restaurant.desc: Big Bang Sushi is a Japanese restaurant established in 2016 with two locations in Metro Vancouver, including this Richmond outpost in the Commerce Parkway commercial area. The menu spans traditional nigiri and sashimi to specialty rolls, donburi, udon, and teriyaki, with online ordering available for carryout. Vegetarian options are explicitly listed on the menu alongside a broad selection of sushi combinations and party trays.

restaurant.name: Lougheed Village Bar and Grill

It offers a relaxed atmosphere with sports viewing, sit-down meals, and table reservations for larger groups. The venue validates parking for up to six hours, making it a genuine rest stop, though cyclists should be aware that the entrance involves a staircase descent.

restaurant.name: Kamikaze Sushi
restaurant.desc: Kamikaze Sushi is a quick-service sushi counter in the Woodgrove Mall Food Court in north Nanaimo, offering rolls, poke bowls, ramen, and bento boxes made fresh daily on-site. The kitchen sources ingredients from local suppliers and uses traditional Japanese techniques, with a menu broad enough to suit vegetarians alongside seafood lovers. It is accessible via delivery apps or phone-ahead takeout, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Woodgrove area.

restaurant.name: Freshii
restaurant.desc: Freshii is a fast-casual health-food chain serving salads, wraps, burritos, poke bowls, energii bowls, and smoothies. The Abbotsford location sits at 1878 McCallum Road in a unit-format retail setting. Touring cyclists looking for a quick, nutrition-focused meal stop would find a familiar menu offering.

restaurant.name: Honey Doughnuts & Goodies
restaurant.desc: Honey Doughnuts & Goodies has been a Deep Cove institution since 1996, celebrated for freshly made doughnuts that have drawn fans including Kate Winslet. Situated in the heart of Deep Cove village — a natural endpoint for cycling routes around Indian Arm and the North Shore — the café serves a full menu of breakfasts, house-made sandwiches on vegan potato bread, homemade soups, and specialty espresso drinks. Owners Ashak and Ashifa Saferali have built a community hub equally loved by locals and visiting tourists.

detail.address: 4373 Gallant Avenue, North Vancouver, BC V7G 1L1

restaurant.name: Neptune Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Neptune Seafood Restaurant is a well-regarded Chinese seafood restaurant established in 1997 by the Neptune Restaurant Group, known throughout Greater Vancouver for its abalone specialties and gourmet dim sum. The Burnaby location occupies the second floor of Station Square and carries recognition as one of Vancouver's Top Ten Chinese Restaurants along with membership in the Commanderie des Cordons Bleu de France. It is one of three Neptune Seafood locations in the Lower Mainland, supported by a suite of delivery partners.

restaurant.name: La Belle Patate/Poutine
restaurant.desc: La Belle Patate has been serving authentic Québécois poutine on Vancouver's Davie Street since December 2009, offering over 40 varieties made with hand-cut fries and fresh cheese curds. Beyond poutine, the menu includes Montréal smoked meat sandwiches, authentic steamed hot dogs (steamies), and Canadian beer — a hearty fuel stop for cyclists passing through the West End. The restaurant has indoor seating and is wheelchair accessible.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian poutine option available (#15, green peppers/onions/mushrooms) and gravy is explicitly stated as vegetarian-friendly. Website explicitly states: 'we do NOT have any Vegan, Halal or Gluten Free dishes.'

restaurant.name: The Main
restaurant.desc: The Main on Main is a long-running neighbourhood restaurant and live music venue that has served Mediterranean, Western, and Italian classics since 1997. The space features warehouse-height ceilings, steel beams, and wood floors, giving it a rustic, unhurried atmosphere where regulars linger. An extensive cocktail, wine, and draft beer list — including local BC craft ales — rounds out the food and music experience.

detail.address: 4210 Main Street, Vancouver, British Columbia, V5V 3P9

restaurant.name: Ricardo's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Ricardo's Pizza is a Fraser Valley pizza chain that has operated since 1997, with three locations in Abbotsford, Chilliwack, and Mission. The menu covers pizza, pasta, wings, ribs, and sides with fully customizable pizza options available for online ordering or pickup. They also provide catering for events of all sizes, including hot school lunch programs and large group orders.

detail.address: 32750 George Ferguson Way #6, Abbotsford, BC V2T 4V6

restaurant.name: Free Bird Table & Bar
restaurant.desc: Free Bird Table & Bar is a Southern-inspired restaurant in Richmond, BC, serving comfort food classics like fried chicken and traditional Southern dishes in a warm, rustic atmosphere. Located within the Executive Hotel Vancouver Airport complex on Alderbridge Way, it offers a full sit-down dining experience with event hosting capacity for up to 800 guests. The brand also operates a second location in Squamish, making it a recognizable culinary name for cyclists riding the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

restaurant.name: Peri Peri Shack
restaurant.desc: The Peri Peri Shack is a flame-grilled chicken restaurant in New Westminster specializing in Portuguese-African peri peri cuisine, offering whole and half chickens marinated for 24 hours in a house spice blend across seven heat profiles from Plain to Peri Nero. The menu also covers seafood skewers, sharing packs, rice bowls, and a range of sides, with catering available for groups. It grew from a single location into a multi-location brand with franchising on offer, positioning itself as a community gathering spot.

restaurant.name: 66 Dessert House
restaurant.desc: 66 Dessert House is an Asian dessert cafe on Kingsway in Vancouver, offering a specialty dessert menu in a neighbourhood known for its density of Asian food businesses. restaurant.name: The Federal Store
restaurant.desc: The Federal Store is a small neighbourhood grocery and cafe in the heart of Mount Pleasant, Vancouver, specializing in local groceries, lunches, handmade baking, artisan cakes, and specialty coffee. It carries a curated selection of locally made products and offers an online shop for custom cake orders with pick-up or delivery. A touring cyclist passing through Mount Pleasant would find it a solid stop for a meal, coffee, and locally sourced provisions.

restaurant.name: Poke N Chat
restaurant.desc: Poke N Chat is a casual Gastown eatery specializing in poke bowls, ramen, and bubble tea, situated steps from the historic Steam Clock on Water Street. It is known for fresh ingredients and a cozy atmosphere with views of this Vancouver landmark. Cyclists exploring the waterfront or Gastown can order online for pickup or opt for delivery.

restaurant.name: Station BBQ
restaurant.desc: Station BBQ is a Southern-style smokehouse established in 2013 in Vernon, BC, built on the philosophy of cooking meats low and slow over real wood with no shortcuts. Brisket, pork ribs, pulled pork, and sausage are served 'naked' with house-made sauces on the side, and the kitchen also offers catering for events of all sizes. Hungry cyclists can dine in with table reservations or order takeout online, including BBQ by the pound to take on the road.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated /gluten-free page lists 14 GF-labelled items across appetizers, mains, sides, and takeout categories. No explicit vegetarian or vegan options noted

restaurant.name: Blend Bites Kelowna

The menu bridges chai culture and modern boba trends, offering a distinctive and refreshing stop compared to typical cafés. With over 235 items available for pickup through its online ordering system, it covers a wide range of cravings for cyclists passing through the downtown core.

restaurant.name: The Games Room
restaurant.desc: The Games Room is a dedicated sports and games bar within the multi-venue Strathcona Hotel complex in downtown Victoria, featuring 14 plasma screens, an 18-foot projector screen, pool tables, and a raised mezzanine dart hall. It is part of Vancouver Island's self-described largest pub operation and draws a lively crowd for major sporting events. Touring cyclists stopping in downtown Victoria will find solid pub fare and a full bar in a high-energy atmosphere.

restaurant.name: Pizzability

restaurant.name: Triple O's
restaurant.desc: Triple O's is a BC-born premium quick-service burger chain known for its secret Triple 'O' sauce, hand-scooped milkshakes, and fresh Canadian beef patties. This Abbotsford location is co-sited at a Chevron gas station on Clearbrook Road, one of over 70 locations across BC, Alberta, and Ontario. Delivery via Skip the Dishes is available in addition to the drive-thru and takeout window.

restaurant.name: Cactus Club Cafe
restaurant.desc: Cactus Club Cafe at Coquitlam Centre is a polished, chef-driven casual dining chain set inside the Coquitlam Centre shopping complex in the Tri-Cities area. The menu spans modern international dishes—sushi, steaks, pastas, bowls, and shareables—served in a lounge-forward space with a patio and private dining rooms. It opened in January 2023 and offers a convenient full-service meal stop for cyclists passing through the Barnet Highway corridor.

restaurant.name: Ricky's COUNTRY - Restaurant -
restaurant.desc: A country-style restaurant in Chilliwack. Detailed information about amenities and services is not currently available due to website connectivity issues.

restaurant.name: Sarpino's Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Sarpino's Pizzeria is a franchise pizza chain with a location on Esquimalt Road at the western edge of Greater Victoria. The menu spans classic, gourmet, and signature pizzas alongside pastas, salads, wings, and desserts, with a gluten-free crust upgrade available. The business is takeout- and delivery-focused, making it a quick fuel stop for cyclists moving through Esquimalt.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Gluten-free crust explicitly listed as an add-on option across all pizza sizes

restaurant.name: Chef's Choice Chinese Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Chef's Choice Seafood Restaurant is a Michelin-recommended Chinese seafood establishment on West Broadway in Vancouver, specialising in premium live seafood — King Crab, Lobster, Abalone, and Sea Cucumber — alongside traditional dim sum. The restaurant features private dining rooms accommodating groups of up to 24 and is rooted in traditional Chinese culinary arts. It would suit a touring cyclist seeking a substantial sit-down meal in a full-service restaurant setting.

restaurant.name: Branch on Bowen
restaurant.desc: Branch on Bowen is a community gathering place established in 2016 that began as a taco shop and has grown into a multi-season destination, serving handmade corn-tortilla tacos with locally sourced BC ingredients — grass-fed beef, free-range chicken, smoked salmon, and vegan sweet potato — alongside Earnest Ice Cream and seasonal ramen and dumplings. The counter-service format and individually priced menu items make it a practical stop for a quick, satisfying meal. It also houses the Narwhal gift shop, adding a browsing option to the visit.

detail.address: 400 Bowen Island Trunk Rd, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Sweet Potato Taco explicitly marked 'GF & Vegan'; all tacos served on corn tortillas marked GF; About page references 'Creamy Vegan Ramen'

restaurant.name: Annabelle's
restaurant.desc: A cafe offering online ordering on Quebec Street in Vancouver. Blends casual cafe service with studio elements, providing a quick refreshment option for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Don Tacos
restaurant.desc: Don Tacos is a Mexican fast-food spot in Richmond, BC offering dine-in alongside delivery and pickup ordering. The OSM record places it on level 1 of a building, suggesting an upstairs or mall-level unit rather than a street-front location. Cyclists passing through Richmond's busy urban grid will find it a convenient stop for a quick Mexican meal.

restaurant.name: Cafe Lokal
restaurant.desc: A neighborhood cafe on West 4th Avenue in Vancouver's Kitsilano area, serving as a local gathering spot. Details about amenities and services are unavailable due to website access issues.

restaurant.name: YL's Curry Bowl
restaurant.desc: YL's Curry Bowl is a Malaysian-style fast-food stall specializing in authentic Penang-inspired curry, Hainanese chicken, and laksa noodles, located inside the Surrey Guildford T&T Supermarket Food Court. The kitchen uses premium ingredients including A-grade beef brisket and New Zealand lamb, with everything made fresh daily. For a touring cyclist in the Surrey area, it offers a filling, flavourful hot meal in a covered, climate-controlled setting.

notes.Takeout: Online ordering available; family combos are pick-up only. Walk-in ordering at the food court stall also available

restaurant.name: Discovery Coffee
restaurant.desc: Discovery Coffee is a locally rooted Victoria specialty coffee roaster operating multiple cafe locations across the city, including this Oak Bay Avenue outpost. The company runs its own roastery on Rock Bay Avenue and partners with Yonni's Doughnuts, making it a notable stop for coffee and baked goods. Touring cyclists will find it a convenient neighbourhood cafe in the heart of Oak Bay.

restaurant.name: Middlechild
restaurant.desc: Middlechild is a small coffee shop on Sechelt's main commercial strip, Cowrie Street, operating out of a unit in a commercial building in the heart of town. The cafe has outdoor seating, making it a potential stopping point for cyclists passing through Sechelt on the Sunshine Coast route. Its Instagram-only web presence suggests a locally rooted, independent operation.

detail.address: 5641 Cowrie Street, Unit 102, Sechelt, BC V0N 3A0

restaurant.name: Belgian Fries
restaurant.desc: Belgian Fries is a bar and restaurant on Vancouver's busy Commercial Drive, serving Belgian-style fries and Canadian comfort food since 1998. The menu anchors on hand-cut fries and 18 varieties of poutine, alongside burgers, fish and chips, and sandwiches. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the restaurant offers a pickup/takeout option for cyclists on the move.

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: A Starbucks Coffee location in Langley, BC, occupying a retail unit at 8840 210 Street in what appears to be a shopping centre. The store offers the full Starbucks menu of hot and cold beverages and food items with both indoor and outdoor seating areas. Touring cyclists passing through Langley can expect public-access washrooms and free Wi-Fi.

restaurant.name: The Chopped Leaf
restaurant.desc: The Chopped Leaf in Tsawwassen is a health-focused fast-casual franchise serving customizable salads, bowls, wraps, sandwiches, and soups made with fresh, hand-chopped ingredients and exclusive signature dressings. The restaurant is designed to accommodate a wide range of dietary needs, with vegan, vegetarian, gluten-friendly, dairy-free, and nut-free options all available. Situated in Delta near the Tsawwassen ferry terminal, it offers a practical and nutritious stop for cyclists moving through the southern Lower Mainland.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists 'gluten friendly vegan vegetarian dairy-free nut-free' as menu options on the location page

restaurant.name: Maruhachi Ra-men
restaurant.desc: Maruhachi Ra-men is a ramen restaurant chain with a West End Vancouver branch on Bidwell Street, a short ride from Stanley Park and the Seawall. It is part of Maruhachi Ra-men Canada and offers pickup ordering in addition to dine-in service. The West End location puts it within easy reach of several popular urban cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Pine House Bread and Cake House
restaurant.desc: Pine House Bread and Cake House is a Chinese bakery on East Hastings Street in Vancouver, offering breads and cakes in the Chinese baking tradition. It operates out of a retail building along a busy commercial corridor, making it a convenient stop for cyclists travelling along the Hastings Street route. The shop's focus on baked goods means touring cyclists can pick up quick, portable snacks.

restaurant.name: Kelly O'Bryan's Neighborhood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kelly O'Bryan's is a lively neighborhood restaurant and pub occupying three distinct spaces in downtown Kelowna: the Kelly O'Bryan's Restaurant, the Carlos O'Bryan's Pub, and a rooftop patio called the Rooftop Paddy 'O. The location sits close to Okanagan Lake in the heart of the downtown core, making it a convenient stop on any waterfront ride. Part of a BC-wide chain, the Kelowna outpost runs a full calendar of evening events including karaoke nights, DJ shows, and themed drink specials.

restaurant.name: Felicita's Campus Pub
restaurant.desc: Felicita's is a student-owned and operated campus pub at the University of Victoria, named in honour of Felicita Gomez — a beloved custodian who worked at UVic from 1967 to 1996 and was regarded as a mother figure by generations of students. Located in the Student Union Building, it offers a pub-style food menu alongside a rotating selection of local BC craft beers on tap from breweries including Hoyne, Vancouver Island Brewing, and Phillips. Cyclists riding through the UVic campus will find an outdoor patio and a community-rooted atmosphere with deep ties to Victoria's university neighbourhood.

detail.address: Student Union Building, University of Victoria, Victoria, BC V8W 3P3

notes.Takeout: Menu page states 'Daily Features pricing is not available to-go', implying other menu items are available for takeout orders
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a Veggie Burger, a vegetarian fries option listed as '10 Veg / 12 Meat', and Whistler Forager gluten-free beer by the bottle

restaurant.name: Joy Cafe Vancouver
restaurant.desc: Joy Cafe Vancouver is a Cantonese restaurant on SW Marine Drive serving a broad menu that spans traditional dim sum, Hong Kong-style baked rice and spaghetti dishes, and fusion Asian fare. The cha chaan teng-style offerings — baked Portuguese chicken rice, pan-fried rice noodles, congee, and a full dim sum selection — make it a satisfying full-meal stop for cyclists in south Vancouver. Online pickup ordering is available directly through the restaurant's website.

detail.address: 525 Southwest Marine Drive, Vancouver, BC V6P5X8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes plant-based items such as Stuffed Whole Eggplant in Thai Sauce (B8) and various dim sum with vegetable fillings. No gluten-free labelling found

restaurant.name: Earls
restaurant.desc: Earls Yaletown is a full-service location of the Earls Kitchen + Bar chain, situated in Vancouver's lively Yaletown neighbourhood on Mainland Street. The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor patio seating alongside dine-in, takeout, and delivery options. It serves American-style cuisine with vegetarian options, making it a substantial meal stop for cyclists moving through central Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: No contradiction found in website content

restaurant.name: Kim Express
restaurant.desc: Kim Express is a Vietnamese restaurant on West King Edward Avenue in Vancouver's Cambie Village neighbourhood. Situated along a busy arterial corridor, it offers a casual dining option for cyclists moving through the area between the Cambie greenway and Queen Elizabeth Park. The 'Express' branding suggests a quick-service focus suited to riders on the move.

restaurant.name: Pinche Taco Shop
restaurant.desc: Pinche Taco Shop is a counter-service Mexican taqueria in downtown Vancouver, part of the La Taquería group that also operates the La Taquería Restaurant in Burnaby and Comedor on Yukon Street. The menu centres on authentic tacos with a wide range of fillings — from pollo al carbón and lechón to Baja fish — plus burritas, burritos, and bowls. Its Seymour Street location places it squarely in the city's downtown core, making it a practical fast-food stop for cyclists moving through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple meatless fillings available as tacos and burritos: Papas con Crema, Hongos con Queso, Acelga con Huevo, Rajas Con Crema, Frijoles Refritos

restaurant.name: Haveli Indian Bistro
restaurant.desc: Haveli Indian Bistro is a casual sit-down Indian restaurant in Surrey serving a broad menu of traditional appetizers, tandoori dishes, biryanis, and Indo-Chinese fusion fare made with fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, and online ordering, and also operates a full catering service for weddings, corporate events, and private parties. With a 4.2-star rating and a party hall on-site, it functions as both a neighbourhood dining destination and an event venue.

detail.address: 7488 King George Boulevard, Surrey, BC V3W 0H9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Extensive vegetarian options confirmed: Veg Thali, Hara Bhara Kebab, Paneer Tikka, Veg Kathi Roll, Pav Bhaji, Gol Gappa, Dahi Bhalla, and multiple BOGO vegetarian offers

restaurant.name: Hồng Phát
restaurant.desc: Hủ Tiếu Hồng Phát is the Canadian outpost of a Saigon noodle institution that has been serving Nam Vang-style rice noodle soup since 1975 and earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand in Vietnam in 2023 and 2024. The Richmond location is one of two BC branches (the other in Vancouver) and sits in a commercial unit on Ackroyd Road, bringing a well-regarded Vietnamese comfort-food tradition to the Lower Mainland.

detail.address: 8291 Ackroyd Road, Unit 100, Richmond, BC V6X 3K5

restaurant.name: Tofino Waves and Tacos
restaurant.desc: Tofino Waves and Tacos is an authentic Mexican restaurant founded by Magdalena, who spent over a decade in Tofino before opening the spot to share the flavours of her home region of Veracruz. The menu centres on tacos, quesadillas, and tostadas made with house sauces and slow-cooked meats, with most items available on gluten-free corn tortillas. It is an independent, locally owned restaurant and a genuine find for cyclists looking for a satisfying hot meal in Tofino.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items explicitly labelled 'corn tortillas (gluten free)' — El Clasico, Beef in Adobo, Pork en Green, Green & Adobo tacos, and several quesadillas and tostadas. No explicitly vegetarian or vegan dishes identified on the website

restaurant.name: Neptune Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Neptune Seafood Restaurant is a long-established Cantonese and seafood dining destination founded in 1997 by the Neptune Restaurant Group, with a reputation for abalone specialties and gourmet dim sum across its Greater Vancouver locations. It holds membership in the Commanderie des Cordons Bleu de France and has been recognized as one of Vancouver's Top Ten Chinese Restaurants. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond can stop for a sit-down dim sum lunch or dinner, or order takeout through several delivery and pickup platforms.

restaurant.name: Ichi Sushi
restaurant.desc: Sushi Ichi is a Japanese restaurant on the East Island Highway in Parksville serving sushi rolls, tempura, katsu, gyoza, sashimi, and other traditional Japanese dishes made with fresh ingredients. The cozy wood-accented dining room accommodates both intimate dinners and larger group gatherings, and the restaurant has built a loyal local following for attentive service and artful dish presentation. Takeout and catering options are available for cyclists who prefer to eat on the go or at a destination.

detail.address: 541 E Island Hwy E, Parksville, BC V9P 1V2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website front page states 'Special dietary choices such as vegetarian sushi are also available, ensuring everyone can indulge in a delicious meal without compromise.'

restaurant.name: Jim's Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Jim's Pizzeria and Spaghetti House is a well-established Chilliwack pizza and pasta spot known for dough made in-house daily and house sauce using local tomatoes. The broad menu covers specialty pizzas, lasagna, spaghetti, wings, and salads, with a dedicated gluten-free and vegan section. The business has two Chilliwack locations and offers both dine-in and delivery, making it a substantial meal stop for cyclists moving through the Fraser Valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated 'Gluten Free & Vegan' page: gluten-free crusts available in small, medium, and large; vegan Daiya cheese add-on for any pizza or pasta; vegetarian pizza listed on main menu

restaurant.name: Afghan Horsemen Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Established in 1974, Afghan Horsemen is the first Afghan restaurant ever opened in Canada, a family-managed institution that has anchored the Granville Island neighbourhood for over 50 years. The second-floor dining room offers both indoor and outdoor seating with a full menu of authentic Afghan cuisine, from lamb and chicken kebab platters to a wide range of vegetarian dishes. It has earned multiple Georgia Straight Readers' Choice Golden Plates awards for Best Middle Eastern Restaurant and remains a well-known culinary landmark in Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu confirms multiple vegetarian dishes including Humous, Sabzi Mast, Eggplant Dip, Cauliflower Pakwara, Potato Boulany, Spinach & Feta Boulany, and various vegetarian sides. No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Veggie Bowl
restaurant.desc: Vietnamese restaurant with a vegetarian-focused menu located on Kingsway in Vancouver. Offers indoor seating in a no-smoking environment. A convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking plant-based dining options.

restaurant.name: Jaide & Joel's Baking Company
restaurant.desc: Jaide & Joel's Baking Co is a fully dedicated vegan and gluten-free bakery and café in Kelowna's Rutland neighbourhood, offering fresh-baked donuts, loaves, scones, cakes, and freshly brewed organic coffee daily with no pre-ordering required. The shop prides itself on zero taste compromise for dietary restrictions, and also handles custom celebration cakes for events. Complimentary parking is available in the lot behind the building, and DoorDash delivery is available for those not stopping in.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'our entire store is dedicated vegan and gluten-free'; OSM confirms and

restaurant.name: Sahel
restaurant.desc: Sahel is a Persian restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver with 25 years of experience, specializing in kebabs, slow-cooked stews, and aromatic rice dishes rooted in traditional Persian and Mediterranean cuisine. The restaurant is described as a 'luxe spot' with elegant décor and attentive service, positioning itself as a destination for refined dining and special occasions. Touring cyclists will find a broad sit-down menu that includes several vegetarian and vegan options alongside hearty meat platters.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Veggie Kebab' (onion, zucchini, mushroom, eggplant, sweet pepper, tomato, basmati rice) and 'Vegan Eggplant Stew' (explicitly labelled vegan on the menu)

restaurant.name: On Lok Restaurant & Wun Tun House
restaurant.desc: On Lok has been a family-owned East Vancouver institution since 1982, built around authentic Chinese comfort food like duck wonton noodle soup, chow mein, and congee served in generous portions. Located on East Hastings in the Hastings-Sunrise neighbourhood, it has a decades-long loyal following among locals who prize its consistently good food and relaxed atmosphere. A touring cyclist passing through East Vancouver will find it a filling and unpretentious stop, with online ordering available through Square.

restaurant.name: Haidilao Express
restaurant.desc: Haidilao Express is part of the internationally renowned Haidilao hot pot chain, which entered Canada in December 2018 and has grown to thousands of locations worldwide. The hot pot concept centres on customizable soup bases, thinly sliced meats, fresh seafood, and a mix-your-own dipping sauce bar. This North Vancouver location sits on the second floor and is an indoor-only dining environment.

detail.address: 4567 Lougheed Highway (Amazing Brentwood TABLES Food Court), Burnaby, BC

restaurant.name: Lamb Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Lamb Hot Pot is a casual Chinese hotpot restaurant in a Richmond strip mall specializing in lamb-based pots served with bones, marrow, and cumin lamb skewers. The restaurant features a DIY dipping sauce cart and offers plastic gloves for hands-on eating — a fun, communal experience well suited to groups. Reviewers highlight generous portions and a welcoming atmosphere despite the no-frills setting.

detail.address: 3779 Sexsmith Road Suite 1103, Richmond, BC V6X 2H6

restaurant.name: Tenen Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Tenen Restaurant is a Serbian and Eastern European diner in Burnaby, founded in 2015 by two childhood friends from Knin — a Roman-era town whose ancient name, Tenen, the restaurant carries. The menu features hearty Balkan staples like chevapi, karadjordjeva schnitzel, cabbage rolls, and traditional meze, served in a kitschy, homey atmosphere that reviewers describe as feeling like coming home. A loyalty program and catering service round out the offering.

detail.address: 7569 Royal Oak Avenue, Burnaby, BC V5J 4J8

restaurant.name: La Cuisson Cafe
restaurant.desc: La Cuisson Cafe is a family-owned artisan coffee shop and in-house roaster in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, founded in 2004 by owner Jason Hsu after 30 years of coffee expertise. The café is known for rare and specialty brewing methods including syphon-style, pour-over, and Italian-style coffees using single-origin beans sourced globally and roasted weekly on-site. It also offers an extensive menu of fresh in-house baked pastries, toasts, sandwiches, waffles, and desserts, making it a well-rounded café stop.

restaurant.name: Old Town Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Old Town Ice Cream is an ice cream shop located in the historic downtown core of Ladysmith on Vancouver Island. Ladysmith's First Avenue is a heritage commercial strip popular with cyclists riding the E&N corridor or touring the island, making a sweet stop here a natural fit for a long ride.

restaurant.name: The Peri Peri Shack
restaurant.desc: The Peri Peri Shack is a North Vancouver restaurant specializing in flame-grilled chicken marinated for 24 hours in a peri peri spice blend, available in seven heat levels from Mild to Peri Nero. The concept draws on the culinary tradition of the African bird's eye chili, carried to the Iberian Peninsula by Portuguese explorers and now reimagined as a cornerstone of the local community. Cyclists can fuel up on generous sharing packs, a range of sides, and a vegetarian paneer option, with online ordering also available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Paneer and Rice (V)' explicitly marked as vegetarian

restaurant.name: La Meza Grill
restaurant.desc: La Meza Grill is a family-owned Filipino restaurant that has been serving traditional regional cuisine in North Delta since June 2014. The extensive menu draws on culinary traditions from across the Philippine archipelago — from grilled chicken inasal and pork sisig to breakfast silog plates — offering a hungry cyclist a substantial and flavourful sit-down meal. DoorDash delivery is also available for those who prefer to eat on the go.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegetarian items on menu: Pritong Lumpia (fried vegetable spring roll), Fresh Lumpia (fresh vegetable roll), Tofu Sisig (diced tofu in soya and calamansi), Ensaladang Talong (grilled eggplant salad), Ukoy (deep fried vegetable fritters). No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Mink
restaurant.desc: Mink is an artisan chocolate café in downtown Vancouver specializing in handcrafted ganache chocolate bars and bonbons made with Cacao Barry chocolate. The signature experience is a personal fondue where guests roast marshmallows at their table and dip them in their choice of milk, dark, or dairy-free dark chocolate ganache. A touring cyclist would find it a memorable indulgence stop right in the city centre, across from a park at the Hornby cross street.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists a VEGAN CHOCOLATE product category and offers a dairy-free dark chocolate ganache option for the fondue experience

restaurant.name: Golestan Bakery
restaurant.desc: A Persian bakery located on Marine Drive in North Vancouver with indoor and outdoor seating. Offers fresh-baked goods in a smoke-free environment.

restaurant.name: Oystercatcher Seafood Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: Oystercatcher is a waterfront seafood and cocktail bar on Salt Spring Island, opened in 2002 and part of the locally-owned Salt Spring Group. Cyclists can dine casually by the river-rock fireplace or on the waterfront deck, with a menu highlighting local seafood, Salt Spring lamb, and regional craft beverages. Its Ganges harbour location makes it a natural stop on a Salt Spring Island cycling loop.

detail.address: 110 Purvis Ln #201, Ganges Salt Spring Island, BC

restaurant.name: The Ruby on Douglas
restaurant.desc: The Ruby is a locally owned scratch brunch restaurant with three Victoria locations, open since 2015 and built around relationships with local suppliers. It offers a refined take on eclectic southern brunch fare paired with the city's best vinyl collection and warmly attentive service. A touring cyclist arriving hungry would find generous, hearty dishes with strong vegan and gluten-free options well-suited to refuelling.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: All three location menus include a dedicated 'VEGAN FARE' section (Vegan Mexi Hash, The Greenhouse Sandwich, Vegan Breakfast Tacos) and a gluten-free biscuit substitution option available throughout the menu

restaurant.name: Szechuan Chili Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Szechuan Chili Restaurant has been serving bold, spice-forward Szechuan cuisine on Vancouver's West 6th Avenue since 2001. Signature dishes include Dry Szechuan Chili Ginger Beef, General Tso's Chicken, and a wide range of dumplings and noodle dishes. The restaurant offers both dine-in and online ordering with pickup, and also provides catering services.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'Vegetarian' as a dedicated menu category under 'We Serve For You'

restaurant.name: Big Bite Donair
restaurant.desc: Big Bite Donair has been a fixture of the Lynn Valley community since 2016, serving authentic Middle Eastern and Mediterranean fare — kababs over open flame, homemade sauces, shawarma, falafel, and rich Afghan rice dishes. It is primarily a takeout operation with very limited seating, and the owner is widely praised by customers for personal attention and food quality. The restaurant also accepts Bitcoin Lightning payments, an unusual feature for a small neighbourhood eatery.

detail.address: 1252 Lynn Valley Road, North Vancouver, V7J 2A3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website banner reads 'Planty of vegeterian options'; falafel dishes are described as 'Irresistible Taste for Vegans'; menu includes a note: 'NOTE FOR VEGANS: Please report by placing order not to add dairy.' No GF mention found

restaurant.name: Sal y Limon
restaurant.desc: Sal y Limon is a family-founded Mexican restaurant inspired by traditional recipes from Manzanillo, Mexico, serving tacos, tortas, burritos, and other street food-style dishes. The South Surrey location is part of a small Vancouver-area chain created by four food enthusiasts who wanted to bring authentic Mexican flavour to BC. The restaurant emphasizes a welcoming, family-friendly atmosphere and offers both pick-up and delivery ordering.

restaurant.name: Monarch Burger
restaurant.desc: Monarch Burger is a Vancouver cult-favourite burger spot born out of the legendary 'Dirty Burger' served at Campagnolo Upstairs, where a nightly limit of 35 burgers created a ravenous following. The kitchen uses dry-aged, freshly ground BC beef, hand-shaped buns baked at a local East Van bakery, and housemade pickles and sauces. In addition to its fixed Main Street location, Monarch runs seasonal pop-ups across the Lower Mainland.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a 'Veggie Mushroom Burger' confirming at least one vegetarian option. No vegan or GF options mentioned

restaurant.name: Yuan Soy Food
restaurant.desc: Yuan Soy Food (人和豆腐) is a Chinese fast food spot on East 1st Avenue in Vancouver's East Side, with a name suggesting a focus on soy and tofu-based dishes. Located on the ground floor of a commercial building, it offers a quick stop for cyclists riding through this neighbourhood. Its Instagram presence hints at an active local following, though the content is only accessible to logged-in users.

restaurant.name: Captain's Oven Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Captain's Oven Pizza is an authentic Neapolitan-style pizzeria founded by siblings who trained in Naples and Istanbul before bringing their craft to Vancouver. Pizzas are hand-stretched daily using San Marzano tomatoes and fresh mozzarella, then baked in a 3-ton stone-brick oven imported from Tuscany. The North Vancouver location is one of five Lower Mainland outposts and offers dine-in, takeout, and local delivery.

detail.address: 935 Marine Dr, North Vancouver, BC V7P 1S3

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Can I order online or over the phone for pickup? Yes, we do offer online ordering' and specials are noted as 'For pick up and dine in only'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states 'We offer a gluten free pizza crust' and 'We offer vegan cheese and you can customize your pizza to make it both vegan and vegetarian'; salads can also be customized for dietary needs

restaurant.name: Lighthouse
restaurant.desc: Lighthouse is a fast-food fish and chips spot in Richmond, BC. Fish and chips is a classic refuelling meal for touring cyclists, offering a hearty, portable option. The Richmond area is popular with cyclists on the Dyke Trail network, making local quick-service spots like this potentially convenient pit stops.

detail.address: 12031 Second Ave #100, Richmond, BC V7E 3L6, Canada

restaurant.name: Kirin Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kirin Seafood Restaurant is a long-established fine Cantonese seafood and dim sum restaurant that has been a fixture of Richmond's culinary scene since 1987, operating under world-class chefs with roots in Hong Kong's celebrated 'New Era' cuisine movement. The Richmond location sits in Three West Centre at Westminster Highway and No. 3 Road, offering elaborate menus featuring whole abalone, lobster, and dim sum alongside banquet and wedding services. For touring cyclists exploring Richmond, it represents a notable opportunity to experience high-end Cantonese cooking in one of Canada's most acclaimed Chinese-food destinations.

detail.address: 200 Three West Centre, 7900 Westminster Highway, Richmond, BC V6X 1A5

notes.Takeout: Menu lists 'Roasted Suckling Pig Special Set Menu (take out only)' and 'Frozen Dim Sum & Entrées' as packaged takeout products

restaurant.name: Manoush'eh
restaurant.desc: Manoush'eh is a halal Lebanese and Levantine restaurant on Vancouver's Davie Street specializing in freshly baked manousheh — a traditional Middle Eastern flatbread topped with everything from za'atar and cheese to kafta, falafel, and soujouk. The menu also features plates, wraps, soups, and desserts such as knafeh, with many items clearly marked vegan or vegetarian. Reviewers consistently praise the handmade dough quality and the warm, community-oriented atmosphere.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu labels vegan items (VG) — e.g. Zaatar Manousheh, Falafel Manousheh, Hummus, Mutabal — and vegetarian items (V) — e.g. Cheese Manousheh, Muhamara; homepage states 'Whether a vegan, vegetarian or a meat lover.' No GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Amble Coffee
restaurant.desc: Amble Coffee is a specialty coffee shop and mobile truck tucked near the Vedder River, built around the philosophy of slowing down and connecting with nature. The 'Amble' name is intentional — it invites customers to linger over coffee or tea rather than rush. For touring cyclists finishing a ride along the Vedder, it offers a nature-adjacent café stop in Chilliwack.

restaurant.name: Kumare Express
restaurant.desc: Kumare Express is the Vancouver outpost of the Kumare family of Filipino restaurants, which also operates a Richmond location and a roving street food truck serving the Lower Mainland. The kitchen leans into the full breadth of Filipino regional cooking — silog breakfast combos, slow-cooked soups like bulalo and sinigang, and fried appetizers like lumpiang Shanghai — alongside a bakery offering authentic Filipino pastries available for provincial shipping. The restaurant embraces both dry and saucy versions of classic dishes, reflecting the rich regional diversity of Filipino cuisine.

notes.Packed lunches: 'Boxed Lunch' is listed as a dedicated menu category and navigation item on the website
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website About page states: 'Our menu at Kumare is designed to cater to a variety of dietary needs and preferences, including vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options.'

restaurant.name: Breka Bakery & Café
restaurant.desc: Breka Bakery & Café is a locally rooted, family-owned Vancouver institution open around the clock every day of the year, with roots in a German bakery founded in the Sunset neighbourhood in 2006. The Bute Street location is one of eight spread across the city, each carrying a wide range of baked goods, sandwiches, soups, snacks, and hot beverages alongside dedicated vegan and gluten-friendly items. It has become a neighbourhood anchor regularly voted among Vancouver's best cafés, and its 24/7 availability makes it an unusually reliable resupply stop for touring cyclists at any hour.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website has dedicated 'Vegan' and 'Gluten-Free' menu sections with multiple labelled items

restaurant.name: Peaceful Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Peaceful Restaurant has served Northern Chinese cuisine in Vancouver since 1998, led by owner-chef Charlie Huang whose hand-pulled noodles, dumplings, and beef rolls have earned recognition from Food Network, USA Today, and local food media. The menu centres on Xi'an-inspired flavours — aromatic spices, bold sauces, and house-made dim sum — drawing on the culinary crossroads of the ancient Silk Road. Situated on West 4th Avenue, a key cycling corridor connecting Kitsilano to downtown Vancouver, it is a convenient mid-ride dining stop.

restaurant.name: Hoshi
restaurant.desc: Hoshi is a Japanese cuisine restaurant tucked beneath the Burrard Bridge on Beach Avenue, steps from the Vancouver Harbour seawall—one of the city's busiest cycling routes. The kitchen spans everyday sushi, teishoku lunch sets, and traditional kaiseki multi-course dinners available by pre-order, offering a broad range of dining experiences in one spot. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the restaurant provides free validated parking in the adjacent building for those arriving by car or with a loaded touring bike.

detail.address: Unit 3-1010 Beach Avenue, Vancouver, BC V6E 1T7

notes.Takeout: Website navigation includes a dedicated 'Take Out' section and online ordering; menu page lists combos and party trays explicitly marked 'ONLY FOR TAKE OUT'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a dedicated VEGETABLE COMBO (Avocado Oshi, Veggie Roll, Inari nigiri). No vegan or GF labelling explicitly stated

restaurant.name: 3 Dogs Brewing
restaurant.desc: 3 Dogs Brewing is a craft microbrewery and pub located in a commercial unit in Tsawwassen, BC. OSM tags it as both a brewery and a retail alcohol shop, suggesting it may operate a taproom alongside production. Tsawwassen is near the BC Ferries terminal and the US border crossing, making it a potential stop for cycle tourists on the Salish Sea corridor.

restaurant.name: Everest Indian & Nepalese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Everest Indian & Nepalese Restaurant is a family-owned, licensed fine dining establishment in West Kelowna, BC, run by owner Ram Sapkota who immigrated from Nepal in 2007 and trained as a chef across Europe. The restaurant serves an extensive menu of authentic Indian and Nepalese cuisine—from tandoori specialties and Nepalese meals to fusion dishes—and has accumulated over 200 five-star Google reviews. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery with an online ordering option make it a flexible stop for touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian Dishes' section; customer review states 'Lots of vegan/vegetarian options'; menu page notes 'ALL SOUPS & SALADS ARE GLUTEN FREE'

restaurant.name: Bubble World Surrey
restaurant.desc: Bubble World is a Chinese restaurant located at 10090 152 Street in Surrey, BC. Beyond its OSM classification as a Chinese cuisine restaurant, no operational details are available as the business website is currently a placeholder.

restaurant.name: Faubourg
restaurant.desc: Faubourg is a family-owned French boulangerie-pâtisserie founded in Vancouver in 2010, with three city locations including this Kerrisdale outpost. The bakery produces croissants, artisanal breads baked five times daily in a French deck oven, and a full range of pastries and macarons alongside a specialty coffee program. Touring cyclists will find a solid stop for quality food and espresso drinks in Vancouver's west side, with both dine-in and takeout available.

restaurant.name: Wendy's
restaurant.desc: Wendy's is a major North American fast food chain specialising in fresh, never-frozen beef burgers, chicken sandwiches, and sides. This Chilliwack location offers drive-through and takeout service, making it a quick calorie stop for cyclists passing through the area. As a well-known chain it provides predictable food options including salads and chili alongside its signature burgers.

notes.Wi-Fi: Not confirmed or contradicted by the corporate website

restaurant.name: Fountain Diner
restaurant.desc: Langfords Fountain Diner is a restaurant in the Langford area west of Victoria, situated along Bryn Maur Road. The diner-style name suggests a casual, approachable eatery that could be a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists travelling through the western communities of Greater Victoria.

restaurant.name: Gateway to India
restaurant.desc: Gateway to India is an authentic Indian restaurant in Nanaimo serving dishes prepared with imported spices from both northern and southern India. The restaurant offers full dine-in service as well as takeout, with a menu spanning appetizers, curries, tandoor-baked breads, and desserts. Their spice blends and sauces are also sold at grocery stores across Vancouver Island and the Lower Mainland, reflecting the depth of their culinary operation.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Open for Take-Out & Dine-In' and 'Pre Order Available 4PM-9PM'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu has a dedicated 'VEGETARIAN OPTIONS' section with multiple dishes; Pappadum is explicitly described as 'GLUTEN FREE'

restaurant.name: Pokérrito
restaurant.desc: Pokérrito is a proudly Canadian fast-casual chain serving customizable poke bowls, sushi burritos, and warm bowls at its Marine Way Market location in Burnaby. Cyclists can build their own bowl choosing from a wide range of proteins, bases, and toppings, with many vegan and gluten-free options clearly marked on the menu. The location features indoor seating and air conditioning, making it a comfortable stop after a ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu subpages explicitly mark items with vegan (🌱) and gluten-free (GF) icons; options include tofu, avocado, fried tofu, citrus ponzu (vegan), and multiple GF sauces such as Creamy Mayo (GF), Wasabi Basil (GF), and Umami (GF)

restaurant.name: Saint Germain Bakery
restaurant.desc: Saint Germain Bakery is an award-winning chain founded in 1984 that has trained under pastry chefs from France, Japan, Hong Kong, and Australia, earning multiple Culinary Olympics gold medals. The Kerrisdale location is a standalone street-front shop in a quiet residential neighbourhood, offering cakes, pastries, and baked goods. It is part of a broad BC and Ontario chain, with wholesale supply to major hotels and airlines.

restaurant.name: Varsha Indian Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Varsha Indian Kitchen is a modern Indian restaurant on Government Street in downtown Victoria, billing itself as Victoria's finest Indian restaurant. The menu blends traditional tandoor cooking — fish, prawns, paneer tikka, seekh kebab — with Indo-Chinese fusion dishes and a strong vegetarian lineup. Catering is also available, and online ordering and takeout make it convenient for cyclists passing through the inner harbour area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a 'VEGETARIAN STARTERS' section and individual items marked 'V' throughout; no vegan or GF claims confirmed

restaurant.name: Tendon Kohaku
restaurant.desc: Tendon Kohaku is a downtown Vancouver outpost of an international Japanese tempura rice bowl (tendon) chain, born from a collaboration between Nadai Fujisoba — Japan's largest soba chain — and the Kings Know Group. The restaurant distinguishes itself with specially selected Hokkaido rice varieties, a proprietary vegetable-sesame oil blend, and a secret sauce slow-boiled for over 12 hours with more than 15 ingredients. The menu spans prawn, chicken, vegetable, eel, and sashimi tendon bowls alongside udon noodles, offering a hearty and distinctive meal stop in the heart of downtown Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists a dedicated 'Vegetable Tendon' bowl (kabocha pumpkin, seaweed, French bean, shiitake, enoki, yam, baby corn, rice, Kohaku Tendon Sauce)

restaurant.name: Cha House
restaurant.desc: Cha House is a bubble tea cafe located inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre, one of Kelowna's main retail hubs along Harvey Avenue. It specializes in milk tea, fruit tea, slushies, and a wide range of specialty drinks. For a touring cyclist, it offers a cool indoor respite from the Okanagan heat in a large, well-serviced mall environment.

restaurant.name: Speed's Pub
restaurant.desc: Speed's Neighbourhood Pub has been a Ladner fixture since 1995, recently renovated under new ownership with a refreshed ambiance and river views over the historic Mitchell Bay waterway. The pub's patio overlooks a moored WWII-era vessel that inspired its logo, lending a uniquely local character. The menu spans classic pub fare through elevated dishes, with craft beers, wines, and cocktails alongside a kids menu and daily specials.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Happy hour menu explicitly labels multiple items as Gluten free, Vegetarian, and Vegan (e.g., Chips & Pico, Beet & Arugula Salad, Brussels Sprouts)

restaurant.name: Saigon Subs
restaurant.desc: A Vietnamese sandwich restaurant on the Trans-Canada Highway in Duncan. The menu features Vietnamese-style subs and sandwiches. Situated along a primary transportation corridor for Vancouver Island travelers.

restaurant.name: Vina Vietnamese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Vina Vietnamese Restaurant is a sit-down Vietnamese restaurant on Marine Drive in West Vancouver, offering both indoor and outdoor seating. It sits along a busy cycling corridor on the north shore, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists exploring the area. The restaurant maintains a smoke-free environment.

restaurant.name: Newton Pizza
restaurant.desc: Newton Pizza is a local pizza chain with a White Rock/South Surrey location on King George Boulevard, offering 36 specialty pizzas across multiple crust styles and sauces, plus wings, sides, and salads. The air-conditioned dine-in space and online ordering make it a practical meal stop along the King George corridor. It is one of three Surrey-area locations operated by the same brand.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists whole wheat multigrain crust option and numerous vegetable-topped specialty pizzas

restaurant.name: Mongo Bongo
restaurant.desc: Mongo Bongo is a Mongolian grill in New Westminster where diners build their own stir-fry bowl by selecting proteins, noodles, fresh vegetables, and sauces before watching chefs cook it on a large grill. The interactive concept — taglined 'a self-inspired creation' — makes it a filling, customizable stop with both lunch and dinner seatings. A full bar including beer, wine, and signature martinis rounds out the menu for cyclists looking for a proper sit-down meal.

detail.address: 512 Sixth Avenue, New Westminster, BC V3L

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page states 'your choice of meat or vegetarian protein alternative,' confirming vegetarian options. No mention of vegan or GF

restaurant.name: Steamship Grill & Bar
restaurant.desc: Steamship Grill & Bar occupies the historic 1924 Heritage Steamship Terminal building on Victoria's inner harbour, designed by Francis Rattenbury in the Beaux-Arts style and now a landmark directly across from the BC Legislature. The restaurant specializes in fresh local seafood — halibut, salmon, oysters, mussels — paired with BC wines and Victoria craft beers, served on a heated and covered harborfront patio voted one of Canada's Top 100. It can accommodate groups from 10 to 200, making it a practical stop for cycling tour groups passing through downtown Victoria.

restaurant.name: B House
restaurant.desc: B House is an Asian fusion eatery on Vancouver's lively Commercial Drive, blending Eastern and Western culinary traditions across an all-day menu that spans brunch, lunch, dinner, and happy hour snacks. The restaurant emphasizes fresh local ingredients, contemporary presentation, and a guest-first philosophy, with reservations available and walk-ins welcome. Its location on one of Vancouver's most walkable and cyclist-friendly strips makes it a natural rest stop on a Commercial Drive touring route.

restaurant.name: Okanagan Estate Wine Shop
restaurant.desc: Okanagan Estate Wine Cellars is a Kitsilano neighbourhood wine shop devoted exclusively to British Columbia wines, sourced from regional winemakers and sold at winery prices with no obligations to hotels or restaurants. The 3669 West 4th Avenue location is one of two Vancouver stores and offers in-store wine flights and tastings alongside online ordering with in-store pickup. Staff are trained specifically in BC wine and food pairing, making it a useful stop for cyclists looking to bring home a bottle from their tour.

restaurant.name: Kita no Donburi
restaurant.desc: Kita no Donburi is a fast-food Japanese restaurant specializing in donburi rice bowls with seafood and sushi options. Located on Seymour Street in downtown Vancouver, it offers online ordering for quick, convenient meals. The restaurant provides indoor seating and wheelchair accessibility.

restaurant.name: Pot Empire
restaurant.desc: Pot Empire is a Chinese hotpot restaurant on Kingsway in Burnaby, offering the communal hot-pot dining style popular in Chinese cuisine. Located on a busy arterial road with transit and commercial amenities nearby, it sits along a corridor cycling tourists may pass through when travelling east-west across Burnaby. Hotpot restaurants typically offer a sit-down, customizable meal experience where diners cook ingredients in a simmering broth at the table.

restaurant.name: Ladurée
restaurant.desc: Ladurée is the iconic Parisian macaron brand operating a boutique and tea salon on downtown Vancouver's Robson Street shopping corridor. The space features Parisian-style tea rooms offering classic French dishes and an Afternoon Tea service, alongside a retail selection of macarons, pastries, jams, and specialty teas. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a scenic urban rest stop, though it is a specialty destination rather than a practical resupply point for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: The Dime
restaurant.desc: The Dime is a budget-friendly pub and late-night dining spot on Commercial Drive, one of 17 locations in the Warehouse Group chain that blends casual restaurant comfort with a bar and nightlife atmosphere. It sits in the heart of the eclectic 'Drive' neighbourhood, within easy cycling distance of Trout Lake, and the kitchen keeps turning out wings, burgers, and comfort food well into the night. The chain's value-oriented pricing and all-day service make it a practical stop for cyclists exploring East Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu previews include Black Bean Burger, Southwest Tortilla Ensalada (plant-based as listed), and General Tao Bowl (mixed vegetables)

restaurant.name: The Junction
restaurant.desc: The Junction is an LGBTQ-primary pub situated on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, the heart of the city's queer village. It operates as a full-service bar with a food menu, lounge drinks, and a regular events program including a guestlist system for special occasions. The venue is smoke-free, wheelchair accessible, and offers both indoor and outdoor seating.

restaurant.name: Grace of India
restaurant.desc: Grace of India is a small, intimate Indian restaurant on Kingsway in Vancouver, founded in 2018 and helmed by a chef with over 25 years of experience drawing inspiration from across the Indian subcontinent. The menu spans tandoori specialties, karahi dishes, lamb, seafood, and a range of vegetarian options, with rotating weekday specials. Online ordering with pickup, delivery, and dine-in is available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'we cater to all types of dietary requirements'; menu includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian Specialties' section and a vegetarian thali Wednesday special

restaurant.name: Mr. Greek Donair Shop
restaurant.desc: Mr. Greek Donair Shop is a Greek and donair restaurant located in a unit at 7155 Kingsway in the Burnaby area, a busy commercial corridor accessible by bike. It offers a quick-stop option for touring cyclists looking for a filling Mediterranean-style meal along the Kingsway route.

restaurant.name: Doe Coffee
restaurant.desc: Doe Coffee Roasters is a community-focused Vancouver café that small-batch roasts its own beans on-site and bakes all pastries fresh in-house overnight. The shop has removed tipping at checkout as a deliberate policy, and its Doe Pass subscription model reflects an unusually loyal neighbourhood following. A reviewer notes at least two locations — the original East Hastings spot and a newer Clarke Street outpost — suggesting growing local presence.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Green Goddess (Veg)' sandwich with avocado, Monterey Jack, cucumber, seasonal vegetable, mayo, ranch, mustard on house-made croissant

restaurant.name: Fatburger
restaurant.desc: Fatburger Nanaimo is a casual burger restaurant on Rutherford Road offering cooked-to-order burgers made with fresh, never-frozen Alberta Angus beef. A Canadian-owned franchise of the iconic chain founded in 1952, it offers a broad menu including plant-based burgers, chicken, milkshakes, and poutine. Takeout and delivery are available, making it a convenient fuelling stop for cyclists in the south Nanaimo area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists 'plant-based burgers' as a distinct menu category

restaurant.name: New Amsterdam Bakery
restaurant.desc: New Amsterdam Bakery is a family-run Surrey bakery with over 25 years of experience producing handmade specialty breads, custom cakes, and pastries with no chemicals or preservatives. The shop offers vegetarian (egg-free), vegan, sugar-free, and salt-free options alongside classics like cinnamon buns, danishes, and Black Forest cake. For a touring cyclist, it is a practical stop to pick up fresh bread or baked goods in a residential Surrey neighbourhood next to a TD Bank.

restaurant.name: 101 BoBA
restaurant.desc: 101 Canada Boba is a Metro Vancouver bubble tea chain founded in 2020, specializing in grab-and-go fruit teas, milk teas, and seasonal specialty drinks made with premium ingredients sourced predominantly from Taiwan. The Cambie Street location is one of six BC stores in a rapidly expanding Canadian brand built around a streamlined, fast-service model. Cyclists passing through the Cambie corridor will find a quick refreshment stop with indoor seating but a strictly beverage-focused menu.

restaurant.name: The Thirsty Vintner
restaurant.desc: The Thirsty Vintner is a winemaking kit shop that has operated at the same Shelbourne Street location in Victoria for over 25 years, offering customers the choice of making wine on-site with staff guidance or purchasing Winexpert kits to craft at home. The shop carries an extensive range spanning reds, whites, rosés, fruit wines, and oak-barrel aged varieties from wine regions around the world. Staff speak English, Cantonese, Mandarin, French, and Tagalog, making it an unusually welcoming stop for a diverse range of visitors.

restaurant.name: Casa de Nata Portuguese Custard Tarts
restaurant.desc: A Portuguese bakery specializing in nata (custard tarts). Business operational status and amenities are unclear from the 'Coming Soon' website.

restaurant.name: Gooi-Ga Korean BBQ
restaurant.desc: Gooi-Ga Korean BBQ is a Korean barbecue restaurant located in North Vancouver, offering the interactive tabletop grill experience typical of the genre. Korean BBQ restaurants are popular refuelling stops for touring cyclists seeking high-protein, communal meals with generous portions. The restaurant was verified as open in late December 2024 via OSM.

detail.address: Canada, British Columbia, Coquitlam, Glen Dr, unit 107

restaurant.name: The Captain's Boil
restaurant.desc: The Captain's Boil is a seafood boil franchise restaurant on Vancouver's busy Robson Street in the West End, serving fresh seafood feasts where diners choose their catch, flavour sauce, and heat level. The hands-on, bag-style dining format is designed for group feasting. The Robson Street location is wheelchair accessible and sits on a major pedestrian and cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Le Coq Frit
restaurant.desc: Le Coq Frit is a Korean-influenced fried chicken eatery with a North Vancouver outpost at Lonsdale Quay, serving hand-battered chicken in several styles—honey garlic soy, Nashville hot, sweet & spicy, and a double-fried 'real crispy' version—alongside chicken burgers on French brioche buns. The restaurant sources ingredients locally from Canadian farms and has committed to zero-waste, eco-friendly non-woven bag packaging. It is one of two Greater Vancouver locations, with menus available in multiple languages including Korean, French, and Chinese.

detail.address: 123 Carrie Cates Court Unit 134, North Vancouver, BC V7M 3K7

restaurant.name: Kam Tou Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kam Tou Seafood Restaurant serves authentic Chinese cuisine in Richmond's Sexsmith Road area, specializing in dim sum and seafood dishes such as steamed scallop dumplings and traditional dry-fried beef ho fun. The restaurant offers online ordering through its own website for those wanting takeout. It operates within a commercial unit, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through Richmond's busy Brighouse area.

detail.address: 779 Sexsmith Rd Unit 1298, Richmond, BC V6X 3Z9

restaurant.name: Chaiiwala of London - King George Hub
restaurant.desc: Chaiiwala of London is a South Asian-inspired chai cafe serving globally popular drinks like Karak Chaii and Pink Chaii alongside street food such as samosas, Aloo Paratha, and Butter Chicken Poutine. Located at King George Hub just one to two minutes' walk from the King George SkyTrain station, it's a convenient urban rest stop for cyclists connecting to the transit network. The cafe has outdoor seating, accepts cash and cards, and is wheelchair accessible.

detail.address: 9908 King George Blvd unit 15, Surrey, BC V3T 0A8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Owner post lists multiple vegetarian items: Aloo Paratha, Masala Fries, Karak Chaii, Pink Chaii, Falooda Milkshake (Rose or Mango)

restaurant.name: Sushi Mori
restaurant.desc: Sushi Mori has been a Coquitlam institution since 2008, serving Japanese fusion cuisine that blends fresh local ingredients with traditional techniques across an extensive menu of rolls, sashimi, and specialty dishes. The restaurant is known for its warm vintage interior with cozy booths, cherry blossom décor, and attentive service. It sits along the Barnet Highway corridor, making it a solid stop for cyclists travelling through Port Moody and Coquitlam.

restaurant.name: Panago
restaurant.desc: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain with a location in Chilliwack, notable for its commitment to quality ingredients: dough made fresh in-house from 100% Canadian wheat, organic tomato sauce, and meats raised without antibiotics. The menu spans pizzas, salads, sides, dips, and beverages, with a strong emphasis on plant-based and meat-free choices. Touring cyclists can call ahead or order online for pickup.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We've got abundant veggie, dairy-free and meat-free choices to help you live your best plant life.'

restaurant.name: Old Yale Brewing Co.
restaurant.desc: Old Yale Brewing Co. is an award-winning craft brewery and kitchen that has been brewing since 1999, now running three taprooms across BC and Alberta. The Abbotsford location pours 15+ craft beers on tap and serves a full Campfire Kitchen menu in a family- and dog-friendly space with outdoor patio seating. Touring cyclists will find a well-rounded stop with a broad food and drink menu, including non-alcoholic options, in a comfortable sit-down setting.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website FAQ: 'Our menu includes some very yummy vegetarian and vegan-friendly items' and 'Our menu features some delicious gluten-friendly menu items and beverages'
notes.Wi-Fi: Not explicitly mentioned in website content

restaurant.name: Sturdies Bay Cafe and Bakery
restaurant.desc: A cafe and bakery on Galiano Island serving coffee and baked goods to visitors. Listed in the local dining directory as a community gathering spot. Offers casual refreshments to touring cyclists exploring the island.

restaurant.name: Beaucoup Bakery & Cafe
restaurant.desc: Beaucoup Bakery & Café is an award-winning French pastry destination in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, celebrated for delicate viennoiseries and East-West fusion creations such as the Peking Duck Croissant and Golden Mochi Croissant. Opened in 2012 and now co-owned by pastry chef Betty Hung and her brother Jacky, it has earned recognition from Lonely Planet, Forbes Travel Guide, and USA Today. Cyclists stopping here can expect espresso-based beverages, savoury seasonal sandwiches, and a rotating menu of baked goods.

restaurant.name: Meat & Bread
restaurant.desc: Meat & Bread is a well-established Vancouver sandwich chain with multiple locations, known for its house-roasted porchetta and craft sandwiches served on artisan bread. The Robson Street outpost sits in the heart of downtown Vancouver and offers breakfast sandwiches in the morning alongside a full lunch lineup. Cyclists passing through the city centre will find a compact, efficient spot for a hearty midday meal with online pickup ordering available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian options confirmed: 'Two Egg Veg' breakfast sandwich and 'Grilled Cheese' on menu. No GF options mentioned

restaurant.name: Chipotle
restaurant.desc: Chipotle Mexican Grill is a fast-casual chain located near Douglas and Fort Streets in downtown Victoria, offering customizable burritos, bowls, quesadillas, tacos, and salads. The chain emphasizes its 'Food with Integrity' sourcing philosophy, using only 53 real ingredients from farms adhering to humane and sustainable practices. It's a reliable downtown stop for a quick, filling meal with in-store pickup and delivery options.

restaurant.name: Momo Chen Cakes
restaurant.desc: Momo Chen Cakes is a custom cake design studio specializing in elaborate wedding cakes, celebration cakes, and sweet treats such as cupcakes, cookies, cake pops, and macarons. The studio operates primarily on a consultation-and-order model, with an online shop offering a wide range of pre-designed cake options. It delivers to the Greater Vancouver area, making it a potential stop for cyclists seeking a sweet treat or special-order cake in the Richmond area.

restaurant.name: Cilantro Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Cilantro Indian Cuisine is a full-service Indian restaurant on West Broadway serving a broad menu of North and South Indian dishes alongside Indo-Chinese fusion items, with freshly ground spices and house-made chutneys. The kitchen has over 20 years of experience spanning India, Malaysia, the UK, and North America, and the Vancouver location is a second outpost of an original White Rock restaurant. Touring cyclists will find a wide range of dietary accommodations including vegan, gluten-free, and Jain dishes, plus online ordering for convenient takeout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states: 'we offer a variety of vegan and gluten free options' and 'we offer a variety of Jain dishes.' Menu includes many vegetarian and vegan items

restaurant.name: Cheese Slap
restaurant.desc: Cheese Slap is a Halal fusion restaurant on Vancouver's Granville Strip blending North American comfort food with South Asian flavors through dishes like Tandoori Chicken Cheesesteak, Butter Chicken Pizza, and Double Slap Smash Burgers. Set in a modern, renovated space at the heart of the downtown entertainment district, it caters to both lunchtime and late-night crowds. Free pickup ordering via the ZOMI platform makes it a practical and flavorful stop for cyclists passing through downtown Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian pizzas (Margherita, Cheese, Pesto Margarita, Vegetarian, Spicy Supreme Veggie)

restaurant.name: Big Way Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Big Way Hot Pot is a growing BC-based chain offering a self-serve individual hot pot experience with over 100 fresh ingredients and more than 18 broths and dry mixes. The Kerrisdale location sits on West 41st Avenue and is part of a network that spans Metro Vancouver and beyond. Diners cook their own selection of premium meats, seafood, and vegetables in flavourful broths ranging from Signature Mala to vegan-friendly Tomato.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu page explicitly states 'Vegan Option Available' for the Tomato Broth

restaurant.name: Pür & Simple
restaurant.desc: Pür & Simple is a Canadian breakfast and brunch franchise with over 65 locations nationwide, with this Burnaby outpost anchored inside Station Square Metro Town. The restaurant specialises in creative comfort-food twists on classics — think Eggs Benedict, French toast, pancakes, and crepes — served in an upscale indoor setting with dedicated vegan and vegetarian menu sections. Cyclists coming off the Burnaby routes can order online for takeout or join a same-day waitlist on weekends.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu pages label items 'V' (vegetarian) and 'Vg' (vegan) and include a 'gluten sentitive' filter category

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: McDonald's on Ladner Trunk Road is a fast food restaurant in Tsawwassen offering burgers, breakfast, McCafé coffee, and snacks with a drive-through and outdoor patio seating. OSM records it as open 24/7, making it a reliable any-hour stop for touring cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen area. An on-site PlayPlace adds to its appeal as a rest and refuel point for families on tour.

restaurant.name: Obanhmi
restaurant.desc: Obanhmi is a BC-based Vietnamese street food chain specializing in bánh mì sandwiches, fresh rolls, and iced coffee, now operating 9 locations across Metro Vancouver. The menu ranges from French-influenced cold cuts to fully vegan and halal options, all built on house-made ingredients and freshly baked baguettes. Cyclists passing through the West Broadway corridor can place an online order for fast in-store pickup.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'options for vegetarians, vegans, and halal diets'; menu lists a dedicated VEGETARIAN / VEGAN bánh mì (tofu, avocado, secret-recipe filling) with explicit vegan option by omitting house mayo. No gluten-free mention found

restaurant.name: Mykonos Pizza and Spaghetti House
