restaurant.desc: Mykonos Pizza and Spaghetti House is a sit-down restaurant in Penticton, BC, offering pizza and pasta in a retail-building setting. It sits near the heart of Penticton, a popular hub on the Kettle Valley Rail Trail and Okanagan cycling routes, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through town.

detail.address: 329 Main St, Penticton, BC V2A 5B7, Canada

restaurant.name: Rivers Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Rivers Restaurant is a casual diner in Chilliwack. It provides a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking for a sit-down meal. Limited details about specific amenities are currently available due to website access limitations.

detail.address: 42239 Yarrow Central Rd, Chilliwack, BC V2R 5E3, Canada

restaurant.name: Dining Room Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Dining Room Restaurant is set inside the historic Butchart family residence at The Butchart Gardens, one of Vancouver Island's most celebrated horticultural destinations. It serves a seasonally inspired Afternoon Tea and summer dinners using locally sourced ingredients, with menus that include gluten-free, vegetarian, and vegan options. Cyclists should be aware that paid admission to The Butchart Gardens is required to access the restaurant.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We offer a variety of dietary teas including Gluten Free, Dairy Sensitive, Vegetarian, and Vegan. We are able to accommodate these requests with 24 hours' notice.'

restaurant.name: Breka Bakery & Café
restaurant.desc: Breka Bakery & Café is a Vancouver-born, local family bakery operating continuously since 2006 across 8 locations, including this East Hastings outpost. It is one of the rare cafes open around the clock every day of the year, making it a reliable stop for cyclists at any hour. The menu spans artisan breads, pastries, sandwiches, soups, cakes, and hot beverages, with dedicated gluten-free and vegan selections.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website has dedicated 'VEGAN' and 'GLUTEN-FREE' (labelled 'Gluten Friendly') menu sections with multiple named items including vegan wraps, chia puddings, granola cookies, and gluten-free mousse cakes

restaurant.name: Prado Cafe
restaurant.desc: Prado Coffee is a Vancouver-born specialty coffee roaster that grew from a single bar into a multi-neighbourhood chain, with its Commercial Drive location anchoring the brand on one of the city's most cycling-friendly streets. Founded by Sammy with a stated goal of making great coffee and making people feel welcome, the company now roasts its own beans and ships subscriptions across the region. Cyclists riding the Drive will find a familiar neighbourhood café atmosphere at a location well-placed for an East Side route.

restaurant.name: Esquimalt Roasting Company
restaurant.desc: Esquimalt Roasting Company is a small-batch specialty coffee roastery that roasts its beans on-site in the Esquimalt neighbourhood of Victoria, British Columbia. The ERC Gateway café at 854 Esquimalt Road is one of two physical locations where customers can enjoy freshly roasted single-origin and blended coffees. Beans are also available for online purchase with delivery across BC and Canada, reflecting the roastery's community-focused, locally rooted ethos.

restaurant.name: The Cambie
restaurant.desc: The Cambie is one of Vancouver's oldest continuously operating bars, established in 1897 in the aftermath of the Great Vancouver Fire and a fixture in downtown Vancouver ever since. The venue runs as a full bar and grill with a patio, regular live music nights, karaoke, and a wide rotating selection of BC craft beer on tap. An associated Cambie Hostel operates on the same property, making it a natural waypoint for budget-conscious touring cyclists passing through the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu pages display VG (vegetarian), V (vegan), and GF (gluten-free) dietary filter labels, indicating the menu categorizes items by these dietary needs

restaurant.name: Banchan Korean Bistro 반찬
restaurant.desc: Banchan Korean Bistro is a Korean restaurant in the Willoughby Town Centre mall in Langley, specializing in Korean, Korean Fried Chicken, and Asian cuisine. The restaurant operates primarily as a takeout destination with online ordering and real-time pickup notifications. It is a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Willoughby commercial corridor.

detail.address: 20689 Willoughby Town Centre Dr A160, Langley, BC V2Y 0X7

restaurant.name: Ong Ba Vietnamese Eatery
restaurant.desc: Vietnamese restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End specializing in vegan and vegetarian dishes. Features both indoor and outdoor seating. A convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking quality Vietnamese food with dietary flexibility.

restaurant.name: Butter Lane Bake Shop
restaurant.desc: Butter Lane Bake Shop is a North Vancouver bakery founded in 2014 and specializing in custom cakes for weddings, birthdays, and celebrations, alongside savoury catering and dessert bars. The shop operates from two locations: a dedicated bakery at 175 W 3rd St and a stall inside the Lonsdale Quay Market. Cyclists passing through the Lonsdale area or the Lower Lonsdale neighbourhood can stop in for freshly baked pastries and sweets.

restaurant.name: Hoxton Gastown
restaurant.desc: Hoxton Gastown is a comedy-focused bar and restaurant in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, offering a chef-driven food menu alongside stand-up shows, weekly trivia nights, and a full bar. The venue doubles as a rentable creative space for film shoots, music videos, private parties, and brand activations. A touring cyclist stopping in Gastown would find a lively, food-forward spot with a distinct comedy-club atmosphere.

restaurant.name: Shawarma 2 Go Grill
restaurant.desc: Shawarma 2 Go Grill is an authentic Mediterranean fast-food restaurant in Richmond's Brighouse neighbourhood with over 30 years of shawarma expertise. The menu spans classic chicken and beef shawarma wraps, made-to-order falafels, lamb shank plates, and fusion items like shawarma poutine. It is one of two Richmond locations and offers online ordering with free in-store pickup.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Order online & pick up No fees at 100-6020 No 3 Road Location'; no drive-through
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a 'Veggie Lover' plate (falafels and dolmades with hummus, tabouli, garden salad, and pita) and a Made-to-order Falafels wrap; no vegan or GF claims confirmed

restaurant.name: Crust Bakery
restaurant.desc: Crust Bakery is an award-winning, female-owned French-inspired bakery and pastry shop that has been a downtown Victoria institution since 2013. Made-from-scratch breads, tarts, pastries, savoury snacks, and fresh Caffe Umbria espresso draw long lines of locals and visitors alike. A second location also operates at the Uptown Mall; the Fort Street shop is the original and sits within easy reach of Victoria's inner harbour cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Flourist
restaurant.desc: Flourist is a bakery located on Commercial Street in Vancouver's vibrant Commercial Drive neighbourhood, a corridor well-known to local cyclists. The shop offers both indoor and outdoor seating and is wheelchair accessible.

restaurant.name: Mr Mikes
restaurant.desc: Mr Mikes is a steakhouse and part of an established Canadian casual dining chain. Located in Merritt, it provides a straightforward option for touring cyclists to stop for a meal.

restaurant.name: Mount Pleasant Vintage and Provisions
restaurant.desc: Mount Pleasant Vintage & Provisions is a cocktail bar and Argentinian-style wood-fired grill tucked into Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, described on its own site as 'an unassuming cocktail bar disguised as a postmodern thrift shop.' The bar runs an ever-rotating cocktail list with an emphasis on forward-thinking techniques alongside elevated classic bar food cooked over wood and charcoal. It has earned recognition from The Pinnacle Guide (one pin, 'Excellent') and hosted the North America's 50 Best 2025 gala, signalling a destination-worthy stop for cyclists wanting a full sit-down meal and craft drinks.

restaurant.name: Home Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Home Restaurant is a long-established homestyle diner on the Lougheed Highway in Maple Ridge's West Central neighbourhood, part of a small BC chain with four locations. It has served the community for over 20 years, with a menu centred on all-day breakfast, comfort classics, and house-made pies. Pickup and third-party delivery are both available, making it a flexible stop for cyclists on the Lougheed corridor.

detail.address: 21667 Lougheed Hwy, Maple Ridge, BC V2X 2S2

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: A Starbucks coffee shop location on Douglas Street in Victoria offering drive-through and takeaway service. Convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking quick beverages and snacks.

restaurant.name: Rocky Point Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Rocky Point Ice Cream is a family-owned artisan ice cream brand that started as a seasonal scoop shack at Rocky Point Park in 1997 and now operates four Lower Mainland storefronts, including this one set within Coquitlam's Town Centre Park. All ice cream is made from scratch in BC's first licensed dairy plant dedicated exclusively to craft production, and the Coquitlam outpost offers outdoor seating in a park environment that suits a mid-ride stop well. The menu regularly features plant-based and lactose-free options alongside rotating seasonal flavours.

detail.address: Trevor Wingrove Way, Coquitlam, BC V3B 7S4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website front page explicitly lists plant-based options including 'Plant-Based Blackberry Crumble: Plant-based coconut vanilla ice cream'; /about page notes '3 plant-based/sorbet options' on trucks

restaurant.name: Bernies
restaurant.desc: Bernie's is a supper club and cinema experience on Kelowna's main downtown strip, pairing a full-service restaurant with an in-house movie theatre. The menu leans heavily on Okanagan-region ingredients and a dedicated raw bar featuring oysters, seafood towers, and caviar. Touring cyclists looking for an upscale downtown Kelowna dinner stop will find local craft beers, creative cocktails, and a distinctive dine-in-film atmosphere.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ page states: 'Our menu has a variety of gluten free, vegetarian, and vegan options and our kitchen team does the best they can to accommodate to any dietary restrictions or allergies.'

restaurant.name: Moo-Lix Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Moo-Lix Ice Cream is a local ice cream destination on Kelowna's main downtown commercial strip, Bernard Avenue. Situated in the heart of the city's walkable core, it offers a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring the Okanagan. The late evening hours make it a popular warm-weather treat stop after a day on the trail.

restaurant.name: Grand Chinese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Grand Chinese Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant on Lougheed Highway in Burnaby, one of two locations operated by the same brand. The menu centres on Sichuan cuisine, Northern Chinese-style dim sum, Shanghai-style xiao long bao made fresh daily, and handcrafted Lanzhou noodles. The restaurant also caters private group events for parties of 10 to 200.

restaurant.name: Red Rose Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A Greek restaurant in Surrey offering dine-in, takeout, and delivery service, with online ordering available. Catering services are offered for events of any size.

restaurant.name: The Bubble Tea Shop
restaurant.desc: The Bubble Tea Shop is a local café specializing in freshly made bubble teas, with a Vancouver location in the cycling-adjacent Olympic Village neighbourhood and a second location in Richmond. Beyond in-store drinks, the shop sells DIY bubble tea kits, loose-leaf teas, syrups, and toppings for home brewing. The Olympic Village location sits near the seawall cycling corridor, making it a plausible refreshment stop for cyclists on popular Vancouver routes.

restaurant.name: Jimmy's Lunch Box
restaurant.desc: Jimmy's Lunch Box is a brunch cafe in Port Coquitlam offering online ordering and breakfast and brunch service. It provides a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking a substantial meal without a long wait.

detail.address: 2652 Shaughnessy St, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 3G8

restaurant.name: Trees Organic Coffee
restaurant.desc: Trees Organic Coffee is a Vancouver cafe chain founded in 1996, celebrated for small-batch organic coffee roasting and award-winning homemade New York-style cheesecakes. The Joyce-Collingwood location is one of 13–14 stores across Greater Vancouver, offering a full menu of sandwiches, baked goods, teas, and cold drinks alongside the signature cheesecake. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website highlights natural/organic ingredients and a menu inclusive of vegetarian items

restaurant.name: Gary's
restaurant.desc: Gary's is a small, farm-to-table dinner restaurant in Vancouver's Fairview neighbourhood, sourcing from over a dozen named BC farms and producers including suppliers from the Fraser Valley, Bowen Island, and the Gulf Islands. The intimate space seats up to 26 at a long communal table or 36 standing, making it well-suited for a group meal at the end of a day's ride. Walk-ins are welcome, though space is limited on busy evenings.

restaurant.name: Autostrada Oyster Bar and Grill
restaurant.desc: Autostrada Oyster Bar and Grill is a seafood-forward restaurant perched in the small coastal community of Britannia Beach along the Sea-to-Sky corridor, operated by the same hospitality group behind a Vancouver Italian osteria. The menu leans into local Pacific ingredients — fresh-shucked oysters, BC albacore tuna, Salt Spring mussels, sockeye salmon — alongside pastas, burgers, and Italian-inspired starters. For a touring cyclist riding between Vancouver and Squamish, it is one of the few full-service dining options in this stretch of highway.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes: Rigatoni Alla Norma (eggplant, tomato, chili, garlic), Forager burger (wild mushrooms, caramelized onion, pecorino), Bucatini Cacio e Pepe (pepper, pecorino), and Seasonal Greens Salad

restaurant.name: Hot House Pizza
restaurant.desc: Hot House Pizza is a pizza restaurant in Victoria's Cook Street Village offering a broad menu of specialty, chicken, veggie, and classic pizzas alongside calzones, wings, and beverages. Multiple crust options are available including original, gourmet thin, whole wheat thin, and gluten free. It's a filling and convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through one of Victoria's busiest neighbourhood commercial strips.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists a dedicated 'Veggie Pizzas' menu category and offers 'Gluten Free Crust' as a crust option (medium size only)

restaurant.name: Tasty Indian Bistro
restaurant.desc: Tasty Indian Bistro is a contemporary Indian restaurant in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, one of three Lower Mainland locations alongside Delta and Abbotsford. The menu blends traditional subcontinental dishes—tandoori, curries, biryanis—with inventive fusion plates like Blue Cheese Naan and Tasty Bao Buns, plus a full cocktail bar. The Yaletown location offers a lounge, patio, private dining, and delivery, making it a versatile stop in a walkable, transit-friendly urban corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu dietary filters include Vegetarian, Dairy-Free, Gluten-Free, and Nut-Free; numerous vegetarian and GF items are flagged throughout the Yaletown menu

restaurant.name: 4 Mile Restaurant & Brewpub
restaurant.desc: The 4 Mile Restaurant & Brewpub is a full-service pub and craft brewery located in View Royal on the Island Highway, one of Victoria's main cycling corridors. The venue houses a restaurant, an in-house brewery with a rotating lineup of craft beers, a sports bar called 4 Below, and a High Tea service — an unusually broad range for a single stop. Online ordering is available, and weekend brunch is offered, making it a viable option for cyclists at multiple points in the day.

restaurant.name: The American
restaurant.desc: The American is a bar on Main Street in central Vancouver. It offers a rest stop for food and drink during cycling tours through the city.

restaurant.name: Camy's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Camy's Pizza has operated in Surrey since 1985 and claims to be the originator of the butter chicken pizza. Located in Townline Plaza (Cedar Hill), it offers an unusually broad menu spanning specialty pizzas, Indian cuisine, Greek dishes, pasta, calzones, and wings, all made to order. Both pickup and delivery are available, making it a practical food stop for cyclists passing through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website mentions 'Vegetarian pizza and more' and menu lists Vegetarian Pizza, Veggie Garlic Pizza, and Vegetarian Mediterranean Pizza among house specialties

restaurant.name: Fiamo Pizza & Wine Bar
restaurant.desc: Fiamo is an Italian kitchen, pizza, and wine bar in downtown Victoria occupying a warm, European-bistro-style space with exposed brick walls adorned with authentic Italian racing bikes and a centrepiece chandelier. The menu leans traditional Italian with Mediterranean, French, and Spanish influences, featuring wood-fired pizzas, house-made pasta, and a broad international wine list. A heated patio, a mezzanine for private gatherings of up to 18, and a late-night pizza service make it a versatile stop on the Yates Street corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian items: Verdure pizza (rapini, roasted red peppers, red onion, mozzarella, pesto), Margherita pizza, Caprese salad, Brussels Sprouts, and Barbabietole salad. No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Mr. Mike's
restaurant.desc: Mr. Mike's is a Canadian casual steakhouse franchise with roots going back to 1960, serving premium steaks, burgers, pastas, salads, and shareable appetizers in a relaxed, unpretentious setting. The Fort St. John location sits on Alaska Road North along the Alaska Highway corridor, a natural waypoint for cyclists travelling through northeastern BC. The restaurant welcomes walk-ins and also offers takeout and delivery.

detail.address: 9324 Alaska Road North, Fort St. John, V1J 6L5

restaurant.name: Picnic
restaurant.desc: Picnic K-Street Food is a compact Korean street food counter on the second floor of a New Westminster building, specialising in kimbap rolls, bibimbap, deopbap (rice bowl) dishes, and ddeokbokki. The menu is tightly focused on traditional Korean staples with both meat and tofu-based options, and online ordering enables quick pickup. Recent reviews consistently praise the food quality and the friendly owner.

detail.address: 800 Carnarvon St #372, New Westminster, BC V3M 0G3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Marinated Tofu Bibimbap and Marinated Tofu Deopbap as vegetarian options

restaurant.name: Hitoe Sushi Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Hitoe Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant situated on West 4th Avenue in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, a well-travelled cycling corridor connecting downtown to the city's western districts. The restaurant distinguishes itself with an explicit gluten-free focus, prominently featured across its web presence. Touring cyclists passing through Kitsilano will find it a compact dining option on a route that sees heavy bicycle traffic year-round.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website blog title explicitly reads 'HITOE SUSHI Gluten Free OFFICIAL ( Business hours, Gluten Free )' — gluten-free options are a stated feature of the restaurant

restaurant.name: Papi's Seafood and Oyster Bar
restaurant.desc: Papi's Seafood and Oyster Bar is a casual seafood restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, situated steps from the English Bay Seawall with a heated outdoor patio offering panoramic water views. The interior draws on Greek mythology, anchored by a full-wall mural of the sea goddess Amphitrite painted by local artists Arden Marow Ross and Peter Ricq. Part of the award-winning Viaggio Hospitality group, the restaurant focuses on fresh Pacific Northwest catches paired with sea-inspired cocktails.

restaurant.name: Tulip Donair
restaurant.desc: Tulip Donair is a Mediterranean and pizza restaurant in Chilliwack specializing in donairs — lamb, beef, chicken, and vegetarian falafel — alongside pizzas, salads, and poutines. The restaurant operates a streamlined online pickup ordering system, making it a practical quick-stop option for cyclists moving through the area. A kids' menu and a range of vegetarian items round out the offering for mixed groups.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Vegetarian Falafel Donair, Vegetarian Falafel Donair Salad, Vegetarian Falafel Donair Platter, Four Seasons Veggie Pizza, and Spinach Feta Pizza; menu legend includes a vegetarian marker. No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Casereccio Foods
restaurant.desc: Casereccio Foods is a restaurant located on Vine Street in Vancouver. As a food establishment in an urban area, it offers a dining option for cycling tourists passing through the neighborhood.

restaurant.name: Romeo's
restaurant.desc: Romeo's is a multi-location Vancouver Island pizza and Italian restaurant chain that has operated in this Westshore Town Centre location since 1982. The Langford restaurant offers dine-in with a patio, plus delivery and takeout across a broad menu of pizzas, pastas, burgers, and mains. It is part of a four-location family operation serving Vancouver Island since 1974, making it a reliable and familiar stop for cyclists riding through the Westshore corridor.

restaurant.name: Sushi Mura
restaurant.desc: Sushi Mura is a Japanese sushi chain that has operated in Vancouver since 2012, with the Main Street location one of several across the Lower Mainland. The restaurant emphasises daily-delivered fresh fish and a broad menu spanning rolls, sashimi, nigiri, noodle bowls, and hot appetisers. Dine-in, takeout, and third-party delivery are all offered, making it a convenient stop on a busy urban cycling corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes vegetarian-suitable items: Veggie Wakame (seaweed salad), Agedashi Tofu, Vegetable Sunomono, and Green Salad; note some 'Veggie'-labelled items contain seafood

restaurant.name: Focacciaza
restaurant.desc: Focacciaza is Vancouver's only focacceria on wheels, run by 'Focaccia Joe' — a Red Seal chef who studied sustainable food development and draws on Italian heritage to serve pizza al taglio (Roman-style focaccia) cut to order. The all-electric cart runs on zero emissions and is solar-panel assisted, using biodegradable paper-sleeve packaging throughout. Cyclists will appreciate the quick street-food format and the eco-conscious ethos of this one-of-a-kind mobile vendor.

restaurant.name: Scratch Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Scratch Kitchen is a North Shore artisan pizza restaurant that started in Deep Cove in 2018 and expanded to Central Lonsdale in 2024; this record covers the Lonsdale location. Everything is made from scratch using fresh, locally sourced ingredients, with artisan pizzas, sharing plates, and salads paired alongside local craft beer and BC wine. The kitchen caters broadly to dietary needs, with gluten-free, dairy-free, and fully plant-based options available across the menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu marks items GF (gluten-free) and DF (dairy-free); all pizzas can be made gluten-free; vegan cashew mozza substitute available; website states 'We also cater to plant lovers and have lots of flavourful options available.'

restaurant.name: Sweethoney Dessert
restaurant.desc: Sweethoney Dessert is a Hong Kong dessert chain with a Burnaby franchise offering handcrafted traditional desserts made fresh in-store, including mango pomelo sago, tofu pudding, and housemade grass jelly. The chain was founded to bring authentic Hong Kong dessert culture to North America using premium, natural ingredients. It is one of several BC locations and markets itself as a relaxed gathering spot.

restaurant.name: Goodside Pastry House
restaurant.desc: GoodSide Pastry House is a Victoria neighbourhood pastry shop founded in 2020 by pastry chefs Haley Landa and Curtis Helm, each with over a decade of professional kitchen experience. The shop specializes in Euro-style cakes, croissants, and pastries crafted with traditional French techniques and West Coast-inspired flavours and ingredients. A rotating monthly menu and pre-order custom cakes make it a distinctive artisan food stop on Fort Street.

restaurant.name: White Spot
restaurant.desc: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, operating since 1928 and known for its classic burgers made with fresh Canadian beef and locally sourced ingredients. This Surrey location is a full-service family restaurant offering breakfast, lunch, and dinner in a sit-down setting. Touring cyclists will find a familiar, accessible stop with takeout options available.

restaurant.name: Street Hawker
restaurant.desc: Street Hawker is a halal-certified smashed burger and fried chicken fast-food joint in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, known for creative fusion riffs like Filipino adobo chicken sandos, kimchi burgers, and palabok poutine. All beef is 100% Canadian and chicken is hormone-free farm-fed, with an explicit commitment to plant-based options. Online ordering and pickup are available, making it a quick and filling stop for cyclists passing through the Main Street corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists 'vegan options' in header and states 'veggie warriors - we've got you covered with some seriously rad plant-based options.'

restaurant.name: Blenz Coffee
restaurant.desc: Blenz Coffee is a BC-born specialty coffee chain founded in Vancouver in 1992, now operating locally owned and franchised cafés across Canada. The menu spans handcrafted espresso drinks, nitro coffee and tea, whole-leaf organic teas, protein shakes, and a broad food selection including croissants, sandwiches, samosas, and baked goods. A touring cyclist stopping in can expect a community-focused café atmosphere with a diverse range of beverages and snacks.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website food menu includes explicit dietary preference filters for 'vegan' and 'gluten free', and lists dairy-free Dacaron™ items

restaurant.name: New Lakeview Restaurant
restaurant.desc: New Lakeview Restaurant is a Chinese dining establishment in North Vancouver with indoor seating and a no-smoking environment. Website access is currently unavailable, preventing verification of additional details about services and amenities.

restaurant.name: Lala Ji's Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Lala Ji's Pizzeria is a family-run Indian-pizza fusion restaurant in downtown Penticton, owned and operated by a father-and-son chef team with decades of combined experience in Germany, India, and Canada. The kitchen specializes in authentic Indian-style pizzas alongside traditional Indian dishes, making it a genuinely distinctive stop on the Okanagan touring circuit. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery are all available, and the online ordering system supports scheduled pickup.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes dedicated vegetarian/vegan items (Veggie Garden pizza, Veggie Mediterranean pizza, Veggie Samosa marked 'Vegetarian Vegan'). Website front page banner explicitly states 'GLUTAN FREE & DAIRY FREE' as a menu feature

restaurant.name: Awesome Bagel & More
restaurant.desc: Awesome Bagel & More is a downtown Vancouver café located steps from Canada Place, serving handcrafted bagels baked fresh daily, gourmet sandwiches, artisan pastries, Italian-style gelato, and espresso drinks. It positions itself as a gathering spot for locals, tourists, and professionals and operates with indoor seating only. The online menu spans over 57 items across categories including breakfast bagels, paninis, soups, and a full espresso bar.

restaurant.name: The Heatley
restaurant.desc: The Heatley is a community pub on East Hastings Street in East Vancouver, self-described as the neighbourhood homebase since 2015 and known for an inclusive, diversity-celebrating atmosphere. It hosts a regular live events calendar and has earned press coverage from The Daily Hive and The Globe and Mail. The pub serves a casual shareable-food menu alongside a full bar, making it a solid stop for a post-ride pint in a genuinely local venue.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels multiple items V (vegetarian), GF (gluten-free), and vegan — e.g. Heatley House Salad (V & GF), Kale Caesar with vegan caesar dressing, Heatley Burger with vegan Impossible Burger option, Veggie Chilli (V & GF)

restaurant.name: Tandoori Fusion
restaurant.desc: Tandoori Fusion is an Indian cuisine restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver. As a full-service restaurant, it offers meal service to customers and would provide a dining and rest stop for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Little Caesars
restaurant.desc: Little Caesars is a national pizza chain franchise offering carryout and delivery pizza at this Burnaby location. The store operates on a takeout-only model with no indoor or outdoor seating, making it a quick-stop option for cyclists needing a hot, filling meal without lingering. The menu includes pizzas, Crazy Bread, and wings, with vegetarian options available.

notes.Takeout: Website prominently offers 'Pickup' and 'Delivery' as the only ordering modes with no dine-in option
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes customizable pizzas which would support vegetarian configurations

restaurant.name: Woking Dragon China Bistro
restaurant.desc: Woking Dragon is a family-owned Chinese restaurant operating since 2003, known for western-style Chinese cuisine with a modern twist on tradition. The brand has been voted favourite Chinese food in Coquitlam and offers online ordering across its locations. Touring cyclists would find familiar comfort-food options with some vegan and gluten-free adaptations available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Some menu items are able to be made Vegan & Gluten-Free.'

restaurant.name: Popeyes
restaurant.desc: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen is a large international fast food chain known for its Southern-style fried chicken, located on 96 Avenue in Langley. The location offers both dine-in and drive-through service, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area. It sits in a commercial corridor with easy road access.

restaurant.name: The Crabapple Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Crabapple Cafe is a popular all-day breakfast and brunch spot in Brackendale, a community within Squamish, well-positioned on the corridor between Vancouver and Whistler. Formerly known as the Red Bench, it draws a loyal crowd with creative West Coast dishes like a Cajun BBQ Salmon Hash made with wild barbecued salmon and house-made hollandaise. A heated patio and a warm local atmosphere make it a comfortable stop year-round.

restaurant.name: Domino's
restaurant.desc: Domino's Pizza is a national pizza chain franchise located in a unit at 19265 Airport Way in Pitt Meadows, offering delivery and carryout orders. The location serves the Pitt Meadows area and is one of the few late-night food options along this corridor. Touring cyclists can grab a hot meal to go without needing to sit down.

restaurant.name: The Modern Pantry
restaurant.desc: The Modern Pantry is a bakery, cafe, and retail shop in Ambleside, West Vancouver, known for seasonally inspired pastries, organic sourdough breads, and made-from-scratch soups and sandwiches. The space doubles as an event venue and stocks a freezer of freshly prepared take-home meals alongside artisan retail goods. Owner Kendall Parslow brings an international food background — including a Masters in Food Culture and time at Borough Market in London — to this locally beloved North Shore spot.

detail.address: 102 - 2232 Marine Drive, West Vancouver, BC V7V 1K4

restaurant.name: Noodlebox
restaurant.desc: Noodlebox is a Canadian fast-casual chain specializing in wok-fired noodle and rice bowls inspired by Asian cuisines — from Pad Thai and Kung Pao to Butter Chicken and Cambodian Jungle Curry. This Port Place location in Nanaimo lets cyclists fuel up with a customizable hot meal made fresh to order. The chain's broad menu and quick-service format make it a practical stop for touring cyclists moving through downtown Nanaimo.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Can be made VEGAN Please ask when ordering' and 'Can be made GLUTEN-FRIENDLY Please ask when ordering' across the menu

restaurant.name: Dolly's Fish Market Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Dolly's Fish Market Restaurant is a licensed seafood restaurant and working fish market on the waterfront Cow Bay strip in Prince Rupert, one of the northernmost communities on BC's coast. It is part of a multi-location Northern BC operation that combines a sit-down restaurant with fresh seafood retail, custom and commercial fish processing, and wholesale sales. Cow Bay is a well-known visitor destination, making this a natural meal stop for cyclists arriving by ferry or touring the Yellowhead corridor.

detail.address: 7 Cow Bay Road, Prince Rupert, v8j 1a5

restaurant.name: Riddim & Spice
restaurant.desc: Riddim & Spice is a Caribbean restaurant on Vancouver's lively Commercial Drive, specializing in Jamaican and Caribbean cuisine including slow-cooked oxtail, jerk chicken, and golden flaky patties filled with spiced beef, chicken, or vegetables. Situated on one of the city's most cycling-friendly corridors, it offers both in-person pickup and online delivery ordering. Its hearty, flavour-forward dishes make it a distinctive cultural stop for cyclists rolling through East Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Yanaki Sushi
restaurant.desc: Yanaki Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Vancouver with both dine-in and online ordering options. Located on West 6th Avenue, it serves as a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists and other visitors passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Stages Bistro & Lounge
restaurant.desc: Stages Bistro & Lounge is a full-service restaurant and lounge situated on the lobby floor of the Holiday Inn Vancouver-Centre on West Broadway. It offers an extensive menu spanning breakfast, lunch, and dinner, plus a Friday seafood lunch buffet and a daily happy hour with discounted cocktails and appetizers. The Broadway location makes it a convenient stop for cyclists moving through central Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple items on the lunch buffet menu are explicitly labeled 'V' (Vegetarian), including vegetable medley, coconut rice, garlic noodles, and several salads; gluten-free bread is available as a substitute for toast. Website notes the restaurant is 'not a gluten-free or vegetarian restaurant' but vegetarian and GF options do exist

restaurant.name: Taco Time
restaurant.desc: Taco Time is a fast-food Mexican restaurant in Courtenay. As a branch of a national Canadian chain, it provides reliable casual dining for travelers passing through the community. Touring cyclists can grab a quick meal without lengthy wait times typical of sit-down restaurants.

restaurant.name: Blenz Coffee
restaurant.desc: Blenz Coffee is a BC-born specialty coffee chain that has been hand-crafting beverages since 1992, opening its first store on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. The 550 Burrard Street location sits in the heart of Vancouver's financial district, offering espresso drinks, nitro coffee, whole-leaf teas, protein shakes, and a broad range of baked goods and lunch items. As a locally founded chain with franchised community-oriented stores, it provides a familiar and comfortable stop for cyclists passing through downtown.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website food menu includes filters for vegan, dairy free, and gluten free items (e.g. dairy-free Dacaron™, vegan filter on menu page)

restaurant.name: Funky Winker Beans
restaurant.desc: Funky Winker Beans is a self-described 'hardcore' dive bar in Vancouver's Downtown East Side, known for its low-lit, utilitarian atmosphere that welcomes everyone. The bar features pool tables, pinball machines, and art from local artists for sale on the walls. Regular karaoke and open mic comedy events make it a lively destination in the heart of downtown.

restaurant.name: Pizza Factory

restaurant.name: Macu Tea

Everything is freshly made to order, making it a quick refreshment stop in a quiet residential-commercial strip of West Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Little Bird Dim Sum + Craft Beer
restaurant.desc: Little Bird Dim Sum + Craft Beer is a three-generation family restaurant on Kitsilano's West 4th Avenue, pairing traditional Cantonese dim sum with a curated lineup of BC craft beers and wines. The restaurant earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition, tracing its roots to the family's earlier Flamingo Chinese Restaurant. Touring cyclists passing through Kitsilano will find a full sit-down dim sum experience alongside takeout pickup.

restaurant.name: Stickleback West Coast Eatery

The menu leans toward house-made burgers, wraps, pastas, Baby Back Ribs, and local halibut, with gluten-free options throughout. Situated right beside Rush Kayak Adventures, it's a natural stop for cyclists exploring the Sooke waterfront corridor.

restaurant.name: Starbucks

restaurant.name: SURA Korean BBQ

restaurant.name: Manohar Vegetarian Bakery

restaurant.name: Victoria Sushi

The restaurant supports online ordering, offering touring cyclists a convenient way to have a meal ready on arrival. It is a straightforward sit-down dining stop in a neighbourhood accessible from Victoria's network of urban cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Halu Sushi

restaurant.name: Toro's Liquor Store

It offers personalized staff guidance and a curated focus on local craft breweries, artisanal cideries, and regional vineyards. Touring cyclists could use it as a resupply stop for locally sourced beverages to enjoy at camp or a destination accommodation.

restaurant.name: Elks Club
restaurant.desc: A non-profit social club dedicated to fundraising for local charities. The club features live music performances, pool tables, shuffleboard, and darts, creating a community gathering space for locals and visitors. Touring cyclists will find a casual venue for food, drink, and social connection.

restaurant.name: Portobello

A full-service bar with local craft beers, a market-style retail space, and a summer outdoor patio with Adirondack chairs and a fire pit complete the rustic alpine setting.

restaurant.name: Topinoy

It operates as a counter-service window — no dine-in, no delivery — making it a fast and convenient stop for cyclists passing through town. Bubble tea in multiple flavors rounds out the menu, offering a refreshing option after a long ride.

restaurant.name: Sushi Town

Its emphasis on sustainability and community connection makes it a natural rest point for cyclists riding through the Lynn Valley area.

restaurant.name: Earl of Sandwich

restaurant.name: Saint Germain Bakery

The Burnaby outlet is a counter-service unit inside Metropolis at Metrotown, offering takeaway-only baked goods including cakes, pastries, and breads made without artificial essences. The chain supplies desserts to nine airlines and major hotel brands across North America, giving it an unusually high culinary pedigree for a mall bakery stop.

restaurant.name: Reddy Made Cakes

Every component — ganache, fondant, buttercream, preserves — is made in-house using what the business describes as only the best quality ingredients. Cyclists can stop in for walk-in cupcakes and treats, including gluten-free options, or arrange custom pickup orders.

restaurant.name: Milton Street Public House

Touring cyclists passing through Nanaimo's historic downtown will find a polished sit-down dining experience in a characterful Victorian setting.

restaurant.name: The Taco Hole

The takeout-only format makes it a practical grab-and-go option rather than a sit-down rest.

restaurant.name: My Greek Taverna
restaurant.desc: My Greek Taverna is a family-style Greek restaurant in Coquitlam's Brunette Avenue corridor, serving traditional Mediterranean dishes including souvlaki, moussaka, rack of lamb, and fresh seafood prepared with time-honored recipes. Touring cyclists will find satisfying, protein-rich plated meals with generous accompaniments of Greek salad, rice, roast potato, and pita bread.

restaurant.name: Brewhall

The kitchen focuses on scratch-made, locally sourced food paired with 22 taps of craft beer and cider, and the walls display a museum-grade collection of BC and Canadian artwork.

restaurant.name: A-Frame Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: A-FRAME Brewing Co. is an award-winning craft brewery and tasting room in Squamish, BC, celebrated for its relaxed 'cabin vibes' atmosphere—an outdoor patio with a fire pit, mountain backdrop, and an inclusive, welcoming community ethos. The brewery names its beers after BC lakes and earned Gold and Silver at the 2023 Canadian Brewing Awards. Cyclists will find a natural post-ride stop with growler fills, cold packaged cans to go, and regular on-site food truck service.

restaurant.name: 49th Parallel & Lucky's Doughnuts Cafe
restaurant.desc: The original 49th Parallel café, opened in Kitsilano in 2007, now pairs specialty coffee roasted in-house with Lucky's Doughnuts made on site—a combination that has made it a neighbourhood institution. The spot sits steps from the beach and the Seaside Greenway, making it a natural pitstop for cyclists riding along Vancouver's waterfront corridor. An enclosed patio and ample bike racks round out the appeal for anyone arriving on two wheels.

restaurant.name: Prado Coffee
restaurant.desc: Prado Cafe, now trading as Prado Coffee, is a specialty coffee brand founded by Sammy Piccolo, a four-time Canadian Barista Champion who has represented Canada at the World Barista Championships. Starting as a single shop on Commercial Drive focused on quality espresso and neighbourhood hospitality, the brand has grown to multiple locations across Vancouver and Burnaby. The company roasts its own blends, ranging from approachable everyday espresso to seasonal single-origin offerings.

restaurant.name: Analog Coffee
restaurant.desc: Analog Coffee is a specialty coffee chain founded in Calgary in 2011 with a strong emphasis on sourcing and carefully crafting single-origin coffees. The brand built its identity around an obsessive attention to every detail of the guest experience, from equipment to décor. A touring cyclist stopping in can expect a serious, community-oriented café with a full espresso program and a range of brewing methods.

restaurant.name: Original Joe's
restaurant.desc: Original Joe's is a bar and grill restaurant with a location on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. The venue features indoor and outdoor seating in a no-smoking environment. It offers vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free menu options.

restaurant.name: The Keg
restaurant.desc: The Keg Morgan Creek is a full-service steakhouse and bar located in South Surrey's Morgan Creek neighbourhood, about 10 minutes from White Rock Beach. The location features a heated and covered patio, a lounge with bar and TVs, and free parking. It is a well-established chain destination offering a sit-down dining experience as well as takeout and DoorDash delivery.

restaurant.name: Reggiano's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Reggiano's Pizza is an authentic Neapolitan-style pizzeria with multiple Lower Mainland locations, baking pies in a traditional Marra Forni wood-fired oven using Caputo '00' flour and mozzarella di bufala for a characteristic charred, leopard-spotted crust. The Port Coquitlam location offers both dine-in and takeout, including pizza by the slice for a quick stop on the go. Beer and wine are served on premises.

restaurant.name: Pallet Coffee Roasters HQ, Cafe + Roastery
restaurant.desc: Pallet Coffee Roasters is a locally owned Vancouver specialty coffee company established in East Vancouver in 2014, and this location serves as the company's flagship HQ and working roastery. With eight café locations across Metro Vancouver, Pallet is also a wholesale partner and barista training provider, making the HQ a hub where cyclists can experience freshly roasted coffee alongside food and baked goods. The company emphasizes ethical sourcing and long-term relationships with farmers from origin countries such as Peru, Colombia, and Brazil.

restaurant.name: Presotea
restaurant.desc: Presotea is a Taiwanese bubble tea franchise established in 2006, now operating multiple Lower Mainland locations including this Metrotown branch on Kingsway. The shop specialises in freshly brewed teas made using a high-pressure espresso-style machine, offering an extensive menu of milk teas, fruit teas, and slushes. It is a takeout-only counter with no indoor or outdoor seating.

restaurant.name: Blind Angler
restaurant.desc: The Blind Angler is a full-service lakeside restaurant on Beach Avenue in Peachland, named after a legendary local figure who continued fishing on Lake Okanagan after losing his sight in WWI. The restaurant sits overlooking the marina with views described as among the best in the Okanagan, and serves everything from eggs benedict at breakfast to seafood and steaks at dinner. It is a notable stop for cyclists riding the Okanagan lakefront corridor.

restaurant.name: Afghan Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Afghan Kitchen is a family-run restaurant in South Surrey built around the owner's personal journey from Kabul to Canada, serving traditional Afghan dishes made entirely from his mother's recipes. The restaurant earned the South Surrey & White Rock Chamber of Commerce Business of the Year (Medium) award for 2023 and was featured on the Food Network in March 2021. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a welcoming sit-down dining experience with catering available for group events.

restaurant.name: Sisto's Pub
restaurant.desc: Sisto's Pub has anchored the Hatzic neighbourhood of Mission since 1978, earning a reputation as a hidden gem and home-away-from-home for locals. Part of the Springs Group chain, it serves classic, large-portioned pub food with in-house dining, patio seating, and a seasonal back lawn with lawn games. Weekly events include Music Bingo, Karaoke, Family Feud, and Trivia nights, making it a lively stop for cyclists looking for a full meal and evening entertainment.

restaurant.name: On the Rocks
restaurant.desc: On the Rocks is a pub and grill that bills itself as Kamloops' local favourite, serving an extensive menu that spans Maple-Glazed Salmon, AAA Prime Sterling Silver Sirloin, and hearty pub fare alongside a wide selection of draft and bottled beers from around the world. The venue doubles as an entertainment hub, with big-screen TVs for major sporting events and regular live music performances. Touring cyclists arriving in Kamloops would find a full sit-down meal option with a varied menu and a lively atmosphere.

restaurant.name: BarBurrito
restaurant.desc: BarBurrito is Canada's largest Mexican-inspired burrito chain, proudly Canadian since 2005 and now operating 385+ locations nationwide. This Langley location serves fully customizable burritos, bowls, tacos, and quesadillas assembled from fresh, in-house ingredients with a wide range of proteins. Cyclists looking for a quick, filling meal will find substantial options including vegetarian and gluten-free choices.

restaurant.name: Stick In The Mud Roastorium
restaurant.desc: Stick In The Mud Roastorium is a specialty coffee roastery located in Sooke, BC, offering freshly roasted coffee beans, brewing equipment, and coffee education classes. The business operates both a physical roasting facility and an online shop selling single-origin coffees, grinders, brewers, and accessories. A touring cyclist rolling into Sooke's outskirts will find a craft-roaster destination rather than a typical café counter.

restaurant.name: Axum Ethiopian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Axum Ethiopian Restaurant serves traditional Ethiopian cuisine — spiced stews, injera-based communal plates, and a robust vegetarian selection — from its East Hastings Street location in Vancouver. The restaurant offers full sit-down dining alongside online ordering, private event hosting, and catering packages for all occasions. It is a lively neighborhood destination known for both hearty meat dishes and a wide range of entirely plant-based options.

restaurant.name: Woodstone Pizza Inc.

The kitchen uses premium ingredients including fior di latte, hand-stretched dough, and prosciutto cotto, with a menu spanning classic Italian specialties and local-style combinations. The restaurant is currently open and operating normally while a full rebrand is in progress.

restaurant.name: Thunderbird
restaurant.desc: Thunderbird is a Korean Fried Chicken restaurant tucked into Cook Street Village, one of Victoria's most bike-friendly neighbourhood strips. Founded by Korean-Canadians who moved to Victoria in 2009 and found no KFC restaurants in the city, it specialises in double deep-fried chicken with sauces like Yang-nyeom (sweet & spicy) and Megan Burger (spicy soy). The menu also features bao, chicken katsu curry, cro-waffles, and rice bowls, making it a solid stop for a calorie-rich refuel after a coastal ride.

restaurant.name: JiangNan Wok
restaurant.desc: JiangNan Wok is a Chinese restaurant in Richmond's Capstan Way commercial district, drawing its name from the Jiangnan region along China's lower Yangtze River, known for refined home-style cooking. The restaurant offers indoor seating only, making it a sit-down dining option for cyclists passing through the area. It is located in a multi-unit commercial building, typical of Richmond's dense mixed-use developments.

restaurant.name: L'aromas Coffee Southlands
restaurant.desc: L'aromas Coffee Southlands is one of four locations of a Delta-based coffee brand that grew from a backyard roasting project and community market presence into a local café chain, officially opening its first location in July 2015. Founded by three friends with a mission to create a 'home away from home,' the brand is community-rooted and independently owned. The Southlands location offers a full café experience with outdoor seating and on-site washrooms.

restaurant.name: Kiyo Sushi
restaurant.desc: Kiyo Sushi is a sushi restaurant located in Richmond, BC. Additional details about the business and its facilities are unavailable due to website fetch failure.

restaurant.name: La Ruelle Bakery
restaurant.desc: La Ruelle Bakery is a small-batch French Canadian artisan bakery tucked into a charming back alley in downtown Nelson, BC, specializing in organic sourdough breads, handmade pastries, and fresh sandwiches to go. The open-concept bakehouse lets customers watch bakers at work, using organic flours and seasonal locally sourced ingredients — continuing a tradition inherited from the predecessor bakery Au Soleil Levant. All sales are takeaway-only, making it a straightforward stop for a freshly baked loaf or a quick lunch on the road.

restaurant.name: O Sushi
