The menu spans appetizers, curries, tandoori meats and seafood, and desserts, with a notably broad vegetarian selection. Cyclists riding the Tsawwassen corridor would find it a substantial sit-down meal stop with plenty of meatless options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes dedicated vegetarian dishes: Vegetable Pakora, Vegetable Samosa/Aloo Tikki, Chaat Papri, Paneer Pakora, Channa Bhatura, Vegetable Manchurian, Chilli Paneer, Malai Paneer Tikka, Paneer Tikka, Pudina Paneer Tikka, Veggie Noodles, Chilli Cauliflower, and a full vegetarian section

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: McDonald's at 1701 Robson Street sits in the heart of Vancouver's busy Robson Street corridor, one of the city's most prominent tourist and cycling routes through the West End. This location features both indoor and outdoor seating and a full fast-food menu including McCafé beverages, with multiple ordering modes including Drive-Thru, Curbside, and McDelivery. Its central urban location makes it a recognizable and accessible refueling point for cyclists moving through downtown Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Laowai
restaurant.desc: Laowai is a 1930s Shanghai-inspired speakeasy concealed behind the BLND TGER dumpling shop in Vancouver's Chinatown, entered via a secret code. The venue pairs theatrical cocktails with a compact menu of dumplings drawn from regional Chinese cuisines — Sichuan, Tibetan, Xinjiang, and more. It's a genuinely hidden-gem bar experience in one of Vancouver's most historically dense and walkable neighbourhoods.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: BLND TGER menu lists Vegetable Shaomai (V) and Tmrw Foods & Cabbage Jiaozi (V) as vegetarian options; Tmrw Foods is a plant-based alternative meat brand, suggesting at least one vegan-friendly item

restaurant.name: New Fuji
restaurant.desc: New Fuji is a Japanese restaurant located on West 1st Avenue in Vancouver, near the False Creek seawall — a popular cycling corridor. It is part of a larger Vancouver-area restaurant group that includes Kingyo, Rajio Raisu, Toyokan, and several other Japanese concepts. Diners can reserve a table, order pickup, or arrange delivery.

restaurant.name: Joe Pesto's Wood Fired Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Joe Pesto's is a locally owned and operated wood-fired pizzeria in downtown Squamish, voted best pizza in the city. Their Neapolitan-style pies are baked at 800–900°F in an Italian brick oven, producing a crispy crust with a soft interior, alongside a creative menu spanning classics to inventive specials. Cyclists finishing a ride in the Sea-to-Sky corridor will find a full dine-in experience with local beer and wine on tap, or a quick takeout option to fuel the next leg.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Gluten-free crust explicitly offered ('best gluten free crust in town'); multiple vegetarian pizzas on the menu including Veggie Supreme, The Popeye, Just Beet It, and Margarita

restaurant.name: SpearHead Winery
restaurant.desc: SpearHead Winery is an award-winning Kelowna estate winery specializing in single-vineyard Pinot Noir from the Central Okanagan Valley, led by winemaker Grant Stanley who brings experience from New Zealand, Oregon, and BC. The winery earned the 2024 Best Performing Winery and Winery of the Year honours and offers tastings, a wine shop, wine club memberships, and a private events venue. Situated on Spiers Road in the heart of Okanagan wine country, it makes a natural destination stop on a cycling wine tour through the Kelowna region.

restaurant.name: White Spot
restaurant.desc: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, operating since 1928 and known for burgers made with 100% fresh Canadian beef and locally sourced BC ingredients including BC chicken and BC-grown potato fries. The Fort Street Victoria location is a full sit-down family restaurant offering breakfast, lunch, and dinner, with dine-in, takeout, curbside pickup, and third-party delivery options. It's a reliable, familiar stop for a touring cyclist wanting a full hot meal in a comfortable setting.

restaurant.name: Noah's Cafe
restaurant.desc: Noah's Cafe is a Japanese fusion bistro and cocktail bar on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, a short ride from the Stanley Park seawall. The kitchen offers creative tapas-style sharing plates — from aburi tuna tataki to wagyu beef tartare — alongside an omakase course experience. The bar program leans on Japanese spirits and techniques, making this an atmospheric evening stop for cyclists exploring the neighbourhood.

notes.Takeout: Dinner menu notes one specific item (Hokkaido Scallop Motoyaki) as 'Not available for take out,' implying takeout is otherwise available for other items

restaurant.name: The Sandbar
restaurant.desc: The Sandbar is a full-service seafood restaurant on Granville Island, situated on the water between the Arts Club Theatre and Ocean Cement, directly under the Granville Street Bridge with views over False Creek. Part of the Sequoia Company of Restaurants (est. 1978), it is a Vancouver institution with a 300-seat capacity, live music, and a menu anchored in Pacific seafood including fresh oysters, Dungeness crab, and a sushi and raw bar. Cycling tourists on the Vancouver Seawall will find it a natural stopping point, as it sits steps from False Creek Water Ferries and the Seawall itself.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists 'Vegetarian Gluten-Free Organic' as explicit filter categories, confirming both vegetarian and gluten-free options are available

restaurant.name: Acquafarina
restaurant.desc: Acquafarina is a Michelin Guide-recommended Italian fine dining restaurant in the heart of downtown Vancouver, operated by the Perse Hospitality Group. The kitchen specializes in modern Italian cuisine made from scratch with locally sourced ingredients, spanning handmade pasta, fresh seafood, Wagyu beef, and a curated caviar program. A polished bar program, weekend brunch, private event spaces, and a unique Liquor Locker membership add to its reputation as one of Vancouver's most refined dining destinations.

detail.address: 425 West Georgia Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 5A1

restaurant.name: Di Muzio Ristorante
restaurant.desc: Di Muzio Ristorante is an Italian restaurant located in Kamloops, BC. It appears to be a dinner-focused establishment, suggesting a sit-down dining experience suited to cyclists looking for an evening meal after a day on the road.

detail.address: 152 Victoria St, Kamloops, BC V2C 1Z7, Canada

restaurant.name: Selkirk Cafe
restaurant.desc: Selkirk Cafe is a neighbourhood cafe situated on Jutland Road in Victoria, BC, a corridor that sees steady commuter and recreational cycling traffic near the Gorge waterway. The cafe operates weekday mornings and lunchtimes, making it a potential mid-ride stop for cyclists exploring the west side of the city. Beyond its OSM listing and Facebook presence, little additional detail is publicly verifiable.

restaurant.name: LITTLE SPROUT café
restaurant.desc: Little Sprout Café is a social enterprise café operated by Communitas Supportive Care Society, a BC charity supporting people living with disabilities, with all profits reinvested into that mission. The menu centres on microgreens grown in-house and Fraser Valley sourced ingredients, prepared in a fully visible open-kitchen concept by an inclusively hired team. It is a community-rooted, values-driven spot that offers a genuinely local and nutritious food stop in the Abbotsford area.

detail.address: 102 – 2776 Bourquin Crescent West, Abbotsford, BC V2S 6A4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Microgreens page states 'Locally sourced ingredients and plant-forward recipes are part of how we express our values'; menu is built around in-house-grown microgreens and fresh plant-based ingredients

restaurant.name: Bori Korean Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Bori Korean Restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue serves home-style Korean meals inspired by the nourishing qualities of barley ('Bori'), with a menu spanning traditional pancakes, deep-fried dishes, and hearty mains. The restaurant operates as both a sit-down dining room and a takeout spot, with online pick-up ordering available. It sits on a busy commercial corridor in North Vancouver that cyclists commonly travel when exploring the North Shore.

detail.address: 2039 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2K4

restaurant.name: Tartan Toque
restaurant.desc: The Tartan Toque is a Victoria neighbourhood taphouse and wing restaurant that has won 'Victoria's Best Wings' multiple times since opening in 2012. Known for double-cooked crispy wings with dozens of house-made sauces, scratch-made burgers, and a rotating selection of local craft beers on tap, it offers casual comfort food in a relaxed setting. Dietary-friendly options including gluten-free, lactose-free, and vegetarian items are available throughout the menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'We are proud to offer many dietary restrictive options'; menu lists crispy tofu wings, falafel, veggie sticks, and plant-based salad add-ons. OSM corroborates with and

restaurant.name: Green Waves - Tofino's Salad Joint
restaurant.desc: Green Waves Salads is a salad-focused fast food establishment located in Tofino, BC. As a quick-service spot in a popular surf and cycling destination, it would cater to health-conscious visitors seeking fresh food options. Current operational status is uncertain.

restaurant.name: Top Cantonese Cuisine Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A Cantonese restaurant on Kingsway in Vancouver offering indoor seating. Touring cyclists can stop for sit-down meals of traditional Cantonese cuisine.

restaurant.name: Samz Pub
restaurant.desc: Samz is a neighbourhood pub in Surrey offering food, drinks, and live sports viewing, with an attached liquor store on the same premises. It is one of two Lower Mainland locations operated by the same company, and the Surrey pub also carries Skip the Dishes delivery. The liquor store next door stocks beer, wine, and spirits at competitive prices, making this a convenient stop for cyclists looking to resupply.

restaurant.name: Burnt Orange Cafe + Bistro
restaurant.desc: Burnt Orange Cafe + Bistro is a brunch and lunch spot on Hastings Street in Burnaby, known for its specialty fluffy pancakes and 49th Parallel coffee. It operates seven days a week and offers table reservations, suggesting a sit-down dining experience. A touring cyclist rolling along the Hastings corridor would find it a solid mid-morning or midday refuelling stop.

restaurant.name: Two Horns Korean BBQ House
restaurant.desc: Two Horns is an upscale Korean and Japanese BBQ steakhouse in Richmond specializing in premium cuts including dry-aged beef and Canadian Prime Beef. The restaurant emphasizes quality sourcing and tableside grilling, and has drawn attention as one of the few authentically run Korean BBQ spots in the Richmond area. A touring cyclist visiting the Richmond cycling network would find a full sit-down dining experience with lunch specials and delivery/online ordering available.

restaurant.name: Epic Grill Silogs + Sans Rival
restaurant.desc: Epic Grill Silogs is a small restaurant serving Chinese and Filipino cuisine, including the Filipino staple silog dishes (garlic rice with protein). It operates as a takeout-friendly spot and maintains a no-smoking environment. Touring cyclists passing through the New Westminster area may find it a quick stop for hearty, inexpensive Filipino comfort food.

restaurant.name: Laughing Bean Coffee Co.
restaurant.desc: A family-run neighbourhood café that has been caffeinating East Vancouver since 2003, The Laughing Bean is known for locally roasted coffee, fresh-baked pastries, and a dog-friendly patio on East Hastings Street. It is one of the few cafés in BC to accept Bitcoin and Lightning Network payments, alongside a full catering and online ordering service.

restaurant.name: The Roost Farm Bakery
restaurant.desc: The Roost is a working 10-acre farm in North Saanich that grows and mills its own wheat for daily fresh bread, tends a 2-acre vineyard producing estate wines, and raises free-range hens and sheep — making the food genuinely farm-to-table rather than a marketing claim. The property encompasses a farm bakery, a Vineyard Bistro with breakfast and lunch counter service, a winery tasting room, and guided farm tours. A short ride from the Victoria International Airport ferry corridor, it offers cyclists a genuinely pastoral stop with regional cuisine and local wine.

detail.address: 9100 East Saanich Road, North Saanich, BC V8M 2B4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states the bakery offers 'gluten free options'; a customer review states 'superb menu offering many gluten free options'

restaurant.name: Kavalas
restaurant.desc: Kalvas The Loghouse Restaurant is an upscale fine-dining destination in Parksville housed in a distinctive log building, specializing in prime-grade steaks and fresh Pacific Northwest seafood including wild sockeye salmon, halibut, and Dungeness crab. Its circular dining room and European-influenced menu — featuring dishes like schnitzel, escargot, and oysters Rockefeller alongside an extensive BC wine cellar — make it a notable splurge for touring cyclists passing through the Parksville area. The restaurant also offers phone-ahead pickup for those wanting a quality meal on the go.

restaurant.name: Bella Roma
restaurant.desc: Bella Roma Pizzeria & Ristorante is a locally owned Italian restaurant in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, helmed by chef Jimmy Khinda who trained for three years in Italy before bringing his craft home to BC. The menu centres on pizza and pasta, with customer reviews highlighting generous portions and fresh seafood dishes. A patio at the back of the restaurant provides an outdoor seating option.

restaurant.name: Chez Christophe
restaurant.desc: Chez Christophe is a Swiss-inspired chocolaterie and patisserie founded by Swiss-trained pastry chef Christophe Bonzon, with this White Rock location opening in 2019. The shop offers handcrafted artisan chocolates, freshly baked croissants and pastries, custom cakes, and a full espresso café bar using locally roasted beans from Pallet Coffee Roasters. A rewarding stop for touring cyclists seeking quality coffee or an indulgent chocolate treat along the Johnston Road corridor.

restaurant.name: Smokehouse 93
restaurant.desc: Smokehouse 93 is a slow-smoked BBQ restaurant located at the Crossroads in downtown Invermere, serving Canadian meats hand-rubbed with a signature spice blend and smoked for 12–20 hours until fall-off-the-bone tender. The fully licensed restaurant features a dining room and what the website bills as Invermere's largest outdoor patio, which is dog-friendly and occasionally hosts live music. Meat is prepared in limited daily quantities and sold until it runs out, so hungry cyclists can call ahead to pre-order and guarantee their meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly states the house-made BBQ sauce is 'handcrafted Gluten Free'; no vegetarian or vegan options mentioned

restaurant.name: Gmen@NanChuu Ramen Shop
restaurant.desc: Gmen@NanChuu Ramen Shop is a ramen restaurant located in Richmond's Alexandra Road dining corridor, a dense stretch of East Asian eateries popular with locals and visitors alike. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's flat, bikeable streets will find it a convenient stop for a hot bowl after riding the dyke trails or nearby greenways.

restaurant.name: Bao
restaurant.desc: Bao is an Asian fusion restaurant situated in Victoria's historic Chinatown, specializing in Taiwanese steam buns (Gua Bao) with a rotating cast of fillings alongside ramen, bibimbap, and Korean fried chicken. The compact, focused menu reflects a blend of East and Southeast Asian flavours, with most dishes available in vegetarian, vegan, or gluten-free adaptations on request. It makes a solid mid-ride meal stop given its Chinatown location and dine-in or takeout flexibility.

notes.Takeout: Website states '15% Gratuity added to all takeout orders over $100', confirming takeout service is offered
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists dedicated vegetarian/vegan items (Shanghai Black Bean Croquette, Mala 5 Mushroom bao, Korean Fried Tofu Bibimbap) and notes 'GF upon request' and 'Vegetarian/Vegan options available upon request' on multiple dishes

restaurant.name: Junior's Pub
restaurant.desc: Junior's Pub & Grill is a neighbourhood pub on the corner of Commercial Drive and Graveley in Vancouver's East Side, positioning itself as a welcoming community gathering spot. It features 11 HD big screens showing live sports including NFL, UFC, European soccer, and Canucks games. The pub also hosts regular events such as Friday live entertainment, Sunday karaoke, and fundraiser nights for local sports teams and charities.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Fundraiser page states: 'All of the burgers (either beef or veggie) will come with mayo, lettuce, tomato and onion on the bun.'

restaurant.name: Namiya
restaurant.desc: Namiya is a sushi restaurant on Vancouver's West Broadway offering Japanese cuisine. The business offers online ordering for convenient takeout. Located on a busy urban street, it provides a casual dining option for cyclists in the neighborhood.

restaurant.name: Kyuzo Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kyuzo is a Japanese restaurant on Granville Street specializing in omakase dining, where the chef curates a personalized meal based on guest preferences and allergies using fresh, seasonal ingredients. The restaurant is notable for offering certified Tajima and Kobe beef sourced from Hyogo Prefecture, Japan. With 85 seats and a transit-accessible location near Oakridge-41st SkyTrain, it offers a full sit-down dining experience in southwest Vancouver.

restaurant.name: The Village Baker Cafe'
restaurant.desc: A breakfast and coffee cafe on Bowen Island with outdoor seating. Located on Dorman Road in the island community. No additional details confirmed due to website unavailability.

restaurant.name: Thai Orchid Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Little Thai Place has served authentic Thai cuisine in Victoria since 2003, operated by a Bangkok family with a strong local reputation for fresh ingredients, house-made sauces, and consistent quality. The Shelbourne Plaza location has since been rebranded as Thai Orchid Restaurant under the same ownership, with a refreshed menu while retaining many classic dishes. The broader Little Thai Place brand holds two active locations (Cook Street and Royal Oak) and has been voted Best Thai in the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About Us page: 'many dishes available as vegetarian or gluten-free options.' FAQ confirms vegan options available

restaurant.name: Irish Times
restaurant.desc: The Irish Times is a Victoria institution on Government Street, voted best pub in North America in 2017 and best Irish Entertainment Venue in 2018. Open since 2004, it offers an authentic Irish pub experience with food, drink, and live music in a warm, welcoming atmosphere. Located on one of Victoria's main cycling corridors, it serves as a natural stopping point for touring cyclists exploring the city.

restaurant.name: Crust n Crunch Pizza + Donair
restaurant.desc: Crust n Crunch is a BC-based pizza and donair chain with over 11 years in the industry, known for bold flavour combinations including South Asian-inspired options like Shahi Paneer and Butter Chicken pizzas alongside classic donairs. The brand emphasizes halal-certified ingredients and caters to schools, businesses, and events. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a fast, filling meal with strong vegetarian options and online ordering.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegetarian pizzas listed on menu (marked 🌿): Greek Delight, Pesto Cheesy, Pesto Garden, Shahi Paneer Delight, Spinach Feta Delight, Tandoori Paneer, Veggie Trio

restaurant.name: Sakura Sushi & Grocery
restaurant.desc: Sakura Sushi & Grocery is a beloved Victoria institution that opened in 1997 and has grown into one of the city's most popular Japanese takeout destinations, offering handmade sushi rolls, hot kitchen dishes like udon, donburi, curry, and bento, as well as Japanese grocery items. The business is now owned by chef Morgan Onda, who brings over 40 years of culinary experience including travels through Japan. It operates takeout-only from its compact downtown location beside the market on Quadra Street.

notes.Takeout: Website front page: 'for the best Japanese Take Away and Grocery Items in Downtown Victoria.' About page: 'one of the most popular Take-outs in Victoria.' In-dining closed since COVID

restaurant.name: The Corner Hotpot
restaurant.desc: The Corner Hotpot is a hotpot restaurant located on West Broadway in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood. Hotpot dining is a communal, interactive style of meal where diners cook ingredients in a simmering broth at the table — a warm and filling stop for a hungry cyclist. The West Broadway corridor offers a dense strip of food and services along a common cycling route connecting central Vancouver to the western suburbs.

restaurant.name: GAON Korean Cuisine
restaurant.desc: GAON Korean Cuisine is a Korean restaurant on Kingsway in Burnaby, offering indoor seating in a no-smoking environment. The restaurant sits along a busy commercial corridor, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists passing through the area. Beyond its Korean menu, little detail is publicly verifiable due to an inaccessible website.

restaurant.name: Pho Ten
restaurant.desc: Pho Ten is a Vietnamese restaurant in Richmond specializing in traditional dishes including phở, rice plates, vermicelli bowls, bánh mì, and spring rolls, all prepared with fresh ingredients and traditional recipes. Located in a strip mall on No. 5 Road, it offers both dine-in and pick-up ordering, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area. The warm, casual atmosphere and broad menu offer a satisfying refuelling option after a ride.

restaurant.name: Mama Said Pizza Co.
restaurant.desc: Mama Said Pizza Co. is a Brooklyn-style pizza restaurant in Port Moody, BC, serving scratch-made deck-oven pies with premium toppings. The spot doubles as a bar with a rotating tap list, making it a solid stop for a post-ride meal. Takeout and delivery are both available for cyclists on the move.

detail.address: 3135 Murray St, Port Moody, British Columbia V3H 2R8

restaurant.name: Gateway to India Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Gateway to India is an Indian restaurant in Nanaimo serving authentic dishes made with exotic spices imported from the northern and southern regions of the Indian subcontinent. The restaurant offers both dine-in and takeout, with an extensive menu of tandoor-baked breads, curries, pakoras, and a broad selection of vegetarian dishes. Their spice products are also sold at grocery stores across Vancouver Island and the Lower Mainland.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu has a dedicated 'VEGETARIAN OPTIONS' section with multiple dishes; Pappadum is explicitly labelled 'GLUTEN FREE'

restaurant.name: Jacks On The Water
restaurant.desc: Jacks On The Water is a waterfront restaurant and bar that opened in 2024 on Sidney's Seaport Place, offering panoramic views of the Saanich Peninsula shoreline in a casual, inviting setting. The menu spans regional dishes, sushi (available daily), tacos, burgers, and shareable appetizers, with a first-come-first-served patio that welcomes well-behaved leashed dogs. Cyclists finishing a ride on the Lochside or Galloping Goose trails will find it a convenient stop just steps from the Sidney waterfront.

notes.Takeout: FAQ states: 'Yes, we offer takeout! You can place an order online under the order online tab on the website. Take out options include our full menu except for the Tiramisu and Beef Aburi.'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states gluten-free options are marked on the menu with a symbol; vegetarian/vegan options available on request. Multiple menu items are labelled 'Gluten friendly'

restaurant.name: The Cabin Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Cabin is an upscale-casual restaurant in the seaside community of Crescent Beach, serving Pacific Northwest cuisine centred on fresh local seafood, AAA steaks, and gourmet pasta alongside a full bar with craft beers and signature cocktails. It sits at the edge of the Boundary Bay area, a popular destination for Lower Mainland cyclists, and positions itself as a community favourite for relaxed, quality dining. The restaurant accommodates large groups and offers a seasonal group set menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Front page states 'many GLUTEN FREE options'; lunch and dinner menus include a Plant Based Burger (cauliflower and chickpea patty), Herb Infused Veggie Fillets, Maple Chili Cauliflower Wings, flatbread pizzas, and multiple salads suitable for vegetarians

restaurant.name: the apron
restaurant.desc: The apron is a contemporary Canadian farm-to-table restaurant inside the Westin Wall Centre, steps from Vancouver International Airport, serving Pacific Northwest cuisine sourced from local farmers, growers, and fishers. It is led by Executive Chef Clement Chan, a National Chef of the Year and Culinary Team Canada member known from Food Network's Chopped Canada and Top Chef Canada. The setting spans an indoor dining room and terrace, making it a polished full-service stop for cyclists passing through the Richmond/YVR corridor.

detail.address: 3099 Corvette Way, Richmond, British Columbia, Canada V6X 3A3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu throughout uses (v) vegetarian, (ve) vegan, (gf) gluten-free, and (df) dairy-free markers; multiple options in every meal period including gluten-free bread/buns available as a substitute

restaurant.name: Fiore Famiglia
restaurant.desc: Fiore Famiglia is a neighbourhood Italian restaurant in Vancouver's west side, focused on 'simple Italian done right' with a full menu spanning lunch, dinner, happy hour, and takeout. It is part of a local restaurant group that also operates Brasserie Coquette and The Stable House Bistro, all sharing a community-gathering ethos. Cyclists in the Arbutus Ridge area will find a sit-down Italian option with a dedicated takeout menu and online or phone reservations.

notes.Takeout: Website promotes 'Fiore Takeout Specials!' with a dedicated takeout menu (PDF available), and states 'Last order for takeout 8:30 p.m.'

restaurant.name: Thunderbird Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Thunderbird Café occupies the admission-free lower level of the Squamish Lil'wat Cultural Centre in Whistler's Upper Village, serving Indigenous-inspired dishes such as bannock tacos, venison chili, and cedar plank salmon chowder prepared with fresh local ingredients. Staffed by Cultural Ambassadors of the Squamish and Lil'wat Nations, the café offers a culturally grounded dining experience that stands apart from Whistler's typical resort fare. Free Wi-Fi and a comfortable seating environment make it a practical rest stop for cyclists before or after exploring the museum exhibits.

restaurant.name: Nubo Kitchen + Bar
restaurant.desc: Nubo Kitchen + Bar is a Japanese fusion restaurant in the historic Janion building near the Johnson Street Bridge in downtown Victoria, serving fresh sushi, sashimi, ramen, tapas-style sharing plates, and modern cocktails since 2019. Part of the multi-location Nubo Group, the kitchen blends traditional Japanese technique with global influences and sources from local and international ingredient partners. Walk-ins are welcome during quieter hours, making it a natural downtown refueling stop for cyclists arriving without a reservation.

notes.Takeout: Menu page notes 'take out is not available' only for the lunch special, implying takeout is available for other menu items; front page confirms 3rd-party delivery is also offered
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu marks multiple items 'GF' (e.g., Kaiso Seaweed Salad 'GF. DF') and notes 'GF option available' on salads; vegetarian items include Avocado Tempura, Edamame, Yam Roll, Avocado Roll, and Tofu Teriyaki Don

restaurant.name: O'Hare's Gastropub
restaurant.desc: O'Hare's Gastropub is a full-service pub and liquor store in Richmond's Steveston neighbourhood, a popular destination for cyclists exploring the flat dyke trails and waterfront. The venue offers dine-in food service as well as takeout and delivery options. Its combined gastropub-and-liquor-store format makes it a practical stop for resupplying on a longer ride through the Fraser River delta.

restaurant.name: Pizza Pizza
restaurant.desc: Pizza Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 1967 with over 750 locations coast to coast, operating here as a counter-service restaurant in a Burnaby strip unit along the busy Lougheed Highway corridor. The menu spans classic and specialty pizzas, panzerottis, poutine, chicken sandwiches, and sides. Indoor seating is available, and the kitchen offers plant-based, gluten-free, and vegetarian options, making it a practical calorie stop for cyclists moving through this part of Burnaby.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'Veggie Favourites' and 'Plant-Based' menu sections (Plant-Based Chick'n Bites, etc.) and confirms gluten-free crust is available

restaurant.name: Sushi Aji
restaurant.desc: Sushi Aji is a neighbourhood Japanese restaurant on Kingsway in East Vancouver offering a broad menu of sushi rolls, nigiri, sashimi, oshi sushi, bento boxes, and hot dishes. The shop supports online ordering with a stated 15-minute pickup window, making it a practical quick stop. With nearly 300 customer reviews it appears to be a well-established local spot.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian items: Vegetable Roll (G02), Avocado Roll (G09), Mango and Avocado Roll (G25), Yam Tempura Roll (G15), Veggie Dragon Roll (H10), Forest Roll (H11), and others. No explicit vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: The Ivanhoe Pub
restaurant.desc: The Ivanhoe Pub is a no-frills East Vancouver neighbourhood bar established in 1907, serving locals on Main Street for over a century. It's known for affordable drinks, live music, pool tables, and darts, with Irwin's kitchen turning out comfort food including burgers, bannock tacos, and poutine. Cyclists can also grab takeout cans, coolers, and bottles to go.

notes.Takeout: Dedicated '/take-out' subpage lists cans, coolers, and bottles; noted as available daily till 11PM

restaurant.name: Sushi Tendo
restaurant.desc: Sushi Tendo is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver's Cambie Village neighbourhood, offering indoor-only seating with no outdoor patio. The restaurant supports online ordering with a pickup discount, making it a practical stop for cyclists wanting a sit-down or takeout Japanese meal along this busy commercial corridor.

restaurant.name: Triple O's
restaurant.desc: Triple O's is a BC-born quick-service burger chain and sibling brand to White Spot, known for its signature Triple 'O' sauce, hand-scooped milkshakes, and Kennebec fries. This Richmond location is co-located inside a Chevron gas station on Bridgeport Road, making it a practical stop for cyclists in the area. Drive-thru and takeout are available, with delivery offered through Skip the Dishes.

restaurant.name: Numero Uno Pizza
restaurant.desc: Numero Uno Pizza is a family-run thin-crust gourmet pizza shop on Davie Street in downtown Vancouver, baking with house-made dough and sauce and offering a broad menu of meaty and vegetarian pies available by the slice or whole. The shop supports dine-in, takeout, delivery, and catering, making it a flexible stop for solo riders or larger cycling groups. Its location in the heart of the West End puts it within easy reach of the Seawall route.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple gourmet veggie pizzas, vegan cheese as a topping and crust-cheese substitute, and cauliflower crust option

restaurant.name: Take Five Cafe
restaurant.desc: Take Five Cafe is a Metro Vancouver coffee franchise that has been operating since 2003, serving specialty Arabica espresso drinks alongside Italian-inspired savouries such as panini and wraps, freshly baked pastries, and seasonal specialty drinks. The café has both indoor and outdoor seating and operates a loyalty rewards program. It is one of several franchise locations across the region, including New Westminster, Surrey, Port Coquitlam, North Vancouver, Vancouver, and Burnaby.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Catering menu explicitly lists 'Gluten Friendly Muffins' as a distinct product category with 3 items

restaurant.name: Bless'd Sips & Slices
restaurant.desc: Bless'd Sips & Slices is a family-owned artisan pizza-by-the-slice restaurant located near Gyro Beach in Kelowna, cooking pizzas in a gas-fired brick oven using slow-fermented Italian flour and no canola oil. The restaurant also operates what it bills as the first dirty soda bar in Kelowna, offering hundreds of customizable fizzy drink combinations. Ten percent of profits are donated to local community organizations, and the location is walkable from the popular Okanagan lakeside cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Brownstone
restaurant.desc: The Brownstone has been a downtown Kamloops landmark since 2004, housed in the beautifully restored 1904 Canadian Bank of Commerce building — once the workplace of poet Robert Service. The kitchen leans heavily on local BC producers, with rustic breads, charcuterie, and cheeses made in-house and herbs grown in the restaurant's own garden courtyard. Featured on Food Network Canada's Big Food Bucket List, it offers touring cyclists an upscale but welcoming dinner destination in the heart of Kamloops.

restaurant.name: Dublin Crossing Irish Pub
restaurant.desc: Dublin Crossing is a full-service Irish pub on SW Marine Drive in South Vancouver, offering a broad menu of pub classics alongside a robust bar program featuring Irish whiskeys, draught beers, and creative cocktails. The pub hosts live music on Friday and Saturday evenings and Sunday afternoons, making it a lively destination any day of the week. An adjacent MG Liquor Store adds convenience for self-catering cyclists passing through.

restaurant.name: Popeyes
restaurant.desc: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen is a well-known fast food chain specializing in Southern-style fried chicken with Louisiana-inspired seasoning. Located on the busy Lougheed Highway commercial corridor, it offers a high-calorie, quick-service stop for cyclists passing through the area. Takeout is confirmed available.

restaurant.name: Big Chicken Town
restaurant.desc: Big Chicken Town is a Korean fried chicken restaurant in Surrey, BC, specializing in double-fried chicken with traditional Korean recipes and signature sauces such as Honey Garlic, Black Yummy, and Green Mountain. The menu also includes Korean classics like spicy rice cakes. Online ordering is available for pickup or delivery, and the restaurant has its own mobile app.

restaurant.name: Pizza Camp
restaurant.desc: Pizza Camp is a fast-food restaurant offering pizza and Indian cuisine with both indoor and outdoor seating. It operates via an online ordering platform, providing convenient takeout options for touring cyclists in need of a quick meal.

restaurant.name: Canada Cafe
restaurant.desc: Canada Cafe is a restaurant in Merritt, BC offering dining for local patrons and travelers. Limited amenity details are available, but the business is confirmed to be operating and accessible by phone for inquiries.

restaurant.name: Lido Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Lido Restaurant (麗都餐廳) is a Cantonese restaurant located in Richmond's Aberdeen area, a neighbourhood known for its concentration of authentic Hong Kong-style dining. It operates as a cash-only establishment, which is worth noting for cyclists who may need to plan ahead. The restaurant offers a traditional dim-sum and Cantonese menu in a community-oriented setting.

restaurant.name: Quesada
restaurant.desc: Quesada Burritos & Tacos is a Canadian fast-casual Mexican chain with locations across BC and the rest of Canada. The North Vancouver outpost on Lonsdale Avenue serves burritos, tacos, quesadillas, and nachos with customizable toppings including house-made guacamole and pickled red onions. It is a takeout-friendly stop well positioned along the Lonsdale corridor for cyclists passing through North Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Chalo Momo Nepali Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Chalo Momo is a quick-casual Nepali kitchen serving traditional momos, Indo-Chinese noodles, tandoori dishes, and fusion items made fresh to order. The kitchen highlights its Nepali roots while offering a broad menu of vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-friendly options. Located in a Clearbrook Road strip mall in Abbotsford, it offers dine-in and online takeout ordering.

restaurant.name: Noma Sushi Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Noma Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in the Willoughby Town Centre shopping complex in Langley. The restaurant offers online ordering and takeout options, providing a convenient food stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

detail.address: C120-20678 Willoughby Town Centre Drive, Langley

restaurant.name: PappaRoti
restaurant.desc: PappaRoti is a Vancouver outpost of a Malaysian-origin cafe chain celebrated for its signature coffee-caramel buns — a soft, buttery roti with a crisp coffee crust born from a family recipe in Malaysia around 2000. Situated on Robson Street in Vancouver's West End, it sits close to the Stanley Park seawall cycling corridor. The cafe offers both indoor and outdoor seating and has grown to multiple BC locations.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu items (coffee-caramel buns with salted butter) are inherently vegetarian. No vegan or GF claims found on website

restaurant.name: Angel Cake Cafe
restaurant.desc: Angel Cake Cafe is a restaurant located on Fraser Street in Vancouver. It accepts cash payments only. Additional business details are unavailable due to website connectivity issues.

restaurant.name: Part and Parcel
restaurant.desc: Part and Parcel is a neighbourhood restaurant in Victoria's Quadra Village that has been cooking for its community since 2013, known for seasonal small plates, creative cocktails, and low-intervention wines sourced from small producers. The kitchen works closely with Vancouver Island growers and changes the menu with the seasons, offering everything from a quick lunch sandwich at the bar to a multi-course sharing feast at dinner. Walk-ins are welcome at the bar, making it an approachable stop for a cyclist wanting a quality, unhurried meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Private events page states: 'We work with dietary restrictions (vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, and allergies) with at least 24 hours notice.' Menu also lists vegetarian items such as the charred broccoli sandwich and seasonal vegetable plates

restaurant.name: Mercado Mexican Market & Taqueria
restaurant.desc: Mercado Mexican Market & Taqueria is a Coquitlam outpost of the Restco restaurant group, combining a Mexican grocery market stocked with salsas and ready-to-cook essentials with a quick-service counter. Cyclists can fuel up on street-style tacos, burritos, quesadillas, and salad bowls made with family-rooted recipes, with several vegetarian and plant-based protein choices. The business also offers catering and wholesale products, and is part of a wider network of Mexican concepts across the Tri-Cities and Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a 'VEGETARIAN' protein option (black bean, avocado, cheese, pico & sour cream) and two plant-based proteins: Rajas con Queso and Champiñones al Ajillo

restaurant.name: Convivial Café and Bakery
restaurant.desc: A small neighbourhood café and scratch bakery on the Vancouver seawall at Leg In Boot Square, a few minutes west of the Cambie Street Bridge. Convivial bakes everything fresh on-site throughout the day — from triple chocolate cookies and cheese-jalapeño scones to handmade artisan loaves — and serves rotating daily soups, toasted sandwiches, and espresso-based drinks. The café has a strong community focus, outdoor seating, and is a natural pit stop for cyclists riding the seawall.

detail.address: 680A Leg In Boot Square, Vancouver, BC V5Z 4B4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian options: vegetarian chili, miso roasted broccoli soup, a range of savory vegetarian scones (cheese jalapeño, four cheese, tomato basil parmesan, etc.), and a vegetarian sandwich (Sincronizada). No explicit vegan or gluten-free claims found

restaurant.name: The Fernwood Inn
restaurant.desc: The Fernwood Inn is a community gathering place anchoring Fernwood Square in one of Victoria's oldest and most colourful neighbourhoods, serving artisan pub fare, locally-sourced organic ingredients, wild seafood, and Island microbrews. The property includes a sunny patio and a dedicated Art/Band Room that hosts live music, open mics, quiz nights, and group events. It sits directly across from the Belfry Theatre and Victoria High School, making it a lively neighbourhood landmark.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website (/whoweare/) states 'fresh and healthy options (including gluten-free)'; menu page notes salads and light bites alongside pub comfort food

restaurant.name: Crow & Gate English Pub
restaurant.desc: The Crow & Gate holds the distinction of being BC's first neighbourhood pub, having opened in 1972 in rural Yellow Point south of Nanaimo. Its Tudor-style architecture and sprawling English gardens attract visitors from around the world, and well-behaved leashed dogs are welcome on the patio. The pub even fields helicopter landings on its back field during good weather, hinting at the kind of off-the-beaten-path character a touring cyclist will appreciate.

detail.address: 2313 Yellow Point Road, Nanaimo, British Columbia V9X 1W5, Canada

restaurant.name: Tong Fei
restaurant.desc: Tong Fei is a Chinese restaurant in Chilliwack serving the local community. It provides a sit-down dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area. Contact the restaurant directly for current menu and operational details.

restaurant.name: Second Slice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Second Slice Pizza is a late-night pizza counter on Douglas Street in downtown Victoria, built around fresh multigrain dough made daily and an extensive by-the-slice menu. It offers classic, gourmet, and vegetarian pies alongside a 'take & bake' option for those with access to an oven. Its central location and very late closing hours make it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists finishing a long day in the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian pizzas: Superb Veggie (tomato sauce, green peppers, onions, mushrooms, black olives, tomatoes, mozzarella), Greek Pizza, and Pesto Fiesta. No explicit vegan or gluten-free options mentioned

restaurant.name: Villa Rosa
restaurant.desc: Villa Rosa Ristorante is one of Penticton's most established Italian restaurants, open at the same Westminster Avenue location since 1996 and under current owners Tyler and Nicole Gable since 2007. The grapevine-covered patio with twinkle lights was recognized by OpenTable among Canada's 100 best for outdoor dining, and the kitchen leans heavily on fresh local Okanagan produce. Voted best Italian in the South Okanagan, it is a well-regarded dinner stop in the heart of Penticton's cycling corridor.

detail.address: 795 Westminster Ave West, Penticton, BC V2A 1K9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels gluten-free items (e.g. 'VR Caprese (GF)'); multiple vegetarian-compatible Italian dishes visible on menu

restaurant.name: Masala Junction
restaurant.desc: Masala Junction is a family-owned Indian restaurant founded in 2013, drawing on over 25 years of culinary experience across India and Europe. The menu spans tandoori specialties, biryanis, curries, Indo-Chinese dishes, desi street food, and a range of house-made Indian sweets. Catering is available for weddings, corporate events, and private parties.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian Specialities' section plus multiple vegetarian appetizers (Vegetable Samosa, Aloo Tikki, Vegetable Pakora, Gobi Pakora, Onion Bhaji, Paneer Pakora, etc.)

restaurant.name: Bubble World Tea House
restaurant.desc: Bubble World Tea House is a bubble tea and tea shop cafe on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. It provides tea-based beverages as a casual refreshment option. Touring cyclists passing through the area can stop here for a drink and rest.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A 24/7 McDonald's fast food location in Chilliwack on DeLair Road, offering burgers, chicken, McCafé beverages, and a full drive-through. As a round-the-clock restaurant, it can serve touring cyclists at any hour needing a hot meal, snack, or caffeine fix. The location is part of the Canadian McDonald's chain with takeout and drive-through service confirmed.

restaurant.name: Ricky's Country Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Ricky's Country Restaurant is a sit-down family-style diner operating under the ABC Country Restaurants brand, a chain known for comfort-food classics and a homey atmosphere. The Mission-area location sits along a highway corridor that touring cyclists on the Fraser Valley route may pass through. The chain emphasises fresh ingredients and generous portions in a relaxed, all-day dining setting.

restaurant.name: Happy Noodle House
restaurant.desc: Happy Noodle House is a compact, casual Chinese noodle restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's downtown core, specializing in handmade noodles — including Dan Dan Noodles and Lanzhou beef soup noodles — alongside dim sum and small plates. The atmosphere is unpretentious and neighborhood-friendly, with friendly, efficient service and generous portions that draw both locals and visitors. For touring cyclists passing through central Vancouver, it offers a solid fuel stop with both dine-in and takeout options on a well-connected transit corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists 'Serves vegetarian dishes' and mentions vegetable dumplings as a menu item

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast food restaurant in North Vancouver offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, fries, and McCafé beverages. The location includes a drive-through lane alongside a dine-in option, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area. As a well-known chain with consistent service, it provides a reliable spot to refuel on longer rides.

restaurant.name: Burnaby Mountain Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Burnaby Mountain Restaurant is a city-operated sit-down dining venue at Burnaby Mountain, a popular recreational hub with hiking and cycling trails overlooking the Lower Mainland. It is managed by Burnaby Hospitality alongside several other restaurants and event venues across Burnaby, and the mountain setting makes it one of the few full-service restaurant options near the summit. For cyclists who climb Burnaby Mountain — a well-known local challenge — this is a natural mid-ride or post-ride destination.

restaurant.name: Barley Mill
restaurant.desc: Barley Mill Brew Pub is a Penticton institution operating since 1982 in a distinctive Tudor-style building, with its own craft brewery producing house beers since 1997. The pub offers both indoor seating and a misted outdoor patio designed for hot Okanagan afternoons, plus a family-friendly upstairs bistro. Touring cyclists will find a full hearty menu spanning wings and flatbreads to steaks and ribs, alongside a lineup of in-house craft ales.

detail.address: 2460 Skaha Lake Rd, Penticton, BC V2A 6E9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels Gluten Free items (e.g. Nachos Extravaganza, Apple Cranberry Spinach Salad) and Gluten Friendly items (Dry Ribs, Potato Skins, Spinach Dip); vegetarian options include Mediterranean Flatbread, Veggies & Dip, and Spinach Dip. Vegan not explicitly stated

restaurant.name: Mario's Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Mario's Kitchen is a family-owned Italian restaurant in Tsawwassen operated by Liz and Darren Gates, serving fresh food, wine, and craft beers in a fun, welcoming neighbourhood atmosphere. The restaurant also operates an adjacent venue, Gracie's Next Door, which hosts live music on weekends and offers cocktails and craft beer in a relaxed setting. The kitchen runs brunch through dinner service with rotating weekly specials and online ordering with local delivery.

notes.Takeout: Website prominently features 'ORDER NOW' button and states 'We offer FREE DELIVERY on local orders when you spend $75 or more', confirming online ordering and takeout/delivery service

restaurant.name: Pokay
restaurant.desc: A sushi restaurant in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighborhood offering takeout service. Limited information is available on cyclist-specific amenities due to website access issues.

restaurant.name: Peace Country Delite
restaurant.desc: Peace Country Delite is a local coffee shop located in Fort St. John, in the heart of British Columbia's Peace Country region in the province's northeast. Situated on 100 Avenue, it serves as a stop for travellers passing through this hub community on the Alaska Highway corridor. Cyclists making their way through Fort St. John on long-distance routes would find it a convenient spot for a hot drink.

restaurant.name: Shiok Canteen
restaurant.desc: Shiok is a Singapore-inspired canteen that transplanted hawker-style cuisine to the Lower Mainland in 2019, founded by a family for whom food and the kitchen table are central to life. The name itself is Singaporean slang meaning 'delicious' or 'highly enjoyable,' and the menu reflects a genuine home-cooking ethos rather than a generic pan-Asian concept. Cyclists will find a sit-down restaurant with both indoor and outdoor seating and the option to order online for pickup.

restaurant.name: Gill Veggie Bakery & Pizza
restaurant.desc: Gills Vegetarian Bakery is a 100% vegetarian bakery and pizza shop located in Chilliwack, BC, operating from unit 107 of a commercial building. The establishment offers plant-based baked goods and pizza under the registered name Gill Veggie Bakery & Pizza Ltd. Touring cyclists looking for vegetarian food options in Chilliwack may find this a useful stop.

detail.address: 107-32883 South Fraser Way, Abbotsford, BC V2S 2A6

restaurant.name: Bamboo Express
restaurant.desc: Bamboo Express is a Chinese takeout and delivery restaurant serving Cantonese-style dishes in Richmond's Blundell Centre. The menu spans classics like Sweet & Sour Pork, Chow Mein, and Beef with Broccoli, with multi-person dinner combination sets and a dedicated Vegetarian Special section. Cyclists stopping in Richmond's suburban south end will find it a reliable quick-service option with free delivery within 5 km for larger orders.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists a dedicated 'Vegetarian Special' section. No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Booster Juice
restaurant.desc: Booster Juice is a Canadian fast-casual juice and smoothie chain with a location in Kamloops' Lansdowne Street commercial corridor. The menu centres on freshly blended smoothies, cold-pressed juices, açai bowls, and grab-and-go snacks designed for health-conscious customers on the move. A touring cyclist can stop here for a quick, portable nutrition boost without a long wait.

notes.Takeout: Corporate website confirms counter-service grab-and-go model with no dine-in emphasis

restaurant.name: Bozzini's Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Bozzini's has been a Chilliwack fixture since April 1982, drawing roughly 100,000 guests a year with an eclectic, largely house-made menu spanning half-pound burgers, AAA steaks cut in-house, pastas, seafood, souvlaki, and more — including the restaurant's own Caesar dressing and BBQ sauce unchanged since opening day. The no-gimmicks, no-coupons philosophy reflects a decades-long confidence in straightforward quality at fair value. An intimate upstairs lounge regularly hosts live music acts, making it a natural choice for a post-ride evening meal and show.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Group menu explicitly labels 'Baked Lasagne with Meat Sauce or Marinara (vegetarian)' as a vegetarian option

restaurant.name: Ana's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Ana's Pizza is a pizza restaurant located in Coldstream, BC. Limited information is available due to website unavailability.

detail.address: 2090 Norris Ave, Lumby, BC V0E 2G0, Canada

restaurant.name: Admiral Pub
restaurant.desc: A pub located on Hastings Street in Burnaby with indoor seating. No additional details about amenities or cyclist services are available.

restaurant.name: Pho Quynh Express
restaurant.desc: Pho Quynh Express (Yaletown) is one of three Vancouver locations of a Vietnamese noodle chain serving pho, vermicelli bowls, rice dishes, and spring rolls, with menu items in Vietnamese, English, and Chinese. The Yaletown outpost sits on Pacific Boulevard and offers both dine-in and online pickup ordering. Its broad Southeast Asian menu — spanning Vietnamese, Thai, and Cambodian flavours — makes it a practical mid-ride fuel stop in a busy urban cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Hop & Vine
restaurant.desc: Hop & Vine is a long-established taphouse in Burnaby's Greystone Village near Burnaby Mountain Golf Course, with over 20 years as a community fixture. It features 24 rotating draught lines and one of the largest craft beer selections in the area, alongside a food menu built around fresh, local, and sustainable ingredients well beyond typical pub fare. Cyclists exploring the Burnaby Mountain trails will find a warm, lively atmosphere and a full menu of scratch-made food and drink. Note that this is a 19+ venue with no minors permitted.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu notes '*Spuds are Gluten Free' for the hand-cut fries option

restaurant.name: Pizza Pizzria
restaurant.desc: Pizza Pizzeria is a neighborhood fast-food spot in Burnaby's East 10th corridor serving a fusion of classic and Indian-influenced pizzas alongside a full Indian menu. Cyclists will find an unusually diverse selection ranging from Butter Chicken and Butter Paneer pizzas to palak dishes, samosas, mango lassi, and masala tea. The blend of quick-service pizza and hearty Indian comfort food offers practical refueling choices for riders with varied dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists a dedicated Vegetarian pizza, vegetarian samosa, and explicitly states 'Gluten- and dairy-free options available' for the Palak Chana dish

restaurant.name: Pizza 73
restaurant.desc: Pizza 73 is a Western Canadian pizza chain founded in Edmonton in 1985, now operating over 85 locations across the region, with this Fort St. John outlet serving the northeastern BC community. The menu centers on customizable pizzas with 21 specialty options, multiple crust styles, and a broad array of toppings and sauces, along with wings, sides, and dips. Touring cyclists passing through Fort St. John can pick up a substantial takeout meal with dietary-friendly options including gluten-free, keto, and cauliflower crusts, as well as vegan cheese.

A touring cyclist arriving for dinner would find a warm, convivial sit-down experience on Kingsway celebrating fresh, regional cooking in a lively neighbourhood setting.

restaurant.name: Continuum Coffee Roasters

restaurant.name: Innocent Ice Cream Parlour

The shop crafts hand-made ice cream sandwiches, milkshakes, cones, and soda floats entirely in-store year-round, with plant-based and non-dairy options available. Beyond the storefront, Innocent also operates a solar-powered ice cream truck and a pink tricycle for catering events across the city.

restaurant.name: The Orca Inn

It offers oceanview rooms, suites with kitchenettes, a restaurant, and a pub with live music overlooking Johnstone Strait. Alert Bay is a compelling destination for First Nations culture and orca whale watching, making this inn a natural base for cyclists exploring British Columbia's remote north coast.

restaurant.name: El Caracol Mexican Cafe
restaurant.desc: El Caracol Mexican Cafe is a sit-down Mexican restaurant located on Victoria Drive in Vancouver's Sunset neighbourhood. The Victoria Drive corridor is a well-travelled cycling route connecting south Vancouver to the city centre, making this cafe a convenient stop for riders coming from or heading toward Fraserview and Champlain Heights. As a neighbourhood cafe with regular hours, it offers a full-service dining experience in an area with relatively few comparable options.

restaurant.name: Amogha Indian Kitchen & Bar
restaurant.desc: Amogha Indian Kitchen & Bar is a full-service Indian restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street built around twelve distinct regional cuisines — from Hyderabadi dum biryani to Malabar moilee — developed after two years of research across the subcontinent. The kitchen pairs regionally-specific cooking with a craft cocktail bar built on Indian aromatics like tamarind, cardamom, and saffron. With 80 seats and a menu extensively marked for dietary preferences, it is a substantial dining stop for cyclists riding the Main Street corridor.

restaurant.name: J&J Wonton Noodle House

A distinctive glassed-in kitchen lets diners watch chefs at work, and the extensive menu ranges from wonton noodle soups to Sichuan specialties. Vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options are well-represented, making it a practical and satisfying stop for cyclists with varied dietary needs.

restaurant.name: Ancora

restaurant.name: Samurai Sushi on Fraser

restaurant.name: Viet Flavour Restaurant

restaurant.name: Mr Pickwick's Fish & Chips

restaurant.name: Country Vines Winery

The winery hosts live music throughout the summer season and is proudly pet- and family-friendly.

restaurant.name: T-Bay Bistro
restaurant.desc: T-Bay Bistro is a noodle restaurant situated on Granville Street near the Marpole neighbourhood of Vancouver. OSM records it as an active restaurant as of mid-2024. Cyclists riding the Granville corridor would find it a convenient stop for a hot noodle meal.

restaurant.name: Ross Bay Pub
restaurant.desc: Ross Bay Pub is a cozy neighborhood pub on Fairfield Road in Victoria, tucked close to the Dallas Road waterfront and the Fairfield and Oak Bay neighborhoods. It offers food, drinks, daily specials, and community events, positioning itself as a local gathering spot. The location makes it a convenient stop for cyclists exploring the scenic coastal routes of Victoria's south shore.

restaurant.name: Delicado's
restaurant.desc: Delicado's is a funky, high-energy southwestern cafe and deli known for freshly made wraps, burritos, enchiladas, and homemade soups prepared daily on the premises. The Nanaimo North location is one of several BC franchises offering both dine-in and takeout, with a mini-market stocked with specialty hot sauces, salsas, and oil-free hummus. It's a solid stop for cyclists wanting a filling, colourful meal with plenty of vegetarian-friendly options.

restaurant.name: John's Place
restaurant.desc: John's Place is a beloved Victoria institution that has been serving scratch-made breakfast and lunch for over 40 years from its downtown Pandora Avenue location. A touring cyclist rolling into Victoria will find a relaxed, diner-style room and hearty Canadian comfort fare to fuel the next leg.

restaurant.name: Paragon Pizza

restaurant.name: Otaru Japanese Kitchen

restaurant.name: Nonna's Cucina Pop-up

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza

restaurant.name: Japanese Bistro Kamome

Touring cyclists can combine a meal stop here with a stroll through some of the most spectacular gardens in the Victoria region.

restaurant.name: Dosa Crepe Cafe

restaurant.name: Cannery Café

restaurant.name: Shanzee's Biscuit Café

Located in Victoria's Old Town area on Pandora Avenue, the café features outdoor seating.

restaurant.name: Unique Green

restaurant.name: Tino's Pizza

Cyclists can eat in or grab a carry-out order from a full menu of pizzas, pastas, and salads.

restaurant.name: The Oxy Pub

restaurant.name: Starbucks

restaurant.name: Kernels Popcorn

A touring cyclist stopping here can grab a quick snack to go while the mall's broader services are also accessible.

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza

restaurant.name: Lee's Donuts

restaurant.name: Panago

restaurant.name: Zenya
