restaurant.name: Hanaya Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Hanaya Japanese Restaurant is a Japanese sushi and dining restaurant in Surrey, BC, in operation since at least 2004. It offers dine-in, online ordering, and delivery, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking for a full sit-down Japanese meal. The restaurant is wheelchair accessible and accepts credit and debit cards.

restaurant.name: King's Kitchen
restaurant.desc: King's Kitchen is a restaurant located in Maple Ridge. The business website is currently under development and does not yet provide information about the establishment.

restaurant.name: Donnellan's Irish Pub
restaurant.desc: Donnellan's Irish Pub is an authentic Irish-themed bar in Vancouver's Granville Entertainment District, known for live music and DJs every weekend and a hearty Irish menu anchored by what the pub bills as the best pint of Guinness in the city. The venue includes a second-floor Balcony event space with its own private bar for up to 60 guests, as well as a large open-plan main bar with a stage, pool table, and dart boards. Part of the IRL Group, Donnellan's also hosts a monthly newcomer networking event and has been featured in several local media outlets as a community hub.

restaurant.name: The Coconut
restaurant.desc: The Coconut is a South Indian restaurant in downtown Kamloops helmed by Chef Lalichan Joseph, whose background cooking aboard cruise lines shapes his commitment to quality and technique. The menu spans the regional breadth of South India — dosas, coconut curries, tandoori dishes, and street-food favourites — made with locally sourced west coast ingredients. Touring cyclists get a warm reception, with a customer-praised bike parking spot right out front and an extensive vegetarian menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Customer review notes 'Lots of vegetarian options!!'; menu lists numerous vegetarian dishes including Veg Pakoras, Veg Samosa, Garden Veg Salad, Idily, Pav Bhaji, Vada Pav, Chole Bhature, and Chilli Paneer Pizza

restaurant.name: BarBurrito
restaurant.desc: BarBurrito is a Canadian fast-casual burrito chain founded in 2005 and now operating 385+ locations across the country. The Abbotsford West Oak location serves customizable burritos, bowls, tacos, and quesadillas made with fresh, in-house ingredients and a wide range of proteins. A touring cyclist looking for a quick, filling, customizable meal on South Fraser Way would find this a reliable stop.

detail.address: 32700 South Fraser Way, Unit 29, Abbotsford, BC V2T 4M5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website nutrition pages list 'Veggie Ground' and 'Falafel' protein options, and a 'Gluten Free' tortilla option for burritos and quesadillas

restaurant.name: Me Coffee&Tea
restaurant.desc: Me Coffee&Tea (覓Me) is a bubble tea café situated in the busy Number 3 Road retail corridor in Richmond, a hub of the city's vibrant Chinese-Canadian food scene. The shop offers takeaway service, positioning it as a quick hydration stop for cyclists moving through Richmond's commercial centre. Its Chinese-language name and bubble tea focus reflect the cultural character of the surrounding neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Umi Sushi Express
restaurant.desc: Umi Sushi Express is a quick-service Japanese cuisine franchise operating over 30 locations across Canada, offering fresh sushi and related dishes for customers on the go. The Burnaby outlet on Kingsway is a takeout-only counter with no on-site seating, making it a grab-and-go stop for cyclists passing through the corridor. It is one of three banner formats in the Umi family, focused on fresh, healthy Japanese food made with care.

restaurant.name: Omni Kitchen + Bar
restaurant.desc: Omni Kitchen + Bar is a lively full-service restaurant and bar in historic Fort Langley serving smashed burgers, Neapolitan-style pizzas, brunch, and creative cocktails. The venue is deeply community-oriented, hosting weekly Open Mic nights, ticketed Mixology Showcases, and watch parties for major sporting events. It also operates a food truck and catering service, making it a versatile stop for group rides or events passing through the Fraser Valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'plant-based, dairy-free or gluten-free dining' is available and 'everything on our menu can be made the way you like it'; menu lists gluten-free crust option for pizzas and GF modifications on multiple items

restaurant.name: Aroma Indian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Aroma Indian Restaurant is an award-winning fine-dining Indian restaurant in Port Moody, operated by chef CM Bhatt whose recipes were developed in India's 5-star hotels and refined over 26 years. The restaurant has been recognized with multiple Yelp business excellence awards and was repeatedly voted a favourite for Indian food in the Tri-City News A-List contest. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down dining experience with an extensive menu of both meat and vegetarian dishes, plus live music on weekends.

detail.address: Unit 101 - 3003 Saint Johns Street, Port Moody, BC V3H 2C4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'extensive menu of meat and vegetarian dishes'

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Freshslice Pizza is a BC-based pizza chain known for by-the-slice and whole-pie sales with any toppings, available for in-store pickup or delivery. The Vancouver location sits at level 0 with indoor seating and no drive-through. The chain also offers a gluten-free cauliflower crust, making it a flexible quick-stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Nutritional info page lists 'Gluten Free Cauliflower' crust and multiple vegetarian toppings (mushrooms, peppers, spinach, olives, etc.); veggie pizza is a named menu option

restaurant.name: Ki Isu Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A Japanese restaurant located in downtown Vancouver with both indoor and outdoor seating options. Offers casual dining for touring cyclists seeking a substantial meal break.

restaurant.name: Threefold Tasting Lounge
restaurant.desc: Threefold is a brewery collective that brings together three craft breweries — Temporal Artisanal Ales, Boombox, and Slow Hand — under one roof on Powell Street in East Vancouver. The tasting lounge pairs rotating craft beers on tap with a full Neapolitan-style pizza menu plus snacks and desserts. It offers a relaxed, food-forward taproom experience with a strong selection of vegetarian and vegan options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels items: (vg) vegetarian (e.g. Margherita, Mushroom Bianca), (v) vegan (e.g. Vegan Hawaiian, Vegan Sausage & Mushroom, Vegan Ice Cream), and (g/f) gluten-free (e.g. Castelvetrano olives, Chips and Dip, Vegan Ice Cream)

restaurant.name: Great Dane Coffee
restaurant.desc: Great Dane Coffee is a family-run cafe on the UBC campus, founded in 2012 by mother-and-son team Toni and Andrew, built around house-made food and locally sourced ingredients including Brightside Beans espresso. The shop bakes its own focaccia bread for a range of sandwiches and produces daily pastries such as scones, cinnamon buns, and croissants. Set beside Gage Towers with a patio and large windows, it offers an off-the-beaten-track feel along with online ordering for quick pickup.

detail.address: 6011 Walter Gage Road, Vancouver, BC V6T0B4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated Veggie sandwich (grilled zucchini, cucumber, tomato, pickled cabbage, bocconcini, arugula, hummus, balsamic reduction on house-baked focaccia)

restaurant.name: Fufú Café
restaurant.desc: Fufú Café is a Japanese-inspired dessert café on West Broadway in Vancouver, known for its signature soufflé pancakes in both sweet and savory varieties. The menu also features Japanese-style sandos (sandwiches), espresso drinks, matcha beverages, and seasonal specialty sodas. It's a sit-down café that also offers online ordering for pickup and delivery.

detail.address: 1266 West Broadway, Vancouver, British Columbia V6H 1G6, Canada

restaurant.name: Coffee Central Roasting
restaurant.desc: Coffee Central Roasting bills itself as Vancouver's first coffee roasting commissary — a fully permitted, shared roastery where clients book time to roast their own batches and train with industry experts on machines, Cropster software, and coffee science. It also offers access to small-lot specialty green coffees imported seasonally, and a fully equipped coffee bar for cupping and team training sessions. Access is by appointment, making it a destination for coffee professionals and enthusiasts rather than a drop-in café.

restaurant.name: Megabite
restaurant.desc: Megabite is a Vancouver-based pizza franchise with several Lower Mainland locations, including this one on Granville Street in the heart of the city's entertainment district. The menu spans pizza, wings, poutine, and sides, with online ordering, delivery, and a catering service. Vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options are available, making it a practical food stop for groups with mixed dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website catering page explicitly mentions 'Vegetarian and meat pizzas' among menu options

restaurant.name: JJ Bean
restaurant.desc: JJ Bean is a Vancouver-based independent specialty coffee roaster with cafés across Metro Vancouver, founded in 1996 by the Neate family and repeatedly voted Vancouver's best. This location at Big Bend in Richmond serves freshly roasted espresso and drip coffee alongside house-made baked goods and an all-day breakfast and lunch menu. JJ Bean sources high-quality single-origin and blended coffees roasted daily in small batches at their Powell Street roastery.

detail.address: 8288 North Fraser Way, Unit 101, Richmond, BC

restaurant.name: Tera V Burger
restaurant.desc: Tera V Burger is an all-vegan fast-casual restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver, specializing in plant-based burgers, loaded bowls, fries, and shakes — with every menu item fully vegan rather than just vegan-optional. It offers dine-in with reservations, takeaway, and home delivery, making it a flexible stop for cyclists passing through the Kitsilano–Point Grey corridor. Reviewers consistently praise the bold flavors and welcoming atmosphere, noting the food impresses even committed meat-eaters.

detail.address: 2961 W Broadway, Vancouver, BC V6K 2G9, Canada

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website describes entire menu as plant-based/vegan ('every single item thoughtfully crafted to deliver a premium plant-based experience')

restaurant.name: Kocomo's
restaurant.desc: Kocomo's is a coffee house cafe in Grand Forks offering espresso and coffee beverages. The business features Wi-Fi access and maintains an outdoor smoking area, making it a potential rest stop for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Kaede Sushi
restaurant.desc: Kaede Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Kelowna offering a full menu of sushi rolls, nigiri, sashimi, and cooked Japanese dishes alongside housemade desserts. The kitchen draws on Japanese culinary traditions with items like mozuku seaweed from Okinawa and house-crafted mochi ice cream. Touring cyclists will find a broad menu with plentiful vegetarian options and takeout available by phone.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes dedicated vegetarian items: Veggie Roll, Veggie Tempura, Veggie Kushiage, Agedashi Tofu, Tofu Steak, Tofu Dengaku, Edamame, Kinpira, and more

restaurant.name: Macchiato Caffe
restaurant.desc: Macchiato Caffe is a locally owned Italian-inspired café that has been a downtown Victoria fixture for nearly two decades, operating at the Johnson Street address as 'Macchiato @ The Juliet'. The café serves artisan espresso from Caffe Umbria — a third-generation family roaster based in Vancouver — alongside freshly made panini, salads, soups, and baked goods prepared on-site daily. Both downtown locations offer comfortable indoor seating and an outdoor patio, making them a natural mid-ride stop in the heart of Victoria's Old Town.

restaurant.name: Joey
restaurant.desc: JOEY is a family-owned upscale casual dining chain operating since 1992, with locations across Canada and the US. Each restaurant is custom-built with a distinct design and serves a globally inspired menu of handcrafted dishes and cocktails developed by a team of Executive Chefs. The Kelowna outpost sits along Highway 97, making it a recognizable stop on one of the Okanagan's main cycling corridors.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast food location on Kingsway in Vancouver, offering burgers, chicken, McCafé beverages, and a full breakfast menu. It is an indoor-seating location with no drive-through, positioned on a major arterial road that cycling routes frequently cross. As a 24/7 operation per OSM, it could serve as an around-the-clock food stop for touring cyclists passing through Burnaby/Vancouver.

restaurant.name: The Ramen Butcher
restaurant.desc: The Ramen Butcher serves authentic Hakata-style tonkotsu ramen in Vancouver's Chinatown, with chefs trained in Japan through the parent Menya Kouji Group. Everything — noodles, gyoza, and rice bowls — is handmade daily, and the menu spans classic tonkotsu, tsukemen, miso, and vegetarian broths. The Chinatown location is a takeout-friendly stop in a dense, walkable neighbourhood.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes 'Vegetarian' ramen (creamy miso and soy milk broth with vegetables and shiitake), 'Vege Tantan' (soy milk broth with minced soy meat), and 'Vege Gyoza' (meat-free gyoza with matcha wrappers)

restaurant.name: Walnut Grove Pub & Liqour Store
restaurant.desc: A pub and liquor store in Langley, BC. Limited information is available due to the business website being non-functional.

restaurant.name: Bar Luna
restaurant.desc: Bar Luna is a Mexican cantina housed in a beautifully restored 1890s fire hall in downtown Nanaimo, offering bold-flavoured tacos, quesabirria, ceviche, and handcrafted mezcal cocktails with a West Coast twist. The heritage building gives the restaurant a distinctive character, though its original front steps make wheelchair access challenging. It can accommodate groups up to 18 in its loft and up to 96 for private events, with catering available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms GF options (all taco shells are 100% organic corn; staff guide guests through GF menu) and vegan options ('we have a couple of options')

restaurant.name: Jerusalem Shwarma
restaurant.desc: Jerusalem Shawarma is a Palestinian-rooted family business serving shawarma, donair, falafel, hummus, and kababs on busy Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. The restaurant offers dine-in seating indoors alongside takeout and online ordering for pickup. It is part of a multi-location chain with roots in its founder's grandfather's village restaurant in Palestine, emphasizing fresh Mediterranean cuisine.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Homepage states 'We are famous for our Shawarma Donair Vegan or Vegetarian Kababs'; no GF claim found

restaurant.name: The Firewood Café
restaurant.desc: The Firewood Café is a family-owned Mount Pleasant institution that has been crafting hand-tossed, thin-crust pizzas in a firewood brick oven since 1989. Located at the corner of 14th and Cambie, it offers a broad menu of classic and creative pizzas alongside made-to-order pasta dishes. Cyclists can grab a quick pickup order or settle in at one of the small number of dine-in tables.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website has a dedicated 'VEGETARIAN PIZZAS' section including Classic Veggie, Greek, and Spanako options; no vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Med Grill Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Med Grill occupies a 100-year-old heritage building — the former Saanich Municipal Hall — in Royal Oak, just minutes from Downtown Victoria. Head chef Andrew Johnson crafts seasonal Mediterranean-inspired menus with west coast flair, served in a candlelit interior with a cozy fireplace or on a spacious wrap-around patio. The restaurant has been a local Victoria favourite since 1997 and features a rotating Tuscan Table three-course dinner alongside a rotating monthly menu.

restaurant.name: Joe Fortes
restaurant.desc: Joe Fortes Seafood & Chop House is a celebrated Vancouver institution operating for over 35 years, named after Seraphim 'Joe Fortes,' the city's first official lifeguard. The restaurant spans multiple distinctive spaces — a horseshoe oyster bar grand room, mezzanine with live music, mahogany-walled wine room, and a rooftop garden with a living green wall and outdoor fireplace. It is known for its daily-sourced Pacific Northwest seafood, 300-bottle award-winning wine list, and loyal following of locals, tourists, and celebrities.

restaurant.name: Yummy Slice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Yummy Slice Pizza is a Canadian-owned pizza-by-the-slice chain with a Richmond location on Number 1 Road, offering pickup and delivery seven days a week. The menu spans classic and signature pies including a broad range of vegetarian and South Asian-inspired options such as Tandoori Paneer and Yummy Potato. With multiple Lower Mainland locations and a catering program, it is a reliable quick-stop for a hot meal on a Richmond cycling route.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists multiple vegetarian pizzas: Veggie, Spinach Tomato Feta, Veggie Lovers, Greek, Garden Pesto, Yummy Veggie, Yummy Potato, Yummy Paneer, Tandoori Paneer, Creamy Corn. No vegan or GF options confirmed

restaurant.name: Hungry Guys Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Hungry Guys Kitchen is a downtown Vancouver fast food restaurant with two Granville Street locations, serving hand-crafted gourmet burgers, fries, shakes, salads, and build-your-own bowls made from locally sourced, fresh ingredients. Founded by entrepreneur Aldo Velaj, the concept emphasizes allergen-friendly customization and sustainable sourcing. The 988 Granville location has indoor seating and is wheelchair accessible, making it a comfortable urban refuelling stop for cyclists.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu offers tofu as a protein substitute across all build-your-own items, salads, and bowls, with multiple fully plant-based combinations available

restaurant.name: Kam Wai Dim Sum
restaurant.desc: Kam Wai Dim Sum is a family-run dim sum shop that has been a fixture of Vancouver's Chinatown since 1991, specializing in both frozen take-home dim sum classics and ready-to-eat takeaway items. The menu spans pork siu mai, wonton soup, BBQ pork bao, and vegan mushroom dumplings, with staff serving customers in English, Mandarin, and Cantonese. A second location (Kam Wai Legacy) now operates in the Hastings-Sunrise neighbourhood at 2285 E Hastings St.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'Vegan Mushroom Dumplings' (素三菇餃) explicitly as a menu item available frozen or ready-to-eat

restaurant.name: Boba Boy
restaurant.desc: Boba Boy is a bubble tea chain with locations across BC, Ontario, and the US, operated by Tea Shop 168 Group Inc. The South Surrey location sits in a strip unit on Highway 10 and distinguishes itself by producing tapioca in-store from fresh ingredients rather than using pre-manufactured pearls. Cyclists on the Highway 10 corridor can stop in for made-to-order boba drinks and place orders online for pickup.

restaurant.name: Swad Indian Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Swad Indian Kitchen is a family-owned North Indian restaurant on Marine Drive in West Vancouver, founded by Kamal Mroke who arrived from Punjab in the early 1980s and worked his way from dishwasher to restaurateur over 35 years. The menu spans aromatic curries, tandoori dishes, and street food classics, with strong vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free coverage. A private dining room with ocean views is available for groups, and free parking is provided at the rear of the building.

detail.address: 1734 Marine Dr, West Vancouver, BC V7V 1J3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Enjoy our wide selection of vegetarian and gluten-free dishes'; menu items individually marked (v) for vegetarian and (gf) for gluten-free; vegan options explicitly called out

restaurant.name: JanesTea
restaurant.desc: Jane's Tea Garden is a specialty tea shop in Richmond offering premium loose-leaf teas sourced from traditional Chinese tea-growing regions, alongside hand-crafted ceramic teaware. The shop operates both as an online retailer and a physical location where visitors can taste teas and explore Chinese tea culture in person. It is a niche destination for tea enthusiasts rather than a full-service café.

restaurant.name: Whitby's Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Whitby's Coffee House is a cafe and ice cream shop in Tsawwassen located on Marine Drive. It offers outdoor seating for patrons. The establishment serves local cyclists and travelers passing through the community.

restaurant.name: The Madras Diaries
restaurant.desc: The Madras Diaries is a South Indian and Indo-Chinese restaurant on Kingsway in Vancouver, drawing on the cuisines of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh with dishes like Chettinadu chicken, Mandhi biryani, and an extensive dosa menu. Clay pot preparations and regional specialties such as Kozhi Kuzambu and Gongura Lamb distinguish it from generic Indian restaurants. Online ordering with a quick pickup window makes it a practical fueling stop for cyclists passing through East Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated Vegetable Curries section (Dal Fry, Vegetable Stew, Palak Paneer, Mutter Paneer, Dal Makhni, etc.), Vegetable Biriyani, Plain Dosa, and multiple vegetable-based dosa and appetizer options

restaurant.name: Avik Bakery
restaurant.desc: AVIK is a tech-driven franchise specialty coffee shop on West Broadway offering espresso drinks crafted with beans from Moving Coffee Roastery, locally sourced high-grade teas, and artisanal pastries baked in-house daily. The brand blends a digital-first experience — including a mobile app with an order-ahead and rewards system — with a self-described fun, vibrant atmosphere. It sits in a busy urban neighbourhood convenient to cyclists travelling the Broadway corridor.

restaurant.name: Tsukiji Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Tsukiji Kitchen is a grab-and-go seafood kitchen and community hub on lower Lonsdale in North Vancouver, opened December 2025 and run by Takuya Hikita, a former Tsukiji Market auctioneer with a marine biology background and a mandate to promote sustainable BC seafood. The Ocean Wellness Bowls pair Japanese-sourced seaweed and salmon roe with locally sourced BC proteins such as salmon, shrimp, and scallop. The space also includes a coffee corner and a second-floor event room used for cultural programming and community gatherings.

detail.address: 228 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2G1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items (Ocean Wellness Bowls A, B, C) are labeled Gluten-Free and Dairy-Free on the menu page

restaurant.name: Mr. Pan Pizza
restaurant.desc: A fast-food pizzeria in Burnaby offering pizza with Indian-fusion options. Convenient for cyclists seeking quick meals on Canada Way.

restaurant.name: Pho Fresh
restaurant.desc: Phở Fresh is a family-owned Northern Vietnamese restaurant in Tsawwassen, Delta, founded in 2018 by a Vietnamese-Canadian engineer who spent 15+ hours daily simmering scratch-made bone broth in the Hanoi tradition. The clean, modern dining room is designed for a comfortable sit-down meal, and the restaurant also caters events and offers delivery through major apps. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a restorative, allergen-conscious bowl of phở made entirely from local BC ingredients where practical.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'We offer vegetarian options' and includes a vegan filter on the menu page. Homepage prominently notes '98% Gluten-Free'

restaurant.name: Cowichan Bay Pub
restaurant.desc: A pub serving the Cowichan Bay community on Vancouver Island's south coast. Offers casual food and drink service to locals and travelers. Website is currently under redesign but remains accessible via phone and social media.

detail.address: 1695 Cowichan Bay Rd, Cowichan Bay, BC V0R 1N0

restaurant.name: Il Greco Pizzeria & Kebab
restaurant.desc: Il Greco is a Greek and pizza restaurant located in Victoria's Gorge neighbourhood, operating as a takeout and delivery focused spot. With a gmail contact address and a compact unit-suite location, it has the feel of a neighbourhood quick-service restaurant rather than a sit-down destination. Cyclists passing through the Gorge Road corridor could use it as a pickup stop, though amenity details beyond takeout are unverified.

restaurant.name: Kiku Sushi
restaurant.desc: Kiku Sushi is a Japanese restaurant at Metrotown in Burnaby, one of two Lower Mainland locations, serving sushi, rolls, grilled entrees, noodles, and kitchen appetizers. The restaurant describes a large dining hall with a cozy interior and a broad menu designed to suit varied tastes. A touring cyclist riding the Kingsway corridor would find a full sit-down meal option here with online ordering also available.

restaurant.name: Social 242 Lounge & Grill
restaurant.desc: Social 242 Lounge & Grill is a full-service lounge and restaurant in downtown Kelowna offering wings in 26 flavours, AAA steaks, and a creative cocktail program with signature and seasonal drinks. The venue also features a dedicated vegan menu and gluten-free options throughout, catering to a wide range of dietary needs. Its central Lawrence Avenue location makes it a convenient food-and-drink stop for cyclists exploring the Okanagan.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated Vegan Menu subpage with multiple vegan dishes including Cauli Wings, Chickn' Parm, and Alfredo Mac N Cheeze. Main menu widely annotated with GFO (gluten free option available)

restaurant.name: D Spot Dessert Cafe
restaurant.desc: D Spot Dessert Café is a Canadian dessert franchise established in 2014, specializing in homemade ice cream, fresh waffles and crepes, Belgian chocolate creations, and savoury items. The Delta location is part of a growing national chain known for inventive, social-media-worthy desserts made with high-quality ingredients. All products are halal-certified and kosher, making this a broadly inclusive stop for cyclists seeking a sweet break.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms: 'We carry Gluten Free waffles, crepes and pancakes.' Dessert menu items are also confirmed halal and kosher; many items are inherently vegetarian

restaurant.name: Papa John's
restaurant.desc: Papa John's is a national pizza chain franchise located in a strip-mall unit in Langley, BC, offering takeout pizza. Touring cyclists passing through the area can pick up a ready-made or custom pizza order by phone or in person. No drive-through is available, making it a walk-in or call-ahead stop.

restaurant.name: Taku Japanese Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Taku Japanese Kitchen is a neighbourhood Japanese restaurant on Royal Oak Avenue in Burnaby, serving a sit-down menu in a no-smoking indoor dining room. With no outdoor seating, it offers a quieter indoor respite for cyclists passing through the Royal Oak corridor. It accepts Visa and Mastercard, making it a convenient cashless stop mid-ride.

restaurant.name: Mucho Burrito
restaurant.desc: Mucho Burrito is a Mexican fast-casual chain offering burritos, bowls, quesadillas, and tacos with what the brand calls a 'Modern Mexicana' twist. Located on Lansdowne Street in downtown Kamloops, it is a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the city's commercial core. Takeout and online ordering are available, making it a quick resupply option.

restaurant.name: Mishmish
restaurant.desc: Mishmish (مشمش, meaning 'apricot' in Arabic) is a third-culture Middle Eastern bakery and café on Fraser Street in Vancouver, founded in 2024 and named Vancouver Magazine's Best Bakery 2026. Chef/owners Abdallah El Chami and Leah Christ blend Lebanese, Iranian, German, and Canadian traditions into creations like the Baklava Cream Top and Mishmish Bar. The café features covered outdoor seating where dogs are welcome, and serves coffee from Modus Coffee and tea from Tea Sparrow.

restaurant.name: Baiyulan Shanghai Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Baiyulan Shanghai Cuisine is a sit-down Shanghainese restaurant in a Richmond strip mall, specializing in authentic dishes like Jelly Pork, Ham & Taro Soup, and Crispy Ginger Beef alongside a broad menu of specialty noodles, dim sum, and cold appetizers. The restaurant has built a loyal local following with 84 online reviews and caters to vegetarian diners. Cyclists can order online for pickup or delivery as well as dine in.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu legend explicitly includes vegetarian and vegan category markers; reviews note 'good vegetarian varieties' and 'They cook vegetarian options'

restaurant.name: The Dutch Bakery & Diner
restaurant.desc: The Dutch Bakery & Diner is a beloved Victoria institution on Fort Street, now celebrating 70 years of operation under three generations of the Dutch-immigrant Schaddelee family. The diner serves all-day breakfast and lunch including Dutch specialties like croquettes, burgers, omelettes, and salads, alongside an extensive selection of house-made pastries, cakes, cookies, and chocolates from the bakery counter. It's a characterful, old-fashioned stop in the heart of downtown Victoria with a loyal following and a long-tenured staff.

restaurant.name: Chen's Garden
restaurant.desc: Chen's Garden (operating as Chan's Garden) is a Chinese restaurant in New Westminster serving an extensive menu of Cantonese and Szechuan-inspired dishes, from Ginger Beef and Wonton Noodle Soup to stir-fried lamb and whole-category seafood selections. The restaurant offers indoor dine-in seating alongside a full online ordering system for pickup and delivery. With nearly 500 customer reviews, it is a well-established neighbourhood stop suited to refuelling a hungry touring cyclist.

detail.address: 441 E Columbia St, New Westminster, BC V3L 3X4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu legend explicitly marks vegetarian items; confirmed vegetarian dishes include Vegetarian Lettuce Wrap, Vegetable Spring Roll, Stir-Fried Vegetable, String Bean, and Broccoli with Garlic

restaurant.name: Pagliacci's
restaurant.desc: Pagliacci's is a Victoria institution that has been serving Italian-influenced comfort food since 1979, with housemade focaccia, pasta, fresh local seafood, and AAA Angus steaks. The restaurant claims the longest-running free live music program of any restaurant in Canada, with nightly performances spanning jazz, klezmer, and more. It operates on a no-reservations basis with a famously fast-moving queue, and is located in the heart of downtown Victoria.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lunch description mentions 'gluten-free rice bowls' as a menu item

restaurant.name: Ocean Palace
restaurant.desc: Ocean Palace is a long-established Chinese restaurant in the heart of Tsawwassen, serving authentic dishes for over 28 years with an emphasis on fresh ingredients and high standards. The extensive menu spans seafood, pork, poultry, beef, and vegetarian options, with popular items including special fried rice, chicken chow mein, and ginger beef. No-MSG preparation is available on request, and dinner combo packages cater to groups of varying sizes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian Delights & Vegetables' section and Vegetarian Egg Rolls are listed as a menu item

restaurant.name: Gramma's Marine Pub
restaurant.desc: Gramma's Marine Pub is a waterfront sports pub established in 1989 on the Lower Sunshine Coast, with an enclosed patio overlooking Shoal Channel, Keat's Island, and Gibsons Harbour. Originally BC's first licensed 'Marine Pub', the building has a colourful history stretching back to the early 1900s and still includes an attached cold beer and wine store. Cyclists will find a full scratch kitchen, a rotating selection of 10–12 draught taps featuring local Sunshine Coast breweries, and accessible street-level and waterfront seawall entrances.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Sunday pierogi special explicitly lists a vegan-friendly (vf) option and 'vegan Bratwurst' add-on on the weekly specials menu

restaurant.name: Perfecto Cafe
restaurant.desc: Perfecto Cafe is a Vancouver artisan cafe chain where every pastry, cake, sandwich, and gelato is made entirely from scratch in-house, with bakers starting at 5am daily and gelato crafted using techniques from the Carpigiani Gelato University in Italy. The Davie Street location is one of four, pairing a custom coffee blend developed exclusively with Agro Roasters alongside an ever-changing seasonal baked goods menu. Outdoor seating and a community-hub ethos make it a quality mid-ride refueling stop in the West End.

restaurant.name: The Hanoi Corner

restaurant.name: Papito's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Papito's Pizza is a local pizza restaurant that has been serving the Kettle Valley area for over 20 years, situated on the main Highway 97 corridor through Lake Country. The menu runs well beyond pizza — wings, pasta, poutine, salads, and a broad roster of specialty pies — making it a solid stop for a hot meal on a long ride. Online ordering and everyday take-out specials make it convenient for cyclists passing through.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists a dedicated 'Vegetarian' specialty pizza (mushrooms, onion, green pepper, olives, tomato) and a 'Gluten Free (Medium only)' crust add-on; dairy-free cheese is also listed as an available topping

restaurant.name: Kowloon Delight Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kowloon Delight Restaurant is a Cantonese cuisine spot in Richmond's McKim Way commercial area, serving a broad bilingual menu of Hong Kong-style dishes spanning dim sum, seafood casseroles, congee, and classic stir-fries. The extensive menu covers over 15 categories including steamed dim sum, rice rolls, and seasonal chef specials, with dishes presented in both English and traditional Chinese. Online pickup ordering is available directly through the restaurant's website.

restaurant.name: Church's Chicken
restaurant.desc: Church's Chicken (operating here as Church's Texas Chicken) is a fried chicken fast food chain with a Lower Mainland BC franchise presence. The Hastings Street location is one of roughly 19 outlets listed on the regional franchise website, serving hand-battered chicken meals, sandwiches, tenders, and Honey-Butter biscuits. It is a potential quick-stop option for touring cyclists on the East Hastings corridor.

restaurant.name: Goldie's
restaurant.desc: Goldie's Donuts & Bakery is a growing Lower Mainland chain specializing in Korean-inspired brioche donuts made with a 24-hour slow fermentation process for exceptional texture and flavour. The North Vancouver outpost offers inventive flavours like Matcha Cream and Mango Passion Fruit alongside signature drinks such as a Peanut Butter Cream Latte. Inspired by a golden retriever mascot, the shop aims for a warm, cozy atmosphere and also offers online pre-order pickup.

detail.address: 279 East 8th Street, North Vancouver City, V7L1Y9

restaurant.name: WELA Healthy Foods
restaurant.desc: WELA is a health-focused fast-casual restaurant at the Lonsdale Quay Market in North Vancouver, serving globally-inspired healthy bowls, wraps, smoothies, and cold-pressed juices rooted in a Thai philosophy of balance. Founded in 2019, it was designed to bridge the gap between convenience and nutritious eating, with a broad menu of vegan, gluten-free, and dairy-free options. Its location near the waterfront entrance of Lonsdale Quay, just a 1-minute walk from the Seabus Terminal, makes it a natural refueling stop for cyclists crossing between North Vancouver and downtown Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists multiple items marked Ⓥ (vegan) and GF (gluten-free), including Bangkok Bowl, Green Curry Bowl, Shroomami, Chilango, and Avocado/Falamus wraps. Smoothies described as 'all-natural, no-sugar added, and dairy-free.'

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: A Starbucks coffee shop with outdoor seating in Richmond. Offers free Wi-Fi and takeaway service, making it a useful rest stop for touring cyclists needing refreshment and connectivity.

notes.Wi-Fi: Free Wi-Fi (SSID: Starbucks Wifi, no fee)

restaurant.name: The Keefer Bar
restaurant.desc: The Keefer Bar is an apothecary-inspired cocktail bar located in the heart of Vancouver's historic Chinatown, recognized as the 2nd best bar in Canada three years running. It offers a menu of over 25 unique handcrafted cocktails drawing on fresh herbs, exotic spices, and homemade concoctions in a dark, moody atmosphere. It is a liquor-primary venue for guests 19 and older, making it a distinctive evening destination for cyclists exploring the city.

restaurant.name: Glass House Estate Winery
restaurant.desc: Glass House Estate Winery is a restaurant and bar in Township of Langley serving regional cuisine. The venue features outdoor seating and complimentary wireless internet for customers.

restaurant.name: BG Cafe
restaurant.desc: BG Cafe is a sandwich restaurant in Kamloops. Website access was unavailable, preventing detailed verification of amenities and services for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Wo Fung Noodle Express
restaurant.desc: Wo Fung Noodle Express is a Chinese noodle restaurant in Richmond specializing in Hong Kong-style cart noodles (車仔麵), a customizable dish where diners choose noodle type and toppings. The Cantonese name 和豐車仔麵 places it squarely in the tradition of this beloved Hong Kong street-food format. It sits in Richmond's densely food-rich Park Road corridor, convenient for cyclists exploring the city's extensive flat bike network.

restaurant.name: The Cake Workshop
restaurant.desc: The Cake Workshop is a bakery in Richmond with bilingual (English-Chinese) branding, serving a diverse community. As a specialized cake shop, it may appeal to touring cyclists seeking fresh baked goods.

restaurant.name: Nautical Nellies Steak & Seafood House
restaurant.desc: Nautical Nellies Steak & Seafood House has anchored Victoria's Inner Harbour waterfront since 1997, founded by Jeff and Betty Furneaux from Newfoundland with a focus on warm hospitality and premium ingredients. The restaurant is known for Ocean Wise-certified Pacific seafood, prime-aged steaks including a signature tomahawk, hand-rolled sushi, and daily brunch, served from a heated harbour-view patio or a cozy interior with original artwork by co-owner Jeff Furneaux. A live lobster and crab tank, an oyster bar with fresh shucking, and a Wine Spectator award-winning list of 165+ wines round out an experience that places it firmly among Victoria's most celebrated dining destinations.

restaurant.name: Pizza Twist
restaurant.desc: Pizza Twist is a fast-food pizza chain offering quick-service pizza dining. Located in Tsawwassen, it provides a quick meal option for travelers and local customers.

restaurant.name: Jang Mo Jib Restaurants
restaurant.desc: Jang Mo Jib Restaurants is a Korean restaurant (장모집 外母屋) located on Kingsway in Vancouver's busy commercial corridor. The name references a traditional Korean concept evoking home-style cooking. It offers indoor seating in a non-smoking environment.

restaurant.name: Breka Bakery & Café
restaurant.desc: Breka Bakery & Café is a Vancouver-born family business operating since 2006 with 8 locations across the city, each open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Originally rooted in a German bakery tradition in the Sunset neighbourhood, it has grown into a beloved local institution offering artisan breads, pastries, cakes, sandwiches, and hot beverages. The Main Street location is a reliable stop for touring cyclists at any hour, with a broad menu that includes explicitly labeled vegan and gluten-free items.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website has dedicated 'VEGAN' and 'GLUTEN-FREE' (labelled 'gluten friendly') menu sections with multiple explicitly tagged items including wraps, cakes, cookies, and muffins

restaurant.name: Quds Halal Noodle House
restaurant.desc: Quds Halal Noodle House is a halal-certified Chinese noodle restaurant in Richmond specializing in Lanzhou-style hand-pulled beef noodle soup, a regional Chinese staple rarely found in the Lower Mainland. The menu also includes cold dishes, BBQ dishes, and dinner specials, offering a substantial meal for hungry cyclists. Online ordering with pickup is available through the restaurant's own app-based platform.

restaurant.name: WAKAYAMA RAMEN
restaurant.desc: Wakayama Ramen is a ramen restaurant in Kamloops serving Japanese noodle dishes. It provides a sit-down dining venue for touring cyclists seeking a quick, filling meal.

restaurant.name: USSC Marina Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: An ice cream window located within the Union Steamship Co. Marina complex in Snug Cove, Bowen Island — a historic boutique marina resort just minutes from the ferry terminal. Cyclists arriving on Bowen Island by ferry would pass directly through Snug Cove, making this a natural first or last stop on any island ride. The broader marina complex also includes a boardwalk Company Store stocking local souvenirs and a well-stocked Chandlery.

detail.address: 431 Bowen Island Trunk Road, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G0

restaurant.name: Sushi Bar Maumi
restaurant.desc: Sushi Bar Maumi is a family-run, 17-seat counter restaurant on Robson Street specializing in traditional Edo-style omakase nigiri sushi — the first in Vancouver to offer this counter-based format focused solely on nigiri. Chef Maumi Ozaki brings over 33 years of experience, preparing each piece individually and serving it directly over the counter with fish imported daily from Japan. The restaurant has received Michelin recognition and emphasizes a quiet, respectful atmosphere centred on the flavours of authentic Japanese technique.

restaurant.name: Sushi Langford
restaurant.desc: Sushi Langford is a casual Japanese restaurant in Langford serving fresh sushi, rolls, sashimi, tempura, and noodle dishes made with a blend of Japanese ingredients and local products. Located in a strip mall on Millstream Road, it offers both lunch and dinner service and sits along cycling routes through the Westshore communities of Greater Victoria.

restaurant.name: Bold Knight Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Bold Knight Restaurant is a classic full-service steak and seafood house in Nanaimo, established in 1977 and voted Nanaimo's Best Steakhouse in 2025. The menu leans heavily into charbroiled cuts, fresh BC seafood, and surf-and-turf combinations, with a broad cocktail and wine list. It sits along the Trans-Canada Highway, making it a recognizable landmark for cyclists passing through the south Nanaimo corridor.

restaurant.name: Sanctuary Cafe
restaurant.desc: Sanctuary Cafe is a bike-friendly community coffee shop on the eastern edge of Steveston Village, deliberately positioned along a popular year-round cycling and running route in Richmond. Owner Tim Lee is an avid cyclist who has ridden iconic climbs in the Alps and Dolomites, and the cafe partners with local clubs Steveston Velo and Steveston Run Crew to foster a cycling and running community. The menu rotates BC-roasted coffees alongside artisan baked goods and hearty handhelds designed to fuel riders before, during, or after a ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu lists 'Power Breakfast (Vegan)' cookie and 'Southwestern Breakfast (Veg)' wrap, confirming vegan and vegetarian options

restaurant.name: Queens Cross
restaurant.desc: Queens Cross is a neighborhood pub on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver, serving a full kitchen menu alongside a cold beer and wine store. The pub broadcasts live sports across 14+ screens and a projector, covering NFL, CFL, NHL, and golf. Families with minors are welcome until 8:30 PM, making it a practical stop for cycling groups of mixed ages.

detail.address: 2989 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7N 3J3

restaurant.name: Pho Quynh Express
restaurant.desc: Pho Quynh Express is a Vietnamese noodle house in downtown Vancouver offering a broad menu of phở, vermicelli bowls, rice dishes, and appetizers including Vietnamese and vegetarian options. It is one of three Vancouver locations in the Pho Quynh Express chain, making it a predictable and familiar stop for cyclists passing through the city core. Online ordering with pickup is available, allowing cyclists to call ahead and minimize wait time.

detail.address: 625 Howe St., Suite 100, Vancouver, BC V6C2T6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu legend marks vegetarian items and lists dedicated vegetarian appetizers and a no-meat noodle soup option

restaurant.name: Pizza Rubato
restaurant.desc: Pizza Rubato Napoletana is an independent artisan pizzeria drawing inspiration from the musical concept of 'tempo rubato' — applying rhythmic freedom to Neapolitan pizza tradition. The restaurant uses 48-hour fermented '00' flour dough, imports most ingredients directly from Italy, and bakes in an AVPN-approved Valoriani oven that replicates a wood-fired experience. Cyclists stopping here can expect a full sit-down meal or takeout with an extensive menu of specialty Neapolitan pizzas, from classic Margherita to inventive pistachio-pesto and chili-honey creations.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated VERDURE section with multiple vegetarian pizzas: Margherita, Verde Noce, Rucola, Patate al Forno, Rossa Verdure (RVP), Quattro Formaggi, Pesto Spinaci, Ricotta con Aglio, and Funghi Tartufo

restaurant.name: Gilly's
restaurant.desc: Gilly's is a Chinese restaurant located on Central Avenue in Grand Forks, a small community in the Boundary region of British Columbia's interior. It provides a sit-down dining option for touring cyclists passing through town.

restaurant.name: Viti Wine and Lager
restaurant.desc: Viti Wine and Lager is a neighbourhood bottle shop chain with five locations across Greater Vancouver, stocking over 500 wines, 300 craft beers, and 160 spirits including exclusive Okanagan selections unavailable without travelling to the interior. The Broadway location on Nanaimo Street serves the Commercial Drive area and is part of the award-winning Viaggio Hospitality group. Touring cyclists can pick up beverages for the road and delivery via Skip the Dishes, Uber Eats, and DoorDash is available.

restaurant.name: Alchemy
restaurant.desc: Alchemy Bar and Kitchen is a lively Italian-inspired restaurant and bar located in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, serving pizza, pasta, and globally-influenced cuisine alongside cocktails and mocktails. The restaurant has been recognized as a Rising Stars pick by Restaurant Guru 2024, and is known for its attentive service and creative menu. Its Yaletown location puts it within easy reach of the Seawall cycling route, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists exploring the area.

restaurant.name: Route 14
restaurant.desc: Route 14 is a family-friendly restaurant and pub established in 2016 in the heart of downtown Sooke, BC, winner of the 2024 Business Excellence Award for Dining from the Sooke Region Chamber of Commerce. The menu focuses on locally sourced ingredients — premium steaks, house-made burgers, Kennebec fries, organic herbs, and Ocean Wise seafood — complemented by a full bar with handcrafted cocktails and local beers. Positioned near the Juan de Fuca Trail, Sombrio Beach, and Whiffin Spit, it serves as a natural refueling stop for cyclists touring the southwest Vancouver Island corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We're proud to offer a variety of gluten-free and vegetarian options, ensuring there's something delicious for everyone to enjoy.'

restaurant.name: Delhi delite indian cuisine & sweets
restaurant.desc: Delhi Delite is an Indian restaurant and sweets shop occupying a unit in a commercial complex in Surrey's south end, offering indoor dining with air conditioning. The pairing of a full restaurant menu with a sweets counter sets it apart from a typical curry house and gives cyclists the option of a substantial meal or a quick sweet pick-me-up. OSM data notes wheelchair accessibility and card payments accepted.

restaurant.name: My-Chosen Cafe
restaurant.desc: My-Chosen is a beloved family-owned country destination on Happy Valley Road outside Victoria, operating since 1987 and grown into a complex that includes a full-service cafe, a pizza shop, and a Sugar Shack dessert bar serving banana splits and fresh-baked goods. The property features a 'Critter Corner' with live animals and an unhurried, roam-at-your-own-pace atmosphere that reviewers describe as a genuine escape from the city. Touring cyclists will find hearty comfort-food plates, gluten-sensitive options, and a memorable sweet stop — all under one rustic roof.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Pizza menu lists 'Hungry Hippie – Delicious deluxe veggie'; cafe menu includes a 'Gluten-Sensitive' section explicitly listed in the menu tabs

restaurant.name: The Nook Cafe + Bar
restaurant.desc: The Nook Cafe + Bar is a cafe and bakery in central Kelowna offering takeaway service for cyclists seeking coffee and baked goods. The business is wheelchair accessible.

restaurant.name: Pho Mr. Do
restaurant.desc: Pho Mr. Do is a family-owned Vietnamese restaurant on East Hastings Street in Burnaby, serving authentic pho and Vietnamese dishes prepared from scratch with fresh produce. The menu spans an extensive selection of rice noodle soups, vermicelli dishes, and appetizers, making it a substantial refueling stop for hungry cyclists. Vegan and vegetarian options are well-represented throughout the menu, and takeout and delivery are both available.

detail.address: 4532 E. Hastings Street, Burnaby, BC V5C 2K4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Phở Chay (Vegan Rice Noodle Soup), Gỏi Cuốn Chay (Vegan Salad Roll), Chả Giò Chay (All Veggie Spring Roll), and Đậu Hũ Chiên (Deep Fried Tofu)

restaurant.name: Ukee Dogs Cafe & Eatery
restaurant.desc: Ukee Dogs Cafe & Eatery is a casual restaurant and cafe in Ucluelet. The business name suggests a focus on hot dog-based fare. The location in this popular coastal community makes it a convenient stop for cyclists touring Vancouver Island.

restaurant.name: Brass Fish
restaurant.desc: Brass Fish Kitchen & Tavern is a grandiose yet earnest pub occupying a prominent space inside Vancouver's iconic Marine Building on Burrard Street in the Financial District. The 3,900 sq ft venue offers a modern pub menu alongside a curated selection of 250+ whiskies, a mezzanine lounge, private dining room, and a small stage with DJ booth. Part of the Freehouse Collective group, it sits among several sister establishments in downtown Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Central City Beer Store
restaurant.desc: A beer and beverage retail shop under the Central City Brewing brand, located in North Vancouver. The shop serves as a direct point-of-sale location for brewery products.

restaurant.name: Sea Harbour Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Sea Harbour Restaurant is an award-winning Chinese fine dining establishment offering authentic dim sum, fresh seafood, and a live cooking station for made-to-order congees and other dishes. Located next to The Hotel at River Rock and a short walk from Bridgeport SkyTrain Station, it occupies a recently renovated contemporary space with a sophisticated ambience. A touring cyclist seeking a substantial sit-down meal would find an extensive menu spanning traditional dim sum to premium ingredients such as South African abalone and king crab.

restaurant.name: Kennedy's Sports Pub
restaurant.desc: Kennedy's Sports Pub is a North Delta institution that has been welcoming locals since 1979, seating over 200 guests across a main room, a darts game room, a dance floor, and an outdoor patio with both covered and uncovered sections. The kitchen turns out a broad all-day menu—from breakfast through burgers, pasta, wings, and weekend brunch—supported by a full bar and weekly entertainment including live bands, trivia, and bingo nights. A separately operated Kennedy's Liquor, Beer & Wine Store sits about one block away.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Veggie Quesadilla and Veggie Benny; vegetarian options present across multiple menu sections

restaurant.name: Matcha Corner
restaurant.desc: Matcha Corner is a specialty dessert shop on Kingsway in Vancouver, offering matcha ice cream, ceremonial-grade matcha powder, hojicha powder, and the currently trending Dubai Chewy Cookie. The shop also sells retail matcha products and handles catering and events bookings. It sits on the busy Kingsway corridor, making it a convenient sweet stop for cyclists passing through this part of Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Soho
restaurant.desc: Soho Bar & Billiards is Yaletown's original billiards bar, operating for over 20 years with twelve Diamond pool tables, foosball, pinball, and darts. The venue offers a full bar and food menu including wings, flatbread pizzas, and appetizer platters, along with HD big-screen TVs for sporting events. It caters to groups and private events in a dedicated room in the heart of Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Fresh Donair
restaurant.desc: Fresh Donair is a downtown Vancouver restaurant on Granville Street offering vegetarian dining options to touring cyclists. The non-smoking venue provides indoor seating, accepts credit and debit card payments, and maintains wheelchair accessibility for customers.

restaurant.name: The Raj Indian Kitchen
restaurant.desc: The Raj Indian Kitchen is an authentic Indian restaurant in the heart of downtown Kamloops, serving a wide range of traditional dishes from butter chicken and tikka masala to regional specialties, all prepared with fresh ingredients. The restaurant offers a comfortable dine-in experience alongside online ordering for pickup and phone-in takeout. A large share of the menu — including all tandoori, rice, and entree categories — is explicitly labelled gluten-free, making it a practical stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Veg Entree (All Gluten Free)' category; Tandoori Special, Rice and Biryani, Chicken, Lamb, and Seafood entree sections are all labelled 'All Gluten Free'

restaurant.name: Local Pizza
restaurant.desc: Local Pizza is a Vancouver Island-founded pizza chain emphasizing fresh ingredients and local ownership, with multiple locations across the island and into Victoria and Vancouver. The Nanaimo Terminal Avenue outlet offers both pickup and delivery, with an online ordering system. The chain leans into its BC roots, branding itself as run by local employees serving neighbourhood-style pizzas.

restaurant.name: Royal Donair
restaurant.desc: Royal Donair is a fast food spot specializing in donairs and kebabs, offering takeaway service in North Vancouver. Quick, filling, and portable, donairs are a practical fuel stop for touring cyclists. The business appears to be a small independent or regional chain operation.

detail.address: 105 E 12th St, North Vancouver, BC V7L 2J3, Canada

restaurant.name: Guilt & Co
restaurant.desc: Guilt & Co is an underground live music pub in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, operating since 2010 with two non-ticketed live shows every night, seven days a week. The venue is first-come-first-served, emphasising spontaneous discovery of new artists, and charges a music fee at the door that goes entirely to performers or to Downtown Eastside charities on GroundUp Thursdays. Food is made in-house from fresh, ethically sourced ingredients, and the cocktail program draws on local distilleries.

detail.address: 1 Alexander Street, Underground, Vancouver, BC V6A 1B2

restaurant.name: The Mexican Corner
restaurant.desc: The Mexican Corner is an authentic regional Mexican restaurant and mezcal-and-tequila bar that has operated in Whistler Village for over a decade, with dishes rooted in specific Mexican regional traditions rather than a generic pan-Mexican style. Located on the first floor of the Sundial Hotel building (accessible via elevator through the hotel lobby), it features slow-braised short rib, complex Oaxacan mole, and a curated artisan mezcal list. It presents itself explicitly as a destination dining experience rather than a quick stop, making it well-suited for cyclists seeking a substantial sit-down meal after a ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu confirms multiple vegan/vegetarian dishes including Chipotle Piña Tostada (tofu, black beans) and Charred Corn and Zucchini Enchiladas. No gluten-free options explicitly mentioned

restaurant.name: Manpuku Bento
restaurant.desc: Manpuku Bento is an authentic Japanese bento shop in Vancouver's Chinatown, founded in 2019 and built around scratch-made staples like house-roasted chicken stock and premium wild Sockeye salmon. The shop focuses on generous, affordable bento boxes designed for takeout, with online ordering available for pickup or delivery. A sister location, Manpuku Sushi, operates in Squamish.

detail.address: 288 E Pender St, Vancouver, BC V6A 1T7

notes.Packed lunches: Website describes menu as 'JAPANESE LUNCH BOXES' and all bento items are packaged for portability and takeout
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu uses a dedicated vegetarian icon (🥕) across both Vancouver and Squamish menus; vegetarian items include Croquette Bento, Kappa maki, Ume-Avo, Edamame, Kinpira, and others

restaurant.name: The Great Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: The Great Indian Cuisine is an authentic Indian restaurant on Fraser Highway in Surrey with a broad menu spanning tandoori specialties, vegetarian dishes, chicken, meat, and seafood — each customizable to mild, medium, or hot spice levels. The restaurant serves both dine-in and takeout, and extends its offerings to event catering throughout Surrey. Its dedicated vegetarian section and Lassi-and-dessert drinks menu make it a substantive meal stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley corridor.

detail.address: Unit 101, 15953 Fraser Highway, Surrey, BC V4N 0Y3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Veggie Specialties' section; website states 'Our menu contains non-vegan and veggie lover dishes.'

restaurant.name: Lucky Sushi Company
restaurant.desc: Lucky Sushi Co. is a sit-down sushi restaurant in Vancouver's West End, founded by someone who arrived in Canada in the early 2000s and spent years mastering the craft in a small family-run restaurant. The menu draws on traditional Japanese sushi technique with a modern, retro-inspired atmosphere emphasizing warm rice and top-quality fish. The restaurant is located on the second floor of a Denman Street building, accessed via stairs next to a Starbucks.

restaurant.name: Eggette House
restaurant.desc: Eggette House is a Hong Kong-style street food stall inside Richmond Public Market specializing in bubble waffles made with a specially imported waffle iron and a house recipe designed for a crispy exterior and pillowy interior. Founded by young Vancouver entrepreneurs, the shop offers an extensive menu of both traditional and innovative flavors, including matcha, taro, purple yam, and Portuguese egg tart, alongside hand-made bean cubes and Hong Kong-style milk tea. A one-stop sweet-treat stop for cyclists passing through the busy Richmond Public Market complex.

notes.Takeout: Market stall format serving street food to go; reviews describe receiving orders after a wait, consistent with takeout-only service

restaurant.name: Peaked Pies
restaurant.desc: Peaked Pies is a family-run Australian bakery café that has operated since 2013, serving handmade savoury and sweet pies, artisan coffee, and Australian-style desserts across locations in Vancouver, Burnaby, and Whistler. The Denman Street location sits at the gateway to the Stanley Park seawall cycling routes, making it a natural stop for cyclists exploring Vancouver's waterfront. The signature 'peaked' pie — a meat pie topped with mashed potatoes, mushy peas, and gravy — is a hearty, portable meal well-suited to refuelling after a long ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'traditional meat and veggie options available'; blog post titled 'Calling All Vegans…' indicates vegan offerings

restaurant.name: Salty's Beach House
restaurant.desc: Salty's Beach House is a full-service waterfront restaurant on the sunny southern shore of Okanagan Lake, serving an eclectic menu that spans fresh seafood, sushi, plant-based bowls, and weekend brunch. The two-level space features an outdoor upper deck and an upstairs event lounge called The Pearl. Its prime spot on Lakeshore Drive puts it directly on one of Penticton's most popular cycling corridors.

detail.address: 1000 Lakeshore Dr W, Penticton, BC V2A 1C1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a dedicated 'PLANT-BASED' category; multiple dishes marked 'Ask GA' (gluten aware), e.g. Island Chowder and Scallops Remoulade

restaurant.name: Wa-Ku Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Wa-Ku Japanese Restaurant is a Japanese cuisine restaurant located in Nanaimo, BC, operating from a unit in a multi-tenant building. As one of Nanaimo's Japanese dining options, it offers touring cyclists a sit-down meal after riding the area's trails and roads. The restaurant's exact offerings are unverifiable from available sources, but its OSM record shows it as an active establishment.

restaurant.name: Gobong Korean Hotpot
restaurant.desc: Gobong Korean Hotpot is a Korean restaurant in North Vancouver specialising in hotpot, a communal table-cooking style where diners simmer meat, vegetables, and other ingredients in a shared broth. The restaurant is fully indoor with a no-smoking policy, offering a warm and social dining experience. It would make a satisfying stop for cyclists looking for a substantial, warming meal after a ride on the North Shore.

restaurant.name: Maharaja Catering
restaurant.desc: Maharaja Catering Ltd. is a long-standing Indian restaurant and catering company located in Surrey's Payal Business Centre, offering authentic cuisine prepared using traditional tandoor (clay oven) cooking and house-made herbs and spices. The business operates a full sit-down restaurant with a fine dining lounge, a sweet shop, and a takeout counter — plus large-event catering for weddings and conventions. Touring cyclists would find a broad menu anchored in South Asian flavours with strong vegetarian representation.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu has dedicated 'APPETIZER-VEGETARIAN' and 'MAIN COURSE - VEGETARIAN' sections with multiple dishes

restaurant.name: Virtuous Pie
restaurant.desc: Virtuous Pie is an exclusively vegan restaurant in Vancouver's Chinatown serving pizza and ice cream. Opened in 2016, it offers plant-based casual dining.

restaurant.name: Basha
restaurant.desc: Basha is a Lebanese restaurant in Vancouver offering both dine-in and takeaway service. The waterfront location suggested by its Facebook page name provides a distinctive setting. It caters to casual diners seeking Middle Eastern cuisine.

restaurant.name: Vietnam Village
restaurant.desc: Vietnam Village is a family-run Vietnamese restaurant that has served Kelowna since 2002 from its location on busy Highway 97. The menu spans Phở, Bánh mì, fresh salad rolls, vermicelli bowls, and chef specials, with a wide range of vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options. Cyclists passing through on the Okanagan corridor will find a fully licensed sit-down dining room alongside takeout and delivery options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Homepage states 'many vegetarian and vegan options'; menu labels crispy pork spring rolls and fresh salad rolls as 'gluten-free'; a dedicated Vegetarian Menu section is present; tofu substitutions offered across multiple dishes

restaurant.name: Blackfin Pub
restaurant.desc: The Blackfin Pub is a locally owned and operated oceanfront restaurant and pub perched at the edge of the Comox Marina on Vancouver Island, offering sweeping views of the Beaufort Mountains and Comox Glacier. The menu leans into Pacific Northwest seafood and locally sourced ingredients, with an extensive BC and Comox Valley wine list. Note that this is a 19+ establishment — all guests must be of legal drinking age to enter.

detail.address: 132 Port Augusta Street, Comox, BC V9M 3N7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a 'GLUTEN SENSITIVE' section; falafel is listed as a salad add-on option, indicating vegetarian choices are available

restaurant.name: Dan's Diner
restaurant.desc: Dan's Diner is a social enterprise takeout counter operated by Dan's Legacy, a registered charity that supports youth who have experienced trauma. Students in the culinary training program prepare daily-changing packaged soups, stews, curries, and chilis under professional chef guidance, developing both cooking and life skills. Purchasing a meal here directly funds youth employment training and mental health support in the New Westminster community.

restaurant.name: Paradiso Italian Gelato
restaurant.desc: Paradiso Caffè e Gelato is a beloved Kitsilano dessert shop that has been crafting small-batch artisanal gelato and sorbetto using fresh BC milk and cream since 2002. Cyclists rolling through the Yew Street corridor can refuel with gelato in a cone, on egg waffles, or paired with locally roasted Vancouver coffee or ceremonial-grade matcha. The shop also offers catering and gift cards, suggesting a well-established local presence.

restaurant.name: Clayburn Village Store & Gift Shop
restaurant.desc: Clayburn Village Store is a heritage retail shop built in 1911 and painstakingly restored by its current owners since 1987, occupying a century-old building with original fir floors and a period tin-look ceiling in the historic Clayburn Village near Abbotsford. The store specialises in international and nostalgic candies alongside specialty European foods, and the owner bakes fresh scones, cornish pasties, sausage rolls, and quiche on-site each open morning. It offers touring cyclists a genuinely unhurried, step-back-in-time stop on Fraser Valley routes.

restaurant.name: Heron Rock Bistro
restaurant.desc: Heron Rock Bistro is a full-service neighbourhood bistro founded in 2005 in Victoria's James Bay district, offering breakfast, lunch, and dinner seven days a week alongside a curated wine list featuring BC and international bottles. The restaurant has built a 20-year reputation as a community gathering place known for consistent quality and a warm atmosphere, with regular live music events adding to its appeal. For a touring cyclist arriving in Victoria, it represents a dependable sit-down meal option close to the Inner Harbour area.

restaurant.name: Crave Cheesesteaks
restaurant.desc: Crave Cheesesteaks is a downtown Vancouver restaurant specializing in Philly-inspired cheesesteaks made fresh to order using 100% sirloin steak, real provolone and cheddar, and house-made sauces. Located at Robson and Richards, steps from BC Place, Rogers Arena, and the Vancouver Public Library, it serves a compact menu of steak, chicken, and jackfruit cheesesteaks in 8-inch and 12-inch sizes. Dine-in, takeout, and third-party delivery are all available, making it a practical mid-ride fuel stop in the heart of the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website FAQ confirms a 'vegetarian option made with mesquite-marinated jackfruit'; menu lists 'Jack Fruit (V)' as a distinct category

restaurant.name: Ramie's Greek Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Ramie's Greek Restaurant is a family-owned establishment celebrating 25 years of serving Greek cuisine, with its second location on Highway 17A in Delta. The original Burnaby location earned the Quality Business Award for Best Greek Restaurant in both 2023 and 2024. The Delta outpost brings the same menu — including lunch, dinner, liquor, and happy hour offerings — to a Highway 17A corridor that sees significant cycling traffic.

restaurant.name: Breakfast Table
restaurant.desc: Breakfast Table is a family-run brunch spot on South Granville founded in 2016 by brothers-in-law George Koay and Michael Lee, blending Asian flavour influences with classic comfort-food brunch dishes. Popular items include Breakfast Ratatouille, Challah French Toast, and an Ube Latte. The restaurant operates on a walk-in-only basis with a street-front patio at the Granville location.

restaurant.name: Nando's
restaurant.desc: Nando's is an international chain with roots in a 1987 Portuguese eatery in Johannesburg, South Africa, built around flame-grilled chicken marinated for 24 hours in PERi-PERi chili sauce. The Kerrisdale location sits on West 41st Avenue in a residential neighbourhood and offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery across a broad menu of chicken, sandwiches, salads, and sides. It is one of several BC locations in a chain operating across 23 countries.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Veggie Burger, Portobello Mushroom & Halloumi Wrap, Mediterranean Salad, Rainbow Bowl, and multiple plant-based sides

restaurant.name: The Clouds Vietnamese Cuisine
restaurant.desc: The Clouds Vietnamese Cuisine is a sit-down Vietnamese restaurant on Victoria Drive in East Vancouver, serving a full dine-in menu alongside bubble tea. The restaurant also offers takeout, making it a practical stop for cyclists passing through the neighbourhood. It sits on a busy arterial route that connects several residential communities in South Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Red Baron Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Red Baron Restaurant is a family-owned seaside eatery at Crescent Beach in Surrey serving fish and chips, ice cream, and frozen yogurt. Situated beside the beach, it offers a quiet atmosphere with outdoor seating, making it a natural pit stop for cyclists riding the coastal routes. The shop carries a wide variety of ice cream flavors and accepts U.S. currency.

restaurant.name: La Taqueria Pinche Taco Shop
restaurant.desc: The La Taquería group operates three distinct Mexican concepts across Metro Vancouver, and 2450 Yukon St. is home to Comedor, their counter-service street-food outpost offering tacos, burritos, and specialties like Quesabirria and Birriamen. The casual, fast-service format makes it a practical stop for a touring cyclist looking for a filling, flavourful meal near the Cambie Street corridor. A broad menu with several plant-based options adds to its appeal for mixed groups.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Comedor menu lists multiple vegetarian items: Hongos Salteados, Rajas con Crema, Frijoles Refritos, Guacamole & Chip, Pico de Gallo and Chips

restaurant.name: Pho in Love
restaurant.desc: Pho in Love is an authentic Vietnamese restaurant and bar on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, a busy commercial strip popular with locals and visitors alike. Sitting close to the Stanley Park seawall and beach cycling routes, it would be a natural stop for cyclists exploring the area. The bar component suggests a full-service dine-in experience beyond a quick noodle counter.

restaurant.name: Onda by Casereccio
restaurant.desc: Onda by Casereccio is an Italian restaurant in Vancouver's Olympic Village neighbourhood, serving homemade pasta, Neapolitan-style pizza, panini, and antipasti rooted in traditional Italian culinary philosophy. The menu spans classic dishes like Lasagna Bolognese, Gnocchi Pesto Verde, and Tuna Crudo made with local albacore, alongside a curated selection of Italian cured meats and cheeses. Its location on Salt Street places it squarely in one of Vancouver's most cycle-friendly urban districts.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists Lasagna Vegetariana, Vegetariano panini (zucchini, eggplant, red pepper), Minestrone Soup labelled 'Vegeterian', and Gnocchi Pesto Verde

restaurant.name: Los Sapos Tacos
restaurant.desc: Los Sapos Tacos is a Vancouver street-taco specialist focused on authentic Al Pastor and Birria, earning a 4.9-star Google rating. Located in Chinatown on Keefer Street, it operates as both a sit-down restaurant and a ghost kitchen with delivery through major apps. A second location exists in Kitsilano, and the business also offers full-service catering with a personal chef.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website prominently states 'Delicious Vegan Tacos Too!' and a Google reviewer confirms 'the vegetarian tacos were awesome.'

restaurant.name: Sunny M Coffee & Tea
restaurant.desc: SUNNY M is a specialty coffee brand based in Richmond, BC, running both a small-batch online coffee release store and a physical café that serves selected roasts. The brand's approach is research-driven, selecting coffees for clarity, structure, and how they evolve as they cool. The physical SUNNY M Café in Richmond is where touring cyclists can experience these releases in person.

restaurant.name: The Best Grill
restaurant.desc: The Best Grill is a casual American-style diner in Langley Township serving all-day breakfast alongside a broad menu of homemade burgers, eggs benedicts, and sandwiches. The extensive made-from-scratch menu — including multiple burger builds and a full eggs benedict lineup — makes it a solid refuelling stop for cyclists riding the Fraser Valley. Online ordering and delivery are available through the Focal Eats platform.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a 'Vege Sandwich' (Lettuce, Tomato, Pepper, Cucumber, Swiss Cheese) and a 'Florentine Benny' (Spinach, Tomato, Mushroom, Feta) as vegetarian options. No vegan or GF options explicitly mentioned

restaurant.name: Lime and Moon Pie Company
restaurant.desc: Lime and Moon Pie Company is listed in OSM as a pie-cuisine restaurant in North Vancouver. No corroborating details about the physical business — menu, location, or operations — could be found, as the associated domain has been repurposed as an unrelated content-farm blog. Its current operational status is unverifiable from available evidence.

detail.address: 400 Bowen Trunk Road, Bowen Island, BC

restaurant.name: Doppio Zero Pizza
restaurant.desc: Doppio Zero is an Italian sit-down restaurant in Coquitlam specializing in Vera Pizza Napoletana alongside house-made pastas, antipasti, and an Italian-focused wine list. The kitchen takes its craft seriously — the award-winning Boschetti pizza features truffle cream, speck DOP, and shaved parmesan — making it a memorable stop for cyclists looking for a proper meal rather than a quick bite. Reservations are recommended as the restaurant may close early on slow nights.

detail.address: 103-1655 Como Lake Avenue, Coquitlam, BC V3J 3P7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu marks numerous items as vegetarian (V) across all courses; 'Beyond – Vegan' pizza available; gluten-free pasta offered as a substitute on pasta dishes

restaurant.name: Brasserie L'école
restaurant.desc: Brasserie L'école is a classic French brasserie in the heart of downtown Victoria, serving seasonal, locally sourced ingredients prepared in a French-country style. The restaurant is known for its curated selection of Belgian and French beers alongside a wine list that emphasises French regional varieties and value. Touring cyclists looking for a destination sit-down meal in Victoria will find classic brasserie fare — moules et frites, duck confit, beef tartare — on a menu updated daily.

restaurant.name: Nook Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Nook Restaurant (Shipyards) is an Italian neighbourhood restaurant in North Vancouver's Shipyards district, serving housemade pasta, pizza, antipasto, and cocktails with locally sourced ingredients and Italian imports. Part of a Metro Vancouver chain founded in 2009, this location sits in the lively Shipyards waterfront area — a natural stop for cyclists riding the North Shore. Dine-in, pickup, and delivery are all available, and the restaurant is wheelchair accessible.

detail.address: 150 Victory Ship Way, North Vancouver, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Shipyards menu shows 'GF Organic Quinoa Pasta +3' substitution option; multiple vegetarian dishes visible (Margherita pizza, Tonnarelli Cacio Pepe, Ricotta pizza, Whipped Ricotta Crostini, etc.)

restaurant.name: Passione Gelato
restaurant.desc: Passione Gelato is a takeaway-only ice cream shop on Smithe Street. With no seating available, it's ideal for cyclists wanting a quick frozen treat without stopping for long. Card payments are accepted.

notes.Takeout: takeaway only

restaurant.name: C - Lovers
restaurant.desc: C-Lovers Fish & Chips is a BC-based chain specializing in hand-battered fish and chips, with a North Vancouver outpost on Pemberton Ave. The menu features multiple species—halibut, cod, haddock, salmon, and prawns—alongside classic sides like hand-cut chips and coleslaw. The chain participates in the Ocean Wise sustainable seafood program, indicating a commitment to responsibly sourced fish.

restaurant.name: JoJo's Fish & Chips Bana Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A fish and chips restaurant in Chilliwack, BC. The restaurant offers free Wi-Fi to customers, making it a convenient spot for touring cyclists to stop for a meal and connectivity.

detail.address: 32700 George Ferguson Way #9, Abbotsford, BC V2T 4V6, Canada

restaurant.name: Brandts Creek Neighborhood Pub
restaurant.desc: Brandt's Creek Neighbourhood Pub has been a Kelowna fixture since 1990, offering a country-style interior with vaulted ceilings and a large summer patio. The kitchen spans classic pub comfort food, rotating seasonal dishes, and weekend brunch service. It is a 19+ venue with a full-size parking lot and overflow parking next door.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Brunch menu lists a GF bread substitution option; menu includes multiple salad and vegetable-forward dishes

restaurant.name: Longtail Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Named after the iconic long-tail water taxis of Thailand, Longtail Kitchen is a Thai and Southeast Asian street food restaurant set inside the River Market on the Fraser River waterfront. Celebrated chef Angus An steers the menu toward BC ingredients while staying true to traditional Southeast Asian methods — think brightly spiced curries, fish stews, noodle bowls, and snacks inspired by dishes eaten by Southeast Asian fishermen. The riverside market setting, with both indoor and outdoor seating, makes it a scenic stop for cyclists riding the Central Valley Greenway or Quayside paths.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian items: Veggie Spring Roll, Fried Enoki Mushroom, Green Papaya Salad, Pad Thai Tofu, Singaporean Noodles Tofu, Stir Fried Eggplant, and daily curry with tofu option. Vegan or GF status not explicitly stated

restaurant.name: Piast Bakery & Deli
restaurant.desc: Piast Bakery & Deli is a European-style bakery and deli located on Cambie Street in Vancouver. It offers baked goods and prepared deli items, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking quick food and supplies.

restaurant.name: AJ's Brooklyn Pizza Joint
restaurant.desc: AJ's Brooklyn Pizza Joint is a Vancouver pizza restaurant that has been slinging authentic Brooklyn-style pies since 2017, with a philosophy rooted in respect for craft and community. Everything is homemade — including dough that takes three days to prepare — using ingredients sourced from specific local suppliers. The restaurant offers dine-in with reservations, online ordering, and Uber Eats delivery, making it a solid stop for a hungry cyclist on East Broadway.

restaurant.name: Nemesis
restaurant.desc: Nemesis is a specialty coffee roaster and café with five Metro Vancouver locations, including this one at Carrie Cates Court near Lonsdale Quay in North Vancouver.
