The brand operates its own in-house bakery, Dope Bakehouse, and offers single-origin and signature espresso drinks alongside fresh pastries. It is a compact, no-smoking indoor café — a reliable urban stop for a quality coffee and a croissant mid-ride.

detail.address: 101 Carrie Cates Ct, North Vancouver, BC

restaurant.name: Khoe
restaurant.desc: Khoe is a plant-based Vietnamese restaurant on East Georgia Street in Vancouver's Commercial Drive neighbourhood. It focuses entirely on vegan cuisine, making it a reliable stop for plant-based touring cyclists seeking Vietnamese flavours. The compact storefront is a neighbourhood spot rather than a large dining destination.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Business operates under the name 'Khoe Plant Based' confirming fully plant-based/vegan menu

restaurant.name: Moon Wok (Aberdeen)
restaurant.desc: A family-owned Chinese restaurant in Kamloops' Aberdeen neighbourhood, widely regarded as the city's top choice for Chinese take-out. Moon Wok uses fresh ingredients with no MSG added and caters to a range of dietary needs including vegetarian, allergy-conscious, and gluten-free diners. Take-out, dine-in, delivery, and catering are all available at this South Shore location.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Whether you're vegetarian or have food allergies, we have plenty of delicious menu choices to choose from. Be sure to ask about our gluten-free menu for Kamloops diners.'

restaurant.name: Sushi Hyun Omakase
restaurant.desc: Sushi Hyun Omakase is a Japanese omakase restaurant on Jervis Street in Vancouver's West End, offering a chef's-choice multi-course sushi experience. OSM records both indoor and outdoor seating, suggesting a sit-down dining environment. A touring cyclist looking for a special-occasion meal in the West End would find this a distinctive stop.

restaurant.name: Afghan Chopan Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Afghan Chopan Restaurant has been serving Richmond and the Lower Mainland since 2001, specializing in traditional Afghan kebabs — lamb shoulder chops, beef tenderloin tekka, and ground-beef shami — all grilled and served with fresh baked naan, chutney, and Afghan-style Pallow. The kitchen uses 100% halal meat and prepares everything from scratch, reflecting the Afghan hospitality the owners describe as central to their culture. It is a sit-down restaurant with a party room and also offers takeout ordering online.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a Vegetarian Combo (Bolani, Ashak, one Vegetable Dish) and Ashak is described as 'Vegeterian Dumplings filled with Leeks.' No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Pizza Pizza
restaurant.desc: Pizza Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain established in 1967, offering dine-in, takeout, and delivery from this Abbotsford location on South Fraser Way. The menu spans pizzas with multiple crust options, chicken wings, poutine, panzerottis, and strombolis, alongside dairy-free, vegan, and gluten-free options. This location is A-Level Certified and is noted as open late, making it a practical stop for cyclists finishing a long day on the road.

detail.address: 32151 South Fraser Way, Unit 120, Abbotsford, BC V2T 1W3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'Vegetarian Options', 'Vegan Options', 'Gluten-Free Options', and 'Dairy-Free' under available menu items at this location

restaurant.name: Small Victory Bakery
restaurant.desc: Small Victory Bakery is a family-owned neighborhood bakery and cafe whose founders grew up in a family baking business started by Kenyan immigrant parents on West Broadway. The Mount Pleasant location on West 6th Avenue specializes in artisan breads, laminated pastries, and specialty coffee sourced from local roasters. A full brunch and lunch menu rounds out the offering, making it a worthwhile stop for cyclists wanting a proper sit-down meal or fresh bread to carry onward.

restaurant.name: The Poke Guy
restaurant.desc: The Poke Guy is a Hawaiian-inspired poke and grill restaurant in downtown Vancouver, recognized as Canada's first restaurant partnering with Ocean Wise to serve sustainably sourced, wild-caught seafood. The menu centres on build-your-own poke bowls, Hawaiian hot plates, and poke wraps, all made with daily-fresh wild-caught fish and in-house marinades. With extensive vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options and a catering program, it offers a health-conscious and customizable meal for cyclists moving through the city core.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website confirms 'vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, and dairy-free options'; catering FAQ states 'We offer vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, and dairy-free options'; about page states 'nearly all of our marinades are gluten-free'; menu includes Fried Tofu Curry and Da Buddha bowl

restaurant.name: Maxim's Bakery
restaurant.desc: Maxim's Bakery is a Hong Kong-style bakery chain with a location inside Lansdowne Centre mall in Richmond. It is known for freshly baked breads, pineapple buns, and Asian pastries typical of the chain. A cyclist stopping at this mall location could pick up baked goods as a quick snack or light resupply.

restaurant.name: Neptune Wonton Noodle
restaurant.desc: Neptune Wonton Noodle is a Chinese noodle restaurant operated by the Neptune Group, situated inside the McArthurGlen Designer Outlet adjacent to Vancouver International Airport. It is one of two Neptune Wonton Noodle outlets in Richmond, part of a multi-brand restaurant group that has operated in Greater Vancouver since 1997. The outlet shares the mall footprint with sibling brand Ryuu Japanese Kitchen.

restaurant.name: Yummy Sushi Gallery
restaurant.desc: Yummy Sushi Gallery is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Abbotsford offering dine-in and online takeout ordering. The establishment features outdoor seating, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Bubble World Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Bubble World Restaurant is a Taiwanese eatery in New Westminster offering indoor dining in a no-smoking environment. Its name suggests a focus on bubble tea alongside Taiwanese cuisine, making it a potential rest stop for cyclists seeking a full meal or a cold drink. No street address is recorded in OSM, so riders should confirm the exact location before visiting.

restaurant.name: The 515 Bar
restaurant.desc: The 515 Bar is a cozy craft cocktail and craft beer bar in the heart of Downtown Vancouver, named for the idea of unwinding after the 9-to-5. It specializes in hand-crafted, original cocktails alongside a curated food menu, served in an intimate space with eclectic music and whimsical lighting. The small, first-come-first-serve venue also offers full private event buyouts.

detail.address: 521 Seymour St, V6B 3H6, Vancouver, BC Canada

restaurant.name: East is East
restaurant.desc: East is East is a Silk Road-inspired restaurant drawing on culinary traditions stretching from Mongolia through Tibet, India, Persia, and Istanbul, with all food made from natural whole ingredients, organic and local where possible. The Main Street location is one of two Vancouver outposts and is described as a candle-lit 'Chai Gallery' experience that transports diners to a different world. Touring cyclists will find a broad menu of largely plant-based dishes alongside wines, cocktails, and masala chai, with a takeout option available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Extensive V (vegan), VO (vegan option), GF (gluten-free), and D (dairy) labels throughout both dinner and lunch menus; the majority of main dishes are V/GF or GF. Menu notes food is made from 'natural, whole ingredients, organic and local where possible.'

restaurant.name: Stega Eatery
restaurant.desc: Stega Eatery is a restaurant located in Vancouver's Olympic Village neighbourhood on Columbia Street, a popular cycling corridor near the False Creek seawall. The OSM record notes indoor seating and a smoke-free environment. Its location in one of Vancouver's most cycle-friendly districts makes it a natural stop for riders exploring the seawall or commuting through the area.

restaurant.name: Katana
restaurant.desc: Katana is a Japanese Steak and Seafood House in Langley specializing in teppan yaki, where master chefs cook Triple-A steaks and fresh seafood directly at tableside grills. The interactive dining experience features premium cuts alongside lobster tails, giant shrimp, and king scallops in a casual, lively atmosphere. It is a well-established local hotspot with an extensive international wine list.

restaurant.name: Forage Farm and Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Forage Farm and Kitchen is a family-run farm-to-table restaurant on Hornby Island, building its seasonal menus around organically grown fruit, vegetables, berries, and edible flowers from their own farm. Located in the Ringside commercial area, the restaurant also offers vibrant cocktails and patio seating. For cyclists touring the Gulf Islands, it is one of the few year-round dining options on Hornby.

detail.address: 5875 Central Road, Hornby Island, BC V0R 1Z0

restaurant.name: Sweet Thea Bakery
restaurant.desc: Sweet Thea Bakery is an artisan bakery-café in Vancouver's Riley Park neighbourhood run by pastry chef Thea Mercer and her partner Laurie, where every loaf of sourdough takes three days to make using certified organic BC wheat. The open-kitchen space serves hearty scratch-made breakfasts, daily soups, and creative sandwiches alongside buttery croissants, focaccia, and 49th Parallel coffee, with a take-a-book-leave-a-book nook and a standing commitment to donating daily surplus to local charities. The business has grown from farmers' market pop-ups to three locations including a BC Ferries terminal outpost, making it a well-established community fixture.

restaurant.name: Drake Eatery
restaurant.desc: The Drake Eatery & Craft Beer Parlour has been a fixture of Victoria's Historic Market Square since 2014, pouring West Coast craft beer across 29 rotating taps alongside a food program built on simply prepared quality local ingredients. The space is intentionally low-key — no TVs, no loud music — designed as a neighbourhood gathering spot with order-at-the-bar service. It also hosts community fundraising events, including the annual Thirsty Chef beer and food festival benefiting the Victoria Cool Aid Society.

restaurant.name: The Keg
restaurant.desc: The Keg Steakhouse + Bar is a well-established Canadian steakhouse chain with a Kelowna outpost at the intersection of Highway 97 and Underhill Street, making it easy to reach from either the airport corridor or downtown. The location features a year-round heated and covered patio alongside a lounge, bar, and semi-private dining room. Touring cyclists rolling into Kelowna along the Highway 97 corridor will find it a convenient sit-down or takeout option with free parking on site.

detail.address: 1825 Underhill Street, Kelowna, British Columbia, V1X 8G8

restaurant.name: Ramen Danbo
restaurant.desc: Ramen Danbo is a popular chain originating from Fukuoka, Japan, specializing in traditional Tonkotsu pork-broth ramen with signature broth made daily in-house at each location. The Vancouver shops were the chain's first restaurants outside Japan, and the menu offers extensive customization of noodle firmness, broth richness, and toppings. A touring cyclist can count on a hot, filling bowl of ramen with pickup and delivery also available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated 'Vegan Menu' listed alongside the regular menu on the Vancouver menu page

restaurant.name: Hillcrest Bakery and Deli
restaurant.desc: Hillcrest Bakery and Deli is a White Rock institution with over 40 years of history, owned by David and Sheana Moyer since 2011. David trained with a German bakery and the shop is known for hand-crafted breads, custom cakes, and deli items made entirely from scratch. Cyclists can pick up fresh baked goods, deli items, and prepared take-out dinners here.

detail.address: 15231 Thrift Ave, White Rock, BC V4B 2K9

restaurant.name: Biryani Palace
restaurant.desc: Biryani Palace is a halal Indian and Pakistani restaurant on Quadra Street in Victoria, specializing in slow-cooked dum biryani, tandoori dishes, and a broad menu of curries and kebabs. The restaurant features an open-concept kitchen where guests can watch dishes being prepared with traditional methods and authentic ingredients. They also offer full catering services for events of any size.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated Vegetable section and Veggie Dum Biryani; catering copy references vegetarian platters. No mention of vegan or GF specifically

restaurant.name: Han Korea
restaurant.desc: Han Korea is a Korean BBQ restaurant in Chilliwack with online ordering capability. The restaurant serves Korean cuisine and provides a dining stop for cyclists seeking substantial meals.

restaurant.name: Il Terrazzo
restaurant.desc: Il Terrazzo is a long-established Victoria landmark tucked into Waddington Alley, an old-town courtyard behind the Willie's Bakery Building on Johnson Street. The restaurant specializes in Northern Italian cuisine with a Pacific Northwest influence, served in a candlelit room with brick fireplaces. A certified sommelier program oversees a cellar of more than 1,000 wine selections, making it a notable destination for a special evening meal on a multi-day tour.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states chef makes 'an excellent vegan or vegetarian pasta upon request' (described as 'very limited options') and 'Many of our entrees can be adjusted to be gluten free'; no GF pasta or pizza but risotto available

restaurant.name: Valley Sushi
restaurant.desc: Valley Sushi is a Japanese cuisine and sushi bar in Lynn Valley, North Vancouver, serving authentic Japanese food for over a decade. Located in a shopping centre unit on Lynn Valley Road, it offers dine-in, online ordering, and delivery. A touring cyclist riding through the Lynn Valley corridor would find a full sit-down meal option with a broad Japanese menu.

detail.address: 1233 Lynn Valley Rd #125, North Vancouver, BC V7J 0A1

restaurant.name: Delta Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Delta Indian Cuisine is an authentic Indian restaurant in Delta, BC, serving a broad menu of traditional dishes crafted with freshly ground spices and house recipes developed by experienced chefs. The menu spans appetizers, tandoori items, curries, breads, and desserts, with a notable selection of vegetarian choices throughout. Online ordering is available, and the restaurant runs rotating promotional offers.

notes.Takeout: Offers page states '15% off your takeout order when you spend $30 or more'; site also features an 'Order Online' function
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page tags multiple items as 'Veg': Vegetable Pakora, Paneer Pakora, Aloo Tikki, Veggie Samosa, Veggie Wrap, Veg Manchurian, Veggie Noodles, Veggie Spring Roll

restaurant.name: Sprout Bread
restaurant.desc: Sprout Bread is an artisan bakery located on Cannery Lane in Kelowna. Situated in what appears to be a commercial retail area, it would be a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking to pick up fresh bread and baked goods.

restaurant.name: Boomtown
restaurant.desc: Boomtown is an independent beer garden and burrito bar in downtown Victoria, built around locally-sourced Mexican-inspired food and a rotating lineup of BC craft beers on draught from breweries like Driftwood, Hoyne, and Whistle Buoy. The atmosphere is proudly unfussy, with a covered year-round patio that has earned local recognition as one of Victoria's best. Well-behaved dogs on leash are welcome on the outdoor patio, and the venue explicitly embraces cyclists with dedicated bike parking.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ explicitly confirms vegan options (burritos, salads, bowls, vegan cashew queso, vegan Boom Sauce) and gluten-free options (bowls, house-made corn chips, doughnuts)

restaurant.name: Roundhouse Lodge
restaurant.desc: Roundhouse Lodge is Whistler Blackcomb's main mid-mountain dining hub, situated at approximately 1,850 m elevation at the top of the Whistler Village Gondola. In summer it serves as the gateway to the Whistler Mountain Bike Park, making it a natural rest stop for uplift-assisted mountain bikers. The two-storey building is a landmark on Whistler Mountain and offers views of the surrounding Coast Mountains.

restaurant.name: Little Caesars
restaurant.desc: Little Caesars is a well-known Canadian pizza chain franchise offering ready-made and made-to-order pizzas for pickup or delivery. This Fraser Street location serves the southeast Vancouver neighbourhood and is a convenient hot-food stop for cyclists on a budget. The chain is known for its Hot-N-Ready model and Detroit-style deep dish options.

restaurant.name: The Greek Gastown
restaurant.desc: The Greek Gastown is the Gastown outpost of The Greek by Anatoli, a Vancouver-area restaurant group with over 40 years of Greek hospitality. Located in the historic Carrall Street corridor, it offers a Mediterranean-inspired dining room, handcrafted cocktails, and a full menu of grilled meats, fresh seafood, and house-made dips. Private dining spaces and catering are available, making it a capable stop for solo cyclists and larger groups alike.

restaurant.name: SinAmen Bun Co.
restaurant.desc: SinAmen Bun Co. is a cinnamon bun specialist bakery located in Chilliwack. The shop maintains an active social media presence on Facebook and Instagram.

restaurant.name: Church's Chicken
restaurant.desc: Church's Chicken (operating in BC as Church's Texas Chicken) is a fast-food chain specializing in fried chicken, sandwiches, tenders, and sides. This Coquitlam location offers drive-through and pickup service and is one of roughly 18 Lower Mainland locations under the same franchise. Delivery is available through DoorDash, Skip, Uber Eats, and Fantuan.

restaurant.name: Soupa Cafe
restaurant.desc: Soupa Cafe is a Victoria institution specializing in fresh, daily-made soups and sandwiches crafted from local ingredients, with a rotating weekly special alongside six permanent classics. The menu leans heavily toward inclusive eating — at least three vegan soups are offered every day, and many dishes are gluten-free. Dine-in tables are available and described as accessible to all guests, making it a comfortable mid-ride stop for cyclists looking for a nourishing, quick meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states 'at least three different vegan soups daily'; multiple menu items (Summer Ginger Broccoli, Tuscan Tomato Basilico, Split Pea and Ham, African Yam Peanut, Creamy Coco Mushroom, Red Lentil Gala, One-Pot Chicken Stew, Homestyle Meat Chili) are explicitly labeled gluten-free on the website

restaurant.name: Congee Noodle Delight
restaurant.desc: Congee Noodle Delight is a family-owned Hong Kong-style restaurant inside International Village Mall in downtown Vancouver, operating since 2015. It serves traditional congee, BBQ meats, wonton noodle soup, and sizeable sharing plates drawn from classic Hong Kong cuisine. Touring cyclists passing through downtown Vancouver will find both dine-in and takeout options at street level along West Pender Street.

detail.address: 1021-88 West Pender St, Vancouver, BC V6B 6N9

restaurant.name: Homeslice Cafe & Bakery
restaurant.desc: Homeslice Cafe & Bakery is a family-owned, made-from-scratch bakery on the outskirts of the Kerrisdale neighbourhood in Vancouver. The shop produces breads, loaves, and other baked goods, with pre-orders available online and walk-in shopping during regular business hours. Cyclists passing through the Kerrisdale/Arbutus corridor will find it a welcoming stop for fresh-baked provisions.

restaurant.name: Dhamaka Indian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Dhamaka Indian Restaurant is a full-service Indian eatery on Vancouver's Main Street, specializing in Hyderabadi Biryani, fragrant curries, and tandoori dishes drawn from regional Indian culinary traditions. The name 'Dhamaka' — meaning 'explosion of flavour' in Hindi — captures the restaurant's emphasis on bold, authentic spicing. In addition to dine-in, the restaurant offers online ordering, pickup, and catering services.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website references 'comforting vegetarian favourites' and positions vegetarian dishes as a core part of the menu

restaurant.name: Pho Hong on Fraser
restaurant.desc: Pho Hong on Fraser is a family-operated Vietnamese restaurant that has anchored its South Vancouver neighbourhood since 1998, built on a signature pho broth slow-cooked for 24 hours using AA-AAA Canadian beef. The menu spans pho variations, bún bò Huế, grilled-meat rice and noodle bowls, fresh salad rolls, and takeout-only bánh mì with all fillings made in-house. It is a well-established local spot with a loyal following and a broad menu that accommodates omnivores and vegans alike.

notes.Takeout: 'Take away' listed as a service on the homepage; bánh mì section is explicitly marked 'TAKE OUT ONLY'; delivery available via Uber Eats, DoorDash, and Skip the Dishes
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items marked 🌿 vegan: vegetarian bánh mì (B4 BÁNH MÌ CHAY), veggie spring rolls (A2 CHẢ GIÒ CHAY), vegetable salad rolls (A4 BÌ CUỐN CHAY); PHỞ SATE notes 'Vegan option available'. No gluten-free confirmation found

restaurant.name: Ogenki
restaurant.desc: Ogenki is a sushi restaurant on Main Street in Vancouver, operating since 2003. The restaurant offers both fusion and vegan-focused sushi menus, accommodating various dietary preferences.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegan menu available (Ogenki Vegan menu)

restaurant.name: Sirka Gourmet Takeout
restaurant.desc: Sirka Takeout is an Indian restaurant in Surrey specializing in bold, authentic regional cuisine rooted in Punjabi culinary traditions, created by Chef Kanwardeep and Chef Baldeep. The menu spans chaat street food, tandoori kebabs, Indo-Chinese dishes, and rich curries. Its takeout-focused format and broad menu — including many vegetarian options — make it a practical and flavourful stop for cyclists moving through Surrey.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes numerous vegetarian items: Dahi Bhalla, Aloo Tikki Chana Chaat, Papdi Chaat, Bang-Bang Cauliflower, Paneer Fingers, Bhatti da Paneer Tikka, SIRKA Soy Champ, Veg Manchurian, Cheese Chilli, Chilli Mushroom, and multiple paneer curries

restaurant.name: Coastal Coffee & Tea
restaurant.desc: Coastal Coffee House is a cafe located along 56 Avenue in Langley. The business maintains a Facebook presence but no standalone website has been identified. Details about the menu, atmosphere, and cyclist-friendly features are currently unavailable.

restaurant.name: Sushi Box
restaurant.desc: SushiBox MK is a fast-food sushi counter in Abbotsford, BC, also listed under the alternate name Young's Kitchen Sushi, suggesting a possible rebranding or shared kitchen arrangement. It offers quick Japanese-style food in a strip-mall unit, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists passing through the central Abbotsford area.

restaurant.name: Sushi Box
restaurant.desc: Sushi Box is a sushi restaurant in south Burnaby operating out of 8671 Tenth Avenue. It offers both in-person dining with reservations and online ordering for pick-up or delivery. Its location along Tenth Avenue in a residential-commercial area makes it a potential meal stop for cyclists riding routes through south Burnaby.

restaurant.name: The Penny Farthing Pub
restaurant.desc: The Penny Farthing Pub is a well-established (est. 2001) Olde English-style pub in the heart of Victoria's Oak Bay Village, with four crackling fireplaces, Victorian-etched glass, and an extended patio where dogs and kids are welcome. It takes its name directly from the iconic 19th-century penny farthing bicycle and celebrates that era's whimsical, adventurous spirit through its decor and memorabilia. Part of a four-venue Victoria pub group, it serves modern British comfort food sourced from local land and sea.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states: 'Do you have gluten free menu items? Yes! Many items on our menu can be made Gluten free. Please inform your server of any dietary restrictions or allergies.'

restaurant.name: Seaport City Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Seaport City Seafood Restaurant is a contemporary Chinese fine dining destination on Cambie Street in Vancouver, specializing in premium seafood dishes made with carefully hand-picked fresh ingredients. The bilingual (English and Chinese) establishment aims to deliver a multisensory dining experience that blends the soul of traditional Chinese seafood cuisine with a modern, upscale atmosphere.

restaurant.name: Sorriso Restaurant & Deli
restaurant.desc: Sorriso Italian Restaurant is an Italian eatery located in Kamloops, BC. Beyond its cuisine type, no further details about the establishment — its setting, specialties, or cyclist amenities — could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Conte Store & Deli
restaurant.desc: Conte Store & Deli is an Italian specialty market and café in Richmond, offering prepared foods and imported items. The business serves customers seeking quick meals or provisions typical of an Italian marketplace, making it a useful stop for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: The Crane and Robin
restaurant.desc: The Crane and Robin is a seasonal dine-in restaurant tucked into Montague Harbour Marina on Galiano Island, serving sustainably caught BC seafood, pasture-raised meats from Berryman Farms on the Saanich Peninsula, and a menu heavily weighted toward vegan and gluten-free options. It draws a mix of boaters, hikers, and cyclists visiting the Gulf Islands, operating on a strictly first-come, first-served basis with no reservations. The setting at the marina means cyclists arriving via the Galiano ferry land in easy riding distance.

notes.Takeout: FAQ states takeout is case-by-case: not reliably available in high season due to dine-in demand, but possible in shoulder seasons or slower days
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ explicitly confirms: 'All of our vegetarian items are vegan, only the sandwiches contain gluten.' Menu marks V and GF items throughout including salads, tacos, soups, and sandwiches

restaurant.name: Abbott St. Cafe
restaurant.desc: Abbott St. Cafe is a casual cafe in Kelowna, BC. Without access to its website or detailed OSM amenity tags, specific facilities and services for touring cyclists cannot be confirmed.

restaurant.name: SULA Indian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Sula is an award-winning Indian restaurant established in 2010 on Commercial Drive, named best Indian restaurant in Vancouver by both Vancouver Magazine and Georgia Straight in 2025. The menu spans traditional Indian dishes, tandoor cooking, street food, and signature craft cocktails, with three Vancouver locations. Touring cyclists can dine in or order takeout from the original Commercial Drive location on one of the city's most vibrant cycling corridors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website FAQ states: 'all Sula Indian Restaurant locations offer a dedicated vegetarian and vegan section. Enjoy plant-based starters, dairy-free curries, and breads made without animal products.' No gluten-free claim confirmed

restaurant.name: Smoke and Bones
restaurant.desc: Smoke & Bones BBQ is an authentic Southern-style barbecue restaurant on North Vancouver's Marine Drive, cooking meats low and slow in hardwood smokers sourced from the Deep South. The owners trained under pitmasters Dr. BBQ and Paul Kirk — a 7-time World BBQ Champion — and hold both the Canadian National BBQ Championship and a US Best-of-the-Best Rib title. Cyclists can eat inside or on the heated outdoor patio, with takeout and Metro-wide delivery also available.

detail.address: 999 Marine Drive, North Vancouver, BC V7P1S4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Non-Meat Sides N' Sweets' section, a Beyond Burger described as 'Great non meat option!', Los Cabos Salad, Mexican Street Corn Salad, Caesar Salad, and Brussels Sprouts

restaurant.name: Butter Baked Goods
restaurant.desc: Butter Baked Goods is a beloved neighbourhood bakery and café in Vancouver's MacKenzie Heights, founded by bestselling cookbook author Rosie Daykin. The shop is known for its handmade pastries, custom celebration cakes, cupcakes, and seasonal Afternoon Tea service. A touring cyclist could stop here for freshly baked goods and coffee in a welcoming community setting.

restaurant.name: MYST Asian Fusion
restaurant.desc: MYST Asian Fusion is a multi-award-winning Taiwanese-inspired restaurant on the Kingsway corridor in Burnaby, named 2023 Burnaby Business Excellence Awards Business of the Year and repeatedly recognized as Best Fusion by local media. The team of Taiwanese chefs curates a broad menu spanning breakfast through late-night snacks, drawing on Taiwanese night-market traditions alongside fresh local ingredients. It is part of a growing Lower Mainland chain with locations also in Vancouver and Langley.

restaurant.name: Conversations Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Conversations Coffee House is a cafe on MacKenzie Avenue in Revelstoke. It serves the local community and provides a convenient stop for cyclists traveling through this mountain destination. Specific details about services and amenities could not be verified.

restaurant.name: Japolo
restaurant.desc: Pho Japolo is a proudly family-run Vietnamese and Japanese fusion restaurant in business since 1995, now with four locations across Metro Vancouver. The North Vancouver spot on Marine Drive serves classic pho in multiple configurations alongside inventive sushi creations like sushi pizza and sushi burgers that have made it a long-standing neighbourhood favourite. Generous portions and a welcoming, homey atmosphere make it a solid stop for a substantial meal after a ride.

detail.address: 2070 Marine Drive, North Vancouver, BC V7P 1V7

notes.Takeout: Website shows 'Order Online' for the North Vancouver location; menu also notes 'for take-out, only large available' for pho items

restaurant.name: Edo Japan
restaurant.desc: Edo Japan is a Canadian-founded, Japanese-inspired fast-casual chain established in Calgary in 1979, now with over 200 locations nationwide. The Outlook Village location in Mission serves teppanyaki-grilled meals, hand-rolled sushi, ramen, and bubble tea from a shopping-centre unit on the Lougheed Highway. Dine-in seating, takeout, and delivery are all available, making it a practical hot-meal stop on a Highway 7 corridor ride.

detail.address: 31999 Lougheed Highway, Unit 102D, Mission, BC V2V 1A4

restaurant.name: Shavasana Cafe
restaurant.desc: Shavasana Art Gallery & Café is a combined art gallery and café perched on a promontory at the edge of 'The Village' on Mayne Island, with views of Active Pass. The café offers coffee, a reported 23 varieties of tea, and locally baked cookies and squares alongside rotating exhibitions of local and regional artists running May through October. Described as one of only about seven things to do on Mayne Island, it's a distinctive cultural stop for cyclists exploring the Gulf Islands.

detail.address: 457 Village Bay Road, Mayne Island, BC V0N 2J2

restaurant.name: Icy Bar
restaurant.desc: Icy Bar is a dessert-focused restaurant on Granville Street in South Vancouver, tagged in OpenStreetMap under the cuisine category 'dessert'. It offers indoor seating and maintains an Instagram presence under @icybar_granville. For touring cyclists passing through the Marpole-Oakridge corridor, it represents a potential rest stop for sweet treats along a busy urban arterial.

restaurant.name: Charles Dickens' Pub
restaurant.desc: A lively public house on Beacon Ave in Sidney offering 20 local, domestic, and imported drafts and ciders — including several Vancouver Island craft beers — alongside a full pub food menu ranging from wings and poutine to roasted salmon cobb salad. The kitchen stays open late on weekends and the pub hosts regular events including pool, darts, open mic nights, and music bingo. It sits on Sidney's main commercial strip, making it a natural refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the Saanich Peninsula.

notes.Takeout: Several menu items are explicitly marked 'Dine in only. Not for takeout' (calamari, nachos, taco salad), implying takeout is available for the remainder of the menu

restaurant.name: Wendy's
restaurant.desc: Wendy's is a major North American fast-food chain known for its square, fresh-never-frozen beef burgers, the iconic Frosty dessert, and year-round chili. This location offers outdoor seating and takeout, making it a serviceable calorie stop for touring cyclists moving through the area east of Vancouver. The full menu includes burgers, chicken sandwiches, salads, baked potatoes, and breakfast items.

restaurant.name: Rusty Rail Outdoor B.B.Q. & Beer Garden
restaurant.desc: The Rusty Rail is a seasonal outdoor BBQ and beer garden located at the summit of Grouse Mountain, part of the broader Grouse Mountain resort complex above North Vancouver. It sits within the same destination that hosts the Grouse Bike Park, making it a natural post-ride stop for mountain bikers accessing the lift-served trails. The outdoor seating area faces the mountain environment with views toward Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Taka
restaurant.desc: Taka Japanese Restaurant is a locally beloved spot in Kamloops specializing in fresh handcrafted Japanese cuisine, most famous for its Oshi Sushi — a pressed or box-style sushi unique to the menu. The restaurant combines traditional Japanese flavours with Western influences, offering an extensive menu of sushi rolls, teriyaki, ramen, tempura, and bento boxes. Alcohol is served on premises, vegan options are available, and delivery is offered through UberEats, Skip the Dishes, and DoorDash, making it convenient for cyclists who may prefer to order ahead.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'Vegan Options' in the amenity summary; gluten-free soy sauce available as an add-on in the online ordering system

restaurant.name: Krispy Samosa
restaurant.desc: Krispy Samosa is a family-owned takeout shop serving freshly made samosas crafted from a grandmother's recipe with a variety of fillings including potato and peas, paneer, butter chicken, tandoori chicken, and halal beef. All items are halal-certified and the shop offers vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options. It is a quick, flavourful pit stop for cyclists looking for an affordable and filling snack.

detail.address: 110-2940 King George Blvd, Surrey BC V4P 0E4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists Vegetarian Samosa (labelled 'Vegetarian. Vegan.') and gluten-free options explicitly available across multiple menu items

restaurant.name: Mr. Mango
restaurant.desc: Mr. Mango is a bubble tea cafe occupying a commercial unit at 8260 Westminster Highway in Richmond. It sits in a busy retail corridor of Richmond that is accessible to cyclists travelling along Westminster Highway. Beyond the OSM bubble-tea classification, further details about the business cannot be confirmed due to a mismatch with the discovered website.

restaurant.name: Chai Coffee Company
restaurant.desc: Chai Coffee Company is a specialty chai and coffee café founded by a Punjabi family with a three-generation-old homemade chai masala spice blend, positioned at the doorstep of Surrey's Scott Road Transit Hub. Alongside its signature chai varieties, it serves specialty coffee sourced from Canadian roasters and a food menu spanning Indian snacks like samosas and kathi rolls to croissants and freshly prepared sandwiches. Its transit-hub location and strong takeout focus make it a practical and culturally distinctive stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: No GF claim found on website or in

restaurant.name: The Old Caboose Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Old Caboose Restaurant is a Clearwater landmark originally constructed from a historic local railway caboose, giving the dining room a genuinely distinctive character. It serves a broad all-day menu spanning breakfast, burgers, pizza, pasta, and seafood, with a fully licensed pub on site. Situated on Highway 5 directly across from the Wells Gray Tourist Information building, it sits at a natural gateway for cyclists heading into Wells Gray Provincial Park.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Veggie Omelet (mushrooms, green pepper, tomato), House Salad, Greek Salad, and other vegetable-based items. No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Sweet Thea Bakery
restaurant.desc: Sweet Thea Bakery is an artisan bakery-café with multiple BC locations; the Tsawwassen outpost sits inside the BC Ferries terminal, making it a natural resupply stop for cyclists boarding or disembarking a ferry. The operation is known for its three-day naturally leavened sourdough using certified organic BC-grown wheat, alongside freshly baked pastries and a made-from-scratch café menu of breakfasts, soups, and sandwiches. The bakery donates its daily surplus to local charities, reflecting the founders' community-first ethos.

detail.address: Tsawwassen Quay BC Ferries Terminal, Tsawwassen, BC

restaurant.name: Friesen's Country Tyme Garden
restaurant.desc: Friesen's Countrytyme Gardens is a farm-to-table breakfast and lunch institution that has served the Coldstream community since 1994, nestled in a picturesque outdoor garden setting on Kalamalka Lake Road and surrounded by local farms including their own. The menu spans house-baked breads (sourdough, rye, gluten-free buckwheat), an extensive pastry selection, eggs benedicts, and specialty espresso drinks — nearly everything made in-house. The welcoming outdoor patio and rural Okanagan setting make it a natural and rewarding stop for cyclists riding through the North Okanagan.

detail.address: 9172 Kalamalka Lake Rd, Coldstream BC V1B 3C4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a Veggie Benny (vegetarian eggs benedict); bakery menu lists Gluten Free Buckwheat bread as a house-baked option

restaurant.name: Migoto sushi
restaurant.desc: Migoto Sushi is a Japanese and sushi restaurant located in North Vancouver. It appears to specialise in rolls based on the Facebook handle 'rollspecialist', suggesting a focus on creative or specialty sushi rolls. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a sit-down Japanese dining option in the North Vancouver area.

restaurant.name: Neptune Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Neptune Seafood Restaurant is a long-established Cantonese seafood and dim sum restaurant founded in 1997, part of the Neptune Restaurant Group's multi-location Lower Mainland chain. The Coquitlam Centre location is renowned for abalone and gourmet dim sum, holds membership in the Commanderie des Cordons Bleu de France, and has received Vancouver's Top Ten Chinese Restaurant award. The space includes flexible banquet rooms, making it a substantial full-service dining stop for cyclists in the Tri-Cities area.

restaurant.name: Yaki Joe's Gormet Pizza
restaurant.desc: Yaki Joe's is a locally owned and independently operated pizza restaurant with locations in both Merritt and Kamloops, BC, known for stone-oven baking, made-from-scratch crusts, and a commitment to fully fresh, handmade ingredients. Beyond pizza, the menu spans calzones, wings, wraps, salads, and pastas — all made in-house with no packaged shortcuts. Travelling cyclists will find a sit-down restaurant with a kids menu, online ordering, and delivery available from 4 PM.

restaurant.name: Dairy Queen
restaurant.desc: Dairy Queen serves ice cream and burgers at this Hastings Street location. The shop offers takeaway service, making it a convenient food stop for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Pink Geranium
restaurant.desc: The Pink Geranium is a market, café, and e-bike rental hub at the north end of Galiano Island, reopened in 2021 in a historic building that first housed a beloved island restaurant founded in 1972. The café serves espresso drinks, breakfast and lunch sandwiches, baked goods, and pantry items, making it a natural provisioning stop for cyclists on the island. It also operates as the island's designated e-bike rental point and check-in location for the Bodega Ridge resort properties.

detail.address: 18585 Porlier Pass Rd, Galiano Island, BC V0N 1P0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'VEGGIE BREAKFAST SANDWICH'; no GF options mentioned on website

restaurant.name: Pizza 64
restaurant.desc: Pizza 64 is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 2010 with 20+ locations across British Columbia, known for freshly made dough and sauce prepared at each location. The Abbotsford location offers a broad menu of specialty, signature, and gourmet pizzas alongside wings, pasta, and sides. Online ordering is available, making it a convenient takeout stop for cyclists passing through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian pizzas: Garden Fresh (vegetables, no meat), Pesto Veggie (garlic, spinach, onions, green peppers, tomatoes), Passion of India and Shahi Paneer (tandoori paneer). No explicit vegan or gluten-free claims found

restaurant.name: Roll N Bowl
restaurant.desc: Roll N Bowl is a Japanese-inspired restaurant on Yates Street in the heart of downtown Victoria, serving an extensive menu of sushi rolls, rice bowls, poke, and Asian fusion dishes. Online ordering with pickup from the 788 Yates St location is fully supported through their Square-powered website. Its central location in a dense commercial block makes it an easy refuelling stop for cyclists moving through downtown.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian items including Edamame, Seaweed Salad, Avocado roll, Kappa (cucumber) roll, Yam Roll, Shiitake roll, Yam Tempura, and the Spring house roll (avo, cucumber, salad, mango)

restaurant.name: Cafe Vosino
restaurant.desc: Cafe Vosino is a community-owned cooperative café in the heart of Sooke, BC, born when local patrons pooled resources to purchase and reopen the much-loved 'Stick in the Mud' coffee house — its new name a nod to Sooke's historic postal code V0S 1N0. Operated under the Sooke Community Investment Cooperative, it functions as both a neighbourhood gathering place and a small retail hub offering locally baked bread and café merchandise. Touring cyclists passing through Sooke will find a welcoming stop with outdoor seating and a strong community character.

restaurant.name: COBS Bread
restaurant.desc: COBS Bread is a Canadian franchise bakery (part of the Australian Bakers Delight family) baking all products fresh from scratch on-site every day — no frozen or refrigerated goods. The Commercial Drive location on one of Vancouver's most vibrant neighbourhood corridors offers a wide range of breads, rolls, scones, cruffins, croissants, and savoury items including pizza-style products. Leftover baked goods are donated to local charities at day's end, a notable community practice.

restaurant.name: Fatburger
restaurant.desc: Fatburger is a classic burger chain with roots going back to a 1947 Los Angeles hamburger stand, now Canadian-owned and operated since 2005. The Kamloops location at Summit Drive serves build-your-own burgers made with fresh, never-frozen Alberta Angus beef, alongside chicken, plant-based options, and hand-scooped milkshakes. Every order is cooked-to-order, making it a solid stop for a hot, customizable meal mid-ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists 'plant-based burgers' as a menu item

restaurant.name: Ava Bakery
restaurant.desc: Ava Bakery is a family-owned Persian bakery in Port Coquitlam, founded during the COVID-19 pandemic by a couple who pivoted from hospitality and healthcare into traditional Iranian baking. The shop specializes in authentic Persian breads — Taftoon, Barbary, Lavash, Shirmal, and whole wheat Barbari Naan — alongside pastries, sweets, and prepared dishes such as Haleem and Persian Noodle Soup. It offers touring cyclists a rare chance to stock up on freshly baked breads and traditional Iranian snacks in the Tri-Cities area.

detail.address: 2627 Shaughnessy St #155, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 0E1

restaurant.name: Sushi Gio Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Sushi Gio is a Japanese restaurant in Langley offering sushi and Japanese cuisine with dine-in and online ordering for takeout. It provides a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Sabhai Thai
restaurant.desc: Sabhai Thai is a family-owned authentic Thai restaurant that has operated since 2006, now running two Vancouver Island locations — Sidney and Langford. The Sirimalalak family cooks from scratch using traditional Thai recipes and ingredients, and has earned repeat recognition as the top ethnic restaurant in Sidney. A touring cyclist stopping in Langford will find a full sit-down menu spanning noodles, curries, soups, and appetizers, with vegetarian and vegan options throughout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states the menu includes 'a variety of dishes to choose from for everyone, including meat, vegetarian, and vegan meals.' Specific vegetarian and vegan items appear on both lunch and dinner menus (e.g., Vegetarian Spring Rolls, Vegetarian Phad Thai, Garden Delight combo)

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: This McDonald's on 152 Street in Surrey is a drive-through fast food location serving burgers, breakfast, and McCafé coffee to go. It sits in a busy commercial corridor and is wheelchair accessible, making it a convenient roadside stop for touring cyclists cutting through the Fraser Valley region. The broad menu and takeout-friendly format make it a reliable resupply point for calories on the road.

restaurant.name: Sol Lee's Korean Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Sol Lee's Korean Restaurant is a Korean eatery located in a unit at 329 North Road in Coquitlam, BC. It offers touring cyclists a chance to refuel with Korean cuisine in the heart of the Tri-Cities area. The restaurant was confirmed present as of August 2024 via OSM community verification.

restaurant.name: Chuan Ku BBQ Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Chuan Ku BBQ Restaurant is a Richmond dining destination specializing in Old Beijing cuisine, with a menu spanning grilled whole fish, skewers, copper stove hot pot, spicy crab, and sheep scorpion. The restaurant offers more than 100 dishes rooted in traditional northern Chinese cooking, making it a distinctive stop for cyclists exploring Richmond's diverse food scene. Online ordering for pickup is available.

restaurant.name: Owl's Nest
restaurant.desc: Owl's Nest Bakery Bistro is a cozy all-day breakfast and lunch spot in Chemainus offering house-made baked goods, eggs benedicts on fresh focaccia, and a full espresso bar. The cafe offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a comfortable stop for cyclists passing through town. A Saltair location also exists, giving touring cyclists along that corridor another option.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'We have gluten free and dairy free options'; menu labels Veggie Bowl, Gluten Free Veggie Bowl, Roast Veggie Grilled Sandwich, and Apple Pecan Spinach Salad as vegetarian or gluten-free

restaurant.name: Joga's
restaurant.desc: Joga's is a local coffee shop in Grand Forks offering wireless internet access to customers. It serves as a convenient rest stop for touring cyclists passing through town.

restaurant.name: Village Bistro
restaurant.desc: A vegetarian-only restaurant located in Crescent Valley. Serves as a plant-based dining destination for local and touring visitors.

restaurant.name: Steveston Seafood House
restaurant.desc: Steveston Seafood House is an award-winning fine dining restaurant in the heart of historic Steveston village, celebrated for its creative Pacific seafood menus built around locally sourced BC ingredients including Qualicum Bay scallops, Salt Spring Island mussels, and daily-catch fish. The menu also draws on the Calabrian coastal cooking traditions of the chef's family, weaving West Coast bounty with rustic Italian heritage across dinner, lunch, and weekend brunch services. Steveston sits at the terminus of popular Metro Vancouver cycling routes along the waterfront and dyke trail network.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dinner menu includes a dedicated 'plantbased' section featuring Cauliflower Steak and Roasted Red Pepper Linguini

restaurant.name: Panago
restaurant.desc: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain known for using fresh dough made from 100% Canadian wheat and organic tomato sauce, with a broad menu of customizable pizzas, salads, sides, and desserts. This North Vancouver location on Hastings Street offers delivery and takeout. The chain emphasizes clean ingredients with no artificial colours or flavours, making it a convenient calorie-replenishment stop for cyclists passing through the area.

detail.address: 6665 Hastings Street, Unit E, North Vancouver, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We've got abundant veggie, dairy-free and meat-free choices to help you live your best plant life.'

restaurant.name: Samurai Bowl
restaurant.desc: Samurai Bowl is a Japanese-Asian fusion quick-service restaurant in Whistler's Creekside neighbourhood, open 7 days a week and serving ramen, Korean fried chicken, poke bowls, and Thai curry. It is part of a locally owned family of four Samurai restaurants across Whistler and Squamish, established in Creekside in 2006. The restaurant emphasizes eco-friendly practices, using compostable and recyclable takeout containers—an appeal for environmentally conscious cyclists on tour.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page states 'We also have family friendly and vegetarian options.'

restaurant.name: Hui Lau Shan
restaurant.desc: Hui Lau Shan is a well-known Hong Kong dessert chain with over 50 years of history, specialising in handmade mango desserts, Chinese herbal jelly, and nourishing sweet soups. The Richmond location serves the Lower Mainland's large Chinese-Canadian community with authentic Hong Kong-style treats. Takeout is available, making it a quick stop for a sweet break on a ride through Richmond.

restaurant.name: Caffè W
restaurant.desc: Caffè W has been serving the West Broadway neighbourhood since 1995, making it one of Vancouver's longer-running independent cafés. The menu ranges from classic espresso drinks and specialty lattes to smoothies, frappes, and a full brunch lineup. The café is known for its exclusive 'Dubai Chocolate' creations — a pistachio-and-chocolate dessert series not found elsewhere — and a rotating display of artisan pastries.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Hot drinks menu explicitly lists alternative milks: Oat, Almond, Soy — confirming dairy-free/vegan-friendly options available

restaurant.name: Green Leaf Salad Bar
restaurant.desc: Green Leaf Salad Bar is a Lebanese restaurant and by-weight salad bar in Vancouver's West End, celebrated as a Readers' Choice 'Best of the City 2014' winner by WE Vancouver and a four-time consecutive Yelp People's Choice award recipient (2016–2019). The menu centres on Lebanese staples — chicken shawarma, falafel wraps, daily rotating hot specials such as beef kafta and moussaka — alongside a fresh seasonal salad bar priced by weight. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a compact, fast-casual spot with both indoor and outdoor seating and a full catering operation.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a dedicated 'Vegetarian Plate' (falafel, hummus, salads) and 'Falafel Wrap'; catering page labels Tabouleh and Fattoush as (VG, DF) and Hummus and Fattoush as (GF)

restaurant.name: Pho Japolo
restaurant.desc: Pho Japolo is a proudly family-run Vietnamese and Japanese fusion restaurant operating since 1995, with the Kitsilano outpost anchoring a four-location Lower Mainland chain. The menu spans hearty beef noodle soups with a range of traditional pho combinations alongside inventive sushi creations like sushi pizza and sushi burgers. Regulars highlight the generous portions, warm homey atmosphere, and reliably consistent food as reasons to keep coming back.

notes.Takeout: Menu page notes 'for take-out, only large available' under the pho section, confirming takeout service

restaurant.name: Papa John's
restaurant.desc: Papa John's on Bainbridge Avenue is a pizza chain location in Burnaby offering both delivery and carryout, with a menu featuring pizza, breadsticks, and wings. It is a no-drive-through format, making it a straightforward stop for cyclists looking to grab a hot meal or order ahead for pickup. The location is part of the Papa John's Canadian franchise network.

restaurant.name: La Cerveceria Astilleros
restaurant.desc: La Cervecería Astilleros is a Mexican-inspired craft brewery and taproom in the Shipyards district of Lower Lonsdale, bringing Mexican ingredients and brewing traditions to BC craft beer. Their award-winning Salted Lime Lager took first place at the 2023 Canadian Brewing Awards, and a constantly rotating small-batch tap list means there is always something new on pour. Cyclists can refuel with tacos, burritos, and margaritas alongside the house lagers, with both indoor and outdoor seating available.

detail.address: 226 Esplanade E, North Vancouver BC, V7L 1A3
