restaurant.desc: Jackknife Brewing is a punk-metal-inspired craft brewery and pizzeria in Kelowna, BC, celebrated for experimental beers brewed with centuries-old Nordic Kveik farmhouse yeasts and locally foraged ingredients like spruce tips, juniper, and wild berries — earning a World Beer Cup silver in 2024. The space doubles as an intimate live music venue they call 'the dungeon,' hosting regular metal and rock shows. Touring cyclists can refuel on classic New York-style pizza alongside creative, award-winning ales.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple pizza options (The Convincer, The Matango Terror) explicitly offer 'your choice of vegetarian or vegan' on the menu page

restaurant.name: The Shepherd's Inn - Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Shepherd's Inn is a family-owned highway stop at Mile 72 of the Alaska Highway, about 42 km northwest of Fort St. John, serving home-cooked western and breakfast meals with bread, soups, and pies made from scratch on-site. It is part of a larger complex that includes a motel, convenience store, and fueling station — functioning as a genuine full-service oasis on a remote stretch of highway. Bus and RV tour groups are welcome with advance notice, and the restaurant takes to-go orders by phone.

detail.address: 11890 Shepherds Inn Frontage Road, Charlie Lake, BC V1J 8L5

restaurant.name: Hatsuki Sushi
restaurant.desc: Hatsuki Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Kamloops. The business maintains an online presence but provides limited information about its facilities and services on the website.

restaurant.name: Harry's Fish & Chips
restaurant.desc: Harry's Fish & Chips is a British-inspired fish and chip restaurant that opened in 2021 in the Tsawwassen area of Delta, BC. The kitchen hand-cuts fresh local Delta potatoes daily and makes its batter, tartar sauce, and coleslaw in-house. Both dine-in and takeout are offered, with ample seating and straightforward parking according to customer reviews.

detail.address: 4949 Canoe Pass Way, Unit 902, Delta, BC V4M 0B2

restaurant.name: Fable Diner & Bar
restaurant.desc: Fable Diner & Bar occupies the base of Vancouver's historic Lee Building on Richards Street, growing out of the farm-to-table tradition established by Fable Kitchen in Kitsilano in 2012. The kitchen crafts nearly everything from scratch using locally sourced BC ingredients, offering a menu that spans hearty breakfasts, eggs benedicts, smash burgers, and cocktails. Named among 2025's top brunch and lunch destinations in Vancouver, it provides a full sit-down dining experience in the heart of downtown.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu confirms multiple vegetarian items including Garden Salad (mixed greens, avocado, burrata, edamame), House Made Focaccia, Truffle Parm Fries, and Creamy Tomato Soup

restaurant.name: Willows Galley
restaurant.desc: Willows Galley Fish & Chips has been an Estevan Village institution since 1980, tucked into Oak Bay's neighbourhood shopping strip in Victoria. Current owners Dave and Jennifer Higgins returned in 2011 to resurrect the shop's original sourdough fish batter and house-made menu that generations of locals remember. It operates as a takeout counter with a full seafood and burger menu, and uses compostable packaging throughout.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'We welcome call in orders any time for pick up' — appears to be a takeout-only operation
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Landlubber' veggie burger ('Our veggie burger comes with mayo and coleslaw served on a fresh kaiser bun')

restaurant.name: The Irish Heather Shebeen
restaurant.desc: An Irish pub on East Georgia Street in Vancouver offering indoor seating and casual dining. A convenient food and drink stop for cyclists exploring the downtown area.

restaurant.name: All About Pho
restaurant.desc: All About Pho is a Vietnamese restaurant in Surrey serving traditional pho, vermicelli bowls, banh mi, bubble tea, and a broad range of Vietnamese favourites prepared with fresh organic ingredients and family recipes. The restaurant emphasises cleanliness and friendly service and has drawn a loyal local following. Both dine-in and takeout are available, making it a practical stop for a quick, filling meal.

detail.address: 10190 King George Blvd, Surrey, BC V3T 2W4

restaurant.name: Le Petit Saigon
restaurant.desc: A family-owned Vietnamese restaurant that has been serving Victoria since 1986, making it one of the city's most enduring independent eateries. The menu features authentic dishes including grilled lemongrass pork, aromatic pho, and rich coconut curry, all made with fresh ingredients and traditional recipes. Located on Langley Street in downtown Victoria, it's a welcoming sit-down option for cyclists passing through the city core.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Vegetarian options are also available.'

restaurant.name: La Quercia
restaurant.desc: La Quercia is a refined northern Italian restaurant on Vancouver's West 4th Avenue, anchored by a seasonally focused menu built on slow-cooking traditions with housemade bread, charcuterie, preserves, and butchery. Chef Adam Pegg offers both à la carte dining and convivial family-style tasting menus, supported by an in-house sommelier and an extensive all-Italian wine list. An attached Deli counter sells prepared meals, sandwiches, and piadine to take away, offering touring cyclists a quality grab-and-go option on a well-travelled cycling corridor.

notes.Packed lunches: Deli sells sandwiches and piadine as takeaway items suitable for on-road meals
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms vegetarian antipasti and pasta options; vegans accommodated with advance notice at booking; gluten-free made-to-order carnaroli risotto available nightly

restaurant.name: The Boxcar
restaurant.desc: The Boxcar is a cozy cocktail bar and beer parlour on Vancouver's Main Street corridor, pouring craft cocktails and local beers alongside Roma-style pizza from award-winning Mortadella Pizzeria located next door. Named among Canada's Top 50 bars in 2020, it has a neighbourhood feel with indoor seating and a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere. A solid after-ride destination in the Mount Pleasant area for cyclists looking to unwind.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Pizza menu lists Margherita (tomato, fior di latte, basil) and Caprese sandwich (roasted tomato, fior di latte, basil, jalapeño ranch, arugula) — both vegetarian by ingredient listing

restaurant.name: Liquids + Solids
restaurant.desc: Liquids + Solids is a scratch-made soup café that has been feeding Vancouverites since 2001, now operating solely from its factory café on Franklin Street at Commercial Drive. The kitchen turns out a rotating selection of house-made soups, stews, and chilis alongside grilled sandwiches, salads, pot pies, and quiches. It doubles as the production hub for their retail soupetc! brand, giving the spot an authentic, working-kitchen feel distinct from a typical café.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu pages list dedicated Vegan Sandwiches (e.g. Mom's Meatless Loaf(V)) and Gluten-Free Sandwiches (e.g. Mom's Meatless Loaf(GF)), plus the note 'Ask us about our gluten-free options!'

restaurant.name: Famous ROME Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Famous ROME Ice Cream is a family-run gelato and ice cream shop on Marine Drive in White Rock, opened in October 2021 by a Korean-Canadian family. Situated near the beach and pier, it offers over 50 flavours spanning gelato, sorbetto, and ice cream — including a dedicated kid's zone and vegan-friendly sorbetto — alongside coffee, tea, and handmade baked goods. The outdoor seating and waterfront location make it a natural refreshment stop for cyclists on the White Rock waterfront.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website products page lists 'Sorbetto for Vegan (non-dairy)' with multiple flavours (Strawberry, Mango, Lemon, Passion fruit, etc.) and 'No Sugar Added' gelato options

restaurant.name: Carnitas Don Jose
restaurant.desc: Carnitas Don Jose is a Mexican food-court stall in downtown Vancouver run by Don José Velázquez, an 8-time Mexican charrería national champion turned chef who brings traditional Carnitas Estilo Michoacán from Zamora, Michoacán to the city. The menu centres on slow-cooked carnitas served with corn tortillas, salsas, and fresh accompaniments, made with locally sourced ingredients. With over 1,500 Uber Eats reviews at 4.7 stars, it has earned a devoted following as a quick, affordable stop for authentic Mexican street food in the heart of Vancouver.

detail.address: 88 West Pender Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 6N9

restaurant.name: Noodle Island
restaurant.desc: Noodle Island is a Vietnamese restaurant situated in a commercial unit on Fraser Highway in Surrey. It serves noodle-based dishes consistent with Vietnamese cuisine, making it a potential stop for touring cyclists looking for a filling meal along this busy corridor.

restaurant.name: Black's Pub
restaurant.desc: Black's Pub is a warm, lively pub and restaurant at the base of Whistler Mountain in the heart of Whistler Village, part of the Gibbons Whistler hospitality group. It serves breakfast through to late evening, with a full all-day food menu alongside local craft beers, curated wines, and creative cocktails. A patio with panoramic mountain views and weekly events like Bandaoke (live-band karaoke) make it a hub for both outdoor adventurers and the local community.

restaurant.name: Mogu Fried Chicken
restaurant.desc: Mogu Fried Chicken is a 34-seat izakaya-style Japanese fried chicken restaurant on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, opened by Yuji and Kumiko Aoki after seven years operating the Mogu food truck at Howe and Dunsmuir. The restaurant is known for its umami-rich boneless fried chicken paired with an extensive selection of Japanese draft beers, sake flights, whisky, and house cocktails. Both dine-in and takeout are offered, including family- and party-sized fried chicken packs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple items explicitly marked '(vegetarian)' on both dine-in and takeout menus: Mogu Salad, Creamy Potato Salad, Curried Macaroni Salad, Shio Garlic Cabbage Salad, Edamame, Sea Salt & Aonori Fries, Spicy Garlic Fries, Korokke (v)

restaurant.name: Ithaka Greek Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Ithaka is a family-owned Greek restaurant open since 2014, serving authentic Mediterranean cuisine from recipes passed down through the family. It holds the distinction of being the only Greek restaurant in North America to serve as a gastronomy sponsor of the Great Greek Wines awards, and claims the largest selection of Greek wines in western Canada. The restaurant operates as a dine-in, takeout, and delivery destination in central Victoria, and also hosts private events and catering.

restaurant.name: BarBurrito
restaurant.desc: BarBurrito is Canada's largest burrito chain, proudly Canadian since 2005 and now operating 385+ locations nationwide. This Abbotsford Village location serves fully customizable Mexican-inspired meals — burritos, bowls, tacos, and quesadillas — made to order from fresh in-house ingredients. It's a convenient fast-casual stop for cyclists moving through Abbotsford along the Sumas Way corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Nutrition page lists 'Veggie Ground' and 'Falafel' protein options and a 'Gluten Free' tortilla option

restaurant.name: Bombay Kitchen + Bar
restaurant.desc: Bombay Kitchen on Denman is an Indian restaurant in Vancouver's West End, situated on Denman Street — a primary cycling corridor linking the city to Stanley Park. The kitchen serves a broad menu of curries, tandoori dishes, and street-food items like kathi rolls, drawing on traditional Indian recipes and fresh local ingredients. Catering for events from small private parties to corporate gatherings and weddings is also offered.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Catering menu lists a dedicated 'Vegetarian / Vegan' combo option; gluten-free naans noted as available across multiple menu sections ('Gluten-free naans available')

restaurant.name: The Ruddy on Bowen
restaurant.desc: The Ruddy on Bowen is an independent grocery store and café that has served Bowen Island's Snug Cove since 1997, situated within walking distance of the ferry terminal at Horseshoe Bay. It combines a full market — fresh produce, local meats and seafood, artisanal bakery, and specialty cheeses — with a café serving freshly brewed coffee and ready-made meals to go. The store has a sustainability focus, including a soap refill station and a sharewares reusable cup program.

detail.address: 996 Dorman Road, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G0

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: This Starbucks location sits along Ladner Trunk Road in Tsawwassen, positioning it as a convenient stop for cyclists traveling through the Delta region or connecting to the BC Ferries terminal. As a full-service Starbucks café, it offers a broad menu of hot and cold beverages alongside grab-and-go food items. The corporate brand's consistent service model makes it a reliable refuelling point on longer coastal rides.

restaurant.name: Dumpling Drop
restaurant.desc: Dumpling Drop has been operating in Victoria's historic Chinatown since 2018, serving deep-fried dumplings with housemade chili oil alongside rotating sides like cucumber salad and mango sticky rice. Founded by Tarn and Toom, the restaurant uses traditional methods with a modern twist and offers dine-in, takeout, and frozen dumplings available at the counter or through Vancouver Island grocery wholesalers. It is a compact, focused spot well-suited to a quick hot meal or stocking up frozen dumplings for the road.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a 'Vegan' dumpling and a 'Vegan Weekly Rotating Special'. FAQ confirms gluten-free sides (rice & chili oil, cucumber salad, yuzu Brussels sprouts), though dumplings themselves are explicitly stated as not gluten-free

restaurant.name: New Bhaia Sweet Shop and Restaurant
restaurant.desc: New Bhaia Sweet Shop and Restaurant has been a community fixture on Fraser Street since 1997, specializing in East Indian sweets and widely known for their beef, chicken, and veggie samosas. The kitchen offers a broad menu of South Asian classics — butter chicken, lamb and goat curries, biryani, and tandoori dishes — alongside catering services for larger occasions. For a touring cyclist rolling through South Vancouver, it is a reliable stop for a sit-down or take-away meal with real depth of menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists veggie samosa and a dedicated Vegetarian menu category

restaurant.name: OAKBERRY AÇAI
restaurant.desc: OAKBERRY AÇAI is a Brazilian-origin global açaí chain serving organic açaí bowls, smoothies, and snacks with unlimited toppings, located in the food court of the Metropolis at Metrotown mall in Burnaby. The brand sources its açaí from the Amazon region of Brazil and markets its products as vegan, antioxidant-rich, and free from artificial additives. Cyclists stopping at Metrotown can fuel up with a nutrient-dense bowl, though they would need to navigate mall parking and access.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website front page lists 'Vegan' as a product attribute alongside 'Rich in Antioxidants, Cholesterol Free, Free from Trans Fats'

restaurant.name: Koerner's Pub
restaurant.desc: Koerner's Pub is the long-standing campus pub at the University of British Columbia, tucked into the West Mall area of the UBC Endowment Lands. Self-described as 'the mother of all pubs,' it serves food and drinks and doubles as an event venue for everything from weekly socials to wedding receptions. It is a 19+ establishment and a natural refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the UBC campus loop.

restaurant.name: Harbour House Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Victoria Harbour House is a family-owned steak and seafood restaurant that has been a local favourite since 1980 and has been voted one of the best restaurants in Victoria. The menu features modern regional dishes with seasonal flavours, including a full dinner and drinks menu alongside house-made desserts. The restaurant accommodates walk-in diners as well as reservations for larger parties, making it a solid option for a sit-down meal on a touring itinerary.

restaurant.name: Sushi Heaven
restaurant.desc: Sushi Heaven is a Japanese restaurant in New Westminster offering a broad menu of maki, nigiri, sashimi, donburi, bento boxes, tempura, and aburi oshi. Online ordering is available through the restaurant's own website. The casual sit-down setting with indoor seating makes it a reasonable stop for a touring cyclist moving through the lower mainland.

detail.address: 457B E Columbia St, New Westminster, BC V3L 3X6

restaurant.name: Pendray Tea House
restaurant.desc: Pendray Tea House is the signature restaurant of the Pendray Inn & Tea House, a heritage Victorian mansion built in 1897 and now operating as an upscale boutique hotel steps from Victoria's Inner Harbour. The tea house offers Afternoon Tea, Scottish High Tea, and Traditional Sunday Roast Dinner in period-furnished rooms that evoke the late 19th century. Touring cyclists passing through Victoria's Inner Harbour area — already a hub for Fisherman's Wharf and the ferry terminals — will find it a distinctive stop for a British-style meal.

restaurant.name: Breka Bakery & Cafe
restaurant.desc: Breka Bakery & Café is a local Vancouver family business that started in 2006 and has grown to eight locations, all operating around the clock every day of the year. The Denman Street outpost offers a broad menu of fresh-baked pastries, artisan breads, sandwiches, cakes, donuts, and hot beverages, with dedicated vegan and gluten-free selections. Regularly voted among Vancouver's best bakeries, Breka has built its reputation entirely through word-of-mouth and is a fixture for both locals and visitors.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website's selection page has dedicated 'Vegan' and 'Gluten-Free' sections with multiple labelled items (e.g. Chocolate Banana Coconut Muffin [Vegan & Gluten Friendly], Curried Chickpeas & Kale Wrap [Vegan])

restaurant.name: Boiling Point
restaurant.desc: Boiling Point is a Taiwanese hot soup specialty restaurant chain serving individual hot pot meals cooked at the table, with a wide range of broth bases from Taiwanese spicy to Korean bean paste to Milk Cream Curry. The Vancouver Main Street location is part of a chain with three Canadian outlets and outposts across the US and Japan. Touring cyclists will find a sit-down meal with substantial protein and vegetarian options, plus takeout availability.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists 'Mushroom Veggie' as a soup base option and 'Steamed Veggie' as an appetizer, confirming vegetarian choices

restaurant.name: Camp Café
restaurant.desc: Camp Café occupies a heritage building in Silverton (constructed between 1903 and 1906) and serves freshly baked grab-and-go food made with local, organic, and farm-fresh ingredients. Situated at the gateway to Valhalla Provincial Park on the shores of Slocan Lake, it positions itself as a launching point for outdoor adventures and explicitly describes itself as bike friendly. Staff can provide maps and day-trip inspiration for cyclists exploring the surrounding Slocan Valley.

restaurant.name: Banzai Sushi House
restaurant.desc: Banzai Sushi House is a Japanese sushi restaurant located in a strip mall unit on Westminster Highway in Richmond, operated as a division of Samurai Cambie. The menu spans nigiri, sashimi, donburi, udon, tempura, and an extensive roster of specialty and classic rolls, with party trays available via advance telephone order. It sits across from the Richmond Public Market, placing it in a busy retail hub convenient for cyclists passing through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian items: Kappa Roll (Cucumber), Avocado Roll, Vegetable Roll, Yam Tempura Roll, Yam Cheese Roll, Edamame, Wakame Salad, Miso Soup. No vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Catch Kitchen + Bar
restaurant.desc: Catch Kitchen + Bar is an upscale casual waterfront restaurant on the second floor of Bayview Pier at Fisherman's Wharf in historic Steveston Village, featuring a rooftop patio with a 270-degree panoramic view of the harbour and river inlet. The menu is seafood-forward with locally inspired dishes ranging from fresh crab cakes to peppercorn New York steak, alongside a sports lounge with seven HD screens. Steveston Village is a landmark stop on Richmond's popular cycling dyke routes, making this a natural destination for touring cyclists.

detail.address: 200 - 3866 Bayview St, Steveston Village, Richmond, BC V7E 3B6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes a 'Filter by diet' feature and lists plant-based items including Mediterranean Flatbread (hummus, olives, artichokes), Edamame, and Parmesan Garlic Truffle Yam Fries

restaurant.name: Oh! Zzhu Sam Korean Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Oh! Zzhu Sam Korean Restaurant has been part of the Burnaby community since 2016, offering creative Korean cuisine including stir-fry, octopus with pork belly, and signature Korean fried chicken. The restaurant emphasizes the harmony of food, atmosphere, and service as central to showcasing Korean food and culture. Dine-in service is available, as is delivery.

restaurant.name: The Black Antler
restaurant.desc: The Black Antler is an independent restaurant and bar in downtown Penticton, run by husband-and-wife team Dan and Lynn, who relocated from elsewhere in the Okanagan to fulfil a lifelong dream. The operation includes a microbrewery producing its own Antler lager, and the couple also runs a companion restaurant called The Forest next door. A touring cyclist passing through Penticton will find a locally owned spot with a full bar, weekend brunch, and a personal backstory that sets it apart from chain dining.

restaurant.name: Sushi Maru
restaurant.desc: Maru Sushi (branded as Sushi Maru on its website) is a casual Japanese restaurant on Fraser Highway in Langley, focused on quality sushi made from premium fish and rice. The restaurant seats guests for lunch and dinner and is set up to host family dinners and birthday parties in a relaxed atmosphere. Online ordering is available for those wanting a quick takeout stop.

restaurant.name: Akane Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Akane Japanese Restaurant is a sushi and teriyaki spot in the Walnut Grove neighbourhood of Langley, serving Japanese and Asian cuisine prepared with fresh ingredients. Located in a strip-mall unit, it offers both dine-in and takeout options, including online ordering. It sits along a suburban corridor that cycling routes through the Fraser Valley pass near.

restaurant.name: The Coda
restaurant.desc: The Coda is a live music venue and bar in downtown Victoria hosting jazz, indie rock, folk, swing, and dance music across two stages (Bar Stage and Main Stage). It is primarily a 19+ venue with occasional all-ages events and draws both local talent and touring acts from across Canada. The venue is noted as accessible by stairs only.

restaurant.name: Propaganda Coffee
restaurant.desc: Propaganda Coffee is a specialty multi-roaster café in Vancouver's Chinatown neighbourhood that rotates a curated lineup of Canadian roasters through filter, pour-over, and espresso brewing styles. Three to four coffees are available on the espresso bar at any given time, with batch brew and single-serving pour-overs highlighting different origins. Tea alternatives sourced from O5 Tea and a housemade chai round out the menu for non-coffee drinkers.

detail.address: 209 East Pender Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 1T8

restaurant.name: Takara Sushi
restaurant.desc: Takara Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Burnaby whose name means 'treasure' — a nod to the freshness of their fish and the care put into their craft. They offer both dine-in and takeout service, plus online ordering, making them a convenient stop for a cycling lunch or dinner on Canada Way. The crew's emphasis on friendliness and quality sushi makes it a worthwhile detour for touring cyclists passing through the Burnaby corridor.

restaurant.name: The Keg
restaurant.desc: The Keg Richmond South is a well-known steakhouse and bar situated near the Ironwood Complex at Steveston and No. 5 Road. The location features a heated and covered patio, bar, and lounge, and is wheelchair accessible with free car parking on site. Touring cyclists exploring the Steveston dyke network will find it a convenient spot for a full sit-down dinner.

detail.address: 11151 No. 5 Road, Richmond, British Columbia, V7A 4E8

restaurant.name: Amato Gelato & Cafè
restaurant.desc: Amato Gelato & Cafè is a classic Italian gelato shop in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, carrying on over 85 years of family tradition through the Mario's Gelati lineage. The shop rotates over 72 flavours of authentic Italian gelato and sorbetti made from traditional family recipes using locally sourced BC fruits and dairy. It serves as the public retail storefront for the Mario's Gelati wholesale brand, making it a Vancouver institution for handcrafted Italian frozen desserts.

restaurant.name: C-Lovers
restaurant.desc: C-Lovers is a BC-born fish and chips chain founded in 1984, serving hand-battered halibut, haddock, cod, salmon, and prawns alongside hand-cut Kennebec potato chips in a casual, family-friendly dine-in setting. The Abbotsford location is an Ocean Wise partner, meaning its seafood is certified as responsibly and sustainably sourced. Both dine-in and takeout are available, making it a practical stop for a hungry cyclist wanting a filling seafood meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Take-out menu labels the C-Food Chowder as 'Gluten Friendly!' No vegetarian or vegan options explicitly identified

restaurant.name: Coastal Crust Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Coastal Crust is a family-run pizzeria on Sechelt's Cowrie Street offering handmade-daily-crust pizzas by the slice, artisan deep-dish whole pies, calzones, pastas, and salads. The menu features rotating seasonal specialties and creative topping combinations alongside house favourites. It serves eat-in, takeout, and delivery across a stretch of the Sunshine Coast from Davis Bay to Halfmoon Bay.

restaurant.name: Donair Dude
restaurant.desc: Donair Dude is a BC-born fast food chain that opened its first location during the 2010 Winter Olympics, growing from a single shop into a multi-location franchise serving Mediterranean-style donair wraps, platters, and poutine. The kitchen emphasizes locally sourced BC farm meats slowly roasted in-house, with a broad menu spanning chicken, beef, lamb, and dedicated vegan options. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making this a solid hot-meal stop for cyclists on the North Shore.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website front page lists 'VEGAN' as a distinct menu category; menu includes falafel wraps, falafel platters, falafel plates, tabouli salad, dolmades, hummus, and rice pilaf

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast-food restaurant on Scott Road in the Tsawwassen/Delta area, offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, McCafé coffee drinks, and a drive-through. It is a convenient stop for touring cyclists needing a quick, familiar meal along this corridor. The MyMcDonald's Rewards app provides loyalty points on purchases.

restaurant.name: Mean Poutine
restaurant.desc: Mean Poutine is a family-run gourmet poutine and specialty hot dog chain founded in 2011 by a former BC Lions football player, with origins in Vancouver's Granville entertainment district. The New Westminster location serves a broad menu of creative poutine combinations — from classic Quebec-style to Southern BBQ and Mean Mexicana — alongside a full hot dog lineup, all made with handcrafted recipes and quality ingredients. Indoor seating is available, making it a solid hearty-meal stop for cyclists passing through New Westminster.

detail.address: 581 Sixth St, New Westminster BC V3L 3B9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website front page: 'Have you TASTED OUR VEGETARIAN DISHES? We provide gourmet poutine options for everyone! Check out our Vegetarian & Halal menu items'; New Westminster menu includes 'Mean And Green' with vegetarian gravy. No GF options: Downtown Vancouver menu states 'we do not offer Gluten Free options on our poutine, hot dogs or fries menu.'

restaurant.name: Habit Coffee
restaurant.desc: Habit Coffee is a community-focused coffee shop in Victoria's Chinatown with a strong sustainability ethos, having maintained carbon-neutral operations across both its locations for over 10 years. Beans are ethically sourced through exclusive roasting partner BowsxArrows, and supplies are transported between the two Habit locations via Dutch cargo bike. The shop sources ingredients from local Victoria producers and partners, positioning itself as a genuine neighbourhood hub.

restaurant.name: Ton Ton Sushi
restaurant.desc: Ton Ton Sushi is a Japanese and Korean sushi restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver, serving sushi and a fusion of Japanese and Korean dishes. The restaurant offers online ordering through their website and a dedicated app. Located along the Cambie Street corridor near the Canada Line, it is a convenient stop for cyclists moving through South Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Pho Khanh Express
restaurant.desc: Khanh Express is a family-founded Vietnamese-Cambodian noodle soup restaurant in downtown Vancouver, built as a tribute to the owner's father and his love of pho. The Beatty Street location sits in the heart of a well-connected cycling corridor and offers a broad menu spanning pho, vermicelli, banh mi, and rice dishes with dedicated vegetarian options. Online ordering and a digital loyalty program via LoyLap make it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu page lists a dedicated 'Vegetarian' category alongside other menu sections

restaurant.name: BjornBar Bakery - Burquitlam
restaurant.desc: BjornBar Bakery is a boutique bakery café founded by Tamera Clark, best known for over 30 handcrafted dessert bars — from classic Nanaimo to adventurous Spumoni — all made in-house by hand. The Burquitlam location is one of three Metro Vancouver outposts and serves fresh pastries, savoury lunch items, specialty coffee, and their signature Ganookies (five-inch ganache-filled cookies). It's a sit-down café with a warm, carefully designed atmosphere that makes it a worthwhile stop for cyclists passing through Coquitlam.

notes.Takeout: Online pre-order with in-store pickup is explicitly offered via the website; orders placed at least 48 hours in advance, pickup from 10:00 AM on selected date

restaurant.name: Annalena
restaurant.desc: AnnaLena is a Michelin-starred tasting menu restaurant in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, steps from Kitsilano Beach, owned since 2015 by Chef Michael Robbins and General Manager Jeff Parr. Consistently ranked among Canada's Top 100 Restaurants and an En Route Top 10 New Restaurant in its opening year, it offers an exclusively reservation-based, multi-course tasting menu driven by seasonal local farms and suppliers. The restaurant pairs its evolving menu with an award-winning wine program curated by Michelin-recognised Wine Director Reverie Beall.

restaurant.name: Bloo bby Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Bloo Lounge is a modern shisha and hookah bar on Hastings Street in Burnaby that also serves food and drinks in a lounge setting. The menu spans appetizers, pizza, desserts, and a full drinks list alongside an extensive hookah selection. It bills itself as a social destination where guests can relax, celebrate, and enjoy an immersive sensory atmosphere.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian-suitable items: Vegetariano pizza (green pepper, mushrooms, arugula, fresh tomato, parsley, mozzarella), Margherita pizza, Funghi pizza (mushrooms, kale, mozzarella), yam fries, nachos (meat optional add-on), and garlic parmesan fries

restaurant.name: Five Guys
restaurant.desc: Five Guys on Robson Street is a well-known American-style burger chain in the heart of downtown Vancouver, offering extensively customizable burgers, hot dogs, fresh-cut fries double-cooked in peanut oil, and over 1,000 milkshake combinations. The restaurant uses fresh (never frozen) beef and hand-prepares ingredients daily, providing a calorie-dense refueling option for cyclists riding through the city centre. Both indoor seating and takeout are available, and the location is confirmed open.

restaurant.name: Soft Peaks Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Soft Peaks Ice Cream is an artisanal soft-serve counter near Metrotown in Burnaby, distinguished by monthly rotating flavors such as the earthy matcha 'Green Forest' and seasonal offerings like festive eggnog. Beyond ice cream, the shop serves a full espresso and tea menu in a bright, airy space with distinctive wooden step seating. It offers a calm, welcoming rest stop for cyclists looking for a sweet treat and coffee in the Metrotown area.

restaurant.name: High Tide Grill

restaurant.name: Mama's Rice Bowl

restaurant.name: Vina Taste

restaurant.name: Domino's

restaurant.desc: RMU is an employee-owned mountain bike and ski brand with a flagship restaurant and bar located at the Le Chamois Hotel in Whistler's Upper Village. The shop sells its own line of bikes — including the NIGHTTRAIN 170mm enduro freeride model — alongside skis, mountain bike packs, and apparel, all under the same roof as a full food and beverage offering spanning coffee and breakfast through pizza and burgers. For a cycling tourist, it is a practical dual-purpose stop: refuel with a meal or coffee while browsing or servicing gear in the heart of Whistler's mountain bike scene.

restaurant.name: Panaderia Latina Bakery
restaurant.desc: A Latin American bakery and pastry shop specializing in traditional baked goods and specialty products. Operating as takeaway-only, it serves as a convenient quick-stop for touring cyclists to grab fresh provisions. Located on Joyce Street in Vancouver's east side.

restaurant.name: Yudi Patisserrie
restaurant.desc: Yudi Patisserrie is a patisserie and bakery located in a unit along Alexandra Road in Richmond, a street known for its dense concentration of Asian food businesses. As a pastry shop it would offer baked goods and sweet items useful for cyclists looking to refuel on a ride through the Richmond area. Its Instagram presence (handle: @patisserieyudi) suggests an active, small independent operation.

restaurant.name: Superior Pizza
restaurant.desc: Superior Pizza is a fast-food pizza restaurant in downtown Victoria, established in 2011. They offer takeout via online and phone ordering. A quick meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the city.

restaurant.name: Boston Pizza
restaurant.desc: Boston Pizza Dilworth Centre is a franchise location of Canada's largest casual dining chain, founded in 1964 and now celebrating 60 years of operation. Situated on Highway 97 North, it operates as both a family restaurant and a sports bar, offering a broad menu of pizza, pasta, wings, sandwiches, and more. For cyclists travelling the Okanagan corridor, it provides a familiar, high-capacity sit-down meal stop with dine-in, takeout, and delivery options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'Vegan and Glutenwise® options also available.' GlutenWise® is Boston Pizza's gluten-sensitive menu line; a dedicated GlutenWise® menu category is listed

restaurant.name: Fresh Restaurant & Lounge
restaurant.desc: Fresh Restaurant & Lounge offers regional cuisine in an indoor dining setting in North Vancouver. As a restaurant, it serves as a potential meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: New York Hotdog & Coffee
restaurant.desc: Nooi's New York Hotdog & Coffee is a lively street-food counter on White Rock's Marine Drive offering an eclectic menu that ranges from jumbo hotdogs, BBQ chicken skewers, corn dogs, and ramen to an extensive espresso and specialty beverage program. The Marine Drive waterfront is one of BC's most popular coastal cycling corridors, placing this spot directly in the path of touring cyclists. Sweet options—popsicles, snow cones, croffles, and milkshakes—complement savoury choices, making it viable for a quick mid-ride refuel.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Ramen menu explicitly lists 'Vegetable' as a named noodle option alongside Bacon, Chicken, and Beef variants

restaurant.name: Four Olives Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Four Olives is a casual Mediterranean fusion restaurant in Vancouver's Point Grey neighbourhood, serving Greek-inspired dishes including souvlaki, mezze-style salads, and baked pastas in an upscale-casual setting. The restaurant offers both a lunch menu and a dinner menu with online ordering, and also provides catering services. Located on West 10th Avenue, it sits along a well-used cycling corridor connecting the UBC endowment lands to central Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Lunch menu includes multiple vegetarian options: Beetroot & Arugula Salad, Three Cheese Baked Penne, and Pesto Penne Cream Sauce

restaurant.name: Baan Thai
restaurant.desc: Baan Thai is a multi-location Thai restaurant group with a long-standing presence in Victoria, holding the Thai SELECT certification from the Royal Thai Government as a mark of authentic Thai cuisine. The downtown Victoria location sits on Blanshard Street near the inner harbour, surrounded by shopping and attractions. The restaurant has been voted Best of the City for ten consecutive years (2013–2023) and emphasizes locally sourced ingredients from BC farms and breweries.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu allergy filter labels confirm 'Can Be Vegan Friendly', 'Can Be Vegetarian Friendly', and 'Can Be Gluten Friendly' options across menu items

restaurant.name: Amsterdam Pub
restaurant.desc: Amsterdam Pub is a pub located on Village Stroll in Whistler. It serves food and beverages to the local and visiting community.

restaurant.name: Ichiya Japanese Ramen
restaurant.desc: A Japanese ramen and sushi restaurant on Commercial Drive in Vancouver with outdoor seating. The restaurant offers takeaway, making it convenient for quick meals or provisions on the road.

restaurant.name: QV Coffee House
restaurant.desc: QV Coffee House is a neighbourhood cafe on Fort Street in Victoria, open seven days a week and serving the Oak Bay Avenue corridor — a popular cycling route connecting downtown to the seaside communities to the east. The retail-building setting and consistent hours suggest a small independent coffee shop well-positioned for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Happy Tree House BBQ
restaurant.desc: Happy Tree House BBQ is a full-service restaurant on Kingsway serving Chinese and kebab dishes with indoor seating and wheelchair access. Vegetarian options are available, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking a casual meal.

restaurant.name: Caffe Divano
restaurant.desc: Caffé Divano is a locally owned neighbourhood café in Coquitlam, part of a small Tri-Cities family of cafés founded by Patrick and Lisa Beecroft. The Coquitlam location has been operating since 2013, serving handcrafted beverages and food made daily from scratch using simple, natural ingredients. The café is connected to the Beecrofts' Gabi & Jules bakery, which supplies all baked goods across the Divano locations.

restaurant.name: Makan Time
restaurant.desc: Makan Time is a Southeast Asian casual dining concept ('星馬飯堂' — Singapore-Malaysia food hall) operating under the Neptune Palace restaurant group inside Brentwood Mall, Burnaby. It offers dine-in, takeout, pick-up, and delivery, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Lougheed corridor. The concept draws on Singaporean and Malaysian hawker-style cuisine as a distinct offering from its sister Neptune Palace Seafood restaurants.

restaurant.name: Shanghai City Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Shanghai City Restaurant has been a Nanaimo institution since 1999, serving over 110 Chinese dishes spanning Szechuan, seafood, chow mein, and dim sum traditions. It claims the largest buffet in Nanaimo and is particularly noted for its traditional weekend dim sum lunch service. Takeout, delivery, and a buffet-to-go option make it a practical fuel stop for cyclists moving through the Island Highway corridor.

detail.address: 215-2000 Island Hwy N., Nanaimo, BC V9S 3V5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists a dedicated 'Vegetarian and Gluten free' section and specifically includes Vegetarian Dumplings

restaurant.name: Vintner's Grill
restaurant.desc: Vintner's Grill is the signature restaurant at the Coast Capri Hotel in Kelowna, offering seasonal Canadian and globally inspired dishes for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The enclosed poolside patio opens to the hotel courtyard during summer, creating a pleasant outdoor dining atmosphere. The restaurant is open to both hotel guests and the general public, and hosts live music on select Friday evenings.

restaurant.name: Eleven 22
restaurant.desc: A regional cuisine restaurant in Golden offering dine-in service. The business is wheelchair accessible and centrally located on 10th Avenue, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the community.

restaurant.name: Vodka Ice Bar
restaurant.desc: The Vodka Ice Bar is a seasonal, immersive vodka-tasting experience tucked inside Lizard Creek Lodge, a ski-in ski-out resort at Fernie Alpine Resort. Guests don Helly Hansen parkas to sample vodkas from around the world — including Canadian-made Crystal Head Vodka — in a sub-zero environment. It is part of a full-service mountain lodge that also includes a restaurant, spa, pool, and hot tubs.

restaurant.name: Moxie's
restaurant.desc: Moxie's West Georgia is a newly renovated premium casual bar and grill in downtown Vancouver, featuring floor-to-ceiling windows, lush greenery, and an exclusive rooftop patio near BC Place and Rogers Arena. Situated at the corner of West Georgia and Cambie Street, it is steps from the Stadium-Chinatown SkyTrain Station and the Vancouver Financial District. An OpenTable Diners' Choice 2024 winner, it serves brunch, happy hour menus, and full dinner, and can host private events in dedicated event spaces.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page labels 'Vegetarian items' and 'Gluten conscious with some modifications from our kitchen' across menu categories

restaurant.name: Gold & Jade Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Gold & Jade Restaurant is a family-owned, Western-style Chinese restaurant in the heart of Princeton, BC, a common stop on the Similkameen cycling corridor. The restaurant accepts all Canadian credit cards and has an updated menu as of June 2025. Princeton sits at the confluence of the Similkameen and Tulameen rivers and is a key resupply point for cyclists on multi-day tours through the region.

restaurant.name: Thai Food Near Me
restaurant.desc: Thai Food Near Me is an authentic Thai restaurant on Fort Street in downtown Victoria, serving a broad menu of traditional appetizers, curries, stir-fries, and noodle dishes prepared with fresh ingredients and classic techniques. The restaurant emphasizes communal, family-style dining rooted in Thailand's regional culinary heritage, and also offers online ordering for takeout and delivery.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists tofu as a selectable protein across multiple dishes including Fresh Tofu Salad Rolls, Deep Fried Tofu, and tofu substitutions in stir-fry and fried rice items

restaurant.name: Smile's Seafood Cafe
restaurant.desc: Smile's Seafood Cafe is a seafood-focused restaurant in Prince Rupert's Cow Bay area. It serves the local community and visitors exploring the Prince Rupert region.

detail.address: 113 Cow Bay Road, Prince Rupert, V8J 3X4

restaurant.name: Refire Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Refire Kitchen is a prepared-meals concept where customers select from a rotating menu of fully cooked entrées, soups, and desserts that simply need to be reheated at home. The Sidney location on Beacon Avenue is one of four stores spanning Greater Victoria, making it a convenient stop for cyclists touring the Saanich Peninsula. The menu spans comfort-food classics to vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-friendly options.

notes.Takeout: Entire business model is in-store shopping and pre-order pickup of take-and-bake prepared meals; no dine-in component

restaurant.name: Banter
restaurant.desc: Banter is a handmade ice cream shop housed in the Eddy at the Bridge Building along the Vedder River in Chilliwack, one of two Fraser Valley locations founded by Laura and Zach. The shop creates four brand-new seasonal scoops each month, many drawing on ingredients sourced from local Fraser Valley farmers and artisans. Touring cyclists can grab a scoop and continue on a river walk in a relaxed, community-focused riverside setting.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website marks select flavours with '(V)' (e.g., Mango listed on front page), indicating vegan options are available

restaurant.name: Spark Kitchen and Bar
restaurant.desc: Spark Kitchen and Bar is a kitchen and bar concept in Richmond, BC offering both a food menu and a drinks menu, with online ordering and table booking advertised on its website. The venue presents itself as a sit-down restaurant-bar hybrid. Touring cyclists stopping in Richmond's dining corridor would find it a potential refuelling option, though the business's web presence is currently sparse.

restaurant.name: The Whole Bowl
restaurant.desc: The Whole Bowl is a macro-balanced meal prep kitchen and grab-and-go counter in Surrey specializing in high-protein, nutritionally calibrated rice bowls and wraps designed for fitness and wellness goals. Cyclists can pick up a fresh meal on the spot or pre-order from a rotating menu that accommodates vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, and low-carb needs. The storefront also offers multi-meal prep packages for those planning ahead on longer tours.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Ordering policy page states meals cater to 'vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, and low-carb options'; a customer review also mentions gluten allergy accommodation

restaurant.name: Yolks
restaurant.desc: Yolks is a scratch-cooking breakfast and brunch chain founded by Chef Steve Ewing, with its Davie Street location sitting in Vancouver's West End. The restaurant is known for Perfectly Poached™ eggs, house-made hollandaise, truffle lemon potatoes, and free-range eggs sourced from Coligny Creek in Abbotsford. Indoor-only seating and a community-focused ethos make it a reliable full-meal stop for cyclists passing through central Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu features eggs benedict, pancakes, and egg-based dishes consistent with vegetarian options. No vegan or GF claims

restaurant.name: The Juice Truck
restaurant.desc: The Juice Truck began as a cold-pressed juice food truck on a Vancouver street corner and has grown into a plant-based wellness brand with brick-and-mortar juice bars and an online marketplace. The 4420 Lougheed Highway location offers made-to-order cold-pressed juices, wellness shots, cleanses, and a range of plant-based grocery and supplement products. Everything on the menu is vegetarian and vegan, with organic produce sourced where available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly describes a fully plant-based menu with organic produce

restaurant.name: Flying Beaver Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: A pub and grill located in Richmond on Inglis Drive with indoor seating. Serves food and beverages in a casual bar-restaurant setting. Offers a non-smoking environment with dine-in service.

restaurant.name: Perc's Place
restaurant.desc: Perc's Place is a cafe in Kelowna, BC operating under the handle @percsplacekelowna on Instagram. It appears to be a neighbourhood café serving the Kelowna community on weekday and Saturday hours. Touring cyclists passing through Kelowna would find it a potential stop for a coffee or bite.

detail.address: 1876 Cooper Rd #146, Kelowna, BC V1Y 8B7, Canada

restaurant.name: Bamboo Inn
restaurant.desc: Bamboo Inn is a long-established Chinese restaurant on the north side of Kamloops, serving authentic cuisine for over four decades and widely regarded as a local institution. Chefs combine classic Chinese recipes with locally sourced produce for dine-in, takeout, and delivery, and the kitchen also handles banquets and catered events. A touring cyclist passing through the north end of Kamloops will find a reliable sit-down meal or quick takeout option here.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Whether you're joining us for dine-in, take-out, or free delivery within 3 km'; online ordering and call-ahead pickup are both offered

restaurant.name: Five Forks Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: Five Forks Bar & Grill is a full-service bar and restaurant on the Lougheed Highway in Mission, BC, serving regional cuisine with a broad menu of starters, mains, wings, tacos, and bowls. The kitchen emphasises fresh, high-quality ingredients and caters to a range of dietary needs, including gluten-wise and vegetarian dishes. The venue also offers private event spaces and catering, making it a social anchor along a main cycling corridor east of Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes vegetarian starters (Honey Chilli Cauliflower, Tofu option in Lettuce Wraps) and multiple items tagged 'GW' (e.g., Chicken Wings, Yam Fries, Fish Tacos, Garlic Butter Shrimp), likely denoting gluten-wise options

restaurant.name: Tasty Indian Bistro
restaurant.desc: Tasty Indian Bistro is a multi-location Indian restaurant rooted in Gujarat culinary tradition, founded by Avtar Saini, with its Delta location at 8295 120th Street (Scott Road). The restaurant offers dine-in, private dining, and corporate events, and also sells branded sauces, pickles, and masala chai mix. A touring cyclist would find a full sit-down meal in a well-established local chain with a broad Indian menu.

restaurant.name: The Ventura Room
restaurant.desc: Ventura Room is an intimate cocktail bar on Cambie Street in Vancouver, formerly known as the Media Club, specializing in carefully curated cocktails alongside small plates. The venue hosts live music and events and has both indoor and outdoor seating. A touring cyclist stopping in the evening would find a lively neighbourhood bar with table reservations available.

restaurant.name: Redbud Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A dining establishment in Richmond, BC. The website provides minimal information about the venue's specific offerings or amenities. Touring cyclists can find this location as a food service option in the area.

restaurant.name: Best Falafel
restaurant.desc: Best Falafel is a family-owned Syrian-Lebanese fast food restaurant founded by Damascus-born Hisham Wattar, who has grown the business to three Metro Vancouver locations over more than two decades. The North Vancouver outpost on Lonsdale Avenue is the newest, described as a grand opening location. Cyclists stopping here will find a broad menu of wraps, plates, and salads built on fresh Middle Eastern ingredients, with vegetarian and gluten-free choices available.

detail.address: 1829 Lonsdale Avenue, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2S8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Vegetarian Plate', 'Falafel Wrap' (vegetarian), and 'Gluten Free Tabbouleh Salad'

restaurant.name: Silver Dragon Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Silver Dragon Restaurant is a White Rock institution with over fifty years of history, known for its authentic Chinese cuisine, particularly its wonton soup made from turkey giblet broth and its sweet and sour pork. The fully licensed restaurant was honored as the Best Chinese Restaurant by the Now Regional Newspaper in 2003 and has built a multigenerational local following. It offers dine-in, online ordering with delivery, and a Sunday all-you-can-eat smorgasbord.

restaurant.name: Container Brewing Ltd.
restaurant.desc: Container Brewing is an award-winning craft brewery and taproom that opened in November 2019 in the heart of Vancouver's Yeast Van Brewing District, built largely by hand by two longtime friends. Their brewer David Dayco has earned recognition at the Canada Beer Cup, BC Beer Awards, and Growlies, with nearly 100 unique beers produced since opening. The space features a patio with a massive outdoor screen for live events, rotating food trucks, and a welcoming, accessibility-conscious atmosphere with a first-floor ramp and accessible washrooms.

restaurant.name: Red Swan Pizza
restaurant.desc: Red Swan Pizza is a franchise pizza outlet located in a strip-mall unit on North Parallel Road in Abbotsford's Whatcom area, next to Pacific North Wellness. It specializes in fresh-made pizza available for takeout or delivery. Touring cyclists in the area can pick up a hot meal without a sit-down commitment.

restaurant.name: OZ Korean Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Korean restaurant with locations in Richmond and Coquitlam offering online ordering for takeout. A casual dining spot serving Korean cuisine to the local community.

detail.address: 4351 Number 3 Road Unit 170, Richmond, BC V6X 3A7

restaurant.name: Cliff House Restaurant & Bar
restaurant.desc: The Cliff House Restaurant is a casual West Coast dining venue inside Capilano Suspension Bridge Park, paying homage to the original Cliff House built on the canyon's edge in 1889. It serves fresh local ingredients, Ocean Wise seafood, BC wines, and regional craft beer on tap, with a summer patio overlooking the park canyon and cozy indoor seating with local history. Access requires paid park admission, making this a destination experience rather than a casual drop-in stop for touring cyclists.

detail.address: 3735 Capilano Road, North Vancouver, BC V7R 4J1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Black Bean & Corn Burger, Butter Paneer (vegetarian variant of Butter Chicken), Capilano Canyon Salad, Hummus & Pita, and a Rice Bowl with plant-based topping options

restaurant.name: Nemo Sushi
restaurant.desc: Nemo Sushi Bar is a family-run Japanese restaurant on Hastings Street in Burnaby with over a decade of experience in Japanese cuisine. The cozy spot is known for fresh, creative interpretations of traditional dishes, including specialty rolls, in a welcoming atmosphere. It has been ranked among the top restaurants in its area for nine consecutive years.

notes.Device charging: Customer review (Danny Hwang): 'I could charge my phone during dine-in.'

restaurant.name: Home BBQ Lab
restaurant.desc: Home BBQ Lab has been serving authentic Northeastern Chinese charcoal-grilled skewers in Richmond since 2015, building a loyal following in the local Chinese community. The campfire-inspired atmosphere — open flame grilling, bold spices, communal tables — is designed to evoke a real campsite feast without leaving the city. The restaurant also operates private rooms seating up to 40 and an outdoor catering service for groups.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page: 'options for both vegans and meat lovers'; Menu page: 'We offer vegetarian and vegan-friendly options.' No GF claim found

restaurant.name: Karakoram Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Karakoram is a traditional Pakistani fine-dining restaurant on Victoria Drive in Vancouver, named after the mountain range where K2 stands. The kitchen specializes in authentic regional Pakistani dishes spanning Western, Punjabi, and Peshawari styles — from sizzling Karahi to slow-cooked Paya — and claims to be a pioneer of real Karahi in Western Canada. A touring cyclist looking for a substantial, flavour-forward South Asian meal will find an extensive menu and weekend brunch service.

restaurant.name: Soy
restaurant.desc: SOY Asian Fusion Restaurant is a family-owned spot in Kelowna's Pandosy Village, opened in 2011 by Tokyo-trained chef Takeshi Ishizaka and his wife Tomo. The menu draws from Japanese, Korean, and broader Asian traditions — highlights include Spicy Coconut Ramen, Chicken Karaage, and Korean BBQ — with dedicated gluten-free and vegan menus. The licensed dining room pours sake, beer, and local BC wines, and the restaurant also offers delivery through Skip the Dishes, DoorDash, and Uber Eats.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu has dedicated 'Gluten Free Menu' and 'Vegan Menu' sections; individual items throughout are labeled gluten free, vegetarian, and/or vegan

restaurant.name: Hang Lee Wok
restaurant.desc: Hang Lee Wok is a fast-food Chinese restaurant located in Tsawwassen, BC. It offers indoor seating, giving cyclists a place to sit down and eat out of the elements after a ride through the South Delta area. The wok-centric name suggests a quick-service Chinese stir-fry menu.

restaurant.name: Basasak
restaurant.desc: Basasak is a Korean chicken restaurant in Creston serving a range of Korean-inspired dishes including sauced and fried chicken in multiple styles, rice and noodle bowls, burgers, and poutine. The restaurant offers both brunch and dinner service and accepts online orders for pickup. It is one of the few Korean dining options in the Creston Valley, making it a distinctive stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Crispy Tofu, Bibim-Bob (Korean mixed rice bowl), and Japchae (sweet potato starch noodles) as vegetarian-compatible items

restaurant.name: Mike's Place
restaurant.desc: Mike's Place is a beloved Gibsons institution that has been hand-crafting house-made gelato from natural, fresh ingredients since 2003, with dozens of flavors including a full dairy-free lineup. Beyond gelato, it operates as a full café serving espresso drinks, paninis, soups, sandwiches, wraps, and fresh-baked sourdough bread, all enjoyed on a scenic outdoor deck overlooking the seaside town. It also serves as a Purolator quick-stop depot, making it a genuine community hub for locals and visitors alike.

detail.address: 268 Gower Point Road, Gibsons, BC V0N1V0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dairy-free gelato flavors listed (Strawberry, Mango, Lemon, etc.); vegetarian panini (Veggie, Caprese) and wrap (Pesto Veggie) options on menu; gluten-free gelato cake base available for additional cost

restaurant.name: Shun Feng Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Shunfeng Seafood Restaurant is a large-format Cantonese dining destination in Richmond's Number 3 Road corridor, spanning 8,000 square feet with capacity for over 350 guests. It is known for award-winning dim sum as well as elaborate wedding banquets and private VIP dining rooms on a mezzanine level. Located in a shopping centre near the SkyTrain and Vancouver International Airport, it draws a broad clientele looking for full-service Chinese cuisine.

restaurant.name: Jam Café
restaurant.desc: Jam Café is a beloved West Coast breakfast and brunch chain that has been serving comfort food since 2012, with its Kitsilano outpost sitting on West 4th Avenue — one of Vancouver's most popular cycling corridors. The menu leans Southern-inspired, with crowd favourites like Fried Chicken French Toast, fluffy three-stack pancakes, and the hearty Charlie Bowl, all made with locally sourced ingredients. The cozy, vintage-eclectic interior and signature cocktails (mimosas, bacon Caesars) make it a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring the Kitsilano neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Gokudo Shabu Shabu
restaurant.desc: Gokudo Shabu Shabu is a Japanese-Taiwanese fusion hot pot restaurant with locations in Richmond and Burnaby, BC. Diners choose from 17 unique soup bases — including sukiyaki, satay, spicy mix, and a vegetarian broth — and cook thinly sliced meats and fresh vegetables at the table in a customizable, interactive format. The restaurant emphasizes sustainable and locally sourced ingredients alongside house-crafted sauces developed by the founder's wife.

detail.address: 3779 Sexsmith Rd Unit 2133, Richmond, BC V6X 3Z9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We also offer a vegetarian broth to satisfy all tastes.'

restaurant.name: The Reach Neighbourhood Pub & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Reach is a community-rooted neighbourhood pub on Dewdney Trunk Road in Maple Ridge, serving no-fuss comfort food alongside a rotating selection of local craft beers. It functions as a genuine local gathering place with weekly themed food specials, live music nights, and Sunday trivia. Touring cyclists passing through Maple Ridge's Fraser Valley corridor would find a welcoming, unpretentious stop with a full pub menu and a strong sense of neighbourhood hospitality.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Cauliflower as a Taco Tuesday filling option alongside Chicken, Beef, and Fish; pasta dishes (Marinara Rotini, Pesto Cream Linguine, Rosé Penne) also appear vegetarian. No explicit GF or vegan claim made

restaurant.name: Cosmos Pizza & Pasta
restaurant.desc: Cosmos Pizza & Pasta is a family-run Italian restaurant that has been serving fresh pizzas and pastas in Victoria since 2007, located inside The Burnside Plaza on Tillicum Road near Tillicum Mall. With a consistent recipe and emphasis on fresh ingredients, it's a well-established neighbourhood spot for a sit-down or pick-up meal. A touring cyclist would find it a convenient dinner stop on the western side of Victoria.

restaurant.name: Banana Leaf Surrey
restaurant.desc: Banana Leaf Surrey is the South Surrey outpost of a well-established Malaysian restaurant group with five Lower Mainland locations. The kitchen prepares family-style dishes with freshly made in-house sauces and offers multi-course tasting menus alongside an à la carte menu spanning satay, laksa, seafood curries, and roti canai. Takeout and third-party delivery round out the options for cyclists who want a flavourful meal on the go.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu items marked 🌿 (vegetarian) include spring rolls, eggplant fries, and tofu goreng; multiple dishes labelled 'GF'; menu notes 'all dishes can be made... without meat or seafood.'

restaurant.name: Angus T
restaurant.desc: Angus T is a Belgian-style croissant bakery founded in 2016 in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, built around a family recipe passed down through generations from a small Belgian village. All pastries are handcrafted daily in an open kitchen using locally and European-sourced ingredients, spanning an extensive menu of sweet and savory croissants, cinnamon buns, babka buns, and specialty coffee. A touring cyclist stopping in will find a broad selection of quick, filling baked goods and café drinks in a warm indoor seating environment.

restaurant.name: Pho 24 Express
restaurant.desc: Pho 24 Express is a Vietnamese restaurant on Kingsway in Burnaby, self-described as the area's top Vietnamese food destination, with a menu built around phở, salad rolls, and a variety of savory starters. The restaurant is open late every day of the week, including statutory holidays, making it a reliable option for cyclists finishing a long day on the road. Catering services and reservations are also available.

restaurant.name: Piggy & Paisley
restaurant.desc: Piggy & Paisley is a boutique cafe nestled in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood, steps from the oceanside bluffs and cycling paths along Dallas Road. It specialises in premium globally-sourced teas, handcrafted in-house pastries, and locally-roasted coffee from suppliers including Bows and Fantastico. The cafe is also known for its reservation-only Afternoon Tea service, offering tiered trays of scones, sandwiches, and desserts in a deliberately serene setting.

restaurant.name: Chucila Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Chucila Restaurant is listed as a restaurant on Number 3 Road in Richmond. No functioning website exists to confirm its cuisine, character, or current status.

restaurant.name: Poseidon Restaurant & Bar
restaurant.desc: Poseidon Restaurant & Bar is an authentic Greek and Mediterranean restaurant in Langley, BC, with a special emphasis on daily-caught seafood and dishes prepared on a charcoal brazier. The 90-seat dining room offers a modern, contemporary setting for experiencing traditional Greek cuisine and hospitality. The restaurant also caters to private functions including group bookings, weddings, and corporate events.

detail.address: Unit 5 - 20811 Fraser Highway, Langley, BC V3A 4G7

restaurant.name: Il Cappello
restaurant.desc: Il Cappello is a full-service Italian enoteca in Burnaby, proudly part of the Dolce Amore family founded by Giancarlo and Daniela Cusano. The kitchen is led by Sicilian-born Head Chef Daniele Navarria—trained at Pétrus and Le Gavroche—with a menu spanning antipasti, house-made pasta, and Neapolitan-style pizza made from 100% organic Canadian flour. The sommelier-curated wine list spotlights Italian estates and indigenous varietals alongside select BC favourites.

restaurant.name: Viet Family Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Viet Family is a fully vegan Vietnamese restaurant on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most-cycled urban corridors, established in 2022 by the Ho family and relocated to its current spot in 2024. The menu centres on Vietnamese staples — pho, summer rolls, bún bowls, and dry vermicelli platters — all plant-based and crafted with house-made broths and sauces. The restaurant also offers catering and private event hosting, suggesting a comfortable, full-service dining environment well suited for a group rest stop.

restaurant.name: Tacofino
restaurant.desc: Tacofino is the West Coast Mexican food brand that got its start in Tofino, built around a beach-casual menu of tacos and burritos inspired by surf culture. The brand now has two Tofino presences — the original food truck on Pacific Rim Highway and a newer town-centre location on Campbell Street — both offering quick counter-service meals. For cyclists riding the Pacific Rim corridor, either stop provides a well-known, no-fuss refuelling option.

restaurant.name: Bread Culture

The menu spans an impressive range of organic sourdoughs, croissants, Danish pastries, brioches, choux, and baguette sandwiches, with pre-ordering strongly recommended two days in advance for specialty or large items. It accepts pre-orders via email and processes checkouts securely through Square.

restaurant.name: Vancouver Pizza Kitchen

restaurant.name: Hot House Pizza

The Victoria West location caters to takeout and delivery customers, with slices available to-go — a quick refuelling option for cyclists passing through the Vic West neighbourhood. Dietary accommodations include gluten-free, dairy-free, and vegan cheese options.

restaurant.name: L'Onore Pizza

It sits in a mixed-use building (unit 110) in a walkable urban neighbourhood, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists riding through the city. No further details about the restaurant's character or offerings could be retrieved from its online presence.

restaurant.name: Container Brewing Lounge
restaurant.desc: Container Brewing is an award-winning craft brewery taproom in Vancouver's Strathcona neighbourhood, recognized at the Canada Beer Cup, Growlies, and BC Beer Awards for a lineup ranging from hop-forward IPAs to rich stouts, all brewed on-site by head brewer David Dayco. The taproom hosts a rotating roster of visiting food trucks and runs regular events including sports screenings on a big screen. Touring cyclists will find a lively local stop with reservations available for groups.

restaurant.name: Notch8
restaurant.desc: Notch8 Restaurant & Bar is the signature dining room of the Fairmont Hotel Vancouver, one of the city's most storied heritage properties in the heart of downtown. Recognized as one of Canada's Top 50 Hotel Restaurants for 2025, it serves breakfast through late-night dinner and a celebrated Afternoon Tea program. The kitchen blends classic French technique with Pacific Northwest ingredients under Executive Chef Mike Reid.

restaurant.name: Pho Spot

restaurant.name: Himalayan Spice Bistro

It offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery, making it a flexible stop for cyclists moving through the Elk Valley. The menu includes vegetarian options alongside a range of traditional South Asian dishes.

restaurant.name: Beacon Brewing

It brews small-batch craft beers on-site — ranging from a cold IPA to a dark mild — and pairs them with local snacks, pizza, and a rotating lineup of cider and wine. A dog-friendly patio, weekly vinyl nights, and live Friday music make it a lively community hub well worth a stop on a Saanich Peninsula ride.

restaurant.name: McDonald's

The location includes a drive-through and is part of the Canadian McDonald's chain, which operates the MyMcDonald's Rewards app for order-ahead and loyalty points. Touring cyclists will find it a reliable all-hours food stop on a busy suburban arterial.

restaurant.name: Superflux Cabana
restaurant.desc: Superflux Cabana is a craft beer bar and restaurant in Victoria, BC, operated by Superflux Beer Company as their 'island outpost.' Located upstairs at 804 Broughton Street, the 110-seat venue features two rooftop patios and an indoor lounge styled after a 1970s Vegas hotel bar, with the latest Superflux beers always on tap and a full late-night kitchen serving burgers and casual fare.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website FAQ states: 'We have veggie and vegan options. There are gluten-friendly options {gluten-free buns} as well.'

restaurant.name: Yokidomo Sushi
restaurant.desc: Yokidomo Sushi is a Japanese restaurant on West Saanich Road in Victoria offering a broad menu of sushi rolls, sashimi, donburi, noodles, bento boxes, and party trays, with a newer Korean Fried Chicken section. The menu is notably diverse in dietary options, with many dishes explicitly marked gluten-free, vegetarian, and vegan. Located in a strip-mall unit, it serves as a practical sit-down meal stop for cyclists exploring the Saanich Peninsula.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels numerous items as Vegetarian, Vegan, and Gluten free across appetizers, salads, and other categories (e.g., edamame, wakame salad, vegetable sunomono)

restaurant.name: Shiro Japanese Restaurant

The restaurant supports online ordering with pickup ready in 30–45 minutes, making it a practical stop for cyclists wanting a quick, satisfying Japanese meal on a key Vancouver cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Bjornbar Cafe - Lynnmour
restaurant.desc: BjornBar Cafe is a boutique bakery and café located inside the DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel in North Vancouver's Lynnmour neighbourhood, one of three Lower Mainland locations of this local chain. The shop is best known for over 30 flavours of handmade dessert bars — from classic Nanaimo to adventurous Spumoni — alongside fresh pastries, lunch items, and specialty coffee. For cyclists on the North Shore, it offers a quality café stop in a hotel setting.

restaurant.name: Feast & Fallow
restaurant.desc: Feast & Fallow is a fully plant-based/vegan café in Vancouver's Cambie corridor, serving locally sourced coffee, house-baked pastries and breads, savoury toasts, and a Saturday brunch menu. The café operates with a volunteer crew and is deeply mission-driven, advocating for a just urban food system through community workshops on topics like urban agriculture, composting, and food security. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a welcoming, community-minded space with a full espresso bar and substantial vegan food options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website self-describes as 'plant-based/vegan cafe'; entire menu uses plant-based ingredients only (Violife, Daiya, Just Egg, tofu bacon, oat milk as default)

restaurant.name: Golden Island Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Golden Island is a long-running Chinese restaurant that has served Salt Spring Island for over 40 years, operating as a takeout and delivery operation. The menu features house-made BBQ pork, crispy ginger beef, house-made sauces, and a range of combination meals, plus beer, wine, and ciders to go. A local institution with a loyal following, it is a practical meal stop for cyclists touring Salt Spring Island.

restaurant.name: Indian Curry Corner
restaurant.desc: Indian Curry Corner is a family-owned North Indian restaurant on Victoria Drive with over 25 years of culinary experience behind its kitchen. The menu spans a wide range of curries, tandoori items, biryanis, breads, and appetizers, with a notably deep vegetarian selection including paneer dishes and plant-based options. The restaurant also offers catering and in-store food pickup, making it a practical stop for a sit-down meal or grab-and-go order.

restaurant.name: Fudo Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Fudo is a Japanese restaurant and sushi bar that opened in 2017 at Broadmead Village Shopping Centre, specializing in traditional and fusion cuisine under Executive Chef Yang, one of Victoria's only female sushi chefs. The restaurant is known for locally sourced BC seafood — including spot prawns, sockeye salmon, and bluefin tuna — and has been voted best Japanese food in Victoria by Yam Magazine. Raku Ramen is also served on-site, rounding out the menu for cyclists looking for a substantial, varied meal.

restaurant.name: River's Reach Pub
restaurant.desc: River's Reach Pub is a multi-award-winning neighbourhood pub in New Westminster that has been operating since December 2000, collecting six Newsleader A-List and thirteen Record Reader's Choice Best Pub awards. The interior recreates an early 1900s West Coast atmosphere with river rock, old-growth hardwoods, fireplaces, and 19th-century antiques. Cyclists stopping in will find a full kitchen menu, an extensive beer list with domestic, import, and craft options, wines, and cocktails — with a 19+ age restriction throughout.

restaurant.name: Good Kid Coffee
restaurant.desc: Good Kid Coffee is an independent specialty coffee shop in Abbotsford founded by Tim and Lisa Rosebush, who honed their craft in Calgary before bringing their vision for a welcoming community space to the Fraser Valley. The shop features a rotating filter coffee menu, a full espresso bar, teas, pastries, bagels, and breakfast and lunch items. Online ordering with in-store pickup is available, making it a practical stop for cyclists planning their route.

restaurant.name: Roma Italian Ristorante
restaurant.desc: Roma Italian Ristorante is a casual Italian restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver, turning out handmade pizza from a wood-fired oven alongside fresh pasta prepared from scratch by a seasoned chef. The space blends rustic and modern design and is set up for everything from walk-in lunches to private group events and off-site catering. A touring cyclist will find a sit-down meal with full table service, online ordering for pickup, and delivery partnerships for off-bike days.

detail.address: 1352 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2H8

restaurant.name: Thomas Haas Chocolates
restaurant.desc: Thomas Haas Chocolates is a celebrated Vancouver-area patisserie and chocolatier with two café locations, known for handcrafted chocolates, French macarons, cakes, and gourmet sandwiches made by an in-house team of pastry chefs. The North Shore location sits at Harbourside Drive near the North Vancouver waterfront, making it a natural refuelling stop on the popular seaside cycling routes of the area. The shop also carries a 'Powered by Chocolate' cycling jersey line, signalling a deliberate nod to cycling culture.

restaurant.name: The Well Student Pub
restaurant.desc: The Well is the Students' Union pub at UBC Okanagan, situated on the first floor of the University Centre Building on campus. It serves food and drinks including burgers and beer, and hosts regular events such as monthly trivia nights and club gatherings. A touring cyclist arriving at the UBCO campus would find a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere typical of a campus pub.

restaurant.name: Pho Tru
restaurant.desc: Pho Tru is a Vietnamese restaurant in downtown Victoria rooted in the street-side food culture of Vietnam, serving pho noodle soups, vermicelli salad bowls, jasmine rice plates, Saigon subs, and fresh spring rolls made from family recipes passed through generations. The restaurant has two Victoria locations — downtown on Blanshard Street and inside Mayfair Shopping Centre — with dine-in, pick-up, and delivery available. Touring cyclists moving through central Victoria will find generous, affordable bowls well-suited to refuelling on a long ride.

restaurant.name: Mr Mikes
restaurant.desc: Mr Mikes is a Canadian casual steakhouse chain with roots going back to 1960, offering premium steaks, burgers, pastas, salads, and shareable appetizers in a relaxed, come-as-you-are atmosphere. The Kamloops location on Summit Drive serves dine-in, takeout, and delivery, making it a solid option for a sit-down meal or a meal to go after a long day on the road. The brand prides itself on being unstuffy and welcoming to locals and tourists alike.

restaurant.name: Cafe W
restaurant.desc: Caffe W is a Vancouver café that has been operating since 1995, with its original home on West Broadway and a newer downtown outpost on Robson Street. The café serves a broad menu of espresso drinks, iced coffees, smoothies, brunch plates, and a distinctive signature item — the Dubai Chocolate Strawberry Cup with pistachio and kenaf — found nowhere else. Situated on a busy pedestrian strip in the West End, it offers both indoor and outdoor seating.

restaurant.name: Tamarind Hill

It offers a focused, authentic Southeast Asian menu with both meat and seafood specialties alongside a solid selection of vegetarian dishes. Online ordering with quick pickup is available, making it a practical stop for cyclists riding the Lonsdale corridor.

restaurant.name: Crema Icecream
restaurant.desc: Crema Ice Cream & Desserts is a small-batch artisan scoop shop founded in 2019 by a Taiwanese-Peruvian couple who blend Asian and Latin American flavours into creative, culturally-inspired ice creams made with natural ingredients and seasonal local produce. Beyond classic scoops, the shop offers milkshakes, sundaes, handmade sammies, ice cream cakes, and even dog-friendly pawsicles. The business also runs an ice cream cart and truck catering service for events throughout the Lower Mainland.

restaurant.name: Istanbul Döner Shop

restaurant.name: La Taquisa

It has two Victoria locations — downtown on Blanshard Street and a second outpost in Vic West — and bills itself as the city's most authentic Mexican fare. Catering with a fully customizable build-your-own taco bar is also available for events.

restaurant.name: New Novelty Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A family-friendly Indian restaurant and sweets shop on Fraser Street in Vancouver, offering authentic curries, freshly baked breads, savory snacks, and a large selection of traditional Indian sweets made fresh daily. The menu includes vegetarian options and daily combo specials, making it a convenient and affordable refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the South Vancouver corridor.
