restaurant.name: Memphis Blues
restaurant.desc: Memphis Blues is an award-winning Southern BBQ chain with a well-established location on Vancouver's cycling-friendly Commercial Drive, recognized by Georgia Straight, Vancouver Magazine, and Food Network Canada for its applewood-smoked meats cooked low and slow on-site daily. The restaurant operates a lively dine-in format with occasional special events and a catering operation serving up to 800 guests. It sits on one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors and offers a hearty, casual meal for riders passing through the East Side.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A 24/7 McDonald's franchise on Kingsway in Vancouver, offering the full Canadian McDonald's menu including breakfast, burgers, McCafé beverages, and seasonal limited-time items. restaurant.name: Andonis
restaurant.desc: Andonis is a Mediterranean and Greek supper club on Granville Street in downtown Vancouver, blending elevated cuisine with live music, DJ sets, and curated entertainment into one immersive experience. Self-described as Vancouver's first true supper club, it draws on Greek coastal culinary traditions with a contemporary twist and a private dining room (Cretes Room) that seats up to 14 guests. For touring cyclists, it represents an upscale dinner destination in the heart of Vancouver's entertainment corridor.

restaurant.name: Chancho Tortilleria
restaurant.desc: Chancho Tortilleria is an authentic Mexican tortilleria on Vancouver's vibrant Commercial Drive, making fresh tortillas daily from ancient, non-GMO corn sourced directly from small Mexican farms. The menu revolves around tacos, tortas, and tragos (cocktails), with an emphasis on high-quality pork and locally sourced ingredients. The walk-in, no-reservations format makes it a relaxed and accessible stop for cyclists passing through the Drive.

restaurant.name: Two Sparrows

The menu spans a full range of espresso-based hot and iced drinks, frappes, dirty sodas, and handmade cupcakes, with gluten-free and vegan options available on request. For a touring cyclist passing through north Nanaimo, it offers a sweet resupply and a quality coffee stop in a covered indoor setting.

restaurant.name: Kung Pao Wok

Touring cyclists will find a quality urban refueling stop with outdoor seating and an Italian-inspired menu that goes well beyond standard cafe fare.

restaurant.name: Phở Sunrise

A touring cyclist in the South Surrey area would find it a convenient stop for a restorative bowl of noodle soup.

restaurant.name: The Narrow Lounge
restaurant.desc: The Narrow Lounge is an intimate, dimly lit bar and lounge at 1898 Main Street in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, part of The Narrow Group's collection of restaurants and art spaces. It serves creative house cocktails and wine alongside Mexican-inspired fast food from its in-house Taco Kat menu, with a covered summer patio offering a livelier outdoor alternative. The venue has a reputation for a lively, unpretentious atmosphere and a devoted local following.

restaurant.name: Ovaltine Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Ovaltine Cafe is one of Vancouver's oldest continuously operating diners, open since 1942 in the Downtown Eastside and virtually unchanged in decor — retro booths, neon signage, and a classic counter. Named among the world's 50 greatest cafes by The Telegraph in 2018, it has appeared in The X-Files, Supernatural, and I, Robot. Owned since 2014 by Grace Chen, the cafe maintains a strong community focus, keeping prices affordable for locals and offering classic all-day breakfast alongside lunch staples.

restaurant.name: Browns Socialhouse

restaurant.name: Sushi Lovers
restaurant.desc: Sushi Lovers is a sushi and sashimi restaurant in Richmond's Blundell Road area, offering a menu that includes party trays and more. The business is affiliated with a 'Seafood Group' that includes Sylvia's Seafood and Meat Lovers, suggesting a broader seafood operation. Cyclists passing through Richmond's flat, bikeable streets will find this a convenient stop for Japanese fare.

restaurant.name: Neptune Eats
restaurant.desc: Neptune Eats is a Cantonese-style restaurant in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, specializing in Hong Kong-style cuisine with a menu spanning breakfast through dinner and seafood feasts. The restaurant operates bilingually in English and Chinese and offers both dine-in and online ordering with pickup. It sits on West 41st Avenue, a quiet residential commercial strip popular with local cyclists.

restaurant.name: Sal Y Limón Mexican Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Sal y Limón is a Vancouver-born Mexican restaurant founded by four food enthusiasts drawing on family recipes from Manzanillo, Mexico, serving tacos, tortas, burritos, and other street food favourites. The Fraser Street location is one of three across Metro Vancouver and positions itself as a welcoming, family-friendly spot with a vibrant atmosphere. Catering, gift cards, and both pick-up and delivery ordering are available.

restaurant.name: Joe Fortes
restaurant.desc: Joe Fortes Seafood & Chop House is a Vancouver institution open for over 35 years, named after Seraphim 'Joe Fortes,' the city's first official lifeguard who became one of its most beloved citizens. The restaurant spans multiple distinct spaces — a grand horseshoe oyster bar, a mezzanine with live entertainment, a mahogany-walled wine room, and a rooftop garden with a living green wall and outdoor fireplace. It specializes in Pacific Northwest seafood and premium chops, serving more than 50 kinds of fresh fish alongside an award-winning list of over 300 wines.

restaurant.name: Ground Up
restaurant.desc: Ground Up Cafe & Catering is a community-rooted breakfast and lunch spot in the heart of Gabriola village, run by born-and-raised Gabriolans who source ingredients from local farms and make everything from scratch. The cafe doubles as a catering operation for weddings, luncheons, and conferences, and has built a strong following for its specialty coffee and fresh-baked goods. For a touring cyclist arriving by ferry to Gabriola Island, this is a natural first stop at the village center.

restaurant.name: Red Tomato Pies
restaurant.desc: Red Tomato Pies is a BC-born pizza chain founded in Williams Lake by Jason and Amber Akeson, now operating 11 locations across Western Canada. The Fort St. John location offers a broad menu of handcrafted pizzas, pasta, wings, salads, and desserts with takeout and delivery. The chain has earned a reputation for quality pizza and offers notable dietary flexibility including plant-based and gluten-free options.

restaurant.name: Pho V. Ta Vietnamese Restaurant

Touring cyclists will find a stylish dine-in space with takeout available and menu options clearly labelled for dietary needs.

restaurant.name: Buy the Sea

restaurant.name: Chopsticks

It offers dine-in, takeout, and local delivery, and has won Gold and Platinum West Kootenay's Best of Business Awards five years running. Sushi-making classes are also available, making it a locally well-rooted stop for touring cyclists passing through the Kootenay region.

restaurant.name: Terra Breads
restaurant.desc: Terra Breads is a Vancouver artisan bakery founded in 1993, known for naturally leavened sourdough loaves, specialty breads, and small-batch granola made with no added preservatives and locally sourced ingredients. The Granville Island location sits inside the iconic Granville Island Public Market, a busy destination accessible by bike paths along False Creek. Touring cyclists can pick up high-quality bread and granola for the road in one of the city's most scenic cycling-accessible spots.

restaurant.name: Original Tandoori Kitchen

restaurant.name: Frog City Cafe
restaurant.desc: Frog City Cafe is a seasonal cafe and live music venue set within a 6-acre heritage garden in Kaleden, BC, operated by owners with deep personal ties to the land and the Hayter family who built it. The menu centers on house-baked breads turned into hearty sandwiches and salads at lunch, with Neapolitan flatbreads served on live-music evenings and weekend breakfasts in peak season. The dog-friendly garden patio, rotating art and music shows, and a strong community ethos make it an unexpectedly rich cultural stop along the Okanagan cycling corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes The Hippy (vegetarian sandwich with Swiss, guac, cucumbers, sunflower seeds, greens), Chickpea Salad Sandwich, and Frog City Salad; no explicit GF or vegan labeling found

restaurant.name: Marina Dockside Eatery
restaurant.desc: Marina Dockside Eatery is a fully licensed oceanfront cafe at Oak Bay Marina in Victoria, serving a west coast menu of house-made sandwiches, paninis, soups, salads, and gelato alongside locally roasted Caffé Fantastico coffee and Silk Road teas. The eatery sits on a scenic marina-facing deck and explicitly notes that cyclists stop to take in the views alongside locals and boaters. A long-standing community anchor, it sources ingredients from local farms and fishers and holds 100% Ocean Wise certification across all its Vancouver Island locations.

detail.address: 1327 Beach Drive, Victoria, British Columbia V8S 2N4, Canada

restaurant.name: The Pink House
restaurant.desc: The Pink House Bistro is a Mediterranean-inspired second-storey restaurant in Gibsons Landing, where Head Chef Kit Pollack's seasonal menus put bold flavours and humble vegetables front and centre alongside meat and seafood. The cozy, colourful dining room and uncovered patio offer sweeping views of the harbour and nearby islands, making it a destination spot for special meals. The curated bar program includes local beers, global wines, and house cocktails.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page labels multiple dishes 'Vegetarian' throughout all sections; customer review states 'so many options for gluten-free and vegetarian'

restaurant.name: Bright Jenny
restaurant.desc: Bright Jenny is a specialty coffee roaster and café in Kelowna that roasts its own beans and serves a range of blends and single-origin coffees in a welcoming, personality-forward space. The business runs multiple café locations and a full online shop, with mobile ordering that lets customers order ahead for quick pickup. With outdoor seating and a food menu alongside drinks, it makes a solid pit stop for cyclists moving through the Kelowna area.

restaurant.name: Hello Nori
restaurant.desc: Hello Nori bills itself as Canada's premier Japanese hand roll bar, specializing in Temaki-style sushi made with crispy nori, warm seasoned rice, and Ocean Wise-certified sustainable seafood. The restaurant has a refined, design-forward atmosphere drawing on Japanese aesthetic traditions, with sake served in cedar Masu boxes and individually prepared hand rolls delivered one at a time for maximum freshness. It operates multiple BC locations and accepts walk-ins on a first-come, first-served basis.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page shows 'Gluten-Free - Vegan - Oceanwise' label and lists plant-based hand roll options including Avocado, Pickled Vegetables, and Cucumber

restaurant.name: Nuba
restaurant.desc: Nuba is a beloved Lebanese restaurant in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, founded in 2003 and celebrated for fresh, organic, locally-sourced ingredients prepared daily from scratch. The menu leans heavily plant-based, featuring a wide array of vegan and gluten-free mezze, falafel, and hummus dishes rooted in generations-old Lebanese family recipes. This Gastown outpost, branded 'Underground Gastown,' is one of four Vancouver locations and offers both sit-down dining and online ordering.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page states 'A large portion of our menu items are vegan.' Individual menu items throughout are labelled Vegan and GF

restaurant.name: Wally's Burger
restaurant.desc: Wally's Burgers is a family-operated BC institution with over 65 years of history, now running seasonally out of Cates Park in North Vancouver. The menu features classic smash burgers, loaded hot dogs, fish and chips, poutine, and old-school milkshakes, all made with fresh local ingredients and their signature Wally's Sauce. Cates Park is a well-known cycling destination on the North Shore waterfront, making this a natural and well-loved pit stop for riders on that route.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Veggie Deluxe burger; sauce recipes page features a Veggie Burger Wrap. No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Green Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Green Cuisine is a fully plant-based restaurant and café tucked into Market Square's courtyard in downtown Victoria, serving sustainable vegan food since 1990. The café is Victoria's first to serve Certified Climate-Positive coffee, and also offers handcrafted plant-based gelato, freshly baked treats, and a wide range of gluten-free options. All ingredients are listed with allergens highlighted, and the business composts and recycles on-site as part of a long-standing sustainability commitment.

detail.address: 560 Johnson Street, #5 At Market Square's Courtyard, Victoria, BC V8W 3C6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Fully plant-based menu (). Website notes 'lots of gluten-free, sugar-free' options and all food is made from plant-based ingredients

restaurant.name: J Squared Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: J Squared Ice Cream is an ice cream shop in Richmond offering a variety of flavours and seasonal products. The business provides a casual refreshment stop suitable for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Whipple Tree Bakery
restaurant.desc: Whipple Tree Bakery is a bakery on Menzies Street in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood, a short ride from the Inner Harbour and Beacon Hill Park. The Facebook page indicates it is a recently established business. As a neighbourhood bakery, it could offer a convenient stop for cyclists seeking fresh baked goods while exploring Victoria.

restaurant.name: Roland's Creekside Pub
restaurant.desc: Roland's Creekside Pub has been a fixture in Whistler's Creekside village since 2008, situated next to the Nita Lake Lodge. It operates as a full pub and sports bar with nine flat-screen TVs, serving pub fare made with Ocean Wise seafood, Certified Angus Beef, and non-medicated BC chicken, alongside housemade desserts. An attached Cold Beer & Wine Store operates 365 days a year, making it a convenient stop for stocking up after a ride.

detail.address: 2129 Lake Placid Road, Creekside, Whistler, BC V0N 1B2

restaurant.name: The Rack Bistro
restaurant.desc: The Rack Bistro is a West Coast-inspired bistro with two locations in Greater Victoria — Langford and Saanich — built around fresh, locally-sourced ingredients in a cozy, rustic setting. The Saanich location on Cedar Hill Cross Road is the newer of the two, opened by owner Cole Byers alongside wife Jasmine and Chef Rel. An all-day menu of West Coast favourites with a family-friendly atmosphere makes it a solid sit-down option for cyclists in the Victoria area.

detail.address: 1550 Cedar Hill Cross Road, Victoria, V8P 2P4

restaurant.name: Pizza 64
restaurant.desc: Pizza 64 is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 2010 with over 20 British Columbia locations, including this Chilliwack outpost on the Lougheed Highway. The menu spans specialty, signature, and gourmet pizzas made with fresh dough and sauce prepared at each location, alongside wings, pasta, and sides. Online ordering for pickup makes it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian pizzas: Garden Fresh (onions, mushrooms, olives, tomatoes, green peppers), Pesto Veggie (garlic, spinach, onions, green peppers, tomatoes), and Passion of India (Tandoori Paneer). No vegan or gluten-free claims found

restaurant.name: Saha Eatery
restaurant.desc: Saha Eatery is a Squamish restaurant drawing on Silk Road culinary traditions, combining Lebanese and Middle Eastern flavours with ethically sourced meats, grains, and legumes prepared from scratch daily. Located just two minutes from the Sea to Sky Highway, it has been recognized as one of the best restaurants in Squamish by Restaurantji. The menu features a wide range of mezze, wraps, bowls, and platters with extensive vegan and gluten-free options.

notes.Takeout: Dedicated 'Take Out Only Meals' menu section; detailed pickup instructions on website; online ordering available
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Extensive vegan (vg) and gluten-free (gf) items throughout the menu including hummus, falafel, baba ganooj, deep fried cauliflower, mujadrah, and a dedicated Nabatti vegan platter; OSM also confirms and

restaurant.name: Aburi To-Go
restaurant.desc: Aburi To-Go bills itself as Vancouver's first 'grocerant' — a hybrid grocery store and restaurant — offering fresh Japanese ready-to-eat meals, daily bento boxes, onigiri, ramen kits, house-made sauces, and imported Japanese snacks in the Yaletown neighbourhood. Founded in 2020 as an extension of the acclaimed Aburi Restaurants Canada group (behind Miku and Minami), it sits directly next to Minami Restaurant on Mainland Street. Cyclists riding the nearby seawall or passing through Yaletown will find a wide selection of travel-friendly packaged meals and plant-based options well-suited to the road.

notes.Packed lunches: Daily bento boxes, Ready-to-Eat packaged salads, sando sandwiches, and bowls available as grab-and-go items
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: SHOJIN plant-based line: 'daily chef-crafted in-house items, as well as exclusive imports from Japan. Available at both Aburi To-Go locations.'

restaurant.name: Victoria Sushi
restaurant.desc: Victoria Sushi is a Japanese and Asian restaurant tucked into the Victoria Hill neighbourhood of New Westminster, billing itself as 'The Friendly Neighborhood Sushi Restaurant.' It offers fresh, shareable plates made with Japanese ingredients alongside sake, beer, and wine. Takeaway and online ordering are available, making it a practical food stop for cyclists moving through New Westminster.

restaurant.name: Dosa Factory
restaurant.desc: Dosa Factory is a South Indian restaurant on Kingsway specializing in over 100 varieties of dosa — fermented rice-and-lentil crepes served with house-made chutneys and sambar — alongside Indo-Chinese, North Indian, and Tandoori dishes. The 100+ seat dining room doubles as a party hall for large gatherings. The menu stands out for its breadth of vegetarian options and an explicitly gluten-free dosa lineup.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated 'Veg Appetizers' and 'Veg Dosa' menu sections; website states dosas are 'South Indian style fermented crepe — 100% Gluten Free'

restaurant.name: Tsukiji Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Tsukiji Japanese Restaurant is a long-established Richmond dining room that has been serving traditional Japanese cuisine since 2003, built around a legacy of head chefs whose techniques continue to define the kitchen. The menu centres on sashimi prepared with ingredients imported daily from Japan, alongside 25+ varieties of aburi and nigiri, A5 wagyu beef, and an exclusive premium sake selection the restaurant claims is unavailable elsewhere in Vancouver. The site is also offered in Chinese, reflecting the multilingual community it serves.

detail.address: #130 – 4751 Garden City Rd, Richmond, BC V6X 3M7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian dishes: Vegetable Miso Soup, House Green Salad, Spinach Ohitashi, Spinach Gomaae, Kinpira Gobo (Burdock Root). No explicit vegan or gluten-free labelling found

restaurant.name: 97 Street Pub
restaurant.desc: 97 Street Pub is a full-service pub and sports bar attached to the Best Western Plus Kelowna Hotel & Suites on Highway 97 North, featuring 16 screens, a dining room, and a daily-open patio with a wide selection of local Okanagan beer, wine, and a broad food menu. The pub hosts regular live entertainment on Saturday nights and offers delivery through DoorDash. Its location near the mall and supermarkets makes it a convenient stop for visitors passing through the north end of Kelowna.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page includes explicit dietary filters for Vegetarian, Vegetarian-modifiable, Vegan, Vegan-modifiable, Gluten-Free, Gluten-Free Available, Gluten-Free modifiable, and Dairy-Free options

restaurant.name: The Mainstay
restaurant.desc: The Mainstay is the central bar of British Columbia's first licensed food hall, anchoring 18 independent food kitchens inside the Lonsdale Quay Market on North Vancouver's waterfront. Opened in January 2026, it serves BC craft beers on draft, a curated wine list, cocktails, and alcohol-free options alongside a live music program. The food hall format gives touring cyclists rolling in off the SeaBus a rare combination of a proper licensed bar and access to a wide variety of food vendors all under one roof.

detail.address: 123 Carrie Cates Ct, North Vancouver, BC V7M 3K7

restaurant.name: Wheelies Cafe
restaurant.desc: Wheelies Cafe is a sandwich-focused eatery in Victoria, BC, offering both dine-in and takeout with outdoor seating — a straightforward stop for a touring cyclist looking for a quick meal. The name 'Wheelies' hints at a possible two-wheeled theme, though whether that extends to bicycles or motorcycles is unconfirmed. Its outdoor seating makes it a comfortable spot to rest before continuing a ride.

restaurant.name: Bamboo Grove Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Bamboo Grove Restaurant is one of Richmond's oldest Chinese restaurants, established in 1963 as a coffee shop and now an award-winning Cantonese dining destination in the city's busy Number 3 Road corridor. It has earned multiple Metro Vancouver Chinese Restaurant Awards since 2010, with celebrated signature dishes including geoduck with scrambled eggs and a slow-boiled pork stomach and ginkgo soup. A touring cyclist will find a full-service sit-down restaurant serving an extensive menu of live seafood, clay pot dishes, and Cantonese classics.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes identifiably vegetarian dishes: Deep Fried Spicy Tofu ($29.95), Stir Fried Luffa w/ Black Fungus & Assorted Mushrooms ($35.95), Lettuce w/ Preserved Bean Curd Sauce Chilli Pepper Hot Pot ($29.95). No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Hong Kong Flavor Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Hong Kong Flavor Restaurant is a Hong Kong-style Chinese eatery in Richmond serving a broad menu that spans breakfast, lunch, afternoon tea, and dinner. The restaurant runs seasonal specials including elaborate Lunar New Year poon choi (basin feast) sets that require advance booking. It is wheelchair accessible and offers both dine-in and takeout service.

restaurant.name: The Keg
restaurant.desc: The Keg Steakhouse + Bar at Park Royal is a Canadian steakhouse chain located on the south side of Park Royal Mall in West Vancouver, known for aged beef, a full bar, and a covered heated patio. The location is wheelchair accessible and includes a semi-private dining room suitable for groups. Takeout and DoorDash delivery are available for those who want a meal on the go.

detail.address: 731 Main Street, Unit 110, West Vancouver, British Columbia, V7T 0A5

restaurant.name: Alfa
restaurant.desc: Alfa Greco Roman Cuisine is a long-running Greek restaurant in Tsawwassen that has served the community since 1979, making it one of the area's most enduring eateries. The menu spans classic Greek fare — souvlaki platters, kalamari, spanakopita, and homemade dips — alongside pizzas, pastas, and BBQ ribs, offering substantial post-ride meals. Catering, table reservations, and both dine-in and pick-up options make it a flexible stop for solo riders and cycling groups alike.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Dine-in and Pick-up only' for specials; catering page confirms 'We offer both dining and delivery, as well as pick-up.'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists multiple vegetarian items (spanakopita, homous, tzatziki, dolmades, salads). No explicit vegan confirmation

restaurant.name: Pho 777 Vietnamese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Pho 777 is a Vietnamese restaurant on Fraser Highway in central Langley serving pho and a full menu of Vietnamese cuisine for dine-in, takeout, and delivery. It also offers catering, banquet services, and explicitly advertises tourist group meals, suggesting it can accommodate larger cycling groups. Its location on Fraser Hwy at 206 Street puts it on a main arterial through Langley convenient to cyclists passing through.

restaurant.name: The Fort Pub & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Fort Pub & Grill is a storied neighbourhood pub in the heart of historic Fort Langley, situated about half a kilometre from the Fort Langley National Historic Site trading post. The building traces its roots to the Fort Langley Hotel and has survived floods, fires, and Prohibition, giving it an atmosphere filled with local artefacts and genuine character. Cyclists will find two large patios, a broad menu from wings to salmon chowder, weekend brunch, and delivery or pickup options for those in a hurry.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian items including Vegetarian Flatbread Grill, KFC: Killer Fried Cauliflower, Fort Greens salad, Roasted Beet Salad, Strawberry Pecan Salad, Mac & Cheese, and Smashed Avocado Toast. No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Big Bend
restaurant.desc: Big Bend Cafe is a locally owned breakfast and lunch spot that has been serving Golden since 2009, winning best breakfast in the Kootenay Rockies multiple years running. The menu spans 60 items — from eggs benedict and huevos rancheros to homemade soups — designed to fuel a day of mountain adventures. A sunny patio with views of the surrounding mountains makes it a welcoming stop for cyclists passing through Golden.

restaurant.name: Classic Pizza
restaurant.desc: Canadian Classic Pizza Ltd. is a community pizza restaurant that has been serving the Abbotsford area since 2007. The menu is notably diverse, blending classic Canadian toppings with South Asian-inspired options like Paneer, Palak Paneer, and Shahi Paneer pizzas, plus gluten-free crust available on request. Cyclists can dine in or take out, with delivery also available.

detail.address: 31789 South Fraser Way, Abbotsford, BC V2T 1V2

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website contact page states 'We serve gluten free pizza upon your request and we are not using any nuts in our ingredients.' Menu includes an extensive dedicated Vegetarian Pizzas section with 12+ options

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's Canada fast-food outlet located in North Vancouver, serving burgers, chicken, breakfast, and McCafé beverages. The location includes a drive-through and offers takeaway. As a large chain presence on a cycling route, it could serve as a calorie stop, though the site is primarily designed around vehicle access.

restaurant.name: Shuck Taylor's
restaurant.desc: Shuck Taylor's is a casual, walk-in oyster bar in downtown Victoria run by the Wandering Mollusk, focusing on freshly shucked Pacific oysters, lobster rolls, and global shellfish including Nova Scotia lobster and Caspian Sea caviar. The restaurant operates on a first-come, first-serve basis with no reservations, and also offers sustainable seafood boil buckets available for online order and in-store pickup. The parent brand, Wandering Mollusk, also runs pop-up oyster bars and catering events across Vancouver Island and the Lower Mainland.

restaurant.name: Silom Thai Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Silom Thai Cuisine is a Vancouver restaurant inspired by the lively Silom Road dining district of Bangkok, known for its street food and restaurant culture. The restaurant emphasizes authentic Thai cooking using traditional ingredients and recipes rooted in Thailand's culinary heritage. It operates as a full sit-down dining establishment with reservations available, making it a viable stop for cyclists looking for a proper meal on the Knight Street corridor.

restaurant.name: Cascadia Bakehouse
restaurant.desc: Cascadia Bakehouse is a wife-and-husband-run neighbourhood micro bakehouse and caffè in Port Moody, specialising in naturally leavened heritage grain breads, viennoiserie, and house-made pastries using seasonal, local, and organic BC ingredients. The menu rotates around relationships with BC farmers and Italian and Japanese culinary influences from owners Kaitlin and Marco. Cyclists can stop for freshly baked bread, house-made preserves and nut butters, and espresso-based drinks.

restaurant.name: Wildflower
restaurant.desc: The Wildflower is a family-friendly, full-service restaurant inside the Fairmont Chateau Whistler, one of Whistler's landmark luxury mountain resorts at the base of Blackcomb Mountain. It serves locally inspired breakfast and dinner dishes alongside Whistler's most extensive wine list and a selection of regional craft beers. A touring cyclist finishing a ride in Whistler would find a welcoming, sit-down dining experience with a broad menu and a family-friendly atmosphere.

detail.address: 4599 Chateau Boulevard, Whistler, British Columbia V8E 0Z5

restaurant.name: The Basic
restaurant.desc: The Basic Eats is a casual all-day breakfast and lunch spot with three Vancouver locations, emphasizing affordable prices, generous portions, and locally sourced ingredients. The Main Street location sits in one of Vancouver's most bicycle-friendly corridors, making it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists. The menu leans heavily on egg dishes, griddle items, and Eggs Benedict variations, with a solid selection of vegetarian options throughout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items explicitly labeled 'Vegetarian' (e.g., Simply Eggs, Eggs Florentine, Veggie Hash, Beyond Sausage Brekkie, Avocado & Tomato Benny); gluten-free bread available as a substitute

restaurant.name: Ono Poké & Grill
restaurant.desc: Ono Poké is a Victoria-based Hawaiian poké bar with four shopping-centre locations across the city, founded by a restaurateur who discovered traditional Hawaiian poké on a trip to the islands and set out to recreate that experience on the West Coast. The menu centres on customizable ahi tuna bowls marinated in house shoyu blends, alongside Hawaiian hot plates like Loco Moco and Garlic Shrimp. It's a fast-casual, build-your-own concept with a broad range of dietary accommodations, making it a practical and flavourful refuelling stop for cyclists passing through Victoria's commercial centres.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'With options for gluten-free, vegan, keto-friendly, and high-protein lifestyles, there's something at Ono for everyone to enjoy!' Menu also marks GF and V options on individual items

restaurant.name: Hapag
restaurant.desc: Hapag — a Filipino word meaning 'table' — is a neighbourhood Filipino grill on Victoria Drive in East Vancouver, serving classic dishes like Crispy Pata (deep-fried pork hock), Sisig, and a roster of grilled meats straight from the ihaw-ihaw (charcoal grill) tradition. The menu spans street-food staples such as BBQ pork skewers and Isaw, through to baked desserts like Ube Cheesecake and Leche Flan, alongside party trays for larger groups. Dine-in and takeout are both available, making it a solid stop for a hearty, culture-rich meal on a long ride through East Van.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian option: Lumpiang Gulay (veggie spring rolls with cabbage, carrots, leeks, tofu). Gluten-free: Leche Flan explicitly labelled 'Gluten-free' on menu

restaurant.name: Farm Country Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: Farm Country Brewing is a Langley craft brewery producing a wide roster of beers from German Pilsners and hazy IPAs to fruit sours and stouts, served in a plaza tasting room with a full food menu built around locally-sourced ingredients. The space hosts regular live music, open-mic nights, and themed trivia evenings, giving it a lively community-hub feel. Cyclists in the Fraser Valley corridor will find a solid sit-down meal and a rotating selection of house-brewed beer within a short detour of the Langley Central transit hub.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Tasting Room Menu page tags Spinach Artichoke Dip as [V] and Chips + Salsa as [V] [GF], confirming vegetarian and gluten-free options

restaurant.name: Donegal's Irish House
restaurant.desc: Founded in 1978 by the Allen and Green families, Donegal's Irish House is an independently owned, family-operated neighborhood pub in Surrey with nearly five decades of community history. It hosts regular live music events and serves a broad menu of pub classics alongside a creative cocktail list. Cyclists stopping in will find a genuinely welcoming atmosphere shaped by Irish hospitality tradition rather than corporate formula.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items marked 'GF*' including Fries, Hot-Honey Fries, Potato Skins, and Mini Nachos; vegetarian options include Fried Perogies (spinach & feta) and Mini Nachos

restaurant.name: Timbertrain Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Founded in 2011 by two friends, Timbertrain Coffee Roasters has grown into a well-regarded Vancouver specialty roaster with three café locations, including this Gastown outpost on West Cordova Street. The café emphasizes single-origin and seasonal coffees sourced through direct, transparent relationships with farms across multiple origins. Situated in one of Vancouver's most cycling-accessible and tourist-frequented neighbourhoods, it offers a welcoming community space for a post-ride espresso or bag of freshly roasted beans.

restaurant.name: Pokébar
restaurant.desc: Pokébar is a fast-casual Hawaiian-style poké bowl restaurant where guests build fully customizable bowls starting from rice, noodles, or greens bases and layered with fresh-daily fish and a wide array of proteins, mix-ins, sauces, and toppings. The chain traces its roots to a family sushi restaurant opened in 1989 and now operates multiple BC locations, with the Davie Street outlet serving Vancouver's busy West End. Touring cyclists will find a quick, filling, and relatively healthy meal option with both counter pickup and major delivery app support.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Tofu listed as a protein option; mixed greens available as a bowl base, supporting vegetarian builds. No explicit vegan or gluten-free labelling found on the website

restaurant.name: Indian Oven
restaurant.desc: The Indian Oven is a sit-down Indian restaurant on the second floor of a Kitsilano building on West 4th Avenue, a well-travelled cycling corridor. The kitchen emphasizes authenticity, preparing every dish from scratch with hand-picked spices and locally sourced produce, and the menu spans appetizers, tandoori, a wide range of curries, and freshly baked breads. Online ordering and delivery are available, making it a convenient stop or meal-ahead option for cyclists passing through the neighbourhood.

notes.Takeout: Website features 'Order Online' and 'Get Free Delivery on Online Orders' (within 5 km, minimum $40 before tax)
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists dedicated Vegetarian and Paneer sections; Veg Combo and multiple veg appetizers/curries explicitly offered. No GF or vegan claims found

restaurant.name: 49 Below Craft Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: 49 Below is a small-batch, slow-churned craft ice cream company rooted in Oak Bay, Victoria, making nearly all mix-ins and sauces in-house using a custom dairy base from a local Vancouver Island farm. Founded after a chance encounter with Tuscan gelato, it has grown from a home kitchen subscription business into two neighbourhood scoop shops with seasonal rotating flavours and custom ice cream cakes. The Oak Bay shop on Cadboro Bay Road is a welcoming stop with a community-first ethos and genuine local character.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Gluten free and vegan options available' for ice cream cakes

restaurant.name: Tugwell Creek Honey Farm and Meadery
restaurant.desc: A farm-based producer of mead and honey located in Sooke. Classified as a wine shop reflecting its focus on mead (honey-based wine) and honey products.

restaurant.name: Four Winds Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: Four Winds Brewing's Tilbury taproom is a craft brewery tasting room paired with a full in-house kitchen, serving handmade tacos, burgers, and seasonal tapas made from locally sourced and organic ingredients. It functions as a community hub where the brewery's freshest beers on tap are poured alongside food made entirely from scratch. Takeout taco kits and beer to-go are available for those who want to grab something on the road.

restaurant.name: Fezziwig's Bakery-Cafe
restaurant.desc: Fezziwig's is a Kelowna institution that has been baking all its bread fresh on-site every morning since 2006, using locally sourced and organic ingredients where possible. Named after the warm-hearted Dickens character, the cafe offers hearty home-style breakfasts and a generous sandwich menu, alongside Cherry Hill Coffee — a local, organic, fair-trade roaster. This Guisachan Village Centre location is one of three around Kelowna, making it a reliable mid-ride stop in the city's south end.

notes.Takeout: Website lunch menu states: 'Takeaway sandwiches come with bag of Kettle Chips but no garnish.'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Explicit 'Vegetarian' sandwich on lunch menu (avocado, cream cheese, sun-dried tomato, cucumber, red onions); gluten-free options noted across menus (GF wraps, GF desserts, GF salads with cashews instead of croutons)

restaurant.name: Pizza Factory
restaurant.desc: Pizza Factory has been a neighbourhood pizza staple in Burnaby's Metrotown area since 1996. The menu spans customizable pizzas in multiple sizes alongside pastas, salads, and sides, with vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free crust options available. Situated on the Kingsway corridor, it offers both walk-in pickup and online ordering, making it a practical refuelling option for cyclists passing through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists dedicated 'Vegetarian' and 'Pesto Vegetarian' classic pizzas; GF crust available as a paid add-on

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: This Tim Hortons in Sardis is a full-service outpost of Canada's most ubiquitous coffee chain, located in a retail plaza on Luckakuck Way in Chilliwack. It offers a complete menu spanning freshly brewed coffee, espresso drinks, breakfast wraps with Canadian eggs, baked goods, soups, and chili — enough variety for a proper mid-ride fuel stop. The dine-in setting with drive-through availability makes it a dependable and familiar waypoint on routes through the Fraser Valley.

detail.address: 45793 Luckakuck Way Unit# 105, Chilliwack, BC V2R 5S3

restaurant.name: Okoman Sushi
restaurant.desc: Sushi restaurant in North Vancouver with takeout and delivery service. Provides on-site washrooms for customer use.

restaurant.name: Sainam
restaurant.desc: Sainam is an Isaan-style Thai eatery and bar in Vancouver's West End, helmed by award-winning chef Angus An. The menu centres on the bold, rustic flavours of Thailand's northeastern Isaan region — papaya salads, grilled meats, and fermented dishes meant to be shared with sticky rice. It sits on lively Davie Street, making it a convenient stop for cyclists riding through the West End.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu pages include a 'VIEW VEGETARIAN OPTIONS' link; lunch menu labels specific items '(VG)' (e.g. Crispy Mushroom Nam Tok) and notes 'VG Available' on some dishes

restaurant.name: Sushi Royal Tokyo
restaurant.desc: Sushi Royal Tokyo is a Japanese restaurant in downtown Kamloops with a broad menu spanning sushi rolls, sashimi, nigiri, tempura, katsu, teriyaki, and donburi. It offers both dine-in and online ordering, which suits cyclists looking to order ahead or grab a quick meal. Its central Victoria Street location puts it in the heart of Kamloops's downtown core.

restaurant.name: Embers Brewhouse
restaurant.desc: Embers Brewhouse is a craft brewpub that opened in 2025 in downtown Kamloops, serving house-made beers alongside a food menu in a casual sit-down setting. Situated on Victoria Street in the city core, it sits on a natural route through town for cyclists riding the TransCanada or exploring the Kamloops area. Regular programming like Saturday trivia nights points to an active local gathering spot rather than a purely tourist-facing operation.

restaurant.name: Pho Ever
restaurant.desc: Pho Ever is a Vietnamese restaurant on Granville Street in South Vancouver offering authentic pho, Vietnamese sandwiches (bánh mì), and bubble teas. It serves both dine-in and takeout customers seven days a week. The Granville Street corridor is a common cycling route, making this a convenient stop for riders exploring the area.

restaurant.name: Train Wreck Brewing + BBQ
restaurant.desc: Train Wreck Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom in Port Moody that brews unfiltered, full-flavoured beers on-site using traditional techniques and quality local ingredients. The sprawling event space hosts daily rotating food vendors, bar games, and live music, making it a lively community gathering spot rather than a typical pub. Brewery tours are also on offer for visitors wanting a behind-the-scenes look at the brewing operation.

detail.address: 3044 St Johns St, Port Moody, BC V3H 2C5

restaurant.name: Lot 1 Pasta Bar
restaurant.desc: Lot 1 Pasta Bar is Victoria's original pasta bar, blending family-heritage Italian recipes with international flavours and locally sourced BC ingredients in a warehouse-style space with 17-foot ceilings and an industrial aesthetic. Founded by the team behind Victoria's original burger lounge, it offers handcrafted pasta, creative cocktails featuring local distilleries, and a rotating selection of Vancouver Island draught beers. A touring cyclist looking for a substantial sit-down meal with gluten-free and vegan options in the heart of Victoria would find this a solid choice.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'delicious gluten-free options available'; menu includes a Vegan 'Cheese'cake and multiple dishes with tofu as a protein add-on, indicating vegetarian/vegan accommodation

restaurant.name: Hula Poke
restaurant.desc: Hula Poké is a Hawaiian-inspired poke bowl chain expanding across Western Canada, with a location inside Tsawwassen Mills mall. Diners build custom bowls from proteins like ahi tuna, salmon, chicken, or tofu over coconut or sushi rice, picking from a range of globally-influenced signature sauces. The fresh, customizable format makes it a practical and satisfying stop for cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple bowls explicitly labeled 'VEGAN FRIENDLY' (e.g. YUZU TRADITIONAL, KOKO SPICY KOREAN, PONZU, CALI VEG) and 'GLUTEN FRIENDLY'; tofu and sweet potato listed as protein options

restaurant.name: Ocean Park Pizza & Village Pub
restaurant.desc: Ocean Park Pizza & Village Pub is a family-owned restaurant and neighbourhood pub that has anchored the Ocean Park community for over 47 years, earning the 2018 South Surrey & White Rock Chamber of Commerce Medium Sized Business of the Year award. The current Craftsman-style building, opened in 2006, combines a full-service pizza and Italian-American restaurant with a pub featuring 20 beers on tap. It is open 364 days a year and well-regarded locally, having been voted best pub and best pizza in South Surrey/White Rock by multiple community readers' choice polls.

restaurant.name: Rosalinda's All Day Breakfast
restaurant.desc: Rosalinda's is a family diner in downtown Vernon serving all-day breakfast and lunch with a Filipino-Canadian twist — think Pancit Noodles and Mano Dino Burger alongside classic Eggs Benny and French Toast. Home-baked bread, buns, desserts, and pastries are made in-house. It's a welcoming neighbourhood spot steps from Polson Park and within reach of Kalamalka and Ellison Provincial Park trails.

restaurant.name: Myth Grill & Yakitori Bistro
restaurant.desc: Myth Grill & Yakitori Bistro is a modern Japanese charcoal-grill restaurant in Richmond, cooking skewers and grilled meats over traditional binchotan charcoal to highlight seasonal ingredients. Part of the Myth Group restaurant family, it aims for a relaxed urban tavern atmosphere blending yakitori tradition with sake and a cozy wooden interior. Cyclists passing through Richmond's Ackroyd Road commercial corridor could use it as a sit-down or takeout meal stop.

restaurant.name: Delhi Fusion Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Delhi Fusion Indian Cuisine is a sit-down Indian restaurant on Vancouver's bustling Commercial Drive, blending traditional tandoor cooking with inventive fusion dishes such as Butter Chicken Pizza and Samosa Chaat Burger. The menu spans a wide range from street chaat and Indo-Chinese momos to biryanis and tandoori specialties, with a full catering service available for events. Commercial Drive is one of Vancouver's main cycling corridors, making this a convenient full-meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the east side.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'VEG DISHES' section; multiple vegetarian items listed throughout (Veggie Pakora, Paneer Pakora, Veggie Samosa, Onion Bhaji, etc.). No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Taste of Saigon Cafe
restaurant.desc: Taste of Saigon Cafe is a Vietnamese restaurant on Squamish's main commercial strip, Cleveland Avenue, sitting along the Sea to Sky cycling corridor between Vancouver and Whistler. It offers indoor seating in a smoke-free environment, making it a sheltered rest stop for cyclists passing through town. Vietnamese cuisine — pho, banh mi, and similar dishes — tends to be hearty and well-suited to the appetite of a touring cyclist.

restaurant.name: Chilango
restaurant.desc: Chilango Modern Mexican is a contemporary sit-down restaurant on Kelowna's main downtown corridor, Bernard Avenue, specializing in Mexican street-food-inspired dishes including tacos, burritos, and craft cocktails spanning brunch through late-night service. It is the sister restaurant to El Taquero, a Kelowna institution next door that has been serving traditional street tacos for over 10 years. Positive guest reviews highlight the food quality, friendly service, and lively atmosphere, making it a viable meal stop for cyclists rolling through downtown Kelowna.

restaurant.name: Hermann's Jazz Club
restaurant.desc: Hermann's Jazz Club is Canada's longest continuously running jazz club, tracing its roots to 1981 and now a civic institution in the heart of downtown Victoria. Operated by the non-profit Arts on View Society with the City of Victoria as building owner since 2024, it offers an intimate 130-seat lounge and restaurant featuring nightly live jazz, blues, and world music alongside a full dinner menu. A touring cyclist finishing a day's ride will find a convivial evening venue with hearty entrées and a rich local music culture steps from the city centre.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a Mushroom Wellington entrée labelled as vegetarian, a 'Vegetarian 18' substitution option for Chicken Linguine, and a 'Gluten Free Chocolate Torte' dessert

restaurant.name: naán club Exquisite Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Naan Club is a modern Indian bistro in a Coquitlam retail plaza bringing authentic Indian cuisine with westernized hospitality — spanning classic butter chicken and naan through to tandoori sliders and masala fries. The restaurant features a full cocktail bar with signature drinks and a heated lounge patio under development. Dishes can be customized by spice level, making it accessible to a wide range of palates.

detail.address: 100 Schoolhouse Street, Unit 102, Coquitlam, BC V3K 6V9

restaurant.name: Fraser Park Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Fraser Park Restaurant is a long-running Burnaby neighbourhood institution founded in 1997 by Anton and Sylvia Heggen, serving hearty homestyle German-Filipino fusion food made from scratch. The restaurant is known for its signature schnitzel burger, German breakfast with housemade potato pancakes and sausages, and daily housemade soups. Described as one of the most notable eateries in BC's lower mainland, it offers substantial, calorie-rich meals well suited to hungry touring cyclists.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a 'Vegetarian with cheese' sandwich option under Burgers & Sandwiches; porridge is also vegetarian

restaurant.name: V-Show Karaoke
restaurant.desc: V-Show Karaoke is a karaoke bar in Burnaby offering air-conditioned indoor seating with a no-smoking policy. The venue accepts credit and debit cards and is wheelchair accessible. Touring cyclists may find it a convenient stop for evening entertainment and refreshment.

restaurant.name: Ignite Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Ignite Pizzeria is a Vancouver-born stone-fired pizza restaurant that opened its Mount Pleasant location in 2017, now the flagship of a growing multi-location chain across Metro Vancouver. Pizzas are hand-tossed with low-sodium dough given a three-day rest before firing at 800°F, with a menu that covers both meat-forward and fully vegan options. The Mount Pleasant location is licensed, making it a sit-down dining option for cyclists coming off the Main Street corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu has a dedicated 'Herbivore + Vegan' section; gluten-friendly housemade crust available for medium pizzas (+$5 fee); catering page explicitly lists 'gluten-friendly, vegetarian, and vegan selections'

restaurant.name: Small Victory
restaurant.desc: Small Victory is a family-owned artisan bakery and café whose founders trace their roots to a Kenyan immigrant bakery started by their parents on West Broadway. The Yaletown location sits on Marinaside Crescent, steps from the False Creek seawall — one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors — making it a natural stop for riders. The menu runs from handcrafted sourdough loaves and laminated pastries to full brunch and lunch offerings including sandwiches, power bowls, and specialty coffee sourced from local roasters.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes 'Vegan Chickpea Masala Sandwich', 'Mango Coconut Cake (Gluten Friendly)', and multiple plant-based items (Avocado Toast, Spinach & Feta Turnover, Spring Edamame & Quinoa Power Bowl)

restaurant.name: Legends Bistro
restaurant.desc: Legends Bistro is the clubhouse restaurant at Cultus Lake Golf Club, set in a beautiful solarium with views of the fairways and surrounding mountains. It serves the public year-round across breakfast, lunch, and dinner, with a menu spanning American classics, pizza, sandwiches, and salads alongside a full bar. Themed weekly dinner nights and proximity to Cultus Lake's recreational area make it a natural stop for cyclists passing through the Columbia Valley corridor.

detail.address: 4000 Columbia Valley Road, Cultus Lake, BC V2R 5H6

restaurant.name: Sol Fine Foods
restaurant.desc: Sol Fine Foods is a scratch-kitchen cafe and deli on the Selkirk Waterfront in Victoria, serving locally sourced breakfast and lunch made with Berryman's meats, farm-fresh eggs, and produce from regional suppliers. Coffee is roasted by The Stick in the Mud Roastoreum, and the daily fresh sheet rotates hot specials alongside staple sandwiches, burgers, soups, and baked goods. Indoor dining and a sun-bathed patio are available, along with catering and online ordering for fresh and frozen take-home provisions.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian options confirmed across menus: Veggie Burger, Falafel Greek Bowl, Spinach-Mushroom Lasagna, Mexi-Black Bean Avocado Burrito, and protein bowls note 'can accommodate vegetarian.' No explicit vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Good Earth Coffeehouse
restaurant.desc: Good Earth Coffeehouse at Village Walk is a franchise café on Oak Bay Avenue in Victoria's Oak Bay neighbourhood, serving espresso drinks, fresh baked goods, breakfast sandwiches, soups, and seasonal specialty beverages. The menu spans a wide range of dietary needs — vegan, vegetarian, gluten-friendly, and dairy-free items are labelled throughout. Online ordering and catering are available, and the café sits on a well-travelled commercial strip convenient to cyclists exploring the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu pages include dietary filter options for Vegan (V), Vegetarian, Gluten Friendly (GF), Dairy Free, Wheat Free, and Egg Free, with labelled items across all menu categories

restaurant.name: Slow Coast Coffee
restaurant.desc: A coffee and bakery cafe located on Pender Island's Schooner Way. Serves the local community and provides a convenient rest stop for touring cyclists exploring the Gulf Islands.

restaurant.name: Heavenly Desserts
restaurant.desc: Heavenly Desserts is a premium dessert restaurant franchise originating in the UK in 2008, now with multiple Canadian locations. The Victoria outpost serves signature dishes including the Croffle (a croissant-waffle hybrid), elaborate American waffles, milk cakes, and crêpes, all with full table service. Each location features unique, elegantly designed interiors described as atmospheric and refined.

restaurant.name: Sunrise Pizza and Steak House
restaurant.desc: Sunrise Pizza & Steak House is a neighbourhood pizzeria on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most celebrated cycling corridors on the East Side. The broad menu spans handmade pizzas with fresh homemade crust, Greek specialties, Italian dishes, seafood, and steaks, making it well-suited for groups with varied tastes. Online ordering with delivery is available, offering a convenient refueling option for cyclists passing through the area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a dedicated Vegetarian Pizza (mushrooms, green peppers, onions, tomatoes, pineapple, olives, cheese & tomato sauce)

restaurant.name: Park Royal South Food Court
restaurant.desc: Park Royal South Food Court is housed within Park Royal, which opened in 1950 as Canada's first enclosed shopping centre, located in West Vancouver on the lands of the Squamish Nation. The food court features more than a dozen counter-service vendors including Tim Hortons, Subway, Booster Juice, Vina Vietnamese, and OPA! of Greece, making it a practical multi-option meal stop. The broader mall complex provides bicycle racks and, at the Park Royal North building, a dedicated Bike Stop with a tire pump and North Shore biking map.

detail.address: 2002 Park Royal South, West Vancouver, BC V7T 2W4

restaurant.name: Kokomo
restaurant.desc: Kokomo is a plant-based cafe and eatery in Kitsilano serving freshly made bowls, salads, acai bowls, and smoothies with an entirely vegan menu. It is one of four Metro Vancouver locations operated by Kokomo Foods Inc., offering both indoor and outdoor seating. The kitchen focuses on whole-food, globally inspired dishes — from lemongrass noodle salad to shawarma macro bowls — making it a solid refuelling stop for cyclists.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website describes Kokomo as a 'plant-based eatery' with an entirely plant-based menu across all locations

restaurant.name: Syros Pizza & Spaghetti

restaurant.name: Season's Apple Café
restaurant.desc: Season's Apple Café is a small Italian-cuisine café in Burnaby, operated by Park Chul Sung and Kim Kyung Hwa. Situated in a unit at 8699 Tenth Avenue, it appears to serve a neighbourhood clientele as a morning-to-afternoon café stop. Its Italian food focus may appeal to cyclists looking for a sit-down coffee or meal break in the area.

restaurant.name: The Modest Butcher
restaurant.desc: The Modest Butcher is a full-service restaurant and market situated on the grounds of Mt. Boucherie Estate Winery in West Kelowna, offering locally sourced meats, handcrafted cocktails, and an award-winning wine portfolio. The kitchen serves everything from casual burgers to tomahawk steaks dry-aged in-house, with a playful, irreverent personality that has made it a notable Okanagan dining destination since 2020. A touring cyclist looking for a substantial sit-down meal with local wine in the West Kelowna area will find this a solid stop.

restaurant.name: Grand Forks Station Pub
restaurant.desc: Grand Forks Station Pub is a pub in the village of Grand Forks. The establishment serves food and drink to locals and travelers in this small community. Outside smoking is permitted on the premises.

restaurant.name: Silvestre Deli & Bistro
restaurant.desc: Silvestre is a family-run Peruvian restaurant on Water Street in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, opened by Peruvian immigrants to share the authentic flavours of their homeland. The menu centres on traditional Peruvian classics — ceviche, causa rellena, chicharron, and tamales — alongside breakfast plates and housemade gelato. Its location on a popular urban cycling corridor makes it a convenient stop for riders exploring the waterfront.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes vegetarian options: causa rellena de vegetales, salpicon de verduras, yuquita frita (fried yuca), and egg-based breakfast dishes

restaurant.name: Yama Sushi
restaurant.desc: Yama Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in North Vancouver offering dine-in and online ordering. A casual dining spot convenient for cyclists seeking Japanese cuisine during their travels through the area.

restaurant.name: Rain or Shine Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Rain or Shine is a beloved Vancouver homemade ice cream chain making small-batch flavours with locally sourced BC ingredients, including custom-formula dairy from Birchwood Dairy Farm in Abbotsford. The UBC location sits on University Boulevard at the edge of campus, placing it directly on a popular cycling corridor near Pacific Spirit Regional Park trails. A rotating seasonal menu complements permanent flavours, with dedicated vegan and gluten-free options throughout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Numerous flavours are also labelled 'Gluten free. Egg free.'

restaurant.name: Kibune Sushi
restaurant.desc: Kibune Sushi is a sushi restaurant on Yew Street in Vancouver. As a full-service dining establishment, it provides a food and refreshment option for cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: Ms Tiffins
restaurant.desc: Ms Tiffin is a Vancouver Indian street food restaurant and tiffin subscription service founded in 2017 by Seema Nanda, offering bold dishes from crispy chaats and frankies to butter chicken poutine alongside home-style tiffin meal deliveries and a selection of mithai. Customer reviews praise the spacious, relaxed dining area and the authenticity of the food, which draws comparisons to roadside dhabas. The operation also handles wedding catering and group orders, making it a notable community hub for Indian cuisine in the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states: 'All tiffins are vegetarian by default. Non-veg upgrades are available on six days a week.'

restaurant.name: The Peri Peri Shack
restaurant.desc: The Peri Peri Shack is a flame-grilled peri peri chicken restaurant drawing on the African and Portuguese culinary tradition of the Peri-Peri pepper, with chicken marinated 24 hours in a secret spice blend before grilling. Cyclists can choose from seven flavour profiles ranging from Plain and Mild through Citrus & Herb, Mango, and Hot up to the signature Peri Nero. The restaurant also offers catering and sharing packs suited for groups.

restaurant.name: Toto Sushi
restaurant.desc: Toto Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Tsawwassen (Delta, BC) that relocated from Steveston, bringing the same quality-focused approach to its new community. The kitchen emphasizes wild sockeye salmon, premium Japanese Yamabuki sushi vinegar, roasted sea salt, and preservative-free nori. Cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen area will find a full menu spanning nigiri, sashimi, specialty rolls, teriyaki, ramen, and party trays.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Gallery page lists 'Tofu Teriyaki'

restaurant.name: Stanley's Bar and Grill
restaurant.desc: Stanley's Bar & Grill is a full-service restaurant housed inside the historic Stanley Park Pavilion, offering what the venue describes as Stanley Park's largest outdoor patio overlooking the park's lush gardens. The menu is built around local ingredients, Ocean Wise seafood, BC craft beers, and local wines, with award-winning dishes like the Royal Huntsman Burger. Situated at the heart of one of Vancouver's premier cycling destinations, it is a natural midride stop for anyone exploring Stanley Park's network of seawall and park paths.

restaurant.name: Sixth Street Grill
restaurant.desc: Sixth Street Grill is a sit-down restaurant in North Vancouver's uptown area, offering both indoor and outdoor seating in a no-smoking environment. Its outdoor patio and central street address make it a plausible rest stop for cyclists passing through the neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: Tim Hortons is a Canadian quick-service chain offering coffee, baked goods, soups, and breakfast wraps. It is a practical pit stop for cyclists moving through the downtown core who need a quick meal or beverage.

restaurant.name: Belleville's

Large-group and private event bookings are available, and the Inner Harbour location puts it squarely on the path of cyclists touring the Victoria waterfront.

restaurant.name: Chimac
restaurant.desc: Chimac is a Korean fried chicken and pub located on Yates Street in downtown Victoria. It offers casual indoor dining with a focus on Korean-style fried chicken and pub fare. restaurant.name: Kennedy's Liquor Beer & Wine Store

restaurant.name: Guacamole Mexican Grill
restaurant.desc: Guacamole Mexican Grill is a locally operated Mexican restaurant on King George Boulevard in Surrey, serving traditional Mexican specialties prepared with an emphasis on fresh ingredients. Cyclists passing through the King George corridor would find this a convenient stop for a full meal.

The menu also spans fresh pastries, desserts, and Banh Mi sandwiches. It is part of a small growing chain with a second Vancouver location on Hornby Street and a Saskatchewan outpost.

restaurant.name: Panago

The menu spans classic and specialty pizzas alongside wings, salads, cheesy bread, and desserts, with dedicated vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-smart options. For a touring cyclist passing through Delta, it provides a wide range of filling, customisable meal choices.

restaurant.name: Carlino Restaurant

restaurant.name: Courtyard Café
restaurant.desc: The Courtyard Café is a café located within Hotel Grand Pacific, a full-service hotel positioned steps from Victoria's Inner Harbour and the BC Legislature. Sitting at one of Victoria's most-visited tourist corridors, it is a natural stop for cyclists exploring the harbour front. The café operates daily and serves hotel guests and walk-in visitors alike.

restaurant.name: Samurai Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Samurai is an authentic Japanese sushi restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver, offering traditional Japanese cuisine in a full-service dining setting. The restaurant provides a sit-down dining experience in Vancouver's vibrant Davie Street neighborhood.

restaurant.name: Joju Hotpot
restaurant.desc: JoJu Hotpot and Asian Cuisine serves authentic Taiwanese and Cantonese food in the Burnaby Heights neighbourhood, offering a full dine-in menu of hotpot and Asian dishes. The restaurant also offers a catering menu for group celebrations and sells house-made frozen dim sum for takeaway. It is a neighbourhood staple appealing to cyclists looking for a hearty, inexpensive sit-down meal along the Hastings Street corridor.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: A Subway franchise located inside the Okanagan Lake Shopping Centre on Highway 97 in West Kelowna, offering made-to-order Footlongs, 6" sandwiches, wraps, and salads with fresh-baked bread. Cycling tourists on the Highway 97 corridor have access to quick pickup or dine-in options at this shopping centre stop.

restaurant.name: Messob Ethiopian
restaurant.desc: Messob Ethiopian Cuisine has been serving authentic Ethiopian food in Victoria since 2002, with all meals accompanied by injera, the traditional spongy flatbread that doubles as both plate and utensil. The restaurant is a compact neighbourhood spot on McKenzie Street that has built a loyal local following over more than two decades.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated 'Vegetarian - Vegan Plates' section on the menu; individual dishes labelled 'Vegetarian Vegan'. No gluten-free mention found

restaurant.name: Subway

Orders can be placed in-store, via app, through delivery, or at curbside pickup. As an independently owned and operated franchise, it provides a widely recognizable and accessible meal stop along a busy urban corridor.

restaurant.name: Finley's

The venue features a patio and hosts regular live music events, karaoke nights, and community fundraisers, making it a notable gathering spot on Nelson's main strip. Online ordering with delivery and takeout is available alongside full dine-in service.

restaurant.name: Bacayon's Chibugan

A touring cyclist looking for a substantial, flavour-forward meal in the Surrey area would find a broad selection of rice, noodle, pork, chicken, and vegetable dishes.

restaurant.name: Billy Gruff Creamery
restaurant.desc: Billy Gruff Creamery is an ice cream and gelato shop that has been a fixture at The Old Country Market in Coombs for decades, part of a beloved Vancouver Island landmark famous for its rooftop goats. The creamery sits within a large, bustling complex of restaurants, groceries, and gift shops that draws travellers heading to and from the west coast of Vancouver Island. The dog-friendly patio and extensive parking area—including a shaded lot suited to large vehicles—make it a natural mid-route stop.

restaurant.name: The Vicious Poodle
restaurant.desc: The Vicious Poodle is a bar and full-service restaurant on Johnson Street in the heart of downtown Victoria, serving both brunch and dinner menus alongside a lively weekly entertainment programme of drag shows and themed nights. The kitchen offers strong vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options alongside pub classics, making it a genuinely inclusive stop for hungry riders finishing a day's ride into the city. OSM confirms wheelchair accessibility at the venue.

restaurant.name: Delara
restaurant.desc: Delara is Chef Bardia Ilbeiggi's modern Persian restaurant on Vancouver's West 4th Avenue cycling corridor, named for a Persian word meaning 'beloved — she who brings beauty to hearts.' Dishes are designed for sharing family-style and range from kebabs and rice stews to date-walnut baklava and turmeric cake with saffron ice cream.

restaurant.name: Bartholomew

The majority of seating runs along a long bar, giving guests an up-close view of the bar and kitchen teams at work.

restaurant.name: 7th Taste

restaurant.name: Deer One Hotpot

The restaurant is located in a commercial complex with two hours of free indoor parking. It offers a warm sit-down experience suited for a longer meal stop on a cycling tour of the Richmond area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website soup menu explicitly lists 'Mixed Mushroom Soup (Vegan)' as an available soup base

restaurant.name: Oh Sweet Day! Bake Shop

Located on East 1st Avenue near the Commercial Drive cycling corridor, it can serve as a sweet-treat stop for cyclists passing through East Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Garden City Bakery

The Chilliwack location serves authentic Mexican street food — tacos, burritos, burrito bowls, and quesadillas — with traditional fillings like al pastor, carnitas, and carne asada. A dedicated social enterprise with operations in both Canada and Mexico, it offers a range of dietary-friendly options well suited to hungry touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Ki Tea House Cafe

restaurant.name: Lila Restaurant

Touring cyclists will find a genuine sit-down meal with broad dietary accommodation and online order-ahead for takeout.

restaurant.name: Commercial Street Cafe

Its unpretentious, welcoming character and proximity to Trout Lake make it a natural refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the area.

restaurant.name: ManTung Cafe

restaurant.name: Parachute
restaurant.desc: Parachute Ice Cream is a locally owned Victoria institution handcrafting small-batch ice cream from Vancouver Island ingredients, including house-made waffle cones and seasonal rotating flavours. The Bridge Street location is one of three scoop shops across greater Victoria, with pints also available at numerous independent grocers throughout the region. A touring cyclist will find a wide range of options including multiple vegan and gluten-friendly scoops, sorbets, and frozen yogurt.

restaurant.name: The Broughton Street Deli

restaurant.name: Phillips Tasting Room

The tasting room and adjacent beer shop together offer a full house selection in a family-friendly setting with an outdoor backyard event space. Phillips actively sponsors local cycling events and causes, making it a particularly fitting stop for bike tourists rolling through central Victoria.

restaurant.name: Chitos Chicken & Beer

Located in a commercial plaza on 88 Avenue, it offers dine-in and online ordering. A touring cyclist would find a substantial sit-down meal here after a ride in the Langley area.

restaurant.name: Cafe Calabria
restaurant.desc: Cafe Calabria is a long-standing Italian cafe on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, the street once known as 'Little Italy,' built around a custom espresso blend developed by founder Francesco Murdocco over 30 years ago. It has attracted a loyal multi-generational customer base and earned coverage in The Vancouver Sun, The Globe & Mail, Enroute, and numerous other publications. A touring cyclist will find a full espresso bar, Italian paninis, gelato, and warm indoor seating in one of Vancouver's most vibrant and walkable neighbourhoods.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast-food restaurant in Richmond, BC, located on Alderbridge Way with drive-through and indoor seating. Touring cyclists passing through the Richmond area will find it a convenient and predictable stop for a quick meal or snack.

restaurant.name: Poke by Ryuu

Situated within the busy UBC campus corridor, it offers a convenient food stop for cyclists exploring the university grounds or passing through on the Pacific Spirit Park routes. It is one of a handful of Neptune Group concepts at UBC, alongside a Chinese kitchen and wonton noodle bar.

restaurant.name: Greek On the Street
restaurant.desc: Greek On the Street is a family-owned Victoria operation that grew from a roving food truck into a permanent Greek eatery at 492 Bay Street. The menu centres on classic dishes like chicken souvlaki, lemon potatoes, and vegetarian plates, with the food truck still operating at markets and events around Victoria. The business also runs a full catering arm (Estia Gourmet) serving weddings, corporate events, and film sets across Vancouver Island.

The venue regularly hosts paint parties, live Celtic music, and other community events, creating a lively atmosphere unlike a typical cafe stop. Notably, the business accepts Bitcoin Lightning Network payments.

restaurant.name: Chic Chic Chicken

restaurant.name: My Chau Restaurant

Its location on Main Street — a heavily cycled corridor in Vancouver — places it squarely in the path of touring and commuter cyclists.

restaurant.name: HardDrive Cafe
restaurant.desc: The HardDrive Café is a full-service café and catering operation that has anchored the Vancouver Island Technology Park since the campus opened in 2002, operated by Geffen Gourmet Catering. It serves a diverse clientele of tech workers, researchers, conference-goers, and visitors from adjacent Camosun College, with a strong sustainability ethos encompassing fair-trade coffee, Island Farms dairy, local produce, and biodegradable to-go packaging. The café also caters private receptions, boardroom events, and major conferences held in the on-site VITP Conference Centre.

restaurant.name: Atrevida
restaurant.desc: Atrevida is a fine-dining oceanfront restaurant at the Galiano Oceanfront Inn & Spa on Galiano Island, a popular Gulf Islands cycling destination accessible by BC Ferries. Under Executive Chef Dean Hillier, the kitchen focuses on carefully sourced BC and Pacific Northwest ingredients presented in a contemporary West Coast style, with sweeping ocean views as a backdrop. The restaurant serves both inn guests and the general public, making it a noteworthy dining destination for cyclists touring the island.

Its corner location at West Cordova and Abbott, steps from Waterfront Station and both Rogers Arena and BC Place, makes it a practical and lively refuelling stop for cyclists riding through downtown Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Mango Mama

restaurant.name: Salt Spring Inn

As both an inn and a full-service restaurant, it offers a sit-down dining experience in one of BC's most popular cycling destinations. Touring cyclists riding the island's rural roads would find it a convenient stop for a full meal.

restaurant.name: Royal Garden

Now run by their daughter Susie, the restaurant serves North American Chinese cuisine from a spacious Anderson Way location with free parking and wheelchair accessibility. Dine-in, takeout, and buffet options make it a versatile stop for cyclists wanting a substantial sit-down meal in Vernon.

It is a distinctive, atmospheric stop for cyclists exploring downtown Victoria's nightlife.

restaurant.name: Swift Brewing & Good Time Tasting Room

The taproom pours house-crafted beers alongside cocktails and snacks in a retro-basement aesthetic, and operates a patio that welcomes pets. Canned beers are available to take away, making it a handy stop for cyclists passing through the harbour area.

restaurant.name: The Oaks Restaurant

Established under its current name in 2012, it blends family dining with a touch of tradition: all-day breakfast, traditional afternoon tea with homemade jams and made-from-scratch desserts, and weekly live music nights. A touring cyclist arriving in the historic Oak Bay village would find a welcoming community gathering spot serving everything from burgers and haddock and chips to full English-style afternoon tea.

restaurant.name: Hill's Bakery

restaurant.name: Sai Plant Deli

The brand highlights antibiotic-free meat, organic tomato sauce, and daily fresh dough, and explicitly carries vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-smart options. As a fast-food takeout operation, it provides a quick and accessible meal stop for cyclists passing through central Penticton.

restaurant.name: Tough City Sushi

The menu draws heavily on locally sourced Vancouver Island seafood — wild sockeye salmon, fresh-shucked oysters, local albacore tuna — presented as sashimi, nigiri, and a long list of specialty rolls alongside Japanese cooked dishes. Tofino is a popular endpoint for cycle tourists riding Vancouver Island's west coast, and this sit-down restaurant is a well-positioned stop in the heart of town.

restaurant.name: Chef Hung

The menu centres on pho, banh mi, rice dishes, and vermicelli bowls in a quick-service format with online pre-ordering to minimize wait times. The chain has been named best Vietnamese and best pho in Westender Magazine's 'Best of City' awards multiple times.

restaurant.name: McDonald's

The location has a drive-through and is part of the MyMcDonald's Rewards app program. As a well-known chain stop, it is a predictable resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the Richmond area.

restaurant.name: España Restaurant
restaurant.desc: España Restaurant is a Spanish tapas restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, offering an extensive menu of traditional and modern Spanish dishes ranging from patatas bravas and grilled Humboldt squid to daily paella and a substantial charcuterie and cheese board program. The restaurant carries a tightly curated all-Spanish wine list with options by the glass. Its location near the Stanley Park Seawall makes it a natural dinner destination for cyclists riding the West End corridor.

restaurant.name: Restaurant Kavita
restaurant.desc: Restaurant Kavita is an upscale Indian restaurant in Vancouver's Fairview neighbourhood, led by Chef Tushar Tondvalkar whose résumé spans Michelin-starred kitchens in Bangkok and respected Vancouver dining rooms including Blue Water Café and Bauhaus. The centrepiece is the Ammakase, a seasonal tasting menu that traces India's regional cuisines using locally sourced BC produce. Named Best Indian 2026 Gold, it is a deliberate destination-dining experience rooted in storytelling and traditional technique.

restaurant.name: The Curious Artistry & Alchemy Café
restaurant.desc: The Curious Café is a downtown Kelowna restaurant built around wood-fired Neapolitan-style pizza, casual comfort food, and craft cocktails in a relaxed, welcoming space. The café features a seasonal patio, a private speakeasy-style room seating up to 30 guests, and offsite catering — making it a flexible destination for solo riders and group cycling trips alike. Its central Ellis Street location in the heart of Kelowna places it within easy reach of the Okanagan Rail Trail and downtown waterfront cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Nicli Pizzeria + Bar
restaurant.desc: NICLI Antica Pizzeria at UBC's Wesbrook Village is a full-service Italian restaurant specializing in authentic Neapolitan pizza baked in wood/brick fired ovens imported directly from Naples, cooking each pizza at 900°F in 90 seconds. Open since 2004, it has earned local and international recognition as one of Vancouver's top pizzerias, with a full menu of pizza, pasta, antipasti, cocktails, and Italian wines. The UBC campus location in Wesbrook Village makes it a convenient dine-in or takeout stop for cyclists riding through the university area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'Many of our items can be modified to be gluten friendly and/or vegan. Please advise your server of any restrictions.' Front page also highlights 'Best Gluten Free Pizza' as a key feature

restaurant.name: Marble Slab Creamery
restaurant.desc: Marble Slab Creamery is a Canadian ice cream franchise that mixes custom flavours and toppings on a frozen granite slab in-store, with over 50 flavours including vegan options and handrolled waffle cones. The Fort St. John location sits along 96 Street and offers ice cream cakes and pre-packed take-home options in addition to fresh scoops. It's a handy sweet stop for cyclists moving through the Peace Region of northeastern BC.

detail.address: Unit 104 - 9317 96 Street, Fort St. John, BC V1J 6V5
