restaurant.name: Dose Espresso Bar
restaurant.desc: Dose Espresso Bar is a cafe located on West Broadway in Vancouver. It serves the local community and cyclists passing through the neighborhood.

restaurant.name: Mediterranean Donair House
restaurant.desc: Mediterranean Donair House is a takeout-focused fast food spot on Sixth Street in North Vancouver serving Greek and donair cuisine. With outdoor seating and no indoor dining, it offers an al fresco stop for cyclists passing through the area. The Greek-donair combination makes it a distinctive quick-eat option in the neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Maya's
restaurant.desc: Maya's is a seasonal ice cream and gelato shop on White Rock's scenic Marine Drive, right along a popular seaside cycling route. The shop was born from the owners' international travels and offers handcrafted gelato, creative soft serve sundaes, floats, paninis, and a full espresso bar. Online ordering is available for pint pickup and local delivery.

detail.address: 15045 Marine Drive, White Rock, BC V4B 1C3

restaurant.name: The Red Brick Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Red Brick Cafe is a cafe located in Sidney, BC, a community on the Saanich Peninsula that sits along popular cycling routes connecting to BC Ferries terminals and the broader Gulf Islands touring network. Beyond its OSM classification as a cafe, no details about its offerings, atmosphere, or cyclist amenities could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Living Forest Cafe
restaurant.desc: Living Forest Cafe is the in-house dining experience at Living Forest Oceanside Campground & RV Park, a 53-acre waterfront property on the Nanaimo River estuary. The cafe operates seasonally in summer and donates its profits to charity each year since opening over a decade ago. Touring cyclists will find it a relaxed stop within a scenic oceanside campground that also offers Wi-Fi on the cafe patio.

restaurant.name: LIX Cafe
restaurant.desc: LIX Cafe is an ice cream shop and cafe on Hornby Island with outdoor seating. It provides a refreshment stop for touring cyclists navigating the rural island.

restaurant.name: Sushi Yamato
restaurant.desc: Sushi Yamato is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, offering both dine-in and takeout service with delivery available through DoorDash. The restaurant accepts credit and debit cards and sits in a dense urban neighbourhood close to the Stanley Park Seawall and other popular cycling routes. An OSM check in April 2026 confirms it remains open.

restaurant.name: Continental Coffee
restaurant.desc: A family-run coffee institution that has been roasting beans for six generations, with its Vancouver flagship on Commercial Drive dating to 1979. The shop sources and roasts its own blends, sold in-café and by subscription, making it a neighbourhood anchor on one of Vancouver's most cycle-friendly streets. A second location operates on Main Street and a roasting plant operates in Burnaby.

restaurant.name: Little Pisces Taiyaki & Soft Serve
restaurant.desc: Little Pisces is a Japanese-inspired dessert shop specializing in taiyaki — crispy, chewy mochi-batter fish-shaped pastries available in rotating fillings — alongside seasonal soft serve flavors and specialty café drinks. The Richmond location opened in May 2025 as the brand's second outpost, following their original Lougheed store in Burnaby. Dairy-free and vegan options are clearly marked on the menu, with oat milk available for most drinks.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website FAQ states: 'Our dairy-free and vegan options are indicated on our menu. We usually have at least one vegan soft serve option. Most of our drinks can be made with oat milk upon request.'

restaurant.name: Bar Tartar
restaurant.desc: Bar Tartare is a natural wine bar in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood that rotates guest chefs through its kitchen, offering a dining experience that shifts with each chef's creative vision. The intimate venue at 54 Alexander Street pairs its evolving food program with a curated list of natural wines. Touring cyclists exploring Gastown will find it a distinctive option for an evening meal in one of Vancouver's most storied districts.

restaurant.name: Pizza Heaven
restaurant.desc: Pizza Heaven is the New Westminster outpost of the Vancouver Pizza Heaven chain, located near the Fraser River and, according to at least one customer review, situated inside a bar. The kitchen emphasizes fresh, locally sourced ingredients, house-made dough, and a signature pan crust, with a broad menu that covers classic, vegan, gluten-free, and fusion styles. The location also offers catering for events.

notes.Takeout: Offers page explicitly lists 'dine-in, takeout, and delivery orders'; some deals are marked 'PICKUP ONLY'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website front page explicitly lists 'Gluten-free • Cauliflower • Vegan • Fusion • Classic — Something for every taste and every diet.'

restaurant.name: Heritage Asian Eatery
restaurant.desc: Heritage Asian Eatery's Lonsdale Quay outpost is a quick-serve counter-service spot in North Vancouver's busy waterfront public market, part of a small BC multi-location chain. The menu celebrates classic Chinese comfort food — fried rice, chow mein, orange chicken, sweet and sour pork, and an in-house BBQ case offering char siu, roast duck, soy chicken, and roast pork alongside handcrafted dim sum. Its location inside Lonsdale Quay Market places it steps from the SeaBus terminal and the North Shore waterfront cycling routes.

detail.address: 123 Carrie Cates Court, North Vancouver, BC

restaurant.name: Dock's Fish & Chips
restaurant.desc: Dock's Fish & Chips is a fast-food fish-and-chips spot situated on White Rock's Marine Drive, the scenic waterfront road that draws cyclists from across the Lower Mainland and beyond. The location on Marine Drive places it directly along one of BC's most popular recreational cycling routes, with the White Rock Pier and beach just steps away. It would serve as a natural rest and refuel stop for riders completing the South Surrey–White Rock coastal loop.

restaurant.name: Big Star Sandwich Co.
restaurant.desc: Big Star Sandwich Co. is a Lower Mainland sandwich chain founded in 2013, now operating six locations across the region. The Burnaby shop on Canada Way specialises in hearty, made-to-order sandwiches built on a fresh rustic Filone roll with house slow-roasted beef, hand-pulled turkey, and other in-house cooked meats. Catering is available, and an online ordering option makes it a convenient refuelling stop on a longer ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: GF not mentioned on website

restaurant.name: Tocador

The associated website domain has been repurposed as an unrelated Chinese movie streaming site, making current operating status difficult to confirm.

restaurant.name: Hometown Pizza
restaurant.desc: Hometown Pizza is a neighbourhood pizza and fast-food restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver's south end, offering a broad menu spanning pizzas, baked pastas, fish and chips, pakora, wings, and fries. The shop operates primarily as a call-ahead takeout and delivery spot with three phone lines. It sits along a well-travelled south Vancouver cycling corridor and makes a practical hot-meal stop for riders heading toward the river or the airport greenway.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Vegetarian / Meat Sauce' as an option for lasagna, spaghetti, and ravioli dishes

restaurant.name: Tairyou ichiba

restaurant.name: Sawmill TapHouse & Grill
restaurant.desc: Sawmill TapHouse and Grill has been a Chemainus dining staple since 2017, celebrated for its forno oven pizzas, slow-cooked smoked meats, and rotating Pacific Northwest craft beer taps. Described by Traveler's Island as 'really nothing quite like it in the Cowichan Valley,' the restaurant blends an urban vibe with local Chemainus history in a family-friendly atmosphere. The kitchen accommodates a range of dietary needs and offers on-site takeout, making it a practical stop for cyclists passing through.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options are all available.'

restaurant.name: Kuro Sushi & Bar

restaurant.name: Pizzability Glenlake

The Langford location sits beside Bucky's Taphouse at the Glen Lake Inn on Sooke Road, serving the Westshore corridor. The menu spans classic and gourmet pizzas, pastas, wings, garlic ribs, and sides available for pickup or local delivery.

restaurant.name: Bubble World

restaurant.name: Water Street Cafe

It serves classic Italian cuisine with West Coast influence, an award-winning BC-focused wine list, and hosts nightly live music through its 2nd Floor Gastown venue. The restaurant is locally owned and independent, offering brunch, lunch, happy hour, and dinner in a relaxed heritage setting.

restaurant.name: Xing Fu Tang

This Burnaby location on Dawson Street is operated by Luscioussip Teahouse Ltd and offers both indoor and outdoor seating alongside takeaway and delivery service. A touring cyclist can stop for a cold drink, use the on-site washrooms, and pay by cash or card.

restaurant.name: The Rebel Garage
restaurant.desc: The Rebel Garage is a coffee bar, culture space, and arts venue in Victoria's Burnside neighbourhood, serving Discovery Coffee, Saltchuck Pies, and fresh treats by day. By night it transforms into a live music, comedy, and arts event space, and maintains a standing open jam policy with house instruments available for spontaneous sessions. It shares the Rebel Company complex at 1 Burnside Road West with Rebel Ink tattoo studio.

restaurant.name: Pho Khang

restaurant.name: La Dulceria Sweets & Treats

restaurant.name: LA Grill and Bistro

Grill is a casual, sports-bar-style restaurant in Richmond, BC with over two decades of experience, offering a wide variety of comfort food including burgers, pastas, seafood, and salads in generous portions. Touring cyclists would find a large, varied menu at everyday-friendly prices in a sit-down setting.

restaurant.name: DooBoo

restaurant.name: Hail Mary's
restaurant.desc: Hail Mary's is a small, irreverent local bar and restaurant on East Broadway in East Vancouver, offering creative cocktails with names like 'Exorcism' and 'The Resurrection' alongside a snack-forward food menu including house-made potato chips, Jamaican jerk chicken patties, and double-baked nachos. The spot runs strictly first-come, first-served with no reservations, keeping things unpretentious and drop-in friendly. Vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options are woven throughout the menu.

restaurant.name: The Society
restaurant.desc: Society at the Hall in Maple Bay is a multi-concept venue combining a full-service barbershop with a coffee cafe (NOTACAFE) and a tequila-and-local-beer bar (NOTABAR), all under the family-owned NOTACULT LLC umbrella. The bar serves daily baked goods and savory pies alongside a curated selection of tequilas and local craft beers from breweries like Red Arrow, Deadhead, Hoyne, and Driftwood. It is one of several locations operated by founders Ian and Rhiannon, with the head office and main barbershop in downtown Duncan.

restaurant.name: Hashtag Donair
restaurant.desc: Hashtag Donair is a local multi-location chain specializing in donairs, gyros, and Middle Eastern-inspired wraps and platters, with this outlet situated inside the Willoughby Town Centre shopping area in Langley. The menu ranges from classic beef, lamb, and chicken donairs to rice platters, loaded poutines, and a keto bowl, with multiple vegetarian options clearly flagged. The kitchen also handles catering and group orders, making it a practical high-protein fueling stop for solo riders and cycling groups alike.

detail.address: 20689 Willoughby Town Centre Drive, Langley, BC V2Y 0X7

restaurant.name: Meat & Bread

The restaurant offers breakfast sandwiches, salads, soups, and its namesake hot sandwiches with both indoor and outdoor seating. A catering and group-orders option adds practical appeal for organized cycling groups moving through the urban core.

restaurant.name: Cartems Donuts

restaurant.name: Velo Star Cafe
restaurant.desc: Velo Star Cafe is a cycling-themed cafe in Vancouver serving sandwiches and coffee with outdoor seating. The name suggests a strong cycling connection, making it a natural gathering spot for cycling enthusiasts. A convenient stop for food and refreshment on local cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Isetta Cafe Bistro
restaurant.desc: Isetta is a beautifully renovated 1962 mid-century modern building on Marine Drive, perched between Howe Sound and the North Shore mountains in West Vancouver. Reopened in 2022 as a destination cafe bistro, it takes its name from the iconic Isetta micro-car, a 1950s Italian-German collaboration. The contact page explicitly calls out Marine Drive as 'a beautiful bicycle ride' and lists Lighthouse Park, Cypress Mountain, and Whytecliff Park as nearby attractions, making it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu uses (V) vegetarian, (VF) vegan-friendly, and (GS) gluten-sensitive tags across multiple items including Avocado Toast, Caponata & Grits, Field Greens, and Truffle Fries

restaurant.name: 88 Malaysian Crystal BBQ Pork & Food
restaurant.desc: A Malaysian-Chinese fast-food stall specializing in crystal BBQ pork (char siu style), situated in a food-court unit in Richmond. The name points to a focused menu of barbecue pork and related dishes typical of Malaysian hawker-stall cooking. Richmond's dense concentration of authentic Asian eateries makes this a convenient fuel stop for cyclists passing through the city's commercial core.

restaurant.name: Lou's Grill
restaurant.desc: Lou's Grill is a bar and grill established in 1991 and voted Fraser Valley's Favourite Bar & Grill, with the top-rated burger joint distinction from Zomato. The restaurant features a heated smoking patio, a fireplace, and a full cocktail and craft beer menu alongside its food program. It operates as a late-night venue with delivery via Skip the Dishes and in-house takeout available seven days a week.

restaurant.name: Miu Japanese Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Miu Japanese Cuisine is a contemporary fusion restaurant in Port Coquitlam offering a creative East-meets-West take on Japanese cooking, with specialties including aburi oshi sushi, sushi pizza, and bento sets. The restaurant describes its philosophy as a respectful yet imaginative reinterpretation of traditional Japanese flavors incorporating West Coast influences. It caters to a wide range of occasions, from solo meals to group gatherings.

detail.address: 2540 Mary Hill Rd. #103, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 3B2

restaurant.name: Fantacity Karaoke
restaurant.desc: Fantacity Karaoke is an Asian restaurant with karaoke on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver, one of the city's busiest pedestrian and cycling corridors. The venue offers indoor dining and private karaoke rooms, making it an evening dining-and-entertainment destination rather than a quick cyclist fuel stop. Its Robson Street location places it near the downtown bike network.

restaurant.name: Royal Canadian Legion - Branch 2 (New Westminster)
restaurant.desc: Royal Canadian Legion Branch 2 is a veterans' social club and pub on Sixth Street in New Westminster, part of the BC/Yukon Command's network of over 145 branches across British Columbia and the Yukon. Founded by and for veterans, the Legion supports current and former Canadian Armed Forces and RCMP members and their families through community gathering space and veteran advocacy services. The venue is non-smoking and features both indoor and outdoor seating.

restaurant.name: Ryuu Izakaya
restaurant.desc: Ryuu Izakaya, marketed on its own website as Ryuu Japanese Kitchen, is a Japanese restaurant operated by Neptune Group in Richmond's YVR outlet retail area near the airport. It is part of a well-established Greater Vancouver multi-brand restaurant group and serves Japanese cuisine including food party trays. Cyclists exploring the Richmond dyke routes or the Sea Island area would find this a convenient sit-down or takeout stop in a commercial hub just off the cycling network.

restaurant.name: Craft Cafe
restaurant.desc: Craft Cafe is a neighbourhood cafe and cocktail bar on Quayside Drive along the New Westminster waterfront of the Fraser River. It serves single-origin espresso from The Barn, a Berlin roastery recognized internationally for specialty coffee, alongside food including grilled cheese sandwiches and pasta. A hidden backroom speakeasy—The Back Room—offers craft cocktails and riverfront views in an adults-only lounge tucked behind the main cafe.

detail.address: 960 Quayside Dr Unit 115, New Westminster, BC V3M 6G2

restaurant.name: Sharetea
restaurant.desc: Sharetea is a Taiwanese bubble tea chain founded in 1992, now operating over 400 stores worldwide, including this Coquitlam location. The menu spans classic milk teas, fruit teas, matcha, and ice-blended drinks, all made to order with ingredients sourced from Taiwan. Cyclists looking for a cold, customizable drink stop in Coquitlam will find a wide range of caffeinated and non-caffeinated options.

restaurant.name: Sundays Coffee and Provisions
restaurant.desc: Sundays Coffee Bar + Provisions is a community-oriented café on Somenos Road in Duncan, BC, formerly operating as the Guild Coffee & Lifestyle Boutique. The owner describes it as a gathering space built around excellent coffee and shared connection — a deliberate 'Sunday kind of vibe' rather than a transactional stop. The café also sells provisions, giving touring cyclists a potential combined opportunity to refuel and resupply.

restaurant.name: Blue Fox Cafe
restaurant.desc: Blue Fox Cafe has been Victoria's go-to all-day breakfast spot since 1991, claiming the title of the city's first and foremost all-day breakfast restaurant. Located on Fort Street in the downtown core, it serves a broad menu of egg dishes, griddle cakes, and specialty items leaning on local and organic ingredients. Cyclists can sit down for a substantial fuel-up or grab takeout before hitting the road.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu confirms vegetarian options (Veggie Migas, black bean dishes, organic tofu substitutes) and gluten-free toast available as a substitute

restaurant.name: Masayoshi
restaurant.desc: Masayoshi is a Michelin-starred, 24-seat omakase sushi restaurant in Vancouver's Fraserhood neighbourhood, led by Chef Masayoshi Baba who trained in Japan before spending a decade at Tojo's. The experience is hyper-seasonal and fully bespoke, with guests seated at a sushi bar or dining tables for an approximately 20-course progression of appetizers and nigiri. Reservations are mandatory and must be secured through Tock with a credit card.

restaurant.name: Red Cedar Cafe
restaurant.desc: Red Cedar Café is a registered non-profit community meal program founded in April 2020 in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, operating out of a commercial kitchen at 1900 Douglas Street in Victoria. It prepares around 1,000 free or pay-what-you-can frozen meals weekly — vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options included — and runs a Free Store distributing produce, bread, and groceries from the same location. A touring cyclist in need of accessible food support will find a welcoming, volunteer-run operation rooted in mutual aid principles.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We provide vegetarian, vegan, and gluten free options where possible' and 'Our weekly menus offer meat-based, vegetarian, gluten-free and vegan options.'

restaurant.name: Kokoro Ramen
restaurant.desc: Kokoro Ramen is a craft Japanese ramen restaurant in East Vancouver, founded in 2016 by a team of culinary professionals with formal ramen and udon school training in Japan. The restaurant emphasizes authentic, health-conscious ramen made from fresh ingredients, and has expanded into retail with frozen ramen kits sold at grocery stores across the Lower Mainland. Both dine-in and takeout are available, making it a sit-down or grab-and-go option for cyclists on Victoria Drive.

restaurant.name: Sushi Han
restaurant.desc: Sushi Han is a Japanese restaurant tucked into Blundell Centre in Richmond, offering an extensive menu that spans aburi oshi, sashimi, nigiri, specialty rolls, ramen, robata BBQ, and bento boxes. The breadth of the menu — from casual rolls to full donburi and hot dishes — makes it a satisfying option for touring cyclists wanting a substantial sit-down or takeout Japanese meal in south Richmond.
