restaurant.name: La foret
restaurant.desc: La Forêt is a cafe and bakery chain with roots going back to 2013, with the Jubilee location created in 2017 by transforming a former auto body shop into what became one of the Lower Mainland's largest cafes. The menu spans espresso drinks, specialty matcha and signature lattes, full brunch platters, waffles, croissants, and custom cakes available for pre-order. It's a spacious, community-oriented stop with indoor seating, air conditioning, and accessible washrooms — well-suited for a mid-ride break.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Avocado Platter and multiple plant-based drink options, confirming vegetarian-friendly offerings. Vegan and GF status not explicitly stated on website

restaurant.name: Copper Mug
restaurant.desc: The Copper Mug claims to be the oldest pub in Penticton and the second oldest in British Columbia, having operated since 1974. Located in the Safeway Plaza on Main Street, it serves a full food menu alongside daily chef's specials and house-made soups. A lively weekly events calendar — including Friday music trivia, Thursday wing nights, and Sunday brunch — makes it a neighbourhood anchor in a town that sits on popular cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Perk And Puff Cafe
restaurant.desc: Perk & Puff Cafè is a hookah lounge and café serving specialty tea, baklava, and flavoured hookah in a relaxed social atmosphere. The venue has two floors with TV screens and comfortable seating, and reviewers highlight attentive owner-operated service. It is a sit-down establishment catering to groups, making it a rest stop option for cyclists looking for a social break rather than a quick bite.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: McDonald's at Davie & Cardero is a 24/7 fast food location in Vancouver's West End, operating without a drive-through in a walkable, pedestrian-dense neighbourhood. The branch offers a full menu including breakfast, McCafé beverages, and takeaway service from a street-level unit with indoor seating. For touring cyclists moving through central Vancouver at any hour, it functions as a reliable food resupply stop.

restaurant.name: Anton's Pasta Bar
restaurant.desc: Anton's Pasta Bar is a Burnaby institution founded in 1983 by Calabrian immigrant Tony Mauro and widely credited as Vancouver's original pasta bar. The restaurant offers over 70 fresh pasta creations in famously generous portions, served in a warm, no-reservations neighbourhood setting that has built a loyal following across Greater Vancouver for more than 25 years. Touring cyclists will find it a reliable carb-loading stop on East Hastings, with a broad menu spanning red sauces, seafood pastas, vegetarian dishes, and risottos.

detail.address: 4260 East Hastings Street, Burnaby, BC V5C 2J6

notes.Takeout: Website contact page references takeout orders and a catering fee for orders over $200
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dinner menu includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian' section with multiple pasta dishes

restaurant.name: Mr. Sushi
restaurant.desc: Mr. Sushi Lynn Valley is a family-owned Japanese sushi restaurant that has anchored the Lynn Valley neighbourhood since 1992, growing from a 500-square-foot space into a three-location North Vancouver institution. A North Shore News Readers' Choice Award winner, the restaurant is known for personalized service — staff pride themselves on remembering regulars' names and favourite orders. Touring cyclists rolling through Lynn Valley will find a full sit-down sushi experience as well as convenient online pickup ordering.

detail.address: 1250A Lynn Valley Road, North Vancouver, BC V7J 2A3

restaurant.name: Indian Burgers Joint
restaurant.desc: Indian Burger Joint is a 100% vegetarian and vegan fast-casual chain founded in 2023 by Navneet Bhadu, serving Indian-spiced fusion burgers, grilled sandwiches, naan-wiches, tacos, and Indian street food across five BC locations. The White Rock outpost on Marine Drive offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery, with a menu rooted in traditional Indian flavors rather than meat imitation. Culturally immersive décor, Indian-themed murals, and a broad beverage selection including masala chai, falooda, and Indian refreshers make it a distinctive stop for cyclists seeking a fully plant-based meal.

detail.address: 15527 Marine Dr, White Rock, BC V4B 1C7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states '100% Vegetarian burgers' and 'All vegan and vegetarian options'; OSM confirms and. No gluten-free claim found

restaurant.name: Grandt Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Grandt Kitchen is an authentic Filipino restaurant in Surrey, BC, serving traditional dishes like pork sisig, halo-halo, dinuguan, and squid BBQ using time-honored recipes passed down through generations. Located on King George Boulevard, it offers both dine-in and online ordering for pickup or delivery, and has its own mobile app.

detail.address: 10257 King George Blvd, Surrey, BC V3T 2W6

restaurant.name: Crepe Delicious
restaurant.desc: Crepe Delicious is a Canadian franchise concept founded in 2004, serving made-to-order sweet and savory crepes alongside handcrafted gelato available in over 100 flavors. The Tsawwassen location at 5000 Canoe Pass Way sits near Canoe Pass, offering cyclists a quick yet distinctive stop for fresh, customizable crepes ranging from Nutella-filled sweet options to heartier savory varieties with chicken, steak, or egg. The brand positions itself as an upscale alternative to traditional fast food, blending European crepe tradition with counter-service convenience.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian options: Feta Tomato (tomato, feta, balsamic glaze, evoo), Popeye (spinach, mushroom, mozzarella, feta), Romeo & Juliet (sugar, butter), and numerous sweet crepes. About page states 'we proudly offer options that cater to various dietary preferences.' Vegan and GF not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: Pizza Garden
restaurant.desc: Pizza Garden is a BC-based Neapolitan pizza chain operated by Neapolitan Pizza Ltd., with over 25 years in the pizza industry and locations across the Lower Mainland and beyond. The Metrotown location serves wood-fired pizzas with authentic charred crusts, classic Italian toppings, and outdoor seating — a reasonable stop for a cyclist coming through Burnaby's commercial core. Pickup, delivery, and a mobile rewards app are all available.

restaurant.name: Zapoteca Mexican Grill & Seafood
restaurant.desc: Zapoteca is an authentic Mexican restaurant on White Rock's Marine Drive waterfront, opened on Valentine's Day 2018 by a trio of founders with roots in Guadalajara, Guanajuato, and Nelson, BC. Its beloved sidewalk patio has been a fixture of the beachside community for over six years, blending Oaxacan-influenced dishes with local seafood in a lively outdoor setting. Now with a second location in Kitsilano, it remains a cornerstone of White Rock's dining scene.

notes.Takeout: Dedicated 'Take-out' section in site navigation; website states 'Please make reservations and takeout orders by website only.'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Happy-hour menu lists 'champiñones V' and 'vegan chilorio V'; contact FAQ notes many menu items are gluten-free and have been enjoyed by celiac guests, though cross-contamination risk is acknowledged

restaurant.name: John 3:16 Malaysian Delights
restaurant.desc: Founded in 2014, John 3:16 Malaysian Delights is Richmond's original and most prominent Malaysian restaurant, serving authentic dishes such as Beef Rendang, Nasi Lemak, Hainanese Chicken, and Roti Canai prepared from freshly sourced ingredients. The restaurant has since grown to four Lower Mainland locations — Richmond, Vancouver, Aberdeen, and Burnaby — with online ordering available at all dine-in branches. Cyclists stopping along the Number 3 Road corridor will find a full sit-down Malaysian dining experience as well as takeout options.

restaurant.name: Sazón Mexican Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Sazón is a traditional Mexican restaurant in the heart of Kitsilano, just a short walk from Kits Beach on the popular West 4th Avenue cycling corridor. Dishes are prepared by cooks from Mexico using recipes passed down through generations, with ingredients imported from Mexico when needed. The restaurant offers a warm family atmosphere with both dine-in and online ordering for pickup and delivery.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu filter includes explicit Vegetarian and Vegan categories; 'Gluten free option' noted in menu information block; plant-based entree options include Butternut Squash & Mushroom taco and Chile Poblano & Potato empanada and tamal

restaurant.name: Domino's
restaurant.desc: Domino's is a large international pizza chain franchise on Shelbourne Street in Victoria, offering delivery and carryout pizza, cheesy bread, chicken, and desserts. It is a standard suburban chain outlet with no distinct character or cyclist-focused amenities. Touring cyclists could use it as a calorie stop, but it offers little beyond food.

restaurant.name: The Village Burgery
restaurant.desc: The Village Burgery is a burger-focused fast food spot situated in Steveston, the historic fishing village at the southwestern tip of Richmond that draws visitors year-round. Steveston's waterfront and dyke trail system make it a popular destination on regional cycling routes, and a quick-service burger stop near the harbour is a natural refuelling point. The business was OSM-verified as of mid-2024.

restaurant.name: Little Caesars
restaurant.desc: Little Caesars is a large North American pizza chain that has operated in Canada since 1969, known for its value-priced ready-to-go pizzas available for immediate carryout. This Richmond location on Blundell Road is a takeout-focused spot with no drive-through, offering both in-store pickup and delivery. It is a straightforward option for a quick, filling pizza stop on a cycling route through the area.

restaurant.name: Neptune BBQ House
restaurant.desc: Neptune Barbecue House is a Cantonese restaurant on Granville Street in Vancouver, part of the multi-location Neptune Group established in 1997. The restaurant is well-known for its BBQ Pork, Roast Duck, and Party Tray Combos, and bills itself as one of the top Chinese restaurants in Greater Vancouver. Cyclists can order takeout directly through the website or via major delivery apps including DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Skip TheDishes.

restaurant.name: Protein Go Smoothie Bar Food and Drinks
restaurant.desc: Protein Go Smoothie Bar Food and Drinks is a juice and smoothie quick-service bar located in a unit at 5668 Hollybridge Way in Richmond. Geared toward grab-and-go customers, it sits in a multi-unit commercial building and would offer a refreshment stop for cyclists navigating the Richmond area. The specific menu and in-store experience cannot be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Haida Sandwich
restaurant.desc: Haida Sandwich is a halal-certified sandwich and pizza chain with a North Vancouver location serving massive subs, oven-roasted hot sandwiches, and fully loaded pizzas. The restaurant has been serving the halal community for over eight years with large portions and a broad menu spanning cold-cut and grilled options. Catering for corporate and private events is also available, making it a useful fuel stop for cyclists wanting a substantial, customizable meal.

detail.address: 121 15th St E, North Vancouver, BC V7L 2P7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian Pizza explicitly listed on the menu (mozzarella, green pepper, olive, mushroom, tomato, corn, potato sticks, tomato sauce); no vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: White Spot
restaurant.desc: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, founded in 1928 and widely regarded as one of BC's most beloved brands. The Coquitlam Sunwood Square location is a full-service family restaurant serving burgers made with 100% fresh Canadian beef and locally sourced BC ingredients, with a patio and a full range of dine-in, takeout, and delivery options. It offers a reliable, familiar stop for touring cyclists looking for a substantial sit-down or takeout meal along the Lougheed Highway corridor.

restaurant.name: Tina Cake Desserts
restaurant.desc: Tina Cake Desserts is a Vietnamese dessert and food café on Kingsway in East Vancouver, billing itself as the number one Vietnamese desserts and foods spot in the city. The shop specializes in traditional Vietnamese cuisine alongside fresh fruit desserts and ice cream. It sits on a busy arterial corridor with regular cycling traffic between central Vancouver and Burnaby.

restaurant.name: Bayside Lounge
restaurant.desc: Bayside Lounge is a retro cocktail lounge on the second floor above the corner of Denman and Davie Streets in Vancouver's West End, offering sweeping panoramic views of English Bay. Established in the 1970s and anchored by its iconic sunken circular bar, it serves West Coast-inspired small plates, handcrafted cocktails, and weekend brunch alongside nightly DJ sets. Cyclists riding the nearby Seawall will find it a scenic and lively stop steps from the beach.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels multiple items: Vegetarian Spring Rolls (vegan, vegetarian, dairy-free), Elote Corn (vegetarian, GF), Beyond Burger (vegan, vegetarian, dairy-free), Honey Roasted Carrots (GF, vegetarian), Tuna Kinilaw (dairy-free, GF), and others

restaurant.name: Uncle Fatih's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Uncle Fatih's Pizza is a popular Vancouver-based pizza chain with this Downtown location on Nelson Street, known for fresh dough made daily and never-frozen ingredients. The menu leans heavily on vegetables and offers extensive customization including vegan cheese, gluten-free crust, and halal chicken options. With outdoor seating and online ordering for pickup or delivery, it's a practical and filling stop for cyclists moving through downtown Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website catering FAQ: 'Do you offer vegan cheese? Yes - We use Daiya Cheese.' and 'Do you offer gluten free options? Yes - We use OGGI brand gluten free crust.' Dedicated Veggie Pizzas section on menu

restaurant.name: Caffè Mira
restaurant.desc: Caffè Mira is a Vancouver neighbourhood coffee shop that opened its first location in 2017 and has since grown to three locations across the city and New Westminster. The Main Street location sits on one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors and offers dine-in or takeout with a menu of beverages, sandwiches, and pastries. Catering and third-party delivery (DoorDash, Uber Eats, SkipTheDishes) are also available.

restaurant.name: The Charlatan
restaurant.desc: The Charlatan is a well-established gastro-pub at the corner of Commercial Drive and Grant, in the heart of one of Vancouver's most eclectic and cycling-friendly neighbourhoods. It occupies multiple levels including a south-facing, willow-fringed patio, an upper bar with 21 draught lines (heavily weighted toward BC craft breweries), a lounge, and a private downstairs den. The broad menu spans share plates, mussels, bowls, and brunch, making it a solid stop for a full meal at any time of day.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Kitchen menu explicitly labels items Ve (Vegetarian), Vg (Vegan), and Gf (Gluten Free) throughout share plates, bowls, and happy hour specials — e.g. Crispy Tofu Bites (Vg|Gf), Edamame (Ve|Vg|Gf), Chili Crisp Green Beans (Vg|Gf), Chilled Sesame Noodle Bowl (Ve|Gf)

restaurant.name: Earnest Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Earnest Ice Cream is a values-driven Vancouver ice cream company founded in 2012, crafting small-batch scoops from local and seasonal ingredients across four city locations including this Fraser Street shop. They run a jar-return zero-waste program and rotate monthly flavours, including a selection of dairy-free vegan options made from coconut, oat, and house-made nut milks. The outdoor seating and community-facing ethos make it a welcoming stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Street corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website FAQs confirm rotating vegan flavours (dairy, egg, and honey free) made with coconut, oat, and nut milk bases. Explicitly not a gluten-free facility

restaurant.name: Banh Mi Bar
restaurant.desc: Banh Mi Bar is a Vietnamese restaurant on Carnarvon Street in downtown New Westminster, serving banh mi and related fare in a smoke-free, indoor-seating setting. It caters to vegetarians, making it a useful stop for plant-based touring cyclists passing through the Royal City. New Westminster's compact downtown is a natural rest point for riders on the Central Valley Greenway or connecting routes along the Fraser River.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Unconfirmable via website due to Facebook block

restaurant.name: Dos Bros Fresh Mexican Grill
restaurant.desc: Dos Bros is a fast-casual Mexican grill in Abbotsford serving burritos, bowls, tacos, quesadillas, nachos, and salads built from locally sourced ingredients with scratch-made daily sauces. The chain distinguishes itself with biodegradable packaging, a wide range of dietary accommodations including vegan and gluten-free options, and catering services. A solid calorie-replenishment stop for cyclists passing through the Abbotsford corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page states 'vegan, vegetarian and gluten free options'; menu page labels items with GF, VEGETARIAN, and VEGAN icons; includes organic spicy tofu and dedicated veggie protein option

restaurant.name: Karma Indian Bistro
restaurant.desc: Karma Indian Bistro is a locally loved sit-down restaurant in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood serving authentic Indian cuisine with a modern twist — from tandoori specialties to rich curries and vegetarian dishes. The restaurant is listed on the Michelin Guide and has a heated outdoor patio for al fresco dining. Located on West 4th Avenue, a popular cycling corridor connecting central Vancouver to the waterfront.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items labeled 'Gluten-free' and 'Dairy-free' (e.g. Vegetable Pakora, Aloo Gobi, Butter Chicken). Website and reviews explicitly mention vegetarian options and a vegetarian appetizer platter

restaurant.name: Yuji's from Japan
restaurant.desc: Yuji's from Japan is a small, chef-driven Japanese restaurant in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, where owner-chef Yuji trained under the traditional Japanese apprenticeship system in Yokohama before bringing his skills to BC. The menu centres on fresh sushi and sashimi made with fish imported directly from Japan, alongside traditional Japanese dishes. A premium Omakase experience is available with three days' advance notice.

restaurant.name: GOGO Sushi
restaurant.desc: GOGO Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Lake Country's Oceola Road commercial area serving sushi, sashimi, teriyaki, noodles, donburi, and a range of specialty rolls. The kitchen makes its sauces — including teriyaki and ponzu — in-house, and the menu features clearly labelled vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options alongside lunch specials. Both dine-in and takeout are available, making it a convenient stop on a ride through the Lake Country corridor.

detail.address: 504-11850 Oceola Road, Lake Country, BC V4V 2T5

notes.Takeout: Homepage states 'Come dine in or take out'; contact page specifies 'Take-out last call is 8:15 pm'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page explicitly labels multiple items as Gluten Free, Vegetarian, and Vegan (e.g., Edamame, Seaweed Salad, Vegetable Gyoza, Brown Rice, Miso Soup)

restaurant.name: Donair Town
restaurant.desc: Donair Town is a family-run Lebanese fast-food restaurant that has been serving the Greater Vancouver area since 1993, specializing in chicken, beef, and lamb donairs alongside plates and Middle Eastern appetizers like falafel, hummus, and tzatziki. It operates four Lower Mainland locations, with the Clarke Road unit in Coquitlam being one of the original outposts. A touring cyclist passing through Coquitlam would find a filling, protein-rich meal with online and phone ordering available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists falafel, hummus and pita, tzatziki and pita, and donair salads — multiple vegetarian-suitable items

restaurant.name: The Train Station Pub
restaurant.desc: The Train Station Pub occupies Kelowna's historic 1926 CN railway station, one of the few remaining heritage station buildings in the BC Interior still in active daily use. Part of the Station Hospitality Group, it serves food, local beer, wine, and craft cocktails in a characterful setting that doubles as a community gathering spot. Touring cyclists rolling into downtown Kelowna will find a full-service pub with an early-day menu starting at 9 am.

restaurant.name: Chameleon
restaurant.desc: Chameleon is a sit-down restaurant in Maple Ridge offering lunch, brunch, happy hour, and dinner menus with an emphasis on fresh, local ingredients. The restaurant features a second-floor private dining room with AV equipment and can accommodate full buyouts for up to 75 guests, making it a versatile venue for both casual meals and special events. Touring cyclists will find a full-service dine-in option with an extensive wine, craft cocktail, and mocktail list in the heart of Maple Ridge.

restaurant.name: Red Robin
restaurant.desc: A Red Robin Gourmet Burgers and Brews location offering casual burger-focused dining and a full bar. As part of a major North American chain, this Vancouver location provides reliable full-service dining for touring cyclists seeking a sit-down meal in the city.

restaurant.name: Fatburger
restaurant.desc: Fatburger Ladner is a casual burger restaurant that cooks every meal to order using fresh-never-frozen Alberta Angus beef, with a menu spanning burgers, chicken tenders, veggie options, hand-scooped milkshakes, and house-made onion rings. Part of the Fatburger Canada chain (proudly Canadian-owned since 2005), this location offers both dine-in and takeout with no drive-through. A touring cyclist stopping in the Delta–Ladner area would find a reliable hot meal with vegetarian choices available.

detail.address: 5239 Ladner Trunk Road, Delta, BC V4K 1W4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'veggie burgers & sandwiches'

restaurant.name: Sushi Hanabi
restaurant.desc: Sushi Hanabi serves Japanese sushi cuisine in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighborhood. The restaurant offers dine-in and takeout service, with online ordering available for convenient meal options.

restaurant.name: And Drinks
restaurant.desc: And Drinks is a bubble tea cafe tucked inside a commercial complex at 3700 Number 3 Road in Richmond. Specializing in beverages in the style of contemporary Asian-influenced drink shops, it sits at ground level within a larger retail environment. For cyclists riding through Richmond's central corridor, it offers a convenient stop for a cold or hot drink.

restaurant.name: Baoguette Vietnamese Bistro
restaurant.desc: Baoguette Vietnamese Bistro is a sit-down Vietnamese restaurant in Richmond offering authentic dishes including bánh mì, pho, spring rolls, and noodle soups prepared with traditional flavours. The Richmond location is one of two Metro Vancouver outposts, with online ordering available. A touring cyclist passing through Richmond's busy No. 3 Road corridor could stop here for a filling bowl of pho or a banh mi to go.

notes.Takeout: Menu page states 'Only large size for take out,' confirming takeout orders are accepted; online ordering also available via website

restaurant.name: Once More Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Once More Restaurant is listed in OpenStreetMap as a restaurant at 8231 Ackroyd Road in Richmond, BC. Beyond its name and location, no website content is available to characterize the cuisine, setting, or offerings, as the business's domain has expired and is currently parked.

restaurant.name: Vedder Sushi
restaurant.desc: Vedder Sushi is a Japanese and Asian fusion sushi restaurant in Sardis/Chilliwack, operated by a chef with 40 years of experience. The menu features an extensive list of specialty rolls alongside sashimi and other Japanese fare, all made with fresh ingredients and no MSG. Online ordering and takeout are available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Freshly Squeezed
restaurant.desc: Freshly Squeezed is a juice bar concept located inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre, Kelowna's large indoor mall on Harvey Avenue. Originally founded as 'Orange Cup' serving only freshly squeezed orange juice, the brand has grown into a broader fresh-juice offering. A touring cyclist passing through on the Harvey Avenue corridor can stop here for a cold, freshly pressed drink in a climate-controlled mall environment.

restaurant.name: COBS Bread
restaurant.desc: COBS Bread is a Canadian franchise bakery (part of the Australian Bakers Delight group) with roughly 190 locations across Canada, including this Shelbourne Plaza outpost in Victoria. Every item — loaves, scones, cruffins, croissants, bagels, and savoury treats — is baked from scratch on-site daily with no added preservatives. Unsold baked goods at day's end are donated to local charities, making it a reliable stop for fresh carbohydrates on a touring ride.

restaurant.name: Pawan's Indian Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Pawan's Indian Kitchen is an Indian restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver serving dine-in, takeout, and delivery. Customer reviews highlight generous portions and bold flavours, making it a filling stop for cyclists passing through the Lonsdale corridor. Takeout and delivery options add flexibility for riders who prefer to eat on the go.

detail.address: 1925 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2K3

restaurant.name: Elma
restaurant.desc: Elma is a Turkish-inspired waterfront restaurant on Lake Okanagan in Penticton, owned and operated by Michael and Ayse Barluk, blending traditional Turkish culinary techniques with local Okanagan ingredients and imported Turkish décor. The shareable-plate menu evolves seasonally, and the restaurant runs an immersive Regional Dinner Series exploring distinct culinary regions of Türkiye. A second-floor event space with lake views is available for private bookings.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists dedicated labels: (ve) vegan, (v) vegetarian, (gf) gluten free, (df) dairy free, (nf) nut free, with many dishes marked accordingly and a note that some dishes 'may be modified vegan'

restaurant.name: La Routa Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: La Ruota Pizzeria is a Neapolitan-style pizza chain with multiple BC locations, cooking handcrafted pizzas in a 900°F oven using Caputo '00' flour and ingredients sourced directly from Italy and BC. The West 4th Avenue location sits on a popular cycling corridor through Kitsilano. Online ordering, delivery, and a loyalty rewards program are available.

restaurant.name: Serena's Pizzeria and Hoagies
restaurant.desc: Serena's is a downtown Victoria restaurant specializing in Philadelphia-style hoagies and pizza, built around authentic Philly traditions of layered cold cuts, provolone, and fresh vegetables on a proper hoagie roll. With over 1,600 reviews averaging 4.9 stars, it has earned recognition as one of Victoria's top-rated pizzerias. A touring cyclist stopping on Fort Street can expect hearty, made-to-order meals with a reputation for fast, friendly service.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Veggie Pizza' category

restaurant.name: Haidilao Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Haidilao Hot Pot is a location of the internationally renowned Chinese hotpot chain, housed inside The Amazing Brentwood shopping centre in Burnaby's Brentwood neighbourhood. At over 8,600 sq.ft, it is B.C.'s largest Haidilao location, offering an immersive dining experience with daily dinner-time performances and the brand's signature tableside service. Touring cyclists stopping here can expect a substantial sit-down meal with interactive, customizable hotpot dining.

restaurant.name: Cafe Zen
restaurant.desc: Cafe Zen is a Kitsilano institution that has been serving honest brunch and lunch daily since 1989, earning a 4.4-star rating across 728+ reviews. Located steps from Kitsilano Beach on Yew Street, it draws regulars with rotating chalkboard specials, multiple eggs Benedict variations, and hearty breakfast plates at approachable prices. Touring cyclists finishing a ride along the nearby seawall or Vanier Park will find it a welcoming, unpretentious refuelling stop in the heart of the neighbourhood.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes: avocado toast, garden omelette, roast mushroom pesto Benedict, Cali Benedict (avocado & tomato), avocado omelette; tofu substitution available in Rancheros at no charge

restaurant.name: Wings Port Moody
restaurant.desc: Wings Port Moody is a location of the WINGS Restaurants chain, known for award-winning wings offered in 28 globally inspired flavours. It is a full-service restaurant and bar on St. Johns Street serving wings, burgers, pizza, pasta, and salads. Note that it is a liquor-primary establishment, so minors under 19 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.

detail.address: 2414 St. Johns St., Port Moody, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes cauliflower wingerz (vegetarian), gluten-smart halal wings, and salads

restaurant.name: Peaked Pies
restaurant.desc: Peaked Pies is a family-run Australian bakery cafe operating since 2013, specialising in handmade savoury and sweet meat pies at four BC locations including this Burnaby Heights outpost. The signature 'peaked' pie is served topped with mushy peas, mashed potatoes, and gravy — a format inspired by Australian street food tradition. The cafe also offers artisan coffee, breakfast pies, and housemade desserts, making it a solid stop for a hot, hearty meal on a ride through Burnaby.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists 'traditional meat and veggie options' and a blog post titled 'Calling All Vegans...' confirms vegan-specific menu items

restaurant.name: Grill Master
restaurant.desc: Grill Master is a fast-food stall serving Chinese cuisine in the MBC Food Court on Simon Fraser University's Burnaby campus. It sits among several other food court concepts including Ben Gong's Tea, Mad Chicken, and Big Hot. A touring cyclist passing through Burnaby Mountain would find it a convenient stop for a quick meal in a sheltered indoor setting.

restaurant.name: JJ Bean
restaurant.desc: JJ Bean Coffee Roasters is a Vancouver-founded independent specialty coffee chain established in 1996, known for small-batch daily roasting, seasonal single-origin coffees, and distinctive neighbourhood-inspired café designs. This location on Lougheed Highway sits in a unit plaza and serves espresso drinks, brewed coffee, and fresh-baked goods made in-house daily. Cyclists on Lougheed corridor routes will find it a reliable stop for coffee and food.

restaurant.name: Pizza Cavern
restaurant.desc: Pizza Cavern is a compact takeout-focused pizza shop in Duncan, BC, serving a broad menu of specialty and build-your-own pizzas, baked subs, wraps, and calzones. The kitchen leans into variety — from a Birria pulled pork pizza to a Greek and a Buffalo Chicken option — making it a practical mid-ride fuel stop for cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley. Gluten-free crust and several vegetarian builds are available for riders with dietary needs.

detail.address: 142 Fulford-Ganges Rd, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2T8

notes.Takeout: Website states 'All orders from 6:15pm onward are takeout only,' confirming takeout service is offered
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists a dedicated Vegetarian pizza, Pesto Veggie pizza, House Veggie pizza and wrap, and explicitly offers 'Gluten free (12" +$4)' crust under Build Your Own

restaurant.name: Mamalee
restaurant.desc: Mamalee is an authentic Malaysian restaurant with two Vancouver locations; this downtown Chinatown outpost serves Hainanese chicken, laksa noodle soup, roti canai, and curry beef brisket. The restaurant's roots trace back to founder Betty Lee, who began sharing her Malaysian family recipes on West Broadway in 1991 after immigrating from Kuala Lumpur. Dine-in and takeout are both available with no reservations accepted.

restaurant.name: Apollos's
restaurant.desc: Apollo's Restaurant is a Greek-inspired brunch and dinner destination on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors. The menu blends classic Hellenic dishes—Saganaki, Paidakia, Moussaka, and house-made Spanakopita—with West Coast brunch staples like Fried Chicken Waffles and Stuffed French Toast. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the restaurant holds a full liquor licence with a robust cocktail and wine list.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists Vegan Omelette (brunch), Moussaka Vegetarian (dinner), and Gluten Free Spanakopita (dinner starter)

restaurant.name: L'Atelier Pâtisserie
restaurant.desc: L'Atelier Pâtisserie is a French bakery in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, founded in 2015 to bring the flavours of southern France—particularly Marseille and Provence—to the city. The shop specialises in laminated pastries, artisanal breads made with organic flour, and a rotating menu of seasonal specials and gourmet sandwiches. It has been featured in local media and is a well-established neighbourhood fixture for fresh-baked goods and light meals.

restaurant.name: Only U Cafe
restaurant.desc: Only U Cafe is a cafe in Vancouver. Details about its menu, service, and amenities could not be verified due to website unavailability during data collection.

restaurant.name: Nonbiri Cafe
restaurant.desc: Nonbiri Cafe is a Japanese-inspired specialty cafe newly opened inside the Oishii Food Hall in Richmond, BC, built around a philosophy of slow, mindful hospitality. The menu centres on hand-whisked ceremonial matcha, hojicha and black sesame lattes made with oat milk, alongside Japanese parfaits and house-made Danish pastries. Its calm aesthetic and food-hall setting make it a convenient stop for cyclists navigating Richmond's No. 3 Road corridor.

restaurant.name: Sprout
restaurant.desc: Sprout is a plant-based eatery in the heart of Nelson, BC, focused on creative vegan food served for dine-in, takeout, and delivery. The restaurant emphasizes fresh, accessible plant-based eating and also offers catering and online ordering. Nelson is a hub for cycling in the Kootenays, and Sprout makes a welcoming stop for cyclists seeking hearty, health-conscious meals.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website title reads 'Sprout Plant Based Eatery' and body text references 'delicious plant based food'

restaurant.name: Amorosa Pasta House
restaurant.desc: Amorosa Pasta House is an Italian-Greek restaurant located on Edmonds Street in the Burnaby area, operated by Amorosa Pasta House Inc. It offers indoor seating and a menu spanning pasta and Mediterranean cuisine. Beyond these basics, no further detail is available from the blocked Facebook page.

restaurant.name: C Market Coffee
restaurant.desc: C Market Coffee is a design-forward café chain with four Tri-Cities and Vancouver locations that roasts high-quality Arabica micro-lot beans in-house and pairs them with freshly made food. The Coquitlam outpost is part of a brand that also runs coffee classes, pop-up markets, and room rentals, giving it a community hub character beyond a typical café stop. Note that the business is cashless, so card or app payment is required.

restaurant.name: Uncle Lu Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Uncle Lu Restaurant is a Taiwanese restaurant in Richmond, BC, known for home-style dishes like pork knuckle with sweet ginger dip and braised pork belly on rice. The menu spans traditional stir-fries, marinated meats, noodle soups, and classic Taiwanese street snacks in a cozy, unpretentious setting. It has built a local reputation as a hidden gem for those seeking authentic Taiwanese flavours.

restaurant.name: Viti Wine and Lager
restaurant.desc: Viti Wine and Lager is a multi-location BC liquor retailer with five Lower Mainland stores, part of the award-winning Viaggi Hospitality group. The Hastings location anchors East Vancouver's main commercial strip, offering wine, lager, gift cards, and custom orders. It is a convenient resupply stop for touring cyclists riding the East Hastings corridor.

restaurant.name: Fat Mao
restaurant.desc: Fat Mao is a modern Thai-style noodle bar by acclaimed Vancouver chef Angus An, inspired by small family-run storefronts that specialize in perfecting a single dish over generations. The 25-seat open-kitchen Downtown location focuses on regional Thai noodle soups such as Khao Soi, Nham Ngeaw, and Tom Yum Goong, alongside small plates drawing on Southeast Asian and Sichuanese flavours. It is one of two Fat Mao locations in Vancouver, with a sister restaurant in Chinatown.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'Vegetarian Cauliflower and Tofu Khao Soi Curry' on both menus and marks Roti with Curry as 'Vegetarian Available'

restaurant.name: The Social Tavern
restaurant.desc: The Social Tavern is a two-storey pub in Surrey's Fleetwood neighbourhood, marketed as a community social spot. The menu spans eating, drinking, happy hour, and brunch, and the venue hosts community events including an annual Fleetwood Block Party talent show. Takeout is available alongside dine-in reservations.

restaurant.name: Milano Espresso Lounge
restaurant.desc: Milano Espresso Lounge is the Gastown outpost of Milano Coffee, a Vancouver institution founded in 1984 by Italian master roaster Francesco Curatolo and now helmed by Brian Turko, whose blends have earned 15 gold medals from the International Institute of Coffee Tasters. The cafe is part of a network of locations known for espresso tasting bars offering up to 8 different espresso varieties simultaneously — a rarity in the city. Cyclists passing through Gastown will find a serious specialty coffee stop with deep roots in Vancouver's Little Italy neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: Hard Bean Brunch Co.
restaurant.desc: Hard Bean Brunch Co. is a casual all-day brunch restaurant that bridges the gap between fine dining and breakfast, built around the idea that brunch is a feeling rather than a time of day. Founded by hospitality veteran Heather Rhodes, the concept offers brunch-inspired food alongside craft cocktails and a wide selection of BC beers on tap across multiple Lower Mainland locations. The Port Moody Clarke Street location sits in a community well-travelled by cyclists exploring the Burrard Inlet corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website navigation lists dedicated 'Vegan Menu' and 'Glutenwise Menu' tabs

restaurant.name: Macondo
restaurant.desc: Macondo is a Colombian fast-food restaurant in Victoria on McKenzie Street. It offers dine-in and takeout service without a drive-through, providing a quick meal stop for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Frozen Paddle Inc
restaurant.desc: Frozen Paddle is a craft ice creamery that makes all its ice cream in-house using local ingredients, with a scoop shop in Prince George and a second location in Kamloops. The shop offers its signature 'Frozen 8' rotating flavours, seasonal specials, popsicles, pints, and milkshakes, with at least one dairy-free option always on scoop. Inspired by the Fraser River paddle steamers and the ice cream churn paddle, it has built a community-focused presence at local events, farmers markets, and fundraisers.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'at least one dairy free option' is always available on scoop

restaurant.name: BarBurrito
restaurant.desc: BarBurrito is Canada's largest burrito chain, proudly Canadian since 2005, with 385+ locations offering customizable Mexican-inspired burritos, bowls, tacos, and quesadillas made with fresh, in-house ingredients. The Mission location sits at C105-31954 Lougheed Hwy in a strip-mall unit. Touring cyclists can order online or in person, with delivery available via DoorDash and SkipTheDishes.

detail.address: C105-31954 Lougheed Hwy, Mission, British Columbia V2V 1A4

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Nutrition calculator lists Veggie Ground and Falafel as protein options; Gluten Free tortilla available for burritos and quesadillas

restaurant.name: Jag's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Jag's Pizza is a Burnaby pizzeria specializing in handcrafted, hand-tossed pizzas baked in stone ovens, with an eclectic menu that spans classic Italian recipes and creative offerings like a Durian Pizza. The restaurant offers dine-in seating, takeout, and home delivery, and accepts all major credit and debit cards. Party bookings are available, making it a potential rest-and-refuel stop for group cycling tours passing through the Royal Oak corridor.

restaurant.name: Kebab On Fire
restaurant.desc: Kebab on Fire is a halal Mediterranean grill that opened in 2024 on Victoria's main commercial strip, serving slow-cooked lamb, beef, and kebab wraps with house-made sauces. It positions itself as a modern, fast-casual take on traditional Mediterranean grilling, with an emphasis on fresh ingredients and generous portions. A touring cyclist riding Government Street will find it a convenient stop for a protein-rich meal with online ordering available.

restaurant.name: A la Mode
restaurant.desc: A la Mode is a gourmet pie café inside the Granville Island Public Market, founded in 1986 when Angus McKay brought his original homemade recipes from his restaurant bakeries. The café offers over 40 handmade sweet and savoury pies, artisan croissants, an espresso bar, bubble tea, and smoothies, with extensive dietary options including vegan and gluten-friendly menus. Featured in international travel guides, it has earned a loyal following among both locals and visitors to one of Vancouver's most-visited public markets.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists dedicated Vegetarian Savoury Pies, Vegan, Gluten Friendly, and Sugar Free menu sections. FAQ confirms all dessert pies are vegetarian, no lard is used, and separate vegan, gluten-free, and sugar-free menus exist. Facility is not fully gluten-free

restaurant.name: Seoul Hotdog UBC
restaurant.desc: Seoul Hotdog UBC is a Korean-style quick-service restaurant on the UBC campus specializing in corn-dog-style hotdogs with a wide range of fillings, from kimchi and bulgogi to shrimp and pizza. Beyond hotdogs, the menu spans Korean dumplings (mandu), K-pancakes, rice bowls, and shaved-ice bingsu desserts. It sits on University Boulevard in the heart of the UBC campus, making it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists riding through the university endowment lands.

restaurant.name: Floyd's Diner
restaurant.desc: Floyd's Diner is a Victoria-area landmark established in 2004, famous as 'Home of the Mahoney' and known for satisfying portions in a fun, family-friendly atmosphere. This is the Langford location, the chain's second, opened in 2012. Touring cyclists riding through the Langford corridor will find it a solid breakfast-and-lunch stop open seven days a week.

restaurant.name: @26 Viet Cafe
restaurant.desc: A Vietnamese café on West 41st Avenue in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, operating as a casual dining spot with Vietnamese cuisine. Its OSM record was verified as recently as September 2024, suggesting it is an active, established local business. Cyclists passing through the quiet residential streets of South Vancouver's west side will find it a straightforward meal stop.

restaurant.name: Patra Pizza & Curry House
restaurant.desc: Patra Pizza & Curry House is a casual restaurant in Gibsons on the Sunshine Coast serving an eclectic menu that blends classic Canadian-style pizza with Indian-inspired dishes like butter chicken, curry poutine, and samosas, alongside burgers, wraps, and pasta. The breadth of offerings — including a notably wide range of vegetarian options — makes it a practical refuelling stop for mixed groups of touring cyclists. Online ordering with a pickup option allows riders to pre-order before rolling in.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Vegetarian Pizza, Veggie Korma Pizza, Extra Veggie Pizza, Super Veggie Pizza, Organic Veggie Burger, Regular Veggie Burger, Veggie Patty Wrap, Paneer Wrap, Vegetable Samosa, and Vegetable Burger Combo

restaurant.name: Pizza Pizza
restaurant.desc: Pizza Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 1967, operating coast to coast with franchise locations across every province. This Pitt Meadows location sits on Lougheed Highway and offers pizza delivery and takeout. It provides a familiar, quick-service meal stop for cyclists moving through the Fraser Valley corridor.

restaurant.name: Sushi Ru
restaurant.desc: Sushi Ru is a sushi restaurant on Quadra Street in Victoria offering online orders. The restaurant provides a convenient dining option for cycling tourists. It's a straightforward neighborhood spot for a sit-down meal.

restaurant.name: Momi Noodle
restaurant.desc: Momi Noodle is a downtown Victoria restaurant specializing in authentic Guilin rice noodles, street snacks, and handcrafted Asian drinks. The menu centres on individual claypot hotpot noodles and traditional rice noodle bowls, with catering also available. Customer reviews highlight soul-soothing broths and a cozy atmosphere, making it a notable dining stop on Pandora Avenue.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists explicitly meat-free options including 'H6. Mix vege Mushroom Soup hotpot noodle (漓江野菌吊锅粉)' and 'B14. Chinese Cucumber Salad (凉拌黄瓜)'

restaurant.name: Rolling Hills
restaurant.desc: Rolling Hills is a full-service restaurant on Highway 97 in 108 Mile Ranch offering diverse cuisine options. The establishment provides outdoor seating and takeaway service, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through.

restaurant.name: Baci Ristorante
restaurant.desc: Baci Ristorante is a full-service Italian restaurant on East Hastings Street in Burnaby, serving a broad menu of housemade pastas, wood-fired pizzas, and classic veal and chicken dishes. The renovated dining room has a warm, intimate atmosphere with live music on weekend evenings, and the kitchen accommodates group banquets and special events. Takeout and third-party delivery are also available for cyclists who need a quick refuel.

detail.address: 3728 E Hastings St, Burnaby, BC V5C 2H5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels several dishes as '(vegetarian)' (e.g., Casarecce Putanesca, Gnocchi ai Quattro Formaggi, Pizza Fungi e Tartufo); gluten-free pizza options are listed as available for an upcharge. No explicit vegan labelling found

restaurant.name: The Bee's Knees Cafe
restaurant.desc: Established in 2015, The Bee's Knees Cafe is a community-rooted cafe and catering operation in central/south Nanaimo, notable for being one of the only spots on Vancouver Island to serve authentic Persian cuisine alongside espresso drinks and house-baked goods. Everything is made from scratch using locally sourced ingredients, with a strong commitment to vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options. The cafe has grown to two locations and is a well-loved neighbourhood hub with outdoor seating.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Sourcing page states 'Specializing in vegetarian, vegan and gluten free options'; About page notes 'Lots of Gluten free options available'; menu items are extensively labelled Vegetarian, Vegan, and Gluten free throughout

restaurant.name: Kawartha Dairy
restaurant.desc: Kawartha Dairy is a 100% Canadian, family-owned dairy company founded in 1937 in Bobcaygeon, Ontario, known for rich, creamy ice cream made with fresh milk and cream from Canadian farms. Their Britannia Beach location brings a beloved Ontario institution to BC's Sea-to-Sky corridor, making it a natural sugar stop for cyclists on the route between Squamish and Vancouver. With over 85 years of craftsmanship, the brand is well-regarded across Canada for its distinctive premium flavours.

restaurant.name: Choowee
restaurant.desc: Choowee is a bubble tea cafe located in a unit at 6386 Number 3 Road in Richmond, BC. Bubble tea shops are a popular refreshment stop for cyclists navigating Richmond's flat, bike-friendly streets. The Instagram-only web presence suggests a small, independent operation.

restaurant.name: The Cider House
restaurant.desc: Billed as Vancouver's first cider taphouse, The Cider House pours over 20 BC-crafted ciders on tap in the heart of Kitsilano, steps from Kitsilano Beach. The kitchen is fully plant-based, with locally sourced ingredients and a menu spanning shareable bites, burgers, tacos, and bowls — all vegan, many gluten-free. Its community-driven ethos and beach-adjacent location make it a distinctive stop for cyclists exploring the Kitsilano corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu page states 'All products are 100% plant-based'; many items labelled [GF]

restaurant.name: Chutneys Indian Grill
restaurant.desc: Chutneys Indian Grill is a fast-casual Indian restaurant chain positioning itself as a modern, health-forward take on Indian cuisine, with a build-to-order menu featuring items like tandoori chicken platters, stuffed buns, and signature fries. The Abbotsford location is one of three Fraser Valley–area branches and offers both pickup and delivery ordering online. Catering is also available for group events.

detail.address: 32500 South Fraser Way #190, Abbotsford, BC V2T 1X3

restaurant.name: Xpress Donair House
restaurant.desc: Xpress Donair House is a halal donair restaurant in Coquitlam specializing in lamb donairs served with mixed veggies and specialty sauces. The restaurant offers freshly prepared food and partners with major delivery platforms, making it a convenient stop for cyclists exploring the Coquitlam area. It operates a second location in Maple Ridge, serving riders along the Lougheed corridor as well.

restaurant.name: Sanjo Sushi
restaurant.desc: Japanese sushi restaurant in New Westminster offering both dine-in and takeout service. Specializes in sushi and Japanese cuisine, providing a convenient food stop for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Donair Affair
restaurant.desc: Donair Affair is a donair-focused restaurant on Grandview Highway in east Vancouver, serving the Canadian-style spiced meat sandwiches that have become a staple of the city's diverse food scene. The spot offers indoor seating in a smoke-free environment, making it a sit-down option for cyclists passing through the commercial strip. Its presence on a delivery platform suggests it also handles takeout orders.

restaurant.name: Dastaan modern Indian Café and Bistro
restaurant.desc: Dastaan is a modern Indian café and bistro on Marine Drive in White Rock, situated directly across from Canada's longest pier with sweeping Pacific Ocean views. The menu weaves together regional Indian culinary traditions — Delhi street food, Goa coastal flavours — with contemporary technique, including handcrafted cocktails. Its waterfront location on a popular cycling corridor makes it a distinctive scenic dining stop.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu blog explicitly describes multiple vegetarian dishes: Dal Arancini (creamy lentil filling), Papdi Chaat, Aloo Tikki (potato patties), and Cajun Spiced Potato Cocktail Kebabs

restaurant.name: Panago
restaurant.desc: Panago is a BC-based pizza chain with this North Vancouver outpost located in Northwood Village near the first exit off the Second Narrows Bridge on Dollarton Highway, making it a convenient stop for cyclists riding the Dollarton corridor toward Deep Cove or Indian River. The menu features gourmet-inspired pizzas built with fresh-daily dough, antibiotic-free proteins, and organic tomato sauce, alongside salads, wings, and desserts. Vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-smart options are available.

detail.address: 103 - 2120 Dollarton Highway, North Vancouver, BC V7H 0B5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Panago offers vegan, vegetarian and gluten-smart options.'

restaurant.name: Royal Bay Bakery
restaurant.desc: Royal Bay Bakery has been baking on Vancouver Island since 1974, producing a wide range of artisan breads, pastries, savory pies, and café-style lunches using organic flour and locally sourced ingredients. The building runs on solar panels and the bakery offers a free EV charging station for customers, reflecting a genuine sustainability commitment that goes beyond marketing. A solid resupply stop for touring cyclists seeking fresh baked goods, made-to-order sandwiches, soups, and quality coffee in the Metchosin corridor west of Victoria.

restaurant.name: Pho Tru
restaurant.desc: Pho Tru is a casual Vietnamese restaurant in Victoria that brings traditional street-side recipes to BC, with a menu built around pho noodle soups, Saigon subs, vermicelli bowls, and jasmine rice plates made fresh daily from generational recipes. The Mayfair location sits inside Mayfair Shopping Centre on Douglas Street, a natural waypoint for cyclists on one of Victoria's busiest arterials. Portions are noted by reviewers as filling, and the range of proteins and broths gives hungry riders plenty to choose from.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Tofu Salad Roll (Goi Cuon Chay), a vegetable jasmine rice plate (tofu, broccoli, cauliflower, carrots with ginger lemongrass sauce), and a PhoVegg soup option

restaurant.name: Kernels
restaurant.desc: Kernels Popcorn is a 100% Canadian-owned franchise founded in 1983 in Toronto, specializing in flavored popcorn sold through mall retail locations across Canada. The chain offers a wide range of gluten-free, whole-grain popcorn flavors and operates a loyalty perks card program. If a location exists in North Vancouver, it would serve as a quick snack stop for cyclists passing through a mall corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'GLUTEN FREE — Corn is the basis for any No Gluten diet, and so we ensure nothing is added to change that.' Products are also whole grain and nut-free

restaurant.name: Sun Sui Wah Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Sun Sui Wah is a long-established Cantonese seafood restaurant with origins in Hong Kong spanning over 30 years, celebrated as one of Vancouver's most recognized Chinese dining destinations. The Richmond location on busy No. 3 Road is one of two BC outposts, serving dim sum, fresh seafood, and the restaurant's signature award-winning roasted squab. It has been a repeat winner of Georgia Straight Golden Plates readers' choice awards.

restaurant.name: Discovery Coffee
restaurant.desc: Discovery Coffee is a locally owned specialty coffee roaster based in Victoria, BC, with multiple cafe locations around the city. They roast all their beans in-house and are known for their craft approach to coffee. The Blanshard Street location sits in downtown Victoria, convenient for cyclists passing through the city centre.

restaurant.name: Serano Greek Pastry
restaurant.desc: Serano Greek Pastry is a neighbourhood bakery on West Broadway in Vancouver specializing in Greek pastries, cakes, and desserts. Customer reviews highlight a warm, friendly atmosphere and a broad selection of traditional Greek baked goods. It would make a pleasant mid-ride sweet stop for cyclists travelling along the Broadway corridor.

detail.address: 3141 W Broadway, Vancouver, BC V6K 2H2, Canada

restaurant.name: The Queen's
restaurant.desc: The Queen's is a historic pub and live music venue in downtown Nanaimo, established in 1892 and located on Victoria Crescent. It bills itself as Nanaimo's premiere live music venue, consistently hosting local, national, and international artists across all genres. Touring cyclists passing through Nanaimo's downtown core will find a full pub experience with food and regular live entertainment.

restaurant.name: The Well Pub
restaurant.desc: The Wellington Pub (locally known as The Well Pub) is a casual neighbourhood bar and dining spot in Wellington, a district of Nanaimo on Vancouver Island. It offers draught beers, spirits, and a food menu, making it a practical stop for a meal or drink on a ride through the area. An on-site liquor store allows cyclists to pick up supplies for the road.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Visit our Liquor Store for take-home sales,' confirming at least liquor takeout; food takeout not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: Up Tea
restaurant.desc: Up Tea (上茶) is a bubble tea café tucked inside a retail unit at 4540 Number 3 Road in Richmond. It sits along one of Richmond's main commercial corridors, offering a spot for cyclists to grab a cold or hot tea drink. The café has no outdoor seating according to OSM tagging.

restaurant.name: Seaside Village Cafe
restaurant.desc: Seaside Village is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a cafe on Royal Avenue in North Vancouver. No further detail about its character, cuisine, or offerings could be confirmed due to the inaccessibility of its website. Its name could refer to a community hub, a neighbourhood café, or a development amenity.

restaurant.name: House of Dosas
restaurant.desc: House of Dosas is a South Indian restaurant chain with three Lower Mainland locations; this Surrey outlet serves the full menu of crispy dosas, idlis, biryanis, and Indo-Chinese dishes that have made the brand a Vancouver-area staple for over 16 years. The kitchen explicitly caters to gluten-free, vegan, and omnivore diners, drawing on locally sourced ingredients and recipes rooted in South Indian home cooking. Dine-in seating is available alongside online pick-up and delivery ordering.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page states 'Whether you are gluten-free, vegan or just a plain omnivore, our team will ensure their ancient recipes, local products and friendly service will cater to your needs.' Menu items are individually labelled (VG) for vegan and (GF) for gluten-free throughout both Kingsway and White Rock menus

restaurant.name: Zugba Flame Grilled Chicken
restaurant.desc: Zugba Flame Grilled Chicken is a Filipino take-out restaurant inside the Henlong Market in Surrey, specializing in flame-grilled chicken Inasal and Filipino comfort foods like tocino, chicken mami, and hardinera. The restaurant draws on the founders' food memories from across the Philippines, offering a menu rooted in regional Filipino street food traditions. Dine-in seating is available inside the market, and the kitchen also fulfills large family and party tray orders.

restaurant.name: Aggarwal Sweets
restaurant.desc: Aggarwal Sweets is a 100% vegetarian Indian sweets and cuisine restaurant with over 20 years of history serving the South Asian community in Surrey, located in the Payal Business Center. Founded to bring connoisseur-quality Indian sweets made with pure desi ghee to Canada, it offers an extensive menu spanning appetizers, snacks, South Indian dishes, paneer dishes, paranthas, desserts, and freshly made traditional sweets. A second location has recently opened at 6899 King George Blvd, Surrey.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states '100% Vegetarian' and '100% vegetarian kitchen' throughout; no mention of vegan or gluten-free options

restaurant.name: Bodega Ridge
restaurant.desc: Bodega Ridge is a 22-acre resort on the wild north end of Galiano Island, built around a collection of rustic log cabins, The Pink Geranium Café and General Store, and the restaurant Lola (currently temporarily closed). Originally a horse ranch from 1980, the property has been reimagined as a destination for rest, retreats, and weddings amid arbutus trees with views of the Salish Sea. Cyclists passing through Galiano Island can stop at The Pink Geranium to refuel before continuing their island exploration.

restaurant.name: Urban Gate Specialty Market
restaurant.desc: Urban Gate Specialty Market is a family-owned Persian-inspired boutique grocery store and takeout operation that has served the Tri-Cities area since 2010. The market features an in-house butcher with daily-fresh locally sourced meats, a bakery producing Persian pastries and custom cakes, and a full Persian takeout menu. Cyclists can grab a quick sit-down-quality takeout meal — from koobideh to lamb shank — or stock up on fresh groceries for the road.

detail.address: #104 - 1158 The High Street, Coquitlam, BC V3B 0C6

restaurant.name: Matcha Cafe Maiko
restaurant.desc: Matcha Cafe Maiko is a specialty matcha cafe chain originating from Hawaii, known for its premium matcha soft serve and drinks made with stone-ground Kyoto matcha. This Richmond location is situated in the Saba Road commercial area, convenient for cyclists on the flat, bike-friendly roads of central Richmond.

restaurant.name: Le Petit Saigon
restaurant.desc: Le Petit Saigon is a Vietnamese restaurant on East Hastings Street in Vancouver's east side, offering both dine-in and takeout service with delivery available. It sits along a busy arterial corridor that connects central Vancouver to outer eastside neighbourhoods, making it a potential refuelling stop for cyclists passing through.

restaurant.name: The Rack West Coast Bistro
restaurant.desc: The Rack West Coast Bistro is a family-friendly sit-down restaurant in Langford serving West Coast-inspired meals made from fresh, locally-sourced ingredients in a warm, rustic setting. Founded by Cole Byers and his wife Jasmine, the bistro has grown to a second location in Saanich and positions itself as a neighbourhood gathering spot with an all-day menu covering food, drinks, and breakfast. Touring cyclists passing through the Greater Victoria area will find both dine-in and takeout options available.

restaurant.name: Harvest Rd.
restaurant.desc: Harvest Rd. is a farm-to-table outdoor dining and takeout spot located directly on the Lochside Trail Bicycling Path, making it a natural and convenient stop for cyclists travelling between Victoria and Sidney. The menu draws heavily from the adjacent Michell's Farm Market, with house-ground burgers, sandwiches, hot dogs, and custom cold-pressed apple juice all featuring locally raised and grown ingredients. Harvest Rd. holds the highest recognition from the Vancouver Island Green Business Certification Program and was named the Greenest Restaurant on Vancouver Island in 2017, operating a fully zero-waste service model with compostable packaging.

detail.address: 2451 Island View Road, Saanichton, BC V8M 1W3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Herbie Burger — Herbivore's Choice vegan and gluten free patty', 'Bun O Love — Vegan!', and a 'Vegan smoked apple/sage sausage substitute' for the Papa T Dog

restaurant.name: Bean Around the World
restaurant.desc: Bean Around the World is a specialty coffee roaster with over 30 years of operation, hand-roasting small batches daily at its North Vancouver roastery headquarters. The brand operates physical cafe locations in the region and sells beans, brew gear, and accessories online. A touring cyclist stopping in would find a quality coffee stop with a long local heritage.

restaurant.name: Pizza Factory
restaurant.desc: Pizza Factory Steveston is a family-owned pizzeria in Steveston Village that has been serving Richmond for over 30 years. The family makes dough fresh daily with homemade tomato sauce and sources cheese and toppings daily, offering a wide range of classic and creative pies including tandoori chicken, seafood, and heart-shaped specialty pizzas. The business is deeply embedded in the local community, sponsoring schools and charities and hosting annual free-slice appreciation days.

notes.Takeout: Website deals page lists 'Pick Up & Delivery' as ordering options; 'Pick Up Only' deals listed separately, confirming in-store pickup is available
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Customer reviews note 'lots of vegetarian options' and specifically call out 'Black bean Taco pizza with vegan cheese' and 'vegetarian Greek' pizza; menu also lists Margherita and vegetable-based options

restaurant.name: Kirin Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Kirin Restaurant is a long-established fine Chinese dining institution that has operated from its original Alberni Street location in Downtown Vancouver since 1987. The restaurant is known for handcrafted dim sum, whole abalone, Peking duck, and Cantonese seafood dishes prepared by internationally trained chefs using local BC ingredients. EnRoute Magazine has called it 'posh, comfortable and smoothly run' with a vast menu, making it a notable sit-down dining destination in the city core.

notes.Takeout: Website menu lists 'Roasted Suckling Pig Special Set Menu (take out only)' and describes home delivery and store pickup options for frozen dim sum and entrées
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Downtown Vancouver menu page lists a dedicated 'Gluten Free Menu (無麩質菜譜)'

restaurant.name: Island Bagel
restaurant.desc: Island Bagel and Bannock is an Indigenous-owned social enterprise and café on the unceded traditional territory of the Quw'utsun mustimuhw in Duncan, BC. The menu centres on freshly made bagels, traditional bannock, handcrafted drinks, and Indigenous-inspired salads and soups, with all-day breakfast service. Beyond food, the space is a cultural gathering place guided by Elders, with a reservable meeting room and catering services.

restaurant.name: Bubble Bear Cafe
restaurant.desc: Bubble Bear Cafe is a bubble tea café on Granville Street in Vancouver, operating since 2017 with bilingual English and Chinese branding that reflects the neighbourhood's diverse clientele. It offers online ordering and e-gift cards, suggesting a takeout-friendly operation suited to a quick cyclist stop. The Granville Street corridor is a busy arterial route connecting central Vancouver to the south, making this a plausible refreshment stop on longer urban rides.

restaurant.name: Yaletown Brewing Company
restaurant.desc: Founded in 1994, Yaletown Brewing Company is Vancouver's original brewpub, established in the historic warehouse district of Yaletown just as it was transforming into a vibrant neighbourhood. The pub brews its own flagship and seasonal beers on-site — including a lager, wheat beer, IPA, and pale ale — and pairs them with a full pub food menu. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists passing through the heart of downtown Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu includes vegetarian dishes such as Gochujang Cauliflower and Edamame

restaurant.name: Sprezzatura
restaurant.desc: Sprezzatura is a pizza restaurant located on Kingsway in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood. Situated along a well-travelled urban corridor, it offers a convenient stop for cyclists moving through the city.

restaurant.name: Valhalla Smoke House
restaurant.desc: Valhalla Smoke House is a family-friendly BBQ restaurant in Kamloops that evolved from a food truck started in 2020 into a full restaurant in 2024. They specialize in slow-smoked meats — including brisket, pulled pork, ribs, and chicken — alongside house-made sides and salads. The restaurant also runs a full catering operation and can host large group bookings, making it a solid stop for cycling groups.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Catering menu labels multiple items: Potato Salad (Vegetarian, Gluten Free), Macaroni Salad (Vegetarian), Caesar (Dairy Free, Vegetarian), Coleslaw (Vegetarian, Gluten Free), House Salad (Vegan, Gluten Free)

restaurant.name: Krishna Dosa Grill South Surrey
restaurant.desc: Krishna's Dosa Grill South Surrey (OSM-listed as Krishnas Curry and Crepes House) is an authentic South Indian restaurant in South Surrey specializing in handcrafted dosas, idlis, vadas, and biryanis prepared from traditional recipes and fresh ingredients. The restaurant is notable for its extensive vegetarian and vegan menu alongside meat dishes, with some items naturally gluten-free. Cyclists can dine in or order takeout, with delivery coverage spanning much of Surrey.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'extensive vegetarian and vegan options' and notes the Masala Ghee Podi Idli is 'naturally gluten-free.'

restaurant.name: Fire Hall Kitchen & Tap
restaurant.desc: Fire Hall Kitchen & Tap is a craft beer tap house and gastropub housed in the heritage Fire Hall No.1 building in downtown Cranbrook, a couple of turns off the Crowsnest Highway. It pours exclusively BC craft beers across 20 taps and offers a full food menu in a Kootenay-culture setting. A natural post-ride stop for cyclists exploring the southern Rockies, trails, and surrounding backcountry.

detail.address: 37 11th Ave S, Cranbrook, British Columbia V1C 2N9, Canada

restaurant.name: Baan Wasana
restaurant.desc: Baan Wasana is a family-owned Thai restaurant in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, serving homestyle family-style Thai food since 2005. The restaurant takes its name from its owner, Wasana — 'Baan' meaning 'house' in Thai — reflecting her philosophy that every guest is welcomed as if in her own home. The menu spans classic Thai appetizers, soups, salads, curries, and stir-fries, built around the four foundational Thai flavour profiles: sweet, sour, salty, and spicy.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Vegetarian spring rolls stuffed with cabbage, carrot and glass noodles,' Tow Hoo Tod (deep-fried tofu), and Tom Kah with choice of Vegetable or Tofu

restaurant.name: Little Saigon
restaurant.desc: Little Saigon is a Vietnamese restaurant with two Abbotsford-area locations serving pho, vermicelli bowls, and rice plates made with no MSG and clean, house-made broths. The McCallum Road location is a modern dine-in spot with free parking and online ordering for quick pickup. It also operates a warehouse retail and wholesale outlet, suggesting a larger operation than a typical single-location restaurant.

restaurant.name: Ramen Arashi
restaurant.desc: Ramen Arashi is a Japanese ramen franchise founded in Banff in 2017 by Ken Seki and Yuji Yokomori, dedicated to bringing authentic regional ramen styles to Canada without trendy twists. The Victoria location opened in 2022 as the brand's first franchise and has been described as Victoria's best-rated ramen shop on Google, with features on the popular YouTube channel Abroad in Japan. Touring cyclists looking for a warm, sit-down restorative meal will find a focused ramen menu in a busy Douglas Street retail strip.

detail.address: 2950 Douglas St Unit 222, Victoria, BC V8T 4N4

restaurant.name: The Praguery Café & Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: The Praguery is a Czech-inspired specialty café in Coquitlam known for freshly baked chimney cakes (kürtőskalács) — spiral pastries served plain or as loaded 'chimney smashes' with house-made sauces, whipped cream, and toppings like pistachio, Nutella, or salted caramel. They also offer ice cream cones, sundaes, espresso drinks, and hot chocolate. The café is takeout/pickup only with outdoor seating and wheelchair accessibility, making it a sweet stop for cyclists passing through the Pinetree Way corridor.

notes.Takeout: Website is a dedicated pickup ordering platform with 'Pickup from 1207 Pinetree Wy' as the only fulfillment method

restaurant.name: Purple panda
restaurant.desc: Purple Panda Chi-Thai Bistro is a cozy Thai and Chinese restaurant in Whistler, BC, serving dishes like Massaman Beef Curry, Panang Curry Chicken, and Thai Laksa Curry Noodles. Customer reviews praise its authentic flavours and welcoming atmosphere, making it a notable dining option in a mountain resort town. The restaurant offers daily happy hour specials on appetizers and drinks.

restaurant.name: Blue House Korean Buffet & Sushi
restaurant.desc: A Korean buffet and sushi restaurant in Squamish with indoor seating. Provides a mix of Korean buffet and sushi options for touring cyclists seeking a sit-down meal.

restaurant.name: Rice & Noodle
restaurant.desc: Rice & Noodle is a casual counter-service Asian kitchen specializing in pad thai and customizable rice and noodle dishes, operating as a franchise chain. Diners choose from 13 dishes, then select protein (chicken, beef, prawn, tofu, or mixed veggies) and spice level up to 'extreme.' The relaxed, fast-casual format is well suited to a quick refuel stop on Kingsway.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Tofu and Mixed Veggies listed as explicit protein options across all dishes; vegetarian spring rolls offered as a side

restaurant.name: Pizzeria PrimaStrada
restaurant.desc: Pizzeria Prima Strada is a neighbourhood wood-fired Neapolitan pizza restaurant in Cook Street Village that has been serving Victoria for over 15 years. The menu centres on thin-crust pizzas baked in a wood-fired oven, housemade gelato, antipasti, pasta, and a curated selection of Italian wines and craft beer. The relaxed, community-focused atmosphere makes it a natural rest stop for touring cyclists exploring Victoria's south end.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple meatless pizzas: Margherita (tomato, mozzarella, basil), Capricciosa verde (basil pesto, artichoke hearts, mushrooms, red onion), and Funghi supremo (portobello, button and oyster mushrooms). No explicit vegan or gluten-free labelling found

restaurant.name: Pho Triple 7
restaurant.desc: Pho Triple 7 is a fully-licensed Vietnamese restaurant in Chemainus, BC, specializing in traditional pho and Vietnamese cuisine prepared with fresh herbs and a variety of topping choices. The restaurant draws customers from across the region including Duncan, Ladysmith, Nanaimo, and Victoria, suggesting it is a notable destination rather than a casual local spot. Cyclists passing through the Chemainus area would find it a comfortable sit-down meal option with attentive service.

restaurant.name: The Flying Pig
restaurant.desc: The Flying Pig is a West Coast farm-to-table restaurant in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, operating since 2011 with a menu built around locally sourced BC seafood (steelhead trout, ling cod, wild coho salmon), meats, and seasonal produce. Named for the idea of making the impossible happen, the restaurant cultivates a convivial, family-style atmosphere drawing on the diversity of fresh coastal ingredients. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the location is wheelchair accessible.

restaurant.name: Deer Park Diner
restaurant.desc: Deer Park Diner is a brunch-focused restaurant on Deer Park Avenue in Kimberley, a small mountain city in BC's East Kootenays. It serves morning and midday meals daily and would make a natural refueling stop for cyclists touring the Kootenay Rockies region. The diner-style format and all-day brunch cuisine are well suited to riders starting or finishing a day on local trails and roads.

detail.address: 130 Deer Park Avenue, Kimberley, BC V1A 2J4

restaurant.name: Honjin Ramen
restaurant.desc: Honjin Raman is a Japanese ramen restaurant listed in OSM for the North Vancouver area. Very limited public data is available for this location, and the OSM record's coordinates and associated web presence appear to point toward a Coquitlam business rather than a confirmed North Vancouver establishment.

restaurant.name: Old Yale Brewing
restaurant.desc: Old Yale Brewing is an award-winning craft brewery established in 1999 with a full taproom and kitchen in Chilliwack, pouring 15+ beers on tap including lagers, IPAs, sours, and stouts. The Chilliwack location is one of three brewery-kitchen sites spanning BC and Alberta, and offers a broad menu of burgers, pizza, and mains alongside cocktails, cider, and non-alcoholic drinks. Dogs are welcome on the patio and kids are fully accommodated, making it a relaxed and well-rounded stop for touring cyclists in the Fraser Valley.

detail.address: 44550 S Sumas Rd #404, Chilliwack, BC V2R 5M3

restaurant.name: Sun Tea
restaurant.desc: SunTea Canada is a BC-founded bubble tea chain (est. 2019) serving fresh-brewed fruit teas and milk teas, now operating 13 stores across British Columbia and Alberta. This Lougheed Highway location sits in a Burnaby shopping complex and offers online pickup ordering and a loyalty rewards app. For a touring cyclist, it is a convenient stop for a cold or hot tea drink on routes through the Burnaby–Coquitlam corridor.

restaurant.name: COBS Bread
restaurant.desc: COBS Bread is a Canadian franchise of the Australian Bakers Delight chain, with over 190 locations across Canada. This Abbotsford location at Gladwin Crossing bakes all bread and pastries fresh on-site daily with no freezing or refrigeration, and donates unsold goods to local charities at day's end. Touring cyclists can resupply with fresh bread, loaves, scones, bagels, and savoury items like mini pizzas.

restaurant.name: Jo's Italian Deli
restaurant.desc: Jo's Italian Deli is a family-owned Italian deli in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, serving homemade sandwiches on house-baked bread, fresh pasta with homemade sauces, espresso, and deli groceries sourced the same way the family eats at home. It is part of a small multi-location BC operation with branches on Main Street and in Chilliwack. Cyclists riding the Kitsilano and Point Grey corridors will find a filling, made-from-scratch meal in a casual neighbourhood setting.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists green salads and deli sides consistent with vegetarian options. Vegan explicitly not offered

restaurant.name: Vallarta's Mexican Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Vallarta's Mexican Restaurant is a sit-down Mexican restaurant on East Broadway in east Vancouver. It offers touring cyclists a place to enjoy a full meal and rest from cycling. As a restaurant serving Mexican cuisine, it provides hearty dining options for travelers.

restaurant.name: Blue Parrot Coffee
restaurant.desc: Blue Parrot Coffee is a family-owned café operating since 1979, named after the competing bar in the Humphrey Bogart film Casablanca. The Hillcrest Community Centre location offers freshly squeezed juices, real fruit smoothies, and food made without preservatives or deep-frying, catering to active patrons. The business holds Beyond Green™ certification for its eco-friendly practices, and is one of the few cafés still serving lattes in signature clear glass mugs.

detail.address: 4575 Clancy Loranger Way, Vancouver, BC, V5Y 2M4

restaurant.name: Miion Café
restaurant.desc: Miion Café is an artisan coffee shop in Richmond, BC, whose name and identity are built around the chemistry concept of ions — the idea that a cup of coffee can trigger a transformative 'ionic state' of energy or inspiration. Founded by owner Mia, it serves a full espresso bar alongside stone-milled teas and a food menu of house-baked croissants, bagel sandwiches, salads, and fruit bowls. The café also runs latte art workshops, giving it a community hub quality beyond a standard coffee stop.

detail.address: 6386 No. 3 Rd Unit 130, Richmond, BC V6Y 0L8

restaurant.name: Firehouse Subs
restaurant.desc: Firehouse Subs is a Canadian fast-food sandwich chain serving hot, toasted subs with a focus on hearty, flavourful fillings. The brand is also known for its Public Safety Foundation of Canada, which has donated over $6.3 million in equipment grants to first responders across the country. Touring cyclists will find it a convenient stop on South Fraser Way for a filling meal with takeout and online ordering available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website footer navigation includes a dedicated 'Gluten Free Roll' link, confirming a GF bread option is available on the Canadian menu

restaurant.name: The Shellfish Shack
restaurant.desc: The Shellfish Shack is a restaurant on Alexandra Road in Richmond, BC, whose name suggests a focus on shellfish and seafood.
