restaurant.name: GoodCo
restaurant.desc: Good Co. Northwoods is a full-service sports bar and restaurant at the eastern end of Dollarton Highway in North Vancouver, part of the Good Co. Bars multi-location chain. The venue blends a broad food menu — tacos, burgers, wings, salads — with a strong events calendar of trivia nights, watch parties, and dance evenings, plus a dedicated FIFA 2026 sports-viewing programme. OSM confirms wheelchair accessibility and a no-smoking policy throughout.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Veggie Burger (mushroom-rice patty), Veggie Dumplings, Sofritas Tacos, Glory Bowl with tofu, and explicitly offers a 'gluten free vegan bun' substitute; multiple salads are also vegetarian

restaurant.name: Yumyai Thai Food
restaurant.desc: Yum Yai Thai Food is an authentic Thai restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street corridor, formerly known as Bob Likes Thai Food, serving home-style Thai cuisine under the philosophy of 'we serve what we eat.' The name YumYai blends the Thai words for bold mixed flavours (yum) and big-hearted (yai), reflecting a menu that ranges from papaya salads and chicken satay to coconut curries and classic Pad Thai. Touring cyclists on the Main Street bike route will find a compact, takeout-friendly stop with vegetarian and gluten-free options across most menu categories.

restaurant.name: DaBao
restaurant.desc: Ike's Café was a UBC Food Services–operated café on the UBC Vancouver campus; the URL for this listing now resolves to DaBao, a quick-service outlet specializing in bao, dim sum, tarts, buns, and bubble tea in partnership with Kam Wai Dim Sum, Pine House Bakery, and Pearl Fever. The location sits inside the Irving K. Barber Learning Centre and serves the broader UBC campus community.

restaurant.name: Papa Dave's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Papa Dave's Pizza is a neighbourhood institution in New Westminster that has been hand-tossing pizzas for over two decades, building a loyal following with signature sauce recipes and locally sourced toppings. Beyond pizza, the menu spans Indian curry dishes, biryani, chicken tandoori, and pasta, making it an unusually eclectic and filling stop. An all-you-can-eat buffet and indoor/outdoor seating round out the experience for cyclists looking to refuel after a long ride.

restaurant.name: Taco Bell
restaurant.desc: A Taco Bell fast-food location in Surrey serving Tex-Mex staples including tacos, burritos, and the Crunchwrap Supreme, with both dine-in seating and a drive-through lane. The restaurant also offers a Veggie Cravings Menu with vegetarian options such as the Cheesy Bean and Rice Burrito. Convenient for touring cyclists passing through the 56 Avenue corridor needing a quick, filling meal with online ordering and delivery available.

restaurant.name: Mr. Ho Wonton House
restaurant.desc: Mr. Ho Wonton House is a Chinese restaurant on Kingsway in Burnaby serving fresh wonton, noodle soups, congee, hot pot, and a broad menu of classic Cantonese dishes. The restaurant offers indoor seating with air conditioning, and accepts online orders for both pickup and delivery via its own app. It sits on a busy arterial cycling corridor connecting Burnaby to Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Khao San Thai Street Food
restaurant.desc: Khao San Thai Street Food is a Thai street-food restaurant on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most vibrant and cycling-friendly main streets. The name references Bangkok's famous Khao San Road, suggesting a focus on casual, street-style Thai dishes. Commercial Drive is well-served by bike lanes and is a natural stop on any urban cycling route through East Vancouver.

restaurant.name: Discovery Coffee
restaurant.desc: Discovery Coffee is a locally owned Victoria roaster and cafe that began with a love of the craft and has grown into a multi-location operation with a devoted following. They roast all their beans in Victoria and offer house blends alongside single-origin coffees, with a partnership with Yonni's Doughnuts rounding out the food offering. The Menzies Street location puts touring cyclists close to the Inner Harbour and James Bay neighbourhoods.

restaurant.name: Barnside Brewery Co.
restaurant.desc: Barnside Brewing is a true farm-based destination brewery in Ladner (Delta), BC, crafting award-winning beers from hops and grains grown on the surrounding family farms. The taproom occupies a converted heritage barn with century-old beams and a four-season patio overlooking the hop yards, making it an unusually atmospheric rural stop. The brewery has roots going back to 1899 and produces a full range of craft lagers, ales, and sours alongside a farm-focused food menu.

restaurant.name: The Bay Leaf
restaurant.desc: The Bay Leaf is an Indian fusion restaurant in downtown Creston run by chef-owner Dilip Chand, a Nepal-born chef whose culinary career spans India, Bahrain, Ottawa, and Kelowna before he brought his cooking to the East Kootenays. The menu blends Indian, Nepalese, and Hakka dishes with a full-service bar featuring BC and local Creston wines. The restaurant is part of a small regional chain with locations also in Fernie and Cranbrook.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Cheesy Kofta, Cauli Aloo, Aubergine Bharta, Paneer Butter Masala, Karahi Paneer Fry, Palak Paneer, and more

restaurant.name: Aburiya Sushi
restaurant.desc: Aburiya Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Maple Ridge offering online takeout ordering. Located on Dewdney Trunk Road, it serves passing traffic in a busy commercial area. Useful for touring cyclists needing a quick, fresh meal without the need to dine in.

restaurant.name: Miko Sushi
restaurant.desc: Miko Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant situated on Robson Street in Vancouver's West End, one of the city's most walkable and cyclable commercial corridors. The restaurant offers indoor table seating in a smoke-free environment. Its Robson Street location puts it within easy reach of the city's downtown cycling network.

restaurant.name: Desi Village Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Desi Village is a full-service Indian restaurant on Lougheed Highway in Maple Ridge, serving a broad menu of traditional dishes including biryanis, tandoori specialties, curries, and North Indian street foods like momos and amritsari kulcha. The restaurant emphasizes cultural immersion through traditional decor and music alongside its food. Online ordering and table reservations are both available, making it a convenient meal stop for cyclists travelling through Maple Ridge.

restaurant.name: Gian's Indian Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Gian's Indian Cuisine is a sit-down Indian restaurant located on South Fraser Way in Chilliwack, BC. It sits along a main arterial corridor that cycling tourists travelling through the Fraser Valley may pass through. Beyond its cuisine type, no additional details about the dining experience or facilities could be confirmed.

restaurant.name: Eden
restaurant.desc: Coastal Eden Cafe is a social enterprise in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside operated by Coastal Church, where all cafe proceeds fund the Eden DTES community program supporting marginalized individuals. The cafe offers a full espresso bar, housemade sandwiches, protein smoothies, and specialty drinks in a welcoming dine-in space designed for people from all walks of life. It also runs a 3–6 month transitional employment and barista training program for individuals facing barriers to work.

detail.address: 643 East Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 1R2

restaurant.name: LanaLou's
restaurant.desc: LanaLou's is an owner-operated rock n' roll eatery on Powell Street in Vancouver, celebrated for its live music, rotating art, and quirky, unpretentious decor. The 100-seat licensed restaurant serves comfort food crafted from locally sourced ingredients in a community-minded atmosphere. It is fully wheelchair accessible and operates as both a restaurant and a live music venue.

restaurant.name: Roll & Chicken
restaurant.desc: Roll & Chicken is a sushi and Korean restaurant on Ross Road in Nanaimo, BC, combining two popular cuisines under one roof. The name hints at a menu pairing Korean-style fried chicken with rolls or rice-based dishes, offering a filling stop for cyclists needing a substantial meal. It sits in a residential-commercial corridor on the south side of Nanaimo.

restaurant.name: BNA Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: BNA Brewing Co. is a locally owned craft brewery, eatery, and entertainment venue occupying a restored century-old brick warehouse — originally a British North American Tobacco Company facility — in downtown Kelowna since 2015. All beer is brewed on-site and served alongside a full food menu featuring shareable, culturally-inspired dishes, cocktails, and local Okanagan wine. The venue also houses six 10-pin bowling lanes, making it a lively stop in the heart of the Okanagan.

restaurant.name: Did's Pizza
restaurant.desc: A casual pizza restaurant serving thin-crust pizza by the slice, calzones, and pasta. Located on Dunsmuir Street in downtown Vancouver, it offers indoor seating and represents a quick meal stop for cyclists passing through the city.

restaurant.name: Emporia
restaurant.desc: Emporia is a family-owned restaurant and live music venue in the heart of Langford on Vancouver Island's Westshore, serving elevated West Coast comfort food made almost entirely from locally sourced ingredients — farms in Metchosin, Sooke, Saanich, and Saltspring Island among them. The space offers cozy booths, a private lounge, and a south-facing patio, with craft BC beers, spirits, and regional wines on tap. As the evening progresses, a live stage hosts local bands, DJs, and open-mic nights.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu items labelled 'VG' (vegetarian) and 'GF' (gluten-free) — e.g. 'Mozzarella Arancini • VG GF' and 'Bocconcini Bruschetta • VG'

restaurant.name: Sprinkles Gelato and Dessert House
restaurant.desc: Sprinkles Gelato and Dessert House is a gelato and dessert shop located in Steveston, the historic fishing village neighbourhood of Richmond, BC. Steveston sits at the terminus of popular cycling routes including the West Dyke Trail and the Steveston Scenic Loop, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists exploring the Fraser River delta.

restaurant.name: Pho Goodness
restaurant.desc: Pho Goodness is a Vietnamese comfort food restaurant established in 2011, originally on Davie Street in the West End and now operating three Vancouver locations. The Main & 15th location sits in the heart of the Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, serving pho, banh mi, rice dishes, and vermicelli bowls with dine-in and takeout options. The restaurant has earned multiple 'Best Of City' recognitions from Westender Magazine for best Vietnamese food and best pho.

restaurant.name: IHOP
restaurant.desc: IHOP is a well-known North American chain specializing in pancakes and all-day breakfast, with this Richmond location sitting on a busy commercial corridor on Number 3 Road. The restaurant offers a full sit-down dining experience alongside takeout and delivery options under the IHOP 'N GO brand. Touring cyclists looking for a reliable, filling meal stop in Richmond would find familiar comfort-food options here.

restaurant.name: Donair Dude
restaurant.desc: Donair Dude is a Vancouver-born Mediterranean fast-food chain that got its start during the 2010 Winter Olympics and has grown into a multi-location franchise. The Gastown location on West Hastings Street serves freshly prepared donairs, falafel wraps, platters, and poutine using BC-sourced meat roasted in-house. It offers a wide menu including chicken, beef, lamb, and vegan options, making it a solid calorie stop for cyclists moving through downtown Vancouver.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu filter includes a dedicated 'VEGAN' category; falafel wraps and falafel platters are listed

restaurant.name: A-1Pizza
restaurant.desc: A-1 Pizza is a locally owned fast-food pizza shop in Surrey, BC, specializing in Punjabi-style pizzas with a distinctive Desi-influenced flavour profile. The menu features a broad range of vegetarian options alongside customizable pies, drawing a loyal local following. Cyclists will find ample free parking on site, with both a parking lot and parking garage noted in customer reviews.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Customer review states: 'Vegetarian options: A tonne of veggie options!'

restaurant.name: Best Falafel
restaurant.desc: Best Falafel is a family-owned Syrian-Lebanese fast food restaurant founded by Damascus-born Hisham Wattar, who has been feeding Vancouverites since 2000. The Kitsilano location sits on West 4th Avenue, a well-travelled cycling corridor, and serves wraps, plates, and falafel made from fresh ingredients rooted in Syrian and Lebanese tradition. With three Metro Vancouver locations and a robust catering operation, it has grown from a single Commercial Drive fixture into a recognizable local chain.

restaurant.name: Sneakers Sports Lounge

restaurant.name: Wildcat Grill
restaurant.desc: The Wildcat Grill is an independently owned restaurant in Rosedale, BC, serving the Fraser Valley since 1996 and home of the famous Rowdy Rosedale Burger — three half-pound patties on half a loaf of French bread with all the trimmings. The menu spans burgers, prime aged beef, seafood, and salads in a sit-down dining room with an outdoor patio, and takeout is available seven nights a week. The location beside an Esso station near the Highway 9 and Yale Road roundabout makes it easy to spot from the road.

restaurant.name: JJ Dosai
restaurant.desc: JJ Dosai is a South Indian restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver serving traditional dishes like dosai. It offers a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: Lunch Matters... Breakfast Too
restaurant.desc: A restaurant in Vernon with a name suggesting breakfast and lunch service. Website access failed due to DNS resolution error, making current operational status uncertain.

restaurant.name: Café Prado
restaurant.desc: Prado Coffee is a well-regarded Vancouver specialty coffee roaster and café group founded by four-time Canadian Barista Champion Sammy Piccolo, with origins on Commercial Drive and now spanning eight-plus neighbourhood locations across Vancouver, Burnaby, and Surrey. The Fir Street location sits in the Fairview/South Granville area, serving carefully sourced espresso drinks and fresh baked goods under the brand's community-first ethos. Cyclists will find it a welcoming mid-ride coffee stop in a walkable, mixed-use corridor of the city.

restaurant.name: Pho Capital
restaurant.desc: Pho Capital is a cozy Vietnamese restaurant in Richmond that has been serving slow-simmered pho, bánh mì sandwiches, and fresh vermicelli bowls since 2022. The kitchen starts early each day to simmer broth and prep fresh herbs, with a broad menu spanning beef soups, grilled meats, salad rolls, and a range of appetizers. It is a welcoming sit-down spot well suited to a mid-ride meal, with complimentary Wi-Fi and online ordering available.

restaurant.name: Wo's Chinese Restaurant

The restaurant accommodates dine-in, pickup, delivery, catering, and tourist group meals, making it a flexible option for cycling groups or solo riders refuelling on a long ride through South Vancouver. The OSM check_date of May 2025 confirms it remains actively operating.

restaurant.name: Bun Cha Ca Hoang Yen
restaurant.desc: Bun Cha Ca Hoang Yen is a long-established East Vancouver Vietnamese restaurant specializing in bún chả cá (fish cake vermicelli soup), phở, and a broad range of rice and vermicelli noodle dishes. Operating since at least 2012, it earned a 'Best Vietnamese' finalist nod in Vancouver in 2018. The restaurant expanded into a larger 3000 sq ft premises on the same Victoria Drive block, making it a substantial neighbourhood dining destination.

restaurant.name: Old Barley Market Beer & Wine Store
restaurant.desc: The Old Barley Market Beer & Wine Store is a liquor retail outlet in Merritt, BC, appearing to operate in connection with the Coldwater Hotel on Quilchena Avenue. Merritt sits at the junction of several major cycling routes through the Nicola Valley, making this a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through. The store offers beer and wine retail in a community that sees significant through-traffic on the Coquihalla corridor.

restaurant.name: Snack Pack Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Snack Pack Ice Cream is an ice cream shop on West 4th Avenue in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, a busy cycling corridor connecting downtown to UBC. The business maintains an Instagram presence under @snackpackvancouver, consistent with artisan or independent dessert shops common to the area. Its location on a high-traffic cycling route makes it a natural rest stop for touring cyclists passing through.

restaurant.name: Chef's Kebab
restaurant.desc: Chef's Kebab is an Indian restaurant on Fraser Highway in Surrey serving an extensive menu of authentic kebabs, curries, and biryanis, with breakfast items like Chole Puri and Paranthas rounding out the all-day offering. The menu spans lamb, chicken, seafood, and vegetarian dishes, with rotating daily specials that keep regulars coming back. Online ordering, delivery, and full catering services are all available.

restaurant.name: The Phoenix
restaurant.desc: The Phoenix is a restaurant in Ladysmith, BC, offering a local dining option for touring cyclists. Website content is currently unavailable due to technical issues, so menu specialties and specific amenities cannot be verified.

restaurant.name: Hog Shack Cook House
restaurant.desc: Hog Shack Cook House bills itself as Steveston's first and only BBQ and casual cookhouse, specializing in Kansas City-style smoked meats with all rubs and sauces made in-house from scratch. The restaurant is distinctive for its 100% craft beer list — no mass-market brands — curated specifically to pair with their smoked dishes. Located in Steveston Village, a popular destination along Richmond's extensive waterfront dyke cycling network, it offers a relaxed, kid-friendly dine-in experience with four HD TVs and a casual atmosphere.

restaurant.name: Pizza64
restaurant.desc: Pizza64 is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 2010 as a family business, with 20+ locations across British Columbia. Each location makes its sauce and dough fresh on-site, and the menu spans specialty, signature, and gourmet pizzas alongside wings, pasta, and sides. Online ordering is available, making it a convenient quick-stop for cyclists needing a calorie-dense meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists multiple meatless options: Garden Fresh (vegetables only), Pesto Veggie (garlic, spinach, onions, peppers, tomatoes), Passion of India (Tandoori Paneer), and Shahi Paneer. No explicit vegan or gluten-free claims found

restaurant.name: Chambar
restaurant.desc: Chambar is an award-winning full-service restaurant in Vancouver's Crosstown neighbourhood, celebrated for its Belgian-influenced menu, craft cocktail and beer programs, and a platinum distinction wine list. The venue features both a reservable indoor dining room and a first-come, first-serve patio, sitting at the edge of one of downtown Vancouver's most active pedestrian and cycling corridors near BC Place. Owners Karri and Nico have built a reputation around what they call 'Civilized Debauchery,' combining fine-dining quality with a lively, welcoming atmosphere.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website FAQ confirms: 'Our kitchen team is happy to accommodate allergies. Please discuss any allergies or dietary restrictions with your server.'

restaurant.name: Trish Juice
restaurant.desc: Trish Juice is a 100% vegan juice bar and café that is part of a growing Canadian franchise, with a Downtown Vancouver outpost on Hornby Street. The menu ranges from freshly pressed juices and smoothie bowls to grilled wraps, salads, wellness shots, and baked goods. OSM tags indicate indoor seating is available, making it a plausible fuelling stop for cyclists on the Hornby Street corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states '100% Vegan' and lists menu as 'Freshly squeezed Juice | Bubble Tea | Smoothies | Milk Shakes | Fruit & Veg Salads | 100% Vegan'

restaurant.name: Tsujiri
restaurant.desc: Tsujiri is a Japanese matcha-focused tea house and restaurant rooted in Kyoto tradition, founded by Riemon Tsuji whose refinement of Gyokuro cultivation earned him a statue in Japan. The Richmond branch brings authentic ceremonial-grade matcha from Uji, Kyoto to Canada, offering specialty matcha beverages, desserts, and whole cakes. It sits within a multi-unit commercial complex in Richmond, making it a distinctive cultural stop for cyclists exploring the city's network of paths.

restaurant.name: Minerva
restaurant.desc: Minerva's has been a family-owned landmark in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood since 1975, serving hand-pressed pizzas, charbroiled steaks, hearty pastas, and traditional Greek dishes. The restaurant features a cozy dining room alongside a lounge and patio with happy hour specials, and supports takeout and delivery for those on the go. Its central west-side location makes it a potential refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the Arbutus Greenway corridor or the broader neighbourhood.

restaurant.name: River Road Café
restaurant.desc: River Road Café is a family-run Brazilian café in Richmond bringing authentic flavours — from street-food pastels and party snacks to imported Brazilian goods — to the table. Founded by a Brazilian couple and their team, the café offers dine-in meals, an online shop with home delivery for frozen and imported products, and catering services. It sits along River Road, a popular cycling corridor on the south arm of the Fraser River.

restaurant.name: Yummy Slice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Yummy Slice Pizza is a Canadian-owned pizza chain offering takeout and delivery, with locations across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. The McCallum Road location is one of several Lower Mainland branches of the growing franchise, known for pizza by the slice and a broad menu of classic and signature pies. Touring cyclists passing through Abbotsford will find a quick, filling stop with a wide range of topping combinations.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists multiple vegetarian pizzas: Veggie Lovers, Greek, Garden Pesto, Yummy Veggie, Yummy Potato, Yummy Paneer, Tandoori Paneer, Creamy Corn, Spinach Tomato Feta, and more. No vegan or GF options explicitly identified

restaurant.name: Little Tokyo Sushi
restaurant.desc: Little Tokyo is a Japanese restaurant in North Vancouver's Chadwick Court, specializing in sushi and Japanese cuisine. They offer online ordering for individual items and can prepare party trays for larger groups with advance notice by phone. It's a compact, takeout-oriented spot convenient for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Sushi Bella
restaurant.desc: Sushi Bella is a French-Japanese fusion restaurant established on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver in 2010, blending traditional Japanese technique with West Coast and French influences. The menu goes well beyond sushi to include chicken dishes, gyoza, calamari, and crab cakes, making it a welcoming stop for riders who aren't sushi fans. Takeout and delivery via Skip the Dishes are available, offering flexibility for cyclists who want to eat on the go.

detail.address: 152 Lonsdale Avenue, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2E8

restaurant.name: Bubble Waffle Cafe
restaurant.desc: Bubble Waffle Cafe is a Hong Kong-style street food restaurant specialising in egg waffles (雞蛋仔), fish soup noodle combos, curry fish balls, rice noodle rolls, and a wide range of Asian bubble-tea and fruit drinks. It is part of a small Lower Mainland chain with locations in Richmond and West Vancouver, with this branch on Blundell Road serving the residential south Richmond area. Online and app-based ordering is available alongside counter service.

restaurant.name: The Lazy Gecko
restaurant.desc: The Lazy Gecko is a Mexican restaurant in Sooke's Seabreeze Business Centre, billing itself as serving the 'Largest Burritos on the Island.' It sits on Sooke Road — the main cycling corridor connecting Greater Victoria to the southern tip of Vancouver Island — making it a natural meal stop for touring cyclists passing through Sooke. The restaurant also operates a bar.

restaurant.name: Down Low Chicken
restaurant.desc: A multi-location fried chicken fast food restaurant with locations across Vancouver and Toronto. The UBC-area location offers takeaway service and quick meal options for touring cyclists passing through the neighborhood.

restaurant.name: Grounds For Coffee
restaurant.desc: Grounds For Coffee is a Vancouver institution founded in 1993, best known for its hand-made cinnamon buns crafted daily from locally-sourced, preservative-free ingredients. Beyond baked goods, the cafe serves premium organic coffee, savory wraps, calzones, breakfast buns, and rotating vegan and gluten-free options, making it a genuine refueling stop rather than just a pastry shop. The Alma Street flagship sits in the Point Grey/Kitsilano neighborhood and has been a neighborhood anchor for over three decades.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Bakery page states: 'VEGAN, VEGETARIAN & GLUTEN-FREE — It's important to us to provide options for everyone'; rotating vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free baked goods plus vegan/veggie wraps and vegan cheese buns listed

restaurant.name: Roy's Indian
restaurant.desc: Roy's Indian is a family-run restaurant in Tsawwassen operated by Roy and Lopa, who previously ran the Atithi restaurant on Burrard Street in Vancouver for nine years. The menu features traditional Indian dishes including Butter Chicken, Bengali Samosas, Lamb Roganjosh, and several vegan options, with catering services also available. Tsawwassen receives roughly 40% less rain than downtown Vancouver, making it a pleasant stop on a coastal cycling route.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu lists 'Aloo Gobi (Vegan)' and 'Dal Makhani (Vegan)'

restaurant.name: The Captain's Boil
restaurant.desc: The Captain's Boil is a Cajun-style seafood boil franchise restaurant on Kingsway in Vancouver, where diners choose their catch, sauce flavour, and heat level for a hands-on, communal feast experience. Part of a growing Canadian chain with locations across BC, Alberta, Manitoba, and Ontario, this location offers indoor seating and accepts cash, credit, and debit. It is a sit-down seafood destination rather than a quick-stop cyclist café.

restaurant.name: ASA Sushi
restaurant.desc: ASA Sushi (also branded as Asa Japanese Raw Bar & Kitchen) has been a fixture in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood since 1996, serving classic nigiri, sashimi, and rolls alongside its own creative Canadian-influenced house creations. All dishes are made to order with fresh ingredients, and the restaurant offers online ordering with in-store pickup, a practical option for cyclists who want a quick meal without a long wait.

restaurant.name: Garry Point Grill & Fish 'N' Chips
restaurant.desc: Garry Point Grill and Fish & Chips is a casual seafood counter in the heart of historic Steveston Village, steps from Garry Point Park and the Fraser River waterfront — a natural pause point on Richmond's popular cycling routes. The menu centres on hand-battered fish and chips made with locally caught wild cod, salmon, and halibut, alongside burgers and a dedicated vegan section. Outdoor seating and a relaxed neighbourhood feel make it a welcoming rest stop for cyclists exploring the Steveston area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page explicitly labels multiple items vegan: Garden Veggie Burger (Vegan), Falafel Wrap, Teriyaki Cauliflower, Vegan Ckun Strips & Fries, BC Local Plant Based Smoothies (vegan), Organic Frozen Fruit Bars (Vegan). No GF options mentioned

restaurant.name: Palisades Cafe
restaurant.desc: Palisades Cafe is a community-focused cafe in Houston, BC, situated just off the Highway 16 corridor — a key artery for touring cyclists crossing northern BC on the Yellowhead route. Founded by Liz Watson, it serves ethically sourced locally roasted coffee and espresso, fresh daily lunch specials, homemade soups and salads, and a wide selection of gluten-free and vegan baked goods. The cafe doubles as a cultural hub hosting arts initiatives and community events, and also operates a mobile Cafe Cruiser for off-site catering.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'We specialize in offering an abundance of gluten free and vegan treats'; About page adds 'Finding Gluten Free and Vegan options in small communities can be challenging - but not anymore for Houston.'

restaurant.name: Midam Cafe
restaurant.desc: Midam Cafe is a restaurant located on West Broadway in Vancouver. The business website could not be accessed during enrichment, limiting available information about its cuisine and amenities.

restaurant.name: Icy Bar
restaurant.desc: Icy Bar is a Taiwanese-style dessert shop on the Kingsway corridor in Vancouver, specializing in shaved ice in a wide range of fruit and flavored combinations alongside drinks like milk tea and grass jelly. The menu also includes hot desserts, pancakes, honey toast, and snacks, making it a broad sweet-focused stop. Online ordering is available for quick pickup or delivery.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: This McDonald's at Market Crossing is a full-service fast food location offering dine-in and drive-through service with the complete Canadian McDonald's menu including burgers, chicken, and McCafé beverages. Indoor seating provides a sheltered rest stop for cyclists passing through the commercial area, and the menu includes vegetarian and limited vegan options. It functions as a practical food resupply point on routes through the greater Vancouver area.

restaurant.name: Sushi Field
restaurant.desc: Sushi Field is a casual Japanese restaurant located in Fairfield Plaza in Victoria, offering dine-in and takeout. The restaurant emphasizes premium ingredients and chef precision in every piece of sushi. It also offers catering, making it a potential option for group cycling events.

restaurant.name: Dell Lanes
restaurant.desc: Dell Lanes is a bowling alley with an on-site restaurant located on King George Boulevard in Surrey. As a combined bowling and dining venue, it likely offers a full food and beverage service alongside its lanes. Touring cyclists passing through Surrey would find it a distinctive stop for a meal or snack.

restaurant.name: Birdies
restaurant.desc: Birdies is a California-inspired, casually elevated restaurant in Burnaby known for its diverse menu of tacos, handcrafted pizzas, sushi handrolls, and steaks alongside vibrant cocktails. The kitchen clearly labels gluten-aware, plant-based, and vegetarian options throughout the menu, and a provisions fridge stocks ready-made items for take-home. The restaurant features an epic outdoor patio and free on-site parking, making it a convenient stop on Lougheed Highway.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels items as 'Vegetarian', 'Plant-based', and 'Gluten Aware' throughout

restaurant.name: ATLAS Steak + Fish
restaurant.desc: ATLAS Steak + Fish is a modern, upscale steakhouse chain located inside Cascades Casino Kamloops, offering a casually-elegant take on the classic North American steakhouse with seafood, steaks, and craft cocktails. Part of Gateway Casinos' restaurant group, the Kamloops location welcomes minors and operates as a destination dining venue with table-side service and globally-inspired cuisine. Touring cyclists looking for a sit-down dinner will find it on Versatile Drive in a casino complex with full-service dining and takeout.

restaurant.name: Pelican Rouge
restaurant.desc: Pelican Rouge Cafe is a White Rock coffee shop serving drinks and food under the Pelican Rouge brand, which claims over 150 years of European coffee craftsmanship. The café offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a comfortable stop in the South Surrey area. Online ordering is available for takeout pickup.

detail.address: 15142 North Bluff Road, White Rock, BC V4B 5M1

restaurant.name: Taco Bell
restaurant.desc: A Taco Bell fast-food location on Granville Street in Vancouver serving Tex-Mex staples including tacos, burritos, and Crunchwrap Supremes. The restaurant offers indoor seating with air conditioning, making it a reasonable stop for cyclists needing a quick, filling meal in a busy urban corridor. A dedicated vegetarian menu is available alongside the standard lineup.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists a 'Veggie Cravings Menu' with items such as the Cheesy Bean and Rice Burrito described as 'indulgent vegetarian items.'

restaurant.name: YOTEA
restaurant.desc: YOTEA is a modern fruit-tea brand founded in Shenzhen in 2014, credited as the originator of the 'Square Cup Fruit Tea,' now operating its first British Columbia location inside Richmond's Continental Shopping Centre. The menu features signature fruit teas with fresh-cut fruit, lemon teas made with air-flown fragrant lemons from Guangdong, fresh fruit slushes, and cold-pressed juices served in the brand's distinctive hedgehog-branded bottles. Cycling through Richmond's south end, a rider could stop here for a cold, fruit-forward drink rather than a full meal.

restaurant.name: Shirley Delicious Cafe
restaurant.desc: Shirley Delicious is a celebrated little cafe tucked in the rainforest on the Pacific Marine Circle Route, roughly 20 minutes west of Sooke on western Vancouver Island. Everything on the menu is made in-house — from housemade focaccia and butter croissants to brunch plates and daily soups — served alongside Fernwood Coffee and local artisan teas and kombuchas. Rated 13th overall in Canada by Yelp (the highest-ranking eatery on Vancouver Island), it draws cyclists and adventurers looking for a genuine quality stop amid the wilderness.

detail.address: 2794 Sheringham Point Road, Shirley, BC, V9Z 1G4

restaurant.name: Delight Street Eats
restaurant.desc: Delight Street Eats is an Indian street food restaurant in Delta serving an extensive menu of chaat, biryani, thalis, and Asian fusion items from breakfast through late night. The kitchen accommodates vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, and nut-free diets with menu filters available on their online ordering platform. Dine-in, pickup, and delivery within 15 km are all supported.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu filter options on website include Vegetarian, Vegan, Gluten Free, Dairy Free, and Nut Free

restaurant.name: Mükasi Coffee Roasters
restaurant.desc: Mükasi Coffee Roasters is a specialty coffee roaster based in Chilliwack offering a curated selection of single-origin beans from Ethiopia, Guatemala, Honduras, Vietnam, and beyond, alongside carefully crafted house blends. The business is notably focused on traceability and quality, providing detailed sourcing and cupping notes for each coffee. A touring cyclist stopping in can explore an independently operated roaster with an e-commerce presence and local delivery, rather than a conventional chain café.

detail.address: 32900 South Fraser Way, Unit 303, Chilliwack, BC V2S 5A1

restaurant.name: Pomodoro Pizza
restaurant.desc: Pomodoro Pizza is a Port Coquitlam pizzeria specialising in hand-made dough prepared fresh in-house daily. The restaurant offers both pick-up and delivery, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Oxford Street area. Online ordering is available through their website.

detail.address: 3-2850 Oxford Street Port Coquitlam, BC V3B 5L7

restaurant.name: Pho 101
restaurant.desc: Pho 101 is a Vietnamese restaurant and bubble tea spot on the Hastings Street corridor, serving pho and other Vietnamese dishes alongside bubble tea drinks. The combination of hearty noodle soups and refreshing bubble teas makes it a practical refuelling stop for a cyclist. Its location on Hastings Street places it along a busy arterial route through the Burnaby area.

restaurant.name: Cofu Pressed Sushi
restaurant.desc: COFU Pressed Sushi is a 100% plant-based pressed sushi restaurant near the entrance to Granville Island, founded by Akiko Otsuka and open since fall 2021. The menu features inventive vegan interpretations of sushi classics — jackfruit tuna and konjac salmon — with a near-zero food waste philosophy and eco-friendly, recyclable packaging. The restaurant is alcohol-free and encourages guests to bring their own containers for takeout.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'ORDER LAST ORDER AT 8:30 P.M FOR DINE-IN & TAKEOUT'; also offers pick-up and delivery via Uber Eats and SkipTheDishes
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'ALL Plant-Based'. Entirely vegan menu

restaurant.name: Sunshine Woods Golf Centre
restaurant.desc: Sunshine Woods Golf Centre is a golf facility with a clubhouse restaurant in Tsawwassen offering Chinese and burger cuisine. Public accessibility and amenities could not be verified due to website unavailability.

restaurant.name: Yummy Slice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Yummy Slice Pizza is a fast-food pizza shop on Scott Road in Delta, BC. It sits along a busy suburban corridor that connects to regional cycling routes through Surrey and Delta.

restaurant.name: Nomad
restaurant.desc: Nomad is an eco-conscious espresso bar, café, and bakery that operates as a proudly 100% single-use cup-free shop—customers bring their own tumbler, use an on-site ceramic mug, or rent a sustainably 3D-printed clay cup made from clay, salt, and water. Founded by Annette Kim, whose earlier North Vancouver café reduced landfill waste by 95%, Nomad has collectively diverted over 250,000 single-use cups from landfills since 2022. The Kitsilano location opened in early 2026, bringing this zero-waste coffee culture to a neighbourhood popular with cyclists riding the waterfront and nearby routes.

restaurant.name: Olivier's la Boulangerie
restaurant.desc: Olivier's la Boulangerie is an artisan French bakery and café founded in 2009 by Olivier Audibert, a baker from southern France, and is the original 'main bakery' location of what has grown into a small multi-location chain. The shop is distinguished by its commitment to traditional long-fermentation ('slow-crafted') methods using no chemical preservatives, GMO grains, or high-gluten additives — a genuine taste-of-France pit stop in the Coquitlam area. Cyclists can pick up freshly baked breads, croissants, and pastries, and the café space can also be reserved for private events.

detail.address: 12 King Edward St #101, Coquitlam, BC V3K 0E7

restaurant.name: West Village Cafe
restaurant.desc: West Village Café is a community-focused café in South Surrey that emphasizes natural, locally sourced ingredients — drawing on BC suppliers like Evergreen Herbs, 63 Acres, and Terra Breads to produce organic coffee drinks, fresh-pressed juices, handcrafted salads, nourishing bowls, and daily baked pies. The interior is designed for comfortable lingering, with a communal island counter, cozy couches with marble tables, and plug-in stations for devices. Delivery is available through Skip the Dishes, Uber Eats, and DoorDash for cyclists who prefer to order ahead.

notes.Device charging: About page states the Communal Island Counter has plug-ins: 'Plug in the phone or tablet, and recharge for getting back to work + school.'

restaurant.name: The Broken Seal
restaurant.desc: The Broken Seal is a waterfront bar and restaurant in Squamish, situated on the waterfront side of a building facing Howe Sound and the Stawamus Chief. It serves an eclectic Japanese-French-Peruvian small plates menu alongside a craft cocktail program led by an award-winning bar team, using locally sourced ingredients from the Sea to Sky corridor. With capacity for up to 80 guests and a seasonal menu that rotates twice a year, it bills itself as Squamish's new favourite waterfront hangout.

restaurant.name: holsem
restaurant.desc: holsem is listed in OpenStreetMap as a cafe in Madeira Park, BC. The business maintains an online shopping presence, though the website provides minimal information about physical location, operations, or amenities available to customers.

detail.address: 12808 Madeira Park Road, Madeira Park, V0N 2H0

restaurant.name: Boston Pizza
restaurant.desc: Boston Pizza is a well-established Canadian casual dining chain and sports bar with a long history rooted in BC, first franchised in Penticton in 1968. The Chilliwack location on Luckakuck Way offers a full dine-in restaurant experience alongside takeout and delivery, with an extensive menu spanning pizza, pasta, wings, burgers, and more. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a familiar, reliable sit-down meal option with broad menu variety in a suburban commercial area of Chilliwack.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu page states 'Vegan and Glutenwise® options also available'; nutritional info page lists a dedicated GlutenWise® menu category

restaurant.name: Raku Japanese Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Raku Japanese Kitchen is a sushi and Japanese cuisine restaurant situated on Marine Drive in West Vancouver, a route popular with cyclists traveling along the North Shore. The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating, providing a comfortable rest stop. Online ordering is available, suggesting a takeout option for cyclists on the go.

restaurant.name: Sushi Bar Shyun
restaurant.desc: Sushi Bar Shyun is a small, reservation-recommended Japanese restaurant in Port Coquitlam that has been crafting authentic sushi since 2004. The name 'Shyun' means 'in season,' reflecting the kitchen's commitment to local, fresh ingredients and limited-quantity seasonal fish imported directly from Japan. All sauces are house-made, and the menu spans traditional nigiri, sashimi, and maki including several vegetarian rolls.

notes.Takeout: Website temporary notice states 'We will not be able to... serve walk-ins (both dine and take out)' during a limited period, confirming that takeout is a normal part of operations
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels five maki items as 'Vegetarian': Oshinko (pickled radish), Ume-jiso (real plum), Kanpyo (home-made), Natto (real natto bean), and Kappa (cucumber)

restaurant.name: Cedar Café
restaurant.desc: Cafe MOA — listed on the museum's own website as 'Cedar Café' — is the in-house café at the Museum of Anthropology at UBC, one of Canada's foremost anthropological museums housed in an Arthur Erickson-designed building overlooking the Pacific. The café sits inside the museum, up the ramp from the admission desk, so a cyclist stopping here would be stepping into a world-class cultural institution. The site anchors the end of a scenic but demanding cycling route along NW Marine Drive.

restaurant.name: Canton Garden
restaurant.desc: Canton Garden is a family-owned Cantonese restaurant with more than 60 years of history in Chilliwack, originally operating out of the Royal Hotel before moving to its current location near Highway 1. The dining room seats up to 200 people and includes private banquet facilities at no extra room charge, making it an easy stop for large cycling groups. Takeout is readily available by phone, and the extensive menu spans classic Cantonese dishes alongside a full vegetarian section.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian Delight' section with Vegetarian Delight Chop Suey and Vegetarian Delight Fried Rice, plus multiple vegetarian lunch platters and combo options

restaurant.name: Social Crust Cafe & Catering
restaurant.desc: Social Crust Cafe & Catering is a social enterprise cafe in downtown Vancouver operated by Coast Mental Health, channeling revenue toward mental health programs and services. The cafe offers food and catering in the heart of the city's business district on West Pender Street. As of spring 2026 it expanded to seven-day-a-week service, making it more accessible to weekend riders passing through.

restaurant.name: Ironworks Café & Crêperie
restaurant.desc: Ironworks Café & Crêperie is a cozy downtown Nanaimo café founded in March 2018, specializing in made-from-scratch Belgian crêpes alongside locally roasted Italian coffee. It is part of a small Vancouver Island chain with locations in Duncan, Ladysmith, and seasonal Chemanius. The menu offers both sweet and savoury crêpes with a choice of original Belgian, gluten-free buckwheat, or whole-wheat vegan batter, making it a flexible stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists three batter choices: Original Belgian, Gluten-Free Buckwheat, and Whole Wheat Vegan. Many sweet and savoury crepes are marked as vegan-adaptable with substitutions and gluten-free capable; kitchen notes a cross-contamination risk for celiac guests

restaurant.name: Beaufort Pizza & Pasta
restaurant.desc: Beaufort Pizza & Pasta is a pizza and pasta restaurant in Nanaimo. Touring cyclists can stop here for a meal during their journey through the region. The restaurant provides dining services in a mid-sized BC community.

restaurant.name: Hong Kong House Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Hong Kong House Restaurant is a locally owned Nanaimo institution serving Szechuan, Cantonese, and Shanghai-style Chinese cuisine for over 17 years. It is best known for hosting what it bills as the biggest Chinese food buffet in Nanaimo, alongside a full dine-in menu and takeout or delivery service. All dishes are MSG-free and cooked in 100% vegetable oil, making it a solid refuelling stop for cyclists rolling through central Nanaimo near Country Club Centre.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists Vegetable Chow Mein, Vegetable Fried Rice, and other vegetable dishes; services page highlights 'vegetable dishes' among offerings

restaurant.name: Bella Pizza
restaurant.desc: Bella Pizza is a family-owned pizzeria that has operated since 1979, originally on Denman Street in Vancouver before relocating to its current Burnaby spot on Imperial Street. The kitchen specializes in stone-baked, hand-tossed Italian-style pizzas using house-made tomato sauce and premium cheeses, alongside pastas, subs, wings, and salads. The restaurant has earned Reader's Choice recognition from both Vancouver Magazine and The Georgia Straight over its decades in business.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: No GF evidence found

restaurant.name: Breakfast Table
restaurant.desc: Breakfast Table is a family-owned brunch restaurant in Steveston Village, Richmond, founded in 2016 by brothers-in-law George Koay and Michael Lee and known for weaving Asian flavour influences into classic comfort-food brunch dishes. The Steveston location is the brand's second spot, expanding from its original South Granville home in Vancouver. The restaurant operates on a first-come, first-served basis with a digital waitlist, and delivery is available via DoorDash.

restaurant.name: Tonkotsu Ramen Tsukiya
restaurant.desc: Tsukiya is a compact ramen shop on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, just steps from Stanley Park and the seawall cycling route. The restaurant specializes in house-made tonkotsu ramen featuring a rich pork bone broth and specially crafted chewy noodles. It operates on a walk-in-only basis with no reservations, making it an accessible spontaneous stop for cyclists exploring the area.

notes.Takeout: Website states: 'We take takeout orders in-store only, once the payment is received.' Phone takeout orders not accepted

restaurant.name: California Thai
restaurant.desc: California Thai is a Thai fusion chain offering dishes such as Pad Thai, curries, noodle soups, and fried rice across mall food-court locations. The brand is built around Thai culinary philosophy, emphasizing harmonious teamwork and rich fusion flavours. The chain's official website lists no British Columbia locations, making the existence of this Tsawwassen listing difficult to verify.

detail.address: 5000 Canoe Pass Way, Unit FC-12, Tsawwassen Mills, Delta, BC V4M 0B3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian dishes including Mixed Vegetables, Zucchini Mix, Eggplant Tofu, Mango Salad, and Green Beans

restaurant.name: AfterThoughts
restaurant.desc: Afterthoughts is a family-owned gourmet dessert restaurant and café that has been baking in-house since 1994, known for cheesecakes, pies, cakes, and rotating seasonal treats made entirely from scratch on-site. Beyond desserts, it serves freshly made sandwiches, wraps, salads, soups, and quiches alongside specialty café beverages featuring locally roasted coffee. The modern space at Central Park Village in Abbotsford features a heated patio and a private party and meeting room.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We bring in gluten-free treats for our celiac guests' and references 'gluten-free choices for our celiac and gluten' patrons; also mentions Keto treats

restaurant.name: Papa John's
restaurant.desc: Papa John's is a national pizza chain operating a delivery and carryout location on Kingsway in Vancouver's East Side. The store focuses on pizza, breadsticks, and wings for takeout or delivery, with no dine-in component. Cyclists passing through the area can pick up a carryout order without a sit-down stop.

restaurant.name: iDen & Quanjude
restaurant.desc: iDen & Quanjude is a Beijing Duck House restaurant established in 1864, specializing in authentic Beijing-style Chinese cuisine. Located on Cambie Street in Vancouver with indoor seating and on-site wheelchair-accessible washrooms, it provides a full-service dining option for touring cyclists seeking substantial meals.

restaurant.name: Baskin-Robbins
restaurant.desc: Baskin-Robbins is a large international hard-scoop ice cream chain with nearly 8,000 stores across 50 countries, offering an extensive rotating menu of ice cream flavours, cakes, sundaes, and frozen beverages. This Surrey location sits on Fraser Highway and is part of the Canadian franchise network. The brand has introduced dairy-free, plant-based options alongside its classic lineup.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website confirms dairy-free, plant-based vegan ice cream (Chocolate Extreme) was rolled out as a pilot program in Canada (May 2020). All ice creams except Rocky Road and Maple Walnut are Kosher per FAQ

restaurant.name: Me-n-Ed's
restaurant.desc: Me-n-Ed's is a proudly Canadian-owned pizza parlour chain operating in the Lower Mainland since 1969, known for specialty and classic pizzas made with fresh ingredients. This Kingsway location is one of five family-operated restaurants and serves local BC craft beers on tap alongside its full pizza menu. A touring cyclist looking for a filling sit-down meal or a quick takeout order on a busy arterial route will find a reliable, long-established stop here.

restaurant.name: HY's Steakhouse
restaurant.desc: Hy's Steakhouse & Cocktail Bar is one of Canada's oldest and most storied steakhouse brands, founded in Calgary in 1955 and now anchoring a prime block of Hornby Street in downtown Vancouver. The two-storey restaurant is known for its dark mahogany interiors, tableside service theatre, and Canada Prime Grade beef. It sits in the heart of the downtown core, making it a recognizable landmark for cyclists navigating the Hornby Street bike corridor.

restaurant.name: Starbucks

restaurant.name: Khan Sahab Kitchen

Steveston Village is a popular cycling destination on the Lower Mainland's extensive bike network, making this a naturally convenient dining stop for touring cyclists.
