restaurant.desc: K Ramyun is a Korean fast-food spot serving ramyun (Korean-style ramen noodles). The '_sfu' in its Instagram handle suggests a student-adjacent location. A touring cyclist passing through the area would find it a quick stop for a hot noodle meal.

restaurant.name: Perfecto
restaurant.desc: Perfecto is an artisan cafe on Robson Street in Vancouver that produces all its pastries, cakes, sandwiches, and gelato from scratch daily in a central kitchen using quality ingredients. The cafe uses a custom coffee blend developed exclusively with Agro Roasters, and its gelato is crafted by a Maestro trained at the Carpigiani Gelato University in Italy. It is one of four Perfecto locations across Vancouver and Burnaby, making it a recognizable and reliable stop along a popular urban cycling corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists a 'Gluten-Friendly Apple Muffin', confirming at least one gluten-friendly option

restaurant.name: Kyle's Cafe
restaurant.desc: Chinese restaurant on Commercial Drive with both indoor and outdoor seating. Offers casual dining suitable for a meal break on a Vancouver cycling tour.

restaurant.name: Red Swan Pizza
restaurant.desc: Red Swan Pizza is a Canadian-owned pizza franchise founded in Saskatchewan in 1993 and now operating 160+ locations across six provinces. The Langley location offers fresh, made-from-scratch gourmet pizza available for pickup or delivery, with a full menu of pizzas, pastas, salads, wings, and desserts. Catering services are also available, making it a practical stop for groups or events along a cycling route.

restaurant.name: Szechuan Delicious Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Szechuan Delicious Restaurant is a Szechuan Chinese restaurant on Alexandra Road in Richmond, BC. Located in a commercial unit, it provides a dining option for cyclists and other customers in the area.

restaurant.name: Panago
restaurant.desc: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain that prides itself on using 100% Canadian wheat dough made fresh in-house and organic tomato sauce, with most meats raised without antibiotics. This North Vancouver location operates as takeout-only with no indoor or outdoor seating, making it a grab-and-go stop for hungry cyclists. The menu includes pizzas, salads, sides, and a range of plant-based and dairy-free options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We've got abundant veggie, dairy-free and meat-free choices to help you live your best plant life.'

restaurant.name: Pho Khanh Express
restaurant.desc: Khanh Express is a family-founded Vietnamese restaurant on East Hastings Street serving traditional and contemporary noodle soups — pho, vermicelli, banh mi, and satay — made with rich broths and fresh ingredients. The restaurant is the owner's heartfelt tribute to their father's love of noodle soup, aiming for a cozy, welcoming atmosphere. It is one of two Vancouver locations and offers online ordering and a digital loyalty program.

detail.address: 987 East Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 0H1

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists 'Vegetarian' as a distinct menu category alongside Pho, Vermicelli, Banh Mi, etc

restaurant.name: Pizza 64
restaurant.desc: Pizza 64 is a Canadian pizza chain that has operated since 2010, with 20+ British Columbia locations making fresh dough and sauce on-site at each franchise. The Abbotsford location offers a broad menu of specialty, signature, and gourmet pizzas alongside wings, pasta, and sides. Takeout and delivery are available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Bourquin Crescent area.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian pizzas: Garden Fresh (vegetables, no meat), Pesto Veggie (garlic, spinach, onions, green peppers, tomatoes), Passion of India and Shahi Paneer (tandoori paneer). No vegan or GF options confirmed

restaurant.name: Mekong
restaurant.desc: Mekong is a Southeast Asian restaurant in Whistler's Creekside Village, helmed by Bangkok-born Executive Chef Bonnie Khummuang and Culinary Director Angus An — Vancouver Magazine's Chef of the Year 2025. The menu is built around sharing: small plates, aromatic noodles, wok-fired dishes, and inventive desserts, paired with a creative cocktail program. A touring cyclist looking for a flavour-forward sit-down dinner near the Creekside base will find this a memorable post-ride stop.

detail.address: 204-2067 Lake Placid Rd, Whistler, BC V8E 0B6

restaurant.name: Szechuan Cuisine
restaurant.desc: Szechuan Cuisine is a Chinese restaurant on Kingsway in Burnaby specializing in the bold, spicy flavours of Sichuan cooking. Located on a busy arterial road, it offers indoor seating and is accessible to cyclists riding through the Burnaby corridor. No website content specific to the restaurant was retrievable to add further detail.

restaurant.name: Take Out Shack
restaurant.desc: Take Out Shack is a small, independent fast-food counter in Vancouver's Gastown area specializing in smash burgers built around a playful comic-book theme centred on their mascot, Captain Sizzle. The menu spans beef and crispy chicken smash burgers, milkshakes, poutine-style burgers, and classic sides. A gluten-free bun substitution and no-charge lettuce-wrap option broaden accessibility for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website menu header explicitly lists 'Sub Gluten free bun' and 'Sub lettuce wrap at no charge'; vegetarian or vegan options are not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: Delta Pizza
restaurant.desc: Delta Pizza is a vegetarian-only pizza restaurant in Surrey operating under the tagline 'Think Vegetarian.' The menu leans heavily on South Asian-inspired flavours, with options like Veggie-Paneer, Punjabi-Style Veggie, and Roasted Garlic Paneer alongside more familiar western pies. It is a takeout-focused spot that accepts cash and debit only.

notes.Takeout: Website states 'Take outs daily from 11 AM to 11 PM'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Entire menu is vegetarian ('Think Vegetarian' tagline); gluten-free crust available upon request per website

restaurant.name: Observatory Wines
restaurant.desc: Observatory Wines is a boutique estate winery perched 400 metres above Okanagan Lake near Summerland, with panoramic views stretching north to Peachland and south toward Naramata. Winemaker and owner Blair Gillingham specializes in Grüner Veltliner, shaped by years working in Austria, alongside small-production estate wines from the east-facing lakefront vineyard. Drop-in tastings are welcome for small groups, making it a natural scenic stop along the southern Okanagan cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Woody's on Brunette
restaurant.desc: Woody's is a well-established neighbourhood pub in Coquitlam that has been serving the community since 1932. It is best known for its extensive tap selection — over 30 beers including 15 rotating BC craft beers — and its famously inexpensive wings. An attached liquor store and cannabis shop operate on the same premises, making it a one-stop destination on Brunette Avenue.

restaurant.name: Royston Roasting Company
restaurant.desc: Royston Roasting Company is a coffee shop in the small Vancouver Island community of Royston, situated on the South Island Highway — a key corridor for cycle tourists riding the island's eastern coast. The shop operates out of its own building and accepts both cash and credit cards, making it a convenient stop for riders. It is closed Sundays and public holidays.

restaurant.name: Village Idiot
restaurant.desc: The Village Idiot Bar & Grill is a casual, après-themed restaurant and bar in the heart of Revelstoke, widely regarded as a local favourite and known globally for its made-to-order pizzas. The menu spans burgers, poutine, mussels, and signature cocktails, with an emphasis on housemade sauces, soups, and dressings. The patio and relaxed atmosphere make it a natural stop for visitors winding down after a day on the road or trails.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu items explicitly labelled (Veg), (Vegan), and (GF) throughout; About page states 'a large variety of quality gluten and dairy free items to choose from.'

restaurant.name: Renaissance Coffee
restaurant.desc: Renaissance Coffee has been a fixture of Simon Fraser University's Burnaby Mountain campus for over 20 years, run by Parminder and his team from the AQ 3000 level of the Academic Quadrangle. It serves Fair Trade espresso beverages, brewed coffee, wholesome meals, and desserts to the SFU community. The venue is takeout-only with no outdoor seating, making it a quick-stop option for cyclists passing through the SFU campus on weekdays.

restaurant.name: Laleh Bakery
restaurant.desc: Laleh Bakery is a Persian pastry shop on North Vancouver's Lonsdale Avenue with over 30 years of experience producing traditional sweets such as baklava, saffron-infused cookies, and crispy zaban puff pastry. The bakery also hand-crafts fresh daily roulades and custom celebration cakes, making it a distinctive and aromatic stop on a North Shore cycling route. Indoor seating is available and both credit and debit cards are accepted.

detail.address: 2041 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2K4

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: McDonald's is a globally recognized fast-food chain offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, wraps, breakfast items, and McCafé coffee beverages. This North Vancouver location on Lougheed Highway includes drive-through and takeout service. It sits along a major arterial corridor that touring cyclists may pass through when navigating the North Shore.

restaurant.name: Sidney Bakery
restaurant.desc: Sidney Bakery is a landmark family-owned institution on Beacon Ave in the heart of Sidney, established in 1903 and in the same family for over 70 years. Famous locally for gooey cinnamon rolls, powdered donuts, butter croissants, and sausage rolls, it uses recipes unchanged since 1944. Cyclists passing through Sidney on Vancouver Island will find a well-stocked range of breads, pastries, sandwiches, and sweets available for pickup or online pre-order.

restaurant.name: Café Gloucester
restaurant.desc: Café Gloucester is a Hong Kong-style Chinese café serving breakfast and all-day menus, with roots in Vancouver's Cambie Street and a newer Richmond location on Alexandra Road. The Richmond outpost offers dine-in alongside online delivery ordering, making it a convenient stop in the heart of Richmond's restaurant district.

restaurant.name: Domino's
restaurant.desc: Domino's Pizza is a well-known Canadian pizza chain franchise operating out of a retail unit on McMillan Road in Abbotsford. The store offers both delivery and carryout orders, making it a convenient calorie stop for cyclists passing through the area. A broad menu of pizzas, sides, and drinks is available.

detail.address: 2618 McMillan Road, Unit 104, Abbotsford, BC V3G 1C4

restaurant.name: PIzza Pi
restaurant.desc: Pizza 314PIE (listed in OSM as PIzza Pi) is a locally owned pizza restaurant in Kamloops, BC, with a playful mathematical branding theme built around the number π. The menu stretches beyond pizza to include items like falafel bites and homestyle mac and cheese, giving touring cyclists a range of quick, filling options. Online ordering is prominently featured, making it easy to have a meal ready on arrival.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Falafel Bites listed as a featured menu item, indicating at least vegetarian options are available

restaurant.name: Desi Turka
restaurant.desc: Desi Turka is an Indian restaurant located in Burnaby's 6th Street corridor. It offers indoor, smoke-free dining in a sit-down setting. Touring cyclists looking for a South Asian meal in Burnaby's central neighbourhoods would find it a convenient stop.

restaurant.name: i cafe express
restaurant.desc: iCafe Express is a modern Hong Kong-style café inside City Square Shopping Centre on West 12th Avenue, serving a fusion of traditional and contemporary fast food dishes. The kitchen is led by a chef with over 30 years of experience in authentic Hong Kong cuisine, offering both quick counter-service meals and catering for corporate and private events. It is well-positioned for cyclists navigating the Broadway corridor, with multiple ordering options including in-store pickup with no delivery fees.

notes.Takeout: Website promotes in-store pickup via Clover (no fee), plus delivery via DoorDash and UberEats; 'Order online and pick up your meal hassle-free!'

restaurant.name: Jam Cafe
restaurant.desc: Jam Cafe is a family-owned West Coast breakfast and brunch cafe that began in Victoria in 2012 and expanded to North Vancouver's Lonsdale neighbourhood in 2023. The cafe is known for its rustic vintage decor and Southern-inspired comfort dishes like Fried Chicken French Toast and fluffy three-stack pancakes made with locally sourced ingredients. The Lonsdale location is the chain's newest outpost and accepts reservations on weekdays, making it a sit-down stop well-suited for a mid-ride meal.

detail.address: 110 – 100 1st Street E., North Vancouver, BC V7L 1B1

restaurant.name: Kinemi's Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Kinemi's Kitchen is a small, family-run eatery tucked away in Vancouver's Champlain Heights neighbourhood, serving an inventive Japanese-style Italian menu of house pastas, pizza, and daily specials. The restaurant prides itself on fresh, quality ingredients and operates on a cash-only, no-reservations basis, giving it a distinctly local, unhurried character. For a touring cyclist, it's a low-key spot to refuel with a hearty pasta or seafood linguine in a quiet residential corner of Vancouver.

notes.Takeout: Website header states 'Offering Take Out Options Only'

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: This independently owned Subway franchise in Burnaby's Royal Oak neighbourhood offers freshly made sandwiches, wraps, salads, and breakfast items to order. The location supports in-restaurant dining, curbside pickup, and delivery, making it a convenient stop for a quick customizable meal. It accepts multiple payment methods including cash, and is part of the Subway Rewards loyalty program.

restaurant.name: Skewers Souvlaki Pita Bar
restaurant.desc: Skewers Souvlaki Pita Bar is an authentic Greek restaurant in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighborhood, serving souvlaki wraps, platters, and fresh salads made with BC-farmed chicken and pork and New Zealand lamb sirloin marinated in-house for twelve hours. Located on Powell Street near the waterfront, it is a convenient and filling stop for cyclists passing through the city core. Online ordering and pickup are available for those who want to grab a hearty meal on the go.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes vegetarian options: Halloumi Cheese wrap, Mixed Salad with Feta, Greek Salad, and Cretan Salad. No explicit vegan or gluten-free claims found

restaurant.name: Bobadog Bubble Tea & Hot Dogs
restaurant.desc: Bobadog is a Victoria counter-service spot with an inventive fusion menu pairing Asian-inspired hot dogs — topped with kimchi, Japanese BBQ sauce, pineapple salsa, or imitation crab — alongside a large selection of bubble teas, sparkling boba, and fruit teas. The eclectic combination makes it a distinctive quick-stop for cyclists passing through downtown Victoria. The compact format and varied drink menu suit a mid-ride refuel.

restaurant.name: Dairy Queen
restaurant.desc: Dairy Queen fast food restaurant serving ice cream and burgers. Offers indoor and outdoor seating for dining.

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: A Starbucks Coffee location on Harvey Avenue in Kelowna, situated along one of the city's main commercial corridors. It offers the full range of Starbucks espresso drinks, Refreshers, and food items including sandwiches. Outdoor seating is available according to OSM tags, making it a potential rest stop for cyclists passing through.

restaurant.name: Kuma Sushi
restaurant.desc: Kuma Sushi is the sushi arm of Jack's Place, a casual full-service patio restaurant situated at Bear Mountain resort in Langford. The combined venue offers an unusually eclectic menu spanning hand-rolled sushi, wood-fired pizza, pub appetizers, and craft cocktails — all available for lunch and dinner. Its resort-community setting and relaxed patio atmosphere make it a comfortable meal stop for cyclists exploring the Bear Mountain area.

detail.address: 2020 Country Club Way, Langford, BC V9B 6R3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Sushi menu lists avocado roll and tempura yam roll (both vegetarian); pizza menu includes Margherita and The G.O.A.T. (goat cheese, artichokes, tomatoes, spinach) as vegetarian options. Drink menu lists Whistler Forager GF beer as a gluten-free option

restaurant.name: Super Stars Cafe
restaurant.desc: Super Stars Cafe is a Hong Kong-style Chinese, Asian, and Thai restaurant with two Metro Vancouver locations, the Richmond outpost occupying a unit in a commercial plaza on Leslie Road. The menu leans toward Cantonese comfort food — baked pork chop rice, Portuguese beef brisket, dry-fried beef ho fun — alongside dim sum and Thai options. Online ordering with a 15-minute pickup window makes it a practical stop for cyclists passing through Richmond's food-heavy commercial corridors.

restaurant.name: Everything Wine
restaurant.desc: Everything Wine is a BC-based specialty wine and spirits retailer offering a broad selection of wines by region and varietal, beer, cider, and spirits. The North Vancouver location is part of a multi-store chain that also runs a wine club, corporate gifting, and event consultation services. Touring cyclists exploring the North Shore could stop here to pick up local BC wines or craft beverages for the road.

restaurant.name: Islands Bar
restaurant.desc: Islands Bar — branded on the website as Islands Patio & Lounge — is the casual outdoor bar and lounge at Harrison Hot Springs Resort & Spa. It serves a relaxed food menu alongside a wide selection of wine, beer, and specialty cocktails on a patio overlooking the resort grounds. For touring cyclists exploring the Harrison Hot Springs area, it offers a scenic spot to wind down after a ride.

restaurant.name: Masa Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Masa Sushi is a Japanese restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver, offering dine-in and online ordering. Located on a busy cycling corridor connecting the Kitsilano and South Granville neighbourhoods, it is a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the city. The restaurant's late-night hours make it a useful option after a long day on the road.

restaurant.name: Tetsu Sushi Bar
restaurant.desc: Tetsu Sushi Bar is a Michelin Guide-recommended omakase restaurant in Vancouver's West End, operated by Chef Satoshi Makise since 2017. With only 12 seats and a focus on Edomae-style nigiri made from fish sourced directly from Tokyo's Toyosu Market, it ranked 47th on Canada's 100 Best Restaurants list in 2022. A touring cyclist planning a special evening meal will find an intimate, chef-driven experience unlike anything else on the Denman Street corridor.

restaurant.name: Revolver
restaurant.desc: Revolver is a specialty coffee shop tucked into Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, operating under the Revolver Coffee Inc. brand with a physical café and a Canada-wide online bean shop. The café has produced branded collaborations — including handmade Vancouver ceramics and outdoor-gear partnerships — suggesting a strong local identity beyond the average coffee stop. Touring cyclists passing through Gastown's compact streets will find it a well-established independent spot for quality coffee.

restaurant.name: the Buffet
restaurant.desc: The Buffet is a full-service buffet restaurant inside Cascades Casino Delta, offering weekend brunch, themed dinner nights, and a rotating array of international specialties. It sits within a large casino-hotel complex that includes multiple dining venues, a spa, and conference facilities. As a destination buffet in a casino resort, it is well-suited for a hungry touring cyclist looking for a substantial all-you-can-eat meal.

restaurant.name: Kawawa Ramen
restaurant.desc: Kawawa is an all-you-can-eat Japanese restaurant located inside Metropolis at Metrotown, one of BC's largest shopping centres in central Burnaby. The restaurant offers an extensive menu spanning sushi, ramen, rolls, sashimi, tempura, and seasonal specials, with both à la carte and all-you-can-eat options in a roomy dining room. Its mall setting provides easy access to a full commercial hub, making it a substantial refuelling stop for cyclists riding the Kingsway corridor.

restaurant.name: Black Swan Pub
restaurant.desc: Black Swan Pub is a two-generation family-owned neighbourhood pub and liquor store nestled in the village of Shawnigan Lake on Vancouver Island. It offers a full English pub experience with a daily kitchen, weekly food specials, and an on-site liquor store with delivery service. As a long-standing community institution, it provides a welcoming sit-down meal option for touring cyclists passing through the Shawnigan Lake area.

detail.address: 2890 Shawnigan Lake Road, Shawnigan Lake, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Wednesday specials list a 'Veggie Cheeseburger with Fries, Soup or Garden Salad' as an explicit vegetarian option

restaurant.name: Beauregard Commons
restaurant.desc: Beauregard Commons is a café in Sidney, BC located on Verdier Avenue. It serves as a gathering space for locals and travelers seeking food and refreshment. Touring cyclists will find this a convenient stop when passing through the community.

restaurant.name: Keto Caveman
restaurant.desc: Caveman Cafe — branded 'King of Keto' — is a health-focused restaurant and keto/paleo/vegan bakery at its Tinseltown location in downtown Vancouver. The menu spans globally-inspired dishes including burritos, butter chicken, keto pizza, and grass-fed steaks, all made with whole-food ingredients and zero processed foods or refined sugar. It actively caters to a wide range of dietary protocols — keto, paleo, vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free — with generous, fully customizable portions.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists 'Many Vegetarian and Vegan Options – Plant-based entrees and raw-vegan dessert items that are Gluten-free and nutrient-dense'; menu filter covers paleo, vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free

restaurant.name: The Jade Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Jade Seafood Restaurant (玉庭軒) is an award-winning Cantonese dining destination in Richmond's commercial heart, recognized multiple times by the Chinese Restaurant Awards for both its cuisine and service. The restaurant offers dim sum, dinner, and take-out menus alongside banquet facilities with private rooms that can seat up to 20 tables. A touring cyclist arriving in Richmond's busy Number 3 Road corridor will find a full-service sit-down meal or a take-out option with a substantial menu rooted in authentic Cantonese seafood cooking.

detail.address: 2811 No. 3 Road, Unit 280, Richmond, BC V6X 2B2

restaurant.name: Pizzeria Antico
restaurant.desc: Pizzeria Antico is Whistler's only Neapolitan pizza restaurant, serving wood-fired pies alongside fresh house-made pastas, with all dough, sauces, fior di latte, ricotta, and bread made daily in-house. Located in the Apenglow Lodge on Main Street, it pours 18 BC craft beer taps and 8 BC wine taps, making it a strong showcase of local producers. A semi-private dining area accommodates larger groups, and the rustic casual setting suits post-ride refuelling.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegetarian options visible on both lunch and dinner menus: Margherita pizza (tomato, fior di latte, basil), Ortolana pizza (oven roasted mixed vegetables, fior di latte), Ruccola con Limone salad (arugula, lemon vinaigrette), and Monte Bianco pasta (oven roasted vegetables, tomato sauce, ricotta). No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Ferris'
restaurant.desc: Ferris' Burger & Oyster Bar has occupied the same corner on Yates Street in downtown Victoria since February 4, 1991, built on fresh-shucked Baynes Sound oysters sourced from the same waters for nearly four decades and hand-ground chuck burgers whose recipe has not changed since opening day. The brick-walled dining room crowned by a glass atrium seats up to 60 and carries an Ocean Wise seafood certification earned through decades of responsible sourcing, not marketing. It sits a ten-minute walk from the Inner Harbour and is served by multiple bus routes, making it a convenient mid-ride stop in the heart of the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists a Sunflower Seed Burger (house-made sunflower seed patty, special sauce, cheddar) and a Falafel with lemon feta and grilled naan as vegetarian options; GF-tagged items include Seafood Laksa GF and Steamed Shellfish & Fries GF; a GF Bun substitute is available on burgers for an upcharge

restaurant.name: Big Orange
restaurant.desc: Big Orange is a long-running bubble tea franchise whose first store opened at Burnaby's Metrotown Mall in 1996, now operating dozens of locations across Canada, the US, and Malaysia. The North Vancouver outlet serves fresh fruit bubble teas, ice cream bubble teas, waffles, and desserts, with takeout available. On a hot cycling day the fruit-based slushes and teas make it a plausible refreshment stop.

restaurant.name: Serious Coffee
restaurant.desc: Serious Coffee is a café situated on Beacon Avenue in Sidney, BC, a busy commercial street in a community that sees significant cycling traffic as a gateway to the Saanich Peninsula trail network. As a café-type establishment, it would likely offer the kinds of refreshments and rest opportunities that touring cyclists seek. No further detail about the business character or offerings can be confirmed from available evidence.

restaurant.name: Angry Vegan
restaurant.desc: Angry Vegan is a vegan-focused cafe located on Main Street in Penticton. It specializes in vegan and vegetarian cuisine. The downtown location provides a convenient dining option for touring cyclists.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: OSM confirms vegan and vegetarian options (). Gluten-free not specified

restaurant.name: Sushi Mura
restaurant.desc: Sushi Mura is a fast-growing Japanese sushi chain that has been operating in Vancouver since 2012, with this location in the River District neighbourhood. The restaurant features experienced sushi chefs preparing fresh-daily fish with secret recipes, offering both dine-in and takeout service. It is part of a multi-location franchise with seven branches across Metro Vancouver.

notes.Packed lunches: Corporate Lunch Program offering bento box orders for business lunch delivery
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items marked 'Veggie' including Veggie Wakame, Vegetable Sunomono, Veggie Ika Karage, and vegetable rolls

restaurant.name: Salt Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Salt Pizzeria is an artisanal pizzeria on Vancouver Island billing itself as BC's #1-rated pizza, building every pie on aged sourdough made from 100% organic flour with freshly sourced toppings. Beyond pizza they serve Salt Spring Island gelato, dairy-free sorbet, and in-house or to-go beer, wine, and cider. A 'half-baked' take-and-bake option lets touring cyclists pick up a pizza and finish it wherever they're staying.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ confirms vegetarian pizzas available; vegan options offered via two vegan cheese substitutes (crushed cashew/nutritional yeast blend or Violife Vegan Mozzarella). FAQ explicitly states no gluten-free options

restaurant.name: Kisha Poppo Japanese Resturant
restaurant.desc: Kisha Poppo is a Japanese all-you-can-eat buffet restaurant on Steveston Highway in Richmond, serving freshly prepared items with no time or item limits brought directly to the table. The restaurant offers both dine-in and takeout (with online ordering), plus delivery through Skip the Dishes and DoorDash. Located near the Steveston area cycling routes, it provides a substantial sit-down meal option for touring cyclists passing through Richmond.

restaurant.name: Big Wave Café1
restaurant.desc: Big Wave Cafe is a surf-themed espresso bar and breakfast café on Peninsula Road in Ucluelet, fueling visitors with locally roasted coffee and breakfast sandwiches and bowls made with island ingredients. Founded by chef Chris Bennett, it is positioned as a launching pad for days on the beach or trails, located next to Howler's Restaurant near the Petro-Can Gas Station. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a casual, welcoming atmosphere tailored to outdoor adventurers heading into Pacific Rim country.

notes.Takeout: Website offers an online menu and online ordering: 'Click to view the current seasonal menu or order online.'

restaurant.name: The Metropole Community Pub
restaurant.desc: The Metropole Community Pub — known locally as 'The Met' — is a casual neighbourhood bar in Vancouver's Gastown district, offering drink specials, food, pool, skeeball, and a ping pong table. The pub has been operating since at least 2017 and maintains an active social calendar including Super Bowl watch parties and New Year's events. Its Gastown location puts it within easy reach of the seawall and downtown cycling routes.

restaurant.name: Happy Lamb Hot Pot
restaurant.desc: Happy Lamb Hot Pot is a Canadian Mongolian-style hot pot chain with 11 locations, offering individual hot pots with a signature slow-simmered broth made from hens, beef bones, and 36 herbal ingredients including goji berries and ginseng. The Coquitlam location is a full sit-down restaurant with both all-you-can-eat and à la carte options, making it a solid stop for a substantial, warming meal. The chain has earned a strong following in the Lower Mainland for its broth quality and generous portions.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists vegetable section including Tofu, Tofu Platter, Yam Basket, and Celtuce as orderable items

restaurant.name: Gone Village Eatery
restaurant.desc: Gone Village Eatery is a fully licensed, locally owned cafe tucked behind Armchair Books in the heart of Whistler Village, reachable via two entrances — through the bookstore or from the adjacent car park. The kitchen emphasizes fresh, healthy meals built around locally baked breads, rotating homemade soups, and organic coffees, with menus that shift seasonally to draw on local producers. It has been recognized multiple times by Pique Newsmagazine as Whistler's best quick lunch spot.

restaurant.name: Catch 122
restaurant.desc: Catch 122 is a full-service restaurant in North Vancouver's Shipyards District (Lower Lonsdale), specializing in brunch, pastries, high tea, and dinner with a menu featuring house-made charcuterie, breads, and globally inspired dishes. The restaurant occupies an open dining room and bar space suited for both casual visits and private events for up to 80 guests. It is a notable destination on the North Shore waterfront for cyclists riding the lower Lonsdale area.

detail.address: 128 Carrie Cates Court, Shipyards District, North Vancouver

notes.Takeout: Website lists 'BREAKFAST TO GO (weekdays only 9-11am)' with items including a Chorizo Cheddar Milk Bread Sando and Ham & Cheese Croissant Sando
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple vegetarian items marked (V) across brunch and happy hour menus, including Cauliflower Benny, Brussels Sprouts, Flat Bread Margherita, and a Cauliflower taco option

restaurant.name: Hoduya
restaurant.desc: Hoduya is a bakery on Keefer Place in Vancouver with indoor seating and a smoke-free environment. It provides a convenient refreshment stop for cyclists in the area.

restaurant.name: Little Pisces Taiyaki & Soft Serve
restaurant.desc: Little Pisces is a Japanese-inspired dessert shop serving mochi-batter taiyaki — crispy on the outside, soft and chewy on the inside — alongside soft serve ice cream and specialty café drinks. The shop opened its first location in June 2024 on the second floor of a Lougheed-area plaza in Burnaby, with a rotating menu of creative flavors and a strong community following. A good stop for a sweet break, with pickup and delivery available.

detail.address: 4501 North Rd, Unit 202B, Burnaby, BC V3N 4R7

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Our dairy-free and vegan options are indicated on our menu. We usually have at least one vegan soft serve option. Most of our drinks can be made with oat milk upon request.'

restaurant.name: Rice Holic
restaurant.desc: Rice Holic is a specialty dessert stall inside the Admiralty Centre Food Court in Richmond, best known for its fresh Mango Mochi — daily hand-picked mangoes individually wrapped in soft, chewy mochi dough and produced in limited quantities each day. The business also operates a second stall at Empire Centre on Number 3 Road. Online pre-order for in-person pickup is the standard way to secure an order.

notes.Takeout: FAQ states 'All orders must be picked up at our location' — pickup/takeout only, no delivery offered

restaurant.name: The Salted Vine
restaurant.desc: The Salted Vine Kitchen + Bar occupies Squamish's oldest surviving building, a 1910 structure at the corner of Second and Victoria, outfitted with modern-country farmhouse décor of reclaimed poplar panels, grey teak tables, and custom-milled maple accents. The menu centres on sustainably sourced, seasonal Pacific Northwest ingredients—fresh daily oysters, BC salmon, handcrafted cocktails, and an extensive wine list—making it one of the most refined dining stops on the Sea-to-Sky corridor between Vancouver and Whistler. A 70-seat dining room and lounge is complemented by a 20-seat patio.

notes.Takeout: Website states: 'Take out and dine in available from 5:00-9:00pm Wednesday-Sunday.'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated Gluten Free Menu listed in site navigation; menu includes vegetarian items such as Pad Thai (tofu), House Greens, North Arm Farm Beet Salad, and Warm Olives

restaurant.name: The Block Eatery
restaurant.desc: The Block at Railtown is a breakfast-and-lunch eatery on Baker Street in Nelson's Railtown neighbourhood, built around comfort food with a French flair and an unwavering commitment to local, seasonal Kootenay-region ingredients. Every item on the menu — from crafted sandwiches and chowder to espresso drinks and fresh-baked cookies — is made from scratch using produce sourced directly from regional farmers. For a touring cyclist arriving in Nelson mid-morning, it offers a hearty, regionally rooted refuel in the centre of town.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes 'The Goddess' sandwich (vine-ripe tomatoes, living lettuce, smoked Gouda, basil mayo) — a meat-free option. No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Cora
restaurant.desc: Cora is a Canadian breakfast-and-lunch franchise chain known for colourful, fruit-laden plates, crêpes, waffles, and skillets. The Victoria location sits on Douglas Street in the downtown core, making it a convenient mid-ride fuel stop for cyclists passing through the city centre. The menu leans heavily toward morning fare served until mid-afternoon.

restaurant.name: Panda Pancakes & Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Panda Pancakes & Ice Cream serves pancakes and ice cream in Vancouver, providing casual dining suitable for touring cyclists looking to refuel or enjoy a dessert break.

restaurant.name: Firerock Lounge
restaurant.desc: The FireRock Lounge is a cozy upscale lounge inside the Westin Resort & Spa in Whistler Village, featuring a fireplace, two summer patios (one with mountain views, one a quiet courtyard), and creative small plates alongside BC wines, craft beers, and signature cocktails. It is part of the Gibbons Hospitality Group, a major operator of iconic Whistler Village venues. Touring cyclists finishing a mountain ride would find it a stylish spot to refuel with lunch, dinner, or après drinks in the heart of the village.

restaurant.name: Novo Pizzeria & Winery
restaurant.desc: Novo is a Kitsilano Italian pizzeria and wine bar serving authentic Neapolitan-style pizza baked in a solid brick oven, made with imported Caputo '00' flour and San Marzano tomatoes grown exclusively for the restaurant in the Naples countryside. House-made fresh pasta, antipasti, a full Italian wine list, and classic cocktails like Negroni and Aperol Spritz round out a substantial meal offering well-suited to cyclists finishing a ride along the nearby Burrard corridor or seawall. Takeout and delivery through Uber Eats and DoorDash provide flexibility for those who want to eat on the go.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels 'MARGHERITA (V)' as vegetarian; multiple salad, pasta (e.g. Spaghetti Pomodoro, Spaghetti Aglio e Olio), and antipasti items are also vegetarian. No explicit vegan or gluten-free designations found on the website

restaurant.name: Kings Links Clubhouse
restaurant.desc: Kings Links Clubhouse is the restaurant at Kings Links Golf Course, a seaside par-72 championship links course in Tsawwassen recognized by Golf Canada as one of Canada's best links-style courses. The clubhouse features a patio with spectacular views of the golf course, Coast Mountains, Mount Baker, and the Gulf Islands. The restaurant is explicitly open to the public, not just members or golfers.

restaurant.name: Manila Social
restaurant.desc: Manila Social is a Filipino-inspired restaurant in downtown Kamloops helmed by Chef Romeo Oloresisimo, celebrating traditional Filipino comfort food — from open-flamed rotisserie chicken to classic Silog breakfast plates — with a modern, locally rooted twist. The restaurant serves brunch, lunch, and dinner and offers catering and curated private dining experiences. Situated in the heart of Kamloops' downtown core, it stands out as one of the few dedicated Filipino kitchens in the BC Interior.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dinner menu includes Zen Poke Bowl (marinated tofu), Spiced Chickpea Burrata, East-Style Salad, Nutty Brussels, and Classic Caesar Salad — multiple vegetarian dishes confirmed. No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Wendy's
restaurant.desc: Wendy's is a major fast-food chain known for its square-pattied fresh-beef burgers, chicken sandwiches, and signature Frosty desserts. This Chilliwack location on Vedder Road in the Fraser Valley offers a drive-thru alongside dine-in service and a full breakfast menu with fresh-cracked eggs. The menu also includes salads and a range of chicken options, giving cyclists something for every appetite.

restaurant.name: The Chopped Leaf
restaurant.desc: The Chopped Leaf at Sumas Mountain Village is a fast-casual franchise restaurant in Abbotsford specializing in customizable salads, bowls, wraps, and soups made from fresh ingredients with signature dressings. The menu is designed around diverse dietary needs, offering vegan, vegetarian, gluten-friendly, dairy-free, and nut-free options throughout. Located in a commercial village area, it provides a quick, health-focused refueling option for cyclists passing through the eastern Fraser Valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Location page explicitly lists 'vegan', 'vegetarian', and 'gluten friendly' as store features; website copy also states 'from vegan and vegetarian, to kid-friendly and gluten-friendly options'

restaurant.name: Grounds & Greens Cafe
restaurant.desc: Grounds & Greens Cafe is a family-owned, fully plant-based cafe run by chefs Mannel and Ben Kilford, located in the heart of historic Fort Langley village. The menu centres on hearty power bowls, toasties, wraps, and bites made with locally sourced ingredients — substantial fuel for a cycling day. The cafe has eliminated single-use containers in favour of reusables as part of a zero-waste commitment.

detail.address: 9124 Glover Road Unit 3A, Fort Langley, BC V1M 2S8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Entirely plant-based/vegan menu; OSM confirms. Fort Langley menu lists multiple items marked GF (e.g. egg bites, bowls, nooch popcorn). Gluten-free bread also available

restaurant.name: Honey Salt
restaurant.desc: Honey Salt is a restaurant on Smithe Street in downtown Vancouver offering both indoor and outdoor seating. The establishment is wheelchair accessible and maintains a non-smoking environment. Touring cyclists will find convenient dining options for breaks along their route through the city.

restaurant.name: Rollzzy
restaurant.desc: Rollzzy is a fast-casual Indian street food chain specializing in authentic Kathi Rolls — handmade paratha wraps filled with spiced meats, paneer, and vegetarian fillings rooted in Kolkata street food tradition. The Robson Street location is part of a growing Lower Mainland franchise (TGI Foods Corp) with over 20 roll varieties plus momos, Indian-style burgers, and chai. Cyclists touring downtown Vancouver will find it a quick, customizable stop with a wide range of vegetarian and vegan options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states 'we have a wide range of vegetarian rolls (paneer, aloo, soya, etc.) and can accommodate vegan preferences — just ask at the counter or select the option.' No mention of gluten-free

restaurant.name: North Road Sushi & Kitchen
restaurant.desc: North Road Sushi & Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant in the Lougheed Town Centre area of Burnaby, offering a broad menu of sushi, sashimi, nigiri, tempura, noodles, katsu, and donburi. The restaurant is noted by customers for generous portions, fresh fish, and good value. Both dine-in and online pickup or delivery orders are available through their Foodly partnership.

restaurant.name: Cold Comfort
restaurant.desc: Cold Comfort has been crafting Victoria's original hand-made frozen custard since 2010, using organic cream, cane sugar, freshly cracked local eggs, and local sea salt. Alongside their dairy line they offer a full vegan 'Nicecream' made with coconut milk, plus gluten-friendly options, ice cream sandwiches, and Baked Alaskas. They also cater events, arriving by bicycle or truck, making them a genuinely bike-friendly presence in the city.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly offers 'premium vegan ice cream (Nicecream)' made with coconut milk, plus 'Gluten Friendly options'; Cook Street location lists 6 dairy-free Nicecream flavours and 6 organic dairy; multiple menu items labelled VEGAN and/or gluten-friendly

restaurant.name: HiFive Chicken
restaurant.desc: HiFive Chicken is a BC-born fast food chain founded in 2016, now with over 11 locations across the province, specializing in roasted and fried chicken made with in-house marinades. The Abbotsford location sits on Mount Lehman Road and offers both dine-in and online ordering. Cyclists can choose from a broad menu including sandwiches, tenders, wings, sides, and desserts.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists a 'Veggie Sandwich' (toasted bun, mayo, lettuce, veggie patty, tomato, onion rings). No GF or vegan items explicitly identified

restaurant.name: Starbucks
restaurant.desc: Starbucks is a globally recognized coffeehouse chain serving espresso drinks, teas, Frappuccinos, and a range of food items. This Vancouver location offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a convenient rest stop on a cycling route. Touring cyclists will find a familiar, accessible venue for a hot or cold drink and a snack.

restaurant.name: Heart & Bone Provisions
restaurant.desc: Heart & Bone Provisions is a health-focused café and provisions shop in Ganges on Salt Spring Island, specializing in premium bone broth made from organic, free-range ingredients with a keto-oriented menu. Cyclists can pick up take-home items from a self-serve cooler and freezer stocked with frozen broth, soups, eggs, butter, and low-sugar sweet treats, or dine in for a nourishing meal. The shop also offers online ordering with pickup and delivery, making it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists on the island.

restaurant.name: Spice Hut Indian Cuisine;Adventure Tofino Wildlife Tours
restaurant.desc: Spice Hut Canada is an East Indian restaurant in Tofino, a scenic coastal destination on Vancouver Island's west coast. It provides a dining option for touring cyclists passing through this popular tourist community.

restaurant.name: Blue Nile African Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Blue Nile is an Ethiopian and Eritrean restaurant in central Victoria, serving authentic communal-style meals atop injera flatbread with an array of spiced meat stews, lentils, and vegetable dishes. The restaurant also prepares traditional Bunna (Ethiopian coffee) from scratch — roasting green beans and grinding them with cloves and cinnamon served in a traditional pot. A wide range of vegan and gluten-free options makes it a flexible stop for cyclists with varied dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About Us page: 'Vegetarian and vegan options are plentiful and equally delicious.' Menu page: 'All dishes are gluten free except injera. For Gluten Free option substitute rice instead of Injera.'

restaurant.name: The Snug
restaurant.desc: The Snug holds the distinction of being Victoria's first neighbourhood pub, dating back to 1954, and is now housed within the Oak Bay Beach Hotel on the city's scenic waterfront. Floor-to-ceiling ocean views and an oceanfront patio define the casual coastal atmosphere, while the kitchen draws on seasonal BC produce and pours a healthy selection of local brews on tap. It is a historic and beloved local institution well worth a detour for cyclists riding the Oak Bay shoreline.

restaurant.name: Shobu Ramen
restaurant.desc: Shobu Ramen is a Japanese ramen restaurant in Coquitlam specializing in traditional noodle dishes. The restaurant offers takeout service, making it convenient for quick meals during cycling trips. Hearty ramen bowls provide substantial refueling options for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Hello Bubble
restaurant.desc: Hello Bubble is a bubble tea café located in Maple Ridge, BC, identifiable from its Facebook presence under the handle 'hellobubble.bubbletea.' Bubble tea shops of this type typically offer a range of cold blended and tea-based drinks that can be appealing to cyclists on warm-weather routes. Its location in the Maple Ridge urban area places it along potential cycling corridors in the Fraser Valley.

restaurant.name: Jeffer's Fryzz
restaurant.desc: Jeffer's Fryzz is a street-vending fish-and-chips outfit based in Penticton, BC. As a mobile or pop-up vendor it likely operates at markets, events, or rotating street locations rather than a fixed address. restaurant.name: Guu Original Thurlow

Situated on Thurlow Street in the West End, it offers a full Japanese izakaya menu including classic dishes like Yaki Udon and Oden in a lively, high-energy indoor atmosphere. Touring cyclists looking for a substantial sit-down meal near the downtown core will find a long-established destination with both lunch and dinner service.

restaurant.name: Spin Roll

restaurant.name: Yuan Coffee
restaurant.desc: Yuan Coffee is a specialty coffee shop on Clark Drive in Vancouver, operating as a small-format café focused on quality coffee. restaurant.name: North Burnaby Wonton House

restaurant.name: Ibex Café + Kitchen

Outdoor seating is available according to OSM tags.

restaurant.name: bb.q Chicken

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Freshslice Pizza is a BC-based pizza chain offering by-the-slice and whole pies for dine-in, takeout, and delivery. The Cambie Street location sits on a major urban cycling corridor in Vancouver's Cambie Village neighbourhood, making it a convenient quick-stop for hungry riders. Vegetarian toppings are available across the menu.

restaurant.name: Kinder Cup

They serve locally roasted Drumroaster Coffee from Cobble Hill alongside freshly baked goods, sandwiches, and a range of vegan and gluten-free options. Their Kindness Fund lets customers pay forward a coffee for someone else in the community.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About Us page states: 'fresh-made sandwiches, baked goods, and a variety of vegan and gluten-free options.'

restaurant.name: Bubble TastyTea
restaurant.desc: Bubble TastyTea is an independent bubble tea shop founded by a young couple in Abbotsford, BC, offering an extensive menu of milk teas, fruit teas, slushes, coffee, and specialty drinks made with premium tea leaves and top-grade toppings. The shop rounds out its menu with bubble waffles and bingsu (shaved ice), making it a more substantial refreshment stop than a typical tea counter. It has built a strong local following since opening and positions itself as Abbotsford's favourite bubble tea destination.

restaurant.name: The King's Head Public House
restaurant.desc: The King's Head Public House is an iconic Kitsilano neighbourhood pub set in a Tudor-style building constructed in 1897, originally a fish market and beauty parlour before becoming the area's first pub in 1973. Recently fully renovated, it features a modern olde-style interior with live entertainment, locally inspired food, and daily happy hours. It sits on Yew Street close to the Kits Beach waterfront and the Arbutus Greenway, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring Vancouver's west side.

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: Tim Hortons is a national Canadian coffee and quick-service chain located on Douglas Street in central Victoria. This location offers dine-in, takeout, and drive-through service, with a menu spanning brewed coffee, baked goods, breakfast wraps, soups, and sandwiches. A touring cyclist passing through would find it a convenient and familiar stop for a quick meal or hot drink.

The menu is adaptable to dietary needs and draws on scratch-baked ingredients throughout.

restaurant.name: Cielito Lindo
restaurant.desc: Cielito Lindo is an authentic Mexican restaurant on West Hastings in downtown Vancouver, serving traditional dishes such as birria, cochinita pibil, enmoladas, and carne en su jugo alongside house-crafted cocktails like the signature Licuachelas and Azulitos. The restaurant emphasizes an immersive cultural experience through vibrant handmade decor, bold flavors, and an atmosphere that ranges from intimate weeknight dining to festive weekend energy. Reservations are accepted, making it a reliable choice for touring cyclists seeking a full sit-down Mexican meal in the heart of the city.

restaurant.name: Powell Brewery Tasting Room

Touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver can stop in to sample fresh-poured pints in a neighbourhood setting.

restaurant.name: B&P Ice Cream Coffee
restaurant.desc: B&P Ice Cream Coffee is a small ice cream and coffee shop located in Richmond, BC, operating from a unit-level retail space on 2nd Avenue. No further details about seating, menu, or facilities could be confirmed from available sources.

restaurant.name: Bar Gobo

The music program is curated live on vinyl by a resident enthusiast, giving the space an intimate, unpredictable character that sets it apart from conventional bars. A touring cyclist finishing a day's ride on the nearby Seaside Greenway or Central Valley Greenway would find a sophisticated but relaxed spot for an evening glass.

restaurant.name: Marcello Woodfire Pizza Oven
restaurant.desc: Marcello Ristorante & Pizzeria is a long-standing neighbourhood favourite on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, serving traditional Southern Italian cuisine rooted in owner Marcello's upbringing in Palermo and professional training in Milan. The full menu spans woodfire pizza, house-made pasta, antipasti, and an extensive Italian cocktail list in a sit-down ristorante setting. The restaurant accommodates group events for up to 24 guests, making it a practical stop for cycling club dinners or post-ride celebrations.

restaurant.name: Minato Japanese Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Minato Japanese Restaurant is a long-established sushi and traditional Japanese restaurant on Vancouver's busy West Broadway corridor, in operation since 1991. The restaurant offers a full dine-in experience alongside delivery and catering services, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists riding one of Vancouver's key east-west routes. It is located in a retail unit at 1001 West Broadway, close to the Cambie Street intersection.

restaurant.name: Barpa Bill's

restaurant.name: Osmow's

It is a quick counter-service stop with takeout available, convenient for cyclists passing through the Ironwood area.

restaurant.name: Kickturn Coffee Roasters

The shop sources single-origin beans almost directly from a single farming family in Antigua, Guatemala, roasting to order for both walk-in visitors and a Canada-wide online subscription. Customer reviews highlight the owner's genuine passion and the welcoming atmosphere, making it a natural stop for cyclists passing through the East Kootenays.

restaurant.name: Caramba! Restaurante

Run by owner-operators Jay and James Pare, it draws both visitors and locals with handcrafted pastas, wood-fired pizzas, and craft cocktails in a lively, casual atmosphere. Takeout is available, making it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists moving through the village.

restaurant.name: Uncle Tetsu's Cheesecake
restaurant.desc: Uncle Tetsu's is a Japanese cheesecake chain originating in Fukuoka, Japan, with a Vancouver location on busy Robson Street. The shop bakes everything fresh in an open-concept kitchen using locally sourced ingredients, producing their signature soft and fluffy Japanese cheesecakes, honey madeleines, and triple-baked cheese tarts. It is a well-known destination on one of Vancouver's main urban cycling corridors.

restaurant.name: Coasters Coffee
restaurant.desc: Coasters Coffee is an independent cafe in New Westminster founded by two sisters who designed the space around a West Coast nature aesthetic, bringing the feel of the outdoors inside. The cafe sources its coffee from local roasters committed to organic and ethical growing practices, and its loose-leaf teas from a 100% Canadian-owned supplier. Touring cyclists will find a calm indoor setting with a broad menu of specialty espresso drinks, teas, matcha, and food including salads and pastries.

restaurant.name: Grindstone Cafe

A sunny street-side patio adds an appealing spot to rest on a ride through Victoria.

restaurant.name: Dai Cha Fan

restaurant.name: Donair Addict

It bills itself as the high-quality shawarma option in an oceanside surf town not otherwise known for Middle Eastern food.

restaurant.name: Pita Pit

The build-your-own format and healthy ingredient focus make it a practical refuelling stop for touring cyclists moving through the Fraser Valley.

restaurant.name: Flipside Burgers

The pairing of craft beer and scratch-made burgers in an outdoor setting makes it a popular rest stop on Squamish's busy cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Elisa Wood-Fired Grill
restaurant.desc: Elisa is a Michelin Guide-recommended wood-fired grill in Vancouver's Yaletown neighborhood, celebrated for its fine steaks and seafood. Ranked among the 101 Best Steak Restaurants in the World and named Vancouver Magazine's Restaurant of the Year, it features both indoor and outdoor seating with a full bar. The restaurant also operates Luigi & Sons Butcher Shop as a companion venture.

restaurant.name: Alysa's Pho & Banh Mi
