restaurant.name: Barn Nork Aharn Thai
restaurant.desc: Barn Nork Aharn Thai is a small, well-loved Thai restaurant in Whistler running a busy made-to-order kitchen with only four dine-in tables and a strong takeout focus. The menu features house-made dishes such as crispy chive cakes, green papaya salad, and a family-recipe grilled chicken, with a clear emphasis on fresh, authentic preparation. Cyclists looking for a flavourful post-ride meal will find genuine Thai cooking with vegan and gluten-free options available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly labels 'Deep Fried Tofu / TAI HOO TOD (Vegan)' and marks Uncle B's Grilled Chicken, Chicken Skewer, and Green Papaya Salad as '(Gluten Free)'

restaurant.name: Neptune Palace Seafood
restaurant.desc: Neptune Palace Seafood is a large-format Chinese seafood restaurant in Vancouver's Marpole neighbourhood, part of a multi-location chain also operating in Surrey and Burnaby. The Vancouver flagship is known for its dim sum service, signature roasted duck preparations, and banquet-style event hosting with space for roughly 200 guests. It is a substantial sit-down destination on the SW Marine Drive corridor, popular for family and group gatherings.

detail.address: 308 - 470 SW Marine Drive, Vancouver, BC V5X 0C4

restaurant.name: Mister Artisan Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Mister Artisan Ice Cream is a Vancouver artisan ice cream shop that uses liquid nitrogen to create exceptionally rich, dense, made-to-order ice cream from scratch with natural, locally sourced ingredients. The Robson Street location sits on one of Vancouver's busiest pedestrian corridors, making it a convenient sweet stop for cyclists touring the downtown core. Seasonal rotating flavours and vegan options give it broad appeal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website emphasizes natural, pure ingredients and vegan-friendly positioning

restaurant.name: Phở Hòa
restaurant.desc: Phở Hòa is an international Vietnamese noodle-soup chain founded in California in 1983, now operating in over 60 locations across 6 countries including Canada. The brand positions itself around a health-conscious broth made from lean meats rather than traditional bone marrow, alongside a full menu of pho variants, rice plates, vermicelli bowls, and fresh rolls. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a warm sit-down meal with substantial noodle-soup options designed for comfort after a long ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Vegetarian Phở Chay' — tofu, broccoli, cauliflower, mushrooms, and carrots in a mushroom broth. No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Woking Dragon
restaurant.desc: Woking Dragon is a family-owned Chinese restaurant operating since 2003, offering modern western-style Chinese cuisine across three Lower Mainland locations including Willoughby Town Centre in Langley. The restaurant has earned recognition as a favourite Chinese food destination in the Tri-Cities market. A touring cyclist stopping here can expect a sit-down meal with online ordering and takeout options available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Some menu items are able to be made Vegan & Gluten-Free.'

restaurant.name: Nubo Japanese Tapas
restaurant.desc: Nubo Japanese Tapas is an intimate Japanese sushi bar and izakaya established in Victoria in March 2016, combining traditional Japanese flavors with a modern tapas-style dining format. The menu spans fresh sashimi and nigiri, hot small plates, rolls, teppan dishes, and an extensive sake and cocktail list. It offers a relaxed sit-down experience well suited to cyclists looking to refuel with Japanese fusion cuisine in downtown Victoria.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian items: yam roll, avocado roll, agedashi tofu, edamame, avocado tempura, goma-ae, kungpao tofu, kabocha croquette, and rice dishes with tofu option

restaurant.name: Lunitas Mexican Eatery
restaurant.desc: Lunitas is a casual, colourful Mexican eatery perched on the hillside overlooking Gibsons Harbour, serving creative tacos, ceviche, and craft cocktails made with local seasonal ingredients alongside B.C. wines and microbrewed beer. It has been voted Best Cocktail Establishment five years running and Best Tacos four years in a row on the Sunshine Coast. Access to the restaurant involves a staircase or boardwalk route, with the host stand moving down to the SeaWalk Patio in summer.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Food menu key lists: v = vegan, gf = gluten free, c = celiac, df = dairy free

restaurant.name: The Barkley Cafe
restaurant.desc: The Barkley Cafe is a family-run cafe in Davison Plaza on Peninsula Road in the heart of Ucluelet, on the west coast of Vancouver Island. It serves fresh-to-order breakfast and lunch — including sandwiches, house-baked goods, and specialty coffees from Victoria-based Caffe Fantastico — with a notable commitment to sustainability including composting coffee grounds in an on-site herb garden. A warm, welcoming stop with both dine-in and grab-and-go options suited to cyclists passing through.

detail.address: Unit 1-1620 Peninsula Rd, Davison Plaza, Ucluelet BC V0R 3A0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu labels include 'Vegetarian' on the Veggie Sandwich, 'Vegan' and 'GF' on the Berry fruit square, and explicit gluten-free upgrade options for the Bagel Breakfast Sandwich and Bagel and Cream Cheese

restaurant.name: Fish With You
restaurant.desc: Fish With You is a Sichuan-inspired Chinese restaurant in Richmond specializing in fish-centric dishes including Sauerkraut Fish, Spicy Sichuan Fish Fillet, and Tomato Fish Soup. Diners receive unlimited steamed rice alongside customizable add-ins such as tofu, wood ear mushrooms, and vermicelli. The Richmond location on Alexandra Road is part of a two-branch chain also operating in Burnaby, offering both dine-in and online ordering through delivery platforms.

restaurant.name: Onigiri Ya
restaurant.desc: Onigiri Ya is a Japanese rice ball shop on Robson Street in Vancouver's downtown core, one of three Vancouver locations operated by the Maruhachi Ramen Group. The shop focuses on freshly made onigiri available for pre-order pickup, offering a quick and portable meal well-suited to cyclists on the move. The Robson branch is steps from the seawall and major cycling routes through the city centre.

notes.Takeout: Online pre-order pickup model; website states orders are prepared for customer pickup. No dine-in ordering flow mentioned — pickup is the core service

restaurant.name: Sangam Sweets & Curry Express
restaurant.desc: A restaurant and confectionery shop specializing in Indian cuisine, located on Lougheed Highway in Chilliwack. The business combines a sit-down restaurant with an attached sweets shop offering both prepared Indian meals and confectionery items.

restaurant.name: The Galley Restaurant and Grill
restaurant.desc: The Galley Patio & Grill is a casual, long-running waterfront restaurant at the Jericho Sailing Centre in Vancouver, serving West Coast comfort food including beer-battered BC rockfish, locally sourced burgers, and seasonal salads on an open patio. It has been operating since at least 2003 — its signature Jamaican Jerk Chicken Burger is noted as a Galley original from that year — and sources humanely raised beef from Semlin Valley Ranch in Cache Creek. The restaurant also provides catering for events at the Jericho Sailing Centre, making it a well-established fixture on Vancouver's western waterfront cycling corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Jericho Veggie Burger (veggie patty, romesco sauce, iceberg, tomato, house pickles) and Mish-Mash Salad (roasted seasonal vegetables, fried chickpeas, farro, kale, tahini dressing); no explicit vegan or GF labels on the menu

restaurant.name: Rabbit Rabbit
restaurant.desc: Rabbit Rabbit is a small wine bar and restaurant on the edge of Victoria's historic Chinatown, helmed by Executive Chef Billy Nguyen and Wine Director Sydney Cooper, with a frequently changing menu of locally sourced, seasonally driven cuisine. The wine program is curiosity-driven and focuses on small, sustainable producers from around the world, with notable representation from Vancouver Island wineries and appellations. The bar earned recognition in Air Canada's Best New Restaurants 2025 and has been nominated for the 2026 Vancouver Magazine Restaurant Awards.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian dishes including Cucumber Salad, Charred Romaine, Agedashi Tofu, Dan Dan Noodles, Seared Cabbage Puttanesca, and Mushroom Lo Bok Go

restaurant.name: The Barley Merchant
restaurant.desc: The Barley Merchant is a craft-focused taproom and kitchen in Langley, BC, built around a strict 'We Serve BC' philosophy: all 50 taps pour exclusively from independently owned BC breweries, cideries, and distilleries. Since opening, it has rotated through more than 2,100 unique BC craft beers from over 165 breweries across the province. A full food menu sourced from BC ingredients accompanies the drinks program in a relaxed, upbeat setting.

detail.address: 20090 91a Avenue - Building B - Unit #101, Langley, BC, V1M 3Y9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website navigation explicitly lists dedicated menu pages for Vegan Options, Gluten Free Options, and Dairy Free Options

restaurant.name: Wild Sushi
restaurant.desc: Wild Sushi is a sushi restaurant located on Dunbar Street in Vancouver. As a restaurant, it serves prepared food to customers. Limited website information is available due to access issues.

restaurant.name: Kumare Restaurant & Bakery
restaurant.desc: Kumare Restaurant & Bakery is a Richmond Filipino restaurant celebrating the regional diversity of Filipino cuisine through an extensive menu of silog breakfasts, soups, mains, and classic pastries. The business also operates a street food truck serving pop-ups and community events across the Lower Mainland, and ships authentic Filipino baked goods throughout BC. A touring cyclist will find a community-oriented dining destination with broad dietary accommodation and dedicated takeout and boxed lunch services.

notes.Packed lunches: Website navigation includes a dedicated 'Boxed Lunch' section alongside catering services
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About page states: 'Our menu at Kumare is designed to cater to a variety of dietary needs and preferences, including vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options.' Menu also lists Crispy Tofu, Fresh Lumpia, and Vegetable Spring Roll

restaurant.name: The Bay Gibsons
restaurant.desc: The Bay Gibsons is a New York-style thin-crust pizza restaurant in Gibsons, BC, known for creative named pies made with cold-fermented, fresh-milled flour dough. The menu ranges from classic pepperoni to inventive signatures like the Dirty Little Peach and Mary Had a Little Lamb, with vegetarian options throughout. Notably, the restaurant accepts Bitcoin and Lightning Network payments in addition to conventional methods.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu uses a 🥬 symbol to mark vegetarian pizzas. Dough described as safe for gluten-sensitive individuals, but explicitly not suitable for those with gluten allergies

restaurant.name: Run With Soup
restaurant.desc: Run With Soup is a restaurant in Sechelt. The website was inaccessible during verification, limiting available information about the establishment's character and amenities for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Pizza Dough Therapy by Ojas Blend
restaurant.desc: Pizza Dough Therapy by Ojas Blend is an independent artisan pizza shop on Johnston Road in White Rock, offering an eclectic lineup of globally inspired pies—think jerk chicken and pineapple, palak paneer, and chipotle chorizo alongside classic margherita. The menu is unusually broad for a fast-food format, with a full vegetarian section and vegan cheese available as an add-on. Pickup orders can be placed online, making it a convenient refuelling stop on the White Rock waterfront cycling corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'VEGGIE MEDLEY' section with seven vegetarian pizzas; 'VEGAN CHEESE' and 'NUTRITIONAL YEAST' are listed as add-on options

restaurant.name: Papa John's
restaurant.desc: Papa John's is a national pizza chain franchise located in a strip-mall unit in north Nanaimo, offering pizza, breadsticks, and wings for delivery or carryout. It sits along the Rutherford Road corridor, which connects residential areas to the highway, making it a reachable stop for cyclists passing through the north end of the city. The carryout option makes it a practical choice for a hot meal on the road.

restaurant.name: West Coast Poké
restaurant.desc: West Coast Poké is a Vancouver poke bowl restaurant on West 8th Avenue built around chef-inspired flavours, fresh ingredients, and sustainable sourcing. It offers both signature classic bowls (featuring Ahi tuna, Atlantic salmon, prawn, and albacore tuna) and a fully customizable build-your-own option with a wide range of proteins, toppings, and house sauces. The emphasis on an on-the-go, nourishing meal format makes it a practical and appealing fuel stop for touring cyclists.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Tofu as a protein option and offers White Rice, Brown Rice, or Salad as bases, confirming vegetarian and vegan-compatible bowl options. No explicit gluten-free claim found

restaurant.name: North Garden Cafe Restaurant
restaurant.desc: North Garden Cafe is a Hong Kong-style Chinese restaurant in Coquitlam serving an extensive menu of seafood, hot pot, congee, chow mein, and more. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery with online ordering available. It accepts cash or debit only.

detail.address: 552 Clarke Road Suite 411, Coquitlam, BC V3J 3X5

restaurant.name: The Bean Scene
restaurant.desc: Bean Scene Coffee House is a long-established independent coffee shop in the heart of downtown Vernon, BC, with a loyal local following built on good coffee and a relaxed social atmosphere. The business describes itself as a place where 'a cup of coffee is a moment to share,' emphasising community and conversation over quick turnover. For touring cyclists moving through the Okanagan, it offers a welcoming downtown rest stop on 30th Avenue.

restaurant.name: Tan's Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Tan's Kitchen is a Chinese restaurant on the West Island Highway in Parksville serving Cantonese and Szechuan dishes including Salt & Pepper Squid, Ginger Beef, and General Tso's Chicken. The restaurant offers all-you-can-eat service and outdoor dining, and advertises no MSG in its food. It sits on a main cycling corridor along eastern Vancouver Island, making it a convenient full-service meal stop.

detail.address: 332 Island Hwy, West, Parksville, BC V9P 1K8

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'Vegetarian Spri...' (Vegetarian Spring Rolls) and 'Spicy Green Bea...' indicating at least some vegetarian menu items

restaurant.name: Seaside restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Seaside Restaurant is a historic waterfront kitchen in Vesuvius Bay, located steps from the Vesuvius Ferry Terminal on Salt Spring Island — making it a natural stop for cyclists arriving or departing by ferry. The site has been a community landmark since the 1940s, beginning as Vesuvius Marine with a hand-pumped gas station before evolving into the beloved seaside eatery it is today. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the restaurant offers catering and online ordering.

detail.address: 795 Vesuvius Bay Road, Salt Spring Island, British Columbia V8K 1L6, Canada

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website also invites customers with dietary concerns to reach out

restaurant.name: Gong Cha
restaurant.desc: Gong Cha is a globally recognized bubble tea brand operating over 1,650 stores across 20 countries, with more than 50 locations across Canada. This Kelowna location serves handcrafted tea-based drinks in a primarily takeaway format, ideal for a quick stop on a cycling route. A rewards program lets customers accumulate points across all Canadian locations.

restaurant.name: Hongdae Korean Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Hongdae Korean Restaurant is a Korean eatery in Coquitlam specializing in jokbal (braised pig's trotters), advertised as freshly prepared daily. Located at the intersection of North Road and Lougheed Highway, it offers indoor seating and online ordering. The late closing time makes it a viable stop for cyclists finishing a long evening ride.

restaurant.name: Granville Island Brewing Taproom
restaurant.desc: Established in 1984, Granville Island Brewing operates this taproom on Granville Island where visitors can sample the full core lineup alongside exclusive small-batch Taproom Series releases brewed on-site — beers unavailable anywhere else. The taproom offers indoor and outdoor patio seating with a food menu, dogs are welcome on the patio and brewery entrance, and the space is wheelchair accessible via a side-door ramp.

restaurant.name: Noodlebox
restaurant.desc: Noodlebox is a Canadian fast-casual franchise specializing in wok-fired Asian noodle and rice dishes built to order from a customizable menu of sauces and proteins. The chain operates multiple BC locations and emphasizes fresh, made-to-order cooking with broad dietary accommodation. A cyclist stopping in Chilliwack would find a quick, filling meal with vegan and gluten-friendly options available on request.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'Can be made VEGAN — Please ask when ordering' and 'Can be made GLUTEN-FRIENDLY — Please ask when ordering.'

restaurant.name: Salmon Wave
restaurant.desc: A sushi and poke restaurant with indoor seating in Burnaby. A casual dining option for cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Little Caesar's
restaurant.desc: Little Caesar's is a well-known Canadian pizza chain offering hot-and-ready pizzas for carryout and delivery. This Nanaimo location (unit 3) is part of the globally recognized franchise founded in Michigan in 1959. For a touring cyclist looking for a quick, filling meal, it offers an accessible fast-food option in the Nanaimo area.

restaurant.name: Creekside Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A pub and fast food restaurant in Scotch Creek serving the local community and traveling guests. Located on Squilax Anglemont Road, it offers casual dining and refreshment options for cyclists and other travelers.

restaurant.name: The Teahouse
restaurant.desc: The Teahouse has occupied the heritage building at Ferguson Point in Stanley Park since 1978, offering west coast seafood and seasonal menus with unobstructed ocean views from window-lined dining rooms and a waterfront patio. Part of the Sequoia Company of Restaurants, it sits directly along the Stanley Park Seawall—one of the most heavily cycled routes in Vancouver—making it a natural candidate rest stop for touring cyclists. The restaurant operates a full dinner, brunch, and lunch service with dedicated private event spaces including a glass-roofed conservatory and garden lawn.

detail.address: Ferguson Point Stanley Park, Vancouver, BC

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page explicitly labels 'Vegetarian Gluten-Free Organic' categories

restaurant.name: The Edge
restaurant.desc: The Edge is an award-winning fine dining restaurant perched 1,000 feet above Okanagan Lake at The Rise Resort golf club on the edge of Vernon, named Vernon's Restaurant of the Year 2025. The 30,000-square-foot space features floor-to-ceiling windows and a multi-level patio delivering 360-degree panoramic views of the Okanagan Valley. The kitchen sources almost exclusively from named Okanagan and broader BC producers—farmers, foragers, stone millers, and charcutiers—with a wine program anchored in local Okanagan vintages.

restaurant.name: Interactivity Board Game Cafe
restaurant.desc: Victoria's first and largest board game cafe, offering access to over 1,500 games to play in-venue for a flat per-person fee with no time limit. Fully licensed since 2018 and family-friendly, the cafe serves an extensive menu of toasted sandwiches, flatbread pizzas, snacks, coffee drinks, and dozens of housemade milkshake flavours. A touring cyclist looking for a relaxed, social stop in downtown Victoria will find good food, cold drinks, and a genuinely unique atmosphere.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists gluten-free bread upgrade (+$1) on sandwiches marked with *; vegetarian options include The Mediterranean (hummus, feta, olives, cucumbers, tomato), Jack's Cheese, Grilled Cheese, Spicy Grilled Cheese, and multiple cheese-based flatbreads. Dairy-free milkshake options also noted

restaurant.name: Pür & Simple
restaurant.desc: Pür & Simple is a Canadian breakfast and brunch franchise chain with over 65 locations across North America, bringing upscale daytime dining to Kelowna with creative twists on comfort-food classics like Eggs Benedict, pancakes, French toast, and waffles. The restaurant also offers a full Nespresso coffee bar, smoothies, and a kids menu, making it a well-rounded fueling stop for groups of all sizes. Both dine-in and online ordering for delivery or takeout are available.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu pages explicitly list Vegan (Vg) and Vegetarian (V) labelled items, and include a 'gluten sensitive' filter category

restaurant.name: Harvest Community Foods
restaurant.desc: Harvest Community Foods is a community-supported, locally sourced grocery store and noodle soup café in Vancouver's Strathcona neighbourhood, owned and operated by local chefs Andrea Carlson and Gabriella Meyer. The shop serves a rotating menu of ramen, udon, and rice bowls with multiple vegan options, alongside a grocery section emphasizing urban produce and small-batch local foods. It also functions as a pickup hub for CSA (Community Supported Agriculture) bags filled with seasonal produce sourced from regional farms.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items explicitly labelled vegan: '#17 Ramen w/squash & miso broth... (make it Vegan)', '#23 Udon w/ coconut turmeric curry, puff tofu, shiitake, greens (Vegan)', '#31 Rice Noodle w/almond hazelnut sauce... (Vegan)'; grocery section notes 'small production vegan and local foods'

restaurant.name: Maison d'la Poutine House
restaurant.desc: Maison d'la Poutine House is a Quebec-inspired restaurant in Chilliwack offering classic poutine alongside handmade-dough pizzas with toppings like Montreal smoked meat and pepperoni. The menu leans into hearty, comfort-food staples that make for a satisfying refuel after a long day in the saddle. Orders can be placed online for pickup or delivery.

restaurant.name: Bailey's Pub
restaurant.desc: Bailey's Pub is a locally owned neighbourhood pub in North Kamloops serving scratch-made Canadian food for breakfast, lunch, and dinner seven days a week. The casual, welcoming atmosphere caters to groups of any size, with walk-ins accepted alongside reservations. Touring cyclists will find a full-service meal stop with takeout available and regular entertainment including karaoke and trivia nights.

restaurant.name: Mission Station Grill
restaurant.desc: A sit-down restaurant in Chilliwack with outdoor seating and a reservation option. Provides a rest stop with dine-in service for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Mount Currie Coffee Company
restaurant.desc: Mount Currie Coffee Co. is a locally rooted coffee shop with two locations serving the Sea-to-Sky corridor — Pemberton and Whistler Village — pouring premium espresso drinks from Gradient Coffee roasted just up the road in the Pemberton Industrial Park. Active supporters of both PORCA and WORCA, they co-sponsor annual mountain bike events and describe themselves as 'a place to start your adventure,' making them a natural gathering spot for cyclists in the region. Call-ahead ordering is available for groups heading out on the trails.

restaurant.name: K & H Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: K & H Seafood Restaurant is a Chinese seafood dining destination on Kingsway, one of Vancouver's main east-west arterials and a common cycling corridor. The restaurant sits in a dense commercial strip in East Vancouver that serves a large Chinese-Canadian community. Touring cyclists passing through on Kingsway or nearby routes will find a full-service sit-down option for seafood and Chinese cuisine.

restaurant.name: Hook Cantina
restaurant.desc: Hook Cantina is a restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, situated near the Stanley Park seawall and popular urban cycling routes. Its cantina-style name suggests a casual dining concept well-suited to the neighbourhood's active, outdoor-oriented clientele. No further details about the menu or interior could be confirmed due to a website access issue.

restaurant.name: My Island Cafe
restaurant.desc: A cafe serving the Vancouver community. Limited wheelchair access is available. No vegan options are offered according to OSM records.

restaurant.name: Oriental Gardens
restaurant.desc: A family-owned Chinese and Japanese restaurant that has anchored downtown Kamloops since 1971, making it one of the longest-running restaurants in the city. The menu spans Cantonese stir-fries, house-recipe Szechuan dishes, an extensive sushi selection, and in-house roasted duck — all prepared by the restaurant's own chefs. A private tatami room accommodating up to 16 guests adds a distinctive dining option that sets it apart from typical downtown restaurants.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Our menu includes a variety of vegetarian options as well'; Chinese menu explicitly marks multiple dishes as '(GF) Gluten Free option available'

restaurant.name: Frank's Pizza & Bar at Resurrection Spirits
restaurant.desc: Frank's Pies & Slices is a New York-inspired pizza restaurant tucked along North Commercial Drive in East Vancouver, operating out of the Resurrection Spirits space. The menu leans into creative, shareable pies with names like 'Notorious P.I.E.' and 'Silk Tracksuit', alongside share plates and late-night pizza slices. A cyclist finishing a ride along the nearby Commercial Drive corridor would find a lively, independently run spot well suited to a post-ride meal.

notes.Takeout: Website prominently features 'ORDER ONLINE NOW' and notes pizza slices available after last call, confirming takeout service
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian options: 'The Green Monster' pizza (no meat), arugula salad, castelvetrano olives, and cheese bread. No explicit vegan or GF labeling found

restaurant.name: Aroma Eatery
restaurant.desc: Aroma Eatery is a Chinese restaurant offering takeaway service. It provides a convenient food and refueling stop for touring cyclists. Amenities such as bike parking and water access are unconfirmed.

restaurant.name: Smith's Irish Pub
restaurant.desc: Smith's Irish Pub is an Irish-owned bar in the heart of Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, spread across two adjoining storefronts. The venue offers a cozy main bar, an elegant lounge with private snugs, and The Forge — a hidden cocktail and whiskey bar that can be hired privately. Touring cyclists arriving in Gastown will find a lively house-of-rugby atmosphere with live music and food service from SMASHED!

detail.address: 208 & 212 Carrall Street, Gastown, Vancouver, BC V6B 2J1

restaurant.name: Townhall
restaurant.desc: Townhall is a pub operated by Joseph Richard Group with a location in Chilliwack on Vedder Road. The venue features outdoor seating and serves as a casual food and beverage stop for the community.

restaurant.name: Ricky's & Famoso
restaurant.desc: A dual-concept restaurant combining Ricky's breakfast café with Famoso Pizzeria, allowing cyclists to stop for either breakfast or pizza at a single location. Both brands operate together under FDF Restaurant Brandz ownership and management. This location on Sumas Way offers diverse dining options for touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Hellcrust Pizza
restaurant.desc: HellCrust Pizza is a franchise pizza chain with a North Vancouver location operating as a fast-food format. The location offers both indoor air-conditioned seating and outdoor seating, making it a potential mid-ride meal stop. A dedicated app and coupon program suggest it caters to frequent, convenience-oriented customers.

restaurant.name: Charlotte & the Quail Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Charlotte & the Quail is a farm-to-plate breakfast and lunch restaurant perched on the edge of a 10-acre botanical garden on Quayle Road, serving seasonal menus built around produce from neighbouring farms and Vancouver Island. It is directly accessible via the Galloping Goose and Lochside Trail, making it a natural destination stop on a cycling day. The restaurant has operated at this location since 2010 and dishes are garnished with edible flowers harvested fresh each morning.

notes.Packed lunches: Website offers 'picnic boxes to take away in the summer season' described as suitable for birthdays, showers, and group celebrations
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Many dishes are gluten free, all have lots of vegetables, and some are prepared with ethically raised meat.'
notes.Pump: Bike repair stand on-site described as offering 'just in case some air, a tire or a seat fix' — confirms air/pump access

restaurant.name: Fable
restaurant.desc: Fable Kitchen is a farm-to-table sit-down restaurant in Kitsilano's West 4th corridor, open since 2012 and built around locally sourced, seasonal ingredients that change with the menu. Head chef Michael Broadbent leads a team known for creative cuisine paired with a notable cocktail and wine program. The restaurant has been featured in the Michelin Guide Vancouver coverage and multiple Best Brunch lists, making it a noteworthy destination on a popular cycling corridor.

restaurant.name: Rainbow Butterfly
restaurant.desc: Rainbow Butterfly is a Chinese restaurant in North Vancouver. Additional details about amenities and facilities were unavailable for verification.

restaurant.name: Uprising Breads Bakery
restaurant.desc: Uprising Breads Bakery Café is a 40-plus-year community institution at the corner of Venables and Commercial Drive in East Vancouver, baking multigrain breads, pastries, and honey-sweetened goods on site every morning. The café serves a full lunch menu of homemade soups, hot savory items, and sandwiches made on fresh-baked bread, alongside espresso drinks. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available in a bright, welcoming space that locals describe as a neighborhood meeting spot.

restaurant.name: Angels Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Angels Ice Cream is an artisan gelato and gift shop on White Rock's famous Marine Drive, steps from the beach promenade and pier — a natural stop for cyclists riding the waterfront. The shop offers handcrafted gelato alongside coffee, gifts, jewellery, and seashells, blending a sweet treat with a souvenir experience. Its location on one of BC's most scenic coastal cycling routes makes it a memorable mid-ride destination.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: OSM description tag lists 'Vegan Flavors' as an explicit offering

restaurant.name: Dalina
restaurant.desc: Dalina is a small cafe in Vancouver's Broadway-Oak neighborhood offering indoor seating. Specifics about menu offerings, service options, and cyclist amenities could not be verified due to website access issues.

restaurant.name: Tacofino
restaurant.desc: Tacofino is a BC-born taco chain that grew from a Tofino food truck into a multi-location restaurant group serving West Coast-inspired Mexican food. The Kitsilano outpost sits directly on West 4th Avenue, one of Vancouver's busiest protected cycling corridors linking Point Grey to downtown. It is a well-known casual stop with pickup ordering available through multiple platforms.

restaurant.name: Hanks
restaurant.desc: Hanks is a small, independently operated restaurant on Douglas Street in downtown Victoria, built around an ever-changing menu sourced directly from local farmers and fishers. The kitchen leans into flavour combinations you don't typically encounter, served in a casual, deliberately loud setting. A touring cyclist rolling into the city centre would find a neighbourhood spot with a strong local identity and a rotating selection of ingredient-driven dishes.

detail.address: G3 - 1001 Douglas St, Victoria, BC V8W 2C5

restaurant.name: Aroma Pizza
restaurant.desc: Aroma Pizza is a long-established Italian restaurant in Kelowna that claims to have been serving pizza, pasta, subs, and focaccia since 1978. Located in a commercial unit on Kane Road, it offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery. The About page lists free Wi-Fi, parking, and live music as in-house amenities.

restaurant.name: Come Along Seafood Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Come Along Seafood Restaurant serves Chinese seafood cuisine in Vancouver. The restaurant's web presence is currently under development, limiting verification of current operations and amenities.

restaurant.name: Tim Hortons
restaurant.desc: Tim Hortons is Canada's ubiquitous quick-service coffee and food chain, and this Chilliwack location on Vedder Road offers both dine-in and drive-thru service. The menu spans freshly brewed coffee, soups, wraps, baked goods, and Timbits, making it a practical rest stop for cyclists needing a hot meal or a caffeine fix. The location is wheelchair accessible and includes free Wi-Fi.

detail.address: 6640 Vedder Rd Unit 100c, Chilliwack, BC V2R 0J2

restaurant.name: Sushi Crave
restaurant.desc: Sushi Crave is a sushi restaurant located in a unit within a commercial strip at 10880 Number 5 Road in Richmond, BC. The Number 5 Road corridor runs through agricultural and commercial areas of Richmond and is traveled by cyclists exploring the city's flat, bikeable terrain. Touring cyclists in the area may find this spot a convenient stop for Japanese cuisine.

restaurant.name: Kokanee Pub

restaurant.name: Cumberland Village Bakery

Cumberland is a renowned mountain biking destination, and this bakery is a beloved and iconic stop in the village core.

restaurant.name: Fanny Bay Inn

restaurant.name: Beatniks Bistro

The bistro serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner alongside a seasonal patio recognized as one of the top patios in the Fraser Valley. Live music every Thursday evening makes it a particularly lively stop for cyclists riding through the historic village of Fort Langley.

restaurant.name: The Station Pub

It sits on 6th Avenue in the heart of the Columbia Valley, a popular region for cycling the Kootenay Rockies. The patio and full kitchen make it a natural mid-ride stop for cyclists exploring the valley.

restaurant.name: Mr Mikes

The Terrace location welcomes walk-ins and accepts reservations, and the brand positions itself as a welcoming community gathering spot for locals and tourists alike. Touring cyclists passing through Terrace's North Coast corridor will find it a full sit-down dining option with online ordering and takeout available.

restaurant.name: Eagle's Eye
restaurant.desc: Eagle's Eye is a mountaintop restaurant perched at the summit of Kicking Horse Mountain Resort near Golden, BC, marketed as Canada's most elevated dining experience. Diners reach it exclusively by gondola, gazing over five national parks while enjoying seasonal menus crafted by resort chefs. The restaurant has earned over 250 'excellent' ratings on TripAdvisor and also hosts special dining events; it operates in both winter and summer seasons.

restaurant.name: Ocean Park Pizza
restaurant.desc: Ocean Park Pizza & Village Pub is a family-owned restaurant and pub anchoring the Ocean Park neighbourhood of South Surrey since 1978, earning multiple readers' choice awards for best pizza and best pub from Lower Mainland newspapers. The Craftsman-style building, rebuilt in 2006, houses a full pub with 20 beers on tap alongside classic pizzas and an expanded menu. Nearly five decades of community involvement — sponsoring local sports teams, youth groups, and charities — make it a genuine neighbourhood institution.

restaurant.name: Pita Pit

restaurant.name: BarBurrito

For a touring cyclist grinding through northern BC, this is a rare oasis with a wide range of services in an otherwise very sparse corridor.

restaurant.name: Skookumchuck Bakery & Cafe

The bakery is renowned for its 'Skookum' cinnamon buns and serves sandwiches on house-made organic sourdough, espresso drinks, smoothies, and a rotating selection of baked goods using local and organic ingredients. It sits at the end of a short walk along Doriston Highway and makes an ideal stop for cyclists doing the Sunshine Coast before or after the 4 km hike to the Narrows.

restaurant.name: Lighthouse Pub

The scenic wharf-side setting makes it a natural rest stop for cyclists riding the Sunshine Coast.

restaurant.name: Mikado Sushi

The restaurant is currently operating take-out only, making it a practical stop for cyclists passing through town who want a quick, quality meal to go. Princeton sits along popular cycling routes in the Similkameen Valley, and Mikado's diverse menu includes options for a range of dietary needs.

restaurant.name: Hong Kong Restaurant

detail.address: 111 Chartrand Ave, Logan Lake, BC V0K 1W0, Canada

restaurant.name: CorLan Vineyard & Farm
restaurant.desc: CorLan Vineyard & Farm is a 10-acre, 100% certified organic boutique winery and farm on Denman Island, producing award-winning wines under the 'To Ewe' label — including four gold medals at international competitions. Owners Pat and Selwyn Jones cleared the property in 2006, planted 5,000 vines from their own cuttings, and opened to the public in 2015; the estate now includes a tasting room, a restaurant, and farm stay accommodation. Cyclists can walk the vineyard and gardens, sample wines in the tasting room, and enjoy homemade lunches in a scenic south-facing forest setting.

detail.address: 8441 McFarlane Rd, Denman Island, BC V0R 1T0

restaurant.name: Islander Pizza & Pasta
restaurant.desc: Islander Pizza & Pasta is a fast food restaurant serving pizza and pasta on Vancouver Island, offering convenient meal options for touring cyclists in the region.

restaurant.name: Clam Bucket Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Clam Bucket Restaurant is a seafood-focused destination on the Port Alberni waterfront, self-billed as 'world famous' for its West Coast seafood. Customer reviews highlight generous portions of fish and chips, chowder, salmon, and prawns, along with an outdoor patio that buzzes in season. It sits at the heart of Port Alberni's Victoria Quay, making it a natural and memorable stop for cyclists touring central Vancouver Island.

restaurant.name: Paparazzi Pizza
restaurant.desc: Paparazzi Pizza is a fast-food pizza restaurant on Franklin Avenue. It operates as a quick-service establishment serving pizza to customers. Touring cyclists in the area can find this pizza spot for a meal break during their travels.

restaurant.name: Smitty's
restaurant.desc: Smitty's is a Canadian family restaurant chain operating since 1960, with this location on Comox Avenue serving the Comox Valley on Vancouver Island. The chain positions itself as 'more than breakfast,' offering a full all-day menu. A familiar and accessible stop for touring cyclists making their way through the Comox area.

restaurant.name: Delphi Cafe
restaurant.desc: Delphi Cafe is a restaurant featuring regional cuisine on Willowbrook Drive. It provides a dining option for the local community and area visitors.

restaurant.name: Backeddy Marine Pub
restaurant.desc: Backeddy Resort & Marina is a remote waterfront resort on BC's Sunshine Coast near Egmont, built along 600 feet of shoreline on the Sechelt Inlet, with an oceanfront pub serving food and craft beer alongside a full-service marina. The pub features live music most weekends and an on-site fleet of mountain bike rentals for exploring the surrounding trails and Skookumchuk Narrows Provincial Park. Reached via the Langdale ferry and a scenic drive up Highway 101, it is a notable destination stop on the Sunshine Coast cycling route.

restaurant.name: Granny's Chicken & Grill
restaurant.desc: Granny's Chicken is a fast food restaurant located at 3675 3rd Avenue in Port Alberni on Vancouver Island. It sits on a main arterial street that touring cyclists passing through the Alberni Valley would naturally use. Its current operating status is uncertain as the business's previously listed website domain now hosts an entirely different restaurant.

restaurant.name: Zythos Greek Restaurant;Zythos
restaurant.desc: Zythos Greek Mediterranean Grill is a full-service Greek restaurant in Langley's Port Kells neighbourhood, seating up to 85 people with a private party room for groups of up to 26. The menu centres on traditional Greek fare including souvlaki, roast lamb, spanakopita, and house salads. Touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley will find a substantial sit-down meal option as well as pickup and delivery through major platforms.

restaurant.name: Firecrust Neapolitan Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Firecrust Neapolitan Pizzeria is a fast-casual chain specializing in customizable Neapolitan-style pizzas and salads built from over 30 premium ingredients, including a notable range of vegan substitutes. Inspired by authentic Naples pizzerias, the restaurant uses non-GMO 00 flour and Italian tomato sauce for its bases. The Langley location is one of two BC outposts in a small Canadian franchise and offers dine-in, takeout, and third-party delivery.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists Vegan Sausage, Vegan Chicken, Vegan Mozza (contains nuts), Vegan Parmesan, and Vegan Hickory BBQ Sauce; vegetarian pizzas include Margherita, Vegetale, and Quattro Formaggi. No gluten-free option mentioned

restaurant.name: Foolish Wine
restaurant.desc: Foolish Wine is a small, family-run winery founded by the Coghill and Main families — the same duo behind Neighbourhood Brewing — situated in Oliver's District Wine Village in the heart of BC wine country. The winery produces terroir-driven, old-world-inspired wines from their North Naramata home vineyard and carefully selected Okanagan growers, releasing modest case quantities from a boutique cellar. The Village setting also hosts live music events, making it a lively stop for cyclists riding through the South Okanagan.

restaurant.name: Jimy Mac's Neighbourhood Pub
restaurant.desc: Jimy Mac's is a neighbourhood pub and liquor store in Langley, BC, serving a full menu of pub classics from weekend brunch through late-night burgers and share plates. The pub pours a broad selection of local and imported draught beers, house cocktails, and wine, and offers a delivery service. Cyclists on the Fraser Valley road network will find it a convenient full-service stop for a substantial meal in a casual community setting.

restaurant.name: Waffle Bar
restaurant.desc: The Waffle Bar is a made-to-order waffle counter nestled within Krause Berry Farms & Estate Winery, a family-owned Fraser Valley farm that has been operating since 1974 across more than 200 acres. Toppings rotate with the seasons — summer brings fresh strawberries, raspberries, and blueberries harvested directly from the surrounding fields, while winter and spring feature warm fruit compotes. It is a distinctive, farm-direct food stop in the agricultural flatlands east of Langley, with takeout served in fully biodegradable packaging.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegan Gluten-Friendly Waffle confirmed on menu (made with soy, rice flour, potato starch, tapioca starch, coconut milk, topped with vegan coco whip). Note: website explicitly states this is not a certified gluten-free facility and cross-contamination is possible

restaurant.name: Oya
restaurant.desc: Oya is a fusion Japanese cuisine restaurant housed inside the Hearthstone Lodge Building at Sun Peaks Resort, a year-round mountain destination popular with skiers and mountain bikers. The kitchen rotates its menu regularly and offers a diverse sake selection, aiming to give returning guests something new each visit. Its compact resort-village location makes it one of the primary sit-down dining options within easy reach of the Sun Peaks resort core.

detail.address: 3170 Creekside Way, Unit 230, Sun Peaks, BC V0E 5N0

restaurant.name: Caffe Americano
restaurant.desc: Caffe Americano is a community-rooted café and restaurant in downtown Trail, BC, established in 2001 and named in tribute to victims of the 9/11 attacks. The kitchen produces a wide range of house-made food — from wood-fired pizzas and Italian-inspired burgers to fresh daily baking, soups, and gourmet take-home meals — alongside a full espresso and smoothie bar. The same building houses Esposito's Boutique Hotel, with suites overlooking the Columbia River in the heart of a Kootenay cycling hub.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Vegetarian pizza explicitly listed; 'Veggie Pot Pies' and 'Vegetarian Lasagna' listed in Gourmet to Go. No vegan or GF claims found

restaurant.name: Ying Cafe
restaurant.desc: Ying Cafe is a Chinese restaurant on Columbia Avenue in the Kootenays. It provides sit-down dining to traveling cyclists and local customers.

restaurant.name: Ironworks Café & Crêperie
restaurant.desc: Ironworks Café & Crêperie is a Vancouver Island cafe chain founded in 2018 by owner Dina Stuehler, built around made-from-scratch Belgian-style crepes — both sweet and savoury — paired with locally-roasted Italian coffee. The cafe accommodates a wide range of dietary needs through gluten-free buckwheat and whole wheat vegan batters, with a vegetarian savoury crepe also on the menu. Current locations are in Duncan and Nanaimo, making it a well-regarded food stop for cyclists passing through either community.

detail.address: 5262 Argyle St Unit G, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 1T9

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists Gluten-Free Buckwheat Batter and Whole Wheat Vegan Batter; multiple items marked vegan-substitutable (*) and gluten-free (+); a dedicated Veggie Crepe is listed. Note: website states kitchen cannot safely accommodate celiac disease due to cross-contamination risk

restaurant.name: Home Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Home Restaurant is a community staple in Salmon Arm, serving classic North American comfort food for over two decades from its perch near the Salmon Arm Wharf and surrounding hiking trails. Part of a small BC chain, the Salmon Arm location is a sit-down diner-style restaurant with a broad menu spanning all-day breakfast, burgers, and house-made pies. Its location at the top of the hill near outdoor recreation corridors makes it a natural refueling stop for cyclists passing through.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items explicitly marked GF, including Eggs Only Breakfast, Broccoli & Cheddar Omelette, Ham & Swiss Omelette, HOME Country Omelette, and Farmer's Sausage & Eggs

restaurant.name: Love's Ice Cream
restaurant.desc: Love's Ice Cream is an artisan shop in Cumberland, BC, crafting small-batch ice cream from locally sourced whole ingredients — including high-fat grass-fed cow milk and full-fat coconut milk for vegan varieties — served in hand-rolled waffle cones. Founded by sisters Rachel and Sanchia, the business grew from a vision of bringing genuinely wholesome frozen treats to a town that previously only had chemically processed options. Cumberland is one of Vancouver Island's premier cycling hubs, and the outdoor seating makes this a natural sweet stop for riders rolling through the village core.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Dedicated vegan ice cream line made from full fat coconut milk and coconut cream (Creamy Coconut and Chocolate Coconut flavours listed on website)

restaurant.name: UFO Ukrainian Food Awesome
restaurant.desc: UFO Ukrainian Food Awesome is a restaurant serving Ukrainian cuisine on Main Street in BC's North Coast region. The playful acronym name — Ukrainian Food Awesome — hints at a casual, character-driven dining experience. For touring cyclists riding through this relatively remote corridor, a sit-down restaurant specializing in hearty Eastern European fare could be a welcome and memorable stop.

restaurant.name: One Tiny Farm
restaurant.desc: One Tiny Farm is a community growing space on the Sunshine Coast operated by One Straw Society, a registered Canadian charity building a sustainable local food system. The farm hosts public events such as 'Tiny Farm, Big Table' dinners, seed exchanges, educational workshops, and farm tours, and is available to rent as a gathering space. Touring cyclists looking for a community food hub or local food event on the Sunshine Coast may find it a worthwhile detour.

restaurant.name: Pita Pit
restaurant.desc: Pita Pit is a national fast-food chain franchise located in Prince George's College Heights neighbourhood, serving customizable pita wraps, salads, and rice bowls made to order from a wide range of ingredients. It offers both takeout and delivery, making it a convenient quick-service stop for cyclists moving through the north end of Prince George. A loyalty rewards app is available for frequent visitors.

detail.address: 5240 Domano Boulevard, Prince George, BC V2N 4A1

restaurant.name: Savvios Family Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Established in 2006 in Oliver, BC, Savvios Family Restaurant sits in the heart of the Okanagan Valley wine country, serving Greek specialties, Italian dishes, steaks, and seafood alongside an extensive local wine list. The restaurant offers both indoor dining and patio seating, with regular lamb and pig BBQ events and live entertainment on the patio. Touring cyclists riding through wine country will find a full sit-down meal, takeout options, and walk-ins welcome.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu marks multiple items as vegetarian '(V)' (e.g. Spanakopita, Tiropita, Zucchini Sticks) and gluten-free '(GF)' (e.g. Garithes Skorthato, Greek Dip)

restaurant.name: Rock Water Grill & Bar
restaurant.desc: The Rockwater Grill & Bar is a full-service restaurant and entertainment venue in Golden, BC, with both a riverside patio and a rooftop patio along the Columbia Valley. It bills itself as the region's premier nightlife spot, hosting weekly live music spanning folk, punk rock, DJs, and comedy in a 360-person room. Touring cyclists finishing a day at Kicking Horse or in the Rockies will find a broad menu of hand-crafted food and cocktails in a lively, welcoming atmosphere.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'VEGAN SPINACH & ARTICHOKE DIP' (cashew base) and 'crispy tofu' as a salad add-on, confirming vegan options

restaurant.name: Trees
restaurant.desc: Trees Restaurant & Bakery is a full-service scratch kitchen and bakery on Vancouver Island's Alberni Highway in Parksville, serving breakfast, brunch, lunch, and dinner with a strong emphasis on fresh, locally sourced ingredients including island-raised free-range eggs and house-made breads. The menu is notable for its broad gluten-free offerings — including house-baked GF bread — and clearly labeled vegetarian options across multiple meal periods. A customer review notes a dog-friendly covered patio, which may appeal to cyclists travelling with pets.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Multiple menu items marked '*Vegetarian Options Available' and '*Gluten-Free Options Available'; customer review confirms house-made GF bread and GF croutons on-site

restaurant.name: The Woods
restaurant.desc: The Woods is a restaurant located within Big White Ski Resort, one of BC's largest ski destinations situated in the Okanagan highlands east of Kelowna. It operates as part of the resort's dining lineup in a mountain village setting. Big White is a four-season resort, and visiting cyclists may find it on route to or from the resort during summer operations.

restaurant.name: Sonbadas Steak House
restaurant.desc: Sonbadas Steakhouse is a long-standing Terrace institution, serving the community for over 50 years with AAA-plus sterling silver meats alongside homemade Greek dishes and fresh seafood — all made without preservatives or dyes. The menu spans brunch through dinner, with appetizers, pastas, salads, and a kids' menu, plus handcrafted cocktails, wine, and beer. Touring cyclists riding through the Skeena region will find a proper sit-down meal with online ordering and pickup available.

restaurant.name: Brown Bridge Pub
restaurant.desc: Brown Bridge Pub is a neighbourhood pub established in 2008 on Vermilion Avenue in Princeton, BC, in the Okanagan-Similkameen region. It serves a wide scratch-kitchen menu spanning wings, tacos, burgers, poutine, and ramen bowls alongside weekly specials. Princeton sits at a key crossroads for cyclists riding the Crowsnest Highway or exploring the Similkameen Valley, making this a natural mid-route meal stop.

restaurant.name: Yoko Sushi
restaurant.desc: Yoko Sushi & Noodle is a Japanese restaurant in Surrey's Fraser Valley serving sushi and noodle dishes. Located in a strip-mall unit on 56 Ave, it offers dine-in and online ordering. Touring cyclists passing through Surrey's suburban corridors will find it a convenient lunch or dinner stop.

restaurant.name: April Point Dining Room
restaurant.desc: April Point Dining Room is the restaurant of April Point Resort on Quadra Island, offering guests spectacular ocean views from its dining room and deck. The resort, operated by North Coast Hotel Resort Ltd., is a destination property in Quathiaski Cove with fishing, whale watching, and kayak rentals rounding out the experience. Touring cyclists making the ferry crossing to Quadra Island will find this a scenic spot for a sit-down meal in season.

restaurant.name: Land & Sea Tasting Room
restaurant.desc: Land & Sea Brewing Co. is a community-focused craft brewery and tasting room in Comox, BC, opened in December 2018 as the third craft brewery in the Comox Valley. The bright, welcoming space seats 70 guests indoors around an open kitchen, with a patio for 40 more on sunny days, and the brewery explicitly encourages cyclists to visit — calling it out in their parking policy alongside transit and walking. In-house craft beers are complemented by rotating BC guest taps and a small in-house food menu.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Gluten-free beer explicitly listed on the beer menu: 'Whistler Forager Lager - 375ml / 5% ABV'. No explicit mention of vegetarian or vegan food options in the available website content

restaurant.name: Trail Coffee & Tea Co.
restaurant.desc: Trail Coffee Co. is a downtown Trail café and in-house roastery serving fair-trade, organic espresso drinks alongside a from-scratch breakfast and lunch menu of sandwiches, wraps, and salads. The shop roasts its own beans on-site and sells them retail and wholesale, making it a genuine local coffee destination in the West Kootenays. Cyclists passing through Trail will find a full meal, quality espresso, and online ordering for quick pickup.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes clearly vegetarian items: The Gardener Wrap (chickpeas, artichokes, vegetables, no meat), Avo Toast, Bagel & Spread, and Green Goddess Salad. No explicit vegan or GF labelling on the published menu

restaurant.name: Flourishing Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Flourishing Chinese Seafood Restaurant is a family-owned Cantonese and Szechuan restaurant that has served the Langley community on Fraser Highway for over 25 years. The menu spans dim sum on Sundays, hot pot, sizzling teppan platters, fresh seafood, and customizable lunch combinations. A touring cyclist can order in, take out, or have food delivered, with customization available for dietary needs.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page states 'No ADDED MSG; vegetarian and gluten-free options are available upon request.'

restaurant.name: Oak & Thorne
restaurant.desc: Oak & Thorne is a sports-bar-style neighbourhood public house in Langley operated by the Joseph Richard Group, combining arcade games (ping-pong, foosball, Skee-Ball), a never-ending tap list, and large viewing screens for a game-day atmosphere. The menu spans pub classics to shared plates with a strong selection of dietary options, and the venue shifts into a nightlife destination on weekends. Outdoor seating is available, making it a viable refuelling stop for cyclists riding through the Fraser Valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website explicitly lists 'VEGETARIAN VEGAN GLUTEN AWARE DAIRY-FREE' as menu filter categories

restaurant.name: Kasiks Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Kasiks Kitchen is a café and bakery operated by the Kitsumkalum First Nation as part of their Kasiks Wilderness Resort, located on Tsimshian Traditional Territory along Highway 16 between Terrace and Prince Rupert. The kitchen serves fresh-baked goods, coffee, and made-in-house grab-and-go meals inspired by the flavours of the Northwest Coast, with pre-order options for house-made breads, pies, and specialty baked goods. The café earned broader recognition after being featured on Season 4, Episode 7 of Chuck's First Peoples' Kitchen, highlighting Indigenous food knowledge and the cultural connection to the land.

restaurant.name: The 626
restaurant.desc: The 626 is a multi-concept eatery in Masset on Haida Gwaii, built around fresh locally-caught halibut fish and chips but also serving handmade sourdough pizza, burgers, ice cream in 25 flavours, and craft cocktails from a novelty automated cocktail machine. What began as a food truck has grown into a full restaurant with a Haida Art Gallery showcasing local indigenous artists. Located on Main Street across from the Delmas Co-op, it is a distinctive culinary destination at the north end of Haida Gwaii.

detail.address: 2011 Harrison Ave.+Main St. Masset BC Canada V0T 1M0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Vegan options available'; menu includes a 'RICE AND BLACK BEAN VEGETARIAN' burrito; guacamole served with 'Gluten-free Corn Chips on the side'

restaurant.name: Desert Hills Ranch Taco Stand
restaurant.desc: Desert Hills Ranch is a family-owned BC farm operation since 1983, rooted in Ashcroft's rich volcanic soil and known for fresh produce. Their Cache Creek Taco Stand is a Mexican food outlet positioned on the Cariboo Highway (Hwy 97), making it a convenient warm-meal stop for cyclists traversing the Thompson River corridor. The stand operates under the same family umbrella as the main Ashcroft farm market, giving it a distinctly local character.

restaurant.name: Fruitvale Pub & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Fruitvale Pub & Grill is a neighbourhood pub on historic Main Street in the Beaver Valley, serving hand-ground burgers, dry ribs, crispy chicken, and fresh salads from an open-concept kitchen. It also operates a convenient to-go counter for cold beer, coolers, and wine — handy for cyclists stocking up mid-route. The relaxed atmosphere, local draft beer, and scratch-made sauces make it a genuine community gathering spot in the Kootenays.

restaurant.name: The Tree Hugger Smoothie & Juice Bar
restaurant.desc: The Tree Hugger Smoothie & Juice Bar is a juice-focused fast-food spot located in the Fraser Valley region of BC. Specializing in smoothies and juice bowls, it offers a refreshing stop for cyclists passing through the area. Its focus on fresh, plant-based drinks makes it a natural fit for health-conscious touring riders.

restaurant.name: Tonys Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Tonys Restaurant is a local eatery situated in British Columbia's remote Cariboo, Chilcotin and Central Interior region. For touring cyclists navigating this sparsely populated stretch of BC, it represents a potential resupply and meal stop in an area where services can be widely spaced. Beyond OSM tagging as a restaurant, details about the establishment remain unverifiable.

detail.address: 210 Chowsunket St, Fraser Lake, BC V0J 1S0, Canada

restaurant.name: Spice and Grill
restaurant.desc: Spice and Grill is an Indian restaurant in Hope, BC, offering a broad menu of South Asian classics — Butter Chicken, Tandoori specialties, biryanis, and an extensive vegetarian lineup alongside Indo-Chinese dishes and pizzas. The restaurant supports online ordering with both delivery and pickup, making it practical for cyclists who need a quick refuel or a full sit-down meal. Hope sits at the junction of the Trans-Canada and Crowsnest highways, making this a strategically placed dining stop for long-distance touring cyclists.

detail.address: 575 Old Hope Princeton Way, Hope, BC Canada V0X1L4

restaurant.name: Bigfoot Donuts
restaurant.desc: Bigfoot Donuts is a family-owned artisan bakery and espresso bar that has anchored Downtown Courtenay since 2017, known for handcrafted, made-from-scratch donuts and in-house roasted coffee. The name pays homage to the Pacific Northwest and Indigenous Sasquatch/B'gwus traditions, reflecting the owners' deep roots in the Comox Valley — a family business lineage stretching back to 1920. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a full breakfast and lunch menu alongside espresso drinks and a rotating lineup of fresh baked goods.

restaurant.name: J & L Drive-In
restaurant.desc: J & L Drive-In is a classic burger drive-in located in Port Alberni on Vancouver Island, serving quick meals in the traditional curbside style. The no-smoking policy (confirmed via OSM) makes it a comfortable roadside stop for cyclists moving through the Alberni Valley. Drive-in format means quick service without a long sit-down commitment.

restaurant.name: BFF Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: BFF Bar & Grill is a locally owned neighborhood restaurant in Prince George, founded by three partners and built around the idea that great food is best enjoyed with good company. The menu runs from classic comfort foods and bar bites to drinks specials, with a dedicated gluten-free menu and online ordering. It bills itself as a casual all-day spot equally suited to catching a game or sitting down for a proper meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page lists a dedicated 'Gluten Free Menu' section

restaurant.name: Mo's
restaurant.desc: Mo's Restaurant is a Port Hardy institution with over 24 years serving the community at the northern tip of Vancouver Island. The menu centres on freshly made pizza with a broad selection of toppings, alongside Greek pita wraps, gyros, donairs, fried chicken, chicken wings, salads, and soups. For cycle tourers reaching the end of the island route, it offers a well-rounded comfort-food stop with both pickup and delivery options.

detail.address: 7070 Market St., W Port Hardy, BC, V0N-2P0

restaurant.name: Jade Buffet
restaurant.desc: Jade Buffet of China is a Chinese and Western buffet restaurant situated on the Trans-Canada Highway in the heart of Salmon Arm, BC. The restaurant is known for its Asian buffet alongside a full a la carte menu, with dishes hand-prepared from locally sourced ingredients. Both dine-in and takeout are available, and an online ordering system makes it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan-Thompson corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu category 'Vegetarian' is explicitly listed on the website menu

restaurant.name: Cedar Cafe at CMTN
restaurant.desc: Cedar Cafe at CMTN is a weekday campus cafe serving Coast Mountain College in Terrace, BC, catering primarily to students and staff. Located on a post-secondary college campus, it offers a coffee shop experience in a busy educational setting. Touring cyclists passing through Terrace on Highway 16 may find it a convenient stop during college operating hours.

restaurant.name: The Brickhouse Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Brickhouse Bar & Grill occupies the main floor of Fernie's historic 1909 Imperial Bank of Canada Building, a Renaissance Revival heritage structure sensitively restored to blend original architectural elements with a modern mountain aesthetic. The venue serves a Mediterranean-influenced pub menu alongside live music, with windows that open to create a patio feel in the heart of Fernie's historic downtown. Owner Matt Brazeau is a long-standing figure in Fernie's hospitality scene, and the space also includes a lower-level venue called The Underground.

restaurant.name: Blue Ocean Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: Blue Ocean Bar & Grill is the full-service restaurant at Blue Ocean Golf Club in Sechelt on the Sunshine Coast, with capacity for up to 110 guests for lunch, dinner, and private events. It has built a reputation as a local favourite, with a dedicated head chef and recurring special events such as Prime Rib Nights and seasonal brunch buffets. The scenic golf course property makes it a worthwhile dining stop for cyclists touring the Sunshine Coast.

restaurant.name: Likely Lodge
restaurant.desc: Likely Lodge is a combined hotel, restaurant, and pub in the tiny, remote community of Likely, BC, deep in the Cariboo region near Quesnel Lake. It serves American cuisine and operates a separate pub, making it a rare full-service stop in an otherwise sparsely serviced stretch of the Cariboo backroads. The lodge also functions as a hub for area information on circle tours, hiking, and fishing.

restaurant.name: Papa's Burgers
restaurant.desc: Papa's Burgers is a homestyle burger joint on Vancouver Island's Highway 19A corridor in Parksville, known for hand-cut fries, creamy milkshakes, and poutine made from fresh daily ingredients. The restaurant has built a strong local following with consistently five-star Google reviews praising food quality and service. A touring cyclist rolling through Parksville would find this a well-regarded quick-service stop with online ordering available.

restaurant.name: Bakkerij Lobelle
restaurant.desc: Bakkerij Lobelle is a Dutch-named bakery-café tucked into the Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior region of BC, a stretch of highway that sees touring cyclists crossing vast distances between supply points. The Dutch 'bakkerij' suggests European baking traditions — a potential standout in a region where fresh baked goods are rare. For cyclists grinding through the interior plateau, a bakery stop can be a significant morale boost.

detail.address: 153 Stewart St E, Vanderhoof, BC V0J 0A8, Canada

restaurant.name: PHO TRAN
restaurant.desc: Pho Tran is a Vietnamese restaurant on Fraser Highway in Aldergrove, BC, focused on delivering authentic Asian cuisine in a welcoming dining environment. It is a sit-down restaurant with online ordering available, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley corridor. The restaurant emphasizes the dining experience and pride in their Vietnamese dishes.

restaurant.name: The Shady Rest Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A historic waterfront institution on Qualicum Beach's Island Highway, The Shady Rest has operated since 1924 and encompasses a family-friendly restaurant, an adult-only (19+) pub, and a liquor store — all perched on the shore with ocean views. The pub rotates local craft taps and hosts weekly live music and trivia nights. Takeout is available by phone, making it a practical stop for cyclists passing through on the Island Highway.

detail.address: 3109 West Island Hwy, Qualicum Beach, BC, V9K 2C5

restaurant.name: Marg's Bar
restaurant.desc: A bar located on Wakas Drive in the North Coast & Haida Gwaii region. Serves as a local gathering point for the community.

restaurant.name: Strait Coffee Traders
restaurant.desc: Strait Coffee is a café and in-house roastery that has been serving the Wilson Creek area of Sechelt since 1996, growing from a small space into a larger corner location at Wilson Creek Plaza on the Sunshine Coast Highway. The café offers an extensive made-from-scratch menu spanning specialty espresso drinks, full breakfasts, sandwiches, and wraps alongside retail and wholesale coffee beans roasted on-site. A wholesale operation runs in parallel, making it a notable regional coffee producer as well as a full-service sit-down café.

detail.address: Unit 1, 4330 Sunshine Coast Hwy, Sechelt, BC

restaurant.name: Moku Famous Hawaiian Bbq
restaurant.desc: Moku Famous Hawaiian Bbq is a Hawaiian-style barbecue restaurant located in the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley region of British Columbia. The name 'Moku' references the Hawaiian concept of an island district, suggesting a menu rooted in the smoky, sweet flavours of Hawaiian plate-lunch and BBQ tradition. It is a compact stop for touring cyclists seeking a hearty, flavourful meal after a long ride through the Fraser Valley corridor.

detail.address: 8353 200A St #120, Langley Twp, BC V2Y 5K5, Canada

restaurant.name: Wildflower Bakeshop and Cafe
restaurant.desc: Wildflower Bakeshop and Cafe is a community-oriented brunch cafe in Port Alberni's Alberni Valley, founded by a husband-and-wife team with over 30 years of combined hospitality experience. The kitchen works entirely from scratch using organic, seasonal ingredients sourced from local Vancouver Island farmers and the team's own garden, with a drinks list featuring exclusively BC craft beers, ciders, and natural wines. It's a dog-friendly, welcoming spot that also offers DoorDash delivery and made-to-order custom cakes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'Many of our dishes are easily modified to accommodate gluten free, dairy free, and vegan diets.'

restaurant.name: Kelly & Carlos O'Bryan's
restaurant.desc: Kelly & Carlos O'Bryan's is an Irish-themed neighborhood restaurant and pub chain with a Courtenay outpost that has been serving the Comox Valley for over six years.
