The kitchen follows traditional North Indian and Mughalai culinary traditions, with signature dishes like butter chicken, saffron biryani, and a range of tandoor-cooked items. Catering is also available for groups, and the restaurant welcomes customization of spice levels on any menu item.

detail.address: 487 East Island Hwy, Parksville, BC V9P 1T5

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian options including Veggie Samosa, Vegetable Pakora, Onion Bhaji, Paneer Pakora, Paneer Tikka, and a Vegetables Dish category

restaurant.name: Realm Food Co
restaurant.desc: Realm Food Co is a locally-focused eatery in Parksville, BC, built around seasonal, farm-sourced ingredients and a strong commitment to supporting Vancouver Island growers. The menu is broad and accommodating, spanning tacos, ramen, sandwiches, and substantial salads with clear GF, vegan, and dairy-free labelling throughout. Takeout and catering are available, and the kitchen cooks fresh to order, making it a solid meal stop for cyclists with varied dietary needs.

detail.address: Unit 2 - 180 Craig Street, Parksville, BC V9P 2G8

notes.Takeout: Website footer explicitly states 'CATERING. TAKE OUT. NO RESERVATIONS.'
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu items consistently tagged V (vegan), GF (gluten-free), DF (dairy-free), NF; about page states 'From vegan to paleo and everything in-between' and notes kitchen accommodates dietary needs to order

restaurant.name: Cravings Brookswood Coffee & Bakery
restaurant.desc: Cravings Brookswood Restaurant presents itself online as a Korean food destination offering fried chicken, kimchi rice, mussel soup, and traditional dishes available for online ordering. The OSM record places it in the Brookswood area of Langley, but the website lists a Vancouver (Davie St) address, raising significant uncertainty about whether the business still operates at the mapped location. The relaxed, cozy environment described on the site would otherwise be a welcome stop for cyclists in the Fraser Valley.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: A Subway sandwich franchise situated on Highway 97 in Clinton, BC, a small interior town and common waypoint for cyclists riding the Cariboo Highway corridor. As one of the few chain food options in this stretch of the BC interior, it offers a predictable, relatively quick meal stop with customizable sandwiches. Clinton sits roughly midway between Cache Creek and 100 Mile House, making this a practical refueling point on a multi-day touring route.

restaurant.name: Cafe Mount Robson
restaurant.desc: Cafe Mt Robson is a historic stop at the base of Mount Robson Provincial Park, operating for over 100 years along Yellowhead Highway 16 between Jasper and McBride. The cafe micro-roasts organic, fairly traded coffee in small batches and offers a broad menu spanning espresso drinks, Napoli-style pizza, chuck wagon BBQ burgers, soups, and homemade baked goods. Sitting at the gateway to the tallest peak in the Canadian Rockies and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, it is a natural landmark rest stop for cyclists riding the Yellowhead corridor.

detail.address: 18344 Yellowhead Highway 16, Mount Robson, BC, Canada

restaurant.name: The Turning Point
restaurant.desc: The Turning Point is a family-style restaurant in Golden, BC that has been a local institution for over 35 years. The menu is wide-ranging, spanning pizzas (including the locally celebrated Terminator Ridge), burgers, pasta dishes, butter chicken, and fish and chips, with weekly specials and a kids' menu. For touring cyclists rolling through the Columbia Valley, it offers a solid sit-down meal with the option to order online for pickup.

restaurant.name: Roberts Lake Resort
restaurant.desc: Roberts Lake Resort is a rustic lakeside retreat nestled in BC's Sayward Rain Forest, roughly midway between Campbell River and Sayward on Vancouver Island. Family-owned for 47 years, it offers furnished cabin rentals and RV lots steps from a white sandy beach, with canoes and kayaks for rent and access to trails including nearby Ripple Rock. Touring cyclists riding the Campbell River–Sayward corridor would find it a remote but well-appointed overnight stop.

detail.address: PO BOX 488 Campbell River, BC V9W 5C1

notes.Wi-Fi: Homepage states 'Wi-Fi access' as a modern convenience; cabin rentals page confirms 'All cabins also have easy access to... Wi-Fi'; RV FAQ states 'all our cabins equipped with Wi-Fi' — coverage for RV/camping area not explicitly confirmed

restaurant.name: The Artful Dodger Pub
restaurant.desc: The Artful Dodger is a neighbourhood pub in Langley, BC, serving a full food and bar menu alongside an on-site liquor store. It runs a community shuttle service on Friday and Saturday evenings within 10km, reflecting its strong local character in the Fraser Valley. Touring cyclists can stop in for a sit-down meal or call ahead for takeout.

restaurant.name: Omai Sushi
restaurant.desc: Omai Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Langley, BC, serving contemporary Japanese cuisine with an emphasis on fresh, high-quality ingredients in generous portions. It brands itself as the best-value sushi option in Langley and sits near the Langley ICBC Driver Licensing office on Willowbrook Drive. Online ordering and free delivery are available alongside dine-in service.

detail.address: 19950 Willowbrook Dr #4, Langley Twp, BC V2Y 1A2

restaurant.name: Seven Summits Coffee
restaurant.desc: Seven Summits Coffee Company is a specialty coffee roaster with a public coffee bar in the heart of Rossland, BC, serving locally baked goods alongside their artisan roasted beans. The company sells beans, brewing equipment, and merchandise online and through retail partners across the Kootenays. For a touring cyclist, it offers a dedicated café experience in a mountain town well-known for outdoor adventure.

detail.address: 2044 Columbia Ave, Rossland, British Columbia V0G 1Y0

restaurant.name: Bugwood
restaurant.desc: Bugwood Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe on Main Street in downtown Smithers, BC, housed in a distinctive timber-frame building constructed from mountain pine beetle-damaged 'bugwood' lumber — the forestry history that gives it its name and character. Founded by Nick and Mika Meyer, who drew on their own forestry backgrounds, the business sources and hand-roasts its own beans and has earned a strong local reputation as Smithers' best coffee, complete with a sample bar and regular latte art events. A separate roastery and coffee-education space operates nearby on Fulton Ave, making it a genuine destination for coffee-curious touring cyclists passing through north-central BC.

restaurant.name: Nikko Sushi
restaurant.desc: A sushi restaurant located in a multi-unit commercial building. Website unavailable, limiting information about menu, service style, or amenities available to touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Kevins Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Kevin's Kitchen is a traditional Chinese home-style restaurant in downtown Revelstoke specializing in hand-made dumplings, wonton soup, noodle soups, and Northern Chinese cold salads. Situated on 1st Street West in a mountain town that draws cyclists from across BC and beyond, it offers a full sit-down meal of house-made comfort food including hand-folded JiaoZi and SaoZi noodle soups.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists explicit 'Vegetable Only' protein substitution for noodle soups and chow mein; cold vegetable salads include smashed cucumber, red cabbage, and shredded LoBok; FuZhu dish is tofu skin with vegetables

restaurant.name: Riverhouse At The Aspen
restaurant.desc: The Riverhouse Restaurant is a full-service restaurant and lounge attached to the Aspen Inn & Suites in Smithers, offering breakfast, lunch, and dinner in what it describes as a 'thoroughly unique atmosphere.' It can accommodate groups of up to 150 people with buffet or à la carte options, making it a notable stop for larger cycling groups. Located on Highway 16, it sits on a major touring corridor through north-central BC.

restaurant.name: Freddie's Pub
restaurant.desc: Freddie's Pub is a neighbourhood pub on South Island Highway in the Vancouver Island & Gulf Islands region of British Columbia. The OSM record includes a building footprint and a BC-area-code phone number, suggesting an established, physical venue. No further details about the interior, offerings, or cyclist facilities are available from verified sources at this time.

restaurant.name: Ban Chok Dee
restaurant.desc: Ban Chok Dee is an award-winning Thai restaurant in Langley City holding 'Thai Select Premium' status granted by the Royal Thai Consulate General for authentic and outstanding Thai cuisine. The restaurant uses a mix of locally grown and imported traditional ingredients and offers a full sit-down dining environment styled with traditional Thai decor. A second location operates in Maple Ridge, and both can host large groups of up to 80 people.

restaurant.name: Old Abbey Ales
restaurant.desc: Old Abbey Ales is a small-batch craft brewery and tasting room in Abbotsford, BC, founded in 2013 and brewing since 2015, with a community-first ethos where a suggestion board on the tasting room wall shapes what ends up on tap. The brewery specializes in unconventional styles—from a chai-spiced hazy to an award-winning local raspberry sour—using Fraser Valley ingredients throughout. Cyclists travelling the Fraser Highway corridor can stop in for fresh pours of a rotating lineup that spans lagers, IPAs, and fruit sours.

restaurant.name: Domino's Pizza
restaurant.desc: Domino's Pizza in Gibsons is a franchise location on the Sunshine Coast, serving pizza, cheesy bread, chicken, and desserts with both delivery and carryout options. It sits along the main Sunshine Coast Highway corridor that touring cyclists traverse between Langdale Ferry and Sechelt. The store accepts cards and cash and carries vegetarian pizza options.

detail.address: 1100 Sunshine Coast Hwy Unit 108, Gibsons, BC V0N1V0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Coupons page lists a Veggie pizza among featured options

restaurant.name: Pind Balluchi North Indian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Pind Balluchi is a North Indian restaurant in Williams Lake, BC, serving a broad menu of tandoori dishes, curries, biryanis, and street-food appetizers. It stands out as one of the few Indian dining options in the Cariboo interior, making it a notable meal stop for cyclists on long-haul routes through the region. Online ordering with 15-minute pickup is available, which suits cyclists who want a hot meal ready on arrival.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu page includes a dedicated 'Vegetarian Dishes' section with items such as Vegetable Korma, Aloo Gobi, Palak Paneer, Dal Makhani, Chana Masala, Malai Kofta, and others. No explicit vegan or GF labelling found

restaurant.name: Lunchbox
restaurant.desc: The Lunchbox is a fresh-focused eatery in downtown Fernie run by longtime hospitality veterans Jarod and Erin Rae, specializing in homemade wraps, curries, soups, and salads built entirely from scratch. The menu leans on bold flavours — think slow-roasted pulled pork wraps, authentic curries over rice or noodles, and a rotating fresh soup of the day served with a bread roll. The business also operates a food truck component, making it a flexible stop for cyclists passing through the Elk Valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly states 'All Wraps can be made gluten free with your choice of a Rice Bowl or Quinoa Bowl.' Dedicated vegetarian items include Falafel Wrap, Garden of Fernie salad, and Thai Peanut salad with marinated tofu

restaurant.name: Edo Japan
restaurant.desc: Edo Japan Courtenay Crossing is a Japanese-inspired fast-casual franchise in the Courtenay Crossing strip mall on Cliffe Avenue, serving teppanyaki grilled meals, hand-rolled sushi, ramen, and bubble tea. Founded in Calgary in 1979, it is one of Canada's largest teriyaki chains with over 200 locations nationwide. Touring cyclists will find a full dine-in room alongside takeout and delivery options.

restaurant.name: I&J FUSION
restaurant.desc: I&J Fusion is a family-owned Pan Asian restaurant in Creston, BC, run by Isabel and John, who make all sauces, noodles, and desserts from scratch using fresh, local ingredients. The dining room offers views of the surrounding mountains and valley, giving touring cyclists a scenic stop in the Kootenays. The menu spans lunch and dinner with a range of fusion Asian dishes, bubble tea, and a strong selection of gluten-free, dairy-free, and vegetarian options.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We also strive to offer a large selection of gluten free, dairy free, and vegetarian options.'

restaurant.name: Silverado
restaurant.desc: Silverado is a cafe in a remote stretch of Northern BC, tagged as serving cafe fare alongside pizza and burgers — a combination that could make it a welcome full-meal stop for cyclists traveling through one of BC's most sparsely serviced regions. Its location near the BC-Alaska border corridor means it may be one of very few food options for long-distance tourers passing through. The Facebook page could not be retrieved, so details about the interior, seating, and services remain unconfirmed.

restaurant.name: Ryan's Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Ryan's Pizzeria is a fast-food pizza outlet located on Vancouver Island in the Campbell River area, occupying unit A of its building. It offers a quick, informal stop for cyclists traveling the Island Highway corridor who need a hot meal without a long sit-down wait.

detail.address: Unit A, Campbell River area, BC

restaurant.name: Strawberry Moose
restaurant.desc: A cafe offering outdoor seating and takeaway service in the Cariboo region. A potential refreshment stop for cyclists travelling through the area.

restaurant.name: Chutney's Indian Grill
restaurant.desc: Chutneys Indian Grill is a fast-casual Indian restaurant chain serving fresh, modern Indian food including tandoori dishes, stuffed buns, and build-your-own bowls. The Langley location is one of three Lower Mainland branches of a BC-based franchise positioning itself as a quick, healthy alternative to typical fast food. Touring cyclists will find it a convenient stop for a filling sit-down or takeout meal along the 200 Street corridor.

restaurant.name: Brown's Socialhouse Langley Centre
restaurant.desc: A regional cuisine restaurant with outdoor seating located in Langley Centre. Part of the established Brown's Socialhouse chain, this casual dining venue provides a stop for locals and touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Quesnel Bakery
restaurant.desc: Quesnel Bakery is a local bakery serving the Quesnel area in BC's Cariboo region. For touring cyclists passing through this stretch of the interior, it represents a potential stop for fresh baked goods on a route that can be remote between larger centres. The OSM record was verified as recently as August 2023.

detail.address: 468 Reid St, Quesnel, BC V2J 2M6, Canada

restaurant.name: Nasir's Super Donair
restaurant.desc: A fast-food kebab establishment specializing in donairs and Middle Eastern street food. Located in the Kamloops area with free Wi-Fi access, it provides quick dining for touring cyclists passing through the region.

restaurant.name: Big Bang bagels
restaurant.desc: Big Bang Bagels is a beloved Fernie institution that has been hand-making fresh bagels every morning for over 10 years. Located on 2nd Avenue in the heart of town, it's known as the busiest café in Fernie, with lineups out the door during peak seasons. Touring cyclists will find a huge variety of hearty bagelwiches and breakfast bagels—perfect fuel for a day in the saddle through the Elk Valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Gluten-free bagels available (not baked in-store). Vegetarian options include Avolauncher (avocado, red onion, cream cheese, cheddar) and spinach & sprouts substitutions. Allergen notice lists nuts, eggs, milk, seeds, flour, fish on site

restaurant.name: Heaven's Door Yurt cafe
restaurant.desc: Heaven's Door Yurt is a casual yurt-style café set at the base of the Stairway to Heaven chairlift at Kicking Horse Mountain Resort near Golden, BC. It serves beverages, build-your-own hot dogs, grilled sandwiches, and more in a distinctive rustic shelter. The venue is well-positioned for mountain bikers and hikers exploring the resort's extensive trail network.

restaurant.name: Silvia`s Cafe
restaurant.desc: Sylvia's Café is a full-service rural outpost established in 1986 and situated at Km 42 of the Nazko Highway, roughly 47 km west of Quesnel between Puntchesakut and Tibbles lakes. The property combines a café, general store, gas and diesel, laundromat, showers, tent and RV camping, and a cozy cabin rental — a rare cluster of services in remote Cariboo country. Cyclists riding the Nazko Highway corridor would find this a practical and substantial resupply stop.

restaurant.name: Mary Brown's
restaurant.desc: Mary Brown's is a 100% Canadian-owned fast food chain specializing in fresh, hand-cut and hand-breaded chicken and hand-cut potato Taters, with roots going back to St. John's, Newfoundland in 1969. This Langley location is one of nearly 300 locations across Canada, offering takeout service. Cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley corridor may find it a convenient calorie stop on longer routes.

restaurant.name: Misty Mountain Pizza
restaurant.desc: Misty Mountain Pizza has been feeding mountain bikers and skiers since 1991 across two BC locations: Rossland and Whistler. The pizzeria offers whole pies, pasta, and in-store slices, with gluten-free crusts and dairy-free cheese available. The Rossland location sits in the heart of Kootenay mountain bike and ski country, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists passing through the region.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Gluten free and dairy options available' and lists Daiya Dairy Free Cheese; gluten-free 9" and 12" pizzas and cauliflower crusts explicitly listed on menu

restaurant.name: The Painted Turtle
restaurant.desc: Dutch Lake Resort & RV Park sits on the shore of Dutch Lake in Clearwater, BC, at the gateway to Wells Gray Provincial Park — one of BC's largest and most spectacular wilderness parks featuring 41 named waterfalls. The resort's on-site restaurant, The Painted Turtle, operates seasonally and offers breakfast, lunch, and dinner to guests and visitors. It sits along the travel corridor between Jasper, Sun Peaks, and Vancouver, making it a potential stop for touring cyclists traversing central BC.

detail.address: 361 Dutch Lake Rd, Clearwater, BC V0E 1N2

restaurant.name: Senor Duggies
restaurant.desc: Senor Duggies Tacos & Pizzeria is the only Mexican restaurant within 200 kilometres in the Fraser Lake area of central BC, serving tacos, burritos, enchiladas, and chimichangas alongside pizza, burgers, fish and chips, and coconut shrimp. Reviewers passing through on road trips consistently praise the food and friendly atmosphere, and the restaurant also offers margaritas and tequilas. For a touring cyclist on the remote Highway 16 corridor between Prince George and Burns Lake, this is a rare full-service dining stop in a very sparse stretch of interior BC.

detail.address: 324 McMillan Ave, Fraser Lake, BC V0J 1S0

restaurant.name: Red Tomato Pies
restaurant.desc: Red Tomato Pies is a pizza chain founded in Williams Lake, BC by Jason and Amber Akeson, making this location the birthplace of what has grown to 11 locations across Western Canada. The menu spans specialty meat, chicken, Hawaiian, seafood, and veggie pizzas with extensive customization options, plus sides, salads, pasta, and desserts. It has earned a strong word-of-mouth following and awards recognition for its handcrafted approach to pizza.

detail.address: 360D Proctor Street, Williams Lake, BC V2G 4P6

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states: 'We carry Plant based Pepperoni, and a large selection of veggies to choose from for you to create an amazing plant based/vegan friendly pizza of your choice.' Gluten-free crust available on 10" size for an additional charge

restaurant.name: Hideaway Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Hideaway Bistro is a fully licensed lakeside bar and restaurant at the Lakeside Heffley Hideaway resort on Heffley Lake, situated between Kamloops and Sun Peaks along a popular cycling and recreation corridor. It grew out of a food truck tradition known for Chef Juan's tacos and now offers a broader menu of comfort food with Mexican flair, served from a dog-friendly patio overlooking the lake. Cyclists can ride straight in from the road or paddle up to a public dock, making it a natural stop on a Sun Peaks–Kamloops route.

detail.address: 2544 Golden Horn Road, Heffley Creek, BC V0E 1Z0

restaurant.name: Twisted Hills Craft Cider
restaurant.desc: Twisted Hills Craft Cider is the first standalone cidery in the Similkameen Valley, established in 2012 in Cawston and producing BC's first full line-up of certified organic ciders from estate-grown, cider-specific apple varieties. The cidery operates a seasonal tasting room—dubbed the CiderDome—on a 12-acre organic orchard where visitors can taste a diverse range of single-varietal and fruit-infused ciders. Touring cyclists on the Crowsnest Highway (HWY 3) can stop in to sample and purchase bottles directly, or arrange curbside pickup of online orders.

restaurant.name: Mikonos Cafe
restaurant.desc: Mikonos Cafe is a restaurant located in Port Hardy, BC, at the northern tip of Vancouver Island — a key waypoint for cyclists completing the Island or completing a ferry crossing. The Greek-inflected name suggests a Mediterranean-style menu, though no further detail is verifiable from available sources.

detail.address: 7050 Rupert Street, Port Hardy, BC V0N 2P0

restaurant.name: dent island lodge
restaurant.desc: Dent Island Lodge is a remote, family-run all-inclusive wilderness lodge situated on Dent Island in BC's Discovery Islands, reachable only by seaplane or water taxi. The lodge offers destination dining overlooking the famous Dent Rapids, salmon fishing, jet boat tours, and helicopter excursions into the surrounding wilderness. It is operated by the Farr family, who have called the island home since 2007.

detail.address: Box 8 Stuart Island, British Columbia V0P 1V0

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: FAQ states: 'We are happy to cater for dietary restrictions and other allergies. Should you have a serious allergy, please let us know when you make your reservation so we can prepare accordingly.'

restaurant.name: Session Taproom & Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Session Taproom + Kitchen is a casual, artisanal restaurant and craft-beer taproom that has operated in Campbell River since 2019, featuring 12 rotating taps of local craft beer and cider alongside cocktails, pizza, and salad bowls. The business is kid-friendly and locally owned, with an emphasis on locally sourced ingredients and staff. It shares its building with a spin and yoga studio, making it a lively community gathering spot on the Island Highway corridor.

detail.address: 926 Island Hwy, Campbell River, BC V9W2C3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Session offers a variety of both meat and plant-based food options'; front page also lists salad bowls in the menu offerings

restaurant.name: RHM Donair
restaurant.desc: RHM Donair is a fast-food business located on Gertrude Street in the Vancouver Island area. It provides quick meals for touring cyclists and other travelers passing through.

restaurant.name: Waypoint Restaurant and Bar
restaurant.desc: The Waypoint Restaurant and Bar occupies a prime lakefront position within the historic Kaslo Hotel on the shores of Kootenay Lake, offering a seasonally evolving, regionally inspired menu alongside craft cocktails, an espresso bar, and a curated selection of BC wines and craft beers. A spacious patio with sweeping lake views draws locals and travellers alike, and the hotel's own adventure pages explicitly direct mountain bikers from Kaslo's trail network back to The Waypoint for a post-ride drink. The hotel holding a 'Green' certification with BC Green Business adds a sustainability dimension appealing to conscious travellers.

restaurant.name: Riders Pizza
restaurant.desc: Riders Pizza is a pizza restaurant in Cumberland, BC, home to creative, locally-inspired pies like 'The Cumberlander' and the cheekily named 'Pesto Pedaler' — a nod to the village's celebrated cycling culture. The menu spans classic and inventive options, including a wheat-free potato-polenta crust for those avoiding gluten. Outdoor seating and easy takeout make it a natural stop after a ride in one of Vancouver Island's premier mountain biking destinations.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes multiple vegetarian dishes (Halloumi & Kale Salad, Fennel & Citrus Salad, several veggie pizzas) and an explicit wheat-free crust: 'Our wheat-free crust is made of grated potatoes and polenta.'

restaurant.name: Nico's Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Nico's Pizzeria is a casual dine-in pizza restaurant in Revelstoke serving pizzas, poutine, and a rotating selection of BC craft beers. It operates seven days a week and accepts both dine-in and takeout orders, as well as delivery. The restaurant also accommodates private events such as birthdays and anniversaries, offering a communal spot for groups of cyclists passing through town.

restaurant.name: Fatburger
restaurant.desc: Fatburger is a North American fast-food chain founded in 1952, known for hand-pressed, never-frozen beef patties served in sizes from 1/3 lb up to 1.5 lb. This Langley location also offers turkey burgers, chicken sandwiches, and a plant-based Impossible Burger with vegan topping options. It provides quick, filling, made-to-order meals with some vegetarian and vegan flexibility for touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website confirms Impossible Burger (vegan-compatible with Daiya dairy-free cheese and no mayo), Turkeyburger, and Craig's Vegan dairy-free shakes

restaurant.name: Queen India Jumbo Pizza
restaurant.desc: Queen India Jumbo Pizza is a family-owned restaurant in Langley Township that fuses bold Indian spices with Italian pizza traditions — think Butter Chicken Pizza and Paneer Pizza alongside creamy curries and freshly baked naan. The family has over 25 years in the food industry and makes their dough by hand daily from egg- and dairy-free ingredients. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery are all available, making it a flexible stop for hungry cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

detail.address: 26426 56 Ave Unit # C, Langley Twp, BC V4W 3Z3

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: About Us page states 'Halal, Vegetarian, and Vegan Options Available'; no gluten-free mention found

restaurant.name: Guesthouse bistro @ earthclubfactory
restaurant.desc: Earth Club Factory is a long-running community institution on Denman Island, weaving together a bistro/cafe, a 20-bed hostel, performance venue, art gallery, and organic food buying club within a 110-year-old farmhouse property. A touring cyclist arrives to find not just coffee and grilled food but a full cultural hub — on-site coffee roasting, live music nights, a mosaic outdoor kitchen, and a cob oven speak to the deeply community-rooted character of the place. The property sits centrally to the Denman ferry and village, and the owners have explicitly cultivated a welcoming stop for cyclists exploring what they describe as easy, rewarding island terrain.

detail.address: 3806 Denman Road, Denman Island, BC V0R 1T0

restaurant.name: Yan's
restaurant.desc: Famous Yan's Restaurant is a well-established Chinese and Western cuisine destination in Salmon Arm, offering an extensive wok-based menu spanning seafood, noodle, and poultry dishes alongside a popular weekend smorgasbord. The restaurant accepts online orders and reservations, adding convenience for cyclists planning stops along the Okanagan–Shuswap corridor. Its location approximately four minutes from the highway on 21st St NE makes it accessible from major touring routes.

detail.address: 880 21 St NE, Salmon Arm, BC V1E2K9

restaurant.name: Wee Geordie's Cold Beer & Wine Store
restaurant.desc: Wee Geordies is a long-standing Kitimat neighbourhood pub and sports bar that has been serving the community for over 40 years, featuring live music on weekends, open mic nights, pool, darts, and multiple big screens for sports. Directly adjacent is the Wee Geordies Cold Beer & Wine Store, offering a wide selection of domestic and craft beers, wines, and spirits with a drive-up entrance for convenience. Together they form a one-stop social hub for anyone stopping in Kitimat on the North Coast.

restaurant.name: Back Eddy Pub
restaurant.desc: Back Eddy Pub is a local pub on Lakelse Avenue, the main commercial strip in Terrace, a hub community in the Skeena River valley of northwest BC. Terrace sits on the Yellowhead Highway corridor and is a common resupply stop for cyclists touring the region. As a pub, it would typically offer food, drinks, and a place to rest indoors.

restaurant.name: Subway
restaurant.desc: Subway is a global sandwich chain serving made-to-order subs, wraps, and salads at this Vancouver Island location on 10th Avenue. The vegetarian-friendly menu and takeaway service make it a convenient refueling stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. No drive-through is present, so all service is counter-based inside the restaurant.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Consistent with Subway's brand-wide menu offering vegetarian sub options

restaurant.name: The Fruitvale Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Fruitvale Kitchen is a casual takeout-focused restaurant in Fruitvale in the Kootenays, offering online ordering and counter pickup. It markets itself on value and a wide range of flavours, making it a potential quick resupply stop for cyclists riding the Kootenay back roads. The pickup-only model lets riders order ahead and collect food without a long sit-down wait.

notes.Takeout: Website explicitly states 'Pickup Only' with online ordering available

restaurant.name: Gigglin Grizzly Pub
restaurant.desc: Gigglin' Grizzly is a neighbourhood pub and family restaurant in McBride, BC, sitting along Highway 16 in the Robson Valley — a key corridor for touring cyclists crossing Northern BC. The property doubles as a full-service RV park with water, hydro, and septic hookups, making it a multi-use stop for long-distance travellers. McBride is a hub for mountain biking, hiking, and equestrian trails, and the pub is affiliated with the Robson Valley Mountain Bike Association.

restaurant.name: COBS Bread
restaurant.desc: COBS Bread Willowbrook Park Bakery is a franchise location of the Canadian artisan-style bakery chain, part of the Bakers Delight family with over 190 locations across Canada. Everything is baked from scratch on-site each day, with no refrigeration or freezing of products, and leftovers are donated to local charities at closing. Touring cyclists will find a range of breads, rolls, bagels, scones, croissants, and savoury items like mini pizzas available fresh throughout the day.

restaurant.name: Wells Hotel Pub
restaurant.desc: The Wells Hotel is a heritage country inn operating since 1934 in the small gold-rush town of Wells, BC, serving as the community's primary pub, restaurant, and gathering place. Situated at the gateway to Barkerville Historic Town, the Bowron Lakes Canoe Chain, and Troll Ski Resort, it is a natural waypoint for cyclists exploring the remote Cariboo region. The pub features an extensive BC craft beer selection and claims the largest single malt Scotch collection in Western Canada.

restaurant.name: e.b.'s Ice Cream Shop
restaurant.desc: e.b.'s Ice Cream Shop is a locally beloved scoop shop situated steps from the Salish Sea on Sechelt's waterfront, offering flavours from Rocky Point Ice Cream alongside their own homemade small-batch creations. The shop moved to a new indoor location at 5514 Wharf Ave for summer 2025, adding expanded seating and menu items. They even cater to cycling companions — the website notes ice cream is available for dogs too.

restaurant.name: Karahi King
restaurant.desc: Karahi King is a family-owned and operated Indian restaurant in downtown Prince George, serving traditional dishes cooked in a karahi pot and tandoor clay oven. Located on 5th Ave across from the Ramada Hotel, it is a fully licensed establishment offering dine-in and takeout with an all-you-can-eat lunch buffet. Chef Jagdish Gill won first prize at the 2015 Iron Ore Chef vs. Chef Challenge, and the restaurant is praised locally as one of Prince George's best-kept secrets.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes a dedicated 'VEGETARIAN SPECIALTIES' section; additional vegetarian items appear throughout (vegetable pakora, vegetable samosa, paneer pakora, paneer kulcha, channa bhatura, etc.)

restaurant.name: Taco Bandido

The standalone retail building opened in late 2021 and offers takeout service. It is wheelchair accessible and has on-site washrooms, making it a practical stop for cyclists passing through this busy commercial corridor.

restaurant.name: TacoRiendo Mexican Cantina Inc
restaurant.desc: Taco Riendo is a Mexican restaurant mapped in the Okanagan region of British Columbia. No verified details about its physical format, address, or offerings are available beyond the OSM cuisine tag. The only discovered website resolves to an unrelated food truck in Florida.

restaurant.name: The Office Pub & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Office Pub & Grill is a pub and grill located in Burns Lake in BC's Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior region. OSM tags indicate a wide-ranging menu spanning American, burger, chicken, diner, fish and chips, German, and Italian cuisine, suggesting it caters to a broad appetite. Burns Lake sits along Highway 16 (the Yellowhead), making it a natural stop for touring cyclists crossing the interior of British Columbia.

detail.address: BC-16, Burns Lake, BC V8J 1L2, Canada

restaurant.name: Kool Beans
restaurant.desc: Kool Beans is a coffee and ice cream shop in Keremeos, a small town along the Similkameen Valley cycling corridor in the southern Okanagan. For touring cyclists passing through on the Crowsnest or connected routes, it offers a natural stop for cold treats and a coffee fix. Keremeos is known as the 'Fruit Stand Capital of Canada,' and a local ice cream and coffee spot fits right into the town's character.

restaurant.name: Boer Mountain Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Boer Mountain Coffee House is a café on the Yellowhead Highway in BC's Central Interior, a major cycling corridor through the Cariboo and Bulkley regions. Located at a ground-level highway address, it offers sit-down and takeout service with a no-smoking policy. For touring cyclists passing through this remote stretch, it represents a rare opportunity for a hot drink and a rest stop.

restaurant.name: Sidebar Grill
restaurant.desc: Sidebar Grill is a restaurant and bar in the Latimer Heights neighbourhood of Langley, describing itself as the area's newest culinary destination where classic bar atmosphere meets modern comfort food. The kitchen reimagines comfort food classics with gourmet twists across a broad menu of shareables, tacos, wings, pastas, and mains, complemented by a full bar stocked with craft cocktails, curated beers, and fine wines. The venue hosts live local music nights and private dining, and has earned a Diners' Choice Award from its guests.

detail.address: Unit B – 100 20018 83A Ave Langley BC, V2Y 3R4

restaurant.name: Omega II
restaurant.desc: Omega II is a Greek restaurant located in the Okanagan & Thompson region of British Columbia. It occupies a dedicated building, suggesting a sit-down dining establishment rather than a takeout counter. Greek cuisine — with its emphasis on grilled meats, salads, and substantial portions — can be a satisfying stop for touring cyclists looking to refuel.

restaurant.name: Iron Horse Pub
restaurant.desc: The Iron Horse Pub & Grill is a community institution in Lone Butte, BC, serving the South Cariboo for over 20 years and continuing under new management. Situated directly on Highway 24 about 10 minutes east of the Cariboo Highway (Hwy 97), it offers a family-friendly atmosphere with a full dine-in menu and take-out service. For cyclists riding the Hwy 24 corridor through this rural stretch of the Interior, it stands as one of the few substantial meal stops along the route.

restaurant.name: Wasabiya
restaurant.desc: Wasabiya Japanese Sushi Cafe is a long-established Campbell River restaurant opened in 2001 by chef/owner Takahiro Matsuzawa, offering traditional and contemporary Japanese cuisine including sushi, sashimi, yakitori, and seasonal specials. Guests can sit at the dining room or at chef Hiro's sushi bar, or call ahead for takeout including bento boxes and artistically arranged sushi platters. Its West Coast–meets–Japan menu draws on local ingredients such as albacore tuna and sockeye salmon, making it a distinctive dine-in or takeout stop for cyclists exploring the Campbell River area.

detail.address: Suite A3 – 465 Merecroft Road, Campbell River, BC V9W 6K6

notes.Packed lunches: Bento boxes explicitly offered as a takeout item on the lunch and takeout menus, described as a packaged meal with roll, main, and sides

restaurant.name: Rove food truck
restaurant.desc: Rove Wandering Kitchen is a gourmet food truck founded by Comox Valley twins Devon and Tavis Shute, with Devon drawing on a background as sous-chef at Atlas Cafe and executive chef at Avenue Bistro to craft a rotating, seasonally-inspired menu well beyond typical fast food. Dishes range from fresh hand-cut fries to roasted cauliflower korma and thyme-infused bone broth, all made from scratch. The truck accepts Bitcoin on-chain and Lightning payments and is available for catering.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists roasted cauliflower korma as a seasonal offering, confirming at least one vegetarian option

restaurant.name: Northern Spice Pizza & Donair
restaurant.desc: Northern Spice Pizza & Donair is a pizza and donair restaurant located in Northern BC, serving the community around the 50th Avenue North corridor. For touring cyclists making their way through this remote stretch of the province, it represents one of the few sit-down dining options in the area. The donair offering reflects the Western Canadian tradition of this Middle Eastern-inspired street food staple.

restaurant.name: Carve Kitchen + Meatery
restaurant.desc: Carve Kitchen + Meatery is a modern, premium-casual restaurant anchored inside Naturally Pacific Resort on the outskirts of Campbell River, open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The menu leans on Canadian beef, fresh local seafood, and plant-based dishes shaped by onsite gardens and regional producers — a step up from typical highway dining for a cyclist rolling into town. A complimentary shuttle is offered for groups of six or more, and a striking live-edge Harvest Table seats up to 18 for group meals.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website describes 'vibrant plant-based dishes' and 'vibrant vegetarian dishes' as core menu categories alongside beef and seafood

restaurant.name: Steven's Cocktail Bar and Kitchen
restaurant.desc: Steven's Cocktail Bar and Kitchen is a lively Langley bar and kitchen with an inventive cocktail program spanning craft originals, frozen drinks, and large-format pitchers. The kitchen turns out creative comfort food — smash burgers, pour-over chicken wings, birria grilled cheese, and puffy tacos — alongside a snack-focused happy hour. The venue also hosts 'Whiskey Bent,' a curated guided tasting of five under-the-radar whiskies paired with bar snacks, available to groups.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists 'smoked cauliflower' as a standalone taco filling option; vegetable-forward bowls (Szechuan Chicken Bowl, Crispy Pork Bowl) also feature cauliflower, brussels sprouts, and kale, suggesting vegetarian-friendly sides

restaurant.name: Riverfront Pub & Grill
restaurant.desc: Riverfront Pub & Grill is a full-service riverside pub and restaurant in BC's Okanagan/Thompson Interior, known for live entertainment, local craft beers on tap (including Mt. Begbie and Crannog Ale), and Okanagan wines. The venue is family-friendly with an upper patio for summer dining, pool tables, and a rotating calendar of live music, karaoke, comedy, and stunt shows. It actively markets to outdoor recreation enthusiasts of many kinds and sources produce locally and beef from Alberta.

restaurant.name: Ming & Sing Chinese Express
restaurant.desc: Ming & Sing is a family-founded fast-casual Canadian Chinese restaurant in Langley's Power Centre, started by brothers Dan and Peter who grew up in their parents' local restaurant. The kitchen preps daily — hand-cut vegetables, in-house sauces, and freshly marinated and fried meats every morning — making it a reliable stop for a hot, freshly cooked meal. Online ordering, catering trays, and a straightforward combo-plate menu make it easy for a cyclist to grab a quick, filling meal.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu lists multiple vegetarian items: vegetable chow mein, vegetable shanghai noodle, vegetable fried rice, vegetable stir fry, and veg egg roll. No vegan or GF labeling mentioned

restaurant.name: Spilt Milk
restaurant.desc: Spilt Milk is Revelstoke's Australian-inspired specialty coffee roaster and café, roasting every batch in-house on a low-emission Loring S15 Falcon for clean, consistent results. The café on 2nd Street East serves specialty coffee and food in a deliberately community-focused space that explicitly welcomes cyclists passing through town. The business rebranded from Dose Coffee after a legal name conflict, drawing its new identity from skate culture and a philosophy of resilience.

restaurant.name: Island Attitude Café
restaurant.desc: Island Attitude Coffee is an OSM-listed cafe in the Tahsis area of west-coast Vancouver Island, one of the most remote cycling destinations in BC. The only associated website found is Westview Marina & Lodge, which operates a marina grillhouse, pub, and ice cream stand on the docks of Tahsis Inlet. Whether Island Attitude Coffee is a distinct business, a former name, or a coffee counter within the marina complex cannot be determined from available evidence.

detail.address: 775 S Maquinna Dr, Tahsis, BC V0P 1X0

restaurant.name: The Ground
restaurant.desc: The Ground is a cafe and coffee house in British Columbia's North Coast and Haida Gwaii region, a remote and strikingly scenic destination for touring cyclists. Its Facebook presence suggests it doubles as a gallery space, making it a cultural as well as culinary stop. Cyclists passing through this area will find few services, making this kind of community-oriented cafe a notable waypoint.

restaurant.name: Nomad So.Cial Eatery
restaurant.desc: Nomad So.Cial Eatery is an independently owned restaurant in Hope, BC, built around a culinary philosophy it calls Rocky Mountain food — rugged, backcountry-inspired cooking blended with health-conscious choices. The restaurant leans into Hope's layered history as a gold rush waypoint and railway gateway, positioning itself as a destination stop for travellers moving through the Fraser Canyon corridor. Lunch and dinner menus rotate seasonally, and the kitchen offers catering services alongside periodic special dining events.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states menus feature 'a limited number of gluten-free, vegetarian, or vegan dishes' and the chef can modify most dishes to accommodate dietary restrictions; fully vegan experiences require advance notice

restaurant.name: Heritage House Pub
restaurant.desc: Heritage House Pub is a community-centred pub in Courtenay, BC, run by a trio with combined backgrounds in cooking, hospitality management, and customer service. The kitchen serves a broad mix of pub classics alongside more inventive offerings like seafood chowder poutine and beet poke bowl. It's a welcoming sit-down stop in the Comox Valley for a meal and cold drink after a ride.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Beet Poke Bowl (ginger soy tossed beets, sushi seasoned rice — vegetarian), House Salad, Greek Salad, Spinach & Artichoke Dip, Jalapeno Popper Dip, Yam Fries, and plain Nachos. No explicit vegan or GF labeling found on the menu

restaurant.name: Chartreuse Moose
restaurant.desc: Chartreuse Moose Cappuccino Bar & Bistro is a cafe in BC's Cariboo/Chilcotin region that roasts all of its coffee in-house. It offers a full menu of food, beverages, baked goods, and desserts available for in-store dining or curbside pickup, with online ordering via the website or a dedicated mobile app. For a touring cyclist passing through a sparsely serviced stretch of central BC interior, it stands out as a well-equipped stop with free Wi-Fi.

restaurant.name: Fat Jack's Homestyle Diner
restaurant.desc: Fat Jack's Homestyle Diner is a diner-style eatery located in the Okanagan & Thompson region of British Columbia. The Facebook URL slug suggests it may double as a pub, offering a combination of casual dining and drinks. Touring cyclists passing through the area would find it a likely stop for a hearty, home-cooked style meal.

restaurant.name: Campbell's Gold Honey Farm & Meadery
restaurant.desc: Campbell's Gold is a family-owned honey farm and apiary in southwest Abbotsford producing specialty honeys and honey wines (mead) from their own hives. Visitors can sample and purchase mead, local and specialty honeys, beeswax candles, and beekeeping supplies directly from the farm. The operation also runs educational farm tours and workshops, making it a distinctive rural stop in the Fraser Valley agricultural corridor.

restaurant.name: Fatburger & Buffalo's Express
restaurant.desc: Fatburger & Buffalo's Express in Courtenay is a casual fast-food burger restaurant offering cooked-to-order burgers made with fresh, never-frozen Alberta Angus beef, alongside chicken tenders and wings, veggie burgers, and hand-scooped real ice cream milkshakes. Part of the Canadian-owned Fatburger chain with roots going back to 1952, this Courtenay location also carries the Buffalo's Express chicken menu. Takeout and online ordering are available, making it a potential quick refueling stop for cyclists passing through the Ryan Road corridor.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website lists 'veggie burgers & sandwiches' as a menu category

restaurant.name: Freshslice Pizza
restaurant.desc: Freshslice Pizza is a BC-based pizza chain known for its any-toppings-included slice model, with this location inside Valley Fair Mall in the Fraser Valley. Touring cyclists stopping here can grab a quick, filling slice or a full pie for takeout. The chain also offers delivery, catering, and a rewards app for frequent visitors.

restaurant.name: Lola's Tortas
restaurant.desc: Lola's Tortas is a Mexican fast-food spot in Hope, BC, serving tacos and burritos. It sits at a unit address on Wallace Street, placing it within reach of cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley gateway town. Hope is a common stop on the TransCanada and Crowsnest cycling corridors, making a quick, filling Mexican meal here a practical refuel option.

restaurant.name: Mill Canteena
restaurant.desc: Steam Pot Cafe is a food service reportedly located within the McLean Mill National Historic Site, a 12.8-hectare former sawmill and logging operation in the Alberni Valley that was designated a national historic site of Canada in 1989. The surrounding site features 35 heritage buildings, a restored steam-driven sawmill, and trail access including the Log Train Trail which welcomes hikers, cyclists, and equestrians. Whether the cafe still operates under this name or has been rebranded to 'Mill Canteena' is unconfirmed.

detail.address: 5633 Smith Road, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 8M1

restaurant.name: Grind + Filter Cafe
restaurant.desc: Grind + Filter Cafe is a café in the Lower Mainland & Fraser Valley region of British Columbia, with a name suggesting a specialty coffee focus. restaurant.name: Two Scoop Steve
restaurant.desc: Two Scoop Steve is a seasonal ice cream stop and Garden Bistro tucked into the small historic community of Yahk in the Kootenays, serving 24 flavours of hard ice cream alongside breakfast and lunch. The bistro features outdoor-only seating, making it a breezy trailside-style pause for cyclists passing through on the highway. It sits next door to Yahk Soap & Candle Co., giving it a relaxed village-stop character.

restaurant.name: Lillooet's Cookhouse Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Lillooet's Cookhouse Restaurant is a full-service breakfast-through-dinner establishment offering a wide-ranging menu that includes classic diner breakfasts, omelettes, wraps, eggs benedict variations, pizza, and kids' options. Multiple vegetarian-friendly choices appear throughout the menu, including a dedicated Veggie Omelette, avocado substitutions for meat dishes, and plant-based wrap fillings. The restaurant's links page references the Route 99 Cruz-In event, placing it on a key highway corridor through Lillooet.

restaurant.name: Umami Sushi

restaurant.name: Goldfield Bakery
restaurant.desc: Goldfield Bakery is a scratch bakery located inside Barkerville Historic Town & Park, western North America's largest living history museum and a National Historic Site of Canada. The bakery is known for its sourdough bread and fresh-baked goods prepared entirely on the premises, offering a distinctive stop within an immersive 19th-century gold rush townscape. It operates as an independent licensee within the historic site and accepts Visa, MC, and Debit.

restaurant.name: Crab shack
restaurant.desc: Crab shack is a restaurant located near Nitinat Lake on the remote southwest coast of Vancouver Island, an area known for windsurfing and backcountry adventure. The Instagram handle 'nitinat_crabshack' suggests a seafood focus fitting the coastal setting. For touring cyclists making the long journey into this isolated region, it appears to be one of the very few food options available.

restaurant.name: Begginnings
restaurant.desc: Begginnings is a breakfast-forward restaurant established in 2021 in Invermere, BC, whose name cleverly fuses 'beginnings' and 'egg' while paying homage to the pioneer history of the Columbia Valley. It serves high-quality, made-from-scratch breakfast, brunch, and lunch alongside craft beers, handcrafted cocktails, and Prosecco in a vintage-themed dining room that welcomes families and travel groups. A separate lounge with plush seating, world-class espresso pulled by expert baristas, free Wi-Fi, and device charging makes it a natural stop for cyclists wanting to linger and recharge.

notes.Device charging: Lounge section states 'charging outlets for your phone and laptop'

restaurant.name: Big Al's Bakery and Deli
restaurant.desc: Big Al's Bakery and Deli has been a beloved institution in Oliver, BC — Canada's wine capital — for over 40 years, turning out fresh-baked breads, donuts, cakes, and pies daily alongside a full deli counter stocked with premium meats and cheeses. The bistro-style restaurant serves breakfast and lunch, with specialty coffees from local Okanagan roasters and hot lunch options like brisket grilled cheese and poutine. It's an ideal stop for touring cyclists to grab a hot meal, stock up on picnic provisions, or pick up locally produced milk and yogurt.

restaurant.name: Dellas Café
restaurant.desc: Della's Coffee Shop & Grocery sits at Sproat Lake Landing on Vancouver Island, positioned as the midpoint stop on the popular route between Nanaimo and Tofino/Ucluelet. The café offers espresso drinks, fresh-baked pastries, handmade tacos (seasonal), artisanal paninis, grab-and-go fruit and veggie trays, and over 20 flavours of ice cream. It doubles as a small grocery for the local community, stocking staples and household items alongside a picnic area for travellers.

restaurant.name: Winemaker's Cut
restaurant.desc: Winemaker's Cut is a boutique Okanagan winery founded by Slovakian-born winemaker Michal and his wife, crafting estate wines from Deadman Lake Vineyard just south of Oliver. The operation is notable for playing classical music — Mozart, Beethoven, Puccini — in both the vineyard and cellar as part of the winemaking philosophy. Touring cyclists can visit the tasting room and explore multiple wine ranges including the flagship CUT collection, natural BOHO wines, and a sparkling line named after opera characters.

restaurant.name: Anja's Motel & Meals
restaurant.desc: A motel with an on-site restaurant located on Takla Road in the Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior region. Provides dining and overnight accommodations for travelers.

restaurant.name: Bluebird Cafe
restaurant.desc: Bluebird Cafe is a scratch-bakery café in Golden, BC, situated on the road to Moonraker Mountain Bike Trails, Kicking Horse Resort, and other nearby adventures. The kitchen bakes muffins and desserts fresh daily, serves organic Caffe Monte coffee, and offers made-from-scratch breakfasts and lunches. Cyclists will find purpose-built bagged trail lunches, broad vegetarian and vegan menu options, and an environmentally conscious take-away setup.

notes.Packed lunches: Menu lists a 'Bagged Lunch' item: sandwich choice (Ham & Swiss Panini, Turkey Cheddar Cranberry Panini, or Veggie Panini), trail mix, and treat snacks
notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu includes Veggie Falafel Wrap, Cranberry Veggie Feta Quinoa Salad, Veggie Samosa with Vegan Tomato Relish, Veggie or Ham & Cheddar Muffins, and Gluten Free Bread as a listed add-on

restaurant.name: BJ's Indian Kitchen
restaurant.desc: BJ's Indian Kitchen is a dine-in Indian restaurant in Qualicum Beach driven by a mission to restore authenticity to Indian cuisine in Canada, with experienced chefs preparing dishes such as biryani and tandoori chicken. The restaurant has earned positive reviews from diners across Vancouver Island and from visitors as far as Victoria and Vancouver. Online table reservations are available alongside phone booking, making it a convenient sit-down meal stop for cyclists passing through Qualicum Beach.

restaurant.name: gm Restaurant
restaurant.desc: GM Restaurant is an Indian restaurant in the Lower Mainland serving authentic curries, award-winning house-made cheesecake, and artisan chai teas. It operates as both a dine-in and takeout establishment, with delivery available through major apps and a branded retail spice-and-tea line called Shah Foods. The kitchen explicitly accommodates vegan and gluten-free requests.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states 'Looking for Vegan Options? How about gluten free? No matter what, we're sure we can accommodate you and help you build a meal' that suits dietary needs

restaurant.name: Kicking Horse Day Lodge
restaurant.desc: The Kicking Horse Day Lodge is the base-area hub at Kicking Horse Mountain Resort near Golden, BC, home to the Whitetooth Grill — a casual counter-service spot offering pizza, sandwiches, salads, snacks, and cold beer. The resort is a major mountain bike destination with a full bike park, rentals, and lessons, making the Day Lodge a natural stop for riders. The venue also hosts après-ski live music events on weekends.

restaurant.name: Lung Duck Tong Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Lung Duck Tong Restaurant is a long-standing local favourite situated within Barkerville Historic Town & Park, the largest living history museum in western North America. Renowned for fresh, authentic Chinese cooking, it draws visitors from around the world to this remote gold-rush heritage town deep in the Cariboo. For touring cyclists making the journey up Highway 26, it offers a distinctive dining experience unlike anything else along the route.

restaurant.name: Aldergrove Indian Bistro
restaurant.desc: Aldergrove Indian Bistro is a sit-down Indian restaurant on Fraser Highway serving authentic dishes prepared fresh daily, including biryanis, tandoori grills, and curries made with freshly ground spices and traditional recipes. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery to communities across the Fraser Valley including Langley, Abbotsford, and Surrey. Customer reviews highlight a small but welcoming atmosphere with attentive service, making it a solid meal stop for cyclists riding through Aldergrove.

restaurant.name: Lodge
restaurant.desc: The Lodge is the central accommodation building at Manning Park Resort, a major year-round destination in the Cascade Mountains drawing over one million visitors annually. It sits within a full-service resort offering cabins, chalets, camping, and the Pinewoods Restaurant serving comfort food in a mountain setting. For touring cyclists, it represents one of the few substantial service stops along Highway 3 through Manning Provincial Park.

restaurant.name: The Cove
restaurant.desc: The Cove is a cafe located at Earl's Cove on the Sunshine Coast Highway, a community that serves as a BC Ferries terminal for the Earls Cove–Saltery Bay route. Its position on this key cycling corridor makes it a natural stop for touring cyclists navigating the Sunshine Coast. The current status of its website is uncertain, as the domain appears to be listed for sale.

restaurant.name: The Canadian Brewhouse & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Canadian Brewhouse is a large Canadian sports-bar chain with a sit-down restaurant and full bar, known for oversized portions and a lively atmosphere centred on live sports viewing. The Abbotsford location occupies a second-floor unit (layer 2 per OSM), placing it in a mall or mixed-use complex. It replaced a previous Irish pub (Ceili's Modern Irish Pub) on the same site.

restaurant.name: Rockies Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Rockies Pizzeria & Grill is a full-service family restaurant in Radium Hot Springs serving handcrafted pizzas, BBQ ribs, steaks, burgers, and pastas with hearty portions. It holds a 5-star TripAdvisor rating and is a noted local favourite in the Columbia Valley. Takeout, delivery, and online ordering are all available, making it a flexible refuelling option for touring cyclists passing through.

detail.address: 7555 Main St West, Radium Hot Springs, BC, Canada

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Veggie Burger' and 'Veg Spring Rolls'; no explicit vegan or GF labelling found on the site

restaurant.name: Famoso Neapolitan Pizzeria
restaurant.desc: Famoso is a Neapolitan-style pizza bar situated on the second level of the High Street Shopping Centre in Abbotsford, adjacent to the Cineplex theatre. The menu spans wood-fired Neapolitan and new-world pizzas, artisan pastas, craft beers, and cocktails, served in a lively atmosphere with a street-side patio. Online takeout and delivery are available, making it a possible resupply stop for cyclists passing through the Mt. Lehman Road corridor.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: McDonald's is a globally recognized fast-food chain offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, breakfast items, and McCafé beverages. This Cliffe Avenue location serves the Courtenay area of Vancouver Island and includes a drive-through alongside dine-in and takeout service. It is a reliable, predictable food stop for touring cyclists passing through the Comox Valley corridor.

restaurant.name: Dona Donair & Kebab
restaurant.desc: Dona Donair & Kebab is a Mediterranean fast-food shop in Maple Ridge serving donairs, kebab plates, falafel, shawarma, and salads from a location on Dewdney Trunk Road. It is part of the Dona Donair chain and offers an extensive menu spanning meat, fish, and vegetarian options, all made with hand-picked ingredients. Cyclists passing through Maple Ridge on Dewdney Trunk Road will find it a practical stop for a filling, hot meal.

restaurant.name: Creekside Coffee Factory

restaurant.name: Sushi Kobo

It sits in the heart of the Comox Valley, a popular cycling destination with connections to regional trail networks and the Island Highway route. Touring cyclists passing through the area would find it a potential lunch or dinner stop for Japanese cuisine.

restaurant.name: Cakebread Artisan Bakery
restaurant.desc: Hot Chocolates & Cakebread Artisan Bakery is a family-owned artisan food shop in downtown Courtenay that has been hand-crafting chocolate truffles and confections since 1986 and baking European-style artisan breads and custom cakes under the Cakebread name since 2006. Everything is made in-house using GMO-free Canadian flours and ethically sourced single-origin Colombian chocolate. Touring cyclists passing through Courtenay will find freshly baked breads, cookies, savoury lunch items, and an eclectic range of handcrafted chocolate confections.

restaurant.name: The Station Neighborhood Pub
restaurant.desc: The Station Pub is a neighbourhood pub in Invermere, BC, situated in the Columbia Valley — one of British Columbia's premier cycling corridors. It operates a full kitchen and a patio, making it a natural stop for cyclists passing through town. The pub explicitly does not take reservations, keeping the experience casual and drop-in friendly.

restaurant.name: Canyon Alpine Restaurant

Its roadside motel-restaurant setting would make it a practical stop for touring cyclists passing through this stretch of BC's interior. No further details about the restaurant could be confirmed due to the Facebook page being inaccessible.

restaurant.name: Cappuccino Bar
restaurant.desc: The Cappuccino Bar is a cozy café tucked into the front of Mountain Outfitters rental shop at Panorama Mountain Resort in the BC Kootenay Rockies. It serves locally roasted espresso drinks, tea, baked goods, lunch items, and summer-only ice cream, with a sunny patio just steps from the Panorama Springs Pools. A self-described locals' favourite, it offers a quieter alternative to the resort's larger dining options.

restaurant.name: River City Coffee

The cafe seats more than 80 people in a spacious room with high industrial ceilings, cozy nooks, and a sun-kissed patio — a welcoming stop after a ride. Food is made to order from scratch with full breakfast and lunch menus, daily specials, and a dedicated baking program.

restaurant.desc: Dog n Suds Diner is a diner-style restaurant on Broadway Avenue South in Williams Lake, a hub city for cyclists traveling through British Columbia's Cariboo region. The name nods to the classic North American drive-in diner tradition, suggesting hearty comfort food in a casual setting. Williams Lake sits at a key junction on routes through the Central Interior, making this a potential resupply stop for long-distance touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: Apricus Cellars
restaurant.desc: Apricus Cellars is a boutique winery situated within the District Wine Village in Oliver — Canada's first multi-winery village concept of its kind. Founded as a partnership between indigenous and non-indigenous owners, it produces whites, rosés, and reds from South Okanagan fruit grown minutes from the winery. Touring cyclists can purchase bottles on-site or ship wines home through the online shop, and the venue also hosts live music events on its patio.

restaurant.name: Blue Moose Coffee House
restaurant.desc: Blue Moose Coffee House is a casual cafe serving coffee and cafe fare. The business offers online ordering and a loyalty rewards program. It provides a social gathering space with amenities like backgammon games.

restaurant.name: Flying Canoe West Coast Pub
restaurant.desc: Flying Canoe West Coast Pub is a pub serving the Vancouver Island community as a casual dining and drinking destination. It provides hospitality typical of West Coast social venues. Limited information is available from its web presence to verify specific amenities or services.

restaurant.name: Cactus Club Cafe
restaurant.desc: Cactus Club Cafe is an upscale casual dining chain with a chef-driven international menu served in a stylish, energetic space just blocks from Willowbrook Shopping Centre in Langley. The restaurant features a full lounge, patio seating, and private dining rooms, making it one of the more polished sit-down options along this stretch of the Fraser Valley. Touring cyclists looking for a substantial meal, happy hour, or late-night stop will find a reliable full-service restaurant with delivery and pickup also available.

restaurant.name: Forbidden Zone Pizza
restaurant.desc: Forbidden Zone Pizza & Specialty Coffee Bar is a gourmet pizza and specialty coffee destination in Campbell River with roughly 16 years of history, built around hand-pressed dough, house-made Forbidden Pizza sauce, and locally sourced ingredients. Beyond pizza, the menu spans breakfast items, baked pasta, and specialty espresso drinks, making it an all-day stop. A small outdoor seating area rounds out the experience for those who want to eat outside.

restaurant.name: Dockside F&C
restaurant.desc: Dockside F&C is a fish and chips restaurant located in Haida Gwaii, one of British Columbia's most remote and dramatically beautiful cycling destinations, accessible only by ferry or floatplane. Operating seasonally, it offers a classic coastal meal to visitors exploring the islands. For touring cyclists making the journey to Haida Gwaii, a hot dockside fish supper is a memorable reward.

restaurant.name: The Office Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: The Office Bar & Grill is an American restaurant and bar in Northern BC. Located on MacKenzie Boulevard, it serves as a convenient food and beverage stop for the local community and traveling cyclists.

restaurant.name: Marg's Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: A local bar and grill restaurant serving the North Coast & Haida Gwaii area. An established dining option for the community and traveling cyclists. Limited details available online to confirm specific amenities.

restaurant.name: Popsey's
restaurant.desc: Popsey's is a homestyle breakfast and lunch restaurant in Campbell River that has been serving the community for over 20 years. Operating out of what the website calls the 'Log Cabin Restaurant,' it offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery, as well as pre-made 'Homestyle Meals' that customers can take home and reheat. A touring cyclist could stop in for a hearty meal from a broad menu of sandwiches, burgers, soups, and wraps, or pick up a packaged meal for later.

restaurant.name: Sushi Shun
restaurant.desc: Sushi Shun is a Japanese sushi restaurant in a strip-mall unit in Surrey's Clayton neighbourhood, serving the Lower Mainland. The restaurant offers online ordering through its website and a dedicated app with a points-and-rewards program, letting cyclists pre-order before arriving. It is a sit-down option for a hot meal after a ride through the Fraser Valley.

restaurant.name: Clyde's
restaurant.desc: Clyde's Pub is a casual neighbourhood pub in Grand Forks, BC, serving American-style food and drinks with entertainment options including two coin-operated pool tables, a 10-foot projection screen, and five flat-screen TVs. The venue offers both dine-in and takeout meals and features a patio deck for outdoor dining and a horseshoe bar for gathering with friends. It is a well-rounded social stop for cyclists passing through the Boundary Country region.

detail.address: 7248 Second Street, Grand Forks, BC V0H 1H0

restaurant.name: New Fraser Lake Restaurant
restaurant.desc: A restaurant in the Fraser Lake area of British Columbia's Cariboo-Chilcotin region. Minimal information is available as the business website could not be accessed.

restaurant.name: C & U Vietnamese And Cambodian Restaurant
restaurant.desc: C&U Vietnamese Restaurant is a Vietnamese and Cambodian cuisine eatery located in the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley region of BC. The dual-cuisine offering suggests a menu that goes beyond standard Vietnamese fare to include Cambodian dishes, which would be relatively uncommon in the region. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a distinctive dining option.

restaurant.name: Benja Thai
restaurant.desc: Benja Thai is a family-run Thai restaurant in the quiet Similkameen Valley town of Keremeos, with recipes rooted in Grandma Meechai Chaicomdee's forty years as a street-food vendor in Nongkhai, Thailand. The kitchen sources organic vegetables from nearby Parson's Fruit Stand and local farms, and pours wines from surrounding Similkameen wineries. During renovations, a 1952 chocolate bar was discovered inside the restaurant walls — a local curiosity still on display inside.

restaurant.name: Ima's Bakery
restaurant.desc: Ima's Kitchen is a small-scale organic bakery and vegan ice cream shop on Denman Island, run by a couple who met while volunteering on the Thai-Burmese border and settled on the island after years of world travel. The bakery produces Middle Eastern-inspired breads — challah, pita, za'atar pita, and sourdough — while the ice cream line features globally inspired flavours made on a coconut milk base. Denman Island is a short ferry hop from Buckley Bay on Vancouver Island, making this an offbeat and locally rooted food stop for cyclists exploring the Gulf Islands.

restaurant.name: Nourish
restaurant.desc: Nourish Kitchen is an inclusive community eatery in Sechelt on BC's Sunshine Coast, helmed by Chef Cheryl with over 20 years of experience and a farm-to-table philosophy using local, seasonal ingredients. The kitchen caters equally to vegans, gluten-free diners, and traditional meat eaters, offering dine-in, takeout, catering, and chef's table experiences. Touring cyclists will find a genuinely accommodating stop with global flavours and adventure-ready meal packs designed for on-the-go eating.

restaurant.name: Austin Fish & Chips
restaurant.desc: Austin Fish & Chips is a fish-and-chips restaurant in Maple Ridge, BC, located along the Lougheed Highway in the Fraser Valley. It offers both dine-in and takeout service, making it a practical roadside stop for cyclists passing through the corridor. The menu centres on classic fish-and-chips fare with a range of food and beverage options.

restaurant.name: McDonald's
restaurant.desc: A McDonald's fast food location on Fraser Highway in the Lower Mainland/Fraser Valley, offering burgers, fries, McCafé beverages, and drive-through service. As a franchise of Canada's largest fast food chain, it provides takeout and drive-through options for travellers on this busy highway corridor. The corporate website offers no location-specific details about amenities relevant to touring cyclists.

restaurant.name: The Flying Apron Café and Bakery
restaurant.desc: The Flying Apron is a scratch bakery and café in Comox, BC, where a Red Seal Pastry Chef—three-time Skills Canada Provincial medallist—leads a team that begins baking before sunrise daily. The menu rotates seasonally and spans fresh breads, laminated pastries, artisan cakes, and cookies, all made in-house from locally sourced ingredients. Dedicated gluten-free and vegan options are consistently available, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

restaurant.name: Beach Gardens Beer & Wine Store
restaurant.desc: The Beach Gardens Beer & Wine Store is a retail cold-beer and wine shop situated at the Beach Gardens Resort & Marina on Powell River's waterfront at Grief Point on the Sunshine Coast. It sits within a full-service marina and resort complex that also houses the award-winning Seasider Bistro, an on-site distillery, and overnight accommodation. For touring cyclists on the Sunshine Coast route, it is a convenient cold-beverage resupply stop with on-site washrooms and a restaurant steps away.

restaurant.name: Anie's Pizza & Bakery
restaurant.desc: Anie's Pizza & Bakery is a small owner-operated restaurant in Cache Creek sitting along the Cariboo Highway (also known as the Gold Trail), serving made-from-scratch pizza with hand-tossed dough, home-baked bread, and freshly rolled cinnamon buns. The kitchen locally sources produce and deli meats and makes everything in-house, from custom pizzas to sandwiches built on house-baked loaves. Catering is available, and the location on a major Interior BC highway makes it a natural resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through.

detail.address: 1206 Cariboo Highway, Cache Creek, BC V0K1H0

restaurant.name: The Elements Restaurant
restaurant.desc: The Elements Restaurant is a Chinese-Canadian restaurant on the Trans-Canada Highway (Highway 16) in Houston, BC, serving a broad menu of chow mein, fried rice, chop suey, sizzling hot pots, and combination dinners. Situated in a small interior BC community along a major touring corridor, it stands out as one of the few full-service dining options for cyclists passing through the region. Online ordering with 15–30 minute pickup is available, and recent reviewers consistently praise generous portion sizes.

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Menu explicitly lists 'Meatless Chop Suey' and multiple mushroom-based dishes (Mushroom Chow Mein, Mushroom Fried Rice, Mushroom Chop Suey) as vegetarian-friendly options; no vegan or GF labeling found

restaurant.name: De l'Île Restaurant
restaurant.desc: De l'Île Restaurant is a small dinner-service restaurant on Vancouver Island, operating out of 129 Second Avenue West in the Vancouver Island & Gulf Islands region. The associated website has evolved into a food and travel blog alongside a digital recipe store, suggesting a chef-driven operation with interests spanning Italian cuisine, wine, and amaro. For touring cyclists, it offers a sit-down dining option in a community not saturated with evening restaurant choices.

restaurant.name: White Tower
restaurant.desc: The White Tower is a long-established Campbell River institution on Vancouver Island, serving authentic Greek cuisine alongside pizza, steak, lobster, and curry dishes for over 30 years. The restaurant is family-operated by Bill and Surinder Tsangaris and seats more than 120 guests, making it well-suited for larger cycling groups. A full licensed bar with wine, beer, and cocktails rounds out the sit-down dining experience.

restaurant.name: Projekt + Blend
restaurant.desc: Projekt Blend is a contemporary specialty café in Langley serving precision espresso drinks, signature lattes, and freshly made food in a workspace-friendly environment. The menu features creative items like smash burgers, Monte Cristo sandwiches, and a rotating roster of seasonal drinks, all made with locally sourced ingredients where possible. The café actively positions itself as a community gathering space — a warm 'third place' well-suited to a mid-ride stop or a longer work session.

restaurant.name: Sushi Wara
restaurant.desc: Sushi Wara is a Japanese restaurant in Qualicum Beach specializing in sushi and traditional Japanese cuisine. The restaurant provides online ordering for convenient meal stops. It serves the Qualicum Beach community as a useful dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

restaurant.name: Mazatlán Mexican Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Mazatlán is a Mexican restaurant offering dine-in service with outdoor seating available. A casual spot for cyclists seeking a meal break during their travels through the Lower Mainland.

restaurant.name: Oliver Street Bar & Grill
restaurant.desc: Oliver Street Bar & Grill is a neighbourhood pub and American-cuisine restaurant in Williams Lake, BC, billing itself as a local gathering spot for food, cold drinks, and community. It offers both a dine-in experience and a dedicated to-go menu, giving passing cyclists a convenient option for a sit-down meal or a quick pickup. Williams Lake sits at a key crossroads in BC's Cariboo region, making this a practical stop on longer interior touring routes.

detail.address: 23 Oliver St, Williams Lake, BC V2G 1L6

restaurant.name: Gneiss Wines
restaurant.desc: Gneiss Wines is a small-lot artisan winery housed in the District Wine Village in Oliver, BC, a curated cluster of South Okanagan wine, beer, and spirits producers a few minutes from downtown. The name references the gneiss rock formations underlying their Naramata Bench vineyard, which runs along more than a kilometre of the Kettle Valley Railway cycling trail. Founded by partners with multi-generational Okanagan roots, the winery crafts small-batch varietals including Tempranillo, Cabernet Franc, Pinot Gris, and Pinot Noir from sustainably managed local vineyards.

restaurant.name: Café Artigiano
restaurant.desc: Café Artigiano is a pioneering BC specialty coffee chain with over 25 years of history, known for expertly crafted espresso drinks using in-house roasted 100% Arabica beans from their Burnaby roastery. This Langley location is part of a network of 25 cafes across BC and Alberta, each serving artisanal baked goods made from organic, local ingredients free of artificial additives. Some locations now operate as Cafe-Bars offering cocktails and Italian bites into the evening.

restaurant.name: Red Rock Grill
restaurant.desc: Red Rock Grill is a locally owned and operated restaurant in 100 Mile House, BC, established in 2009 by a second-generation restaurateur born and raised in the South Cariboo. The kitchen turns out chef-prepared food made fresh daily — spanning creative small plates, burgers, mains, and pasta — alongside what the restaurant bills as the largest selection of BC craft beers on tap in town. It is a community-rooted, full-service stop for cyclists seeking a quality sit-down meal in the Cariboo interior.

restaurant.name: Jolly Coachman Pub

It has a community-focused identity with Lions Club ties, meat draws, and local fundraisers. A touring cyclist passing through the Pitt Meadows area would find a full sit-down pub menu alongside an attached liquor store.

restaurant.name: MNT Takao Café
restaurant.desc: MNT Takao Café is a café located at 1265 Ironwood Street on Vancouver Island, in the Campbell River area. The name suggests a Japanese-influenced theme, and the unit address indicates a multi-tenant commercial setting. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a useful stop for refreshments.

restaurant.name: Joe Poutine
restaurant.desc: Chez Joe Poutine is a French-Canadian inspired poutine restaurant in Sun Peaks, BC, opened in 2017 by Suzanne, a Quebec transplant who set out to recreate authentic Quebecois poutine on the west coast. The menu spans classic and specialty poutines, grill items (burgers, smokies, hot dogs, chicken tenders), and ice cream, with an unusually inclusive range of gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian adaptations. For a touring cyclist arriving at Sun Peaks, it offers a calorie-dense, customizable hot meal in a casual counter-service setting.

restaurant.name: Pescadores Bistro
restaurant.desc: Pescadores Bistro is a walk-in-only brunch and lunch restaurant in Port Alberni, perched across from the Alberni Inlet and Marina with a landscaped outdoor patio where wildlife sightings are common. The menu ranges from eggs benedict and omelettes to fish tacos and fresh-ground beef burgers, with vegan and gluten-free options throughout. It sits on the main highway corridor to Tofino, positioning it as a natural midpoint fuel stop for cyclists heading to the Pacific coast.

restaurant.name: Flying Saucers

restaurant.name: Rusty Iron Coffee Co.
