The café offers a full menu of specialty espresso drinks, iced beverages, breakfast and lunch wraps, and housemade baked goods, sourcing beans from Smoking Gun Coffee Roasters in Abbotsford. Cyclists travelling the Cariboo corridor will find a welcoming, wheelchair-accessible stop for hot or cold drinks, light meals, and branded merchandise including retail coffee beans and insulated mugs.

restaurant.name: J & V Restaurant

The business operates exclusively as drive-through pickup with no dine-in or delivery, making it a quick stop for touring cyclists passing through the Castlegar area. Catering is also available on request.

restaurant.name: Juice Five O - Noodle bar

Takeout and delivery are available alongside a drink menu that includes bubble tea, smoothies, and coffee.

restaurant.name: Kershaw's Cafe

restaurant.name: Tod Mountain Cafe

The café emphasizes locally sourced seasonal ingredients and describes a warm, comfortable atmosphere suited to refueling after outdoor adventure. It is a natural stop for cyclists passing through or based at Sun Peaks Resort.

restaurant.name: The Beach Hut

restaurant.name: Bull Wheel

Sitting at elevation in the resort village, it is part of a full-service dining lineup for resort guests.

restaurant.name: Q's Restaurant
restaurant.desc: Q's Restaurant is a Korean and Japanese fusion dining room in Golden, BC, established in 2017 and situated along the Trans-Canada corridor. The menu spans Korean BBQ, sushi rolls, ramen, udon, and Pad Thai, with an emphasis on locally sourced vegetables and seafood and house-made sauces. For touring cyclists riding the Kootenay or Columbia Valley routes, it offers a full sit-down meal with vegetarian and tofu options in a warm indoor setting.

restaurant.name: Stikine River Song

The café is celebrated locally and by travellers for hearty homemade meals and freshly baked pies, and doubles as the community gathering place. The same building holds nine renovated lodge rooms — some with kitchenettes — making it a rare full-service stop for cyclists undertaking wilderness expeditions in the upper Stikine River corridor.

restaurant.name: Hungry Herbie's
restaurant.desc: Hungry Herbie's is a Cache Creek institution that has been serving made-to-order burgers, hand-cut fries, and fried chicken on the Cariboo Highway since 1957. Home of the famous MONSTERBURGER™, the restaurant built its reputation by resisting the shortcuts of chain fast food — buns are baked fresh and fries are cut in-house daily. Sitting directly on the main highway through town, it is a well-regarded and long-standing refueling stop for travellers along this busy cycling corridor.

The kitchen emphasizes quality sourcing — Gold Standard Certified Angus Beef burgers, sustainable wild salmon, hormone-free proteins, and house-made sauces — with wheat-free menu options available. The on-site lodge offers apartment-style lakefront suites for cyclists seeking an overnight stay in the Kootenays.

restaurant.name: Blacksmith Bakery

The original Fort Langley location occupies the historic site of Reid's Blacksmith Shop (circa 1910), giving the brand its name and a strong sense of local character. With four locations across Fort Langley, Langley, and Maple Ridge, it offers European-style pastries, brunch, and bistro fare — a solid food stop for cyclists moving through the Fraser Valley.

grocery.name: Sacred Mountain Lavender
grocery.desc: Sacred Mountain Lavender is a boutique lavender farm established in 2001 on the southern slopes of Mount Tuam near Fulford Harbour, Salt Spring Island, growing over 60 varieties of lavender organically across 2.5 acres. The farm distills its own essential oils on-site and produces a range of handcrafted culinary and spa products. Visiting cyclists can take a self-guided tour of the lavender fields, drying room, and distillation equipment, and browse the seasonal farm shop for locally made lavender goods.

A 'Locations' page suggests at least one physical retail presence, though the specific address was not captured in the fetched content.

grocery.name: Seasons Farm Market
grocery.desc: Seasons Farm Market is a barn-based farm market in Abbotsford's agricultural corridor, stocking local free-range eggs, fresh dairy, garden produce, baked goods, and quality cuts of meat. The market emphasizes ethically raised, sustainable, and locally sourced food, and positions itself as a community gathering spot as much as a grocery stop. For a touring cyclist passing through the Fraser Valley farmland, it offers a genuine farm-fresh resupply point.

grocery.name: G & R Ginseng Trading Ltd
grocery.desc: G & R Ginseng Trading Ltd (養生堂 — 'Health Preservation Hall') is a Richmond-based specialty retailer focused on premium ginseng varieties, dried seafood (abalone, sea cucumber, fish maw, scallop), bird's nest, Korean red ginseng, and a broad range of Traditional Chinese Medicine products. The store offers both in-person and online shopping with delivery, serving Metro Vancouver's Chinese-Canadian community. A touring cyclist passing through Richmond's Capstan Way shopping area could find specialty health supplements and some dry-goods groceries, though the product range skews toward high-value culinary and medicinal items rather than everyday cycling supplies.

grocery.name: Red Cliff Farm
grocery.desc: Red Cliff Farm is a small organic farm on the outskirts of Kamloops selling farm-fresh eggs and organically grown vegetables, including garlic varieties such as Red Russian and Music. The farm is home to free-ranging chickens and operates as a direct-to-consumer farm stand. Notably, it accepts Bitcoin payments via Lightning and on-chain, making it an unusual and locally distinctive stop for cyclists seeking fresh, organic food.

grocery.name: Buckerfield's
grocery.desc: Buckerfield's is BC's original country store, founded in 1919 and now operating ten locations across the province, with the Duncan store also serving as the company's head office. The large-format store carries farm and livestock supplies, pet products, garden centre items, wild bird feed, and outdoor clothing — a useful one-stop rural retailer on the Trans-Canada Highway corridor. The store is wheelchair-friendly, pet-friendly, and publicly accessible with free parking.

detail.address: 5410 Trans Canada Hwy, Duncan, BC V9L 6W4

grocery.name: Brightside Blueberries & Such
grocery.desc: Brightside Blueberries & Such is a small veganic farm stand in the Cowichan Valley near Duncan, selling blueberries, produce, seeds, fruits, and nuts directly from the farm. The operation proudly bypasses retail middlemen entirely, with customers buying straight from the roadside stand. A cyclist passing through the valley in summer can expect seasonal BC-grown blueberries and other veganic farm goods.

grocery.name: Play
grocery.desc: Play is Kelowna's premium athletic footwear and apparel specialty store, focused on running, training, hiking, and lifestyle products from top brands including Salomon, HOKA, On, Brooks, Patagonia, and Arc'teryx. Located at Harvey Avenue and Spall Road, the shop stocks a wide range of performance gear including nutrition products (Tailwind, Skratch Labs, Maurten), hydration vests, and accessories relevant to endurance athletes. They also host a Play Run Club, making them a community hub for active locals and visiting athletes.

grocery.name: Monster Vinyards
grocery.desc: Monster Vineyards is a boutique winery in Penticton that playfully debunks the Ogopogo legend of Lake Okanagan, celebrating the imaginative contraptions people might have built to fake the mythical creature. Winemaker Stefan Arnason sources grapes from select Okanagan vineyards to produce bold, fruit-forward wines available through an on-site tasting room and wine shop. A patio is referenced in the photo gallery, making it a potential rest stop for cyclists exploring the South Okanagan wine route.

grocery.name: Sunset Farm
grocery.desc: Sunset Farm is a 45-year-old working sheep farm run by Sandy Robley on Salt Spring Island's Sunset Drive, spanning over 300 acres of owned and leased Gulf Islands pasture. The farm shop offers farm-fresh eggs, island lamb, and chicken alongside a wide selection of wool goods including yarns, blankets, sheepskins, and handmade crafts. The farm has a notable history of supplying lamb for Queen Elizabeth's visit to Victoria in the 1980s.

detail.address: 1325 Sunset Drive, Salt Spring Island, V8K1E2

grocery.name: Dickinson Family Farm
grocery.desc: Dickinson Family Farm is an RV campground set within a cherry orchard in Summerland, offering U-pick cherries across six varieties each July. The sites sit among the trees in a quiet, green setting with no concrete — a contrast to typical campgrounds. Touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan during cherry season can pick fruit directly from the trees alongside RV guests.

grocery.name: Charlie Brown's Health Foods
grocery.desc: Charlie Brown's Health Foods is a family-owned local institution in Nanaimo, operating since 1971 and voted Best Health Food Store in the area. Located in a unit at 1533 Estevan Rd, it offers alternative and holistic health products and groceries. Touring cyclists looking to stock up on natural foods or specialty health items in Nanaimo will find this a long-established community staple.

grocery.name: Granny's Fruit Store
grocery.desc: Granny's is an iconic fruit stand and bakery just off Highway 97 in Summerland, celebrating the Okanagan with locally sourced ingredients and homemade baked goods. The shop leans into a nostalgic 1950s–60s atmosphere, complete with antiques and a working 1961 Nordemende radio playing golden oldies. Cyclists on the Okanagan highway corridor will find fresh espresso, sandwiches, waffles, and locally roasted coffee waiting for them.

notes.Hot food: Menu includes grilled cheese, breakfast sandwich, Granny's Waffle with seasonal fruit, and a full espresso bar

grocery.name: Docksteader Source For Sports
grocery.desc: Docksteader Source for Sports is an independently owned member of the national Source for Sports buying group, with over 150 affiliated stores across Canada. Located in Surrey on King George Boulevard, it specializes in hockey, baseball, softball, lacrosse, racquet sports, inline skating, and team merchandise, along with equipment services like skate sharpening, racquet stringing, and glove repair. Touring cyclists may find athletic apparel, footwear, and hydration products here, but the store does not appear to stock cycling-specific equipment or offer bike repair services.

grocery.name: Sport Chek
grocery.desc: Sport Chek is a major Canadian sports retail chain with a Penticton location on Skaha Lake Road, stocking a broad range of sporting goods including cycling gear, apparel, and footwear. As one of the larger sports retailers in the region, it may carry bike accessories and parts that a touring cyclist could source in a pinch. The chain's website references a 'Sports Equipment Servicing' section, suggesting some in-store service capability beyond pure retail.

detail.address: 2701 Skaha Lake Road, Penticton, BC V2A 9B8

grocery.name: Community Farm Store
grocery.desc: Now operating as Pomme Natural Market Duncan after joining the Pomme chain, this natural and organic grocery store sits on the Trans-Canada Highway in Duncan, making it a convenient stop for cyclists travelling the Cowichan Valley corridor. The store emphasizes local and organic products, weekly produce specials, and a community-oriented ethos with long-standing staff continuity through the rebrand.

grocery.name: Adidas
grocery.desc: Adidas is a global sportswear brand with a retail location on Burrard Street in downtown Vancouver. The store carries Adidas apparel, footwear, and accessories across a range of sports. A touring cyclist passing through might find running shoes, base layers, or casual athletic wear here, but should not expect dedicated cycling or bike-service offerings.

grocery.name: Don-O-Ray Farm Market
grocery.desc: Don-O-Ray Farms is a family-owned farm market in Kelowna's Lower Mission with over 20 years of operation, growing and selling fresh-picked fruit, vegetables, and herbs including standout items like giant peaches, sweet corn, and purple cauliflower. Alongside fresh produce, the farm offers its Nature's Kitchen line of prepared products — jams, hot sauces, spice blends, and homemade pies — available for online order with farm pickup year-round. The full in-person market is open through the core of the cycling season, making it a practical fresh-food stop for riders touring the Okanagan.

grocery.name: Gulraj Farm
grocery.desc: Gulraj Farm is a family-operated blueberry farm in Tsawwassen run by Bainsdavinder and Nirlep. As a direct-sales farm shop, it offers cyclists on the South Delta route a chance to pick up fresh local blueberries close to the Tsawwassen ferry terminal area. Farm stands like this are classic touring stops for fresh, locally grown produce.

grocery.name: Duck Creek Farm
grocery.desc: Duck Creek Farm is a 13-acre family farm on Salt Spring Island that has operated since 1990, growing over 30 varieties of fruits and vegetables using organic, no-till, and non-chemical permaculture practices. The farm sells directly to cyclists and visitors via an on-farm farmstand, a seasonal on-farm Friday market, and the Tuesday market at Centennial Park in town. The property also stewards a salmon enhancement creek, and on any given visit you may encounter eagles, turtles, or beavers alongside the market garden.

detail.address: 134 Tripp Rd, Salt Spring Island, BC

grocery.name: Urban Farm Market
grocery.desc: Urban Farm Market is a fruit and vegetable store located on Westminster Highway in Richmond, BC. It operates as a small farm-market format shop, the kind of stop a touring cyclist might seek out for fresh produce along a route. Its social media presence is minimal and has seen little activity since 2022.

grocery.name: Mountain Warehouse
grocery.desc: Mountain Warehouse is a UK-based outdoor gear chain that designs and sells its own exclusive branded products, positioning itself as a lower-cost alternative to multi-brand outdoor retailers. The Kelowna location sits inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre, a large regional mall on Harvey Avenue. Touring cyclists may find general outdoor clothing, footwear, and camping accessories here, though it is not a dedicated cycling or bike service shop.

grocery.name: Maan Farms
grocery.desc: Maan Farms is a multi-generational family farm in Abbotsford's Fraser Valley offering U-pick and pre-picked strawberries, raspberries, and blueberries alongside an award-winning estate winery that produces berry wines entirely from fruit grown on the property. Founded in 1977, the farm has grown from a roadside stand into a full agritourism destination featuring a Country Market, barnyard animals, a corn maze, goat yoga, and a restored heritage barn. For touring cyclists, it is a distinctive Fraser Valley stop to stock up on fresh local berries in season.

grocery.name: Sport Chek
grocery.desc: Sport Chek is one of Canada's largest sporting goods retail chains, operated by Canadian Tire, carrying a broad range of athletic clothing, footwear, and equipment. This Vancouver Broadway location sits at Broadway and Ontario Street in a well-trafficked urban area. Touring cyclists may find helmets, cycling apparel, hydration gear, and basic accessories, though it is not a dedicated bike shop.

grocery.name: Sport Chek
grocery.desc: Sport Chek is Canada's largest national sporting goods chain, with this location inside the Sevenoaks Shopping Centre in Chilliwack. The store carries a broad range of outdoor and athletic gear, and OSM notes bicycle sales on-site. Touring cyclists passing through Chilliwack may find it useful for basic supplies, cycling apparel, and potentially bike-related accessories.

grocery.name: JoieFarm
grocery.desc: JoieFarm is an estate winery perched on the Naramata Bench with vineyards spread across the South Okanagan, one of BC's most celebrated cycling wine routes. The property features a tasting room and The Hot Dog Lounge, offering visiting cyclists a place to sample wines and grab a bite alongside the vines. The winery positions itself as a pursuer of 'West Coast wonder and beauty,' crafting small-lot, terroir-driven wines from its estate vineyards.

grocery.name: Lepp Farm Market
grocery.desc: A family-run, year-round farm market on Clayburn Road in Abbotsford featuring a full-service butcher shop, in-season local produce, and farm-to-table products. They have an on-site cafe and a culinary team preparing ready-made meals — ideal for a touring cyclist looking to restock with quality local food. Part of the Fraser Valley Circle Farm Tour self-guided route.

notes.Hot food: On-site cafe and ready-made meals prepared by culinary team

grocery.name: Lucky Farms
grocery.desc: Lucky Farms is a blueberry farm and direct-sales operation located on Ladner Trunk Road in the Tsawwassen/Ladner area of Metro Vancouver, operated by Lucky Farms Corp. It sits in the agricultural flatlands of the Fraser River delta, a popular cycling region with low-traffic dyke paths and rural roads. Cyclists passing through during blueberry season could pick up fresh local fruit directly from the farm.

grocery.name: Best Choice BlueBerry Farm
grocery.desc: Best Choice Blueberry Farm is a family-run u-pick and pre-picked blueberry farm on the Tsawwassen/Delta agricultural flats, open seasonally from July through early September. Cyclists can hand-pick fresh blueberries straight from the field or buy pre-packed boxes and organic garlic on-site, with no reservations or entry fee required. The farm is cash-only and is well-regarded by repeat local visitors for its large, sweet berries.

notes.Basic groceries: Sells fresh u-pick and pre-picked blueberries and organic Red Russian Garlic directly to customers on-site; cash only

grocery.name: Mt. Waddington's Outdoors
grocery.desc: Mt. Waddington's Outdoors is a backcountry equipment retailer with stores in Chilliwack and Whistler, carrying premium outdoor gear across camping, hiking, climbing, paddling, and snow sports. The shop stocks high-end brands such as Arc'teryx, Blue Ice, Alpacka, and NRS, and offers gear-fitting, repair, and consultation services. A touring cyclist passing through Chilliwack may find useful camp and hiking consumables here, though no dedicated cycling section is evident.

detail.address: 9270 Sasquatch Alley #101, Chilliwack, BC V2P 0J6, Canada

grocery.name: Mi Tierra Latina
grocery.desc: Mi Tierra Latina (listed in OSM as My Latin American Grocery Store) is a specialty Latin American grocery stocking authentic products from nine countries — Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, El Salvador, Guatemala, Mexico, Peru, and Venezuela. The store carries a broad range of packaged goods including beverages, sauces, corn and bean products, frozen food, snacks, and spices. A touring cyclist passing through North Vancouver could use it as a food resupply point for specialty and everyday pantry staples.

grocery.name: Natural Focus
grocery.desc: Natural Focus is a natural health products retailer that has been operating for 30 years, starting on Hastings Street in Burnaby and now based in Surrey. The store carries a broad selection of vitamins, supplements, protein, herbal products, and natural grocery items, available both in-store and online. A touring cyclist passing through could pick up natural snacks, protein supplements, and wellness staples from a well-stocked specialty health shop.

detail.address: 6350 120th Street - Unit 131, Surrey, BC, Canada, V3X 3K1

grocery.name: Time Out Source for Sports
grocery.desc: Time Out Source for Sports is a North Vancouver sporting goods store specializing in hockey equipment — sticks, skates, protective gear, and goalie equipment from Bauer, CCM, True, and Warrior — alongside baseball, soccer, football, and inline hockey gear. The store also serves a number of local teams and associations on the North Shore. No cycling products, bike repairs, or cycling-related services are mentioned anywhere on the website.

grocery.name: North End Farm
grocery.desc: North End Farm is a small organic farm stand on Salt Spring Island offering fresh vegetables, fruits, meats, bread, pies, and treats, alongside products from other local island producers. It operates on a self-serve honour system — customers pay via cash box or e-transfer — making it a relaxed and characterful stop. For touring cyclists, it's a genuine source of fresh, local food in a community known for its agricultural identity.

detail.address: 2521 North End Road, Salt Spring Island, V8K 1A5

grocery.name: Strathcona Beer Company
grocery.desc: Strathcona Beer Company is a craft brewery and taproom anchored in Vancouver's oldest residential neighbourhood, housed in a purpose-built 12,000 square foot facility that includes a 25-hectolitre brewhouse with five fermenters and five brite tanks — every pint poured is brewed on site. The 67-seat tasting room serves a rotating lineup spanning classic international styles like Premium Pilsner, Belgian Golden Ale, and British IPA alongside seasonal specialties and cask brews. A gourmet pizza kitchen and retail area selling exclusive apparel make it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the Strathcona area of East Vancouver.

grocery.name: Coastal Olive Oils
grocery.desc: Coastal Olive Oils Co. is a family-owned specialty tasting room in Tsawwassen that stocks around 40 extra virgin, fused, and infused olive oils alongside balsamic vinegars sourced from Modena, Italy. Customers are invited to sample before buying, giving it the feel of a curated food-experience shop rather than a grocery. The shop also carries artisanal Pappardelle's pasta and offers home delivery to Tsawwassen and Ladner.

grocery.name: Bench 1775
grocery.desc: Bench 1775 is an award-winning winery on a 30-acre waterfront estate along Naramata Road — one of BC's most celebrated cycling routes — with sweeping 180-degree views over Okanagan Lake. The winery produces whites, reds, rosés, and icewines across multiple Okanagan and Similkameen Valley vineyards, and operates the Bench Patio Bistro, described by prominent critic Anthony Gismondi as 'the best patio in the world.' Cyclists riding the Naramata Bench pass directly by this destination winery, which offers tastings, retail wine purchases, and full patio dining.

grocery.name: JM Fruit And Veg. Market
grocery.desc: JM Fruit And Veg. Market is a farm-stand style produce market on Douglas Road in West Kelowna, selling fresh local fruit and vegetables including BC cherries in season. It operates as a small independent roadside market typical of the Okanagan region, where farm-direct produce stops are a staple of cycling routes through the valley. Touring cyclists passing through West Kelowna can expect fresh local produce but should not count on other services.

grocery.name: Hofstede's Country Barn
grocery.desc: Hofstede's Country Barn is a well-established farm market in Chilliwack offering locally sourced produce from Okanagan growers, a full deli with nitrate-free meats and cheeses, and an in-house bakery turning out fresh buns, breads, and pastries daily. The on-site cafe serves hot sandwiches, salads, and rotating homemade soups, making it a genuine resupply destination in the Fraser Valley rather than a convenience stop. The store also stocks a broad selection of European specialty groceries, organic items, and gluten-free products.

notes.Hot food: Cafe page lists hot items including Curried Apple Panini, Raw Power Salad, and four homemade soups of the day, available for in-store pickup or delivery

grocery.name: Sport Chek
grocery.desc: Sport Chek is Canada's largest sporting goods chain, stocking a wide range of athletic clothing, footwear, and outdoor equipment. This North Vancouver location is part of an indoor retail complex and would carry cycling accessories, apparel, and potentially bikes as part of its broad sporting goods inventory. Touring cyclists passing through may find helmets, tubes, and gear essentials here even without a dedicated bike service department.

detail.address: 1000 Park Royal, Mall South, West Vancouver, BC V7T 1A1, Canada

grocery.name: The Hatch
grocery.desc: The Hatch is a quirky, art-infused winery tasting room in West Kelowna, part of the Jason Parkes Customs collective of Okanagan wine venues. It leans into irreverence — eccentric label art, eclectic wine series, and a deliberately offbeat atmosphere that blends a working cellar with a creative hangout. Touring cyclists on Boucherie Road can book a flight of five wines in advance or walk in when space allows.

detail.address: 3225 Boucherie Rd, West Kelowna, BC V1Z 4E1

grocery.name: Bates Beach Farm
grocery.desc: Bates Beach Farm is a small family-run farm market in the Comox Valley, situated beside Seal Bay Regional Park on Vancouver Island's east coast. It exploits an ocean-influenced microclimate to grow standout berries, tomatoes, garlic, and peppers, with a declared focus on Mediterranean-style produce. In addition to fresh seasonal fruit and vegetables, the market carries house-made frozen soups and fresh salsas, and also hosts a booth at the Comox Valley Farmers Market.

grocery.name: Sport Chek
grocery.desc: Sport Chek at Metropolis @ Metrotown is a large-format Canadian sporting goods chain located inside one of BC's busiest shopping malls in Burnaby. The store carries bikes, cycling apparel, and accessories across multiple sport categories, and the chain operates an equipment servicing program at many locations. For a touring cyclist, it is a useful stop for gear, clothing, and possibly basic parts in an otherwise commercially dense area.

grocery.name: Great Mountain Ginseng
grocery.desc: Great Mountain Ginseng is a specialty Chinese health food retailer focused on Canadian (American) ginseng, bird's nest, sea cucumber, and traditional Chinese herbal medicines, operating both an e-commerce store and a physical retail location in Richmond. The store is housed inside a shopping complex and offers in-store pickup alongside online orders. Touring cyclists could find dried goods, snack foods, specialty hot drink powders, and a range of health-focused food items here.

grocery.name: Snow Farms
grocery.desc: A certified organic vegetable farm in South Delta growing more than forty varieties of produce. They operate a farm stand for most of the year and also sell bedding plants and organic seedlings. A good stop for touring cyclists looking for fresh, locally grown food near the Tsawwassen ferry terminal area.

grocery.name: The Egg Store
grocery.desc: The Egg Store is a family-owned farm retail shop selling farm-fresh eggs picked daily and brought directly from local farms. It carries multiple varieties including freerange, organic, double yolkers, and enriched white eggs in bulk and by the dozen. A standout feature for passing cyclists is the on-site 'Eggspress' egg vending machine, stocked daily with fresh eggs for after-hours purchases.

notes.Basic groceries: Sells farm-fresh eggs in multiple varieties (freerange, organic, double yolkers, enriched white) available individually, by the dozen, or in bulk trays; egg-only specialty retail
notes.Vending machines: Website describes an 'Eggspress' egg vending machine on-site, stocked daily with fresh eggs and available when the store is closed

grocery.name: Surrey Farms
grocery.desc: Surrey Farms is a family-operated farm market established in 1989, now farming over 400 acres and operating two retail locations in Surrey. The business is best known for its exceptional fresh berries—strawberries, blueberries, raspberries, and blackberries—alongside seasonal Okanagan fruit and local vegetables. The popular U-Pick fields draw visitors from across the Lower Mainland, making this a distinctive stop for cyclists seeking fresh, locally grown produce.

grocery.name: Brightside Eggs
grocery.desc: Brightside Eggs is a third-generation family farm in Chilliwack producing certified-organic, cage-free, free-range eggs audited annually by ECO-CERT Canada. The farm operates 'The Egg Shack,' a self-serve on-site vending machine where visitors can purchase hand-sorted, ungraded eggs in recyclable cartons at any time without needing cash. A stop here offers touring cyclists a direct connection to Fraser Valley agricultural heritage and a genuinely local food purchase.

notes.Vending machines: On-farm egg vending machine ('The Egg Shack') at 6899 Evans Rd; accepts tap-capable credit/debit and mobile wallet — no cash accepted

grocery.name: Red Roof Family Farm
grocery.desc: Red Roof Family Farm is a farm-direct shop in Lake Country, situated in the Okanagan fruit-belt corridor popular with touring cyclists. OSM tags it as a farm shop, suggesting seasonal produce and farm goods. Its roadside location on Okanagan Centre Road would make it a natural stop on regional cycling routes, but current operating status is uncertain.

detail.address: 10483 Okanagan Centre Road, Lake Country, V4V 1K9

grocery.name: Seek & Surf
grocery.desc: Seek & Surf is a husband-and-wife-run surf and skate shop on Sooke Road, anchoring the Juan de Fuca Strait surf community with surfboards, wetsuits, fins, and a curated selection of outdoor lifestyle goods. Founded by Mike and Cas, the shop positions itself as an inclusive gathering place for outdoor enthusiasts rather than a purely transactional retailer. Touring cyclists passing through Sooke may find it worth a stop for dry bags, sun care products, footwear, or simply a welcoming local vibe.

detail.address: 5871 Sooke Road, Sooke, British Columbia V9Z 0C3

grocery.name: MEC Mountain Equipment Company
grocery.desc: MEC (Mountain Equipment Company) is one of Canada's largest outdoor retailers, operating a location in Kelowna. As a full-service outdoor shop, it typically carries a broad range of cycling gear, apparel, and accessories suited to touring and adventure cyclists. The Kelowna store serves the broader Okanagan cycling community in a region known for its extensive trail networks and long-distance touring routes.

grocery.name: Meridian Farm Market
grocery.desc: Meridian Farm Market is a Lower Mainland farm market chain emphasizing locally sourced, farm-fresh products including grass-fed and free-range meats, seasonal produce, artisan baked goods, deli items, and a full range of pantry staples. The market positions itself on BC-local sourcing and craft quality, making it a well-stocked resupply stop beyond a typical convenience store. Multiple physical locations operate across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver region.

grocery.name: 12 Baskets Nutrition & Health Co
grocery.desc: 12 Baskets Nutrition & Health Co is a natural health and supplement retailer in Richmond, BC, stocking an extensive lineup of vitamins, herbs, probiotics, homeopathic remedies, and natural beauty products from dozens of Canadian and international brands. The store also carries a food section with superfoods, dried fruits, nuts, seeds, natural condiments, and manuka honey — useful resupply items for a touring cyclist. It operates both a physical retail location and an active online store with Canada-wide shipping.

grocery.name: Centennial Park Farmstand
grocery.desc: Sea Dog Farm is a 5-acre certified organic operation in Sidney, BC growing a wide variety of fruits, vegetables, berries, herbs, cut flowers, and free-range eggs. The Centennial Park Farmstand sits at the south end of the property beside a trail in Centennial Park, offering direct farm-to-consumer sales. A live stand cam on the website lets visitors check what is currently stocked before making the trip.

notes.Basic groceries: Website confirms seasonal fruits, vegetables, berries, herbs, cut flowers, and free-range eggs sold directly from the farm stand

grocery.name: Rockweld Farm
grocery.desc: Rockweld Farm is a family-owned ethical chicken and egg operation run by Tim and Flo Rempel, featuring an on-farm store in Abbotsford's agricultural heartland. The store sells free-roam, non-medicated chicken in a remarkable range of forms — whole birds, cuts, sausages, pot pies, smoked meats, and bone stock — alongside organic beef, cheese, assorted fish, and locally grown frozen berries. Cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley farm country will find a genuine farm-direct stop with an unusually broad selection of locally sourced foods.

grocery.name: Fruition Farm Stand
grocery.desc: Fruition Farm Stand is a family-run roadside farm stand on the south end of Quadra Island, operated by the Greenland family since 2021, offering sustainably grown vegetables, small fruits (blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, cherries), garlic, and free-range eggs. The farm uses low- to no-till practices with no synthetic fertilizers or pesticides and has a completed Environmental Farm Plan. Cyclists exploring Quadra Island can stop at this working farm for a genuine local produce pickup just steps from the fields.

detail.address: 247 Jones Farm Road, Quathiaski Cove, V0P 1N0

notes.Basic groceries: Farm stand sells fresh vegetables (greens, carrots, radishes, onions, garlic), small fruits (blueberries, raspberries, boysenberries, blackberries, cherries), and free-range eggs, as documented across multiple website pages and seasonal news updates

grocery.name: JX Surf Shop by Relic
grocery.desc: JX Campground and Surf Shop is a campground, surf rental, and e-bike rental hub sitting on the Tofino-Ucluelet Highway on Vancouver Island's rugged west coast. The property hosts T-Bird E-bike Rentals for exploring the surrounding Yuułuʔiłʔatḥ First Nation territory, alongside tent and RV campsites and multiple on-site food trucks. It offers a convenient overnight and resupply stop for touring cyclists riding the Pacific Rim corridor.

grocery.name: Mountain Equipment Company
grocery.desc: Mountain Equipment Company (MEC) is a major Canadian outdoor retailer operating from a four-storey retail building in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood at 111 East 2nd Avenue. The brand — widely known by its short name MEC — has long been a destination for cyclists and outdoor enthusiasts seeking gear, apparel, and equipment. Its central Vancouver location places it within reach of cyclists arriving in or transiting through the city.

grocery.name: Valhalla Pure Outfitters
grocery.desc: Valhalla Pure Outfitters Nelson has been serving the outdoor community since 1996 and is part of a BC-wide chain billing itself as 'Canada's Mountain Sports Specialists.' The Nelson location carries gear for backcountry skiing, avalanche safety, split boards, snowshoeing, hiking, and camping, with a focus on tested, quality brands. Touring cyclists passing through Nelson may find general outdoor apparel and gear, though bike-specific services are not confirmed at this location.

grocery.name: Body Energy Club
grocery.desc: Body Energy Club is a Vancouver-born health food chain founded in 2002, offering sports supplements, vitamins, energy gels, electrolytes, protein bars, and a smoothie and cold-pressed juice bar. The Waterfront Station location is tucked inside one of Vancouver's busiest transit hubs at the edge of the seawall cycling network. Cyclists can stock up on ride nutrition — gels, electrolytes, and snacks — or grab a smoothie or healthy to-go meal before or after a ride.

grocery.name: See Ya Later Ranch
grocery.desc: See Ya Later Ranch is a historic winery and bistro perched high atop Hawthorne Mountain above Okanagan Falls, with roots going back to 1920 when founder Major Hugh Fraser planted the first vines. It is one of the highest-elevation vineyards in the Okanagan Valley and holds the largest planting of Gewürztraminer in North America across 65 acres. Touring cyclists who make the climb are rewarded with award-winning tastings, a valley-view bistro, and a lively events calendar including a Pride celebration.

detail.address: 2575 Green Lake Road, Okanagan Falls, BC V0H 1R0

grocery.name: Neufeld Farm Berry Barn
grocery.desc: A family-run farm market operating since 1980 on King Road in Abbotsford, the Berry Barn is the produce and berry arm of Neufeld Farm Market. They grow their own strawberries, raspberries, blackberries, and blueberries on-site, hand-picked daily in season, and also stock Okanagan fruit, everyday produce, meats, seafood, and soft ice cream. A touring cyclist passing through the Fraser Valley can load up on fresh local fruit and staple groceries here.

grocery.name: Nature's Essence
grocery.desc: Nature's Essence is a health food and natural products shop located inside a Richmond shopping centre, stocking a broad range of vitamins, supplements, and wellness brands alongside a modest food section (honey, proteins, teas, maple products). The store carries hundreds of brands spanning organic, vegan, and whole-food lines, making it a useful stop for cyclists seeking sports nutrition, electrolyte products, or natural snacks. It also offers beauty and body care, essential oils, and cleaning products.

grocery.name: Dawson Creek Health Food Centre
grocery.desc: The Health Food Centre is a family-owned and operated health store that has served Dawson Creek for 49 years, making it a long-standing institution in this northern BC community. The store stocks a broad range of wellness products including supplements, bulk herbs, GF and vegan food options, aromatherapy, natural beauty care, and an in-store refillery station for eco-friendly household products. For touring cyclists passing through Dawson Creek, it offers a useful stop for specialty dietary staples and natural health supplies.

grocery.name: Surrey Farms
grocery.desc: Surrey Farms is a family-run operation founded in 1989 that has grown from a small roadside stand to over 400 acres, with two farm market locations in Surrey. The red Surrey Farms market on 152 Street is a longtime community landmark, known for exceptional fresh strawberries, blueberries, raspberries, and blackberries, as well as a broad selection of local fruits and vegetables. U-Pick berry fields are open to the public during the seasonal harvest and draw visitors from across the Lower Mainland.

grocery.name: Madrona Farm
grocery.desc: Madrona Farm is a long-running organic farm at the foot of Mt. Doug, just minutes from downtown Victoria, operating under The Land Conservancy and selling freshly harvested produce at a roadside veggie stand. The farm grows over 105 varieties of vegetables and 35 varieties of fruit across all four seasons, with staff picking the morning of each market day and washing produce on-site. A touring cyclist would find an exceptional selection of fresh local vegetables and fruit in a working farm setting.

grocery.name: Nature's Fare Markets
grocery.desc: Nature's Fare Markets is a BC-based health food grocery chain with a well-established Kelowna location staffed by more than 75 employees, some with over 20 years tenure. The store carries certified organic produce, zero-waste bulk goods, vitamins, supplements, and clean beauty products alongside ethically sourced meat and dairy. An on-site Bistro serves local, organic, and sustainable foods, and grab-and-go salads, smoothies, and kombucha on tap make it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists.

notes.Hot food: Website lists Bistro ('Fuel up with local, organic and sustainable foods and drinks') and grab-and-go salads, entrees, and breakfast

grocery.name: West Coast Natural Foods
grocery.desc: West Coast Natural Foods is a long-established health food store in Sooke serving the community since 1980. It carries organic and natural groceries including quality meat and fish alongside a broad range of vitamins, minerals, herbal remedies, and nutritional supplements from brands such as Natural Factors, Sisu, and Flora. For a touring cyclist passing through Sooke, it offers a compact resupply stop for whole foods and wellness products.

detail.address: 6716 W Coast Rd #5, Sooke, BC V9Z 1H4

grocery.name: New Generation Foods
grocery.desc: New Generation Foods is a multicultural natural foods grocery store specializing in staple pantry items — flours, grains, beans, lentils, rice, spices, dried fruit, and nuts — sourced for Latin American, African, Middle Eastern, South Asian, and European communities. The store produces its own Kismet brand of bulk-style dry goods, with a strong emphasis on dietary-restriction-friendly flours (corn, rice, quinoa, sorghum, amaranth, oat, barley, teff). For a touring cyclist, it offers a practical resupply point for high-calorie, lightweight staples at what the store describes as competitive prices.

grocery.name: Schoolhouse Farm
grocery.desc: Schoolhouse Farm is a small, woman-owned, family-run diversified farm in Ladner operating with no-spray, no-till, regenerative practices. Its farm store carries seasonally harvested vegetables, culinary and medicinal herbs, and cut flowers, plus a curated selection of third-party goods, accepting cash, card, and e-transfer. When fields are blooming, the farm also offers u-pick flower sessions in a working farm setting framed by willow trees and public seating.

notes.Basic groceries: Farm store stocks seasonal open-pollinated vegetables, culinary and medicinal herbs, and fruits harvested on-site, plus a small number of curated third-party food items

grocery.name: Sparkes Corn Barn
grocery.desc: Sparkes Corn Barn is a family-owned farm stand that has grown and sold fresh sweet corn in the Chilliwack area since 1998, operating a network of distinctive green-and-yellow drive-thru roadside barns across the Fraser Valley. All corn is non-GMO, picked fresh daily, and sold the same day directly from their own fields. During the summer harvest season, cyclists will also find locally grown strawberries, raspberries, and blueberries at the stands.

grocery.name: Dolson's Source For Sports
grocery.desc: Dolson's Source For Sports is the Kamloops location of Canada's largest sports equipment buying group, Source For Sports. The store specializes in hockey, skiing, lacrosse, racquet sports, and outdoor recreation gear, offering a wide range of equipment services from skate sharpening to ski stone grinding. A touring cyclist might find athletic apparel, water bottles, hydration gear, and trail/hiking accessories here, but the store shows no dedicated cycling focus.

detail.address: 500 Notre Dame Dr #200, Kamloops, BC V2C 6T6, Canada

grocery.name: Sport Chek
grocery.desc: Sport Chek is a major Canadian sporting goods chain located inside Hillside Mall in Victoria. It operates an in-store Service Shop staffed by technicians who perform bike tune-ups and repairs, bookable online, by phone, or as walk-ins. As part of the Canadian Tire family of brands, it also stocks a broad range of cycling apparel, footwear, and accessories.

grocery.name: Sunshine Coast Olive Oil Co.
grocery.desc: Sunshine Coast Olive Oil Co. is an independent, family-owned gourmet food store in Gibsons specializing in award-winning single-estate and infused extra virgin olive oils and balsamic vinegars sourced with full farm-to-table traceability through direct farmer relationships. The shop carries oils certified to the Ultra Premium (UP) standard—the highest tier within the extra virgin category—alongside specialty groceries including crackers, olives, spreads, gourmet pasta, and condiments from BC, Greece, Italy, and Spain. It also operates an online store with in-store pickup, making it a distinctive artisan provisions stop on the Sunshine Coast.

detail.address: 305 – 287 Gower Point Road, Gibsons, BC V0N 1V8

grocery.name: Crooked Horn Farm
grocery.desc: Crooked Horn Farm is a certified organic vegetable farm in the Slocan Valley near Winlaw, BC, run by Gord and Ange. The farm offers seasonal CSA shares with weekly pickup options in the Slocan Valley and Nelson, providing fresh locally grown produce from late spring through fall. A touring cyclist riding through the rural Slocan corridor could find fresh organic vegetables here during the growing season.

notes.Basic groceries: Certified organic veggie farm selling vegetables via CSA shares and direct sales; Facebook describes fresh seasonal produce including potatoes and other vegetables

grocery.name: Sportstop
grocery.desc: Sportstop Source for Sports is a member of Canada's largest sporting goods buying group (Source for Sports), located in the Crystal Lodge North Wing in Whistler Village. The shop carries sporting goods and sportswear serving the outdoor enthusiast community in one of BC's premier mountain resort destinations. A touring cyclist passing through may find outdoor apparel, accessories, and general sports gear here.

detail.address: 4154 Village Green, Whistler, BC, Canada, V0N 1B4

grocery.name: Vitasave
grocery.desc: Vitasave is an independently owned Canadian health supplement and natural wellness retailer that has been operating since 2010, now serving over a million customers across two Vancouver storefronts. The Robson Street location stocks 3,000+ vitamins, supplements, protein products, and grocery superfoods — all NPN-certified and third-party tested — and also offers a smoothie menu. For cyclists seeking to restock on nutritional or health-focused supplies mid-tour, it is one of the more comprehensive natural health shops on central Vancouver's main retail corridor.

grocery.name: Neufeld Farm Market
grocery.desc: A family-run farm market operating since the early 1980s on King Road in Abbotsford, rooted in a raspberry and chicken farm started by the Neufeld family in 1966. The market specializes in free-run, hormone-free chicken along with turkey, beef, pork, seafood, produce, berries, and local specialty items. They also operate The Berry Barn for seasonal produce and soft ice cream, and run a well-known community fundraising program.

grocery.name: Climb On Equipment
grocery.desc: Climb On Equipment is a specialty outdoor and technical climbing gear retailer in Vancouver, stocking a broad range of products for rock climbing, alpine climbing, ice climbing, work and rescue applications, and backcountry camping. The store carries harnesses, ropes, protection hardware, helmets, footwear, tents, sleep systems, and technical apparel from leading brands. Cycle tourists may find it useful for camping supplies and outdoor apparel, but it is not a bike shop.

grocery.name: Haslam Creek Berry Farm
grocery.desc: Haslam Creek Berry Farm is a certified organic U-pick blueberry operation on Rugby Road outside Nanaimo, offering two varieties of blueberries — Chandler and Draper — during the summer and early fall picking season. The farm operates on a seasonal schedule with weekend picking days during harvest, making it a potential detour for cyclists passing through the Nanaimo area seeking fresh local produce. Cash and e-transfer are the only accepted payment methods.

grocery.name: Southlands Grange Centre For Farming And Food
grocery.desc: Southlands Grange is a community-based farm and market district on the Tsawwassen peninsula anchored by a working community farm, a flower farm, and the Southlands Tsawwassen Farmers Market featuring fresh local produce, baked goods, and handmade goods from local growers. The campus surrounds an open-air Market Square beside an orchard, with a restored historic Red Barn, commissary kitchen, and nearby cafés and local shops. A touring cyclist arriving here encounters authentic Metro Vancouver working farmland alongside a lively, food-focused community hub.

grocery.name: Vancouver Island Refillery
grocery.desc: Vancouver Island Refillery is a health food and refill shop on Wesley Street in Nanaimo, operating under a zero-waste, bring-your-own-container retail concept. The store has a membership program and an online shop, suggesting a community-oriented operation appealing to sustainability-minded shoppers. For touring cyclists, it represents a stop for health-oriented supplies in central Nanaimo.

grocery.name: Evo Village Sports
grocery.desc: Evo Village Sports is a Whistler outpost of Evo, an outdoor and action-sports retailer known for cycling, snow sports, and related gear. Located in Whistler Village, it serves the resort's active clientele with equipment and apparel. Touring cyclists passing through Whistler may find it a useful stop for gear and supplies.

detail.address: 4341 Village Ln #110, Whistler, BC V8E 1B9, Canada

grocery.name: Running Room
grocery.desc: Running Room is a Canadian running-specialty chain carrying running footwear, performance apparel, and training accessories for men and women. The North Vancouver location is part of a national network founded on the philosophy of helping everyday runners improve. A touring cyclist might find nutrition products, socks, or moisture-wicking apparel here, but no cycling-specific services are offered.

detail.address: 2601 Westview Dr Suite 754, North Vancouver, BC V7N 3X3, Canada

grocery.name: E.P. Orchards
grocery.desc: E.P. Orchards is a certified-organic farm shop on Bentley Road in Naramata, situated in the heart of the Okanagan's fruit-growing country. The operation offers self-harvesting (U-pick), making it a hands-on stop for cyclists exploring the Naramata Bench. It sells exclusively organic produce, a rarity along the route.

grocery.name: 50th Parallel Estate
grocery.desc: 50th Parallel Estate is an award-winning Okanagan estate winery specializing in Pinot Noir and aromatic white wines, set in Lake Country along a popular cycling corridor between Kelowna and Vernon. The property includes the Block One fine-dining restaurant focused on regional-seasonal ingredients, wine caves open for exploration, and a tasting room with appointment and walk-in options. Event and wedding venues accommodate groups from 10 to 350 people, making it a notable destination stop on a multi-day Okanagan cycling tour.

detail.address: 17101 Terrace View Road, Lake Country, BC V4V 1B7

grocery.name: Goodway's Specialty Foods
grocery.desc: A long-running specialty food store (formerly Galloway's, dating back to the 1930s on Robson Street) now located in New Westminster. Stocks a large selection of spices, grains, coffee, ethnic foods, organic items, and gluten-free products not found in conventional grocery stores. Small and cozy with knowledgeable staff and a reputation as a destination shop for customers across the Lower Mainland.

detail.address: 702 Sixth Ave, New Westminster BC V3M 2B3

grocery.name: BCB Honey Farm
grocery.desc: BCB Honey Farm is a South Surrey farm store founded in 2003 by Dr. Tabari, who runs thousands of honeybee hives across the Lower Mainland and Peace River to support BC's pollination independence. The farm produces internationally award-winning raw honey — taking First Place at the 2019 International Honey Commission and a Quality Gold Award at the London Honey Quality Competition. Cyclists can stop in at the farm store or pull up to the drive-thru window to pick up locally produced honey and honey infusions.

detail.address: 4121 King George Blvd, Surrey, BC V3Z 1G6

grocery.name: Applebarn Pumpkin Farm (Taves Farms)
grocery.desc: A multi-generational family farm in Abbotsford operating since 1990, known for seasonal ticketed experiences including tulip gardens, pumpkin patches, and sunflower fields. They also run Taves Estate Cidery on-site and have a country store with farm products and u-pick apple fields. The farm sits on Gladwin Road in the Fraser Valley's agricultural lowlands.

detail.address: 333 Gladwin Rd, Abbotsford, BC V2T Y51

grocery.name: Purcell Outdoors
grocery.desc: Purcell Outdoors is a compact 950-square-foot outdoor gear shop in downtown Kimberley's Platzl, stocking a wide range of brands for trail running, hiking, backpacking, and ski touring. Kimberley sits at the centre of extensive trail networks and is a stop on the Powder Highway, making this a natural resupply point for adventure travellers passing through. Staff are active endurance athletes with deep local knowledge of the surrounding Purcell Mountains terrain.

grocery.name: Gatzke Orchard
grocery.desc: Gatzke Orchard is a four-generation family farm and fruit stand situated on the isthmus between Kalamalka and Wood Lakes in Oyama, operating each season with fresh cherries, raspberries, berries, house-made pies baked from a 1941 Grandma Gatzke recipe, and a range of locally-made value-added products. The farm also hosts Pedego Electric Bikes as a partner operation, positioning it as a natural hub for cyclists riding the Okanagan Valley Rail Trail. A wood-fired pizzeria (Pane Vino) operates on the property, making it a well-rounded stop for touring cyclists seeking fresh local food.

detail.address: 15686 Pelmewash Parkway, Lake Country, BC V4V 2J2

notes.Hot food: Pane Vino Wood Fired Pizzeria operates at Gatzke Orchard; bakery also produces pies on-site

grocery.name: Rewilding Roses (Farm Stand)
grocery.desc: Rewilding Roses is a small Roberts Creek operation combining a farm stand with a line of grass-fed tallow skincare products, organic meat, and handcrafted goods. The producer appears at the Sechelt Farmers Market and operates a roadside farm stand at their Joe Road property. The business accepts Bitcoin and Lightning Network payments, which is unusual for a rural farm stand.

grocery.name: Body Energy Club
grocery.desc: Body Energy Club is a Vancouver-born health food and supplement retailer founded in 2002 in a humble 500-square-foot Davie Street shop, now grown into a multi-location chain spanning Vancouver, the Lower Mainland, and US cities. Each location combines a retail supplement floor with a smoothie and bowl bar, stocking everything from creatine and protein to energy gels, electrolytes, cold-pressed juices, and vitamins. It has also expanded into one of Canada's largest online vitamin and supplement retailers, with in-store pickup available in about 30 minutes via app.

grocery.name: Honeymoon Bay Food & General Store
grocery.desc: The Honeymoon Bay General Store is a community cornerstone general store nestled on the south shore of Cowichan Lake, stocking groceries, camping supplies, beer/wine/spirits, and a full hot take-out menu including stone-baked pizzas, all-day breakfast, burgers, butter chicken, and samosas. It is also a designated stop on the West Coast Trail Express bus, making it a natural resupply and staging point for cyclists heading to or from the Bamfield trailhead. The store explicitly markets itself as the essential pit stop for hikers, bikers, and campers exploring the Cowichan Lake area.

detail.address: 10056 South Shore Rd, Honeymoon Bay, BC V0R 1Y0

notes.Hot food: Full hot take-out menu: all-day breakfast, burgers, sandwiches, stone-baked pizzas (including vegan/vegetarian), chicken wings, zucchini sticks, butter chicken, samosas, fries, ice cream
notes.Camping fuel: Biking/camping subpage explicitly lists propane as a stocked item: 'Need propane... No Problem, we got your back!'

grocery.name: MEC Mountain Equipment Company
grocery.desc: MEC (Mountain Equipment Company) is Canada's largest outdoor specialty retailer, and this Victoria location on Government Street is a major outdoor gear hub in the city centre. The store carries cycling equipment, apparel, and accessories alongside a broad range of outdoor gear. Touring cyclists passing through Victoria will find it a convenient resupply point for kit and consumables.

grocery.name: Hillpoint Estate Farm Stand
grocery.desc: Hillpoint Estate Farm Stand is a working estate farm in the Cowichan Valley near Duncan, operating as both a farm stand and a farmers market. The property also functions as a wedding venue, reflecting the broader agri-tourism character of this part of Vancouver Island. Its active social media presence documents day-to-day farm life, from haying to seasonal produce.

grocery.name: Stotan Falls Wood Products and Farm
grocery.desc: Stotan Falls Wood Products and Farm is a small regenerative farm and forestry operation outside Courtenay on Duncan Bay Mainline, focused on putting carbon back into the soil. The farm sells direct from a farm stand, offering seasonal produce including garlic, sunchokes, and berries, as well as native and ornamental trees grown on site. It accepts Bitcoin and Lightning network payments, which is unusual for a rural farm stand.

notes.Basic groceries: Farm stand sells seasonal produce including garlic, sunchokes, berries, and trees per Instagram posts

grocery.name: Glanford Greenhouses
grocery.desc: A family-run greenhouse operation on Glanford Ave that has been growing produce at this site since the 1920s, with the current family farming here since 1960. The roadside stand sells a broad range of greenhouse and garden vegetables — tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, eggplants, kale, beans, herbs, and more — direct from the farm. Cyclists passing through the Saanich area can stop in to stock up on fresh local produce, and the farm also appears at several Greater Victoria farmers markets throughout the season.

notes.Basic groceries: Roadside farm stand selling a wide range of fresh vegetables including tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, eggplants, kale, lettuce, beans, basil, zucchini, and more; fresh produce only, no packaged staples mentioned

grocery.name: Berry Bounty Farms
grocery.desc: Berry Bounty Farms is a four-generation family-run berry operation in Chilliwack's Fraser Valley, cultivating 17 acres of raspberries and 20 acres of blueberries. The year-round self-serve store runs on a debit/credit vending machine stocked with frozen berries, farm-fresh eggs restocked daily, raspberry jams and juices, and Fricey's ice creams. A seasonal roadside stand supplements the store during the summer berry harvest, offering cyclists a distinctive farm-fresh stop along Chilliwack Central Road.

detail.address: 48260 Chilliwack Central Road, Chilliwack, BC V2P6H3

notes.Vending machines: Self-serve vending machine accepts debit or credit; stocked with frozen fruit, eggs, jam, and juice

grocery.name: Local Refillery Grocer
grocery.desc: Local Refillery is the Comox Valley's zero-waste bulk grocery and lifestyle store, selling package-free dry foods, fresh and frozen foods, spices, and cleaning and beauty products through a 'weigh and pay' bring-your-own-container model. Shoppers can also order online for in-store or curbside pickup, with staff filling orders into deposit jars or compostable paper bags. Founded by Ginette Matthews and now in its seventh year, the store acts as a community hub for sustainable, plastic-free living in Courtenay.

grocery.name: Richmond Country Farms
grocery.desc: Richmond Country Farms is a family-owned working farm that has operated in Richmond for over 60 years, selling produce grown directly on-site through its farm market. The market shifts with the seasons — spring greens and herbs give way to summer variety, then fall pumpkins and squash — alongside baked goods and local pantry staples. The property also includes a winery with tastings and a lounge, plus seasonal events like the Sunflower Festival and Pumpkin Patch, making it a genuine destination rather than just a roadside stand.

grocery.name: Health Essentials
grocery.desc: Health Essentials is a community-oriented health and wellness shop founded in 2011 by a Victoria couple, located at the corner of Tillicum and Gorge Road West directly across from Gorge Waterway Park. The store carries a curated selection of supplements, specialty foods (local organic meats, dairy, keto items), barefoot shoes, light therapy products, and natural body care. It hosts educational seminars and workshops and ships Canada-wide, with a loyal local following drawn by its knowledgeable staff and competitive pricing.

grocery.name: Vital Health
grocery.desc: Vital Health is a health food shop in the small Kootenay town of Creston, BC, a popular stop on touring routes through the southern interior. As a dedicated health food store, it likely carries natural and specialty grocery items that can be harder to source in rural areas. Creston sits in a fertile valley and is a practical resupply point for cyclists riding between the Rockies and the Okanagan.

grocery.name: Red Rooster
grocery.desc: A Naramata Bench winery established in the 1990s, crafting a range of BC VQA whites, reds, and rosés. The tasting room sits right along the popular Naramata cycling corridor, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists riding the bench. They host regular events including live music, comedy shows, and seasonal festivals.

detail.address: 891 Naramata Bench Rd, Penticton, BC V2A 8T5

grocery.name: Evo Backcountry
grocery.desc: Evo Backcountry is the Whistler location of Evo, a well-known outdoor and action-sports retailer headquartered in the Pacific Northwest. The store caters to backcountry and mountain recreation enthusiasts and is situated in one of Canada's premier mountain resort communities. Touring cyclists passing through Whistler may find relevant gear, apparel, or cycling equipment here.

detail.address: 4154 Village Green, Whistler, BC V8E 1H1, Canada

grocery.name: Sea Dog Farm
grocery.desc: Sea Dog Farm is a 5-acre certified-organic-practice farm in Sidney tucked behind Centennial Park, operating two self-serve honor-system stands stocked with seasonal vegetables, fruits, berries, herbs, cut flowers, and free-range eggs. One stand sits directly beside a Centennial Park trail, making it a natural stop for cyclists passing through. The farm uses only certified organic fertilizers and no herbicides, pesticides, or rodenticides.

notes.Basic groceries: Farm stands sell seasonal vegetables (peas, kale, tomatoes, cucumbers, squash, garlic), fruits, berries (strawberries, raspberries, blueberries), herbs, and free-range eggs

grocery.name: Ponderosa Sports
grocery.desc: Ponderosa Sports is a general sports retailer located on Voght Street in Merritt, BC, a town that sits at a key junction on routes through the Nicola Valley. As a sports shop in a small interior community, it may carry outdoor and cycling supplies that would be hard to find elsewhere in the area, making it a potential resource for passing touring cyclists.

grocery.name: Consignors Sports
grocery.desc: Consignor Sports is a consignment and new sporting goods store that has served Kamloops since 2006, dealing in both new and used equipment across a wide range of sports. The shop carries new and used bikes along with accessories and accepts bike consignment on a rolling basis, meaning inventory changes frequently. For touring cyclists it offers basic mechanical services including tube changes, tire changes, and tune-ups, making it a practical stop for common roadside fixes.

detail.address: 789 Notre Dame Dr, Kamloops, BC V2C 5N8

grocery.name: Evo
grocery.desc: Evo is a sports retailer with a Whistler location, tagged in OSM as a sports shop. The store is situated in one of Canada's premier mountain biking and ski destinations, making it a plausible stop for outdoor gear. No further detail about its specific cycling offerings could be verified from available sources.

detail.address: 4341 Village Ln #110, Whistler, BC V8E 1B9, Canada

grocery.name: Cyclone Taylor
grocery.desc: Cyclone Taylor is a sports shop located in south Vancouver, named after Fred 'Cyclone' Taylor, the legendary early-20th-century hockey star associated with Vancouver. The shop is listed under a general sports category in OSM, and its exact product focus — including whether cycling gear or bike services are offered — could not be confirmed due to a website fetch failure. Touring cyclists considering a stop should call ahead to verify relevant services.

grocery.name: Valhalla Pure
grocery.desc: Valhalla Pure (now operating as VPO Canada) is a multi-brand outdoor gear and apparel retailer with a location in downtown Revelstoke. The store carries an extensive range of outdoor clothing, footwear, and technical gear from over 450 brands. Revelstoke's position as a major mountain recreation hub makes this a potential stop for touring cyclists seeking general outdoor supplies.

grocery.name: Green Bliss
grocery.desc: Green Bliss is a health food shop on Main Street in Vancouver, a corridor popular with cyclists commuting through the Mount Pleasant neighbourhood. The OSM record was field-checked in September 2024, suggesting the location was active at that time. No web presence could be confirmed to provide further detail about the shop's offerings.

grocery.name: Body Energy Club
grocery.desc: Body Energy Club is a Vancouver-born health food and supplement chain founded in 2002, now with multiple Lower Mainland locations and an extensive online store. The West 4th Avenue shop sits on one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors and carries sports supplements, electrolytes, energy gels, protein bars, and vitamins alongside a full smoothie and bowl bar. Touring cyclists can resupply on ride fuel and recovery nutrition or grab a freshly made smoothie or healthy to-go meal.

grocery.name: Earthwise Society
grocery.desc: Earthwise Agassiz is a 58-acre organic teaching farm and environmental education centre situated between Harrison Hot Springs and Agassiz, featuring the Miami River along its eastern boundary, native wetland ecosystems, and a heritage farmhouse and barn dating to circa 1910. Operated by the Earthwise Society, the property hosts CSA programs, a Farm Store, and community food-security initiatives serving the eastern Fraser Valley. Overnight stays and venue rental are also available, making this a genuinely distinctive rural stop for cyclists exploring the Harrison corridor.

grocery.name: Better U Market
grocery.desc: Better U Market is a health food and organic grocery store in the heart of Qualicum Beach, founded by local couple Mike and Regan after their own wellness journey. The shop carries fresh organic produce sourced from BC farmers alongside natural supplements, vitamins, and clean personal care products—all hand-selected to be free of additives and harmful chemicals. A touring cyclist stopping here will find genuine fresh-food resupply options in a community-focused setting that emphasizes local ingredients.

detail.address: 149 Second Avenue West, Qualicum Beach, V9K 1S1

grocery.name: Good Life Juice
grocery.desc: Good Life Juice is a Vancouver Island-based cold-pressed juice and health food shop offering unpasteurized juices, nut milks, smoothies, cleanses, salads, bowls, and soups made from fresh produce. The shop operates a walk-in fridge stocked seven days a week with no pre-order required, making it an easy stop for a nutrient-packed pick-me-up. They also supply commercial clients across Vancouver Island including hotels, restaurants, and local distilleries.

grocery.name: Hundo-P
grocery.desc: Hundo-P is a Whistler-born smoothie and non-dairy ice cream shop that opened in Whistler Village in 2019, built around real-fruit superfood smoothies and coconut-cashew ice cream made fresh in front of customers. The menu emphasizes whole, clean ingredients — organic nuts, dates, fruit, and protein — making it a natural refuelling stop after a big day on the bike. The shop also stocks packaged protein bars, baked goods, and snacks for riders on the go.

grocery.name: Elements Outfitters
grocery.desc: Elements Outfitters is a proudly Canadian-owned outdoor gear retailer and self-described leading dealer of Patagonia, Filson, and Hooké in Canada, with locations including this Tsawwassen outlet near the BC Ferries terminal. The store carries a curated selection of durable, purpose-driven outdoor apparel and gear, and is a member of 1% for the Planet. Touring cyclists passing through Tsawwassen could find quality rain gear, layering pieces, and outdoor accessories here.

detail.address: 5000 Canoe Pass Way, Unit 105, Tsawwassen, BC

grocery.name: Sporting Life
grocery.desc: Sporting Life is a mid-to-upscale Canadian sporting goods chain retailer located in the Lougheed Town Centre mall in Burnaby. The brand is known nationally for carrying cycling, running, and outdoor gear alongside premium apparel. A touring cyclist passing through would find it a potential source for cycling accessories, apparel, or gear rather than workshop-style repair services.

detail.address: 4501 Lougheed Highway, Unit P21-01, Burnaby, BC V5C 0B3

grocery.name: Red Cliff Farm at the Kamloops Regional Farmer's Market
grocery.desc: Red Cliff Farm is a small family farm outside Kamloops growing organic produce and raising free-range chickens for farm-fresh eggs, with a stall at the Kamloops Regional Farmer's Market on St Paul Street. The farm sells exclusively organic products and notably accepts Bitcoin payments (both on-chain and Lightning Network). Recent posts show seasonal highlights like garlic scapes, making it a worthwhile stop for cyclists seeking fresh local provisions.

grocery.name: Homesteaders Health
grocery.desc: Homesteader Health Foods is a locally owned natural grocery chain with its original location in Fort St. John, BC, open since 1989. The store carries certified organic produce, bulk grains, legumes and herbs, vitamins and supplements, and a range of natural personal care products. For a touring cyclist resupplying in Fort St. John, it offers one of the broader selections of organic and whole-food staples in the region, with three Registered Nutritional Consultant Practitioners on staff.

grocery.name: Sport Chek
grocery.desc: Sport Chek is a large national Canadian sporting goods chain carrying bikes, cycling apparel, and accessories alongside broader outdoor and athletic gear. This Kelowna location on Harvey Avenue is part of a major retail hub and serves a wide range of sport and recreation needs. The store's sports equipment servicing page suggests some repair capability, though the scope of bike-specific services is not confirmed from available content.

grocery.name: Stay Wild Natural Health Food Store And Juice Bar
grocery.desc: Stay Wild Natural Health Food Store And Juice Bar is a community-focused natural health grocer and juice bar in Pemberton, BC, stocking organic and local foods, supplements, herbs, and natural health products. The store's mission centres on holistic nourishment and natural medicine, making it a distinctive stop for health-conscious travellers in the Sea-to-Sky corridor. Delivery is also available, and the store maintains an active online presence for local updates and recipes.

grocery.name: MEC Mountain Equipment Company
grocery.desc: MEC Mountain Equipment Company is a major Canadian outdoor retailer with a location in North Vancouver, stocking gear for cycling, hiking, camping, and other outdoor pursuits. As a large-format outdoor co-op store, it typically carries a wide range of cycling equipment and accessories. Touring cyclists in the North Vancouver area would find it a useful stop for resupply and potentially mechanical support.

detail.address: 212 Brooksbank Avenue, North Vancouver City, V7J 2C1

grocery.name: House of Nutrition
grocery.desc: House of Nutrition is a family-owned health food and supplement store that has served Victoria's wellness community since 1980. The shop carries supplements, herbs, sports nutrition products, healthy alternative foods, and health and beauty items for all ages. As a member of the Health First Network, it stocks an exclusive line of Canadian-made supplements formulated without GMOs, gluten, or artificial additives — potentially useful for cyclists seeking specialized nutrition support.

grocery.name: Day's Century Growers Fruit Stand and Packing House
grocery.desc: A 136-acre family farm in the heart of the Okanagan that has been operated by the Day family for over 120 years across five generations. The on-farm stand opens mid-July with seasonal produce including sweet corn, tomatoes, and cantaloupe, all grown on-site. Cyclists can stock up on free-range meats (chicken, pork, beef, lamb), fresh eggs, handmade sourdough bread, wildflower honey, and seasonal vegetables. The farm practices regenerative agriculture and its flooded fields serve as winter habitat for the recovering Trumpeter Swan population.

notes.Basic groceries: Year-round supply of free-range poultry, pork, beef, lamb, eggs, handmade sourdough bread, wildflower honey, and seasonal vegetables sold at the farm stand and online for pickup

grocery.name: Silver Meadows Farm Market
grocery.desc: Silver Meadows Farm Market is a family-run farm market in Errington near Parksville on Vancouver Island, best known for its fresh corn and strawberries. It offers a range of locally grown produce, meat, eggs, baked goods, and handmade crafts, and hosts a seasonal corn maze that draws community interest. With nearly 9,500 Facebook followers and regular fresh-harvest posts, it is a well-regarded local food stop along the rural Vancouver Island cycling corridor.

grocery.name: Road 7 Country Fruit Stand
grocery.desc: Road 7 Country Fruit Market is a family-owned farm market in Oliver, BC, operated by the Dhaliwal family who have been farming the Okanagan Valley since the early 1980s. Opened formally in 2021, the market sells handpicked seasonal fruit and vegetables — cherries, strawberries, apricots, peaches, apples, pears, herbs — along with jams and cherry juice, all grown on their own orchards. The market also offers orchard tours and a cider club, making it a destination stop for cyclists exploring the South Okanagan.

notes.Basic groceries: Website lists fresh seasonal fruit (cherries, strawberries, apricots, peaches, apples, pears), handpicked herbs and vegetables every morning, and jams

grocery.name: Orchard Hill Estate Cidery & Fruit Market
grocery.desc: Orchard Hill Estate Cidery is a small family-run operation on the Golden Mile bench between Oliver and Osoyoos, producing hand-crafted apple cider exclusively from Okanagan-grown dessert apples since 2006. The Dhaliwal family tends 14 acres of high-density orchard on a scenic south-facing bench, with their flagship Red Roof cider distributed across BC. Cyclists on the Golden Mile route may find local cider and potentially fresh fruit available, though the retail farm stand component is not explicitly detailed on the website.

grocery.name: Dhillon Farms Fruits & Vegetables
grocery.desc: Dhillon Farms Fruits & Vegetables is a farm-direct produce stand located near Oliver, BC, in the South Okanagan. Tagged in OSM as shop=farm, it sits in one of BC's most productive orchard and market-garden regions, where roadside farm stands are a staple of the local landscape. Touring cyclists passing through the South Okanagan may find it a useful stop for fresh seasonal produce.

grocery.name: PineRidge Farm Market
grocery.desc: PineRidge Farm Market is a farm-direct retail shop located on Vancouver Island, tagged in OpenStreetMap as a farm shop. Farm markets in this region typically offer locally grown seasonal produce and farm goods direct to customers. Cyclists passing through the area may find it a useful stop for fresh provisions.

detail.address: 2715 Turnbull Road, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 2L7

grocery.name: Honeyberry Farm Market
grocery.desc: Honeyberry Farm Market is a small family-run farm stand near Heffley Lake, roughly 40 minutes north of Kamloops on the road to Sun Peaks Resort. The farm specialises in haskap berries (also called honeyberries), offering U-Pick sessions in July alongside spray-free seasonal vegetables, farm-fresh eggs, local wildflower honey, and homemade jams. Set at 944 m elevation with scenic valley views, picnic tables, and livestock to visit, it sits right beside the Heffley Recreation Site and Campground.

grocery.name: Omineca Source for Sports
grocery.desc: Omineca Source for Sports is a Source for Sports franchise retail location in the Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior region of British Columbia. Source for Sports stores typically carry a range of sporting goods that may include cycling equipment, though no bike-specific inventory or services could be confirmed for this particular location. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it worth a visit, but should call ahead to confirm bike service availability.

grocery.name: Cask & Barrel
grocery.desc: Cask & Barrel is a specialty liquor store in West Kelowna that has been operating since 2015, billing itself as the Okanagan's premier destination for local and international alcoholic beverages. The store is particularly well-regarded for its curated craft beer program — with a focus on bringing lower mainland BC breweries to the interior — alongside a thoughtful wine selection guided by a certified ISG Sommelier on staff. Touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan can stock up on local wines, BC craft beers, craft ciders, and spirits.

detail.address: 1135 Stevens Road, West Kelowna, BC V1Z 2S8

grocery.name: Polonia Sausage House
grocery.desc: Polonia Sausage House is a family-owned Polish delicatessen operating since 1989, one of six Lower Mainland locations, offering house-made gluten-free Polish sausages crafted from traditional family recipes. Beyond deli meats, the shop carries imported Eastern European cheeses, pickles, sauerkraut, perogies, and baked goods. It has been recognized as one of the top three meat products in Canada by the Ukrainian-Canadian Professional Business Association.

detail.address: 2745 East Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V5K 1Z8

grocery.name: Shannon Lake Convenience Store
grocery.desc: A convenience store located in the Shannon Lake area near Kelowna, serving the local community with typical retail items.

detail.address: 3099 Shannon Lake Rd, West Kelowna, BC V4T 2M2, Canada

grocery.name: The Liquor Co. 1977
grocery.desc: The Liquor Co. 1977 is a cooperative liquor retailer grown out of the Peninsula Co-op, which was founded in 1977 by Saanich Peninsula residents committed to community and cooperative values. Operating multiple Vancouver Island locations, the Esquimalt outlet is situated in Esquimalt Plaza and carries beer, wine, and spirits with an emphasis on local and Canadian products. As a co-op, members receive rebates and exclusive offers, distinguishing it from a typical chain liquor store.

detail.address: Unit 12 - 1153 Esquimalt Rd, Victoria, BC V9A 3N7

grocery.name: Whole Foods Market
grocery.desc: Whole Foods Market's Robson Street location is a full-service natural and organic supermarket in Vancouver's West End, steps from Stanley Park. The store features in-house eateries including a coffee bar, juice bar, sandwich counter, and a hot and salad bar — making it a solid stop for cyclists looking to restock or grab a hot meal. Grocery delivery via Instacart and Amazon Prime savings are also available.

notes.Hot food: Website lists a 'Hot & Salad Bar' with 'customizable seasonal entrées, salads and sides with keto- and paleo-friendly options', plus a WFM Coffee Bar and sandwich counter

grocery.name: Rail Trail Cafe & Market
grocery.desc: A convenience store and cafe on Kalamalka Road in Coldstream, BC, positioned near the Rail Trail. Offers market goods and light food for quick resupply. A useful stop for cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Success Supermarket
grocery.desc: Success Supermarket is a neighbourhood greengrocer in Richmond's Blundell area, offering fresh produce and grocery staples to the local community. Situated in a strip-mall unit, it would serve as a resupply point for cyclists riding Richmond's extensive dyke and connector trails.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
