grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a provincially operated retail outlet in Langley's Walnut Grove neighbourhood, selling wine, beer, spirits, coolers, ciders, and non-alcoholic beverages across a broad selection. Operated by the BC Liquor Distribution Branch, it is one of 198 BCLIQUOR stores across the province and accepts cash, debit, Visa, and Mastercard. The store also accepts empty beverage container returns for deposit refunds, a potential convenience for touring cyclists carrying empties.

grocery.name: Meridian Farm Market
grocery.desc: Meridian Farm Market is a farm-focused grocery store in Maple Ridge offering a wide range of locally sourced and craft products including grass-fed beef, free-run chicken, fresh produce, artisan cheese, and baked goods. It operates as both a physical retail location and an online ordering service with delivery across the Lower Mainland. Touring cyclists passing through Maple Ridge would find it a well-stocked stop for resupply across most food categories.

grocery.name: North Shore Liquor Shop
grocery.desc: North Shore Liquor Shop is a neighborhood liquor retailer on Lynn Valley Road in North Vancouver. It serves the local community and provides a convenient retail stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Lakeview Store
grocery.desc: The Lakeview Store has been a grocery anchor on the remote east shore of Kootenay Lake since the early 1940s, operating as part of the larger Kootenay Lakeview resort complex. It offers a surprisingly full selection including fresh produce, specialty cheeses, organic and bulk foods, a rural liquor agency, and espresso drinks made from locally roasted beans. Lakeshore picnic tables make it a natural stop for cyclists travelling the scenic Highway 3A corridor, which is rated the number one motorcycle road in southern BC.

notes.Basic groceries: Website describes a fully stocked grocery store with fresh produce, specialty cheeses, organic and bulk foods, fresh bread, canned and frozen foods, and seasonal local products
notes.Hot food: Store page lists samosas and sausage rolls, fresh sandwiches, and espresso drinks (latte, americano, cappuccino, espresso shots) made from locally roasted beans

grocery.name: Mid Island Liquor
grocery.desc: Mid Island Liquor is a liquor retail store located in Duncan on Cowichan Lake Road, serving the mid-Island region of Vancouver Island. As a stop on routes through the Cowichan Valley, it offers touring cyclists a convenient place to pick up beverages. The shop is situated in a unit within a commercial complex near Duncan.

grocery.name: Xwup Xwup Store
grocery.desc: Xwup Xwup Store is a supermarket on Highway 101 in Powell River. As a grocery store, it provides touring cyclists with an opportunity to resupply provisions during their journey through the region.

grocery.name: Tom's Food Market
grocery.desc: Tom's Food Market is a convenience and food market on 148 Street in the Surrey area of Metro Vancouver. As a neighbourhood food market, it could serve as a basic resupply point for cyclists travelling through this urban corridor. Very little detail about the store's offerings is publicly available.

grocery.name: Chevron
grocery.desc: A Chevron-branded gas station and convenience store in Chilliwack, BC, sitting near postal code V2S 2A4. As a fuel and convenience stop, it likely carries snacks and packaged goods typical of gas station c-stores. Touring cyclists passing through Chilliwack may find it a convenient roadside resupply point.

grocery.name: Four Season Farm
grocery.desc: Four Season Farm is a greengrocer vendor at Granville Island Public Market, one of Vancouver's most popular waterfront destinations and a frequent stop for cyclists exploring the False Creek seawall. The market sits in an indoor setting and is reachable via the well-travelled Seaside Greenway. As a farm-focused produce stand, it likely offers fresh local fruits and vegetables to market visitors.

grocery.name: Country Grocer
grocery.desc: Founded in 1986 as Village Market by Pete and Jo-Anne Pimlott, this family-owned 26,000-square-foot store is the only grocery store serving Lake Cowichan's 3,000 year-round residents, along with a large seasonal influx of campers, hikers, and lake visitors. The store includes a bakery, deli, health foods department, fresh floral, and a café with wireless internet. A well-stocked outdoor section appears seasonally to serve the area's active recreation community.

detail.address: 83 Lake Cowichan Rd, Lake Cowichan, BC V0R 2G0

notes.Basic groceries: Full-service supermarket described as Lake Cowichan's only grocery store, with bakery, deli, health foods, and seafood departments

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: Circle K is a 24-hour convenience store chain location in Vancouver's West End on Davie Street, a busy urban corridor. This location functions as both a petrol station and convenience store, offering snacks, fresh food, hot roller grill items, and coffee. Its around-the-clock availability makes it a reliable resupply stop for touring cyclists at any hour.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Fresh Food Fast', 'Coffee', and 'Roller Grill' as store services

grocery.name: Nadleh Store
grocery.desc: A convenience store serving the Fort Fraser area with basic supplies and goods. Located on Nautley Road, it offers a practical stop for cyclists and travelers passing through this central BC community.

grocery.name: Co-op Tappen Food Store
grocery.desc: Co-op Tappen Food Store is a locally-owned, member-governed co-operative grocery on the Trans-Canada Highway in the small community of Tappen, BC, part of the Federated Co-operatives network. Non-members are explicitly welcome to shop alongside member-owners. Its Trans-Canada location makes it a natural resupply point for cyclists travelling through the Shuswap corridor.

grocery.name: Polish Deli Metrotown
grocery.desc: Metrotown Polish Deli is a specialty food shop on Kingsway in Burnaby offering Polish cuisine products. Located near the busy Metrotown commercial area, it caters to those seeking Eastern European deli goods. Cyclists passing through Burnaby's urban corridor may find it a distinctive food resupply option.

grocery.name: Proviland Gtocery
grocery.desc: Proviland Gtocery is a supermarket on Hastings Street serving the North Vancouver area. The OSM record was field-checked in March 2026 and shows no signs of closure, suggesting it is an active neighbourhood grocery store. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a convenient stop for resupply.

grocery.name: Urban Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Urban Liquor Store is a privately owned wine-specialist liquor store in Kelowna, staffed by WSET-certified sommeliers, Cicerone-trained beer specialists, and wine scholars who offer personalized guidance. Located in the heart of BC's premier wine region, it curates craft beers, local pet nat and piquette wines, innovative spirits, and ciders. Cyclists passing through wine country can also take advantage of local delivery services and online ordering.

grocery.name: Vancouver Fresh Mart
grocery.desc: Vancouver Fresh Mart is a supermarket rebranded from SuperValu. It operates as a typical grocery store for resupply during cycling tours.

grocery.name: Persia Foods
grocery.desc: Persia Foods is a family-owned grocery chain that has served the Vancouver Lower Mainland since 1996, positioning itself as an affordable source of fresh, healthy, and ethnically diverse foods. The Commercial Drive location sits on one of Vancouver's most vibrant and cycle-friendly streets, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the city. With nine locations across Metro Vancouver, it is a well-established local institution known for cultural variety in its product range.

grocery.name: Gastronomia Italia
grocery.desc: Gastronomia Italia is a specialty Italian food shop and deli operated by Chef Delbert Cirfera in the heart of historic downtown New Westminster. The shop handcrafts Roman-style pizza and artisan focaccia sandwiches using imported D.O.P.-certified meats and cheeses, bakes breads and pastries fresh daily, and stocks a curated selection of imported Italian pantry goods. For a touring cyclist passing through the area, it offers a genuine espresso and a made-to-order sandwich that stands well apart from typical convenience stops.

notes.Hot food: Website confirms freshly made Roman-style pizza, artisan sandwiches on homemade focaccia, deli platters, and espresso/coffee brewed to order

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a provincial government-operated retail outlet selling wine, spirits, beer, coolers, and ciders, part of the 198-store BCLIQUOR chain run by the BC Liquor Distribution Branch. Located on 100 Street in Fort St. John, it serves as the primary source for packaged alcohol in this northern BC hub city. Touring cyclists passing through Fort St. John can stock up on beverages here as a convenient stop along the Alaska Highway corridor.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: A Walmart Supercenter (Store 3188) located in Langford, BC, on the outskirts of Greater Victoria. As a full-format Supercenter, it carries a broad grocery section alongside general merchandise including clothing, electronics, and household goods. For touring cyclists passing through the Westshore corridor, it offers one-stop resupply potential for food, basic gear, and sundries.

grocery.name: Terra Nova Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Terra Nova Liquor Store is a retail alcohol shop located in a strip-mall unit along Westminster Highway in Richmond's Terra Nova area. It serves the surrounding residential and cycling community near the Terra Nova Rural Park and the popular riverside cycling routes. Cyclists passing through the area may find it a convenient stop for beverages.

grocery.name: London Drugs
grocery.desc: London Drugs is a 100% Canadian-owned retail department store chain. The Nanaimo location is a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking general merchandise and supplies.

grocery.name: Galey Farms
grocery.desc: Galey Farms is a family-run farm market, corn maze, and miniature railway in the Blenkinsop Valley on the southern tip of Vancouver Island. During the growing season they sell their own-grown strawberries, corn, potatoes, broccoli, kale, blueberries, pumpkins, and squash alongside local honey products, making it a genuine source of fresh food rather than a convenience stop. The farm sits directly adjacent to the Lochside Regional Trail and won Canada's top ecological award in 2002 for restoring a 600-metre section of Blenkinsop Creek alongside that trail.

grocery.name: Fetch Panda
grocery.desc: Fetch Panda is a Canadian convenience store chain launched in 2020, operating stores, gas stations, liquor outlets, and car washes across multiple provinces. The Nanaimo location on Nicol Street offers convenience shopping including snacks, beverages, hot food items, and automotive supplies. It is part of a growing independent chain serving millions of Canadians annually.

notes.Hot food: About page states: 'Our well-stocked store features a variety of snacks, beverages, Hot food items, pizzas and automotive supplies.'

grocery.name: S Mart
grocery.desc: S Mart is a convenience store on Beresford Street in Burnaby. It stocks typical convenience items and supplies accessible to the local community and passing cyclists.

grocery.name: Mitra's Market
grocery.desc: A local supermarket in North Vancouver offering everyday groceries and household items. Located on Clyde Avenue with convenient street-level access for touring cyclists.

grocery.name: Afra Bakery & Supermarket
grocery.desc: Afra Bakery & Supermarket is a neighbourhood convenience store and bakery in North Vancouver combining grocery staples with baked goods. Its dual bakery-and-supermarket identity suggests a local, independent character that distinguishes it from chain convenience outlets. Touring cyclists moving through the North Shore corridor may find it a practical stop for resupply.

grocery.name: Nature's Fare Markets
grocery.desc: Nature's Fare Markets is a BC natural and organic grocery chain with a strong commitment to certified-organic, non-GMO, and locally sourced products, banning over 500 ingredients from its shelves. The West Kelowna location has operated since 2008 and includes an in-store Bistro offering grab-and-go prepared foods and smoothies made with local and organic ingredients. Cyclists will find a wide range of organic produce, health foods, vitamins, supplements, and ready-to-eat options under one roof.

detail.address: 104-3480 Carrington Road, West Kelowna, BC V4T 3C1

grocery.name: Kempf Orchard
grocery.desc: Kempf Orchards is a family-run U-pick cherry orchard in Kelowna's Okanagan region, with an orcharding tradition going back to 1966. Cyclists passing through during cherry season can pick their own fresh cherries directly from the trees, choosing from several varieties including Rainier, Lapins, and Sour cherries. The orchard is a beloved local summer destination and a genuine taste-of-place stop on any Okanagan tour.

grocery.name: Harrison Lake Market
grocery.desc: Harrison Lake Market is a convenience store located on Esplanade Avenue in Harrison Hot Springs, a small lakeside resort community popular with cyclists exploring the Fraser Valley. Sitting steps from the shores of Harrison Lake, it is a practical resupply point for touring cyclists passing through or staying in the area. The two-storey retail building suggests a well-established commercial presence in this tourist-oriented town.

grocery.name: The Bottle Shop Liquor Store at the Waldorf
grocery.desc: A liquor store located in the Waldorf building on East Hastings Street in Vancouver. Provides beverages and convenience items for cyclists passing through the downtown area.

grocery.name: Copperside Foods
grocery.desc: Copperside Foods is a convenience store in Terrace, BC located on Kalum Street. It provides quick access to basic supplies and refreshments. A practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the region.

grocery.name: Jack's Place Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Jack's Place, co-located with Kuma Sushi, is a casual lunch and dinner patio hangout at Bear Mountain in Langford, BC, offering a wide-ranging menu of comfort food, wood-fired pizza, sushi rolls, and handcrafted cocktails. The eclectic menu — spanning halibut tacos, poke bowls, dragon rolls, and meatball sliders — makes it a satisfying mid-ride or post-ride meal stop for cyclists exploring the Bear Mountain and Langford area west of Victoria. Online ordering and gift cards are available.

detail.address: 2020 Country Club Way, Langford, BC V9B 6R3

grocery.name: Chef on the Run
grocery.desc: Chef on the Run is a family-run gourmet takeout business in the heart of Sidney that has operated since 1997, offering rotating weekly menus of fresh ready-to-heat entrées alongside frozen take 'n' bake pies and pasta dishes. Their in-store deli serves made-to-order sandwiches and homemade soups, and the shop stocks a selection of imported English groceries for a taste of British pantry staples. Touring cyclists could stop here for a hot meal, a hearty soup, or unique specialty provisions not found in a typical grocery store.

notes.Basic groceries: Website confirms selection of imported English groceries and frozen grab-and-go items; not a full-range supermarket but food products are available for purchase
notes.Hot food: In-store deli serves made-to-order sandwiches and homemade soups per the About Us page

grocery.name: Fairway Market Quadra Village
grocery.desc: Fairway Market is a family-owned Vancouver Island grocery chain operating since 1963, now one of the largest independent grocers on the island with nine locations. The Quadra Village store is a full-service supermarket offering a wide range of departments including a deli, bakery, Asian kitchen, and sushi counter alongside standard grocery aisles. It is locally focused, stocking BC and island-produced goods and catering to diverse community tastes.

notes.Hot food: Website lists Deli, Asian Kitchen, and Sushi Village as in-store departments, indicating prepared and hot food service

grocery.name: J-Zone
grocery.desc: J-Zone is a Japanese specialty store operated by J-Zone Trading Inc., stocking imported Japanese food products including instant noodles, frozen meat and fish, seasonings, snacks, and drinks alongside non-food items like stationery, toys, and trading cards. The store describes itself as 'a small trip to Japan' with staff knowledgeable about Japanese products. Touring cyclists passing through Vancouver's Renfrew neighbourhood can resupply here with packaged foods, snacks, and cold drinks.

grocery.name: Persian Baanou Supermarket
grocery.desc: Persian Baanou Supermarket is a Persian grocery store located in North Vancouver on Sixth Street. Touring cyclists looking for Middle Eastern and Persian specialty products — including pantry staples, prepared foods, and imported goods not found in mainstream supermarkets — will find this a useful stop. The supermarket format suggests a reasonably broad selection for restocking supplies.

grocery.name: Al Baraka Specialty Foods & Bakery LTD
grocery.desc: Al Baraka is a small convenience store in Surrey specializing in high-quality halal meat and Middle Eastern groceries, including fresh-baked Iraqi bread available daily and pita bread five days a week. The shop also stocks frozen traditional Iraqi food alongside everyday convenience items like snacks, soft drinks, toiletries, and tobacco products. A touring cyclist looking for halal provisions or culturally specific Middle Eastern staples in the Surrey area would find this a unique stop.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a government-operated retail liquor outlet in the Saanich area of Greater Victoria, part of the province-wide BCLIQUOR network run by BC's Liquor Distribution Branch. The store carries a broad selection of wine, spirits, beer, coolers, ciders, and non-alcoholic products. For touring cyclists, it is a convenient stop to resupply with beverages on routes through the McKenzie Avenue corridor.

grocery.name: Liquor Giant
grocery.desc: Liquor Giant is a family-owned liquor retail chain that has been serving the Fraser Valley since 2011, operating multiple stores across Chilliwack and Abbotsford under the Liquor Giant Group banner. The Chilliwack location was named Best Beer and Wine Store in Chilliwack by the 2026 Chilliwack Progress A-List readers' choice awards. Touring cyclists can stock up on BC craft beers, local wines, spirits, and ready-to-drink beverages, with bulk and event ordering also available.

grocery.name: Nature's Fare Markets
grocery.desc: Nature's Fare Markets is a health-focused natural food supermarket chain with a location in White Rock, BC, opened in 2016. The store stocks certified organic produce, ethically sourced meat and dairy, vitamins, and a wide range of dietary-specific products (vegan, keto, gluten-free, paleo). An in-store Bistro and grab-and-go section offer smoothies, salads, entrees, and breakfast items for cyclists looking for a quality food stop.

detail.address: 15180 North Bluff Road, White Rock, BC V4B 3E5

notes.Hot food: In-store Bistro serving 'local, organic and sustainable foods and drinks'; grab-and-go salads, entrees, breakfast, and smoothies listed on store page

grocery.name: A&G Supermarket
grocery.desc: A&G Supermarket is a South Asian grocery store that opened in August 2025 on South Fraser Way in Abbotsford. The store carries a range of South Asian staples — including atta, besan, and pulses — alongside fresh produce and international snack items. Cyclists passing through Abbotsford on South Fraser Way will find it a convenient stop for provisions.

grocery.name: Mi Tierra Latina
grocery.desc: Mi Tierra Latina is a specialty Latin American grocery store stocking products from nine countries including Colombia, Mexico, Brazil, Peru, and Venezuela. It carries a wide range of authentic staples — tortillas, chiles, sauces, rice and beans, coffees, and sweets — that would be difficult to find at a mainstream supermarket. The store also operates an online shop with delivery across Vancouver and in-store pickup.

grocery.name: Shallon Refillery & Naturals
grocery.desc: Shallon Refillery & Naturals is a small zero-waste shop in Brentwood Bay on Vancouver Island, carrying a curated range of sustainable Canadian-made body care, personal care, and household cleaning products. The refillery model allows customers to bring their own containers and refill products like soaps, lotions, and cleaning concentrates. The shop has a friendly neighbourhood feel, complete with Mabel the shop dog, and is rooted in the local community since opening in 2021.

detail.address: 7175 West Saanich Road, Brentwood Bay, BC V8M 1P7

grocery.name: China World Supermarket
grocery.desc: China World Supermarket is a Chinese-language-oriented supermarket in Richmond, BC, serving the area's large East Asian community. The store operates from a standalone building on Odlin Crescent and stocks a broad range of Asian grocery products. For a touring cyclist, it offers a full supermarket resupply opportunity in suburban Richmond.

grocery.name: All Of Oils, Wholesome Oils & Vinegars
grocery.desc: All Of Oils is a Fraser Valley specialty retailer focused on extra virgin olive oils, flavoured balsamic vinegars, and gourmet foods, operating two tasting-room locations in South Surrey and Langley. Their EVOOs are imported twice yearly from growers across multiple hemispheres, with full chemistry and tasting-panel data displayed for every product. In-store samplings are available, and the shop offers custom corporate gifting and olive oil tasting events.

grocery.name: Urban Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Urban Liquor Store is a privately-owned Kelowna liquor store that positions itself as a community hub, with staff including WSET Advanced-certified and Cicerone-trained specialists who focus on local BC craft beer, wine, spirits, and cider. Founded in 2015 and led by a WSET Sommelier owner, the shop emphasises quality craft products and sustainability alongside a loyalty program and event services. Delivery is available within 8 km of the store, and online ordering is offered for customers further afield.

grocery.name: Nesters Market
grocery.desc: Nesters Market is a Western Canadian neighbourhood grocery chain founded in Whistler in 1987 and now operating 16+ locations across BC and Alberta. The Main Street Vancouver location offers a full range of fresh produce, deli and bistro, in-store bakery, pharmacy, and a strong selection of local, organic, and specialty products. Operated by the Pattison Food Group, it positions itself as a quality-focused community grocer and would serve touring cyclists well for resupply.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Deli & Bistro' as an in-store service

grocery.name: Murray's Grocery
grocery.desc: Murray's Grocery is a convenience store in Ucluelet on Vancouver Island's west coast. It serves as a supply stop for local residents and passing cyclists.

grocery.name: Green Lake Station
grocery.desc: Green Lake Station is a café and Chevron fuel stop on Crazy Canuck Drive near Green Lake in Whistler, open seven days a week. It serves an all-day breakfast kitchen, pizza, burgers, and paninis alongside BC-roasted drip coffee and espresso drinks, with a patio and a live-edge wooden communal table inside. The shop also stocks souvenirs and gifts, rounding out its appeal as a rest stop for anyone rolling through the area.

detail.address: 8110 Crazy Canuck Dr, Whistler, BC V8E 0G8

notes.Hot food: All-day breakfast kitchen, pizza (from 11am), burgers, paninis, and breakfast sandwiches confirmed on the menu page
notes.Device charging: Website states 'Free wifi and plenty of outlets' in the café seating area

grocery.name: The Frog Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Frog Liquor Store is a neighbourhood institution that has been serving the Coquitlam–Port Moody border area since the 1980s. Originally part of a pub-and-liquor-store complex (the pub closed June 2024), the liquor store carries an extensive selection of craft beer, wine, and spirits. A local delivery service covers Coquitlam, Port Moody, and Port Coquitlam.

grocery.name: Cropthorne Farm
grocery.desc: Cropthorne Farm is a Certified Organic family farm on Westham Island, accessible via a century-old wooden bridge where the Fraser River meets the Salish Sea. The year-round farm stand is stocked with fresh-picked organic vegetables and seasonal flowers grown on-site across 24 acres. It is a genuine farm-gate stop with a rural, wildlife-rich setting that touring cyclists exploring the Westham Island loop would find rewarding.

notes.Basic groceries: Farm stand fully stocked with fresh organic vegetables and seasonal flowers, grown on-site; open year-round

grocery.name: Sunshine Market
grocery.desc: Sunshine Market is a neighbourhood grocery store in Kelowna's Lakeshore area, claiming the largest selection of Indian groceries in the city alongside fresh Okanagan produce sourced through direct farm partnerships. Beyond standard grocery staples, it runs a full grill and deli serving hot breakfasts, daily lunch specials, and Indian dishes such as butter chicken and chicken biryani. Touring cyclists can resupply with fresh fruit, ready-to-eat hot meals, specialty provisions, and baked goods all under one roof.

notes.Hot food: Fresh Daily Buffet with breakfast platters and daily rotating lunch specials; Grill & Deli serving chicken wings, poutine, fish & chips, Indian dishes, and more

grocery.name: Berezan Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Berezan Liquor Store (Willoughby location) is one of six BC outlets operated by the Berezan Hospitality Group, a 100% Canadian family-owned company with over 30 years in hospitality. The store is situated in a strip-mall unit in Langley's Willoughby neighbourhood and is part of a larger group that also runs Sasquatch Mountain Resort, gaming centres, and a hostel at Big White. The group markets its stores on friendly staff, broad product selection, and in-store contests.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercenter in Cranbrook serving the Kootenay region, carrying groceries alongside electronics, clothing, toys, and furniture under one roof. As a large-format supercenter, it is one of the most comprehensive resupply stops available to touring cyclists passing through Cranbrook. Store 3183 is located on Willowbrook Drive on the commercial strip west of the city centre.

grocery.name: Halal Urban Fresh Meats
grocery.desc: Halal Urban Fresh Meats is a specialty halal butcher shop and deli mart on Victoria's Quadra Street, offering certified Zabiha Halal cuts of beef, lamb, chicken, and goat prepared by master butchers with vacuum-packed, ready-to-cook convenience. Beyond fresh meat, the shop carries a global selection of sauces, marinades, and spices alongside grocery staples like canned goods, frozen items, breads, and rice. All products come with a 100% satisfaction guarantee, making it a reliable stop for cyclists seeking halal provisions in the city.

grocery.name: Whole Foods Market
grocery.desc: Whole Foods Market in West Vancouver is a large natural and organic supermarket carrying a wide selection of organic produce, sustainable seafood, and specialty grocery items. The store houses multiple in-house eateries including a coffee bar, pizza counter, burrito bar, juice bar, made-to-order sandwich counter, and a sushi bar, making it a convenient one-stop resupply point. As an Amazon-affiliated location, it also offers grocery pickup and delivery for Prime members.

notes.Hot food: Multiple in-store eateries confirmed by website: WFM Coffee Bar, West Van Pizza, Burrito Bar, Juice Bar, West Van Sandwich, and Kikka Sushi

grocery.name: Angry Otter Liquor @ West Railway
grocery.desc: Angry Otter Liquor is the liquor retail brand of Otter Co-op, a locally-owned co-operative serving communities across BC including Chilliwack, Abbotsford, Langley, and several Interior towns. The West Railway branch sits at 2520 Montvue Avenue in Chilliwack and offers beer, wine, and spirits. As part of a multi-location regional co-op, it caters primarily to neighbourhood retail customers.

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: Circle K is a 24/7 convenience store and petrol station on East Broadway in Vancouver, part of the international Circle K/Couche-Tard chain. Touring cyclists can pick up snacks, beverages, and hot food from the Roller Grill at any hour. Its around-the-clock operation makes it a reliable resupply point on this busy commercial corridor.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Roller Grill' as a store service, a standard Circle K hot food offering

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: A Circle K convenience store and petrol station on Cook Street in Victoria, open around the clock every day of the week. The store offers packaged snacks and drinks alongside hot food options including a roller grill and freshly brewed coffee. Its central Victoria location and 24-hour availability make it a practical resupply stop for cyclists passing through.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Fresh Food Fast', 'Coffee', and 'Roller Grill' as in-store services

grocery.name: Choices Market
grocery.desc: Choices Market is a 100% BC-owned and operated natural and specialty grocery chain that has been serving communities since 1990, with locations from Kitsilano to Kelowna. The Yaletown location on Richards Street stocks local, organic, and specialty food items, and offers free personalized nutrition tours with on-staff dietitians and holistic nutritionists. For touring cyclists, it provides a full-service grocery stop in the heart of Vancouver with a wide range of health-focused and specialty dietary products.

grocery.name: Nesvog Meats & Sausage
grocery.desc: Nesvog Meats & Sausage is a family-owned butcher, deli, and specialty grocer established in 2005 with Scandinavian roots, operating two Nanaimo locations. The Bowen Road shop carries store-made sausages, fresh and frozen meats, ready-to-eat deli items, baked goods, local produce from the Nesvog Family Farm, and a range of groceries. Voted #1 Best in the City for meat and deli, it offers a broad selection of gluten-free, dairy-free, and sugar-free options.

detail.address: 2139 Bowen Road, Nanaimo, British Columbia V9S 1H8

grocery.name: Ayoub's Dried Fruit and Nuts
grocery.desc: Ayoub's is a BC-based specialty food chain selling daily in-house roasted nuts, dried fruits, seeds, sweets, and spices sourced from around the world. The Main Street Vancouver location is one of nine retail stores across the Lower Mainland and beyond. Touring cyclists will find a strong selection of high-calorie trail mixes, energy mixes, and dried fruit blends well-suited for long rides.

grocery.name: Gibo Health
grocery.desc: Gibo Health is a convenience shop in Vancouver. Based on its name, it may specialize in health-related products. Specific amenities and current details could not be verified due to website access issues.

detail.address: 4551 Number 3 Rd #190, Richmond, BC V6X 2C3, Canada

grocery.name: Urban Grocer
grocery.desc: Urban Grocer is a neighbourhood grocery store situated at The Junction of Oak Bay Avenue and Fort Street in Victoria, run by people with over 50 years of experience in the Vancouver Island and Gulf Islands grocery trade. The store emphasises fresh and organic produce, operates an in-house deli, and carries a curated selection of local Vancouver Island products under the Island Good brand. It is a convenient resupply stop for cyclists riding the Oak Bay and Fort Street corridors.

grocery.name: Kingswood Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Kingswood Liquor Store is a community-serving independent liquor retailer on No 5 Road in Richmond, stocking spirits, wines, coolers, beer, snacks, and tobacco with a large cold single-beer and cooler section. The store advertises competitive pricing below government rates and offers delivery through SkipTheDishes and Fantuan. Free on-site parking makes it an easy stop for cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Liquor Giant
grocery.desc: Liquor Giant is a privately operated retail liquor store on Young Road near the Chilliwack Airport, part of the Fraser Valley–based Liquor Giant Group chain operating since 2011. The store stocks a wide selection of spirits, wine, domestic and BC craft beer, and ready-to-drink products, and positions itself on competitive pricing. Third-party delivery through Woww Delivery is also available for those who can't make it in person.

grocery.name: Esso
grocery.desc: An Esso fuel station and convenience store in Ashcroft, BC, operating under the name Ashcroft Travel Centre on its brand page. Located on Cornwall Road, it offers fuel including diesel, an ATM, and a car wash. For touring cyclists passing through this small Interior BC community, it provides a practical stop for convenience store goods and fuel.

notes.Pump: Website lists 'Air Tower / Air' as a station top feature; gas station air towers can be used by cyclists to inflate tires

grocery.name: Winning Trading Co
grocery.desc: Winning Trading Co is a Vancouver-based wholesale distributor supplying sushi restaurants and other food service businesses with frozen seafood, dry goods, paper products, and cleaning supplies. Operating out of a two-storey building in the Grandview-Woodland neighbourhood near Venables Street, it serves the Lower Mainland's Japanese restaurant industry. Access appears trade-only, so a touring cyclist stopping by would find a commercial loading environment rather than a retail shop floor.

grocery.name: Annieville Market
grocery.desc: Annieville Market is a supermarket in Delta located on River Road. It serves the local community and offers a grocery shopping stop for touring cyclists.

grocery.name: Fetch Panda Market
grocery.desc: Fetch Panda Market is a convenience store and gas station operated by the Fetch Panda chain in the small rural community of Celista on Squilax-Anglemont Road. The chain's locations offer fuel (regular and premium), a stocked convenience store, and hot food. For cyclists touring the Shuswap area, this is a notable resupply point in an otherwise sparsely serviced stretch.

notes.Hot food: Website about page states locations offer 'Hot food items, pizzas'

grocery.name: Express News
grocery.desc: Express News is a convenience store located on Southwest Marine Drive in Vancouver, near the Marine Gateway transit hub. It serves the surrounding residential and commercial area and would be a practical stop for cyclists on Marine Drive needing snacks or supplies. The Instagram handle suggests an active local presence, though no detailed content was retrievable.

grocery.name: H Mart
grocery.desc: H Mart is an Asian-focused supermarket chain located on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. It serves as a full-service grocery resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the neighborhood.

grocery.name: KBF Farm Market
grocery.desc: KBF Farms is a local berry farm and produce operation with fruit stands throughout the Chilliwack/Abbotsford area, selling fresh-picked blueberries, raspberries, strawberries, corn, garlic, and ice cream. The 40040 No. 3 Road location serves as the farm's head office, while retail stands operate at Yale Road, Evans Road, and Young Road in Chilliwack. Visiting cyclists on routes near Highway 1 in the Fraser Valley may find this a convenient seasonal stop for fresh local produce.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a provincial chain location in Vancouver's West End. The store offers a range of alcoholic beverages and is a convenient stop for touring cyclists in an urban area.

grocery.name: Beacon Landing Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Beacon Landing Liquor and More is a full-service liquor retailer on Beacon Avenue in Sidney, offering beer, wine, and spirits for in-store pickup or local delivery. The shop runs a rewards program and regular tastings, and its central location on Sidney's main commercial strip makes it a convenient resupply point for cyclists passing through the Saanich Peninsula.

grocery.name: 7-Eleven
grocery.desc: A 7-Eleven convenience store in North Vancouver, offering quick access to basic supplies and refreshments for touring cyclists. Standard chain location suitable for brief stops during a ride.

grocery.name: Choices Market
grocery.desc: Choices Market on Commercial Drive is part of Western Canada's largest natural and organic food grocery chain, emphasizing locally sourced and Canadian-produced products. The Commercial Drive location sits on one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors, making it a convenient provisioning stop for touring cyclists passing through the city. The store carries an extensive selection of organic, natural, and local food items.

grocery.name: Maple Pizza and Grace Market
grocery.desc: Maple Pizza, Grace Market appears to be a combined pizza and convenience shop in Richmond, BC, tagged in OSM with a convenience store designation alongside pizza, ice cream, and chicken cuisine. The OSM record offers minimal detail and no verified contact information for this location. Touring cyclists may find snacks or quick food here, but the listing requires on-the-ground verification before it can be confidently recommended.

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: Circle K is a 24/7 convenience store and petrol station in Vancouver's Fairview neighbourhood, part of the global Circle K/Couche-Tard chain. It offers standard convenience-store goods alongside hot prepared foods including roller grill items and fresh coffee. Its around-the-clock hours make it a reliable resupply stop for cyclists at any point in the day or night.

notes.Hot food: Website store page lists 'Fresh Food Fast', 'Roller Grill', and 'Coffee' as available services

grocery.name: Harvest
grocery.desc: Harvest Market is UBC Food Services' flagship campus grocery store, situated at Ponderosa Commons on the University of British Columbia's Vancouver campus. It stocks basic groceries alongside gourmet prepared foods including rotisserie chicken, fresh salads, epic sandwiches, and take-out meals, making it a well-rounded provisioning stop. The market sits at a busy campus crossroads and serves tens of thousands of students, staff, and faculty daily.

detail.address: Ponderosa Commons, Corner of University Blvd & West Mall, Vancouver, BC

notes.Hot food: Website lists rotisserie chicken and take-out meals as available offerings

grocery.name: Bangla Bazar
grocery.desc: Bangla Bazar is a Halal-certified Bangladeshi supermarket in Vancouver specializing in South Asian groceries and products. It serves as a neighborhood market focused on halal-compliant items and Southeast Asian specialty ingredients. Touring cyclists may find it useful as a source for specialty groceries and international foods not typically found in mainstream supermarkets.

grocery.name: The Liquor Co. 1977 – Keating
grocery.desc: Liquor Express is a liquor retail store on Keating Cross Road on the Saanich Peninsula, serving the area between Victoria and Sidney. The store sells beer, wine, and spirits and may be a convenient stop for cycling tourists passing through on routes connecting the ferry terminal at Swartz Bay with the broader peninsula. No cycling-specific amenity information is currently verifiable.

grocery.name: Laughing Llama II
grocery.desc: Laughing Llama II is a convenience store sitting directly on the Trans-Canada Highway in the Cowichan Valley, a well-travelled touring corridor on Vancouver Island. The 'II' in the name suggests it is a second location of a local independent brand. Cyclists riding the Island Highway between Victoria and Nanaimo pass this stretch and would find it a potential roadside resupply point.

grocery.name: Hope River General Store
grocery.desc: Hope River General Store is a family-owned roadside institution established in 2001 along the Trans-Canada Highway in the Fraser Canyon, attached to Emory Bar RV Park. It combines a general store, in-house bakery and deli, licensed restaurant, gift shop featuring First Nations arts and crafts, and an ESSO Gas Bar — making it a notable all-in-one stop in an otherwise rural stretch of highway. The store is particularly well known for its smoked sockeye salmon, Indian candy, and complimentary salmon BBQ on July 1st.

notes.Hot food: In-Store Bakery & Deli; restaurant serving daily specials, real milkshakes, and smoked salmon sandwiches; fully licensed with a kid's menu

grocery.name: LIQUORFORLESS.com
grocery.desc: Liquor For Less is a Fraser Valley independent liquor retail chain operating six locations in Abbotsford and Langley, positioning itself as a lower-cost alternative to government liquor stores with a large selection of beer, wine, and spirits. The 5 Corners branch sits near Jubilee Park in Abbotsford and carries a broad inventory including local craft options. Touring cyclists looking to resupply with beverages would find a wide selection available here.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercenter (Store 5853) in Surrey South is a large-format retail store offering groceries alongside electronics, clothing, toys, furniture, and more. As a supercenter format, it is a practical one-stop resupply point for touring cyclists needing to restock food, household supplies, or gear. The store is wheelchair accessible and includes public washrooms.

grocery.name: 24 Seven
grocery.desc: 24 Seven is a convenience store in Penticton, BC, tagged in OpenStreetMap as a shop=convenience. The Facebook URL slug '24sevenpetro' suggests a possible affiliation with a Petro-Canada fuel station, which would make it a combined fuel-and-convenience stop — a common and practical waypoint for touring cyclists moving through the Okanagan.

grocery.name: Joyce Way Market
grocery.desc: Joyce Way Market is a family-run convenience store that has been serving the Joyce-Collingwood neighbourhood of Vancouver for over 10 years. It stocks drinks, ice cream (Ben & Jerry's and Häagen-Dazs), snacks, and grocery staples like eggs, milk, and bread, plus lottery tickets and cigarettes. The store also offers in-store computer services including black-and-white printing, scanning, and computer use.

grocery.name: PriceSmart Foods
grocery.desc: PriceSmart Foods is a British Columbia supermarket chain known for competitive pricing and a broad multicultural product selection, reflected in its Chinese-language name (佳廉超市). This Burnaby location sits along Kingsway, a major arterial corridor with established cycling infrastructure. Touring cyclists will find a full-service grocery stop with fresh produce, bakery, and deli/ready-made meal options.

grocery.name: Gage Mini Mart
grocery.desc: Gage Market is a self-checkout convenience market inside the Walter Gage Residence complex on the UBC Vancouver campus, open to the general public. It carries sandwiches, sushi, snacks, beverages, and personal sundries. Entry is via a credit or debit card swipe to open a secure gate, with items automatically tallied upon exit — cash is not accepted.

grocery.name: H Mart
grocery.desc: H Mart is a major Asian supermarket chain with this location in Surrey. As a supermarket, it serves as a reliable resupply point for groceries and basic necessities on cycling routes in the region.

grocery.name: The Shepherd's Inn - Convenience Store
grocery.desc: The Shepherd's Inn is a family-owned roadside complex positioned at Mile 72 of the Alaska Highway, 42 km northwest of Fort St John — a remote stretch where services are scarce. The property combines a motel, sit-down restaurant, convenience store, and gas/diesel fueling station, billing itself as 'an oasis on the Alaska Highway.' For touring cyclists riding the Alaska Highway corridor, it is one of the few full-service stops between Fort St John and Fort Nelson.

detail.address: 11890 Shepherds Inn Frontage Road, Charlie Lake, V1J 8L5

notes.Hot food: Full restaurant on site: 'Home cooked meals, breakfast all day, homemade breads, baked goods and soups made from scratch.' To-go orders also available

grocery.name: Lord Aberdeen Market
grocery.desc: A convenience store in Vernon serving everyday shopping needs. Stocked with basic groceries and general merchandise for quick stops.

grocery.name: Grand Marpole Market
grocery.desc: Grand Marpole Market is a small Asian grocery store in Vancouver's Marpole neighbourhood, stocking daily fresh fruits and vegetables, a butcher counter with a good meat selection, and a wide range of rice, noodles, and Asian dried goods. It sits on Granville Street directly across from a Safeway, making it a practical resupply point for cyclists passing through south Vancouver.

grocery.name: Gospa's Delightful Food
grocery.desc: Gospa's Delightful Food is a supermarket in Vancouver offering basic groceries. Website information was unavailable to assess additional amenities or services of interest to cycling tourists.

grocery.name: Denman Island General Store
grocery.desc: A convenience store serving the Denman Island community and visiting cyclists. Located on Northwest Road, it provides basic groceries and essential supplies to residents and island visitors.

grocery.name: Deroche General Store & Liquor
grocery.desc: Deroche appears to be a small retail store located along the Lougheed Highway in the rural community of Deroche, BC. The OSM record tags it as an alcohol shop, though the Facebook page slug ('DerocheGeneralStore') hints at a broader general store offering. This stretch of the Lougheed Highway through the Fraser Valley is a popular cycling corridor with limited services, making any local stop potentially valuable to touring cyclists.

grocery.name: Pomme Natural Market
grocery.desc: Pomme Natural Market is a 100% BC-owned natural grocery chain with its original and largest location in Port Coquitlam, repeatedly voted #1 grocery, health/organic food, and vitamin store in the Tri-Cities A-List. The store stocks certified organic and local spray-free produce, all-natural groceries, vitamins and supplements, eco-friendly home goods, and a deli offering fresh ready-to-eat meals and snacks. It is a strong resupply option for touring cyclists riding the Lougheed Highway corridor.

detail.address: #9-2755 Lougheed Highway, Port Coquitlam, BC V3B 5Y9

grocery.name: Olivia's Oils & Vinegars
grocery.desc: Olivia's Oils & Vinegars is a specialty boutique inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre — Kelowna's largest mall — devoted entirely to artisan extra virgin olive oils and balsamic vinegars sourced from around the world. Every product is available for tasting before purchase, with bottles filled and sealed in-store. The brand has a second Kelowna location at Guisachan Village Centre.

grocery.name: Persia Foods
grocery.desc: Persia Foods is a family-owned grocery chain that has served the Lower Mainland since 1996, positioning itself as Vancouver's most affordable source for fresh, healthy, and ethnically diverse foods. With multiple locations across Metro Vancouver including two in North Vancouver, it offers touring cyclists a culturally rich resupply option with a wide variety of international and everyday grocery staples. The chain is locally rooted and welcomes both local and global producers, giving it a broad and varied product selection.

grocery.name: Esso
grocery.desc: An Esso gas station and convenience store on North Road in Burnaby, operating under the Smart Stop banner. The site includes a car wash and an air tower, making it a handy roadside stop for cyclists needing a tire top-up or snacks. An ATM is also on site.

notes.Pump: Website lists 'Air Tower / Air' as a top station feature — standard forecourt air compressor usable for bicycle tires

grocery.name: Nesters Market
grocery.desc: Nesters Market is a full-service neighbourhood supermarket in Osoyoos, part of a BC-born chain founded in Whistler in 1987 and now operated by the Pattison Food Group. The store emphasizes fresh, local, natural, and organic products alongside a deli and bistro, in-store bakery, and pharmacy. For touring cyclists in the South Okanagan, it offers one of the most comprehensive resupply stops in the region.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Deli & Bistro' as an in-store service, indicating hot and prepared food availability

grocery.name: Angry Otter Liquor @ Clearbrook
grocery.desc: Angry Otter Liquor is a retail liquor store operated by Otter Co-op, a locally-owned co-operative with locations across the Fraser Valley and beyond. The Clearbrook branch is one of several Angry Otter stores serving the Abbotsford region. Touring cyclists passing through the area could stop here to resupply on beverages.

grocery.name: Lucky's Exotic Bodega
grocery.desc: Lucky's Exotic Bodega is a specialty convenience store and bodega on Vancouver's East Side, stocking an eclectic mix of exotic snacks and beverages sourced from around the world alongside streetwear, sneakers, and smoke accessories. It has a strong local following amplified through Instagram (@Luckysbodega) and operates its own e-commerce platform with free local delivery. Touring cyclists passing through the area can resupply on chips, candy, energy drinks, water, and other packaged foods in an distinctly non-chain environment.

grocery.name: Vegas Convenience Store
grocery.desc: Vegas Convenience Store is a neighbourhood convenience shop located in Victoria, BC. For touring cyclists, it represents a potential quick resupply stop in the city. Very limited public information is available about its specific offerings or facilities.

grocery.name: Mile One Eating House
grocery.desc: Mile One Eating House is a Pemberton institution founded in 2011, serving regionally inspired British Columbian comfort food — think natural beef burgers, slow-roasted brisket, and mac 'n' cheese made with local ingredients. Positioned at the gateway to Pemberton's wild spaces, it bills itself as 'the beginning, end, or middle of one's journey,' making it a natural refuel stop for cyclists on the Whistler–Pemberton corridor. In 2022 it joined the Whistler Cooks group of companies and operates several sub-brands including a coffee bar and a take-home fridge concept.

notes.Hot food: Website confirms 'Open daily for Breakfast, Lunch & Dinner'; menu includes natural beef burgers, mac 'n' cheese, slow roasted brisket and pork belly sandwiches, and Chicken Parm

grocery.name: Quality Greens
grocery.desc: Quality Greens is a locally focused farm market that has been supporting Okanagan growers and suppliers for over 25 years, offering fresh produce, a gourmet deli with grab-and-go options, dairy, bakery, and a full grocery department. The store operates under a 'Down to Earth' environmental philosophy, using compostable packaging, accepting reusable bags, and carrying Fair Trade, organic, and Non-GMO products. For a touring cyclist resupplying in Penticton, it offers a broad range of fresh and prepared foods in a single stop.

grocery.name: Stag's Head Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Stag's Head Liquor Store is a retail bottle shop situated inside City View Centre along the Princeton-Kamloops Highway on the eastern edge of Kamloops. It carries a broad selection of beer, wine, spirits, coolers, ciders, and snacks, including specialty items available on request. Delivery is offered through Skip the Dishes for those staying nearby.

grocery.name: Beauty For Ashes
grocery.desc: Beauty For Ashes is a specialty African grocery and beauty products store carrying authentic West and Central African staples — including gari, palm oil, dried fish, pap varieties, plantain chips, and fresh vegetables — that are difficult to find elsewhere in the Lower Mainland. The Burnaby location is one of two stores (the other in Surrey), and the business also offers online ordering with delivery via Genie Delivery and in-store pickup. A touring cyclist looking for an unusual resupply stop would find a broad range of packaged and fresh African food products here.

grocery.name: Mission Springs Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Mission Springs Liquor Store is part of the Springs Group chain, which operates over a dozen liquor retail locations alongside craft brew pubs and cannabis stores across the Lower Mainland and Vancouver Island. The group is connected to Mission Springs Brewing Company, meaning this location likely stocks locally brewed craft beer. For touring cyclists, it serves as a resupply point for beverages along a route through the Fraser Valley.

grocery.name: Aura Natural Market
grocery.desc: Aura Natural Market is a natural and organic health foods store in Langley, BC, stocking a broad range of fresh produce, meats, dairy, baked goods, and pantry staples alongside a deep selection of vitamins, supplements, and natural personal care products. The store also operates a juice and smoothie counter and offers on-site Registered Holistic Nutritionist (RHN) consultations, making it a more comprehensive wellness destination than a typical grocery stop. Touring cyclists will find it a solid resupply point for whole foods, snacks, and natural energy products.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercenter (Store 3199) is one of the largest retail destinations in Quesnel, offering a full grocery department alongside electronics, clothing, toys, furniture, and baby products under one roof. For a touring cyclist on Highway 97, it represents a reliable resupply point in a mid-sized northern BC city where options can be sparse between communities.

grocery.name: Alenka European Foods
grocery.desc: Alenka European Foods is a family-run specialty grocery store that has been serving Metro Vancouver since 2009, stocking a carefully curated selection of products from Russia, Ukraine, Georgia, Armenia, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, and other Eastern European countries. The store carries everything from deli meats and dairy to baked goods, frozen meals, preserved foods, and seafood — all from authentic Eastern European producers. It is a genuine neighbourhood grocery destination on Kingsway with an online store offering local pickup.

grocery.name: Super Kourosh
grocery.desc: Kourosh Foods Market is a Persian-focused supermarket in North Vancouver stocking fresh produce, meats, dairy, and a wide range of Middle Eastern and Iranian specialty products including traditional flat breads, Persian cookies, rose water, and pomegranate paste. The store also operates an online shop with delivery. Touring cyclists passing through North Vancouver would find it a useful resupply point for fresh fruit, snacks, and pantry staples.

detail.address: 1860 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2J9

grocery.name: Save-On-Foods
grocery.desc: Save-On-Foods is a supermarket in Sidney, BC, offering a range of groceries and supplies. As a full-service supermarket, it provides the typical selection of food and beverages useful for cycling trips. It serves as a resupply point for both local customers and passing travellers.

grocery.name: Organic Warehouse
grocery.desc: Organic Warehouse is a supermarket in Tsawwassen. While specific amenities could not be verified, it serves as a potential resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercenter (Store #1015) in Squamish serves as a one-stop shop for touring cyclists needing to restock on groceries, clothing, camping supplies, and general merchandise. As a large-format supercenter, it carries a broad range of food and household goods that make it a practical resupply stop on routes through the Sea-to-Sky corridor. The store is located in Squamish's commercial district off Discovery Way.

grocery.name: Lansdowne Central Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Lansdowne Central Liquor Store is a beverage and liquor retailer in Kamloops' Lansdowne Central shopping centre. It provides a convenient stop for cyclists and other travellers passing through the area. Located in a shopping centre, it offers proximity to other amenities.

grocery.name: Munchies N More
grocery.desc: Munchies N More is a convenience store on Smith Avenue in Vancouver offering snacks and basic supplies to customers. It provides a quick stop for supplies and refreshments.

grocery.name: Bear
grocery.desc: Bear (known on-site as Big Bear Gas Bar / Tuckkwiowhum Gas) is a convenience store and gas station operated by Boston Bar First Nation at the Tuckkwiowhum Village property in the heart of BC's Fraser Canyon, nestled where Anderson Creek meets the Fraser River. The store stocks road-trip staples — snacks, sandwiches, coffee, cool drinks — alongside camping essentials and locally made First Nations carvings, handicrafts, and indigenous products such as healing salves and huckleberry jam. It doubles as the gateway to the adjacent Tuckkwiowhum Heritage Village, making it a culturally distinctive resupply stop for cyclists riding Highway 1 through the canyon.

grocery.name: Fresh St. Market
grocery.desc: Fresh St. Market is a BC-based supermarket chain with a strong emphasis on fresh and locally sourced products. The West Vancouver location on Marine Drive is a full-service store spanning two floors with departments ranging from a full deli and prepared foods counter to fresh seafood, bakery, floral, and a broad international foods selection. For a touring cyclist on the Sea-to-Sky corridor or the North Shore, it represents a well-stocked resupply point with a wide variety of food options.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Ready to Eat Meals' and 'Deli & Prepared Foods' department including platters and fresh salads

grocery.name: Sunlight Market & Vape Shop
grocery.desc: A convenience shop in Tsawwassen offering vape products alongside standard convenience store items. Serves local travelers and cycling tourists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Oomomo Japan Living
grocery.desc: Oomomo Japan Living is a Japanese lifestyle variety store on Robson Street carrying a wide range of imported Japanese goods including health and beauty products, stationery, kitchenware, houseware, apparel, and collectibles. It also stocks a selection of Japanese food and drinks — snacks, candy, tea, coffee, and seasonings — making it a useful stop for specialty provisions. The store is wheelchair accessible according to OSM.

grocery.name: Island Meat and Deli
grocery.desc: Island Meat and Deli is a small grocery and deli shop on Gabriola Island, an accessible stop for touring cyclists seeking provisions. Established in 2016, it serves the local island community and travelers.

grocery.name: Sendex Latino Store
grocery.desc: Sendex Latino Store is a convenience shop in Vancouver offering basic groceries and retail items. The business provides a useful resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the neighborhood.

grocery.name: Country Grocer
grocery.desc: Country Grocer is a family-owned Vancouver Island grocery chain with deep roots in the Chemainus community, emphasizing locally-sourced BC products and supporting local events and initiatives. The Chemainus location offers a full-service supermarket experience including deli, sushi, bakery, seafood, and fresh floral departments. It is part of an eleven-store Island chain that has served the region since the mid-1980s.

grocery.name: Pepper's Foods
grocery.desc: Pepper's Foods is a 100% locally owned, full-service supermarket anchoring the Cadboro Bay Village neighbourhood of Victoria, with departments spanning bakery, deli, meat, seafood, produce, and floral. The store has a strong emphasis on Island-sourced products and has won Gold Medal recognition as Best Grocery Store in both BC and Canada two years running. The deli serves hot food daily including breakfast sandwiches, paninis, and BBQ chicken, making it a solid resupply stop for touring cyclists.

detail.address: 3829 Cadboro Bay Road, Victoria, BC V8N 4G1

notes.Hot food: Deli department serves breakfast sandwiches, fresh hot paninis, BBQ chickens and wings, and locally made sausage rolls

grocery.name: Boemma Euro Foods & Deli
grocery.desc: Boemma Euro Foods & Deli is a European specialty food shop and deli located on Burnaby's busy Kingsway corridor, stocking traditional imported European products alongside freshly made items from their in-house kitchen. The shop also offers catering services including charcuterie boards, meat platters, and custom orders. It's a distinctive provisioning stop for cyclists who appreciate specialty European ingredients and prepared deli goods.

grocery.name: Clayburn Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Clayburn Liquor Store is one of 13 Springs Group liquor store locations across British Columbia, carrying a staff-curated selection of craft beer, wine, and spirits. The store offers curbside pickup and delivery in addition to in-store shopping, and participates in the Springs Group VIP loyalty program redeemable across all chain locations. It is situated in Abbotsford in the Fraser Valley, a well-travelled cycling corridor.

detail.address: Unit 150, 3033 Immel Street, Abbotsford, BC V2S 4L3

grocery.name: Great Two Supermarket
grocery.desc: A supermarket on Kingsway in Vancouver serving the local community with groceries and supplies. Touring cyclists can stop here to restock provisions during their journey.

grocery.name: Great Canadian Liquor Warehouse
grocery.desc: Great Canadian Liquor Warehouse is an established Cranbrook liquor retailer operating since 2005, offering a wide selection of beer, wine, and spirits. The store takes pride in stocking local Kootenay craft breweries including Fisher Peak Brewing Company, Fernie Brewing Company, and Encore Brewing. For touring cyclists passing through Cranbrook, it is a convenient stop to pick up local craft beers and other refreshments.

detail.address: 2100 E/F Willowbrook Drive, Cranbrook, BC V1C 7H2

grocery.name: Osoyoos Produce
grocery.desc: Osoyoos Produce is a Vancouver neighbourhood Chinese grocery store with over two decades of service, specializing in authentic ingredients including fresh daily vegetables, live seafood, hand-pulled noodles, fermented sauces, and traditional teas. Located on Victoria Drive in East Vancouver, it serves the local Chinese community with a curated selection of specialty and everyday pantry items. A touring cyclist passing through the area would find a wide range of fresh produce and packaged goods for resupply.

grocery.name: Vandula Farms
grocery.desc: Vandula Farms is a Canadian-owned plant nursery and farm market located in Tsawwassen, BC, offering a range of indoor and outdoor plants, kokedama, and plant care accessories alongside a farm market. The business operates both a physical retail location and an online shop. Cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen area may find it a useful stop for farm-fresh goods from the market side of the operation.

grocery.name: Big Box Outlet Store
grocery.desc: Big Box Outlet Store is a Canadian family-owned value retail chain operating since 1985, specializing in heavily discounted brand-name merchandise sourced through reverse logistics and open-box channels. The Murrayville location on Fraser Highway is one of 21 stores across BC and Alberta, offering inspected and re-certified items at up to 70% off retail. It is a large general merchandise outlet — useful for a touring cyclist stocking up on sundries or electronics, though it is not primarily a food retailer.

grocery.name: Doncaster Grocery
grocery.desc: Doncaster Grocery is a convenience shop in Victoria. Limited amenity information is available due to website access issues. As a neighborhood convenience store, it provides a nearby supply point for cycling travelers in the area.

detail.address: 3490 Cedar Hill Rd, Victoria, BC V8P 1T5, Canada

grocery.name: Spirits of Mt Seymour
grocery.desc: Spirits of Mt Seymour is a liquor retailer located in Parkgate Village at the base of Mt Seymour, stocking over 400 local and global craft beers, BC VQA and imported wines, single malt scotches, and a broad range of spirits. The shop also runs a delivery service covering the North Shore, Downtown Vancouver, and Burnaby. For a cyclist finishing a ride on the Mt Seymour trails or road, it is a convenient stop to grab a cold local craft beer or a bottle of BC wine.

detail.address: 120-1133 Mt Seymour Rd, North Vancouver, BC V7H 2Y4

grocery.name: Save-On-Foods
grocery.desc: Save-On-Foods is a Canadian supermarket chain offering standard groceries. The location is wheelchair accessible and provides basic resupply services for touring cyclists. It's a practical food stop for cyclists traveling through Vancouver.

grocery.name: Santa Barbara Market
grocery.desc: Santa Barbara Market is a long-established Italian and Mediterranean grocery market on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, operating continuously since 1981. The shop offers a curated selection of imported Italian goods alongside fresh produce, deli meats, artisan cheeses, pasta, olive oils, and sauces. Commercial Drive is one of Vancouver's main cycling corridors, making this a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the city.

grocery.name: On the Run
grocery.desc: On the Run is a 24-hour convenience store chain location in Richmond, BC, situated along Number 3 Road. It offers convenience store goods, a restaurant, and washrooms, making it a practical stop for cyclists needing supplies at any hour. The brand also supports EV charging at select locations, suggesting some infrastructure for modern mobility.

detail.address: 6386 No. 3 Road Unit 170, Richmond, BC V6Y 2B3

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Restaurant' under Services & Amenities

grocery.name: The Corner Store Grocery and Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Corner Store Grocery and Liquor Store is a convenience and liquor store located on Georgeson Bay Road on Galiano Island, BC. For touring cyclists making their way through the Southern Gulf Islands, it serves as a key provisioning stop for groceries and alcohol in a community with limited retail options. The store's combination of grocery and liquor retail under one roof makes it a practical resupply point on this quiet island.

grocery.name: The Landing Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Landing Liquor Store is an alcohol retail shop mapped at 5449 Ladner Trunk Road in Tsawwassen. No website content could be matched to this specific location, so its current offerings and amenities for touring cyclists are unconfirmed.

grocery.name: Valleycliffe General Store
grocery.desc: Valleycliffe General Store is a neighbourhood convenience store serving the Valleycliffe area of Squamish, a gateway community to world-class mountain biking and road cycling. As a general store in a residential district, it offers a local alternative to the larger grocery chains in central Squamish. Cyclists passing through or based in the area would find it a convenient stop for resupply.

grocery.name: Metro Liquor
grocery.desc: Metro Liquor Tsawwassen is a private specialty liquor store voted South Delta's #1, located in the Tsawwassen Mills area. The store is stocked by specialist buyers focused on hard-to-find products, local craft beer and cider, and organic and biodynamic wines, with a rotating selection of limited releases. A liquor concierge service is also available for event planning and Special Event Permits.

grocery.name: FraserCart
grocery.desc: FraserCart is a supermarket in Kamloops serving both local shoppers and passing cyclists with groceries and supplies.

grocery.name: Fairway Market Shelbourne Plaza
grocery.desc: Fairway Market Shelbourne Plaza is part of a Vancouver Island–owned grocery chain operating since 1963, now with nine locations across the island. This full-service supermarket stocks produce, meat, dairy, bakery goods, and an international food selection, plus in-store Asian Kitchen and Sushi Village prepared-food counters. It is a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists moving through Victoria's Saanich area.

notes.Hot food: Website lists Asian Kitchen and Sushi Village as in-store departments, indicating prepared/hot food availability

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A government-operated BCLIQUOR retail store on Robson Street in Vancouver's West End, one of 198 provincial locations selling wine, spirits, beer, coolers, and ciders. The Robson Street location is situated in a high-traffic tourist and residential corridor. Knowledgeable product consultants are available in-store for beverage recommendations.

grocery.name: Happy Veggie World
grocery.desc: Happy Veggie World (operating as Global Vegetarian Foods Corp) is a Richmond-based plant-based meat alternatives brand that has been crafting vegan faux-meat products for over 25 years, including heat-and-serve meals and drumstick and bacon analogues. The company sells directly to food-service partners and through its own retail store. Touring cyclists with vegan or vegetarian diets may find specialty plant-based proteins here, though this is not a full-range grocery outlet.

grocery.name: Templeton Market
grocery.desc: Templeton Market is a neighborhood convenience store serving Vancouver's East side. It provides everyday groceries and supplies for residents and passing travelers.

grocery.name: Nester's Market
grocery.desc: Nesters Market is a full-service neighbourhood grocery store near the Kelowna Airport area, part of the BC-founded Pattison Food Group chain that originated in Whistler in 1987. The store stocks a broad range of fresh, local, organic, and specialty products alongside in-house departments including a deli and bistro, bakery, pharmacy, and health and wellness section. Touring cyclists will find it a well-stocked resupply point with prepared foods, grab-and-go entrees, and a comprehensive grocery selection.

notes.Hot food: Deli & Bistro page states 'select an item from our daily hot menu or take home an in house prepared Grab and Go entrée.'

grocery.name: Bosa Foods
grocery.desc: Bosa Foods is a Vancouver institution with over 60 years of experience importing and distributing specialty Italian and Mediterranean foods, carrying more than 7,000 SKUs across categories like olive oils, cured meats, cheeses, pastas, olives, and preserved vegetables. The Victoria Drive retail location is one of two Vancouver stores and stocks hard-to-find imported ingredients alongside a full deli. An in-store café serves homemade panini and espresso, offering a satisfying resupply stop for cyclists exploring East Vancouver.

notes.Hot food: Website states 'have a delicious homemade panini and espresso in our cafe' — café on premises serving prepared food

grocery.name: BCLIQUOR Ganges
grocery.desc: This BC Liquor Store (store #204) is a provincial government-operated retail outlet in Ganges, the main commercial hub of Salt Spring Island. It stocks wine, beer, spirits, coolers, and ciders, making it a practical stop for cycle tourists looking to pick up local BC craft beer or island-area wines. The store also accepts empty container returns for recycling.

grocery.name: Omnitsky Delicatessen
grocery.desc: Omnitsky Kosher is one of Vancouver's only full-service kosher delicatessens, founded in Winnipeg in 1910 and operating in Vancouver since 1997. The deli handcrafts over 150 products — corned beef, pastrami, smoked meats, gluten-free hot dogs — using traditional recipes with no MSG or by-products. The 3435 Fraser Street location, opened May 2025, combines a retail deli store with a sit-down restaurant serving soups, deli sandwiches, burgers, and hot entrées.

notes.Hot food: On-site kosher deli restaurant serves soups from scratch, deli sandwiches (5 oz and 8 oz), hot dogs, burgers, chicken wings, open-face roast beef with gravy and fries, and breakfast items

grocery.name: Bird Cages Confectionery
grocery.desc: Bird Cages Confectionery is a convenience and confectionery shop on Victoria's main tourist thoroughfare, Government Street, steps from the Inner Harbour. The name likely nods to the historic 'Bird Cages' — the nickname given to BC's original colonial government buildings. Its location on one of Victoria's busiest streets makes it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the city core.

grocery.name: The British Store
grocery.desc: Family-run specialty British grocery store founded by London-born Andy Bradshaw, claiming to be the largest British grocery store in North America with over 1,400 imported products. Located in Surrey since 2014, it stocks a wide range of imported British food cupboard staples, drinks, sweets, chocolate, crisps, and in-store-only chilled and frozen goods. It also operates as the exclusive wholesaler for GB Foods, a producer of traditional British-style meat products made on-site.

grocery.name: 7-Eleven
grocery.desc: 7-Eleven is a convenience store chain offering quick access to snacks, beverages, and basic packaged goods. The store includes an ATM and represents a reliable pit stop for touring cyclists needing immediate supplies.

grocery.name: Mediterranean Specialty Foods
grocery.desc: Mediterranean Specialty Foods is a specialty grocery on Vancouver's Commercial Drive carrying a wide range of Mediterranean products including authentic olives from Italy, Greece, Turkey, Lebanon, and Spain, and cheeses from Northern Macedonia, Greece, Turkey, and the Balkans. The store is known for daily fresh-baked pies, hand-crafted baklava, and borek, alongside an extensive selection of dry goods, frozen items, and dairy. Commercial Drive is a well-established cycling corridor in Vancouver, making this a natural resupply stop for touring cyclists seeking specialty provisions.

grocery.name: Big Box Outlet Store
grocery.desc: Big Box Outlet Store is a Canadian family-owned discount outlet chain (operating since 1985) selling open-box and re-certified furniture, appliances, electronics, clothing, outdoor gear, and everyday groceries at up to 70% off retail. The Chilliwack location on Vedder Road is one of three Fraser Valley stores in a network of 20 across BC and Alberta. Touring cyclists could find a broad mix of supplies here, including groceries and occasional outdoor or hardware items.

grocery.name: Dollar Max
grocery.desc: Dollar Max is a discount variety retail store located in Richmond, BC, tagged in OpenStreetMap as a department store. Shops of this type typically stock a mix of household goods, seasonal items, and basic packaged foods at low price points. It could serve as a convenient supply stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Lions Bay Liquor
grocery.desc: The Lions Bay General Store & Café is a long-standing Sea to Sky Corridor institution combining a liquor store — stocked with craft beer, wine, and ciders with an emphasis on Howe Sound and local producers — with a general store carrying artisan breads, fine meats, cheeses, and local souvenirs. The attached café serves coffee and a seasonal breakfast and lunch menu, and the 'Howe Sound Patio & Beer Garden' features live music on Saturdays. Situated in the small village of Lions Bay between Vancouver and Squamish, it is a natural resupply stop for cyclists on the Sea to Sky route.

grocery.name: Co-op
grocery.desc: Slocan Valley Co-op is a locally-owned Federated Co-operatives affiliate serving Slocan Park and Castlegar, operating as both a grocery supermarket and a fuel/gas bar on Highway 6. As one of the few full-service stops in this rural stretch of the Kootenay region, it is a practical resupply point for cyclists travelling the Slocan Valley. The co-op model means it is community-owned and oriented toward serving local residents and travellers alike.

grocery.name: Mi Tierra Latina
grocery.desc: Mi Tierra Latina is a Latin American specialty grocery store offering a broad selection of imported pantry staples, beverages, spices, snacks, frozen foods, and personal care products sourced from countries across Latin America including Colombia, Mexico, Brazil, Peru, Argentina, and more. The store also runs an active e-commerce shop and caters to customers seeking authentic regional ingredients that are hard to find at mainstream supermarkets. A touring cyclist looking to resupply with shelf-stable, calorie-dense Latin American snacks and pantry items would find a distinctive selection here.

grocery.name: Bale Banh Mi Sandwiches
grocery.desc: Ba Le Deli & Bakery is a family-owned Vietnamese deli and bakery that has been crafting bánh mì sandwiches since 1987, with the Victoria outpost at 774 Fort Street. Baguettes are baked fresh in-house daily, and the menu extends beyond sandwiches to vermicelli bowls and Vietnamese appetizers. It is part of a small multi-location chain with roots in Vancouver, making it a reliable and affordable quick-stop for touring cyclists seeking a filling Vietnamese meal.

notes.Hot food: Menu includes vermicelli bowls (lemongrass chicken, beef, pork, tofu) and a Classic Vietnamese Fried Egg Sandwich — all cooked/warm dishes served on-site

grocery.name: Jack Lonsdale's Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Jack Lonsdale's is North Vancouver's original public house, established in 1988 and located on Lonsdale Avenue. It offers a full food menu — burgers, salads, and signature pizzas — alongside 24 craft beers on tap, 8 wines on tap, and an extensive cocktail list spanning prohibition-era classics to modern martinis. A liquor store operates alongside the pub, making it a convenient one-stop for cyclists wanting a meal and provisions.

detail.address: 127-1433 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2H9

grocery.name: Langley Farm Market
grocery.desc: Langley Farm Market is a Metro Vancouver grocery chain with over 25 years of history, built around fresh, locally sourced BC produce delivered directly from regional farms. The Pitt Meadows location is one of six across the region, stocking everything from Okanagan fruit and organic vegetables to fresh meat, seafood, deli cold cuts, and in-store baked goods. The market won the 2025 Vancouver Consumer Choice Award for Best Fruit & Vegetable Market, making it a well-regarded stop for cyclists seeking quality provisions.

grocery.name: The Cheese​ Man
grocery.desc: The Cheese Man is a specialty cheese retailer tucked behind Capilano Mall on the south side of West 3rd Street in North Vancouver — self-described as 'not easy to find but definitely worth the trip.' The shop carries a curated selection of cheeses and accepts cash only. It is a worthwhile provisions stop for touring cyclists seeking quality artisan food rather than a full grocery run.

detail.address: 991 West 3rd Street, North Vancouver, BC V7P 1E4

grocery.name: Fratelli Foods
grocery.desc: Fratelli's Foods is a convenience store located in Kamloops, BC, a major hub along cycling routes through the Thompson River valley. As a convenience-format grocer, it would likely carry snacks, beverages, and basic supplies useful to touring cyclists moving through the area. Its Facebook presence suggests it is an active local business, though detailed information about its offerings is not publicly available.

grocery.name: On The Rocks Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A liquor store in Fort St. John offering alcoholic beverages to the local community. A straightforward retail stop for touring cyclists stocking supplies.

grocery.name: Unsworth Market
grocery.desc: Unsworth Market is a convenience store situated in Chilliwack, BC. With the 'Market' name and a shop=convenience classification, it represents a neighbourhood resupply option for touring cyclists moving through the Fraser Valley corridor. Very little public detail is available about the store's specific layout or offerings.
