grocery.name: Emma Lea Farms
grocery.desc: Emma Lea Farms is a family-run farm market and U-pick operation on Westham Island, accessed via a century-old wooden bridge, with roots going back to 1885. The farm market carries BC-grown fruit, local vegetables, spot prawns, honey, jams, SPCA Certified beef, and frozen goods — all sourced from the farm or elsewhere in British Columbia. An on-site Ice Cream Shoppe serving cones, milkshakes, smoothies, coffee, tea, and fresh baked goods makes it a memorable rest stop for cyclists riding the Westham Island loop.

notes.Hot food: Ice Cream Shoppe offers tea, coffee, and fresh baked goods

grocery.name: Windermere Market
grocery.desc: Windermere Market is a neighbourhood convenience store in North Vancouver's Windermere Street area. For touring cyclists moving through the Lower Mainland, it offers a local stop for grab-and-go supplies in a residential pocket of the city.

grocery.name: The Old Farm Market
grocery.desc: The Old Farm Market is a locally beloved multi-location grocery chain, with the Oak Bay location on Cadboro Bay Road voted #1 Best Local Grocery Store and #1 Best Produce Store. Produce arrives daily from local and BC-grown sources, and the store also runs a full-serve deli offering pastries, pies, fresh salads, and heated samosas. Cyclists will find it a solid resupply point for fresh food, deli items, and made-to-order sandwiches.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Sandwiches Made Your Way' with unlimited veggies and free guac, plus 'Get your samosa heated up!' at the Oak Bay location

grocery.name: Squamish Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Squamish Liquor Store on Cleveland Avenue claims the largest selection of craft beer and gluten-free beer options in the Sea to Sky Corridor. The store carries BC boutique wines not available at government liquor stores, along with a broad range of artisan and organic beers, ciders, coolers, and spirits. Cyclists resupplying in Squamish can also order delivery through the Dine Easy app if heading back to accommodation.

grocery.name: Langley Farm Market
grocery.desc: Langley Farm Market is a Metro Vancouver grocery chain with seven locations, built around the concept of freshly picked local produce sourced directly from BC farms—including fruit from Okanagan growers and organic vegetables from Metro Vancouver. The Burnaby location on Kingsway offers a full-service market with produce, fresh meat, chilled seafood, deli, in-store bakery, dairy, and specialty grocery. The chain is the 2025 Vancouver Consumer Choice Award winner for Best Fruit & Vegetable Market.

grocery.name: On the Run
grocery.desc: On the Run is a 24-hour Chevron-affiliated convenience store on Alaska Road North in Fort Saint John, a key route for cyclists heading into or out of northeastern BC. The store offers convenience goods alongside fuel (94 octane and diesel), making it a practical resupply stop in a region where services can be sparse. It accepts cash, credit, debit, and contactless payment.

detail.address: 10812 Alaska Road North, Fort Saint John, V1J 5T5

grocery.name: Save-On-Foods
grocery.desc: Save-On-Foods is a supermarket chain offering full-service grocery shopping. Touring cyclists can stop to resupply with food, drinks, and other provisions.

grocery.name: Ezymart
grocery.desc: EZYMart is a family-run convenience store in Vancouver with a multicultural product focus, stocking fresh produce, organic goods, snacks, drinks, and home and personal care items. Customer reviews praise its organized layout and friendly ownership. The brand appears to operate multiple Vancouver locations under a shared website.

grocery.name: Victoria Food & Florist
grocery.desc: Victoria Food & Florist is a long-standing neighbourhood shop on Cook Street that has operated as a flower establishment for over 30 years, recently renovated and revamped. Their seasonal floral arrangements are inspired by the natural beauty of BC's western coast, and the shop carries fresh-cut flowers, hanging baskets, and potted plants. It sits just minutes from the lively Cook Street Village, a well-known stop on Victoria's urban cycling network.

grocery.name: Krave Smoke Vape Shop & Convenience
grocery.desc: Krave Smoke Vape Shop & Convenience is a combined vape/smoke shop and convenience store located in North Vancouver. As a convenience store, it likely stocks snacks, drinks, and everyday essentials that a passing cyclist might need. The shop was verified open as recently as May 2025 via OSM check.

grocery.name: Your Independent Grocer
grocery.desc: Your Independent Grocer is a full-service Loblaws-operated supermarket in Vancouver's West End, situated on busy Davie Street near the English Bay waterfront. It carries a broad range of groceries, fresh produce, and household goods, making it a well-positioned resupply point for cyclists exploring the Seawall or passing through the city core. The store is wheelchair accessible and was recently field-verified as open.

grocery.name: Stong's Market
grocery.desc: Stong's Market is a locally owned independent grocery chain with a Squamish location stocking major brands alongside local, gourmet, and organic products across specialized departments including produce, bakery, seafood, and wellness. The chain has a strong sustainability focus, partnering with Ocean Wise for sustainable seafood and the Food Stash Foundation to reduce food waste. It is a Canadian Independent Grocer of the Year award recipient and offers online ordering with express delivery to the Squamish area.

grocery.name: Sabzi Mandi Supermarket
grocery.desc: Sabzi Mandi Supermarket is a 100% family-owned South Asian grocery chain with 15 locations across Canada, founded to serve BC's South Asian community with fresh produce, specialty groceries, and imported goods that were historically hard to find locally. The Nanaimo location offers cyclists access to a broad range of fresh fruits and vegetables, bulk staples, and specialty ingredients from around the world. The chain also carries household items and cooking appliances, making it a genuinely comprehensive resupply stop.

grocery.name: Mecca Halal Meats & Grocery
grocery.desc: Mecca Halal Meats & Grocery is a halal-certified meat and grocery shop on King George Boulevard serving the South Surrey/Delta area. It offers a specialty selection of halal meats alongside general grocery staples, making it a useful resupply stop for cyclists seeking halal options. The shop was recently verified in OSM as of late May 2026.

grocery.name: Lil'wat Gas
grocery.desc: A convenience store and fuel station in Mount Currie serving the local Lil'wat First Nation community. As a fuel and supply stop, it offers a basic resupply opportunity for touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Blundell Market
grocery.desc: Blundell Market is a supermarket located in Richmond, BC on Number 3 Road, serving the surrounding residential community. It accepts both cash and credit cards, making it accessible to cyclists who may carry either form of payment. A touring cyclist passing through Richmond's cycling network would find it a convenient provisioning stop.

grocery.name: Liquor Warehouse 110
grocery.desc: Liquor Warehouse 110 is a retail liquor store located in Fort St. John, BC, stocking beer, wine, spirits, coolers, and ciders. Fort St. John sits on the Alaska Highway and serves as a major resupply hub for cyclists touring northern BC. A stop here offers touring cyclists the opportunity to restock beverages for remote stretches of the Peace Region.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Ambleside BC Liquor Store on Marine Drive is one of 198 government-operated BCLIQUOR retail locations across British Columbia, stocking wine, spirits, beer, ciders, coolers, and non-alcoholic products. It sits on a key North Shore cycling corridor, making it a convenient resupply stop for touring cyclists. OSM tagging records wheelchair accessibility for this two-storey commercial building.

detail.address: 1434 Marine Drive, North Vancouver, BC V7T 1B7

grocery.name: Whole Foods Market
grocery.desc: Whole Foods Market is a large natural and organic supermarket chain location in Victoria, BC, stocking a wide range of organic produce, sustainable seafood, and specialty grocery items. The store includes several in-house eateries — a pizza counter, a Mexican burrito bar (Market Cocina), and a sushi counter (Kikka Sushi) — making it a convenient stop for a full meal as well as resupply. Amazon Prime members receive exclusive in-store discounts, which may be useful for longer touring cyclists looking to stock up.

notes.Hot food: Website lists three in-store eateries: Victoria Pizza (signature and custom pizzas, vegan/vegetarian options), Market Cocina (burrito bar), and Kikka Sushi (fresh-rolled sushi)

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercentre is a large-format big-box store in Nelson, BC, offering a full grocery section alongside electronics, clothing, furniture, and baby products. For a touring cyclist passing through Nelson, it represents one of the most comprehensive resupply points in the region, with a broad product range under one roof. Nelson is a relatively remote Interior BC town, making this Supercentre an important provisioning stop on longer routes through the Kootenays.

grocery.name: Artisan Sake Maker
grocery.desc: Artisan SakeMaker is Canada's original sake winery, operating for two decades on Granville Island and crafting sake from Canadian ingredients shaped by Japanese tradition. Their Sake & Tapas Central tasting room offers OSAKE flights, sake cocktails, and small plates in a relaxed setting steps from the brewing room. The adjoining retail shop carries handcrafted sake, sake kasu products, koji condiments, amazake, Japanese glassware, and gifts — making it a distinctive and unhurried stop on the Granville Island cycling route.

grocery.name: JJ Sri Lankan Store
grocery.desc: A Sri Lankan specialty supermarket in Vancouver. Serves the local South Asian community and passing cyclists with grocery provisioning, though specific amenities cannot be verified from available sources.

grocery.name: Active Pass Auto/Marine
grocery.desc: Active Pass Auto/Marine appears to be an automotive and marine supply business located in Sidney, BC, near the Saanich Peninsula ferries and recreational boating areas. Its OSM tagging as a convenience shop may reflect incidental retail stock, but the business's primary orientation is unclear without accessible website content. Touring cyclists in the area should verify whether it carries supplies relevant to their needs before relying on it as a stop.

detail.address: 424 Fernhill Rd, Mayne Island, BC V0N 2J2

grocery.name: Express News Convenience
grocery.desc: Express News Convenience is a neighborhood convenience store on Fraser Street in Vancouver. Like many small convenience shops, it offers refreshments and basic supplies for local residents and passing cyclists.

grocery.name: Southpoint Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Southpoint Liquor Store is a neighbourhood alcohol retail shop in Surrey, BC. Touring cyclists passing through the South Surrey area may find it a convenient stop for beverages. No additional business details could be confirmed from the available sources.

grocery.name: Mountain View Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Mountain View Liquor Store is an independent off-sales retailer on Fraser Street in Vancouver carrying over 1,000 products spanning wine, craft beer, spirits, coolers, cider, and a small selection of non-alcoholic soft drinks. The shop operates an online catalogue through SwypePOS, suggesting a modern, well-organised inventory. It sits in the Mount Pleasant–Fraserhood corridor, a neighbourhood increasingly popular with cyclists commuting and touring through south Vancouver.

grocery.name: Gardenia Foods
grocery.desc: Gardenia Foods is an organic greengrocer in North Vancouver. Touring cyclists can stop to restock fresh produce and vegetables.

grocery.name: Full-Fill Zero Waste Market
grocery.desc: Fullfill Zero Waste Market is Kimberley's dedicated zero-waste and bulk-goods shop, stocking package-free pantry staples, spices, supplements, and a range of reusable everyday items including water bottles and coffee cups. The store also carries solid shampoo, conditioner, and body bars — useful for cycle tourers looking to lighten their load with compact, plastic-free personal care. It is one of the few businesses of its kind in the East Kootenay region and offers both in-store and online shopping.

grocery.name: Best Buy Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Best Buy Liquor Store is part of the Riverside Inn complex on the Cowichan River in Lake Cowichan, and claims the largest selection of beer, wine, ciders, coolers, and spirits in town alongside a full wall of grab-and-go chilled product. The store also stocks tobacco, mix drinks, snacks, and bagged ice, making it a practical resupply stop for self-catering touring cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley. It shares a riverside property with a boutique hotel and a breakfast-and-lunch cafe.

detail.address: 56 North Shore Road, Lake Cowichan, BC V0R 2G0

grocery.name: Langley Farm Market
grocery.desc: Langley Farm Market is a Metro Vancouver chain specializing in freshly picked local produce, working directly with BC farms to stock everything from Okanagan fruit to organic Metro Vancouver vegetables. The Richmond location sits inside Lansdowne Centre and also carries natural and organic groceries, in-store baked goods, fresh meat, deli cold cuts, and chilled seafood. It won the 2025 Vancouver Consumer Choice Award for Best Fruit & Vegetable Market, making it a well-regarded stop for cyclists seeking quality fresh food.

detail.address: Unit 640, 5300 Number 3 Road, Richmond, BC V6X 2X9

grocery.name: Tasty Express
grocery.desc: A convenience store at an Esso service station. Unable to verify current amenities or operational status due to website unavailability.

grocery.name: Gah Lok Dim Sum
grocery.desc: Gah Lok Dim Sum is BC's first frozen dim sum manufacturer, operating since 1986 under its original name Happy Family Dim Sum. The company hand-wraps all its dumplings and produces a wide range of products including har gow, shu mai, wontons, and xiao long bao for restaurants, hotels, and catering companies. Retail customers can purchase directly at the Powell Street location or a newer Richmond store.

grocery.name: Your Independent Grocer
grocery.desc: Your Independent Grocer is a Canadian full-service supermarket chain operated by Loblaw Companies Limited, offering a broad range of grocery, fresh produce, household, and personal care products. This Vancouver location would serve touring cyclists as a resupply point for food and provisions. The chain's PC Express service also supports online ordering for pickup.

grocery.name: Broadway Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Broadway Liquor Store is a full-service private liquor store on Vancouver's West Broadway corridor stocking a broad range of beer, wines, and spirits, including rotating craft beer selections. The store caters to special occasions and offers delivery through Uber Eats and Skip the Dishes. For a touring cyclist, it represents a convenient urban stop for resupply of beverages along a major east-west cycling route.

detail.address: 1169 West Broadway, Vancouver, British Columbia V6H 1G1, Canada

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: Circle K is a 24/7 convenience store and petrol station chain with a location in Surrey's Guildford area. This location offers snacks, beverages, fresh food options, coffee, and a roller grill for hot food. Public restrooms are available on-site, and the round-the-clock hours make it a practical resupply stop for cyclists at any point in their ride.

notes.Hot food: Website services list explicitly includes 'Fresh Food Fast' and 'Roller Grill' at this location

grocery.name: Fraser Commons Liquor Co.
grocery.desc: A liquor retailer on Southeast Marine Drive in Vancouver. Serves as a waypoint for touring cyclists seeking beverages or retail goods.

grocery.name: Queensborough Landing Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Queensborough Landing Liquor Store is a privately operated liquor retailer in New Westminster offering a wide selection of beer, wine, and spirits. It participates in the More Rewards loyalty program and runs monthly in-store specials and giveaways. Cyclists can also order for delivery via Skip the Dishes or DoorDash rather than visiting in person.

detail.address: 805 Boyd St, New Westminster, BC V3M 5X2

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: One of 198 government-operated BCLIQUOR retail stores across British Columbia, this Commercial Drive location carries wine, spirits, beer, coolers, ciders, and non-alcoholic products. It sits on one of Vancouver's most bike-friendly streets and is operated by the BC Liquor Distribution Branch, a Crown corporation. Staff are described as knowledgeable product consultants who assist with food and beverage pairings.

grocery.name: Co-op
grocery.desc: Armstrong Regional Co-op operates a gas bar and convenience store at this Salmon Arm location, part of a community-owned cooperative with roots going back over 104 years and locations across the BC Interior. The co-op model means profits are returned to members and reinvested locally, and the convenience store carries quick-deal grocery items alongside fuel and propane. For a touring cyclist, it serves as a practical fuel-and-supplies stop on the northeast edge of Salmon Arm.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store (store #59) is a provincial government-run BCLIQUOR retail outlet in Sidney, BC, offering wine, spirits, beer, coolers, and ciders. The chain operates 198 stores across British Columbia and serves over 36 million customers annually. Cyclists passing through Sidney could stop here for beverage resupply, though the store does not appear to offer dedicated cyclist services.

grocery.name: City Avenue Market
grocery.desc: City Avenue Market is a family-owned grocery chain founded in Vancouver in 1986, now operating four locations across Greater Vancouver. The West Broadway store, opened in 2022, specializes in organic, local, and international produce alongside a broad pantry selection including bulk goods, dairy, meat, and fresh baked goods. Touring cyclists will find a well-rounded resupply stop with an emphasis on fresh fruits and vegetables, natural foods, and locally sourced products.

grocery.name: The Gull Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Gull Liquor Store bills itself as the largest private liquor store on the North Shore, stocking over 5,000 beer, wine, RTD, cider, and spirits options from local BC producers to international imports. Located in the Park and Tilford Mall on Brooksbank Avenue, it is locally owned and operated with knowledgeable staff and same-day delivery available. Friday and Saturday in-store tastings with winemakers, distillers, and brewers give it a community-focused character beyond a typical bottle shop.

detail.address: 900–333 Brooksbank Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7J 3S8

grocery.name: Country Grocer
grocery.desc: Country Grocer is a family-owned Vancouver Island supermarket chain founded in 1984, now operating eleven stores across Greater Victoria, the Gulf Islands, and Vancouver Island. This Nanaimo location (Chase River) is one of two Country Grocer stores in the city, offering a full supermarket with deli, bakery, seafood, and fresh floral departments. The chain has a strong emphasis on local BC suppliers and farmers and deep community roots spanning over four decades.

grocery.name: Canco
grocery.desc: Canco is an Esso-branded gas station and convenience store on Tranquille Road in Kamloops. For touring cyclists passing through the north end of Kamloops, it offers a roadside stop with convenience store supplies. The combination of fuel sales and a convenience shop is typical of this chain format.

grocery.name: Buy-Low Foods
grocery.desc: Buy-Low Foods is a full-service supermarket chain operated under the Pattison Food Group, with this location in Surrey's Whalley neighbourhood. It offers a broad range of groceries under both national brands and the chain's own Western Family and Only Goodness private labels. The store carries a loyalty rewards program (More Rewards) redeemable for groceries and other perks, making it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Jealous Fruits
grocery.desc: Jealous Fruits is a wholesale fruit and grocery business in Lake Country. Without access to its website, details about retail operations, customer access, and cycling amenities remain unverified.

grocery.name: Fresh St. Market
grocery.desc: Fresh St. Market is a BC-based grocery chain with a focus on fresh, local, and Canadian products. The Whistler location on Northlands Boulevard offers a full-service supermarket experience including a deli and prepared-foods counter, bakery, fresh produce, meat, and seafood departments. For touring cyclists resupplying in Whistler, it represents one of the more comprehensive grocery options in the area.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Deli & Prepared Foods', 'Ready to Eat Meals', and 'Platters' as dedicated departments

grocery.name: The Spot In Midway
grocery.desc: A convenience store and fuel station in Midway serving the local community and travelers. Provides basic supplies and fuel for those passing through the area.

grocery.name: H Mart
grocery.desc: H Mart is a Korean-founded pan-Asian supermarket chain with a Victoria location inside a Douglas Street shopping complex. The store stocks a broad range of Asian groceries, fresh produce, and specialty ingredients not commonly found in mainstream Canadian supermarkets. For a touring cyclist, it is a reliable stop for resupply with a notably diverse selection of shelf-stable and fresh foods.

grocery.name: Wisbey Veggies
grocery.desc: Wisbey Veggies is a beloved roadside farm stand with more than 35 years of history, located just outside the village of Yarrow between Abbotsford and Chilliwack on the Sumas Prairie. The Meredith family grows an extensive range of vegetables on-site and supplements with local fruit, artisan goods, and a u-pick flower field and pumpkin patch. A food truck and picnic tables make it a natural rest stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

notes.Basic groceries: Seasonal homegrown vegetables (beets, carrots, peppers, corn, squash, sweet potatoes, etc.), fresh fruit from local growers, and curated local and artisan-made goods available June through October
notes.Hot food: Website mentions 'a snack or meal from our NEW food truck' alongside picnic tables on site

grocery.name: Visitor Centre
grocery.desc: The Tofino Visitor Centre is the official tourism information office for the region, located on the Pacific Rim Highway near Cox Bay. It is operated by Tourism Tofino and serves as the primary resource for visitors seeking local trip planning, area maps, and guidance on activities throughout the Tofino area. For a touring cyclist arriving on the West Coast, this is a logical first stop for route information and local knowledge.

detail.address: 1119 Pacific Rim Hwy - Tin Wis Road, Tofino, V0R 3A0

grocery.name: Burnaby Heights Persian Market and Halal Meats
grocery.desc: A Persian specialty supermarket and halal meats shop in Burnaby. It serves the local community with ethnic groceries, halal products, and specialty items. A useful stop for cyclists needing to resupply groceries.

grocery.name: My Udder Store
grocery.desc: My Udder Store is listed as a corner store in Greenwood, BC — Canada's smallest city and a notable stop on Highway 3 cycling routes through the Boundary Country. The website linked in OSM belongs to Shoestring Importers, describing a broad general-merchandise shop selling unique gifts, antiques, crafts, collector plates, and hardware supplies with paint. Whether this reflects a trading name, a co-location, or a data discrepancy is unclear, but a real retail presence on South Copper Avenue appears to exist.

grocery.name: The White Rock Bread Box
grocery.desc: A greengrocer located in White Rock, providing fresh produce and grocery supplies to the local community. Touring cyclists can stop to purchase provisions along Johnston Road.

grocery.name: Lucifer's
grocery.desc: Lucifer's House of Heat is a Canadian specialty retailer focused entirely on hot sauces, hot peppers, and related condiments, stocking hundreds of products from Canadian and international producers including brands featured on the Hot Ones web series. The Vancouver location on Davie Street doubles as a restaurant, making it a destination for spice enthusiasts. A Richmond location also operates separately.

notes.Hot food: Contact page describes the Davie Street location as 'Vancouver Retail Store & Restaurant'; website navigation includes a dedicated 'Restaurant Menu' section

grocery.name: Millway Market
grocery.desc: Millway Market is a convenience store and fuel stop operating under the Wayne Procter Group's Gas N Go division on Vancouver Island. Part of a long-established, locally owned Island business group, it aims to provide one-stop shopping combining fuel with everyday grocery items. Touring cyclists on MacMillan Road in Nanaimo will find it a practical resupply point.

notes.Basic groceries: Gas N Go division description states locations offer 'not simply fuel but also groce[ries]'

grocery.name: City Avenue Market
grocery.desc: City Avenue Market is a family-owned grocery chain founded in Vancouver in 1986, with its New Westminster location established in 2010 on the scenic Quayside Drive waterfront along the Fraser River. It emphasizes fresh local and organic produce alongside a broad selection of groceries, bulk items, dairy, meat, baked goods, and a newly added deli offering freshly sliced meats and cheeses. The store is wheelchair accessible and also offers online ordering with Greater Vancouver delivery.

detail.address: Unit 130 - 810 Quayside Drive, New Westminster, BC V3M 6B9

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercentre is a large-format retail store in Kelowna offering a full grocery department alongside electronics, clothing, furniture, and baby goods under one roof. As one of the largest grocery destinations in the area, it is a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists needing food staples, packaged goods, or basic household supplies. The store operates under the Walmart Canada banner as store 3042.

grocery.name: Coal Harbour Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Coal Harbour Liquor Store is a licensed wine and spirits retailer (BC Liquor License 195427) in the Coal Harbour neighbourhood of downtown Vancouver. The shop operates both a walk-in retail location and a Shopify-based online delivery service, with a curated focus on wine. Touring cyclists passing through the area could stop to pick up beverages, though the business's public-facing identity centres strongly on home delivery.

detail.address: 1218 W Pender St., Vancouver, BC V6E 4N1

grocery.name: Juniper Market
grocery.desc: Juniper Market is a neighbourhood specialty grocery and convenience store that has served the Juniper Ridge community in southeast Kamloops since 2009. It stocks fresh produce, bakery items from Craig's Bakery, and a deli with daily-made "Grab & Go" sandwiches and salads alongside hot items like samosas and butter chicken from local partner Mystikk Flavors. For touring cyclists resupplying in Kamloops, it offers a genuine one-stop shop without needing to descend into the city centre.

notes.Hot food: Deli subpage describes hot case items including samosas, pakoras, butter chicken, and rice from in-store partner Mystikk Flavors

grocery.name: Port Moody Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Port Moody Liquor Store is part of the Neighbourhood Liquor chain and carries a broad, ever-changing selection of wine, beer, and spirits with a focus on niche and craft products. Staff offer knowledgeable recommendations and the store hosts weekly in-store tastings covering beer, wine, coolers, and spirits. A touring cyclist stopping in will find complementary cookies on weekends and dog treats on request.

detail.address: #4 – 2929 St John's Street, Port Moody, BC

grocery.name: Easy Click Wholesaler
grocery.desc: Easy Click Wholesaler is a Nanaimo-based B2B supplier of sustainable food service packaging, offering takeout containers, bags, foil trays, cutlery, and cups in bulk to restaurants, caterers, and food trucks across Canada. The business focuses on eco-conscious materials such as bagasse, recyclable aluminum, and kraft paper. A touring cyclist arriving here would find a packaging warehouse oriented entirely toward trade customers, with no food, groceries, or public-facing retail services.

grocery.name: Nesters Market
grocery.desc: Nesters Market SFU is a full-service neighbourhood grocery store located in the UniverCity community on Burnaby Mountain, adjacent to Simon Fraser University. Part of the BC-founded Nesters chain (established Whistler, 1987) and now operated by the Jim Pattison Group, this location offers fresh produce, natural and organic products, an in-store bakery, deli and bistro, and a pharmacy. It serves both campus residents and the surrounding hillside community, making it a useful resupply stop for cyclists on routes through the Burnaby Mountain area.

notes.Hot food: Deli & Bistro listed as an in-store service on the SFU store page

grocery.name: High Point
grocery.desc: High Point is a specialty beer, wine, and spirits shop on East Hastings Street carrying more than 400 craft beer and cider selections and over 350 wines scoring 90+ points. The store hosts regular in-store producer tastings and runs a loyalty program that credits repeat purchases. Cyclists can shop online for in-store pickup or use the back loading bay for larger case orders.

grocery.name: Select
grocery.desc: Select is Shell's convenience store brand operating at this 24-hour Shell service station on Kingsway in Burnaby. The station carries fuel, a convenience shop with food and drink options, and offers delivery partnerships with Uber Eats and Skip the Dishes. Its round-the-clock availability and location on a major east-west corridor make it a practical resupply point for cyclists moving through the Burnaby area.

notes.Camping fuel: Website amenities list includes 'BBQ Propane Cylinder Exchange'
notes.Pump: Website amenities list includes 'Air', indicating an on-site compressed air station for tire inflation

grocery.name: Snaw-Naw-As Store
grocery.desc: The Snaw-Naw-As Store is a convenience store located within the territory of the Snaw-naw-as (Nanoose) First Nation, a Coast Salish community at Nanoose Bay on southeastern Vancouver Island. The First Nation's traditional lands straddle the eastern coastline between Nanaimo and Parksville, a stretch frequently cycled by touring cyclists on the Island. This store serves the local First Nation community and may offer a useful stop for cyclists passing through this rural coastal corridor.

grocery.name: Legacy Liquor
grocery.desc: Legacy Liquor Store is Vancouver's largest privately-owned liquor store, founded in 2010 in the Olympic Village neighbourhood just off the southeast shore of False Creek near Science World. The store carries over 5,000 unique items — including hundreds of exclusives — spanning wine, spirits, beer, cider, sake, and non-alcoholic options from more than 70 countries, with staff that includes sommeliers, cicerones, and spirits specialists. A touring cyclist rolling through the False Creek Greenway corridor will find an exceptionally well-curated stop for BC craft beer, local spirits, and hard-to-find international selections, with online ordering and in-store pickup also available.

grocery.name: Fields
grocery.desc: Fields is a Canadian-owned department store chain that has served rural Western Canadian communities since 1948, making it a familiar landmark for highway travellers across the region. The Skidegate location on Haida Gwaii offers everyday items spanning basic groceries, clothing, footwear, and household goods — a rare all-in-one stop in a remote community. For cyclists riding through Haida Gwaii, it represents one of the more comprehensive resupply options along the route.

grocery.name: Sungiven Foods
grocery.desc: Sungiven Foods is a Vancouver-based Asian grocery chain with a strong focus on 'more natural, less processed, and fewer additives' products, championing local and organic sourcing. The West Broadway location carries a broad range including premium meats (Wagyu beef, Berkshire pork), fresh seafood, produce, dairy, and packaged goods. An in-house Sungiven Kitchen prepares ready-to-eat Asian dishes — a convenient option for cyclists wanting a quick, hot meal without cooking.

notes.Hot food: Website features a 'Ready to Eat' category and 'Sungiven Kitchen' section listing multiple prepared dishes including Sweet & Sour Pork, Korean Army Stew, and Teriyaki AAA Beef

grocery.name: Port Coquitlam Farmer's Market
grocery.desc: The Port Coquitlam Farmers Market is a seasonal outdoor market held at Leigh Square in the heart of downtown Port Coquitlam, operated by the Fraser North Farmers Market Society. It brings together local farmers, artisan food producers, and makers offering fresh produce, handcrafted goods, and small-scale food products. The market also features live music and community activities, making it a lively resupply stop for cyclists passing through the Tri-Cities area.

detail.address: 2253 Leigh Square Pl, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 3B8

grocery.name: Nesters Market
grocery.desc: Nesters Market is a full-service neighbourhood supermarket in Squamish, part of a BC-founded chain now operating 16+ locations across Western Canada under the Pattison Food Group. The Squamish location offers a broad range of groceries alongside in-store departments including a bakery, deli and bistro, pharmacy, and health and wellness section. For touring cyclists passing through Squamish, it represents a well-stocked resupply point with fresh produce, natural and organic products, and prepared food options.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Deli & Bistro' as an in-store service, indicating hot or prepared food is available

grocery.name: Parkcrest Neighbourhood Store
grocery.desc: Parkcrest Neighbourhood Store is a convenience store in the Parkcrest neighbourhood of Kamloops, BC. It serves as a local corner store for residents in the North Kamloops area, making it a potential resupply stop for cyclists passing through the region.

grocery.name: Gold Creek Market
grocery.desc: Gold Creek Market is a convenience store and fuel station located in Cranbrook, BC. As a combined gas station and convenience outlet, it would serve as a practical roadside stop for touring cyclists needing to top up supplies along their route. Its location in Cranbrook puts it within reach of the Crowsnest Pass and Rocky Mountain cycling corridors.

grocery.name: Organic Acres Market
grocery.desc: Organic Acres Market is a compact but fully stocked organic grocery store at the corner of Main Street and East 20th Avenue in Vancouver, part of the Be Fresh and SPUD.ca family of local food businesses. Despite its modest size, the store carries fresh organic produce, prepared to-go entrees and salads, and cold-pressed juices from The Juice Box. It is a convenient urban resupply stop for cyclists traveling the Main Street corridor.

grocery.name: Pinoy Dragon Mart
grocery.desc: Pinoy Dragon Mart is a Filipino-oriented convenience store in North Vancouver, offering a selection of Asian and everyday grocery items to the local community. Cyclists passing through the area may find it a useful stop for snacks and packaged goods. The store's niche product focus makes it a distinctive neighbourhood shop rather than a generic convenience stop.

grocery.name: Express News Convenience
grocery.desc: Express News Convenience is a convenience store in Vancouver serving the local McKay Avenue area. Convenient for quick refreshment stops and supplies during cycling trips through the neighborhood.

grocery.name: Sisto's River City Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Sistos River City Liquor Store is a retail liquor outlet in downtown Mission operated by Springs Group, a multi-location BC hospitality company that also runs brew pubs and restaurants across the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley. The store is staffed by a team that hand-picks its can and jar selection, and customers can earn VIP loyalty points redeemable at any Springs Group location. Curbside and delivery ordering are available through the Springs Group platform.

grocery.name: Whole Foods Market
grocery.desc: Whole Foods Market Cambie is a large natural and organic supermarket situated in Vancouver's South Cambie neighbourhood, part of a 500+ store global chain known for strict quality and sustainability standards. Beyond groceries, the store hosts a cluster of in-house eateries including a coffee bar, pizza counter, burrito bar, sandwich station, and cold-pressed juice bar. For a touring cyclist, it offers one of the more comprehensive resupply options in the city, with organic and specialty food alongside ready-made hot meals.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Hot & Salad Bar' under Store Amenities and multiple in-store eateries: Burrito Bar, Cambie Pizza, Cambie Coffee Bar, Cambie Sandwich, The Juice Truck, and Kikka Sushi

grocery.name: Lakeview Liquor
grocery.desc: A liquor store in West Kelowna offering beverages and supplies to residents and visitors. Serves as a convenient retail stop for touring cyclists seeking refreshments.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercenter is a large-format department and grocery store serving Vernon, BC. As a Supercenter, it carries a full grocery section alongside general merchandise including electronics, clothing, toys, and baby products. Touring cyclists will find it a convenient one-stop shop for resupply in the Vernon area.

grocery.name: Oyama General Store
grocery.desc: A family-run general store perched on the Oyama Isthmus directly on the Okanagan Rail Trail, between Wood Lake and Kalamalka Lake — widely described as the trail's natural midpoint rest stop for cyclists riding between Kelowna and Vernon. Beyond groceries, liquor, and Canada Post services, it operates a rental hub offering European-designed e-bikes, paddleboards, and kayaks. Established in 2003 and sole-proprietor owned since 2015, it is a genuine community anchor that serves both locals and trail visitors.

detail.address: Oyama Isthmus, Lake Country, BC (off Hwy 97 via Pelmewash Pkwy)

notes.Ice: Ice explicitly listed under store offerings: 'Canada Post · Hardware · Lotto · Ice' and 'Groceries, dairy, snacks, hardware, ice & more'

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: A large-format Walmart Supercentre located on Scott Road in Delta, offering a full grocery section alongside general merchandise including electronics, clothing, and baby products. As one of the largest retail stores in the area, it provides comprehensive resupply options for touring cyclists passing through the South Surrey/Delta corridor. The store was verified open as recently as May 2026.

grocery.name: Duncan Butcher Shop
grocery.desc: A butcher and deli shop on the Trans-Canada Highway in Duncan, offering provisions to cyclists and other travelers.

grocery.name: Thrifty Foods
grocery.desc: Thrifty Foods is a British Columbia-based supermarket chain with locations throughout the region. The Nanaimo location offers a convenient stop for cyclists to restock essential groceries and supplies.

grocery.name: Tommy's Market
grocery.desc: Tommy's Market is a greengrocer shop in North Vancouver offering fresh produce and basic provisions to the local community. As a small grocery retailer, it serves as a convenient resupply stop for touring cyclists in the area. Limited information is available regarding customer-facing amenities such as bike parking or water access.

grocery.name: The Blackfish Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Blackfish Liquor Store is the Sunshine Coast's largest private liquor store, situated in Gibsons and known for its extensive cold selection alongside hard-to-find exclusives and limited releases. The store actively supports local BC wineries, breweries, cideries, and distilleries. Staff 'Spirit Guides' are on hand to assist with selections, and customers can submit product requests via an in-store request book.

detail.address: 101-1100 Sunshine Coast Hwy, Gibsons, BC V0N1V7

grocery.name: Little Acre Fruitstand
grocery.desc: A fruit and vegetable stand in Naramata, situated in the Okanagan Valley wine region. Convenient stop for touring cyclists to purchase fresh local produce.

grocery.name: Choices Market
grocery.desc: Choices Market is a 100% BC-owned natural and organic grocery chain that has operated since 1990, billing itself as Western Canada's largest grocer of natural and organic foods. The Kerrisdale location carries a broad selection of local, organic, and specialty food items with a strong emphasis on Canadian-sourced products. Registered dietitians and holistic nutritionists are on staff and offer free personalized in-store nutrition tours.

grocery.name: Alchemist distiller
grocery.desc: Alchemist Distiller is an award-winning micro-distillery run by French couple Sandrine and Simon, who hand-craft distinctive spirits from Okanagan apples including gin, absinthe, vodka, and fruit liqueurs. Their Nectar apple liqueur won Canada's best fruit liqueur in 2023, and their range reflects a blend of French distilling tradition and local terroir. Cyclists can visit the Summerland tasting room for sales, tastings, and tours.

grocery.name: Best Buy Liquor
grocery.desc: Best Buy Liquor #2 is a liquor store on MacMillan Road in the Cedar area of Nanaimo, operated by the Vancouver Island–based Wayne Procter Group. It sits next to the Millway Gas N Go, forming a convenient one-stop cluster for provisions. Part of a multi-location Best Buy Liquor chain spanning Vancouver Island.

grocery.name: Greco's Specialty Foods Market
grocery.desc: Greco's Specialty Foods Market is a long-established gourmet provisions shop in Surrey, operating since 1984, specializing in Mediterranean and European specialty foods. The store carries an eclectic mix of imported cheeses, cured meats (guanciale, pancetta, pastirma), Greek yogurt, award-winning pizza shells, olive oils, and custom charcuterie boards. For a touring cyclist, it's a compelling stop for high-calorie, shelf-stable or refrigerated specialty provisions unavailable at typical grocery chains.

detail.address: 6886 King George Blvd, Surrey, BC V3W 4Z9

grocery.name: Peace Arch Duty Free
grocery.desc: Peace Arch Duty Free is a duty-free retail shop located at the Peace Arch border crossing between Canada and the United States. Situated in Surrey, it serves travelers passing through the international border. Specific offerings and cyclist-oriented amenities are unverified due to website access limitations.

grocery.name: Tama Supermarket
grocery.desc: Tama Supermarket is a family-owned neighbourhood grocery store founded in 2017, taking its name from the founders' surnames Tabon and Martinez. Specializing in Filipino and Asian groceries — stocking brands like Mama Sita's, Datu Puti, and Lucky Me! alongside fresh produce, frozen goods, and body care imports — it functions as a cultural food hub on the Kingsway corridor. Cyclists passing through can resupply with a wide range of pantry staples, fresh fruit and vegetables, snacks, and beverages.

grocery.name: Produce Gone Wild
grocery.desc: Produce Gone Wild is a fresh produce retailer with two Chilliwack-area locations built around direct relationships with Fraser Valley and Okanagan farmers who supply the stores seasonally. Their inventory runs from everyday staples to more exotic varieties, with an emphasis on local and regional sourcing. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a well-stocked selection of fresh fruit and vegetables, with curbside pickup and local delivery also on offer.

grocery.name: The Local
grocery.desc: Local is an indoor year-round food store in downtown Fernie operated by Wildsight Elk Valley, a not-for-profit conservation organization, and opened in December 2020. It functions like a permanent indoor farmers' market, connecting residents and visitors with small local farmers and food producers from across the Elk Valley. For touring cyclists, it offers a rare opportunity to resupply with locally sourced produce and food products in a community where nearly all groceries are otherwise imported.

notes.Basic groceries: Website describes a retail storefront selling local food and seasonal produce year-round: 'A spot to stock up on delicious seasonal produce' and 'local food, year-round in the heart of downtown Fernie.'

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store — branded BCLIQUOR — is one of 198 provincial government-operated retail outlets across British Columbia, offering an extensive selection of wine, spirits, beer, coolers, and ciders. The Fairfield Road location sits in one of Victoria's most cycle-friendly residential neighbourhoods, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists heading through the area. Staff are described as knowledgeable about product selection and pairings.

grocery.name: R & B
grocery.desc: R & B is an alcohol shop in Vancouver's East 4th Avenue neighborhood. It serves as a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking refreshments during their journey through the area.

grocery.name: Kuo Hua Trading Co
grocery.desc: Kuo Hua Trading Co is a Taiwanese specialty supermarket and food importer, originally founded in Toronto in 1995 and expanded to Richmond in 2010 as its Vancouver flagship store. It carries over 2,000 imported Taiwanese products — from fresh produce and packaged snacks to sauces, teas, and ceramics — and serves as the exclusive Canadian agent for several major Taiwanese food brands. Touring cyclists will find a well-stocked source of Asian specialty groceries, fresh fruit, and packaged energy snacks in the heart of Richmond.

detail.address: 4551 Number 3 Road, Unit 120, Richmond, BC V6X 2C3

grocery.name: St. Regis Fine Wines & Spirits
grocery.desc: St. Regis is mapped in OSM as a basement-level alcohol shop on Dunsmuir Street in downtown Vancouver. The associated website is non-functional, and the URL referencing a 'bar and grill' does not align with the OSM shop:alcohol tag, leaving the current nature of the business unclear. Insufficient evidence exists to characterize what a visiting cyclist would find here.

grocery.name: Asom Store
grocery.desc: Asom Store is a neighbourhood convenience store occupying a single-storey retail building on Oxford Street in North Vancouver, formerly operating as Oxmore Market. It serves the surrounding residential community with everyday essentials typical of a convenience shop. For touring cyclists moving through North Vancouver, it is a local stop for snacks and supplies.

grocery.name: Dip Co Delights
grocery.desc: DIP Co. Delights is a family-run gourmet sandwich shop in Deep Cove built around Focabari, the Daniali family's signature house-baked bread that fuses Italian focaccia with Persian barbari. Opened in 2022, the shop imports specialty cured meats, cheeses, and olive oils directly from Europe to craft bold European-Middle Eastern fusion sandwiches. Deep Cove is a popular cycling destination, making this a standout food stop for riders exploring the area.

detail.address: 4381 Gallant Avenue, Deep Cove, North Vancouver, BC

grocery.name: KC Fresh Market
grocery.desc: KC Fresh Market is a greengrocer in North Vancouver. It provides a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking fresh produce and related grocery items while traveling in the area.

grocery.name: The Windmill Deli
grocery.desc: The Windmill Deli is a neighborhood deli in Chilliwack that combines prepared foods with grocery items. It provides a convenient refueling stop for touring cyclists seeking fresh food while passing through the local area.

grocery.name: Ben's Market
grocery.desc: Ben's Market is a convenience store and flower shop in Delta, BC, serving the local North Delta neighbourhood. As a combined market and flower shop, it likely stocks everyday essentials that touring cyclists passing through the area would find useful.

grocery.name: 88 Supermarket
grocery.desc: 88 Supermarket is a Canadian-owned authentic Asian supermarket on Victoria Drive in Vancouver. It stocks a broad range of Asian and western groceries including daily fresh meat cuts, live seafood, an extensive produce department with exotic and hard-to-find fruits and vegetables, dairy, and bakery items. The store runs a loyalty club card program and regular weekly specials, and has recently expanded with a new Richmond location.

grocery.name: Naramata Store
grocery.desc: The Naramata General Store is a family-owned community hub in the heart of Naramata village, operating since 1979 and a finalist in Western Living's 2022 Foodies of the Year. It stocks full groceries alongside locally sourced Naramata Bench wines, craft beer, deli sandwiches, house-made soups, and seasonal Okanagan produce — a natural resupply stop for cyclists riding the Naramata Bench wine-country roads. The store also functions as a community notice board and parcel depot, making it a genuine village centre rather than just a convenience shop.

notes.Hot food: Deli offers house-made soups, hearty sandwiches, and 'Red Neck Taco's every Friday'; mini charcuterie boards also available in the fridge
notes.Ice: Website homepage explicitly mentions 'load the cooler with ice and some local beer & wine'

grocery.name: My Nicholson Store
grocery.desc: A general store in Nicholson serving the local community with basic provisions and supplies.

grocery.name: Choices Market
grocery.desc: Choices Market is a British Columbia-based specialty grocery chain known for prioritizing local producers, natural and organic products, and strong community engagement. The Abbotsford location, open since 2015, offers a full range of departments including Bakery, Deli, Bulk, Produce, and Wellness. It sits in a retail complex on Immel Street and would serve as a well-stocked resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart is a large-format Supercenter on Barnet Highway in Coquitlam, offering a full grocery section alongside general merchandise including clothing, electronics, and household goods. It sits on a major arterial corridor connecting Port Moody and central Coquitlam, making it a practical resupply point for cyclists touring the eastern Metro Vancouver area. As a supercenter-format store, it stocks a broader range of goods than a typical grocery stop.

grocery.name: Devonshire Flowers & Food
grocery.desc: Devonshire Flowers & Food is an independent convenience shop on Goldstream Avenue combining grocery staples with a flower offering — an unusual pairing that gives the store a local, neighbourhood character. Located on a key cycling corridor west of Victoria toward Langford, it sits in a two-storey building and would serve as a potential resupply point for touring cyclists heading in or out of the city. Its dual identity as both a market and flower shop makes it a distinctive stop on the route.

grocery.name: Tama Organic Life
grocery.desc: Tama Organic Life is a small, family-run organic produce store that has operated in East Vancouver since the mid-1990s, built around sourcing locally grown seasonal fruits, vegetables, and Japanese specialty produce (daikon, burdock root, komatsuna) directly from BC farms. The store also carries a curated Japanese pantry including fermented foods, dried goods, and specialty ingredients. A touring cyclist would find it a practical resupply stop for fresh organic produce and daily-made vegan bento boxes prepared to order.

notes.Hot food: Website prominently features 'Tama's Bento – made daily, made to order – using all organic ingredients'; described as vegan bento-style lunch boxes with a weekly changing menu

grocery.name: Co-op
grocery.desc: Armstrong Regional Co-op is a community-owned cooperative with roots going back to 1922, operating gas bars with attached convenience stores across the North Okanagan region of BC. This Vernon-area location is part of a network offering fuel, convenience items, and liquor under the Co-op brand. Touring cyclists passing through can expect a roadside stop with fuel and convenience store goods typical of a Co-op gas bar.

grocery.name: Greenrock Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Greenrock Liquor is an independent community liquor store in Nanaimo carrying a broad selection of beer, wine, spirits, ciders, and ready-to-drink beverages, with a browsable online catalogue of nearly 3,000 products. The store emphasises locally relevant options including BC VQA wines, Vancouver Island wine, and craft beer, and hosts regular in-store tastings. A touring cyclist passing through Nanaimo will find a well-stocked stop for beverage resupply across a wide range of categories and dietary preferences.

grocery.name: Cioffi's Deli
grocery.desc: Cioffi's is a long-established Italian deli, meat market, and specialty grocery founded in 1990 by the Cioffi family, offering over 200 deli meats, 250+ cheeses, and a broad pantry of Italian and European imports. The in-house Cucina turns out scratch-made hot meals, award-winning panini, espresso drinks, and daily specials using the market's own ingredients. A touring cyclist stopping here will find an unusually rich selection of high-quality ready-to-eat food and provisions in a single stop.

notes.Hot food: Cucina section describes daily hot specials (veal parmigiana, lasagna, pizza, roasted chickens), hot panini, and Lavazza espresso/cappuccino/latte to-go

grocery.name: Washington Community Market
grocery.desc: Washington Community Market is a community-rooted grocery store that has served Vancouver's Downtown Eastside neighbourhood for over 20 years, offering affordable essential goods to residents, local businesses, and community organizations. Operated since 2021 by Community Impact Real Estate Society, it stocks a broad range of groceries — dairy, deli meats, canned goods, frozen meals, bread, and cleaning supplies — with many items available in small or single-serve portions to support customers with limited incomes. It also accommodates wholesale and bulk purchasing for non-profits and housing operators in the area.

detail.address: 179 East Hastings St, Vancouver, BC V6A 1N5

notes.Hot food: 'Warm & Ready Meals' is a named product category on the website, indicating prepared/hot food is available in-store

grocery.name: Arzon Market
grocery.desc: Arzon Market is a convenience store located in North Vancouver, identifiable on OpenStreetMap as shop=convenience. Its Facebook presence (arzonmarket2020) suggests it has been operating since around 2020. As a neighbourhood convenience market, it may serve as a quick resupply stop for cyclists on local routes, though details about its specific offerings could not be verified.

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: Circle K is a major chain convenience store and gas station on Rutland Rd. N. in Kelowna's east side. It stocks packaged snacks, beverages, and fresh prepared food alongside a roller grill for hot items. Public restrooms are available on-site, making it a functional resupply and rest stop for cyclists moving through the Rutland corridor.

detail.address: 1007 Rutland Rd. N., Kelowna, BC V1X 4Y9

notes.Hot food: Website store services list includes 'Roller Grill' and 'Fresh Food Fast'

grocery.name: M & B Grocery
grocery.desc: M & B Grocery is a convenience store on Royal Oak Avenue in Vancouver. This neighborhood shop offers quick access to snacks, drinks, and supplies for touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Crosstown Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A retail liquor store located on Abbott Street in downtown Vancouver. Offers beverages and spirits for purchase.

grocery.name: Foody World
grocery.desc: Foody World is a large-format Chinese supermarket spanning approximately 60,000 sq ft with ten departments and over 40,000 product varieties, making it one of the more comprehensive grocery stops in the Richmond area. Part of a chain founded in 2001 and headquartered in Toronto, this Richmond location offers a wide selection of Asian and general grocery products in a spacious shopping environment. A touring cyclist needing to restock with a broad range of fresh foods, produce, and pantry items will find it a well-stocked one-stop option.

grocery.name: Nu Leaf Produce Market
grocery.desc: Nu Leaf Produce Market is a family-run fresh produce shop in Kamloops that has been supplying locally sourced fruits, vegetables, dairy, and pantry staples since 2011, working with over 60 regional farmers and its own Heffley Farms. It recently expanded to a second location at 1415 Hillside Drive, and also produces its own line of BC-fruit juices and reusable bags. Reviewers highlight a broad selection of in-season local produce alongside everyday grocery staples, making it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through Kamloops.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Distribution Branch - Wholesale Customer Centre
grocery.desc: The BC Liquor Distribution Branch Wholesale Customer Centre in Victoria is a government-operated B2B facility supplying alcohol to over 200 licensed hospitality and retail customers in the greater Victoria area. It functions as a trade-only order and pickup point for restaurants, bars, hotels, and licensed retailers — not a walk-in retail store. The facility is part of the broader LDB Wholesale Operations network with distribution centres in Burnaby and Kamloops.

grocery.name: Nu Leaf Market
grocery.desc: Gourmet Greens is listed in OSM as a supermarket in Kamloops, BC. The associated website domain is currently parked and inactive, and discovery notes suggest the business may have rebranded as Nu Leaf Market. Its current operational status and exact location cannot be confirmed from available evidence.

grocery.name: Souk Mediterranean - Dollar Store & Mediterranean Grocery
grocery.desc: Souk Mediterranean is a Richmond grocery store specialising in pantry ingredients sourced from over 30 countries, with a catalogue of nearly 1,800 products including bread, dairy, canned goods, spices, halawa, tahini, grape leaves, and dried fruits. It doubles as a dollar store, making it a one-stop shop for both specialty Mediterranean staples and everyday essentials. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's Number 5 Road corridor will find an unusually wide selection of shelf-stable snacks, nuts, dried fruits, and drinks well-suited for topping up supplies on the road.

grocery.name: Mid Island Liquor
grocery.desc: Mid Island Liquor is a locally-owned co-operative liquor retailer with 18 locations across Vancouver Island and surrounding communities, from Nanaimo and Parksville to Duncan, Ladysmith, and beyond. It recently acquired the Landlubber Liquor Store and hosts community events such as the Parksville Beer Festival, reflecting deep regional ties. For touring cyclists, it offers a reliable stop for beverages across a wide stretch of the island.

grocery.name: Silver Dollar Food/Deli Groceries
grocery.desc: Silver Dollar Food/Deli Groceries is a convenience store and deli located in Chilliwack, BC. The combined food, deli, and grocery format suggests it functions as a neighbourhood one-stop shop for prepared and packaged food items. It could serve as a handy resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the Chilliwack area.

grocery.name: Moet's Convenience Stores
grocery.desc: Moet's Convenience Stores is a 24/7 corner shop on Dundas Street in Vancouver, making it accessible to cyclists at any hour of the day or night. As a neighbourhood convenience store, it likely stocks the kind of quick-grab supplies — snacks, drinks, and sundries — that touring cyclists often need on the road. Its round-the-clock availability distinguishes it from most other grocery options in the area.

grocery.name: For Good Measure
grocery.desc: For Good Measure James Bay is a neighbourhood grocery institution at 579 Niagara Street that has anchored the community in various forms since 1908, operating as For Good Measure since April 2020. The store stocks bulk foods, local produce, fresh baked goods, and prepared quick eats alongside a year-round sunny cafe and patio called The Hideaway, which hosts live music and community events. It draws on an impressive network of local suppliers — from Mile Zero Coffee to Kildonan Farm chicken — making it a well-rounded resupply stop for cyclists in the James Bay area.

notes.Hot food: The Hideaway cafe serves espresso drinks; quick eats include Mosi sandwiches, Sookjai Thai curry, and Caribbean Village Jamaican patties

grocery.name: Ribbon
grocery.desc: Market Ribbon is a Korean supermarket on Kingsway in Burnaby offering a wide range of Korean groceries, house-brand kimchi, seafood, and pantry staples under its 'Club Ribbon' label. The in-store deli section carries ready-to-eat Korean items including Triangle Kimbap and Tteokbokki. The store has a second location in Coquitlam and is currently undergoing a rebranding.

notes.Hot food: Website lists a 'Market Ribbon Deli Foods' section with Triangle Kimbap, Kimbap rolls, Tteokbokki, and Cheese Tteokbokki — prepared/ready-to-eat Korean deli items

grocery.name: Mona's Shop
grocery.desc: Mona's Shop is a general store in North Vancouver described in OSM as an African multicultural bazaar, suggesting a curated selection of goods from African and multicultural communities. It is tagged as wheelchair accessible. Touring cyclists riding through North Vancouver may find it a distinctive stop for specialty or imported pantry items.

grocery.name: 7-Eleven
grocery.desc: A 7-Eleven convenience store on Number 2 Road in Richmond. A convenient stop for touring cyclists needing quick snacks, beverages, and basic supplies.

grocery.name: Sungiven Foods
grocery.desc: Sungiven Foods is a Chinese-focused supermarket chain serving Greater Vancouver with locations including North Vancouver, emphasizing fresh, natural products such as sustainably sourced seafood, antibiotic-free meats, and produce grown with natural fertilizers. The store operates a 'Sungiven Kitchen' line of ready-to-eat prepared meals alongside a broad conventional grocery selection spanning produce, dairy, eggs, meat, packaged goods, and beverages. For a touring cyclist, it offers a well-stocked resupply point with the bonus of grab-and-go hot prepared food.

notes.Hot food: Website navigation includes 'READY TO EAT' and 'Sungiven Kitchen' sections featuring prepared dishes such as Spicy Pork Intestine, Sweet & Sour Pork, Korean Army Stew, and Stir-Fried Free-Range Emperor Chicken

grocery.name: Sungiven Foods
grocery.desc: Sungiven Foods is a health-focused Asian grocery chain at City Square in Vancouver's Cambie corridor, emphasizing natural, less-processed products with fewer additives. The store carries a broad range of fresh produce, meat, seafood, dairy, packaged goods, beverages, and snacks, as well as its own Sungiven Kitchen line of prepared meals. It would serve touring cyclists well as a full resupply stop with quality fresh food options.

grocery.name: Cacao Mexican Foods
grocery.desc: Cacao Mexican Foods appears to be a specialty food shop offering Mexican food products, tagged in OSM as a general shop. The business maintains an Instagram presence under the handle @cacaomexicanfoodsltd, suggesting an active operation. A touring cyclist looking for specialty or ethnic grocery items may find it a useful stop, though its exact location requires verification.

grocery.name: Fleetwood Farm Market
grocery.desc: Fleetwood Farm Market is a neighbourhood supermarket-style farm market on 152 Street in the Fleetwood area of Surrey. Its farm market branding suggests a focus on fresh produce and local goods alongside general grocery staples. Cyclists passing through the Fleetwood corridor will find it a practical resupply point for food and provisions.

grocery.name: Ferarro Foods
grocery.desc: Ferraro Foods is a family-owned supermarket in Rossland that has operated since 1943, making it one of the oldest independent grocers in the Kootenays. The Rossland location carries a full-service Meat & Seafood Shoppe, Deli with Grab-n-Go meals and sandwiches, Cheese Shoppe, in-house bakery, and a broad produce and grocery selection. It is a well-stocked resupply point for touring cyclists moving through the Columbia and Kootenay region.

notes.Hot food: Deli page confirms Grab-n-Go Meals, Sandwiches, Panini Sandwiches, and Soups available at the Rossland location

grocery.name: 2000 Supermarket
grocery.desc: A supermarket in Richmond offering basic groceries to the local community. Useful as a resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Esso
grocery.desc: A full-service Esso fuel station on Warren Avenue in Kimberley, combining a convenience store with standard gas-station amenities. It sits on a main arterial road making it a practical supply stop for cyclists passing through or exploring the Kimberley area. The station includes an air tower for tire inflation, a useful resource for loaded tourers.

notes.Pump: Website lists 'Air Tower / Air' under Station Top Features

grocery.name: Takla Trading Post
grocery.desc: A convenience store and trading post operated by Takla Nation in the remote community of Takla Landing. Offers an important supply stop for travelers in this sparsely populated region.

detail.address: 84 Lake Shore Drive, Takla Landing, BC

grocery.name: Yaletown Express
grocery.desc: Yaletown Express is a convenience store in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood that also operates as a Canada Post outlet, located on Pacific Boulevard near the seawall. It combines postal services with convenience retail in an accessible premises. Touring cyclists passing through Yaletown may find it useful for parcel pickup or basic supplies.

grocery.name: Nature's Fare Markets
grocery.desc: Nature's Fare Markets is a BC-based natural and organic grocery chain; the Langley location opened in 2010 as the brand's first lower mainland store. The shop carries certified organic produce, ethically sourced meats and dairy, vitamins, and clean beauty products, all held to strict ingredient standards with over 500 banned additives. An in-store Bistro rounds out the stop with smoothies, made-to-order sandwiches, grab-and-go salads, and specialty espresso drinks.

notes.Hot food: In-store Bistro with made-to-order sandwich bar, grab-and-go salads and entrees, smoothies, and specialty hot drinks and espresso beverages

grocery.name: Yaletown Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Yaletown Liquor Store is a premium bottle shop in Vancouver's historic Yaletown neighbourhood, offering a curated selection of wines, beers, spirits, coolers, ciders, and non-alcoholic beverages from around the world. The store features a large cold beer fridge and knowledgeable staff who provide personalized pairing recommendations. Delivery is available through Skip the Dishes and Uber Eats for cyclists who prefer doorstep convenience.

grocery.name: Daana Paani - The Indian Grocery Store
grocery.desc: Daana Paani is a supermarket located on Seymour Street in downtown Kamloops. The name suggests South Asian origins, which may indicate a specialty grocery selection alongside general provisions. Kamloops is a key stop on several Interior BC cycling routes, making downtown grocery access valuable for touring cyclists.

grocery.name: Value on Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Value on Liquor Store is an independent liquor retailer that has operated since 2012, marketing itself on prices that beat BC government liquor stores. It is notable for housing what it claims is BC's longest cooler, stocking a broad selection of cold beer, ciders, wine, spirits, and sake. Free on-site parking and a curbside pickup option make it a convenient stop for cyclists traveling along Southwest Marine Drive.

detail.address: 1450 SW Marine Drive, Vancouver, BC V6P 5Z9

grocery.name: Red Barn Market
grocery.desc: Red Barn Market began as a farm stand at this West Saanich location in 2002 and has grown into a locally owned chain of eight stores across Greater Victoria. The market emphasises Island Grown, Island Raised, and Island Made products, including its own on-site Smokehouse producing small-batch bacon, sausages, and deli meats. The West Saanich store also houses a Sandwich Bar and a Pet Food & Feed Market, making it a notably well-stocked stop on the rural West Saanich Road corridor.

notes.Hot food: Sandwich Bar at West Saanich location

grocery.name: Chase River Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Chase River Liquor Store is a retail liquor outlet located in Nanaimo's Chase River area (unit 10 of a multi-unit property). As a licensed alcohol retailer, it stocks beer, wine, and spirits for off-premise consumption. It is a routine convenience stop rather than a destination hospitality venue for touring cyclists.

detail.address: 1273 Island Highway #10, Nanaimo, BC V9R 6Z9, Canada

grocery.name: Copper Valley Grocery & Gas
grocery.desc: A convenience store and Esso fuel station in Logan Lake offering basic supplies to traveling cyclists and motorists. The presence of compressed air service makes it a practical stop for emergency bike tire maintenance.

grocery.name: Town Centre Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Town Centre Liquor Store is a large independent liquor retailer located in the Willoughby Town Centre shopping complex in Langley. It carries an extensive range of beer, wine, and spirits, and is notable for a massive walk-in cold beer fridge stocked with domestic, imported, and craft brews. A convenient stop for touring cyclists looking to pick up beverages after a ride through the Langley area.

detail.address: A110-20678 Willoughby Town Centre Dr, Langley, BC V2Y 0L7

grocery.name: Pemberton Valley Supermarket
grocery.desc: Pemberton Valley Supermarket is the community grocery store in downtown Pemberton, located in the village centre about 25 minutes north of Whistler on Highway 99. It is a full-service store with deli, bakery, meat, and produce departments, and offers online ordering with curbside pickup or delivery. Touring cyclists passing through the Sea-to-Sky corridor will find a well-stocked stop with credit and debit card acceptance.

grocery.name: Nesters Market
grocery.desc: Nesters Market Yaletown is a full-service neighbourhood grocery store in Vancouver's Yaletown district, part of a BC-born chain founded in Whistler in 1987 and now operated by the Pattison Food Group. The chain built its identity around local, organic, natural, and specialty products not typically found at larger chains, and the Yaletown location — the brand's second store, opened in 2003 — sits in a dense, walkable urban neighbourhood well-positioned for urban bike tourists. In-store services include a bakery, deli and bistro, pharmacy, and health and wellness department.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Deli & Bistro' as an in-store service

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: A Walmart Supercenter (store 1192) in the New Westminster area, offering a broad range of departments including grocery, electronics, clothing, and baby products. As a large-format supercenter, it is one of the more comprehensive resupply stops available to touring cyclists in the region. The grocery section provides access to a wide variety of food and household supplies under one roof.

grocery.name: 88 Supermarket
grocery.desc: 88 Supermarket is a Canadian-owned Asian grocery chain operating since 2008, with a recently opened Richmond location on Garden City Road. The store stocks an extensive range of Asian and western foods including daily fresh cuts of meat, live seafood, exotic produce, bakery, and dairy. A free membership club card with points rewards is available to shoppers.

grocery.name: Oyama Sausage
grocery.desc: Oyama Sausage is a celebrated artisan charcuterie shop founded over 30 years ago and now located inside the historic Granville Island Public Market. Founded by fifth-generation charcutier John van der Lieck, the shop produces over 400 products annually including fresh sausages, cured salamis, hams, pâtés, terrines, and a curated selection of cheeses. Its multicultural Vancouver flavour profile — think Butter Chicken Sausage alongside classic saucisson sec — makes it a distinctive provisioning stop for touring cyclists exploring the city.

detail.address: Box 126 – 1689 Johnston Street, Granville Island Public Market, Vancouver, BC V6H 3R9

grocery.name: Island Afrikan Supermarket
grocery.desc: Island Afrikan Supermarket has been serving Victoria since 2000, offering African groceries, beauty products, fashion, and accessories. As an independent specialty grocer on Quadra Street, it has built relationships with vendors to source quality African food products. A touring cyclist passing through Victoria would find it a distinctive stop for provisions not available at mainstream supermarkets.

grocery.name: Sardis Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Sardis Liquor Store is a retail alcohol shop located in the Sardis neighborhood of Chilliwack, BC, on Luckakuck Way. It serves the local community with beer, wine, and spirits, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists moving through the Fraser Valley corridor. The Sardis area sits near the Trans Canada Trail and popular cycling routes connecting Chilliwack to the broader Lower Mainland.

grocery.name: Wasa Lake Gas & Food
grocery.desc: A convenience shop combined with a gas station serving the Wasa Lake area. Located on Wasa Lake Park Drive, it provides a refueling and supply stop for travelers passing through the region.

detail.address: 6112 Wasa Lake Park Drive, Wasa, V0B 2K0

grocery.name: Abbotsford Super Market
grocery.desc: Abbotsford Super Market is an Asian-focused supermarket in the Chilliwack area offering basic groceries for touring cyclists. As a standard supermarket, it provides resupply for food and supplies. Limited additional amenity details are available due to website inaccessibility.

grocery.name: Lifestyle Markets Health Foods
grocery.desc: Lifestyle Markets Health Foods is a natural health food store and supplement retailer with multiple locations across greater Victoria, including this Douglas Street location. They stock a broad range of organic produce, pantry staples, snacks, beverages, refrigerated and frozen items alongside vitamins and supplements — making it a solid health-focused resupply stop for touring cyclists. The store is wheelchair accessible per OSM.

detail.address: 2950 Douglas Street, Unit 180, Victoria, BC V8T 4N4

grocery.name: Sabzi Mandi Supermarket
grocery.desc: Sabzi Mandi Supermarket is a 100% family-owned South Asian grocery chain with 15 locations across BC, established in 1991 to serve the South Asian community's demand for fresh produce and specialty groceries unavailable elsewhere in the region. The Richmond location stocks fresh fruits and vegetables, a wide range of specialty and international groceries, household items, and cooking appliances. It is a useful full-service resupply stop for touring cyclists looking for a broad selection of fresh food and pantry staples.

grocery.name: Miller's Crossing
grocery.desc: Miller's Crossing is a general merchandise store on the Trans-Canada Highway in Savona, positioned to serve travelers and local residents. Located at a key transportation junction, it functions as a practical resupply point for cycling tourists traveling through BC's Interior plateau region. As a highway-community store, it represents the type of essential supply stop that supports long-distance touring.

grocery.name: Bulk Barn
grocery.desc: Bulk Barn is Canada's largest bulk food retailer, selling hundreds of products — nuts, dried fruit, grains, pasta, spices, baking ingredients, and candy — by weight so customers buy exactly what they need. This Victoria location (store #661) is part of a national chain with over 300 stores. For a touring cyclist it is a practical resupply stop for calorie-dense trail staples like nuts, dried fruit, and granola purchased in precisely the quantities needed.

grocery.name: Mi Tierra Latina
grocery.desc: Mi Tierra Latina is a Latin American grocery store stocking products from nine countries including Mexico, Colombia, Brazil, Peru, and El Salvador. The store carries an unusually broad range of specialty items — tortillas, chiles, frozen empanadas, Latin coffees, and regional snacks — making it a standout source of authentic ingredients on Commercial Drive. Cyclists exploring Vancouver's diverse east-side food scene would find it a compelling stop for culturally specific pantry staples.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store Richmond Seafair is a provincial government-operated retail outlet selling wine, beer, spirits, coolers, and ciders, part of the 198-store BCLIQUOR chain across British Columbia. The store is located in a strip-mall unit at Seafair in Richmond. It offers a broad product selection and accepts multiple payment methods including cash, debit, Visa, Mastercard, and American Express.

grocery.name: PriceSmart Foods
grocery.desc: PriceSmart Foods is a British Columbia supermarket chain known for competitive pricing and a wide selection of fresh produce, deli items, bakery goods, and prepared meals. The Austin Road location serves the Coquitlam area and stocks a broad range of everyday grocery staples that touring cyclists can use to restock. The chain also offers ready-made deli meals, which can be convenient for cyclists looking for a quick, substantial meal.

grocery.name: Sandown Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Sandown Liquor Store is the first Springs Group location on Vancouver Island, situated in the Sandown Shopping Centre just off the second exit from the Swartz Bay ferry terminal — a convenient stop for cyclists arriving by ferry. The store features a spacious floorplan and a massive walk-in cooler stocked with local island craft beers, ciders, wines, seltzers, and spirits. Free ice is offered with any purchase, and a VIP Points loyalty program is available.

detail.address: 10330 McDonald Park Rd. Suite #108, North Saanich, BC V8L 5X7

grocery.name: Southridge Country Store
grocery.desc: Southridge Country Store is a family-owned specialty grocery on Pender Island, sourcing ethical meats, organic produce, specialty charcuterie, and a rotating selection of Canadian and imported cheeses. The store's in-house chef prepares soups, sandwiches, dips, pies, and seasonal items available fresh or from the freezer section. An adjoining Picnic Park provides a family-friendly outdoor space with games and board games — a convenient rest stop for cyclists exploring the island.

detail.address: 3327 Port Washington Road, Pender Island, V0N 2M1

notes.Hot food: In-house made hot soups and sandwiches prepared by an in-house chef using store ingredients

grocery.name: Bruce's Country Market
grocery.desc: Bruce's Country Market is a family-owned institution in Maple Ridge operating since 1948, founded by the McEachern family as a local fish market supplying fresh West Coast seafood from their own fishing fleet.
