Today it has grown into a full-service market featuring an extensive fresh and smoked wild salmon counter, deli and restaurant with house-made soups and hot meals, and a produce section sourcing from local lower mainland farms. The market ships its branded products across North America and remains one of the original 'ocean to you' seafood destinations in the Fraser Valley.

detail.address: 23963 Lougheed Highway, Maple Ridge, BC V2W 1J1

notes.Hot food: Website states deli and restaurant offers 'soups, crisp salads and a variety of hot meal items to satisfy your breakfast, lunch or dinner cravings'; evening takeout also mentioned

grocery.name: West Coast Liquor Company
grocery.desc: West Coast Liquor Company is a multi-location BC liquor retailer operating under Gibson Hospitality, with this branch serving the Burnaby Royal Oak neighbourhood. The store offers hundreds of local craft and international wine, beer, spirits, coolers, and ciders, and supports online ordering with delivery. It is one of three Lower Mainland locations alongside Vancouver Fraser Street and Kerrisdale.

detail.address: 7651 Royal Oak Ave, Burnaby, BC V5J 4K2

grocery.name: Esso
grocery.desc: The Maple Leaf Store is an Esso-branded fuel and convenience stop on Highway 6 in Crescent Valley, a small community in the Slocan Valley between Nelson and Slocan. It offers convenience store goods, an ATM, and a car wash, making it a practical resupply point in a rural stretch with limited services. For cyclists travelling BC-6, this is one of the few accessible stops in the valley.

grocery.name: Brock Centre Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Brock Centre Liquor Store is an independent liquor retailer in Kamloops' Brock neighbourhood, operating at the same location since 2003. The renovated 2,500+ sq ft store features a large walk-in cooler stocked with cold beer, ciders, and coolers, plus a selection of over 200 wines and 174 hard spirits. A unique 'Pick a Beer' bulk option lets shoppers build their own package sizes, and the store carries local Kamloops and BC craft beers.

grocery.name: The Stock Market
grocery.desc: The Stock Market has operated from stall 147 in Vancouver's Granville Island Public Market since 1986, selling freshly made soups, stocks, pestos, sauces, and dressings crafted from local ingredients. It is a well-known local institution in one of BC's most popular cycling-accessible urban destinations. Touring cyclists exploring Granville Island will find it tucked in the far east corner of the Public Market.

notes.Hot food: Website states 'Hot soups served until 30 minutes before closing.'

grocery.name: College Park Liquor Store
grocery.desc: College Park Liquor Store is an alcohol retailer in Chilliwack's McCallum Road shopping area. It serves as a convenient stop for beverages during cycling trips through the region.

grocery.name: AC Gas
grocery.desc: AC Gas is the retail gas station and convenience store of locally owned AC Petroleum, situated in downtown Pemberton on Prospect Street. It stocks convenience store items alongside gasoline, diesel, oils, and propane cylinder exchanges — making it a practical multi-stop for touring cyclists passing through the Sea-to-Sky corridor. Compressed air is available on site, and the broader AC Petroleum network also operates 24/7 cardlock stations in Pemberton and Whistler.

Cyclists riding through this part of Kamloops may find it a potential resupply point, though its current operational status is uncertain.

grocery.name: El Paisano
grocery.desc: El Paisano is a family-owned Latin American grocery store with two downtown Vancouver locations — one on Davie Street and one inside Granville SkyTrain Station — specializing in authentic ingredients, spices, snacks, and beverages from Mexico, Colombia, Brazil, and Venezuela. Founded by food lovers with roots in Mexico, the shop brings hard-to-find Latin pantry staples to the heart of the city. The Davie Street location is walkable from the Seawall cycling route and the West End.

grocery.name: Proviant International Foods

Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a useful stop for provisioning with a wider variety of foods.

grocery.name: ABURI Market
grocery.desc: ABURI Market is an elevated Japanese grocery concept by the award-winning restaurant group behind Miku and Minami, offering premium imported Japanese products in a grocerant format at its Ambleside location in West Vancouver. Cyclists stopping in will find finish-at-home meal kits, ready-to-eat bento and bowls, exclusive A5 Iwate Wagyu cuts, fresh sashimi-grade fish via Hyoketsu flash-freeze technology, imported snacks, and Japanese lifestyle goods. The store is situated within the Grosvenor Ambleside development, a 2021 ULI Americas Award of Excellence winner.

grocery.desc: JV Convenience Store is a neighborhood shop on Dewdney Trunk Road in Maple Ridge specializing in exotic snacks and drinks sourced from around the world, alongside everyday household essentials. The store carries an eclectic mix of international candies, chips, glass-bottled beverages, energy drinks, Mexican snacks, and treats like mini donuts and screamers. Cyclists passing through Maple Ridge on this busy commercial corridor would find it a useful stop for an unusual variety of snacks and refreshments.

grocery.name: Bulk Barn

The Tsawwassen location accepts reusable containers brought by customers, making it a practical resupply stop for cyclists who want to portion exactly what they need for the road. The all-bulk format means a touring cyclist can pick up trail mix, oats, or energy-dense snacks without paying for excess packaging.

Positioned along Chilliwack Lake Road, it functions as a one-stop resupply point for anglers, campers, and hikers heading into the valley, carrying groceries, hardware, camping gear, fishing tackle, ice, and firewood. Historical photographs from the early 1980s line the walls, and a hot dog stand operates right next door.

The chain operates across Vancouver, Richmond, Burnaby, Surrey, White Rock, Coquitlam, and Langley, making it a recognizable resupply option for cyclists touring the Lower Mainland.

Its location in a ferry-adjacent community makes it a potentially useful stop for cyclists passing through or catching the Tsawwassen–Swartz Bay or Tsawwassen–Duke Point sailings.

Stephan is a certified Fleischer Meister who crafts housemade sausages and charcuterie entirely from traditional German and European recipes — all gluten-free, no binders or fillers. Touring cyclists will find a rich selection of housemade sausages, European-style breads and cheeses, pastries, condiments, custom sandwiches, and homemade soups.

grocery.name: Blackcomb Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Blackcomb Liquor Store is a locally owned and operated bottle shop at the base of Blackcomb in Whistler's Upper Village, run since 2006 by sommelier Michael Kompass and chef Rachel Kompass. It claims Whistler's widest selection of regional and craft beverages, with over 300 cold beers and more than 400 wine listings — including the largest selection of premium BC boutique wines in town. The about page specifically calls out bicycle wine carriers among its curated specialty products, a nod to its cycling-aware clientele.

grocery.name: The Landing Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Landing Liquor Store is Nanaimo's largest private liquor retailer, housed in a spacious unit at the Brooks Landing shopping centre on Island Highway North. The store carries over 5,000 products including 750+ craft beers, 400 BC VQA wines, and 300+ scotch varieties, with an on-site sommelier available for consultation. A rentable private tasting room with a bar, projector, and food service makes it a notable stop for groups looking to explore BC's wine and craft beer scene.

detail.address: 120-2000 Island Hwy N, Nanaimo, BC V9S 5W3

grocery.name: Langley Farm Market
grocery.desc: Langley Farm Market is a Metro Vancouver chain specializing in freshly picked local produce sourced directly from BC farmers, including Okanagan fruit and organic Metro Vancouver vegetables. This Lougheed/Maple Ridge location offers a broad selection including fresh meat, deli cold cuts, chilled seafood, in-store baked goods, and natural and organic groceries. The market won the 2025 Vancouver Consumer Choice Award for Best Fruit & Vegetable Market, reflecting a strong reputation for freshness and quality.

grocery.name: Quality Foods
grocery.desc: Quality Foods is a full-service BC-based supermarket chain with a Nanaimo location on Turner Road offering a comprehensive range of groceries including fresh produce, bakery, deli and ready-made meals, and household supplies. The store stocks Canadian products alongside international selections and operates an online ordering platform for the local community. Touring cyclists resupplying in Nanaimo will find a wide variety of food and pantry staples here.

grocery.name: Nature's Fare Markets
grocery.desc: Nature's Fare Markets is a well-established natural and organic grocery chain that has served Penticton since 1998, moving to this larger Main Street location in 2018. The store carries certified organic produce, ethically sourced meat and dairy, vitamins, and clean beauty products alongside a Bistro offering local, organic grab-and-go meals, entrees, and smoothies. With over 40 employees and a long-tenured store manager, it functions as a full-service health-focused supermarket — a strong resupply point for cyclists seeking quality whole foods.

grocery.name: Circle K

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a provincial government-operated retail outlet at Nanaimo's Port Place mall, part of the 198-store BCLIQUOR chain run by the Liquor Distribution Branch. It carries an extensive selection of wine, beer, spirits, coolers, and ciders. Cycling tourists passing through could stop to purchase beverages for the road, though it functions as a retail shop rather than a hospitality venue.

grocery.name: El Negociante Abbotsford "Mexican & Latin Store"
grocery.desc: El Negociante is a Mexican and Latin specialty grocery store in Abbotsford, BC, tagged as a supermarket and stocking products oriented toward Latin American cuisine. The store is located in a unit (unit 20), suggesting a plaza or strip-mall setting.

grocery.name: Sungiven Foods
grocery.desc: Sungiven Foods is a BC-based Asian supermarket chain focused on natural, minimally processed foods, stocking produce, meat, seafood, dairy, and a wide range of packaged and frozen Asian staples. The Richmond One Park location is one of several Lower Mainland stores. The in-store Sungiven Kitchen offers a rotating selection of ready-to-eat prepared hot dishes, making it a practical resupply stop for cyclists wanting a cooked meal alongside full grocery shopping.

grocery.name: Bainbridge Liquor Store

It bills itself as a destination for wine, beer, and spirit enthusiasts with a frequently rotating selection that includes hard-to-find products. Touring cyclists passing along the Lougheed corridor can pick up beverages for camp or a rest stop, with UberEats delivery also available.

grocery.name: 7-Eleven
grocery.desc: 7-Eleven is a convenience store franchise serving North Vancouver. It offers standard convenience store products including snacks, beverages, and basic supplies for quick shopping needs. The location provides a convenient stop for touring cyclists and other travelers in the area.

grocery.name: Viti Nordel
grocery.desc: Viti Nordel is a wine and lager retail shop in North Delta, one of five Lower Mainland locations in the Viti Wine and Lager chain operated by the award-winning ViaggioHospitality group. The store offers a curated selection of wines, beers, and other beverages, and is positioned along a suburban commercial strip near the Nordel corridor. Touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley flatlands could stop here to pick up drinks for camp or an evening stay.

grocery.name: Angry Otter Liquor
grocery.desc: Angry Otter Liquor is a liquor store in North Vancouver. It is a retail alcohol shop that accepts cash, credit, and debit cards, though it does not have a drive-through.

grocery.name: Corona Foods
grocery.desc: Corona Foods is a convenience store located on Sooke Road in Victoria. As a typical convenience store, it serves as a quick stop for supplies and refreshments for travelers. Specific cyclist amenities are not documented online.

Part of the Canco independent Canadian fuel and retail chain, it operates as a 'One Stop by Canco' combining fuel, in-store convenience shopping, and loyalty programs. Its highway location makes it a natural resupply stop for touring cyclists travelling through the Thompson River corridor.

grocery.name: Calvin's Farm Market
grocery.desc: Calvin's Farm Market is a local greengrocer and farm market in the Delta/Surrey area of BC, selling fresh produce and farm goods. For a touring cyclist cutting through the Fraser Valley delta region, it represents a potential fresh-food resupply stop on an otherwise suburban stretch. The market's farm-direct nature suggests seasonal local produce rather than a full-service grocery.

grocery.name: Pink Mountain General Store (Mile 143)
grocery.desc: Pink Mountain General Store is a critical resupply stop at Mile 143 of the Alaska Highway in one of BC's most remote stretches, operating year-round including in winter. Part of a larger campsite and RV park, it offers an unusually broad range of services for such an isolated location: groceries, fishing supplies, clothing, souvenirs, all fuels, laundry, coin-operated showers, WiFi, a post office, and a liquor outlet. For a touring cyclist on the Alaska Highway, this is a genuine lifeline between very long service gaps.

Touring cyclists may find affordable gear, used books, or odds and ends at this community-oriented shop on Kipp Ave.

grocery.name: Safeway

It combines a convenience store stocked with basic groceries, a gas bar (unleaded and diesel), the Little Teapot Café serving fresh bannock, soup, and coffee for takeout, and an on-site ATM. An attached four-room B&B (AH'DA) makes it one of the very few places in this sparsely serviced stretch of northern BC where a touring cyclist can resupply, eat, and find overnight shelter.

Cyclists travelling through the Cowichan Valley can stop here to resupply with beer, wine, or spirits from a well-established local institution.

It also runs a takeout kitchen serving classic Persian grilled dishes and stews. Touring cyclists will find a well-stocked boutique grocery stop with a notably broad selection of specialty and organic items beyond standard supermarket fare.

grocery.name: Nesters Market

It sits in the historic Woodwards building in the heart of Vancouver's Gastown/Downtown Eastside area, making it a convenient resupply stop for cyclists touring the city.

grocery.name: Canco Gas
grocery.desc: Canco Gas is a Canadian-owned independent gas station and convenience store in Christina Lake, part of the PR Petroleum-operated Canco chain with over 100 locations across Canada. grocery.name: Commons Liquor & More

For touring cyclists looking to resupply with craft beer, wine, or a prized dram at the end of a riding day, this store offers a notably broad selection in the Duncan area.

Dogs are welcome on leash, and the market runs rain or shine as an essential community food service.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store

For touring cyclists passing through North Vancouver, it is a convenient stop to resupply with beverages.

grocery.name: Fujiya
grocery.desc: Fujiya is a long-running Japanese grocery chain with its Richmond location opened in 1989, offering a wide selection of Japanese food products for home cooking and ready-to-go prepared items including sushi. Founded in Vancouver's Japantown in 1977, Fujiya has become a staple of Japanese-Canadian food culture across BC. A touring cyclist would find this a useful stop for specialty Japanese groceries, packaged snacks, and catering-style prepared sushi available for pickup.

grocery.name: Super Grocer
grocery.desc: Super Grocer is a long-standing neighbourhood supermarket in Richmond's Steveston area, serving the community since at least the 1970s. It stocks groceries, dairy, meats, and produce, and shares the building complex with an in-house pharmacy and flower shop. Its location between Moncton and Chatham Streets makes it a convenient supply stop for cyclists touring the Steveston waterfront.

grocery.name: City Avenue Market
grocery.desc: City Avenue Market is a family-owned grocery chain that has anchored Vancouver's Commercial Drive since 2005, emphasising fresh, local, and organic produce alongside a broad conventional grocery selection. In March 2025 the Vancouver Eastside location completed a renovation that added a full-service deli counter offering freshly sliced meats, cheeses, and prepared items. One of four Greater Vancouver locations, it also offers online ordering with delivery or pickup across the region.

grocery.name: Pan-Asia Market & Deli
grocery.desc: Pan-Asia Market & Deli is a small Asian-focused convenience store and deli located in Chilliwack, BC. It combines everyday convenience store staples with Asian grocery products and deli offerings, making it a distinctive neighbourhood resupply option. Cyclists passing through Chilliwack would find it a useful stop for snacks, prepared foods, and specialty ingredients.

detail.address: Unit 1-32288 South Fraser Way, Abbotsford, BC V2T 1W9

grocery.name: Chan's Ocean Park
grocery.desc: A greengrocer located in Tsawwassen. Limited information available beyond the OSM categorization; website contact details could not be verified.

grocery.name: Mayhew Sherwood Produce and Flowers
grocery.desc: Mayhew Sherwood Produce and Flowers is a greengrocer in Vancouver selling fresh produce and flowers. The shop accepts both credit and debit cards, making it convenient for cyclists passing through. Beyond its core produce offering, details about its layout or additional services are not publicly documented.

detail.address: 3691 W Broadway, Vancouver, BC V6J 1Z2, Canada

grocery.name: Sari Sari Store
grocery.desc: Sari Sari Store is a convenience store located on Joyce Street in Vancouver. It offers basic groceries and supplies for the local community.

grocery.name: Farm Gate Store
grocery.desc: Farm Gate Store is an independent, community-rooted grocery on Mayne Island, one of the Gulf Islands, open since April 2011 and founded by farmer-and-chef owners Don and Shanti. It stocks organic and locally sourced produce, artisan cheeses, specialty foods, and eco-friendly household goods, with a daily deli counter turning out chef-made sandwiches, entrees, and hot meals using in-season local ingredients. For cyclists ferrying through the Gulf Islands, it offers one of the most complete fresh-food stops available on Mayne Island.

detail.address: 568 Fernhill Rd, Mayne Island, BC V0N2J2

notes.Hot food: Website prominently features a daily deli with chef-prepared hot meals: roast pork shoulder, Chinese braised duck leg with rice and vegetables, sandwiches, burritos, and pasta dishes made with local, organic ingredients

grocery.name: IGA
grocery.desc: IGA on Robson Street is a full-service neighborhood supermarket in the heart of downtown Vancouver, stocking a broad range of fresh produce, deli and prepared meals, meat, dairy, bakery goods, and household supplies. It is one of the more centrally located grocery resupply points for cyclists touring Vancouver's downtown core. The store accepts cash, credit, and debit cards and is tagged as wheelchair accessible in OSM.

grocery.name: Hayat Supermarket
grocery.desc: Hayat Supermarket is a retail grocery store located in Richmond, BC, tagged in OpenStreetMap as a full supermarket. Its position along Number 1 Road places it on a route accessible to cyclists travelling through the Richmond area. Touring cyclists would find it a potential stop for provisioning along this flat, cycling-friendly corridor.

grocery.name: Brandt's Creek Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Brandt's Creek Liquor Store is a neighbourhood liquor retailer in Kelowna's Glenmore area, carrying a broad selection of domestic and international wines, craft beers, spirits, coolers, and ciders. It places particular emphasis on Okanagan regional and international wine selections, making it a potential stop for cyclists exploring BC's wine country. Some products are seasonal or limited-release, and the store encourages customers to call ahead for specific brand availability.

grocery.name: Andes Latin Foods
grocery.desc: Andes Latin Foods is a Venezuelan-family-owned Latin mini market and coffee shop serving the Port Moody community. Their menu spans multiple South American countries, offering Colombian, Peruvian, Argentine, and Venezuelan empanadas alongside tequeños, pão de queijo, and fresh-pressed fruit juices. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a culturally distinctive spot for a hot snack or coffee with a genuine Latin American flavour.

notes.Hot food: Menu includes fried and baked prepared foods: aborrajado (deep-fried plantain), Venezuelan/Colombian/Peruvian/Argentinian empanadas (fried or baked), tequeños (fried cheese sticks), and almojábana/pandebono baked goods

grocery.name: Gas Plus
grocery.desc: Gas Plus — marketed by GP Fuels as 'Fairmont Gas Plus' — is a fuel station and convenience store on Fairmont Frontage Road in the Columbia Valley resort community of Fairmont Hot Springs. Part of the regional GP Fuels network operating in the East Kootenay region of BC, it is one of the few roadside service stops in a stretch of valley dominated by the Fairmont Hot Springs resort. For touring cyclists riding the Columbia Valley corridor between Radium Hot Springs and Canal Flats, it serves as a natural waypoint.

detail.address: 4966 Fairmont Frontage, Fairmont Hot Springs, V0B 1L0

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a provincial government-operated alcohol retail chain with 198 locations across British Columbia, selling wine, beer, spirits, coolers, and ciders. The chain serves over 36 million retail customers annually and is operated by the BC Liquor Distribution Branch. A touring cyclist stopping here could pick up beer or wine, but the store is primarily an alcohol retailer rather than a rest stop or hospitality venue.

grocery.name: Valoroso Foods
grocery.desc: Valoroso Foods is an Italian-style deli located on Pacific Boulevard in Vancouver's Yaletown area, near the seawall. The shop is wheelchair accessible and accepts both credit and debit cards, making it a convenient stop for cyclists riding the False Creek route.

grocery.name: Brassneck
grocery.desc: Brassneck Brewery is a well-established craft brewery on Vancouver's Main Street corridor, celebrated for a rotating lineup of inventive beers spanning crisp Kölsch to barrel-aged fruit ales and double-digit stouts. The tasting room at 2148 Main Street offers draft pours and cans to go, with food sourced from sister restaurant The Magnet. It sits in one of Vancouver's most bike-friendly neighbourhoods, making it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the city.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercentre Store #3019 is a large-format department and grocery store serving east Abbotsford, stocking a full range of food staples alongside electronics, clothing, and general merchandise. For a touring cyclist it serves as a one-stop resupply point with accessible washrooms and free in-store Wi-Fi. The store is wheelchair accessible throughout.

grocery.name: Golden Star Supermarket
grocery.desc: A supermarket located on Victoria Drive in Vancouver.

grocery.name: Blundell Liquor Town
grocery.desc: Blundell Liquor Town is an alcohol retailer in the Richmond area serving local shoppers and passing travelers. No specific cyclist amenities have been confirmed from available information. It may serve as a convenience stop for basic refreshment restocking during a cycling tour.

grocery.name: Laurelle's Fine Foods
grocery.desc: Laurelle's Fine Foods is a family-owned bakery deli operating inside the Granville Island Public Market since 1990, with an open kitchen where customers can watch baked goods come out of the oven fresh daily. The shop offers scones, muffins, cookies, pastries, salads, casseroles, and ready-to-eat meals, with a notable selection of vegan and gluten-free items. It sits just steps from the Granville Island waterfront courtyard — a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring the False Creek seawall.

grocery.name: Nesters Market
grocery.desc: Nesters Market is a Western Canadian full-service supermarket chain founded in Whistler in 1987 and now part of the Pattison Food Group, with locations across BC and Alberta including major tourist destinations like Banff and Jasper. The Lakeview location offers a broad selection including fresh produce, natural and organic products, an in-store bakery, a deli and bistro counter, and a pharmacy. It positions itself as a neighbourhood-focused store with an emphasis on local, specialty, and quality goods that go beyond a typical chain supermarket.

grocery.name: Resthaven Store
grocery.desc: Resthaven Store is a convenience store located in Sidney, BC, on the southern Saanich Peninsula — a popular cycling destination connecting the BC Ferries terminal at Swartz Bay with the town of Sidney and the Lochside Regional Trail. As a neighbourhood convenience store, it may offer basic supplies useful to touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: A taste of Ukraine
grocery.desc: A Ukrainian deli in Vancouver offering traditional Eastern European groceries and prepared foods. A useful resource for touring cyclists seeking specialty ingredients or a quick prepared meal.

grocery.name: Skyline Market
grocery.desc: A convenience store in Tsawwassen, BC. Website information is unavailable.

grocery.name: Marco Market
grocery.desc: Marco Market is a convenience store located on Rumble Street in Vancouver. It offers basic retail goods and groceries to local customers and passing cyclists.

grocery.name: Davie Street Market
grocery.desc: Davie Market is a small convenience store on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, close to English Bay. The area is a popular destination for cyclists accessing the seawall and Stanley Park routes. No current web presence could be confirmed to provide further detail about the store's current offerings.

grocery.name: Beverly Corners Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Voyage Liquor is a locally owned chain that has been serving Vancouver Island and Salt Spring Island since 2006, with the Duncan location being one of five stores. It stocks a curated mix of local, national, and global wines, spirits, and beers, with staff described as friendly and knowledgeable. Same-day delivery and a loyalty rewards program are also available, which could be handy for cyclists planning a rest-day resupply.

grocery.name: Robinhood Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Robinhood Liquor Store is a neighbourhood retail liquor store on 72nd Avenue in Surrey carrying beer, wine, and spirits with monthly rotating specials and a loyalty program through More Rewards. The store offers delivery via Skip the Dishes and DoorDash in addition to in-person shopping. A touring cyclist could stop here to resupply on beverages, though no cycling-specific amenities are advertised on the website.

grocery.name: Red Label Produce
grocery.desc: Red Label Produce, also operating as Zhao Feng Produce Ltd., is a fresh fruits and vegetables market located inside Parker Place mall on No. 3 Road in Richmond. The store sources produce from local farms as well as international suppliers and emphasizes freshness and quality selection. A touring cyclist passing through the Richmond shopping corridor would find a full range of fresh produce and grocery provisions here.

detail.address: 4380 No. 3 Road, Store #1040, Parker Place, Richmond, BC V6X 3V7

grocery.name: Tsartlip (Wjolelp) Pump
grocery.desc: Tsartlip PUMP is a First Nations-owned convenience store and fuel station operated by the Tsartlip First Nation on W̱SÁNEĆ territory in Saanichton, BC. The store carries groceries, beverages, coffee, frozen treats, ice, and souvenirs including Native Northwest apparel, alongside regular, mid-grade, premium, and diesel fuel. Eligible customers can access tax-exempt purchasing on fuel and select in-store items.

notes.Ice: Ice listed under Grocery products on website
notes.Pump: Air listed under Services on website; gas station air compressors are usable by cyclists for tyre inflation

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercentre #5838 is a large-format big-box store in Surrey's west end, carrying a full supermarket alongside electronics, clothing, toys, and furniture departments. As one of the largest single-stop retail destinations in the South Fraser region, it offers touring cyclists a broad resupply opportunity for food and general goods. The store accepts cash, credit, and debit and offers in-store Wi-Fi for customers.

grocery.name: Save-On-Foods
grocery.desc: A Save-On-Foods supermarket on Cambie Street in Vancouver providing convenient resupply of food and essentials for touring cyclists. As a full-service grocer, it offers the core provisions cyclists need while traveling through the city. The street-level location makes it easily accessible from major cycling routes.

grocery.name: Thurga Grocery
grocery.desc: Thurga Grocery is a Sri Lankan and South Indian supermarket that has been serving Metro Vancouver for over 25 years, founded by Thulasi who immigrated from Sri Lanka and saw a gap in the local market for authentic South Asian goods. The store stocks fresh produce, traditional spices, and exotic fruits sourced from India and Sri Lanka, along with the owner's own branded Thurga products. Freshly made traditional Sri Lankan meals are also available on-site, making it a worthwhile stop for a hot meal.

detail.address: 6027 Fraser St, Vancouver, BC V5W 2Z8, Canada

notes.Hot food: Website states 'serve freshly made traditional Sri Lankan meals' on the Products page

grocery.name: Co-op
grocery.desc: Armstrong Regional Co-op is a member-owned cooperative founded in 1922 by the townspeople of Armstrong and Spallumcheen, making it one of the oldest co-ops in the Okanagan. It operates gas bar and convenience locations, bulk fuel services, and an associated liquor store (ARC Liquor). For touring cyclists it offers a one-stop roadside convenience stop with snacks, drinks, and fuel in the North Okanagan.

grocery.name: Scotch Creek Market
grocery.desc: Scotch Creek Market is a supermarket serving the Scotch Creek community on Squilax-Anglemont Road. It functions as a standard grocery stop for local residents and travelers in the region.

grocery.name: New Pacific Supermarket
grocery.desc: New Pacific Supermarket is an Asian-focused full-service supermarket inside Henderson Place Mall in Coquitlam, offering produce, grocery, dairy and frozen goods, fresh meat, and live seafood. The in-store NP Kitchen serves hot meals daily, including BBQ pork and other Asian dishes. Touring cyclists heading through Coquitlam will find a broad selection of fresh and packaged food under one roof.

notes.Hot food: Blog post (June 2020) states 'NP Kitchen has expanded its department and now provides hot meals daily'; store departments page confirms NP Kitchen serves daily menu items including BBQ pork

grocery.name: London Drugs
grocery.desc: London Drugs is a pharmacy and department store chain located in Lougheed Town Centre, a shopping mall in Burnaby. The store provides pharmaceutical services and general retail merchandise. Touring cyclists can access retail and pharmacy services, though cyclist-specific amenities are not confirmed online.

grocery.name: Mount Douglas Market
grocery.desc: Mount Douglas Market is a neighbourhood grocery store on Shelbourne Street in Victoria, stocking a curated mix of specialty, organic, and plant-based products alongside everyday staples. The store runs weekly specials covering fresh BC produce, deli items, and artisan packaged goods. Same-day in-store and curbside pickup are available.

grocery.name: Sabayons
grocery.desc: A department store located on Government Street in downtown Victoria's basement shopping level. Could serve as a general shopping stop for cyclists passing through the city center.

grocery.name: Meinhardt
grocery.desc: Meinhardt is a supermarket in Vancouver. As a full-service grocery store, it serves touring cyclists needing to resupply basic provisions.

grocery.name: Voyage Liquor Express
grocery.desc: Voyage Liquor Express (branded 'Ganges Express' on the company website) is one of five locations in the locally owned Voyage Liquor chain serving Vancouver Island and Salt Spring Island since 2006. Situated on Lower Ganges Road in the main commercial hub of Salt Spring Island, it offers a curated selection of local, national, and global beer, wine, and spirits. Cyclists passing through Ganges can stock up on cold drinks, with same-day delivery and a loyalty rewards program also available.

grocery.name: Sashimiya
grocery.desc: Sashimiya is a grab-and-go sushi and sashimi shop founded by Tokyo-born Chef Taka Omi, a veteran of the Fairmont Royal York and Fairmont Vancouver's RawBar. The shop stocks premium sashimi-grade fish alongside Japanese pantry staples — rice, nori, miso, soy sauce — making it a destination for both ready-to-eat meals and home cooking supplies. It has been featured by Eater, the Globe & Mail, and other outlets as one of Vancouver's essential takeout stops.

grocery.name: Organic Acres Market
grocery.desc: Organic Acres Market is an indoor greengrocer in Vancouver focused on organic produce. The shop's name suggests a specialty in organic goods, making it a useful stop for cyclists seeking fresh, health-conscious provisions. No further detail about the store's layout or offerings could be confirmed from available sources.

detail.address: 3603 Main St, Vancouver, BC V5V 3N6, Canada

grocery.name: Co-op Ucluelet Food & Hardware
grocery.desc: Co-op Ucluelet Food & Hardware is a community-owned co-operative supermarket and hardware store on the main commercial strip of Ucluelet, a remote surf and hiking town on the west coast of Vancouver Island. As the primary full-service grocery option in a small, geographically isolated community, it is a key resupply point for cyclists riding the Pacific Rim or doing the West Coast route. Being a member-owned co-op, it has deep local roots and an emphasis on community connection.

grocery.name: Sahali Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Sahali Liquor Store is a private bottle shop located behind the Sahali Mall in Kamloops, operated by the adjacent Fox N Hounds Pub. It stocks 28 fully loaded cooler doors of cold beer, cider, and craft brews alongside wines, spirits, and BC VQA selections, making it a convenient cold-drink stop for cyclists passing through the city. The store also offers a call-ahead cold delivery service and a loyalty program shared with the neighbouring pub.

grocery.name: Nesters Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Nesters Liquor Store is the largest locally owned private liquor store in Whistler, tracing its roots to the mid-1990s Boot Cold Beer and Wine Store and carrying the same iconic ski-boot logo since 1966. The shop stocks an extensive range of BC and imported wines, craft beers, and spirits, and is well-regarded among locals and visitors for staff expertise and custom-order capability. A delivery service runs daily and will bring orders directly to hotels, condos, and homes across the resort.

detail.address: Unit 101 - 7015 Nesters Road, Whistler, British Columbia, V8E 0X1

grocery.name: Fairway Market McKenzie
grocery.desc: Fairway Market is a locally owned Vancouver Island grocery chain founded in 1963, now operating nine locations including this Saanich store on McKenzie Avenue. As one of the island's largest independent grocers, it stocks a broad range of departments — produce, dairy, meat, bakery, deli, and dedicated Asian Kitchen and Sushi Village counters. The chain emphasizes local BC and Canadian producers alongside international specialties, making it a well-stocked resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through Victoria's eastern suburbs.

notes.Hot food: Website lists Asian Kitchen and Sushi Village as in-store departments, indicating prepared and hot food counters

grocery.name: Quilchena Ranch General Store
grocery.desc: A convenience store and fuel station in rural Quilchena serving the local community with general merchandise and supplies. Located on Highway 5A, it is a practical stop for touring cyclists passing through the region seeking provisions and fuel for campstoves.

grocery.name: Odd Society
grocery.desc: Odd Society is a small-batch craft distillery on Powell Street in East Vancouver's port district, founded by Gordon Glanz, who holds an MSc in brewing and distilling from Heriot Watt University in Edinburgh. The distillery is known for experimental, award-winning spirits — including a Porcini & Candy Cap Single Malt Whisky that won the Product Innovation Award at the Canadian Artisan Spirit Competition — alongside collaborations with local breweries and wineries. Cyclists can stop in at the cocktail lounge, pick up bottles from the on-site bottle shop, or book the space for small group events.

grocery.name: Lennox Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Lennox Liquor Store is a retail alcohol shop located in Vancouver. It serves as a convenient stop for purchasing beverages while cycling through the area.

grocery.name: The Turkey House & Deli
grocery.desc: The Turkey House & Deli is a specialty deli shop on King George Boulevard in Tsawwassen, BC. The name suggests a focus on turkey and deli provisions, making it a potential stop for cyclists seeking ready-to-eat or prepared foods. It sits in the South Delta area near the Tsawwassen ferry terminal, a corridor used by touring cyclists travelling to and from Vancouver Island.

grocery.name: Good Neighbour Supermarket
grocery.desc: A neighborhood greengrocer and supermarket on Kingsway in Vancouver, specializing in produce and staple groceries for local residents and passing cyclists.

grocery.name: Spinnakers Gastro Brewpub
grocery.desc: Spinnakers Gastro Brewpub is Canada's first purpose-built gastro brewpub, crafting beer on Victoria's Inner Harbour since 1984 and helping define BC's craft brewing culture. The waterfront complex features a covered heated patio, a taproom pouring an extensive range of house-brewed ales, ciders, and spirits, a full farm-to-table restaurant, and heritage guesthouse accommodations. With partnerships across more than 35 local farmers and producers, it delivers a distinctly Vancouver Island experience in the heart of Vic West.

grocery.name: Proud Pinoy Grocery Store
grocery.desc: Proud Pinoy Grocery Store is a Filipino-specialty supermarket on Fraser Street in Vancouver. It provides groceries and provisions to local shoppers.

grocery.name: Market Fresh Foods
grocery.desc: Market Fresh Foods is a supermarket in Kamloops offering basic groceries and supplies. It serves both the local community and touring cyclists needing provisions while passing through the area.

grocery.name: Neighbours Café + Provisions
grocery.desc: Neighbours Café + Provisions (formerly Gaia Grocery) is Tofino's community hub combining specialty espresso drinks, locally sourced groceries, and fresh lunch options under one roof. New owners Kevin and Marie — the team behind Cocofino dairy-free yogurt — took over the Gaia Grocery space and have built it into a neighbourhood gathering spot that serves both long-time locals and visitors passing through. For touring cyclists, it offers a compact grocery stop and café in the heart of Tofino.

notes.Hot food: Website: 'yummy lunch options' alongside espresso drinks and frozen yogurt

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: Circle K is a 24-hour convenience store and petrol station on Quadra Street in Victoria, part of the international Couche-Tard/Circle K chain. It stocks the standard convenience-store range of snacks, drinks, and packaged foods, and offers coffee on-site. Its round-the-clock hours make it a reliable resupply point for touring cyclists passing through Victoria at any time of day or night.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a provincial government-operated retail outlet selling wine, beer, spirits, coolers, and ciders, forming part of the 198-location BCLIQUOR chain. This South Burnaby location is a standard chain store with a broad product selection and knowledgeable staff for beverage recommendations. A touring cyclist could stop to pick up packaged alcoholic beverages, but the store offers no food, prepared drinks, or documented cyclist services.

grocery.name: Urban Fare
grocery.desc: Urban Fare is a supermarket located in Vancouver's Shangri-La building on Alberni Street, offering typical grocery store supplies including gluten-free options. It's a convenient resupply stop for cycling tourists in downtown Vancouver.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: A two-level Walmart Supercenter in New Westminster offering a full grocery section alongside general merchandise including electronics, clothing, and furniture. As one of the larger retail destinations in the area, it provides a one-stop resupply option for touring cyclists needing food, household goods, or basic supplies. The supercenter format means a broad grocery selection is available under one roof.

grocery.name: Co-op Mt. Lehman Food Store
grocery.desc: Co-op Mt. Lehman Food Store is part of the Otter Co-op network, a locally-owned cooperative serving communities across the Fraser Valley and beyond. Located in Abbotsford on Mount Lehman Road, this food store also includes a pharmacy. As a full-service grocery co-op, it would be a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Afghan Super Market
grocery.desc: Afghan Super Market is a supermarket in Chilliwack specializing in Afghan and halal groceries. It serves the local community with specialty food items rooted in Afghan culinary traditions.

grocery.name: Red Barn Market
grocery.desc: Red Barn Market is a locally owned Victoria grocery chain with eight locations across Greater Victoria, emphasizing Island-grown produce and Island-made products. The Latoria Walk location in the Western Communities features a full grocery floor alongside a Smokehouse deli, fresh produce section, Sandwich Bar, and Ice Cream Bar. It sits inside the Latoria Walk mall near Colwood and is noted on the website as a handy stop en route to Royal Bay Beach or Matheson Lake.

notes.Basic groceries: Website describes 'a large Grocery selection' plus fresh Produce, Meat and Deli, Pet Food, and Seasonal Flowers and Plants
notes.Ice: Website amenities list explicitly includes 'Ice Freezer' for this location

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: Circle K is a large international convenience store chain operating 24/7 at this Surrey location, offering snacks, beverages, and fresh food alongside fuel. The chain has rolled out EV charging infrastructure across many locations. As a 24/7 stop with restrooms, it serves as a practical resupply point for cyclists needing food and water along 108 Avenue.

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: A large-format Walmart Supercentre on the Island Highway North corridor in Nanaimo, offering full grocery and general merchandise departments. As one of the largest retail stores in the area, it is a significant resupply point for touring cyclists navigating Vancouver Island. The store serves a broad range of needs beyond groceries, including clothing, electronics, and baby supplies.

grocery.name: Berezan Liquor Store - Langley
grocery.desc: Berezan Liquor Store - Langley (Willowbrook) is one of six Lower Mainland and Okanagan locations operated by the family-owned Berezan Hospitality Group, a BC-based company with over 30 years in the hospitality industry. The store carries a broad selection of beer, wine, and spirits and is located in the Willowbrook shopping area of Langley Township. Touring cyclists passing through suburban Langley could use it as a beverage resupply stop.

detail.address: 19665 Willowbrook Dr #100, Langley Twp, BC V2Y 1A5

grocery.name: Pedder Bay Resort
grocery.desc: Pedder Bay RV Resort & Marina is a waterfront destination on Vancouver Island about 40 minutes from downtown Victoria, combining an RV park, marina, and general store. The resort sits on the traditional territory of the Sc'ianew First Nation in the Metchosin area and is bike-packing friendly, with bunkies available as a cozy overnight option. The on-site general store and licensed café offer supplies and refreshments in a scenic oceanfront setting.

detail.address: 925 Pedder Bay Drive, Victoria, BC V9C 4H1

grocery.name: Woody's Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Woody's Liquor Store is part of the long-established Woody's Pub & Liquor Store complex in Coquitlam, a community fixture since 1932. The store is known for its selection of BC VQA wines and local craft beers, and offers walk-in retail as well as online ordering with Uber Eats delivery. It operates alongside Woody's Pub and Brunette Cannabis Co. on the same property.

grocery.name: Polonia Sausage House
grocery.desc: A Polish deli in North Vancouver specializing in traditional sausages and charcuterie. Offers a convenient neighborhood food stop for cycling tourists looking to resupply.

grocery.name: Jood Halal Meats And Grocery
grocery.desc: Jood Halal Meats And Grocery is a halal-certified butcher and grocery store in Vancouver, offering halal meats alongside general grocery items. For touring cyclists navigating the city, it serves as a resupply stop with a focus on halal products not always available at mainstream supermarkets. The OSM record was verified as recently as February 2026.

detail.address: 757 E Broadway, Vancouver, BC V5T 1X8, Canada

grocery.name: Day To Day Express Grocery & Produce
grocery.desc: Day To Day Grocery & Produce is a South Asian wholesale cash-and-carry grocery chain established in 2020 under Guruji Foods Inc., specializing in products from the South Asian region including premium basmati rice, ayurvedic herbs, exotic spices, and fresh produce. The chain positions itself as one of the largest South Asian grocery operations in the Lower Mainland, carrying over 5,000 products across groceries, kitchenware, and homeware under one roof.

grocery.name: Whole Foods Market
grocery.desc: Whole Foods Market North Burnaby is a large-format natural and organic grocery store on Lougheed Highway, stocking a full range of organic produce, sustainable seafood, and specialty foods. Beyond the main grocery floor, the store hosts multiple in-house eateries including a coffee bar, pizza counter, burrito bar, sandwich shop, sushi counter, and a cold-pressed juice bar, making it a strong resupply point for cyclists who want a hot meal alongside their grocery run. The store is wheelchair accessible and part of the Amazon Prime ecosystem for online ordering and pickup.

notes.Hot food: Multiple in-store eateries listed on website: WFM Coffee Bar, Burnaby Pizza, Burrito Bar, Burnaby Sandwich, Kikka Sushi, and The Juice Truck

grocery.name: Tudor House Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Tudor House Liquor Store is a wine, beer, and spirits retailer in the Victoria area, operating a physical storefront alongside a Shopify-based online shop with home delivery. The store emphasises wine selection and features a regularly updated new arrivals section.

grocery.name: European Butcher Boy
grocery.desc: European Butcher Boy is a European-style deli and butcher shop operated by European Butcher Boy Ltd. It offers a specialty food stop for cyclists looking for deli products and prepared provisions along the Edmonds Street corridor. As a neighbourhood deli, it may carry cured meats, cheeses, and other European specialty items suited to stocking up for a tour.

grocery.name: Sun Farm
grocery.desc: Sun Farm is a greengrocer in North Vancouver offering fresh produce to the local community. As a dedicated fruit and vegetable shop, it would be a natural stop for touring cyclists seeking fresh food along their route through the North Shore.

notes.Basic groceries: No further detail available from website

grocery.name: Metchosin Country Store
grocery.desc: A convenience store located in Metchosin, a rural area west of Victoria. Serves the local community and travelers on Metchosin Road with basic supplies.

grocery.name: Hardy's Grocery
grocery.desc: Hardy's Grocery is a convenience store in North Vancouver serving both the local community and travelers. Like most neighborhood convenience stores, it stocks groceries, snacks, and beverages. A practical stop for touring cyclists passing through the North Shore.

detail.address: 1127 Montroyal Blvd, North Vancouver, BC V7R 2H8, Canada

grocery.name: Don Chendo
grocery.desc: Don Chendo is a family-owned Mexican food wholesale and retail business that has operated in the Vancouver area for over 10 years, billing itself as Western Canada's number one Mexican food wholesaler. Its Burnaby storefront stocks more than 2,000 authentic products — dried chiles, spices, tortillas, canned goods, dairy, frozen tamales, and ready-to-eat proteins — sourced directly from manufacturers in Mexico. Cyclists looking for specialty Latin American pantry staples unavailable at mainstream supermarkets will find an unusually deep selection here.

grocery.name: Renzullo Food Market
grocery.desc: Renzullo Food Market is a family-owned Italian specialty grocer that has anchored Vancouver's Hastings-Sunrise neighbourhood for over 50 years, now run by one of the founding family's daughters. The shop stocks imported Italian provisions—cold cuts, olive oils, tomato pastes, and more—alongside house-made spaghetti sauce and meatballs, and serves made-to-order paninis and espresso at a community table. Reviewers consistently describe the atmosphere as warm and convivial, likening it to sitting on an Italian piazza.

notes.Hot food: Made-to-order paninis and espresso drinks confirmed by multiple reviews; house-made meatballs and spaghetti sauce also available

grocery.name: 7-Eleven
grocery.desc: A 7-Eleven convenience store in North Vancouver offering quick access to snacks, beverages, and supplies for travelers. As part of a widely recognized chain, it provides consistent, predictable service for cyclists stopping en route.

grocery.name: Lennox Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A liquor retailer in Richmond offering beverages and packaged goods. Convenient stop for touring cyclists needing refreshments. Located in a shopping center on Blundell Road.

grocery.name: The Ruddy Potato
grocery.desc: The Ruddy Potato is a supermarket on Bowen Island. It provides grocery resupply for the island's cycling visitors and local community.

grocery.name: Maria's European Deli
grocery.desc: Maria's European Deli is a specialty deli in Port Coquitlam with a European cuisine focus. The business offers prepared foods and groceries, making it a useful stop for touring cyclists needing provisions. It appears to be a locally-operated, family business.

grocery.name: Northgate Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Retail liquor store located in Nanaimo's Northgate area. Website information was unavailable to verify amenities or specific services.

grocery.name: Starzzz Convenience
grocery.desc: Starzzz Convenience is a small-format Indian grocery and convenience store (1,324 sq ft) carrying South Asian groceries, dairy, frozen foods, drinks, and personal care products. The brand also offers ATM cash withdrawal and courier/package services. It sits in a strip-mall unit on King Road in Abbotsford, making it a potential stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

grocery.name: Grocery Checkout
grocery.desc: Grocery Checkout is a grocery store operated by the UBC Alma Mater Society (AMS), located on Level 1 of the AMS Student Nest building on the UBC Vancouver campus. It focuses on healthy, locally-sourced, and socially conscious foods at affordable prices. Its central campus location makes it a convenient resupply stop for cyclists exploring the UBC peninsula.

detail.address: Level 1, 6133 University Blvd, UBC Campus, Vancouver BC, V6T 1Z1

grocery.name: Creekside Market
grocery.desc: Creekside Market is a locally owned and operated full-service grocery store anchored in Whistler's Creekside Village since 1988, spanning 7,500 square feet of fresh produce, fine meats, seafood, a hot and cold deli, and artisan baked goods. It has been voted Whistler's Best Grocery Store in 2023 and 2024 and Best Customer Service four years running, making it a community institution for locals and visitors alike. Positioned at the base of Whistler Mountain in Creekside Village, it offers convenient one-stop resupply for touring cyclists moving through the Sea to Sky corridor.

detail.address: #305-2071 Lake Placid Road, Whistler, BC, Canada

notes.Hot food: About page lists 'Hot & Cold Deli' as a core store department

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercentre at Burnaby Metrotown is a large-format big-box store carrying groceries alongside electronics, clothing, furniture, and baby goods. The location includes an in-store pharmacy and garden centre, making it one of the most comprehensive one-stop supply stops in the Burnaby area. Touring cyclists passing through the Metrotown corridor can stock up on a wide range of food and household staples.

grocery.name: EverGreen
grocery.desc: EverGreen is a convenience store in Crescent Valley serving the local community and travelers. For touring cyclists, it offers a stop for basic grocery supplies along their route.

grocery.name: Marine Drive Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Marine Drive Liquor Store is a small retail bottle shop situated on the White Rock beachfront strip, described by customers as a convenient beach-front stop with a wide drink selection and notably friendly staff. The store offers online ordering for pickup and has built a local following for personalized service, including sourcing special-occasion bottles on short notice.

grocery.name: Snack Land!
grocery.desc: Snack Land! is a convenience store on Main Street in Vancouver, situated at the corner of Main and 14th Avenue in a busy urban cycling corridor. As a neighbourhood snack and convenience shop, it offers a quick stop for cyclists passing through the Mount Pleasant area. The Instagram handle suggests an active local presence.

grocery.name: South Kelowna Harvest Grocery
grocery.desc: A convenience store and grocery shop in south Kelowna offering supplies to local residents and touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Fresh St. Market
grocery.desc: Fresh St. Market is a BC grocery chain with a strong focus on fresh and locally sourced products, operating a full-format supermarket at the West Esplanade Street location in North Vancouver. The store carries a wide range of departments including a deli with prepared foods and ready-to-eat meals, bakery, produce, seafood, and household goods — making it a capable resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. The North Vancouver location sits near the waterfront, convenient for cyclists coming off the North Shore routes.

detail.address: Unit 130, 150 West Esplanade Street, North Vancouver, BC

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Deli & Prepared Foods', 'Ready to Eat Meals', and 'Platters' as dedicated departments, indicating hot/prepared food is available

grocery.name: Krave Smoke - Vape & Convenience
grocery.desc: Krave Smoke is a vape and convenience store located on West Hastings Street in downtown Vancouver. As a convenience shop it likely stocks basic packaged goods, snacks, and beverages useful for a cyclist passing through. The store sits in a dense urban corridor with good street access.

grocery.name: West Coast Liquor
grocery.desc: West Coast Liquor operates multiple locations across the Vancouver area (Vancouver, Burnaby, Kerrisdale). The business offers both in-store shopping and online ordering with same-day delivery service.

grocery.name: Angry Otter Liquor @ Cherry Lane
grocery.desc: Originally known as Cherry Lane Liquor Store, this Penticton location now operates as Angry Otter Liquor under the Otter Co-op, a locally-owned cooperative with stores across BC. Situated on Main Street in Penticton, it is conveniently positioned for cyclists passing through the Okanagan. Stock options would include cold beverages suitable for touring riders, though no cycling-specific amenities have been confirmed.

grocery.name: Queenside Market;Queensdale Market
grocery.desc: Queensdale Market is a locally independent organic grocery store on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver, offering a broad selection of organic, natural, and conventional products across full produce, meat, bakery, dairy, and deli departments. Its in-store deli prepares hot food fresh daily, including BBQ chickens and soups, and the store prides itself on sourcing from local and organic suppliers. For touring cyclists it represents a well-stocked resupply stop with substantially more variety than a typical convenience store.

detail.address: 3030 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7N 3J5

notes.Hot food: Deli section offers a daily-changing hot case including regular and specialty BBQ chickens, soups, and hot catering items, all prepared on-site

grocery.name: City Avenue Market
grocery.desc: City Avenue Market is a family-owned organic and natural grocery chain founded in Vancouver in 1986, with the Port Coquitlam location on Shaughnessy Street opening in January 2016. The store focuses on fresh, local, and organic produce alongside a broad selection of bulk items, dairy, meat, and a deli now operating at this location. It was voted a favourite local grocery in the 2025 NW A-List and PoCo A-List, offering online shopping and delivery in addition to in-store shopping.

grocery.name: Mary Hill Market
grocery.desc: Mary Hill Market is a neighbourhood convenience store located on Pitt River Road in Port Coquitlam, occupying a two-storey building. It sits in a residential area near the Mary Hill neighbourhood, making it a potential resupply stop for cyclists riding the Pitt River corridor or nearby greenways. No additional details were available from the business's online presence.

detail.address: 1985 Pitt River Road, Port Coquitlam, BC

grocery.name: Sandy's Ukrainian Market
grocery.desc: Sandy's Ukrainian Market is a convenience shop in Nanaimo offering what appears to be Ukrainian specialty grocery items alongside general convenience goods. It accepts credit and debit cards and is wheelchair accessible. For touring cyclists passing through the area, it represents a compact stop for supplies.

detail.address: Rutherford Rd #157-4750, Nanaimo, BC V9T 4K6, Canada

grocery.name: Nesters Market
grocery.desc: Nesters Market is a full-service neighbourhood supermarket operated by the Pattison Food Group, part of a BC-born chain founded in Whistler in 1987. The Summerland location stocks fresh produce, an in-store bakery, deli and bistro counter, pharmacy, and a broad natural and organic selection. For cyclists riding the Okanagan's wine-country routes, it is a well-stocked resupply point in the South Okanagan.

detail.address: 13604 Victoria Road North, Summerland, BC V0H 1Z5

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: This Walmart Supercenter on Saanich Road in Victoria is a large-format retailer carrying groceries alongside electronics, clothing, furniture, and more. As one of the area's major big-box stores, it offers a broad range of supplies that a touring cyclist might need to restock — from food staples to basic household goods. The store is wheelchair accessible and offers public Wi-Fi.

grocery.name: Close to Home Market
grocery.desc: Close to Home Grocery & Deli is a neighborhood grocery and deli in Chilliwack stocking fresh produce, deli items, and household essentials alongside a menu of freshly made wraps, sandwiches, and snacks. The grab-and-go selection spans breakfast wraps with bacon, sausage, or egg-and-cheese through lunch items like chicken salad sandwiches and vegetable samosas, making it a practical mid-route meal stop. Located in a commercial unit in the Sardis/Promontory area, it serves the day-to-day needs of the surrounding neighborhood.

detail.address: Unit 110-5615 Teskey Way, Chilliwack, BC V2R 0K5

notes.Hot food: Menu includes freshly made Bacon Breakfast Wrap, Sausage and Egg Breakfast Wrap, and other prepared deli items described as 'freshly made.'

grocery.name: River Rock Casino Gift Shop
grocery.desc: The Gift Shop at River Rock Resort is a retail shop located within the River Rock Casino Resort complex in Richmond, BC. As part of a large casino resort property, it is accessible to the general public and may carry convenience items alongside souvenirs and resort merchandise. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond on routes near the Fraser River could use this as a potential stop within the resort.

grocery.name: Storm Growler Fills
grocery.desc: Storm Brewing is Vancouver's longest-running craft brewery, operating since 1994 out of a working brewery on Commercial Drive that customers enter through the loading dock door. Brewer James Walton and team have produced over 400 different 'Brainstorm' brews, earning a reputation as one of Canada's most creative craft beer producers — celebrated by Lonely Planet as a 'legendary local brewery.' Cyclists on the Commercial Drive corridor can pick up growler fills, tall cans, or wax-sealed bottles; the brewery's own FAQ notes customers have collected kegs by bicycle trailer.

grocery.name: Westwold General Store
grocery.desc: Westwold General Store is a general store in the rural Westwold community along Highway 97. It serves as a local supply source for residents and travelers passing through the area. Small general stores like this are essential infrastructure in rural BC communities.

grocery.name: Cap's Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Cap's Liquor Store is a cold beer, wine, and spirits retailer located on Harvey Ave in Kelowna, affiliated with the Coast Capri Hotel. It carries a broad selection of beer, coolers, ciders, spirits, and wines and offers an online shop for browsing inventory. For touring cyclists passing through Kelowna, it is a convenient stop to pick up beverages for camp or the road.

grocery.name: Snack Pack
grocery.desc: Snack Pack is a convenience store located on West 4th Avenue in Kitsilano, one of Vancouver's most cycle-active corridors and home to the popular Arbutus Greenway and seaside routes. The shop's name and convenience classification suggest a grab-and-go focus well-suited to cyclists needing a quick stop. Its late evening hours make it a viable option for cyclists finishing longer rides.

grocery.name: Sparkes Corn Barn
grocery.desc: Sparkes Corn Barn is a family-owned seasonal operation that has been growing and selling fresh sweet corn in the Chilliwack area since 1998, running multiple drive-thru stands across the Fraser Valley and Okanagan. The Whatcom Road location is a drive-thru stand at a Shell station, selling corn picked fresh from the field daily along with strawberries, raspberries, and blueberries. All corn is non-GMO and delivered directly from the farm on the day of harvest.

grocery.name: KJA Ventures Shopping Centre & Online Pickup
grocery.desc: KJA Ventures is a family-run general store and freight hub in Fort St. John, stocking branded snacks, drinks, household goods, and toiletries at wholesale prices. It also serves as an authorized parcel handling point for UPS, FedEx Express, Loomis, DHL, Canpar, and Canada Post, making it a useful stop for resupply and logistics in this remote northern BC community. Customer reviews highlight the friendly, community-minded ownership and a broad selection of everyday essentials.

detail.address: 10528 Alaska Rd N, Fort St John, V1J 1B3

grocery.name: Day To Day Grocery & Produce
grocery.desc: Day To Day Grocery & Produce is a South Asian wholesale cash-and-carry grocery chain operating under Guruji Foods Inc., founded in 2020. It specializes in South Asian staples — premium basmati rice, Ayurvedic herbs, exotic spices, fresh fruits and vegetables — stocking over 5,000 products across its BC locations. The chain positions itself as one of the largest South Asian grocery stores in the Lower Mainland, with locations in Surrey, Delta, Langley, Abbotsford, Victoria, and Kamloops.

grocery.name: Hatzic Prairie Market
grocery.desc: Hatzic Prairie Market is a small convenience store serving the rural Hatzic Prairie area near Mission, BC. Sitting in an agricultural flatland community with limited services, it likely serves as one of the few nearby stops for supplies. Touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley backroads may find it a useful resupply point.

detail.address: 10814 Farms Rd, Mission, BC V2V 7G9, Canada

grocery.name: BV Foods
grocery.desc: BV Foods is a supermarket in Houston, a small community in north-central British Columbia. It provides groceries and local supplies to residents and traveling cyclists passing through the region.

grocery.name: Kin's Farm Market
grocery.desc: Kin's Farm Market is a family-founded, 100% Canadian-owned specialty produce retailer that grew from an 8-foot table at Granville Island Market in 1983 to 23 locations across the Lower Mainland. The Williams Road location in Richmond is part of a chain known for locally-grown BC fruits and vegetables alongside global produce. It is a practical fresh-food resupply stop for cyclists touring the Richmond area.

grocery.name: Esso
grocery.desc: An Esso fuel and convenience station in Dawson Creek, a key service node on the Alaska Highway corridor in northeastern BC. The station features an air tower, making it a practical stop for cyclists needing to inflate tires, as well as an ATM on site. As a full-service fuel stop with a convenience store, it is one of the more useful resupply points for long-distance tourers passing through town.

notes.Pump: Website station page lists 'Air Tower / Air' under 'Station Top features' for this specific location

grocery.name: Ross Creek Country Store
grocery.desc: Ross Creek Country Store is a full-service country store and fuel station in Magna Bay on the sunny North Shuswap, operating alongside a family campground nestled among trees near Shuswap Lake. The store stocks groceries, fresh deli, a bakery, hot takeout meals, ice cream, camping and BBQ supplies, and propane, making it a remarkably comprehensive resupply stop along the Squilax-Anglemont Road. Touring cyclists can eat at outdoor picnic tables with WiFi access, and the adjacent campground offers a place to stay the night.

notes.Hot food: Hot case with breakfast, lunch, and dinner items; take-out burgers, pizza, fries, chicken; daily deli specials
notes.Ice: Front page explicitly lists Ice among store offerings
notes.Camping fuel: Store page lists propane fill-ups and camping/BBQ supplies

grocery.name: Your Independent Grocer
grocery.desc: Your Independent Grocer is a full-service Canadian supermarket chain (a Loblaws banner) with a location in Squamish, BC. As a large-format grocery store, it would offer touring cyclists a comprehensive resupply point for food staples, snacks, and beverages. The store participates in the PC Optimum loyalty program and offers online ordering with in-store pickup.

grocery.name: ARC Liquor Glenmore
grocery.desc: Glenmore Liquor Store is a neighbourhood alcohol retail shop located in the Glenmore district of Kelowna. It accepts cash, Interac, Visa, and Mastercard, and OSM records it as a no-drive-through location, suggesting a walk-in retail format. Cyclists passing through the area could stop for beer, wine, or spirits, though no cyclist-specific services have been confirmed.

grocery.name: Galiano Garage, Groceries & Liquor Agency
grocery.desc: Galiano Garage is a convenience store on Galiano Island, one of the Southern Gulf Islands accessible by BC Ferries. The island has very limited services, making any convenience stop potentially valuable for touring cyclists navigating its quiet rural roads. The name suggests the business may also offer vehicle-related services alongside retail goods, though this could not be confirmed.

detail.address: 14 Madrona Dr, Galiano Island, BC V0N 1P0

grocery.name: Hannam Supermarket
grocery.desc: Hannam Supermarket is Western Canada's leading Korean grocery chain, with this Metrotown location being its newest branch, opened in 2025. The store carries over 11,000 Korean food products and household items, serving both the Korean-Canadian community and anyone seeking authentic Asian ingredients. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a full-scale supermarket with fresh produce, pantry staples, and Korean specialty goods.

grocery.name: Red Barn Market
grocery.desc: Red Barn Market is a locally owned Victoria grocery chain with a strong focus on Island Grown, Island Raised, and Island Made products sourced from regional growers and producers. The James Bay location sits in a central, cyclist-accessible neighbourhood and includes a Sandwich Bar offering custom made-to-order sandwiches. With multiple Victoria-area locations, it serves as a reliable resupply point for touring cyclists moving through the region.

grocery.name: Market Ribbon
grocery.desc: Assi Market is a Korean supermarket that has since rebranded as Market Ribbon, offering Korean grocery staples and prepared foods such as dumplings, fried chicken, and soups. It operates as a full-service supermarket in the eastern Greater Vancouver area. A touring cyclist seeking Korean specialty groceries or prepared Korean food items may find this a useful stop.

grocery.name: Convenience Cove
grocery.desc: A convenience store in Abbotsford serving the Auguston neighborhood. Offers everyday goods and supplies to local residents and travelers.

grocery.name: Kootenay co-op
grocery.desc: Kootenay Co-op is a community-owned grocery store in Nelson with a strong focus on local and organic products, featuring a "True Local" program highlighting items made or grown within 160km. The store hosts community classes and taste tours, and supports local farmers, artisans, and sustainability initiatives. A solid resupply option for touring cyclists passing through the West Kootenay.

grocery.name: Royston General Store
grocery.desc: Royston General Store is a convenience and general store on the South Island Highway in the small coastal community of Royston, operated by the Wayne Procter Group, a multi-division Vancouver Island retail company. It sits on a key cycling corridor connecting Courtenay and Comox to points south, making it a natural resupply stop for touring cyclists on this stretch of the Island. The operator runs a network of similar general stores across Vancouver Island under its Omni Foods and Gas N Go umbrella.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Cardero branch of BCLIQUOR is one of 198 provincial government liquor retail stores operated by the BC Liquor Distribution Branch, offering wine, spirits, beer, coolers, ciders, and non-alcoholic products. Located on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, it sits close to popular cycling routes including the Seawall. The store also accepts empty container returns for recycling, which may be useful for cyclists managing pack weight.

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercentre at 3585 Grandview Highway is a large-format big-box grocery and general merchandise store in East Vancouver. As a Supercentre format, it carries a full grocery department alongside apparel, electronics, home goods, and seasonal merchandise. For touring cyclists, it represents one of the most comprehensive one-stop restocking points in the area.

grocery.name: 16th Street Liquor Store
grocery.desc: 16th Street Liquor Store is a neighbourhood alcohol retail shop in West Vancouver, serving the residential and recreational corridor along 16th Street on the North Shore. For touring cyclists riding the Sea-to-Sky or North Shore routes, it offers a convenient stop to pick up beer, wine, or spirits. The store is categorized in OSM as a standard alcohol shop serving the local community.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is part of British Columbia's provincial government-operated liquor retailer chain. This Bute Street location in Vancouver offers wine, spirits, and beer for cycling tourists seeking refreshments. The well-established chain provides consistent service and selection across all locations.

grocery.name: Bold 'n' Cold Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Bold 'N' Cold Liquor is a locally operated liquor store in Nanaimo offering an extensive selection of craft beers, fine wines, and spirits across more than 175 SKUs. Multiple service options — in-store, curbside pickup, and same-day delivery — make it a flexible stop for cyclists restocking supplies. An on-site ATM and cigarette sales add further convenience for those travelling without a card.

detail.address: 6201 Blueback Rd Unit 101, Nanaimo, BC V9V 1M8

grocery.name: BC Market
grocery.desc: BC Market is a specialty deli focused on Arabic and Mediterranean foods, operating out of a retail building on Twelfth Street. It offers a niche selection likely to appeal to cyclists looking for something beyond standard convenience store fare. The shop is small-format and community-oriented in character.

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: Circle K is an international convenience store and fuel station chain with a location on Jacklin Road in the western Victoria area. This location offers fresh grab-and-go food, hot roller grill items, coffee, and public restrooms under one roof. It is a practical resupply stop for cyclists passing through the Langford/Colwood corridor.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Fresh Food Fast' and 'Roller Grill' as services at this location

grocery.name: Bimini's Private Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Bimini's is a full-service private liquor store on West 4th Avenue in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, offering a broad selection of beer, wines, and spirits including rotating craft beer taps. The store accepts special occasion orders via its contact form and offers delivery through Uber Eats. Cyclists on the popular West 4th Avenue corridor could stop here for beverage resupply.

grocery.name: Mediterranean Market
grocery.desc: Mediterranean Market is a specialty food shop in Vernon focusing on Italian, Mediterranean, and European products, with a well-stocked deli counter featuring cured meats and cheeses. The store is known for award-winning sub sandwiches made to order, making it a practical stop for a hot or fresh meal. A second Kelowna location also exists, and the business runs a seasonal home wine-making grape and juice program.

grocery.name: Euro Food Tri City
grocery.desc: Euro Food Tri-City is a specialty European grocery and deli in Coquitlam, stocking an extensive range of Eastern European imports including cured meats, aged cheeses, herring, pierogies, pelmeni, preserves, and a vast confectionery selection from Russia, Ukraine, Poland, and beyond. In-store, freshly made hot soups, salads, pastries, and coffee are available daily. The shop also operates as an official Meest parcel agency for shipments to Eastern Europe.

notes.Hot food: About page states: 'In the store you can always enjoy a hot daily soup, salads, cup of tea or coffee, freshly backed European pastry.'

grocery.name: Nesters Market
grocery.desc: Nesters Market is a full-service Western Canadian supermarket chain founded in Whistler in 1987, now operated by the Pattison Food Group. The Kelowna Airport location offers a broad selection of fresh produce, deli and bistro prepared foods, in-store bakery, pharmacy, and a focus on local, organic, and natural products. It sits near the Kelowna Airport in a commercial area and caters to both locals and travelers passing through.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Deli & Bistro' as an in-store service

grocery.name: 7-Eleven
grocery.desc: 7-Eleven is a convenience store providing quick access to snacks, drinks, and basic supplies. Touring cyclists commonly use convenience stores as rest stops along routes.

grocery.name: West Coast Smokerie Co.
grocery.desc: West Coast Smokery is a South Vancouver neighbourhood deli and specialty food shop located in Champlain Square, operating for over seven years and recently under new ownership since 2024. The shop specialises in organic, non-medicated smoked meats — grass-fed beef, artisan sausages, and halal/kosher selections — alongside hard-to-find Mexican and European imports such as dried chiles and artisan cheeses. A touring cyclist passing through South Vancouver can stock up on high-quality protein and specialty provisions not found in chain stores.

grocery.name: Happy Days Food Store
grocery.desc: A convenience store in Vernon, BC. Offers basic supplies, snacks, and refreshments suitable for touring cyclists needing a quick stop.

grocery.name: Creston Card & Stationary
grocery.desc: Creston Card & Stationery is a locally operated card, stationery, and office supply shop in downtown Creston, BC, serving the community as an Official Office Pro Dealer. The store operates both a physical location and an online ordering platform with flyers and a full product catalogue. A touring cyclist passing through Creston might stop here for stationery needs, envelopes, or basic office supplies rather than groceries or cycling gear.

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: A large-format Walmart Supercentre (Store 3098) in the Guildford area of Surrey, offering full grocery, electronics, clothing, furniture, toys, and baby departments across a two-storey retail building. The store is a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists covering the Fraser Valley corridor, with a broad range of goods from food staples to general merchandise. Parking is noted as rooftop in OSM.

grocery.name: Chevron Town Pantry
grocery.desc: Chevron Town Pantry is the convenience store format attached to Chevron-branded fuel stations, typically stocking snacks, beverages, and basic travel necessities. This location sits in Chilliwack, BC, a common waypoint on cycling routes through the Fraser Valley. As a gas station convenience store it may offer basic resupply options for passing cyclists, though no location-specific details could be confirmed.

grocery.name: Pomme Natural Market
grocery.desc: Pomme Natural Market is a 100% BC-owned natural grocery store offering certified organic and local spray-free produce, ethically sourced groceries, and a large wellness department stocked with natural supplements and skincare. The Nanaimo location has been voted Best of the City by the Nanaimo News Bulletin for five consecutive years and partners with growers and producers across Vancouver Island and the Gulf Islands. It is a solid resupply stop for touring cyclists seeking high-quality, whole-food provisions.

grocery.name: Isabel Creek Store
grocery.desc: Isabel Creek Store is a small grocery store in Daajing Giids (formerly Queen Charlotte City) on Haida Gwaii, a remote archipelago off BC's north coast accessible only by ferry or floatplane. The store carries organic products, making it a notable resupply point for cyclists who have made the journey to the islands. As one of the few grocery options in this small and isolated community, it is a practical stop for any touring cyclist exploring Haida Gwaii.

grocery.name: Angry Otter Liquor @ Riverside
