grocery.desc: Once operated as Riverside Liquor Store, this shop in Penticton's Riverside Village off Highway 97 was acquired in 2023 by Angry Otter Liquor, now one of BC's largest private liquor retailers operating under Otter Co-op. It is one of six Otter Co-op locations in Penticton and accepts co-op memberships offering cashback on purchases. Touring cyclists passing through on Highway 97 could stop for beverages, but the store offers no confirmed cycling-specific services.

grocery.name: Our Root Cellar
grocery.desc: Our Root Cellar is the fresh produce department of The Old Country Market, a Coombs landmark that began as a roadside stand over 50 years ago and is now famous for its rooftop goats. It stocks fresh produce sourced from Vancouver Island and beyond, and sits within a sprawling complex that also includes a deli, bakery, multiple restaurants, a gift shop, and an ice cream stand. A large shaded forested parking lot at the rear of the property accommodates RVs and makes the whole complex a natural rest stop for cyclists on the route toward the west coast of Vancouver Island.

notes.Hot food: Multiple on-site food outlets confirmed in website navigation: Market Café, Taqueria Cantina, Cuckoo's Italian Restaurant, Bakery, and Doughnut Shop

grocery.name: The Root Cellar Village Green Grocer
grocery.desc: The Root Cellar Village Green Grocer is a beloved Victoria institution specializing in farm-fresh, locally grown BC produce at affordable prices, with a full-service butcher (The Chop Shop), deli, bulk grocery, and a coffee bar. This is the Cook Street Village location, one of two Root Cellar stores in the greater Victoria area. Touring cyclists resupplying in the Cook Street neighbourhood will find a wide range of fresh and packaged food options in a walkable, bike-friendly urban village.

grocery.name: Los Guerreros Mexican Food Products
grocery.desc: Los Guerreros Latin Foods is a well-established Latin American grocery and prepared food market that has served Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley for over 30 years. The Kingsway location stocks authentic ingredients from Mexico, Colombia, El Salvador, Peru, Argentina, and beyond, including hard-to-find dried chile varieties, masa harina, and traditional seasonings. Cyclists stopping in will also find freshly made hot foods like tamales, pupusas, empanadas, and chimichangas.

notes.Hot food: Website explicitly lists freshly made Latin foods including tamales, empanadas, pupusas, chimichangas, and sopes available as ready-to-eat meals

grocery.name: Langley Farm Market
grocery.desc: Langley Farm Market is a Metro Vancouver grocery chain that has operated for over 25 years with a focus on freshly picked produce sourced directly from BC farms, including Okanagan fruit and locally grown organic vegetables. The Maple Ridge 207 Street location carries a broad range of products: local and organic produce, fresh meat, chilled seafood, deli cold cuts, and in-store baked goods. The chain won the 2025 Vancouver Consumer Choice Award for Best Fruit & Vegetable Market, making it a well-regarded resupply stop for cyclists passing through Maple Ridge.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A BC government-operated retail liquor store at the corner of 8th Avenue and Cambie Street in Vancouver, part of the 198-location BCLIQUOR chain run by the BC Liquor Distribution Branch. This location may be a Signature store offering an expanded selection of wines, spirits, beer, ciders, and non-alcoholic products, along with knowledgeable staff for pairing recommendations. For touring cyclists, it is a convenient stop to stock up on beverages in a central Vancouver neighbourhood.

grocery.name: Happy Valley Market
grocery.desc: Happy Valley Market is a convenience store located on Happy Valley Road in the Victoria area of British Columbia. Situated on a rural road corridor west of Langford, it serves the local community and any cyclists passing through this semi-rural stretch. Its specific offerings and facilities are not documented in available sources.

grocery.name: 786 Spice Bazaar
grocery.desc: 786 Spice Bazar is a convenience shop on Cameron Street in North Vancouver, specializing in South Asian spices and related goods. The store's name and Facebook presence suggest a specialty focus rather than a broad general grocery offering. For touring cyclists passing through North Vancouver, it may serve as a stop for pantry staples depending on its actual stock.

grocery.name: 大統華 T&T Supermarket
grocery.desc: T&T Supermarket is an established Asian supermarket chain serving the Coquitlam community. As a full-service supermarket, it offers a broad range of groceries and is a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the region.

grocery.name: Private Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A liquor store in Chilliwack operated by Fraser Valley Inn. For touring cyclists, it provides a retail stop for beverages and supplies within the community.

grocery.name: Captain Meat & Poultry
grocery.desc: Captain Meat & Poultry is a BC-wide franchise specialty meat and poultry shop with over 10 years of experience, preparing fresh products using exotic Indian spices and proprietary recipes. The Nanaimo location offers items including raw goat meat, achar goat, and turkey, making it a distinctive stop for cyclists seeking specialty protein. It is part of a growing chain with locations across the Lower Mainland and Vancouver Island.

grocery.name: Country Grocer
grocery.desc: Country Grocer Royal Oak is a 29,000-square-foot, family-owned Vancouver Island supermarket anchoring the Royal Oak Shopping Centre just north of Victoria, offering a full-service meat counter, deli, bakery, and floral centre. It is part of an eleven-store Island chain with over four decades of history and a strong commitment to local sourcing from BC farmers and producers. The Royal Oak team actively supports local cycling initiatives, including the Cycle of Life Tour.

grocery.name: Eternal Abundance
grocery.desc: Eternal Abundance is a 100% organic, fully vegan market and café on Commercial Drive in Vancouver, one of the city's most cycling-friendly corridors. The market stocks an impressive range of whole foods including local and farm-direct produce, bulk dry goods, superfoods, artisan vegan cheeses, and organic spices — with a zero-waste ethos using returnable glass jars and compostable packaging. The attached café serves an entirely organic, vegan, and gluten-friendly menu with call-ahead and DoorDash delivery options.

notes.Hot food: On-site café offers an organic, vegan, gluten-friendly menu with call-ahead ordering available

grocery.name: Ashton Creek General Store
grocery.desc: A general store and convenience shop in rural Enderby serving the Mabel Lake Road area. As a general store in a remote location, it likely carries essential supplies for travelers. Specific cyclist-oriented amenities could not be verified due to website access limitations.

grocery.name: Silver Star Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Silver Star Liquor Store is a 100% locally owned and operated alcohol retailer that has served Vernon since June 2008. Located at the corner of Silver Star Road and Pleasant Valley Road on the parking lot side of the historic Butcher Boys Grocery building — a family site since 1961 — it carries a broad selection of beer, wine, ciders, spirits, and BC craft options. Cyclists on the Silver Star corridor can stop to pick up packaged beverages, though the store offers no dedicated cycling services.

detail.address: 4803 Pleasant Valley Road, Vernon, BC V1B 3L7

grocery.name: Foody World
grocery.desc: Foody World is a large-format Chinese supermarket spanning roughly 60,000 sq ft with ten departments and over 40,000 product varieties, offering a comprehensive one-stop grocery experience. Originally founded in 2001 and headquartered in Toronto, this Richmond BC location operates under its own website and serves the broader Metro Vancouver area. Touring cyclists will find an unusually wide selection of Asian and mainstream groceries at a single stop open every day of the year.

grocery.name: Italian Food Imports
grocery.desc: A family-owned Italian deli and specialty grocery in Victoria operating since 1985, stocking a wide range of imported Italian pastas, olive oils, balsamic vinegars, meats, and cheeses. The shop is equally well known for its freshly grilled paninis made on house-baked focaccia and an espresso bar serving lattes and cappuccinos. Touring cyclists looking for quality provisions or a sit-down lunch in the heart of Victoria will find a well-curated selection of Italian staples here.

notes.Hot food: Freshly grilled paninis, Pasta del Giorno, meatballs, and espresso bar drinks

grocery.name: Valley Sunrise Fresh Foods
grocery.desc: Valley Sunrise Fresh Foods is a fresh-focused supermarket serving the Chilliwack area of the Fraser Valley. For touring cyclists passing through this agricultural region, it represents a community grocery stop with access to fresh produce and provisions. The 'fresh foods' branding suggests an emphasis on perishables and local produce typical of the Fraser Valley.

grocery.name: Cut Rate Foods
grocery.desc: A supermarket serving Stewart and the surrounding community in northern British Columbia. As a general grocery store in a remote area, it provides essential supplies and resupply opportunities for touring cyclists passing through this region.

grocery.name: Osaka Supermarket
grocery.desc: Osaka Supermarket is a full-service supermarket in Richmond offering grocery and general provisions. It serves as a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. The business operates as a retail supermarket with a range of food items and supplies.

grocery.name: Gia Foods
grocery.desc: Gia Foods is a Canadian wholesale importer and distributor of premium imported groceries, operating since 2004 from a warehouse facility at 8288 North Fraser Way. Their catalogue spans basmati rice in bulk sizes, lentils, pure ghee, frozen flatbreads, Portuguese tarts, spices, and snacks, serving households, retailers, and foodservice professionals across Canada. The North Fraser Way location is an industrial-area warehouse rather than a conventional retail storefront, so the practical accessibility for a drop-in cyclist is uncertain.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a provincial government-operated off-licence retail outlet, one of 198 BCLIQUOR locations across British Columbia, selling wine, spirits, beer, ciders, and non-alcoholic beverages. This Burnaby location sits on Skyline Drive and carries the standard broad BCLIQUOR product range. It operates as a walk-in retail store with no on-site food service or cyclist support infrastructure noted.

grocery.name: Stong's Market
grocery.desc: Stong's Market Northwoods is an award-winning, locally owned independent grocery store on Dollarton Highway, a popular cycling corridor leading to Deep Cove. It stocks major brands alongside local, gourmet, and organic products across specialized departments covering fresh produce, bakery, deli, seafood, and wellness. The store has been recognized as a Canadian Independent Grocer of the Year and the 2025 North Vancouver Chamber Business of the Year.

grocery.name: Samz Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Samz is a retail liquor store co-located with a neighbourhood pub at a single address in Port Coquitlam, part of a two-location Lower Mainland chain (also in Surrey). The store carries beer, wine, and spirits and markets itself on selection and competitive pricing relative to BC Government Liquor Stores. Touring cyclists passing through PoCo can stop in for supplies at the attached liquor store or grab a meal at the adjoining pub.

detail.address: 2342 Elgin Avenue, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 2B5

grocery.name: Caribou Creek Market Gardens
grocery.desc: Caribou Creek Market Gardens is a greengrocer in Burton operated by Monica Lange. As a produce-focused shop, it serves the local community with fresh vegetables and fruits.

grocery.name: Day to Day Grocery & Produce
grocery.desc: Day to Day Grocery & Produce is a South Asian wholesale cash-and-carry grocery chain with multiple BC locations, including this Abbotsford store centrally situated on South Fraser Way. The brand specializes in specialty South Asian products that are difficult to find elsewhere, including ayurvedic herbs, exotic spices, premium basmati rice, and fresh produce imported from India. Touring cyclists looking to resupply with pantry staples or explore an unusually broad range of South Asian grocery items will find this a distinctive stop.

grocery.name: Bacayon's Chibugan
grocery.desc: Bacayon's Chibugan is a Filipino food restaurant and catering service in Surrey, BC, specialising in traditional dishes such as adobo, kare-kare, pancit, and kakanin desserts available as full party trays for pickup. The operation leans heavily toward catering orders rather than walk-in retail, with a broad menu spanning beef, pork, chicken, noodle, rice, and dessert trays alongside soft drinks and coconut juice. A touring cyclist would find prepared Filipino food available for pickup but would not find the convenience-store staples the OSM category implies.

grocery.name: Africa Trading
grocery.desc: A deli and grocery shop in Port Moody serving the local community. It provides essential provisions for residents and travelers passing through the area.

grocery.name: Sun Farm Produce
grocery.desc: Sun Farm Produce is a convenience and produce shop located in Surrey, BC, likely offering fresh fruits and vegetables alongside general grocery items. The name suggests a farm-direct or produce-focused retail operation, which could appeal to touring cyclists looking to stock up on fresh food. The shop is situated along 160 Street in the Fraser Valley region.

grocery.name: 7-Eleven
grocery.desc: A 7-Eleven convenience store located in Tsawwassen. Offers basic groceries and snacks as a quick supply stop for touring cyclists.

grocery.name: The Whistler Grocery Store
grocery.desc: The Whistler Grocery Store has operated as an anchor business in purpose-built Whistler Village since January 1981, making it one of the most enduring locally owned institutions in the resort. Named Canadian Independent Grocer of the Year in 2002 and a repeat Award of Merit recipient from the Canadian Federation of Independent Grocers, it stocks local and international products across a wide range of dietary needs. The store also operates the Delish Café and offers small-scale catering including picnic and hiking lunches, handy for cyclists planning a day in the backcountry.

grocery.name: Beauty 4 Ashes
grocery.desc: Beauty For Ashes is a specialty African grocery and beauty products store stocking authentic items difficult to find elsewhere in the Lower Mainland, including palm oil, dried and frozen fish, pap/ogi, kenkey, and a wide variety of herbs, spices, and health and beauty products sourced from across the African continent. The store operates from Surrey and Burnaby locations and offers online ordering with in-store pickup at both sites. It serves a broad African diaspora community and bills itself as the finest African grocery store in the region.

detail.address: B-10671 King George Blvd, Unit B, Surrey, BC V3T 2X6

grocery.name: Fas Gas
grocery.desc: The Chehalis Store & Gas is an Indigenous-owned Fas Gas convenience store and fuel station operated by the Sts'ailes Development Corporation on the Sts'ailes First Nation territory along Morris Valley Road. Open since 1978, it stocks a wide range of groceries, prepared foods, camping supplies, and unique Sts'ailes Sasquatch-branded merchandise alongside local Indigenous artwork. For touring cyclists passing through this rural corridor between Harrison Mills and Agassiz, it is one of the few full-service stops available.

notes.Hot food: Website lists Sasq'ets Basket Products including sandwiches, salads, yogurt parfaits, breakfast bowls, fruit cups, protein boxes, breads, cinnamon buns, and seasonal soups
notes.Ice: Website explicitly lists 'ice' under camping items available in-store
notes.Camping fuel: Website lists 'fuel for camping stoves' under camping items for sale

grocery.name: Government Street Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A liquor store on Government Street in Penticton's downtown. Limited website information is available due to a failed prefetch, preventing verification of cycling-specific amenities.

grocery.name: Top of The Hill Grocery & Gas Bar
grocery.desc: Top of the Hill is a convenience store and gas bar perched at the top of Wildwood Hill in Powell River, strategically positioned as the last major resupply point for cyclists heading north toward Lund. Beyond fuel and snacks, the business has evolved into a surprisingly broad one-stop shop, now offering a deli with fresh sandwiches and pizza, RV repairs, solar equipment, and a showroom featuring e-bikes and scooters. For touring cyclists on the Sunshine Coast route, it offers a rare combination of food, fuel, and cycling-adjacent services in a single stop.

notes.Hot food: Website highlights a deli offering 'great fresh snacks, sandwiches,' pizza, and fresh coffee

grocery.name: Deep Cove Market
grocery.desc: A supermarket in Sidney, BC serving the Deep Cove community. Useful as a supply stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Angry Otter Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A liquor store in Kamloops offering beverages and spirits. Serves as a convenient stop for purchasing refreshments while cycling through the area.

grocery.name: Noor Asia Foods
grocery.desc: Noor Asia Foods is an Asian grocery supermarket located in Langley, BC, offering what appears to be a specialty food selection catering to the local community. As a supermarket-category store, it would likely carry a range of groceries suitable for resupply on a cycling tour. The store is located on 88 Avenue in Langley, a corridor accessible to cyclists travelling through the Fraser Valley.

grocery.name: Mid-Island Liquor
grocery.desc: Mid Island Liquor is part of Mid Island Co-op, a locally-owned co-operative with 18 locations serving communities across Vancouver Island and the Gulf Islands. This Nanaimo location on Haliburton Street offers a retail selection of beer, wine, and spirits from a co-operative that emphasizes local products and community involvement. Touring cyclists will find it a convenient stop for resupply in central Nanaimo.

grocery.name: Izumiya Japanese Marketplace
grocery.desc: Founded in 2003, Izumiya is a 100% BC-owned Japanese marketplace spanning over 10,000 sq ft of dry and frozen goods, housewares, cosmetics, and appliances imported directly from Japan. The in-house kitchen prepares fresh bento boxes, sushi, and ready-to-eat foods daily, and the store also offers online ordering for pickup and catering trays. Bilingual staff assist in both Japanese and English, making it Richmond's go-to destination for authentic Japanese groceries.

notes.Hot food: In-house kitchen prepares fresh bento boxes, sushi, and ready-to-eat foods daily; catering trays and online pickup orders also available

grocery.name: Corner Store
grocery.desc: Corner Store is a grab-and-go market operated by UBC Food Services, located inside the UBC Bookstore on the main UBC Vancouver campus. It carries sushi, sandwiches, a wide selection of instant ramen, groceries, and snacks from local businesses, making it a useful resupply stop for cyclists passing through the university endowment lands. The store accepts UBCcard and Residence Meal Plan payments in addition to standard payment methods.

grocery.name: Twin Rivers Market
grocery.desc: Twins Rivers Market is a supermarket in Kamloops, BC, located near the confluence of the North and South Thompson Rivers. As a local grocery store, it would serve touring cyclists passing through the Kamloops area as a resupply point. Very little detail is publicly available about the store's offerings or facilities.

detail.address: 1420 Hugh Allan Drive, Unit A, Kamloops, BC V1S 1L8

grocery.name: Little Green Apple
grocery.desc: A neighborhood greengrocer in Chilliwack specializing in fresh produce and fruit. The shop focuses on quality produce items for the local community. It provides a convenient grocery stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Denman Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Denman Beer Wine & Spirits is a full-service retail liquor store in Vancouver's West End, steps from Stanley Park and the Seawall cycling routes. Part of the Glacier Liquor group, it stocks a broad range of fine wines, craft beers, and premium spirits with knowledgeable staff. For touring cyclists finishing a loop around the park or passing through on the Denman Street corridor, it offers a convenient stop to stock up on beverages.

grocery.name: Red Truck Growler Filling Station
grocery.desc: Red Truck Beer Company is a Vancouver craft brewery and taproom known for its 'workshop' approach to slow-brewed lagers, ales, and IPAs, plus a Truck Stop Diner serving Southern-style smoked meats and brewhouse burgers. The growler filling station lets cyclists top up a reusable vessel with fresh draft beer to go. The venue also hosts live music and a summer concert series, and has noted events ranging from beer festivals to bike rides.

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: Circle K is a 24-hour convenience store and petrol station on Columbia Street in New Westminster, part of the international Couche-Tard family of stores. It offers the typical Circle K lineup including packaged snacks and drinks, hot beverages, and Roller Grill hot food items. Its round-the-clock operation makes it a reliable stop for touring cyclists needing supplies at any hour.

detail.address: 435 Columbia Street, New Westminster, BC V3L 1A9

notes.Hot food: Website services list includes 'Roller Grill', Circle K's signature hot food program (hot dogs, taquitos, etc.)

grocery.name: Meadow Creek Store
grocery.desc: Meadow Creek Store is a classic general store nestled in the remote Lardeau Valley between Kootenay Lake and Duncan Lake, serving a wide network of small communities along Highway 31. Under the ownership of Mark and Kris Healy since 2003, the store stocks groceries (with fresh deliveries three times a week), local and organic products, beer and liquor, and automotive supplies alongside fuel (gas, diesel, propane). An associated on-site Bakery, Bar & Grill offers homemade meals, baked goods, and freshly made sandwiches — making this a significant resupply and rest stop for cyclists touring one of BC's more isolated corridors.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Coffee to Go and Homemade Baking' and 'Freshly Made Sandwiches & Salads'; associated Meadow Creek Bakery, Bar & Grill offers homemade meals on-site
notes.Camping fuel: Website explicitly lists 'Gas, Diesel, Propane, & Air' under store products

grocery.name: Urban Fare
grocery.desc: Urban Fare is a supermarket in Vancouver's Yaletown neighborhood on Davie Street. It serves as a grocery resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Great Bear Pub & Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Great Bear Pub is a progressive neighborhood pub on Kingsway in Burnaby, offering a modern pub menu with live entertainment six nights a week. It features a games room with Darts Live and a pool table that can be booked for private events, and it hosts regular community programming including karaoke, trivia, and open jam nights. Online ordering for pickup and takeout is available.

grocery.name: Whistler Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Whistler Liquor Store is a community-focused alcohol retailer offering a wide selection of boutique wines, craft beer and cider, and spirits. Staff will source specific products on request and help with selections for special occasions. For touring cyclists, it is a convenient stop to pick up local and craft beverages while passing through Whistler.

detail.address: 105 - 8200 Bear Paw Trail, Whistler, BC V0N 1B9

grocery.name: The Uphill Market
grocery.desc: The Uphill Market is a historic corner store and café in the Uphill neighbourhood of Nelson that has operated at the same location since 1902. It stocks daily household essentials including high-quality meats, dry goods, local farm-fresh eggs, vegetables, frozen foods, and ice cream in summer, alongside café service. As the only store in Uphill Nelson, it serves as a genuine community anchor and a convenient stop for visitors passing through.

detail.address: 1224 Stanley Street, Nelson, British Columbia, Canada

grocery.name: LIQUORFORLESS.com - GLENN MOUNTAIN
grocery.desc: Liquor For Less is a Fraser Valley discount liquor retail chain guaranteeing prices below government liquor stores, with six locations across Abbotsford and Langley. The Glenn Mountain location sits inside the Glenn Mountain Shopping Centre next to a Scotia Bank branch. Cyclists touring the Fraser Valley corridor will find a broad selection of beer, wine, and spirits available for purchase.

detail.address: Unit 102 - 2618 McMillan Road, Abbotsford BC V3G 1C4

grocery.name: Butcher Boys
grocery.desc: Butcher Boys Food Market is a locally-owned neighbourhood grocery store that has served the Vernon community for over 40 years, sitting at the corner of Pleasant Valley Road and Silver Star Road. The store operates full meat, produce, bakery, and deli departments under family management, preserving what they describe as an old-fashioned, personal-touch shopping experience. It is conveniently located on the route toward Silver Star Mountain and offers grocery delivery to surrounding areas including Coldstream and the BX.

detail.address: 4803 Pleasant Valley Road, Vernon, BC V1B 3L7

grocery.name: Simply Market
grocery.desc: Simply Delicious Natural and Gourmet Market is a locally owned Vernon institution offering bulk foods (the largest bulk section in Vernon), fresh local produce, small-batch dairy and meats, vitamins, and a wide range of organic and specialty items. In business for over 40 years and now operated by long-time Vernon residents, it positions itself as a farmer's market with longer hours. For a touring cyclist resupplying, the store's variety of fresh, local, and health-focused products — including Keto and gluten-free options — makes it a practical and distinctive stop.

grocery.name: Canco
grocery.desc: Canco is a Canadian independent chain of gas stations with attached convenience stores, operating under the 'One Stop by Canco' retail brand and owned by PR Petroleum Ltd., which runs over 160 locations coast to coast. This Vernon location on Okanagan Landing Road combines fuel sales with in-store convenience shopping and is part of the Canco Cash loyalty program. Touring cyclists will find it a practical roadside stop for snacks and supplies along the Okanagan Landing corridor.

grocery.name: Shree Supermarket
grocery.desc: Shree Supermarket is a South Asian grocery store specializing in Indian vegetables, fresh fruit, spices, snacks, and pantry staples, aiming to bring authentic Indian flavors to Canadian kitchens. The store operates a Square online storefront offering local delivery of products including basmati rice, fresh produce, and packaged Indian goods. The physical store's exact location is uncertain, as the website URL references Burnaby while the OSM record places it in North Vancouver.

grocery.name: IGA
grocery.desc: A full-service IGA supermarket serving the Summerland/Naramata area of BC's Okanagan, stocking a wide range of fresh produce, deli, bakery, and packaged goods. Located on Prairie Valley Road, it sits in prime wine country cycling territory and offers a convenient resupply point for touring cyclists exploring the Naramata Bench and Kettle Valley Rail Trail. The store operates as a standard neighbourhood IGA with in-store pickup available.

notes.Hot food: Website lists Deli & Prepared Foods, Hand Sliced Meats, Ready to Eat Meals, and Platters as store departments

grocery.name: Punjab Food Center
grocery.desc: Punjab Food Center is a South Asian grocery supermarket on Main Street in Vancouver, offering a wide array of consumer products including many unique and hard-to-find items. The business operates both a physical storefront and an online ordering platform. It sits on a major arterial corridor through South Vancouver, making it a convenient resupply stop for cyclists passing through the neighbourhood.

grocery.name: Donald's Market
grocery.desc: Donald's Market is a locally owned neighbourhood grocery store on East Hastings Street in East Vancouver, operating since 1986 and a multiple-time winner of Best Grocery Store in Vancouver. The store emphasises organic, natural, non-GMO, and gluten-free products, with roughly 90% of its inventory sourced from local BC businesses such as Salt Spring Coffee, Uprising Breads, and Artisan Bake Shoppe. Touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver will find a well-stocked, community-minded grocery with a broad selection of whole and specialty foods.

detail.address: 2342 East Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V5L 1V5

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercentre is a large-format big-box retailer in Salmon Arm offering a full grocery section alongside general merchandise including electronics, clothing, and baby goods. As one of the largest retail footprints in the area, it is a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the Shuswap region. The store carries a broad range of consumables that would appeal to cyclists stocking up for extended touring.

grocery.name: Greens Organic and Natural Market
grocery.desc: Greens Market is an independently owned full-service grocery store in Kitsilano, operating since 2009, specialising in 100% certified organic produce and locally sourced products across produce, butcher, kitchen, cheese, and health and wellness departments. The store is notable for its nose-to-tail butcher shop, an in-house kitchen preparing food from scratch, a zero-waste bulk section, and a health and wellness department staffed by trained specialists. It sits at the corner of Broadway and Maple Street — a well-travelled cycling corridor — and offers online ordering with delivery or curbside pickup.

notes.Hot food: In-house kitchen staffed by chefs making 'healthy real food from scratch'; butcher department also offers fully cooked products as one of its three tiers of sale

grocery.name: Cascadia Liquor Stores
grocery.desc: Cascadia Liquor is a Vancouver Island-based liquor retail chain with multiple locations offering a broad selection of wine, beer, spirits, and coolers, with a deliberate focus on BC wines and Vancouver Island craft beers. The Fifth Street Victoria location is part of a community-engaged business that hosts in-store masterclasses and tasting events. Touring cyclists finishing a day on the road will find a well-curated local product selection here.

grocery.name: Libations Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Libations Liquor Store is a community-oriented alcohol retailer in Vancouver's Shaughnessy neighbourhood, offering a curated selection of wines, beers, and spirits. The store is staffed by knowledgeable employees and hosts educational and social events for locals and visitors alike. Phone-ahead ordering is available for convenient in-store pickup.

detail.address: 962 West King Edward Avenue, Vancouver, BC V5Z 2E2

grocery.name: Amigos Mios Mexican & Latino Grocery Store
grocery.desc: Amigos Mios is a Mexican and Latino specialty grocery store in the Vancouver/Burnaby area. It serves the local Latin American community with authentic groceries and ingredients that may be difficult to find at mainstream retailers.

grocery.name: Westgate Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Westgate Liquor Store is a retail liquor outlet located in a unit within a commercial complex on Dewdney Trunk Road in Maple Ridge. It is a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the Maple Ridge corridor looking to pick up beverages or supplies. The store maintains an Instagram presence under the handle @westgateliquorstore.

detail.address: 20398 Dewdney Trunk Road, Unit 160, Maple Ridge, BC

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A BC Liquor Store Signature Store branch located in a strip-mall unit on South Fraser Way in Chilliwack, operated by the provincial government retailer. Signature Store locations typically carry an expanded selection of wine, beer, and spirits compared to standard branches. A touring cyclist might stop here to stock up on beverages, but it offers no specific cycling-oriented services.

grocery.name: Jaffray Pump & Pantry
grocery.desc: Shell gas station with attached convenience store on BC-3 in Jaffray. Provides diesel and regular fuel plus basic groceries and refreshments—a convenient resupply point for cyclists on the route.

grocery.name: Slocan Valley Co-op
grocery.desc: Slocan Valley Co-op is a locally-owned, member-governed co-operative serving the small rural communities of Slocan Park and Castlegar in BC's Kootenay region. It operates a gas bar alongside its co-op store, making it a potential multi-purpose stop for cyclists traveling the Slocan Valley corridor. Its community co-op model reflects the self-reliant, cooperative character of this remote valley.

grocery.name: Oceanside Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Oceanside Liquor Store is a family-run alcohol retailer located in the Park Royal shopping centre in West Vancouver, offering a wide selection of beer, coolers, wine, and spirits including exclusive local and imported labels. The shop runs a customer rewards program and weekly in-store specials, and can accommodate large orders for events like weddings or catered parties with advance notice. Orders can also be placed online for in-store pickup or delivered via Skip the Dishes or DoorDash.

detail.address: 100 Park Royal S #104, West Vancouver, BC V7T 1A2

grocery.name: Mi Tierra Latina
grocery.desc: Mi Tierra Latina is a Latin American specialty grocery store on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, offering products from over nine countries including Colombia, Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, and Peru. The store carries a broad range of shelf-stable and frozen goods, from traditional Colombian empanadas and bunuelos to Juan Valdez coffee and regional sauces and spices. Commercial Drive is a well-established cycling corridor in Vancouver, making this a convenient resupply stop for touring cyclists seeking specialty or ethnic grocery items.

grocery.name: Salt Spring Mercantile
grocery.desc: Salt Spring Mercantile — 'The Merc' — is a licensed rural convenience store situated directly at the Fulford ferry terminal on Salt Spring Island, making it the natural first and last stop for cyclists crossing to or from the island. It stocks a broad range of groceries, alcohol, camping supplies, and gifts alongside a rotating lineup of goods from dozens of Salt Spring Island producers. An in-house bakery and a ready-made 'Meals to Go' program round out the offering for travellers looking to eat well on the road.

detail.address: #101-2915 Fulford Ganges Road, Salt Spring Island, V8K 1X6

notes.Hot food: Website promotes 'Meals to Go' — 'ready-made meals… fresh, hearty, and delicious' — and mentions house-made weekly specials and Taco Tuesday pulled pork, indicating freshly prepared hot food available in store

grocery.name: Country Grocer
grocery.desc: The Cobble Hill Country Grocer is a full-service supermarket located just off Highway 1 at Cowichan Bay Road, part of a family-owned Vancouver Island chain operating since 1984. Opened in 1999, this store serves the communities of Mill Bay, Shawnigan Lake, Cobble Hill, and Duncan, making it a natural resupply stop for cyclists on the island corridor. It is known for its scratch bakery, bustling produce department, full deli and meat counter, and an on-site nutrition advisor.

detail.address: #33 - 1400 Cowichan Bay Rd, Cobble Hill, BC V0R 1L3

grocery.name: Maggie's Convenience Store
grocery.desc: Maggie's Convenience Store is located on Royal Oak Avenue in Vancouver. It operates as a convenience store serving the local community. The business provides a practical stop for cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Thumper's Patch
grocery.desc: Thumper's Patch is a local greengrocer operating out of a retail building on George Ferguson Way, offering fresh produce to the community. For a touring cyclist, it represents a stop for fruits and vegetables that larger chain stores may not emphasize. The shop's focused greengrocer format suggests a farm-stand character that can be a welcome break on a long ride.

detail.address: 32610 George Ferguson Way, Abbotsford, BC V2T 4V6

grocery.name: Seymour Mini Mart
grocery.desc: A convenience store on Seymour Street in downtown Vancouver. Serves as a practical stop for cycling tourists seeking supplies and provisions in the urban core.

grocery.name: Dickens Liquor Shoppe
grocery.desc: Dickens Liquor Shoppe is a full-service private liquor retailer on Sidney's main commercial street, Beacon Avenue, operating as a local institution since 1988. It stocks wine, spirits, and beer with regular sale pricing and a members loyalty program offering points and discounts. A delivery service is available, and the store is within easy walking distance of Sidney's waterfront cycling routes.

grocery.name: Nesters Market
grocery.desc: Nesters Market is a full-service neighbourhood supermarket on Gabriola Island, part of the BC-based Pattison Food Group chain founded in Whistler in 1987. The store offers a broad range of groceries with a strong emphasis on local, organic, and natural products alongside a deli and bistro, in-store bakery, and pharmacy. For cyclists arriving by ferry to Gabriola, it serves as a key provisioning stop on a relatively small island with limited retail options.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Deli & Bistro' as an in-store service

grocery.name: Mini European Deli
grocery.desc: A European delicatessen in Vancouver specializing in specialty and imported groceries. A neighbourhood deli offering the kind of provisioning and local character that appeals to touring cyclists exploring the area.

grocery.name: Cinnabar Valley Farms
grocery.desc: Cinnabar Valley Farms is a wholesale distributor of premium garden and agricultural supplies, serving the Vancouver Island region with a wide portfolio of soils, amendments, fertilizers, garden tools, fencing, and bird care products under both house brands and third-party labels. The business operates as a B2B wholesale platform with weekday trade hours and an online ordering system requiring account registration. A touring cyclist would find no food, beverages, or cyclist-specific services at this location.

grocery.name: Red Barn Market
grocery.desc: Red Barn Market is a locally owned grocery chain with eight locations across Greater Victoria and the Saanich Peninsula, founded at the West Saanich farm stand site in 2002 and built around Island-grown produce and locally sourced products. The Sandown location near Sidney includes a full sandwich bar and access to the chain's celebrated in-house Smokehouse line — including its famous Double Smoked Bacon and specialty sausages. Cyclists touring the Saanich Peninsula will find a well-stocked community market with a strong emphasis on local food producers.

detail.address: 10330 McDonald Park Rd, North Saanich, BC

grocery.name: Big Crazy Supermarket
grocery.desc: Big Crazy Supermarket (柏仁超市) is a Chinese supermarket located in the busy Number 3 Road commercial corridor in Richmond, offering a broad selection of Asian groceries including fresh vegetables, seafood, frozen foods, canned goods, condiments, and specialty snacks from Chinese brands. The store operates an online shopping platform alongside its physical location, suggesting a well-established operation serving Richmond's large Chinese-Canadian community. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond will find a wide variety of grocery staples here, with particular depth in Asian pantry goods.

grocery.name: Jarry's Market
grocery.desc: Jarry's Market is a local supermarket serving the Tsawwassen community near the BC Ferries terminal and the US border crossing — a strategically located resupply point for touring cyclists on the southern BC coast. Its position in Tsawwassen makes it a natural stop for cyclists arriving or departing by ferry or crossing the border at Peace Arch.

detail.address: 4857 Elliott St #126, Delta, BC V4K 2X7, Canada

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercenter in Tsawwassen is a large-format general merchandise and full grocery store close to the BC Ferries Tsawwassen terminal, making it a convenient resupply point for cyclists arriving from or heading to Vancouver Island or the Gulf Islands. The Supercenter format means touring cyclists can source groceries, clothing, camping basics, and other supplies under one roof. It is one of the larger retail options in the South Delta area.

grocery.name: Beaches Grocery
grocery.desc: Beaches Grocery is a small but well-positioned convenience and general store located right beside Chesterman Beach, one of Tofino's most popular stretches of coastline. It offers a compact selection of groceries and general goods to beachgoers, surfers, and visitors exploring the outer edges of Tofino. For touring cyclists, it represents a practical resupply point on the southern end of town near the beach access roads.

grocery.name: Peninsula Co-op Food Store (Keating)
grocery.desc: Peninsula Co-op Food Store at Keating is the sole full-service grocery supermarket operated by Peninsula Co-op, a 100% locally owned co-operative serving the Saanich Peninsula since 1977. With over 125,000 member-owners and a mandate to return profits to the community, it functions as both a major grocery destination and a community institution. Touring cyclists passing through the Saanichton area will find a full supermarket range here.

notes.Basic groceries: Website describes this location as a 'Food Centre (full-service grocery store)' — the co-op's only grocery store

grocery.name: Farm to Table
grocery.desc: Farm to Table is a full-service grocery store in downtown Vancouver's Richards Street corridor, offering an extensive range of conventional and plant-based groceries, fresh produce, dairy, meat, deli, and bakery products. It operates as both a physical retail store and an online store (currently directing online orders through third-party delivery apps). Its broad product range — including organic produce, specialty items, and ready-to-eat meals — makes it a useful resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the city.

grocery.name: Di Oliva Tasting Bar
grocery.desc: Di Oliva Tasting Bar is a locally owned specialty shop on East Hastings Street in Vancouver carrying over 50 premium extra virgin olive oils sourced from around the world alongside artisan balsamic vinegars imported from Modena, Italy. Visitors can sample oils and vinegars in-store before purchasing, and the shop also stocks truffle oil, gourmet pastas, salts, spices, and curated gift baskets. It is more of a culinary destination than a everyday grocery stop.

detail.address: 2632 East Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V5K 1Z6

grocery.name: Delitalia Fine Foods
grocery.desc: Delitalia is a specialty Italian food shop in the Ocean Park neighbourhood of south Surrey, operating for over 25 years. Owners Penny and Romolo stock high-quality authentic Italian imports including charcuterie, deli items, groceries, and Italian beers, wines, and liqueurs. A touring cyclist passing through would find it a well-stocked stop for provisions and ready-made charcuterie platters.

grocery.name: La Tiendita de Valentina
grocery.desc: La Tiendita de Valentina ('Valentina's Little Store') is a small convenience shop on Kingsway in East Vancouver's diverse commercial strip, operated by Melissa Chacon. The Spanish name suggests a Latin-focused selection of goods, making it a distinctive stop in a neighbourhood with strong Latin American community ties. Cyclists riding the Kingsway corridor will find it a convenient mid-route option for resupply.

grocery.name: Maple Ridge Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Maple Ridge Liquor Store is a large independent liquor retailer on Lougheed Highway offering an ever-changing selection of wine, beer, and spirits as part of the six-location Neighbourhood Liquor chain. The store is notable for its broad range of craft and niche products, knowledgeable staff picks, weekly in-store tastings, and weekend complimentary cookies. Fresh-cut flowers arrive every Friday and the store welcomes leashed dogs with treats from staff.

detail.address: 20690 Lougheed Highway, Maple Ridge, BC V2X 2P8

grocery.name: Zara's Italian Deli & Fresh Pasta
grocery.desc: Zara's is a deli listed inside what appears to be the Granville Island Public Market area in Vancouver, tagged in OpenStreetMap as a specialty deli. Its website domain has been hijacked by an unrelated third party, making current operational status and offerings unverifiable from online sources.

grocery.name: 7-Eleven
grocery.desc: 7-Eleven is a convenience store chain known for consistent service and familiar operations. This Granville Street location provides a predictable, accessible stop for cycling tourists traveling through Vancouver.

grocery.name: SKT Farm Market
grocery.desc: SKT Farm Market is a farm market and greengrocer serving the Sardis/Chilliwack area of BC, operating under a regional brand with at least one Chilliwack branch. As a farm market, it would typically offer fresh produce and grocery staples useful for a touring cyclist resupply stop.

grocery.name: Superette
grocery.desc: Superette is a supermarket in Nanaimo, BC, listed in OpenStreetMap with a Facebook presence under the name SuperetteFoods. As a grocery store in a mid-Island city, it could serve as a resupply point for cyclists travelling the east coast of Vancouver Island. Details about store layout, specialty offerings, or cyclist-specific amenities are not available from current sources.

detail.address: 687 Albert St, Nanaimo, BC V9R 2W3, Canada

grocery.name: Parthenon Market
grocery.desc: Parthenon Market is a Greek and Mediterranean specialty grocery store that has anchored Kitsilano's Greek Town since 1967, stocking imported olive oils, olives, fetas, legumes, and pantry staples not commonly found elsewhere in Vancouver. The store relocated across the street in 2019 and expanded its offerings to include a Grab & Go deli counter with freshly prepared Mediterranean meals made daily. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a genuine neighbourhood institution with a wide range of packaged groceries and ready-to-eat options.

notes.Hot food: Grab & Go page describes chef-prepared, ready-to-eat meals made fresh daily including soups, souvlaki, lamb shank, and whole roasted chickens

grocery.name: Kaleidoscope Fruit Ranch
grocery.desc: Kaleidoscope Fruit Ranch is a 10-acre certified organic orchard in the Okanagan Valley, specializing in apples alongside smaller quantities of cherries, apricots, peaches, table grapes, hardy kiwi, and pears. The farm is run by Devon Scott-Leslie and Katie Sardinha, who emphasize ecological stewardship and a family-scale operation. During summer and fall, a touring cyclist can find their produce at the Summerland Farmers' Market or through local food distributors; bulk orders can also be arranged directly with the farm.

notes.Basic groceries: Certified organic apples (Spartan, Ambrosia, Gala, Pink Lady), cherries, apricots, peaches, table grapes, and other fruit; sold seasonally at Summerland Farmers' Market and through LocalMotive Low Waste Market and Urban Harvest Organic Delivery

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: This government-operated BCLIQUOR retail store sits on Sidney's main commercial strip, Beacon Avenue, offering wine, spirits, beer, ciders, and non-alcoholic products. As one of 198 provincial locations, it provides a wide selection and knowledgeable staff for food and beverage pairings. A touring cyclist passing through Sidney could use it as a resupply point for evening camp or accommodation beverages.

grocery.name: Clancy's Meat Co.
grocery.desc: Clancy's Meat Co. is a family-owned specialty butcher and prepared-foods shop established in 1997, with its Chilliwack location at 45800 Promontory Rd on Promontory Heights. The shop carries fresh and frozen meats, locally sourced BC products, and ready-to-eat meals prepared fresh daily — a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists looking for high-quality provisions. Staff are known for hands-on food knowledge, offering cooking tips and cut recommendations.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a provincially operated retail outlet in Rossland, the mountain-biking mecca of the BC Kootenays, offering a full range of wine, beer, spirits, and ciders. For touring cyclists passing through, it serves as a convenient stop to restock beverages after a day on the trails. The Rossland location sits on Columbia Avenue, the town's main commercial corridor.

grocery.name: Holland Shopping Centre
grocery.desc: Holland Shopping Centre is a long-established Dutch specialty import store serving the Dutch-Canadian community since 1958, stocking an extensive range of Dutch candies, stroopwafels, cookies, cheese, baking mixes, beverages, and giftware. Founded by John and Helen de Haas and now owned by Tako Slump, the shop has operated from its current Columbia Street East location since 2009 and also runs a mail-order service reaching customers across North America and beyond. A touring cyclist stopping in New Westminster will find a distinctive one-stop source for Dutch specialty snacks unavailable in ordinary grocery stores.

detail.address: 141 E. Columbia Street, New Westminster, BC V3L 3V9

grocery.name: The Local General Store
grocery.desc: The Local General Store is a neighbourhood grocery and gift shop at Haultain Corners in Victoria, specializing in locally sourced and organic produce, fresh bread from a rotating roster of artisan bakeries, and ethically sourced gifts. Open since 2013 and under new ownership since May 2023, it serves as a community hub connecting customers directly with local farmers, bakers, and artisans. A touring cyclist could resupply here with fresh fruit, vegetables, baked goods, and vegan or gluten-free options.

grocery.name: Twin Lakes Maket
grocery.desc: A convenience store with attached gas station, deli, and liquor sales located on BC-3A in Twin Lakes. The combination of groceries, prepared food, and fuel makes it a practical stop for touring cyclists needing provisions and a quick meal.

notes.Hot food: Deli noted in OSM description

grocery.name: PickEco Refills
grocery.desc: PickEco Refills is an eco-friendly refill and apothecary store operating out of Chilliwack's District 1881 heritage shopping complex, where customers bring their own containers to refill with zero-waste cleaning and personal care products. It is a distinctive stop for environmentally conscious travellers passing through the Fraser Valley. Cyclists may find it useful for biodegradable soaps and cleaning supplies suitable for touring.

grocery.name: Kokanee Park Marina
grocery.desc: Kokanee Park Marina is a full-service marina and outdoor store that has operated continuously since 1986 on the western arm of Kootenay Lake, nestled beside Kokanee Creek Provincial Park on BC-3A. Cyclists riding the North Shore route will find a convenience and grocery store stocked with sandwiches, snacks, and camping supplies, alongside vehicle and boat fuel. The marina doubles as a community hub, offering boat moorage, repairs, canoe and paddleboard rentals, and access to surrounding trails and the lake.

grocery.name: Esso
grocery.desc: Esso is a branded fuel and convenience stop on Aspen Drive in Sparwood, a small coal-mining town in the Elk Valley near the Alberta border. The station carries Synergy and Diesel fuel and operates a convenience store, making it a practical resupply point for cyclists on the Crowsnest Pass corridor. An on-site air tower provides compressed air, useful for topping up tires mid-tour.

notes.Pump: Website lists 'Air Tower / Air' as a confirmed station top feature; compressed air towers can be used to inflate bike tires

grocery.name: Backcountry Growlers & Store
grocery.desc: Backcountry Brewing is a craft brewery, tasting room, and kitchen that opened in 2017 in Squamish, winning BC Beer Awards 'Rookie of the Year' that same year. The 70s ski cabin-inspired taproom offers over 50 limited-edition beers annually alongside a full food menu of pizzas, salads, and snacks developed by a Red Seal chef. A shipping container patio, a 38-seat Barrel Lounge for groups, and covered bike parking out front make it a natural stop on any Sea-to-Sky corridor ride.

notes.Covered bike parking: FAQ explicitly references 'covered bike parking in front of the taproom.'

grocery.name: ABURI Market
grocery.desc: ABURI Market is an elevated Japanese grocerant by ABURI Restaurants Canada, the award-winning team behind Miku and Minami, situated at Granville Station inside CF Pacific Centre in downtown Vancouver. It functions as both a specialty grocery and prepared-foods counter, stocking A5 Iwate Wagyu (of which it is the exclusive Canadian retailer), Hyoketsu flash-frozen sashimi-grade seafood, imported Japanese snacks, sauces, tableware, and ready-to-eat bento and bowls. A touring cyclist passing through downtown Vancouver will find it a convenient stop for high-quality provisions unlikely to be found at a conventional supermarket.

detail.address: 609 Granville Street, Unit 101, Vancouver, BC V7Y 1H2

grocery.name: Persia Foods
grocery.desc: Persia Foods is a family-owned grocery chain that has served Metro Vancouver since 1996, operating multiple locations across the Lower Mainland. The Main Street location stocks fresh, healthy, and ethnically diverse foods and markets itself as one of Vancouver's most affordable grocery options. Its broad product range and accessible pricing make it a practical resupply point for touring cyclists passing through South Vancouver.

grocery.name: The Market Garden
grocery.desc: A supermarket in Victoria with regular operating hours. Community-focused with active social media presence. Verified as operating as of September 2025.

grocery.name: Sapperton Liquor Sore
grocery.desc: A liquor store in North Vancouver's Sapperton neighborhood. The business provides alcoholic beverages to the community. Limited additional information available due to website access issues.

grocery.name: Burrard Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Retail liquor store located on Burrard Street in Vancouver. Offers beverages and alcohol products to customers.

grocery.name: International News Market
grocery.desc: International News Market (INS) is a small convenience shop run by the AMS student union, tucked into the lower level of the AMS Student Nest at UBC Vancouver. It stocks snacks, chocolate, chips, ice cream, cold drinks, gift cards, and lottery tickets, catering primarily to the campus community. Cyclists riding through the UBC endowment lands can stop here for a quick snack, though it is not a full-service grocery store.

detail.address: Lower Level, AMS Student Nest, 6133 University Blvd, Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1

notes.Basic groceries: Website lists healthy snacks, gum, chocolate, chips, ice cream, and cold drinks — convenience-level grocery items, not a full grocery range

grocery.name: Vessel Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Vessel Liquor Store is an independent bottle shop on Fort Street in Victoria, BC, with a carefully curated selection spanning wine (including natural, biodynamic, and vegan-certified options), spirits, and local Vancouver Island craft beer. The store runs educational classes and a loyalty program, signalling a community-focused approach well beyond a standard convenience shop. Touring cyclists finishing a ride in Victoria can stop in for a local BC craft beer or a bottle of wine to enjoy at the end of the day.

grocery.name: Lighthouse Liquor
grocery.desc: Lighthouse Liquor Store is a private liquor retailer located in Trail Bay Centre in Sechelt, open 365 days a year. It stocks a wide selection of BC VQA wines, craft beers from BC breweries, and spirits from local distilleries alongside national and international brands. Touring cyclists resupplying on the Sunshine Coast will find it a convenient one-stop shop for beverages.

detail.address: Unit 2 – 5755 Cowrie Street, Sechelt, BC V0N 3A0

grocery.name: Aria Market
grocery.desc: Aria Market is a supermarket in Vancouver's West End offering basic groceries and provisions for daily needs. Located on Bidwell Street, it serves as a convenient provisioning stop for traveling cyclists.

grocery.name: Mariners Market & Espresso Bar
grocery.desc: Mariners Market & Espresso Bar is a convenience store and espresso bar operated by Maple Bay Marina on Genoa Bay Road near Duncan. Sitting within a marina complex on the shores of Maple Bay, it is positioned to serve both boaters and cyclists exploring this quiet coastal side road south of Duncan. The espresso bar component makes it a natural refreshment stop for those on the Cowichan Valley's back roads.

grocery.name: Daily Fresh
grocery.desc: Daily Fresh is a supermarket on Quadra Street in Victoria, BC. Its Instagram handle references it as 'Daily Fresh Market Victoria', suggesting a locally branded fresh-food focus. For touring cyclists, it offers a convenient grocery stop in a central Victoria neighbourhood.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The BC Liquor Store Yaletown branch is a provincial government-operated retail outlet selling wine, beer, spirits, coolers, and ciders. It is part of the 198-store BCLIQUOR chain run by the BC Liquor Distribution Branch. A touring cyclist seeking food, water, or rest would find no food-service offerings here.

grocery.name: Market on Yates
grocery.desc: Market on Yates is a locally owned, family-operated full-service supermarket in downtown Victoria with departments spanning produce, deli, meat and seafood, bakery, and grocery. The in-house bakery is known for specialty cakes, muffins, and artisan breads, while the deli runs a hot case stocked with rotisserie chicken and made-from-scratch meals — a practical refuel stop for cyclists passing through the city core. It is one of two Market Stores locations and positions itself as a genuine community grocery rather than a chain.

notes.Hot food: Deli page describes a hot case with rotisserie Maple Hill free-range chicken and made-from-scratch dinners, entrees, and soups

grocery.name: 7-Eleven
grocery.desc: A 24-hour 7-Eleven convenience store co-located at an Esso fuel station on 2nd Avenue West in Prince Rupert. Prince Rupert sits at the western end of the Yellowhead Highway and is a major BC Ferries hub for Haida Gwaii and Alaska sailings, making this round-the-clock stop particularly valuable for cyclists catching early or late ferries. The station also has an ATM on-site.

grocery.name: Urban Express Market
grocery.desc: Urban Express Market is a convenience store located on Johnson Street in downtown Victoria, a busy corridor for both locals and visitors. Its central location makes it a potential quick-stop for touring cyclists moving through the city core. As a convenience-format grocery, it likely carries the basics a cyclist would need to resupply on the go.

grocery.name: GG's Unisex Beauty & African Caribbean Market
grocery.desc: GG's African Caribbean Market is listed in OSM as a supermarket on King George Boulevard in Surrey, BC, likely serving the area's African and Caribbean communities with specialty grocery products. However, the record is sourced from 1985 GIS data, and no current web presence could be verified to confirm the business remains active or to characterize what a visiting cyclist would find today.

grocery.name: Sweláps Market
grocery.desc: Sweláps Market is an independent, community-driven full-service grocery store of roughly 22,000 sq. ft., proudly owned and operated by the Tḱemlúps te Secwépemc First Nation. The store carries a full range of departments — bakery, deli, produce, dairy, meat & seafood, and pantry — along with catering services and a loyalty program. Its name honours the bighorn sheep (sweláps) that roam the traditional Secwépemc territory, and the store is open to the entire community.

grocery.name: Deroche General Store
grocery.desc: Deroche General Store is a small convenience/general store serving the rural community of Deroche in the Fraser Valley, situated along the Lougheed Highway corridor. For touring cyclists passing through this sparsely serviced stretch between Mission and Agassiz, it likely represents one of the few resupply points in the area. The 'General Store' name suggests a traditional country store offering a mix of everyday goods to a small rural community.

grocery.name: Tuan Tuan Food Mart
grocery.desc: Tuan Tuan Food Mart is a supermarket located in a retail unit at 4200 Number 3 Road in Richmond, BC, a busy commercial corridor in a city known for its diverse Asian food retail scene. Cyclists riding through Richmond's flat, grid-like streets will find this stop convenient for restocking supplies. The shop=supermarket OSM tag suggests a fuller grocery range than a convenience store.

grocery.name: 7-Eleven
grocery.desc: A 24/7 convenience store and fuel station on Southeast Marine Drive in South Vancouver, part of the global 7-Eleven chain. It offers a full range of grab-and-go foods, hot roller grill items, espresso, Slurpee drinks, and an ATM, making it a reliable any-hour stop for cyclists needing to restock. The on-site fuel station also sells diesel.

detail.address: 688 Southeast Marine Drive, Vancouver, BC V5X 2T4

notes.Hot food: Website Store Features explicitly lists 'Hot Foods,' 'Espresso,' and 'Roller Grill' as available at this location
notes.Pump: Website Store Features lists 'Fuel' and 'Diesel'; live fuel prices (Regular, Mid-grade, Premium, Diesel) are displayed on the location page, confirming an active fuel station

grocery.name: Lucky's Exotic Bodega
grocery.desc: Lucky's Exotic Bodega is a North Vancouver shop specializing in exotic and imported snacks, candies, and beverages alongside fashion accessories and collectibles. The store's curated selection of international treats — gummies, chips, energy drinks, and novelty items — draws a niche following, and it operates both a physical location on Lonsdale Avenue and an online storefront with local delivery. Touring cyclists passing through North Vancouver could stop in for specialty snacks and beverages not found at conventional grocery stores.

grocery.name: King's Market
grocery.desc: King's Market (康乐超市) is a full-service grocery store at Kingsway and Gilley Ave in Burnaby, operated by Spark International Trading Ltd., a company founded in 2003 that also runs a Non-GMO soy foods factory and a retail outlet in Crystal Mall. The store is best known for its house-made soybean products delivered fresh from the factory daily, alongside a broad range of everyday grocery essentials. A large parking lot sits directly behind the store, and the location is well-served by public transit.

notes.Hot food: Hot Tofu Pudding available in-store

grocery.name: Kootenay Market
grocery.desc: Kootenay Market is a supermarket located in Castlegar serving the local community with general groceries. It provides a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the region.

grocery.name: Dank Mart
grocery.desc: Dank Mart is a specialty exotic snack shop in Downtown Vancouver stocking hard-to-find candy, chips, chocolate, drinks, and novelty food items from around the world. It operates both a physical retail location and an online store with international shipping. The contact page describes it as a 'Rare Snack Shop Downtown Vancouver,' suggesting a curated selection that goes well beyond a standard corner store.

grocery.name: Liquor Quicker
grocery.desc: Liquor Quicker is a retail liquor store in Tsawwassen, BC, listed in OSM as operated by Rose and Crown Pub. It is located in a strip-mall unit near the Tsawwassen town centre, potentially offering a resupply stop for touring cyclists on the South Delta cycling network.

grocery.name: Gaia Grocery
grocery.desc: Originally Gaia Grocery and now rebranded as Neighbours Café + Provisions under new ownership, this community hub at 150 Fourth St in Tofino combines a full grocery store with a specialty espresso café serving beans from Tofino Coffee Roasting Company. The store emphasises locally sourced products and affordable pricing, and also carries Cocofino dairy-free frozen yogurt made by the owners. It bills itself as a community gathering place where anyone passing through Tofino — resident or visitor — is treated as a neighbour.

grocery.name: Jackson's Resto Butcher
grocery.desc: Jackson's Resto Butcher is a family-owned Kitsilano institution operating since 1911, originally a butcher shop and expanded in 2020 into a full neighbourhood restaurant. Cyclists on the West 4th Avenue corridor can stop for a hot meal of smoked and grilled meats, burgers, or salads, or grab provisions from the butcher and deli counter to take on the road. BC craft beers on tap, craft cider, and a selection of BC wines round out the stop.

notes.Hot food: Full restaurant menu includes in-house smoked and grilled meats, burgers, wings, ribs, salads, and vegetarian options; takeout available by phone

grocery.name: More Foods Mart
grocery.desc: More Foods Mart is a small convenience store on Victoria Drive in East Vancouver, a commercially active corridor popular with neighbourhood cyclists. The shop is tagged in OSM as a convenience store, suggesting a range of everyday grocery and household staples. No website content about the business is currently available, as the listed domain has been taken over by an unrelated third party.

grocery.name: Herencia Latina
grocery.desc: Herencia Latina is a Latin supermarket serving the Tsawwassen community, offering groceries oriented toward Latin American cuisine and culture. For touring cyclists passing through the South Delta area, it provides a culturally distinct grocery stop with likely specialty pantry items not found in mainstream chains.

grocery.name: Famous Foods
grocery.desc: Famous Foods is Vancouver's original natural and bulk foods store, independently owned and operated since 1930, now located on Kingsway in East Vancouver with the entrance on Perry Street. The store carries over 1,000 bulk items including grains, flours, beans, spices, and herbs, alongside full grocery departments for produce, meat, dairy, and bakery. The deli section offers a range of ready-to-eat items — samosas, calzones, pakoras, Jamaican patties, sushi, and more — useful for cyclists looking for a quick, varied meal.

grocery.name: Glen Lake Liquor & More
grocery.desc: Glen Lake Liquor & More is a liquor and convenience store situated on Sooke Road in the Glen Lake area west of Victoria. It sits along a popular cycling corridor connecting the city to the Highlands and Sooke, making it a practical stop for riders heading in or out of town. The 'More' in its name suggests a convenience offering beyond spirits and beer.

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: Circle K is a 24-hour international convenience store chain with a petrol station at this Surrey location on King George Highway. The store offers snacks, beverages, fresh food, and hot items from a Roller Grill and coffee bar, making it a practical resupply stop for cyclists on a major arterial route. Public restrooms are available on-site.

detail.address: 1751 King George Highway, Surrey, BC V4A 4Z9

notes.Hot food: Website lists Fresh Food Fast, Coffee, and Roller Grill as store services

grocery.name: Caribbean Market
grocery.desc: Caribbean Market is the leading retailer of Caribbean, African, and Newfoundland specialty foods in Western Canada, operating from New Westminster for over 20 years. Their shelves carry authentic groceries from across the Caribbean (with a strong Jamaican focus), as well as African and Newfoundland products — from ackee and breadfruit to spices, fresh produce, frozen foods, and baked goods. Touring cyclists passing through New Westminster will find an unusually broad range of cultural staples and everyday groceries that are hard to source elsewhere in the region.

grocery.name: Vibe & Bite
grocery.desc: Vibe & Bite is a convenience store located on Main Street in Vancouver. As a neighbourhood convenience shop, it would offer cyclists a quick stop for grab-and-go snacks and everyday essentials on a busy urban corridor.

grocery.name: Dan's Farm and Country Market
grocery.desc: Dan's Farm & Country Market is a working farm stand and country market on over 40 acres near Saanichton, selling a wide range of their own-grown vegetables, berries, and tree fruit alongside an in-house bakery and grocery selection. The market is notable for the breadth of its local produce — from a dozen apple varieties to seasonal corn, berries, and squash — as well as Portofino breads, Galloping Goose sausages, and Level Ground coffee. A visiting cyclist can also stop to see the farm animals (ducks, goats, chickens, rabbits) and use a picnic area on site.

detail.address: 2030 Bear Hill Rd, Saanichton, BC V8M 1X7

grocery.name: Otter Co-op
grocery.desc: Otter Co-op is a locally-owned co-operative with locations across the Fraser Valley and Interior, offering food, fuel, pharmacy, and liquor services. The Tsawwassen location sits along a key cycling corridor near the BC Ferries terminal, making it a potential resupply point for touring cyclists arriving on or departing to the Gulf Islands. The co-op also operates a 'Highwayman' service and a liquor store, suggesting a broader retail footprint than a typical convenience stop.

grocery.name: Kim's Mart
grocery.desc: Kim's Mart is a supermarket on East Broadway in Vancouver. As a neighborhood grocery store, it serves local residents and passing cyclists with food and household supplies.

grocery.name: Crosstown Food Market
grocery.desc: Crosstown Food Market is a neighbourhood convenience and food market on 196 Street in Surrey, BC. Tagged as air-conditioned, it offers a climate-controlled stop for cyclists traveling through the Cloverdale area. As a locally named food market rather than a chain store, it likely carries a broader range of everyday provisions than a typical convenience outlet.

grocery.name: The Other Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Other Liquor Store is a retail beer, wine, and spirits shop in Chilliwack operated by Springs Group, a BC-based chain of over 13 liquor stores and brew pubs. Staff hand-pick the selection and are available in-store to help customers discover new favourites. The store also offers delivery and curbside ordering for those who prefer not to stop in.

grocery.name: SKT Farm Market
grocery.desc: SKT Farm Market is a farm-market-style greengrocer located in a unit at 2369 McCallum Road in Abbotsford. As a produce-focused retailer under a regional brand, it likely offers fresh fruits and vegetables typical of BC's Fraser Valley agricultural area. Touring cyclists passing through the Abbotsford corridor may find it a useful stop for fresh provisions.

grocery.name: Smart 'n Save
grocery.desc: Smart 'n Save is a supermarket in Richmond offering groceries and general supplies. For touring cyclists, it provides a convenient place to stock up on food and supplies during travel through the area.

grocery.name: Kin's Farm Market
grocery.desc: Kin's Farm Market is a 100% Canadian-owned specialty produce retailer founded in 1983 from a small stand at Granville Island Public Market by a family of immigrants who built the business from scratch. Now spanning 23 locations across the Lower Mainland, the Davie Street store offers an extensive selection of locally-grown BC fruits and vegetables alongside global produce, with an emphasis on organic options. It sits in Vancouver's West End, making it a convenient resupply point for cyclists traveling along the Davie Street corridor.

grocery.name: Persia Food
