notes.Hot food: Website features 'Sungiven Kitchen' with named prepared dishes (e.g. Stir-Fried Free-Range Emperor Chicken, Korean Army Stew, Braised Tofu with Minced Pork) and a 'Ready to Eat' product category

grocery.name: Cedar Cottage Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Cedar Cottage Liquor Store is the retail liquor arm of the Cedar Cottage complex on Clark Drive in Vancouver, which also houses a neighbourhood pub and coffee house. The store carries a broad selection of craft, import, and domestic beer, wines, spirits, and liqueurs from around the world, and runs regular product tastings and contests. Staff are noted for being knowledgeable and accommodating of special orders, making it a practical stop for stocking up on a multi-day tour.

grocery.name: 大統華 T&T Supermarket
grocery.desc: T&T Supermarket is a full-service supermarket in East Vancouver offering groceries and supplies to the community. The location is wheelchair accessible and provides a convenient resupply stop for cyclists traveling in the area.

grocery.name: On the Run
grocery.desc: On the Run is a Chevron-affiliated convenience store chain location operating around the clock on Adams Road in Kelowna. The site includes a restaurant, fuel options (94 Octane, Diesel), and EV charging alongside a standard convenience store. Touring cyclists will find washrooms and food available at any hour.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Restaurant' as a confirmed service/amenity

grocery.name: Breezy Buys
grocery.desc: Breezy Buys is a convenience store located in Vancouver, BC, tagged in OpenStreetMap and verified as recently as September 2024. As a neighbourhood convenience stop, it would likely serve passing cyclists with basic supplies. No further details about its layout, stock, or facilities are publicly verifiable from available sources.

detail.address: 2063 W 41st Ave, Vancouver, BC V6M 1Y7, Canada

grocery.name: Jak's Liquor
grocery.desc: JAK's Beer Wine Spirits is a neighbourhood liquor retailer with 10 locations across Greater Vancouver, stocking wine, craft beer, and premium spirits. The brand emphasises knowledgeable, relationship-driven service and offers online ordering with home delivery through third-party platforms. A stop here could allow a touring cyclist to restock beverages, though no cycling-specific services are advertised.

detail.address: 8555 Sea Island Way, Unit 135, Richmond, BC V6X 0A8

grocery.name: Nesvog's Meats & Sausages Co.
grocery.desc: Nesvog Meats & Sausage is a family-owned butcher shop and deli that has served Nanaimo since 2005, earning a #1 Best in the City recognition for meat and deli. The Terminal Park location carries an extensive range of store-made sausages and deli meats, fresh and frozen local produce from the Nesvog Family Farm, ready-to-eat salads, baked goods, and general groceries. For a touring cyclist, it offers a well-stocked food resupply stop with many house-made and locally sourced options.

grocery.name: Wholesale Club
grocery.desc: Wholesale Club is a Canadian bulk and wholesale grocery chain operated by Loblaws, catering to both businesses and value-focused shoppers with a wide selection of foodservice and household staples. The Kingsway location in Burnaby/Vancouver carries grocery, produce, meat, dairy, frozen, bakery, and snack categories, making it a practical large-format resupply stop on a busy arterial route. Membership is available but the no-fee business membership option makes access relatively straightforward.

grocery.name: Alpha Grocery
grocery.desc: Alpha Grocery is a multicultural convenience and grocery store in Abbotsford serving the area's diverse community with fresh produce, international foods, and everyday essentials under one roof. The shop stocks a broad range of categories including meat, dairy, bread (pita, sangak), pantry staples, spices, nuts, frozen goods, and Middle Eastern and global beverages. For a touring cyclist passing through the Fraser Valley, it offers a solid resupply point with an unusually wide ethnic-food selection.

grocery.name: Co-op
grocery.desc: Tofino Co-op is a locally-owned co-operative that has served the remote surf and cycling community of Tofino for over 70 years, making it the main full-service grocery stop on this isolated stretch of Vancouver Island's west coast. As a Federated Co-operatives member store it carries a broad range of groceries and accommodates gluten-free, halal, and kosher dietary needs. The store also operates a gas bar on the same site (currently undergoing renovation).

grocery.name: Buy Low Foods
grocery.desc: Buy Low Foods is a full-service supermarket chain operating under the Pattison Food Group umbrella, serving communities across British Columbia. The North Vancouver location is a conventional neighbourhood supermarket stocking a broad range of grocery staples, produce, and in-house Western Family and Only Goodness branded products. Cyclists passing through North Vancouver can use it as a resupply point for food and household essentials.

grocery.name: Sparkes Corn Barn
grocery.desc: Sparkes Corn Barn is a family-owned, seasonal farm stand that has been growing and selling fresh-picked sweet corn in the Chilliwack area since 1998, operating as a drive-thru stand with multiple Fraser Valley locations. Corn is harvested daily and delivered directly from their fields to each stand the same day, with non-GMO varieties including Peaches-n-Cream and their signature Triple Sweet Jubilee. They also grow strawberries, raspberries, and blueberries, and appear at several regional farmers markets during the season.

grocery.name: Smart N Save Grocery & Cafe
grocery.desc: A Smart N Save Grocery & Cafe in Burnaby.

grocery.name: Teng's Market
grocery.desc: Teng's Market is a greengrocer in Vancouver offering fresh produce and groceries. A useful stop for touring cyclists restocking fresh supplies along Victoria Drive.

grocery.name: Seafair Smoke & Mixers
grocery.desc: Seafair Smoke & Mixer is a Richmond neighbourhood institution with over 40 years of community service, specializing in an extensive selection of premium Cuban and non-Cuban cigars, loose tobacco, and a full range of vape devices, disposables, and e-liquids from brands such as ELF BAR, ALLO, and VUSE. Beyond tobacco, the shop functions as a local convenience stop and offers FedEx and Neighbour Express parcel drop-off and pick-up services. It is located in a strip-mall unit on No 1 Road in the Seafair area of Richmond.

grocery.name: Kitsilano Natural Foods
grocery.desc: A natural foods supermarket in Kitsilano, this store serves as a convenient resupply point for cyclists touring through Vancouver. Located on York Avenue, it's a solid stop for stocking up on groceries and provisions before continuing on a tour.

grocery.name: Malakwa Supermarket & Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Malakwa Supermarket & Liquor Store is a community anchor in the small settlement of Malakwa, sitting along the Trans-Canada Highway roughly midway between Sicamous and Revelstoke. Beyond groceries and liquor it stocks hardware items and sells fuel, and it is one of the very few commercial stops in this rural stretch of the corridor. Touring cyclists will find it a practical all-in-one resupply point in an otherwise sparse service area.

grocery.name: Quality Foods
grocery.desc: Quality Foods is a Vancouver Island-based grocery chain operating a full-service supermarket on Bruce Avenue in Nanaimo. The store carries a broad range of departments including fresh produce, bakery, deli and ready-made meals, baby care, and household supplies. For touring cyclists on Vancouver Island, it offers a convenient one-stop resupply point in the heart of Nanaimo.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercenter (store #1036) is a large-format retailer on Crawford Avenue in Merritt, BC, offering a full grocery department alongside general merchandise including clothing, electronics, and household goods. For a touring cyclist passing through the interior of BC, it is one of the most comprehensive one-stop resupply points on the Coquihalla corridor. The Supercenter format typically includes a pharmacy, vision centre, and photo department inside a single large building.

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: Circle K is a 24-hour convenience store and petrol station on Williams Road in Richmond, part of the global Couche-Tard/Circle K network. Touring cyclists will find a broad selection of packaged snacks and drinks alongside hot food options including a Roller Grill and fresh coffee. The store operates around the clock, making it a reliable stop at any hour of the day or night.

notes.Hot food: Website services list includes 'Fresh Food Fast', 'Coffee', and 'Roller Grill'

grocery.name: Oceanside Convenience Store
grocery.desc: Oceanside Convenience Store is a neighbourhood convenience shop on Marine Drive in Tsawwassen, situated in a coastal community near the BC Ferries Tsawwassen terminal. For cyclists riding the South Fraser or ferry-connection routes, it represents a potential resupply point close to the water. The store's proximity to the terminal approach road could make it a useful last stop before boarding or a first stop after arriving by ferry.

grocery.name: Paynter's Fruit Market
grocery.desc: A family farm market operating since 1919, located just one block off Highway 97 in the Westbank neighbourhood of West Kelowna, surrounded by over 10 acres of peaches, apricots, plums, apples, and pears. Now in its fifth generation of family ownership, the market stocks an extensive range of seasonal BC-grown produce sourced directly from the farm behind the stand. Cyclists passing through the Okanagan Valley will find a wide selection of fresh fruit, vegetables, and herbs, with a you-pick orchard open mid-July through October.

notes.Basic groceries: Extensive fresh produce listed on site including potatoes, onions, cucumbers, peppers, tomatoes, greens, herbs, grapes, and seasonal BC fruit; confirmed as primary business

grocery.name: Fas Gas Plus Chevron Fort St John
grocery.desc: A Chevron-branded fuel station and convenience store on Alaska Road North in Fort Saint John, sitting along the route to the Alaska Highway. For touring cyclists heading north or resupplying in the Peace River region, it is one of the larger-format fuel stops in the area, tagged in OSM as accommodating large vehicles and offering diesel alongside regular grades.

detail.address: 10812 Alaska Road North, Fort Saint John, V1J 5T5

grocery.name: Smoke & Food Market
grocery.desc: A convenience store located on Smithe Street in downtown Vancouver offering essentials to passing cyclists. The 'Food Market' name indicates availability of food and beverage items.

grocery.name: Whole Foods Market
grocery.desc: The Kitsilano branch of Whole Foods Market is a full-service natural and organic supermarket on West 4th Avenue, one of Vancouver's most heavily cycled arterials. Beyond the broad grocery selection spanning organic produce, sustainable seafood, and specialty packaged goods, the store hosts four in-house eateries including a coffee bar, sandwich counter, burrito bar, and juice bar. It is a well-stocked resupply point in a neighbourhood with strong cycling infrastructure.

notes.Hot food: Four named in-store eateries confirmed on store page: WFM Coffee Bar, Kitsilano Sandwich, Burrito Bar, and Juice Bar

grocery.name: Edsa Mart Filipino Specialty Grocery
grocery.desc: Edsa Mart is a Filipino specialty grocery store serving Richmond's large Filipino community from its location on Number 5 Road. It likely stocks specialty ingredients, snacks, and pantry staples from the Philippines not commonly found in mainstream supermarkets. Touring cyclists looking for unique provisions or catering to Filipino dietary preferences may find it a worthwhile stop in Richmond.

grocery.name: Lee's Market
grocery.desc: Lee's Market is a family-owned neighbourhood grocery store in the historic village of Fort Langley, BC, run by the Lee family since 1975. The store emphasizes local and sustainable sourcing, carrying produce, meats, and goods from nearby farms including Aldor Acres and Rossdown Farm. For touring cyclists passing through Fort Langley, it offers a well-stocked resupply stop in the heart of an otherwise small village.

grocery.name: North Asian Foods
grocery.desc: North Asian Foods is a supermarket in Fort St. John, BC, serving as a resupply point for touring cyclists traveling through northern British Columbia. It provides access to groceries and general provisions for the community and passing travelers.

grocery.name: Desi Bazaar
grocery.desc: Desi Bazaar is a South Asian grocery supermarket located in the Renfrew-Collingwood neighbourhood of Vancouver. It likely serves a range of South Asian food staples, pantry goods, and specialty items not commonly found in mainstream supermarkets. For touring cyclists exploring Vancouver's diverse east side, it offers a culturally distinct resupply stop.

grocery.name: Lucky's Exotic Bodega
grocery.desc: Lucky's Exotic Bodega is a specialty snack and drink shop focused on exotic and hard-to-find international products, including chips, candy, gummies, energy drinks, and baked goods. The shop also carries fashion, accessories, and collector cards, giving it a distinctly curated, pop-culture vibe. It offers free local delivery and maintains an active online store, with a physical North Vancouver location mapped in OSM.

grocery.name: Danial Market
grocery.desc: Danial Market is a supermarket located in Vancouver's West End. It serves the local community with groceries and supplies.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A government-operated BCLIQUOR retail store located in the Whalley area of Surrey, part of the BC Liquor Distribution Branch's network of 198 stores province-wide. The store offers an extensive selection of wine, spirits, beer, coolers, ciders, and non-alcoholic products, with knowledgeable staff available for food and beverage pairing recommendations. Touring cyclists passing through the King George Boulevard corridor can stock up on beverages here.

grocery.name: Sumas Mountain Abbotsford liquor store
grocery.desc: Sumas Mountain Abbotsford liquor store is a retail alcohol shop located in unit 140 of a commercial building near Sumas Mountain in Abbotsford, BC. Formerly known as Sumas Mountain Wines, it now operates as a general liquor store serving the local community. It may be a convenient stop for cyclists riding routes in the Sumas Mountain area looking to pick up beverages.

detail.address: 2362 Whatcom Rd #150, Abbotsford, BC V3G 0C1, Canada

grocery.name: Fresh Street Market
grocery.desc: Fresh St. Market Vancouver House is a full-service grocery store situated within the Vancouver House mixed-use development in central Vancouver. It stocks an extensive range of fresh, local, and specialty foods spanning produce, deli, seafood, bakery, and prepared meals. For touring cyclists, it represents a well-stocked urban resupply point with broad grocery selection.

grocery.name: West Coast Liquor Company
grocery.desc: West Coast Liquor Company is a liquor store in Vancouver offering both in-store shopping and online ordering with same-day delivery. It provides a convenient source for purchasing beverages for cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: Circle K
grocery.desc: Circle K is a convenience store and petrol station on KLO Road in Kelowna, part of the international Couche-Tard/Circle K chain. The store carries packaged snacks, drinks, and convenience items alongside hot roller grill food and fresh coffee. Public restrooms are available on-site, making it a practical resupply stop for cyclists in the KLO Road corridor.

notes.Hot food: Website services list explicitly includes 'Roller Grill'

grocery.name: Thu Hien Deli Ltd.
grocery.desc: Thu Hien Deli is a Vietnamese specialty grocery and deli on Kingsway, in one of Vancouver's most concentrated Vietnamese commercial strips. The shop carries a broad range of Vietnamese packaged goods including cured meats (chả lụa, lạp xưởng), fresh noodles, fish sauces, snacks, and Vietnamese coffee. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find it a useful stop for shelf-stable provisions and prepared deli items.

grocery.name: Kluachon Centre Store
grocery.desc: The Kluachon Store & Cafe is a combined convenience store, fuel station, and full-service café operated by the Iskut Development Corporation on the Stewart-Cassiar Highway (Highway 37) in the remote community of Iskut, BC. The café serves everything from eggs and omelettes at breakfast to burgers, sandwiches, poutine, and 16-inch pizzas at lunch. For touring cyclists on this isolated northern corridor—where OSM notes there is no mobile reception—it is a rare multi-service resupply stop.

notes.Hot food: Full café menu
notes.E-bike charging: Website prominently lists 'EV Chargers' as a core service alongside gas and diesel

grocery.name: The Bargain! Shop
grocery.desc: The Bargain! Shop is a Canadian discount general merchandise chain with over 140 small-town locations, operating under Red Apple Stores ULC. The Golden store offers a broad mix of food staples, snacks, clothing, home goods, and candy at low prices — making it a useful resupply stop for cyclists passing through a town with limited retail options. It is part of a well-established chain that deliberately targets small Canadian communities.

grocery.name: Banana Grove Market & Deli
grocery.desc: Banana Grove Market & Deli is a full-service neighbourhood grocery store in East Vancouver, offering fresh produce, a deli counter, and a dedicated meat department with weekly specials. The store operates seven days a week and stocks a broad range of pantry staples alongside fresh and prepared deli items. It serves as a solid resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the Renfrew-Collingwood area of Vancouver.

grocery.name: Ed's Market
grocery.desc: Ed's in Brookswood is a specialty exotic snack and candy shop in Langley's Brookswood neighbourhood, stocking international products from Japan, the UK, Germany, South Korea, and over a dozen other countries. The shop's standout offering is reportedly the largest collection of Haribo candies from around the world, alongside popular items like PRIME drinks and regional Skittles varieties. It operates both as a physical storefront (per OSM opening hours) and as an online Shopify store shipping across Canada.

grocery.name: Cook Street Liquor
grocery.desc: Cook Street Liquor is an independently owned bottle shop established in 2008, now anchored at 304 Cook Street in the heart of Victoria's Cook Street Village. It carries a carefully curated mix of local and international wines, craft beers, and spirits alongside flowers, artisan cheeses, and local charcuterie. A loyalty program, online ordering with free in-store pickup, and free local delivery round out the offer for visitors stocking up.

grocery.name: Sunrise Market
grocery.desc: Sunrise Market is a greengrocer in Vancouver's Powell Street neighborhood. It provides fresh produce and basic groceries as a local resupply point for touring cyclists.

grocery.name: Meridian Farm Market
grocery.desc: Meridian Farm Market is a BC-based farm market chain emphasising locally sourced and sustainably raised products, including grass-fed beef, free-run chicken, local pork, fresh produce, artisan deli items, and a full bake shoppe. The Tsawwassen outlet is one of several Lower Mainland locations and stocks a wide range of fresh, packaged, and frozen goods well suited to restocking a loaded touring bike. The brand's farm-fresh focus means cyclists are likely to find higher-quality local provisions than a typical chain supermarket.

grocery.name: Springfield Bulk Foods
grocery.desc: Springfield Bulk Foods is a locally owned, three-generation bulk food store occupying unit 133 of a Springfield Road shopping centre in Kelowna. It stocks a wide range of dry goods sold by weight — flours, rices, sugars, beans and lentils, nuts, dried fruits, pasta, seasonings, and specialty items like multiple quinoa varieties and organic grains. For a touring cyclist resupplying calories, the bulk-format shopping makes it easy to buy exactly the quantity needed.

grocery.name: T-Bones
grocery.desc: T-Bones is a BC-based specialty meat and butcher shop with multiple locations, including Vernon, offering a wide selection of fresh and frozen beef, poultry, pork, seafood, lamb, deli items, prepared sides, and house-made sauces. The Vernon location supports online ordering with curbside pickup, making it convenient for cyclists looking to stock up on protein-rich provisions. The deli section includes ready-to-eat items such as roasted potatoes and Greek salad made fresh in-store.

notes.Basic groceries: Specialty meat and butcher shop carrying beef, poultry, pork, seafood, lamb, deli items, sauces, seasonings, desserts, and prepared sides; not a full-range grocery store but a substantial food resupply option

grocery.name: Wildeye Beer Store
grocery.desc: Wildeye Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom in North Vancouver with a wide rotating lineup of house-brewed beers spanning Czech Pilsners, hazy IPAs, creative sours, and stouts, alongside a full bistro menu and bar snacks. The venue regularly hosts live music, trivia nights, and line dancing events, and can accommodate private groups of up to 75. A dedicated non-alcoholic 'Easy Series' beer line — marketed explicitly for active occasions including hitting the trails — makes it a welcoming stop for cyclists who prefer to ride dry.

detail.address: 1385 Main Street, North Vancouver, BC V7J 1C4

grocery.name: Hannam Supermarket
grocery.desc: Hannam Supermarket is Western Canada's pioneering large-scale Korean grocery chain, founded in 1998 and now operating six Metro Vancouver locations serving over 4,000 customers daily. The Surrey store, open since 2003 in the Guildford area, stocks over 11,000 Korean food products and household items alongside a broad range of other Asian groceries. A touring cyclist looking to resupply with Asian pantry staples, fresh produce, or specialty items will find this a well-stocked stop.

grocery.name: ESSO JAI-PUSHPA & CHRIS
grocery.desc: This independently operated Esso station on Main Street is a key fuel and supplies stop in Lillooet, a remote Interior BC town along the Fraser River corridor. Run by Jai-Pushpa and Chris, it offers a convenience store, diesel, LPG, and an ATM under the Esso brand. For cyclists on the Duffy Lake Road or Gold Rush Trail, it represents one of the few resupply options in a very long stretch of highway.

grocery.name: Puccini's Deli
grocery.desc: Puccini's Deli is a family-owned Italian specialty food shop on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver, founded by the Pucci family and serving the North Shore since 2009. The store stocks over 150 specialty cheeses, aged in-house salami, premium cured meats, antipasti, and artisan oils sourced from Italy, Spain, and Greece, alongside made-to-order panini sandwiches on ciabatta or focaccia. A touring cyclist passing through North Vancouver will find it a reliable stop for a substantial sandwich and quality Italian provisions.

detail.address: 2027 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2K4

notes.Hot food: Made-to-order panini sandwiches served on 'warm crisp ciabatta or golden focaccia'; full menu of 11 panini options listed on the sandwiches page

grocery.name: On the Run
grocery.desc: On the Run is a Chevron-affiliated convenience store and fuel station on Industrial Road in West Kelowna. It combines a full convenience store with an on-site restaurant, making it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. The location also offers washrooms and a tire air station.

detail.address: 1192 Industrial Rd, West Kelowna, BC V1Z 1G1

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Restaurant' as a confirmed service and amenity
notes.Pump: Website lists 'Air' as a confirmed service; this is a compressed air station for tires, usable by cyclists

grocery.name: Hudson's Bay
grocery.desc: Hudson's Bay is a department store on Island Highway North in Nanaimo, offering apparel, home goods, and general merchandise. The store is part of a major Canadian retail chain and serves as a shopping destination for the community and travelers. Specific amenities useful to cyclists could not be verified.

grocery.name: Konbiniya Japan Centre
grocery.desc: Konbiniya Japan Centre is a Japanese convenience store operating in Vancouver since 1991, specializing in Japanese foods, snacks, drinks, and everyday supplies at its flagship Robson Street location. It also operates an in-store Bon Crepe counter offering Japanese-style crepes, soft serve, and corn dogs. The store has a second location in Kerrisdale and an online shop, and is known for stocking a curated selection of Japanese imported goods.

notes.Hot food: On-site Bon Crepe counter at 1238 Robson St offers Japanese-style crepes, soft serve, and corn dogs

grocery.name: Paddlewheeler Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Paddlewheeler Liquor Store is a retail alcohol shop located at ground level on Quayside Drive along New Westminster's Fraser River waterfront, a stretch popular with recreational and touring cyclists. It sits in a mixed-use development near the Quayside boardwalk, making it a potential resupply stop for cyclists passing through the area. The store shares a name and likely proximity with the Paddlewheeler Pub next door.

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercentre is a large-format big-box retail store in Courtenay offering a full grocery section alongside electronics, clothing, toys, and household goods. As one of the largest retail destinations on the mid-Island, it provides a one-stop resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the Comox Valley. The store (number 3163) is located on Cliffe Avenue, a major commercial corridor in Courtenay.

grocery.name: Nanyang Asian Supermarket
grocery.desc: Nanyang Asian Supermarket is a full-service Asian grocery supermarket located in Surrey's Fleetwood area, occupying a multi-unit ground-floor retail space. It carries the range of products expected of an Asian-focused supermarket, making it a useful provisioning stop for touring cyclists seeking specialty ingredients alongside everyday staples.

grocery.name: Squamish Valley Gas Bar
grocery.desc: Squamish Valley Gas Bar is a fuel station and convenience stop operated by Nch'ḵay̓ Development Corporation, the business arm of the Squamish Nation, located on Valley Drive in Squamish. It is one of several Nation-owned enterprises under the 'Fueling Our Future' mandate. For touring cyclists on the Sea-to-Sky corridor, it serves as a practical roadside stop near the Squamish River watershed.

grocery.name: The Liquor Co. 1977
grocery.desc: The Liquor Co. 1977 is a member-owned cooperative liquor store on Yates Street in the heart of downtown Victoria, one of 10 locations operating under the Peninsula Co-op network across Vancouver Island. The co-op traces its roots to 1977, when Saanich Peninsula residents banded together around shared community values, and it continues to emphasize local products, profit-sharing with members, and community investment. Touring cyclists passing through downtown Victoria can stop in for a selection of beer, wine, and spirits.

grocery.name: Halfmoon Bay General Store
grocery.desc: Halfmoon General is the longest-running business in Halfmoon Bay, operating since 1937 on BC's Sunshine Coast in a location once served by Union Steamship Co. The store combines a grocery section stocked with locally sourced and produced goods, a liquor store featuring Sunshine Coast craft beverages, and a dog-friendly café with a patio overlooking the ocean — a natural resupply and rest stop for cyclists on the Sunshine Coast route.

detail.address: 5642 Mintie Road, Halfmoon Bay, BC V7Z 1E8

notes.Hot food: Café menu includes Soup of the Day (house-made), specialty sandwiches (e.g. Halfmoon Hero, Chicken Pesto, Breakfast Croissant), and baked goods; dinner rotating features Thu–Sun

grocery.name: Olive Us Olive Oil and Vinegar Tasting Room
grocery.desc: Olive Us Oils is an independent, family-owned specialty tasting room that opened in Vernon in 2013, offering complimentary samples of ultra-premium extra virgin olive oils and aged balsamic vinegars in a warm, urban-rustic setting. The shop stocks a curated range of gourmet products including flavoured olive oils, artisan vinegars, sea salts, pasta, and charcuterie, alongside gift baskets and specialty items. Owners Ray Morin and Janet Cody built the business around a passion for sharing the culinary and health potential of fresh-crushed EVOO and fine aged vinegars.

grocery.name: Horsting's Farm Market
grocery.desc: Horsting's Farm Market is an 85-acre family-owned agri-tourism destination situated 2 km north of Cache Creek on Highway 97 along the Bonaparte River, making it a natural stop for cyclists on the Cariboo Highway corridor. The farm offers homegrown fruits and vegetables, a bakery famous for its potato bread and pies, and a café serving custom sandwiches, soups, and specialty coffee. Beyond the market, the property features u-pick berries, apples, and flowers, a corn maze, and an adventure field, giving it a distinct character as a roadside oasis in the dry BC interior.

detail.address: 2540 Cariboo Hwy 97, Cache Creek, BC V0X 1H0

notes.Hot food: Farm café serves breakfast sandwiches (potato bun with egg, bacon, cheddar), custom handmade sandwiches, and hearty homemade soups using farm-fresh ingredients

grocery.name: MB Mart
grocery.desc: MB Mart is a small deli and mart located on Stewart Avenue in Nanaimo. Tagged in OpenStreetMap as a deli, it appears to be a neighbourhood food shop that may carry grab-and-go items useful to cyclists passing through. Nanaimo is a key hub on Vancouver Island cycling routes, making street-level food stops like this potentially valuable to touring riders.

grocery.name: Zando Market
grocery.desc: Zando Market is a convenience store on Main Street in Chilliwack, serving the local community from a straightforward storefront. For touring cyclists passing through the Chilliwack area, it represents a potential stop for snacks and basic supplies. Its Facebook presence suggests an active, community-facing business.

notes.Basic groceries: No website content available to confirm specific inventory

grocery.name: Mostafa Supermarket
grocery.desc: Mostafa Supermarket is a halal greengrocer and supermarket serving the Edmonds area of Burnaby. It stocks produce and grocery items under halal certification, making it a practical resupply stop for cyclists on routes through the area. The shop operates seven days a week with extended morning-to-evening hours.

grocery.name: Barley & Grapes Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Barley Mill Brew Pub in Penticton operates a full-service liquor store — marketed as the city's biggest independent, with many items priced below government store rates — alongside a family bistro and on-site brewery. The liquor store is notable as Penticton's only drive-thru liquor outlet, with delivery also available via Skip the Dishes. The broader brew pub complex features an extensive made-in-house food menu and regular live music events on a patio.

detail.address: 2460 Skaha Lake Rd, Penticton, BC V2A 6E9

grocery.name: Merritt Licensed Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A licensed liquor retailer in central Merritt, providing beverages and general supplies for travelers. A convenient resupply stop for cyclists transiting the region.

grocery.name: Loblaws
grocery.desc: Loblaws is a major Canadian full-service supermarket located in downtown Vancouver's Yaletown/BC Place area at 658 Homer Street. As one of Canada's largest grocery chains, it offers a broad range of food and household products in a large-format store environment. Its central location makes it a convenient resupply stop for cyclists touring or transiting through Vancouver's urban core.

grocery.name: Esso
grocery.desc: This Esso fuel station in Salmo operates locally as 'The Salmo Pump' and is situated at 519 Railway Avenue in the small BC interior town. It offers gasoline and diesel alongside a convenience store, making it a practical resupply point for cyclists on routes through the Salmo valley. An on-site air tower provides tire inflation, a handy bonus for touring riders.

notes.Pump: Website lists 'Air Tower / Air' under Station Top Features

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: This Walmart Supercenter on Hillside Drive in Kamloops is one of the largest one-stop retail destinations in the region, carrying a full grocery section alongside electronics, clothing, furniture, and baby products. For touring cyclists passing through Kamloops, it offers a broad resupply opportunity — from food and camping consumables to clothing and electronics — under one roof. The store provides free in-store WiFi according to OSM tags.

grocery.name: Daniel's Market
grocery.desc: Daniel's Market is a convenience store in Sooke, a community on the south edge of Vancouver Island. It maintains an active social media presence. Touring cyclists passing through may find it useful for quick supply stops.

grocery.name: Aggarwal Grocery Hub
grocery.desc: Aggarwal Grocery Hub is a South Asian grocery store specializing in fresh produce, lentils, grains, spices, and snacks such as namkeen, bhujia, and mithai. This King George Boulevard location is the chain's second store, with daily fresh shipments from locally sourced and trusted-farmer suppliers. It offers a wide range of South Asian staples that would be difficult to find at a conventional supermarket, making it a distinctive resupply option for cyclists in the Surrey area.

grocery.name: Greendale Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Greendale Liquor Store is a retail liquor shop on Yale Road (off Highway 1 Exit 109) in Chilliwack, operated by the Liquor Giant Group with six Fraser Valley locations. The store carries spirits, wine, BC craft beer, and ready-to-drink products, and offers bulk ordering for events as well as third-party delivery. It is a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the Greendale area who need to resupply on beverages.

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: A large-format Walmart Supercentre located in Richmond, BC, offering a full grocery department alongside electronics, clothing, toys, and household goods. As a three-level Supercentre it is one of the larger Walmart formats in the Lower Mainland, giving touring cyclists access to a wide range of resupply options under one roof. Accepts cash, credit, and debit.

grocery.name: Jak's
grocery.desc: Jak's (formerly Moonrakers Cold Beere & Wine Store) is a neighbourhood liquor retail chain with 10 locations across Greater Vancouver, carrying craft beer, wine, and premium spirits. The New Westminster store is one of ten, with in-store browsing supported by knowledgeable staff trained to make personalised recommendations. Online ordering with home delivery is also available through the JAK's website.

grocery.name: Castle Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Castle Liquor Store is a retail alcohol shop located in Sooke, a popular stop along Vancouver Island's coastal cycling routes. Touring cyclists passing through Sooke may find it a convenient place to pick up beverages for the road or camp.

grocery.name: Mahtot East Africa Market
grocery.desc: Mahtot East Africa Market is an East African-focused supermarket in North Vancouver, recently rebranded from the formerly Persian-oriented Baanou Supermarket. Situated on Sixth Street, it offers touring cyclists a convenient urban provisioning stop with a specialty grocery selection not commonly found at mainstream stores. The neighbourhood location makes it a useful resupply point for riders moving through the North Shore.

grocery.name: Vancouver European Deli
grocery.desc: Vancouver European Deli is a specialty deli shop located on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End neighbourhood. It offers European deli products in a wheelchair-accessible space, making it a potential resupply stop for cyclists riding through the area.

grocery.name: Well Seasoned
grocery.desc: Well Seasoned is a gourmet specialty food store in Langley offering artisan cheeses, charcuterie, deli items, specialty pantry staples, and a range of house-made gourmet-to-go meals and soups. The store also runs a regular calendar of cooking classes and offers catering services, making it a destination rather than a routine stop. Touring cyclists passing through Langley can pick up specialty provisions — nuts, crackers, snacks, pasta, and housemade prepared foods — at this locally rooted shop.

grocery.name: Duso's Italia
grocery.desc: Duso's is a Vancouver institution founded in the late 1960s when Italian immigrant Mauro Duso set up one of the original stalls at the now-iconic Granville Island Market, selling handmade pasta and authentic family-recipe sauces. The flagship Granville Island shop remains the original retail location and carries more than twenty varieties of specialty filled pasta alongside a range of fresh sauces, all made with locally sourced Canadian ingredients. For cyclists exploring Granville Island, it is a well-established destination for premium take-home Italian food.

grocery.name: LIQUORFORLESS.com - MARSHALL / RIVERSIDE
grocery.desc: Liquor For Less is a Fraser Valley independent liquor retailer competing on price against government stores, with six locations across Abbotsford and Langley. The Marshall/Riverside location sits next to a Dollarama in a strip mall setting. A touring cyclist could stop to purchase beer, wine, or spirits for the road or camp.

detail.address: Unit 1 - 34252 Marshall Road, Abbotsford BC V2S 1L9

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercentre is a large-format retail store in Chilliwack's Eagle Landing area, offering a full grocery department alongside general merchandise including electronics, clothing, and household goods. As a supercentre format, it is one of the most comprehensive one-stop shopping destinations in the region for a touring cyclist needing to restock supplies. The OSM record indicates 24/7 operation.

grocery.name: The Well Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Well Liquor Store is a liquor retail shop located in Nanaimo, BC, in what appears to be a unit within a commercial complex (unit 1 per OSM). As a local liquor store, it offers a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking to pick up beverages along their route through the Nanaimo area.

grocery.name: Anar Food and Grocery
grocery.desc: Anar Food and Grocery is a family-run Persian grocery market and takeaway restaurant that has been operating in Victoria since 2014. The store carries a broad selection of Middle Eastern and Persian pantry staples — dried fruits, nuts, fresh dates, olive oil, and specialty ingredients — alongside a deli counter stocked with house-made dips and spreads. The attached takeaway kitchen turns out authentic Persian dishes such as kebabs and slow-cooked stews, with third-party delivery also available.

detail.address: 3949 Quadra St A, Victoria, BC V8X 1J5

notes.Hot food: Website states takeaway restaurant offers 'a wide range of delicious home cooked meals' including kebabs and Persian stews; delivery available via Skip the Dishes, Uber Eats, and DoorDash

grocery.name: Lulu Island Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Lulu Island Liquor Store is a retail alcohol shop located in Richmond on Lulu Island, the main landmass of the municipality. For touring cyclists passing through the Richmond area, it offers a convenient stop to pick up beverages. The OSM record notes no drive-through, suggesting a standard walk-in retail format.

grocery.name: Chris' Flowers
grocery.desc: A convenience store located on East Columbia Street in North Vancouver. Specific amenities and services could not be verified due to website access failure (401 error) during validation.

grocery.name: Swans Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Swans Liquor Store is the retail bottle shop of the historic Swans complex, a Victoria waterfront institution since 1989 that also encompasses a craft brewery, pub, and boutique hotel. Located at 514 Pandora Ave near the Inner Harbour, the store stocks beer, wine, and spirits including Swans' own range of locally brewed craft lagers, ales, and IPAs. Touring cyclists passing through downtown Victoria can resupply with local BC craft beverages from a well-established neighbourhood landmark.

grocery.name: Harris Green Liquor Express
grocery.desc: Harris Green Liquor is a locally-owned, family-run neighbourhood liquor store in the heart of Victoria's Harris Green district, in business since 2005. It carries a broad selection of BC craft beers, international spirits, wine, ciders, coolers, and non-alcoholic beverages. A touring cyclist moving through Victoria's urban core could stop here to restock on drinks.

grocery.name: Country Grocer
grocery.desc: Country Grocer is a family-owned Vancouver Island supermarket chain with over 40 years of history, emphasizing locally sourced BC products and strong community ties. The Ladysmith location sits in the heart of town across from Aggie Fields, offering a full supermarket selection plus deli, sushi, bakery, and seafood platters prepared fresh to order. It is part of an eleven-store independent Island chain that prioritizes relationships with local farmers and producers.

grocery.name: Express News
grocery.desc: Express News Convenience is a BC-born convenience store franchise founded in 1998, now operating 30+ locations across British Columbia. This Burnaby location sits at unit P25-04 on Lougheed Highway — the compact store format (typically 200–1,500 sq ft) is intentionally placed in high-traffic hubs like SkyTrain stations and malls for quick, in-and-out stops. Cyclists can expect grab-and-go essentials: cold drinks, fresh bean-to-cup coffee, snacks, sandwiches, pastries, and lottery tickets.

notes.Hot food: Website specifically mentions 'fresh bean-to-cup coffee, sandwiches & pastries' as grab-and-go food

grocery.name: Liquor Plus
grocery.desc: Liquor Plus is a Vancouver Island–owned chain of full-service liquor stores founded in 2002, with eight locations across the island including this Nanaimo outpost. The stores carry an extensive selection of local and international wines, spirits, beer, and cider, with a noted emphasis on craft beer and everyday competitive pricing. For touring cyclists, it is a convenient stop to stock up on beverages in central Nanaimo.

grocery.name: Lake Country Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Lake Country Liquor Store is a full-service retail liquor shop located between Kelowna and Vernon in Lake Country, BC, stocking an extensive range of craft and import beers, wines, spirits, coolers, and ciders. Staff are described as well-trained and knowledgeable, and the store offers case lot pricing and price-matching against other local retailers. For touring cyclists traveling the Okanagan corridor, it serves as a convenient stop for beverages and supplies.

detail.address: 72-9522 Main Street, Lake Country, BC V4V 2L9

grocery.name: Nesters Market
grocery.desc: Nesters Market is Whistler's original full-service grocery store, founded in 1987 and widely regarded as 'Where the Locals Shop' in this mountain resort community. It carries a broad range of fresh produce, natural and organic products, and specialty items alongside an in-store bakery, deli & bistro, and pharmacy. For touring cyclists riding the Sea-to-Sky corridor, it represents one of the most complete resupply options in the area.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Deli & Bistro' as an in-store service, indicating prepared hot food availability

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a government-operated retail outlet run by BC's Liquor Distribution Branch, one of 198 locations across the province selling wine, beer, spirits, and coolers. This East Vancouver location on Kingsway serves a busy commercial corridor. It is a standard retail shop with no food service or cyclist-specific services evident.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A provincial government-operated retail liquor store in Victoria's Cedar Hill neighbourhood, carrying wine, spirits, beer, coolers, and ciders. Part of the BCLIQUOR chain of 198 stores across British Columbia, it offers a broad product selection including BC craft beers that might appeal to a touring cyclist looking to pick up local beverages. Staff are described as knowledgeable on product recommendations.

grocery.name: Karl's Meat Market
grocery.desc: Karl's Meat Market is a deli and butcher shop established in 1966, offering fresh meat and deli products to the local community. It provides a food resource for residents and travelers seeking quality provisions beyond standard convenience stores.

detail.address: 2621 W Railway St, Abbotsford, BC V2S 2E6, Canada

grocery.name: Wings Grocery
grocery.desc: Wings Grocery is a Nelson institution, first established in 1969 by the Wings family and rebuilt at 371 Baker Street after a 1976 fire. Now operated as a convenience store under new ownership, it has expanded into an online novelty and goods e-commerce platform while maintaining a physical storefront on Nelson's main commercial strip. Cyclists passing through Nelson's Baker Street corridor will find this long-standing local shop a potential stop for convenience items.

grocery.name: Matchi African Market
grocery.desc: Matchi African Market is a convenience store specializing in African groceries and products. It serves the local Vancouver community with culturally-focused supplies and goods.

grocery.name: M.A.M. Convenience World
grocery.desc: M.A.M. Convenience World is a convenience store on Aberdeen Road in Prince George, BC. It provides quick access to basic groceries and supplies for local residents and touring cyclists passing through the area.

grocery.name: The Britannia Beach General Store
grocery.desc: The Britannia General Store is a boutique community hub in Britannia Beach, operated by The Boatshed Group and designed with a nod to the area's historic copper mining heritage through rustic décor and vintage touches. It stocks fresh groceries, liquor, handmade pizza, and local goods, making it a convenient one-stop resupply point on the Sea-to-Sky corridor between Vancouver and Whistler. Touring cyclists riding Highway 99 will find it right in the heart of Britannia Beach village.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'freshly baked pizza' and 'handmade pizza' as a featured product

grocery.name: Fairway Market
grocery.desc: Fairway Market is a Vancouver Island–owned grocery chain founded in 1963, now operating 9 locations including this Langford store at Goldstream Village. The store carries a broad range of departments — deli, meat, produce, dairy, bakery, floral, an Asian kitchen, and a sushi counter — making it a well-stocked resupply point for touring cyclists. The company emphasizes local BC and Island producers alongside an extensive international product selection.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Asian Kitchen' and 'Sushi Village' as in-store departments, indicating prepared and hot food service

grocery.name: Seymour's Pub & Grill
grocery.desc: Seymour's Pub is a North Shore community pub known for 22 beers on draught spanning local craft, domestic, and international selections, plus a scratch kitchen that makes its sauces and dressings fresh daily. The venue hosts live music, DJ nights, and broadcasts major sporting events on fifteen screens throughout the bar. A free parking lot with overnight allowance makes it accessible, and a twice-daily happy hour draws a regular local crowd.

detail.address: 720 Old Lillooet Road, North Vancouver, BC V7J 2H5

grocery.name: SunFarm International Specialty Foods
grocery.desc: SunFarm International Specialty Foods is a specialty grocery store in the Metro Vancouver area stocking international and ethnic food products. The focus on specialty and international offerings suggests a diverse product range that may appeal to cyclists looking for unique resupply options. Beyond the OSM tagging, no further details about the store's layout or offerings could be confirmed.

detail.address: 10116 Whalley Blvd, Surrey, BC V3T 4G1, Canada

grocery.name: Choices Market
grocery.desc: Choices Market is a 100% BC-owned and operated natural and organic grocery chain that has anchored the Kitsilano neighbourhood since 1990. The store specialises in local, organic, and specialty food items—including thousands of Canadian-sourced products—making it a well-stocked resupply point for cyclists travelling through Vancouver's west side. An in-store Nutrition Team of Registered Dietitians offers free personalised consultations and guided store tours.

grocery.name: BK Market
grocery.desc: BK Market is a greengrocer on East Hastings Street in Vancouver's Hastings-Sunrise neighbourhood, stocking fresh fruits and vegetables. The shop sits on a busy arterial road that connects several residential and commercial areas, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through east Vancouver. As a produce-focused shop, it offers cyclists an opportunity to restock on fresh food mid-route.

grocery.name: Osaka - Park Royal
grocery.desc: Osaka is a supermarket in the Park Royal shopping center in North Vancouver. It offers basic groceries and supplies for touring cyclists needing to resupply.

grocery.name: General Store
grocery.desc: The General Store is a full-service convenience grocery inside Panorama Mountain Resort's Toby Creek Lodge, stocking dry goods, fresh produce, dairy, meat, and specialty gifts. As an official BC Liquor Agency, it also carries beer, wine, and spirits at standard BC prices. It serves as the primary provisioning stop for guests and visitors in the remote Panorama village in the Kootenay Rockies.

grocery.name: Cherryville Emporium
grocery.desc: Cherryville Emporium is a convenience store and fuel stop in rural Cherryville. It provides basic supplies and fuel to travelers passing through this small community, including cycling tourists.

grocery.name: Country Grocer
grocery.desc: Country Grocer Salt Spring Island is a 28,000-square-foot destination market conveniently located at Ganges Village Marketplace in the heart of Ganges, serving both locals and visitors since the chain's founding in the 1980s. The store features a vibrant produce section with organic and locally grown selections, full deli, bakery, sushi, and meat/seafood departments, and an on-site pharmacy. An in-store Café offers fresh coffee, hot breakfast sandwiches, and casual lunch — useful for cyclists restocking or refuelling in Ganges.

notes.Hot food: In-store Café described as offering fresh coffee, hot breakfast sandwiches, and casual lunch

grocery.name: Jasmine Mediterranean Foods
grocery.desc: Jasmine Mediterranean Foods is a neighborhood grocery and halal butcher shop on Main Street in Vancouver, stocking fresh halal meats alongside packaged Mediterranean and Middle Eastern specialty foods. The business also runs a separate wholesale distribution operation at a different Fraser Street address. Cyclists riding Main Street will find it a useful resupply stop for specialty pantry items, teas, and packaged goods with a Middle Eastern focus.

grocery.name: Koji Mini Mart
grocery.desc: Koji Mini Mart is a small neighbourhood grocery store in Richmond's Steveston area, near the southern tip of Lulu Island. It accepts cash, credit, and debit cards, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. Its location in a quiet residential corner of Richmond puts it near the popular Steveston waterfront cycling routes.

grocery.name: Select Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Select Liquor Store is an independent liquor retailer in Port Coquitlam that has been serving customers since 2002. The shop carries an extensive selection of beer, wine, cider, cocktails, and spirits, and staff will attempt to source specific products on request. Online ordering with curbside pickup is also available for customers who prefer a quick stop.

detail.address: 1760 Kingsway Avenue, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C1S5

grocery.name: Long Beach Market
grocery.desc: Long Beach Market is a convenience and general store in Tofino operated by The Wayne Procter Group as part of their Vancouver Island General Stores division. In addition to convenience goods, it sells gasoline (regular, mid-grade, premium, and diesel) and propane in both auto and cylinder formats. Situated in one of BC's most popular cycling destinations on the west coast of Vancouver Island, it serves as a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists heading into or out of the Tofino area.

notes.Camping fuel: Website listing explicitly states 'Auto and cylinder propane' available

grocery.name: Tatak Pinoy Filipino Store
grocery.desc: Tatak Pinoy Filipino Store is a Filipino specialty grocer on Joyce Street serving Vancouver's local community. It stocks authentic Filipino groceries, foods, and ingredients not typically found in mainstream supermarkets. A touring cyclist can access a neighborhood grocery option for culturally-specific supplies and refreshments.

grocery.name: Cambie Plaza Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Cambie Plaza Liquor Store is a retail alcohol shop situated in the Cambie Plaza area of Richmond, BC. It offers beer, wine, and spirits for purchase with no drive-through service. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's central corridors may find it a convenient stop for resupply.

grocery.name: 1933 Liquor
grocery.desc: 1933 Liquor Co. is a neighbourhood liquor store on Great Northern Way in Vancouver, stocking wine, beer, and spirits from local and international producers alongside a growing selection of non-alcoholic beverages. The store regularly hosts in-store events including whiskey masterclasses and wine-and-pizza nights, and partners with local restaurants and breweries for weekly tastings. It also offers online ordering with delivery across Vancouver and the Lower Mainland.

detail.address: 895 Great Northern Way, Vancouver, BC V5T 1E1

grocery.name: Balfour Superette
grocery.desc: Balfour Superette is the only grocery store in Balfour, BC, positioned on Highway 3A in the Kootenays and functioning as a full community hub for travelers and locals. Beyond a complete grocery offering, it houses a BC licensed liquor agency, hardware supplies, Canada Post, an ATM, and a water bottle filling station. Cyclist testimonials highlight it as a reliable one-stop stop for everything from cold beer to ice cream, making it a practical alternative to the longer ride into Nelson.

grocery.name: Co-op
grocery.desc: The Fort St. James location of Four Rivers Co-op, a member-owned co-operative that is part of the Federated Co-operatives network serving communities across northern and central BC. As a full-service co-op, it offers food, home centre, agro, fuel, and propane services under one banner. For touring cyclists passing through Fort St. James, it represents a significant resupply point in a remote region of the Cariboo and Chilcotin interior.

notes.Vending machines: Website lists 'Vending' as a distinct named service category in the site navigation
notes.Camping fuel: Website lists 'Propane' as a distinct named service category; propane is commonly sold for camping stoves at Co-op locations

grocery.name: Savary Island General Store
grocery.desc: Savary Island General Store appears to be the general store serving Savary Island, a small island off the Sunshine Coast accessible only by water taxi or private boat. As likely the sole grocery option on the island, it would be a critical resupply point for any touring cyclist making the trip to Savary. The island is known for its white sand beaches and is a popular summer destination.

grocery.name: Golden Ears General Store
grocery.desc: Golden Ears General Store is a convenience-style general store located in the Lower Mainland / Fraser Valley region of BC, near the Golden Ears area known for its provincial park and cycling routes. As a general store, it likely serves as a community supply point for locals and visitors passing through. Touring cyclists riding the area may find it a useful stop given its proximity to recreational corridors.

grocery.name: Country Store
grocery.desc: The Country Store is a grocery store, Return-It bottle depot, and freight forwarding location serving Lillooet, BC, operating seven days a week. It is a rare multi-function stop in a small interior community along cycling routes through the Lillooet area. Touring cyclists will find it a practical resupply point with grocery shopping and beverage container returns under one roof.

grocery.name: AM Market & Convenience Store
grocery.desc: AM Market is a convenience store in Langley City, BC, stocking grocery staples including fresh produce, dairy, snacks, and baked goods. It sits on Douglas Crescent in a residential neighbourhood of Langley, which is within cycling distance of several Fraser Valley routes. No information about cyclist-specific facilities is available from the business's current web presence.

grocery.name: Eric's Meat Market & Deli
grocery.desc: Eric's Meat Market & Deli is a cornerstone of downtown Kaslo with over 80 years of continuous operation, originally part of Burns & Co. before becoming a community institution under its current family ownership. The shop hand-cuts fresh meats daily and produces house-made sausages, smoked fish, and beef jerky using traditional recipes — making it a standout provisioning stop for cyclists touring the Kootenays. The deli counter carries imported and Canadian cheeses, cold cuts, and ready-to-eat specialties well suited to a lakeside picnic.

grocery.name: Twig & Berry Trading Company
grocery.desc: Twig & Berry Trading Company, also known as the Parson General Store, is a convenience shop located along Highway 95 in the Kootenays. Sitting in the small community of Parson, it likely serves as a community hub and supply point for travellers passing through this relatively remote stretch of the Columbia Valley. For touring cyclists riding the Columbia Valley route, it may represent one of few resupply options in the area.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a provincially operated retail chain — one of the largest retailers in British Columbia — offering a broad selection of wine, beer, spirits, ciders, and coolers. This Vancouver Island location on East Island Highway is a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking to resupply with beverages. The store also accepts empty container returns for deposit refunds, a useful service for riders carrying empties.

grocery.name: Qualicum Foods
grocery.desc: Quality Foods is a Vancouver Island–based supermarket chain, and this Qualicum Beach location offers a full range of grocery departments including fresh produce, bakery, deli, and household goods. It serves as a well-stocked resupply point for touring cyclists on the Island's east coast route. The deli and ready-made meals section provides a convenient option for riders looking for quick, ready-to-eat food.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a government-operated retail outlet run by the BC Liquor Distribution Branch, one of 198 BCLIQUOR stores across the province. It sells wine, beer, spirits, coolers, and ciders. Touring cyclists in Northern BC may find it useful as a beverage resupply stop, though specific store details for this location are not available.

grocery.name: Jimmy Macs Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Jimmy Macs Liquor Store is the retail liquor arm of Jimy Mac's Neighbourhood Pub, a full-service neighbourhood pub in Langley, BC. The adjoining pub serves a broad menu spanning weekend brunch, burgers, appetizers, and a wide selection of draught beers, wines, and cocktails. A touring cyclist stopping here can resupply on beverages and step next door into the pub for a sit-down meal.

grocery.name: New Market Foods
grocery.desc: New Market Foods is a community-anchored grocery store in New Denver opened in 2011, with management born and raised in the area and a strong commitment to locally sourced products. The store actively gives back to the community, supporting the local volunteer fire department and nearby school fundraisers. For cyclists touring the Kootenays, it is the accessible full-service food stop in this small Slocan Valley town.

grocery.name: Eagle Bay Mercantile
grocery.desc: Eagle Bay Mercantile is a family-owned convenience and Rural Agency Liquor store that has served the Shuswap community since 2016, located 19km down Eagle Bay Road from Trans-Canada Highway 1. The store stocks groceries, liquor, tobacco, and lottery tickets, and offers propane refills, making it a practical all-in-one resupply stop on an otherwise remote rural corridor. It is locally celebrated as the home of 'the coldest beer in the Shuswap.'

It sits along the Kispiox Valley Road corridor, making it a notable resupply point for touring cyclists passing through one of BC's more isolated northern regions. The market appears to serve primarily as the local grocery anchor for the reserve community.

As a general store in an isolated community, it may carry a broad range of everyday goods.

grocery.name: Vanderhoof Department Store

grocery.name: LiquorForLess
grocery.desc: LiquorForLess is a discount liquor retail chain with six locations across the Fraser Valley, positioning itself as priced below government liquor stores with a large selection of beer, wine, and spirits. The Langley outlet sits in a strip-mall unit at 216th Street and Fraser Highway, adjacent to a Starbucks. The chain has been voted Favourite Liquor Store and Favourite Winery/Wine Store by local voters, making it a recognizable regional stop for touring cyclists looking to stock up on beverages.

grocery.name: Jolly Coachman Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Jolly Coachman Pub and Liquor Store has been a community institution in Pitt Meadows since 1976, combining a full-service pub with an attached liquor store under one roof. The pub offers a varied daily menu spanning pub classics, pasta nights, prime rib dinners, and weekend breakfasts, alongside regular live music and community fundraising events that have raised over a million dollars locally. An online ordering system supports both pub food and liquor store purchases.

grocery.name: Krause Farm Store & Café
grocery.desc: Driediger Farms Market is a longstanding on-farm berry market in Langley, BC, growing and selling fresh and frozen BC berries since 1964 across 160 acres of prime Fraser Valley farmland. The market is now operated by Krause Berry Farm under the name Krause Express and is open seasonally. It caters to locals and visitors seeking a direct farm-to-consumer connection with BC-grown strawberries, raspberries, blackberries, and blueberries.

grocery.name: Double G Service
grocery.desc: Double G Service is a landmark Alaska Highway stop at Mile 456, just south of Muncho Lake in remote northern BC, established in 1978 and run by owner-operator Jack Gunness. It offers touring cyclists a rare cluster of services in an isolated stretch of highway: a cafe renowned for homestyle breakfasts, a bakery with homemade bread and cookies, a convenience store, motel rooms, vehicle fuel, and even Canada Post service. Its longevity and breadth of services make it a well-known resupply and rest point for Alaska Highway travelers.

As the apparent main grocery option in an isolated community, it likely stocks a broad range of provisions for multi-day trips.

grocery.name: Paz Fuels
grocery.desc: Paz Fuels is a family-owned independent gas station that has served the Fraser Valley for over 50 years, operating around the clock and offering diesel, propane, dyed fuels, and EV charging alongside a full market café. The on-site Paz Market sets this station apart from typical convenience stops, serving fresh made-to-order meals from a chef, smoothies, pizzas, and café-quality coffee. The plaza functions as a convenient multi-stop service hub for both residents and travellers passing through the Oyster River area. For cyclists touring the Island, the cluster of services — groceries, liquor, food, and an on-site ATM — makes it a practical resupply point.

The Uptown Salmon Arm location is a full-service store with dedicated pharmacy, deli, bakery, meat, produce, and floral departments — a well-stocked resupply option for touring cyclists passing through town. The company emphasizes sourcing from local farmers and suppliers, reflecting a strong community-oriented tradition maintained across four generations of the Askew family.

grocery.name: Sundance Liquor Store

It carries wine, beer, coolers, ciders, and spirits, with a selection of over 200 different wines. For touring cyclists passing through or staying at Sun Peaks, it serves as a convenient spot to pick up drinks after a day on the trails or bike park.

The Alert Bay location is a two-storey general store with a full grocery department — including a bakery, delicatessen, fresh produce, and a cut-meat counter — on the main floor, and a hardware store carrying building supplies, power tools, and plumbing on the second floor. For a touring cyclist reaching Alert Bay by ferry, it is one of the most complete provisioning options in this remote island community.

grocery.name: Le Marché Gourmet

The store carries over 500 international and BC wines, craft beer, locally made spirits, and ice-cold ready-to-drink options with no chill charge.

grocery.name: Langley Liquor Warehouse
grocery.desc: Langley Liquor Warehouse is a bottle shop situated on the Langley Bypass in the Fraser Valley, positioned along a major arterial route through the region. As a warehouse-style liquor store, it likely carries a broad selection of beer, wine, and spirits. For a touring cyclist, it represents a convenient resupply point on a well-traveled corridor between communities.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercenter in Trail, BC (Store 1011) is a large-format retail store serving the Kootenay region. It stocks a full grocery department alongside electronics, clothing, toys, and furniture, making it a comprehensive resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. Trail is a small city in the southern Interior, and this Walmart is likely one of the largest retail stores in the immediate region.

grocery.name: Angry Otter Liquor @ 248th

The store carries beer, wine, and spirits for takeaway purchase.

grocery.name: Campground Office & General Store
grocery.desc: Located at Fair Harbour on northern Vancouver Island, this combined campground office and general store serves as a supply point at the remote gateway to Kyuquot Sound. For touring cyclists venturing into this isolated stretch of Vancouver Island, it represents one of the very few commercial stops in the area. Its dual role as campground office and store suggests it caters to travellers needing basic supplies in a region with limited services.

grocery.name: Liquor 4 Less
grocery.desc: Liquor 4 Less (branded Liquor For Less) is a private liquor retail chain with six Fraser Valley locations across Abbotsford and Langley. The Highstreet Mall location is the chain's original Abbotsford store, formerly operating as Mt. Lehman Liquor Store, and carries a broad selection of beer, wine, and spirits. It has been voted a local favourite liquor store and winery/wine store by community readers.

detail.address: Unit M115 - 3122 Mt.Lehman Road, Abbotsford BC V2T 0C5

grocery.name: Gibsons Landing Sunday Market
grocery.desc: The Gibsons Landing Sunday Market is a periodic outdoor market situated in the Gibsons Landing waterfront neighbourhood on the Sunshine Coast. Its name indicates it operates only on Sundays, making it a highly conditional stop for touring cyclists depending on their travel day. The market is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a convenience shop, suggesting it offers food and goods typical of a local farmers or artisan market.

grocery.name: Fruiticana
grocery.desc: Fruiticana is a BC- and Alberta-based grocery chain specializing in fresh produce and South Asian pantry staples, including their own Indican spice and ingredient brand. The chain emphasizes a farm-to-table philosophy and carries a broad range of ethnic grocery products suited to diverse communities. Touring cyclists in the Abbotsford area would find it a useful stop for fresh fruit, vegetables, and specialty ingredients.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A provincial government-operated retail liquor store serving Qualicum Beach on Vancouver Island, stocking wine, beer, spirits, ciders, and non-alcoholic beverages. As a Crown corporation outlet, it carries a broad and consistent selection including BC VQA wines and local craft beer. Touring cyclists resupplying for an evening camp or cottage stay will find it a reliable stop in the Qualicum area.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercenter Store 1077 is a large-format retail location in Campbell River serving Vancouver Island's Discovery Coast. As a Supercenter, it carries a full grocery department alongside general merchandise including electronics, clothing, and baby products. For a touring cyclist, it represents one of the most comprehensive resupply stops on this stretch of the island.

grocery.name: Tseshaht Market
grocery.desc: Tseshaht Market is a First Nations-owned convenience store and full-service gas station operated by the Tseshaht First Nation on the Pacific Rim Highway, and is notably the last fuel stop between Port Alberni and the west coast communities of Ucluelet and Tofino. Beyond fuel, the market stocks fresh produce, take-out fried chicken, fishing supplies, and First Nations giftware, with a picnic and rest area plus a Totem Pole Garden on site. It has served travellers on this corridor since 1979.

grocery.name: Ford's Cove Store and Pizzeria
grocery.desc: Ford's Cove is a marina and resort on Hornby Island combining a convenience store and pizzeria with waterfront cottages and a campground. As one of the few service points on this remote Gulf Island, it functions as a key resupply and rest stop for cyclists making the ferry crossing. The property is open year-round with ocean views of Vancouver Island's mountains.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Store & Pizza'; business name includes 'Pizzeria'

grocery.name: Canco
grocery.desc: Canco is a convenience store in Clinton, BC, a small interior town that serves as a waypoint for travellers on Highway 97. The auto-discovered Facebook page suggests a possible historical connection to a Shell fuel station and budget food store at the same location.

grocery.name: Express News Convenience
grocery.desc: Express News Convenience is a convenience store in the Lower Mainland / Fraser Valley region of British Columbia. grocery.name: Kersley General Store
grocery.desc: Kersley General Store is a rural general store serving the small community of Kersley in BC's Cariboo region, one of the few supply points along this sparsely populated stretch of interior BC. For touring cyclists riding through the Cariboo, it represents a potentially critical resupply stop in an area where services are widely spaced. The store's general merchandise character suggests it stocks a range of everyday goods for locals and travellers alike.

grocery.name: Quality Foods
grocery.desc: Quality Foods is a BC-based independent supermarket chain with a full-service store in Port Alberni on Vancouver Island. The store carries a wide range of fresh produce, bakery, deli, and household goods, making it a strong resupply stop for cyclists touring the island. An online shop and weekly flyer are available, and the store accepts cash, credit, and debit.

grocery.name: Freshmart Kitwanga
grocery.desc: Kitwanga General Store is a small general store in the village of Kitwanga, located in the Skeena Country of northwestern British Columbia along the Yellowhead Highway corridor. It serves a remote community where the next significant supply stop can be many kilometres away, making it a potentially valuable resupply point for touring cyclists on the Stewart-Cassiar or Yellowhead routes. The store's exact offerings are unverified due to inaccessible web content.

grocery.name: Heartstrings
grocery.desc: Heartstrings is a sprawling 10,000-square-foot home decor, gifts, and furniture shop housed in a log-framed building in downtown Smithers, BC, founded in 2003 and recently relocated to 1207 Main Street. The store carries an eclectic mix of home accessories, pottery, jewellery, bath and body products, indigenous souvenirs, gourmet food, and freshly made in-house fudge. It is a well-established local institution offering custom gift baskets, complementary gift wrapping, and worldwide shipping.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: This BC Liquor Store is part of the provincial government's chain of 198 BCLIQUOR retail locations operated by the Liquor Distribution Branch across British Columbia. Located on Main Street in Oliver — the self-described Wine Capital of Canada — it offers wine, spirits, beer, coolers, ciders, and non-alcoholic products. A practical resupply stop for touring cyclists riding through the Okanagan wine country.

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: A large-format Walmart Supercentre located in Port Alberni on Vancouver Island, offering a full range of grocery, household, clothing, and electronics departments. As one of the larger retail destinations in the region, it is a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists traversing the island. The store accepts cash and major cards.

grocery.name: Rainbow Gas Bar & Convenience
grocery.desc: Rainbow Gas Bar & Convenience is a combined fuel station and convenience store located in the Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior region of BC. Positioned in a remote part of the province, it represents one of the few resupply points touring cyclists might encounter on a long stretch of road. The gas bar component suggests this is a full-service roadside stop rather than a standalone shop.

grocery.name: OTTER CO-OP
grocery.desc: Otter Co-op is a member-owned cooperative with deep roots across the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley, operating food, fuel, pharmacy, feed, and liquor divisions under one roof. The co-op's wide regional footprint — spanning communities from Aldergrove and Langley to Chilliwack and Penticton — makes individual locations potentially useful resupply stops on several popular cycling corridors. Its 'Highwayman' brand suggests at least some locations are oriented toward road travellers.

grocery.name: Eat Fresh Urban Market
grocery.desc: Eat Fresh Urban Market is a locally owned specialty grocery in Parksville offering butcher, bakery, deli, fresh seafood, bulk items, and a curated selection of artisan imports. Red Seal chefs prepare gourmet meals and salads on site using local ingredients. The store has a community-oriented feel, positioning itself as a return to the era of the neighbourhood grocer where staff have deep expertise in their departments.

notes.Hot food: On-site Red Seal chefs create prepared foods and gourmet dishes; website also mentions 'come in for a coffee'

The store stocks a hand-picked selection of cold beer, wine, and spirits and offers online ordering with curbside pickup and delivery. It sits on Dewdney Trunk Road, a common cycling corridor through Maple Ridge.

grocery.name: Alberni Co-op

For a touring cyclist rolling into Port Alberni, it represents a full-service community grocery stop with the breadth typical of Western Canadian Co-op associations.

For cyclists travelling through this vast and roadless wilderness corridor, it represents one of the only service points for many kilometres in any direction.

The combination of fuel and convenience goods makes it a likely resupply point on an otherwise isolated stretch of road.

Situated on Anahim Foothills Road in one of the most remote cycling corridors in the province, it represents a rare resupply point for cyclists on the Chilcotin plateau. The Nation's government website also lists a 'Chilcotin River Trading' at the same phone number, suggesting the store may have been rebranded or replaced.

grocery.name: The Salty Woodsman
grocery.desc: The Salty Woodsman is a specialty shop founded in 2020 by a local couple in Port Alberni, stocking handpicked local and frozen seafood, small-batch pantry provisions, snacks, and drinks alongside gifts, clothing, and home goods from local artisans and makers. Set in a forested location en route to the west coast, it describes itself as a destination stop and 'Port Alberni secret' for travelers passing through the Alberni Valley. Cyclists will find provisions including frozen seafood, condiments, candies, coffee, tea, and preserves.

grocery.name: Co-op Skidegate Food Store
grocery.desc: Co-op Skidegate Food Store is a member-owned grocery co-operative in Skidegate on Haida Gwaii, part of the Haida Gwaii Co-op network that also serves Masset. In this remote island community, it serves as one of the primary food resupply points for cyclists exploring the archipelago. No membership is required to shop — anyone can walk in as a regular customer.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store

For touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan & Thompson corridor, it is a convenient stop to pick up beverages for the evening camp or the next stretch of road.

grocery.name: Choices Market

The 22,000 sq ft store carries a wide selection of organic produce, local and specialty foods, natural wellness products, and hosts an in-store Pure Integrative Pharmacy. It was recognised as Organic Retailer of the Year 2025 by the Canada Organic Trade Association and won the 2025 PQB News Readers' Choice Award for the Oceanside community.

grocery.name: Jim's Foodmarkets

grocery.name: Canim Lake General Store
grocery.desc: Canim Lake General Store is a rural convenience and general store serving the small community at Canim Lake in BC's Cariboo region, one of the more remote stretches of the interior plateau. The combination of 'general store' identity and convenience-shop tagging suggests a broad range of everyday goods.

grocery.name: Invermere Liqour Store
grocery.desc: Invermere Liquor Store is a locally operated retail alcohol shop situated in front of the Canadian Tire on the main commercial strip in Invermere. It stocks a wide selection of beer, wine, and spirits including a dedicated cold room for chilled beer, coolers, and ciders, and carries a notable range of BC wines with knowledgeable staff on hand. For touring cyclists passing through the Columbia Valley, it is a convenient stop to resupply for an evening at camp.

grocery.name: Tru Value Foods
grocery.desc: Tru Value Foods Quathiaski Cove is a community-oriented grocery store located just seconds from the Quadra Island/Campbell River ferry terminal, making it a natural first or last stop for cyclists arriving on or departing from the island. The store has an old-school market feel that its manager describes as complementing the character of the surrounding area. It is part of a small, independently minded BC island chain with locations on Pender, Mayne, and Quadra Island.
