grocery.name: Metro Liquor
grocery.desc: Metro Liquor is a BC specialty liquor retailer with a focus on hard-to-find, limited-release, and local craft products including wine, beer, cider, and spirits. The chain operates three confirmed locations across the province and is known for knowledgeable staff, rotating specialty selections, and public tasting events.

grocery.name: Galiano Italiano Market
grocery.desc: Galiano Italiano Marketplace is a specialty Italian food shop in Sechelt that carries on the legacy of the Old Boot Eatery, a community favourite established in 1995 and now reimagined in a new space. Cyclists can pick up housemade prepared pasta dishes — chicken dijon, prawn linguini, lasagna — plus desserts like tiramisu and Nanaimo bars, and bulk case-lot items to take away. The shop also features an antique collection of vintage collectibles curated by owner Danny, adding an unexpected layer of local character.

grocery.name: The Leeward Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A liquor store on Anderton Road, Vancouver Island. Provides beverage retail to the local community and passing travelers.

grocery.name: Co-op Masset Food Store

As one of the primary grocery options in Masset, it functions as an essential resupply point for touring cyclists on this isolated island chain. Non-members are welcome to shop alongside co-op members.

grocery.name: Otter Co-op
grocery.desc: Otter Co-op is a locally-owned co-operative with locations across the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley, offering food, fuel, feed, pharmacy, and liquor services under one roof. As a member-owned business, it participates in community support programs and offers a member savings program. Touring cyclists will find it a useful multi-service stop, with the potential for groceries and fuel in one location.

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre

For a touring cyclist it represents one of the most comprehensive resupply stops in the region, with full supermarket inventory under one roof. The store is wheelchair accessible and customer washrooms are available on site.

grocery.name: Tsideldel Gas Station and General Stores
grocery.desc: Tsideldel Gas Station and General Stores is a combined fuel stop and general store serving the remote Tsideldel community in BC's Cariboo-Chilcotin region. For touring cyclists crossing the sparsely populated Chilcotin Plateau, this is a rare resupply point in a stretch of road with very few services. The combination of fuel, general merchandise, and its location in a small First Nations community makes it a notable waypoint on long-distance rural routes.

grocery.name: Squirrel Cove General Store
grocery.desc: Squirrel Cove General Store is a multi-purpose community facility offering general groceries, liquor, laundromat services, and shower facilities. The combination of showers and basic supplies makes it a practical stop for touring cyclists needing to refresh and clean up.

grocery.name: Pacific Point Market
grocery.desc: Pacific Point Market is Powell River's locally owned neighbourhood corner market, operating full-service deli, butcher, bakery, fresh produce, seafood, and dairy departments under one roof. The store participates in the 100 Mile Challenge, actively sourcing meat, dairy, and produce from local BC suppliers to reduce food miles and support regional growers. A touring cyclist arriving in Powell River will find a well-stocked resupply point with deli sandwiches, ready-to-go meals, fresh-baked goods, and Serious Coffee.

grocery.name: Los Guerreros
grocery.desc: Los Guerreros is a Latin American specialty grocery store that has been serving the Langley and Fraser Valley community for about a decade, representing the chain's first expansion from its original Vancouver flagship. The store stocks a curated selection of Latin American staples including fresh tortillas, imported snacks, pantry essentials, and beverages from brands like Jarritos and Electrolit. It is part of a three-location BC chain with stores also in Vancouver and Delta.

grocery.name: Atlin Lake Grocery Store
grocery.desc: Atlin Lake Grocery Store is a supermarket serving Atlin, one of BC's most remote and isolated communities near the Yukon border, accessible only by a long gravel spur road off the Alaska Highway. For touring cyclists making the journey to Atlin, it is one of the only food resupply points in the region and a critical stop before or after the ride into town. The surrounding landscape — boreal wilderness, glaciers, and the striking Atlin Lake — makes this an extraordinary destination, and the store anchors the small townsite.

grocery.name: Bamfield Mercantile & Marine
grocery.desc: Bamfield Mercantile & Marine is a historic general store on Bamfield's west boardwalk that has served the remote community since the 1920s, with goods still arriving mostly by boat. Run by Kevin and Marnie McAughtrie since 2015, it stocks fresh groceries, produce, deli sandwiches, ice cream, fishing tackle, and liquor alongside locally sourced artisan products. The store also operates a 25-foot landing craft offering water taxi and charter services throughout Barkley Sound.

grocery.name: Tahltan Centre
grocery.desc: Tahltan Centre is a convenience store serving the remote Tahltan Nation community in northwestern British Columbia, near Telegraph Creek. Located in one of BC's most isolated regions along the Stikine River watershed, it represents a rare resupply point for cyclists venturing through this sparsely populated northern landscape. The centre appears to be a community-oriented facility reflecting the Tahltan Nation's presence in this area.

grocery.name: Cloverdale Country Farm Market
grocery.desc: Cloverdale Country Market is a locally-owned, award-winning organic specialty grocer in Surrey's Cloverdale neighbourhood, voted best produce store for 15 consecutive years by local shoppers. The market sells fresh fruits and vegetables sourced from its own family farm and local BC growers, alongside an extensive organic section, gluten-free groceries, full-service gourmet deli, and freshly baked goods. An on-site Garden Bistro serves Nespresso coffee, hot soups, grilled paninis, and ice cream, making it a well-rounded stop for a touring cyclist needing real food.

notes.Hot food: Garden Bistro serves freshly grilled paninis, soups, and gourmet sub sandwiches; baked goods made in-house daily

grocery.name: Co-op Food Market - Sayward

For cyclists riding the logging roads and highways of the northern Island, it represents a critical resupply point before long stretches with little services. As part of the broader Co-op network, profits are returned to members and reinvested in the local community.

grocery.name: Destiny Bay Grocers
grocery.desc: Destiny Bay Grocers is a year-round convenience store on Highway 3A serving the small lakeside communities of Sanca, Destiny Bay, and Boswell on Kootenay Lake. Part of the Destiny Bay Resort property (the store sits across the highway from the resort itself), it stocks a full grocery range at supermarket prices, cold beer, wine, liquor, ice, and seasonal fresh produce. Cyclists on this remote Kootenay corridor will also find fresh-baked bread, buns, and the store's locally famous butter tarts, plus a modest selection of fishing and camping supplies.

notes.Ice: Website explicitly lists 'ice' among products carried

grocery.name: Sabzi Mandi Supermarket
grocery.desc: Sabzi Mandi Supermarket is a 100% family-owned South Asian grocery chain with 15 locations across Canada, founded in Vancouver in 1991 to serve a growing immigrant community lacking access to South Asian produce and specialty ingredients. This Vancouver Island location carries fresh fruits and vegetables, a broad selection of specialty and imported groceries, household items, and private-label products under the Sabzi Mandi and Roshni brands. Touring cyclists will find it a well-stocked one-stop shop for diverse fresh foods and pantry staples.

grocery.name: West End Grocery
grocery.desc: West End Grocery is a convenience store located in the west end of a community on BC's North Coast. For touring cyclists passing through this remote region, it represents a potential resupply point in an area where services can be scarce. The store's Facebook presence suggests it is an active local business.

grocery.name: Maverick Foods
grocery.desc: Maverick Foods is a convenience store situated on 11th Avenue East in Prince Rupert, BC, within the North Coast and Haida Gwaii region. Prince Rupert is a key hub for cyclists touring BC's remote northern coast and is a ferry terminal connecting to Haida Gwaii and Alaska, making local food shops like this a practical stop. The store maintains a Facebook presence for community engagement.

grocery.name: Fernie Mountain Spirits
grocery.desc: Fernie Mountain Spirits is a well-stocked liquor store on 7th Avenue in the heart of Fernie, offering over 350 wines, a curated sour beer selection (helpfully marked with orange labels), a wide range of imports and domestics, and an impressive tequila selection. Located in a popular mountain-biking and cycling hub, it's a natural resupply stop for touring cyclists looking to pick up cold beer or wine for the campsite or the next leg of the journey.

grocery.name: Grim Cat Farm
grocery.desc: Grim Cat Farm is a greengrocer on Central Lake Road offering fresh produce and groceries. Touring cyclists can access food supplies here, though specific amenities cannot be confirmed.

grocery.name: Shaggy Jack's Market
grocery.desc: Shaggy Jack's Food Market is a specialty food shop inside the Gibsons Public Market on the Sunshine Coast, focusing on local, wild, artisan, and sustainable foods. Alongside the retail store, the business runs mushroom foraging eco-tours and culinary forest adventures that have operated since 2018. It sits in a picturesque waterfront market building in Gibsons, making it a worthwhile stop for cyclists exploring the Sunshine Coast.

grocery.name: Omineca General Store
grocery.desc: A convenience store in remote Northern BC serving the Omineca region. Functions as a general store and resupply stop for the local community and travelers passing through. Located in one of BC's most isolated areas.

grocery.name: Tetsa River Lodge
grocery.desc: Tetsa River Lodge is a three-generation family-run roadside stop at Historic Mile 375 of the Alaska Highway in northern BC, operating since 1942 and self-proclaimed the 'Cinnamon Bun Centre of the Galactic Cluster.' Ben Andrews continues the family tradition with freshly baked cinnamon buns and hand-crafted artisan meats that have made this a beloved landmark among Alaska Highway travelers. On a remote stretch with very few services between Fort Nelson and the Yukon, it offers tenting, cabins, a cafe, gas and diesel, and WiFi — making it a rare and welcome resupply point for touring cyclists.

notes.Basic groceries: Gift shop/cafe sells homemade breads, artisan meats, cinnamon buns, and soup made on premises; not a full grocery but food staples available for purchase
notes.Hot food: Cafe serves breakfast and daily homemade soup; website states 'does not offer full meals but serves a wonderful breakfast and has a variety of meats, bread and the daily homemade soup.'

grocery.name: King Edward Liquor Store
grocery.desc: King Edward Liquor Store is a liquor retailer offering beverages and related products to travelers and locals. It serves as a convenient stop for touring cyclists in need of refreshment or a brief rest.

grocery.name: Otter Co-op
grocery.desc: Otter Co-op is a locally-owned co-operative serving communities across the Lower Mainland, Fraser Valley, and Okanagan, offering food, fuel, pharmacy, feed, and liquor under one roof. As a member-owned organization, it is part of a long-standing BC co-operative tradition. The breadth of services makes it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the Langley/Aldergrove area.

grocery.name: Day To Day Grocery & Produce
grocery.desc: Day to Day Grocery & Produce is a large South Asian wholesale cash-and-carry grocery chain with multiple BC locations, including this Langley branch near Willowbrook Mall. The store stocks over 5,000 products under one roof, specialising in South Asian staples such as premium basmati rice, exotic spices, Ayurvedic herbs, and fresh produce sourced from India and elsewhere. A touring cyclist looking to restock on a wide variety of groceries, fruits, and pantry items would find this one of the larger options in the Langley area.

grocery.name: Alberni District Liquor
grocery.desc: Alberni District Liquor is a liquor retail store serving the Port Alberni area on Vancouver Island, a gateway community to the scenic Alberni Valley and Pacific Rim routes. Cyclists travelling the west coast corridor can stop here to pick up beer, wine, or spirits. The store appears to be a locally operated shop rather than a major chain.

detail.address: 5086 Johnston Rd, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 5L7, Canada

grocery.name: Mom and Pop's Farm Market
grocery.desc: Mom and Pop's Farm Market is a family-owned operation in Keremeos — billed as the 'fruit stand capital of Canada' — founded in 1987 by Paul and Sarbjit Uppal, who built the business from orchard labourers to local institution over the following decade. Beyond fresh locally grown fruits and vegetables, the market sells house-made jams, juices, salsa, soft-serve ice cream, and samosas, all produced with a zero-waste ethos. It's a natural resupply stop for cyclists riding the Similkameen Valley corridor.

notes.Hot food: About page explicitly lists samosas and soft-serve ice cream among the product mix

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: This Walmart Supercenter in Langley, BC is a large-format retail destination carrying groceries alongside electronics, clothing, toys, and furniture. For touring cyclists, it represents a reliable resupply point in the Fraser Valley corridor with broad product availability. The two-storey building is a landmark-scale stop on routes through the Lower Mainland.

grocery.name: Dunster General Store
grocery.desc: Dunster General Store is a convenience store serving the Dunster community in British Columbia's Cariboo region. As a small community general store, it provides groceries and everyday goods for residents and visitors. Touring cyclists in this remote area may rely on it for basic provisions and supplies.

grocery.name: Lillwat Station
grocery.desc: Líl̓wat Station is a Chevron gas station and convenience store operated by the Líl̓wat Nation's business arm, opened in 2019 in Mount Currie approximately 35 km north of Whistler. The well-stocked store carries grab-and-go food, snacks, and Líl̓wat branded merchandise, and also houses a Canada Post outlet — a useful combination for cyclists passing through on the Sea-to-Sky corridor. It serves Líl̓wat Nation citizens, neighbouring communities, and tourists alike.

detail.address: 407 IR 10 Road, Líl̓wat Nation, Mount Currie, BC

grocery.name: Falkland Store Ltd.
grocery.desc: Falkland Store Ltd. is a convenience store serving the small community of Falkland, situated directly on the Okanagan Highway — a well-travelled cycling corridor connecting the Thompson and Okanagan regions. As one of the few retail stops in this rural stretch, it serves as a natural resupply point for touring cyclists passing through. The store accepts cash withdrawals on foreign cards, a handy feature for international cyclists.

grocery.name: Peninsula Co-Op
grocery.desc: Peninsula Co-op's Aspen Gas Centre is a member-owned co-operative gas station and convenience store in Comox, one of 17-plus Co-op fuel locations spanning Victoria, Duncan, Comox, and Campbell River. Cyclists can resupply on snacks and convenience staples, swap a propane bottle for camping stoves, and grab a coffee before continuing along the Comox Valley. As a co-operative, regular shoppers who join as members earn an annual rebate on purchases.

notes.Camping fuel: Website services list for this location explicitly includes 'Propane – Bottle Exchange'; also confirmed on the /services/propane/ subpage listing 'Aspen Road Gas Centre' under bottle-exchange locations

grocery.name: Fairmont Mountainside Market
grocery.desc: Fairmont Mountainside Market is a local supermarket serving the Fairmont Hot Springs community in the Kootenay Rockies of British Columbia. Situated in a small resort community at roughly 50.34°N along the Columbia Valley, it likely serves as the primary grocery stop for residents and visitors in the area. For touring cyclists passing through on the Columbia Valley route, it represents a key resupply point between larger centres.

detail.address: 4992 Fairmont Frontage Rd #8, Fairmont Hot Springs, BC V0B 1L0, Canada

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercenter in Powell River is a large-format department and grocery store serving the northern Sunshine Coast. For touring cyclists, it is one of the most comprehensive resupply options in the area, stocking groceries alongside clothing, electronics, and general merchandise. Powell River's semi-remote location on the Sunshine Coast — accessible only by ferry — makes a full-service store like this a notable landmark on longer touring routes.

grocery.name: Causeway Convenience
grocery.desc: Causeway Convenience is a convenience store located on Haida Gwaii in BC's remote North Coast region. For touring cyclists exploring this archipelago, it represents a key resupply point in an area with limited retail options. The OSM record was field-checked as recently as July 2024, suggesting the store remains active.

detail.address: 101 Causeway, Daajing Giids, BC V8J 1H9, Canada

grocery.name: Country Store & Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Country Store & Liquor Store is a convenience and liquor store operated by Manning Park Resort, situated along Highway 3 in Manning Provincial Park — one of BC's most popular cycling corridors connecting Hope to Princeton. As the resort's on-site retail store, it serves both resort guests and through-travelers at a remote location where resupply options are otherwise scarce. Cyclists crossing the Hope-Princeton pass will find it a strategically located stop in a stretch of highway with very few services.

notes.Basic groceries: Website confirms resort-operated retail presence but does not enumerate specific stock

grocery.name: Michael's nofrills
grocery.desc: Michael's No Frills is a discount supermarket franchise located in Langley, BC, part of the Loblaw-owned No Frills chain known for low-price grocery staples. As a full supermarket, it offers a broad range of packaged and fresh foods that touring cyclists can use to stock up before or after longer stretches of the Fraser Valley. The store is independently franchised under the Michael's banner, a common format for No Frills locations across British Columbia.

grocery.name: Numas One Stop shop
grocery.desc: A convenience store on Vancouver Island, the type of stop where cyclists often pick up quick supplies and refreshments. Unable to confirm specific amenities due to website access issues, but generally such stores offer basic groceries and beverages.

grocery.name: Marg's Minimart
grocery.desc: Marg's Minimart is a convenience store in a remote stretch of Northern BC, serving a community well off the main touring corridors. For cyclists passing through this area, it represents a rare resupply point in a region with very limited services. The OSM record suggests the location may now operate under a different name.

detail.address: 9718 Beattie Dr, Hudson's Hope, BC V0C 1V0, Canada

grocery.name: Mason & Daly General Merchants
grocery.desc: Mason & Daly General Merchants is a heritage-themed general store operating within Barkerville Historic Town & Park, western North America's largest living history museum and a National Historic Site of Canada. Set in a reconstructed 1870s gold-rush townsite deep in the Cariboo Mountains, the shop would transport a touring cyclist arriving via Highway 26 into a remarkably well-preserved slice of BC's gold-rush era. The site is managed by the Barkerville Heritage Trust and hosts a range of independent merchants, restaurants, and cultural programming.

grocery.name: Mason Place
grocery.desc: Mason Place is a convenience store on the Sunshine Coast of British Columbia, tagged in OpenStreetMap as a neighbourhood shop. The Facebook page slug 'masonplacemarket' suggests it operates as a small market. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a useful stop for basic supplies.

detail.address: 6506 Norwest Bay Rd, Sechelt, BC V7Z 0N4, Canada

grocery.name: Washtock Campground Camp Store
grocery.desc: Washtock Family Farm is a 4th-generation off-grid farm established in 1912, situated at the confluence of the Fraser and Nahatlatch Rivers near Boston Bar. The on-site camp store serves campers and passing travellers with ice, snacks, beef cuts, firewood, and eggs. The farm generates its own electricity via a Pelton wheel and offers a peaceful, remote farm-based camping experience in the Fraser Canyon.

detail.address: P.O. Box 302, 52702 Chaumox Road, Boston Bar, BC, V0K-1C0

notes.Ice: OSM description explicitly lists 'Ice' as a camp store product

grocery.name: Town Pantry
grocery.desc: This is an On the Run convenience store and restaurant operating at a Chevron station in Courtenay, BC, open around the clock every day of the week. It offers fuel, a convenience store, and a restaurant under one roof, making it a reliable all-hours resupply stop on Vancouver Island. Touring cyclists will find food, washrooms, and a compressed-air station on site.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Restaurant' as a service/amenity
notes.Pump: Website lists 'Air' as an amenity — compressed air station available at the forecourt, usable for bicycle tires

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Revelstoke BC Liquor Store is a government-operated retail outlet carrying wine, spirits, beer, coolers, and ciders, including BC VQA wines and BC craft beers. It is one of 198 BCLIQUOR locations across the province, offering knowledgeable staff recommendations and in-store container recycling. Touring cyclists passing through Revelstoke can resupply with local and import beverages here.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store is a provincial government-operated retail chain with 198 locations across British Columbia, making this Campbell River outlet one of the most reliably stocked spots on Vancouver Island for wine, spirits, beer, ciders, and non-alcoholic beverages. The store accepts empty container returns for deposit refunds, a practical perk for cyclists who have been carrying empties. As a BCLIQUOR Signature-format store, it offers an expanded selection and on-site product consultants.

grocery.name: Rainbow Market
grocery.desc: Rainbow Market is a convenience store located on Prince Rupert Boulevard in the North Coast region of British Columbia. Sitting along a key coastal corridor near Prince Rupert, it serves as a local stop for everyday supplies. Touring cyclists passing through this remote stretch of BC will find it a useful resupply point in an area with limited services.

grocery.name: Capones Cellar
grocery.desc: Capones Cellar is Powell River's liquor store, situated at the corner of Duncan and Joyce, stocking a broad range of wines, beers, and spirits. Its signature walk-in beer cooler lets you grab a cold beverage to go, and the store's walls are decorated with images and authentic signatures of Al Capone, Carlo Gambino, and Al Pacino — an unexpected bit of atmosphere for a bottle shop. A loyalty program and weekly senior's discount reflect its community-focused character.

grocery.name: Blind Bay Village Grocer
grocery.desc: Blind Bay Village Grocer is a community-focused full-service grocery store serving the Shuswap region, stocking fresh local meat, produce, bakery and deli goods alongside a broad selection of beer, wine, and spirits. The Blind Bay location also includes an on-site Shell fuel station (bronze, silver, premium, diesel, and marked premium) and a Canada Post outlet, making it a genuine one-stop stop on a touring route. A sister store in nearby Sorrento offers additional coverage for cyclists moving through the corridor.

notes.Hot food: 'Weekly Hot Dinners' is listed as a dedicated section under Flyers & Specials on the website navigation

grocery.name: Coombs Corner Convenience
grocery.desc: Coombs Corner Convenience is a convenience store on the Alberni Highway in Coombs, a small Vancouver Island community sitting between Parksville and Port Alberni. It occupies a natural rest point for cyclists riding the highway corridor toward Pacific Rim National Park or the Comox Valley. As a corner store on a touring route, it offers the kind of quick resupply stop that matters when the next town is many kilometres away.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Lillooet branch of BC Liquor Store is a government-operated retail outlet on Main Street offering wine, beer, spirits, coolers, and ciders. Located in a remote Interior BC community along the Duffey Lake Road and Fraser Canyon cycling corridors, it is one of the few places in the area to resupply on beverages. The store carries both BC VQA wines and a broad national and import selection.

grocery.name: Provisions
grocery.desc: False Bay Provisions is a general store, bakery, and café that has served the remote community of Lasqueti Island since 2015, offering organic and international groceries, fresh-baked bread and pastries, soups, sandwiches, and meals to go. Lasqueti is accessible only by foot-passenger ferry — no vehicle ferry exists — making this the island's primary provisioning stop for cyclists exploring on foot or by bike. The shop also stocks local arts, crafts, books, and seasonal produce, reflecting the self-sufficient character of island life.

notes.Hot food: Website states: 'We serve organic coffee, pie, ice cream, sandwiches, soups, salads, fresh bread and pastries. Open for breakfast, lunch and meals to go.' Coffee and soups confirm hot food

grocery.name: Merecroft Village Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A liquor store located in the Merecroft Village complex on northern Vancouver Island, apparently associated with a pub (MVP Pub). It sits in a strip-mall-style unit and could serve as a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking to pick up beverages.

grocery.name: Mariposa
grocery.desc: Mariposa is a fruit stand and greengrocer located in the Okanagan & Thompson region of British Columbia, an area celebrated for its orchards, vineyards, and abundant local produce. The OSM tag 'shop=greengrocer' and the Facebook page name 'Mariposa fruit stand' suggest a roadside or farm-stand style operation typical of this agricultural corridor. For touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan, it represents a potential stop for fresh local fruit and seasonal produce.

grocery.name: Appletree Market
grocery.desc: Appletree Market is a convenience store located at 908 5th Street on Vancouver Island. It sits in the Vancouver Island and Gulf Islands region, an area popular with cycle tourists on multi-day tours. No further details about the store's offerings or character could be verified due to a website mismatch.

grocery.name: Station Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Station Liquor Store is a retail alcohol shop located in a commercial unit along Fraser Highway in Abbotsford, BC. It sits within the Lower Mainland & Fraser Valley region and could serve touring cyclists seeking beverages or supplies on a major arterial corridor.

grocery.name: Emart
grocery.desc: E-Mart is a small Filipino ethnic convenience store in Sechelt on the Sunshine Coast, stocking over 300 traditional Filipino food products including fresh, frozen, and shelf-stable items such as Aling Mary fresh goods, tocino, longanisa, lumpia, and a wide range of Filipino sauces and canned goods. The store also functions as an I-Remit money transfer agent and LBC Box Agent, making it a community hub for the local Filipino diaspora. Touring cyclists passing through Sechelt will find a distinctive specialty grocery stop with products unavailable at mainstream supermarkets.

grocery.name: Golden Ears Store
grocery.desc: Golden Ears Store is a convenience shop located within or adjacent to Golden Ears Provincial Park, one of BC's largest and most visited parks just over an hour east of Vancouver. Serving campers, hikers, and day-use visitors drawn to Alouette Lake and the park's extensive trail network, it is a potentially valuable resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley corridor.

grocery.name: Fields
grocery.desc: Fields is a Canadian-owned rural general store chain that has served highway-bound travellers and remote communities across Western Canada since 1948. This location carries everyday essentials including basic groceries, clothing, and household goods — a useful resupply stop in an area where options are limited. The familiar red-lettered storefront is a landmark for road-trippers passing through small BC communities.

grocery.name: The Stock Pile Market Grocery Store & Deli
grocery.desc: A grocery store and deli in Lund serving the local community and passing tourists. Website information was not accessible to verify specific amenities or services offered.

grocery.name: Garlic n Pepper
grocery.desc: Garlic N Pepper is a family-run Korean/Japanese grocery store and eatery in Courtenay that has been operating since 2019. It stocks a notably broad Asian grocery selection — 30+ ramen varieties, Korean and Japanese sauces, snacks, frozen foods, and house-made small-batch kimchi — that would be hard to find elsewhere in the Comox Valley. The eatery side serves hot Korean comfort food including bibimbap, bulgogi, spicy pork, and mandu, available for dine-in, pickup, or delivery.

notes.Hot food: Full Korean eatery menu: Korean Fried Chicken Bowl, Bibimbap, Bulgogi, Spicy Pork, Japchae, Soondubu, Kimchi Fried Rice, and more. Also available via SkipTheDishes and DoorDash

grocery.name: Mount Robson Store & Gift Shop
grocery.desc: Cafe Mt Robson is a landmark stop on Yellowhead Highway 16 at the foot of Mount Robson Provincial Park, the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Operating for over 100 years, the café micro-roasts its own organic fair-trade coffee in small batches and serves a full menu ranging from espresso drinks to homemade pizza and chuck wagon BBQ burgers. Sitting on a remote stretch roughly 100 km west of Jasper and 75 km east of McBride, it represents one of the few substantial commercial stops for cyclists travelling this corridor.

detail.address: 18344 Yellowhead Highway 16, Mount Robson, BC, Canada

notes.Hot food: Menu lists soups, chili, stew, french fries, poutine, Napoli-style homemade pizza, and hamburgers from a chuck wagon BBQ

grocery.name: Mountain Mart
grocery.desc: Mountain Mart is a convenience store in or near Golden, BC, a gateway community to Yoho and Kootenay National Parks and a key waypoint on cycling routes through the Columbia Valley. The OSM tag discouraging large vehicles suggests a compact, accessible site well-suited to arriving by bike. For touring cyclists, it represents a potential resupply stop in a region where services can be spread thin.

grocery.name: The Belmont Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Belmont is a combined pub and liquor store in Prince Rupert, a key North Coast hub for cyclists beginning or ending ferry journeys to Haida Gwaii or Alaska. The store advertises cold beer sold at government liquor store prices. Prince Rupert is a notable waypoint on remote northern touring routes, making a liquor resupply stop potentially relevant to multi-day cyclists.

detail.address: 725 3rd Ave West, Prince Rupert, BC V8J 1M7

grocery.name: European Deli & Catering
grocery.desc: European Deli & Catering Co is a specialty European food shop on Fraser Highway in Langley offering Dutch and other European products including charcuterie, cheeses, breads, and imported candy. Customer feedback highlights friendly staff and delicious sandwiches and deli meats. It would make a distinctive food stop for touring cyclists seeking something beyond standard convenience-store fare.

detail.address: 22314 Fraser Hwy, Langley, BC V3A 8M6, Canada

grocery.name: Glover Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Glover Liquor Store is a local alcohol retail shop located in the Milner area of Langley in BC's Fraser Valley. The Instagram handle suggests it serves the Milner community, making it a potential convenience stop for cyclists on routes through this agricultural corridor. As a liquor store, it would carry beer, wine, and spirits suitable for an end-of-ride stop.

detail.address: 6808 216 St Unit 102, Langley Twp, BC V2Y 0W9, Canada

grocery.name: IGA
grocery.desc: IGA Enderby is a full-service neighbourhood supermarket on Russell Avenue in the small city of Enderby, situated in the Okanagan-Shuswap region along a popular cycle touring corridor. Operating under the IGA Stores of BC banner, it offers a comprehensive range of departments including a bakery, in-house butcher, deli with ready-to-eat meals, fresh produce, dairy, and wellness products. For touring cyclists moving through the Thompson-Okanagan, it represents one of the more complete resupply options in the area.

grocery.name: Bradner General Store
grocery.desc: Bradner General Store is a small convenience and general store located on Bradner Road in the rural Bradner area of the Fraser Valley. It serves as a local community hub in an agricultural neighbourhood east of Abbotsford, making it a useful stop for touring cyclists passing through the region on rural roads. The name 'General Store' suggests a broad range of everyday goods beyond a typical convenience store.

grocery.name: Sage Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Sage Pub & Liquor Store is a combined full-service pub and liquor store in Osoyoos, BC, in the heart of the Okanagan cycling corridor. The pub offers a wide dine-in and takeout menu spanning hand-made pizzas, chicken wings, ribs, poutine, and entrées, alongside weekly events such as trivia nights and karaoke. The attached liquor store operates daily, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking to resupply or sit down for a hot meal after a ride.

grocery.name: Cheers Liqour Store
grocery.desc: Cheers Liquor Store is a locally operated bottle shop in downtown Revelstoke, situated adjacent to the Regent Hotel and convenient to the historic town core. It stocks a broad selection of cold beer, wine, coolers, ciders, and spirits with a particular emphasis on BC craft breweries and local producers. A delivery service is also available, making it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists seeking beverages after a day on the road.

grocery.name: Metro Liquor
grocery.desc: Metro Liquor is a BC specialty liquor retailer emphasizing craft beer, local and organic wines, and hard-to-find limited-release spirits. The company operates three confirmed locations (Tsawwassen, West Kelowna, and Kelowna Train Station) and hosts public tasting events with knowledgeable staff. However, no location at 801 Hilchey Road appears on the company website, raising doubts about whether this OSM record corresponds to a current, active outlet.

grocery.name: Askew's Foods
grocery.desc: Askew's Foods is a locally owned, family-operated supermarket chain founded in 1929, with its Sicamous location serving as a key resupply point at the junction of the Trans-Canada Highway and Highway 97A. The store runs full departments including bakery, deli, meat, and produce, staffed by named department managers. Grocery delivery to local accommodations is also available by phone or email.

grocery.name: Union Bay Market
grocery.desc: Union Bay Market is a convenience store located on the South Island Highway in Union Bay on Vancouver Island, a popular cycling corridor connecting communities along the eastern coast. For touring cyclists riding the Island, it serves as a roadside stop in a small community with limited services. The shop's position on the main highway route makes it a natural waypoint for provisioning.

grocery.name: Walmart Supercentre
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercentre is a large-format retail store on the Yellowhead Highway in Terrace, serving the North Coast and Haida Gwaii region. It offers a full grocery department alongside electronics, clothing, furniture, and general merchandise, making it one of the most comprehensive resupply points in northern BC. For touring cyclists on the Yellowhead corridor, it represents a rare opportunity to restock nearly any category of supplies in a single stop.

grocery.name: Askew's Foods
grocery.desc: Askew's Foods is a locally owned independent supermarket in downtown Salmon Arm, founded in 1929 and still family-run across four locations in the Shuswap and Thompson-Okanagan region. The downtown store on Lakeshore Drive carries a full range of groceries with dedicated produce, meat, and deli departments, and sources from local farmers and suppliers. For touring cyclists passing through Salmon Arm, it is a well-established full-service resupply point in the heart of town.

detail.address: 111 Lakeshore Drive, Salmon Arm, BC V1E 4N3

grocery.name: West Chilcotin Trading LTD
grocery.desc: West Chilcotin Trading LTD is a convenience store situated on Highway 20, the remote Chilcotin Highway that cuts through one of BC's most isolated and scenically dramatic cycling regions. For touring cyclists travelling this long, sparsely serviced corridor, a resupply stop of any kind is a significant landmark. The store's exact offerings are unconfirmed due to inaccessible online information, making on-the-ground verification especially worthwhile.

grocery.name: Ridgeway Spirits
grocery.desc: Ridgeway Spirits is a private liquor store on Lougheed Highway at the corner of Laity Street in Maple Ridge, operated by the Springs Group network of 13-plus BC liquor stores and brew pubs. The store focuses on craft beer, wine, and spirits with a stated emphasis on quality selection and community service. Curbside pickup and home delivery are available in addition to in-store shopping.

detail.address: 21280 Lougheed Highway, Maple Ridge, BC V2X 2R7

grocery.name: Salmo Village Grocery on Main
grocery.desc: Salmo Village Grocery is a 100% independent, family-owned grocery store that has served the Salmo community since 1982, positioning itself as 'where the village shops' in the hub of the west Kootenays. Part of the Coast Grocery Co. network, it stocks everyday groceries, seasonal produce, and deli meats. For touring cyclists passing through this part of the Kootenays, it offers a full resupply point in a small mountain town with limited alternatives.

notes.Basic groceries: Website states: 'Pick up all your favourite grocery items, seasonal produce, tasty deli meats and more.'

grocery.name: Griffin Pub & Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Griffin Pub & Liquor Store has been a Comox Valley institution since 1984, nestled next to the airbase on Kilmorley Road. The pub pours from 16 taps including local BC craft beers and house wines from Chabberton Estate, alongside a seasonal kitchen menu built around Comox Valley produce. An attached liquor store lets cyclists grab supplies to go, making this a combined eat-drink-and-stock-up stop.

grocery.name: Big Bay General Store & Post Office
grocery.desc: Big Bay General Store & Post Office is a combined general store and post office serving the remote community of Big Bay on Stuart Island, British Columbia, accessible only by ferry. Founded in a region of dramatic coastal inlets, it is one of the very few commercial supply points on this isolated island. For touring cyclists venturing this far off the beaten path, it represents a rare opportunity to resupply in an otherwise extremely remote off-grid environment.

grocery.name: Hilltop Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Hilltop Liquor Store is a neighbourhood alcohol retailer in Quesnel, BC, serving the Cariboo region of British Columbia's Central Interior. For touring cyclists passing through Quesnel on routes such as Highway 97, it represents a convenient stop to pick up beer, wine, or spirits. The Facebook page slug confirms the Quesnel location, though no further details about the store's layout or offerings are available from accessible online sources.

grocery.name: Global Supermarket
grocery.desc: A multicultural grocery store in the southern Okanagan sourcing fresh produce from local farms and stocking global ingredients to serve the region's diverse community. The store is family-owned and positions itself as a neighbourhood anchor in the Oliver-to-Penticton corridor — a stretch of Highway 97 popular with touring cyclists. Riders will find a full-range grocery offering suitable for resupply in a part of BC better known for wineries than supermarkets.

grocery.name: The Witch Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Witch Liquor Store is one of 13 Springs Group retail locations across British Columbia, situated on Dewdney Trunk Road in Maple Ridge. It stocks an extensive range of ice-cold beer, coolers, ciders, fine wines, and spirits, with curbside pickup and home delivery also available. Frequent promotional deals and knowledgeable staff make it a well-regarded neighbourhood liquor stop for anyone riding through the Maple Ridge area.

detail.address: 22644 Dewdney Trunk Rd. Maple Ridge, BC V2X 3J9

grocery.name: Telegraph Cove General Store
grocery.desc: A general store in Telegraph Cove, a remote community on northern Vancouver Island. Services to touring cyclists cannot be confirmed due to website unavailability.

grocery.name: Government Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC LIQUOR Port Alberni is a provincial government liquor retail store on 10th Avenue in Port Alberni, part of the 198-store BCLIQUOR network operated by the BC Liquor Distribution Branch. It stocks wine, spirits, beer, coolers, ciders, and non-alcoholic beverages, and accepts credit and debit cards. OSM notes wheelchair accessibility, and the store offers a container-recycling deposit refund program.

grocery.name: Ocean Lounge & Liquor Store
grocery.desc: Ocean Liquor Store is a retail liquor outlet located on Island Highway East in Parksville, on Vancouver Island's popular cycling corridor. The store offers an online ordering system with in-store pickup and carries a range of alcohol products. Cyclists passing through Parksville on the Island Highway route would find it convenient for resupply.

detail.address: 491 Island Highway East, Parksville, BC V9P1V9

grocery.name: Black Creek Country Market
grocery.desc: A convenience store in the Black Creek area on Vancouver Island. Serves as a resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the region. Specific amenities beyond basic groceries could not be verified due to website access failure.

grocery.name: Dawson Co-op Food Store
grocery.desc: Dawson Co-op is a member-owned co-operative supermarket serving Dawson Creek and the surrounding northern BC communities of Chetwynd, Tumbler Ridge, and Rolla. As a full-service community grocery store, it offers the kind of provisioning stop a long-distance touring cyclist needs before tackling the remote roads of this region. The co-op model means local ownership and community reinvestment, giving it a distinct character compared to chain supermarkets.

grocery.name: Riondel Market
grocery.desc: A convenience store in Riondel, a small community in the Kootenays region of British Columbia. A potential resupply point for touring cyclists traveling through the area.

grocery.name: Sana'aih Market
grocery.desc: Sana'aih Market is a full-service community grocery store located on Nakazdli Whuten territory along Highway 27 in Fort St. James, BC, operating as part of the AGfoods buying group. It bills itself as a hospitality-based grocer focused on high-quality customer service, with dedicated departments for produce, meat, and bakery/deli. For touring cyclists passing through the Cariboo-Central Interior, it is a key resupply point in an otherwise remote stretch of the province.

detail.address: 380 Hwy 27, Fort St. James, BC V0J 1P0

grocery.name: City Centre Stores Ltd.
grocery.desc: City Centre Stores Ltd. is a supermarket serving the community of Queen Charlotte City (Daajing Giids) on Haida Gwaii, one of British Columbia's most remote and spectacular cycling destinations. For touring cyclists making the journey to this island archipelago, it represents a critical resupply point in an area with very limited retail options. The store was verified open as recently as July 2024 and is noted as wheelchair accessible.

detail.address: 121 Oceanview Dr, Daajing Giids, BC V8J 1H9, Canada

grocery.name: Corfield Liquor Depot
grocery.desc: Corfield Liquor Depot is a retail alcohol store located on Vancouver Island, operating as part of the Liquor Depot chain. It offers a selection of beer, wine, and spirits, and the chain advertises volume discounts for larger orders. As a convenience resupply stop, it is limited in cyclist-focused services.

grocery.name: Co-op
grocery.desc: The Co-op Food store is part of Dawson Co-op, a locally-owned co-operative serving communities in the Peace Country region of northeastern BC including Dawson Creek, Chetwynd, Tumbler Ridge, and Rolla. It operates as a full-service grocery store with a staffed meat counter (including in-house sausage and jerky), fresh produce, deli, and an in-store bakery. As a member-owned co-op, it provides comprehensive grocery services in a remote northern BC hub along the Alaska Highway corridor.

grocery.name: Aldergrove Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A government-operated BCLIQUOR retail store in Aldergrove, one of 198 locations run by the BC Liquor Distribution Branch across the province. It carries the full BCLIQUOR range of wine, beer, spirits, coolers, and ciders. Touring cyclists passing through Aldergrove may find it a practical stop for resupply before a campsite or overnight.

grocery.name: Ferraro Foods
grocery.desc: Ferraro Foods is an independently owned, full-service supermarket that has anchored the Trail and Rossland communities since 1943, now employing over 150 people across its two Kootenay locations. The Trail store features a full-service Meat & Seafood Shoppe, Cheese Shoppe, Deli, in-house Bakery, and an in-store Starbucks kiosk. The store produces an impressive range of house-made items under its own brand, from over 25 sausage varieties to heat-and-serve meals, making it a well-stocked resupply point for cyclists passing through the region.

notes.Hot food: Deli page confirms made-in-store Grab-n-Go meals, soups, panini, and sandwiches; Trail location also has an in-store Starbucks kiosk

grocery.name: Good Fridays
grocery.desc: Good Fridays is a cheerful general store in Gibsons on BC's Sunshine Coast, stocking a curated mix of snacks, home goods, apparel, wellness products, and gifts. The shop also runs a grazing and charcuterie service — graze boxes and platters — ideal for a beach picnic or boat day. It's a compact lifestyle boutique with a local, community feel, useful for a cyclist looking for snacks or a small gift.

grocery.name: Ingenika Trading Post
grocery.desc: The Ingenika Trading Post is the community general store of the Tsay Keh Dene Nation, one of British Columbia's most remote First Nations communities in the northern Rocky Mountain Trench. It serves as a one-stop shop for food, clothing, and hunting and gear supplies, and offers daily fresh food service with hot coffee and tea in an outdoor seating area. The community is accessible only by scheduled floatplane from Prince George, making this store a critical provisioning point for anyone spending extended time in the region.

detail.address: 1 Main Street, Tsay Keh Dene V0J 3N0

notes.Hot food: Website states: 'we also provide fresh food services, hot coffee, and tea daily with outdoor seating.'

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store in Gold River is a provincial government-run retail outlet selling wine, beer, spirits, ciders, and non-alcoholic alternatives. Located in a small, remote Vancouver Island community, it may represent the only opportunity for multi-day touring cyclists to resupply with beer or wine before continuing into the backcountry. Staff can advise on product selection but the store is not oriented toward cycling services.

grocery.name: Bulkley Valley Wholesale
grocery.desc: Bulkley Valley Wholesale is a long-established grocery and food service wholesaler that has operated out of Smithers since 1959, now part of the Pattison Food Group. Originally wholesale-only, the store opened to retail customers in 2000, giving the general public access to its broad selection of grocery and food service products at competitive prices. Situated on Highway 16, it is a practical resupply stop for cyclists touring northwest BC's main corridor.

grocery.name: IGA
grocery.desc: IGA Murrayville is a full-service neighbourhood supermarket on 48th Avenue in Langley's Murrayville area, part of the IGA Stores of BC network. It carries a broad range of fresh produce, meat, dairy, deli, bakery, and household goods, making it a practical resupply stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley. The store's extensive department selection—including prepared and ready-to-eat meals—is well suited for touring cyclists looking to stock up quickly.

notes.Hot food: Website lists 'Deli & Prepared Foods', 'Ready to Eat Meals', and 'Platters' as active departments

grocery.name: Cornucopia
grocery.desc: Cornucopia is a supermarket serving the small lakeside community of Kaslo, BC in the Kootenay region. For touring cyclists on routes through the Kootenays, it represents a rare full-service grocery resupply point in an otherwise remote stretch of riding. The town of Kaslo itself is a popular overnight destination on multi-day touring routes.

detail.address: 422 Front St, Kaslo, BC V0G 1M0, Canada

grocery.name: Walnut Grove Food Market
grocery.desc: A convenience store in the Walnut Grove area of the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley. Provides basic grocery items and convenience supplies to residents and travelers.

detail.address: 20793 96 Ave, Langley Twp, BC V1M 2H2, Canada

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: Walmart Supercenter (Store 1106) in Williams Lake, serving the Cariboo region with a full grocery department alongside electronics, clothing, furniture, toys, and baby goods. As one of the largest retail stores in the area, it is a significant resupply point for touring cyclists passing through central British Columbia. The Supercenter format means a broad range of supplies are available under one roof.

grocery.name: Anahim Lake Trading Post & General Store
grocery.desc: Anahim Lake Trading Post & General Store is a convenience shop located in the remote Anahim Lake area of the Cariboo Chilcotin, a region of BC that sees significant cycle touring traffic on routes such as the Chilcotin Highway. As one of the few commercial stops in this sparsely populated area, it likely serves as a critical resupply point for self-supported tourers crossing the interior plateau.

grocery.name: Sanderson Farms Market
grocery.desc: Sander Farms is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a greengrocer in the Okanagan & Thompson region of British Columbia. No further verified details about its offerings, location, or facilities are available from the OSM record or accessible website content. A touring cyclist passing through the Keremeos area may find farm-direct produce here, but this cannot be confirmed.

grocery.name: Eat Pure Mountain Market
grocery.desc: Eat Pure Mountain Market is Golden's organic grocer since 2014, founded by holistic chef Nicole Du Vent and stocked with fresh produce, dairy, grass-fed and free-range meat, baking essentials, natural body care, and supplements. The in-store Hive Cafe serves organic lunches, smoothies, coffee, and vegan and gluten-free treats, making it a substantive resupply stop for cyclists passing through the Columbia Valley on the Trans-Canada corridor. The store is community-rooted, sourcing pork, eggs, and garlic from the owners' own permaculture farm.

notes.Hot food: The Hive Cafe offers organic lunch, smoothies, coffee, elixirs, and vegan and gluten-free treats

grocery.name: Wayward Distillation House
grocery.desc: Wayward Distillery is a craft spirits producer operating in Courtenay in the Comox Valley since 2014, still run by its original three founders. The distillery is best known for fermenting most of its lineup — vodkas, gins, rum, and liqueurs — from sustainable BC honey, and donates 1% of all spirit sales to Pollinator Partnership Canada. Cyclists can visit the distillery store directly or browse an award-winning range of spirits, with the business also holding Rainbow Registered and Living Wage Employer status.

grocery.name: Walmart
grocery.desc: A Walmart Supercenter located in Prince George, BC, offering a broad range of groceries alongside general merchandise including electronics, clothing, toys, and furniture. As one of the larger retail destinations in the Central Interior, it serves as a convenient resupply point for touring cyclists passing through Prince George. The supercenter format means a full grocery section is available alongside household goods and other supplies.

grocery.name: E&B Market
grocery.desc: E&B Market is a convenience store located on McPhee Avenue, serving the local community with everyday essentials. As a small neighbourhood market, it is a practical stop for touring cyclists needing to resupply. The surrounding area on Vancouver Island is a popular corridor for cycle touring.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: A BC government-operated retail liquor store on Highway 97 in the Okanagan & Thompson corridor, stocking wine, beer, spirits, coolers, and ciders. It is one of 198 BCLIQUOR locations province-wide and accepts empty container returns for deposit refunds. Touring cyclists passing through on BC-97 may stop to purchase beverages, but no cyclist-specific services are documented for this location.

grocery.name: Georgia Park Store
grocery.desc: Georgia Park Store is a convenience shop located along the West Island Highway on Vancouver Island, a corridor commonly used by touring cyclists travelling the island's east coast. As a roadside convenience store in a rural stretch, it likely serves as a resupply point for travellers passing through. No further detail about its offerings or facilities could be confirmed from available sources.

detail.address: 6871 Island Hwy W, Bowser, BC V0R 1G0

notes.Basic groceries: No website content available to confirm further

grocery.name: Waverley Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Waverley Liquor Store is a cold beer and wine shop attached to The Waverley Hotel in Cumberland, BC, a town celebrated as one of Canada's premier mountain biking destinations. Despite its compact size, the store carries a broad selection that emphasises local BC wines and regional craft beers. It sits within a larger hospitality complex — the same building houses a pub, a kitchen, and hotel rooms — making it a natural post-ride stop.

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: The Haney branch (store #65) is part of the province-wide BCLIQUOR government retail chain, offering wine, spirits, beer, ciders, and non-alcoholic products. It is one of 198 stores operated by the BC Liquor Distribution Branch across British Columbia. Touring cyclists passing through Maple Ridge could use it as a beverage resupply point.

grocery.name: Tyee Pier fuel dock and convenience store
grocery.desc: Tyee Pier fuel dock and convenience store is a marine fuel and retail stop operated by Port Alberni Marine Fuels and Services Ltd., situated on a pier in the Port Alberni area of Vancouver Island. The facility primarily serves recreational and commercial boaters but, as a waterfront convenience store, could offer a useful supply stop for touring cyclists passing through the region. Its pier setting and marine focus make it an unusual entry point for land-based travellers.

detail.address: 990-3300 Harbour Rd, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 4B9

grocery.name: BC Liquor Store
grocery.desc: BC Liquor Store (BCLIQUOR) in Port Alice is a provincial government-operated retail outlet and one of 198 stores across British Columbia, offering wine, beer, spirits, coolers, ciders, and non-alcoholic beverages. It is the only government liquor store serving this remote northern Vancouver Island community, making it a notable resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the area. The store also accepts returns of empty beverage containers for deposit refunds, a useful service for cyclists carrying empties.

grocery.name: Cassidy Farm Market
grocery.desc: Cassidy Farm Market is a greengrocer on the Trans-Canada Highway in the Cassidy/Cedar area. It accepts both cash and card payments, making it accessible to most cyclists. As a dedicated grocery store, it provides fresh produce and staples useful for re-provisioning during a touring journey through the region.

grocery.desc: H Mart (Hanahreum Mart) is a Canadian branch of a large Korean-founded supermarket chain specializing in Asian groceries, fresh produce, seafood, and specialty food items. The Richmond location sits within a shopping centre on Hazelbridge Way and serves the city's substantial Asian-Canadian community. Touring cyclists will find an extensive selection of packaged foods, fresh fruit, and pantry staples well suited for resupply.

visitor.name: Penticton Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Penticton Community Centre is a City of Penticton–operated public facility offering a pool and fitness room to residents and visitors in the South Okanagan. As a full-service municipal rec centre, it has the potential to serve touring cyclists needing showers or a place to freshen up mid-route. Penticton sits at the heart of several major cycling corridors including the Kettle Valley Rail Trail.

visitor.name: Goldstream Suspension Bridge
visitor.desc: The Goldstream Suspension Bridge is a striking pedestrian and cycling feature spanning a forested river gorge in the greater Goldstream/Sooke Hills wilderness area west of Victoria. It sits along a popular trail network managed by the Capital Regional District and serves as a scenic highlight on the Vancouver Crossing Loop route. Touring cyclists passing through the region frequently use it as a landmark waypoint amid old-growth Douglas fir and western red cedar.

visitor.name: Chown Adult Centre
visitor.desc: Chown Adult Centre is a community centre in Vancouver's east side serving adult residents with programming and shared facilities. As a publicly accessible community hub, it may offer basic amenities useful to touring cyclists passing through the neighbourhood. The centre is located near East 15th Avenue in a residential area of Vancouver.

visitor.name: Heritage Park
visitor.desc: Heritage Park Museum is a living history museum set on nearly 2 acres overlooking the City of Terrace, featuring several historical log buildings and artifacts drawn from across the region. Exhibits weave together themes of mining, telegraph lines, logging, pioneer life, and farming, representing the area's history up to 1950. The museum offers guided public tours, audio tours in English and French, and a full range of accessibility-focused options including wheelchair-accessible and sensory-friendly tours.

visitor.name: Planet Bee - ferme de miel
visitor.desc: Planet Bee is a working honey farm and meadery on the outskirts of Vernon, BC, where visitors can observe on-site beehives, stroll bee-friendly gardens, and sample honey and mead at the daily tasting bar — all free of charge. The farm produces Western Canada's largest curated selection of raw honey, bottled by hand on-site in the Okanagan Valley. Educational group presentations are offered seasonally, making it a genuinely engaging stop for curious travellers.

detail.address: 5011 Bella Vista Road, Vernon, BC V1H 1A1

visitor.name: West Richmond Community Centre
visitor.desc: West Richmond Community Centre is a City of Richmond–operated public recreation facility serving the western part of Richmond, BC. It is part of the city's municipal network of community centres delivering programs and activities for residents of all ages. Touring cyclists in the Richmond area may find it a useful urban waypoint, though specific cyclist-facing services are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Historic Downtown Abbotsford
visitor.desc: Historic Downtown Abbotsford is a walkable heritage neighbourhood established in 1891, sitting on the unceded territory of the Semá:th and Mathxwí First Nations and home to over 225 businesses including boutique retailers, award-winning restaurants, galleries, and murals. The Abbotsford Downtown Business Association manages a dedicated outdoor events space called Open Space and hosts seasonal festivals such as Berry Fest and Winter Jubilee. Touring cyclists will find a dense cluster of dining and shopping options within a compact, strollable footprint in the Fraser Valley.

detail.address: 33660 South Fraser Way, Abbotsford, BC V2S 2B9

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 205+ restaurants and describes an award-winning food and coffee culture throughout the downtown district

visitor.name: Guildford Recreation Centre Pool
visitor.desc: Guildford Recreation Centre Pool is a large municipal aquatic facility operated by the City of Surrey, featuring an 80-metre, 8-lane competition-capable pool. It is part of the broader Guildford Recreation Centre complex in Surrey's Guildford neighbourhood. Touring cyclists passing through the Surrey area may find it a useful stop for a swim and associated change facilities.

visitor.name: Fernie Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Fernie Aquatic Centre is a City of Fernie-operated indoor aquatic facility featuring a six-lane 25-metre competitive pool, a warm leisure pool for young children, a 25-person hot tub, and a steam room. The centre includes a full-service retail swimming boutique and a comprehensive suite of accessibility features including a pool lift and ramp access. A shower-only access option makes it a practical stop for touring cyclists wanting to freshen up mid-route.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Facility admission rate table on the official webpage lists 'Shower Only' as a distinct admission category, confirming showers are available to visitors without full aquatic admission

visitor.name: VIRL: Cowichan Lake Branch
visitor.desc: The Cowichan Lake branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library has served its community since informal services began in 1936, moving into a purpose-built facility in 2013. It holds a collection of more than 14,500 items and offers six public-access computers alongside free Wi-Fi. For touring cyclists passing through Lake Cowichan, it provides a welcoming public space to get online, rest, and access local resources.

visitor.name: Xinde Antique Gallery
visitor.desc: Xinde Antique Gallery is a gallery specializing in antiques located in a commercial unit on Number 3 Road in Richmond, BC. It sits along one of Richmond's main arterial corridors, making it a potential stop for cyclists exploring the city's cultural offerings. The gallery's focus on antiques suggests a curated collection likely of interest to visitors seeking distinctive local finds.

visitor.name: Bert Flinn Park
visitor.desc: Bert Flinn Park is a nature reserve in Port Moody, BC, offering natural green space within an urban area. It is managed by the City of Port Moody and provides trail access through forested terrain. Touring cyclists passing through the Tri-Cities area may find it a worthwhile stop for a natural respite.

visitor.name: VPL: Collingwood Branch
visitor.desc: The Collingwood Branch is one of the Vancouver Public Library's neighbourhood locations, situated on the busy Kingsway corridor in East Vancouver. It occupies a two-storey retail building and serves the surrounding Collingwood and Renfrew communities with free public library services. For a touring cyclist, it offers a publicly accessible urban rest stop with the resources of a full library branch.

visitor.name: Greater Vernon Athletics Park
visitor.desc: A municipal athletics park in Vernon managed by the Regional District of North Okanagan. It functions as a sports centre, likely oriented toward organized athletics and field sports rather than general recreation or tourism.

visitor.name: SS Naramata
visitor.desc: The SS Naramata is a historic tugboat preserved at the S.S. Sicamous Marine Heritage Park on the Penticton waterfront, alongside the famous SS Sicamous sternwheeler and other Okanagan lake vessels. The park interprets over a century of inland marine transportation history in the Okanagan Valley, with connections to the Kettle Valley Railway era that cycling tourists on the KVR trail will find compelling. It is run by the S.S. Sicamous Marine Heritage Society, a volunteer-driven nonprofit dedicated to education and community outreach.

detail.address: 1099 Lakeshore Drive West, Penticton, BC V2A 1B7

visitor.name: Museum of the Cariboo-Chilcotin
visitor.desc: The Museum of the Cariboo-Chilcotin is a regional history museum in Williams Lake and the home of the BC Cowboy Hall of Fame, with exhibits spanning First Nations peoples, ranching and rodeo culture, railway history, mining, and forestry. The museum features rotating exhibitions including a powerful collection documenting the 2017 Cariboo Chilcotin wildfires. Located directly off Highway 97, it offers touring cyclists a rich cultural detour into the deep heritage of British Columbia's interior.

detail.address: B-1660 Broadway Ave S, Williams Lake, BC V2G 2W4

visitor.name: Koksilah River Park
visitor.desc: Koksilah River Park is an undeveloped provincial park on southern Vancouver Island, tucked along the Koksilah River and Canyon about 7 km west of Shawnigan Lake within the Vancouver Island Forest Reserve. Visitors come for rustic hiking routes, river swimming, and canoeing or kayaking in a quiet forested setting with no crowds or developed infrastructure. Access is via Renfrew Road, a logging road off Shawnigan Lake Road, making it a scenic detour for touring cyclists exploring the Cowichan Valley.

visitor.name: Mountain Fitness Center
visitor.desc: Mountain Fitness Center is a community gym in Squamish that has operated since 2015 with a focus on making fitness enjoyable and accessible for locals and visitors alike. It offers full facility access through memberships and drop-in passes, group fitness classes included with membership, and personal training from a credentialed team that includes kinesiologists and athletic therapists. Squamish is a world-class mountain biking and outdoor recreation hub, making this gym a potential resource for touring athletes seeking cross-training or recovery facilities.

visitor.name: Aberdeen Tiny Library
visitor.desc: Opened in 2023, the Aberdeen Tiny Library is only 352 square feet — the smallest branch in the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system — and is located inside a mall on the Trans-Canada Highway in southwest Kamloops. It is the first new library location in Kamloops since 1974, serving a rapidly growing part of the city. A touring cyclist passing through can access free Wi-Fi and library resources in a wheelchair-accessible, climate-controlled space.

visitor.name: Kelowna Community Theatre
visitor.desc: Kelowna Community Theatre is a municipally operated performing arts venue on the downtown Kelowna waterfront, hosting live theatre, concerts, and community events. It has its own Wikipedia entry (Wikidata Q14874642), reflecting its standing as a significant cultural landmark in the Okanagan. A touring cyclist exploring Kelowna's vibrant downtown would find it situated near the lakefront promenade.

visitor.name: Hillcrest Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: Hillcrest Aquatic Centre is a public City of Vancouver recreation facility focused on swimming, situated in the Hillcrest neighbourhood near Queen Elizabeth Park. It is part of Vancouver's municipal parks and recreation network, making it a convenient mid-ride stop for cyclists exploring the central and south Vancouver area. The facility serves both drop-in and program participants.

visitor.name: 47 Mile Sport Complex
visitor.desc: The 47 Mile Sports Complex is Clinton's community arena, offering both ice surface and dry-floor rentals for events ranging from hockey tournaments to weddings and flea markets. Managed by the Village of Clinton, it serves as a multi-purpose gathering hub for this small Cariboo Highway community. Touring cyclists passing through Clinton could potentially use it as a landmark or event venue, but no dedicated cycling services are advertised.

visitor.name: Sunnyside Acres Urban Wildlife Area
visitor.desc: Sunnyside Acres Urban Forest Park is a 140-hectare second-growth forest park in South Surrey, operated by the City of Surrey. The forest regenerated after logging in the early 1900s and is home to birds, coyotes, and black-tailed deer. Touring cyclists can explore a network of nature trails through this urban wilderness.

visitor.name: GVPL: Central Branch
visitor.desc: The Central Branch is the flagship location of the Greater Victoria Public Library system, situated in downtown Victoria. It houses the Heritage Room, a broad physical and digital collection, and public computer access, making it a genuine community hub. Touring cyclists passing through the city core may find it a convenient stop for connectivity and rest.

visitor.name: FVRL: Dean Drysdale Library
visitor.desc: A branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system located in Langley's Walnut Grove neighbourhood. The library offers public computers, free Wi-Fi, and a fully accessible ground-level facility with outdoor bike racks — a handy stop for touring cyclists needing a rest, a charge, or a read.

detail.address: 8889 Walnut Grove Drive, Langley, BC V1M 2N7

visitor.name: SL: Port Kells Branch
visitor.desc: Port Kells Branch is a compact (1,200 sq ft) neighbourhood public library in Surrey's Port Kells area, operated by Surrey Libraries. It offers free computers, free Wi-Fi (including Eduroam for university students), self-checkout, and a 24-hour book return drop. The branch is notably car-dependent — the nearest bus stop is 1.8 km away — which is worth noting for cyclists navigating to or from the site.

visitor.name: Cheakamus River Suspension Bridge
visitor.desc: The Cheakamus River Suspension Bridge spans the Cheakamus River near Whistler's Cheakamus Crossing/Function Junction area, providing the primary legal access to the celebrated Train Wreck site—a forest clearing where boxcars from a 1956 railway derailment remain among towering old-growth cedar and fir. The suspension footbridge has a locomotive-inspired design and connects directly to the Sea to Sky Trail, making it accessible to trail cyclists and hikers alike. The surrounding site has evolved into a free, open-air graffiti art gallery that local photographers, trail runners, and mountain bikers have long frequented.

visitor.name: Glen Harper Curling Centre
visitor.desc: The Glen Harper Curling Centre is home to the Duncan Curling Club, one of Vancouver Island's established curling communities offering weekly leagues for seniors, juniors, mixed, and recreational players of all skill levels. The facility hosts a full seasonal calendar of bonspiels and its lounge is available for private events ranging from weddings to corporate gatherings. Cyclists passing through Duncan in the cooler months could drop in for a firsthand look at this quintessentially Canadian sport.

visitor.name: Schubert Centre
visitor.desc: The Schubert Centre is a volunteer-run community hub in Vernon primarily serving seniors, offering social and recreational programs, a drop-in coffee shop, thrift store, Meals on Wheels, and several rentable event spaces ranging from intimate meeting rooms to a 300-person hall. It receives no provincial or federal funding and relies on its food services, catering, and donations to keep the doors open. A touring cyclist could stop in for a break at the social café, which is open to the public.

notes.Café or food on site: On-site coffee shop described as 'an inviting and versatile space' open to the public; full food services including lunch menu and catering also offered

visitor.name: Spirit Garden
visitor.desc: Spirit Garden is a free-access community garden in Victoria managed by the City. Located on Kings Road, it offers a peaceful green-space stop for touring cyclists passing through the neighbourhood.

visitor.name: Parkview Activity Centre
visitor.desc: Parkview Activity Centre is a City of Kamloops-operated community centre located in the North Shore neighbourhood of Kamloops. It is part of the city's broader recreation and culture network, offering programming for residents. As a neighbourhood activity hub, it may serve as a convenient rest point for cyclists moving through the area, though specific cycling amenities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: White Rock Community Centre
visitor.desc: The White Rock Community Centre is a City of White Rock-operated multipurpose facility housing a fitness gym, dance studio, arts room, gallery, presentation hall, and several rentable meeting spaces. Situated on Russell Avenue in the coastal city of White Rock, it serves as the primary hub for community programs, cultural events, and recreational activities for residents and visitors. Touring cyclists passing through White Rock may find it a convenient central facility, though no cycling-specific amenities are advertised on the website.

detail.address: 15154 Russell Avenue, White Rock, BC V4B 0A6

visitor.name: Stephens Coyote Ridge Regional Park
visitor.desc: Stephens Coyote Ridge Regional Park is a regional nature reserve near Kelowna managed by the Regional District of Central Okanagan. It is part of a network of 30 regional parks encompassing over 2,100 hectares, with designated trails winding through Central Okanagan landscapes. The park is day-use only, offering a natural rest stop or side trip for touring cyclists exploring the Kelowna area.

visitor.name: Fraser Library
visitor.desc: Fraser Library is the Surrey branch of Simon Fraser University Library, located inside SFU's Central City campus in the heart of Surrey's city centre. It serves the SFU Surrey community with research resources, study spaces, and technology access, and is open to the public per OSM access tags. A touring cyclist could stop here for Wi-Fi, a quiet indoor rest, and proximity to the Central City transit hub.

visitor.name: Ukrainian Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: A community hub operated by the Ukrainian-Canadian Cultural Society of Vancouver Island, dedicated to preserving and celebrating Ukrainian-Canadian heritage on Vancouver Island. The centre hosts cultural events, Ukrainian supper nights with homemade perogies and cabbage rolls, a Ukrainian library, gift shop, dance programs, and choirs. Located on Douglas Street in Victoria, it doubles as a licensed event venue with a spacious hall, stage, and kitchen facilities.

notes.Café or food on site: Ukrainian suppers with homemade perogies, cabbage rolls, and sausage served at scheduled community events; catering services also available; prominent 'BUY UKRAINIAN FOOD' option on website

visitor.name: Howard Horel Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: Howard Horel Nature Reserve is a 25-hectare protected area on Salt Spring Island within the globally rare Coastal Douglas-fir zone, featuring forested terrain, rocky bluffs, Garry oak, small wetlands, and streams flowing into upper Fulford Creek. The reserve harbours seven Species at Risk and was acquired in 2018 through an anonymous donation honouring a long-time Salt Spring family. Touring cyclists can access the reserve's easy trail network via Bryant Hill Park, reached from the end of Mereside Road or Sarah Way.

detail.address: 265 Blackburn Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2B8

visitor.name: Abkhazi Garden
visitor.desc: Abkhazi Garden is a historic show garden in Victoria's Fairfield neighbourhood, operated by The Land Conservancy of British Columbia as one of its featured conservation projects. The garden is publicly accessible with donations requested, set on a heritage property preserved as a naturalistic landscape. It sits within easy cycling distance of downtown Victoria and offers a quiet green respite for touring cyclists passing through the city.

visitor.name: Hill's Native Art Gallerty
visitor.desc: Hill's Native Art is a long-established BC chain specializing in Indigenous Canadian art, jewelry, and cultural items. The Vancouver Broadway location brings authentic First Nations artwork to a neighbourhood commercial strip in Vancouver. Touring cyclists passing through would encounter a curated gallery focused on West Coast Indigenous traditions.

visitor.name: The Tennis Centre
visitor.desc: The Tennis Centre is a multi-location indoor and outdoor tennis facility founded by coach Larry Jurovich, who has coached players to Grand Slam appearances and served as Head of Coach Education for the UK's Lawn Tennis Association. The Coquitlam location opened in 2017 as the network's second site, part of a vision to make tennis accessible beyond the traditional country-club model. A touring cyclist arriving here would find a dedicated sports facility, though current operational status of this specific location is uncertain.

visitor.name: Visitor Center
visitor.desc: The Whistler Visitor Centre is Whistler's official in-resort information hub, staffed by knowledgeable Tourism Whistler employees who can assist with accommodation, activity bookings, transit schedules, and broader BC travel planning. Located adjacent to the bus and taxi loop at 4230 Gateway Drive, it is a natural stopping point for anyone arriving by public transit or exploring the valley. Touring cyclists would find it particularly useful for local maps, event listings, and regional destination information.

visitor.name: Langham Court Theatre
visitor.desc: Langham Court Theatre is one of Western Canada's longest-running community theatres, operating for over 95 years out of a converted 1876 carriage house tucked into Victoria's residential Rockland neighbourhood. The 175-seat venue produces five shows per season ranging from Shakespeare to contemporary drama and offers a licensed lounge for intermissions and receptions. Cycling visitors to Victoria exploring the Rockland area—near the Art Gallery of Greater Victoria and the Lieutenant Governor's residence—will find a charming neighbourhood theatre worth an evening stop.

visitor.name: Willingdon Community Centre
visitor.desc: Willingdon Community Centre is a City of Burnaby-operated civic recreation facility set within Willingdon Heights Park in northwest Burnaby. It offers weight and cardio rooms, fitness and yoga classes, and gym and racquet sports alongside children's and preschool programs. As a publicly accessible facility in a park setting, it could serve as an urban rest point for cyclists riding through the area, though no dedicated cycling services are advertised.

visitor.name: Mary Winspear Centre
visitor.desc: The Mary Winspear Centre is a 30,000 sq ft non-profit community and performing arts venue in Sidney, BC, hosting theatre productions, concerts, art exhibitions, conferences, and community celebrations. Operated by the Saanich Peninsula Memorial Park Society, the wheelchair-accessible facility includes the Charlie White Theatre, Bodine Family Hall, an art gallery, and meeting rooms.
