Situated close to the BC Ferries Swartz Bay terminal and with a seaside setting, it is a cultural hub for visitors arriving on the Saanich Peninsula by bike or ferry.

visitor.name: Vancouver Whale Watch
visitor.desc: Established in 1998, Vancouver Whale Watch is the original whale watching company in Vancouver, departing from the historic fishing village of Steveston in Richmond. Tours run 3 to 5 hours through the Gulf Islands and Strait of Georgia aboard a fleet of zodiacs, with professional wildlife guides focused on Orcas, Humpback Whales, and other marine life. The company boasts a 98% whale sighting rate and offers a lifetime free return guarantee if no whale is spotted.

visitor.name: West Vancouver Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: West Vancouver Recreation Centre is a public recreation facility serving the District of West Vancouver on BC's North Shore. It is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a tourist attraction and represents a significant community hub situated near popular North Shore and Sea-to-Sky cycling routes.

visitor.name: The Hive
visitor.desc: The Hive Vancouver Heights is a dedicated bouldering gym occupying a three-storey commercial building in Vancouver's industrial east side. It is part of a multi-location climbing chain with a second Hive location (Vancouver Boulder) just steps away at 520 Industrial Ave. Cycling tourists with a taste for indoor climbing will find it easy to reach by bike given its location in a flat industrial corridor.

visitor.name: The Cultch
visitor.desc: The Cultch is a landmark community arts hub in East Vancouver, presenting over 20 productions per year across three theatre spaces — the Historic Theatre, Vancity Culture Lab, and York Theatre — as well as a gallery and multi-use spaces. Operating since 1973, it programs contemporary work in theatre, dance, music, circus, and visual arts from local, national, and international artists, and underwent a $30 million refurbishment under its current Executive Director. A touring cyclist arriving in East Van will find a vibrant cultural destination known for diverse, risk-taking programming and strong community ties.

visitor.name: Steveston Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: Steveston Outdoor Pool is a City of Richmond–operated seasonal outdoor swimming facility located in the historic Steveston fishing village neighbourhood. Sitting near the Steveston waterfront, it is a classic community pool well-positioned for cyclists riding the popular Richmond dyke trail network. The pool operates as a summer destination, making it a natural cooling-off stop on a warm-weather tour of the Fraser River delta.

visitor.name: ORL: UBCO Branch
visitor.desc: The ORL UBCO Branch is a public library branch of the Okanagan Regional Library system located on the University of British Columbia Okanagan campus in Kelowna. It functions primarily as a holds pick-up location with a small selection of popular materials, and is staffed only on Tuesday mornings and during occasional special events. Multiple bus routes serve the campus, and the building's book drop is always accessible.

visitor.name: Centennial Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: Centennial Outdoor Pool is a City of Port Coquitlam-operated outdoor swimming facility located on Chester Street in the Tri-Cities area. Run by the municipality as part of its aquatics programming alongside spray parks and indoor pools, it offers a seasonal aquatic destination for residents and visitors. The facility is wheelchair accessible and charges an admission fee, making it a potential summer refreshment stop for touring cyclists passing through Port Coquitlam.

visitor.name: NVDPL: Capilano Branch
visitor.desc: The Capilano Branch of the North Vancouver District Public Library is a community cornerstone located in the heart of Edgemont Village, offering a reading area, children's and teen sections, a quiet study room, and public computer workstations. Uniquely, the NVDPL system lists E-Cargo Bikes among its borrowable items, making this library system of direct interest to cycling-curious visitors. Free Wi-Fi and an accessible central location make it a practical stop for touring cyclists passing through North Vancouver's residential hillside neighbourhoods.

detail.address: 3045 Highland Blvd, North Vancouver, BC V7R 2X4

visitor.name: Castlegar Museum
visitor.desc: The CPR Station Museum occupies a beautifully preserved 100+ year old Canadian Pacific Railway station in Castlegar, considered one of the finest remaining examples of its kind in British Columbia. The museum explores the railway and pioneer heritage of the Columbia River Valley through exhibits, newspaper archives, and a restored station agent's residence on the upper floor. The same society also manages nearby Zuckerberg Island Heritage Park, featuring a Russian Orthodox-influenced chapel house, a 473-foot military-built suspension bridge, and over 8 hectares of river woodland trails.

notes.Wi-Fi: Gift shop page states: 'the museum offers Internet access for visitors and residents to use free of charge'

visitor.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
visitor.desc: VanDusen Botanical Garden is a 55-acre urban oasis in Vancouver's Shaughnessy neighbourhood, home to over 7,500 plant species from around the world. The garden hosts seasonal exhibitions, botanical education programs, and features both a fine-dining restaurant and a casual Garden Café inside the LEED-certified Visitor Centre. The accessibility page explicitly encourages arriving by bike, transit, or car, making it a natural destination for cycle tourists exploring central Vancouver.

notes.Café or food on site: Shaughnessy Restaurant (fine dining, lunch/afternoon tea/dinner/weekend brunch) and The Garden Café (Fair Trade coffee, sandwiches, soups) both located on site at VanDusen

visitor.name: Belfry Theatre
visitor.desc: The Belfry Theatre is a professional theatre company housed in a beautifully restored 19th-century heritage church in Victoria's eclectic Fernwood neighbourhood. Now celebrating its 50th anniversary, it produces contemporary plays from the international repertoire with a focus on new Canadian work. The intimate venue places every audience member no more than 8 metres (25 feet) from the stage, making for an unusually close and engaging experience.

notes.Café or food on site: Website navigation includes a dedicated 'Food & Beverage' section under the Plan menu, indicating food/beverage service is available at the venue

visitor.name: McKitrick Garden
visitor.desc: McKitrick Garden is a publicly accessible garden operated by the City of Delta as part of its environmental sustainability initiatives. Situated in the Delta municipality of Metro Vancouver, it appears to serve an educational or demonstration role connected to the city's environmental programmes. Visiting cyclists would find a free, open-access green space, though specific visitor facilities are not documented on the city's website.

visitor.name: Haida Heritage Centre at Kay Llnagaay
visitor.desc: The Haida Heritage Centre at Ḵay Llnagaay is an award-winning Indigenous cultural attraction on Haida Gwaii, designed to resemble a traditional oceanside Haida village and spanning 50,000 square feet of museum, performance, carving, and canoe spaces. It sits at the ancient village site of 'Sea-Lion Town' and houses the Haida Gwaii Museum alongside a bistro, teaching centre, and rotating cultural programming. Located just a 10-minute walk from the Skidegate ferry landing, it is a natural first stop for cyclists arriving on the island by BC Ferries.

notes.Café or food on site: About page lists 'Ḵay Bistro' as one of the named spaces housed within the centre

visitor.name: Summerland Arena
visitor.desc: Summerland Arena is a publicly operated multi-sport indoor facility managed by the District of Summerland, hosting ice skating, curling, ice hockey, broomball, and lacrosse. It is a community hub for local sport in the South Okanagan. Touring cyclists passing through Summerland may find it a useful landmark, but it functions primarily as a local sports venue rather than a cycling-oriented attraction.

visitor.name: Sprit Rock Climbing Center
visitor.desc: Spirit Rock Climbing Center is a three-story indoor climbing gym in the heart of Kimberley's Platzl, open since 2013. It offers bouldering, auto-belays, top-rope and lead climbing on walls ranging from 8 to 50 feet, welcoming all ages and abilities with no experience or booking required. The facility also has a retail shop for climbing gear and runs youth and adult programs.

detail.address: 110 Deer Park Ave, Kimberley, BC V1A 2J4

visitor.name: Kaatza Station Museum & Archives
visitor.desc: The Kaatza Station Museum and Archives occupies the original 1913 Canadian Pacific train station in Lake Cowichan, operated by the Kaatza Historical Society since 1975. The museum focuses on the Cowichan Lake region's history with particular depth on the forestry industry, the IWA union, and ethnic minority communities. Outdoor grounds feature rolling stock including a Shay steam locomotive, a Plymouth Switcher, a CN passenger car, and restored historic structures such as the Bell Tower School.

detail.address: 125B South Shore Road, Lake Cowichan, BC V0R 2G0

visitor.name: UBC Botanical Garden
visitor.desc: An outdoor amphitheatre nestled within UBC Botanical Garden, Canada's oldest university botanical garden spanning 20 hectares on Vancouver's west side. The garden is home to over 5,300 different kinds of plants and features attractions like the GreenHeart TreeWalk, Nitobe Memorial Garden, and various themed garden collections. Touring cyclists exploring the UBC campus area will find this a peaceful stop combining nature, science, and culture.

visitor.name: Grouse Mountain Regional Park
visitor.desc: Grouse Mountain Regional Park is a Metro Vancouver regional park and nature reserve situated in North Vancouver, managed by Metro Vancouver's regional parks system. It is home to the Grouse Grind, a strenuous trail famously known as 'nature's StairMaster,' making it a popular destination for active outdoor visitors. Touring cyclists riding into North Vancouver may consider it a scenic endpoint or detour, though the terrain is rugged and the park is oriented primarily toward hiking.

visitor.name: Kirkland House
visitor.desc: Kirkland House is a fully restored 1911 Edwardian farmhouse situated within over two acres of groomed gardens inside Hawthorne Grove Park in Ladner, maintained entirely by the volunteer-run Kirkland House Foundation. The site features heritage architecture, a gazebo built by Delta Secondary students, a model train room, and an agricultural display shed. Owned by the City of Delta and freely accessible to the public, it offers a genuine window into early 20th-century pioneer farm life in the Fraser Delta.

visitor.name: Bing Kee Food Forest
visitor.desc: Bing Kee Food Forest is a publicly accessible community food forest in Nanaimo, BC, listed under the City's parks and community gardens network. Food forests are designed to mimic layered forest ecosystems while producing edible plants, offering a distinctive green-space experience compared to conventional parks. Cyclists exploring Nanaimo's urban greenways may find it a pleasant and unusual detour.

visitor.name: VIRL: Bowser Branch
visitor.desc: The Bowser Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library opened in 2008 as VIRL's first purpose-built library building, featuring large locally sourced beams and a West Coast architectural style. Situated in this small coastal community along the Island Highway corridor, it functions as a lively community hub offering free WiFi, public computers, a seed library, and a reading nook. Touring cyclists passing through the Bowser area will find a welcoming, no-cost indoor rest space with internet access.

detail.address: 6996 West Island Highway, Bowser, BC V0R 1G0

visitor.name: Art Gallery Of Golden-Kicking Horse Culture
visitor.desc: The Art Gallery of Golden (AGOG) is a non-profit gallery and studio gift shop in downtown Golden that serves as a cultural hub for the Columbia Valley. It presents 8–10 exhibitions annually featuring contemporary and regional work, and the Studio Gift Shop carries pieces from over 100 artists across the Columbia River Basin. Part of the broader Kicking Horse Culture organization, the gallery is a worthwhile stop for touring cyclists passing through Golden.

visitor.name: The Core
visitor.desc: Whistler Core Climbing & Fitness Gym is a full-service training facility located in the lower level of the Whistler Conference Center in Whistler Village. It offers a climbing gym with bouldering, top-roping, auto-belays, and an adjustable training wall, alongside a comprehensive fitness floor featuring Olympic weightlifting platforms, cardio equipment, and a functional fitness studio. The gym also runs guided outdoor rock climbing experiences, making it a hub for active visitors seeking both indoor training and backcountry adventure.

visitor.name: Centennial Theatre
visitor.desc: Centennial Theatre has anchored North Vancouver's cultural life since 1966, presenting multi-disciplinary performances ranging from folk festivals to Vancouver Symphony Orchestra concerts in the mid-Lonsdale neighbourhood. Operated by North Vancouver Recreation & Culture, it also serves as a home stage for local schools and community groups, and hosts high-profile events like the Vancouver International Mountain Film Festival. A touring cyclist exploring the Lonsdale corridor would find this a notable cultural landmark within easy reach of the waterfront.

visitor.name: The Adventure Group
visitor.desc: Operating under the brand 'The Adventure Group,' this multi-activity adventure complex sits on Cougar Mountain just north of Whistler and offers whitewater rafting, ziplining, side-by-side off-road tours, an aerial obstacle course, snowmobile and snowshoe tours, and the Vallea Lumina night walk. A free shuttle runs from Whistler Village to the base camp, where guests can also eat at an on-site café. It bills itself as Whistler's only local whitewater rafting operation.

detail.address: Sixteen Mile Creek Forest Service Road, Whistler, BC V0N 1B8

notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'enjoy food from our café' and 'grab a tasty bite at our café' at the base camp

visitor.name: Davies Park
visitor.desc: Davies Park is a nature reserve on Bowen Island, operated by the Bowen Island Municipality. It sits within the Howe Sound region, an area of significant natural beauty accessible by ferry from Horseshoe Bay. Touring cyclists exploring Bowen Island may pass through or near the park as part of a day trip or island loop.

visitor.name: ORL: Naramata Branch
visitor.desc: The Naramata Branch of the Okanagan Regional Library is a small community library in this Okanagan wine-country village, part of the 30-branch ORL system serving over 399,000 people across the region. The branch offers three public internet computers, a permanently accessible outdoor book drop, and hosts regular community programs including knitting groups and preschool storytimes. Free parking, including an accessible space, is available directly in front of the building.

visitor.name: Cloverdale Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Cloverdale Recreation Centre is a City of Surrey municipal facility serving the historic Cloverdale neighbourhood with a broad range of indoor recreation programs for all ages. The centre is publicly accessible and offers fitness, aquatic, and community programming on a drop-in and registered basis. Touring cyclists passing through Surrey's eastern suburbs may find it a useful urban waypoint, though cyclist-specific services are not advertised.

visitor.name: Kaslo Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Kaslo Visitor Centre is the official tourism information office for Kaslo and the surrounding Kootenay Lake area, operated by the Kootenay Lake Historical Society. Situated in the charming lakeside town of Kaslo in the West Kootenays, it serves as a natural first stop for visitors seeking local knowledge and regional resources. Touring cyclists arriving in Kaslo would likely find it a useful hub for area route information and local orientation.

visitor.name: Butterfly World
visitor.desc: Butterfly World is an indoor tropical garden attraction in Coombs, BC, home to hundreds of free-flying live butterflies along with reptiles, small birds, and other invertebrates. The grounds also include a turtle pond, an outdoor water garden, and an orchid garden, making it a multi-faceted natural-world experience. Coombs sits on a popular Vancouver Island cycling corridor near the famous Old Country Market, so visiting cyclists will find it a natural stop.

visitor.name: Gabriola Island Community Hall
visitor.desc: The Gabriola Island Community Hall is a beloved 100-year-old institution at the south end of Gabriola Island, rebuilt by volunteers in 1984 after the original hall burned down in 1979. It serves as the social heart of the island, hosting weddings, dances, meetings, theatre, badminton, and its signature Annual Salmon BBQ — now in its 70th year. A cyclist riding South Road will pass this historic landmark, which is a genuine window into small-island BC community life.

visitor.name: Alma VanDusen Garden
visitor.desc: VanDusen Botanical Garden is a 55-acre public oasis in the heart of Vancouver, home to over 7,500 plant species and varieties from around the world. It features a landmark Visitor Centre built to living-building standards, formal garden rooms, and a maze, alongside fine dining at the Shaughnessy Restaurant and a casual Garden Cafe. Cyclists exploring Vancouver's west side will find it a leafy, well-maintained destination worth a stop.

notes.Café or food on site: Two venues confirmed: Shaughnessy Restaurant (fine dining, open for lunch, afternoon tea, dinner, and weekend brunch) and The Garden Cafe inside the Visitor Centre (coffees, sandwiches, soups)

visitor.name: The Roxy
visitor.desc: The Roxy is an independent neighbourhood movie theatre in Victoria's North Park area, screening a mix of new releases, classic films, Studio Ghibli retrospectives, and community events like talent show socials. Its eclectic programming and intimate single-screen format make it a distinctive cultural stop for visitors exploring the city by bike.

notes.Café or food on site: Privacy policy references 'Online ticket or concession purchases,' confirming concession sales on site

visitor.name: Rotary Centre for the Arts
visitor.desc: The Rotary Centre for the Arts is Kelowna's primary arts and culture hub, operating multiple gallery spaces, performance venues, and artist studios in the downtown core. It presents a year-round slate of live performances, art education programs, and community events, and has earned Silver at the Best of Kelowna Awards every year since 2014. The on-site Roma Nord Bistro adds a dining option for visitors catching a show or exploring the centre's exhibitions.

notes.Café or food on site: Roma Nord Bistro is listed as an on-site venue under the Venue section of the website

visitor.name: Blue Dog Kayaking
visitor.desc: Blue Dog Kayaking is a Paddle Canada-certified sea kayaking and paddleboarding collective operating out of Mill Bay Marina, offering instruction from beginner to advanced levels including guide and instructor certification courses. Founded in 2015, it has grown into a collaborative model where independent instructors run their own programs under a shared framework, with a particular commitment to inclusive and women-specific programming. Touring cyclists passing through Mill Bay can access the marina waterfront for a paddle break or take a guided trip into the surrounding coastal waters.

visitor.name: The Plaza Galleries
visitor.desc: The Plaza Galleries is a contemporary fine art gallery established in 1996, situated in the heart of Whistler Village overlooking the 2010 Olympic Rings. Specializing in art inspired by wildlife, mountain scenery, and winter sports, the gallery exhibits both established and emerging artists from its location within the Whistler Blackcomb resort community. It is steps away from the Maury Young Arts Centre and the Audain Art Museum, making it part of a walkable cultural cluster in the village core.

visitor.name: East Delta Community Hall
visitor.desc: East Delta Community Hall — originally opened in 1931 as the McKee Athletic Hall — is a two-storey heritage building on a prominent corner of Ladner Trunk Road in the agricultural flatlands of Delta. Operated by the McKee Athletic Association, the hall is available for private functions of up to 190 people and hosts community events such as artisan holiday markets. Its roadside visibility and historic character make it a recognizable landmark for cyclists touring Delta's farmland routes.

detail.address: 10379 Ladner Trunk Road, Delta, BC V4G1K2

visitor.name: Bear Creek Gardens
visitor.desc: Bear Creek Gardens is a free public botanical garden hidden within Bear Creek Park in Surrey, surrounded by second-growth forest of Cottonwoods, Alders, and Western Red Cedars. Originally cleared and seeded in 1973, the garden has grown to include a Rhododendron Bed, Heather Bed, Conifer Bed, a Native Walk featuring Pacific Northwest plants, and a watercourse with pond. A pleasant stop for touring cyclists riding through the Fraser Valley, offering a peaceful forested setting just off 88 Avenue.

visitor.name: VIRL: Port Clements Branch
visitor.desc: The Port Clements branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served this small Haida Gwaii community since 1983, and relocated to its current Cedar Avenue home in 2009. The branch is housed in a multiplex alongside the Village of Port Clements municipal office and the local elementary school, making it a genuine community hub. For touring cyclists on Haida Gwaii—one of BC's most remote and scenically dramatic cycling destinations—it represents a rare public facility and rest stop in an area with very limited services.

detail.address: 36 West Cedar Avenue, Port Clements, V0T 1R0

visitor.name: Kimberley Alpine Resort
visitor.desc: Kimberley Alpine Resort is a four-season mountain resort set between the Selkirk and Rocky Mountains in southeastern BC, boasting over 1,800 acres of terrain and recognised as having North America's largest gladed ski terrain. In summer the resort pivots to offer mountain bike rentals and multi-use trails on the mountain, making it a destination for cyclists as well as skiers. The resort village includes lodging, a full-service restaurant, and a golf course, giving touring cyclists a range of services in one location.

detail.address: 301 North Star Blvd, Kimberley, BC V1A 2Y5

notes.Café or food on site: Buckhorn and Main Restaurant at the base area; website features 'Eat, drink, and après!' with dedicated dining section including Trickle Creek Lodge dining

visitor.name: Norway House
visitor.desc: Norway House (operating as Eidsvold Lodge #7-53, Sons of Norway) is a fraternal community organization in Victoria's Hillside neighbourhood dedicated to Norwegian heritage, cultural programming, and community philanthropy. It occupies a community centre building and hosts events such as concerts and cultural gatherings. Cyclists passing through the area may find it a point of cultural interest.

visitor.name: VPL: Kensington Branch
visitor.desc: The Kensington Branch is a neighborhood outpost of the Vancouver Public Library system, serving the Cedar Cottage area of East Vancouver. It sits within a community hub and offers the full range of public library services. For a touring cyclist cutting through East Vancouver, it is a convenient landmark with potential for a rest break in a climate-controlled public space.

visitor.name: təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre
visitor.desc: A modern aquatic and community centre operated by the City of New Westminster, opened in April 2024. Its name, təməsew̓txʷ (Sea Otter House), reflects the city's commitment to Indigenous reconciliation. The three-storey facility with its distinctive sawtooth roof serves as a recreation and community hub in New Westminster's downtown area.

visitor.name: Lebanon Creek Greenway
visitor.desc: Lebanon Creek Greenway is a nature reserve greenway in the Okanagan region of British Columbia, offering a natural corridor through riparian and forested terrain. For touring cyclists, it represents a scenic detour or rest stop away from road traffic. The greenway is managed as a public park, making it freely accessible to anyone passing through the area.

visitor.name: Bird Museum
visitor.desc: The George C. Reifel Migratory Bird Sanctuary is a 300-hectare managed wetland complex on Westham Island in Delta, BC, managed by the BC Waterfowl Society since 1963 as one of Canada's 92 federal Migratory Bird Sanctuaries. Nearly 300 bird species have been recorded here, and the sanctuary draws over 100,000 visitors a year, making it one of Canada's top birdwatching destinations. Touring cyclists will find a flat, scenic destination on the dykes and trails of the Fraser River Estuary, roughly an hour's ride from Vancouver.

visitor.name: Mount Boucherie Community Centre & Arena
visitor.desc: Royal LePage Place Arena is West Kelowna's premier multipurpose ice facility, built in 2007 with a 1,500-seat capacity and a full NHL-size ice sheet. It serves as home ice for the West Kelowna Warriors of the BC Hockey League and hosts public skating, minor hockey, figure skating, and ringette. The facility also features a free indoor walking track and can accommodate concerts and trade shows.

detail.address: 2760 Cameron Road, West Kelowna, BC, V1Z 2T6

notes.Vending machines: Website explicitly lists 'vending machines' as a facility amenity

visitor.name: Chinese Canadian Military Museum Society
visitor.desc: The Chinese Canadian Military Museum Society, founded in 1998, documents and commemorates the role of Chinese Canadians in Canada's military, with particular focus on the 'unwanted soldiers' who served despite systemic discrimination and whose service was intertwined with the community's fight for equal rights. The museum has expanded beyond military history to surface lesser-known stories of everyday Chinese Canadian life through artifacts, records, and veteran accounts. Located in Vancouver, it offers a distinctive cultural and historical perspective that connects military sacrifice to the broader Chinese Canadian experience.

visitor.name: Bridgeview Community Center
visitor.desc: Bridgeview Community Centre is a City of Surrey municipal recreation facility located in the Whalley neighbourhood, offering drop-in programs, gymnasium access, and various community activities. It serves a residential area of Surrey and provides seniors, youth, and general recreation programming. Touring cyclists passing through Surrey could potentially use it as a rest stop, though it is not a destination attraction.

visitor.name: Mount Pleasant Community Centre
visitor.desc: Mount Pleasant Community Centre is a Vancouver Park Board facility in the heart of the Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, serving the local community with fitness and recreation programs. Its location on Kingsway places it along a busy cycling corridor connecting downtown Vancouver to East Vancouver. As a public community centre, it offers basic amenities that touring cyclists passing through may find useful.

visitor.name: FVRL: Clearbrook Library
visitor.desc: The Clearbrook Library is a community branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, the largest public library network in British Columbia, serving Abbotsford's Clearbrook neighbourhood since 1995. As part of a 25-branch system reaching over 800,000 residents, it offers books, digital resources, public computers, and a range of community programs. For a touring cyclist moving through Abbotsford, it provides a welcoming, publicly accessible rest stop with washrooms and free Wi-Fi.

visitor.name: CRDL: 100 Mile House Branch
visitor.desc: The 100 Mile House Branch of the Cariboo Regional District Library is the public library hub for the South Cariboo region, operated by the Cariboo Regional District. It offers free Wi-Fi, public computers, scanning, and one-on-one tech support — practical amenities for a touring cyclist needing connectivity in a small Interior BC community. The branch also loans a Library of Things collection including specialty items, and hosts regular community programming.

detail.address: 449 South Birch Avenue, 100 Mile House, BC V0K 2E0

visitor.name: Kelowna Art Gallery
visitor.desc: A public art gallery in the heart of downtown Kelowna's Cultural District, featuring four exhibition spaces showcasing contemporary and historical Canadian art along with a permanent collection of nearly 1,000 works. The gallery is a Rainbow Registered non-profit that also offers art classes, workshops, camps, and community events including artist talks and film screenings. Located on Water Street near the waterfront, it makes a worthwhile cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan.

detail.address: 1315 Water Street, Kelowna, BC, Canada V1Y 9R3

visitor.name: Whistler Sliding Centre
visitor.desc: The Whistler Sliding Centre is Canada's only Olympic-standard bobsleigh, luge, and skeleton track, purpose-built for the 2010 Winter Games and perched on the side of Blackcomb Mountain above Whistler Village. Run as a non-profit, it welcomes the public for free self-guided interpretive tours and sightseeing year-round, and offers paid summer bobsleigh experiences that let visitors feel the G-forces of an Olympic run. A touring cyclist looking for a unique off-bike experience in Whistler will find this venue genuinely memorable.

detail.address: 4910 Glacier Ln, Whistler, BC V8E 0C2, Canada

visitor.name: VIRL: Union Bay Branch
visitor.desc: The Union Bay branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library is the smallest branch in the VIRL system at just 300 square feet, adjoined to the historic Union Bay Post Office building constructed in 1913. Open since 1949, it holds a collection of over 4,400 items and offers free public WiFi. For a touring cyclist passing through this small community on the South Island Highway, it represents a rare public facility stop with internet access.

detail.address: 5527 South Island Highway, Union Bay, V0R 3B0

visitor.name: Port Clements Museum
visitor.desc: The Port Clements Museum, built in 1987 and run by the Port Clements Historical Society, documents the pioneer and logging history of Haida Gwaii through more than 2,000 artifacts — including the famous White Raven and a preserved piece of the legendary Kiidk'yass (Golden Spruce). It doubles as the village's tourist information centre, making it a natural first stop for cyclists arriving in Port Clements. The waterfront grounds include a short trail overlooking Stewart Bay with picnic tables and benches.

visitor.name: Killarney Rink
visitor.desc: Killarney Rink is a City of Vancouver-operated civic ice facility offering public ice skating and ice hockey in the Killarney neighbourhood of East Vancouver. As a municipally run arena, it serves both recreational skaters and hockey programs throughout the community. Touring cyclists passing through Southeast Vancouver would find it a recognizable city landmark with wheelchair-accessible access.

visitor.name: The OV Arts Centre
visitor.desc: The OV Arts Centre is a City of Nanaimo-operated cultural facility listed under the municipality's Cultural Spaces & Facilities program. It serves as a dedicated arts venue within Nanaimo's broader parks, recreation, and culture portfolio. Touring cyclists exploring Nanaimo's cultural offerings may find it a worthwhile stop, though specific visitor amenities are not documented in available sources.

visitor.name: Oceanside Place
visitor.desc: Oceanside Place Arena is a publicly operated multi-sport recreation facility in Parksville, managed by the Regional District of Nanaimo. Situated on the West Island Highway, it serves the Oceanside region as a community hub for indoor sport and recreation. Touring cyclists passing through Parksville may find it a convenient stop given its accessible highway-side location.

visitor.name: Sapperton Community Hall
visitor.desc: The Sapperton Community Hall is a historic two-storey, 7,000+ sq ft community gathering space in New Westminster's Sapperton neighbourhood, built in 1962 and operated by the Sapperton Old Age Pensioners Association. It hosts public events ranging from comic book fairs to cultural gatherings, serving as a neighbourhood anchor for one of BC's older working-class communities. Touring cyclists passing through New Westminster may find it a useful local landmark and potential stop, though cyclist-specific facilities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Goldcorp Centre for the Arts
visitor.desc: The Goldcorp Centre for the Arts is SFU's downtown Vancouver arts facility, located in the landmark Woodward's Building on West Hastings Street in the heart of the Downtown Eastside. It serves as a hub for theatre, performance, and arts education under Simon Fraser University's Woodwards campus umbrella, blending academic programming with community and professional arts activity. A touring cyclist visiting Vancouver's urban core would find this venue in a dense, walkable neighbourhood well-connected by cycling infrastructure.

visitor.name: Hyde Creek Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: Hyde Creek Nature Reserve is a protected natural area in Port Coquitlam managed by the City, offering access to riparian habitat and natural trails. It appears in the city's parks directory alongside the Traboulay PoCo Trail, suggesting it may be accessible as part of a broader trail network. Touring cyclists passing through the Tri-Cities area may find it a worthwhile natural detour, though facility details are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Abbotsford Sports Hall of Fame
visitor.desc: The Abbotsford Sports Hall of Fame honours local athletes, coaches, and builders who have achieved national and international recognition in their sports, and is housed on the first floor of the Legacy Sports Centre at Abbotsford Exhibition Park. Founded following the 1995 Western Canada Summer Games, it features inducted plaques and a yearly Wall of Fame recognizing junior athletes. A secondary display of inductee plaques is also located at Abbotsford Centre, making it a small but meaningful stop for cyclists interested in local sporting heritage.

visitor.name: Lord Byng Pool
visitor.desc: Lord Byng Pool is a City of Vancouver public aquatic and recreation centre situated in the Point Grey neighbourhood. In addition to lap and recreational swimming, the facility features a hot tub and sauna, making it a worthwhile rest stop for cyclists looking to recover after a long ride. It is operated by the City of Vancouver Parks, Recreation and Culture department.

visitor.name: Bowen Island Public Library
visitor.desc: Founded in 1924 and housed in the former Old General Store building, the Bowen Island Public Library is a long-standing community hub serving residents and visitors on this ferry-accessed island. It offers an unusually broad range of borrowable items through its 'Library of Things' — including telescope kits, medical equipment, and seed libraries — alongside digital resources, tech tutoring, and rentable meeting space. For a touring cyclist arriving by BC Ferries, it is a convenient first stop with free internet access and a welcoming, community-oriented atmosphere.

detail.address: 430 Bowen Island Trunk Road, Bowen Island, V0N 1G0

visitor.name: Harbour Heritage Centre
visitor.desc: The Harbour Heritage Centre is operated by the Ladysmith Maritime Society, a non-profit charitable organization that has been preserving and promoting Ladysmith's maritime history since 1985. The Society restores heritage vessels — including the wooden tug Saravan, returned to service in 1991 — and offers public harbour tours departing from Ladysmith Fishermen's Wharf. A touring cyclist arriving in Ladysmith could visit the waterfront heritage site as part of exploring this scenic harbour town on Vancouver Island.

visitor.name: S.P.A.R.C. Museum
visitor.desc: The Society for the Preservation of Antique Radio in Canada (SPARC) operates a public museum on the historic Riverview Hospital grounds in Coquitlam, preserving radio and electronic communications artifacts from the spark era through to television with an emphasis on Canadian history. The site offers hands-on restoration workshops and repair services for old radios, and the sprawling Riverview arboretum and heritage architecture make for a pleasant explore on foot or by bike. Admission is by donation.

detail.address: Kerria Drive, Riverview Hospital, Coquitlam, BC

visitor.name: VIRL: Parksville Branch
visitor.desc: The Parksville Branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the community since 1937, with its current Jensen Avenue location open since 2001 and refreshed aesthetically in 2019. It is part of the Vancouver Island Regional Library system, one of the largest public library systems in BC, offering public computers, free Wi-Fi, and bookable meeting rooms. Bike racks at all three building entrances make it a cyclist-friendly stop in the heart of Parksville.

visitor.name: VIRL: Tahsis Branch
visitor.desc: The Tahsis branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library sits upstairs from the village office in one of the most remote communities reachable by road on Vancouver Island. It offers free public Wi-Fi, two public computer stations, printing, and a comfortable reading area for visitors. For touring cyclists who have made the long journey up the Tahsis Inlet corridor, this small but active branch provides a welcome spot to connect and rest.

visitor.name: Michael J. Fox Theatre
visitor.desc: The Michael J. Fox Theatre is a community performing arts venue in Burnaby named after the town's most famous alumnus, the actor and activist Michael J. Fox. Operating under the motto 'Fostering Excellence – Building Community,' it hosts school productions, dance recitals, and local arts events throughout the year. For a touring cyclist, it represents a culturally notable landmark in Burnaby with a connection to one of Canada's most celebrated public figures.

visitor.name: North Surrey Sport and Ice Complex
visitor.desc: North Surrey Sport & Ice Complex is a City of Surrey municipal recreation facility housed in a three-storey building in the Whalley area. It offers public drop-in skating, dry floor programs, fitness classes, and weight room access to residents and visitors. A touring cyclist seeking an active rest day could use the skating or fitness facilities here.

visitor.name: Harper Park
visitor.desc: Harper Park is a City of Coquitlam nature reserve on Burke Mountain featuring a network of trails designed for walkers, hikers, and off-road cyclists. The park was updated in 2020 with expanded trails, amenities, and signage. Picnic areas and tables make it a good rest stop for cyclists exploring the Burke Mountain area.

visitor.name: FLUX Media Gallery
visitor.desc: FLUX Media Gallery is a contemporary media arts centre operated by MediaNet, a registered non-profit in Victoria, BC. It exhibits innovative media art works by local, national, and international artists, serving as a community gathering place for dialogue on media arts practice. MediaNet also provides access to specialized video and post-production equipment and runs public augmented-reality art projects across Victoria's public spaces.

visitor.name: Ice Arena | West Vancouver
visitor.desc: The West Vancouver Ice Arena is a municipally operated ice rink serving the North Shore community. Located in a residential neighbourhood near Ambleside, it offers public skating and hockey programming. For touring cyclists, it is a publicly accessible recreation facility in a scenic waterfront community.

visitor.name: Carousel Theatre
visitor.desc: Carousel Theatre for Young People (CTYP) is Vancouver's mainstage theatre for young audiences, founded in 1976 and located on Granville Island. The company produces award-winning plays, family musicals, and community events, with productions ranging from original works to Disney stage adaptations. Granville Island is a popular cycling hub in Vancouver, making this venue an accessible cultural stop for families touring by bike.

visitor.name: Bear Creek Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: Bear Creek Outdoor Pool is a free seasonal outdoor public swimming pool operated by the City of Surrey, set within Bear Creek Park near 88 Avenue and King George Boulevard. The park setting offers a refreshing stop on a hot day for touring cyclists passing through Surrey. The pool is seasonal, typically operating from mid-May through early September.

visitor.name: Prospera Place
visitor.desc: Prospera Place is a 6,886-seat sports and entertainment arena in the heart of downtown Kelowna, home to the WHL's Kelowna Rockets since opening in 1999. The venue hosts a wide range of events from major concerts and comedy shows to championship hockey, and includes an on-site restaurant called Manhattan Point. Touring cyclists passing through Kelowna may find events of interest, though the venue is primarily a ticketed event facility.

notes.Café or food on site: Multiple concessions and an on-site restaurant called Manhattan Point with its own menu

visitor.name: Kelowna Karting
visitor.desc: Kelowna Karting is an indoor entertainment centre offering high-speed electric go-kart racing on a technical indoor track, along with free-roam Zero Latency VR, BC's only Gel Blaster Nexus arena, laser tag, interactive axe throwing, and an arcade. It caters to families, birthday parties, and corporate events, making it a potential rainy-day activity for touring cyclists passing through Kelowna.

visitor.name: FVRL: George Mackie Library
visitor.desc: George Mackie Library is a public branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, serving the North Delta community. It offers computers and printing, digital library resources, programming, and a broad collection of materials. As a free public facility, it provides a welcoming indoor rest space for touring cyclists moving through the Delta area.

visitor.name: Marysville Arena
visitor.desc: Marysville Arena is a seasonal multi-sport facility in the Marysville neighbourhood of Kimberley, BC, operated under the City of Kimberley's recreation portfolio. Tagged as an ice rink with multi-sport use, it primarily serves the local community for winter activities. Its seasonal operating status means it may not be accessible during the main cycling touring season.

visitor.name: BLAH
visitor.desc: BLAH (Benjamin Lumb Art House) is an art gallery in North Vancouver operated by artist Benjamin Lumb, situated on Marine Drive. The acronymic name reflects the kind of self-aware wit common to independent artist-run spaces. Touring cyclists riding the Marine Drive corridor would find this a compact cultural stop worth a visit.

visitor.name: Peach Creek Spawning Channels
visitor.desc: Peach Creek Spawning Channels is a nature reserve in Chilliwack where visitors can observe salmon returning to spawn. It is listed within the City of Chilliwack's parks and trails system and sits near the Lickman Road area. For touring cyclists, it offers a chance to experience BC's wild salmon lifecycle up close during migration season.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Food Vendor : Food Vendor location is in the Lickman Road Parking lot' under park amenities

visitor.name: Mahon Hall
visitor.desc: Mahon Hall, officially Mahon Memorial Hall, is a beloved century-old landmark in the heart of Ganges village on Salt Spring Island, originally built in 1904 as an agricultural display hall and now home to the Salt Spring Arts Council. The hall hosts a busy calendar of concerts, theatrical performances, exhibitions, and community events, and has been a cultural anchor for the island for over a hundred years. Touring cyclists exploring Salt Spring Island — a popular cycling destination — may find it a worthwhile cultural stop in the village centre.

detail.address: 114 Rainbow Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2V5

visitor.name: Elkford Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Elkford Aquatic Centre is a municipally operated, family-friendly facility serving this remote East Kootenay mountain community, offering a four-lane pool, two water slides, a diving board, a whirlpool hot tub, and an electric sauna. The building also houses the Elkford Public Library and a rentable multi-purpose meeting room, making it a genuine community hub. Cycling visitors arriving in Elkford will find it a rare chance to soak tired muscles with views of the Rocky Mountains.

visitor.name: Bettie Allard YMCA
visitor.desc: The Bettie Allard YMCA is a three-storey civic sports centre in North Vancouver, operated by YMCA BC. As part of a regional network, it offers fitness, aquatics, and community programming to residents of the North Shore. Touring cyclists passing through North Vancouver may find it a useful stop given its sports-centre facilities.

visitor.name: New Westminster Public Library - Queensborough Branch
visitor.desc: The Queensborough Branch is part of the New Westminster Public Library, which holds the distinction of being the first public library established in British Columbia. The branch appears to be located inside a community facility in the Queensborough neighbourhood on the south arm of the Fraser River. It offers the full range of NWPL services including public computers, Wi-Fi, and accessible services.

visitor.name: Dried Flower Arrangers' Garden
visitor.desc: The Dried Flower Arrangers' Garden is a named themed garden feature within VanDusen Botanical Garden in Vancouver, dedicated to plants cultivated for dried flower arranging. It exists as a distinct, labeled sub-garden within VanDusen's broader grounds, offering a quiet horticultural experience for cyclists exploring the city. Access and facilities would be those of the parent VanDusen Botanical Garden complex.

visitor.name: Hillside Park
visitor.desc: Hillside Park is a nature reserve in the North Vancouver/Port Moody area, offering a natural green space for visitors. As a designated nature reserve it likely provides trails through natural habitat, making it a potential rest or detour point for cyclists passing through the region. Specific facilities and trail character are not documented in available sources.

visitor.name: Nanaimo Ice Centre
visitor.desc: The Nanaimo Ice Centre is a City of Nanaimo-operated indoor arena primarily dedicated to ice hockey and skating. As a municipal recreation facility it serves local leagues and public skate sessions. Touring cyclists in Nanaimo may find it a potential rest stop, though it is not a cycling-specific attraction.

visitor.name: Burnaby Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Burnaby Art Gallery is the only public art museum in Canada dedicated exclusively to collecting works of art on paper, representing artists of diverse backgrounds and practices. It is housed in a beautifully restored arts and crafts mansion on the shores of Deer Lake, making it a scenic destination in its own right. Admission is always free, and the gallery offers rotating exhibitions, curator talks, workshops, and school programs throughout the year.

visitor.name: Kensington Park Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: A municipally operated heated outdoor pool in Kensington Park, Burnaby, open year-round with a covered and heated deck area for fall and winter swimming. The 6-lane pool includes a diving board, sauna, and change rooms with showers — a welcome stop for touring cyclists looking to cool off or warm up depending on the season.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Shower houses available, heated for fall and winter
notes.Luggage / bag storage: Lockers available in change rooms; not coin-operated — visitors must bring their own lock

visitor.name: Taiba Mussala Cultural Center
visitor.desc: Taiba Mussala Cultural Center is an Islamic community centre and prayer space (mussala) serving the Metro Vancouver Muslim community at 1206 Kingston Street. As a community gathering facility, it likely hosts religious and cultural programming for local residents. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a potential stop, though available amenities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
visitor.desc: The Australia & New Zealand Garden is a themed horticultural section within VanDusen Botanical Garden, a 55-acre oasis in the heart of Vancouver featuring over 7,500 plant species and varieties from around the world. Cyclists visiting as part of an urban tour will find themselves in one of Canada's most celebrated botanical collections, set within a verdant neighbourhood park context. The parent garden also houses fine dining and a casual cafe, making it a pleasant mid-ride stop.

notes.Café or food on site: Shaughnessy Restaurant (fine dining, West Coast menu, lunch/dinner/brunch) and The Garden Cafe (fair trade coffees, sandwiches, soups) both described on services page

visitor.name: Museum of Surrey
visitor.desc: The Museum of Surrey is a City of Surrey-operated local history museum in the Cloverdale neighbourhood exploring the region's cultural and natural heritage through permanent galleries and rotating exhibitions. It hosts a dedicated Textile Centre with programs, museum school programs, and community events including Indigenous heritage celebrations and sensory-friendly days. The museum is wheelchair accessible and serves as a substantive cultural stop for cyclists touring Surrey's historic town centre.

visitor.name: Richmond Ice Centre
visitor.desc: The Richmond Ice Centre is a City of Richmond-operated indoor ice facility offering public skating and ice hockey year-round. Situated in Richmond, BC, it serves both recreational skaters and competitive hockey players as a municipally run arena. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond could visit as a recreational stop or spectator attraction.

visitor.name: H. R. MacMillan Space Centre
visitor.desc: The H.R. MacMillan Space Centre, also known as the Planetarium, has been British Columbia's premier space science attraction since 1968, situated in Vanier Park on the waterfront just off the popular Vancouver seawall cycling route. It offers an immersive full-dome planetarium theatre, hands-on exhibits featuring moon rocks and meteorites, and live science demonstrations. Cycling visitors exploring the Kitsilano and Vanier Park area will find it a natural cultural detour.

visitor.name: Queen Elizabeth Theatre
visitor.desc: The Queen Elizabeth Theatre, opened in July 1959 and named for Queen Elizabeth II, is a landmark Vancouver performing arts venue that was built from an international design competition and served as a prototype for theatre complexes across North America. The striking mid-century modern building hosts opera, Broadway shows, classical music, and independent productions in an auditorium finished with dramatic crimson seating, and also features a curated gallery exhibiting works by emerging local artists. Cycling visitors arrive in a walkable downtown core steps from the SkyTrain and served by nearby Mobi bike-share docks.

notes.Café or food on site: Website has a dedicated 'Food & Beverage' navigation section; sustainability page references concessions and 'food and beverage offerings include many local products.'

visitor.name: UBC Tennis Centre
visitor.desc: The UBC Tennis Centre is a dedicated tennis facility on the University of British Columbia's Vancouver campus, operated by UBC Recreation. It serves students, faculty, and community members with court bookings and tennis programs. Located within the broader UBC Recreation network, it sits amid the extensive campus greenery of Point Grey.

detail.address: 6000 Student Union Boulevard, Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada V6T1Z1

visitor.name: Tourist Information Centre (Fort St. John)
visitor.desc: The City of Fort St. John's official Visitor Information Centre sits along the Alaska Highway corridor in northeastern BC, one of the most remote stretches of long-distance cycling in the province. Operated by the municipality, it serves as the primary resource for travellers seeking local maps, route guidance, and regional attractions in the Peace River country. For cycle tourists riding the Alaska Highway or connecting routes through the Peace region, this centre is a logical stop for orientation and local knowledge.

visitor.name: Chillibowl Lanes
visitor.desc: Chillibowl Lanes is a classic indoor entertainment venue in Chilliwack featuring ten-pin bowling, three styles of billiards (8-ball, 9-ball, and snooker), and an arcade. Beyond casual play, the venue runs bowling leagues, events, and tournaments, giving it a genuine competitive community feel. Touring cyclists looking for a social rest-day activity or a sheltered stop in the Fraser Valley would find a lively, all-ages destination here.

notes.Café or food on site: Website describes the visit as a chance to 'have some snacks,' indicating food/snacks are available on site

visitor.name: Greek Seniors Society
visitor.desc: The Greek Seniors Society is a senior citizen community organization serving Vancouver's Greek diaspora from its Kitsilano location on West Broadway. Operating in both Greek and English, it hosts cultural events, activities, and gatherings — including an annual general meeting — for its membership. Touring cyclists passing through the West Broadway corridor will find it a neighbourhood anchor with deep roots in Vancouver's Hellenic community.

visitor.name: Chilliwack Museum
visitor.desc: A community museum housed in a historic building in downtown Chilliwack, featuring 1,200 square feet of gallery space with rotating exhibitions on local and Stó:lō history. Admission is always free. The museum also operates a separate archives facility on Corbould Street for researchers interested in the region's documentary and photographic history.

visitor.name: Kitsilano Outdoor Swimming Pool
visitor.desc: Kitsilano Pool is one of the longest outdoor saltwater swimming pools in North America, stretching 137 metres along the waterfront in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood. Operated by the City of Vancouver, it sits steps from the Seaside Greenway cycling route, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists riding the waterfront. The pool also offers diving and is noted as wheelchair accessible.

visitor.name: VIU Permaculture Club Garden
visitor.desc: A small permaculture demonstration garden on the Vancouver Island University Nanaimo campus, located on the north side of the campus library. Founded in 2008 as the Community Peace Garden, it is now run by the VIU Students' Union Permaculture Club and focuses on food growing, seed saving, plant medicine, and traditional ecological knowledge. It functions primarily as a student learning and gathering space rather than a formal public attraction.

visitor.name: Salt Spring Island Visitor Information Centre
visitor.desc: The Salt Spring Visitor Centre is operated by the Salt Spring Island Chamber of Commerce and serves as the main information hub for visitors to Salt Spring Island in the Southern Gulf Islands. Located in Ganges, it is a natural first stop for touring cyclists arriving by ferry who need local maps, trail information, and recommendations for food, lodging, and attractions across the island.

detail.address: 121 Lower Ganges Rd, Ganges, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2T1

visitor.name: Kwisitis Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: A striking west coast building perched at the south end of Wickaninnish Beach in Pacific Rim National Park Reserve. Inside features exhibits on local ecology, First Nations culture, a replica longhouse, and giant marine mammal murals. The outdoor deck offers year-round views of whales, storms, and surfers along the open Pacific coast.

visitor.name: Richmond Public Library, Cambie Branch
visitor.desc: The Richmond Public Library Cambie Branch is one of four branches in the Richmond Public Library system, located within a commercial plaza at 11590 Cambie Road. The library offers free public Wi-Fi, computer access, and a multilingual collection reflecting Richmond's diverse community. As a fully publicly accessible facility with no admission requirements, it is a potential connectivity and rest stop for touring cyclists moving through the area.

visitor.name: Centre culturel francophone
visitor.desc: Founded in 1975 and marking its 50th anniversary in 2025, the Centre culturel francophone de Vancouver is the anchor institution for French-language arts and culture in Metro Vancouver, presenting professional theatre, music, visual arts exhibitions, improv competitions, and an annual summer festival. It also runs a French-language library, language courses, and a summer camp, making it a full-service community hub rather than just a venue. The building houses the Café Salade de Fruit, a sit-down restaurant open most days, which adds practical value for visitors exploring the Kitsilano neighbourhood.

notes.Café or food on site: Café Salade de Fruit operates on-site; confirmed on /infos-pratiques page with its own website listed as https://www.saladedefruits.com/

visitor.name: Vancouver Police Museum
visitor.desc: The Vancouver Police Museum & Archives occupies the city's historic Coroner's Court building in Gastown, a space that served as Vancouver's city morgue and autopsy suite from 1932 to 1980, processing over 20,000 bodies. Visitors can walk through the authentic recreated 1970s autopsy suite, explore mugshot archives, confiscated weapons, and exhibits on Vancouver's most notorious criminal cases. Founded in 1986 to mark the Vancouver Police Department's centennial, it is an independent museum operated by the Vancouver Police Historical Society and is a genuinely singular stop for any cyclist touring through Gastown.

detail.address: 240 East Cordova Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 1L3

visitor.name: Sidney Information Centre
visitor.desc: The Sidney Information Centre is a volunteer-staffed visitor centre operated by the Sidney Business Improvement Area, situated on Beacon Avenue in the heart of downtown Sidney by the Sea. It serves as the primary resource hub for anyone exploring this charming waterfront community, offering guidance on local dining, events, accommodation, and attractions. Touring cyclists will find it a useful waypoint for route planning, local knowledge, and discovering what this peninsula town has to offer.

visitor.name: Winter Garden
visitor.desc: The Winter Garden is one of more than twenty gardens on the grounds of Government House, the official residence of British Columbia's Lieutenant Governor, in Victoria's Rockland neighbourhood. The estate grounds are open to the public every day of the year and are free to explore. Touring cyclists will find the gardens a pleasant stop, with a seasonal garden cafe (Rudi's Tea Room), free guided garden tours, and the Cary Castle Mews & Costume Museum also on site.

notes.Café or food on site: Rudi's Tea Room, described as 'the beloved garden cafe,' operates seasonally on the Government House grounds

visitor.name: Eileen Dailly Leisure Pool & Fitness Centre
visitor.desc: Eileen Dailly Leisure Pool & Fitness Centre is a City of Burnaby public recreation facility in the Burnaby Heights neighbourhood, offering a beach-entry leisure pool, a deep tank main pool, and a well-equipped weight and cardio room. It sits directly adjacent to Confederation Park, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring the area. The centre is operated by the City of Burnaby and offers both drop-in and registered aquatic and fitness programming for the community.

notes.Luggage / bag storage: Lockers available for item storage; website notes coin-operated lockers are being removed July 6 and patrons should bring their own personal padlock or purchase one at the front desk

visitor.name: Sunnyside Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: Sunnyside Outdoor Pool is a seasonal municipal outdoor pool operated by the City of Surrey, offering free public swimming through the summer months. It also provides swimming lessons by phone registration. A refreshing stop for touring cyclists passing through South Surrey during the summer season.

visitor.name: Cal Revelle Nature Sanctuary
visitor.desc: Cal Revelle Nature Sanctuary is a protected nature reserve near Sidney on southern Vancouver Island. It sits within the District of Highlands and offers natural open space that cycling tourists exploring the region's rural backroads might visit as a quiet stop. No formal visitor infrastructure details are publicly documented for this site.

visitor.name: Dicken's Sweets & British Museum
visitor.desc: Dickens Sweets & British Museum is a two-floor immersive attraction in Chilliwack combining a British confectionery and grocery shop with themed museum rooms inspired by the era of Charles Dickens — including a replica Tally Ho pub, a Titanic room, a vintage toy shop, and a Yesteryears office filled with antique typewriters. The experience wraps up with Oliver's Tearoom offering High Tea and Pickwick's Pie Shop serving freshly baked British meat and fruit pies. An outside patio makes it a pleasant stop for cyclists looking for a cultural detour and a hearty bite.

notes.Café or food on site: Oliver's Tearoom (High Tea), Pickwick's Pie Shop (freshly baked pies and sausage rolls baked in-house daily), British grocery shop, Dickens Sweet Shop, and an outside patio — all

visitor.name: The Port Theatre
visitor.desc: The Port Theatre is an 800-seat community performing arts centre on the Nanaimo waterfront, co-managed by the Port Theatre Society and the City of Nanaimo on the traditional territory of Snuneymuxw First Nation. One of British Columbia's busiest theatres, it hosts over 250 events annually—concerts, dance, theatre, film, festivals, and graduation ceremonies—drawing more than 100,000 visitors per year. Its nationally acclaimed Spotlight Series brings Canadian and internationally renowned touring artists to central Vancouver Island, making it a significant cultural destination for anyone riding through Nanaimo.

notes.Café or food on site: Our Team page lists multiple named bartenders on staff (Dawn Burgar, Georgia Carmichael-Douglas, Leeyah Davis, Olivia Mah, Janet Marren, Maria Noel, Joanne Swain, Henryka Szado, Robyn Thompson, Kyra Van Shaik), confirming on-site bar/beverage service

visitor.name: Amelia Douglas Gallery
visitor.desc: The Amelia Douglas Gallery is a public art gallery located on the third floor of Douglas College, showcasing works by emerging and established artists with a focus on contemporary practice. Named after a historical figure significant to British Columbia, it serves as a cultural hub within the college community. Touring cyclists stopping in the area can visit for free cultural programming alongside other campus amenities.

visitor.name: Dawson Creek Art Gallery
visitor.desc: The Dawson Creek Art Gallery is housed in a beautifully renovated annex of a historic prairie grain elevator in NAR Park, making it architecturally distinctive and the first public art gallery established in northern BC. Managed by the South Peace Art Society since 1983, the gallery presents local, regional, and touring visual arts exhibitions year-round, and was recognized as the northern winner of the Architecture Foundation of BC's best building contest in 2014. The on-site Grainery Artisan and Gift Shop offers handcrafted items from local artisans, and the gallery also provides custom framing services.

detail.address: 101 - 816 Alaska Avenue, Dawson Creek, BC V1G 4T6

visitor.name: Lavington Pool
visitor.desc: Lavington Outdoor Pool is a free, publicly accessible outdoor swimming pool operated by the City of Vernon, located in the Lavington area near Coldstream. It offers a refreshing stop for touring cyclists riding through the North Okanagan, particularly welcome on hot summer days in the valley.

visitor.name: FVRL: Yarrow Library
visitor.desc: Yarrow Library is a community branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system serving the small rural village of Yarrow, southwest of Chilliwack. It offers free public WiFi, public computers, and a range of accessibility features in a welcoming community space. For touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley lowlands, it provides a convenient rest stop with outdoor bike parking.

visitor.name: FVRL: Tsawwassen Library
visitor.desc: The Tsawwassen Library is a public branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, serving the Tsawwassen community in Delta, BC. It offers a broad range of services including bookable meeting rooms, public computers, self-checkout, and a dedicated children's and teens' space. For cycling visitors, it provides outdoor bike racks and free WiFi, making it a practical stop on a coastal touring route.

visitor.name: The Glass Foundry
visitor.desc: The Glass Foundry is a working glassblowing studio and gallery on Salt Spring Island that recycles scrap glass into wholesale giftware while producing unique blown, cast, and fused art pieces. Visitors are welcome to watch glassmaking in progress and can participate in drop-in workshops or adult classes. The studio is set on a rural farming acreage just outside Ganges village, making it a distinctive craft destination for cyclists exploring the island.

detail.address: 401 Upper Ganges Road, Salt Spring Island, V8K 1R7

visitor.name: Headwaters Park
visitor.desc: A 15-acre municipal park on Bowen Island centred on a fen wetland, with a perimeter trail and boardwalk crossing a portion of the fen. The park is an important link in an island-wide trail and greenbelt system, and its wetlands filter into Terminal Creek, one of the sources for the Cove Bay Water District.

visitor.name: Hillcrest Centre
visitor.desc: Hillcrest Centre is a multi-sport recreation facility in Vancouver offering swimming, curling, and ice skating under one roof, and carries a Wikipedia entry indicating it is a well-known public venue. Built to serve the 2010 Winter Olympics, it sits in the Queen Elizabeth Park neighbourhood and draws both local and visiting users year-round. A touring cyclist riding through the area would find a large public facility with the full amenity range typical of a City of Vancouver recreation centre.

visitor.name: Waterfront Gallery
visitor.desc: The Waterfront Gallery was operated by the Arts Council of Ladysmith & District, the primary visual arts organization in Ladysmith, but the OSM record is tagged closed and the 'Waterfront Gallery' name no longer appears on the operator's website. The ACLD now runs the Ladysmith Gallery at Unit 7 - 32 High Street in downtown Ladysmith, hosting monthly member exhibitions, a boutique of local artworks, and guest artist shows open to the public. The organization is actively fundraising for a new Arts & Heritage Hub intended to house expanded gallery, classroom, and interpretive spaces.

visitor.name: Pitt Meadows Museum Hoffman
visitor.desc: A community heritage museum split across two sites on Harris Road beside the CPR tracks in Pitt Meadows. The Hoffmann & Son Machine Shop houses over sixty restored stationary gasoline engines and a working forge, while the Old General Store (1908) features permanent and temporary exhibits on the area's settlement history plus a small community archives. Admission is by donation, making it an easy stop for touring cyclists passing through the Pitt Meadows area.

visitor.name: Hornby Creative
visitor.desc: Hornby Creative is an artisan boutique nestled inside the Ringside Market on Hornby Island, showcasing a curated mix of local arts, crafts, unique goods, and naturally-made products from the surrounding community. Run by Tamara Lamont, it aims to balance fine local artistry with quality West Coast merchandise. For a touring cyclist exploring Hornby Island, it offers a taste of the island's creative culture in a single browsable stop.

visitor.name: Ron Andrews Community Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Ron Andrews Community Recreation Centre is a full-service public recreation facility in North Vancouver operated by the North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission. It features a 37.5-meter six-lane pool plus a tank, fitness studio, squash court, a TRX training room, and an outdoor Windsor Patio, with programming ranging from aquafit to gymnastics to martial arts. Touring cyclists passing through the Deep Cove and Lynn Valley corridor may find this a practical rest stop given the breadth of facilities typical of a major community rec centre.

visitor.name: VIRL: Cortes Island Branch
visitor.desc: The Cortes Island branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has been housed in the former school building at Linnaea Farm since 2013, serving this remote Gulf Island community. Situated on unceded Klahoose First Nation territory, it offers an expanded collection and friendly staff to both locals and visitors. For touring cyclists making the ferry crossing to Cortes Island, it is one of the few public facilities in Manson's Landing.

visitor.name: FVRL: Mission Library
visitor.desc: The Mission Library is a branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, a public network serving communities across the Fraser Valley. Located on 2nd Avenue in downtown Mission, it offers public computers, printing, digital collections, and programming for residents and visitors alike. For a touring cyclist, it provides a quiet, climate-controlled rest stop with free Wi-Fi in the heart of Mission.

visitor.name: Arthur Vickers Gallery
visitor.desc: Arthur Vickers is a celebrated Tlingit and Tsimshian artist whose work draws on Northwest Coast Indigenous traditions. His gallery near Cowichan Bay offers touring cyclists a notable cultural stop on the Vancouver Crossing Loop, showcasing original paintings and prints. The gallery represents one of BC's prominent Indigenous art destinations in the southern Vancouver Island region.

detail.address: 1719 Cowichan Bay Rd, Cowichan Bay, BC V0R 0C2, Canada

visitor.name: NVDPL: Lynn Valley
visitor.desc: The Lynn Valley Library is the main hub of the North Vancouver District Public Library system, situated at the corner of Lynn Valley Road and Mountain Highway. Built in 2007 as a LEED-certified structure, it features a StoryLab digital creativity studio, study spaces, and programs for all ages. Notably, NVDPL lends e-cargo bikes from its collection — a rare and practical resource for cyclists passing through the area.

visitor.name: North Burnaby Neighbourhood House
visitor.desc: North Burnaby Neighbourhood House (BNH North House) is a community-driven social services centre offering programs for families, seniors, newcomers, youth, and food-insecure residents in the Hastings corridor of Burnaby. It is one of three locations operated by Burnaby Neighbourhood House, a registered charity with deep roots in the surrounding communities. A touring cyclist passing through the area might stop here for community resources or as a rest point along Hastings Street.

visitor.name: VIRL: Comox Branch
visitor.desc: VIRL: Comox Branch is a public library operated by Vancouver Island Regional Library, housed in the Portside building on Beaufort Avenue just two blocks from the Comox waterfront. The branch has served the community since 1937 and moved to its current location in 2009, making it a long-established landmark in the heart of town. It offers a comfortable, accessible public space with free WiFi and air conditioning—a practical rest point for cyclists passing through Comox.

visitor.name: X̱wi7x̱wa
visitor.desc: X̱wi7x̱wa Library is the only Indigenous branch of an academic library in Canada, housed in a building whose architecture represents an Interior Salish pit-house on the UBC campus. Its collections and services reflect Indigenous approaches to teaching, learning, and research, and it is open to everyone — not just UBC students. The library is a culturally significant stop for visitors interested in Indigenous scholarship and knowledge systems in British Columbia.

visitor.name: TNRL: Kamloops Library
visitor.desc: The Kamloops branch of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library is a public library serving the city of Kamloops in BC's interior. As a civic institution in the heart of downtown, it offers touring cyclists a quiet stop in a central location. Libraries of this type typically provide a welcoming indoor environment with seating and connectivity, making them a practical mid-ride refuge.

visitor.name: Mission Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Mission Visitor Centre is a tourism information office operated by Tourism Mission on the Lougheed Highway, serving as a gateway resource for visitors to the Mission area. Located along a major through-route in the Fraser Valley, it would be a natural stop for touring cyclists seeking local route information and area orientation. The operator Tourism Mission is distinct from the City of Mission municipal government.

visitor.name: Lochdale Community Hall
visitor.desc: Lochdale Community Hall is a stucco-clad civic building constructed in 1925 and granted heritage designation in 1992, making it one of Burnaby's older community gathering spaces. The hall hosts a variety of public events — from diecast toy shows to community functions — and its central Burnaby location on Sperling Avenue puts it within easy reach for cyclists passing through the area.

visitor.name: ORL: Kelowna Branch
visitor.desc: The Kelowna Downtown branch of the Okanagan Regional Library is a large, full-service public library in the city centre, part of a 30-branch regional system serving over 399,000 people across the Okanagan. It houses an impressive Makerspace with a 3D printer, laser cutter, audio recording studio, and video production gear. Touring cyclists will find a welcoming public space with computers, Wi-Fi, and bookable meeting rooms in a convenient downtown location.

visitor.name: Kerrisdale Community Centre
visitor.desc: One of Vancouver's oldest community centres, Kerrisdale Community Centre has been operated by the Kerrisdale Community Centre Society since 1943 and celebrated its 80th anniversary in 2023. Its facilities span an indoor pool, exercise room, gymnasium, public library, seniors wing, an ice arena (Cyclone Taylor Arena), and an outdoor pool at nearby Maple Grove. Touring cyclists passing through the Kerrisdale neighbourhood may find the range of recreation facilities useful as a mid-route stop.

notes.Café or food on site: Staff directory lists a Food Services Coordinator with dedicated kitchen email (kitchen.kccs@gmail.com)

visitor.name: Grouse Mountain Skyride Base
visitor.desc: Grouse Mountain is a major mountain resort overlooking Metro Vancouver, accessed from the base station on Nancy Greene Way via the iconic Skyride gondola. The mountain hosts a lift-accessed bike park with rentals and structured lessons, as well as the world-famous Grouse Grind trail that climbs directly from the base—making it a natural destination for cycling-adjacent outdoor adventurers. A new gravity coaster, ziplines, wildlife habitat, and multiple summit dining venues round out the experience.

detail.address: 6400 Nancy Greene Way, North Vancouver, BC

notes.Café or food on site: Multiple dining venues listed on website: The Observatory, Altitudes Bistro, Lupins Café, Grouse Grind Coffee Bar, Starbucks; Grizzly Lookout Café, Rusty Rail BBQ, and BeaverTails noted as (closed). Most venues are at the summit, accessed via the Skyride gondola

visitor.name: REVS
visitor.desc: REVS Burnaby bills itself as Western Canada's largest 10-pin bowling centre, with 48 lanes accommodating up to 300 people and a full-service entertainment complex under one roof. Beyond bowling, the facility includes a fitness centre with five racquetball courts, a cardio room, strength training area, and a boxing club operated by the North Burnaby Boxing Club. Striker's Bar & Restaurant serves meals and handcrafted pizzas on site, and the venue is located directly beside the Holdom SkyTrain station.

notes.Café or food on site: Striker's Bar on site; website describes 'delicious meals and handcrafted pizzas at Striker's Bar' and references 'food and beverage packages'

visitor.name: Trail & District Public Library
visitor.desc: The Trail & District Public Library is a busy community hub in Trail, BC, serving residents of all ages with programs ranging from STEAM labs and drum circles to tech coaching and senior yoga. It runs a 'Book Bike' outreach program, signalling a genuine connection to active and low-barrier community access. The library explicitly commits to being a welcoming, safe, and inclusive space under the Accessible BC Act, which bodes well for drop-in visitors.

visitor.name: Seymour Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Seymour Art Gallery is a free, non-profit public gallery established in 1985 and the only public gallery in the District of North Vancouver, situated in the heart of Deep Cove — a hugely popular cycling destination. The gallery welcomes over 26,000 visitors annually to a rotating schedule of visual arts exhibitions, performance events, and public programs. It shares the Deep Cove Cultural Centre building with several other arts organizations, making it a natural cultural stop at the end of a scenic ride.

detail.address: 4360 Gallant Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7G 1L2

visitor.name: Killarney Community Centre
visitor.desc: Killarney Community Centre is a full-service public recreation facility in southeast Vancouver offering aquatics, fitness, ice skating, and senior programs. The aquatic wing includes 15 and 25 metre lap pools, a large water slide, lazy river, steam room, whirlpool, and a climbing wall. Touring cyclists will find a well-equipped public facility serving the surrounding Killarney neighbourhood.

visitor.name: Squamish Public Library
visitor.desc: The Squamish Public Library is a welcoming public institution on Second Avenue in downtown Squamish, open free of charge to residents and visitors alike. Cyclists can drop in to use free Wi-Fi, public computers, and comfortable reading and workspace areas without needing a library card. The library also maintains a dedicated Squamish Visitor Information section, making it a practical orientation stop for those new to the area.

notes.Water without admission: Library is free to enter for all

visitor.name: Delbrook Community Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Delbrook Community Recreation Centre is a publicly operated facility run by the North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission (NVRC), serving the District of North Vancouver with fitness, swimming, skating, and multipurpose programming. The centre includes a fitness centre, pottery studio, youth centre, and several rentable rooms including the Ash Room with a sprung wood floor, ballet bar, and projection system. As a full-service municipal recreation hub open early mornings through evenings, it could be a convenient stop for touring cyclists in the North Shore area.

detail.address: 851 West Queens Rd, North Vancouver, BC V7N 4E3

visitor.name: Newton Recreation Facility
visitor.desc: Newton Recreation Centre is a City of Surrey municipal facility offering drop-in fitness, sport, and swimming activities. The pool complex includes a main pool, wading pool, hot tub, and steam room. It is conveniently located next to a bus route in the Newton neighbourhood of Surrey.

visitor.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
