visitor.desc: A named garden area within VanDusen Botanical Garden, a 55-acre oasis in the heart of Vancouver featuring over 7,500 plant species and varieties from around the world. VanDusen offers guided walking and cart tours, a fine dining restaurant, a garden café, a gift shop, and seasonal floral installations. A worthwhile stop for touring cyclists exploring Vancouver's quieter Shaughnessy neighbourhood.

notes.Café or food on site: Shaughnessy Restaurant (fine dining, lunch/afternoon tea/dinner/weekend brunch, seasonal patio) and The Garden Café in the Visitor Centre (Fair Trade coffees, handcrafted beverages, sandwiches, soups)

visitor.name: Birdie Indoor Golf Center
visitor.desc: Birdie Indoor Golf Center is the first venue in Canada to offer GreenJoy golf simulators to the public, featuring 7 open bays and 3 private VIP rooms where visitors can play world-class courses rain or shine. The facility includes professional golf instruction, active tournaments, and a lounge with bar and food service. It operates as a multi-location brand with the Richmond site being the flagship open location.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Bar Service Available' and 'Food & Drink' under Features & Amenities

visitor.name: Canadian Music Centre in BC
visitor.desc: The Canadian Music Centre in BC is the British Columbia branch of Canada's national organization dedicated to promoting and preserving the works of Canadian composers, offering a library and resource centre for scores, recordings, and music research. Situated on Davie Street in downtown Vancouver, it serves musicians, educators, and music enthusiasts in a central, accessible neighbourhood. A touring cyclist passing through Vancouver with an interest in Canadian contemporary music culture may find it a worthwhile cultural stop.

visitor.name: Mayne Island Museum
visitor.desc: The Mayne Island Museum is housed in the original 1896 Plumper Pass Gaol — one of the oldest surviving structures on the island — and tells the stories of First Nations, Japanese, and European settlers who shaped island life. A separate Dalton Deacon Barn adjacent to the gaol holds donated farm machinery and larger heritage pieces. Two digital collections, including the John Aitken Historic Photograph Collection, extend the museum's reach for visitors and researchers alike.

visitor.name: Contemporary Art Gallery
visitor.desc: The Contemporary Art Gallery (CAG) is a free public contemporary art institution in downtown Vancouver presenting rotating exhibitions of Canadian and international contemporary artists. Situated on the traditional territories of the xʷməθkʷəy̓əm, Sḵwx̱wú7mesh, and səlilwətaɬ peoples, it also operates a library, an archive, and a shop specialising in artists' books, editions, and catalogues. Admission is always free, making it an accessible cultural stop for cyclists passing through the city centre.

visitor.name: Western Financial Place
visitor.desc: Cranbrook's main arena and recreation complex, home to the Cranbrook Bucks junior hockey team. The facility houses a swimming pool, hot tub, sauna, and ice rinks — appealing for a touring cyclist looking to recover after a long ride through the East Kootenay. Located just north of downtown Cranbrook with bus service on multiple routes.

notes.Café or food on site: Concessions operated by Cranbrook Bucks offering pizza, hot dogs, popcorn; full-service restaurant above the seating area open during hockey games and major events

visitor.name: Robert F. Osborne Centre - Unit 2
visitor.desc: The Robert F. Osborne Centre (UBC building #431) is a sports facility on the University of British Columbia's Point Grey campus in Vancouver. Tagged as 'Unit 2,' it represents a specific sub-space within the larger centre building. UBC Recreation operates a range of fitness and recreational programs across the campus, though the current status and public accessibility of this particular unit is unclear.

visitor.name: Port Moody Rec Center Tennis Courts
visitor.desc: An outdoor public tennis facility operated by the City of Port Moody, fenced and mapped as a sports centre. Touring cyclists in the Port Moody area may find it a convenient stop for recreation alongside nearby trails and waterfront. The broader Port Moody recreation network also includes parks, the Shoreline Trail, and other active amenities in the vicinity.

visitor.name: Nelson Curling Centre
visitor.desc: The Nelson Curling Centre is home to the Nelson Curling Club, a community curling facility in the heart of Nelson, BC. Situated on Cedar Street, it serves as a local gathering point for curling leagues and drop-in play in the Kootenay region. A touring cyclist passing through Nelson could visit this attraction to catch a glimpse of one of Canada's classic winter sports in an authentic club setting.

visitor.name: Fort St. John Arts Council ArtsPost
visitor.desc: The Fort St. John Arts Council ArtsPost is the home base of the city's community arts council, operating as a gallery and arts hub in the Peace River region of northeastern BC. The council supports and promotes a wide network of local arts organizations, from choral societies and dance groups to potters and quilters, and hosts rotating exhibitions and community arts events. For a touring cyclist passing through Fort St. John, it offers a window into the region's vibrant arts scene.

detail.address: 10320 94 Avenue, Fort St. John, BC V1J 4X3

visitor.name: Jericho Beach Consession
visitor.desc: Jericho Beach Concession is a casual fish-and-chips stand operated within Jericho Beach Park, one of Vancouver's most popular waterfront cycling destinations along the Seaside Greenway. Run by Organic Villa Catering, it serves beachgoers and cyclists passing through this scenic stretch of Point Grey Road. The park setting makes it a natural rest stop on any coastal touring route.

detail.address: 3941 Point Grey Road, Vancouver, BC V6R 1B5

notes.Café or food on site: Facebook page categorizes the business as a 'Fish & Chips Restaurant' with a food menu communicated to the community via the page

visitor.name: UBC Life Building
visitor.desc: The Life Building (formerly the UBC Student Union Building) is the main hub of student life at UBC Vancouver, operated by the Alma Mater Society — Canada's largest student union. It houses multiple food venues, shops, services, bookable study rooms, and event spaces spread across a purpose-built facility at the heart of the UBC campus. Touring cyclists riding through the UBC endowment lands can use this as a central rest stop with access to food and services.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Places To Eat' as a quick link and 'Food Order Online' as a building service, indicating multiple food venues on site

visitor.name: Kin Pool
visitor.desc: Kin Pool is a municipal outdoor swimming pool in Nanaimo, formerly known as the Kinsmen Outdoor Swimming Pool. Operated by the City of Nanaimo as part of its Parks, Recreation & Culture department, it offers drop-in swimming in the Bowen Park area. For a touring cyclist on Vancouver Island, it can be a welcome place to cool off and clean up.

visitor.name: Visitor Information
visitor.desc: The Chetwynd Visitor Centre is a staffed municipal tourism office operated by the District of Chetwynd, serving as the gateway for travelers to this northern BC community renowned for its world-class chainsaw carvings. Staff can equip visiting cyclists with local trail maps, community maps, and area tourism information including access to Chetwynd's greenspace trail network. The centre is the starting point for exploring both the town's unique outdoor art and the surrounding wilderness trails.

detail.address: 5400 North Access Road, Chetwynd, BC V0C 1J0

visitor.name: Petey's Pumpkin Patch
visitor.desc: Petey's Pumpkin Patch is a seasonal fall attraction near Chilliwack, BC, operated by Fantasy Farms. It opens during the October harvest season as a pumpkin patch experience in the Fraser Valley agricultural corridor. Touring cyclists passing through the region in autumn could stop here for a classic BC farm attraction.

visitor.name: Sidney Archives
visitor.desc: The Sidney Archives collects and maintains historical records, photographs, cartographic materials, and oral histories related to Sidney and the Saanich Peninsula, with holdings spanning from roughly 1850 to the present. It operates as a department of the Sidney Museum and houses significant collections including a complete run of 'The Review' newspaper (1912–1989) and Dominion Experimental Farm records. Access is by research appointment only, making it a destination for cyclists with a specific interest in local and regional history rather than a casual drop-in stop.

visitor.name: Axe & Grind
visitor.desc: Axe & Grind is an indoor entertainment venue in the heart of downtown Victoria offering axe throwing, knife throwing, golf simulators, karaoke, and virtual reality. As a certified member of both the World Axe Throwing League and World Knife Throwing League, it brings a competitive dimension alongside casual drop-in and group bookings. Experienced staff guide newcomers through safe throwing techniques, making it a novel stop for touring cyclists seeking an off-bike adventure in the city core.

visitor.name: Wellington Hall
visitor.desc: Wellington Hall is a community centre situated in the Wellington neighbourhood of Nanaimo, BC. Community halls of this type typically serve as gathering spaces for local events, meetings, and recreational programmes. For touring cyclists passing through the area, it may offer a convenient public stopping point.

visitor.name: Seaparc Leisure Complex
visitor.desc: SEAPARC is a municipal recreation complex operated by the Capital Regional District, serving Sooke and the Juan de Fuca Electoral Area. The facility includes a pool, ice arena, fitness centre, weight room, golf course, and the Sooke Bike Park—a dedicated cycling facility that makes it a relevant stop for touring cyclists on Vancouver Island's southwest coast. The complex also manages the Sooke Skate Park, currently being rebuilt as of late 2025.

visitor.name: Artspeak Gallery
visitor.desc: Artspeak is an artist-run exhibition and programming space in Vancouver's Gastown/Chinatown area dedicated to fostering dialogue between contemporary visual art and writing. The gallery maintains an on-site bookstore and presents exhibitions, workshops, and screenings by emerging and established artists, including a current show by Bahamian-Canadian artist Christopher Outten. Its commitment to intersectional participation and its location in a walkable, bike-accessible neighbourhood make it a distinctive cultural stop for touring cyclists.

visitor.name: Burnside / Gorge Community Centre
visitor.desc: Burnside Gorge Community Association is a neighbourhood community centre in Victoria's Burnside-Gorge area, operated by the Capital Regional District. It offers a wide range of programs including youth recreation, family services, licensed childcare, and community events like the Selkirk Waterfront Festival and Gorge Waterway Cleanup. The centre also manages the Cecelia Ravine Community Gardens and hosts facility rentals.

visitor.name: Roedde House Museum
visitor.desc: Roedde House Museum is a meticulously restored 1893 Queen Anne Revival home designed by architect Francis Rattenbury, now preserving the domestic world of Vancouver's first bookbinder, Gustav Roedde. Unlike many heritage houses, all eleven furnished rooms are fully accessible to visitors rather than roped off, with self-guided and docent-led tours available in eight languages. Located in the West End's Barclay Heritage Square, it also hosts a regular Jazz in the Parlour series and rotating exhibits, making it a cultural landmark a short ride from the Stanley Park seawall.

visitor.name: Engine 374 Pavilion
visitor.desc: The Engine 374 Pavilion houses the restored CPR locomotive that pulled Canada's first transcontinental passenger train into Vancouver on May 23, 1887. Housed in a glass pavilion at the corner of Davie Street and Pacific Boulevard, it is staffed by enthusiastic West Coast Railway Association volunteers who offer free tours of the engine and share its colourful history. It sits next to the Roundhouse Community Centre in Yaletown, a 10-minute walk from downtown Vancouver.

visitor.name: SS Sicamous
visitor.desc: The S.S. Sicamous is a restored 1914 CPR sternwheeler permanently moored on Okanagan Lake in Penticton, now the centrepiece of a marine heritage park preserving Okanagan waterway history. Cyclists touring the Lakeshore Drive corridor will find a striking piece of regional heritage with exhibits on the KVR railway, early Okanagan history, and a collection of historic vessels including the S.S. Naramata. The ship features an elevator providing access to its primary museum level, and is available for community events year-round.

detail.address: 1099 Lakeshore Drive West, Penticton, BC V2A 1B7

visitor.name: Cominco Gardens
visitor.desc: Cominco Gardens is a public ornamental garden in Kimberley, BC, with historical ties to the former Consolidated Mining and Smelting Company that once dominated the region. Set in the East Kootenays, it offers a green respite for touring cyclists passing through the Kimberley area. The garden is tagged as a leisure destination in OpenStreetMap and appears on local attractions maps.

detail.address: 290 Rossland Blvd, Kimberley, BC V1A 2R6, Canada

visitor.name: Irving House
visitor.desc: Irving House is one of the oldest community heritage sites in British Columbia, a well-preserved 1859 colonial home built for Captain William Irving, a prominent figure in early Fraser River steamboat navigation. Operated by the City of New Westminster, it offers visitors a step back into 19th-century domestic life in the province's first capital. Touring cyclists riding through the Lower Mainland will find it a compact, walkable stop in the heart of historic New Westminster.

visitor.name: Indoor Pools & Spa
visitor.desc: The indoor and outdoor mineral pools at Harrison Hot Springs Resort are fed by geothermal springs averaging 1,300 parts per million of dissolved mineral solids — among the most concentrated in North America. The facility comprises five distinct pools ranging from a 38–40°C indoor hot pool in a quiet-zone spa building to a large outdoor family pool with natural rock formations and a cascading waterfall. For a touring cyclist, it offers a genuine restorative soak at one of BC's most storied hot-springs destinations.

notes.Café or food on site: Resort home page lists Lakeside Restaurant (breakfast/buffet) and The Copper Room (dinner) as on-site dining facilities

visitor.name: Greenglade Community Centre
visitor.desc: Greenglade Community Centre is a publicly operated recreation facility in Sidney, BC, run by Panorama Recreation (a service of the Peninsula Recreation Commission) and located about 25 minutes from Victoria. It offers a gymnasium, weight room, fitness studios, pottery studio, and an accessible playground on a single-level, fully accessible campus. Touring cyclists in the Saanich Peninsula area could use it as a rest stop with washroom access.

visitor.name: Matsqui Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Matsqui Recreation Centre is a City of Abbotsford municipal facility offering multi-sport programming to the broader community. Located in the Clearbrook neighbourhood, it serves as a full-service sports centre under the city's Parks, Recreation & Culture department. For touring cyclists, it represents a potential urban rest point with indoor facilities in the Abbotsford area.

visitor.name: Stanley Industrial Alliance Stage
visitor.desc: The Stanley Industrial Alliance Stage — better known as the Stanley Theatre — is a historic two-storey theatre at 2750 Granville Street in Vancouver, operated by the Arts Club Theatre Company. Situated in the South Granville neighbourhood, it is one of the city's landmark performing arts venues. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find it a recognizable cultural landmark along the Granville corridor.

visitor.name: Gibsons Swimming Pool
visitor.desc: The Gibsons & District Aquatic Facility is a publicly operated swimming and aquatics centre run by the Sunshine Coast Regional District, serving the Gibsons community on BC's Sunshine Coast. It sits on Gibsons Way and offers swimming programs alongside broader aquatic recreation. For touring cyclists arriving by ferry from Vancouver, it represents a convenient stop for a swim after a day on the saddle.

visitor.name: Government House Gardens
visitor.desc: The Terraces is one of over 20 named gardens within the Government House grounds in Victoria's Rockland neighbourhood, the official residence of the Lieutenant Governor of British Columbia. The gardens were originally designed in 1911 and feature a mix of English garden styles, public art including a 24-foot totem pole, and a wheelchair-accessible path. The grounds are open year-round with free admission, making it a pleasant stop for touring cyclists exploring Victoria.

notes.Café or food on site: Rudi's Tea Room is listed as an on-site facility within the Government House complex

visitor.name: Crag X Climbing Centre
visitor.desc: Crag X is a downtown Victoria indoor climbing gym founded in 1995 by outdoor climbers, housed in its own building with 15m-high walls, a dramatic glass street-front facade, and two bouldering areas. Its state-of-the-art ventilation system fully replaces the air every 2–3 hours, making it, as the gym puts it, 'the closest thing to outside you can fit in a building.' Beyond day passes, it offers beginner lessons, a transition-to-outdoors program, and a community-focused ethos welcoming all ages and abilities.

visitor.name: Cosports
visitor.desc: Cosports is a large indoor racket sports facility in Port Coquitlam featuring 17 professional badminton courts with Tinsue rubber flooring, plus table tennis, light volleyball, and newly opened pickleball courts. Courts can be rented by the day, week, or year, and the facility hosts competitive tournaments such as the Thanksgiving Cup table tennis event. Racket stringing services are also available on site.

visitor.name: Abbotsford Centre
visitor.desc: Rogers Forum (formerly Abbotsford Centre) is Abbotsford's premier indoor sports and entertainment arena, home to the Abbotsford Canucks — the 2025 AHL Calder Cup Champions and the AHL affiliate of the Vancouver Canucks. The venue hosts a busy calendar of concerts, comedy shows, and live sports drawing roughly 200,000 visitors per year from across the Fraser Valley and BC's Lower Mainland. A touring cyclist passing through Abbotsford will find a fully accessible, full-service event venue on King Road.

notes.Café or food on site: Website navigation includes a dedicated 'Food & Beverage' section under 'Plan Your Visit', confirming food and drink service is available at the venue

visitor.name: Jubilee Arts Centre
visitor.desc: The Jubilee Arts Centre is a community arts venue housed in the historic MSA Centennial Library Building in downtown Abbotsford, jointly operated by the Abbotsford Arts Council and the Abbotsford Downtown Business Association. Situated at Jubilee Park on South Fraser Way, it functions as a cultural gathering point for local arts events, exhibitions, and community programming. Touring cyclists passing through downtown Abbotsford will find it in the civic core, close to other downtown services.

visitor.name: ORL: Summerland Branch
visitor.desc: The Summerland Branch is part of the Okanagan Regional Library system, which has served the region since 1936 across 30 branches. It offers six public internet stations, Wi-Fi, printing, meeting and study rooms, and a regular calendar of community events. Located on Main Street in Summerland with free parking, it makes a convenient rest stop for touring cyclists passing through the southern Okanagan.

visitor.name: VIRL: Ladysmith Branch
visitor.desc: The Ladysmith branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the community since 1937, making it one of the older branches in the regional system. Located on the unceded territory of the Stz'uminus First Nation on First Avenue, the branch moved to its current downtown location in 1994 and now holds over 26,000 items. For touring cyclists passing through Ladysmith, it offers a welcoming public space with digital resources.

visitor.name: Secwépemc Museum & Heritage Park
visitor.desc: The former Kamloops Indian Residential School, located on Tk̓emlúps Te Secwépemc territory, is a site of profound historical and cultural significance—it gained international attention in 2021 following the confirmation of unmarked graves of 215 children on the grounds. The Tk̓emlúps Te Secwépemc nation also operates the adjacent Secwépemc Museum & Heritage Park, which preserves and shares the history and culture of the Interior-Salish Secwépemc people. Cyclists visiting Kamloops may wish to pay their respects at this site, though specific visitor protocols should be confirmed with the nation directly.

visitor.name: The Conservation Area at Maplewood Flats
visitor.desc: The Conservation Area at Maplewood Flats is the North Shore's only wild bird sanctuary, managed by the Wild Bird Trust of BC on the unceded territory of the Tsleil-Waututh Nation, featuring 5km of trails through restored mudflat habitat along Burrard Inlet. The site includes a Nature House, rotating and permanent exhibits, and a Coast Salish Plant Nursery that weaves ecological conservation with Indigenous cultural heritage. Situated on Dollarton Highway near the Second Narrows Bridge, it offers touring cyclists a distinctive and peaceful detour through one of North Vancouver's most ecologically significant green spaces.

detail.address: 2649 Dollarton Highway, North Vancouver, BC, V7H 1B1

visitor.name: Stanley Park Information Booth
visitor.desc: Stanley Park Information Booth is a visitor services office operated within Stanley Park, one of Canada's most celebrated urban parks and a centrepiece of Vancouver's cycling culture. The booth serves as an orientation hub for the park's iconic 10 km seawall loop and its network of interior cycling paths. Touring cyclists arriving in Vancouver frequently use the park as a gateway ride, making this information office a natural first stop.

visitor.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
visitor.desc: The Heritage Rose Garden is a named feature within VanDusen Botanical Garden, a 55-acre urban botanical oasis in Vancouver's Shaughnessy neighbourhood hosting over 7,500 plant species from around the world. The broader garden complex includes fine dining at the Shaughnessy Restaurant and casual fare at the Garden Cafe, set amid curated plant collections and seasonal floral exhibitions. Cycling is listed as a recommended way to arrive, and the site sits in a central Vancouver neighbourhood well-served by bike routes.

notes.Café or food on site: Shaughnessy Restaurant (fine dining, West Coast menu, open for lunch, afternoon tea, dinner, and weekend brunch, with a seasonal patio) and The Garden Cafe (Fair Trade coffees, handcrafted beverages, sandwiches, soups, and daily-changing entrees; seats 58 inside, 40 on heated patio) are both confirmed on site at VanDusen Botanical Garden

visitor.name: Robert Burnaby Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: A heated seasonal outdoor pool set in beautiful Robert Burnaby Park, operated by the City of Burnaby. The facility features a 6-lane, 22.86-metre pool with a 1-metre diving board and a free wading pool, plus full change rooms and shower houses — potentially useful amenities for touring cyclists passing through Metro Vancouver on a warm day.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Men's and women's shower houses listed under pool features

visitor.name: Greendale Acres
visitor.desc: Greendale Acres is a family-operated farm attraction that opened Canada's first corn maze in 1999 and has grown into a multi-season destination featuring tulip and flower fields, a corn maze, a farm shop, orchard cider, and live music events including the annual Chilliwack Corn Festival. The farm sits on a historic old dairy property in the Fraser Valley and is now run by the founding family's third generation, who host school groups, corporate events, and large seasonal festivals. Touring cyclists exploring the agricultural back roads near Chilliwack will find it a distinctive, authentically local stop.

detail.address: 41905 Yale Road West, Chilliwack, BC V2R 4J4

notes.Café or food on site: Dedicated Food page lists a Spring Food Menu and on-site food hut; food policy page confirms food service is available on site

visitor.name: Newton Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: The Newton Cultural Centre is a beautifully restored heritage firehall (Firehall #10) that now serves as the headquarters of the Arts Council of Surrey, a nonprofit supporting visual, performing, and literary arts since 1967. The building houses a 100-seat sprung-floor theatre, an intimate 50-viewer art gallery with monthly rotating exhibitions, and bookable meeting rooms—all openly accessible to the public without appointment. Touring cyclists interested in local culture and community arts would find it a compelling stop in the heart of Newton.

visitor.name: District of Metchosin Municipal Hall
visitor.desc: The District of Metchosin Municipal Hall is the civic heart of one of BC's smallest and most rural municipalities, nestled on the southwestern tip of the Saanich Peninsula near Victoria. Metchosin is known for its pastoral landscapes, heritage farmland, and quiet back roads that make it a popular destination for cyclists seeking a contrast to urban riding. The hall represents a tangible piece of small-town governance in a community that has actively resisted suburban sprawl.

visitor.name: Bowen Island Visitor Information Centre
visitor.desc: The Bowen Island Visitor Information Centre occupies a picturesque heritage building known as the Boulevard Cottage, situated immediately off the Bowen Island ferry terminal — making it the natural first stop for day-trippers and touring cyclists arriving by ferry. Operated by Tourism Bowen Island, it offers maps, local guides, and trip-planning advice covering the island's cycling trails, outdoor activities, restaurants, and accommodations. A downloadable 2025 Visitor Map & Guide is available covering parks, trails, beaches, and ferry schedules.

detail.address: 432 Cardena Road, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G1

visitor.name: Brakendale Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Brackendale Art Gallery — known locally as 'The BAG' — is Squamish and Sea-to-Sky's top-rated event venue, combining an art gallery, live music stage, and multiple rental spaces in a single destination. The on-site Zephyr Cafe serves locally sourced, scratch-made meals and baked goods with gluten-free and vegan options, making it a genuine food stop rather than just a gallery visit. Situated in the historic Brackendale neighbourhood on Squamish Nation territory, it serves as a community cultural hub with rotating exhibitions and frequent live events.

notes.Café or food on site: Zephyr Cafe on site serving locally sourced, scratch-made meals, baked goods, and beverages; gluten-free, vegan, and celiac-friendly options available

visitor.name: Rose Garden
visitor.desc: The Rose Garden is a free public garden in Vancouver, situated near Stanley Park and widely recognized as one of the city's most visited green spaces. Formal rose plantings make it a scenic rest stop for cyclists touring the seawall or Stanley Park loop. Admission is free and the garden is openly accessible to the public.

visitor.name: Wild Pacific Trail - Lighthouse Loop
visitor.desc: The Wild Pacific Trail is an 8-kilometre coastal trail on Ucluelet's west coast of Vancouver Island, winding through temperate rainforest, coastal bogs, mudflats, and dramatic ocean headlands in the traditional territory of the Yuułuʔiłʔatḥ First Nation. Managed by the Wild Pacific Trail Society, it features interpretive signage, free guided naturalist walks, and the Amphitrite House Interpretive Centre. The trail is particularly celebrated for storm-watching and its Ancient Cedars section, drawing visitors year-round.

visitor.name: The Clayoquot Sound Theatre
visitor.desc: The Clayoquot Sound Theatre is a 40-year-old community performing arts venue tucked into downtown Tofino, operated by the non-profit Clayoquot Sound Community Theatre Association. Despite its unassuming exterior on Campbell Street, the intimate 72-seat hall is known for exceptional acoustics and a warm atmosphere that has impressed performers from across the country. It is the year-round home of Monday Night Movies, the Tofino Pop concert series, the Tofino Jazz Festival, and a wide range of live music and stage productions.

notes.Café or food on site: Website /about page describes 'a small concession kitchen in the outer foyer from which beverages and appetizers can be served'; movie listings reference an 'ALL-ORGANIC CONCESSION' open before screenings

visitor.name: Carnegie Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Carnegie Community Centre occupies Vancouver's original Carnegie Library building, a landmark heritage structure at the corner of Main and Hastings in the Downtown Eastside. Operated by the City of Vancouver, it functions as a major community hub offering programs, services, and gathering space for one of the city's most storied neighbourhoods. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find it a recognizable and historically significant stop.

visitor.name: Weaver Creek Spawning Channel
visitor.desc: Weaver Creek Spawning Channel is a federally operated salmon enhancement facility run by Fisheries and Oceans Canada, located along Morris Valley Road near Harrison Mills. It is one of BC's most accessible spots to witness Pacific salmon returning to spawn, drawing visitors each autumn to observe thousands of sockeye and other salmon. For touring cyclists exploring the Fraser Valley, it offers a striking natural spectacle in a rural setting alongside quiet backroads.

visitor.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
visitor.desc: The Japanese Collection is a garden feature within VanDusen Botanical Garden, a 55-acre oasis in Vancouver's Shaughnessy neighbourhood with over 7,500 plant species from around the world. The parent garden offers fine dining at Shaughnessy Restaurant and a Garden Cafe inside its award-winning Visitor Centre, providing a genuine rest stop for cyclists. The grounds are accessible via bike and are well situated midway through several popular Vancouver cycling routes.

notes.Café or food on site: Shaughnessy Restaurant (fine dining, lunch/tea/dinner/brunch) and The Garden Cafe (Fair Trade coffee, sandwiches, soups, curries) are both located within VanDusen Botanical Garden

visitor.name: Tourism Abbotsford Visitors Centre
visitor.desc: Tourism Abbotsford Visitors Centre is the official visitor information office for the City of Abbotsford, operated by Tourism Abbotsford, which promotes the region's outdoor adventures, farm experiences, arts, and local food scene. Situated near the Trans-Canada corridor, it is a natural stopping point for touring cyclists entering or passing through the Fraser Valley. Staff would typically be able to assist with local route information, points of interest, and regional tourism resources.

visitor.name: Canadian Country Music Hall of Fame
visitor.desc: The Canadian Country Music Hall of Fame is a museum and landmark in Merritt, BC — a town that bills itself as the Country Music Capital of Canada. It honours inductees from across the Canadian country music industry, including both performing artists and behind-the-scenes builders. A touring cyclist passing through Merritt's compact downtown would find it a short detour off the main corridor.

visitor.name: SASCU Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: SASCU Recreation Centre is a large community facility in Salmon Arm operated by the non-profit Shuswap Recreation Society, featuring a pool, hot tub, fitness room, racquet courts, indoor walking track, and the twin-sheet NHL-regulation Rogers Rink arena. The complex also includes an auditorium, meeting rooms, and nearby sports fields, serving as a major recreational hub for residents and visiting athletes alike. Touring cyclists passing through Salmon Arm may find it a practical stop for aquatic and fitness amenities.

detail.address: 2550 10th Avenue NE, Salmon Arm, BC V1E 4N2

notes.Café or food on site: Contact page lists a dedicated 'Food Services Manager' staff role (Crystal de Boer EXT 201), indicating on-site food services operate within the complex

visitor.name: Venables Theatre
visitor.desc: Venables Theatre is a modern 400-seat performing arts venue in Oliver, BC, opened in 2014 and serving as a cultural hub for the South Okanagan Valley. The theatre presents a full season of concerts, comedy, tribute shows, theatrical productions, and family programming, drawing audiences from Oliver, Osoyoos, Penticton, and surrounding communities. It features a spacious lobby, state-of-the-art sound and lighting systems, and an intimate proscenium stage suitable for everything from school productions to professional touring acts.

visitor.name: Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery
visitor.desc: A contemporary art gallery on the UBC campus, established in 1948 as the UBC Fine Arts Gallery and rededicated in 1995 in a purpose-built Peter Cardew–designed building. It focuses on contemporary art exhibitions, publications, and public programs, and houses UBC's art collection and outdoor art collection. Admission is always free, making it an easy cultural stop for cyclists passing through the UBC endowment lands.

notes.Luggage / bag storage: Backpacks and large bags must be checked at the front desk

visitor.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge
visitor.desc: Capilano Suspension Bridge Park is widely described as BC's most popular attraction, set in a temperate rainforest canyon in North Vancouver. Visitors cross the iconic 140-metre suspension bridge, explore the Treetops Adventure canopy walkway, and wind along the Cliffwalk high above the canyon. The park is a paid-admission destination with a free shuttle from downtown Vancouver, making it a feasible day-trip goal for touring cyclists exploring the North Shore.

detail.address: 3735 Capilano Road, North Vancouver, BC V7R 4J1

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists three on-site dining options: The Cliff House Restaurant, Loggers' Grill, and On-the-Go (quick-service)

visitor.name: Kitsilano Showboat
visitor.desc: Kitsilano Showboat is an open-air theatre venue in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood. It offers outdoor performances in a public-facing setting that cycling visitors passing through the area may find worthwhile. The venue's open-air format and proximity to the waterfront make it a natural stopping point on a coastal cycling route.

visitor.name: Big Splash Water Slide Park
visitor.desc: Big Splash Water Slide Park is a seasonal outdoor water park in Tsawwassen featuring over a dozen body and tube slides for all skill levels, a kids splash zone, family and adults-only hot tubs, beach volleyball, basketball, and multiple on-site eateries and a licensed sports bar. Ranked #1 among BC waterparks by several media outlets and rated among North America's most affordable, it draws families from across the Lower Mainland. Notably, the park offers a complimentary shuttle from the Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal, making it a natural stop for cyclists arriving via BC Ferries.

detail.address: 4775 Nulelum Way, Tsawwassen, British Columbia V4M 4G9

notes.Café or food on site: Three eateries listed: Big Splash Grill (burgers, hot dogs, fish and chips, poutine), AJ's Pizza Joint, BV's Sports Bar (fully licensed), and Candy Cafe
notes.Luggage / bag storage: Keyed lockers available for rental on-site; listed under Equipment on guest-services page and hours-map page

visitor.name: South Okanagan Events Centre
visitor.desc: The South Okanagan Events Centre is Penticton's premier sports and entertainment arena, a 5,000-seat facility owned by the City of Penticton and home to the Penticton Vees BCHL junior hockey team. Opened in 2008, it hosts major touring concerts—Bryan Adams, Dwight Yoakam, and similar acts—and features a unique retractable seating system that converts between hockey and other configurations. The broader SOEC Complex includes an indoor walking track and connects directly to the Penticton Trade and Convention Centre.

detail.address: 853 Eckhardt Avenue West, Penticton, BC V2A 9C4

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Food and Beverage' as a dedicated section under Arena Information, indicating on-site food service

visitor.name: River Safari
visitor.desc: River Safari operates guided wildlife boat tours through Grizzly Bear Valley in BC's inland temperate rainforest, using native-style catamarans and custom jet boats to explore up to 12 kilometres of glacier-fed rivers and lakes in search of grizzly bears, moose, and eagles. The site also features The Forest Table, a floating-dock restaurant voted one of Canada's most unique dining experiences, and on-site lodge accommodation. Located 1 km off Yellowhead Highway 5 between Jasper and Kamloops, it is a memorable stop for touring cyclists on that corridor.

detail.address: 6080 Mud Lake Forest Service Rd, Blue River, BC V0E 1J0

notes.Café or food on site: The Forest Table Restaurant is on-site on a floating dock; full menu served, voted #3 most unique dining experience in Canada by TheTravel.com

visitor.name: GVPL: Langford Heritage Branch
visitor.desc: A branch of the Greater Victoria Public Library, located in Langford. The library offers free public computer access, Wi-Fi, and a wide digital collection including ebooks, audiobooks, and streaming media. A useful rest stop for touring cyclists passing through the western communities of Greater Victoria.

visitor.name: Nelson & District Community Complex
visitor.desc: The Civic Centre is a public community facility in downtown Nelson, BC, tagged in OpenStreetMap as a community centre at 305 Hall Street. It is operated under the Regional District of Central Kootenay's recreation portfolio alongside other community complexes in the region. Touring cyclists passing through Nelson may find it a useful landmark, but specific services for cyclists have not been confirmed.

visitor.name: Granville Island Stage
visitor.desc: The Granville Island Stage is one of three professional venues operated by the Arts Club Theatre Company, one of Canada's largest not-for-profit theatre companies, founded in 1964 and welcoming over a quarter million guests annually. It presents a full season of dramas, musicals, and new works in the heart of Granville Island, one of Vancouver's most popular urban cycling destinations. A touring cyclist riding the seawall or exploring the island can easily combine a visit here with the market, galleries, and waterfront that make Granville Island a standout stop.

notes.Café or food on site: Website 'Your Visit' navigation includes a dedicated 'Concession Menu' link, indicating food and drink are available at the venue

visitor.name: Glenora Community Hall
visitor.desc: A heritage community hall built in 1924 in the Cowichan Valley, four minutes southwest of Duncan on Vancouver Island. The hall sits near the Cowichan Valley Trail (part of the Trans-Canada Trail) in a rural area known for vineyards, farms, and artisan studios. It is managed by the Glenora Community Association and used for community social events and private rentals.

visitor.name: Chén̓chenstway Healing Garden and Indigenous Food Forest
visitor.desc: Chén̓chenstway — meaning 'to lift each other up, to stand and work together' in the Squamish language — is a free, publicly accessible Indigenous healing garden and food forest in Oxford Park, created through a partnership between the Vancouver Urban Food Forest Foundation, the Aboriginal Mother Centre Society, and the Vancouver Park Board. The site includes a Running Free Wildflowers Memorial Garden honouring children who never returned from residential schools. Regular community volunteer jams and plant teachings make it a living gathering space rooted in intergenerational, cross-cultural land stewardship.

notes.Water without admission: Water fountain installed at Oxford Park (2050 Wall Street); site has free admission (, no fees mentioned on website)

visitor.name: Waterslide
visitor.desc: A floating pier in Vancouver that doubles as a natural waterslide into the ocean, accessible only in summer and only during high tide. With a capacity of one, it offers a simple and memorable swim experience at what is likely Second Beach near Stanley Park. It is a free, publicly accessible curiosity that cycling visitors to the seawall would pass directly.

visitor.name: Stuart Park Outdoor Skating Rink
visitor.desc: Stuart Park Outdoor Skating Rink is a seasonal public ice rink situated within Stuart Park on the waterfront of Okanagan Lake in Kelowna. Lit for evening use and set on a paved surface, it draws locals and visitors alike as a free community gathering spot in winter. Touring cyclists passing through Kelowna may find the park a scenic rest stop or detour along the lakeshore corridor.

visitor.name: Silk Purse
visitor.desc: The Silk Purse is a community arts centre operated by the District of West Vancouver, situated along Argyle Avenue near the waterfront. It hosts art programs, exhibitions, and serves as a venue rental space for local cultural events. Cyclists exploring the West Vancouver shoreline route would find it a notable cultural stop in a scenic coastal setting.

visitor.name: Doctor Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
visitor.desc: The first full-scale traditional Ming Dynasty classical Chinese garden built outside of China, opened in 1986 in the heart of Vancouver's Chinatown. Named World's Top City Garden by National Geographic in 2011 and Canadian Garden of the Year in 2012, it was born from the community effort that defeated a proposed freeway through Chinatown and redirected Vancouver toward walking, cycling, and transit-oriented planning. Touring cyclists will find a tranquil cultural oasis steps from major urban cycling routes, offering guided garden and Chinatown walking tours, tea ceremonies, exhibitions, and a gift shop.

visitor.name: Mission Museum
visitor.desc: The Mission Museum is a community history museum housed in a meticulously restored 1907 former Canadian Bank of Commerce building — a pre-fabricated structure that arrived in Mission by 12 railcars — in the historic downtown core. Operated by the Mission District Historical Society, it stewards over 10,000 donated artifacts that document the region's past through exhibits, events, and public programming. The museum is surrounded by an Edwardian Garden maintained by community volunteers, offering a pleasant stop for cyclists exploring Mission's heritage streetscape.

visitor.name: Abbotsford Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Abbotsford Recreation Centre (ARC) is a large City of Abbotsford–operated multi-sport facility offering a broad range of fitness and recreation programming to residents and visitors. Located in the heart of Abbotsford, it is a typical municipal recreation complex that touring cyclists might use as a rest and refresh stop. The facility is wheelchair accessible and tagged in OSM as supporting multiple sports.

visitor.name: North Vancouver Tennis Centre
visitor.desc: The North Vancouver Tennis Centre is a public indoor tennis facility operated by the North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission (NVRC). It sits within the NVRC network of community recreation centres serving the District of North Vancouver. Touring cyclists in the area may find it a useful stop given its recreation-centre context, which often includes complementary amenities.

visitor.name: Johnson Bentley Memorial Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Johnson Bentley Memorial Aquatic Centre (JBMAC) is a publicly operated, accessible multi-use aquatic and fitness facility run by the City of West Kelowna, serving people of all ages and abilities. In addition to a swimming pool and weight room, it features a hot tub and steam room — amenities that touring cyclists finishing a long day in the saddle may find especially appealing. The facility operates under the motto 'Promote Safe Swimming and Healthy Lifestyles.'

visitor.name: Hassen Memorial Arena
visitor.desc: Hassen Memorial Arena is a lacrosse-tagged sports centre recorded in OpenStreetMap near Vernon, BC. Beyond its sport designation, very little verifiable detail is available about this facility from the sources at hand. Touring cyclists in the area may find limited services here without further on-the-ground confirmation.

detail.address: 3315 Pleasant Valley Road, Armstrong, BC V0E 1B0

visitor.name: Tighrope Improv Theatre
visitor.desc: Tightrope Theatre is an East Vancouver improv comedy venue offering weekly shows and a structured class program ranging from beginner to advanced levels, rooted in the Impro tradition of Keith Johnstone. Founded by Ali Froggat, a Capilano University theatre faculty member with an international reputation in improv, the theatre recently relocated to a new dedicated space on Napier Street. A touring cyclist looking for an evening of live comedy in a neighbourhood venue would find a lively, community-oriented space with multiple show formats.

visitor.name: Kasugai Gardens
visitor.desc: Kasugai Gardens is a public Japanese-style garden in downtown Kelowna, named after Kelowna's sister city Kasugai, Japan. Admission is free per OSM tags, making it an accessible rest stop for touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan. The garden offers a quiet, landscaped environment in an urban setting.

visitor.name: Hand of Man Museum
visitor.desc: The Hand of Man Museum is a museum of natural history, cultural arts, and conservation located in Maple Bay near Duncan. It features exhibits on ancient civilizations, historic hunting and gathering traditions, diverse ecosystems, and handcrafted artifacts, with a focus on education and conservation awareness. The museum has welcomed over 100,000 visitors and is associated with outdoorsman Jim Shockey.

visitor.name: Davie Village
visitor.desc: Gay Village (commonly called Davie Village) is Vancouver's historic LGBTQ+ neighbourhood, centered on Davie Street in the West End. Known for its rainbow-painted crosswalks, welcoming bars and restaurants, and strong community identity, it is both a cultural landmark and a lively destination for visitors. Its location near the Stanley Park Seawall and other major cycling routes makes it a natural waypoint for touring cyclists passing through central Vancouver.

detail.address: Davie Street at Bute Street, Vancouver, BC

visitor.name: Burnaby Village Museum
visitor.desc: Way Sang Yuen Wat Kee is a historical Chinese herbalist shop exhibit within Burnaby Village Museum, a 10-acre living history site set in Deer Lake Park, Burnaby. The museum brings early 20th-century BC community life to life through period buildings, costumed interpreters, and a restored heritage carousel, with particular recognition for its preservation of Chinese Canadian history. Admission is free, making it an accessible cultural stop on a cycling tour through Burnaby.

detail.address: 6501 Deer Lake Ave, Burnaby BC V5G 3T6

notes.Café or food on site: Mai's Café is confirmed on-site per the FAQ page: 'Mai's Café is open Tuesdays to Saturdays and statutory holidays from 11 am-4 pm.'

visitor.name: Kerry Park Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Kerry Park Recreation Centre is a publicly operated multi-sport facility managed by the Cowichan Valley Regional District, situated on Shawnigan-Mill Bay Road in the Mill Bay area of Vancouver Island. As a regional recreation centre serving the surrounding Cowichan Valley communities, it offers a range of sports and fitness programming. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a convenient stop, though specific cyclist-oriented amenities could not be confirmed from available sources.

visitor.name: Penticton Speedway
visitor.desc: Penticton Speedway bills itself as the fastest quarter-mile oval race track on the West Coast, hosting street stock, late model, hit-to-pass, monster truck, and winged sprint events from April to October. The facility also offers go-karting on a dedicated circuit and a driving-experience program where visitors can pilot legend and RS1 race cars with professional instruction. Located on Carmi Avenue in Penticton, it is a family-oriented motorsport venue in the heart of the Okanagan.

visitor.name: VPL: Firehall Branch
visitor.desc: The Firehall Branch is one of the Vancouver Public Library system's neighbourhood locations, serving the Fairview and South Granville area of Vancouver. As a free, publicly accessible institution, it offers a useful midpoint stop for touring cyclists moving through the city's west side. The VPL system is a well-established public resource with multiple branches across Vancouver.

visitor.name: Historic Hat Creek Ranch
visitor.desc: Historic Hat Creek Ranch is a BC heritage site designated since 1981, encompassing roughly 130 hectares of farmyards, fields, and rangeland along with approximately twenty historic wooden buildings dating from 1861 into the early 20th century. Located near Cache Creek on the Gold Rush Trail, it offers a rare glimpse into the era of roadhouse travel and early BC ranching. Touring cyclists passing through the Interior could find it a compelling cultural stop along a route that follows historic wagon roads.

visitor.name: Chilliwack Track Complex
visitor.desc: The Chilliwack Track Complex is an 8.46-hectare public athletic facility constructed as a joint venture between School District No. 33 and the City of Chilliwack for the 1993 BC Summer Games. It features a 400-metre synthetic running track built to international standards, set behind Sardis Senior Secondary School. A fieldhouse on site includes washrooms and a concession stand, making it a functional rest stop for cyclists passing through Sardis.

notes.Café or food on site: Website mentions a 'concession' as part of the fieldhouse

visitor.name: Canadian Museum of Flight
visitor.desc: The Canadian Museum of Flight, established in 1996 at Langley Airport, preserves and displays a collection of historic Canadian aircraft and aviation artifacts. It is one of British Columbia's dedicated aviation heritage museums and a notable destination for those cycling the Fraser Valley region. Touring cyclists will find it a distinctive stop offering a look at Canada's aviation history in an airport setting.

visitor.name: VIRL: Port Alberni Branch
visitor.desc: The Port Alberni Branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the community since 1936, with origins in the back of McVicar's Drug Store where shop employees acted as library attendants. The branch moved to the Echo Centre in 1972 and underwent a major refurbishment and expansion in 2007, now holding a collection of over 35,000 items. Touring cyclists can drop in for free public WiFi, sit-down service, and public access computers in a fully wheelchair-accessible space.

detail.address: 4255 Wallace Street, Unit B, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 3Y6

visitor.name: Remote Passages
visitor.desc: Remote Passages Marine Excursions has run eco-tours out of Tofino's Wharf Street since 1986, pioneering zodiac-based whale watching on BC's west coast and expanding to sea kayaking, black bear watching, Meares Island old-growth rainforest tours, and the boat-and-hike journey to Hot Springs Cove. Operating in the Clayoquot Sound UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, the company offers one of the longest wildlife viewing seasons on BC's west coast, from February to November. Touring cyclists who have ridden to Tofino can extend their adventure onto the water, encountering gray whales, humpbacks, orcas, sea otters, and coastal bears in their natural habitat.

visitor.name: Museum of Northern British Columbia
visitor.desc: The Museum of Northern British Columbia is a century-old regional institution in Prince Rupert dedicated to preserving and interpreting the natural and cultural heritage of the Northwest Coast, with a particular focus on Tsimshian First Nations history and art. It administers several related sites including the 'Wiwaabm Ts'msyeen Tsimshian Performance Longhouse and the Kwinitsa Station Railway Museum, and offers immersive guided tours combining gallery visits with live feast experiences and traditional dance. For a touring cyclist arriving in Prince Rupert, it represents a compelling cultural anchor in a remote northern port city steeped in Indigenous and maritime history.

visitor.name: Tom Hopkins Ravine Park
visitor.desc: Tom Hopkins Ravine Park protects over 6.5 hectares of sensitive second-growth forest ravine ecosystem in Surrey, with more than 1 km of Delta Creek running through it. Natural area trails in the west section of the park offer a quiet forest walk, with a pedestrian bridge crossing Delta Creek. Access is from 98A or 99 Avenue, and most of the ravine interior is inaccessible to protect the sensitive habitat.

visitor.name: Cumberland Museum & Archives
visitor.desc: The Cumberland Museum and Archives is a community history museum on Vancouver Island that chronicles the diverse stories of Cumberland's coal mining heritage, its multicultural workforce, and the social and political struggles that shaped the region. Founded in 1969 and operated by a non-profit historical society, it houses permanent and rotating exhibitions alongside a community research library and digital photograph archive. Cumberland is a celebrated cycling destination — particularly for mountain biking — making this a natural cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Comox Valley.

visitor.name: S.S. Moyie National Historic Site
visitor.desc: The S.S. Moyie is the oldest known intact passenger-carrying sternwheel steamer in the world, built in 1898 for the Canadian Pacific Railway and now permanently ashore in Kaslo on Kootenay Lake. Designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 1958, it offers tours of the original vessel—including the freight deck, saloon, pilot house, and paddlewheel—alongside a Visitor Centre, Gift Shop, Caboose, and the Kootenay Lake Archives. For a touring cyclist completing the Kootenay Lake loop, this waterfront site is a genuinely remarkable piece of BC and CPR history.

visitor.name: YMCA-YWCA Downtown
visitor.desc: The YMCA-YWCA Downtown Victoria is a full-service community fitness and recreation centre operated by the YMCA-YWCA of Vancouver Island, offering pool and aquatics, fitness programs, and community health services in the heart of downtown. It is one of two YMCA facilities on Vancouver Island and offers a 'Member for a Day' option that allows drop-in visitors to access facilities without a full membership. As a non-profit with financial assistance programs, it functions as an accessible community hub for both residents and visitors.

visitor.name: Queensborough Community Centre
visitor.desc: Queensborough Community Centre is a civic, two-storey recreation facility operated by New Westminster Parks and Recreation Department, situated in the Queensborough neighbourhood—a relatively isolated community on the south arm of the Fraser River. As the primary public recreation hub for this island neighbourhood, it serves residents with a range of programming and facilities. Touring cyclists crossing through Queensborough may find it a useful waypoint, though specific cyclist-oriented amenities are not confirmed.

visitor.name: Parkgate Community Centre
visitor.desc: Parkgate Community Centre is a publicly operated recreation facility run by the North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission (NVRC) in the eastern reaches of North Vancouver, near the Deep Cove area and popular North Shore cycling routes. The centre houses a large gymnasium with badminton, pickleball, basketball, and volleyball courts, a climbing wall, a fitness centre, a pottery studio, and several bookable meeting and multi-purpose rooms. As a community hub near trailheads and scenic coastal roads, it could serve as a practical rest or regrouping point for touring cyclists passing through the area.

detail.address: 3625 Banff Court, North Vancouver, BC V7H2Z8

visitor.name: CFB Esquimalt Naval & Military Museum - NAD20
visitor.desc: The CFB Esquimalt Naval & Military Museum preserves the heritage of Canada's West Coast naval and military presence, housed in Buildings 37 and 39 on Naden, the country's oldest active naval base. Exhibits span Canada's West Coast Navy, the Canadian Women's Army Corps, the Women's Royal Canadian Naval Service, and the West Coast Defences, with artifacts ranging from a turn-of-the-century deep-sea diving helmet to optical rangefinders. The museum also holds an expanding archive of photographs, ship plans, and naval documents, and offers both guided and self-guided tours.

detail.address: Naden 20, CFB Esquimalt, Esquimalt, BC V9A 7N2

visitor.name: Scotia Barn
visitor.desc: Scotia Barn (formerly Burnaby 8 Rinks) is one of Canada's largest multi-rink indoor ice facilities, operated by Canlan Sports and featuring six NHL-sized ice rinks, a dedicated figure skating rink, and an indoor soccer field. It hosts competitive leagues, drop-in programs, camps, and tournaments year-round for youth and adults across Metro Vancouver. As a large commercial sports complex, it caters primarily to ice hockey and skating participants rather than touring cyclists.

visitor.name: Juan de Fuca Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Juan de Fuca Recreation Centre is a publicly operated civic sports and recreation facility run by Westshore Parks and Recreation in the Westshore area near Victoria. It serves the broader Capital Regional District community and is typical of large multi-purpose Canadian recreation centres that anchor neighbourhood activity. Touring cyclists in the Victoria area may find it a useful stop given its public mandate and likely range of facilities.

visitor.name: Peace Gallery North
visitor.desc: Peace Gallery North is a public art gallery housed within the North Peace Cultural Centre, a community arts hub that has operated in Fort St. John since 1992. It represents both established and emerging artists from the Peace Region, rotating exhibits throughout the year. The centre's About page explicitly positions Fort St. John as a key touring stop in northeast BC, seven hours north of Edmonton and a gateway to Prince George.

notes.Café or food on site: About page states the North Peace Cultural Centre is 'Host to a Theatre, Café, Library, Art Gallery, and Child Care.'

visitor.name: SL: Fleetwood Branch
visitor.desc: Fleetwood Branch is one of ten Surrey Libraries locations serving the Fleetwood neighbourhood of Surrey, BC. As a public library, it offers free access to books, digital resources, computer terminals, and community programming. Touring cyclists may find it a useful urban rest stop with Wi-Fi and public-use computers available without admission.

visitor.name: Large Quarry Garden
visitor.desc: The Large Quarry Garden is a sunken ornamental garden carved into a former basalt quarry within Queen Elizabeth Park in Vancouver, featuring tiered flowerbeds and reflecting pools set against the quarry walls. Situated at one of the highest points in Vancouver, the surrounding park offers panoramic views of the city and North Shore mountains. It is a popular stop on cycling routes through the area and is freely accessible to the public.

visitor.name: Irving K. Barber Learning Centre
visitor.desc: The Irving K. Barber Learning Centre is a landmark four-storey building on UBC's Vancouver campus, publicly accessible to all British Columbians as a hub for research, lifelong learning, and community engagement. It houses multiple library services including the Music, Art & Architecture Library and Chapman Learning Commons, alongside rotating art exhibits, event spaces, and community programs. Named after BC philanthropist Irving K. Barber, it is a notable cultural and educational destination for anyone exploring UBC's campus by bike.

visitor.name: NWPL: Queensborough Library
visitor.desc: The Queensborough Library is a branch of the New Westminster Public Library, situated inside the Queensborough Community Centre on Ewen Avenue. It offers free public Wi-Fi, public computers, borrowing services, and regular community programming including employment services drop-ins. For a touring cyclist, it represents a welcoming public indoor stop with digital access in the Queensborough neighbourhood of New Westminster.

detail.address: 920 Ewen Avenue, New Westminster, BC V3M 5C8

visitor.name: The Hive
visitor.desc: The Hive is a bouldering-focused climbing gym occupying a two-storey building in Vancouver's Industrial Avenue corridor. It is part of a multi-location BC and Manitoba chain and is notable as one of two Hive branches within walking distance of each other on the same street. For touring cyclists looking for an active rest day, it offers a drop-in climbing experience in an urban industrial setting.

visitor.name: Art Gallery of Greater Victoria
visitor.desc: The Art Gallery of Greater Victoria is anchored by a striking 1889 Victorian mansion alongside seven modern galleries, holding the largest public art collection in British Columbia — over 22,000 works — including the most significant collection of Asian art in Western Canada. Founded in 1951 when the Spencer Mansion was donated to the city, the AGGV is a genuine landmark in Victoria's Rockland neighbourhood and a draw for visitors from across the island and beyond. Cyclists will find it a culturally rich stop, with free admission days and a coat-room locker area where large bags can be safely stored.

notes.Luggage / bag storage: Free lockers with keys in the coat room available to all visitors for storing personal belongings while browsing the Gallery. Note: bags larger than 12″ × 12″ × 9″ are prohibited in exhibition spaces (except medical/first aid), so cyclists with large panniers would need to use these lockers

visitor.name: CPL: Poirier Branch
visitor.desc: The CPL Poirier Branch is a single-storey civic library operated by Coquitlam Public Library, providing free access to books, digital resources, computers, and community programming. As a no-admission-required public facility in the Tri-Cities area, it offers a welcoming rest environment for touring cyclists passing through Coquitlam. The branch is fully wheelchair accessible and runs a broad range of programs for adults, teens, and children.

visitor.name: War Memorial Gym
visitor.desc: The War Memorial Gymnasium is a historic university sports facility at the University of British Columbia, built as a memorial to UBC alumni who served in World War II. It functions as a major campus recreation centre hosting intramural sports, competitive programs, and sport clubs including a Cycling Sport Club. Situated on UBC's scenic Point Grey campus, it is a notable landmark for cyclists exploring this corner of Vancouver.

visitor.name: Grouse Grind Trailhead
visitor.desc: The Grouse Grind is one of Metro Vancouver's most iconic challenges, a steep trail climbing nearly 900 metres up the face of Grouse Mountain in North Vancouver. Touring cyclists can ride to the base at 6400 Nancy Greene Way and experience the mountain complex, which also hosts the Grouse Bike Park with lift access, bike rentals, and mountain bike camps — making it relevant beyond just the hiking trail. The summit is home to grizzly bear habitat, wildlife demonstrations, scenic lookouts, and multiple dining venues with panoramic views of Vancouver.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists multiple food/beverage outlets: Grouse Grind Coffee Bar (name implies base-area location), Starbucks, Altitudes Bistro, Lupins Café, The Observatory. Several others noted as closed: Grizzly Lookout Café, Rusty Rail BBQ, BeaverTails

visitor.name: Other Guise
visitor.desc: Other Guise is a community-motivated theatre company founded in 2001 and based at 716 Johnson Street in downtown Victoria, dedicated to original theatrical presentations that reflect Vancouver Island's history and culture while supporting local professional and emerging artists. The fully ground-level, step-free venue features automated entry doors, a main performance and lounge space, and a bar, making it a welcoming stop in the heart of Victoria. The company holds charitable status and takes a zero-waste approach to its operations.

visitor.name: The Fields at Richmond Olympic Oval
visitor.desc: The Fields is a 4,200 square metre outdoor multi-use turf and court complex situated at the Richmond Olympic Oval, a landmark legacy of the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympic Games on Richmond's Fraser River waterfront. It offers sport turf, three hard-surface basketball courts, and a field-side high performance training facility available for both programmed sport events and public drop-in use. The adjacent Oval building—originally the long-track speed skating venue—houses over 14,000 square metres of indoor sport and fitness space, making this a substantial multi-sport destination.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Time Out, Tap & Snack' as an on-site support service under The Fields amenities section

visitor.name: Surf Sister
visitor.desc: Founded in 1999 with a mission to create a more inclusive surf community, Surf Sister is Tofino's well-known surf school and shop offering lessons, camps, and rentals for all ages and abilities. The main 'Shred Quarters' location sits in downtown Tofino, with a second outpost at Pacific Sands Beach Resort. A repeat Tripadvisor Traveller's Choice Award winner, it draws visitors from around the world to BC's rugged west coast surf scene.

visitor.name: village host
visitor.desc: The Whistler Visitor Centre is Whistler's official in-resort information hub, staffed by knowledgeable locals who can assist with activity bookings, transit schedules, maps, and trip planning across British Columbia. Located adjacent to the bus and taxi loop at 4230 Gateway Drive, it is a logical stopping point for touring cyclists arriving by transit or seeking local route and trail information. Staff are also reachable by phone, email, and a mobile live chat concierge service.

visitor.name: BC Golf Museum and Hall of Fame
visitor.desc: The BC Golf Museum and Hall of Fame chronicles the history of golf in British Columbia, honouring the province's notable players, courses, and contributors to the sport. Located in Point Grey near UBC, it sits along routes popular with Vancouver-area cyclists. A touring cyclist passing through the area would find it a compact cultural stop in a quiet residential neighbourhood.

visitor.name: New Brighton Pool
visitor.desc: New Brighton Pool is a seasonal outdoor public swimming pool operated by the City of Vancouver, situated near the waterfront in the Hastings-Sunrise neighbourhood of East Vancouver. It is open during summer months and is one of several outdoor pools the city operates for public recreation. Touring cyclists riding the nearby Central Valley Greenway or exploring the East Vancouver waterfront will find it a convenient stop on a warm summer day.

visitor.name: Mossom Creek Park
visitor.desc: Mossom Creek Hatchery and Education Centre is one of the longest-running community hatcheries in British Columbia, established in 1976 by high school volunteers and now managed by the Burrard Inlet Marine Enhancement Society within Mossom Creek Park in Port Moody. The facility sits in a pristine watershed setting with forest and creek views, wildlife cameras, and hands-on salmon enhancement and education programs. In 2023 it received the Gold Accessibility Certification from the Rick Hansen Foundation.

detail.address: 12 Mossom Creek Drive, Port Moody, BC

visitor.name: The HUB at Cowichan Station
visitor.desc: The HUB at Cowichan Station is a volunteer-run community centre housed in a restored 100-year-old elementary school building in the rural Cowichan Valley, operated by the Cowichan Station Area Association. It offers fitness classes, a film club, disc golf, and an on-site café, making it a lively gathering place for locals and visitors alike. Cyclists touring the Cowichan Valley's back roads will find it a welcoming stop in a small agricultural settlement between Duncan and the Saanich Peninsula.

notes.Café or food on site: Website navigation includes 'Eat at the Café' and recurring events list 'HUB Café Fridays', confirming an on-site café

visitor.name: Chinese Cultural Centre Museum
visitor.desc: The Chinese Cultural Centre Museum and Archives is a free-admission cultural institution in Vancouver's historic Chinatown, preserving and presenting the history of Chinese Canadians in British Columbia. It is part of the larger Chinese Cultural Centre of Greater Vancouver, which has operated since 1981 and offers community events, Cantonese opera performances, and organized walking tours of Chinatown. A cyclist passing through Chinatown will find this a meaningful stop for understanding the neighbourhood's deep cultural heritage.

visitor.name: Ayum Creek Regional Park Reserve
visitor.desc: Ayum Creek Regional Park Reserve is a nature reserve in the Sooke area, managed by the Capital Regional District. It sits along Ayum Creek and offers a natural setting for visitors exploring Vancouver Island's southern coast by bike.

visitor.name: Wasa Hotel Museum
visitor.desc: The Wasa Hotel Museum is a historic two-storey hipped-roof building within Fort Steele Heritage Town, a sweeping outdoor heritage complex of more than 60 historic and reconstructed structures operated by the Cranbrook Archives, Museum, and Landmark Society. The site interprets BC's late-19th-century Gold Rush and ranching era on the ancestral territory of the Ktunaxa and Secwépemc peoples, now under renewed stewardship since April 2025. Touring cyclists will find the Wasa Hotel listed as one of the site's designated cooling stations, making it a useful mid-ride refuge on hot Kootenay days.

notes.Café or food on site: Website navigation includes a 'Food & Drink' section; contact page lists a Food & Beverage Coordinator; FAQ confirms the Wildhorse Theatre sells popcorn, candy, and cotton candy on site

visitor.name: Grand Forks Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: A year-round public aquatic centre in Grand Forks, originally opened in 1987 and operated by the Regional District of Kootenay Boundary. The facility features four 25-metre lanes, a large shallow-water leisure area, sauna, whirlpool, and a fitness and wellness centre. For touring cyclists passing through the Boundary region, it offers a welcome chance to swim, soak in the hot tub, and clean up.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Shower available as a drop-in service, listed separately in the admission fee table

visitor.name: Nanaimo Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Nanaimo Art Gallery is an ambitious public contemporary art gallery founded in 1976 and now situated in the heart of downtown Nanaimo on Commercial Street, on the traditional territory of the Snuneymuxw First Nations. The gallery presents rotating exhibitions of contemporary art alongside robust programs for all ages, and operates on an admission-by-donation model that makes it genuinely accessible to all visitors. A touring cyclist exploring downtown Nanaimo will find it a short walk from the waterfront, neighboured by cafes and shops along a lively commercial strip.

visitor.name: VIRL: Qualicum Beach Branch
visitor.desc: The Qualicum Beach branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the community since 1937 and has been housed in the Town Hall building since 1997. Part of the Vancouver Island Regional Library system — one of the largest public library networks in BC — it provides free public services to residents and visitors across a wide stretch of Vancouver Island. Its central Qualicum Beach location makes it a natural waypoint for cyclists passing through town.

detail.address: 660 Primrose Street, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 2R5

visitor.name: Shaw Centre for the Salish Sea
visitor.desc: The Shaw Centre for the Salish Sea is BC's only not-for-profit aquarium in Greater Victoria, situated on the Sidney waterfront on the traditional territory of the W̱SÁNEĆ (Saanich) people. The centre offers interactive self-guided exhibits, daily animal ambassador programs, and behind-the-scenes aquarist tours focused on the ecology of the 110,000 sq km Salish Sea bioregion. Touring cyclists riding the Saanich Peninsula or catching ferries from Sidney will find it a compelling cultural stop, recognized among the top attractions on Vancouver Island.

detail.address: 9811 Seaport Place, Sidney, BC, Canada V8L 4X3

visitor.name: Coast Capital Playhouse
visitor.desc: Founded in 1944, White Rock Players' Club is one of BC's longest-running community theatre companies, operating out of the 176-seat Oceana PARC Playhouse on Johnston Road in White Rock. The volunteer-run non-profit stages roughly five productions per season ranging from classic dramas to holiday pantomimes, and also hosts rental comedy and music shows. It sits on the main commercial strip in White Rock, a short ride from the waterfront promenade popular with touring cyclists.

detail.address: 1532 Johnston Road, White Rock, BC V4B 3Z7

notes.Café or food on site: Small concession in the lobby mentioned on the About page

visitor.name: Kerrisdale Cyclone Taylor Arena
visitor.desc: The Kerrisdale Cyclone Taylor Arena is a City of Vancouver civic ice sports facility in the Kerrisdale neighbourhood, named in honour of early hockey legend Fred 'Cyclone' Taylor. Tagged in OpenStreetMap as a sports centre with skating, it serves the community as a public recreation venue. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a useful rest stop given its civic status and central Kerrisdale location.

visitor.name: Rosemary Brown Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Rosemary Brown Recreation Centre is a year-round City of Burnaby multi-sport facility anchored by two NHL-sized ice rinks seating 263 and 148 spectators respectively. The centre hosts public skating, hockey leagues, figure skating, ringette, and in the off-season converts to dry-floor sports including pickleball and lacrosse. Named after a pioneering BC politician and social activist, it functions as a busy community hub on Burnaby's south slope.

visitor.name: ORL: Mission Branch
visitor.desc: The Mission Branch is part of the Okanagan Regional Library (ORL), a regional system of 30 branches serving over 399,000 people across the Okanagan and surrounding areas, established in 1936. Located in the Mission neighbourhood of Kelowna on Gordon Drive, it offers typical public library services including books, digital resources, and programs. As a free public institution, it can be a useful rest and resource stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

visitor.name: Gallery 1710
visitor.desc: Gallery 1710 is the home of the South Delta Artists Guild in Tsawwassen, showcasing rotating monthly exhibitions of original works by local artists spanning realism to abstract, watercolour to mixed media and 3D art. Located just minutes from the Tsawwassen ferry terminal and close to the Delta dike cycling network, it makes a natural cultural stop for cyclists passing through the area. The guild, incorporated in 1975, also runs workshops and Saturday artist demonstrations open to the public.

visitor.name: Art Works
visitor.desc: A Canadian art gallery in East Vancouver's light-industrial Venables corridor, operating since 1986. Represents BC and North American artists across painting, photography, and digital art with rotating exhibitions. Free admission and no appointment needed on weekdays, making it an easy cultural stop.

visitor.name: Heritage Gallery
visitor.desc: The Heritage Gallery, also known as the Carriage House, is a historic outbuilding within the MSA Museum Society complex near Abbotsford, British Columbia. The MSA Museum Society is a registered non-profit dedicated to preserving the history of the Abbotsford–Mission–Matsqui area, centred on the restored 1920 Trethewey House Heritage Site built for a local timber baron. A touring cyclist visiting the area would find a tangible connection to the Fraser Valley's early industrial and domestic history.

visitor.name: Royal Theatre
visitor.desc: The Royal Theatre is a 1416-seat premier performing arts venue that has anchored Victoria's cultural life since 1913, showcasing its original Rococo/Renaissance Revival architecture fused with modern production technology. It hosts an eclectic range of events from Broadway touring productions and symphony concerts to comedy, opera, and rock shows, drawing over 200,000 visitors annually. For a touring cyclist, it represents a landmark stop in downtown Victoria steps from Blanshard and Broughton Streets.

visitor.name: Christine Sinclair Community Centre
visitor.desc: Christine Sinclair Community Centre is a City of Burnaby recreation facility named after Canadian soccer icon Christine Sinclair, situated in the Burnaby Lake 'sports central' hub alongside sports fields and ice arenas. Formerly known as Fortius Sport & Health, it was rebranded as part of Burnaby's community recreation network and offers state-of-the-art fitness amenities including cardio and weight rooms, a gymnasium, and a steam room. Its central location near Bill Copeland Sports Centre makes it a substantial recreation node for the eastern Burnaby area.

visitor.name: Pemberton & District Public Library
visitor.desc: The Pemberton & District Public Library is a modern community library serving the Pemberton valley, a popular hub for cycling in the Sea-to-Sky corridor. Beyond books, it offers a 'Library of Things' collection, free digital resources, and a bookable 2-person meeting pod. Touring cyclists would find free Wi-Fi and public computers available during open hours.

visitor.name: Sooke Fine Arts Society
visitor.desc: The Sooke Fine Arts Society runs Vancouver Island's longest-running juried fine art show, celebrating its 40th anniversary in 2026. Each summer the show brings together the finest artists from Vancouver Island and BC's coastal islands for a 10-day run of gallery exhibitions, artist demonstrations, live music, and community events. Held at SEAPARC Recreation Centre in Sooke, it is a genuine cultural highlight on the southern Vancouver Island touring circuit.

visitor.name: VIRL: Chemainus Branch
visitor.desc: The Chemainus Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library is a modern civic library that opened in January 2020, the community's third location since the original library debuted in the local Masonic Hall in 1949. It offers free public WiFi, computers, printing, scanning, and research assistance as part of the broader VIRL network spanning Vancouver Island. Wheelchair accessible and centrally located, it makes a practical indoor rest stop for touring cyclists seeking connectivity while passing through Chemainus.

visitor.name: Gallery Gachet
visitor.desc: Gallery Gachet is an artist-run centre in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside with a mandate to support artists addressing mental health and socio-political marginalization. The gallery hosts rotating exhibitions, curator talks, and workshops in a single-level accessible space. Located near Pigeon Park between Carrall and Columbia Streets, it's easily reached by transit or bike.

detail.address: 9 W Hastings St, Vancouver, BC V6B 1G4
