visitor.name: Prince George Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Prince George Aquatic Centre is a City-operated public facility offering swimming and fitness services, with OSM-tagged amenities including a hot tub, sauna, and steam room. Situated at 1770 George Paul Lane, it serves as a notable recreational stop in Prince George for those seeking a full recovery experience. The 'Leisure Access Program' listed on the city website suggests inclusive access options for the public.

detail.address: 1770 George Paul Lane, Prince George, V2N 0E1

visitor.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
visitor.desc: The Canadian Medicinal Garden is a specific themed garden section located within VanDusen Botanical Garden, a 55-acre public botanical garden in Vancouver featuring over 7,500 plant species from around the world. VanDusen is a well-established cultural and natural attraction in the Shaughnessy neighbourhood, easily reachable by bike. Visiting cyclists will find on-site dining at the Shaughnessy Restaurant and Garden Café, as well as a gift shop and seasonal public programming.

notes.Café or food on site: Website confirms two food venues on site: Shaughnessy Restaurant (fine dining, lunch/afternoon tea/dinner/weekend brunch) and The Garden Café (Fair Trade coffees, sandwiches, soups) inside the Visitor Centre

visitor.name: Annette Beaudreau Amphitheatre
visitor.desc: The Annette Beaudreau Amphitheatre is an outdoor performance venue set within Memorial Park in West Kelowna, hosting a free public summer concert series across multiple genres including blues, reggae, Cuban music, and tribute acts. The venue draws community audiences with food trucks and a Friday market operating alongside concerts. Admission to all performances is free, making it an accessible cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan.

visitor.name: Nelson Public Library
visitor.desc: The Nelson Public Library is a well-established community library in the heart of Nelson, serving residents and visitors with an extensive physical and digital collection including books, audiobooks, DVDs, and online databases. Open to anyone for on-site use, it offers a welcoming space to learn, study, and relax, with free access to computers and wireless internet. The library sits on the traditional territory of the Sinixt, Ktunaxa, and Syilx peoples and has been a pillar of the community for over 125 years.

visitor.name: Guilford Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: A City of Surrey municipal recreation centre in the Guildford neighbourhood offering swimming, sports, and fitness programs. The facility includes a pool and hosts a wide variety of drop-in and registered programs. Wheelchair accessible.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Swimming pool facility; showers are a mandatory part of public pool facilities

visitor.name: Ranger Station Art Gallery
visitor.desc: The Ranger Station Art Gallery occupies the original 1951 Forestry Ranger Station building on the shore of Harrison Lake, operated by the not-for-profit Kent Harrison Arts Council since 1972. It is the only public art gallery in the area, hosting monthly exhibitions by visual artists and running a year-long national artist-in-residence program with on-site living and studio space. Cyclists passing through Harrison Hot Springs can step into this historic building to catch rotating shows featuring a wide range of visual art media.

visitor.name: Mayne Island Community Library
visitor.desc: A small community library on Mayne Island, part of the Southern Gulf Islands Community Libraries network. It offers free Wi-Fi, printing services, and a quiet place to rest for cyclists exploring the Gulf Islands by ferry. The library also connects visitors to community resources including the Mayne Island Museum and Chamber of Commerce.

detail.address: 411 Naylor Road, Mayne Island, BC V0N 2J2

visitor.name: Teafarm
visitor.desc: Westholme Tea Company is a working organic tea farm and artisanal teashop in the Cowichan Valley near Chemainus, one of only a handful of places in Canada growing true Camellia sinensis tea plants. The farm imports and hand-blends organic loose-leaf teas from estates around the world alongside their own rare Canadian-terroir harvest. Cyclists touring the Cowichan Valley have specifically noted stopping in here for tea samples and welcoming service from staff.

visitor.name: VIRL: Nanaimo Harbourfront Branch
visitor.desc: The Creativity Commons (Nanaimo Harbourfront) is a public library branch operated by Vancouver Island Regional Library, situated on Nanaimo's waterfront with a history of library services in the community dating to the 1860s. The branch occupies floors 2 and 3 of its building and offers meeting room bookings, digital learning resources, and a broad range of collections. Its central harbourfront location makes it a natural stopping point for touring cyclists passing through downtown Nanaimo.

visitor.name: Hillcrest Rink
visitor.desc: Hillcrest Rink is a public ice facility operated by the Vancouver Park Board in the Hillcrest area of Vancouver, offering both ice hockey and recreational skating year-round. Situated near Queen Elizabeth Park, it is part of a broader recreation complex that draws locals and visitors alike. Touring cyclists passing through south Vancouver will find it a recognizable public landmark in a well-connected neighbourhood.

visitor.name: Patricia Bay Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Patricia Bay Visitor Centre is operated by the Saanich Peninsula Chamber of Commerce and serves as a tourism information office on the Patricia Bay Highway corridor between Victoria and the Swartz Bay ferry terminal. It is a practical first or last stop for cyclists arriving or departing via the BC Ferries route, offering regional orientation for Sidney, North Saanich, and Central Saanich. The Chamber has served the peninsula since 1912 and represents over 250 local businesses.

detail.address: 10382 Patricia Bay Hwy, North Saanich, BC V8L 5S8

visitor.name: VPL: Oakridge Branch
visitor.desc: VPL Oakridge Branch is a public library in Vancouver's Oakridge neighbourhood operated by the Vancouver Public Library system. It is freely accessible to the public and offers Wi-Fi, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists needing internet access or a quiet place to rest. As part of a major urban library network, it is a well-established civic resource.

visitor.name: Renfrew Park Fitness Centre
visitor.desc: Renfrew Park Fitness Centre is a City of Vancouver municipal recreation facility located within Renfrew Park in East Vancouver. It operates as a fee-based fitness centre, making it part of Vancouver's network of publicly accessible community recreation spaces. A touring cyclist passing through the area could use it for a workout or to take advantage of typical recreation centre amenities.

visitor.name: Dunbar Community Centre
visitor.desc: Dunbar Community Centre has served the Dunbar neighbourhood of Vancouver since 1958, jointly operated by the Vancouver Parks Board and the volunteer-run Dunbar Community Centre Association. The facility houses a fitness centre, squash courts, pottery room, and a preschool, offering a wide range of recreational and social programs. Touring cyclists passing through southwest Vancouver may find it a convenient neighbourhood stop, though it is primarily a local community resource rather than a destination attraction.

visitor.name: Creston Museum
visitor.desc: The Creston Museum is a community history museum operated by The Creston & District Historical & Museum Society, dedicated to the unique pioneer, Indigenous, agricultural, and industrial heritage of the Creston Valley at the heart of the Kootenays. It features rotating exhibits on subjects ranging from WWI soldiers to a model railway, alongside archives, photo galleries, and children's programs. For a touring cyclist rolling through the valley between the Purcell and Selkirk ranges, it offers rich local context on the landscape and communities they are riding through.

visitor.name: VIRL: Port Hardy Branch
visitor.desc: The Port Hardy branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served this northernmost Vancouver Island community since 1972, situated on the unceded traditional territory of the Kwakwaka'wakw peoples. As a full-service public library, it offers books, digital resources, computers, and meeting room facilities to the public at no charge. For touring cyclists reaching the end of the Island Highway, it provides a welcoming indoor rest stop with community resources in a remote location.

visitor.name: Vancouver Christmas Market
visitor.desc: Vancouver's German Christmas Market is a long-running seasonal tradition (15+ years) held at Jack Poole Plaza near Canada Place, bringing hundreds of thousands of visitors each winter for holiday food, crafts, and entertainment in an outdoor market setting. The market draws on authentic German Christmas market traditions and is one of the largest such events in Canada. A touring cyclist arriving in Vancouver during the holiday season would find this a major cultural attraction in the downtown core.

detail.address: Jack Poole Plaza, Canada Place, Vancouver, BC

visitor.name: Steveston Village
visitor.desc: Steveston Village is a heritage fishing village at the mouth of the Fraser River in Richmond, voted #1 Metro Vancouver neighbourhood out of 192 in 2020 and declared a heritage zone in 1960. It remains a working fishing village where cyclists can buy fresh seafood off the dock, explore national historic sites like the Gulf of Georgia Cannery and Britannia Shipyards, and stroll the waterfront along Fishers Walk. The village's Moncton Street streetscape—lined with cafés, bookshops, and film locations—makes it a compelling stop on any cycling tour of the Lower Mainland.

visitor.name: Bald Mountain Park
visitor.desc: Bald Mountain Park is a nature reserve managed by the Cowichan Valley Regional District, situated near Lake Cowichan on Vancouver Island. As a CVRD-administered park, it likely offers natural trail experiences through the region's characteristic coastal forest and mountain terrain. Touring cyclists in the Lake Cowichan area may find it a worthwhile side trip for scenery and a break from the road.

visitor.name: PoMo Arts Centre (Old City Hall)
visitor.desc: Housed in the historic Old City Hall and Appleyard House buildings in the heart of Port Moody, PoMoArts is a community arts centre offering over 350 classes annually across visual, ceramic, performing, and media arts. It also serves as Port Moody's official Visitor Centre, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists exploring the Tri-Cities. The centre features a contemporary gallery, the Blackberry Gift Shop with locally crafted items, and is steps from the Moody Centre SkyTrain station on the Evergreen extension.

detail.address: 2425 St. Johns Street, Port Moody, BC V3H 2B2

visitor.name: Vancouver Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Vancouver Aquatic Centre is a City of Vancouver-operated indoor public pool situated on Beach Avenue at the edge of English Bay, one of the most scenically located aquatic facilities in the city. It offers lap swimming and diving programs and sits directly along the popular Seaside Cycling Route and Seawall corridor. For touring cyclists riding the downtown waterfront, it is a natural urban stopover point with full recreational facilities.

visitor.name: Kelowna Curling Club
visitor.desc: The Kelowna Curling Club is one of the largest curling clubs in the world, with 12 sheets of ice and over 1,200 members in the sunny Okanagan Valley. It offers drop-in 'Try Curling' sessions with an instructor and rental equipment, making it accessible to complete newcomers. A fully licensed upstairs lounge and restaurant serves as the social hub of the club, giving visiting cyclists a place to refuel and experience a uniquely Canadian sport.

notes.Café or food on site: Fully licensed lounge/restaurant upstairs; kitchen menu listed; Burger & Curl events (beef, chicken, or veggie burger with side dish) available Saturdays and Sundays

visitor.name: International Friendship Garden & Cultural Gateway
visitor.desc: The International Friendship Garden & Cultural Gateway is a public garden in Abbotsford operated by the City of Abbotsford Parks, Recreation & Culture, celebrating cultural diversity through landscape design. Tagged in OSM with a fence barrier, it is a defined, enclosed attraction along George Ferguson Way. Touring cyclists riding through Abbotsford may find it a worthwhile rest or sightseeing stop in an urban park setting.

visitor.name: Great West Fitness & Tennis
visitor.desc: Great West Fitness & Tennis is a full-service fitness and tennis club in Abbotsford offering indoor tennis courts, group fitness classes, personal training, childcare, and a pro shop. The club hosts regular tennis tournaments and social events and describes itself as a community-oriented facility. Non-members can access tennis courts and racquet stringing services without a full membership.

visitor.name: Vallea Lumina
visitor.desc: Vallea Lumina is an immersive multimedia night walk through the forest on Cougar Mountain, blending lighting installations, soundscapes, and interactive storytelling along a designated trail. Operated by The Adventure Group, the experience runs year-round after sunset and follows either a 1 km winter course or a 1.5 km summer course through the forest. A free bookable shuttle connects Whistler Village Gateway Bus Loop to the Cougar Mountain basecamp, making it accessible without a vehicle.

detail.address: Sixteen Mile Creek Forest Service Road, Whistler, BC V0N 1B8

visitor.name: Bau-Xi Gallery
visitor.desc: Bau-Xi Gallery is one of Canada's oldest and most respected contemporary art galleries, founded in 1965 and situated on Vancouver's South Granville gallery strip. It shows a rotating programme of painting, sculpture, photography, and mixed media by Canadian and international artists, with free admission. The Granville Street corridor is a natural waypoint for cyclists exploring the city's west side.

visitor.name: Kiyo Park
visitor.desc: Kiyo Park is a small urban nature park in Surrey's Whalley neighbourhood, threaded by King Creek and connected by a pedestrian pathway and bridge that doubles as a wildlife viewing platform. The park is notably good for spotting spawning salmon in autumn, along with resident bird life along the creek corridor. The western portion offers open meadows and shade trees, making it a quiet spot for a short break on a local ride.

visitor.name: Guildford Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Guildford Recreation Centre is a municipal sports and recreation facility operated by the City of Surrey in the Guildford neighbourhood. As a full-service recreation centre, it offers programs and activities typical of a large municipal complex. It sits along 152 Street, a major corridor in Surrey's suburban east side.

visitor.name: FVRL: Hope Library
visitor.desc: The Hope Library is Fraser Valley Regional Library's branch serving the town of Hope, BC, housed in a civic building on 6th Avenue. It offers digital library services, computers, printing, and a range of community programs as part of FVRL's extensive regional network. For touring cyclists moving through the Fraser Canyon gateway, it represents a quiet rest point in the heart of the downtown core.

visitor.name: Oliver Woods Community Centre
visitor.desc: Oliver Woods Community Centre is a City of Nanaimo public recreation facility on Oliver Road. It is part of the city's network of community and activity centres offering recreation programs and drop-in activities. Touring cyclists passing through south Nanaimo may find it a convenient municipal stop.

visitor.name: Millennium Sport Centre
visitor.desc: The Millennium Sport Centre is a civic sports facility in Vancouver's Hillcrest neighbourhood, built as part of the 2010 Winter Olympics legacy infrastructure. It sits adjacent to Nat Bailey Stadium and Hillcrest Park, making it a notable landmark on the southeast side of the city. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find it a recognizable civic anchor in a well-connected recreational corridor.

visitor.name: Victoria Chinatown Museum
visitor.desc: A museum dedicated to the history and culture of Chinese Canadians, housed in the Hoy Sun Ning Yung Benevolent Association building on Fan Tan Alley — North America's narrowest commercial street. Located in Canada's oldest surviving Chinatown (est. 1858), it features rotating exhibits, artifacts, and community programming. Free admission makes it an easy stop for touring cyclists passing through downtown Victoria.

detail.address: 10 Fan Tan Alley, Victoria, BC V8W 1N6

visitor.name: Castle Theatre
visitor.desc: The Old Castle Theatre is a community live entertainment venue in Crescent Valley in BC's Kootenay region, hosting punk concerts, dance parties, and film screenings. It books national acts alongside local artists and serves as a cultural hub for the area. A touring cyclist passing through the Kootenays could catch a live show here in an intimate, locally run setting.

visitor.name: Amphitrite House Interpretive Centre
visitor.desc: The Amphitrite House Interpretive Centre is a single-storey, wheelchair-accessible tourism information office situated on Coast Guard Road at the western edge of Ucluelet, near the tip of the peninsula. It provides interpretive information for visitors to this dramatic stretch of Vancouver Island's outer coast. The building's location in the Coast Guard Road area places it close to the Amphitrite Point Lighthouse and the rugged Pacific shoreline.

visitor.name: Monterey Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: A municipal recreation centre in Oak Bay operated by Recreation Oak Bay, part of the District of Oak Bay's parks and recreation system. The facility offers registered programs, drop-in activities, and community services in a residential neighbourhood near the Victoria waterfront.

visitor.name: Mark Hobson Gallery
visitor.desc: Mark Hobson Gallery is the dedicated showroom for Canadian wildlife and landscape artist Mark Hobson, who has painted professionally from Tofino since 1984. His work — executed in watercolour, acrylic, and oil — captures the West Coast's pounding surf, rain forests, and coastal wildlife, with many pieces begun outdoors on location. Touring cyclists rolling into Tofino can browse original paintings, limited-edition giclée prints, and commission custom artwork directly from the artist.

visitor.name: Upper Canyon Open Space
visitor.desc: Upper Canyon Open Space is a nature reserve managed by the City of Kelowna, situated in the upper canyon area of the city. As a publicly accessible open space, it offers natural terrain that may appeal to cyclists looking to explore Kelowna's canyon landscapes on foot or by trail. The area is part of Kelowna's parks and beaches network.

visitor.name: Andy Livingstone Field
visitor.desc: Andy Livingstone Field is a City of Vancouver municipal sports facility hosting soccer and baseball in the downtown core near False Creek. The site is wheelchair accessible and fenced, making it a structured outdoor venue rather than a passive greenspace. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a convenient landmark or rest stop given its central location.

visitor.name: Sagebrush Theatre
visitor.desc: Sagebrush Theatre is a 685-seat proscenium theatre near downtown Kamloops, owned by School District 73 and managed by Western Canada Theatre, serving as the home stage for the Kamloops Symphony and Western Canada Theatre. The fully-equipped venue hosts a wide range of local, community, and touring productions year-round, making it the cultural heart of Kamloops' performing arts scene. A touring cyclist attending a show will find accessible lobby facilities including a concession stand, bottle-fill station, and fully accessible washrooms.

notes.Café or food on site: About Us page references 'concession offerings' available to patrons in the lobby prior to events

visitor.name: Talking Trees Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: A 42-hectare nature reserve on Galiano Island protecting one of the last intact tracts of mature and old-growth Coastal Douglas-fir forest in the Southern Gulf Islands. The reserve stretches from Trincomali Channel to the island's central ridgeline, encompassing rare Garry Oak woodlands, creek and wetland habitats, and 600 metres of undeveloped coastline. Established in 2024 by the Galiano Conservancy Association through Canada's Old Growth Nature Fund.

visitor.name: Bowen Creek Corridor
visitor.desc: Bowen Creek Corridor is a nature reserve within the City of Kelowna, offering a natural greenway along Bowen Creek. As a linear corridor, it likely provides a route through natural habitat that touring cyclists in the Kelowna area could use for recreation or as a connector. The site is managed by the City of Kelowna as part of its parks and beaches network.

visitor.name: Railway Museum of British Columbia
visitor.desc: The Railway Museum of British Columbia, operated by the non-profit West Coast Railway Association, preserves 95 heritage locomotives and railway cars in the spectacular mountain setting of Squamish on the Sea to Sky corridor. Visitors can climb into the cab of the Royal Hudson 2860 steam locomotive, ride the BC-21 Budd Rail Diesel Car, and explore restored luxury passenger cars inside the CN Roundhouse. It is a hands-on, immersive destination telling the story of the railways that shaped British Columbia and Western Canada.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'Snacks, drinks and picnic area on site.'

visitor.name: Thornton Creek Enhancement Society
visitor.desc: Thornton Creek Enhancement Society is a non-profit salmon hatchery near Ucluelet dedicated to sustaining Chinook, Coho, and Chum salmon populations in Barkley and Clayoquot Sounds, operating since 1981 within the traditional territories of the Toquaht, Ucluth Aht, and Tla-o-qui-aht Nations. During the fall salmon run the hatchery becomes a popular destination, offering educational tours by donation where visitors can observe the salmon lifecycle up close. It also runs school programs and snorkel surveys, making it one of the more ecologically engaged visitor experiences on the west coast of Vancouver Island.

visitor.name: Gleneagles Community Centre
visitor.desc: Gleneagles Community Centre is a municipally operated recreation facility in the Gleneagles neighbourhood of West Vancouver, situated along Marine Drive near Howe Sound. Run by West Vancouver Municipality, it serves as a hub for local recreation programs and community gatherings. Its location on the scenic Marine Drive cycling corridor makes it a natural waypoint for touring cyclists passing through the area.

visitor.name: Downtown Eastside Seniors Centre
visitor.desc: The Downtown Eastside Seniors Centre is a drop-in community hub operated by the Vancouver Second Mile Society, a non-profit charity established in 1958 to serve low-income seniors in one of Vancouver's most challenging urban neighbourhoods. The centre provides daily recreational activities, affordable meals prepared by volunteers, computers with internet access, and social programs reaching nearly 2,000 participants annually. It is one of two seniors centres run by VSMS and serves as a community anchor on East Hastings Street.

detail.address: 509 East Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 1P9

notes.Café or food on site: Website states: 'Affordable meals — Inexpensive and nutritious breakfast and lunches are prepared by dedicated volunteers and staff.'

visitor.name: Rossland Arena
visitor.desc: Rossland Arena is a municipal ice facility operated by the City of Rossland, offering ice skating, ice hockey, and curling. It is a seasonal venue serving the local community and is situated in Rossland, a small city in the West Kootenay region of BC known primarily for its mountain terrain.

visitor.name: Extreme Air Park
visitor.desc: Extreme Air Park Richmond bills itself as Canada's largest indoor trampoline park, spanning 42,000 sq ft of interlocking trampolines across activities including dodgeball courts, rock climbing, a foam pit, and slam-dunk basketball. The facility can accommodate up to 440 jumpers simultaneously and is part of a three-location Lower Mainland chain. It is a high-energy indoor attraction with no evident connection to cycling tourism.

visitor.name: City of Vancouver Archives
visitor.desc: The City of Vancouver Archives is the official repository for historical records relating to the City of Vancouver, preserving documents, photographs, maps, and other materials that document the city's history. Operated by the City of Vancouver, it serves researchers, historians, and the general public. Touring cyclists passing through Vanier Park may find it a worthwhile cultural stop given its proximity to the waterfront cycling routes.

visitor.name: Nelson Fitness Centre
visitor.desc: The Nelson & District Community Complex is a publicly operated recreation facility run by the Regional District of Central Kootenay, serving the Nelson area. As a community complex it likely encompasses fitness, aquatic, and multi-use spaces typical of a regional recreation centre. Touring cyclists passing through Nelson may find it a useful stop for basic amenities, though specific offerings could not be confirmed from available web content.

visitor.name: YMCA of Northern BC
visitor.desc: The YMCA of Northern BC is a community sports and recreation centre in Prince George offering fitness, aquatics, child care, youth support, and outdoor education programs. As the regional hub for YMCA services in northern BC, it anchors a wide range of health and wellness programming for residents and visitors. Touring cyclists passing through Prince George may find it a useful urban stop given its full-service nature, though specific cycling amenities are not confirmed.

visitor.name: Qualicum Beach Visitor Information and Chamber of Commerce
visitor.desc: The Qualicum Beach Chamber of Commerce has served as the voice of local business since at least the 1920s, acting as the town's primary visitor information hub on the east coast of Vancouver Island. Cycling tourists passing through can use it as a starting point to discover local restaurants, accommodations, shops, and community events. The organization also promotes Qualicum Beach as a tourism destination and maintains an active local business directory.

detail.address: 2711 Island Hwy W., Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 2C4

visitor.name: WildPlay Element Park
visitor.desc: WildPlay Element Park is an outdoor adventure park near the Nanaimo River offering aerial obstacle courses through the forest canopy, ziplines, a bungy jump, a giant primal swing, and axe throwing. The park features multiple course difficulty levels—including a kids' course and an extreme course reaching 60 feet high—and is part of a multi-location BC chain. It makes for a memorable active detour for touring cyclists seeking an adrenaline break mid-route.

notes.Café or food on site: Drinks and snacks for sale at Guest Services, confirmed on both Plan Your Visit and FAQ pages
notes.Luggage / bag storage: FAQ states 'There are lockers at the park for storing valuab[les]' (text truncated but lockers confirmed)

visitor.name: Robert F. Osborne Centre
visitor.desc: The Robert F. Osborne Centre is a UBC recreation facility on the Vancouver campus, part of UBC Recreation's broader network of sports and fitness infrastructure serving students, staff, and community members. Located on Thunderbird Boulevard in the heart of the UBC campus, it sits within a well-connected network of cycling paths that link UBC to the broader Metro Vancouver trail system. Touring cyclists passing through the UBC endowment lands may find campus recreation facilities a useful stop.

visitor.name: Cowichan Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Cowichan Community Centre is a regional-district-operated community facility in Duncan, BC, formerly known as the Island Savings Centre. It serves the broader Cowichan Valley area as a multi-use civic venue. A touring cyclist passing through Duncan might consider it a potential rest stop, though specific cycling-oriented amenities are not confirmed.

visitor.name: Thompson Community Centre
visitor.desc: Thompson Community Centre is a City of Richmond civic recreation facility serving the south Richmond neighbourhood near Granville Avenue. As part of Richmond's network of publicly operated community centres, it offers recreational programming to local residents and visitors. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's flat, cycling-friendly terrain may find it a convenient rest point, though specific cyclist-oriented amenities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: St. Joseph's Church
visitor.desc: St. Joseph's Catholic Church is the oldest church in Kamloops, built jointly by Catholic missionaries and the Tk'emlups te Secwepemc in the late 19th century on Tk'emlups band lands near the industrial park. Designated a Canadian heritage site, it has been fully renovated with artifacts restored, including a striking gold-gilded altar. For a touring cyclist with an interest in Indigenous and colonial history, it represents a rare surviving piece of early Kamloops cultural heritage.

visitor.name: Beban Park Pool
visitor.desc: Beban Park Pool is an indoor public swimming pool operated by the City of Nanaimo within the Beban Park recreational complex. It offers drop-in swim sessions alongside programmed aquatic activities for residents and visitors. For touring cyclists, it represents a chance to relax and recover in a heated indoor pool mid-route through Nanaimo.

visitor.name: ORL: Westside Learning Lab
visitor.desc: The Westside Learning Lab is a community branch of the Okanagan Regional Library, a 30-branch regional system established in 1936 that serves over 399,000 people across south-central British Columbia. Located on the Okanagan Highway on Kelowna's west side, it gives the public free access to ORL's digital collections, e-learning resources, and system-wide programs including Makerspaces and a Library of Things technology-lending service. As a publicly accessible library branch it provides a useful rest stop for touring cyclists passing through the Westside corridor.

visitor.name: False Creek
visitor.desc: False Creek is an urban inlet cutting through the heart of Vancouver, best known to cyclists as the body of water encircled by Vancouver's world-famous seawall multi-use path. The waterway separates downtown Vancouver from the False Creek South and Olympic Village neighbourhoods, and the surrounding shoreline offers continuous, car-free cycling along parks, marinas, and public plazas. It is a central landmark on any cycling tour of Vancouver's waterfront.

visitor.name: North Langford Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Bear Mountain is a large golf and tennis resort community located just outside Victoria, BC, featuring 36 holes of Nicklaus Design golf, indoor/outdoor red clay tennis courts, a spa, and multiple dining venues. The resort also boasts a hiking and mountain biking trail network in its natural hillside setting. The OSM record refers to the Activity Centre building within the resort complex.

notes.Café or food on site: Multiple dining venues on site: Masters Lounge, The Cellar & Friday Night Flights, and Bella

visitor.name: Admiralty Point Lands (Parks Canada)
visitor.desc: Admiralty Point Lands is a nature reserve on Indian Arm in the Belcarra area of North Vancouver, part of the broader Belcarra Regional Park managed by Metro Vancouver. The waterfront lands offer coastal forest and shoreline habitat. Despite the OSM name crediting Parks Canada, the area appears to fall under Metro Vancouver Regional Parks stewardship.

visitor.name: Alliance Française
visitor.desc: Alliance Française Vancouver is a Francophone cultural centre serving the city since 1904, now housed in a new three-storey building in the Oakridge neighbourhood that opened in 2024. It hosts public cultural events including film screenings, theatre, concerts, art exhibitions, and book clubs, alongside a French-language library and a VR library. Conveniently accessible via the Canada Line (Oakridge–41st or Langara–49th stations), it offers a welcoming cultural stop for curious visitors.

visitor.name: Pearkes Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Pearkes Recreation Centre is a municipally operated multi-sport facility run by Saanich Parks & Recreation in the Tillicum neighbourhood of Victoria. As a full-service community recreation centre, it serves as a practical stop for touring cyclists passing through the western side of the city. The centre is publicly accessible and part of the broader Saanich Parks & Recreation network.

visitor.name: Blacksmith Shop
visitor.desc: The Blacksmith Shop is a historic building within the Britannia Mine Museum, a National Historic Site perched on the shores of Howe Sound along the Sea to Sky corridor between Vancouver and Whistler. The museum complex includes an underground mine train, gold panning, and the award-winning multi-sensory BOOM! experience inside historic Mill No. 3. It is a well-established destination stop for cyclists riding the Sea to Sky route.

notes.Café or food on site: Chatterbox Cafe listed as a named section in the site navigation under the Visit menu

visitor.name: National Hockey Training Centre
visitor.desc: The National Hockey Training Centre is Langley's premier ice hockey and skating facility, operating two rinks across the city and offering year-round programs from learn-to-skate for beginners to elite development camps. With over 15 years of experience and more than 5,000 players trained, it serves skaters of all ages across the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley. The facility also offers ice, synthetic, and gym rentals, making it a notable destination for anyone interested in catching a hockey session or birthday party on the ice.

visitor.name: Ground Up Climbing Centre
visitor.desc: Ground Up Climbing Centre is Squamish's anchor indoor climbing gym, offering both roped climbing and bouldering in a town world-famous for its outdoor granite walls and deep adventure culture. The gym caters to everyone from first-timers to competitive youth teams, and visiting climbers stopping in for a session are explicitly welcomed. For touring cyclists rolling through Squamish, it offers a direct connection to the region's iconic climbing scene right in the heart of town.

notes.Café or food on site: Contact page lists the Operations Manager as handling 'customer service, café and retail queries', indicating an on-site café and retail area

visitor.name: Chilliwack Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Chilliwack Visitor Centre is operated by Tourism Chilliwack and serves as the official gateway for trip planning in the Fraser Valley region. It offers downloadable guides, local event listings, and connections to outdoor adventure, farm experiences, and arts and culture. For a touring cyclist passing through Chilliwack, it is a practical first stop for maps, local knowledge, and regional cycling routes.

visitor.name: Penticton Public Library
visitor.desc: The Penticton Public Library is a full-service community library on Main Street in the heart of Penticton, offering free public Wi-Fi, computers, printing, scanning, and a makerspace. It runs a 'Library of Things' lending program that includes outdoor exploration gear alongside tech items like Nintendo Switch consoles. For touring cyclists, it serves as a practical downtown hub for connectivity, rest, and trip planning.

visitor.name: Kerrisdale Lawn Bowling Club
visitor.desc: One of British Columbia's oldest lawn bowling clubs, established in 1915 and playing continuously at its Elm Park location since 1917. The club welcomes drop-in visitors and provides coaching and equipment for newcomers, set in a scenic neighbourhood park with a clubhouse and shaded patio. A quirky, distinctly local attraction in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood.

visitor.name: VIRL: Daajing Giids Branch
visitor.desc: The Daajing Giids branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served this remote Haida Gwaii community since 1983 and is housed in the refurbished Community Hall. Situated on the traditional territory of the Haida Nation, it is one of the few public indoor spaces available to touring cyclists exploring the archipelago. The branch offers free public Wi-Fi and public computer access, making it a practical waypoint in an area with limited connectivity.

visitor.name: Cowichan Estuary Nature Centre
visitor.desc: A volunteer-operated, admit-by-donation nature interpretive centre perched at the edge of the Cowichan Estuary — a 400-hectare ecosystem and internationally designated Important Bird Area — in Hecate Park, Cowichan Bay. Visitors can explore interactive exhibits about the estuary, marine and bird life, and the Cowichan and Koksilah watersheds, including a live heron-rookery webcam. For touring cyclists passing through Cowichan Bay, it doubles as a tourist information hub and a quiet stop to learn about one of Vancouver Island's most ecologically significant coastal habitats.

detail.address: 1845 Cowichan Bay Rd, Cowichan Bay, BC V0R 1N0

visitor.name: Newton Wave Pool
visitor.desc: Newton Recreation Centre is a City of Surrey municipal facility featuring a wave pool, wading pool, hot tub, and steam room. It offers drop-in fitness, sport, and swimming activities and is conveniently located next to a bus route. Touring cyclists passing through Surrey's Newton neighbourhood could stop in for a refreshing swim.

visitor.name: Ladysmith Museum
visitor.desc: A community heritage museum in historic downtown Ladysmith showcasing the town's mining, lumber, and railway history through permanent displays and rotating exhibits. Run by volunteers of the Ladysmith & District Historical Society, it also houses a gift shop featuring local artists and a downstairs Learning Centre. Leashed pets are welcome, and the museum is temporarily located in a town-owned building.

visitor.name: Student Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Student Recreation Centre is a large multi-sport facility on UBC Vancouver's campus, operated by UBC Recreation. It serves students, faculty, and community members with a wide range of programming including aquatics, fitness, ice sports, bouldering, intramurals, and sport clubs. Touring cyclists visiting UBC's expansive and scenic campus will find a well-equipped recreation hub near the heart of the university.

notes.Luggage / bag storage: UBC Recreation website navigation explicitly lists 'Lockers & Locker Rentals' as a service offering

visitor.name: Elder Cedar Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: A nature reserve protected by Islands Trust Conservancy, also known by its Hul'qumi'num name S'ul-hween X'pey. Located in the Nanaimo area within the Islands Trust region, it is part of a network of conservation lands preserved over 31 years of partnership between the Conservancy, local organizations, and landowners.

visitor.name: Princeton & District Museum
visitor.desc: Founded in 1958 and operated by the Princeton and District Museum and Archives Society, this community museum houses an impressive range of collections including over 40,000 fossil and mineral specimens, a First Peoples basket display, approximately 10,000 historic photographs, and an original 1880s cabin. It has grown from a small log cabin to a multi-wing facility and is widely praised as one of the best small-town museums in BC. Touring cyclists interested in the natural and human history of the Similkameen Valley will find it a rewarding stop.

visitor.name: Trethewey House Heritage Site
visitor.desc: Trethewey House is a 1920s heritage home built for B.C. timber baron J.O. Trethewey, restored to its circa-1925 appearance and operated as a history museum by the non-profit MSA Museum Society in Abbotsford. The Arts and Crafts-style house was constructed of first-growth fir milled at the family's own Abbotsford Lumber Company and features bricks made from locally mined clay. It serves as a living record of the Fraser Valley's early industrial and domestic history.

visitor.name: Nakusp Hot Springs
visitor.desc: Nakusp Hot Springs is a community-owned natural mineral hot springs facility nestled in the Kuskanax Valley in the foothills of the Selkirk Mountains, accessible via a 14 km paved road northeast of the village of Nakusp. The site features two soaking pools continuously fed by natural mineral springs, set within over 200 acres of year-round outdoor recreation including hiking and biking trails. As of 2025, 70 hectares surrounding the springs have been formally designated as a protected natural area under the Municipal Protected Areas Project.

detail.address: 8500 Hot Springs Road, Nakusp, BC V0G 1R0

visitor.name: Chinese Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: The Chinese Cultural Centre of Greater Vancouver is a long-established community institution at the heart of Vancouver's historic Chinatown, operating the largest Chinese language school in British Columbia with over 300 classes in Cantonese and Mandarin. Beyond education, it hosts Cantonese opera performances, calligraphy competitions, and organized walking tours of Chinatown, making it a genuine cultural landmark for visitors. A separate museum and archives facility preserving Chinese-Canadian heritage operates at 555 Columbia Street nearby.

visitor.name: Creekside Theatre
visitor.desc: Creekside Theatre is a community performing arts venue operated by the District of Lake Country, hosting live music concerts, tribute acts, and fundraising dinner-shows. It sits in the Lake Country municipality between Kelowna and Vernon in the heart of the Okanagan, making it a potential evening-out destination for cyclists touring the region. The venue offers theatre rentals in addition to its own programming calendar.

detail.address: 10241 Bottom Wood Lake Road, Lake Country, V4V 1Y7

visitor.name: Roy Henry Vickers Gallery
visitor.desc: Roy Henry Vickers Gallery is a world-renowned First Nations art gallery in Tofino built in 1986 by artist Roy Henry Vickers himself alongside close friends and family. The building is modelled after a traditional Northwest Coast longhouse with cedar-planked walls, and showcases limited edition prints, original paintings, and carvings that draw visitors from around the world. It is considered a cultural landmark in Tofino and a distinctive stop on BC's west coast.

visitor.name: Science World
visitor.desc: Science World is Vancouver's iconic science museum housed in a striking geodesic dome on the False Creek waterfront, operated as a charitable non-profit focused on STEAM education. Visitors explore interactive, hands-on exhibits and galleries designed to spark curiosity across all ages. The museum actively engages with the cycling community, hosting Go By Bike Week events and situated along one of Vancouver's most popular waterfront cycling corridors.

visitor.name: Town of Sidney Municipal Hall
visitor.desc: The Town of Sidney Municipal Hall is the civic administrative centre for Sidney, a seaside town on the Saanich Peninsula near the BC Ferries Swartz Bay terminal. The building houses town council chambers and municipal offices. Sidney's website highlights dedicated cycling routes and waterfront access, making the town a natural stop on Vancouver Island touring itineraries.

visitor.name: Greenaway Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: Historic Greenaway Outdoor Pool is a free seasonal outdoor swimming pool operated by the City of Surrey, located in Greenaway Park on 60th Avenue just east of Fraser Downs Racetrack. It offers free public swims and swimming lessons during summer months, making it a welcome refreshment stop for touring cyclists passing through Surrey's south side.

visitor.name: BC Forest Discovery Centre
visitor.desc: The BC Forest Discovery Centre is a 100-acre open-air museum in Duncan, BC, featuring an operational narrow-gauge railway, forest and marsh trails, heritage logging camp buildings, and exhibits chronicling the history of BC's coastal forest industry. Visitors can walk through an 1930s logging camp, board a steam or gas-powered train, and explore over a century of forestry artifacts and heritage structures. The museum is operated by the BC Forest Museum Society, a registered charitable non-profit, and hosts seasonal special events throughout the year.

visitor.name: GVPL: Juan de Fuca Branch
visitor.desc: The Juan de Fuca Branch is part of the Greater Victoria Public Library system, serving the western communities of the Capital Regional District along the Island Highway corridor. As a public library it offers a welcoming, climate-controlled indoor space with public computers and digital collections. It is operated by the Greater Victoria Public Library, which maintains a network of branches across the greater Victoria area.

visitor.name: Bulman Trail
visitor.desc: Buhlman Road Park Reserve is a nature reserve near Sidney, BC, managed by the Capital Regional District. It appears to correspond to the CRD's Bulman Trail, a natural-surface trail in the Greater Victoria region. Touring cyclists exploring the Saanich Peninsula may use it as a short off-road detour through protected green space.

detail.address: Bulman Road (access across from 211 Bulman Rd), Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 1X5

visitor.name: Sea to Sea Regional Park
visitor.desc: Sea to Sea Regional Park is a wilderness nature reserve managed by the Capital Regional District in the hills above Sooke on southern Vancouver Island. It forms part of a green corridor linking regional parks and wilderness areas accessible from the Greater Victoria region. The park is listed in the CRD's regional parks and trails network, making it a potential destination or waypoint for touring cyclists exploring the Sooke area.

visitor.name: Hedley Museum
visitor.desc: The Hedley Heritage Museum is a volunteer-run heritage museum celebrating the gold-rush mining history of Hedley and the Similkameen Valley, featuring a replica miner's cottage, a hospital and school exhibit, vintage mining machinery displayed across the street, and a Miners' Lounge with historical photographs and a family history centre. It doubles as the village's tourist information booth, making it a natural stop for cyclists passing through on Highway 3 (the Crowsnest). The on-site tea room with a shaded veranda and gift shop selling ore samples and local crafts add a pleasant rest-stop dimension.

notes.Café or food on site: Tea Room serves refreshments (tea, coffee, baked goods); guests can sit in the air-conditioned room or on the veranda overlooking the garden. Gift shop also sells items on site

visitor.name: Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: This information node sits at the entrance to The Butchart Gardens, a 122-year-old, 55-acre world-famous display garden in Brentwood Bay designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 2004. Still privately owned by the founding Butchart family, the gardens feature distinct themed sections—Sunken, Rose, Japanese, Italian, and Mediterranean—along with summer evening illuminations and fireworks. A touring cyclist arriving from Victoria (approximately 22 km via Highway 17 and Tanner Road) would find multiple dining venues and a gift store on site.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists four on-site dining venues: The Dining Room Restaurant, The Blue Poppy Restaurant, Coffee Shop, and Gelateria

visitor.name: Forests for the World
visitor.desc: Forests for the World is a City of Prince George-managed park and trail destination, listed prominently in the city's parks-and-trails portfolio. Situated near Prince George, it is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a tourism attraction, suggesting it draws visitors as a destination in its own right. Touring cyclists passing through Prince George may find it a worthwhile stop, though specific on-site facilities could not be confirmed from available evidence.

visitor.name: Port Moody Public Library
visitor.desc: Port Moody Public Library is the public library serving Port Moody and the broader Tri-Cities region, located in the Newport Village neighbourhood. Beyond books, the library lends unusual items like ukulele kits, coding kits, and 'Bat Packs,' and offers accessible-format materials for patrons with visual or physical disabilities. Free public Wi-Fi makes it a practical rest stop for touring cyclists looking to plan routes, check in, or simply decompress.

detail.address: 100 Newport Drive, Port Moody, BC V3H 5C3

visitor.name: VIRL: Port Alice Branch
visitor.desc: The Port Alice Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library has served this remote North Vancouver Island community since 1972, on the unceded traditional territory of the Quatsino nation. As one of the few public indoor spaces in Port Alice, it offers free WiFi, public computers, printing, and photocopying in a wheelchair-accessible building. For touring cyclists riding the isolated north island routes, it provides a rare opportunity to rest indoors and get connected.

visitor.name: The Theatre At Hendry Hall
visitor.desc: The Theatre at Hendry Hall is the permanent home of the North Van Community Players, a 100% volunteer non-profit society founded in 1972. The hall itself dates to 1942, originally built as an Air Raid Precautionary Post and later remodeled for community use, giving it an unusually layered local history. A touring cyclist with an interest in live performance could catch drama, comedy, or musical productions in this intimate neighbourhood venue.

visitor.name: Saanich Commonwealth Place
visitor.desc: Saanich Commonwealth Place is a large municipal aquatic and fitness centre operated by the District of Saanich, anchored by a 50-metre competition pool alongside a wave pool, tots pool, dive tank, and water slide — one of the most comprehensive aquatic complexes on Vancouver Island. The facility also offers a steam room, sauna, hot tub, weight room, gymnasium, and functional fitness studio, giving touring cyclists a rare opportunity to recover thoroughly after a long day on the road. It sits near Elk Lake, a popular cycling destination in its own right, making it a natural stop on routes through the Saanich Peninsula.

visitor.name: Wild Coast Nature Refuge
visitor.desc: The Wild Coast Nature Refuge is a 32-acre waterfront conservation area on Bowen Island at Cape Roger Curtis, acquired by the Bowen Island Conservancy in December 2020. It protects a rare coast bluff ecosystem where whales can be spotted just offshore from lichen-covered cliffs, and a Conservation Covenant ensures permanent protection of its biological diversity. Public access is limited to a loop walking trail connecting viewpoints on the coastal bluffs.

detail.address: P.O. Box 301, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G0

visitor.name: Bard On The Beach (Summer Only)
visitor.desc: Bard on the Beach is Western Canada's largest not-for-profit professional Shakespeare Festival, staging plays and special events in two modern performance tents set against a backdrop of mountains, sea, and sky in Vancouver's Sen̓áḵw/Vanier Park. Now in its 37th season, the festival presents multiple Shakespeare productions alongside related dramas and special events such as improv nights. The Vanier Park site sits directly along Vancouver's waterfront seawall cycling corridor, making it a natural cultural stop for touring cyclists exploring the city's coastline.

notes.Café or food on site: 'Bard Picnics' is prominently listed under the 'Your Visit' navigation section on the website, indicating food/picnic service is available on the festival site

visitor.name: Kilby General Store
visitor.desc: The Kilby Historic Site is BC's only reminder of the once-thriving community of Harrison Mills, centred on an original 1906 general store now filled with artifacts, hands-on activities, and costumed interpreters. The site encompasses heritage farm buildings, friendly farm animals, a café, and a 41-site campground — making it a rare attraction where touring cyclists can arrive, explore, eat, and camp all in one place. Celebrating its 120th anniversary, it sits in a scenic corner of the Fraser Valley within easy riding distance of Mission, Chilliwack, and Harrison Hot Springs.

detail.address: 215 Kilby Road, Harrison Mills, BC V0M 1L0

notes.Café or food on site: Kilby Cafe is an on-site café confirmed throughout the website; the group tours page shows a sandwich menu served in the café or tea garden, and picnic tables are available on the grounds

visitor.name: Surrey Nature Centre at Green Timbers
visitor.desc: The Surrey Nature Centre is a publicly operated interpretive facility nestled alongside Green Timbers Urban Forest, one of Surrey's largest tracts of second-growth forest. Visitors can borrow activity backpacks or fishing rods from the front desk, explore the Birds of Green Timbers exhibit, and browse a library of field guides and nature books. The centre serves as a natural trailhead destination for cyclists exploring the Green Timbers Urban Forest trail network.

visitor.name: VPL: Britannia Branch
visitor.desc: Britannia Branch is a public branch of the Vancouver Public Library serving the Grandview-Woodland neighbourhood. As a publicly operated library, it offers free access to books, digital resources, and community programming. For touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver, it represents a free, welcoming rest stop in a well-serviced urban neighbourhood.

visitor.name: Malkin Bowl
visitor.desc: Malkin Bowl is an outdoor amphitheatre nestled in Stanley Park, hosting live music concerts and the long-running Theatre Under the Stars productions. The venue is accessed directly from Stanley Park's main cycling and walking paths, making it an easy stop or evening destination for touring cyclists exploring the seawall. General admission standing with a hillside viewing area gives it a relaxed, festival-like atmosphere.

visitor.name: Community Peace Garden
visitor.desc: A small permaculture demonstration garden on the Vancouver Island University Nanaimo campus, located on the north side of the campus library. Originally established in 2008 as the Community Peace Garden, it is now maintained by the VIU Permaculture Club and focuses on food growing, seed saving, plant medicine, and traditional ecological knowledge. The garden is open and publicly accessible, designed to welcome the maximum number of people.

detail.address: 900 Fifth Street, Nanaimo, BC (VIU campus, north side of library)

visitor.name: Japanese Garden
visitor.desc: The Japanese Garden is a tranquil ornamental garden located within Polson Park in Vernon, BC. Polson Park is a large municipal park in the heart of the city and is a popular stop for visitors passing through the Okanagan. The Japanese Garden forms a scenic centrepiece within the park grounds.

visitor.name: Waterfront Theatre
visitor.desc: The Waterfront Theatre is an intimate, air-conditioned 224-seat performance venue on Granville Island, housed in the converted Tyee Machinery Building. Owned by CMHC Granville Island and managed by the Granville Island Cultural Society, it has been a cornerstone of Vancouver's arts community for over 30 years. Granville Island is a popular cycling destination, making this theatre a potential cultural stop for touring cyclists exploring the area.

visitor.name: Seymour River Fish Hatchery & Education Centre
visitor.desc: The Seymour River Fish Hatchery & Education Centre is operated by the non-profit Seymour Salmonid Society and raises hundreds of thousands of coho, steelhead, chum, and pink salmon annually to supplement fish stocks cut off from spawning grounds by Seymour Falls Dam. The society runs a well-regarded 'Gently Down the Seymour' education program serving 1,200–1,500 school children per year and hosts public events such as Family Fishing Day. Access to the hatchery site is gate-controlled and the road is explicitly stated to be not open to the general public.

detail.address: PO Box 30085, North Vancouver, BC V7H 2Y8

visitor.name: North Delta Centre for the Arts
visitor.desc: North Delta Centre for the Arts is a municipal arts facility operated by the City of Delta, located in the North Delta neighbourhood. It serves the local community as a venue for arts and cultural programming. Touring cyclists exploring the Fraser Delta region may find it a worthwhile cultural stop.

visitor.name: Panorama Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Panorama Recreation Centre is a large community recreation facility operated by the Peninsula Recreation Commission, serving the communities of North Saanich, Central Saanich, and Sidney on the Saanich Peninsula. The centre includes a full aquatic complex with pools, a waterslide, lazy river, and hot tub, alongside arenas, a weight room, fitness studio, and racquet courts. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find accessible changerooms with showers and a notably comprehensive accessibility infrastructure.

detail.address: 1885 Forest Park Dr, North Saanich, BC V8L 4A3

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Website confirms 'Inclusive and accessible universal changeroom including accessible stalls with beds, handrails and showers' and 'Gendered changerooms include accessible stalls with handrails and showers.'

visitor.name: VPL: Dunbar Branch
visitor.desc: The Dunbar Branch is a neighborhood outpost of the Vancouver Public Library system, serving the quiet residential Dunbar-Southlands area of Vancouver's west side. As a free, publicly accessible municipal building, it offers a welcoming rest stop for touring cyclists moving through this part of the city. The branch sits on a low-traffic stretch of Dunbar Street, making it an easy detour off the north-south corridor.

visitor.name: 8EAST
visitor.desc: 8EAST is a social space for new culture operated by the New Orchestra Workshop (NOW) Society in the heart of Vancouver's Historic Chinatown. It functions as a meeting place and performance venue for musicians and community members, hosting regular improvised music events, installations, and artist talks. A touring cyclist interested in Vancouver's contemporary arts scene might stop in for a performance, but the space offers no confirmed cyclist-specific services.

detail.address: 8 East Pender Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 1T1

visitor.name: Powerhouse Theatre
visitor.desc: The Powerhouse Theatre is Vernon's volunteer-run community theatre, housed in a repurposed 1963 electrical power house building with a storied 60-plus-year history. The 236-seat auditorium hosts a full season of plays and musicals — from classic comedies to full-scale musicals — typically playing to near sell-out crowds. The building is also available for private rentals and the society maintains an extensive costume bank spanning six decades of productions.

visitor.name: NewPort Village Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: Newport Village is a walkable, open-air boutique shopping and dining destination in Port Moody, designed with a European village atmosphere and described as Port Moody's premier lifestyle hub. The visitor information office within the mall serves as an entry point for the complex, which includes cafés, a gastropub, specialty food vendors, health services, and seasonal events. Touring cyclists passing through Port Moody will find bike racks, multiple food and drink stops, and a lively community atmosphere.

notes.Café or food on site: Website describes multiple on-site food and drink options including a coffee bar (pet-friendly patio), gastropub, Socialhouse, fresh-baked goods, and gourmet specialty food vendors

visitor.name: Rocky Point Swimming Pool
visitor.desc: Rocky Point Swimming Pool is a seasonal outdoor public pool operated by the City of Port Moody, located within Rocky Point Park. The facility offers public swims, swim lessons, and Aquafit classes during the summer season. Rocky Point Park sits along the Burrard Inlet shoreline, making it a scenic stop for cyclists exploring the Tri-Cities area.

visitor.name: Centre 64
visitor.desc: Centre 64 is Kimberley's community arts hub, operated by the Kimberley Arts Council in partnership with the City of Kimberley. It hosts a 126-seat theatre, a 1,050 sq ft gallery with two-storey ceilings, a pottery studio, and regular programming spanning film screenings, live theatre, live music, and art workshops. A touring cyclist looking to engage with local culture would find a lively, year-round venue at the heart of this Bavarian-themed mountain town.

detail.address: 64 Deer Park Ave, Kimberley, BC V1A 2J2

visitor.name: Nisg̱aʼa Museum
visitor.desc: The Nisg̱aʼa Museum in Lax̱g̱altsʼap (Greenville) is the official cultural institution of the Nisg̱aʼa Nation, housing ancestral regalia, art, and historical artifacts returned to the community. Designed by Hillel Architecture, the building itself is architecturally significant and sits within Nisg̱aʼa Lands in the remote Nass Valley of northwestern BC. For touring cyclists venturing into this rarely visited region, it offers a compelling cultural destination at the end of a long ride.

visitor.name: Studio & Stage Door
visitor.desc: The Studio & Stage Door is a city-owned heritage building dating to 1909, originally built by the local Masons as their Temple, and home to Cranbrook Community Theatre for over 50 years. The venue features an 83-seat theatre and a 1,050-square-foot hardwood dance floor, and has hosted everything from ballet classes to punk rock concerts and professional touring shows. Cranbrook Community Theatre has been producing theatrical works in the East Kootenays since the 1960s, making this a genuine cultural landmark for the region.

visitor.name: Public Mineral Pool
visitor.desc: The Public Mineral Pool in Harrison Hot Springs is an indoor facility fed by the area's famous natural mineral hot springs, one of the most celebrated hot spring destinations in British Columbia. Operated as a public pool on Hot Springs Road, it offers access to geothermally heated mineral water in a setting long prized for its restorative qualities. For a touring cyclist arriving after a long day in the saddle, a soak here would be a memorable highlight of the Harrison River Valley.

detail.address: 101 Hot Springs Road, Harrison Hot Springs, BC

visitor.name: Centre of the Universe
visitor.desc: The Centre of the Universe is the visitor centre of the Dominion Astrophysical Observatory, a National Historic Site perched on a hill about 20 minutes from downtown Victoria. At its heart is the 1.8-metre Plaskett Telescope, in continuous use since 1918 and once the largest operational telescope in the world. Visitors can explore interactive exhibits, attend a planetarium show, and experience guided telescope access — a genuinely singular destination for a cycling day trip.

visitor.name: Sid Williams Theatre
visitor.desc: The Sid Williams Theatre is a 500-seat performing arts centre in downtown Courtenay, BC, operated by the Sid Williams Theatre Society as a registered charitable organization. Originally opened in 1935 as the Bickle Theatre, it has evolved into the Comox Valley's primary live performance venue, hosting everything from Indigenous dance companies and stand-up comedy to tribute acts and professional touring productions. It is a significant cultural landmark on Vancouver Island's cycling routes and a natural stop for touring cyclists spending time in Courtenay.

visitor.name: Western Financial Place
visitor.desc: Western Financial Place (locally known as Rex Plex) is Cranbrook's primary arena and multi-use recreation complex, home to the Junior A Cranbrook Bucks hockey team and a wide range of live events. The facility includes The Studio fitness centre offering spin, yoga, and barre classes, a full-service restaurant, and concession stands. With 953 parking stalls, full elevator and accessibility features, and bus service on four routes, it functions as the entertainment and recreation hub for the East Kootenay region.

notes.Café or food on site: Full-service restaurant above the seating area (normally open during hockey games and major events) plus Cranbrook Bucks-operated concessions offering pizza, hot dogs, and popcorn

visitor.name: Albion Community Centre
visitor.desc: A single-storey municipal community centre in the Albion neighbourhood of Maple Ridge, operated by the City. It serves as a cultural centre, community hall, events venue, and meeting space with designated wheelchair accessibility. For touring cyclists passing through Maple Ridge, it offers a public civic facility with washroom access.

visitor.name: George Derby Conservation Area
visitor.desc: George Derby Conservation Area is a nature reserve located in Burnaby, BC, offering natural green space within the Metro Vancouver region. As a conservation area, it provides cyclists with a quiet natural respite along their route. No facility details are currently available from the park's web presence.

visitor.name: coFood Collaborative Garden Project
visitor.desc: A collaborative community food garden in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, situated between Main Street and Scotia Street. The garden hosts neighbourhood events including music nights, film screenings, and food education workshops, and invites visitors to help tend the space. The garden features places to sit and relax amid food plantings, with ground-level accessibility from East 4th Avenue.

visitor.name: Little Campbell River Hatchery
visitor.desc: The Little Campbell River Hatchery is a fish hatchery operated by the Semiahmoo Fish & Game Club, a community-based conservation organization in Surrey, BC. Located along the Little Campbell River, it supports salmon and steelhead enhancement programs in the watershed. Cyclists exploring the rural farmland and greenways of south Surrey may find it a worthwhile stop as a working conservation attraction.

visitor.name: Quadra Island Community Centre
visitor.desc: A volunteer-run community centre on Quadra Island, situated in Blenkin Memorial Park in Quathiaski Cove. The centre is the social hub of the island, hosting annual events like May Day celebrations, a fall fair, and a Christmas craft fair, and the society publishes a Quadra Island Trails Map useful for exploring the island. The centre has roots going back to the 1890s settlers of what was then Valdez Island.

detail.address: 970 West Rd, Quathiaski Cove, BC V0P 1N0

visitor.name: Chilliwack Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: The Chilliwack Cultural Centre is the Fraser Valley's primary performing arts and creative hub, featuring two performance theatres, an art gallery, 21 music studios, and four arts and crafts studios on the traditional territory of the Stó:lō Coast Salish People. It presents live theatre, concerts, gallery exhibitions, and creative classes year-round, making it a significant cultural stop for cyclists passing through Chilliwack.

visitor.name: Robert's Lake Regional Park
visitor.desc: Robert's Lake Regional Park is a nature reserve and regional park situated near Kelowna in British Columbia's Okanagan region. Tagged in OpenStreetMap as a nature reserve, it offers a natural outdoor setting typical of the semi-arid lake country surrounding Kelowna. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a scenic detour or rest point along their route.

visitor.name: Pomeroy Sport Centre
visitor.desc: The Pomeroy Sport Centre is a large municipal recreation facility in Fort St. John operated by the City. It features ice hockey, speed skating, and a walking track across a four-storey building. Fort St. John sits on the Alaska Highway, making it a common stopover for touring cyclists heading north.

visitor.name: Harper Mountain
visitor.desc: Harper Mountain is a family-owned ski hill that has operated since 1973, sitting just 20 minutes from Kamloops with 1,400 vertical feet of terrain across more than 400 acres. The mountain centres on a cozy log day lodge with a large wood fireplace and a licensed hot-food cafeteria, offering skiing, snowboarding, snowshoeing, a terrain park, night skiing, and lift-operated snow tubing. An Enduro race is listed among the mountain's resources and a Summer Rentals section appears in the site navigation, hinting at warm-season activity that may appeal to mountain bikers.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'a licensed hot food cafeteria' inside the log day lodge; also confirmed under Services as 'Lodge, Ski Shop, Cafeteria'

visitor.name: Yellow Bird Arts Gallery
visitor.desc: Yellow Bird Arts Gallery is a locally-owned art gallery and custom framing studio located inside Country Club Centre mall in Nanaimo, with over 30 years serving Central Vancouver Island. It showcases original works, Giclee canvas prints, and giftware from internationally recognized local and Vancouver Island artists, offering cyclists a genuine window into the region's vibrant arts scene. The gallery also provides specialty framing services and actively supports the broader Nanaimo and Vancouver Island arts community.

detail.address: #13-3200 Island Hwy N, Nanaimo, BC V9T 1W1

visitor.name: Rotary Interpretive Centre
visitor.desc: The Rotary Interpretive Centre is a volunteer-run nature education facility within the Great Blue Heron Nature Reserve, built and donated by the Chilliwack Rotary Club in the early 2000s and now welcoming over 20,000 visitors annually. Staffed by knowledgeable volunteers who provide maps and answer questions, it also houses the Blue Heron Gift Shop and is renowned as a bird-watching destination with year-round stocked feeders. Touring cyclists passing through the Sumas Prairie area will find a genuinely welcoming community stop open nearly every day of the year.

visitor.name: Templeton Park Pool
visitor.desc: Templeton Park Pool is a City of Vancouver-operated indoor aquatic facility in the Grandview-Woodland neighbourhood, featuring an inground pool and sauna. It is a fully accessible public recreation centre serving drop-in swimmers and community programs. Touring cyclists in East Vancouver will find it a convenient stop for a swim and use of change facilities.

visitor.name: Glenora Trails Head Park
visitor.desc: Glenora Trails Head Park is a Cowichan Valley Regional District park near Duncan on Vancouver Island, providing trailhead access to the Glenora trail network. It sits along the Vancouver Crossing Loop cycling route, making it a natural rest or navigation waypoint for touring cyclists travelling through the Cowichan Valley. As a regional district facility, it offers a natural forested setting typical of the southern Vancouver Island landscape.

visitor.name: Chemainus Theatre
visitor.desc: The Chemainus Theatre Festival is a fully professional, non-profit theatre in the seaside community of Chemainus on Vancouver Island, presenting Canadian performers in a 274-seat wheelchair-accessible auditorium with a raked floor for clear sightlines from every seat. Founded in the early 1990s as part of Chemainus's celebrated arts renaissance, the theatre pairs live productions with an on-site Playbill Dining Room serving meals for up to 160 guests. It serves as a cultural anchor for the community and a compelling stop for visitors exploring Vancouver Island.

notes.Café or food on site: On-site Playbill Dining Room seats up to 160 guests and serves continental breakfasts, nutrition breaks, lunches, and dinners; dining can be added to theatre ticket bookings

visitor.name: Kaslo Park Tennis Courts
visitor.desc: Kaslo Park Tennis Courts is a fenced outdoor public tennis facility within Vancouver's parks system. As a City of Vancouver park amenity, it is freely accessible to the public and sits within a neighbourhood park setting. Touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver may find it a convenient spot to stretch legs or take a break.

visitor.name: The Capitol Theatre
visitor.desc: The Capitol Theatre is a restored heritage performing arts venue in the heart of downtown Nelson, operated by the nonprofit Capitol Theatre Restoration Society since its restoration. It stages professional touring shows alongside two annual community productions — a summer youth show and a winter pantomime — and houses the Norma Vecchio Costume Shop, a collection of over 10,000 costume pieces open to the public. Touring cyclists stopping in Nelson will find a culturally significant landmark that anchors the city's vibrant arts scene.

visitor.name: BCIT Recreation Services
visitor.desc: BCIT Recreation Services is the campus sports and fitness centre for the British Columbia Institute of Technology at its main Burnaby campus. As a post-secondary institution recreation facility, it serves students, staff, and potentially community members with athletic and fitness programming. A touring cyclist arriving at BCIT would find a large institutional campus with a range of on-site services.

visitor.name: Osoyoos Desert Centre
visitor.desc: Osoyoos Desert Centre is a 67-acre nature interpretive facility operated by the Osoyoos Desert Society, showcasing one of Canada's rarest antelope-brush desert ecosystems in the South Okanagan. Visitors explore along a 1.5 km elevated wooden boardwalk with guided or self-guided tours, plus an interpretive building with hands-on exhibits and a native plant demonstration garden. Located just 3 km north of Osoyoos off Highway 97, it makes a compelling stop for cyclists riding through the valley.

visitor.name: Samuel and Frances Belzberg Library
visitor.desc: The Samuel and Frances Belzberg Library is the downtown Vancouver branch of Simon Fraser University Library, situated in the Harbour Centre building at the heart of the city's core. It offers study spaces, 18 desktop computers, and an equipment lending program to SFU affiliates, while community members can obtain guest passes for limited computer access. Its central location on West Hastings Street makes it a potential urban waypoint for touring cyclists navigating downtown Vancouver.

detail.address: 515 West Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 5K3

notes.Device charging: Library lends phone chargers, laptops, and dongles; available to students, faculty, and staff — community members require a guest pass

visitor.name: Brennan Park Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Brennan Park Recreation Centre is Squamish's municipal multi-sport facility, hosting a swimming pool, ice hockey rink, and skating arena in the heart of one of BC's premier outdoor adventure towns. As a District of Squamish facility it is fully wheelchair accessible with accessible washrooms. Touring cyclists passing through Squamish would find it a practical stop for public amenities in a well-maintained civic building.

visitor.name: Chali Rosso
visitor.desc: Chali-Rosso Art Gallery is a fine art gallery operating since 2005, specializing in original works on paper by Modern Masters including Picasso, Dalí, Chagall, Miró, and Matisse, alongside Inuit art and contemporary Canadian artists. The gallery also holds a notable collection of limited-edition Salvador Dalí sculptures created via the lost-wax process. Situated at Canada Place on Vancouver's waterfront, it offers worldwide shipping and services including art appraisal and consignment.

visitor.name: FINA Gallery
visitor.desc: The FINA Gallery is a public art gallery space located in the foyer of the Creative and Critical Studies Building on the UBC Okanagan campus, programmed by the UBC Okanagan Gallery. It presents research-based and experimental exhibitions with a strong focus on Indigenous, decolonial, and intersectional artistic practices, drawing on a permanent public art collection of over 700 works spread across campus. Visiting cyclists can engage with rotating solo and group shows that foreground Syilx Territory and contemporary Indigenous voices.

visitor.name: VIRL: Cumberland Branch
visitor.desc: The Cumberland Branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the community since 1947, now operating from a purpose-built ~3,200 sq. ft. civic building on Dunsmuir Avenue that opened in 2013. Part of the VIRL regional system spanning Vancouver Island and the central BC coast, this public library is a welcoming stop in Cumberland's compact historic downtown. Free public Wi-Fi is available to all visitors without a library card.

visitor.name: Vogue Theatre
visitor.desc: The Vogue Theatre is a 1,161-capacity Art Deco concert hall built in 1941 on Vancouver's historic Granville Street entertainment strip, one of the last surviving venues from the city's famed Theatre Row. Operated by the MRG Group, it hosts upwards of 200 live music, cinema, and community events annually and has repeatedly won the Canadian Music Week Best Performing Arts Centre Award. A touring cyclist looking for an evening of live entertainment in downtown Vancouver would find this a distinctive and historically significant destination.

visitor.name: Rose Garden
visitor.desc: The Rose Garden is a public park in Sidney, BC, maintained by the Town of Sidney and listed among its official parks. As a garden attraction in the seaside community of Sidney on the Saanich Peninsula, it would offer a pleasant green stop for cyclists touring the area. Specific facilities and amenities could not be confirmed from the available website content.

visitor.name: Munson Mountain Park
visitor.desc: Munson Mountain Park is a municipal nature reserve and prominent hilltop landmark in Penticton, BC, managed by the City of Penticton. The site offers a popular hiking destination within the city, with sweeping views over Okanagan Lake and Skaha Lake that draw both residents and visiting cyclists. It is a well-known attraction on the cycling tourism circuit through the South Okanagan.

visitor.name: Jim Ciccone Civic Center
visitor.desc: The Jim Ciccone Civic Center is Prince Rupert's main municipal sports and recreation complex, operated by the City of Prince Rupert's Recreation Department. As the community's primary civic recreation hub in a remote coastal city accessible mainly by ferry or the Yellowhead Highway, it represents a significant community facility for residents and visitors alike. Touring cyclists arriving in Prince Rupert — a common BC ferry terminus — may find it a useful stop, though specific cyclist amenities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Compass Customer Service
visitor.desc: Compass Customer Service is TransLink's in-person office for Metro Vancouver's transit fare card, located inside Waterfront Station — the main interchange hub for SkyTrain, SeaBus, and West Coast Express. Cyclists who plan to combine riding with transit can pick up or manage a Compass card here, or get system-wide trip planning assistance. The office is staffed by TransLink agents and can provide service in over 300 languages via a third-party interpreter line.

visitor.name: Cliff McNabb Arena
visitor.desc: Cliff McNabb Arena is a City of Nanaimo municipal ice arena located in Nanaimo on Vancouver Island. It is part of the city's parks and recreation network, offering skating programs and arena activities. It functions primarily as a local sports facility rather than a visitor attraction.

visitor.name: Cowichan Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Cowichan Aquatic Centre is a public swimming facility operated by the Municipality of North Cowichan, located in Duncan on southern Vancouver Island. It sits within North Cowichan's broader recreation portfolio, which includes sports fields, trails, and court sports. As a community aquatic centre, it may offer useful amenities for touring cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley.

visitor.name: Saltair Community Centre
