visitor.desc: A not-for-profit community hub housed in the former Mount Brenton Elementary School in Saltair, operated by the Saltair Community Society under a 20-year lease with the Cowichan Valley Regional District. The converted school building offers multiple rental halls and rooms hosting arts groups, yoga classes, daycare, and cultural events for the surrounding Cowichan Valley community. The Society has been steadily improving the facility and identified bicycle rack installation as a planned upgrade.

detail.address: 3850 South Oyster School Road, Ladysmith, BC V9G 1Z4

visitor.name: VIRL: Nanaimo Wellington Branch
visitor.desc: The Nanaimo Wellington branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library is a public library situated inside Country Club Centre, halfway between downtown Nanaimo and the north end of the city. The branch relocated to its current space in May 2017, offering books, digital resources, meeting rooms, and community programming. For a touring cyclist, it provides a mid-city indoor stop in a well-established commercial centre.

visitor.name: Cowichan Community Centre Sports Complex
visitor.desc: The Cowichan Community Centre Sports Complex is a major public recreation facility in Duncan operated by the Cowichan Valley Regional District. It offers swimming and ice hockey as its primary sports, making it one of the larger community recreation hubs on Vancouver Island's mid-section. Touring cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley may find it a useful stop for post-ride recovery.

visitor.name: Landmark Cinemas
visitor.desc: Landmark Cinemas is a major Canadian cinema chain with a Fort St. John location in a commercial area on 93 Avenue. For touring cyclists passing through the Peace River region, it offers a climate-controlled indoor break in a community that sits along the Alaska Highway corridor. It is the only cinema serving this northern BC city.

visitor.name: Gordon MacMillan Southam Observatory
visitor.desc: The Gordon MacMillan Southam Observatory is a public optical telescope facility in Vanier Park, operated by the H.R. MacMillan Space Centre—BC's premier space science institution since 1968. Situated on the waterfront near Kitsilano, it offers public stargazing through a research-grade telescope. Cyclists arriving via the nearby Seaside Greenway will find it bundled into a broader complex that includes a planetarium and interactive science galleries.

detail.address: Vanier Park, 1100 Chestnut Street, Vancouver, BC, V6J 3J9

visitor.name: Agassiz-Harrison Museum & Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Agassiz-Harrison Museum & Visitor Centre occupies one of Canada's oldest surviving wood-built Canadian Pacific Railway stations, constructed in 1893 and located in the heart of downtown Agassiz. It serves as both a regional history museum and an official visitor centre for the area, making it a natural waypoint for touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley. The on-site Local Motive Giftshop offers locally made artisan goods and country-fresh jams.

visitor.name: Brocklehurst Pool
visitor.desc: Brocklehurst Pool is a municipal outdoor swimming pool operated by the City of Kamloops, located in the Brocklehurst neighbourhood. Kamloops is one of BC's hottest cities in summer, making a pool stop especially appealing for touring cyclists passing through the Thompson Valley. The facility offers public swimming, fitness programs, and lesson programs.

visitor.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
visitor.desc: The Canadian Heritage Garden appears to be a themed section within VanDusen Botanical Garden, a celebrated 55-acre botanical oasis in Vancouver featuring over 7,500 plant species and varieties from around the world. VanDusen offers a full visitor experience including fine dining at the Shaughnessy Restaurant, a Garden Cafe, educational programming, and seasonal events. The garden is explicitly accessible by bike and is situated in a central Vancouver neighbourhood well-connected by cycling routes.

notes.Café or food on site: Shaughnessy Restaurant (fine dining, West Coast menu, lunch/afternoon tea/dinner) and The Garden Cafe (Fair Trade coffees, sandwiches, soups) both confirmed on site per the Services page

visitor.name: BC Wildlife Park
visitor.desc: BC Wildlife Park is a non-profit wildlife park and rehabilitation centre in Kamloops, BC, operating since 1965 and home to nearly 200 animals representing 65 species native to British Columbia, including cougars, wolves, bears, and the only Kermode bear in human care in the world. Many animals are permanent residents after being rescued or orphaned. The 18,000 sq. ft. Discovery Centre houses interactive exhibits, a reptile display, a gift shop, and the Blue Heron Cafe, making it a worthwhile stop for touring cyclists exploring the Kamloops area.

notes.Café or food on site: Blue Heron Cafe located inside the Discovery Centre, as stated on the /visitorcentre.htm subpage

visitor.name: Ferry Building Gallery
visitor.desc: The Ferry Building Gallery is a public community art gallery housed in a heritage building over 100 years old at Ambleside Landing in West Vancouver, operated by the District of West Vancouver. The building began as a bustling ferry terminal and now presents up to 11 exhibitions annually featuring regional artists from the North Shore, Sea-to-Sky Corridor, and Sunshine Coast. Cyclists exploring the Ambleside waterfront will find a welcoming cultural stop with rotating juried and invitational exhibitions and a gift shop stocked with works by local BC artists.

detail.address: 1414 Argyle Avenue, West Vancouver, BC V7T 1C2

visitor.name: Archie Browning Sports Centre
visitor.desc: The Archie Browning Sports Centre is a municipally operated recreation facility in Esquimalt, run by the Township of Esquimalt. It hosts a range of programs including ice skating, aquatics, fitness, and pickleball, making it a multi-sport hub for the community. Touring cyclists passing through the Esquimalt area may find it a useful stop given its public recreation mandate.

visitor.name: Salvation Army Temple
visitor.desc: The Salvation Army Temple is a three-storey heritage civic building at 301 East Hastings Street in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside, designed by architects Mercer & Mercer and completed in 1949. It is registered on the Canadian Register of Historic Places and associated with the Salvation Army's Harbour Light social services mission in the neighbourhood. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find it a notable piece of mid-century institutional architecture in one of Vancouver's most storied corridors.

visitor.name: Blackburn Lake Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: Blackburn Lake Nature Reserve is an 18.4-hectare protected area managed by the Salt Spring Island Conservancy, surrounding about two-thirds of Blackburn Lake at the geographic centre of Salt Spring Island. The reserve features mowed public walking trails through meadows, wetlands, and forest edges, and is home to over 100 bird species and 21 Species at Risk, including Great Blue Herons, Peregrine Falcons, and Northern Red-legged Frogs. Cyclists exploring Salt Spring Island can lock up and walk the trails, though dogs are strictly prohibited to protect the sensitive wildlife habitat.

detail.address: 265 Blackburn Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2B8

visitor.name: VPL: Mount Pleasant Branch
visitor.desc: The Mount Pleasant Branch of the Vancouver Public Library is a public branch library serving the Mount Pleasant neighbourhood at the corner of Kingsway. As part of the VPL system, it offers community programming and public access resources in one of Vancouver's most cycling-friendly urban neighbourhoods. For touring cyclists it represents a convenient urban rest stop with public access in a lively, bikeable part of the city.

visitor.name: Inverholme Schoolhouse
visitor.desc: The Inverholme Schoolhouse is a preserved one-room schoolhouse originally built in 1909 in East Ladner and physically relocated to Deas Island Regional Park in 1981, where it stands as a heritage museum within the park grounds. Situated on a tidal island in the lower Fraser River delta, it offers touring cyclists an evocative stop connecting agricultural and pioneer history of the region. The park itself lies along popular cycling corridors connecting Ladner, Delta, and the Tsawwassen area.

visitor.name: Qw'xwulwis Cable Bay Protected Area
visitor.desc: A 26.5-hectare conservation area on Galiano Island featuring over 1 km of undeveloped coastline along the northern half of Cable Bay, acquired by the Nature Trust of BC in 2022. The area is traditionally known as Qw'xwulwis, the Hul'qumi'num word for the action of paddling, and was historically an important gathering place for Coast Salish Peoples before and after crossing the Strait of Georgia. Public trails run along the shoreline and inland edges as part of the 600+ hectare Mid-Island Protected Areas Network.

visitor.name: Sungod Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: A municipal recreation centre operated by the City of Delta in the North Delta area. As a sports centre it likely offers fitness and recreation programs for the surrounding community. It sits within Delta's parks and recreation network, which also maintains local trails and cycling infrastructure.

visitor.name: Pender Islands Museum
visitor.desc: A local history museum housed in a restored 1908 'kit house' farmstead within the Gulf Islands National Park Reserve on Pender Island. The museum tells stories of the W̱SÁNEĆ People and settler families through artifacts including an ancient sandstone whale carving. The waterfront location features a heritage orchard with picnic tables and trail access to Ella Bay at low tide.

detail.address: 2408 South Otter Bay Road, Pender Island, V0N 2M1

visitor.name: Karen Magnussen Community Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Karen Magnussen Community Recreation Centre is a public facility operated by North Vancouver Recreation and Culture (NVRC), offering an aquatic centre, arena, fitness centre, and multipurpose gymnasiums. It runs a broad range of programs including public swimming, aquafit, skating, and fitness classes, making it a well-rounded community hub on the North Shore. Touring cyclists passing through North Vancouver may find it a practical stop given its pool and change facilities, though cycling-specific services are not explicitly advertised.

detail.address: 2300 Kirkstone Road, North Vancouver, BC V7J 1Z6

visitor.name: Kariton Art Gallery + Boutique
visitor.desc: Kariton Art Gallery + Boutique is a community art gallery operated by the Abbotsford Arts Council, housed in a detached heritage building on Ware Street in Abbotsford. It presents rotating exhibitions, workshops, open calls for artists, and a gift shop, and also hosts the Downie Wenjack Legacy Space dedicated to Indigenous reconciliation. The gallery is wheelchair accessible and sits in a quiet residential-scale neighbourhood, offering a cultural detour for cyclists touring the Fraser Valley.

visitor.name: La Boussole Centre Communataire
visitor.desc: La Boussole (French for 'the compass') is a Francophone community centre and NGO serving Vancouver's French-speaking community at 312 Main Street in the Downtown Eastside. As a community hub, it likely offers meeting spaces, programs, and services for local residents and newcomers. Touring cyclists passing through may find it a useful stop for local knowledge or basic facilities.

visitor.name: Oliver & District Heritage Society Museum
visitor.desc: The Oliver & District Heritage Society Museum is a not-for-profit community museum preserving the history of Oliver and the surrounding Okanagan region, encompassing mining heritage, First Nations culture, and the agricultural story of Canada's Wine Capital. The museum features permanent galleries including the Historic Fairview Jail exhibit and a fully wheelchair-accessible Heritage Garden with interpretive signage about local natural history and syilx Okanagan culture. A separate archival facility on Fairview Road serves researchers seeking deeper engagement with the region's documentary past.

visitor.name: O'Keefe Ranch
visitor.desc: O'Keefe Ranch is a historic living museum near Vernon, BC, preserving one of British Columbia's oldest cattle ranches across a sprawling multi-building property with year-round resident farm animals. Operated by the O'Keefe Ranch & Interior Heritage Society, the site offers seasonal heritage exhibitions, glamping, and community events from spring through fall. Touring cyclists will find it a substantial destination stop along Hwy 97, with an on-site restaurant and a property covering roughly 1.2 km of walking through heritage buildings and grounds.

notes.Café or food on site: Rustlers Table Restaurant confirmed open on-site; website front page states 'Rustlers Table Restaurant is OPEN'

visitor.name: Killarney Leisure Pool
visitor.desc: Killarney Leisure Pool is a City of Vancouver public recreation facility in the Killarney neighbourhood, offering a swimming pool and hot tub in a covered, wheelchair-accessible building. It is part of Vancouver's municipal parks and recreation network, making it a convenient stop for cyclists seeking a swim or soak after a long ride. The facility charges an entry fee and is operated year-round.

visitor.name: Helmcken House
visitor.desc: Helmcken House is one of the oldest surviving residential buildings in British Columbia, constructed in 1852 for Dr. John Sebastian Helmcken, a physician and influential figure in early colonial BC politics. Situated within Victoria's Cultural Precinct alongside the Royal BC Museum and BC Legislature, it offers touring cyclists an intimate window into mid-19th century domestic life in the province. The house is a designated National Historic Site and stands as a compelling cultural stop on any cycling tour of downtown Victoria.

notes.Café or food on site: Royal BC Museum Cultural Precinct website lists Sound Bites Concession and The Yummy Truck as food options on the same campus where Helmcken House is located

visitor.name: Ian Tan Gallery
visitor.desc: Ian Tan Gallery is a long-established (1999) contemporary Canadian art gallery occupying a striking storefront on Vancouver's South Granville arts corridor, known for its floor-to-ceiling windows and soaring ceilings filled with rotating exhibitions of paintings, drawings, glass works, and sculpture. The gallery represents both emerging and established Canadian artists and admission is free. Services extend well beyond viewing — collectors can access art consulting, framing, installation, and worldwide shipping.

visitor.name: Clayton Community Centre
visitor.desc: Clayton Community Centre is Surrey's newest municipal recreation facility, operated by the City of Surrey and combining fitness and recreation programs, a branch library, and childminding services under one roof. Located in the Clayton neighbourhood of Surrey's southeastern suburbs, it serves a broad cross-section of the local community. Touring cyclists moving through the area may find it a convenient urban stop, though confirmed cyclist-specific amenities are not documented on the website.

visitor.name: VIRL: Sidney / North Saanich Branch
visitor.desc: The VIRL Sidney/North Saanich Branch is a public library situated a few blocks from Sidney's downtown waterfront, part of the Vancouver Island Regional Library system. The branch underwent a significant renovation in 2019, resulting in a completely reimagined interior and new building systems. It offers public meeting spaces and serves as a community hub for the Sidney and North Saanich area.

visitor.name: Browne Creek Wetlands
visitor.desc: Browne Creek Wetlands is a nature reserve situated within the Vedder Greenway along the south bank of the Vedder River in Chilliwack. The area centres on a salmon spawning channel network constructed by Fisheries and Oceans Canada and the Fraser Valley Watersheds Coalition, with trail infrastructure developed through a partnership between the City of Chilliwack and the Rotary Club of Chilliwack. Its location within the Vedder Greenway corridor makes it a natural detour point for cyclists riding the greenway route.

visitor.name: Canlan Ice Sports North Shore
visitor.desc: Canlan Ice Sports North Shore is an indoor ice skating facility in North Vancouver, part of the Canlan Ice Sports network of recreational ice complexes across Canada. Tagged as a public building in OSM, it serves recreational skaters and hockey players in the North Shore area. A touring cyclist passing through North Vancouver may find it a notable stop or landmark in the community.

visitor.name: Fort Langley Library
visitor.desc: Fort Langley Library is a public branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library (FVRL) system, nestled in the heritage village of Fort Langley. The library is freely open to all and provides computers, printing, and a full lending collection. Its location in one of BC's most historically rich cycling destinations makes it a natural rest stop for riders passing through the area.

detail.address: 23430 Mavis Avenue, Fort Langley, BC V1M 2S2

visitor.name: Britannia Shipyards National Historic Site
visitor.desc: Britannia Shipyards National Historic Site is a free, eight-acre outdoor heritage site on the banks of the Fraser River in Steveston, showcasing the oldest shipyard community in British Columbia through preserved heritage buildings arranged along a wooden boardwalk. The site brings BC's fishing, canning, and boatbuilding history to life through exhibits, programs, and an active wooden boat restoration project. Located just minutes from Steveston village, it is easily reached by bike and offers a scenic stop on a Fraser River cycling route.

visitor.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
visitor.desc: VanDusen Botanical Garden is a 55-acre urban oasis in Vancouver's Shaughnessy neighbourhood featuring over 7,500 plant species and varieties from around the world. It offers a range of on-site food options from a casual garden café to a full fine-dining restaurant, making it a worthwhile mid-ride destination. Seasonal events and rotating public art installations give the garden recurring appeal for cyclists returning to the area.

notes.Café or food on site: Shaughnessy Restaurant (fine dining, West Coast menu, lunch/afternoon tea/dinner/weekend brunch, seasonal patio) and The Garden Café (Fair Trade coffees, handcrafted beverages, sandwiches, soups, curries, picnic baskets in summer) both confirmed on site at VanDusen Botanical Garden per the Services subpage

visitor.name: Westwood Park
visitor.desc: Westwood Park is a publicly accessible outdoor tennis facility in Coquitlam, featuring concrete courts enclosed by a fence. It is tagged as a sports centre in OpenStreetMap and appears to be a municipal recreational space maintained by the City of Coquitlam. A touring cyclist passing through the area could stop here, though it is primarily a tennis destination rather than a cycling-focused facility.

visitor.name: Earthwise Society Agassiz
visitor.desc: A 58-acre nonprofit organic teaching farm and garden nestled between Harrison Hot Springs and Agassiz, featuring restored wetlands, old-growth forest groves, heritage farmhouse and barn circa 1910, and a trail system with interpretive signs along the Miami River. Free to visit, with ecotours, a farm store, and community food security programs on site.

notes.Café or food on site: Farm store on site; also offers seasonal organic produce from the working farm

visitor.name: VIRL: Sooke Branch
visitor.desc: The Sooke branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the community since 1963, sitting on the unceded traditional territory of the T'sou-ke First Nation. It offers a quiet, air-conditioned, scent-free space with meeting rooms available to book, making it a comfortable rest stop for touring cyclists passing through Sooke.

visitor.name: Ucluelet Community Centre
visitor.desc: Ucluelet Community Centre is a municipal recreation facility run by the District of Ucluelet, offering seasonal programs in fitness, arts, and youth activities. Located in the small west-coast town of Ucluelet on Vancouver Island's rugged Pacific Rim, it serves as a community hub for residents and visitors alike. Touring cyclists on the Pacific Rim Highway may find it a useful stop in a town with limited public facilities.

visitor.name: Manley Creek Park
visitor.desc: Manley Creek Park is a nature reserve managed by the Cowichan Valley Regional District on southern Vancouver Island. As a protected natural area, it offers cyclists a quiet stop amid BC coastal forest and riparian habitat. The park is part of CVRD's regional parks network, which preserves ecologically sensitive lands across the valley.

visitor.name: False Creek Community Centre
visitor.desc: False Creek Community Centre is a publicly operated civic facility on Granville Island, jointly managed by the Vancouver Park Board and the non-profit False Creek Community Association since 1980. It offers a broad range of programs including kayaking, canoeing, tennis, fitness classes, pottery, and performing arts for all ages. Located steps from Granville Island's public market and waterfront seawall, it sits along one of Vancouver's most popular cycling corridors.

notes.Café or food on site: Saturday Morning Youth Concession sells coffee, tea, juice boxes, granola bars, chip bags, and more on site

visitor.name: Marianne and Edward Gibson Art Museum
visitor.desc: The Marianne and Edward Gibson Art Museum is a new purpose-built public art museum on SFU's Burnaby Mountain campus that opened in Fall 2025, consolidating SFU Galleries' collections into a single, more accessible facility. It mounts contemporary visual art exhibitions, public commissions, residencies, and a wide array of public programs rooted in decolonial and interdisciplinary approaches. The museum sits directly beside the SFU Transit Exchange at the top of Burnaby Mountain, making it a notable cultural destination reachable from across Metro Vancouver.

visitor.name: Climb Base5
visitor.desc: Climb Base5 is a premier indoor rock climbing facility in Coquitlam offering bouldering, auto-belay, top rope, and lead climbing for all skill levels. With a second location in North Vancouver, the gym runs structured courses from beginner belay through lead climbing technique, plus youth camps and group bookings. It bills itself as a community-focused space emphasizing inclusivity, skill development, and a culture of climbing.

visitor.name: Cineplex Odeon International Village Cinemas
visitor.desc: Cineplex Odeon International Village Cinemas, also known as Tinseltown, is a multi-screen movie theatre situated on the 3rd floor of the International Village mall in downtown Vancouver. It is notable for a broad selection of international films screened in Cantonese, Mandarin, Punjabi, Hindi, Vietnamese, and other languages, reflecting the multicultural character of the surrounding neighbourhood. The venue also hosts event cinema, sensory-friendly screenings, and is equipped with closed-caption and described-narration assistive technology.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists Starbucks, Outtakes, Pizza by Outtakes, and Melt as in-theatre vendors, plus a full concessions menu offering wraps, sandwiches, premium nachos, hot dogs, fries, poutine, and Coca-Cola Freestyle drinks

visitor.name: Historic Hat Creek Ranch
visitor.desc: Historic Hat Creek Ranch is a provincially recognized heritage landscape spanning some 130 hectares of farmyards, fields, and range land along the historic Cariboo Wagon Road near Cache Creek. The site includes approximately twenty original wooden domestic and farm buildings dating from 1861 into the 20th century, offering cyclists a rare glimpse into BC's gold-rush and ranching era. It sits on a well-traveled touring corridor between Cache Creek and points north.

visitor.name: Seabreeze Gallery
visitor.desc: Seabreeze Gallery is a cooperative art gallery nestled in the heart of Snug Cove on Bowen Island, dedicated exclusively to handmade works by local artists spanning jewellery, glassblowing, sculpture, painting, fibre arts, ceramics, leatherwork, and more. The bright, naturally lit space is designed to let each maker's work breathe within a calm, neutral setting. For cyclists riding the Bowen Island Trunk Road, it offers a compelling cultural stop in the village centre steps from the ferry terminal.

detail.address: 455 Bowen Island Trunk Road, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G2

visitor.name: Centennial Activity Centre
visitor.desc: The Centennial Activity Centre is a City of Coquitlam recreation facility built around a large gymnasium operated jointly with School District 43. It serves local residents of all ages through a mix of drop-in sports and registered programs. The centre is accessible via several Coquitlam transit routes and sits in a residential neighbourhood near Poirier Street.

visitor.name: Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Recreation Centre sits within the Royal Roads University campus at Hatley Park, a 260-hectare National Historic Site roughly 25 minutes west of downtown Victoria. The wider estate encompasses Hatley Castle, formal Italian and Japanese gardens, and an extensive network of walking, hiking, and biking trails through old-growth coastal forest. Touring cyclists can combine a trail ride with visits to the castle and gardens, making this a notable stop on the Victoria–Sooke corridor.

notes.Café or food on site: Habitat Café mentioned repeatedly in site navigation and the /visit page as an on-site food option

visitor.name: Ladner Leisure Centre
visitor.desc: Ladner Leisure Centre is a City of Delta-operated municipal recreation facility in the Ladner neighbourhood, with swimming as its primary programmed sport. It occupies a purpose-built recreation building on Clarence Taylor Crescent and functions as a community hub for fitness and aquatic programming for Delta residents.

visitor.name: Romper Room
visitor.desc: Romper Room is a long-established indoor rock climbing centre that has served the mid Vancouver Island climbing community since 1996, offering 7,500 sq ft of climbing surface including top rope, lead walls, a bouldering cave, auto-belays, and two MoonBoards. The facility welcomes complete beginners through experienced climbers, with rental gear available on site and structured courses ranging from introductory sessions to lead certification. For a touring cyclist visiting Nanaimo, it represents a well-rounded active recreation stop with a strong local community reputation.

visitor.name: Champlain Heights Community Centre
visitor.desc: Champlain Heights Community Centre is a neighbourhood recreation hub in southeast Vancouver featuring a fitness centre with sauna, squash and racquetball courts, a dance studio, and indoor cycling programs. It sits adjacent to Everett Crowley Park, the fifth-largest park in Vancouver, which was reclaimed from a former landfill and has grown into a young urban forest. The centre serves the local community with programs for all ages and also offers room rentals and birthday party venues.

visitor.name: Castlegar and District Community Complex
visitor.desc: The Castlegar and District Community Complex is a publicly operated recreation facility run by the Regional District of Central Kootenay, serving residents and visitors in the Castlegar area. As a sports centre, it is a practical stop for touring cyclists looking to access indoor recreation amenities in this hub city along the Kootenay River. The complex is one of several RDCK-managed recreation facilities in the region.

visitor.name: Thetis Island Community Centre
visitor.desc: Forbes Hall Community Centre is the civic heart of Thetis Island, a quiet Gulf Island in the Salish Sea reachable by ferry from Chemainus. The hall hosts everything from health clinics and a food bank to community events and a library, functioning as a true village commons for the island's small, close-knit population. Touring cyclists venturing off the main Gulf Islands circuit to explore Thetis Island would encounter this volunteer-run hub as one of the island's central gathering places.

visitor.name: McArthur Island Sport and Event Centre
visitor.desc: McArthur Island Sport and Event Centre is a City of Kamloops municipal facility situated on McArthur Island in the Thompson River, primarily serving lacrosse and multi-sport events. The island setting is accessible via a short bridge and sits within a larger park complex that is popular with walkers and cyclists riding the river trail network. As a public facility it may offer services useful to touring cyclists passing through Kamloops, though specific amenities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Matson Conservation Area
visitor.desc: A protected nature conservation area in Esquimalt on the traditional territories of the Lək̓ʷəŋən Peoples, managed by Habitat Acquisition Trust since 2004. The site was saved through a community-driven partnership among HAT, Nature Conservancy of Canada, and the Township of Esquimalt, and ongoing restoration work maintains its ecological integrity. A touring cyclist would find a quiet green space for a rest stop, though it is a conservation area rather than a developed park.

visitor.name: Oak Bay Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Oak Bay Recreation Centre is a full-service municipal sports and recreation facility operated by Recreation Oak Bay in the seaside District of Oak Bay, adjacent to Victoria. It offers a range of registered and drop-in programs across fitness, aquatics, and active living. As a community hub near popular cycling routes on southern Vancouver Island, it is a plausible rest and refresh stop for touring cyclists.

visitor.name: Lardeau Valley Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Lardeau Valley Community Centre is a volunteer-sustained community hub in the remote Lardeau Valley along Highway 31, serving both long-time residents and passing visitors. A notable perk for touring cyclists is the dedicated showerhouse and laundry facility on site. Funded by regional grants, the centre is a genuine lifeline in this sparsely populated mountain corridor.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Contact page explicitly lists 'Showerhouse and Laundry' as an on-site facility

visitor.name: Moody Park Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: Moody Park Outdoor Pool is a municipal outdoor swimming pool operated by the City of New Westminster, located in Moody Park at 701 Tenth Street. It offers seasonal outdoor swimming and is a refreshing stop for touring cyclists passing through New Westminster on a warm day.

visitor.name: Nelson & District Community Complex
visitor.desc: The Nelson Aquatic Centre is a publicly operated recreation facility in Nelson, BC, run by the Regional District of Central Kootenay. It features a swimming pool along with a hot tub, sauna, and steam room — amenities that make it a compelling recovery stop for touring cyclists completing a long day in the Kootenays. The complex is part of a broader community recreation hub serving the Nelson area.

visitor.name: Westbank Museum
visitor.desc: The Westbank Museum in West Kelowna preserves the cultural heritage of the Westbank area—spanning pioneer families, forestry, farming, Indigenous history, and regional conflicts—on the traditional territory of the Syilx/Okanagan Peoples. It also functions as a Visitor Information Centre, making it a practical stop for route advice as well as history. A working miniature sawmill is a standout exhibit, and admission is by donation.

detail.address: 2376 Dobbin Rd (Hwy 97), West Kelowna, BC V4T 2H9

visitor.name: Kimberley Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Kimberley Aquatic Centre is a municipally operated public swimming facility run by the City of Kimberley in the East Kootenays. In addition to a pool, OSM records indicate it offers a hot tub and steam room, making it a potentially appealing recovery stop for cyclists finishing a day on the region's renowned trail network. It is one of the main indoor recreation facilities serving the Kimberley community.

visitor.name: Ladysmith Maritime Society Museum
visitor.desc: The Ladysmith Maritime Society is a volunteer-run non-profit charitable organization that has been preserving maritime heritage and providing ocean access to the community since 1985. It operates popular 90-minute harbour tours aboard restored heritage vessels departing from Ladysmith Fishermen's Wharf, offering wildlife viewing of otters, seals, eagles, and more. The Society also runs an annual Sea Life Celebration drawing over 1,000 visitors, a Sea Life Centre on Thetis Island, and family-friendly beach events at Transfer Beach.

visitor.name: MNP Place
visitor.desc: MNP Place (formerly Capital News Centre) is Kelowna's largest indoor sports facility, featuring two NHL-size ice surfaces, a seasonal leisure ice surface, and two full-size indoor turf fields serving minor and adult hockey, soccer, and skating programs. Operated by GSL Group, the facility anchors a broader network of BC arenas and hosts major provincial tournaments. On-site tenants include a full-service restaurant and bar, a fitness centre, a physiotherapy clinic, and an Okanagan Regional Library branch.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists Boomers Bar & Grill (described as a 'full-service restaurant') and a concession stand as on-site food and beverage options

visitor.name: Pacific Institute for Sport Education
visitor.desc: PISE is a non-profit sport and physical literacy institute located in Victoria, BC, and is recognized as the first summer sport institute in Canada. It offers a broad range of programs for all ages and abilities, including a dedicated 'Kids on Wheels' cycling program, a performance fitness centre, and a 4-lane indoor track. Families on cycling tours with children interested in a structured bike skills program may find it a worthwhile stop.

detail.address: 4371 Interurban Rd, Victoria BC V9E 2C5, Canada

visitor.name: Bellevue Creek Greenway
visitor.desc: Bellevue Creek Greenway is a municipal nature reserve in Kelowna, BC, following the Bellevue Creek corridor through the city. As a linear greenway, it likely offers a natural, off-road route through an urban area — the kind of quiet, scenic detour that touring cyclists often seek when passing through a city. It is managed by the City of Kelowna as part of its parks and beaches network.

visitor.name: Stop of Interest 59 - Britannia Mine
visitor.desc: Britannia Mine Museum is an award-winning National Historic Site on the Sea to Sky Highway between Vancouver and Whistler, occupying the former site of what were the British Empire's largest copper producers from 1930–35. Touring cyclists can rumble aboard an underground train, pan for gold, and take in the multi-sensory BOOM! experience inside the historic Mill No. 3. The site is a natural stop on the Sea to Sky cycling corridor, drawing visitors heading between Vancouver and Squamish.

notes.Café or food on site: Chatterbox Cafe is listed in the site navigation under the Visit section of the museum website

visitor.name: South Arm Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: South Arm Outdoor Pool is a City of Richmond-operated seasonal outdoor swimming facility located in the South Arm neighbourhood of Richmond, BC. It is one of several outdoor aquatic facilities managed by the city's parks and recreation department and serves the surrounding community. For touring cyclists, it represents a potential summer stop in a municipality well known for its flat, cycling-friendly terrain.

visitor.name: Brockton Point Totem Poles
visitor.desc: The Brockton Point Totem Poles are a celebrated outdoor cultural site within Stanley Park, featuring a collection of monumental Indigenous poles representing First Nations from across British Columbia. The site sits along the Stanley Park Seawall, one of the most popular cycling routes in Vancouver, making it a natural stopping point for touring cyclists circumnavigating the park. As a free, open-air attraction on public parkland, it requires no admission and is accessible year-round.

visitor.name: Richmond Art Gallery
visitor.desc: The Richmond Art Gallery is a free public contemporary art gallery situated within the Richmond Cultural Centre, presenting rotating exhibitions alongside a robust program of artist talks, workshops, school outreach, and youth programming. Admission is by donation, making it an accessible cultural stop for cyclists exploring Richmond. The gallery is within walking distance of the Canada Line's Richmond-Brighouse station and is accompanied by free 3-hour parking in the Cultural Centre parkade.

visitor.name: Bell Performing Arts Centre
visitor.desc: Built in 2001 and owned by Surrey School District No. 36, the Bell Performing Arts Centre is the largest professional theatre in the Fraser Valley, hosting dance, concerts, theatre, and community events. The venue is noted for excellent sightlines and outstanding acoustics, drawing performers and audiences from across the region. Touring cyclists passing through Surrey's eastern suburbs will find a well-established cultural landmark available for public events and rentals.

visitor.name: The Hive
visitor.desc: The Hive is a multi-location indoor climbing gym chain with a North Shore outpost in North Vancouver's Dollarton area. It offers bouldering and climbing in a purpose-built sports facility, making it a potential activity stop for touring cyclists exploring the North Shore. Visitors must sign a waiver on their first visit, and youth require parental consent and adequate adult supervision.

visitor.name: Farmstrong Cider Company
visitor.desc: Farmstrong Cider Company is a family-run craft cidery and farm restaurant operating out of a restored heritage barn on a century-old farm in Armstrong, BC's Okanagan Valley. Small-batch ciders are made on-site from locally sourced fruit, with guided cellar tours and tasting flights available. Touring cyclists can stop for a full lunch or dinner menu featuring wood-fired pizza, with outdoor seating and a dog-friendly patio.

notes.Café or food on site: Full lunch and dinner menu including wood-fired pizza; vegan and gluten-free options available. Kitchen takes last orders 30 minutes before closing

visitor.name: Swan Lake Christmas Hill Nature Sanctuary
visitor.desc: Swan Lake Christmas Hill Nature Sanctuary is a 135-acre urban nature refuge in Victoria encompassing a significant wetland around Swan Lake and a rocky Garry oak forest atop Christmas Hill, with 4.5 km of walking trails drawing roughly 100,000 visitors annually. Managed by a non-profit society for over 50 years, it protects rare and threatened native plants and wildlife along the Pacific Flyway migration corridor. The on-site Nature House serves as an interpretive centre and includes a gift shop, making it a rewarding cultural and ecological stop for cyclists touring the Greater Victoria area.

detail.address: 3873 Swan Lake Road, Victoria, BC V8X 3W1

visitor.name: ArtSpring
visitor.desc: ArtSpring is Salt Spring Island's premier community performing and visual arts centre, occupying an 11,800 sq ft heavy timber building with a 259-seat theatre and a 5,200 sq ft gallery and multi-purpose space. Opened in 1999, it hosts around 300 events annually—from local community productions to international touring artists, gallery exhibitions, and workshops—making it the cultural hub of the Gulf Islands. Cycling visitors to Salt Spring Island will find it a compelling stop for live music, dance, theatre, and visual art in one of BC's most scenic island communities.

detail.address: 100 Jackson Avenue, Salt Spring Island, V8K 2V8

visitor.name: PGPL: Bob Harkins Branch
visitor.desc: The Bob Harkins Branch is the downtown flagship of the Prince George Public Library, a non-profit municipal library serving approximately 700 people daily in its three-storey building on Canada Games Way. It offers public internet access, community event programming, a Knowledge Garden, and accessible spaces including study rooms. For a touring cyclist, it makes a practical downtown rest stop with free wifi and washroom access in the heart of Prince George.

detail.address: 888 Canada Games Way, Prince George, V2L 5T6

visitor.name: Museum of Natural History
visitor.desc: The Museum of Natural History is operated by Vancouver Island University on its main Nanaimo campus, housing collections related to natural science disciplines taught at the university. As a university teaching museum, it serves both students and the broader public with exhibits in areas such as geology, botany, and natural history. Touring cyclists exploring Nanaimo can visit the campus setting, which sits within the broader VIU grounds.

visitor.name: Sea to Sky Gondola
visitor.desc: The Sea to Sky Gondola is a year-round aerial gondola attraction near Squamish, BC, lifting visitors to a mountain summit with sweeping views of Howe Sound and surrounding peaks. At the top, guests can cross a suspension bridge, explore hiking and via ferrata routes, and dine at several on-site restaurants. It sits directly on the Sea to Sky corridor, making it a natural and compelling detour for touring cyclists travelling between Vancouver and Whistler.

notes.Café or food on site: Multiple on-site dining venues listed: Sky Pilot Smokehouse, Co-Pilot Cafe, Edge Bar, Backyard Burgers, The Praguery, and Oceanview Grill at the summit

visitor.name: Chilliwack Community Forest
visitor.desc: The Chilliwack Community Forest is a 100-acre City-owned forest park developed in partnership with the Chilliwack Parks Society and the Fraser Valley Mountain Bike Association, providing public access to an otherwise closed urban forest. The multi-use trail network includes a 2.5km beginner-level loop and several moderate loops purpose-built for hiking, biking, and running. Its co-development with a dedicated mountain bike association signals genuine commitment to cycling-friendly infrastructure and trail quality.

visitor.name: CFBCHS Chilliwack Military Museum
visitor.desc: The Chilliwack Military Museum collects, preserves, and displays military artifacts connected to the former CFB Chilliwack, located in historic downtown Chilliwack. The museum maintains an extensive library of military history books available for loan, hosts guided group tours and veteran chats, and participates in joint exhibitions with other local museums. It is a not-for-profit registered society, and its Legacy Walk links the museum's collection to interpretive markers at the former garrison site.

visitor.name: Cowichan Bay Maritime Centre
visitor.desc: A non-profit maritime museum in the quirky seaside village of Cowichan Bay, operated by the Cowichan Wooden Boat Society since the late 1980s. Visitors walk a 100-meter heritage pier with themed exhibit pods covering Indigenous canoe history, interactive boat-building activities, and meticulously restored vintage motors. The centre also hosts an annual wooden boat festival and maintains an active wooden-boat workshop.

detail.address: 1761 Cowichan Bay Road, Cowichan Bay, V0R 1N0

visitor.name: Pebble Beach Reserve
visitor.desc: The Pebble Beach Reserve is a protected natural area on Galiano Island managed by the Galiano Conservancy Association, encompassing several kilometres of undeveloped shoreline, accessible pebble beaches, and a culturally significant archaeological site recognized by Hul'qumi'num-speaking peoples as Qw'xwulwis. District Lot 63 — the specific parcel recorded in OSM — is the subject of a long-running forest restoration project begun in 2001 to reverse the ecological damage of intensive mid-20th-century clear-cutting. The adjacent area includes one of the largest remaining stands of mature Coastal Douglas-fir forest on the island, making it a rewarding off-road detour for cyclists exploring the Gulf Islands.

visitor.name: Cowichan Garry Oak Preserve
visitor.desc: The Cowichan Garry Oak Preserve is a protected natural area near Duncan on Vancouver Island, managed by the Nature Conservancy of Canada. It safeguards Garry oak ecosystems, one of the most endangered habitat types in Canada, which are found in the Cowichan Valley and support a rich diversity of plants and wildlife. Touring cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley would find this a compelling stop to experience a rare and distinctive coastal BC landscape.

visitor.name: Artisans' Studio
visitor.desc: Artisans' Studio is a local artist co-operative and gift shop located in downtown Nanaimo, describing itself as having 'a global reach.' Housed at 70 Bastion Street, it offers original artwork and gifts from local artists in a gallery setting. A touring cyclist exploring Nanaimo's Old City Quarter could stop in to browse local art and pick up a unique souvenir.

visitor.name: Kimberley Heritage Museum
visitor.desc: The Kimberley Heritage Museum is a community heritage institution operated by the City of Kimberley in British Columbia's East Kootenay region. It is listed alongside the public library and arts centre as one of the city's core cultural offerings. Touring cyclists passing through Kimberley — a well-known destination near Kootenay Pass and the Rocky Mountain Trench — may find it a worthwhile stop to connect with the area's storied past.

visitor.name: Kaslo & District Public Library
visitor.desc: Kaslo & District Public Library is a public library serving the village of Kaslo and surrounding area on Kootenay Lake, offering physical collections, digital lending, computer access, and outreach programs. It functions as a community hub with accessible services and multilingual digital resources. For a touring cyclist passing through this small historic village, it represents one of the few spots offering free public services in town.

visitor.name: The Salt Spring Centre of Yoga
visitor.desc: The Salt Spring Centre of Yoga is BC's longest-running spiritual and wellness retreat centre, established in 1981 on 69 acres of protected Agricultural Land Reserve on Salt Spring Island. Founded by master yogi Baba Hari Dass, the non-profit centre offers yoga teacher training, multi-day silent and themed retreats, a working organic farm, and personal retreat stays in a serene rural setting. A cycling tourist exploring Salt Spring Island could find this a distinctive cultural and wellness destination, though it operates primarily as a reservation-based facility rather than a drop-in attraction.

detail.address: 355 Blackburn Road, Salt Spring Island, BC, Canada

visitor.name: Pacific Rim National Park Reserve of Canada - Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Pacific Rim National Park Reserve Visitor Centre is the main Parks Canada gateway to one of BC's most iconic stretches of coastline, spanning Long Beach, the West Coast Trail, and the Broken Group Islands. Operated by Parks Canada on the traditional territories of the Nuu-chah-nulth First Nations, it serves as the orientation hub for visitors exploring kilometres of sandy beaches and old-growth temperate rainforest. Touring cyclists riding the Pacific Rim Highway will find this a natural stopping point before or after riding the Long Beach area, which is explicitly listed as a cycling destination within the park.

visitor.name: Lynn Canyon Park Visitors Centre
visitor.desc: A nature education centre and museum set in North Vancouver's temperate rainforest at Lynn Canyon Park. The centre features interactive nature exhibits, a gift shop, park naturalists, and serves as the trailhead for the free Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge and surrounding hiking trails. Admission is by donation, and the park actively encourages visitors to arrive by bike or transit.

detail.address: 3663 Park Road, North Vancouver, British Columbia, V7J 3G3

notes.Café or food on site: Lynn Canyon Cafe is on site within the park, with stairs and elevator access

visitor.name: VPL: Kitsilano Branch
visitor.desc: The Kitsilano Branch of the Vancouver Public Library serves one of Vancouver's most cycling-friendly neighbourhoods, sitting close to the Arbutus Greenway and the beaches of English Bay. As a public library, it offers a quiet, free indoor space where touring cyclists can rest, connect, and recharge. It is operated by the Vancouver Public Library system, one of the busiest public library systems in Canada.

visitor.name: McPherson Playhouse
visitor.desc: McPherson Playhouse is a historic performing arts venue in the heart of downtown Victoria, operated alongside the Royal Theatre by the Royal & McPherson Theatres Society (RMTS). Located at Centennial Square on the corner of Government Street and Pandora Avenue, it has been hosting world-class entertainment for over a century. Touring cyclists passing through Victoria's walkable downtown core will find it a short ride from the Inner Harbour and surrounding amenities.

visitor.name: Kootenay Mountain Zipline
visitor.desc: Kokanee Mountain Zipline operates a six-line guided zipline tour above Kokanee Creek Canyon within Kokanee Creek Provincial Park, situated on 44 acres of old-growth Douglas fir and pine forest. The tour covers nearly a mile of ziplines with views stretching to Kootenay Lake and the Kokanee Glacier, and is billed as the original zipline company in the West Kootenay region. A touring cyclist looking for a half-day adventure detour near Nelson will find a fully guided, family-friendly experience with a strong safety and ecotourism focus.

visitor.name: ORL: Lake Country Branch
visitor.desc: The ORL Lake Country Branch is a public library in Lake Country, BC, part of the Okanagan Regional Library's 30-branch network serving over 399,000 people across the Okanagan and Shuswap regions. The branch offers meeting and study rooms, community programming, and free on-site parking with additional overflow parking at nearby Swalwell Park. Membership is free to residents, and the branch is a walkable community hub in the heart of Lake Country.

visitor.name: Lions Gate Community Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Lions Gate Community Recreation Centre is a modern municipal recreation facility operated by the North Vancouver Recreation & Culture Commission (NVRC) in the Lions Gate neighbourhood of the District of North Vancouver. It features a full gymnasium configurable for badminton, pickleball, volleyball, basketball, ball hockey, and futsal, along with rentable community rooms and a kitchen. Touring cyclists passing through North Vancouver's lower slopes may find it a convenient urban waypoint, though it is primarily a community facility rather than a destination attraction.

detail.address: 1733 Lions Gate Ln, North Vancouver, BC V7P 0C7

visitor.name: VIRL: Ucluelet Branch
visitor.desc: The Ucluelet Branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the community since 1971 and is now housed in the Ucluelet Community Centre, a LEED-certified recreational facility shared with a music hall, youth centre, and community rooms. The branch offers free public WiFi and public computer stations, making it a practical connectivity stop for touring cyclists passing through this remote stretch of Vancouver Island's west coast. With 24/7 book returns, the exterior of the building is accessible around the clock.

visitor.name: Slocan Community Library
visitor.desc: The Slocan Community Library is a small, 100% volunteer-run public library serving the village of Slocan in the Slocan Valley. It offers a curated book catalogue, DVDs, audio books, and a collection with a focus on Indigenous reads, making it a genuine community hub in a rural cycling corridor. Touring cyclists passing through Slocan may find it a useful rest point for local information, though hours are limited to four partial days per week.

visitor.name: Abbotsford Arts Centre
visitor.desc: The Abbotsford Arts Centre is a 700+ seat performing arts facility operated by the Abbotsford School District, equipped with full concert lighting, sound, and fly systems capable of supporting major productions. It hosts a diverse year-round calendar of theatre, dance, and cultural events serving local schools, touring productions, community groups, and the general public. The adjacent 3,150 sq. ft. Community Arts Addition seats an additional 260 and is available for banquets, receptions, and rehearsals.

visitor.name: City Centre Community Centre
visitor.desc: City Centre Community Centre is a publicly operated recreation facility run by the City of Richmond, located at 5900 Minoru Boulevard in the heart of Richmond. As part of Richmond's network of community centres, it offers programs and services to the local community. Touring cyclists passing through central Richmond may find it a useful stop, though specific cyclist-facing amenities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Museum Of North Vancouver
visitor.desc: MONOVA (Museum of North Vancouver) is a public history museum on the North Vancouver waterfront, a short walk from the Seabus terminal. Its permanent gallery explores the region's stories through artifacts and digital content across themes of place, industry, and Indigenous connections, including an upcoming Squamish Nation feature exhibit. The museum runs a robust slate of drop-in programs, guided gallery tours, and sensory-friendly events, making it a culturally rich stop on any North Shore cycling route.

detail.address: 115 West Esplanade, North Vancouver, BC V7M 0G7

visitor.name: The Dance Centre
visitor.desc: Established in 1986, The Dance Centre is BC's flagship dance facility and resource hub, supporting professional dance companies and individual artists through studios, a black box theatre, residency programs, and public performances. Located on Level 6 of a building in downtown Vancouver's Davie Street corridor, it presents a wide range of dance styles and hosts the provincial BC Dance Calendar and Directory. A touring cyclist with an interest in the performing arts could catch live dance performances or explore the publicly accessible common areas.

visitor.name: Miniature World
visitor.desc: Miniature World is a long-running indoor attraction located inside the iconic Fairmont Empress Hotel on Victoria's Inner Harbour, featuring over 85 detailed miniature dioramas spanning history, fantasy, and science fiction. Highlights include the world's smallest operational sawmill, one of the world's largest model railways depicting Canada's 1880s transcontinental rail build, and two enormous Victorian-era dollhouses with over 50 furnished rooms. Having operated for more than 50 years, it draws visitors of all ages and sits in one of downtown Victoria's most walkable and bikeable districts.

visitor.name: Town Centre Park Community Centre
visitor.desc: Town Centre Park Community Centre is a City of Coquitlam public facility overlooking Lafarge Lake, offering arts, culture, and nature programs for all ages. The building features an outdoor patio, lounge space, and the Praguery Café for coffee and snacks. Its prominent lakeside location makes it a natural waypoint on the Lafarge Lake trail loop in Coquitlam's Town Centre Park.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'The Praguery Café is now open. Drop by for a coffee or delicious treat!'

visitor.name: Penticton Museum
visitor.desc: The Penticton Museum & Archives is a free civic museum operated by the City of Penticton, situated in the heart of downtown along Main Street. It offers exhibits, family programs, museum tours, and archival resources exploring the history of the South Okanagan region. Touring cyclists passing through Penticton's downtown core will find it a no-cost cultural stop in a community renowned for its cycling routes.

visitor.name: University Farquhar Auditorium
visitor.desc: Farquhar Auditorium is a 1,200-seat soft-seat performing arts venue located at the heart of the University of Victoria campus. It hosts concerts, lectures, recitals, and professional recordings, drawing audiences from both the campus community and greater Victoria. Touring cyclists exploring Victoria's south end will find the leafy UVic campus itself scenic, with the Farquhar serving as a cultural anchor for events year-round.

visitor.name: Summit Centre Multiplex
visitor.desc: The Rinks at Summit Centre (formerly Apollo Multiplex Centre) is a multi-sheet ice arena in Abbotsford that has operated since 1999, hosting hockey leagues, figure skating, youth skills camps, and competitive tournaments. The facility is home to the Penalty Box Skate Shop and features LiveBarn streaming so fans can watch games remotely. Touring cyclists in the Fraser Valley area could visit as a spectator venue or to participate in adult drop-in hockey and public skating sessions.

visitor.name: The Hive
visitor.desc: The Hive is a multi-location indoor climbing gym chain with a Port Coquitlam outpost inside a village-style retail complex. It offers bouldering and roped climbing in a community-focused environment, making it a natural rest-day destination for cyclists touring the Tri-Cities area. Waivers are required for all visitors and can be signed online before arrival.

detail.address: Unit 145, 815 Village Drive, Port Coquitlam, BC V3B 0G9

visitor.name: Agi Hall
visitor.desc: Agi Hall is a community hall on Gabriola Island rebuilt in 1967 after a fire, operated by the Gabriola Agricultural Co-op. It hosts the weekly Growers and Makers Market showcasing local farmers and artisans, and is available for community rentals. A touring cyclist passing through Gabriola could time a visit to coincide with the Saturday market for fresh local produce and handmade goods.

visitor.name: Burnaby Lake Nature House
visitor.desc: The Burnaby Lake Nature House is a visitor centre operated by Metro Vancouver Regional Parks, located within Burnaby Lake Regional Park — a popular destination for cyclists riding the Burnaby Lake Loop trail network. It functions as a nature interpretive centre where visitors can learn about the lake's wetland ecosystem and wildlife. The park is a well-known recreational destination in the Metro Vancouver area, easily accessed by bicycle.

visitor.name: Italian Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: Il Centro has anchored Vancouver's Italian community since 1977, growing into a multi-faceted hub that houses a museum, a public library, Italian language school, and banquet halls used for weddings and major events. The on-site Osteria al Centro serves authentic Italian cuisine from pizza and pasta to aperitivi, and the centre hosts a year-round calendar of concerts, art exhibitions, and cultural festivals. With over 700 member families and programs open to all backgrounds, it is one of Vancouver's most distinctive neighbourhood cultural destinations.

notes.Café or food on site: Osteria al Centro is an on-site restaurant serving pizza, pasta, aperitivi, and Italian comfort food; catering menus also available for events

visitor.name: Archer Gallery
visitor.desc: Archer is the public art persona of Paul, a self-described international nomadic artist known for large-format murals painted on walls across Canada and beyond. His Facebook page shows striking works on brick, concrete, and other challenging surfaces — including a highly praised Marilyn Monroe mural in Victoria. Cyclists touring the region may encounter his murals in public spaces throughout BC and further afield.

visitor.name: Chilliwack Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: The Chilliwack Cultural Centre is the city's flagship arts venue, housing two performance theatres, the Odlum Brown Art Gallery, 21 music studios, and four arts and crafts studios on the territory of the Stó:lō Coast Salish People. Run by the Chilliwack Arts & Cultural Centre Society, it presents live performances, creative classes, and gallery exhibitions year-round, making it a significant cultural stop in the Fraser Valley. A touring cyclist passing through Chilliwack could take in a show, visit the gallery, or explore ongoing creative programming.

visitor.name: Tourism Kelowna Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: Tourism Kelowna Visitor Centre is the official tourism information office for Kelowna, BC, a UNESCO City of Gastronomy set in the Okanagan Valley. Positioned in downtown Kelowna, it serves as the regional gateway for visitors seeking guidance on wine touring, outdoor recreation, and local experiences across a destination the site describes as 'Canada's four-season playground.' For touring cyclists, it is a natural first stop for route advice, local maps, and orientation to the region's extensive cycling opportunities through vineyards and lake-side corridors.

visitor.name: Monkey C Interactive's Artcade
visitor.desc: Monkey C Interactive's Artcade is Victoria's award-winning interactive art playground featuring tech-retrofitted vintage machines filled with wild sounds, pulsating music, and blinking lights created by local composers, DJs, and visual artists. Run by artists David Parfit and Scott Amos since 2024, the venue presents an ever-evolving collection of sculptural installations designed to be touched, pressed, and played with by visitors of all ages. Located on Fort Street in Victoria's downtown core, it offers a genuinely unexpected cultural detour for cyclists exploring the city.

visitor.name: Scottish Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Victoria Scottish Community Centre is a multipurpose performing arts venue and Scottish cultural hub in the View Royal neighbourhood of Greater Victoria. Built by the Victoria Highland Games Association, it hosts community events, weddings, performances, and exhibitions. On its grounds sits Craigflower Manor, one of BC's oldest standing farmhouses (1853–1856), which offers guided tours exploring early colonial and Scottish heritage on Vancouver Island.

visitor.name: South Delta Artists Guild Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Gallery 1710 is a community art gallery run by the South Delta Artists Guild, a nonprofit founded in 1975, located just five minutes from the Tsawwassen ferry terminal off Highway 17. The gallery presents rotating monthly exhibitions of original works by local artists spanning watercolour, mixed media, and 3D art, with free admission. It sits at the gateway to the Tsawwassen dike cycling routes, making it a natural stop for cyclists arriving by ferry or exploring the South Delta farmlands.

visitor.name: Alvin Indridson Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: A 128-hectare nature reserve on Salt Spring Island managed by the Salt Spring Island Conservancy, encompassing Coastal Douglas-fir and Coastal Western Hemlock ecosystems alongside a 4-acre lake, streams, and small wetlands. The reserve supports at least 6 Species at Risk and offers public hiking trails accessed from Musgrave Road near Mt Tuam Road. It was donated by the estate of Alvin Indridson following his death in 2009, fulfilling his longstanding wish to preserve the land as parkland.

visitor.name: ORL: Peachland Branch
visitor.desc: The Peachland Branch of the Okanagan Regional Library is a publicly accessible branch of the 30-location ORL network, one of the 16th largest library systems in Canada, situated in the small lakeside community of Peachland on the western shore of Okanagan Lake. The branch is fully wheelchair accessible via ramp and offers public internet computers and wireless printing to anyone who visits. Free public parking is available at the adjacent Peachland Village Mall, making it a convenient stop along the Okanagan cycling corridor.

visitor.name: VIRL: Masset Branch
visitor.desc: The Masset Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library is a newly opened 3,870-square-foot public library developed in partnership with X̱aad Kíl Née and the Haida Language Office, featuring a dedicated Haida Language Immersion Lab. Situated on Haida Gwaii, the branch serves as a community hub for learning, cultural preservation, and engagement with Haida heritage. Touring cyclists passing through Masset will find a welcoming public space with meeting rooms and community resources.

visitor.name: Maple Grove Pool
visitor.desc: Maple Grove Pool is a seasonal outdoor public swimming pool in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, operated by the Vancouver Parks Board. Open only in the summer months, it serves the surrounding residential community and draws visitors to the area near the Fraser River foreshore trails. As a fee-based public facility, it offers a refreshing stop for cyclists exploring this part of the city.

visitor.name: Whistler Olympic Plaza
visitor.desc: Whistler Olympic Plaza is a public outdoor gathering space in Whistler tagged as a tourism attraction in OpenStreetMap. Based on its name, it is associated with Whistler's Olympic heritage and serves as a central community venue in the resort municipality. Touring cyclists passing through Whistler Village may find it a convenient stop given its public accessibility.

visitor.name: Sunshine Coast Arts Council
visitor.desc: The Sunshine Coast Arts Council (SCAC) is a volunteer-founded charitable society operating a unique log-constructed arts centre at the corner of Trail and Medusa in Sechelt, with two gallery spaces, a music and visual arts studio, and curated gardens. Founded in 1966, the centre has been a cultural anchor for the Sunshine Coast for over 50 years, hosting rotating exhibitions by regional artists, public programs, craft fairs, and youth art camps. A touring cyclist with an interest in local arts and culture would find an active, community-rooted gallery destination in the heart of Sechelt.

visitor.name: Whistler Bungee
visitor.desc: Whistler Bungee has operated since 2002 with a perfect safety record, offering 160ft (50m) jumps off a bridge over the glacial Cheakamus River. The site is surrounded by basalt column cliffs, old-growth forest, and views of Black Tusk, making it one of the most scenic bungee locations in the world. It sits just off the Sea to Sky Highway about 20 minutes south of Whistler Village, directly along a major cycling corridor, with free parking at the bridge.

detail.address: Calcheak Forest Service Rd, Whistler, BC, Canada

visitor.name: Glen Pine Pavilion
visitor.desc: Glen Pine Pavilion is a City of Coquitlam community centre open to adults 19 and over, with programming particularly oriented toward the 50+ demographic through the Glen Pine 50 Plus Society. It houses the Alpine Fitness Centre, a lending library, lounge, computer lab, and the Lemon Tree Café, all within a facility that also includes an outdoor plaza with picnic seating called Spirit Square. A touring cyclist would find it a potential rest stop with café access in the Port Coquitlam/Coquitlam area.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Food services (Lemon Tree Café)' as an on-site amenity

visitor.name: Ladner Fishermen's Hall
visitor.desc: The Ladner Fishermen's Hall is a heritage community centre dating to 1903, originally built as the Victoria Terminal Railway & Ferry Company Station and now listed on Canada's Historic Places registry. Operated by the Ladner Fishermen's Cooperative Association, it stands in the historic fishing village of Ladner, a charming detour for cyclists exploring the Fraser River delta. Its century-old character makes it a notable landmark on any bike tour through Delta.

visitor.name: ORL: Armstrong
visitor.desc: The Armstrong branch of the Okanagan Regional Library is part of a 30-branch regional system serving the North Okanagan's small agricultural city of Armstrong. The branch offers free public computer and internet access, two reservable meeting/study rooms, and free car parking directly in front of the building. Its accessible, single-level facility with automatic doors and a wheelchair ramp makes it a practical indoor rest stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

visitor.name: Old Growth Conservancy
visitor.desc: The Old Growth Conservancy is a 54-hectare protected forest at 760 metres elevation on West Vancouver's mountainside, containing western redcedars up to 900 years old that survived a golf course development threat in 1990. The Old Growth Conservancy Society runs free guided tours into the reserve's interior, including off-trail sections not normally open to the public, offering a rare encounter with one of BC's last remnants of ancient temperate rainforest. The society's board includes mountain bikers and hikers, and it collaborates with the North Shore Mountain Biking Association on trail access matters in adjacent areas.

visitor.name: Steffich Fine Art
visitor.desc: Steffich Fine Art is a curated contemporary gallery founded in 1992 on Salt Spring Island, now one of the Gulf Islands' most recognized cultural landmarks after more than three decades of operation. The gallery represents an eclectic roster including works by Norval Morrisseau, Robert Bateman, and Abraham Anghik Ruben, alongside a unique Rock & Roll Art collection of vintage Fillmore West concert posters and Canada's sole representation of kinetic wind sculptor Lyman Whitaker. Cyclists visiting Salt Spring Island will find this a distinctive stop in a community renowned for its outsized artistic output.

detail.address: 149 Fulford Ganges Road, Suite 101, Salt Spring Island, BC

visitor.name: Finnie's Garden
visitor.desc: Finnie's Garden is a named garden within the historic Riverview Lands arboretum in Coquitlam, BC, stewarded by the non-profit Riverview Horticultural Centre Society. The broader Riverview Lands encompass over 1,800 tagged heritage trees on a site established in 1904 as a therapeutically designed hospital campus and BC's first botanical garden. Entry to the grounds is free and publicly accessible, making it a quiet green stop for cyclists passing through the Coquitlam area.

visitor.name: Shawnigan Lake Museum
visitor.desc: A community history museum in Shawnigan Lake highlighting the area's rich past, including the story of the Kinsol Trestle and the famous landscape painter E.J. Hughes. Located along the Shawnigan Lake-Mill Bay corridor, it features exhibits on local First Nations heritage, pioneer history, and the railway era. The museum also operates a gift shop and hosts school programs and community events.

detail.address: 1775 Shawnigan Lake-Mill Bay Rd, Shawnigan Lake, BC V8H 3B7

visitor.name: Roundhouse Community Centre
visitor.desc: A historic roundhouse building in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, this is the city's only combined arts and recreation centre. It houses Engine 374, the first transcontinental passenger train to arrive in Vancouver, and offers a wide range of programs, exhibitions, and community events. The converted brick industrial building has been a community landmark since the late 1980s.

visitor.name: UBC Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The UBC Aquatic Centre is a LEED Gold-certified facility on the UBC Vancouver campus housing a 50m competition pool, 25m recreational pool, leisure pool with lazy river, hot tub, steam room, and sauna. The facility serves athletic training, competition, and neighbourhood leisure needs, accommodating nearly 1,000 bathers with spectator seating for 460. It is notable for its sustainability design, saving approximately 2.7 million litres of water annually through rainwater harvesting.

notes.Café or food on site: Food and beverage kiosk listed under facility amenities
notes.Luggage / bag storage: Term locker rentals and day lockers listed under facility amenities

visitor.name: Hudson's Hope Museum
visitor.desc: Hudson's Hope Museum tells the story of the Peace River Valley from ancient dinosaurs through the fur trade era to modern times, including the construction of the W.A.C. Bennett Dam. Situated on the edge of the Peace River in a small town of about 1,100 people, the museum features historical displays, heritage cabins, and guided programs. A gift shop offers local books, handmade crafts, and regional edibles, making it a worthwhile cultural stop on a northeastern BC cycling route.

detail.address: 9510 Beattie Drive, Hudson's Hope, BC V0C 1V0

visitor.name: Galiano Island Community Library
visitor.desc: The Galiano Island Community Library is a small volunteer-supported public library on Galiano Island, part of the Southern Gulf Islands Community Libraries consortium. Located near Sturdies Bay — the main ferry terminal — it serves as a community hub offering books, digital resources, and internet access. For touring cyclists arriving by ferry, it is one of the few publicly accessible facilities close to the landing point.

visitor.name: Nelson & District Community Complex
visitor.desc: The Civic Centre Arena is Nelson's community ice facility, home to ice hockey and public skating in the heart of downtown. Operated by the Regional District of Central Kootenay, it serves as a hub for local recreation. Touring cyclists passing through Nelson may find it a useful landmark near the downtown core.

visitor.name: Canadian Indigenous Art
visitor.desc: Canadian Indigenous Art Inc. is a gallery dedicated to promoting the artwork of Coast Salish and Squamish Nation artists, offering one of the largest collections of West Coast Indigenous and Aboriginal art in Canada. Founded in 1999 by collector Maike Marnet, who spent over thirty years building relationships with local Indigenous artists, the gallery carries original paintings, wood carvings, masks, totem poles, sculptures, and jewellery. The Nanaimo gallery recently relocated to 78 Wharf St., a waterfront address that makes it a natural stop for cyclists exploring downtown Nanaimo.

visitor.name: GVPL: Saanich Centennial Library Branch
visitor.desc: The GVPL Saanich Centennial Library Branch is part of the Greater Victoria Public Library system, which operates branches across the greater Victoria region on southern Vancouver Island. Public libraries offer a quiet, climate-controlled environment with public computers and programming open to all visitors. This branch is wheelchair accessible and serves the broader Saanich community.

visitor.name: Vernon Museum & Archives
visitor.desc: The Museum & Archives of Vernon (MAV) is a not-for-profit community institution tracing Greater Vernon's history from Indigenous heritage through settler times, housed in a civic complex that opened in 1966. It operates permanent, temporary, and virtual exhibits alongside one of the most respected archival research facilities in BC. Touring cyclists visiting Vernon will find rotating thematic exhibits, historical programming, and a connection to the region's deep Syilx and Okanagan Nation roots.

visitor.name: Oliver Tourism Association
visitor.desc: The Oliver Tourism Association operates the official visitor centre for Oliver, BC, branded as 'Canada's Wine Capital' and producing fifty percent of BC's wine grapes. Located on Station Street, it serves as the primary trip-planning hub for the South Okanagan, covering wine tours along the Golden Mile and Black Sage Road as well as outdoor recreation including cycling, hiking, and golf. For a touring cyclist, it is a logical first stop for local route information, winery directories, and U-pick fruit stand listings.

visitor.name: Ladner Community Centre
visitor.desc: Ladner Community Centre is a two-storey municipal recreation facility operated by the City of Delta, located in the Ladner neighbourhood. It offers fitness programs, recreation activities, and community services. Touring cyclists passing through the flat farmland of south Delta will find it a convenient public facility with washrooms.

visitor.name: Garden Railway
visitor.desc: The Garden Railway is a free outdoor model train display within the Burnaby Central Railway park, operated by the British Columbia Society of Model Engineers. Opened permanently in July 2018, it features G gauge (45mm) and O gauge (32mm) scale trains — some battery powered, some electric, and some live steam — running on a track with bridges and gradients. When volunteers are present for an operating session, visitors can watch the miniature trains run up close, making it a quirky and charming stop for touring cyclists passing through Burnaby.

detail.address: 120 North Willingdon Avenue, Burnaby, BC V5C 6K1

visitor.name: Deer Lake Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Deer Lake Gallery (DLG) is a contemporary art house operated by the Burnaby Arts Council within the cultural campus of Deer Lake Park, Burnaby. Founded to support emerging and established artists, it hosts 10–12 exhibitions per year featuring thought-provoking and experimental work from local and regional artists. Touring cyclists riding through Burnaby's scenic Deer Lake area will find a free cultural stop with rotating shows just steps from the park's trails.

detail.address: 6584 Deer Lake Ave, Burnaby, BC V5G 3T7

visitor.name: Cranbrook Public Library
visitor.desc: Cranbrook Public Library is a full-service public library in downtown Cranbrook offering a broad range of collections, digital resources, and an Idea Lab equipped with a 3D printer, recording studio, digitization station, and other creative technology. It hosts regular community programs and events for all ages and provides meeting room rentals. For a touring cyclist, it is a welcoming downtown public space to access local information, rest indoors, and connect digitally.

visitor.name: Kal Tire Place
visitor.desc: Kal Tire Place (listed in OSM as Kal Tire Arena) is Vernon's primary multi-use indoor sports facility, hosting ice hockey and lacrosse on its main ice surface. Operated by the City of Vernon, it is the home venue for local competitive hockey leagues and occasional regional events. A touring cyclist passing through Vernon is unlikely to visit as a destination, though the arena sits within the city's broader recreation complex.

visitor.name: Penticton Memorial Arena
visitor.desc: Penticton Memorial Arena is a community sports facility and heritage-listed building in Penticton, BC, historically home to ice hockey and lacrosse. Its inclusion on the City of Penticton Heritage Registry reflects its significance as a civic landmark in the South Okanagan. Touring cyclists passing through Penticton may recognize it as a local landmark, though it functions primarily as a spectator and participant sports venue.

visitor.name: Community Peace Garden
visitor.desc: A permaculture demonstration garden on the Vancouver Island University Nanaimo campus, located on the north side of the campus library. Founded in 2008 as the Community Peace Garden and now run by the VIU Permaculture Club, it serves as a space for learning about food growing, seed saving, plant medicine, and traditional ecological knowledge. The garden is designed to be as accessible as possible to the public.

visitor.name: Whistler Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Whistler Visitor Centre is Tourism Whistler's official in-resort information office, located at 4230 Gateway Drive beside the village bus and taxi loop. Staff help visitors with accommodation bookings, Whistler Transit schedules, activity planning, and BC-wide travel information, and a mobile live chat service extends that assistance beyond the building. Touring cyclists will find it a practical first stop for free maps, local insider knowledge, and transit connections into or out of the valley.

visitor.name: Winfield Arena
visitor.desc: Winfield Arena is a municipal ice facility operated by the District of Lake Country, serving the community with public skating sessions, recreational hockey programs, and ice rentals for youth, families, and adults. It is a seasonal community hub with free public skating on select evenings. The arena sits in Lake Country, a region known for its wine trails and recreational cycling routes around Wood Lake and Kalamalka Lake.

detail.address: 9830 Bottom Wood Lake Road, Lake Country, V4V 1T1

visitor.name: Langley Events Centre
