visitor.desc: salishan Place by the River is a new 40,000-square-foot arts, culture and heritage centre in Fort Langley, developed in partnership with Coast Salish First Nations and housing a museum, library, printmaking studio, coffee shop, Indigenous Garden, and outdoor amphitheatre. The three-storey civic building holds a collection of over 23,000 objects documenting the region's history and offers conference, gallery, and community event spaces. Fort Langley is a well-travelled cycling destination on regional trails, making this a natural cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Township of Langley.

detail.address: 23430 Mavis Avenue, Township of Langley, V1M 2S2

notes.Café or food on site: Website FAQ lists 'coffee shop, gift shop' as part of the facility alongside museum and studio spaces

visitor.name: Rutland Community Center
visitor.desc: Rutland Community Center is a publicly accessible sports and recreation facility in the Rutland neighbourhood of Kelowna, BC. The facility is operated under the City of Kelowna and, based on the associated URL, appears to encompass an arena and recreation park. It would serve as a practical rest or refill stop for cyclists touring the eastern Kelowna area.

visitor.name: VIRL: Quadra Island Branch
visitor.desc: The Quadra Island branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the Quathiaski Cove community since 1988, situated on the unceded traditional territory of the Wei Wai Kai First Nation. It is part of a large regional public library system spanning Vancouver Island and adjacent islands, and is currently undergoing an expansion to improve services. For a touring cyclist arriving by ferry to Quadra Island, this public library offers free Wi-Fi and a welcoming community space.

visitor.name: Oaklands Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Oaklands Community Association is a neighbourhood association serving the Oaklands area of Victoria, bounded by Cook Street, Haultain Street, Shelbourne Street, and North Dairy Road. It operates from three locations — Oaklands Community Centre, Oaklands Neighbourhood House, and Hamilton Park — offering recreation programs, child care, a community garden, food security initiatives, and a seasonal Wednesday evening Sunset Market. The association is community-run and membership-based, with a broad range of programs for all ages.

visitor.name: Freeman King Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Freeman King Visitor Centre is the interpretive hub of Goldstream Provincial Park, just 16 km from downtown Victoria on the Trans-Canada Highway. Park naturalists offer programs and lectures on the area's natural history, from 600-year-old Douglas fir and western red cedar to the dramatic annual chum salmon spawning run that draws bald eagles and thousands of visitors each autumn. The park's trail network—ranging from easy, wheelchair-accessible riverside walks to the summit of Mount Finlayson—makes this a compelling and scenic detour for touring cyclists moving through southern Vancouver Island.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states: 'For your convenience during the summer season, this park has a small concession managed by the park operator.'

visitor.name: Studio Bauer
visitor.desc: Studio Bauer is the gallery and studio of Victoria-based visual artist Craig Bauer, presenting and selling original fine art works. The gallery operates from level 1 of its Victoria location, offering an intimate, artist-run experience distinct from larger commercial galleries. For cyclists exploring Victoria's arts scene, it represents a small independent stop where one can engage directly with a working artist's practice.

visitor.name: Ruby Creek Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Ruby Creek Art Gallery is an Indigenous-owned gallery on the scenic Lougheed Highway (Hwy 7) between Agassiz and Hope, proudly operated by the Sq'ewá:lxw First Nation since 2005. It showcases an extensive collection of handcrafted Coast Salish artwork including carvings, masks, drums, limited-edition prints, gold and silver jewellery, and textiles by both emerging and established First Nations artists. For touring cyclists riding the Fraser Valley corridor, it offers a culturally rich roadside stop with an online shop for those who want to browse before visiting.

visitor.name: British Columbia Regimental Museum
visitor.desc: The BCR Museum Society has operated this regimental museum since 1982, preserving the history of the BC Regiment (Duke of Connaught's Own) through uniforms on mannequins, World War One and Two weapons displays, and artefacts from the 6th Duke of Connaught's Own Rifles era. Run entirely by dedicated volunteers, the collection includes items on long-term loan alongside pieces owned outright by the society. It sits within the historic Beatty Street Drill Hall, one of Vancouver's oldest military landmarks.

visitor.name: Whistler Public Library
visitor.desc: The Whistler Public Library is a LEED Gold certified 12,000-square-foot public facility that has anchored the Whistler community since 1986 and is celebrating its 40th anniversary in 2026. Located centrally on Main Street in Whistler Village, it offers an impressive range of programs and creative spaces including a Wonder Lab, Creation Station, Digitization Station, Green Screen, and Sound Booth. Touring cyclists will find a welcoming, fully accessible public space steps from the village core.

visitor.name: Salt Spring Island Public Library
visitor.desc: A modern public library in Ganges village on Salt Spring Island, featuring an Indigenous Learning Area with names gifted by local Language Keepers, a FabLab Makerspace with assistive device program, and a pop-up recording studio. For touring cyclists arriving via BC Ferries, it offers a free, air-conditioned rest stop with computers, printing services, and community information about the island.

detail.address: 129 McPhillips Ave, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2T6

visitor.name: Ron Basford Park Amphitheatre
visitor.desc: Ron Basford Park Amphitheatre is a free outdoor amphitheatre within Ron Basford Park on Granville Island, one of Vancouver's most celebrated public spaces and a natural stop on the False Creek seawall cycling route. Managed by CMHC on behalf of the Government of Canada, Granville Island draws millions of visitors annually with its mix of markets, artisan studios, theatres, and waterfront atmosphere. The open-air amphitheatre sits at the heart of this pedestrian and cycling-friendly district.

visitor.name: Action BMX
visitor.desc: Action BMX is a CCC/UCI-affiliated BMX racing club in the Surrey/Richmond area of British Columbia with over 1,500 members. It operates as a competitive racing club on a weekly schedule, making it a notable stop for cyclists interested in BMX culture and racing. The club's Facebook group is active and serves as the primary public-facing presence.

visitor.name: Richmond Public Library, Steveston Branch (Easthope Hub)
visitor.desc: The Steveston Branch of Richmond Public Library, also known as the Easthope Hub, is located in historic Steveston Village—a popular destination for cyclists exploring Richmond's extensive dyke trail network and heritage waterfront. As part of the Richmond Public Library system, it provides a welcoming public space with digital resources, community programming, and creation technology including 3D printers and Cricut machines. Cyclists passing through Steveston will find it a convenient mid-ride stop with free internet access and public washrooms.

visitor.name: Don Bosco Youth Centre
visitor.desc: Don Bosco Youth Centre is a Catholic parish-run community centre operated by Our Lady of Good Counsel Parish, with a strong local presence evidenced by over 2,100 Facebook check-ins. It functions as a gathering place for youth and community programming in the Surrey/North Vancouver area. A touring cyclist passing through the neighbourhood may find it a recognisable landmark and potential rest point.

visitor.name: Chehalis River Hatchery
visitor.desc: The Chehalis River Hatchery, also known as the Chehalis River Salmonid Enhancement Facility, is a federally operated fish hatchery run by Fisheries and Oceans Canada's Salmonid Enhancement Program since 1982. Situated on Morris Valley Road in the Fraser Valley near Chilliwack, it focuses on rebuilding vulnerable Pacific salmon stocks in the Chehalis watershed. For a touring cyclist, it represents a working conservation facility that may offer interpretive interest as a roadside stop along rural Morris Valley Road.

visitor.name: Or Gallery
visitor.desc: Or Gallery is a non-profit artist-run centre founded in 1983, known for championing emerging, conceptual, and experimental contemporary art by local, national, and international artists. The gallery has presented formative exhibitions by major figures in Canadian contemporary art including Stan Douglas, Jeff Wall, and Brian Jungen, and operates an onsite bookstore for publications and artist editions. Located in Vancouver's East End, it also hosts public events, artist talks, and community programming.

visitor.name: VIRL: Sandspit Branch
visitor.desc: The Sandspit Branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has been part of this remote Haida Gwaii community since the early 1980s, moving to its current Beach Road location in 1987. Situated on the traditional territory of the Haida Nation, the branch is wheelchair accessible and offers free public WiFi with two public computers — a meaningful connectivity stop for touring cyclists in an area with limited services. Its collection of nearly 4,500 items reflects its role as a genuine community hub rather than a token outpost.

visitor.name: Myra Canyon Bicycle Rental and Tours Inc.
visitor.desc: Myra Canyon Bicycle Rental and Tours Inc. is the first and only on-site bike rental company at the Myra Station trailhead of the Kettle Valley Railway's Myra Canyon section, roughly 40 minutes from downtown Kelowna. Cyclists can explore 18 historic wooden trestles and two tunnels on a flat, 12 km (one-way) trail that draws over 75,000 visitors a year. The family-operated business, recognized as a Biosphere Committed Entity for Tourism Sustainability, offers comfort bikes, e-bikes, guided half-day tours, a full-day self-guided Kelowna-to-Penticton option, and adaptive cycling coordination through People in Motion.

detail.address: Myra Station Parking, Kelowna, BC, Canada

notes.Café or food on site: FAQ confirms 'a small concession stand at the Myra Station parking lot with water, Clif bars, and souvenirs'; homepage also mentions 'bottled water and snacks' and 'ponchos for those rainy days.'

visitor.name: Okanagan Mission (Pandosy's Farm)
visitor.desc: Father Pandosy Mission is Kelowna's oldest European settlement — a historic site preserving the region's first European land claim, school, church, and large-scale agricultural operation. Original pioneer buildings and artifacts from multiple eras are scattered across a park-like property that draws 7,000–10,000 visitors annually from around the world. Touring cyclists exploring the south Kelowna area can stop here for a self-guided walk through the earliest chapter of the Okanagan's agricultural heritage.

visitor.name: Kariton Art Gallery
visitor.desc: An outdoor performance stage at the Kariton complex in Abbotsford, operated by the Abbotsford Arts Council. The adjacent Kariton Art Gallery hosts rotating exhibitions and a gift shop featuring handmade items from Fraser Valley artisans — jewellery, pottery, fabric arts, and woodwork. The gallery sits near Mill Lake, a pleasant stop along Abbotsford's urban trail network.

visitor.name: Port Moody Arts Centre (Old City Hall)
visitor.desc: A community arts centre and Port Moody's official Visitor Centre, housed in the historic Old City Hall building in the heart of the city. It offers a contemporary art gallery with rotating exhibitions, a co-op gift shop featuring local artists' work, and over 350 arts classes annually. For touring cyclists passing through Port Moody, it doubles as a visitor information stop where staff can point you to local businesses and attractions.

detail.address: 2425 St. Johns Street, Port Moody, BC, V3H 2B2

visitor.name: FVRL: Chilliwack Library
visitor.desc: The Chilliwack Library is part of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, the largest public library network in British Columbia, serving over 800,000 people across 25 community locations. As a public library, it offers free access to computers, printing, and Wi-Fi, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists needing to connect, plan a route, or take shelter. The branch is centrally located in downtown Chilliwack, making it a convenient waypoint along the Fraser Valley cycling corridor.

visitor.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: VanDusen Botanical Garden is a 55-acre urban oasis in the heart of Vancouver featuring over 7,500 plant species and varieties from around the world. The Visitor Centre serves as the gateway to the garden's extensive programming — botanical illustration courses, public art, family events, and guided tours — and houses The Garden Café with its panoramic views of the surrounding flora. Touring cyclists will find a well-rounded destination in a lush green setting, accessible via Oak Street in the Oakridge neighbourhood.

notes.Café or food on site: The Garden Café is located inside the Visitor Centre and offers Fair Trade coffees, handcrafted beverages, sandwiches, soups, curries, and daily-changing entrees; the Shaughnessy Restaurant (fine dining, West Coast menu) is also on the garden grounds

visitor.name: Harrison Hot Springs Visitor Centre & Sasquatch Museum
visitor.desc: Tourism Harrison Hot Springs is the official visitor information office for the Harrison River Valley, a region encompassing Harrison Hot Springs, Agassiz, Harrison Mills, and surrounding communities. The office serves as a gateway for exploring the area's mix of outdoor adventure, hot springs, agricultural landscapes, and Indigenous cultural heritage. Touring cyclists passing through can expect access to regional maps, itineraries, trails and routes information, and accessibility resources.

detail.address: 499 Hot Springs Road, Harrison Hot Springs, V0M 1K0

visitor.name: VIRL: Hornby Island Branch
visitor.desc: The Hornby Island branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library sits in a picturesque forested setting at the New Horizons Centre, serving this small Gulf Island community since before its 2016 renovation. As a free public facility on an island popular with cyclists, it offers public computers and free WiFi — practical resources for a touring cyclist needing to check routes, communicate, or simply rest indoors. The branch is operated by Vancouver Island Regional Library, one of the largest public library systems in BC.

visitor.name: Rainbow Lodge historic cabins
visitor.desc: Rainbow Lodge historic cabins is a heritage attraction in Whistler's Rainbow Park, documented in Wikipedia (en:Rainbow Lodge) and significant enough to hold a Wikidata entry, indicating it is among the more historically notable sites in the Sea-to-Sky corridor. The site is managed by the Resort Municipality of Whistler and sits within the broader Rainbow Park area near Alta Lake. A touring cyclist visiting Whistler would encounter it as a cultural waypoint rather than a service stop.

visitor.name: West Vancouver Memorial Library
visitor.desc: The West Vancouver Memorial Library is a national and international award-winning public library, opened November 11, 1950 as a living War Memorial dedicated to those who served in the Second World War. Situated in the Ambleside neighbourhood directly across from Memorial Park and steps from the waterfront, it offers an art gallery, live music events, technology programs, and extensive research databases. For touring cyclists passing through West Vancouver, it represents a well-located community hub in a scenic seaside neighbourhood.

visitor.name: Victoria City Hall - siʔem tawen'ewtxw
visitor.desc: Victoria City Hall is a National Historic Site of Canada, a Victorian-era civic landmark anchoring Centennial Square in the heart of downtown Victoria. Known in the WSÁNEĆ language as siʔem tawen'ewtxw, the building reflects the city's commitment to reconciliation alongside its heritage architecture. Cyclists exploring downtown Victoria will find it centrally located near major cycling routes and tourist corridors.

visitor.name: Dominion Brook Park
visitor.desc: Sam's Garden (also referred to as the Sunken Garden) is a named feature within Dominion Brook Park, a 10-acre heritage arboretum and ornamental garden on the Saanich Peninsula created in 1913 by the Canadian Department of Agriculture. The park holds a remarkable collection of mature conifers and ornamental shrubs sourced from nurseries in Britain, France, Japan, and elsewhere, including specimens descended from seed collected in Western China by the renowned plant hunter Ernest 'Chinese' Wilson. Maintained by a volunteer society since 2001, the park is freely open to the public and offers guided tours by arrangement.

detail.address: 8801 East Saanich Road, North Saanich, BC

visitor.name: FVRL: Maple Ridge Public Library
visitor.desc: The Maple Ridge Public Library is a branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, serving the Maple Ridge community with a full range of lending, digital, and programming services. It is a publicly accessible civic facility located in a unit at 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road in central Maple Ridge. Touring cyclists may find it a useful urban stop for rest and connectivity, though specific cycling amenities are unconfirmed.

detail.address: 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, Maple Ridge, BC V2X 5Z6

visitor.name: Port Coquitlam Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Port Coquitlam Community Centre is a municipally operated recreation complex serving the City of Port Coquitlam. The broader city recreation network includes aquatics, skating, fitness, and arts programming, making this a multi-use destination for residents and visitors alike. For touring cyclists, it sits in a community with dedicated cycling infrastructure including the Traboulay PoCo Trail.

visitor.name: Vancouver Island Military Museum
visitor.desc: The Vancouver Island Military Museum bills itself as British Columbia's most significant military museum, housing more than 25 exhibits tracing Canadian military involvement from the War of 1812 through to Afghanistan, including coverage of women in the armed forces and the HMCS Nanaimo. The museum is situated in downtown Nanaimo's waterfront precinct, within walking distance of the Inner Harbour Boat Basin, Port Theatre, and the cruise ship facility — a handy stop for cyclists exploring the harbour area. Admission is by donation-scale fees with free entry for veterans and serving members.

visitor.name: Kensington Community Centre & Pool
visitor.desc: Kensington Community Centre & Pool is a City of Vancouver civic facility serving the Kensington-Cedar Cottage neighbourhood. The centre includes an aquatic facility, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists seeking washrooms or a swim. As a publicly operated recreation centre, it is open to drop-in visitors from the general public.

visitor.name: Castlegar and District Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Castlegar & District Community Complex is a public recreation facility operated by the Regional District of Central Kootenay, offering ice hockey and fitness amenities to residents and visitors. Situated in Castlegar in the West Kootenay region, the complex serves a broad community catchment and is the primary indoor recreation hub for the area. Touring cyclists passing through Castlegar may find it a useful stop, though specific cyclist services are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Chemainus Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Chemainus Visitor Centre is the official tourism information office for the Chemainus and District area, operated by the Chemainus + District Chamber of Commerce. Chemainus is widely known as 'The Little Town That Did,' famous for its large-scale outdoor murals depicting local history. A touring cyclist stopping here can expect local maps, route suggestions, and area information from knowledgeable staff.

visitor.name: VIRL: Sointula Branch
visitor.desc: The Sointula Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library is a small public library serving the community of Sointula on Malcolm Island, accessible only by BC Ferries from Port McNeill. Opened in 1990 and renovated in 2003, it features a cozy reading nook and is part of the broader VIRL network spanning Vancouver Island and the central BC coast. For cyclists touring this remote island, it offers a quiet public space with free WiFi and public computers.

visitor.name: Yale Historic Site
visitor.desc: Yale Historic Site is a multi-building heritage museum in the small Fraser Canyon town of Yale, where Indigenous, Chinese, and settler histories converge at a place that was pivotal to British Columbia's Gold Rush and path to Confederation. The site encompasses historic structures including Creighton House Museum, St. John the Divine Church, and the Ward House, and is managed by the Forager Foundation. Touring cyclists riding the Fraser Canyon corridor will find immersive exhibits, guided tours narrated by local community experts, and a living sense of one of BC's most storied boomtowns.

visitor.name: The Columbia
visitor.desc: The Columbia is a heritage performance and event venue built in 1927 in downtown New Westminster, BC. Listed as a historic building, it has operated for nearly a century as a community theatre and continues to host live events. A touring cyclist passing through New Westminster's historic downtown core would find it a notable cultural landmark on Columbia Street.

detail.address: 530 Columbia Street, New Westminster, BC V3L 1B1

visitor.name: Arts Pacific Gallery
visitor.desc: Arts Pacific Gallery is a community collective of Bowen Island artists, operating since 1998 in Artisan Square and showcasing original paintings, sculpture, ceramics, handknits, fibre arts, and jewellery by over a dozen local artists. Described on its own website as a 'small-town art gallery well worth the visit,' it has been a favourite destination for tourists exploring Bowen Island's creative community for nearly three decades.

detail.address: 455 Bowen Island Trunk Rd, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G1

visitor.name: ORL: Vernon Branch
visitor.desc: The Vernon Branch of the Okanagan Regional Library is a full-service public branch within a 30-branch regional system covering 59,600 square kilometres of BC's interior. The branch is unusually well-equipped for a public library, featuring a makerspace with 3D printers, an audio recording studio, digitization stations, a sewing machine, and a Cricut cutter. It also offers exam invigilation and a range of community programming, making it a substantive stop for a touring cyclist needing connectivity, rest, or creative tools.

visitor.name: Cowichan Valley Museum
visitor.desc: Housed in the beautifully preserved 1912 E&N Duncan Train Station, the Cowichan Valley Museum and Archives sits in the picturesque Charles Hoey V.C. Memorial Park, surrounded by totem poles and gardens in the heart of Duncan. Operated by the Cowichan Historical Society since 1974, the museum offers curated artifact displays tracing the valley's history from Indigenous heritage to Duncan's origins as a 19th-century railway crossing. Admission is by donation, making it a welcoming cultural stop on any Cowichan Valley cycling itinerary.

visitor.name: Grafton Agricultural Commons
visitor.desc: Grafton Agricultural Commons, also known as Grafton Gardens, is a community garden operated by the Bowen Island Food Resilience Society, a local organization focused on food security and sustainable agriculture. The site is freely accessible to the public with no entry fee, making it a pleasant stop for cyclists passing through the area. As a working community garden, it offers a glimpse into local food production and community life.

visitor.name: Castlegar & District Recreation & Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Castlegar and District Aquatic Centre is a publicly operated swimming and recreation facility in the Regional District of Central Kootenay. It features a hot tub and steam room alongside its aquatic programming, making it a potential rest and recovery stop for touring cyclists passing through the Castlegar area. The facility is part of a broader community complex managed by the RDCK.

visitor.name: VPL: Hastings Branch
visitor.desc: The Hastings Branch is one of the Vancouver Public Library's neighbourhood branches, serving the East Hastings corridor in East Vancouver. As a public library, it offers free access to books, computers, and community programs to all visitors. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a useful rest stop in a busy urban neighbourhood.

visitor.name: Rogers Rink
visitor.desc: Rogers Rink is a major multi-arena sports and events complex in Salmon Arm featuring two NHL-regulation ice surfaces, including the Newnes Spectator Arena with seating for 1,500 and Hucul Pond with seating for 300. The facility hosts hockey, ringette, speed skating, figure skating, lacrosse, trade shows, concerts, and large conventions year-round. A touring cyclist passing through Salmon Arm might visit for a public skating session or a community event.

detail.address: 2600 10 Avenue NE, Salmon Arm, BC V1E 4N2

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Concession' as a facility feature and notes 'Two large concession stands are located along the concourse'

visitor.name: White Rock Museum & Archives
visitor.desc: The White Rock Museum & Archives occupies a heritage train station right on the beach at Semiahmoo Bay, placing it squarely on Marine Drive — a scenic waterfront route popular with cyclists. It holds rotating exhibitions on local and First Nations history alongside a substantial archival collection spanning newspapers from 1940–1973. Admission is by donation, and guided walking tours of the beach, pier, and train station are offered by appointment.

detail.address: 14970 Marine Dr, White Rock, BC V4B 1C4

visitor.name: The Western Front
visitor.desc: Western Front is a non-profit artist-run centre founded in 1973 in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, housed in a distinctive three-story heritage building with green wooden siding and a pioneer-like false-front façade. It supports multidisciplinary programming spanning music, media art, visual art, performance, and literature, and maintains a growing audiovisual archive documenting decades of artistic production. Touring cyclists can lock bikes at racks directly in front of the building, with a Mobi bike-share station on the adjacent corner.

visitor.name: Vernon Public Art Gallery
visitor.desc: The Vernon Public Art Gallery is the oldest and largest public art gallery in the North Okanagan, with over 60 years of community history and approximately 20 rotating exhibitions per year featuring emerging, mid-career, and established artists working in painting, sculpture, video, and installation art. Located on the ground level of the Vernon Parkade, VPAG is a recognized hub for cultural tourism in the Okanagan and offers a Gallery Shop and Art Rental Program alongside its exhibition programming. Admission is by donation, making it a low-barrier cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through Vernon.

detail.address: 3228-31st Ave, Vernon, British Columbia VIT 2H3, Canada

visitor.name: Cheam Wetlands Regional Park
visitor.desc: Cheam Lake Wetlands Regional Park is a Fraser Valley Regional District nature reserve near Rosedale, sitting in the floodplain below Cheam Peak. The wetlands support rich birdlife and offer a peaceful contrast to the nearby Trans-Canada Highway cycling corridor. For touring cyclists, it makes a worthwhile detour off the Chilliwack valley routes into quiet, flat terrain.

visitor.name: John Braithwaite Community Centre
visitor.desc: John Braithwaite Community Centre is a public recreation facility operated by the North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission, situated in the Lower Lonsdale neighbourhood of North Vancouver. It houses a fitness centre with weight and cardio equipment, a multi-sport gymnasium supporting badminton, basketball, pickleball, volleyball, indoor soccer, and ball hockey, plus art and woodworking studios. Touring cyclists exploring the North Shore would find it a well-equipped community hub in a central, walkable district.

detail.address: 145 West 1st St, North Vancouver, BC V7M 1B1

visitor.name: Two Rivers Gallery
visitor.desc: Two Rivers Gallery is a public art gallery situated on the traditional and unceded territory of the Lheidli T'enneh, dedicated to contemporary Canadian art and lifelong learning through the arts in Prince George and the Central Interior. The gallery hosts rotating exhibitions, artist programs, and a shop featuring work by artists and artisans from Western Canada. It is a significant cultural landmark in northern BC and a worthwhile stop for cyclists touring through Prince George.

detail.address: 725 Canada Games Way, Prince George, V2L 5T1

visitor.name: Doukhobor Discovery Centre
visitor.desc: A heritage museum celebrating Doukhobor life in BC's southern interior from 1908 to 1938, spread across ten historical buildings on ten acres of land. Features over 1,600 donated artifacts, audio/visual galleries, interactive displays, a gift shop with traditional Doukhobor crafts, and guided tours. Located just off Highway 3 in Castlegar, it makes a worthwhile cultural stop for cyclists passing through the Kootenays.

notes.Café or food on site: Village Bistro (currently closed for renovations) and Village Market listed as on-site facilities

visitor.name: Earthwise Society Garden and Farm
visitor.desc: Earthwise Society is a not-for-profit charitable organization operating a demonstration garden and teaching farm near Boundary Bay in South Delta, focused on environmental education, regenerative agriculture, and community food security. The site features demonstration gardens, a nursery, and teaching programs including therapeutic horticulture and ecotours. Cyclists exploring the Boundary Bay and Tsawwassen area will find it a peaceful and educational stop in a scenic agricultural setting.

visitor.name: FVRL: White Rock Library
visitor.desc: The White Rock Library is a public branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, housed in a government building on Buena Vista Avenue near the heart of White Rock. It offers a full range of library services including digital resources, computers and printing, reading programs, and interlibrary loans. For a touring cyclist, it represents a quiet, publicly accessible building in an otherwise seaside-resort community.

detail.address: 15342 Buena Vista Avenue, White Rock, V4B 1Y6

visitor.name: Thomson Creek
visitor.desc: Thomson Creek is a nature reserve in Kelowna, BC, managed by the City of Kelowna as part of its parks and natural areas network. Situated along a creek corridor, it offers a natural green space within the Okanagan landscape that touring cyclists may find useful as a rest stop or scenic detour. As a City of Kelowna property, it is publicly accessible.

visitor.name: Old Barn Community Centre
visitor.desc: A residential community centre on UBC's campus operated by the University Neighbourhoods Association, serving the surrounding residential neighbourhoods. The centre hosts family events, recreation programs, fitness facilities, and community services. It functions as a civic hub for UBC-area residents rather than a visitor-facing attraction.

visitor.name: Splash BC Water Parks
visitor.desc: Splash BC is a family-operated chain of large floating inflatable obstacle courses (Wibit) set on public beaches across the Okanagan, operating since 2014. Each park features climbing walls, slides, trampolines, monkey bars, and interconnected water features designed for active, high-energy fun for ages 5 and up. With four BC locations in Kelowna, Penticton, Peachland, and Osoyoos, it has become a signature summer attraction for the region's locals and touring visitors alike.

visitor.name: London Heritage Farm
visitor.desc: London Farmhouse is a large Edwardian Builder-style farmhouse built around 1898, set among the remnants of a working farm on Richmond's South Arm and designated a City of Richmond heritage site in 2003. Situated on Dyke Road, it sits directly along the South Dyke Trail corridor, making it a natural stop for cyclists exploring Richmond's scenic dyke network. The farm has operated continuously since the 1880s and represents one of the few surviving historic agricultural properties in the region.

visitor.name: Salt Spring Island Multi Space (SIMS)
visitor.desc: Salt Spring Island Multi Space (SIMS) is a government-operated community recreation facility run by SSIPARC (Salt Spring Island Parks, Arts, Recreation & Culture), a service of the Capital Regional District. The facility offers drop-in gym programs, aquatics, roller-skating, pickleball, kindergym, and a broad range of community programs across all age groups. For a touring cyclist arriving by ferry to Salt Spring Island, SIMS represents one of the island's primary public recreation hubs.

detail.address: 124 Rainbow Road, Salt Spring Island, V8K 2V5

visitor.name: Victoria Drive Community Hall Rentals
visitor.desc: Victoria Drive Community Hall Rentals is a City of Vancouver community facility located in the Victoria-Fraserview neighbourhood of East Vancouver, available for community events and private rentals. Situated near the busy Victoria Drive corridor, it serves as a neighbourhood gathering point in a residential area with good cycling connections. Touring cyclists riding through the area may find it useful as a landmark or community resource.

visitor.name: UFV Library
visitor.desc: The UFV Library serves the University of the Fraser Valley community across campuses in Abbotsford, Chilliwack, and Mission, offering access to print and digital collections, research assistance, and study spaces. As an academic library on a large university campus, it primarily serves students and faculty but is accessible to community members via guest access. A touring cyclist passing through Abbotsford would find a large institutional building with campus surroundings.

visitor.name: Whistler Village Host
visitor.desc: A small tourism information kiosk in Whistler Village, tagged as a hut-style building on OpenStreetMap. It appears to be one of the informal host stations where visitors can ask questions about the area, distinct from the larger Whistler Visitor Centre on Gateway Drive.

visitor.name: Poirier Sport and Leisure Complex
visitor.desc: A massive 190,000-square-foot municipal recreation complex in Coquitlam featuring a lap pool, leisure-therapy pool, whirlpool, steam room, dry sauna, fitness centre, and indoor track. It's also home to the Coquitlam Sports Hall of Fame and a licensed café. For touring cyclists, the drop-in pool and showers offer a welcome refresh, and the facility has parking available in the surrounding Poirier Precinct area.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Website states 'shower before you dive in,' confirming showers available as part of the pool/aquatic facility; drop-in swimming available without pre-registration
notes.Café or food on site: Licensed café on site, confirmed by website

visitor.name: Gibsons Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: Gibsons Visitor Centre is the official tourism information office for Gibsons, operated by the Gibsons Chamber of Commerce on BC's Sunshine Coast. Located at unit 101 on South Fletcher Road, it serves as a first stop for visitors arriving to this ferry-accessible coastal community. Touring cyclists riding the Sunshine Coast route would find it a natural stop for local maps, route advice, and community information.

visitor.name: Japanese Garden
visitor.desc: The Japanese Gardens is a community-built memorial garden within Dinner Bay Park on Mayne Island, commemorating Japanese settlers who lived and worked on the island between 1900 and 1942. Created largely by volunteers from 1999 onward, it features a pond with island, bridges including a traditional zigzagging yatsuhashi, a meditation hut, waterfall, and seasonal plantings including cherry trees donated by descendant families. A touring cyclist visiting Mayne Island can explore a quietly moving cultural landscape shaped entirely by community hands.

visitor.name: SL: City Centre Branch
visitor.desc: The Surrey Libraries City Centre Branch is a flagship four-floor, 79,900 sq ft public library in Surrey's civic core, LEED Gold certified and featuring original Indigenous murals, a meditation room, and a Newcomer Welcome Centre. Located just 150 m from Surrey Central SkyTrain station, it is one of the most accessible public buildings in the region and serves as a major community and cultural hub. Touring cyclists would find free Wi-Fi, free computers, and a central urban location convenient, though the building's breadth of community programming sets it apart from a typical library.

visitor.name: Canadian Museum of Rail Travel
visitor.desc: The Cranbrook History Centre is a nationally recognized cultural institution housing a nationally designated historic railcar collection, internationally recognized paleontology specimens, and an interactive model railway exhibit. Guided tours step visitors back into the golden age of rail travel aboard original Trans-Canada Limited cars, weaving in Indigenous, labour, and immigration history. The museum is a short walk from downtown Cranbrook, close to cafés and shops, with free on-site parking accessed from Highway 95.

visitor.name: Ted and Mary Greig Rhododendron Garden
visitor.desc: The Ted and Mary Greig Rhododendron Garden is a curated public garden in Vancouver operated by the Vancouver Parks Board, named in honour of its founding benefactors. It is celebrated for its extensive collection of rhododendrons and related species, making it a notable stop for cyclists exploring Vancouver's green spaces. As a publicly accessible garden with no admission charge implied by OSM tags, it offers a quiet natural detour on a cycling tour of the city.

visitor.name: Vancouver Playhouse
visitor.desc: Built in 1962 and managed by Vancouver Civic Theatres, the Vancouver Playhouse is an intimate performing arts venue seating audiences in close proximity to the stage, making it especially suited for chamber music, spoken theatre, and dance. Located in downtown Vancouver steps from the Stadium-Chinatown SkyTrain station, it regularly hosts DanceHouse, Friends of Chamber Music, and the Vancouver Recital Society. Accessible parking is available in the adjacent Queen Elizabeth Theatre parkade with elevator access to the Hamilton Street entrance.

visitor.name: Royston Community Hall
visitor.desc: Royston Community Hall is a community-operated meeting and events hall in the small coastal village of Royston on Vancouver Island's east coast, sitting along the South Island Highway. Operating under the Royston Community Club and Recreation Commission, it hosts local events and group activities for this rural community. For touring cyclists riding the Island, it represents a potential rest stop in an otherwise quiet stretch between Courtenay and Union Bay.

visitor.name: Eva Bene Butterfly Garden
visitor.desc: Eva Bene Butterfly Garden is a community-run green space in Tsawwassen, BC, dedicated since 2003 to protecting and increasing local populations of butterflies, beneficial insects, and hummingbirds. It is a grassroots initiative with a public-access designation and an active Facebook community of around 185 followers. For touring cyclists, it offers a quiet natural stop in the Tsawwassen area.

visitor.name: Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre
visitor.desc: The Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre is a YMCA-operated community recreation facility in Chilliwack offering a range of indoor amenities for all ages. Tagged in OSM as a sports centre with ice hockey, it is part of Chilliwack's broader municipal recreation network. Touring cyclists passing through Chilliwack may find it useful as a rest stop, though specific cyclist-relevant amenities could not be confirmed from available content.

visitor.name: University of British Columbia Okanagan Library
visitor.desc: The UBC Okanagan Library is the central academic library on the UBC Okanagan campus, situated on the territory of the Syilx Okanagan Nation in Kelowna. It serves students, faculty, staff, and community visitors, offering a wide range of study and collaboration spaces, special collections, and an Inclusive Technology Lab. Community members and visitors are explicitly welcomed, making it a potential rest stop for touring cyclists passing through the UBCO campus.

visitor.name: Frankie's Jazz Club
visitor.desc: Frankie's Jazz Club bills itself as Vancouver's premier live music venue, hosting seven jazz shows weekly from Wednesday through Sunday in the Georgian Court Hotel on Beatty Street. The venue runs a curated late-night After Dark series every Friday and Saturday featuring local and visiting jazz artists. It offers a full dinner menu alongside its music programming, making it a destination evening out for a touring cyclist exploring downtown Vancouver's cultural scene.

notes.Café or food on site: Website navigation includes 'Dinner Menu', 'After Dark Menu', 'Wine Menu', and 'Drink Menu', confirming food and drink service on site

visitor.name: Ladysmith Gallery
visitor.desc: The Ladysmith Gallery is a community art gallery operated by the Arts Council of Ladysmith and District, located in the heart of downtown Ladysmith. It hosts rotating monthly member exhibitions featuring visual artists from across Vancouver Island and the Gulf Islands, alongside a boutique of smaller local artworks and periodic guest artist shows. A touring cyclist passing through Ladysmith can drop in to see original regional art and support local artists in an accessible downtown storefront.

visitor.name: Community Peace Garden
visitor.desc: A small permaculture demonstration garden on the Vancouver Island University campus in Nanaimo, located on the north side of the campus library. Founded in 2008 as the Community Peace Garden, it is now run by the VIU Permaculture Club as a space for food growing, seed saving, and learning about traditional ecological knowledge. The garden is described as designed to be as accessible as possible.

visitor.name: Wilson Creek Linear Park
visitor.desc: Wilson Creek Linear Park is a nature reserve and linear greenway managed by the City of Kelowna in British Columbia. As a linear park, it likely follows a creek corridor and offers a natural off-road passage through the community. Touring cyclists passing through Kelowna may find it a pleasant, low-traffic route or rest stop along their journey.

visitor.name: Bonsor Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Bonsor Recreation Complex is a large municipal recreation facility operated by the City of Burnaby, situated in the dense Metrotown neighbourhood near a major SkyTrain interchange. It offers a swimming pool, gymnasium, weight and cardio rooms, a martial arts studio, and arts and music studios under one roof. The facility is a hub of community programming for the broader Burnaby area.

visitor.name: Open Space
visitor.desc: Open Space is a 1500-square-foot flexible cultural venue in the heart of historic Downtown Abbotsford, operated by the Abbotsford Downtown Business Association. It hosts curated art exhibitions, artisan markets, workshops, and micro-events, serving as a creative hub connecting local artists and small businesses. A touring cyclist passing through downtown Abbotsford could drop in to browse a gallery show or catch a pop-up market.

visitor.name: Kamloops Museum
visitor.desc: The Kamloops Museum and Archives is a free, publicly operated institution in downtown Kamloops dedicated to preserving the history and heritage of the region and the Secwépemc people. It houses permanent and rotating exhibitions, a Children's Museum, archival collections, and educational programs for all ages. As a no-fee attraction operated by the City of Kamloops, it is an accessible cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the downtown core.

visitor.name: Hjorth Road Swimming Pool
visitor.desc: Hjorth Road Outdoor Pool is a seasonal municipal outdoor swimming pool operated by the City of Surrey, offering public swims and swimming lessons. It sits in a residential neighbourhood and could serve as a refreshing stop for touring cyclists passing through Surrey during summer months.

visitor.name: Eagle Ridge Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: Eagle Ridge Outdoor Pool is a competitive eight-lane, 25-metre municipal outdoor pool in Coquitlam, part of Eagle Ridge Park. It features two diving boards (1M and 3M), large change room facilities, and adjoining grass picnic and deck areas for lounging. The pool includes notable accessibility features such as a ramp, transfer lift, and water wheelchair.

notes.Water without admission: Water fountain is listed as a general facility feature; washrooms are noted as accessible to park users without swimming

visitor.name: Kangaroo Creek Farm
visitor.desc: An exotic animal farm near the north end of Kelowna airport where visitors can get up close with red kangaroos, wallabies, capybaras, an African crested porcupine, parrots, and other animals. Guides provide free treats for hand-feeding the macropods. The farm has unpaved gravel, dirt, and grass pathways and a picnic area, making it a quirky Okanagan roadside stop.

detail.address: 5932 Old Vernon Road, Kelowna, BC V1X 7V2

visitor.name: Sea Island Community Centre
visitor.desc: Sea Island Community Centre is a City of Richmond public facility situated on Sea Island, the same island that hosts Vancouver International Airport, making it a rare community hub in an otherwise airport-dominated landscape. The two-storey building serves the small residential population of Sea Island and would be a natural rest stop for cyclists navigating the flat, dyke-lined roads of this area. As a municipal community centre, it is likely to offer standard civic amenities, though none can be confirmed from available evidence.

visitor.name: BPL: Tommy Douglas Library
visitor.desc: Tommy Douglas Library is a full-service branch of Burnaby Public Library, located on the corner of Kingsway and Walker Avenue and easily accessible via several cycling routes including the Highland Park Line and Urban Train Lakes Bikeway. The branch offers a welcoming civic space with community rooms, a teen space, public computers, and Wi-Fi. It is fully wheelchair accessible and features inclusive washroom facilities.

visitor.name: Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre
visitor.desc: Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre is a municipally owned recreation facility operated by the YMCA of Greater Vancouver, offering indoor amenities for all ages. The OSM record indicates the primary sport is swimming, suggesting aquatic facilities are central to the venue. Touring cyclists in the Chilliwack area may find this a useful stop for post-ride recovery, though specific cyclist-oriented services are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Tourism Victoria Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The official visitor centre for Destination Greater Victoria, situated in the heart of the Inner Harbour on Wharf Street. It serves as the city's primary trip-planning hub, offering local expertise, maps, and guidance across accommodations, tours, and outdoor activities in the Greater Victoria region. Touring cyclists stopping here can tap into the same resources used by visitors arriving by any mode, with the city's cycling-friendly downtown and accessible waterfront just outside the door.

visitor.name: Capitol theatre
visitor.desc: The Capitol Theatre is a historic performing arts venue in downtown Nelson operated by the Capitol Theatre Restoration Society, whose mission is community enrichment through the arts. It hosts live productions including an annual pantomime, a summer youth show, and community performances open to public audition. The theatre also maintains a costume shop holding over 10,000 individual pieces and offers extensive accessibility accommodations including a hearing loop and accessible seating.

visitor.name: Kensington Pool
visitor.desc: Kensington Pool is a City of Vancouver–operated public swimming facility in the Kensington-Cedar Cottage neighbourhood. As a municipal aquatic centre, it offers a dedicated aquatic environment managed under the city's parks and recreation department. Touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver may find it a useful stop for a swim or to freshen up.

visitor.name: Cloverdale Branch
visitor.desc: The Cloverdale Branch is one of ten public library locations operated by Surrey Libraries in Surrey, BC. The system offers borrowing, public computing, community programs, and specialized accessibility services across its branches. Surrey Libraries completed the Sustainable Library Certification Program in 2025 and has invested in green building practices and zero-waste initiatives.

visitor.name: Nanaimo Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Nanaimo Art Gallery is a well-established public art gallery founded in 1976, now located in the heart of downtown Nanaimo at the intersection of Commercial and Bastion streets, close to the Old City Quarter and the waterfront. The gallery presents rotating exhibitions of contemporary and Indigenous art and runs diverse programs for all ages, including a strong emphasis on Snuneymuxw cultural perspectives. It is a culturally significant landmark for cyclists exploring Nanaimo's downtown core.

detail.address: 150 Commercial Street, Nanaimo, British Columbia V9R 5G6

visitor.name: MRC Sports Complex
visitor.desc: MRC Sports Complex (also known as Matsqui Recreation Complex Sports Complex) is a municipally operated outdoor turf facility in Abbotsford, BC, offering soccer and Canadian football fields. It is jointly run by the City of Abbotsford Department of Parks, Recreation & Culture and Abbotsford School District #34, and has been in operation since April 2016. Touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley may find it a useful landmark or rest stop near the Matsqui trail corridor.

visitor.name: FVRL: Murrayville Library
visitor.desc: The Murrayville Library is a branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, serving the Murrayville neighbourhood of Langley as a free public institution. It offers access to library collections, digital services, public computers, and printing. Touring cyclists passing through Langley may find it a convenient community hub for a rest indoors.

visitor.name: Deep Cove Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: Deep Cove Cultural Centre is a community arts building in the village of Deep Cove, a scenic waterfront destination at the end of a popular cycling route on the North Shore. The building is home to the Deep Cove Stage Society, a community theatre company that has been producing live performances since 1974 and is currently in its 51st season. Cyclists passing through Deep Cove's compact village core would find this venue at the heart of the community.

visitor.name: BPL: Temporary Cameron Branch
visitor.desc: The Temporary Cameron Branch of Burnaby Public Library operates inside the City of Lougheed Shopping Centre while a permanent location is presumably unavailable. It is a fully wheelchair-accessible branch offering public computers, Wi-Fi, and a mix of work, study, and lounge seating. Washrooms are available just outside the library in the mall, including a universal single-stall washroom.

visitor.name: Clarance Greenspace
visitor.desc: Clarance Greenspace is a nature reserve within Kelowna's municipal parks system, situated in the city's southern area near the coordinates 49.799°N, 119.479°W. As a publicly accessible green corridor, it offers a quiet natural escape that touring cyclists passing through Kelowna might appreciate as a rest or detour point. The City of Kelowna maintains a dedicated listing for it within their parks and beaches directory.

visitor.name: The Ice House Gallery
visitor.desc: The Ice House Artists Cooperative is a collectively run gallery and marketplace established in 2004, representing over 40 artists from Haida Gwaii to Telkwa along BC's North Coast. Located near the scenic Cow Bay waterfront in Prince Rupert, the gallery showcases handcrafted artwork, jewellery, pottery, clothing, and more. It also hosts community events including paint nights and art auctions, making it a lively cultural stop for visitors passing through.

detail.address: 217 1st Avenue East, Prince Rupert, BC V8J 1A8

visitor.name: Yellowhouse Art Centre
visitor.desc: A non-profit contemporary community art space in the heart of Sturdies Bay on Galiano Island, housed in a converted building. The centre hosts rotating curated exhibitions, live music performances, workshops, life drawing sessions, and an artist-in-residency program. A cultural stop for cyclists exploring the Gulf Islands, with a lively calendar of events from spring through fall.

detail.address: 2517 Sturdies Bay Rd, Galiano Island, BC V0N 1P0

visitor.name: Harry Jerome Sports Centre
visitor.desc: The Burnaby Velodrome Club operates inside Harry Jerome Sports Centre as the only indoor velodrome in the Pacific Northwest and one of three indoor velodromes in Canada. The 200-metre wooden track — built between 1991 and 1997 — offers programs ranging from introductory 'Learn to Ride' sessions to competitive UCI-regulated racing, and the club maintains an explicit out-of-town rider policy along with private track bookings and bike rentals. It is a Cycling Canada Training Centre and has contributed significantly to Canada's track cycling development at the international level.

visitor.name: Richmond Public Library, Ironwood Branch
visitor.desc: The Ironwood Branch is one of several Richmond Public Library locations serving the city's south end, offering free public computing, internet access, and a broad multilingual collection. As a fully public facility with no admission charge, it provides a useful midday stop for touring cyclists passing through Richmond's suburban corridor. The library also hosts programs and maker-style equipment (3D printers, Cricut machines) through its Launchpad initiative.

visitor.name: Museum of Vancouver
visitor.desc: The Museum of Vancouver is Canada's premier civic history museum, situated in Vanier Park near the waterfront and sea wall — a natural stop on one of Vancouver's most popular cycling routes. As an independent non-profit, MOV explores Vancouver's diverse communities and histories through rotating and permanent exhibitions, with current features on redress, repatriation, and design sustainability. Cyclists exploring the Vanier Park precinct can pair a visit here with the nearby Vancouver Maritime Museum and H.R. MacMillan Space Centre.

notes.Vending machines: FAQ states: 'There are vending machines available with cold drinks and snacks in the Lower Lobby.'

visitor.name: Hastings Community Centre
visitor.desc: Hastings Community Centre is a multi-program neighbourhood facility in East Vancouver, jointly operated by the Hastings Community Association and the Vancouver Board of Parks and Recreation. It offers a fitness centre, licensed child care, family, youth, and seniors' programs, and room rentals. A companion facility, Templeton Park Pool at 700 Templeton Drive, is operated by the same organization nearby.

visitor.name: Vancouver Aquarium
visitor.desc: The Vancouver Aquarium is a world-class marine science centre situated in Stanley Park, one of Canada's most celebrated urban parks and a hub for cycling tourism. As the largest aquarium in Canada, it is home to thousands of aquatic animals and is internationally recognized for marine research and conservation. Touring cyclists riding the Stanley Park Seawall or passing through the park will find it a prominent landmark along one of Vancouver's most iconic cycling routes.

visitor.name: Sechelt Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Sechelt Visitor Centre is the primary tourism information office for the Sunshine Coast community of Sechelt, BC, offering regional travel guidance to visitors arriving by ferry from Vancouver. Located in the heart of Sechelt, it serves as the gateway for exploring the Sunshine Coast's coastline, trails, and communities. OSM indicates the facility is wheelchair accessible.

visitor.name: Gulf of Georgia Cannery National Historic Site
visitor.desc: The Gulf of Georgia Cannery National Historic Site is a preserved early-20th-century salmon cannery in the historic fishing village of Steveston, telling the story of Canada's West Coast fishing industry through immersive exhibits and collections. The site features Indigenous perspectives on the Salish Sea, a large-scale LEGO model of the cannery, and rotating cultural programming. Steveston is a popular endpoint on Richmond's scenic dyke cycling routes, making this a natural stop for touring cyclists exploring the Fraser River delta.

visitor.name: Cheyenne Community Garden
visitor.desc: Cheyenne Community Garden is a community-managed growing space in Vancouver's Renfrew-Collingwood area, operated under the RC Food network. Community gardens in this network typically offer residents shared plots for growing food and green space for the neighbourhood. A passing cyclist might find it a pleasant rest spot in a residential area, though public access varies by site.

visitor.name: Britannia Community Centre
visitor.desc: Britannia Community Centre is a sprawling 17-acre campus in East Vancouver, managed through a partnership of city agencies and celebrating its 50th year in 2026. The complex encompasses a pool, ice rink, fitness centre, multiple gyms and courts, community gardens, public art installations, a library, and an art gallery, making it one of Vancouver's most comprehensive neighbourhood hubs. Touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver will find a genuinely community-rooted destination with a wide range of recreational and cultural offerings in a single campus.

visitor.name: Colbourne House
visitor.desc: Colbourne House is a 1912 heritage building on Southwest Marine Drive that has served as the home of the Marpole Museum & Historical Society since 2005. The volunteer-run museum preserves the history of one of Vancouver's oldest neighbourhoods, whose Indigenous settlement dates back to roughly 3500 BC. Touring cyclists on the SW Marine Drive corridor will find a small but characterful community museum in a quiet residential setting.

visitor.name: Formal Rose Garden
visitor.desc: The Formal Rose Garden is a long-established public garden within Stanley Park, one of Canada's most celebrated urban parks, featuring thousands of roses in curated beds that attract visitors from spring through fall. It sits along the network of roads and paths used by cyclists touring the park's interior. Admission to the garden is free and it is open to the public year-round.

visitor.name: Simon Fraser University
visitor.desc: Simon Fraser University's main Burnaby campus sits atop Burnaby Mountain at roughly 365 m elevation, offering panoramic views across Metro Vancouver, the Fraser Valley, and the North Shore mountains. Designed by Arthur Erickson and completed in 1965, the campus is widely regarded as a landmark of West Coast brutalist architecture and is a draw for visitors in its own right. The university has three campuses (Burnaby, Surrey, Vancouver) and is ranked Canada's top comprehensive university by Maclean's.

notes.Café or food on site: SFU website lists 'Food' as a campus resource under Campus Resources, indicating on-campus food services exist; specific vendor names or locations not confirmed in scraped content

visitor.name: Cowichan Performing Arts Centre
visitor.desc: Described on its own homepage as Vancouver Island's Premier Theatre, the Cowichan Performing Arts Centre is a regional facility operated by the Cowichan Valley Regional District presenting local, national, and international performances spanning dance, theatre, film, and music. It also offers an art gallery, theatre rentals, and a curated CPAC Presenting Series featuring acclaimed touring artists. A touring cyclist stopping in Duncan could take in a performance or a gallery visit as a cultural highlight of the Cowichan Valley.

visitor.name: Victoria Curling Club
visitor.desc: The Victoria Curling Club has been in continuous operation since 1953, making it one of BC's longest-running curling facilities with a history that includes provincial, national, and world champions. Open to the public through 'Try Curling' events, group bookings, and ice rentals, it offers a genuine taste of a beloved Canadian sport in a welcoming community setting. The club is currently undergoing a major ice plant upgrade funded through community donations and a City of Victoria grant, securing its future as a local hub.

notes.Café or food on site: Venue rental page references 'Slider's Cafe and Catering' as the on-site food services provider, available for venue rentals and events

visitor.name: Kamloops Heritage Railway
visitor.desc: The Kamloops Heritage Railway Society stewards the #2141 'Spirit of Kamloops,' a historic 1912 Canadian Locomotive Company steam engine that is the sole surviving example of its class. The society is currently undertaking a major reactivation project in partnership with the City of Kamloops and CN Rail, with an ambitious vision of running steam-powered excursions along the Okanagan Subdivision between Kamloops and Vernon. For a touring cyclist, this could eventually be a remarkable heritage attraction on the Thompson-Okanagan corridor, but it is not currently operational.

visitor.name: Metchosin School Museum
visitor.desc: The Metchosin Schoolhouse Museum occupies BC's first school building constructed after Confederation, dating to 1872. Restored over three years with a new foundation, electrical wiring, and a wheelchair-access lift, the museum's interior focuses on education artifacts and pioneer pedagogy. It is volunteer-run by the Metchosin Museum Society and sits along Happy Valley Road in a quiet rural setting west of Victoria.

visitor.name: Xwísten Experience Tours
visitor.desc: Xwísten Experience Tours is an Indigenous-owned cultural attraction operated by the St'át'imc people at the historic Bridge River fishing grounds six kilometres north of Lillooet. Visitors join guided walking tours of active salmon-drying sites and a pit-house archaeological village containing over 80 identified s7ístken (traditional winter homes). The on-site Bearfoot Grill rounds out the visit with burgers, sandwiches, salads, and local favourites served in a casual setting.

notes.Café or food on site: Bearfoot Grill is an on-site restaurant offering burgers, sandwiches, salads, and local favourites; BBQ Salmon meals are also served as part of tour packages

visitor.name: Richmond Country Farms
visitor.desc: Richmond Country Farms is a family-owned working farm in Richmond, operating for over 60 years, where crops are grown on-site and sold directly in a seasonal farm market alongside baked goods and local products. The property also includes a winery with tastings, a lounge, and a picnic area, plus farm animals and a nursery, making it a genuinely multifaceted rural destination in an urban setting. Cyclists exploring the Steveston area will find it a distinctive stop combining fresh local produce with agricultural character.

notes.Café or food on site: Farm market sells fresh produce, baked goods, and pantry goods on site; winery has a lounge and picnic area

visitor.name: The Rex Hall
visitor.desc: The Rex Hall is a theatre venue located in downtown Kamloops at 417 Seymour Street, as recorded in the City of Kamloops dataset. It sits in the heart of Kamloops, making it a potentially convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the city centre. No further details about the venue's character or offerings could be confirmed due to website unavailability.

visitor.name: Cambie Community Centre
visitor.desc: Cambie Community Centre is a City of Richmond municipal recreation facility serving the Cambie neighbourhood. It is one of several community centres operated by Richmond Parks & Recreation, offering programs and activities for residents. For touring cyclists passing through Richmond, it may serve as a potential rest stop, though specific cycling amenities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Railway & Forestry Museum
visitor.desc: The Central BC Railway & Forestry Museum sits at the confluence of the Nechako and Fraser Rivers in Prince George, preserving rail and forest industrial heritage from Northern Interior BC on the ancestral territory of the Lheidli T'enneh Nation. Its collection spans locomotives, rolling stock, and heritage railway buildings from lines including the Grand Trunk Pacific, Canadian National, and BC Rail, most of which visitors can board and explore. A touring cyclist passing through Prince George will find a richly immersive outdoor and indoor heritage experience with programming ranging from school field trips to facility rentals and seasonal special events.

visitor.name: Chase Visitor Information Centre
visitor.desc: The Chase Chamber & Visitor Centre is the official Destination BC visitor information office for the Village of Chase, positioned just off the Trans-Canada Highway at the western gateway to the Shuswap. Staffed by certified Visitor Information Counsellors, it provides local maps, event listings, souvenirs, and Indigenous heritage context for the surrounding Secwepemcúl'ecw territory. Outside, ample parking accommodates large motorhomes, a small covered picnic area offers a rest spot, and an EV charging station sits on the exterior.

visitor.name: ORL: Lumby Branch
visitor.desc: The Lumby Branch of the Okanagan Regional Library is a small community library serving the village of Lumby in the North Okanagan. Part of the 30-branch ORL system, it offers public computer access, a makerspace with digitization stations and a Cricut machine, and a rotating local art display in partnership with the Monashee Arts Council. For a touring cyclist passing through, it is a quiet, free indoor stop with internet access.

visitor.name: Edmonds Community Centre
visitor.desc: Edmonds Community Centre is a City of Burnaby recreation facility offering swimming, fitness rooms, gym and racquet sports, plus youth and seniors centres. It also hosts community programs and drop-in activities for families. Located on Edmonds Street in Burnaby, it sits within Metro Vancouver's urban cycling network.

visitor.name: Pemberton Youth Centre
visitor.desc: The Pemberton Youth Centre is a publicly operated sports and recreation facility in Pemberton, BC, run by the Village of Pemberton. It serves as a community hub for youth programs and sports activities in this small agricultural town situated in the Pemberton Valley, roughly 30 km north of Whistler. Touring cyclists passing through Pemberton may find it a useful stop given its public nature and recreation mandate.

visitor.name: Linden Gardens
visitor.desc: Linden Gardens is a picturesque 9-acre ornamental garden and event venue in Kaleden, built on a 75-year-old fruit farm lovingly transformed by owners Ken and Margaret Hayter into a lush landscape of flowers, ponds, and winding paths. The on-site Frog City Cafe serves handcrafted drinks and fresh-baked goods amid the gardens. It is a seasonal destination primarily known as a wedding venue but open to visitors during its operating season.

notes.Café or food on site: Frog City Cafe on site — website describes handcrafted drinks and fresh-baked goodies available in the gardens

visitor.name: North Vancouver City Library
visitor.desc: The North Vancouver City Library is a full-service public library serving the City of North Vancouver with physical collections, an extensive digital library, and community programming. A 'Spokes 'n' Words' book bike initiative brings library materials to the community on two wheels, reflecting an active cycling culture. Free Wi-Fi and public computer access are available, making it a potential connectivity stop for touring cyclists.

visitor.name: Original Hot Yoga Abbotsford
visitor.desc: Original Hot Yoga Abbotsford is the Fraser Valley's first hot yoga studio, open since 2007 in Abbotsford's downtown core. It offers a range of heated yoga formats including the classic 26-posture Bikram sequence, Yin Yoga, Hot Core Fusion, and Kundalini Yoga and Meditation. Touring cyclists seeking muscle recovery and flexibility work between riding days may find a drop-in class appealing.

visitor.name: Means of Production Community Garden
visitor.desc: Means of Production is a long-running community garden established in 2002 and operated by the EartHand Gleaners Society under the City of Vancouver's parks system. It offers touring cyclists a quiet green stop in the city, with the garden's community focus reflecting Vancouver's strong urban agriculture culture. As a publicly accessible City of Vancouver attraction, it is a genuine destination for cyclists interested in local food and community initiatives.

visitor.name: YMCA/YWCA Westhills
visitor.desc: The YMCA/YWCA Westhills is a full-service recreation and community centre operated by the YMCA-YWCA of Vancouver Island in the Westhills area of Langford. The facility offers fitness, aquatics (pool), child care, and community health programming as part of a well-established non-profit network with locations across Greater Victoria. Touring cyclists would find it a potentially useful services stop, though most amenities are oriented toward members and registered participants.

visitor.name: Roberts Creek Community Library
visitor.desc: Known locally as 'The Reading Room,' this volunteer-run community library is operated by the Roberts Creek Community Association and serves as a quiet neighbourhood institution on the Sunshine Coast. Membership is free and the collection spans fiction, non-fiction, and children's books with an emphasis on Canadian authors. A cycle tourist stopping in Roberts Creek will find a welcoming, low-key spot to browse books and connect with the community.

detail.address: 1044 Roberts Creek Road, Roberts Creek, V0N 2W0

visitor.name: O.U.R. Ecovillage
visitor.desc: O.U.R. Ecovillage is a 25-acre permaculture demonstration site and educational research centre established in 1999 on Vancouver Island near Shawnigan Lake, operating as a non-profit community services cooperative. It hosts guided public tours that walk visitors through natural building examples, food gardens, and ecological systems, reflecting decades of hands-on sustainable design. A touring cyclist would find it a genuinely unusual cultural stop — an intercultural, intergenerational living community with working farm, cob structures, and immersive courses ranging from permaculture design to natural building.

detail.address: 1565 Baldy Mountain Rd, Shawnigan Lake, BC V0R 2W2

notes.Café or food on site: Website's public tours page states: 'We offer a mostly vegetarian, yummy, mostly organic, and mostly from OUR Garden' — lunch is available on tour days for those staying after the tour

visitor.name: Vancouver Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Major not-for-profit art gallery founded in 1931, housed in a landmark building in downtown Vancouver. Known for its extensive Emily Carr collection and rotating international exhibitions. A natural rest stop for cyclists on the downtown seawall loop, with on-site dining and a gallery shop.

notes.Café or food on site: 'Dine' listed as a visitor option under the Visit section of the main navigation

visitor.name: Jeremy Koreski
visitor.desc: Jeremy Koreski Gallery is a photography gallery in the heart of Tofino showcasing the work of local outdoor photographer Jeremy Koreski, who grew up in this coastal town and built his career documenting surfing, wildlife, and the wild landscapes of the BC coast. Koreski's distinctive aerial images — captured by hanging out of helicopters over Clayoquot Sound — have been published internationally by outlets including The New York Times and Patagonia. A visit offers a compelling window into the natural world that cyclists riding the West Coast are passing through, with hand-signed prints also available online.

visitor.name: H2O Adventure and Fitness Centre
visitor.desc: Kelowna's major municipal waterpark and fitness centre, owned by the City and operated by the YMCA of Southern Interior BC. Features include wave pool, lazy river, waterslides, FlowRider, diving boards, hot tub, steam room, and a full fitness area with cardio, conditioning, and cycle studio. Drop-in access is available for non-members.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Locker rooms and showers listed as open amenities; drop-in rates available for non-members

visitor.name: Billy Lewis Centenary Rose Garden
visitor.desc: The Billy Lewis Centenary Rose Garden is a public rose garden located within Bowen Park in Nanaimo, BC. It is a named ornamental garden feature managed by the City of Nanaimo as part of its broader parks system. Cyclists touring Nanaimo's urban parks may encounter it as a scenic stop, though it is a sub-feature of the larger Bowen Park rather than a standalone facility.

visitor.name: Sparwood Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Sparwood Visitor Centre, operated by the Sparwood Chamber of Commerce, is the first visitor information stop in BC for travellers arriving from Alberta via Highway 3. It is home to the iconic Terex Titan — one of the largest trucks ever built — which draws over 60,000 visitors annually. Touring cyclists can pick up local and provincial trail maps, get route information for the Elk Valley's mountain biking and Trans Canada Trail network, and take advantage of free on-site amenities.

detail.address: 141 A Aspen Dr, Sparwood, BC V0B 2G0

notes.Water without admission: Water filling stations listed as a free visitor centre amenity; no admission fee to access the centre

visitor.name: Kamloops Paintball
visitor.desc: Kamloops Paintball Games is a long-running outdoor paintball park located on Harper Mountain Road, about 20 minutes from downtown Kamloops, offering woodsball, speedball, and low-impact formats for a wide age range. Run by three experienced paintball operators with over 100 combined years in the BC paintball industry, the park hosts public walk-on days as well as private group bookings for birthdays, corporate events, and school outings. A touring cyclist looking for an active half-day excursion off the main route could make this a destination stop, though it sits well off the highway on a mountain road.

visitor.name: Cascade Falls Regional Park
visitor.desc: Cascade Falls Regional Park is a Fraser Valley Regional District park located near Deroche, offering access to a scenic waterfall in the mountains east of Mission. Operated by a regional government body, it sits along Ridgeview Road and draws visitors into the forested terrain of the lower Fraser Valley. Touring cyclists riding the corridor between Mission and Harrison Hot Springs would find this a worthwhile natural detour.

visitor.name: Point Atkinson Lighthouse
visitor.desc: Point Atkinson Lighthouse, built in 1912 and designated a National Historic Site of Canada, stands at the tip of the Lighthouse Park headland in West Vancouver. The lighthouse remains an active navigational aid and is one of the most photographed landmarks on the BC coast. Cyclists riding the West Vancouver waterfront routes often make it a destination, reaching it via the trail network through old-growth forest in Lighthouse Park.

visitor.name: Steveston Museum
visitor.desc: Built in 1905 as Steveston's first bank, this heritage building in the heart of the historic fishing village now functions as both a working Canada Post office and a free-admission museum. The site spans three areas: the original bank/post office building, exhibits on Steveston's Japanese Canadian community, and the adjacent Steveston Town Square Park. It sits at the centre of a walkable and bikeable village filled with restaurants, shops, and historic landmarks along the Fraser River estuary.

visitor.name: Renfrew Community Centre
visitor.desc: A Vancouver Parks community centre in the Renfrew-Collingwood neighbourhood, situated at the south end of Renfrew Ravine Park. The facility includes an indoor swimming pool with sauna and whirlpool, a fitness centre, and family change rooms — useful for a touring cyclist wanting a shower and rest stop in east Vancouver. Accessible via SkyTrain at 29th Avenue Station on the Expo Line.

visitor.name: Lost Lagoon Nature House
visitor.desc: The Lost Lagoon Nature House is a nature interpretation center operated by Stanley Park Ecology on the southeast shore of Lost Lagoon, right in the heart of Stanley Park — one of Vancouver's most popular cycling destinations. Visitors can explore interactive displays on local ecology, handle real wildlife specimens, and get current trail and wildlife insights from knowledgeable park naturalists. It sits along the inner park cycling routes and seawall, making it a natural and rewarding pause on any Stanley Park bike tour.

detail.address: South-east shore of Lost Lagoon, Stanley Park, Vancouver, BC

visitor.name: Mosaic Art Studio
visitor.desc: Mosaic Art Studio is a multi-location social enterprise offering hands-on Turkish lamp and mosaic art workshops, framed as intercultural experiences drawing on West and Central Asian craft traditions. Participants build their own glowing mosaic lamp piece by piece using hand-cut coloured glass and beads under the guidance of expert instructors. The Vancouver location is part of a Canadian chain also operating in Calgary, Edmonton, Ottawa, Montreal, Toronto, and Winnipeg, as well as internationally.

visitor.name: Burnaby Mountain Conservation Area
visitor.desc: Burnaby Mountain Conservation Area is a 576-hectare mountain park overlooking Burrard Inlet and the Vancouver skyline, adjacent to Simon Fraser University. It features forested trails through old-growth deciduous and coniferous terrain, including the Velodrome 'Grind' trail popular with mountain bikers year-round. Wildlife such as black-tailed deer, bald eagles, and occasional black bears and cougars inhabit the creeks and forest slopes, offering a wild backcountry feel minutes from the city.

visitor.name: tree peonies
visitor.desc: Tree peonies is a named garden feature within Stanley Park, one of North America's most celebrated urban parks situated on a forested peninsula adjacent to downtown Vancouver. The garden showcases tree peony specimens and is accessed as part of the broader Stanley Park experience, which is a marquee destination on the Vancouver cycling circuit. A fee is noted in OSM tags, suggesting it may be within a ticketed section of the park such as the Stanley Park Rose Garden area.

visitor.name: Rossland Public Library
visitor.desc: The Rossland Public Library has served this small mountain community since 1939, operating today from a renovated garage building that was last updated in 2018. It draws roughly 50,000 visits annually to a town of 3,700 residents and offers free membership, digital resources, and rotating local art exhibitions. For a touring cyclist, it is a welcoming indoor stop with free internet access in a community hub at the heart of Rossland.

visitor.name: North Delta Recreation Centre
