visitor.desc: North Delta Recreation Centre is a City of Delta–operated multi-sport facility offering ice hockey, curling, swimming, skating, fitness, and a wide range of court sports under one roof. It serves the North Delta community as a hub for year-round indoor recreation. Touring cyclists passing through the Delta area may find it a practical stop given its breadth of facilities, though cyclist-specific services are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: The General Store
visitor.desc: The General Store is part of the Pitt Meadows Museum, housed in the oldest known structure in Pitt Meadows with parts dating to 1886. The heritage building contains permanent and temporary exhibits on local settlement history, a community archives, and a reference library. Across Harris Road, the companion Hoffmann Site features a restored machine shop with over sixty stationary engines and a working forge.

visitor.name: Air Force Garden of Remembrance
visitor.desc: The Air Force Garden of Remembrance is a memorial garden within Stanley Park dedicated to Royal Canadian Air Force personnel. It offers a quiet, contemplative space nestled within one of Canada's most celebrated urban parks, easily reached by cyclists on the Stanley Park seawall or internal park roads. As part of Stanley Park, it sits within a world-class cycling destination on Vancouver's waterfront.

visitor.name: FVRL: Terry Fox Library
visitor.desc: Terry Fox Library is a branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, the largest public library network in British Columbia serving over 800,000 people across 25 community locations. Situated in Port Coquitlam, it offers a welcoming public space with outdoor bike racks, free WiFi, public computers, and accessible all-gender restrooms. A touring cyclist can drop in to rest, recharge devices, and access the internet in a comfortable, inclusive environment.

detail.address: 2150 Wilson Avenue, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 6J5

notes.Water without admission: Public library (free entry) with 'Low Water Fountains' listed as a facility feature

visitor.name: Pacific Museum of Earth
visitor.desc: The Pacific Museum of Earth is a free, public museum at the University of British Columbia operated by the Faculty of Science, housing nearly 100 years of combined mineral and fossil collections alongside exhibits spanning geology, oceanography, atmospheric science, and deep time. Visitors can touch real dinosaur bones, explore the forces shaping the planet, and experience galleries spread across two adjacent campus buildings. In 2026, the museum is a designated stamp stop in the UBC Tourism Challenge, making it a worthwhile detour for cyclists exploring the UBC campus.

visitor.name: SpringTide Whale Tours & Charters
visitor.desc: Family-owned whale and wildlife watching company operating out of Victoria's Inner Harbour for over 33 years. Tours head into the Salish Sea to see orcas, humpbacks, sea lions, and eagles aboard either a comfortable ocean cruiser or high-speed zodiacs. They run a 95%+ whale sighting success rate with a come-back-free guarantee if no whales are spotted.

notes.Café or food on site: Complimentary hot chocolate, coffee, and tea on Ocean Cruiser tours; granola bars and protein bars available for cash purchase onboard

visitor.name: Saint Ann's Schoolhouse
visitor.desc: Saint Ann's Schoolhouse is a pioneer-era heritage building managed as an outdoor exhibit within the Royal BC Museum's Cultural Precinct in Victoria's Inner Harbour district, where it stands alongside the historic Helmcken House. Listed on Wikimedia Commons as 'St. Ann's Pioneer Schoolhouse,' it offers visitors a tangible connection to early settler life and colonial-era education in British Columbia. Cycling tourists exploring Victoria's compact and bikeable downtown core will find it a rewarding heritage stop within the same precinct as one of BC's premier museums.

notes.Café or food on site: Royal BC Museum Cultural Precinct website lists Sound Bites Concession and The Yummy Truck as on-site food options within the precinct grounds where the schoolhouse is located

visitor.name: Nikkei National Museum & Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: The Nikkei National Museum & Cultural Centre preserves and shares the history and heritage of Japanese Canadians, housed in a multi-use campus in Burnaby that includes a Japanese Canadian garden, gallery spaces, and a research archive. Its permanent exhibit TAIKEN explores generations of resilience, and rotating exhibits highlight community stories. The campus also hosts a Japanese bookstore, a gift shop, and Suzuya Japanese Market.

visitor.name: Nicola Valley Memorial Arena
visitor.desc: The Nicola Valley Memorial Arena is Merritt's primary indoor recreation facility, hosting public skating, minor hockey, lacrosse, and large dry-floor events such as car shows and weddings. The rink operates on ice from August through April, then converts to a dry floor through July, making it a year-round community hub. It is home to the Merritt Centennials junior hockey club and the Nicola Valley Skating Club.

visitor.name: Shoal Centre
visitor.desc: SHOAL Centre is a busy community hub in Sidney operated by Beacon Community Services, serving Peninsula residents aged 55 and older with fitness classes, yoga, woodworking, lapidary, pottery, auditoriums, and a games room. The centre also offers on-site dining and a full suite of senior wellness and support programs. A touring cyclist passing through Sidney could use it as a rest stop for a meal in a welcoming, publicly accessible facility.

notes.Café or food on site: Website navigation includes 'Dining at SHOAL' as a dedicated section; /shoal/ page states 'Whether you're looking for engaging activities or a nutritious meal, our welcoming space is designed to make you feel at home.'

visitor.name: Ambleside D Field
visitor.desc: Ambleside D Field is a fenced outdoor sports pitch within Ambleside Park in West Vancouver, designated for soccer and field hockey. Ambleside Park sits on the waterfront of West Vancouver and is a popular stop along the Seaside route, making this field a navigational landmark for cyclists passing through. The park setting means touring cyclists are likely to pass by this field as part of a broader park visit.

visitor.name: The Rickshaw
visitor.desc: The Rickshaw Theatre is a celebrated live music venue in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside, originally built in 1971 as the Shaw Theatre — part of the legendary Shaw Brothers' Hong Kong cinema empire. Reopened as a concert venue in 2009, it has won multiple 'Best Live Music Venue' awards from local outlets including the Georgia Straight (2018, 2019) and The Whammys (2016–2019). Touring cyclists can catch shows spanning punk, metal, hip hop, folk, and beyond, with full-service bars and a coat check on site.

notes.Luggage / bag storage: FAQ confirms coat check is available ('Do you have a coat check? Yes!')

visitor.name: Museum of Anthropology
visitor.desc: The Museum of Anthropology at UBC is one of Canada's premier anthropology museums, holding an internationally significant collection of Northwest Coast First Nations art including monumental totem poles and ceremonial objects. Perched on the cliffs of Point Grey overlooking the Strait of Georgia, it is housed in a landmark modernist building and draws visitors from around the world. Touring cyclists can reach it via a scenic coastal route along NW Marine Drive, though the museum's own website cautions that the approach involves a significant hill.

notes.Café or food on site: Cedar Café confirmed on site, located up the ramp from the admission desk

visitor.name: The Gardens at HCP
visitor.desc: The Gardens at HCP is a not-for-profit botanical garden and home to the Pacific Horticulture College, set on a scenic property in Saanich near Victoria. Features include a Japanese garden with Takata ponds, a W̱SÁNEĆ Ethnobotany Trail, a children's garden, a gift shop, a library, and an on-site partner restaurant. The ambling garden paths make for a pleasant stop, and touring the grounds takes roughly an hour.

notes.Café or food on site: Partner restaurant The Charlotte & The Quail is on site, with its own phone line and menu at charlotteandthequail.ca

visitor.name: Nanaimo Lawn Bowling Club
visitor.desc: A historic lawn bowling club in Nanaimo's Bowen Park, established in 1923 and still thriving with competitive leagues, social bowls, and drop-in coaching for newcomers. The club describes itself as a premier destination for lawn bowling on Vancouver Island, welcoming all ages and skill levels. Touring cyclists passing through Nanaimo could try a uniquely British Columbian social sport in a well-maintained parkland setting.

visitor.name: TBC Indoor Racing
visitor.desc: TBC Indoor Racing is Greater Vancouver's longest-running indoor go-kart facility, operating since 2000 in a Richmond warehouse. It claims the distinction of being the last venue in the Lower Mainland to offer real gas-powered racing, with karts reaching 75 km/hr on an F1-inspired 11-turn track. Private banquet halls, meeting rooms, and on-site pizza make it a self-contained event venue popular for corporate outings and celebrations.

notes.Café or food on site: Website prominently features a 'New Pizza Menu'; pizza can be ordered for groups during events, and the venue offers catering and 'post-victory lunches' in private banquet halls

visitor.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge Park
visitor.desc: One of BC's most visited attractions, set in a rainforest canyon in North Vancouver. Visitors cross a 137-metre suspension bridge high above the Capilano River, walk through the treetop canopy on elevated boardwalks, and follow a cantilevered walkway along the granite cliff face. A free shuttle runs from downtown Vancouver, making it reachable without a car.

detail.address: 3735 Capilano Road, North Vancouver, BC V7R 4J1

notes.Café or food on site: Three dining options: The Cliff House Restaurant, Loggers' Grill, and On-the-Go

visitor.name: Secwepemc Heritage Museum
visitor.desc: The Secwépemc Museum & Heritage Park in Kamloops celebrates the living culture and history of the Secwépemc Nation through curated galleries, interactive exhibits, and guided tours of the Kamloops Indian Residential School (1923–1977). Visitors can explore traditional craftsmanship, language, and stories spanning generations in a space stewarded closely with Secwépemc elders and knowledge keepers. For a touring cyclist passing through the Thompson region, it offers a rare and substantive encounter with the Indigenous heritage of the land they are riding through.

detail.address: 330 Chief Alex Thomas Way #200, Kamloops, BC V2H 1H1, Canada

notes.Luggage / bag storage: FAQ states: 'Beside the gift shop, there are coat racks and shelves for backpacks. They are not permitted in the museum exhibition galleries. Be aware there is limited storage for personal items.'

visitor.name: Kelowna Memorial Arena
visitor.desc: Kelowna Memorial Arena is a public sports facility in Kelowna, BC, primarily associated with lacrosse. As a City of Kelowna recreation facility, it serves the local community and may offer amenities typical of municipal arenas. Touring cyclists passing through Kelowna may find it a useful landmark or rest stop depending on events and access.

visitor.name: Horticulture Gardens
visitor.desc: The Horticulture Gardens are a botanical and landscaped garden space located on the Thompson Rivers University campus in Kamloops. Listed under TRU's conference centre facilities, the gardens serve both as a campus green space and an event venue. Touring cyclists passing through Kamloops may find it a pleasant short detour while visiting the university area.

visitor.name: Alternatives Gallery and Studio
visitor.desc: Alternatives Gallery and Studio is a collective art gallery and studio in East Vancouver that supports artists with developmental disabilities, operating under the umbrella of posAbilities since 2013. Located just off Commercial Drive on Venables Street, the bright and spacious space features floor-to-ceiling street-front windows, skylights, and exposed wooden beams. The collective has exhibited locally and internationally, including at Vancouver's Eastside Culture Crawl and in Auvillar, France.

visitor.name: FVRL: Muriel Arnason Library
visitor.desc: The Muriel Arnason Library is part of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, serving the Willowbrook neighbourhood of Langley. As a public library, it offers computers, printing, digital resources, and community programming in a welcoming, publicly accessible space. Touring cyclists may find it a useful urban rest stop for connectivity and shelter.

visitor.name: Kyle Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Kyle Centre is one of two main recreation facilities operated by the City of Port Moody, located at 125 Kyle St. It serves as a hub for drop-in programs, registered programs, and community activities, and also houses Recreation Administration offices for in-person and phone customer service.

visitor.name: Pacific Theatre
visitor.desc: Pacific Theatre is a Vancouver professional theatre company founded in 1984 with a mandate to explore spiritual and existential dimensions of human experience through live performance. After more than 30 years at the Chalmers Heritage Building on West 12th Avenue, PT relocated to Granville Island in 2026 and now performs at the intimate 200-seat Revue Stage adjacent to the Public Market. It is a not-for-profit registered charity with an active 2026/2027 season featuring new Canadian works.

visitor.name: VIRL: Gold River Branch
visitor.desc: The Gold River branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library is a small public library situated on the unceded traditional territory of the Mowachaht and Muchalaht First Nations, first opened in 1967 and operating at its current location since December 1992. It is one of the few public amenities in this remote Vancouver Island community and offers free WiFi and public computers to all visitors. For touring cyclists moving through Gold River, it serves as a connectivity and rest point in a town with limited services.

visitor.name: Robson Square Ice Rink
visitor.desc: Robson Square Ice Rink is a free public outdoor ice rink operated by the City of Vancouver, nestled beneath the plaza level of Robson Square in the heart of downtown. It sits at the civic core of the city, surrounded by government buildings, retail, and public art — making it a distinctive stop for cyclists exploring the downtown core. The rink is seasonal, typically operating in winter months only.

visitor.name: Fort Langley CN Station
visitor.desc: Fort Langley CN Station is a meticulously restored 1915 Canadian Northern Railway station and one of the few remaining 3rd Class Type stations in western Canada — the only one surviving from its era in the Langley region. Inside, visitors explore the original waiting room, telegraph office, and freight room, then step aboard a 1947 passenger car and an adjoining 1920s CNR caboose complete with a working model HO railway. Operated by the Langley Heritage Society as a volunteer-run heritage museum, the station sits at the corner of Mavis and Glover in the historic village of Fort Langley, a popular destination on Fraser Valley cycling routes.

visitor.name: Vancouver Tourism Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: Operated by Destination Vancouver (the Metro Vancouver Convention and Visitors Bureau), this is the official visitor information office for Vancouver, located in the heart of downtown at 200 Burrard Street. Staff can help touring cyclists and other visitors plan trips, find accommodations, and navigate the city's neighbourhoods, trails, and attractions. The centre serves as a gateway to resources covering everything from accessible travel to Indigenous cultural experiences across the region.

visitor.name: Hackett Park Stage and Amphitheater
visitor.desc: Hackett Park Stage and Amphitheater is a public outdoor performance venue operated by the District of Sechelt, situated in Hackett Park near the heart of Sechelt on the Sunshine Coast. The open-air amphitheatre hosts community events, summer concerts, and cultural programming. Its park setting makes it a natural stopping point for cyclists exploring downtown Sechelt.

visitor.name: Kiwanis Longhouse
visitor.desc: Gallery 1710 is a free public art gallery housed in the historic Kiwanis Longhouse, operated by the South Delta Artists' Guild (est. 1975), showcasing rotating monthly exhibitions of original work by local and regional artists in styles from watercolour to mixed media. Situated just off Highway 17 on 56th Street, only five minutes from the Tsawwassen ferry terminal, it makes a natural stop on a dike-cycling loop through the South Delta farmlands. Entry is free and guild-member docents are on hand to assist visitors.

visitor.name: Stone Garden
visitor.desc: Stone Garden is a small garden feature located within Stanley Park, one of Vancouver's most iconic urban parks and a magnet for cycling tourism. The park itself is renowned for its seawall loop and network of trails, making this a natural waypoint for touring cyclists exploring the area. As a publicly accessible outdoor feature within a major municipal park, it offers a quiet moment amid a larger cycling destination.

visitor.name: Reginald Hill Park Reserve
visitor.desc: Reginald Hill Park Reserve is a protected nature reserve managed by the Nature Conservancy of Canada, situated in the Salish Sea region near Sidney, BC. It is part of NCC's broader Salish Sea conservation initiative, preserving native ecosystems and wildlife habitat. Touring cyclists exploring the Gulf Islands area may find it a worthwhile natural attraction to visit.

visitor.name: Maple Ridge Leisure Centre Pool
visitor.desc: The Maple Ridge Leisure Centre Pool is a municipally operated aquatic facility within a larger multi-sport complex run by the City of Maple Ridge, offering swimming lessons and drop-in swim programs alongside skating, fitness, and racquet sports. Situated in central Maple Ridge at Haney Place, the facility participates in the city's Smart-Lock Bike Rack program, providing free secure bike parking on-site. For a touring cyclist, the combination of secure bike storage and mandatory pre-swim showers makes this a practical mid-route stop.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Website navigation includes 'Please Shower Before Swimming' as a linked page specifically under Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, confirming showers are available at the facility

visitor.name: Gyro Pool
visitor.desc: Gyro Pool is a seasonal outdoor swimming pool located in Gyro Park in the center of Nelson. The pool operates during July and August with lifeguards provided through a partnership with the Regional District of Central Kootenay. The surrounding Gyro Park features curving flower gardens, a gazebo, and a spectacular rocky-outcrop viewpoint offering a bird's-eye view of Nelson's heritage downtown and waterfront.

visitor.name: Meadow Park Sports Centre
visitor.desc: Meadow Park Sports Centre is Whistler's primary municipal recreation facility, operated by the Resort Municipality of Whistler on shared L̓il̓wat7úl and Sḵwx̱wú7mesh territory. The centre offers a swimming pool, indoor ice skating, weight room, fitness classes, and squash courts, making it a multi-sport hub for both residents and visitors. For touring cyclists, it sits on Highway 99 and represents a rare full-service recreation stop in the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

visitor.name: Okanagan Heritage Museum
visitor.desc: Kelowna's flagship local history museum, the Okanagan Heritage Museum traces the geological formation of the Okanagan Valley, the culture of the syilx/Okanagan people, and the region's trading and settler history — including a recreated window into Kelowna's historic Chinatown. It also houses the Central Okanagan Sports Hall of Fame and hosts rotating exhibitions. As a self-described Biosphere committed entity, the museum actively encourages visitors to arrive by active transportation and is situated in downtown Kelowna adjacent to the Queensway Transit Exchange and near major cycling corridors.

visitor.name: Zuckerberg Island
visitor.desc: Zuckerberg Island is an 8-hectare outdoor heritage park on an island in the Columbia River at Castlegar, reached via a 473-foot suspension bridge built by the 44th Field Engineer Squadron in 1984. The park centres on a unique Russian Orthodox-style Chapel House built by Alexander Zuckerberg, an Estonian civil engineer and self-taught sculptor who settled here decades ago. Woodland paths, picnic tables, carved sculptures, and a layered Indigenous and European history make it a compelling stop in the Columbia River Valley.

visitor.name: Surrey Nature Centre
visitor.desc: The Surrey Nature Centre is a hands-on interpretive facility nestled beside Green Timbers Urban Forest, where visitors can borrow activity backpacks and fishing rods for self-guided outdoor exploration. Inside, a Birds of Green Timbers exhibit introduces local species and the centre maintains a library of field guides alongside a family reading nook with a puppet theatre. Touring cyclists passing through Surrey's trail network may find it a worthwhile stop for a nature-themed break.

detail.address: 14225 Green Timbers Way, Surrey, BC V3T 0J2

visitor.name: Trail Memorial Centre
visitor.desc: Trail Memorial Centre is a large City of Trail civic sports complex encompassing two hockey arenas, a curling club, a full gymnasium, and racquetball and squash courts. The facility marked its 75th year of operation in 2024, making it a longstanding community landmark in the Kootenay region. Touring cyclists passing through Trail may find it useful as a public facility hub, though cycling-specific amenities are not confirmed on the website.

visitor.name: Richmond Public Library, Brighouse (Main) Library
visitor.desc: The Brighouse branch is the main branch of Richmond Public Library, a multi-floor public institution at the centre of Richmond's civic core near Minoru Park. Beyond books, it offers maker-space equipment (3D printers, Cricut machines), study rooms, multilingual collections serving Richmond's diverse population, and free public Wi-Fi. For a touring cyclist, it is a useful urban rest stop with air conditioning and a full suite of digital resources.

visitor.name: VIRL: Woss Branch
visitor.desc: The Woss Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library is a modern public facility that opened in a beautiful new building in December 2020, serving this small community in the unceded traditional territory of the Namgis nation. Part of the 40-branch Vancouver Island Regional Library system, it provides books, digital resources, and meeting spaces to one of the more remote communities on northern Vancouver Island. For touring cyclists, it represents one of the very few publicly accessible stops along this stretch of highway.

visitor.name: Wentworth Villa
visitor.desc: Wentworth Villa is a Carpenter Gothic heritage house built in 1863 and attributed to local architects Wright and Sanders, operated as an architectural heritage museum by the Pacific Northwest Heritage Homes Foundation. Its exhibitions explore Victoria's residential architectural history through artifacts, historic photography, and the stories of the architects and families who shaped the city. The museum won the Heritage BC Conservation Award in 2016 and also hosts guided historic walking tours of Fort Street.

visitor.name: Kerrisdale Community Center
visitor.desc: Kerrisdale Community Centre is one of Vancouver's earliest community centres, jointly operated by the Kerrisdale Community Centre Society and the Vancouver Board of Parks and Recreation since 1943. The facility spans an indoor pool, exercise room, gymnasium, public library, seniors wing, indoor arena (Cyclone Taylor Arena), an indoor play space, and access to Maple Grove Outdoor Pool. Located at West 42nd Avenue and West Boulevard, it sits one block south of the Kerrisdale village business district, making it a convenient urban stop.

visitor.name: Alix Goolden Performance Hall
visitor.desc: The Alix Goolden Performance Hall is the principal concert venue of the Victoria Conservatory of Music, a charitable institution founded in 1964 and located in downtown Victoria. The hall hosts a full calendar of classical music concerts, masterclasses, and student recitals, drawing performers and audiences from across the region. Touring cyclists exploring Victoria's cultural scene will find it a central and accessible live-music destination on Johnson Street.

visitor.name: Fernwood Community and Arts Association
visitor.desc: The Fernwood Community and Arts Association operates from a heritage building in Victoria's Fernwood neighbourhood, housing the Paul Phillips Hall (a 60-seat theatre and music venue), the Little Fernwood Gallery, and several studio spaces. The association hosts live music, art exhibitions, theatre performances, workshops, and community events, and also offers self-guided neighbourhood walking tours covering the area's history dating back to 1843.

visitor.name: Taves Family Farms
visitor.desc: Taves Family Farms is a three-generation working farm in Abbotsford's Fraser Valley offering seasonal agri-tourism experiences across spring, summer, and fall — from tulip and pumpkin gardens to apple orchard u-pick, petting barns, hayrides, and a jumping pillow. Founded in 1990 by the Taves family, it also operates an estate cidery and on-site Country Store. A touring cyclist in the Fraser Valley would find this a distinctive rural detour with food and farm goods available on site.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Country Store & Concession' as an included attraction across multiple seasonal passes; cider sampling also offered on site

visitor.name: Wildhorse Theatre
visitor.desc: Wild Horse Theatre is a heritage building within Fort Steele Heritage Town, a large open-air museum with over 60 historic and reconstructed buildings near Cranbrook on Highway 95. The theatre currently operates as a cooling station and film space showing free short films about local history, with snacks available. Fort Steele Heritage Town is now managed by the Cranbrook Archives, Museum, and Landmark Society (CAMAL) and sits on the ancestral territory of the Ktunaxa people.

notes.Café or food on site: Popcorn, candy, and cotton candy available at the theatre; Fort Steele Heritage Town also has a Food & Beverage department

visitor.name: The Shipyards Skate Plaza
visitor.desc: The Shipyards Skate Plaza is a covered outdoor ice rink operated by the City of North Vancouver, situated in the vibrant Shipyards waterfront district on the North Shore of Burrard Inlet. Part of a larger public space that includes Shipbuilders' Square and a splash park, it draws visitors to one of North Vancouver's most animated gathering spots. It operates seasonally, so touring cyclists would encounter it as a landmark waterfront destination rather than a year-round attraction.

visitor.name: Phoenix Theatre
visitor.desc: The Phoenix Theatre is Fort Nelson's cultural centrepiece — a 250-seat legitimate stage house and cinema opened in 1992 through a community-wide effort, and the only professional live-entertainment venue serving this remote northern community. Operated by the non-profit Phoenix Theatre Management Society, it functions simultaneously as a movie theatre, art gallery, rental facility, and convention centre, drawing over 21,000 visits annually. Touring cyclists passing through Fort Nelson can catch a first-run film or live show in a venue that has hosted Juno Award winners and major touring acts.

detail.address: 5319 50th Avenue South, Fort Nelson, BC V0C 1R0

notes.Café or food on site: Website navigation prominently features 'POPCORN BUG DELIVERY!' and film listings reference popcorn, confirming food/snacks are sold on-site

visitor.name: VPL: South Hill Branch
visitor.desc: The South Hill Branch is part of the Vancouver Public Library system, serving the South Hill neighbourhood along the Fraser Street corridor. As a public library, it provides a welcoming indoor rest stop for touring cyclists passing through this part of Vancouver. The branch is operated by the City of Vancouver and offers a publicly accessible space with no admission required.

visitor.name: Surrey Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Surrey Visitor Centre is the official tourism information office for Surrey, BC, operated by Surrey Tourism. Located at 730 176 Street, it serves as a gateway resource for visitors exploring the region. A touring cyclist arriving in Surrey could use it as an orientation stop for local maps, routes, and area highlights.

visitor.name: Surrey Archives
visitor.desc: Surrey Archives is the City of Surrey's official repository for historical municipal records, documents, photographs, and maps relating to the history of Surrey and its communities. Operated by the City of Surrey under its Arts & Culture umbrella, it serves researchers, genealogists, and history enthusiasts seeking primary source materials. For a touring cyclist, it offers a window into the region's past and is a quiet, air-conditioned stop in a civic facility.

visitor.name: Permaculture Club (Community Peace Garden)
visitor.desc: A small permaculture demonstration garden on the Vancouver Island University campus in Nanaimo, located on the north side of the campus library. Founded in 2008 as the Community Peace Garden and now run by the VIU Permaculture Club, it serves as a space for learning about food growing, seed saving, and traditional ecological knowledge. The garden is designed to be accessible and open to the public on the university grounds.

visitor.name: Sp'áḵw'us Gathering Stage
visitor.desc: An open-air gathering stage within Sp'akw'us Feather Park, an 11-acre oceanfront park at the tip of the Squamish Oceanfront Peninsula. The park features significant art pieces by local and Sḵwx̱wú7mesh artists, an Indigenous-youth-designed playground, boardwalk, and public beach where windsurfing and wingfoiling are permitted. A culturally rich stop near downtown Squamish along the Sea to Sky corridor.

visitor.name: Julie Anne's Art & Framing
visitor.desc: Julie Anne's has been a Chilliwack creative institution since 1984, combining a well-stocked art supply shop — carrying brands such as Golden, Fabriano, Van Gogh, and Heinz Jordan — with a custom framing service and a working gallery. The store also hosts drop-in art classes led by local artists covering acrylics, watercolour, drawing, and mixed media, making it a genuine community arts hub rather than a simple retail stop. A cycling tourist with artistic inclinations could browse original works, stock up on supplies, or join a Saturday morning drop-in class.

visitor.name: Hastings Mill Park Museum
visitor.desc: Housed in Vancouver's oldest surviving building — originally the Hastings Sawmill store, barged to its current Point Grey location in 1931 — this volunteer-run museum holds artifacts from the 1886 Great Vancouver Fire, the historic steamship SS Beaver, and a notable collection of First Nations basketry and carvings. It is stewarded by the Native Daughters of B.C., a non-profit society founded in 1919. A touring cyclist following the Point Grey waterfront would find it a compact but richly atmospheric step into the city's logging and maritime past.

visitor.name: Red Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Red Art Gallery is a free-admission fine art gallery in Sidney, BC, operating out of a unit on Beacon Avenue — the town's main pedestrian-friendly commercial strip. The gallery appears to be associated with artist Marion Evamy based on the website domain. Sidney's compact, walkable downtown makes it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the Saanich Peninsula.

detail.address: 2506 Beacon Avenue, Unit 108, Sidney, BC V8L 3R5

visitor.name: Pender Island Public Library
visitor.desc: A small public library on Pender Island, part of the Southern Gulf Islands Community Libraries network. It serves as a community hub offering Wi-Fi, meeting rooms, printing services, and equipment loans. Touring cyclists arriving by ferry to Pender Island will find it along Bedwell Harbour Road, a natural route from the ferry terminal.

detail.address: 4407 Bedwell Harbour Road, Pender Island, BC V0N 2M0

visitor.name: Chilliwack Curling Club
visitor.desc: The Chilliwack Curling Club has been a community fixture since 1952, growing from a three-sheet facility built with help from CFB Chilliwack into a full community centre with eight sheets of seasonal curling ice. Beyond curling, the building hosts events and gatherings in its banquet halls and meeting rooms, and the on-site 9th End Café serves dine-in meals. The facility also features a fully stocked pro shop, dart boards, and a licensed bar and lounge.

notes.Café or food on site: 9th End Café offers dine-in, buffet service for events, banquet menus, plated meals, platters, and take-and-bake options

visitor.name: South Cariboo Rec Centre
visitor.desc: The South Cariboo Recreation Centre is a multi-sport facility anchored by an ice rink in 100 Mile House, operated by Canlan Ice Sports. It serves as a community hub in the South Cariboo region, offering a range of sport and recreation opportunities. For a touring cyclist passing through 100 Mile House, it represents the main indoor recreation facility in town.

visitor.name: Planet Ice Delta
visitor.desc: Planet Ice Delta is a large four-rink ice sports facility located near the south end of the Alex Fraser Bridge in Delta. It is home to the Delta Hockey Academy (in partnership with North Delta Secondary School) and hosts numerous adult and youth hockey leagues as well as premier tournaments year-round. The complex includes a pro shop, skate sharpening, a health and performance clinic, and food and beverage options — making it a substantial stop for cyclists exploring the area.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists Blueline Concessions and Boomers Bar & Grill as on-site food and beverage venues

visitor.name: Cowichan Regional Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Cowichan Regional Visitor Centre is operated by the Duncan Cowichan Chamber of Commerce and serves as the primary tourism information hub for the Cowichan Valley region. Staffed by accredited travel counsellors, it helps visitors discover local experiences including hiking, biking, kayaking, whale-watching, and the Cowichan wine trail. Located on the Trans-Canada Highway adjacent to the BC Forest Discovery Centre, it also stocks local artisanal products and regional merchandise.

visitor.name: FVRL: Ladner Pioneer Library
visitor.desc: A branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system located in the village of Ladner in Delta. The library offers free public computer and internet access, making it a convenient rest and recharge stop for cyclists on the flat Delta dyke routes nearby.

visitor.name: The Polygon Gallery
visitor.desc: The Polygon Gallery is a contemporary art institution on the North Vancouver waterfront focused on photography and lens-based practices. It moved into its Governor General's Medal-winning building in 2017 after operating as Presentation House Gallery for forty years, and has presented over 300 exhibitions. Admission is always by donation, making it an easy stop for touring cyclists exploring the North Shore.

detail.address: 101 Carrie Cates Court, North Vancouver, BC V7M 3J4

visitor.name: BC Aviation Museum
visitor.desc: The Restoration Hangar is an active aircraft restoration facility that forms part of the British Columbia Aviation Museum, a major Vancouver Island attraction situated beside Victoria International Airport. The museum's broader collection spans over 40 civil and military aircraft, with the legendary Hawaii Martin Mars flying boat as its centrepiece. Cyclists arriving from the Saanich Peninsula trail network will find a full-sized working aviation heritage site, including the opportunity to see restoration work in progress.

detail.address: 1910 Norseman Road, North Saanich, BC V8L 5V5

visitor.name: University of British Columbia Botanical Garden
visitor.desc: Founded in 1916, UBC Botanical Garden is Canada's oldest university botanical garden, spanning 20 hectares and home to more than 5,300 plant species on the western edge of Vancouver. A highlight for visitors is the GreenHeart TreeWalk, with suspended walkways and tree platforms high above the forest floor. The adjacent Nitobe Memorial Garden is considered one of the most authentic Japanese gardens outside Japan, making this a rich cultural and natural destination on any Vancouver cycling itinerary.

visitor.name: Intrepid Theatre Studio
visitor.desc: Intrepid Theatre is a performing arts company founded in 1986, best known for producing the Victoria Fringe Theatre Festival, Vancouver Island's biggest theatre event held every August/September. They also run OUTstages (a queer theatre festival) and an Incoming new-works festival, plus a year-round presenting series at their two downtown Victoria venues. Located on Blanshard Street in the heart of the city, it's an easy stop for culture-seeking touring cyclists passing through Victoria.

visitor.name: Rose Valley Regional Park
visitor.desc: Rose Valley Regional Park is a nature reserve managed by the Regional District of Central Okanagan, located near Kelowna. The park is part of the RDCO's network of over 2,100 hectares of regional parkland with 86+ km of designated trails. It is day-use only, offering a natural setting for hiking and exploring the Central Okanagan landscape.

visitor.name: One Mile Lake Park
visitor.desc: One Mile Lake Park is a nature reserve on the outskirts of Pemberton, also known by its Lil'wat name Snent'. Situated along the Sea to Sky Highway, it offers a natural lakeside setting that makes it a appealing rest stop for cyclists traveling through the Pemberton Valley. The park is managed by the Village of Pemberton and is noted as wheelchair accessible.

detail.address: 7262 Sea to Sky Highway, Pemberton, V0N 2L1

visitor.name: Brennan Park Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: A municipal aquatic centre in Squamish operated by the District of Squamish, featuring a swimming pool and sauna. Located along the Sea to Sky corridor, it offers touring cyclists a potential stop for a refreshing swim in a wheelchair-accessible facility.

visitor.name: Stewart Farmhouse
visitor.desc: Historic Stewart Farm is a City of Surrey-operated heritage site nestled within Elgin Heritage Park along the Nicomekl River, bringing to life the story of a working Surrey farming family from the early 1900s. Visitors can take guided house tours of the Victorian-era farmhouse and stroll through heritage gardens that bloom with seasonal flowers. Elgin Heritage Park is open dawn to dusk, offering a scenic and historically rich stop for cyclists exploring Surrey's agricultural landscape.

notes.Café or food on site: Website navigation lists 'Teas at Historic Stewart Farm' as a distinct program section, indicating on-site tea service is offered

visitor.name: Memorial Arena
visitor.desc: Memorial Arena is a heritage concrete and steel sports arena built in 1948, featuring a distinctive high dual-pitched roof and a red brick entry pavilion with clerestory ribbon windows facing Victoria Street in downtown Kamloops. Designated as a historic place, it has been the home of lacrosse in Kamloops for over seven decades. Touring cyclists with an interest in mid-century civic architecture and local sports heritage may find it a worthwhile stop in the city centre.

visitor.name: FVRL: Aldergrove Library
visitor.desc: The Aldergrove Library is a branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library, Canada's largest public library system by geographic coverage, serving over 800,000 residents across 25 community locations. As a publicly accessible civic facility in a small community, it offers a quiet stop for touring cyclists passing through Aldergrove in the Langley area. FVRL branches typically offer public computers, printing, and community programming.

notes.Wi-Fi: Consistent with FVRL system-wide 'Computers & Printing' service listing, though not confirmed specifically for Aldergrove branch via website

visitor.name: VPL: Central Library
visitor.desc: The VPL Central Library is the flagship branch of the Vancouver Public Library system, occupying the iconic Moshe Safdie-designed elliptical building at Library Square in the heart of downtown Vancouver. The structure — loosely modelled on the Roman Colosseum — is one of the city's most recognizable architectural landmarks and a popular destination in its own right. Touring cyclists will find it centrally located on West Georgia Street, one of the main east-west cycling corridors through the downtown core.

visitor.name: Nelson Museum Archives & Gallery
visitor.desc: The Nelson Museum Archives & Gallery, established in 1902, is housed in a heritage post office and city hall building in Nelson and holds over 7,000 objects of regional historical significance, along with extensive photo, family history, and audiovisual archives. Unique draws include a Cold War bunker exhibit — one of 50 built across Canada — and a walking tour tracing filming locations from the movie Roxanne. Touring cyclists exploring the West Kootenays will find a rich cultural stop with rotating art and history exhibitions, a performance series in the building's historic turret, and an artist-in-residence program.

visitor.name: Bowen Island Historians Museum and Archive
visitor.desc: The Bowen Island Museum & Archives is a community-run institution founded in 1967 that preserves the island's social and natural history through photographs, letters, maps, oral histories, and artifacts. Highlights include the permanent Higgins Cabin exhibit — a two-room recreation of a 1948 logger's life — and a rotating gallery in the Catherine Carter Room. For cycling visitors arriving by BC Ferries, the museum sits a short ride from the Snug Cove ferry terminal and offers admission by donation.

detail.address: 1014 Miller Road, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G1

visitor.name: TRU Library
visitor.desc: TRU Library is the academic library of Thompson Rivers University, Kamloops—one of British Columbia's major post-secondary institutions. It sits on the main Kamloops campus and primarily serves students and faculty. Touring cyclists passing through the city may find the campus a convenient urban waypoint, though cyclist-specific services are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: The ACT Arts Centre
visitor.desc: The ACT Arts Centre is the primary performing arts and exhibition venue serving Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows, operated by Arts On (formerly Maple Ridge Pitt-Meadows Arts Council). It hosts live performances, community events, art exhibitions, and youth arts programs throughout the year. The venue sits near the core of Maple Ridge and draws visitors from across the region for cultural programming.

visitor.name: Lynn Creek Community Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Lynn Creek Community Recreation Centre is a municipal facility operated by North Vancouver Recreation and Culture, serving both the City and District of North Vancouver. The centre features a full gymnasium with an official-size volleyball or basketball court, fitness studios with TRX training anchors, and several multi-purpose rooms including a makerspace. It sits on Hunter Street in the Lynn Creek neighbourhood, a short distance from the popular Lynn Valley trail network.

detail.address: 1491 Hunter Street, North Vancouver, BC V7J 1H3

visitor.name: ORL: Enderby Branch
visitor.desc: A branch of the Okanagan Regional Library in the small Shuswap town of Enderby, with free parking in front and in the Russell Avenue community lot at the rear. The branch has an active Friends group called the Enderby Library Friends (E.L.F.) that funds community programs, a children's mural, and guest presenters. Part of a 30-branch system serving over 399,000 people across 59,600 square kilometres of BC's interior.

visitor.name: Warfield Centennial Pool
visitor.desc: The Warfield Centennial Pool is a seasonal outdoor municipal pool operated by the Village of Warfield, nestled between Trail and Rossland in the Kootenay region. The L-shaped 25-metre pool features a 9'6" deep diving tank and open deck areas for relaxing, set against the Selkirk and Monashee Mountains. For touring cyclists passing through in summer, it offers a genuine open-water swim stop in a community nicknamed 'The Jewel of the Kootenays.'

visitor.name: Okanagan Science Centre
visitor.desc: The Okanagan Science Centre is a hands-on science museum located in Polson Park, Vernon, featuring two floors of interactive exhibits covering physics, chemistry, biology, engineering, and environmental science. It operates a planetarium and offers more than 30 curriculum-aligned education programs for students from Pre-K to Grade 7+. As a registered charity, it also hosts birthday parties, sleepovers, and summer science camps, making it a family-oriented stop on a Vernon cycling tour.

visitor.name: Crystal Pool and Fitness Centre
visitor.desc: Crystal Pool and Fitness Centre is Victoria's main municipal aquatic and fitness facility, operated by the City of Victoria on Quadra Street in a central neighbourhood. It offers a swimming pool, fitness equipment, and a sauna, making it a practical urban stop for touring cyclists seeking a full shower and workout. A city-run replacement project is underway, so visitors should confirm current operations before planning a stop.

visitor.name: Aldergrove Community Museum & Archives
visitor.desc: The Aldergrove Community Archives & Telephone Museum is operated by the Alder Grove Heritage Society, a registered non-profit charity since 1990 dedicated to preserving the history of the Aldergrove region through artifacts, archives, and heritage buildings. The society runs an active digitization programme—including a full run of the local Aldergrove Star newspaper on microfilm—and hosts annual Community Heritage Days. Admission is by donation, making it a low-barrier cultural stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

visitor.name: Rolla Community Hall
visitor.desc: Rolla Community Hall, operating since 1962, is the civic heart of the small rural community of Rolla in northeastern BC. It functions as a rentable community gathering space and event venue, available for private bookings. For touring cyclists on remote roads in the Peace region, it represents a rare community landmark and potential rest point.

visitor.name: Wake Lake Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: Wake Lake Nature Reserve is a protected natural area managed by the Cowichan Valley Regional District near Duncan on Vancouver Island. As a nature reserve, it offers a quiet stop for cyclists riding through the Cowichan Valley, though facilities appear to be minimal or undocumented.

visitor.name: Rivercity Players Stage
visitor.desc: Rivercity Players Stage is a 100% volunteer-run community theatre in Campbell River that stages fall, winter, and spring productions and participates in Theatre BC's North Island Zone festival circuit. The single-level venue features ground-level entry and full wheelchair accessibility throughout the stage, wings, and audience areas. Beyond live theatre, the space is available for facility rentals including private events and business presentations.

visitor.name: Creekside Community Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Creekside Community Recreation Centre is a City of Vancouver-operated facility situated in the Olympic Village neighbourhood at Athletes Way, adjacent to False Creek. The three-storey building sits at the heart of a district purpose-built for the 2010 Winter Olympics and is now a hub for the surrounding community. Its location along one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors makes it a natural landmark for touring cyclists navigating the False Creek seawall route.

visitor.name: City Centre Aquatic Complex
visitor.desc: The City Centre Aquatic Complex is a large municipal aquatic and fitness facility operated by the City of Coquitlam, featuring an eight-lane Olympic-sized lap pool, a free-form wave pool with lazy river and slide, and a relaxation area with dry sauna, steam room, and whirlpool. A full fitness centre rounds out the amenities, making it a practical recovery stop for touring cyclists looking to swim, stretch, or unwind after a long day on the road. The facility also offers adapted aquatics programming and childminding services.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Website directs visitors to 'wash off before you jump in' and links to a 'pre-swim showers' FAQ page, confirming shower facilities are available at the facility

visitor.name: Sointula Museum
visitor.desc: The Sointula Museum traces the 125-year history of a Finnish socialist Utopian settlement on Malcolm Island, housed in the former Malcolm Island Superior School. Three exhibition rooms cover everything from Indigenous presence and early settler life to the fishing industry, a legendary town midwife, and a working 1905 fog-horn from Pulteney Point Lighthouse. Reaching Sointula requires a BC Ferries crossing, making the museum a natural anchor for cyclists exploring this remote island community between Vancouver Island and the BC mainland.

visitor.name: North Bend Community Center
visitor.desc: The North Bend Community Centre is a volunteer-run community hub situated across the Fraser River from Boston Bar, housing a local history museum with records dating back to the 1800s, a thrift store, and a drop-in room with free computer internet access. The museum holds an extensive collection of historical photos, census records, and community memorabilia documenting the area's railway heritage and settlement history. Cyclists touring the Fraser Canyon can stop in to explore the deep local heritage of this small riverside community.

detail.address: 64901 North Bend Station Road, North Bend

visitor.name: Earl Mah Aquatic Center
visitor.desc: The Earl Mah Aquatic Center is Prince Rupert's municipally operated public swimming facility, housed in a two-storey building on McBride Street and managed by the City of Prince Rupert Recreation Department. It serves as the community's primary aquatic venue in one of BC's northernmost coastal cities, a significant waypoint for cyclists arriving by BC Ferries from the south. Specific cyclist-friendly amenities are not documented in available online sources.

visitor.name: Chinatown Storytelling Centre
visitor.desc: The Chinatown Storytelling Centre is a cultural museum operated by the Vancouver Chinatown Foundation, housed in a historic Bank of Montreal building at the corner of Main and Pender Streets in Vancouver's Chinatown. It documents the stories of Chinese Canadians through artifacts, historic photographs, head tax certificates, and interactive exhibits celebrating their contributions to building Vancouver and Canada. The centre also includes Foo Hung Curios, an in-house shop featuring contemporary work by Chinese Canadian designers and artists.

detail.address: 168 East Pender Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 1T3

visitor.name: Nelson & District Community Complex
visitor.desc: The Nelson & District Community Complex is a publicly operated recreation facility managed by the Regional District of Central Kootenay, serving Nelson and surrounding communities. OSM identifies it as a sports centre with an ice hockey focus, suggesting it includes arena ice surfaces alongside other community recreation amenities. Touring cyclists passing through Nelson would find it listed among the RDCK's network of regional community complexes.

visitor.name: Ben Franklin
visitor.desc: The Ben Franklin (PX-15) is a 1968-built mesoscaphe — a pressurized drifting submarine — that completed a landmark 30-day unmanned drift through the Gulf Stream in 1969 and is now on permanent display at the Vancouver Maritime Museum in Vanier Park. The museum occupies a prime waterfront location along the Kitsilano shoreline, a route well-travelled by touring cyclists, and contextualizes the vessel within broader Pacific Northwest and Canadian maritime history. It is one of very few surviving research submersibles accessible to the public.

visitor.name: Capilano Tennis Club
visitor.desc: Capilano Tennis Club is a tennis facility in North Vancouver, tagged in OSM as a sports centre with a perimeter fence. As a member or visitor tennis venue on the North Shore, it sits within a residential area accessible to cyclists exploring the community. Amenity details could not be confirmed due to a failed website fetch.

visitor.name: Shadbolt Centre For the Arts
visitor.desc: The Shadbolt Centre for the Arts is an award-winning, multi-purpose community arts facility set within Deer Lake Park in Burnaby, named after acclaimed BC painter Jack Shadbolt and his wife Doris. It hosts theatre performances, festivals, fine arts programs, and exhibitions, and includes an art supply store on site. The park setting makes it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the Deer Lake area.

visitor.name: Second Beach Pool
visitor.desc: Second Beach Pool is a well-known outdoor public swimming pool located in Stanley Park near English Bay in Vancouver. It operates seasonally in summer and is a popular destination for families and visitors exploring the seawall. Touring cyclists riding the Stanley Park loop will find it a natural rest stop along one of BC's most scenic urban cycling routes.

visitor.name: Juan de Fuca Arena
visitor.desc: Juan de Fuca Arena is a sports centre in the Westshore area near Victoria, BC, identified in OpenStreetMap as a lacrosse facility. As a public arena, it would serve as a landmark and potential rest stop for cyclists touring the western suburbs of Greater Victoria. No further details could be confirmed due to a broken website URL.

visitor.name: Valemount Public Library
visitor.desc: Valemount Public Library is a community hub in this small mountain town, notable for an unusually eclectic 'Library of Things' collection that includes snowshoes, a drone, VR headsets, a telescope, and outdoor summer games alongside traditional books. The library offers computer training and serves as a public gathering space for events, author talks, and community programs. For a touring cyclist passing through Valemount, it represents a welcoming, free public resource in a town with limited services.

visitor.name: McPherson Library
visitor.desc: The Mearns-McPherson Library is the main branch of UVic Libraries on the University of Victoria campus in Victoria, BC, serving students, researchers, alumni, and the broader community. The library offers study spaces, computer stations, media and making facilities, and houses the University Art Collections and Special Collections & University Archives. It is wheelchair accessible and sits on the traditional territory of the Lək̓ʷəŋən (Songhees and Xʷsepsəm/Esquimalt) Peoples.

visitor.name: Blackie Spit Environmental Sensitive Area
visitor.desc: Blackie Spit is a dramatic coastal spit extending into Mud Bay at the mouth of the Nicomekl River, offering sweeping views of Mud Bay and the North Shore Mountains. Operated by the City of Surrey, the park features nature trails, picnic areas, and two fully fenced off-leash dog areas, and is home to the Surrey Sailing Club and the Crescent Beach Swim Club. It makes a rewarding detour for touring cyclists exploring the South Surrey and Crescent Beach area.

visitor.name: Deep Cove Shaw Theatre
visitor.desc: The Deep Cove Shaw Theatre is home to the Deep Cove Stage Society, a not-for-profit community theatre organization that has been entertaining audiences since 1974. Now in its 51st season, it produces four shows annually with an all-volunteer cast in the historic Shaw Theatre at the heart of Deep Cove. The venue offers accessible seating with a designated area for wheelchairs and walkers, and operates a shuttle bus service for patrons.

visitor.name: Charleson Park Community Garden
visitor.desc: Charleson Park Community Garden is a fenced community garden nestled within Charleson Park near False Creek in Vancouver. It is a publicly accessible green space and a pleasant rest point for cyclists riding the nearby False Creek seawall route. The site is fully wheelchair accessible, suggesting a well-maintained and welcoming public facility.

visitor.name: Island 22 Regional Park
visitor.desc: Island 22 Regional Park is a Fraser Valley Regional District nature reserve situated along the Fraser River near Chilliwack, at the area historically known as Island 22 where the Chilliwack River meets the Fraser. The park offers a natural riverside environment popular for walking, wildlife viewing, and off-leash dog areas. For touring cyclists, it provides a scenic natural detour in the agricultural flatlands east of Chilliwack.

visitor.name: VIRL: Bella Coola Branch
visitor.desc: The Bella Coola Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library is a small but long-established public library serving a remote community at the end of Highway 20, the legendary Freedom Highway through BC's Coast Mountains. Originally opened in 1981 with just 4,000 books in a tiny room, it has grown into a community hub now housed in the local Co-op building on the territory of the Nuxalk Nation. For touring cyclists completing the dramatic climb or descent into the Bella Coola Valley, this library represents one of few public indoor spaces in the community.

visitor.name: Kelowna Actors Studio
visitor.desc: Kelowna Actors Studio is a 200-seat professional theatre established in 2003 in Kelowna's Cultural District, producing Broadway-style musicals and hosting youth education programs. The venue offers a dinner-and-show experience with full table service — including appetizers, mains, wines, and cocktails — alongside traditional theatre-style seating. Voted the Okanagan's Favourite Theatre Company and Best Arts Organization, it sits directly across from the Kelowna Public Library in a former packinghouse building.

notes.Café or food on site: On-site kitchen and licensed bar with full dinner table service for evening performances; themed menu per production includes appetizers, mains, beverages, wines, and cocktails. Complimentary dessert served during intermission for table seating guests

visitor.name: Rossland Pool
visitor.desc: Rossland Pool is a public swimming facility operated by the City of Rossland, located on Columbia Avenue in this historic mountain town in the West Kootenay region of BC. Rossland is well known among cyclists for its mountain biking trails and its position along scenic routes through the Kootenays, making the pool a potential refreshing stop for touring riders.

visitor.name: Orpheum
visitor.desc: The Orpheum is a grand 1927 concert hall in downtown Vancouver, best known as the permanent home of the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra, the largest performing arts organization in Western Canada. Designed by architect B. Marcus Priteca, the 2,672-seat auditorium retains its original opulence — sweeping staircases, Romanesque and Gothic arches, a domed ceiling mural, and a giant crystal chandelier. Originally a vaudeville house, it has hosted performers ranging from Fred Astaire to world-touring classical ensembles and is a National Historic Site.

notes.Café or food on site: Website navigation includes a Food & Beverage section; sustainability page references concessions using reusable materials and local products

visitor.name: Richmond Library and Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: The Richmond Library and Cultural Centre is a City of Richmond civic facility combining library services with cultural programming under one roof. Situated in the Minoru area of Richmond, it is part of the city's broader arts and culture precinct alongside the Richmond Art Gallery and Gateway Theatre. Touring cyclists exploring Richmond's flat, well-connected cycling network may find it a useful cultural stop near Minoru Park.

visitor.name: North Peace Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: A community cultural centre in downtown Fort St. John that has been the hub of arts and culture in the region since 1992. It houses a 400+ seat proscenium theatre, the Peace Gallery North art gallery, a café, and a public library branch. For touring cyclists on the Alaska Highway corridor, it offers a notable cultural stop in the northeast corner of British Columbia.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states the centre is 'Host to a Theatre, Café, Library, Child Care and Art Gallery'

visitor.name: Burnaby Village Museum
visitor.desc: The Home Bakery is a historical exhibit within the Burnaby Village Museum, a 10-acre heritage village in Deer Lake Park that recreates early 20th-century BC pioneer life. The museum features period buildings, costumed interpreters, a restored carousel, and rotating exhibits on Burnaby's history. Admission is free, making it an accessible stop for cyclists exploring Burnaby.

detail.address: 6501 Deer Lake Ave, Burnaby BC V5G 3T6

notes.Café or food on site: Mai's Café operates on site (Tuesdays to Saturdays and statutory holidays); an Ice Cream Parlour is also mentioned in visitor survey options

visitor.name: FVRL: Agassiz Library
visitor.desc: The Agassiz Library is a branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library, serving the small community of Agassiz at the eastern end of the Fraser Valley. It is a fully accessible, ground-level building with automatic doors, making it an easy and welcoming indoor rest stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. The library is part of a regional system spanning numerous communities across the Fraser Valley.

visitor.name: Buntzen Lake Recreation Area
visitor.desc: Buntzen Lake Recreation Area is a nature reserve operated by BC Hydro in the Indian Arm area east of Vancouver. The lake and surrounding trails are a popular destination for outdoor recreation, offering a scenic stop for cyclists exploring the Tri-Cities and North Shore region.

visitor.name: Wild Pacific Trail
visitor.desc: The Wild Pacific Trail is an 8-kilometre coastal trail network on the Ucluth Peninsula near Ucluelet, BC, created through the vision of 'Oyster Jim' Martin and maintained by the Wild Pacific Trail Society, a registered non-profit. The trail traverses temperate rainforest, coastal bogs, mudflats, and dramatic ocean headlands, with multiple loops ranging from 0.5 to 5 kilometres. Free guided naturalist walks and an Amphitrite House Interpretive Centre make this a rich stop for cyclists exploring the west coast of Vancouver Island.

visitor.name: MacPherson Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: A heated outdoor pool situated in Lewarne Park in south Burnaby, featuring a 6-lane, 22.86-metre pool with depths from 1 to 3.5 metres and a 1-metre diving board. The facility is seasonal, typically open for the summer, and includes a free wading pool. A touring cyclist passing through south Burnaby could enjoy a refreshing swim and use the change rooms and showers.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Men's and women's shower houses listed under pool features

visitor.name: Fort Rodd Hill and Fisgard Lighthouse National Historic Sites
visitor.desc: Fort Rodd Hill and Fisgard Lighthouse National Historic Sites encompass a 19th-century coastal artillery fortress that guarded Esquimalt Harbour from 1895 to 1956, alongside Fisgard Lighthouse — the oldest permanent lighthouse on Canada's west coast — connected to the fort by a built causeway. The site occupies a dramatic coastal headland near Victoria, surrounded by rare Garry Oak ecosystems and sweeping ocean views. Cyclists exploring the area can tour the grounds and historic buildings via a free self-guided app, and oTENTik glamping accommodations are available inside the working fort for those seeking an overnight coastal experience.

detail.address: 603 Fort Rodd Hill Road, Victoria BC V9C 2W8

visitor.name: Canada Place
visitor.desc: Canada Place is an iconic waterfront complex in downtown Vancouver, originally constructed as the Canadian Pavilion for Expo 86 and now home to a cruise ship terminal, convention centre, and the FlyOver Canada attraction. Operated by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority, it anchors the northern end of Vancouver's famous seawall and offers sweeping views of Burrard Inlet and the North Shore mountains. Touring cyclists arriving via the seawall will find it a natural and prominent waypoint at the heart of the city's waterfront.

visitor.name: Camosun Bog | xʷməm̓qʷe:m
visitor.desc: Camosun Bog is a rare 3,000-year-old sphagnum bog located within Pacific Spirit Park on Vancouver's west side, on the unceded territory of the xʷməθkʷəy̓əm (Musqueam) Nation. The site features a 300-metre nature boardwalk with interpretive signage covering the bog's ecology, Indigenous history, and ongoing restoration work by the volunteer Camosun Bog Restoration Group. Touring cyclists can lock up and walk through a genuinely unusual urban wilderness featuring carnivorous sundews, cloudberry, and other subarctic plant species.

visitor.name: Gulf Islands National Park Reserve – Operations Centre
visitor.desc: Gulf Islands National Park Reserve spans a remarkable southern Gulf Islands archipelago off Vancouver Island's eastern coast, where sheltered Salish Sea waters teem with orcas, seals, and seabirds. The Operations Centre in Sidney is the administrative and visitor information hub for the reserve, which explicitly features cycling, kayaking, hiking, and wildlife viewing among its activities. Touring cyclists can use this office to obtain permits, camping reservations, and information about routes and regulations across the island reserve.

visitor.name: Lido Theatre
visitor.desc: Originally built as Fort St. John's only movie theatre in 1957, The Lido was reimagined as a live-events venue in 2007 and has since become a cultural anchor for the Peace Region. With a dinner-theatre layout, a capacity of 300, and a full stage and bar, it hosts concerts, comedy shows, weddings, and community events year-round. Touring cyclists spending a night in Fort St. John could find evening entertainment here, as it sits centrally in the downtown core.

visitor.name: Ambleside E Field
visitor.desc: Ambleside E Field is an outdoor multi-sport pitch within Ambleside Park in West Vancouver, designated for soccer and field hockey and enclosed by a fence. The field sits within one of the Lower Mainland's most popular waterfront parks, which stretches along Burrard Inlet and is a common stop on the popular Spirit Trail cycling route. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find the surrounding park a natural rest point near the seawall.

visitor.name: West Vancouver Art Museum
visitor.desc: A municipal art museum housed in the historic 1939 Gertrude Lawson house, a stone residence inspired by Scottish castles. The museum focuses on contemporary and historical art, architecture, and design, with rotating exhibitions and a bookstore. Admission is by donation, making it an easy cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through West Vancouver's Ambleside area.

visitor.name: Craigflower Schoolhouse
visitor.desc: The Craigflower Schoolhouse is reputed to be the oldest surviving school building in western Canada, erected during the colonial era as part of the Craigflower Farm operated by the Hudson's Bay Company and converted into a museum as early as 1931. It sits at the edge of Victoria near the Gorge waterway and is recognized through Wikidata and Wikipedia as part of the 'Craigflower Manor and Schoolhouse' national historic site. Touring cyclists exploring Victoria's heritage corridor would encounter a rare pre-Confederation landmark whose history spans colonial schoolmasters, the Gold Rush era, and the early settlement of Vancouver Island.

visitor.name: Surrey Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Surrey Art Gallery is a public contemporary art gallery operated by the City of Surrey, presenting changing exhibitions and permanent artworks by local and national artists. It offers talks, tours, and courses alongside visual arts classes and an UrbanScreen digital art program, making it a culturally rich destination within the Surrey Arts Centre complex. The gallery is wheelchair accessible.

visitor.name: Thornton Creek Hatchery
visitor.desc: Thornton Creek Hatchery is a community-run salmon hatchery operated by the non-profit Thornton Creek Enhancement Society since 1981, focused on enhancing Chinook, Coho, and Chum salmon stocks in Barkley and Clayoquot Sounds. Situated just outside Ucluelet, it offers educational tours where visitors can observe salmon fry and learn about hatchery science and conservation. The site draws particular interest during the fall salmon run, when bears are also frequently present on the grounds.

visitor.name: Holly Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: Holly Outdoor Pool is a seasonal public outdoor swimming pool operated by the City of Surrey, offering public swim sessions and swimming lessons during the summer months. Located in the Holly neighbourhood, it provides touring cyclists passing through Surrey with a chance to cool off on hot days. The pool also offers bookings and rentals through the Tides Out program.

visitor.name: Sunset Rink
visitor.desc: Sunset Rink is a City of Vancouver municipal indoor ice facility in the Sunset neighbourhood of south Vancouver, supporting both recreational skating and ice hockey. As a civic recreation centre, it serves the surrounding community year-round and is managed under Vancouver Parks, Recreation and Culture. Touring cyclists passing through or staying nearby may find it a useful landmark and potential rest stop.

visitor.name: Watershed Park
visitor.desc: Watershed Park is a municipal nature park in Tsawwassen, managed by the City of Delta and listed on the Vancouver Crossing Loop cycling route. It offers a natural green space setting in the Tsawwassen area, making it a potential rest or exploration point for touring cyclists passing through Delta. The park is part of Delta's broader parks and trails network.

detail.address: 11600 Kittson Pkwy, Delta, BC V4E 1C5, Canada

visitor.name: Kuno Garden
visitor.desc: Kuno Garden is a Japanese-style memorial garden in Richmond, BC, operated by the City of Richmond as a municipal green space. Situated near the Fraser River delta, it offers a quiet, contemplative stop reflecting Japanese landscape design traditions. Touring cyclists exploring Richmond's flat dyke trail network may find it a peaceful waypoint.

visitor.name: VPL: Terry Salman Branch
visitor.desc: The Terry Salman Branch is a neighbourhood branch of the Vancouver Public Library system, located in the Cambie Village area near 31st Avenue. As a public library, it offers a welcoming, free indoor space for visitors. Touring cyclists will find it a useful urban waypoint in an otherwise residential corridor connecting the Cambie Street cycling route.

visitor.name: Norval Arena
visitor.desc: Norval Arena (also known as the Nor Val Sports Centre) is Armstrong's community sports facility and home ice/floor for the Junior B North Okanagan Knights hockey team and the Armstrong Shamrocks lacrosse team. The Parks and Recreation Commission office is located upstairs in the arena, administering recreational facilities jointly for the City of Armstrong and the Township of Spallumcheen. For cycling visitors, the arena offers a chance to catch a local game in a small-town BC sporting atmosphere.

visitor.name: Ruby Alton Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: Ruby Alton Nature Reserve is a conserved natural area on Salt Spring Island, protected and managed by the Islands Trust Conservancy to preserve biodiversity and natural habitat. It represents the kind of undeveloped green space that makes Gulf Island cycling distinctive, offering touring cyclists a chance to experience the islands' natural character away from developed areas.

detail.address: Isabella Point Road, Salt Spring Island, BC

visitor.name: Centennial Pool
visitor.desc: A 25-metre, 8-lane outdoor competition pool operated by Recreation Excellence on behalf of the City of Abbotsford. The facility features a rope swing, splashpad, playground, and a covered picnic shelter on the grounds. Fully wheelchair-accessible with ramp water entry, water wheelchair, and barrier-free change rooms—a welcome stop for touring cyclists looking to cool off on a hot day.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Barrier-free shower in change room and accessible shower in family change room; facility accepts drop-in admission

visitor.name: VIRL: Port McNeill Branch
visitor.desc: The Port McNeill Branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library is a public library serving a remote community on northern Vancouver Island, on the unceded traditional territory of the Kwakwaka'wakw peoples. Established in 1972 and at its current Broughton Boulevard location since 1990 (renovated 2006), it is a rare indoor rest point in a small, isolated town. Touring cyclists will find free WiFi and public computers available during branch hours.

visitor.name: Bloedel Floral Conservatory
visitor.desc: The Bloedel Floral Conservatory is a distinctive triodetic dome perched at the summit of Queen Elizabeth Park in Vancouver, sheltering hundreds of free-flying exotic birds and a rich collection of tropical and subtropical plants year-round. Operated by the City of Vancouver through the Vancouver Botanical Gardens Association, it shares ticketing and membership benefits with the nearby VanDusen Botanical Garden. Cyclists exploring central Vancouver's greenways will find it a memorable cultural stop in one of the city's most scenic parks.

visitor.name: Gibsons Curling Club
visitor.desc: The Gibsons Curling Club is a non-profit community curling facility on the Sunshine Coast, founded in 1976 and now celebrating its 50th anniversary with over 200 members across seven leagues. Beyond the curling season, the club hosts summer flea markets, bonspiels, and venue rentals including a licensed lounge and commercial kitchen. It operates entirely through volunteers and keeps fees low to remain accessible to the whole community.

visitor.name: VIRL: Gabriola Island Branch
visitor.desc: The Gabriola Island Branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has anchored island community life since 1999, when it opened inside the bustling Gabriola Folklife Village after replacing a bookmobile and a books-by-mail service. The branch has grown steadily in size and scope over the decades and offers free Wi-Fi alongside bookable meeting spaces. For touring cyclists arriving on the island by ferry, it serves as a convenient public landmark and rest stop in the heart of the village commercial area.

detail.address: 575 North Road, Unit 5, Gabriola, BC V0R 1X3

notes.Wi-Fi: Free Wi-Fi not explicitly restated on the website page but consistent with a public library

visitor.name: Kettle Valley Rail Trail
visitor.desc: The Kettle Valley Rail Trail through Myra Canyon is a converted abandoned railway corridor designated for cycling, featuring a gentle grade and a tunnel section as it winds through the canyon. The trail is famous for its historic wooden trestles and is stewarded by the Friends of the South Slopes Society (FOSS), which maintains trails and signage across Kelowna's South Slopes. A free Myra Canyon Explorer mobile guide with 21 Points of Interest is available, making it a rich destination for touring cyclists seeking history and scenery.

detail.address: Kettle Valley Rail Trail, British Columbia, Canada

visitor.name: Log Amphitheatre
visitor.desc: The Log Amphitheatre is a historic outdoor amphitheatre nestled within Queen Elizabeth Park, one of Vancouver's most iconic green spaces. Set among manicured gardens and towering trees, the open-air venue hosts summer performances and community events against a backdrop of city views. Cyclists arriving by bike will find the park's network of paths connecting to the surrounding neighbourhood.

visitor.name: Price Creek Park
visitor.desc: Price Creek Park is a 7.32-hectare natural conservation area in Surrey's Fleetwood neighbourhood, established to protect the Price and Cub Creek watersheds and over 1,344 metres of sensitive riparian habitat. The park includes a large meadow along 146 Street ideal for picnicking or casual games, as well as natural forested areas. It has been in City of Surrey stewardship since the late 1970s.

visitor.name: Goldstream Welcome Centre
visitor.desc: Goldstream Park is a provincial park just 16km from downtown Victoria, featuring 600-year-old Douglas fir trees, the 47.5-metre Niagara Falls waterfall, and a celebrated annual chum salmon spawning run that draws bald eagles and thousands of visitors. The visitor centre (tagged in OSM as Goldstream Welcome Centre, identified on the BC Parks website as the Freeman King Visitor Centre) offers naturalist-led interpretive programs about the park's natural history. Cyclists will find a dramatic old-growth setting with trails ranging from easy riverside walks to the strenuous summit of Mount Finlayson, one of the highest points in Greater Victoria.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states: 'For your convenience during the summer season, this park has a small concession managed by the park operator.' Seasonal availability only

visitor.name: Mah Society of Canada
visitor.desc: The Mah Society of Canada is a clan/family association community hall located in Vancouver's historic Chinatown on East Pender Street. It serves as a cultural and social gathering place for members of the Mah family association, a type of organization with deep roots in BC's Chinese-Canadian community. Touring cyclists riding through Chinatown will find it embedded in one of the most historically significant urban neighbourhoods in the province.

visitor.name: Native Plant Gardens
visitor.desc: The Native Plant Gardens is an outdoor exhibition garden on the grounds of the Royal BC Museum in Victoria, showcasing plants indigenous to British Columbia. Located in the heart of the city near the Inner Harbour, it offers a quiet green space within walking distance of one of BC's premier cultural institutions. For touring cyclists exploring Victoria's downtown core, it makes a worthwhile and low-key stop alongside the broader museum complex.

notes.Café or food on site: Museum website lists 'Sound Bites Concession' and 'The Yummy Truck' operating on the museum grounds

visitor.name: Maple Bay Campground Amphitheatre
visitor.desc: The Maple Bay Amphitheatre is an outdoor amphitheatre located within Cultus Lake Provincial Park, one of the Lower Mainland's most popular destination parks situated about 90 minutes east of Vancouver. The park surrounds a large, warm freshwater lake backed by forested mountains, with four campgrounds and extensive recreational facilities in the southeast section. The amphitheatre is associated with the Maple Bay campground area of the park.

visitor.name: Mill Farm Regional Park Reserve
visitor.desc: Mill Farm Regional Park Reserve is a nature reserve managed by the Capital Regional District near Duncan on southern Vancouver Island. It protects a rural landscape within the CRD's regional parks network, offering visitors a chance to experience natural habitat close to the Cowichan Valley. Touring cyclists in the area may find it a worthwhile natural detour, though specific on-site facilities have not been confirmed.

visitor.name: Pender Islands Community Hall
visitor.desc: A volunteer-built log post-and-beam community hall set at the edge of a pine forest on Pender Island in the Southern Gulf Islands. It hosts a popular Saturday Farmers Market from May through Labour Day, plus concerts, plays, art exhibitions, and the annual Fall Fair.
