The Bear Mother Welcoming Poles at the entrance and the surrounding farmland setting make it a distinctive stop for visitors exploring the island.

detail.address: 4418 Bedwell Harbour Road, Pender Island, BC V0N 2M1

notes.Café or food on site: Friday Community Café (with Community Gathering Lunch); Monday café during Seniors Activity Day; concession available during film nights

visitor.name: Sointula Resource Centre
visitor.desc: The Sointula Resource Centre is the official Destination BC Visitor Centre for Malcolm Island, a remote ferry-access-only community founded by Finnish immigrants in 1901 as a utopian colony. Operating as a non-profit since 2002, it serves as the island's primary information hub and community services centre. Notably for cyclists, it maintains a fleet of free bikes for visitors and residents to explore the island, and is associated with a MIBike Rental Advisor program.

visitor.name: VIRL: Nanaimo North Branch
visitor.desc: The Nanaimo North Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library opened in July 2014 and has become one of the busiest branches in the VIRL system. Its 17,600 square foot facility houses over 60,000 items in a bright, open floor plan with large windows overlooking a natural environment of local conifers. Bookable meeting rooms with TV connectivity and a laptop bar make it a welcoming community hub along Hammond Bay Road in north Nanaimo.

visitor.name: Q1 Billiards
visitor.desc: Q1 Billiards is an indoor billiards and darts venue occupying a commercial unit in a Richmond, BC shopping complex. It accepts cash, Visa, and Mastercard, suggesting a full-service operation aimed at casual and recreational players. Touring cyclists looking for an evening of indoor recreation in the Richmond area would find both pool tables and dartboards on offer.

visitor.name: Simplex Sportszone
visitor.desc: Simplex Sportszone is a large indoor sports simulation centre in Kelowna's Enterprise Way commercial district, offering over 400 virtual golf courses via Trackman 4, a full suite of multi-sport simulators (baseball, hockey, soccer, and more), and six full-motion 5DOF racing cockpits under the RaceZone brand. The facility is licensed, family-friendly, and caters to groups of up to 40 people with deli food and event packages. It could serve as a rainy-day or rest-day diversion for touring cyclists exploring the Kelowna area.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states the facility is "licensed, offering deli food, snacks, and catered options."

visitor.name: Argyle Village Pollinator Garden
visitor.desc: Argyle Village Pollinator Garden is a community garden in North Vancouver dedicated to supporting pollinators such as bees and butterflies through native and flowering plantings. As a quiet green space tucked into a residential neighbourhood, it offers a pleasant stop for cyclists exploring the North Shore. The garden reflects a growing network of community-led urban greening initiatives across Metro Vancouver.

visitor.name: Capilano River Hatchery
visitor.desc: Built in 1971 to offset salmon stock declines caused by the Cleveland Dam, the Capilano River Hatchery is a federal Fisheries and Oceans Canada facility that draws nearly 250,000 visitors each year. It produces coho and chinook salmon that sustain recreational fisheries in Burrard Inlet and supports ceremonial fisheries for the Squamish First Nation. Set at the end of Capilano Park Road inside Capilano River Regional Park, it sits close to the canyon and the famous Capilano Suspension Bridge, making it a natural stop on a North Shore cycling loop.

visitor.name: Carter Park
visitor.desc: Carter Park is a nature reserve on Bowen Island managed by Bowen Island Municipality. Bowen Island is a short ferry ride from Horseshoe Bay and draws cyclists looking to explore its forested roads and natural areas. The park's exact facilities and trail character are not documented in available sources.

visitor.name: Maple Ridge Museum
visitor.desc: A community museum and archives in Maple Ridge exploring the local history of the area, situated on the traditional territories of the Katzie and Kwantlen First Nations. The museum features permanent and temporary exhibits, a community archives with image search, and also manages the nearby historic Haney House on 224th Avenue. It hosts events like heritage preservation projects and "Music on the Wharf," making it a worthwhile cultural stop along the route.

visitor.name: Gateway Theatre
visitor.desc: Gateway Theatre is a professional performing arts venue operated by the City of Richmond, presenting a full mainstage season alongside community events, educational programs, and venue rentals. It is situated on the traditional lands of the hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓-speaking peoples and serves both Richmond and Greater Vancouver audiences. Touring cyclists approaching from the Canada Line or nearby cycling routes will find the theatre a notable cultural stop in the heart of Richmond.

notes.Café or food on site: Accessibility page references a '2nd floor lobby concession,' indicating food/drink service is available

visitor.name: Creston Valley Seniors Hall
visitor.desc: The Creston Valley Seniors Hall is a community gathering space operated by the Creston Valley Seniors Association in Creston, BC, described in posts as 'the red hall.' It hosts a busy calendar of social activities including weekly Canasta afternoons and a Wednesday quilting group. Touring cyclists passing through Creston will find an active community hub, though it primarily serves local seniors.

visitor.name: Valemount & Area Museum
visitor.desc: The Valemount & Area Museum is a community heritage museum on Main Street in Valemount, a small mountain town at the junction of the Rockies, Cariboos, and Monashees. It documents the history of the Valemount region and its people, offering touring cyclists a cultural stop in one of BC's most scenic interior corridors. Valemount is a natural waypoint on routes between Jasper and the rest of BC's interior.

visitor.name: Vancouver Maritime Museum
visitor.desc: The Vancouver Maritime Museum has occupied a scenic waterfront location in Vanier Park for over 60 years, focusing on the maritime history of the Pacific Northwest and the Arctic. Its flagship exhibit is the RCMP Vessel St. Roch, a National Historic Site sheltered in an iconic mid-century A-frame building, currently undergoing a major revitalization slated for Winter 2026/2027. The museum also stewards Heritage Harbour and the Blue Cabin, making it a multi-site cultural destination steps from the Seawall cycling route.

visitor.name: Texada Island Museum
visitor.desc: The Texada Island Museum, operated by the Texada Island Heritage Society, preserves and presents the remarkably rich history of Texada Island — from First Nations occupation and early Spanish charting to a 19th-century mining boom so scandalous it toppled the provincial government of Amor de Cosmos. The museum also maintains archives and hosts community events, making it a cultural hub for the small Van Anda community that cycling tourists reach via BC Ferries. Admission is by donation.

detail.address: 2003 Waterman Ave, Van Anda, BC V0N 3K0

visitor.name: Planet Ice Maple Ridge
visitor.desc: Planet Ice Maple Ridge is a two-rink public ice facility that opened in 1998 and operates in partnership with the City of Maple Ridge. The main rink, Cam Neely Arena, seats 1,200 spectators and both sheets are full NHL size (85 by 200 feet). The facility hosts hockey leagues, public skating, tournaments, and on-site services including a pro shop, skate sharpening, and a medical and performance clinic.

detail.address: 23588 Jim Robson Way, Maple Ridge, BC V2W 1B8

notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'Concession stands and Break Away Bar & Grill' under Food & Beverages

visitor.name: Community Peace Garden
visitor.desc: A permaculture demonstration garden on the Vancouver Island University Nanaimo campus, located on the north side of the campus library. Originally called the Community Peace Garden, the space has been cultivated since 2008 as a place for learning about food growing, seed saving, plant medicine, and traditional ecological knowledge. The garden is designed to be accessible to as many people as possible and visitors are invited to participate.

visitor.name: PoMo Museum
visitor.desc: PoMo Museum is a community heritage museum housed in a relocated 1908 CPR Train Station on Murray Street in Port Moody, owned and operated by the Port Moody Heritage Society since the late 1970s. The museum features historical exhibitions, a 1921 Venosta train car, and a Meditation Garden, making it a distinctive stop on Port Moody's heritage corridor. Cyclists riding the Shoreline Trail area will find this a culturally rich detour with ties to the railway history that shaped the region.

detail.address: 2734 Murray Street, Port Moody, BC V3H 1X2

visitor.name: Port Kells Community Hall
visitor.desc: Port Kells Community Hall is a publicly operated community hall in the Port Kells neighbourhood of Surrey, BC, run by the Port Kells Community Association. Community halls of this type typically serve as gathering spaces for local events, meetings, and recreational programs. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a useful landmark or rest point, though specific visitor amenities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Kidooland Art Studio
visitor.desc: Kidooland Art Studio is a children's art and music education studio located in Richmond, BC. It is tagged as an arts centre in OpenStreetMap and operates its own dedicated website. Touring cyclists traveling with children may find it a worthwhile stop in the Richmond area.

visitor.name: Cheam Leisure Centre
visitor.desc: Cheam Leisure Centre is a City of Chilliwack-operated community recreation complex offering fitness programs, swimming lessons, and a variety of drop-in activities. It is a multi-sport facility serving Chilliwack residents and visitors. The facility maintains its own dedicated website at cheamleisurecentre.ca and is active on social media.

visitor.name: North Shuswap Community Hall
visitor.desc: The North Shuswap Community Hall is a historic landmark in Celista, BC, built entirely by volunteer labour and completed in 1934 — celebrating its 90th anniversary in 2024. Situated in the picturesque lakeside community of the North Shuswap, it serves as the social and civic heart of the region, hosting dances, concerts, weddings, and community meetings in its main hall (capacity 200), clubroom, and outdoor gazebo. A touring cyclist passing through Celista may find it a useful landmark and community touchpoint, though it primarily operates as a bookable event venue.

notes.Wi-Fi: Wi-Fi available in Main Hall (at additional fee per event) and included with Clubroom rental; tied to hall rental bookings, not a freely available drop-in service

visitor.name: Greg Moore Raceway
visitor.desc: Greg Moore Raceway is an outdoor go-kart track in Chilliwack, BC, established in 2002 and affiliated with the West Coast Kart Club. The venue bills itself as one of the best karting tracks in North America and sits in the Fraser Valley near the dike road network. Named in honour of Canadian racing driver Greg Moore, it offers a recreational motorsport experience for visitors passing through the region.

visitor.name: VPL: Joe Fortes Branch
visitor.desc: The Joe Fortes Branch is a Vancouver Public Library location tucked into the West End on Denman Street, steps from English Bay and Stanley Park — one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors. Named after Joe Fortes, the city's first official lifeguard and a beloved community figure, the branch serves a dense, walkable neighbourhood popular with cyclists. As a publicly operated library it offers a quiet, no-cost indoor space for a touring cyclist to rest, recharge, and get oriented.

visitor.name: Kootenay Trout Hatchery
visitor.desc: The Kootenay Trout Hatchery and Visitor Centre is operated by the Freshwater Fisheries Society of BC, a non-profit that raises and releases trout, char, and kokanee into hundreds of lakes across the province. Located just outside Cranbrook in Fort Steele, the facility welcomes drop-in visitors with self-guided hatchery tours and a seasonal public fishing pond. It is one of six major hatcheries in BC and offers educational programs including Learn to Fish sessions.

detail.address: 4522 Fenwick Road, Fort Steele, BC V0B 1N0

visitor.name: Jonanco Hobby Workshop
visitor.desc: Jonanco Hobby Workshop is a non-profit artisan community workshop tucked just south of Nanaimo, serving Central Vancouver Island with studio space and tools for lapidary, woodworking, quilting, jewellery-making, and painting. Drop-in membership is available, making it accessible to visitors passing through without a full commitment. The workshop spans a wide age range of participants and hosts a rotating calendar of classes and seasonal craft markets.

notes.Café or food on site: Calendar page states: 'Refreshments can be purchased throughout the day' during sessions

visitor.name: Richmond Rod and Gun Club - Indoor Archery Range
visitor.desc: The RRGC Indoor Archery Range is a drop-in and membership archery club welcoming all skill levels and bow types — recurve, compound, beginner, and expert — across up to 8 full shooting lanes at 18m. The facility also hosts an Olympic-style 10m airgun range and has competed at the provincial level, hosting the 2025 BC Archery Indoor Provincial Championships. Equipment rentals are available, making it accessible to cyclists traveling without their own gear.

visitor.name: Jericho Sailing Centre
visitor.desc: Jericho Sailing Centre is a long-established waterfront community hub on English Bay's south shore, providing low-cost access to sailing, rowing, and paddling through rentals, lessons, camps, and affiliated clubs. Cyclists on the nearby Jericho Beach trails will find a lively venue with boat-watching, a rooftop deck, and the public-facing Galley restaurant serving grill fare and craft beer with ocean views. The centre describes itself as 'Vancouver's Ocean Community Centre' and has been a fixture of the city's outdoor recreation scene for over 50 years.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Website states members 'Gain access to showers, changing rooms'; showers confirmed on site but public/drop-in availability not specified
notes.Café or food on site: The Galley — described as a 'relaxed Canadian eatery serving grill fare & craft beer in a picturesque setting with water views' — is confirmed open to the public

visitor.name: Mt. Pleasant Neighbourhood House
visitor.desc: Mount Pleasant Neighbourhood House is a community hub that has served the Mt. Pleasant neighbourhood of Vancouver since 1976, offering programs spanning childcare, family support, literacy, food security, newcomer services, and seniors programming. The building is fully wheelchair accessible on both floors and operates as a scent-reduced, inclusive space. A touring cyclist passing through could make use of the publicly available washrooms and free guest WiFi.

visitor.name: Cranbrook Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The City of Cranbrook's municipal Aquatic Centre is an indoor public swimming facility located at Western Financial Place in downtown Cranbrook. It offers pool programming, swim lessons, and a Leisure Access Program for community members. For touring cyclists, it represents a potential mid-tour stop for a swim or rinse in the East Kootenay region.

detail.address: Unit 3-1777 2nd Street N, Cranbrook, BC V1C 7G9

visitor.name: ORL: Rutland Branch
visitor.desc: The Rutland Branch is one of 30 locations in the Okanagan Regional Library system, a free public library network serving over 399,000 people across 59,600 square kilometres of British Columbia. The ORL offers physical and digital lending, makerspaces, and a Library of Things tech-lending program. As a publicly accessible community hub in the Rutland neighbourhood of Kelowna, it offers touring cyclists a convenient rest stop along Highway 33 West.

visitor.name: Chinese Canadian Museum
visitor.desc: The Chinese Canadian Museum is permanently housed in the Wing Sang Building (1889), the oldest brick structure in Vancouver's Chinatown, originally built by merchant Yip Sang. Opened July 1, 2023, it honours the history, contributions, and heritage of Chinese Canadians through rotating exhibitions and public programs. Its Dream Factory: CantoPop MandoPop exhibition won a 2025 Canadian Museums Association Award for Outstanding Achievement.

detail.address: 51 East Pender Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 1S9

visitor.name: London Farm
visitor.desc: London Farm is a heritage history museum dating to 1880, operated by the City of Richmond on Dyke Road along the Richmond dyke trail network. The site offers a glimpse into early agricultural and settler life in the Fraser delta region. As a free-admission, government-operated attraction situated directly on a popular cycling route, it represents a culturally significant stop for touring cyclists exploring the Richmond waterfront.

visitor.name: Pat Duke Memorial Arena
visitor.desc: Pat Duke Memorial Arena is Lumby's community ice facility, hosting ice hockey, lacrosse, and public skating for residents of the North Okanagan. Operated by the Regional District of North Okanagan, it serves as a central community gathering point in this small Interior BC town. Touring cyclists passing through Lumby may find it a convenient landmark, though it is primarily a local sports venue rather than a cycling-specific destination.

visitor.name: Allan Brooks Nature Centre Lot Plan 25404
visitor.desc: Allan Brooks Nature Centre is a registered Canadian charity perched atop the grasslands above Vernon, offering panoramic views of Okanagan and Kalamalka lakes. A former Upper Air Weather Station converted into one of the Okanagan's leading environmental education destinations, it features scenic bunchgrass walking trails, interactive indoor exhibits on local flora and fauna, and seasonal events including live birds-of-prey demonstrations. Admission is by donation, making it an accessible and memorable stop for a touring cyclist exploring the North Okanagan.

visitor.name: Richmond Cultural Centre Annex
visitor.desc: The Richmond Cultural Centre Annex is a City of Richmond–operated community facility described as Richmond's only dedicated older adult community centre. Located at Minoru Gate, it sits within the broader Minoru Park recreation complex that includes arenas and an active living centre. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's city centre area may find it a useful stop given its public municipal nature and accessible facilities.

visitor.name: Galiano Community Hall
visitor.desc: The Galiano Community Hall is the central gathering place of Galiano Island, hosting concerts, dances, weddings, exhibitions, and ongoing community events in a facility with a recently renovated professional kitchen. In 2015, a bicycle repair station and sturdy bike stand were installed in the upper parking lot with support from the Galiano Island Recycling & Reuse Society, alongside a local island info map — making it a purposeful stop for cyclists touring the Southern Gulf Islands. The hall is operated by the long-running Galiano Club, which also stewards local parks and runs community food programs.

detail.address: 141 Sturdies Bay Rd, Galiano Island, BC V0N 1P0

visitor.name: Tuscan Farm Gardens
visitor.desc: Tuscan Farm Gardens is a family-run lavender farm outside Abbotsford featuring thousands of lavender plants, a labyrinth, lily pond, rose gazebo, and perennial gardens. Visitors can tour the fields, browse the apothecary shop stocked with handmade lavender soaps and skin-care products made on-site, and stop at the covered outdoor cafe for lavender ice cream, drinks, and baked goods. The farm also offers a farmhouse vacation rental and seasonal weddings, making it a distinctive destination on a Fraser Valley cycling route.

notes.Café or food on site: Information and Tickets page describes an on-site cafe serving lavender ice cream, hot and cold drinks, milkshakes, baking and desserts, with a covered outdoor patio adjacent to the shop and additional seating in the gardens
notes.Water without admission: Water bottle refill is offered; the shop and cafe are explicitly accessible without purchasing a garden admission ticket ('You do not need a ticket to visit the shop and cafe'), so refills appear available without paid admission

visitor.name: GVPL: Nellie McClung Branch
visitor.desc: The Nellie McClung Branch is a neighborhood branch of the Greater Victoria Public Library system, located on Shelbourne Street in Victoria and named after the celebrated Canadian suffragist and author. It offers the full range of GVPL physical and digital collections, public computers, and programming. As a free public institution, it provides a quiet indoor stop for touring cyclists passing through the Shelbourne corridor.

visitor.name: Main Hangar
visitor.desc: The British Columbia Aviation Museum is a major attraction on Vancouver Island, situated adjacent to Victoria International Airport in North Saanich, with a collection of over 40 civilian, commercial, and military aircraft documenting BC's aviation heritage. Its headline exhibit is the Hawaii Martin Mars, the world's largest flying boat, with weekly Flight Deck Tours offered on Saturdays. The museum also features a gift shop, children's play area, archives, and is wheelchair accessible.

detail.address: 1910 Norseman Rd, North Saanich, BC V8L 5V5

visitor.name: Nk'Mip Desert Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: The Nk'Mip Desert Cultural Centre (pronounced in-ka-meep) is a state-of-the-art interpretive centre built into the hillside of a 1,600-acre desert conservation area — the largest remnant of the Great American Desert and one of Canada's most endangered places. Operated by the Osoyoos Indian Band, it features immersive multi-sensory theatres, a reconstructed village, a sculpture gallery, and self-guided desert walking trails with views from Chief's Lookout. A touring cyclist passing through Osoyoos would find it a compelling stop for learning about Syilx culture and the unique desert ecology of the southern Okanagan.

visitor.name: GVPL: Oak Bay Branch
visitor.desc: A neighbourhood branch of the Greater Victoria Public Library system located in Oak Bay. The library offers browsing, public computers, and access to a large digital collection including ebooks, streaming, and archival BC newspapers. A quiet indoor rest stop for touring cyclists passing through Oak Bay Village.

visitor.name: CPL: City Centre Branch
visitor.desc: The City Centre Branch of the Coquitlam Public Library is a full-service public branch located in the heart of Coquitlam's City Centre neighbourhood. It offers programs for all ages, a library lounge, room bookings, computers and printing, and an extensive digital collection. For touring cyclists moving through the Tri-Cities area, it represents a potential urban rest stop with public services.

visitor.name: Cleveland Dam
visitor.desc: Cleveland Dam is a concrete arch dam on the Capilano River in North Vancouver, forming Capilano Reservoir, the primary drinking water supply for Metro Vancouver. It sits within Capilano River Regional Park and offers a dramatic viewpoint over the canyon and river gorge below. The dam and surrounding park are a popular destination for outdoor recreationists on the North Shore, accessible via several trail networks.

detail.address: Cleveland Dam, North Vancouver, BC V7S 1A5, Canada

visitor.name: Fort Steele Heritage Town
visitor.desc: Fort Steele Heritage Town is a living history site near Cranbrook featuring a cluster of restored historic buildings — including a general store, bakery, theatre, tin shop, and hotel-turned-museum — along with working livestock and immersive interpretive programs. Now stewarded by the Cranbrook Archives, Museum, and Landmark Society (CAMAL) since April 2025, the site offers guided tours and hands-on activities spread across extensive outdoor grounds. Positioned directly on BC Highway 95, it is a standout cultural landmark for cyclists touring the East Kootenay corridor.

notes.Café or food on site: Bakery on site (named in winter hours listing); Wildhorse Theatre sells popcorn, candy, and cotton candy; dedicated Food & Drink section in site navigation; Food & Beverage Coordinator listed in staff directory

visitor.name: FVRL: Brookswood Library
visitor.desc: Brookswood Library is a community branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system serving the Brookswood neighbourhood of Langley, BC. It offers public computers, printing services, and an extensive digital library catalogue to residents and visitors alike. For a touring cyclist, it provides a quiet spot to rest, access free internet resources, and connect with local community services in the Township of Langley.

visitor.name: Fraser River Discovery Centre
visitor.desc: The Fraser River Discovery Centre is a museum dedicated to the ecology, history, and cultural significance of the Fraser River, situated on the New Westminster waterfront on the traditional territory of the hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ and Halq̓eméylem speaking peoples. The centre offers permanent and temporary exhibits, Indigenous education programming, guided tours, and summer camps. A touring cyclist following the Fraser River route would find this a meaningful cultural stop along the waterfront.

visitor.name: Gabriola Museum
visitor.desc: The Gabriola Museum is a community heritage institution operated by the Gabriola Historical and Museum Society, telling the stories of Gabriola Island's Indigenous Snuneymuxw people and settler communities through exhibits, archives, and events. Founded in 1986 and opened in 1995 on land donated by the McRae family, the museum also stewards 19 acres of conservation covenant land and features a gift shop with locally made goods. Cyclists arriving by BC Ferry from Nanaimo face a 1.2 km uphill ride from the Descanso Bay dock to reach the museum.

visitor.name: North Peace Leisure Pool
visitor.desc: North Peace Leisure Pool is a City of Fort St. John-operated public aquatic and leisure centre serving the communities of the Peace River region in northeastern BC. It is the main publicly accessible swimming facility in Fort St. John and is managed under the city's parks and recreation department. For touring cyclists, it represents a potential stop for a swim or refresh in a remote part of the province.

visitor.name: Ucluelet Aquarium
visitor.desc: The Ucluelet Aquarium holds the distinction of being Canada's first collect-and-release aquarium, returning all its marine animals to local waters at the end of each season. Situated on the traditional territory of the Yuułuʔiłʔatḥ – Ucluelet First Nation, it offers hands-on encounters with fish and invertebrates drawn from Clayoquot and Barkley Sounds. For cyclists exploring the west coast of Vancouver Island, it is a compelling cultural and natural-history stop in the heart of Ucluelet village.

visitor.name: Metro Theatre
visitor.desc: Metro Theatre is a community theatre in Vancouver's Marpole neighbourhood that has been producing comedies, mysteries, and musicals since its founding in 1963 by a collective of local theatre groups. The 300-seat auditorium and 50-person upstairs lounge host a full annual season of performances ranging from musicals to classic mysteries. It has served as a launching pad for many artists who have gone on to careers in theatre, film, and television.

notes.Café or food on site: Volunteers handle concession operations (mentioned in 'Who We Are'); upstairs lounge with capacity of 50 noted on Plan Your Visit page

visitor.name: Wongs' Benevolent Association
visitor.desc: The Wongs' Benevolent Association of Canada (加拿大黄氏宗親總會) is a nonprofit community organization in Vancouver's historic Chinatown dedicated to preserving the history and stories of early Chinese Canadian immigrants from the Wong clan. Located in the heart of Chinatown on East Pender Street, it serves as a cultural and community hub that has been part of the neighbourhood for generations. A touring cyclist exploring Chinatown would find it a meaningful stop for understanding the area's deep Chinese Canadian heritage.

detail.address: 123A East Pender Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 1T6

visitor.name: Saturna Library
visitor.desc: Saturna Library is a small community library located in the basement of a local church on Saturna Island, operating as a partner branch within the Southern Gulf Islands Community Libraries network. It offers free Wi-Fi and access to digital collections including ebooks and eAudiobooks. For cycling tourists exploring the Southern Gulf Islands, it serves as one of the few public gathering points on this lightly serviced island.

detail.address: 140 East Point Road, Saturna Island, BC V0N 2Y0

visitor.name: Malahat Skywalk
visitor.desc: Malahat Skywalk is a forest-to-sky attraction that opened in 2021 along the Trans-Canada Highway on Vancouver Island, roughly 35 minutes from Victoria. Visitors ascend through coastal forest via a treewalk and spiral tower to a 360° summit platform, with extras including a glass-cube overhang suspended above the Salish Sea and a 20-metre slide. The site is consistently awarded TripAdvisor Travellers' Choice honours and is designed for full accessibility, with wide, paved pathways suitable for strollers and wheelchairs.

notes.Café or food on site: Dedicated 'Food & Beverage' section listed in site navigation; homepage references 'plenty of spots to pause, refuel, and regroup' on site

visitor.name: Walled Garden
visitor.desc: The Walled Garden is a garden feature within Hatley Park, a magnificent Edwardian estate and National Historic Site situated on 565 oceanfront acres just 25 minutes from downtown Victoria. The grounds are home to Royal Roads University and encompass Italian, Japanese, and Rose gardens, old-growth forest trails, biking trails, and the iconic Hatley Castle. Cycling tourists will find a scenic and historically rich destination with the Olympic Mountains visible across the Strait of Juan de Fuca.

notes.Café or food on site: Habitat Café on site — website lists it under Visit Us and describes it as 'Enjoy a snack at our café'

visitor.name: VIRL: Courtenay Branch
visitor.desc: The Courtenay Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library is a civic landmark in the heart of downtown Courtenay, recognized for its striking wood beam architecture that locals liken to the historic Creamery building that once stood in the area. Situated on the unceded traditional territories of the K'ómoks First Nation, it is described on its own website as a popular attraction for both residents and visitors. The branch offers meeting room bookings, technology help, and a broad range of library services through the Vancouver Island Regional Library system.

visitor.name: RayCam Co-operative Centre
visitor.desc: RayCam Co-operative Centre is a City of Vancouver community centre serving the Strathcona neighbourhood on East Hastings Street. It offers recreational and community programming in one of Vancouver's most historically significant and densely cycled urban corridors. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find public washrooms on site.

visitor.name: Centre of International Contemporary Art Vancouver
visitor.desc: CICA Vancouver is a non-profit, BIPOC and female-led contemporary art organization founded in 2021 in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, dedicated to showcasing international and local contemporary artists through three to four seasonal exhibitions per year. The gallery bridges local and global creative communities, regularly featuring immersive and large-scale works by artists such as James Turrell, James Jean, and Ayako Rokkaku. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a compact, accessible gallery with a rotating program of ambitious international art just steps from the downtown core.

visitor.name: Lower Mount Erskine Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: Lower Mount Erskine Nature Reserve is a protected natural area on Salt Spring Island managed by the Islands Trust, preserving forest and ecological habitat on the lower slopes of Mount Erskine. The reserve forms part of a broader conservation corridor on one of BC's most popular Gulf Islands cycling destinations. Touring cyclists riding Salt Spring Island's hilly roads may find the reserve a rewarding natural waypoint, though visitor infrastructure details are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: VPL: nə́c̓aʔmat ct Strathcona Branch
visitor.desc: The nə́c̓aʔmat ct Strathcona Branch is a Vancouver Public Library location serving the historic Strathcona neighbourhood at the edge of the Downtown Eastside. As a public library, it offers a welcoming, free indoor space where cyclists can rest, use public computers, and access resources. The branch name honours the Indigenous place name for the area, reflecting the community it serves.

visitor.name: Castlegar & District Public Library
visitor.desc: The Castlegar & District Public Library is a free public institution in downtown Castlegar serving the city and surrounding Regional Districts H, I, and J in the West Kootenay. It offers an unusually broad range of services for a small-town library, including a 'Library of Things' lending collection, meeting room rentals, and computers with printing. For touring cyclists passing through Castlegar, it provides a welcoming indoor space in the heart of a hub town.

visitor.name: Canadian Lacrosse Hall of Fame
visitor.desc: The Canadian Lacrosse Hall of Fame is a non-profit museum chartered in 1964 by the Canadian Lacrosse Association and located in New Westminster, the historic heart of Canadian lacrosse. It preserves artifacts, stories, and records celebrating players, builders, and teams who shaped Canada's national summer sport, with roots tracing back to First Nations origins. Touring cyclists interested in Canadian sports heritage can explore physical and virtual exhibits, inductee galleries, and a comprehensive lacrosse timeline.

detail.address: 777 Columbia Street, New Westminster, BC V3M 1B6

visitor.name: Squamish Lil'wat Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: The Squamish Lil'wat Cultural Centre celebrates the living cultures of the Sḵwx̱wú7mesh (Squamish) and Líl̓wat7úl (Lil'wat) First Nations through the Great Hall, story poles, canoes, regalia, and hourly guided tours led by Cultural Ambassadors. It sits on the shared traditional territories of both nations in Whistler's Upper Village, offering a distinctive lens on the mountain landscape that surrounds it. The admission-free Thunderbird Café serves Indigenous-inspired cuisine — including bannock tacos and cedar plank salmon chowder — and is open to the public regardless of museum admission.

notes.Café or food on site: Thunderbird Café is located downstairs in the admission-free area of the SLCC; serves bannock tacos, venison chili, salmon chowder, and other Indigenous-inspired dishes

visitor.name: Fairfield Community Place
visitor.desc: Fairfield Community Place is the neighbourhood house of the Fairfield Gonzales Community Association, a non-profit serving the Fairfield and Gonzales neighbourhoods of Victoria since 1975. The single-storey building hosts a wide range of community programs including licensed childcare, youth drop-ins, community gardens, and neighbourhood events. It sits in a quiet residential area of Victoria near the waterfront.

visitor.name: Grandview Heights Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: A municipal aquatic centre in Surrey's Grandview Heights neighbourhood, operated by the City of Surrey. The facility features a swimming pool with a family hot tub and a weight room, open for drop-in use. Touring cyclists passing through south Surrey may appreciate the chance to take a refreshing swim and stretch out in the weight room.

visitor.name: Peachland Museum
visitor.desc: Housed in a unique 8-sided former Baptist Church built by volunteers in 1910, the Peachland Museum has served the community since 1980 and was declared an official British Columbia Heritage site in 1981. Hundreds of historical artifacts, photographs, newspapers, and documents offer a glimpse into Peachland's pioneer history. The upper floor features a scale model of the Kettle Valley Railway as it existed between 1955 and 1965, which would be of particular interest to cyclists riding the KVR trail.

visitor.name: Richmond Olympic Experience
visitor.desc: The Richmond Olympic Experience is North America's first Olympic Museum Network member, housed inside the Richmond Olympic Oval that hosted long-track speed skating during the 2010 Vancouver Winter Games. Spanning three levels with over 30 exhibits, it blends artifact galleries with hands-on physical challenges and 180° virtual sport simulators — including Olympic bobsleigh, whitewater kayak, and sit-ski. A touring cyclist can pause their ride to test stickhandling skills, view historic Olympic medals up close, and explore Canada's full sport story in one immersive stop.

visitor.name: Deeley Motorcycle Exhibition
visitor.desc: The Deeley Motorcycle Exhibition houses Canada's largest privately-owned collection of vintage motorcycles, spanning over 100 years of motorcycling history with machines of all makes and models from Trev Deeley's personal collection. The Deeley family's commercial roots go back to 1914 when Fred Deeley originally sold bicycles before pivoting to motorcycles, giving the venue an interesting connection to two-wheeled transport history. Located just off Highway 1 on the Vancouver/Burnaby border with free onsite parking, it offers an interactive exhibit where visitors can sit on a display bike for photos.

visitor.name: AMS Nest (Student Union Building)
visitor.desc: The AMS Nest is the student union building of UBC Vancouver, operated by the Alma Mater Society — Canada's largest student union, founded in 1915. Situated at the heart of the UBC campus, it is a multi-storey community hub housing restaurants, shops, event spaces, and student support services, making it a natural gathering point for cyclists exploring the UBC endowment lands. The building hosts a lively year-round calendar of public events and offers a range of food and retail options.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Places To Eat' as a top-level quick link and 'Order Online' under the Food section; recurring public events are held at The Gallery Patio and Lounge, confirming on-site food and beverage services

visitor.name: TNRL: North Kamloops Library
visitor.desc: The North Kamloops Library is a branch of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system, serving the North Kamloops neighbourhood since 2010. It offers free public Wi-Fi, public computers, printing, and a wheelchair-accessible space — making it a practical rest stop for touring cyclists needing connectivity or a quiet break. The library is currently open during a phased interior refresh project, though some collections and meeting rooms are temporarily unavailable.

visitor.name: Surrey Arts Centre
visitor.desc: Surrey Arts Centre is a City of Surrey arts hub that brings together the Surrey Art Gallery, Surrey Civic Theatres' Main Stage and Studio Theatre, and the SPARK Stages weekend programming for kids and families. Visitors can explore contemporary and permanent art exhibitions, attend live performances by actors, dancers, and musicians, or take art classes. Many gallery events and tours are free, making it a low-barrier cultural stop for cyclists passing through the area.

visitor.name: Sunshine Coast Museum & Archives
visitor.desc: The Sunshine Coast Museum & Archives is a community-driven heritage institution in the heart of Gibsons Landing, about 10 minutes from the BC Ferries terminal at Langdale. Spread across two floors, it presents exhibits on First Nations history, early logging, marine transportation, beachcomber relics, and over 9,000 archival photographs and documents. A touring cyclist coming off the ferry will find it a compelling introduction to the region's layered history, with a gift shop and virtual museum resources as well.

visitor.name: GVPL: Goudy Branch
visitor.desc: The Goudy Branch is one of the Greater Victoria Public Library's community branches, serving the Langford/Goldstream corridor in the western CRD. It offers physical and digital collections, public computers, and regular programming in a publicly accessible storefront location. For touring cyclists passing through the Westshore, it provides a quiet indoor stop with free Wi-Fi and computer access.

visitor.name: VPL: Carnegie Branch
visitor.desc: The Carnegie Branch is a Vancouver Public Library location housed inside the historic Carnegie Centre building at Main and Hastings, a landmark 1903 Carnegie library in the heart of Vancouver's Downtown Eastside. It serves as both a public library and part of a broader community centre complex, making it a well-used stop in one of the city's most densely walkable and transit-rich neighbourhoods. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find it a convenient urban rest point.

visitor.name: Harbour Centre Lookout Tower
visitor.desc: Vancouver Lookout is a 168-metre observation tower atop Harbour Centre in downtown Vancouver, opened in 1977 and inaugurated by Neil Armstrong — at the time the tallest building in the city. A glass elevator whisks visitors to a 360° deck with views spanning Stanley Park, Gastown, the North Shore Mountains, and the working port. Centrally located across from Waterfront Station, it makes a natural landmark stop mid-ride for cyclists exploring the downtown core or Seawall.

visitor.name: Emily Carr House
visitor.desc: Emily Carr House is a beautifully restored provincial and national historic site in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood, marking the birthplace of renowned Canadian artist and writer Emily Carr. The heritage building and gardens now operate as a vibrant cultural centre offering guided and self-guided tours, educational programs, and community events inspired by Carr's themes of art, nature, and indigenous peoples. It is a notable stop for cyclists exploring Victoria's historic south end, located steps from the Inner Harbour.

detail.address: 207 Government Street, Victoria, British Columbia V8V 2K8, Canada

visitor.name: Yellow Point Park
visitor.desc: Yellow Point Park is a nature reserve on Vancouver Island near Ladysmith, managed by the Cowichan Valley Regional District. It sits within a region popular with touring cyclists for its quiet roads and coastal scenery. As a CVRD-operated natural area, it offers a potential rest or exploration stop along routes through the Cowichan Valley.

visitor.name: Lokier Gardens
visitor.desc: Lokier Gardens is a heritage garden located in the District of Oak Bay, recognized on the municipality's list of historic sites. Situated in the Victoria area, it represents a preserved piece of Oak Bay's horticultural and residential heritage. A touring cyclist passing through Oak Bay might visit as a quiet scenic stop amid the neighbourhood's tree-lined streets.

visitor.name: Finnerty Gardens
visitor.desc: Finnerty Gardens is a free, publicly accessible botanical garden on the southwest edge of the University of Victoria campus, renowned for its collection of over 4,000 trees and shrubs including more than 1,500 rhododendron and azalea varieties. Open every day of the year at no charge, the gardens offer a self-guided walking tour by PDF and a tranquil setting for anyone seeking a peaceful stop on a ride through Victoria. The garden has deep historical roots tied to Lake Cowichan and is stewarded by a volunteer Friends group that funds ongoing enhancements.

visitor.name: SL: Newton Branch
visitor.desc: Newton Branch is a 15,800 sq ft public library operated by Surrey Libraries in the Newton neighbourhood of Surrey. The branch is fully accessible and offers free public Wi-Fi, computers, a scanner, and mobile printing services. A 24-hour book return is available, and the branch hosts local artists and regularly scheduled community programs.

visitor.name: Horticulture Centre of the Pacific
visitor.desc: A 103-acre site in Saanich featuring over nine acres of cultivated gardens including Japanese-style Takata Garden, a Zen Garden, Rhododendron and Heather gardens, plus conservation parkland with nature trails, wetlands, and birding areas. Home to the accredited Pacific Horticulture College, HCP also features the W̱SÁNEĆ Ethnobotany Trail highlighting Indigenous plant knowledge. The gardens have been in bloom since 1983 and include a gift shop, library, and on-site restaurant.

notes.Café or food on site: Website navigation includes a 'Restaurant' menu item under the Visit section

visitor.name: Courtenay & District Museum
visitor.desc: Home of BC's Provincial Fossil, this combined museum and palaeontology centre has spent over 60 years interpreting the natural and cultural heritage of the Comox Valley. Highlights include the Great Elasmosaur find, guided fossil tours that travel 80 million years back in time, and a rotating gallery of exhibits spanning First Nations history, local industry, and natural science. Located on 4th Street in downtown Courtenay, it is an easy stop for cyclists riding through the Comox Valley.

visitor.name: Ukama Gallery
visitor.desc: Ukama Gallery is a free-admission contemporary art gallery on Granville Island specializing in original stone sculptures by over 200 emerging and world-renowned artists from Zimbabwe, alongside paintings and mixed media works by Canadian artists. Opened in 2015, the gallery takes its name from a Shona word for the bonds of an extended family, reflecting its mission to foster personal connections between visitors and African art. Situated in the heart of Granville Island—a hub accessible by bike path, ferry, and transit—it offers a culturally distinctive stop on Vancouver's waterfront cycling circuit.

visitor.name: Zipzone Peachland
visitor.desc: ZipZone Peachland is an adventure park perched above Deep Creek Gorge near Peachland, BC, featuring six ziplines described as among Canada's highest, longest, and fastest at 381 feet above the gorge. Beyond ziplining, the site offers a dynamic climbing wall, ninja course, and games area. Access requires driving a partly rough road for the final 2 km to the site.

detail.address: 5875 Brenda Mines Rd, Peachland, British Columbia V0H 1X1

visitor.name: Queen's Park Arena
visitor.desc: Queen's Park Arena is a historic indoor ice rink operated by the City of New Westminster, dating to 1930 and seating up to 3,500 spectators. One of the older arenas still in use in Metro Vancouver, it hosts community hockey, skating, and events. A touring cyclist arriving in New Westminster could visit as a heritage sports landmark in the Queen's Park neighbourhood.

visitor.name: Leigh Square Community Arts Village
visitor.desc: Leigh Square Community Arts Village is a City of Port Coquitlam cultural facility hosting arts programming, community events, and performances. It serves as a civic gathering hub in the heart of PoCo and is connected to the broader city recreation network. The square is associated with the 'Music in the Square' and other public outdoor events listed on the city's calendar.

detail.address: 2253 Leigh Square Pl, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 3B8

visitor.name: Ocean Park Community Orchard
visitor.desc: Ocean Park Community Orchard is a small, resident-initiated orchard established in 2016 on the northern lot of Ocean Park Terrace park in South Surrey. The surrounding green space features large open fields suitable for a rest or picnic stop. The site is publicly accessible and managed by the City of Surrey.

visitor.name: Clover Point
visitor.desc: Clover Point is a prominent coastal headland on Victoria's southern waterfront, managed by the City of Victoria and sitting along the Dallas Road seafront corridor. It is a popular stop for cyclists riding the waterfront route, offering open views across the Strait of Juan de Fuca toward the Olympic Mountains. The exposed grassy point is well known locally as a prime spot for kite flying and watching marine traffic.

visitor.name: Pemberton Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Pemberton & District Community Centre is a municipally operated recreation hub serving Pemberton and the surrounding district, offering fitness classes, drop-in activities, and programs for all ages. It houses a fitness centre and is the primary indoor recreation facility for the community at the base of the Sea-to-Sky corridor north of Whistler. Accessible recreation programming is listed as a service, and the OSM record notes wheelchair accessibility.

visitor.name: The Chinese Freemasons
visitor.desc: The Chinese Freemasons is a historic fraternal organization and community hall located in the heart of Vancouver's Chinatown on East Pender Street. Founded in the 19th century, it has deep roots in the Chinese-Canadian community and occupies a building of significant cultural heritage value. Touring cyclists passing through Chinatown will find it a notable landmark in one of North America's oldest and most storied Chinatowns.

visitor.name: Tsawwassen Arts Centre
visitor.desc: The Tsawwassen Arts Centre is a municipally operated arts facility run by the City of Delta, serving the Tsawwassen community with cultural programming and events. Located in the southwest corner of Metro Vancouver near the Tsawwassen ferry terminal, it sits in an area frequently traversed by touring cyclists travelling to or from Vancouver Island. As a community arts venue, it may offer a cultural rest stop for cyclists exploring the South Delta area.

visitor.name: Sunken Rose Garden
visitor.desc: The Sunken Rose Garden is one of more than 20 gardens on the Government House estate in Victoria's Rockland neighbourhood, the official residence of BC's Lieutenant Governor. The gardens were originally designed in 1911 and later redesigned in the style of traditional English gardens; they are maintained by a dedicated volunteer society. The entire grounds are open to the public year-round and free to visit, making them an easy stop for touring cyclists exploring Victoria.

notes.Café or food on site: Rudi's Tea Room is listed as an on-site amenity at Government House

visitor.name: FVRL: Boston Bar Library
visitor.desc: The Boston Bar Library is a small community branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library, the largest public library system in British Columbia, serving the Boston Bar and surrounding Nlaka'pamux territory. Cyclists passing through this remote Fraser Canyon community can stop in for free WiFi, public computers, and copying/printing/scanning services. The branch offers outdoor bike racks, making it a practical rest stop on an otherwise isolated stretch of highway.

detail.address: 47632 Old Boston Bar Road, Boston Bar, BC V0K 1C0

visitor.name: gallery2
visitor.desc: A public art gallery housed in a handsome 1911 Edwardian provincial courthouse in downtown Grand Forks, operating since 1984 and featuring exhibitions by local, regional, and national artists. The building also hosts the Grand Forks Visitor Centre, where touring cyclists can pick up maps, guides, and trip-planning help for the Boundary–Kootenay region. There is a gift shop on site and the gallery offers a rotating program of exhibitions and community art events.

detail.address: 524 Central Avenue, Grand Forks, BC V0H 1H0

visitor.name: Peachland Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Peachland Community Centre is a municipal facility operated by the District of Peachland, featuring a large main hall seating over 500 and a banquet room for 118, plus a commercial kitchen and stage. It sits along the Okanagan Lake corridor and offers shower facilities, which could be of interest to touring cyclists passing through the small lakeside community of Peachland.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Shower facilities listed under Facility Features on the community centre page; unclear whether available on a drop-in basis or only for renters

visitor.name: Canso Bomber Crash Site
visitor.desc: The Canso Bomber Crash Site preserves the remarkably intact wreckage of RCAF Canso 11007, a WWII-era flying boat that crashed on a hillside shortly after takeoff on February 12, 1945. The 5km return trail from Radar Hill passes through a notoriously muddy bog, a creepy abandoned wartime building, and a bomb-crater pond before reaching the fuselage, which visitors can climb into and inspect. It is one of the most unusual and historically evocative hikes on the west coast of Vancouver Island.

visitor.name: V-Zone Tactical Laser Tag
visitor.desc: Nu-Zone (V-Zone) Tactical Laser Tag is an indoor combat-simulation entertainment venue pioneered in 2016 as the first of its kind in Western Canada, using equipment originally developed for law enforcement and military tactical training. Its 15,000-square-foot facility features a 10,000-square-foot main battlefield with multi-level structures, plus electronic darts, billiards, and arcade machines. Private event bookings and public drop-in sessions are both available, making it a potential rainy-day destination for touring cyclists passing through Richmond.

visitor.name: Firehall Arts Centre
visitor.desc: The Firehall Arts Centre is one of Vancouver's oldest arts venues, housed in a converted heritage firehall in the Downtown Eastside and presenting theatre, dance, music, comedy, and community events. It is a producing and presenting house with capacity for 175, championing local and Indigenous storytelling on unceded Musqueam, Squamish, and Tsleil-Waututh territory. A touring cyclist exploring Vancouver's DTES cultural corridor would find a lively, year-round performance calendar here.

visitor.name: Kokanee Creek Provicial Park Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The visitor centre and nature centre at Kokanee Creek Provincial Park sits right on Highway 3A between Nelson and the Kootenay Lake ferry at Balfour, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists on this popular Kootenay route. The park features over a kilometre of sandy Kootenay Lake beach, old-growth cedar forest, a canyon with viewing platform, and a spawning channel where kokanee salmon run from mid-August to mid-September. The nature centre offers environmental education programs, a gift shop, and coffee during the summer season.

detail.address: Hwy 3A, 19 km east of Nelson, BC

notes.Café or food on site: Nature centre offers coffee and a gift shop (seasonal, mid-May to mid-September)
notes.Wi-Fi: Nature centre offers WiFi access (seasonal, mid-May to mid-September)

visitor.name: White Rock Sea Tours and Whale Watch Vancouver
visitor.desc: White Rock Sea Tours is a family-owned marine tour company operating from Crescent Beach Marina in Surrey, roughly 30 minutes south of Vancouver. They run small-group Zodiac expeditions to the Canadian Gulf Islands and US San Juan Islands in search of orcas, humpbacks, sea lions, and seabirds, with a 100% whale sighting guarantee from April to October. Beyond whale watching, they offer sea lion tours, sunset cruises, private charters, and ash scattering ceremonies along the BC coastline.

visitor.name: Douglas Park Community Centre
visitor.desc: Douglas Park Community Centre is a long-established neighbourhood hub in Vancouver's Cambie corridor, offering programs ranging from licensed preschool and daycamps to adult fitness and a working pottery studio. The centre hosts an annual Community Day festival and has served a Social Club for people with disabilities since 1968. Cyclists passing through the area would find this a potential rest stop, though the facility is primarily oriented toward registered programming rather than drop-in visitor services.

visitor.name: Hatzic Prairie Community Hall
visitor.desc: Hatzic Prairie Community Hall has anchored the rural Durieu community near Mission since 1933, surviving the great Fraser Valley flood of 1948 and kept alive by volunteer labour ever since. Nestled among mountains and pastures of the Lower Mainland, the hall hosts everything from community dances and weddings to first-aid classes. With a capacity of 150 guests and recently updated appliances including air conditioning, it is the social hub of the Hatzic Prairie area.

visitor.name: Rainbow Road Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: Rainbow Road Aquatic Centre is a public swimming facility on Salt Spring Island, operated by SSIPARC (Salt Spring Island Parks, Arts, Recreation & Culture) as a service of the Capital Regional District. The centre offers drop-in aquatic programs and scheduled swim sessions for island residents and visitors alike. For touring cyclists riding Salt Spring Island's famously hilly roads, it represents the island's primary public aquatic resource.

visitor.name: VPL: Marpole Branch
visitor.desc: VPL Marpole Branch is a neighbourhood branch of the Vancouver Public Library system, situated on Granville Street in Vancouver's Marpole community. It is part of one of Canada's busiest and most celebrated public library networks, offering a publicly accessible indoor space to the community. For a touring cyclist, it represents a convenient stop in a residential neighbourhood close to the Fraser River cycling routes.

visitor.name: Vancouver Public Library Kerrisdale Branch
visitor.desc: The Kerrisdale Branch is one of the neighbourhood branches of the Vancouver Public Library system, serving the quiet residential Kerrisdale district in southwest Vancouver. OSM data indicates it is situated on a lower level (level -1), suggesting it occupies a basement or below-grade space within its building. As a public library, it offers a welcoming rest stop for touring cyclists passing through the area, with free Wi-Fi noted in OSM.

visitor.name: Inuit Gallery Of Vancouver
visitor.desc: The Inuit Gallery of Vancouver is a commercial fine-art gallery specializing in Inuit and Northwest Coast First Nations sculpture, prints, drawings, and jewelry by established and emerging Indigenous artists. It recently moved to the Shipyards District of North Vancouver, in the same building as the North Vancouver Museum and Archives, directly across from Lonsdale Quay Market. The waterfront neighbourhood is compact and walkable, surrounded by restaurants, cafes, craft breweries, and a summer night market—making the gallery a natural cultural stop for cyclists exploring the North Shore.

visitor.name: Hollow Tree
visitor.desc: The Hollow Tree is a massive ancient western red cedar stump in Stanley Park, one of Vancouver's most iconic natural landmarks, estimated to be over 1,000 years old. Cyclists riding the Stanley Park perimeter road or seawall pass close to this storied giant, which has been a popular photo stop for generations of visitors. It was nearly removed in 2006 but a public campaign led to its preservation and structural reinforcement.

visitor.name: Walter C. Koerner Library
visitor.desc: The Walter C. Koerner Library is a five-storey academic library at the heart of the UBC Vancouver campus, housing major humanities and social sciences collections. It is publicly accessible and sits within UBC's expansive campus grounds, which are popular with cyclists connecting to the Pacific Spirit Regional Park trail network. Touring cyclists passing through the Point Grey area will find it a convenient landmark stop on campus.

visitor.name: Canada Games Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Canada Games Aquatic Centre is a municipal swimming facility in Kamloops operated by the City of Kamloops. It offers swimming alongside amenities including a hot tub, sauna, and steam room, making it a notable stop for touring cyclists looking to recover after a long day on the road. It is wheelchair accessible and located on McGill Road near the Thompson Rivers University campus.

visitor.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
visitor.desc: VanDusen Botanical Garden is a 55-acre public botanical garden in the heart of Vancouver featuring over 7,500 plant species from around the world, set within a Visitor Centre built on a living-building philosophy. It hosts year-round programming, guided cart tours for those with mobility challenges, and fine-dining and café options on site. The OSM record 'Black Garden' appears to be a named sub-garden feature within VanDusen's grounds rather than a separate venue.

notes.Café or food on site: Two confirmed on-site food venues: Shaughnessy Restaurant (fine dining, lunch/afternoon tea/dinner/weekend brunch, located in Garden Pavilion) and The Garden Café (Fair Trade coffees, handcrafted beverages, sandwiches, soups, inside Visitor Centre) — both confirmed on the services page

visitor.name: Hillkeep Regional Park
visitor.desc: Hillkeep Regional Park is a nature reserve managed by the Fraser Valley Regional District on the outskirts of Chilliwack, offering natural landscapes typical of the lower Fraser Valley foothills. As one of several FVRD regional parks in the area, it provides a quiet escape into nature with designated trails. Touring cyclists exploring the Chilliwack region may find it a worthwhile side-trip destination, though the park's specific facilities remain unconfirmed from available sources.

visitor.name: Circle Wellness Spa
visitor.desc: Circle Wellness is a private, self-guided thermal spa on Granville Island that blends ancient rituals with modern technology in individual 'WellPod' suites. It bills itself as the first experience of its kind in the world, with a second location coming soon in Seattle. Located in one of Vancouver's most bike-accessible neighbourhoods, it could serve as a recovery stop for touring cyclists.

visitor.name: Gallery 7 Theatre
visitor.desc: Gallery 7 Theatre is a community-based performing arts society with over 30 years of history producing professional-quality live theatre in the Fraser Valley. The company mounts five mainstage productions per season at venues including the Matsqui Centennial Auditorium and Abbotsford Arts Centre, drawing over 12,000 audience members annually with up to 200 volunteers contributing more than 10,000 hours. It also runs a summer theatre academy offering camps for youth aged 8–17 taught by working professionals.

visitor.name: Joan Blakeborough Museum
visitor.desc: A community history museum housed within the North Bend Community Center, preserving the story of this small Fraser Canyon railway town from the 1800s to the present day through school browse binders, census sheets, military lists, family histories, and a model railway depicting the original town site. Operated by volunteers of the Boston Bar-North Bend Historical Society, the museum draws former residents, genealogists, and curious travellers passing through the canyon. The outer building holds larger artefacts, and an active thrift store and community garden share the same grounds.

detail.address: 64901 North Bend Station Road, North Bend

visitor.name: Greater Victoria Public Library - Bruce Hutchison Branch
visitor.desc: The Bruce Hutchison Branch is a full-service public library branch of the Greater Victoria Public Library system, located on Elk Lake Drive adjacent to Elk Lake Regional Park—a hub for cycling, running, and paddling in the Capital Regional District. As a public institution, it provides free access to books, digital resources, and public computers in a climate-controlled setting. Its position along a well-used cycling corridor makes it a natural potential waypoint for touring and recreational cyclists passing through Saanich.

visitor.name: Squamish Adventure Cenre
visitor.desc: The Squamish Adventure Centre is Squamish's primary visitor information hub, offering trip planning, bookings, brochures, and expert local advice on trails, accommodations, dining, and more. The 5,773 square foot building is an architectural landmark constructed from locally-sourced Douglas fir timber, with a signature curved roof inspired by the eagles that migrate annually through the Squamish Valley. Situated directly on the Sea to Sky Highway, it serves as the natural first stop for touring cyclists arriving in Squamish.

visitor.name: Hume Park Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: A municipal outdoor swimming pool operated by the City of New Westminster, located in Hume Park. As a seasonal outdoor facility it could serve as a refreshment stop for touring cyclists passing through New Westminster along the Fraser River corridor.

visitor.name: Fred Randall Pool
visitor.desc: Fred Randall Pool is an indoor public swimming facility operated by the City of Burnaby, offering drop-in swim sessions and aquafit classes. It may be the named pool within the Edmonds Community Centre complex, a full-service municipal recreation facility in Burnaby. Touring cyclists could potentially use it as a rest stop with shower access, though amenity details are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Nanoose Place Community Centre
visitor.desc: Nanoose Place Community Centre is a volunteer-run, non-profit hub in Nanoose Bay that has served the local community since 1992, offering fitness classes, pickleball, floor curling, seniors programs, and rentable event halls. It is operated by the Nanoose Bay Activities and Recreation Society (NBARS) and also functions as a designated emergency reception centre for the area. The surrounding grounds include Eswyn's Alpine & Rock Garden, a volunteer-established feature that adds a quiet outdoor element.

detail.address: 2925 Northwest Bay Road, Nanoose Bay, British Columbia V9P 9J9

visitor.name: Strathcona Community Centre
visitor.desc: Strathcona Community Centre is a City of Vancouver recreation facility serving one of the city's oldest and most historically significant neighbourhoods, located near the intersection of Keefer Street and Gore Avenue in the Strathcona district. As a publicly operated community centre, it offers recreational programming to residents and visitors in a neighbourhood that sits along several popular urban cycling routes connecting downtown Vancouver to East Van.

visitor.name: GVPL: Emily Carr Branch
visitor.desc: The Emily Carr Branch is a neighbourhood branch of the Greater Victoria Public Library system, located on Blanshard Street in Victoria. It provides public access to books, digital resources, and public computers as part of a multi-branch municipal library network. Touring cyclists passing through the north end of Victoria may find it a convenient urban pause point.

visitor.name: Nanaimo Ceramic Arts Studio & Gallery
visitor.desc: A community pottery studio and gallery in downtown Nanaimo run by professional artists and potters. Offers drop-in Saturday night pottery wheel sessions requiring no experience, making it accessible to passing visitors. Also features rotating artist-in-residence exhibitions in the gallery space.

visitor.name: Somenos Garry Oak Protected Area
visitor.desc: A protected area near Duncan sheltering both shallow-soil and deep-soil Garry Oaks along with three federally endangered plant species and rare wildflowers. The site borders Ye'yumnuts, a sacred ancestral place of the Quw'utsun people with over 2,000 years of documented history. Touring cyclists can park at the end of York Road off Trillium Terrace and walk wide gravelly trails through the oak meadows.

visitor.name: Eagle Ridge Community Centre
visitor.desc: Eagle Ridge Community Centre is a multi-sport community facility located in Langford, in the Greater Victoria area. Tagged in OSM as both a community_centre and a sports_centre, it likely serves residents with a range of recreational programs and shared amenities. Touring cyclists passing through the Langford Parkway corridor may find it a useful stop, though current operational status could not be confirmed.

visitor.name: Swan Lake Nature House
visitor.desc: Swan Lake Christmas Hill Nature Sanctuary is a 135-acre urban refuge in Victoria encompassing a wetland around Swan Lake and a Garry oak forest atop Christmas Hill, drawing over 100,000 trail visitors annually. The Nature House serves as the interpretive hub, with a gift shop and native plant resources, while 4.5 km of walking trails wind through two distinct ecosystems rich in rare native plants and Pacific Flyway bird species. For over 50 years this non-profit sanctuary has operated as a living classroom for ecological stewardship, making it a compelling stop for cyclists exploring Greater Victoria.

detail.address: 3873 Swan Lake Road, Victoria, B.C. Canada, V8X 3W1

visitor.name: Luso Canadian Multicultural Society of Penticton
visitor.desc: The Luso Canadian Multicultural Society is a Portuguese-Canadian community organization based in Penticton that operates a rentable meeting and event hall. It serves as a cultural hub celebrating Lusophone heritage in the South Okanagan. Touring cyclists passing through Penticton may find it a potential rest or event stop, particularly during community gatherings.

visitor.name: BMO Theatre Centre
visitor.desc: The BMO Theatre Centre is one of three Vancouver venues operated by the Arts Club Theatre Company, one of Canada's largest not-for-profit theatre companies, founded in 1964 and welcoming more than a quarter million guests annually. Located in the Olympic Village neighbourhood along False Creek, the venue hosts world and Canadian premieres, new works development, and youth programs. A cycling tour of Vancouver's False Creek waterfront puts this professional theatre a short ride from the seawall.

notes.Café or food on site: Website navigation includes a dedicated 'Concession Menu' subpage under the Venues section, indicating food and drink service at the venue

visitor.name: Jewish Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Jewish Community Centre of Greater Vancouver (JCCGV) is a large, multi-programme urban hub anchoring South Vancouver's Jewish community with facilities that include an aquatic centre, fitness centre, gymnasium, performing arts schools, and an art gallery and library. It hosts significant regional cultural events such as the Chutzpah! Festival, the Jewish Book Festival, and the Festival of Jewish Culture. Touring cyclists passing through the Oakridge/South Cambie corridor would find a well-resourced institutional facility within a residential neighbourhood.

visitor.name: Summerland Museum and Archives
visitor.desc: The Summerland Museum and Archives has been collecting and preserving local history since 1965, with permanent exhibits covering Indigenous pre-contact history, Okanagan fruit farming, and the era of the Kettle Valley Railway. Its most popular exhibit is a working scale model of the Kettle Valley Railway, complemented by a striking 15-metre mural painted by Summerland local artist Bruce Crawford. Located near the shores of Okanagan Lake and a short drive from Penticton, it is a natural cultural stop on a southern Okanagan cycling tour.

visitor.name: Protection Island Museum
visitor.desc: The Protection Island Museum is a small community museum located on Protection Island, a car-free island community in Nanaimo Harbour accessible only by a short passenger ferry. The island has gravel roads with a 20 km/h speed limit and is home to roughly 330 full-time residents. It sits alongside a small library and community centre at Gallows Point, offering a quiet glimpse into the island's local history.

visitor.name: Whytecliff Marine Protected Area
visitor.desc: Whytecliff Marine Protected Area is a coastal park and dive destination in West Vancouver, widely recognized as one of Canada's first marine protected areas. Managed by the District of West Vancouver, it protects a rich underwater ecosystem popular with scuba divers and snorkellers. The park sits at the end of the Horseshoe Bay peninsula and offers dramatic cliff-top views of Howe Sound, making it a scenic detour for touring cyclists on the Sea to Sky corridor.

visitor.name: Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre
visitor.desc: The Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre is a nature museum and interpretive centre operated by the District of North Vancouver, situated at the gateway to Lynn Canyon Park's temperate rainforest. Visitors can explore interactive natural history exhibits, consult with park naturalists about local flora and fauna, and pick up trail maps before heading out to the famous Suspension Bridge. As the orientation hub for multiple trail loops including the Twin Falls Loop and Thirty Foot Pool Trail, it is a natural first stop for cyclists exploring North Vancouver's park network.

visitor.name: Thunderbird Community Centre
visitor.desc: Thunderbird Community Centre is a neighbourhood facility jointly operated by the Vancouver Board of Parks and Recreation and the Thunderbird Neighbourhood Association, providing recreational, educational, and social programs for residents of all ages in East Vancouver. The centre includes a fitness facility, licensed childcare, gymnasium, and multi-purpose rooms available for rental. Touring cyclists passing through the Hastings-Sunrise corridor may find it a functional rest point, though it is oriented primarily toward local community use.

visitor.name: Chilliwack River Rafting
visitor.desc: Established in 1983, Chilliwack River Rafting is British Columbia's first whitewater rafting resort, operating on a 5-acre private property nestled in the Cascade Mountains alongside the Chilliwack River, roughly 90 minutes from Vancouver. The operation offers guided paddle raft trips ranging from family-friendly Class 2 floats to continuous Class 4+ canyon runs, plus sit-on-top inflatable kayaking. The on-site Raft Ranch includes camping, a cookhouse serving hearty buffet meals, showers, beach volleyball, and fire pits, making it a self-contained outdoor adventure destination.

detail.address: 49704 Chilliwack Lake Road, Chilliwack, BC V4Z 1A7

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Resort page explicitly lists showers among guest amenities: 'Indoor and outdoor sheltered areas, showers, and fire pits are all available for our guests.'
notes.Café or food on site: Resort page describes a cookhouse serving hearty meals (sausage and eggs, chilli, butter chicken, etc.) with vegetarian options, tea, coffee, and hot chocolate. Trips page notes a buffet lunch is included with day trips

visitor.name: WAC Bennett Library
visitor.desc: The WAC Bennett Library is the main academic library at Simon Fraser University on Burnaby Mountain, a seven-storey building serving the university's research and learning needs. It is primarily oriented toward SFU students, faculty, and staff, with access restrictions that may limit utility for casual visitors. The hilltop campus setting offers sweeping views but requires a significant climb to reach by bike.

visitor.name: Royal BC Museum
visitor.desc: BC's flagship museum covering natural and human history, with an IMAX theatre on the Inner Harbour.

detail.address: 675 Belleville St., Victoria, BC V8W 9W2, Canada

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Sound Bites Concession' and 'The Yummy Truck' as on-site food options

visitor.name: Provincial Court of British Columbia
visitor.desc: The Provincial Court of British Columbia in Abbotsford is a publicly accessible government courthouse handling criminal, family, small claims, and traffic matters for the Fraser Valley region. As a civic building, it may offer incidental utility to passing cyclists such as washrooms or water, though no cyclist-specific amenities are confirmed. It sits on South Fraser Way, a main arterial road in Abbotsford.

visitor.name: Centennial Park Leisure Centre and Arena
visitor.desc: Centennial Park Leisure Centre and Arena is a City of White Rock-operated multi-use complex featuring an ice rink, auditorium, large hall, and meeting rooms. The arena transitions to a dry-floor venue from April through August for indoor sports and community events, giving it year-round community relevance. Cyclists exploring the White Rock and South Surrey area may find it a useful urban landmark near the North Bluff Road corridor.

detail.address: 14600 North Bluff Road, White Rock, BC V4B 3C9

visitor.name: Rose Gardens Park
visitor.desc: Rose Gardens Park is a publicly maintained rosarium operated by the City of Penticton as part of its parks and gardens network in the South Okanagan. The garden is mapped in OSM as a dedicated rose-style garden, making it a distinctive green-space destination amid the orchard and vineyard landscape of Penticton. Touring cyclists riding through the Okanagan can use it as a scenic rest stop in the heart of the city.

visitor.name: Aviary
visitor.desc: The Aviary is a volunteer-run indoor climbing wall on the second floor of the AMS Nest at UBC Vancouver, open to the public regardless of UBC affiliation. It offers top rope and lead climbing, a full adaptive climbing program with specialized equipment at no extra charge, and free gear rentals for all visitors. The facility is reached via elevator within the Nest building and is served by multiple TransLink bus routes along University Boulevard.

visitor.name: VPL: Champlain Heights Branch
visitor.desc: The Champlain Heights Branch is part of the Vancouver Public Library system, serving the Champlain Heights and Killarney neighbourhoods in east Vancouver. As a public library, it offers free access to books, digital resources, and community programming in a welcoming, publicly accessible space. Touring cyclists passing through this residential corner of Vancouver will find a quiet rest stop with indoor seating.

visitor.name: Poirier Forum
visitor.desc: Poirier Forum is a 25,000-square-foot municipal multi-purpose facility in southwest Coquitlam used for sports such as lacrosse, ball hockey, and soccer, as well as community events. It sits across from the Poirier Sport & Leisure Complex and features a polished concrete floor, changerooms, and wheelchair accessibility. The facility operates only for scheduled programs and rental groups, so drop-in access is limited to posted schedules.

visitor.name: New Westminster Museum
visitor.desc: The New Westminster Museum is a municipal history museum operated by the City of New Westminster, located on the third floor of 777 Columbia Street in the heart of the city's historic downtown. It explores the rich heritage of New Westminster, BC's first capital city on the mainland, through locally focused exhibits and archival collections. Entry is by donation, making it an accessible cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Fraser River corridor.

visitor.name: Maillardville Community Centre
visitor.desc: Maillardville Community Centre is a 22,000-square-foot municipal recreation facility in Coquitlam featuring a gymnasium, dance/fitness studio, teaching kitchen, and multipurpose rooms. It is the heart of the historic Maillardville francophone neighbourhood and is accessible by several bus routes (153, 156, 157). The centre has underground parking and extensive accessibility features including power-operated doors and an elevator.

visitor.name: South Surrey Indoor Pool
visitor.desc: South Surrey Indoor Pool is a City of Surrey public recreation facility offering drop-in swimming, weight room access, a sauna, and a hot tub. Located in the South Surrey neighbourhood near the White Rock border, it serves the broader community as an affordable fitness and leisure destination. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a convenient stop for a post-ride swim and recovery.

visitor.name: The Norm Theatre
visitor.desc: The Norm Theatre is a cinema venue operated by the Alma Mater Society (AMS) at UBC's Student Nest on the University of British Columbia campus.
