As an AMS venue, it serves the UBC student community and sits within a large multi-use building that also houses food, services, and student resources. Touring cyclists passing through the UBC campus area will find it conveniently located along the university's well-developed cycling network.

detail.address: 6133 University Blvd, UBC Campus, Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1

visitor.name: Nelson & District Youth Centre
visitor.desc: The Nelson & District Youth Centre is a City of Nelson-operated community facility offering programs, drop-in services, and rentals to local youth. It is tagged in OSM as both a community centre and sports centre, suggesting multi-use recreational space. Touring cyclists passing through Nelson may find it a useful stop given its community-facility nature and central city location.

visitor.name: Climb Base5
visitor.desc: Climb Base5 is an indoor rock climbing gym serving Metro Vancouver with facilities in North Vancouver and Coquitlam, offering bouldering, auto-belays, top rope, and lead climbing for all skill levels. The gym emphasizes community, inclusivity, and progression through structured courses, youth programs, and adult training. A touring cyclist looking for an active rest day activity will find a well-equipped facility with beginner-friendly entry points including auto-belay orientations and introductory belay courses.

visitor.name: Victoria Butterfly Gardens
visitor.desc: Victoria Butterfly Gardens is a year-round tropical jungle attraction on the Saanich Peninsula, located just minutes from Butchart Gardens in Brentwood Bay. Visitors stroll through lush indoor gardens and encounter free-flying butterflies, flamingos, blue-and-gold macaws, tortoises, poison dart frogs, a Cuvier's dwarf caiman, and more. It is accessible from downtown Victoria by BC Transit bus, making it a reachable side-trip for touring cyclists on the peninsula.

detail.address: 1461 Benvenuto Avenue, Brentwood Bay, BC V8M 1J5

visitor.name: Parkinson Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Parkinson Recreation Centre is a full-service civic recreation facility operated by the City of Kelowna offering an indoor pool, hot tub, steam sauna, fitness centre, and basketball. As a municipally run centre it serves both residents and visitors looking to recover, train, or swim during a tour through the Okanagan. Admission fees apply.

visitor.name: Greater Vernon Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: A public recreation centre operated by the Regional District of North Okanagan in Vernon, featuring swimming facilities. It serves as a community sports and recreation hub in the North Okanagan.

visitor.name: Cowichan Lake Sports Arena
visitor.desc: The Cowichan Lake Sports Arena is a multi-sport community recreation centre in Lake Cowichan, operated by the Cowichan Valley Regional District. Situated near the lake in a region popular with cycling tourists exploring the Cowichan Valley, it serves as the main indoor recreation hub for the community. As a regional district facility it likely hosts ice, court, and fitness activities, though specific offerings could not be confirmed from available web content.

visitor.name: Sooke Region Museum
visitor.desc: The Sooke Region Museum and Visitor Centre preserves the natural and human history of the Sooke Region, operating since 1977 on the territories of the T'Sou-ke, Pacheedaht and Scia'new peoples. Visitors can explore extensive outdoor exhibits including heritage buildings like Moss Cottage, the Servants' Quarters, and a Forestry Path, while the indoor collection covers basketry, early settlers, forestry, and maritime themes. It also serves as the area's official visitor centre and includes a Gift & Book Shop, making it a natural orientation stop for cyclists arriving in Sooke.

visitor.name: Swan Lake Wildlife Refuge
visitor.desc: Swan Lake Sanctuary is a 57-hectare nature reserve near Princeton, BC, managed by the Vermilion Forks Field Naturalists, centred on a kettle lake surrounded by riparian zones and native grasslands. The sanctuary features hiking trails, two bird blinds, benches, and picnic tables, with over 128 bird species recorded on-site — making it a rewarding stop for wildlife-minded touring cyclists. Gates restrict motorized vehicle access, preserving a quiet atmosphere for self-propelled visitors.

visitor.name: Memorial South Turf
visitor.desc: Memorial South Turf is an artificial turf sports field located within Memorial South Park in Vancouver, operated by the City of Vancouver Parks, Recreation and Culture department. The facility is fenced and wheelchair accessible, suggesting a managed multi-use sports surface suitable for organized play. Touring cyclists passing through South Vancouver may find it a useful waypoint within the broader park.

visitor.name: Fraser Heights Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Fraser Heights Recreation Centre is a City of Surrey municipal facility serving the Fraser Heights neighbourhood with a weight room, gymnasium sports, fitness classes, and outdoor sport fields and courts. It is a civic-grade community hub that touring cyclists passing through the Guildford/Fraser Heights corridor might use for rest, recreation, or to access facilities. The centre is operated by the City of Surrey Parks & Recreation department.

visitor.name: Audain Art Museum
visitor.desc: The Audain Art Museum is a purpose-built art museum in Whistler housing a permanent collection of over 300 works tracing British Columbia art history from the 18th century to the present day. It holds one of the world's finest collections of Northwest Coast First Nations masks alongside a comprehensive Emily Carr collection and works by major contemporary BC artists such as Jeff Wall and Stan Douglas. The award-winning building sits on the unceded territory of the Sḵwx̱wú7mesh (Squamish) and Lil̓wat7úl (Lil'wat) Nations.

visitor.name: The Improv Centre
visitor.desc: The Improv Centre is Vancouver's home for live comedy, located on Granville Island and internationally recognized for its flagship Theatresports™ shows — a high-energy, audience-judged improv competition the company has been performing for over 40 years. It operates as a registered charitable organization offering unscripted performances, improv classes, and community workshops in a waterfront theatre setting. Granville Island is a natural cycling destination, and the venue explicitly lists bicycle as one of the recommended ways to arrive.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'Our bar and lounge opens 1 hour before first showtime'; a Bar Menu is listed in the site navigation

visitor.name: Maury Young Arts Centre
visitor.desc: The Maury Young Arts Centre is the cultural heart of Whistler Village, operated by Arts Whistler as a registered charity. The facility includes a 200-seat theatre, a mountain-view art gallery, a sprung-floor studio, and the Arthentic boutique selling handcrafted works by local Sea to Sky artists. Cyclists finishing a ride on the Sea to Sky corridor will find rotating exhibitions, live performances, and community events year-round.

visitor.name: Vernon Community Arts Centre
visitor.desc: The Vernon Community Arts Centre is a multi-discipline arts hub offering classes, workshops, and specialty studios in clay, glass, printmaking, fibre arts, and more for all ages. It is home to the Arts Council of the North Okanagan, a registered charity supporting arts education and community development across the region. Cyclists visiting Vernon can browse the Centre Gallery — which rotates monthly member exhibitions — and the on-site Art Shop carrying local art and supplies.

visitor.name: Windermere Valley Museum
visitor.desc: The Windermere Valley Museum is an outdoor heritage complex managed by the Windermere District Historical Society, featuring eight historic buildings relocated to a single site including a CPR train station, pioneer cabins, a schoolhouse, and an implement shed. Visitors follow a self-guided tour through grassy, shaded grounds with views of Windermere Lake, the Columbia River, and the surrounding mountains. Admission is by donation, and the grounds with outside displays are accessible at any time.

visitor.name: NWPL: New Westminster Public Library
visitor.desc: The New Westminster Public Library holds the distinction of being the first public library established in British Columbia, giving it genuine historical significance for visitors. Located in the heart of New Westminster across from Royal City Centre, it offers public computers, Wi-Fi, and a surprisingly eclectic collection that includes a seed library and ukulele lending. A touring cyclist can drop in to get connected, rest, and explore the community programming on offer.

visitor.name: Mundy Park Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: Mundy Park Outdoor Pool is a newly renovated municipal aquatic facility within Mundy Park in Coquitlam, featuring a leisure pool with beach entry, splash area, lazy river, deep end, a separate lap pool, warming pool, and diving board. The expanded deck spaces and surrounding parkland make it a refreshing stop for touring cyclists passing through the Tri-Cities area. Formerly known as Spani Outdoor Pool, the facility reopened with modern accessibility features and universal change rooms.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Universal change rooms with showers; two large accessible change/shower rooms, one equipped with a full bed and ceiling-mounted lift
notes.Café or food on site: Concession listed as a feature; 'Variety of tasty food options from Canuel Caterers'

visitor.name: Manzanita Ridge Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: Manzanita Ridge Nature Reserve is a 20-hectare conservation area on the southeast end of Salt Spring Island's Mt. Erskine ridge, protecting one of the island's rare south-facing coastal Douglas-fir habitats with an Arbutus-Hairy Manzanita ecosystem. Acquired in 2003 through a mix of donation and community fundraising, it is managed by the Salt Spring Island Conservancy under a conservation covenant. The reserve offers 0.5 km of public hiking trails — a quiet natural detour for cyclists exploring Salt Spring Island.

detail.address: 265 Blackburn Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2B8

visitor.name: Hatley Castle
visitor.desc: Hatley Castle is a grand Edwardian stone castle built for coal baron James Dunsmuir, now the centrepiece of Royal Roads University's Hatley Park — a National Historic Site spanning 260 hectares of oceanfront parkland on southern Vancouver Island. The estate offers self-guided wandering through Italian, Japanese, and rose gardens, old-growth forest hikes, biking trails, and sweeping views of the Olympic Mountains across the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Guided tours of the castle's interior run seasonally, and the on-site Habitat Café provides a welcome rest stop.

notes.Café or food on site: Habitat Café named explicitly in site navigation and on the /visit page as an on-site dining option

visitor.name: South Shore Gallery
visitor.desc: South Shore Gallery is a free-admission art gallery in the heart of Sooke showcasing original paintings, ceramics, glass, metalwork, jewellery, fibre art, and gifts by over 80 British Columbia artists. The gallery also carries a selection of art supplies and offers professional custom picture framing done entirely on-site by owner Rebecca Hornsby. It is a worthwhile cultural stop for touring cyclists exploring the southern tip of Vancouver Island.

detail.address: 2046 Otter Point Road, Sooke, BC V9Z 0P7

visitor.name: W̱MÍYEŦEN Nature Sanctuary
visitor.desc: W̱MÍYEŦEN Nature Sanctuary is a 42-acre protected forest and riparian area in the Highlands District, about 25 km from downtown Victoria, formerly known as Mary Lake Nature Sanctuary. The property encompasses 10 different ecosystems, a 7-acre lake, the Nature Kinship House perched on the water's edge, and streamside trails through old-growth Coastal Douglas Fir forest. It is operated by a non-profit society in alliance with the W̱SÁNEĆ (Saanich) Coast Salish Peoples and focuses on conservation, ecological research, and reconciliation.

visitor.name: Cheeky Monkey Glassworks
visitor.desc: Cheeky Monkey Glassworks is a glass art gallery and studio in Nanaimo operated by artist Brenda McIntyre, who has been creating custom glass art for over 25 years. The shop features original stained, fused, sandblasted, and mosaic glass pieces all made in-house, and also offers hands-on workshops and a well-stocked glass art supply section. Located on Terminal Avenue, it occupies a bright, welcoming studio space that Brenda describes as having a fun, cheeky atmosphere.

detail.address: 427 N Terminal Ave, Nanaimo, BC V9S 4J8

visitor.name: Evelyne Saller Centre
visitor.desc: The Evelyne Saller Centre is a City of Vancouver community centre located in the Downtown Eastside neighbourhood at 404 Alexander Street. Operated by Vancouver Parks, Recreation and Culture, it serves as a community hub for the surrounding area. A touring cyclist passing through the DTES would find it a publicly accessible municipal facility in a central urban location.

visitor.name: Stewart Museum
visitor.desc: The Stewart Museum, operated by the Stewart Historical Society, preserves the history of Stewart, one of BC's most remote communities near the Alaska-BC border. Exhibits include a new avalanche display and extensive coverage of the region's mining heritage, offering touring cyclists a window into the rugged pioneer history of the area. The museum also houses archives and a gift shop featuring Canadian-made goods and historical literature.

visitor.name: West End Ice Rink
visitor.desc: West End Ice Rink is a public ice rink located at 1750 Haro Street in Vancouver's West End neighbourhood, operated through the City of Vancouver Parks system in association with the West End Community Centre. Situated close to Stanley Park and the English Bay waterfront, it offers a skating experience in one of Vancouver's most cycle-friendly urban neighbourhoods. Touring cyclists passing through the seawall or West End routes may find it a worthwhile stop.

visitor.name: Sidney Museum and Archives
visitor.desc: The Sidney Museum and Archives, established in 1971, preserves and displays historical artifacts and archival materials from Sidney, North Saanich, and the Saanich Peninsula. Located in the Lower Level of the Olde Post Office Building on Beacon Avenue, it features rotating exhibits including a current travelling show on Chinese Canadian history co-produced with the Chinese Canadian Museum. Admission is by donation, making it an accessible cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through Sidney.

visitor.name: Cameron Library
visitor.desc: Cameron Library is a branch of Burnaby Public Library currently operating as 'Temporary Cameron' from inside the City of Lougheed Shopping Centre while its permanent Cameron Street location is unavailable. The branch provides public computers, Wi-Fi, and a variety of seating areas for work, study, and lounging. Washrooms are located just outside the library within the shopping centre, with accessible and universal options available.

visitor.name: Delta Agricultural Hall / Deas Island Regional Park
visitor.desc: The Delta Agricultural Hall is a three-storey historic civic building originally constructed in 1899, relocated from downtown Ladner to its present site within Deas Island Regional Park in 1989. Sitting in the Fraser River delta near Tsawwassen, it is a rare surviving example of Delta's agricultural-era civic architecture. Cycling tourists exploring the flat dyke trails and farmlands of the Fraser delta may encounter it as a heritage landmark within the regional park.

visitor.name: Rose Garden
visitor.desc: The Rose Garden is a garden attraction in Vancouver, identified via OSM as a leisure garden and associated with Queen Elizabeth Park. It is a publicly accessible outdoor space likely appealing to touring cyclists as a scenic rest stop or sightseeing destination. No further detail is available from the fetched website due to a Cloudflare block.

visitor.name: Project Climbing Centre
visitor.desc: Project Climbing Centre is an indoor climbing facility with multiple Lower Mainland locations, including Chilliwack. As a dedicated climbing gym, it likely offers changing facilities and community programming suited to active visitors. A touring cyclist passing through Chilliwack might stop here for a rest-day activity or to connect with local outdoor enthusiasts.

visitor.name: Gathering Place
visitor.desc: Gathering Place is a City of Vancouver–operated community centre located in the downtown core on Helmcken Street. It serves as a publicly accessible gathering and recreation hub in one of Vancouver's densest urban neighbourhoods. A touring cyclist passing through downtown Vancouver could use it as a rest and services stop.

visitor.name: Studio 58
visitor.desc: Studio 58 is Langara College's nationally recognized professional theatre arts conservatory, founded in 1965 and named after the room number of its original theatre space. The program presents four full-length and two indie-style productions annually, all open to the public and reviewed by local press, with professional directors and designers on every production. It offers relaxed-performance options for accessibility-conscious audiences and is a five-minute walk from the Canada Line's Langara-49th Ave Station.

notes.Café or food on site: Your Visit page notes 'The concession is cash only,' confirming a concession stand is available

visitor.name: Priest Valley Arena
visitor.desc: Priest Valley Arena is a City of Vernon municipal recreation facility primarily serving the local community as a venue for ice hockey and lacrosse. Operated by Vernon's Parks & Recreation department, it is part of the city's broader network of indoor recreation facilities. Cyclists riding through Vernon may encounter it as a landmark or potential rest point, though its core function is as a local indoor sports arena.

visitor.name: Grand Forks & District Public Library
visitor.desc: A welcoming community library in downtown Grand Forks offering free access to books, computers, printing, an Idea Lab & Think Tank, and equipment loans. It sits on the Trans-Canada cycling corridor through the Boundary region, giving touring cyclists a comfortable indoor stop with seating and connectivity. The library also serves as a satellite for Christina Lake with a monthly outreach location there.

visitor.name: VIRL: Cowichan Branch
visitor.desc: The Cowichan (Duncan) branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library traces its roots to a lending library in the late 1800s, surviving multiple relocations across Duncan before settling at its current James Street location. Part of the Vancouver Island Regional Library system serving communities across Vancouver Island and the BC coast, it offers public library services, meeting rooms, digital resources, and a range of community programming. As a free public facility in the heart of Duncan, it functions as a central community hub within easy reach of the Cowichan Valley's cycling routes.

visitor.name: Metchosin Pioneer Museum
visitor.desc: A volunteer-run heritage museum housed in a converted horse barn on the municipal grounds of the District of Metchosin. The collection focuses on pioneer-era farm machinery, rural artifacts, and local history from the Metchosin area. Located next to the Metchosin Farmers' Market on Happy Valley Road, it makes a quirky stop for cyclists exploring the rural roads west of Victoria.

visitor.name: Steveston Seabreeze Adventures
visitor.desc: Steveston Seabreeze Adventures is a marine eco-tour operator established in 1998, running small-group whale watching and fishing charters from the historic Steveston fishing village on the Fraser River delta. Tours depart aboard either an intimate 12-passenger Zodiac or larger semi-enclosed vessels with certified marine naturalists, exploring the Salish Sea in search of whales and local marine life. Steveston itself is a popular cycling destination, and this long-running family operation sits at the heart of the waterfront among seafood stalls, heritage buildings, and artisanal breweries.

detail.address: 12551 No. 1 Road Bldg 43, Richmond, BC V7E 1T7

visitor.name: Sunnyside Community Hall
visitor.desc: Sunnyside Community Hall is a City of Surrey-operated community centre in the Sunnyside neighbourhood of Surrey, BC. As a publicly accessible municipal facility, it serves the local community with programming and events. Touring cyclists may find it a useful waypoint in an otherwise suburban stretch of Surrey.

visitor.name: Whistler Shooting Adventures
visitor.desc: Whistler Shooting Adventures is a guided outdoor shooting range nestled in the mountains about 20 minutes north of Whistler Village on the Sea to Sky Highway. Visitors can try a variety of firearms under professional supervision with no prior experience or licenses required. The range is located at the Pemberton Wildlife Association shooting grounds in a scenic but remote setting with only basic pit-toilet facilities on site.

detail.address: Sea to Sky Highway, Pemberton, V0N 2L1

visitor.name: Fernie Heritage Library
visitor.desc: The Fernie Heritage Library is a welcoming three-storey public facility in downtown Fernie, housing fiction, non-fiction, reference collections, and a Tech Hub with fabrication, audio, and media creation equipment. Beside the building is a beautifully maintained garden open to the public 24 hours a day, complete with picnic tables and bike racks — a genuinely pleasant rest stop for cyclists passing through the Elk Valley. Membership and programming are free, and the library hosts community programs ranging from literacy support to a volunteer income tax clinic.

visitor.name: BPL: McGill Library
visitor.desc: McGill is a branch of Burnaby Public Library situated at the corner of Albert Street and Alpha Street, near the Willingdon Urban Trail and Trans Canada Trail cycling corridors. The branch hosts rotating art exhibitions from the Burnaby Art Gallery and houses the City of Burnaby Archives, which holds municipal records dating back to 1892. For touring cyclists, it offers fully accessible public washrooms, free Wi-Fi, and public computers in a welcoming public space.

visitor.name: Liard River Hot Springs
visitor.desc: Liard River Hot Springs is home to the second largest hot spring in Canada, set within a lush boreal spruce forest of national ecological significance. The Alpha pool sits at the end of a boardwalk that winds through a warm-water swamp and old-growth forest, making it a remarkable natural detour for cyclists touring the Alaska Highway. The park is open year-round and is one of the most popular stopovers on the entire Alaska Highway corridor.

detail.address: Km 765 Alaska Highway, Liard River, V0C 1Z0

visitor.name: The Gallery George
visitor.desc: The Gallery George is a 1,540-square-foot street-level contemporary art gallery in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside that champions local established and emerging artists through rotating exhibitions and pop-up markets. The elegant space features bright bay windows and 12.5-foot ceilings, and doubles as a flexible venue for events and workshops. A touring cyclist stopping in Vancouver's downtown core would find a welcoming cultural stop with a small but lively roster of regional artists.

visitor.name: Saturna Recreation and Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: The Saturna Recreation and Cultural Centre is the community hub of Saturna Island, one of BC's most remote and crowd-free southern Gulf Islands, home to just 350 full-time residents. The facility features an auditorium/gym holding up to 300 people with a performance stage, a fully equipped industrial kitchen, a fitness and weight room, and a lounge. Cyclists ferrying to Saturna Island from Vancouver or Victoria can tap into the centre's year-round recreational, arts, and cultural programming open to all visitors.

detail.address: 104 Harris Road, P.O. Box 171, Saturna Island, BC V0N 2Y0

visitor.name: BoulderHouse Langford
visitor.desc: BoulderHouse Langford is the largest indoor bouldering facility on Vancouver Island, developed in partnership with the City of Langford to bring climbing to the West Shore. The two-storey building features 150 linear feet of main climbing wall, a dedicated training area, and a 6,000 sq ft kids section called the TreeHouse on the upper floor. Colour-coded bouldering circuits accommodate all skill levels, from first-timers to experienced climbers.

visitor.name: NVDPL: Parkgate Library
visitor.desc: Opened in 1994, Parkgate Library is a North Vancouver District Public Library branch situated near Deep Cove and the Tsleil-Waututh Nation, at the base of Mt. Seymour — a hub for cycling and hiking trails. The library is a free, welcoming public space with cozy reading areas, a fireplace, public computers, and WiFi. Notably, NVDPL offers E-Cargo Bikes as borrowable items, making this branch a surprisingly bike-friendly stop for touring cyclists exploring the area.

detail.address: 3675 Banff Court, North Vancouver, BC V7H 2Z8

visitor.name: Abbotsford Arts Centre Theatre
visitor.desc: The Abbotsford Arts Centre Theatre is a performing arts venue operated by the Abbotsford Arts Centre in the heart of Abbotsford, BC. It serves as a cultural hub for the Fraser Valley, hosting theatrical productions, live performances, and community arts events. Touring cyclists passing through Abbotsford may find it a worthwhile stop for a cultural experience.

visitor.name: Fort Kamloops
visitor.desc: A reconstructed historical fort within the Secwépemc Museum & Heritage Park in Kamloops, celebrating the cultural heritage of the Secwépemc Nation. The heritage park includes museum galleries, a gift shop, and tours including the Kamloops Indian Residential School and an ethnobotany walk. A meaningful cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through Kamloops.

notes.Luggage / bag storage: FAQ states: 'Beside the gift shop, there are coat racks and shelves for backpacks. They are not permitted in the museum exhibition galleries. Be aware there is limited storage for personal items.'

visitor.name: PoCo Heritage Museum and Archives
visitor.desc: The PoCo Heritage Museum and Archives is Port Coquitlam's only museum, operated by the volunteer-driven Port Coquitlam Heritage and Cultural Society since 1988 and housed in The Outlet at Leigh Square, the city's old post office. The museum celebrates Port Coquitlam's diverse heritage through rotating and permanent exhibits drawn from its archival collections, including a historical interpretive panel series installed along the nearby Traboulay PoCo Trail. General admission is free, making it an accessible stop for touring cyclists exploring the Coquitlam River corridor.

detail.address: 150-2248 McAllister Avenue, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 2A5

visitor.name: The Relief
visitor.desc: The Relief is a 1929 West Coast fishing vessel permanently moored on display beneath the Granville Street Bridge in Vancouver. It is one of the hidden gems of Granville Island, offering cyclists passing through the seawall and island area a glimpse of BC's maritime heritage. The site is an outdoor, publicly accessible exhibit managed under the Granville Island umbrella.

visitor.name: Festival Lawn at Deer Lake Park
visitor.desc: Deer Lake Park is an open-air concert venue in Burnaby managed by Live Nation, hosting a seasonal schedule of major outdoor shows on a large lawn setting. It is accessible via multiple transit routes and sits adjacent to the Shadbolt Centre for the Arts. Cyclists attending events will find limited bike racks near the East Gate entrance, though bikes are not permitted inside the venue grounds.

detail.address: 6450 Deer Lake Ave., Burnaby, BC V5G 2J3

visitor.name: Maritime Museum of British Columbia
visitor.desc: The Maritime Museum of BC is Victoria's dedicated institution for the province's nautical history and ocean sciences, housed near the Inner Harbour. It holds an extensive collection of objects, archives, photographs, and historic vessels, and runs rotating exhibits alongside programs for adults and children. The museum is currently partnering with Lekwungen Peoples on the Future of History project, a significant redevelopment in the Inner Harbour.

visitor.name: Kings Park
visitor.desc: Kings Park is a municipal sports field complex in Penticton, managed by the City of Penticton's Parks & Recreation department. Situated in the South Okanagan, the park serves as a local sports venue and green space that touring cyclists may pass on routes through town.

visitor.name: Bonsor 55+ Centre
visitor.desc: The Bonsor 55+ Centre is a dedicated seniors community centre within the Bonsor Recreation Complex in Burnaby, constructed in 2013. It serves adults 55 and over with recreation, fitness, and social programming in a purpose-built facility near Central Park. A touring cyclist passing through Burnaby may find it a useful stop for rest and facilities.

visitor.name: SL: Guildford Branch
visitor.desc: The Guildford Branch is one of ten public library branches operated by Surrey Libraries across Surrey, BC. It is a two-storey facility and is one of only three branches in the system equipped with assistive technology stations, including screen-reading and magnification software. As a free public space, it offers a welcoming stop for cyclists in the Guildford neighbourhood.

visitor.name: Whistler Blackcomb
visitor.desc: Whistler Blackcomb is North America's largest ski resort and a world-renowned four-season mountain destination operated by Vail Resorts. In summer it transforms into a major cycling hub anchored by the Whistler Mountain Bike Park, offering lift-accessed trail riding across both mountains. Touring cyclists passing through Whistler will find a full resort village with dining, rentals, and guest services at the mountain base.

detail.address: 4545 Blackcomb Wy, Whistler, BC V0N 1B4, Canada

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'On Mountain Dining' as a dedicated section and 'Dining' under Village Overview, confirming food service on site

visitor.name: Britannia Shipyards National Historic Site
visitor.desc: Britannia Shipyards is an eight-acre outdoor national historic site on the banks of the Fraser River in Steveston, preserving the oldest shipyard community in British Columbia. Heritage buildings from the 1880s are arranged along wooden boardwalks and tell the stories of the Chinese, European, Indigenous, and Japanese workers who lived in this once-thriving fishing, canning, and boatbuilding community. Admission is free and the site is easily reachable by bike from Steveston Village centre.

visitor.name: FVRL: Sardis Library
visitor.desc: The Sardis Library is a single-storey public branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library serving the Sardis neighbourhood of Chilliwack. As a fully accessible, free-admission public facility, it welcomes all visitors with outdoor bike racks, free Wi-Fi, public computers, and quiet study zones. Touring cyclists will find it a practical rest stop with accessible restrooms, baby changing stations, and a range of community services.

notes.Water without admission: Free public library (; no admission required to enter

visitor.name: Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre is a public recreation facility operated by North Vancouver Recreation and Culture, named after celebrated Canadian sprinter Harry Jerome who grew up in North Vancouver. The centre serves residents with a range of sports and fitness programs. A new replacement facility appears to be in planning or construction based on references to 'Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre (new)' alongside '(current)' in the city's navigation.

visitor.name: South Bonson Community Centre
visitor.desc: South Bonson Community Centre is a City of Pitt Meadows municipal recreation facility in the South Bonson neighbourhood, offering drop-in fitness classes, gymnasium and sport programs, and programming for early years, seniors, and youth. Operated by the City, it is a public facility situated along Barnston View Road in a predominantly residential area of Pitt Meadows. It could serve as a rest point for touring cyclists passing through the area, though specific cyclist-facing amenities are unconfirmed.

detail.address: 10932 Barnston View Road, Pitt Meadows, BC V3Y 2J5

visitor.name: Tofino Clayoquot Heritage Museum
visitor.desc: The Tofino Clayoquot Heritage Museum is a permanent exhibition housed in the lower level of the Royal Canadian Legion in Tofino, developed by the non-profit Tofino Clayoquot Heritage Society. It chronicles over 15,000 years of regional history, from the retreat of the last glaciers through Nuu-chah-nulth culture to the Clayoquot Sound logging protests that drew international attention. For touring cyclists on Vancouver Island's wild west coast, it offers rich cultural and environmental context to the landscapes they are riding through.

visitor.name: SFU Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The SFU Aquatic Centre is an indoor swimming facility operated by Simon Fraser University on its Burnaby Mountain campus, open to the public. As a university aquatic centre, it offers competitive-length pool swimming in a setting accessible to community members and visitors. Touring cyclists tackling the climb to SFU may find it a useful rest stop with facilities typical of a university rec centre.

visitor.name: Oliver Pool
visitor.desc: Oliver Pool is a community swimming facility in Oliver, BC, in the heart of the South Okanagan. Run by Oliver Recreation, it serves as the town's public aquatic centre and is tagged as a fee-based sports centre specializing in swimming. For touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan, it represents a potential mid-ride stop for a refreshing swim.

visitor.name: Grabenhorst Garden
visitor.desc: Grabenhorst Garden is a free, publicly accessible community garden operated by the City of Pitt Meadows, situated on Harris Road in the agricultural lowlands of Pitt Meadows. As a municipal green space, it offers a peaceful stop amid the flat, dyke-road cycling terrain of the lower Fraser Valley. Dogs are not permitted on site.

visitor.name: LoveCraft Art Gallery
visitor.desc: LoveCraft Art Gallery is a local art gallery situated in Tofino, BC, a hub for cycling tourism on Vancouver Island's rugged west coast. The gallery's distinctive teal building on Campbell Street (OSM building colour #5ecdcf) makes it a recognizable stop for cyclists exploring Tofino's compact downtown. Its Facebook presence under 'localtofinoart' suggests a focus on locally produced art from the region.

visitor.name: North View Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: North View Nature Reserve is a 7.2-hectare protected area on Salt Spring Island, managed by the Salt Spring Island Conservancy and donated to conservation in 2008. The reserve features a mix of coastal Douglas-fir forest, hardwoods, and restored areas once clear-cut and now being replanted with native species to remove invasive Scotch Broom. Touring cyclists stopping on Salt Spring Island can walk the full trail network in about half an hour to an hour, making it a short, accessible nature detour.

detail.address: 265 Blackburn Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2B8

visitor.name: Shawnigan Lake Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Shawnigan Lake Community Centre is a CVRD-operated public facility serving the Shawnigan Lake area of the Cowichan Valley on southern Vancouver Island. It sits at the edge of the Shawnigan Lake community, a popular destination for cyclists riding the Cowichan Valley region. As a regional district community centre, it likely serves as a gathering hub for local recreation and events.

visitor.name: FVRL: Abbotsford Community Library
visitor.desc: The Abbotsford Community Library is a public branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, centrally located in Abbotsford on Bevan Avenue. It offers a broad range of collections, digital services, computer access, and community programs in a welcoming, publicly accessible space. Touring cyclists passing through Abbotsford may find it a useful urban rest point, though specific cyclist amenities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Deep Cove Cultural Center
visitor.desc: Deep Cove Stage Society is a community theatre company that has been performing in Deep Cove since 1974, now celebrating its 51st season. The venue is tagged in OSM as an amphitheatre and hosts a full season of live productions. Cyclists exploring the scenic Deep Cove area may find this a worthwhile cultural stop, though the site is housed in what appears to be a multi-tenant cultural building.

visitor.name: VIRL: South Cowichan Branch
visitor.desc: The South Cowichan Branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the Mill Bay area since opening in 1989, with roots in the original Shawnigan Lake branch established in 1946. Located in a multi-unit commercial building, the branch offers meeting room bookings, public computing resources, home delivery for patrons unable to visit, and a full range of library services. It sits on the traditional territory of the Quw'utsun' (Cowichan) and Malahat peoples.

detail.address: 2720 Mill Bay Road, Mill Bay, V8H 1H9

visitor.name: Sooke Centre for the Performing Arts:
visitor.desc: The Sooke Centre for the Performing Arts is the home stage of Sooke Harbour Players, a community theatre society that has been producing live performances in Sooke since 1982. Located on the upper floor above Bosley's on Sooke Road, the venue hosts full theatrical productions as well as a monthly improv comedy series (PoSH Improv). As a registered BC charity, the Players have been a cultural anchor for Sooke and surrounding communities for over 40 years.

visitor.name: Port Moody Recreation Complex
visitor.desc: Port Moody Recreation Complex is a full-service municipal sports and fitness facility featuring a fitness and weight room, hot tub, and steam room alongside programs for all ages. The facility supports a wide range of activities including indoor cycling, hockey, curling, basketball, and running. Touring cyclists could use the hot tub and steam room for post-ride recovery.

visitor.name: West Highlands Park
visitor.desc: West Highlands Park is a municipal nature reserve in Kamloops, BC, managed by the City of Kamloops. Listed under the city's parks and sports fields, it may offer natural scenery for cyclists passing through the West Highlands neighbourhood.

visitor.name: Steveston Museum and Post Office
visitor.desc: The Steveston Railway Museum is a heritage attraction in the historic fishing village of Steveston, Richmond, BC — a popular destination for cyclists riding the dyke trails along the Fraser River delta. The OSM record links to the Steveston Historical Society, which has been preserving and promoting Steveston's history since 1976 and coordinates a network of heritage sites in the village. Steveston's compact, walkable village core, waterfront, and cannery sites make it a natural stop on any cycling tour of Metro Vancouver's south arm.

visitor.name: VIRL: Campbell River Branch
visitor.desc: The Campbell River branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library serves the second-largest population in the VIRL system, situated in the heart of downtown on Shoppers Row on the unceded traditional territory of the Ligwiłda'xw people. The branch offers bookable meeting rooms, digital learning resources, and a broad range of community programs spanning literacy, technology, and local culture. It is a well-established civic anchor for a community described as poised for significant growth.

visitor.name: Ambleside Rutledge Field
visitor.desc: Ambleside Rutledge Field is a field hockey pitch located within Ambleside Park on the West Vancouver waterfront, one of the North Shore's most popular recreational destinations. The park sits along the Burrard Inlet shoreline and is easily reached by the Spirit Trail and other cycling routes, making it a natural waypoint for touring cyclists riding the North Shore. As a public sports facility within a large municipal park, it offers a scenic rest stop with open green space.

visitor.name: VPL: Renfrew Branch
visitor.desc: The Renfrew Branch is part of Vancouver Public Library's network of neighbourhood branches, serving the Renfrew-Collingwood area of East Vancouver. Housed in a two-storey civic building, it offers a welcoming public space in a predominantly residential part of the city. Touring cyclists routing through East Vancouver's quieter streets will find it a convenient and accessible stop.

visitor.name: Stowel Lake Farm
visitor.desc: Stowel Lake Farm is a 115-acre organic farm and retreat centre on Salt Spring Island, founded by Lisa Lloyd in the mid-1970s on land originally known as the Old Reynolds Farm. It hosts wellness retreats, yoga classes, gardening workshops, and community events throughout the season, drawing guests from across BC and beyond. A Farm Stand sells farm produce to visitors, making it a potential stop for cyclists exploring the island.

detail.address: 190 Reynolds Road, Salt Spring Island, B.C. Canada, V8K 1Y2

notes.Café or food on site: Website prominently features 'The Farm Stand' as a dedicated section, selling farm produce on site

visitor.name: Zen Natural Wellness
visitor.desc: ZEN Natural Wellness is a multi-service wellness centre offering float therapy, halotherapy (dry salt therapy), infrared sauna, cold plunge, red light therapy, and EMS body sculpting. Formerly operating as Float House, the business has grown into a full recovery and wellness destination in the McCallum Junction area of Abbotsford. Touring cyclists looking for deep recovery could find the contrast therapy (Fire & Ice: sauna + cold plunge) and float sessions particularly restorative after long days in the saddle.

visitor.name: Bernie Legge Theatre
visitor.desc: Bernie Legge Theatre is home to Vagabond Players, the oldest community theatre in British Columbia, tracing its roots to 1922 and its current Queen's Park, New Westminster location to 1951. Over 350 productions have been staged here, and the theatre counts Raymond Burr and Bruno Gerussi among its notable alumni. Set within a public park and entirely volunteer-run, it offers an intimate, historic playhouse experience for visitors exploring New Westminster.

detail.address: Queen's Park, New Westminster, BC V3L 1L7

notes.Café or food on site: Coffee Bar on site offering beverages and snacks before the show and during intermission; beer and wine available for evening performances. Cash, debit, and credit accepted

visitor.name: Finn Slough (Tidal Community)
visitor.desc: Finn Slough is a tidal heritage community on the Fraser River in Richmond, BC, managed by the Finn Slough Heritage & Wetland Society. It is tagged as a tourism attraction in OpenStreetMap, suggesting it is a publicly accessible site of cultural or natural interest. Cyclists riding the Richmond dyke trail network may find it a worthwhile stop along the river.

visitor.name: ORL: West Kelowna Branch
visitor.desc: The West Kelowna Branch is part of the Okanagan Regional Library, BC's 16th largest library system, located in the Westridge Centre on Old Okanagan Highway. The branch offers two free study rooms, a 40-seat meeting room, exam invigilation services, and regular community programming. Free parking is available in the Westridge Centre lot, making it a convenient and sheltered stop in the heart of West Kelowna.

detail.address: 3731 Old Okanagan Highway, West Kelowna, V4T 1K7

visitor.name: 305 - Library
visitor.desc: The Nanaimo Harbourfront Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library is a major civic library serving Nanaimo from its location on Diana Krall Plaza, with roots in the community stretching back to the 1860s. The current five-storey building has been at its harbourfront location since 1997 and stands on the unceded territory of the Snuneymuxw First Nation. It offers a broad range of resources including a video game collection, meeting spaces, and skill-building programs, making it a substantial public hub in downtown Nanaimo.

visitor.name: The Trail Museum & Archives
visitor.desc: The Trail Museum & Archives is a free municipal museum opened in 2018 inside the Riverfront Centre, a shared civic facility that also houses the city library and visitor centre. It features three galleries, extensive archival holdings, and a gift shop developed in partnership with the Trail Historical Society, bringing local Kootenay history and heritage to life. For touring cyclists, it offers a no-cost cultural stop in central Trail with the added convenience of co-located visitor services.

visitor.name: Port Moody Station Museum;Port Moody Station
visitor.desc: The POMO Museum occupies an authentic 1908 CPR Train Station and has been run by the Port Moody Heritage Society since opening to the public in 1983. The site includes a 1921 Venosta train car, rotating heritage exhibitions, and a meditation garden. Admission is by donation and the museum is wheelchair accessible, making it an approachable heritage stop on a cycling tour of Port Moody's waterfront.

detail.address: 2734 Murray Street, Port Moody, BC V3H 1X2

visitor.name: The Britannia Mine Museum
visitor.desc: An award-winning National Historic Site located on the Sea to Sky Highway between Vancouver and Squamish, built on a former copper mine. Visitors can board a mine train for a guided underground tour, pan for gold, and experience the multi-sensory BOOM! show inside the historic Mill No. 3. A compelling stop for touring cyclists riding the Sea to Sky corridor, with an on-site cafe (Chatterbox Cafe) to refuel.

detail.address: Sea to Sky Highway, Britannia Beach, V0N 1J0

notes.Café or food on site: Chatterbox Cafe listed in the site navigation under Visit

visitor.name: Pebble Beach Recreation Site
visitor.desc: Pebble Beach Recreation Site protects several kilometres of undeveloped shoreline and beaches on Galiano Island in the area known to Hul'qumi'num-speaking peoples as Qw'xwulwis. The reserve encompasses a rare archaeological site, mature Coastal Douglas-fir forest, and lands managed by the Galiano Conservancy as part of a long-running ecological restoration program. It is part of the broader Qw'xwulwis – Cable Bay Conservation Area and offers a striking natural coastal setting for visitors arriving by bike or ferry.

visitor.name: Bob Prittie Metrotown Library
visitor.desc: A large three-story public library in Burnaby's Metrotown area, conveniently situated along the BC Parkway Urban Trail and Metrotown Bikeway. The branch features a digital studio, low-vision reader workstation, microfilm reader, and rotating art exhibitions from the Burnaby Art Gallery. It is well connected by SkyTrain and bus, with free underground parking available for those arriving by car.

notes.Wi-Fi: Free Wi-Fi listed as in-branch facility; OSM confirms SSID Burnaby-Library-Wifi with no password required

visitor.name: Tuckkwiowhum Heritage Interpretive Village
visitor.desc: Tuckkwiowhum Heritage Interpretive Village is operated by the Boston Bar First Nations and interprets the history and culture of the Indigenous peoples of the Fraser Canyon region. Located along the historic Hicks Road corridor near Boston Bar, it offers visitors an immersive look at traditional village life and heritage. For a touring cyclist passing through the rugged Fraser Canyon, it represents a rare opportunity to engage with the deep Indigenous history of this corridor.

visitor.name: Italian Garden
visitor.desc: The Italian Garden is a serene, symmetrical formal garden completed in 1914, located within the grounds of Hatley Park — a National Historic Site on the Royal Roads University campus about 25 minutes from downtown Victoria. Part of a larger garden complex including Japanese and rose gardens, the grounds are freely accessible and sit within a 260-hectare parkland that also offers hiking and biking trails. The iconic Hatley Castle provides a dramatic backdrop to the manicured grounds.

notes.Café or food on site: Habitat Café is listed on the Hatley Park site as an on-campus amenity alongside the gardens

visitor.name: Canada Place Welcome Centre
visitor.desc: Canada Place Welcome Centre is a tourist information office situated at the landmark Canada Place complex on Vancouver's downtown waterfront. It serves as a visitor orientation point for one of the city's most recognizable destinations, which also functions as a cruise ship terminal and convention venue. Touring cyclists arriving at the waterfront could use it as a starting point for maps and local visitor information.

visitor.name: Key City Theatre
visitor.desc: Key City Theatre is Cranbrook's primary performing arts venue, presenting live theatre, symphony concerts, and touring productions in the East Kootenay region. The building also houses a rotating art gallery featuring local and regional artists. It additionally hosts the annual Kootenay Children's Festival, making it a significant cultural hub for the community.

visitor.name: Cloverdale Sport & Ice Complex
visitor.desc: The Cloverdale Sport & Ice Complex is a City of Surrey municipal recreation facility in the Cloverdale neighbourhood offering multiple ice sheets for hockey, figure skating, public lessons, and skating sessions, with dry-floor summer conversion for lacrosse and ball hockey. Operated by the City of Surrey, the complex features outdoor amenities, landscaping, and ample vehicle parking. A touring cyclist passing through Cloverdale could visit as a local recreational attraction, though it is primarily a community sports facility.

visitor.name: Frederic Wood Theatre
visitor.desc: Frederic Wood Theatre is a 400-seat, 1960s proscenium theatre on the UBC Vancouver campus, featuring a fly tower, traps, and a built-in revolve. It is operated by UBC's Department of Theatre and Film and hosts student and professional productions throughout the academic year. Situated near the UBC Rose Garden at the western edge of campus, it is accessible via transit and is one of three performance venues run by the department.

visitor.name: Central Park Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: A heated 50-metre, 8-lane outdoor pool set in Burnaby's Central Park, open seasonally from late spring through summer. The facility includes a 1-metre diving board, men's and women's change rooms, and accessible amenities including a portable pool lift. A refreshing detour for cyclists riding through Burnaby on a warm day.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Accessible shower explicitly mentioned on website; change rooms imply shower facilities; requires pool admission
notes.Luggage / bag storage: On deck lockers available; own lock required

visitor.name: Capilano River Regional Park
visitor.desc: Capilano River Regional Park is a Metro Vancouver regional park and nature reserve in North Vancouver, tagged in OSM as wooded natural land along the Capilano River. It is a major green space destination on the North Shore, offering a natural contrast to the urban cycling routes of the surrounding area. Touring cyclists passing through North Vancouver would find it a notable landscape waypoint, though specific on-site facilities could not be verified from available sources.

visitor.name: Coastal Peoples Fine Arts Gallery
visitor.desc: Coastal Peoples Gallery is a long-established Indigenous art gallery in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, advocating for Northwest Coast, Inuit, Plains, and Maori artists and their communities since 1996. The gallery carries original artwork, jewelry, and graphics, and offers services ranging from art rentals and consignment to framing and installation. Located on Water Street, it sits in the heart of one of Vancouver's most cycle-accessible tourist districts.

visitor.name: Nanaimo Museum
visitor.desc: The Nanaimo Museum traces the city's history from Snuneymuxw First Nation living culture and oral traditions through to the coal-mining era that built the city, housed in a modern facility at the Vancouver Island Conference Centre that opened in 2008. Rotating feature exhibits complement permanent galleries on coal mining, local sports heritage, and the historic Bastion. A non-profit gift shop featuring Indigenous artwork, jewellery, and carvings by local artists makes it a distinctive stop in downtown Nanaimo.

visitor.name: Community Peace Garden
visitor.desc: A permaculture demonstration garden on the Vancouver Island University campus in Nanaimo, located on the north side of the campus library. Originally established in 2008 as the Community Peace Garden, it serves as a hands-on space for food growing, seed saving, and plant identification. The garden is open and accessible, offering a quiet green stop for anyone passing through the VIU campus.

visitor.name: Place des Arts
visitor.desc: Founded in 1972, Place des Arts is a not-for-profit arts education centre nestled in the historic Maillardville neighbourhood of Coquitlam, offering instruction in visual arts, music, dance, theatre, and literary arts for all ages and skill levels. The centre operates three gallery spaces and an Artisan Shop showcasing local and emerging artists, making it a genuine cultural hub for the region. Touring cyclists with an interest in the arts will find a busy, welcoming community venue with year-round programming and rotating exhibitions.

detail.address: 1120 Brunette Avenue, Coquitlam, British Columbia, Canada V3K 1G2

visitor.name: Valemount Arena
visitor.desc: The Canoe Valley Recreation Centre (listed in OSM as Valemount Arena) is a publicly operated multi-use facility in Valemount managed by the Regional District of Fraser-Fort George. During spring and summer the arena floor converts to host pickleball, basketball, ball hockey, and rollerblading, complemented by a fitness room with free weights and cardio equipment. Drop-in showers are available for a fee, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists moving through the Robson Valley.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Website fee table explicitly lists 'showers $3 per person drop-in for up to 2 hours use per visit'

visitor.name: Miner's Cottage
visitor.desc: The Coal Miner's Cottage is a municipally designated heritage site originally built by coal miner Frederick Rowbottom in the 1890s and now situated in Piper Park, Nanaimo. At just 360 square feet, it was once home to up to eight family members and is furnished with period artifacts representing life from 1914–1918. Programming and exhibits are managed by the Nanaimo Museum, making it an accessible stop for cyclists exploring Nanaimo's coal-mining history.

visitor.name: Iona Beach Park
visitor.desc: Iona Beach Regional Park is a Metro Vancouver regional park situated on the Iona spit in Richmond, extending into the Strait of Georgia near the mouth of the Fraser River. The park offers expansive views of the ocean, mountains, and the Vancouver skyline, making it a notable destination for cyclists exploring the Fraser River delta area. It is managed by Metro Vancouver as part of the regional parks system.

visitor.name: Massey Theatre
visitor.desc: Massey Theatre opened in 1949 as British Columbia's largest theatre and has been a cornerstone of New Westminster's performing arts life for over 75 years. The 1260-seat proscenium venue hosts professional orchestras, Broadway-style productions, international dance companies, and touring music acts, and also houses the Plaskett Gallery for visual artists. The complex is currently undergoing a significant renovation and expansion as part of the broader Eighth & Eight Creative Spaces project.

detail.address: 735 Eighth Avenue, New Westminster, BC V3M 2R2

notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'Patron services include ticketing, front of house / ushering, and food and beverages' on both the Rental & Services and Plan Your Visit pages

visitor.name: Lang Centre
visitor.desc: Lang Centre is a community centre operated by the City of Richmond in Richmond, BC. It is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a municipal community facility, but no further details about its programs, layout, or cyclist-relevant services could be confirmed due to a URL attribution mismatch in the source data.

visitor.name: Princeton Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: A year-round visitor information office in the heart of downtown Princeton, serving as a hub for the lower Similkameen Valley. It features a Virtual Reality Room where visitors can virtually kayak the Similkameen River, and staff can direct you to gold panning spots, hikes, dining, and accommodations. The centre also provides guides for the Bronze Sculpture walking tour through Princeton, known as the Bronze Statue Capital of Canada.

visitor.name: Campbell River Whale Whatching
visitor.desc: Campbell River Whale Watching and Adventure Tours is a carbon-neutral eco-tour company that has operated from the E-dock at Campbell River harbour since 2008, offering whale watching, grizzly bear, kayaking, eagle, and ocean rapids tours throughout Discovery Passage and surrounding waters. The company has grown to a fleet of seven vessels and is northern Vancouver Island's first carbon-neutral eco-tour operator. They hold Rainbow Registered accreditation as the first whale watching company in Canada to receive it, and partner with First Nations on grizzly bear tours that include cultural interpretation.

visitor.name: Anvil Centre
visitor.desc: Anvil Centre is a four-storey public arts and culture complex in downtown New Westminster, branded on its own site as 'Downtown's Living Room.' It brings together a professional theatre, conference facilities, a new media and art-technology gallery, a community art gallery, the New Westminster Museum & Archives, and the Canadian Lacrosse Hall of Fame under one roof. Touring cyclists will find a dense concentration of BC cultural heritage and active year-round programming in a single accessible downtown building.

visitor.name: Gur Sikh Temple
visitor.desc: The oldest existing Sikh Temple in North America, built by Sikh migrants between 1908 and 1911, and designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 2002. The ground floor houses the Sikh Heritage Museum, which has featured rotating exhibitions on topics from the Komagata Maru to South Asians in hockey since 2011. Guided group tours are available and a virtual tour allows remote visitors to explore the site.

detail.address: 33089 South Fraser Way, Abbotsford, BC V2S 2A8

visitor.name: Evergreen Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: Evergreen Cultural Centre is the Tri-Cities' premier professional arts venue, housing a 257-seat flexible black box theatre, a 1,500 sq ft public art gallery, and multiple rehearsal and studio spaces. Operated as a non-profit society, it serves Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, and Port Moody with performing arts, visual arts exhibitions, and education programs. The centre sits just steps from scenic Lafarge Lake and the Lafarge Lake-Douglas SkyTrain station, making it a convenient cultural stop on a ride through Coquitlam's city centre.

visitor.name: Mackin House Museum
visitor.desc: Mackin House Museum is built around a 1909 Edwardian-era heritage home originally constructed for the Sales Manager of Fraser Mills, and is operated by the Coquitlam Heritage Society to celebrate the multicultural history of Coquitlam and Maillardville — the largest French-speaking settlement in Western Canada. Visitors can tour the restored heritage interior, explore rotating and permanent exhibits on local and regional history, and visit the adjacent Fraser Mills Train Station and a 1970s Caboose. The museum offers guided tours, school programs, venue rentals, and recurring afternoon tea events in the heritage dining room.

notes.Café or food on site: Afternoon tea with homemade tea and scones served in the heritage dining room as part of a museum tour package

visitor.name: FVRL: City of Langley Library
visitor.desc: The City of Langley branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library is a full-service public library operated by FVRL, one of the largest regional library systems in British Columbia. Located in the heart of the City of Langley, it offers a range of programs, digital collections, and community services. For touring cyclists, public libraries are classic rest stops offering shelter, internet access, and often public washrooms, though specific amenity details are not confirmed on the website.

visitor.name: Hell's Gate
visitor.desc: Hell's Gate Airtram is an iconic Fraser Canyon attraction near Boston Bar, BC, where a Swiss-built aerial tramway descends 157 metres into one of the most dramatic river gorges in North America. At the bottom, visitors can explore a suspension bridge, fisheries exhibit, gold panning, and Simon's Cafe overlooking the Fraser River churning through a channel only 110 feet wide. Sitting directly on the Trans-Canada Highway roughly halfway between Vancouver and Kamloops, it is a natural landmark stop for cyclists touring the canyon corridor.

notes.Café or food on site: Simon's Cafe and a Fudge Factory (up to 100 flavours made on site) are listed as on-site experiences at the bottom of the gorge, accessible via the tram

visitor.name: Bill Reid Gallery of Northwest Coast Art
visitor.desc: The Bill Reid Gallery is Canada's only public gallery dedicated exclusively to Northwest Coast Indigenous art, established in 2008 to honour legendary Haida artist Bill Reid (1920–1998) and the living traditions of the Northwest Coast. Its permanent collection includes monumental works such as Mythic Messengers, the white onyx Raven and the First Men, and an exquisite jewelry collection, alongside rotating exhibitions of contemporary Indigenous artists. Located in the heart of downtown Vancouver, it also hosts a gallery shop selling authentic Indigenous art and merchandise, accessible without a paid admission ticket.

visitor.name: Coyote Cruises - Channel Float
visitor.desc: Coyote Cruises rents inner tubes and luxury party islands for a leisurely float down the 7-kilometre Penticton Channel, the natural waterway connecting Okanagan Lake to Skaha Lake. A shuttle bus returns floaters to the starting point, and the operation sells dry bags and waterproof cases to protect valuables. It is consistently rated one of Penticton's top summer bucket-list experiences, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists spending time in the Okanagan.

visitor.name: Summerhill Winery
visitor.desc: Summerhill Pyramid Winery is Canada's most-visited organic and biodynamic winery, nestled on the east shore of Okanagan Lake with sweeping views of the lake and surrounding mountains. The estate is anchored by a full-scale replica Egyptian pyramid used to age and clarify wines, a concept unique in the wine world. Touring cyclists will find a full bistro restaurant, a wine shop, and regular special events in a scenic lakeside setting accessible by public transit.

detail.address: 4870 Chute Lake Road, Kelowna, BC V1W 4M3

notes.Café or food on site: Nature's Table bistro on site offering lunch and dinner with lake views, plus catering services; restaurant menu pages

visitor.name: Coal Harbour Community Centre
visitor.desc: Coal Harbour Community Centre is a City of Vancouver facility located in the upscale Coal Harbour neighbourhood, steps from the seawall and marina. Operated jointly by the City and the West End Community Centre Association, it serves local residents with recreation and community programming. Touring cyclists riding the seawall route will find it a convenient stop in a scenic urban waterfront area.

visitor.name: Kwantlen Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: Kwantlen Outdoor Pool is a seasonal municipal outdoor swimming pool operated by the City of Surrey, located in the Whalley neighbourhood next to Kwantlen Park Secondary School. It is easily accessible on 104 Avenue from King George Boulevard, making it a convenient summer cool-down stop for cyclists passing through Surrey.

visitor.name: Kootenay Gallery of Art, History & Science
visitor.desc: The Kootenay Gallery of Art, History and Science is a non-profit public art gallery in Castlegar serving the entire West Kootenay Region, one of 28 original rural exhibition centres established in the 1970s to bring regional, national, and international art to BC's interior communities. It mounts rotating exhibitions, offers hands-on workshops, and maintains a gift shop, making it a cultural anchor for the region. Situated next to the Doukhobor Discovery Centre and across from the Castlegar Airport, it offers a compelling cultural detour for cyclists exploring the Kootenays.

visitor.name: Garry Oak Learning Meadow
visitor.desc: The Garry Oak Learning Meadow is an educational garden within Fort Rodd Hill and Fisgard Lighthouse National Historic Sites, managed by Parks Canada on the southern tip of Vancouver Island. It showcases one of Canada's rarest ecosystems — a native Garry Oak meadow filled with blooming wildflowers and abundant pollinators. The surrounding historic site also features a 19th-century coastal artillery fortress and Fisgard Lighthouse, the oldest permanent lighthouse on Canada's Pacific coast.

detail.address: 603 Fort Rodd Hill Road, Victoria BC V9C 2W8

visitor.name: ORL: Kalenden Branch
visitor.desc: The Kaleden Branch is a small public library serving the rural community of Kaleden, BC, roughly 15 km south of Penticton, as part of the Okanagan Regional Library system. It offers borrowing, digital resources, and community programming in a compact neighbourhood setting. A 24/7 outdoor book drop is located to the right of the front entrance.

visitor.name: Strawberry Hill Branch
visitor.desc: The Strawberry Hill Branch is a 11,100 sq. ft. single-floor public library operated by Surrey Libraries in the Strawberry Hill neighbourhood of Surrey. Located roughly 400m from the Scottsdale Exchange, it is served by over ten Translink bus routes and offers free parking on site. The branch includes a public art installation of E.D. Blodgett poetry above the service desk, giving it a modest cultural draw alongside its practical amenities.

visitor.name: Pinetree Community Centre
visitor.desc: Pinetree Community Centre is a City of Coquitlam municipal recreation facility offering group fitness classes, a weight room, multi-sport drop-in activities, youth programming, and rental meeting space. The centre is fully accessible with power-operated entrances, accessible washrooms, and elevator access. It is served by four bus routes and the Millennium SkyTrain line, making it convenient for cyclists moving through northeast Coquitlam.

visitor.name: Summerland Ornamental Gardens
visitor.desc: A historic 6-hectare ornamental garden originally established in 1914 as part of the Dominion Experimental Farm, now maintained by the volunteer-driven Friends of the Summerland Ornamental Gardens Society. Sitting directly on Highway 97 South — one of the Okanagan's primary cycling corridors — the gardens feature heritage trees, rose collections, and extensive xeriscape plantings, with a focus on water conservation and native pollinator habitat. Admission is by donation, making it an accessible stop for cyclists passing through the South Okanagan.

visitor.name: Chemainus Valley Museum
visitor.desc: The Chemainus Valley Museum is a community museum operated by the Chemainus Valley Historical Society, dedicated to preserving the cultural and industrial heritage of the Chemainus Valley, including artifacts from the historic local sawmill industry. The museum features rotating exhibits, a gift shop stocked with locally-made items and historical books, and can arrange group tours on request. It is wheelchair accessible and sits within the well-known mural town of Chemainus, a popular stop on Vancouver Island cycling routes.

visitor.name: Kimberley Public Library
visitor.desc: The Kimberley Public Library has served the community since 1927 and has operated from its dedicated building since 1980. Beyond books, it offers borrowable Outdoor Adventure Kits and hiking backpacks — a genuinely useful service for touring cyclists exploring the East Kootenays. It also hosts regular community programs and provides access to digital resources including e-books and online learning platforms.

visitor.name: Clayburn Schoolhouse Museum
visitor.desc: A volunteer-run museum preserving the history of Clayburn, British Columbia's first company town, built around the Vancouver Fireclay Company's brick works at the base of Sumas Mountain. The museum occupies the ground floor of the historic schoolhouse in a quaint heritage village with a brick church, creek, and park. A worthwhile stop for cyclists interested in BC's industrial heritage and early 20th-century company town life.

visitor.name: Fairacres Mansion
visitor.desc: Fairacres Mansion is a 1911 arts-and-crafts heritage building on Deer Lake Avenue in Burnaby, now home to the Burnaby Art Gallery — the only public art museum in Canada dedicated exclusively to works of art on paper. The restored mansion hosts rotating exhibitions, public programs, and school programs, and admission is always free. It is set near Deer Lake Park, making it a natural cultural stop for cyclists exploring the Burnaby lake-and-park corridor.

visitor.name: Japanese Fishermen's Benevolent Society Building
visitor.desc: The Japanese Fishermen's Benevolent Society Building is a free museum exhibit in historic Steveston that chronicles the Japanese Canadian fishing community's arrival, contributions, WWII internment, and postwar return — told through their own words, objects, and archival images. The building itself is a heritage landmark that once sat between the Japanese Hospital and Japanese Language School, both community-funded institutions. Steveston's compact, bike-friendly village makes this a natural stop on any cycling tour of Richmond's waterfront.

visitor.name: Chan Shun Concert Hall
visitor.desc: Chan Shun Concert Hall is the centrepiece of the Chan Centre for the Performing Arts at the University of British Columbia, celebrated internationally for its cello-inspired design and stellar acoustics since opening in 1997. The hall seats concertgoers beneath a striking 22.7-tonne adjustable acoustic canopy and has hosted artists from Jeremy Dutcher to Jon Batiste. Located on the scenic UBC campus along cycling-friendly routes, it is reachable by bike with dedicated racks steps from the main entrance.

visitor.name: Ladner Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: A municipal outdoor swimming pool in Ladner operated by the City of Delta. Situated along the flat cycling-friendly roads of south Delta, it could serve as a refreshing stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. As an outdoor facility it is likely seasonal.

visitor.name: Vernon and District Performing Arts Centre
visitor.desc: The Vernon and District Performing Arts Centre is a community theatre operated by a non-profit society on behalf of the Regional District of the North Okanagan, hosting over 100 concerts, festivals, and events each year alongside a curated SPOTLIGHT Presentation Season. Opened in October 2001 after a successful 1999 referendum, the facility features a Main Auditorium and the smaller Marie Fleming Studio, welcoming audiences of all ages to professional and community productions spanning dance, theatre, music, and special presentations. Touring cyclists passing through Vernon's North Okanagan corridor could take in live performances here as a cultural stop.

visitor.name: The Raptors
visitor.desc: The Raptors (also operating as Pacific Northwest Raptors Ltd.) is a birds-of-prey education and experience centre set in woodland near Duncan on Vancouver Island. Visitors can watch daily free-flight demonstrations featuring eagles, hawks, owls, and vultures, or book hands-on experiences such as walking with a hawk or holding a falcon on the glove. The centre has a conservation focus and also runs summer camps and a week-long falconry course, making it a memorable detour for touring cyclists exploring the Cowichan Valley.

detail.address: 1877 Herd Rd. Duncan, BC. Canada. V9L 5W4

visitor.name: Alaksen National Wildlife Area
visitor.desc: Alaksen National Wildlife Area is a federally managed 349-hectare nature reserve on the Fraser River Delta, established in 1976 across four former deltaic islands joined by causeways and dykes. It sits within a globally significant Important Bird Area and Ramsar Site, attracting up to 1.4 million migratory birds annually from Siberia to South America — including spectacular concentrations of snow geese exceeding 25,000 birds. For a touring cyclist, it offers a rare and peaceful wildlife experience on the flat, dyke-laced landscape of the Fraser Delta just south of Vancouver.

visitor.name: Theatre in the Park
visitor.desc: Theatre in the Park is an open-air theatre located in Whistler, BC, likely situated within or adjacent to Whistler Olympic Plaza. As an outdoor venue it offers a scenic setting for performances amid the mountain landscape of Whistler village. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a worthwhile cultural stop.

visitor.name: Fernwood Community Centre
visitor.desc: Fernwood Community Centre, operated by the Fernwood Neighbourhood Resource Group Society (Fernwood NRG), is a vibrant charitable non-profit hub in Victoria's Fernwood neighbourhood. The centre offers an eclectic mix of programming including weekly community meals, bike polo, yoga, queer boxing, and community gardens, alongside licensed childcare and affordable housing. It also hosts the annual FernFest, a free neighbourhood celebration with live music, food, and an artisan market.

visitor.name: Cameron Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Cameron Recreation Centre is a City of Burnaby community facility currently operating from temporary premises on the lower level of The City of Lougheed Shopping Centre while its permanent home is demolished and rebuilt. The temporary location offers fitness classes, table tennis, and drop-in PlayZone programming for families. The new permanent facility is planned to better serve northeast Burnaby's growing Lougheed Town Centre population.

visitor.name: Castlegar & District Curling Club
visitor.desc: The Castlegar & District Curling Club is a multi-league curling facility serving the Castlegar area with men's, ladies', mixed, junior, and doubles leagues as well as regional bonspiels. The club has a pro shop stocking Goldline curling equipment and rentals, and the facility — including the curling arena, kitchen, and lounge — is available for event rentals. A touring cyclist passing through the Kootenays during the winter season could experience a distinctly Canadian community sport tradition here.

visitor.name: Renfrew Pool
visitor.desc: Renfrew Pool is a City of Vancouver public swimming facility located in the Renfrew neighbourhood of East Vancouver. Operated by Vancouver Parks, Recreation & Culture, it is a fee-based aquatic centre serving the local community. Touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver may find it a convenient stop for a swim or facilities access.

visitor.name: Premier's Rose Garden
visitor.desc: The Premier's Rose Garden is a formal heritage rose garden situated on the exterior grounds of British Columbia's Legislative Assembly in the heart of Victoria's Inner Harbour. It forms part of the legislature's self-guided exterior tour and sits amid one of the most photographed civic landscapes in the province. Cyclists touring Victoria's waterfront will find it a natural and effortless detour given its central location.

visitor.name: Ness Lake Regional Park
visitor.desc: Ness Lake Regional Park is a 14-hectare day-use park managed by the Regional District of Fraser-Fort George, situated on a lake 30 km north of Prince George. The park offers 1.2 km of natural trails and a sandy beach suitable for canoeing, swimming, and winter ice fishing. For touring cyclists passing through Central BC, it provides a scenic lakeside rest stop with picnic tables and fire pits.

detail.address: Lakeside Drive, Electoral Area A (Salmon River-Lakes), BC

visitor.name: Museum at Campbell River
visitor.desc: The Museum at Campbell River is an award-winning regional history museum set on a seven-acre wooded site overlooking Discovery Passage, preserving the human history of Northern Vancouver Island from Oyster River to Rivers Inlet and beyond. Its 21,000 square foot facility opened in 1994 and holds ethnographic, archaeological, and archival collections alongside permanent, temporary, and outdoor exhibits. Cyclists riding the Island Highway will find a full program of guided hikes, boat tours, weaving workshops, and interpretive theatre rooted in First Nations and colonial-era history.

visitor.name: Alberni Valley Multiplex
visitor.desc: The Alberni Valley Multiplex is a large municipal ice sports complex in Port Alberni featuring two NHL-sized ice sheets and home to the Alberni Valley Bulldogs and Alberni Bombers hockey teams. The facility includes upper and lower lounges, dressing rooms, and concession stands on both levels, making it a hub for community sport and events. Touring cyclists passing through Port Alberni could visit for a local hockey game or to grab a meal at the concessions.

detail.address: 3737 Roger Street, Port Alberni BC V9Y 8E3

notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'upper and lower concessions' as part of the facility description

visitor.name: Widzin Kwah Canyon House Museum (Widzin Kwah Diyik Be Yikh)
visitor.desc: The Widzin Kwah Canyon House Museum sits above the famous Widzin Kwah (Bulkley River) Canyon, where visitors can watch traditional Witsuwit'en fishermen at work below. The museum holds artifacts and recently excavated stone tools carbon-dated back 6,000 years from the ground on which it stands, and offers professionally guided 45-minute cultural tours covering Witsuwit'en clan history, archaeology, and traditional fishing technologies. Authentic locally made moccasins, beaded jewelry, and native art are available for purchase on site.

notes.Café or food on site: Website notes 'a limited number of confectionary items' for sale and a 'complimentary cup of coffee' offered to visitors at the museum

visitor.name: Yaaguun Suu Heritage Site/Conservancy
visitor.desc: Yaaguun Suu Heritage Site/Conservancy is a protected wilderness area on Graham Island, Haida Gwaii, holding deep cultural, social, and spiritual significance for the Haida Nation since time immemorial. It encompasses Yakoun Lake and its tributaries, intact old-growth forests, and a network of traditional Haida trails connecting to other significant sites across the island. The conservancy is part of a broader system of protected areas covering half of Haida Gwaii's land base, making it a notable destination for cyclists exploring the archipelago's wild interior.

visitor.name: Union Bay Museum at the Old Gaolhouse
visitor.desc: The Union Bay Museum at the Old Gaolhouse is a community heritage museum operated by the Union Bay Historical Society, located in a historic former jail building on the South Island Highway on Vancouver Island. Union Bay itself has a rich coal-mining and industrial history dating to the late 19th century, making it a notable stop for cyclists exploring the Comox Valley corridor. The unusual gaolhouse setting gives the museum a distinctive character among small-town BC heritage sites.

visitor.name: Enderby Lions swimming pool
visitor.desc: A seasonal heated outdoor pool in Barnes Park in Enderby, where the Shuswap meets the Okanagan.
