The 25-yard, four-lane pool is surrounded by a playground, spray park, skateboard park, outdoor gym, and picnic area — making the whole park a worthwhile stop for touring cyclists on a hot day. A brand-new replacement pool is set to open in June 2026.

visitor.name: Shoe Tree
visitor.desc: The Shoe Tree near Holberg on northern Vancouver Island is a roadside folk-art landmark where passing travellers have decorated a tree with hundreds of thrown shoes over the years. It sits in a remote stretch of road on the way to Cape Scott Provincial Park, making it a natural stopping point for cyclists tackling the island's wild northwest coast. It is the kind of quirky, photogenic curiosity that punctuates long touring days.

visitor.name: Cariboo Memorial Recreation Complex
visitor.desc: The Cariboo Memorial Recreation Complex is the primary public recreation hub for Williams Lake and the Central Cariboo region, housing twin ice rinks, the West Fraser Aquatic Centre with a 25-metre lap pool and leisure pool, a fitness centre, and the multi-purpose Gibraltar Room. The aquatic wing features a waterslide, lazy river, hot swirl pool, steam room, and sauna — an impressive range of amenities for a mid-size interior BC city. The facility hosts year-round community programs from swimming lessons and aquafit to hockey leagues, film festivals, and day camps.

detail.address: 525 Proctor Street, Williams Lake, BC V2G 4J1

visitor.name: Artful: The Gallery
visitor.desc: Artful: The Gallery is a contemporary art gallery in Courtenay, BC, founded by multi-media artist and counsellor Kristina Campbell during the pandemic to provide exhibition space for emerging and mid-career artists working in diverse mediums. The welcoming, unpretentious space features oversized couches and chairs so visitors can linger with the work, and also hosts small events such as poetry readings, book launches, and workshops. Located in the Comox Valley, it is a genuine cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through Courtenay.

visitor.name: Riverside Adventures
visitor.desc: A family-owned whitewater rafting operation on the Clearwater River in Wells Gray Provincial Park, running for over 30 years. They offer owner-guided trips ranging from scenic float tours to multi-day rafting expeditions on the Babine and Nass rivers. All gear is provided including wetsuits, helmets, and life jackets, so touring cyclists could join a trip without carrying any extra equipment.

notes.Luggage / bag storage: Change room with lockers provided for customers to store personal belongings during trips

visitor.name: You + Me Studio
visitor.desc: You + Me Studio is a bright, 864-square-foot shared studio space in the centre of Qualicum Beach's small business district, available for yoga and pilates classes, wellness workshops, creative events, and private rentals. The modern space features white brick walls, nine-foot ceilings, and a turnkey setup with furniture and tech included. Touring cyclists seeking a drop-in wellness or movement class may find it a worthwhile stop in this popular Island cycling corridor.

detail.address: #1, 668 Beach Road, Qualicum Beach, BC, V9K 2R1

visitor.name: Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The New Denver Visitor Centre is a tourism information office situated in the small historic village of New Denver on the western shore of Slocan Lake in the West Kootenay region. New Denver anchors a scenic cycling corridor through the Slocan Valley and is home to the nationally significant Nikkei Internment Memorial Centre, making it a culturally rich stop on any touring itinerary. The village also offers access to local trails, Centennial Park, and the Kohan Reflection Garden.

detail.address: 115 Slocan Avenue, New Denver, BC V0G 1S0

visitor.name: Fog Alarm Building
visitor.desc: The Fog Alarm Building is a historic structure within Gulf Islands National Park Reserve, tagged in OpenStreetMap as a museum, reflecting its role in interpreting the maritime and navigational heritage of the southern Gulf Islands. The park reserve spans multiple islands and is accessible by ferry, making it a distinctive destination for cycle-touring visitors exploring the archipelago. Parks Canada operates interpretive programs throughout the reserve, though details specific to this building are not available from the associated web content.

detail.address: East Point Light Station, Saturna Island, BC V0N 2Y0

visitor.name: Glenwood Centre
visitor.desc: Glenwood Centre is a municipal community centre in Port Alberni operated by the City's Parks, Recreation & Culture department. It offers public drop-in programs and facility rentals, and is part of a broader network of recreation facilities in the Alberni Valley. The surrounding area features an extensive trail system popular with hikers and mountain bikers.

visitor.name: Harris Road Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: A municipal outdoor swimming pool and spray park operated by the City of Pitt Meadows. Located along Harris Road in the Fraser Valley, it offers a refreshing stop for touring cyclists riding the flat agricultural dyke routes of Pitt Meadows and Maple Ridge. The adjacent spray park adds a free cool-down option on hot days.

visitor.name: John Daly Park
visitor.desc: John Daly Park, also known as the John Daly Nature Reserve and by its Sechelt (Shíshálh) name ḵelx̱aminkwu, is a nature reserve managed by the Sunshine Coast Regional District on BC's Sunshine Coast. The park sits at 5930 Roosen Road and offers a natural green space in the region. Touring cyclists exploring the Sunshine Coast may find it a worthwhile scenic stop, though specific trail and facility details are not confirmed from available sources.

visitor.name: Golden BC Museum
visitor.desc: The Golden BC Museum is a community history museum operated by the Golden & District Historical Society, a volunteer non-profit established in 1968 and opened to the public in 1974. It preserves artifacts, archives, and stories from the Columbia River region — covering Indigenous Peoples of the Ktunaxa and Kinbasket Nations, CPR-era settlement, and generations of local pioneers — and draws roughly 3,500 on-site visitors per year. A companion BC Medical Museum is also housed under the same society, giving touring cyclists two distinct collections in one stop in the heart of Golden.

visitor.name: Gina Guu Aahljuu Naay Performance House
visitor.desc: The Gina Guu Aahljuu Naay (Performance House) is one of several traditional longhouse-style buildings within the award-winning Haida Heritage Centre at Ḵay Llnagaay in Skidegate, Haida Gwaii. The 50,000 sq ft Centre celebrates the living culture of the Haida people through art, language, and stories in a complex designed to resemble a traditional oceanside Haida village. Reaching Haida Gwaii requires a ferry from Prince Rupert or a flight to Sandspit, making the Centre a destination highlight for cyclists who make the journey.

detail.address: #2 Second Beach Road, PO Box 1523, Skidegate, B.C. V0T 1S1

notes.Café or food on site: Ḵay Bistro listed as one of the spaces within the Haida Heritage Centre (About page)

visitor.name: Bralorne Pioneer Museum
visitor.desc: The Bralorne Pioneer Museum preserves the history of the Bridge River Valley's storied gold mining era in the remote community of Bralorne, BC. It sells a curated selection of books and merchandise documenting mining life and backcountry adventures in the valley. For touring cyclists making the long ride into this seldom-visited corner of the Sea-to-Sky region, the museum offers a rare cultural anchor in an otherwise wilderness setting.

visitor.name: Dawson Creek Municipal Library
visitor.desc: The Dawson Creek Municipal Library is a full-service public library serving the northeastern corner of British Columbia, offering an extensive physical collection of books, DVDs, and magazines alongside a robust digital lending program. It provides free computer and internet access to the public and maintains a community information hub with local recreation and tourism links. For touring cyclists passing through Dawson Creek — gateway to the Alaska Highway — the library offers a welcoming indoor rest stop with connectivity.

detail.address: 1001 McKellar Avenue, Dawson Creek BC V1G 4W7

visitor.name: Kootenae House National Historic Site
visitor.desc: Kootenae House National Historic Site marks the location of the first fur trade post established west of the Rockies, built by explorer David Thompson in 1807 near present-day Invermere in the Columbia Valley. It is a federally designated monument commemorating a pivotal moment in Pacific Northwest exploration and the fur trade. Touring cyclists riding the Columbia Valley corridor will find this a notable historical waypoint in a region rich with natural and Indigenous history.

visitor.name: Rotary Bike Park
visitor.desc: Rotary Bike Park is a City of Merritt-operated outdoor cycling facility tagged as a BMX venue in OSM, located in the Nicola Valley region of BC's Okanagan & Thompson area. It sits within the broader network of Merritt's municipal parks, which also includes a bike pumptrack at nearby Central Park. The facility caters primarily to BMX and freestyle riders.

visitor.name: Atlin Museum, Gift Shop and Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Atlin Museum occupies a heritage building originally constructed as Atlin's first schoolhouse in 1902, later relocated and converted into a museum in 1972 by the Atlin Historical Society. Its exhibits and archives document the region's Klondike-era gold rush, Taku River Tlingit culture, and early settler life. The museum's most striking outdoor exhibit is an IRI-A steam shovel described as the only operational steam shovel of its kind in North America—a rare find for any visitor passing through this remote northern BC community.

visitor.name: Revelstoke Dam Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Revelstoke Dam Visitor Centre, operated by BC Hydro, sits at the base of the Revelstoke Dam on the Columbia River and offers guided and self-guided exploration of one of BC's major hydroelectric facilities. The centre is a seasonal stop that gives visitors a striking close-up view of the dam's massive concrete structure and the reservoir above. For touring cyclists passing through the Revelstoke area, it represents a distinctive engineering landmark well off the usual commercial strip.

visitor.name: Lighthouse Community Centre
visitor.desc: Lighthouse Community Centre is a community facility located on Vancouver Island in British Columbia. As a community centre, it would typically serve as a hub for local programs and public services, potentially useful to touring cyclists passing through the area. The current operational status cannot be confirmed as the associated website has expired.

visitor.name: Bralorne Pioneer Museum
visitor.desc: A small community heritage museum in the remote former gold-mining town of Bralorne, housed in the historic post office building. Bralorne sits at the end of a long mountain road in the Bridge River Valley, making it an adventurous destination for touring cyclists exploring the backcountry of the Squamish-Lillooet region. The museum is operated under the Squamish-Lillooet Regional District's heritage program.

visitor.name: Walcott Quarry
visitor.desc: Walcott Quarry is the original excavation site of the Burgess Shale, one of the world's most celebrated paleontological discoveries and a UNESCO World Heritage Site within Yoho National Park. The quarry preserves extraordinarily detailed half-billion-year-old marine fossils and is accessible only via strenuous guided hikes offered by Parks Canada. Touring cyclists based in the Field, BC area can book a guided day-hike to the quarry as a once-in-a-lifetime side trip from the Kicking Horse corridor.

visitor.name: Port McNeill & District Museum
visitor.desc: The Port McNeill & District Museum is a community-built institution dedicated to logging memorabilia from British Columbia's North Island, opened in 2000. It features video exhibits including 'The Last Logging Railway in North America' and 'Women in Log Scaling,' offering a compelling look at the industrial heritage of the region. Admission is by donation, making it an accessible cultural detour for cyclists exploring the northern tip of Vancouver Island.

visitor.name: Ray Farm
visitor.desc: Ray's Farm is identified in OSM as a tourism attraction located within the Wells Gray Park area of British Columbia's Cariboo Mountains. Based on discovery notes, it appears to be a historic homestead site inside Wells Gray Provincial Park, a spectacular destination known for old-growth rainforest, alpine meadows, and numerous waterfalls. No dedicated information about the site's history, facilities, or visitor experience was found in available sources.

visitor.name: Kootenay River Theatre
visitor.desc: The Kootenay River Theatre is a community performing arts venue housed in the southwest corner of the Kootenay River Secondary School building in Creston, BC. It is supported by the Creston Community Auditorium Society, which fundraises for equipment upgrades and manages online ticket sales independently from School District #8. Touring cyclists passing through the Kootenays could catch a live performance here as a cultural stop in the region.

visitor.name: SL: Clayton Branch
visitor.desc: The Clayton Branch is a 13,500 sq. ft. public library operated by Surrey Libraries, co-located within the Clayton Community Centre in Surrey's Fraser Valley. It is fully accessible and offers free Wi-Fi, public computers, silent and private study rooms, and a range of community programming. Touring cyclists will find clean, plentiful washrooms and a welcoming public space to rest and recharge devices.

visitor.name: Alexandra Suspension Bridge
visitor.desc: Alexandra Bridge Park is a small BC Parks day-use site preserving the historic crossing point where Joseph Trutch's 1861 Cariboo Wagon Road bridge—named after Princess Alexandra of Wales—once spanned the Fraser River. Touring cyclists on the Trans-Canada Highway through the Fraser Canyon will find it a natural rest stop with picnic facilities, situated about 40 km north of Hope with access from both highway directions. The park occupies territory that has served as a Fraser River crossing and fishing ground for over 9,500 years, lending it exceptional cultural and historical depth.

visitor.name: Sunshine Coast Botanical Garden Society
visitor.desc: A community botanical garden in Sechelt on the Sunshine Coast, situated in shíshálh Nation territory and focused on collecting and conserving plants of the Pacific Northwest. Founded in 2002, the garden features an extensive network of paths through native plant habitats, a rhododendron walk, viewing platform, and ponds. The garden actively encourages cyclists to ride there and provides a bike rack in the parking lot.

visitor.name: The Learning Farm
visitor.desc: The Langley Learning Farm is a community-based food production demonstration site located at the Derek Doubleday Arboretum on parkland within the Agricultural Land Reserve. Established in September 2020, it is a student-led initiative where Grade 11/12 students from Langley Secondary School tend growing beds, a hoop house, and a fruit-bearing hedgerow as part of an experiential Environmental Science course. Public informational signage explains the project, making it a modest stop for cyclists curious about urban agriculture and food security efforts in the Fraser Valley.

visitor.name: Little Prairie Heritage Museum
visitor.desc: The Little Prairie Heritage Museum is a community heritage museum near Chetwynd in the Peace River region of Northern BC, preserving the history of the Little Prairie settlement area. It sits in a remote and scenic part of the province that touring cyclists traversing the region may pass through. The museum maintains a Facebook presence at the contact listed in OSM.

visitor.name: Alert Bay ArtLoft Gallery and Gift Shop
visitor.desc: The Alert Bay ArtLoft Gallery and Gift Shop is an art gallery and retail space located in Alert Bay, a small community on Cormorant Island off northeastern Vancouver Island. Alert Bay is a culturally rich destination known for its Indigenous heritage and totem poles, making this gallery a likely showcase for local and Indigenous art. Touring cyclists arriving by ferry would find it a natural stop in a compact, walkable village.

visitor.name: Pender Hill Park
visitor.desc: Pender Hill Park is a nature reserve managed by the Sunshine Coast Regional District on the upper Sunshine Coast. The park occupies elevated terrain near Madeira Park and is likely accessed via Coastview Drive, offering natural area recreation in a coastal BC setting. Touring cyclists in the Pender Harbour area may find it a worthwhile side trip, though on-site facilities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Pearl Ellis Gallery
visitor.desc: Pearl Ellis Gallery is a non-profit, volunteer-run art gallery located in the heart of Comox, founded in 1977 as the Comox Arts Society and renamed in 2005 to honour one of its founders. The gallery showcases rotating exhibitions of local painters, sculptors, and photographers, with new shows opening every few weeks throughout the year. Entry is by donation, making it an easy and low-barrier cultural stop for cyclists passing through the Comox Valley.

visitor.name: Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Port McNeill Visitor Information Centre is the official municipal tourism gateway for Port McNeill on northern Vancouver Island, operated by the Town of Port McNeill. It provides information on local attractions including whale watching, the world's largest burl, Broughton Strait Campground, and the Outer Islands. For touring cyclists exploring northern Vancouver Island, this centre is a useful stop for regional information and trip planning.

visitor.name: Miller (Shantz) House
visitor.desc: The Miller (Shantz) House is a heritage building within the Pemberton & District Museum & Archives complex, situated in the heart of the Pemberton Valley on the traditional territory of the Lil'wat and St'át'imc Nations. The museum society, now in its 42nd year, preserves and shares regional history through collections of 700+ objects, 2,000+ photographs, and 250+ videos. Admission is by donation, making it an accessible cultural stop for cyclists passing through Pemberton on the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

visitor.name: Merville Community Hall
visitor.desc: Known locally as 'the Big Yellow Hall,' the Merville Community Hall is a rural gathering place in the Comox Valley countryside, operated by the Merville Community Association. It hosts live music, contra dances, community fairs, and other events, drawing visitors from across Vancouver Island. For touring cyclists on the Old Island Highway corridor, it is a recognizable landmark and potential stop in an otherwise sparsely served rural stretch.

visitor.name: LALA: Gold Bridge Library
visitor.desc: The Gold Bridge Library is a branch of the Lillooet Area Library Association, a community non-profit serving the small and isolated Bridge River Valley. It offers internet access and a community room in a part of BC where services are scarce. For cyclists riding the Hurley Forest Service Road or exploring the Bralorne area, the branch represents a rare digital lifeline in an otherwise off-grid landscape.

visitor.name: Heritage Air Park
visitor.desc: Heritage Air Park is an outdoor aircraft display area operated by the Comox Air Force Museum, featuring aircraft models that have flown at 19 Wing Comox — from the Dakota to the Aurora — along with Heritage Stones, a Search and Rescue memorial, and the Clarkston Memorial. Situated on Military Row/Little River Road roughly 600m from the main museum building, the park offers up-close access to historic RCAF aircraft in a relaxed, picnic-friendly setting. It is part of the broader RCAF Museum Enterprise and commemorates West Coast military aviation history dating back to WWII.

detail.address: Military Row / Little River Rd, Lazo, BC V0R 2K0

visitor.name: Jipsi Tree Brick and Mortar
visitor.desc: Jipsi Tree Brick and Mortar is a nature-inspired art and style gallery on Vancouver Island, operating as the physical retail counterpart to an online brand. The 'Brick and Mortar' name signals it is a dedicated storefront presence, and OSM records it as a free-admission gallery. Cyclists passing through the Courtenay/Cumberland corridor may find it a worthwhile stop for locally made goods and art.

visitor.name: Elksentre Arena
visitor.desc: A City of Prince George municipal arena in the Cariboo region, primarily serving local ice sports and skating programs. It is part of the city's network of civic recreation facilities.

visitor.name: Lerwick Nature Park
visitor.desc: Lerwick Nature Park is a nature reserve in the Comox Valley Regional District on Vancouver Island, managed by the CVRD. Its location near coordinates 49.692°N, 124.957°W places it in the broader Comox Valley, a region popular with touring cyclists exploring Vancouver Island. As a nature reserve, it may offer scenic natural surroundings as a rest or exploration stop, though specific facilities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Fort Nelson Heritage Museum
visitor.desc: The Fort Nelson Heritage Museum sits at the historic Mile 300 marker on the Alaska Highway, preserving the story of the highway's dramatic nine-month WWII construction and the region's broader history from fur-trade origins to the oil-and-gas era. Spread across more than eight buildings and outdoor grounds, the collection includes vintage and WWII-era vehicles, a trapper's cabin, a general store display, and a life-sized sculpture of the record Chadwick Ram. The museum was founded by mechanic Marl Brown, who began rescuing discarded Army equipment in the 1950s and devoted the rest of his life to building the collection.

visitor.name: Tetsa River Park
visitor.desc: Tetsa River Regional Park and Campground sits along the Alaska Highway just past Steamboat Mountain in the remote Northern Rockies of BC, making it a natural overnight stop for cyclists riding the iconic highway corridor. The park features trails suited to hiking, biking, and horseback riding, with 25 unserviced campsites available by reservation or drop-in. Its isolation and scenic river setting offer a genuine wilderness experience far from the nearest town.

detail.address: Mile 580/KM 365 Alaska Highway, Northern Rockies, BC

visitor.name: Red Chairs
visitor.desc: The Red Chairs are Parks Canada's iconic red Adirondack-style chairs placed at scenic viewpoints within Glacier National Park, inviting visitors to pause and take in the dramatic alpine scenery of the Selkirk and Purcell Mountains. Situated along the Rogers Pass corridor on the Trans-Canada Highway, this stop is directly on one of Canada's most storied long-distance cycling routes. The viewpoint offers a sense of place at the heart of a park renowned for ancient cedar forests, avalanche terrain, and deep mountaineering history.

detail.address: 9520 Trans-Canada Highway, Rogers Pass, BC V0E 2S0

visitor.name: Hemlock Grove Boardwalk
visitor.desc: The Hemlock Grove Boardwalk is a circular nature walk through old-growth forest within Glacier National Park, located near Rogers Pass along the Trans-Canada Highway. The boardwalk winds through moss-draped cedars in what Parks Canada describes as the world's only inland cedar rainforest. It lies within a park renowned for dramatic alpine scenery and deep river valleys, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists travelling the Trans-Canada corridor.

detail.address: 9520 Trans-Canada Highway, Rogers Pass, BC V0E 2S0

visitor.name: The Langham
visitor.desc: The Langham is a Provincial Heritage Site in Kaslo, BC, operating as a multi-faceted cultural centre with two public art galleries, a 70-seat theatre, and a Japanese Canadian Internment Museum that commemorates the WWII-era internment through artifacts and personal stories. Founded in 1975 and run by the Langham Cultural Society, it presents year-round performances, exhibitions, and community events showcasing Canadian and regional artists. Touring cyclists passing through Kaslo's historic downtown will find it a compelling cultural stop, with gallery admission by donation.

visitor.name: ORL: Salmon Arm Branch
visitor.desc: The Salmon Arm Branch of the Okanagan Regional Library is part of a 30-branch regional system serving over 399,000 residents across the BC interior, and is housed within the Piccadilly Mall complex in central Salmon Arm. It offers computers, Wi-Fi, meeting rooms, and a Library of Things lending collection, making it one of the more substantive community gathering points in the Shuswap for travellers. Free parking in the adjacent Piccadilly Mall lot adds to its accessibility as an urban rest stop.

visitor.name: FVRL: Pitt Meadows Library
visitor.desc: The Pitt Meadows Public Library is a full-service branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, offering public computers, a teens' space, children's area, quiet study zones, and a broad range of community programming. It is a fully accessible modern facility with automatic doors, elevators, and wheelchair-accessible computer stations. Touring cyclists will find it a practical urban rest stop in the heart of Pitt Meadows, with outdoor bike racks, washrooms, water fountains, and free WiFi.

notes.Water without admission: Public library with free public access; water fountains listed as a facility feature

visitor.name: Splatsin Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Splatsin Community Centre is a 33,581 sq ft multipurpose venue built by the Splatsin First Nation in Enderby, with a roof modelled after the traditional Kekuli winter shelter, planted with living greenery, and ancient pictographs adorning the exterior. It functions as a regional cultural hub accommodating meetings, banquets, weddings, concerts, and conferences for groups of 10 to 1,000. An indoor walking track and an art gallery are available as day-use amenities, making it a distinctive cultural landmark in the North Okanagan for cyclists passing through.

detail.address: 5767 Old Vernon Road, Enderby, BC V0E 1V0

visitor.name: Tumbler Ridge Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Tumbler Ridge Community Centre is a multi-facility municipal complex in this small northern BC resource town, housing an arena, aquatic centre, curling rink, fitness area, and indoor play park. Situated in a remote region near the Tumbler Ridge Global Geopark and its renowned dinosaur fossil sites, the centre serves as a hub for community services in one of BC's more isolated communities. For touring cyclists on long-haul northern routes, it may offer a rare opportunity to access indoor facilities in an area with limited services.

detail.address: 305 Illes Way, Tumbler Ridge, BC V0C 2W0

visitor.name: CRDL: Williams Lake Library
visitor.desc: The Williams Lake branch of the Cariboo Regional District Library is one of three main branches in a 15-branch regional system serving the Cariboo and Chilcotin. It offers on-site tech services, community programmes, and room bookings. A practical stop for touring cyclists passing through Williams Lake on Highway 97 or the Gold Rush Trail corridor.

visitor.name: Big White Ski Resort
visitor.desc: Big White is a major four-season mountain resort in the Okanagan Highlands east of Kelowna, primarily known as a ski destination but operating a summer bike park and guided eBike tours through alpine terrain. The resort village is largely self-contained, with restaurants, food trucks, a market, medical services, shopping, and a range of accommodation. For cycling tourists, it functions as a destination attraction with lift-accessed mountain biking and organized eBike experiences.

detail.address: 5315 Big White Rd, Kelowna, BC V1P 1T4, Canada

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Restaurants, Food Trucks & Market' and 'Order Groceries Online' under Food & Dining in the summer season navigation

visitor.name: CF-101 Voodoo
visitor.desc: The CF-101 Voodoo (tail number 101035) is a Cold War-era RCAF fighter-interceptor that stands on a pedestal at the entrance to the Abbotsford International Airport. The aircraft served in the RCAF from 1961 to 1987 and was transferred to the Abbotsford International Airshow Society in 1992 following its retirement. It is a visible roadside landmark for anyone cycling past or to the airport in the Fraser Valley.

visitor.name: Thorsen Creek Conservancy
visitor.desc: Thorsen Creek Conservancy is a BC Parks protected area located approximately 10 kilometres southeast of Bella Coola, established as part of the Central Coast land use decision. It is home to one of the largest and most significant collections of petroglyphs on the British Columbia coast, holding deep cultural heritage significance to the Nuxalk First Nation. The conservancy also protects valuable fish habitat along Thorsen Creek, a tributary of the lower Bella Coola River.

visitor.name: Red Creek Fir
visitor.desc: The Red Creek Fir is recognized as the largest Douglas-fir tree on Earth, standing 73.8 metres tall with a trunk 4.2 metres wide (DBH), located approximately 15 kilometres east of Port Renfrew on Vancouver Island. It is listed in the BC Big Tree Registry and represents a remarkable old-growth giant in a region popular with cycle tourists. Access is via forest road, making it a potential off-bike side trip for riders exploring the Port Renfrew area.

detail.address: Juan de Fuca, BC V0S 1K0, Canada

visitor.name: CRDL: Interlakes Branch
visitor.desc: The Interlakes Branch is a small community library branch of the Cariboo Regional District Library system, serving the Lone Butte area of the Central Interior. It is staffed by a community librarian and offers borrowing services, digital library access, and a novel 'Library of Things' that now includes items like a bat-detection device and pickleball sets. For touring cyclists passing through this remote stretch of BC, it offers a quiet stop with internet access and community resources.

detail.address: 7170 Levick Cr., Lone Butte, BC V0K 1X1

visitor.name: Sandspit Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Sandspit Visitor Centre is a tourism information office located at Sandspit Airport on Haida Gwaii, one of Canada's most remote and ecologically rich cycling destinations. Situated at the island's main air entry point, it serves as a first stop for travellers — including cyclists flying in with their bikes — seeking local knowledge and orientation. The centre is wheelchair accessible per OSM, and its remote island setting makes it a notable waypoint for adventure cyclists exploring the archipelago.

visitor.name: Tems Swiya Museum
visitor.desc: The Tems Swiya Museum is operated by the shíshálh Nation and holds a significant collection of Indigenous cultural artifacts, including cedar baskets, stone tools, and a 3,500-year-old mortuary stone. Situated on the Sunshine Coast Highway beside the Raven's Cry Theatre in Sechelt, it sits directly on a popular cycling corridor. Cyclists passing through gain rare direct access to the living cultural heritage of the shíshálh people.

detail.address: 5555 Sunshine Coast Highway, Sechelt, BC V0N 3A0

visitor.name: Comox Valley Rhododendron Garden
visitor.desc: The Comox Valley Rhododendron Garden is a community garden established in 1996 through a partnership between the North Island Rhododendron Society and the City of Courtenay under the 'Partners In Parks' program. It now contains 7 beds with over 130 rhododendron varieties, including the 'BOVI' bed featuring only plants hybridized on Vancouver Island. The garden sits along the public walking path between the Historic Train building on Cliffe Ave. and the Courtenay Airpark, making it easily accessible to cyclists travelling through the area.

visitor.name: Roy Stewart Morrison Nature Park
visitor.desc: Roy Stewart Morrison Nature Park is a nature reserve near Courtenay on Vancouver Island, documented by BC Nature, the provincial federation of naturalist clubs. The park is situated on Vancouver Island's east coast and would appeal to touring cyclists seeking a natural area to explore. No further details about the park's size, trails, or history were recoverable from the available sources.

visitor.name: Emerald Lake
visitor.desc: Emerald Lake is Yoho National Park's largest and most iconic lake, renowned for its vivid turquoise colour produced by glacial rock flour suspended in glacial meltwater. Nestled beneath the President Range on the western slopes of the Great Divide, it sits at the end of a dedicated access road off the Trans-Canada Highway near Field, BC. The lake is a popular day-use destination within a UNESCO World Heritage-associated park also known for the nearby Burgess Shale fossil beds.

detail.address: Emerald Lake, Columbia-Shuswap, BC V0A, Canada

visitor.name: Horne Lake Caves Provincial Park Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: Horne Lake Caves is a year-round professionally guided caving destination within a BC provincial park on Vancouver Island, and the site of Canada's first cave interpretive centre, built in 2011. Tours range from beginner-friendly walks through spacious Riverbend Cave to multi-hour vertical adventures involving rope swings, rappels, and cable ladder climbs deep underground. The caves are entirely wild and undeveloped — no installed lighting, paved walkways, or handrails — offering an authentic caving experience in a system that has been welcoming visitors since the park's establishment in 1971.

visitor.name: ORL: Keremeos Branch
visitor.desc: The Keremeos Branch is a small public library in the southern Okanagan's Similkameen Valley, operated by the Okanagan Regional Library — a regional system of 30 branches serving over 399,000 people across 59,600 square kilometres. The branch hosts community programming including LEGO Club events and is supported by a Friends of the Library volunteer group that runs book sales and organizes community gatherings. As one of the few public facilities in the small town of Keremeos, it can serve as a community anchor point for cyclists passing through the valley.

visitor.name: Pemberton & District Museum & Archives Society
visitor.desc: The Pemberton & District Museum & Archives Society has been collecting, preserving, and sharing the heritage of the Pemberton Valley since 1982, nestled on the traditional territory of the Lil'wat and St'át'imc Nations. Its archives hold over 180 documents, 700 objects, 2,000 photographs, and 250 videos, with several online exhibits covering themes like logging and railway history. Admission is by donation, making it an accessible cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

visitor.name: Terrace Sportsplex
visitor.desc: The Terrace Sportsplex is a municipal ice arena and sports complex operated by the City of Terrace, primarily hosting ice hockey and public skating. Located in the heart of Terrace in BC's North Coast region, it serves as a community recreation hub for residents and visitors. A touring cyclist passing through Terrace might visit for a rest stop, though its primary draw is ice-based sport rather than cycling-specific services.

visitor.name: ORL: Revelstoke Branch
visitor.desc: The Revelstoke Branch of the Okanagan Regional Library is a public library located next to the Community Centre, offering free public Wi-Fi, seven internet computers, and a makerspace with equipment including a Cricut cutting machine and digitization stations. Part of one of Canada's 16th-largest library systems, the branch serves the Revelstoke community with programming, events, and a broad digital and physical collection. For a touring cyclist, it provides a comfortable indoor rest space with seating, accessible facilities, and free parking in the adjacent Community Centre lot.

visitor.name: Smithers District of Commerce
visitor.desc: The Smithers District Chamber of Commerce operates the Bulkley Valley's primary Visitor Centre, offering personalized trip planning, regional and provincial tourism information, BC Ferries and accommodation reservations, and a curated selection of road, backcountry, and forest service maps. A mobile outreach team called VIBE takes visitor services directly to community events and farmers markets throughout town. For a touring cyclist arriving in the Smithers area, this is a practical first stop for local knowledge and free wireless internet.

visitor.name: Powder King Mountain Resort
visitor.desc: Powder King Mountain Resort is a remote ski resort situated near Pine Pass in Northern BC, celebrated locally as 'the whisper of the north' for its deep powder and uncrowded terrain. Beyond skiing, the resort operates the Azouzetta Lake Lodge & Campground year-round, offering summer camping beside Azouzetta Lake in a dramatic mountain setting. Touring cyclists passing through the Pine Pass corridor would find food, lodging, and camping options at this otherwise isolated location.

detail.address: Mile 122 John Hart Highway, Mackenzie, BC V0J 2C0

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists multiple dining options: Dining Room & Pub, Cafeteria, and Cafe97 (with phone 1 250 783 1529); Cafe97 stated open year-round

visitor.name: Coquihalla Canyon
visitor.desc: Coquihalla Canyon Provincial Park preserves a dramatic stretch of the Kettle Valley Railway, including five tunnels blasted through 300-foot-deep granite gorge walls in 1914, now known as the Othello Tunnels. The easy 3.5 km round-trip trail through the tunnels is part of the Trans Canada Trail and offers a flat gravel surface accessible to cyclists and walkers alike. Located just north of Hope, it is one of the most visited heritage railway attractions in southern BC and a natural stop on any Kettle Valley Rail Trail tour.

detail.address: Tunnels Rd, Hope, BC V0X 1L1, Canada

visitor.name: Columbia National Wildlife Area
visitor.desc: Columbia National Wildlife Area is a federally protected wetland complex in the Rocky Mountain Trench of southeastern BC, consisting of four separate units — Wilmer, Spillimacheen, Brisco, and Harrogate — strung along the Columbia Valley. The area forms part of the larger Columbia Wetlands system, one of the longest continuous wetlands in North America and a major corridor of the Pacific Flyway. Touring cyclists riding the Columbia Valley route pass through or near these units and can observe migratory waterfowl and wetland wildlife in a dramatic mountain setting.

visitor.name: Shuswap Theatre
visitor.desc: Shuswap Theatre is a nonprofit community theatre society that has been entertaining audiences in Salmon Arm since 1977, staging a full season of plays, improv comedy, and youth productions in its 149-seat venue in downtown Salmon Arm. It also co-hosts the annual Theatre on the Edge festival with the Salmon Arm Arts Centre, a multi-venue performing arts event featuring new works and outdoor performances. Touring cyclists stopping in Salmon Arm will find a lively local cultural institution within easy reach of the town centre.

detail.address: 41 Hudson Street NW, Salmon Arm, BC V1E 4R4

visitor.name: Silverbrook U-catch Trout Farm
visitor.desc: Silverbrook Farm is a U-catch trout fishing destination in Abbotsford that has operated for over 50 years, set on a working farm in the Fraser Valley. Beyond fishing, visitors can enjoy a petting zoo, kids' camps, BBQ packages, and signature 'Fishin' in the Dark' live music events. It won a 2025 Travel & Hospitality Award for Family Friendly Experience of the Year in BC and an Abbotsford Outstanding Agritourism award.

visitor.name: West Fraser Centre
visitor.desc: The West Fraser Centre is a municipal ice rink operated by the City of Quesnel in the Cariboo region of British Columbia. Situated along a key northern BC corridor, it serves as a community recreation facility that touring cyclists passing through Quesnel may encounter.

visitor.name: TNRL: Merritt Library
visitor.desc: The Merritt Library is part of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system and occupies a purpose-built 2001 building on the site of the town's historic railyard, with architecture inspired by the old CP Rail station. A standout feature is the working model railway that circles near the ceiling — staff will run it on request. The library offers free Wi-Fi and public computers, and is fully wheelchair accessible, making it a useful indoor stop for touring cyclists passing through the Nicola Valley.

detail.address: 1691 Garcia Street, Box 1510, Merritt, BC V1K 1B8

visitor.name: Pitt Meadows Museum General Store
visitor.desc: The Pitt Meadows Museum occupies two heritage sites facing each other on Harris Road beside the CP Rail tracks: the 1908 General Store (the oldest known structure in Pitt Meadows, with parts dating to 1886) and the Hoffmann and Son Machine Shop, which displays over 60 restored stationary gasoline engines and a working forge. The General Store houses permanent and temporary exhibits on early settlement history alongside a community archives and reference library. Admission is by donation.

detail.address: 12294 Harris Rd, Pitt Meadows BC V3Y 2E9

visitor.name: Mackenzie & District Museum
visitor.desc: The Mackenzie & District Museum preserves the human and natural history of the Parsnip Valley region in Northern BC, spanning from Summit Lake to Sifton Pass. Its standout exhibits include 35 original paintings by Marge McDougall documenting the Tse'khene First Nation, and the massive LeTourneau Tree Crusher — a diesel-electric machine once used to clear boreal forest during the region's development. The museum is part of Northern Routes, a network of cultural attractions in Northern BC.

detail.address: Unit #1 – 320 Mackenzie Blvd, Mackenzie, British Columbia V0J 2C0

visitor.name: Wild Cortes
visitor.desc: Wild Cortes is the permanent off-site Natural History Education Centre of the Cortes Island Museum & Archives, housed at Linnaea Education Centre on Cortes Island. It presents rotating exhibitions on local ecology, wildlife, and conservation—past shows have covered humpback whale recovery, old-growth forest trust, cougars and wolves, and the cascade effects of climate change—alongside a unique taxidermy collection curated by Laurel Bohart and a hands-on EcoLab with microscopes. The centre is a collaborative project of the Cortes Wild! partnership, bringing together local societies, biologists, geologists, and educators.

detail.address: 1255 Seaford Rd #2, Mansons Landing BC V0P 1K0

visitor.name: Elk Lakes Park
visitor.desc: Elk Lakes Park is a wilderness provincial park in the western ranges of the southern Rocky Mountains, featuring outstanding sub-alpine landscapes, remnant glaciers, and rugged peaks in the Kootenay region. The park offers a range of hiking experiences on maintained trails suitable for families with backcountry experience, as well as more remote routes for experienced climbers and off-trail travellers. A cabin bookable through the Alpine Club of Canada provides an overnight base, making it a compelling destination for touring cyclists looking to explore high-alpine terrain.

visitor.name: Peak Axe Throwing
visitor.desc: Peak Axe Throwing is Revelstoke's top-rated attraction on TripAdvisor, offering supervised indoor axe throwing sessions for individuals, birthday parties, and groups with no prior experience required. In addition to their indoor location on Victoria Street West, they partner with Revelstoke Mountain Resort for outdoor throwing in summer and operate a mobile trailer for off-site events. For touring cyclists seeking a memorable evening activity after a long day on the road, this is a well-established local highlight.

visitor.name: Fraser Lake Public Library
visitor.desc: Fraser Lake Public Library is a small public library serving the village of Fraser Lake, incorporated in 1970, situated along Highway 16 in BC's remote Central Interior. It offers computer and internet services, community programming, and acts as a community hub that also hosts a local community calendar. For touring cyclists on the long Highway 16 corridor, it represents one of the few public amenity stops between larger centres.

detail.address: 228 Endako Avenue, Box 520, Fraser Lake BC V0J 1S0

visitor.name: U'mista Cultural Centre
visitor.desc: The U'mista Cultural Centre in Alert Bay is a nationally significant First Nations museum dedicated to preserving the cultural heritage of the Kwakwaka'wakw people, including the celebrated Potlatch Collection of ceremonial regalia. Visitor reviews describe it as one of the finest small museums in existence, with well-organized exhibits and powerful historical context. Cyclists reaching Alert Bay by ferry will find guided tours, artist demonstrations, and a gift shop selling authentic Indigenous art.

detail.address: 1 Front Street, Alert Bay, BC V0N 1A0

visitor.name: Fleetwood Gardens
visitor.desc: A beautifully designed municipal display garden within Fleetwood Park in Surrey's Fleetwood neighbourhood. Features include a large pergola draped in wisteria and clematis, a classically designed knot garden with three varieties of boxwood, and an award-winning perennial border with over 100 varieties. A European-style bosque of 50 red maples adds dramatic structure as the trees mature.

visitor.name: sports center 2 (sc 2)
visitor.desc: This facility appears to be a secondary ice surface ('SC 2') within the Comox Valley Sports Centre complex, operated by the Comox Valley Regional District near Courtenay, BC. OSM tags indicate it supports both recreational ice skating and ice hockey and is open year-round. As a public recreation facility in the heart of the Comox Valley, it could serve as a rainy-day indoor stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

visitor.name: Snootli Creek Hatchery
visitor.desc: Snootli Creek Hatchery is a Fisheries and Oceans Canada facility operating under the federal Salmonid Enhancement Program, located in the Cariboo, Chilcotin and Central Interior region of British Columbia. Community hatcheries of this type typically support salmon and steelhead restoration and may offer informal educational visits, making them a potentially interesting cultural and ecological stop along remote cycling routes in the Bella Coola corridor.

visitor.name: Damaxyaa Heritage Site/Conservancy
visitor.desc: A heritage site and conservancy on Haida Gwaii covering 822 hectares near the community of Sandspit on North Moresby Island. The site protects old-growth cedar and hemlock forests with Haida cultural values, productive marine foreshore habitat, and overwintering grounds for Brant geese. The popular Louise Dover Trail is a 4 km moderate loop along a salmon river through ancient forest.

visitor.name: Tlall Heritage Site/Conservancy
visitor.desc: Tlall Conservancy is a protected area on the east side of Graham Island, Haida Gwaii, encompassing the Tlell River watershed and a 350-hectare fen and marsh area known as the Tlell Pontoons. It features the Anvil Trail, a 5 km loop through old-growth Sitka spruce, western redcedar, and hemlock forests along the Tlell River. The conservancy is part of an archipelago-wide system of protected areas and supports notable bird species including sandhill crane and trumpeter swan.

visitor.name: CRDL: Nazko Branch
visitor.desc: The Nazko Branch is a small community library branch of the Cariboo Regional District Library, serving the remote Nazko area of BC's Central Interior. It is one of 15 branches across the CRD library network and is staffed by community librarian Tammy Aiello. For touring cyclists passing through this sparsely populated region, it represents one of the few public institutions in the area.

visitor.name: Museum & Archives
visitor.desc: A community-led museum on Cortes Island exploring the social, cultural, and natural history of the island and surrounding region. It also houses Destination BC's Visitor Information booth with free maps, guides, and brochures—some available on a covered porch even outside staffed hours. Admission is free, and touring cyclists will find an e-bike charging station on site.

detail.address: 957 Beasley Rd, Mansons Landing, BC V0P 1K0

notes.E-bike charging: An e-bike charging station is available by donation, mentioned on the tourist information page

visitor.name: Castle Giant
visitor.desc: Castle Giant is a massive western redcedar (Thuja plicata) with a 16-foot (5-meter) diameter trunk, located in the Lower Castle Grove of the Central Walbran Valley on Vancouver Island. The surrounding Castle Grove is considered one of the highest-density concentrations of monumental ancient redcedars in the world, and has been documented by the Ancient Forest Alliance as one of Canada's most significant unprotected old-growth stands. Reaching this remote natural monument requires travel deep into the Walbran Valley watershed.

visitor.name: Campbell River Women's Resource Centre
visitor.desc: The Campbell River Women's Resource Centre is a nonprofit organization operated by the Campbell River and North Island Transition Society (CRNITS), providing shelter, drop-in services, crisis and support counselling, and poverty reduction programs to women and children on Northern Vancouver Island for over 30 years. Founded in 1985, the centre is one of the community's longest-running social services organizations. A touring cyclist passing through Campbell River may find the drop-in centre a welcoming community resource.

visitor.name: Sparwood Public Library
visitor.desc: Sparwood Public Library is a community hub in the Elk Valley, serving Sparwood and the surrounding Kootenay region with free library cards, print and digital collections, and a variety of programming for all ages. The library offers computer and internet access along with digital resources including e-books, audiobooks, and online learning platforms such as LinkedIn Learning. For cyclists riding the Crowsnest Pass corridor, it provides a sheltered indoor stop with connectivity in an otherwise remote stretch of southeastern BC.

visitor.name: Columbia National Wildlife Area
visitor.desc: The Columbia National Wildlife Area is a federally protected nature reserve in the Kootenay region of British Columbia, managed by Environment and Climate Change Canada. It serves as critical habitat for migrating waterfowl and a range of rare, threatened, and endangered wildlife, fish, and plant species. Touring cyclists riding through the Columbia Valley will find this a notable natural landmark along their route.

visitor.name: Revelstoke Visual Arts Centre
visitor.desc: The Revelstoke Visual Arts Centre is a non-profit public art gallery and community centre housed in Revelstoke's former police station, lending it a distinctive historical character complete with original jail cells visitors are invited to explore. The gallery presents rotating solo and group shows across one main open space and three adjoining side galleries, while the broader facility includes a community woodshop, pottery studio, xeriscape gardens, and outdoor picnic seating. It is one of the first buildings visible when arriving in Revelstoke off Highway 1, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists riding into town.

visitor.name: Miyazaki House
visitor.desc: The Miyazaki Heritage House is a beautifully preserved Second Empire-style home in Lillooet with a distinctive mansard roof and ornate dormer windows, a rare architectural style for rural British Columbia. The house serves as a history museum with historic photos, antiques, and a gift shop, telling the stories of the prominent families who lived there, including Doctor Masajiro Miyazaki. It also hosts community art exhibits, music concerts, and cultural events on its grounds throughout the warmer months.

visitor.name: Strathcona Gardens Recreation Complex
visitor.desc: Strathcona Gardens Recreation Complex is a regional public facility in Campbell River operated by the Strathcona Regional District, housing an aquatic centre and ice arena under one roof. It offers pools, arenas, fitness and rehabilitation programs, and outdoor recreation programs serving residents across the region. Touring cyclists passing through Campbell River may find it a useful stop for recovery and basic services, though specific cycling amenities are not advertised on the site.

detail.address: 225 South Dogwood Street, Campbell River, BC V9W 8C8

visitor.name: Forestry Building
visitor.desc: The Forestry Building is a seasonal heritage museum structure associated with the Powell River Museum, situated in Powell River, BC on the Sunshine Coast. It appears to be a dedicated exhibit space exploring the region's forestry history, a defining industry of the Powell River area. Visiting cyclists exploring the Sunshine Coast region would find it a culturally grounding stop amid one of BC's most scenic touring routes.

visitor.name: Wabco 50T Haulpak Mining Truck
visitor.desc: A 1962 Wabco 50-ton Haulpak mining truck preserved as an outdoor static display in Ashcroft, British Columbia, representing the region's industrial and copper-mining heritage. At roughly 50 tonnes capacity, these massive haul trucks were workhorses of mid-twentieth-century open-pit mining operations. It functions as a roadside heritage landmark and photo opportunity rather than a staffed attraction.

detail.address: Heritage Place Park, Railway Avenue, Ashcroft, BC

visitor.name: TNRL: Logan Lake Library
visitor.desc: A public library in the small community of Logan Lake, part of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system. The current 3,708-square-foot building opened in 2013, replacing the original library that had served the community from the local mall since 1975. For touring cyclists passing through this relatively remote Highland Valley community, the library offers free Wi-Fi, public computers, and a comfortable place to rest.

detail.address: 130 Chartrand Avenue, Logan Lake, BC V0K 1W0

visitor.name: World Largest Goat Walk
visitor.desc: The World Largest Goat Walk is a striking wooden roadside attraction at Log Barn 1912 in Armstrong, BC, standing 30 feet high and 60 feet wide and visible for miles along Highway 97A. Built by a Mennonite farming family on a property anchored by an original 1912 barn, the site is home to seventeen goats and four horses. The adjacent farm store sells artisan smoked meats, old-fashioned baked goods, cheeses, jams, and candy — making it a natural rest stop for cyclists riding the Okanagan corridor on Hwy 97A.

notes.Café or food on site: Log Barn 1912 farm store at the same property sells smoked beef jerky, baked goods, meat and cheese products, candy, and giftware on site

visitor.name: 'Namgis Bighouse
visitor.desc: The 'Namgis Bighouse is a traditional Indigenous gathering structure belonging to the 'Namgis First Nation, whose territory encompasses the entire Nimpkish and Kokish River Watersheds on northern Vancouver Island. Located in Alert Bay (Ya̱lis) on Cormorant Island, it stands as a tangible expression of a culture that has occupied these lands and waters since time immemorial. Cyclists travelling to Cormorant Island via ferry from Port McNeill may encounter it as a prominent cultural landmark in a community renowned for its Kwakwaka'wakw heritage.

visitor.name: Robson Valley Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Robson Valley Visitor Centre is the official tourism information office for McBride and the surrounding Robson Valley region in central British Columbia. It operates under the Visit McBride tourism organization and is the primary point of contact for travellers seeking local knowledge about the area. For touring cyclists passing through this remote mountain corridor, a visitor centre in a small community like McBride is often a key resupply of information, maps, and regional guidance.

visitor.name: Fernie Alpine Resort
visitor.desc: Fernie Alpine Resort is a four-season mountain resort in the Kootenays offering one of the largest lift-accessed mountain bike trail networks in Western Canada, with 38 trails spanning beginner-friendly machine-made flows to advanced technical singletrack with berms and wall rides. In summer, cyclists can rent bikes at the on-site rental centre, book lessons or guided hikes, and dine at several on-hill restaurants. The resort also offers lodging, a day spa, and kids' camps, making it a full-service destination for a multi-day cycling trip.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'Fernie Alpine Resort offers several on-hill options for dining and nightlife' under 'LEGENDARY DINING'

visitor.name: Kettle River Museum
visitor.desc: The Kettle River Museum sits at Mile 0 of the legendary Kettle Valley Railway in the Village of Midway, making it a natural landmark stop for cyclists riding the KVR Trail. Set on 2.5 acres, the site features the original 1901 Station House, a restored Canadian Pacific Railway caboose, an artifacts yard, and a shaded picnic area adjacent to Highway 3. The museum actively welcomes trail travellers, offering registered parking by donation for TransCanada Trail users and a small gift shop stocked with regional history books, memorabilia, and information for cyclists.

visitor.name: TNRL: Clinton Library
visitor.desc: The Clinton Library is a small public branch of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system, having served the community since its Tingley Street building opened in December 1975. At 1,977 square feet, it offers free Wi-Fi, public computers, printing, and a bookable meeting room in a welcoming, wheelchair-accessible space. Touring cyclists passing through the BC Interior will find it a practical stop for connectivity and a quiet place to regroup.

detail.address: 1506 Tingley Street, Box 550, Clinton, BC V0K 1K0

visitor.name: Langley Demonstration Garden
visitor.desc: The Langley Demonstration Garden is a public garden attraction in the Langley area of the Fraser Valley, tagged in OpenStreetMap as a leisure garden. Demonstration gardens of this type typically showcase horticultural techniques and plantings of regional interest, making them a pleasant stop for cyclists passing through the area. No further details about facilities or features could be confirmed from available sources.

visitor.name: The Enchanted Forest
visitor.desc: The Enchanted Forest is a long-running family attraction set in an old-growth forest 32 km west of Revelstoke on the Trans-Canada Highway, featuring over 350 handcrafted fairy tale figurines, BC's tallest treehouse, and a castle with dungeons. A 2 km self-guided wildland interpretive nature walk winds through the lush BC forest, and in autumn visitors can watch Kokanee, Sockeye, Spring, and Cohoe salmon spawning from an on-site bridge. The sister attraction SkyTrek Adventure Park is located immediately adjacent on Highway 1.

detail.address: 7060 Trans Canada Hwy, Revelstoke, BC V0E 2S0

visitor.name: Zeballos Library
visitor.desc: Zeballos Library is a branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library system serving this small, remote community at the end of a logging road on northern Vancouver Island. For touring cyclists making the long journey to Zeballos, it stands as one of the few public facilities in a community otherwise defined by its wilderness setting and limited services. As a public library, it offers a quiet indoor space in an area where such amenities are rare.

visitor.name: Black Creek Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Black Creek Community Centre serves as the cultural and recreational hub of the Black Creek area on Vancouver Island, grown through many expansions from its community roots. It offers a fitness room, facility rentals for events, program registration, and outdoor amenities to the surrounding region. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find a publicly accessible facility with multiple services and a community atmosphere.

visitor.name: Entrance-BC Ferries-Prince Rupert Terminal
visitor.desc: The BC Ferries Prince Rupert Terminal is a critical gateway for touring cyclists, connecting Northern BC to Haida Gwaii via the Prince Rupert–Skidegate route and serving as an interchange point with the Alaska Marine Highway System. For cyclists travelling the northwest coast, this terminal marks the start or end of a significant leg of remote touring through some of BC's most dramatic landscapes. The website confirms bicycles are accommodated as a distinct passenger category.

detail.address: 2000 Park Avenue, Prince Rupert, BC V8J 3S1

visitor.name: Logan Lake Recreation Center
visitor.desc: The Logan Lake Recreation Centre is the community hub of this small Thompson-Nicola town, housing an ice arena, curling rink, and an 800-square-foot fitness room operated by the LIFT Society with free weights, universal machines, and cardio equipment. It sits in the centre of town on Chartrand Avenue, a short walk from the downtown commercial area. The surrounding area features a trail network that includes purpose-built mountain bike trails, making Logan Lake a potential stop for cycling-focused visitors.

visitor.name: Natural Bridge
visitor.desc: Natural Bridge is a striking geological formation in Yoho National Park where the emerald-green Kicking Horse River has eroded through solid limestone to create a natural stone arch. Located just off the Yoho Valley Road, it is a well-known and easily accessible roadside stop within one of Canada's most scenic mountain national parks. Touring cyclists riding through the Canadian Rockies often include it as a short detour from the Trans-Canada corridor.

visitor.name: Lung Duck Tong Restaurant
visitor.desc: The Lung Duck Tong Restaurant is a heritage building within Barkerville Historic Town & Park, a National Historic Site in BC's Cariboo region that preserves more than 125 Gold Rush-era structures along a historic streetscape. Barkerville brings the 1860s gold rush to life with costumed interpreters, working museums, and period shops set amid forests and mountains. For a touring cyclist, it represents a rare immersive step back into BC's frontier history in a remote but well-developed heritage destination.

detail.address: Front St, Barkerville, BC V0L 1N0, Canada

visitor.name: ORL: Sicamous Branch
visitor.desc: The Sicamous Branch of the Okanagan Regional Library serves this small community at the junction of the Trans-Canada and Hwy 97A in the Shuswap region. Part of a 30-branch network that ranks as the 16th largest library in Canada, this branch offers public computers, internet access, scanning to email, and a rotating art wall showcasing local artists. For touring cyclists passing through Sicamous, it provides a welcoming public space with connectivity and free on-site parking.

visitor.name: Hell's Gate Airtram
visitor.desc: The Fisheries Exhibit is one of several attractions within the Hell's Gate Airtram experience, situated 157 metres down in the Fraser Canyon gorge near Boston Bar. The exhibit features an award-winning documentary 'Run Sockeye Run,' which won a bronze at the New York City film festival, along with displays tracing the full life cycle of salmon and the history of the International Hell's Gate Salmon Fishways. Admission to the Fisheries display is bundled with the airtram fare, which also grants access to a suspension bridge, gold panning, a café, and a fudge factory.

detail.address: 43111 Trans-Canada Highway, Boston Bar BC V0K 1C0

notes.Café or food on site: Simon's Cafe is located in the gorge at the bottom of the airtram; Fudge Factory also on site offering up to 100 flavours made on site

visitor.name: Pender Harbour Community Hall
visitor.desc: The Pender Harbour Community Hall is operated by the Pender Harbour Community Club Society, a volunteer-driven organization that serves as the social anchor for the Pender Harbour area on BC's Sunshine Coast. The hall hosts a range of community events including an annual May Day celebration, Winter Fest, and seasonal markets, and is available for public rental. The club is currently running a 'Raise the Roof' campaign to fund significant hall upgrades.

visitor.name: Denman Island Museum & Archives
visitor.desc: The Denman Island Museum & Archives preserves the layered history of Denman Island in the Salish Sea, with collections and archives spanning First Nations heritage, early settler families, logging, farming, and decades of island social movements. Located right in the village as an annex of the Denman Activity Centre, it holds extensive archival fonds from local organizations, individuals, and community publications. A touring cyclist exploring Denman Island would find it a compact window into the island's distinctive cultural identity.

detail.address: 1111 Northwest Road, Denman Island, BC V0R 1T0

visitor.name: ORL: Osoyoos Branch
visitor.desc: The Osoyoos Branch of the Okanagan Regional Library is a free public library serving one of BC's sunniest and most visited cycling communities in the South Okanagan. Located at the Sonora Community Centre, it provides public computers, free Wi-Fi, and rotating art displays from local quilters and the Artists on Main collective. Part of a 30-branch regional system established in 1936, the branch is an accessible indoor stop for anyone passing through Osoyoos.

visitor.name: Kwinitsa Station Museum
visitor.desc: Kwinitsa Station Museum is a historic Canadian National Railway station building that was relocated to Prince Rupert's waterfront, preserved as a snapshot of the region's railway-building era. It is administered by the Museum of Northern British Columbia, which stewards the natural and cultural heritage of the Northwest Coast. For touring cyclists arriving by ferry or passing through Prince Rupert, it offers a compact, walkable piece of local industrial history near the waterfront.

visitor.name: Cloverdale Arena
visitor.desc: Cloverdale Arena is a City of Surrey municipal recreation facility in the Cloverdale neighbourhood offering both ice and dry-floor programming to the public. It is a community-oriented arena operated by Surrey Parks & Recreation, primarily serving local residents with drop-in and registered sport programs. Touring cyclists passing through the area might find it a recognizable civic landmark, though it is not cycling-focused.

visitor.name: Union Bay Community Hall
visitor.desc: A member-owned community hall in Union Bay that has served as the village's social hub for over seventy years. The hall and its grounds host annual events including craft fairs, a fall supper, Bay Day family celebration, and a well-known Halloween fireworks show. The outside field area includes picnic tables, a playground, and a concession booth.

detail.address: 5401 South Island Highway, Union Bay, BC

visitor.name: VIRL: Port Renfrew Branch
visitor.desc: The Port Renfrew Branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library is a small public library housed within the Port Renfrew Community Centre, sitting at the trailhead gateway for both the West Coast Trail and the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail — two of BC's most iconic cycling-adjacent adventures. The branch traces its roots to a book deposit station established in 1964 and remains open year-round, making it a reliable community anchor in this otherwise remote coastal village. For touring cyclists passing through, it offers a quiet indoor refuge with computer access available on request.

visitor.name: Walhachin Museum
visitor.desc: The Walhachin Museum is housed in the 1911 Soldiers Memorial Hall in the tiny South Thompson River community of Walhachin, west of Kamloops, and tells the story of an ambitious early-1900s British settlement that attempted to grow orchards on arid benchlands. The community holds a remarkable WWI legacy: 97 of 107 able-bodied men enlisted, leading to the settlement's eventual decline. Free admission makes it a low-barrier cultural stop for cyclists riding the Thompson River corridor.

visitor.name: Gitwangak Battle Hill National Historic Site
visitor.desc: Gitwangak Battle Hill National Historic Site (formerly Kitwanga Fort) sits atop a high grassy knoll overlooking the scenic Kitwanga River valley, marking the site of a fortified Gitxsan village actively defended in the mid-1700s to 1800s. The adjacent Gitwangak Village is home to the oldest surviving collection of totem poles in British Columbia. The site is managed in partnership with the Simgiget'm Gitwangak Society (hereditary leaders) and is open year-round for self-guided exploration.

detail.address: Gitwangak, Kitwanga, Kitimat-Stikine District BC V0J 2A0

visitor.name: Golden Gate/Xáat Yádi Aani Conservancy
visitor.desc: A remote conservancy at the junction of Tagish Lake and Graham Inlet, about 35 kilometres northwest of Atlin in northern BC. Established in partnership with the Taku River Tlingit First Nation, its Tlingit name (X̱áat Yádi Aani) refers to a village near where humpback whitefish congregated. The conservancy protects a culturally significant landscape of islands, bays, and shoreline with no developed visitor facilities.

visitor.name: Enderby & District Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Enderby & District Visitor Centre, operated by the Enderby & District Chamber of Commerce, is housed in a log building at Belvidere Park along the Shuswap River. It serves as the official tourism hub for Enderby and surrounding communities including Grindrod, Ashton Creek, Kingfisher, and Mabel Lake. The centre promotes a region where the Shuswap meets the Okanagan, with cycling listed among the area's highlighted outdoor activities.

visitor.name: CRDL: Anahim Lake Branch
visitor.desc: The Anahim Lake Branch is a small community library operated by the Cariboo Regional District Library, serving one of the most remote communities along Highway 20 in BC's Chilcotin region. For touring cyclists riding the long Chilcotin corridor, it represents one of very few public institutions in the area where human contact and potential services might be found. The branch is staffed by a community librarian and falls under the broader CLN network offering digital and physical lending services.

detail.address: Unit #1, 2409 Whispering Pines Trailer Court, Hwy 20, Anahim Lake, BC V0L 1C0

visitor.name: Kicking Horse Mountain Resort
visitor.desc: Kicking Horse Mountain Resort is a major four-season alpine resort near Golden, BC with a dedicated summer Bike Park featuring downhill singletrack loaded with berms, jumps, wooden features, and rock slabs, all accessible by gondola. The village includes a bike pump track, mountain bike rentals and repairs, and guided lessons, making it a destination for riders of all abilities. A gondola sightseeing experience, grizzly bear refuge, and alpine restaurant round out the appeal for touring cyclists spending time in the Columbia Valley.

notes.Café or food on site: Eagle's Eye Restaurant ('Dine In The Alpine'); additional restaurants listed under The Village section of site navigation

visitor.name: Revelstoke Visitor Center
visitor.desc: The Revelstoke Visitor Center is a tourism information office serving this celebrated mountain town, where the Selkirk and Monashee ranges converge around the Columbia River. Revelstoke is renowned among cyclists for challenging road routes and world-class mountain biking, making a visitor centre stop a natural fit for trip planning. A REVY Store is housed within the Visitor Centre, per the Tourism Revelstoke website.

visitor.name: Nicola Valley Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Nicola Valley Aquatic Centre is a City of Merritt–operated public recreation facility featuring a 6-lane 25-metre lap pool, a lazy river and vortex leisure pool, two whirlpools, a sauna, and a fully equipped fitness room. It is fully accessible and situated next to the Nicola Valley Memorial Arena, a short walk from the Merritt Civic Centre. For touring cyclists, it offers a rare opportunity in the Thompson–Nicola region to recover with a proper swim session or soak after a long day in the saddle.

visitor.name: Wynndel Community Centre
visitor.desc: A historic community landmark dating back to 1930, located in the heart of the Kootenays less than 10 minutes from Creston. The grounds feature a park with a playground, green space, a creek-side path, and a disc golf course open to visitors of all ages. The main building is currently unoccupied, though a small arts centre at the back remains available for meetings and small gatherings.

visitor.name: Lillooet REC Centre and Library
visitor.desc: The Lillooet R.E.C. Centre (Recreation, Education, and Cultural Centre) is a regional civic facility operated by the Squamish-Lillooet Regional District on Main Street in Lillooet. It combines recreation, library, and cultural services under one roof, making it a community hub in this small Interior BC town that sits at the junction of several long-distance cycling routes. For touring cyclists passing through Lillooet, it represents a logical stop in a community with limited services.

visitor.name: Rossland Mining Museum & Discovery Center
visitor.desc: The Rossland Museum & Discovery Centre chronicles the history of Rossland from its gold-mining origins through its evolution into a celebrated ski town in the Kootenays. It also houses the Rossland Visitor Centre, making it a natural first stop for touring cyclists arriving in the area. A major renewal project — The Mine Experience — is underway, with over $5M raised toward an expanded underground mine exhibit.

visitor.name: The Arts Station
visitor.desc: The Arts Station is Fernie's community arts centre and cultural hub, operated by the Fernie and District Arts Council on the unceded territory of Yaq̓it ʔa·knuqⱡi'it. It hosts a public gallery, pottery studio, paint-by-number studio, live performances, and a regular schedule of workshops and social events. For a touring cyclist passing through the Elk Valley, it offers a genuine taste of Fernie's creative community.

visitor.name: Comox Archives & Museum
visitor.desc: A free community museum exploring the history of Comox from its earliest days to the present, including a K'omox First Nation component and a dedicated 102nd Battalion WWI exhibit. The museum also houses local archives and a small shop selling books, cards, and gifts. A compact cultural stop right on Comox Avenue for cyclists passing through town.

visitor.name: Ferguson Lake Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: Ferguson Lake Nature Reserve is a municipal nature reserve managed by the City of Prince George, situated in BC's Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior region. It offers natural outdoor space within reach of Prince George and appears on the city's parks and trails network. Touring cyclists passing through Prince George may find it a scenic detour, though on-site facilities are unconfirmed.

detail.address: 9915 Ferguson Lake Road, Prince George, BC

visitor.name: Valley Alley Bowling Ctr
visitor.desc: Valley Alley Bowling Ctr is a community bowling alley situated directly on the Highway 93/95 corridor in Windermere in BC's Columbia Valley. It sits on one of the main cycling routes connecting Radium Hot Springs and Invermere, making it a convenient stop for a recreational break. The venue is a genuine local gathering spot with confirmed check-ins on Facebook.

visitor.name: Mt Begbie Trailhead
visitor.desc: Mt Begbie Trailhead is the starting point for a steep, difficult hike to a backcountry campground and alpine viewpoint near Revelstoke, BC. Managed by BC Parks, it offers a rugged wilderness experience with dramatic mountain scenery. Touring cyclists exploring the Revelstoke area may find this a worthwhile side trip on foot.

visitor.name: PGPL: Nechako Branch
visitor.desc: The Nechako Branch is one of two public library locations operated by the Prince George Public Library, serving the Hart neighbourhood of Prince George in BC's Central Interior. Situated entirely on one level with full wheelchair accessibility, it offers free public internet and computer access alongside a broad collection of physical and digital resources. For touring cyclists on the Hart Highway corridor, it provides a free, welcoming stop for connectivity and a rest from the road.

detail.address: 6547 Hart Highway, Prince George, BC V2K 3A4

visitor.name: Fernie Museum
visitor.desc: The Fernie Museum, operated by the Fernie & District Historical Society, occupies two floors in Historic Downtown Fernie and traces 140 years of Elk Valley history through its permanent 'This Is Our Fernie' exhibit and rotating second-floor gallery. An archives and collections centre supports research visits, and summer walking tours cover colourful local history including the 1908 Great Fire and Prohibition-era rum-running. Admission is by donation, making it an accessible and rewarding cultural stop for cyclists touring the Kootenays.

visitor.name: Cathedral Grove
visitor.desc: Cathedral Grove, within MacMillan Park, is one of Vancouver Island's most iconic natural sites — a stand of ancient Douglas fir trees up to 800 years old and over 9 metres in circumference, preserved as an old-growth provincial park. The park straddles Highway 4 between Parksville and Port Alberni, with trail networks on both sides of the road threading through towering coastal forest. A severe 1997 windstorm reshaped parts of the park, and ongoing natural regeneration makes each visit distinctive.

visitor.name: Courtenay & District Memorial Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: The Courtenay & District Memorial Outdoor Pool is a municipally operated outdoor swimming facility in Courtenay on Vancouver Island, serving the broader Comox Valley community. As a public outdoor pool run by the City of Courtenay, it offers a seasonal aquatic destination for residents and visitors alike. Touring cyclists passing through the Comox Valley region may find it a worthwhile stop for a swim and a break from the road.

visitor.name: West Coast Trail Information & Orientation Centre
visitor.desc: This Parks Canada information and orientation centre serves hikers preparing for the 75-kilometre West Coast Trail, one of British Columbia's most famous multi-day backcountry routes on the west coast of Vancouver Island. The trail passes through the traditional territories of the Huu-ay-aht, Ditidaht, and Pacheedaht First Nations. The centre is located near the Gordon River trailhead at the southern end of the trail.

visitor.name: Hanna-Tintina Conservancy
visitor.desc: Hanna-Tintina Conservancy is a remote wilderness area in northwest BC near Meziadin Junction, encompassing the watersheds of Hanna and Tintina Creeks with steep timbered hillsides, alpine slopes, and extensive wetlands. It protects critical salmon spawning habitat—approximately 75 percent of Nass River sockeye spawn here—along with provincially significant grizzly bear habitat and moose winter range. Touring cyclists on Highway 37 or 37A pass through this area, but should note there are no developed visitor facilities.

visitor.name: Totems
visitor.desc: The Totems site near Kispiox is an outdoor cultural heritage attraction showcasing traditional Gitksan totem poles in one of six ancient Gitksan communities estimated to be roughly 3,000 years old. Located in the Skeena River valley, Kispiox sits within Anspayaxw territory and is a recognized stop on touring routes through northwest British Columbia. The totem poles represent a living cultural tradition of the Gitksan people and offer a meaningful historical waypoint for cyclists exploring the region.

detail.address: 1336 Kispiox Valley Rd, Kispiox BC V0J 1Y4, Canada

visitor.name: Visitor Center
