visitor.desc: The New Hazelton Visitors Centre occupies a charming log building at the junction of Highways 16 and 62, serving as the gateway to the Hazeltons and Upper Skeena region for travellers on the Yellowhead corridor. Staffed by knowledgeable locals, it provides maps, brochures, and expert advice on trails, attractions, and cultural experiences. A 2024 exhibit upstairs documents the history of the Gitxsan, Wet'suwet'en, and settler peoples of the region.

visitor.name: Beecher Linton Conservation Area
visitor.desc: Linton Conservation Area is a protected nature reserve on Vancouver Island in the Comox Valley region, operated by the Province of British Columbia. It sits within a landscape of ecologically significant land and wildlife habitat that land trusts and provincial stewards actively work to conserve. Touring cyclists passing through the Comox Valley may find it a scenic natural detour, though visitor facilities and formal public access details are not documented in available sources.

visitor.name: Music Makers Hall
visitor.desc: Music Makers is a not-for-profit community theatre society incorporated in 1974 that has spent over 50 years bringing live theatre and concerts to Fort St. James and the surrounding Cariboo region. The venue hosts an eclectic mix of productions — comedies, dramas, Shakespeare, musicals, and live music shows — and aims to make Fort St. James a travel destination for performing arts. For touring cyclists passing through central BC, it offers a rare chance to catch a high-calibre live performance in a remote northern community.

detail.address: 255 2nd Avenue West, Fort St. James, BC V0J 1P0

visitor.name: Tallheo Hot Springs - No Name Creek Conservancy
visitor.desc: Hot Springs-No Name Creek Conservancy is a remote BC Parks wilderness conservancy on the west side of South Bentinck Arm, encompassing two coastal watersheds with steep valleys. The area is best known for Talheo Hot Springs and is home to grizzly bears and mountain goats in largely undisturbed habitat. It holds high cultural importance to local First Nations and was established as part of the Central Coast land use planning process.

visitor.name: Creston & District Community Complex
visitor.desc: The Johnny Bucyk Memorial Arena is a seasonal indoor ice facility in the Creston area of the Kootenays, operated by the Regional District of Central Kootenay as part of the Creston & District Community Complex. Named in honour of hockey legend Johnny Bucyk, it serves the local community for ice skating and ice hockey. As a seasonal facility, it is likely closed during peak summer cycling season.

visitor.name: The Old School House Gallery & Arts Centre
visitor.desc: The Old School House Arts Centre is a historic former school building in Qualicum Beach that has been transformed into the mid-Vancouver Island hub for visual and performing arts. It hosts rotating juried exhibitions, art classes ranging from printmaking to watercolour, resident artist studios, and intimate live music concerts. A registered non-profit welcoming visitors of all backgrounds, it is a genuine cultural landmark on a coastal cycling route through central Vancouver Island.

detail.address: 122 Fern Road West, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 1T2

visitor.name: Mackay Whale Watching
visitor.desc: Mackay Whale Watching is a family-owned and operated whale watching company based in Port McNeill, Northern Vancouver Island, with over 40 years of experience and pioneers in killer whale watching in BC. Their vessel, the Naiad Explorer, takes guests on tours through the waters of the Kwakwaka'wakw nation to encounter orcas, humpbacks, dolphins, and other marine wildlife. For touring cyclists exploring the northern tip of Vancouver Island, this is a standout excursion offering a rare perspective on the rugged BC coast from the water.

detail.address: 1514 Broughton Boulevard, Port McNeill, British Columbia

visitor.name: CRDL: Horsefly Branch
visitor.desc: The CRDL Horsefly Branch is a community library in the remote Horsefly area, part of the 15-branch Cariboo Regional District Library network. It provides residents and visitors with access to physical collections, digital resources, and community programming. For touring cyclists in this sparsely serviced Interior BC region, it represents a rare public stop with connectivity and community information.

visitor.name: Grizzly Helicopters Ltd
visitor.desc: Grizzly Helicopters is a family-owned operator that has been flying out of Campbell River and Port McNeill since 2008, offering glacier tours, heli-fishing fly-ins, and commercial charters across north-central Vancouver Island and the BC coast. Touring cyclists looking to add an aerial dimension to their trip can join a scenic glacier landing tour or a catch-and-release heli-fishing adventure in otherwise inaccessible wilderness rivers. The fleet of Astar 350 helicopters carries up to five passengers with panoramic visibility from all seats.

visitor.name: Kitimat Library
visitor.desc: The Kitimat Public Library is the public library serving the District of Kitimat in BC's North Coast region, operated by the Kitimat Public Library Association and a member of the Northwest Library Federation. It offers computer and internet access, 3D printing, photocopying and scanning, digital collections, and a range of community programs. For a touring cyclist passing through a relatively remote part of northern BC, it represents a potential rest stop with Wi-Fi and access to regional information resources.

visitor.name: Fernie Historic Oil Derrick
visitor.desc: The Fernie Historic Oil Derrick is the last standing wooden oil derrick in British Columbia, situated at the eastern gateway to Fernie on Highway 3. Its metal components were salvaged from early 20th-century oil exploration rigs in the Flathead Valley and reassembled on the current site in 1984. Touring cyclists arriving from the Crowsnest Pass will pass directly by this landmark, which offers a tangible glimpse into BC's brief and largely unsuccessful oil-prospecting era.

detail.address: 102 Commerce Rd, Fernie, BC V0B 1T2, Canada

visitor.name: Centennial Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: Centennial Outdoor Pool is a municipally operated seasonal outdoor swimming pool in Campbell River on Vancouver Island. It offers a refreshing stop for touring cyclists passing through during the summer months, managed by the City of Campbell River's Parks, Recreation and Culture department.

visitor.name: Chartwell Garden
visitor.desc: The Xeriscape Garden is a public demonstration garden operated by the Regional District of Nanaimo, showcasing water-wise, drought-tolerant landscaping techniques suited to Vancouver Island conditions. Located on Yambury Road, it is a free community resource intended to educate residents about outdoor water conservation. Touring cyclists in the Parksville/Qualicum area may find it a pleasant stop, though on-site cyclist services are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Worlds Largest Fly Fishing Pole-Houston
visitor.desc: Canada's Largest Fishing Rod (as the District of Houston bills it) is an outdoor roadside landmark in Houston, BC, conceived in the 1980s when BC tourism promoters encouraged communities to erect signature structures to put themselves on the map. The rod was championed by local fly fisherman Warner Jarvis and became Houston's defining roadside attraction. Cyclists riding the Yellowhead Highway (Hwy 16) corridor pass through Houston and this quirky giant landmark serves as a notable community waypoint.

visitor.name: Indian Grove Riding Stables
visitor.desc: Indian Grove Riding Stables is an equestrian facility in the Okanagan region of British Columbia offering horseback riding experiences. Tagged as both a sports centre and tourism attraction in OSM, it appears to serve recreational visitors looking for guided or self-guided trail rides in the area. Touring cyclists passing through the South Okanagan may find it a worthwhile stop for a riding excursion.

visitor.name: Pitt Meadows Family Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Pitt Meadows Family Recreation Centre is a municipal leisure facility operated by the City of Pitt Meadows, offering programs including a fitness centre, gymnasium sports, public skating, and an outdoor swimming and spray park. It functions as the primary community recreation hub for the city and draws a broad range of residents across age groups. Touring cyclists moving through the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley area may find it a convenient midpoint stop, though specific cyclist amenities are not confirmed.

visitor.name: Henry Place Archives
visitor.desc: A community heritage museum and archives in the heart of Pemberton Valley, on the traditional territory of the Lil'wat and St'át'imc Nations. Open since 1982, it houses over 2,000 photographs, 700+ objects, 250+ videos, and online exhibits on logging and railway history. Admission is by donation, making it an easy stop for touring cyclists passing through Pemberton.

visitor.name: Powell River Public Library
visitor.desc: The Powell River Public Library is a full-service public library on the Sunshine Coast offering books, digital resources, and community programs including 3D printing and a 'Library of Things' lending collection. It serves as a cultural and community hub on Tla'amin Nation traditional territory. Touring cyclists passing through Powell River can use its free internet and computer services.

detail.address: 100-6975 Alberni Street, Powell River BC V8A 2B8

visitor.name: CRDL: Lac la Hache Branch
visitor.desc: The Lac la Hache Branch is a small community library operated by the Cariboo Regional District Library system, serving the rural Lac la Hache area along Highway 97 in the Cariboo. It offers access to the full CRDL network including interlibrary loans, digital resources, and e-books through a single community librarian. For cyclists riding the Interior plateau, it is a rare public amenity in an otherwise remote stretch between 100 Mile House and Williams Lake.

detail.address: 4787 Clark St, Lac La Hache, BC V0K 1T0

visitor.name: Derby Reach Regional Park
visitor.desc: Derby Reach Regional Park is a Metro Vancouver regional park along the Fraser River in Langley, featuring trails through forest, wetland, and heritage farmland. The park sits on the Fraser River floodplain and offers a mix of riverside and upland walking and cycling paths. It is a pleasant stop for touring cyclists riding through the Lower Mainland's eastern communities.

visitor.name: Bonanza Marsh Conservations Area (NCC)
visitor.desc: Bonanza Marsh Conservation Area is a Nature Conservancy of Canada-managed nature reserve in the Kootenays region of British Columbia, protecting wetland and marsh habitat. Operated by one of Canada's leading private land conservation organizations, the site represents NCC's ongoing work to safeguard biodiversity in the Columbia Basin. Touring cyclists passing through the Kootenays may find it a scenic natural stop along their route.

visitor.name: Rhododendron Garden
visitor.desc: The Rhododendron Garden is a public natural garden and woodland in the Whonnock area of Maple Ridge, BC. It draws visitors for its seasonal blooms and forested character, making it a quiet detour for cyclists passing through the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley region. Amenity details are currently unverifiable due to an unavailable website.

visitor.name: Kunxalas Heritage Site/Conservancy
visitor.desc: A 3,360-hectare heritage site and conservancy on the northeast coast of North Moresby Island, Haida Gwaii, protecting five historic Haida villages and seasonal camps on the Cumshewa Peninsula. The site features a regionally significant coastal hiking trail easily accessed by road at Gray Bay, connecting beaches, Sheldens Lagoon, and Secret Cove. A frontcountry campground and day-use area at Gray Bay serves as the main visitor hub.

visitor.name: Xatsull Heritage Village
visitor.desc: Xatśūll Heritage Village is a National Award-Winning Indigenous cultural attraction operated by the Xatśūll First Nation on the banks of the Fraser River near Williams Lake. The site offers guided daily tours, Elder storytelling, and hands-on cultural workshops in an unspoiled natural landscape where the Fraser River has shaped community life for generations. Cyclists touring the Cariboo region can experience authentic teepee accommodation and rare participatory access to traditional spiritual and cultural practices.

detail.address: 3405 Mountain House Road, Williams Lake, B.C. V2G 5L5

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Website states 'modern washrooms and showers are on-site (hidden from view)'
notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'will provide meals if you book in advance'

visitor.name: Visitor Center
visitor.desc: The Vanderhoof Tourism and Cultural Centre sits at the geographic centre of British Columbia along the historic Nechako River, combining visitor information services with a museum and cultural exhibits celebrating the area's Indigenous and settler heritage. It serves as the primary gateway for exploring the Vanderhoof region, which lies on the Yellowhead Highway (Highway 16) and offers access to a migratory bird sanctuary, heritage trails, and backcountry routes toward Fort St. James and Kenney Dam. For a touring cyclist passing through central BC, this is a well-resourced stop for local knowledge and trip planning.

visitor.name: Powell River Curling Club
visitor.desc: The Powell River Curling Club is a non-profit community society (S-04186) that has been promoting the sport of curling in Powell River since 1955. It offers a wide range of leagues for all ages and skill levels — including youth programs, a Learn to Curl option, and Special Olympics participation — alongside competitive bonspiels and social events. Operated entirely by volunteers and member fees, it reflects the tight-knit community character that cyclists travelling to Powell River often seek out.

detail.address: 5750 Crown Ave, Powell River, BC V8A 4B3

visitor.name: ORL: North Shuswap Branch
visitor.desc: The North Shuswap Branch is a small community library operated by the Okanagan Regional Library, one of 30 branches in a network serving over 399,000 people across 59,600 square kilometres of interior BC. Situated along Squilax-Anglemont Road in a rural stretch of the North Shuswap, it offers public computers and Wi-Fi, making it a potential connectivity stop for cyclists passing through this quieter corridor east of Shuswap Lake.

visitor.name: The Tennis Centre
visitor.desc: The Tennis Centre is a multi-location indoor and outdoor tennis facility founded by internationally recognized coach Larry Jurovich, with three Lower Mainland locations in Surrey, Langley, and Coquitlam. The Surrey location is home to the only outdoor red clay courts in Western Canada, while the Langley facility includes a fitness centre and childcare services alongside six indoor courts. The centre offers a full range of programming for juniors and adults at all skill levels.

visitor.name: Tom Forsyth Memorial Arena
visitor.desc: The Tom Forsyth Memorial Arena is the ice rink component of Burns Lake's Lakeside Multiplex, a municipal recreation complex in the Cariboo-Chilcotin region. The rink seats 640 spectators and includes six change rooms, hosting Minor Hockey, adult leagues, and public skating for all ages and abilities. The arena shares the Lakeside Multiplex building with a fitness centre, climbing wall, squash and racquetball courts, and a curling rink.

visitor.name: Parksville Museum
visitor.desc: The Parksville Museum is a heritage park operated by the Parksville & District Historical Society, featuring a collection of historic buildings some dating to 1885 and hands-on exhibits exploring the pioneer history of Parksville, Errington, Coombs, and Nanoose Bay. Highlights include the only traditional Japanese blacksmith forge in Western Canada, an interactive E&N Railway exhibit, and archives containing over 6,000 historical photographs. The open-air Marion Craig Courtyard is available year-round and makes a pleasant stop for cyclists to rest and have a picnic.

detail.address: 1245 Island Hwy E, Parksville, BC V9P 2E5

visitor.name: Dora Drinkwater Community Library
visitor.desc: The Union Bay branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library, opened in 1949, is the smallest VIRL branch at just 300 square feet and occupies the historic Union Bay Post Office building constructed in 1913. It holds a collection of more than 4,400 items and offers free public WiFi, making it a modest digital rest stop in a small coastal community on Vancouver Island. The heritage building setting gives this tiny branch an outsized sense of place for cyclists passing through the area.

visitor.name: Sproat Lake Petroglyphs
visitor.desc: The Sproat Lake Petroglyphs, known by the Nuu-chah-nulth name K'ak'awin, are an archaeological site within Sproat Lake Provincial Park on central Vancouver Island and are considered one of the finest panels of prehistoric rock carvings in British Columbia. Cyclists can reach the carvings via a 0.5 km trail from the main parking lot, ending at a small pier at the east end of the park where the ancient carvings are viewable at the lake's edge. The surrounding provincial park on the north shore of Sproat Lake, reached via Highway 4 about 13 km northwest of Port Alberni, also offers swimming, canoeing, and fishing.

visitor.name: Elkford Community Garden
visitor.desc: The Elkford Community Garden is a public growing space in Elkford, a small mountain municipality in the East Kootenay region of British Columbia, known locally as the Wilderness Capital of BC. Situated in a remote community surrounded by the Canadian Rockies, the garden represents a community gathering point in an otherwise rugged, wilderness-oriented town. Touring cyclists passing through Elkford on routes through the Elk Valley may find it a quiet stop amid the town's otherwise outdoor-adventure-focused offerings.

visitor.name: Burnt Bridge Creek Conservancy
visitor.desc: Burnt Bridge Creek Conservancy is a wilderness conservancy on the western boundary of Tweedsmuir Park in the Central Coast region, established through BC's Central Coast land use planning process. It encompasses a segment of the historic Nuxalk-Carrier Grease Trail, a First Nations trade route linking the BC coast to the interior, and is the site where Alexander Mackenzie first reached the Bella Coola Valley in 1793. The area is remote and undeveloped, offering a backcountry experience with deep cultural and historical significance.

visitor.name: Tom Rooney Playhouse
visitor.desc: The Tom Rooney Playhouse — affectionately called 'the Rooney' — is an intimate 80-seat black box theatre in the heart of downtown Prince Rupert, home to the Harbour Theatre Society, a not-for-profit community theatre organization founded in 1981. The society stages classic and contemporary productions, improv events including the annual Udderfest festival, and youth programming, drawing on locally developed talent. For a touring cyclist passing through Prince Rupert on the North Coast, it offers a genuine slice of community cultural life.

detail.address: 954 3rd Avenue West, Prince Rupert, BC V8J1M8

visitor.name: Port McNeill Swimming Pool
visitor.desc: The Town of Port McNeill Swimming Pool is a publicly accessible outdoor municipal pool operated by the Town of Port McNeill on northern Vancouver Island. It offers community swim lessons and recreational swimming in one of the few public pool facilities along the remote northern stretch of the Island Highway corridor. For touring cyclists, it serves as a welcome community hub and refreshment stop in an otherwise sparsely serviced region.

detail.address: 2181 McNeill Road, Port McNeill, BC V0N 2R0

visitor.name: Almer Carlson Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: The Almer Carlson Outdoor Pool is a seasonal public swimming facility operated by the Fraser Valley Regional District as part of the Hope Recreation Complex. It is one of two recreation facilities run by the FVRD in the Hope area, serving residents and visitors with family-oriented aquatic programming during the summer months. For touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Canyon corridor, it represents a potential warm-weather refreshment stop.

visitor.name: Mile 0 Alaska Highway
visitor.desc: Mile 0 of the Alaska Highway is one of BC's most iconic landmarks, marking the official southern terminus of the historic 2,237-km Alaska Highway in downtown Dawson Creek. The famous milepost is a pilgrimage site for road travellers — cyclists and motorcyclists especially — completing or beginning the legendary northern route. The adjacent Visitor Information Centre (1000 102 Ave) offers tourism support and a gift shop for those celebrating the milestone.

detail.address: 800 Hwy 2, Dawson Creek, BC V1G 3V8, Canada

visitor.name: Walnut Grove Community Centre
visitor.desc: A large Township of Langley municipal recreation centre in Walnut Grove featuring a 50-metre pool with waterslide, diving boards, a 5-metre dive tower, leisure pool, sauna, steam room, and whirlpools. The facility also houses a fitness centre, gymnasium, library branch, and a fresh food café. Accessibility features include a portable aquatic lift, water wheelchairs, and ramp access into the therapy and leisure pools.

detail.address: 8889 Walnut Grove Drive, Langley, BC V1M 2N7

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Change rooms with handheld shower heads available as part of pool facility; drop-in schedules referenced on website
notes.Café or food on site: Second Wave - fresh food café listed as leased space on-site (604-888-7995)

visitor.name: Strathcona Gardens Recreation Complex
visitor.desc: Full Pool is an indoor covered swimming pool within the Strathcona Gardens Recreation Complex, a regional district facility in Campbell River on northern Vancouver Island. The larger complex offers pools, arenas, aquatic fitness, and registered swim programs, making it a destination for recreation-seeking cyclists passing through the area. It is operated by the Strathcona Regional District and serves both local residents and visitors.

detail.address: 225 South Dogwood Street, Campbell River, BC V9W 8C8

visitor.name: Sechelt Public Library
visitor.desc: Sechelt Public Library is a community public library located on Cowrie Street in downtown Sechelt on the Sunshine Coast. It offers a broad range of in-library services including WiFi, computer and internet access, and print/copy/fax/scan facilities. The library also maintains strong ties to local Indigenous and community organizations, making it a useful orientation stop for visiting cyclists exploring the region.

visitor.name: Nunns Creek
visitor.desc: Nunns Creek is a municipal nature reserve in Campbell River on northern Vancouver Island, managed by the City of Campbell River. The reserve protects a creek corridor within an urban setting, offering a natural respite along what is otherwise a mid-sized coastal city. Touring cyclists riding the Vancouver Island route through Campbell River may find it a useful green-space stop, though specific trail and facility details were not available from the website.

visitor.name: Studio Connection Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Studio Connexion Art Gallery is a community art gallery in Nakusp, BC, showcasing local artists through rotating exhibitions including summer and winter group shows. Located in the Kootenays, it is now in its 18th Summer Exhibition Series, suggesting an established presence in this small Arrow Lakes town. A touring cyclist passing through Nakusp could stop in to experience regional visual arts in a gallery-sized venue.

visitor.name: Cache Creek Visitor Information Centre
visitor.desc: The Cache Creek Visitor Information Centre is the official tourism office for the Village of Cache Creek, a small community at the junction of Highways 1 and 97 in the Thompson region of BC. Situated at a major crossroads for trans-provincial travel, it serves as a natural stop for cyclists riding either the Trans-Canada or the Cariboo Highway corridor. As a municipal information office it would typically provide local area maps, attraction guides, and trip-planning assistance.

visitor.name: Alert Bay Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Alert Bay Visitor Centre is a Destination BC visitor information office located on Cormorant Island, accessible by ferry. Alert Bay is known as the 'Home of the Killer Whale' and features rich First Nations cultural heritage, including the 'Namgis Big House and an ecological park with boardwalk trails. A touring cyclist arriving by ferry would find this a useful first stop for local information and orientation.

visitor.name: Willow Creek Greenway
visitor.desc: Willow Creek Greenway is a natural trail corridor near Campbell River managed by the Greenways Land Trust, a registered charity focused on stream and land stewardship in the region. It is listed among the organization's most popular local trails and lies within the ecologically rich watersheds that drain eastward to the sea on northern Vancouver Island. Touring cyclists exploring the Campbell River area would find it a worthwhile natural detour through preserved greenway habitat.

visitor.name: Clayton Falls Conservancy
visitor.desc: Clayton Falls Conservancy is a protected wilderness area in BC's remote Cariboo region, managed by BC Parks under the provincial conservancy designation. The only activity explicitly listed on the BC Parks page is hunting during open season, suggesting it is a largely undeveloped wild area. Touring cyclists passing through the Central Interior may find it of scenic or exploratory interest, but no developed visitor facilities are described.

visitor.name: Ksan Historical Village and Museum
visitor.desc: 'Ksan Historical Village, Campground and Museum sits at the confluence of the Bulkley and Skeena Rivers near Hazelton, BC, on land the Gitxsan peoples have inhabited for over 8,000 years. It is a premier showcase of Gitxsan Aboriginal culture and is featured on the regional 'Hands of History Tour.' The site also includes a campground, making it a potential overnight stop for touring cyclists passing through the North Coast corridor on Highway 16.

visitor.name: Industrial Heritage Centre
visitor.desc: The Industrial Heritage Centre is operated by the Western Vancouver Island Industrial Heritage Society, a volunteer-driven organization founded in 1983 that restores and displays vintage logging trucks, steam engines, railway equipment, and other industrial machinery from mid-Vancouver Island. The society also runs the Alberni Pacific Railway, where visitors can board a train hauled by a fully restored 1929 Baldwin steam locomotive at the 1912 CPR Station and ride to the McLean Mill National Historic Site. Knowledgeable volunteer-led guided tours are available on request at either the Heritage Centre or the railway roundhouse.

visitor.name: Riondel Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Riondel Community Centre is managed by the Riondel Commission of Management, a local governance body serving this small village on the east shore of Kootenay Lake in the Kootenays. The Commission oversees community programming, water services, and emergency preparedness for the area, and the centre functions as the main civic gathering space for Riondel. For touring cyclists exploring the East Shore route along Kootenay Lake, Riondel represents a remote but scenic stop in an area with few services.

visitor.name: Fort St. James Public Library
visitor.desc: A small-town public library in the historic fur-trade community of Fort St. James on Stuart Lake, whose Carrier-language name Nawhulnukw bayoh means 'house for shared stories.' The library offers free computer and internet access, community event listings, and a wealth of local-history and First Nations cultural resources. The surrounding area features the Fort St. James National Historic Site, provincial parks, and Stuart Lake Golf Club.

detail.address: 425 Manson Street, Fort St. James, BC V0J 1P0

visitor.name: Houston & District Chamber of Commerce
visitor.desc: The Houston & District Chamber of Commerce operates the Visitor Information Centre on Highway 16 in northwest BC, located right next to Canada's Largest Fly Rod. It serves as a useful stop for cyclists travelling between Prince George and Prince Rupert, offering local area information and a downloadable digital visitor guide covering accommodations, paddling, hiking, and fishing in the region.

visitor.name: Walhachin Soldiers Memorial Hall
visitor.desc: A historic community hall built by pioneers in 1911 in the tiny settlement of Walhachin along the South Thompson River west of Kamloops. It houses a museum established in 2011 focused on Walhachin's fascinating history as a failed English orchard colony from the early 1900s, where 97 of 107 able-bodied men enlisted in WWI and few returned. The hall also features a cenotaph constructed in 2018 and hosts the annual Walhaschindig music festival.

detail.address: 4359 Central Avenue, Box 35, Walhachin, BC V0K 2P0

visitor.name: Old Church Theatre
visitor.desc: The Old Church Theatre is an intimate 180-seat performing arts venue in Courtenay, BC, housed in a converted church building. It presents a broad range of programming including live music, theatre, dance, comedy, film, and lectures. The small, community-oriented venue offers a distinctive atmosphere that sets it apart from larger regional arts centres.

visitor.name: At The Water's Edge Adventures
visitor.desc: At the Water's Edge Adventures is a sea kayaking tour operator based at Telegraph Cove, BC, offering guided day trips and multi-day expeditions into Johnstone Strait, Blackfish Sound, and the Broughton Archipelago — some of Canada's richest marine wildlife habitat. Tours are fully nomadic and small-group, featuring orca, humpback, and minke whale encounters alongside Steller sea lions, dolphins, and bald eagles. In 2023 the company acquired Butterfly Tours, extending its reach to Haida Gwaii kayaking expeditions.

visitor.name: Beaver Valley Public Library
visitor.desc: The Beaver Valley Public Library is a community public library serving the Beaver Valley area of the Kootenays, located on traditional Indigenous territory. Beyond books, it offers a notable Library of Things collection that includes items like hiking backpacks, food dehydrators, and an egg incubator — a practical resource for adventurous visitors. Touring cyclists passing through Fruitvale will find free computer and internet access as well as a range of digital and in-person programming.

visitor.name: Nicola Valley Art Centre
visitor.desc: The Nicola Valley Arts Centre is a community arts hub in Merritt operated by the Nicola Valley Community Arts Council, offering a rotating art gallery, an artisan gift shop, and classes and events for children and adults. Located on Voght Street beside the Kekuli Cafe, it serves as a creative gathering place for the Thompson-Nicola region. Touring cyclists will find a lively cultural stop with regular exhibitions and a locally curated gift shop.

visitor.name: Pipe Mountain Coaster
visitor.desc: The Pipe Mountain Coaster is billed as Revelstoke's #1 summer attraction, featuring two alpine coaster tracks that wind through ski runs on Revelstoke Mountain. It sits within the larger Revelstoke Mountain Resort complex, which also operates an extensive mountain biking program including rentals, lessons, e-bike guided tours, and bike repairs. A touring cyclist in Revelstoke looking for a non-pedaling thrill between rides would find this a natural stop.

visitor.name: Fort Forum Arena
visitor.desc: Fort Forum is a community centre in Fort St. James, a small historic town in BC's Central Interior on the shores of Stuart Lake. As part of the District of Fort St. James Parks & Recreation portfolio, it likely serves as a hub for local recreation and community events. Touring cyclists passing through Fort St. James may find it a useful orientation point, though specific cyclist-facing services are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Lil'wat7ul Culture Centre
visitor.desc: The Lil'wat7ul Culture Centre is the cultural hub of the Líl̓wat Nation, the third-largest First Nation in British Columbia, situated in the dramatic mountain and river landscape around Mount Currie near Pemberton. It sits within Líl̓wat territory whose people have inhabited this region for more than 5,400 years, making it a significant stop for cyclists exploring the Sea-to-Sky and Pemberton corridors. The centre serves as a living space for Lil̓wat7úl language, culture, and heritage.

detail.address: 82 IR 10 Road, Mount Currie, British Columbia, V0N 2K0

visitor.name: MV Tarahne
visitor.desc: The MV Tarahne is a 36-metre historic sternwheeler built in 1917 for passenger and freight service on Atlin Lake, now permanently beached in Atlin and restored by the volunteer-run Atlin Historical Society as a heritage landmark. Launched at a time when Atlin was drawing tourists 'from all over the world,' the vessel embodies over a century of the region's gold-rush, tourism, and Taku River Tlingit history. Cyclists making the remote journey to this far-northern BC community can visit the ship, arrange walking tours with local historians, and even book the vessel for private events.

visitor.name: Campbell River Art Gallery & Gift Shop
visitor.desc: The Campbell River Art Gallery (CRAG) is an established public art gallery in downtown Campbell River showcasing rotating exhibitions by local, regional, and national artists alongside a permanent collection. The gallery also operates satellite campus spaces, educational programs, and an Art Hive, making it a significant cultural hub on Vancouver Island's cycling routes. A gift shop offering artist-consigned work is on site, providing a meaningful stop for cyclists interested in local art.

visitor.name: Victory Hall
visitor.desc: Victory Hall is a civic community centre located in Oliver, BC, in the heart of the Okanagan Valley. As a community gathering space, it likely hosts local events, performances, and public functions. Touring cyclists passing through Oliver may find it a useful landmark or event venue in this small wine-country town.

visitor.name: Miracle Beach Nature House
visitor.desc: Miracle Beach Nature House is an interpretive nature center within Miracle Beach Provincial Park on Vancouver Island, situated on the coast between Courtenay and Campbell River. The park features a broad sandy beach with rich tide pools at low tide, about 2 km of walking trails through second-growth and old-growth forest, and access to the Black Creek estuary. Touring cyclists on the Oceanside Route (Hwy 19a) can reach the park via a short 2 km side road from the highway.

visitor.name: CRDL: Wells Branch
visitor.desc: The Wells Branch is a small community library serving the historic gold-rush town of Wells in BC's Cariboo region, operating as part of the 15-branch Cariboo Regional District Library network. Staffed by a community librarian, it offers borrowing services, digital resources including e-books and databases, and serves as a local community gathering point. For touring cyclists exploring this remote stretch of central BC, it provides a quiet stop with internet and community information resources.

visitor.name: George Preston Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: A Township of Langley municipal recreation centre located in the Brookswood neighbourhood, featuring an ice arena, the Langley Curling Centre, and an outdoor sports box. The facility also houses The Lodge Steakhouse and The Horse & Ryder Pub, making it a potential rest stop with on-site dining options. Room rentals and a large parking lot are available.

notes.Café or food on site: The Lodge Steakhouse and The Horse & Ryder Pub are listed as on-site amenities

visitor.name: Willoughby Community Park
visitor.desc: Willoughby Community Park is a large Township of Langley public park in the Willoughby neighbourhood offering an extensive mix of outdoor recreation including bocce courts, pickleball, basketball, tennis, rugby, soccer, lacrosse, and a spray park. The park also features an amphitheatre, picnic shelters, change rooms, and ample parking, making it a well-equipped community hub in the Lower Mainland. Touring cyclists can use it as a convenient rest stop with access to drinking water and restroom facilities.

notes.Water without admission: Public park with no admission fee; Drinking Water explicitly listed as a park amenity

visitor.name: Terrace Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Terrace & District Aquatic Centre is a municipal swimming facility operated by the City of Terrace in northern BC's North Coast region. Programs listed on the city website include public swimming, swimming lessons, lifeguard training, and a combined swim-and-gym offering. For touring cyclists riding through this remote corridor, the facility represents a potential rest stop with access to water and a pool.

visitor.name: Canlan Ice Sports Langley Twin Rinks
visitor.desc: Canlan Ice Sports Langley Twin Rinks is a twin-sheet ice facility operated by Canlan Sports, one of Canada's largest private ice sports operators. The venue hosts recreational skating, hockey drop-ins, leagues, camps, tournaments, and birthday parties. A touring cyclist in Langley could use it as a recreational stop or a rainy-day indoor activity.

visitor.name: Bella Coola Museum
visitor.desc: The Bella Coola Valley Museum, established in 1963 and housed in a heritage building dating to approximately 1892, documents the human history of the Bella Coola Valley from European contact to 1955. Run by a non-profit society, it offers guided tours, historic videos, a gift shop, and a Historic Walking Tour brochure that touring cyclists could use to explore the town. A companion archives branch provides year-round research access, making it a substantive cultural stop on the remote Highway 20 corridor.

detail.address: 269 Alexander MacKenzie Highway, Bella Coola, BC V0T 1C0

visitor.name: Thunderbird Show Park
visitor.desc: Thunderbird Show Park is one of North America's premier equestrian event facilities, hosting ten weeks of internationally recognized hunter and jumper tournaments each year just east of Vancouver in Langley. The park welcomes everyone from first-time junior amateur competitors to world-class FEI Grand Prix athletes, and spectators can watch show jumping from the grandstands alongside restaurants, bars, and boutique shops on site. The venue is large enough to accommodate RVs and hosts a dedicated spectator entrance on 248th Street separate from the competitor and show office entrance.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states spectator events feature 'an array of restaurants, bars and boutique shops.'

visitor.name: Discover Powell River
visitor.desc: The Powell River Visitor Centre is the official tourism information hub for Powell River and the qathet Regional District, staffed to provide maps, directions, local adventure bookings, and accommodation assistance. It serves as the recommended first stop for visitors arriving in a region celebrated for cycling, kayaking, the Sunshine Coast Trail, and diverse outdoor recreation on BC's Northern Sunshine Coast. The centre is operated by qathet Tourism Society and actively promotes cycling as one of the top ten things to do in the area.

visitor.name: Barkerville
visitor.desc: Barkerville Historic Town & Park is a National Historic Site born from Billy Barker's legendary 1862 gold strike on Williams Creek, preserving more than 125 heritage buildings along a reconstructed Gold Rush-era streetscape. Costumed interpreters, working historical displays, and museums bring 19th-century Cariboo life to vivid detail. The site also offers on-site campgrounds and accommodations, making it a compelling multi-day destination for touring cyclists passing through the central interior.

visitor.name: Worlds Largest Fly Rod
visitor.desc: Houston's signature roadside landmark, this oversized fishing rod was conceived in the 1980s when BC tourism promoters encouraged small towns to build eye-catching monuments to put themselves on the map. Local fly fisherman Warner Jarvis championed the idea at a Chamber of Commerce workshop, and the result is a free, publicly accessible outdoor sculpture that has become a regional curiosity. Touring cyclists passing through Central BC on Highway 16 will find it a memorable photo opportunity in the community of Houston.

detail.address: 3367 - 12th Street, PO Box 370, Houston, BC V0J 1Z0

visitor.name: South Cariboo Theatre
visitor.desc: South Cariboo Theatre is a theatre venue located in the 100 Mile House area of British Columbia's Cariboo region. It represents a cultural anchor for this rural community, offering performing arts in an area more commonly associated with outdoor recreation. Touring cyclists passing through the South Cariboo may find it a worthwhile stop for evening entertainment.

detail.address: 585 Birch Avenue, 100 Mile House, BC V0K 2E0

visitor.name: Sechelt Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Sechelt Aquatic Centre is a public indoor swimming facility operated by the Sunshine Coast Regional District in Sechelt, BC. It sits in the heart of town and serves the local community as a year-round covered aquatic venue. For touring cyclists passing through the Sunshine Coast, it represents a potential stop for a swim or a post-ride rinse, though specific amenities have not been confirmed.

visitor.name: Chetwynd & District Recreation Complex
visitor.desc: The Chetwynd & District Recreation Complex is a municipal multi-use facility operated by the District of Chetwynd in Northern BC. It encompasses an arena, curling rink, gymnasium, indoor playground and climbing wall, and a running/walking track, making it one of the primary year-round recreation hubs in this remote community along Highway 97. For a touring cyclist passing through Chetwynd, it represents a central public facility in an otherwise sparsely serviced stretch of northern BC.

visitor.name: Courtenay & District Museum & Palaeontology Centre
visitor.desc: An award-winning natural and cultural history museum that has been celebrating the Comox Valley's heritage for over 60 years, and serves as home to BC's Provincial Fossil. The museum is renowned for its paleontology collection, including the Great Elasmosaur Find, and offers fossil tours, rotating gallery exhibits, and deep dives into local First Nations and settler history. It is a well-established cultural anchor in downtown Courtenay, making it a natural destination stop for touring cyclists passing through the Comox Valley.

visitor.name: Tourism Sun Peaks
visitor.desc: Tourism Sun Peaks is the visitor and member services office for Sun Peaks Resort, BC's second-largest four-season mountain resort. Located in the village, it serves as the central information hub for a resort spanning three mountains with an extensive bike park, hiking network, golf, and alpine skiing. Touring cyclists riding into the area can use it as a first stop for local trail conditions, event information, and resort orientation.

visitor.name: Stone Cottage Gallery
visitor.desc: Stone Cottage Gallery is a working artist's studio and gallery in Qualicum Beach showcasing wildlife sculptures and carvings by award-winning Canadian artist Del C. Mark, who brings over 50 years of outdoor experience to lifelike depictions of BC wildlife in soapstone, alabaster, and antler. Subjects range from black bears and orca whales to herons and jumping salmon, carved from materials including Brazilian Soapstone and African Wonderstone. Located just a short distance from uptown Qualicum Beach, it offers cycling tourists a distinctive glimpse into fine craft art rooted in the natural world of Vancouver Island.

detail.address: 306 Fern Road East, Qualicum Beach, BC

visitor.name: Garibaldi Park
visitor.desc: Garibaldi Park is a vast provincial park in the heart of the Coast Mountains, centred on the 2,678 m peak of Mount Garibaldi and spanning diverse terrain from glacial lakes to alpine meadows. It offers over 90 km of established hiking trails across multiple backcountry zones including Garibaldi Lake, Black Tusk, Cheakamus Lake, and Diamond Head. A day-use pass is required for entry, and the access roads are shared with cyclists and wildlife, making it a landmark stop along the Sea to Sky corridor.

detail.address: British Columbia 99, Brackendale, BC V0N 1H0, Canada

visitor.name: Hamber Park
visitor.desc: Hamber Park is a vast remote wilderness in BC's Kootenay region, forming part of one of the world's largest contiguous protected area blocks and designated a UNESCO Canadian Rocky Mountains World Heritage Site. Access to the interior requires a 22 km journey from the Sunwapta Falls trailhead in Jasper National Park, with the primary destination being Fortress Lake and its surrounding alpine terrain. Facilities are minimal by design: a rustic campground with a toilet exists at the east end of the lake, while the rest of the park is undeveloped backcountry.

visitor.name: Tamitik Arena
visitor.desc: Tamitik Arena is a municipal ice rink in Kitimat, BC, operated by the District of Kitimat and used primarily for ice hockey. It is listed alongside the Kitimat Ice Rink and Riverlodge Recreation and Fitness Centre as part of the city's recreation portfolio, suggesting it serves both organized sport and public recreation. For touring cyclists passing through the northwest BC community of Kitimat, it represents one of the town's main indoor recreation facilities.

visitor.name: Dawson Creek & District Memorial Arena
visitor.desc: The Dawson Creek & District Memorial Arena is a municipal ice arena serving the community at the southern end of the Alaska Highway. As a city-operated sports centre, it hosts ice sports, community events, and recreational skating. Touring cyclists passing through Dawson Creek — the Mile Zero of the Alaska Highway — may find it a useful landmark and rest stop.

visitor.name: Fort Bowling Lanes
visitor.desc: Fort Bowling Lanes is a long-established 5-pin bowling alley in Fort St. John, BC, serving the community for over 40 years with 12 lanes including themed 'Cosmic' bowling. The venue features a snack bar offering pizza, Mac & Cheese Bites, and Mini Donuts alongside a fully licensed lounge, and can accommodate up to 120 guests — making it one of Fort St. John's primary indoor social hubs. Touring cyclists passing through this Northern BC gateway city could stop for a meal, a drink, and a few frames in a wheelchair-accessible, community-oriented setting.

detail.address: 10116 104 Street, Fort St John, BC V1J 4C3

notes.Café or food on site: Snack bar offering Mac & Cheese Bites, Mini Donuts, and pizza (pre-order only); fully licensed lounge also on site

visitor.name: Garibaldi Park
visitor.desc: Garibaldi Park is a spectacular BC provincial wilderness park in the Coast Mountains, 64 km north of Vancouver, anchored by the 2,678 m peak of Mount Garibaldi and featuring over 90 km of established hiking trails through alpine meadows, glaciers, and glacier-fed lakes. The park spans multiple backcountry zones — including Black Tusk, Garibaldi Lake, Wedgemount Lake, and Cheakamus Lake — each accessible via separate trailhead access roads. Touring cyclists riding the Sea to Sky corridor will find it a premier natural landmark, though the backcountry is demanding and full self-sufficiency is required.

detail.address: British Columbia 99, Brackendale, BC V0N 1H0, Canada

visitor.name: Tutshi Sleddog Tours
visitor.desc: Tutshi Sleddog Tours appears to be a dog sledding attraction in far northern BC near Tutshi Lake, potentially connected to Muktuk Adventures — an established Yukon wilderness operator with over 30 years of sled dog heritage. Muktuk Adventures offers guided dog sledding, canoeing, and hiking from a solar-powered off-grid lodge along the Takhini River, with accommodation and home-cooked meals included in packages. The relationship between the OSM-named Tutshi operation and the Whitehorse-based Muktuk Adventures is not clarified on the website.

visitor.name: Takakkaw Falls
visitor.desc: Takakkaw Falls is one of Canada's tallest waterfalls at 373 metres, plunging from the Daly Glacier high above the Yoho Valley in Yoho National Park. The Yoho Valley Road leading to the falls is a celebrated cycling destination in the Canadian Rockies, featuring a series of tight switchbacks and dramatic mountain scenery. The falls sit within a national park that also protects the world-renowned Burgess Shale fossil beds and a network of alpine trails.

detail.address: Yoho National Park, Field, BC V0A 1G0, Canada

visitor.name: Fort Langley
visitor.desc: A Parks Canada national historic site on the banks of the Fraser River, Fort Langley recreates life at a Hudson's Bay Company fur trading post from the 1800s. Visitors can explore rough-hewn timber buildings inside a log palisade, meet costumed interpreters, and participate in hands-on workshops. The site also offers oTENTik overnight camping within the fort walls.

detail.address: 23433 Mavis Avenue, Fort Langley, BC V1M 2R5

visitor.name: Upper Skeena Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Upper Skeena Recreation Centre is a full-service community recreation facility in Hazelton, operated by Recreation Excellence on behalf of the Regional District of Kitimat-Stikine. Situated on Highway 62 in the remote northern BC Skeena corridor, it houses an NHL-size ice arena, full gymnasium, weight room, and cardio area. For touring cyclists passing through this isolated region, the centre offers showers, lockers, and a barrier-free drinking fountain.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Universal change room includes 'barrier free sink, toilet, shower and lockers'; drop-in admission is available per the FAQs page
notes.Luggage / bag storage: Lockers available in the universal change room ('barrier free sink, toilet, shower and lockers') and implied in gendered change rooms

visitor.name: Hamilton Hobby Farm
visitor.desc: Hamilton Hobby Farm is a 12-acre family-run petting farm tucked into the Coombs Country corridor on Vancouver Island, just across from Butterfly World and minutes from the famous Goats on the Roof Market. Visitors can brush goats, feed chickens, see ponies, and take hayrides across the back forty — making it a lively roadside stop along the Alberni Highway for families and curious cyclists alike. The farm also sells fresh eggs, seasonal produce, homemade jams, and farm-raised poultry directly on site.

detail.address: 2679 Alberni Highway, Coombs, BC, Canada, V9K 1X1

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'drinks and snacks' under Gifts & Seasonal Products, plus farm-fresh eggs, seasonal fruits and vegetables, and homemade jams available for purchase on site

visitor.name: Sudeten Park
visitor.desc: Sudeten Park is a nature reserve in the Peace River Country of Northern British Columbia, located near Dawson Creek — the Mile 0 city of the Alaska Highway. Captured in Canada's national NRCan-CanVec geographic dataset, it preserves a tract of the expansive northern landscape that defines this remote touring corridor. Cyclists riding the Alaska Highway or exploring the Dawson Creek area will find it a natural waypoint in one of BC's most storied long-distance routes.

visitor.name: Tutshi Lake/T'ooch' Áayi Conservancy
visitor.desc: Tutshi Lake/T'ooch' Áayi Conservancy protects the eastern half of Tutshi Lake, a culturally significant body of water whose Tlingit name means 'charcoal lake', referencing its distinctively dark water. Established through the Wóoshtin Wudidaa Atlin Taku Land Use Plan and a Taku River Tlingit First Nation Strategic Engagement Agreement, the conservancy sits roughly 65 kilometres northwest of Atlin in a remote corner of northwest BC. The lake supports high-value lake trout habitat and represents a rare example of co-governed protected land in the region.

visitor.name: Port Hardy Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: Port Hardy Visitor Centre is a year-round tourism information office on the waterfront of Hardy Bay, staffed by professional visitor services personnel who help travellers plan trips across the North Island region. Port Hardy sits at the northern end of Vancouver Island and is the departure point for the BC Ferries Northern Expedition route to Prince Rupert, making it a natural waypoint for touring cyclists heading up-island or connecting to the mainland. The centre offers local knowledge on transportation, accommodation, attractions, and day trips.

detail.address: 7250 Market Street, Port Hardy, BC V0N 2P0

visitor.name: FVRL: Yale Library
visitor.desc: Yale Library is a small public branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, situated in the historic village of Yale along the Fraser Canyon — a corridor popular with touring cyclists. Part of a 25-branch regional network, it offers free public computers and WiFi alongside a children's space and accessible facilities. For cyclists passing through this otherwise sparse stretch of Highway 1, it provides a rare opportunity for a rest, connectivity, and a 24-hour item return drop box.

visitor.name: Halverson House
visitor.desc: Halverson House is a historic building within Barkerville Historic Town & Park, a National Historic Site in the Cariboo region of British Columbia. Barkerville preserves over 125 heritage buildings from the Gold Rush era along Williams Creek, with costumed interpreters, working displays, and museums bringing 19th-century life to vivid detail. Touring cyclists on the Gold Rush Trail will find the site a compelling stopover, though it is remote and set deep in the forests and mountains of the Cariboo.

visitor.name: Tunnel of Flags
visitor.desc: The Tunnel of Flags is a historic one-lane road tunnel in Greenwood, BC, dating to 1913, that was rediscovered above ground after a new road was built in 1993. To combat graffiti, then-mayor Arno Hennig launched a community project that resulted in 210 hand-painted country flags covering the exterior walls by 2000. It is a quirky and photogenic roadside stop in Canada's smallest city, easily accessible to passing cyclists on the Crowsnest Highway corridor.

visitor.name: Nature House at Red Barn
visitor.desc: The Nature House at Red Barn is a seasonal nature interpretation centre operated by Metro Vancouver Parks within Campbell Valley Regional Park near Langley. It focuses on natural history and functions as a visitor centre for park guests. Campbell Valley is a popular multi-use regional park, making this a worthwhile stop for touring cyclists exploring the Lower Mainland trail network.

visitor.name: Royal Canadian Legion
visitor.desc: Golden Branch #122 of the Royal Canadian Legion is a veterans' community organisation serving the Golden area. As part of the BC/Yukon Command's 145-branch network, it supports veterans, ex-service personnel, and the broader community. Like many small-town Legion halls, it may serve as an informal community gathering point for visitors passing through Golden.

visitor.name: Centennial Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: A municipal outdoor swimming pool in Princeton, BC, operated by the Town of Princeton as part of its Parks & Recreation facilities. Located right on Highway 3, the pool is a convenient seasonal refreshment stop for cyclists passing through the Similkameen Valley.

visitor.name: Panorama Mountain Village
visitor.desc: Panorama Mountain Resort is a four-season alpine destination in BC's Kootenay Rockies, built around an intimate ski-in/ski-out village with 1,300 metres of vertical and nearly 3,000 acres of terrain. In summer the resort pivots to mountain biking, hiking, and guided adventures, with bike lessons and equipment rentals and repairs available on site. The self-contained village encompasses restaurants, pubs, cafés, hot pools, and accommodations, making it a notable stop for cyclists venturing deep into the Kootenays.

detail.address: 2000 Panorama Dr, Panorama, BC V0A 1T0, Canada

notes.Café or food on site: Website navigation lists 'Restaurants, Eateries & Bars' and describes dining options 'from rustic to elegant, down-to-earth to up-in-the-alpine.'

visitor.name: Nim Nim Interpretive Centre
visitor.desc: The Nim Nim Interpretive Centre is a cultural gallery on K'ómoks First Nation territory near Courtenay on Vancouver Island, situated within the traditional lands of the K'ómoks and Pentlatch peoples. The K'ómoks First Nation has a deeply layered cultural heritage encompassing distinct origin stories, languages, and histories from several formerly separate tribes. A touring cyclist passing through the Comox Valley would find this a meaningful stop for Indigenous cultural education and interpretation.

visitor.name: Campbell River Curling Club
visitor.desc: The Campbell River Curling Club has been a cornerstone of the community since opening in 1964, growing from a volunteer-built facility into a member-owned club with around 375 active curlers across leagues spanning juniors, seniors, and adaptive programs including Special Olympics and Blind and Vision Impaired curling. The facility features five sheets of ice maintained by a professional ice technician and an upstairs lounge with darts, pool, shuffleboard, and big-screen TVs, along with a professional kitchen serving meals and local beers on tap. A touring cyclist arriving in Campbell River during the curling season would find a genuine, long-established community hub with on-site food and drink.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'professional kitchen, where meals are prepared by paid kitchen staff' and lounge with 'great food with local beers on tap'; all servers and bartenders are club employees

visitor.name: Caledonia Nordic Ski Club
visitor.desc: The Caledonia Nordic Ski Club is a non-profit outdoor recreation facility founded in 1957, located about 15 minutes from downtown Prince George on the unceded lands of the Lheidli T'enneh. It offers kilometres of maintained trails for nordic skiing, snowshoeing, single-track mountain biking, hiking, and disc golf across beginner to advanced terrain. In summer it hosts youth mountain bike camps and sessions, making it a notable trail destination for cyclists visiting the Prince George area.

visitor.name: CRDL: Alexis Creek Branch
visitor.desc: The Alexis Creek Branch of the Cariboo Regional District Library is a small community library serving one of BC's most remote and sparsely populated corridors along Highway 20 through the Chilcotin. For touring cyclists grinding through this long, isolated stretch between Williams Lake and Bella Coola, it represents one of the very few publicly accessible indoor spaces in the community. The branch is staffed by a community librarian and is part of the broader Cariboo Regional District Library network.

detail.address: 7651 Yells Rd, Alexis Creek, BC V0L 1A0

visitor.name: Fort Langley National Historic Site
visitor.desc: A historic fur baling press exhibit within Fort Langley National Historic Site, a reconstructed Hudson's Bay Company fur trading post on the banks of the Fraser River. The site features rough-hewn timber buildings recreating 1800s fort life, costumed interpreters, and hands-on activities. Fort Langley is where the Crown Colony of British Columbia was proclaimed in 1858.

detail.address: 23433 Mavis Avenue, Fort Langley, BC V1M 2R5

visitor.name: ORL: Oliver Branch
visitor.desc: The Oliver Branch is part of the Okanagan Regional Library, one of Canada's 16 largest library systems serving over 399,000 people across 30 branches. Located inside a mall building in Oliver, BC, this branch offers public computers, Wi-Fi, and a novel lock-and-charge station where visitors can securely store and charge their devices. A touring cyclist rolling through the South Okanagan wine country would find it a useful stop for connectivity, rest, and community programming.

notes.Device charging: Lock and Charge Station on site: 'individually stores, charges phones, small tablets and mini iPads... works like a hotel safe'

visitor.name: Raven's Cry Theatre
visitor.desc: Raven's Cry Theatre is the Sunshine Coast's premier movie and live-event venue, located in Sechelt and showing first-run films weekly alongside broadcasts of the Metropolitan Opera, live music concerts, and dance recitals. The theatre is available for community rental and partners with local arts organizations including the Sunshine Coast Film Society and Coast Recital Society. For a touring cyclist, it offers a full evening's entertainment in a central Sechelt location.

visitor.name: ARTWRX Studio Gallery
visitor.desc: Art Alchemy Studio is an art gallery and working studio space in Courtenay on Vancouver Island, associated with local artist Sharon Lalonde who works in the Comox Valley. The studio participates in community arts events and exhibitions in the region. A touring cyclist passing through Courtenay's arts district may find it a worthwhile stop for locally created visual art.

visitor.name: Haig-Brown Heritage House
visitor.desc: The Haig-Brown Heritage House is a designated historic property sitting on the banks of the Campbell River, once home to Roderick Haig-Brown — celebrated fly-fisher, pioneering conservationist, acclaimed author, and magistrate. Operated by the Museum at Campbell River, the farmhouse and its tranquil riverside gardens serve as a bed and breakfast, garden event venue, and writer-in-residence program site. Located on Highway 28 near its junction with Highway 19, it makes a compelling cultural stop for cyclists touring northern Vancouver Island.

detail.address: 2250 Campbell River Road, Campbell River, BC V9W 4N7

visitor.name: Valley Fitness Centre
visitor.desc: Valley Fitness Centre is a community-run gym and physical fitness centre in Invermere, BC, situated in the Columbia Valley region of the Kootenays. Governed by a Board of Directors and boasting nearly 1,800 Facebook followers, it has a strong local membership base. Touring cyclists riding through Invermere may find it a useful stop given its gym facilities in a small mountain town.

visitor.name: Milner Gardens and Woodland
visitor.desc: A 70-acre coastal estate featuring wild-style woodland gardens, old-growth Douglas-fir forest, and an extensive collection of rare rhododendrons integrated among native plants on the sheltered east coast of Vancouver Island. The property includes historic Milner House, which dates to 1929 and houses the Camellia Tea Room. Located directly on the Island Highway between Parksville and Qualicum Beach, it makes a natural stop for touring cyclists riding Vancouver Island's east coast route.

detail.address: 2179 Island Hwy W, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 1G1

notes.Café or food on site: Camellia Tea Room located in the Drawing Room of historic Milner House; takes debit/credit only, no cash

visitor.name: Chamber of Commerce
visitor.desc: The Terrace Chamber of Commerce serves as a tourism information office for the North Coast region of British Columbia, providing a public resource for visitors and travellers passing through Terrace. As a publicly accessible information office, it is a natural stop for touring cyclists seeking local knowledge, maps, and regional guidance. The building is tagged as a public facility, suggesting a welcoming environment for drop-in visitors.

visitor.name: Geoffrey R Weller Library
visitor.desc: The Geoffrey R. Weller Library is the main academic library of the University of Northern British Columbia, located on the Prince George campus. It serves both the university community and external community members who can become registered patrons. Touring cyclists passing through Prince George may find it a quiet destination for research, study space, or print services.

detail.address: 3333 University Way, Prince George, BC V2N 4Z9

visitor.name: Vanderhoof Public Library
visitor.desc: Vanderhoof Public Library is the community library for the District of Vanderhoof and surrounding area in BC's Central Interior, serving residents with books, digital resources, computers, and internet access. The library also hosts a multipurpose room, adult literacy programs, and a wide range of online learning tools. For a touring cyclist, it offers a welcoming public space with internet access and a quiet place to rest in the heart of town.

visitor.name: Sunshine Coast Arena
visitor.desc: Sunshine Coast Arena is a publicly operated ice hockey facility managed by the Sunshine Coast Regional District, serving the Sechelt area. It is listed among SCRD's core recreation facilities alongside aquatic centres and community halls. Touring cyclists passing through Sechelt may find it a convenient landmark, though it is primarily a sporting venue rather than a dedicated cycling destination.

visitor.name: Comox Valley Art Gallery
visitor.desc: The Comox Valley Art Gallery is an independent non-profit public gallery in Courtenay dedicated to presenting contemporary art by regional, national, and international professional artists. Operating on the unceded territory of the K'ómoks Nation, it mounts rotating exhibitions alongside community art projects, creative residencies, public performances, and youth mentorship programs. A gift shop selling work from hundreds of local artists rounds out the visit, making it a culturally rich stop in the heart of the Comox Valley.

visitor.name: Yukon Suspension Bridge
visitor.desc: The Yukon Suspension Bridge crosses 65 feet above the white-water rapids of the Tutshi River on the South Klondike Highway, roughly 30 minutes from Skagway and 90 minutes from Whitehorse. The site includes an outdoor museum featuring real mammoth bones and regional history exhibits, wildlife viewing opportunities for bears and moose, and the Assayers Café for meals on a patio surrounded by wilderness. It is a popular stop for highway travellers and Alaska cruise ship passengers exploring the northern corridor.

notes.Café or food on site: Assayers Café on site: website states 'Visit the Assayers Café – Grab a snack or lunch and sit on our patio surrounded by nature.'

visitor.name: Revelstoke Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Revelstoke Aquatic Centre is the city's municipal swimming complex, featuring a 25-metre lap pool alongside a leisure pool with a lazy river, wild water slide, diving board, hot tub, sauna, and steam room. A climbing wall rounds out a surprisingly diverse recreation offering for a community facility. Touring cyclists arriving in Revelstoke after riding through the surrounding mountain terrain will find it a practical recovery stop.

visitor.name: Lester Centre of the Arts
visitor.desc: The Lester Centre of the Arts is Prince Rupert's premier performing arts venue, a 702-seat theatre at the foot of Hays Mountain that has anchored the cultural life of BC's North Coast since opening in 1987 as the Prince Rupert Performing Arts Centre. Renamed in 2006 to honour patrons Peter and Mary Lester, the venue hosts an eclectic mix of theatre, rock concerts, dance recitals, and community events. For touring cyclists passing through Prince Rupert, it is a notable cultural landmark and evening destination.

detail.address: 1100 McBride Street, Prince Rupert BC, V8J 3H2

notes.Café or food on site: Website /about-the-lester page states the facility includes 'two concession stands'

visitor.name: North Thompson Sportsplex
visitor.desc: The North Thompson Sportsplex is a municipal recreation facility in Clearwater, BC, situated in the heart of Wells Gray Country. It features a covered regulation-sized ice rink used for both ice and dry-floor events, with locker rooms and spectator viewing platforms. Operated by the District of Clearwater, it serves both local athletes and visitors to the region.

visitor.name: Tree Crusher
visitor.desc: Tree Crusher is a tourism attraction located near Mackenzie in Northern BC, listed under the District of Mackenzie's visitors program. It is geotagged in OpenStreetMap as a point of interest on the outskirts of the community. No further descriptive detail could be confirmed due to the attraction's web page returning a 404 error.

visitor.name: Smithers Public Library
visitor.desc: The Smithers Public Library is a full-service community library situated on the unceded territory of the Gidimt'en Clan and Witsuwit'en people in the Bulkley Valley. It offers a broad collection of physical and digital materials, computer and internet access, and regular programs for all ages. Touring cyclists passing through Smithers would find a quiet, welcoming community hub with internet services.

visitor.name: I-Hos Gallery
visitor.desc: I-Hos Gallery is a K'ómoks First Nation-owned gallery situated on the site of the original K'ómoks Village in the Comox Valley, overlooking the Comox Glacier on Vancouver Island. It presents traditional and contemporary Pacific Northwest Coast artwork hand-crafted by over 50 Indigenous artists, including masks, carvings, jewellery, prints, and woven cedar pieces. Voted Comox Valley's best art gallery in both 2024 and 2025, it also operates a satellite exhibition space at the Cumberland Visitor Information Centre.

visitor.name: Riverlodge Recreation Complex;Riverlodge Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Riverlodge is a municipally operated recreation and fitness centre in Kitimat, BC, run by the District of Kitimat. It is one of several public recreation facilities in the city, listed alongside an arena, ice rink, and aquatic centre, suggesting a substantial multi-use complex. Touring cyclists passing through Kitimat would find this a logical stop for its potential fitness and recovery amenities in a remote northern BC community.

visitor.name: Qualicum Beach Museum
visitor.desc: A community museum operated by the Qualicum Beach Historical and Museum Society since 1984, housing one of the finest paleontological collections in Western Canada alongside exhibits on Qualicum First Nation history, local social history, and natural history. The grounds feature notable outdoor exhibits including a totem pole by master Coast Salish carver Simon Charlie, and a restored Powerhouse heritage building with an energy history exhibit. Located on Beach Road in the heart of Qualicum Beach on Vancouver Island, it makes a worthwhile cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Oceanside region.

detail.address: 587 Beach Road, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 1K7

visitor.name: Salmo Valley Youth & Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Salmo Valley Youth & Community Centre is a non-profit society that saved a former high school from demolition in 2004, converting it into a hub for community programming in the small Kootenay town of Salmo. The centre offers a gymnasium, event rentals, youth drop-ins, workshops, and seasonal festivals, making it a notable gathering point for local and visiting community members. Touring cyclists passing through Salmo may find it a useful community contact point, though cyclist-specific amenities are not advertised.

visitor.name: CRDL: Forest Grove Branch
visitor.desc: The Forest Grove Branch is a small community library operated by the Cariboo Regional District Library, one of 15 branches spread across the vast Cariboo region of BC's Central Interior. It serves the rural Forest Grove community with physical collections, digital borrowing services, and community event programming. For touring cyclists making their way through this sparsely serviced stretch of interior BC, it is one of the few publicly accessible stops along the route.

detail.address: 4485 Eagle Creek Road, Forest Grove, BC V0K 1M0

visitor.name: Cottonwood House Historic Park
visitor.desc: Cottonwood House Historic Park is a BC Parks-managed heritage property in the Cariboo region of British Columbia, tagged in OSM as a nature reserve. The park's name suggests a historic roadhouse or dwelling site, making it a point of cultural interest for cyclists travelling through the Cariboo, Chilcotin, and Central Interior. The park is situated near coordinates 53.05°N, 122.16°W in a region traversed by touring cyclists on longer interior routes.

visitor.name: McLean Mill National Historic Site
visitor.desc: McLean Mill National Historic Site is a federally designated historic site near Port Alberni on Vancouver Island, preserving a historic steam-powered sawmill. It operates as a museum under the Alberni Heritage organization and draws visitors interested in BC's industrial logging heritage. The site is seasonal, making it a worthwhile destination stop for cyclists touring the Port Alberni valley in summer months.

visitor.name: Prince Rupert Library
visitor.desc: The Prince Rupert Library is also known by its Tsimshian name Waap Liitsx, meaning 'House of Reading,' reflecting the deep Indigenous cultural heritage of the North Coast region. It is a full-service public library offering free Wi-Fi, public computers, printing and scanning, accessibility services, and multilingual resources in French, Spanish, Punjabi, Tagalog, and Chinese. For touring cyclists arriving in this remote northern port city, it provides a welcoming indoor space with digital access and community information.

visitor.name: Sandspit Library
visitor.desc: The Sandspit Library is a small public branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library system, situated on Haida Gwaii (formerly the Queen Charlotte Islands) — one of British Columbia's most remote and spectacular cycling destinations. The branch began as a book deposit station in the early 1980s and moved to its current location in 1987, now holding nearly 4,500 items. It is open to walk-in visitors and offers free public WiFi, making it a potential rest stop for cyclists exploring the island.

visitor.name: Millard Nature Park
visitor.desc: Millard Conservation Area & Nature Park is a forested nature reserve near Courtenay on Vancouver Island, managed or recognized by BC Nature. It offers a natural green space in the Comox Valley region, which is a popular destination for cycling tourism. The park appears to be a quiet natural area, though detailed trail and facility information is not publicly documented online.

visitor.name: Hazelmere Pumpkin Patch
visitor.desc: Hazelmere Pumpkin Patch is a multi-generational family farm in South Surrey's Hazelmere Valley, operated by Gabriel Farms Ltd. since 2001 on land the Gabriel family has farmed since the 1930s. The 20-acre farm grows 12+ acres of pumpkins and gourds and features a mini corn maze, farm animal interaction areas, and play zones during its fall harvest season. Year-round, the farm also offers educational programs, school tours, spring break camps, and summer farm camps for children.

visitor.name: Langley Spirit Square
visitor.desc: Langley Spirit Square is a covered open-air public amphitheatre located within the Douglas Park area of Langley City, BC. Tagged in OSM as an open-air theatre with a roof structure, it serves as a community gathering and performance space in the heart of the city. Touring cyclists passing through Langley may find it a useful landmark and rest stop in an urban park setting.

visitor.name: On the Rocks
visitor.desc: On the Rocks is an indoor climbing and bouldering gym in Campbell River staffed by certified rock climbing guides, offering three distinct climbing areas and a full program roster spanning beginner intro sessions through advanced outdoor multi-pitch and rock rescue courses. The gym fosters a strong local community through regular events like crag clean-ups and competitions, and also serves as a gateway to nearby outdoor climbing at Crest Creek Crags. A touring cyclist looking for an active day off the bike or wanting to connect with local outdoor adventure culture would find this a compelling stop.

detail.address: 1980 North Island Hwy, Campbell River, BC

visitor.name: Revelstoke Railway Museum
visitor.desc: The Revelstoke Railway Museum preserves and interprets the history of the Canadian Pacific Railway through the mountains of Western Canada, a story central to the formation of Canada as a nation. Visitors can operate a diesel locomotive simulator using a real control stand, walk through an outdoor Heritage Railcar collection adjacent to a park on museum grounds, and explore multiple galleries tracing the people and machines of Canadian railways. For touring cyclists passing through Revelstoke on Trans-Canada or Rogers Pass routes, this is a well-established cultural landmark with an active events calendar.

detail.address: 719 Track St W, Revelstoke, BC V0E 2S0

visitor.name: Invermere Public Library
visitor.desc: Invermere Public Library serves the Columbia Valley from Spillimacheen to Canal Flats, offering a broad range of public services including a Library of Things, a Bookmobile for remote communities, and a dedicated work pod called the Loop Booth. It functions as a community hub with computers, WiFi, free tax clinics, and a seed library. Touring cyclists will find it a practical town-centre stop for connectivity, community information, and local resources.

visitor.name: Creston Valley Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Creston Valley Visitor Centre is operated by the Creston Valley Tourism Society and serves as the official tourism information hub for the Kootenay region's 'hidden gem'. Staff can assist visitors with area maps, local recommendations, event listings, and up-to-date travel advisories including border crossings, ferry schedules, and road conditions. For touring cyclists passing through the southern Kootenays, it is a natural stop for regional trip-planning resources and insider knowledge of the valley.

visitor.name: Greenwood Public Library
visitor.desc: Greenwood Public Library serves Canada's smallest city by area, a historic Boundary Country town with deep heritage roots. The library offers public computer and internet access, an accessible digital services program, and a range of community programming. Touring cyclists passing through Greenwood's heritage district would find it a quiet, public indoor stop.

detail.address: 346 South Copper Avenue, Greenwood BC V0H 1J0

visitor.name: Amphitheatre
visitor.desc: An outdoor amphitheatre in Creston, BC, operated by the Town of Creston in the Kootenays region. As an open-air venue of the amphi type, it likely hosts community events and performances in a public park setting. Touring cyclists passing through Creston may find it a scenic rest or cultural stop, though specific facilities are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Campbell River Community Centre
visitor.desc: Municipal community centre operated by the City of Campbell River, offering a pool, fitness classes, weight room, and indoor court rentals. Located on Vancouver Island, it serves as a public recreation hub that touring cyclists could use for rest and facilities.

visitor.name: The Hangar Climbing Lounge
visitor.desc: The Hangar is a bouldering-only climbing gym on the Sunshine Coast in Sechelt, founded in 2017 as a community hub for active locals and visitors. It features thick foam flooring, weekly route setting, and a self-serve snack and drinks bar, positioning itself as much a social hangout as a climbing facility. Touring cyclists on the popular Sunshine Coast route may enjoy it as a rest-day activity or rainy-day diversion.

notes.Café or food on site: Self-serve honour system snack and drinks bar available on site

visitor.name: Redwood Park
visitor.desc: Redwood Park is one of Surrey's most spectacular nature destinations, distinguished by a large forest of exotic tree species rarely found in the Lower Mainland.
