The park offers over 5 kilometres of scenic nature trails winding through the natural area, along with rustic picnic shelters and an all-access playground. It makes a pleasant detour or rest stop for cyclists exploring the South Surrey area.

visitor.name: Cathedral Grove
visitor.desc: Cathedral Grove, within MacMillan Park, is one of Vancouver Island's most celebrated natural landmarks: a roadside stand of ancient Douglas fir trees up to 800 years old and more than 9 metres in circumference, straddling Highway 4 between Qualicum Beach and Port Alberni. Touring cyclists heading to or from Tofino pass directly through the park and can walk the network of old-growth trails on both sides of the highway. A severe 1997 windstorm reshaped parts of the forest, adding ecological interest to an already dramatic landscape.

detail.address: BC-4, Port Alberni, BC V0R 1G0, Canada

visitor.name: Trail Aquatic and Leisure Centre
visitor.desc: The Trail Aquatic & Leisure Centre is the largest aquatic and multi-sport facility between Kelowna and Cranbrook, built in 1996 and recognized with several design awards. It features an 8-lane 25-metre competition pool, leisure pool, waterslide, diving boards, steam room, and a fully equipped fitness centre. Touring cyclists looking to recover with a swim or workout in the West Kootenay will find this a substantial public facility in the heart of Trail.

visitor.name: The Last Spike Gift Shop
visitor.desc: The Last Spike marks the exact spot in Craigellachie, BC where the final spike of the Canadian Pacific Railway was driven on November 7, 1885, completing Canada's transcontinental railway. Located just off the Trans-Canada Highway 45 km west of Revelstoke, this national monument draws history enthusiasts, railway buffs, and road-trip travelers to what is one of Canada's most iconic historical sites. For touring cyclists, it offers a meaningful and accessible roadside stop with picnic areas, washrooms, and a gift shop featuring coffee, snacks, and railway-themed souvenirs.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Coffee, Icecream, Snacks' as available at the gift shoppe

visitor.name: Courtenay Recreation - Lewis Centre
visitor.desc: The Lewis Centre is a municipal recreation and sports facility operated by the City of Courtenay on Vancouver Island, offering drop-in fitness, drop-in sports, a Wellness Centre, personal training, and adapted programs. It is one of several City of Courtenay recreation facilities and serves the broader Comox Valley community. Touring cyclists passing through Courtenay may find it a practical stop, though specific cyclist-facing amenities have not been confirmed from available sources.

visitor.name: Vibe Arts
visitor.desc: A cozy, light-filled art gallery in the heart of Qualicum Beach showcasing Canadian talent from emerging and local creators. The space emphasizes community connection and curated exhibitions, making it a pleasant stop for a touring cyclist looking to stretch their legs and take in some local culture on Vancouver Island.

detail.address: 152 2nd Avenue West, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 2T7

visitor.name: Sparwood Chamber Of Commerce & Business Information Centre
visitor.desc: The Sparwood Chamber of Commerce and Visitor Information Centre operates from Titan Park and serves as the first tourism stop in BC for travelers arriving from Alberta on Highway 3. The facility is home to The Titan, one of the largest trucks in the world, which draws over 60,000 visitors annually as a symbol of the region's coal mining heritage. Touring cyclists can pick up trail maps and local tourism information for mountain biking and the extensive Elk Valley trail network.

detail.address: 141 A Aspen Dr, Sparwood, BC V0B 2G0

notes.Water without admission: Water filling stations listed as free public VIC amenities inside and out; no admission or fee mentioned

visitor.name: Rossland Community Garden
visitor.desc: Rossland Community Garden is a shared community growing space in Rossland, BC, nestled in the Kootenay mountain region. Community gardens of this type typically offer plots tended by local residents, with seasonal produce and flowers. For a touring cyclist passing through Rossland's scenic mountain terrain, it may serve as a quiet green stopping point in the town.

detail.address: Jubilee St, Rossland, BC V0G 1Y0, Canada

visitor.name: McAbee Fossil Beds Heritage Site
visitor.desc: McAbee Fossil Beds is a nationally significant paleontological heritage site in the Thompson-Nicola region, preserving Eocene-epoch fossils over 50 million years old on unceded Secwépemc territory. After a seven-year closure it is now operated by the St'uxwtews Pesuten Heritage Society in collaboration with Bonaparte First Nation, blending rigorous paleontological science with Indigenous cultural stewardship. Touring cyclists can join guided interpretive walks along 8 km of trails where fossils of plants, insects, fish, and birds are visible in their natural setting.

visitor.name: W.C. Blair Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: W.C. Blair Recreation Centre is a large municipal recreation facility operated by the Township of Langley, featuring a free-form wave pool with six 25-metre lanes, a climbing wall, spray lagoon, sauna, steam room, and whirlpool. The centre offers a full range of fitness amenities including cardio and weight rooms alongside extensive aquatic programming. Touring cyclists would find useful services here including change rooms, showers, and quarter-operated lockers.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Website lists change rooms with a hand-held shower head under accessibility features; standard showers implied by full change room facilities at an aquatic centre
notes.Luggage / bag storage: Website lists quarter-operated lockers (Canadian quarters only)

visitor.name: ORL: Cherryville Branch
visitor.desc: The Cherryville Branch of the Okanagan Regional Library is a small public library on Highway 6 serving the rural Cherryville community, part of the ORL system spanning 30 branches across the Okanagan-Shuswap region. It claims to offer the fastest internet access in Cherryville, with two public internet stations and Wi-Fi available in and around the building at no charge. An always-open exterior book-drop and free vehicle parking in front make it an accessible indoor pause point for cyclists traveling the Monashee Highway corridor.

visitor.name: Rogers Pass Discovery Centre
visitor.desc: The Rogers Pass Discovery Centre is a Parks Canada visitor information facility at Rogers Pass in Glacier National Park, perched at one of the most historically significant mountain crossings in Canada — the original route of the CPR transcontinental railway through the Selkirk Mountains. Operated by Parks Canada and tagged as both a historic site and information office, the centre interprets the natural and human drama of this avalanche-prone alpine corridor. Cyclists riding the Trans-Canada Highway through Glacier National Park pass directly through Rogers Pass, making this a natural and notable landmark stop.

visitor.name: Telkwa Museum
visitor.desc: The Telkwa Museum is a local history attraction in the small village of Telkwa, situated at the confluence of the Bulkley and Telkwa rivers along Highway 16 (the Yellowhead). The village sits on the traditional territory of the Gidim'ten Clan of the Witsuwit'en people, and the museum offers touring cyclists a chance to explore a piece of northwestern BC's history mid-route. It is operated in connection with the village's Reading Centre and promoted through the Village of Telkwa's municipal tourism pages.

visitor.name: N.A.R. Station Museum
visitor.desc: The NAR Railway Station Museum preserves the heritage of the Northern Alberta Railways in the Dawson Creek area of northeastern British Columbia. It is located within NAR Park and commemorates the railway history that was pivotal to the region's development. A touring cyclist passing through Dawson Creek would find it a notable heritage stop, though operational details could not be verified.

detail.address: 900 Alaska Ave, Dawson Creek, BC V1G 4T6

visitor.name: Apex Mountain Resort
visitor.desc: Apex Mountain Resort is a full-service ski destination roughly 30 minutes from Penticton in BC's South Okanagan, offering 85 runs across 1,112 skiable acres with a northeast-facing aspect known for dry champagne powder. Four lifts, including a high-speed quad, serve terrain ranging from novice to expert, complemented by terrain parks and a tube park. The resort hosts events including an annual mountaintop electronic music festival (INVERSION) and has on-site dining and slope-side accommodations.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'a great selection of restaurants to indulge in' and lists 'Dining' as a top-level navigation section; Tim Hortons also referenced under Other Activities

visitor.name: Greg Moore Youth Centre
visitor.desc: The Greg Moore Youth Centre is a City of Maple Ridge municipal recreation facility serving youth and the broader community in the Haney area. As part of the city's network of recreation centres, it sits alongside the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre and Albion Community Centre. Touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley may find it a potential rest stop, though its primary mandate is youth programming.

visitor.name: FSJ Community Garden
visitor.desc: FSJ Community Garden is a publicly accessible community garden in Fort Saint John in Northern BC. Community gardens in this region offer touring cyclists a quiet green space to rest and connect with local growing culture. The garden has hosted public events including a garden tour, suggesting it is an active community asset.

detail.address: 9803 87 St, Fort St John, BC V1J 4Y6, Canada

visitor.name: Station House Gallery
visitor.desc: Station House Gallery occupies Williams Lake's oldest building — a Pacific Great Eastern Railway station constructed in 1919 — and has operated as a community arts hub since the Station House Studio & Gallery Society formed in 1981. The non-profit runs two gallery spaces with rotating monthly exhibitions and a gift shop stocked with locally made pottery, jewellery, woodwork, paintings, and artisan food products. Admission is always free, making it an easy and enriching stop for a touring cyclist passing through the Cariboo.

detail.address: 1 MacKenzie Avenue North, Williams Lake, BC V2G 1N4

visitor.name: North Island Wildlife Recovery & Educational Centre
visitor.desc: Founded in 1985, the North Island Wildlife Recovery Association (NIWRA) is a non-profit wildlife rehabilitation and education centre set on 8 acres in Errington, just minutes from Parksville. The facility houses over 60 resident non-releasable animals — including eagles, black bears, owls, and turkey vultures — and is home to what it describes as the largest eagle flight enclosure of its kind in Canada. Visitors follow a self-guided tour through graveled, wheelchair-accessible paths, with picnic areas, a wildlife garden featuring a mini-wetland, and an on-site gift shop.

detail.address: 1240 Leffler Road, Box 364, Errington, BC V0R 1V0

visitor.name: TidePools Aquarium
visitor.desc: Nicholas Sonntag TidePools Aquarium is a collect-and-release marine aquarium operated by BlueAct Marine Society inside the Gibsons Public Market on the Sunshine Coast. It showcases over 70 local species across interactive touch tanks and exhibits representing Rocky Intertidal, Eelgrass, Kelp Forest, Deep Sea, and other habitats. The non-profit facility pairs open exhibits with educational camps, conservation programs, and community events focused on coastal ecology.

detail.address: 473 Gower Point Road, Gibsons, BC V0N 1V4

visitor.name: Aurora Creek Marvel Pass TH
visitor.desc: The Aurora Creek Marvel Pass trailhead is an access point into the backcountry of Mount Assiniboine Provincial Park, part of the Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks UNESCO World Heritage Site famed for its glaciers, alpine lakes, and peaks reaching 3,618 m. The park has no road access — trails are the only way in — making any visit a true wilderness undertaking. Bikepacking or mountain biking visitors would be entering a remote environment where self-sufficiency is essential, as services and facilities are absent across most of the park.

visitor.name: Heiltsuk Cultural Education Centre
visitor.desc: The Heiltsuk Cultural Education Centre has operated for over thirty years in Bella Bella (Waglisla) on BC's remote Central Coast, dedicated to researching, preserving, and revitalizing the history, language, and cultural traditions of the Heiltsuk Nation. Its museum program showcases Heiltsuk art and artifacts with a focus on visual and hands-on learning, and the Centre actively pursues repatriation of heritage objects. A public resource centre offers access to archival and cultural materials, making it a meaningful stop for travellers reaching Bella Bella via the Discovery Coast ferry passage.

detail.address: P.O. Box 880, Bella Bella, British Columbia, CANADA V0T 1Z0

visitor.name: Natural Bridge
visitor.desc: Natural Bridge is a striking geological formation in Yoho National Park where the Kicking Horse River has carved a natural rock arch, creating a dramatic canyon viewpoint accessible by road near Field, BC. It sits within one of Canada's most scenic national parks on the western slopes of the Continental Divide, making it a compelling stop for cyclists touring the Trans-Canada corridor. The surrounding Yoho landscape — glaciers, waterfalls, and ancient Burgess Shale fossil beds — adds significant depth to any cycling itinerary through the Canadian Rockies.

visitor.name: MV Atlinto
visitor.desc: The MV Atlinto is a 12.5-metre wooden steam launch built in 1911 that served as a glacier-tour vessel in Atlin's early tourism era before being beached in the early 1950s and later restored. It is maintained by the volunteer-run Atlin Historical Society as a heritage attraction in the remote northwest corner of British Columbia, near the Yukon and Alaska borders. Touring cyclists riding through Atlin—itself a historic gold-rush town on unceded Taku River Tlingit territory—may encounter this vessel as part of the area's outdoor heritage landscape.

visitor.name: ORL: Hedley Public Library
visitor.desc: The Hedley Public Library is a small branch of the Okanagan Regional Library, serving the historic gold-mining village of Hedley along Highway 3 in the southern Okanagan. Part of a 30-branch regional network established in 1936, the branch offers free public Wi-Fi to both members and visiting guests. A parking lot on the north side of the building provides access to this remote community stop along a popular cycling corridor.

visitor.name: Beacon Theatre
visitor.desc: The Beacon Theatre is Canada's second community-owned cinema, purchased in 2010 by the Lakes District Film Appreciation Society and located in Burns Lake on the Yellowhead Highway. Upgraded from a 1950s 35mm projector system to full digital projection and sound, it now shows first-run films, 3D movies, and satellite events. For touring cyclists passing through the Cariboo–Chilcotin interior on Highway 16, it offers a rare chance to catch a current film in a small, community-run venue.

visitor.name: Loon Lagoon
visitor.desc: Loon Lagoon is the indoor aquatic and wellness facility at Manning Park Resort, featuring a 50-ft heated swimming pool, hot tubs, a steam room, and a sauna. Situated along the Highway 3 cycling corridor in Manning Provincial Park, it is open to day visitors as well as resort guests, giving touring cyclists a rare chance to recover properly after crossing the Cascades. An on-site fitness centre with cardio equipment and free weights adds to the recovery options.

notes.Café or food on site: Pinewoods Restaurant and Bear's Den Pub are listed as on-site food and beverage outlets on the resort's hours page

visitor.name: Maritime Heritage Centre
visitor.desc: The Maritime Heritage Centre is a community museum in Campbell River celebrating west coast maritime history, anchored by the fully restored BCP45 fishing seiner — the vessel that once graced the back of the Canadian $5 bill. Born from a 1998 partnership between the Campbell River Daybreak Rotary Club and the City of Campbell River, the centre sits near Discovery Pier with ocean views and houses exhibits, guided tours led by knowledgeable volunteer docents, and versatile event spaces. It is an engaging cultural stop for touring cyclists riding the Island Highway corridor through Campbell River.

detail.address: 621 Island Highway, Campbell River BC, V9W 0B7

visitor.name: Gym of Rock
visitor.desc: An all-abilities indoor rock climbing gym located inside WestGate Public Market in Salmon Arm. The facility offers drop-in climbing, belay certification, lessons, and camps. A good rainy-day or rest-day activity for touring cyclists passing through the Shuswap region.

detail.address: 111-2090 10th Ave. SW, Salmon Arm, BC V1E 0E1

visitor.name: Driftwood Marine Regional Park
visitor.desc: Driftwood Marine Regional Park is a nature reserve in the Comox Valley on Vancouver Island, managed by the Comox Valley Regional District. Its marine setting along Baynes Sound offers coastal scenery that touring cyclists passing through the area may enjoy as a rest stop or side trip.

visitor.name: The Village Theatre - E.C.H.O. Players Society
visitor.desc: The Village Theatre is a designated Heritage Building in Qualicum Beach, originally built in 1949 as a movie theatre in the Streamline Moderne style and purchased by the ECHO Players Society in 1974 for conversion into a live performance venue. The volunteer-driven community theatre has over 240 members and produces five mainstage shows per season alongside the Vancouver Island Juried One-Act Play Festival, with a continuous performance history spanning more than 50 years. Cyclists touring the Oceanside area will find it a notable cultural stop, with the outdoor mural by artist David Goatley visible on the building's exterior.

detail.address: 110 Second Avenue West, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 1S8

visitor.name: Laurie Guichon Memorial Grasslands Interpretive Site
visitor.desc: The Laurie Guichon Memorial Grasslands Interpretive Site is a 102-hectare outdoor interpretive area on Provincial Crown land approximately 11 km east of Merritt, established in 2001 to educate the public about the ecological, economic, and social values of BC's Southern Interior grasslands. Named in honour of Laurie Guichon, a fourth-generation Nicola Valley rancher and founding member of the Nicola Watershed Community Round Table, the site includes a viewing platform and supports school groups and general visitors. Touring cyclists in the Merritt area would encounter open grassland scenery and interpretive programming about one of BC's most distinctive and threatened ecosystems.

visitor.name: Port Kells Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: Port Kells Outdoor Pool is a City of Surrey municipal outdoor swimming pool in the Port Kells neighbourhood. It offers public swims and swimming lessons during the summer season. A touring cyclist passing through Surrey's rural-fringe east side could use the pool as a refreshing mid-ride stop on a hot day.

visitor.name: Leisure Pool
visitor.desc: The Leisure Pool is an indoor covered swimming pool situated within the Strathcona Gardens Recreation Complex, a multi-use public facility operated by the Strathcona Regional District in Campbell River on Vancouver Island. The larger complex encompasses pools, arenas, fitness studios, and a range of aquatic and dry-floor programming. For touring cyclists, it represents a potential stop for a swim or post-ride clean-up at a full-service community recreation centre.

detail.address: 225 South Dogwood Street, Campbell River, BC V9W 8C8

visitor.name: The Grist Mill and Gardens at Keremeos
visitor.desc: The Grist Mill and Gardens is a heritage attraction near Keremeos in the Similkameen Valley, operating a historic flour mill surrounded by period gardens. It is currently under new management and transitioning into its 2026 season. The surrounding Similkameen countryside makes it a natural stop on cycling routes through the southern Okanagan.

detail.address: 2691 Upper Bench Rd, Keremeos, BC V0X 1N4

visitor.name: Prince George Playhouse
visitor.desc: Prince George Playhouse is a performing arts theatre located in Prince George, British Columbia, serving as a cultural hub for the Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior region. As a publicly accessible venue, it offers touring cyclists a chance to take in live performance while passing through the city. The facility is situated on Recplace Drive, near other recreational amenities in the area.

visitor.name: TNRL: Blue River Library
visitor.desc: The Blue River Library is a small public branch of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system serving this remote community in BC's central interior along the Yellowhead Highway corridor. Originally opened in 1975 and operated out of a trailer before moving to a permanent portable in that same year, the current 1,008-square-foot building has been in service since 1998. Cycle tourists passing through one of the more isolated stretches of the Yellowhead route will find free Wi-Fi and a wheelchair-accessible public space in an area with few services.

visitor.name: Egmont Heritage Centre
visitor.desc: The Egmont Heritage Centre is a community museum in the remote coastal village of Egmont, BC, situated on the unceded territory of the shíshálh (Sechelt) Nation directly across from Skookumchuck Narrows Provincial Park. The museum chronicles Indigenous and pioneer history of the Sunshine Coast through exhibits that include rare Vivian and Easthope marine engines alongside a collection of depression glass and antique bottles. Touring cyclists will find a welcoming stop with a picnic area, free WiFi, clean restrooms, and a gift shop stocked with work by local artisans.

notes.Café or food on site: Gift shop stocks 'snacks' sourced from local Sunshine Coast artisans, per website front page

visitor.name: Haney House
visitor.desc: Haney House is a heritage home built in 1883 by Thomas Haney, the founder of the Haney neighbourhood in Maple Ridge. Three generations of the Haney family lived here before it was donated to the city in 1979 and converted into a historic house museum. It offers a glimpse into early settler life in the Fraser Valley and is operated by the Maple Ridge Historical Society.

visitor.name: Seal Bay Regional Nature Park
visitor.desc: Seal Bay Regional Nature Park is a forested nature reserve managed by the Comox Valley Regional District on the eastern coast of Vancouver Island near Courtenay, also known by its K'ómoks name Xwee Xwhya Luq. The park encompasses old-growth woodland and provides trail access toward the Strait of Georgia shoreline, making it a scenic detour or destination for cyclists exploring the Comox Valley. It is one of the larger intact natural areas remaining on the eastern Vancouver Island lowlands.

visitor.name: Bulkley Valley Museum
visitor.desc: The Bulkley Valley Museum preserves and presents the history and heritage of the Bulkley Valley region of northwestern British Columbia, including Indigenous, settler, and industrial history. It occupies a public building on Main Street in Smithers, a key stop on the Yellowhead Highway (Hwy 16) corridor — a major cross-Canada touring route. Cyclists riding this remote stretch will find it a meaningful cultural pause in an area where heritage sites are sparse.

visitor.name: Simms Creek Greenway
visitor.desc: Simms Creek Greenway is a protected nature reserve greenway in the Campbell River area of Vancouver Island, situated within the region's salmon-bearing watershed landscape. The area falls within the mandate of Greenways Land Trust, a registered charity operating since 1996 that conserves ecological and recreational greenways on the traditional territories of the Wei Wai Kum, We Wai Kai, and Kwiakah First Nations. Touring cyclists in the Campbell River corridor may find it a scenic natural detour, though on-site facilities are unconfirmed.

detail.address: 354 Cottonwood Dr, Campbell River, BC V9W 6P5

visitor.name: The Gardens on Anderton
visitor.desc: The Gardens on Anderton is a community therapeutic garden in Comox operated by the Anderton Therapeutic Gardens Society, featuring a lily-covered fishpond, labyrinth, small orchard, children's garden, beekeeping, and a covered performance stage amid extensive lawns and flower beds. Entry is by donation, making it an accessible and restorative stop for cyclists passing through the Comox Valley. The garden hosts concerts, farmers' markets, and community events, and includes a snack bar cafe and over 40 allotment plots.

notes.Café or food on site: Website features list includes 'Garden Cafe'; Q&A confirms 'Yes, we have a Snack Bar. We do not sell cooked foods or alcohol.'

visitor.name: Port Alberni Maritime Discovery Centre
visitor.desc: A waterfront maritime museum at Port Alberni's Harbour Quay, operated by the Port Alberni Maritime Heritage Society since 1989. Exhibits cover West Coast shipwrecks, navigation history, the restored Bamfield Lifeboat, ship models spanning centuries of local maritime activity, and the 1964 tsunami. Situated near restaurants and shops at the quay, it makes a natural stop for cyclists riding through the Alberni Valley.

detail.address: 2900 Harbour Rd, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 7X2

visitor.name: Glow Gardens Langley
visitor.desc: Glow Gardens Langley is a large-scale outdoor Christmas light festival held annually from late November through December at a former greenhouse site in Langley, BC. Founded in 2017, the festival features over a million lights arranged in themed immersive lands, a Merry Makers Market with artisan vendors, gourmet food trucks, and live entertainment. Each year brings a new narrative theme — making it a destination-worthy seasonal attraction in the Fraser Valley.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Gourmet food trucks offering mouthwatering culinary delights' as a festival highlight

visitor.name: Princeton Arena
visitor.desc: Princeton Arena is a municipally operated ice facility in Princeton, BC, offering ice hockey and skating to the community. It is part of the Town of Princeton's parks and recreation network, which also includes a bike park, outdoor pool, and campground. A touring cyclist passing through Princeton might visit as a spectator or to use shared municipal facilities.

visitor.name: M&DPL: Lena Schultz Reading Room (LSRR)
visitor.desc: A tiny rural reading room in Dome Creek, housed in a former public school alongside the Dome Creek Community Association. It offers books, DVDs, magazines, internet access, and community programs like a book club and children's events. For a touring cyclist on the remote Yellowhead Highway corridor, it's one of the few public indoor spaces between McBride and Prince George.

visitor.name: Kelly's Go Karts
visitor.desc: Kelly's Go Karts has been a summertime fixture in Sicamous, BC since 1987, offering a 1,000-foot track with a scenic mountain backdrop just off Highway 1 near Shuswap Lake. Family-owned and operated, the venue runs double-seater karts for adults with children, kid-friendly karts, and adult karts reaching 15–25 km/h. It is a walk-up, first-come-first-served venue with free on-site parking, making it a casual roadside stop for touring cyclists passing through the Shuswap corridor.

visitor.name: Dan Bosch Park
visitor.desc: Dan Bosch Park is a nature reserve on British Columbia's Sunshine Coast, operated by the Sunshine Coast Regional District and situated directly along the Sunshine Coast Highway — a popular touring corridor. The park permits leashed dogs, suggesting trail access suitable for active visitors. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a scenic roadside stop, though specific on-site facilities are not documented.

visitor.name: Nakusp Public Library
visitor.desc: Nakusp Public Library is a community library serving the small Kootenay town of Nakusp, offering physical and digital collections including ebooks and audiobooks via Libby, plus computers, printing, and photocopying. The library hosts a lively schedule of programs and events for all ages, making it a genuine community hub. For touring cyclists, it is a welcoming public space to rest, use a computer, and connect with local community life in a town that sees relatively few services.

detail.address: 92A 6th Ave NW, Box 297, Nakusp, BC V0G 1R0

visitor.name: Kynoch Adventures
visitor.desc: Kynoch Adventures is a locally owned wilderness tour operator in the Bella Coola Valley, founded in 2002 and specializing in grizzly bear viewing on the Atnarko River, wilderness eco-rafting, guided hiking, and ultramarathon run camps in the Great Bear Rain Forest. Lead guides are professional biologists and long-time residents with over three decades of ecological expertise in Tweedsmuir Park. For touring cyclists who ride the remote Highway 20 into Bella Coola, this operator offers a rare chance to experience world-class grizzly bear habitat with knowledgeable local naturalists.

visitor.name: Comox Valley Horticultural Society Herb Garden
visitor.desc: The Comox Valley Horticultural Society Herb Garden is a curated botanical attraction featuring a named collection of herbs with detailed taxonomic, historical, and medicinal descriptions, maintained by an active member-driven society in the Courtenay area of Vancouver Island. The CVHS is notably cycling-friendly, operating a dedicated 'Garden Cycling Tours' program — a self-guided 11 km bike route through downtown Courtenay gardens in partnership with the Comox Valley Cycling Coalition. The garden represents the society's educational mission and serves as a reference point for the region's broader garden-tourism network.

visitor.name: Othello / Quintette Tunnels
visitor.desc: The Othello Tunnels (also called the Quintette Tunnels) are five rock-cut railway tunnels blasted through a 300-foot granite gorge on the Kettle Valley Railway in 1914, now preserved within Coquihalla Canyon Provincial Park near Hope. The 3.5 km round-trip trail threads through the tunnels and across suspension bridges above the churning Coquihalla River, forming part of the Trans Canada Trail on a flat, gravel surface. Cyclists are welcome on the trail but must dismount and walk through the tunnels, and flashlights are strongly recommended for the longer, darker sections.

visitor.name: Burns Lake Public Library
visitor.desc: Burns Lake Public Library is the community library serving Burns Lake and the surrounding Lakes District in BC's Central Interior. It offers public computers, printing, photocopying, exam invigilation, meeting room rentals, and an extensive digital media collection. For touring cyclists, it represents a potential rest stop in a smaller community that sits along routes through the Central Interior.

detail.address: 585 Government Street, Burns Lake, BC V0J 1E0

visitor.name: Timberlane Track
visitor.desc: Timberlane Track is a City of Powell River outdoor sports facility perched high above Townsite, offering panoramic views of the Salish Sea and the surrounding BC coast. It is home to the Villa Soccer Club and hosts a full-sized soccer pitch as well as a 400-metre walking and running track. The dramatic coastal setting makes it a potentially scenic stop for touring cyclists exploring the Powell River area.

detail.address: 5400 Timberlane Ave, Powell River, BC V8A 5M8

visitor.name: CRDL: McLeese Lake Branch
visitor.desc: The McLeese Lake Branch is a small community library serving the rural McLeese Lake area along Highway 97, operated as part of the 15-branch Cariboo Regional District Library network. It offers access to physical collections, digital lending (ebooks and audiobooks via Libby), and community programming. For touring cyclists on the Cariboo Highway corridor, it represents a quiet, publicly accessible rest stop in an otherwise sparsely serviced stretch of road.

visitor.name: Dreamcycle Motorcycle Museum
visitor.desc: Dreamcycle Motorcycle Museum in Sorrento houses one of Canada's most unique and diverse collections of over 100 historic motorbikes, each selected for its story and displayed as a work of art spanning more than a century of motorcycle history. Situated directly on the Trans-Canada Highway in the Shuswap, it is a natural waypoint for touring cyclists passing through the region. The museum offers virtual-headset and live guided tours, a gift shop, and an on-site café.

notes.Café or food on site: Sprokkets Cafe on site serving homemade sandwiches and baked goods baked daily, confirmed via multiple website passages

visitor.name: Japanese Canadian Museum
visitor.desc: The Langham Japanese Canadian Museum in Kaslo commemorates the forced internment of over 22,000 Japanese Canadians during WWII, including the nearly 1,100 interned in Kaslo itself — some of whom lived in the very Langham building that now houses the museum. Exhibits include period artifacts, archival photographs, audio recordings, interpretive displays, and the newly completed Ten-Chi-Jin Japanese Garden. Operated by the Langham Cultural Society, the museum is part of a vibrant cultural hub that also encompasses two galleries, an intimate theatre, and artist studios.

visitor.name: Merritt Visitor Information
visitor.desc: The Merritt Visitor Information Centre is housed at the Baillie House Historic Site on Voght Street and is operated by the Baillie House Historical Society. It serves as the primary tourism information hub for the City of Merritt and the broader Nicola Valley, offering directions, local resources, and travel guidance to visitors. Touring cyclists passing through Merritt can stop here for orientation to the area's attractions, parks, and amenities.

visitor.name: Bill Reid Millennium Amphitheatre
visitor.desc: The Bill Reid Millennium Amphitheatre is an outdoor performance venue in Surrey, BC, named in honour of the celebrated Haida artist Bill Reid. It serves as a public gathering and concert space within Surrey's arts and culture landscape, making it a potential rest or sightseeing stop for touring cyclists passing through the Lower Mainland.

visitor.name: The Pillar
visitor.desc: The Pillar (also known as Pillar Rock) is a protected BC Parks site 11 km northwest of Falkland, established to preserve a striking conglomerate stone hoodoo formation. A steep trail leads to the pillar in about 15 minutes, rewarding hikers with a distinctive geological landmark in the Thompson region. The park is a simple day-use natural area with no on-site infrastructure, making it a rugged but scenic detour for cyclists exploring the Falkland-Chase Road corridor.

visitor.name: The Exploration Place
visitor.desc: The Exploration Place is a museum and science centre situated in Lheidli T'enneh Memorial Park in Prince George, offering hands-on exhibits spanning regional Indigenous history, natural history, and science. It hosts multiple themed galleries, an onsite café and teaching kitchen (Origins Kitchen), a retail shop, and Fort George Railway — billed as Canada's shortest passenger railway. A touring cyclist making a stop in Prince George could spend several hours here exploring BC's interior history and ecology.

notes.Café or food on site: Origins Kitchen described on main page as an 'onsite café and teaching kitchen' serving 'delicious, local food and beverages.'

visitor.name: Seafarers' Mission
visitor.desc: The Seafarers' Mission (also called Lighthouse Harbour Mission) is a nonprofit organization in Prince Rupert that provides welfare support and a welcoming space for merchant mariners visiting the port from around the world. Prince Rupert is one of Canada's busiest container ports, making this a meaningful stop for seafarers in need of assistance or companionship. A touring cyclist passing through this northern BC port city may find it a point of cultural interest tied to the town's strong maritime identity.

detail.address: 245 3rd Ave W, Prince Rupert, BC V8J 3P6

visitor.name: Prince George Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Prince George Visitor Information Centre is the official tourism hub for the city, offering expert travel advice, maps, and local recommendations to help visitors explore the region. Run by Tourism Prince George, it also features a gift shop stocked with locally made products and exclusive souvenirs. For touring cyclists passing through central BC, it serves as a useful resource for route planning and discovering local experiences.

detail.address: 850 Canada Games Way, Prince George, BC V2L 5T6

visitor.name: Creative Cove
visitor.desc: Creative Cove is a paint-your-own-pottery and art studio concept founded in Alberta with roots in Yukon and Northern BC, offering drop-in ceramic painting, guided workshops, birthday parties, and private events. The brand positions itself as a relaxed, community-driven creative space accessible to all ages and skill levels. A Comox Valley location is referenced on the main website, suggesting a presence in the Courtenay area, though location-specific details are not publicly confirmed online.

visitor.name: Hope Recreation Centre Arena
visitor.desc: The Hope Recreation Centre is a municipal facility in Hope, BC, housing the Dan Sharrers Aquatic Centre with a 25-metre lap pool, leisure pool, hot tub, sauna, and steam room, alongside an arena, weight and cardio rooms, fitness studio, and conference centre. Located along the Trans-Canada corridor, it could serve as a welcome mid-ride stop for touring cyclists passing through Hope. The centre is operated by the Fraser Valley Regional District.

visitor.name: Pemberton Museum
visitor.desc: A heritage museum and archives in the heart of the Pemberton Valley, on the traditional territory of the Lil'wat and St'át'imc Nations, collecting and sharing the region's history since 1982. The site includes a historic schoolhouse and features exhibits on logging, railways, and pioneer life. Admission is by donation, making it an easy and worthwhile stop for touring cyclists passing through Pemberton on the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

visitor.name: Bella Coola Estuary Conservancy
visitor.desc: The Bella Coola Estuary Conservancy is a protected BC Parks area where the Bella Coola River meets the North Bentinck Arm, forming one of the coast's richest estuarine habitats. The area supports grizzly bears, trumpeter swans, Barrow's goldeneyes, and five species of juvenile salmon, making it a compelling wildlife-watching destination for touring cyclists in the Bella Coola Valley. It is an undeveloped conservancy with no built visitor infrastructure.

visitor.name: Fort McLeod Provincial Historic Park
visitor.desc: Fort McLeod Provincial Historic Park is a BC Parks-managed nature reserve in Northern BC. The park carries provincial historic designation, suggesting cultural or heritage significance at this remote location. Touring cyclists travelling through the region may find it a worthwhile stop along what would otherwise be a sparsely serviced corridor.

visitor.name: Wells Museum
visitor.desc: The Wells Museum occupies one of the few surviving original Cariboo Gold Quartz Mining Company buildings, telling the story of prospector Fred Wells and the hard-rock gold rush that built the town in the 1930s. Run entirely by volunteers, it preserves artifacts, photographs, and historical sketches connecting Wells' mining heritage to its present-day community of artists, miners, and outdoor enthusiasts. Cyclists exploring the Barkerville corridor will find it a compelling stop that contextualizes the broader Cariboo gold country.

visitor.name: Aldergrove Credit Union Community Centre
visitor.desc: A large municipal recreation complex in Aldergrove operated by the Township of Langley, featuring indoor pools with waterslides, a wave pool, river channel, spray park, ice arena, fitness centre, indoor walking track, and an outdoor experience area. Touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley will find it a practical stop with change-room showers, washrooms, and on-site food options including a Triple O's restaurant.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Change rooms with handheld shower head mentioned under accessibility amenities
notes.Café or food on site: Food truck listed as an amenity; Triple O's restaurant operates as a leased space on site

visitor.name: ORL: Silver Creek Branch
visitor.desc: Silver Creek Branch is a small rural outpost of the Okanagan Regional Library system, serving the Silver Creek community near Salmon Arm. It offers public computers, Wi-Fi, and a community gathering space, and features a rotating monthly art wall showcasing local artists. The library welcomes clubs and groups and can help organize book clubs, craft circles, or game groups — a quiet local hub in an otherwise rural stretch.

visitor.name: Sam Lindsey Aquatic Center
visitor.desc: The Sam Lindsey Aquatic Center is a municipally operated public swimming facility serving the community of Kitimat in BC's North Coast region, situated within the unceded territory of the Haisla Nation. As the town's dedicated aquatic venue, it offers swimming programs and recreational water access to residents and visitors alike. For touring cyclists making the journey to this remote industrial and natural destination, it represents a potential venue for a recovery swim or a rinse after time on the road.

visitor.name: Drylands Arena
visitor.desc: Drylands Arena is a Village of Ashcroft–owned community sports facility centred on a single ice sheet used for figure skating and minor hockey through the winter season. In warmer months the arena converts to a dry-floor venue hosting events like the annual Fall Fair, concerts, and community gatherings, making it a year-round social hub for this small desert-climate town. A visiting cyclist would find it a lively local landmark with a concession and washrooms, set in one of the driest landscapes in Canada.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'a concession' as a facility feature of the arena

visitor.name: R.W. Starratt Wildlife Sanctuary
visitor.desc: The R.W. Starratt Wildlife Sanctuary protects Cranberry Marsh near Valemount in the Robson Valley, a wetland known for bird and wildlife viewing. The trailhead provides access to a nature trail through this BC Nature-recognized sanctuary. It sits in a scenic mountain corridor that touring cyclists passing through Valemount on Highway 5 may find worth a short detour.

visitor.name: Salmo Valley Public Library
visitor.desc: The Salmo Valley Public Library is a small community library serving the Salmo area in BC's Kootenay region. It is a publicly accessible municipal facility and a natural rest point for touring cyclists passing through this quiet rural village on routes such as the Salmo-Creston corridor. As a public library, it typically offers a calm indoor environment and free internet access to visitors.

visitor.name: TNRL: Savona Library
visitor.desc: The Savona Library is a small branch of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library, built in 2005 to replace a decades-old bookmobile stop in this tiny community on the Trans-Canada Highway corridor west of Kamloops. At 1,400 square feet it is a modest but fully functional public library offering free Wi-Fi, public computers, and printing. For a cyclist passing through rural Savona, it represents one of very few public indoor stops between Kamloops and Cache Creek.

visitor.name: Elkford Visitor's Centre
visitor.desc: The Elkford Visitor's Centre is a publicly operated tourism information office run by the District of Elkford in the Kootenay region of British Columbia. It serves as a gateway resource for visitors exploring the area's significant wilderness and outdoor recreation opportunities. Touring cyclists passing through can expect regional tourism guidance and local area information.

visitor.name: Daajing Giids Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Daajing Giids Visitor Centre is the essential first stop for anyone exploring Haida Gwaii, offering local knowledge on trails, camping, culture, and logistics that no website or app can replicate. Staffed by people who live and travel these roads daily, it serves as the gateway to Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve, the ancient Haida villages, and dozens of hiking trails across Graham Island. A touring cyclist arriving here will find curated regional intelligence, a gift shop stocked with locally made souvenirs, and a waterfront deck overlooking the bay.

detail.address: 3220 Wharf Way, Daajing Giids, BC V0T 1S0

visitor.name: Comox Valley Sports Centre
visitor.desc: The Comox Valley Sports Centre is a publicly operated multi-sport facility managed by the Comox Valley Regional District, hosting swimming, fitness, ice hockey, lacrosse, and figure skating programs. Located in the Comox Valley near Courtenay, it functions as the region's primary indoor recreation hub. Touring cyclists may find it a practical mid-route stop given its likely shower and washroom facilities associated with aquatic programming.

visitor.name: Yaaguun Gandlaay Heritage Site/Conservancy
visitor.desc: Yaaguun G̱andlaay Conservancy protects the mouth of the Yakoun River and Yakoun Bay on Graham Island, Haida Gwaii, a place used since time immemorial by the Haida Nation for cultural, social, and spiritual purposes. The area contains 25 registered archaeological sites and hundreds of culturally modified trees, making it one of the most significant cultural landscapes in Haida Gwaii. Touring cyclists riding the roads near Port Clements may find this conservancy a meaningful detour into deeply rooted Haida history and salmon country.

visitor.name: Quesnel Arts and Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Quesnel Arts and Recreation Centre is a city-operated facility serving the Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior region, offering ice hockey and swimming among its programs. As the main municipal recreation hub for Quesnel, it functions as a community gathering point for residents and visitors alike. Touring cyclists passing through Quesnel on the interior plateau could potentially use its aquatic facilities to refresh after long days on the road.

visitor.name: House of Huu-ay-aht
visitor.desc: The House of Huu-ay-aht is a striking community hall of the Huu-ay-aht First Nations, located in the community of Anacla near Pachena Bay on the west coast of Vancouver Island. Opened in 2000 with a traditional ceremony welcoming over 1,000 guests, it was constructed beneath four massive 30-ton spruce logs supporting two dozen smaller roof logs in a form deeply rooted in Nuu-chah-nulth architecture. It sits in the Barkley Sound region near the southern trailhead of the West Coast Trail, an area popular with adventure cyclists exploring Vancouver Island's remote west coast.

visitor.name: Japanese Garden
visitor.desc: The Japanese Garden is a botanical garden set within Millennium Park in Creston, BC, in the southern Kootenays. Operated by the Town of Creston, it offers a tranquil cultural landscape in a region known for its agricultural valley and mountain scenery. A touring cyclist passing through Creston on routes connecting the Kootenay Lake corridor would find it a scenic detour in the heart of town.

visitor.name: Eddie Mountain Memorial Arena
visitor.desc: Eddie Mountain Memorial Arena (EMMA) is a community sports facility operated by the Regional District of East Kootenay (RDEK), located in the Columbia Valley area of the East Kootenays. As a municipal arena, it serves the surrounding communities with ice and recreational programming. Touring cyclists passing through the Kootenays may find it a potential rest stop, though specific cyclist-oriented services are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: LALA: Lillooet Public Library
visitor.desc: The Lillooet Area Library Association operates this public library serving the communities of Lillooet, Gold Bridge, and Shalalth in the Fraser Canyon region. It functions as a broad community hub offering a Library of Things, device lending, digital media access, and a range of adult and youth programs. For touring cyclists passing through Lillooet — a key waypoint on the Duffey Lake Road corridor — it offers computers, Wi-Fi, and community resources in a welcoming public space.

visitor.name: Ashcroft Pool
visitor.desc: Ashcroft Pool is a seasonal outdoor public swimming pool operated by the Village of Ashcroft, situated in one of the driest and hottest regions of British Columbia where summer temperatures regularly soar. The main pool features a graduated entry designed for wheelchair access, plus a wading area and waterslide, making it a true community hub during summer. For touring cyclists grinding through the arid Thompson River valley, this municipal pool is a compelling cooling-off stop.

visitor.name: Sunset Theatre
visitor.desc: The Sunset Theatre is the only professional theatre in BC's Cariboo/Chilcotin region, located in the small historic town of Wells. Founded in 2000, it operates three distinct series — Exploration, Presentation, and Production — as well as a long-running Cabaret event, drawing touring artists and audiences from across Canada. For cyclists making their way through the Cariboo, it offers a rare opportunity to catch live professional performance in a genuinely remote setting.

visitor.name: LALA: Bridge River Library
visitor.desc: The Bridge River Library is a small branch of the Lillooet Area Library Association serving the remote Shalalth community in the Bridge River Valley. It is one of three branches run by LALA, which connects rural and Indigenous communities across a large area of BC's interior. For touring cyclists passing through an area with very few services, it offers a rare public access point with internet connectivity.

visitor.name: Rainbow Lanes
visitor.desc: Rainbow Lanes is a 16-lane, five-pin bowling alley and lounge in the heart of Port Alberni that has operated from the same address for over 65 years. It runs multiple leagues catering to bowlers of various ages and skill levels, from senior afternoon leagues to evening sessions, and also offers pinball machines for a retro entertainment experience. A touring cyclist rolling through Port Alberni will find a well-established community gathering spot with a lounge on site.

visitor.name: Kelsey Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Kelsey Recreation Centre is the Village of Sayward's municipal recreation facility, housing a swimming pool, weight room, gymnasium, and multipurpose room. It is one of the few public recreation facilities in this remote stretch of northern Vancouver Island between Campbell River and Port McNeill. For touring cyclists riding the Island Highway corridor, it represents a rare inland stop in a small, isolated coastal community.

visitor.name: Kiišḥniqʷus Conservancy
visitor.desc: Kiišḥniqʷus Conservancy is a protected nature conservancy on Vancouver Island in British Columbia, situated in the traditional territories of First Nations peoples along the west coast of the island. As a BC Parks conservancy, it preserves natural ecosystems while permitting low-impact recreational activities. Its remote wilderness setting makes it a destination for touring cyclists exploring the wilder reaches of Vancouver Island.

visitor.name: Hope Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Hope Recreation Centre is a full-service municipal facility operated by the Fraser Valley Regional District in downtown Hope, BC, home to the Dan Sharrers Aquatic Centre featuring a 25-metre lap pool with diving boards, a leisure pool with spray features and rapids channel, and hot tub, sauna, and steam room. The complex also includes an arena, cardio and weight rooms, a fitness studio, and a conference centre. For touring cyclists, it offers a rare opportunity to access pool facilities, steam room, and full changerooms in a small interior BC gateway town.

visitor.name: Townsite Heritage Society
visitor.desc: The Townsite Heritage Society stewards the Powell River Townsite, a National Historic Site of Canada and one of the most intact examples of a planned early-20th-century mill town in North America. The heritage district features over 400 buildings dating from the 1910s onward, built to house workers at the Powell River paper mill. Touring cyclists exploring the Sunshine Coast will find the townsite an atmospheric stop with distinctive period architecture set along the waterfront.

visitor.name: Echo Aquatic and Fitness Centre
visitor.desc: The Echo Community Centre & Swimming Pool is a municipally operated aquatic and fitness facility in Port Alberni, a central Vancouver Island hub for cyclists travelling the Island or Alberni Valley routes. As a public sports centre with a swimming pool, it may offer showers and washrooms that would benefit touring cyclists, though specific amenities could not be confirmed from available sources. Port Alberni sits at the head of the Alberni Inlet and serves as a logical overnight or rest stop on multi-day island cycling itineraries.

visitor.name: Douglas Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Douglas Recreation Centre is a municipally operated community centre in the Township of Langley, BC. As a public recreation facility, it likely serves as a hub for fitness and community programming in the Lower Mainland's Fraser Valley region. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a useful stop, though specific amenities could not be confirmed from available sources.

visitor.name: Tourist Info
visitor.desc: The Fort Nelson Visitor Information Centre sits on the Alaska Highway at the edge of BC's Northern Rockies, a key stop for cyclists heading toward the Yukon. Located next to the recreation complex, Art Fraser Park, and the Fort Nelson Museum, it offers brochures, maps, a gift shop featuring local artists' work, and free Wi-Fi. Staff are knowledgeable about the Northern Rockies Regional Municipality and can help plan routes through this remote region.

detail.address: 5500 Alaska Hwy, Fort Nelson, BC V0C 1R0

visitor.name: Alpine Helicopters
visitor.desc: Alpine Helicopters is one of Canada's most established rotary-wing operators, in business since 1961 and running over 20,000 flight hours per year across seven Western Canada bases. The company specializes in scenic sightseeing tours of the Canadian Rockies alongside heli-skiing, wildfire management, and back-country rescue. A touring cyclist passing through the Columbia Valley or Kootenay region might consider a scenic flight as a dramatic add-on to their mountain route.

visitor.name: Blowhole
visitor.desc: The Blowhole is a natural coastal feature within Naikoon Provincial Park on Haida Gwaii, situated on the traditional territory of the Haida Nation near the northeastern tip of the island. Naikoon Park encompasses over 100 km of expansive remote beach and wilderness, making it a remarkable destination for adventurous touring cyclists who have made the journey to this remote archipelago. The surrounding wilderness is characterized by moist Pacific rainforest, dramatic headlands, and culturally significant Haida heritage sites.

visitor.name: Red Chairs
visitor.desc: Red Chairs is part of Parks Canada's signature program placing iconic red Adirondack-style chairs at scenic viewpoints throughout Canada's national parks, inviting visitors to pause and take in the landscape. This location sits within Kootenay National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site spanning glacially carved valleys, dramatic canyons, and fire-influenced grasslands along the historic Banff–Windermere Highway. For touring cyclists riding through the Rockies, it represents a photo-worthy and contemplative stop amid outstanding mountain scenery.

visitor.name: Clayton Falls
visitor.desc: Clayton Falls is a waterfall in BC's Cariboo, Chilcotin and Central Interior region, listed as a recreation site managed by BC Hydro. Located in one of BC's more remote and sparsely populated regions, it would serve as a scenic natural waypoint for touring cyclists on longer routes through the interior. The BC Hydro recreation site designation suggests some level of recreational infrastructure may be present, though details could not be confirmed.

visitor.name: Original Fort Langley Site
visitor.desc: The Original Fort Langley Site marks the location where the Hudson's Bay Company first established Fort Langley in 1827 at Derby Reach on the Fraser River, before the fort was relocated inland to its present site in 1840. Designated as part of Canada's national historic site network, this monument commemorates the origins of one of BC's most significant fur-trade era landmarks. The site sits within the broader Fraser Valley cycling corridor, making it of interest to history-minded touring cyclists passing through the Lower Mainland.

visitor.name: Tolkien Giant
visitor.desc: The Tolkien Giant is a massive ancient western redcedar (Thuja plicata) in Vancouver Island's central Walbran Valley, documented by the Ancient Forest Alliance as the ninth-widest western red cedar in British Columbia with a circumference of 14.4 metres and a height of 42 metres. It is a designated natural monument situated within a protected reserve, though nearby old-growth is under forestry pressure. For adventurous cyclists willing to travel deep into the Walbran, it represents a rare encounter with one of BC's most impressive living trees.

visitor.name: Stamp Falls Fish ladder
visitor.desc: Stamp River Park on central Vancouver Island is home to the Stamp Falls fish ladder, where thousands of Pacific salmon — sockeye, coho, and chinook — can be watched fighting their way upstream through autumn and into December. A short 0.5 km interpretive trail leads from the day-use parking area to the falls and fish ladder, with lookout points offering close-up views of the annual run. The salmon draw black bears to the riverbank as well, making this a genuinely wild and memorable stop for cyclists touring the Port Alberni area.

visitor.name: Ross Street Stage
visitor.desc: Ross Street Stage is a City of Salmon Arm-operated outdoor theater in the heart of downtown Salmon Arm, serving as the main venue for the summer Downtown Live music series. Every Saturday in summer, live performances coincide with the Downtown Farmer's Market, creating a lively cultural gathering point in the downtown core. The stage is also part of a broader downtown arts ecosystem that includes a registered busking program (BuskStop) and public art walking tours.

visitor.name: Salmon Arm Arts Centre
visitor.desc: Salmon Arm Arts Centre, operated by the Shuswap District Arts Council since 1970, is a downtown cultural hub housing the Salmon Arm Art Gallery, artist studios, and a 149-seat theatre. It runs a rich slate of programs including Theatre on the Edge, Wednesday on the Wharf, and the Salmon Arm Pride Project, making it a vibrant stop for travellers passing through the Shuswap. The centre sits in the heart of downtown, easily accessible and well-regarded as a community arts anchor in the BC interior.

detail.address: 70 Hudson Ave. NE, Salmon Arm, BC

visitor.name: Elkford Public Library
visitor.desc: Elkford Public Library is the community library serving Elkford, a small and remote municipality in the Kootenay Rockies near the headwaters of the Elk River. It provides public computers, digitization services, printing and scanning, and a broad range of community programs. For a touring cyclist riding through this isolated valley, it stands as one of the few publicly accessible indoor facilities in town.

detail.address: 816 Michel Road (Building C), Elkford BC V0B 1H0

visitor.name: Charles Bailey Theatre
visitor.desc: The Bailey Theatre is the primary performing arts venue for Trail and the surrounding Kootenays region, with a seating capacity of 721 and an intimate atmosphere where all seats have good sightlines. Operated by the Trail & District Arts Council, it hosts a wide range of events from major touring acts to classical and jazz series. A smaller adjacent space, the Muriel Griffiths Recital Room, accommodates 80–100 people for chamber performances, meetings, and community events.

notes.Café or food on site: Website states: 'Our bar and concession are open at most shows for your convenience, and our food and drink items are permitted in the theatre.' Available at most (not all) events

visitor.name: Kitty Coleman Woodland Gardens
visitor.desc: A 24-acre informal show garden near Courtenay featuring over 3,000 rhododendrons, bark mulch paths winding through natural forest, and numerous water features. Recognized as one of the world's finest informal show gardens and a Canada 150 Garden Experience, the gardens were hand-built by one man over decades. Located 15 minutes north of Courtenay just off the Old Island Highway, it also hosts annual art festivals and summer concerts.

notes.Café or food on site: Tea room listed as a visitor amenity on the visitors page

visitor.name: Chase Museum
visitor.desc: The Chase & District Museum & Archives is a non-profit community museum and archives that has preserved Shuswap regional history since 1987, surviving a 2011 fire and rebuilding under the motto 'From the Ashes.' It occupies a single-story accessible building and houses rotating exhibits, a historic Laviolette Cabin, archival photograph collections, and a gift shop stocked entirely by local artisans. Touring cyclists passing through Chase will find it a welcoming cultural stop, with admission by donation and engaging monthly scavenger hunts for all ages.

visitor.name: Silvery Slocan Museum
visitor.desc: The Silvery Slocan Museum occupies the historic former Bank of Montreal building on Main Street in New Denver, a community landmark for over 100 years. It showcases the Slocan Lake District's mining, logging, and agricultural heritage, highlighted by a recently restored Lancet motor launch. The museum also co-hosts the local Chamber of Commerce Visitor Info Centre, making it a natural cultural stop for cyclists passing through the Slocan Valley.

detail.address: Main Street, New Denver, BC V0G 1S0

visitor.name: Tourism Information & Municipal Campground Office
visitor.desc: The Logan Lake Municipal Campground is a 50-site lakeview facility operated by the District of Logan Lake, offering both powered RV sites and tent-only sites. Amenities include hot showers, free WiFi, potable water taps throughout the grounds, a fish cleaning station, and a boat launch on the lake. A bike park, mountain bike and hiking trails, two disc golf courses, and a golf course are all within walking distance.

detail.address: #1 Opal Drive, Logan Lake, BC V0K 1W0

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Website lists 'washrooms/hot showers' as an included campground amenity

visitor.name: Monarch Mountain/A Xéegi Deiyi Conservancy
visitor.desc: Monarch Mountain/A Xéegi Deiyi Conservancy is a BC Parks–managed protected area located immediately east of Atlin in northern BC, on the traditional territory of the Taku River Tlingit First Nation. The 5.3 km Monarch Mountain Trail—the most popular trail in the Atlin region—climbs from a trailhead on Warm Bay Road to summit views and culturally significant lakes used for spiritual activities. The conservancy also permits snowshoeing in winter and wildlife viewing throughout the summer.

visitor.name: The HUB
visitor.desc: The HUB is a community innovation centre founded in 2020 on Northern St'at'imc territory, serving Lillooet and surrounding communities as a space for collaboration, shared workspaces, and economic development. It operates a commission-based retail store at 633 Main Street showcasing locally made art, gifts, and products from regional artisans, making it a distinctive stop for visitors seeking locally sourced goods. The HUB also hosts gatherings, art shows, and supports community projects through its membership and project management services.

visitor.name: Barkerville, British Columbia
visitor.desc: Barkerville Historic Town & Park is a National Historic Site in BC's Cariboo region, built on the site of Billy Barker's legendary 1860s gold strike on Williams Creek that triggered a multi-billion-dollar industrial revolution. The preserved streetscape features more than 125 heritage buildings, costumed interpreters, and working historical displays, making it western North America's largest living history museum. Touring cyclists who make the journey into this remote mountain setting will find on-site campgrounds and accommodations alongside full immersion in a 19th-century Gold Rush town.

visitor.name: Daajing Giids Community hall
visitor.desc: The Daajing Giids Community Hall is a non-profit, volunteer-run community centre serving the town of Daajing Giids (formerly Queen Charlotte) on Haida Gwaii. It hosts a variety of local events including open mic nights, literacy awards, and community society meetings. For touring cyclists making the remote journey to Haida Gwaii, this hall represents a genuine community gathering point in a small, tight-knit island town.

detail.address: 134 Bay Street, Queen Charlotte, BC V0T 1S0

visitor.name: Garibaldi Park
visitor.desc: Garibaldi Park is a spectacular BC provincial park in the heart of the Coast Mountains, sitting astride the Sea to Sky corridor roughly 64 km north of Vancouver. The park's volcanic landscape features the 2,678 m summit of Mount Garibaldi, glacier-fed turquoise lakes, and more than 90 km of established trails ranging from day hikes to multi-day backcountry routes. Touring cyclists riding the Sea to Sky Highway (Highway 99) will find this iconic park a natural destination for side trips into world-class alpine terrain.

visitor.name: Sun Bowl Arena
visitor.desc: Sun Bowl Arena is Osoyoos's municipal ice facility, operated by the Town of Osoyoos in Canada's southernmost and warmest city. Situated in the Okanagan, it offers an indoor skating surface that serves the community for hockey, public skating, and events. For a touring cyclist passing through the hot, arid Okanagan, the arena can serve as a cool respite and a local recreation anchor.

visitor.name: Fort St. James National Historic Site
visitor.desc: Fort St. James National Historic Site preserves Canada's largest collection of faithfully restored wooden buildings from the fur trade era, set on the shores of Stuart Lake in north-central BC. Costumed interpretive staff bring Hudson's Bay Company life back to the present, and the site's famously quirky chicken races are a highlight of any summer visit. Free admission and a self-guided audio tour make it an accessible and memorable stop on a long-distance cycling route through the Cariboo and Central Interior.

detail.address: 280 Kwah Rd. West, Fort St. James, BC V0J 1P0

notes.Café or food on site: Website states 'dine at the Home Stretch Diner' on site

visitor.name: South Peace Community Multiplex
visitor.desc: The South Peace Community Multiplex is a municipal sports and recreation centre operated by the City of Dawson Creek in Northern BC. It serves as a community hub for athletics and leisure activities in the Peace River region. Touring cyclists passing through Dawson Creek — a key stop on routes through northeastern BC — may find it a useful rest point, though specific amenities could not be verified.

visitor.name: Sportsplex
visitor.desc: The Sportsplex is a City of Campbell River-operated indoor multi-sport facility located on South Alder Street. It is one of several municipal recreation venues in Campbell River, a hub community on northern Vancouver Island. Touring cyclists passing through may find it a useful stop given the typical amenities associated with a public sports centre, though specifics require direct verification.

visitor.name: ʔuuʔinmitis Conservancy
visitor.desc: ʔuuʔinmitis Conservancy is a protected nature reserve on Vancouver Island managed by BC Parks, with a name drawn from the Nuu-chah-nulth language reflecting the area's deep Indigenous cultural significance. As a conservancy rather than a developed provincial park, it preserves coastal wilderness in one of the more remote stretches of the island's west coast. Touring cyclists exploring the region may find it a worthwhile destination for its wild character.

visitor.name: CDRL: Likely Branch
visitor.desc: The Likely Branch is a small community library operated by the Cariboo Regional District Library system, serving the remote village of Likely in BC's Cariboo region. It is staffed by Community Librarian Beverly Fox and offers borrowing services, digital resources, and programmes as part of the broader CLN network. For touring cyclists passing through this isolated area along Keithley Creek Road, it represents one of the few publicly accessible indoor stopping points in the community.

detail.address: 6163 Keithley Creek Rd, Likely, BC, V0L 1N0

visitor.name: Parksville Curling Club
visitor.desc: Founded in 1991 and operating out of a converted arena since 2003, the Parksville Curling Club is a member-run community institution offering leagues, junior programs, and Learn to Curl sessions open to all ages and skill levels. The club welcomes groups of 1–60 for team-building events, birthday parties, and bonspiels, with a lounge and bar available year-round. For a touring cyclist, it offers a rare chance to experience one of Canada's most distinctively social sports in a welcoming small-town setting.

detail.address: 220 Corfield St N, Parksville, BC V9P 2S5

notes.Café or food on site: Website explicitly states 'our building, lounge, and bar are available to host your events throughout the year,' confirming a bar and lounge exist on site

visitor.name: Watson Lake Trailhead
visitor.desc: Watson Lake Trailhead provides access to the Watson Lakes Trail in Seven Sisters Provincial Park, a wilderness park situated between Terrace and Hazelton off Highway 16. The trail is an easy 3 km walk passing three small lakes with picnic sites, suitable for families and novice visitors, and offers fishing (rainbow trout), swimming in summer, and exceptional wildlife viewing including grizzly bears, mountain goats, and wolverines. Cyclists touring Highway 16 may find it a worthwhile detour into one of BC's more remote and scenic wilderness areas.

visitor.name: Martini Town
visitor.desc: Martini Town is an immersive holiday experience set on the backlot of a working Langley film studio, where meticulously constructed outdoor sets have served as backdrops for dozens of Hallmark-style Christmas productions. Open to the public only once a year during the holiday season, it features live entertainment, local artisan vendors, and themed food and drinks. Touring cyclists visiting Langley in late autumn or winter would find a festive, photo-worthy stop here, though advance tickets are required and no gate sales are available.

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'Food & Hot Drinks — Choose from a selection of comfort food and hot seasonal drinks to keep your entire party fed and in the holiday spirit.'

visitor.name: Ralph's Grove
visitor.desc: Ralph's Grove is an old growth cedar grove near Creston in the Kootenays, managed or formerly managed by the Trails for Creston Valley Society. The grove offers touring cyclists a short detour into towering ancient cedars, a striking contrast to the agricultural flats of the Creston Valley. It is a natural, undeveloped attraction with no built infrastructure confirmed.

visitor.name: qathet Museum and Archives Society
visitor.desc: The qathet Museum and Archives Society — formerly the Powell River Forestry Museum — preserves and presents the history of the qathet region on BC's Sunshine Coast. Housed on Marine Avenue in Powell River, it offers archival records and exhibits documenting the area's forestry, Indigenous, and settler heritage. Touring cyclists passing through Powell River will find it a worthwhile cultural stop in a town rich with industrial and maritime history.

visitor.name: Rotary Sport Field
visitor.desc: Rotary Sport Field is a fenced outdoor municipal sports facility in Maple Ridge, BC, associated with Samuel Robinson Technical School and managed by the City of Maple Ridge. It sits within the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley region, offering open recreational space for community sport. Touring cyclists in the area may find it a convenient open-air rest stop between destinations.

visitor.name: Nymph Falls Regional Nature Park
visitor.desc: Nymph Falls Regional Nature Park is a regional nature reserve managed by the Comox Valley Regional District, located along Forbidden Plateau Road near Courtenay on Vancouver Island. The park is named for a scenic waterfall on the Puntledge River and offers forested trails through old-growth woodland. It makes a worthwhile stop for touring cyclists riding through the Comox Valley.

visitor.name: Granisle Public Library
visitor.desc: Granisle Public Library is a small community library serving the remote village of Granisle on Babine Lake in northern BC. It functions as a local hub offering digital resources, programs, and a community history archive. For cyclists passing through this isolated stretch of northern BC, the library provides free WiFi that extends into its parking lot, along with public computers and printing.

detail.address: #2 Village Square, McDonald Avenue, Granisle, BC V0J 1W0

visitor.name: Hoodoos
visitor.desc: The Hoodoos are a natural geological formation within Yoho National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site straddling the western slopes of the Canadian Rockies near Field, BC. These distinctive erosion pillars are a compelling roadside attraction for cyclists riding the Trans-Canada Highway corridor through the park. The surrounding landscape features glaciers, waterfalls, and world-renowned Burgess Shale fossil sites, making this stretch a highlight of any Rocky Mountain touring route.

visitor.name: Eden Grove
visitor.desc: Eden Grove is an unprotected, 30-hectare ancient lowland forest in the Gordon River Valley within Pacheedaht First Nation territory, roughly 45 minutes from Port Renfrew. The grove contains towering old-growth western redcedars and Douglas-firs — some exceeding 13 feet in diameter — and a short trail with boardwalk sections winds through the forest. It sits adjacent to Big Lonely Doug, Canada's second largest Douglas-fir, making it a striking destination for cyclists exploring the Port Renfrew area.

visitor.name: Little River Regional Nature Park
visitor.desc: Little River Regional Nature Park is a nature reserve managed by the Comox Valley Regional District, situated in the Comox Valley on Vancouver Island. It forms part of the regional parks and trails network, offering natural green space in proximity to Courtenay and Comox. Touring cyclists passing through the Comox Valley may find it a worthwhile scenic detour along regional routes.

visitor.name: Viewing Tower
visitor.desc: The Viewing Tower is a public attraction located at the Alberni Harbour Quay in Port Alberni, a waterfront area on Vancouver Island. The quay is a municipal facility managed by the City of Port Alberni and serves as a focal point for visitors to the Alberni Inlet. A cycling tourist passing through Port Alberni might stop here to take in views of the inlet and surrounding mountains.

visitor.name: Creston & District Community Complex
visitor.desc: The Creston & District Community Complex is a publicly operated multi-sport recreation facility run by the Regional District of Central Kootenay, serving the Creston Valley. It hosts a broad range of activities including ice hockey, skating, curling, swimming, fitness, and pickleball under one roof. For a touring cyclist passing through the Kootenays, it represents a significant community hub with potential access to amenities typical of a full-service recreation complex.

visitor.name: Monck Park
visitor.desc: Monck Park is a BC provincial campground on the shore of Nicola Lake in the Thompson region, offering a wide range of recreational activities including camping, swimming, boating, fishing, and hiking in a hot, dry setting. The park protects a Ponderosa pine and bunchgrass ecosystem alongside a volcanic rock cliff landscape, making it an ecologically distinctive stop. Touring cyclists are permitted on park roads, and the park is described as a very popular family-oriented destination.

visitor.name: Hammond Outdoor Pool
visitor.desc: A municipal outdoor swimming pool in the Hammond neighbourhood of Maple Ridge, operated by the city's Parks & Recreation department. Part of Maple Ridge's network of recreation facilities, it offers a seasonal open-air swim experience convenient for cyclists on the Lougheed Highway corridor or exploring the Fraser Valley.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Website states 'Please Shower Before Swimming', confirming shower facilities on site

visitor.name: Lakelse Lake Provincial Park
visitor.desc: Lakelse Lake Provincial Park encompasses three separately accessible areas — Furlong Bay Campground, Lakelse Picnic Site, and Gruchy's Beach — all offering sandy beach access to a stunning lake framed by the Kitimat Mountain Range. The park preserves old-growth cedar, hemlock, and Sitka spruce forests thriving in Pacific-swept moist air, with easy hiking trails connecting coastal forest to salmon streams. Located about 20 km south of Terrace on Highway 37, it is a scenic and accessible destination in the Skeena River Watershed for touring cyclists passing through the North Coast corridor.

notes.Café or food on site: Ice cream stand located at Furlong Bay Campground, the main section of the park; open during operating season

visitor.name: Parksville & District Chamber of Commerce
visitor.desc: The Parksville & District Chamber of Commerce operates a staffed Visitor Centre on the East Island Highway, serving as the primary gateway for travellers exploring Parksville and the surrounding coastal region. Founded as the Parksville Board of Trade in 1935, the organization has deep roots in connecting visitors with local businesses, attractions, and hidden gems. Touring cyclists will find free maps, regional guides, expert local recommendations, and travel planning assistance from knowledgeable staff.

detail.address: 1275 E Island Hwy E, Parksville, BC V9P 2G3

visitor.name: Visitors Centre
visitor.desc: A tourism information office serving the Fort Langley area and broader Township of Langley, operated in connection with Tourism Langley, the regional destination marketing organization. Visitor centres of this type typically provide local maps, attraction guides, and trip-planning assistance for the Fraser Valley region. As a publicly accessible information hub, it is a natural stop for touring cyclists exploring the area.

visitor.name: Namgis Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Lawrence Ambers Memorial Recreation Centre is a community gathering facility operated by the 'Namgis First Nation in Alert Bay on Cormorant Island, accessible by BC Ferries from Port McNeill. It serves as the main recreation hub for 'Namgis community members and is available to rent for events by contacting the rec centre directly. Alert Bay itself is a culturally rich destination on the northern Vancouver Island ferry circuit, home to the U'mista Cultural Centre and significant First Nations heritage.

visitor.name: FVRL: Mount Lehman Library
visitor.desc: Mount Lehman Library is a small community branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system serving the rural Mount Lehman area east of Abbotsford. As a public library, it offers free WiFi, public computers, all-gender washrooms, and a 24-hour item return drop.
