It is a welcoming, accessible public space on a rural road corridor where amenities are otherwise sparse.

detail.address: 5875 Mount Lehman Road, Abbotsford, BC V4X 1V5

visitor.name: Mansons Hall
visitor.desc: Mansons Hall has served as the heart of community life on Cortes Island since 1922, operated by the Southern Cortes Community Association as a registered non-profit and federal charity. The facility includes a main hall with a professional stage, commercial kitchen, yoga studio, a free-use public computer station, and a retail boutique featuring local makers, alongside tenants such as the Mansons Landing Post Office and Cortes Community Radio. For a touring cyclist on Cortes Island, it is the central hub for live music events, the weekly Friday Market, and year-round community programming.

detail.address: 983 Beesley Road, Mansons Landing, BC V0P 1K0

visitor.name: Big Lonely Doug
visitor.desc: Big Lonely Doug is Canada's second-largest Douglas-fir — 69 metres tall with a 12-metre circumference — left standing alone after its surrounding ancient forest in the Gordon River Valley was clearcut in 2011, making it a striking symbol of old-growth loss. Located within Pacheedaht First Nation territory roughly 45 minutes from Port Renfrew, the tree stands adjacent to the unprotected Eden Grove, which features a short boardwalk trail through towering old-growth redcedars and Douglas-firs. For cycling tourists exploring the Port Renfrew big-tree circuit, it offers a sobering and visually arresting detour into a clearcut landscape dominated by a single colossal survivor.

visitor.name: Fraser Lake Museum
visitor.desc: The Fraser Lake Museum and Visitor Information Centre is housed in an original log home and presents exhibits on the rich history of the Fraser Lake area, including an informative display on Dakelh (Carrier) culture. Operated by the Village of Fraser Lake, it doubles as the community's official tourist information hub for visitors exploring regional outdoor activities such as canoeing, hiking, and trails at Mouse Mountain.

detail.address: PO Box 430, 210 Carrier Cres. Fraser Lake, BC V0J 1S0

visitor.name: Enderby & District Museum and Archives
visitor.desc: A community museum established in 1973 that tells the story of Enderby and the surrounding North Okanagan through changing and permanent displays, including a model of the town and railway station from 1905. Located in the City Hall complex right on Highway 97A, it also offers a self-guided historical walking tour of downtown Enderby and the Jim Watt Heritage Riverwalk along the river. Admission is by donation and the gift shop carries local history books and Secwepemc Cultural Education Society publications.

visitor.name: Radium Visitor Center
visitor.desc: The Radium Hot Springs Visitor Information Centre is a year-round community hub open 363 days a year, staffed by knowledgeable Visitor Information Counsellors who can provide directions, sightseeing tips, and local knowledge for the Columbia Valley. The centre houses wildlife displays, geographic exhibits, and Indigenous cultural history interpretation, making it an attraction in its own right. Touring cyclists can also purchase Parks Canada day or annual passes on site.

detail.address: 7556 Main Street East, Radium Hot Springs, BC

visitor.name: Mackenzie Public Library
visitor.desc: A public library housed inside the Mackenzie Recreation Centre, serving a small northern BC community of about 3,300 near Williston Lake — the largest man-made reservoir in North America. The library offers free computer and internet access, a seed library, a Library of Things with equipment and technology lending, and serves as a community hub with local event listings and information for the area.

visitor.name: Pouce Coupe Municipal Library
visitor.desc: A small-town public library in Pouce Coupe, in BC's Peace River region. Offers computer and printing access, a digital library through Libby/Overdrive, and research databases. A quiet indoor stop for touring cyclists passing through the northern Peace country.

visitor.name: Vancouver Island Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Vancouver Island Visitor Centre is the regional tourism hub for the Comox Valley, instantly recognizable by the full-scale CT-114 Tutor Jet (formerly Snowbird 5) displayed on its grounds just off the main highway. Inside, it features K'ómoks First Nation art, an exhibition gallery, and a gift shop, with knowledgeable staff ready to help plan local adventures. The outdoor picnic area and playground make it a pleasant rest stop, and it serves as the go-to resource for area maps, route ideas, and local recommendations.

visitor.name: Osoyoos Desert Society
visitor.desc: The Osoyoos Desert Society, also known as the Osoyoos Desert Centre, is a seasonal summer attraction and museum dedicated to Canada's only true desert ecosystem, located in the South Okanagan near Osoyoos, BC. It offers visitors an educational experience in one of the most ecologically unique landscapes in the country. Touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan Valley route will find it a distinctive cultural and natural history stop.

visitor.name: Mount Lehman
visitor.desc: Mount Lehman is a Canada Post post office serving the small rural community of Mount Lehman in the Fraser Valley east of Abbotsford. It offers standard postal services including parcel shipping, money orders, and PO box rental in a civic building. For touring cyclists passing through this quiet agricultural area, it provides a useful stop for mailing items home, receiving general delivery, or handling money services.

visitor.name: Mount 7 launch site 1
visitor.desc: Mount 7 is a prominent free flight site above Golden, BC, regularly hosting national hang gliding and paragliding competitions and drawing pilots from around the world. The Lookout launch area doubles as a public recreation site managed by Rec Sites and Trails BC, attracting cyclists, hikers, snowmobilers, and sightseers. The summit offers sweeping Rocky Mountain views and the access road was upgraded to 2WD-capable in 2000, making it reachable without a 4x4.

visitor.name: W.A.C. Bennett Dam Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The W.A.C. Bennett Dam Visitor Centre is operated by BC Hydro at one of Canada's largest earth-fill hydroelectric dams, situated in the Peace River region of Northern BC near Hudson's Hope. Cyclists tackling the remote roads of this corner of the province can stop to explore exhibits on the dam's construction and its role in BC's power grid. The site itself — overlooking the massive Williston Reservoir — is a striking destination in its own right.

visitor.name: Charles Richardson Nature Reserve
visitor.desc: Charles Richardson Nature Reserve is a protected natural area in Surrey, BC, catalogued in City of Surrey GIS data. As a nature reserve in the Lower Mainland, it likely offers trails and natural habitat for wildlife observation. Touring cyclists in the Fraser Valley area may find it a worthwhile off-bike detour.

visitor.name: Kitimat Centennial Museum
visitor.desc: The Kitimat Museum & Archives (originally the Kitimat Centennial Museum, opened 1969) preserves and shares the natural, cultural, and Indigenous history of Kitimat and the Haisla Nation, and is rated the #1 Indoor Attraction in Kitimat. It offers permanent and rotating exhibitions, an archival collection, visual arts galleries, educational programs, and a gift shop, making it a substantial cultural stop for cyclists passing through the region. The museum is committed to amplifying Haisla voices and history, operating on unceded Haisla territory.

visitor.name: Guest Services
visitor.desc: A guest services information office located in Sun Peaks Village, at the base of Canada's second-largest ski and mountain-bike resort. Sun Peaks operates a substantial bike park with lift-accessed trails, a pedal-access network, rentals, and guided tours, making this village the hub for a significant cycling destination in the Thompson-Okanagan region. Cyclists passing through can expect a well-developed resort village with multiple support services, though the specific offerings of this information office are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Lax Kw'alaams Recreation Centre and Pool
visitor.desc: The Lax Kw'alaams Reginald Sampson Recreation Centre is a full-service community facility operated by the Lax Kw'alaams Band in a remote First Nations community on BC's North Coast. It features a swimming pool with water-slide, lazy river, hot tub, and steam and dry saunas, alongside a gymnasium and a fully equipped fitness room with cardio and weight equipment. The centre also supports outdoor activities including kayaking and canoeing, and hosts the on-site Swimmer's Café.

detail.address: 1600 Church Street, Lax Kw'alaams, BC V0V 1H0

notes.Café or food on site: Website references 'Rec Center and Swimmer's Café Facebook page', indicating an on-site café called Swimmer's Café

visitor.name: The Zone
visitor.desc: The Zone is a youth centre in the Kootenays region of British Columbia, operated by New Life Church. As a community-focused facility run by a religious operator, it likely serves local youth programming and community gatherings. Touring cyclists passing through may find it a potential rest point, though services available to the general public are unconfirmed.

visitor.name: Surrey Sports & Leisure Complex
visitor.desc: A large City of Surrey municipal recreation complex offering a pool, arena, and weight room. Located on Fraser Highway in the Fleetwood-Tynehead area, it serves as a multi-sport hub for the surrounding community. Touring cyclists passing through Surrey's suburban corridor may find it a convenient stop for a swim or skate.

visitor.name: McLean Mill National Historic Site
visitor.desc: McLean Mill National Historic Site is a former steam-driven sawmill and logging camp complex designated a national historic site of Canada in 1989, comprising 35 historic buildings and structures on 12.8 hectares in the Alberni Valley. Visitors can explore the self-contained community of residences, offices, and industrial buildings at their own pace via a 24-stop heritage signage programme. The site also operates a campground with both serviced RV sites and rustic walk-in tent sites, making it a potential overnight destination for touring cyclists.

detail.address: 5633 Smith Road, Port Alberni, BC, V9Y 8M1

visitor.name: Comox Air Force Museum
visitor.desc: The Comox Air Force Museum and Heritage Air Park commemorates West Coast military aviation history from WWI through Afghanistan, with indoor galleries, hands-on exhibits including a CF-101 Voodoo ejection seat, and an outdoor air park featuring historic aircraft. Founded in 1982 and officially opened to the public in 1987 as an accredited Canadian Forces Museum, it is part of the national RCAF Museum Enterprise spanning 11 sites across Canada. Admission is by donation, and a research library with over 3,000 volumes is available for those interested in deeper history.

detail.address: Corner of Ryan Road and Military Row, 19 Wing Comox, Lazo, BC V0R 2K0

visitor.name: TNRL: Ashcroft Library
visitor.desc: The Ashcroft Library is a branch of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system serving this small Interior BC community. It holds the distinction of operating the first 'Service Extender' program in British Columbia, allowing registered patrons aged 15 and older to access the building for self-service borrowing outside of staffed hours using a keycard-style system. Cyclists passing through Ashcroft will find free public Wi-Fi, public computers, a bookable meeting room, and a fully wheelchair-accessible space.

detail.address: 201 Brink Street, Box 789, Ashcroft, BC V0K 1A0

visitor.name: Graceworks Gallery
visitor.desc: Graceworks Gallery is a gallery and retail shop located in Port Hardy, at the northern tip of Vancouver Island — the traditional endpoint for cyclists completing the full island route. The shop participates in regional tourism initiatives such as Vancouver Island North's Giveback Getaways program, reflecting its connection to the local visitor economy.

detail.address: 7210 - 5B Market Street, Port Hardy, BC V0N 2P0

visitor.name: Port Hardy Museum
visitor.desc: The Port Hardy Museum, operated by the Port Hardy Heritage Society, is a community museum housing permanent exhibits of First Nations artifacts—including pieces over 8,000 years old—alongside settlers' effects, fossils, geology, and local industry displays. Rotating temporary exhibits and videos complement the permanent collection. The gift shop features locally produced native art including silver jewelry and carvings, offering a tangible connection to the region's Indigenous heritage.

detail.address: 7110 Market Street, Box 2126, Port Hardy, B.C. V0N 2P0

visitor.name: Revelstoke Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Revelstoke Community Centre is the city's main municipally operated recreation hub, offering an aquatic centre, arena, fitness centre, meeting rooms, and outdoor ball and soccer fields. It sits adjacent to walking and biking trails, making it a natural waypoint for cyclists passing through Revelstoke. The facility is run by the City of Revelstoke Parks, Recreation & Culture department.

visitor.name: Al Anderson Memorial Pool
visitor.desc: Al Anderson Memorial Pool is a municipal aquatic facility operated by the City of Langley, offering public swimming, swimming lessons, and pool rentals. As a community recreation centre in the Lower Mainland, it serves as a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking a swim or a rinse after a long day on the road. The facility is listed as an active recreation venue on the City of Langley's official website.

visitor.name: Old Pemberton Meadows Schoolhouse / Pemberton Museum
visitor.desc: A restored heritage schoolhouse that is part of the Pemberton & District Museum & Archives complex, nestled in the Pemberton Valley on the traditional territory of the Lil'wat and St'át'imc Nations. The museum has been collecting, preserving, and sharing the region's heritage since 1982, with archives containing over 2,000 photographs, 700+ objects, and 250+ videos. Admission is by donation, making it an easy stop for touring cyclists passing through Pemberton on the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

visitor.name: Vanderhoof Tourism and Cultural Centre & Community Museum
visitor.desc: The Vanderhoof Tourism and Cultural Centre is situated on the museum grounds along Highway 16, making it a natural stop for cycle-tourers on the Yellowhead corridor. The site features a striking 12-metre wooden carving by master carver Peter Rodseth alongside historical exhibits from the Nechako Valley and Saik'uz First Nation. Visitor centre staff offer regional maps and travel information, and a 1.25 km Heritage Nature Trail loops through the museum grounds along Stoney Creek.

visitor.name: Stewart Public Library
visitor.desc: Stewart Public Library is the community hub of one of BC's most remote towns, situated at the end of Portland Canal roughly 350 km from the nearest large urban centre. The library serves both residents and visitors, offering internet access, an extensive digital collection, and a warm gathering space in a town known for its wildlife and dramatic scenery. A touring cyclist reaching Stewart will find this a rare opportunity for connectivity and a quiet rest in a very isolated corner of the province.

visitor.name: Kinuseo Falls
visitor.desc: Kinuseo Falls is a dramatic 60-metre waterfall in Monkman Provincial Park where the Murray River plunges over a geological fault — taller than Niagara Falls and widely considered the highlight of the park. The falls are accessible via Kinuseo Falls Road in the Hart Ranges of the Central Rocky Mountains, set within 62,867 hectares of alpine meadows, forested valleys, and rugged peaks. A wheelchair-accessible viewing platform provides impressive views, and a campsite with amenities sits nearby.

visitor.name: Wilfred Campbell Community Centre
visitor.desc: Wilfred Campbell Community Centre is a community facility located in the Boothroyd area of the Fraser Canyon in BC's Thompson region, likely serving the local First Nations community. The coordinates place it in a remote stretch of the canyon where services for touring cyclists are sparse. No detailed information about the centre's facilities or programming is publicly available online.

visitor.name: Kanaka Creek Watershed Stewardship Centre
visitor.desc: The Kanaka Creek Watershed Stewardship Centre, also known as the Bell-Irving Fish Hatchery, is an environmental education facility within Kanaka Creek Regional Park in Metro Vancouver's regional park system. Operated by the Kanaka Education and Environmental Partnership Society, it focuses on watershed stewardship and salmon habitat along Kanaka Creek. Touring cyclists exploring the Fraser Valley's regional trail network may find it a worthwhile nature stop en route through Maple Ridge.

visitor.name: Columbia National Wildlife Area
visitor.desc: Columbia National Wildlife Area is a federally protected nature reserve managed by Environment and Climate Change Canada, comprising four separate units — Wilmer, Spillimacheen, Brisco, and Harrogate — spread across the Rocky Mountain Trench in southeastern BC. It forms part of the broader Columbia Wetlands system, one of the longest undyked floodplain wetlands in North America and a critical Pacific flyway corridor for migratory waterfowl. Cyclists touring the Columbia Valley will find the area offers exceptional wildlife viewing, including rare and threatened wetland species, as a backdrop to riding through this dramatic mountain valley.

visitor.name: Golden Ears Park
visitor.desc: Golden Ears Park is one of BC's largest provincial parks, situated about an hour east of Vancouver in the Lower Mainland, and one of the province's most popular camping destinations. The park encompasses rugged backcountry mountains, coastal western hemlock forest, and Alouette Lake — a hub for paddling, swimming, and water sports. Its three large campgrounds and extensive trail network make it a significant destination for touring cyclists seeking wilderness access at the edge of Metro Vancouver.

visitor.name: TNRL: Cache Creek Library
visitor.desc: The Cache Creek Library is a branch of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library System, housed in a 2013-built, 1,672-square-foot building located directly on the Trans-Canada Highway. It is part of one of the larger regional library networks in British Columbia's interior, serving the small community of Cache Creek. For touring cyclists passing through this otherwise sparse stretch of highway, it offers free Wi-Fi and public computers as a rest-stop resource.

visitor.name: Dunster Train Museum
visitor.desc: The Dunster Station Museum is a heritage railway attraction in the small community of Dunster in BC's Robson Valley, preserving the history of the region's rail era. It operates in cooperation with a network of regional heritage institutions including the Central BC Railway & Forestry Museum and Valley Museum and Archives in nearby McBride. Cyclists touring the Robson Valley corridor between McBride and Valemount may find it a worthwhile cultural stop along the route.

visitor.name: CRDL: Big Lake Branch
visitor.desc: The Big Lake Branch is a small community library serving the rural Big Lake Ranch area in BC's Cariboo region, operating as one of 15 branches of the Cariboo Regional District Library. It provides access to books, eBooks, audiobooks, online databases, and community programming for residents and visitors in this remote interior location. For touring cyclists passing through this sparsely populated stretch of the Cariboo, it represents a rare publicly accessible facility with a named community librarian on site.

detail.address: 4056 Lakeview Rd, Big Lake Ranch, BC, V0L 1G0

visitor.name: World's Largest Paddle
visitor.desc: The World's Largest Paddle is a Guinness World Records-certified roadside attraction near Golden, BC — a locally crafted Western Red Cedar and LVL paddle scaled 13 times to over 60 feet, set against the backdrop of the Canadian Rockies and Columbia River Valley. Adjacent to the paddle is the Columbia Wetlands Outpost, where visitors can rent canoes, kayaks, SUPs, and pedal boats, or join a guided cataraft float through wetlands home to over 350 wildlife species. Located on Hwy 95 about 26 km south of Golden, it is a natural stop for cyclists touring the Columbia River corridor.

visitor.name: China Creek Campground & Marina
visitor.desc: China Creek Regional Park is a nature reserve managed by the Alberni-Clayoquot Regional District, located south of Port Alberni on Vancouver Island. The park sits along the Alberni Inlet, offering a natural stopover for cyclists touring the Highway 4 corridor between Port Alberni and the west coast.

detail.address: 2011 Franklin River Rd, Port Alberni, BC V0R 2B0

visitor.name: Powell River Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: The Powell River Recreation Complex is a large municipal hub offering two NHL-sized ice surfaces, a six-lane 25-metre aquatic centre with leisure and swirl pools, a fitness centre, and the 720-seat Evergreen Theatre. Adjacent to the complex is the Powell River Bike and Skateboard Park, a 1.5 km paved multi-use pathway, and hiking and biking trails throughout Millennium Park. For touring cyclists passing through Powell River, the complex provides change rooms and coin lockers alongside a well-connected outdoor trail network.

detail.address: 5001 Joyce Avenue, Powell River, BC V8A 5R2

notes.Luggage / bag storage: Website states 'coin lockers for safe keeping of valuables' are available in the Aquatic Centre change rooms

visitor.name: Comox Valley Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Comox Valley Aquatic Centre is a publicly operated indoor swimming facility run by the Comox Valley Regional District, serving residents and visitors across the Comox Valley on Vancouver Island. As a regional aquatic facility, it likely offers amenities typical of public swim centres — pool access, change rooms, and showers — making it a potential rest stop for touring cyclists seeking a swim or rinse-off. It sits on Lerwick Road in the Courtenay area, within easy reach of popular cycling routes on the Island.

visitor.name: Lilac Sun Pottery
visitor.desc: Lilac Sun Pottery is an artist's studio and gallery on Denman Island where the resident potter creates textured sculptural and functional ceramic pieces fired using wood, smoke, or electric kilns. The work is inspired by nature's constant changes and includes distinctive pieces such as wood-fired dishes with melted beach glass and textured flat vases. It is a distinctive cultural stop for cyclists exploring Denman Island's quiet rural roads.

detail.address: 3311 Denman Road, Denman Island, BC V0R 1T0

visitor.name: Radium Hot Springs
visitor.desc: Radium Hot Springs is a natural thermal pool operated by the Government of Canada on Highway 93, tagged in OSM as both a hot spring and a public swimming sports centre. It sits on a well-travelled cycling corridor between the Rockies and the Columbia Valley, making it a logical stop for riders crossing Sinclair Pass. Entry is fee-based and the facility is noted as wheelchair accessible.

visitor.name: Kynoch Adventures
visitor.desc: Kynoch Adventures is Bella Coola Valley's longest-running ecological interpretive tour company, founded in 2002 and now in its second generation of operation. The company specializes in guided grizzly bear viewing by raft on the Atnarko River in Tweedsmuir Park, wilderness eco-rafting on the Bella Coola River, and guided alpine and forest hikes in the Great Bear Rain Forest. For cyclists touring the Chilcotin Highway (Hwy 20), this is the primary outfitter for wildlife and wilderness experiences in one of BC's most remote and spectacular valleys.

detail.address: 1896 Hwy 20, Hagensborg, Bella Coola Valley, BC V0T 1H0

visitor.name: Alty Conservancy
visitor.desc: Alty Conservancy is a provincially protected nature conservancy managed by BC Parks, situated in the remote North Coast and Haida Gwaii region of British Columbia. As a conservancy designation, it balances conservation of natural and cultural heritage with low-impact recreation. Touring cyclists venturing into this remote coastal wilderness would encounter an undeveloped wild landscape typical of BC's northwest coast.

visitor.name: R.E.M. Lee Theatre
visitor.desc: The R.E.M. Lee Theatre is Terrace's largest performing arts venue, opened in 1975 and owned by the Coast Mountain School District 82, with a seating capacity of 691. It hosts a broad mix of professional and community productions — dance, theatre, music, convocations, and concerts — with over 70% of performances being locally driven. The venue also features a Mezzanine Gallery displaying work by local and regional artists, making it a cultural hub for the broader North Coast region.

visitor.name: Northern Rockies Regional Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: A municipal recreation centre in Fort Nelson on the Alaska Highway, serving as the community hub for sports, fitness, and aquatic activities. Facilities include a 25-metre lane pool, a leisure pool, a climbing wall, and a dry pad for court sports. For touring cyclists on the remote Alaska Highway corridor, this is one of the few full-service recreation facilities for hundreds of kilometres.

detail.address: 5500 Alaska Highway, Fort Nelson, BC V0C 1R0

visitor.name: Spirits of the West Coast
visitor.desc: Spirits of the West Coast Art Gallery has been curating Pacific Northwest Coast Indigenous artwork and jewelry since 2006, showcasing original masks, paddles, Haida argillite carvings, totem poles, and silver and gold jewelry by master carvers from Haida, Kwakwaka'wakw, Coast Salish, and Nuu-chah-nulth nations. The gallery hosts rotating exhibitions and offers both in-person and virtual gallery tours, making it a substantive cultural stop on Vancouver Island. Commissions for custom carvings and jewelry are also available.

visitor.name: 108 Heritage Site
visitor.desc: A heritage site and local history museum at 108 Mile Ranch preserving the story of the Cariboo Gold Rush era. The grounds feature over a dozen historic buildings including the McNeil Mansion Museum, a blacksmith shop, a chapel, and a trapper's cabin, all connected by the legendary Cariboo Waggon Road. Touring cyclists on Highway 97 between 100 Mile House and Williams Lake will find it a worthwhile cultural stop, with a gift shop and periodic markets and ghost tours adding variety.

detail.address: 4690 Telqua Drive, Box 225, 108 Mile Ranch, BC V0K 2Z0

visitor.name: Hope Bike Park
visitor.desc: Hope Bike Park is a large, free-admission public bike park in Hope, BC, designed for riders from beginner to expert with progression-focused terrain for both BMX and mountain biking. Set against forested hillsides and mountain scenery, the park has been operating since at least 2015 and receives ongoing professional trail maintenance from crews like Hoots Inc. It is a genuine cycling destination in the Fraser Valley, accessible to the public at no cost.

detail.address: 805 Kawkawa Lake Road, Hope, BC V0X 1L0

visitor.name: Revelstoke Museum
visitor.desc: The Revelstoke Museum & Archives is a two-floor history museum celebrating the heritage of Revelstoke and the surrounding Columbia River region, with exhibits spanning Indigenous peoples, early settlement, railways, mining, forestry, and multicultural history. It also stewards Revelstoke's only downtown Heritage Garden and offers audio tours, guided walking tours, and active archival research services. One UK visitor noted it 'punches way above its weight' for grounding travellers in the history and character of this mountain corridor.

visitor.name: Dixon Entrance Maritime Museum
visitor.desc: The Dixon Entrance Maritime Museum in Masset, Haida Gwaii, is housed in a historic 1914 building — the first on the islands with a concrete foundation, originally the island's first hospital. Its collections span commercial fishing, boat-building, whaling, and cannery history donated by local families, and it claims the oldest European-made artifact found in British Columbia, dredged near Langara Island. The museum also partners with the Council of the Haida Nation on language revitalization, weaving Indigenous and settler maritime heritage into a single compelling stop on Haida Gwaii.

visitor.name: Liz Stubbs Cutting Garden
visitor.desc: The Liz Stubbs Cutting Garden is a volunteer-tended flower garden tucked alongside the ocean within the nine-acre Filberg Park in Comox, named for a longtime local supporter of the park. Seasonal blooms grown from seed are arranged throughout the adjacent heritage lodge, and fresh bouquets are sold from a red flower cart near the on-site Summer Kitchen. The surrounding park is a free, publicly accessible green space featuring rare trees, rhododendrons, ocean views, and a heritage lodge — a pleasant off-bike stop on Vancouver Island.

notes.Café or food on site: Filberg Summer Kitchen is located on site immediately adjacent to the cutting garden; website references it as a place to 'grab a bite to eat' and lists a dedicated phone line (250.339.2750)

visitor.name: Chase Public Library
visitor.desc: Chase Public Library is part of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system and has served the Chase community since 1959, operating in its current 3,320-square-foot building since 1975 following renovations in 2003. Situated in the heart of Chase along the Shuswap corridor, it offers free Wi-Fi and public computers to all visitors, making it a practical rest stop for touring cyclists. The wheelchair-accessible facility is staffed and operates as a full-service branch of the regional library network.

detail.address: 614 Shuswap Avenue, Box 590, Chase, BC V0E 1M0

visitor.name: Village of Alert Bay Community Hall
visitor.desc: The Alert Bay Community Hall is the civic recreation hub of this small island community on Cormorant Island, accessible only by ferry. It houses a bowling alley and sits directly beside the Alert Bay Skate Park, which explicitly welcomes bikes alongside boards and scooters. For cyclists making the crossing to this culturally rich 'Namgis First Nation destination, the hall represents the primary community gathering and recreation facility.

detail.address: Cedar Street, Alert Bay, BC V0N 1A0

visitor.name: Nicola Valley Community Arts Centre
visitor.desc: The Nicola Valley Community Arts Centre is a volunteer-powered, non-profit arts hub in downtown Merritt operated by the Nicola Valley Community Arts Council. It brings together a rotating art gallery with near-monthly exhibitions, an artisan gift shop, and artist studio and clubhouse spaces under one roof. Touring cyclists passing through the Nicola Valley will find a genuine community gathering place celebrating local visual arts, music, and performing arts.

visitor.name: Hell's Gate Airtram
visitor.desc: Hell's Gate Airtram is a Swiss-built cable car that descends 157 metres into the dramatic Fraser Canyon gorge near Boston Bar, carrying up to 22 passengers per cabin at a time. Operating since 1970, it sits at one of BC's most geologically and historically significant spots — a 35-metre-wide passage where the full force of the Fraser River is squeezed through sheer canyon walls. At the gorge floor, visitors can explore a suspension bridge over the International Fishways, a fisheries exhibit, gold panning, and a fudge factory.

detail.address: 43111 Trans Canada Highway, Boston Bar, BC V0X 1L0

notes.Café or food on site: Simon's Cafe and Fudge Factory (up to 100 flavours made on site) are listed as on-site experiences at the gorge level

visitor.name: Alaska Highway Mile 0 Milepost
visitor.desc: The Alaska Highway Mile 0 Milepost in Dawson Creek marks the official southern terminus of the legendary Alaska Highway, one of the most iconic long-distance road routes in North America. For touring cyclists, it is a pilgrimage destination and a natural starting or finishing point for any northbound adventure into the Yukon and Alaska. The milepost anchors a heritage district that includes the Dawson Creek Visitor Information Centre and is the starting point for the city's self-guided Mile 0 Heritage Tour.

detail.address: 800 Hwy 2, Dawson Creek, BC V1G 3V8, Canada

visitor.name: Harris Landing Park
visitor.desc: Harris Landing Park is a wooded nature reserve in Maple Ridge, British Columbia, located near the Fraser River in the Lower Mainland. The 'Landing' in its name suggests historical or current riverfront access, offering a scenic natural stop for cyclists exploring the area. As a public nature reserve, it provides a quiet, forested environment along cycling routes through Maple Ridge.

visitor.name: Charles Jago Northern Sport Centre
visitor.desc: The Charles Jago Northern Sport Centre is a four-season fitness and recreation facility on the UNBC Prince George campus, open to community members, families, seniors, and students alike. It features modern fitness equipment, group fitness and drop-in classes, two squash courts, pickleball, and the only indoor running track in northern British Columbia. Touring cyclists passing through Prince George could potentially use the facility for recovery workouts, though cyclist-specific services are not documented on the website.

detail.address: 3333 University Way, Prince George, BC V2N 4Z9

visitor.name: Gibson Pass Ski Area
visitor.desc: Gibson Pass Ski Area is the alpine ski and snowboard zone at Manning Park Resort, set in the Cascade Mountains along Highway 3 between Hope and Princeton—a major touring corridor in southern BC. The resort is a four-season destination drawing over one million visitors annually, with summer hiking, camping at Lightning Lake, and on-site lodging and dining that make it a natural waypoint for long-distance cyclists. In winter the area offers short lift lines and views across the Cascade range; in summer the infrastructure (lodge, restaurant, pub, campground) remains active and accessible.

notes.Café or food on site: Multiple food and beverage venues

visitor.name: Yoho National Park Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Yoho National Park Visitor Centre is the primary information hub for Yoho National Park, situated along the Trans-Canada Highway in Field, B.C. on the western slopes of the Great Divide. The centre is the gateway to one of Canada's most spectacular mountain parks, home to the UNESCO World Heritage Burgess Shale fossil sites, Lake O'Hara, and a network of trails through glacier-carved peaks and waterfalls. Touring cyclists crossing the Rockies on the Trans-Canada will find it an essential stop for current trail conditions, wildlife advisories, and park regulations.

visitor.name: CRDL: Quesnel Branch
visitor.desc: The Quesnel Branch of the Cariboo Regional District Library is a publicly accessible branch library operated by the Cariboo Regional District, serving Quesnel and the surrounding central interior. Part of a 15-branch regional network, it hosts regular community programming including book clubs, craft clubs, chess clubs, and author events. Located in downtown Quesnel, it sits along a key hub town on the interior touring corridor between Prince George and Williams Lake.

visitor.name: Quesnel Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Quesnel Visitor Centre is the official tourism information office for Quesnel, a community at the confluence of the Quesnel and Fraser rivers in BC's central interior. It serves as a regional trip-planning hub with resources covering mountain biking, trails, fishing, outdoor adventure, and local dining. Touring cyclists passing through the Cariboo would find it a useful stop for local maps, itinerary ideas, and knowledge of the area's extensive trail network.

visitor.name: Wakepilot
visitor.desc: Wakepilot is a premium watersports rental and charter company on Osoyoos Lake — the warmest lake in Canada — with over 20 years of operation and three lakefront locations. They offer Sea-Doo, boat, SUP, kayak, and e-foil rentals alongside wakeboard and surf charters using Supra SA wake boats. Their 2024 Wine Tour by Boat package combines boating with stops at South Okanagan wineries, making it a distinctive activity for touring cyclists who reach the Osoyoos wine country.

detail.address: 8000 45 Street, Osoyoos, BC (one of three lakefront locations; see website)

visitor.name: Taylor Public Library
visitor.desc: Taylor Public Library is a small community library serving the District of Taylor in Northern BC's Peace River region. It offers a range of public services including computer and internet access, interlibrary loans, photocopying, and programs for all ages. For touring cyclists passing through this remote northern corridor, it provides a welcoming public space with free Wi-Fi.

visitor.name: sports center 1 (sc1)
visitor.desc: A seasonal multi-sport facility in the Comox Valley operated under the Comox Valley Regional District, tagged in OSM for ice skating, ice hockey, and lacrosse. The unusual name 'sports center 1 (sc1)' suggests it may be an internal or informal designation rather than a public-facing name. As a seasonal ice facility it may offer limited year-round utility to touring cyclists.

visitor.name: Globe Theatre
visitor.desc: The Globe Theatre is a theatre venue located in Atlin, a remote community in far northern British Columbia near the Yukon border. Atlin itself is a historic gold-rush town accessible via a long gravel spur road, making it a notable destination for adventurous touring cyclists. The theatre represents a cultural anchor in one of BC's most isolated communities.

visitor.name: Valemount Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Valemount Visitor Centre is the official tourism information hub for this mountain village nestled among the Rocky, Monashee, and Cariboo Mountains in the Robson Valley. It is a natural first stop for touring cyclists given Valemount's active cycling culture, including the Valemount Mountain Bike Park spanning two local mountains and the annual Spring Bike Fest. Staff provide local knowledge, maps, and trip-planning resources for the surrounding mountains and trails.

detail.address: 785 – A Cranberry Lake Rd, Valemount, BC V0E 2Z0

visitor.name: Kynoch Adventures
visitor.desc: A locally owned wilderness tour company in Bella Coola Valley offering guided grizzly bear viewing on the Atnarko River, eco-rafting on the Bella Coola River, alpine hiking, and trail running camps in the Great Bear Rainforest. Founded in 2002 by a professional biologist, it is the longest-running adventure tour operator in the valley. Bella Coola sits at the western end of Highway 20, a legendary cycling route across the Chilcotin Plateau.

visitor.name: Hudson's Hope Public Library
visitor.desc: Hudson's Hope Public Library is a small community library serving one of northern BC's more remote towns, offering digital lending through Libby and a locally significant archive known as the Leo Rutledge Historical Collection. The library provides computer and printing services and is committed to accessible digital services, including resources for patrons with print disabilities. For a touring cyclist passing through this isolated community, it represents a rare opportunity for internet access and a welcoming indoor rest stop.

visitor.name: Hardy Mtn Trail
visitor.desc: Hardy Mtn Trail is an OSM-tagged attraction located near Grand Forks in the Okanagan-Boundary region of BC. The area is served by the Grand Forks Community Trails Society, which since 2001 has developed and maintains over 75 km of trails open to cyclists, pedestrians, and other non-motorized users. However, this specific trail does not appear in the GFCTS trail inventory, and little detail is available about its character, length, or condition.

detail.address: Hardy Mountain Road, Grand Forks, BC

visitor.name: Skydive Extreme Yeti
visitor.desc: Skydive Extreme Yeti is a tandem skydiving drop zone operating at Golden Municipal Airport in the heart of the Canadian Rockies, offering jumps from up to 13,000 feet AGL — one of the highest tandem skydives in Western Canada. The dropzone sits at the confluence of the Kicking Horse and Columbia Rivers, surrounded by six national parks including Yoho and Glacier. In operation since 2011, it draws adventure travelers from Banff, Lake Louise, and beyond, making it a notable landmark stop for cyclists touring the Trans-Canada corridor.

visitor.name: Telkwa Reading Room
visitor.desc: The Telkwa Reading Centre is a volunteer-staffed community library nestled beside the spectacular Bulkley River in the historic Village of Telkwa. The centre offers books, programs, and events for all ages, and its riverside setting makes it one of the more scenic library stops in northern BC. It serves as a cultural waypoint on Highway 16 between Smithers and Prince George.

visitor.name: Chetwynd Public Library
visitor.desc: A community public library in Chetwynd, a small town on the Alaska Highway corridor in northern BC. The library offers computer and internet access, meeting rooms, printing and scanning services, and a wide range of programs. Chetwynd is known as the 'Chainsaw Sculpture Capital of the World,' and the library serves as a good rest stop and information point for cyclists passing through the Peace Region.

detail.address: 4522 North Access Road, Chetwynd, BC V0C 1J0

visitor.name: Kaslo Community Garden
visitor.desc: The Kaslo Community Garden is a collectively managed growing space operated by the Kaslo Community Garden Society, situated in the historic lakeside village of Kaslo in British Columbia's West Kootenays. Community gardens like this are typical stopping points for touring cyclists passing through small towns, offering a quiet green space amid Kaslo's scenic mountain and lake surroundings. The garden reflects Kaslo's strong community character and self-reliance ethos.

detail.address: 100 Washington St, Kaslo, BC V0G 1M0, Canada

visitor.name: Forward Harbour/ƛəx̌əʷəyəm Conservancy
visitor.desc: Forward Harbour/ƛəx̌əʷəyəm Conservancy is a protected wilderness area on Vancouver Island in BC's South Central Coast region, managed by BC Parks. The conservancy carries cultural significance for Indigenous Peoples and is acknowledged in BC Parks' ongoing reconciliation work. Hunting is permitted during open season under BC regulations, making it a destination for backcountry users venturing into this remote coastal landscape.

visitor.name: Field Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Field Community Centre serves as the social hub of Field, BC, a small mountain village nestled inside Yoho National Park along the Trans-Canada Highway. Situated at roughly 1,240 metres elevation amid dramatic Rocky Mountain scenery, it is one of the few community facilities available to travellers in this remote corridor. Touring cyclists on the Trans-Canada route may find it a welcome waypoint between Golden and Lake Louise.

visitor.name: Capitol Theatre
visitor.desc: The Capitol Theatre is a historic performing arts venue in Port Alberni's downtown, owned and operated by Portal Players Dramatic Society, an all-volunteer charitable non-profit. The society stages live theatre productions — from classic drama to youth performances — in a building with roots dating to 1936, making it a cultural landmark in the Alberni Valley. Touring cyclists passing through Port Alberni can catch locally produced live theatre, with box office sales open before each performance.

detail.address: 4904 Argyle Street, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 1V7

visitor.name: Colombo Lodge
visitor.desc: Colombo Lodge is a two-storey brick community hall built in 1927 in Trail, BC, operated by the Cristoforo Colombo Lodge, an Italian-Canadian fraternal organization with deep roots in the region's mining heritage. The building is recognized by Heritage BC as a significant cultural landmark in the Columbia Basin. Touring cyclists passing through the Kootenays will find it a notable piece of the area's immigrant and labour history.

visitor.name: Fanny Bay Community Hall
visitor.desc: Fanny Bay Community Hall is a community centre in Fanny Bay, a small coastal settlement on Vancouver Island's east coast along the South Island Highway. Community halls in small BC towns typically serve as the social hub for local events, meetings, and gatherings. Touring cyclists riding the Island corridor pass directly through Fanny Bay and may find this a useful landmark or rest stop.

visitor.name: Moose Lake
visitor.desc: Moose Lake is a natural lake within or adjacent to Mount Robson Provincial Park, situated along the Yellowhead Highway (Highway 16) corridor in eastern BC. The park is one of BC's most celebrated destinations, anchored by Mount Robson at 3,954 m — the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies. Cyclists riding the Yellowhead route pass directly through this dramatic mountain landscape.

visitor.name: Cumberland Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: Cumberland Recreation Centre is a municipal community centre in the heart of the Village of Cumberland, a small town on Vancouver Island well known for its mountain biking trails and outdoor culture. The facility includes a climbing wall and offers drop-in programs and adult social activities. Touring cyclists passing through the Comox Valley will find it centrally located on Dunsmuir Avenue, Cumberland's main street.

visitor.name: Dixon Entrance Maritime Museum
visitor.desc: The Dixon Entrance Maritime Museum in Masset, Haida Gwaii, is dedicated to the maritime history of the Dixon Entrance — the international strait separating Haida Gwaii from Alaska. It occupies a dedicated building on Harrison Avenue in one of the most remote cycling destinations in British Columbia. Cyclists who make it to the north end of Haida Gwaii would find this a fitting stop to absorb the seafaring heritage of the region.

visitor.name: Blaauw Eco Forest
visitor.desc: A mixed and coniferous forest preserve in Langley's Glen Valley lowlands, with ponds, a bog, and over 300 documented species of plants, fungi, and lichen. Donated by the Blaauw family to Trinity Western University for public use, education, and research, the forest is protected by a Township of Langley covenant. A quiet stop for a touring cyclist passing through the Fraser Valley, with walking trails through rare habitats including red-legged frog wetlands.

visitor.name: Fairmont Hot Springs Pools
visitor.desc: Fairmont Hot Springs Pools is the signature natural geothermal swimming attraction of Fairmont Hot Springs Resort, a year-round Rocky Mountain resort in BC's Kootenay region. The broader resort complex includes multiple dining options, a spa, golf, and ski access, making it a substantial destination stop rather than a quick roadside break. Its location along the Columbia Valley corridor places it within reach of several well-travelled touring routes.

detail.address: 5225 Fairmont Resort Road, Fairmont Hot Springs, BC V0B 1L1

notes.Café or food on site: Website lists multiple on-site dining venues including Steamers Café, Bear's Paw Bar & Grill, Antlers at the Lodge, and others

visitor.name: ORL: Falkland Branch
visitor.desc: The Falkland Branch is a small rural outpost of the Okanagan Regional Library, a 30-branch network serving over 399,000 people across the Thompson-Okanagan region. Located directly on Highway 97, it offers public computers, seating, and Wi-Fi that extends outside the building. The branch hosts regular community events including gaming groups and craft workshops, making it a genuine community hub in a small town.

notes.Wi-Fi: Website states: 'WIFI is available inside and outside of the branch from approx. 7am to 10pm daily.'

visitor.name: Langley Sportsplex
visitor.desc: Langley Sportsplex is a major indoor recreation complex housing four ice hockey rinks — described on its own website as the only facility of its kind in Canada — along with a fitness centre, sports equipment retail, health clinics, daycare, and the Offside Cafe. Located roughly 30 minutes from downtown Vancouver, it draws over half a million visitors annually and hosts leagues, tournaments, public skating, training programs, and summer day camps. Touring cyclists in the Fraser Valley would find a sizable hub with on-site food and multiple services, though the facility has no evident cycling focus.

notes.Café or food on site: Offside Cafe named as an on-site tenant in the /advertise subpage; /day-camps page instructs families to order lunch from 'the Offside Café' via phone ext. 702

visitor.name: Ancient Forest / Chun T'oh Whudujut Provincial Park
visitor.desc: Ancient Forest / Chun T'oh Whudujut Provincial Park protects a portion of the only inland temperate rainforest in the world, located on Highway 16 midway between Prince George and McBride. Touring cyclists can explore thousand-year-old western redcedars via a 450-metre universal access boardwalk and an additional 2.3 km of boardwalk leading to old-growth giants and a cascading waterfall. The park sits in the traditional territory of the Lheidli T'enneh and is considered one of BC's must-see hiking destinations.

visitor.name: Bear Island Conservancy
visitor.desc: Bear Island Conservancy is a 317-hectare BC Parks protected area on the shores of Babine Lake, about 60 km east of Smithers, encompassing approximately 4 km of lakeshore and two islands. Established in 2008, it incorporates a former Forest Service recreation site that continues to operate as a vehicle-accessible campground especially popular during the August Sockeye salmon fishery. Visiting cyclists should be aware that the access road is a steep gravel descent and no potable water is available on site.

visitor.name: Gambier Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Gambier Community Centre is a registered charity and the only public facility on Gambier Island, the largest island in Howe Sound, BC, home to roughly 100 permanent residents year-round. The island has no car-ferry access — only a passenger ferry runs between Langdale and New Brighton — giving it a distinctly remote, low-traffic character that touring cyclists who make the crossing would find unusual. As the island's sole community hub, the centre organizes events and is the only place on the island where credit and debit cards are accepted.

visitor.name: Elk Lakes Park
visitor.desc: Elk Lakes Park is a wilderness provincial park set within the western ranges of the southern Rocky Mountains, featuring sub-alpine landscapes, remnant glaciers, rugged peaks, and productive fishing lakes. It offers a range of hiking experiences on maintained trails suitable for families with some backcountry experience, as well as off-trail routes for experienced alpine travelers. A rustic cabin—Elk Lakes Cabin—is available for reservation through the Alpine Club of Canada, making it a viable backcountry destination for multi-day touring cyclists.

visitor.name: Vanderhoof Aquatic Centre
visitor.desc: The Vanderhoof Aquatic Centre is a YMCA BC-operated community sports and aquatics facility in Vanderhoof, a small town in BC's Central Interior roughly midway between Prince George and Smithers. The facility offers swimming programs, aqua-fit classes, and fitness services, making it one of the more comprehensive recreational facilities in this remote corridor. For touring cyclists passing through the region, it represents a potential stop for post-ride recovery in an area with limited amenities.

visitor.name: Phillips Estuary/ʔNacinuxʷ Conservancy
visitor.desc: Phillips Estuary/ʔNacinuxʷ Conservancy protects 1,461 hectares of marine, estuary, lake, and river environments at the head of Phillips Arm on BC's Southern Central Coast, about 53 km north of Campbell River. Established in 2007 following Government-to-Government discussions with First Nations, it offers fishing for all five salmon species and wildlife viewing in a largely undeveloped wilderness setting. There are no developed trails, and cyclists are restricted to roadways within the conservancy.

visitor.name: San Juan Spruce
visitor.desc: The San Juan Spruce is Canada's largest Sitka spruce and the second largest in the world, standing 62.5 metres tall with a circumference of 11.7 metres alongside the San Juan River near Port Renfrew on Vancouver Island. It is an unmanaged natural landmark accessible via a forest setting, roughly 35 minutes from Port Renfrew. Touring cyclists exploring the old-growth forests of southwestern Vancouver Island may detour to see this record-breaking ancient tree.

detail.address: Juan de Fuca, BC V0S 1K0, Canada

visitor.name: Fraser Lake Visitor's Center
visitor.desc: The Fraser Lake Museum and Visitor Information Centre occupies a heritage log home that is itself a fine example of traditional construction. The museum displays artifacts from the rich history of the Fraser Lake area, including an informative exhibit on Dakelh culture. For touring cyclists passing through BC's Central Interior, this is a welcoming stop for local knowledge and regional context.

detail.address: PO Box 430, 210 Carrier Cres. Fraser Lake, BC V0J 1S0

visitor.name: Nang Xaldangaas Heritage Site/Conservancy
visitor.desc: A BC Parks heritage site and conservancy on the northern tip of Graham Island, Haida Gwaii, directly west of Old Massett and Masset. The area holds deep Haida cultural significance with 32 archaeological sites, numerous culturally modified trees, shell middens, and plank house remains, plus a Haida Watchmen camp at George Point in Naden Harbour. It also provides important habitat for Northern goshawks, marbled murrelets, and common murres.

visitor.name: Bijoux Falls Provincial Park
visitor.desc: Bijoux Falls Provincial Park is a day-use rest stop along Highway 97, located 44 km north of McLeod Lake in northern BC, centered on a dramatic cascading waterfall viewable from a fenced overlook. The park is a natural photography stop and wildlife-watching spot, hosting a notable summer population of Stellar's Jays. Basic facilities — toilets and picnic tables — make it a practical break point for cyclists traveling the Highway 97 corridor.

visitor.name: Hurford Hill Nature Park
visitor.desc: Hurford Hill Nature Park is a 10.7-hectare urban nature reserve donated to the City of Courtenay in 1996 and protected in perpetuity by the Comox Valley Land Trust. It forms a critical link along the Valley View Greenway and shelters native species alongside Glen Urquhart Creek's salmon habitat. Cycling is explicitly encouraged within the park, making it a worthwhile green-space stop for cyclists travelling the Comox Valley.

visitor.name: TNRL: Barriere Library
visitor.desc: The Barriere Library is a branch of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system serving the small community of Barriere in BC's Thompson Country. It offers public computers, Wi-Fi, printing, and wheelchair-accessible premises. A notable feature is the adjacent StoryWalk® in Fadear Park next door, where pages of a rotating children's picture book are installed outdoors for a combined walking-and-reading experience.

detail.address: 4511 Barriere Town Road, Box 100, Barriere, BC V0E 1E0

visitor.name: Clearwater Wells Gray Park Visitors Centre
visitor.desc: The Clearwater Wells Gray Park Visitors Centre is operated by Information Wells Gray, a non-profit organization serving as the primary information hub for Wells Gray Provincial Park — one of BC's largest wilderness parks at over 5,000 km². Touring cyclists passing through Clearwater can access up-to-date trail reports, road conditions, and park regulations, as well as guidance on camping, canoeing, hiking, and wildlife. The centre is the logical first stop for anyone planning to explore the park's iconic waterfalls, backcountry routes, or hut-to-hut trail system.

visitor.name: Jamieson Woods Nature Preserve
visitor.desc: Jamieson Woods Nature Preserve is a public nature reserve near Hudson's Hope in northern BC, notable for its ancient sand dunes and likely old-growth aspen forest. Listed among the district's trail network, it sits in a remote and scenic part of the Peace River region that touring cyclists on northern BC routes may pass through.

visitor.name: Beaver Lodge Forest Lands
visitor.desc: Beaver Lodge Forest Lands is a 520-hectare public forest within the city of Campbell River, featuring diverse habitats including stands with old-growth characteristics such as Douglas-fir, western redcedar, and Sitka spruce. Originally donated in 1931 as one of BC's first operational forest plantations, it is now protected under its own provincial legislation and offers a network of trails for walking, running, and cycling. The Greenways Loop trail connects through the forest lands, making it an accessible natural stop for touring cyclists passing through Campbell River.

detail.address: PO Box 22015 RPO Dogwood, Campbell River, BC V9W 8G7

visitor.name: McMillan Creek Park
visitor.desc: McMillan Creek Regional Park is a free public natural area in Prince George where McMillan Creek flows through a forested ravine of Douglas fir on its way to the Nechako River cutbanks. Visitors can choose between a 2.5 km trail or a shorter 1 km route leading to a scenic overlook of the river and the city beyond. The creek is a protected rainbow trout spawning habitat with special provincial fishing regulations, and interpretive signage explains the ecology along the way.

visitor.name: World's Largest Tree Crusher
visitor.desc: The World's Largest Tree Crusher is a landmark outdoor display in Mackenzie, BC, showcasing a massive piece of industrial equipment once used to clear old-growth forest during the region's development era. It is a free, open-air roadside attraction that draws visitors curious about the industrial heritage of British Columbia's northern interior.

visitor.name: Aldergrove Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Aldergrove Community Centre is a large Township of Langley recreation facility featuring an aquatic complex with a wave pool, waterslides, diving boards, hot tub, and sauna, alongside an ice arena and fitness centre. Extensive accessibility infrastructure includes a portable aquatic lift and water wheelchair ramp into the social pool. A touring cyclist would find showers, change rooms, washrooms, and multiple food options within a single facility.

notes.Showers (drop-in or fee): Change rooms with handheld shower head explicitly listed in website amenities; facility admission likely required to access
notes.Café or food on site: Website lists 'food truck' under amenities and Triple O's (604-857-1514) as a leased tenant space within the building

visitor.name: Strike Zone Bowling and Mini Golf
visitor.desc: Strike Zone is a long-running Prince George institution founded in 1994, offering 16 lanes of 10-pin bowling alongside an 18-hole themed indoor glow-in-the-dark mini golf course and an arcade — all under one roof with no reservations required. It is one of the few combined bowling-and-mini-golf venues in BC's central interior, making it a distinctive stop for touring cyclists seeking an off-bike activity in Prince George.

detail.address: 2366 Westwood Drive, Prince George, BC V2N 4H3

visitor.name: Seal Bay Regional Nature Park
visitor.desc: A regional nature park on Vancouver Island near Courtenay, managed by the Comox Valley Regional District and also known by its Indigenous name Xwee Xwhya Luq. The park offers a natural coastal forest experience in the Comox Valley, making it a worthwhile side trip for cyclists touring the east coast of Vancouver Island.

visitor.name: Houston Public Library
visitor.desc: The Houston Public Library is a community public library serving the small town of Houston in BC's Central Interior, offering books, digital resources, computer and internet access, meeting room rentals, and office services including printing, copying, faxing, and scanning. For touring cyclists passing through this remote stretch of highway, it provides a sheltered stop with free internet access and a range of community resources. The library also curates local community information links, making it a useful orientation point for visitors unfamiliar with the region.

visitor.name: Little Hell's Gate Regional Park
visitor.desc: Little Hell's Gate Regional Park is a TNRD-managed regional park in the North Thompson corridor, named for its dramatic canyon scenery reminiscent of the famous Hell's Gate on the Fraser River. Sitting at roughly 51.9°N near the confluence of rugged interior BC geography, it is tagged as a viewpoint in OpenStreetMap, suggesting a scenic overlook experience. Touring cyclists riding through the Cariboo, Chilcotin and Central Interior region may find it a worthwhile detour for the views.

visitor.name: Houston Leisure Centre
visitor.desc: Houston Leisure Centre is a municipal recreation facility operated by the District of Houston in northern BC's Bulkley Valley. It features a swimming pool and offers programs for both residents and visitors. For touring cyclists on Highway 16, it may provide a welcome stop for recreation and refreshment in this small community.

visitor.name: Kʷuḥaa Conservancy
visitor.desc: Kʷuḥaa Conservancy is a BC Parks-managed nature conservancy on Vancouver Island, protecting significant natural and cultural values in the coastal wilderness near latitude 49.4°N. Conservancies in BC permit compatible low-impact recreation alongside conservation objectives, making them potential waypoints for adventure-touring cyclists exploring the island's remote western reaches. The Indigenous name reflects the area's connection to First Nations whose territories encompass this land.

visitor.name: ORL: Golden & District Library
visitor.desc: The Golden & District Library is a branch of the Okanagan Regional Library, serving the Golden community in BC's Columbia Valley as part of one of Canada's larger regional library networks. It houses an ORL Makerspace equipped with an Audio Recording Studio, Creation Station, Digitization Stations, Video Recording Equipment, and a Cricut cutting machine. Free car parking is available both in front and behind the building, and a book drop bin is accessible on the exterior when the library is closed.

visitor.name: Gibsons Beach Access
visitor.desc: Gibsons Beach is a public ocean beach on the northern edge of Powell River near the Wildwood neighbourhood, offering a mix of sand and rocky shoreline along the Salish Sea. It is less busy than the city's main Willingdon Beach and is popular for beachcombing, family picnics, and exploring the tideline. A small boat launch is also present, making it a quiet, multi-use foreshore stop.

detail.address: Gibsons Beach Rd, Powell River, BC

visitor.name: Prince Rupert Visitor Information Centre
visitor.desc: Prince Rupert Visitor Information Centre is the official tourism information hub for Prince Rupert, BC — a coastal city on British Columbia's wild North Coast that serves as a gateway to the Great Bear Rainforest, world-class fishing, and rich Ts'msyen cultural heritage. The centre provides maps, brochures, and downloadable guides covering hiking trails, wildlife viewing, outdoor adventure, and local dining, and also offers phone and email visitor services. For a touring cyclist arriving by BC Ferries or venturing through this remote northern destination, it is a practical first stop for trip planning and local orientation.

visitor.name: Terrace Public Library
visitor.desc: The Terrace Public Library has served the community since 1929 and has been at its Park Avenue location since 1967, sitting on traditional Tsimshian territories. Beyond standard lending, it offers a notable 'Library of Things' program, a publicly accessible 3D printer, remote printing, and an extensive e-library with dozens of digital databases and streaming resources. It functions as a genuine community hub in a northern BC city that touring cyclists use as a resupply stop on the Yellowhead corridor.

visitor.name: Bear Creek Regional Nature Park
visitor.desc: Bear Creek Regional Nature Park is a nature reserve in the Comox Valley on Vancouver Island, managed by the Comox Valley Regional District. It offers a natural green space for outdoor recreation in a region popular with touring cyclists exploring Vancouver Island's trails and coastlines. The park's setting along the Comox Valley makes it a potential rest or exploration stop on cycling routes through the area.

visitor.name: Revelstoke Curling Club
visitor.desc: The Revelstoke Curling Club is a community sports club at 1100 Vernon Avenue offering curling, lounge facilities, and ice rentals for private and group events. It hosts the Annual Revelstoke Open Bonspiel, an event with over 70 years of history that is open to members and non-members alike. Touring cyclists passing through Revelstoke can find a welcoming, locally-rooted gathering spot here.

visitor.name: Fort Nelson Public Library
visitor.desc: The Fort Nelson Public Library serves this remote northern BC community at the heart of Municipal Square, offering a broad range of programs and digital services well beyond a typical small-town library. Located along the Alaska Highway corridor, it is a notable waypoint for long-distance cycle tourists in one of the most isolated stretches of the province. The library provides free public internet access, a seed library, meeting rooms, and an unusually rich roster of community programming.

visitor.name: Ronning's Garden
visitor.desc: Ronning's Garden is a heritage garden carved from BC's northern rainforest by Norwegian homesteader Bernt Ronning, who established his homestead here in 1910 near the terminus of the old San Josef Wagon Road and filled it with exotic plants ordered from around the world. The garden is renowned for hosting one of the oldest and largest Monkey Puzzle trees in British Columbia. Maintained today by a small group of volunteers and free to enter, it is a remarkable off-the-beaten-path destination for cyclists exploring the Cape Scott region of Vancouver Island North, reached by a ten-minute walk along a restored section of the historic wagon road.

detail.address: San Josef Main Fsr, Holberg, British Columbia, Canada

visitor.name: Alexandria Hall
visitor.desc: Alexandria Hall describes itself as 'the heart of Alexandria, BC,' a small rural community in the Cariboo region. It operates as a community organization and hosts local gatherings and dinners, making it a potential stop for touring cyclists passing through this remote stretch of central BC. The hall is actively managed and holds community events.

visitor.name: TNRL: Clearwater Library
visitor.desc: The Clearwater Library is a branch of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system with roots in the community dating to 1946, now housed in a recently renovated building featuring new siding, a covered entrance canopy, and an expanded children's area completed in 2025. It offers free public Wi-Fi, public computers, printing, and a wheelchair-accessible meeting room bookable by the public and non-profit groups. Located in Clearwater, a gateway town to Wells Gray Provincial Park, it sits along a popular cycling corridor in the Thompson-Nicola region.

visitor.name: Forslund-Watson Conservation Land Complex
visitor.desc: The Forslund-Watson Conservation Land Complex is an 80-acre nature reserve in south Langley, BC, managed by the Langley Field Naturalists. The reserve is an active habitat restoration site where volunteers plant native trees and shrubs, remove invasive species, and maintain old-field habitat for raptors and other wildlife. Whether the reserve is open for general public visitation — and what access or facilities may exist — is not described anywhere on the organization's website.

visitor.name: Trail Memorial Centre
visitor.desc: The Trail Memorial Centre is a large multi-purpose recreation facility in Trail, BC, housing two hockey arenas, a curling club, a full gymnasium, racquetball and squash courts, meeting rooms, and a commercial kitchen. The TMC marked its 75th year of operation in 2024 and serves as a major community hub in the Kootenays. Touring cyclists passing through Trail may find it a useful landmark stop, with EV charging stations listed among its on-site amenities.

visitor.name: Haylmore Heritage Site
visitor.desc: The Haylmore Heritage Site commemorates Will Haylmore, the original gold claim mine recorder in the Bridge River Valley, on the property where he lived and operated near Gold Bridge. The Bridge River Valley Community Association has restored one of the buildings and a stage on the grounds, and the site now serves as both a tourism information booth and a place to purchase locally produced artisan goods. A community-owned 4 kW solar array was installed at the site in 2015 as part of a regional renewable energy initiative.

detail.address: 104 Haylmore Ave, Gold Bridge BC V0K1P0

visitor.name: Midway Public Library
visitor.desc: Midway Public Library is a small but far-reaching community library serving the West Boundary of British Columbia, drawing patrons from Midway, Bridesville, Rock Creek, Westbridge, and Beaverdell. It offers physical collections alongside digital resources including ebooks and audiobooks via Libby, office services, and accessible programming. For touring cyclists passing through this remote stretch of Boundary Country, it is one of the few public institutions in the region offering community resources.

visitor.name: Quesnel & District Senior's Society
visitor.desc: The Quesnel & District Senior's Society is a civic community centre serving older residents of Quesnel and surrounding Cariboo region. As a community gathering place, it may offer washrooms and other basic facilities that could be useful to passing cyclists. The centre is situated in Quesnel, a key hub on cycling routes through BC's Central Interior.

visitor.name: Mount Robson Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Mount Robson Visitor Centre is the official BC Parks Welcome Centre at the western entrance to Mount Robson Provincial Park, home to the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies at 3,954 m. Positioned along the Yellowhead Highway (Highway 16), it anchors the 63 km Mount Robson Corridor and serves as the primary information gateway for the world-renowned Berg Lake Trail. Touring cyclists on the transcontinental Yellowhead route will find it a natural stop amid some of the most dramatic mountain scenery in British Columbia.

visitor.name: Greenwood Museum
visitor.desc: The Greenwood Museum Archives & Visitor Centre sits in Greenwood, BC, recognized as the smallest city in Canada, making it a singular cultural stop along a cycling route through the Boundary Country. The museum covers local mining, forestry, and Japanese-Canadian history, and offers a self-guided Heritage Walking Tour with maps available at the front desk. It also serves as the regional visitor centre, stocking provincial and local publications useful for cyclists planning onward routes.

detail.address: 214 South Copper Avenue, Greenwood, BC V0H 1J0

visitor.name: Cariboo Bowling Lanes
visitor.desc: Cariboo Bowl is a 5-pin bowling alley serving the Williams Lake area of BC's Cariboo interior, offering public open bowling, a full slate of adult and youth leagues, and Friday-night Cosmic Bowl. The facility accommodates up to six bowlers per lane and accepts group and birthday-party bookings by reservation. For touring cyclists passing through the region, it provides a social indoor activity option, particularly useful during inclement weather.

visitor.name: Confluence Climbing
visitor.desc: Confluence Climbing is Golden's indoor bouldering gym, offering roughly 1,200 sq ft of climbing surface across walls ranging from a 3-degree slab to a 45-degree overhang, plus Canada's first 12′×12′ adjustable Grasshopper board with a lit-hold, app-connected problem database. The facility also houses a fitness area with free weights, a rowing machine, a stationary bike, hangboards, and a mezzanine lounge. For touring cyclists passing through Golden, it's a standout rainy-day or rest-day option in a mountain town surrounded by the Purcells, Selkirks, and Rockies.

visitor.name: Saahlinda Naay Museum
visitor.desc: Saahlinda Naay (Saving Things House) is the Haida Gwaii Museum in Skidegate, a landmark cultural institution dedicated to Haida knowledge, language, art, and the islands' natural and supernatural heritage. It offers rotating temporary exhibitions alongside permanent galleries exploring the deep connections between the land, sea, and Haida peoples. For a touring cyclist passing through Haida Gwaii, it is one of the most compelling stops on the archipelago — a genuinely remote and rare cultural experience at the edge of the Pacific.

detail.address: #2 Second Beach Road, Skidegate, B.C. V0T 1S1

visitor.name: Pesuta
visitor.desc: The Pesuta is the partially intact wooden hull of a Japanese log barge that ran aground on the north beach of Haida Gwaii on December 11, 1928, and has been weathering on the sand ever since. It sits within Naikoon Provincial Park, a vast wilderness of beach, bog, and old-growth forest on the traditional territory of the Haida Nation. Touring cyclists on Haida Gwaii typically reach it via a beach hike from the Tlell River trailhead, making it one of the most dramatic and remote landmarks on any BC cycling itinerary.

visitor.name: Glover Community Nature Park
visitor.desc: Glover Community Nature Park is a forested nature reserve operated by the Comox Valley Regional District on Vancouver Island. It offers a natural woodland setting for quiet recreation and wildlife observation close to the Comox Valley communities. Touring cyclists looking for a green break or a short trail walk would find it a low-key stop between destinations.

visitor.name: Railway & Chinese Worker Exhibit
visitor.desc: The Railway & Chinese Worker Exhibit is a historical museum node located within the Hell's Gate Airtram attraction in the Fraser Canyon near Boston Bar, BC. The broader site features a Swiss-built gondola that descends 157 metres into the gorge where the Fraser River pushes 200 million gallons of water per minute through a channel only 110 feet wide. Cyclists traveling the Trans-Canada Highway will find a full tourist complex here, including a cafe, fisheries display, suspension bridge, fudge factory, and gold panning alongside the historical exhibits.

detail.address: 43111 Trans-Canada Hwy, Boston Bar, BC V0K 1C0

notes.Café or food on site: Simon's Cafe and Fudge Factory (up to 100 flavours made on site) are listed as gorge-level experiences on the Experiences page

visitor.name: Mackenzie Rec Centre
visitor.desc: The Mackenzie Rec Centre is a publicly operated community recreation facility run by the District of Mackenzie in northern BC. It appears within the district's broader Recreation, Arts & Culture portfolio alongside parks, trails, and program offerings. For a touring cyclist arriving in this remote northern community, it is likely one of the few public facilities offering indoor amenities.

visitor.name: Hazelton District Public Library
visitor.desc: A small-town public library housed in the historic Library and Pioneer Museum Building in Hazelton, in the Upper Skeena region. Beyond books, it features a Pioneer Museum, an art collection, and a local history reference collection that document the area's heritage. Touring cyclists will find free Wi-Fi, computer access, and a welcoming rest stop in a remote stretch of northern BC.

visitor.name: Sicamous & District Recreation Centre
visitor.desc: A publicly operated single-sheet NHL regulation-sized ice arena and fitness centre in Sicamous, surrounded by the Shuswap region's mountain scenery. The facility also houses a recently renovated fitness centre with cardio and strength equipment, a concession stand, and a banquet hall used for tournaments and community events.

detail.address: 1121 Eagle Pass Way, Box 190, Sicamous, BC V0E 2V1

notes.Café or food on site: Concession listed as a facility feature

visitor.name: Ashcroft Museum
visitor.desc: Housed in the historic 1916 brick 'Dominion' building — originally Ashcroft's post office — this local history museum is considered one of the best in any BC village. Its collection spans Ashcroft's early 1900s 'Glory Days,' with exhibits honouring Indigenous Peoples, the Chinese community, ranching, fossils, and a popular coal mine reproduction. The museum also maintains extensive genealogical and historical archives available to visiting researchers.

visitor.name: amphitheatre
visitor.desc: The amphitheatre is an outdoor interpretive or performance structure within E.C. Manning Provincial Park, situated in the Cascade Mountains along Highway 3 between Hope and Princeton. E.C. Manning is one of British Columbia's most popular provincial parks, offering campgrounds, extensive trail networks, and a natural corridor between the Lower Mainland and the Okanagan. The park is a well-known waypoint for touring cyclists traveling the Highway 3 corridor.

detail.address: 750 Pike Mountain FSR, Princeton, BC, Canada, V0X 1W0

visitor.name: Steward Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: The Steward Visitor Centre is a two-storey tourist information office in Stewart, BC, at the head of the Portland Canal near the Alaska border — a remote but iconic stop for cyclists riding the Cassiar Highway. Stewart sits at one of Canada's most northerly ice-free ports, surrounded by glaciers, fjords, and wildlife, and the visitor centre serves as the gateway orientation point for the area. Mobile reception is confirmed on site.

visitor.name: Willow Point Greenway
visitor.desc: Willow Point Greenway is a linear nature reserve corridor in the Willow Point neighbourhood of Campbell River on Vancouver Island, providing a traffic-free green passage for cyclists and pedestrians. It forms part of the City of Campbell River's municipal parkland network and sits within easy reach of the Discovery Passage coastline. Touring cyclists passing through Campbell River can use it as a quieter off-road route through the southern part of the city.

detail.address: 1800 S Alder St, Campbell River, BC V9W 7J1

visitor.name: David E. Enarson Gymnasium
visitor.desc: The David E. Enarson Gymnasium, also known as 'The Gym,' is the main indoor sports facility at Trinity Western University's Langley campus. As a university athletics centre, it serves the Spartans varsity programs as well as campus recreation. Touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley may find it a useful landmark or stopping point on the TWU grounds.

visitor.name: SkyTrek Adventure Park
visitor.desc: SkyTrek Adventure Park is a family-oriented outdoor adventure park situated directly on the Trans-Canada Highway (Highway 1), roughly 32 km west of Revelstoke and 35 km east of Sicamous — a busy touring corridor. The park features a treetop Sky Course with over 30 aerial elements, zip lines, an adventure tower, and kids' zones, and shares its site with the well-known Enchanted Forest attraction. Its highway-accessible location makes it a natural mid-route stop for cyclists riding between Sicamous and Revelstoke.

visitor.name: Cliff Gilker Park
visitor.desc: Cliff Gilker Park is a nature reserve managed by the Sunshine Coast Regional District (SCRD) located near Roberts Creek on BC's Sunshine Coast. It is a publicly accessible park listed under the SCRD's parks portfolio. Touring cyclists passing through the Sunshine Coast area may find it a worthwhile natural stop, though specific on-site cycling facilities are unconfirmed from available sources.
