visitor.name: Fort St. John North Peace Museum
visitor.desc: The Fort St. John North Peace Museum, operated by the North Peace Historical Society, chronicles the North Peace region from ancient dinosaur footprints and Indigenous Dane-Zaa history through the fur trade, agricultural settlement, and the 1942 construction of the Alaska Highway. Visitors explore a rich collection of replica buildings — trapper's cabin, general store, schoolhouse, jail, and more — alongside hands-on interactive exhibits and over 13,000 archival photographs. For a touring cyclist passing through northeastern BC, it offers a compelling half-day stop to understand the dramatic transformation of the landscape they are riding through.

detail.address: 9323 100 St. Fort St. John, BC V1J 4N4

visitor.name: Paint Pots
visitor.desc: The Paint Pots are a series of vivid ochre-coloured mineral springs in Kootenay National Park, reached by a short trail off Highway 93. The iron-rich deposits hold deep cultural significance for Indigenous peoples and have been a gathering place for thousands of years. Touring cyclists riding the Kootenay Parkway pass close by and can make a quick detour to see one of the most distinctive geological features in the Canadian Rockies.

visitor.name: Kitimat Visitor Centre & Chamber of Commerce
visitor.desc: The Kitimat Chamber of Commerce & Visitor Centre has been connecting local businesses and welcoming visitors since 1955. Housed within is the Coastline Collective Gift Store, featuring handmade goods and souvenirs from over 20 local artisans alongside maps, brochures, and community information. It is a natural first stop for touring cyclists arriving in Kitimat who want local knowledge, regional brochures, and a taste of the community's creative economy.

visitor.name: Prince Rupert Fire & BC Police Museum
visitor.desc: The Prince Rupert Fire Museum is a heritage attraction in Prince Rupert, BC, dedicated to preserving the history of firefighting in the region. It was previously associated with the Prince Rupert Public Library's web presence, suggesting a community-operated or volunteer-run institution. Touring cyclists passing through Prince Rupert's compact downtown may find it a worthwhile cultural stop, though current access details are unconfirmed.

detail.address: 200 1st Ave W, Prince Rupert, BC V8J 1A8

visitor.name: Copper Sun Gallery & Journeys
visitor.desc: Copper Sun Journeys is an Indigenous-owned and -operated guided adventure company based in Bella Coola (Q'umk'uts, Nuxalkulmc), offering sacred petroglyph experiences, totem story tours, ancient cedar forest walks, and river rafting in the Great Bear Rainforest. Endorsed by Indigenous Tourism BC as a must-see attraction, it is led by local Nuxalk guides and operates June through October. Touring cyclists passing through the remote Bella Coola Valley would find this a rare opportunity to experience living Indigenous culture and dramatic coastal mountain wilderness.

detail.address: 442 Mackenzie St, Bella Coola, BC V0T 1C0

visitor.name: Elkford Community and Conference Centre
visitor.desc: The Elkford Community and Conference Centre is a municipally operated public facility in Elkford, BC, the self-styled Wilderness Capital of British Columbia, situated in the remote East Kootenay region near the Elk Valley. It serves as a gathering space for local events and conferences in a small mountain community. Touring cyclists passing through this remote area may find it a useful stop in a town with limited services.

detail.address: 744 Fording Drive, Box 340, Elkford, BC V0B 1H0

visitor.name: Exhale
visitor.desc: Exhale (operating as 'Exhale Art & Crystal') is an art gallery and crystal shop located in the Okanagan & Thompson region of British Columbia. It sits at the intersection of fine art and mineral/crystal retail, likely appealing to cyclists looking for a cultural or curiosity stop on a touring route. The minimal web presence makes it something of a hidden gem worth discovering in person.

visitor.name: Osoyoos Visitor Centre
visitor.desc: Destination Osoyoos is the Destination Marketing Organization (DMO) for Osoyoos and operates the Osoyoos Visitor Centre on Main Street. The town bills itself as 'Canada's Warmest Welcome,' sitting beside the warmest lake in Canada in the semi-arid South Okanagan. Cycling tourists will find the centre a useful planning hub for regional biking routes, wine tours, and hiking in the surrounding grasslands and highlands.

visitor.name: Grand Forks Curling Club
visitor.desc: The Grand Forks Curling Club is a community curling facility located in Grand Forks in BC's Boundary region, tagged in OSM as an ice rink with sport=curling. As a classic small-town curling club, it likely serves as a social hub during the winter season. Touring cyclists passing through Grand Forks during the curling season may find it a welcoming spot to connect with locals.

visitor.name: Alberni Valley Museum
visitor.desc: Praised by Lonely Planet as one of Vancouver Island's best community museums, the Alberni Valley Museum documents the richly diverse history of the Alberni Valley through collections spanning First Nations culture, industrial history, and folk art. Its distinctive Visible Storage system makes the entire collection accessible to visitors at all times, accompanied by easy-to-use catalogue books. The museum also presents a rotating program of temporary exhibits and operates a museum shop.

detail.address: 4255 Wallace Street, Port Alberni BC V9Y 3Y6

visitor.name: Golden & District Centennial Arena
visitor.desc: The Golden & District Centennial Arena is a municipally-operated indoor ice facility run by the Town of Golden's Recreation Services department, serving as the primary hockey and skating venue for the Columbia Valley community. Located in Golden, a mountain town at the junction of Highway 1 and Highway 95, the arena functions as a community gathering hub year-round. A dedicated Arena Lounge operates within the facility, suggesting on-site food and beverage service beyond the ice surface itself.

notes.Café or food on site: A dedicated 'Arena Lounge' subpage exists at /recreation-services/facilities/arena-lounge on the Town of Golden website, indicating an on-site lounge/food service. Body content was truncated so specific offerings are

visitor.name: Gitlaxt'aamiks Interpretive Centre
visitor.desc: A cultural interpretive centre in Gitlaxt'aamiks (New Aiyansh), the capital of the Nisg̱a'a Nation, located 100 km northwest of Terrace on Highway 113. The centre showcases traditional artwork of the Gitmidiik (Grizzly Bear) clan, artifacts, displays, and audio-visual presentations on the history of the village, including a replica traditional smokehouse. It also features a restaurant with traditional and western cuisine, a gift shop, and a theatre.

notes.Café or food on site: The centre features a restaurant with traditional and western cuisine

visitor.name: Mansons Landing Community Hall
visitor.desc: Mansons Hall is a historic community centre on southern Cortes Island that has served as a gathering place since 1922. The hall houses a main performance/event space, a commercial kitchen, a cafe room, a yoga studio, a free public computer station, a retail boutique, and several community organizations including a post office and community radio station. Touring cyclists reaching Cortes Island will find it a lively hub with weekly markets, live music, free community lunches, and a skate park on the grounds.

detail.address: 983 Beesley Road, Mansons Landing, BC V0P 1K0

notes.Café or food on site: Free community lunches offered monthly; weekly Friday Market; cafe room with service kitchen available for food events

visitor.name: Gibsons Public Art Gallery
visitor.desc: Gibsons Public Art Gallery (GPAG) is a free non-profit public gallery housed in the historic former Bank of Montreal building at the centre of Gibsons' Landing on BC's Sunshine Coast. Founded in 2003, it anchors a creative district that includes five commercial galleries, artists' studios, and a heritage museum. Gibsons is a 40-minute ferry ride from Vancouver, making GPAG a natural cultural pause for cyclists touring the Sunshine Coast.

visitor.name: Laughing Falls
visitor.desc: Laughing Falls is a natural waterfall situated within Yoho National Park on the western slopes of the Great Divide in British Columbia, part of the Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks UNESCO World Heritage Site. The park is celebrated for its glaciers, dramatic peaks, and cascading waterfalls, and lies along the Trans-Canada Highway corridor — a heavily travelled touring route for cyclists. Visiting the falls requires leaving the road and hiking a trail into the Yoho Valley.

visitor.name: Prince George Golf & Curling Club
visitor.desc: The Prince George Golf & Curling Club is a large multi-sport complex offering golf, curling, an indoor climbing gym called the OVERhang, and racquet courts managed by the PG Tennis and Pickleball Club. The fully public and wheelchair-accessible clubhouse building houses a full-service restaurant and lounge alongside meeting and banquet rooms capable of hosting events of almost any size. Touring cyclists passing through Prince George can access the public restaurant without club membership.

detail.address: 2601 Recplace Drive, Prince George, BC V2N 0G2

notes.Café or food on site: Full-service restaurant and lounge in the publicly accessible clubhouse building; daily specials and full menu

visitor.name: Comox Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Comox Community Centre is a civic facility operated by the Town of Comox, offering fitness programs, racquet courts, and rentable spaces to residents and visitors on Vancouver Island. It sits in the heart of the Comox Valley, a region popular with touring cyclists exploring coastal routes. The centre lists 'Accessible Recreation' as a program area, suggesting a commitment to welcoming a broad range of visitors.

visitor.name: Sandon Historical Society Museum
visitor.desc: The Sandon Historical Society Museum preserves and interprets the history of Sandon, a former silver-mining boomtown in the Kootenays that is now effectively a ghost town. The museum recently added a permanent exhibit, 'Window to the Past – Japanese Canadians in Sandon,' documenting the internment of Nikkei residents during 1942–1944. Located at the end of Slocan Star Street along a route signposted from Three Forks, it is a remote but rewarding destination for cyclists exploring the Slocan Valley.

detail.address: Slocan Star Street, Sandon, BC V0G 1S0

visitor.name: Coast Gravity Bike Park
visitor.desc: Coast Gravity Park is a dedicated mountain bike park in Sechelt, BC, on BC's Sunshine Coast, purpose-built for gravity-oriented trail riding. The park offers bike rentals, enabling visitors who arrive without their own equipment to participate, and runs private bookings and organized events in addition to regular day passes. It is one of the few ticketed MTB bike parks on the Sunshine Coast, making it a notable destination for cycling tourists in the region.

visitor.name: Dene Kǫ^ Cultural and Administration Building
visitor.desc: The Dene Kǫ^ Cultural and Administration Building is the hub of the Daylu Dena Council in Lower Post, a small First Nations community in Northern BC near the Yukon border along the Alaska Highway corridor. It serves dual roles as a cultural centre and administrative office for the local Dene community. For touring cyclists traversing this extremely remote stretch of highway, this building represents one of the few community anchors in the region.

visitor.name: ORL: South Shuswap Branch
visitor.desc: The South Shuswap Branch is part of the Okanagan Regional Library, a 30-branch regional system established in 1936 serving over 399,000 people across 59,600 square kilometres. Located on Golf Course Drive, the branch hosts regular community programs including events like laughter yoga and knitting circles, and maintains a book drop bin outside the main entrance. Free on-site parking is available, making it a practical stop along a cycling route through the South Shuswap area.

visitor.name: Creston & District Community Complex
visitor.desc: The Aquatic Centre is an indoor swimming pool facility in Creston, BC, operated as part of the Creston & District Community Complex by the Regional District of Central Kootenay. It serves the broader Creston area community with indoor aquatic recreation and is part of a multi-use municipal complex. Touring cyclists riding through the southern Kootenays may find it a useful stop for a swim or to clean up after a long day in the saddle.

visitor.name: Mount Robson Park
visitor.desc: Mount Robson Park protects the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies (3,954 m) and is one of British Columbia's most celebrated provincial parks. The 63 km Mount Robson Corridor follows Highway 16 (Yellowhead), giving touring cyclists dramatic views of mountains, creeks, and wetlands as they pass through. A Welcome Centre at the park's western entrance serves as an orientation point, and the world-renowned Berg Lake Trail draws backcountry adventurers from around the globe.

visitor.name: Friendship Community Garden
visitor.desc: Friendship Community Garden is a community garden in the Comox Valley, operated under the Healthy Families Program of Comox Valley Family Services Association. Community gardens like this one offer a pleasant, low-key stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. The garden's connection to a social services organization suggests a community-oriented, welcoming space.

visitor.name: Centennial Pool
visitor.desc: A community outdoor swimming pool in Hagensborg in the Bella Coola Valley, originally built in 1967 as a federal Centennial project. Operated by the Central Coast Regional District during summer months only, it offers public swims, lap swims, and Red Cross swimming lessons. For touring cyclists passing through one of BC's most remote valleys, it's a rare chance to cool off after a long ride through the Coast Mountains.

visitor.name: Alert Bay Public Library & Museum
visitor.desc: Alert Bay Public Library & Museum is a combined public library and museum serving the community of Alert Bay on Cormorant Island, situated on the traditional lands of the Kwakwaka'wakw Peoples. The institution holds a library collection alongside museum resources and offers public computer and internet access. For touring cyclists arriving by ferry to this remote island destination, it provides a cultural stop with connectivity.

visitor.name: Baynes Lake Community Centre
visitor.desc: The Baynes Lake Community Hall is a rural gathering place operated by the Baynes Lake Community Society, situated along Jaffray Baynes Lake Road in the East Kootenays. It serves the small community of Baynes Lake and surrounding area as a hub for local events and organization. Touring cyclists riding through this quiet corner of the Kootenay region may find it a useful landmark or rest stop in an otherwise sparsely serviced stretch of road.

visitor.name: Mt. Baldy Ski Area
visitor.desc: Baldy Mountain Resort is a four-season mountain destination perched above the South Okanagan near Oliver, with a summit of 2,310 m and over 600 acres of skiable and gladed terrain receiving 25–35 feet of dry desert powder annually. In summer the mountain hosts artisan markets, disc golf, and a hilltop coffee bar with panoramic views over Canada's only natural desert and the surrounding wine country. The access road is partly unpaved, making it a realistic destination for gravel or mountain bikers exploring the Oliver–Osoyoos corridor.

detail.address: 2680 Mount Baldy Rd, Oliver, BC V0H 1T0

notes.Café or food on site: Three venues

visitor.name: Masich Place Stadium
visitor.desc: Masich Place Stadium is a municipal athletics facility in Prince George, BC, managed by the City of Prince George. It serves as a track-and-field venue and is part of the city's parks and recreation infrastructure. A touring cyclist passing through Prince George may find it useful as a landmark or rest stop, though it is primarily oriented toward organized athletics events.

visitor.name: McBride & District Public Library
visitor.desc: McBride & District Public Library is a community hub in the small Robson Valley town of McBride, situated along the Yellowhead Highway in BC's Central Interior. The library offers computer and internet access, a Library of Things, a seed library, and meeting room rentals — practical resources for touring cyclists passing through this remote region. It also maintains a satellite reading room in the hamlet of Dome Creek further up the valley, and hosts local history and oral history projects rooted in the area's railway and ranching heritage.

visitor.name: Rogers Pass National Historic Site
visitor.desc: Rogers Pass National Historic Site marks the summit where the Canadian Pacific Railway crossed the Selkirk Mountains in 1885, a pivotal moment in Canada's confederation story. Located within Glacier National Park along the Trans-Canada Highway, the site encompasses ruins of the original CPR right-of-way, ancient cedar groves, and the Rogers Pass Discovery Centre. For touring cyclists, it is one of the most historically resonant high-elevation waypoints on any cross-Canada journey through the Selkirks.

detail.address: 9520 Trans-Canada Highway, Rogers Pass BC V0E 2S0

visitor.name: Kunze Art Gallery
visitor.desc: The Kunze Art Gallery is housed in Creston's historic red grain elevator, giving it a striking industrial character that sets it apart from typical gallery spaces. It showcases a rotating roster of emerging and accomplished regional artists working in large-scale acrylic painting, sculpture, functional pottery, graphite, and clay, complemented by a gift shop called The Elevator featuring handmade local goods. The gallery received the 'Best of the Best Readers Choice Award 2025' and maintains an active presence on the online platform Artsy, making it a recognized cultural stop in the Kootenays.

visitor.name: West Coast Trail Information & Orientation Centre
visitor.desc: The West Coast Trail Information & Orientation Centre is the Parks Canada gateway facility for registering and orienting hikers tackling the legendary 75-km West Coast Trail, one of Canada's most demanding multi-day backcountry routes along the remote west shore of Vancouver Island. The centre sits within Pacific Rim National Park Reserve in the traditional territories of the Huu-ay-aht, Ditidaht, and Pacheedaht First Nations, whose Guardians help maintain the trail. Touring cyclists riding the Vancouver Island coast pass through this isolated region and may find the facility a useful reference point, though it is primarily oriented toward backcountry hikers.

visitor.name: Brian Scott Fine Arts
visitor.desc: Brian Scott Art Gallery is a fine art gallery located on the Island Highway North on Vancouver Island, showcasing the work of artist Brian Scott. Situated along the main touring corridor between Courtenay and Campbell River, it offers cyclists a cultural stop mid-route. The gallery's original web presence has been compromised, so current programming and hours should be confirmed by phone.

visitor.name: Barkerville Historic Town & Park
visitor.desc: The largest living history museum in western North America, Barkerville preserves more than 125 heritage buildings along the original Gold Rush streetscape on Williams Creek in the Cariboo. Designated a National Historic Site in 1924, visitors explore working displays, costumed interpreters, and 19th-century shops set amid mountain forests. Cyclists can ride surrounding roads and trails but must push bikes through the Heritage Zone at walking pace.

detail.address: Box 19 14301 Highway 26 East, Barkerville, BC V0K 1B0

notes.Café or food on site: Main season page references 'Shops, restaurants, and programs' operating on site

visitor.name: Gold Bridge Community Complex
visitor.desc: Gold Bridge Community Complex is a community centre in the remote village of Gold Bridge, operated by the Squamish-Lillooet Regional District. Situated along the rural roads between Lillooet and Pemberton, Gold Bridge is a tiny settlement that touring cyclists may pass through on backcountry routes through the Bridge River Valley. The complex appears to double as the community's gathering space in a very small and isolated area.

visitor.name: Assiniboine Crk Trail
visitor.desc: The Assiniboine Creek Trail is a backcountry trail within Mount Assiniboine Provincial Park, part of the Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks UNESCO World Heritage Site. The park is celebrated for its alpine lakes, glaciers, and dramatic peaks, with no road access — trails provide the only way in. It is a remote wilderness destination requiring full self-sufficiency, suited to experienced backcountry travellers.

visitor.name: Kitimat Ice Rink
visitor.desc: The Kitimat Ice Rink is a municipally operated indoor ice facility in Kitimat, BC, serving the Haisla Nation's unceded territory on British Columbia's North Coast. Tagged in OSM as an ice hockey venue, it sits within the District of Kitimat's broader network of recreation centres that includes Tamitik Arena and the Riverlodge Recreation and Fitness Centre. For touring cyclists, it represents a public recreation anchor in an otherwise remote northern community.

visitor.name: Fernie Visitor Information Centre
visitor.desc: The Fernie Chamber of Commerce supports local businesses, workforce development, and community events in this small mountain town in the East Kootenays. Known for hosting signature celebrations like Griz Days and the Holiday Kick-Off, the Chamber helps sustain Fernie's year-round economy. A touring cyclist passing through may find it useful as a point of contact for local business information, though its primary function is business support rather than visitor services.

visitor.name: CRDL: Tatla Lake Branch
visitor.desc: The Tatla Lake Branch is a small community library operated by the Cariboo Regional District Library system, situated on BC-20 (the Chilcotin Highway) in the remote Tatla Lake settlement of the Central Interior. Staffed by a community librarian, it is one of the few public facilities along this long, sparsely serviced highway corridor popular with cycle tourists. As a publicly accessible institution, it represents a rare community hub in a stretch of BC where services are few and far between.

visitor.name: Radium Hot Springs Public Library
visitor.desc: The Radium Public Library is a small community library serving Radium Hot Springs and the surrounding Columbia Valley, located on Stanley Street in the heart of the village. It offers public computer and internet access, a Library of Things, digital lending, and a variety of community programs. For touring cyclists passing through the Kootenay Rockies, it provides a welcoming indoor stop with Wi-Fi and a range of local community resources and links.

visitor.name: Emily Carr Statue
visitor.desc: A Emily Carr Statue in Victoria.

detail.address: Government ST and, Belleville St., Victoria, BC V8W 1W5, Canada

bikeshop.name: Cycle City
bikeshop.desc: Cycle City is a downtown Vancouver cycling institution operating two adjacent storefronts on Hornby Street — one for guided tours and one for rentals, repairs, and bike sales — rated #1 on TripAdvisor for Vancouver sightseeing with over 7,125 reviews. The shop carries top bicycle brands including Specialized and provides professional tune-ups and repairs with quick turn-around times, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists needing mechanical support. Beyond repairs, the operation offers a large rental fleet spanning city cruisers, e-bikes, performance road and gravel bikes, multiple guided tour formats, self-guided route maps, and luggage storage.

notes.Touring parts stocked: Product catalog includes panniers, handlebar bags, frame bags, saddlebags, front racks, rear racks, fenders, and computers/mounts — core touring accessories
notes.Bike rentals: Hundreds of bikes including city cruisers, e-bikes, kids bikes, performance road bikes (Specialized Allez Comp, Roubaix SL8 Pro), and gravel bikes (Specialized Diverge Expert Carbon); all rentals include helmet, lock, basket/handlebar bag, and map
notes.Guided rides: Multiple guided tour options: Grand Bike Tour, Stanley Park Bike Tour, Family Stanley Park Bike Tour, Epic Electric Bike Tour, and group/private tours with 'story-teller guides'

bikeshop.name: The Lift Ski and Board
bikeshop.desc: The Lift is a Port Moody outdoor sports shop that spans both winter and summer disciplines, selling and servicing ski, snowboard, and cycling equipment under one roof. Their dedicated bike services department handles repairs and stocks parts and accessories, making it a practical stop for cyclists on BC's Lower Mainland trails. The shop also carries bike apparel, helmets, protective gear, and junior bikes.

detail.address: Unit 2, Murray Street, Port Moody, BC

bikeshop.name: Green Man Bikes Shop
bikeshop.desc: Green Man Bikes is a family-owned, service-oriented bike shop positioned just metres from the Galloping Goose Trail at the intersection of Sooke Road and Happy Valley Road — the last repair stop on the trail before Sooke. The shop carries Brodie and Genesis gravel, touring, and hybrid bikes, and also specialises in vintage bike restoration and custom builds. Staff hand out free trail maps and invite cyclists to stop in for a safety check before heading into or out of town.
req_checked: Staff help with urgent mechanical issues

notes.Walk-in repairs: No appointments needed for flats or minor emergency repairs. Minor adjustments can be done on the fly to keep your rolling
notes.Same-day urgent repairs: Walk-in flats and minor emergency repairs accepted without appointment; 'Minor adjustments can be done on the fly to keep you rolling.'
notes.Bike boxes / packing: Services page lists 'Bike Boxing' as a named flat-rate service

bikeshop.name: Cycle Logic
bikeshop.desc: Cycle Logic is a well-established multi-location BC bicycle shop — with branches in Kamloops, Prince George, Quesnel, Revelstoke, and Williams Lake — operating a full repair department out of its downtown Kamloops location. As a certified Shimano Service Center staffed by professionally trained mechanics, the shop handles everything from minor adjustments to complete overhauls, with bike fitting services also available. The retail floor covers a wide range of bicycles including e-bikes, a comprehensive parts selection, clothing, and accessories.
req_checked: Staff help with urgent mechanical issues

notes.Walk-in repairs: walk-ins are welcome in all of our service departments

bikeshop.name: Wentings Cycle & Mountain Shop
bikeshop.desc: A family-owned bike shop in Mission's historic Railway Avenue district, operating continuously since 1978 when the Wenting family purchased the original Planet Earth Cycles. Now occupying 5,200 square feet with 10 staff, the shop carries road, mountain, hybrid, e-bikes, and kids' bikes alongside accessories, GPS computers, clothing, and bike racks. Jerseys from Canadian cycling champions hang on the walls, reflecting deep roots in the local cycling community.

detail.address: 33245 North Railway Avenue, Mission, BC, V2V 1E4

notes.E-bike service: E-bike overhaul listed at separate pricing; e-bike diagnostics offered at hourly shop rate; DH/E-Bike tire/tube services listed

bikeshop.name: Corsa Cycles
bikeshop.desc: Corsa Cycles is a full-service bicycle shop in Squamish, BC, now operating under the Dunbar Cycles & Corsa Cycles banner following its 2018 acquisition. The shop covers mountain, road, gravel, city, and electric bikes alongside a dedicated service centre, making it a comprehensive stop in the Sea-to-Sky corridor. Its broad parts and accessories inventory—including touring-specific luggage and racks—makes it particularly useful for loaded cycle tourers passing through Squamish.

detail.address: 38123 Cleveland Ave, Squamish, BC V8B 0A8, Canada

notes.Touring parts stocked: Website navigation explicitly lists panniers, saddle bags, handlebar bags, frame bags, and racks & carriers under Accessories

bikeshop.name: More Bikes
bikeshop.desc: More Bikes is a full-service independent bike shop with multiple Vancouver locations — Kitsilano (recently relocated to 1828 W. 4th Ave.), UBC, and West Vancouver. The shop carries a broad range of bikes from Giant, Liv, Kona, Rocky Mountain, Brodie, and Cannondale, including e-bikes across several brands, plus a comprehensive parts and accessories floor. A dedicated repair and maintenance department makes it a practical stop for touring cyclists needing mechanical help on the road.

notes.Touring parts stocked: Website product categories explicitly include panniers, pannier racks, frame bags, handlebar bags, saddle bags, and hydration systems — standard touring kit

bikeshop.name: Bicycleitis
bikeshop.desc: Bicycleitis is a small, independent bicycle shop located on Shawnigan Lake Road near Duncan on Vancouver Island. It describes itself on Facebook as 'the Small Shop,' suggesting a boutique or owner-operated character. Touring cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley area may find it a useful stop for bike-related needs.

bikeshop.name: eBikeBC
bikeshop.desc: EbikeBC is Canada's premier electric mobility retailer, founded in 2015 by engineers seeking sustainable transportation solutions, specializing in e-bikes, e-trikes, e-scooters, conversion kits, and accessories. The shop operates a dedicated service center handling e-bike repair, diagnostics, battery refurbishment, and component installation. For touring cyclists on e-bikes, it is a specialist resource for parts and servicing in the Vancouver area.

The shop is a reliable stop for touring cyclists thanks to its walk-in, no-appointment repair model and fast 24-hour service turnaround — with a complimentary demo bike provided if that window is missed. Additional perks include free multi-point inspections, free accessory installation, and local ride recommendations from staff.

bikeshop.name: Edmonds Cycle

bikeshop.name: Cycology Bikes
bikeshop.desc: Cycology Bikes is a service-focused bicycle shop in Castlegar serving the West Kootenays cycling community, with particular expertise in e-bikes and in-house suspension rebuilds. The shop offers tiered service packages ranging from basic inspections to full-rebuild OCD-level overhauls, and performs all suspension work on-site. Beyond repairs, Cycology actively partners with the Castlegar Parks and Trails Society on local trail maintenance and the Millennium Park Bike Park project.

notes.E-bike service: Website explicitly lists an 'E-Stress Tune' package covering drivetrain, battery, drive unit diagnostics, firmware update, and service reset; also states 'We are the local experts for E-bikes.'

bikeshop.name: Sports Junkies
bikeshop.desc: Sports Junkies is a sprawling two-storey new-and-used sporting goods store established in 1992, anchored in Mt. Pleasant between MEC and Sport Chek. Alongside new and used bike sales, they operate a dedicated Tech Shop offering a full range of bicycle mechanical services from flat repairs to complete tune-ups and hub overhauls. Touring cyclists will find a knowledgeable bike department staff and the ability to drop in for service consultations.

bikeshop.name: Ski Base
bikeshop.desc: Ski Base is Fernie's longest-running bike and ski shop, founded in 1968 and still anchored in its downtown location. Current owners Jeff and Jane Johnson are active in local trail building and community organizations, giving the shop genuine roots in Fernie's riding culture. Touring cyclists will find a full-service repair department alongside a broad range of bikes, accessories, and touring-oriented carry gear.

notes.Touring parts stocked: Shop prominently stocks Ortlieb Frame-Pack Top Tube Bike Bag and Arkel Saddle Bag — both touring-specific brands — alongside a general bike parts and accessories category

bikeshop.name: Bishop's Family Cycles
bikeshop.desc: Bishop's Family Cycles is a Victoria cargo-bike specialist situated directly on the Blanshard bike lane between Yates and Johnson streets, making it easily accessible by bicycle. Founded by a family of active cyclists transplanted from Ontario and the US, the shop focuses on helping families, new commuters, and car-replacement cyclists find the right cargo, electric, and kids bikes from brands like Riese & Müller and Tern. They also carry a practical range of parts and tools — tubes, tires, brakes, pumps, and saddles — useful to a cyclist passing through.

bikeshop.name: Bicycle Cafe
bikeshop.desc: Bicycle Cafe is a full-service bike shop in Kamloops, BC, located in a region celebrated as the birthplace of aggressive Interior mountain biking. With over 20 years serving the community, they welcome all riders and bikes — from recreational tourers to competitive racers — and carry bikes, apparel, and accessories from top industry brands. A touring cyclist will find an experienced workshop team capable of handling everything from quick tune-ups to full overhauls.

notes.E-bike service: Service menu lists 'E Bike Classic Tune Up' and 'E Bike Update and Diagnostic' (Bosch, Specialized, Giant, Shimano, Fazua systems only); throttle e-bikes explicitly excluded: 'We don't work on throttle e-bikes'

bikeshop.name: velofix
bikeshop.desc: Velofix is a mobile bike shop franchise that dispatches certified technicians directly to wherever a cyclist needs them — home, trailhead, or accommodation. With 130+ technicians across North America and over 220,000 completed services, it covers a wide range of bikes including road, gravel, mountain, commuter, triathlon, tandem, and e-bikes. For touring cyclists in BC, it offers a practical alternative to hauling a bike to a shop, bookable online or by phone.

notes.E-bike service: Dedicated e-bike service packages (Silver, Gold, Flat Repair) covering safety inspection, drivetrain, braking, wheel truing, and electrical systems; explicitly supports Rad Power, Benno, OHM, Yamaha, and Strome e-bikes

bikeshop.name: Decathlon

A touring cyclist could find replacement accessories or basic cycling components here, though the cycling department is one section within a big-box retail environment.

bikeshop.name: The Gravity MTB Garage
bikeshop.desc: The Gravity MTB Garage is a mountain bike coaching and service hub in downtown Cumberland, housed in a converted auto shop and described on its website as the only full-suspension service centre on Vancouver Island. Founded by Chad and CJ Hendren — Chad serves as Canada's National Downhill Team Coach — it combines a full retail store, a dedicated suspension workshop with specialized tools, a strength training gym, and the island's exclusive Forbidden Bike Co. demo and sales centre. Touring cyclists will find a rider-first atmosphere complete with a bike wash, lounge area, and deep local trail knowledge at the heart of one of BC's premier mountain biking destinations.

notes.Bike rentals: The /forbidden-bikes page title explicitly reads 'Demo Bikes | Rental Bikes | Purchase Today'; Forbidden Druid and Dreadnought models available for 6-hour rides from the Garage

Custom builds are also available, and the shop participates in a tire stewardship recycling program.

A touring cyclist arriving with a mechanical will find a shop with genuine depth — multiple service tiers, suspension work, wheel building, and drivetrain overhaul all on the menu.

They operate the largest rental fleet in Vancouver, spanning cruisers, hybrids, mountain bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, tandems, and a full range of family and child options. bikeshop.name: Bubby's Mechanic Service
bikeshop.desc: Bubby's Bicycle Service Ltd. is a full-service independent bike shop in Errington on central Vancouver Island, run by mechanic Chris. The shop offers a comprehensive repair menu from basic tune-ups to full overhauls, stocks parts from an extensive brand catalogue, and sells used and consignment bikes. A pickup-and-delivery service means cyclists who can't transport their bike can still get it serviced.

notes.Touring parts stocked: Parts page lists Basil (panniers/cycling bags) among carried brands; repair menu includes rack install and fender install, indicating relevant stock

bikeshop.name: Cit-e Cycles
bikeshop.desc: Cit-E Cycles is BC's largest e-bike retailer, founded in Langley in 2011 and now operating six locations across the province, with this Langley address serving as its headquarters. The shop carries 300+ e-bike models from 20+ premium brands spanning urban, mountain, touring, cargo, folding, and trike categories. Touring cyclists will find one of the widest e-bike selections in Canada along with in-store service and repair.

notes.E-bike service: Contact page explicitly lists 'Service & Repairs' as a service category; the entire business is focused on e-bikes, confirming e-bike service is offered

bikeshop.name: Comox Bike Company
bikeshop.desc: Comox Bike Company has been the Comox Valley's local bike shop since 1988, serving island riders across every trail network for over 35 years. An authorized retailer of Specialized, Santa Cruz, Cervélo, and Kona, they offer full sales, repair, professional bike fitting with 2DMA Motion Capture technology, and a premium rental fleet. Located a stone's throw from the Cumberland Trail Network and Forbidden Plateau, this is a natural stop for touring and trail cyclists on Vancouver Island.

notes.Bike rentals: Dedicated rentals page confirms high-end mountain bikes, e-MTBs (Santa Cruz Bullit, Vala; Specialized Levo), and a limited fleet of hybrid and road bikes for adults; all rentals include helmet and lock

bikeshop.name: Western Bike Company
bikeshop.desc: Western Bike Company is a premium cycling component dealer and specialist service shop located in Cumberland, BC — Vancouver Island's legendary mountain biking hub. The shop focuses on custom wheel builds and RideWrap frame protection installation, partnering with high-end brands such as Chris King, NOBL Wheels, Maxxis Tires, and Sapim Spokes. Touring cyclists passing through Cumberland for its hundreds of kilometres of single-track, road, and gravel routes will find a knowledgeable team oriented toward quality builds and bike protection rather than general repair.

bikeshop.name: Trail Bicycles
bikeshop.desc: Trail Bicycles is a full-service bike shop in Courtenay serving the Comox Valley, carrying premium brands including Trek, Norco, Mondraker, Ibis, Pivot, and Salsa. They hold Shimano Service Centre certification, meaning mechanics are trained to the latest standards using genuine Shimano parts. Visiting cyclists can also rent full-suspension mountain bikes with helmets and get insider knowledge on local trails including the renowned Cumberland network.
req_checked: Staff help with urgent mechanical issues

notes.Walk-in repairs: or just fix a flat
notes.E-bike service: Shimano Service Centre certification and active e-bike sales (Norco, Mondraker, Trek Fuel+); service page states 'Any type of bike is welcome at Trail.'
notes.Bike rentals: Dedicated rentals page confirms 'premium performance and well-maintained full suspension mountain bikes ready for you to rent'; fleet includes Trek Fuel EX and Trek Fuel+ EX; rentals include helmet and basic repair kit

transport.name: Modo Car Share
transport.desc: Co-operative car share with hundreds of home locations across the Lower Mainland (Vancouver, Burnaby, Surrey, Richmond, Coquitlam and more), Victoria area (including Esquimalt, Oak Bay, Saanich, Sidney), Nanaimo, Squamish, and Kelowna. Also at major BC Ferries terminals. Open to non-BC residents — N licence or equivalent from any jurisdiction required. Some vehicles have exterior bike racks; SUVs and minivans available for carrying bikes inside.

notes.Interior transport: SUVs and minivans available for carrying bikes inside
notes.Exterior rack: Available on select vehicles — check vehicle listing when booking

transport.name: BC Ferries
transport.desc: Vehicle and passenger ferry operator serving coastal BC. Key routes for cyclists: Horseshoe Bay to Nanaimo (Departure Bay and Duke Point), Tsawwassen to Swartz Bay and Duke Point, and routes to the Sunshine Coast, Gulf Islands, and Vancouver Island.

transport.name: WestJet
transport.desc: Canadian airline serving Kelowna (YLW), Kamloops (YKA), and other BC cities. Bikes must be boxed or bagged; e-bikes not accepted. Bike fee applies.

transport.name: Air Canada
transport.desc: National airline serving Vancouver (YVR), Victoria (YYJ), Kelowna (YLW), Kamloops (YKA), Cranbrook (YXC), and other BC cities. Bikes must be pre-registered; boxed or bagged only; e-bikes not accepted. Fee approximately $50 CAD per direction.

transport.name: Pacific Coastal Airlines
transport.desc: Regional airline connecting Vancouver with smaller BC communities including Cranbrook (YXC), Castlegar (YCG), Trail (YZZ), Campbell River, Port Hardy, and others. Advance booking required; e-bikes explicitly prohibited. Fee approximately $105 CAD per direction. Small aircraft with limited space.

transport.name: Harbour Air Seaplanes
transport.desc: Floatplane service connecting Vancouver, Victoria, Nanaimo, Salt Spring Island, and other coastal BC destinations. Bike transport on space-available basis only; advance booking required; 50 lb weight limit; no trailers. Contact before booking.

transport.name: EBus
transport.desc: Intercity bus service connecting Chilliwack, Abbotsford, Kelowna, Kamloops, and other BC communities. Bikes accepted in the under-bus luggage hold; must be boxed or wrapped in cloth (plastic wrap not accepted). Fee: $30 per bike. E-bike and trailer policy unconfirmed — call before travelling: 1-877-769-3287.

transport.name: Rider Express
transport.desc: Intercity bus service connecting Chilliwack, Kelowna, Kamloops, Cranbrook, and other BC communities. Bikes accepted; must be wrapped or boxed. Fee: $50 per bike, non-refundable even if bike not brought. E-bike and trailer policy unconfirmed — contact before travelling: 1-833-583-3636.

transport.name: VIA Rail
transport.desc: National passenger rail. The Canadian runs Vancouver to Kamloops, Jasper, and Toronto. Walk-on bikes accepted with advance booking; dedicated bike room on The Canadian.

transport.name: Tofino Express Bus (Island Link)
transport.desc: Island Link intercity bus connecting Nanaimo, Port Alberni, Ucluelet, and Tofino. Does NOT accept bicycles.

transport.name: Island Express Bus (Island Link)
transport.desc: Island Link intercity bus connecting Nanaimo, Courtenay, and Campbell River. Does NOT accept bicycles.

transport.name: Victoria Express Bus (Island Link)
transport.desc: Island Link intercity bus connecting Nanaimo and Victoria. Does NOT accept bicycles.

transport.name: Amtrak Cascades
transport.desc: Intercity passenger rail connecting Vancouver (Pacific Central Station) south to Seattle, Portland, and Eugene. Some trains have a dedicated bike car allowing unboxed or bagged bikes; other services require boxing. Bike space must be reserved in advance; fee applies.

transport.name: Black Ball Transport - MV Coho
transport.desc: Car and passenger ferry between Victoria (Inner Harbour) and Port Angeles, Washington. Key international crossing for cyclists on the Pacific Coast route. Walk-on cyclists welcome; bikes travel unboxed on vehicle deck. Bike fee applies. Reservations recommended.

transport.name: Victoria Clipper
transport.desc: High-speed passenger-only catamaran ferry between Victoria (Inner Harbour) and Seattle, Washington. Bikes travel unboxed on the outer deck, exposed to weather. Advance booking required — call or submit a Contact Us form; cannot show up with a bike unannounced. Bike fee: $30/direction (confirm currency — may be USD). Space very limited; first-booked, first-served. E-bike policy unconfirmed.

transport.name: Hullo Ferries
transport.desc: Passenger ferry between Nanaimo and Vancouver (Waterfront Station). Max 2 bike spots per sailing; walk-on, fully assembled, must roll on/off. Fee: $30 one way, $50 return. No e-bikes; no trailers; max 50 lbs and 80 inches. Book ahead — spots are very limited.

transport.name: Enterprise / National Car Rental
transport.desc: Enterprise and National Car Rental (same company) have locations in Squamish, North Vancouver, Vancouver, Chilliwack, Nanaimo, Victoria, Kelowna, Vernon, Kamloops, and Cranbrook. SUVs and minivans available — with seats folded, a disassembled bike fits. One-way rentals available between some locations; drop fee applies. No bike racks for rent. Call to confirm vehicle type and one-way availability before booking.

transport.name: Avis / Budget
transport.desc: Avis and Budget (same company) have the widest BC coverage of the major chains, including Whistler (Avis), Nelson (Budget — call to confirm), and Tofino (Budget — seasonal, airport only). Also in Vancouver, North Vancouver, Chilliwack, Nanaimo, Victoria, Kelowna, Vernon, Kamloops, and Cranbrook. SUVs and minivans available. One-way rentals available between some locations; drop fee applies. No bike racks for rent. Call to confirm vehicle type and one-way availability before booking.

transport.name: Hertz
transport.desc: Hertz has locations in Squamish, North Vancouver, Vancouver, Chilliwack, Nanaimo, Victoria, Kelowna, Kamloops (airport only, limited hours), and Cranbrook. The only major chain in BC that rents hitch-mounted bike racks (4-bike capacity) — availability varies by location. One-way rentals available between some locations; drop fee applies. Call to confirm vehicle type, bike rack availability, and one-way options before booking.

notes.Exterior rack: Hitch-mounted 4-bike rack; availability varies by location — call ahead to confirm

transport.name: Evo Car Share
transport.desc: One-way car share operated by BCAA. Every Evo vehicle is fitted with two Thule roof-mounted bike racks. Free-floating service in Metro Vancouver and Victoria — pick up any available car and drop it off anywhere within the zone. Evo Return is a scheduled one-way option at Nanaimo (Hullo Ferry Terminal) and Tofino — book in advance. Membership required before your trip.

notes.Exterior rack: All vehicles fitted with Thule roof-mounted bike racks (2 bikes per vehicle)

transport.name: Uber
transport.desc: Ride-hailing available in Vancouver, North Vancouver, Squamish, Whistler, Chilliwack, Kelowna, Penticton, Kamloops, Cranbrook, Nelson, Nanaimo, Victoria, Duncan, and Sidney following BC's province-wide expansion in 2025. Not available in Tofino or Ucluelet. Uber XL (minivan or large SUV) is confirmed in Vancouver and Victoria; check the app to see if it's available in your area. Uber XL can typically fit an unboxed bike — contact your driver after matching to confirm before they arrive. No official bike policy; transport is at the driver's discretion.

transport.name: RiLo
transport.desc: App-based ride-hailing from Black Top & Checker Cabs (iOS/Android), using licensed taxi vehicles and professional Class 4 drivers. Fixed fares locked at booking with no surge pricing. Launched June 2026 with an initial focus on the City of Vancouver and trips to/from Vancouver International Airport (YVR); the app works across Metro Vancouver, but wait times and fares for suburban long-distance trips are currently high until more fleet joins. Holds Passenger Transportation Board TNS authorization for Region 1 (Metro Vancouver, Fraser Valley, and the Sea-to-Sky corridor to Squamish, Whistler, and Pemberton). A four-seat or six-seat van option carries oversized items such as a bike; an extra $15 charge applies to the four-seat van if the trip's purpose is to move cargo. Rides can be pre-booked up to three weeks in advance. Wheelchair-accessible vehicles available.

notes.Interior transport: Four-seat or six-seat van with luggage space for a bike; +$15 on the four-seat van if booked to move cargo

transport.name: Coastal Rides
transport.desc: BC-based ride-hailing app covering communities where Uber doesn't operate, including Squamish, Whistler, Tofino, Ucluelet, and Nanaimo. Some drivers have bike racks — use the filter in the app to add the number of bikes to your request. For drivers without a rack, whether a bike fits depends on the vehicle; you may need to remove a wheel or partially disassemble. See coastalrides.ca/blog/sunshine-coast-bike-road-trip for an example of the service in action.

transport.name: Skylynx
transport.desc: Scheduled motor coach between YVR/Downtown Vancouver, Squamish (reservation-only stop), and Whistler Village. Summer service April 18 – November 21. Bikes must be boxed or bagged — no bare bikes. First bike included in fare; additional bikes $10 each. E-bike and trailer policy not published; contact operator before travelling.

transport.name: Squamish Connector
transport.desc: Scheduled bus between Squamish and Vancouver (Waterfront Station and Hyatt Hotel, Melville St), with stops at West Van, Horseshoe Bay, Lions Bay, and Britannia Beach. Summer service May–September. Bikes carried on external rack (max 2 per bus; call ahead to reserve — not all buses have a rack). Fee $15/bike each way per policy pages (homepage states free — confirm by phone). E-bikes generally not permitted. Unboxed bikes OK on rack; bagged or boxed OK in luggage hold.

transport.name: TransLink
transport.desc: Greater Vancouver regional transit. Bikes accepted on all modes: buses (exterior front rack, 2-bike max), SeaBus (up to 6 bikes at peak), SkyTrain Canada Line (1 bike/car, all times), Expo and Millennium lines (2 bikes/car), and West Coast Express (2 bikes/car). No bike fee on any mode.

transport.name: BC Transit
transport.desc: Regional bus systems throughout BC outside Metro Vancouver. Most buses are equipped with exterior front-mounted 2-bike racks; bikes ride unboxed. No bike fee. Trailers not permitted. E-bike policy varies by system — check with your local system before travelling. Regional systems include: Squamish and Whistler (WAVE), Chilliwack, Kelowna Regional, Vernon Regional, Kamloops, Cranbrook/East Kootenay, Nelson, South Okanagan (Penticton), Cowichan Valley, Victoria Regional, and Pacific Rim (Tofino/Ucluelet).

transport.name: Kami Cabs
transport.desc: Local taxi service in Kamloops. Hatchback cabs can carry bikes — phone ahead to arrange.

transport.name: Cowichan Valley Taxi
transport.desc: Local taxi service operating in Duncan and the Cowichan Valley. Ability to transport a bicycle depends on vehicle type and driver discretion.

transport.name: Seabus
transport.desc: Passenger-only catamaran ferry service operated by TransLink connecting Waterfront Station in downtown Vancouver to Lonsdale Quay in North Vancouver. This is the primary transit link from Vancouver to the start of the route. Accommodates bicycles: bikes are permitted on board and taken inside the vessel as-is, no extra fare required beyond standard transit fare. Passenger + bike: riders board with their bicycles directly. Walk-on bikes: cyclists walk their bikes on board. Interior transport: bikes are brought into the enclosed cabin area of the vessel

transport.name: SeaBus (TransLink)
transport.desc: Passenger ferry connecting Lonsdale Quay (North Vancouver) to Waterfront Station (Vancouver). Passenger + bike: cyclists may bring unboxed bicycles aboard and travel with them inside the vessel. Walk-on bikes: bicycles are walked on and stored inside the cabin. Interior transport: bikes are carried inside the vessel, no exterior rack

detail.address: 123 Carrie Cates Ct, North Vancouver, BC V7M 3J8

transport.name: Kootenay Lake Ferry
transport.desc: Free inland vehicle and passenger ferry operated by BC Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure, connecting Balfour to Kootenay Bay across Kootenay Lake. Approximately 35-minute crossing. Year-round service. Accommodates bicycles: cyclists walk or roll bikes aboard as foot passengers at no charge. No reservations; service is first-come, first-served. Passenger + bike: cyclists board as foot passengers with their bike. Walk-on bikes: roll your bike directly onto the vehicle deck. Unboxed bikes OK: no packaging required, bikes roll on as-is

transport.name: West Coast Trail Express
transport.desc: Provides shuttle services to the West Coast Trail and other destinations. Accommodates bicycles: they transport cyclists with bikes on their shuttles. Passenger + bike: shuttle buses have space for passengers and their bicycles

transport.name: Alberni Marine Transportation Ltd.
transport.desc: MV Frances Barkley passenger and cargo ferry between Port Alberni and Ucluelet; carries bicycles with advanced reservation. Shuttle / trip support: ferry transport for cyclists and bikes.

detail.address: P. O. Box 188, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 7M7

notes.Passenger + bike: Carries the cyclist and their bike

transport.name: Penticton Taxi
transport.desc: Local taxi service in Penticton. Larger vehicle requests may be able to accommodate bicycles; confirm capacity and availability when booking

transport.name: FlixBus
transport.desc: Intercity bus service operating routes through the Fraser Valley corridor. Connects to Vancouver and Interior BC destinations

transport.name: Aquabus Ferries
transport.desc: Small passenger ferry service on False Creek with stops at Granville Island, Hornby Street (downtown), Yaletown, David Lam Park, and Stamp's Landing. Passenger + bike: bikes may be accommodated on the small open deck vessels subject to available space; capacity is very limited

transport.name: Epic Ride
transport.desc: Epic Rides offers shuttle services for mountain bikers, accommodating bicycles on their vehicles. Accommodates bicycles: bikes are transported on shuttles designed for mountain biking. Passenger + bike: shuttles can carry both passengers and their bikes

transport.name: Whistler Shuttle
transport.desc: Whistler Shuttle provides transportation services to and from Whistler, accommodating bicycles on their shuttles. Accommodates bicycles: bikes can be transported on shuttles with advance notice. Passenger + bike: shuttles can carry both passengers and their bikes

detail.address: 8056 Nesters Rd #1, Whistler, BC V8E 0G4, Canada

transport.name: Rocky Mountaineer
transport.desc: Multi-day luxury scenic rail through the BC interior and Canadian Rockies, daytime travel only with overnight hotel stops. Routes run Vancouver to Banff, Lake Louise, and Jasper via Kamloops, plus a Vancouver to Seattle Coastal Passage. Bikes are not carried in the coaches; a bicycle travels as oversized checked luggage moved separately by road and meets you at your hotel, likely for a surcharge. Confirm bicycle handling with the operator in advance.

transport.name: Cold Shot
transport.desc: Intercity coach serving northern BC and Alberta. Licensed route: Fort St John to the BC/Alberta border.

transport.name: Cantrail Coach Lines
transport.desc: Scheduled coach between Vancouver and the Washington state border.

transport.name: Greyhound Lines
transport.desc: Cross-border intercity coach between Vancouver and the Washington state border.

transport.name: Quick Shuttle (Quick Coach Lines)
transport.desc: Scheduled cross-border coach between Vancouver and the US border on the Seattle corridor.

transport.name: Mountain Man Mike's
transport.desc: Small Kootenay intercity coach. Licensed routes: Kaslo to Vancouver, Kaslo to the Alberta border, and Osoyoos to Kelowna. Runs on recycled fryer oil.

transport.name: Silver City Stagelines
transport.desc: Intercity coach between Nelson and Kelowna through the Kootenays and Okanagan.

transport.name: Kootenay Charters
transport.desc: Scheduled coach between the City of Nelson and the Paterson border crossing.

transport.name: Sunshine Coast Connector
transport.desc: Scheduled bus along the lower Sunshine Coast between Powell River and the Langdale ferry terminal.

transport.name: Eagle Transit
transport.desc: Local intercity bus on Haida Gwaii between the City of Queen Charlotte (Daajing Giids) and Masset.

transport.name: Kimta Transportation Society
transport.desc: Community intercity bus between Mackenzie and Prince George in northern BC.

transport.name: Atlin Trucking and Cartage
transport.desc: Carrier serving the remote northwest, with a licensed passenger route between Atlin and the Yukon.

transport.name: Thompson Valley Charters
transport.desc: Kamloops-based coach operator. Licensed routes: Kamloops to Sun Peaks Resort and Kamloops to the BC/Alberta border.

transport.name: Waivin Flags
transport.desc: North Vancouver Island carrier running a scheduled route between Port Hardy and Campbell River (also operates a taxi service).

transport.name: Wilson's Transportation (BC Connector)
transport.desc: Scheduled coach network on southern Vancouver Island and the Victoria to Vancouver corridor, operating as BC Connector / Island Connector.

transport.name: Big White Shuttle (Big White Central Reservations)
transport.desc: Seasonal ski shuttle between Kelowna and Big White Ski Resort.

transport.name: Snowbus (Blue Cactus Coach Lines)
transport.desc: Seasonal ski shuttle to Whistler from Richmond and Burnaby.

transport.name: Mount Washington Pacific
transport.desc: Seasonal ski shuttle between Mount Washington Alpine Resort and Courtenay.

transport.name: Smith Transportation
transport.desc: Seasonal ski shuttle to Mount Washington Alpine Resort from Nanaimo and Victoria.

transport.name: Whitewater Shuttle
transport.desc: Seasonal ski shuttle between Nelson and Whitewater Ski Resort.

transport.name: Harbour Air Sunshine Coast Shuttle
transport.desc: Ground connector operated by Harbour Air between Sechelt and Madeira Park on the Sunshine Coast, feeding its floatplane service. Separate from the Harbour Air Seaplanes listing.

transport.name: Alberni District United Cabs Association
transport.desc: United Cabs is a 24/7 on-demand taxi service based in Port Alberni serving the Alberni Valley and broader Vancouver Island area. Fleet includes wheelchair-accessible vans; no stated bike policy.

transport.name: Sicamous Taxi
transport.desc: Locally owned on-demand taxi and shuttle service based in Sicamous, BC, covering the Shuswap and North Okanagan regions; offers airport, event, and golf-trip shuttles as well as local rides. No bike policy stated.

transport.name: Simba Taxi Services
transport.desc: Simba Taxi Services is a taxi operator registered in Victoria, BC; the Facebook page is nearly empty with no posts, no reviews, and no operational details, making current activity unverifiable.

transport.name: Kitimat Taxi
transport.desc: Kitimat Taxi Co. provides on-demand taxi and airport shuttle service in Kitimat and the Terrace area. Bike policy and vehicle fleet are not described on the site.

transport.name: Alberni Island Shuttle
transport.desc: Group charter and shuttle operator based in Port Alberni serving destinations across Vancouver Island, with at least one scheduled route (Port Alberni–Nanaimo). Primarily charter-based; no stated bike policy.

transport.name: Yelllow Cab
transport.desc: Yellow Cab is Vancouver's largest on-demand taxi company (408 cabs, 24/7), covering Metro Vancouver and destinations as far as Whistler, Squamish, and cross-border US cities. No bike carriage policy is stated; fleet includes minivans that could accommodate disassembled bikes.

transport.name: Howe Sound Taxi
transport.desc: On-demand taxi serving Squamish and the Sea to Sky corridor, including airport pickups; vans available but no stated bike policy.

transport.name: Nanaimo Airport Shuttle Service
transport.desc: On-demand door-to-door shuttle serving communities across the Greater Nanaimo Region plus Ladysmith, Duncan, Parksville, and Qualicum Beach, with connections to Nanaimo, Victoria, and Comox airports and all three Nanaimo-area ferry terminals. No bike policy stated.

transport.name: Mountain Shuttle & Cab
transport.desc: Mountain Shuttle connects East Kootenay and Rockies communities—Fernie, Kimberley, Cranbrook, Banff, Golden, and Calgary—via bookable shuttle routes including ski shuttles, golf shuttles, and airport transfers. No bike policy is stated on the website.

transport.name: A.C. Taxi
transport.desc: A.C. Taxi is Nanaimo's largest on-demand taxi company, operating 24/7 year-round with service to Nanaimo Airport, Departure Bay and Duke Point ferries, and surrounding communities. No bike policy is stated, but vans are available.

transport.name: Abbotsford Mission Taxi
transport.desc: On-demand taxi serving Abbotsford, Mission, and the Fraser Valley 24/7 since 1955, with airport runs to YVR and YXX. No bike policy stated on the website.

transport.name: Alouette Taxi
transport.desc: On-demand taxi serving Maple Ridge, Pitt Meadows, and surrounding communities, with runs to Vancouver Airport, Tsawwassen ferry terminal, and Horseshoe Bay. Fleet includes sedans and accessible vans; no stated bike policy.

transport.name: Aldergrove-Langley Taxi Ltd.
transport.desc: On-demand taxi service based in Langley, BC offering airport transfers, long-distance rides, and accessible transportation with wheelchair-equipped vehicles. No stated bike policy; hours are Mon–Sat 9 am–6:30 pm despite '24/7' claims.

transport.name: North Coast Shuttle And Expediting
transport.desc: On-demand limo and shuttle service based in Terrace, BC, connecting Prince Rupert, Kitimat, and Dease Lake for airport, train, employee, and general passenger transport. No bike policy stated; SUVs and coach party buses in fleet.

transport.name: Eco Taxi
transport.desc: On-demand taxi serving Kelowna, Lake Country, and West Kelowna with personalized airport service to YLW; no bike policy stated on the page.

transport.name: Ambassador Taxi
transport.desc: On-demand shuttle and taxi service based in Comox Valley, covering YQQ airport, Mt Washington, and the Little River Ferry Terminal, with runs extending down Vancouver Island to Nanaimo, Tofino, and beyond. No bike policy stated on the site.

transport.name: Bluebird Cabs
transport.desc: Bluebird Cabs is a large on-demand taxi company serving Greater Victoria, BC, available 24/7 with a 100-vehicle fleet including vans and minivans. No stated bike policy; larger vehicles in the fleet could potentially accommodate a bicycle.

transport.name: Cypress Coach Lines
transport.desc: Scheduled shuttle connecting downtown Vancouver, North Vancouver (Lonsdale Quay), and Park Royal to Cypress Mountain; operates winter ski season and summer activities, with charter coach service also available to Whistler, YVR, Victoria, and Seattle.

transport.name: Big Mountain Little Shuttle
transport.desc: Private on-demand shuttle service connecting Kelowna International Airport, Kelowna area communities, and Okanagan ski resorts (Big White, SilverStar, Sun Peaks, Revelstoke). Fleet includes a 12-passenger Ford Transit van and two Ford Expedition SUVs; no bike policy stated.

transport.name: Bee-Line Taxi
transport.desc: Bee Line Taxi is an on-demand taxi serving Campbell River and the surrounding area from Black Creek to the northeast side of Vancouver Island, including airport and long-distance trips. No bike policy is stated.

transport.name: Peachland Taxi
transport.desc: Peachland Taxi is a single-driver taxi and airport shuttle serving Peachland and the broader Kelowna/West Kelowna corridor, with flat-rate runs to Kelowna (YLW) and Penticton (YYF) airports; advance booking required and service is intermittently unavailable.

transport.name: Bel-Air Taxi (1982) Limited
transport.desc: On-demand taxi serving Coquitlam, Burnaby, Port Moody, Port Coquitlam, New Westminster, and Vancouver International Airport, 24/7. No stated bike policy; fleet includes station wagons which may accommodate a bicycle.

transport.name: Victoria Taxi
transport.desc: Victoria Taxi is a 70-car on-demand taxi service operating 24/7 across Greater Victoria, serving the airport, multiple ferry terminals, and destinations as far as Tofino and Campbell River. No bike policy is stated on the website.

transport.name: Safe And Sound Taxi Service
transport.desc: Local taxi service based in Lake Cowichan, BC. No usable business content was accessible from the Facebook page; service details, coverage area, and bike policy are unknown.

transport.name: Apple Cabs
transport.desc: Apple Cabs is an on-demand taxi service based in Kelowna serving city trips, Kelowna Airport, and ski resorts including Big White and Silver Star. No bike policy is stated on the site.

transport.name: Black Top Cabs
transport.desc: Black Top & Checker Cabs is Vancouver's largest taxi operator (200+ units), offering on-demand and pre-booked rides across the city including YVR airport runs. No bike policy is stated; fleet includes wheelchair-accessible vans and 90%+ hybrid vehicles.

transport.name: Bonny'S Taxi
transport.desc: On-demand taxi service based in Burnaby, BC, available 24/7. Most website subpages are unavailable (404), so service area, fleet, and bike policy are unknown.

transport.name: Central Valley Taxi
transport.desc: On-demand taxi service based in Abbotsford serving the Central Fraser Valley area. Bike carriage policy unknown due to website unavailability.

transport.name: Orange Taxi
transport.desc: Orange Taxi is a Sooke-based year-round on-demand taxi and Juan de Fuca Marine Trail shuttle, with published fixed fares from Sooke to all major trailheads (Jordan River, China Beach, Sombrio, Port Renfrew) and the BC Ferry Terminal. Fleet includes Prius cars and a van with fold-down ramp; no bike policy is stated on the site.

transport.name: Campbell River Cabs Ltd.
transport.desc: Campbell River Shuttle runs ferry-synchronized shuttles between Campbell River and Quadra Island (seasonal, resuming June 2026) and year-round airport/BC Ferries terminal transfers across Vancouver Island; bikes are currently not accepted.

transport.name: Cheam Taxi
transport.desc: On-demand taxi serving Chilliwack, Agassiz, and Harrison Hot Springs, with airport runs to YVR and YXX. Fleet includes wheelchair-accessible vans; no bike policy stated.

transport.name: Airport Link Shuttle
transport.desc: On-demand airport shuttle connecting Vancouver International Airport (YVR) to communities across the Fraser Valley, Lower Mainland, and Sea-to-Sky corridor including Abbotsford, Chilliwack, Hope, Squamish, and Whistler. Minimum 24-hour advance booking required; no bike policy stated.

transport.name: Chilliwack Taxi
transport.desc: On-demand taxi and ride service covering Chilliwack, Sardis, Agassiz, Harrison Hot Springs, and surrounding Fraser Valley communities since 1947, with airport pickups and six-seater vans available. No bike policy stated.

transport.name: Checkmate Cabs Ltd.
transport.desc: On-demand taxi service based in Kelowna operating 24/7, covering Kelowna and surrounding areas including airport transfers and Big White ski resort drop-offs. No bike policy stated.

transport.name: Yellow Cab Of Victoria
transport.desc: Yellow Cab of Victoria is an on-demand taxi service operating 24/7 across Greater Victoria and Vancouver Island, with a fleet of 190+ vehicles including minivans and vans. No bike policy is stated on the website.

transport.name: Cobble Hill Taxi
transport.desc: On-demand taxi serving the South Cowichan Valley (Cobble Hill/Shawnigan Lake area), with runs to Nanaimo and Victoria airports and Nanaimo/Swartz Bay ferry terminals. No bike policy stated; fleet includes a wheelchair-accessible van.

transport.name: Creston Cabs
transport.desc: On-demand taxi service covering Creston, Trail, and Castlegar with long-distance trips available to Nelson, Cranbrook, and Vancouver. No bicycle policy is stated anywhere on the site.

transport.name: Coquitlam Taxi
transport.desc: Coquitlam Taxi is an on-demand taxi service operating 24/7 in Coquitlam and Port Coquitlam, offering airport transfers and wheelchair-accessible vehicles; no bike policy is stated.

transport.name: Current Taxi
